Then cover the whole altar with bronze, including the four horns. 3All the equipment for the altar must also be made of bronze—the pans for the hot ashes, the shovels, the sprinkling bowls, the meat forks, and the fire pans. 4-5Halfway up the altar build a ledge around it, and cover the bottom half of the altar with a decorative bronze grating. Then attach a bronze ring beneath the ledge at the four corners of the altar. 6-7Cover two acacia wood poles with bronze and put them through the rings for carrying the altar. 8Construct the altar in the shape of an open box, just as you were shown on the mountain.
The Courtyard around the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 38.9-20)
The Lord said:
9-15Surround the sacred tent with a courtyard 44 meters long on the south and north and 22 meters wide on the east and west. Use 20 bronze posts on bronze stands for the south and north and 10 for the west. Then hang a curtain of fine linen on the posts along each of these three sides by using silver hooks and rods.
Place three bronze posts on each side of the entrance at the east and hang a curtain 6.67 meters wide on each set of posts. 16Use four more of these posts for the entrance way, then hang on them an embroidered curtain of fine linen nine meters long and woven with blue, purple, and red wool.
17-18Make the curtains that surround the courtyard 2.25 meters high and hang them from the bronze posts with silver hooks and rods. 19Make the rest of the equipment for the sacred tent of bronze, including the pegs for the tent and for the curtain surrounding the courtyard.
The Oil for the Lamp in the Holy Place
(Leviticus 24.1-4)
The Lord said to Moses:
20Command the people of Israel to supply you with the purest olive oil. Do this so the lamp will keep burning 21in front of the curtain that separates the holy place from the most holy place, where the sacred chest is kept. Aaron and his sons are responsible for keeping the lamp burning every night in the sacred tent. The Israelites must always obey this command.
translation_text:
Nsaraafan
1«Á dū akasiya dɔŋu kí kpáá nsaraafan ŋun cáá ajannaatil ŋmèe. Dijandi diba ń nīn cáá meetab bili nì dijandi, ní ŋu-fɔkɔŋŋu ń nīn sá meeta ubɔ nì dijandi. 2Ŋu-jaŋŋi naatil kpiŋŋi puee, á kpítí kí lēē iyin án jɔ̄m̀, i nì nsaraafan ń nīn sá mmɔm, ní á dū tasa kúti kí nyùntī. 3Á dū tasa kúti kí mɔ́ɔ́ tin kɔkɔ bi làá nīn cáa tūǹ nsaraafan pu tundee. An dàkà yii asambil ŋin poon bi làá nīn fà ŋkpam min bi wùn̄ee fantam ki ŋáańee nì peelab nì asambil ŋin poon bi làá nīn ŋáań fatiku ki cáa yàantée, nì njiimu mun cáá anyinee nì nsambiyaamu mun poon bi tùutī talaaluee. 4Á dū tasa kúti kí mɔ́ɔ́ kilàaŋ́ŋi ní kí ŋá ki-jaŋŋi naatil pu abɔmbil 5kí dūú nákań nsaraafan taapu kí màntīí tū ní án jɔ̄mìń kí dāá ŋmàntī ŋu-kansikin. 6Á dū akasiya dɔŋu kí kpítí ikpandɔ, kí dū tasa kúti kí nyùntī-mu. 7Á dū ikpandɔee kí bɔ̄ abɔmbil ŋin bí nsaraafan jaŋŋi puee poon bí ŋmā kí nīn yòontí-ŋu. 8Á dū ndɔ kí kpáá nsaraafan gbanti, ŋu-poon ń nīn dɔ̄ fám tiba ń taa nín kā. Á kpáá-ŋu kii m nín dàkā-si dijool nee pu á kpáá puee.
Circir kɔŋkooŋŋu cindi ŋaabui
9«Á yàntī circir kɔŋkooŋŋu ń nīn cáá dicindi. Á dū gulfa un dàfèe kí lù satab kí dūú bàkā ŋgiil pú, ŋfɔkɔn ń nīn sá meetab imuŋku ili nì saalaa. 10Á dū mbɔmbilɔ̀kɔkaamu nì tibakaal tin bi dū animbil kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́yee kí cúú satabee kí dūú sàkan̄ idɔjaa mmuŋku in bi dū tasa kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́yee pu. Idɔjaayee làá nīn cáá titílkaal mmuŋku tin bi dū tasa kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́yee. 11Á ŋá míǹ mbaantiim ŋgan pú jandi mun. Niin mun ń nīn cáá satab meetab imuŋku ili nì saalaa ki sàkā idɔ mmuŋku in tílkaati sá tasa kútee, nì in pu animbil kúti bɔmbilɔkɔkaamu nì ti-bakaati bée. 12Circir kɔŋkooŋŋu ŋwaan pu ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki watilee, satab fɔkɔŋŋu ń nīn sá meetab mmuŋku nì biŋmoo, kí nīn sàkā idɔjaa saalaa in tɔ́kɔ́ titílkaal saalaa mun puee. 13Circir kɔŋkooŋŋu cindi ŋwaan pu dijandi din bí ŋwìiń nyalaŋki watilee mun ń nīn cáá meetab mmuŋku nì biŋmoo. 14Dijandi diba pú satab fɔkɔŋŋu ń nīn sá meetab biluli nì dijandi, nì idɔjaa ita nì i-taapu tílkaati tita. 15Dijandi din kíǹee pú satab fɔkɔŋŋu ń nīn sá meetab biluli nì dijandi, nì idɔjaa ita nì i-taapu tílkaati tita. 16Circir kɔŋkooŋŋu mɔŋkiŋu punyɔkɔ ŋaasakaŋkaaŋu fɔkɔŋŋu ń nīn sá meetab saalaa. Á dū gulfa un dàfì kí máǹ gùŋgumee, nì un máǹ cínciŋee, nì un máǹ wèeeeyee kí nyāantì-i. Í nīn sàkā idɔjaa inaa in tɔ́kɔ́ titílkaal tinaa mun puee. 17Á dū tibakaal tin bi dū animbil kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́yee kí cúú idɔjaa in bi cóoǹ ki māntìi tú circir kɔŋkooŋŋu cindee kí kpāfì. Á dū animbil kúti kí mɔ́ɔ́ mbɔmbilɔ̀kɔkaamuee, ní kí dū tasa kúti kí mɔ́ɔ́ idɔjaa tílkaati. 18Circir kɔŋkooŋŋu cindi púuŋŋu fɔkɔŋŋu ń nīn sá meetab imuŋku ili nì saalaa, ŋu-waaŋŋu ń nīn sá mmuŋku nì biŋmoo, ní aŋaajan fɔkɔŋŋu ń nīn cáá meetab bili nì dijandi. Idɔjaa tílkaati ń nīn sá tasa kúti. 19Á dū tasa kúti kí mɔ́ɔ́ tin kɔkɔ bi làá nīn cáa tūǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu poon tundee ki kpáaǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu kpakpaaŋi nì ŋu-cindi yaŋ.»
Circir kɔŋkooŋŋu fitilab kpam
20«Á tùkù Isirayeel yab yii bí cáań-si ɔliifi kpam min ŋān̄ ki wāĺ kílkilee á nīn cáa sìtī fitilab poon, án nín làá ŋá pu fitilab ń nīn pée fòol̄ ŋyunti kamaayee. 21Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi ń dāá dū fitilab tɔ́kɔŋkaati kí yóoń circir kɔŋkooŋŋu poon ŋŋaapìtikaa ŋun lìkī baa wāĺ Dipoondi dakaauee nimbiin. Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi ń bɔ́ntí fitilab gbanti tiŋan án nín làá ŋá pu bí nīn pée fòol̄ ŋyunti kamaa m-nimbiin kí yòon̄ kujoou kí cáá sāā kutaafaauee. An sá mara ní m yóoǹ Isirayeel yab bí nīn ŋáań míǹ kí nīn pée cáa cá jaanjaan.»

english_text:
The Clothes for the High Priest
(Exodus 39.1-7)
The Lord said to Moses:
1Send for your brother Aaron and his sons Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar. They are the ones I have chosen from Israel to serve as my priests. 2Make Aaron some beautiful clothes that are worthy of a high priest. 3Aaron is to be dedicated as my high priest, and his clothes must be made only by persons who possess skills that I have given them. 4Here are the items that need to be made: a breastpiece, a priestly vest, a robe, an embroidered shirt, a turban, and a sash. These sacred clothes are to be made for your brother Aaron and his sons who will be my priests. 5Use only gold and fine linen, woven with blue, purple, and red wool, for making these clothes.
The Vest for the High Priest
(Exodus 39.2-7)
The Lord said:
6-8Make the entire priestly vest of fine linen skillfully woven with blue, purple, and red wool, and decorate it with gold. It is to have two shoulder straps to support it and a sash that fastens around the waist.
9-12Put two onyx stones in gold settings, then attach one to each of the shoulder straps. On one of these stones engrave the names of Israel's first six sons in the order of their birth. And do the same with his remaining six sons on the other stone. In this way Aaron will always carry the names of the tribes of Israel when he enters the holy place, and I will never forget my people.
13-14Attach two gold settings to the shoulder straps and fasten them with two braided chains of pure gold.
The Breastpiece for the High Priest
(Exodus 39.8-21)
The Lord said:
15From the same costly material make a breastpiece for the high priest to use in finding out what I want my people to do. 16It is to be 22 centimeters square and folded double 17with four rows of three precious stones: In the first row put a carnelian, a chrysolite, and an emerald; 18in the second row a turquoise, a sapphire, and a diamond; 19in the third row a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst; 20and in the fourth row a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper. Mount the stones in delicate gold settings 21and engrave on each of them the name of one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
22-25Attach two gold rings to the upper front corners of the breastpiece and fasten them with two braided gold chains to gold settings on the shoulder straps. 26Attach two other gold rings to the lower inside corners next to the vest 27and two more near the bottom of the shoulder straps right above the sash. 28Then take a blue cord and tie the two lower rings on the breastpiece to those on the vest. This will keep the breastpiece in place.
29In this way Aaron will have the names of the twelve tribes of Israel written on his heart each time he enters the holy place, and I will never forget my people. 30 He must also wear on his breastpiece the two small objects that he uses to receive answers from me.
The Other High-Priestly Clothes
(Exodus 39.22-26,30,31)
The Lord said:
31Under his vest Aaron must wear a robe of blue wool 32with an opening in the center for his head. Be sure to bind the material around the collar to keep it from wearing out. 33-34 Along the hem of the robe weave pomegranates of blue, purple, and red wool with a gold bell between each of them. 35If Aaron wears these clothes when he enters the holy place as my high priest, the sound of the bells will be heard, and his life will not be in danger.
36On a narrow strip of pure gold engrave the words: “Dedicated to the Lord.” 37Fasten it to the front of Aaron's turban with a blue cord, 38so he can wear it on his forehead. This will show that he will take on himself the guilt for any sins the people of Israel commit in offering their gifts to me, and I will forgive them.
39Make Aaron's robe and turban of fine linen and decorate his sash with fancy needlework.
The Clothes for the Other Priests
(Exodus 39.27-29)
40Since Aaron's sons are priests, they should also look dignified. So make robes, sashes, and special caps for them. 41Then dress Aaron and his sons in these clothes, pour olive oil on their heads, and ordain them as my priests.
42Make linen shorts for them that reach from the waist down to the thigh, so they won't expose themselves. 43Whenever they enter the sacred tent or serve at the altar or enter the holy place, they must wear these shorts, or else they will be guilty and die. This same rule applies to any of their descendants who serve as priests.
translation_text:
Bisaraaŋaliibi wampeeŋkaati
1«Á yàntī a-nabiki Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi, Nadaab nì Abiyuu nì Eeleeyasaar nì Itamaar ń dāan̄ a-cee. Á gàntī-bi Isirayeel yab kansikin bí nīn tūǹ man saraaŋatundi. 2Á ŋáĺ a-nabiki Aarɔn circir wampeeŋkaati án nīn cáá kunyaaŋŋu ki dàkà usaraaŋakpil nyooti. 3Á sòoǹ nì bitɔntɔnliibi bin kɔkɔ m gbéeǹ iciin famee, kí yàntī bí ŋáĺ Aarɔn tiwampeeŋkaal. Ú dāá nīn pēē-tì ní á dū-u kí sú-mi ú nīn bí man saraaŋatundin. 4Tiwampeeŋkaal tin a làá yàntī bí ŋáĺ-uee di sá kilɔbiki kin làá nīn pá u-bindi puee nì eefoodi nì dibɔkutifɔkɔl nì poon bɔkutil nì ŋŋaabu ŋun u làá nīn cáa fìǹ u-yilee nì ŋŋaabu dambalau. Á yàntī bí ŋáĺ tiwan gbanti kí tīī Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi bí nīn tūǹ man saraaŋatundi. 5Bí dū gulfab bin cáá sindaariya nyimee nì bin máǹ gùŋgumee, nì bin máǹ cínciŋee nì bin máǹ wèeeeyee nì bigulifapimbi bin dàfèe, kí lù tiwampeeŋkaal gbanti.»
Eefoodi
6«Bitɔntɔnliibi ń dū gulfab bin cáá sindaariya nyimee nì bin máǹ gùŋgumee nì bin máǹ cínciŋee nì bin máǹ wèeeeyee nì bigulifapimbi bin dàfèe kí lù eefoodi. 7Bí ŋáĺ ŋŋaacalimu muli kí bā ajan liitil nyɔɔgbaŋŋi bí nīn cáa cútí. 8Bí ŋáĺ eefoodi nì dambala un u làá nīn cáa cútée ń nīn sá tiwambaantiil. Bí dū gulfab bin cáá sindaariya nyimee nì bin máǹ gùŋgumee nì bin máǹ cínciŋee nì bin máǹ wèeeeyee nì bigulifapimbi bin dàfèe kí ŋáĺ dambala mun. 9Á dū ataŋkpanyaan ŋin bi yíì soowamee ali, kí dū kigaai kí ŋmà Jaakɔb jipɔmbi yiŋŋi ataŋkpeeyee pu. 10Á ŋmà ditaŋkpapeekaal pu ayin aluu, ní kí ŋmà dililiitiil mun pu ayin aluu, án nīn nóó Jaakɔb jipɔmbi nín kpíǹ kpíǹ tɔb puee. 11Á dū kigaai kí cáká Jaakɔb jipɔmbi yiŋŋi ataŋkpeeyee pu kii bi nín cákà kijalii puee, ní kí mɔ́ɔ́ sindaariya sɔnti kí dūú fúuń. 12Á dūú bā ŋŋaacalimu mun bi ŋáĺ ki tábíǹ eefoodee. Ataŋkpeeyee di làá nīn sá kii kudaaŋŋu ki téetí Jaakɔb jipɔmbi pu. Mimmee bi-yiŋŋi làá nīn náká Aarɔn gbigbipati liitil pu man ni-Dindaan nimbiin, ní ḿ nīn pée téetí bi-pu. 13Á dū sindaariya kí mɔ́ɔ́ tisɔnee liitil, 14ní kí dū sindaariyamɔnti kí mɔ́ɔ́ ikusaka ili mpalimu yam kí dūú cúú tisɔn tin poon ataŋkpeeyee fúuńee.»
Kilɔbiki kin pāantí usaraaŋakpil bindi puee
15«Á yàntī bitɔntɔnliibi ń dū gulfab bin cáá sindaariya nyimee, nì bin máǹ gùŋgumee nì bin máǹ cínciŋee nì bin máǹ wèeeeyee nì bigulifapimbi bin dàfèe kí lù kilɔbiki kin pāantí usaraaŋakpil bindi puee kí nákań eefoodi pu. 16Kilɔbiki gbanti jaŋŋi naatil ń nīn ŋmà ní dijandi kamaa ń nīn cáá santimeetab mmuŋku nì biŋmoo. 17Á dū ataŋkpanyaan kí nákań ikuul inaa ki-pu kí nyāantì-kì. Ŋkuupeepeekaa ń nīn sá ataŋkpanyaan ŋin bi yíì oodeemee, nì ŋin bi yíì piitidaayee nì ŋin bi yíì bareekeetee. 18Ŋkuuliliiti ń nīn sá ataŋkpanyaan ŋin bi yíì noofeekee, nì ŋin bi yíì safiiree nì ŋin bi yíì yaaliimee. 19Ŋkuutataatee ń nīn sá ataŋkpanyaan ŋin bi yíì leeseemee nì ŋin bi yíì seebooyee nì ŋin bi yíì alamaayee. 20Á dū ataŋkpanyaan ŋin bi yíì taarsiisee nì ŋin bi yíì soowamee, nì ŋin bi yíì yaasipee kí nákań ŋkuunanaati pu. Á dū sindaariya kí mɔ́ɔ́ tisɔn tin poon a làá dū ataŋkpanyaanee kí fúuńee. 21Á dū kigaai kí cáká Jaakɔb jipɔmbi saalaa nì bilee yiŋŋi ataŋkpanyaanee pu kii bi nín cákà kijalii pu puee. Ditaŋkpanyaandi kamaa puee, á ŋmà kunaakoou kubɔ yindi, di sá tinaakɔti sá saalaa nì tili ní.
22«Á dū sindaariyamɔnti kí mɔ́ɔ́ ikusaka ili mpalimu yam kí dūú cúú kilɔbikee. 23Á dū sindaariya kí mɔ́ɔ́ mbɔmbiyaamu muli kí túuń kilɔbikee nyɔɔgbaŋŋi liitil. 24Á dū sindaariya kusakayee kí bɔ̄ mbɔmbiyaamu muli mun túuń kilɔbikee nyɔɔgbaŋŋi buŋyin, 25ní kí dū anyɔɔgbán ali ŋin kíǹee kí bā sindaariya sɔnti tili tin poon ní ataŋkpanyaan fúuń eefoodi ŋaacalimmu puee, ní an nīn bí kilɔbikee nyɔkɔpu. 26Á dū sindaariya kí gíti mɔ́ɔ́ mbɔmbiyaamu muli kí dūú bā kilɔbikee nyɔɔgbaŋŋi taapu jandi án nīn nákáǹ eefoodi. 27Á dū sindaariya kí mɔ́ɔ́ mbɔmbiyaamu muli mun kí dūú bā iŋmii in bí eefoodi ŋaacalimmu puee taapu nnimbiin pú, laakin bi ŋáĺ ki táb́ee caŋin. Mbɔmbiyaamu gbanti làá nīn bí eefoodi dambalau yilpu pu ní. 28Á dū gulfaman gùŋgum ŋmiiŋu kí bɔ̄ kilɔbiki bɔmbiliŋ nì eefoodi bɔmbiliŋin kí kúĺ, ní kilɔbikee ń nīn pá eefoodi dambalau pu ki pɔ̄ɔ̄ kaa cìŋkī.
29«Ŋyunti kamaa Aarɔn yaa kɔ́ circir kɔŋkooŋŋunee, Jaakɔb jipɔmbi yiŋŋi làá nīn náká kilɔbiki kin pá u-bindi puee. Mimmee man ni-Dindaan làá nīn pée téetí ni-pu. 30Á dū Uriim nì Tumiim kí ŋá kilɔbiki kin pá usaraaŋakpil bindi puee poon. Mimmee án làá nīn pá u-bindi pu ŋyunti ŋun u yaa làá kɔ́nní m-nimbiinee. Di sá yii u yaa bí m-nimbiinee, an máaǹ kí nīn pée pá u-bindi pu ní ú ŋmā kí béé min ní m là Isirayeel yab ń ŋée.»
Asaraaŋabɔkuti ŋin kíǹee
31«Boonee á dū gulfab bin máǹ gùŋgumee kí lù dibɔkutifɔkɔl din pu eefoodi làá nīn pée. 32Á lēē di-kansikin kinyɔkɔ, u yaa làá pèen̄ee ú dū u-yil kí bɔ̄ niin. Á lù kinyɔkɔee nyɔɔgbaŋŋi ń nīn gbìfì ki dàfì kí taa ŋmā kí cátí. 33Á dū gulfab bin máǹ gùŋgumee nì bin máǹ wèeeeyee nì bin máǹ cínciŋee kí lù asubil ŋin bi yíì greenaadee kí lúntí dibɔkutilee júti taapu kí màntīí tū, ní kí dū sindaariya waŋkilimmu mun kí lúntí dibɔkutilee júti taapu kí màntīí tū. 34Á dū sindaariya waŋkilimmu nì greenaadi subiliŋ ŋin ni lùn̄ee kí lúntí dibɔkutil júti taapu kí nīn sākantí kí màntīí tū. 35Aarɔn yaa làá kɔ́ circir kɔŋkooŋŋun kí ŋá saraabi kí tīī-mee, ú nīn pēē dibɔkutil gbanti ní bí nīn gbìl̀ ŋwaŋkilimu siim pu, ní u yaa làá tí nyēē bí nīn gbìl̀ mu-pu. Mimmee waa làá kpú.
36«Á dū sindaariyamɔnti kí nyùntī kí nántiǹ mpumpukum, ní kí ŋmà an pu kii bi nín ŋmà kijalii pu puee yii: <Bi dū-u ki sú ti-Dindaan>. 37Á dū gulfa un máǹ gùŋgumee kí lù kiŋaacaliŋ kí dūú cúú kí nákań ŋŋaabu ŋun u cáa fìǹ u-yilee nyɔkɔpu pú. 38Sindaariya pumpukumee làá nīn pée bí Aarɔn yigbeel pu, án nín làá ŋá pu ú fōō Isirayeel yab nín yīntiǹ circir wanti tin kɔkɔ bi cáań ki ŋá saraayee kpitii kí túńee. Sindaariya pumpukumee làá nīn pée bí u-yigbeel pu ní man ni-Dindaan ń nín fōō saraabi gbanti.
39«Boonee á dū ŋŋaapiin ŋun bí fálfalee kí ŋáĺ Aarɔn bɔkutifɔkɔl poon yal, ní kí dū ŋŋaapiin ŋun bí fálfalee kí lù ŋŋaabu ú nīn cáa fìǹ u-yil ní kí ŋáĺ ŋŋaabu dambalau kí gbá-u.
40«Ní ŋáĺ tiwan gbanti tibaantiil, an dàkà yii dibɔkutifɔkɔl poon yal nì dambala nì ŋŋaabu ŋun bi cáa fìǹ diyilee kí tīī Aarɔn jipɔmbi, án nīn cáá kunyaaŋŋu kí dàkà usaraaŋal nyooti.
41«Á dū asaraaŋabɔkuti gbanti kí pèen̄ a-maan Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi. Á sìtī bi-yiliŋ ŋkpam kí dū-bi kí sú-mi bí nīn bí m-tundin. Mimmee a dū-bi ki sú-mi bi kpántì m-saraaŋaliibi dee. 42Á dū ŋŋaapiin ŋun bí fálfalee kí ŋáĺ-bi ncukutigimu kí bìin̄ bi-cancaŋgbeel pu, kí yòon̄ bi-caŋ kí cáá sāā bi-tapaŋŋi. 43Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi yaa làá kɔ́ circir kɔŋkooŋŋun àá bi yaa làá sútí kí pìl̄ nsaraafan kí tɔ̄ circir laŋki ditundee, bí dū ncukutigimuee kí lòon̄. Mimmee baa làá ŋá ikpiti in làá cáań-bi ŋkúmee. Án nīn sá mara un kaa kpántée ki tīī Aarɔn nì u-naantiibi bin làá dāá páań u-boonee.»

english_text:
Instructions for Ordaining Priests
(Leviticus 8.1-36)
The Lord said to Moses:
1When you ordain Aaron and his sons to serve me as priests, choose a young bull and two rams that have nothing wrong with them. 2Then from your finest flour make three batches of dough without yeast. Shape some of it into larger loaves, some into smaller loaves mixed with olive oil, and the rest into thin wafers brushed with oil. 3Put all of this bread in a basket and bring it when you come to sacrifice the three animals to me.
4Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the sacred tent and tell them to wash themselves. 5Dress Aaron in the priestly shirt, the robe that goes under the sacred vest, the vest itself, the breastpiece, and the sash. 6Put on his turban with its narrow strip of engraved gold 7and then ordain him by pouring olive oil on his head.
8Next, dress Aaron's sons in their special shirts, 9caps, and sashes, then ordain them, because they and their descendants will always be priests.
10Lead the bull to the entrance of the sacred tent, where Aaron and his sons will lay their hands on its head. 11Kill the bull near my altar in front of the tent. 12Use a finger to smear some of its blood on each of the four corners of the altar and pour out the rest of the blood on the ground next to the altar. 13Then take the fat from the animal's insides, as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat, and send them up as an offering to me in the smoke from the altar. 14But the meat, the skin, and the food still in the bull's stomach must be burned outside the camp as an offering to ask forgiveness for the sins of the priests.
15Bring one of the rams to Aaron and his sons and tell them to lay their hands on its head. 16Kill the ram and splatter its blood against all four sides of the altar. 17Cut up the ram, wash its insides and legs, and lay all of its parts on the altar, including the head. 18 Then make sure that the whole animal goes up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
19Bring the other ram to Aaron and his sons and tell them to lay their hands on its head. 20Kill the ram and place some of its blood on Aaron's right ear lobe, his right thumb, and the big toe of his right foot. Do the same for each of his sons and splatter the rest of the blood against the four sides of the altar. 21Then take some of the blood from the altar, mix it with the oil used for ordination, and sprinkle it on Aaron and his clothes, and also on his sons and their clothes. This will show that they and their clothes have been dedicated to me.
22This ram is part of the ordination service. So remove its right hind leg, its fat tail, the fat on its insides, as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat. 23Take one loaf of each kind of bread from the basket, 24and put this bread, together with the meat, into the hands of Aaron and his sons. Then they will lift it all up to show that it is dedicated to me. 25After this, put the meat and bread on the altar and send them up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
26You may eat the choice ribs from this second ram, but you must first lift them up to show that this meat is dedicated to me.
27-28In the future, when anyone from Israel offers the ribs and a hind leg of a ram either to ordain a priest or to ask for my blessing, the meat belongs to me, but it may be eaten by the priests. This law will never change.
29-30After Aaron's death, his priestly clothes are to be handed down to each descendant who succeeds him as high priest, and these clothes must be worn during the seven-day ceremony of ordination.
31Boil the meat of the ordination ram in a sacred place, 32then Aaron and his sons are to eat it together with the three kinds of bread at the entrance to the sacred tent. 33At their ordination, a ceremony of forgiveness was performed for them with this sacred food, and only they have the right to eat it. 34If any of the sacred food is left until morning, it must be completely burned.
35Repeat this ordination ceremony for Aaron and his sons seven days in a row, just as I have instructed you. 36Each day you must offer a bull as a sacrifice for sin and as a way of purifying the altar. In addition, you must smear the altar with olive oil to make it completely holy. 37Do this for seven days, and the altar will become so holy that anyone who touches it will become holy.
Daily Sacrifices
(Leviticus 6.8-13; Numbers 28.1-8)
The Lord said:
38Each day you must sacrifice two lambs a year old, 39one in the morning and one in the evening. 40-41With each lamb offer one kilogram of your finest flour mixed with a liter of pure olive oil, and also pour out a liter of wine as an offering. The smell of this sacrifice on the fires of the altar will be pleasing to me. 42-43You and your descendants must always offer this sacrifice on the altar at the entrance to the sacred tent.
People of Israel, I will meet and speak with you there, and my shining glory will make the place holy. 44Because of who I am, the tent will become sacred, and Aaron and his sons will become worthy to serve as my priests. 45I will live among you as your God, 46and you will know that I am the Lord your God, the one who rescued you from Egypt, so that I could live among you.
translation_text:
Bi dū bisaraaŋaliibi ki sú ti-Dindaan
1«A nín làá dī pu ní kí dū Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi kí sú-mi bí kpántí man saraaŋaliibee sèé.
«Á yòon̄ dinajapɔmbil nì ipijaa ili in laaba kaa wɔ̀b̄ee, 2nì kpɔnɔ un kaa cáá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee, nì kalaabi bin bi dū ŋkpam ki ŋmālim̀ ki búuń ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔ kpá poonee, nì ŋkpɔnɔwaamu mun pu bi yɔ́kɔfì ŋkpam ki púĺ ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔ kpá poonee. Bilee yim ní bí dūú ŋá an kɔkɔ. 3Á dū kɔkɔ kí ŋá kukabiku kubɔn kí cáań circir kɔŋkooŋŋun, kí kpáaǹ dinajapɔmbil nì ipijaa ilee.
4«Á cáań Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu kí fàl̀-bi nnyim bí nyā kí nīn bí circir. 5Á dū abɔkuti ŋin bi ŋáĺ ki dūu sú-mee kí pèen̄ Aarɔn, an dàkà yii poon bɔkutil nì dibɔkutifɔkɔl nì eefoodi nì kilɔbiki, ní kí dū eefoodi dambalau kí cúú. 6Á dū ŋŋaabu kí fìn̄ u-yil ní kí dū tikpáakaal tin dàkà yii bi dū-u ki sú-mee kí cúú ŋŋaabuee. 7Míǹ boonee ní á yòon̄ ŋkpam min bi cáa sìtī unil yilpu kí dū-u kí sú-mee kí sìtī u-yil pu. 8A yaa ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee ní á yàntī u-jipɔmbi ń sútiń kí pìl̄-si, ní á dū bi-bɔkutiŋ poon yaŋ kí pèen̄-bi. 9Á dū bi-dambalab kí gbìn̄-bi, ní kí dū bi-fuulimmu kí cíkiń-bi. Míǹ boonee á dū Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi kí kàan̄ bí nīn bí m-tundin.
Kí yòon̄ ŋyunti gbantee, bi kpántì m-saraaŋaliibi dee kí nīn cá jaanjaan.
10«Á cáań dinajapɔmbilee dikpafindi tantiu nyɔkɔpu, ní Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi ń dū bi-ŋalii kí páań di-yil pu. 11Á làntì dinajapɔmbilee man nimbiin niin circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu. 12Á lēē fatiku kí dū a-ŋambiki kí sēē kí jòotì nsaraafan yiŋyi naatil pu. Boonee ní á kpáatí fatiku un kíǹee kí pɔ̀l̄ nsaraafan taapu. 13Á yòon̄ ŋkpam min kɔkɔ bīī ina puee nì mpɔɔlam nì aceebil liitil nì ŋkpam min bīī ŋi-puee kí cáá wà ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu. 14An di làá nīn sá bisaraaŋaliibi kpitii pɔ̄tam saraau. Ama á yòon̄ dinajapɔmbilee nanti nì di-gbaŋŋu nì di-binti kɔkɔ kí cáá wà ŋŋmi dinaapaal kpaanceetiŋu.
15«Boonee ní á cáań upijapeekaa ní Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi ń dū bi-ŋalii kí páań di-yil pu. 16Á làntì-dì, ní kí dū fatiku kí yàaǹ nsaraafan kɔkɔ pu kí màntīí tū. 17Á càkà di-nanti anaŋkún anaŋkún, kí fíntí di-nai nì di-yakaŋ kí dūú páań anaŋkúnee nì diyil pu. 18Á dū upijamɔnee kí wà ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu. An di sá saraawɔkaa un ni ŋá ki tīī-mee, saraa un sɔnsɔfiŋu sɔ̀ŋkī man ni-Dindaan pɔbilee.
19«Boonee ní á cáań upìjaliliiti, ní Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi ń dū bi-ŋalii kí páań upìjee yil pu. 20Á làntì-u kí lēē fatiku kí jōō Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi tafalam ŋŋaŋgiil yaŋ pu, nì bi-ŋambijaliŋ ŋŋaŋgiil yaŋ pu nì bi-taŋambijaliŋ ŋŋaŋgiil yaŋ pu, ní kí dū fatiku kí yàaǹ nsaraafan kɔkɔ pu kí màntīí tū. 21Á dāá lēē fatiku un bí nsaraafan puee nì ŋkpam min bi cáa sìtī binib yiliŋ pu kí dū-bi kí sú-mee, kí yàaǹ Aarɔn nì u-bɔkutiŋ pu, ní kí yàaǹ u-jipɔmbi nì bi-bɔkutiŋ pu. Mimmee a dū Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi nì bi-wampeeŋkaati ki sú-mi dee. 22Á dāá lēē upìjee kpam nì dijugbindi nì ŋkpam min bīī ina puee, nì mpɔɔlam nì aceebil nì ŋkpam min bīī ŋi-puee, nì diŋaŋgiitaal, kun puee an sá upìja un bi dūu ŋá saraa kí kàan̄ bisaraaŋaliibi bí nīn bí m-tundinee ní. 23Á lēē kpɔnɔb bin bi púĺ kaa ŋá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔ poon an kā kukabikun ki yú m-nimbiinee ubɔ, nì ŋkpɔnɔwaamu mun pu bi yɔ́kɔfì ŋkpam ki púĺ ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔ kpá poonee ubɔ, nì kalaabi bin bi dū ŋkpam ki ŋmālim̀ ki búuńee ubɔ. 24Á dū tiwan gbanti kɔkɔ kí ŋúbiǹ Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi ní kí yàntī bí dúkutí yilpu kí fíiǹ fíiǹ man ni-Dindaan nimbiin. 25Boonee, á fàtīí fōō bi-ŋaan kí dūú kūtì saraawɔkaa un pá nsaraafan puee kí wà ŋŋmi. An saraau sɔnsɔfiŋu sɔ̀ŋkī man ni-Dindaan pɔbil ní. 26Á yòon̄ upìjaliliiti un a dūu ŋá Aarɔn yil pu saraa ki dū-u ki sú-mee bindi kí dúkutí kí fíiǹ fíiǹ man ni-Dindaan nimbiin. Dijandi gbantee, á yòon̄, a-yati dee.
27«Á dū upìja un a dūu ŋá saraa ki kāaǹ Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi disaraaŋal tundinee bindi din a fíiǹ fíiǹee nì u-ŋaŋgiitaal din a lēēyee kí sú man ni-Dindaan. 28Án sá mara ní m yóoǹ ki tīī Isirayeel yab kí nīn pée cáa cá jaanjaan, yii mpèé saraabi bin bi làá nīn ŋáań ki tìì-mee, bí nīn lèekī tinan gbanti míǹ ki tìì Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi.
29«Aarɔn kúm boonee, u-saraaŋabɔkutiŋ làá nīn sá ki tīī u-jipɔmbi ní. Bí dāá pèen̄-ŋi ŋwiin ŋun bi làá sìtī bi-yil pu ŋkpam kí dū-bi kí sú-mi bí kíĺ disaraaŋal tundee. 30U-jipɔmbi kansikin un làá fōō u-yil kí kpántí usaraaŋakpil kí kɔ́ dikpafindi tantiun kí lēē saraa <circir laŋkee> ń dāá pèen̄ asaraaŋabɔkuti gbanti iwiin iluli.
31«Á dū upìjaliliiti un bi dūu ŋá saraa ki kāaǹ usaraaŋakpil ú nīn bí m-tundinee nanti kí tɔ́kɔń mpaan ŋun bi lēē ŋu sá circiree. 32Ní Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi ń ŋmɔ́ tinan gbanti nì kpɔnɔb bin kā kukabikunee dikpafindi tantiu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu. 33Bí ŋmɔ́ tin ní bi dūu ŋá saraa bí ká bi-kpitii pɔ̄tam kí dū-bi kí sú-mi bí kíĺ disaraaŋal tundee. Unifantanti ń taa jī saraabi jinti gbanti, di sá yii tì sá circir ní. 34Saraa un bi ŋá ki kāaǹ-bi bisaraaŋaliibee nanti nì kpɔnɔb yaa kíǹ ní kutaa wúntèe, bí dūú wà ŋŋmi. Bí taa jī tijin gbanti, di sá yii tì sá circir ní.
35«Á ŋá Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi kí nóó nì m nín tīī-si mara puee deedee. Á dū iwiin iluli kí ŋá akoobil ŋin sá á ŋá-bi ní bí nín kpántí bisaraaŋakpilibee.
36«Ŋwiin kamaayee, á dū unaja kí ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau, ní kí ŋá saraa nsaraafan pu kí ŋá-ŋu circir. Boonee á dū ŋkpam kí sìtī ŋu-pu kí dū-ŋu kí sú-mi. 37Á dū iwiin iluli ní kí ŋá akoobil gbanti mun. Míǹ boonee nsaraafan kpántì circir páaa dee ní tin kamaa yaa pée gbēē-ŋuee kpántì circir wanti.»
Ŋwiin kamaa saraawɔkaabi
38«Saraabi bin a làá bɔ́ntí kí páań nsaraafan puee sèé. Ŋwiin kamaayee, á dū apibil ali ŋin cáá dibindi dibee kí ŋá saraa nsaraafan pu. 39Á dū diba kí ŋá saraa kutaafaau, ní kí dū din kíǹee kí ŋá saraa kujoou. 40Á dū ŋyim kiiloobi bita kí dū ɔliifi kpam min wāĺ kílkilee liitiri ubɔ nì dijandi kí búuń ŋyimee kí dūú kūtì dipibipeepeekaalee pu kí ŋá saraa. Á dū ndamam liitiri ubɔ nì dijandi mun kí fá saraapeekaayee ŋátam poon. 41Saraaliliitee, kujoou ní a làá ŋá úǹ kí tīī-mi. Tiwan tin kɔkɔ a kútì ki ŋá saraapeepeekaayee, tíǹ tibaantiil ní a làá tí dūú kūtì kí ŋá saraaliliiti mun. An di sá saraawɔkaa un sɔnsɔfiŋu sɔ̀ŋkī m-pɔbilee. 42Saraawɔkaa gbanti ní ni làá nīn pée ŋáań kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaan circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu man ni-Dindaan nimbiin. Niin ní man nì ni làá nīn kpáfí ní ḿ nīn sòoǹ nì si.
43«Man nì Isirayeel yab làá kpāfì mpaan gbanti pu, ní m-nyooti ń dāá ŋá mpaan gbanti circir. 44M làá dāá ŋá dikpafindi tantiu nì nsaraafan circir, ní kí ŋá Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi circir bí nīn bí m-saraaŋatundin. 45M làá dāá nīn kóò Isirayeel yab kansikin, ní kí nīn sá bi-Nimbɔtiu. 46Bi làá dāá béé yii man bi-Dindaan di sá bi-Nimbɔtiu un di nyántìń-bi Eejipiti tiŋkin kí nīn kóò bi-kansikinee.
«Man di sá bi-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu.»

english_text:
The Altar for Burning Incense
(Exodus 37.25-28)
The Lord said to Moses:
1Build an altar of acacia wood where you can burn incense. 2Make it 45 centimeters square and 90 centimeters high, and make each of its four corners stick up like the horn of a bull. 3Cover it with pure gold and put a gold edging around it. 4Then below the edging on opposite sides attach two gold rings through which you can put the poles for carrying the altar. 5These poles are also to be made of acacia wood covered with gold.
6Put the altar in front of the inside curtain of the sacred tent. The chest with the place of mercy is kept behind that curtain, and I will talk with you there. 7-8From now on, when Aaron takes care of the lamps each morning and evening, he must burn sweet-smelling incense to me on the altar. 9Burn only the proper incense on the altar and never use it for grain sacrifices or animal sacrifices or drink offerings. 10 Once a year Aaron must purify the altar by smearing on its four corners the blood of an animal sacrificed for sin, and this practice must always be followed. The altar is sacred because it is dedicated to me.
The Money for the Sacred Tent
11The Lord said to Moses:
12Find out how many grown men there are in Israel and require each of them to pay me to keep him safe from danger while you are counting them. 13-15 Each man over 19, whether rich or poor, must pay me the same amount of money, weighed according to the official standards. 16This money is to be used for the upkeep of the sacred tent, and because of it, I will never forget my people.
The Large Bronze Bowl
(Exodus 38.8)
17The Lord said to Moses:
18-21 Make a large bronze bowl and a bronze stand for it. Then put them between the altar for sacrifice and the sacred tent, so the priests can wash their hands and feet before entering the tent or offering a sacrifice on the altar. Each priest in every generation must wash himself in this way, or else he will die right there.
The Oil for Dedication and Ordination
(Exodus 37.29)
22 The Lord said to Moses:
23-25Mix four liters of olive oil with the following costly spices: six kilograms of myrrh, three kilograms of cinnamon, three kilograms of cane, and six kilograms of cassia. Measure these according to the official standards. Then use this sacred mixture 26for dedicating the tent and chest, 27the table with its equipment, the lampstand with its equipment, the incense altar with all its utensils, 28the altar for sacrifices, and the large bowl with its stand. 29By dedicating them in this way, you will make them so holy that anyone who even touches them will become holy.
30When you ordain Aaron and his sons as my priests, sprinkle them with some of this oil, 31and say to the people of Israel: “This oil must always be used in the ordination service of a priest. It is holy because it is dedicated to the Lord. 32So treat it as holy! Don't ever use it for everyday purposes or mix any for yourselves. 33If you do, you will no longer belong to the Lord's people.”
The Sweet-Smelling Incense
34-35Mix equal amounts of the costly spices stacte, onycha, galbanum, and pure frankincense, then add salt to make the mixture pure and holy. 36Pound some of it into powder and sprinkle it in front of the sacred chest, where I meet with you. Be sure to treat this incense as something very holy. 37It is truly holy because it is dedicated to me, so don't ever make any for yourselves. 38If you ever make any of it to use as perfume, you will no longer belong to my people.
translation_text:
Talaalutuukaa saraafaŋŋu
1«Boonee á dū akasiya dɔŋu kí kpáá nsaraafan ŋun pu bi làá nīn tùutī talaalubee. 2Á kpáá-ŋu ŋu-jaŋŋi naatil ń nīn ŋmà, dijandi kamaa ń nīn cáá dimeetajandi ní ŋfɔkɔn ń nīn sá meeta ubɔ. Nsaraafan nì ŋu-yiŋyi ń nīn sá mmɔm. 3Á dāá dū sindaariyamɔnti kí nyùntī ŋu-yilpu nì ŋu-boon kí màntīí tū nì ŋu-yiŋyi, ní kí dū sindaariya kí kpākam̀-ŋu kí màntīí tū. 4Á mɔ́ɔ́ sindaariya bɔmbiliŋ ali kí bā bi nín kpákám̀ nsaraafan taapu puee ajan liitil pu, bí nīn cáá ikpandɔ ki bōotí ki yòontí-ŋu. 5Á dū akasiya dɔŋu kí kpítí ikpandɔee ní kí dū sindaariya kí nyùntī-i. 6Á dū nsaraafan gbanti kí yóoń ŋŋaasakaŋkaa ŋun lìkī Dipoondi dakaau nì u-bìilee nimbiin, laakin man nì si làá nīn kpáfée. 7Kutaafaau kamaa Aarɔn yaa kɔ́ kí ŋāŋkì fitilabee, ú péé péé kí tūū talaalub nsaraafan gbanti pu kí wàatī. 8Kujoou kamaa u yaa làá tí tūū fitilabee ú tí ŋá míǹ. Ní nīn pée tùutī talaalub man ni-Dindaan nimbiin míǹ kí nīn pée cáa cá jaanjaan. 9Ní taa tūū talaalu ubɔ fám nsaraafan gbanti pu. Ní taa ŋá saraawɔkaa ŋu-puɔɔɔ, kí taa ŋá tijimpin saraau ŋu-puɔɔɔ, kí taa fá ndamam ŋu-pu. 10Dibindi kamaayee, Aarɔn ń dū kuwaŋkuluu kun u dūu ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam wiŋkpaaŋŋu saraauee fatikuu kí fá nsaraafan yiŋyi pu kí ŋá-i circir. Kí nīn pée cáa cá jaanjaanee, ní nīn ŋáań ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau ki ŋáań nsaraafan circir diba dibindi kamaa poon. Nsaraafan gbanti máaǹ kí nīn sá circir páaa wanti tin ni dūu sú man ni-Dindaanee ní.»
Circir kɔŋkooŋŋu lampoou
11Ti-Dindaan gíti bí Mooyiisi yii: 12«A yaa làá dāá kàaǹ Isirayeel yabee, báà ŋma ń dāá pà kunimbiŋmiiu kubɔ kí dā u-maŋfal, mimmee dikàandi kaa làá dāá cáań-ni mbusu ubɔ. 13Unil un kamaa bi yaa kàan̄ee ń dāá pà bi nín ŋmàntī animbil circir kɔŋkooŋŋun puee dijandi. An nimbiliŋee dāa sá bí dūú ŋá man ní saraa. 14Bininjab bin kɔkɔ bi yaa láa kàan̄ kí yòon̄ abin mmuŋku kí nīn cée ń dāá pà animbil gbanti kí tīī man ni-Dindaan. 15Bigaajab ń taa tīī án páań, bisoodambi mun ń taa tīī ŋgim, ubɔ ń taa nín̄ cáá dipɔndi. Báà ŋma ń pà ti-Dindaan saraau pɔndi kí fīī u-maŋfal. 16A yaa láa fōō Isirayeel yab ŋaan animbil gbantee, á nīn cáa kpèé circir kɔŋkooŋŋu. Án di làá yàntī ḿ nīn téetí Isirayeel yab pu ki bìintí bi-pu.»
Kusampeeu kun poon bi ŋáań nnyim ki fíntée
17Boonee ní ti-Dindaan gíti tí bí Mooyiisi yii: 18«Á dāá dū tasa kúti kí mɔ́ɔ́ kusampeeu kun poon bi làá nīn ŋáań nnyim bisaraaŋaliibi fíntí bi-bee, nì kun pu ku tɔ́kɔ́ee. Á dāá dū-ku kí yóoń circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nì nsaraafan kansikin, kí lúń nnyim kí gbéeǹ. 19Nnyim gbanti ní Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi làá dāá nīn jòotī ki fíntí bi-ŋalii nì bi-taaŋi. 20Kí wàatī bí kɔ́ dikpafindi tantiu poonee, bí fíntí bi-ba ní kí taa kpú. Ŋyunti ŋun bi yaa làá sútí kí pìl̄ nsaraafan kí ŋá saraawɔkaa kí tīī-mee, 21bí fíntí bi-ŋalii nì bi-taaŋi ní kí taa kpú. An sá mara ní m yóoǹ Aarɔn nì u-maaliŋun yab kí nīn pée cáa cá jaanjaan.»
Ŋkpam min bi sìtī unil yil puee
22Ti-Dindaan tí bí Mooyiisi yii: 23«Á nyàab̀ bitalaalumɔntiibi nee: miiri un bí cúlculee kiiloobi biŋmoo, nì siinamoom un sɔ́fèe kiiloobi bili nì dijandi, nì kanneel un sɔ́fèe kiiloobi bili nì dijandi, 24nì kaasi kiiloobi biŋmoo kí nóó nì circir kɔŋkooŋŋu ŋmàntitam. Nyàab̀ ɔliifi kpam liitirib biluu. 25Á dūú ŋmàlim̀ kí ŋá ŋkpam min sɔ́fèe kii utalaaluŋal nín ŋáań puee ní bí nīn cáa sìtī binib yiliŋ pu kí dū-bi kí sú man Unimbɔti. 26Á bàtī ŋkpam gbanti kí sìtī dikpafindi tantiu nì dipoondi dakaau pu. 27Á bàtī kí sìtī teebil nì u-wanti kɔkɔ, nì fitila tɔ́kɔŋkaati nì ti-wanti kɔkɔ, nì nsaraafan ŋun pu bi tùutī talaalubee pu. 28Á tí bàtī kí sìtī nsaraafan ŋun pu bi ŋáań bisaraawɔkaabee nì tin kɔkɔ bi cáa tūǹ ŋu-pu ditundee, nì kusampeeu nì kun pu ku tɔ́kɔ́ee pu. 29Á dū tiwan gbanti kɔkɔ kí sú-mi ní tí kpántí circir páaa wanti, ní tin kamaa yaa pée gbēē-tèe ń kpántí circir wanti. 30Á dāá bàtī ŋkpam gbanti kí sìtī Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi yil pu kí dū-bi kí sú-mi bí nīn bí m-tundin.
31«Á dāá tùkù Isirayeel yab yii: <Ŋkpam nee di sá min bi làá nīn cáa sìtī binib yiliŋ pu kí dū-bi kí sú-mee. Man baba tundi ní ni làá nīn cáá-mì ki ŋáań kí nīn pée cáa cá jaanjaan. 32Ubɔ ń taa dū ŋkpam gbanti kí ŋmìtī u-wunti. Míǹ ní ubɔ ń taa dū talaalub kí ŋmàlim̀ kí ŋá ŋkpam gbanti juti. Mi sá circir kpam ní, ni mun ń béé yii mi lafun sá circir kpam. 33Un kamaa di yaa ŋá ŋkpam gbanti juti, ní ki dū-mì ki sītì unifantanti ubɔ puee, bí nyāntí-u m-nibul kansikin.>»
Bi nín máaǹ kí bɔ́ntí talaalutuukaa puee
34Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Nyàab̀ tin kɔkɔ pée sɔ́fèe, an dàkà yii siitakiti nì ooniikisi nì galbanum nì talaalutuukaa umɔnti, an nì tin béeyee ń nīn ŋmà, á dūú kūtì. 35Á dū ŋyaam kí ŋmàlim̀ kí ŋá talaalumɔnti kii utalaaluŋal nín ŋáań puee, án nīn bí circir. 36Á lēē dijandi diba kí ŋá talaalu un sá ŋyimee kí dūú yóoń circir kɔŋkooŋŋun, dipoondi dakaau nimbiin, laakin man nì si làá nīn kpáfée. Talaalu gbanti ń nīn sá ni-cee circir wanti. 37Ubɔ ń taa dū tin bi dūu ŋmālim̀ ki ŋá talaalu nee ki mun ń ŋmàlim̀ míǹ kí ŋá talaalu ubɔ kí nīn cáa ŋáań tin úǹ u-ba lèe. Ama án nīn sá circir wanti tin sá ti-Dindaan baba wantee. 38Un di yaa ŋá talaalu gbanti kí nīn tíkì u-sɔnsɔfiŋuee, bí nyāntí udaan m-nibul kansikin.»

english_text:
The Lord Chooses Bezalel and Oholiab
(Exodus 35.30—36.1)
1The Lord said to Moses:
2I have chosen Bezalel from the Judah tribe to make the sacred tent and its furnishings. 3-5Not only have I filled him with my Spirit, but I have given him wisdom and made him a skilled craftsman who can create objects of art with gold, silver, bronze, precious stones, and wood. 6I have appointed Oholiab from the tribe of Dan to work with him, and I have also given skills to those who will help them make everything exactly as I have commanded you: 7-11the sacred tent with its furnishings, the sacred chest with its place of mercy, the table with all that is on it, the lamp with its equipment, the incense altar, the altar for sacrifices with its equipment, the bronze bowl with its stand, the beautiful priestly clothes for Aaron and his sons, the oil for dedication and ordination services, and the sweet-smelling incense for the holy place.
Laws for the Sabbath
12-13Moses told the Israelites that the Lord had said:
The Sabbath belongs to me. Now I command you and your descendants to always obey the laws of the Sabbath. By doing this, you will know that I have chosen you as my own. 14-15 Keep the Sabbath holy. You have six days to do your work, but the Sabbath is mine, and it must remain a day of rest. If you work on the Sabbath, you will no longer be part of my people, and you will be put to death.
16Every generation of Israelites must respect the Sabbath. 17 This day will always serve as a reminder, both to me and to the Israelites, that I made the heavens and the earth in six days, then on the seventh day I rested and relaxed.
18When God had finished speaking to Moses on Mount Sinai, he gave him the two flat stones on which he had written all his laws with his own hand.
translation_text:
Circir kɔŋkooŋŋu tɔntɔnliibi
1Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: 2«Kpèè, m lēē Uurii jipɔɔn Beesaleel, Uur un sá Juuda naakookunee naantiiu. 3M dū m-Fam ki ŋá u-ni tikpil ki yāntì ú nīn cáá iciin, ki yáb̀ ditundi poon, kí nīn cáá dinyil ní kí nīn cáá ilandɔkɔ kí ŋmā kí tɔ̄ atuun nín bí pu aba abee kɔkɔ. 4Ú nīn cáá ilandɔkɔ kí ŋmā kí dū sindaariya nì animbil kúti nì tasa kúti kí tɔ̄ atuun. 5Ú ŋmā kí kpítí ataŋkpanyaan bí nīn cáa nākantí tiwan pu, ní kí kpítí idɔ. U làá nīn sá unil un ŋūǹ ki ŋáań tikɔkɔ mmɔntiiminee ní. 6M dū Ayiisamaaki un sá Daani naakookunee jipɔɔn Ooliyaab ki ŋàl̄-u ú nīn tútúǹ-u. Míǹ mbaantiim ní m tīī bitɔntɔnliibi biba mun ŋŋmam bí ŋmā kí ŋá tin kɔkɔ m làá tùkù-ni ní ŋée, an dàkà yii: 7Dikpafindi tantiu nì Dipoondi dakaau nì u-bìil nì circir kɔŋkooŋŋu wanti kɔkɔ, 8nì teebil nì u-wanti nì fitilab tɔ́kɔŋkaati tin sá sindaariyamɔntee nì ti-wanti kɔkɔ, nì nsaraafan ŋun pu bi tùutī talaaluee, 9nì nsaraafan ŋun pu bi ŋáań saraawɔkaayee nì ŋu-tɔntɔŋwanti kɔkɔ, nì kusampeeu nì tin pu ku tɔ́kɔ́ee, 10nì bisaraaŋaliibi wampeeŋkaati nì usaraaŋakpil Aarɔn circir wampeeŋkaati nì u-jipɔmbi mun yati tin bi làá nīn pèentí ki ŋáań disaraaŋal tundee, 11nì ŋkpam min bi cáa sìtī binib yiliŋ pu kí dū-bi kí sú Unimbɔtee, nì talaalutuukaa un bi tùutī circir kɔŋkooŋŋunee. Bitɔntɔnliibi ń ŋá kii m nín tīī-si mara yii bí ŋá puee ní deedee.»
Ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa bɔti
12Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi 13ń tùkù Isirayeel yab yii: «Ní nīn tɔ́ ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa tiŋan. Di sá yii ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa sá kudaaŋŋu kubɔ ní man nì ni kansikin kí nīn pée cáa cá jaanjaan. Ŋu dàkà yii man ni-Dindaan di yāntì ni bí circir. 14An puee ní nīn tɔ́ ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa, ŋú nīn sá circir wiiŋŋu ki tīī-ni. Un di yaa kpēē-ŋu fám ki túń ditundi ŋwiin gbantee, bí kpɔ̀-u. Tiŋman un di yaa túń ditundi ŋwiin gbantee, bí nyāntí-u m-nibul kansikin. 15Ní dū iwiin iluu kí tɔ̄ atuun, winluli dalee, ní dūú ŋùŋfì. Ŋúǹ sá ŋwiin ŋun ni dūu sú man ni-Dindaanee ní. Un kamaa di yaa túń ditundi ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dalee, bí kpɔ̀-u. 16Isirayeel yab ń nīn ŋúb́ ŋwiin gbanti kí nīn pée cáa cá jaanjaan. Di sá yii an sá tibɔti tin bóob́ ki yóoǹ án nīn bí ki cá jaanjaanee ní. 17Ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa làá nīn sá kudaaŋŋu ní man nì Isirayeel yab kansikin kí nīn pée cáa cá jaanjaan. Di sá yii m dū iwiin iluu ní ki náań yilpu nì taapu, ní ŋwinluluútee, m kāl̀ ki ŋūŋfì.»
18Unimbɔti sòon̄ nì Mooyiisi míǹ Siinaayi jool pu ki dóòyee, ní ki dū titaŋkpapilindi tili tin pu u dū u-ŋambiki ki ŋmàn̄ dipoondi marab ki nákáǹee ki tīī-u.

english_text:
The People Make an Idol To Worship
(Deuteronomy 9.6-29)
1 After the people saw that Moses had been on the mountain for a long time, they went to Aaron and said, “Make us an image of a god who will lead and protect us. Moses brought us out of Egypt, but nobody knows what has happened to him.”
2Aaron told them, “Bring me the gold earrings that your wives and sons and daughters are wearing.” 3Everybody took off their earrings and brought them to Aaron, 4 then he melted them and made an idol in the shape of a young bull.
All the people said to one another, “This is the god who brought us out of Egypt!”
5When Aaron saw what was happening, he built an altar in front of the idol and said, “Tomorrow we will celebrate in honor of the Lord.” 6 The people got up early the next morning and killed some animals to be used for sacrifices and others to be eaten. Then everyone ate and drank so much that they began to carry on like wild people.
7The Lord said to Moses:
Hurry back down! Those people you led out of Egypt are acting like fools. 8They have already stopped obeying me and have made themselves an idol in the shape of a young bull. They have bowed down to it, offered sacrifices, and said that it is the god who brought them out of Egypt. 9Moses, I have seen how stubborn these people are, 10and I'm angry enough to destroy them, so don't try to stop me. But I will make your descendants into a great nation.
11 Moses tried to get the Lord God to change his mind:
Our Lord, you used your mighty power to bring these people out of Egypt. Now don't become angry and destroy them. 12If you do, the Egyptians will say that you brought your people out here into the mountains just to get rid of them. Please don't be angry with your people. Don't destroy them!
13 Remember the solemn promise you made to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. You promised that someday they would have as many descendants as there are stars in the sky and that you would give them land.
14So even though the Lord had threatened to destroy the people, he changed his mind and let them live.
15-16Moses went back down the mountain with the two flat stones on which God had written all of his laws with his own hand, using both sides of the stones.
17When Joshua heard the noisy shouts of the people, he said to Moses, “A battle must be going on down in the camp.”
18But Moses replied, “It doesn't sound like they are shouting because they have won or lost a battle. It sounds more like a wild party!”
19As Moses got closer to the camp, he saw the idol, and he also saw the people dancing around. This made him so angry that he threw down the stones and broke them to pieces at the foot of the mountain. 20He melted the idol the people had made, and he ground it into powder. He scattered it in their water and made them drink it. 21Moses asked Aaron, “What did these people do to harm you? Why did you make them sin in this terrible way?”
22Aaron answered:
Don't be angry with me. You know as well as I do that they are determined to do evil. 23They even told me, “That man Moses led us out of Egypt, but now we don't know what has happened to him. Make us a god to lead us.” 24Then I asked them to bring me their gold earrings. They took them off and gave them to me. I threw the gold into a fire, and out came this bull.
25Moses knew that the people were out of control and that it was Aaron's fault. And now they had made fools of themselves in front of their enemies. 26So Moses stood at the gate of the camp and shouted, “Everyone who is on the Lord's side come over here!”
Then the men of the Levi tribe gathered around Moses, 27and he said to them, “The Lord God of Israel commands you to strap on your swords and go through the camp, killing your relatives, your friends, and your neighbors.”
28The men of the Levi tribe followed his orders, and that day they killed about 3,000 men. 29Moses said to them, “You obeyed the Lord and did what was right, and so you will serve as his priests for the people of Israel. It was hard for you to kill your own sons and brothers, but the Lord has blessed you and made you his priests today.”
30The next day Moses told the people, “This is a terrible thing you have done. But I will go back to the Lord to see if I can do something to keep this sin from being held against you.”
31Moses returned to the Lord and said, “The people have committed a terrible sin. They have made a gold idol to be their god. 32 But I beg you to forgive them. If you don't, please wipe my name out of your book.”
33The Lord replied, “I will wipe out of my book the name of everyone who has sinned against me. 34Now take my people to the place I told you about, and my angel will lead you. But when the time comes, I will punish them for this sin.”
35So the Lord punished the people of Israel with a terrible disease for talking Aaron into making the gold idol.
translation_text:
ISIRAYEEL YAB KPĪTÌ MPÈÉ ŊUN BÍ BI NÌ UNIMBƆTI KANSIKINEE (32–34)
Bi dūntì sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ dinabil
1Samaa nín ká yii Mooyiisi yúntìń dijool pu kaa bíi bàńee ní bi cūtìi kpáfì Aarɔn cee ní ki bí-u yii: «Kpèè doo, mɔ́ɔ́-ti unimbɔti ubɔ ú nīn līī ti-nyɔkɔpu, di sá taa nyí tin di yaa bāań Mooyiisi un di nyántìń-ti Eejipiti tiŋkinee.» 2Ní Aarɔn bí-bi yii: «Lēēmaan ni-nimpoobi nì ni-bisalib nì ni-jipɔmbi sindaariyabɔmbiliŋ bi-tafaliŋ pu kí cáaḿmaan-mi.»
3Dicilpu niin ní Isirayeel yab gbákal̀ bi-bɔmbiliŋ bi-tafaliŋ pu ki cáań ki tīī-u. 4Aarɔn fōō tiwan gbantee bi-ŋaanee ní ki dūntì ki dūu sītì tiwan tin bi ŋá ki nántiǹ dinabilee poon, ní an nyántì dinabil. Niinee ní samaa téeń yii: «Isirayeel yab, kpèèmaan ni-Nimbɔtiu un nyántìń-ni Eejipiti tiŋkinee!» 5Aarɔn ká mimmee ní ki máń nsaraafan dinabilee nimbiin ní ki bí yii: «Foolee ti làá fu jī ti-Dindaan jiŋaaliu.» 6Kutaa wúntì kutaafaau pɔ̀lpɔlee ní samaa ŋá bisaraawɔkaabi nì mpèé saraabi. Boonee ní bi kāl̀ ki jíń ki nyùn̄. Bi dóòyee ní ki dūu gùl̄ agbiil pu. 7Niinee ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Sìntī malaa, di sá a-nibul din a nyántìń Eejipiti tiŋkinee bíi ŋáań ikpitikpaan. 8Bi pūtì kpáàa dū nsan ŋun m dàkā-bee ki fá. Bi dūntì tikúti ki mɔ́ɔ́ dinabil, ki gbāaǹ di-nimbiin, ki ŋá-dì saraabi ki lī yii: <Isirayeel yab, kpèèmaan ni-Nimbɔtiu un nyántìń-ni Eejipiti tiŋkinee!» 9Ti-Dindaan gíti tùkū Mooyiisi yii: «M ká yii dinibul nee sá din gáatèe ní. 10Kɔŋkɔnnee, yàntī ḿ fōō bi-pu mbiim kí kúntí-bi. Boonee m làá dī sii pu kí náań ditimbuŋkpaandi.» 11Ama ní Mooyiisi gbāam̀ ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti ú jī kimɔtii ní ki bí yii: «Ti-Dindaan, ba pu ní a fōō dinibul din a nyántìń Eejipiti tiŋkin nì a-pɔŋkpaaŋŋu nì a-kpabilee pu mbiim míǹ? 12A yaa ŋá mimmee Eejipiti yab làá lì yii: <Unimbɔti là kí cáá-bi kí tɔ̄ mbusu poonee pu ní u nyántì-bi ti-tiŋkin. U là kí cáá-bi kí cūnnì ntimu mun bí ajoon puee kí sàaǹ-bi kí kúntí-bi kitiŋ pu ní.> An puee m-Dindaan, sɔ̀ŋkì a-pɔbil, kí gíiǹ mbusu un a bàà làá dūú tɔ̄ a-nibul puee kí yà. 13Téetí Abraam nì Isaaki nì Jaakɔb pu, a-tɔntɔnliibi bin a nìn pūtì ki pōoǹ-bi yii: <M làá bùtī ni-maaliŋun yab bí nīn wīikí kii iŋmalbijaa in bí kutagbɔŋu puee. M làá dū kitiŋ kin m pōoǹ-bee kí tīī-bi bí nīn kíǹ ki yì kí nīn pée cáa cá jaanjaan.>» 14Niinee ti-Dindaan nín bàà bɔ́ntì kí dū mbusu un kí tɔ̄-bee ní u yāntì kaa ti ŋá míǹ.
15Mooyiisi nìn yíkìń dijool pu ki nín kpákatiń ki ŋúbiń titaŋkpapilindi tili u-ŋaan ajan liitil pu bi ŋmàn̄ dipoondi marab. 16Unimbɔti u-ba di nìn kpítì titaŋkpapilindi gbanti. Úǹ u-ba di nìn tí ŋmàn̄ ti-pu kii kigaai ní bi dūu cáká ki ŋmàn̄ee. 17Joosuwa nín gbìl̄ samaa kuŋkuuntii puee ní u bí Mooyiisi yii: «Pīlifì, ijanjakuŋkuunti di tùm̀ ti-naapaal puee.» 18Ní Mooyiisi bí-u yii: «Aayee, doo kaa sá dijajil kuŋkuuntii, kaa tí sá bin bi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹee yaliŋkii. Ilan pu ní man gbìl̀ nee.»
19Bi tóob́ dinaapaalee ní Mooyiisi ká dinabil yú ní samaa bí ki ŋōō ní u fōō diŋuul ŋkpitim pu. U nìn dū titaŋkpapilindi tin u ŋúb́ u-ŋaanee ki lúkú, ní ki gbáń ki wīī-tì dijool taapu niin. 20Ní u cūtìi yōoǹ dinabil din samaa mɔ́ɔ́yee ki tɔ́ ŋŋmin ní an wùn̄. U nìn nàn̄-dì dúsi dusi, ki dūu sītì nnyimin ní ki yāntì Isirayeel yab nyùn̄. 21Ní Mooyiisi bālifì Aarɔn yii: «Ba ní dinibul nee ŋá-si ní a téé-dì ki tɔ́ ikpitikpaan in bí nee poon míǹ?» 22Ní Aarɔn kíí Mooyiisi yii: «M-dindaan, taa fōō m-pu diŋuul. Sii a-ba nyí yii dinibul nee kaa pée pɔ̄ɔ̄ tin kaa ŋān̄ee diŋál. 23Bi bí-mi yii: <Mɔ́ɔ́-ti unimbɔti ubɔ ú lìntī ti-nyɔkɔpu, di sá yii Mooyiisi uninja un di nyántìń-ti Eejipiti tiŋkinee, taa nyí tin di yaa bāań-uee.> 24Niinee ní m bālifì-bi yii: <Ŋma di cáá sindaariya?> Dicilpu niin ní bi túutì abɔmbil bi-tafaliŋ pu ki cáań ki tīī-mi, ní m dūu tɔ́ ŋŋmin ní dinabil nee nyánní.»
Ditafadaaldi
25Mooyiisi ká yii fìkil fikil kɔ́ samaa ní Aarɔn yāntì bi ŋá bi nín là puee, ki dū bi-ba ki tīī binannanliibi ń bèel̀. 26Niinee ní Mooyiisi cūtìi yúl̀ dinaapaal punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu ní ki téeń yii: «Bin kɔkɔ bí ti-Dindaan jandee ń dāan̄ man cee!» Ní Leefii naakookun yab kɔkɔ dɔ́miń ki yúl̀ u-cee ki māntìi tú-u. 27Ní u bí-bi yii: «Kpèèmaan, ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín lī puee sèé yii: <Báà ŋma ń dū u-tàataajiki kí gbìn̄, kí yìiǹ dinaapaal jaŋŋi kɔkɔ poon kí kpɔ̀ u-nabiki nì u-bɔɔ nì u-kɔŋkɔnnaatɔ.>»
28Leefii yab nìn ŋá kii Mooyiisi nín nìn lī puee, di sá yaadal wiiŋŋuee, bi nìn kūū binib kutukub bita. 29Niinee ní Mooyiisi bí Leefii yab yii: «Díǹ nee ni dū ni-ba ki sú ki túń ni-Dindaan tundi, kun puee naa yíì ki ŋúń ki kūū ni-jipɔmbi nì ni-nabiyaamu. An puee ti-Dindaan ń bìin̄ ni-pu díǹ.»
Mooyiisi gbāam̀ Unimbɔti Isirayeel yab pu
30Kutaa wúntèe ní Mooyiisi bí samaa yii: «Ikpitikpaan ní ni baasii ŋá. Kɔŋkɔnnee m làá fàtīí jɔ̄m̀ dijool pu ti-Dindaan cee, an yaa yíì u làá fōō-mi kí dū ni-kpitii kí pɔ̄-ni.»
31Niinee Mooyiisi fātìi nín gítí ti-Dindaan cee, ní ki bí-u yii: «Àaa ti-Dindaan, a-nibul ŋá ikpitikpaŋkpaan ní, bi dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ unimbɔti. 32Ama m gbāam̀-si, dū bi-kpitii kí pɔ̄-bi. An yaa kaa ŋá mimmee, á kpìtī man yindi dimaŋfal gbɔŋku kun a ŋmàn̄ee poon.» 33Ní ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Un yīntiǹ-mee yindi ní m làá kpìtī m-gbɔŋku poon. 34Too kɔŋkɔnnee, nín̄ cá kí yòon̄ dinibul kí cùnnì laakin m bí á cáá-bi kí cùnnèe. M làá yàntī m-tuuŋŋu ń nīn līī a-nyɔkɔpu. Ama dalba m làá dāá dáaĺ bi-tafal bi-kpitii gbanti pu.» 35Ti-Dindaan dáaĺ dinibul tafal Aarɔn nín nìn mɔ́ɔ́-bi dinabil diŋyee pu.

english_text:
The Lord Tells Israel To Leave Mount Sinai
1 The Lord said to Moses:
You led the people of Israel out of Egypt. Now get ready to lead them to the land I promised their ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. 2-3It is a land rich with milk and honey, and I will send an angel to force out those people who live there—the Canaanites, the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. But I will not go with my people. They are so rebellious that I would destroy them before they get there.
4-5Even before the Lord said these harsh things, he had told Moses, “These people really are rebellious, and I would kill them at once, if I went with them. But tell them to take off their fancy jewelry, then I'll decide what to do with them.” So the people started mourning, 6and after leaving Mount Sinai, they stopped wearing fancy jewelry.
The Lord Is with His People
7Moses used to set up a tent far from camp. He called it the “meeting tent,” and whoever needed some message from the Lord would go there. 8Each time Moses went out to this tent, everyone would stand at the entrance to their own tents and watch him enter. 9-11Then they would bow down because a thick cloud would come down in front of the tent, and the Lord would speak to Moses face to face, just like a friend. Afterwards, Moses would return to camp, but his young assistant Joshua would stay at the tent.
The Lord Promises To Be with His People
12Moses said to the Lord, “I know that you have told me to lead these people to the land you promised them. But you have not said who will go along to help me. You have said that you are my friend and that you are pleased with me. 13If this is true, let me know what your plans are, then I can obey and continue to please you. And don't forget that you have chosen this nation to be your own.”
14The Lord said, “I will go with you and give you peace.”
15Then Moses replied, “If you aren't going with us, please don't make us leave this place. 16But if you do go with us, everyone will know that you are pleased with your people and with me. That way, we will be different from the rest of the people on earth.”
17So the Lord told him, “I will do what you have asked, because I am your friend and I am pleased with you.”
18Then Moses said, “I pray that you will let me see you in all of your glory.”
19 The Lord answered:
All right. I am the Lord, and I show mercy and kindness to anyone I choose. I will let you see my glory and hear my holy name, 20but I won't let you see my face, because anyone who sees my face will die. 21There is a rock not far from me. Stand beside it, 22and before I pass by in all of my shining glory, I will put you in a large crack in the rock. I will cover your eyes with my hand until I have passed by. 23Then I will take my hand away, and you will see my back. You will not see my face.
translation_text:
Ti-Dindaan tīī Mooyiisi mara bí nìkī nsan
1Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Yīkì doo, sii nì dinibul din a nyántìń Eejipiti tiŋkinee, kí nīn cá kitiŋ kin m pūtì ki pōoǹ Abraam nì Isaaki nì Jaakɔb yii m làá dūú tīī bi-maaliŋun yabee. 2M làá tɔ̄ń m-tuuŋŋu ŋú lìntī ni-nyɔkɔpu kí jà Kanaan yab nì Amɔɔr yab nì Eeti yab nì Peeriisi yab nì Eefi yab nì Jeebusi yab. 3Ní cùú kɔ́ kitiŋ kin poon nnaabiim nì tisiil còol̀ee. Ama man kaa làá nóó-ni kí cù, kun puee ni sá dinibul din pɔbil gbìfèe ní. Án làá yàntī ḿ kpɔ̀ kí céetí-ni nsanni.»
4Samaa nín gbìl̄ mbusu bɔti gbantee ní bi kāl̀ kii bi ká dikpoolee, ní báà ubɔ kaa dū tiwannyaandi ki ŋá u-ba pu. 5Di sá ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi ń tùkù Isirayeel yab yii: «Ni sá dinibul din pɔbil gbìfèe ní. M yaa bí yii m làá nīn còom̄ ni-kansikin, án kaa làá gāā dikàakil ní ḿ kpɔ̀ kí céetí-ni. Míǹ puee lēēmaan tiwannyaandi ni-wunti pu ḿ kpèè min ní m làá ŋá-nee.» 6Kí yòon̄ Ooreeb jool caŋin niin ní Isirayeel yab kíĺ kaa ti dū tiwannyaandi ki ŋá bi-wunti pu.
Dikpafindi tantiu
7Isirayeel yab yaa nìn bàn̄ laakin ki gāā dinaapaalee, Mooyiisi nìn yòontí tanti ní kí cùnnì kí cóoń dinaapaal boon ndandati. Bi nìn yíì-u yii <circir kɔŋkooŋŋu>. Un yaa nìn là kí bàlifì ti-Dindaan cee tibee nìn nyēē dinaapaalin ní kí cù circir kɔŋkooŋŋun. 8Ŋyunti kamaa Mooyiisi yaa nìn yíkìi cá circir kɔŋkooŋŋunee, samaa nìn yíkí ní báà ŋma yú u-tantiu nyɔkɔpu, ní bi-nimbiliŋ cɔ́ u-pu áli ú tin kɔ́ circir kɔŋkooŋŋun. 9Ŋyunti ŋun u yaa kɔ́ee ní ditagbancancaal ń sìntīń kí dāá yūĺ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu, ní ti-Dindaan ń nīn bíi sòoǹ nì Mooyiisi. 10Isirayeel yab yaa nìn ká ditagbancancaalee sīntìń ki yúl̀ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpuee, ní bi-kɔkɔ ń tàtīí dòon̄ dicincibil bi-tantib nyɔkɔpui. 11Ti-Dindaan nìn sòoǹ nì Mooyiisi bi-nimbiiŋyi túĺ tɔb kii unil nì u-juti nín sòoǹ nì tɔb puee ní. Boonee ní Mooyiisi ń fàtīí nīn gítí dinaapaal pu, ní Nuuni jipɔɔn Joosuwa un nìn bí ki tútúǹ-uee ń gbíntí circir kɔŋkooŋŋun.
Ti-Dindaan nì Mooyiisi bíi sòoǹ
12Mooyiisi bí ti-Dindaan yii: «Kpèè, sii di bí-mi yii ḿ kpòotī dinibul nee, ama ní kaa yāntì m béè un ní a làá tɔ̄ń ú céeǹ-mee. Ama si mun di bí-mi yii: <M nyí-si tiŋan>, ní ki gíti lī yii: <A ká diyimɔɔl m-cee.> 13Míǹ puee m yaa lafun ká diyimɔɔl a-cee, á yàntī ḿ béé a-landɔkɔi nín sá puee. Mimmee m làá béé-si tiŋan ní kí páatí diyimɔɔl gbanti pu. Á nīn nyí yii ditimbundi nee sá a-nibul ní.» 14Ní Unimbɔti kíí Mooyiisi yii: «Mama m-ba di làá céeǹ-ni ní kí tīī-si diŋuŋfil.»
15Ní Mooyiisi bí-u yii: «Sii a-ba yaa kaa bí ti-cee kí céeǹ-ti, á taa lì yii tí yīkì doo kí nīn cá. 16Ba di làá dàkà yii man nì a-nibul ká diyimɔɔl a-cee? See a yaa céeǹ-ti baba di làá gàntì man nì a-nibul nì anibul ŋin kɔkɔ bí kitiŋ puee nib kansikin.» 17Ní ti-Dindaan kíí Mooyiisi yii: «M làá ŋá min a dáá bālifì-mi nee kí tīī-si, di sá a ká m-cee diyimɔɔl, ní man di baasii lēē-si.»
18Ní Mooyiisi bí yii: «M gbàam̄-si, yàntī ḿ ká a-nyooti.» 19Ní Unimbɔti bí-u yii: «M làá yàntī m-ŋanti nín sá puee kɔkɔ ń jītí a-nimbiin á ká, ní kí yíiń man ni-Dindaan yindi a-nimbiin. M sūǹ un saai m là kí sɔ̄ee saai, ní ki ŋáań tiŋan un m là kí ŋá tiŋanee. 20Ama aa ŋūǹ kí wāl̀-mi nì a-nimbiliŋ yéè kpìrrr, di sá unil kaa ŋūǹ kí wāl̀-mi ki gbíntìi bí dimaŋfalin.» 21Ti-Dindaan gíti bí yii: «Kpèè mpaan ŋubɔ bí doo ki pìl̄-mi. Tɔ́kɔń ditaŋkpakpaandi nee pu kí nīn yú. 22Ŋyunti ŋun m-nyooti yaa láa bíi jītée, ḿ dāá dū-si kí báĺ ntaŋkpalɔkɔn ní kí dū m-ŋal kí bìin̄ a-nimbiin ní kí jītí. 23Boonee ní ḿ dāá cúú m-ŋal kí bìitī ní á wāl̀ m-boon, an yaa kíǹ m-nimbiinee, ubɔ kpá kí ká-ŋu.»

english_text:
The Second Set of Commandments
(Deuteronomy 10.1-5)
1One day the Lord said to Moses, “Cut two flat stones like the first ones I made, and I will write on them the same commandments that were on the two you broke. 2Be ready tomorrow morning to come up Mount Sinai and meet me at the top. 3No one is to come with you or to be on the mountain at all. Don't even let the sheep and cattle graze at the foot of the mountain.” 4So Moses cut two flat stones like the first ones, and early the next morning he carried them to the top of Mount Sinai, just as the Lord had commanded.
5The Lord God came down in a cloud and stood beside Moses there on the mountain. God spoke his holy name, “the Lord.” 6 Then he passed in front of Moses and called out, “I am the Lord God. I am merciful and very patient with my people. I show great love, and I can be trusted. 7I keep my promises to my people forever, but I also punish anyone who sins. When people sin, I punish them and their children, and also their grandchildren and great-grandchildren.”
8Moses quickly bowed down to the ground and worshiped the Lord. 9He prayed, “Lord, if you really are pleased with me, I pray that you will go with us. It is true that these people are sinful and rebellious, but forgive our sin and let us be your people.”
A Promise and Its Demands
(Exodus 23.14-19; Deuteronomy 7.1-5; 16.1-17)
10The Lord said:
I promise to perform miracles for you that have never been seen anywhere on earth. Neighboring nations will stand in fear and know that I was the one who did these marvelous things. 11I will force out the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, but you must do what I command you today. 12Don't make treaties with any of those people. If you do, it will be like falling into a trap. 13 Instead, you must destroy their altars and tear down the sacred poles they use in the worship of the goddess Asherah. 14I demand your complete loyalty—you must not worship any other god! 15Don't make treaties with the people there, or you will soon find yourselves worshiping their gods and taking part in their sacrificial meals. 16Your men will even marry their women and be influenced to worship their gods.
17 Don't make metal images of gods.
18 Don't fail to observe the Festival of Thin Bread in the month of Abib. Obey me and eat bread without yeast for seven days during Abib, because that is the month you left Egypt.
19 The first-born males of your families and of your flocks and herds belong to me.
20 You can save the life of a first-born donkey by sacrificing a lamb; if you don't, you must break the donkey's neck. You must save every first-born son.
Bring an offering every time you come to worship.
21 Work for six days and rest on the seventh day, even during the seasons for plowing and harvesting. 22 Celebrate the Harvest Festival each spring when you start harvesting your wheat, and celebrate the Festival of Shelters each autumn when you pick your fruit.
23Your men must come to worship me three times a year, because I am the Lord God of Israel. 24As you advance, I will force the nations out of your land and enlarge your borders. Then no one will try to take your property when you come to worship me these three times each year.
25 When you sacrifice an animal on the altar, don't offer bread made with yeast. And don't save any part of the Passover meal for the next day.
26 I am the Lord your God, and you must bring the first part of your harvest to the place of worship.
Don't boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
27The Lord told Moses to put these laws in writing, as part of his agreement with Israel. 28Moses stayed on the mountain with the Lord for 40 days and nights, without eating or drinking. And he wrote down the Ten Commandments, the most important part of God's agreement with his people.
Moses Comes Down from Mount Sinai
29 Moses came down from Mount Sinai, carrying the Ten Commandments. His face was shining brightly because the Lord had been speaking to him. But Moses did not know at first that his face was shining. 30When Aaron and the others looked at Moses, they saw this, and they were afraid to go near him. 31Moses called out for Aaron and the leaders to come to him, and he spoke with them. 32Then the rest of the people of Israel gathered around Moses, and he gave them the laws that the Lord had given him on Mount Sinai.
33The face of Moses kept shining, and after he had spoken with the people, he covered his face with a veil. 34Moses would always remove the veil when he went into the sacred tent to speak with the Lord. And when he came out, he would tell the people everything the Lord had told him to say. 35They could see that his face was still shining. So after he had spoken with them, he would put the veil back on and leave it on until the next time he went to speak with the Lord.
translation_text:
Marab taŋkpapilinti tipɔn bɔti
1Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Kpítí titaŋkpapilindi tili kii tipeepeekaalee, ní man ń ŋmà tipilindi gbanti pu anyɔɔbun ŋin nìn kā tipilimpeepeekaal pu a dūu lúkú ki wīīyee. 2Á bɔ́ntí kí cīití fool ntaafaabɔmbɔmee. Á fu jɔ̄m̀ Siinaayi jool yilpu kúnti kunti kí yūĺ niin kí cīití-mi. 3Báà ubɔ ń taa fu nóó-si kí jɔ̄m̀. Bí taa ká uniseen dijool gbanti pu laaba. Báà uŋoobu àá upii àá unaa ń taa fu ŋmɔ́ timool di-caŋin!»
4Ní Mooyiisi kpítì titaŋkpapilindi tili kii tipeepeekaalee. Kutaa wúntì ntaafaabɔmbɔmee ní u nín jɔ́ḿ Siinaayi jool pu, ki ŋúb́ titaŋkpapilindi tilee kii ti-Dindaan nín bí yii ú ŋá puee. 5Ti-Dindaan kpákatìń dijool pu ditagbancancaalin ki dɔ́miń ki yúl̀ ki kɔ́ĺ Mooyiisi, ní Mooyiisi yíiń u-yindi yii: «Ti-Dindaan». 6Ní ti-Dindaan dɔ́miń ki jítì Mooyiisi nimbiin ki yíiń úǹ u-ba yindi yii: «Man di sá ni-Dindaan, Unimbɔti un sá ulaŋŋaŋfiti nì tiŋandaan kaa gífí diŋuul malaa, ki cáá dineendi tikpil tikpil ki bí deedeeyee. 7M dàkà binib m-poon nín mɔ̄ puee kí tin cáá sāā anaantitɔntɔkɔ kutuku pu, ki pūǹ ikpiti nì diyìntil nì mpɔɔpɔn, ama maa tàantí unikpiti kii waa ŋá tibee. M dátí bibaatiibi tafal, ní kí dáaĺ bi-biyaamu nì bi-naantiibi tafal kí tin cáá sāā anaantitɔntɔkɔ ata kii anaa pu.»
8Dicilpu niin ní Mooyiisi gbāaǹ ki jáam̀ ti-Dindaan, 9ní ki bí yii: «M yaa lafun ká diyimɔɔl a-cee, ti-Dindaan, m gbāam̀-si, á nīn bí ti-kansikin ti-saŋkindi poon. Dinibul nee sá din gáatèe ní, ama á dū ti-yìntitam nì ti-kpitii kí pɔ̄-ti, ní kí fōō-ti kí ŋá a-nibul.»
Unimbɔti fātìi pōoǹ Isirayeel yab dipoondi
10Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «M làá pùtī kí pòon̄ Isirayeel yab dipoondi. A-nibul kɔkɔ nimbiinee, m làá ŋá maamaacib bin juti kaa láá pée jítì kitiŋ pu laaba nì ditimbundi diba poonee. Dinibul din māntìi tú-si nee làá ká maamaacib bin man ni-Dindaan làá dī a-pu ki ŋée nín kaa cáá juti puee.
11«Á ŋúb́ mara un m làá yóoń-si díǹ nee tiŋan. M làá jà Amɔɔr yab nì Kanaan yab nì Eeti yab nì Peeriisi yab nì Eefi yab nì Jeebusi yab a-nimbiin. 12Á nīn nyíǹ a-ba kí taa ŋá mpèé nì kitiŋ kin poon a cá kí kɔ́ nee yab. A yaa ŋá míǹ, án làá nīn sá kutaliŋŋu ní ki tīī-si. 13Ama ní gbá kí wīī bi-saraafaŋyi, kí kpìtī bi-kumpooŋi kí gàatì bi-windɔi kí lúkú. 14Ní taa gbàan̄ diwaal báà diba nì diba nimbiin, kun puee man ni-Dindaan yindi di sá <Ipoompoon>. M sá Unimbɔti un cáá ipoompoonee ní. 15Si nì kitiŋ kin a làá kɔ́ee yab ń taa pòon̄ tɔb kí ŋá mpèé. Bi yaa láa bíi tòotī bi-waaŋi ki ŋáań saraabi ki tìì-ŋee, bi làá dāá yíiń-ni ní ní jī bi-saraabi jinti. 16A yaa láa cáá bi-bisalib ki tīī a-jipɔmbee, bi-bisalib gbanti làá dāá nīn tòotī bi-waaŋi ní kí yàntī a-jipɔmbi mun ń nīn tòotī bi-waaŋi.
17«Á taa dū tikúti kí dùntī kí mɔ́ɔ́ diwaal.
18«Á dāá jī jiŋaal un bi ŋmóò kpɔnɔb bin kaa cáá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee. Á ŋmɔ́ kpɔnɔb bin kaa cáá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee iwiin iluli kii m nín yóoǹ-ni mara puee, Abiibi ŋmaliu un poon bi yóoǹ kí nīn jīǹ-uee. Di sá uŋmal gbanti poon ní bi nyántìń-ni Eejipiti tiŋkin.
19«Kibiseebiki kininjabiki kamaayee, man di yì. Míǹ ní unaa àá upii àá uŋoobu yaa péé péé ki màl̄ kijakee, bí dū-kì kí ŋá-mi saraa. 20Á dū kimaŋ biseemal kijaka kí kpántí dipibil àá diŋɔbil. A yaa kaa làá dūú kpántée, á nyīī kí gíí ki-sil. Ama a-jipɔmbi kansikin un sá kibiseebikee, á pà ki-pu.
«Á taa dāan̄ m-nimbiin nì iŋaŋkulim.
21«Á dū iwiin iluu kí tɔ̄ a-tuuŋŋi, ŋwinluluúti dalee, á kàl̄ kí ŋùŋfì. Báà an yaa sá tikpaal yuntiŋu àá tijin dical yuntiŋu, á kàl̄ ŋwiin gbanti kí ŋùŋfì.
22«Á dū bileepeepeekaa un a cáńee kí jī nnyɔmu jiŋaaliu, ní dibindi yaa bíi kúntée, á jī tantib jiŋaaliu.
23«A-ninjab kɔkɔ ń dāá dāan̄ man ni-Dindaan Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu nimbiin dibindi kamaa poon mita. 24Di sá m làá dāá jà atimbun kí pɔ̄-si mpaan ní kí wàan̄ a-tiŋki, ní ŋyunti ŋun a làá dāá dāan̄ man ni-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu nimbiin dibindi kamaa poon mitee, ubɔ dāa kpá kí màkan̄ yii u làá jáǹ-si kí fōō a-tiŋki.
25«A yaa làá dāá làntì kuwaŋkuluu kí ŋá-mi saraayee, á taa láa dū kpɔnɔb bin poon bi ŋá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee kí kūtì saraayee pu. Á taa láa dū saraabi bin a ŋá Dilákatil jiŋaaliuee nanti kí yóoń kutaa ń wúntí. 26Á dāá cáań tijimpeekaal tin a-sati lòon̄ee circir kɔŋkooŋŋun, ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nimbiin. Á taa dū uŋoobu biim kí ŋàan̄ u-biki nanti.»
27Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Á ŋmà tibɔti nee, kun puee tíǹ pu ní m tɔ́kɔǹ ki pūtì ki pōoǹ si nì Isirayeel yab dipoondi.» 28Mooyiisi nìn kāl̀ ti-Dindaan cee iwiin imuŋku ili, ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu, kaa jíń kaa nyùn̄. Ti-Dindaan nìn ŋmàn̄ dipoondi marab saalaayee titaŋkpapilindi pu.
Mooyiisi fātìi gítìń dinaapaal pu
29Mooyiisi kpákatìń Siinaayi jool pu, ki ŋúbiń titaŋkpapilindi tili tin pu bi ŋmàn̄ dipoondi marabee. Waa nìn nyí yii ŋyunti ŋun u bí ti-Dindaan ceeyee, u-nimbiin cúu kpántì ki kíǹ ki jìliŋkī. 30Aarɔn nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ kpēē Mooyiisee ki ká yii u-nimbiin cúu kpántì ki kíǹ ki jìliŋkī. Ní bi fāŋkì kí sútí kí pìl̄-u. 31Ní Mooyiisi yíiń-bi. Niinee Aarɔn nì samaa kpilib dɔ́miń u-cee ní u bíi sòoǹ nì bi. 32Boonee ní Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ sútìń ki pìl̄-u ní u dū marab bin kɔkɔ ti-Dindaan tīī-u Siinaayi jool puee ki tùkū-bi.
33Mooyiisi sòon̄ nì bi míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki dū ŋŋaabu ki bīiǹ u-nimbiin. 34Ŋyunti ŋun Mooyiisi yaa nìn là kí kɔ́ ti-Dindaan cee kí sòoǹ nì uee, ní ú cúú ŋŋaabu kí bìitī u-nimbiin kí nīn cí ŋyunti ŋun u yaa dóò ki làá nyānnée. U yaa nìn nyánnée ní ú dū marab bin u fōońee kí tùkù Isirayeel yab. 35Isirayeel yab nìn kāntí yii Mooyiisi nimbiin nìn kíǹ ki jìliŋkī. Niinee ní ú gíiǹ ŋŋaabu kí bìin̄ ŋu-pu kí nīn cí ŋyunti ŋun u làá fàtīí kɔ́ kí sòoǹ nì ti-Dindaanee.

english_text:
Laws for the Sabbath
1Moses called together the people of Israel and told them that the Lord had said:
2 You have six days in which to do your work. But the seventh day must be dedicated to me, your Lord, as a day of rest. Whoever works on the Sabbath will be put to death. 3Don't even build a cooking fire at home on the Sabbath.
Offerings for the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 25.1-9; 35.10-19)
4Moses told the people of Israel that the Lord had said:
5I will welcome an offering from anyone who wants to give something. You may bring gold, silver, or bronze; 6blue, purple, or red wool; fine linen; goat hair; 7tanned ram skin or fine leather; acacia wood; 8olive oil for the lamp; sweet-smelling spices for the oil of dedication and for the incense; or 9onyx stones or other gems for the sacred vest and breastpiece.
10If you have any skills, you should use them to help make what I have commanded: 11the sacred tent with its covering and hooks, its framework and crossbars, and its post and stands; 12the sacred chest with its carrying poles, its place of mercy, and the curtain in front of it; 13the table with its carrying poles and all that goes on it, including the sacred bread; 14the lamp with its equipment and oil; 15the incense altar with its carrying poles and sweet-smelling incense; the ordination oil; the curtain for the entrance to the sacred tent; 16the altar for sacrifices with its bronze grating, its carrying poles, and its equipment; the large bronze bowl with its stand; 17the curtains with the posts and stands that go around the courtyard and the curtain at the entrance; 18the pegs and ropes for the tent and the courtyard; 19and the finely woven priestly clothes for Aaron and his sons.
Gifts for the Lord
20Moses finished speaking, and everyone left. 21Then those who wanted to bring gifts to the Lord, brought them to be used for the sacred tent, the worship services, and the priestly clothes. 22Men and women came willingly and gave all kinds of gold jewelry such as pins, earrings, rings, and necklaces. 23Everyone brought their blue, purple, and red wool, their fine linen, and their cloth made of goat hair, as well as their ram skins dyed red and their fine leather. 24Anyone who had silver or bronze or acacia wood brought it as a gift to the Lord.
25The women who were good at weaving cloth brought the blue, purple, and red wool and the fine linen they had made. 26And the women who knew how to make cloth from goat hair were glad to do so.
27The leaders brought different kinds of jewels to be sewn on the special clothes and the breastpiece for the high priest. 28They also brought sweet-smelling spices to be mixed with the incense and olive oil that were for the lamps and for ordaining the priests. 29Moses had told the people what the Lord wanted them to do, and many of them decided to bring their gifts.
Bezalel and Oholiab
(Exodus 31.1-11)
30Moses said to the people of Israel:
The Lord has chosen Bezalel of the Judah tribe. 31-33Not only has the Lord filled him with his Spirit, but he has given him wisdom and made him a skilled craftsman who can create objects of art with gold, silver, bronze, precious stones, and wood. 34The Lord is urging him and Oholiab from the tribe of Dan to teach others. 35And he has given them all kinds of artistic skills, including the ability to design and embroider with blue, purple, and red wool and to weave fine linen.
translation_text:
CIRCIR KƆŊKOOŊŊU CÓONTAM (35–40)
Ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa bɔti
1Mooyiisi kpáfì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ ní ki bí-bi yii: «Kpèèmaan ti-Dindaan nín yóoǹ mara yii ní ŋá puee sèé: 2<A cáá iwiin iluu kí tɔ̄ ditundi, ama ŋwinluluúti dal sá ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa ní, ŋwiin ŋun a dūu sú man ni-Dindaanee. Un kamaa yaa túń ditundi ŋwiin gbantee, bí kpɔ̀-u. 3Laakin kamaa ni yaa kóòyee, ubɔ ń taa kpāā ŋŋmi ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dal.>»
Isirayeel yab cáań bi-saraabi
4Mooyiisi bí Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ yii: «Kpèèmaan ti-Dindaan nín yóoǹ mara yii ní ŋá puee sèé: 5<Ní lēēmaan ni-kansikin tigaajati tin ni cááyee poon kí ŋá ti-Dindaan saraa. Bin làá tīīyee ń tīī nì dipɔbil diba. Bí tīī sindaariya nì animbil kúti nì tasa kúti, 6nì bigulifamambi nì gulfab bin bí gùŋgumee nì bigulifamambi cínciŋ nì bigulifapimbi bin bí fálfalee nì tiŋɔkuti, 7nì ipigban in bi mántèe nì igban in dàfì tikpilee nì akasiya dɔi, 8nì ŋkpam min bi làá nīn cáa ŋáań fitilabinee nì talaalu kpam min bi làá nīn cáa sìtī binib yiliŋ pu kí dū-bi kí sú ti-Dindaanee nì talaalub bin bi làá nīn tùutēe, 9nì ataŋkpanyaan ŋin bi yíì soowamee nì ataŋkpanyaan aba mun bí dūú nákań eefoodi nì kilɔbiki kin pāantí usaraaŋakpil bindi puee. 10Bitɔntɔnliibi bin yáb̀ee kɔkɔ ń kpāfì kí tɔ̄ ditundi din ti-Dindaan bālifì yii ní tɔ̄ee. 11Bí kpāfì kí ŋá circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nì ŋu-biiŋkaati nì ŋu-tabikaati nì ŋu-fukuŋkaati nì ŋu-kalimii nì ŋu-dɔjaatii nì i-tílkaati, 12nì Dipoondi dakaau nì u-kpandɔi nì u-bìil nì ŋŋaasakaŋkaa ŋun pìtī circir laŋki nì circir páaa laŋki kansikinee, 13nì teebil nì u-kpandɔi nì tin kɔkɔ bi cáa tūǹ ditundi u-puee nì kpɔnɔb bin bi cāabìń ki pāantí ti-Dindaan nimbiinee, 14nì fitilab tɔ́kɔŋkaati nì ti-wanti kɔkɔ nì fitilab nì bi-kpam, 15nì talaalutuukaa saraafaŋŋu nì ŋu-kpandɔi nì ŋkpam min bi sìtī unil yil pu kí dū-u kí sú Unimbɔtee nì talaalutuukaa nì ŋŋaabu ŋun sàkā circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔkee, 16nì saraawɔkaa faŋŋu nì ŋu-làaŋ́ki kin sá tasa kútee nì ŋu-kpandɔi nì tin kɔkɔ bi cáa tūǹ ŋu-pu ditundee nì kusampeeu nì tikúti tin pu ku tɔ́kɔ́ee, 17nì iŋaabu in bi làá dūú màntīí gíb́ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu cindee nì i-dɔjaatii nì tikúti tin bi làá dūú tíĺ idɔjaa taapuee nì sata un bi làá dūú sàkan̄ dicindi punyɔkɔkee, 18nì circir kɔŋkooŋŋu kpakpaaŋi nì ŋu-cindi kpakpaaŋi nì ŋu-ŋmiii, 19nì tiwampeeŋkaal tin bi làá nīn pèentí ki tūǹ atuun circir kɔŋkooŋŋunee nì usaraaŋakpil Aarɔn wampeeŋkaati nì u-jipɔmbi yati tin bi làá nīn pèentí ki tūǹ disaraatundee.>»
20Niinee ní Isirayeel yab nyáń Mooyiisi cee. 21Bin nìn cáá tiniti ki làá tīī nì dipɔbil dibee nìn cáań ti-Dindaan bi-wanti bí dūú cóoń circir kɔŋkooŋŋu, kí tɔ̄ atuun ŋin kɔkɔ sá bí dūú tɔ̄ee ní kí dūú ŋáĺ circir wampeeŋkaati. 22Míǹ ní bininjab nì binimpoobi bin cáá tinitee yōoǹní akimbil nì falfatib nì mbɔmbiyaamu nì abɔmbil nì sindaariya wanti tin sá tiwannyɔkɔntikaalee ki dī akoobil nín sá puee ki dūu ŋá saraa ki tīī ti-Dindaan. 23Bin kɔkɔ nìn cáá bi-dumpui bigulifamambi gùŋgumee nì gulfab bin máǹ wèeeeyee nì bin máǹ cínciŋee nì bin pīiǹee nì tiŋɔkuti nì ipigban in bi mántèe nì igban in dàfèe, nìn cáań ki tīī. 24Bin kɔkɔ nìn lēē animbil kúti nì tasa kúti ki yóoǹ kí dūú ŋá ti-Dindaan saraayee nìn cáań. Bin kɔkɔ nìn cáá akasiya dɔyee nìn cáań bí dūú tɔ̄ atuun. 25Binimpoobi bin nìn nyí diwanlulee nìn dū gulfab bin máǹ gùŋgumee nì bin máǹ wèeeeyee nì bin máǹ cínciŋee nì bin pīiǹee ki lùn̄ ki cáań. 26Binimpoobi bin nyí diwanlulee nìn dū bi-pɔbiliŋ ki tīī ki dū tiŋɔkuti ki lùn̄ tiwan. 27Samaa kpilib nìn cáań ataŋkpanyaan ŋin bi yíì soowamee nì ataŋkpanyaan aba mun bí dūú nákań eefoodi lɔbiki kin pāantí usaraaŋakpil bindi puee, 28nì talaalub bin sɔ́fèe nì fitilab kpam nì min bi làá nīn cáa sìtī unil yil pu kí dū-u kí sú Unimbɔtee nì talaalutuukaa. 29Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ, bininjab nì binimpoobi nìn dàkā tiniti ki cáań tin kɔkɔ máaǹ bí dūú tɔ̄ atuunee ki ŋá saraa ki tīī ti-Dindaan nì dipɔbil diba.
Bitɔntɔnliibi bin túń circir kɔŋkooŋŋu tundee
30Mooyiisi bí Isirayeel yab yii: «Kpèèmaan ti-Dindaan lēē Uurii jipɔɔn Beesaleel, Uur un sá Juuda naakookunee naantiiu. 31U tīī-u u-Fam tikpil, ú nīn yáb̀ ki cáá iciin kí ŋmā kí tɔ̄ atuun nín bí a-ba a-ba puee kɔkɔ mmɔntiimin. 32U cáá nlandɔkɔ kí dū sindaariya nì animbil kúti nì tasa kúti kí dūú tɔ̄ atuun. 33U ŋūǹ kí kpítí ataŋkpee kí nákań, kí dū ndɔ kí kpítí kí dūú tɔ̄ atuun ŋí nīn bí a-ba a-ba. 34Ti-Dindaan pú-u ŋŋmam ú dàkà bi nín nāantí tiwan kí dūú tɔ̄ atuun puee kii u nín tí pú Ayiisamaaki un sá Daani naakookunee jipɔɔn Ooliyaab puee. 35U pú-bi dinyil bí ŋmā kí kpítí ataŋkpanyaan kí dūú ŋá tikɔkɔ, kí ŋmā kí lēē tiwan kɔkɔ naŋku tiba pu, ní kí ŋmā kí dū gulfa un máǹ gùŋgumee, nì un máǹ wèeeeyee nì un máǹ cínciŋee nì un pīiǹee kí dūú lù àá kí gbá tiwanee. U pú-bi dinyil bí ŋmā kí tɔ̄ bin kɔkɔ kíǹee tuuŋŋi.

english_text:
1The Lord has given to Bezalel, Oholiab, and others the skills needed for building a place of worship, and they will follow the Lord's instructions.
2Then Moses brought together these workers who were eager to work, 3and he gave them the gifts that the people of Israel had donated for building the place of worship. In fact, so much was being given each morning, 4that finally everyone stopped working 5and said, “Moses, there is already more than we need for what the Lord has assigned us to do.” 6So Moses sent word for the people to stop giving, and they did. 7But there was already more than enough to do what needed to be done.
The Curtains and Coverings for the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 26.1-14)
8-9The skilled workers got together to make the sacred tent and its linen curtains that were woven with blue, purple, and red wool and embroidered with figures of winged creatures. Each of the ten panels was twelve meters long and two meters wide, 10and they were sewn together to make two curtains with five panels each. 11-13Then 50 loops of blue cloth were put along one of the wider sides of each curtain, and the two curtains were fastened together at the loops with 50 gold hooks.
14-15As the material for protecting the tent, goat hair was used to weave eleven sections 13 meters by 2 meters each. 16These eleven sections were joined to make two panels, one with five and the other with six sections. 17Fifty loops were put along one of the wider sides of each panel, 18and the two panels were fastened at the loops with 50 bronze hooks. 19Two other coverings were made—one with fine leather and the other with ram skins dyed red.
The Framework for the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 26.15-30)
20Acacia wood was used to build the framework for the walls of the sacred tent. 21Each frame was 4 meters high and 66 centimeters wide 22-26with two wooden pegs near the bottom. Then two silver stands were placed under each frame with sockets for the pegs, so they could be joined together. Twenty of these frames were used along the south side and 20 more along the north. 27Six frames were used for the back wall along the west side 28-29with two more at the southwest and northwest corners. These corner frames were joined from top to bottom. 30Altogether, along the back wall there were eight frames with two silver stands under each of them.
31-33Five crossbars were made for each of the wooden frames, with the center crossbar running the full length of the wall. 34The frames and crossbars were covered with gold, and gold rings were attached to the frames to run the crossbars through.
The Inside Curtain for the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 26.31-37)
35They made the inside curtain of fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool, and embroidered with figures of winged creatures. 36They also made four acacia wood posts and covered them with gold. Then gold rings were fastened to the posts, which were set on silver stands.
37For the entrance to the tent, they used a curtain of fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool and embroidered with fancy needlework. 38They made five posts, covered them completely with gold, and set each of them on a gold-covered bronze stand. Finally, they attached hooks for the curtain.
translation_text:
1«Beesaleel nì Ooliyaab nì bininjab bin kɔkɔ ti-Dindaan pú dinyil nì iciinee làá tɔ̄ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu tuuŋŋi mmɔntiim án kàl̄ deedee, kii ti-Dindaan nín tīī mara yii bí ŋá puee.»
