2Mooyiisi nìn yíiń Beesaleel nì Ooliyaab nì bininjab bin kɔkɔ ti-Dindaan nìn tīī dinyil bi dū bi-ba ki tīī kí tɔ̄ ditundi nì dipɔbil dibee. 3Ní Mooyiisi dū tiwan tin kɔkɔ Isirayeel yab nìn cáań ki ŋá saraa bí dūú tɔ̄ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu tuuŋŋee ki tīī-bi. Kutaafaau kamaayee, binib nìn gbíntìi cāabìń tiwan nì dipɔbil diba. 4Niinee bitɔntɔnliibi bin Unimbɔti tīī iciin bi bíi tūǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu tuuŋŋee gbēeǹ bi-tuuŋŋi pu, 5ki cūtìi ká Mooyiisi ki bí-u yii: <Binib bíi cāabìń tiwan an wīikí tikpil ki jítiǹ min ti-Dindaan bālifì bí dūú tɔ̄ ditundee pu kpataaa.> 6Ní Mooyiisi tīī mara bi dūu nāatì binib kɔkɔ dinaapaal poon yii: <Bininjab nì binimpoobi kɔkɔ ń gbèen̄ kí taa ti cáań tiwan tin bi làá dūú tɔ̄ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu tuuŋŋee.> Niinee ní báà ŋma gbēeǹ kaa ti bíi cāabìń. 7Di sá yii tiwan tin bi nìn cáań bí dūú tɔ̄ atuun kɔkɔ nín sá puee nìn wīikí tikpil. An nìn wīikí ki lákatì.
Circir kɔŋkooŋŋu bɔ́ntitam
8Bitɔntɔnliibi bin nìn cáá iciin tikpilee nìn bɔ́ntì circir kɔŋkooŋŋu ŋaabui. Bi nìn dū gulfab bin máǹ gùŋgumee nì bin máǹ wèeeeyee nì bin máǹ cínciŋee ki lùn̄ aŋaajan saalaa, ní ki lùn̄ keerubimbi ki nákáǹ ŋi-pu. 9Aŋaajanee fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá meetab ubɔ kpá saalku ní ŋi-waaŋŋu sá meetab bili. Ŋi-kɔkɔ nìn ŋmà ní. 10Bi nìn dū aŋaajan aŋmoo ki ŋáĺ ki kpáfì, ní ki dū aŋmoo ŋin kíǹee mun ki ŋáĺ ki kpáfì. 11Bi nìn dū ŋŋaacalimu mun máǹ gùŋgumee ki kpákám̀ aŋaajan aŋmoo ŋin bi ŋáĺ ki kpáfì mpeekaamee diŋaajandi din lúŋkèe nyɔɔgbandi, nì ŋin bi ŋáĺ ki kpáfì nliliitiimee din pééyee nyɔɔgbandi. 12Bi nín ŋáĺ aŋaajan aŋmoo aŋmoo ki kpáfì puee kamaa nyɔɔgbandi nìn cáá ŋŋaacalimuee imuŋku ili nì saalaa, ní ajanliitilee ŋaacalimmu nìn ŋmà. 13Bi nìn dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ titábikaal imuŋku ili nì saalaa ki cúú ajanliitil ki kpáfì, ní tanti kɔkɔ dūu ŋá tiwambaantiil.
14Boonee bi nìn dū tiŋɔkuti ki lùn̄ aŋaajan saalaa nì diba ki dūu ŋá tantililiiti un làá nīn bìintí circir kɔŋkooŋŋu puee. 15Diŋaajandi kamaa fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá meetab saalku, ní ŋwaan sá meetab bili. 16Bi nìn dū ajan aŋmoo ki ŋáĺ ki kpáfì ubaanti, ní ki dū aluu mun ki ŋáĺ ki kpáfì ubaanti. 17Bi nìn dū ŋŋaacalimu imuŋku ili nì saalaa ki kpákám̀ aŋaajan aŋmoo ŋin bi ŋáĺ ki kpáfèe diŋaajandi din lúŋkèe nyɔɔgbandi, nì aluu ŋin bi ŋáĺ ki kpáfèe din pééyee nyɔɔgbandi. 18Bi nìn dū tasa kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́ titábikaal ki dūu nákáǹ ŋŋaacalimu pu ki dūu cúú diŋaajandi din kíǹee ki táb́, ní an dūu ŋá tiwambaantiil. 19Boonee ní bi mántì tipigban ki dūu bīiǹ tanti un bīī circir kɔŋkooŋŋu puee, ní ki dū ŋgban ŋun dàfèe ki páaǹ.
20Ní bi dū akasiya dɔŋu ki kpáá idɔjaati ki cóoǹ án nīn ŋúb́ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu. 21Idɔjaatee fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá meetab biŋmoo, ní i-waaŋŋu sá santimeetab biŋmoo kpá imuŋku inaa. 22Bi nìn cáká idɔ ili in cāatèe taapui ní i kɔ́ĺ tɔb ili ili. Bi nìn ŋá idɔjaatee kɔkɔ pu míǹ ní. 23Bi nìn kpáá idɔjaati mmuŋku circir kɔŋkooŋŋu ŋgiil pú, 24ní ki dū animbil kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́ titílkaal imuŋku ili. Tíǹ pu ní bi nín kpáá idɔjaati puee làá nīn tɔ́kɔ́. Bi nín kpáá idɔjaati puee kamaa nìn cáá titílkaal tili tin poon ní laakin bi cákée làá kɔ́ee. 25Bi nìn gíti kpáá idɔjaati mmuŋku circir kɔŋkooŋŋu ŋgan pú. 26Bi nìn dū animbil kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́ titílkaal imuŋku ili, ndɔjaati kamaa titílkaal tili. 27Bi nìn kpáá idɔjaati iluu ki cóoǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu boon pú jandi din bí ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki púee. 28Bi nìn kpáá idɔjaati ili ki cóoǹ akpin pu poon pú án nīn tíkí circir kɔŋkooŋŋu. 29Idɔjaati gbanti taapui nìn dátiǹ tɔb, ama ní ki tin dūu kpáfì yilpu dibɔɔbaantiil dibɔmbipeepeekaalin. Míǹ ní idɔjaatiliitilee nìn sá tiwambaantiil ní ki nìn sá titíkiŋkaal. 30Mimmee idɔjaatee nìn sá inii dee, ní i-taapu tílkaati nìn sá animbil kúti ní ki nìn sá saalku nì ubɔ, an dàkà yii ndɔjaati ŋubɔ, titílkaal tili.
31Bi nìn dū akasiya dɔŋu ki kpítì ikalim iŋmoo ki cúú idɔjaati in bi kpááyee circir kɔŋkooŋŋu jandi diba. 32Bi nìn kpítì ikalim iŋmoo mun ki cúú dijandi din kíǹee, ní ki kpítì iŋmoo mun ki cúú boon ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú. 33Ŋkalim ŋun nìn bí kansikinee nìn jítì idɔjaati in bi kpááyee kansikin nì kansikin ní, kí yòon̄ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu kílilaŋki kí tin cáá kátí. 34Bi nìn dū sindaariya ki nyūntì idɔjaati in bi kpááyee nì ikalimee pu, ní ki dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ mbɔmbiyaamu mun poon ní bi dū ikalimee ki bɔ́ee.
35Bi nìn dū gulfab bin máǹ gùŋgumee nì bi máǹ wèeee nì bi máǹ cínciŋee nì gulfab bin bí fálfal ki dàfèe ki lùn̄ ŋŋaasakaŋkaa, ki lùn̄ keerubimbi ki nákáǹ ŋŋaabuee pu. 36Bi nìn dū-ŋu ki sākaǹ akasiya dɔjaai inaa in bi dū sindaariya ki nyūntì sindaariya babikaati túuńee. Bi nìn dū animbil kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́ titílkaal tinaa ki dūu tíĺ taapu.
37Bi nìn dū gulfab bin bí fálfal ki dàfèe, nì bin máǹ gùŋgumee nì bin máǹ cínciŋee nì bin máǹ wèeeeyee ki lùn̄ ŋŋaasakaŋkaa ŋubɔ mun, usatalul nyáantì-ŋu ní bi dūu sākaǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu. 38Bi nìn kpítì akasiya dɔjaatii iŋmoo, ki dū sindaariya ki nyūntì-i ki dūu cóoǹ, ní ki dū titábikaal tin bi dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́yee ki bá, ní ki dū tasa kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́ titílkaal tiŋmoo ki tíĺ idɔjaatee taapu. Idɔjaati gbanti pu ní bi nìn dū ŋŋaasakaŋkaayee ki sākaǹ.

english_text:
The Sacred Chest
(Exodus 25.10-22)
1Bezalel built a chest of acacia wood 110 centimeters long, 66 centimeters wide, and 66 centimeters high. 2He covered it inside and out with pure gold and put a gold edging around the top. 3He made four gold rings and attached one of them to each of the four legs of the chest. 4Then he made two poles of acacia wood, covered them with gold, 5and put them through the rings, so the chest could be carried by the poles.
6The entire lid of the chest, which was made of pure gold, was the place of mercy. 7-9On each of the two ends of the chest he made a winged creature of hammered gold. They faced each other, and their wings covered the place of mercy.
The Table for the Sacred Bread
(Exodus 25.23-30)
10Bezalel built a table of acacia wood 88 centimeters long, 44 centimeters wide, and 66 centimeters high. 11-12He covered it with pure gold and put a gold edging around it with a border 75 millimeters thick. 13He made four gold rings and attached one to each of the legs 14near the edging. The poles for carrying the table were placed through these rings 15and were made of acacia wood covered with gold. 16Everything that was to be set on the table was made of pure gold—the bowls, plates, jars, and cups for wine offerings.
The Lampstand
(Exodus 25.31-40)
17Bezalel made a lampstand of pure gold. The whole lampstand, including its decorative flowers, was made from a single piece of hammered gold, 18with three branches on each of its two sides. 19There were three decorative almond blossoms on each branch 20and four on the stem. 21There was also a blossom where each pair of branches came out from the stem. 22The lampstand, including its branches and decorative flowers, was made from a single piece of hammered pure gold. 23-24The lamp and its equipment, including the tongs and trays, were made of about 35 kilograms of pure gold.
The Altar for Burning Incense
(Exodus 30.1-5)
25For burning incense, Bezalel made an altar of acacia wood. It was 45 centimeters square and 90 centimeters high with each of its four corners sticking up like the horn of a bull. 26He covered it with pure gold and put a gold edging around it. 27Then below the edging on opposite sides he attached two gold rings through which he put the poles for carrying the altar. 28These poles were also made of acacia wood and covered with gold.
The Oil for Dedication and the Incense
(Exodus 30.22-38)
29 Bezalel mixed the sacred oil for dedication and the pure spices for the sweet-smelling incense.
translation_text:
Dipoondi dakaau nì u-bìil
1Beesaleel nìn dū akasiya dɔŋu ki kpáá Dipoondi dakaau. U-púuŋŋu nìn sá meeta ubɔ nì santimeetab mmuŋku nì biŋmoo, ní u-waaŋŋu sá santimeetab biŋmoo kpá imuŋku inaa ní u-fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá santimeetab biŋmoo kpá imuŋku inaa. 2U nìn dū sindaariyamɔnti ki nyūntì poon nì boon, ní ki dū sindaariya ki kpákám̀ anyɔɔgbán. 3U nìn dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ abɔmbil anaa ki báaǹ dakaayee kpiŋŋi naatil, dijandi diba abɔmbil ali, diba mun abɔmbil ali. 4U nìn kpítì akasiya dɔŋu kpandɔi ki dū sindaariya ki nyūntì-i. 5U nìn dū ikpandɔee ki bɔ́ abɔmbil ŋin bá dakaayee kpiŋŋi an cāatì bí ŋmā kí nīn yòontí.
6Míǹ boonee ní u dū sindaariyamɔnti ki mɔ́ɔ́ dakaayee bìil. Di-fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá meeta ubɔ nì santimeetab mmuŋku nì biŋmoo ní di-waaŋŋu nìn sá santimeetab biŋmoo kpá imuŋku inaa. 7U nìn dū sindaariya un bi gbáńee ki mɔ́ɔ́ keerubimbi bili ki tɔ́kɔǹ didakaabiilee nyɔɔgbaŋŋi liitil pu. 8U nìn mɔ́ɔ́ keerubim ubɔ ki tɔ́kɔǹ didakaabiil nyɔɔgbandi diba nín kúntí puee, ní ki mɔ́ɔ́ keerubim ubɔ mun ki tɔ́kɔǹ didakaabiil nyɔɔgbandi din kíǹee nín kúntí puee. Keerubimbi nín tɔ́kɔ́ anyɔɔgbán kúntilaŋki puee nì dakaayee biil nìn kpáfì ki ŋá tiwambaantiil mmɔm. 9Bi nìn kpátì bi-feeŋyi yilpu ki bīiǹ didakaabiil pu. Bi nìn tɔ́kɔ́ ki túĺ tɔb ní bi-nimbiiŋyi tīī didakaabiil pu.
Kpɔnɔb bin bi dūu ŋá ti-Dindaan saraayee teebiliu kpáatam
10Boonee ní u dū akasiya dɔŋu ki kpáá teebil. U-púuŋŋu nìn sá meeta ubɔ, ní u-waaŋŋu sá meeta dijandi, ní u-fɔkɔŋŋu sá santimeetab biŋmoo kpá imuŋku inaa. 11U nìn dū sindaariyamɔnti ki nyūntì-u, ní ki dū sindaariya ki nyūntì ikpaanceeti kɔkɔ ki tú. 12Ní ki kpítì kidɔpampaŋ, kì wāā kii santimeetab binii ki kpákám̀ anyɔɔgbán, ní ki dū sindaariya ki nyūntì ki māntìi tú. 13U nìn mɔ́ɔ́ sindaariya bɔmbiliŋ anaa ki dūu báaǹ ki nákáǹ teebilee kpiŋŋi naatil pu, ataa cee. 14Abɔmbilee nìn náká teebilee kpaanceetii, ní bi dū ikpandɔ ki bɔ́ abɔmbilee poon bí ŋmā kí nīn yòontí teebilee. 15U nìn dū akasiya dɔŋu ki kpítì ikpandɔ, ki dū sindaariya ki nyūntì-i. Íǹ ní bi làá nīn cáa yòontí teebilee. 16U nìn mɔ́ɔ́ palantab nì kɔɔpub nì asambil nì itúun bí nīn cáa ŋáań ndaam ki féeń ti-Dindaan. U nìn dū sindaariyamɔnti ní ki mɔ́ɔ́ an wanti gbanti kɔkɔ.
Fitilab tɔ́kɔŋkaati mɔ́ɔtam
17Míǹ boonee ní u dū sindaariyamɔnti ki mɔ́ɔ́ fitila tɔ́kɔŋkaati. Ti-taapu nì ti-kpinjaatiŋu nì ti-kpiiŋyi nì ti-gbiŋŋi nì ti-pumpukum kɔkɔ nìn sá tiwambaantiil mmɔm ní. 18Ikpiin iluu nìn nyánní ŋkpiinjaatee pu. Dijandi kamaa nìn cáá ikpiin ita ita. 19Fitila tɔ́kɔŋkaati gbanti kpiiŋyi luutil kamaa nìn cáá ŋkɔŋkɔŋkuŋkumu muta mun náań nì asubil ŋin bi yíì amandee nì agbin nì mpumpukum. 20Ŋkpiinjaatee nìn cáá ŋkɔŋkɔŋkuŋkumu munaa mun náań nì asubil ŋin bi yíì amandee nì agbin nì mpumpukum. 21Ikpiin iluu in nìn túkú fitilab tɔ́kɔŋkaati kpinjaatiŋu puee taapu nìn cáá agbin. 22Agbin nì ikpiinee nì fitilab tɔ́kɔŋkaati jaŋŋi ŋin kíǹee nìn sá tiwambaantiil mmɔm ní. U nìn dū sindaariyamɔnti ní ki mɔ́ɔ́ tikɔkɔ. 23U nìn mɔ́ɔ́ fitilab biluli ki tɔ́kɔǹ fitilab tɔ́kɔŋkaati pu, ní ki nìn dū sindaariyamɔnti ki mɔ́ɔ́ tibabiti nì nsambiyaamu mun poon bi ŋáań ŋfantamee. 24U nìn dū sindaariyamɔnti kiiloobi mmuŋku nì saalaa ní ki mɔ́ɔ́ fitilab tɔ́kɔŋkaati nì ti-wanti kɔkɔ.
Talaalutuukaa saraafaŋŋu mɔ́ɔtam
25Boonee ní u dū akasiya dɔŋu ki kpáá nsaraafan ŋun pu bi làá nīn tùutī talaalubee. U nìn kpáá-ŋu ŋu-jaŋŋi naatil ŋmà ní. Dijandi kamaa nìn cáá dimeetajandi ní ŋfɔkɔn yilpu nìn sá meeta ubɔ. Nsaraafan nì ŋu-yiŋyi nìn sá tiwambaantiil mmɔm ní. 26U nìn dū sindaariyamɔnti ki nyūntì ŋu-yilpu nì ŋu-boon ki māntìi tú nì ŋu-yiŋyi, ní ki dū sindaariya ki kpákám̀-ŋu ki māntìi tú. 27U nìn mɔ́ɔ́ abɔmbil ali ki bá bi nín kpákám̀ nsaraafan taapu puee ajan liitil pu, bí nīn cáá ŋi-kpandɔi ki bōotí ki yòontí-ŋu. 28U nìn dū akasiya dɔŋu ki kpítì ikpandɔee ní ki dū sindaariya ki nyūntì-i.
29U nìn ŋá ŋkpam min sɔ́fèe kii utalaaluŋal nín ŋáań puee bí nīn cáa sìtī binib yiliŋ pu kí dū-bi kí sú Unimbɔti nì talaalutuukaa umɔnti.

english_text:
The Altar for Offering Sacrifices
(Exodus 27.1-8)
1Bezalel built an altar of acacia wood for offering sacrifices. It was 2.25 meters square and 1.34 meters high 2with each of its four corners sticking up like the horn of a bull, and it was completely covered with bronze. 3The equipment for the altar was also made of bronze—the pans for the hot ashes, the shovels, the bowls, the meat forks, and the fire pans. 4About halfway up the altar he built a ledge around it and covered the bottom half of the altar with a decorative bronze grating. 5Then he attached a bronze ring beneath the ledge at the four corners to put the poles through. 6He covered two acacia wood poles with bronze and 7put them through the rings for carrying the altar, which was shaped like an open box.
The Large Bronze Bowl
(Exodus 30.18-21)
8 Bezalel made a large bowl and a stand out of bronze from the mirrors of the women who helped at the entrance to the sacred tent.
The Courtyard around the Sacred Tent
(Exodus 27.9-19)
9-17Around the sacred tent Bezalel built a courtyard 44 meters long on the south and north and 22 meters wide on the east and west. He used 20 bronze posts on bronze stands for the south and north and 10 for the west. Then he hung a curtain of fine linen on the posts along each of these three sides by using silver hooks and rods. He placed three bronze posts on each side of the entrance at the east and hung a curtain 6.67 meters wide on each set of posts.
18-19For the entrance to the courtyard, Bezalel made a curtain nine meters long, which he hung on four bronze posts that were set on bronze stands. This curtain was 2.25 meters high, the same height as the one for the rest of the courtyard, and was made of fine linen embroidered and woven with blue, purple, and red wool. He hung the curtain on the four posts, using silver hooks and rods. 20The pegs for the tent and for the curtain around the tent were made of bronze.
The Sacred Tent
21-23Bezalel had worked closely with Oholiab, who was an expert at designing and engraving, and at embroidering blue, purple, and red wool. The two of them completed the work that the Lord had commanded to be done.
Moses put Aaron's son Ithamar in charge of the Levites who kept record of the metals used for the sacred tent. 24According to the official weights, the amount of gold given was a ton, 25 and the silver that was collected when the people were counted came to 3.4 tons. 26 Everyone who was counted paid the required amount, and there was a total of 603,550 men who were 20 years old or older.
27Thirty-four kilograms of the silver were used to make each of the 100 stands for the sacred tent and the curtain. 28The remaining 30 kilograms of silver were used for the hooks and rods and for covering the tops of the posts.
29Two thousand four hundred and twenty-five kilograms of bronze were given. 30And it was used to make the stands for the entrance to the tent, the altar and its grating, the equipment for the altar, 31the stands for the posts that surrounded the courtyard, including those at the entrance to the courtyard, and the pegs for the tent and the courtyard.
translation_text:
Saraawɔkaa faŋŋu nì kusampeeu kpáatam
1Boonee ní u dū akasiya dɔŋu ki kpáá saraawɔkaa faŋŋu ŋun jaŋŋi naatil ŋmèe. Dijandi diba nìn cáá meetab bili nì dijandi, ní ŋu-fɔkɔŋŋu yilpu nìn sá meeta ubɔ nì dijandi. 2Ŋu-jaŋŋi naatil kpiŋŋi puee, u nìn kpítì ki lēē iyin an jɔ́m̀, i nì nsaraafan sá tiwambaantiil mmɔm, ní u dū tasa kúti ki nyūntì. 3U nìn dū tasa kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́ tin kɔkɔ bi làá nīn cáa tūǹ nsaraafan pu tundee. An dàkà yii asambil ŋin poon bi làá nīn fà ŋkpam min bi wùn̄ee fantam ki ŋáańee nì peelab nì asambil ŋin poon bi làá nīn ŋáań fatiku ki cáa yàantée, nì njiimu mun cáá anyinee nì nsambiyaamu mun poon bi tùutī talaaluee. 4U nìn dū tasa kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́ kilàaŋ́ŋi ní ki ŋá ki-jaŋŋi naatil pu abɔmbil, ní ki dūu nákáǹ nsaraafan taapu ki māntìi tú ní an jɔ́mìń ki dāa ŋmāntì ŋu-kansikin. 5U nìn mɔ́ɔ́ abɔmbil anaa ki dūu bá tasa kúti làaŋ́kee kpiŋŋi naatil pu kí ŋmā kí dū ikpandɔ kí bɔ̄ poon. 6U nìn dū akasiya dɔŋu ki kpítì ikpandɔ, ki dū tasa kúti ki nyūntì-i. 7Ní ki dū ikpandɔee ki bɔ́ abɔmbil ŋin bí nsaraafan jaŋŋi puee poon bí ŋmā kí nīn yòontí-ŋu. Bi nìn dū idɔ ki kpáá nsaraafan ní ŋu-poon dɔ̄ fám tiba kpá poon.
8U nìn dū tasa kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́ kusampeeu nì kun pu ku tɔ́kɔ́ee. Bi nìn dū binimpoobi bin nìn tūǹ ditundi circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpuee gitiŋi ní ki túń an tuuŋŋi.
Circir kɔŋkooŋŋu cindi bɔ́ntitam
9Míǹ boonee ní u dū gulfa un dàfèe ki lùn̄ satab ki dūu bàkā ŋgan pú, ŋfɔkɔn nìn sá meetab imuŋku ili nì saalaa ní. 10U nìn dū mbɔmbilɔ̀kɔkaamu nì tibakaal tin bi dū animbil kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́yee ki cúú satabee ki dūu sākaǹ tasa kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́ an bí kii idɔjaatee mmuŋku. Idɔjaatee nìn cáá titílkaal mmuŋku tin bi dū tasa kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́yee. 11U nìn ŋá míǹ mbaantiim ŋgiil pú jandi mun. Niin mun nìn cáá satab meetab imuŋku ili nì saalaa ki sàkā idɔ mmuŋku in tílkaati sá tasa kútee, nì in pu animbil kúti bɔmbilɔkɔkaamu nì ti-bakaati bée. 12Ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki watil muee, satab fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá meetab mmuŋku nì biŋmoo, ki nìn sàkā idɔjaati in tɔ́kɔ́ titílkaal saalaa mun puee ní. Idɔjaati bɔmbilɔkɔkaamu nì i-bákaati nìn sá animbil kúti ní. 13Circir kɔŋkooŋŋu cindi ŋwaan pu dijandi din bí ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee mun nìn cáá meetab mmuŋku nì biŋmoo ní. 14-15Ajan liitil pu satab fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá meetab biluli nì dijandi, nì idɔjaati ita nì i-taapu tílkaati tita.
16Gulfab bin dàfèe ní bi nìn dūu lùn̄ satab ki sākaǹ ki māntìi tú circir kɔŋkooŋŋu cindi. 17Tasa kúti ní bi nìn dūu mɔ́ɔ́ idɔjaati tílkaati, ní ki dū animbil kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́ mbɔmbilɔ̀kɔkaamu nì tibakaal, ní ki mɔ́ɔ́ tikúti ki cíkiǹ idɔjaati yilpu. Bi nìn dū animbil kúti bɔmbilɔkɔkaamu ní ki cúú idɔjaati kɔkɔ ki kpáfì. 18Biwanluliibi nìn dū gulfa un dàfì ki máǹ gùŋgumee, nì un máǹ cínciŋee, nì un máǹ wèeeeyee ní ki lùn̄ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu cindi punyɔkɔki ŋaasakaŋkaaŋu. Ŋu-púuŋŋu nìn sá meetab saalaa ní ŋfɔkɔn sá meetab bili nì dijandi kii dicindi satab nín nìn bí puee. 19I nìn sàkā tasa kúti dɔjaatii inaa in tɔ́kɔ́ tasa kúti tílkaati tinaa mun puee ní. Tibakaal nìn sá animbil kúti ní bi dū animbil kúti ki nyūntì idɔjaatee yilpu nì mbɔmbilɔ̀kɔkaamuee. 20Circir kɔŋkooŋŋu kpakpaaŋi nì dicindi naabakaku kpakpaaŋi kɔkɔ nìn sá tasa kúti ní.
Tiwan tin kɔkɔ bi dūu túń ditundee
21Bi nín nìn dū tiwan tin ki cóoǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu ŋun poon bi làá dū Dipoondi marab kí ŋée nín nyáń puee sèé. Mooyiisi nìn yāntì Leefii yab di túń ditundi gbanti. Bi-kpiliu di nìn sá usaraaŋakpil Aarɔn jipɔɔn Itamaar. 22Kuur un sá Juuda naakookunee naantiiu Uur jipɔɔn Beesaleel di nìn túń atuun ŋin kɔkɔ ti-Dindaan nìn tīī Mooyiisi mara yii ú tɔ̄ee deedee. 23Ayiisamaaki un sá Daani naakookunee jipɔɔn Ooliyaab di nìn tútuǹ-u. U nìn sá ukpiŋkpiiti ní ki nìn ŋūǹ ki lèekī tiwan naŋku tiba pu, ki nìn ŋūǹ kí dū gulfa un máǹ gùŋgumee nì un máǹ cínciŋee nì un máǹ wèeeeyee nì gulfapiin kí dūú lù sata àá kí dūú gbá tiwan pu.
24Sindaariya un kɔkɔ Isirayeel yab nìn cáań bí dūú tɔ̄ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu tuuŋŋi kɔkɔee nìn nyáń kiiloobi alaataa anii nì bita kpá imuŋku inaa nì graambi alaataa ata, ki nóó nì circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nimbiliŋ ŋmàntitam.
25Isirayeel yab bin bi nìn kàan̄ee nín nìn cáań animbil kúti bi ŋmāntì an nyáń puee sá kiiloobi kutukub bita nì saalku nì bili nì graambi alaataa aluli nì imuŋku ili nì saalaa, ki nóó nì circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nimbiliŋ ŋmàntitam. 26An dàkà yii Isirayeel yab bininjab kutukub alaataa aluu nì bita nì bininjab alaataa aŋmoo nì imuŋku ili nì saalaa bin bi nìn kàan̄ kí yòon̄ abin mmuŋku kí nīn cáa cée, unil kamaa yil pu sá graambi biŋmoo dee. 27Bitɔntɔnliibi nìn dū animbil kúti kiiloobi kutukub bita ní ki mɔ́ɔ́ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu dɔjaatii tílkaati dilaataal, nì poon ŋaasakaŋkaaŋu dɔjaatii tílkaati. Mimmee titílkaal kamaa nìn fōō kiiloobi mmuŋku nì saalaa dee. 28Ní kiiloobi saalku nì bili nì graambi alaataa aluli nì mmuŋku nì saalaa bin kíǹee, bi nìn dūu mɔ́ɔ́ tibakaal nì tin bi mɔ́ɔ́ ki cíkiǹ idɔjaa yilpuee nì mbɔmbilɔ̀kɔkaamu mun bi dūu cúú idɔjaati ki kpáfèe.
29Isirayeel yab nín nìn cáań tasa kúti tiŋyee kɔkɔ nìn kpáfì kiiloobi kutukub bili nì dilaataal nì mmuŋku nì binaa. 30Bitɔntɔnliibi nìn dūu mɔ́ɔ́ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki dɔjaatii taapu tílkaati nì tasa kúti saraafaŋŋu nì ŋu-tasa kúti làaŋ́ki, nì tiwan tin kɔkɔ bi cáa tūǹ ŋu-pu ditundee, 31nì circir kɔŋkooŋŋu cindi dɔjaatii taapu tílkaati kɔkɔ, nì di-punyɔkɔki dɔjaatii taapu tílkaati nì ŋu-kpakpaaŋi nì circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nì dicindi naabakaku kpakpaaŋi.

english_text:
Making the Priestly Clothes
(Exodus 28.1-14)
1Beautiful priestly clothes were made of blue, purple, and red wool for Aaron to wear when he performed his duties in the holy place. This was done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
2-3The entire priestly vest was made of fine linen, woven with blue, purple, and red wool. Thin sheets of gold were hammered out and cut into threads that were skillfully woven into the vest. 4-5It had two shoulder straps to support it and a sash that fastened around the waist. 6Onyx stones were placed in gold settings, and each one was engraved with the name of one of Israel's sons. 7Then these were attached to the shoulder straps of the vest, so the Lord would never forget his people. Everything was done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The Breastpiece
(Exodus 28.15-30)
8The breastpiece was made with the same materials and designs as the priestly vest. 9It was 22 centimeters square and folded double 10with four rows of three precious stones: A carnelian, a chrysolite, and an emerald were in the first row; 11a turquoise, a sapphire, and a diamond were in the second row; 12a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst were in the third row; 13and a beryl, an onyx, and a jasper were in the fourth row. They were mounted in a delicate gold setting, 14and on each of them was engraved the name of one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
15-18Two gold rings were attached to the upper front corners of the breastpiece and fastened with two braided gold chains to gold settings on the shoulder straps. 19Two other gold rings were attached to the lower inside corners next to the vest, 20and two more near the bottom of the shoulder straps right above the sash. 21To keep the breastpiece in place, a blue cord was used to tie the two lower rings on the breastpiece to those on the vest. These things were done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The Clothes for the Priests
(Exodus 28.31-43)
22The priestly robe was made of blue wool 23with an opening in the center for the head. The material around the collar was bound so as to keep it from wearing out. 24-26Along the hem of the robe were woven pomegranates of blue, purple, and red wool with a bell of pure gold between each of them. This robe was to be worn by Aaron when he performed his duties.
27-29Everything that Aaron and his sons wore was made of fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool, including their robes and turbans, their fancy caps and underwear, and even their sashes that were embroidered with needlework.
30The words “Dedicated to the Lord” were engraved on a narrow strip of pure gold, 31which was fastened to Aaron's turban. These things were done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The Work Is Completed
(Exodus 35.10-19)
32So the people of Israel finished making everything the Lord had told Moses to make. 33Then they brought it all to Moses: the sacred tent and its equipment, including the hooks, the framework and crossbars, and its posts and stands; 34the covering of tanned ram skins and fine leather; the inside curtain; 35the sacred chest with its carrying poles and the place of mercy; 36the table with all that goes on it, including the sacred bread; 37the lampstand of pure gold, together with its equipment and oil; 38the gold-covered incense altar; the ordination oil and the sweet-smelling incense; the curtain for the entrance to the tent; 39the bronze altar for sacrifices with its bronze grating, its carrying poles, and its equipment; the large bronze bowl with its stand; 40the curtain with its posts and cords, and its pegs and stands that go around the courtyard; everything needed for the sacred tent; 41and the finely woven priestly clothes for Aaron and his sons.
42-43When Moses saw that the people had done everything exactly as the Lord had commanded, he gave them his blessing.
translation_text:
Bisaraaŋakpilib wampeeŋkaati
1Bi nìn dū gulfab bin máǹ gùŋgumee nì bin máǹ cínciŋee nì bin máǹ wèeeeyee ki ŋáĺ circir wampeeŋkaati bí nīn cáa tūǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋun ditundi. Bi nìn ŋáĺ Aarɔn circir wampeeŋkaati kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tīī Mooyiisi mara puee.
2Bi nìn dū sindaariya ŋmiii nì gulfab bin máǹ gùŋgumee nì bin máǹ cínciŋee nì bin máǹ wèeeeyee nì bigulifapimbi bin dàfèe ki lùn̄ eefoodi. 3Bi nìn gbáń ki kpátì sindaariya ní ki gífì ncalimu ncalimu, ní biwanluliibi cáa ŋmàlintí nì gulfab bin máǹ gùŋgum nì bin máǹ cínciŋee nì bin máǹ wèeeeyee nì gulfab bin pīiǹ ki dàfèe ki lùn̄. 4Bi nìn ŋáĺ ŋŋaacalimu muli ki bá ajan liitil nyɔɔgbaŋŋi bí nīn cáa cútí. 5Eefoodi ŋaacalimmu nìn sá tiwambaantiil ní. Bi nìn dū sindaariya ŋmiii nì gulfab bin máǹ gùŋgumee nì bin máǹ cínciŋee nì bin máǹ wèeeeyee nì bigulifapimbi bin dàfèe ní ki ŋáĺ ŋŋaacalimu gbanti, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tīī Mooyiisi mara puee. 6Bi nìn dū ataŋkpanyaan ŋin bi yíì soowamee ali ki fúuń sindaariya sɔntin, ki dū kigaai ki ŋmàn̄ Jaakɔb jipɔmbi yiŋŋi ataŋkpeeyee pu, kii bi nín cákà kijalii pu puee. 7Bi nìn dū ataŋkpeeyee ki bá ŋŋaacalimu mun bi ŋáĺ ki tábiǹ eefoodee. Ŋíǹ di nìn sá kii kudaaŋŋu ki téetí Jaakɔb jipɔmbi pu, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tīī Mooyiisi mara puee.
Kilɔbiki ŋáltam
8Míǹ boonee ní u yāntì bitɔntɔnliibi dū sindaariya ŋmiii nì gulfab bin máǹ gùŋgumee nì bin máǹ cínciŋee nì bin máǹ wèeeeyee nì bigulifapimbi bin dàfèe ki ŋáĺ kilɔbiki. 9Kilɔbiki gbanti jaŋŋi naatil nìn ŋmà ní dijandi kamaa nìn cáá santimeetab mmuŋku nì biŋmoo. 10Bi nìn dū ataŋkpanyaan ki nákáǹ ikuul inaa ki-pu ki nyáantì-kì. Ŋkuupeepeekaa nìn sá ataŋkpanyaan ŋin bi yíì oodeemeeyee, nì ŋin bi yíì piitidaayee nì ŋin bi yíì bareekeetee. 11Ŋkuuliliiti nìn sá ataŋkpanyaan ŋin bi yíì noofeekee, nì ŋin bi yíì safiiree nì ŋin bi yíì yaaliimee. 12Ŋkuutataatee nìn sá ataŋkpanyaan ŋin bi yíì leeseemee nì ŋin bi yíì seebooyee nì ŋin bi yíì alamaayee. 13Bi nìn dū ataŋkpanyaan ŋin bi yíì taarsiisee nì ŋin bi yíì soowamee, nì ŋin bi yíì yaasipee ki nákáǹ ŋkuunanaati pu. Bi nìn dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ tin poon bi làá dū ataŋkpanyaanee kí fúuńee. 14Bi nìn dū kigaai ki cáká Jaakɔb jipɔmbi saalaa nì bilee yiŋŋi ataŋkpanyaanee pu, kii bi nín cákà kijalii pu puee. Ditaŋkpanyaandi kamaa puee, bi nìn ŋmàn̄ kunaakoou kubɔ yindi, di sá tinaakɔti sá saalaa nì tili ní.
15Bi nìn dū sindaariyamɔnti ki mɔ́ɔ́ ikusaka ili mpalimu yam ki dūu cúú kilɔbikee. 16Bi nìn dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ mbɔmbiyaamu muli ki túuń kilɔbikee nyɔɔgbaŋŋi ali. 17Bi nìn dū sindaariya kusakayee ki bɔ́ mbɔmbiyaamu muli mun túuń kilɔbikee nyɔɔgbaŋŋi buŋyin. 18Bi nìn dū anyɔɔgbán ali ŋin kíǹee ki bá sindaariya wanti tili tin poon ní ataŋkpanyaan fúuń eefoodi ŋaacalimmu pu, ní an bí kilɔbiki nyɔkɔpuee. 19Bi nìn dū sindaariya ki gíti mɔ́ɔ́ mbɔmbiyaamu muli ki dūu bá kilɔbikee nyɔɔgbaŋŋi taapu jandi an nákáǹ eefoodi. 20Bi nìn dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ mbɔmbiyaamu muli mubɔ mun ki dūu bá iŋmii in bí eefoodi ŋaacalimmu puee taapu nnimbiin pú, laakin bi ŋáĺ ki táb́ee caŋin. Mbɔmbiyaamu gbanti nìn bí eefoodi dambalau yilpu pu ní. 21Bi nìn dū gulfab bin máǹ gùŋgumee ŋmiiŋu ki bɔ́ kilɔbiki bɔmbiliŋin nì eefoodi bɔmbiliŋin ki kúĺ, ní kilɔbikee pá eefoodi dambalau pu ki pɔ̄ɔ̄ kaa cìŋkī, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tīī Mooyiisi mara puee
Usaraaŋakpil wampeeŋkaati tiba mun ŋáltam
22Boonee ní bi dū gulfab bin máǹ gùŋgumee ki lùn̄ dibɔkutifɔkɔl din pu eefoodi làá nīn pée. 23Bi nìn lēē di-kansikin kinyɔkɔ, bi yaa làá pèen̄ee bí dū diyil kí bɔ̄ niin. Bi nìn lùn̄ kinyɔkɔee nyɔɔgbaŋŋi gbìfì ki dàfì kí taa ŋmā kí cátí. 24Bi nìn dū gulfab bin máǹ gùŋgumee nì bin máǹ wèeeeyee nì bin máǹ cínciŋee ki lùn̄ asubil ŋin bi yíì greenaadee ki lúntì dibɔkutilee júti taapu ki māntìi tú, 25ní ki dū sindaariya waŋkilimmu mun ki lúntì dibɔkutilee júti taapu greenaadi biliŋee kansikin ki māntìi tú. 26Bi nìn dū sindaariya waŋkilimmu nì greenaadi subiliŋ ŋin bi lùn̄ee ki lúntì disaraaŋabɔkutil júti taapu ki sákaǹ sákaǹ ki māntìi tú, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tīī Mooyiisi mara puee.
27Bi nìn dū iŋaapiin in bí fálfalee ki ŋáĺ Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi poon bɔkutiŋ, 28nì iŋaabu in bi cáa fìǹ diyilee, nì bisaraaŋaliibi fuulimmu nì ncukutigimpimu mun ŋaabui dàfèe. 29Ní bi dū gulfapiin un dàfèe nì un máǹ gùŋgumee nì un máǹ wèeeeyee nì un máǹ cínciŋee ki ŋáĺ dambala ki gbáń-u, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tīī Mooyiisi mara puee.
30Míǹ boonee ní bi dū sindaariyamɔnti ki mɔ́ɔ́ ki nántiǹ mpumpukum ní ki dū kigaai ki ŋmàn̄ ti-pu yii: <Bi dū-u ki sú ti-Dindaan.> 31Ní bi dū gulfa un máǹ gùŋgumee ki lùn̄ kiŋaacaliŋ ki cúú sindaariya pumpukumee ki nákáǹ ŋŋaabu ŋun bi cáa fìǹ diyilee yilpu pu, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tīī Mooyiisi mara puee.
Bi dóò circir kɔŋkooŋŋu tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ
32Míǹ ní Isirayeel yab nìn túń circir kɔŋkooŋŋu tuuŋŋi ki dóò. Ti-Dindaan nín nìn dàkā Mooyiisi yii bí ŋá puee, míǹ deedee ní bi nìn ŋá.
33Isirayeel yab nìn yōoǹní tin kɔkɔ bi làá dūú cóoń circir kɔŋkooŋŋuee ki cáań Mooyiisi cee:
- tanti nì u-wanti kɔkɔ an dàkà yii, titábikaal nì tifukuŋkaal nì ikalim nì idɔjaati nì titílkaal,
34- nì tipigban tin bi mántèe nì igban in bi cáa bìintée nì ŋŋaasakaŋkaa ŋun pìtī circir laŋki nì circir páaa laŋki kansikinee,
35- nì Dipoondi taŋkpapilinti dakaau nì u-kpandɔi nì u-bìil,
36- nì teebil nì tin kɔkɔ bi cáa tūǹ ditundi u-puee nì kpɔnɔb bin bi cāabìń ki pāantí ti-Dindaan nimbiinee,
37- nì sindaariyamɔnti fitilab tɔ́kɔŋkaati nì ti-wanti kɔkɔ nì fitilab nì bi-kpam,
38- nì sindaariya saraafaŋŋu nì ŋkpam min bi sìtī unil yil pu kí dū-u kí sú Unimbɔtee nì talaalutuukaa,
- nì circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki ŋaasakaŋkaaŋu,
39- nì tasa kúti saraafaŋŋu nì ŋu-làaŋ́ki kin sá tasa kútee nì ŋu-kpandɔi nì ŋu-wanti,
- nì kusampeeu nì kun pu ku tɔ́kɔ́ee,
40- nì iŋaabu in bi làá dūú màntīí gíb́ dikpafindi tantiu cindee nì i-dɔjaatii nì i-tílkaati nì dicindi punyɔkɔki ŋaasakaŋkaaŋu, nì ŋu-ŋmiii nì ŋu-kpakpaaŋi,
- nì tiwan tin kɔkɔ bi làá nīn cáa tūǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu poon tuuŋŋee,
41- nì tiwampeeŋkaal tin bi làá nīn pèentí ki tūǹ atuun circir kɔŋkooŋŋunee nì usaraaŋakpil Aarɔn wampeeŋkaati nì u-jipɔmbi yati tin bi làá nīn pèentí ki tūǹ disaraatundee.
42Isirayeel yab nìn túń atuun gbanti kɔkɔ, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tīī Mooyiisi mara yii ú ŋá puee ní deedee. 43Mooyiisi nín ká yii bi túń atuun gbanti kɔkɔ kii ti-Dindaan nín bí bí ŋá pueeyee, ní u mēē ki bīiǹ bi-pu.

english_text:
The Lord's Tent Is Set Up
1The Lord said to Moses:
2Set up my tent on the first day of the year 3and put the chest with the Ten Commandments behind the inside curtain. 4Bring in the table and set on it those things that are made for it. Also bring in the lampstand and attach the lamps to it. 5Then place the gold altar of incense in front of the sacred chest and hang a curtain at the entrance to the tent. 6Set the altar for burning sacrifices in front of the entrance to my tent. 7Put the large bronze bowl between the tent and the altar and fill the bowl with water. 8Surround the tent and the altar with the wall of curtains and hang the curtain that was made for the entrance.
9Use the sacred olive oil to dedicate to me the tent and everything in it. 10Do the same thing with the altar for offering sacrifices and its equipment 11and with the bowl and its stand. 12Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the tent and tell them to wash themselves. 13Dress Aaron in the priestly clothes, then use the sacred olive oil to ordain him and dedicate him to me as my priest. 14Put the priestly robes on Aaron's sons 15and ordain them in the same way, so they and their descendants will always be my priests.
16Moses followed the Lord's instructions. 17And on the first day of the first month of the second year, the sacred tent was set up. 18The posts, stands, and framework were put in place, 19then the two layers of coverings were hung over them. 20The stones with the Ten Commandments written on them were stored in the sacred chest, the place of mercy was put on top of it, and the carrying poles were attached. 21The chest was brought into the tent and set behind the curtain in the most holy place. These things were done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
22The table for the sacred bread was put along the north wall of the holy place, 23after which the bread was set on the table. 24The lampstand was put along the south wall, 25then the lamps were attached to it there in the presence of the Lord. 26The gold incense altar was set up in front of the curtain, 27and sweet-smelling incense was burned on it. These things were done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
28The curtain was hung at the entrance to the sacred tent. 29Then the altar for offering sacrifices was put in front of the tent, and animal sacrifices and gifts of grain were offered there. 30The large bronze bowl was placed between the altar and the entrance to the tent. It was filled with water, 31then Moses and Aaron, together with Aaron's sons, washed their hands and feet. 32In fact, they washed each time before entering the tent or offering sacrifices at the altar. These things were done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
33Finally, Moses had the curtains hung around the courtyard and at the entrance.
The Glory of the Lord
34 Suddenly the sacred tent was covered by a thick cloud and filled with the glory of the Lord. 35And so, Moses could not enter the tent. 36Whenever the cloud moved from the tent, the people would break camp and follow; 37then they would set up camp and stay there, until it moved again. 38No matter where the people traveled, the Lord was with them. Each day his cloud was over the tent, and each night a fire could be seen in the cloud.
translation_text:
Bí cóoń tanti kí dū-u kí sú Unimbɔti
1Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: 2«Uŋmapeepeekaa wimpeekaaŋu dalee, á dū tanti un poon dipoondi taŋkpapilinti kēe kí cóoń. 3Á dū dakaa un poon Dipoondi marab kēe kí yóoń ŋŋaapìtikaa boon án nīn lìkī bí taa nín̄ wāĺ. 4Á cáań teebil un pu bi làá nīn pāantí kpɔnɔb m-nimbiinee kpɔnɔb ń nīn pá. Á cáań fitilab tɔ́kɔŋkaati ní kí tūū fitilab. 5Á dū sindaariya saraafaŋŋu ŋun pu bi tùutī talaalubee kí yóoń dakaa un poon Dipoondi marab kēe nyɔkɔpu, ní kí dū ŋŋaasakaŋkaa kí sàkan̄ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki pu. 6Á dū saraawɔkaa faŋŋu kí yóoń circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu. 7Á dū kusampeeu kí yóoń circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nì nsaraafan kansikin, ní kí lúń nnyim kí gbéeǹ. 8Á dū iŋaabu in bi dū gulfab ki lùn̄ee kí màntīí gíb́ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu cindi, ní kí dū ŋŋaasakaŋkaa kí sàkan̄ kipunyɔkɔpu.
9«Á dū ŋkpam min bi cáa sìtī unil yil pu kí dū-u kí sú-mee kí sìtī circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nì tin kɔkɔ bí poonee pu. Míǹ ní a làá ŋá ní kí dū ŋu nì ŋu-wanti kɔkɔ kí sú-mi ní tí kpántí circir. 10Á dū ŋkpamee kí sìtī nsaraafan nì tin kɔkɔ bi cáa tūǹ ŋu-pu ditundee, mimmee a dū-ŋu ki sú-mi dee, ní ŋú kpántí circir. 11Ŋkpamee ní á tí dūú sìtī kusampeeu nì kun pu ku tɔ́kɔ́ee pu ní kú kpántí circir. 12Á cáań Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi kí yóoń dikpafindi tantiu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu, ní kí yàntī bí fàl̀ kí kpántí circir. 13Boonee á dū circir wampeeŋkaati kí pèen̄ Aarɔn, ní kí dū ŋkpam kí sìtī u-yil pu kí dū-u kí sú-mi ú nīn tūǹ man tundi. 14Á yàntī u-jipɔmbi ń sútiń kí pìl̄-si, ní á dū poon bɔkutifɔkɔŋ kí pèen̄-bi. 15Á dū ŋkpam kí sìtī bi-yiliŋ pu kii a nín ŋá bi-baa puee, kí dū-bi kí sú-mi bí nīn sá bisaraaŋaliibi ki tūǹ man saraaŋatundi. Ŋkpam min a sītì bi-yiliŋ pu ki dū-bi ki sú-mee làá yàntī bí kpántí man saraaŋaliibi kí nīn pée cáa cá jaanjaan.»
Mooyiisi yāntì bi dū circir kɔŋkooŋŋu ki cóoǹ
16Mooyiisi túń atuun kɔkɔ an kāl̀ deedee kii ti-Dindaan nín tīī-u mara ú ŋá puee. 17Isirayeel yab nín nyáń kuyuŋun Eejipiti tiŋkinee, an tú dibindi uŋmapeepeekaa wimpeekaaŋu dal ní bi cóoǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu.
18Mooyiisi nìn dū circir kɔŋkooŋŋu ki cóoǹ. U nìn dū titílkaal ki tíĺ ní ki dū tifukuŋkaal ki fúuń ní ki dū ikalim ki cúú ní ki dū idɔjaati ki cóoǹ. 19U nìn kpátì tanti ŋaabui ki bīiǹ, ní ki dū iŋaabiiŋkaa ki páaǹ, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tīī-u mara puee.
20Mooyiisi nìn dū titaŋkpapilindi tin pu bi ŋmàn̄ marab saalaayee ki tākaǹ dakaayee poon, ní ki dū dakaa kpandɔi ki bɔ́ dakaayee bɔmbiliŋin, ní ki dū u-bìil ki púkuǹ. 21U nìn cáá dakaayee ki kɔ́ǹ ki yóoǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋun, ní ki dū ŋŋaasakaŋkaa ki pītì bí taa nín̄ wāĺ dakaayee, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tīī-u mara puee.
22U nìn cáá teebil un pu bi pāantí kpɔnɔb ti-Dindaan nimbiinee ki kɔ́ǹ ki yóoǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋun ŋgan pú, ŋŋaapìtikaa nyɔkɔpu pú. 23U nìn dū kpɔnɔb bin bi pāantí ti-Dindaan nimbiinee ki páaǹ teebilee pu, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tīī-u mara puee.
24U nìn cáá fitilab tɔ́kɔŋkaati ki kɔ́ǹ ki yóoǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋun, ŋgiil pú teebil nyɔkɔpu. 25U nìn tūū fitilab ti-Dindaan nimbiin, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tīī-u mara puee.
26U nìn cáá sindaariya saraafaŋŋu ki kɔ́ǹ ki yóoǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋun, ŋŋaapìtikaa nyɔkɔpu. 27U nìn tūū talaalub ŋu-pu, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tīī-u mara puee.
28U nìn dū ŋŋaasakaŋkaa ki sākaǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔpu. 29U nìn dū nsaraafan ki yóoǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔpu, ní ki ŋá saraawɔkaa nì tijin saraau ŋu-pu, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tīī-u mara puee.
30U nìn dū kusampeeu ki yóoǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nì nsaraafan kansikin, ní ki lúń nnyim ki gbéeǹ bí nīn jòotī ki fíntí. 31Nnyim gbanti ní Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi nìn jòotī ki fíntí bi-ŋalii nì bi-taaŋi. 32Ŋyunti kamaa bi yaa làá kɔ́ circir kɔŋkooŋŋun kí sútí kí pìl̄ nsaraafanee, see bí fíntí míǹ, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tīī Mooyiisi mara puee.
33Mooyiisi nìn dū iŋaabu in bi lùn̄ee ki sākaǹ ki māntìi gíb́ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu cindi nì nsaraafan, ní ki dū ŋŋaasakaŋkaa ki sākaǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu cindi punyɔkɔpu. Míǹ ní Mooyiisi nìn túń circir kɔŋkooŋŋu tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ ki dóò.
Unimbɔti nyooti kɔ́ ki gbí circir kɔŋkooŋŋun
34Niinee ní ditagbandi dɔ́miń ki bīiǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu pu, ní Unimbɔti nyooti kɔ́ ki gbí ŋu-poon. 35Mooyiisi kaa nìn ŋūǹ kí kɔ́ circir kɔŋkooŋŋun, di sá yii ti-Dindaan nyooti nìn gbí ŋu-poon.
36Kí yòon̄ ŋyunti gbantee, ditagbandee yaa nìn yíkìi dāntì circir kɔŋkooŋŋu yilpuee, ní Isirayeel yab ń yīkì dinaapaal din pu bi nìn bée kí nìkī bi-saŋkindi. 37Ama ditagbandee yaa kaa nìn yíkìi dāntèe, bi nìn kā míǹ ní ki cí daliŋkin di làá yīkì kí dàntēe.
38Ti-Dindaan tagbandee nìn bīī circir kɔŋkooŋŋu pu ŋwiimpu, ama ní kunyeeuee an sá ŋŋmi ní Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ wāĺ. An nìn pée bí míǹ ní bi cōom̀ bi-saŋkindi kɔkɔ.

english_text:
1-3The Lord spoke to Moses from the sacred tent and gave him instructions for the community of Israel to follow when they offered sacrifices.
Sacrifices To Please the Lord
The Lord said:
Sacrifices to please me must be completely burned on the bronze altar.
Bulls or rams or goats are the animals to be used for these sacrifices. If the animal is a bull, it must not have anything wrong with it. Lead it to the entrance of the sacred tent, and I will let you know if it is acceptable to me. 4Lay your hand on its head, and I will accept the animal as a sacrifice for taking away your sins.
5After the bull is killed in my presence, some priests from Aaron's family will offer its blood to me by splattering it against the four sides of the altar.
6Skin the bull and cut it up, 7while the priests pile wood on the altar fire to make it start blazing. 8-9Wash the bull's insides and hind legs, so the priests can lay them on the altar with the head, the fat, and the rest of the animal. A priest will then send all of it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
10If you sacrifice a ram or a goat, it must not have anything wrong with it. 11Lead the animal to the north side of the altar, where it is to be killed in my presence. Then some of the priests will splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
12-13Cut up the animal and wash its insides and hind legs. A priest will put these parts on the altar with the head, the fat, and the rest of the animal. Then he will send all of it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
14If you offer a bird for this kind of sacrifice, it must be a dove or a pigeon. 15A priest will take the bird to the bronze altar, where he will wring its neck and put its head on the fire. Then he will drain out its blood on one side of the altar, 16remove the bird's craw with what is in it, and throw them on the ash heap at the east side of the altar. 17Finally, he will take the bird by its wings, tear it partially open, and send it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_text:
SARAABI NÍN BÍ TƆBIN PUEE BƆTI
(Ayil 1–10)
Saraawɔkaa
1Ti-Dindaan yíiń Mooyiisi circir kɔŋkooŋŋun ní ki sòon̄ nì u ki bí-u yii: 2«Sòoǹ nì Isirayeel yab kí tùkù-bi yii:
«Ni-kansikin ubɔ yaa là kí ŋá saraa kí tīī ti-Dindaanee, udaan ń dū unaa àá upii àá uŋoobu ní kí ŋá saraa gbanti.
3«An yaa sá unaa ní udaan cáań kí ŋá saraawɔkaayee, ú nīn sá uja un laaba kaa wɔ̀b̄ee. Ú cáań-u dikpafindi tantiu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu ní ti-Dindaan ń nín fōō u-saraau. 4Ú dū u-ŋal kí páań kuwaŋkuluuee yil pu ní ti-Dindaan ń nín fōō u-saraau ní kí dū u-kpitii kí pɔ̄-u. 5Ú làntì unaayee circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nyɔkɔpu ti-Dindaan nimbiin. Ní Aarɔn jipɔmbi bisaraaŋaliibi ń dū unaayee fatikuu kí yàaǹ kí màntīí tū nsaraafan ŋun bí circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki caŋinee. 6Ú lēē unaayee gbaŋŋu, kí càkà u-nanti. 7Usaraaŋakpil Aarɔn jipɔmbi ń kpāā ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu ní kí dū idɔ kí páań. 8Bí dū tinan tin bi càkēe nì diyil nì ŋkpam kí páań idɔ in bi dūu páaǹ ŋŋmi pu nsaraafan puee. 9Un cáań kuwaŋkuluuee ń dū nnyim kí fíntí ina nì ayaka ní usaraaŋal ubɔ ń dū tinanee kɔkɔ kí wà ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu. An di sá saraawɔkaa, saraa un ní bi dù tinan kɔkɔ kí wà ŋŋmi, u-sɔnsɔfiŋu sɔ̀ŋkī ti-Dindaan pɔbilee.
10«An yaa sá upii àá uŋoobu ní udaan cáań kí ŋá saraawɔkaayee, kuwaŋkuluuee laaba ń taa nīn wɔ̀b̄. 11Ú làntì-ku circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nyɔkɔpu ti-Dindaan nimbiin, nsaraafan caŋin, ŋgan pú. Aarɔn jipɔmbi bisaraaŋaliibi ń dū fatiku kí yàaǹ nsaraafan jaŋŋi kɔkɔ pu kí màntīí tū. 12Ú càkà tinanee ní kí dū diyil nì ŋkpam kí kūtì, ní usaraaŋal ubɔ ń dūú páań idɔ in bi dūu páaǹ ŋŋmi pu nsaraafan puee. 13Un cáań kuwaŋkuluuee ń dū nnyim kí fíntí ina nì ayaka ní usaraaŋal ubɔ ń dū tinanee kɔkɔ kí wà ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu. An di sá saraawɔkaa, saraa un ní bi dù tinan kɔkɔ kí wà ŋŋmi, u-sɔnsɔfiŋu sɔ̀ŋkī ti-Dindaan pɔbilee.
14«An yaa tí sá unoon ní udaan cáań kí ŋá saraawɔkaa kí tīī ti-Dindaanee, an nīn sá kinanjilii àá dibeenanjil. 15Usaraaŋal ubɔ ń fōō unoonee kí cáá cùnnì nsaraafan caŋin, kí tùkutī diyil kí dūú wà ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu, ní kí dū u-fatikuu kí còol̀ nsaraafan kpiŋŋi pu. 16Ú lēē kunyannyanciliu nì tin kā ku-poonee kí fá nsaraafan caŋin ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú, laakin bi bīil̀ ŋkpam min bi wùn̄ee fantamee. 17Ní ú cúú unoonee kí dáaĺ kí cátí mili ifeen kansikin án taa nàbitī, ní kí dūú páań idɔ in bi dūu páaǹ ŋŋmi pu nsaraafan puee án wà. An di sá saraawɔkaa, saraa un bi dù tinan kɔkɔ kí wà ŋŋmi u-sɔnsɔfiŋu sɔ̀ŋkī ti-Dindaan pɔbilee.»

english_text:
Sacrifices To Give Thanks to the Lord
The Lord said:
1When you offer sacrifices to give thanks to me, you must use only your finest flour. Put it in a dish, sprinkle olive oil and incense on the flour, 2and take it to the priests from Aaron's family. One of them will scoop up the incense together with a handful of the flour and oil. Then, to show that the whole offering belongs to me, the priest will lay this part on the bronze altar and send it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me. 3The rest of this sacrifice is for the priests; it is very holy because it was offered to me.
4If you bake bread in an oven for this sacrifice, use only your finest flour, but without any yeast. You may make the flour into a loaf mixed with olive oil, or you may make it into thin wafers and brush them with oil.
5If you cook bread in a shallow pan for this sacrifice, use only your finest flour. Mix it with olive oil, but do not use any yeast. 6Then break the bread into small pieces and sprinkle them with oil. 7If you cook your bread in a pan with a lid on it, you must also use the finest flour mixed with oil.
8You may prepare sacrifices to give thanks in any of these three ways. Bring your sacrifice to a priest, and he will take it to the bronze altar. 9Then, to show that the whole offering belongs to me, the priest will lay part of it on the altar and send it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me. 10The rest of this sacrifice is for the priests; it is very holy because it was offered to me.
11Yeast and honey must never be burned on the altar, so don't ever mix either of these in a grain sacrifice. 12You may offer either of them separately, when you present the first part of your harvest to me, but they must never be burned on the altar.
13Salt is offered when you make an agreement with me, so sprinkle salt on these sacrifices.
14Freshly cut grain, either roasted or coarsely ground, must be used when you offer the first part of your grain harvest. 15You must mix in some olive oil and put incense on top, because this is a grain sacrifice. 16A priest will sprinkle all of the incense and some of the grain and oil on the altar and send them up in smoke to show that the whole offering belongs to me.
translation_text:
Tijimpin saraau
1«Ubɔ yaa là kí cáań tijimpin saraau kí tīī ti-Dindaanee, án nīn sá ŋyim. Ú bàtī ŋkpam kí sìtī, kí dū talaalutuukaa kí páań, 2ní kí cáań kí tīī Aarɔn jipɔmbi bisaraaŋaliibi. Usaraaŋal un làá ŋá saraa gbantee ń yáfí ŋyim diŋaŋkul din sá kudaaŋŋu ti-Dindaan nimbiin yii úǹ di yì saraa gbantee kí dū ŋkpam kí búuń ní kí dū talaalutuukaa un bi cáańee kɔkɔ kí kūtì kí dūú wà ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu. An di sá saraa un sɔnsɔfiŋu sɔ̀ŋkī ti-Dindaan pɔbilee. 3Saraayee jandi din kíǹee, Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi di yì. Dijandi gbanti sá circir páaa wanti ní, kun puee an sá saraa un bi lēē ki wùn̄ ŋŋmi ki tīī ti-Dindaanee ní.
4«An yaa sá tijin tin bi púĺ dibubulinee ní ubɔ yaa cáań kí ŋá saraayee, án nīn sá kpɔnɔ un bi dū ŋyim ki búuń ŋkpamin ki púĺ an kaa cáá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee. 5An yaa sá tijin tin bi pūul̀ titaŋkpapilindi puee saraauee, ú dū ŋkpam kí búuń ŋyim kí taa ŋá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔ. 6Ú càkà càkà-u ní kí bàtī ŋkpam kí sìtī an pu. Tijimpin saraau dee. 7An yaa tí sá tijin tin bi tòó kikpasaŋ poonee saraauee, ú dū ŋkpam kí búuń ŋyim kí ŋá tijin gbanti. 8Ú cáań saraa un u bɔ́ntì kí tīī ti-Dindaanee kí ŋúbiǹ usaraaŋal ní úǹ ń fōō kí cáá síiń nsaraafan caŋin. 9Saraa gbanti poonee, usaraaŋal ń lēē dijandi din sá kudaaŋŋu ti-Dindaan nimbiin yii úǹ di yì saraa gbantee kí wà ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu. An di sá saraa un bi dùú wà ŋŋmi u-sɔnsɔfiŋu sɔ̀ŋkī ti-Dindaan pɔbilee. 10Dijandi din kíǹee, Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi di yì. Dijandi gbanti sá circir páaa wanti ní, kun puee an sá saraa un bi lēē ki wùn̄ ŋŋmi ki tīī ti-Dindaanee ní.
11«Tijimpin saraau un kamaa ni làá ŋá kí tīī ti-Dindaanee, ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔ ń taa nín̄ bí poon. Ubɔ kaa tí máaǹ kí dū ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔ àá tisiil kí ŋá saraa kí wà ŋŋmi kí tīī ti-Dindaan. 12Ama u ŋūǹ kí cáań kí ŋá tijincɔ̀fikaal saraau kí tīī ti-Dindaan. Ú taa pée dū-tì kí wà ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu kii saraa un sɔnsɔfiŋu sɔ̀ŋkī ti-Dindaan pɔbilee.
13«Tijimpin saraau kamaa poon máaǹ kí nīn cáá ŋyaam. Ú taa pée yàntī ŋyaam min sá ni-Nimbɔtiu poondi daaŋkuee ń lóó u-saraabi poon.
14«Tijincɔ̀fikaal ní ubɔ yaa cáań kí ŋá saraa kí tīī ti-Dindaanee, ú púĺ ifin kí yìlifì abil ní kí cáań kí ŋá saraa. 15Ú bàtī ŋkpam kí sìtī an pu ní kí dū talaalutuukaa kí páań. Tijimpin saraau dee. 16Usaraaŋal ń dū saraayee, an dàkà yii abil ŋin bi yīlifèe dijandi nì ŋkpamee nì talaalutuukaayee kɔkɔ kí wà ŋŋmi. An di sá tijimpin saraau un bi dùú wà ŋŋmi kí tīī ti-Dindaanee.»

english_text:
Sacrifices To Ask the Lord's Blessing
The Lord said:
1When you offer sacrifices to ask my blessing, you may offer either a bull or a cow, but there must be nothing wrong with the animal. 2Lead it to the entrance of the sacred tent, lay your hand on its head, and have it killed there. A priest from Aaron's family will splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
3Offer all of the fat on the animal's insides, 4as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat. 5Some of the priests will lay these pieces on the altar and send them up in smoke with a smell that pleases me, together with the sacrifice that is offered to please me.
6Instead of a bull or a cow, you may offer any sheep or goat that has nothing wrong with it. 7If you offer a sheep, you must present it to me at the entrance to the sacred tent. 8Lay your hand on its head and have it killed there. A priest will then splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
9Offer the fat on the tail, the tailbone, and the insides, 10as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat. 11One of the priests will lay these pieces on the altar and send them up in smoke as a food offering for me.
12If you offer a goat, you must also present it to me 13at the entrance to the sacred tent. Lay your hand on its head and have it killed there. A priest will then splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
14Offer all of the fat on the animal's insides, 15as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat. 16One of the priests will put these pieces on the altar and send them up in smoke as a food offering with a smell that pleases me.
All fat belongs to me. 17So you and your descendants must never eat any fat or any blood, not even in the privacy of your own homes. This law will never change.
translation_text:
Mpèé saraau
1«Ubɔ yaa lēē u-nacaŋkpuŋkun unaa kí ŋá mpèé saraauee, ú nīn sá uja àá usal un laaba kaa wɔ̀b̄ee. Ú cáań-u circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nyɔkɔpu ti-Dindaan nimbiin. 2Ú dū u-ŋal kí páań kuwaŋkuluuee yil pu, kí làntì-ku circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu, ní Aarɔn jipɔmbi bisaraaŋaliibi ń dū fatiku kí yàaǹ nsaraafan jaŋŋi kɔkɔ pu kí màntīí tū. 3Tin bi làá lēē mpèé saraau gbanti poon kí wà ŋŋmi kí tīī ti-Dindaanee di sá ŋkpam min bīī ina puee nì ŋkpam min pá i-puee, 4nì aceebil liitil nì ŋkpam min pá ŋi nì ntikakal puee, ní kí lēē mpɔɔlam kɔkɔ kí nákatí kí kpáaǹ aceebil dicilpu. 5Ní Aarɔn jipɔmbi ń dūú kūtì saraawɔkaa un pá idɔ in bi dūu páaǹ ŋŋmi pu nsaraafan puee. An di sá mpèé saraau un bi dùú wà ŋŋmi u-sɔnsɔfiŋu sɔ̀ŋkī ti-Dindaan pɔbilee.
6«An yaa sá upii àá uŋoobu ní ubɔ cáań kí ŋá saraa kí dàkà u nì ti-Dindaan kansikin pèéŋuee, án nīn sá uja àá usal un laaba kaa wɔ̀b̄ee. 7An yaa sá dipibil ní udaan cáań kí dūú ŋá saraayee, ú cáań-dì ti-Dindaan nimbiin. 8Ú dū u-ŋal kí páań dipibilee yil pu ní kí làntì-dì circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu ní Aarɔn jipɔmbi ń dū di-fatikuu kí yàaǹ nsaraafan jaŋŋi kɔkɔ pu kí màntīí tū. 9Tin bi làá lēē mpèé saraau gbanti poon kí wà ŋŋmi kí tīī ti-Dindaanee di sá ŋkpam: dijugbindi din bi lēēyee kɔkɔ nì ŋkpam min bīī ina puee nì ŋkpam min kɔkɔ pá i-puee, 10nì aceebil liitil nì ŋkpam min pá ŋi nì ntikakal puee, ní kí lēē mpɔɔlam kɔkɔ kí nákatí kí kpáaǹ aceebilee dicilpu. 11Niinee ní usaraaŋal ń cáá wà ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu. An di sá tijin saraau un bi dùú wà ŋŋmi kí tīī ti-Dindaanee.
12«An yaa sá uŋoobu ní udaan cáań kí dùú ŋá saraayee, ú cáań-u ti-Dindaan nimbiin. 13Ú dū u-ŋal kí páań uŋoobuee yil pu ní kí làntì-u circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu ní Aarɔn jipɔmbi ń dū u-fatikuu kí yàaǹ nsaraafan jaŋŋi kɔkɔ pu kí màntīí tū. 14Tin bi làá lēē saraa gbanti poon kí wà ŋŋmi kí tīī ti-Dindaanee di sá ŋkpam min bīī ina puee nì ŋkpam min kɔkɔ pá i-puee, 15nì aceebil liitil nì ŋkpam min pá ŋi nì ntikakal puee ní kí lēē mpɔɔlam kɔkɔ kí nákatí kí kpáaǹ aceebilee dicilpu. 16Niinee ní usaraaŋal ń dūú wà ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu. An di sá tijin saraau un bi dùú wà ŋŋmi u-sɔnsɔfiŋu sɔ̀ŋkī ti-Dindaan pɔbilee.
«Tin kamaa pée sá ŋkpamee, ti-Dindaan di yì. 17Án nīn sá dibɔkpaal din làá nīn bí ki cá jaanjaanee ki tīī ni nì ni-biyaamu yii báà laakin kamaa ní ni yaa bàn̄ ki kóòyee, ní nīn nyí yii naa máaǹ kí ŋmɔ́ kuwaŋkuluu fatikuu nì ku-kpam.»

english_text:
Sacrifices for Sin
(Leviticus 6.24-30)
1The Lord told Moses 2to say to the community of Israel:
Offer a sacrifice to ask forgiveness when you sin by accidentally doing something I have told you not to do.
When the High Priest Sins
The Lord said:
3When the high priest sins, he makes everyone else guilty too. And so, he must sacrifice a young bull that has nothing wrong with it. 4The priest will lead the bull to the entrance of the sacred tent, lay his hand on its head, and kill it there. 5He will take a bowl of the blood inside the tent, 6dip a finger in the blood, and sprinkle some of it seven times toward the sacred chest behind the curtain. 7Then, in my presence, he will smear some of the blood on each of the four corners of the incense altar, before pouring out the rest at the foot of the bronze altar near the entrance to the tent.
8-10The priest will remove the fat from the bull, just as he does when he sacrifices a bull to ask my blessing. This includes the fat on the insides, as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat. He will then send it all up in smoke.
11-12The skin and flesh of the bull, together with its legs, insides, and the food still in its stomach, are to be taken outside the camp and burned on a wood fire near the ash heap.
When the Whole Nation Sins
The Lord said:
13When the nation of Israel disobeys me without meaning to, the whole nation is still guilty. 14Once you realize what has happened, you must sacrifice a young bull to ask my forgiveness. Lead the bull to the entrance of the sacred tent, 15where your tribal leaders will lay their hands on its head, before having it killed in my presence.
16The priest will take a bowl of the animal's blood inside the sacred tent, 17dip a finger in the blood, and sprinkle some of it seven times toward the sacred chest behind the curtain. 18Then, in my presence, he must smear some of the blood on each of the four corners of the incense altar, before pouring out the rest at the foot of the bronze altar near the entrance to the tent. 19-21After this, the priest will remove the fat from the bull and send it up in smoke on the altar. Finally, he will burn its remains outside the camp, just as he did with the other bull. By this sacrifice the sin of the whole nation will be forgiven.
When a Tribal Leader Sins
The Lord God said:
22Any tribal leader who disobeys me without knowing it is still guilty. 23As soon as the leader realizes what has happened, he must sacrifice a goat that has nothing wrong with it. 24This is a sacrifice for sin. So he will lay his hand on the animal's head, before having it killed in my presence at the north side of the bronze altar. 25The priest will dip a finger in the blood, smear some of it on each of the four corners of the altar, and pour out the rest at the foot of the altar. 26Then he must send all of the fat up in smoke, just as he does when a sacrifice is offered to ask my blessing. By this sacrifice the leader's sin will be forgiven.
When Ordinary People Sin
The Lord said:
27 When any of you ordinary people disobey me without meaning to, you are still guilty. 28As soon as you realize what you have done, you must sacrifice a female goat that has nothing wrong with it. 29Lead the goat to the north side of the bronze altar and lay your hand on its head, before having it killed. 30Then a priest will dip a finger in the blood; he will smear some of it on each of the four corners of the altar and pour out the rest at the foot of the altar. 31After this, the priest will remove all of the fat, just as he does when an animal is sacrificed to ask my blessing. The priest will then send the fat up in smoke with a smell that pleases me. This animal is sacrificed so that I will forgive you ordinary people when you sin.
32If you offer a lamb instead of a goat as a sacrifice for sin, it must be a female that has nothing wrong with it. 33Lead the lamb to the altar and lay your hand on its head, before having it killed. 34The priest will dip a finger in the blood, smear some of it on each of the four corners of the altar, and pour out the rest at the foot of the altar. 35After this, all of the fat must be removed, just as when an animal is sacrificed to ask my blessing. Then the priest will send it up in smoke to me, together with a food offering, and your sin will be forgiven.
translation_text:
Ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau a. Usaraaŋakpil saraau
1Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Mooyiisi yii: 2«Tùkù Isirayeel yab yii:
«Ubɔ yaa kaa nyí ní ki yīntì ki ŋá tin ti-Dindaan marab nee kansikin ubɔ bí yii bí taa ŋée,
3«an yaa sá usaraaŋakpil di ŋá ikpiti ní u-kpitii gbanti yāntì samaa kɔkɔ kɔ́ ikpitinee, u máaǹ kí cáań dinabil din laaba kaa wɔ̀b̄ee kí ŋá ti-Dindaan saraa ní kí nín ká u-kpitii pɔ̄tam. 4Ú cáań dinabilee circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu ti-Dindaan nimbiin, kí dū u-ŋal kí páań dinabilee yil pu ní kí làntì-dì ti-Dindaan nimbiin niin. 5Usaraaŋakpil ń dū dinabilee fatikuu kí kɔ́ǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu poon, 6ní ti-Dindaan nimbiin niinee ní ú dū u-ŋambiki kí sēē fatikuee kí dūú yàaǹ ŋŋaabu ŋun bi dūu pītì ki yākatì circir páaa nì circir laŋkee pu ŋfunyɔm miluli. 7Usaraaŋakpil ń bàtī fatikuee kí ŋmìtī nsaraafan ŋun pu bi tùutī talaalub ŋu bí circir kɔŋkooŋŋun, ti-Dindaan nimbiinee yiŋyi pu. Ú dū fatiku un kíǹee kɔkɔ kí kpáatí kí pɔ̀l̄ saraawɔkaa faŋŋu ŋun bí circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpuee taapu. 8Ú lēē tinan tin pée cáá ŋkpam ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau gbanti poonee, an dàkà yii ŋkpam min bīī ina puee nì ŋkpam min kɔkɔ pá i-puee, 9nì aceebil liitil nì ŋkpam min pá ŋi nì ntikakal puee, ní kí lēē mpɔɔlam kɔkɔ kí nákatí kí kpáaǹ aceebilee dicilpu, 10kii bi nín lèekī dijandi din mpèé saraau poonee. Ní usaraaŋakpil ń cáá wà ŋŋmi saraawɔkaa faŋŋu pu. 11Ama dinabilee gbaŋŋu nì di-nanti kɔkɔ nì di-yil nì di-yakaŋ nì di-binti kɔkɔee, 12an dàkà yii dinabilee nanti tin pée kíǹee kɔkɔee, ú cáá nyāntí dinaapaal kpaanceetiŋu mpaan ŋun pu bi féeń ŋkpam min bi wùn̄ee fantamee ní kí dūú wà ŋŋmi idɔ pu. Difantancundee pu ní bí dūú wà ŋŋmi.»
b. Samaa kɔkɔ saraau
13«An yaa sá Isirayeel nikitil kɔkɔ di yaa kaa nyí ní ki yīntì ki ŋá tin ti-Dindaan marab nee kansikin ubɔ bí yii bí taa ŋée, bi fōō dibɔkpil. 14Boonee bi yaa láa béè ikpiti in bi ŋée, samaa kɔkɔ ń cáań dinabil kí ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau. Bí cáań-dì circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu, 15ní bitindaŋkpilib ń dū bi-ŋalii kí páań dinabilee yil pu ní bi-kansikin ubɔ ń làntì-dì ti-Dindaan nimbiin niin. 16Usaraaŋakpil ń yòon̄ dinabilee fatikuu kí cáá kɔ́ǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu poon. 17Ú dū u-ŋambiki kí sēē fatiku kí dūú yàaǹ ŋŋaabu ŋun bi dūu pītì ki yākatì circir páaa nì circir laŋkee pu ŋfunyɔm miluli. 18Ú bàtī fatikuee kí ŋmìtī nsaraafan ŋun pu bi tùutī talaalub ŋu bí circir kɔŋkooŋŋun, ti-Dindaan nimbiinee yiŋyi pu. Ú dū fatiku un kíǹee kɔkɔ kí kpáatí kí pɔ̀l̄ saraawɔkaa faŋŋu ŋun bí circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpuee taapu. 19Ú lēē dinabilee kpam kɔkɔ kí cáá wà nsaraafan pu. 20Kii usaraaŋakpil nín ŋá úǹ u-ba kpitii pɔ̄tam saraau nabil puee, míǹ mbaantiim ní u máaǹ kí ŋá dinabil dinee mun. Ní usaraaŋakpil ń ŋá Isirayeel yab pu dikoobil din u máaǹ kí ŋée ní bí ká bi-kpitii pɔ̄tam. 21Míǹ boonee ní ú yòon̄ dinabilee nanti tin kíǹee kɔkɔ kí cáá nyāntí dinaapaal kpaanceetiŋu ní kí dū-tì kí wà ŋŋmi kii u nín wùn̄ dinabipeepeekaalee puee. Samaa kɔkɔ kpitii pɔ̄tam saraau dee.»
c. Dibɔtibil saraau
22«An yaa sá dibɔtibil diba di yaa kaa nyí ní ki yīntì ki ŋá tin ti-Dindaan u-Nimbɔtiu marab nee kansikin ubɔ bí yii bí taa ŋée, udaan fōō dibɔkpil. 23U yaa láa béè ikpiti in u ŋée, ú cáań uŋɔja un laaba kaa wɔ̀b̄ee kí ŋá saraa. 24Ú dū u-ŋal kí páań uŋɔjee yil pu ní kí làntì-u laakin bi làntī saraawɔkaa waŋkuti ti-Dindaan nimbiinee. Ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau dee. 25Usaraaŋal ń dū u-ŋambiki kí sēē uŋɔjee fatikuu kí dūú ŋmìtī saraawɔkaa faŋŋu yiŋyi pu. Ú dū fatiku un kíǹee kɔkɔ kí kpáatí kí pɔ̀l̄ saraawɔkaa faŋŋu taapu. 26Ní ú wà ŋkpam kɔkɔ nsaraafan pu kii bi nín ŋáań mpèé saraau kpam puee. Ní usaraaŋal ń ŋá dibɔtibilee pu dikoobil din u máaǹ kí ŋée ní dí ká di-kpitii pɔ̄tam.
d. Unifantanti saraau
27«An yaa sá unifantanti ubɔ di kaa nyí ní ki yīntì ki ŋá tin ti-Dindaan marab nee kansikin ubɔ bí yii bí taa ŋée, udaan fōō dibɔkpil. 28U yaa láa béè ikpiti in u ŋée, ú cáań uŋɔsal un laaba kaa wɔ̀b̄ee kí ŋá saraa u-kpitii gbanti pu. 29Ú dū u-ŋal kí páań uŋɔsal un u cáań kí ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraauee yil pu ní kí làntì-u laakin bi làntī saraawɔkaa waŋkutee. 30Usaraaŋal ń dū u-ŋambiki kí sēē uŋɔsalee fatikuu kí dūú ŋmìtī saraawɔkaa faŋŋu yiŋyi pu. Ú dū fatiku un kíǹee kɔkɔ kí kpáatí kí pɔ̀l̄ saraawɔkaa faŋŋu taapu. 31Ú lēē ŋkpam kɔkɔ kii bi nín lèekī mpèé saraau kpam puee kí cáá wà nsaraafan pu, ní u-sɔnsɔfiŋu ń sɔ̀ŋkì ti-Dindaan pɔbil. Míǹ ní usaraaŋal máaǹ kí ŋá ní kí fíntí udaan kpitii ní ú nín ká u-kpitii pɔ̄tam.
32«An yaa sá upii ní udaan cáań kí ŋá u-kpitii pɔ̄tam saraauee, ú nīn sá upisal un laaba kaa wɔ̀b̄ee. 33Ú dū u-ŋal kí páań upisalee yil pu ní kí làntì-u laakin bi làntī saraawɔkaa waŋkutee. 34Usaraaŋal ń dū u-ŋambiki kí sēē upisalee fatikuu ní kí dūú ŋmìtī saraawɔkaa faŋŋu yiŋyi pu ní kí dū fatiku un kíǹee kɔkɔ kí kpáatí kí pɔ̀l̄ saraawɔkaa faŋŋu taapu. 35Ú lēē upisalee kpam kɔkɔ kii bi nín lèekī mpèé saraau pibil kpam puee, ní usaraaŋal ń cáá wà ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu nì saraabi bin kɔkɔ sá bí dùú wà ŋŋmi kí tīī ti-Dindaanee. Usaraaŋal ń ŋá udaan pu dikoobil din u máaǹ kí ŋée ní ú ká u-kpitii pɔ̄tam.»

english_text:
The Lord said:
1If you refuse to testify in court about something you saw or know has happened, you have sinned and can be punished.
2You are guilty and unfit to worship me, if you accidentally touch the dead body of any kind of unclean animal.
3You are guilty if you find out that you have accidentally touched anything unclean that comes from a human body.
4You are guilty the moment you realize that you have made a hasty promise to do something good or bad.
5As soon as you discover that you have committed any of these sins, you must confess what you have done. 6Then you must bring a female sheep or goat to me as the price for your sin. A priest will sacrifice the animal, and you will be forgiven.
7If you are poor and cannot afford to bring an animal, you may bring two doves or two pigeons. One of these will be a sacrifice to ask my forgiveness, and the other will be a sacrifice to please me.
8Give both birds to the priest, who will offer one as a sacrifice to ask my forgiveness. He will wring its neck without tearing off its head, 9splatter some of its blood on one side of the bronze altar, and drain out the rest at the foot of the altar. 10Then he will follow the proper rules for offering the other bird as a sacrifice to please me.
You will be forgiven when the priest offers these sacrifices as the price for your sin.
11If you are so poor that you cannot afford doves or pigeons, you may bring one kilogram of your finest flour. This is a sacrifice to ask my forgiveness, so don't sprinkle olive oil or sweet-smelling incense on it. 12Give the flour to a priest, who will scoop up a handful and send it up in smoke together with the other offerings. This is a reminder that all of the flour belongs to me. 13By offering this sacrifice, the priest pays the price for any of these sins you may have committed. The priest gets to keep the rest of the flour, just as he does with grain sacrifices.
Sacrifices To Make Things Right
(Leviticus 7.1-10)
14-15The Lord told Moses what the people must do to make things right when they find out they have cheated the Lord without meaning to:
If this happens, you must either sacrifice a ram that has nothing wrong with it or else pay the price of a ram with the official money used by the priests. 16In addition, you must pay what you owe plus a fine of 20 percent. Then the priest will offer the ram as a sacrifice to make things right, and you will be forgiven.
17-19If you break any of my commands without meaning to, you are still guilty, and you can be punished. When you realize what you have done, you must either bring to the priest a ram that has nothing wrong with it or else pay him for one. The priest will then offer it as a sacrifice to make things right, and you will be forgiven.
translation_text:
ee. Tibɔŋmantikaal tiba
1«Bi yaa bíi sòoǹ tibɔti ní ubɔ ká tibɔtee nín jítì puee ní bi yíiń udaan ú dāá sòoǹ tin u kée, ní u yaa yíì kaa cūtèe, udaan ŋá ikpiti ki fōō dibɔkpil.
2«Ubɔ yaa kaa nyí ní ki gbēē tiwan tin kaa bí circiree kansikin kubɔ, an yaa sá upeel àá kuwaŋkuluu kun kaa bí circiree kubɔ di yaa kpíì àá tin fù ti-pool puee kubɔ di yaa kpíì ní u gbēēyee, u kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi ní ki fōō dibɔkpil.
3«Ubɔ yaa tí gbēē unil jɔkɔnti, àá tin kamaa pée kɔ̄ntí unil tijɔkɔndee kaa kpáàa béèyee, bi yaa láa pée tùkū-u ní u béèyee, udaan fōō dibɔkpil.
4«Àá ubɔ yaa bíi sòoǹ ní u-nyɔkɔ ŋmátì-u ní u pūtì kí ŋá tikpitil àá tiŋan ní boonee ki dāa béèyee, udaan fōō dibɔkpil.
5«Ubɔ yaa ŋá ikpiti nee kansikin ibee, udaan máaǹ kí bìitī u-kpitii gbanti pu. 6Míǹ boonee, u máaǹ kí cáań upisal àá uŋɔsal kí ŋá saraa kí tīī ti-Dindaan kí ŋāŋkì u-bɔkpil. Ní usaraaŋal ń ŋá udaan pu dikoobil din u máaǹ kí ŋá ní ú ká u-kpitii pɔ̄tamee.»
f. Biwɔfib saraau
7«Ubɔ ŋaan yaa kaa nyìm̀ ú dā upii àá uŋoobuee, u ŋūǹ kí cáań nnanjilimu muli àá abeenanjil ali kí ŋāŋkì u-bɔkpil. Ú dū diba kí ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau ní kí dū din kíǹee kí ŋá saraawɔkaa. 8Ú cáań kí tīī usaraaŋal ní úǹ ń lēē unoon un sá bí dūú ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraauee, ní kí míkí kí gíí u-sil kí nákáǹ u-kpaŋkpantaapu, ama ní diyil ń taa tùkutī. 9Usaraaŋal ń dū fatiku kí còol̀ nsaraafan kpiŋŋi pu ní kí dū un kíǹee kí kpáatí kí pɔ̀l̄ nsaraafan taapu. Ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau dee. 10Míǹ boonee, ú dū unoon un kíǹee kí ŋá saraawɔkaa kii mara nín sá puee. Ní usaraaŋal ń ŋá udaan pu dikoobil din u máaǹ kí ŋée ní ú ká u-kpitii pɔ̄tam.
11«U yaa kaa tí cáá nnanjilimu muli àá abeenanjil alee, u ŋūǹ kí cáań ŋyim kiiloobi bita kí ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau. Ama ú taa dū ŋkpam nì talaalutuukaa kí kūtì, kun puee an sá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau ní. 12Ú cáań kí tīī usaraaŋal ní úǹ ń yáfí diŋaŋkul din sá kudaaŋŋu ti-Dindaan nimbiin yii úǹ di yì saraa gbantee, ní kí dūú wà nsaraafan pu kí kpáaǹ saraabi bin bi dùú wà ŋŋmi kí tīī ti-Dindaanee. Ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau dee. 13Ní usaraaŋal ń ŋá udaan pu dikoobil din u máaǹ kí ŋée ní ú ká u-kpitii pɔ̄tam.
«Usaraaŋal ń ŋá saraa nee kii bi nín ŋáań tijimpin saraau puee.»
g. Dibɔkpil saraau
14Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii:
15«Ubɔ yaa kaa nyí ní ki dū saraabi bin sá ki tīī ti-Dindaanee ki ŋá min kaa kítèe ní ki kɔ́ diyìntilinee, udaan máaǹ kí cáań upìja un laaba kaa wɔ̀b̄ee. Ú lēē upìja gbanti u-picaŋkpuŋkun, u-daaku ń nīn nóó nì circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nimbiliŋ ŋmàntitam kí cáań kí ŋá saraa kí ŋāŋkì u nín yīntiǹ ti-Dindaan puee. 16Udaan nín bàà máaǹ kí cáań tin circir kɔŋkooŋŋun ní kaa cáańee, ú téeǹ míǹ ní kí kūtì bi yaa yākatì tin u cáańee miŋmoo puee diba pu. Ní usaraaŋal ń fōō upìjee kí ŋá udaan pu dikoobil din u máaǹ kí ŋée ní ú ká u-kpitii pɔ̄tam.
17«Ubɔ yaa kaa nyí ní ki yīntì ki ŋá tin ti-Dindaan marab nee kansikin ubɔ bí yii bí taa ŋée, udaan ŋá ikpiti ki fōō dibɔkpil. 18Udaan máaǹ kí cáań upìja un laaba kaa wɔ̀b̄ee kí tīī usaraaŋal. Ú lēē upìja gbanti u-picaŋkpuŋkun, u-daaku ń nīn nóó nì kudaau kun bi síiǹ dibɔkpil saraauee. Usaraaŋal ń ŋá udaan pu dikoobil din u máaǹ kí ŋée ní ú ká u-kpitii in waa nyí ki ŋée pɔ̄tam. 19An sá saraa un ŋáŋkí dibɔkpilee ní, di sá yii unilee nìn baasii fōō dibɔkpil ní ti-Dindaan nimbiin.»
20Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii:
21«Ubɔ yaa kaa síl̀ nì ti-Dindaan deedee, ki yaa mɔ́ntì u-nabiki tiwan tin u dūu kpāaǹ-uee pu àá tiwan tin u pīnnèe àá tin u yùn̄ u-nabikee àá tin u fìkēe. 22Tiwan tiba di yaa tí wáŋkì ní u píí ní ki bí ki néè yii waa ká kudɔŋu àá u yaa pūtì fám kí ŋmā kí bìin̄ ikpiti iba puee, 23u ŋá ikpiti ki fōō dibɔkpil. U máaǹ kí téeǹ tin u yùn̄ee àá tin u fìkēe àá tin bi kpāaǹ-uee àá tin u pííyee, 24àá tiwan tin pu ní u pée pūtì fám yii waa kée. U máaǹ kí téeǹ tiwan tin u yōoǹee kɔkɔ ní kí gíti nyàab̀ tiwan gbanti yaa yākatì miŋmoo puee diba pu kí kūtì kí tīī uwandaan ŋwiin ŋun u yaa béè yii u ŋá ikpitee. 25Míǹ boonee ní ú cáań upìja un laaba kaa wɔ̀b̄ee kí nóó nì dibɔkpil saraau daaku kí tīī usaraaŋal ní úǹ ń dūú ŋá saraa kí tīī ti-Dindaan. 26Usaraaŋal ń ŋá udaan pu dikoobil din u máaǹ kí ŋée ti-Dindaan nimbiin ní ú ká u-kpitii in ní u ŋá ki fōō dibɔkpilee pɔ̄tam.»

english_text:
Other Sins That Need Sacrifices or Payments
(Numbers 5.5-10)
1-3 The Lord told Moses what the people must do when they commit other sins against the Lord:
You have sinned if you rob or cheat someone, if you keep back money or valuables left in your care, or if you find something and claim not to have it.
4When this happens, you must return what doesn't belong to you 5and pay the owner a fine of 20 percent. 6-7In addition, you must either bring to the priest a ram that has nothing wrong with it or else pay him for one. The priest will then offer it as a sacrifice to make things right, and you will be forgiven for what you did wrong.
Daily Sacrifices
(Exodus 29.38-43; Numbers 28.1-8)
8-9The Lord told Moses to tell Aaron and his sons how to offer the daily sacrifices that are sent up in smoke to please the Lord:
You must put the animal for the sacrifice on the altar in the evening and let it stay there all night. But make sure the fire keeps burning. 10The next morning you will dress in your priestly clothes, including your linen underwear. Then clean away the ashes left by the sacrifices and pile them beside the altar. 11Change into your everyday clothes, take the ashes outside the camp, and pile them in the special place.
12The fire must never go out, so put wood on it each morning. After this, you are to lay an animal on the altar next to the fat that you sacrifice to ask my blessing. Then send it all up in smoke to me.
13The altar fire must always be kept burning—it must never go out.
Sacrifices To Give Thanks to the Lord
The Lord said:
14When someone offers a sacrifice to give thanks to me, the priests from Aaron's family must bring it to the front of the bronze altar, 15where one of them will scoop up a handful of the flour and oil, together with all the incense on it. Then, to show that the whole offering belongs to me, he will lay all of this on the altar and send it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me. 16-17The rest of it is to be baked without yeast and eaten by the priests in the sacred courtyard of the sacred tent. This bread is very holy, just like the sacrifices for sin or the sacrifices for making things right, and I have given this part to the priests from what is offered to me on the altar.
18Only the men in Aaron's family are allowed to eat this bread, and they must go through a ceremony to be made holy before touching it. This law will never change.
When Priests Are Ordained
19The Lord spoke to Moses 20and told him what sacrifices the priests must offer on the morning and evening of the day they are ordained:
It is the same as the regular morning and evening sacrifices—half a kilogram of flour 21mixed with olive oil and cooked in a shallow pan. The bread must then be crumbled into small pieces and sent up in smoke with a smell that pleases me. 22-23Each of Aaron's descendants who is ordained as a priest must perform this ceremony and make sure that the bread is completely burned on the altar. None of it may be eaten!
Sacrifices for Sin
(Leviticus 4.1,2)
24The Lord told Moses 25how the priests from Aaron's family were to offer the sacrifice for sin:
This sacrifice is very sacred, and the animal must be killed in my presence at the north side of the bronze altar. 26The priest who offers this sacrifice must eat it in the sacred courtyard of the sacred tent, 27and anyone or anything that touches the meat will be holy. If any of the animal's blood is splattered on the clothes of the priest, they must be washed in a holy place. 28If the meat was cooked in a clay pot, the pot must be destroyed, but if it was cooked in a bronze pot, the pot must be scrubbed and rinsed with water.
29This sacrifice is very holy, and only the priests may have any part of it. 30None of the meat may be eaten from the sacrifices for sin that require blood to be brought into the sacred tent. These sacrifices must be completely burned.
translation_text:
Marab bin bi síiǹ bisaraaŋaliibi ń nīn nóóyee: a. Saraawɔkaa marab
1Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii:
2«Dū saraawɔkaa marab nee kí tīī Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi.
«Saraawɔkaa marab sɔ̀. Saraawɔkaa pée máaǹ kí nīn pá nsaraafan pu ki wù míǹ kunyeeu kɔkɔ ní áli kutaa ń wúntí, ŋŋmi kaa máaǹ kí kpú. 3Usaraaŋal ń dū iŋaapiin in bí fálfalee bɔkutikpaandi kí pèen̄, kí dū iŋaapiin in bí fálfalee cukutigiŋki mun kí lòon̄ ní kí wúkutí saraawɔkaa un bi wùn̄ nsaraafan puee kpam fantam kí bíĺ nsaraafan caŋin. 4Míǹ boonee ú kpántí u-wampeeŋkaati ní kí nyāntí ŋfantamee dinaapaal kpaanceetiŋu kí cáá fá mpaan ŋun pu bi féeń saraa fantamee. 5Ŋŋmi kaa pée máaǹ kí kpú nsaraafan pu, ŋu pée máaǹ kí nīn fòol̄ ní ŋyunti kamaa. Kutaafaau kamaayee, usaraaŋal ń nyàab̀ idɔ kí ŋá, kí dū saraawɔkaa nanti kí páań ní kí dū ŋkpam min bi lēē mpèé saraau nanti poonee kí kūtì kí wà ŋŋmi. 6Ŋŋmi pée máaǹ kí nīn wù ŋyunti kamaa nsaraafan pu ní, ŋuaa máaǹ kí kpú.»
b. Tijimpin saraau
7«Tijimpin saraau marab sɔ̀. Aarɔn jipɔmbi bisaraaŋaliibi di máaǹ kí sútí kí pìl̄ nsaraafan kí ŋá tijimpin saraau kí tīī ti-Dindaan. 8Usaraaŋal ubɔ ń yáfí ŋyim diŋaŋkul, kí dū ŋkpam kí búuń ní kí dū talaalutuukaa un bi cáańee kɔkɔ kí kūtì kí dūú wà ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu án nīn sá <kudaaŋŋu> ti-Dindaan nimbiin yii u-saraau dee. An di sá saraa un sɔnsɔfiŋu sɔ̀ŋkī ti-Dindaan pɔbilee. 9Bi nín yáfì ŋyim ki ŋá saraa min kíǹee, Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi ŋūǹ kí dūú ŋá tijin kí jī, ama bí taa ŋá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔ tijinee poon. Bí jī-tì mpaan ŋun bí circiree pu, circir kɔŋkooŋŋu cindin. 10Baa pée máaǹ kí dū ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔ kí ŋá tijin gbanti. Saraabi bin bi cáa wù ŋŋmi ki tìì-mee, dijandi din m dūu tīī-bee dee. Saraa gbantee sá circir páaa wanti ní, a lì kii ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau nì dibɔkpil saraau nín bí circir puee. 11Aarɔn maaliŋu poon bin sá bininjabee baba di ŋūǹ kí jī tijin gbanti, di sá yii saraabi bin bi cāabìń ki tìì ti-Dindaanee, dijandi din sá ki tīī-bi kí nīn pée cáa cá jaanjaanee dee. Unifantanti di yaa gbēē-tèe, udaan nì u-kpuulool dee.»
12Ní ti-Dindaan gíti bí Mooyiisi yii:
13«Daliŋkin bi yaa dū Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi ki sú ti-Dindaanee, saraa un bi máaǹ kí cáańee di sá ŋyim kiiloobi bita. Kutaafaauee bí dū dijandi kí ŋá saraa ní kujoouee bí púntí dijandi din kíǹee kí ŋá saraa. 14Bí dū ŋkpam kí búuń ŋyim kí dūú tɔ̄ kalaa kitaŋkpapiliŋ pu. Míǹ boonee bí càkà kí cáań kí ŋá saraa kí tīī ti-Dindaan ní u-sɔnsɔfiŋu ń sɔ̀ŋkì ti-Dindaan pɔbil. 15An nīn sá dibɔkpaal din làá nīn dɔ̄ ki cá jaanjaanee yii Aarɔn maaliŋunee, un yil pu bi làá sìtī ŋkpam ú kpántí usaraaŋakpilee ń ŋá saraa gbanti kí tīī ti-Dindaan. Bí dū saraa gbanti kɔkɔ kí wà ŋŋmi.
16«Usaraaŋal di yaa cáań tijimpin saraau ki ŋá ki tīī ti-Dindaanee, bí dū saraayee kɔkɔ kí wà ŋŋmi, bí taa jī.»
c. Ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau
17Ní ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii:
18«Sòoǹ nì Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi kí tùkù-bi bi nín máaǹ kí nīn ŋáań ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau puee. Bi yaa cáań kuwaŋkuluu kí ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraauee, bí làntì-ku laakin bi làntī saraawɔkaa waŋkuti ti-Dindaan nimbiinee, kun puee an sá circir páaa wanti ní. 19Usaraaŋal un di ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraauee ń ŋmɔ́ saraayee nanti mpaan ŋun bí circiree pu, circir kɔŋkooŋŋu cindin. 20Un di yaa pée gbēē saraa gbanti nantee, udaan nì u-kpuulool dee. Fatiku yaa yāaǹ dibɔkutil din puee, bí fíntí laakin fatiku yāaǹee circir paaŋŋu pu. 21Bi yaa tɔ́kɔǹ saraa gbanti nanti dikumbool din poonee, bí gbá kí wīī-dì. Ama an yaa sá tasa kumbool poon ní bi yaa tɔ́kɔǹ tinan gbantee, bí fíntí-dì tiŋan ní kí dū nnyim kí cántí-dì. 22Bininjab bin sá bisaraaŋaliibee di ŋūǹ kí ŋmɔ́ tinan gbanti, tì sá circir páaa nanti ní. 23Ama bi yaa ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau ní ki dū u-fatikuu ki kɔ́ǹ dikpafindi tantiun ki ŋá dikoobil din bi máaǹ kí ŋá kí ká ikpiti pɔ̄tamee, bí taa ŋmɔ́ saraa gbanti nanti, bí cáá wà ŋŋmi.»

english_text:
Sacrifices To Make Things Right
(Leviticus 5.14-19)
The Lord said:
1The sacrifice to make things right is very sacred. 2The animal must be killed in the same place where the sacrifice to please me is killed, and the animal's blood must be splattered against the four sides of the bronze altar. 3Offer all of the animal's fat, including the fat on its tail and on its insides, 4as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat. 5One of the priests will lay these pieces on the altar and send them up in smoke to me. 6This sacrifice for making things right is very holy. Only the priests may eat it, and they must eat it in a holy place.
7The ceremony for this sacrifice and the one for sin are the same, and the meat may be eaten only by the priest who performs this ceremony of forgiveness.
8In fact, the priest who offers a sacrifice to please me may keep the skin of the animal, 9just as he may eat the bread from a sacrifice to give thanks to me. 10All other grain sacrifices—with or without olive oil in them—are to be divided equally among the priests of Aaron's family.
Sacrifices To Ask the Lord's Blessing
The Lord said:
11Here are the instructions for offering a sacrifice to ask my blessing: 12If you offer it to give thanks, you must offer some bread together with it. Use the finest flour to make three kinds of bread without yeast—two in the form of loaves mixed with olive oil and one in the form of thin wafers brushed with oil. 13You must also make some bread with yeast. 14Give me one loaf or wafer from each of these four kinds of bread, after which they will belong to the priest who splattered the blood against the bronze altar.
15When you offer an animal to ask a blessing from me or to thank me, the meat belongs to you, but it must be eaten the same day. 16It is different with the sacrifices you offer when you make me a promise or voluntarily give me something. The meat from those sacrifices may be kept and eaten the next day, 17-18but any that is left over must be destroyed. If you eat any of it after the second day, your sacrifice will be useless and unacceptable, and you will be both disgusting and guilty.
19Don't eat any of the meat that has touched something unclean. Instead, burn it. The rest of the meat may be eaten by anyone who is clean and acceptable to me. 20-21But don't eat any of this meat if you have become unclean by touching something unclean from a human or an animal or from any other creature. If you do, you will no longer belong to the community of Israel.
22The Lord told Moses 23to say to the people:
Don't eat the fat of cattle, sheep, or goats. 24If one of your animals dies or is killed by some wild animal, you may do anything with its fat except eat it. 25If you eat the fat of an animal that can be used as a sacrifice to me, you will no longer belong to the community of Israel. 26 And no matter where you live, you must not eat the blood of any bird or animal, 27or you will no longer belong to the community of Israel.
28The Lord also told Moses 29-30to say to the people of Israel:
If you want to offer a sacrifice to ask my blessing, you must bring the part to be burned and lay it on the bronze altar. But you must first lift up the choice ribs with their fat to show that the offering is dedicated to me. 31A priest from Aaron's family will then send the fat up in smoke, but the ribs belong to the priests. 32-33The upper joint of the right hind leg is for the priest who offers the blood and the fat of the animal. 34I have decided that the people of Israel must always give the choice ribs and the upper joint of the right hind leg to Aaron's descendants 35who have been ordained as priests to serve me. 36This law will never change. I am the Lord!
37These are the ceremonies for sacrifices to please the Lord, to give him thanks, and to ask for his blessing or his forgiveness, as well as the ceremonies for those sacrifices that demand a payment and for the sacrifices that are offered when priests are ordained. 38While Moses and the people of Israel were in the desert at Mount Sinai, the Lord commanded them to start offering these sacrifices.
translation_text:
d. Dibɔkpil saraau
1«Dibɔkpil saraau bí circir páaa ní. Bi nín máaǹ kí nīn ŋáań-u puee sèé. 2Laakin bi làntī saraawɔkaa waŋkulukuee, niin ní bi máaǹ kí làntì dibɔkpil saraau waŋkuluku mun, ní bí dū fatiku kí yàaǹ nsaraafan kɔkɔ pu kí màntīí tū. 3Tin bi làá lēē kí wà ŋŋmi kí tīī ti-Dindaanee di sá dijugbindi nì ŋkpam min bīī ina puee, 4nì aceebil liitil nì ŋkpam min pá ŋi nì ntikakal puee, ní kí lēē mpɔɔlam kɔkɔ kí nákatí kí kpáaǹ aceebil dicilpu. 5Niinee ní usaraaŋal ń cáá wà ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu.
