An di sá saraa un ŋáŋkí dibɔkpilee, saraa un bi dùú wà ŋŋmi kí tīī ti-Dindaanee. 6Bisaraaŋaliibi kansikinee, bin pée sá bininjabee ŋūǹ kí ŋmɔ́ tinan gbanti, ama bí ŋmɔ́-tì mpaan ŋun bí circiree pu, kun puee tì sá circir páaa nanti ní. 7Dibɔkpil saraau nì ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau sá ubaanti ní, bi-ŋátam marau mun sá ubaanti ní. Usaraaŋal un di ŋá saraayee di yì kuwaŋkuluu kun bi dūu ŋá saraayee nanti.
ee. Usaraaŋal jandi
8«Ubɔ yaa cáań kuwaŋkuluu ki ŋá saraawɔkaayee, usaraaŋal un ŋá an saraauee di yì kuwaŋkuluuee gbaŋŋu. 9Tijin tin kɔkɔ bi pūul̀ dibubulin àá bi tɔ̄kɔntí kusɔŋun àá bi tòó kitaŋkpapiliŋ pu kí dūú ŋá saraa kí tīī ti-Dindaanee, usaraaŋal un dū saraa gbanti ki tīī ti-Dindaanee di yì. 10Tijin saraabi bin kɔkɔ kíǹ bi dū ŋkpam ki búuń àá baa búuń ŋkpamee, Aarɔn jipɔmbi kɔkɔ di yì, bí yàkatī án nīn ŋmà.»
f. Mpèé saraau
11«Mpèé saraau un bi ŋáań ki tìì ti-Dindaanee ŋátam marau sɔ̀. 12Ubɔ yaa làá ŋá mpèé saraau kí jāam̀ ti-Dindaanee, ú dū kpɔnɔb bin bi dū ŋkpam ki búuń ki púĺ ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔ kpá poonee, nì ŋkpɔnɔwaamu mun pu bi yɔ́kɔfì ŋkpam ki púĺ ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔ kpá poonee, nì kalaabi bin bi dū ŋkpam ki ŋmālim̀ ki búuńee kí kūtì ijaam saraau waŋkuluku pu. 13Míǹ boonee ní ú gíti dū kpɔnɔb bin bi ŋá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔ poon ki púĺee kí kūtì mpèé saraauee pu. 14Bí lēē kpɔnɔbee kɔkɔ pu ubɔ ubɔ kí ŋá saraa kí tīī ti-Dindaan. Kpɔnɔb gbantee, usaraaŋal un dū ijaam saraau waŋkuluku fatikuu ki yāaǹ nsaraafan jaŋŋi puee di yì. 15Bí ŋmɔ́ mpèé saraau un bi ŋá ki jáam̀ ti-Dindaanee nanti ŋwiin ŋun bi ŋá saraa gbantee, tí taa wúntí kutaa.
16«Ama an yaa sá ipoon saraau àá nlammɔntiim saraau nantee, bi ŋūǹ kí ŋmɔ́-tì ŋwiin ŋun bi ŋá saraa gbantee nì ŋwinliliiti dal. 17Ama tin yaa kíǹ winta dalee, bí wà-tì ŋŋmi. 18Ubɔ yaa ŋmɔ́ mpèé saraau nanti winta dalee, ti-Dindaan kaa làá fōō un cáań saraa gbantee saraau. Udaan ŋman ŋá saraa gbanti fám dee, di sá yii tinan gbantee bíil̀. Un ŋmɔ́ tinan gbantee fōō dibɔkpil ní ki làá túń u-yìntitam tafadaaldi. 19Tinan yaa gbēē tiwan tin kɔ́ tijɔkɔndee, bí taa ŋmɔ́-tì, bí dū-tì kí wà ŋŋmi.
«Unil un kamaa pée bí circiree ŋūǹ kí ŋmɔ́ saraa nanti. 20Ama ubɔ yaa bí tijɔkɔndin ní ki ŋmɔ́ tinan tin bi dūu ŋá saraa ki tīī ti-Dindaanee, bí nyāntí udaan Isirayeel nibul kansikin. 21Míǹ mbaantiim un di yaa gbēē tin bí tijɔkɔndinee, an dàkà yii tin kɔ̄ntí unil tijɔkɔndee àá kuwaŋkuluu kun kòóyee àá tin fù ti-pool pu bi kòóyee, ní ki yaa ŋmɔ́ mpèé saraau nantee, bí nyāntí-u Isirayeel nibul kansikin.»
g. Samaa marau
22Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi 23ń tùkù Isirayeel yab yii:
«Ní taa ŋmɔ́ unaa àá upii àá uŋoobu kpam. 24Ni ŋūǹ kí dū tiwaŋkuti tin kpíìyee àá tin ní an cúúyee kpam kí ŋá tiba, ama ní taa ŋmɔ́-mì. 25Ubɔ yaa ŋmɔ́ kuwaŋkuluu kpam min bàà sá bí dūú wà ŋŋmi kí tīī ti-Dindaanee, bí nyāntí-u Isirayeel nibul kansikin. 26Báà laakin kamaa ní ni yaa bàn̄ ki kóòyee, ní taa ŋmɔ́ kinɔmbiki àá kuwaŋkuluu kubɔ fatikuu. 27Un yaa ŋmɔ́ fatikuee, bí nyāntí-u Isirayeel nibul kansikin.»
28Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi 29ń tùkù Isirayeel yab yii:
«Ubɔ yaa cáań mpèé saraau kí tīī ti-Dindaanee, ú lēē dijandi din sá ti-Dindaan yalee. 30Úǹ u-ba ń cáań dijandi gbanti, an dàkà yii ŋkpam nì dibindi, ní kí yòon̄ dibindi gbanti yilpu kí fíiǹ fíiǹ ti-Dindaan nimbiin niin. 31Niinee usaraaŋal ń fōō ŋkpamee kí cáá wà ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu. Ama dibindee, Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi di yì. 32Ní lēē mpèé saraau waŋkuluku diŋaŋgiitaal kí tīī usaraaŋal. 33Aarɔn jipɔmbi kansikin un cūnnì mpèé saraau waŋkuluku fatikuu nì ku-kpam nsaraafan puee di yì diŋaŋgiitaal gbanti. 34Isirayeel yab saraabi bin bi ŋáań an sá mpèé saraabee poonee, m lēē dibindi din bi fīintí fīintí m-nimbiinee nì diŋaŋgiitaal ki tīī usaraaŋakpil Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi. Tin Isirayeel yab máaǹ kí nīn tìì bisaraaŋaliibi kí nīn pée cáa cá jaanjaanee dee.»
35Daliŋkin ti-Dindaan nìn kāaǹ Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi bí nīn sá bisaraaŋaliibee, dijandi din bi nìn lēē ki tīī-bi ti-Dindaan saraabi bin bi nìn cāabìń ki wù ŋŋmi ki tìì-uee poonee dee. 36Ŋwiin gbanti ní ti-Dindaan yóoǹ Isirayeel yab yii bí nīn tìì Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi saraabi jandi gbanti. Án nīn sá dibɔkpaal ki tīī Isirayeel yab kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaan.
37Bi nín máaǹ kí nīn ŋáań saraawɔkaa nì tijimpin saraau nì ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau nì dibɔkpil saraau nì bi yaa làá kàan̄ bisaraaŋaliibee saraau nì mpèé saraau puee dee. 38Ti-Dindaan di nìn dū marab gbanti ki tīī Mooyiisi Siinaayi jool pu, kuteeun, ŋwiin ŋun u nìn bālifì Isirayeel yab yii bí cáań-u bi-saraabee.

english_text:
The Ceremony for Ordaining Priests
(Exodus 29.1-37)
1The Lord said to Moses:
2Send for Aaron and his sons, as well as their priestly clothes, the oil for ordination, the bull for the sin offering, the two rams, and a basket of bread made without yeast. 3Then bring the whole community of Israel together at the entrance to the sacred tent.
4Moses obeyed the Lord, and when everyone had come together, 5he said, “We are here to follow the Lord's instructions.”
6After Moses told Aaron and his sons to step forward, he told them to wash themselves. 7He put the priestly shirt and robe on Aaron and wrapped the sash around his waist. Then he put the sacred vest on Aaron and fastened it with the finely woven belt. 8Next, he put on Aaron the sacred breastpiece that was used in finding out what the Lord wanted his people to do. 9He placed the turban on Aaron's head, and on the front of the turban was the narrow strip of thin gold as a sign of his dedication to the Lord.
10Moses then dedicated the sacred tent and everything in it to the Lord by sprinkling them with some of the oil for ordination. 11He sprinkled the bronze altar seven times, and he sprinkled its equipment, as well as the large bronze bowl and its base. 12He also poured some of the oil on Aaron's head to dedicate him to the Lord. 13Next, Moses dressed Aaron's sons in their shirts, then tied sashes around them and put special caps on them, just as the Lord had commanded.
14Moses led out the bull that was to be sacrificed for sin, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head. 15After it was killed, Moses dipped a finger in the blood and smeared some of it on each of the four corners of the bronze altar, before pouring out the rest at the foot of the altar. This purified the altar and made it a fit place for offering the sacrifice for sin. 16Moses then took the fat on the bull's insides, as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat, and sent them up in smoke on the altar fire. 17Finally, he took the skin and the flesh of the bull, together with the food still in its stomach, and burned them outside the camp, just as the Lord had commanded.
18Moses led out the ram for the sacrifice to please the Lord. After Aaron and his sons had laid their hands on its head, 19Moses killed the ram and splattered its blood against the four sides of the altar. 20-21Moses had the animal cut up, and he washed its insides and hind legs. Then he laid the head, the fat, and the rest of the ram on the altar and sent them up in smoke with a smell that pleased the Lord. All this was done just as the Lord had commanded.
22Moses led out the ram for the ceremony of ordination. Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head, 23and it was killed. Moses smeared some of its blood on Aaron's right earlobe, some on his right thumb, and some on the big toe of his right foot. 24Moses did the same thing for Aaron's sons, before splattering the rest of the blood against the four sides of the altar. 25He took the animal's fat tail, the fat on its insides, and the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat, and the right hind leg. 26Then he took from a basket some of each of the three kinds of bread that had been made without yeast and had been dedicated to the Lord.
27Moses placed the bread on top of the meat and gave it all to Aaron and his sons, who lifted it up to show that it was dedicated to the Lord. 28After this, Moses placed it on the fires of the altar and sent it up in smoke with a smell that pleased the Lord. This was part of the ordination ceremony. 29Moses lifted up the choice ribs of the ram to show that they were dedicated to the Lord. This was the part that the Lord had said Moses could have.
30Finally, Moses sprinkled the priestly clothes of Aaron and his sons with some of the oil for ordination and with some of the blood from the altar. So Aaron and his sons, together with their priestly clothes, were dedicated to the Lord.
31Moses said to Aaron and his sons:
The Lord told me that you must boil this meat at the entrance to the sacred tent and eat it there with the bread. 32Burn what is left over 33and stay near the entrance to the sacred tent until the ordination ceremony ends seven days from now. 34We have obeyed the Lord in everything that has been done today, so that your sins may be forgiven. 35The Lord has told me that you must stay near the entrance to the tent for seven days and nights, or else you will die.
36Aaron and his sons obeyed everything that the Lord had told Moses they must do.
translation_text:
BI DŪ BISARAAŊALIIBI KI SÚ UNIMBƆTI
Bi dū Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi ki sú Unimbɔti
1Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: 2«Yíiń Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi, kí cáań asaraaŋabɔkuti nì ŋkpam nì ikpiti pɔ̄tam nabil nì ipijaa ili nì kpɔnɔb bin baa ŋá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee an nīn kā kukabikun. 3Míǹ boonee á yíiń samaa kɔkɔ ń kpāfì circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu.»
4Ní Mooyiisi ŋá ti-Dindaan nín bí yii ú ŋá puee ní samaa kɔkɔ kóoǹ ki kpáfì circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu. 5Niinee ní Mooyiisi bí samaa yii: «Kpèèmaan ti-Dindaan nín bí yii tí ŋá puee sɔ̀.» 6Ní Mooyiisi cáań Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi nyɔkɔpu ki yāntì bi fùl̄ nnyim kí nyā kí nīn bí circir. 7U nìn dū poon bɔkutil ki pēeǹ Aarɔn ní ki dū ŋŋaabu dambalau ki gbìn̄-u, ní ki dū dibɔkutifɔkɔl mun ki pēeǹ-u, ní ki dū eefoodi ki léeǹ-u, ní ki dū dambala un kā eefoodi puee ki cúú u-caŋ. 8U nìn dū kilɔbiki kin pāantí usaraaŋakpil bindi puee ki páaǹ-u ní ki dū Uriim nì Tumiim ki ŋá kilɔbikee poon. 9U nìn dū ŋŋaabu ki fìn̄ u-yil ní ki dū sindaariya un bi nyūntì ki nántiǹ mpumpukumee ki nákáǹ nyɔkɔpu kí dàkà yii bi dū-u ki sú disaraaŋal tundi, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tùkū Mooyiisi yii ú ŋá puee. 10Mooyiisi yōoǹ ŋkpam ní ki bātì ki yāaǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu pu nì tin kɔkɔ bí ŋu-poonee ní ki dū tiwanee kɔkɔ ki sú ti-Dindaan. 11U nìn dū ŋkpamee ki yāaǹ nsaraafan pu ŋfunyɔm miluli ní ki bātì ki sītì nsaraafan pu nì tin kɔkɔ bi cáa tūǹ ŋu-pu ditundee nì kusampeeu nì kun pu ku tɔ́kɔ́ee ki dū an wantee kɔkɔ ki sú ti-Dindaan. 12U ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki bātì ŋkpamee ki sītì Aarɔn yil pu ki dū-u ki sú ti-Dindaan. 13Míǹ boonee ní Mooyiisi yāntì Aarɔn jipɔmbi mun sútì ki pìl̄-u ní u dū bi-bɔkutiŋ ki pēeǹ-bi ní ki dū dambalab ki gbìn̄-bi ní ki dū iŋaabu ki fìn̄ bi-yiliŋ kii ti-Dindaan nín bí yii ú ŋá puee.
14U dóòyee ní ki dātìń dinabil din bi làá dūú ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraauee ki cáań, ní Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi dū bi-ŋalii ki páaǹ di-yil pu. 15Ní Mooyiisi lāntì-dì ní ki dū u-ŋambiki ki sēē fatiku ki dūu jōō nsaraafan yiŋyi pu ki māntìi tú ki ŋá-ŋu circir. U nìn dū fatiku un kíǹee ki kpáatìi pɔ̀l̄ nsaraafanee taapu. Míǹ ní u ŋá ní ki dū nsaraafan ki sú Unimbɔti, bí nīn ŋáań ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau ŋu-pu. 16Mooyiisi yōoǹ ŋkpam min kɔkɔ bīī ina puee nì mpɔɔlam nì aceebil liitil nì ŋkpam min bīī ŋi-puee ki cáa wùn̄ ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu. 17Ama bi yōoǹ dinabilee gbaŋŋu nì di-nanti nì di-bintee kɔkɔ ki cáa wùn̄ ŋŋmi dinaapaal kpaanceetiŋu kii ti-Dindaan nín kpáafì Mooyiisi yii ú ŋá puee.
18Niinee ní Mooyiisi tí dātì upìja un bi làá dūú ŋá saraawɔkaayee ki cáań ní Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi dū bi-ŋalii ki páaǹ u-yil pu. 19Ní Mooyiisi lāntì-u ní ki dū fatiku ki yāaǹ nsaraafan kɔkɔ pu ki māntìi tú. 20Mooyiisi càkā upìjee nanti ní ki dū diyil nì ŋkpam ki dūu kútì ki wùn̄ ŋŋmi. 21U dū nnyim ki fíntì ina nì ayaka ní ki dū upìjee nanti tin kíǹee kɔkɔ ki kútì ki dūu wùn̄ ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu ki ŋá saraawɔkaa, ní saraayee sɔnsɔfiŋu sɔ̄ŋkì ti-Dindaan pɔbil kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn kpáafì-u yii ú ŋá puee.
22Míǹ boonee ní u dātì upìjaliliiti ki cáań bí dūú ŋá saraa, bisaraaŋaliibi ń kíĺ bi-saraaŋatundi, ní Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi dū bi-ŋalii ki páaǹ upìjee yil pu. 23Ní Mooyiisi lāntì-u ní ki dū fatiku ki jōō Aarɔn tafalam ŋgiil yal pu nì u-ŋambijal ŋgiil yal pu nì u-taŋambijal ŋgiil yal pu. 24Boonee ní Mooyiisi yāntì Aarɔn jipɔmbi sútì ki pìl̄-u ní u dū fatiku ki jōō bi-tafalam ŋgiil yaŋ pu nì bi-ŋambijaliŋ ŋgiil yaŋ pu nì bi-taŋambijaliŋ ŋgiil yaŋ pu ní ki dū fatiku un kíǹee ki kpáatìi pɔ̀l̄ nsaraafan ki māntìi tú. 25Mooyiisi lēē ŋkpam nì dijugbindi nì ŋkpam min bīī ina puee nì mpɔɔlam nì aceebil liitil nì ŋkpam min bīī ŋi-puee nì diŋaŋgiitaal. 26Kikabiki kiba nìn yú niin bi dū-kì ki sú ti-Dindaan. Kpɔnɔb bin baa ŋá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee nìn kā poon. U nìn lēē kpɔnɔb bin bi dū ŋkpam ki búuń ki púĺ ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔ kpá poonee ubɔ, nì ŋkpɔnɔwaamu mun pu bi yɔ́kɔfì ŋkpam ki púĺ ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔ kpá poonee ubɔ, nì kalaabi bin bi dū ŋkpam ki ŋmālim̀ ki búuńee ubɔ. U nìn dū kɔkɔ ki páaǹ upìjee kpam nì u-ŋaŋgiitaal pu. 27Ní Mooyiisi dūu ŋúbiǹ Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi ní bi dúkutì yilpu ki fíiǹ fíiǹ ti-Dindaan nimbiin. 28Bi ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee ní Mooyiisi fātìi fōō bi-ŋaan ki dūu páaǹ saraawɔkaa un pá nsaraafan puee ki wùn̄ ŋŋmi. Míǹ ní bi nìn ŋá saraabi ní bisaraaŋaliibi kíĺ bi-tundi, ní saraayee sɔnsɔfiŋu nìn sɔ̄ŋkì ti-Dindaan pɔbil. 29Mooyiisi nìn yōoǹ upìjee bindi, ki dúkutì yilpu ní ki fíiǹ fíiǹ ti-Dindaan nimbiin. Dijandi gbanti ní bi nìn dūu tīī Mooyiisi kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn síiǹ-u mara puee.
30Niinee Mooyiisi yōoǹ ŋkpam nì fatiku un nìn bí nsaraafan puee ki dūu yāaǹ Aarɔn nì u-wampeeŋkaati pu nì u-jipɔmbi mun nì bi-wampeeŋkaati pu. Míǹ ní u ŋá ki dū Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi nì bi-wampeeŋkaati kɔkɔ ki sú ti-Dindaan.
31Niinee ní Mooyiisi bí Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi yii: «Tɔ́kɔḿmaan tinan dikpafindi tantiu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu. Ni yaa tɔ́kɔǹ-tèe, ní ŋmɔ́-tì niin nì kpɔnɔb bin kā kikabikin bi cáań ki ŋá saraayee kii m nín nìn tīī-si mara ki lī yii: <Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi di làá ŋmɔ́-tèe.> 32Tinan nì kpɔnɔb bin ni ŋmɔ́ an kíǹee, ní dūú wà ŋŋmi. 33Naa máaǹ kí yīkì circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu kí cáá sāā iwiin iluli dal. Naa máaǹ kí nyā áli iwiin iluli in bi síiǹ kí dūú ŋá saraabi ní kíĺ disaraaŋal tundee ń kúntí. 34Kii ti nín ŋá pu díǹ nee, ti-Dindaan u-ba di síiǹ mara yii tí ŋá míǹ ní ní ká ni-kpitii pɔ̄tam. 35Ni máaǹ kí nīn bí circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu kí cáá sāā iwiin iluli. Mimmee ni ŋūǹ kí tɔ̄ ti-Dindaan tundi kí taa kpú. Ti-Dindaan nín kpáafì-mi yii ḿ ŋá puee dee.»
36Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi ŋá tin kɔkɔ ti-Dindaan dī Mooyiisi pu ki síiǹ-bi yii bí ŋée deedee.

english_text:
The First Sacrifices Offered by Aaron and His Sons
1Eight days later Moses called together Aaron, his sons, and Israel's leaders. 2Then he said to Aaron:
Find a young bull and a ram that have nothing wrong with them. Offer the bull to the Lord as a sacrifice for sin and the ram as a sacrifice to please him.
3Tell the people of Israel that they must offer sacrifices as well. They must offer a goat as a sacrifice for sin, and a bull and a ram as a sacrifice to please the Lord. The bull and the ram must be a year old and have nothing wrong with them. 4Then the people must offer a bull and a ram as a sacrifice to ask the Lord's blessing and also a grain sacrifice mixed with oil. Do this, because the Lord will appear to you today.
5After the animals and the grain had been brought to the front of the sacred tent, and the people were standing there in the presence of the Lord, 6Moses said:
The Lord has ordered you to do this, so that he may appear to you in all of his glory. 7 Aaron, step up to the altar and offer the sacrifice to please the Lord, then offer the sacrifices for the forgiveness of your sins and for the sins of the people, just as the Lord has commanded.
8Aaron stepped up to the altar and killed the bull that was to be the sacrifice for his sins. 9His sons brought him the blood. He dipped a finger in it, smeared some on the four corners of the bronze altar, and poured out the rest at its foot. 10But he sent up in smoke the fat, the kidneys, and the lower part of the liver, just as the Lord had commanded Moses. 11Then Aaron burned the skin and the flesh outside the camp.
12After Aaron had killed the ram that was sacrificed to please the Lord, Aaron's sons brought him the blood, and he splattered it against all four sides of the altar. 13They brought him each piece of the animal, including the head, and he burned them all on the altar. 14He washed the insides and the hind legs and also sent them up in smoke.
15Next, Aaron sacrificed the goat for the sins of the people, as he had done with the sacrifice for his own sins. 16And so, he burned this sacrifice on the altar in the proper way. 17He also presented the grain sacrifice and burned a handful of the flour on the altar as part of the morning sacrifice.
18 Finally, he killed the bull and the ram as a sacrifice to ask the Lord's blessing on the people. Aaron's sons brought him the blood, and he splattered it against the four sides of the altar. 19His sons placed all the fat, as well as the kidneys and the lower part of the liver 20on top of the choice ribs. 21Then Aaron burned the fat on the altar and lifted up the ribs and the right hind leg to show that these were dedicated to the Lord. This was done just as the Lord had instructed Moses.
22 Aaron held out his hand and gave the people his blessing, before coming down from the bronze altar where he had offered the sacrifices. 23He and Moses went into the sacred tent, and when they came out, they gave the people their blessing. Then the Lord appeared to the people in all of his glory. 24The Lord sent fiery flames that burned up everything on the altar, and when everyone saw this, they shouted and fell to their knees to worship the Lord.
translation_text:
Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi saraapeepeekaabi bɔti
1Ŋwinniniiti dalee ní Mooyiisi yíiń Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi nì Isirayeel yab kpilib. 2U nìn bí Aarɔn yii: «Nyàab̀ dinabil kí dūú ŋá a-kpitii pɔ̄tam saraau nì upìja kí dūú ŋá a-saraawɔkaau. Tiwaŋkutee liitil laaba ń taa nīn wɔ̀b̄ ní á cáań-tì ti-Dindaan nimbiin. 3Míǹ boonee á tùkù Isirayeel yab bí cáań uŋɔja kí dūú ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau nì dinabil din cáá dibindi dibee nì dipibil din cáá dibindi dibee ŋi-laaba ń taa nīn wɔ̀b̄ bí dūú ŋá saraawɔkaa. 4Bí cáań unaja nì upìja kí ŋá mpèé saraau kí tīī ti-Dindaan, ní kí dū ŋyim min bi dū ŋkpam ki búuńee kí ŋá tijimpin saraau. Kun puee díǹ nee, ti-Dindaan làá nyāntí u-ba kí dàkà-ni.»
5Ní bi cáań tin kɔkɔ Mooyiisi bālifèe circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nyɔkɔpu, ní samaa kɔkɔ sútìń ki kíǹ ki sí ti-Dindaan nimbiin. 6Ní Mooyiisi lī yii: «M làá dàkà-ni tin ti-Dindaan kpáafì-ni ní ŋée. Ni yaa lafun ŋá míǹ, u làá lēē u-nyooti kí dàkà-ni.» 7Niinee ní Mooyiisi bí Aarɔn yii: «Sútí kí pìl̄ nsaraafan kí ŋá a-kpitii pɔ̄tam saraau nì a-saraawɔkaau, kí pítí a-kpitii nì samaa kpitii. Míǹ boonee á ŋá saraabi bin ní samaa cáańee kí pítí bi-kpitii, kii ti-Dindaan nín síiǹ mara puee.»
8Ní Aarɔn sútì ki pìl̄ nsaraafan ní ki lāntì úǹ u-ba kpitii pɔ̄tam saraau nabil. 9Ní u-jipɔmbi cáań-u fatiku ní u dū u-ŋambiki ki sēē fatikuee ki dūu jōō nsaraafan kpiŋŋi pu ní ki kpáatì un kíǹee ki pɔ̀l̄ nsaraafan taapu. 10U dū ŋkpam nì aceebil nì mpɔɔlamee ki wùn̄ ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn kpáafì Mooyiisi puee. 11Ama ní ki yōoǹ tinan nì ŋgbanee ki nyántì dinaapaal kpaanceetiŋu ki wùn̄ ŋŋmi.
12Míǹ boonee ní Aarɔn lāntì upìja un bi cáań kí ŋá saraawɔkaayee, ní u-jipɔmbi cáań-u fatiku ní u dūu yāaǹ nsaraafan pu ki māntìi tú. 13Bi càkā upìjee nanti ní ki dū diyil ki kútì ki tīī-u ní u dūu wùn̄ ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu. 14U fíntì ina nì ayaka ki dūu páaǹ saraawɔkaa un pá nsaraafan puee ki wùn̄ ŋŋmi.
15Míǹ boonee ní Aarɔn cáań samaa kɔkɔ saraabi: u yōoǹ samaa kɔkɔ kpitii pɔ̄tam ŋɔjau ki lāntì ki ŋá saraa kii u nín bàà ŋá dinabil puee. 16Bi cáań saraawɔkaa waŋkutee nyɔkɔpu ki ŋá saraa kii bi nín síiǹ mara bí nīn ŋáań-u puee. 17Bi yōoǹ tijimpin saraau ki yáfì diŋaŋkul ki dūu wùn̄ ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu, ki kpáaǹ saraawɔkaa un bi ŋáań kutaafaau kamaayee. 18Boonee ní u lāntì unaja nì upìja un samaa kɔkɔ cáań kí ŋá mpèé saraauee, ní u-jipɔmbi cáań-u fatiku ní u dūu yāaǹ nsaraafan pu ki māntìi tú. 19Bi gíti tí cáań-u unajee nì upìjee kpam, an dàkà yii ajugbin nì ŋkpam min pá ina puee nì aceebil nì mpɔɔlam, 20ní ki dūu páaǹ unajee nì upìjee biŋŋi pu ní Aarɔn dū ŋkpamee ki wùn̄ ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu. 21Aarɔn yōoǹ tiwaŋkuti biŋŋi nì diŋaŋgiitaal yilpu ní ki fíiǹ fíiǹ ti-Dindaan nimbiin kii Mooyiisi nín nìn pée síiǹ-u mara puee.
22Ŋyunti ŋun Aarɔn ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau nì saraawɔkaa nì mpèé saraau ki dóòyee ní u yōoǹ u-ŋalii ki túĺ samaa ki mēē ki bīiǹ bi-pu ní ki kpákatì nsaraafan pu. 23Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn nín kóò dikpafindi tantiun. Bi dāa fātìi nyánnée ní ki mēē ki bīiǹ samaa kɔkɔ pu. Niinee ní ti-Dindaan nyántì u-nyooti ki dàkā samaa kɔkɔ. 24Ní ŋŋmi ŋubɔ nyánní ti-Dindaan nimbiin ki dɔ́miń ki wùn̄ saraawɔkaa nì ŋkpam min pá nsaraafan puee. Samaa kɔkɔ nín ká mimmee ní bi fáá iwiliili nì dipɔɔpindi, ní ki tātìi dōoǹ dicincibil.

english_text:
Nadab and Abihu
1Nadab and Abihu were two of Aaron's sons, but they disobeyed the Lord by burning incense to him on a fire pan, when they were not supposed to. 2Suddenly the Lord sent fiery flames and burned them to death. 3Then Moses told Aaron that this was exactly what the Lord had meant when he said:
“I demand respect
from my priests,
and I will be praised
by everyone!”
Aaron was speechless.
4Moses sent for Mishael and Elzaphan, the two sons of Aaron's uncle Uzziel. Then he told them, “Take these two dead relatives of yours outside the camp far from the entrance to the sacred tent.” 5So they dragged the dead men away by their clothes.
6Then Moses told Aaron and his other two sons, Eleazar and Ithamar:
Don't show your sorrow by messing up your hair and tearing your priestly clothes, or the Lord will get angry. He will kill the three of you and punish everyone else. It's all right for your relatives, the people of Israel, to mourn for those he destroyed by fire. 7But you are the Lord's chosen priests, and you must not leave the sacred tent, or you will die.
Aaron and his two sons obeyed Moses.
8The Lord said to Aaron:
9When you or your sons enter the sacred tent, you must never drink beer or wine. If you do, you will die right there! This law will never change. 10You must learn the difference between what is holy and what isn't holy and between the clean and the unclean. 11You must also teach the people of Israel everything that I commanded Moses to say to them.
12 Moses told Aaron and his two sons, Eleazar and Ithamar:
The grain sacrifice that was offered to give thanks to the Lord is very holy. So make bread without yeast from the part that wasn't sent up in smoke and eat it beside the altar. 13The Lord has said that this belongs to you and your sons, and that it must be eaten in a holy place. 14-15 But the choice ribs and the hind leg that were lifted up may be eaten by your entire family, as long as you do so in an acceptable place. These parts are yours from the sacrifices that the people offer to ask the Lord's blessing. This is what the Lord has commanded, and it will never change.
16When Moses asked around and learned that the ram for the sin sacrifice had already been burned on the altar, he became angry with Eleazar and Ithamar and said, 17 “Why didn't you eat the meat from this sacrifice in an acceptable place? It is very holy, and the Lord has given you this sacrifice to remove Israel's sin and guilt. 18Whenever an animal's blood isn't brought into the sacred tent, I commanded you to eat its meat in an acceptable place, but you burned it instead.”
19Their father Aaron replied, “Today two of my sons offered the sacrifice for sin and the sacrifice to please the Lord, and look what has happened to me! Would the Lord have approved if I had eaten the sacrifice for sin?”
20Moses was satisfied with Aaron's reply.
translation_text:
Ti-Dindaan ŋmiŋu wùn̄ Aarɔn jipɔmbi bili
1Aarɔn jipɔmbi Nadaab nì Abiyuu yōoǹ bi-sambiyaamu mun poon bi tùutī talaaluee ki pātì ŋŋmi ki dū talaalu ki páká. Bi nìn cáań ŋŋmi ŋun an kaa pú nsan bí cáań ti-Dindaan nimbiinee, kun puee an kaa nìn nóó nì ti-Dindaan nín síiǹ-bi puee. 2Niinee ní ti-Dindaan yāntì ŋŋmi ŋubɔ dɔ́miń ki wùn̄-bi ní bi kpíì dibɔbil pu niin ti-Dindaan nimbiin. 3Ní Mooyiisi bí Aarɔn yii: «An ní ti-Dindaan nìn kpáafì-ni ki lī yii:
<Bin sútiń ki pìl̀-mee
ní m là bí dàkà m nín bí circir puee,
ní ki là bí dàkà m-nyooti samaa kɔkɔ nimbiin.>»
Ní Aarɔn wunti kpíì.
4Niinee Mooyiisi yíiń Aarɔn baawaai Usiyeel jipɔmbi Miisayeel nì Eeliisafan ki bí-bi yii: «Dāam̄maan kí yòon̄ ni-nabiyaamu circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nyɔkɔpu kí cáá nyāntí dinaapaal kpaanceetiŋu.» 5Ní bi dɔ́miń ki yōoǹ bi nì bi-bɔkutiŋ ki nyántì dinaapaal kpaanceetiŋu kii Mooyiisi nín bí yii bí ŋá puee. 6Ní Mooyiisi bí Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi Eeleeyasaar nì Itamaar yii: «Ní taa yàntī ni-yikpiti ń nīn bí fìkil fikil kí taa cátí ni-bɔkutiŋ mun kí dàkà yii ni bí kunimbaaun. Ni yaa ŋá mimmee, ni làá kpú ní kí yàntī ti-Dindaan ń gíí samaa kɔkɔ pu diŋuul. Ní yàntī ni-nabiyaamu Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ ń kàl̄ bin ti-Dindaan dū ŋŋmi ki kūūyee kpool. 7Nimbee, ní taa nyā Circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔpu, án nín làá ŋá pu ní taa kpúee, di sá yii bi bātì ŋkpam ki sītì ni-yiliŋ pu ki dū-ni ki sú ti-Dindaan ní.» Ní Aarɔn nì u-jipɔmbi ŋá ki nóó nì Mooyiisi nín bí yii bí ŋá puee.
Idafi in pɔ̄ɔ̄yee marab
8Ti-Dindaan bí Aarɔn yii: 9«Sii nì a-jipɔmbi, ni yaa kóò circir kɔŋkooŋŋu poonee, ní taa nyɔ̀ ndamam àá ndaam min pɔ̄ɔ̄yee miba, án nín làá ŋá pu ní taa kpúee. Án nīn sá dibɔkpaal ki tīī ni nì ni-biyaamu kí nīn cá jaanjaan. 10Mimmee ni làá ŋmā kí gàntī tin bí circiree nì tin kaa bée, nì tin bi kòóyee nì tin baa kòóyee. 11Ni làá gíti ŋmā kí dàkà Isirayeel yab abɔkpaa ŋin ti-Dindaan dī Mooyiisi pu ki tīī-bee.»
Saraabi nanti marab
12Mooyiisi bí Aarɔn nì Eeleeyasaar nì Itamaar, u-jipɔmbi bili bin kíǹee yii: «Bi nín lēē tijimpin saraau poon dijandi ki wùn̄ ŋŋmi ki tīī ti-Dindaanee, dijandi din kíǹee, ní dūú ŋá tijin kí jī nsaraafan caŋin ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔ ń nīn kpá poon, di sá yii an sá circir páaa jinti ní. 13Mpaan ŋun bí circiree pu ní ní jī tijin gbanti, di sá yii saraabi bin bi cāabìń ki tìì ti-Dindaanee, dijandi din sá ki tīī sii nì a-jipɔmbee dee. Ti-Dindaan nín síiǹ-mi puee dee. 14Tiwaŋkuti bindi din bi yōoǹ kutaa ki fíiǹ fíiǹee nì ditaal din bi lēē ki dūu tīī ti-Dindaanee, sii nì a-jipɔmbi nì a-bisalib ń kàl̄ laakin bí circiree kí jī an jinti, di sá yii mpèé saraau un Isirayeel yab ŋáańee, dijandi gbanti di sá ki tīī sii nì a-jipɔmbi. 15Bi yaa lēē ditaal nì dibindi din bi làá fíiǹ fíiǹee, bí lēē ŋkpam min bi làá cáá wà ŋŋmee, ní kí yòon̄ yilpu kí fíiǹ fíiǹ ti-Dindaan nimbiin. Míǹ boonee sii nì a-jipɔmbi di yì, di sá yii dijandi din sá ki tīī-ni kí nīn cá jaanjaanee dee, kii ti-Dindaan nín tīī mara puee.»
16Boonee Mooyiisi dāa béè yii uŋɔja un bi dūu ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraauee, bi dūu wùn̄ ŋŋmi. Niinee ní Mooyiisi gíí Eeleeyasaar nì Itamaar, Aarɔn jipɔmbi bin kíǹee pu diŋuul, ní ki bālifì-bi yii: 17«Ba pu ní naa ŋmɔ́ ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau nanti mpaan ŋun bí circiree pu ní, kun puee tinan gbanti bí circir páaa ní? Ti-Dindaan di dū-tì ki tīī-ni yii ní fōō samaa kɔkɔ kpitii kí túń kí ŋmā kí fíntí bi-kpitii ti-Dindaan nimbiin. 18Baa dū uŋoobu gbanti fatikuu ki kɔ́ǹ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu poon, an puee an bàà sá ní ŋmɔ́ u-nanti ní, kii m nín síiǹ-ni mara puee.» 19Ní Aarɔn kíí Mooyiisi yii: «Díǹ di sá ŋwimpeepeekaa ŋun bi ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau nì saraawɔkaayee, ní sii a-ba nyí tin jítì m-puee. Mimmee an kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiin yii ḿ bàà ŋmɔ́ ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau nanti díǹ wiiŋŋuaaa?» 20Mooyiisi gbìl̄ an nyɔɔbuŋŋee ní ki tīī-u imɔ̀ń.

english_text:
Clean and Unclean Animals
(Deuteronomy 14.3-21)
1 The Lord told Moses and Aaron 2to say to the community of Israel:
You may eat 3any animal that has divided hoofs and chews the cud. 4-8But you must not eat animals such as camels, rock badgers, and rabbits that chew the cud but don't have divided hoofs. And you must not eat pigs—they have divided hoofs, but don't chew the cud. All of these animals are unclean, and you are forbidden even to touch their dead bodies.
9-12You may eat anything that lives in water and has fins and scales. But it would be disgusting for you to eat anything else that lives in water, and you must not even touch their dead bodies.
13-19Eagles, vultures, buzzards, crows, ostriches, hawks, sea gulls, owls, pelicans, storks, herons, hoopoes, and bats are also disgusting, and you are forbidden to eat any of them.
20-23The only winged insects you may eat are locusts, grasshoppers, and crickets. All other winged insects that crawl are too disgusting for you to eat.
24-28Don't even touch the dead bodies of animals that have divided hoofs but don't chew the cud. And don't touch the dead bodies of animals that have paws. If you do, you must wash your clothes, but you are still unclean until evening.
29-30Moles, rats, mice, and all kinds of lizards are unclean. 31Anyone who touches their dead bodies or anything touched by their dead bodies becomes unclean until evening. 32If something made of wood, cloth, or leather touches one of their dead bodies, it must be washed, but it is still unclean until evening. 33If any of these animals is found dead in a clay pot, the pot must be broken to pieces, and everything in it becomes unclean. 34If you pour water from this pot on any food, that food becomes unclean, and anything drinkable in the pot becomes unclean.
35If the dead body of one of these animals touches anything else, including ovens and stoves, that thing becomes unclean and must be destroyed. 36A spring or a cistern where one of these dead animals is found is still clean, but anyone who touches the animal becomes unclean. 37If the dead body of one of these animals is found lying on seeds that have been set aside for planting, the seeds remain clean. 38But seeds that are soaking in water become unclean, if the dead animal is found in the water.
39If an animal that may be eaten happens to die, and you touch it, you become unclean until evening. 40If you eat any of its meat or carry its body away, you must wash your clothes, but you are still unclean until evening.
41-42Don't eat any of those disgusting little creatures that crawl or walk close to the ground. 43If you eat any of them, you will become just as disgusting and unclean as they are. 44 I am the Lord your God, and you must dedicate yourselves to me and be holy, just as I am holy. Don't become disgusting by eating any of these unclean creatures. 45I brought you out of Egypt so that I could be your God. Now you must become holy, because I am holy!
46-47I have given these laws so that you will know what animals, birds, and fish are clean and may be eaten, and which ones are unclean and may not be eaten.
translation_text:
TIWAN TIN BI KÒÓYEE NÌ TIN BAA KÒÓYEE
Tiwaŋkuti tin bi kòóyee nì tin baa kòóyee
1Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn yii 2bí tùkù Isirayeel yab yii:
«Tiwaŋkuti tin kɔkɔ còom̄ kitiŋ puee poonee, tin ni ŋūǹ kí ŋmɔ́ee sɔ̀. 3Ni ŋūǹ kí ŋmɔ́ tiwaŋkuti tin tafuŋfukuti látì ní tì kpìkitī ki fàtīi ŋmóòyee. 4Ama tiwaŋkuti tin kpìkitī ki fàtīi ŋmóò àá ti-tafuŋfukuti látèe kansikinee,
- ni kòó ugutaamu, di sá yii u kpìkitī ki fàtīi ŋmóò, ama ní kaa cáá titafuŋfukul, ni kòó kuwaŋkuluu gbanti.
5- Ni kòó ujaŋgbeenapul, di sá yii u kpìkitī ki fàtīi ŋmóò, ama ní kaa cáá titafuŋfukul.
6- Ni kòó kiwuŋ, di sá yii u kpìkitī ki fàtīi ŋmóò, ama ní kaa cáá titafuŋfukul.
7- Ni kòó ugbeeti, di sá yii u-tafuŋfukuti látì, ama waa kpìkitī ki fàtīi ŋmóò.
8Ní taa ŋmɔ́ tiwaŋkuti gbanti nanti. Ní taa gbēē ti-waŋkpil, tí nīn sá-ni dikoobil.
9«Tin kɔkɔ kóò nnyiminee, án yaa sá kubɔɔuneeee, dimɔɔlineeee, ibunneeee, ni ŋūǹ kí ŋmɔ́ ijɔm in cáá ipɔkɔ nì ifeenee. 10Ama ní taa ŋmɔ́ tin kɔkɔ pée bí nnyimin, amɔɔ poon àá ibun poon kaa cáá ipɔkɔ nì ifeenee. 11Tí nīn sá-ni dikoobil. Ní taa ŋmɔ́ ti-nanti kí taa gbēē ti-waŋkpil. 12Ni kòó tin kɔkɔ pée bí nnyimin kaa cáá ifeenaaa, kaa cáá ipɔkɔee.
13«Inoon kansikinee, in ni kòó kaa máaǹ kí ŋmɔ́ee sèé: ukaalun nì ukaabu nì nnyimin kaaluŋwu, 14nì kikaaliŋkpaŋ nì kaajiiku nì u-buluku, 15digaliŋgaal nì di-buluku, 16taataa nì kitulinjakpatibooi nì ŋkpinni kpɔkpɔfiiu nì kaasaabi nì bi-buluku, 17ditulinjool nì jɔmbaaŋki nì unanjikaabu, 18nì kpɔkpɔfiibi bin sil fɔ̀kɔ̀ee nì kpɔkpɔfiibi bin cáá nnyɔlee nì ukpiŋkaabu, 19nì naakpaapiin nì kikpiŋkaabiki nì ki-buluku nì yikpitikooja nì kunanjiŋu.
20«Inaaki in kɔkɔ cáá iyakal inaa ki cáá ifeenee, ni kòó. 21Ama ni ŋūǹ kí ŋmɔ́ in cáá iyakal ki yùkufī kitiŋee, 22an dàkà yii inaakitoon nì i-buluku, ipɔɔm nì i-buluku, nì imaliŋgoon nì i-buluku. 23Ama kunaakibuluu kun kíǹ ki cáá ifeen nì iyakal inaayee, ni kòó.»
Tin kɔ̄ntí unil tijɔkɔndee
24«Tiwaŋkuti tiba kɔ̄ntí unil tijɔkɔndi. Un yaa gbēē ti-waŋkpilee kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi kí cáá sāā kujoou. 25Un di yaa tí yōoǹ ti-waŋkpilee kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi kí cáá sāā kujoou, ú fíntí u-wampeeŋkaati. 26Ni kòó tiwaŋkuti tin tafuŋfukuti kaa látì ní kaa kpìkitī kí fàtīí ŋmɔ́ee. 27Ni kòó tiwaŋkuti tin kɔkɔ cáá ataa anaa ki còom̄ ti-taaŋi poonee. Tì yaa kpíì ní ubɔ gbēē-tèe, udaan mun kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi kí cáá sāā kujoou. 28Un mun yaa túǹ ti-waŋkpilee kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi kí cáá sāā kujoou. Udaan ń fíntí tiwan tin u pēēyee, di sá yii ni kòó tiwaŋkuti gbanti.
29«Tiwaŋkuti tin kpátìi gbí kitiŋ puee, tin ni kòó ti-kansikinee sèé: tumbuŋku nì unapul nì dijikpal nì di-buluku, 30nì kijipatii nì jilkantoolii nì kaŋkampu nì ulɔ nì kunaatoou. 31Béémaan yii ni kòó tiwaŋkuti gbanti. Ubɔ yaa gbēē ti-waŋkpilee, udaan kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi kí cáá sāā kujoou. 32Tì yaa kpíì ní ki lítì tiba puee, an yaa sá ndɔ sambikaaa, tiwampeeŋkaalaaa, ŋgbanaaa, ditɔkɔlaaa, tin kamaa ní bi pée cáa tūǹ ditundee, tiwan gbanti kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. Bí dū nnyim ki fíntí-tì ní tí sīĺ kí cáá sāā kujoou ní kí nyā tijɔkɔndin. 33Tiwaŋkuti gbanti kubɔ yaa kpíì ki jéetì ditansambilin àá diboolinee, tin kā poonee kɔkɔ kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi, bi máaǹ kí gbá kí wīī ditansambil àá dibool gbanti. 34An yaa sá nnyim di kā di-ni ní nnyimee kpáatì ki sītì tijin tin baa kòóyee puee, tijin gbanti mun kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. An yaa tí sá nnyinnyɔkaam àá ndaam poon ní nnyim gbanti yaa kɔ́ee, báà mi yaa kā kun poonee, nnyim àá ndaam gbanti mun kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. 35Tiwan tin kamaa ní tiwaŋkutee yaa kpíì ki gbēēyee kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. An yaa sá dibubul àá ŋfan puee, see bí gbá kí wīī-ŋu, di sá yii ŋu mun kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi dee. 36Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, kuwaŋkuluu yaa jéetì nnyimbul àá dinyimbɔbil din poon ní nnyim dɔ̀ee ki kpíìyee, nnyim gbanti kaa kóò tijɔkɔndi. Ama un di yaa gbēē kuwaŋkuluu gbanti wuntee di kóò tijɔkɔndi. 37Diwaŋkpil gbanti dijandi diba yaa lítì ŋwambool puee, ŋwambool gbanti kaa kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. 38Ama bi yaa wōoǹ ŋwambool ní diwaŋkpilee yaa gbēēyee, ŋwambool gbanti kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi.
39«Tiwaŋkuti tin ni jīǹee kubɔ yaa kpíì ní ubɔ gbēē-kuee, udaan kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi kí cáá sāā kujoou. 40Un di yaa ŋmɔ́ tinan gbantee máaǹ kí fíntí u-wampeeŋkaati, udaan kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi kí cáá sāā kujoou. Un mun di yaa yōoǹ diwaŋkpilee máaǹ kí fíntí u-wampeeŋkaati, udaan kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi kí cáá sāā kujoou.
41«Ni kòó ŋwambilimu mun kpátìi gbí kitiŋ pu ki fòotēe. Ní taa pée ŋmɔ́-tì. 42Ni kòó tin fù ti-pooŋi puee nì tin còom̄ ataa anaa àá ataa kupaau puee. Ní taa pée ŋmɔ́-tì. 43Ní taa dū tiwaŋkuti gbanti tiba kí kɔ́ǹ ni-ba tijɔkɔndi. Taa pée yàntīmaan tí kɔ́ǹ-ni tijɔkɔndi án nín làá ŋá pu ní ti-puee, ní kpántí bijɔkɔndambee. 44Di sá yii man di sá ni-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu. Nín̄ bímaan circir, kun puee man bí circir ní. Taa yàntīmaan tiwan tin fòotī ki kpátìi gbí kitiŋ pu nee kansikin kubɔ ń kɔ́ǹ-ni tijɔkɔndi. 45Man di sá ni-Dindaan un nyántìń-ni Eejipiti tiŋkin kí nīn sá ni-Nimbɔtiuee. Míǹ puee nín̄ bímaan circir, kun puee man m-ba bí circir ní.»
46Marab bin bi nìn síiǹ tiwaŋkuti nì inoon nì tiwan tin kɔkɔ fòotī ki kóò nnyiminee nì tin kɔkɔ kpátìi gbí kitiŋ puee dee. 47Marab gbanti di nìn yàntī bi gàntī tiwaŋkuti tin bi kòóyee nì tin baa kòóyee, nì tiwaŋkuti tin bi máaǹ kí jēe nì tin baa máaǹ kí jēe.

english_text:
What Women Must Do after Giving Birth
1The Lord told Moses 2to say to the community of Israel:
If a woman gives birth to a son, she is unclean for seven days, just as she is during her monthly period. 3 Her son must be circumcised on the eighth day, 4but her loss of blood keeps her from being completely clean for another 33 days. During this time she must not touch anything holy or go to the place of worship. 5Any woman who gives birth to a daughter is unclean for two weeks, just as she is during her period. And she won't be completely clean for another 66 days.
6When the mother has completed her time of cleansing, she must come to the front of the sacred tent and bring to the priest a year-old lamb as a sacrifice to please me and a dove or a pigeon as a sacrifice for sin. 7After the priest offers the sacrifices to me, the mother will become completely clean from her loss of blood, whether her child is a boy or a girl. 8 If she cannot afford a lamb, she can offer two doves or two pigeons, one as a sacrifice to please me and the other as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_text:
Umatimpɔɔn marab
1Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Mooyiisi ki bí-u yii: 2«Tùkù Isirayeel yab yii unimpu yaa cáá dipool ki màl̄ kibininjabikee, mara poonee, u kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi kí cáá sāā iwiin iluli dal kii u nín yaa ká u-ba, u bí tijɔkɔndin puee. 3Ŋwinniniiti dalee, bí gíí kibikee dikpancandi. 4Míǹ boonee, ú gíti kàl̄ iwiin mmuŋku nì saalaa nì ita kí nyā fatiku un nyáń-uee jɔkɔntin. Waa máaǹ kí gbēē tiwan tin bí circir bi dūu sú ti-Dindaanee, kaa máaǹ kí kɔ́ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu cindin kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋun u làá nyā u-matinti jɔkɔntinee.
5«An yaa sá kibinimpubiki ní u màl̄ee, mara poonee, u kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi kí cáá sāā nnyɔmu muli kii u nín yaa ká u-ba, u bí tijɔkɔndin puee. Míǹ boonee ní ú gíti kàl̄ iwiin imuŋku ita nì iluu kí nyā fatiku un nyáń-uee jɔkɔntin.
6«An yaa sá kibininjabiki àá kibinimpubiki ní u màl̄ ní ki kāl̀ iwiin in mara bālifèe ki tin sāāyee, ú cùú ká usaraaŋal circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu. Ú cáań dibindi diba pibil kí ŋá saraawɔkaa nì dinanjil àá dibeenanjil kí ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau. 7Ní usaraaŋal ń fōō tiwaŋkutee kí cáá ŋá saraa ti-Dindaan nimbiin kí fíntí unimpuee kpitii ú nyā fatiku un nyáń-uee jɔkɔntin.»
Mara un bi nìn síiǹ unimpu yaa màl̄ kibininjabiki àá kibinimpubikee dee.
8«Unimpu ŋaan yaa kaa nyìm̀ ú dā dipibilee, u ŋūǹ kí cáań ananjil ali àá abeenanjil ali ní kí dū diba kí ŋá saraawɔkaa ní kí dū din kíǹee kí ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau, ní usaraaŋal ń dūú ŋá saraa kí fíntí u-kpitii ní ú nyā fatiku un nyáń-uee jɔkɔntin.»

english_text:
Skin Diseases
1The Lord told Moses and Aaron to say to the people:
2If sores or boils or a skin rash should break out and start spreading on your body, you must be brought to Aaron or to one of the other priests. 3If the priest discovers that the hair in the infected area has turned white and that the infection seems more than skin deep, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
4But if the infected area is white and only skin deep, and if the hair in it hasn't turned white, the priest will order you to stay away from everyone else for seven days. 5If the disease hasn't spread by that time, he will order you to stay away from everyone else for another seven days. 6Then if the disease hasn't become any worse or spread, the priest will say, “You are clean. It is only a sore. After you wash your clothes, you may go home.”
7However, if the disease comes back, you must return to the priest. 8If it is discovered that the disease has started spreading, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
9Any of you with a skin disease must be brought to a priest. 10If he discovers that the sore spot is white with pus and that the hair around it has also turned white, 11he will say, “This is leprosy. You are unclean and must stay away from everyone else.” 12-13But if the disease has run its course and only the scars remain, he will say, “You are clean.” 14-15If the sores come back and turn white again, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
16-17However, if the sores heal and only white spots remain, the priest will say, “You are now clean.”
18-19If you have a sore that either swells or turns reddish-white after it has healed, then you must show it to a priest. 20If he discovers that the hair in the infected area has turned white and that the infection seems more than skin deep, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.” 21But if the white area is only on the surface of the skin and hasn't become any worse, and if the hair in it hasn't turned white, he will tell you to stay away from everyone else for seven days.
22If the sore begins spreading during this time, the priest will say, “You are unclean because you have a disease.” 23But if it doesn't spread, and only a scar remains, he will say, “You are now clean.”
24If you have a burn that gets infected and turns red or reddish-white, 25a priest must examine it. Then if he discovers that the hair in the infected area has turned white and that the infection seems more than skin deep, he will say, “The burn has turned into leprosy, and you are unclean.” 26But if the priest finds that the hair in the infected area hasn't turned white and that the sore is only skin deep and it is healing, he will tell you to stay away from everyone else for seven days. 27On the seventh day the priest will examine you again, and if the infection is spreading, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.” 28However, if the infection hasn't spread and has begun to heal, and if only a scar remains, he will say, “Only a scar remains from the burn, and you are clean.”
29If you have a sore on your head or chin, 30it must be examined by a priest. If the infection seems more than skin deep, and the hair in it has thinned out and lost its color, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.” 31On the other hand, if he discovers that the itchy spot is only skin deep, but that the hair still isn't healthy, he will order you to stay away from everyone else for seven days. 32By that time, if the itch hasn't spread, if the hair seems healthy, and if the itch is only skin deep, 33you must shave off the hair around the infection, but not those on it. Then the priest will tell you to stay away from everyone else for another seven days. 34By that time, if the itch hasn't spread and seems no more than skin deep, he will say, “You are clean; now you must wash your clothes.”
35-36Later, if the itch starts spreading, even though the hair is still healthy, the priest will say, “You are unclean.” 37But if he thinks you are completely well, he will say, “You are clean.”
38If white spots break out on your skin, 39but the priest discovers that it is only a rash, he will say, “You are clean.”
40-41If you become bald on any part of your head, you are still clean. 42-43But if a priest discovers that a reddish-white sore has broken out on the bald spot and looks like leprosy, he will say, 44“This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
45If you ever have leprosy, you must tear your clothes, leave your hair uncombed, cover the lower part of your face, and go around shouting, “I'm unclean! I'm unclean!” 46As long as you have the disease, you are unclean and must live alone outside the camp.
47-50If a greenish or reddish spot appears anywhere on any of your clothing or on anything made of leather, you must let the priest examine the clothing or the leather. He will put it aside for seven days, 51and if the mildew has spread in that time, he will say, “This is unclean 52because the mildew has spread.” Then he will burn the clothing or the piece of leather.
53If the priest discovers that the mildew hasn't spread, 54he will tell you to wash the clothing or leather and put it aside for another seven days, 55after which he will examine it again. If the spot hasn't spread, but is still greenish or reddish, the clothing or leather is unclean and must be burned. 56But if the spot has faded after being washed, he will tear away the spot. 57Later, if the spot reappears elsewhere on the clothing or the leather, you must burn it. 58Even if the spot completely disappears after being washed, it must be washed again before it is clean.
59These are the rules for deciding if clothing is clean or unclean after a spot appears on it.
translation_text:
Iween in tòó unil wunti puee marab
1Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn yii:
2«Ubɔ wunti pu laaba yaa díkí àá tikalindi nyáń u-wunti pu laaba àá u-wunti pu laaba líkitì ki jìl̀ ní ki dāa dūu ŋá mbuun kii dinyaŋgbandee, bí cáá udaan kí dàkà usaraaŋakpil Aarɔn àá u-jipɔmbi kansikin ubɔ. 3Usaraaŋal ń kpèè mbuun ŋun bí udaan wunti puee. Tikuti tin bí mbuunee poonee yaa pīiǹ ní mbuun yaa ŋmɔ́ ki kɔ́ tiwunnan poonee, mimmee an sá dinyaŋgbandi buuŋŋu. Usaraaŋal nín kpēē-u ki ká mimmee ní ú sòoǹ báà ŋma ń gbìl̄ yii udaan kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. 4Ama u-wunti pu laakin líkitèe yaa pīiǹ ní kaa ŋmɔ́ ki kɔ́ tiwunnan poon, ní tikuti mun kaa píil̀ee, usaraaŋal ń dū-u kí pìin̄ kudii ú nīn bí niin u-baba iwiin iluli. 5Ŋwinluluúti dalee ní usaraaŋal ń tí kpèè-u. U yaa ká yii mbuunee kaa kpántì, kaa wāaǹ muee ní ú fàtīí tí dū-u kí pìin̄ kudii ú nīn bí niin u-baba iwiin iluli. 6Ŋwinluluúti dalee ní usaraaŋal ń gíti tí pìitī-u nliliitiim kí kpèè-u. Mbuun yaa píil̀ fàaa kaa wāaǹee, usaraaŋal ń sòoǹ báà ŋma ń gbìl̄ yii unilee kaa kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi, an pée sá tikalindi ní. Udaan ń fíntí u-wampeeŋkaati kí ŋāŋkì. 7Ama usaraaŋal nín ká yii waa kɔ́ tijɔkɔndee ní boonee tikalindee yaa lālim̀ee, ú fàtīí gítí kí dū u-ba kí dàkà usaraaŋal ú kpèè-u. 8Usaraaŋal yaa dáań ki ká yii tikalindi lālim̀ ki gbí tiwun kɔkɔ puee ní ú sòoǹ báà ŋma ń gbìl̄ yii udaan kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi, an sá dinyaŋgbandi.
9«Dinyaŋgbandi weeŋyi iba yaa tɔ́ ubɔee, bí cáań-u usaraaŋal cee. 10Usaraaŋal ń kpèè-u. An yaa sá disiŋkpeepindi di bí udaan wunti pu ní disiŋkpeelee poon tikuti bí ki pīiǹ ní mbuun nútìńee, 11an sá dinyaŋgbandi buuŋŋu di tɔ́ udaan. Usaraaŋal ń sòoǹ báà ŋma ń gbìl̄ yii udaan kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. An kaa ti bàlifī ú dū-u kí pìin̄ kudii, di sá yii an nyáń mpaampiin pu yii u kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. 12Ama usaraaŋal yaa dáań ki ká yii dinyaŋgbandi weeŋŋuee kpátìi gbí udaan wunti kɔkɔ pu kí kíĺ diyil kí cáá sāā ataayee, 13usaraaŋal ń mɔ̀tīí kpèè tiŋan. U yaa ká yii an píń u-wunti kɔkɔ puee, ú sòoǹ báà ŋma ń gbìl̄ yii waa kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. Di sá an píń u-wunti kɔkɔ pu ki pīiǹ, waa kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. 14Ama ŋwiin ŋun u yaa ká udaan wunti léetèe, ŋwiin gbantee u kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. 15Usaraaŋal yaa pée ká udaan wunti léetèe, ú sòoǹ báà ŋma ń gbìl̄ yii u kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. U-wunti nín léetèe dàkà yii an sá dinyaŋgbandi weeŋŋu. 16Ama u-wunti laakin léetèe yaa fātìi píil̀ee, ú gítí kí ká usaraaŋal. 17Usaraaŋal ń gíti kpèè-u. U mun yaa ká yii u-wunti laakin léetèe píil̀ee, ú sòoǹ báà ŋma ń gbìl̄ yii ŋweenee kaa sá tijɔkɔndi weeŋŋu, ní un pu ŋu kēe mun kaa kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi.
18«Dinal yaa nìn tɔ́ ubɔ ní ki kpíì, 19ama ní laakin dinalee nìn tɔ́ee, ndulim miba nyáń àá niin léetì ki pīiǹ fàaayee, udaan ń cáá u-ba kí dàkà usaraaŋal. 20Usaraaŋal ń kpèè-u. Laakin ŋá ndulim àá an léetèe yaa ŋmɔ́ ki kɔ́ tiwunnan poon ní tikuti tin bí ŋu-poonee pīiǹee, usaraaŋal ń sòoǹ báà ŋma ń gbìl̄ yii udaan kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. Dinyaŋgbandi buuŋŋu di nyáń dinalee buŋweekun. 21Ama usaraaŋal yaa dáań ki ká yii tikuti tin bí mbuunee poon kaa pīiǹ ní mbuunee kaa ŋmɔ́ ki kɔ́ tiwunnan poon, ní kaa léetèe, ú dū-u kí pìin̄ kudii u-baba iwiin iluli. 22Míǹ boon mbuunee yaa nyātèe, usaraaŋal ń sòoǹ báà ŋma ń gbìl̄ yii udaan kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi: dinyaŋgbandi buuŋŋu dee. 23Ama mbuunee yaa kaa kpántì kaa wāaǹ muee, mimmee an sá dinalee buŋweeku. Usaraaŋal ń lì báà ŋma ń gbìl̄ yii udaan kaa kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi.
24«Ŋŋmi yaa nìn wùn̄ ubɔ ní an ŋá ndulim kubuŋweeu poon ki pīiǹ fàaa àá ki máǹ wèeeeyee, 25usaraaŋal ń kpèè-u. Tikuti tin bí ndulim poonee yaa pīiǹ ní mbuun yaa ŋmɔ́ ki kɔ́ tiwunnan poonee, an sá dinyaŋgbandi di nyáń kubuŋweeuee poon. Usaraaŋal ń sòoǹ báà ŋma ń gbìl̄ yii udaan kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. 26Ama usaraaŋal yaa ká yii tikupin kaa bí ndulim poon ní kaa ŋmɔ́ ki kɔ́ tiwunnan poon, kaa tí pīiǹ fàaayee, usaraaŋal ń dū-u kí pìin̄ kudii u-baba iwiin iluli. 27Iwiin iluli dal, usaraaŋal yaa fātìi kpēē-u ki ká yii an wāaǹee, usaraaŋal ń sòoǹ báà ŋma ń gbìl̄ yii udaan kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. An sá dinyaŋgbandi buuŋŋu. 28Ama ndulimee yaa kaa wāaǹ ki gbíntì dibɔɔbaantiil ní kaa pīiǹ fàaayee, an sá ndulim fám ní. Usaraaŋal ń sòoǹ báà ŋma ń gbìl̄ yii udaan kaa kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi, an sá ŋŋmi buŋweeku.
29«Ŋween ŋubɔ yaa tɔ́ uninja àá unimpu ubɔ yil àá u-nyɔɔkpaalee, 30usaraaŋal ń kpèè ŋween gbanti. U yaa ká yii ŋweenee ŋmɔ́ ki kɔ́ tiwunnan poon ní tikuti bí ki sá kpalku kaa múkúee, usaraaŋal ń sòoǹ báà ŋma ń gbìl̄ yii udaan kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. An sá kideeŋŋi kin sá dinyaŋgbandi ki tòó diyil àá dinyɔɔkpaalee. 31Ama usaraaŋal yaa ká yii ŋweenee kaa ŋmɔ́ ki kɔ́ tiwunnan poon, ní tikuti tin bɔ̀ǹee kaa bí ki-poonee, ú dū-u kí pìin̄ kudii u-baba iwiin iluli. 32Iwiin iluli dalee, usaraaŋal ń fàtīí kpèè ŋweenee. U yaa ká yii ŋuaa wāaǹ, ní tikuti tin sá kpalkuee kaa bí ŋu-poon ní kaa ŋmɔ́ ki kɔ́ tiwunnan poonee, 33udaan ń kòol̀ u-yil kí gɔ́ntí laakin ŋween bée. Míǹ boonee usaraaŋal ń fàtīí dū-u kí pìin̄ kudii u-baba nliliitiim iwiin iluli. 34Iwiin iluli dalee, usaraaŋal ń fàtīí kpèè ŋween gbanti. An yaa kaa wāaǹ, kaa ŋmɔ́ ki kɔ́ tiwunnan poonee, usaraaŋal ń sòoǹ báà ŋma ń gbìl̄ yii waa kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. Ú pée fíntí u-wampeeŋkaati ní kí nyā tijɔkɔndin. 35Ama usaraaŋal nín kpēē-u ki dóò ki lī yii u bí circiree, boonee kideeŋŋee yaa wāaǹee, 36usaraaŋal ń tí fàtīí kpèè-u. U yaa ká yii kideeŋŋee wāaǹee, an kaa ti bàlifī ú nyàab̀ kí kpèè yii tikuti tin sá kpalkuee báaa an kpá, udaan kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. 37Ama kideeŋŋee yaa kaa wāaǹ ní tikubɔn yaa nyáń ki-nee, mimmee kideeŋŋee kpíì dee, un pu kì tɔ́ee kaa kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. Usaraaŋal ń lì báà ŋma ń gbìl̄ yii udaan kaa kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi.
38«Uninja àá unimpu ubɔ wunti yaa lēē ki ŋá aliki aliki ki pīiǹee, 39usaraaŋal ń kpèè-u. Alikee yaa pīiǹ fàaayee, mimmee an sá ncabiyaamu. Udaan kaa kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi.
40«Ubɔ yaa kaa cáá tiyikpiti u-yil puee, mimmee uyiŋatifu dee, waa kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. 41U-yigbeel yaa kaa cáá tiyikpiti ní ki jɔ̀m̀ee, mimmee un yigbeel ŋātèe dee, waa kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. 42Ama mbuun yaa tɔ́ u-yil kansikin àá u-yigbeel laakin ŋātèe ki pīiǹ fàaayee, an sá dinyaŋgbandi di kíĺ ki bíi tòó-u. 43Usaraaŋal ń kpèè-u. U yaa ká yii mbuun ŋun tɔ́ u-yil kansikin àá u-yigbeel laakin ŋātèe pīiǹ fàaa ki náań nì dinyaŋgbandee, 44mimmee udaan sá unyaŋgbanti ní, ki kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. Di sá u-yil ní ŋweenee tɔ́.
45«Un būǹ dinyaŋgbandee máaǹ kí pèen̄ tiwan tin cátèe, kí taa ti càatī u-yil, kí bìin̄ u-nyɔɔkuti pu, ní kí nīn kūuntí ki lì yii: <M kɔ́ tijɔkɔndeeee! M kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi!> 46Udaan làá nīn bí tijɔkɔndin míǹ kí nīn cí ŋyunti ŋun dinyaŋgbandi buuŋyi làá dóóyee. U làá nīn kóò u-baba, dinaapaal kpaanceetiŋu.
Dinyaŋgbandi din tòó tiwampeeŋkaal puee marab
47«Tí lì yii dinyaŋgbandi daaŋku nyáń ki kā tiwampeeŋkaal tin bi dū ipii kuti àá gulfapiin káŋkaŋ ki lùn̄ee pu, 48àá sata pu àá tiŋgiliisi un bi dū gulfapiin káŋkaŋ ki lùn̄ee pu, àá ŋgban àá tin kɔkɔ pée sá ŋgbanee pu. 49Kudaaŋŋu gbanti yaa sɔ̀m̀ gùuu àá ku yaa máǹ wèeee ki táká tiwampeeŋkaal àá ŋgban, àá sata, àá tiŋgiliisi, àá tin kɔkɔ bi dū ŋgban ki lùn̄ee puee, an sá dinyaŋgbandi. Bí cáá dàkà usaraaŋal. 50Usaraaŋal ń kpèè kudaaŋŋuee ní kí cáá tiwan tin pu ku kēe kí síiń dibalin iwiin iluli. 51Iwiin iluli dalee, ú kpèè kudaaŋŋuee. Ku yaa lālim̀ tiwampeeŋkaal pu, àá sata pu, àá tiŋgiliisi pu, àá ŋgban pu, àá tin kɔkɔ pée sá ŋgbanee puee, an sá dinyaŋgbandi. Tiwan gbanti kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. 52Usaraaŋal ń dū tiwampeeŋkaalee, àá satee, àá tiŋgiliisee, àá tin kɔkɔ pée sá ŋgbanee kí cáá wà ŋŋmi. Kii an nín sá kudaaŋŋu kun baa ŋūǹ kí lēē kí fée puee, bí cáá an wantee kí wà ŋŋmi. 53Ama usaraaŋal yaa kpēē kudaaŋŋuee ki ká yii kuaa lālim̀ tiwampeeŋkaalee pu, àá satee pu, àá tiŋgiliisee pu, àá tin kɔkɔ sá ŋgbanee puee, 54ú yàntī bí fíntí tiwan tin pu kudaaŋŋuee kēe, ní ú cáá síiń dibalin nliliitiim iwiin iluli. 55Bi nín fíntì míǹ ki dóòyee ní usaraaŋal ń fàtīí kpèè. U yaa ká yii kudaaŋŋuee pée gbíntìi bí kii ku nín nìn bí puee, báà ku yaa kaa lālim̀aaa, tiwanee kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. Bí cáá-tì kí wà ŋŋmi, di sá yii tiwanee poon àá ti-boon bíil̀. 56Ama bi nín fíntì míǹ boonee ní usaraaŋal yaa kpēē ki ká yii kudaaŋŋuee gbíntìi kā kaa lālim̀ tiwampeeŋkaal pu àá ŋgban pu, àá sata pu, àá tiŋgiliisi puee, ú gíí kí lēē dijandi gbanti tiwampeeŋkaal pu, àá ŋgban pu, àá sata àá tiŋgiliisi pu kí fá. 57Ama boonee, kudaaŋŋuee yaa fātìi nyáń ki kā tiwampeeŋkaalee pu, àá satee pu, àá tiŋgiliisee pu, àá ŋgban wantee puee, an sá bí wà-tì ŋŋmi ní, kun puee dinyaŋgbandi di bíi tòó-tì.
58«Ama an yaa sá tiwampeeŋkaal, àá sata, àá tiŋgiliisi, àá ŋgban wanti tin bi fíntì ní kudaaŋŋuee wáŋkèe, bí fàtīí fíntí-tì nliliitiim ní tí nyā tijɔkɔndin.»
59Mara un bi nìn síiǹ kí ŋmā kí béé yii tiwampeeŋkaal, àá sata, àá tiŋgiliisi, àá ŋgban wanti tin pu kudaaŋŋu bée kɔ́ tijɔkɔndaaa, taa kɔ́ee dee.

english_text:
The Ceremony for People Healed of Leprosy
1The Lord told Moses to say to the people:
2-3 After you think you are healed of leprosy, you must ask for a priest to come outside the camp and examine you. And if you are well, 4he will order someone to bring out two live birds that are acceptable for sacrifice, together with a stick of cedar wood, a piece of red yarn, and a branch from a hyssop plant. 5The priest will order someone to kill one of the birds over a clay pot of spring water. 6Then he will dip the other bird, the cedar, the red yarn, and the hyssop in the blood of the dead bird. 7Next, he will sprinkle you seven times with the blood and say, “You are now clean.” Finally, he will release the bird and let it fly away.
8After this you must wash your clothes, shave your entire body, and take a bath before you are completely clean. You may move back into camp, but you must not enter your tent for seven days. 9Then you must once again shave your head, face, and eyebrows, as well as the hair on the rest of your body. Finally, wash your clothes and take a bath, and you will be completely clean.
10On the eighth day you must bring to the priest two rams and a year-old female lamb that have nothing wrong with them; also bring 300 milliliters of olive oil and 3 kilograms of your finest flour mixed with oil. 11Then the priest will present you and your offerings to me at the entrance to my sacred tent. 12There he will offer one of the rams, together with the oil, as a sacrifice to make things right. He will also lift them up to show that they are dedicated to me. 13This sacrifice is very holy. It belongs to the priest and must be killed in the same place where animals are killed as sacrifices for sins and as sacrifices to please me.
14The priest will smear some of the blood from this sacrifice on your right ear lobe, some on your right thumb, and some on the big toe of your right foot. 15He will then pour some of the olive oil into the palm of his left hand, 16dip a finger of his right hand into the oil, and sprinkle some of it seven times toward the sacred tent. 17Next, the priest will smear some of the oil on your right ear lobe, some on your right thumb, and some on the big toe of your right foot, 18-20and he will pour the rest of the oil from his palm on your head. Then he will offer the other two animals—one as a sacrifice for sin and the other as a sacrifice to please me, together with a grain sacrifice. After this you will be completely clean.
21If you are poor and cannot afford to offer this much, you may offer a ram as a sacrifice to make things right, together with 300 milliliters of olive oil and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil as a grain sacrifice. The priest will then lift these up to dedicate them to me. 22Depending on what you can afford, you must also offer either two doves or two pigeons, one as a sacrifice for sin and the other as a sacrifice to please me. 23The priest will offer these to me in front of the sacred tent on the eighth day.
24-25The priest will kill this ram for the sacrifice to make things right, and he will lift it up with the olive oil in dedication to me. Then he will smear some of the blood on your right ear lobe, some on your right thumb, and some on the big toe of your right foot.
26The priest will pour some of the olive oil into the palm of his left hand, 27then dip a finger of his right hand in the oil and sprinkle some of it seven times toward the sacred tent. 28He will smear some of the oil on your right ear lobe, some on your right thumb, and some on the big toe of your right foot, just as he did with the blood of the sacrifice to make things right. 29-31And he will pour the rest of the oil from his palm on your head.
Then, depending on what you can afford, he will offer either the doves or the pigeons together with the grain sacrifice. One of the birds is the sacrifice for sin, and the other is the sacrifice to please me. After this you will be completely clean.
32These are the things you must do if you have leprosy and cannot afford the usual sacrifices to make you clean.
When There Is Mildew in a House
33The Lord told Moses and Aaron to say to the people:
34After I have given you the land of Canaan as your permanent possession, here is what you must do, if I ever put mildew on the walls of any of your homes. 35First, you must say to a priest, “I think there is mildew on the wall of my house.”
36The priest will reply, “Empty the house before I inspect it, or else everything in it will be unclean.”
37If the priest discovers greenish or reddish spots that go deeper than the surface of the walls, 38he will have the house closed for seven days. 39Then he will return and check to see if the mildew has spread. 40-41If so, he will order someone to scrape the plaster from the walls, remove the stones covered with mildew, then haul everything off and dump it in an unclean place outside the town. 42Afterwards the wall must be repaired with new stones and fresh plaster.
43If the mildew appears a second time, 44the priest will come and say, “This house is unclean. It's covered with mildew that can't be removed.” 45Then he will have the house torn down and every bit of wood, stone, and plaster hauled off to an unclean place outside the town. 46Meanwhile, if any of you entered the house while it was closed, you will be unclean until evening. 47And if you either slept or ate in the house, you must wash your clothes.
48On the other hand, if the priest discovers that mildew hasn't reappeared after the house was newly plastered, he will say, “This house is clean—the mildew has gone.” 49Then, to show that the house is now clean, he will get two birds, a stick of cedar wood, a piece of red yarn, and a branch from a hyssop plant and bring them to the house. 50He will kill one of the birds over a clay pot of spring water 51-52and let its blood drain into the pot. Then he will dip the cedar, the hyssop, the yarn, and the other bird into the mixture of blood and water. Next, he will sprinkle the house seven times with the mixture, then the house will be completely clean. 53Finally, he will release the bird and let it fly away, ending the ceremony for purifying the house.
54-57These are the things you must do if you discover that you are unclean because of an itch or a sore, or that your clothing or house is unclean because of mildew.
translation_text:
Unyaŋgbanti jɔkɔnti fíntitam marab
1Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Mooyiisi ki bí yii:
2«Unyaŋgbanti yaa pɔ́ɔkèe, saraabi bin u máaǹ kí ŋá ní kí nyā u-weeŋyi jɔkɔntinee sɔ̀. Bi yaa cáań-u usaraaŋal ceeyee, 3ní úǹ ń nyā dinaapaal kpaanceetiŋu kí kpèè-u. Unyaŋgbantee yaa lafun pɔ́ɔkèe, 4ní usaraaŋal ń yàntī bí cáań ubunlee yil pu nnɔmbiyaamu mun ŋān̄ bí dūú ŋá saraayee muli nì mu-nimbiliŋ nì busubu bun bi yíì yii seediree dɔŋu nì gulfaman nì kifaapibiki kin bi yíì isɔpee. 5Usaraaŋal ń yàntī bí làntì nnɔmbiyaamuee kiba kí dū ki-fatikuu kí ŋá ditansambil din poon nnyimbul nnyim kēe. 6Ní ú yòon̄ kinɔmbiki kin kíǹee nì seedir dɔŋuee nì gulfamanee nì isɔpi faapibikee kí dūú bɔ̄ kinɔmbiki kin bi lāntèe fatikuun. 7Niinee ní ú dū fatikuee kí yàaǹ un bi bíi ŋáań saraa kí fíntí u-jɔkɔntee pu ŋfunyɔm miluli. Míǹ boonee ní ú sòoǹ báà ŋma ń gbìl̄ yii udaan nyáń tijɔkɔndin ní kí gíiǹ kinɔmbiki kin baa kūūyee kí líí tisati watil pú. 8Un bi ŋá saraa ki fíntì u-jɔkɔntee máaǹ kí fíntí u-wampeeŋkaati, kí kòol̀ u-wunti kɔkɔ pu kuti, kí fàl̀ ní kí nín nyā tijɔkɔndin. Míǹ boonee, u ŋūǹ kí gítí dinaapaal pu, ama waa nín máaǹ kí kɔ́ u-tantiu poon kí cáá sāā iwiin iluli ní. 9Iwiin iluli dalee ní ú kòol̀ u-wunti kɔkɔ pu kuti, an dàkà yii u-yikpiti nì u-nyimpul nì u-niŋgbuŋkooŋyi nì tikuti tin pée bí u-wunti puee, ní kí fíntí u-wampeeŋkaati, kí fàl̀ ní kí nín nyā tijɔkɔndin.
10«Iwiin inii dalee, ú cáań apibil ŋin laaba kaa wɔ̀b̄ee ali nì dibindi diba pisaliu un laaba kaa wɔ̀b̄ee, nì ŋyim min bi dū ŋkpam ki búuńee kiiloobi biwa nì ŋkpam liitiri dijandi. 11Usaraaŋal un bíi ŋáań saraa gbantee ń dū un jɔkɔnti bi bíi fíntée nì saraabi bin u cáańee kɔkɔ kí síiń circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu. 12Ú yòon̄ apibilee kansikin din bi làá dūú ŋá dibɔkpil saraauee nì ŋkpam liitiri dijandee yilpu kí fíiǹ fíiǹ ti-Dindaan nimbiin. 13U yaa ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee ní ú làntì dipibilee laakin bi làntī ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau nì saraawɔkaa waŋkutee, circir paaŋŋu laŋki gbanti. Di sá yii dibɔkpil saraau nì ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau nanti sá ki tīī usaraaŋal ní. An sá circir páaa wanti ní. 14Usaraaŋal ń dū dipibilee fatikuu kí jōō un jɔkɔnti bi bíi fíntée tafalam ŋgiil yal pu nì u-ŋambijal ŋgiil yal pu nì u-taŋambijal ŋgiil yal pu. 15Míǹ boonee ní ú bàtī ŋkpam kí ŋá u-ŋantilin ŋgan yal. 16Ú dū u-ŋaŋgiiŋambiki kí sēē ŋkpam min kā u-ŋantil ŋgan yal poonee kí yàaǹ ŋfunyɔm miluli ti-Dindaan nimbiin. 17Ú tí sēē ŋkpam min kíǹ ki kā u-ŋantilinee kí dūú jōō kijapaayee tafalam ŋgiil yal pu nì u-ŋambijal ŋgiil yal pu nì u-taŋambijal ŋgiil yal pu, laakin u bàà dū dibɔkpil saraau fatikuu ki jōōyee táb. 18Míǹ boonee ní ú dū ŋkpam min kíǹ ki kā u-ŋantilinee kí sìtī un saraau bi bíi ŋáańee yil pu ní kí ŋá dikoobil nín bālifì puee ti-Dindaan nimbiin kí fíntí udaan kpitii. 19Usaraaŋal ń ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau ní kí ŋá dikoobil nín sá puee kí fíntí kijapaayee ú nyā u-jɔkɔntin. U yaa ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee ní kí làntì saraawɔkaa waŋkuluku. 20Ú yòon̄ saraawɔkaayee kɔkɔ nì tijimpin saraau kí cáá wà ŋŋmi nsaraafan pu. Niinee ní ú gíti ŋá dikoobil nín sá puee kí fíntí udaan kpitii ú nyā tijɔkɔndin.»
Unyaŋgbanti un kaa cáá ŋŋmamee saraabi
21«Ama udaan yaa sá usoodaan ní kaa cáá ŋŋmam kí ŋmā kí ká tin kɔkɔ bi bālifèe, ú cáań dipibil dibaba kí ŋá dibɔkpil saraau ní bí ŋá dikoobil nín sá puee kí fíntí u-jɔkɔnti. Ú cáań ŋyim min bi dū ŋkpam ki búuńee kiiloobi bita kí ŋá tijimpin saraau, nì ŋkpam liitiri dijandi. 22Ú cáań ananjil ali àá abeenanjil ali kí nóó nì tin u ŋūǹ kí kée. Bí dū diba kí ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau ní kí dū din kíǹee kí ŋá saraawɔkaa. 23Iwiin inii dalee, ú cáań saraabi gbanti kɔkɔ kí tīī usaraaŋal, circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu, ti-Dindaan nimbiin, bí dūú ŋá saraa kí fíntí u-jɔkɔnti. 24Usaraaŋal ń yòon̄ dibɔkpil saraau pibil nì ŋkpamee yilpu kí fíiǹ fíiǹ ti-Dindaan nimbiin. 25U yaa ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee ní ú làntì dipibilee ní kí dū di-fatikuu kí jōō un bi bíi fíntí u-jɔkɔntee tafalam ŋgiil yal pu nì u-ŋambijal ŋgiil yal pu nì u-taŋambijal ŋgiil yal pu. 26Ú bàtī ŋkpam kí ŋá u-ŋantil ŋgan yal poon. 27Ú dū u-ŋambidakakaai ŋgiil yal kí sēē ŋkpam min kā u-ŋantil ŋgan yal poonee kí yàaǹ ti-Dindaan nimbiin ŋfunyɔm miluli. 28Míǹ boonee ní ú dū ŋkpam min kā u-ŋantilinee kí jōō un jɔkɔnti u bíi fíntée tafalam ŋgiil yal pu nì u-ŋambijal ŋgiil yal pu nì u-taŋambijal ŋgiil yal pu laakin u bàà dū dibɔkpil saraau fatikuu ki jōōyee táb. 29Ŋkpam min kíǹ ki kā u-ŋantilinee, ú dūú sìtī kijapaayee yil pu kí ŋá kii mara nín bālifì puee ti-Dindaan nimbiin kí fíntí udaan jɔkɔnti. 30U yaa ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee ní ú lēē ananjilee àá abeenanjilee diba, kí nóó nì tin udaan ŋúń ki cáańee. 31Ú dū-dì kí ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau ní kí dū din kíǹee kí ŋá saraawɔkaa, ní kí dū tijimpin saraau kí kūtì. Niinee ní usaraaŋal ń ŋá dikoobil nín bālifì puee ti-Dindaan nimbiin kí fíntí udaan jɔkɔnti.»
32Unyaŋgbanti un kaa cáá ŋŋmam kí cáań tin u máaǹ kí cáańee nín ŋáań saraabi bin kí nyā u-jɔkɔntinee marab dee.
Dinyaŋgbandi din tòó adiin puee marab
33Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn yii:
34«Ni yaa láa kɔ́ Kanaan tiŋki kin m làá dūú tīī-ni ní nīn kíǹ ki yèe poon, ní m yaa láa yāntì dinyaŋgbandi daaŋku nyáń kitiŋ kin poon ni kóòyee diiku kubɔ puee, 35un yì kudii gbantee ń dāá cùú ká usaraaŋal kí tùkù-u yii: <An bí-mi kii dinyaŋgbandi daaŋku bí m-diiku puee.> 36Usaraaŋal ń yàntī bí kóoǹ tin kɔkɔ pée bí kudii gbanti poonee kí nyāntí ní ú nín cù kí kpèè kudaaŋŋuee. Mimmee tin kɔkɔ bí ku-nee kaa kóò tijɔkɔndi. Míǹ boonee ní usaraaŋal ń kɔ́ kí kpèè kudiiyee. 37U yaa kɔ́ ki kpēē kudaaŋŋuee ní ki ká yii apɔkɔ sɔ̀m̀ gùŋgum, àá an máǹ gàaa ki ŋmɔ́ ki kɔ́ kudii guŋŋi poonee, 38ní ú nyā kí yūĺ kudiiyee punyɔkɔpu kí dū-ku kí pìin̄ áli iwiin iluli. 39Iwiin iluli dalee ní usaraaŋal ń fàtīí gítí kí kpèè kudiiyee. U yaa ká yii kudaaŋŋuee lālim̀ kudiiyee guŋŋi puee, 40ú yàntī bí lēē ataŋkpee ŋin pu ní kudaaŋŋuee kēe kí cáá fá kitiŋ kpaanceetiŋu, laakin bi féeń tin pée kɔ́ tijɔkɔndee. 41Ú yàntī bí kɔ́tí kudiiyee guŋŋi kɔkɔ poon kí cáá ntam min bi kɔ́tèe kí fá kitiŋ kpaanceetiŋu, tijɔkɔndi paaŋŋuee pu. 42Míǹ boonee bí nyàab̀ ataŋkpapɔɔn kí téeǹ ŋin bi lēēyee paaŋŋu ní kí fàtīí nyàab̀ ntampɔm kí póoń kudiiyee.
43«Bi yaa lēē ataŋkpee kudii pu míǹ ki kɔ́tì agun ki fātìi póoń ní míǹ boonee kudaaŋŋuee fātìi nyáńee, 44usaraaŋal ń fàtīí gítí kí kpèè. Kudaaŋŋuee yaa lālim̀ ki gbí kudii kɔkɔ poonee, an dàkà yii baa ti ŋūǹ kí nyāntí kudaaŋŋuee kudii gbanti pu dee. Kudiiyee kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. 45Bí gbá kí wīī kudiiyee, ní kí kóoǹ ku-taŋkpeeŋi nì ku-dɔi nì ku-tampóoŋkaam kɔkɔ kí cáá fá kitiŋ kpaanceetiŋu tijɔkɔndi paaŋŋuee pu.
46«Ŋyunti ŋun bi pīiǹ kudiiyee, un yaa kɔ́ ku-nee kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi kí cáá sāā kujoou. 47Un di yaa dōoǹ kudiiyee poon àá ki jíń ku-poon tijinee ń fíntí u-wampeeŋkaati.
48«Ama ŋyunti ŋun bi fātìi póoń kudiiyee, usaraaŋal yaa gítì ki kpēē ní ki ká yii kudaaŋŋuee kaa fātìi nyáńee, ú sòoǹ báà ŋma ń gbìl̄ yii kudiiyee nyáń tijɔkɔndin, kun puee kudaaŋŋuee wáŋkì.
49«Usaraaŋal yaa làá ŋá saraabi kí nyāntí kudiiyee tijɔkɔndinee, ú yòon̄ nnɔmbiyaamu muli nì busubu bun bi yíì yii seediree dɔŋu nì gulfaman nì kifaapibiki kin bi yíì isɔpee. 50Ú yàntī bí làntì nnɔmbiyaamuee kiba kí dū ki-fatikuu kí ŋá ditansambil din poon nnyimbul nyim kēe. 51Míǹ boonee ní ú yòon̄ kinɔmbiki kin kíǹee nì seedir dɔŋuee nì gulfamanee nì isɔpi faapibikee kí dūú bɔ̄ kinɔmbiki kin bi lāntèe fatikuu nì nnyimbul nyimee ni, kí yàaǹ kudiiyee pu ŋfunyɔm miluli. 52Míǹ ní usaraaŋal máaǹ kí ŋá ní kí dū kinɔmbikee fatikuu nì nnyimbul nyimee nì kinɔmbiki kin kíǹee nì seedir dɔŋuee nì isɔpi faapibikee nì gulfaman cínciŋee kí fíntí kudiiyee kí nyāntí-ku ku-jɔkɔntin. 53Ú dāá gíiǹ kinɔmbiki kin kíǹ baa kūūyee kí líí tisati watil pú. Míǹ boonee ní ú ŋá akoobil nín sá puee kí fíntí kudiiyee kí nyāntí ku-jɔkɔntin ní kú lafun nyā tijɔkɔndin.»
54Marab bin bi síiǹ dinyaŋgbandi nì kideeŋŋi, 55nì kudaaŋŋu kun tòó tiwampeeŋkaal nì adiin ki náań nì dinyaŋgbandee, 56nì ndulim nì tikalindi nì unil wunti laaba yaa líkitì ki máǹee puee dee. 57Marab gbanti di nìn yàntī bi béetí yii unil, àá tiwan kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi àá tàa kɔ́. Marab bin bi nìn síiǹ dinyaŋgbandi puee dee.

english_text:
Sexual Uncleanness
1The Lord told Moses and Aaron 2to say to the community of Israel:
Any man with an infected penis is unclean, 3whether it is stopped up or keeps dripping. 4Anything that he rests on or sits on is also unclean, 5-7and if you touch either these or him, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening.
8If you are spit on by the man, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening. 9-10Any saddle or seat on which the man sits is unclean. And if you touch or carry either of these, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening. 11If the man touches you without first washing his hands, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening. 12Any clay pot that he touches must be destroyed, and any wooden bowl that he touches must be washed.
13Seven days after the man gets well, he will be considered clean, if he washes his clothes and takes a bath in spring water. 14On the eighth day he must bring either two doves or two pigeons to the front of my sacred tent and give them to a priest. 15The priest will offer one of the birds as a sacrifice for sin and the other as a sacrifice to please me, then I will consider the man completely clean.
16Any man who has a flow of semen must take a bath, but he still remains unclean until evening. 17If the semen touches anything made of cloth or leather, these must be washed, but they still remain unclean until evening. 18After having sex, both the man and the woman must take a bath, but they still remain unclean until evening.
19When a woman has her monthly period, she remains unclean for seven days, and if you touch her, you must take a bath, but you remain unclean until evening. 20-23Anything that she rests on or sits on is also unclean, and if you touch either of these, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening. 24Any man who has sex with her during this time becomes unclean for seven days, and anything he rests on is also unclean.
25Any woman who has a flow of blood outside her regular monthly period is unclean until it stops, just as she is during her monthly period. 26Anything that she rests on or sits on during this time is also unclean, just as it would be during her period. 27If you touch either of these, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening.
28Seven days after the woman gets well, she will be considered clean. 29On the eighth day, she must bring either two doves or two pigeons to the front of my sacred tent and give them to a priest. 30He will offer one of the birds as a sacrifice for sin and the other as a sacrifice to please me; then I will consider the woman completely clean.
31When any of you are unclean, you must stay away from the rest of the community of Israel. Otherwise, my sacred tent will become unclean, and the whole nation will die.
32-33These are the things you men must do if you become unclean because of an infected penis or if you have a flow of semen. And these are the things you women must do when you become unclean either because of your monthly period or an unusual flow of blood. This is also what you men must do if you have sex with a woman who is unclean.
translation_text:
Uninja jɔkɔnti pu marab
1Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn yii 2bí tùkù Isirayeel yab yii:
«Batiku yaa cúú uninjee, tináti tin nyēē-uee kɔ́ǹ-u tijɔkɔndi. 3Tinátee yaa bíi nyēēyaaa, tì yaa tīkiǹaaa, udaan kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. 4Ndoo ŋun kamaa pu udaan yaa dōoǹee kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi, ní tin kamaa pu ní u yaa kāl̀ee mun kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. 5Un di yaa pée gbēē u-dooŋuee máaǹ kí fíntí u-wampeeŋkaati, kí fàl̀, ní ki làá nīn bí tijɔkɔndin kí cáá sāā kujoou. 6Un di yaa pée kāl̀ kun pu ní ubatikudaan kāl̀ee máaǹ kí fíntí u-wampeeŋkaati, kí fàl̀, ní ki làá nīn bí tijɔkɔndin kí cáá sāā kujoou. 7Un di yaa gbēē ubatikudaanee máaǹ kí fíntí u-wampeeŋkaati, kí fàl̀, ní ki làá nīn bí tijɔkɔndin kí cáá sāā kujoou. 8Ubatikudaan yaa tíil̀ ki pɔ̀l̄ unil un kaa kɔ́ tijɔkɔndee puee, udaan máaǹ kí fíntí u-wampeeŋkaati, kí fàl̀, ní ki làá nīn bí tijɔkɔndin kí cáá sāā kujoou. 9Dijal din kamaa pu ní ubatikudaan yaa kāl̀ ki cūtì nsanee kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. 10Un di yaa pée gbēē tin kamaa dɔ̄ ubatikudaan taapuee kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi kí cáá sāā kujoou. Un di yaa tí yōoǹ tiwan gbanti ki túǹee máaǹ kí fíntí u-wampeeŋkaati, kí fàl̀, ní ki làá nīn bí tijɔkɔndin kí cáá sāā kujoou. 11Unil un kamaa ní ubatikudaan yaa kaa fíntì u-ŋal ki gbēēyee máaǹ kí fíntí u-wampeeŋkaati, kí fàl̀, ní ki làá nīn bí tijɔkɔndin kí cáá sāā kujoou. 12Ditansambil din kamaa ní ubatikudaan yaa gbēēyee, bí gbá kí wīī-dì. An yaa sá ndɔ sambilee, bí dū nnyim tikpil kí fíntí-dì.
13«Tináti tin nìn nyēē ubatikudaan ki kɔ́ǹ-u tijɔkɔndee yaa gúń u pɔ́ɔkèe, ú gíti kàl̄ iwiin iluli ní kí nín nyā u-jɔkɔntin. Ú fíntí u-wampeeŋkaati, kí dū nnyimbul nyim kí fàl̀ ní kí nín nyā tijɔkɔndin. 14Iwiin inii dalee, ú nyàab̀ ananjil ali àá abeenanjil ali kí cáá cùnnì ti-Dindaan nimbiin, circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu, kí dūú tīī usaraaŋal. 15Usaraaŋal ń dū diba kí ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau ní kí dū din kíǹee kí ŋá saraawɔkaa. Ú ŋá dikoobil nín bālifì puee ti-Dindaan nimbiin kí fíntí udaan batikuu jɔkɔnti.
16«Uninja yaa nyéem̀ tijatee, u máaǹ kí fàl̀, ní ki làá nīn bí tijɔkɔndin kí cáá sāā kujoou. 17Tijatee yaa táká tiwampeeŋkaal tiba àá ŋgban wanti tibee, bí dū nnyim kí fíntí-tì. Tì làá nīn bí tijɔkɔndin kí cáá sāā kujoou.
18«Uninja yaa dōoǹ nì unimpuee, bi-liitil máaǹ kí fàl̀, ní ki làá nīn bí tijɔkɔndin kí cáá sāā kujoou.»
Unimpu jɔkɔnti pu marab
19«Unimpu yaa bíi fùul̀ ŋkpinee, u kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi kí cáá sāā iwiin iluli. Un mun di yaa gbēē-uee kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi kí cáá sāā kujoou. 20Ndoo ŋun kamaa pu ní unimpuee yaa dōoǹ ŋyunti gbanti kɔkɔee kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi, ní tiwan tin kamaa pu ní u yaa pée kāl̀ee mun kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. 21Un di yaa pée gbēē u-dooŋuee mun kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. Udaan máaǹ kí fíntí u-wampeeŋkaati, kí fàl̀, ní ki làá nīn bí tijɔkɔndin kí cáá sāā kujoou. 22Un di yaa pée gbēē kun pu ní unimpu gbanti kāl̀ee ń fíntí u-wampeeŋkaati, kí fàl̀, ní ki làá nīn bí tijɔkɔndin kí cáá sāā kujoou. 23Tiba yaa pá ndoo ŋun pu unimpu gbanti dɔ̄ee, àá dijal din pu u kēe ní ubɔ dɔ́miń ki gbēē tiwan gbantee, udaan kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi kí cáá sāā kujoou. 24Uninja yaa dōoǹ nì u ŋyunti gbanti poon ní u-fatikuu nyáń ki gbēē-uee, uninjee mun kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi kí cáá sāā iwiin iluli. Uninja gbanti mun yaa dōoǹ ndoo ŋun puee kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi.
25«Unimpu yaa fùl̄ ŋkpin iwiin kupaau ní an kaa sá u-kpiŋŋu yuntiŋu, àá u-kpiŋŋu yaa jítì iwiin in an bàà sá an gúńee, u bí tijɔkɔndin ŋyunti gbanti kɔkɔ poon kii u nín pée kpààa kāntí u-ba iyunti in máaǹee puee. 26Ndoo ŋun pu ní u yaa pée dōoǹee, àá dijal din pu ní u yaa kāl̀ ŋyunti gbanti poonee kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi kii u nín pée kpààa fùul̀ ŋkpin iyunti in máaǹee puee. 27Un di yaa gbēē ndoo àá dijal gbantee máaǹ kí fíntí u-wampeeŋkaati, kí fàl̀, ní ki làá nīn bí tijɔkɔndin kí cáá sāā kujoou.
28«Ŋwiin ŋun u-kpiŋŋu gúńee, ú gíti kàl̄ iwiin iluli ní kí nín nyā tijɔkɔndin. 29Iwiin inii dalee, ú nyàab̀ ananjil ali àá abeenanjil ali kí cáań kí tīī usaraaŋal, circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu. 30Usaraaŋal ń dū nnɔmbiyaamuee kiba kí ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau, kí dū kin kíǹee kí ŋá saraawɔkaa. Míǹ boonee usaraaŋal ń ŋá dikoobil nín bālifì puee unimpuee pu ti-Dindaan nimbiin kí fíntí u nín fùl̄ ŋkpin puee jɔkɔnti.»
31Ti-Dindaan nìn gíti bí Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn yii: «Ní kpāafì Isirayeel yab bí taa sútí kí pìl̄ m-kɔŋkooŋŋu ŋyunti ŋun bi yaa bí tijɔkɔndinee. Di sá yii bi yaa kɔ́ǹ m-kɔŋkooŋŋu ŋun bí bi-kansikinee tijɔkɔndee, see bí kpú.»
32Marab bin bi síiǹ ubatikudaan àá un di yaa nyéem̀ tijati ki kɔ́ tijɔkɔndinee dee. 33Marab gbanti sá ki tīī unimpu un fùl̄ ŋkpinee àá uninja àá unimpu un fatiku nyēē-uee àá uninja un di yaa dōoǹ nì unimpu un bí tijɔkɔndinee mun.

english_text:
The Great Day of Forgiveness
1-2 Two of Aaron's sons had already lost their lives for disobeying the Lord, so the Lord told Moses to say to Aaron:
I, the Lord, appear in a cloud over the place of mercy on the sacred chest, which is behind the inside curtain of the sacred tent. And I warn you not to go there except at the proper time. Otherwise, you will die!
3 Before entering this most holy place, you must offer a bull as a sacrifice for your sins and a ram as a sacrifice to please me. 4You will take a bath and put on the sacred linen clothes, including the underwear, the robe, the sash, and the turban. 5Then the community of Israel will bring you a ram and two goats, both of them males. The goats are to be used as sacrifices for sin, and the ram is to be used as a sacrifice to please me.
6Aaron, you must offer the bull as a sacrifice of forgiveness for your own sins and for the sins of your family. 7Then you will lead the two goats into my presence at the front of the sacred tent, 8where I will show you which goat will be sacrificed to me and which one will be sent into the desert to the demon Azazel. 9After you offer the first goat as a sacrifice for sin, 10the other one must be presented to me alive, before you send it into the desert to take away the sins of the people.
11You must offer the bull as a sacrifice to ask forgiveness for your own sins and for the sins of your family. 12Then you will take a fire pan of live coals from the bronze altar, together with two handfuls of finely ground incense, into the most holy place. 13There you will present them to me by placing the incense on the coals, so that the place of mercy will be covered with a cloud of smoke. Do this, or you will die right there! 14Next, use a finger to sprinkle some of the blood on the place of mercy, which is on the lid of the sacred chest; then sprinkle blood seven times in front of the chest.
15 Aaron, you must next sacrifice the goat for the sins of the people, and you must sprinkle its blood inside the most holy place, just as you did with the blood of the bull. 16By doing this, you will take away the sins that make both the most holy place and the people of Israel unclean. Do the same for the sacred tent, which is here among the people. 17Only you are allowed in the sacred tent from the time you enter until the time you come out. 18After leaving the tent, you will purify the bronze altar by smearing each of its four corners with some of the blood from the bull and from the goat. 19Use a finger to sprinkle the altar seven times with the blood, and it will be completely clean from the sins of the people.
20After you have purified the most holy place, the sacred tent, and the bronze altar, you must bring the live goat to the front of the tent. 21 There you will lay your hands on its head, while confessing every sin the people have committed, and you will appoint someone to lead the goat into the desert, so that it can take away their sins. 22Finally, this goat that carries the heavy burden of Israel's sins must be released deep in the desert.
23-24 Aaron, after this you must go inside the sacred tent, take a bath, put on your regular priestly clothes, and leave there the clothes you put on before entering the most holy place. Then you will come out and offer sacrifices to please me and sacrifices for your sins and for the sins of the people. 25The fat from these sacrifices for sin must be sent up in smoke on the bronze altar.
26The one who led the goat into the desert and sent it off to the demon Azazel must take a bath and wash his clothes before coming back into camp. 27 The remains of the bull and the goat whose blood was taken into the most holy place must be taken outside the camp and burned. 28And whoever does this must take a bath and change clothes before coming back into camp.
The Lord told Moses to say to the people:
29 On the tenth day of the seventh month of each year, you must go without eating to show sorrow for your sins, and no one, including foreigners who live among you, is allowed to work. 30This is the day on which the sacrifice for the forgiveness of your sins will be made in my presence, 31and from now on, it must be celebrated each year. Go without eating and make this a day of complete rest just like the Sabbath. 32The high priest must offer the sacrifices for cleansing from sin, while wearing the sacred linen clothes. 33He will offer these sacrifices for the most holy place, the sacred tent, the bronze altar, all the priests, and for the whole community. 34You must celebrate this day each year—it is the Great Day of Forgiveness for all the sins of the people of Israel.
Moses did exactly as the Lord had commanded.
translation_text:
Ikpiti pɔ̄tam wiŋkpaaŋŋu bɔti
1Aarɔn jipɔmbi bili nín nìn sútì ki pìl̄ ti-Dindaan ki kpíìyee boonee, ti-Dindaan nìn sòon̄ nì Mooyiisi. 2U nìn bí-u yii: «Tùkù a-maan Aarɔn yii ú taa nín̄ kóò ŋyunti ŋun ní u yaa lèe circir páaa laŋki, ŋŋaapìtikaa boon, laakin dipoondi dakaau nì u-bìil sée.
