Bóob́maan dikɔ̀ndi kí jáǹ-u kí fōō u-tiŋki. 25Kí yòon̄ díǹ kí nīn cée, m làá yàntī anibul ŋin kɔkɔ bí kitiŋ puee ń fàŋkì-ni. Bi yaa láa pée gbìl̄ ni-puee, dinyoondi dāa cútí-bi ní bi-wunti jìkì ki gbáà kpàkpakpa.»
Isirayeel yab jáń ki fōō ubɔti Siiwɔn tiŋki
26Niinee ní m dū binib ki tú doooo Kideemooti teeku bí cù kí sòoǹ nì Siiwɔn, Eesbɔn bɔtiu nì ŋgbansɔŋfi poon kí tùkù-u yii: 27«Pɔ̄-ti nsan tí jītí a-tiŋki pu. Ti làá nīn pée tàkā didandi ní cáaa kí jītí. Taa làá pàatī ŋgan púɔɔɔ, kaa làá kpòotī kí cù ŋgiil pú. 28Nì ti-nimbiliŋ ní ti làá dā tijin kí jī ní kí dā nnyim mun kí nyɔ̀. Kun ti pée là a-ceeyee di sá á pɔ̄-ti nsan tí còom̀ kí jītí a-tiŋki pu. 29Kpèè, Eesayuu yab bin kóò Seeyiir tiŋkinee nì Moowaab yab bin mun kóò Aari tiŋkinee pú-ti nsan ti jítì bi-timmu pu. An puee ti pée là yii á yàntī tí jītí a-tiŋki pu kí tin dùtī Jɔɔdan buŋŋu kí kɔ́ kitiŋ kin ní ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu làá dūú tīī-tee poon ní.» 30Ama Eesbɔn bɔtiu Siiwɔn nìn yíì kaa pú-ti nsan tí jītí u-tiŋki pu, di sá yii ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nìn pɔ́ɔkì u-tafal nì u-pɔbil. U nìn ŋá míǹ kí dū u-tiŋki kí ŋá ni-ŋaan kii díǹ pu nee ni nín lafun yì-kì pu nan ní. 31Niinee ní ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: «Kpèè, kɔŋkɔnnee m dū Siiwɔn nì u-tiŋki ki ŋá ni-ŋaan. Kíĺ kí jámaan kí fōō u-tiŋki kí nīn kíǹ ki yì.» 32Niinee ní Siiwɔn nì u-janjakitil kɔkɔ nyánní kí já nì ti Yaasa tiŋkin. 33Ama ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu nìn dū-u ki ŋá ti-ŋaan ní ti jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ u nì u-jipɔmbi nì u-samaau kɔkɔ. 34Niinee ní ti fōō u-timmu kɔkɔ ní ki kūū ki céetì mu-nib kɔkɔ. Uninjeeee, unimpueeee, kibikeeee, báà unil kaa nìn kíǹ. 35Tin timbi ti-ba nìn pée yōoǹee di nìn sá tiwaŋkuti nì tigaajawan tin ti nìn ká ntimu gbanti poonee. 36Kí yòon̄ Arooweer tiŋki kin bí Arinɔn buŋgbandee nì kitiŋ kin mun bí Arinɔn tantakalin kí cáá sāā Galaadee, kitiŋ kiba kaa nìn kíǹ taa ŋúń ki jáń ki fōō-kì, di sá yii ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu nìn dū mu-kɔkɔ ki ŋá ti-ŋaan ní. 37Asee Amɔn yab tiŋki nì ntimu mun nìn bí Yaabɔki buŋgbaŋŋee nì ntimu mun bí ajoonnee nì laakin ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu nìn kpáafì-ti yii tí taa gbēēyee baba ní taa nìn fōō.

english_text:
The Defeat of King Og of Bashan
(Numbers 21.31-35)
Moses said to Israel:
1When we turned onto the road that leads to Bashan, King Og of Bashan led out his whole army to fight us at Edrei. 2But the Lord told me, “Moses, don't be afraid of King Og. I am going to help you defeat him and his army and take over his land. Destroy him and his people, just as you did with the Amorite King Sihon of Heshbon.”
3-6The Lord our God helped us destroy Og and his army and conquer his entire kingdom of Bashan, including the Argob region. His kingdom had lots of villages and 60 towns with high walls and gates that locked with bars. We completely destroyed them all, killing everyone, 7but keeping the livestock and everything else of value.
8Sihon and Og had ruled Amorite kingdoms east of the Jordan River. Their land stretched from the Arnon River gorge in the south to Mount Hermon in the north, and we captured it all. 9Mount Hermon is called Mount Sirion by the people of Sidon, and it is called Mount Senir by the Amorites. 10We captured all the towns in the highlands, all of Gilead, and all of Bashan as far as Salecah and Edrei, two of the towns that Og had ruled.
Og's Coffin
11King Og was the last of the Rephaim, and his coffin is in the town of Rabbah in Ammon. It is made of hard black rock and is four meters long and almost two meters wide.
The Land East of the Jordan River Is Divided
(Numbers 32.1-42)
Moses said to Israel:
12-17I gave some of the land and towns we captured to the tribes of Reuben and Gad. Their share started at the Arnon River gorge in the south, took in the town of Aroer on the edge of the gorge, and went far enough north to include the southern half of the Gilead region. The northern part of their land went as far east as the upper Jabbok River gorge, which formed their border with the Ammonites. I also gave them the eastern side of the Jordan River valley, from Lake Galilee south to the Dead Sea below the slopes of Mount Pisgah.
I gave the northern half of Gilead and all of the Bashan region to half the tribe of Manasseh. Bashan had belonged to King Og, and the Argob region in Bashan used to be called the Land of the Rephaim. Jair from the Manasseh tribe conquered the Argob region as far west as the kingdoms of Geshur and Maacah. The Israelites even started calling Bashan by the name “Villages of Jair,” and that is still its name. I gave the northern half of Gilead to the Machir clan.
18-19 At that time I told the men of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh:
The Lord our God told me to give you this land with its towns, and that's what I have done. Now your wives and children can stay here with your large flocks of sheep and goats and your large herds of cattle. But all of you men that can serve in our army must cross the Jordan River and help the other tribes, because they are your relatives. 20The Lord will let them defeat the enemy nations on the west side of the Jordan and take their land. Afterwards, you can come back here to the land I gave you.
21-22Then I told Joshua, “You saw how the Lord our God helped us destroy King Sihon and King Og. So don't be afraid! Wherever you go, the Lord will fight on your side and help you destroy your enemies.”
God Refused To Let Moses Enter Canaan
Moses said to Israel:
23 At that time I prayed and begged, 24“Our Lord, it seems that you have just begun to show me your great power. No other god in the sky or on earth is able to do the mighty things that you do. 25The land west of the Jordan is such good land. Please let me cross the Jordan and see the hills and the Lebanon Mountains.”
26But the Lord was angry with me because of you people, and he refused to listen. “That's enough!” he said. “I don't want to hear any more. 27Climb to the top of Mount Pisgah and look north, south, east, and west. Take a good look, but you are not going to cross the Jordan River. 28Joshua will lead Israel across the Jordan to take the land, so help him be strong and brave and tell him what he must do.”
29After this we stayed in the valley at Beth-Peor.
translation_text:
Isirayeel yab jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Baasan bɔtiu Ɔɔgi
1Míǹ boonee ní ti kíĺ Baasan saŋŋu ki nín cá. Ŋyunti ŋun Baasan bɔtiu Ɔɔgi ká-tee ní u nì u-samaau kɔkɔ kíntì-ti Eedreeyii tiŋkin kí já nì ti. 2Niinee ní ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: «Taa fàŋkì-u, kun puee m dū-u ki ŋá a-ŋaan ki kpáaǹ u-samaau kɔkɔ nì u-tiŋki. Kii a nín ŋá Amɔɔr yab bɔtiu Siiwɔn un nìn kóò Eesbɔn tiŋkin puee, míǹ ní á ŋá u mun.» 3Ní ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu dū Baasan bɔtiu Ɔɔgi mun nì u-samaau kɔkɔ ki ŋá ti-ŋaan ní ti kūū ki céetì-bi múb, kaa kíǹ báà ubɔ. 4Niinee ní ti fōō u-timmu kɔkɔ. Báà kitiŋ kaa nìn kíǹ taa fōō u-ŋaan. Ntimu gbanti nìn nyáń imuŋku ita, Argoob laguŋku kɔkɔn, Baasan tiŋkin, laakin Ɔɔgi jíń dibeelee. 5Bi nìn máń aguŋfɔkɔ ki māntìi tú ntimu gbanti kɔkɔ. Mu nìn cáá mpunyɔmu nì tikpàlkaal. Ama ntimbilimu tikpil mun nìn bí baa nìn máń agun ki tú-mu. 6Ti nìn nāaǹ ntimu gbanti kɔkɔ ní ki kūū ki céetì mu-nib kɔkɔ, bininjab nì binimpoobi nì mbiyaamu, kii ti nín nìn ŋá Eesbɔn bɔtiu Siiwɔn puee. 7Ama ti nìn yōoǹ tiwaŋkuti nì tigaajawan tin ti nìn jáń ki fōō ntimu gbanti poonee kɔkɔ.
Bi yākatì Galaadi tiŋki
8Ti nìn jáń nì Amɔɔr yab bɔtiibi bilee ní ki fōō bi-timmu. Ntimu gbanti nìn bí Jɔɔdan, ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú ní, kí yòon̄ Arinɔn buŋŋu kí cáá sāā Eermɔn jool. 9- Siidɔn yab yíì Eermɔn jool yii Siiriyɔn, ní Amɔn yab yíì-dì yii Seeniir. - 10Ti nìn fōō ntimu mun nìn bí kigbantaŋ puee nì Galaadi jool puee kɔkɔ, ki kpáaǹ Baasan tiŋki kɔkɔ ki cáá sāā Salka nì Eedreeyii, Baasan timmu mun pu ubɔti Ɔɔgi nìn kāl̀ dibeelee. 11Reefa yab maaliŋu poonee, Baasan bɔtiu Ɔɔgi di nìn pée sá unibambaanti un nìn kíǹ ki bí dimaŋfalinee. U nìn cáá tikúti lambaŋki kiba. Kilambaŋ gbanti gbíntìi bí díǹ pu nee Raaba, Amɔn yab tiŋkin. Kilambaŋ gbanti púuŋŋu nìn sá meetab binaa ní ki-waaŋŋu sá meetab bili.
Bi yākatì ntimu mun bi jáń ki fōōyee
12Ntimu mun ti nìn jáń ki fōō ŋyunti gbantee dee. M nìn dū dijandi din bí kí yòon̄ Arooweer tiŋki kin bí Arinɔn buŋŋu caŋinee ki kpáaǹ Galaadi jool dijandi nì di-timmu ki tīī Rubeen nì Gaadi naakɔti yab. 13Galaadi jool dijandi din kíǹee nì Baasan tiŋki, an dàkà yii Ɔɔgi nín nìn kā ntimu mun pu dibeelee kɔkɔee, m nìn dūu tīī Manasee naakooku yab dijandi diba ní. Bi nìn yíì Argoob laguŋku kun bí Baasan tiŋkinee yii Reefa yab tinikpaandi tiŋki. 14Yayiir un sá Manasee naantiiuee di nìn jáń ki fōō Argoob laguŋku gbanti kɔkɔ ki tin cáa sāā Geesuur nì Maakati timmu, ní ki nìn dū u-yindi ki pú Baasan timmu gbanti. An pu ní bi yíì ntimbilimu gbanti yii Yayiir timbilimmu ki dāa sāā díǹ. 15M nìn dū Galaadi tiŋki ki tīī Manasee naantiiu Makiir ní. 16Ama Rubeen nì Gaadi yabee, m nìn dū kitiŋ kin dɔ̄ kí yòon̄ Galaadi kí tin cáá sāā Arinɔn buŋŋuee ní ki tīī-bi. Bi-tiŋki kpaanyɔkɔ ń nīn bí mbun gbanti kansikin, kí cáá sāā Yaabɔki buŋŋu ŋun sá Amɔn yab timmu kpaanyɔkɔee. 17Kikpaanyɔkɔ kin bí ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki watil pú ki dī Jɔɔdan tantakal din bí Kiineereeti mɔɔl nì Ŋyaam mɔɔl kansikinee, ní ki nìkī ki tin sāā Piisga jool din bí ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee taapu.
18Niinee ní m kpáafì-bi yii: «Ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu di tīī-ni kitiŋ nee kí nīn sá ni-yaka. Ni-kansikin bininjab bin sá bijanjaliibee kɔkɔ ń gbìn̄ bi-gbajab kí jītí kí lìntī ni-nabiyaamu Isirayeel yab nyɔkɔpu kí dùtī Jɔɔdan buŋŋu kí cù kujaau. 19Ama ni-nimpoobi nì ni-biyaamu nì ni-waŋkuti ń gbíntí ntimu mun m tīī-nee poon, kun puee m nyí ni nín cáá tiwaŋkuti tikpilee. 20Ní tūtuǹ ni-nabiyaamu kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋun ní ti-Dindaan làá tīī-bi diŋuŋfil bi mun ń fōō kitiŋ kin ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá tīī-bi Jɔɔdan buŋgbandi din bí lapu pu kii u nín ŋá pu ki tīī ni muee. Míǹ boonee ní ni-kɔkɔ ń dāá gítí ni-timmu mun ní m yākatì ki tīī-nee poon.»
21Ŋyunti gbanti mbaanti ní m kpáafì Joosuwa yii: «Sii a-ba nimbil ká ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nín ŋá bibɔtiibi bili nee puee. Míǹ mbaantiim ní u làá ŋá ntimu mun bí lapu pu buŋgbandee bɔtiibi bin a làá tin kée mun. 22Ní taa fàŋkì-bi, kun puee ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu di yì dikɔ̀ndi kí já kí tīī-ni.»
Mooyiisi kaa làá kɔ́ Kanaan tiŋkin
23Niinee ní m mēē ki gbāam̀ ti-Dindaan yii: 24«Ti-Dindaan m-Nimbɔtiu, sii di kíĺ ki dàkā man a-tɔntɔnliu a nín sá ukpaan miŋyee nì a-pɔŋŋu, di sá yii unimbɔti ubɔ kaa ti bí yilpu àá taapu ki ŋūǹ kí ŋá a-maamaaci tuuŋŋi nee juti! 25An puee m pée gbàam̄-si ní, á yàntī m pée dùtī Jɔɔdan buŋŋu kí tin ká kitimmɔntii kin bí niinee nì dijoomɔntiil gbanti nì Leebanɔn tiŋki.»
26Ama ni-puee, ti-Dindaan gíí m-pu diŋuul kaa pílifiǹ-mi, ní ki bí-mi yii: «An ŋmēetèe, á taa ti pée sòoǹ tibɔti gbanti man cee. 27Jɔ̄m̀ Piisga jool yilpu kí kpèè kí màntīí tū ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú nì ŋgan pú nì ŋgiil pú nì ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú, kí kpítí a-nimbiliŋ kí kpèè tiŋan, ama a kpá kí dùtī Jɔɔdan buŋŋu nee. 28An puee, á kpāafì Joosuwa, kí tīī-u kunyannyaau ú mɔ̀tīi ká mpɔn, kun puee úǹ di làá nīn līī samaa nee nyɔkɔpu kí cáá-bi kí dùtī Jɔɔdan ní kí fōō kitiŋ kin a làá kpèè nee kí tīī-bi bí nīn kíǹ ki yì.»
29Niinee ní ti gbíntì ditantakalin ki pìlīǹ Beeti-Peewɔɔr tiŋki.

english_text:
Israel Must Obey God
Moses said:
1Israel, listen to these laws and teachings! If you obey them, you will live, and you will go in and take the land that the Lord is giving you. He is the God your ancestors worshiped, 2 and now he is your God. I am telling you everything he has commanded, so don't add anything or take anything away.
3 You saw how he killed everyone who worshiped the god Baal Peor. 4But all of you that were faithful to the Lord your God are still alive today.
5-8 No other nation has laws that are as fair as the ones the Lord my God told me to give you. If you faithfully obey them when you enter the land, you will show other nations how wise you are. In fact, everyone that hears about your laws will say, “That great nation certainly is wise!” And what makes us greater than other nations? We have a God who is close to us and answers our prayers.
9You must be very careful not to forget the things you have seen God do for you. Keep reminding yourselves, and tell your children and grandchildren as well. 10Do you remember the day you stood in the Lord's presence at Mount Sinai? The Lord said, “Moses, bring the people of Israel here. I want to speak to them so they will obey me as long as they live, and so they will teach their children to obey me too.”
11 Mount Sinai was surrounded by deep dark clouds, and fire went up to the sky. You came to the foot of the mountain, 12and the Lord spoke to you from the fire. You could hear him and understand what he was saying, but you couldn't see him. 13 The Lord said he was making an agreement with you, and he told you that your part of the agreement is to obey the Ten Commandments. Then the Lord wrote these Commandments on two flat stones.
14 That's when the Lord commanded me to give you the laws and teachings you must obey in the land that you will conquer west of the Jordan River.
Don't Worship Idols
Moses said to Israel:
15When God spoke to you from the fire, he was invisible. So be careful 16 not to commit the sin of worshiping idols. Don't make idols to be worshiped, whether they are shaped like men, women, 17 animals, birds, 18reptiles, or fish. 19And when you see the sun or moon or stars, don't be tempted to bow down and worship them. The Lord put them there for all the other nations to worship. 20 But you are the Lord's people, because he rescued you from Egypt, that fiery furnace.
21 The Lord was angry with me because of what you said, and he told me that he would not let me cross the Jordan River into the good land that he is giving you. 22So I must stay here and die on this side of the Jordan, but you will cross the river and take the land.
23Always remember the agreement that the Lord your God made with you, and don't make an idol in any shape or form. 24 The Lord will be angry if you worship other gods, and he can be like a fire destroying everything in its path.
25-26Soon you will cross the Jordan River and settle down in the land. Then in the years to come, you will have children, and they will give you grandchildren. After many years, you might lose your sense of right and wrong and make idols, even though the Lord your God hates them. So I am giving you fair warning today, and I call the earth and the sky as witnesses. If you ever make idols, the Lord will be angry, and you won't have long to live, because the Lord will let you be wiped out. 27 Only a few of you will survive, and the Lord will force you to leave the land and will scatter you among the nations. 28There you will have to worship gods made of wood and stone, and these are nothing but idols that can't see or hear or eat or smell.
29-30 In all of your troubles, you may finally decide that you want to worship only the Lord. And if you turn back to him and obey him completely, he will again be your God. 31The Lord your God will have mercy—he won't destroy you or desert you. The Lord will remember his promise, and he will keep the agreement he made with your ancestors.
32-34When the Lord your God brought you out of Egypt, you saw how he fought for you and showed his great power by performing terrifying miracles. You became his people, and at Mount Sinai you heard him talking to you out of fiery flames. And yet you are still alive! Has anything like this ever happened since the time God created humans? No matter where you go or who you ask, you will get the same answer. No one has ever heard of another god even trying to do such things as the Lord your God has done for you.
35-36 The Lord wants you to know he is the only true God, and he wants you to obey him. That's why he let you see his mighty miracles and his fierce fire on earth, and why you heard his voice from that fire and from the sky.
37The Lord loved your ancestors and decided that you would be his people. So the Lord used his great power to bring you out of Egypt. 38Now you face other nations more powerful than you are, but the Lord has already started forcing them out of their land and giving it to you.
39So remember that the Lord is the only true God, whether in the sky above or on the earth below. 40Today I am explaining his laws and teachings. And if you always obey them, you and your descendants will live long and be successful in the land the Lord is giving you.
Safe Towns
41-43 Moses said, “People of Israel, you must set aside the following three towns east of the Jordan River as Safe Towns: Bezer in the desert highlands belonging to the Reuben tribe; Ramoth in Gilead, belonging to the Gad tribe; and Golan in Bashan, belonging to the Manasseh tribe. If you kill a neighbor without meaning to, and if you had not been angry with that person, you can run to one of these towns and find safety.”
The Second Speech: Moses Tells What the Lord Demands
Israel at Beth-Peor
44-46The Israelites had come from Egypt and were camped east of the Jordan River near Beth-Peor, when Moses gave these laws and teachings. The land around their camp had once belonged to King Sihon of Heshbon. But Moses and the Israelites defeated him 47and King Og of Bashan, and took their lands. These two Amorite kings had ruled the territory east of the Jordan River 48from the town of Aroer on the edge of the Arnon River gorge, north to Mount Hermon. 49Their land included the eastern side of the Jordan River valley, as far south as the Dead Sea below the slopes of Mount Pisgah.
translation_text:
Unimbɔti tīī u-nibooliŋu marab
1Kɔŋkɔnnee Isirayeel yab, pīlifìmaan abɔkpaa nì akoobil ŋin mama m-ba bíi cáa dàkà-ni nee kí ŋá ŋi nín bí yii ní ŋá puee. Ni yaa ŋá mimmee, ni làá nīn bí dimaŋfalin ní kí kɔ́ kí fōō kitiŋ kin ní ti-Dindaan, ni-baabi Nimbɔtiu làá dūú tīī-ni nee. 2Ní taa gbéeǹ tiba nì tiba tibɔti tin man cáa kpáafí-ni nee pu, kí taa tí bàtī tiba mun ti-pu kí fá. Ní nīn ŋúb́ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu marab bin m cáa bíi kpáafí-ni nee.
3Nimbi ni-ba ni-nimbil ká tin ti-Dindaan nìn ŋá Baal Peewɔɔr tiŋkinee. Ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nìn kūū ki céetì bin kɔkɔ nìn pée jáam̀ diwaal Baal Peewɔɔree ki nyántì ni-kansikin. 4Ama nimbi bin nìn síl̀ nì ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu deedeeyee, ni-kɔkɔ gbíntìi bí dimaŋfalin díǹ pu.
5Kpèèmaan, m dàkā-ni abɔkpaa nì akoobil kii ti-Dindaan m-Nimbɔtiu nín kpáafì-mi puee. Ni yaa láa bàn̄ kitiŋ kin ni làá kɔ́ kí fōō kí nīn kíǹ ki yèe poonee, ní dū-ŋi kí ŋá ditundi. 6Ni yaa ŋúb́ abɔkpaa gbanti tiŋanee, anibul ŋin kíǹee làá dāá gbìl̄ bi sòoǹ ni-marab nee pu ní bí yíiń-ni binyiliibi nì biciŋfitiibi kí lì yii: «Tiŋman, ditimbuŋkpaandi nee nib lafun sá binyiliibi nì biciŋfitiibeeee!» 7Tiŋman, ditimbundi dilal, báà di yaa sá dikpaandi min min ní di-waaŋi pìl̄-dì kii ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu nín pìl̄-ti ki ŋáań tikɔkɔ ki tìì-ti ŋyunti ŋun ní ti yaa kúuǹ ki yíiń-u na? 8Ditimbuŋkpaandi diba gíti bí ki cáá abɔkpaa nì akoobil sá amɔnti kii marab bin m cáa tìì-ni díǹ naaa?
9Ama ní cúúmaan ni-ba, ní nīn nyíǹ ni-ba tiŋan kí taa súntí tin tin ni-nimbil kée. Ní yàntī tin ni kée ń nīn kā ni-pɔbilin ní nīn cáá-tì ki dàkà ni-biyaamu nì ni-naantiibi, ni-maŋfal wiiŋyi kɔkɔ poon.
10Ní téetí ŋwiin ŋun ni nìn síl̀ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nimbiin Ooreeb jool caŋinee. Ti-Dindaan nìn tùkū-mi yii: «Kóoǹ samaa nee kɔkɔ kí kpāfì m-cee. M làá yàntī bí gbìl̄ m-nyɔɔbuŋŋi án nín làá ŋá pu bi-wiiŋyi in kɔkɔ bi cáá kí kàl̄ kitiŋ nee puee, bí bīfì kí nīn kíǹ ki fàŋkí-mi ní kí nīn cáa dàkà bi-biyaamuee.» 11Ŋyunti gbantee ní ni sútì ki pìl̄ dijool ki yú di-taapu. Dijool nìn fōō ŋŋmi ní aŋmilimbil nìn yíkí ki jɔ́ḿ kutaa ní atagbambɔn nì dibɔmbɔŋkpaandi nìn māntìi tú-dì. 12Ti-Dindaan nìn sòon̄ nì ni ŋŋmee poon. Nneen ŋubɔ nìn sòoǹ ní ni gbìl̀ nneenee pu, ama ní kaa wāĺ ubɔ. Kun kun ni nìn pée gbìl̀ee di sá nneen gbanti. 13U nìn cántì u-poondi din u pōoǹ-nee taapu ki tùkū-ni, ní ki bí yii ní ŋúb́ marab saalaa bin u síiǹ-nee. U nìn ŋmàn̄ marab gbanti titaŋkpapilindi tili pu. 14Ŋyunti gbanti mbaanti poon ní ti-Dindaan tīī-mi mara yii ḿ dàkà-ni abɔkpaa nì akoobil ŋin ni làá nīn ŋúb́ ni yaa bàn̄ kitiŋ kin ni làá dùtī kí fōō kí nīn kíǹ ki yì nee poonee.
Ní nīn nyíǹ ni-ba nì iwaatooti
15Ní nīn nyíǹ ni-ba, di sá yii ŋwiin ŋun ti-Dindaan nìn sòon̄ nì ni ŋŋmi poon Ooreeb jool puee, naa nìn wál̀ báà kujiliŋu kubɔ. 16Ní taa kɔ́ǹ ni-ba tijɔkɔndi kí cùú nīn māā àá ki kpítí awaa aba kí nántíǹ uninja àá unimpu. 17Ní taa tí kpítí tiba kí nántíǹ tiwaŋkuti tin bí kitiŋ puee àá inoon, 18kí taa tí kpítí tiba mun ki nántíǹ tin fù kitiŋee àá ijɔm. 19Míǹ mbaantiim ní ní taa wáaǹ kutaa kí kpèè ŋwìiń nì uŋmal nì iŋmalbijaa, an dàkà yii tin kɔkɔ pée bí kutaa puee, kí yàntī tí lábití ni-landɔkɔŋu ní nīn kíǹ ki gbàantí ti-taapu ki jáaḿ-tì. Ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu dū atuun gbanti ki tīī anibul ŋin kɔkɔ kíǹ ki bí kitiŋ puee ní. 20Ama nimbee, ti-Dindaan yōoǹ-ni ki nyántìń kipaai ŋmiŋu poon Eejipiti tiŋkin ní nīn kíǹ ki sá nnibool ŋun sá ki tīī-uee, kii ni nín sá pu díǹ ki tīī-u nan ní.
21Ni-puee, ti-Dindaan gíí m-pu diŋuul ní ki pūtì yii m kpá kí dùtī Jɔɔdan buŋŋu kí kɔ́ kitimmɔntii kin ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá dūú tīī-ni án kpántí ni-yakee poon. 22Di sá yii m làá kpú kitiŋ kin bí nee poon ní, maa làá ŋmā kí dùtī Jɔɔdan buŋŋu. Ama nimbee, ni làá dùtī-dì kí fōō kitiŋee kí nīn kíǹ ki yì. 23Míǹ puee ní nīn nyíǹ ni-ba kí taa súntí dipoondi din ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu pōoǹ-nee. Ní taa tin nín̄ nāantí awaa ki nántíǹ tiba kii ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nín bí yii ní taa ŋá puee. 24Kun puee ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu sá ŋŋmi ŋun wù ki céetée ní. U sá Unimbɔti un cáá ipoompoonee ní.
25Ni yaa láa kāl̀ kitiŋ gbanti poon ki yúntì ní ki yaa láa cáá mbiyaamu nì naantiibee, ní taa láa kpítí awaa kí nántíǹ tiba kí kɔ́ǹ ni-ba tijɔkɔndi. Ní taa láa ŋá ikpiti gbanti ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nimbiin kí gbítí u-ŋuul. 26Ama ni yaa ŋá mimmee, ibaamɔn ní m bíi tùkù-ni, kutagbɔŋu nì kitiŋ sá m-seeradambi díǹ yii naa làá pée sūŋkì ní kí kpú kí céetí kitiŋ kin ni làá dùtī Jɔɔdan buŋŋu kí tin kɔ́ nee poon. Naa làá kàl̄ ki-poon kí yúntí báà fiii, di sá yii ni làá kpú ní kí céetí malaa. 27Ti-Dindaan làá dāá yàntī ní yàl̄ kí tin nín̄ bí atimbun aban. Ni-wíiŋŋu làá dāá bàtī ní ní kíń fiii atimbun ŋin poon ti-Dindaan làá dāá jà-ni kí cùnnèe. 28Atimbun gbantinee, ni làá dāá nīn tòotī awaa ŋin ní unil dū u-ŋalii ki máńee, awaa ŋin sá idɔ nì ataŋkpee kaa wāĺaaa, kaa gbìl̀aaa, kaa jīǹ tijinaaa, kaa tíkì nnumee. 29Ntimu gbanti poonee, ni làá dāá nyàab̀ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu. Ni yaa láa nyàab̄-u nì ni-pɔbiliŋ kɔkɔ nì ni-nammu kɔkɔee, ni làá dāá ká-u. 30Ni-nimbinaamandi poonee, tin kɔkɔ m sòon̄ nee làá dāá bàń-ni, ní ní dāá fàtīí gítiń ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu cee, ní kí nīn kíǹ ki tɔ́-u. 31Di sá yii ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu sá disaasɔl Nimbɔtiu ní. Waa làá dū-ni kí fá, kaa làá kpɔ̀ kí céetí-ni, kaa làá tí súntí dipoondi din u pūtì ki pōoǹ ni-baabee mun pu.
Ti-Dindaan baba di sá Unimbɔti
32Mimmee Isirayeel yab, naa bàlifī kí béé iyuntikpiki pu níii? Bàlifìmaan ŋyunti ŋun baa nìn dá láá màl̄-nee pu, ŋwiin ŋun Unimbɔti nìn náań unil kitiŋ puee kí cáá sāā díǹ pu. Bàlifìmaan kitiŋ kílilaŋki kí bàlifì ki-kúntilaŋki. Bàlifìmaan kí kpèè yii atuŋkpaan aba gíti ŋá laaba kii ŋi neeee? Ni pée gbìl̄ tiba tì náań nì tin bí nee dalbaaa? 33Dinibul diba nib gíti bí laaba ki gbìl̄ unimbɔti ubɔ sòon̄ nì bi ŋŋmi poon baa kpíì kii ni nín gbìl̄ pu kaa kpíì neeee? 34Àá unimbɔti ubɔ gíti bí laaba ki mākaǹ ki ŋá maamaacib nì atuŋkpaan nì dikɔ̀ndi nì mpɔŋkpaan tuuŋŋi nì atuun ŋin kɔ̄ntí tifaandee dalba kí nyāntí ditimbundi diba di-juti ŋaan kí gāā u-bindaaa? Too míǹ ní ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu ŋá ki nyántì-ni Eejipiti tiŋkin, nimbi ni-ba nimbil ká.
35Ama nimbee, ni cáá diyimɔɔl ki ká an bɔti, án nín làá ŋá pu ní béé yii ti-Dindaan baba di sá Unimbɔti, ní unimbɔti ubɔ kaa ti bí laaba ki kútì úǹ puee. 36Doooo yilpu ní u yāntì ni gbìl̄ u-neen pu kí dàkà-ni ní nīn tɔ́-u, ní ki yāntì ni ká ŋŋmikpaan ŋun poon u sòon̄ nì nee kitiŋ pu. 37Di sá yii u nìn néeń ni-naanjab, ní ki lēē nimbi bin sá bi-naantiibee, ki dū u-pɔŋkpaaŋŋu ki nyántìń-ni Eejipiti tiŋkin. 38U làá jà anibul ŋin sá akpaan ki pɔ̄ɔ̄ ki jítiǹ-nee, kí cáá-ni kí kɔ́ǹ bi-timmu poon, ní kí dū ntimuee kí tīī-ni mú kpántí ni-yamu. 39Ní dàkafì tiŋan kí béé díǹ nee yii yilpu yilpu fɔ́ŋŋŋ nì kitiŋ taapuee, ti-Dindaan di sá Unimbɔti, Unimbɔti ubɔ kaa ti bí laaba. 40Nín̄ ŋúb́maan u-bɔkpaaŋi nì u-marab bin m tīī-ni díǹ pu neeyee. Ni yaa ŋúb́-bee, án làá bútí ni nì ni-biyaamu mun làá dāá páań ni-boonee. Míǹ ní ni làá kàl̄ kí yúntí kitiŋ kin ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá dūú tīī-ni jaanjaanee poon.
41Niinee ní Mooyiisi lēē ntimu muta Jɔɔdan buŋgbandi ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú ki síiǹ, 42yii ubɔ yaa kaa nyí ní ki kūū u-nabiki, ní an kaa sá nì kináŋee, udaan ń sāǹ kí kɔ́ ntimu gbanti kiba poon. Udaan yaa ŋúń ki sáǹ ki kɔ́ ntimu gbanti kiba poonee, ú ŋmátí. 43Ntimuee sɔ̀. Bi nìn lēē Beeseer tiŋki kin bí kuteeu gbantaŋki puee ki tīī Rubeen yab, ní ki lēē Raamooti tiŋki kin bí Galaadee ki tīī Gaadi yab, ní ki lēē Goolan tiŋki kin bí Baasanee ki tīī Manasee yab.
MOOYIISI SÒON̄ NLILIITIIM UNIMBƆTI MARAB PU
(4.44–11.32)
44Marab bin Mooyiisi nìn dūu tīī Isirayeel yabee sɔ̀. 45Isirayeel yab nín nyáń Eejipiti tiŋkinee, marab nì abɔkpaa nì akoobil ŋin Mooyiisi nìn dūu tīī-bee sèé. 46Ŋyunti gbantee, baa nìn dá láá dūtì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu. Bi nìn dá láá bí Beeti-Peewɔɔr tantakal caŋin ní. Dijandi gbanti nìn bí Siiwɔn, Amɔɔr yab bɔtiu un nìn kóò Eesbɔnee tiŋki pu ní. Ubɔti gbanti ní Mooyiisi nì Isirayeel yab nìn jáń ki jíń ŋyunti ŋun bi nyáń Eejipiti tiŋkinee. 47Bi nìn jáń ki fōō u-tiŋki ki kpáaǹ Baasan yab bɔtiu Ɔɔgi tiŋki. Bibɔtiibee liitil nìn sá Amɔɔr yab bin nìn bí Jɔɔdan buŋgbandi, ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee ní. 48Kitiŋ kin Isirayeel yab nìn fōōyee nìn dɔ̄ kí yòon̄ Arooweer tiŋki kin bí Arinɔn buŋgbandee kí cáá sāā Siiwɔn jool, an dàkà yii Eermɔn jool. 49An nìn kpáaǹ Arabaa tiŋki kin kɔkɔ bí Jɔɔdan jandi ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú púee, kí cáá sāā Arabaa mɔɔl din dɔ̄ Piisga jool taapuee.

english_text:
The Ten Commandments
(Exodus 20.1-17)
1Moses called together the people of Israel and said:
Today I am telling you the laws and teachings that you must follow, so listen carefully. 2The Lord our God made an agreement with our nation at Mount Sinai. 3That agreement wasn't only with our ancestors but with us, who are here today. 4The Lord himself spoke to you out of the fire, 5but you were afraid of the fire and refused to go up the mountain. So I spoke with the Lord for you, then I told you that he had said:
6I am the Lord your God, the one who brought you out of Egypt where you were slaves.
7Do not worship any god except me.
8 Do not make idols that look like anything in the sky or on earth or in the ocean under the earth. 9 Don't bow down and worship idols. I am the Lord your God, and I demand all your love. If you reject me and worship idols, I will punish your families for three or four generations. 10But if you love me and obey my laws, I will be kind to your families for thousands of generations.
11 Do not misuse my name. I am the Lord your God, and I will punish anyone who misuses my name.
12 Show respect for the Sabbath Day—it belongs to me. 13 You have six days when you can do your work, 14but the seventh day of the week belongs to me, your God. No one is to work on that day—not you, your children, your oxen or donkeys or any other animal, not even those foreigners who live in your towns. And don't make your slaves do any work. 15This special day of rest will remind you that I reached out my mighty arm and rescued you from slavery in Egypt.
16 Respect your father and mother, and you will live a long and successful life in the land I am giving you.
17 Do not murder.
18 Be faithful in marriage.
19 Do not steal.
20 Do not tell lies about others.
21 Do not desire to possess anything that belongs to another person—not a house, a wife, a husband, a slave, an ox, a donkey, or anything else.
22 When we were gathered at the mountain, the Lord spoke to us in a loud voice from the dark fiery cloud. The Lord gave us these commands, and only these. Then he wrote them on two flat stones and gave them to me.
The People Were Afraid
(Exodus 20.18-21)
Moses said to Israel:
23When fire blazed from the mountain, and you heard the voice coming from the darkness, your tribal leaders came to me 24and said:
Today the Lord our God has shown us how powerful and glorious he is. He spoke to us from the fire, and we learned that people can live, even though God speaks to them. 25But we don't want to take a chance on being killed by that terrible fire, and if we keep on hearing the Lord's voice, we will die. 26Has anyone else ever heard the only true God speaking from fire, as we have? And even if they have, would they live to tell about it? 27Moses, go up close and listen to the Lord. Then come back and tell us, and we will do everything he says.
28The Lord heard you and said:
Moses, I heard what the people said to you, and I approve. 29I wish they would always worship me with fear and trembling and be this willing to obey me! Then they and their children would always enjoy a successful life.
30Now, tell them to return to their tents, 31but you come back here to me. After I tell you my laws and teachings, you will repeat them to the people, so they can obey these laws in the land I am giving them.
Moses said:
32Israel, you must carefully obey the Lord's commands. 33Follow them, because they make a path that will lead to a long successful life in the land the Lord your God is giving you.
translation_text:
Unimbɔti tīī u-nibul marab saalaa
1Mooyiisi yíiń Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ ki kpáfì ní ki bí-bi yii:
«Pīlifìmaan Isirayeel yab, pīlifìmaan abɔkpaa nì akoobil ŋin m làá dūú sòoǹ kí ŋá ni-tafalin díǹ nee, kí bīfì-ŋi, kí nīn ŋúb́-ŋi, kí nīn ŋáań kii ŋi nín bí yii ní ŋá puee. 2Ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu pūtì ki pōoǹ-ti dipoondi Ooreeb jool pu. 3An kaa nìn sá ti-baabi ní ti-Dindaan nìn pūtì ki pōoǹ dipoondi gbanti, ama timbi bin kɔkɔ bí doo díǹ ki bí dimaŋfalin nee ní u nìn pūtì ki pōoǹ dipoondi gbanti. 4Ni-nimbiin niin, dijool pu ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì ni ŋŋmi poon. 5Ŋyunti gbantee, man nìn sí ni nì ti-Dindaan kansikin ní ki cáá ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi ki nàatī-ni, kun puee ni nìn fàŋkí ŋŋmi gbanti kaa nìn kíí kí dàb̄ dijool. Ti-Dindaan nìn lī yii:
6«Man di sá a-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu un di nyántìń-si kuyuŋun Eejipiti tiŋkinee.
7«Á taa jāam̀ unimbɔti ubɔ kí kūtì man pu.
8«Á taa mɔ́ɔ́ diwaal diba kí nántíǹ tiba tin bí yilpuee àá tin bí kitiŋ pu taapu dooyee àá tin bí nnyimin kitiŋ taapuee. 9Á taa gbàan̄ awaa gbanti nimbiin ní kaa nín jáam̀-ŋi, kun puee mama a-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiuee, m sá Unimbɔti un cáá ipoompoonee ní. Ubɔ yaa ná-mee, m dátí udaan tafal ní kí dāá dáaĺ u-biyaamu mun tafal kí cáá sāā anaantitɔntɔkɔ ata kii anaa pu. 10Ama bin néeń-mi ki ŋúb́ m-marabee, m ŋáań-bi tiŋan ní kí cáá sāā anaantitɔntɔkɔ kutuku pu.
11«Á taa nín̄ yíì man a-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu yindi fám fám, kun puee man a-Dindaan kaa làá dūú pɔ̄ un ŋáań mimmee.
12«Á nīn tɔ́ ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa ŋú nīn sá circir wiiŋŋu ki tīī-si, kii man a-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu nín síiǹ-si á ŋá puee. 13A cáá iwiin iluu kí tɔ̄ ditundi, kí ŋá tin kɔkɔ a cáá kí ŋée. 14Ama ŋwinluluúti dal sá ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa ní, ŋwiin ŋun a dūu sú man a-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiuee. Á taa tɔ̄ báà ditundi diba ŋwiin gbanti. Sii a-baaa, a-jipɔmbaaa, a-bisalibaaa, a-tɔntɔnliibi bininjab nì binimpoobaaa, a-naayaaa, a-mammuɔɔɔ, a-waŋkutaaa, binicambi bin kóò a-pueeyaaa, ubɔ ń taa tɔ̄ ditundi. A-tɔntɔnliibi bininjab nì binimpoobi máaǹ kí tɔ̄ bi-ba kí ŋùŋfì kii siiyee ŋwiin gbanti. 15Á téetí yii a nìn kāl̀ kuyuŋu Eejipiti tiŋkin ní man a-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu dū m-pɔŋkpaaŋŋu ki nyántìń-si kitiŋ gbantin. An pu ní man a-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu tīī-si mara yii á nīn tɔ́ ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa.
16«Á nīn tɔ́ a-baa nì a-na kii man a-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu nín síiǹ-si mara yii á ŋá puee. A yaa ŋá mimmee, a làá kàl̄ kitiŋ pu kí yúntí ní an bútí-si kitiŋ kin man a-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu làá dūú tīī-see poon.
17«Á taa kpɔ̀ unil.
18«Á taa ŋá tilaakpaal.
19«Á taa yɔ̀.
20«Á taa lēē inyimɔn seerau kí túń a-juti pu.
21«Á taa nín̄ cáá a-juti nimpuu pu nnimbitaataam. Á taa nín̄ cáá a-juti diiku àá u-tiŋki àá u-tɔntɔnliu uninja àá unimpu àá u-naau àá u-maŋki àá tin pée sá a-juti wantee pu nnimbitaataam.»
22An nìn sá ŋŋmi nì ditagbandi nì dibɔmbɔŋkpaandi poon ní ti-Dindaan nìn sòon̄ nì ni-kɔkɔ mpɔn dijool pu ní ki tīī-ni marab nee. Waa nìn gíti kútì tiba an pu. Míǹ boonee ní u ŋmàn̄ marabee titaŋkpapilindi tili pu ní ki dūu tīī-mi.
Mooyiisi, Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu
23Ŋyunti ŋun ni gbìl̄ nneen sòoǹ dibɔmbɔndi poon dijool mun fōō ŋŋmee ní ni-naakɔti kpilib kɔkɔ nì ni-kpootiliibi sútì ki pìlīń-mi, 24ní ki lī yii: «Kpèè, ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu yāntì ti ká u-nyooti nì u nín sá ukpaan miŋyee, ní ki yāntì ti gbìl̄ u-neen mun pu ŋŋmi poon. Díǹ ní ti nín ká yii Unimbɔti ŋūǹ kí sòoǹ nì unil, ní unil gbantee ń taa kpú kí nīn gbíntìi bí dimaŋfalin! 25Kɔŋkɔnnee, ba pu ní tí dū ti-ba kí tīī ŋŋmikpaan nee ń wà-ti tí kpú ní? Ti yaa gbíntìi bíi pílifí ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu nín sòoǹ pu ŋŋmikpaan nee poonee, see tí kpú. 26Di sá yii nisaal ulɔu di pée gbìl̄ dimaŋfal Nimbɔtiu neen pu, u sòon̄ ŋŋmi poon kii timbi nín bíi gbìl̀ pu nee ki ŋmátì? 27Míǹ puee, sii sútí kí pìl̄ ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu kí pīlifì tin u làá sòoǹee. Míǹ boonee á gítiń kí tùkù-ti tin kɔkɔ ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu tùkū-see. Timbi làá pīlifì tin a làá sòoǹee kí ŋá míǹ.» 28Ti-Dindaan nìn gbìl̄ tibɔti tin ni nìn sòon̄ m-ceeyee ní ki bí-mi yii: «M gbìl̄ tin kɔkɔ binib nee tùkū-see. Tin kɔkɔ bi lēe, an kítì míǹ. 29Bi-pɔbiliŋ yaa bàà bɔ́ntì kí nīn fàŋkí-mi kí ŋúb́ m-marab kɔkɔ baabadal, án bàà làá nīn ŋān̄ ki tīī bi nì bi-biyaamu kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaan! 30Cùú tùkù-bi yii báà ŋma ń nīn gítí u-tantiun. 31Ama siiyee, gbíntí m-cee doo ḿ dū m-marab nì m-bɔkpaaŋi nì m-koobiliŋ kí tīī-si á cáá dàkà-bi, bi yaa bàn̄ kitiŋ kin m làá dūú tīī-bi bí nīn kíǹ ki yèe poonee, bí nīn ŋúb́-bee.»
32An puee ní nīn nyíǹ ni-ba kí ŋá kii ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nín bí yii ní ŋá puee, kí taa kpòotī kí cù ŋgiil púɔɔɔ, kí taa kpòotī kí cù ŋgan pú. 33Ní nīn dī nsan ŋun ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu cátì ki bíl̀ ni-nimbiinee, án nín làá ŋá pu ní nīn bí dimaŋfalin kí jī nnaam kí kàl̄ kitiŋ kin ni làá fōō kí nīn kíǹ ki yèe poon kí yúntée.

english_text:
The Most Important Commandment
Moses said to Israel:
1The Lord told me to give you these laws and teachings, so you can obey them in the land he is giving you. Soon you will cross the Jordan River and take that land. 2And if you and your descendants want to live a long time, you must always worship the Lord and obey his laws. 3Pay attention, Israel! Our ancestors worshiped the Lord, and he promised to give us this land that is rich with milk and honey. Be careful to obey him, and you will become a successful and powerful nation.
4 Listen, Israel! The Lord our God is the only true God! 5 So love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, and strength. 6 Memorize his laws 7and tell them to your children over and over again. Talk about them all the time, whether you're at home or walking along the road or going to bed at night, or getting up in the morning. 8Write down copies and tie them to your wrists and foreheads to help you obey them. 9Write these laws on the door frames of your homes and on your town gates.
Worship Only the Lord
Moses said to Israel:
10 The Lord promised your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob that he would give you this land. Now he will take you there and give you large towns, with good buildings that you didn't build, 11and houses full of good things that you didn't put there. The Lord will give you wells that you didn't have to dig, and vineyards and olive orchards that you didn't have to plant. But when you have eaten so much that you can't eat any more, 12don't forget it was the Lord who set you free from slavery and brought you out of Egypt. 13 Worship and obey the Lord your God with fear and trembling, and promise that you will be loyal to him.
14Don't have anything to do with gods that are worshiped by the nations around you. 15If you worship other gods, the Lord will be furious and wipe you off the face of the earth. The Lord your God is with you, 16 so don't try to make him prove that he can help you, as you did at Massah. 17Always obey the laws that the Lord has given you 18-19and live in a way that pleases him. Then you will be able to go in and take this good land from your enemies, just as he promised your ancestors.
20Someday your children will ask, “Why did the Lord give us these laws and teachings?”
21Then you will answer:
We were slaves of the king of Egypt, but the Lord used his great power and set us free. 22We saw him perform miracles and make horrible things happen to the king, his officials, and everyone else. 23The Lord rescued us from Egypt, so he could bring us into this land, as he had promised our ancestors. 24-25That's why the Lord our God demands that we obey his laws and worship him with fear and trembling. And if we do, he will protect us and help us be successful.
translation_text:
«Nín̄ néeń ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu»
1Marab nì abɔkpaa nì akoobil ŋin ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu tīī-mi ḿ dūú dàkà-ni ni yaa láa dūtì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ki fōō kitiŋ ki kíǹ ki yèe, ní nīn ŋúb́ ki ŋáań kii bi nín bí yii ní ŋá puee dee. 2Án nín làá ŋá pu ní nimbi nì ni-jipɔmbi nì ni-naantiibi ń dāá fàŋkì ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu kí nīn tɔ́ u-bɔkpaaŋi kɔkɔ nì u-marab bin m tīī-ni nee iwiin in kɔkɔ ni cáá kí kàl̄ kitiŋ puee. Míǹ ní ni-maŋfal wiiŋyi làá fɔ̀kɔn̄. 3An puee, Isirayeel yab, pīlifìmaan marab gbanti kí nīn tɔ́-bi, kí ŋá bi nín bí yii ní ŋá puee. Ni yaa ŋá mimmee, án làá bútí-ni, ní ní bùtī tikpil kitiŋ kin poon nnaabiim nì tisiil còol̄ee, kii ti-Dindaan ni-baabi Nimbɔtiu nín pōoǹ-ni puee.
4Pīlifìmaan Isirayeel yab, ti-Dindaan di sá ti-Nimbɔtiu, ti-Dindaan sá ubaanti ní. 5Á nīn néeń ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu nì a-pɔbil kɔkɔ nì a-naŋki kɔkɔ nì a-pɔŋŋu kɔkɔ. 6Á dū marab bin m tīī-si díǹ nee kí kpāafì a-pɔbilin. 7Á dū-bi kí cóoĺ a-biyaamu. A yaa kā a-dumpuɔɔɔ, a yaa tàkā nsan pu ki còom̄ ki cáaa, a yaa tí dɔ̄ɔɔ, a yaa tí yúɔɔɔ, bí nīn kā a-nyɔkɔn. 8Á ŋmà-bi kí dūú fìn̄ a-ŋal nì a-yigbeel án nīn sá-si kudaaŋŋu. 9Á ŋmà-bi kí nákań a-punyɔmmu pu nì a-tiŋki punuubi pu.
Isirayeel ń taa súntí u-Nimbɔtiu pu
10Ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá dāá cáá-ni kí kɔ́ǹ kitiŋ kin ní u nìn pūtì ki pōoǹ ni-naanjab Abraam nì Isaaki nì Jaakɔb yii u làá dūú tīī-nee poon. Kitiŋ gbanti cáá ntimu mun sá ŋkpaamu ki ŋān̄ naa máńee. 11Kitiŋ gbanti gíti cáá adiin ŋin poon naa síiǹ tiba ama ní tigaajawan kɔkɔ nì ti-bulifi gbée, lɔkɔb bin naa gbìn̄ee, fiinyi nì ɔliifi sufii in naa cóoǹee kɔkɔ bí niin. Ni làá dāá jī ní kí díkí. 12Ama ní nīn nyíǹ ni-ba kí taa súntí ti-Dindaan un nyántìń-ni Eejipiti tiŋki kin poon ni nìn sá iyumbuee pu. 13Nín̄ fàŋkímaan ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu. Úǹ baba ní ni máaǹ kí jāam̀, ní úǹ baba yindi mun ní ni máaǹ kí pùtī. 14Ní taa tòotī awaa ŋin anibul ŋin māntìi tú-nee tòotēe. 15Kun puee ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu un bí ni-kansikinee sá ipoompoon Nimbɔtiu ní. Ni yaa ŋá mimmee, see ú gíí ni-pu diŋuul kí kpɔ̀ kí céetí-ni kitiŋ pu. 16Ní taa cɔ̄ŋkì ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu kii ni nín nìn cɔ́ŋkì-u Maasa puee. 17Nín̄ ŋúb́maan ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu marab nì u-bɔkpaaŋi nì u-koobiliŋ ŋin u tīī-nee tiŋan. 18Nimbee, ŋámaan tin kítì ki ŋān̄ ti-Dindaan nimbiinee. Ni yaa ŋá mimmee, ní an bútí-ni ní ní ŋmā kí fōō kitimmɔntii kin u pōoǹ kí tīī ni-naanjabee kí nīn kíǹ ki yì. 19Ni làá jà ni-nannanliibi kii ti-Dindaan nín lī puee.
20Fool boon, ni-biyaamu yaa láa bālifì-ni yii: «Ba pu ní ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu tīī-ni abɔkpaa nì akoobil nì marab nee dee?» 21Ní dāá kíí-bi yii: «Ti nìn sá iyumbu ní Faaroo ŋaan Eejipiti tiŋkin, ní ti-Dindaan dū mpɔŋkpaan ki nyántìń-ti niin. 22Ti-nimbiin niin ní ti-Dindaan dàkā Faaroo nì u-dicaŋku nì u-nib kɔkɔ u-daanti nì u-tuŋkpaaŋŋi, ní ki kɔ́ǹ-bi digìŋ́kpaandin. 23Ama ní timbee, u nyántìń-ti niin ki cáań-ti doo ki dū kitiŋ kin u nìn pōoǹ kí tīī ti-naanjabee ki tīī-ti. 24Ti-Dindaan nìn kpáafì-ti yii tí nīn tɔ́ u-bɔkpaaŋi kí nīn fàŋkí úǹ ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu ní án bútí-ti tikɔkɔ poon, ní tí nīn bí dimaŋfalin kii an nín bí pu ki tīī-ti díǹ pu nee. 25Tin ti máaǹ kí ŋá ní kí nīn kítì ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu nimbiinee di sá tí nīn ŋúb́ marab nee kɔkɔ, kí ŋá kii bi nín bí yii tí ŋá puee.»

english_text:
Force the Other Nations Out of the Land
(Exodus 34.11-16)
Moses said:
1 People of Israel, the Lord your God will help you take the land of the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. These seven nations have more people and are stronger than Israel, but when you attack them, 2the Lord will force them out of the land. Then you must destroy them without mercy. Don't make any peace treaties with them, 3and don't let your sons and daughters marry any of them. 4If you do, those people will lead your descendants to worship other gods and to turn their backs on the Lord. That will make him very angry, and he will quickly destroy Israel.
5 So when you conquer these nations, tear down the altars where they worship their gods. Break up their sacred stones, cut down the poles that they use in worshiping the goddess Asherah, and throw their idols in the fire.
The Lord's Chosen People
Moses said:
6 Israel, you are the chosen people of the Lord your God. There are many nations on this earth, but he chose only Israel to be his very own. 7You were the weakest of all nations, 8but the Lord chose you because he loves you and because he had made a promise to your ancestors. Then with his mighty arm, he rescued you from the king of Egypt, who had made you his slaves.
9 You know that the Lord your God is the only true God. So love him and obey his commands, and he will faithfully keep his agreement with you and your descendants for a thousand generations. 10But if you turn against the Lord, he will quickly destroy you. 11So be sure to obey his laws and teachings I am giving you today.
The Lord Will Bless You if You Obey
(Deuteronomy 28.1-14; Leviticus 26.3-13)
Moses said to Israel:
12 If you completely obey these laws, the Lord your God will be loyal and keep the agreement he made with you, just as he promised our ancestors. 13The Lord will love you and bless you by giving you many children and plenty of food, wine, and olive oil. Your herds of cattle will have many calves, and your flocks of sheep will have many lambs. 14God will bless you more than any other nation—your families will grow and your livestock increase. 15You will no longer suffer with the same horrible diseases that you sometimes had in Egypt. You will be healthy, but the Lord will make your enemies suffer from those diseases.
Destroy the Nations and Their Gods
Moses said to Israel:
16When the Lord helps you defeat your enemies, you must destroy them without pity! And don't get trapped into worshiping their gods.
17You may be thinking, “How can we destroy these nations? They are more powerful than we are.” 18But stop worrying! Just remember what the Lord your God did to Egypt and its king. 19You saw how the Lord used his tremendous power to work great miracles and bring you out of Egypt. And he will again work miracles for you when you face these enemies you fear so much. 20Some of them may try to survive by hiding from you, but the Lord will make them panic, and soon they will be dead. 21So don't be frightened when you meet them in battle. The Lord your God is great and fearsome, and he will fight at your side.
22As you attack these nations, the Lord will force them out little by little. He won't let you get rid of them all at once—if he did, there wouldn't be enough people living in the land to keep down the number of wild animals. 23-24But when you attack your enemies, the Lord will make them panic, and you will easily destroy them. You will defeat their kings one after another until they are gone, and no one will remember they ever lived.
25After you conquer a nation, burn their idols. Don't get trapped into wanting the silver or gold on an idol. Even the metal on an idol is disgusting to the Lord, 26so destroy it. If you bring it home with you, both you and your house will be destroyed. Stay away from those disgusting idols!
translation_text:
Bí nàan̄ Kanaan yab nì bi-waaŋi
1Ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá cáá-ni kí kɔ́ǹ kitiŋ kin ní ni làá fōō ki nìn kíǹ ki yèe poon. U làá jà anibul kupaau ni-nyɔkɔpu kí wàatī-ni. Anibul gbanti nyáń aluli ní ki sá akpaan ki pɔ̄ɔ̄ ki jítiǹ-ni. Ŋíǹ di sá: Eeti yab nì Giirgaasi yab nì Amɔɔr yab nì Kanaan yab nì Peeriisi yab nì Eefi yab nì Jeebusi yab. 2Ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá dū-bi kí ŋá ni-ŋaan, ní ní já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ-bi. Ama ni yaa jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bee, ní kpɔ̀ kí céetí-bi. Ni nì bi ń taa ŋá mpèé, ní taa sɔ̄ bi-saai mun. 3Ní taa nín̄ cāab̀ tɔb. Ní taa dū ni-bisalib kí tīī bi-jipɔmbi ticati, kí taa tí yòon̄ bi-bisalib kí tīī ni-jipɔmbi ticati. 4An yaa kaa sá míǹ, bi làá yàntī ni-biyaamu ń dū ti-Dindaan kí fá kí nīn kíǹ ki tòotī awaa, ní ti-Dindaan ń tí gíí ni-pu diŋuul ní kí kpɔ̀ kí céetí-ni malaa. 5Ni nín máaǹ kí ŋá-bi puee sɔ̀. Ní gbá kí wìil̀ bi-saraafaŋyi nì ataŋkpee ŋin bi dūu cóoǹ ki tòotēe, kí gàatì bi-windɔi ní kí wà bi-waakpitikaaŋi ŋŋmi. 6Di sá yii ni sá dinibul din ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu u-ba yèe ní. Ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu di lēē-ni ki nyántì anibul ŋin kɔkɔ bí kitiŋ puee kansikin ki dū-ni ki ŋá u-nibul, u-gaajawammɔntiiti.
Ti-Dindaan ŋúb̀ u-poondi ní
7Ti-Dindaan yaa dū u-ba ki nákáǹ-ni ki lēē-nee, an kaa sá yii ni nín wīikí ki jítiǹ anibul ŋin kíǹee pu ní u lēē-ni. Di sá yii ni-wíiŋŋu kaa pée dàbiǹ anibul ŋin kíǹee yɔŋu báà fiii. 8Ama, ti-Dindaan yaa dū u-pɔŋkpaaŋŋu ki nyántìń-ni Eejipiti yab bɔtiu Faaroo ŋaan, ní ki dá-ni ki nyántì kuyuŋunee, an sá yii u néeń-ni, ní ki ŋúb́ dipoondi din u nìn pōoǹ ni-naanjabee.
9Míǹ puee, ní béé yii ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu baba di sá Unimbɔti, ibaamɔndaan. Bin tɔ́ u-marabee, u ŋúb̀ u-poondi din u pōoǹ-bee kí cáá sāā anaantitɔntɔkɔ kutuku. U néeń bin néeń-uee ní. 10Ama bin ná-uee, u pée pà bi-paati ní dicilpu dicilpu niin, ní kí nàan̄-bi. Waa pée tàantí kí pà bin ná-uee bi-paati.
11Míǹ puee nín̄ tɔ́maan marab nì abɔkpaa nì akoobil ŋin m tīī-ni díǹ nee kí ŋá ŋi nín bí yii ní ŋá puee.
12Ni yaa pílifì akoobil gbanti ní ki yaa ŋá ŋi nín bí yii ní ŋá pueeyee, ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu mun làá ŋá-ni tiŋan kí ŋúb́ dipoondi din u pōoǹ ni-naanjabee deedee. 13Ni yaa láa kɔ́ kitiŋ kin u nìn pōoǹ ni-naanjab kí tīī-nee poonee, u làá dāá nīn néeń-ni kí bìin̄ ni-boon kí yàntī ní màal̀ kí bùtī, ní kí bìin̄ ni-kpaajinti kɔkɔ pu, an dàkà yii ni-bileeu nì ni-damam nì ni-kpam sufii, ní kí bìin̄ ni-naai nì ni-piii nì ni-ŋoobui pu. 14Ti-Dindaan làá dāá bìin̄ ni-pu kí jītíǹ anibul ŋin kɔkɔ kíǹee. Ni-ninjab àá ni-nimpoobi báà ubɔ dāa kpá kí nīn sá uŋmaŋŋmanti, ki kpáaǹ ni-waŋkuti. 15Ti-Dindaan làá kàkatī iween kɔkɔ kí wàatī-ni, ní kí kàkatī tiweeŋkpiil tin nìn jéetì Eejipiti tiŋki pu nimbi ni-ba nimbil kée kí wàatī-ni. Naa làá pée ká-i ni-cee, ama u làá cáá-i kí tɔ̄ bin kɔkɔ ná-nee pu ní.
16Anibul ŋin kɔkɔ nib ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá dūú ŋá ni-ŋaanee, ní kpɔ̀ kí céetí-bi. Ní taa sɔ̄ bi-saai kí taa tòotī bi-waaŋi mun. Di sá yii an dāa sá kutaliŋŋu ní ki tīī-ni.
17An yaa yíì ni làá dàkafì yii: «Too anibul nee pɔ̄ɔ̄ ki jítiǹ-ti. Kin mana ní ti làá ŋmā kí já nì bi kí fōō bi-tiŋki kí ŋá ti-yaka ní?» 18Ní taa fàŋkìmaan-bi, ama ní téetí ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nín ŋá Faaroo nì Eejipiti nib kɔkɔ puee. 19Nimbi ni-ba ká nì ni-nimbiliŋ agìŋ́kpaan ŋin poon u kɔ́ǹ-bee. Ni ká atuŋkpaan nì mpɔŋkpaan tuuŋŋi ŋin ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu ŋá ki nyántìń-ni kitiŋ gbanti poonee. Too, míǹ mbaantiim ní ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá ŋá anibul ŋin ni fàŋkí nee kɔkɔ. 20Ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá dāá dū inaŋgbansii ní kí tɔ̄ bi-pu, áli gba bin nìn ŋmátì ki nyàab̀ kí sāǹ kí báĺ ní taa ká-bee kɔkɔ ń kpú múb. 21Taa pée fàŋkìmaan-bi báà fiii pu, di sá yii ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu un bí ni-ceeyee sá Unimbɔtikpaan nì Kunimbɔtiwambiiu ní. 22Fiii fiii ní ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá nīn jì anibul gbanti ki tìì-ni. Naa làá ŋmā kí kpɔ̀ kí céetí-bi dicilpu dicilpu niin, an yaa kaa sá míǹ ipeel làá bùtī ní kí nīn páb́-ni. 23Ama ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá dū-bi kí ŋá ni-ŋaan. U làá dū-bi kí tɔ̄ dinyoondi din làá nàan̄-bee poon ní. 24U làá dū bi-bɔtiibi ki ŋá ni-ŋaan ní ní kpɔ̀-bi kí kpìtī bi-yiŋŋi kitiŋ pu. Bi-kansikin báà ubɔ kaa dāa ŋūǹ kí sīĺ ni-nimbiin. Ni làá dāá kpɔ̀ kí céetí-bi ní. 25Ní dāá dū bi-waakpitikaaŋi kí wà ŋŋmi. Ní taa yàntī animbil kúti nì sindaariyab bin bí ŋi-puee ń cúú-ni nnimbitaataam. Ní taa pée yòon̄-ŋi, an yaa kaa sá míǹ, an làá kpántí kutaliŋŋu kí tīī-ni. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu ná tiwan gbanti ní. 26Ní taa pée yòon̄ diwaal din bí mimmee kí kɔ́ǹ ni-diiŋŋin. Ni yaa ŋá mimmee, see bí kpɔ̀ kí céetí-ni kii bi nín máaǹ kí ŋá awaa gbanti puee. Ni máaǹ kí nīn ná awaa gbanti kí taa nyàab̀ kí wāl̀-ŋi gba, kun puee ŋi sá ntimbiil wanti ní.

english_text:
The Lord Takes Care of You
Moses said:
1Israel, do you want to go into the land the Lord promised your ancestors? Do you want to capture it, live there, and become a powerful nation? Then be sure to obey every command I am giving you.
2Don't forget how the Lord your God has led you through the desert for the past 40 years. He wanted to find out if you were truly willing to obey him and depend on him, 3 so he made you go hungry. Then he gave you manna, a kind of food that you and your ancestors had never even heard about. The Lord was teaching you that people need more than food to live—they need every word that the Lord has spoken.
4Over the past 40 years, your clothing hasn't worn out, and your feet haven't swollen. 5 So keep in mind that the Lord has been correcting you, just as parents correct their children. 6Obey the commands the Lord your God has given you and worship him with fear and trembling.
7The Lord your God is bringing you into a good land with streams that flow from springs in the valleys and hills. 8-9You can dig for copper in those hills, and the stones are made of iron ore. And you won't go hungry. Wheat and barley fields are everywhere, and so are vineyards and orchards full of fig, pomegranate, and olive trees, and there is plenty of honey.
Don't Forget the Lord
Moses said to Israel:
10After you eat and are full, give praise to the Lord your God for the good land he gave you. 11 Make sure that you never forget the Lord or disobey his laws and teachings that I am giving you today. If you always obey them, 12you will have plenty to eat, and you will build good houses to live in. 13You will get more and more cattle, sheep, silver, gold, and other possessions.
14But when all this happens, don't be proud! Don't forget that you were once slaves in Egypt and that it was the Lord who set you free. 15Remember how he led you in that huge and frightening desert where poisonous snakes and scorpions live. There was no water, but the Lord split open a rock, and water poured out so you could drink. 16He also gave you manna, a kind of food your ancestors had never even heard about. The Lord was testing you to make you trust him, so that later on he could be good to you.
17When you become successful, don't say, “I'm rich, and I've earned it all myself.” 18Instead, remember that the Lord your God gives you the strength to make a living. That's how he keeps the promise he made to your ancestors.
19-20But I'm warning you—if you forget the Lord your God and worship other gods, the Lord will destroy you, just as he destroyed the nations you fought.
translation_text:
Ti-Dindaan dàkā Isirayeel yab kuteeun
1Ni máaǹ kí nīn ŋúb́ marab bin m tīī-ni díǹ nee ní kí ŋá bi nín bí yii ní ŋá puee. Ni yaa ŋá mimmee, ni làá nīn bí dimaŋfalin ní kí bùtī, ní kí kɔ́ kí fōō kitiŋ kin ti-Dindaan nìn pōoǹ kí tīī ni-naanjabee. 2Ní téetí ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nín yāntì ni cōom̀ disaŋkindi din kuteeun abin imuŋku ilee pu. U nìn yāntì ni ká agìŋ́kpaan kí cɔ̄ŋkì-ni. U nìn ŋá míǹ kí kpèè yii, ni-pɔbiliŋ poonee, ni làá nīn tɔ́ u-marabaaa, naa làá nīn tɔ́-bi. 3Agìń gbanti boonee, u yāntì ŋkùm cúú-ni, ní ki dū maana un nimbi nì ni-naanjab kaa nìn nyée ki kpíiǹ-ni. U nìn ŋá míǹ kí dàkà-ni yii an kaa sá tijin dijil ŋmaniŋma di yì unil maŋfal, ama anyɔɔbun ŋin kɔkɔ nyēeń ti-Dindaan nyɔkɔnee di yì unil maŋfal. 4Abin imuŋku ili ŋin ni ŋá kuteeunee, ni-wampeeŋkaati kaa cátàaa, ni-taaŋi mun kaa díkí. 5Míǹ puee, ni máaǹ kí béé tiŋan yii, kii unil nín dàkà u-biki puee, míǹ mbaantiim ní ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu mun dàkà-ni. 6Nín̄ ŋúb́maan ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu marab, kí nīn ŋáań u nín là puee ní kí nīn fàŋkí-u.
7Kun puee ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá dū-ni kí kɔ́ǹ kitimmɔntii poon ní. Kitiŋ gbanti cáá ibun nì inyimbul nì nnyim min dɔ̄ kitiŋ taapu ki púǹ ditantakalin nì dijool pu ki pùub̀ee. 8Kitiŋ gbanti puee, bilee nì ɔɔji lòoǹ abil ní tikpil ní fiinyi nì fiigi nì greenaadi sufii mun lòoǹ tiŋan, ní ɔliifi kpam nì tisiil gbí. 9Kitiŋ gbanti poonee, dikpaasiil kpá ní tiba nì tiba kaa làá lóó-ni. Kitiŋ gbanti taŋkpeeŋi cáá tikúti ní ki-jooŋŋi sá tikúman. 10Ni yaa láa jíń ki díkée, ní dāá jāam̀ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu, kitimmɔntii kin u tīī-nee pu.
11Ama ní nīn nyíǹ ni-ba kí taa súntí ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu pu kí dū u-marab nì u-bɔkpaaŋi nì u-koobiliŋ ŋin m tīī-ni díǹ nee kí fá. 12Ni làá dāá jī kí díkí, ní kí dāá mā adimɔnti kí nīn kóò. 13Ni làá dāá nīn cáá inaa nì ipii nì iŋoobu tikpil, kí dāá nīn cáá animbil nì sindaariyab tikpil, ní kí dāá nīn cáá tigaajawan kɔkɔ nì ti-bulifi. 14Ama ní nīn nyí kí taa kpántí bilambidambi kí súntí ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu un nyántìń-ni Eejipiti tiŋki kin poon ni nìn sá iyumbuee pu. 15Úǹ di nìn līī ni-nyɔkɔpu ní ki cáá-ni ki jítì kuteeu kun wāā bàaa ki cáá tifaandi, ki sá ikoobu in cáá tiloolee nì inoom ŋmee pu. Kitiŋkuliŋŋi laakin nnyim kpée, u yāntì nnyim nyáń ditaŋkpal din pɔ̄ɔ̄yee poon ki tīī-ni. 16Kuteeu gbanti poonee u kpíiǹ-ni, ki tīī-ni maana un ni-naanjab kaa nìn pée nyí ki kée. U yāntì ni ká agìń kí cɔ̄ŋkì-ni, ní boonee kí dāá ŋá-ni tiŋan ní. 17Naa máaǹ kí lì yii: «An sá nì ti-pɔŋŋu nì ti-pɔɔndi pu ní ti ká tigaajawan nee kɔkɔ.» 18Ama ní téetí ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu pu. Di sá yii úǹ di tīī-ni mpɔn ní ni ŋúń ki túń ditundi ki ká tigaajati gbanti kɔkɔ. U ŋá míǹ kí dàkà yii u nín nìn pōoǹ ni-naanjab dipoondi diŋyee, u bíi ŋáań míǹ kii an nín bíi jītí pu díǹ nan ní.
19Ama ni yaa pée súntì ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu pu ní ki cūtì ki nóó awaa ki gbàantí ŋi-taapu ki jáaḿ-ŋee, ibaamɔn nì ibaamɔn ní m bíi sòoǹ nì ni díǹ yii ni làá dāá pée kpú ní kí céetí múb. 20Ni yaa kaa tɔ́ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiuee, kii ti-Dindaan nín bíi kù ki céetí anibul ŋin bí ni-nyɔkɔpu nee, míǹ mbaantiim ní u làá kpɔ̀ kí céetí ni-mun.

english_text:
Why the Lord Will Help Israel
Moses said:
1Israel, listen to me! You will soon cross the Jordan River and go into the land to force out the nations that live there. They are more powerful than you are, and the walls around their cities reach to the sky. 2Some of these nations are descendants of the Anakim. You know how tall and strong they are, and you've heard that no one can defeat them in battle. 3But the Lord your God has promised to go ahead of you, like a raging fire burning everything in its path. So when you attack your enemies, it will be easy for you to destroy them and take their land.
4-6After the Lord helps you wipe out these nations and conquer their land, don't think he did it because you are such good people. You aren't good—you are stubborn! No, the Lord is going to help you, because the nations that live there are evil, and because he wants to keep the promise he made to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
When Israel Made an Idol
(Exodus 32)
Moses said to Israel:
7Don't ever forget how you kept rebelling and making the Lord angry the whole time you were in the desert. You rebelled from the day you left Egypt until the day you arrived here.
8At Mount Sinai you made the Lord so angry that he was going to destroy you. 9-11 It happened during those 40 days and nights that I was on the mountain, without anything to eat or drink. He had told me to come up there so he could give me the agreement he made with us. And this agreement was actually the same Ten Commandments he had announced to you when he spoke from the fire on the mountain. The Lord had written them on two flat stones with his own hand. But after giving me the two stones, 12he said:
Moses, hurry down the mountain to those people you led out of Egypt. They have already disobeyed me and committed the terrible sin of making an idol.
13I've been watching the Israelites, and I've seen how stubborn and rebellious they are. 14So don't try to stop me! I am going to wipe them out, and no one on earth will remember they ever lived. Then I will let your descendants become an even bigger and more powerful nation than Israel.
Moses said:
15Fire was raging on the mountaintop as I went back down, carrying the two stones with the commandments on them. 16I saw how quickly you had sinned and disobeyed the Lord your God. There you were, worshiping the metal idol you had made in the shape of a calf. 17So I threw down the two stones and smashed them before your very eyes.
18-20I bowed down at the place of worship and prayed to the Lord, without eating or drinking for 40 days and nights. You had committed a terrible sin by making that idol, and the Lord hated what you had done. He was angry enough to destroy all of you and Aaron as well. So I prayed for you and Aaron as I had done before, and this time the Lord answered my prayers.
21It was a sin for you to make that idol, so I threw it into the fire to melt it down. Then I took the lump of gold, ground it into powder, and threw the powder into the stream flowing down the mountain.
22 You also made the Lord angry when you were staying at Taberah, at Massah, and at Kibroth-Hattaavah. 23 Then at Kadesh-Barnea the Lord said, “I am giving you the land, so go ahead and take it!” But since you didn't trust the Lord, you rebelled and disobeyed his command. 24In fact, you've rebelled against the Lord for as long as he has known you.
25After you had made the idol in the shape of a calf, the Lord said he was going to destroy you. So I lay face down in front of the Lord for 40 days and nights 26and prayed:
Our Lord, please don't wipe out your people. You used your great power to rescue them from Egypt and to make them your very own. 27Israel's ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob obeyed you faithfully. Think about them, and not about Israel's stubbornness, evil, and sin. 28If you destroy your people, the Egyptians will say, “The Lord promised to give Israel land, but he wasn't powerful enough to keep his promise. In fact, he hated them so much that he took them into the desert and killed them.” 29But you, our Lord, chose the people of Israel to be your own, and with your mighty power you rescued them from Egypt.
translation_text:
Isirayeel yab kaa sɔ́ǹ bin kíǹee
1Isirayeel yab, Pīlifìmaan! Ni làá dùtī Jɔɔdan buŋŋu dee. Ni làá cù kí já nì anibul ŋin sá akpaan ki jítiǹ-ni ki pɔ̄ɔǹ-nee nib ní kí fōō bi-timmu mun sá ŋkpaamu bi máń agun ki māntìi tú an fɔ̀kɔ̀ ki tin tūū kutaayee. 2Ni làá jà Anaaki yab tinikpaandi nì tinifɔkɔl bin kóò niinee. Nimbi ni-ba nyí-bi ní ki gbìl̄ bi sòon̄ bi-pu yii: «Ŋma di ŋūǹ kí sīĺ Anaaki yab nimbiin dee?» 3Ama béémaan díǹ yii ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu u-ba di līī ni-nyɔkɔpu kii ŋŋmi ŋun wù ki céetí tikɔkɔee. Úǹ di làá nàan̄-bi ní kí dū-bi kí ŋá ni-ŋaan ní ní jà-bi kí nyāntí bi-tiŋki pu, ní kí kpɔ̀ kí céetí-bi malaa kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn pōoǹ-ni puee.
4Ama ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu yaa láa jìn̄-bi ki dū bi-tiŋki ki tīī-nee, ní taa láa lì yii: «An sá ti nín bí deedeeyee pu ní ti-Dindaan cáań-ti tí fōō kitiŋ nee kí nīn kíǹ ki yì.» Aayee, an kaa sá ni nín bí deedeeyee pu, ama an sá anibul nee kpitii pu ní ti-Dindaan làá jà-bi kí fōō bi-tiŋki kí tīī-ni. 5An puee, an kaa baasii sá yii ni bí deedee àá ni-baamɔŋyi pu ní ni làá fōō bi-tiŋki kí nīn kíǹ ki yì. Ama an sá anibul gbanti kpitii pu ní ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá jà-bi kí fōō bi-tiŋki kí tīī-ni. U làá ŋá kii u nín nìn pōoǹ ni-naanjab Abraam nì Isaaki nì Jaakɔbee puee ní. 6Míǹ puee, ní béémaan yii an kaa sá ni nín bí deedee fiii gba puee pu ní ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá fōō kitimmɔntii nee kí tīī-ni ní nīn yì. Ibaamɔn poonee, ni sá dinibul din pɔbil tīlifèe ní.
Sindaariya nabil
7Ní téetímaan tibɔti nee kí taa súntí-tì dalba dalba ni nín kɔ́ǹ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu diŋuul kuteeun puee. Kí yòon̄ ŋwiin ŋun ní ni nyáń Eejipitee kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋun ni bāań laakin ni bí neeyee, ni pée bí ní ki jáà nì Unimbɔti kaa gbèentí. 8Ooreeb jool puee, ni nìn tí gbítì ti-Dindaan ŋuul ní ki yāntì u gíí diŋuul tikpil áli u bàà nìn là kí kpɔ̀ kí céetí-ni. 9M nìn jɔ́m̀ dijool pu kí fōoń titaŋkpapilindi tin pu ti-Dindaan nìn ŋmàn̄ mpèé ŋun u nìn yóoǹ ni nì u kansikinee marab. M nìn ŋá dijool pu niin iwiin imuŋku ili ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu, kaa jíń tibaaa, kaa nyùn̄ tiba mun. 10Ti-Dindaan nìn dū titaŋkpapilindi tili tin pu u nìn dū úǹ u-ba ŋal ki ŋmàn̄ee ki tīī-mi. Tipilindi gbanti pu ní marab bin kɔkɔ ti-Dindaan nìn dūu tīī-ni dijool pu, ŋŋmi poon, ŋyunti ŋun ni nìn kóoǹ ki kpáfì dijool taapuee nìn kā.
11Iwiin imuŋku ili kúntidalee ní ti-Dindaan dū dipoondi taŋkpapilinti tili gbanti ki dūu tīī-mi. 12Míǹ boonee ní ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: «Yīkì m-cee doo kí kpákatí malaa, kun puee dinibul din a nyántìń Eejipiti tiŋkinee kɔ́ tijɔkɔndin. Binibee kaa tāaǹ kí fàtī bi-boon kí tīī m-marab bin m tīī-bee. Bi dūntì tikúti ki dūu mɔ́ɔ́ diwaal.» 13Niinee ní ti-Dindaan gíti bí-mi yii: «M nín kpēē dinibul neeyee, m ká yii di-pɔbil lafun gbìfì. 14Pée yàntī-mi ḿ kpɔ̀ kí céetí-bi bí taa ti pée gbìl̄ bi-pu kitiŋ pu. Ama siiyee, m làá dī sii pu kí náań ditimbundi din cáá mpɔn ki wīikí ki jítiǹ-bee ní.» 15Niinee ní m kíĺ nsan ki nín kpákatiń dijool pu. Ŋŋmi nìn dá láá bí dijool gbanti pu. M nìn ŋúb́ dipoondi taŋkpapilinti tilee m-ŋaan. 16M kpēēyee ki lafun ká yii ni yīntiǹ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu. Ni nìn dūntì tikúti ki dūu mɔ́ɔ́ diwaal ki nántiǹ dinabil. Naa nìn pée tāaǹ ki fātì ni-boon ki tīī ti-Dindaan marab bin u tīī-nee. 17An pu ní m nìn dū titaŋkpapilindi tili tin m nìn ŋúb́ee ki yá kitiŋ ní ki gbáń ki wīī-ŋi ni-nimbiin niin.
Mooyiisi gbāam̀ Unimbɔti Isirayeel yab pu
18Míǹ boonee ní m tātìi dōoǹ dicincibil ti-Dindaan nimbiin, ki ŋá iwiin imuŋku ili ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu, kii mpeepeekaam m nín nìn tí ŋá puee, kaa jíń tijinaaa, kaa nyùn̄ nnyim mun. M ŋá míǹ di sá ni nìn yīntiǹ ti-Dindaan ki ŋá min kaa kítì u-ceeyee ki gbítì u-ŋuul. 19M nìn fāŋkì diŋuul din ti-Dindaan nìn gíí ni-puee. U-ŋuulee nìn pɔ̄ɔ̄ tikpil áli gba u nìn là kí kpɔ̀ kí céetí-ni. Ama min bí nee muee, ti-Dindaan nìn tí pílifiǹ-mi ki fōō m-wimmeem. 20Ti-Dindaan nìn gíí Aarɔn mun pu diŋuul ki nìn là kí kpɔ̀-u. Niinee ní m mēē Aarɔn mun pu. 21M nìn yōoǹ ikpiti in ni ŋée tundi, an dàkà yii dinabilee, ki tɔ́ ŋŋmin, ní ki gbáń ki mátì-dì ki nàn̄-dì dúsi dusi kii ntamee, ní ki dū ntamee ki sītì mbun ŋun nyēeń dijool pu ki pùub̀ ki sìntēe poon.
22Ni nìn tí yāntì ti-Dindaan gíí diŋuul Tabeera nì Maasa nì Kiibirooti-Taafa timmun mun. 23Míǹ mbaantiim ní Kadeesi-Baarneeya, ŋyunti ŋun ti-Dindaan nìn tú-ni ki lī yii: «Cùmaan kí fōō kitiŋ kin ní m dūu tīī-nee», ni nìn ŋá ntafapɔn kaa nìn fātìi tɔ́ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nyɔɔbundi. Naa nìn cáá u-pu dimákal ní kaa nìn dū tin u sòon̄ee ki túń ditundi. 24Doooo ŋwiin ŋun m béè-nee, ni pée sá bin jáà nì ti-Dindaanee ní.
25Ti-Dindaan nìn bíikì ki lī yii u làá kpɔ̀ kí céetí-ni. An di yì-tì ní m nìn tātìi dōoǹ dicincibil ti-Dindaan nimbiin ki ŋá iwiin imuŋku ili ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu. 26M nìn mēē ti-Dindaan yii: «M-Dindaan Unimbɔti, taa kpɔ̀ kí céetí a-nibul nee. Sii di yì-bi ní ki dū a-pɔŋkpaaŋŋu nì a-ŋal pɔfiŋu ki fīī-bi ki nyántìń Eejipiti tiŋkin. 27Téetí a-tɔntɔnliibi Abraam nì Isaaki nì Jaakɔb pu. Taa kpèè binib nee pɔɔpɔŋŋu nì bi-toonam nì bi-kpitii pu kí lì yii a làá ŋá-bi tiba. 28Á taa yàntī kitiŋ kin poon a nyántìń-tee nib ń lì yii: <Bi-Dindaan kaa nìn pée ŋūǹ kí cáá-bi kí kɔ́ǹ kitiŋ kin u nìn pōoǹ kí tīī-bee ni,> àá kí gíti lì yii: <Waa nìn pée néeń-bee pu ní u nyántì-bi Eejipiti tiŋkin kí cáá-bi kí kpɔ̀ kuteeu pu.> 29Ti-Dindaan, bi sá a-nib ní. Sii di yì-bi ní ki dū a-pɔŋkpaaŋŋu nì a-ŋal pɔfiŋu ki nyántìń-bi Eejipiti tiŋkin!»

english_text:
The Second Set of Commandments
(Exodus 34.1-10)
Moses said to the people:
1The Lord told me to chisel out two flat stones, just like the ones he had given me earlier. He also commanded me to make a wooden chest, then come up the mountain and meet with him. 2He told me that he would write on the new stones the same words he had written on the ones I broke, and that I could put these stones in this sacred chest.
3So I made a chest out of acacia wood, and I chiseled two flat stones like the ones I broke. Then I carried the stones up the mountain, 4where the Lord wrote the Ten Commandments on them, just as he had done the first time. The commandments were exactly what he had announced from the fire, when you were gathered at the mountain.
After the Lord returned the stones to me, 5I took them down the mountainside and put them in the chest, just as he had commanded. And they are still there.
Aaron Died
(Numbers 20.22-29)
Moses said to Israel:
6 Later we set up camp at the wells belonging to the descendants of Jaakan. Then we moved on and camped at Moserah, where Aaron died and was buried, and his son Eleazar became the priest. 7Next, we camped at Gudgodah and then at Jotbathah, where there are flowing streams.
The Levites Were Appointed To Carry the Chest
Moses said to Israel:
8 After I put the two stones in the sacred chest, the Lord chose the tribe of Levi, not only to carry the chest, but also to serve as his priests at the place of worship and to bless the other tribes in his name. And they still do these things. 9The Lord promised that he would always provide for the tribe of Levi, and that's why he won't give them any land, when he divides it among the other tribes.
The Lord Answered the Prayers of Moses
(Exodus 34.9,10,27-29)
Moses said to Israel:
10 When I had taken the second set of stones up the mountain, I spent 40 days and nights there, just as I had done before. Once again, the Lord answered my prayer and did not destroy you. 11Instead, he told me, “Moses, get ready to lead the people into the land that I promised their ancestors.”
What the Lord Wants
Moses said:
12People of Israel, what does the Lord your God want from you? The Lord wants you to respect and follow him, to love and serve him with all your heart and soul, 13and to obey his laws and teachings that I am giving you today. Do this, and all will go well for you.
14Everything belongs to the Lord your God, not only the earth and everything on it, but also the sky and the highest heavens. 15Yet the Lord loved your ancestors and wanted them to belong to him. So he chose them and their descendants rather than any other nation, and today you are still his people.
16Remember your agreement with the Lord and stop being so stubborn. 17 The Lord your God is more powerful than all other gods and lords, and his tremendous power is to be feared. His decisions are always fair, and you cannot bribe him to change his mind. 18 The Lord defends the rights of orphans and widows. He cares for foreigners and gives them food and clothing. 19And you should also care for them, because you were foreigners in Egypt.
20Respect the Lord your God, be faithful, and serve only him, making promises in his name. 21Offer your praises to him, because you have seen him work such terrifying miracles for you.
22 When your ancestors went to live in Egypt, there were only 70 of them. But the Lord has blessed you, and now there are more of you than there are stars in the sky.
translation_text:
Ti-Dindaan pūǹ ikpiti
1Niinee ní ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: «Kpítí titaŋkpapilindi tili kii tipeepeekaalee. Míǹ boonee á kpáá ndɔ dakaau. A yaa ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee, á jɔ̄mìń m-cee dijool pu doo. 2M làá ŋmà tipilindi gbanti pu anyɔɔbun ŋin nìn kā tipilimpeepeekaal pu a dūu lúkú ki wīīyee kí tīī-si á dūú ŋá dakaayee poon.» 3Niinee ní m dū busubu bun bi yíì akasiyayee dɔŋu ki kpáá dakaa ní ki kpítì titaŋkpapilindi tili ní ki ŋúb́-tì m-ŋaan, ki cáa jɔ́m̀ dijool pu. 4Kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn ŋmàn̄ pu mpeepeekaaminee, míǹ ní u tí fātìi ŋmàn̄ tipilindee pu marab saalaa bin pu u nìn sòon̄ dijool pu ŋŋmi poon ŋwiin ŋun ni nìn kóoǹ ki kpáfì dijool taapuee. U ŋmàn̄ míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki dū tipilindee ki tīī-mi. 5M fōō tipilindee ní ki kpákatìń dijool pu ní ki dū-tì ki ŋá dakaa un m nìn kpááyee poon. Niin ní tipilindee gbíntìi kā kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn kpáafì-mi puee.
6Míǹ boonee ní Isirayeel yab yíkì Beenee-Yaakan lɔkɔb cee ki cūtì Mooseela. Niin ní Aarɔn kpíì ní bi síb́-u ní u-jipɔɔn Eeleeyasaar fōō u-yil ki kpántì usaraaŋakpil. 7Bi nyáń niinee, ní ki cūtì Guudigoodaa, ní ki nyáń Guudigoodaa ki nín cá Yootibata, kitiŋ kin cáá ibun tikpilee. 8Ŋyunti gbanti ní ti-Dindaan lēē Leefii naakookun yab bí nīn tūntí ti-Dindaan poondi dakaau, kí nīn bí u-nimbiin ki tūǹ u-tundi ní kí nīn bìintí binib pu ti-Dindaan yindi pu. Ditundi din bi gbíntìi tūǹ ki dāa sāā díǹee dee. 9An pu ní bi nín làá yàkatī kitiŋ kí tīī Isirayeel naakɔtee, baa nìn kpáaǹ Leefii naakookun yab. Bíǹ jandi di sá diyimɔɔl din bi cáá kí nīn tūǹ ti-Dindaan tundee, kii ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nín nìn tùkū-bi puee.
10M nìn tí gbíntì dijool pu niin ki ŋá iwiin imuŋku ili ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu kii m nín nìn ŋá pu mpeepeekaamee. Min bí nee muee, ti-Dindaan nìn tí pílifì m-wimmeem ní ki yāntì kaa nāaǹ-ni. 11Ti-Dindaan nìn bí-mi yii: «Yīkìm̄! Lìntī binib nee nyɔkɔpu bí cùú já kí fōō kitiŋ kin ní m nìn pōoǹ bi-naanjab yii m làá tīī-bee!»
Nín̄ néeń ti-Dindaan kí nīn tɔ́-u
12Kɔŋkɔnnee Isirayeel yab, ba ní ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu baasii là yii ní ŋá ní? U là yii ní fàŋkì-u, kí nīn ŋáań u nín là puee, kí nīn néeń-u ní kí nīn tūǹ u-tundi nì ni-pɔbil kɔkɔ nì ni-fam kɔkɔ. 13U là yii ní nīn ŋúb́ u-marab nì u-bɔkpaaŋi ŋin m bíi cáa tìì-ni díǹ nee, án nín làá ŋá pu án nīn ŋān̄ ki tīī-nee! 14Kpèè ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu di yì yilpu fɔ́ŋŋŋ ki yì kitiŋ nì tin kɔkɔ bí ki-puee. 15Ama, ti-Dindaan nìn dū u-ba ki nákáǹ ni-naanjab ŋmaniŋma ní, bíǹ ní u néeń. Kɔŋkɔnnee, nimbi bi-naantiibi ní u lēē anibul kɔkɔ kansikin, kii an nín bí pu díǹ nee. 16Míǹ puee ní kpántímaan ni-pɔbiliŋ kí dū ni-ba kɔkɔ kí sú ti-Dindaan, kí gbèen̄ kí taa ti jáǹ-u. 17Di sá yii úǹ di sá inimbɔti kɔkɔ Nimbɔtiu, ní ki sá bidindambi kɔkɔ Dindaan. U sá Unimbɔtikpaan, ki sá Mpɔŋkɔdaan ní ki sá Unimbɔti un cáá tifaandee. Waa pɔ̀ gandi, kaa fòol̄ ubɔ mun cee tiba kí pɔ̀-u. 18U mɔ́tí ataŋkpiibil nì bikpiipoobi pu, ní ki néeń unicaan un kóò ni-puee ki tìì-u u jīǹ, ki pèentí-u. 19Míǹ puee ni máaǹ kí nīn néeń binicambi bin kóò ni-puee, di sá yii nimbi ni-ba nìn sá binicambi ní Eejipiti tiŋkin.
20Fàŋkìmaan ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu kí nīn jáaḿ-u. Dūmaan ni-ba kɔkɔ kí tīī-u. Úǹ baba yindi pu ní ni máaǹ kí nīn pùtī. 21Úǹ ní ni máaǹ kí nyɔ̄ŋkì. Úǹ baba di sá ni-Nimbɔtiu. Úǹ di ŋá atuŋkpaan nì maamaaci tuuŋŋi ki tīī-ni. Nimbi ni-ba ká míǹ. 22Ni-naanjab nín dɔ́miń ki kɔ́ Eejipitee, bi nìn bí binib imuŋku ita nì saalaa ja ní. Ama kɔŋkɔnnee, ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu yāntì ni būtì kii iŋmalbijaa in bí kutaa puee.

english_text:
If You Are Loyal to the Lord, He Will Bless You
Moses said to Israel:
1The Lord is your God, so you must always love him and obey his laws and teachings. 2Remember, he corrected you and not your children. You are the ones who saw the Lord use his great power 3 when he worked miracles in Egypt, making terrible things happen to the king and all his people. 4 And when the Egyptian army chased you in their chariots, you saw the Lord drown them and their horses in the Red Sea. Egypt still suffers from that defeat!
5You saw what the Lord did for you while you were in the desert, right up to the time you arrived here. 6 And you saw how the Lord made the ground open up in the middle of our camp underneath the tents of Dathan and Abiram, who were swallowed up along with their families, their animals, and their tents.
7With your own eyes, you saw the Lord's mighty power do all these things.
8Soon you will cross the Jordan River, and if you obey the laws and teachings I'm giving you today, you will be strong enough to conquer the land 9that the Lord promised your ancestors and their descendants. It's rich with milk and honey, and you will live there and enjoy it for a long time. 10It's better land than you had in Egypt, where you had to struggle just to water your crops. 11But the hills and valleys in the promised land are watered by rain from heaven, 12because the Lord your God keeps his eye on this land and takes care of it all year long.
13 The Lord your God commands you to love him and to serve him with all your heart and soul. If you obey him, 14-15he will send rain at the right seasons, so you will have more than enough food, wine, and olive oil, and there will be plenty of grass for your cattle.
16But watch out! You will be tempted to turn your backs on the Lord. And if you worship other gods, 17the Lord will become angry and keep the rain from falling. Nothing will grow in your fields, and you will die and disappear from the good land that the Lord is giving you.
18 Memorize these laws and think about them. Write down copies and tie them to your wrists and your foreheads to help you obey them. 19Teach them to your children. Talk about them all the time—whether you're at home or walking along the road or going to bed at night, or getting up in the morning. 20Write them on the door frames of your homes and on your town gates. 21Then you and your descendants will live a long time in the land that the Lord promised your ancestors. Your families will live there as long as the sky is above the earth.
22Love the Lord your God faithfully and obey all the laws and teachings I'm giving you today. If you live the way the Lord wants, 23he will help you take the land. And even though the nations there are more powerful than you, the Lord will force them to leave when you attack. 24 You will capture the land everywhere you go, from the Southern Desert to the Lebanon Mountains, and from the Euphrates River west to the Mediterranean Sea. 25No one will be able to stand up to you. The Lord will make everyone terrified of you, just as he promised.
26You have a choice—do you want the Lord to bless you, or do you want him to put a curse on you? 27Today I am giving you his laws, and if you obey him, he will bless you. 28But if you disobey him and worship those gods that have never done anything for you, the Lord will put a curse on you.
29 After the Lord your God helps you take the land, you must have a ceremony where you announce his blessings from Mount Gerizim and his curses from Mount Ebal. 30You know that these two mountains are west of the Jordan River in land now controlled by the Canaanites living in the Jordan River valley. The mountains are west of the road near the sacred trees of Moreh on the other side of Gilgal.
31Soon you will cross the Jordan River to conquer the land that the Lord your God is giving you. And when you have settled there, 32be careful to obey his laws and teachings that I am giving you today.
translation_text:
Unimbɔti nín ŋá tin ki tīī Isirayeelee
1Nín̄ néeḿmaan ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu kí nīn ŋáań u nín bí yii ní ŋá puee, kí nīn ŋúb́ u-bɔkpaaŋi nì u-koobiliŋ nì u-marab baabadal. 2Nimbi bin sí díǹ nee, ní béé yii an kaa sá ni-biyaamu mun kaa nyí kaa ká ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu dàkatam nì u-pɔŋŋu nì u-tuŋkpaaŋŋee ní m bíi sòoǹ. 3Múǹ di kaa nìn ká maamaacib nì atuun ŋin ní u nìn ŋá Eejipiti tiŋkin ki dàkā Eejipiti bɔtiu Faaroo nì u-tiŋki nib kɔkɔee. 4Muaa nìn tí ká ti-Dindaan nín nìn yāntì Tikati mɔɔl nyim gbí ki léeǹ Eejipiti yab janjaliibi nì bi-taamui nì bi-janjatɔrɔkub pu, ki kūū ki céetì-bi kɔkɔ múb ŋyunti ŋun bi nìn bíi jìń ni-boonee 5An kaa nìn tí sá ni-biyaamu di nìn ká tin kɔkɔ u ŋá ki tīī-ni kuteeun, ki yāntì ni bāań laakin ni bí nee. 6Múǹ di kaa nìn tí ká u nín nìn ŋá Eeliyaab jipɔmbi Datan nì Abiiram bin nìn sá Rubeen naakookunee puee. U nìn yāntì kitiŋ cúu cōotì laakin bi nìn sée, ní bíǹ nì bi-dicaŋŋi nì bi-tantib nì bin kɔkɔ nìn yú bi-boonee jéetì poon ní kitiŋ fātìi dūu ŋéeb́ bi-pu Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nimbiin. 7Ni-nimbilaaliyin ní ti-Dindaan túń atuŋkpaan gbanti kɔkɔ. 8Míǹ puee nín̄ ŋúb́maan marab bin kɔkɔ m tīī-ni díǹ nee. Ni yaa ŋá mimmee, ni làá ŋmā kí ká mpɔn kí kɔ́ kitiŋ kin ni bíi dùtī Jɔɔdan buŋŋu kí tin fōō kí nīn kíǹ ki yì nee poon, 9ní kí ŋmā kí kàl̄ kitiŋ kin ti-Dindaan nìn pōoǹ kí tīī ni-naanjab nì bi-naantiibee poon kí yúntí. Kitiŋ gbanti poonee, tisiil nì nnaabiim còol̀ ní.
Kitiŋ kin ti-Dindaan kpèé tiŋanee
10Kitiŋ kin ni làá cùú fōō kí nīn kíǹ ki yì nee kaa bí kii Eejipiti tiŋki kin poon ni nyánní nee nín bí puee. Niinee, ni yaa nìn kùn̄ ki búĺ ni-wambooliiyee, ni nìn yàantí-i nnyim ní, kii bi nín yàantí tikuŋfaal kpaabu puee. 11Ama kitiŋ kin ni làá dùtī Jɔɔdan buŋŋu kí tin fōō nee sá ajoon nì atantaka tiŋki ní, ní utaa nì ki-pu. 12Kì sá kitiŋ kin pu ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu wúńee ní. Ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nimbil pée cɔ́ ki-pu ní baabadal, kí yòon̄ dibindi kíltam kí cáá sāā di-kúntitam.
13Míǹ puee ni yaa tɔ́ marab bin m tīī-ni díǹ nee, ki néeń ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu, ki nóó-u nì ni-pɔbil kɔkɔ nì ni-naŋki kɔkɔee, 14u làá yàntī utaa ń nīn nì ŋyunti ŋun ní an máaǹee, ukpaasiitaa nì useetaa kɔkɔ. Mimmee ni-bileeu nì ni-fiinyib nì ni-ɔliifib làá nīn lòoǹ tiŋan ní. 15U làá yàntī ni-naakpaapɔɔku ń nīn cáá timɔsɔn kí tīī ni-waŋkuti, ní nimbi ni-ba ń jī kí díkí.
16Ama ní nīn nyíǹ ni-ba an taa ŋmàtiǹ-ni ní fàtī ni-boon kí tīī-u, kí cùú nīn gbàantí awaa taapu ki jáaḿ-ŋi. 17Ni yaa ŋá míǹ, ti-Dindaan làá gíí ni-pu diŋuul ní kí dū kutaa kí pìin̄ ní utaa ń taa ti nì. Ni-tiŋki kaa ti làá ŋmā kí lòoǹ tikpaajin. An yaa ŋá mimmee naa làá sūŋkì ní kí kpú kí céetí kitimmɔntii kin ti-Dindaan tīī-nee poon. 18Dūmaan marab bin m tīī-ni díǹ nee kí ŋá ni-pɔbiliŋin nì ni-nammun. Dūmaan-bi kí fìn̄ ni-ŋalii nì ni-yigbeeŋi pu án nín làá ŋá pu ní taa súntí bi-puee. 19Dūmaan-bi kí dàkà ni-biyaamu. Báà ni yaa bí ni-diikunaaa, ni tàkā nsanni ki còom̄ ki cáaa, ni dɔ̄ɔɔ, ni yúɔɔɔ, bí nīn kā ni-nyɔkɔn. 20Ŋmàmaan-bi kí nákań ni-diiŋŋi punyɔmmu pu nì ni-timmu punuubi pu. 21Ni yaa ŋá mimmee, ni nì ni-biyaamu làá kàl̄ kitiŋ kin ti-Dindaan pōoǹ kí tīī ni-naanjabee pu kí yúntí kii kutaa kun dàn̄ kitiŋ pu nee nín làá yúntí puee.
22Tiŋman, ni yaa lafun ŋúb́ marab bin m tīī-ni díǹ nee kɔkɔ ki néeń ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu ki ŋáań u nín là puee, ki dū ni-ba ki nákáǹ-uee, 23ti-Dindaan làá jà anibul nee kɔkɔ kí tīī-ni ní ní fōō anibul ŋin sá akpaan ki pɔ̄ɔ̄ ki jítiǹ-ni nee timmu kí nīn yì. 24Laakin kamaa ní ni-taal yaa tāāyee làá kpántí ni-wanti ní. Ni-tiŋki làá dāá nīn wāā kí yòon̄ kuteeu kí cáá sāā Leebanɔn, ní kí yòon̄ Eefiraati mɔɔl kí cáá sāā Meediiteeranee tiŋkuu ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú. 25Báà ubɔ kaa dāa ŋūǹ kí sīĺ ni-nimbiin kí jáǹ-ni. Laakin kamaa ní ni yaa pée cūtèe, ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá yàntī niin nib kɔkɔ ń fàŋkì-ni ní bi-wunti ń kpú kii u nín pōoǹ-ni puee.
26Kpèèmaan, m dū dibiindi nì mbusu kí bíl̀ díǹ ni-nimbiin. 27Ni yaa tɔ́ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu marab bin m tīī-ni díǹ neeyee, dibiindi dee. 28Ama ni yaa kaa tɔ́ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu marab, ní ki yaa fātì ni-boon ki tīī tin kɔkɔ m kpáafì-ni díǹ nee ki cūtìi nóó awaa ŋin naa nyée, mbusu dee.
29Ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu yaa láa cáá-ni ki kɔ́ǹ kitiŋ kin ni bíi bɔ́ntí kí cù kí fōō nee poonee, ní tɔ́kɔń Geerisiim jool yilpu kí tīī dibiindi, ní kí tɔ́kɔń Eebaal jool yilpu kí tɔ̄ mbusu. 30Kii ni nín nyí puee, ajoon gbanti bí ni yaa dūtì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ki yōoǹ didandi din dɔ̄ ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee, ní ki bí Kanaan yab bin kóò Arabaa tiŋki poonee, Giilgaal caŋin. An kaa dátiǹ Mooree sukpaaŋyi. 31Ni làá dùtī Jɔɔdan buŋŋu kí cù kí fōō kitiŋ kin ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu tīī-nee dee. Ní fōō kitiŋ gbanti kí nīn kíǹ ki kóò ki-ni. 32Ní pɔ́ɔm̀maan ni-ba kí nīn tɔ́ abɔkpaa nì akoobil ŋin kɔkɔ m tīī-ni díǹ nee.

english_text:
Only One Place To Worship the Lord
Moses said to Israel:
1Now I'll tell you the laws and teachings that you have to obey as long as you live. Your ancestors worshiped the Lord, and he is giving you this land. 2But the nations that live there worship other gods.
