But don't take any with you when you leave. 25In the same way, if you are in a grain field that belongs to someone else, you can pick heads of grain and eat the kernels. But don't cut down the stalks of grain and take them with you.
translation_text:
1Ubɔ ń taa cáá u-baa nimpoobi kansikin ubɔ. U yaa ŋá mimmee, u kpēē u-baa dooŋu fám.
Bin kaa máaǹ kí nīn bí Unimbɔti samaau kansikinee
2Uninja un sá ufaalee àá un ninjati bi yaa gíí ki tūkutèe kaa máaǹ kí kɔ́ ti-Dindaan samaau kansikin.
3Unil un sá dikpacantibilee nì u-naantitɔntɔkɔŋ kí tin sāā saalaa pu gba kaa máaǹ kí kɔ́ ti-Dindaan samaau kansikin.
4Amɔn yab nì Moowaab yab nì bi-naantitɔntɔkɔŋ kí tin sāā saalaa pu gba kaa máaǹ kí kɔ́ ti-Dindaan samaau kansikin. 5Di sá yii ŋyunti ŋun ni nìn nyánní Eejipiti tiŋkin ki dòońee, baa nìn nyánní ki túŋkì-ni kí tīī-ni tijin nì nnyim. Ní míǹ boonee, bi cūtìi yōoǹní Beewɔɔr jipɔɔn, Balaam un sá Peetɔɔr tiŋki kin bí Aram Naarayiimee, ki tīī-u animbil ú tɔ̄-ni mbusu. 6Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu kaa nìn pílifiǹ Balaam gbanti. Ama u nìn yāntì u nín tòó-ni mbusu uŋyee kpántí dibiindi ní ki tìì-ni, kun puee ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu néeń-ni ní. 7Dalba dalba ní taa nyàab̀ atimbun ali gbanti nyɔkɔpu cùtam, kí taa píí-bi kubɔɔtiiu.
8Ní taa nín kpèé ki sìŋkīǹ Eedoom yab kii bi sá ntimbiil nibee, di sá yii bi sá ni-nabiyaamu ní. Ní taa kpèè kí sìŋkīǹ Eejipiti yab mun, di sá yii ni kāl̀ bi-tiŋkin kunicaŋu. 9Bi-naantitɔntɔkɔl ditataatiil ŋūǹ kí kɔ́ ti-Dindaan samaau kansikin.
Dijanjanaapaal pu nyaŋkanti
10Ni yaa yíkì ki cá kí jáǹ ni-nannanliibi ní ki kóoǹ ki kpáfì laaba ki ŋātì dijanjanaapaalee, ní nīn nyíǹ ni-ba kí taa ŋá tin kamaa kaa ŋān̄ee. 11Ni-kansikin ubɔ yaa dɔ̄ ki gèeǹ kunyeeu ní ki nyéem̀ tijati ki kɔ́ tijɔkɔndinee, udaan ń nyā dinaapaalin kí taa kɔ́nní ŋwiin gbanti. 12Ama kujoou yaa bíi jóotée, ú nyàab̀ nnyim kí fàl̀, ní ŋwìiń yaa jéetèe ú fàtīí gítiń bin kíǹee cee.
13Ní lēē dinaapaal kpaanceetiŋu laaba kí nīn cáà niin ataa pu. 14Ujanjal kamaa máaǹ kí nīn cáá tigbakaal ní u yaa cūtì ataa puee, ú gbà mbòó kí sɔ́ntí, ní u yaa dóòyee ú kàfì ntam kí bìin̄. 15Di sá yii ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu dòoń ki màntī ni-naapaal pu kí wúń ni-pu, ní kí nyāntí-ni ni-nannanliibi ŋaan kí tīī-ni dijajil. An puee ni-naapaal máaǹ kí nīn bí circir ní, án nín làá ŋá pu ú taa ká ni-kansikin titantan tiba kí fàtī u-boon kí tīī-nee.
Uyumbu un sáǹee bɔti
16Uyumbu yaa sáǹ ki kɔ́-see, á taa fàtīí gíiǹ-u kí tīī u-dindaan. 17U ŋūǹ kí kɔ́ ni-kansikin, laakin yaa fáatì-uee, nì kitiŋ kin u yaa lēē kí nīn bée poon. Á taa mùul̀-u.
Alaakpaatuun bɔti
18Isirayeel sapɔmbi nì Isirayeel naacimpɔmbi ubɔ ń taa dū u-ba kí tīī alaakpaatuun. 19Unimpu àá uninja yaa ŋá alaakpaatuun ní ki ká animbilee, ú taa cáań animbil gbanti kí pà ipoon in ní u pōoǹ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiuee pɔndi, kun puee alaakpaanimbil sá ntimbiil wanti ní ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti cee.
Kí pìnnì animbil bí pà kí páań
20Ni yaa pīnnì ni-nabiki animbil àá tijin àá tin ní an yaa pée sée, ní taa páb́-u ú téeǹ-ni kí páań. 21Ni ŋūǹ kí pìnnì unicaan kí yàntī ú dāá téeǹ-ni kí páań, ama ní taa ŋá míǹ ni-nabiki Isirayeel niliu cee. Ni yaa ŋá mimmee ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá bìin̄ ni-tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ pu kitiŋ kin ni làá kɔ́ kí fōō ki nīn kíǹ ki yèe poon.
Diwampoondi bɔti
22Ni yaa pōoǹ kí ŋá tiba kí tīī ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiuee, ní pà ni-pɔndi malaa, di sá yii ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá dāá pée bàlifì-ni, ní ní dāá fōō dibɔkpil. 23Ama ni yaa kaa pōoǹ tibee, naa yīntì mun. 24Tin nyáń ni-nyɔkɔnee, see ní pɔ́ɔǹ kí ŋá míǹ, kun puee ni-ba nyɔkɔn ní an nyáń ní ni pōoǹ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu dipoondi.
Nsan pú unil ń kìtī asubil kí ŋmɔ́
25Ni yaa kɔ́ ni-nabiki fiinyi kpaabunee, ni ŋūǹ kí kìtī fiinyi biliŋ kí ŋmɔ́ ni nín là puee, ama ní taa kìtī kí ŋá ni-lookun.
26Ni yaa tí kɔ́ ni-nabiki bilee kpaabun, ni ŋūǹ kí dū ni-ŋalii kí lēē ifin kí ŋmèem̀ kí ŋmɔ́, ama naa máaǹ kí dū ugɔti kí cā.

english_text:
A Law about Divorce
Moses said to Israel:
1 Suppose a woman was divorced by her first husband because he found something disgraceful about her. He wrote out divorce papers, gave them to her, and sent her away. 2Later she married another man, 3who then either divorced her in the same way or died. 4Since she has slept with her second husband, she cannot marry her first husband again. Their marriage would pollute the land that the Lord your God is giving you, and he would be disgusted.
Newlyweds
Moses said to Israel:
5If a man and a woman have been married less than one year, he must not be sent off to war or sent away to do forced labor. He must be allowed to stay home for a year and be happy with his wife.
Loans
Moses said to Israel:
6When you lend money to people, you are allowed to keep something of theirs as a guarantee that they will pay back the loan. But don't take one or both of their millstones, or else they may starve. They need these stones for grinding grain into flour to make bread.
Kidnapping
Moses said to Israel:
7 If you are guilty of kidnapping Israelites and forcing them into slavery, you will be put to death to remove this evil from the community.
Skin Diseases
Moses said to Israel:
8 I have told the priests what to do if any of you have leprosy, so do exactly what they say. 9 And remember what the Lord your God did to Miriam after you left Egypt.
Loans
Moses said to Israel:
10 When you lend money to people, you are allowed to keep something of theirs as a guarantee that the money will be paid back. But you must not go into their house to get it. 11Wait outside, and they will bring out the item you have agreed on.
12Suppose someone is so poor that a coat is the only thing that can be offered as a guarantee on a loan. Don't keep the coat overnight. 13Instead, give it back before sunset, so the owner can keep warm and sleep and ask the Lord to bless you. Then the Lord your God will notice that you have done the right thing.
Poor People's Wages
Moses said:
14 If you hire poor people to work for you, don't hold back their pay, whether they are Israelites or foreigners who live in your town. 15Pay them their wages at the end of each day, because they live in poverty and need the money to survive. If you don't pay them on time, they will complain about you to the Lord, and he will punish you.
The Death Penalty
Moses said to Israel:
16 Parents must not be put to death for crimes committed by their children, and children must not be put to death for crimes committed by their parents. Don't put anyone to death for someone else's crime.
Don't Mistreat the Powerless
Moses said to Israel:
17 Make sure that orphans and foreigners are treated fairly. And if you lend money to a widow and want to keep something of hers to guarantee that she will pay you back, don't take any of her clothes. 18You were slaves in Egypt until the Lord your God rescued you. That's why I am giving you these laws.
Leave Some of Your Harvest for the Poor
Moses said to Israel:
19 If you forget to bring in a stack of harvested grain, don't go back in the field to get it. Leave it for the poor, including foreigners, orphans, and widows, and the Lord will make you successful in everything you do.
20When you harvest your olives, don't try to get them all for yourself, but leave some for the poor. 21And when you pick your grapes, go over the vines only once, then let the poor have what is left. 22You lived in poverty as slaves in Egypt until the Lord your God rescued you. That's why I am giving you these laws.
translation_text:
Unimpu un bi jìn̄ee bɔti
1Ubɔ yaa cáá unimpu ní ki ká yii unimpuee bɔti kaa ti mɔ̄ǹ-u kun puee u ká u-pu tibee, ú ŋmà kugbɔŋu kun dàkà yii u jìn̄-uee kí ŋúbíǹ-u ní kí nín jà-u u-cindi. 2Unimpuee yaa búntì ní ki tin ká uninja ubɔ ki mɔ́ǹ, 3ní uninja liliiti un u mɔ́ǹ gbantee mun yaa bí yii waa ti là-u ní ki mun ŋmàn̄ gbɔŋku kun dàkà yii u jìn̄-uee ki ŋúbiǹ-u ní ki mun tí jìn̄-u u-cindi, àá tí lì yii u-cal liliiti gbanti kpíì. 4Niinee, u-cal peepeekaa un nìn jìn̄-uee kaa ti cáá nsan kí fàtīí cáá-u, di sá yii unimpuee kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. Waa ti ŋūǹ kí cáá-u. U yaa fātìi cáá-uee, an sá ntimbiil tundi ní ti-Dindaan nimbiin. Ní taa kɔ́ǹ kitiŋ kin ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá dūú tīī-ni ní nīn kíǹ ki yèe tijɔkɔndi.
Uninja un cáá unimpucaanee
5Uninja un cáá unimpucaanee kaa máaǹ kí cù kujaau. Baa máaǹ kí tīī-u ditundi diba mun ú tɔ̄. U cáá dibimmɔndi kí tɔ̄ u-ba kí kàl̄ mmɔŋki kí kɔ̀ntī unimpu un u cááyee nimbiliŋ.
Toolima bɔti
6Ubɔ yaa cáá-ni dipɔndee, ní taa cùú yòon̄ u-naaku toolima, kí taa yòon̄ u-namintidɔŋu gba. Ni yaa ŋá mimmee, an bí kii ni fōō kun u ŋáań ki jīǹ ki bí dimaŋfalinee ní toolima.
Unil un bi cúú mpɔnee
7Ni yaa ká ubɔ cúú u-nabiki Isirayeel nib kansikin ubɔ ki dū-u ki kpántì u-yumbuu àá u dū-u ki nyáfèe, ní kpɔ̀ udaan. Ní ŋá míǹ kí nyāntí ikpiti ni-kansikin.
Dinyaŋgbandi bɔti
8An yaa sá dinyaŋgbandi weeŋŋu jandee, ní kpèè tiŋan kí ŋá kii Leefii yab bisaraaŋaliibi nín dàkā yii ní ŋá puee deedee. Ni máaǹ kí ŋá tin m kpáafì-bi bí dūú dàkà-nee. 9Ní téetí ni nín nyáń Eejipiti tiŋkin ki dòoń ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu ŋá Miiriyam pu nsannee.
Toolima bɔti tiba mun
10Ni yaa pīnnì ni-juti tibee, ní taa bìl̄ kí kɔ́ u-dumpu kí yòon̄ tiba toolima. 11Ní nīn yú mmɔŋki ní ni-pɔnliu u-ba ń cáań-ni kun u làá dūú tīī-ni toolimee. 12Udaan yaa sá usoodaan ní ki yaa dū u-satabiiŋkaau ki tīī-ni toolimee, ní taa yàntī kutaa ń wúntí u-toolimau gbanti pu ni-dumpu. 13Ní fàtīí gíiǹ u-satau kí tīī-u ní ŋwìiń ń nín jēetí, án nín làá ŋá pu ú ŋmā kí ká kí bìin̄ kunyeeuee. Ni yaa ŋá mimmee, u làá mèè kí bìin̄ ni-pu ní án nīn sá min kítì ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu ceeyee.
Bí nīn tɔ́ usoodaan
14Ní taa mùul̀ upaadaan un sá usoodaan kaa cáá tibee. An yaa sá ni-nabiyaamu Isirayeel yab ubɔ àá binicambi bin kóò ni-tiŋkinee kansikin ubɔɔɔ, ní taa mùul̀ udaan. 15Ní pà u-paati ní ŋwìiń ń nín jēetí, di sá yii u sá usoodaan, ní animbil gbanti pu ní u máká. An yaa kaa sá mimmee, u làá tīminsì ti-Dindaan kí tɔ̄ ni-pu ní ní kɔ́ ikpitin.
Unil kamaa kpitii pu ní bi làá kpɔ̀-u
16Baa máaǹ kí kpɔ̀ bibaatiibi bi-biyaamu kpitii pu, kaa tí máaǹ kí kpɔ̀ mbiyaamu bi-baabi kpitii pu. Báà ŋma kpitii pu ní u máaǹ kí kpú.
Bi nín máaǹ kí ŋá bisoodambi puee
17Ní taa mùul̀ unicaan àá ditaŋkpiibil ibɔsoon poon, kí taa yòon̄ ukpiipu bɔkutil toolima. 18Téetímaan yii ni nìn sá iyumbu ní Eejipiti tiŋkin ní ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu dá-ni ki líì. An pu ní m kpáafí-ni ní ŋúb́ tibɔti nee.
19Ni yaa bíi cēē ni-kpaajinti ní ki yaa súntì dibɔ́ndi diba pu boonee, ní taa fàtīí gítí ni-boon kí yòon̄-dì. Ní yàntī-dì, binicambi nì ataŋkpiibil nì bikpiipoobi yaa bíi lúlifí ki tin kée, bí yòon̄ ní ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu ń bìin̄ ni-tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ pu. 20Ni yaa kītì ɔliifi biliŋee, ní taa fàtīí gítí kí lūlifì. Ní yàntī abil ŋin kíǹ ki lúń busubu puee kí tīī binicambi nì ataŋkpiibil nì bikpiipoobi. 21Ni yaa tí kītì fiinyi biliŋee, ní taa fàtīí gítí kí lūlifì. Ní yàntī abil ŋin kíǹ ki lúńee kí tīī binicambi nì ataŋkpiibil nì bikpiipoobi. 22Ní taa súntí yii nimbi ni-ba nìn sá iyumbu ní Eejipiti tiŋkin. An pu ní m kpáafí-ni ní ŋúb́ tibɔti nee.

english_text:
Whipping as Punishment for a Crime
Moses said to Israel:
1-2Suppose you and someone else each accuse the other of doing something wrong, and you go to court, where the judges decide you are guilty. If your punishment is to be beaten with a whip, one of the judges will order you to lie down, and you will receive the number of lashes you deserve. 3 Forty lashes is the most that you can be given, because more than that might make other Israelites think you are worthless.
Don't Muzzle an Ox
Moses said to Israel:
4 Don't muzzle an ox while it is threshing grain.
A Son for a Dead Brother
Moses said to Israel:
5-6 Suppose two brothers are living on the same property, when one of them dies without having a son to carry on his name. If this happens, his widow must not marry anyone outside the family. Instead, she must marry her late husband's brother, and their first son will be the legal son of the dead man.
7 But suppose the brother refuses to marry the widow. She must go to a meeting of the town leaders at the town gate and say, “My husband died without having a son to carry on his name. And my husband's brother refuses to marry me so I can have a son.”
8The leaders will call the living brother to the town gate and try to persuade him to marry the widow. But if he doesn't change his mind and marry her, 9she must go over to him while the town leaders watch. She will pull off one of his sandals and spit in his face, while saying, “That's what happens to a man who won't help provide descendants for his dead brother.” 10From then on, that man's family will be known as “the family of the man whose sandal was pulled off.”
When Two Men Fight
Moses said to Israel:
11If two men are fighting, and the wife of one man tries to rescue her husband by grabbing the other man's private parts, 12you must cut off her hand. Don't have any mercy.
Be Honest in Business
Moses said to Israel:
13-14 Don't try to cheat people by having two sets of weights or measures, one to get more when you are buying, and the other to give less when you are selling. 15If you weigh and measure things honestly, the Lord your God will let you enjoy a long life in the land he is giving you. 16But the Lord is disgusted with anyone who cheats or is dishonest.
Wipe Out Amalek
Moses said:
17 People of Israel, do you remember what the Amalekites did to you after you came out of Egypt? 18You were tired, and they followed along behind, attacking those who could not keep up with the others. This showed that the Amalekites have no respect for God.
19The Lord your God will help you capture the land, and he will give you peace. But when that day comes, you must wipe out Amalek so completely that no one will remember they ever lived.
translation_text:
Ubɔsoonli ń sòoǹ tibɔti ti-pú
1Binib bili yaa jáàyee, bí cù kubɔsoondiin ní bibɔsoonliibi ń sòoǹ bi-bɔti kí pɔ̀ un bɔti ŋān̄ee ní kí kpɔ̀ un bɔti kaa ŋān̄ee bɔti. 2An yaa sá bí gbá un jíń dibɔkpilee, ubɔsoonli ń yàntī ú dòon̄ kitiŋ u-nimbiin ní kí yàntī bí gbá-u anaalab. U-bɔkpil nín bàlifī bí gbá-u puee, míǹ ní bi máaǹ kí gbá-u. 3Ama ubɔsoonlee kaa máaǹ kí yàntī bí gbá-u kí jītí anaalab imuŋku ili pu. Kun puee bi yaa gbáń-u an jítì míǹ puee, ni kíǹ ki bíi kpèé ki sìŋkīǹ ni-nabiki dee.
Unaa
4Ní taa bóob́ unaa un tà ki gbátí adibilee nyɔkɔ.
Ukpiipu un kaa cáá kibikee bɔti
5Nnabiyaamu di yaa bí ní ki kóò dicilpu, ní bi-kansikin ubɔ yaa cáá unimpu kaa láá màl̄ kibiki ní ki kpíì ki fá u-nimpuuee, ukpiipuee kaa máaǹ kí nyā kudicaŋuee poon kí cùú mɔ̄ǹ ubɔ laaba. U-cal nabiki kiba di fòol̄-u kí cáá ní kí ŋá kii mara nín bālifì puee. 6U-cal nabikee yaa cáá-uee, kibininjabiki kipeekaai kin u làá màal̀ee di làá téeǹ utaŋkpiilee yil u-yindi ń nīn bí ki cá jaanjaan Isirayeel tiŋkin.
7Ama uninjee yaa kaa là kí fōō u-nabiki kpiipuuee, ukpiipuee ń cù kí ká bitindaŋkpilib, kitiŋ punyɔkɔpu ní kí tùkù-bi yii: «M-cal nabiki kaa là u-nabiki utaŋkpiil yindi ń nīn bí ki cá Isirayeel yab kansikin. M-cal nabiki yíì kaa là kí ŋá min u máaǹ kí ŋá kí tīī-mee.» 8Niinee ní bitindaŋkpilib ń yíiń-u tibuul ní kí sòoǹ nì u. U yaa gbíntìi tɔ́kɔ́ ki lì yii: «Maa là kí fōō ukpiipuee», 9ní ukpiipuee ń còom̀ kí cù u-nimbiin bikpilib nín kā puee, ní kí tákatí u-naatakal diba ní kí tíiĺ kí pɔ̀l̄ u-nimbiin ní kí lì yii: «Bi nín ŋáań unil un kaa là kí màal̀ kí téeǹ u-nabiki yilee puee dee!» 10Niinee ní Isirayeel tiŋki poonee bí pɔ̄ kijapaai gbanti dicaŋku diyindi yii: «Un taalin bi tákatì dinaatakalee dicaŋku.»
Kujaau poon laakin baa máaǹ kí cúúyee
11Bininjab bili yaa bíi jáà ní un bi bíi gbáàyee nimpuu yaa bàà cūtì kí fīī u-cal un bíi gbáà-uee ŋaan, ní u yaa tāntì u-ŋal ki cúú un bíi gbáà u-calee ninjatee, 12ní gāā kí gùutī u-ŋal. Ní taa sɔ̄ u-saai báà fiii pu.
Nnyiŋfi nì mpúun ŋmàntitam bɔti
13Ní taa nín̄ cáá ni-lookun tikúti tin bi cáa ŋmàntī nnyiŋfee mili pu, diba ń nīn nyìm̀, din kíǹee ń taa nín̄ nyìm̀ ní nīn cáa mùul̄. 14Ní taa nín̄ tí cáá ni-dumpu asambiŋmantikaa mili pu, diba ń nīn sá dikpaandi, din kíǹee ń nīn sá kiwaai. 15Ni máaǹ tikúti tin ni cáa ŋmàntī nnyiŋfee ń nīn sá deedee kúti, ní asambil ŋin ni cáa ŋmàntī tiwanee ń nīn sá deedee sambiliŋ. Mimmee ni làá kàl̄ kitiŋ kin ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá tīī-nee poon kí yúntí. 16Di sá yii bin kɔkɔ ŋáań míǹ ki cáa mùul̄ee sá ntimbiil nib ní ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nimbiin.
Bi nín máaǹ kí ŋá Amaleeki yab puee
17Ní téetímaan Amaleeki yab nín nìn ŋá-ni pu ŋyunti ŋun ni nìn nyáń Eejipiti tiŋkin ki dòońee. 18Ŋyunti ŋun ni nìn gīī kaa ti pée ŋūǹ kí ŋá tibee, ní bi cílìń ni-boon pú ki nāaǹ bin nìn pánní boonee. Baa nìn fāŋkì Unimbɔti báà fiii. 19Ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu yaa láa nyántì-ni ni-nannanliibi bin māntì ki tú-nee ŋaan ki tīī-ni diŋuŋfil kitiŋ kin u làá dūú tīī-ni ní nīn kíǹ ki yèe poonee, ní dāá kpɔ̀ kí céetí Amaleeki yab kitiŋ pu, án nín làá ŋá pu báà ubɔ ń taa ti téetí bi-puee. Ní taa súntí tibɔti gbanti!

english_text:
Give the Lord the First Part of Your Harvest
Moses said to Israel:
1The Lord is giving you the land, and soon you will conquer it, settle down, 2 and plant crops. And when you begin harvesting each of your crops, the very first things you pick must be put in a basket. Take them to the place where the Lord your God chooses to be worshiped, 3and tell the priest, “Long ago the Lord our God promised our ancestors that he would give us this land. And today, I thank him for keeping his promise and giving me a share of the land.”
4The priest will take the basket and set it in front of the Lord's altar. 5Then, standing there in front of the place of worship, you must pray:
My ancestor was homeless,
an Aramean who went to live
in Egypt.
There were only a few
in his family then,
but they became great
and powerful,
a nation of many people.
6The Egyptians were cruel
and had no pity on us.
They mistreated our people
and forced us into slavery.
7We called out for help
to you, the Lord God
of our ancestors.
You heard our cries;
you knew we were in trouble
and abused.
8Then you terrified the Egyptians
with your mighty miracles
and rescued us from Egypt.
9You brought us here
and gave us this land
rich with milk and honey.
10Now, Lord, I bring to you
the best of the crops
that you have given me.
After you say these things, place the basket in front of the Lord's altar and bow down to worship him.
11Then you and your family must celebrate by eating a meal at the place of worship to thank the Lord your God for giving you such a good harvest. And remember to invite the Levites and the foreigners who live in your town.
Ten Percent of the Harvest
Moses said to Israel:
12 Every year you are to give ten percent of your harvest to the Lord. But every third year, this ten percent must be given to the poor who live in your town, including Levites, foreigners, orphans, and widows. That way, they will have enough to eat. 13Then you must pray:
Our Lord and our God, you have said that ten percent of my harvest is sacred. I have obeyed your command and given this to the poor, including the Levites, foreigners, orphans, and widows.
14I have not eaten any of this sacred food while I was in mourning; in fact, I never touched it when I was unclean. And none of it has been offered as a sacrifice to the spirits of the dead. I have done everything exactly as you commanded.
15Our Lord, look down from your temple in heaven and bless us and our land. You promised our ancestors that you would give us this land rich with milk and honey, and you have kept your promise.
The Lord Is Your God, and You Are His People
Moses said to Israel:
16Today the Lord your God has commanded you to obey these laws and teachings with all your heart and soul.
17In response, you have agreed that the Lord will be your God, that you will obey all his laws and teachings, and that you will listen when he speaks to you.
18 Since you have agreed to obey the Lord, he has agreed that you will be his people and that you will belong to him, just as he promised. 19The Lord created all nations, but he will make you more famous than any of them, and you will receive more praise and honor. You will belong only to the Lord your God, just as he promised.
translation_text:
Tikpaajin tipeekaal nì tisaalaatiil bɔti
1Ni làá kɔ́ kitiŋ kin ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá dūú tīī-ni ní nīn kíǹ ki yèe poon. Ni yaa láa ká ŋkakaamɔnti ki kāl̀ee, 2báà ŋma ń dāá lēē tikpaajin tin kɔkɔ u kùn̄ kitiŋ gbantinee tipeekaal kí ŋá kukabikun, kí yòon̄ kí cùnnì mpaan ŋun pu ti-Dindaan lēē kí nīn bí ní nīn jáaḿ-uee. 3Ni yaa bàn̄ee ní báà ŋma ń tùkù usaraaŋakpil un bí ŋyunti gbanti niinee yii: «M lì díǹ ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu nimbiin yii m bāań kitiŋ kin poon u nìn pōoǹ ti-naanjab yii u làá dūú tīī-tee.» 4Ní usaraaŋakpil ń fōō kukabikuee u-ŋaan kí dūú síiń ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu saraafaŋŋu caŋin.
5Niinee ní udaan ń lì ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nimbiin yii:
«M-naanja nìn sá uaranja ní ki nìn tú ki yìiǹ, ní ki dāa yíkìi sīntì Eejipiti tiŋkin ki kāl̀ niin kunicaŋu. Bin nìn táá-uee kaa nìn náaǹ, ama boonee bi dāa dūu kpántì ditimbuŋkpaandi. Bi nìn cáá mpɔn ki wīikí mun. 6Ama Eejipiti yab nìn wɔ́b́-ti ki sāaǹ-ti, ní ki nìn yāntì ti túń atuun ŋin pɔ̄ɔ̄yee. 7Niinee ní ti kúuǹ ki yíiń ti-Dindaan, ti-naanjab Nimbɔtiu ní u gbìl̄ ti-neen pu, ki ká ti-falaau nì ti-gìńdi nì bi nín wɔ́b́-ti puee. 8Ti-Dindaan nìn túń atuŋkpaan nì mpɔŋkpaan tuuŋŋi nì atuun ŋin kɔ̄ntí tifaandee 9ki cáań-ti doo, ní ki dū kitiŋ kin pu ní nnaabiim nì tisiil dɔ̄ ki còol̀ nee ki tīī-ti. 10Kɔŋkɔnnee, m-Dindaan, m cáań-si tikpaajin tipeekaal tin m cáń kitiŋ kin ní a tīī-mee pu.»
U yaa lī míǹ ki dóòyee ní ú dū kukabikuee kí síiń ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nimbiin ní kí gbàan̄ kí jāam̀-u. 11Míǹ boonee, ni nì Leefii yab nì binicambi bin kóò ni-puee ń dū tin kɔkɔ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu tīī ni nì ni-dicaŋŋee kí jī kí fàal̀.
Dibintataatiil poon tin bi lèekēe
12Dibintataatiil poonee, an dàkà yii tisaalaatiil bindi poonee, ni yaa láa lēē ni-kpaajinti kɔkɔ pu tisaalaatiil ki síiǹee, ní dāá dū-tì kí tīī Leefii yab nì binicambi bin kóò ni-puee nì ataŋkpiibil nì bikpiipoobi, án nín làá ŋá pu laakin ni kóòyee, bí ká kí jī kí díkée. 13Niinee ní ní tùkù ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu yii: «Ti nyántì ti-kpaajinti dijandi din bí circiree ti-dumpui ki dū-dì ki tīī Leefii yab nì binicambi nì ataŋkpiibil nì bikpiipoobi kii a nín kpáafì-ti yii tí ŋá puee. Taa fātì ti-boon ki tīī a-marab, kaa tí súntì bi-kansikin báà ubɔ mun pu. 14Taa kāl̀ dikpool ki dū tisaalaatiil jandi ki jíń, kaa tí lēē-tì ŋyunti ŋun ní ti bí tijɔkɔndinee, kaa lēē mun ki ŋá saraa ki tīī utaŋkpiil ubɔ. Ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu, ti ŋá a nín kpáafì-ti yii tí ŋá puee deedee. 15Míǹ puee gbóonní doooo yilpu laakin a kóòyee, kí bìin̄ a-niboolii Isirayeel yab nì kitiŋ kin ní a tīī-tee pu, kii a nín nìn pōoǹ ti-naanjab puee. Kitiŋ gbanti puee, nnaabiim nì tisiil di còol̀.»
Isirayeel yab sá ti-Dindaan nibul
16Ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu kpáafì-ni díǹ yii ní nīn ŋúb́ abɔkpaa nì akoobil nee. Ní pɔ́ɔm̀maan ni-ba kí ŋá kii ŋi nín bí yii ní ŋá puee nì ni-pɔbil kɔkɔ nì ni-naŋki kɔkɔ. 17Ni lī díǹ yii ti-Dindaan sá ni-Nimbɔtiu ní ni làá nīn ŋáań u nín là puee, kí nīn ŋúb́ u-bɔkpaaŋi nì u-marab nì u-koobiliŋ ní kí nīn tɔ́-u. 18Ní ti-Dindaan mun pōoǹ-ni ki lī díǹ yii ni sá u-nibul, binib bin u làá nīn yíì u-gaajawammɔntiitee kii u nín pōoǹ puee. Ní nīn ŋúb́ u-marab kɔkɔ. 19Ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá yòon̄-ni yilpu, kí yàntī ní nīn jítiǹ atimbun ŋin kɔkɔ u náańee, kí tīī-ni tinyool, kí yàntī ní nyā diyindi kí jītíǹ ŋi-kɔkɔ. Di sá yii u là ní nīn sá u-circir nibul kii u nín lī puee ní.

english_text:
Build an Altar on Mount Ebal
1Moses stood together with the leaders and told the people of Israel:
Obey all the laws and teachings that I am giving you today. 2-4 Soon you will enter the land that the Lord your God is giving to you. He is the God your ancestors worshiped, and he has promised that this land is rich with milk and honey.
After you cross the Jordan River, go to Mount Ebal. Set up large slabs of stone, then cover them with white plaster and write on them a copy of these laws.
5 At this same place, build an altar for offering sacrifices to the Lord your God. But don't use stones that have been cut with iron tools. 6Look for stones that can be used without being cut. Then offer sacrifices to please the Lord, burning them completely on the altar. 7Next, offer sacrifices to ask the Lord's blessing, and serve the meat at a sacred meal where you will celebrate in honor of the Lord.
8Don't forget to write out a copy of these laws on the stone slabs that you are going to set up. Make sure that the writing is easy to read.
Curses on Those Who Disobey
9Moses stood together with the priests and said, “Israel, be quiet and listen to me! Today you have become the people of the Lord your God. 10So you must obey his laws and teachings that I am giving you.”
11That same day, Moses gave them the following instructions:
12-13 After you cross the Jordan River, you will go to Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal. The tribes of Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Ephraim, Manasseh, and Benjamin will go up on Mount Gerizim, where they will bless the people of Israel. The tribes of Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali will go up on Mount Ebal where they will agree to the curses.
14-26 The people of the Levi tribe will speak each curse in a loud voice, then the rest of the people will agree to that curse by saying, “Amen!” Here are the curses:
We ask the Lord to put a curse on anyone who makes an idol or worships idols, even secretly. The Lord is disgusted with idols.
We ask the Lord to put a curse on all who do not show respect for their father and mother.
We ask the Lord to put a curse on anyone who moves the rocks that mark property lines.
We ask the Lord to put a curse on anyone who tells blind people to go the wrong way.
We ask the Lord to put a curse on anyone who keeps the poor from getting justice, whether these poor are foreigners, widows, or orphans.
We ask the Lord to put a curse on any man who sleeps with his father's wife; that man has shown no respect for his father's marriage.
We ask the Lord to put a curse on anyone who has sex with an animal.
We ask the Lord to put a curse on any man who sleeps with his sister or his half sister or his mother-in-law.
We ask the Lord to put a curse on anyone who commits murder, even when there are no witnesses to the crime.
We ask the Lord to put a curse on anyone who accepts money to murder an innocent victim.
We ask the Lord to put a curse on anyone who refuses to obey his laws.
And so, to each of these curses, the people will answer, “Amen!”
translation_text:
ISIRAYEEL YAB BÍI PÀKÀ UNIMBƆTI POONDI
(27.1–28.68)
Ataŋkpee ŋin bi cóoǹ Eebaal jool puee
1Isirayeel tindaŋkpilib nìn kútì Mooyiisi pu ki tīī Isirayeel yab mara nee yii: «Nín̄ ŋúb́maan marab bin kɔkɔ m tīī-ni díǹ nee. 2Ni yaa láa dūtì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ki kɔ́ kitiŋ kin ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá dūú tīī-nee poonee, ní dāá nyàab̀ ataŋkpakpaan kí cóoń ní kí dū kaaluupiin kí pīil̀-ŋi. 3Ni yaa láa pée dūtì mbunee, ní dāá ŋmà marab nee ataŋkpee gbanti pu. Boonee ní ní dāá kɔ́ kitiŋ kin ní ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu dūu tīī-nee poon. Kitiŋ kin ní ti-Dindaan ni-naanjab Nimbɔtiu làá dūú tīī-ni kii u nín nìn pōoǹ-ni puee poonee, nnaabiim nì tisiil di còol̀. 4Ni yaa láa dūtì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ki dóòyee, ní dāá dū ataŋkpee gbanti kí cóoń Eebaal jool pu kii m nín kpáafì-ni díǹ yii ní ŋá puee, ní kí dāá dū kaaluupiin kí pīil̀-ŋi. 5Míǹ boonee ní dū ataŋkpee ŋin baa dū kukúluu ki kpítèe kí mā ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nsaraafan niin. 6Ni nín pée yōoǹ ataŋkpee ŋi bí pu amɔnee, ní dūú mā ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nsaraafan, ní kí ŋá ŋu-pu saraawɔkaa kí tīī ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu. 7Ní dāá ŋá mpèé saraau mun, ní kí jī kí fàal̀ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nimbiin niin. 8Ataŋkpee ŋin ní ni cóoǹee puee, ní dāá ŋmà marab nee an nīn wāĺ tiŋan.»
9Míǹ boonee ní Mooyiisi nì Leefii yab bisaraaŋaliibee bí Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ yii: «Isirayeel yab, ŋmīĺmaan kí pīlifì. Díǹ nee ni kpántì ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nibul. 10Nín̄ tɔ́maan ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu, kí ŋá kii u-marab nì u-bɔkpaaŋi ŋin m tīī-ni díǹ nee nín bí yii ní ŋá puee.» 11Ŋwiin gbanti mbaanti ní Mooyiisi tīī Isirayeel yab mara nee, yii: 12«Ni yaa láa dūtì Jɔɔdan buŋŋuee, Simeeyɔn nì Leefii nì Juuda nì Isakaar nì Jooseefi nì Beenjameen naakɔti ń dāá sīĺ Geerisiim jool pu kí mèè kí bìin̄ diniwul kɔkɔ pu. 13Ní Rubeen nì Gaadi nì Aseer nì Sabulɔn nì Daani nì Neefitalii naakɔti ń dāá sīĺ Eebaal jool pu kí tɔ̄ mbusu.»
Mbusub saalaa nì bili
14 Leefii yab ń téeń mpɔn kí sòoǹ nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ yii:
15«Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí unil un di kpítì diwaal àá ki dūntì tikúti ki máń diwaal kí nīn jáaḿ-dì dibalinee. Ti-Dindaan nimbil kaa là kí wāl̀ an wanti tin ní unil dū u-ŋalii ki máńee.» Ní samaa kɔkɔ ń kíí yii: <Ameeni!>
16«Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí unil un di kpēē u-baa nì u-na fámee.» Ní samaa kɔkɔ ń kíí yii: <Ameeni!>
17«Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí un di cúú ditaŋkpal din cɔ́ u nì u-juti kpaanyɔkɔ ki cóotì ki nìkēe.» Ní samaa kɔkɔ ń kíí yii: <Ameeni!>
18«Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí un di kaa dàkā ujɔfu nsammɔnti u tin wáŋkèe.» Ní samaa kɔkɔ ń kíí yii: <Ameeni!>
19<Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí un di kaa sòon̄ unicaan nì ditaŋkpiibil nì ukpiipu bɔti nì ibaamɔnee.> Ní samaa kɔkɔ ń kíí yii: <Ameeni!>
20<Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí un di dōoǹ nì u-baa nimpoobi kansikin ubɔee, di sá yii u nín ŋá mimmee, u kpēē u-baa dooŋu fám dee.> Ní samaa kɔkɔ ń kíí yii: <Ameeni!>
21<Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí un di dōoǹ nì kuwaŋkuluuee.> Ní samaa kɔkɔ ń kíí yii: <Ameeni!>
22<Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí un di dōoǹ nì u-niisal, pēē baa àá pēē nee.> Ní samaa kɔkɔ ń kíí yii: <Ameeni!>
23<Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí un di dōoǹ nì u-coo, an dàkà yii u-nimpuu nee.> Ní samaa kɔkɔ ń kíí yii: <Ameeni!>
24<Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí un di gbáń ki kūū u-juti dibalinee.> Ní samaa kɔkɔ ń kíí yii: <Ameeni!>
25<Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí un di kíí ki fōō tiba kí kpɔ̀ maanyiibee.> Ní samaa kɔkɔ ń kíí yii: <Ameeni!>
26<Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí un di kaa tɔ́ Unimbɔti marab nee, kaa ŋá bi nín bí yii ú ŋá puee.> Ní samaa kɔkɔ ń kíí yii: <Ameeni!>

english_text:
The Lord Will Bless You if You Obey
Moses said to Israel:
1-2 Today I am giving you the laws and teachings of the Lord your God. Always obey them, and the Lord will make Israel the most famous and important nation on earth, and he will bless you in many ways.
3The Lord will make your businesses and your farms successful.
4You will have many children. You will harvest large crops, and your herds of cattle and flocks of sheep and goats will produce many young.
5You will have plenty of bread to eat.
6The Lord will make you successful in your daily work.
7The Lord will help you defeat your enemies and make them scatter in all directions.
8The Lord your God is giving you the land, and he will make sure you are successful in everything you do. Your harvests will be so large that your storehouses will be full.
9If you follow and obey the Lord, he will make you his own special people, just as he promised. 10Then everyone on earth will know that you belong to the Lord, and they will be afraid of you.
11The Lord will give you a lot of children and make sure that your animals give birth to many young. The Lord promised your ancestors that this land would be yours, and he will make it produce large crops for you.
12The Lord will open the storehouses of the skies where he keeps the rain, and he will send rain on your land at just the right times. He will make you successful in everything you do. You will have plenty of money to lend to other nations, but you won't need to borrow any yourself.
13Obey the laws and teachings that I'm giving you today, and the Lord your God will make Israel a leader among the nations, and not a follower. Israel will be wealthy and powerful, not poor and weak. 14But you must not reject any of his laws and teachings or worship other gods.
The Lord Will Put Curses on You if You Disobey
(Leviticus 26.14-46)
Moses said:
15Israel, today I am giving you the laws and teachings of the Lord your God. And if you don't obey them all, he will put many curses on you.
16Your businesses and farms will fail.
17You won't have enough bread to eat.
18You'll have only a few children, your crops will be small, and your herds of cattle and flocks of sheep and goats won't produce many young.
19The Lord will make you fail in everything you do.
20No matter what you try to accomplish, the Lord will confuse you, and you will feel his anger. You won't last long, and you may even meet with disaster, all because you rejected the Lord.
21-23The Lord will send terrible diseases to attack you, and you will never be well again. You will suffer with burning fever and swelling and pain until you die somewhere in the land that you captured.
The Lord will make the sky overhead seem like a bronze roof that keeps out the rain, and the ground under your feet will become as hard as iron. Your crops will be scorched by the hot east wind or ruined by mildew. 24He will send dust and sandstorms instead of rain, and you will be wiped out.
25The Lord will let you be defeated by your enemies, and you will scatter in all directions. You will be a horrible sight for the other nations to see, 26and no one will disturb the birds and wild animals while they eat your dead bodies.
27The Lord will make you suffer with diseases that will cause oozing sores or crusty itchy patches on your skin or boils like the ones that are common in Egypt. And there will be no cure for you! 28You will become insane and go blind. The Lord will make you so confused, 29that even in bright sunshine you will have to feel your way around like a blind person, who cannot tell day from night. For the rest of your life, people will beat and rob you, and no one will be able to stop them.
30A man will be engaged to a woman, but before they can get married, she will be raped by enemy soldiers. Some of you will build houses, but never get to live in them. If you plant a vineyard, you won't be around long enough to enjoy the first harvest. 31Your cattle will be killed while you watch, but you won't get to eat any of the meat. Your donkeys and sheep will be stolen from you, and no one will be around to force your enemies to give them back. 32Your sons and daughters will be dragged off to a foreign country, while you stand there helpless. And even if you watch for them until you go blind, you will never see them again.
33You will work hard on your farms, but everything you harvest will be eaten by foreigners, who will mistreat you and abuse you for the rest of your life.
34What you see will be so horrible that you will go insane, 35and the Lord will punish you from head to toe with boils that never heal.
36The Lord will let you and your king be taken captive to a country that you and your ancestors have never even heard of, and there you will have to worship idols made of wood and stone. 37People of nearby countries will shudder when they see your terrible troubles, but they will still make fun of you.
38You will plant a lot of seed, but gather a small harvest, because locusts will eat your crops. 39You will plant vineyards and work hard at taking care of them, but you won't gather any grapes, much less get any wine, because the vines themselves will be eaten by worms. 40Even if your olive trees grow everywhere in your country, the olives will fall off before they are ready, and there won't be enough olive oil for combing your hair.
41Even your children will be taken as prisoners of war.
42Locusts will eat your crops and strip your trees of leaves and fruit.
43Foreigners in your towns will become wealthy and powerful, while you become poor and powerless. 44You will be so short of money that you will have to borrow from those foreigners. They will be the leaders in the community, and you will be the followers.
More Curses for Disobedience
Moses said:
45Israel, if you don't obey the laws and teachings that the Lord your God is giving you, he will send these curses to chase, attack, and destroy you. 46Then everyone will look at you and your descendants and realize that the Lord has placed you under a curse.
47If the Lord makes you wealthy, but you don't joyfully worship and honor him, 48he will send enemies to attack you and make you their slaves. Then you will live in poverty with nothing to eat, drink, or wear, and your owners will work you to death.
49Foreigners who speak a strange language will be sent to attack you without warning, just like an eagle swooping down. 50They won't show any mercy, and they will have no respect for old people or pity for children. 51They will take your cattle, sheep, goats, grain, wine, and olive oil, then leave you to starve.
52All over the land that the Lord your God gave you, the enemy army will surround your towns. You may feel safe inside your town walls, but the enemy will tear them down, 53while you wait in horror. Finally, you will get so hungry that you will eat the sons and daughters that the Lord gave you. 54-55Because of hunger, a man who had been gentle and kind will eat his own children and refuse to share the meal with his brother or wife or with his other children. 56-57 A woman may have grown up in such luxury that she never had to put a foot on the ground. But times will be so bad that she will secretly eat both her newborn baby and the afterbirth, without sharing any with her husband or her other children.
Disobedience Brings Destruction
Moses said to Israel:
58You must obey everything in The Book of God's Law. Because if you don't respect the Lord, 59he will punish you and your descendants with incurable diseases, 60like those you were so afraid of in Egypt. 61Remember! If the Lord decides to destroy your nation, he can use any disease or disaster, not just the ones written in The Book of God's Law.
62There are as many of you now as the stars in the sky, but if you disobey the Lord your God, only a few of you will be left. 63The Lord is happy to make you successful and to help your nation grow while you conquer the land. But if you disobey him, he will be just as happy to pull you up by your roots.
64Those of you that survive will be scattered to every nation on earth, and you will have to worship stone and wood idols that never helped you or your ancestors. 65You will be restless—always longing for home, but never able to return. 66You will live in constant fear of death. 67Each morning you will wake up to such terrible sights that you will say, “I wish it were night!” But at night you will be terrified and say, “I wish it were day!”
68I told you never to go back to Egypt. But now the Lord himself will load you on ships and send you back. Then you will even try to sell yourselves as slaves, but no one will be interested.
translation_text:
Nnaam poondi
1Ni yaa tɔ́ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu tiŋman pu ní ki yaa ŋá kii marab bin kɔkɔ m tīī-ni díǹ nee nín bí yii ní ŋá puee, ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá yòon̄-ni yilpu ní jītíǹ atimbun ŋin kɔkɔ bí kitiŋ puee. 2Ni yaa tɔ́ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiuee, u nín làá bìin̄ ni-pu puee sɔ̀.
3U làá bìin̄ ni-pu ntimun nì tisatin. 4U làá bìin̄ ni-maaliŋu pu ní bùtī, kí bìin̄ ni-kpaajinti pu, ní kí yàntī ni-naai nì ni-piii nì ni-ŋoobui ń bùtī. 5U làá bìin̄ ni-pu kí gbéeǹ ni-kabiti tikpaajin ní ki gbéeǹ ni-yugutiliŋ ŋyim. 6U làá bìin̄ ni-nyātam nì ni-kɔ́tam pu.
7Ti-Dindaan làá yàntī ní já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ ni-nannanliibi bin làá yīkì kí jáǹ-nee. Bi yaa láa dī nsambaanti pu ki dɔ́mińee, bi dāa dì isan iluli pu ní kí kpì. 8Ti-Dindaan làá bìin̄ ni-pu ni-cakalaabi ń gbí tijin ní kí bìin̄ tin kamaa ní làá ŋée pu. Ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá bìin̄ ni-pu kitiŋ kin u làá tīī-nee poon.
9Ni yaa ŋúb́ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu marab, ki yaa ŋáań u nín là puee, u làá dū-ni kí kpántí u-circir nibul kii u nín pōoǹ-ni puee. 10Ní kitiŋ pu nibuliŋ kɔkɔ ń dāa nīn kíǹ ki yíì-ni yii ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti yab, ní kí dāá fàŋkì-ni. 11Ti-Dindaan làá yàntī ní nīn bí digbíl poon, ní màal̀ kí bùtī, ni-waŋkuti mun ń bùtī, ní ni-kpaajinti ń lòoǹ tiŋan kitiŋ kin ti-Dindaan pōoǹ ni-naanjab yii u làá dūú tīī-nee poon. 12Ti-Dindaan làá pìitī kutagbɔŋu, laakin u kpáafì nnyim tiŋan puee, kí yàntī utaa ń nì ni-timmu pu ŋyunti ŋun an máaǹee, ní kí bìin̄ ni-tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ pu. Atimbun tikpil dāa dòoń ni-cee, ní ní pìnnì-bi tin ni cááyee, ama nimbee, naa dāa cá ditimbundi diba cee kí pìnnì tiba. 13Ni yaa ŋúb́ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu marab bin ní m tīī-ni díǹ nee ní ki yaa ŋáań kii bi nín bí yii ní ŋá puee, ni làá nīn sá ditimbundi din làá nīn līī nyɔkɔpuee ní, ni kpá kí lūŋkì boon. Ni làá nīn pée yíkí yilpu ŋma ní, ni kpá kí sìntī taapu. 14Ní taa kàkatī kí cù ŋgiil pú, àá ŋgan pú kí wàatī marab bin m tīī-ni díǹ nee kí dū ni-ba kí nákáǹ awaa kí nīn tòotī-ŋi.
Nnaabu
15Ama ni yaa kaa tɔ́ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu, ki yaa kaa ŋúb́ u-marab nì u-bɔkpaaŋi ŋin kɔkɔ m tīī-ni díǹ nee, mbusu un làá jēetí ni-puee sɔ̀.
16Ti-Dindaan làá tɔ̄-ni mbusu ntimun nì tisatin. 17U làá tɔ̄-ni mbusu ni-kabiti ń lóó tikpaajin ní ni-yugutiliŋ ń lóó ŋyim. 18Ti-Dindaan làá tɔ̄ ni-maaliŋu nì ni-kpaatanti nì ni-naai nì ni-piii nì ni-ŋoobui mbusu. 19U làá tɔ̄ ni-nyātam nì ni-kɔ́tam mbusu.
20Ti-Dindaan làá yàntī mbusu nì fìkil fikil nì sámbu ń jēetí tin kamaa ni làá nīn ŋáańee pu kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋun ní ni làá céetí múbuee. Naa làá pée sūŋkì ní kí nàan̄, di sá yii ni dū-mi ki fá ki kíǹ ki bíi ŋáań atuŋkpiti. 21Ti-Dindaan làá dū iween kí tɔ̄ ni-pu ní í kpɔ̀ kí céetí-ni kitiŋ kin ni làá kɔ́ nee poon. 22U làá dū didúntil nì nnaanyeem nì anal nì diwumpildi kpaŋkpam weeŋyi kí tɔ̄ ni-pu, ní kí yàntī ŋweel ń sīĺ ní ni kpaajinti ń kpā, àá tí sūū. Agìń gbanti kɔkɔ làá jēetí ni-pu kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋun ní ni làá kpú kí céetée. 23Kutaa kun dàn̄ ni-yil pu nee làá kpántí kii tasee, ní kitiŋ kin dɔ̄ ni-taaŋi taapu nee mun ń pɔ̄ɔkì káŋkaŋ kii tikútee. 24An nín bàà sá ti-Dindaan ń yàntī utaa ń nì ni-tiŋki puee, dikpɔŋkpɔndi nì dibul ní u làá yàntī an nyēeń yilpu ki sìtīń ni-pu kí kpɔ̀ kí céetí-ni. 25Ti-Dindaan làá yàntī ni-nannanliibi ń já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ-ni. Ni làá dī nsambaanti pu kí cù kí já nì bi, ama ní kí dī isan iluli pu kí sāǹ-bi. Tin làá bàn̄ ni-puee làá cúú kitiŋ pu beeŋi kɔkɔ tifaandi. 26Ni-nikpiliŋ làá kpántí tijin ní kí tīī inoon in ŋàaǹ kutaa puee nì tiwaŋkuti tin bí kitiŋ puee, ubɔ dāa kpá kí jà-tì.
27Ti-Dindaan làá dū ibunsoon in u nìn tɔ́ Eejipiti yabee nì ncaapa nì digbàndi nì iwàlfi kí tɔ̄ ni-pu. Ni dāa kpá kí ká dicáaǹdi. 28Ti-Dindaan làá dū kuwaatiiu nì ijɔfi nì diyilabitil kí tɔ̄ ni-pu. 29Ni dāa táfí an kɔkɔ kuwiŋkaŋu pu kii ujɔfu nín bí dibɔmbɔndin ki táfí puee ní. Tin kamaa ni yaa bíi ŋáańee, án kaa làá bútí-ni. Bi làá nīn wɔ́b̀-ni baabadal ní kí fūkul̀-ni. Báà ubɔ mun dāa kpá kí fīī-ni.
30Ni làá nīn cáá bɔɔn ki bàà máká kí cáá-u ní ubɔ fám ń cáá-u. Ni yaa máń kudii, naa làá kɔ́-kù. Ni yaa kùn̄ bufiinyikpaa, naa làá ká bu-biliŋ kí kìtī. 31Ni-nimbilaaliyin ní bi làá cúú ni-naai kí làntì, ama naa làá ká i-nanti kí dáká. Ni dāa sí ki kpèé ní bí yɔ̀ ni-mammu, ama baa làá fàtīí gíiǹní-mu kí tīī-ni. Bi dāa dù ni-piii nì ni-ŋoobui kí tīī ni-nannanliibi, ama ubɔ kaa dāa bí kí jòó-ni. 32Ditimbundi diba yab làá cūtì ni-jipɔmbi nì ni-bisalib kuyuŋu, ní ní kpèè bi-saŋŋu pú kí gīī, ama kaa dāa ŋūǹ kí ŋá tiba nì tiba. 33Dinibul din naa nyée di dāa yì ni-timmu jinti nì ni-tuntuŋku paatii kɔkɔ kí jī. Nimbee, bi dāa pée sàantí-ni ní, ki jīǹ ni-pu. 34Tibɔti tin làá nīn jītí ni kāntée làá yàntī ní wáatí.
35Ti-Dindaan làá dū ibunsoon in baa dāa ŋūǹ kí cáaǹee kí tɔ̄ ni-tabiŋyiliŋ nì ni-tapaŋŋi ní an nyàtī kí gbí ni-wunti kɔkɔ pu kí yòon̄ ni-taaŋi poon kí cáá sāā ni-yiliŋ kansikin.
36Ti-Dindaan làá cáá ni nì ni-bɔtiu un ni kāaǹee kí cùnnì ditimbundi din ní nimbi nì ni-naanjab kaa nìn nyée poon. Niin ní ni dāa kíǹ ki tòotī awaa ŋin sá ataŋkpee nì idɔee. 37Tin làá jītí ni-puee làá ŋá atimbun ŋin poon ní ti-Dindaan làá cáá-ni kí cùnnèe nib bitii, ní bi dāa kíǹ ki sòoǹ ni-bɔti ki bèel̄-ni.
38Ni làá kpɔ̀ tisati kí bɔ̄l̀ tikpil tikpil, ama ní kí cā fiii di sá yii inaakitoon làá kēefì kɔkɔ. 39Ni làá kpɔ̀ afiinyikpaan kí cóoń fiinyi sufii kí bɔ́ntí-i an nín máaǹ puee, ama naa dāa kāntí fiinyi gbanti subil báà diba kí kìtī ki dāa nín nyàab̀ ŋi-daam kí nyɔ̀. Di sá yii akoosibil di dāa dù kɔkɔ kí ŋmɔ́. 40Ni làá nīn cáá ɔliifi sufii ni-tiŋki kɔkɔ poon, ama naa dāa kāntí i-kpam kí ŋmìtī, di sá yii ni-ɔliifi sufii yaa láa lòon̄ee, abil kaa dāa bīī ní kí gbátí kɔkɔ. 41Ni làá màal̀ mbininjabiyaamu nì nnimpubiyaamu, ama muaa làá kàl̄ ni-cee, di sá yii bi dāa cútí-mu kí cùnnì kuyuŋu ní. 42Inaakitoon dāa kpátí kí bìin̄ ni-sufii nì ni-kpaajinti pu ní kí kēefì kí céetí an kɔkɔ múb.
43Unicaan un kóò ni-puee làá nīn jítiǹ-ni kpataaa, ní ki tɔ́kɔ́ ni-pu. Ama nimbee, ni dāa mɔ̀tīi sìntī taapu ní ki cá. 44Úǹ di dāa cáá kí pìnnì-ni, ama nimbee, naa dāa cáá tiba kí pìnnì-u. U dāa sá usanliiti ní nimbi sá biboompaanliibi.
45Mbusub nee kɔkɔ làá jēetí ni-pu ní kí nīn dī-ni míǹ kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋun ní ni làá kpú kí céetée. Di sá yii naa tɔ́ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu, ní kaa tí ŋúb́ u-marab nì u-bɔkpaaŋi ŋin u tīī-nee mun. 46Mbusub gbanti làá nīn sá kudaaŋŋu nì atulim ní ki tīī nimbi nì ni-naantiibi ki nín cáa cá jaanjaan.
47Ni yaa kaa jáam̀ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nì mmɔn nì dipɔɔpindin ŋyunti ŋun ní ni bí digbilinee, 48ni làá kpántí ni-nannanliibi bin ti-Dindaan dāa cāabìń kí tɔ̄ ni-puee yumbui ní. Ŋkùm nì nnyinnyoo làá cúú-ni ní ní nīn kíǹ ki gàaǹ kaa ti pée cáá báà tiba. Ti-Dindaan làá dū tikúti kí bóob́ kí páań ni-gbigbipati pu kii bi nín kpàl̀ inaa in kù tikpaalee puee, kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋun ní ni làá kpú kí céetí múbuee. 49Ti-Dindaan làá cáań ditimbundi din nyánní ndandati kitiŋ gbeennyɔkɔee, ditimbundi din sooŋyi naa gbìl̀ee kí tɔ̄ ni-pu kii ukaabu nín tòó puee. 50An dāa sá ditimbundi din nib cáá inimbinaakulimee ní. Baa dāa kpèé utikpil nimbiinaaa, kaa dāa sūǹ binipɔmbi mun saai. 51Bi dāa yòontí ni-waŋkuti kɔkɔ nì ni-kpaajinti kɔkɔ kí jī, ní ní dāá kpú ŋkùm. Baa dāa kīntí-ni dibileebil àá ndamam àá ŋkpam àá ni-naai nì ni-ŋoobui biyaamu gba, ní ní dāá kpú kí céetí. 52Bi làá lùkù kí gíb́ ni-timmu kɔkɔ kí jáǹ-ni kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋun ní ni-timmu mun ni máń aguŋfɔkɔ ki tú ki máká mu-pu yii ubɔ kaa ŋūǹ kí kɔ́ mu-nee ń lítí. Bi dāa lùkù kí gíb́ ntimu mun kɔkɔ bí kitiŋ kin ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu tīī-nee poon ní kí jáǹ-ni. 53Bi yaa láa lùkū ki gíb́ ni-timmu míǹ kí já kí fōō-muee, ni làá kɔ́ falaakpaŋkpaan poon, áli gba ni-poon biyaamu di làá kpántí ni-jinti. Tiŋman, ni làá ŋmɔ́ ni-jipɔmbi nì ni-bisalib bin ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu tīī-nee nanti. 54Unil un dāa mɔ̄ ki gbìl̀ u-juti falaau ni-kansikinee kaa dāa gíti là ki wāl̀ úǹ u-ba maan àá u-naal àá u-nimpuu un u néeńee àá u-biyaamu mun kíǹ-uee gba. 55Di sá yii waa dāa là u nì bi-kansikin ubɔ ń yàkatī u-biyaamu nanti kí ŋmɔ́, kun puee mbiyaamuee di dāa kíǹ ki sá u-jikaati ŋyunti ŋun ní ni-nannanliibi yaa láa lùkū ki gíb́ ni-timmu kí jáǹ-nee. Ni-nannanliibee làá yàntī ni-nimbiliŋ ń mántí tikpil. 56Ni-kansikin unimpu un là u-ba tikpil kaa pée là tiba ń gbēē-u, kaa màkantí gba kí dū u-taal poon kí taa kitiŋee dāa dàab̀ u-cal un u néeńee nì úǹ u-ba jipɔmbi nì u-bisalib ní. 57Di sá yii u dāa là kí ŋmɔ́ kibipɔŋ kin u dáá màl̄ee nì dibɔl dibalin u-baba, kun puee ni-nannanliibi nín lùkū ki gíb́ ni-timmu kɔkɔ pu kí jáǹ-nee làá kɔ́ǹ-ni dinimbinaamandin.
58Ni yaa kaa ŋúb́ marab bin bi ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu nee poon, kí nīn ŋáań bi nín bí yii ní ŋá puee, kaa fāŋkì diyindi din cáá tinyool nì mpɔnee, an dàkà yii <Ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu>, 59ti-Dindaan làá dū maamaaci weeŋyi nì tiweeŋkpiil nì iween in pɔ̄ɔ̄ kaa pée ŋān̄ee kí tɔ̄ nimbi nì ni-naantiibi pu. 60U làá cáań Eejipiti weeŋyi in ni fàŋkí kaa là ni-nimbil ń kée kɔkɔ kí tɔ̄ ni-pu ní í cúú-ni. 61Ti-Dindaan làá dū iween in kɔkɔ baa ŋmàn̄ marab gbɔŋku nee poonee gba kí tɔ̄ ni-pu ní ní kpú kí céetí. 62Nimbi bin nìn wīikí kii iŋmalbijaa in bí kutaa puee dāa kīntí ní fiii, di sá yii naa tɔ́ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu. 63Kii an nín nìn mɔ́ɔkiǹ ti-Dindaan u ŋá-ni tiŋan ki yāntì ni būtì ki bí mmɔnni puee, míǹ mbaantiim ní án làá tí fàtīí mɔ̄ɔkiǹ-u ú nàan̄-ni kí kúntí-ni. U làá jà-ni kí nyāntí kitiŋ kin ni làá kɔ́ kí fōō kí nīn kíǹ ki yì nee poon. 64Ti-Dindaan làá yàntī ní yàl̄ kí kɔ́ atimbun kɔkɔn, kí yòon̄ kitiŋ kpaanyɔkɔ kiba kí cáá sāā kin kíǹee. Ni làá tòotī awaa ŋin sá idɔ nì ataŋkpee nimbi nì ni-naanjab kaa pée nyí ki kée. 65Ni dāa kpá kí ká diŋuŋfil atimbun gbanti poon. Naa dāa ŋūǹ kí ká mpaan fiii yéè kí síiń ni-taaŋi. Niinee ní ti-Dindaan ń dāá yàntī ní fáá diniindi ní ni-nimbiliŋ ń mántí ní ni-wunti ń yɔ̀tī. 66Naa dāa pée gíti nyí tin poon ni bée. Ni dāa bí dinyoondin ní ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu. Ni dāa pée kíǹ ki bí yii ni nín bée ní. 67Tibɔti tin kɔkɔ làá nīn jītí ni kāntée làá bīil̀ ni-pɔbiliŋ tikpil. Kutaafaauee ní ní lì yii: «Ba dal ní ku làá jóotí dee!> ní ku yaa tí jóotèe ní ní lì yii: <Ba dal ní ku wúntí dee!> 68Ti-Dindaan làá yàntī ní kɔ́ meelab kí fàtīí gítí Eejipiti tiŋkin, nì min kɔkɔ u nìn lī yii: <Ni-taal gíti kpá kí tāā kitiŋ gbantinee>. Ni yaa láa bàn̄ niinee, ni dāa nyàab̀ kí dū ni-ba kí nyāfiǹ ni-nannanliibi kí bàà kpántí bi-yumbui, ama naa dāa kāntí udal.»
MOOYIISI BƆJOOLKAATI
(28.69–30.20)
69 Dipoondi din ti-Dindaan nìn yāntì Mooyiisi tīī Isirayeel yab Moowaab tiŋkin ki kútì din u nìn pōoǹ-bi Ooreeb jool puee bɔti dee.

english_text:
The Agreement in Moab
1So Moses finished telling the Israelites what they had to do in order to keep the agreement the Lord was making with them in Moab, which was in addition to the one the Lord had made with them at Mount Sinai.
The Third Speech: Israel Must Keep Its Agreement with the Lord
The Lord Is Your God
2-3Moses called the nation of Israel together and told them:
When you were in Egypt, you saw the Lord perform great miracles that caused trouble for the king, his officials, and everyone else in the country. 4-6He has even told you, “For 40 years I, the Lord, led you through the desert, but your clothes and your sandals didn't wear out, and I gave you special food. I did these things so you would realize that I am your God.”
But the Lord must give you a change of heart before you truly understand what you have seen and heard.
7 When we first camped here, King Sihon of Heshbon and King Og of Bashan attacked, but we defeated them. 8 Then we captured their land and divided it among the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh.
Keep the Agreement
Moses said:
9Israel, the Lord has made an agreement with you, and if you keep your part, you will be successful in everything you do. 10-12Today everyone in our nation is standing here in the Lord's presence, including leaders and officials, parents and children, and even those foreigners who cut wood and carry water for us. We are at this place of worship to promise that we will keep our part of the agreement with the Lord our God.
13-15In this agreement, the Lord promised that you would be his people and that he would be your God. He first made this promise to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and today the Lord is making this same promise to you. But it isn't just for you; it is also for your descendants.
16-17When we lived in Egypt, you saw the Egyptians worship disgusting idols of wood, stone, silver, and gold. Then as we traveled through other nations, you saw those people worship other disgusting idols. 18 So make sure that everyone in your tribe remains faithful to the Lord and never starts worshiping gods of other nations.
If even one of you worships idols, you will be like the root of a plant that produces bitter, poisonous fruit. 19You may be an Israelite and know all about the Lord's agreement with us, but he won't bless you if you rebel against him. You may think you can get away with it, but you will cause the rest of Israel to be punished along with you. 20-21The Lord will be furious, and instead of forgiving you, he will separate you from the other tribes. Then he will destroy you, by piling on you all the curses in The Book of God's Law, and you will be forgotten forever.
22The Lord will strike your country with diseases and disasters. Your descendants and foreigners from distant countries will see that your land 23 has become a scorching desert of salt and sulfur, where nothing is planted, nothing sprouts, and nothing grows. It will be as lifeless as the land around the cities of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, after the Lord became angry and destroyed them.
24People from other nations will ask, “Why did the Lord destroy this country? Why was he so furious?”
25And they will be given this answer:
Our ancestors worshiped the Lord, but after he brought them out of Egypt and made an agreement with them, they rejected the agreement 26and decided to worship gods that had never helped them. The Lord had forbidden Israel to worship these gods, 27-28and so he became furious and punished the land with all the curses in The Book of God's Law. Then he pulled up Israel by the roots and tossed them into a foreign country, where they still are today.
29The Lord our God hasn't explained the present or the future, but he has commanded us to obey the laws he gave to us and our descendants.
translation_text:
Tin Unimbɔti ŋá ki tīī Isirayeel yabee
1Mooyiisi nìn kóoǹ Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ ki kpáfì ní ki bí-bi yii:
«Nimbi ni-ba nimbil ká tin ní ti-Dindaan ŋá Faaroo nì u-tɔntɔnliibi nì u-tiŋki Eejipitee kɔkɔ. 2Nimbi ni-ba nimbil tí ká icɔŋkikpaan in poon u nìn kɔ́ǹ-bee nì maamaacikpaambi bin u ŋá ki dàkā-bee. 3Ama kí dāá sāā díǹ nee, ti-Dindaan kaa tīī-ni nlandɔkɔ ní dàkafì kí béé, kaa tīī-ni animbil ní wāl̀, kaa tí tīī-ni atafal ní gbìl̄.»
4«M nín yāntì ni cōom̀ abin imuŋku ili kuteeu puee, ni-wampeeŋkaati kaa cátàaa, ni-naatakaŋ ŋin ni tákée mun kaa céetì. 5An kaa nìn sá kpɔnɔb ní ni ŋmɔ́, kaa ti sá ndamam àá ndaam min pɔ̄ɔ̄yee ní ni nyùn̄, ama an sá ní ŋmā kí béé yii man di sá ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu. 6Ŋyunti ŋun ni bāań kitiŋ kin pu ni bí neeyee, ní Asibɔn bɔtiu Siiwɔn nì Baasan bɔtiu Ɔɔgi nyáń kí jáǹ-ti, ama ní ti jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi. 7Ti nìn fōō bi-tiŋki ní ki dūu tīī Rubeen naakookun yab nì Gaadi naakookun yab nì Manasee naakookun yab dijandi, án nīn sá bi-kpaatanti. 8Nín̄ ŋúb́maan dipoondi nee koobiliŋ kí ŋá ŋi nín bí yii ní ŋá puee, ní án bútí-ni ni-tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ poon.»
Unimbɔti poondi bɔti páb́
9Isirayeel yab, díǹ nee, ni-kɔkɔ kpáfì ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nimbiin, ni nì ni-kpootiliibi nì ni-naakɔti kpilib nì ni-tindaŋkpilib nì ni-bɔsoonliibi, 10nì ni-biyaamu nì ni-nimpoobi nì binicambi bin kóò ni-pu ki cá-ni idɔ pú àá ki lúù-ni nnyimee. 11Ni làá kɔ́ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu poondin dee. Dipoondi gbanti ní u bíi pùtī ki pòontí-ni díǹ nee, 12kí dàkà yii ni sá u-nibul ní u mun sá ni-Nimbɔtiu kii u nín nìn pōoǹ-ni puee. Míǹ ní u nìn pūtì ki pōoǹ ni-naanjab Abraam nì Isaaki nì Jaakɔb mun. 13An kaa sá nimbi baba ní m bíi pùtī ki pòontí dipoondi nee, 14ama an sá ki kpáaǹ bin bí doo díǹ ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu nimbiinee nì bin mun kaa bí ti-kansikin díǹ nee ní.
15Nimbi ni-ba nyí ti nín kāl̀ Eejipiti tiŋkin tin jítèe, nì tin ti ká atimbun ŋin poon ti jítèe. 16Ni nìn ká bi nín nìn ŋáań ntimbiil tuuŋŋi puee nì bi-waaŋi ŋin bi nìn tòotēe. Bi-waaŋi gbanti nìn sá idɔ nì ataŋkpee nì animbil nì sindaariya ní. 17Bí taa ká ni-kansikin uninja àá unimpu àá kudicaŋu àá tinaakɔti tin bí doo díǹ nee kubɔ nib fātì bi-boon ki tīī ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu ki cūtìi bíi tòotī atimbun gbanti waaŋi. Ní nīn nyíǹ ni-ba ubɔ ń taa kpántí kii kisubiki kin cáá tiloolee. 18Ubɔ ń taa nyā ni-kansikin, ŋyunti ŋun ní u gbìl̄ dipoondi nyɔɔbuŋŋi ŋin bi sòon̄ ki pūtì nee, boonee kí gāā u-bindi kí lì yii: «Báà m yaa gbíntìi ŋáań min m lèe, m làá nīn pée bí ŋgbansɔŋfin». Yaa sá fám, unikpiti làá kpú kí kpáaǹ maanyiiba. 19Ti-Dindaan kaa dāa kíikí kí dūú pɔ̄ udaan, see ú dāá yàntī u-ŋuul ń lítí u-pu ní mbusub bin kɔkɔ bi ŋmàn̄ ki ŋá kugbɔŋu nee poonee ń jēetí u-pu. Ti-Dindaan làá kpìtī udaan yindi kitiŋ pu. 20Isirayeel naakɔti kɔkɔ poonee, ti-Dindaan làá gàntī udaan u-baba nì u-baba ní kí dū mbusub bin ŋmàn̄ ki kā dipoondi marab gbɔŋku nee poonee kí sìtī u-pu.
Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee, u làá ŋá míǹ
21Ni-biyaamu mun làá dāá páanní ni-boonee nì binicambi bin làá dāá nyānní ntimu mun dátèe poon làá dāá ká asaluu un gbáń kitiŋ gbantee nì iween in ti-Dindaan dūu tɔ́ ki-puee ní kí lì yii: 22«Ŋyaam nì farwata ŋmiŋu wùn̄ kitiŋ gbanti kɔkɔ. Baa ti ŋūǹ kí bɔ̄l̀ tiba ki-pu ní tiba nì tiba mun kaa ti ŋūǹ kí nyā ki-pu, ki kpáaǹ timool gba. Kì kpántì kii Soodoom nì Goomoora nì Adima nì Seebooyiim timmuee ní. Ti-Dindaan nìn fōō mbum tikpil ntimu gbanti pu ní ki nāaǹ-mu.» 23Niinee ní atimbun ŋin kɔkɔ kíǹee nib ń dāá bàlifì yii: «Ba pu ní ti-Dindaan nín ŋá kitiŋ nee míǹ dee? Ba pu ní u fōō mbum míǹ tikpil dee?» 24Ní bí dāá kíí-bi yii: «Kun pu tin bí nee bāań-bee di sá yii bi fātì bi-boon ki tīī dipoondi din ti-Dindaan, bi-baabi Nimbɔtiu nìn pūtì ki pōoǹ-bi ŋyunti ŋun ní u nìn nyántìń-bi Eejipiti tiŋkinee. 25Bi cūtìi bíi tòotī awaa ki gbàantí ŋi-taapu. Awaa gbantee, baa nìn nyí-ŋaaa, ti-Dindaan mun kaa nìn pú nsan bí nín tòotī-ŋi. 26Míǹ pu ní ti-Dindaan gíí kitiŋ gbanti nib pu diŋuul ní ki yāntì mbusub bin kɔkɔ bi ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu nee poonee jéetì bi-pu. 27Ti-Dindaan fōō mbum tikpil bi-pu ki gíí diŋuul ŋkpitim pu ní ki nyántì-bi bi-tiŋkin ki dū-bi ki tɔ́ kinicantiŋ kiban kii an nín bí min díǹ pu nee.»
28Tin tin bí dibalinee, ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu di yì, ama tin nyáń ki pá mpaampiin puee, timbi nì ti-naantiibi di yì kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaan. Tíǹ di sá yii tí nīn ŋúb́ marab nee bɔkpaaŋi kɔkɔ.

english_text:
The Lord Will Bring You Back
Moses said to Israel:
1 I have told you everything the Lord your God will do for you, and I've also told you the curses he will put on you if you reject him. He will scatter you in faraway countries, but when you realize that he is punishing you, 2return to him with all your heart and soul and start obeying the commands I have given to you today. 3-4Then he will stop punishing you and treat you with kindness. He may have scattered you to the farthest countries on earth, but he will bring you back 5to the land that had belonged to your ancestors and make you even more successful and powerful than they ever were.
6You and your descendants are stubborn, but the Lord will make you willing to obey him and love him with all your heart and soul, and you will enjoy a long life.
7Then the Lord your God will remove the curses from you and put them on those enemies who hate and attack you.
8You will again obey the laws and teachings of the Lord, 9and he will bless you with many children, large herds and flocks, and abundant crops. The Lord will be happy to do good things for you, just as he did for your ancestors. 10But you must decide once and for all to worship him with all your heart and soul and to obey everything in The Book of God's Law.
Choose Life, Not Death
Moses said to Israel:
11You know God's laws, and it isn't impossible to obey them. 12 His commands aren't in heaven, so you can't excuse yourselves by saying, “How can we obey the Lord's commands? They are in heaven, and no one can go up to get them, then bring them down and explain them to us.” 13And you can't say, “How can we obey the Lord's commands? They are across the sea, and someone must go across, then bring them back and explain them to us.” 14No, these commands are nearby and you know them by heart. All you have to do is obey!
15 Today I am giving you a choice. You can choose life and success or death and disaster. 16-18I am commanding you to be loyal to the Lord, to live the way he has told you, and to obey his laws and teachings. You are about to cross the Jordan River and take the land that he is giving you. If you obey him, you will live and become successful and powerful.
On the other hand, you might choose to disobey the Lord and reject him. So I'm warning you that if you bow down and worship other gods, you won't have long to live.
19Now I call the sky and the earth to be witnesses that I am offering you this choice. Will you choose for the Lord to make you prosperous and give you a long life? Or will he put you under a curse and kill you? Choose life! 20 Be completely faithful to the Lord your God, love him, and do whatever he tells you. The Lord is the only one who can give life, and he will let you live a long time in the land that he promised to your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
translation_text:
Ní fàtīí gítiń ti-Dindaan cee
1Dibiindi nì mbusub bɔti tin m dūu bíl̀ ni-nimbiin nee làá dāá ŋá míǹ. Ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu yaa láa yāntì ni yàl̄ ki búntì nnicantimunee, ní dāá dàkafì tibɔti gbanti pu tiŋan. 2Nimbi nì ni-biyaamu làá fàtīí gítiń ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu cee kí nīn kíǹ ki tɔ́-u nì ni-pɔbil kɔkɔ nì ni-naŋki kɔkɔ, kí nóó nì tin kɔkɔ m dūu kpáafì-ni díǹ nee. 3Ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá dāá dū ni-gìŋ́ŋi kí kpántí mmɔn. U làá dāá sɔ̄ ni-saai ní kí fàtīí kóoǹní-ni atimbun ŋin kɔkɔ poon ní u nìn yāntì ni yàl̄ ki búntèe kí gíiǹní. 4Báà ni yaa yàl̄ ki bínní kitiŋ gbeennyɔkɔ, ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá dāá cù niin kí kóoǹní ni-kɔkɔ kí kpāfì kí fàtīí gíiǹní-ni. 5U làá dāá fàtīí gíiǹní-ni ni-naanjab tiŋkin, ní ní dāá fōō-kì kí nīn kíǹ ki yì. U làá dāá fàtīí tīī-ni mmɔn ní kí yàntī ní bùtī kí jītíǹ ni-naanjab. 6Ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá dāá kpántí ni nì ni-naantiibi pɔbiliŋ, án nín làá ŋá pu ní dāá nīn kíǹ ki néeń-u nì ni-pɔbil kɔkɔ nì ni-naŋki kɔkɔ, kí nīn bí dimaŋfalinee. 7Ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá dāá dū mbusub nee kɔkɔ kí tɔ̄ ni-nannanliibi nì bin ná-ni ki sàantí-nee pu. 8Nimbee, ní dāá fàtīí nīn tɔ́ ti-Dindaan kí nīn ŋúb́ u-marab bin kɔkɔ m tīī-ni díǹ nee. 9Niinee ní ti-Dindaan ń dāá yàntī án bútí-ni ni-tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ poon tikpil, kí bùtī ni-maaliŋu nì ni-waŋkuti ní kí yàntī ni-kpaajinti ń lòoǹ. Di sá yii án làá dāá fáatíǹ ti-Dindaan ú ŋá-ni tiŋan kii an nín nìn fáatiǹ-u u ŋá ni-naanjab puee. 10Kí wàatī míǹ ń nín ŋée, asee ní nīn tɔ́ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu kí nīn ŋúb́ u-marab nì u-bɔkpaaŋi ŋin bi ŋmàn̄ ki ŋá marab gbɔŋku nee poonee, ní kí fàtīí gítiń ti-Dindaan cee nì ni-pɔbil kɔkɔ nì ni-naŋki kɔkɔ.
Dinyɔɔbundee dɔ̄ ki kɔ́ĺ-si
11Marab bin m cáa bíi tìì-ni díǹ nee kaa pɔ̄ɔ̄ tikpil ki jítiǹ ni-pɔŋŋu pu, ní kaa ti bíń laakin naa ŋūǹ kí bèe. 12Baa bíń yilpu ní ní lì yii: «Ŋma di làá jɔ̄m̀ yilpu kí nyàab̀-bi kí cáań kí tùkù-ti, án nín làá ŋá pu tí ŋmā kí béé kí ŋá kii bi nín bí yii tí ŋá puee?» 13Baa tí bí tiŋku gbandi lapu yal ní ní lì yii: «Ŋma di làá dùtī tiŋku kí nyàab̀-bi kí cáań kí tùkù-ti, án nín làá ŋá pu tí ŋmā kí béé kí ŋá kii bi nín bí yii tí ŋá puee?» 14Aayee, dinyɔɔbundee dɔ̄ ki kɔ́ĺ-ni. Di kā ni-nyɔkɔn ki kā ni-pɔbilin, án nín làá ŋá pu ní ŋmā kí ŋá kii di nín bí yii ní ŋá puee.
Lēē dimaŋfal saŋŋu
15Kpèèmaan, díǹ nee, m dū dimaŋfal nì nnaam, ŋkúm nì nnaabu ki bíl̀ ni-nimbiin. 16Mamee, m kpáafí-ni díǹ yii ní nīn néeń ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu, kí nīn ŋáań u nín là puee, kí nīn ŋúb́ u-marab nì u-bɔkpaaŋi nì u-koobiliŋ. Ni yaa ŋá mimmee, ni làá nīn bí dimaŋfalin ní kí bùtī, ní ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu ń bìin̄ ni-boon kitiŋ kin ni làá kɔ́ kí tin fōō kí nīn kíǹ ki yì nee poon. 17Ama ni yaa fātì ni-boon ki tīī-u, ní ki yaa kaa pílifiǹ-u ní ki cūtìi bíi gbàantí awaa taapu ki tòotī-ŋee, 18m tùkū-ni ki gíti bíi tùkù-ni díǹ yii ni làá pée kpú kí céetí ní múb. Naa làá kàl̄ kitiŋ kin poon ni làá dùtī Jɔɔdan buŋŋu kí cùú kɔ́ kí nīn kíǹ ki yì nee kí yúntí.
19Kutagbɔŋu nì kitiŋ sá-mi biseeradambi díǹ yii m dū dimaŋfal nì ŋkúm, dibiindi nì mbusu ki bíl̀ ni-nimbiin ní lēē. Ama ní lēē dimaŋfal án nín làá ŋá pu ni nì ni-naantiibi ń nīn bí dimaŋfalinee. 20Nín̄ néeḿmaan ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu kí nīn tɔ́-u, kí dū ni-ba kí nákáǹ-u. Míǹ ní ti-Dindaan làá yàntī ní nīn bí dimaŋfalin, ní kí yàntī ní kàl̄ kitiŋ kin poon u nìn pūtì ki pōoǹ ni-naanjab Abraam nì Isaaki nì Jaakɔb yii u làá tīī-bee kí yúntí.

english_text:
Final Speeches and the Death of Moses
Joshua Is Appointed the Leader of Israel
1Moses again spoke to the whole nation of Israel:
2 I am 120 years old, and I am no longer able to be your leader. And besides that, the Lord your God has told me that he won't let me cross the Jordan River. 3-5 But he has promised that he and Joshua will lead you across the Jordan to attack the nations that live on the other side. The Lord will destroy those nations just as he destroyed Sihon and Og, those two Amorite kings. Just remember—whenever you capture a place, kill everyone who lives there.
6Be brave and strong! Don't be afraid of the nations on the other side of the Jordan. The Lord your God will always be at your side, and he will never abandon you.
7Then Moses called Joshua up in front of the crowd and said:
Joshua, be brave and strong as you lead these people into their land. The Lord made a promise long ago to Israel's ancestors that this land would someday belong to Israel. That time has now come, and you must divide up the land among the people. 8 The Lord will lead you into the land. He will always be with you and help you, so don't ever be afraid of your enemies.
Read These Laws
9Moses wrote down all of these laws and teachings and gave them to the priests and the leaders of Israel. The priests were from the Levi tribe, and they carried the sacred chest that belonged to the Lord. 10-11 Moses told these priests and leaders:
Each year the Israelites must come together to celebrate the Festival of Shelters at the place where the Lord chooses to be worshiped. You must read these laws and teachings to the people at the festival every seventh year, the year when loans do not need to be repaid. 12-13Everyone must come—men, women, children, and even the foreigners who live in your towns. And each new generation will listen and learn to worship the Lord their God with fear and trembling and to do exactly what is said in God's Law.
Israel Will Reject the Lord
14The Lord told Moses, “You will soon die, so bring Joshua to the sacred tent, and I will appoint him the leader of Israel.”
Moses and Joshua went to the sacred tent, 15and the Lord appeared in a thick cloud right over the entrance to the tent. 16The Lord said:
Moses, you will soon die. But Israel is going into a land where other gods are worshiped, and Israel will reject me and start worshiping these gods. The people will break the agreement I made with them, 17and I will be so furious that I will abandon them and ignore their prayers. I will send disasters and suffering that will nearly wipe them out. Finally, they will realize that the disasters happened because I abandoned them. 18They will pray to me, but I will ignore them because they were evil and started worshiping other gods.
19Moses and Joshua, I am going to give you the words to a new song. Write them down and teach the song to the Israelites. If they learn it, they will know what I want them to do, and so they will have no excuse for not obeying me. 20I am bringing them into the land that I promised their ancestors. It is a land rich with milk and honey, and the Israelites will have more than enough food to eat. But they will get fat and turn their backs on me and start worshiping other gods. The Israelites will reject me and break the agreement that I made with them.
21When I punish the Israelites and their descendants with suffering and disasters, I will remind them that they know the words to this song, so they have no excuse for not obeying me.
I will give them the land that I promised, but I know the way they are going to live later on.
22Moses at once wrote down the words to the song, and he taught it to the Israelites.
23 The Lord told Joshua, “Be brave and strong! I will help you lead the people of Israel into the land that I have promised them.”
24Moses wrote down all these laws and teachings in a book, 25then he went to the Levites who carried the sacred chest and said:
26This is The Book of God's Law. Keep it beside the sacred chest that holds the agreement the Lord your God made with Israel. This book is proof that you know what the Lord wants you to do. 27I know how stubborn and rebellious you and the rest of the Israelites are. You have rebelled against the Lord while I have been alive, and it will only get worse after I am gone. 28So call together the leaders and officials of the tribes of Israel. I will bring this book and read every word of it to you, and I will call the sky and the earth as witnesses that all of you know what you are supposed to do.
29I am going to die soon, and I know that in the future you will stop caring about what is right and what is wrong, and so you will disobey the Lord and stop living the way I told you to live. The Lord will be angry, and terrible things will happen to you.
The Song of Moses
30Moses called a meeting of all the people of Israel, so he could teach them the words to the song that the Lord had given him. And here are the words:
translation_text:
MOOYIISI KĀAǸ ISIRAYEEL YAB KI KPÍÌ
(31–34)
Joosuwa fōō Mooyiisi yil
1Mooyiisi cūtì ki dū tibɔti nee ki tùkū Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ. 2U nìn tùkū-bi yii: «M cáá díǹ nee abin dilaataal nì mmuŋku ní nee. Maa ti ŋūǹ kí nīn gbíntìi līī ni-nyɔkɔpu ki kpòotī-ni. Kí kūtì muee, ti-Dindaan tùkū-mi yii: <Aa làá dùtī Jɔɔdan buŋŋu nee!> 3Ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu u-ba di làá lìntī ni-nyɔkɔpu ní ní dùtī. U làá kpɔ̀ kí céetí atimbun nee nib ní ní fōō bi-timmu kí nīn kíǹ ki yì. Joosuwa di làá nīn līī-ni nsan ní ní dùtī kii ti-Dindaan u-ba nín lī puee. 4Kii ti-Dindaan nín ŋá Amɔɔr yab bɔtiibi Siiwɔn nì Ɔɔgi nì bi-timmu pu ki kūū ki céetì-bee, míǹ mbaantiim ní u làá ŋá bi mun. 5Ti-Dindaan làá dū atimbun gbanti nib kí tīī-ni ní ní ŋá-bi kii m nín kpáafì-ni puee kɔkɔ. 6Ní pɔ́ɔm̀maan ni-ba kí ká dipɔbil. Ní taa fàŋkìmaan-bi kí taa yàntī ni-pɔbiliŋ ń bīil̀ bi-nimbiin. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá nīn bí ni-cee. Waa làá yàntī-ni, kaa làá dū-ni kí fá mun.»
7Niinee ní Mooyiisi yíiń Joosuwa ki tùkū-u Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nimbiin yii: «Pɔ́ɔǹ a-ba kí ká dipɔbil, di sá yii sii di làá cáá dinibul nee kí kɔ́ǹ kitiŋ kin ní ti-Dindaan nìn pōoǹ kí tīī bi-naanjabee poon. Sii di làá yàkatī kitiŋ gbanti kí tīī bi-kɔkɔ an kpántí bi-kpaatanti. 8Ti-Dindaan di làá nīn līī a-nyɔkɔpu ní kí nīn bí a-cee. Waa làá yàntī-si, kaa làá dū-si kí fá mun. Míǹ puee á taa fàŋkì, kí taa yàntī a-wunti ń yɔ̀tī».
Bi máaǹ kí nīn kàaǹ marab abin aluli kamaa
9Niinee Mooyiisi ŋmàn̄ Unimbɔti marab ki dūu tīī Leefii yab bisaraaŋaliibi bin tūntí ti-Dindaan poondi dakaauee nì Isirayeel yab tindaŋkpilib kɔkɔ. 10U kpáafì-bi yii: «Abin aluli kamaa, ŋyunti ŋun ní bi cáá apɔɔn dambi ki pūǹ-bee yaa bàn̄ ni bíi jīǹ tibìń jiŋaaliuee, 11Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ làá cù ti-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu nimbiin mpaan ŋun pu u làá dāá lēē kí nīn bí ní nīn jáaḿ-uee. Ní dāá kàaǹ marab nee Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nimbiin án kɔ́ bi-tafalin. 12Ní dāá kóoǹ samaa kɔkɔ, an dàkà yii bininjab nì binimpoobi nì mbiyaamu nì binicambi bin kóò ni-puee kí kpāfì. Bí dāá kàaǹ marab gbanti bí gbìl̄ kí bīfì kí nīn fàŋkí ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu, kí ŋúb́ marabee ní kí ŋá bi nín lī puee kɔkɔ. 13Niinee, ni-biyaamu mun kaa nìn dá láá nyí marab gbantee ń gbìl̄, ní kí bīfì kí nīn kíǹ ki fàŋkí ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu iwiin in kɔkɔ ni cáá kí kàl̄ kitiŋ kin ní ni làá dùtī Jɔɔdan buŋŋu kí cùú fōō kí nín kíǹ ki yì nee poonee.»
Isirayeel kaa làá yūĺ nì Unimbɔti deedee
14Ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Kpèè, a-wiiŋyi kaa ti náaǹ, a-kúm wiiŋŋu tóobiń. Míǹ puee yíiń Joosuwa ni-kɔkɔ ń dāan̄ kí sīĺ dikpafindi tantiun ḿ tùkù-u tin ní u máaǹ kí ŋée.»
Ní Mooyiisi nì Joosuwa cūtìi kɔ́ circir kɔŋkooŋŋun ki síl̀. 15Bi bí niinee ní ti-Dindaan dɔ́miń bi-cee ntagbanloon poon ní ntagbanloonee cūtì ki síl̀ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu punyɔkɔpu. 16Ní ti-Dindaan bí Mooyiisi yii: «Kpèè, a làá cùú dòon̄ kí ŋàl̄ a-naanjab dee. A-kúm boonee dinibul nee làá cù kí nīn tòotī awaa ŋin bin bí kitiŋ kin bi làá kɔ́ kí fōō kí nīn kíǹ ki yì nee tòotēe. Bi làá dāá dū-mi kí fá ní kí kpìtī dipoondi din m pōoǹ-bee. 17Ŋyunti gbantee, m làá dāá gíí bi-pu diŋuul, kí dū-bi kí fá ní kí fàtī m-boon kí tīī-bi. Agìń tikpil nì dinimbinaamandi làá dāá jēetí bi-pu kí nàan̄-bi ní bi dāa kíǹ ki bàlifī bi-ba yii: <Agìń nee yaa bíi bàń-tee, mimmee an kaa sá ti-Nimbɔtiu nín kaa ti bí ti-kansikinee di yì-tàaa?> 18Bi-kpitii in bi bíi ŋáań ŋyunti ŋun bi cūtìi bíi tòotī awaayee pu ní m làá dāá mɔ̀tīí fàtī m-boon kí tīī-bi. 19Kɔŋkɔnnee, ŋmàmaan nlan ŋun m làá dàkà-ni nee nyɔɔbuŋŋi kí síiń. Sii Mooyiisi, á cáá nlanee kí dàkà Isirayeel yab ní kí yàntī bí bīfì-ŋu kí nīn gà-ŋu. Di sá yii nlan gbanti di làá dāá nīn sá m-seeradaaŋwu Isirayeel yab cee. 20M làá cáá-bi kí kɔ́ǹ kitiŋ kin ní m pūtì ki pōoǹ kí tīī bi-naanjabee, kitiŋ kin pu ní nnaabiim nì tisiil còol̀ee. Bi làá dāá jī kí díkí kí ŋá ŋkpam ní boonee bí dāá cù kí nīn tòotī awaa. Bi làá dāá kpèè-mi fám ní kí gbá kí kpìtī m-poondi. 21Ŋyunti ŋun agìń nì dinimbinaamandi yaa láa bàn̄-bee, nlan nee di làá dāá lēē seera kí kpɔ̀ bi-bɔti. Di sá ki kpáaǹ bi-biyaamu gba kaa làá dāá súntí nlan nee. Bi làá dāá nīn pée téetí ní ki gà-ŋu. M nyí kun bí binib nee pɔbiliŋinee kí wàatī gba ní ḿ nín cáá-bi kí kɔ́ǹ kitiŋ kin m nìn pūtì ki pōoǹ yii m làá tīī-bee poon.»
22Yaadal ní Mooyiisi ŋmàn̄ nlanee ní ki dū-ŋu ki dàkā Isirayeel yab.
23Míǹ boonee ní ti-Dindaan kpáafì Nuuni jipɔɔn Joosuwa ní ki bí-u yii: «Pɔ́ɔǹ a-ba kí ká dipɔbil, di sá yii sii di làá cáá Isirayeel yab kí kɔ́ǹ kitiŋ kin m pūtì ki pōoǹ kí tīī-bee poon. Mama m-ba làá nīn bí a-cee.»
24Ŋyunti ŋun Mooyiisi ŋmàn̄ marab nee kɔkɔ ki ŋá kugbɔŋun ki dóòyee, 25ní u kpáafì Leefii yab bin tūntí ti-Dindaan poondi daakaauee yii: 26«Yòom̄maan marab gbɔŋku nee kí dū-u kí bíĺ kí kɔ́ĺ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu poondi dakaau. Niin ní u làá nīn bí kí nīn sá seeradaan ki kù ni-bɔti. 27Di sá yii m nyí ni-pu, m nyí ni-pɔɔpɔŋŋu pu. Ni yaa jáń nì ti-Dindaan ŋyunti ŋun ní m dá bí dimaŋfalin ki bí ni-cee nee, kin ataa aŋa pu ní, m-kúm boonee, naa dāa jáà nì u kí jītíǹ míǹ? 28Kóom̀maan ni-naakɔti kpilib nì ni-kpootiliibi kɔkɔ bí kpāfì m-cee, ḿ sòoǹ nì bi tibɔti nee bí gbìl̄ ní kutagbɔŋu nì kitiŋ mun ń nīn sá m-seeradambee. 29Di sá yii m nyí yii m-kúm boonee ni làá dāá kɔ́ ikpitin ní kí dāá fàtī ni-boon kí tīī tibɔti tin m dūu kpáafì-ni nee. Ŋyunti gbantee, ni-kpitii in ni làá dāá ŋá ti-Dindaan nimbiinee nì ni-tuŋkpitiŋ ŋin ni làá dāá ŋá kí yàntī ú gíí diŋuulee puee, digìńdi làá dāá kɔ́-ni.»
Mooyiisi laŋŋu
30Niinee ní Mooyiisi dū nlan nee nyɔɔbuŋŋi ki sòon̄ mpɔn an kɔ́ Isirayeel nikitil kɔkɔ tafalin.

english_text:
1Earth and Sky,
listen to what I say!
2Israel, I will teach you.
My words will be like gentle rain
on tender young plants,
or like dew on the grass.
3Join with me in praising
the wonderful name
of the Lord our God.
4The Lord is a mighty rock,
and he never does wrong.
God can always be trusted
to bring justice.
5But you lie and cheat
and are unfaithful to him.
You have disgraced yourselves
and are no longer worthy
to be his children.
6Israel, the Lord is your Father,
the one who created you,
but you repaid him
by being foolish.
7Think about past generations.
Ask your parents
or any of your elders.
They will tell you
8 that God Most High
gave land to every nation.
He assigned a guardian angel
to each of them,
9but the Lord himself
takes care of Israel.
10Israel, the Lord discovered you
in a barren desert
filled with howling winds.
God became your fortress,
protecting you as though
you were his own eyes.
11The Lord was like an eagle
teaching its young to fly,
always ready to swoop down
and catch them on its back.
12Israel, the Lord led you,
and without the aid
of a foreign god,
13he helped you
capture the land.
Your fields were rich
with grain.
Olive trees grew
in your stony soil,
and honey was found
among the rocks.
14Your flocks and herds
produced milk and yogurt,
and you got choice meat
from your sheep and goats
that grazed in Bashan.
Your wheat was the finest,
and you drank the best wine.
15Israel, you grew fat and rebelled
against God, your Creator
you rejected the Mighty Rock,
your only place of safety.
16You made God jealous and angry
by worshiping disgusting idols
and foreign gods.
17 You offered sacrifices
to demons, those useless gods
that never helped you,
new gods that your ancestors
never worshiped.
18You turned away
from God, your Creator;
you forgot the Mighty Rock,
the source of your life.
19You were the Lord's children,
but you made him angry.
Then he rejected you 20and said,
“You are unfaithful
and can't be trusted.
So I won't answer your prayers;
I'll just watch and see
what happens to you.
21 You worshiped worthless idols,
and made me jealous
and angry!
Now I will send a cruel
and worthless nation
to make you jealous and angry.
22“My people, I will breathe out fire
that sends you down
to the world of the dead.
It will scorch your farmlands
and burn deep down
under the mountains.
23I'll send disaster after disaster
to strike you like arrows.
24You'll be struck by starvation
and deadly diseases,
by the fangs of wild animals
and poisonous snakes.
25Young and old alike
will be killed in the streets
and terrified at home.
26“I wanted to scatter you,
so no one would remember
that you had ever lived.
27But I dreaded the sound
of your enemies saying,
‘We defeated Israel with no help
from the Lord.’ ”
28People of Israel,
that's what the Lord
has said to you.
But you don't have good sense,
and you never listen
to advice.
29If you did, you could see
where you are headed.
30How could one enemy soldier
chase a thousand
of Israel's troops?
Or how could two of theirs
pursue ten thousand of ours?
It can only happen if the Lord
stops protecting Israel
and lets the enemy win.
31Even our enemies know
that only our God
is a Mighty Rock.
32Our enemies are grapevines
rooted in the fields
of Sodom and Gomorrah.
The grapes they produce
are full of bitter poison;
33their wine is more deadly
than cobra venom.
34But the Lord has written
a list of their sins
and locked it in his vault.
35 Soon our enemies will get
what they deserve—
suddenly they will slip,
and total disaster
will quickly follow.
36 When only a few
of the Lord's people remain,
when their strength is gone,
and some of them are slaves,
the Lord will feel sorry for them
and give them justice.
37But first the Lord will say,
“You ran for safety to other gods—
couldn't they help you?
38You offered them wine
and your best sacrifices.
Can't those gods help you now
or give you protection?
39Don't you understand?
I am the only God;
there are no others.
I am the one who takes life
and gives it again.
I punished you with suffering.
But now I will heal you,
and nothing can stop me!
40“I make this solemn promise:
Just as I live forever,
41I will take revenge
on my hateful enemies.
I will sharpen my sword
and let it flash
like lightning.
42My arrows will get drunk
on enemy blood;
my sword will taste the flesh
and the blood of the enemy.
It will kill prisoners,
and cut off the heads
of their leaders.”
43 Tell the heavens to celebrate
and all gods to bow down
to the Lord,
because he will take revenge
on those hateful enemies
who killed his people.
He will forgive the sins of Israel
and purify their land.
44-45Moses spoke the words of the song so that all the Israelites could hear, and Joshua helped him. When Moses had finished, 46he said, “Always remember this song I have taught you today. And let it be a warning that you must teach your children to obey everything written in The Book of God's Law. 47The Law isn't empty words. It can give you a long life in the land that you are going to take.”
Moses Will See the Land
48 Later that day the Lord said to Moses:
49Go up into the Abarim Mountain range here in Moab across the Jordan River valley from Jericho. And when you reach the top of Mount Nebo, you will be able to see the land of Canaan, which I am giving to Israel. 50Then you will die and be buried on the mountaintop, just as your brother Aaron died and was buried on Mount Hor. 51Both of you were unfaithful to me at Meribah Spring near Kadesh in the Zin Desert. I am God, but there in front of the Israelites, you did not treat me with the honor and respect I deserve. 52So I will give the land to the people of Israel, but you will only get to see it from a distance.
translation_text:
1Kutagbɔŋu, pīlifì m-bɔti,
kitiŋ, pīlifì m-nyɔɔbuŋŋi.
2M-bɔti tin m dàkèe yàantí kii utaayee,
ní m-nyɔɔbundi tòó kii dimalindee,
kii utaaja nín nì ki sɔ̀ŋkī kumɔsɔŋu puee,
kii putipuuki nín yàantí kumoou pu puee.
3Di sá m làá nyɔ̄ŋkì ti-Dindaan yindi.
Tí nyɔ̄ŋkìmaan ti-Nimbɔtiu kpaanti.
4Ti-Dindaan sá kutaŋkpanaakoou.
Inaatuu kpá u-tuuŋŋi poon,
u-saŋyi kɔkɔ tèen̄ ní.
U sá deedee Nimbɔtiu ní, ikpiti kpá u-ni,
ibaamɔn nì deedeedaan ní u sá.
5Nimbi bin ŋáań ikpiti ki gáatèe,
ni yīntiǹ ti-Dindaan.
Án nīn cáá-ni icoo!
Naa ti sá u-biyaamu!
6Dinibul din nib sá bigbaambi ki lóò dinyilee,
