mimmee tipaal tin ni làá dūú pà ti-Dindaanee deeee?
Úǹ di kaa sá ni-baa ki tīī-ni dimaŋfalaaa?
Úǹ di kaa náań-ni ki dū-ni ki kpántì u-nibulaaa?
7Téetímaan iyuntikpiki pu,
dàkafìmaan ni-naanjab yuntii pu.
Bàlifìmaan ni-baabi bí tùkù-ni!
Ní bàlifì ni-tikpilib bí māafì-ni!
8Yilpu fɔ́ŋŋŋ Nimbɔtiu nín nìn tīī atimbun kɔkɔ bi-timmuee,
ŋyunti ŋun u nìn cúú anibul kɔkɔ ki yākatì tɔbinee,
u nìn tīī ditimbundi kamaa di-kpaanyɔkɔ
ki nóó nì Isirayeel yab nyɔkɔm ní.
9Ama ti-Dindaan nibul di sá u-fakal,
Jaakɔb naantiibi ní u lēē kí nīn yì.
10Ti-Dindaan nìn ká u-nibul kuteeun,
laakin bi gbìl̀ jiiŋkpaaibi siim ŋmaniŋma puee.
U nìn wúń bi-pu ki dàkà-bi,
u nìn cí-bi kii u-nimbibuliiyee.
11U nìn ŋá kii ukaalun nín ŋáań pu,
kí yòon̄ u-biyaamu kí jɔ̄m̀ yilpu
kí gíiǹ-mu kí líiń pu
ní kí kpátiń u-feeŋyi kí nīn sìntīń pu
ki cí mun yaa gīīyee ń dāá páań puee ní.
12Ti-Dindaan baba di nìn kpōotì u-nibul,
unimbɔti ubɔ kaa nìn bí ki kútì u-pu.
13U nìn kāaǹ-bi ŋgbantamu pu,
ní ki dū tikpaajin ki kpíiǹ-bi.
U lēē tisiil ntaŋkpalɔkɔn ki tīī-bi bi ŋmɔ́,
ní ki nyántì ŋkpam ditaŋkpayaabulin ki tīī-bi bi jíń.
14U nìn tīī-bi waagaasii nì mpibiim,
ki tīī-bi apibil nì iŋɔjaa nì ipijaa in bí màlmalee,
ki tīī-bi bileemɔnti yim bi jíń,
ní ki tīī-bi fiinyi damam bi nyùn̄.
15Yeesurun jíń ki díkí ki ŋá ŋkpamee,
ní ki kíǹ ki bíi tòó igbeen.
U gbīfiǹ ki ŋá ŋkpam ki ŋá gbàlgbalee,
ní ki dū Unimbɔti un náań-uee ki fá,
ki kíǹ ki kpèé un sá u-taŋkpanaakooku nì u-fiiliuee fám.
16Isirayeel yab nìn ŋá ntimbiil tuuŋŋi
ki yāntì Unimbɔti gíí diŋuul.
Bi nìn dū bi-waatuuŋŋi
ki gbítì u-ŋuul.
17Bi nìn ŋáań saraabi ki tìì arasiniibi, kaa sá Unimbɔti.
Bi nìn ŋáań ki tìì awaa ŋin baa nìn nyí ki kée,
awaapɔɔn ŋin bi dáá nyántì
bi-baabi kaa nìn nyí ŋi-pu gbee.
18«Isirayeel, a súntì a-taŋkpanaakooku pu,
a súntì un màl̄-see pu,
kaa ti dū Unimbɔti un tīī-si dimaŋfalee ki yíiń tiba.»
19Ti-Dindaan ká mimmee ní ki gíí diŋuul,
u-jipɔmbi nì u-bisalib yīntiǹ-u
ní u dū-bi ki fá.
20Ní ti-Dindaan lī yii: «M làá fàtī m-boon kí tīī-bi,
ní kí kpèè án nín làá dāá kúntíǹ-bi puee.
Kun puee bi sá binib bin gáatèe ní,
binib bin pu baa ŋūǹ kí nīn mákée.
21Bi yāntì kun kaa sá Unimbɔtee
fōō m-paaŋŋu ki kɔ́ǹ-mi ipoompoon,
ní ki dū bi-waaŋi ŋin kaa bí tibanee ki gbítì m-ŋuul.
Ma mun làá dū dinibul din kaa sá m-yalee
kí kɔ́ǹ-bi ipoompoon,
ní kí yàntī bí fōō diŋuul
binib bin kaa cáá iciinee pu.
22Di sá m-ŋuul bíi fòol̄ lìblib kii ŋŋmee.
Di wùn̄ ki tin bàn̄ ditaŋkpiil taapu,
di wùn̄ ki kpáaǹ kitiŋ nì tin kɔkɔ ki lòon̄ee,
ki làá póotí kí wà ajoon nyeel.
23M làá tɔ̄-bi agìń tikpil poon,
m làá tɔ̄-bi m-piiŋyi.
24Ŋkùm yaa láa bàn̄-bi,
ní bìlbil kúm weeŋyi nì iweentintikaa in kùee
yaa láa cúú-bee,
ní ḿ dāá dū ipeecuncuti nì ikoobu in
cáá tiloolee kí tɔ̄ bi-pu.
25Bi làá dū kitàataajiki kí kpɔ̀ bi-biyaamu adan pu,
ní dipɔɔbiildi ń kɔ́ báà ŋma adiinni.
Tin làá bàń unaacimpɔɔnee di làá bàń usapɔɔn,
tin làá bàń kibipɔŋee di làá bàń utikpil.»
26«M dākafì kí bàà nà-bi ní dúsi dusi,
ní kí kúntí bi-yindi kitiŋ pu kpataaa.
27Ama kun m fāŋkèe di sá bi-nannanliibi siibiliŋ.
Bi ŋūǹ kí taa gbìl̄ taapu
ní kí lì yii: <An sá ti-kpabil di tīī-ti dijajil,
an kaa sá bi-Dindaan di ŋá tin bí nee.>
28«Isirayeel yab sá ditimbundi din landɔkɔi gátèe ní,
baa cáá iciin báà fiii.
29Bi yaa bàà cáá dinyil fiii,
bi bàà gbìl̀ taapu tiŋan,
kí dàkafì kí béé tin dɔ̄ ki cí-bee.
30Mana ní unibaanti bàà ŋūǹ kí jà binib kutuku,
ní binib bili ja ń yàntī binib kutukub saalaa ń sāǹ,
an yaa kaa sá yii man bi-Dindaan un sá bi-taŋkpanaakookuee
di dū-bi ki ŋá bi-nannanliibi ŋaan?
31«Di sá yii bi-nannanliibi nyí tiŋan yii
bi-taŋkpanaakooku kaa bí kii Isirayeel taŋkpanaakookuee.
32Bi-fiinyi sufii bí kii Soodoom sufiiyee,
bi-kpaaŋŋi bí kii Goomoora kpaaŋŋee.
Bi-fiinyi sufii lòoǹ abil ŋin cáá tiloolee,
abil ŋin di tū kátí katee.
33Bi-damam sá kii ikoobu lootee ní,
a lì kii ukoowaati lootee.
34«Kpèèmaan kun man bi-Dindaan
bɔ́ntì dibalin an dɔ̄ ki cí-bee.
35Man di làá dāá tɔ̀ ipɔntoon,
man di làá dāá pà bi-tuuŋŋi paati.
Bi-nimbinaamandi wiiŋŋu tóobiń,
tin bɔ́ntì ki cí-bee kaa làá tàan̄ ní kí bàń-bi.»
36Tiŋman, ti-Dindaan làá dāá sòoǹ kí pɔ̀ u-nibul,
ní kí dāá sɔ̄ u-tɔntɔnliibi saai
ŋyunti ŋun u yaa láa ká yii baa ti cáá mpɔn,
ní uyumbu àá un tɔ́ u-bee kaa ti bée.
37U làá dāá bàlifì yii:
<Bi-waaŋi ŋin nìn sá bi-taŋkpanaakooku
bi sáń ki kóòyee bí la ní?
38Awaa ŋin nìn ŋmóò bi-saraabi kpam,
ki nyù ndaam min bi féeń-ŋee bí la?
Ŋí yīkì kí dāá fīī-baa!
Ŋí nyàab̀ kibalilaŋ kí tīī-baa!>
39Míǹ puee ní béémaan díǹ yii,
man baba di sá Unimbɔti,
ubɔ kaa ti bí ki kútì man pu.
Man di ŋūǹ kí lēē unil maŋfal,
man di tí ŋūǹ kí tīī dimaŋfal.
Man di tìì tiweendi,
man di tí cāantí,
ní ubɔ kaa bí ki ŋūǹ kí fīī un kā man ŋaanee.
40M yōoǹ m-ŋal yilpu
ki lī yii: <M bí dimaŋfalin kí nīn cá jaanjaan!
41M yaa lōoǹ m-tàataajiki kì jītí pámpam
ki dū-kì ki tākaǹ m-ŋaan kí kíĺ ibɔsoonee,
m làá tɔ̀ m-nannanliibi ipɔntoon,
ní kí pà bin kɔkɔ ná-mee bi-kpitii paati.
42M-piiŋyi làá dāá nyɔ̀ fatiku kí gbí,
ní m-tàataajiki ń dāá ŋmɔ́ bin fōō tiweendee
nì bin bi cúú kuyuŋuee nanti,
ki kpáaǹ binannanliibi kpilib yiliŋ.>
43Atimbun, ní pàkàmaan ti-Dindaan nikitil,
di sá yii ti-Dindaan làá tɔ̀ u-tɔntɔnliibi
bin bi kūūyee pɔntooŋyi,
kí dáaĺ u-nannanliibi tafal,
ní kí fíntí u-tiŋki nì u-nikitil kpitii.
44Mooyiisi nì Nuuni jipɔɔn Joosuwa dɔ́miń ki dū nlan nee nyɔɔbuŋŋi ki sòon̄ samaa kɔkɔ tafalin.
45Ŋyunti ŋun ní Mooyiisi kàan̄ tibɔti gbanti kɔkɔ ki tīī Isirayeel yab ki dóòyee, 46ní u bí-bi yii: «Ní taa dū tibɔti tin kɔkɔ m kpáafì-ni díǹ nee kí ŋá bugbambu, kí taa dūú gbīiliǹ. Ní dū-tì kí dàkà ni-biyaamu, ní mu mun ń ŋmā kí nīn tɔ́ marab nee nyɔɔbuŋŋi kɔkɔ tiŋan. 47Di sá yii marab gbanti sá tibɔmɔntiil ní, ní ki sá ni-maŋfal. Ni yaa tɔ́-bee, bi làá yàntī ní kàl̄ kitiŋ kin ni làá dùtī Jɔɔdan buŋŋu kí cùú fōō kí nīn kíǹ ki yì nee poon kí yúntí.»
Unimbɔti sòon̄ Mooyiisi kúm bɔti
48Ŋwimbaanti gbantee ní ti-Dindaan tùkū Mooyiisi yii: 49«Cù Abariim jooŋŋi ŋin bí Moowaab tiŋkin, Jeeriikoo tiŋki nyɔkɔpuee kí jɔ̄m̀ Neeboo jool pu kí kpèè Kanaan tiŋki kin m làá dūú tīī Isirayeel yab bí nīn kíǹ ki yèe. 50Dijool din a làá jɔ̄m̀ee pu ní a làá tin kpú kí cùú ŋàl̄ a-naanjab, kii a-maan Aarɔn nín kpíì Ɔɔr jool pu ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ u-yab puee. 51Di sá yii ŋyunti ŋun ni nìn bàn̄ Meeriiba Kadeesi, Siini teeku puee, ni-liitil kaa nìn ŋá Isirayeel yab nimbiin kii m nín nìn bí yii ní ŋá pu kí ká nnyimee, kaa nìn tí dàkā Isirayeel yab yii m sá circir. 52Míǹ puee ndandati ní a làá sīĺ ní kí wāl̀ kitiŋ kin m làá dūú tīī Isirayeel yabee, ama sii a-ba kpá kí kɔ́ ki-ni.»

english_text:
Moses Blesses the Tribes of Israel
1Moses was a prophet, and before he died, he blessed the tribes of Israel by saying:
2The Lord came from Mount Sinai.
From Edom, he gave light
to his people,
and his glory was shining
from Mount Paran.
Thousands of his warriors
were with him, and fire
was at his right hand.
3 The Lord loves the tribes
of Israel,
and he protects his people.
They listen to his words
and worship at his feet.
* 4I called a meeting
of the tribes of Israel
and gave you God's Law.
5Then you and your leaders
made the Lord your king.
6Tribe of Reuben, you will live,
even though your tribe
will always be small.
7The Lord will listen to you,
tribe of Judah, as you beg
to come safely home.
You fought your enemies alone;
now the Lord will help you.
8 At Massah and Meribah Spring,
the Lord tested you,
tribe of Levi.
You were faithful,
and so the priesthood belongs
to the Levi tribe.
9Protecting Israel's agreement
with the Lord
was more important to you
than the life of your father
or mother,
or brothers or sisters,
or your own children.
10You teach God's laws to Israel,
and at the place of worship
you offer sacrifices
and burn incense.
11I pray that the Lord will bless
everything you do,
and make you strong enough
to crush your enemies.
12The Lord Most High loves you,
tribe of Benjamin.
He will live among your hills
and protect you.
13Descendants of Joseph,
the Lord will bless you
with precious water
from deep wells
and with dew from the sky.
14Month by month, your fruit
will ripen in the sunshine.
15You will have a rich harvest
from the slopes
of the ancient hills.
16The Lord who appeared
in the burning bush
wants to give you the best
the land can produce,
and it will be a princely crown
on Joseph's head.
17The armies of Ephraim
and Manasseh
are majestic and fierce
like a bull or a wild ox.
They will run their spears
through faraway nations.
18Be happy, Zebulun,
as your boats set sail;
be happy, Issachar,
in your tents.
19The sea will make you wealthy,
and from the sandy beach
you will get treasure.
So invite the other tribes
to celebrate with you
and offer sacrifices to God.
20Tribe of Gad,
the Lord will bless you
with more land.
So shout his praises!
Your tribe is like a lion
ripping up its victim.
21Your leaders met together
and chose the best land
for your tribe,
but you obeyed the Lord
and helped the other tribes.
22Tribe of Dan,
you are like a lion cub,
startled by a snake.
23The Lord is pleased with you,
people of Naphtali.
He will bless you
and give you the land
to the west and the south.
24The Lord's greatest blessing
is for you, tribe of Asher.
You will be the favorite
of all the other tribes.
You will be rich with olive oil
25and have strong town gates
with bronze and iron bolts.
Your people will be powerful
for as long as they live.
26Israel, no other god
is like ours—
the clouds are his chariot
as he rides across the skies
to come and help us.
27The eternal God
is our hiding place;
he carries us in his arms.
When God tells you
to destroy your enemies,
he will make them run.
28Israel, you will live in safety;
your enemies will be gone.
The dew will fall from the sky,
and you will have plenty
of grain and wine.
29The Lord has rescued you
and given you more blessings
than any other nation.
He protects you like a shield
and is your majestic sword.
Your enemies will bow in fear,
and you will trample
on their backs.
translation_text:
Mooyiisi mēē ki bīiǹ Isirayeel naakɔti pu
1Kí wàatī Unimbɔti niliu Mooyiisi ń kpúee, u nìn mēē ki bīiǹ Isirayeel yab pu.
2U nìn lī yii:
«Ti-Dindaan nyánní Siinaayi jool pu,
u nyáń ki páaǹní Seeyiir jool watil pú,
ní ki ŋmíntì u-samaau pu doooo Paaran jool pu.
U bāań Meeriiba Kadeesi.
Niin ní u nìn ŋúbiń marab bin jìl̀ee u-ŋaan kí tīī-bi.
3Tiŋman ti-Dindaan, a néeń Isirayeel naakɔti.
Bin kɔkɔ bí circiree bí a-ŋaan.
Bi gbāā a-taaŋi taapu kí fōō a-nyɔɔbundi.
4Marab bin ní Mooyiisi tīī-tee,
Jaakɔb naantiibi gaajawanti dee.
5Ŋyunti ŋun samaa kpilib nìn kpáfì
ki kpáaǹ Isirayeel naakɔti kɔkɔee,
ti-Dindaan di nìn sá Yeesurun bɔtiu.»
6Ní Mooyiisi kútì ki lī yii:
«Rubeen naakooku ń nīn bí dimaŋfalin kí taa kpú,
u-nib bin pátèe mun ń nīn bí dimaŋfalin.»
7U sòon̄ Juuda naakooku pu yii:
«Ti-Dindaan, pīlifì Juuda neen,
kí cáań-u u-yab cee bí ŋá ubaanti.
Ú mɔ̄tì u-ba pu nì tininjati.
Tūtuǹ-u ú jáǹ u-nannanliibi.»
8U sòon̄ Leefii naakooku pu yii:
«Ti-Dindaan, a dū a-Tumiimuu nì a-Uriimuu
ki tīī unil un fáatiǹ-see ní.
A nìn cɔ́ŋkì-u Maasa,
sii nì u nìn kpáká Meeriiba nyim laŋki.
9U dàkā a-pu dineendi ki jítiǹ u-baa nì u-na pu,
ki jítiǹ u-nabiyaamu nì u-biyaamu pu.
Di sá bi nìn ŋúb́ a-nyɔɔbundi,
ní ki nìn ŋúb́ a-poondi.
10Bíǹ di dàkà Jaakɔb yab a-koobiliŋ,
ki dàkà Isirayeel yab a-marab.
Bíǹ di tùutī talaalub ki tìì-si,
ki ŋáań saraawɔkaa a-saraafaŋŋu pu.
11Ti-Dindaan, mɔ̀tīí kūtì-bi mpɔn,
yàntī bi-ŋaan tuuŋŋi ń fáatiǹ-si.
Fáá kí tàtī bin yíkì kí jáǹ-bee cammu,
bin ná-bee ń taa ti ŋmā kí yīkì.»
12U sòon̄ Beenjameen naakooku pu yii:
«Ti-Dindaan bineeŋkaaki,
ú nīn bí ŋgbansɔŋfin u-Nimbɔtiu cee.
di sá úǹ di wúń u-pu baabadal,
ní ki kóò u-gbantammu kansikin.»
13Mooyiisi sòon̄ Jooseefi naakooku pu yii:
«Ti-Dindaan ń bìin̄ u-tiŋki pu,
kí tīī-kì dimalindi din nyēeń yilpuee,
nì nnyim min nyēeń kitiŋ taapuee,
14kí tí tīī-kì tikpaajin timɔntiil tin ŋwìiń yàntī an nyēēyee,
nì asubimɔnti ŋin lòoǹ uŋmal kamaayee.
15Tijimmɔntiil ń lòoǹ ki-jooŋŋi ŋin bí doooo jaanjaanee pu,
asubimɔnti ń lòoǹ ki-gbantammu mun bí doooo cannaakuee pu.
16Tigaajati tin gbí kitiŋ nee puee
nì ti-Dindaan un nìn nyántì u-ba kisugbooi poon ki dàkēe
biindi ń dāan̄ kí nīn bí Jooseefi pu,
úǹ un sá kii ubɔti u-nabiyaamu kansikinee.
17U sá unaja un sá dibiseemalee, ki cáá tinyool.
U-yiŋyi bí kii upɔɔnaa yiŋyee,
íǹ ní u làá nīn cáa gbáà atimbun nib
kí cáá sāā kitiŋ kúntilaŋki.
Míǹ ní Eefiraayiim naantiibi cutimaanyee bí,
míǹ ní Manasee naantiibi kutukub kutukubee bí.»
18Mooyiisi sòon̄ Sabulɔn nì Isakaar naakɔti pu yii:
«Sabulɔn, án nīn mɔ̄ǹ-si a-saŋkindi poon.
Isakaar, án nīn mɔ̄ǹ si mun a-tantib poon!
19Ni làá dāá yíiń anibul dijool pu,
kí dāá ŋá saraabi kii bi nín síiǹ mara puee.
Di sá yii ni-gaajati làá dāá nyānní dimɔɔl pu,
ní tiwammɔntiil tin bál̀ee ń dāá nyānní dibulin.»
20U sòon̄ Gaadi naakooku pu yii:
«Nyɔ̄ŋkìmaan ti-Dindaan un wàantí Gaadi tiŋkee!
Gaadi dɔ̄ kii gbikintee ní.
U yaa cúú kuwaŋkuluuee, u tɔ̀ntī-ku ní,
kí yòon̄ ataa kí cáá sāā diyil.
21U lēē kitimmɔntii ki gāā u-bindi,
u dū dijandi din sá ubɔti yalee kí síiǹ u-ba.
U dɔ́miń ki kútì samaa kpilib pu ki ŋá kii ti-Dindaan nín là puee,
ní ki sòoǹ ti-Dindaan bɔkpaaŋi ŋin u nìn tīī Isirayeel yabee pu.»
22Mooyiisi sòon̄ Daani naakooku pu yii:
«Daani sá kii digbikintipɔmbil
din wúliń doooo Baasan tiŋkinee ní.»
23U sòon̄ Neefitalii naakooku pu yii:
«Ti-Dindaan gbéeǹ Neefitalii
u-ŋanti nì u-biindi.
Úǹ di làá nīn yì kitiŋ kí yòon̄ ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki kí cáá cùnnì ŋgiil pú.»
24U sòon̄ Aseer naakooku pu yii:
«Jaakɔb biyaamu kansikinee,
Aseer ń nīn sá un boon ti-Dindaan bīiǹ tikpilee,
u-nabiyaamu ń nīn néeń u-bɔti
ní u-taaŋi ń nīn dēē ɔliifi kpamin.
25U-kampiiŋi ń dāá nīn sá tikúti nì tasa kúti,
ú dāá nīn cáá mpɔn kí cáá sāā u-kúm dal!»
26Ní Mooyiisi nìkī ki lī yii:
«Yeesurun Nimbɔtiu kaa cáá juti.
Úǹ di sá ukpaan ki kāń atagban pu ki jàkàń
ki pùntī kutaa kí dāá jòoń-si.
27Unimbɔti un bí jaanjaanee di sá a-taŋkpanaakooku.
U dàkà u-pɔŋŋu taapu doo baabadal.
Úǹ di jìn̄ a-nannanliibi a-nyɔkɔpu,
ní ki bí-si yii á kpɔ̀ kí céetí-bi!
28«Isirayeel yab bí ŋgbansɔŋfin,
Jaakɔb naantiibi bí dibatɔlin.
Bi tàkā bilee nì ndapɔm tiŋkin,
kitiŋ kin pu dimalindi nyēeń yilpu ki tòóyee.
29«A bí mmɔnneeee Isirayeel!
Ŋma di bí kii sii dinibul din ní ti-Dindaan fīīyee?
Ti-Dindaan di sá a-gbampɔɔl, ki sá un tútúǹ-see.
U sá kitàataajiki kin tìì-si dijajilee.
A-nannanliibi làá dāá gbàan̄ a-nimbiin
ní á dāá tāā bi-waapaaŋyi pùb.»

english_text:
The Death of Moses
1Sometime later, Moses left the lowlands of Moab. He went up Mount Pisgah to the peak of Mount Nebo, which is across the Jordan River from Jericho. The Lord showed him all the land as far north as Gilead and the town of Dan. 2He let Moses see the territories that would soon belong to the tribes of Naphtali, Ephraim, Manasseh, and Judah, as far west as the Mediterranean Sea. 3The Lord also showed him the land in the south, from the valley near the town of Jericho, known as The City of Palm Trees, down to the town of Zoar.
4 The Lord said, “Moses, this is the land I was talking about when I solemnly promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob that I would give land to their descendants. I have let you see it, but you will not cross the Jordan and go in.”
5And so, Moses the Lord's servant died there in Moab, just as the Lord had said. 6The Lord buried him in a valley near the town of Beth-Peor, but even today no one knows exactly where. 7Moses was 120 years old when he died, yet his eyesight was still good, and his body was strong.
8The people of Israel stayed in the lowlands of Moab, where they mourned and grieved 30 days for Moses, as was their custom.
Joshua Becomes the Leader of Israel
9Before Moses died, he had placed his hands on Joshua, and the Lord had given Joshua wisdom. The Israelites paid attention to what Joshua said and obeyed the commands that the Lord had given Moses.
Moses Was a Great Prophet
10 There has never again been a prophet in Israel like Moses. The Lord spoke face to face with him 11and sent him to perform powerful miracles in the presence of the king of Egypt and his entire nation. 12No one else has ever had the power to do such great things as Moses did for everyone to see.
translation_text:
Mooyiisi kúm
1Niinee Mooyiisi dūu dī Moowaab tantakal ki dàb̄ Neeboo jool ki tin jɔ́m̀ Piisga jool yilpu. Piisga jool gbanti nìn bí Jeeriikoo tiŋki nyɔkɔpu ní. Niin ní ti-Dindaan nìn dàkā-u kitiŋ kɔkɔ, ki yōoǹ Galaadi ki tin cáa sāā Daani tiŋki, 2ki kpáaǹ Neefitalii tiŋki kɔkɔ nì Eefiraayiim nì Manasee tiŋki nì Juuda tiŋki kɔkɔ ki tin cáa sāā tiŋku ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú, 3nì Neegeeb tiŋki nì Jɔɔdan tantakal ki yōoǹ Jeeriikoo ibafi tiŋki, ki tin cáa sāā Soowaar. 4Niinee ní ti-Dindaan tùkū-u yii: «Kpèè, kitiŋ kin m nìn pōoǹ yii m làá tīī Abraam nì Isaaki nì Jaakɔbee dee. M nìn tùkū-bi yii: <M làá dāá dū-kì kí tīī ni-naantiibi ní.> M yāntì a wál̀ kitiŋ gbanti nì a-nimbiliŋ, ama aa làá nín kɔ́ ki-ni ní.»
5Míǹ boonee ní ti-Dindaan tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi kpíì Moowaab tiŋkin niin kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn lī puee. 6Ní ti-Dindaan síb́-u Moowaab tiŋkin ditantakalin, Beeti-Peewɔɔr tiŋki nyɔkɔpu. Ama báà ubɔ kaa nyí u-kaakul laŋki ki dāa sāā díǹ. 7Mooyiisi nìn cáá abin dilaataal nì mmuŋku ní ki kpíì. U nìn dáá pée gbíntìi wāĺ tiŋan ní, u-nimbiliŋ kaa pēefì, ní ki nìn gbíntìi dáá cáá u-pɔŋŋu mun.
8Isirayeel yab nìn súń Mooyiisi kpool iwiin mmuŋku nì saalaa ní Moowaab tantakalin. Míǹ boon ní Mooyiisi kpool kúntì. 9Ti-Dindaan nìn gbéeǹ Nuuni jipɔɔn Joosuwa Ŋfam min tīī-u dinyilee, di sá yii Mooyiisi nìn dū u-ŋalii ki páaǹ u-pu ki mēē. An puee Isirayeel yab nìn pílifiǹ-u ní ki nìn ŋáań kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn kpáafì Mooyiisi yii bí ŋá puee.
10Baa ti ká Isirayeel tiŋkin Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu ubɔ bí kii Mooyiisee. Mooyiisi nìn yūlifí ti-Dindaan nimbiin ní bi sòoǹ nì tɔb. 11Ti-Dindaan nìn tú-u Eejipiti tiŋkin u cūtìi ŋá maamaacikpaambi Faaroo nì u-kàliŋkpilib nì u-nib kɔkɔ nimbiin. 12Mooyiisi nìn dàkā mpɔŋkpaan nì maamaaci tuuŋŋi Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nimbiin.

english_text:
Joshua Becomes the Leader of Israel
1Moses, the Lord's servant, was dead. So the Lord spoke to Joshua son of Nun, who had been the assistant of Moses. The Lord said:
2My servant Moses is dead. Now you must lead Israel across the Jordan River into the land I'm giving to all of you. 3 Wherever you go, I'll give you that land, as I promised Moses. 4It will reach from the Southern Desert to the Lebanon Mountains in the north, and to the northeast as far as the great Euphrates River. It will include the land of the Hittites, and the land from here at the Jordan River to the Mediterranean Sea on the west. 5 Joshua, I will always be with you and help you as I helped Moses, and no one will ever be able to defeat you.
6-8 Long ago I promised the ancestors of Israel that I would give this land to their descendants. So be strong and brave! Be careful to do everything my servant Moses taught you. Never stop reading The Book of the Law he gave you. Day and night you must think about what it says. If you obey it completely, you and Israel will be able to take this land.
9I've commanded you to be strong and brave. Don't ever be afraid or discouraged! I am the Lord your God, and I will be there to help you wherever you go.
The Eastern Tribes Promise To Help
10Joshua ordered the tribal leaders 11to go through the camp and tell everyone:
In a few days we will cross the Jordan River to take the land that the Lord our God is giving us. So prepare as much food as you'll need for the march into the land.
12 Joshua told the men of the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh:
13-14The Lord's servant Moses said that the Lord our God has given you land here on the east side of the Jordan River, where you could live in peace. Your wives and children and your animals can stay here in the land Moses gave you. But all of you that can serve in our army must pick up your weapons and lead the men of the other tribes across the Jordan River. They are your relatives, so you must help them 15conquer the land that the Lord is giving them. The Lord will give peace to them as he has given peace to you, and then you can come back and settle here in the land that Moses promised you.
16The men answered:
We'll cross the Jordan River and help our relatives. We'll fight anywhere you send us. 17-18If the Lord our God will help you as he helped Moses, and if you are strong and brave, we will obey you as we obeyed Moses. We'll even put to death anyone who rebels against you or refuses to obey you.
translation_text:
Joosuwa fōō ti-Dindaan tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi yil
1Ti-Dindaan tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi kúm boonee, ní ti-Dindaan tùkū Nuuni jipɔɔn Joosuwa un nìn bí Mooyiisi cee ki tútúǹ-uee yii: 2«M-tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi kpíì dee. Kɔŋkɔnnee, yīkì sii nì samaa nee kɔkɔ ní dùtī Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ŋun bí nee kí kɔ́ kitiŋ kin m làá dūu tīī Isirayeel yabee. 3M làá dū laakin kamaa ní ni-taaŋi yaa tāāyee kí tīī-ni kii m nín nìn tùkū Mooyiisi yii m làá ŋá puee. 4Ni-tiŋki di làá nīn sá kí yòon̄ kuteeu ŋgiil pú kí cáá sāā Leebanɔn jooŋŋi, kí yòon̄ kí nīn cá dimɔɔkpaandi ŋgan pú, an dàkà yii Eefiraati mɔɔl, ní kí yòon̄ Eeti yab tiŋki kɔkɔ ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú kí tin cáá sāā Meediiteeranee tiŋkuu ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú. 5A-maŋfal wiiŋyi kɔkɔ kí tin cáá sāā a-kúmee, ubɔ kpá kí já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ-si. M nín nìn bí Mooyiisi cee puee, míǹ ní m làá nīn bí si mun cee. Maa làá yàntī-si, kaa làá fá-si mun. 6Pɔ́ɔǹ a-ba kí ká dipɔbil, kun puee sii di làá dū kitiŋ kin m pōoǹ dinibul nee naanjab yii m làá tīī bi-naantiibee kí tīī-bi. 7Sii dee ká dipɔbil kí taa fàŋkì báà tiba, kí nīn pée nóó Mara un m-tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi yóoǹ-see deedee, kí taa yìntīǹ an marau gbanti báà fiii. A yaa ŋá mimmee tin kɔkɔ ní a làá ŋée làá nīn còom̄ tiŋan ní ki tīī-si. 8Á yàntī kugbɔŋu kun poon bi ŋmàn̄ Mara ki ŋée ń nīn bí ki kɔ́ĺ-si. Á nīn pée kàaǹ-ku ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu, án nín làá ŋá pu á ŋmā kí nīn ŋáań tikɔkɔ ki nóó nì tibɔti tin bi ŋmàn̄ ku-poonee. A yaa ŋáań mimmee ní a làá ŋmā kí bɔ́ntí a-sàmbiyaamu ní án bútí-si á ŋmā kí ŋá tin kɔkɔ a là kí ŋée. 9Maa kpáafì-si yii á ká dipɔbil kí taa fàŋkì báà tibaaa? Taa yàntī tifaandi ń cúú-si, kí taa yàntī a-wunti ń yɔ̀tī, kun puee man a-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu làá nīn bí a-cee laakin kamaa ní a làá cùee!»
Joosuwa bɔ́ntì kí dùtī Jɔɔdan buŋŋu
10Niinee ní Joosuwa tīī Isirayeel yab tindaŋkpilib mara nee yii: 11«Ní yìim̀maan dinaapaal kɔkɔ pu kí bāakì tibɔti nee kí tùkù samaa kɔkɔ. Ní lì yii: <Ní bɔ́ntímaan tijin kí yóoń, kun puee kí yòon̄ díǹ kí tin sāā iwiin itee, ni làá dùtī Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ŋun dɔ̄ nee kí cùú já kí fōō kitiŋ kin ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu tīī-ni, kí nīn sá ni-yakee.>» 12Boonee ní Joosuwa sòon̄ nì Rubeen naakookun yab, nì Gaadi naakookun yab, nì Manasee naakooku dijandi diba yab ki bí-bi yii: 13«Ní téetímaan mara un ti-Dindaan tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi nìn tīī-nee. U nìn lī yii: <Ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu tīī-ni diŋuŋfil ní kitiŋ kin u tīī-ni nee poon.> 14An puee, yàntīmaan ni-nimpoobi nì ni-biyaamu nì ni-waŋkuti ń gbíntí kitiŋ kin Mooyiisi tīī-ni Jɔɔdan buŋgbandi din bí doo pú nee. Nimbi bibaatandambi kɔkɔ ń bóob́ dikɔ̀ndi kí lìntī ni-nabiyaamu nyɔkɔpu kí cùú tūtuǹ-bi 15bí já kí tin cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋun ní ni-Nimbɔtiu làá dāá tīī-bi diŋuŋfil kii u nín tīī ni mun diŋuŋfil puee, ní bi mun ń ŋmā kí fōō kitiŋ kin ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu tīī-bee. Míǹ boonee ní ní gítiń kí dāá kàl̄ ni-tiŋki kin ti-Dindaan tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi tīī-ni Jɔɔdan buŋgbandi din bí doo pú nee, an dàkà yii dibuŋgbándi din bí ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú nee.»
16Ní bi bí Joosuwa yii: «Ti kíí ki làá ŋá tin kɔkɔ a yaa bí yii tí ŋée. Laakin ní a yaa pée tú-tee, ti làá cù. 17Kii ti nín nìn pée pílifiǹ Mooyiisi tikɔkɔ poon puee, míǹ mbaantiim ní ti làá nīn tí pílifíǹ sii mun. Ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu ń nīn bí a-cee kii u nín nìn bí Mooyiisi cee puee. 18Unil un kamaa yaa ŋèen̄ nì a-marab, ki yíì kaa pílifì a-nyɔkɔ kí ŋá a nín lī puee, bí kpɔ̀ udaan! Siiyee, pɔ́ɔǹ a-ba kí ká dipɔbil!»

english_text:
Rahab Helps the Israelite Spies
1 Joshua chose two men as spies and sent them from their camp at Acacia with these instructions: “Go across the river and find out as much as you can about the whole region, especially about the town of Jericho.”
The two spies left the Israelite camp at Acacia and went to Jericho, where they decided to spend the night at the house of a prostitute named Rahab.
2But someone found out about them and told the king of Jericho, “Some Israelite men came here tonight, and they are spies.” 3-7So the king sent soldiers to Rahab's house to arrest the spies.
Meanwhile, Rahab had taken the men up to the flat roof of her house and had hidden them under some piles of flax plants that she had put there to dry.
The soldiers came to her door and demanded, “Let us have the men who are staying at your house. They are spies.”
She answered, “Some men did come to my house, but I didn't know where they had come from. They left about sunset, just before it was time to close the town gate. I don't know where they were going, but if you hurry, maybe you can catch them.”
The guards at the town gate let the soldiers leave Jericho, but they closed the gate again as soon as the soldiers went through. Then the soldiers headed toward the Jordan River to look for the spies at the place where people cross the river.
8Rahab went back up to her roof. The spies were still awake, so she told them:
9I know that the Lord has given Israel this land. Everyone shakes with fear because of you. 10 We heard how the Lord dried up the Red Sea so you could leave Egypt. And we heard how you destroyed Sihon and Og, those two Amorite kings east of the Jordan River. 11We know that the Lord your God rules heaven and earth, and we've lost our courage and our will to fight.
12Please promise me in the Lord's name that you will be as kind to my family as I have been to you. Do something to show 13that you won't let your people kill my father and mother and my brothers and sisters and their families.
14“Rahab,” the spies answered, “if you keep quiet about what we're doing, we promise to be kind to you when the Lord gives us this land. We pray that the Lord will kill us if we don't keep our promise!”
15Rahab's house was built into the town wall, and one of the windows in her house faced outside the wall. She gave the spies a rope, showed them the window, and said, “Use this rope to let yourselves down to the ground outside the wall. 16Then hide in the hills. The men who are looking for you won't be able to find you there. They'll give up and come back after a few days, and you can be on your way.”
17-20The spies said:
You made us promise to let you and your family live. We will keep our promise, but you can't tell anyone why we were here. You must tie this red rope on your window when we attack, and your father and mother, your brothers, and everyone else in your family must be here with you. We'll take the blame if anyone who stays in this house gets hurt. But anyone who leaves your house will be killed, and it won't be our fault.
21“I'll do exactly what you said,” Rahab promised. Then she sent them on their way and tied the red rope to the window.
22The spies hid in the hills for three days while the king's soldiers looked for them along the roads. As soon as the soldiers gave up and returned to Jericho, 23the two spies went down into the Jordan valley and crossed the river. They reported to Joshua and told him everything that had happened. 24“We're sure the Lord has given us the whole country,” they said. “The people there shake with fear every time they think of us.”
translation_text:
Joosuwa tú bicɔŋkiliibi bili Jeeriikoo tiŋkin
1Isirayeel yab dáá bí Siitiim tiŋkin ní Nuuni jipɔɔn Joosuwa lēē binib bili ki tú dibalin ki bí-bi yii: «Ní cùmaan kí yìiǹ kí cɔ̄ŋkì kí béé Jeeriikoo tiŋki kɔkɔ.» Binibee bàn̄ee ní ki kɔ́ kinimpulaakpaai kiba dumpu ki dōoǹ. Bi yíì kinimpulaakpaai gbanti yii Rakaab. 2Ní binib cūtìi nyá Jeeriikoo bɔtiu kuŋaŋŋaau yii: «Kpèè, Isirayeel yab biba kɔ́nní ti-tiŋki pu doo kunyeeu nee kí yìiǹ kí cɔ̄ŋkì kí béé kitiŋ!» 3Ní Jeeriikoo bɔtiu tú bi tùkū Rakaab yii: «Nyāntiń binib bin dɔ́miń ki kɔ́ a-dumpuee kí tīī-ti, kun puee bi dɔ́miń kí cɔ̄ŋkì kí béé kitiŋ nee filiŋfeetii kɔkɔ ní.» 4Rakaab nìn cáá bininjabee liitil ki bál̀ ní ki kíí bin ubɔti túnnée yii: «Tiŋman, bininjabee lafun dɔ́miń m-cee, ama maa nyí laakin bi nyánnée. 5An nín bɔ̄ntì bi làá pìin̄ kitiŋ punyɔkɔkee ní binib gbanti nyáń, maa nyí laakin bi búntèe. Ní jàmaan bi-boon malaa, ni làá cúú-bi nsanni!»
6Ibaamɔnee Rakaab nìn cáá bininjabee ki jɔ́ntiǹ u-diiku yilpu laakin bi bɔ̀b̄ee, ki dū-bi ki bál̀ tiŋmiil kpaŋkpaatii in u fùkū ki díntì kudii yilpuee taapu. 7Ní ubɔti naacimbee kùl̄ ki páaǹ bininjab bilee boon, ki túĺ Jɔɔdan buŋŋu watil pú laakin kaa nyóò binib còom̄ ki dùtēe. Bi nyáń ki búntèe ní bi dū kitiŋ punyɔkɔki ki pīiǹ. 8Kí wàatī Rakaab nicambi bin u bál̀ee ń dòon̄ee, ní u nín jɔ́ḿ bi-cee kudii yilpu. 9U bàn̄ee ní ki bí-bi yii: «M nyí yii ti-Dindaan dū kitiŋ nee ki ŋá ni-ŋaan. Ni yāntì dinyoondi kɔ́-ti an kaa cáá bí lì. Ni-puee, tifaandi kɔ́ kitiŋ nee nib kɔkɔ bi nyùn̄ ŋkpatim. 10Di sá yii ti gbìl̄ ti-Dindaan nín yāntì Tikati mɔɔl nyim fóotì ni-nimbiin ni dūtì ŋyunti ŋun ni nìn nyáń Eejipiti tiŋkinee. Ti gíti gbìl̄ tin ní ni ŋá Amɔɔr yab bɔtiibi liitil Siiwɔn nì Ɔɔgi bin bí Jɔɔdan buŋŋu lapu puee, nì ni nín nāaǹ bibɔtiibi gbanti liitil nì bi-wanti pílpil puee. 11Ti nín gbìl̄ mimmee, tifaandi kɔ́-ti ní ti nyùn̄ ŋkpatim ní báà unil kaa ti cáá dipɔbil kí ŋmā kí yūĺ ni-nimbiin kí jáǹ-ni. Tiŋman pu, ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu di sá Unimbɔti un bí yilpu fɔ́ŋŋŋee ní ki sá Unimbɔti kitiŋ pu taapu doo mun. 12Kɔŋkɔnnee ní pùtī ti-Dindaan yii m nín ŋá-ni tiniti tin nee, ni mun làá ŋá m-baa dicaŋkun yab tiniti kí téeǹ, ní kí tīī-mi kudaaŋŋu yii ni làá lafun ŋá míǹ. 13Ní yàntī m-baa nì m-na nì m-niijab nì m-mambi nì m-naalib nì bi-dicaŋŋi nib kɔkɔ ń nīn bí dimaŋfalin. Ní taa yàntī bí kpɔ̀-ti». 14Ní bininjabee kíí-u yii: «Ti kíí kí kpú nimbi yil pu, sii dee taa pée yàntī ti-bɔti nee ń nyā ti nì si kansikin ubɔ ń gbìl̄-tì! Ti-Dindaan yaa láa yāntì kitiŋ nee kɔ́ ti-ŋaanee, ti làá dāá ŋá-si tiniti kí dàkà-si ti-baamɔŋyi.»
15Niinee Rakaab dū ŋŋmii ki tɔ́ tɔkɔla boon pú ní bininjabee dī ki kpákatì taapu, kitiŋ boon. Di sá yii kitiŋ gundi pu ní bi nìn máń kudii kun Rakaab kóòyee ki tɔ́kɔǹ. 16Bi làá nīn nyēēyee ní Rakaab kpáafì-bi yii: «Ní túĺmaan dijool watil pú bin bíi jì kí cúú-nee ń taa ká-ni. Ní gbíntí dijool pu niin kí báĺ iwiin ita kí nīn cí binib gbanti ń fàtīí gítiń, boonee ní nín nìkī ni-saŋŋu kí nīn cá.» 17Ní bininjab bilee bí-u yii: «Timbi làá ŋúb́ dipoondi din a yāntì ti pūtì ki pōoǹ-see. 18Ama kpèè, ŋwiin ŋun a yaa láa ká ti kɔ́nní kitiŋinee, á dāá dū gulfaman ŋmiiŋu nee kí kúĺ kí lúntí tɔkɔla un a yāntì ti dī ki nyáń nee. Ŋyunti gbantee, á dāá kóoǹ a-baa nì a-na nì a-nabiyaamu nì a-baa dicaŋkun yab kɔkɔ kí kpāfì dicilpu a-dumpu. 19Un kamaa yaa láa pée nyáń mmɔŋkee, udaan di dāa yì úǹ u-ba kpuulool, an kaa dāa sá timbi bɔti. Ama bi yaa láa pée gbēē unil un kamaa bí a-dumpuee, timbi di dāa yì udaan kpuulool. 20Ama a yaa dū ti-bɔti nee ki máafì binibee, taa làá ti ŋúb́ dipoondi din a yāntì ti pūtì ki pōoǹ-see». 21Ní Rakaab kíí-bi yii: «Ni nín lī puee, án ŋá míǹ!» U lī mimmee ní ki pú-bi nsan bi nín cá, ní u nyàab̄ gulfaman ŋmiiŋu ki dūu kúĺ ki lúntì tɔkɔla pu. 22Ní bininjab bilee nín cá dijool pu ki cūtìi bál̀ niin iwiin ita. Ubɔti naacimbi bin bíi jì kí cúú-bee nyàab̄-bi didandi pu ki gīī kaa ká-bee, ní ki fātìi nín gítí. 23Niinee ní bininjabee liitil kpákatì dijool, ki dūtì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ki cūtì Nuuni jipɔɔn Joosuwa cee ní ki dū bi nín bàn̄ tin jítèe kɔkɔ ki máafì-u. 24Bi bí Joosuwa yii: «Tiŋman pu, ti-Dindaan lafun dū kitiŋee kɔkɔ ki ŋá ti-ŋaan ní. Di sá yii timbi puee, tifaandi kɔ́ ki-nib kɔkɔ ní bi nyùn̄ ŋkpatim!»

english_text:
Israel Crosses the Jordan River
1Early the next morning, Joshua and the Israelites packed up and left Acacia. They went to the Jordan River and camped there that night. 2Two days later their leaders went through the camp, 3-4shouting, “When you see some of the priests carrying the sacred chest, you'll know it is time to cross to the other side. You've never been there before, and you won't know the way, unless you follow the chest. But don't get too close! Stay about a kilometer back.”
5Joshua told the people, “Make yourselves acceptable to worship the Lord, because he is going to do some amazing things for us.”
6Then Joshua turned to the priests and said, “Take the chest and cross the Jordan River ahead of us.” So the priests picked up the chest by its carrying poles and went on ahead.
7The Lord told Joshua, “Beginning today I will show the people that you are their leader, and they will know that I am helping you as I helped Moses. 8Now, tell the priests who are carrying the chest to go a little way into the river and stand there.”
9Joshua spoke to the people:
Come here and listen to what the Lord our God said he will do! 10The Canaanites, the Hittites, the Hivites, the Perizzites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, and the Jebusites control the land on the other side of the river. But the living God will be with you and will force them out of the land when you attack. And now, God is going to prove that he's powerful enough to force them out. 11-13Just watch the sacred chest that belongs to the Lord, the ruler of the whole earth. As soon as the priests carrying the chest step into the Jordan, the water will stop flowing and pile up as if someone had built a dam across the river.
The Lord has also said that each of the twelve tribes should choose one man to represent it.
14The Israelites packed up and left camp. The priests carrying the chest walked in front, 15until they came to the Jordan River. The water in the river had risen over its banks, as it often does in springtime. But as soon as the feet of the priests touched the water, 16-17the river stopped flowing, and the water started piling up at the town of Adam near Zarethan. No water flowed toward the Dead Sea, and the priests stood in the middle of the dry riverbed near Jericho while everyone else crossed over.
translation_text:
Isirayeel yab dūtì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu
1Kutaa wúntì kutaafaau pɔ̀lpɔlee ní Joosuwa yíkì Siitiim kaaŋun, u nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ, ní bi cōom̀ ki tin bàn̄ Jɔɔdan buŋgbandi. Bi bàn̄ niinee ní ki gbíntì ki kāl̀ kí cīití ŋwiin ŋun bi làá dùtī mbunee. 2Iwiin ita boonee ní Isirayeel yab tindaŋkpilib yìin̄ ki māntì dinaapaal kɔkɔ poon, 3ki báakì ki tùkū binib yii: «Ni yaa láa pée ká Leefii naantiibi bisaraaŋaliibi yōoǹ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu Poondi dakaau ki būkuǹee, ní dāá nyā dinaapaalin kí páań bi-boon. 4Mimmee ni làá béé nsan ŋun ní ni máaǹ kí nóóyee, kun puee naa láá pée cōom̀ nsan nee pu ki ká. Ama ní yàntī mpaan ń nīn dɔ̄ ni nì Dipoondi dakaau kansikin kí bà kii ditaŋkpal diba, kí taa nín̄ pìl̄-u tikpil.»
5Ní Joosuwa tùkū samaa yii: «Ní bɔ́ntímaan ni-ba kí nīn bí circir, kun puee fool ti-Dindaan làá fu ŋá maamaaci tuuŋŋi ni-kansikin.» 6Míǹ boonee ní Joosuwa bí bisaraaŋaliibi yii: «Yòom̄maan Dipoondi dakaau kí lìntī samaa nyɔkɔpu!» Ní bi yōoǹ Dipoondi dakaau ki līntì samaa nyɔkɔpu.
7Ní ti-Dindaan tùkū Joosuwa yii: «Díǹ wiiŋŋu nee ní m làá kíĺ kí yàntī á nyā diyindi Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nimbiin ní bí béé yii m làá nīn bí a-cee kii m nín nìn bí Mooyiisi cee puee. 8Tùkù bisaraaŋaliibi bin tú Dipoondi dakaauee yii bi yaa cōom̀ ki bàn̄ Jɔɔdan buŋŋuee, bí kɔ́ poon kí yūĺ nnyimin.» 9Niinee ní Joosuwa bí Isirayeel yab yii: «Ní sútiḿmaan doo kí dāá pīlifì tibɔti tin ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu cáá ki làá sòoǹee!» 10Bi kóoǹní ki kpáfèe ní Joosuwa bí-bi yii: «Tin bí nee di làá yàntī ní béé yii Unimbɔti un bí dimaŋfalinee bí ni-kansikin ní ki làá lafun jà Kanaan yab nì Eeti yab nì Eefi yab nì Peeriisi yab nì Giirgaasi yab nì Amɔɔr yab nì Jeebusi yab kí wàatī-ni. 11Kpèèmaan, duulinya kɔkɔ Dindaan Poondi dakaau làá lìntī ni-nyɔkɔpu kí kɔ́ Jɔɔdan buŋŋun ní nee. 12Kɔŋkɔnnee, ní lēēmaan Isirayeel naakɔti poon binib saalaa nì bili, kunaakoou kamaa unil ubɔ ubɔ. 13Bisaraaŋaliibi bin bùkū ti-Dindaan, duulinya kɔkɔ Dindaan Poondi dakaauee dāa pée lì yii bi dù bi-tafati kí gbēē Jɔɔdan nyimee, nnyim min pùubìń yilpu puee làá gbèen̄ kaa làá ti pùub̀, ní kí kóoǹ kí ŋá dinyiŋgundi.»
14Ní Isirayeel yab nyáń bi-tantibin kí dùtī Jɔɔdan buŋŋu, ní bisaraaŋaliibi bùkū Dipoondi dakaau ki līī samaa nyɔkɔpu. 15An nìn sá ŋyunti ŋun bi cēē tikpaajinee ní. Dibindi poonee, ŋyunti gbanti ní Jɔɔdan buŋŋu gbéè kí páań. Bisaraaŋaliibi bin bùkū Dipoondi dakaauee nín bàn̄ Jɔɔdan buŋgbandi ki tin pée dùŋfī bi-taaŋi kí gbēē nnyimee, 16nnyim min pùubìń yilpu puee síl̀ kaa ti bíi pùubìń, ní ki kóoǹ ki ŋá dinyiŋgundi, doooo kitiŋ kin bi yíì yii Adam kì pìlīǹ Saartan tiŋkee. Ní nnyim min pùub̀ taapu pu ki sìntī Arabaa teeku mɔɔl din bi gíti yíì yii Ŋyaam mɔɔlee watil púee, míǹ púntìi pùub̄ ki búntì. Ní samaa dūtì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu, Jeeriikoo tiŋki nyɔkɔpu. 17Bisaraaŋaliibi bin bùkū ti-Dindaan Poondi dakaauee pée sí Jɔɔdan buŋŋu kansikin ŋkulimmi, ní Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ dāa dūtì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ŋkulimmi ki dóò.

english_text:
The People Set Up a Monument
1After Israel had crossed the Jordan, the Lord said to Joshua:
2-3Tell one man from each of the twelve tribes to pick up a large rock from where the priests are standing. Then tell the men to set up those rocks as a monument at the place where you camp tonight.
4Joshua chose twelve men; then he called them together 5and said:
Go to the middle of the riverbed where the sacred chest is, and pick up a large rock. Carry it on your shoulder to our camp. There are twelve of you, so there will be one rock for each tribe. 6-7Someday your children will ask, “Why are these rocks here?” Then you can tell them how the water stopped flowing when the chest was being carried across the river. These rocks will always remind our people of what happened here today.
8The men followed the instructions that the Lord had given Joshua. They picked up twelve rocks, one for each tribe, and carried them to the camp, where they put them down.
9Joshua set up a monument next to the place where the priests were standing. This monument was also made of twelve large rocks, and it is still there in the middle of the river.
The People of Israel Set Up Camp at Gilgal
10-13The army got ready for battle and crossed the Jordan with everyone else. They marched quickly past the sacred chest and into the desert near Jericho. Forty thousand soldiers from the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh led the way, as Moses had ordered.
The priests stayed right where they were until the people had followed the orders that the Lord had given Moses and Joshua. Then they watched as the priests carried the chest the rest of the way across.
14-18“Joshua,” the Lord said, “tell the priests to come up from the Jordan and bring the chest with them.” So Joshua went over to the priests and told them what the Lord had said. And as soon as the priests carried the chest past the highest place that the floodwaters of the Jordan had reached, the river flooded its banks again.
That's how the Lord showed the Israelites that Joshua was their leader. For the rest of Joshua's life, they respected him as they had respected Moses.
19It was the tenth day of the first month of the year when Israel crossed the Jordan River. They set up camp at Gilgal, which was east of the land controlled by Jericho. 20The men who had carried the twelve rocks from the Jordan brought them to Joshua, and they made them into a monument. 21Then Joshua told the people:
Years from now your children will ask you why these rocks are here. 22-23Tell them, “The Lord our God dried up the Jordan River so we could walk across. He did the same thing here for us that he did for our people at the Red Sea, 24because he wants everyone on earth to know how powerful he is. And he wants us to worship only him.”
translation_text:
Ataŋkpee saalaa nì ali ŋin bi làá nīn cáa téetée
1Ŋyunti ŋun samaa kɔkɔ dūtì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ki dóòyee, ní ti-Dindaan bí Joosuwa yii: 2«Lēē samaa kansikin binib saalaa nì bili, kunaakoou kamaa poon unil ubɔ ubɔ, 3kí tùkù-bi yii: <Ní kɔ́maan kí tòò ataŋkpee saalaa nì ali Jɔɔdan buŋŋu kansikin, dibɔbil din bisaraaŋaliibi yúl̀ee. Ní kpáaǹ-ŋi kí cáá bíĺ laakin ni làá dòon̄ kunyeeu neeyee.>» 4Niinee ní Joosuwa yíiń binib saalaa nì bili bin u yāntì Isirayeel yab lēē bi-kansikinee, kunaakoou kamaa poon unil ubɔ ubɔee ki kpáfì, 5ní ki bí-bi yii: «Ní lìntīmaan ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu Poondi dakaau nyɔkɔpu kí kɔ́ Jɔɔdan buŋŋu kansikin, ní báà ŋma ń yòon̄ ditaŋkpal diba diba kí dūú bùkun̄ u-gbigbil pu, kí nóó nì Isirayeel yab naakɔti nyɔkɔm nín sá puee. 6An taŋkpeeŋee di làá nīn sá-ni kudaaŋŋu. Fool boon ni-biyaamu yaa láa bālifì-ni yii ba ní ataŋkpee nee sá ki tīī-nee, 7ní dāá kíí-bi yii: <Bi nín nìn túǹ ti-Dindaan Poondi dakaau ki dūtì Jɔɔdan buŋŋuee, mi-nyim nìn cúu yākatì mili ní. Ŋyunti ŋun bi nìn bíi dùtī nì Dipoondi dakaauee, nnyim nìn cúu yākatì ní bi jítì. An puee, ataŋkpee nee sá kí nīn téetí Isirayeel yab an bɔti ní kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaan.>»
8Ní Isirayeel yab lafun ŋá kii Joosuwa nín yóoǹ-bi yii bí ŋá puee. Bi nìn lēē ataŋkpee saalaa nì ali Jɔɔdan buŋŋu kansikin, kunaakoou kamaa ditaŋkpal diba, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tùkū Joosuwa yii bí ŋá puee, ní ki cáa cūnnì ki bíl̀ laakin bi nìn dōoǹ kunyeeu gbantee. 9Joosuwa nìn gíti yāntì bi tōō ataŋkpee saalaa nì ali aba mun ki cóoǹ Jɔɔdan buŋŋu kansikin, laakin bisaraaŋaliibi bin nìn tú Dipoondi dakaauee nìn yúl̀ee. Ataŋkpee gbanti dáá gbíntìi bí niin ki dāa sāā díǹ.
10Bisaraaŋaliibi bin nìn tú Dipoondi dakaauee nìn gbíntìi yú Jɔɔdan buŋŋu kansikin míǹ ní tin kɔkɔ ti-Dindaan yāntì Joosuwa tùkū Isirayeel yabee ŋá kii Mooyiisi nín nìn kpáafì Joosuwa yii ú ŋá puee. Boonee ní samaa kɔkɔ ŋá malaa ki dūtì. 11Binib kɔkɔ nín dāa pée dūtì ki dóòyee ní bisaraaŋaliibi kpáaǹ ti-Dindaan Poondi dakaau ki dūtì ní ki jítìi tí līntì samaa nyɔkɔpu. 12Rubeen nì Gaadi naakɔti yab, nì Manasee naakooku yab dijandi diba nìn līntì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nyɔkɔpu, ki bóob́ dikɔ̀ndi, kii Mooyiisi nín nìn kpáafì-bi yii bí ŋá puee. 13Bijanjaliibi kii binib kutukub imuŋku ili nyɔkɔm di nìn dūtì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu, ki ŋúb́ tijanjawan ki còom̄ ti-Dindaan Poondi dakaau nimbiin ki cá Jeeriikoo tantakal watil pú kí cùú já kujaau. 14Ŋwiin gbantee, ti-Dindaan nìn yāntì Joosuwa nyáń diyindi tikpil Isirayeel yab nimbiin, ní bi nìn kíǹ ki tɔ́-u kii bi nín nìn tɔ́ Mooyiisi puee u-maŋfal wiiŋyi kɔkɔ poon.
15Boonee ti-Dindaan bí Joosuwa yii: 16«Tùkù bisaraaŋaliibi bin tú ti-Dindaan Poondi dakaauee yii bí nyānní Jɔɔdan buŋŋu poon.» 17Ní Joosuwa bí bisaraaŋaliibee yii: «Ní nyānnímaan Jɔɔdan buŋŋu poon!» 18Ŋyunti ŋun bisaraaŋaliibi bin tú ti-Dindaan Poondi dakaauee nyáń Jɔɔdan buŋŋunee, bi-tafati tin pée gbèetī kitiŋkuliŋŋee ní Jɔɔdan nyim fātìi kíĺ ki bíi pùub̀ kii mi nín pée kpààa pùub̀ puee, ní ki gbí ki bàn̄ abuŋgbán liitil. 19Uŋmapeepeekaa poon iwiin saalaa dal ní Isirayeel yab dūtì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ní ki cūtìi kāl̀ laakin bi yíì yii Giilgaal, an bí Jeeriikoo tiŋki ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee.
20Giilgaal niin ní Joosuwa yāntì bi cóoǹ ataŋkpee ŋin bi kɔ́ Jɔɔdan buŋŋun ki tōōyee. 21Bi cóoǹ ki dóòyee ní u tùkū Isirayeel yab yii: «Fool boon ni-biyaamu yaa láa bālifì nimbi bibaatiibi yii ba taŋkpeeŋi sèéyee, 22ní dāá lēē taapu kí tùkù-bi yii: <Isirayeel yab nìn dūtì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ŋun dɔ̄ nee nì atakulim ní.> 23Di sá yii ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu yāntì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu nyim fóotì ni-nimbiin ní ni-kɔkɔ dūtì kii úǹ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nín nìn yāntì Tikati mɔɔl nyim fóotì timbi nimbiin ki tin sāā ŋyunti ŋun ti-kɔ dūtèe. 24U ŋá míǹ anibul ŋin bí kitiŋ puee kɔkɔ ń béé yii úǹ ti-Dindaan pɔŋŋu di sá mpɔŋkpaan, ní nimbi ń nīn fàŋkí-u kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaan!»

english_text:
1The Amorite kings west of the Jordan River and the Canaanite kings along the Mediterranean Sea lost their courage and their will to fight, when they heard how the Lord had dried up the Jordan River to let Israel go across.
Israel Gets Ready To Celebrate Passover
2While Israel was camped at Gilgal, the Lord said, “Joshua, make some flint knives and circumcise the rest of the Israelite men and boys.”
3Joshua made the knives, then circumcised those men and boys at Haaraloth Hill. 4-7 This had to be done, because none of Israel's baby boys had been circumcised during the 40 years that Israel had wandered through the desert after leaving Egypt.
And why had they wandered for 40 years? It was because right after they left Egypt, the men in the army had disobeyed the Lord. And the Lord had said, “None of you men will ever live to see the land that I promised Israel. It is a land rich with milk and honey, and someday your children will live there, but not before you die here in the desert.”
8Everyone who had been circumcised needed time to heal, and they stayed in camp.
9The Lord told Joshua, “It was a disgrace for my people to be slaves in Egypt, but now I have taken away that disgrace.” So the Israelites named the place Gilgal, and it still has that name.
10 Israel continued to camp at Gilgal in the desert near Jericho, and on the fourteenth day of the same month, they celebrated Passover.
11-12 The next day, God stopped sending the Israelites manna to eat each morning, and they started eating food grown in the land of Canaan. They ate roasted grain and thin bread made of the barley they had gathered from nearby fields.
Israel Captures Jericho
13One day, Joshua was near Jericho when he saw a man standing some distance in front of him. The man was holding a sword, so Joshua walked up to him and asked, “Are you on our side or on our enemies' side?”
14“Neither,” he answered. “I am here because I am the commander of the Lord's army.”
Joshua fell to his knees and bowed down to the ground. “I am your servant,” he said. “Tell me what to do.”
15“Take off your sandals,” the commander answered. “This is a holy place.”
So Joshua took off his sandals.
translation_text:
1 Amɔɔr yab bin kóò Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki púee bɔtiibi, nì Kanaan yab bin kóò ki pìlīǹ tiŋkuee bɔtiibi nìn gbìl̄ yii ti-Dindaan yāntì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu nyim fóotì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ ŋúń ki dūtì. Niinee bi-pɔbiliŋ bíil̀, ní Isirayeel yab puee, bi nyùn̄ ŋkpatim.
Bi gíí Isirayeel yab bininjab kɔkɔ Giilgaal
2Ŋyunti gbantee ní ti-Dindaan tùkū Joosuwa yii: «Kpítí ntaŋkpajimu kí gíí Isirayeel yab bininjab bin dáá sá binipɔmbee akpancan.» 3Ní Joosuwa kpítì ntaŋkpajimu ki gíí Isirayeel yab bininjab bin dáá sá binipɔmbee kɔkɔ akpancan. Kí yòon̄ yaadal ní bi kíǹ ki yíì niin yii Giibeeyaati Aralɔti. 4Kun yì-tì ní Joosuwa dāa gífí Isirayeel binipɔmbee sèé. Isirayeel nibul nín nìn nyánní Eejipiti tiŋkinee, bininjab bin kɔkɔ nìn bàn̄ kí cù kujaauee nìn kpíì nsanni, kuteeun. 5Bin nìn yíkìń Eejipiti tiŋkinee kɔkɔ nìn pée gíí ní, ama ní mbininjabiyaamu mun bi dāa màl̄ nsanni kuteeunee, múǹ kaa gíí. 6Di sá yii Isirayeel yab nìn gbíntì kuteeun ki bí ki yìiǹ míǹ ki tin sāā abin imuŋku ili, ní bi-kansikin bin nìn nyáń Eejipiti tiŋkin ki nìn bàn̄ kí cù kujaauee kɔkɔ dāa kpíì. Kun yì-tì bi nìn kpíì mimmee di sá yii baa nìn pílifì ti-Dindaan nyɔkɔ, ní ti-Dindaan nìn pūtì yii waa làá yàntī bí ká kitiŋ kin poon nnaabiim nì tisiil còol̀ u nìn pōoǹ bi-naanjab yii u làá dūú tīī-tee. 7Bi-jipɔmbi di yíkì ki fōō bi-yil. Bi-jipɔmbi gbanti ní Joosuwa nìn gíí akpancan, kun puee baa nìn gíiń-bi nsanni. 8Bi gíí-bi míǹ ki dóòyee ní samaa kɔkɔ gbíntì dinaapaal pu niin ki kāl̀ áli ibuun dāa kpíì. 9Ní ti-Dindaan bí Joosuwa yii: «Díǹ wiiŋŋu nee, m cúú Eejipiti tiŋki cooi in nìn bí ni-puee ki lēē.» An di yì-tì ní bi pú mpaan gbanti diyindi yii Giilgaal, ní bi dáá gbíntìi yíì-ŋu míǹ ki dāa sāā díǹ.
Dilákatil jiŋaaliu upeepeekaa un bi jíń Kanaaŋyee
10Isirayeel yab nìn kāl̀ Giilgaal niin, Jeeriikoo tantakalin ní ki jíń Dilákatil jiŋaaliu uŋmal poon ŋwiin ŋubɔ kpá saalku dal kujoou. 11Kutaa wúntèe ní bi kíĺ kitiŋ gbanti jinti dijil. Bi nìn púĺ kpɔnɔb bin baa ŋá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee nì bilee fiŋyi ki ŋmɔ́. 12Ŋwiin ŋun bi jíń an jintee ní maana gbēeǹ kaa ti nyēeń kutaa pu ki lítiń. Dibindi gbanti ní Isirayeel yab kíĺ ki bíi jīǹ tijin tin lòoǹ Kanaan tiŋki puee.
Joosuwa nì ti-Dindaan janjakitil kpiliu
13Dalba Joosuwa nìn bí Jeeriikoo tiŋki caŋin. U dāa pée yáatèe ní ki ká uninja ubɔ yú u-nyɔkɔpu, ki ŋúb́ njicál u-ŋaan. Joosuwa cōom̀ ki cūtì u-cee ní ki bālifì-u yii: «Sii sá ti-yɔu ubɔ naaa, a sá ti-nannanliu ubɔ ní?» 14Ní unaaciinee kíí Joosuwa yii: «Aayee, maa sá bi-kansikin báà ubɔ! Man di sá ti-Dindaan janjakitil kpiliu. Kɔŋkɔnnee ní m bāań!» Niinee ní Joosuwa tātìi dōoǹ dicincibil ki jáam̀-u ní ki bí-u yii: «M-dindaan, ba ní a là yii man a-tɔntɔnliu ń ŋá ní?» 15Ní ti-Dindaan janjakitil kpiliuee bí Joosuwa yii: «Cúú a-naatakaŋ kí tákatí, kun puee laakin a yú nee sá circir paaŋŋu pu ní.» Ní Joosuwa ŋá min ní u tùkū-u yii ú ŋée.

english_text:
1Meanwhile, the people of Jericho had been locking the gates in their town wall because they were afraid of the Israelites. No one could go out or come in.
2-3The Lord said to Joshua:
With my help, you and your army will defeat the king of Jericho and his army, and you will capture the town. Here is how to do it: March slowly around Jericho once a day for six days. 4Take along the sacred chest and tell seven priests to walk in front of it, carrying trumpets.
But on the seventh day, march slowly around the town seven times while the priests blow their trumpets. 5Then the priests will blast on their trumpets, and everyone else will shout. The wall will fall down, and your soldiers can go straight in from every side.
6Joshua called the priests together and said, “Take the chest and tell seven priests to carry trumpets and march ahead of it.”
7-10Next, he gave the army their orders: “March slowly around Jericho. A few of you will go ahead of the chest to guard it, but most of you will follow it. Don't shout the battle cry or yell or even talk until the day I tell you to. Then let out a shout!”
As soon as Joshua finished giving the orders, the army started marching. One group of soldiers led the way, with seven priests marching behind them and blowing trumpets. Then came the priests carrying the chest, followed by the rest of the soldiers. 11They obeyed Joshua's orders and carried the chest once around the town before returning to camp for the night.
12-14Early the next morning, Joshua and everyone else started marching around Jericho in the same order as the day before. One group of soldiers was in front, followed by the seven priests with trumpets and the priests who carried the chest. The rest of the army came next. The seven priests blew their trumpets while everyone marched slowly around Jericho and back to camp. They did this once a day for six days.
15On the seventh day, the army got up at daybreak. They marched slowly around Jericho the same as they had done for the past six days, except on this day they went around seven times. 16Then the priests blew the trumpets, and Joshua yelled:
Get ready to shout! The Lord will let you capture this town. 17But you must destroy it and everything in it, to show that it now belongs to the Lord. The woman Rahab helped the spies we sent, so protect her and the others who are inside her house. But kill everyone else in the town. 18-19The silver and gold and everything made of bronze and iron belong to the Lord and must be put in his treasury. Be careful to follow these instructions, because if you see something you want and take it, the Lord will destroy Israel. And it will be all your fault.
20 The priests blew their trumpets again, and the soldiers shouted as loud as they could. The walls of Jericho fell flat. Then the soldiers rushed up the hill, went straight into the town, and captured it. 21-25 They killed everyone, men and women, young and old, everyone except Rahab and the others in her house. They even killed every cow, sheep, and donkey.
Joshua said to the two men who had been spies, “Rahab kept you safe when I sent you to Jericho. We promised to protect her and her family, and we will keep that promise. Now go into her house and bring them out.”
The two men went into Rahab's house and brought her out, along with her father and mother, her brothers, and her other relatives. Rahab and her family had to stay in a place just outside the Israelite army camp. But later they were allowed to live among the Israelites, and her descendants still do.
The Israelites took the silver and gold and the things made of bronze and iron and put them with the rest of the treasure that was kept at the Lord's house. Finally, they set fire to Jericho and everything in it.
26 After Jericho was destroyed, Joshua warned the people, “Someday a man will rebuild Jericho, but the Lord will put a curse on him, and the man's oldest son will die when he starts to build the town wall. And by the time he finishes the wall and puts gates in it, all his children will be dead.”
27The Lord helped Joshua in everything he did, and Joshua was famous everywhere in Canaan.
translation_text:
Isirayeel yab jáń ki fōō Jeeriikoo tiŋki
1Isirayeel yab puee, Jeeriikoo yab nìn dū bi-tiŋki punyɔmmu ki pīiǹ ki kpàl̄. Báà ubɔ kaa nìn ŋūǹ kí kɔ́ɔɔ, kaa nìn ŋūǹ kí nyā mun. 2Ní ti-Dindaan bí Joosuwa yii: «Kpèè, m dū Jeeriikoo tiŋki nì ki-bɔtiu nì ki-baatandambi ki ŋá a-ŋaan. 3Sii nì a-janjaliibi ń còom̀ kí màntīí tū kitiŋ gbanti diba ŋwiin, kí nīn ŋáań míǹ kí tin sāā iwiin iluu. 4Bisaraaŋaliibi biluli ń nīn ŋúb́ ipijaa yiŋyi ki līī Dipoondi dakaau nyɔkɔpu. Ŋwinluluúti dalee, ní dāá còom̀ kí màntīí tū kitiŋ ŋfunyɔm miluli ní bisaraaŋaliibee ń dāá nīn búǹ iyin. 5Bi yaa láa búń upìja yiŋŋu ni gbìl̄ an súńee, samaa kɔkɔ ń dāá kúuǹ mpɔn mpɔn. Digundi din bi máń ki māntìi tú kitiŋee làá lítí niin niin. Niinee samaa kɔkɔ ń sāǹ kí kɔ́ kitiŋin, báà ŋma ń nīn pée túĺ u-nimbiin.» 6Ní Nuuni jipɔɔn Joosuwa yíiń bisaraaŋaliibi ki bí-bi yii: «Yòom̄maan Dipoondi dakaau kí bùkun̄ ní bisaraaŋaliibi biluli ń nīn ŋúb́ ipijaa yiŋyi ki līī ti-Dindaan dakaau nyɔkɔpu.» 7Ní u bí samaa yii: «Yīkìmaan kí còom̀ kí màntīí tū kitiŋ, bijanjaliibi bin lìntī nsanee ń lìntī ti-Dindaan dakaau nyɔkɔpu.» 8Joosuwa nín tùkū samaa yii bí ŋá puee, míǹ ní bi ŋá. Bisaraaŋaliibi biluli bin nìn ŋúb́ ipijaa yiŋyi ti-Dindaan nimbiinee līntì ki búǹ ní ti-Dindaan Poondi dakaau pá bi-boon. 9Bijanjaliibi bin lìntī nsanee līī bisaraaŋaliibi bin búǹ iyinee nyɔkɔpu, ní bijanjaliibi bin pāantí boonee pá Dipoondi dakaau boon. Ní báà ŋma còom̄ ki cá ní iyin búǹ. 10Ama ní Joosuwa kpáafì samaa yii: «Ní taa kúuǹ, kí taa yàntī bí gbìl̄ ni-neen pu. Báà dinyɔɔbundi ń taa nyā unil nyɔkɔn kí tin sāā ŋwiin ŋun m làá tùkù-ni yii ní kúuǹee, ní ní nín kúuǹ.» 11Míǹ ní Joosuwa yāntì bi būkuǹ ti-Dindaan Poondi dakaau ki cōom̀ ki māntìi tú kitiŋee diba, ní ki fātìi gítì dinaapaal pu ki dōoǹ.
12Ku wúntì, Joosuwa fīntì kutaafaau pɔ̀lpɔlee ní ki yāntì bisaraaŋaliibi fātìi yōoǹ ti-Dindaan Poondi dakaau ki būkuǹ. 13Bisaraaŋaliibi biluli bin ŋúb́ ipijaa yiŋyee cōom̀ ki līntì Dipoondi dakaau nyɔkɔpu, ki pée búǹ iyinee. Bijanjaliibi bin lìntī nsanee līī bíǹ nyɔkɔpu, ní bin pāantí boonee pá ti-Dindaan dakaau boon. Ní bi còom̄ ki cá ní iyin búǹ! 14Ŋwinliliitee, bi tí cōom̀ ki māntìi tú kitiŋ diba ní ki fātìi nín gítí dinaapaal pu. Bi ŋáaǹ míǹ ní ki tin sāā iwiin iluu. 15Ŋwinluluúti dalee, bi péé ki yíkì ntaafaabɔmbɔmin ní ki cōom̀ ki māntìi tú kitiŋ, kii bi nín pée kpàà ŋáań puee miluli pu. Ŋwiin gbanti baba ní bi cōom̀ ki māntìi tú kitiŋ miluli. 16Bi nín māntì nluluútiim ní bisaraaŋaliibi búń iyinee, ní Joosuwa bí samaa yii: «Ní kúum̀maan, kun puee ti-Dindaan dū kitiŋ nee ki ŋá ni-ŋaan ní! 17Ní nàan̄ kitiŋ gbanti nì tin kɔkɔ pée bí ki-poonee kí dàkà yii tì kpántì ti-Dindaan wanti ubɔ kaa ti máaǹ kí gbēē! Asee Rakaab kinimpulaakpaai baba di làá ŋmátí, ní kí kūtì binib bin kɔkɔ pée bí u-cee kudiinee. Kun puee úǹ di nìn bál̀ binib bin ti lēē ki tú bi cūtì ki cɔ́ŋkì ki béè kitiŋee. 18Ama nimbee, ní nīn nyí nì ni-ba kí taa gbēē tin kpántì ti-Dindaan wantee, kí mèè mbusu ki tɔ́ Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ pu kí kɔ́ǹ-bi tibɔtin! 19Tin kɔkɔ pée sá animbil nì sindaariya nì tasa wanti nì tikúti wantee, ní dūú sú ti-Dindaan kí dū-tì kí kūtì u-wanti poon!»
20Ní bisaraaŋaliibi búń iyin ní samaa kɔkɔ kúuǹ mpɔn. Ŋyunti ŋun samaa gbìl̄ iyin pu ki kúuǹ mpɔnee, ní digundi cúu wūtì. Niinee ní Isirayeel yab sáǹ ki nín jɔ́ḿ kitiŋin, báà ŋma túĺ u-nimbiin, ní bi jáń ki fōō kitiŋ. 21Bi kɔ́ mimmee ní ki kūū ki céetì tin kɔkɔ pée bí kitiŋee poon ki cáá kufoouee, an dàkà yii bininjab nì binimpoobi, binipɔmbi nì bitikpilib, inaa nì ipii nì mmamu. Bi nìn pée gāatì kɔkɔ nì ntàataajimu ní ki kūū.
Joosuwa fīī Rakaab nì u-yab
22Joosuwa tùkū bininjab bili bin u nìn lēē ki tú bi cūtìi cɔ́ŋkì ki béè kitiŋ nín bí puee yii: «Ní kɔ́maan kinimpulaakpaayee dumpu kí nyāntiń ki nì ki-yab kɔkɔ, kii ni nín nìn pūtì ki pōoǹ-kì puee!» 23Ní binaacimpɔmbi bin nìn cūtì ki cɔ́ŋkì ki béè kitiŋee kɔ́ ki nyántìń Rakaab nì u-baa nì u-na, nì u-niijab nì u-nabiyaamu mun nìn bí u-ceeyee. Bi nyántìń bi-kɔkɔee ní ki cáań-bi ki kāaǹ Isirayeel yab naapaal kpaanceetiŋu tiba ń taa gbēē-bi. 24Boonee ní bi sēē kitiŋee ŋŋmi ki kpáaǹ tin kɔkɔ bí ki-poonee. Asee animbil kúti nì sindaariya nì tasa wanti nì tikúti wanti ní bi nìn pée gāntì ki dūu kútì ti-Dindaan wanti tin bí u-diikunee pu. 25Ama Joosuwa nìn fīī Rakaab kinimpulaakpaai ki kpáaǹ u-yab kɔkɔ. Rakaab gbíntì ki kāl̀ Isirayeel yab kansikin, ní u-naantiibi dáá gbíntìi kóò niin ki dāa sāā díǹ, kun puee úǹ di nìn bál̀ binib bin Joosuwa nìn lēē ki tú bi cūtìi cɔ́ŋkì ki béè Jeeriikoo tiŋkee.
26Ŋyunti gbanti ní Joosuwa nìn pūtì ki lī yii:
«Ti-Dindaan yindi puee,
mbusu ń kɔ́ unil un kamaa yaa mākaǹ
yii u làá fàtīí mā Jeeriikoo tiŋki neeyee.
Udaan jipɔŋkpiliu ní u làá dūú kíĺ kitiŋ gbanti dimal,
ní kí dū u-jipɔnjoolkaau kí cóoń ki-punuubi!»
27Míǹ ní ti-Dindaan nìn bí Joosuwa cee ní u-yindi nìn gbītì kitiŋ kɔkɔ poon.

english_text:
Achan Is Punished for Stealing from the Lord
1The Lord had said that everything in Jericho belonged to him. But Achan from the Judah tribe took some of the things from Jericho for himself. And so the Lord was angry with the Israelites, because one of them had disobeyed him.
2While Israel was still camped near Jericho, Joshua sent some spies with these instructions: “Go to the town of Ai and find out whatever you can about the region around the town.”
The spies left and went to Ai, which is east of Bethel and near Beth-Aven. 3They went back to Joshua and reported, “You don't need to send the whole army to attack Ai—2,000 or 3,000 troops will be enough. Why bother the whole army for a town that small?”
4-5Joshua sent about 3,000 soldiers to attack Ai. But the men of Ai fought back and chased the Israelite soldiers away from the town gate and down the hill to the stone quarries. Thirty-six Israelite soldiers were killed, and the Israelite army felt discouraged.
6Joshua and the leaders of Israel tore their clothes and put dirt on their heads to show their sorrow. They lay facedown on the ground in front of the sacred chest until sunset. 7Then Joshua said:
Our Lord, did you bring us across the Jordan River just so the Amorites could destroy us? This wouldn't have happened if we had agreed to stay on the other side of the Jordan. 8I don't even know what to say to you, since Israel's army has turned and run from the enemy. 9Everyone will think you weren't strong enough to protect your people. Now the Canaanites and everyone else who lives in the land will surround us and wipe us out.
10The Lord answered:
Stop lying there on the ground! Get up! 11I said everything in Jericho belonged to me and had to be destroyed. But the Israelites have kept some of the things for themselves. They stole from me and hid what they took. Then they lied about it. 12What they stole was supposed to be destroyed, and now Israel itself must be destroyed. I cannot help you anymore until you do exactly what I have said. That's why Israel turns and runs from its enemies instead of standing up to them.
13Tell the people of Israel, “Tomorrow you will meet with the Lord your God, so make yourselves acceptable to worship him. The Lord says that you have taken things that should have been destroyed. You won't be able to stand up to your enemies until you get rid of those things.
14“Tomorrow morning everyone must gather near the place of worship. You will come forward tribe by tribe, and the Lord will show which tribe is guilty. Next, the clans in that tribe must come forward, and the Lord will show which clan is guilty. The families in that clan must come, and the Lord will point out the guilty family. Finally, the men in that family must come, 15and the Lord will show who stole what should have been destroyed. That man must be put to death, his body burned, and his possessions thrown into the fire. He has done a terrible thing by breaking the sacred agreement that the Lord made with Israel.”
16Joshua got up early the next morning and brought each tribe to the place of worship, where the Lord showed that the Judah tribe was guilty. 17Then Joshua brought the clans of Judah to the Lord, and the Lord showed that the Zerah clan was guilty. One by one he brought the leader of each family in the Zerah clan to the Lord, and the Lord showed that Zabdi's family was guilty. 18Finally, Joshua brought each man in Zabdi's family to the Lord, and the Lord showed that Achan was the guilty one.
19“Achan,” Joshua said, “the Lord God of Israel has decided that you are guilty. So tell me what you did, and don't try to hide anything.”
20“It's true,” Achan answered. “I sinned and disobeyed the Lord God of Israel. 21-22While we were in Jericho, I saw a beautiful Babylonian robe, 200 pieces of silver, and a gold bar that weighed the same as 50 pieces of gold. I wanted them for myself, so I took them. I dug a hole under my tent and hid the silver, the gold, and the robe.”
Joshua told some people to run to Achan's tent, where they found the silver, the gold, and the robe. 23They brought them back and put them in front of the sacred chest, so Joshua and the rest of the Israelites could see them. 24Then everyone took Achan and the things he had stolen to Trouble Valley. They also took along his sons and daughters, his cattle, donkeys, and sheep, his tent, and everything else that belonged to him.
25Joshua said, “Achan, you caused us a lot of trouble. Now the Lord is paying you back with the same kind of trouble.”
The people of Israel then stoned to death Achan and his family. They made a fire and burned the bodies, together with what Achan had stolen, and all his possessions. 26They covered the remains with a big pile of rocks, which is still there. Then the Lord stopped being angry with Israel.
That's how the place came to be called Trouble Valley.
translation_text:
Akan yīntì ní ki fōō u-tafadaaldi
1Isirayeel yab yīntiǹ mara un sá yii bí taa gbēē tiwan tin kpántì ti-Dindaan wantee. Di sá yii Kaarmii jipɔɔn, Sabidii naantiiu nì Seera un sá Juuda naakookunee naantitɔntɔkɔl Akan lēē tiwanee poon tiba. An puee ní ti-Dindaan fōō mbum Isirayeel yab pu.
2Jeeriikoo tiŋkin niin ní Joosuwa lēē binib ki tú Aayi tiŋki kin bí Beeteel ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú, ki pìlīǹ Beeti-Aween tiŋkee, bí cù kí cɔ̄ŋkì kí béé kitiŋ gbanti. Ní binibee cūtì ki cɔ́ŋkì ki béè Aayi tiŋki tiŋan. 3Bi fātìi gítìń Joosuwa ceeyee ní ki tùkū-u yii: «Bijanjaliibi kɔkɔ ń taa yīkì yii bi cá kí já nì Aayi tiŋki kujaau. Bijanjaliibi kutukub bili kii bita ŋūǹ kí cùú já kí fōō-kì. Taa yàntī binib ń gīī digìńdi fám, kun puee binib bin bí kitiŋ gbantinee kaa pée náaǹ báà fiii!» 4An puee ní bi lēē bijanjaliibi kutukub bita nyɔkɔm ki dūu tú bí cùú jáǹ Aayi tiŋki, ama ní Aayi yab kpìlìń-bi ní bi sáǹ. 5Aayi yab nìn kpìlìń Isirayeel yab doooo kitiŋ punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu, ki jīǹ-bi ki tin bàn̄ Seebariim ní ki kūū bi-kansikin binib mmuŋku nì saalaa nì biluu, ŋyunti ŋun bi bíi wúntí kigbantaŋee. Niinee ní Isirayeel yab pɔbiliŋ bíil̀ tikpil, ní bi-wunti kpíì.
6Ní Joosuwa nì Isirayeel tindaŋkpilib dáaĺ ki cátì bi-wanti tin bi pēēyee, ki cūtìi dōoǹ ti-Dindaan Poondi dakaau nyɔkɔpu dicincibil. Bi nìn dōoǹ ki tin sāā kujoou, ní ki kàfī ntam ki yàantí bi-yiliŋ pu. 7Ní Joosuwa bí yii: «Áà, m-Dindaan Unimbɔti! Ba pu ní a cáá-ti ki dūtìń Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ní? A cáań-ti ki ŋá Amɔɔr yab ŋaan bí kpɔ̀ kí céetí-ti níii? Ti yaa bàà pūtì gbíntì Jɔɔdan buŋgbandi lapu pu tiŋki pu, an bàà sɔ́ɔ! 8Abàa, m-Dindaan! Kɔŋkɔnnee Isirayeel yab nannanliibi nín kpìl̄-bi bi sáǹ nee, m làá nín lì yii ba dee? 9Kanaan yab nì binib bin kɔkɔ kóò kitiŋ nee puee yaa gbìl̄ tin bí nee, asee bí gbáb́ kí bìin̄ ti-pu ní kí kpɔ̀ kí céetí-ti! Mimmee, mana ní a làá ŋá ní kí yàntī binib ń béé yii a-yindi sá dikpaandi?»
10Niinee ní ti-Dindaan bí Joosuwa yii: «Yīkìm̄! Ba pu ní a dɔ̄ dicincibil míǹ? 11Isirayeel yab yīntì! Bi kpītì dipoondi din m pōoǹ-bee, ki lēē tiwan tin baa máaǹ kí gbēēyee poon tiba. Bi yùn̄-tì ki bál̀ bíǹ bi-ba wanti poon. 12An puee Isirayeel yab kaa làá ti ŋmā kí sútíí pìl̄ bi-nannanliibi. Bi-nannanliibi làá nīn pée sáń ki jì-bi ní, kun puee mbusu kɔ́-bi dikoobil din bi kōotèe pu. Ni yaa kaa nyántì tiwan tin naa máaǹ kí gbēēyee ni-kansikin, maa làá ti nín̄ bí ni-cee! 13Yīkì kí bɔ́ntí samaa bí nīn bí circir man nì bi ń fu kpāfì. Á tùkù-bi yii bí bɔ́ntí bi-ba kí nīn bí circir kí cīití fool taaku, kun puee man ni-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Isirayeel yab, tiwan tin naa máaǹ kí gbēēyee tiba bí ni-cee! Ni yaa kaa nyántì tiwan gbanti ni-kansikin, naa làá ti ŋmā kí sútí kí pìl̄ ni-nannanliibi.> 14An puee, fool kutaafaauee, ni-kɔkɔ ń fu dāan̄ m-cee, kí nīn sútiń kunaakoou kunaakoou. Kunaakoou kun ti-Dindaan yaa fu sāāyee ń fu kpāfì kí nīn sútiń mmaal mmaal. Mmaal ŋun ti-Dindaan yaa fu sāāyee ń fu kpāfì kí nīn sútiń kudicaŋu kudicaŋu. Ní kudicaŋu kun ti-Dindaan yaa fu sāāyee nib ń fu kpāfì kí nīn sútiń ubɔ ubɔ. 15Unil un an yaa fu sāā yii úǹ di ŋúb́ tiwan tin baa máaǹ kí gbēēyee, bí fu wà udaan ŋŋmi kí kpáaǹ tin pée sá u-wantee kɔkɔ. Kun puee udaan kpītì man ni-Dindaan Poondi ki ŋá icoo bɔti Isirayeel tiŋki poon!»
16Joosuwa fīntì kutaafaau pɔ̀lpɔlee ní ki yāntì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ sútìń kunaakoou kunaakoou, ní an sāā Juuda naakooku. 17Ní u yāntì Juuda naakookun yab sútìń, ki nóó nì bi nín pēē pēē mmaal puee, ní an sāā Seera maaliŋu. Ní Seera maaliŋu yab sútìń kudicaŋu kudicaŋu, ní an sāā Sabidii dicaŋku. 18U yāntì Sabidii dicaŋkun nib sútìń ubɔ ubɔ, ní an sāā Kaarmii jipɔɔn, Sabidii naantiiu, Seera un sá Juuda naakookunee naantitɔntɔkɔl Akan. 19Ní Joosuwa bí Akan yii: «M-jipɔɔn, tīī ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu tinyool, kí nyɔ̄ŋkì-u. Māafì-mi tin a ŋée kɔkɔ kí taa báĺ-mi báà tiba!» 20Niinee ní Akan kíí Joosuwa yii: «Tiŋman, man di lafun yīntiǹ ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu. An nín jítì puee sɔ̀. 21M ká tiwan tin ti jáń ki fōōyee poon Siinaar tiŋki bɔkutikpaandi diba, di ŋān̄ kunyaaŋŋu an kaa cáá bí lì, ki ká animbil kúti an nyìm̀ ki bàn̄ kii kiiloobi bita nyɔkɔm, ní ki ká disindaariyakúndi diba, dì nyìm̀ kii kiiloo dijandi nyɔkɔm. Tiwan gbantee kɔ́-mi nnimbitaataam ní m yōoǹ-tì ki cáa bál̀. Min ti kā nee, tì gbìn̄ ki síb́ kitiŋ m-tantiu kansikin, animbil kúti tíĺ taapu.»
22Ní Joosuwa lēē binib ki tú Akan tantiun. Bi bàn̄ ki lafun kpēēyee tiwan di síb́ kitiŋ tanti kansikin, animbil kúti tíĺ taapuee. 23Ní bi kóoǹní tiwanee tanti poon ki cáań Joosuwa nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ cee, ki dūu bíl̀ ti-Dindaan nimbiin. 24Niinee ní Joosuwa yāntì bi cúú Seera naantiiu Akan, ki yōoǹ animbil kútee nì dibɔkutikpaandee nì disindaariyakúndee. Bi nìn cúú ki kpáaǹ u-jipɔmbi nì u-bisalib, nì u-naai nì u-mammu nì u-piii nì tin kɔkɔ pée sá u-wantee, ní u nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ cáá-bi ki cūnnì Akɔɔr tantakalin. 25Bi bàn̄ niinee ní Joosuwa bí Akan yii: «Ba pu ní a pàal̄ ŋŋmii ki léeǹ ti-pu míǹ? Too, díǹ wiiŋŋu nee ní ti-Dindaan làá pée gíiǹ-ŋu kí téeǹ-si!» Ní Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ yáŋkì Akan ataŋkpee ki kūū. Bi nìn yáŋkì u-yab mun ataŋkpee ki kūū ní ki wùn̄ u-wanti kɔkɔ ŋŋmi. 26Boonee ní bi kóoǹ ataŋkpee ki kpúkuǹ bi-pu dikpúkukpaandi. Ditaŋkpakpukul gbanti dáá gbíntìi bí niin díǹ pu nee. An pu ní bi pú mpaan gbanti diyindi yii Akɔɔr tantakal, ki dāa sāā díǹ.
Míǹ boonee ní ti-Dindaan ŋuul sɔ̄ŋkì.

english_text:
Israel Destroys the Town of Ai
1-2The Lord told Joshua:
Don't be afraid, and don't be discouraged by what happened at the town of Ai. Take the army and attack again. But first, order part of the army to set up an ambush on the other side of the town. I will help you defeat the king of Ai and his army, and you will capture the town and the land around it. Destroy Ai and kill its king as you did at Jericho. But you may keep the livestock and everything else you want.
3-4Joshua quickly got the army ready to attack Ai. He chose 30,000 of his best soldiers and gave them these orders:
Tonight, while it is dark, march to Ai and take up a position behind the town. Get as close to the town as you can without being seen, and be ready to attack.
5-6The rest of the army will come with me and attack near the gate. When the people of Ai come out to fight, we'll run away and let them chase us. They will think we are running from them just like the first time. But when we've let them chase us far enough away, 7you come out of hiding. The Lord our God will help you capture the town. 8Then set it on fire, as the Lord has told us to do. Those are your orders, 9now go!
The 30,000 soldiers went to a place on the west side of Ai, between Ai and Bethel, where they could hide and wait to attack.
That night, Joshua stayed in camp with the rest of the army. 10Early the next morning he got his troops ready to move out, and he and the other leaders of Israel led them to Ai. 11They set up camp in full view of the town, across the valley to the north. 12Joshua had already sent 5,000 soldiers to the west side of the town to hide and wait to attack. 13Now all his troops were in place. Part of the army was in the camp to the north of Ai, and the others were hiding to the west, ready to make a surprise attack. That night, Joshua went into the valley.
14-15The king of Ai saw Joshua's army, so the king and his troops hurried out early the next morning to fight them. Joshua and his army pretended to be beaten, and they let the men of Ai chase them toward the desert. The king and his army were facing the Jordan valley as Joshua had planned.
The king did not realize that some Israelite soldiers were hiding behind the town. 16-17So he called out every man in Ai to go after Joshua's troops. They all rushed out to chase the Israelite army, and they left the town gates wide open. Not one man was left in Ai or in Bethel.
Joshua let the men of Ai chase him and his army farther and farther away from Ai. 18Finally, the Lord told Joshua, “Point your sword at the town of Ai, because now I am going to help you defeat it!”
As soon as Joshua pointed his sword at the town, 19the soldiers who had been hiding jumped up and ran into the town. They captured it and set it on fire.
20-21When Joshua and his troops saw smoke rising from the town, they knew that the other part of their army had captured it. So they turned and attacked.
The men of Ai looked back and saw smoke rising from their town. But they could not escape, because the soldiers they had been chasing had suddenly turned and started fighting. 22-24Meanwhile, the other Israelite soldiers had come from the town and attacked the men of Ai from the rear. The Israelites captured the king of Ai and brought him to Joshua. They also chased the rest of the men of Ai into the desert and killed them.
The Israelite army went back to Ai and killed everyone there. 25-26Joshua kept his sword pointed at the town of Ai until every last one of Ai's 12,000 people was dead. 27But the Israelites took the animals and the other possessions of the people of Ai, because this was what the Lord had told Joshua to do.
28-29Joshua made sure every building in Ai was burned to the ground. He told his men to kill the king of Ai and hang his body on a tree. Then at sunset he told the Israelites to take down the body, throw it in the gateway of the town, and cover it with a big pile of rocks. Those rocks are still there, and the town itself has never been rebuilt.
Joshua Reads the Blessings and Curses
(Deuteronomy 27.1-26)
30-32 One day, Joshua led the people of Israel to Mount Ebal, where he told some of his men, “Build an altar for offering sacrifices to the Lord. And use stones that have never been cut with iron tools, because that is what Moses taught in The Book of the Law.”
Joshua offered sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask his blessing. Then with the Israelites still watching, he copied parts of The Book of the Law of Moses onto stones.
33-35 Moses had said that everyone in Israel was to go to the valley between Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim, where they were to be blessed. So everyone went there, including the foreigners, the leaders, officials, and judges. Half of the people stood on one side of the valley, and half on the other side, with the priests from the Levi tribe standing in the middle with the sacred chest. Then in a loud voice, Joshua read the blessings and curses from The Book of the Law of Moses.
translation_text:
Isirayeel yab jáń kí fōō Aayi tiŋki
1Míǹ boonee ní ti-Dindaan tùkū Joosuwa yii: «Taa fàŋkì, kí taa yàntī a-wunti ń yɔ̀tī! Yīkì kí yòon̄ binib bin bàn̄ kí cù kujaauee kɔkɔ ní cùú jáǹ Aayi tiŋki! Á nīn nyí yii m dū Aayi bɔtiu nì u-nib kɔkɔ, nì kitiŋ kin poon u kóòyee, nì kitiŋ kin pu u jīǹ dibeelee kɔkɔ ki ŋá a-ŋaan. 2Á ŋá Aayi tiŋki nì ki-bɔtiu kii a nín ŋá Jeeriikoo tiŋki nì ki-bɔtiu puee. Ama ni ŋūǹ kí yòon̄ kitiŋ nee kíǹ wanti tin ni jáń ki fōōyee nì ki-waŋkuti. Á lēē bijanjaliibi biba bí cùú nákań kitiŋ boon pú.»
3Ní Joosuwa bɔ́ntì u nì u-yab bí cùú jáǹ Aayi tiŋki. U dá láá péé ki lēē bibaatandambi kutukub mmuŋku nì saalaa ní bíǹ līntì ki nín cá kunyeeu gbanti. 4Bi làá búntée ni u bí-bi yii: «Ni káa! Nimbi ń lìntīmaan kí cùú nákań kitiŋee boon pú, kí taa nín̄ dátiǹ-kì tikpil, kí bɔ́ntí ni-ba kí nīn cí. 5Man nì samaa un kíǹee làá sútí kí pìl̄ kitiŋ. Bi yaa tí nyánní kí jàkà-ti kii bi nín nìn ŋá pu mpeekaamee, ti làá ŋá kii ti sáǹee ní bí páań ti-boon. 6Ti yaa bíi sáń ní bi yaa kùl̄ ki páaǹ ti-boonee, ní tí ŋmàtiǹ-bi kí dáaĺ-bi kí nyāntí kitiŋin. Bi làá dàkafì yii ti tí bíi sáń-bi, kii bi nín nìn jìn̄-ti ti sáǹ mpeekaam puee. 7Niinee ní nimbi ń nyānní laakin ní ni náká nákée, kí kɔ́ kí já kí fōō kitiŋee. Ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu làá dū-kì kí ŋá ni-ŋaan. 8Ni yaa jáń ki fōō kitiŋ gbantee, ní sēē-kì ŋŋmi kí wà, kí nóó nì ti-Dindaan nín tùkū-ni yii ní ŋá puee. Man nín yóoǹ-ni yii ní ŋá puee, ní ŋámaan míǹ deedee!» 9Ní Joosuwa dū-bi ki tú ní bi nín cá ki cūtìi nákáǹ nákáǹ Beeteel nì Aayi timmu kansikin, kí nīn bí Aayi tiŋki ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú. Kunyeeu gbantee, Joosuwa nì bijanjaliibi bin kíǹee di nìn kpáfì ki dōoǹ dinaapaal pu.
10Kutaa wúntì kutaafaau pɔ̀lpɔlee ní Joosuwa yíkì ki yíiń bininjab bin bàn̄ kí cù kujaauee ki kpáfì kí kpèè bi nín bɔ́ntì puee, ní u nì Isirayeel tindaŋkpilib līntì bi-nyɔkɔpu bí cùú jáǹ Aayi tiŋki yab. 11Míǹ ní u nì bijanjaliibi bin pá u-boonee nín jɔ́ḿ, ki cōom̀ ki tin bàn̄ Aayi tiŋki caŋin. Bi bàn̄ee ní ki gāā dijanjanaapaal Aayi tiŋki ŋgan pú, ní ditantakal bí bi nì Aayi tiŋki kansikin. 12Ní Joosuwa lēē bijanjaliibi kii kutukub biŋmoo nyɔkɔm ki yóoǹ Beeteel nì Aayi timmu kansikin, ki gítí Aayi tiŋki ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú. 13Míǹ ní bijanjaliibi tikpil nìn gāā dijanjanaapaal Aayi tiŋki ŋgan pú, ní bin kíǹee bíǹ náká náká kitiŋ boon, ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú. Kunyeeu gbantee, Joosuwa nìn fātìi gítì ditantakalin. 14Kutaa wúntì Aayi bɔtiu ká mimmee ní u nì u-yab bɔ́ntì malaa ki nyáń kí cùú jáǹ Isirayeel yab, laakin bi nìn pée tí jáńee, ki gítí Jɔɔdan tantakal watil pú. Ubɔti kaa nìn nyí yii bi nìn píĺ ki cí-u kí jáǹ-u kitiŋ boon pú. 15Di sá ní Joosuwa nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ yāntì Aayi yab kpìlìń-bi, ní bi sáǹ ki túĺ kuteeu watil pú. 16Bi nìn sāal̀ Aayi tiŋkin ninjab kɔkɔ bí nyā kí jà Isirayeel yab boon. Bi bíi jì-bee ní ki mɔ̀tīi kóò ndandati ki wàatī kitiŋ. 17Báà uninja kaa nìn kíǹ Aayi nì Beeteel timmun kaa nyáń ki jìn̄ Isirayeel yab boon. Ŋyunti ŋun bi nìn bí ki jì Isirayeel yab mimmee, Aayi tiŋki punyɔkɔki nìn kíǹ ki wāā fám dee. 18Ní ti-Dindaan bí Joosuwa yii: «Tàntī kikpaŋ kin a ŋúb́ee kí dàkà Aayi tiŋki, kun puee m làá dū kitiŋ gbanti ki ŋá a-ŋaan!» Ní Joosuwa tāntì u-ŋal ki fātì kikpaŋ kin u ŋúb́ee ki túĺ Aayi tiŋki watil pú. 19U tin lì yii u tàntī u-ŋalee, bijanjaliibi bin u yóoǹ kitiŋ boonee kɔkɔ ŋá malaa ki nyánní laakin bi nìn náká nákée, ki sáǹ ki kɔ́ kitiŋin, ki jáń ki fōō-kì ní ki sēē-kì ŋŋmi niin niin.
20Aayi yab fātìi kpēē bi-boonee ní ki ká yii bi-tiŋki fōō ŋŋmi, nnyiim yíkí ki-poon jòooo ki jɔ́ḿ kutaa. Bi-pɔbiliŋ bíil̀ bi bākatì kaa ti nyí laakin pú bi làá túĺee. Di sá yii Isirayeel yab bin sáń ki līī nyɔkɔpu ki cá kuteeu watil púee fātìi lábitì ki bíi jì Aayi yab bin pá bi-boon ki jì-bee. 21Joosuwa nì Isirayeel yab nín ká yii bi-yab bin náká náká kitiŋ boon púee kɔ́ ki jáń ki fōō kitiŋ, ki ká nnyiim nín bí ki nyēē kitiŋ gbanti poon jòooo ki jɔ́ḿ puee, ní bi fātìi lábitì Aayi yab pu ki kíĺ ki bíi kù-bi. 22Ní Isirayeel yab bin kíǹee nyánní kitiŋin ki nín túŋkiń-bi, ní ki dū Aayi yab ki ŋá kansikin nì kansikin, ki māntìi gíb́-bi. Di sá ní Isirayeel yab kūū ki céetì Aayi yab kɔkɔ múb, báà uniseen kaa ŋúń ki sáǹ ki ŋmátì. 23Aayi bɔtiu baba ní bi pée cúú kaa kūū, ní ki cáań-u Joosuwa cee. 24Isirayeel yab nìn kūū Aayi janjaliibi tisatin, kuteeu poon laakin bi páaǹ bi-boonee ki dóò. Bi nìn dū ntàataajimu ki kūū ki kúntì bi-kɔkɔ kaa nìn kíǹ bi-kansikin báà ubɔ. Boonee ní Isirayeel yab fātìi nín gítiń Aayi tiŋkin ní ki dɔ́miń ki púntìi kūū Aayi yab bin kíǹ ki bí kitiŋinee kɔkɔ pílpil. 25Ŋwiin gbantee, bi nìn kūū Aayi tiŋki yab kɔkɔ, bininjab nì binimpoobi. Bi nìn nyáń binib kutukub saalaa nì bili ní. 26Joosuwa ŋal nìn pée gbíntìi tèen̄ ki ŋúb́ kikpaŋ ní, ki tin sāā ŋyunti ŋun Isirayeel yab dāa kūū ki céetì Aayi yab kɔkɔee. 27Ama Isirayeel yab nìn kóoǹ Aayi yab wanti tin bi nìn jáń ki fōōyee kɔkɔ, ní ki yōoǹ ki kpáaǹ tiwaŋkuti, ki nóó nì ti-Dindaan nín nìn tùkū Joosuwa puee. 28Joosuwa yāntì bi wùn̄ Aayi tiŋki ŋŋmi ní ki-digbuŋŋi wūtì ki kíǹ ki dɔ̄ dikpúkul kii an nín dáá gbíntìi dɔ̄ pu díǹ pu nee ní. 29U nìn lúntì Aayi bɔtiu úǹ busubu bubɔ pu, ní ki yāntì u lúń míǹ ki tin sāā kujoou. Ŋwìiń cá kí jéetée ní u yāntì bi cúú dinikpilee ki sākatìń busubu pu ki cáa lúkú kitiŋ punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu, ní ki kóoǹ ataŋkpee ki nyīkiǹ u-pu ní an ŋá ditaŋkpakpukul dikpaandi. Ditaŋkpakpukul gbanti dáá dɔ̄ niin díǹ pu nee.
Bi kàan̄ Unimbɔti marau Eebaal jool pu
30Niinee ní Joosuwa máń ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu, nsaraafan ŋubɔ Eebaal jool pu, 31ki nóó nì ti-Dindaan tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi nín nìn yóoǹ Isirayeel yab yii bí ŋá puee, kii an nín ŋmàn̄ ki kā Mooyiisi marab gbɔŋku poon puee. U nìn dū ataŋkpee ŋin bi tōoń kaa kpítì-ŋi, kaa pée dū kukúluu ki gbēēyee ní ki máń nsaraafan gbanti. Bi nìn ŋá bisaraawɔkaabi nì mpèé saraabi nsaraafan gbanti pu ki tīī ti-Dindaan. 32Isirayeel yab nimbiin niin ní Joosuwa dū Mooyiisi Marau un u nìn ŋmàn̄ ki síiǹ Isirayeel yabee ki fātìi dūu ŋmàn̄ ataŋkpee pu. 33Isirayeel yab nìn yú akiti ali bi-nimbiin túĺ Dipoondi dakaau un bi nìn dūu yóoǹ bi-kansikinee. Bi-tindaŋkpilib nì bi-gbaŋŋmaliibi nì bi-bɔsoonliibi nì binicambi bin nìn kóò bi-kansikinee mun nìn yú akiti ali gbanti poon. Dikitil diba nìn yú ki gítí Geerisiim jool pú ní dikitil din kíǹee yú ki gítí Eebaal jool pú. Ti-Dindaan tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi nìn yóoǹ yii bisaraaŋaliibi ń ŋá míǹ ní kí bìin̄ Isirayeel yab pu. 34Boonee ní Joosuwa kàan̄ tibɔti tin kā Marab gbɔŋkunee kɔkɔ, tin sá dibiindi bɔtee nì tin sá mbusu bɔtee. U nìn kàan̄ tikɔkɔ ki nóó nì bi nín ŋmàn̄-tì pu tì kā Marab gbɔŋku poonee ní. 35Báà kubɔluu kubɔ kaa nìn kíǹ tin kɔkɔ Mooyiisi yóoǹee poon Joosuwa kaa kàan̄-tì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nimbiin, ki kpáaǹ binimpoobi nì mbiyaamu nì binicambi bin kóò bi-kansikinee kɔkɔ nimbiin.

english_text:
The People of Gibeon Trick the Leaders of Israel
1-2The kings west of the Jordan River heard about Joshua's victories, so they got together and decided to attack Joshua and Israel. These kings were from the hill country and from the foothills to the west, as well as from the Mediterranean seacoast as far north as the Lebanon Mountains. Some of them were Hittites, others were Amorites or Canaanites, and still others were Perizzites, Hivites, or Jebusites.
3The people of Gibeon had also heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and Ai. 4So they decided that some of their men should pretend to be messengers to Israel from a faraway country.
