16Then the Israelites got rid of the idols of the foreign gods, and they began worshiping only the Lord. Finally, there came a time when the Lord could no longer stand to see them suffer.
The Ammonites Invade Gilead
17The rulers of Ammon called their soldiers together and led them to Gilead, where they set up camp.
The Israelites gathered at Mizpah and set up camp there. 18The leaders of Gilead asked each other, “Who can lead an attack on the Ammonites?” Then they agreed, “If we find someone who can lead the attack, we'll make him the ruler of Gilead.”
translation_text:
Bibɔsoonliibi biba mun: Toola nì Yayiir
1Abimeeleeki kúm boonee, Puuwa jipɔɔn Toola, Doodoo naantiiu un nìn sá Isakaar naakookunee di nìn līntì Isirayeel yab nyɔkɔpu ki nìn fīī-bi bi-nannanliibi ŋaan. U nìn kóò Samiir tiŋki kin bí Eefiraayiim jooŋŋi puee ní. 2U nìn kpōotì Isirayeel yab abin mmuŋku nì ata ní ki dāa nín kpíì ní bi síb́-u Samiir tiŋkin.
3Toola kúm boonee, Yayiir un nìn sá Galaadi tiŋkinee di nìn fōō-u. U nìn kpōotì Isirayeel yab abin mmuŋku nì ali ní. 4Yayiir nìn cáá jipɔmbi mmuŋku nì saalaa, bi-kɔkɔ nìn kàal̀ mmanjamu mmuŋku nì saalaa ní ki nìn cáá ntimbilimu mmuŋku nì saalaa. Díǹ pu nee bi-timmu gbanti ní bi dáá gbíntìi yíì yii Yayiir timbilimmu Galaadi tiŋkinee. 5Yayiir nìn kpíì ní bi síb́-u Kamɔn tiŋkin.
Amɔn yab bíi jáà nì Isirayeel yab
6Isirayeel yab nìn fātìi kíĺ ki bíi ŋáań tin kaa kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee. Di sá yii bi nìn fātìi kíĺ ki bíi tòotī Baal nì Asitaartee, ní ki tòotī Aram yab nì Siidɔn yab nì Moowaab yab nì Amɔn yab nì Fiiliistii yab waaŋi. Bi nìn dū ti-Dindaan ki fá, kaa nìn gíti jáaḿ-u. 7Ti-Dindaan nìn gíí diŋuul Isirayeel yab pu ní ki nìn dū-bi ki ŋá Fiiliistii yab nì Amɔn yab ŋaan. 8Kí yòon̄ dibindi gbanti kí cáá sāā abin saalku nì atee, an nibee nìn nāaǹ Isirayeel yab bin nìn kóò Galaadi tiŋkee, an dàkà yii Amɔɔr yab tiŋki kin nìn bí Jɔɔdan buŋŋu lapu pu gbandi jaaŋŋu púee, ki nìn sāaǹ-bi tiŋan. 9Amɔn yab nìn dūtìń Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ki dɔ́miń ki jáń nì Juuda naakookun yab nì Beenjameen naakookun yab nì Eefiraayiim naakookun yab. Isirayeel yab nimbaaku kun poon bi nìn kíǹ ki bée nìn gíti nyāŋkì tikpil. 10Niinee ní Isirayeel yab kúuǹ ki yíiń ti-Dindaan ki lī yii: «Tilafuŋman ní ti yīntiǹ-si, kun puee ti dū sii un sá ti-Nimbɔtiuee ki fá ní ki bí ki tòotī Baal.» 11Ti-Dindaan nìn bí Isirayeel yab yii: «Ŋyunti ŋun ní Eejipiti nì Amɔɔr nì Amɔn nì Fiiliistii yab, 12nì Siidɔn nì Amaleeki nì Maawɔn yab nìn wɔ́b́-ni ni kúuǹ ki yíiń-mee, maa nìn fīī-ni bi-ŋaanaaa? 13Ama ní nimbi dū man ki fá ki bíi jáaḿ inimbɔticaan. An puee maa làá ti fīī-ni. 14Ní cùmaan kí nīn kūuntí ki yíì awaa ŋin ni lēē yii ni là kí nīn tòotēe, ŋí fīī-ni ni-nimbaakun!» 15Ní Isirayeel yab fātìi bí ti-Dindaan yii: «Ti-Dindaan, ti yīntì ní. Ŋá-ti min di yaa pée ŋān̄ a-ceeyee, ama ti gbàam̄-si ní, fīī-ti díǹ wiiŋŋu nee!» 16Isirayeel yab nìn lī mimmee ní ki dū awaa ŋin nìn bí bi-ceeyee ki fá ní ki fātìi bíi jáaḿ ti-Dindaan. Niinee falaau un bi nìn bí ki jīǹee nìn kɔ́ ti-Dindaan tikpil.
17Amɔn yab nìn yíiń tɔb ki kpáfì ní ki ŋātì bi-janjanaapaal Galaadi tiŋkin, ní Isirayeel yab kóoǹ ki kpáfì ki ŋātì bi-janjanaapaal Miisipa tiŋkin. 18Niin ní Isirayeel yab nì Galaadi tindaŋkpilib nìn bíi bàlifī tɔb yii: «Ŋma di làá nín kíĺ kujaau nì Amɔn yab dee? Udaan di bàà làá kpántí Galaadi tiŋki nib kɔkɔ kpiliu!»

english_text:
Jephthah
1-5The leaders of the Gilead clan decided to ask a brave warrior named Jephthah son of Gilead to lead the attack against the Ammonites.
Even though Jephthah belonged to the Gilead clan, he had earlier been forced to leave the region where they had lived. Jephthah was the son of a prostitute, but his half brothers were the sons of his father's wife.
One day his half brothers told him, “You don't really belong to our family, so you can't have any of the family property.” Then they forced Jephthah to leave home.
Jephthah went to the country of Tob, where he was joined by a number of men who would do anything for money.
So the leaders of Gilead went to Jephthah and said, 6“Please come back to Gilead! If you lead our army, we will be able to fight off the Ammonites.”
7“Didn't you hate me?” Jephthah replied. “Weren't you the ones who forced me to leave my family? You're only coming to me now because you're in trouble.”
8“But we do want you to come back,” the leaders said. “And if you lead us in battle against the Ammonites, we will make you the ruler of Gilead.”
9“All right,” Jephthah said. “If I go back with you and the Lord lets me defeat the Ammonites, will you really make me your ruler?”
10“You have our word,” the leaders answered. “And the Lord is a witness to what we have said.”
11So Jephthah went back to Mizpah with the leaders of Gilead. The people of Gilead gathered at the place of worship and made Jephthah their ruler. Jephthah also made promises to them.
12After the ceremony, Jephthah sent messengers to say to the king of Ammon, “Are you trying to start a war? You have invaded my country, and I want to know why!”
13The king of Ammon replied, “Tell Jephthah that the land really belongs to me, all the way from the Arnon River in the south, to the Jabbok River in the north, and west to the Jordan River. When the Israelites came out of Egypt, they stole it. Tell Jephthah to return it to me, and there won't be any war.”
14Jephthah sent the messengers back to the king of Ammon, 15and they told him that Jephthah had said:
Israel hasn't taken any territory from Moab or Ammon. 16When the Israelites came from Egypt, they traveled across the desert to the Red Sea and then to Kadesh. 17 They sent messengers to the king of Edom and said, “Please, let us go through your country.” But the king of Edom refused. They also sent messengers to the king of Moab, but he wouldn't let them cross his country either. And so the Israelites stayed at Kadesh.
18 A little later, the Israelites set out into the desert, going east of Edom and Moab, and camping on the eastern side of the Arnon River gorge. The Arnon is the eastern border of Moab, and since the Israelites didn't cross it, they didn't even set foot in Moab.
19 The Israelites sent messengers to the Amorite King Sihon of Heshbon. “Please,” they said, “let our people go through your country to get to our own land.”
20Sihon didn't think the Israelites could be trusted, so he called his army together. They set up camp at Jahaz, then they attacked the Israelite camp. 21But the Lord God helped Israel defeat Sihon and his army. Israel took over all of the Amorite land where Sihon's people had lived, 22from the Arnon River in the south to the Jabbok River in the north, and from the desert in the east to the Jordan River in the west.
23The messengers also told the king of Ammon that Jephthah had said:
The Lord God of Israel helped his nation get rid of the Amorites and take their land. Now do you think you're going to take over that same territory? 24If Chemosh your god takes over a country and gives it to you, don't you have a right to it? And if the Lord takes over a country and gives it to us, the land is ours!
25 Are you better than Balak the son of Zippor? He was the king of Moab, but he didn't quarrel with Israel or start a war with us.
26For 300 years, Israelites have been living in Heshbon and Aroer and the nearby villages, and in the towns along the Arnon River gorge. If the land really belonged to you Ammonites, you wouldn't have waited until now to try to get it back.
27I haven't done anything to you, but it's certainly wrong of you to start a war. I pray that the Lord will show whether Israel or Ammon is in the right.
28But the king of Ammon paid no attention to Jephthah's message.
29Then the Lord's Spirit took control of Jephthah, and Jephthah went through Gilead and Manasseh, raising an army. Finally, he arrived at Mizpah in Gilead, where 30he promised the Lord, “If you will let me defeat the Ammonites 31and come home safely, I will sacrifice to you whoever comes out to meet me first.”
32From Mizpah, Jephthah attacked the Ammonites, and the Lord helped him defeat them.
33Jephthah and his army destroyed the 20 towns between Aroer and Minnith, and others as far as Abel-Keramim. After that, the Ammonites could not invade Israel any more.
Jephthah's Daughter
34When Jephthah returned to his home in Mizpah, the first one to meet him was his daughter. She was playing a tambourine and dancing to celebrate his victory, and she was his only child.
35 “Oh no!” Jephthah cried. Then he tore his clothes in sorrow and said to his daughter, “I made a sacred promise to the Lord, and I must keep it. Your coming out to meet me has broken my heart.”
36“Father,” she said, “you made a sacred promise to the Lord, and he let you defeat the Ammonites. Now, you must do what you promised, even if it means I must die. 37But first, please let me spend two months, wandering in the hill country with my friends. We will cry together, because I can never get married and have children.”
38“Yes, you may have two months,” Jephthah said.
She and some other girls left, and for two months they wandered in the hill country, crying because she could never get married and have children. 39Then she went back to her father. He did what he had promised, and she never got married.
That's why 40every year, Israelite girls walk around for four days, weeping for Jephthah's daughter.
translation_text:
Jeefita kpántì Galaadi yab kpiliu
1Jeefita un nìn sá Galaadi tiŋkinee nìn sá ubaatandaan un cáá dipɔbilee. U-na nìn sá kinimpulaakpaai ní. U-baa ní bi nìn yíì yii Galaadi. 2Galaadi nimpuu un u nìn cááyee nìn màl̄-u mbininjabiyaamu. Unimpu gbanti jipɔmbi dāa cíkitèe, ní ki jìn̄ Jeefita bi-baa cindin ki lī-u yii: «Saa làá ká báà tiba ti-baa fakal poon, kun puee a sá unimpu ubɔ fám biki ní.» 3Jeefita nìn sáǹ ki wāatì u-nabiyaamu ki cūtìi kóòń Toob tiŋkin. U nìn bí niin mimmee ní ki nyàab̄ naayeekub biba ki kútì u-ba pu ní u nì bi nyēē ki cá ki jáà kujaau.
4Too, an kaa nìn súŋkì ní Amɔn yab bíi jáà nì Isirayeel yab. 5Ŋyunti ŋun ní Amɔn yab nìn bí ki jáà nì Isirayeel yabee ní Galaadi tindaŋkpilib nìn nín cá Toob tiŋkin kí cùú cáań Jeefita. 6Bi nìn bàn̄ee ní ki bí Jeefita yii: «Dāan̄ kí nīn sá ti-janjakpiliu tí ŋmā kí já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ Amɔn yab.» 7Ní Jeefita bí Galaadi tindaŋkpilib yii: «Kéè ni nìn ná-mi ní ki jìn̄-mi m-baa dicaŋkunaa! Ba gíti ŋá ní ni dòoń m-cee kɔŋkɔnnee, ŋyunti ŋun ní dinimbinaamandi bāań-nee?» 8Ní Galaadi tindaŋkpilib kíí Jeefita yii: «Too, kɔŋkɔnnee ti yaa dɔ́miń a-ceeyee, ti là yii á kíí kí nóó-ti kí cùú jáǹ Amɔn yab, kí nīn sá timbi Galaadi yab kɔkɔ kpiliu ní.» 9Ní Jeefita bí Galaadi tindaŋkpilib yii: «Ni lafun kíí tiŋman yii m yaa nóó-ni ki gítì ki cūtìi jáń nì Amɔn yab ní ti-Dindaan yaa dū-bi ki ŋá m-ŋaan, man di làá nīn sá ni-kɔkɔ kpiliuaaa?» 10Ní Galaadi tindaŋkpilib bí Jeefita yii: «Ti-Dindaan sá ti-seeradaaŋwu, ti làá ŋá a nín lī puee.»
11Niinee ní Jeefita kíí ki páaǹ Galaadi tindaŋkpilib boon bi nín cá, ní samaa tin kāaǹ-u ú nīn sá bi-kpiliu nì bi-janjakpiliu. Ní Jeefita fātìi sòon̄ anyɔɔbun ŋin u nìn pée sòon̄ee kɔkɔ ti-Dindaan nimbiin Miisipa tiŋkin.
Jeefita tú ituun Amɔn yab cee
12An ŋá mimmee ní Jeefita lēē binib ki tú Amɔn yab bɔtiu cee bi cūtìi bālifì-u dinyɔɔbundi u-yil pu yii: «Man nì si yii ba ní a dɔ́miń m-tiŋki pu ki bíi jáà nì man nì m-yab?» 13Ní Amɔn yab bɔtiu kíí Jeefita tuuŋyi yii: «Kun pu m ŋá mimmee di sá yii, ŋyunti ŋun Isirayeel yab nìn nyánní Eejipiti tiŋkin ki jɔ́mińee, bi nìn fōō m-tiŋki kí yòon̄ Arinɔn buŋŋu kí tin cáá sāā Yaabɔki buŋŋu nì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu. An puee, kɔŋkɔnnee á gíiǹ m-tiŋki gbanti kí tīī-mi soooo.»
14Ní Jeefita fātìi lēē binib ki tú Amɔn yab bɔtiu cee 15bí tùkù-u tin Jeefita sòon̄ee yii: «Isirayeel yab kaa fōō Moowaab yab tiŋkaaa, kaa tí fōō Amɔn yab mun tiŋki. 16An nín nìn ŋá puee di sá yii, Isirayeel yab nín nìn nyánní Eejipiti tiŋkin ki jɔ́mińee, bi nìn cōom̀ kuteeun míǹ ní ki dāa dūu nyáń Tikati mɔɔl pu, ní ki nìkī ki tin dūu bàn̄ Kadeesi tiŋki. 17Isirayeel yab nìn kā niin ní ki lēē binib ki tú Eedoom yab bɔtiu cee ki lī yii: <Ti mèé-si á pɔ̄-ti nsan tí jītí a-tiŋki poon!> Ama ní Eedoom yab bɔtiu kaa nìn pílifiǹ-bi. Bi nìn tú Moowaab yab bɔtiu mun cee ní u mun kaa nìn kíí ki pú-bi nsan. Di sá ní Isirayeel yab nìn gbíntì Kadeesi tiŋkin. 18Boonee, bi nìn cōom̀ kuteeun, ki gɔ́ntì Moowaab tiŋki ki fātìi nyánní ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú ní ki dāa dūu nyáń Moowaab tiŋki pu. Bi nìn kāl̀ Arinɔn buŋgbandi lapu pu yal ní, kaa nìn kɔ́ Moowaab yab tiŋkin, di sá yii Arinɔn buŋŋu di nìn sá Moowaab tiŋki kpaanyɔkɔ. 19Isirayeel yab nìn lēē binib ki tú Amɔɔr yab bɔtiu, an dàkà yii Eesbɔn tiŋki bɔtiu Siiwɔn cee bi cūtìi tùkū-u yii: <Ti mèé-si yii á pɔ̄-ti nsan tí jītí a-tiŋki poon kí cù laakin ti cée!> 20Ama ubɔti Siiwɔn kaa nìn cáá Isirayeel yab pu dimákal, di sá ní waa nìn kíí bi jítì u-tiŋkin. U nìn kóoǹ u-janjaliibi ki kpáfì Yakaasi tiŋkin ki kíĺ kujaau nì Isirayeel yab. 21Ní ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu dū ubɔti Siiwɔn nì u-janjaliibi kɔkɔ ki ŋá Isirayeel yab ŋaan ní bi ŋúń ki jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi. Isirayeel yab nìn fōō Amɔɔr yab tiŋki kin bi nìn kóòyee kɔkɔ. 22Bi nìn fōō Amɔɔr yab tiŋki kɔkɔ, kí yòon̄ Arinɔn buŋŋu kí cáá sāā Yaabɔki buŋŋu ní kí yòon̄ kuteeu kí cáá sāā Jɔɔdan buŋŋu. 23An puee ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu di nìn yāntì timbi u-nibul ŋúń ki jáń ki fōō Amɔɔr yab tiŋki bi-cee, ní sii là kí cúú kitiŋ gbanti kí fōō ti-ceeee? 24Man nyí a ŋúb́ tin kɔkɔ ní a-waal Keemoosi tīī-see naa! Kin ba pu ní timbi ń taa nín̄ yì tin ní ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu dūu ŋá ti-ŋaanee? 25A dàkafī yii a jítiǹ Moowaab bɔtiu Balaaki, Siipɔɔr jipɔɔn níii? A ká u táká Isirayeel yab ki dāa nín lì yii u làá já nì baaa? 26Isirayeel yab nìn kāl̀ Eesbɔn tiŋki nì ki-timbilimmu, ki kāl̀ Arooweer tiŋki nì ki-timbilimmu, ki kāl̀ ntimu mun kɔkɔ pée bí ki nákáǹ Arinɔn buŋgbaŋŋee abin alaataa ata ní. Ba pu ní naa nìn fātìi fōō an timmuee bi-cee ŋyunti gbanti? 27Mbaamɔn pu, man kaa yīntiǹ-si tiba. Ama a nín bí ki jáà nì mi kujaau min nee, á nīn nyí yii sii di yīntiǹ-mi. Ti-Dindaan baba di sá Ubɔsoonli, úǹ di làá sòoǹ Isirayeel yab nì Amɔn yab bɔti díǹ nee.>»
28Ama Amɔn yab bɔtiu kaa nìn pílifì tibɔti tin Jeefita nìn yāntì bi cáań ki tùkū-uee.
Jeefita pōoǹ ti-Dindaan ipoon
29Ti-Dindaan Fam nìn gbí Jeefita. U nìn yíkì ki dī Galaadi nì Manasee timmu pú, ki pɔ́ĺ ki dī Miisipa, Galaadi timbiliiki pú, ní ki dī niin ki kɔ́ Amɔn yab tiŋkin. 30Jeefita nìn pūtì ki pōoǹ ti-Dindaan yii: «A yaa lafun dū Amɔn yab ki ŋá m-ŋaan ki yāntì m jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bee, 31unil un di yaa láa péé ki nyáń m-cindin ki túŋkì-mi nsanni ŋyunti ŋun ní m yaa láa nyánní Amɔn yab tiŋkin ki fātìi bāań nì alaafiyee, m làá dāá dū udaan kí ŋá saraawɔkaa kí tīī sii ti-Dindaan.» 32Jeefita nìn lafun kɔ́ Amɔn yab tiŋki pu ki jáń nì bi ní ti-Dindaan dū-bi ki ŋá u-ŋaan. 33U nìn jáń ki fōō ntimu mmuŋku ní, ki yōoǹ Arooweer tiŋki ki tin cáa sāā Miiniiti tiŋki kpaanyɔkɔ, ní ki fātìi yōoǹ ki tin cáa sāā Abeel-Keeramiim tiŋkin. An nìn baasii sá dijajikpaandi ní ki tīī Isirayeel yab, di sá ní Isirayeel yab nìn nyīī Amɔn yab ki gùl̄ bi-taapu.
Jeefita dū u-bisal ki ŋá saraa ki tīī ti-Dindaan
34Ŋyunti ŋun Jeefita nìn fātìi bàn̄ Miisipa tiŋkin ki làá kɔ́ u-cindinee, ní u-bisal nyánní ki ŋúb́ kigaŋgaŋ ki bɔ̀ɔ́ ki ŋōoń ki túŋkí-u nsanni. Jeefita bisal gbanti di nìn pée sá u-bibaabil. Waa nìn gíti màl̄ kibininjabikaaa, kaa nìn màl̄ kibinimpubiki ki kútì u-bisal gbanti pu. 35Jeefita nín nìn pée wál̀ u-bisal túŋkiń-uee, ní u dáaĺ ki cátì u-wanti tin u nìn pēēyee ní ki bí yii: «Óò, m-bisal, a kɔ́ǹ-mi kunimbaaun. Sii di yì nnaabu ŋun dòoń-mi nee. Di sá yii m gíti dáá pōoǹ ti-Dindaan ipoon ní kaa ti ŋūǹ kí yíí yii maa làá ŋá tin ní m pōoǹ-uee.» 36Ama ní u-bisal kíí-u yii: «M-baa, a nín gíti dáá pōoǹ ti-Dindaan ipoonee, ŋá tin ní a pōoǹ-u yii a làá ŋée. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan di yāntì a ŋúń ki tɔ̀n̄ a-nannanliibi Amɔn yab ipɔntoon.» 37Ní u nìkī ki lī u-baa yii: «Ama kuwambaantiiu kun m làá mèè-see di sá yii, á pɔ̄-mi nsan ḿ nīn bí dimaŋfalin kí gíti bà iŋmal ili man nì m-bɔɔbi ń nóó kí cù ajoonni kí sɔ̄ m nín làá kpú m-sapɔnti poon kaa béè uninjee pu.» 38Ní Jeefita pú u-bisal nsan ki yāntì u búntì ki cūtìi ŋá iŋmal ili ajoonni u nì u-bɔɔbi, ki súń u nín làá kpú u-sapɔnti poon kaa béè uninjee pu. 39Iŋmal ilee jítèe, ní Jeefita bisal fātìi gítìń u-baa cee ní u-baa dū-u ki ŋá u nín pōoǹ yii u làá ŋá puee. Too, u nín kaa nìn béè uninja ní ki kpíìyee pu ní an dūu kpántì dikoobil Isirayeel tiŋkin. 40Dikoobil gbanti di sá yii dibindi kamaayee, Isirayeel sapɔmbi kɔkɔ ń cù kí kpāfì kí sɔ̄ ugalaadija Jeefita bisal pu iwiin inaa dibindi poon.

english_text:
The Ephraim Tribe Fights Jephthah's Army
1The men of the Ephraim tribe got together an army and went across the Jordan River to Zaphon to meet with Jephthah. They said, “Why did you go to war with the Ammonites without asking us to help? Just for that, we're going to burn down your house with you inside!”
2“But I did ask for your help,” Jephthah answered. “That was back when the people of Gilead and I were having trouble with the Ammonites, and you wouldn't do a thing to help us. 3So when we realized you weren't coming, we risked our lives and attacked the Ammonites. And the Lord let us defeat them. There's no reason for you to come here today to attack me.”
4But the men from Ephraim said, “You people of Gilead are nothing more than refugees from Ephraim. You even live on land that belongs to the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh.”
So Jephthah called together the army of Gilead, then they attacked and defeated the army from Ephraim. 5The army of Gilead also posted guards at all the places where the soldiers from Ephraim could cross the Jordan River to return to their own land.
Whenever one of the men from Ephraim would try to cross the river, the guards would say, “Are you from Ephraim?”
“No,” the man would answer, “I'm not from Ephraim.”
6The guards would then tell them to say “Shibboleth,” because they knew that people of Ephraim could say “Sibboleth,” but not “Shibboleth.”
If the man said “Sibboleth,” the guards would grab him and kill him right there. Altogether, 42,000 men from Ephraim were killed in the battle and at the Jordan.
7Jephthah was a leader of Israel for six years, before he died and was buried in his hometown Mizpah in Gilead.
Ibzan
8Ibzan, the next leader of Israel, came from Bethlehem. 9He had 30 daughters and 30 sons, and he let them all marry outside his clan.
Ibzan was a leader for seven years, 10before he died and was buried in Bethlehem.
Elon
11Elon from the Zebulun tribe was the next leader of Israel. He was a leader for ten years, 12before he died and was buried in Aijalon that belonged to the Zebulun tribe.
Abdon
13-15Abdon the son of Hillel was the next leader of Israel. He had 40 sons and 30 grandsons, and each one of them had his own donkey. Abdon was a leader for eight years, before he died and was buried in his hometown of Pirathon, which is located in the part of the hill country of Ephraim where Amalekites used to live.
translation_text:
Kujaau kɔ́ Jeefita nì Eefiraayiim yab kansikin
1Eefiraayiim yab kóoǹ ki kpáfì ní ki dūtì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ki cūtì Saafɔn tiŋkin ki bālifì Jeefita yii: «Ba pu ní a kɔ́ Amɔn yab tiŋkin a-baba ki cūtìi jáń nì bi kaa yíiń-ti ti nì si ń nóó kí cù? Ti làá wà a-dicaŋku ŋŋmi kí kpáaǹ sisi a-ba!» 2Ní Jeefita kíí-bi yii: «Man nì m-nib nìn bí kujaau pu an pɔ̄ɔ̄, ti nì Amɔn yab. M nín nìn yíiń-nee, naa nìn dɔ́miń ki fīī-mi bi-ŋaan. 3M nín nìn ká yii naa bíi dòoń kí fīī-mee, maa mɔ́tì m-maŋfal pu ní ki kɔ́ Amɔn yab tiŋkin ki jáń nì bi, ní ti-Dindaan dū-bi ki ŋá m-ŋaan. Too, ba gíti ŋá ní ni yíkìń díǹ nee kí dāá já nì mi?» 4Niinee ní Jeefita kpáfì Galaadi janjaliibi kɔkɔ ní bi jáń nì Eefiraayiim naakookun yab ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi. Kun pu bi nìn jáń kujaau gbantee di sá yii Eefiraayiim yab nìn lī-bi yii: «Nimbi Galaadi yab, ni sá Eefiraayiim naakookun nib ní ki yíkì Eefiraayiim yab kansikin ki sáǹní ki dɔ́miń ki kā Manasee naakookun yab kansikin!» 5Galaadi yab nìn pīiǹ Eefiraayiim naakookun yab isan in bi nìn dìŋfī ki dùtī Jɔɔdan buŋŋuee. Ŋyunti ŋun ní Eefiraayiim naakookun yab bin nìn sáǹ ki ŋmátèe kansikin ubɔ yaa nìn bāań ki là kí dùtēe, ní Galaadi yab ń bàlifì-u yii: «A sá Eefiraayiim niliu níii?» Udaan yaa kíí yii: «Aayeeyee», 6ní Galaadi yab ń bí-u yii: «Lì yii: <Ciibooleeti>.» Ní udaan ń bí yii: <Siibooleeti>, kun puee Eefirayiim yab kaa nìn ŋūǹ kí lì an nín bàà sá bí lì puee. Niinee ní bí cúú udaan kí làntì kí bíĺ laakin ní bi dìŋfī ki dùtī Jɔɔdan buŋŋuee caŋin niin. An yuntiŋuee, bi nìn kūū Eefiraayiim janjaliibi binib kutukub imuŋku ili nì bili ní.
7Ugalaadija Jeefita nìn kpōotì Isirayeel yab abin aluu ní ki dāa nín kpíì, ní bi síb́-u Galaadi timmu kiba poon.
Yibisan nì Eelɔn nì Abidɔn
8Jeefita kúm boonee, Yibisan un sá Beetileem tiŋkinee di nìn kpōotì Isirayeel yab. 9U nìn cáá jipɔmbi mmuŋku nì saalaa ní ki nìn cáá bisalib mun mmuŋku nì saalaa. U nìn dū u-bisalib ki tīī biniyaŋyambi ticati ní ki nìn cáá bisapɔnnyanyambi mmuŋku nì saalaa ki tīī u-jipɔmbi. U nìn kpōotì Isirayeel yab abin aluli ní. 10Yibisan nìn kpíì ní bi síb́-u Beetileem tiŋkin.
11Yibisan kúm boonee, Eelɔn un nìn sá Sabulɔn naakookunee di nìn kpōotì Isirayeel yab. U nìn kpōotì Isirayeel yab abin saalaa ní. 12Eelɔn nìn kpíì ní bi síb́-u Eelɔn, Sabulɔn tiŋki poon.
13Eelɔn kúm boonee, Yileel un nìn sá Pireeyatɔn tiŋkinee jipɔɔn Abidɔn di nìn kpōotì Isirayeel yab. 14Abidɔn nìn cáá jipɔmbi imuŋku ili nì naantiibi mmuŋku nì saalaa ní, ní bi nìn kàal̀ mmanjamu imuŋku ita nì saalaa. U nìn kpōotì Isirayeel yab abin anii ní. 15Yileel un nìn sá Pireeyatɔn tiŋkinee jipɔɔn Abidɔn nìn kpíì ní bi síb́-u Pireeyatɔn tiŋki kin sá Eefiraayiim naakookun timmu kibee poon, Amaleeki yab jool pu.

english_text:
Samson Is Born
1Once again the Israelites started disobeying the Lord. So he let the Philistines take control of Israel for 40 years.
2Manoah from the tribe of Dan lived in the town of Zorah. His wife was not able to have children, 3-5 but one day an angel from the Lord appeared to her and said:
You have never been able to have any children, but very soon you will be pregnant and have a son. He will belong to God from the day he is born, so his hair must never be cut. And even before he is born, you must not drink any wine or beer or eat any food forbidden by God's laws.
Your son will begin to set Israel free from the Philistines.
6She went to Manoah and said, “A prophet who looked like an angel of God came and talked to me. I was so frightened, that I didn't even ask where he was from. He didn't tell me his name, 7but he did say that I'm going to have a baby boy. I'm not supposed to drink any wine or beer or eat any food forbidden by God's laws. Our son will belong to God for as long as he lives.”
8Then Manoah prayed, “Our Lord, please send that prophet again and let him tell us what to do for the son we are going to have.”
9God answered Manoah's prayer, and the angel went back to Manoah's wife while she was resting in the fields. Manoah wasn't there at the time, 10so she found him and said, “That same man is here again! He's the one I saw the other day.”
11Manoah went with his wife and asked the man, “Are you the one who spoke to my wife?”
“Yes, I am,” he answered.
12Manoah then asked, “When your promise comes true, what rules must he obey and what will be his work?”
13“Your wife must be careful to do everything I told her,” the Lord's angel answered. 14“She must not eat or drink anything made from grapes. She must not drink wine or beer or eat anything forbidden by God's laws. I told her exactly what to do.”
15“Please,” Manoah said, “stay here with us for just a little while, and we'll fix a young goat for you to eat.” 16Manoah didn't realize that he was really talking to one of the Lord's angels.
The angel answered, “I can stay for a little while, although I won't eat any of your food. But if you would like to offer the goat as a sacrifice to the Lord, that would be fine.”
17Manoah said, “Tell us your name, so we can honor you after our son is born.”
18“No,” the angel replied. “You don't need to know my name. And if you did, you couldn't understand it.”
19So Manoah took a young goat over to a large rock he had chosen for an altar, and he built a fire on the rock. Then he killed the goat, and offered it with some grain as a sacrifice to the Lord. But then an amazing thing happened. 20The fire blazed up toward the sky, and the Lord's angel went up toward heaven in the fire. Manoah and his wife bowed down low when they saw what happened.
21Although the angel didn't appear to them again, they realized he was one of the Lord's angels. 22Manoah said, “We have seen an angel. Now we're going to die.”
23“The Lord isn't going to kill us,” Manoah's wife responded. “The Lord accepted our sacrifice and grain offering, and he let us see something amazing. Besides, he told us that we're going to have a son.”
24Later, Manoah's wife did give birth to a son, and she named him Samson. As the boy grew, the Lord blessed him. 25Then, while Samson was staying at Dan's Camp between the towns of Zorah and Eshtaol, the Spirit of the Lord took control of him.
translation_text:
Samsɔn màaltam
1Isirayeel yab nìn fātìi kíĺ ki bíi ŋáań tin kaa kítì ti-Dindaan ceeyee ní ti-Dindaan dū-bi ki ŋá Fiiliistii yab ŋaan abin imuŋku ili.
2Uninja ubɔ nìn bí ki nìn sá Sooreeya tiŋkin, Daani naakookun maaliŋu ŋubɔ poon, ní bi nìn yíì-u yii Manoowa. U-nimpuu nìn sá uŋmaŋŋmanti ní, waa nìn cáá kibiki. 3Ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋu nìn lēē ŋu-ba ki dàkā unimpu gbanti ki bí-u yii: «M nyí a nín sá uŋmaŋŋmanti kaa cáá kibikee, ama a làá cáá dipool kí màal̀ kibininjabiki. 4Kí yòon̄ díǹ kí nīn cée, á taa ti nyɔ̀ ndamam àá ndaam min kamaa pɔ̄ɔ̄yee, kí taa jī tijin tin kamaa kaa bí circiree, 5kibininjabiki kin a làá cáá dipool kí màal̀ee pu. Bɔlfi ń taa pée gbēē kibikee yil, di sá kí yòon̄ ŋwiin ŋun ní a làá díkí u-poolee, u làá nīn sá un bi dūu sú Unimbɔtee ní. Úǹ di làá kíĺ kí fīī Isirayeel yab Fiiliistii yab ŋaan.» 6Ní unimpuee nín kùǹ ki cūtìi máafì u-cal yii: «Unimbɔti niliu ubɔ dɔ́miń m-cee. U náań nì Unimbɔti tuuŋŋu ní a yaa kpēē-uee, an cáá tifaandi. Maa bālifì laakin ní u sée, ní u mun kaa tùkū-mi u-yindi. 7U bí-mi yii: <Á nīn nyí yii a làá cáá dipool kí màal̀ kibininjabiki. Kí yòon̄ díǹ kí nīn cée, á taa ti nyɔ̀ ndamamaaa, kí taa ti nyɔ̀ ndaam min pɔ̄ɔ̄yee. Á taa jī tijin tin kaa bí circiree mun, kun puee kibininjabiki kin a làá màal̀ee, bi làá dū-kì kí sú Unimbɔti ní kí dāá sāā ki-kúm dal.>»
8Niinee ní Manoowa mēē ti-Dindaan ki lī yii: «M-Dindaan, m gbāam̀-si, yàntī Unimbɔti niliu un a túnní ti-ceeyee ń fàtīí gítiń kí dàkà-ti min ti máaǹ kí ŋá kí tīī kibikee bi yaa láa màl̄-kèe.» 9Unimbɔti nìn fōō Manoowa wimmeem ní ki nìn yāntì u-tuuŋŋuee fātìi gítìń unimpuee cee. U nìn kā bukpaan ní, ama u-cal Manoowa kaa nìn bí u-cee. 10Niin niin ní unimpuee yíkìi sáǹ ki cūtìi tùkū u-cal yii: «Kpèè, kijapaai kin nìn dɔ́miń m-cee yaadalee fātìi tí lēē u-ba ki dàkā-mi!» 11Ní Manoowa yíkì ki páaǹ u-nimpuu boon ki nín cá kijapaayee cee ki bàn̄ ki bālifì-u yii: «Sii di sá kijapaai kin nìn sòon̄ nì unimpu neeyeeee?» Ní kijapaayee kíí yii: «Iiin, an sá man!» 12Ní Manoowa bālifì-u yii: «Kɔŋkɔnnee, a nín lī puee yaa láa ŋá mimmee, akoobil ŋilaŋ ní tí kòò kibikee maŋfal wiiŋyi nì ditundi din kì làá tɔ̄ee pu?» 13Ní ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋuee kíí Manoowa yii: «Tin kɔkɔ ní m kōoǹ a-nimpuuee, ú kòò-tì. 14Ú taa pée dáká tin kamaa ní bi yaa dū fiinyi subil ki ŋée. Ú taa nyɔ̀ ndamam àá ndaam min pɔ̄ɔ̄yee. Ú taa jī tijin tin kamaa kaa bí circiree, ní kí ŋá tin kɔkɔ ní m tùkū-u yii ú ŋée.» 15Niinee ní Manoowa bí ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋuee yii: «Yàntī tí tàan̄-si fiii. Ti làá kpɔ̀ diŋɔbil kí tɔ́kɔń kí cáań-si.» 16Ní ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋuee kíí-u yii: «Báà a yaa tāaǹ-maaa, maa làá jī tijin tin a làá ŋá kí tīī-mee. Ama a yaa là kí ŋá saraawɔkaa, a ŋūǹ kí ŋá kí tīī ti-Dindaan.» Di sá yii Manoowa kaa nìn nyí yii u nì ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋu di nìn bíi sòoǹ. 17Ní Manoowa bí ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋuee yii: «Bi yíì-si yii ba? Tùkù-ti án nín làá ŋá pu ní tibɔti tin a sòon̄ee yaa láa ŋée tí dāá nyɔ̄ŋkì-see.» 18Ní ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋuee bí-u yii: «Ba pu ní a baasii là kí béé m-yindi ní? Dì sá maamaaci yindi ní.» 19Manoowa nìn bɔ́ntì diŋɔbil nì saraa wanti ki dūu páaǹ ditaŋkpal pu ki ŋá saraa ki tīī ti-Dindaan un ŋáań maamaaci tuuŋŋee. Manoowa nì u-nimpuu nìn kíǹ ki yú ki kpèé. 20Bi dāa kpēēyee, ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋuee bí aŋmilimbil ŋin nìn nyēē nsaraafan pu ki jɔ́ḿee poon ki nín jɔ́ḿ yilpu. Manoowa nì u-nimpuu nín ká mimmee ní bi tātìi dōoǹ dicincibil. 21Ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋuee kaa nìn gíti lēē ŋu-ba ki dàkā Manoowa nì u-nimpuu. Niin ní Manoowa nìn dūu béè yii kijapaayee nìn lafun sá ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋu. 22Ní Manoowa bí u-nimpuu yii: «Ti nín pée ká Unimbɔti nì ti-nimbiliŋ nee, ti làá pée kpú ní.» 23Ama ní u-nimpuu kíí-u yii: «Ti-Dindaan yaa bàà là kí kpɔ̀-tee, waa bàà fòol̄ ti-saraawɔkaau nì ti-saraau. Waa bàà làá dàkà-ti tin kɔkɔ ti ká nee, kaa bàà làá tùkù-ti tibɔti tin u tùkū-ti kɔŋkɔnnee.»
24Unimpuee nìn màl̄ kibininjabiki ní ki pú-kì diyindi yii Samsɔn. Kibiki gbanti nìn wíiǹ, ní ti-Dindaan nìn bīiǹ ki-boon. 25Maanee-Daani tiŋki kin bí Sooreeya nì Eesitawool timmu kansikinee poon ní ti-Dindaan Fam nìn yāntì Samsɔn péé péé ki nyántì u-pɔŋŋu ki dàkā.

english_text:
Samson Gets Married
1One day, Samson went to Timnah, where he saw a Philistine woman. 2When he got back home, he told his parents, “I saw a Philistine woman in Timnah, and I want to marry her. Get her for me!”
3His parents answered, “There are a lot of women in our clan and even more in the rest of Israel. Those Philistines are pagans. Why would you want to marry one of their women?”
“She looks good to me,” Samson answered. “Get her for me!”
4At that time, the Philistines were in control of Israel, and the Lord wanted to stir up trouble for them. That's why he made Samson desire that woman.
5As Samson and his parents reached the vineyards near Timnah, a fierce young lion suddenly roared and attacked Samson. 6But the Lord's Spirit took control of Samson, and with his bare hands he tore the lion apart, as though it had been a young goat. His parents didn't know what he had done, and he didn't tell them.
7When they got to Timnah, Samson talked to the woman, and he was sure that she was the one for him.
8Later, Samson returned to Timnah for the wedding. And when he came near the place where the lion had attacked, he left the road to see what was left of the lion. He was surprised to see that bees were living in the lion's skeleton, and that they had made some honey. 9He scooped up the honey in his hands and ate some of it as he walked along. When he got back to his parents, he gave them some of the honey, and they ate it too. But he didn't tell them he had found the honey in the skeleton of a lion.
10While Samson's father went to make the final arrangements with the bride and her family, Samson threw a big party, as grooms usually did. 11When the Philistines saw what Samson was like, they told 30 of their young men to stay with him at the party.
12Samson told the 30 young men, “This party will last for seven days. Let's make a bet: I'll tell you a riddle, and if you can tell me the answer before the party is over, I'll give each of you a shirt and a full change of clothing. 13But if you can't tell me the answer, then each of you will have to give me a shirt and a full change of clothing.”
“It's a bet!” the Philistines said. “Tell us the riddle.”
14Samson said:
Once so strong and mighty—
now so sweet and tasty!
Three days went by, and the Philistine young men had not come up with the right answer. 15Finally, on the seventh day of the party they went to Samson's bride and said, “You had better trick your husband into telling you the answer to his riddle. Have you invited us here just to rob us? If you don't find out the answer, we will burn you and your family to death.”
16Samson's bride went to him and started crying in his arms. “You must really hate me,” she sobbed. “If you loved me at all, you would have told me the answer to your riddle.”
“But I haven't even told my parents the answer!” Samson replied. “Why should I tell you?”
17For the entire seven days of the party, she had been whining and trying to get the answer from him. But that seventh day she put so much pressure on Samson that he finally gave in and told her the answer. She went straight to the young men and told them.
18Before sunset that day, the men of the town went to Samson with this answer:
A lion is the strongest—
honey is the sweetest!
Samson replied,
This answer you have given me
doubtless came
from my bride-to-be.
19Then the Lord's Spirit took control of Samson. He went to Ashkelon, where he killed 30 men and took their clothing. Samson then gave it to the 30 young men at Timnah and stormed back home to his own family.
20The father of the bride made Samson's wife marry one of the 30 young men that had been at Samson's party.
translation_text:
Samsɔn cáá Fiiliistii yab sapɔɔŋwu ubɔ
1Dalbee Samsɔn sīntì Tiimina tiŋkin ní ki tin dūu ká Fiiliistii yab sapɔmbi kansikin usapɔnnyaan ubɔ. 2U nín nìn fātìi jɔ́m̀ u-tiŋkinee ní ki sòon̄ unimpuee bɔti u-baa nì u-na cee ki bí yii: «M nín cūtì Tiimina tiŋkinee, m ká usapɔɔn ubɔ Fiiliistii yab sapɔmbi kansikin. Kɔŋkɔnnee m là yii ní cáá úǹ ní kí tīī-mi.» 3Ní u-baa nì u-na bí-u yii: «Mimmee usapɔɔn kaa bí a-maaliŋu nì a-nibul kɔkɔ sapɔmbi poon á cááaaa? Ba di ŋá ní a là kí cáá Fiiliistii yab bin kaa gíí akpancan nee sapɔmbi ubɔ ní?» Ní Samsɔn bí u-baa yii: «Usapɔɔn gbanti ní m pée là yii á cáá kí tīī-mi, kun puee úǹ di kɔ́-mi!» 4Samsɔn baa nì u-na kaa nìn nyí yii ti-Dindaan di nìn bíi téekí bi-jipɔɔn ú lēē yii u là an nimpuuee. Ti-Dindaan nìn bíi nyàab̀ nsan ŋun ní u làá dī kí táká Fiiliistii yab tibɔtee ní, kun puee ŋyunti gbantee, u-nibul Isirayeel yab nìn bí Fiiliistii yab taapu ní.
5Samsɔn nìn nín sìntī Tiimina tiŋkin, u nì u-baa nì u-na. Ŋyunti ŋun bi bàn̄ fiinyi sufii in yú Tiimina tiŋki caŋinee, kpalaayee digbikintipɔmbil diba nyánní kumooun, ki mùuǹ ki túŋkí Samsɔn. 6Niin ní ti-Dindaan Fam kɔ́ Samsɔn ní u cúú digbikintipɔmbilee ŋŋancal, ki dáaĺ ki tɔ̄ntì-dì kii bi nín dátí kí tɔ̀ntī kiŋɔbiki puee. Ama waa nìn tùkū u-baa nì u-na tin ní u nìn ŋée. 7Míǹ boonee u nìn nín sìntī Tiimina tiŋkin ki cūtìi sòon̄ nì usapɔɔnee. Usapɔɔnee nìn kɔ́-u tikpil. 8Iwiŋkaaŋkaa boonee, Samsɔn nìn fātìi yíkì u-dumpu ki nín gítí Tiimina tiŋkin kí cùú cáá unimpuee. U bàn̄ laakin u nìn kūū gbikinti ki bíl̀ee ní ki pāatì kí kpèè digbikintikpilee. U nìn ká dinaŋgbansikitil kā gbikintee wunti poon nì tisiil. 9Ní Samsɔn lēē tisiil ki ŋá u-ŋaan ki còom̄ ki ŋmóò ki cá. U cōom̀ ki fātìi cúú u-baa nì u-nee, ní ki lēē tisiil ki tīī-bi ní bi mun ŋmɔ́, ama waa nìn tùkū-bi yii digbikintikpil poon ní u lēeń tisiil.
Samsɔn pɔ́ɔǹ Fiiliistii yab mpɔ́ɔn
10Samsɔn baa nìn sīntì unimpuee dumpu ní Samsɔn cūtìi bɔ́ntì dinimpucaal jiŋaaliu niin, kii binaacimpɔmbi nín nìn pée ŋáań puee. 11Fiiliistii yab nín nìn pée ká-uee, ní bi lēē binaacimpɔmbi mmuŋku nì saalaa bí nīn bí u-cee. 12Ní Samsɔn bí-bi yii: «M làá pɔ́ɔǹ-ni mpɔ́ɔn ŋubɔ. Ni yaa ŋúń ki béè-ŋu ní ki lēē ŋu-taapu ki tùkū-mi iwiin iluli in ti làá dūú jī jiŋaal nee poonee, m làá tīī-ni abɔkutifɔkɔ mmuŋku nì saalaa, kí tīī-ni abɔkutikpántikaa mun mmuŋku nì saalaa. 13Ama ni yaa kaa ŋúń ki lēē ŋu-taapu ki tùkū-mee, nimbi di làá tīī man abɔkutifɔkɔ mmuŋku nì saalaa nì abɔkutikpántikaa mun mmuŋku nì saalaa.» Ní bi bí-u yii: «Pɔ́ɔǹ a-pɔɔŋŋu gbanti tí pīlifì!» 14Ní Samsɔn bí-bi yii:
«Un ŋmóò poon
ní tiŋmɔkaal nyánní.
Un pɔ̄ɔ̄yee poon
ní mmɔn nyánní.
An sá ba?»
Iwiin ita dāa dūu jítì, binaacimpɔmbee kaa ŋúń ki lēē mpɔɔnee taapu ki tùkū Samsɔn. 15Ŋwinluluúti dalee ní bi bí Samsɔn nimpuu yii: «Ŋmàtiǹ a-cal ú tùkù-ti mpɔɔnee taapu, an yaa sá fám ti làá wà-si ŋŋmi kí kpáaǹ a-baa dicaŋku kɔkɔ. Ni yíiń-ti kí fūkul̀-ti níii?» 16Niinee ní Samsɔn nimpuu bíi sūǹ lɔ̀lɔ ní ki bí-u yii: «A pée ná-mi ní, aa néeń-mi. A pɔ́ɔǹ m-dumpu yab mpɔ́ɔn, ama ní kaa lēē ŋu-taapu ki tùkū-mi.» Ní Samsɔn kíí-u yii: «Maa lēē mpɔ́ɔn gbanti taapu ki tùkū m-baa nì m-na gba, ní ki dāa cáa tùkū siii?» 17Samsɔn nimpuu nìn súń míǹ ní kinyɔmmɔŋ kin bi dūu jíń jiŋaalee kɔkɔ. Ŋwinluluúti dalee, Samsɔn nimpuu nìn páb́-u an gíti lákáǹee, ní Samsɔn lēē mpɔɔnee taapu ki tùkū-u. Ní unimpu yíkìi nín cá ki cūtìi lēē mpɔɔnee taapu ki tùkū u-yab. 18Ŋwinluluúti gbanti dal kí wàatī ŋwìiń ń jēetée ní kitiŋee nib bí Samsɔn yii:
«Ba gíti mɔ̄ ki jítiǹ tisiil?
Ba gíti pɔ̄ɔ̄ ki jítiǹ gbikinti?»
Ní Samsɔn kíí-bi yii: «Ni yaa kaa bàà dū m-nasaliu ki kùn̄ tikpaal, naa bàà làá ŋmā kí béé man pɔɔŋŋu nee taapu!»
19Niinee ní ti-Dindaan Fam gbí Samsɔn ní u yíkì ki nín sìntī Asikeelɔn tiŋkin. U bàn̄ ní ki cúú niin yab binib mmuŋku nì saalaa ki kūū, ki fúkúl̀ bi-wanti kɔkɔ ní ki cáań bi-bɔkutiŋ ki tīī binib bin nìn ŋúń ki lēē u-pɔɔŋŋuee taapu ki tùkū-uee. Míǹ boonee ní u fātìi nín kùǹ u-baa dumpu, ki díkí diŋuul an kaa cáá bí lì. 20Bi nìn dū unimpuee úǹ ki tīī Samsɔn bɔɔ u nì un nìn pée nóó u-nimpucaal jiŋaaliu yuntiŋuee ticati.

english_text:
1Later, during the wheat harvest, Samson went to visit the young woman he thought was still his wife. He brought along a young goat as a gift and said to her father, “I want to go into my wife's bedroom.”
“You can't do that,” he replied. 2“When you left the way you did, I thought you were divorcing her. So I arranged for her to marry one of the young men who were at your party. But my younger daughter is even prettier, and you can have her as your wife.”
3“This time,” Samson answered, “I have a good reason for really hurting some Philistines.”
Samson Takes Revenge
4Samson went out and caught 300 foxes and tied them together in pairs with oil-soaked rags around their tails. 5Then Samson took the foxes into the Philistine wheat fields that were ready to be harvested. He set the rags on fire and let the foxes go. The wheat fields went up in flames, and so did the stacks of wheat that had already been cut. Even the Philistine vineyards and olive orchards burned.
6Some of the Philistines started asking around, “Who could have done such a thing?”
“It was Samson,” someone told them. “He married the daughter of that man in Timnah, but then the man gave Samson's wife to one of the men at the wedding.”
The Philistine leaders went to Timnah and burned to death Samson's wife and her father.
7When Samson found out what they had done, he went to them and said, “You killed them! And I won't rest until I get even with you.” 8Then Samson started hacking them to pieces with his sword.
Samson left Philistia and went to live in the cave at Etam Rock. 9But it wasn't long before the Philistines invaded Judah and set up a huge army camp at Jawbone.
10The people of Judah asked, “Why have you invaded our land?”
The Philistines answered, “We've come to get Samson. We're going to do the same things to him that he did to our people.”
11Three thousand men from Judah went to the cave at Etam Rock and said to Samson, “Don't you know that the Philistines rule us, and they will punish us for what you did?”
“I was only getting even with them,” Samson replied. “They did the same things to me first.”
12“We came here to tie you up and turn you over to them,” said the men of Judah.
“I won't put up a fight,” Samson answered, “but you have to promise not to hurt me yourselves.”
13-14“We promise,” the men said. “We will only tie you up and turn you over to the Philistines. We won't kill you.” Then they tied up his hands and arms with two brand-new ropes and led him away from Etam Rock.
When the Philistines saw that Samson was being brought to their camp at Jawbone, they started shouting and ran toward him. But the Lord's Spirit took control of Samson, and Samson broke the ropes, as though they were pieces of burnt cloth. 15Samson glanced around and spotted the jawbone of a donkey. The jawbone had not yet dried out, so it was still hard and heavy. Samson grabbed it and started hitting Philistines—he killed 1,000 of them! 16After the fighting was over, he made up this poem about what he had done to the Philistines:
I used a donkey's jawbone
to kill a thousand men;
I beat them with this jawbone
over and over again.
17Samson tossed the jawbone on the ground and decided to call the place Jawbone Hill. It is still called that today.
18Samson was so thirsty that he prayed, “Our Lord, you helped me win a battle against a whole army. Please don't let me die of thirst now. Those heathen Philistines will carry off my dead body.”
19Samson was tired and weary, but God sent water gushing from a rock. Samson drank some and felt strong again.
Samson named the place Caller Spring, because he had called out to God for help. The spring is still there at Jawbone.
20Samson was a leader of Israel for 20 years, but the Philistines were still the rulers of Israel.
translation_text:
Samsɔn sēē Fiiliistii yab sati ŋŋmi
1Iwiŋkaaŋkaa boonee, an nìn ŋmāntì ŋyunti ŋun bi cēē bilee jintee, ní Samsɔn nìn nín gítí kí cùú màntì u-nimpuu pu. U nìn ŋúb́ diŋɔbil diba ní ki bí yii: «M là kí kɔ́ m-nimpuu didooŋkaaku poon.» Ama u-nimpuu baa nìn yíì kaa pú-u nsan u kɔ́. 2U nìn bí Samsɔn yii: «Man dākafì yii aa ti pée là-u ní, an puee man dū-u ki tīī a-bɔɔ un nìn pée nóó-si a-nimpucaal jiŋaaliunee ticati. Ama u-naal bí, ki gíti ŋān̄ ki jítiǹ-u gba. A ŋūǹ kí yòon̄ úǹ kí téeǹ u-maan yil!» 3Ní Samsɔn bí-bi yii: «Min bí nee m yaa ŋá Fiiliistii yab inikpiti, ubɔ kaa làá kɔ̄kɔl̀-mi.»
4Niinee ní Samsɔn cūtìi cúú ŋŋɔkɔmu alaataa ata ní ki bɔ́ntì iŋminaapool mun míǹ. U ŋée ní ki kpáfì ŋŋɔkɔmu muli muli, mu-juuŋi túĺ tɔb. Ní u cúú ajuuyee ki gbìn̄ gbìn̄ tɔb, ní ki dū ŋŋminaapool ŋubɔ ki nēeǹ ajuu ali gbindi kamaa kansikin. 5U ŋá mimmee ní ki dū ŋŋmi ki sēē iŋminaapool, ki gíiǹ ŋŋɔkɔmu ki líì ní mu nín kóò Fiiliistii yab satin. Ŋŋmi nìn wùn̄ bilee un bi nìn cáń ki bíl̀ee nì un dáá gbíntìi yú baa láá cáńee, ki wùn̄ ki kpáaǹ fiinyi sufii nì ɔliifi sufii. 6Fiiliistii yab bālifì yii: «Ŋma ŋá mimmee?» Ní binib kíí-bi yii: «An sá utiiminaja coo Samsɔn di ŋá míǹ, kun puee u-coo gbanti fōō u-nimpuu ní ki dūu tīī u-bɔɔ un nìn nóó-u u-nimpucaal jiŋaaliunee ticati.» Ní Fiiliistii yab nín jɔ́ḿ Tiimina tiŋkin ki cūtìi wùn̄ unimpu gbanti ŋŋmi, ki kpáaǹ u-baa. 7Samsɔn tùkū-bi yii: «Too, ní béé yii ni nín ŋá min nee puee, m yaa kaa tɔ̀n̄-ni ipɔntoon maa làá dūú cà.» 8U nìn cūtìi jáń nì Fiiliistii yab ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi. Míǹ boon ní u nín sìntī Eetaam tiŋkin ki cūtìi kɔ́ ntaŋkpalɔkɔ ŋubɔn.
Samsɔn dū kimaŋ nyɔɔkpaweeŋŋu ki pɔ̄fì Fiiliistii yab
9Fiiliistii yab nìn jɔ́m̀ Juuda tiŋkin ki ŋātì dijanjanaapaal, ki kāaǹ bi-janjaliibi ki tin sāā mpaan ŋun bi yíì yii Leeyiiyee. 10Ní Juuda naakookun yab bālifì-bi yii: «Ba pu ní ni jɔ́mìń kí jáǹ-ti ní?» Ní Fiiliistii yab kíí Juuda naakookun yab yii: «Ti jɔ́mìń kí cúú Samsɔn kí ŋá-u kii u nín ŋá-ti puee kí téeǹ ní.» 11Niinee ní Juuda naakookun yab bininjab kutukub bita yíkì ki nín sìntī Eetaam tiŋkin, ntaŋkpalɔkɔ ŋun poon Samsɔn nìn bée ki bí-u yii: «Saa nyí ti nín bí Fiiliistii yab taapueeee? Ba bɔti ní a ŋá-ti mimmee?» Ní Samsɔn kíí-bi yii: «Bi nín ŋá-mi puee, míǹ ní ma mun ŋá-bi ki téeǹ!» 12Ní bi bí-u yii: «Too, timbi sīntìń kí bóob́-si iŋmii kí cáá-si kí ŋúbiǹ Fiiliistii yab ní!» Ní Samsɔn bí-bi yii: «Ní pùtīmaan yii nimbi ni-ba kaa làá kpɔ̀-mi.» 13Ní bi kíí-u yii: «Aayee, ti pée là kí bóob́-si iŋmii kí cáá-si ki cùnnì kí tīī-bi ní, taa làá kpɔ̀-si.» Ní u kíí bi dū iŋmipɔɔn ili ki bóob́-u ki cáá-u ki nyántì ntaŋkpalɔkɔn. 14Ŋyunti ŋun u tóob́ kí bà mpaan ŋun bi yíì Leeyiiyee ní Fiiliistii yab túŋkì-u nsanni ki kūuntí mpɔn. Ama ti-Dindaan Fam nìn kɔ́-u ní iŋmii in nìn bóob́ u-ŋaliiyee dūu kpántì kii gulfa ní ŋŋmi wùn̄ee, ní ki gbátì u-ŋaliiyin ki lítì. 15Samsɔn kpēēyee kimaŋ kin bi kūū an kaa láá yúntèe nyɔɔkpaweeŋŋu di dɔ̄ee. Ní u yōoǹ-ŋu ki dūu fátì ki kūū binib kutuku ubɔ. 16Ní Samsɔn bí yii:
«Kimaŋ nyɔɔkpaweeŋŋu
ní m dūu pɔ̄fì-bi.
M dū kimaŋ nyɔɔkpaweeŋŋu
ki kūū binib kutuku ubɔ.»
17U lī míǹ ki ŋmíl̀ee, ní ki dū nnyɔɔkpaweenee ki tɔ́ ki fá ndan, ní bi yíiń laakin ŋu tin lítèe yii Ramati Leeyii, taapu di sá yii <nnyɔɔkpaween gbantaŋki>. 18Ŋyunti gbantee nnyinnyoo nìn bàn̄-u tikpil, ní u tíminsì ki yíiń ti-Dindaan ki lī yii: «Sii di yāntì ní man a-tɔntɔnliu ká dijajikpaandi din bí nee. Mimmee kɔŋkɔnnee nnyinnyoo làá kpɔ̀-mi, ḿ kɔ́ bin kaa gífí nee ŋaanaaa?» 19Unimbɔti nìn yāntì ditaŋkpakpaandi din nìn bí Leeyii paaŋŋu pu ki cáá mbùńee cúu látì, ní nnyim nyánní. Samsɔn nìn nyùn̄ u-nimbiliŋ cúu ŋāatì ní u fātìi ká mpɔn. An pu ní bi nìn pú nnyimbul gbantee diyindi yii Eeni-Kooree, taapu di sá yii <un yíińee nyimbuliŋu>. Nnyimbul gbanti dáá gbíntìi bí Leeyii paaŋŋu pu ki dāa sāā díǹ.
20Fiiliistii yab yuntiŋu gbantee, Samsɔn nìn kpōotì Isirayeel yab abin mmuŋku ní.

english_text:
Samson Carries Off the Gates of Gaza
1One day while Samson was in Gaza, he saw a prostitute and went to her house to spend the night. 2The people who lived in Gaza found out he was there, and they decided to kill him at sunrise. So they went to the city gate and waited all night in the guardrooms on each side of the gate.
3But Samson got up in the middle of the night and went to the town gate. He pulled the gate doors and doorposts out of the wall and put them on his shoulders. Then he carried them all the way to the top of the hill that overlooks Hebron, where he set the doors down, still closed and locked.
Delilah Tricks Samson
4Some time later, Samson fell in love with a woman named Delilah, who lived in Sorek Valley. 5The Philistine rulers went to Delilah and said, “Trick Samson into telling you what makes him so strong and what can make him weak. Then we can tie him up so he can't get away. If you find out his secret, we will each give you 1,100 pieces of silver.”
6The next time Samson was at Delilah's house, she asked, “Samson, what makes you so strong? How can I tie you up so you can't get away? Come on, you can tell me.”
7Samson answered, “If someone ties me up with seven new bowstrings that have never been dried, it will make me just as weak as anyone else.”
8-9The Philistine rulers gave seven new bowstrings to Delilah. They also told some of their soldiers to go to Delilah's house and hide in the room where Samson and Delilah were. If the bowstrings made Samson weak, they would be able to capture him.
Delilah tied up Samson with the bowstrings and shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!”
Samson snapped the bowstrings, as though they were pieces of scorched string. The Philistines had not found out why Samson was so strong.
10“You lied and made me look like a fool,” Delilah said. “Now tell me. How can I really tie you up?”
11Samson answered, “Use some new ropes. If I'm tied up with ropes that have never been used, I'll be just as weak as anyone else.”
12Delilah got new ropes, and again some Philistines hid in the room. Then she tied up Samson's arms and shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!”
Samson snapped the ropes as if they were threads.
13“You're still lying and making a fool of me,” Delilah said. “Tell me how I can tie you up!”
“My hair is in seven braids,” Samson replied. “If you weave my braids into the threads on a loom and nail the loom to a wall, then I will be as weak as anyone else.”
14While Samson was asleep, Delilah wove his braids into the threads on a loom and nailed the loom to a wall. Then she shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!”
Samson woke up and pulled the loom free from its posts in the ground and from the nails in the wall. Then he pulled his hair free from the woven cloth.
15“Samson,” Delilah said, “you claim to love me, but you don't mean it! You've made me look like a fool three times now, and you still haven't told me why you are so strong.” 16Delilah started nagging and pestering him day after day, until he couldn't stand it any longer.
17Finally, Samson told her the truth. “I have belonged to God ever since I was born, so my hair has never been cut. If it were ever cut off, my strength would leave me, and I would be as weak as anyone else.”
18Delilah realized that he was telling the truth. So she sent someone to tell the Philistine rulers, “Come to my house one more time. Samson has finally told me the truth.”
The Philistine rulers went to Delilah's house, and they brought along the silver they had promised her. 19Delilah had lulled Samson to sleep with his head resting in her lap. She signaled to one of the Philistine men as she began cutting off Samson's seven braids. And by the time she was finished, Samson's strength was gone. Delilah tied him up 20and shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!”
Samson woke up and thought, “I'll break loose and escape, just as I always do.” He did not realize that the Lord had stopped helping him.
21The Philistines grabbed Samson and poked out his eyes. They took him to the prison in Gaza and chained him up. Then they put him to work, turning a millstone to grind grain. 22But they didn't cut his hair any more, so it started growing back.
23The Philistine rulers threw a big party and sacrificed a lot of animals to their god Dagon. The rulers said:
Samson was our enemy,
but our god Dagon
helped us capture him!
24-25Everyone there was having a good time, and they shouted, “Bring out Samson—he's still good for a few more laughs!”
The rulers had Samson brought from the prison, and when the people saw him, this is how they praised their god:
Samson ruined our crops
and killed our people.
He was our enemy,
but our god helped us
capture him.
They made fun of Samson for a while, then they told him to stand near the columns that supported the roof. 26A young man was leading Samson by the hand, and Samson said to him, “I need to lean against something. Take me over to the columns that hold up the roof.”
27The Philistine rulers were celebrating in a temple packed with people and with 3,000 more on the flat roof. They had all been watching Samson and making fun of him.
28Samson prayed, “Please remember me, Lord God. The Philistines poked out my eyes, but make me strong one last time, so I can take revenge for at least one of my eyes!”
29Samson was standing between the two middle columns that held up the roof. He felt around and found one column with his right hand, and the other with his left hand. 30Then he shouted, “Let me die with the Philistines!” He pushed against the columns as hard as he could, and the temple collapsed with the Philistine rulers and everyone else still inside. Samson killed more Philistines when he died than he had killed during his entire life.
31His brothers and the rest of his family went to Gaza and took his body back home. They buried him in his father's tomb, which was located between Zorah and Eshtaol.
Samson was a leader of Israel for 20 years.
translation_text:
Samsɔn fātìi tí dàkā u-pɔŋŋu
1Dalbee, Samsɔn cūtì Gaasaa tiŋkin. U bàn̄ ki ká kinimpulaakpaai kiba ní ki kɔ́ ki-cee. 2Gaasaa yab nín nìn gbìl̄ yii Samsɔn bí bi-tiŋkinee, bi nìn cōom̀ ki māntì kitiŋ punyɔkɔpu ki cɔ́ŋkì-u kunyeeu gbanti kɔkɔ. Kunyeeu gbantee, baa nìn ŋá kìrikiri ní ki lī bi-neen yii: «Ti làá yàntī kutaa yaa fu wúntèe ní tí fu kpɔ̀-u.» 3Ama Samsɔn úǹ nìn pée dōoǹ ki bàn̄ kunyataasiiu ní. U nìn yíkì kunyataasiiu gbanti ní ki cūtìi cóotì kitiŋ punyɔkɔki punuubi nì idɔ in pu punuubi sàkantée liitil, ki dúkutì ki kpáaǹ idɔkpalikaa kɔkɔ ki dūu páaǹ u-gbigbipati pu ki cáa jɔ́ntiǹ dijool din bí Eebrɔn tiŋki nimbiinee yilpu.
Daliila nyáń Samsɔn boon ní bi ŋúń ki cúú-u
4Míǹ boonee, Samsɔn ká unimpu ubɔ ki néeń. U nìn kóòń Sooreeki tantakalin ní bi yíì-u yii Daliila. 5Fiiliistii yab bɔtiibi biŋmooyee nín béè mimmee ní ki cūtìi ká Daliila ki tùkū-u yii: «Ŋmàtiǹ Samsɔn kí béé an nín dī pu ní u baasii cáá mpɔŋkpaan ŋun u cáá nee, nì min ní ti máaǹ kí ŋá kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ-u kí ŋmā kí bóob́-u iŋmii ú taa ti ŋmā kí ŋá báà tibee. A yaa ŋúń ki ŋá mimmee, timbi ŋmootil báà ŋma làá tīī-si animbil kúti jitɔmbi kutuku ubɔ nì dilaataal dilaataal.» 6Niinee ní Daliila bí Samsɔn yii: «M gbàam̄-si, tùkù-mi an nín dī pu ní a cáá mpɔŋkpaan ŋun a cáá nee, kí tùkù-mi min unil máaǹ kí ŋá ní kí ŋmā kí bóob́-si iŋmii á taa ti ŋmā kí ŋá báà tibee.» 7Ní Samsɔn bí-u yii: «A yaa dū itaŋŋmii in dáá sɔ̀m̀ baa láá díntì-iee iluli ki dūu bóob́-mee, m-pɔŋŋu làá pèefì ní ḿ gítí kii unifantantee.» 8Ní Fiiliistii yab bɔtiibi biŋmooyee tīī Daliila itaŋŋmii in dáá sɔ̀m̀ baa láá díntì-iee, ní u cáa cūnnì ki bóob́ Samsɔn. 9Ŋyunti ŋun ní Fiiliistii yab kɔ́ ki nákáǹ nákáǹ Samsɔn diikunee, ní Daliila téeń yii: «Samsɔn, Fiiliistii yab dòoń kí cúú-seeee!» Ní Samsɔn dáaĺ ki tīfì itaŋŋmiiyee kii gulfa yaa pìl̄ ŋŋmi u nín tìfī puee. Ama binib kaa nìn béè laakin ní Samsɔn pɔŋkpaaŋŋu gbanti nìn nyánnée.
10Niinee ní Daliila bí Samsɔn yii: «Kpèè a ŋúb́-mi ki gbíilíǹ ki mɔ́ntí-mi inyimɔn. Kɔŋkɔnnee baasii tùkù-mi min ní unil máaǹ kí ŋá ní kí ŋmā kí bóob́-si iŋmiiyee.» 11Ní Samsɔn bí-u yii: «A yaa dū iŋmipɔmpɔɔn in baa láá dūu ŋá báà tiba nì tibee ki gúĺ-mi mpɔnee, m-pɔŋŋu làá pèefì ní ḿ gítí kii unifantantee.» 12Ní Daliila nyàab̄ iŋmipɔmpɔɔn ki gúĺ Samsɔn ní ki téeń yii: «Samsɔn, Fiiliistii yab dòoń kí cúú-seeee!» Nì mimmee Fiiliistii yab nìn pée náká náká Samsɔn diikun niin dee. Ama Samsɔn nìn dáaĺ ki tīfì iŋmipɔmpɔɔn in nìn bóob́ u-ŋaliiyee, a lì kii gulfatɔkaayee.
13Ní Daliila bí Samsɔn yii: «Kí yòon̄ kí dāá sāā nee, a pée ŋúb́-mi ki gbíilíǹ ní ki mɔ́ntí-mi inyimɔn. Pée tùkù-mi min ní unil máaǹ kí ŋá ní kí ŋmā kí bóob́-see!» Ní Samsɔn bí-u yii: «A yaa dū bi nín lùn̄ m-yikpiti tifɔkɔl miluli puee ki lùn̄ ki nákáǹ kun bi cáa lù satabee pu ní ki dū mpiin ki cúúyee, m-pɔŋŋu làá pèefì ní ḿ gítí kii unifantantee.» 14Ní Daliila ŋmáliŋkì ŋmáliŋkì Samsɔn ní u gèen̄. Samsɔn gèen̄ee ní Daliila cúú bi nín lùn̄ u-yikpiti tifɔkɔl miluli puee ki lùn̄ ki nákáǹ kun bi cáa lù satabee pu ní ki dū mpiin ki cúú. U dóòyee ní ki téeń yii: «Samsɔn, Fiiliistii yab dòoń kí cúú-seeee!» Ní Samsɔn fīntì ŋgeem pu ki cúú mpiin nì kun bi cáa lù satabee ki dáaĺ ki cóotì ki kpáaǹ gulfa un bi nìn dūu bóob́ u-yikpitee.
15Ní Daliila bí Samsɔn yii: «Mana ní a ŋūǹ kí lì yii a néeń-mi, ama ní a-naŋki kaa kā m-pu? Kpèè, mita kɔkɔ ní a ŋúb́-mi ki gbíilíǹ kaa tùkū-mi laakin ní a-pɔŋkpaaŋŋuee nyánnée.» 16Baabadalee Daliila nìn pée páb́ Samsɔn nì tibɔbaantiil gbanti dibalifil kaa gbèentí. Samsɔn nìn ŋmēē ki ŋmēē ki tin gīī, 17ní ki dāa lēē tin kā u-pɔbilinee ki tùkū Daliila yii: «Bɔlfi kaa láá gbēē m-yikpiti ki ká, kun puee doooo m-na poon ní bi dū-mi ki sú Unimbɔti. Bi yaa pée kōol̀ m-yikpitee, m-pɔŋŋu làá nyā m-ni ní m-wunti ń pèefì, ní ḿ gítí kii unifantantee.» 18Daliila nín ká yii kɔŋkɔnnee Samsɔn lafun lēē tin kā u-pɔbilinee ki tùkū-uee, ní u tú bí yíiń Fiiliistii yab bɔtiibee ki bí-bi yii: «Nín̄ dòoḿmaan, kun puee min bí nee u baasii lēē u-pɔbil poon bɔti ní ki tùkū-mi.» Niin ní Fiiliistii yab bɔtiibee yíkì ki nín jɔ́ḿ Daliila dumpu, ki ŋúb́ animbil ŋin bi nìn pōoǹ-uee. 19Daliila nìn dū Samsɔn ki páaǹ u-taaŋi pu ki ŋmáliŋkì ŋmáliŋkì-u ní Samsɔn gèen̄, ní u yíiń uninja ubɔ dɔ́miń ki cúú Samsɔn yikpiti tin bi lùn̄ tifɔkɔl miluli puee ki kōol̀. Niin ní Samsɔn wunti kíĺ ki bíi yɔ̀tī, ní u-pɔŋŋu nyáń u-ni kɔkɔ. 20Niinee ní Daliila téeń yii: «Samsɔn, Fiiliistii yab dòoń kí cúú-seeee!» Ní Samsɔn cúu fīntì ki dākafì u-neen yii: «Min bí nee m làá tí ŋmátí, kí ŋmā kí fōō m-ba kii m nín kpààa fòol̄ m-ba puee!» Waa nìn béè yii ti-Dindaan kaa nìn gíti bí u-cee. 21Fiiliistii yab nìn cúú-u ní ki sāā ki cɔ́tì u-nimbiliŋ liitil. Boonee ní bi cáá-u ki sīntì Gaasaa tiŋkin ki tin dū ikusaka in bi dū tasa kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́yee ki pɔ́b́ mili ki dūu gbìn̄-u. Bi nìn yāntì u bí kusarkadiin ki màntī kunaau taŋkpeeŋi ŋin nà ŋyimee. 22Ama Samsɔn yikpiti tin bi nìn cúu kōol̀ee nìn fātìi kíĺ ki bíi nyēē.
Samsɔn tɔ̀n̄ u-pɔntooŋyi ijoolkaa ní ki nín kpíì
23Dalbee, Fiiliistii yab bɔtiibee kpáfì ki ŋá saraakpaan ki tīī bi-waal Daagɔn. Bi nìn bí ki fàal̀ ki lì yii:
«Ti-waal dū ti-nannanliu Samsɔn
ki ŋá ti-ŋaan!»
24Fiiliistii yab nín wál̀ bi-waalee, bi bíi nyɔ́ŋkí-dì ki lì yii:
«Ti-waal dū ti-nannanliu Samsɔn
un nìn bí ki bíiĺ ti-tiŋki,
ki nìn pɔ̄fì ti-yab tikpilee
ki ŋá ti-ŋaan!»
25Ŋyunti ŋun ní an bíi nyàatī-bee, ní bi bí yii: «Ní yíiḿmaan Samsɔn ú dāan̄ kí láaǹ-taa!» Ní bi lēē binib ki tú bi cūtìi nyántìń Samsɔn kusarkadiin, ní u dɔ́miń ki láaǹ-bi. Bi láń láń ki dóòyee ní ki cáá-u ki sákaǹ kuwaadii jaantalkub bili kansikin. 26Niin ní Samsɔn bí unaacimpɔɔn un nìn ŋúb́ u-ŋal ki dàtī-uee yii: «Cúú m-ŋal kí dàkà-mi ḿ ŋmā kí gbēē jaantalkub bin ŋúb́ kudiiyee. M là kí nyīī bi-pu ní.»
27Bininjab nì binimpoobi nìn gbí kudii gbanti ní an kaa cáá bí lì. Fiiliistii yab bɔtiibi biŋmooyee nìn bí niin, ní samaa un Samsɔn nìn láaǹee nìn dáá bí kudii yilpu, ki nìn bàn̄ kii binib kutukub bita nyɔkɔm. 28Niinee Samsɔn mēē ti-Dindaan yii: «Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti, m mèé-si yii á pée téetí m-pu. M-baa Unimbɔti, fàtīí tīī-mi mpɔn, báà min bí nee baba, ḿ ŋmā kí téeǹ Fiiliistii yab bi nín sāā ki cɔ́tì m-nimbiliŋ liitil puee dibaba pu.» 29Samsɔn mēē míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki máań máań jaantalkub bili bin nìn cɔ́ kansikin ní ki ŋúb́ kudiiyee pɔŋŋuee. U nìn dū u-ŋaŋgiil ki nyīī jaantalkubee ubɔ ní ki dū u-ŋaŋgan ki nyīī un kíǹee. 30Samsɔn nyīī nyīī jaantalkub liitil mimmee ní ki téeń mpɔn yii: «Yàntī man nì Fiiliistii yab ń kpāfì kí kpú!» Niinee ní u gúkúǹ u-ba ki nyīī jaantalkubee nì u-pɔŋŋu kɔkɔ, ní kudiiyee lítì ki tābitì ki kūū Fiiliistii yab bɔtiibee nì samaa un nìn pée kpáfì ki bí niinee kɔkɔ. Binib bin ní Samsɔn nìn kūū u-kúm wiiŋŋu gbanti dalee nìn jítiǹ bin kɔkɔ u nìn kūū ŋyunti ŋun u nìn dáá bí dimaŋfalinee.
31Samsɔn nabiyaamu nì u-baa dicaŋkun yab kɔkɔ nìn sīntìń ki yōoǹ u-wunti ki cáa nín jɔ́ḿ bi-tiŋkin. Bi nìn síb́-u Sooreeya nì Eesitawool timmu kansikin, u-baa Manoowa kaakul poon. Samsɔn nìn kpōotì Isirayeel yab abin mmuŋku ní.

english_text:
Micah Makes Idols and Hires a Priest
1Micah belonged to the Ephraim tribe and lived in the hill country. 2One day he told his mother, “Do you remember those 1,100 pieces of silver that were stolen from you? I was there when you put a curse on whoever stole them. Well, I'm the one who did it.”
His mother answered, “I pray that the Lord will bless you, my son.”
3-4Micah returned the silver to his mother, and she said, “I give this silver to the Lord, so my son can use it to make an idol.” Turning to her son, she said, “Micah, now the silver belongs to you.”
But Micah handed it back to his mother. She took 200 pieces of the silver and gave them to a silver worker, who made them into an idol. They kept the idol in Micah's house. 5He had a shrine for worshiping God there at his home, and he had made some idols and a sacred priestly vest. Micah chose one of his own sons to be the priest for his shrine.
6 This was before kings ruled Israel, so all the Israelites did whatever they thought was right.
7-8One day a young Levite came to Micah's house in the hill country of Ephraim. He had been staying with one of the clans of Judah in Bethlehem, but he had left Bethlehem to find a new place to live where he could be a priest.
9“Where are you from?” Micah asked.
“I am a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah,” the man answered, “and I'm on my way to find a new place to live.”
10Micah said, “Why don't you stay here with me? You can be my priest and tell me what God wants me to do. Every year I'll give you ten pieces of silver and one complete set of clothes, and I'll provide all your food.”
The young man went for a walk, 11-12then he agreed to stay with Micah and be his priest. He lived in Micah's house, and Micah treated him like one of his own sons. 13Micah said, “I have a Levite as my own priest. Now I know that the Lord will be kind to me.”
translation_text:
Miika nì mpaan ŋun pu u jáaḿ Unimbɔtee bɔti
1Uninja ubɔ di nìn bí, ki nìn kóò Eefiraayiim jooŋŋi pu ní bi nìn yíì-u yii Miika. 2Dalbee ní u bí u-na yii: «Tikúti nimbiliŋ ŋin bi nìn yùn̄-si jitɔmbi kutuku ubɔ nì dilaataal, ní a sòon̄ ki tɔ́ udaan un yùn̄-see mbusu mama m-ba gbìl̄ee, an nimbiliŋ gbanti bí man cee. An sá man di nìn yōoǹ-ŋi!» Ní u-na bí-u yii: «Ti-Dindaan ń bìin̄ a-boon, m-jipɔɔn!» 3Miika nìn gíiǹ tikúti nimbiliŋ jitɔmbi kutuku nì dilaataalee ki tīī u-na, ní u-na bí-u yii: «Mama m-ba lēē kí dū animbil gbanti kí sú ti-Dindaan sii m-jipɔɔn pu. M làá dū-ŋi kí tīī bí mɔ́ɔ́ diwaal kí dùntī tikúti kí nyùntī-dì. Kɔŋkɔnnee m gíiǹ animbil gbanti ki tīī-si.» 4An pu ní Miika nín fātìi gíiǹ animbilee ki tīī u-nee, u-na nìn lēē ŋi-poon jitɔmbi kulaafaau ki dūu tīī ucaa u mɔ́ɔ́ diwaal ki dūntì tikúti ki nyūntì-dì ní bi cáa yóoǹ Miika dumpu.
5Too, Miika gbanti nìn cáá mpaan ŋun pu u jáaḿ inimbɔtee u-cindin. U nìn yāntì bi fātìi mɔ́ɔ́-u diwaal diba, ki kpítì-u awaa ŋin làá nīn cí u-cindee mun ní u dūu kútì, ní ki lēē u-jipɔɔn ubɔ ki kāaǹ ú nīn sá u-saraaŋaliu. 6Ŋyunti gbantee bibɔtiibi kaa nìn dá láá bí Isirayeel tiŋkin. Báà ŋma nìn ŋáań min u lèe ní.
7An yuntiŋuee, unaacimpɔɔn ubɔ nìn bí, ki nìn sá Leefii naakookun ní ki nìn kālìń Beetileem, Juuda tiŋkin kunicaŋu. 8Unaacimpɔɔnee nìn yíkì Beetileem, Juuda tiŋkinee, ní ki nìn bíi yìiǹ ki nyàab̀ laaba kí gíti kàl̄ kunicaŋu. U nìn bíi yìiǹ ki tin kɔ́ Eefiraayiim jooŋŋi timmunee, ní ki tin nyáń Miika dicaŋku pu. 9Ní Miika bālifì-u yii: «La ní a nyánní ní?» Ní u kíí Miika yii: «Man sá Leefii naakookun ní ki nyánní Beetileem, Juuda tiŋkin. M bíi yìiǹ ki nyàab̀ laaba kí kàl̄ kunicaŋu ní.» 10Niinee ní Miika bí-u yii: «Yaa sée gbíntí m-cee doo kí nīn sá m-baa nì m-saraaŋaliu. M làá nīn tìì-si animbil jitɔmbi saalaa dibindi poon, kí nīn tìì-si tiwampeeŋkaal nì tijikaal.» Leefii naakookun naacimpɔɔŋwuee nìn kíí ki gbíntì niin. 11U nìn kíí ki kāl̀ Miika dicaŋkun ní Miika dū-u ki ŋá kii úǹ u-ba jipɔɔn ubɔee. 12Miika nìn dū usaraaŋal tundi ki ŋúbiǹ Leefii naakookun naacimpɔɔŋwuee. U nìn kíǹ ki kóò Miika dumpu ní. 13Niinee ní Miika lī yii: «Min bí nee, m nín ká Leefii naakookun niliu ú nīn sá m-saraaŋaliu nee, m lafun béè yii ti-Dindaan làá dàkà-mi u-ŋanti dee!»

english_text:
1These things happened before kings ruled Israel.
The Tribe of Dan Takes Micah's Priest and Idols
About this time, the tribe of Dan was looking for a place to live. The other tribes had land, but the people of Dan did not really have any to call their own. 2The tribe chose five warriors to represent their clans and told them, “Go and find some land where we can live.”
The warriors left the area of Zorah and Eshtaol and went into the hill country of Ephraim. One night they stayed at Micah's house, 3because they heard the young Levite talking, and they knew from his accent that he was from the south. They asked him, “What are you doing here? Who brought you here?”
4The Levite replied, “Micah hired me as his priest.” Then he told them how well Micah had treated him.
5“Please talk to God for us,” the men said. “Ask God if we will be successful in what we are trying to do.”
6“Don't worry,” answered the priest. “The Lord is pleased with what you are doing.”
7The five men left and went to the town of Laish, whose people were from Sidon, but Sidon was too far away to protect them. Even though their town had no walls, the people thought they were safe from attack. So they had not asked anyone else for protection, which meant that the tribe of Dan could easily take over Laish.
8The five men went back to Zorah and Eshtaol, where their relatives asked, “Did you find any land?”
9-10“Let's go!” the five men said. “We saw some very good land with enough room for all of us, and it has everything we will ever need. What are you waiting for? Let's attack and take it. You'll find that the people think they're safe, but God is giving the land to us.”
11Six hundred men from the tribe of Dan strapped on their weapons and left Zorah and Eshtaol with their families. 12One night they camped near Kiriath-Jearim in the territory of Judah, and that's why the place just west of Kiriath-Jearim is still known as Dan's Camp. 13Then they went into the hill country of Ephraim.
When they came close to Micah's house, 14the five men who had been spies asked the other warriors, “Did you know that someone in this village has several idols and a sacred priestly vest? What do you think we should do about it?”
15-18The 600 warriors left the road and went to the house on Micah's property where the young Levite priest lived. They stood at the gate and greeted the priest. Meanwhile, the five men who had been there before went into Micah's house and took the sacred priestly vest and the idols.
“Hey!” the priest shouted. “What do you think you're doing?”
19“Quiet!” the men said. “Keep your mouth shut and listen. Why don't you come with us and be our priest, so you can tell us what God wants us to do? You could stay here and be a priest for one man's family, but wouldn't you rather be the priest for a clan or even a whole tribe of Israel?”
20The priest really liked that idea. So he took the vest and the idols and joined the others 21from the tribe of Dan. Then they turned and left, after putting their children, their cattle, and the rest of their other possessions in front.
22They had traveled for some time before Micah asked his neighbors to help him get his things back. He and his men caught up with the people of Dan 23and shouted for them to stop.
They turned to face him and asked, “What's wrong? Why did you bring all these men?”
24Micah answered, “You know what's wrong. You stole the gods I made, and you took my priest. I don't have anything left.”
25“We don't want to hear any more about it,” the people of Dan said. “And if you make us angry, you'll only get yourself and your family killed.” 26After saying this, they turned and left.
Micah realized there was no way he could win a fight with them, and so he went back home.
The Tribe of Dan Captures Laish
27-28The tribe of Dan took Micah's priest and the things Micah had made, and headed for Laish, which was located in a valley controlled by the town of Beth-Rehob. Laish was defenseless, because it had no walls and was too far from Sidon for the Sidonians to help defend it. The leaders of Laish had not even asked nearby towns to help them in case of an attack.
The warriors from Dan made a surprise attack on Laish, killing everyone and burning it down. Then they rebuilt the town and settled there themselves. 29But they named it Dan, after one of Israel's sons, who was the ancestor of their tribe.
30-31Even though the place of worship was in Shiloh, the people of Dan set up the idol Micah had made. They worshiped the idol, and the Levite was their priest. His name was Jonathan, and he was a descendant of Gershom the son of Moses. His descendants served as priests for the tribe of Dan, until the people of Israel were taken away as prisoners by their enemies.
translation_text:
Daani naakookun yab bíi nyàab̀ kitimpɔŋ kí kàl̄
1Ŋyunti gbantee bibɔtiibi kaa nìn dá láá bí Isirayeel tiŋkin. An yuntiŋuee Daani naakookun yab nìn bí ki nyàab̀ kitiŋ kin bi làá kàl̄ee dee, kun puee kí cáá sāā ŋyunti gbantee, baa nìn cáá ditinjandi Isirayeel naakɔti tin kíǹee kansikin. 2Daani naakookun yab nìn lēē bi-maaliŋu poon bibaatandambi biŋmoo ki tú, bí yīkì Sooreeya nì Eesitawool timmun kí yìiǹ kí cɔ̄ŋkì kí béé kitiŋ tiŋan. Binib biŋmoo gbanti nìn yìin̄ ki bàn̄ Eefiraayiim jooŋŋi timmunee, kunyeeu mɔ́ ní bi kɔ́ Miika dumpu. 3Bi nìn bí Miika dumpu niin ní ki gbìl̄ unaacimpɔɔn un sá Leefii naakookunee neen, ní ki béè dinicil din u sée. Bi nìn cūtì u-cee ki bālifì-u yii: «Ŋma di cáań-si doo nee ní? Ba tundi ní a bí doo ki tūǹ? Ba di ŋúb́-si ní a kā doo nee?» 4Ní u kíí-bi yii: «An sá Miika di fōō-mi ditundi. U yāntì m sá u-saraaŋaliu ní u pà-mi.» 5Ní bi fātìi bí-u yii: «Bàlifì Unimbɔti kí kpèè yii nsan ŋun ti bíi còom̄ nee làá nīn sá nsammɔntaaa, ŋuaa làá nīn sá.» 6Ní usaraaŋalee kíí-bi yii: «Ní taa pée fàŋkìmaan báà tiba! Ti-Dindaan làá céeǹ-ni nsan ŋun ni bíi còom̄ nee poon!»
7Ní binib biŋmooyee nìkī bi-saŋŋu, ki cōom̀ ki tin bàn̄ Layiisi tiŋkin. Bi bàn̄ kitiŋ gbantinee ní ki ká yii binib bin nìn kóò niinee nì ubɔ kaa nìn cáá tɔb kujaau. Bi kā nì ŋgbansɔŋfi nì dipɔɔsɔŋkil kii Siidɔn yab nín nìn bí puee. Ubɔ kaa nìn bí ki páb́-baaa, ditimbundi diba mun nib kaa nìn bí ki cáá mpɔn bi-pu. Layiisi yab nìn kóò ki dátiǹ Siidɔn yab, ní kaa nìn bí báà ubɔ taapu. 8Niinee ní binib biŋmooyee fātìi nín gítí bi-dumpu Sooreeya nì Eesitawool timmun, ní bi-nabiyaamu tin bālifì-bi yii: «Ni kánní yii ba?» 9Ní bi kíí bi-nabiyaamu yii: «Yīkìmaan tí cù kí táká Layiisi tiŋki yab! Timbi nín cūtèe, ti dáań ki ká yii kitiŋ gbanti ŋān̄ tikpilku. Ní taa nín̄ kāmaan ki jòon̄ iŋal, ní yīkì tí cùú já kí fōō kitiŋ gbanti! 10Ni yaa bàn̄ niinee, ni làá ká yii binib bin kóò kitiŋ gbantee kā nì ŋgbansɔŋfi ní kaa dàkafī yii tiba ŋūǹ kí ŋá-bi. Bi-tiŋkee wāā tiŋan ní tikɔkɔ nì tikɔkɔ bí ki-poon. Ti nyí yii Unimbɔti làá dū kitiŋ gbanti kí tīī-ni!»
11Niinee ní Daani naakookun yab binib alaataa aluu bóob́ dikɔ̀ndi ní ki yíkì Sooreeya nì Eesitawool timmun ki nín cá. 12Bi yíkì mimmee ní ki jɔ́m̀ ki cūtìi ŋātì dijanjanaapaal Kiiriyati-Yeeyariim tiŋki kin sá Juuda naakookun timmu kibee poon. An pu ní bi pú mpaan gbanti diyindi yii Maanee-Daani ki dāa sāā díǹ pu nee. Mpaan gbanti bí Kiiriyati-Yeeyariim tiŋkin, ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú. 13Bi yíkì niinee ní ki pūntì Eefiraayiim jooŋŋi, ki cōom̀ ki bàn̄ Miika dumpu. 14Niinee ní binib biŋmoo bin bi nìn lēē bi yìin̄ ki cɔ́ŋkì ki béè Layiisi tiŋkee fōō dinyɔɔbundi ki bí yii: «Ni nyí yii diwaal diba, nì kudicaŋu waaŋi, nì diwaal din bi mɔ́ɔ́ ki dūntì tikúti ki nyūntèe bí adican nee kubɔ poonaaa? Too, kɔŋkɔnnee ní dàkafìmaan kí kpèè ni nín làá ŋá puee!» 15Binib biŋmooyee lī mimmee ní ki dūu túĺ Miika cindi, laakin ní unaacimpɔɔn un sá Leefii naakookunee nìn kóòyee, ki bàn̄ ki kɔ́ ní ki jáam̀-u ki bālifì u-gbampɔŋŋu pu. 16Ŋyunti ŋun binib biŋmooyee nìn bí dicindinee, Daani naakookun yab binib alaataa aluu bin kíǹee bíǹ nìn gbíntì ki yú kipunyɔkɔpu ki ŋúb́ bi-janjawanti. 17Ní binib biŋmooyee nín jɔ́ḿ yilpu cindin ki cūtìi kɔ́ kudiin ki yōoǹní diwaalee, nì kudicaŋu waaŋi, nì diwaal din bi dūntì tikúti ki nyūntèe. Ŋyunti gbantee usaraaŋal nìn bí kipunyɔkɔpu, u nì Daani naakookun yab binib alaataa aluu bin kíǹee, bíǹ yú ki ŋúb́ bi-janjawanti. 18Bin nìn kɔ́ kudiinee nín nìn yōoǹní diwaalee, nì kudicaŋu waaŋi, nì diwaal din bi dūntì tikúti ki nyūntèe ki nyántìńee, ní usaraaŋalee bālifì-bi yii: «Ba ní ni ŋáańee?» 19Ní bi kíí-u yii: «Ŋmīĺ niin! Taa ti pée wàan̄ a-nyɔkɔ kí lì báà tiba! Dāan̄ kí nóó-ti kí nīn sá usaraaŋal ki tīī-ti. Dàkafì kí kpèè yii á nīn sá usaraaŋal ki tīī unibaanti dicaŋku nì á nīn sá usaraaŋal ki tīī Isirayeel naakooku kumɔŋu kɔkɔee, la di ŋān̄?» 20Tibɔti gbanti nìn mɔ́ɔkiǹ usaraaŋalee tikpil, di sá ní u nìn fōō diwaalee, nì kudicaŋu waaŋi, nì diwaal din bi dūntì tikúti ki nyūntèe ki nóó-bi bi nín cá.
21Míǹ ní Daani naakookun yab nìn nìkī bi-saŋŋu, ki nìn dū mbiyaamu nì tiwaŋkuti nì awaŋgul ki līntì bi-nyɔkɔpu. 22Daani naakookun yab nìn cōom̀ ki kɔ́ ndan kaa ti pìlīǹ Miika dumpu ní Miika nì u-kɔŋkɔnnaatɔb kóoǹ ki kpáfì ki bóob́ butɔbu ní ki yíkìi kùl̄ ki páaǹ bi-boon. 23Daani naakookun yab nín gbìl̄ Miika nì u-kɔŋkɔnnaatɔb pánní bi-boon ki tátí ki yíì-bee ní bi fātì ki bālifì Miika yii: «Ba cáá-si ní? Ba yì-tì ní a kóoǹní dinikitil nee ki páaǹní a-boon mimmee?» 24Ní Miika kíí-bi yii: «Ni yōoǹ awaa ŋin m yāntì bi mɔ́ɔ́-mee, ki yōoǹ ki kpáaǹ m-saraaŋaliu, báà tiba nì tiba kaa ti kíǹ-mi ní ni gíti bàlifī-mi yii ba di cáá-maaa?» 25Ní Daani naakookun yab fātìi kpātì u-pu ki bí-u yii: «A yaa pée nyí nnyiimee, á ŋmīĺ a-nyɔkɔ laakin a yú nee, kí taa ti sòoǹ kí páb́ timbi! Yaa sá fám, a làá yàntī ti-kansikin biba ń dū bi-ŋuul kí nyìntī a-pu, kí kpɔ̀ kí céetí sii nì a-dicaŋku yab kɔkɔ.» 26Daani naakookun yab kpātì Miika pu mimmee ní ki nìkī bi-saŋŋu. Miika nín ká yii bi cáá mpɔn ki jítiǹ-uee, ní u fātìi nín kùǹ u-dumpu.
Daani naakookun yab kāl̀ Layiisi tiŋkin
27Daani naakookun yab nìn yōoǹ tiwan tin Miika nìn yāntì bi mɔ́ɔ́-uee. Bi nìn kpáaǹ usaraaŋal un u nìn fōō ditundee ki cáa búntì. Bi nìn cūtìi táká Laayiisi tiŋki kin nib kā nì ŋgbansɔŋfi kaa nìn fàŋkí yii tiba bí ki làá ŋá-bee. Bi nìn pɔ̄fì-bi ki sēē bi-tiŋki ŋŋmi kì wùn̄ kɔkɔ. 28Layiisi tiŋki nìn bí Beeti-Reewɔɔfi tantakalin ní, ki nìn dátiǹ Siidɔn tiŋki ní kaa nìn bí kitiŋ báà kiba taapu. An puee báà unil kaa nìn dɔ́miń ki fīī-kì. Daani naakookun yab nìn fātìi máń kitiŋ gbanti ki kāl̀ niin. 29Bi nìn kpántì kitiŋee diyindi, ki nìn kíǹ ki yíì-kì yii Daani, kii bi nín nìn yíì bi-naanja, Jaakɔb jipɔɔn puee. Njaminee, ki-yindi di nìn dáá láá sá Layiisi. 30Daani naakookun yab nìn dū Miika waalee ki yóoǹ bi-tiŋki gbantin. Geersɔm jipɔɔn Joonatan, Mooyiisi naantiiu di nìn sá Daani naakookun yab saraaŋaliu. Joonatan boonee, u-naantiibi di nìn tɔ́kɔǹ ki nìn sá Daani naakookun yab saraaŋaliibi míǹ ki tin cáa sāā ŋyunti ŋun ní bi dāa cúú Isirayeel yab ki cūnnì kuyuŋuee. 31Bi nìn dū Miika waal din u nìn yāntì bi mɔ́ɔ́-uee ki síiǹ bi-ba bi-tiŋkin. Di nìn gbíntìi niin ní ŋyunti ŋun kɔkɔ Unimbɔti diiku nìn dáá bí Siiloo tiŋkinee.

english_text:
A Woman Is Murdered
1Before kings ruled Israel, a Levite was living deep in the hill country of the Ephraim tribe. He married a woman from Bethlehem in Judah, 2but she was unfaithful and went back to live with her family in Bethlehem.
Four months later 3her husband decided to try and talk her into coming back. So he went to Bethlehem, taking along a servant and two donkeys. He talked with his wife, and she invited him into her family's home. Her father was glad to see him 4and did not want him to leave. So the man stayed three days, eating and drinking with his father-in-law.
5When everyone got up on the fourth day, the Levite started getting ready to go home. But his father-in-law said, “Don't leave until you have a bite to eat. You'll need strength for your journey.”
6The two men sat down together and ate a big meal. “Come on,” the man's father-in-law said. “Stay tonight and have a good time.”
7The Levite tried to leave, but his father-in-law insisted, and he spent one more night there. 8The fifth day, the man got up early to leave, but his wife's father said, “You need to keep up your strength! Why don't you leave right after lunch?” So the two of them started eating.
9Finally, the Levite got up from the meal, so he and his wife and servant could leave. “Look,” his father-in-law said, “it's already late afternoon, and if you leave now, you won't get very far before dark. Stay with us one more night and enjoy yourself. Then you can get up early tomorrow morning and start home.”
10But the Levite decided not to spend the night there again. He had the saddles put on his two donkeys, then he and his wife and servant traveled as far as Jebus, which is now called Jerusalem. 11It was beginning to get dark, and the man's servant said, “Let's stop and spend the night in this town where the Jebusites live.”
12“No,” the Levite answered. “They aren't Israelites, and I refuse to spend the night there. We'll stop for the night at Gibeah, 13or maybe we can even reach Ramah before dark.”
14They walked on and reached Gibeah in the territory of Benjamin just after sunset. 15They left the road and went into Gibeah. But the Levite couldn't find a house where anyone would let them spend the night, and they sat down in the open area just inside the town gates.
16Soon an old man came in through the gates on his way home from working in the fields. Most of the people who lived in Gibeah belonged to the tribe of Benjamin, but this man was originally from the hill country of Ephraim. 17He noticed that the Levite was just in town to spend the night. “Where are you going?” the old man asked. “Where did you come from?”
18“We've come from Bethlehem in Judah,” the Levite answered. “We went there on a visit. Now we're going to the place where the Lord is worshiped, and later we will return to our home in the hill country of Ephraim. But no one here will let us spend the night in their home. 19We brought food for our donkeys and bread and wine for ourselves, so we don't need anything except a place to sleep.”
20The old man said, “You are welcome to spend the night in my home and to be my guest, but don't stay out here!”
21The old man brought them into his house and fed their donkeys. Then he and his guests washed their feet and began eating and drinking. 22 They were having a good time, when some worthless men of that town surrounded the house and started banging on the door and shouting, “A man came to your house tonight. Send him out, so we can have sex with him!”
23The old man went outside and said, “My friends, please don't commit such a horrible crime against a man who is a guest in my house. 24Let me send out my daughter instead. She's a virgin. And I'll even send out the man's wife. You can rape them or do whatever else you want, but please don't do such a horrible thing to this man.”
25The men refused to listen, so the Levite grabbed his wife and shoved her outside. The men raped her and abused her all night long. Finally, they let her go just before sunrise, 26and it was almost daybreak when she went back to the house where her husband was staying. She collapsed at the door and lay there until sunrise.
27About that time, her husband woke up and got ready to leave. He opened the door and went outside, where he found his wife lying at the door with her hands on the doorstep. 28“Get up!” he said. “It's time to leave.”
But his wife didn't move.
He lifted her body onto his donkey and left. 29 When he got home, he took a butcher knife and cut her body into twelve pieces. Then he told some messengers, “Take one piece to each tribe of Israel 30and ask everyone if anything like this has ever happened since Israel left Egypt. Tell them to think about it, talk it over, and tell us what should be done.”
Everyone who saw a piece of the body said, “This is horrible! Nothing like this has ever happened since the day Israel left Egypt.”
translation_text:
Beenjameen naakookun yab ŋá digaŋgam Giibeeya
1Ŋyunti gbantee bibɔtiibi kaa nìn dá láá bí Isirayeel tiŋkin. Leefii naakookun niliu ubɔ nìn kóòń Eefiraayiim jooŋŋi timmu mun bínní poon poon púee kiban. U nìn cáá ubɔnti ubɔ sá Beetileem, Juuda tiŋkin. 2U-bɔɔn gbanti nìn nyáń u-boon ní ki nìn yíkì-u ki nín kùǹ u-baa dumpu Beetileem, Juuda tiŋkin. U nìn kāl̀ niin ki bàn̄ kii iŋmal inaa nyɔkɔm. 3U-cal nìn jìn̄ u-boon ki cūtì kí sɔ̀ŋkì u-pɔbil kí fàtīí gíiǹní-u u-cee. U nìn kpáaǹ u-tɔntɔnliu nì mmamu muli. U-bɔɔnee nìn cáá-u ki kɔ́ǹ u-baa dumpu. U-baa nín nìn ká u-cooyee, an nìn mɔ́ɔkiǹ-u tikpil ní u fōō-u nì dipɔɔpindi. 4U nìn cúú u-coo ki kāaǹ u-dumpu iwiin ita kɔkɔ. Iwiin ita gbantee, u nì u-tɔntɔnliu nìn jīǹ, ki nyù ní ki dɔ̀ niin. 5Ŋwinnanaati dal bi fīntì kutaafaau pɔ̀lpɔlee, uleefiijee bíi bɔ́ntí bí yīkèe, ní unimpu baa bí-u yii: «Kāl̀ kí jī tijin kí tíkiń a-fam kí wàatī ní nín búntáa!» 6Ní u kíí ki kāl̀ ní bi-liitil jíń ki nyùn̄. Ní unimpu baa bí-u yii: «Gbíntí kí dòon̄ doo kunyeeu nee kí gíti ŋùŋfì fiiiyaa!» 7Uleefiijee nín bàà nìn yíkì kí nīn cée, ní u-coo kā u-pu yii ú gbíntí kí dòon̄, ní u dāa kíí ki lafun gbíntì niin ki dōoǹ kunyeeu gbanti. 8Ŋwiŋŋmooŋmooti dal, u tí yíkì malaa ki bɔ́ntì kí bàà nín̄ cée, ní unimpu baa tí bí-u yii: «M gbāam̀-si, kàl̄ kí jī tijin, kí cīití ŋwìiń yaa sɔ̄ŋkèe á nīn cá!» Ní bi-liitil tí kāl̀ ki jíń tijin. 9Uninjee nì u-bɔɔn nì u-tɔntɔnliu tí bɔ́ntì kí yīkèe, ní u-coo tí bí-u yii: «Kpèè ŋwìiń jéetì ní nee, kunyeeu bíi móotí! An puee ní pūtìi gbíntí kí dòon̄ á gíti ŋùŋfì fiii. Fool kutaafaauee, ní fu yīkì malaa kí nīn kùǹ a-dumpu.»
10Ama uninjee nìn yíì kpataaa, kaa ti kíí kí dòon̄ niin kunyeeu gbanti. U nìn yíkì ki cōom̀ ki tin bàn̄ Jeebusi tiŋki kin bi gíti yíì yii Jeerusaleem tiŋkee. U nìn kpáaǹ u-mammu liitil mun u nìn túǹ awaŋgulee nì u-bɔɔn. 11Ŋyunti ŋun bi bàn̄ Jeebusi tiŋki caŋinee, ŋwìiń ŋman nìn pée jéetì ki dóò, ní utɔntɔnlee bí u-kpiliu yii: «Ukpil, yàntī tí pàatī kí kɔ́ Jeebusi yab tiŋki nee poon kí dòon̄ kunyeeu nee!» 12Ní u-kpiliu kíí-u yii: «Taa làá yūĺ binicambi tiŋki kin poon Isirayeel niliu báà ubɔ kaa bí nee. Ti làá nìkī kí bà Giibeeya tiŋkin ní.» 13U nìn kútì ki lī yii: «Tí pɔ́ɔm̀maan kí nìkī kí bà Giibeeya tiŋkin àá Raama tiŋkin. Ti tin ŋūǹ kí dòon̄ ntimu gbanti liitil kiban.» 14Bi nìn lafun nìkī ki tin bàn̄ Giibeeya, Beenjameen tiŋkinee ŋwìiń nìn bíi jēetí. 15Bi nìn pāatì Giibeeya tiŋkin niin kí dòon̄ kunyeeu gbanti. Bi nìn kɔ́ kitiŋin ní ki cūtìi kāl̀ kitiŋ punyɔkɔpu, ama báà unil kaa nìn fōō-bi bí kɔ́ kí dòon̄ u-dumpu.
16Bi dāa kpēēyee ujaŋkpil ubɔ di nyánní kusaau ki kùnnée.
