28David heard how Joab had killed Abner, and he said, “I swear to the Lord that I am completely innocent of Abner's death! 29Joab and his family are the guilty ones. I pray that Joab's family will always be sick with sores and other skin diseases. May they all be cowards, and may they die in war or starve to death.”
30Joab and his brother Abishai killed Abner because he had killed their brother Asahel in the battle at Gibeon.
31David told Joab and everyone with him, “Show your sorrow by tearing your clothes and wearing sackcloth! Walk in front of Abner's body and cry!”
David walked behind the stretcher on which Abner's body was being carried. 32Abner was buried in Hebron, while David and everyone else stood at the tomb and cried loudly. 33Then the king sang a funeral song about Abner:
Abner, why should you
have died like an outlaw?
34No one tied your hands
or chained your feet,
yet you died as a victim
of murderers.
Everyone started crying again. 35Then they brought some food to David and told him he would feel better if he had something to eat. It was still daytime, and David said, “I swear to God that I won't take a bite of bread or anything else until sunset!”
36Everyone noticed what David did, and they liked it, just as they always liked what he did. 37Now the people of Judah and Israel were certain that David had nothing to do with killing Abner.
38David said to his officials, “Don't you realize that today one of Israel's great leaders has died? 39I am the chosen king, but Joab and Abishai have more power than I do. So God will have to pay them back for the evil thing they did.”
translation_text:
1Saayuul yab nì Daafiidi yab jaaku nìn yúntì tikpil. Daafiidi nìn mɔ̀tīi kāntí mpɔn ki cá, ama ní Saayuul yab bíǹ mɔ̀tīi pèefī ki cá.
Daafiidi jipɔmbi bin u màl̄ Eebrɔn tiŋkinee
(Kpèè 1 Kroo 3.1-4)
2Daafiidi nín màl̄ mbininjabiyaamu mun Eebrɔn tiŋkinee sɔ̀. U-jipɔŋkpiliu di sá Aminɔn, ní bi yíì u-na yii Ayiinoowaam, u sá Jisirayeel tiŋkin. 3U-jipɔnliliitiu di sá Kiileeyab, ní bi yíì u-na yii Abiigayiil, Naabaal un sá Kaarmeel tiŋkin ki kpíìyee nimpuu. U-jipɔntataatiu di sá Abisaloom, ní bi yíì u-na yii Maaka, Geesuur bɔtiu Talimayi bisal. 4U-jipɔɔn unanaati di sá Adooniyawuu, ní bi yíì u-na yii Agiiti, ní u-jipɔɔn uŋmooŋmooti sá Seefatiya, ní bi yíì u-na yii Abitaal. 5U-jipɔɔn ululuuti di sá Yitireeyam, ní bi yíì u-na yii Eegila, Daafiidi nimpuu ubɔ mun. Daafiidi jipɔmbi bin u nìn màl̄ Eebrɔn tiŋkinee dee.
Kujaau kɔ́ Abineer nì Isi-Booseeti kansikin
6Ŋyunti ŋun Saayuul yab nì Daafiidi yab nìn bí ki jáàyee, Abineer úǹ nìn mɔ̀tīi kāntí mpɔn Saayuul yab kansikin. 7Saayuul nìn cáá ubɔnti ubɔ bi yíì-u yii Riispa ní ki yíì u-baa yii Aaya. Ní Isi-Booseeti bí Abineer yii: «Ba pu ní a dōoǹ nì m-baa bɔɔn ní?» 8An bɔtee nìn yāntì Abineer fōō diŋuul ŋkpitim pu, ní ki bí Isi-Booseeti yii: «M sá kibɔkɔ ki pá Juuda yab boonaaa? Doooo nee, maa pée nyáń a-baa cindin yab nì u-nabiyaamu nì u-bɔɔbi boon. M mɔ̀n̄ a-pu á taa kɔ́ Daafiidi ŋaan, ní díǹ nee, a bí ki wòoǹ-mi unimpu nee puɔɔ! 9Unimbɔti ń dáaĺ m-tafal ŋkpitim pu, m yaa kaa ŋá min ti-Dindaan pōoǹ yii u làá ŋá kí tīī Daafiidee! 10Di sá yii ti-Dindaan pūtì yii u làá fōō Saayuul dicaŋkun yab ŋaan dibeel. U làá wàan̄ Daafiidi beel Isirayeel nì Juuda timmu pu, kí yòon̄ Daani ŋgan pú kí cáá sāā Beerseeba ŋgiil pú.» 11Isi-Booseeti kaa nìn ŋúń ki gātì Abineer báà dinyɔɔbundi, kun puee u nìn fàŋkí-u.
Abineer gítì Daafiidi jandi pú
12Ní Abineer tú binib Daafiidi cee bí tùkù-u yii: «Ŋma di yì kitiŋ nee ní? Ŋá mpèé nì man, ní ḿ tūtuǹ-si á kóoǹ Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ kí páań a-boon.» 13Ní Daafiidi kíí-u yii: «M làá ŋá mpèé nì si, ama kí wàatī á dāan̄ kí ká-mee, á péé péé kí dū m-nimpuu Miikaal, Saayuul bisal kí tīiń-mi.» Niinee a ŋūǹ kí dāan̄ kí ká-mi. 14Ní Daafiidi tú binib Saayuul jipɔɔn Isi-Booseeti cee bí tùkù-u yii: «Dū m-nimpuu Miikaal kí tīiń-mi, di sá yii m dū Fiiliistii yab kuncooti dilaataal ní ki pàn̄ u-pu kucootiiu.» 15Niinee Isi-Booseeti fōoń-u u-cal uliliiti, Layiisi jipɔɔn Paltiyeel cee. 16Ní u-cal céeǹ-u ki pá u-boon ki sūǹ ki tin bàn̄ Bawuriim. Niinee Abineer bí-u yii ú nīn gítí u-dumpu ní u nín gítí.
17Abineer kíĺ ki bíi sòoǹ nì Isirayeel tindaŋkpilib yii: «An yúntì ni nín bíi nyàab̀ yii Daafiidi ń nīn sá ni-bɔtiuee. 18Toooo, ŋyunti bāań ní ŋá tiba. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan sòon̄ Daafiidi pu yii: <M-tɔntɔnliu Daafiidi pu ní m làá dī kí fīī Isirayeel m-nibul kí nyāntí Fiiliistii yab nì bi-nannanliibi bin kɔ kíǹee ŋaan.>»
19Abineer nìn sòon̄ nì Beenjameen naakookun yab mun. Boonee ní u nín cá Eebrɔn ki tùkū Daafiidi u nì Isirayeel yab nì Beenjameen naakookun yab kɔkɔ nín sòon̄ ki gbìlīǹ tɔb ki yóoǹ miŋyee. 20Bininjab mmuŋku di nìn céeǹ Abineer ní bi dūu bàn̄ Daafiidi cee Eebrɔn tiŋkin. Daafiidi nìn ŋá tican ki fōō-bi. 21Ní Abineer bí-u yii: «M làá cùú kóoǹ Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ kí páań sii ti-baa ubɔti boon. Bi làá ŋá mpèé nì si, ní á jī dibeel an kɔkɔ pu kii a nín là puee.» U sòon̄ míǹ ki dóòyee ní Daafiidi pú-u nsan ú nīn kùǹ, ní u nín kùǹ nì ŋgbansɔŋfi.
Joowaab kūū Abineer
22Míǹ boonee Joowaab nì Daafiidi janjaliibi dūu bāań. Bi nìn cūtì kujaau ki jáń ki fōoń tigaajawan tikpil. Ŋyunti gbantee, Abineer kaa nìn gíti bí Daafiidi cee Eebrɔn, di sá yii Daafiidi nìn yāntì u fātìi nín kùǹ nì ŋgbansɔŋfi. 23Joowaab nì u-janjaliibi kɔkɔ nín nyánní kujaau ki bāańee, ní bi tùkū-u yii: «Neer jipɔɔn Abineer dɔ́miń ki ká ubɔti ní u yāntì u nín kùǹ nì ŋgbansɔŋfi.» 24Ní Joowaab nín cá ubɔti cee ki bí-u yii: «Ba pu ní a ŋá mimmee? Abineer dɔ́miń a-cee ní a yāntì u fātìi nín kùǹ nì ŋgbansɔŋfaaa? 25Kéè sii a-ba nyí Neer jipɔɔn Abineer gbantaa! U dɔ́miń ki kíil̀-si, kí béé a-filiŋfeetii kɔkɔ ní.»
26Joowaab nyáń ubɔti ceeyee ní ki tú binib bí jà Abineer boon. Bi nìn jìn̄ ki cúú-u Siira nyimbɔbil caŋin ní ki fātìi gíiǹní-u Daafiidi kaa nyí. 27Abineer fātìi gítìń Eebrɔn tiŋkinee, ní Joowaab cáá-u ki kākatì ŋkpaanceeti kitiŋ punyɔkɔ poon pú kii u là kí lɔ̄kɔfì-u tibee. Niin ní u sāā u-pool kitàataajiki ki kūū-u ki tɔ̀n̄ u-nabiki Asayeel kúm pɔntooŋyi.
28Boonee Daafiidi nín dāa gbìl̄ tin jítèe ní u fáá mbiil yii: «Ti-Dindaan nyí yii man nì m-beel kaa kútì Neer jipɔɔn Abineer kúm bɔti poon. 29Abineer kúm kpuulool ń lítí Joowaab nì u-dicaŋku yil pu. U-dicaŋku poonee, bin wunti làá nīn yàkà, àá bin dinyaŋgbandi làá cúúyee, àá bin làá nīn sá bideembi ki ŋúb́ ŋkpandɔ ki nyìitēe, àá bin bi làá dū kitàataajiki kí kpɔ̀ee, àá bin ŋkùm làá cúúyee ń taa lóó.» 30Joowaab nì u-nabiki Abisayi nìn sāā ki kūū Abineer, kun puee u nìn kūū bi-nabiki Asayeel kujaaun Gabawɔn tiŋkin.
31Daafiidi nìn tùkū Joowaab nì bijanjaliibi bin kɔkɔ bí u-ceeyee yii: «Cátímaan tiwan tin ni pēēyee, kí dū kutukub kí gbìn̄ kí dàkà yii ni bí kunimbaaun kí sɔ̄ Abineer kpool.» Ubɔti Daafiidi nìn còom̄ ki pá utaŋkpiil boon ní. 32Eebrɔn ní bi síb́ Abineer. Ubɔti nìn súń ki yíkintì Abineer kaakul pu, ní samaa kɔkɔ bíi sūǹ. 33Ní ubɔti gāā Abineer kúm pu ŋkpiisilan nee yii:
Abineer, ba pu ní a kpíì
kii ugbaan nín kúù puee?
34Baa nìn bóob́ a-ŋalii,
kaa bá a-taaŋi abaa.
Ama ní bi kūū-si
kii unil un kɔ́ binikpɔliibi ŋaanee.
Ní samaa kɔkɔ mɔ̄tìi bíi sūǹ u-pu. 35Ŋyunti ŋun ní ŋwìiń dáá bée ní samaa dɔ́miń ki páb́ Daafiidi yii ú jī tijin fiii. Ní Daafiidi pūtì ki lī yii: «Ŋwìiń yaa kaa jéetì ní m yaa ŋmɔ́ kpɔnɔ àá m jíń tibee, Unimbɔti ń dáaĺ m-tafal ŋkpitim pu.»
36Samaa kɔkɔ nìn dáań ki ká míǹ ní an nìn ŋān̄ bi-cee. Tin kɔkɔ ubɔti nìn ŋáańee nìn ŋān̄ samaa cee ní. 37Juuda nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nìn béè yaadal wiiŋŋu yii ubɔti kaa nìn nyí Neer jipɔɔn Abineer kúm poon tiba. 38Ní Daafiidi gíti bí u-naacimbi yii: «Naa nyí yii dibɔtibil, unikpaan di kpíì díǹ wiiŋŋu Isirayeel tiŋkinaaa? 39Nì min kamaa bi sītì m-yil pu ŋkpam m kpántì ubɔtee, maa ŋūǹ kí dàkà mpɔn kii binib bin na bi yíì yii Seeruya nee nín ŋá puee. Ti-Dindaan ń téeǹ utɔŋfiti u-toom paati nín sá puee.»

english_text:
Ishbosheth Is Killed
1Ishbosheth felt like giving up after he heard that Abner had died in Hebron. Everyone in Israel was terrified.
2Ishbosheth had put the two brothers Baanah and Rechab in charge of the soldiers who raided enemy villages. Rimmon was their father, and they were from the town of Beeroth, which belonged to the tribe of Benjamin. 3The people who used to live in Beeroth had run away to Gittaim, and they still live there.
4 Saul's son Jonathan had a son named Mephibosheth, who had not been able to walk since he was five years old. It happened when someone from Jezreel told his nurse that Saul and Jonathan had died. She hurried off with the boy in her arms, but he fell and injured his legs.
5One day about noon, Rechab and Baanah went to Ishbosheth's house. It was a hot day, and he was resting 6-7in his bedroom. The two brothers went into the house, pretending to get some flour. But once they were inside, they stabbed Ishbosheth in the stomach and killed him. Then they cut off his head and took it with them.
Rechab and Baanah walked through the Jordan River valley all night long. 8Finally they turned west and went to Hebron. They went in to see David and told him, “Your Majesty, here is the head of Ishbosheth, the son of your enemy Saul who tried to kill you! The Lord has let you get even with Saul and his family.”
9David answered:
I swear that only the Lord rescues me when I'm in trouble! 10 When a man came to Ziklag and told me that Saul was dead, he thought he deserved a reward for bringing good news. But I grabbed him and killed him.
11You evil men have done something much worse than he did. You've killed an innocent man in his own house and on his own bed. I'll make you pay for that. I'll wipe you from the face of the earth!
12Then David said to his troops, “Kill these two brothers! Cut off their hands and feet and hang their bodies by the pool in Hebron. But bury Ishbosheth's head in Abner's tomb near Hebron.” And they did.
translation_text:
Isi-Booseeti kúm
1Saayuul jipɔɔn Isi-Booseeti nín gbìl̄ yii Abineer kpíì Eebrɔn tiŋkinee, ní u-pɔbil bíil̀ ní tifaandi kɔ́ Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ.
2Saayuul jipɔɔn Isi-Booseeti nìn cáá bijanjakpilib bili bi kpòotī ajanjakiti. Bi nìn yíì ubɔ yii Baana ní ki yíì un kíǹee yii Reekaab. Bi nìn sá Beerooti tiŋkin, ní bi nìn yíì bi-baa yii Riimɔn, u sá Beenjameen naakookun. - Beerooti nìn sá Beenjameen naakookun yab timmu kiba ní. 3Beerooti yab nìn sáǹ ki cūtìi kɔ́ Giitayiim tiŋkin, ní ki gbíntì niin ki kāl̀ ki dāa sāā díǹ. 4Di sá Saayuul jipɔɔn Joonatan nìn cáá jipɔɔn ubɔ u-taaŋi wɔ̀b̄. U nìn cáá abin aŋmoo ŋyunti ŋun binib nìn nyánní Jisirayeel tiŋkin ki dɔ́miń ki lī yii Saayuul nì Joonatan kpíìyee. Un nìn lòó-uee nìn kpáaǹ-u kí sāǹ. U nín bíi nyàab̀ malaa puee ní kibiki nyáń ki lítì ní ki kpántì udeen. Bi nìn yíì-u yii Meefiibooseeti ní.
5Riimɔn un sá Beerooti tiŋkinee jipɔmbi Reekaab nì Baana nìn nín cá Isi-booseeti dumpu kuwiŋkuluu. Úǹ nìn dɔ̄ u-diikun ki ŋùŋfī. 6Bi nìn tú bilee ki kpáaǹ ki kɔ́ u-diiku poon ní ki sāā u-pool ki kūū-u. Bi ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki nyáń ki kátì. 7Bi nìn kɔ́ u-dumpu ŋyunti ŋun ní úǹ nìn dɔ̄ u-dooŋu pu u-didooŋkaakun ki gèeǹee. Bi nìn kūū-u ki lēē u-yil ki dūu dī Jɔɔdan tantakal saŋŋu ki cōom̀ kunyamɔŋu. 8Bi yōoǹ Isi-Booseeti yil ki cáa tīī Daafiidi Eebrɔn tiŋkin ní ki bí-u yii: «Kpèè, Saayuul un nìn sá a-nannanliu ki nìn nyàab̀ kí kpɔ̀-see jipɔɔn Isi-Booseeti yil sɔ̀. Ti-Dindaan kūū Saayuul nì u-maaliŋun yab ki tɔ̀n̄ a-pɔntooŋyi díǹ.» 9Ní Daafiidi kíí Riimɔn un sá Beerooti tiŋkinee jipɔmbi Rakaab nì u-nabiki Baana yii: «Ti-Dindaan un nyántì-mi animbinaaman kɔkɔ poonee bí dimaŋfalin! 10Unil un nìn dɔ́miń ki tùkū-mi yii Saayuul kpíìyee nìn dākafì yii u nìn cáań-mi dinyɔɔbummɔɔndi ní. Ama m nìn yāntì bi cúú-u ki kūū-u Siikilaagi tiŋkin ki pàn̄ u-nyɔɔbummɔɔndi paati. 11Kin ataa aŋa pu ní maa làá pà binikpitib bin sāā ki kūū maanyiiba un dɔ̄ u-dooŋu pu u-diikunee. M làá dáaĺ ni-tafal nnikpaakoon gbanti pu ní kí kúntí-ni kitiŋ pu.»
12Niinee ní Daafiidi pú u-naacimpɔmbi kinyɔkɔ yii bí kpɔ̀-bi. Bi nìn kūū-bi ní boonee ki gūutì bi-ŋalii nì bi-taaŋi ki dūu lúntì Eebrɔn nyimbɔbil caŋin. Bi nìn yōoǹ Isi-Booseeti yil ki cáa síb́ Abineer kaakulin, Eebrɔn tiŋkin.

english_text:
David Becomes King of Israel
(1 Chronicles 11.1-3)
1Israel's leaders met with David at Hebron and said, “We are your relatives. 2Even when Saul was king, you led our nation in battle. And the Lord promised that someday you would rule Israel and take care of us like a shepherd.”
3During the meeting, David made an agreement with the leaders and asked the Lord to be their witness. Then the leaders poured olive oil on David's head to show that he was now the king of Israel.
4 David was 30 years old when he became king, and he ruled for 40 years. 5He lived in Hebron for the first seven and a half years and ruled only Judah. Then he moved to Jerusalem, where he ruled both Israel and Judah for 33 years.
How David Captured Jerusalem
(1 Chronicles 11.4-9; 14.1,2)
6 The Jebusites lived in Jerusalem, and David led his army there to attack them. The Jebusites did not think he could get in, so they told him, “You can't get in here! We could keep you out, even if we couldn't see or walk!”
7-9David told his troops, “You will have to go up through the water tunnel to get those Jebusites. I hate people like them who can't walk or see.”
That's why there is still a rule that says, “Only people who can walk and see are allowed in the temple.”
David captured the fortress on Mount Zion, then he moved there and named it David's City. He had the city rebuilt, starting with the landfill to the east. 10David became a great and strong ruler, because the Lord All-Powerful was on his side.
11King Hiram of Tyre sent some officials to David. Carpenters and stone workers came with them, and they brought cedar logs so they could build David a palace.
12David knew that the Lord had made him king of Israel and that he had made him a powerful ruler for the good of his people.
David's Sons Born in Jerusalem
(1 Chronicles 14.3-7)
13After David left Hebron and moved to Jerusalem, he married many women from Jerusalem, and he had a lot of children. 14His sons who were born there were Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon, 15Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia, 16Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet.
David Fights the Philistines
(1 Chronicles 14.8-17)
17The Philistines heard that David was now king of Israel, and they came into the hill country to try and capture him. But David found out and went into his fortress. 18So the Philistines camped in Rephaim Valley.
19David asked the Lord, “Should I attack the Philistines? Will you let me win?”
The Lord told David, “Attack! I will let you win.”
20David attacked the Philistines and defeated them. Then he said, “I watched the Lord break through my enemies like a mighty flood.” So he named the place “The Lord Broke Through.” 21David and his troops also carried away the idols that the Philistines had left behind.
22Some time later, the Philistines came back into the hill country and camped in Rephaim Valley. 23David asked the Lord what he should do, and the Lord answered:
Don't attack them from the front. Circle around behind and attack from among the balsam trees. 24Wait until you hear a sound in the treetops like marching troops. Then attack quickly! That sound will mean I have marched out ahead of you to fight the Philistine army.
25David obeyed the Lord and defeated the Philistines. He even chased them all the way from Geba to the entrance to Gezer.
translation_text:
Daafiidi kpántì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ bɔtiu
(Kpèè 1 Kroo 11.1-3)
1Isirayeel yab naakɔti kɔkɔ dɔ́miń Eebrɔn tiŋkin ki ká Daafiidi ki bí-u yii: «Ti baasii pēē dinabiil ní. 2Iyunti in jítèe, min Saayuul nìn sá ti-bɔtiuee, sii di nìn līī Isirayeel yab janjaliibi nyɔkɔpu ki cáǹ-bi kujaau. Ní ti-Dindaan nìn pōoǹ-si yii: <Sii di làá dāá kpàà Isirayeel yab man nibul kí nīn sá bi-bɔtiu.>» 3Isirayeel yab kpilib kɔkɔ nìn dɔ́miń Eebrɔn tiŋkin Daafiidi cee. Niin ní u nì bi ŋá mpèé ti-Dindaan nimbiin, ní bi bātì ŋkpam ki sītì u-yil pu ú nīn sá Isirayeel yab bɔtiu. 4Daafiidi nìn cáá abin mmuŋku nì saalaa ní ki jíń dibeel. U nìn kāl̀ dibeel abin imuŋku ili ní. 5U nìn kāl̀ Eebrɔn tiŋkin ki jíń Juuda yab pu dibeel abin aluli nì dijandi, ní ki kāl̀ Jeerusaleem ki jíń dibeel Isirayeel yab nì Juuda yab kɔkɔ pu abin mmuŋku nì saalaa nì abin ata.
Daafiidi jáń ki fōō Jeerusaleem tiŋki
(Kpèè 1 Kroo 11.4-9, 14.1-2)
6Ubɔti Daafiidi nì u-yab bóob́ kí já nì Jeebusi yab bin kóò Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee. Binib gbanti nìn bí Daafiidi yii: «Aa làá kɔ́nní kitiŋ nee poon! Bijɔfub nì bideembi saaleen di làá jà-si kí gíiǹ.» Bi nìn là kí lì yii Daafiidi kaa làá ŋmā kí kɔ́. 7Daafiidi jáń ki fōō Siiyɔn, kitiŋ pɔŋŋu pɔ̀ti pu laakin bi máń diguŋkpaandi ki túee. Kí yòon̄ ŋyunti gbantee ní bi kíǹ ki yíì niin yii Daafiidi Tiŋki.
8Daafiidi nìn lī ŋwiin gbanti yii: «Un yaa là kí já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ Jeebusi yabee, udaan ń dī kubùŋu kun bi cátì kitiŋee pu kí kɔ́ kí nyā bi-pu. An yaa kíǹ bijɔfub nì bideembee, maa là bi-bɔti.» Niin ní dilìmbil nee nyáń yii: «Bijɔfub nì bideembi kaa kóò kunimbɔtidiin.»
9Daafiidi cūtìi kāl̀ kitiŋ pɔ̀ti pu laakin bi máń diguŋkpaandi ki túee ní ki pú niin diyindi yii <Daafiidi Tiŋki>. Boonee, u nìn fātìi máń ki māntìi tú kí yòon̄ Miiloo kí nīn cá poon pú. 10Daafiidi nìn mɔ̀tīi kāntí mpɔn ki cá, ní ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan nìn bí u-cee.
11Tiir yab bɔtiu Iram nìn túnní binib Daafiidi cee. Bi nìn cáań-u busubu bun bi yíì seediree dɔi nì kapintab nì bitaŋkpakpitiliibi bí mā-u dibeecindi. 12Niinee, Daafiidi nìn béè yii ti-Dindaan u-ba di kāaǹ-u Isirayeel tiŋki pu dibeel, ní Isirayeel u-nibul puee, u bíi yòontí u-beel yilpu.
Daafiidi jipɔmbi bin u màl̄ Jeerusaleemee
(Kpèè 1 Kroo 3.5-9, 14.3-7)
13Daafiidi nín nìn yíkì Eebrɔn ki cūtìi kíǹ ki bí Jeerusaleemee, u nìn gíti cáá binimpoobi tikpil ki kútì, binimpukpilib nì nnimpuwaamu, ní bi nìn màl̄-u mbininjabiyaamu nì nnimpubiyaamu. 14Nninjabiyaamu mun u màl̄ Jeerusaleemee yiŋŋi sèé: Samuwa nì Soobaab nì Naatan nì Saloomɔn, 15nì Yiibaar nì Eelsuwa nì Neefeegi nì Yaafiya nì 16Eelsama nì Eeliyadaa nì Eeliifeeleeti.
Daafiidi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Fiiliistii yab
(1 Kroo 14.8-16)
17Fiiliistii yab nín nìn gbìl̄ yii bi bātì ŋkpam ki sītì Daafiidi yil pu ki kāaǹ-u dibeelee, ní bi-kɔkɔ nín cá kí nyàab̀-u kí cúú-u. Daafiidi gbìl̄ an bɔtee ní ki nín sìntī kibalilaŋin. 18Fiiliistii yab bàn̄ee ní ki yàl̄ ki gbí Reefayiim tantakalin. 19Ní Daafiidi bālifì ti-Dindaan yii: «Ḿ cùú já nì Fiiliistii yabaaa? A làá dū-bi kí ŋá m-ŋaanaaa?» Ní ti-Dindaan kíí Daafiidi yii: «Cùú já nì bi, m làá dū-bi kí ŋá a-ŋaan.»
20Niinee Daafiidi nín cá áli Baal Peerasiim ki jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi niin. Ní ki bí yii: «Kii nnyim nín cífí nnyimbilkaam gundi dibùndi puee, míǹ ní m-Dindaan cátì nsan m-nimbiin m-nannanliibi kansikin!» An pu ní bi pú niin diyindi yii Baal-Peerasiim. Taapu di sá yii: «Un cífí dibùndee Kpiliu.» 21Fiiliistii yab nìn sáǹ ki fá bi-waaŋi niin, ní Daafiidi nì u-naacimbi dɔ́miń ki yōoǹ.
22Fiiliistii yab fātìi tí gítìń ki yàl̄ ki gbí Reefayiim kí já nì Daafiidi. 23Ní Daafiidi bālifì ti-Dindaan ní úǹ kíí-u yii: «Á taa bíití bi-nimbiin pú kí já nì bi! Màntī bi-boon pú, ní kí dāá nyā bi-pu isufi taapu. 24A yaa láa gbìl̄ bi-tagbiŋŋi pu isufee yilpuee, á yáb́ malaa. Ti-Dindaan di līntì a-nyɔkɔpu kí já nì Fiiliistii yab janjakitil.» 25Ní Daafiidi ŋá kii ti-Dindaan nín bí ú ŋá puee, ní ki jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi, ki jìn̄-bi kí yòon̄ Geeba ki tin cáa sāā Geeseer kpaanyɔkɔ.

english_text:
David Brings the Sacred Chest Back to Jerusalem
(1 Chronicles 13.1-14; 15.1—16.3,43)
1David brought together 30,000 of Israel's best soldiers and 2 led them to Baalah in Judah, which was also called Kiriath-Jearim. They were going there to get the sacred chest and bring it back to Jerusalem. The throne of the Lord All-Powerful is above the winged creatures on top of this chest, and he is worshiped there.
3 They put the sacred chest on a new ox cart and started bringing it down the hill from Abinadab's house. Abinadab's sons Uzzah and Ahio were guiding the ox cart, 4with Ahio walking in front of it. 5Some of the people of Israel were playing music on small harps and other stringed instruments, and on tambourines, castanets, and cymbals. David and the others were happy, and they danced for the Lord with all their might.
6But when they came to Nacon's threshing-floor, the oxen stumbled, so Uzzah reached out and took hold of the sacred chest. 7The Lord God was very angry with Uzzah for doing this, and he killed Uzzah right there beside the chest.
8David got angry with God for killing Uzzah. He named that place “Bursting Out Against Uzzah,” and that's what it's still called.
9David was afraid of the Lord and thought, “Should I really take the sacred chest to my city?” 10He decided not to take it there. Instead, he turned off the road and took it to the home of Obed Edom, who was from Gath.
11-12 The chest stayed there for three months, and the Lord greatly blessed Obed Edom, his family, and everything he owned. Then someone told King David, “The Lord has done this because the sacred chest is in Obed Edom's house.”
At once, David went to Obed Edom's house to get the chest and bring it to David's City. Everyone was celebrating. 13The people carrying the chest walked six steps, then David sacrificed an ox and a choice cow. 14He was dancing for the Lord with all his might, but he wore only a linen cloth. 15He and everyone else were celebrating by shouting and blowing horns while the chest was being carried along.
16Saul's daughter Michal looked out her window and watched the chest being brought into David's City. But when she saw David jumping and dancing for the Lord, she was disgusted.
17They put the chest inside a tent that David had set up for it. David worshiped the Lord by sacrificing animals and burning them on an altar, 18then he blessed the people in the name of the Lord All-Powerful. 19 He gave all the men and women in the crowd a small loaf of bread, some meat, and a handful of raisins, then everyone went home.
Michal Talks to David
20David went home so he could ask the Lord to bless his family. But Saul's daughter Michal went out and started yelling at him. “You were really great today!” she said. “You acted like a dirty old man, dancing around half-naked in front of your servants' slave-girls.”
21David told her, “The Lord didn't choose your father or anyone else in your family to be the leader of his people. The Lord chose me, and I was celebrating in honor of him. 22I'll show you just how great I can be! I'll even be disgusting to myself. But those slave-girls you talked about will still honor me!”
23Michal never had any children.
translation_text:
Daafiidi lēē kí cùnnì mpèé dakaau Jeerusaleem
(Kpèè 1 Kroo 13.4-14, 15.25–16.3)
1Daafiidi fātìi kpáfì Isirayeel yab janjamɔntiibi. Bi nìn nyáń binib kutukub mmuŋku nì saalaa ní. 2Daafiidi nì binibee nìn nín cá Baala tiŋki kin bí Juuda tiŋkinee kí gíiǹní mpèé Dakaau. Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan un kā keerubimbi puee yindi ní bi nìn dūu pú Dakaa gbanti. 3Bi nìn dū Unimbɔti dakaau ki tākaǹ tɔrɔkupɔɔn poon. Bi nìn yōoǹní-u Abinadaab dumpu kigbantaŋ pu. Abinadaab jipɔɔn Usa nì Ayiiyoo di nìn kpòotī inaa in dàtī tɔrɔkupɔɔn gbantee. 4Bi nín yōoǹ Unimbɔti dakaau Abinadaab dumpu kigbantaŋ pu mimmee, ní Ayiiyoo līī u-nyɔkɔpu. 5Daafiidi nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nìn bí ki fàal̀ nì dipɔɔpindi ti-Dindaan nimbiin ki bɔ̀ɔ́ tiwambɔɔkaal tin bi dū siipreesi dɔi ki kpítèe kɔkɔ nì ti-bulifi, nì kubeeu nì saŋgu nì ŋgaŋgamu nì icaal nì cancakantib. 6Bi bàn̄ Naakɔn tuulool caŋinee ní inaa gbéetì ní Usa tāntì u-ŋal ki cúú Unimbɔti dakaau. 7Ti-Dindaan nìn fōō Usa pu diŋuul, ní ki fáá-u niin u nín yīntèe pu. Usa nìn kpíì Unimbɔti dakaau caŋin niin.
8Niinee Daafiidi fōō diŋuul, kun puee ti-Dindaan nìn dáaĺ Usa tafal. Ní bi pú mpaan gbanti diyindi yii Peereesi-Usa. Bi dáá gbítìi yíì mpaan gbanti míǹ ki dāa sāā díǹ. 9Daafiidi nìn fāŋkì ti-Dindaan yaadal wiiŋŋu, ní ki bí yii: «Maa làá ŋmā kí cùnnì ti-Dindaan dakaau m-dumpu!» 10Daafiidi kaa nìn gíti là kí yòon̄ ti-Dindaan dakaau kí cùnnì Daafiidi Tiŋkin. U nìn yāntì bi cáa yóoǹ Oobeedi-Eedoom dumpu. Kijapaai gbanti nìn sá Gaati tiŋkin ní. 11Dakaayee nìn yúl̀ Oobeedi-Eedoom dumpu iŋmal ita, ní ti-Dindaan bīiǹ u nì u-dicaŋku kɔkɔ pu.
Bi cáá ti-Dindaan dakaau ki kɔ́ǹ Jeerusaleem
12Bi nìn dɔ́miń ki tùkū Daafiidi yii: «Unimbɔti dakaau puee, ti-Dindaan bīiǹ Oobeedi-Eedoom pu ki yāntì u-tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ bíi còom̄-u tiŋan.» Niinee Daafiidi cūtì Oobeedi-Eedoom dumpu ki yōoǹ Unimbɔti dakaau ki cáa cūnnì Daafiidi Tiŋkin ifaal poon. 13Ŋyunti ŋun ní bin tú ti-Dindaan dakaauee yaa dāatì ataa aluuyee ní bí yūĺ kí dū unaja nì dinabil din bí màlmalee kí ŋá saraa. 14Daafiidi nìn baasii bíi ŋōō nì u-pɔŋŋu kɔkɔ ní ti-Dindaan nimbiin. U nìn pée pēē bisaraaŋaliibi bɔkutil din bí fálfalee ní. 15Daafiidi nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nìn yōoǹ ti-Dindaan dakaau ki cáa cūnnì Jeerusaleem nì dipɔɔpindi kuŋkuuntii ki búǹ ŋyin.
16Ŋyunti ŋun bi cáá ti-Dindaan dakaau ki kɔ́ǹ Daafiidi Tiŋkinee, Saayuul bisal Miikaal gbóoń tɔkɔlee ki ká ubɔti Daafiidi nín pée yùkufī ki tìintí pu ki ŋōō ti-Dindaan nimbiinee. U-ŋool gbanti puee, u nìn kpēē ki sīŋkiǹ-u u-pɔbilin. 17Daafiidi nìn gāā tanti dakaa gbanti pu. Bi nìn yōoǹní dakaayee ki kɔ́ǹ tantee poon ki yóoǹ mpaan ŋun Daafiidi nìn lēē kí síiń-uee. Míǹ boonee ní Daafiidi ŋá bisaraawɔkaabi nì mpèé saraabi ki tīī ti-Dindaan. 18U ŋá saraabi míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki mēē ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan ki bīiǹ samaa pu. 19Míǹ boonee ní u yākatì Isirayeel samaau kɔkɔ tijin. Uninja kamaa nì unimpu kamaa nìn fōō kpɔnɔ nì dinaŋkúndi nì fiinyi subiliŋ akulim kalaau. Míǹ boonee ní báà ŋma fātìi nín kùǹ.
20Daafiidi fātì u-dumpu kí cùú mèè kí bìin̄ u-dicaŋku yab pu, ní Miikaal nyáń ki túŋkì-u ki bí-u yii: «Bi baasii tīī sii Isirayeel bɔtiu díǹ tinyool ní. A lēē a-cancaŋgbeel ki dàkā a-kàliŋkpilib tɔntɔnliibi binimpoobi kii unil un kaa bí tibanee nín ŋáań puee!»
21Ní Daafiidi kíí-u yii: «An sá kí tīī m-Dindaan tinyool pu ní m ŋɔ́ń míǹ. Úǹ di lēē-mi, kun puee m-bɔti fáatiǹ-u ki jítiǹ a-baa nì a-dicaŋkun yab kɔkɔ, ní ki kāaǹ-mi dibeel Isirayeel u-nibul pu. U-nimbiin ní m làá nīn fàal̀. 22M làá gíti sìntī m-ba taapu kpataaa kí taa nín̄ sá tiba kí jītíǹ min bí nee. Míǹ gba di làá yàntī bitɔntɔnliibi bin bɔti a sòoǹ nee ń tīī-mi tinyool.» 23Saayuul bisal Miikaal kaa ká mmaal ní ki dāa kpáàa kpíì.

english_text:
The Lord's Message to David
(1 Chronicles 17.1-15)
1King David moved into his new palace, and the Lord let his kingdom be at peace. 2Then one day, as David was talking with Nathan the prophet, David said, “Look around! I live in a palace made of cedar, but the sacred chest has to stay in a tent.”
3Nathan replied, “The Lord is with you, so do what you want!”
4That night, the Lord told Nathan 5to go to David and give him this message:
David, you are my servant, so listen to what I say. Why should you build a temple for me? 6I didn't live in a temple when I brought my people out of Egypt, and I don't live in one now. A tent has always been my home wherever I have gone with them. 7I chose leaders and told them to be like shepherds for my people Israel. But did I ever say anything to even one of them about building a cedar temple for me?
8 David, this is what I, the Lord All-Powerful, say to you. I brought you in from the fields where you took care of sheep, and I made you the leader of my people. 9Wherever you went, I helped you and destroyed your enemies right in front of your eyes. I have made you one of the most famous people in the world.
10I have given my people Israel a land of their own where they can live in peace, and they won't have to tremble with fear any more. Evil nations won't bother them, as they did 11when I let judges rule my people. And I have kept your enemies from attacking you.
Now I promise that you and your descendants will be kings. 12 I'll choose one of your sons to be king when you reach the end of your life and are buried in the tomb of your ancestors. I'll make him a strong ruler, 13and no one will be able to take his kingdom away from him. He will be the one to build a temple for me. 14 I will be his father, and he will be my son.
When he does wrong, I'll see that he is corrected, just as children are corrected by their parents. 15But I will never put an end to my agreement with him, as I put an end to my agreement with Saul, who was king before you. 16 I will make sure that one of your descendants will always be king.
17Nathan told David exactly what he had heard in the vision.
David Gives Thanks to the Lord
(1 Chronicles 17.16-27)
18David went into the tent he had set up for the sacred chest. Then he sat there and prayed:
Lord All-Powerful, my family and I don't deserve what you have already done for us, 19and yet you have promised to do even more. Is this the way you usually treat people? 20I am your servant, and you know my thoughts, so there is nothing more that I need to say. 21You have done this wonderful thing, and you have let me know about it, because you wanted to keep your promise.
22 Lord All-Powerful, you are greater than all others. No one is like you, and you alone are God. Everything we have heard about you is true. 23 And there is no other nation on earth like Israel, the nation you rescued from slavery in Egypt to be your own. You became famous by using great and wonderful miracles to force other nations and their gods out of your land, so your people could live here. 24You have chosen Israel to be your people forever, and you have become their God.
25And now, Lord God, please do what you have promised me and my descendants. 26Then you will be famous forever, and everyone will say, “The Lord God All-Powerful rules Israel, and David's descendants are his chosen kings.” 27After all, you really are Israel's God, the Lord All-Powerful. You've told me that you will let my descendants be kings. That's why I have the courage to pray to you like this, even though I am only your servant.
28 Lord All-Powerful, you are God. You have promised me some very good things, and you can be trusted to do what you promise. 29Please bless my descendants and let them always be your chosen kings. You have already promised, and I'm sure that you will bless my family forever.
translation_text:
Unimbɔti pōoǹ Daafiidi nì u-naantiibi dipoondi
(Kpèè 1 Kroo 17.1-15)
1Daafiidi kɔ́ u-beecindin, ní ti-Dindaan nyántì-u u-nannanliibi bin māntìi tú-uee ŋaan, ki tīī-u ŋgbansɔŋfi. 2Dalbee ní u bí Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Naatan yii: «Kpèè, man kóò dibeecindi din bi dū idɔmɔnti in bi yíì seediree ki kpááyee. Ama ní Unimbɔti dakaau yú tanti un poon bi dū iŋoobu kuti satab ki gāāyee.» 3Ní Naatan bí ubɔti yii: «Tin kā a-pɔbilin a là kí ŋée, cùú ŋá míǹ, di sá yii ti-Dindaan bí a-cee.»
4Ama kunyeeu gbantee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Naatan yii: 5«Cùú tùkù m-tɔntɔnliu Daafiidi yii man ni-Dindaan nín lī puee sɔ̀. Sii di kaa làá mā-mi Kudii ní ḿ kɔ́. 6Kí yòon̄ daliŋkin m nyántì Isirayeel yab Eejipiti tiŋkin ki dāa sāā díǹ nee, ubɔ kaa máń-mi kudii m kɔ́ ki ká. M nìn sá kii usaŋkinlee ní ki nìn kàal̀ ntimu ki nìkì, ní ki nìn kóò tantin. 7Kí kūtèe, ŋyunti ŋun m dūu céeǹ Isirayeel yab bi-saŋkindi poonee, m nìn kāaǹ bikpilib tikpil. Bíǹ di nìn kpāā Isirayeel yab m-nibul. Maa láá pée bālifì-bi dalba dalba yii: <Ba pu ní naa dū seedir dɔi ki máń-mi kudii?> 8Kɔŋkɔnnee á tùkù m-tɔntɔnliu Daafiidi yii: <Man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di páatì-si ipii boon kupikpaaun ki dū-si ki kāaǹ dibeel m-nibul Isirayeel yab pu. 9Laakin kamaa a cūtèe, m bí a-cee. M kúntì a-nannanliibi kɔkɔ a-nimbiin. M làá yòon̄ a-yindi yilpu kii binikpaambi bin kāl̀ kitiŋ puee. 10M làá tīī Isirayeel m-nibul mpaan ŋun pu m làá kàan̄-bee. Bi làá nīn kóò niin kaa làá fàŋkì tiba. Binikpitib biba kaa làá ti dāan̄ kí wɔ́b́-bi kii dooooyee, 11ŋyunti ŋun ní m nìn kāaǹ bibɔsoonliibi m-nibul Isirayeel puee. M làá fīī-si a-nannanliibi kɔkɔ ŋaan kí líí ní á ŋùŋfì. Di sá man ni-Dindaan bíi tùkù-si yii m làá náań-si dicindi. 12Ŋyunti ŋun ní sii yuntiŋu yaa láa sāā a cūtìi dōoǹ ki ŋàl̄ a-baabee, m làá dāá lēē a-maaliŋun ubɔ, un sá a-poon naŋuee kí kàan̄ dibeel a-yil pu. M làá dāá yàntī u-beel ń nīn bá ki pɔ̄ɔ̄. 13Úǹ di làá dāá mā-mi Kudii kí tīī m-yindi tinyool, ní ḿ dāá yàntī u-beel ń nīn bá ki pɔ̄ɔ̄ ki cá jaanjaan. 14Man làá nīn sá-u ubaati, ní úǹ ń nīn sá-mi ujipɔnti. U yaa yīntèe, m làá dáaĺ u-tafal kii ubaati nín dátí u-jipɔɔn tafal puee ní. 15Ama maa làá cúú m-laŋŋaŋfitiiku kí fōō u-cee kii m nín fōō-ku Sayuul cee puee. M nìn dū Sayuul ki fá ní ki dū sii ki kāaǹ u-paaŋŋu pu. 16M làá yàntī a-dicaŋku nì a-beel ń nīn bá ki pɔ̄ɔ̄ kí nīn cá jaanjaan. Tiba kaa làá ŋmā kí cìŋkì a-beel pɔŋŋu ŋwindal.» 17Ní Naatan cáá tibɔti tin Unimbɔti sòon̄ nì u dileedakal poonee kɔkɔ ki tùkū Daafiidi.
Daafiidi wimmeem
(Kpèè 1 Kroo 17.16-27)
18Niinee ní ubɔti Daafiidi cūtì ti-Dindaan nimbiin ki mēē-u yii: «M-Dindaan Unimbɔti, ba ní m sá, ní m-dicaŋku bí tilatin ní a cáá-mi ki bàn̄ laakin m bí nee ní? 19Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, a wāĺ yii tin a ŋá nee pátì a-cee. Di sá a gíti pōoǹ man a-tɔntɔnliu dicaŋku ipoon iba in bɔti dáá dátìńee. M-Dindaan Unimbɔti, tin a ŋá nee máaǹ unilaaa? 20M-Dindaan Unimbɔti, a nyí man a-tɔntɔnliu tiŋan. Too tilati ní m làá gíti lì kí kūtì. 21Kii a nín pōoǹ ki lī yii a làá ŋá pu a-pɔbilinee ní a túń atuŋkpaan nee ki nyántì-ŋi ki dàkā man a-tɔntɔnliu. 22Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti, a lafun baasii sá ukpaan ní! Aa cáá juti! Sii boonee, Unimbɔti ubɔ gíti kpá, kii ti nín gbìl̀ bi sòoǹ puee. 23Dinibul diba gíti bí kitiŋ pu doo ki bí kii Isirayeel nibuleeee? A cūtìi dá-dì ki nyántì Eejipiti yab nì bi-waaŋi ŋaan ki dū-dì ki kpántì a-nibul. A yōoǹ di-yindi yilpu, ki túń atuŋkpaan nì maamaaci tuuŋŋi ki tīī-dì a-tiŋkin. Ditimbundi diba gíti bí ki náań nì a-timbundi din a dá ki nyántì Eejipiti yab timbundi nì bi-waaŋi ŋaaneeee? 24Ti-Dindaan, a dū Isirayeel yab ki kpántì a-nibul kí nīn cá jaanjaan, ní a kpántì bi-Nimbɔtiu. 25Kɔŋkɔnnee m-Dindaan Unimbɔti, a nín sòon̄ yii a làá ŋá pu kí tīī man a-tɔntɔnliu nì m-dicaŋkuee, ŋá míǹ án nīn bí ki cá jaanjaan, kii a nín pōoǹ puee. 26Bí yòon̄ a-yindi yilpu kí nīn pée cá jaanjaan, binib ń lì yii: <Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan di sá Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu!> Ní man a-tɔntɔnliu Daafiidi dicaŋku ń nīn bá ki pɔ̄ɔ̄ a-nimbiin. 27An puee ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu, sii a-ba di tùkū man a-tɔntɔnliu yii: <M làá náań-si dicindi>. An pu ní man a-tɔntɔnliu ká kunyannyaau kí mèè-si ŋwimmeem nee. 28Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti, sii di sá Unimbɔti. A yaa lī puee, míǹ ní a ŋáań, ní a pōoǹ man a-tɔntɔnliu nnaam! 29Kɔŋkɔnnee, bìin̄ man a-tɔntɔnliu naantiibi pu bí nīn pée bí a-nimbiin ki cá jaanjaan. Di sá yii sii ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti di pōoǹ míǹ. A-biindi puee, man a-tɔntɔnliu dicaŋku làá fōō dibiindi kí nīn cá jaanjaan!»

english_text:
A List of David's Victories in War
(1 Chronicles 18.1-13)
1Later, David attacked and badly defeated the Philistines. Israel was now free from their control.
2David also defeated the Moabites. Then he made their soldiers lie down on the ground, and he measured them off with a rope. He would measure off two lengths of the rope and have those men killed, then he would measure off one length and let those men live. The people of Moab had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him.
3David set out for the Euphrates River to build a monument there. On his way, he defeated the king of Zobah, whose name was Hadadezer the son of Rehob. 4In the battle, David captured 1,700 cavalry and 20,000 foot soldiers. He also captured war chariots, but he destroyed all but 100 of them. 5When troops from the Aramean kingdom of Damascus came to help Hadadezer, David killed 22,000 of them. 6He left some of his soldiers in Damascus, and the Arameans had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him.
Everywhere David went, the Lord helped him win battles.
7Hadadezer's officers had carried their arrows in gold cases hung over their shoulders, but David took these cases and brought them to Jerusalem. 8He also took a lot of bronze from the cities of Betah and Berothai, which had belonged to Hadadezer.
9-10King Toi of Hamath and King Hadadezer had been enemies. So when Toi heard that David had attacked and defeated Hadadezer's whole army, he sent his son Joram to praise and congratulate David. Joram also brought him gifts made of silver, gold, and bronze. 11David gave these to the Lord, just as he had done with the silver and gold that he had captured from 12Edom, Moab, Ammon, Philistia, Amalek, and from King Hadadezer of Zobah.
13 David fought the Edomite army in Salt Valley and killed 18,000 of their soldiers. When he returned, he built a monument. 14David left soldiers all through Edom, and the people of Edom had to accept him as their ruler.
Wherever David went, the Lord helped him.
A List of David's Officials
(1 Chronicles 18.14-17)
15David ruled all Israel with fairness and justice.
16Joab the son of Zeruiah was the commander in chief of the army.
Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept the government records.
17Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Abiathar the son of Ahimelech, were the priests.
Seraiah was the secretary.
18Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was the commander of David's bodyguard.
David's sons were priests.
translation_text:
Daafiidi nín jáń tijáti tiŋyee
(Kpèè 1 Kroo 18.1-13)
1Míǹ boonee Daafiidi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Fiiliistii yab, ki nyīī-bi ki gùl̄ taapu, ki fōō bi-ŋaan mpɔn ŋun bi nìn cáá kitiŋ gbanti puee. 2U nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Moowaab yab, ní ki yāntì bi dōoǹ kitiŋ ipɔ̀n ita pu. U nìn kūū bin nìn dɔ̄ ipɔ̀n ili ipeepeekaa puee ní ki kíǹ bin dɔ̄ mpɔ̀nluŋkikaa puee. Míǹ boonee ní Moowaab yab kpántì Daafiidi yumbui ki kíǹ ki pà lampoo ki tìì-u. 3Daafiidi nìn tí jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Reewoob jipɔɔn Adadeeseer, Sooba yab bɔtiu, ŋyunti ŋun úǹ nìn bíi bɔ́ntí kí já kí fōō Eefiraata tiŋki kí ŋá u-taapuee. 4Daafiidi nìn cúú u-tanjakaliibi kutuku ubɔ nì alaataa aluli nì u-janjaliibi bin còom̄ ataa puee kutukub mmuŋku. U nìn lēē itaamu dilaataal in làá nīn dátí u-tɔrɔkubee, ní ki gāā ki kpātì in kíǹee tabilɔnti. 5Siirii yab bin kóò Damaasee nìn dɔ́miń ki tíkiǹ Adadeeseer, Sooba yab bɔtiu, ní Daafiidi kūū bi-kansikin binib kutukub mmuŋku nì bili. 6Daafiidi nìn kāaǹ kɔmandambi Siirii yab bin kóò Damaasi tiŋkinee ní ki dū-bi ki kpántì u-yumbui, ní bi kíǹ ki pà lampoo ki tìì-u. Laakin kamaa ní Daafiidi yaa nìn pée cūtèe, ti-Dindaan nìn tìì-u dijajil ní. 7Daafiidi nìn jáń ki fōō sindaariya gbampɔɔŋi ŋin Adadeeseer janjaliibi nìn ŋúb́ee, ki cáa cūnnì Jeerusaleem. 8U nìn fōō tasa kúti tikpil ubɔti Adadeeseer timmu Beeta nì Beerootayi poon.
9Amaati yab bɔtiu Tooyi nìn gbìl̄ yii Daafiidi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Adadeeseer janjaliibi kɔkɔ. 10Ní Tooyi dū u-jipɔɔn Yooram ki tú ú cùú jāam̀ Daafiidi kí pàkà-u u nín jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Adadeeseeree. Di sá Tooyi pulincɔnti mbaa di nìn sá Adadeeseer. Yooram nìn cáá sindaariya nì animbil kúti nì tasa kúti wanti ki tīī Daafiidi. 11Daafiidi nìn dū tiwan gbanti mun ki sú ti-Dindaan, kii u nín nìn dū sindaariya nì tikúti nimbiliŋ tin u nìn jáń ki fōoń atimbun ŋin u nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹee ki sú puee. 12Atimbun gbanti di sá Siirii yab bin kóò Damaasee nì Amɔn yab nì Fiiliistii yab nì Amaleeki yab nì tiwan tin u nìn jáń ki fōoń Reewoob jipɔɔn Adadeeseer, Sooba yab bɔtiu ceeyee. 13Daafiidi yindi nìn mɔ̄tìi yíkì yilpu.
U nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Siirii yab ki kūū binib kutukub bili kpá mmuŋku Ŋyaam tantakalin ní ki fātìi gítìń. 14Daafiidi nìn kāaǹ kɔmandambi bi-timmun, ní ki nyīī Eedoom yab ki gùl̄ taapu. Míǹ ní ti-Dindaan nìn tīī Daafiidi dijajil ajan ŋin kɔkɔ pu u nìn cūtèe.
Daafiidi kàliŋkpilib yiŋŋi
(Kpèè 1 Kroo 18.14-17)
15Daafiidi nìn kāl̀ dibeel Isirayeel tiŋki kɔkɔ pu. U nìn sòoǹ samaa bɔti nì mbaamɔn kaa pɔ̀ gandi. 16Joowaab un na bi yíì Seeruyee di nìn sá ujanjakpil ní Ayiiluudi jipɔɔn Joosafaati sá ubɔti kpambal. 17Ayiituub jipɔɔn Saadooki nì Abiyataar jipɔɔn Ayiimeeleeki di nìn sá bisaraaŋaliibi ní Seeraya sá ugbaŋŋmal. 18Yeeyooda jipɔɔn Beenaya di nìn bí ki kpèé Keereeti nì Peeleeti yab. Daafiidi jipɔmbi mun nìn sá bisaraaŋaliibi ní.

english_text:
David Is Kind to Mephibosheth
1 One day, David thought, “I wonder if any of Saul's family are still alive. If they are, I will be kind to them, because I made a promise to Jonathan.” 2David called in Ziba, one of the servants of Saul's family. David said, “So you are Ziba.”
“Yes, Your Majesty, I am.”
3 David asked, “Are any of Saul's family still alive? If there are, I want to be kind to them.”
Ziba answered, “One of Jonathan's sons is still alive, but he can't walk.”
4“Where is he?” David asked.
Ziba replied, “He lives in Lo-Debar with Machir the son of Ammiel.”
5-6David sent some servants to bring Jonathan's son from Lo-Debar. His name was Mephibosheth, and he was the grandson of Saul. He came to David and knelt down.
David asked, “Are you Mephibosheth?”
“Yes, I am, Your Majesty.”
7David said, “Don't be afraid. I'll be kind to you because Jonathan was your father. I'm going to give you back the land that belonged to your grandfather Saul. Besides that, you will always eat with me at my table.”
8Mephibosheth knelt down again and said, “Why should you care about me? I'm worth no more than a dead dog.”
9David called in Ziba, Saul's chief servant, and told him, “Since Mephibosheth is Saul's grandson, I've given him back everything that belonged to your master Saul and his family. 10You and your 15 sons and 20 servants will work for Mephibosheth. You will farm his land and bring in his crops, so that Saul's family and servants will have food. But Mephibosheth will always eat with me at my table.”
11-13Ziba replied, “Your Majesty, I will do exactly what you tell me to do.” So Ziba's family and servants worked for Mephibosheth.
Mephibosheth was lame, but he lived in Jerusalem and ate at David's table, just like one of David's own sons. And he had a young son of his own, named Mica.
translation_text:
Daafiidi fōō Meefiibooseeti ki kāaǹ u-cee
1Dalbee ní Daafiidi bālifì yii: «Unil ubɔ kaa kíǹ Saayuul dicaŋkun ki bí dimaŋfalinaaa? Joonatan puee, ḿ bàà ŋá-u tiŋan.» 2Uninja ubɔ nìn bí Saayuul cindin ki sá u-tɔntɔnliu bi yíì-u yii Siiba. Bi nìn cáań uninjee ubɔti cee, ní ubɔti bí-u yii: «Sii ní bi yíì Siibaaa?» Ní u kíí-u yii: «Iiin, ti-baa an sá man.» 3Ní ubɔti bí yii: «Unil ubɔ kaa kíǹ Saayuul dicaŋkun ḿ ŋá udaan tiŋan kii m nín nìn pōoǹ Unimbɔti nimbiin yii m làá ŋá pueeee?» Ní Siiba kíí-u yii: «Joonatan jipɔɔn ubɔ kíǹ, u-taaŋi wɔ̀b̄.» 4Ní ubɔti bí yii: «U bí la?» Ní Siiba kíí-u yii: «U bí Amiyeel jipɔɔn Maakiir cee Loo-Deebaar.»
5Ní ubɔti Daafiidi tú unil Loo-Deebaar tiŋkin, Amiyeel jipɔɔn Maakiir cee ú cáań Meefiibooseeti. 6Joonatan jipɔɔn Meefiibooseeti, Saayuul naantiiu bāań Daafiidi ceeyee ní ki tātìi dōoǹ Daafiidi nimbiin dicincibil. Ní Daafiidi bālifì-u yii: «Sii di sá Meefiibooseetaaa?» Ní u kíí-u yii: «Iiin ti-baa, an sá man.» 7Ní Daafiidi bí-u yii: «Taa fàŋkì. A-baa Joonatan puee, m làá ŋá-si tiŋan. M làá gíiǹ a-naanja Saayuul timmu kɔkɔ ki tīī-si, ní man nì si ń nīn pēē disambibaantiil ki jīǹ baabadal.» 8Ní Meefiibooseeti tātìi dōoǹ dicincibil ní ki bí yii: «Ti-baa, ba pu ní a dū man a-tɔntɔnliu un kaa pée bí tiban kii kibɔkɔ kin kpíìyee bɔti ki páb́ a-ba?»
9Ubɔti yíiń Saayuul tɔntɔnliu Siiba ní ki bí-u yii: «M dū tin kɔkɔ sá Saayuul nì u-dicaŋku wantee ki tīī Meefiibooseeti, a-kpiliu naantiiu. 10Sii nì a-biyaamu nì a-tɔntɔnliibi di làá nīn gbāā ki kù ki tìì-u. Á nīn cāabìń tijin tin u-dicaŋku làá nīn jīǹee, ama man nì u di làá nīn pēē disambibaantiil ki jīǹ baabadal.» Siiba nìn cáá jipɔmbi saalku nì bitɔntɔnliibi mmuŋku. 11Ní Siiba bí ubɔti yii: «Ti-baa, m làá ŋá tin kɔkɔ a bí yii ḿ ŋée.» Kí yòon̄ ŋyunti gbantee, Meefiibooseeti nì ubɔti di nìn kíǹ ki pēē disambibaantiil ki jīǹ kii ubɔti jipɔɔnee.
12Meefiibooseeti nìn cáá kibininjabiki bi yíì-kì Miika. Bin kɔkɔ nìn kóò Siiba dumpuee nìn tūǹ ditundi ki tìì Meefiibooseeti ní. 13Meefiibooseeti taaŋi liitil nín nìn wɔ̀b̄ee puee, u nìn kíǹ ki kóò Jeerusaleem ní, kí ŋmā kí nīn cá ubɔti cee ki jīǹ tijin.

english_text:
Israel Fights Ammon
(1 Chronicles 19.1-19)
1Some time later, King Nahash of Ammon died, and his son Hanun became king. 2David said, “Nahash was kind to me, and I will be kind to his son.” So he sent some officials to the country of Ammon to tell Hanun how sorry he was that his father had died.
3But Hanun's officials told him, “Do you really believe David is honoring your father by sending these people to comfort you? He probably sent them to spy on our city, so he can destroy it.” 4Hanun arrested David's officials and had their beards shaved off on one side of their faces. He had their robes cut off just below the waist, and then he sent them away. 5They were terribly ashamed.
When David found out what had happened to his officials, he sent a message and told them, “Stay in Jericho until your beards grow back. Then you can come home.”
6The Ammonites realized that they had made David very angry, so they hired more foreign soldiers. Twenty thousand of them were foot soldiers from the Aramean cities of Beth-Rehob and Zobah, 1,000 were from the king of Maacah, and 12,000 were from the region of Tob. 7David heard what they had done, and he sent out Joab with all of his well-trained soldiers.
8The Ammonite troops came out and got ready to fight in front of the gate to their city. The Arameans from Zobah and Rehob and the soldiers from Tob and Maacah formed a separate group in the nearby fields.
9Joab saw that he had to fight in front and behind at the same time, and he picked some of the best Israelite soldiers to fight the Arameans. 10He put his brother Abishai in command of the rest of the army and gave them orders to fight the Ammonites. 11Joab told his brother, “If the Arameans are too much for me to handle, you can come and help me. If the Ammonites are too strong for you, I'll come and help you. 12Be brave and fight hard to protect our people and the cities of our God. I pray that the Lord will do whatever pleases him.”
13Joab and his soldiers attacked the Arameans, and the Arameans ran from them. 14When the Ammonite soldiers saw that the Arameans had run away, they ran from Abishai's soldiers and went back into their own city. Joab stopped fighting the Ammonites and returned to Jerusalem.
15The Arameans realized they had lost the battle, so they brought all their troops together again. 16Hadadezer sent messengers to call in the Arameans who were on the other side of the Euphrates River. Then Shobach, the commander of Hadadezer's army, led them to the town of Helam.
17David found out what the Arameans were doing, and he brought Israel's whole army together. They crossed the Jordan River and went to Helam, where the Arameans were ready to meet them. 18The Arameans attacked, but then they ran from Israel. David killed 700 chariot drivers and 40,000 cavalry. He also killed Shobach, their commander.
19When the kings who had been under Hadadezer's rule saw that Israel had beaten them, they made peace with Israel and accepted David as their ruler. The Arameans were afraid to help Ammon any more.
translation_text:
Bi kɔ́ǹ Daafiidi kàliŋkpilib icoo
(1 Kroo 19.1-5)
1Míǹ boonee ní Amɔn yab bɔtiu kpíì, ní u-jipɔɔn Anuun fōō u-yil ki kāl̀ dibeel. 2Niinee Daafiidi bí yii: «M làá ŋá Naasi jipɔɔn Anuun tiŋan kii u-baa nín nìn ŋá-mi tiŋan puee.» Ní Daafiidi lēē u-kàliŋkpilib ki tú bí cùú jāam̀-u u-baa kpool. Bikàliŋkpilib bin Daafiidi nìn túee nìn dūu bàn̄ Amɔn yab tiŋkin. 3Amɔn yab bɔtibiliŋ bí bi-kpiliu ubɔti Anuun yii: «A dàkafī yii Daafiidi là kí tīī a-baa jilmee pu ní u túnní binib bí dāá jāam̀-si u-kpoolaaa? An kaa sá bí cɔ̄ŋkì kitiŋ kí béé ki-filiŋfeetii kí dāá já kí fōō-kì dalba pu ní bi dɔ́mińaaa?» 4Niinee ní Anuun yāntì bi cúú Daafiidi kàliŋkpilib, ki kōol̀ bi-nyimpuliŋ dijandi, ki gíí bi-bɔkutiŋ ki ŋāatì bi-kpiliŋ pu, ní ki gíiǹ-bi ki líì. 5Daafiidi nìn gbìl̄ tin jítèe. Niinee ní u lēē binib bí cùú tūŋkì u-kàliŋkpilibee, di sá yii bi nìn kɔ́ǹ-bi icoo tikpil. Ní ubɔti bí bí tùkù-bi yii: «Ní kàl̄maan Jeeriikoo ni-nyimpuliŋ ń túkú, boonee ní nīn nín kùnní.»
Daafiidi jáń nì Amɔn yab nì Siirii yab
(Kpèè 1 Kroo 19.6-19)
6Amɔn yab nín béè yii bi kɔ́ Daafiidi poon ki lēē baadakamee ní bi nyàab̄ binib ki tú Siirii yab bin kóò Beeti-Reeyoob nì Soobayee cee ki pàn̄ bijanjaliibi kutukub mmuŋku, ki pàn̄ ubɔti Maaka janjaliibi kutuku, ní ki pàn̄ Toob yab janjaliibi kutukub saalaa nì bili. 7Daafiidi gbìl̄ mimmee ní ki dū Joowaab nì bijanjaliibi bin kɔkɔ cáá dibaatandee ki tú bí cùú já nì bi. 8Amɔn yab nìn nyáń ki yúl̀ mpɔ̀n pu kitiŋ punyɔkɔki caŋin ki cí kí já. Ní Siirii yab bin kóò Sooba nì Beeti-Reeyoobee nì Toob yab nì Maaka yab náká náká tisatin. 9Joowaab dáań ki ká yii an sá anikiti ali ní u làá jáǹ, diba bí nyɔkɔpu diba bí boon pú. Niinee ní u lútì Isirayeel janjaliibi kansikin bimɔntiibi ní ki dū-bi ki yóoǹ ki bíitì Siirii yab. 10Ní ki dū bin kíǹee ki ŋúbiǹ u-nabiki Abisayi, ki bíitiǹ Amɔn yab. 11Joowaab tùkū u-nabiki yii: «Siirii yab yaa bíi pɔ́ɔkíǹ-mee, á dāá tíkiń-mi. M yaa tí ká yii Amɔn yab bíi pɔ́ɔkíǹ-see, ma mun làá dāan̄ kí tíkiń-si. 12Dàkà dibaatandi, tí dàkà dibaatandi kí fīī ti-nibul nì ti-Nimbɔtiu timmu. Ti-Dindaan ń ŋá min u lèe.» 13Niinee Joowaab nì u-janjaliibi nín cá kí já nì Siirii yab, ní bíǹ sáǹ-bi. 14Amɔn yab nín ká yii Siirii yab sáǹee, ní bi mun sáǹ Abisayi, ki kɔ́ kitiŋin. Niinee Joowaab gbēeǹ kaa ti bíi jì Amɔn yab, ní ki nín fàtī Jeerusaleem.
15Siirii yab nín ká yii Isirayeel yab pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bee, ní bi kóoǹ bi-janjaliibi kɔkɔ ki kpáfì. 16Ubɔti Adadeeseer tú binib Siirii yab bin kóò Eefiraati mɔɔl lapu puee cee, ní bíǹ yíkìń ki dūu bāań Eelam. Adadeeseer janjakpiliu Soobaaki di nìn līī bi-nyɔkɔpu. 17Ní bi tùkū Daafiidi an bɔti, ní u kóoǹ Isirayeel yab janjaliibi kɔkɔ ki kpáfì, ní bi nín cá ki dūtì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ki dūu bàn̄ Eelaam. Siirii yab nìn yúl̀ mpɔ̀n pu ki tātìi gbāaǹ dikɔmbool pu kí já nì Daafiidi. 18Ama Isirayeel yab jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi, ní bi sáǹ. Daafiidi yab nìn kūū itaamu in dátí janjatɔrɔkubee alaataa aluli, ní ki kūū bitanjakaliibi kutukub imuŋku ili. Bi nìn tīī Siirii yab janjakpiliu Soobaaki tiweendi, ní u kpíì niin. 19Bibɔtiibi bin kɔkɔ nìn bí Adadeeseer taapuee nìn ká yii Isirayeel yab jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi. Niinee ní bi nì Isirayeel yab sòon̄ ki gbìlīǹ tɔb ŋgbansɔŋfi ń nīn bí bi-kansikin, ní ki sīntì bi-ba taapu ki tīī-bi. Kí yòon̄ ŋyunti gbantee, Siirii yab kíǹ ki fàŋkí kí jòò Amɔn yab.

english_text:
David and Bathsheba
(1 Chronicles 20.1a)
1 It was now spring, the time when kings go to war. David sent out the whole Israelite army under the command of Joab and his officers. They destroyed the Ammonite army and surrounded the capital city of Rabbah, but David stayed in Jerusalem.
2-4Late one afternoon, David got up from a nap and was walking around on the flat roof of his palace. A beautiful young woman was down below in her courtyard, bathing as her religion required. David happened to see her, and he sent one of his servants to find out who she was.
The servant came back and told David, “Her name is Bathsheba. She is the daughter of Eliam, and she is the wife of Uriah the Hittite.”
David sent some messengers to bring her to his palace. She came to him, and he slept with her. Then she returned home. 5But later, when she found out that she was going to have a baby, she sent someone to David with this message: “I'm pregnant!”
6David sent a message to Joab: “Send Uriah the Hittite to me.”
Joab sent Uriah 7to David's palace, and David asked him, “Is Joab well? How is the army doing? And how about the war?” 8Then David told Uriah, “Go home and clean up.” Uriah left the king's palace, and David had dinner sent to Uriah's house. 9But Uriah didn't go home. Instead, he slept outside the entrance to the royal palace, where the king's guards slept.
10Someone told David that Uriah had not gone home. So the next morning David asked him, “Why didn't you go home? Haven't you been away for a long time?”
11Uriah answered, “The sacred chest and the armies of Israel and Judah are camping out somewhere in the fields with our commander Joab and his officers and troops. Do you really think I would go home to eat and drink and sleep with my wife? I swear by your life that I would not!”
12Then David said, “Stay here in Jerusalem today, and I will send you back tomorrow.”
Uriah stayed in Jerusalem that day. Then the next day, 13David invited him for dinner. Uriah ate with David, who gave him so much to drink that he got drunk. But Uriah still did not go home. He went out and slept on his mat near the palace guards. 14Early the next morning, David wrote a letter and told Uriah to deliver it to Joab. 15The letter said: “Put Uriah on the front line where the fighting is the worst. Then pull the troops back from him, so that he will be wounded and die.”
16Joab had been carefully watching the city of Rabbah, and he put Uriah in a place where he knew there were some of the enemy's best soldiers. 17When the men of the city came out, they fought and killed some of David's soldiers—Uriah the Hittite was one of them.
18Joab sent a messenger to tell David everything that was happening in the war. 19He gave the messenger these orders:
When you finish telling the king everything that has happened, 20he may get angry and ask, “Why did you go so near the city to fight? Didn't you know they would shoot arrows from the wall? 21 Don't you know how Abimelech the son of Gideon was killed at Thebez? Didn't a woman kill him by dropping a large rock from the top of the city wall? Why did you go so close to the city walls?”
Then tell him, “One of your soldiers who was killed was Uriah the Hittite.”
22The messenger went to David and reported everything Joab had told him. 23He added, “The enemy chased us from the wall and out into the open fields. But we pushed them back as far as the city gate. 24Then they shot arrows at us from the top of the wall. Some of your soldiers were killed, and one of them was Uriah the Hittite.”
25David replied, “Tell Joab to cheer up and not to be upset about what happened. You never know who will be killed in a war. Tell him to strengthen his attack against the city and break through its walls.”
26When Bathsheba heard that her husband was dead, she mourned for him. 27Then after the time for mourning was over, David sent someone to bring her to the palace. She became David's wife, and they had a son.
The Lord's Message for David
The Lord was angry because of what David had done,
translation_text:
Daafiidi nì Beetiseeba bɔti
1Dibindi tú, ŋyunti ŋun bibɔtiibi jáà kujaauee, ní ubɔti Daafiidi tú ujanjakpil Joowaab nì u-kàliŋkpilib nì Isirayeel janjaliibi kɔkɔ bí cùú já nì Amɔn yab. Bi nìn pɔ̄fì Amɔn yab, ní ki māntìi tú bi-tiŋyil Raaba kí já nì kì. Daafiidi úǹ nìn gbíntì ki kā Jeerusaleem.
2Kujoou kubɔ Daafiidi dōoǹ ki ŋūŋfì ki yíkèe, ní ki jɔ́m̀ ki tɔ́kɔǹ bi nín bɔ̀b̄ u-beecindi yilpu puee ki bíi yìiǹ. U nìn ká unimpu ubɔ yú ki fùul̀. Unimpuee nìn ŋān̄ tikpil. 3Ní Daafiidi tú bí bàlifì kí béé un ní unimpuee sée, ní bi kíí-u yii: «An sá Eeliyaam bisal Beetiseeba, uyitiija Urii nimpuu.» 4Daafiidi nìn tú binib cūtìi yíiń unimpuee ki cáań-u, ní u dōoǹ nì u. Unimpuee nìn fùl̄ ŋkpin ki dóò ki ŋá dikoobil nín sá puee kpalaa dee. Míǹ boonee ní u yíkìi nín kùǹ.
5Beetiseeba gbíntì uŋmal gbanti poon. Ní u tú bi tùkū Daafiidi yii: «M cáá dipool.» 6Niinee ubɔti Daafiidi tú bí tùkù Joowaab yii: «Yàntī uyitiija Urii ń dāan̄ kí ká-mi.» Ní Joowaab dū Urii ki tú Daafiidi cee. 7Urii dūu bāań ubɔti Daafiidi ceeyee, ní u bālifì-u Joowaab nì bijanjaliibi pu, nì kujaau nín bíi còom̄ puee. 8Míǹ boonee ubɔti bí Urii yii: «Nín̄ cá a-dumpu kí dòon̄ kí ŋùŋfì.» Urii nìn nyáń ubɔti dumpu ní ubɔti nyàab̄ tiwampɔkaal ki tú bí cáá tīī-u.
9Ama Urii kaa nìn cūtì u-dumpu. U nìn gbíntì dibeecindi punyɔkɔpu ki dōoǹ, u nì ubɔti janjaliibi. 10Kutaa wúntèe ní Daafiidi gbìl̄ yii Urii kaa fu cūtìi dōoǹ u-dumpu. Ní ubɔti yíiń-u ki bālifì-u yii: «A nyánní nsan ŋun fɔ̀kɔ̀ee ní. Ba pu ní aa fu cūtì a-dumpu?» 11Ní Urii kíí Daafiidi yii: «Dipoondi dakaau yú tantin, ní Isirayeel yab nì Juuda yab kóò tantin. Ujanjakpil Joowaab nì u-janjaliibi dɔ̄ mpaampiin pu dijanjanaapaal pu. Ní man ń nīn cá m-dumpu kí jī kí nyɔ̀ kí dòon̄ m-nimpuu ceeee? M pūtì yii m kpá kí ŋá míǹ jaanjaan.» 12Ní ubɔti bí Urii yii: «Too, gíti kàl̄ díǹ, foolee ḿ fu yàntī á nīn gítí.» Ní Urii gbíntì Jeerusaleem yaadal wiiŋŋu nì kutaa kun gíti wúntèe. 13Ní Daafiidi yíiń-u ú dāan̄ u-dumpu kí jī tijin. Daafiidi nìn yāntì u nyùn̄ ndaam ki gbí. Ama Urii nyáńee ki gbíntì ubɔti janjaliibi cee ki dōoǹ, kaa cūtì u-dumpu.
14Ku wúntì kutaafaauee, Daafiidi ŋmàn̄ Joowaab kugbɔŋu ki dūu ŋúbiǹ Urii ú cáá tīī-u. 15Tin u nìn ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu gbanti poonee sèé: «Laakin dikɔ̀ndi yaa píĺ ki pɔ́ɔkèe, á dū Urii kí lìntī nyɔkɔpu. Míǹ boonee bí sútí kí wàatī-u bí kpɔ̀-u.»
Daafiidi yāntì bi kūū Batiseeba cal Urii
16Joowaab di nìn cí kitiŋ kin bi nìn māntìi tú kí já kí fōōyee. U nìn dū Urii ki síiǹ laakin u nyí yii binannanliibi baatandambi bée. 17Kitiŋee yab nìn nyáń ki jáń nì Joowaab nì u-yab. Bi nìn kūū Daafiidi janjaliibi biba. Bi nìn kūū uyitiija Urii mun. 18Ní Joowaab tú ntuun cūtìi máafì Daafiidi tin jítì kujaaunee kɔkɔ. 19U nìn tīī ntuunee mara yii: «A yaa máafì-u tin jítì kujaaunee kɔkɔ ki dóò, 20ní ubɔti yaa fōō diŋuul ki bí-si yii: <Ba pu ní ni sútì ki pìl̄ kitiŋ tikpil ki bíi jáà ní? Naa nyí yii bi ŋūǹ kí nīn yú digundi poon pú ki tòó ki lákatí án dāá cúú-naaa? 21Ŋma di kūū Yeerubaal jipɔɔn Abimeeleeki Teebeesi tiŋkin ní? An kaa sá unimpu ubɔɔɔ? U nìn dū kunaau ki tɔ́ an lákatì digundi boon ní ki yá ki kūū-u! Kin ba pu ní nimbi sútì ki pìl̄ digundi ní?> Ubɔti yaa lī mimmee, á kíí-u yii: <A-janjakpiliu Urii, uyitiija mun kpíì.>»
22Ní ntuunee búntì ki bàn̄ ki dū Joowaab nín tùkūń-u pu ú dāá tùkù Daafiidee ki máafì-u. 23U bí Daafiidi yii: «Binannanliibee nìn pɔ́ɔkiǹ-ti. Bi nyáń ki kpìlìń-ti, ama ní ti téé-bi ki cáa gūū bi-tiŋki punyɔkɔki. 24Niinee ní bipintɔliibi yúl̀ digundi poon pú ki tòoń ki lákatí digundi ní an cúú ti-janjaliibi biba ní bi kpíì. A-janjakpiliu Urii, uyitiija mun kpíì.» 25Ní Daafiidi bí ntuunee yii: «Á tùkù Joowaab yii: <Taa dū tibɔti nee kí páb́ a-ba. Kujaau poonee, ŋkúm kù ní kaa gàntī. Pɔ́ɔǹ kí já kí fōō kitiŋ gbanti kí kpēelikì-kì.> Á tīī-u kunyannyaau míǹ.»
26Beetiseeba nín gbìl̄ yii u-cal Urii kpíìń kujaaunee ní u kāl̀ u-kpool. 27Dikpool jítèe ní Daafiidi yāntì bi cūtìi cáań-u u-dumpu. U nìn dū-u ki kpántì u-nimpuu, ní u màl̄-u kibininjabiki. Ama tin Daafiidi nìn ŋée kaa nìn mɔ́ɔkiǹ ti-Dindaan.

english_text:
1 and he sent Nathan the prophet to tell this story to David:
A rich man and a poor man lived in the same town. 2The rich man owned a lot of sheep and cattle, 3but the poor man had only one little lamb that he had bought and raised. The lamb became a pet for him and his children. He even let it eat from his plate and drink from his cup and sleep on his lap. The lamb was like one of his own children.
4One day someone came to visit the rich man, but the rich man didn't want to kill any of his own sheep or cattle and serve it to the visitor. So he stole the poor man's lamb and served it instead.
5David was furious with the rich man and said to Nathan, “I swear by the living Lord that the man who did this deserves to die! 6And because he didn't have pity on the poor man, he will have to pay four times what the lamb was worth.”
7Then Nathan told David:
You are that rich man! Now listen to what the Lord God of Israel says to you: “I chose you to be the king of Israel. I kept you safe from Saul 8and even gave you his house and his wives. I let you rule Israel and Judah, and if that had not been enough, I would have given you much more. 9Why did you disobey me and do such a horrible thing? You murdered Uriah the Hittite by letting the Ammonites kill him, so you could take his wife.
10“Because you wouldn't obey me and took Uriah's wife for yourself, your family will never live in peace. 11 Someone from your own family will cause you a lot of trouble, and I will take your wives and give them to another man before your very eyes. He will go to bed with them while everyone looks on. 12What you did was in secret, but I will do this in the open for everyone in Israel to see.”
13-14David said, “I have disobeyed the Lord.”
“Yes, you have!” Nathan answered. “You showed you didn't care what the Lord wanted. He has forgiven you, and you won't die. But your newborn son will.” 15Then Nathan went back home.
David's Young Son Dies
The Lord made David's young son very sick.
16So David went without eating to show his sorrow, and he begged God to make the boy well. David would not sleep on his bed, but spent each night lying on the floor. 17His officials stood beside him and tried to talk him into getting up. But he would not get up or eat with them.
18After the child had been sick for seven days, he died, but the officials were afraid to tell David. They said to each other, “Even when the boy was alive, David wouldn't listen to us. How can we tell him his son is dead? He might do something terrible!”
19David noticed his servants whispering, and he knew the boy was dead. “Did my son die?” he asked his servants.
“Yes, he did,” they answered.
20David got up off the floor; he took a bath, combed his hair, and dressed. He went into the Lord's tent and worshiped, then he went back home. David asked for something to eat, and when his servants brought him some food, he ate it.
21His officials said, “What are you doing? You went without eating and cried for your son while he was alive! But now that he's dead, you're up and eating.”
22David answered:
While he was still alive, I went without food and cried because there was still hope. I said to myself, “Who knows? Maybe the Lord will have pity on me and let the child live.” 23But now that he's dead, why should I go without eating? I can't bring him back! Someday I will join him in death, but he can't return to me.
Solomon Is Born
24David comforted his wife Bathsheba and slept with her. Later on, she gave birth to another son and named him Solomon. The Lord loved Solomon 25and sent Nathan the prophet to tell David, “The Lord will call him Jedidiah.”
The End of the War with Ammon
(1 Chronicles 20.1b-3)
26Meanwhile, Joab had been in the country of Ammon, attacking the city of Rabbah. He captured the royal fortress 27and sent a messenger to tell David:
I have attacked Rabbah and captured the fortress guarding the city water supply. 28Call the rest of the army together. Then surround the city, and capture it yourself. If you don't, everyone will remember that I captured the city.
29David called the rest of the army together and attacked Rabbah. He captured the city 30and took the crown from the statue of their god Milcom. The crown was made of about 35 kilograms of gold, and there was a valuable jewel on it. David put the jewel on his own crown. He also carried off everything else of value. 31David made the people of Rabbah tear down the city walls with iron picks and axes, and then he put them to work making bricks. He did the same thing with all the other Ammonite cities.
David went back to Jerusalem, and the people of Israel returned to their homes.
translation_text:
Naatan wòon̄ Daafiidi u-kpitii pu
1Unimbɔti nìn tú u-bɔnaatiliu Naatan Daafiidi cee. U bàn̄ ki ká-uee ní ki bí-u yii: «Binib bili nìn bí kitiŋ kiban, ubɔ nìn sá ugaaja ní un kíǹee sá usoodaan. 2Ugaajee nìn cáá ipii nì iŋoobu nì inaa tikpil. 3Usoodaanee úǹ kaa nìn pée cáá báà tiba, asee kipisalii kiba ní u nìn dá. U nìn kpīintí-kì ní ki nì u-biyaamu wīintí mbaantiim. Tijin tin u nìn jīǹee nì nnyim min u nìn nyùee ní u tìì-kì. Kipisaliiyee nìn dɔ̀ ki kɔ́l̀-u, ní kì bí kii u-bisalee. 4Dalbee unicaan ubɔ kɔ́ ugaajee. Ama ugaajee kaa là kí cúú u-piii àá u-ŋoobui àá u-naai kansikin ubɔ kí ŋá u-nicaaŋwu tijin. Ama ní ki cúú usoodaan pisaliiki ki kūū ki ŋá u-nicaaŋwu tijin.»
5Ní Daafiidi fōō ugaajee pu diŋuul ŋkpitim pu, ní ki bí Naatan yii: «M pūtì ti-Dindaan un bí nee yii unil un ŋá mimmee máaǹ bí kpɔ̀-u. 6U nín ŋá pu kaa súń u-juti saayee, ú pà mpisalimu munaa kí téeǹ kipisaliiyee pu.» 7Ní Naatan bí Daafiidi yii: «Unil un ŋá mimmee, sii dee! Kpèè ti-Dindaan Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu nín lī puee sèé: <Man di lēē-si á nīn sá Isirayeel yab bɔtiu. Man di fīī-si ki nyántì Saayuul ŋaan. 8M dū a-kpiliu Saayuul dicaŋku ki tīī-si, ki dū u-nimpoobi ki ŋá a-ŋaan. M dū-si ki kāaǹ á jī dibeel Isirayeel yab nì Juuda yab pu. An yaa bàà pátì, m bàà ŋūǹ kí kūtì-si tin jítiǹ mimmee. 9Ba pu ní a kpēē man a-Dindaan fám ki ŋá min kaa fáatiǹ-mee? A kūū uyitiija Urii. A yāntì Amɔn yab kūū-u, ní sii fōō u-nimpuu ki cáá. 10An puee kí yòon̄ kɔŋkɔnnee kí nīn cée, nnikpaakoon pée kpá kí lóó a-dicaŋkun, di sá yii a kpēē-mi fám ki fōō uyitiija Urii nimpuu ki cáá. 11Man ni-Dindaan nín lī puee sɔ̀. M làá yàntī mbusu ń jēetí a-pu, ní mbusu gbantee làá nyānní sii a-ba dicaŋkun ní. A-nimbilaaliyin ní m làá fōō a-nimpoobi kí tīī a-yab ubɔ ní ú dòon̄ nì bi ŋwiimpu. 12Di sá yii sii ŋá dibalin ní, ama man làá nyāntí tin a ŋée Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nimbilaaliyin ŋwiimpu ní.»
13Ní Daafiidi bí Naatan yii: «M yīntiǹ ti-Dindaan.» Ní Naatan kíí Daafiidi yii: «Ti-Dindaan mun dū a-kpitii ki pú-si. Aa làá kpú. 14Ama tibɔti nee poonee, a kpēē ti-Dindaan fám. An puee kibininjabiki kin bi màl̄-si nee làá kpú.» 15Niinee ní Naatan nín kùǹ.
Batiseeba biki kúm
Ti-Dindaan yāntì iween iba dɔ́miń ki cúú Urii nimpuu Batiseeba biki kin u màl̄ Daafiidee. 16Daafiidi nìn mēē Unimbɔti kibiki gbanti pu. U nìn bōob̀ kinyɔkɔ, ní u yaa nìn kɔ́ u-diikunee, u dɔ̀ kitiŋ fám ní. 17U-kàliŋkpilib bin bí u-cindinee dɔ́miń u-cee ki gbāam̀-u ú yīkì kitiŋ ní u yíì, ní kaa là kí jī tijin bi-cee. 18An dāa tú kinyɔŋee, kibikee kpíì. Daafiidi tɔntɔnliibi nìn fàŋkí kí tùkù-u yii kibiki kpíì. Bi nìn bíi lì yii: «Ŋyunti ŋun kibikee dáá bée, ti nìn sòon̄ nì u waa pílifiǹ-ti. Kɔŋkɔnnee ti làá ŋá mana kí tùkù-u yii kì kpíì. U ŋūǹ kí ŋá u-ba tin kaa ŋān̄ee!» 19Daafiidi gbìl̄ bi nín bí ki mùkufī bi-ŋmaniŋmee, ní u béè yii kibikee kaa ti bí. Ní u bālifì-bi yii: «Kibikee kpíì níii?» Ní bi kíí-u yii: «Iiin, kì kpíì.» 20Niinee Daafiidi yíkì kitiŋ, ki cūtìi fùl̄ ki yāaǹ u-wunti pu talaalu ní ki kpántì tiwampeeŋkaal. Míǹ boonee ní u nín cá circir kɔŋkooŋŋun ki gbāaǹ ki jáam̀ ti-Dindaan.
U fātìi bāańee ní ki yāntì bi ŋá-u tijin u jíń. 21U-tɔntɔnliibi bālifì-u yii: «Ti-baa, tin a bíi ŋáań nee là kí lì yii ba dee? Di sá ŋyunti ŋun kibiki dáá bée, a nìn bōob̀ kinyɔkɔ ní ki sūǹ. Kɔŋkɔnnee kì nín kpíìyee ní a yíkìi kāl̀ ki bíi jīǹ tijin.» 22Ní Daafiidi kíí-bi yii: «Ŋyunti ŋun kibiki dáá bée, m nìn bōob̀ kinyɔkɔ ki sūǹ, di sá m nìn dàkafī yii an yaa yíì ti-Dindaan làá sɔ̄ m-saai kí cáaǹ-kì. 23Ama kɔŋkɔnnee kì kpíì, ba pu ní m nín gíti bōob̀ kinyɔkɔ? M ŋūǹ kí gíiǹní-kì dimaŋfalinaaa? Man di làá dāá cù ki-cee, kíǹ kaa ti ŋūǹ kí gítiń m-cee.»
Bi màl̄ Saloomɔn
24Daafiidi ŋméeǹ u-nimpuu Batiseeba. Boonee ní u nì u kpáfì ní u cáá dipool ki màl̄ kibininjabiki ní ki pú-kì diyindi yii Saloomɔn. Ti-Dindaan nìn néeń-kì. 25U nìn dī u-bɔnaatiliu Naatan pu ní ki tùkū Daafiidi míǹ. Ní Naatan pú-kì diyindi yii Yeediidiya, an taapu di sá yii: «Un ti-Dindaan néeńee.»
Daafiidi jáń ki fōō Raaba tiŋki
(1 Kroo 20.1-3)
26Ŋyunti gbantee ujanjakpil Joowaab nìn cūtìi jáń nì Amɔn yab tiŋki Raaba ki fōō laakin ubɔti kóòyee. 27Joowaab nìn tú binib bí tùkù Daafiidi yii: «M bíi jáà nì Raaba tiŋkin yab, ki fōō bi-tiŋki laakin bi bíl̀ nnyimee. 28An puee kpāfì bijanjaliibi bin kíǹee, sii a-ba ń dāan̄ kí já kí fōō-kì. Maa là kí já kí fōō-kì m-ba kí fōō diyindi.» 29Ní Daafiidi kpáfì bijanjaliibi bin kíǹee ní bi dɔ́miń ki jáń nì Raaba ki fōō-kì. 30Bi nìn cíkitì Amɔn yab bɔtiu beefuuliiki u-yil pu ki dūu cíkiǹ Daafiidi. Kibeefuuliiyee nyiŋfiŋu nìn sá kiiloobi mmuŋku nì saalaa nyɔkɔm, ní ataŋkpamɔnti náká ki-pu. Kí kūtèe, Daafiidi nìn jáń ki fōō tiwan tikpil, ní ki kóoǹ ki kpīnnì. 31Daafiidi nìn cúú kitiŋ gbanti nib kuyuŋu bi tūǹ atuun ŋin pɔ̄ɔ̄yee. Biba nìn sèekì ki kpítí ataŋkpee, ní biba gà isufi, ní biba mun māā brikisib. Míǹ ní u nìn ŋá Amɔn yab bin bí ntimu mun kɔkɔ kíǹee poon. U ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee ní u nì u-janjaliibi nín gítí Jeerusaleem.

english_text:
Amnon Disgraces Tamar
1David had a beautiful daughter named Tamar, who was the sister of Absalom. She was also the half sister of Amnon, who fell in love with her. 2But Tamar was a virgin, and Amnon could not think of a way to be alone with her. He was so upset about it that he made himself sick.
3Amnon had a friend named Jonadab, who was the son of David's brother Shimeah. Jonadab always knew how to get what he wanted, 4and he said to Amnon, “What's the matter? You're the king's son! You shouldn't have to go around feeling sorry for yourself every morning.”
Amnon said, “I'm in love with Tamar, my brother Absalom's sister.”
5Jonadab told him, “Lie down on your bed and pretend to be sick. When your father comes to see you, ask him to send Tamar, so you can watch her cook something for you. Then she can serve you the food.”
6So Amnon went to bed and pretended to be sick. When the king came to see him, Amnon said, “Please, ask Tamar to come over. She can make some special bread while I watch, and then she can serve it to me.”
7David told Tamar, “Go over to Amnon's house and fix him some food.” 8When she got there, he was lying in bed. She mixed the dough, made the loaves, and baked them while he watched. 9Then she took the bread out of the pan and put it on his plate, but he refused to eat it.
Amnon said, “Send the servants out of the house.” After they had gone, 10he said to Tamar, “Serve the food in my bedroom.”
Tamar picked up the bread that she had made and brought it into Amnon's bedroom. 11But as she was taking it over to him, he grabbed her and said, “Come to bed with me!”
12She answered, “No! Please don't force me! This sort of thing isn't done in Israel. It's disgusting! 13Think of me. I'll be disgraced forever! And think of yourself. Everyone in Israel will say you're nothing but trash! Just ask the king, and he will let you marry me.”
14But Amnon would not listen to what she said. He was stronger than she was, so he overpowered her and raped her. 15Then Amnon hated her even more than he had loved her before. So he told her, “Get up and get out!”
16She said, “Don't send me away! That would be worse than what you have already done.”
But Amnon would not listen. 17He called in his servant and said, “Throw this woman out and lock the door!”
18The servant made her leave, and he locked the door behind her.
The king's unmarried daughters used to wear long robes with sleeves. 19Tamar tore the robe she was wearing and put ashes on her head. Then she covered her face with her hands and cried loudly as she walked away.
Absalom Kills Amnon
20Tamar's brother Absalom said to her, “How could Amnon have done such a terrible thing to you! But since he's your brother, don't tell anyone what happened. Just try not to think about it.”
Tamar soon moved into Absalom's house, but she was always sad and lonely. 21When David heard what had happened to Tamar, he was very angry. But Amnon was his oldest son and also his favorite, and David would not do anything to make Amnon unhappy.
22Absalom treated Amnon as though nothing had happened, but he hated Amnon for what he had done to his sister Tamar.
23Two years later, Absalom's servants were cutting wool from his sheep in Baal-Hazor near the town of Ephraim, and Absalom invited all of the king's sons to be there. 24Then he went to David and said, “My servants are cutting the wool from my sheep. Please come and join us!”
25David answered, “No, my son, we won't go. It would be too expensive for you.” Absalom tried to get him to change his mind, but David did not want to go. He only said that he hoped they would have a good time.
26Absalom said, “If you won't go, at least let my brother Amnon come with us.”
David asked, “Why should he go with you?” 27But Absalom kept on insisting, and finally David let Amnon and all his other sons go with Absalom.
Absalom prepared a banquet fit for a king. 28But he told his servants, “Keep an eye on Amnon. When he gets a little drunk from the wine and is feeling relaxed, I'll give the signal. Then kill him! I've commanded you to do it, so don't be afraid. Be strong and brave.”
29Absalom's servants killed Amnon, just as Absalom had told them. The rest of the king's sons quickly rode away on their mules to escape from Absalom.
30While they were on their way to Jerusalem, someone told David, “Absalom has killed all of your sons! Not even one is left.” 31David got up, and in his sorrow he tore his clothes and lay down on the ground. His servants remained standing, but they tore their clothes too.
32Then David's nephew Jonadab said, “Your Majesty, not all of your sons were killed! Only Amnon is dead. On the day that Amnon raped Tamar, Absalom decided to kill him. 33Don't worry about the report that all your sons were killed. Only Amnon is dead, 34and Absalom has run away.”
One of the guards noticed a lot of people coming along the hillside on the road to Horonaim. He went and told the king, “I saw some men coming along Horonaim Road.”
35Jonadab said, “Your Majesty, look! Here come your sons now, just as I told you.”
36No sooner had he said it, than David's sons came in. They were weeping out loud, and David and all his officials cried just as loudly. 37-38 David was sad for a long time because Amnon was dead.
David Lets Absalom Come Home
Absalom had run away to Geshur, where he stayed for three years with King Talmai the son of Ammihud. 39David still felt so sad over the loss of Amnon that he wanted to take his army there and capture Absalom.
translation_text:
Aminɔn nì Taamaar bɔti
1Míǹ boonee tin jítèe sèé. Daafiidi jipɔɔn Abisaloom nìn cáá niisal ubɔ bi yíì-u Taamaar. U nìn cáá kunyaaŋŋu tikpil. Usapɔɔnee nìn kɔ́ Daafiidi jipɔɔn Aminɔn tikpil. 2Aminɔn niisal Taamaar nín nìn kɔ́-u puee nìn yāntì an dūu ŋá-u iween. U-niisalee nín kaa nìn nyí uninjee puee, an nìn pɔ̄ɔ̄ ú ŋmā kí sútí kí pìl̄-u. 3Aminɔn nìn cáá bɔɔ ubɔ bi yíì-u Yoonadaab. U nìn sá Daafiidi maan Simeeya jipɔɔn ní. Kijapaayee nìn wálifì tikpil. 4U nìn bālifì Aminɔn yii: «Sii sá ubɔti jipɔɔn ní, ba pu ní kutaafaau kamaa a pée kā kunandaŋu míǹ? Tiba yaa bí tùkù-maa!» Ní Aminɔn kíí-u yii: «An sá m-naal Abisaloom niisal Taamaar di kɔ́-mi tikpil.» 5Niinee ní Yoonadaab bí-u yii: «Dòon̄ a-dooŋu pu kí ŋá kii a būǹee. A-baa yaa dɔ́miń kí màntì a-puee ní á bí-u yii: <Yàntī m-niisal Taamaar ń dāan̄ kí ŋá-mi tijin. Ú nīn kā m-nimbiin ki ŋáań tijin m wāĺ-u. U yaa dóòyee, úǹ u-ba ń cáań kí tīī-mi ḿ jī.>»
6Niinee Aminɔn dōoǹ ki ŋá kii u būǹee. Ubɔti dɔ́miń kí màntì u-puee ní Aminɔn bí-u yii: «Yàntī m-niisal Taamaar ń dāan̄ kí kàl̄ m-nimbiin kí tɔ̄-mi kalaabi bili pu yéè kí tīī-mi ḿ ŋmɔ́.» 7Ní Daafiidi tú ubɔ Taamaar dumpu ú tùkù-u yii: «Cù a-niija Aminɔn cee kí ŋá-u tijin.» 8Ní Taamaar nín cá u-niija Aminɔn cee, ki bàn̄ ki ká-u u dɔ̄ ndoo pu. Ní u kāl̀ u-nimbiin niin ki búuń ŋyim ki tɔ́-u kalaabi. 9U wūutì kalaayee ní ki cáa yóoǹ u-nimbiin ú ŋmɔ́, ní u yíì. Ní Aminɔn bí yii: «Nyāntímaan binib kɔkɔ doo». Ní bin kɔkɔ nìn bí u-ceeyee nyáń. 10Ní u bí Taamaar yii: «Cáań-mi kalaabee m-diikun, kí lēē kí tīī-mi ḿ ŋmɔ́.»
Ní Taamaar yōoǹ kalaabi bin u tɔ́ee ki cáa kɔ́ǹ u-niija Aminɔn diikun. 11Ŋyunti ŋun u lēē kalaa ki tīī-u ú ŋmɔ́ee ní u cúú-u ki bí yii: «M-niisal, yàntī ḿ dòon̄ nì si.» 12Ní Taamaar fáá mbiil yii: «M-niija, taa bīil̀-mi. Baa ŋáań míǹ Isirayeel yab tiŋkin. A taa ŋá icoo bɔti gbanti. 13A yaa ŋá mimmee, la ní m làá cáá m-cooi gbanti kí báĺ? A làá kpántí kpayiliku Isirayeel tiŋkin. Míǹ puee, sòoǹ nì ubɔti, waa làá yíí yii á taa cáá-mi.» 14Aminɔn kaa pée là kí pīlifiǹ-u. U cúú-u mpɔn ní ki dōoǹ nì u.
15Míǹ boonee, Aminɔn nìn kíǹ ki ná Taamaar. Kináŋ kin u nìn kíǹ ki cáá u-puee nìn pɔ̄ɔ̄ ki jítiǹ dineendi din u nìn bí yii u néeń-uee. Ní Aminɔn bí-u yii: «Yīkìí nyā doo!» 16Ní Taamaar kíí-u yii: «A yaa jìn̄-mee kpitii làá nyàŋkiǹ in a dáá ŋá nee.» Ama ní Aminɔn kaa ti pée là kí pīlifiǹ-u. 17Ní u yíiń u-tɔntɔnliu ki bí yii: «Jà usapɔɔn nee kí nyāntí doo kí dū kudii kí pìin̄ kí kpàl̄.» 18Ní utɔntɔnlee jìn̄ Taamaar ki nyántì ki dū kudii ki pīiǹ ki kpàl̄.
Taamaar nìn pēē dibɔkutifɔkɔl dimɔntiil diba, di sá yii bɔtiisalib bin kaa nìn nyí uninjee nín nìn pèentí puee dee. 19Ní Taamaar dū ŋfantam ki pùkū u-yil, ki dáaĺ ki cátì dibɔkutimɔntiil din u pēēyee, ní ki dū u-ŋalii ki túǹ u-yil pu ki còom̄ ki cá ki gbáà ibiil. 20Ní u-niija Abisaloom bālifì-u yii: «A-niija Aminɔn bíil̀-si níii? Taa ti lì tiba, m-niisal, a-niija dee. Taa dūú páb́ a-ba.» Kí yòon̄ ŋyunti gbantee, Taamaar nìn kíǹ ki bí u-niija Abisaloom cee icoo poon. 21Ubɔti Daafiidi nìn gbìl̄ tin jítèe kɔkɔ ní ki fōō diŋuul ŋkpitim pu. Ama waa nìn wòon̄ Aminɔn, di sá yii úǹ di nìn sá u-jipɔŋkpiliu ní u nìn néeń-u tikpil. 22Ama Abisaloom kaa nìn gíti sòoǹ nì Aminɔn. U nìn kíǹ ki ná-u, kun puee u nìn bíil̀ u-niisal Taamaar.
Abisaloom yāntì bi kūū Aminɔn ní ki sáǹ
23Tíǹ jítì abin ali boonee, bi bíi cēē Abisaloom piii kuti Baal-Asɔɔr, Eefiraayiim tiŋki caŋin. Abisaloom nìn yíiń ubɔti jipɔmbi kɔkɔ bí jī bi nín bíi cēē u-piii kutee jiŋaaliu. 24Abisaloom cūtìi ká u-baa Daafiidi ki bí-u yii: «Ti-baa, bi bíi cēē man a-tɔntɔnliu piii kuti. M gbāam̀-si, si nì a-kàliŋkpilib ń céeǹ man a-tɔntɔnliu tí cùú jī jiŋaal gbanti.» 25Ní ubɔti kíí-u yii: «Aayee m-jipɔɔn, ti-kɔkɔ kaa máaǹ kí cù, án làá nīn sá-si digìŋ́kpaandi ní.» Ní Abisaloom pée gbíntìi cɔ́ yii bí cù, ní ubɔti yíì, ama ní ki mēē ki bīiǹ u-pu. 26Ní Abisaloom bí yii: «Mimmee sii yaa kaa làá cùee, pɔ̄ nsan m-maan Aminɔn ń céeǹ-ti.» Ní ubɔti kíí-u yii: «Ba pu ní ú céeǹ-si?» 27Ní Abisaloom gbíntìi cɔ́. Ubɔti dāa gīīyee ní ki yāntì Aminɔn nì u-jipɔmbi bin kíǹee cūtì.
Ní Abisaloom bɔ́ntì tijin mbɔtiyaamin. 28Abisaloom tīī u-tɔntɔnliibi mara nee yii: «Ní nīn cɔ́ŋkí Aminɔn. U yaa láa nyùn̄ ndaam ki bál̀ an nyāatì-u ní m yaa láa bí-ni yii: <Kpɔ̀maan Aminɔŋyee!> Ní kpɔ̀-u! Ní taa fàŋkì tiba, man di tīī-ni mara yii ní kpɔ̀-u. Kámaan dipɔbil kí dàkàmaan tininjati.» 29Ní Abisaloom tɔntɔnliibi kūū Aminɔn kii u nín bí yii bí ŋá puee. Niinee ubɔti jipɔmbi bin kíǹee yíkìi yōoǹ bi-mambooŋyi ki sáǹ ki kátì.
30Bi dáá bí nsanni ki sáń ki cá ní Daafiidi gbìl̄ yii: «Abisaloom kūū ubɔti jipɔmbi kɔkɔ pílpil báà ubɔ kaa kíǹ.» 31Niinee ubɔti cúú tiwan tin u pēēyee ki cátì ní ki dōoǹ kitiŋ. Ní u-kàliŋkpilib mun cátì bi-wanti tin bi pēēyee ki yú ki gɔ́ń-u. 32Niinee ní Daafiidi maan Simeeya jipɔɔn Yoonadaab bí yii: «Ti-baa ubɔti, a taa dàkafì yii bi kūū a-jipɔmbi kɔkɔ. Aminɔn baba ní bi kūū. Doooo ŋyunti ŋun Aminɔn bíil̀ u-niisalee ní Abisaloom nìn lī ki yóoǹ yii u làá kpɔ̀-u. 33An puee, á taa dàkafì yii bi kūū a-jipɔmbi kɔkɔ, Aminɔn baba ní bi kūū. 34Abisaloom úǹ sáǹ.»
Un nìn sí sintilee kpēē ndanee ki ká dinikitikpaandi diba tàkāń Ooroonayiim dandi ki kpàkaǹ dijool ki dòoń. 35Ní Yoonadaab bí ubɔti yii: «Ti-baa, kpèè a-jipɔmbi di dòońee! M nín bàà pée tùkū-si puee, míǹ ní ti wāĺ nee.» 36U sòon̄ kaa láá ŋmíl̀ ní ubɔti jipɔmbi dūu bāań. Bi nìn kíĺ nsiim, ní ubɔti nì u-kàliŋkpilib mun bíi sūǹ lɔ̀lɔlɔ.
37Abisaloom nín sáǹee, u nìn cūtìi kɔ́ Amiiyuur jipɔɔn Talimayi, Geesuur bɔtiu pu. Ŋyunti gbanti kɔkɔee, Daafiidi pée gbíntìi kā u-jipɔɔn kpool. 38Abisaloom un nìn sáǹ ki cūtìi bí Geesuur tiŋkinee nìn ŋá niin abin ata ní. 39Ubɔti Daafiidi nìn bíi súntí Aminɔn kúm pu fiii fiii, ní diŋuul din u nìn gíí Abisaloom puee mun sɔ̄ŋkì.

english_text:
1Joab knew that David couldn't stop thinking about Absalom, 2-3and he sent someone to bring in the wise woman who lived in Tekoa. Joab told her, “Put on funeral clothes and don't use any makeup. Go to the king and pretend you have spent a long time mourning the death of a loved one.” Then he told her what to say.
4The woman from Tekoa went to David. She bowed very low and said, “Your Majesty, please help me!”
5David asked, “What's the matter?”
She replied:
My husband is dead, and I'm a widow. 6I had two sons, but they got into a fight out in a field where there was no one to pull them apart, and one of them killed the other. 7Now all of my relatives have come to me and said, “Hand over your son! We're going to put him to death for killing his brother.” But what they really want is to get rid of him, so they can take over our land.
Please don't let them put out my only flame of hope! There won't be anyone left on this earth to carry on my husband's name.
8“Go on home,” David told her. “I'll take care of this matter for you.”
9The woman said, “I hope your decision doesn't cause any problems for you. But if it does, you can blame me.”
