2Kudii kun ní ubɔti Saloomɔn nìn máń ki tīī ti-Dindaanee nìn fɔ̀kɔ̀ mpúun pu meetab mmuŋku nì saalaa, ní ku-waaŋŋu nìn sá meetab saalaa, ní ku-fɔkɔŋŋu sá meetab saalku. 3Kunimbɔtidii dikpaaŋku nyɔkɔpuee, kudii kubɔ nìn bí bi tà kí kɔ́, ku-waaŋŋu nìn sá meetab saalaa kii kunimbɔtidii ku-ba waaŋŋuee, ní ku-púuŋŋu sá meetab biŋmoo. 4U nìn lēē tɔkɔlab kunimbɔtidii guŋŋi pu. Tɔkɔlabee nìn cáá tifukuŋkaal nì nlaamu. 5U nìn máń adiin ata ki tɔ́kɔǹ tɔb pu ki nákáǹ kudikpaaŋŋu gundi boon yal pu nì kudii kun bí poon púee ki kútì. 6Aditɔntɔkɔ gbanti kun bí taapuee waaŋŋu nìn sá meetab bili nì dijandi, ní kun bí kansikinee waaŋŋu sá meetab bita, ní kun tɔ́kɔ́ yilpuee waaŋŋu sá meetab bita nì dijandi. Di sá yii kunimbɔtidii boon pú gundi gbifiŋŋu kaa nìn sá mbaanti ki tin kátì yilpu. An puee bi nín nìn bɔ̀b̄ aditɔntɔkɔ yilpu puee kaa nìn kɔ́ kunimbɔtidii guŋŋi poon. 7Bi nìn lēē laaba ní ki kpítíi ŋáŋkí ataŋkpee. Ataŋkpee ŋin bi nìn kpítíi ŋáŋkée ní bi nìn dūu máń kunimbɔtidii. An puee bi nín nìn bíi māāyee, baa nìn gbìl̀ aama puɔɔɔ, kicɔkɔ puɔɔɔ, tikúti tɔntɔŋwanti tiba pu. 8Adiin ŋin bi nìn máń ki tɔ́kɔǹ tɔb puee, kansikin yɔkɔee punyɔkɔki nìn bí kunimbɔtidii ŋgiil pú ní. Akɔl pu ní bi nìn dìŋfī kí kɔ́ ku-poon nì yilpu diiku poon. 9Saloomɔn nín nìn máń Unimbɔti diiku ki dóòyee, u nìn dū seedir dɔi ní ki bɔ̀b̄ yilpu. 10Aditɔntɔkɔ ŋin u nìn máń ki tú kunimbɔtidii kɔkɔee, kudii kamaa fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá meetab bili nì dijandi, ní bi dū seedir dɔjaliŋ ki páaǹ yilpu ní an dāa tɔ́kɔǹ kunimbɔtidii gundi pu.
11Ní ti-Dindaan bí Saloomɔn yii: 12«A bíi māā kudii nee kí tīī-mi ní nee. Ama a yaa nóó m-bɔkpaaŋi, ki ŋúb́ m-koobiliŋ ŋin m tīī-see, ní ki yaa ŋáań m-marab nín bí yii á ŋá puee, m làá ŋá m nín nìn pōoǹ a-baa Daafiidi a-pu puee kí tīī-si. 13M làá dāan̄ kí nīn kóò Isirayeel yab kansikin kudii nee poon. M kpá kí dū m-nibul Isirayeel yab kí fá jaanjaan.»
Bi nín nyɔ̄kɔntì kunimbɔtidii poon puee
14Saloomɔn nín nìn máń kunimbɔtidii ki dóòyee, 15u nìn látì seedir dɔpampaŋŋi ki nákáǹ ku-poon ki yōoǹ ku-taapu ki cáa sāā yilpu, ní ki dū siipreesi dɔi in bi látèe ki bíl̀ ku-taapu. 16Bi nìn tí dū seedir dɔi in bi látì apampanee ki nákáǹ poon diiku guŋŋi ki yōoǹ taapu ki cáá sāā yilpu. Kudii gbanti fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá meetab saalaa ní. Bi nìn bɔ́ntì-ku ki dū-ku ki ŋá kunimbɔtidii pɔ̀ti pu, circir páaa laŋki. 17Kudikpaaŋŋu kun nìn bí Circir páaa laŋki nyɔkɔpuee púuŋŋu nìn sá meetab mmuŋku ní. 18Bi nìn lēē koolookinti subiliŋ nì nsupumpukum min mātèe ki nákáǹ seedir dɔpampaŋŋi ŋin bi nìn dūu nákáǹ kunimbɔtidii guŋŋi puee. Seedir dɔi ní bi nìn dūu bīiǹ tikɔkɔ pu, an puee baa nìn wāĺ báà ditaŋkpal. 19Bi nìn bɔ́ntì kudikpaaŋŋu poon circir diiku kubɔ ní ki dū ti-Dindaan poondi dakaau ki síiǹ. 20Kudii gbanti púuŋŋu nìn sá meetab saalaa, ní ku-waaŋŋu sá meetab saalaa, ní ku-fɔkɔŋŋu sá meetab saalaa. Sindaariyamɔnti ní bi nìn dūu nyūntì-kù. Kudiiyee poonee, nsaraafan nìn bí ní bi dū seedir dɔi ki nákáǹ-ŋu ki māntìi tú. 21Bi nìn dū sindaariyamɔnti ki nyūntì kunimbɔtidii poon kɔkɔ. Bi nìn dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ ikusaka yam ki dūu sākaǹ circir diiku gbanti punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu, ní ki fātìi dū sindaariya ki nyūntì. 22Bi nìn dū sindaariyamɔnti ní ki nyūntì kunimbɔtidii kɔkɔ, ki kpáaǹ nsaraafan ŋun nìn yú circir páaa laŋki punyɔkɔki caŋinee.
23Bi nìn dū ɔliifi dɔŋu ki kpítì keerubimbi bili ki síiǹ Circir páaa laŋki diikun, keerubim kamaa fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá meetab biŋmoo ní. 24Keerubimpeekaa feeŋŋu ŋubɔ nìn sá meetab bili nì dijandi ní ŋun kíǹee mun meetab bili nì dijandi. Mimmee ifeen liitil waaŋŋu nìn sá meetab biŋmoo ní. 25Keerubim liliitee mun waaŋŋu nìn sá meetab biŋmoo kii upeekaayee, bi nìn ŋmà ní. 26Keerubimpeekaayee fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá meetab biŋmoo, míǹ mbaantiim ní uliliitee mun fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá. 27Bi nìn dū keerubimbi gbanti ki síiǹ Circir páaa laŋki poon ní. Bi nìn kpátì bi-feeŋyi, upeekaayee feeŋŋu ŋubɔ nìn tùutī digundi ní uliliitee feeŋŋu ŋubɔ tùutī digundi din kíǹee, ní bi-feeŋyi in kíǹee tùutī tɔb. 28Bi nìn dū sindaariya ní ki nyūntì keerubimbi liitil.
29Bi nìn kpítì keerubimbi nì ibafi nì nsupumpukum min mātèe ki nákáǹ kunimbɔtidii guŋŋi poon nì boon ki māntìi tú. 30Bi nìn dū sindaariya ní ki ŋàl̄ adiin liitil poon.
31Bi nìn dū ɔliifi dɔŋu ki kpáá kipunyɔkɔ kin cáá punuubi bilee ki pīiǹ Circir páaa laŋki diiku. Bi yaa nìn yākatì punuu waaŋŋu miŋmoo puee, punuu yilpu dɔŋu nì idɔ ili in pu punuu cɔ́ee nìn fòol̄ diba pu ní. 32Bi nìn kpítì punuubi bilee pu keerubimbi nì ibafi nì nsupumpukum min mātèe, ní ki dū sindaariya ki nyūntì. Bi nìn dū sindaariya ki nyūntì keerubimbi nì ibafee mun. 33Bi nìn kpáá punuu ubɔ mun ki pīiǹ kunimbɔtidii dikpaaŋku. Ama niinee, bi yaa nìn yākatì punuu gbanti waaŋŋu minaa puee, diba pu sá punuu yilpu dɔŋu nì idɔ ili in pu punuu cɔ́ee ní. 34U nìn gíti dū siipreesi dɔŋu ki kpáá punuubi bili, ní ki kpítì abɔmbil ali ki nyɔ̄kɔntì punuubi liitilee. 35Bi nìn gíti kpítì punuubee pu keerubimbi nì ibafi nì nsupumpukum min mātèe ki nyɔ̄kɔntì, ní ki dū sindaariya ki nyūntì laakin bi kpítèe.
36Míǹ boonee ní u máń poon cindi. Bi nín nìn máń dicindi gundi puee sɔ̀. Bi nìn máń ataŋkpee ikuul ita nì seedir dɔi ŋkuul ŋubɔ.
37Saloomɔn nín kāl̀ dibeelee, dibinnanaatiil ŋmaliliitiu poon, an dàkà yii uŋmal un bi yíì Siifee poon ní bi bíl̀ ti-Dindaan diiku nyeel. 38Saloomɔn nín kāl̀ dibeelee abin saalaa nì diba ŋmaniniitiu poon, an dàkà yii uŋmal un bi yíì yii Buulee poon ní bi dóò kunimbɔtidii tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ pái. Saloomɔn nìn dū abin aluli ní ki máń-ku.

english_text:
Solomon's Palace Is Built
1Solomon's palace took 13 years to build.
2-3Forest Hall was the largest room in the palace. It was 44 meters long, 22 meters wide, and 13.5 meters high, and was lined with cedar from Lebanon. It had 4 rows of cedar pillars, 15 in a row, and they held up 45 cedar beams. The ceiling was covered with cedar. 4Three rows of windows on each side faced each other, 5and there were three doors on each side near the front of the hall.
6Pillar Hall was 22 meters long and 13.5 meters wide. A covered porch supported by pillars went all the way across the front of the hall.
7Solomon's throne was in Justice Hall, where he judged cases. This hall was completely lined with cedar.
8 The section of the palace where Solomon lived was behind Justice Hall and looked exactly like it. He had a similar place built for his wife, the daughter of the king of Egypt.
9From the foundation all the way to the top, these buildings and the courtyard were made out of the best stones carefully cut to size, then smoothed on every side with saws. 10The foundation stones were huge, good stones—some of them four and a half meters long and others three and a half meters long. 11The cedar beams and other stones that had been cut to size were on top of these foundation stones. 12The walls around the palace courtyard were made out of three layers of cut stones with one layer of cedar beams, just like the front porch and the inner courtyard of the temple.
Hiram Makes the Bronze Furnishings
(2 Chronicles 3.15-17; 4.1-10)
13-14Hiram was a skilled bronze worker from the city of Tyre. His father was now dead, but he also had been a bronze worker from Tyre, and his mother was from the tribe of Naphtali.
King Solomon asked Hiram to come to Jerusalem and make the bronze furnishings to use for worship in the Lord's temple, and he agreed to do it.
15Hiram made two bronze columns eight meters tall and almost two meters across. 16For the top of each column, he also made a bronze cap just over two meters high. 17The caps were decorated with seven rows of designs that looked like chains, 18with two rows of designs that looked like pomegranates.
19The caps for the columns of the porch were almost two meters high and were shaped like lilies.
20The chain designs on the caps were right above the rounded tops of the two columns, and there were 200 pomegranates in rows around each cap. 21Hiram placed the two columns on each side of the main door of the temple. The column on the south side was called Jachin, and the one on the north was called Boaz.
22The lily-shaped caps were on top of the columns.
This completed the work on the columns.
23Hiram also made a large bowl called the Sea. It was just over two meters deep, about 4.5 meters across, and 13.5 meters around. 24Two rows of bronze gourds were around the outer edge of the bowl, ten gourds to every 45 centimeters. 25The bowl itself sat on top of twelve bronze bulls with three bulls facing outward in each of four directions. 26The sides of the bowl were 75 millimeters thick, and its rim was like a cup that curved outward like flower petals. The bowl held about 40,000 liters.
27Hiram made ten movable bronze stands, each one over a meter high, almost two meters long, and almost two meters wide. 28-29The sides were made with panels attached to frames decorated with flower designs. The panels themselves were decorated with figures of lions, bulls, and winged creatures. 30-31Each stand had four bronze wheels and axles and a round frame 68 centimeters across, held up by four supports 45 centimeters high. A small bowl rested in the frame. The supports were decorated with flower designs, and the frame with carvings.
The side panels of the stands were square, 32and the wheels and axles were underneath them. The wheels were about 68 centimeters high 33and looked like chariot wheels. The axles, rims, spokes, and hubs were made out of bronze.
34-35Around the top of each stand was a 22-centimeter strip, and there were four braces attached to the corners of each stand. The panels and the supports were attached to the stands, 36and the stands were decorated with flower designs and figures of lions, palm trees, and winged creatures. 37Hiram made the ten bronze stands from the same mold, so they were exactly the same size and shape.
38 Hiram also made ten small bronze bowls, one for each stand. The bowls were almost two meters across and could hold about 800 liters.
39He put five stands on the south side of the temple, five stands on the north side, and the large bowl at the southeast corner of the temple.
40Hiram made pans for hot ashes, and also shovels and sprinkling bowls.
A List of Everything inside the Temple
(2 Chronicles 4.11—5.1)
This is a list of the bronze items that Hiram made for the Lord's temple: 41two columns; two bowl-shaped caps for the tops of the columns; two chain designs on the caps; 42400 pomegranates for the chain designs; 43ten movable stands; ten small bowls for the stands; 44a large bowl; twelve bulls that held up the bowl; 45pans for hot ashes, and also shovels and sprinkling bowls.
Hiram made these bronze things for Solomon 46near the Jordan River between Succoth and Zarethan by pouring melted bronze into clay molds.
47There were so many bronze things that Solomon never bothered to weigh them, and no one ever knew how much bronze was used.
48 Solomon gave orders to make the following temple furnishings out of gold: the altar; the table that held the sacred loaves of bread; 49 ten lampstands that went in front of the most holy place; flower designs; lamps and tongs; 50cups, lamp snuffers, and small sprinkling bowls; dishes for incense; fire pans; and the hinges for the doors to the most holy place and the main room of the temple.
51 After the Lord's temple was finished, Solomon put into its storage rooms everything that his father David had dedicated to the Lord, including the gold and the silver.
translation_text:
Ubɔti naakooku mātam
1Saloomɔn nìn máń úǹ u-ba diiku. U nìn dū abin saalaa nì ata ní ki máń-ku ki dóò. 2U nìn máń kudii kun bi yíì yii <Leebanɔn Bambaŋkuee>. Kudii gbanti púuŋŋu nìn sá meetab imuŋku ili nì saalaa, ní ku-waaŋŋu sá meetab mmuŋku nì biŋmoo, ní ku-fɔkɔŋŋu sá meetab saalku. Bi nìn dū seedir dɔi ki ŋá jaantalkub ki cóoǹ ikuul inaa pu, ní ki dū seedir dɔi ki páaǹ jaantalkubee pu. 3Bi nìn látì seedir dɔi apampan ki bɔ̀b̄ idɔlalikaa in pá jaantalkub puee pu. Idɔlalikaa gbanti nìn bí imuŋku ili nì iŋmoo ní, di sá yii ikuul nìn sá ita ní ŋkuul kamaa pu cáá idɔlalikaa saalku. 4Bi nìn lēē kudiiyee pu tɔkɔlab bin cáá tifukuŋkaalee ikuul ita ní tɔkɔlabee túĺ tɔb. 5Mpunyɔmu kɔkɔ nì idɔ in pu punuubi cɔ́ee nìn cáá ajan anaa, ki túĺ tɔb ní ki bí ikuul ita pu.
6U nìn gíti máń kudii kubɔ bi yíì-ku yii <Jaantalkub Diiku>. Ku-púuŋŋu nìn sá meetab mmuŋku nì saalaa, ní ku-waaŋŋu sá meetab saalku. Ku nìn sá kii kunaakoou yamee, ní ki cáá jaantalkub nì idɔ in bi dūu kpákám̀ kipunyɔkɔpuee. Kudii gbanti nìn bí kun bi yíì <Leebanɔn Bambaŋkuee> nimbiin ní.
7U nìn máń <Dibeejal diiku>, bi gíti yíì-ku yii <Ibɔsoon Diiku>, di sá yii niin ní Saloomɔn nìn sòoǹ tibɔti. U nìn dū seedir dɔpampaŋŋi ki nákáǹ kudiiyee guŋŋi pu kí yòon̄ taapu kí cáá sāā yilpu.
8Kudii kun poon Saloomɔn nìn kóòyee nìn bí dicindi diba mun poon ní. Ku nìn bí <Kubɔsoondii> boon pú ní, ama bi nín máń-ŋi puee sá mbaantiim ní.
Saloomɔn nìn gíti máń kudii kubɔ kii úǹ u-ba yɔkɔee ki tīī u-nimpuu, Faaroo bisal.
9Bi nìn dū ataŋkpee ŋin pɔ̄ɔ̄ kudaauee ní ki máń adiin gbanti kɔkɔ. Bi nìn ŋmàntī ataŋkpee gbanti ní kí gùutī, ní kí dū kijiseekikaai kí sèekī boon pú nì poon pú. Ataŋkpee gbanti ní bi nìn dūu máń adiin ki yōoǹ ŋi-nyeel ki tin látì-ŋi, ki kpáaǹ diciŋkpaandi guŋŋi. 10Ataŋkpamɔnti ŋin sá akpaan ŋi-fɔkɔŋŋu sá meetab binaa kii biŋmooyee ní bi nìn dūu bíl̀ adiin nyeel. 11Ataŋkpakpaan gbanti pu ní bi nìn cáá ataŋkpee ŋin bi ŋmāntì ki kpítèe nì seedir dɔyee ki pāantí ki māā. 12Bi nìn máń digundi ní ki māntìi tú diciŋkpaandi. Bi nìn dū ataŋkpee ŋin bi kpítèe ní ki máń ikuul ita ní ki nìn dū seedir dɔjaliŋ ki páaǹ. Míǹ ní bi nìn tí máń kunimbɔtidii cindi nì kudii kun bi tà kí nín kɔ́ kunimbɔtidiinee.
Ditundi din bi nìn tīī Yiiramee
(Kpèè 2 Kroo 2.12-13)
13Ubɔti Saloomɔn nìn tú bi yíiń utiirja Yiiram. 14U-na nìn sá Neefitalii naakookun ní ki sá ukpiipu ní u-baa sá utiirja. U nìn tūǹ tasa tundi ní. U nìn yáb̀, ki cáá iciin, ki nyí tasa tundi tiŋan. U nìn kíí ki dɔ́miń ubɔti Saloomɔn cee ki túń u-tuuŋŋi ŋin di sá tasa kúti tuuŋŋee kɔkɔ.
Tasa jaantalkub
(Kpèè 2 Kroo 3.15-17)
15U nìn dū tasa ki mɔ́ɔ́ jaantalkub bili. Bi-fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá meetab biwa ní kí màntīí tūee sá meetab biluu. 16U nìn dūntì tasa ki mɔ́ɔ́ akɔl ali yam ki páaǹ jaantalkubee pu. Akɔlee fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá meetab bili nì dijandi. 17U nìn gíti ŋá tinyɔkɔntikaal tilaandi nì ikusaka yam ki lúntì akɔl ŋin pá jaantalkubee pu. Dikɔl kamaa nìn cáá tinyɔkɔntikaal gbanti tiluli tiluli ní. 18U nìn tí lēē greenaadi subiliŋ ki nyɔ̄kɔntì. U nìn ŋá ikuul ili ní ki dūu lúntì tilaandi tin bīī akɔl puee pu. 19U nìn gíti mɔ́ɔ́ tin bí kii akɔlee tiba mun ki páaǹ jaantalkubee pu. Tì nìn bí kii nsupumpukumee ní ti-fɔkɔŋŋu sá meetab bili. 20Akɔlee yilpuee, bi nìn lēē laaba ki ŋá an gbìfì. Laakin nìn gbìfì gbantee nìn bí kilàaŋ́ŋi nì greenaadi biliŋ alaataa ali ŋin bi nìn dūu páaǹ mpɔ̀n pu ki māntìi tú dikɔl kamaa puee yilpu ní. 21Bi nìn dū jaantalkubee liitil ki cóoǹ kudii kun bi tà kí kɔ́ kunimbɔtidiinee nyɔkɔpu ní. Bi nìn yíì un bi cóoǹ ŋgan púee yii Yakiin, taapu di sá yii <Unimbɔti tìì mpɔn>, ní ki yíì un bi cóoǹ ŋgiil púee yii Boowaasi, taapu di sá yii <Unimbɔtin ní m-pɔŋŋu bí>. 22Bi nìn ŋá jaantalkubee yilpu kii nsupumpukumee ní. Míǹ ní Yiiram nìn mɔ́ɔ́ jaantalkubee ki dóò.
Bi dū tasa ki mɔ́ɔ́ kusɔŋkpaaŋŋu
(Kpèè 2 Kroo 4.2-5)
23Yiiram nìn dū tasa ki mɔ́ɔ́ kusɔŋkpaaŋŋu. Ku-waaŋŋu nìn sá meetab biŋmoo, ní ku-fɔkɔŋŋu sá meetab bili nì dijandi, ní kí màntīí tū-kùee sá meetab saalku. 24Bi nìn dū tasa kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́ koolookinti subiliŋ ki māntìi tú kusɔŋuee nyɔɔgbandi. Meeta kamaa fɔkɔŋŋuee, asubilee mmuŋku di nìn bí, ní bi ŋá ikuul ili. Ŋyunti ŋun bi dūntì tasa ki mɔ́ɔ́ kusɔŋuee ní bi dūntì ki ŋá asubil gbanti mun. 25Bi nìn dūntì tasa ní ki dūu mɔ́ɔ́ inajaa saalaa nì ili: ita nìn kpèé ŋgan pú ní ita kpèé ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú ní ita kpèé ŋgiil pú ní ita mun kpèé ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú, ní bi dū kusɔŋuee ki tɔ́kɔǹ i-pu. 26Kusɔŋuee gbifiŋŋu nìn sá santimeetab binii. Bi nìn ŋáŋkì ku-nyɔɔgbandi kii kɔŋkɔnnyɔkaa nyɔɔgbaŋŋee, ní an gíti bí kii nsupumpukumee. Nnyim liitirib kutukub imuŋku inaa di nìn kàal̀ poon.
Tasa tɔrɔkub
27Yiiram nìn gíti dū tasa ki mɔ́ɔ́ tɔrɔkub saalaa. Tɔrɔku kamaa waaŋŋu nìn sá meetab bili ní ku-púuŋŋu sá meetab bili, ní ku-fɔkɔŋŋu sá meeta ubɔ nì dijandi. 28Bi nín nìn mɔ́ɔ̀-bi puee sèé: bi nìn gbáń tasa kúti an ŋá apampan ki dūu fúuń tifuuŋkaal poon. 29Bi nìn lēē tasa kúti apampanee pu gbikintib nì inajaa nì keerubimbi. Bi nìn dū tasa kútee ki mɔ́ɔ́ tinyɔkɔntikaal tin bí kii ikusaka yamee ki lúntì gbikintib nì inajaayee taapu. 30Bi nìn dū tasa ki mɔ́ɔ́ tɔrɔkubee taaŋi anaa ní ki mɔ́ɔ́ tasa kujaliŋ ki dū ataayee ki báaǹ. Akpinnaatilee puee, bi nìn dū akújalee ki báaǹ tiba pu tì náań nì ataa. Tin náań nì ataa gbantee, bi nìn dūntì tasa kúti ní ki mɔ́ɔ́-tì ŋyunti ŋun bi nìn dūntì ki mɔ́ɔ́ tifuuŋkaalee. Ama an kaa nìn jítiǹ tinyɔkɔntikaal tin bí kii ikusaka yamee pu. 31Bi nìn lēē kipunyɔkɔ dikuŋkundi tɔrɔku kamaa yilpu, kii santimeetab imuŋku ili nì saalaa. Kipunyɔkɔ gbanti di nìn tíkí kusɔŋuee. Ki-waaŋŋu nìn sá santimeetab biŋmoo kpá imuŋku inaa ní. Ki-jandi din nìn lībitì tifuuŋkaal puee jannaatiliŋ nìn ŋmà ní, dàa nìn bí dikuŋkundi. Bi nìn kpítì tiwan ki nyɔ̄kɔntì tasa kúti tin bi gbáń an ŋá apampanee. 32Tifuuŋkaalee nyɔɔgbandi pu ní ataa anaayee nìn bá ní akújal ŋin pu ataayee bée pūntì tɔrɔku taapu. Kí màntīí tū ditaalee nìn sá santimeetab biŋmoo kpá imuŋku inaa ní. 33Bi nìn mɔ́ɔ́ ataa gbanti kii janjatɔrɔkub taaŋee ní. Bi nìn dūntì tasa kúti ní ki dūu mɔ́ɔ́ ataa gbanti nì di-wanti kɔkɔ. 34Tiwan tinaa tin náań nì ataa ki bí tɔrɔkub kpiŋŋee nì tifuuŋkaalee nìn dūu ŋá tiwambaantiil ní. 35Tɔrɔku kamaa yilpuee, bi nìn lēē kipunyɔkɔ dikuŋkundi ŋwaan sá santimeetab mmuŋku nì biŋmoo. Bi nìn lēē aŋaŋkul an pu nì tasa kúti tin bi gbáń apampanee ní an ŋá ubaanti nì tɔrɔku jaŋŋi ŋin kɔkɔ kíǹee. 36Yiiram nìn gíti mɔ́ɔ́ ajan ŋin kaa nìn cáá aŋaŋkulee nì tasa kúti apampanee pu keerubimbi nì gbikintib nì tikpakpati. U nìn gíti mɔ́ɔ́ ikusaka iba mun ki nyɔ̄kɔntì. 37Míǹ ní bi nìn mɔ́ɔ́ tɔrɔkub saalaayee kɔkɔ: tiwambaantiil ní bi nìn dūu mɔ́ɔ́ bi-kɔkɔ, ní bi-fɔkɔŋŋu ŋmà ki náań.
38Yiiram nìn gíti dū tasa kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́ tisɔn saalaa ki tɔ́kɔǹ tɔrɔkub saalaayee pu. Kusɔŋu kamaa fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá meetab bili ní. Nnyim liitirib kutuku ubɔ nì alaataa aluu di nìn kàal̀ kusɔŋu kamaa poon. 39U nìn dū tɔrɔkubee biŋmoo nì bi-sɔnti ki síiǹ kunimbɔtidii ŋgiil pú ní ki dū biŋmoo bin kíǹee nì bi-sɔnti ki síiǹ ŋgan pú. U nìn dū kusɔŋkpaaŋŋu dikuŋkundee ki síiǹ kunimbɔtidii ŋgiil pú, ŋfaŋfakam min bí ŋgiil pú nì ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee.
Tiwan tin kɔkɔ bi nìn mɔ́ɔ́yee nyɔkɔm
(Kpèè 2 Kroo 4.7–5.1)
40Yiiram nìn gíti mɔ́ɔ́ nsampeemu nì peelab nì asambil ŋin poon bi ŋáań fatiku ki cáa yàantée.
U nìn túń ti-Dindaan Diiku tuuŋŋi ŋin ubɔti Saloomɔn nìn tīī-u ú tɔ̄ee ki dóò:
41Jaantalkub bili,
akɔl akuŋkun ŋin bi làá dūú páań jaantalkubee yilpuee,
tilaandi tili tin bi làá dūú bìin̄ akɔl ŋin pá jaantalkubee puee,
42nì greenaadi subiliŋ alaataa anaa ŋin bi làá dūú lúntí tilaandee puee, an dàkà yii kulaaŋŋu kamaa puee bi nìn lúntì greenaadi subiliŋ gbanti ikuul ili pu ní ki bīiǹ jaantalkub kɔliŋee pu,
43nì tɔrɔkub saalaa,
nì tisɔn saalaa tin tɔ́kɔ́ tɔrɔkub gbanti puee,
44nì kusɔŋkpaaŋŋu dikuŋkundee,
nì inajaa saalaa nì ili in tú kusɔŋu gbantee,
45nì asambil nì peelab nì asambil ŋin poon bi ŋáań fatiku ki cáa yàantée.
Tasa kúmɔntiiti ní Yiiram nìn dūu mɔ́ɔ́ tiwan gbanti kɔkɔ ki tīī ubɔti Saloomɔn ú dūú síiń ti-Dindaan Diikun. 46Jɔɔdan tantakalin, Sukooti nì Saartan kansikin ní ubɔti yāntì bi dūntì tasa kúti kuyɔkɔu paamun ki mɔ́ɔ́ tiwan gbanti kɔkɔ. 47Míǹ boonee ní Saloomɔn yāntì bi dū tiwan gbanti kɔkɔ ki síiǹ ti-Dindaan Diikun. Ama tiwanee nín nìn wīikí puee, baa nìn gíti ŋūǹ gba kí ŋmàntī kí béé tasa kúti tin bi nìn dūu ŋá an wantee nyiŋfiŋu.
48Saloomɔn nìn gíti yāntì bi dū sindaariya ki ŋá ti-Dindaan Diiku wanti tin an bàlifēe:
bi nìn dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ nsaraafan ŋun pu bi tùutī talaalubee,
ki dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ teebil un pu bi pāantí kpɔnɔb kí dūú sú ti-Dindaanee,
49ní ki dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ fitilab tɔ́kɔŋkaati saalaa ki síiǹ circir páaa laŋki nyɔkɔpu, tiŋmoo nìn bí ŋgiil pú ní tiŋmoo mun bí ŋgan pú,
ní ki dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ nsupumpukum nì fitilab nì tibabiti,
50ní ki dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ nsampeemu nì bɔlfitantab nì asambil ŋin poon bi ŋáań fatiku ki cáa yàantée nì asambil nì nfantansamu,
ní ki dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ circir páaa laŋki nì kudikpaaŋŋu punuubi nín sàkā tin puee.
51Míǹ ní ubɔti Saloomɔn nìn túń kunimbɔtidii tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ ki dóò. Míǹ boonee ní u yāntì bi cáań tiwan tin kɔkɔ u-baa Daafiidi nìn dūu sú ti-Dindaanee, an dàkà yii animbil nì sindaariya nì tiwan tikpil. Bi nìn dūu síiǹ ti-Dindaan Diiku nimbikpaafidiikun.

english_text:
Solomon Brings the Sacred Chest to the Temple
(2 Chronicles 5.2—6.2)
1-2 The sacred chest had been kept on Mount Zion, also known as the city of David. But Solomon decided to have the chest moved to the temple while everyone was in Jerusalem, celebrating the Festival of Shelters during Ethanim, the seventh month of the year.
Solomon called together the important leaders of Israel. 3-4Then the priests and the Levites carried to the temple the sacred chest, the sacred tent, and the objects used for worship. 5Solomon and a crowd of people stood in front of the chest and sacrificed more sheep and cattle than could be counted.
6The priests carried the chest into the most holy place and put it under the winged creatures, 7whose wings covered both the chest and the poles used for carrying it. 8The poles were so long that they could be seen from right outside the most holy place, but not from anywhere else. And they stayed there from then on.
9 The only things kept in the chest were the two flat stones Moses had put there when the Lord made his agreement with the people of Israel at Mount Sinai, after bringing them out of Egypt.
10 Suddenly a cloud filled the temple as the priests were leaving the most holy place. 11The Lord's glory was in the cloud, and the light from it was so bright that the priests could not stay inside to do their work. 12 Then Solomon prayed:
“Our Lord, you said that you
would live in a dark cloud.
13Now I have built a glorious temple
where you can live forever.”
Solomon Speaks to the People
(2 Chronicles 6.3-11)
14Solomon turned toward the people standing there. Then he blessed them 15-16 and said:
Praise the Lord God of Israel! Long ago he brought his people out of Egypt. He did not choose a city from any tribe in Israel where his temple would be built, but he kept his promise to make my father David the king of Israel.
17 So when David wanted to build a temple for the Lord God of Israel, 18the Lord said, “It's good that you want to build a temple where I can be worshiped. 19 But you're not the one to do it. Your son will build a temple to honor me.”
20The Lord has done what he promised. I am the king of Israel like my father, and I've built a temple for the Lord our God. 21I've also made a place in the temple for the sacred chest. And in that chest are the two flat stones on which is written the solemn agreement the Lord made with our ancestors when he led them out of Egypt.
Solomon Prays at the Temple
(2 Chronicles 6.12-42)
22Solomon stood facing the altar with everyone standing behind him. Then he lifted his arms toward heaven 23and prayed:
Lord God of Israel, no other god in heaven or on earth is like you!
You never forget the agreement you made with your people, and you are loyal to anyone who faithfully obeys your teachings. 24My father David was your servant, and today you have kept every promise you made to him.
25 Lord God of Israel, you promised my father that someone from his family would always be king of Israel, if they do their best to obey you, just as he did. 26Please keep this promise you made to your servant David.
27 There's not enough room in all of heaven for you, Lord God. How could you possibly live on earth in this temple I have built? 28But I ask you to answer my prayer. 29 This is the temple where you have chosen to be worshiped. Please watch over it day and night and listen when I turn toward it and pray. 30I am your servant, and the people of Israel belong to you. So whenever any of us look toward this temple and pray, answer from your home in heaven and forgive our sins.
31Suppose someone accuses a person of a crime, and the accused has to stand in front of the altar in your temple and say, “I swear I am innocent!” 32Listen from heaven and decide who is right. Then punish the guilty person and let the innocent one go free.
33 Suppose your people Israel sin against you, and then an enemy defeats them. If they come to this temple and beg for forgiveness, 34listen from your home in heaven. Forgive them and bring them back to the land you gave their ancestors.
35Suppose your people sin against you, and you punish them by holding back the rain. If they turn toward this temple and pray in your name and stop sinning, 36listen from your home in heaven and forgive them. The people of Israel are your servants, so teach them to live right. And please send rain on the land you gave them to be theirs forever.
37Sometimes the crops may dry up or rot or be eaten by locusts or grasshoppers, and your people will be starving. Sometimes enemies may surround their towns, or your people will become sick with deadly diseases. 38Listen when anyone in Israel truly feels sorry and sincerely prays with arms lifted toward your temple. 39You know what is in everyone's heart. So from your home in heaven answer their prayers, according to the way they live and what is in their hearts. 40Then your people will worship and obey you for as long as they live in the land you gave their ancestors.
41-42Foreigners will hear about you and your mighty power, and some of them will come to live among your people Israel. If any of them pray toward this temple, 43listen from your home in heaven and answer their prayers. Then everyone on earth will worship you, just like your people Israel, and they will know that I have built this temple to honor you.
44Our Lord, sometimes you will order your people to attack their enemies. Then your people will turn toward this temple I have built for you in your chosen city, and they will pray to you. 45Answer their prayers from heaven and give them victory.
46Everyone sins. But when your people sin against you, suppose you get angry enough to let their enemies drag them away to foreign countries. 47-49Later, they may feel sorry for what they did and ask your forgiveness. Answer them when they pray toward this temple I have built for you in your chosen city, here in this land you gave their ancestors. From your home in heaven, listen to their sincere prayers and do what they ask. 50Forgive your people no matter how much they have sinned against you. Make the enemies who defeated them be kind to them. 51Remember, they are the people you chose and rescued from Egypt that was like a blazing fire to them.
52I am your servant, and the people of Israel belong to you. So listen when any of us pray and cry out for your help. 53When you brought our ancestors out of Egypt, you told your servant Moses to say to them, “From all people on earth, the Lord God has chosen you to be his very own.”
Solomon Blesses the People
54When Solomon finished his prayer at the altar, he was kneeling with his arms lifted toward heaven. He stood up, 55turned toward the people, blessed them, and said loudly:
56 Praise the Lord! He has kept his promise and given us peace. Every good thing he promised to his servant Moses has happened.
57The Lord our God was with our ancestors to help them, and I pray that he will be with us and never abandon us. 58May the Lord help us obey him and follow all the laws and teachings he gave our ancestors.
59I pray that the Lord our God will remember my prayer day and night. May he help everyone in Israel each day, in whatever way we need it. 60Then every nation will know that the Lord is the only true God.
61Obey the Lord our God and follow his commands with all your heart, just as you are doing today.
Solomon Dedicates the Temple
(2 Chronicles 7.4-10)
62-63Solomon and the people dedicated the temple to the Lord by offering 22,000 cattle and 120,000 sheep as sacrifices to ask the Lord's blessing. 64On that day, Solomon dedicated the courtyard in front of the temple and made it acceptable for worship. He offered the sacrifices there because the bronze altar in front of the temple was too small.
65Solomon and the huge crowd celebrated the Festival of Shelters at the temple for seven days. There were people from as far away as the Egyptian Gorge in the south and Lebo-Hamath in the north. 66Then on the eighth day, he sent everyone home. They said goodbye and left, very happy, because of all the good things the Lord had done for his servant David and his people Israel.
translation_text:
Bi dū ti-Dindaan Poondi Dakaau ki síiǹ kunimbɔtidiin
(Kpèè 2 Kroo 5.2–6.2)
1Míǹ boonee ní ubɔti Saloomɔn yíiń Isirayeel tindaŋkpilib nì tinaakɔti kpilib kɔkɔ nì Isirayeel dicaŋŋi kpilib u-cee bí yòon̄ ti-Dindaan Poondi Dakaau Daafiidi Tiŋkin, an dàkà yii Siiyɔn jool pu, kí cáá cùnnì kunimbɔtidiin. 2Niinee ní Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ kóoǹ ki kpáfì ubɔti Saloomɔn cee bí jī tibìń jiŋaaliu Eetaniim ŋmaliu, an dàkà yii uŋmaluluúti poon. 3Ŋyunti ŋun ní Isirayeel kpilib kɔkɔ bāańee ní bisaraaŋaliibi yōoǹ Dipoondi Dakaau ki túǹ. 4Bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab nìn yōoǹ ti-Dindaan Poondi Dakaau nì circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nì tiwan tin kɔkɔ nìn bí ŋu-poonee ki túǹ. 5Isirayeel samaau kɔkɔ nìn kóoǹ ki kpáfì ubɔti Saloomɔn cee ní bi kūū Dipoondi Dakaau nimbiin ipii nì inaa ki ŋá saraabi an kaa cáá ŋkaan.
6Míǹ boonee ní bisaraaŋaliibi nín dū Dipoondi Dakaau ki kɔ́ǹ Circir Páaa laŋki diikun ki síiǹ u-paaŋŋu pu, keerubimbi feeŋyi taapu. 7Di sá yii keerubimbi nìn kpátì bi-feeŋyi mpaan ŋun bi nìn bɔ́ntì kí síiń Dipoondi Dakaauee yilpu, ní ki nìn bīī Dipoondi Dakaau nì idɔ in bi cáa tūntí-uee pu. 8Dakaa dɔi gbanti nìn fɔ̀kɔ̀ tiŋan, an puee a yaa nìn bí Circir laŋkee, a nìn wāĺ i-nyɔkɔ ní, ama a yaa nìn bí mmɔŋkee, an kaa nìn wāĺ. Idɔee dáá gbíntìi bí ki dāa sāā díǹ. 9Tiba kaa nìn bí Dipoondi Dakaau poon an yaa kaa sá ataŋkpee pilinti tili tin Mooyiisi nìn dūu ŋée. Ti-Dindaan nín nìn nyántì Isirayeel yab Eejipiti tiŋkin u nì bi ŋá mpèé Ooreeb jool puee ní Mooyiisi dū ataŋkpee pilinti gbanti ki ŋá dakaayee poon.
10Ŋyunti ŋun ní bisaraaŋaliibi nyánní Circir laŋkee ní ditagbandi diba dɔ́miń ki bīiǹ ti-Dindaan Diiku pu. 11Ditagbandee puee, bisaraaŋaliibi kaa nìn gíti ŋūǹ kí sīĺ poon kí tɔ̄ bi-tundi, di sá yii ti-Dindaan nyooti nìn gbí u-diiku poon. 12Niinee ní Saloomɔn bí yii:
«Ti-Dindaan, a nìn lēē yii a làá nīn kóò ditagbambɔndin ní.
13Ama m máń-si kudinyaaŋŋu nee,
kudii kun poon ní a làá nīn kóò talkuee!»
Saloomɔn mēē ki dū kudii ki sú Unimbɔti
(2 Kroo 6.3-11)
14Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nìn sí ní ubɔti fātì u-nimbiin ki túĺ-bi ní ki mēē ki bīiǹ bi-pu. 15U nìn bí yii: «Tí jāam̀maan ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu! Úǹ u-ba ŋá kii u nín nìn pōoǹ m-baa Daafiidi puee. U nìn bí-u yii: 16<Man di nyántì m-nibul Isirayeel Eejipiti tiŋkin. Kí yòon̄ ŋwiin gbantee, maa lēē Isirayeel timmu kɔkɔ kansikin kiba kin poon ní bi làá mā-mi kudii ḿ nīn lèekī m-ba ki dàkèe. Ama m lēē sii Daafiidi á nīn sá m-nibul Isirayeel bɔtiu.> 17M-baa Daafiidi nìn cáá nlandɔkɔ kí mā kudii kí dū-ku kí sú ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu. 18Ama ti-Dindaan nìn bí-u yii: <A nín ká nlandɔkɔ yii a làá mā kudii kí tīī-mee, an ŋān̄ tikpil. 19Tin bée di sá yii an kaa sá sii di làá mā kudii gbanti, ama sii a-ba jipɔɔn un a màl̄ee di làá mā kudii gbanti kí tīī-mi.> 20Kɔŋkɔnnee, ti-Dindaan nín nìn pōoǹ puee u ŋá míǹ. Di sá yii m fōō m-baa Daafiidi yil ki jíń Isirayeel tiŋki pu dibeel, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn lī puee, ní m máń kudii nee ki dū-ku ki sú ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu. 21M kpáàa bɔ́ntì mpaan ki tīī Dipoondi Dakaau un poon ti-Dindaan Poondi nyɔɔbuŋŋi kēe. Dipoondi gbantee, u nín nìn nyántìń ti-naanjab Eejipiti tiŋkinee ní u nìn pōoǹ.»
Saloomɔn wimmeem
(Kpèè 2 Kroo 6.12)
22Míǹ boonee ní Saloomɔn yíkìi síl̀ ti-Dindaan saraafaŋŋu nì Isirayeel yab bin kɔkɔ nìn kóoǹ ki kpáfèe nimbiin, ní ki yōoǹ u-ŋalii ki túĺ kutaa 23ní ki bí yii: «Ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu, Unimbɔti ubɔ kaa bí yilpu àá kitiŋ pu ki bí kii siiyee. A ŋúb̀ a-poondi ki dàkà a-tɔntɔnliibi bin sí nì si nì dipɔbil dibee kulaŋŋaŋfitiiu. 24A nín nìn pōoǹ a-tɔntɔnliu m-baa Daafiidi yii a làá ŋá pu kí tīī-uee, a ŋá míǹ. Mbaamɔn tin a nìn pōoǹ-uee, sii a-ba ŋá míǹ ki tīī-u díǹ. 25Kɔŋkɔnnee, ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu, ŋá a nín nìn pōoǹ a-tɔntɔnliu m-baa Daafiidi yii a làá ŋá pu kí tīī-uee. A nìn bí-u yii: <A-naantiibi yaa nóó-mi ibaamɔn poon kii sii a-ba nín nóó-mi puee, ibaamɔn ní m tùkù-si, a-kpátam boonee, a-naantiibi kansikin ubɔ làá nīn pée sá ubɔti ní Isirayeel tiŋkin.> 26Míǹ puee Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu, m gbàam̄-si ní, ŋá kɔŋkɔnnee a nín nìn pōoǹ a-tɔntɔnliu m-baa Daafiidi yii a làá ŋá puee kí tīī-u!
27«Mimmee Unimbɔti ŋūǹ kí kɔ́ kitiŋ puɔɔɔ? Áli gba kutagbɔŋu nín wāā pu nee kaa bàn̄-si á kɔ́, ki dāa nín kàaǹ kudii kun m máń nee! 28Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, m-Dindaan m-Nimbɔtiu, pīlifì man a-tɔntɔnliu wimmeem nì m-gbaamii! Pīlifì m-kuŋkuuntii nì m-wimmeem min man a-tɔntɔnliu bíi mèé-si díǹ neeyee! 29A-nimbikpeeŋu ń nīn pée cɔ́ kudii nee pu ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu, ŋú nīn pée cɔ́ mpaan ŋun pu a nìn sòon̄ yii: <M-yindi làá nīn bí niin> nee pu. Pīlifì ŋwimmeem min m bí doo ki mèé-si nee.» 30Pīlifì man a-tɔntɔnliu nì Isirayeel, a-nibul wimmeem min ti bí doo ki mèé-si nee. Pīlifiǹ-ti doooo yilpu laakin a kóòyee. Pīlifiǹ-ti kí dū ti-kpitii kí pɔ̄-ti.
31Ubɔ yaa yīntiǹ u-juti, bi ŋūǹ kí lì yii ú pùtī yii u yaa ká mbusu ń lítí u-pu. Udaan yaa lafun dɔ́miń kudii nee poon a-saraafaŋŋu nyɔkɔpu ki pūtèe, 32á pīlifì doooo yilpu kí kpèè tibɔti gbanti kí sòoǹ a-tɔntɔnliibi bɔti. Á kpɔ̀ dibɔkpil daan bɔti kí dáaĺ u-tafal, ní kí pɔ̀ un bɔti ŋān̄ee báà ŋma ń béé yii u sá maanyiiba.
33«Isirayeel yab a-nibul yaa yīntiǹ-si ní bi-nannanliibi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi, ní bi fātìi gítìń a-cee, ki nyɔ́ŋkì-si, ki mēē-si ní ki gbāam̀-si kudii nee poonee, 34sii ti-Dindaan, á pīlifì a-nibul Isirayeel yab doooo yilpu, kí dū bi-kpitii kí pɔ̄-bi, ní kí fàtīí gíiǹní-bi kitiŋ kin a nìn dūu tīī bi-naanjabee pu.
35«A-nibul yaa yīntiǹ-si ní a dū kutaa ki pīiǹ utaa kaa ti bíi nì, ní bi fātì bi-ba ki túĺ mpaan nee pú ki mēē ki nyɔ́ŋkì a-yindi, ní ki fātì bi-boon ki tīī bi-kpitii a nín dáaĺ bi-tafal pueeyee, 36sii ti-Dindaan, á pīlifiǹ a-tɔntɔnliibi Isirayeel yab doooo yilpu. Á dū bi-kpitii kí pɔ̄-bi, kí dàkà-bi nsammɔnti ŋun bi máaǹ kí nóóyee, ní kí yàntī utaa ń nì a-tiŋki nee pu, kitiŋ kin ní a dūu tīī a-nibul án nīn sá bi-fakalee.
37«Ŋkùm àá bìlbil kúm yaa jéetì kitiŋ nee pu, àá tikpaajin kaa láá bīń ní ki kūń àá ki sūū, àá inaakitoon nì inaaki di ŋmɔ́ ki bíil̀ tikpaajin, àá bi-nannanliibi di māntìi tú bi-timmu kí já nì bi, àá an yaa pée sá tibumbun àá igbaŋween iŋyee, 38Isirayeel yab kansikin ubɔ àá a-nibul Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ di yaa béè tin bāań-bee, ki yōoǹ bi-ŋalii ki túĺ Kudii nee watil pú ki mēē-si àá ki gbāam̀-see, 39sii ti-Dindaan, á pīlifiǹ-bi doooo yilpu laakin a kóoǹnée. Á dū bi-kpitii kí pɔ̄-bi, ní kí ŋá kí tīī báà ŋma kii an nín máaǹ puee. Di sá yii a nyí báà ŋma pɔbil poon bɔti. 40Ŋá míǹ án nín làá ŋá pu ní Isirayeel yab ń fàŋkì-si iwiin in kɔkɔ bi cáá kí kàl̄ kitiŋ kin a tīī bi-naanjabee puee.
41«Unicaan un kaa sá a-nibul Isirayeel yab kansikin ubɔee yaa nyánní kitindandatii ki dɔ́miń a-yindi pu, 42di sá yii u gbìl̄ bi sòon̄ a-yiŋkpaandi nì a-pɔŋkpaaŋŋu pu. U yaa dɔ́miń míǹ ki yōoǹ u-ŋalii ki túĺ kudii nee ki mēēyee, 43sii ti-Dindaan, á pīlifiǹ-u doooo yilpu laakin a kóoǹnée, kí ŋá u nín bālifì-si puee kí tīī-u. A yaa ŋá míǹ, kitiŋ pu nib kɔkɔ làá béé a-yindi, kí fàŋkì-si kii Isirayeel yab nín fàŋkí-si puee. Bi làá béé yii a lafun bí kudii kun m máń nee ni.
44«A yaa tīī a-nibul Isirayeel yab mara yii bí cù kí já nì bi-nannanliibi, ní bi fātì bi-ba ki túĺ kitiŋ kin a lēē nee nì kudii kun m máń-si nee watil pú ki mēēyee, 45á pīlifì bi-wimmeem nì bi-gbaamii doooo yilpu, ní kí tīī-bi dijajil.
46«An ŋūǹ kí ŋá yii Isirayeel yab yīntiǹ-si, di sá yii unil ubɔ kpá kaa yìntī. Bi yaa ŋá míǹ ní a gíí bi-pu diŋuul ki yāntì binannanliibi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi ki cúú-bi ki cūnnì bi-tiŋki kin dátèe àá kin kaa dátèe ni kuyuŋu, 47ní bi yaa kíĺ ki bíi dàkafī, ki kpántì bi-bimbim, ki gbāam̀-si kitiŋ gbanti poon ki lī yii: <Ti ŋá ikpiti, ti yīntì, ti jíń dibɔkpil>. 48Bi-nannanliibi tiŋki gbanti poonee, bi yaa fātìi gítìń a-cee nì bi-pɔbil kɔkɔ nì bi-naŋki kɔkɔ, ní ki fātì bi-ba ki túĺ kitiŋ kin a tīī bi-naanjab nì kitiŋ kin ní a lēē nee nì kudii kun ní m máń-si nee ki mēē-see, 49sii ti-Dindaan, á pīlifiǹ-bi doooo yilpu laakin a kóoǹnée. Pīlifì bi-wimmeem nì bi-gbaamii kí jòoń-bi. 50Dū a-nibul kpitii kí pɔ̄-bi. Dū bi nín jáà nì si puee kí pɔ̄-bi, ní kí yàntī bin ŋúb́-bi kuyuŋuee ń sɔ̄ bi-saai kí dàkà-bi kulaŋŋaŋfitiiu. 51Di sá yii bi sá a-nibul ní. Sii di yì-bi ní ki nyántìń-bi Eejipiti yab paaki ŋmiŋun.
52«Ŋúbití a-nimbiliŋ, ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti. Pīlifì man a-tɔntɔnliu gbaamii nì a-nibul Isirayeel gbaamii. Pīlifiǹ-ti ŋyunti ŋun kamaa ní ti yaa pée kúuǹ ki yíiń-see. 53Di sá yii sii di lútì-ti kitiŋ pu nibuliŋ kɔkɔ kansikin tí nīn sá difakal ki tīī-si, kii a nín nìn dī a-tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi pu ki sòon̄ pu ŋyunti ŋun a nìn nyántì ti-naanjab Eejipiti tiŋkinee.»
Saloomɔn mēē Unimbɔti ń bìin̄ samaa pu
54Saloomɔn nìn gbāaǹ u-tabiŋyiliŋ pu ti-Dindaan saraafaŋŋu nyɔkɔpu, ki yōoǹ u-ŋalii yilpu, ní ki mēē ki gbāam̀ ti-Dindaan. U nìn mēē míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki yíkì 55ki síl̀ ki mēē mpɔn ki bīiǹ Isirayeel samaau pu ki lī yii: 56«Tí nyɔ̄ŋkìmaan ti-Dindaan un di tīī u-nibul Isirayeel ŋgbansɔŋfi kii u nín nìn pōoǹ puee. Di sá yii u nín nìn dī u-tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi pu ki pōoǹ-ti ipoon iŋyee, báà iba kaa gbíntì waa ŋá. 57Tin m mèé ti-Dindaan Unimbɔtee di sá ú nīn bí ti-cee kii u nín nìn bí ti-naanjab cee puee. Ú taa dū-ti kí fá, kí taa fàtī u-boon kí tīī-ti. 58Ú gíiǹní ti-pɔbiliŋ u-cee! Niinee ti làá ŋmā kí nīn bí kii u nín là tí nīn bí puee, ní tí nīn ŋúb́ u-marab nì u-bɔkpaaŋi nì u-koobiliŋ ŋin u nìn dūu tīī ti-naanjabee. 59Ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu ń nīn téetí m-gbaamii in m dūu bíl̀ u-nimbiin nee pu ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu. Ú pɔ̀ man u-tɔntɔnliu nì u-nibul Isirayeel yab. 60An yaa ŋá mimmee, kitiŋ pu nib kɔkɔ làá béé yii ti-Dindaan baba di sá Unimbɔti, ubɔ kaa ti bí. 61Nín̄ símaan nì ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu deedee, kí nīn ŋúb́ u-bɔkpaaŋi kí nīn tɔ́ u-marab, kii ni nín bíi ŋáań pu díǹ nee.»
Saraabi bin bi ŋá ki tīī ti-Dindaanee
(Kpèè 2 Kroo 7.4-10)
62Ubɔti saloomɔn nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ kpáfì ki ŋá saraabi ki tīī ti-Dindaan. 63Saloomɔn nìn kūū inaa kutukub mmuŋku nì bili, ní ki kūū ipii nì iŋoobu kutukub dilaataal nì mmuŋku ki ŋá mpèé saraau. Bi nín ŋá pu ki dū kunimbɔtidii ki sú ti-Dindaanee dee. 64Ŋwiin gbanti mbaanti ní ubɔti dū dicindi din bí kunimbɔtidii nyɔkɔpuee ki sú ti-Dindaan. Di sá yii tasa kúti saraafaŋŋu ŋun nìn bí kunimbɔtidii punyɔkɔki caŋinee kaa nìn náaǹ bí ŋmā kí wà saraabi kɔkɔ. An puee kunimbɔtidii cindin ní u nìn dū saraawɔkaa nì tijin saraabi nì mpèé saraabi kpam ki wùn̄ ki ŋá saraa.
65Ŋyunti gbanti mbaanti ní Saloomɔn nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ kpáfì ki jíń tibìń jiŋaaliu. An nìn sá dinikitikpaandi ní, binib nìn nyánní doooo Leeboo-Amaati kitiŋ yilpu pú ki cáá sāā Eejipiti buŋŋu kitiŋ taapu pú. Bi nìn jíń jiŋaal gbanti iwiin iluli ní ti-Dindaan nimbiin, ní ki gíti kútì iwiin iluli, an kpáfìi ŋá ŋwiin ŋubɔ kpá saalku. 66Kinyɔnliliitii iwiin inii dalee ní Saloomɔn yāntì Isirayeel yab nín gítí bi-dumpui. Samaa nìn jáam̀ ubɔti ní ki nín kóò bi-tantibin nì mmɔn nì dipɔɔpindi, kun puee ti-Dindaan nìn dàkā u-tɔntɔnliu Daafiidi nì u-nibul Isirayeel kulaŋŋaŋfitiiu.

english_text:
The Lord Appears to Solomon Again
(2 Chronicles 7.11-22)
1The Lord's temple and Solomon's palace were now finished, and Solomon had built everything he wanted. 2 Some time later the Lord appeared to him again in a dream, just as he had done at Gibeon. 3 The Lord said:
I heard your prayer and what you asked me to do. This temple you have built is where I will be worshiped forever. It belongs to me, and I will never stop watching over it.
4You must obey me, as your father David did, and be honest and fair. Obey my laws and teachings, 5 and I will keep my promise to David that someone from your family will always be king of Israel.
6But if you or any of your descendants disobey my commands or start worshiping foreign gods, 7I will no longer let my people Israel live in this land I gave them. I will desert this temple where I said I would be worshiped. Then people everywhere will think this nation is only a joke and will make fun of it. 8 This temple will become a pile of rocks! Everyone who walks by will be shocked, and they will ask, “Why did the Lord do such a terrible thing to his people and to this temple?” 9Then they will answer, “We know why the Lord did this. The people of Israel rejected the Lord their God, who rescued their ancestors from Egypt, and they started worshiping other gods.”
Other Things Solomon Did
(2 Chronicles 8.1-18)
10It took 20 years for the Lord's temple and Solomon's palace to be built. 11Later, Solomon gave King Hiram of Tyre 20 towns in the region of Galilee to repay him for the cedar, pine, and gold he had given Solomon.
12When Hiram went to see the towns, he did not like them. 13He said, “Solomon, my friend, are these the kind of towns you want to give me?” So Hiram called the region Cabul because he thought it was worthless. 14He sent Solomon only five tons of gold in return.
15After Solomon's workers had finished the temple and the palace, he ordered them to fill in the land on the east side of Jerusalem, to build a wall around the city, and to rebuild the towns of Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer.
16Earlier, the king of Egypt had captured the town of Gezer; he burned it to the ground and killed the Canaanite people living there. Then he gave it to his daughter as a wedding present when she married Solomon. 17So Solomon had the town rebuilt.
Solomon ordered his workers to rebuild Lower Beth-Horon, 18Baalath, and Tamar in the desert of Judah. 19They also built towns where he could keep his supplies and his chariots and horses. Solomon ordered them to build whatever he wanted in Jerusalem, Lebanon, and anywhere in his kingdom.
20-22Solomon did not force the Israelites to do his work. They were his soldiers, officials, leaders, commanders, chariot captains, and chariot drivers. But he did make slaves of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites who were living in Israel. These were the descendants of those foreigners the Israelites could not destroy, and they remained Israel's slaves.
23Solomon appointed 550 officers to be in charge of his workers and to watch over his building projects.
24Solomon's wife, the daughter of the king of Egypt, moved from the older part of Jerusalem to her new palace. Then Solomon had the land on the east side of Jerusalem filled in.
25 Three times a year, Solomon burned incense and offered sacrifices to the Lord on the altar he had built.
Solomon had now finished building the Lord's temple.
26He also had a lot of ships at Ezion-Geber, a town in Edom near Eloth on the Red Sea. 27-28King Hiram let some of his experienced sailors go to the country of Ophir with Solomon's own sailors, and they brought back about 14 tons of gold for Solomon.
translation_text:
Ti-Dindaan lēē u-ba ki dàkā Saloomɔn nliliitiimin
(2 Kroo 7.11-22)
1Saloomɔn nìn máń ti-Dindaan Diiku nì úǹ u-ba naakooku nì tin u nìn pée là kí mēe ki dóò. 2Míǹ boonee ní ti-Dindaan nyántì u-ba nliliitiim ki dàkā-u kii u nín nìn nyántì u-ba ki dàkā-u Gabawɔn puee. 3Ti-Dindaan nìn bí-u yii: «M gbìl̄ a-wimmeem nì a-gbaamii in a dūu bíl̀ m-nimbiinee. M ŋá kudii kun a máńee circir, ní m kíí bí nīn jáaḿ m-yindi ku-poon kí nīn cá jaanjaan. M-nimbikpeeŋu làá nīn pée cɔ́ ku-pu, ní m làá nīn wúń ku-pu baabadal. 4Ama siiyee, nín̄ nóó-mi nì dipɔbil diba nì ibaamɔn poon kii a-baa Daafiidee. Nín̄ ŋáań tin m kpáafì-see, ní kí nīn ŋúb́ m-bɔkpaaŋi nì m-koobiliŋ. 5A yaa ŋá míǹ, m làá tīī a-bɔtiiti Isirayeel nibul pu mpɔn kí nīn cá jaanjaan. M nín nìn pōoǹ a-baa Daafiidi puee dee. M nìn bí-u yii: <A-kpátam boonee, a-naantiibi kansikin ubɔ làá nīn pée sá ubɔti ní Isirayeel tiŋkin.> 6Ama sii nì a-jipɔmbi yaa kaa ŋúb́ m-marab nì m-koobiliŋ ŋin m tīī-nee, ní ki yaa fātì ni-boon ki tīī-mi ki cūtìi nóó awaa ki gbàantí ŋi-taapuee, 7m làá jà Isirayeel yab kitiŋ kin m tīī-bee pu. M làá fàtī m-boon kí tīī kudii kun m dūu sú m-ba nee. Anibul kɔkɔ làá nīn kíǹ ki bèel̄ Isirayeel yab ní ki lāā-bi. 8Kudii nee làá dāá kpántí adigbun ní. Un kamaa yaa láa jītí kudii nee caŋinee làá dāá bàkatī ní kí bàlifì yii: <Ba yì-tì ní ti-Dindaan nín ŋá kitiŋ nee nì kudii nee míǹ?> 9Niinee ní bí dāá kíí-bi yii: <Kun yì-tèe di sá yii Isirayeel yab dū ti-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu un di nyántìń-bi Eejipiti tiŋkinee ki fá. Bi dū bi-ba ki tīī awaa ki gbàantí ŋi-taapu ki jáaḿ-ŋi. An pu ní ti-Dindaan yāntì nnaabu nee bāań-bi.>»
Saloomɔn nín túń atuun ŋiŋyee
(Kpèè 2 Kroo 8.1-18)
10Abin mmuŋku ní Saloomɔn nìn dūu máń adiin liitil, an dàkà yii ti-Dindaan Diiku nì kubɔtinaakoou. 11Tiir bɔtiu Yiiram di nìn tīī Saloomɔn seedir dɔi nì siipreesi dɔi nì sindaariya kii u nín nìn là puee. An puee ubɔti Saloomɔn nìn tīī-u Galiilee tiŋkpaaŋkin ntimu mmuŋku. 12Niinee ní Yiiram nyánní Tiir tiŋkin ki dɔ́miń kí kpèè ntimu mun Saloomɔn tīī-uee, ama ntimuee bɔti kaa nìn fáatì-u. 13Niinee ní u bí yii: «M-nabiki, ba timmu ní a nín tīī-mi nan dee!» An pu ní nìn díǹ, bi yíì ntimu gbanti yii Kabuul timmu. 14Nì míǹ kɔkɔee Yiiram nìn gíti tīī Saloomɔn sindaariya tɔnnib bita nì dijandi.
15Diwɔ́bil tundi ní Saloomɔn nìn dūu máń ti-Dindaan Diiku nì úǹ u-ba diiku nì kudii kun bi yíì Miilooyee nì digundi din bi máń ki tú Jeerusaleem tiŋkee nì Asɔɔr nì Meegiidoo nì Geeseer timmu. 16Eejipiti bɔtiu Faaroo nìn cūtìi jáń ki fōō Geeseer tiŋki. U nìn kūū Kanaan yab bin nìn kóò niinee kɔkɔ ní ki tūū adiin ŋŋmi, ní ki dū kitiŋee ki pàn̄ u-bisal un mɔ́ǹ Saloomɔŋyee cootiiku. 17An pu ní an nìn bālifì yii Saloomɔn ń fàtīí mā Geeseer tiŋki gbanti. Saloomɔn nìn gíti máń Beeti-Oorɔn-Taapu, 18nì Balaati timmu nì Tamaar tiŋki kin bí kuteeunee, 19nì ntimu mun kɔkɔ poon ní bi nìn bīil̀ u-jintee, nì ntimu mun poon ní u-janjatɔrɔkub nìn sīlifée, nì mun poon ní u-taamui nìn bée.
Saloomɔn nìn gíti máń kun ní u nìn lèe Jeerusaleem tiŋkin nì Leebanɔn jool pu nì ntimu mun kɔkɔ nìn pée bí u-taapuee. 20Amɔɔr yab nì Eeti yab nì Peeriisi yab nì Eefi yab nì Jeebusi yab biba nìn kíǹ ki bí Isirayeel tiŋkin, bíǹ gbanti kaa nìn sá Isirayeel yab. 21Bi nìn gbíntìi bí kun puee Isirayeel yab kaa nìn ŋúń ki kūū ki céetì-bi. Saloomɔn nìn dū bi-naantiibi ki ŋá diwɔ́bil tundin ki dāa sāā díǹ. 22Ama Saloomɔn kaa nìn dū Isirayeel yab ki ŋá diwɔ́bil tundi gbantin. Bíǹ di nìn sá u-janjaliibi nì u-janjakpilib nì u-janjakpootiliibi nì bin ŋàal̀ janjatɔrɔkubee nì bitanjakaliibi. 23Kɔmandambi nìn lēē bikàliŋkpilib alaataa aŋmoo nì imuŋku ili nì saalaa bí nīn kpèé bin bí ki tūǹ Saloomɔn tuuŋŋee.
24 Faaroo bisal nín jɔ́m̀ Daafiidi Tiŋkin ki kɔ́ kudii kun Saloomɔn nìn máń ki tīī-uee, boonee ní u nín máń Miiloo diiku.
25Saloomɔn nìn ŋáań bisaraawɔkaabi nì mpèé saraabi nsaraafan ŋun u nìn máń ti-Dindaanee dibindi poonee mita pu ní. U nìn gíti tùutī talaalub nsaraafan pu ki tìì ti-Dindaan. Míǹ ní u nìn ŋáań ki dàkà kun pu kunimbɔtidii bée.
26Ubɔti Saloomɔn nìn kpáá meelab Eesiiyɔn-Geebeer tiŋkin Eelaati tiŋki caŋin. Eelaati tiŋki gbanti bí Tikati Mɔɔl gbandi, Eedoom tiŋkin ní. 27Yiiram nìn dū u-tɔntɔnliibi bimeelaŋaaliliibi bin nyí tiŋku bɔti tiŋanee ki tú bí tūtuǹ Saloomɔn tɔntɔnliibi. 28Bimeelaŋaaliliibi gbanti nìn cūtì Oofiiri tiŋkin ki nyàab̄ sindaariya tɔnnib saalaa nì bili ki cáa cūnnì ki tīī ubɔti Saloomɔn.

english_text:
The Queen of Sheba Visits Solomon
(2 Chronicles 9.1-12)
1 The Queen of Sheba heard how famous Solomon was, so she went to Jerusalem to test him with difficult questions. 2She took along several of her officials, and she loaded her camels with gifts of spices, jewels, and gold. When she arrived, she and Solomon talked about everything she could think of. 3He answered every question, no matter how difficult it was.
4-5The Queen was amazed at Solomon's wisdom. She was breathless when she saw his palace, the food on his table, his officials, his servants in their uniforms, the people who served his food, and the sacrifices he offered at the Lord's temple. 6She said:
Solomon, in my own country I had heard about your wisdom and all you've done. 7But I didn't believe it until I saw it with my own eyes! And there's so much I didn't hear about. You are wiser and richer than I was told. 8Your wives and officials are lucky to be here where they can listen to the wise things you say.
9I praise the Lord your God. He is pleased with you and has made you king of Israel. The Lord has always loved Israel, so he has given them a king who will rule fairly and honestly.
10The Queen of Sheba gave Solomon more than four tons of gold, many jewels, and more spices than anyone had ever brought into Israel.
11-13In return, Solomon gave her the gifts he would have given any other ruler, but he also gave her everything else she wanted. Then she and her officials went back to their own country.
Solomon's Wealth
(2 Chronicles 9.13-28)
King Hiram's ships brought gold, juniper wood, and jewels from the country of Ophir. Solomon used the wood to make steps for the temple and palace, and harps and other stringed instruments for the musicians. It was the best juniper wood anyone in Israel had ever seen.
14Solomon received almost 23 tons of gold a year. 15The merchants and traders, as well as the kings of Arabia and rulers from Israel, also gave him gold.
16Solomon made 200 gold shields and used almost seven kilograms of gold for each one. 17He also made 300 smaller gold shields, using almost two kilograms for each one, and he put the shields in his palace in Forest Hall.
18His throne was made of ivory and covered with pure gold. 19-20The back of the throne was rounded at the top, and it had armrests on each side. There was a statue of a lion on both sides of the throne, and there was a statue of a lion at both ends of each of the six steps leading up to the throne. No other throne in the world was like Solomon's.
21Since silver was almost worthless in those days, everything was made of gold, even the cups and dishes used in Forest Hall.
22Solomon had a lot of seagoing ships. Every three years he sent them out with Hiram's ships to bring back gold, silver, and ivory, as well as monkeys and peacocks.
23He was the richest and wisest king in the world. 24People from every nation wanted to hear the wisdom God had given him. 25Year after year people came and brought gifts of silver and gold, as well as clothes, weapons, spices, horses, or mules.
26 Solomon had 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horses that he kept in Jerusalem and other towns.
27 While he was king, there was silver everywhere in Jerusalem, and cedar was as common as ordinary sycamore trees in the foothills.
28-29 Solomon's merchants bought his horses and chariots in the regions of Musri and Kue. They paid 600 pieces of silver for a chariot and 150 pieces of silver for a horse. They also sold horses and chariots to the Hittite and Syrian kings.
translation_text:
Sabaa nimpubɔtiu māntì Saloomɔn pu
(Kpèè 2 Kroo 9.1-12)
1Sabaa nimpubɔtiu nìn gbìl̄ ti-Dindaan nín yāntì Saloomɔn nyáń diyindi puee, ní u dɔ́miń kí màntì u-pu, kí pɔ́ɔǹ-u ipɔɔn kí màkan̄-u kí kpèè. 2U nìn bāań Jeerusaleem nì dinikitikpaandi nì igutaamu i tú talaalub nì sindaariya tikpil nì ataŋkpamɔnti. U bāań Saloomɔn ceeyee ní ki bālifì-u tibɔti tin kɔkɔ pée kā u-pɔbilinee. 3Saloomɔn nìn pée kíí-u tin kɔkɔ u nìn bālifì-uee ní. Tiba kaa nìn bí ki pɔ̄ɔ̄ ki tīī ubɔti waa ŋúń ki kíí. 4Sabaa tiŋki nimpubɔtiu nín ká Saloomɔn ciiŋyi nì kudii kun u máńee 5nì tijin tin tɔ́kɔ́ u-teebiliu puee nì u-tɔntɔnliibi kɔŋkooŋyi nì u-tɔntɔnliibi bin tìì-u tijin u jīǹ nì nnyim u nyùee wampeeŋkaati nì saraabi bin u nìn ŋáań kunimbɔtidiinee ní an ŋá-u bitii waa ti nyí tin poon u bée. 6Niinee ní u bí ubɔti yii: «Tin m gbìl̄ m-tiŋkin a-tuuŋŋi pu nì a-ciiŋyi puee lafun sá mbaamɔn ní. 7Ama maa nìn fōō ki kíí, see m nín dɔ́miń m-ba ki ká nì m-nimbilee. Tin bi máafì-mee kaa bàn̄ tin m ká nee dijandi gba. A-ciiŋyi nì a-gaajati jítiǹ tin m gbìl̄ee pu kpataaa. 8A-nib nì a-tɔntɔnliibi bin bí a-nimbiin baabadal ki pílifí a-ciiŋyi nyɔɔbuŋŋee bí mmɔnneeee! 9Tí nyɔ̄ŋkì ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu un di lēē-si á kàl̄ Isirayeel tiŋki pu dibeelee! Kun puee u néeń Isirayeel kí nīn cá jaanjaan, an pu ní u dū-si ki kāaǹ dibeel á yàntī tin bí deedeeyee nì ibaamɔn ń nīn bí.»
10Míǹ boonee ní Sabaa tiŋki nimpubɔtiu tīī ubɔti Saloomɔn sindaariya tɔnnib bita nì dijandi nì talaalub tikpil nì ataŋkpamɔnti. Sabaa nimpubɔtiu nín nìn tīī ubɔti Saloomɔn talaalub puee, baa ti pée ká an talaalub bulifi kɔ́ Isirayeel tiŋkin dalba dalba.
11Yiiram meelab bin nìn túǹní sindaariya Oofiiri tiŋkin ki cáańee nìn cáań santaal dɔi tikpil tikpil nì ataŋkpamɔnti mun. 12Ubɔti nìn dū idɔ gbanti ki ŋá jaantalkub ki tíkiǹ ti-Dindaan Diiku nì kubɔtinaakoou, ní ki nìn lēē ki kpítì tibati ki tīī u-laŋgaaliibi. Santaal dɔi kaa ti pée kɔ́ Isirayeel tiŋkin míǹ ki dāa sāā díǹ.
13Ubɔti Saloomɔn mun nìn tīī Sabaa nimpubɔtiu tin kɔkɔ u nìn là ki bālifèe, ní kí nín kūtì tin úǹ ubɔti nìn pú-u mbɔtiyaaminee. Míǹ boonee ní u nì u-tɔntɔnliibi nín gítí bi-tiŋkin.
Ubɔti Saloomɔn gaajati
(Kpèè 2 Kroo 1.14-17, 9.13-28)
14Dibimbaantiil poonee, sindaariya un bi cáań ki tīī ubɔti Saloomɔŋyee nìn nyáń tɔnnib mmuŋku ní, 15ní kí nín kūtì bibantiliibi nì binyampoobi nín nìn cāabìń sindaariya un ki pà patantibee, nì ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú bɔtiibi nì Isirayeel tiŋgbammu nín lèekī pu ki cāabìń ki pà lampoobee.
16Ubɔti Saloomɔn nìn yāntì bi dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ agbampɔɔ alaataa ali. Bi nìn dū sindaariya kiiloobi biluu ní ki mɔ́ɔ́ digbampɔɔl kamaa. 17U nìn gíti dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ agbampɔɔ ŋwaamu alaataa ata. Bi nìn dū sindaariya kiiloo ubɔ nì dijandi ní ki mɔ́ɔ́ digbampɔɔl kamaa. Ubɔti nìn dū agbampɔɔyee ki síiǹ kudii kun bi yíì yii <Leebanɔn Pɔɔkuee> poon ní.
18Ubɔti nìn gíti kpítì dibeejal dikpaandi diba ní ki dū sindaariyamɔnti ki nyūntì ní ki dū kunti nyiŋŋi ki nákáǹ nákáǹ. 19Dibeejalee nìn cáá akɔl aluu, ní di-yilpu pú bí dikuŋkundi, ní ki cáá laakin bi pāantí iŋalee. Bi nìn kpítì gbikintib bili ki síiǹ laakin bi pāantí iŋalee. 20Gbikintib nìn bí saalaa nì bili ní ki bí akɔl aluuyee nín kúntí puee. Baa nìn pée kpítì dibeejal diba míǹ dibeel diba poon ki ká.
21Ubɔti Saloomɔn kɔŋkɔnnyɔkaabi kɔkɔ nìn sá sindaariya ŋma ní, ní asambil ŋin bí <Leebanɔn Pɔɔku> diikunee nìn sá sindaariyamɔnti ŋma. Baa nìn dù animbil kúti kí ŋá tiba, di sá yii Saloomɔn yuntiŋuee, animbil kúti kaa nìn cáá kunyampoou. 22Di sá yii ubɔti nìn cáá meelab Taarsiisi tiŋkin bin tūntí binyampoobee bi cá ki gítiń bi nì Yiiram meelab. Abin ata poon diba puee, meelab gbanti nìn cāabìń sindaariya nì animbil kúti nì kunti nyiŋŋi nì ilantan nì ikooŋaan.
23Ubɔti Saloomɔn nìn jítiǹ kitiŋ pu bɔtiibi kɔkɔ tigaajati poon nì iciin poon. 24Kitiŋ pu nib kɔkɔ nìn nyàab̀ kí ká Saloomɔn kí ŋmā kí pīlifì iciin in Unimbɔti nìn tīī-uee. 25Bi yaa nìn dòońee, báà ŋma nìn cāabìń animbil kúti wanti nì sindaariya wanti nì tiwampeeŋkaal nì tijanjawan nì talaalub nì itaamu nì imamboon ki pūǹ-u. Dibindi kamaayee, binib nìn pée ŋáań míǹ ní.
26Saloomɔn nìn kóoǹ janjatɔrɔkub nì itaamu ki kpáfì. U nìn cáá janjatɔrɔkub kutuku ubɔ nì alaataa anaa, ní ki cáá itaamu kutukub saalaa nì bili. Tijanjawan gbanti tiba nìn bí ntimu mun poon ní ajanjanaapaa nìn bée, ní tiba mun bí u-cee Jeerusaleem. 27Ubɔti nìn yāntì animbil gbí Jeerusaleem kii ataŋkpeeyee ní, ní seedir dɔi wīikí kii Seefeelaa tiŋkin sufii in bi yíì siikoomɔɔree. 28Saloomɔn taamui nìn nyēeń Eejipiti nì Siisilii timmun ní. Niin ní ubɔti nyampoobi nìn dāań-i. 29Bi yaa nìn cáań janjatɔrɔku Eejipiti tiŋkinee, u-nyampooku nìn sá animbil kúti jitɔmbi alaataa aluu ní, ní utaamu nyampooku sá animbil kúti jitɔmbi dilaataal nì imuŋku ili nì saalaa. Binyampoobi gbanti nìn cāabìń janjatɔrɔkub nì itaamu gbanti ki nyáfíǹ Eeti yab nì Siirii yab bɔtiibi kɔkɔ mun.

english_text:
Solomon Disobeys the Lord
1-2 The Lord did not want the Israelites to worship foreign gods, so he had warned them not to marry anyone who was not from Israel.
Solomon loved his wife, the daughter of the king of Egypt. But he also loved some women from Moab, Ammon, and Edom, and others from Sidon and the land of the Hittites. 3-4Seven hundred of his wives were daughters of kings, but he also married 300 other women.
As Solomon got older, some of his wives led him to worship their gods. He wasn't like his father David, who had worshiped only the Lord God. 5Solomon also worshiped Astarte the goddess of Sidon, and Milcom the disgusting god of Ammon. 6Solomon's father had obeyed the Lord with all his heart, but Solomon disobeyed and did what the Lord hated.
7Solomon built shrines on a hill east of Jerusalem to worship Chemosh the disgusting god of Moab, and Molech the disgusting god of Ammon. 8In fact, he built a shrine for each of his foreign wives, so all of them could burn incense and offer sacrifices to their own gods.
9-10The Lord God of Israel had appeared to Solomon two times and warned him not to worship foreign gods. But Solomon disobeyed and did it anyway. This made the Lord very angry, 11and he said to Solomon:
You did what you wanted and not what I told you to do. Now I'm going to take your kingdom from you and give it to one of your officials. 12But because David was your father, you will remain king as long as you live. I will wait until your son becomes king, then I will take the kingdom from him. 13When I do, I will still let him rule one tribe, because I have not forgotten that David was my servant and Jerusalem is my chosen city.
Hadad Becomes an Enemy of Solomon
14Hadad was from the royal family of Edom, and here is how the Lord made him Solomon's enemy:
15-16Some time earlier, when David conquered the nation of Edom, Joab his army commander went there to bury those who had died in battle. Joab and his soldiers stayed in Edom six months, and during that time they killed every man and boy who lived there.
17-19Hadad was a boy at the time, but he escaped to Midian with some of his father's officials. At Paran some other men joined them, and they went to the king of Egypt. The king liked Hadad and gave him food, some land, and a house, and even let him marry the sister of Queen Tahpenes. 20Hadad and his wife had a son named Genubath, and the queen let the boy grow up in the palace with her own children.
21When Hadad heard that David and Joab were dead, he said to the king, “Your Majesty, please let me go back to my own country.”
22“Why?” asked the king. “Do you want something I haven't given you?”
“No, I just want to go home.”
Rezon Becomes an Enemy of Solomon
23Here is how God made Rezon son of Eliada an enemy of Solomon:
Rezon had run away from his master, King Hadadezer of Zobah. 24-25He formed his own small army and became its leader after David had defeated Hadadezer's troops. Then Rezon and his army went to Damascus, where he became the ruler of Syria and an enemy of Israel.
Both Hadad and Rezon were enemies of Israel while Solomon was king, and they caused him a lot of trouble.
The Lord Makes a Promise to Jeroboam
26Jeroboam was from the town of Zeredah in Ephraim. His father Nebat had died, but his mother Zeruah was still alive. Jeroboam was one of Solomon's officials, but even he rebelled against Solomon. 27Here is how it happened:
While Solomon's workers were filling in the land on the east side of Jerusalem and repairing the city walls, 28Solomon noticed that Jeroboam was a hard worker. So he put Jeroboam in charge of the work force from Manasseh and Ephraim.
29-30One day when Jeroboam was leaving Jerusalem, he met Ahijah, a prophet from Shiloh. No one else was anywhere around. Suddenly, Ahijah took off his new coat and ripped it into twelve pieces. 31Then he said:
Jeroboam, take ten pieces of this coat and listen to what the Lord God of Israel says to you. “Jeroboam, I am the Lord God, and I am about to take Solomon's kingdom from him and give you ten tribes to rule. 32But Solomon will still rule one tribe, since he is the son of David my servant, and Jerusalem is my chosen city.
33“Solomon and the Israelites are not like their ancestor David. They will not listen to me, obey me, or do what is right. They have turned from me to worship Astarte the goddess of Sidon, Chemosh the god of Moab, and Milcom the god of Ammon.
34“Solomon is David's son, and David was my chosen leader, who did what I commanded. So I will let Solomon be king until he dies. 35Then I will give you ten tribes to rule, 36but Solomon's son will still rule one tribe. This way, my servant David will always have a descendant ruling in Jerusalem, the city where I have chosen to be worshiped.
37“You will be king of Israel and will rule every nation you want. 38I'll help you if you obey me. And if you do what I say, as my servant David did, I will always let someone from your family rule in Israel, just as someone from David's family will always rule in Judah. The nation of Israel will be yours.
39“I will punish the descendants of David, but not forever.”
40When Solomon learned what the Lord had told Jeroboam, Solomon tried to kill Jeroboam. But he escaped to King Shishak of Egypt and stayed there until Solomon died.
Solomon Dies
(2 Chronicles 9.29-31)
41Everything else Solomon did while he was king is written in the book about him and his wisdom. 42After he had ruled 40 years from Jerusalem, 43he died and was buried there in the city of his father David. His son Rehoboam then became king.
translation_text:
Saloomɔn fātì u-boon ki tīī Unimbɔti
(Kpèè 2 Kroo 11.18–12.1)
1Ubɔti Saloomɔn nìn cáá binicannimpoobi tikpil. U nín cáá Faaroo bisal boonee, u nìn gíti cáá Moowaab yab nì Amɔn yab nì Eedoom yab nì Siidɔn yab nì Eeti yab nimpoobi ki kútì. 2Ti-Dindaan nìn kpáafì Isirayeel yab atimbun gbanti nib pu ki lī yii: «Ní taa tīī-bi ni-bisalib ticati kí taa yòon̄ bi mun bisalib kí cáá, an yaa kaa sá míǹ bi làá yàntī ní nīn kíǹ ki tòotī bi-waaŋi.» Ama bíǹ ní Saloomɔn nìn néeń ki dū u-ba ki yá ki nákáǹ-bi. 3Saloomɔn nìn cáá binimpoobi alaataa aluli ní ki cáá bibɔntiibi alaataa ata. U-nimpoobi gbanti nìn yāntì u-pɔbil gáatì. 4Di sá yii ŋyunti ŋun Saloomɔn púĺee ní u-nimpoobee yāntì u cūtìi bíi tòotī awaa. Waa nìn gíti sí nì ti-Dindaan u-Nimbɔtiu deedee kii u-baa Daafiidee. 5Saloomɔn nìn kíǹ ki tòotī Siidɔn yab waal Asitaartee, nì Amɔn yab timbiiliwaal Miilkɔm. 6Saloomɔn nìn ŋá tin kaa nìn kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee, di sá yii waa nìn nóó ti-Dindaan nì dipɔbil diba kii u-baa Daafiidee. 7Áli gba Saloomɔn máń kuwaadii dijool din bí ki bíitiǹ Jeerusaleemee ki tīī Moowaab yab timbiiliwaal Keemoosi nì Amɔn yab timbiiliwaal Mooleeki. 8U nìn pée ŋá míǹ ní ki tīī u-nicannimpoobi kɔkɔ. Bi nìn tùutī talaalub ki kù tiwaŋkuti ki ŋáań saraabi ki tìì bi-waaŋi.
9Ti-Dindaan nìn gíí Saloomɔn pu diŋuul, kun puee u nìn fātì u-boon ki tīī úǹ Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu un nìn nyántì u-ba ki dàkā-u mili pu kɔkɔee. 10U nìn kpáafì-u ú taa nóó awaayee, ama Saloomɔn kaa nìn ŋá kii Unimbɔti nín nìn kpáafì-u puee. 11Niinee ní ti-Dindaan bí Saloomɔn yii: «A nín ŋá pu ní ki ŋá míǹ kaa ŋúb́ m-poondi nì m-marab bin m tīī-see, m làá fōō dibeel a-ŋaan, ní kí dū-dì kí tīī a-tɔntɔnliibi kansikin ubɔ. 12Ama a-baa Daafiidi puee, maa làá ŋá m nín bí yii m làá ŋá puee a-maŋfal wiiŋyi poon. M làá dāá fōō dibeel a-jipɔɔn ŋaan ní. 13Ama maa làá fōō dibeel kɔkɔ, Daafiidi m-tɔntɔnliu pu nì Jeerusaleem tiŋki kin m lēēyee puee, m làá kíń kunaakoou kubɔ kí tīī a-jipɔɔn.»
Saloomɔn pulincɔntiibi
14Ti-Dindaan nìn yāntì ueedoomja Adaadi, u sá Eedoom yab beecindin ubɔee yíkì ki bíi jáà nì Saloomɔn. 15Daafiidi yuntiŋuee, u nìn cūtìi jáń nì Eedoom yab. U-janjakpiliu Joowaab nìn cūtì kí síb́ Isirayeel yab bin bi nìn kūū kujaaunee ní ki kpáàa kūū Eedoom ninjab nì bi-bininjabiyaamu kɔkɔ. 16Di sá yii Joowaab nì Isirayeel yab bin nìn táá-uee nìn kāl̀ Eedoom tiŋkin iŋmal iluu ní áli ki dāa kūū ki céetì bi-ninjab nì bi-bininjabiyaamu kɔkɔ. 17Ama Adaadi un nìn dáá sá kinaacimpɔmbikee nì u-baa tɔntɔnliibi biba nìn ŋúń ki sáǹ ki cūtìi kāl̀ Eejipiti tiŋkin. 18U nìn yíkì Madiyan tiŋkin ní ki dūu dī Paraan teekun. Niinee ní u kpáaǹ Paraan yab biba ní bi nín cá ki tin bàn̄ Eejipiti bɔtiu Faaroo cee. Faaroo nìn tīī Adaadi kudii nì tikpaatan ní ki pōoǹ-u kí nīn kpīintí-u. 19Adaadi bɔti nìn fáatiǹ Faaroo ní úǹ dū u-nimpuu Tapaneesi naal ki tīī-u u cáá. 20Tapaneesi naal màl̄ Adaadi kibininjabiki ní ki pú-kì diyindi yii Geenubaati. Tapaneesi nìn yāntì kì bí dibeecindi ubɔti biyaamu kansikin ní u kpēē-kì.
21Adaadi bí Eejipiti mimmee ní ki gbìl̄ yii Daafiidi kpíì, ní ujanjakpil Joowaab mun kpíì. Niinee ní u bí Faaroo yii: «Yàntī ḿ nīn gítí m-tiŋkin.» 22Ní Faaroo bālifì-u yii: «Ba di lóò-si m-cee doo ní a nyàab̀ kí nīn gítí a-tiŋkin?» Ní u kíí yii: «Tiba kaa lóò-mi, sii dee yàntī ḿ nín cá.»
23Unimbɔti nìn gíti yāntì Eeliyadaa jipɔɔn Reesɔn jáń nì Saloomɔn. Reesɔn gbanti nìn sáǹ u-kpiliu Adadeeseer, Sooba bɔtiu ní. 24U nìn kóoǹ bininjab biba ki kpáfì u-cee ní ki kpántì bi-kpiliu. Daafiidi nín nìn kūū ki céetì Adadeeseer janjaliibi puee ní bíǹ sáǹ ki cūtìi kāl̀ Damaasi tiŋkin, ní ki dāa dūu kpántì Damaasi bɔtiu. 25Saloomɔn maŋfal wiiŋyi kɔkɔ poonee, Reesɔn nìn pée sá Isirayeel nannanliu ní, ní kí nín kūtì inikpiti in Adaadi nìn ŋá Isirayeel yabee. U nìn jíń dibeel Aram tiŋkin ní u-nimbil kaa nìn pée là kí wāl̀ Isirayeel yab.
Jeerooboowaam yíkìi jáń nì Saloomɔn
(2 Kroo 9.29-31)
26Neebaati jipɔɔn Jeerooboowaam nìn sá Eefiraayiim naakookun ní ki kóò Seereeda. U-na nìn sá ukpiipu ní bi yíì-u yii Seeruya. U nìn sá Saloomɔn tɔntɔnliu ní ki yíkìi bíi jáà nì ubɔti. 27Kun pu u nìn yíkì ki bíi jáà nì ubɔtee sɔ̀. Saloomɔn nìn bíi māā Miiloo diiku ní ki yāntì bi ŋéeb́ mbùń ŋun nìn bí u-baa Daafiidi Tiŋki gundi puee. 28Jeerooboowaam gbanti nìn dáá sá kinaacimpɔmbiki ki cáá difaŋgiil ki ŋūǹ ditundi tiŋan. Saloomɔn nìn ká yii u tūǹ ditundi tiŋan ní u lēē-u ú nīn kpèé Eefiraayiim nì Manasee naakɔti tɔntɔnliibi. 29Dalbee Jeerooboowaam nyáń Jeerusaleem kí nīn cée ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Ayiiya, usiilooja kíntì-u nsanni. Bi-liitil di nìn pée bí tisatin ní Ayiiya pēē dibɔkutikpaandi dipɔndi. 30Ayiiya cúú dibɔkutikpaandi dipɔndi din u nìn pēēyee ní ki cátì saalaa nì mili pu. 31Niinee ní u bí Jeerooboowaam yii: «Yòon̄ m nín cátì dibɔkutilee puee ajan saalaa, di sá yii ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Kpèè m làá fōō Saloomɔn ŋaan dibeel ní kí dū tinaakɔti saalaa kí tīī-si. 32M-tɔntɔnliu Daafiidi nì Jeerusaleem tiŋki kin m lēē Isirayeel naakɔti kɔkɔ kansikinee puee, m làá pée kíń-u kunaakɔbambaantiiu ní. 33M làá ŋá míǹ kun puee Isirayeel yab dū-mi ki fá, ní ki cūtìi bíi jáaḿ Siidɔn yab waal Asitaartee nì Moowaab yab waal Keemoosi nì Amɔn yab waal Miilkɔm. Baa nóó m-saŋŋu kí nīn ŋáań tin kítì m-nimbiinee, kaa tí ŋúb́ m-bɔkpaaŋi nì m-koobiliŋ kii u-baa Daafiidee. 34Nì míǹ kɔkɔee maa làá fōō dibeel Saloomɔn ŋaan, di sá yii m-tɔntɔnliu Daafiidi un m lēē ní u nìn ŋúb́ m-marab nì m-bɔkpaaŋee puee, m dū-u ki kāaǹ ú nīn sá ubɔti u-maŋfal wiiŋyi kɔkɔ poon ní. 35Ama m làá fōō dibeel u-jipɔɔn ŋaan ní kí dū tinaakɔti saalaa kí tīī-si. 36M làá kíń u-jipɔɔn kunaakoou kubɔ. Mimmee m-tɔntɔnliu Daafiidi làá nīn pée cáá naantiiu ubɔ kā dibeel pu Jeerusaleem tiŋkin. Di sá yii kitiŋ kin ní m lēē kí nīn lèekī m-ba ki dàkèe dee. 37Siiyee, m làá tīī-si dibeel kii a nín là puee. A làá jī Isirayeel tiŋki pu dibeel. 38A yaa pílifì tin ní m làá tùkù-see, ki yaa nóó m-saŋŋu, ki yaa ŋáań tin kítèe m-nimbiin, ki ŋúb́ m-bɔkpaaŋi nì m-marab kii m-tɔntɔnliu Daafiidi nín nìn ŋúb́ puee, m làá nīn bí a-cee, ní kí yàntī a-kpátam boonee, a-naantiibi ń nīn pée kā dibeel kii Daafiidi yab nín bí puee. M làá dū Isirayeel tiŋki kí ŋá a-ŋaan. 39M làá dáaĺ Daafiidi naantiibi tafal, ama maa làá dáaĺ bi-tafal kí nīn cá jaanjaan.>»
40Saloomɔn béè mimmee ní ki nyàab̄ kí kpɔ̀ Jeerooboowaam. Úǹ béè mimmee ní ki sáǹ ki nín cá Eejipiti ki tin kɔ́ Eejipiti bɔtiu Siisaaki pu, ki dāa sāā ŋyunti ŋun ní Saloomɔn kpíìyee.
Saloomɔn kúm
41Bi ŋmàn̄ Saloomɔn maam, tin kɔkɔ u ŋée nì u-ciiŋyi bɔti kɔkɔ ki ŋá Saloomɔn Tuuŋŋi Gbɔŋku poon. 42Saloomɔn nìn kāl̀ Jeerusaleem ki jíń Isirayeel tiŋki kɔkɔ pu dibeel abin imuŋku ili ní. 43Saloomɔn kpíì ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ u-naanjab ní bi síb́-u u-baa Daafiidi Tiŋkin. U-jipɔɔn Rooboowaam di fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.

english_text:
Some of the People Rebel against Rehoboam
(2 Chronicles 10.1-19)
1Rehoboam went to Shechem where everyone was waiting to crown him king.
2Jeroboam son of Nebat heard what was happening, and he stayed in Egypt, where he had gone to hide from Solomon. 3But the people from the northern tribes of Israel sent for him. Then together they went to Rehoboam and said, 4“Your father Solomon forced us to work very hard. But if you make our work easier, we will serve you and do whatever you ask.”
5“Give me three days to think about it,” Rehoboam replied, “then come back for my answer.” So the people left.
6Rehoboam went to some leaders who had been his father's senior officials, and he asked them, “What should I tell these people?”
7They answered, “If you want them to serve and obey you, then you should do what they ask today. Tell them you will make their work easier.”
8But Rehoboam refused their advice and went to the younger men who had grown up with him and were now his officials. 9He asked, “What do you think I should say to these people who asked me to make their work easier?”
10His younger advisors said:
Here's what we think you should say to them: “Compared to me, my father was weak. 11He made you work hard, but I'll make you work even harder. He punished you with whips, but I'll use whips with pieces of sharp metal!”
12Three days later, Jeroboam and the others came back. 13Rehoboam ignored the advice of the older advisors. 14He spoke bluntly and told them exactly what his own advisors had suggested: “My father made you work hard, but I'll make you work even harder. He punished you with whips, but I'll use whips with pieces of sharp metal!”
15-19 When the people realized that Rehoboam would not listen to them, they shouted: “We don't have to be loyal to David's family. We can do what we want. Come on, people of Israel, let's go home! Rehoboam can rule his own people.”
Adoniram was in charge of the forced labor, and Rehoboam sent him to talk to the people. But they stoned him to death. Then Rehoboam ran to his chariot and hurried back to Jerusalem.
So the people from the northern tribes of Israel went home, leaving Rehoboam to rule only the people from the towns in Judah. Ever since that day, the people of Israel have opposed David's family in Judah. All of this happened just as the Lord's prophet Ahijah had told Jeroboam.
20When the Israelites heard that Jeroboam was back, they called everyone together. Then they sent for Jeroboam and made him king of Israel. Only the people from the tribe of Judah remained loyal to David's family.
Shemaiah Warns Rehoboam
(2 Chronicles 11.1-4)
21After Rehoboam returned to Jerusalem, he decided to attack Israel and take control of the whole country. So he called together 180,000 soldiers from the tribes of Judah and Benjamin.
22Meanwhile, God told Shemaiah the prophet 23to give Rehoboam and everyone from Judah and Benjamin this warning: 24“Don't go to war against the people from Israel—they are your relatives. Go home! I am the Lord, and I made these things happen.”
Rehoboam and his army obeyed the Lord and went home.
Jeroboam Makes Religious Changes
25Jeroboam rebuilt Shechem in Ephraim and made it a stronger town, then he moved there. He also fortified the town of Penuel.
26-27One day, Jeroboam started thinking, “Everyone in Israel still goes to the temple in Jerusalem to offer sacrifices to the Lord. What if they become loyal to David's family again? They will kill me and accept Rehoboam as their king.”
28 Jeroboam asked for advice and then made two gold statues of calves. He showed them to the people and said, “Listen everyone! You won't have to go to Jerusalem to worship anymore. Here are your gods who rescued you from Egypt.” 29Then he put one of the gold calves in the town of Bethel and the other in the town of Dan. 30The people sinned because they started going to these places to worship.
31Jeroboam built small places of worship at the shrines and appointed men who were not from the tribe of Levi to serve as priests. 32-33 He also decided to start a new festival for the Israelites on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, just like the one in Judah. On that day, Jeroboam went to Bethel and offered sacrifices on the altar to the gold calf he had put there. Then he assigned the priests their duties.
translation_text:
Siikeem kooŋyi
(Kpèè 2 Kroo 10.1-15)
1Rooboowaam nìn cūtì Siikeem, di sá yii niin ní Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nìn kóoǹ ki kpáfì kí kàan̄-u dibeel. 2Neebaati jipɔɔn Jeerooboowaam nìn dáá gbíntìi bíń Eejipiti tiŋkin, laakin u nìn sáǹ ubɔti Saloomɔn ki cūtìi kāl̀ee. U nín gbìl̄ Siikeem kooŋyi gbanti puee ní u gbíntì Eejipiti niin. 3Ama ní bi tú binib bi cūtìi yíiń-u. U bāańee ní u nì Isirayeel beel samaau kɔkɔ bí Rooboowaam yii: 4«A-baa nìn túǹ-ti ditúndi din nyìm̀ee. Siiyee, ti là yii á bàtī-ti ditumpɔɔl din a-baa nìn yāntì ti túńee nì diwaŋgul din u nìn dūu nyīkiǹ ti-puee. A yaa ŋá míǹ ti kíí kí nīn sá a-tɔntɔnliibi.» 5Ní u kíí-bi yii: «Nín̄ cámaan, iwiin ita dalee ní fàtīí gítiń.»
U lī mimmee ní samaa nín cá. 6Niinee ní Rooboowaam bālifì bitindaŋkpilib bin nìn bí u-baa Saloomɔn tundin ŋyunti ŋun u nìn dáá bí dimaŋfalinee yii: «Ni sáŋkí-mi ḿ kíí binib nee yii ba?» 7Ní bikpilibee bí-u yii: «Díǹ nee, a yaa kíí kí nīn sá binib nee tɔntɔnliu ní ki kíí-bi kinyɔɔmɔɔyee, bi làá nīn sá a-tɔntɔnliibi kí nīn cá jaanjaan.» 8Ama ní Rooboowaam kaa dū bikpilibee saŋkii ki túń ditundi, ní ki yíiń binipɔmbi u nì bin jíń tinaacimpɔn dicilpu bi bí u-tundinee. 9U nìn bí bíǹ yii: «Nimbi fáà, ni sáŋkí-mi yii ba? Ḿ kíí binib bin bíi bàlifī-mi ḿ bàtī diwaŋgul din m-baa nìn dūu túǹ-bee nyiŋfiŋu pu yii ba?» 10Ní binipɔmbi u nì bin kpáfìi jíń tinaacimpɔnee kíí-u yii: «Kpèè a nín làá kíí binib bin dɔ́miń ki bí-si yii: <A-baa nìn túǹ-ti diwaŋgul din nyìm̀ee, siiyee bàtī di-nyiŋfiŋu pu kí tīī-ti> puee sɔ̀: <M-ŋambikpakpalii gbìfiǹ m-baa ŋal. 11M-baa yaa nìn túǹ-ni diwaŋgul din nyìm̀ee, man làá gíti kūtì diwaŋgul gbanti nyiŋfiŋu pu. M-baa nìn dū anaalab ní ki dáaĺ ni-tafal, mamee, m làá dū anaalab ŋin cáá agatee ní kí dáaĺ ni-tafal.>»
12Ŋwintataati dalee Jeerooboowaam nì samaa dɔ́miń ki ká Rooboowaam kii úǹ u-ba nín nìn lī puee yii: «Fàtīí gítiḿmaan ŋwintataati dal kí ká-mee.» 13Bikpilib nín nìn sáŋkì u-bɔti puee, waa dūu túń ditundi, ní ki sòon̄ nì samaa an pɔ̄ɔ̄. 14Binipɔmbee nín nìn sáŋkì-u puee, míǹ ní u dūu sòon̄ nì binibee. U bí-bi yii: «M-baa yaa nìn túǹ-ni diwaŋgul din nyìm̀ee, man làá gíti kūtì diwaŋgul gbanti nyiŋfiŋu pu. M-baa nìn dū anaalab ní ki dáaĺ ni-tafal, mamee, m làá dū anaalab ŋin cáá agatee ní kí dáaĺ ni-tafal.» 15Ubɔti kaa nìn pílifiǹ binibee, kun puee ti-Dindaan di nìn bɔ́ntì míǹ kí ŋmā kí ŋá kii u nín nìn dī u-bɔnaatiliu usiilooja Ayiiya pu ki pōoǹ Neebaati jipɔɔn Jeerooboowaam puee ní.
Isirayeel beel cúu yākatì
(Kpèè 2 Kroo 10.16–11.4)
16Isirayeel yab nín ká yii ubɔti kaa bíi pílifíǹ-bee ní bi bí-u yii:
«Ti nì Daafiidi cáá tilati?
Ti nì Jeesee jipɔɔn kaa cáá mpèé ŋubɔ!
Isirayeel yab, tí nīn gítímaan ti-tantibin!
Kɔŋkɔnnee sii Daafiidi, nín̄ jīǹ a-dicaŋku pu dibeel!»
Bi lī mimmee ní báà ŋma nín gítí u-tantiun. 17Ama Isirayeel yab bin nìn kóò Juuda tiŋkinee baba pu ní Rooboowaam nìn nìkī ki jíń dibeel. 18Nì míǹ kɔkɔee ubɔti Rooboowaam nìn dū Adooram un kpèé diwɔ́bil tuuŋŋee ki tú Isirayeel yab cee, ama ní bíǹ yáŋkì-u ataŋkpee ki kūū. Niinee ní ubɔti Rooboowaam ŋá malaa ki jɔ́m̀ u-tɔrɔkuu poon ki sáǹ ki nín cá Jeerusaleem. 19Kí yòon̄ ŋwiin gbanti ní Isirayeel yab bin kóò ŋgan pú beelinee kíĺ ki jáà nì Daafiidi dicaŋku bɔtiibi. Kujaau gbanti bí ki dāa sāā díǹ.
20Ŋyunti ŋun Isirayeel yab bin kɔkɔ kóò ŋgan pú beelinee gbìl̄ yii Jeerooboowaam fātìi gítìńee, ní bi kóoǹ samaa kɔkɔ ki kpáfì ní ki tú ki yíiń-u ní ki dū-u ki kāaǹ bi-pu ubɔti. Juuda naakooku baba yab di nìn pée síl̀ nì Daafiidi dicaŋku deedee.
21Ŋyunti ŋun Rooboowaam bàn̄ Jeerusaleemee ní u kóoǹ Juuda nì Beenjameen naakɔti janjaliibi bimɔmmɔntiibi kutukub imuŋku ili nì saalaa ki kpáfì kí cùú já nì Isirayeel yab, án nín làá ŋá pu úǹ Saloomɔn jipɔɔn ń fàtīí fōō dibeelee. 22Ama ní Unimbɔti bí u-bɔnaatiliu Seemaya yii: 23«Tùkù Juuda bɔtiu Rooboowaam, Saloomɔn jipɔɔn nì Juuda nì Beenjameen naakɔtin yab nì samaa un kɔkɔ pée kíǹee yii, 24ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Naa máaǹ kí cùú já nì ni-nabiyaamu Isirayeel yab. Báà ŋma ń nīn gítí u-dumpu, di sá yii man di yāntì tin bíi jītí nee bāań.>» Niinee ní bi gbìl̄ ki tīī nì ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi ní ki nín gítí bi-dumpui.
25Jeerooboowaam nìn máń digundi ki tú Siikeem tiŋki kin bí Eefiraayiim jooŋŋi puee, ki kíǹ ki kóò niin. Boonee ní u dāa yíkì niin ki cūtìi máń digundi ki tú Peenuyeel tiŋki.
Jeerooboowaam kpitii
26Jeerooboowaam nìn lī u-neen yii: «An nín bíi jītí pu nee, Daafiidi dicaŋku dāa ŋūǹ kí fàtīí fōō dibeel. 27Di sá yii binib nee yaa gbíntìi cáà Jeerusaleem ki ŋáań saraabi ti-Dindaan Diikunee, bi-pɔbiliŋ làá fàtīí gítí bi-kpiliu Juuda bɔtiu Rooboowaam cee. Bi làá dāá kpɔ̀-mi ní kí fàtīí gítí Juuda bɔtiu Rooboowaam cee.» 28Niinee ní ubɔti Jeerooboowaam ká nlandɔkɔ ní ki yāntì bi dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́-u anabil ali, ní u bí samaa yii: «Ni jɔ́m̀ Jeerusaleem tiŋkin ki gīī Isirayeel yab, kpèèmaan ni-Nimbɔtiu un nyántìń-ni Eejipiti tiŋkinee.» 29U ŋá mimmee ní ki dū dinabil diba ki síiǹ Beeteel tiŋkin ní ki dū din kíǹee ki síiǹ Daani tiŋkin. 30U nín ŋá pu ki yāntì samaa ŋá ikpitee dee. Di sá yii binib tikpil nìn pá dinabililiitiil boon ki tin bàn̄ Daani tiŋkin.
31Jeerooboowaam nìn gíti yāntì bi máń awaadiin ŋgbantamu pu, ní ki nìn lēē bin kaa sá Leefii yabee bí nīn sá bisaraaŋaliibi. 32Dibindi poon ŋmaniniitiu iwiin saalku dalee ní Jeerooboowaam yāntì bi jíń jiŋaal kii un bi jīǹ Juuda tiŋkinee, ní úǹ u-ba ŋá saraabi nsaraafan pu. U nìn ŋá míǹ mbaantiim Beeteel ki ŋá saraabi ki tīī anabil ŋin u nìn mɔ́ɔ́yee. U nìn kāaǹ bisaraaŋaliibi ŋgbantamu mun bí Beeteel u bɔ́ntì mu-pu bí nīn ŋáań saraabee. 33Dibindi poon ŋmaniniitiu, iwiin saalku dalee ní u yíiń samaa kɔkɔ bí jī jiŋaal Beeteel. Ŋwiin gbantee, úǹ di gāā u-bindi ki lēē-ŋu. Jiŋaal gbanti yuntiŋuee, úǹ u-ba di nìn pée ŋá saraa nsaraafan ŋun u nìn yāntì bi máńee pu.

english_text:
A Prophet Condemns the Altar at Bethel
1-2 One day, Jeroboam was standing at the altar in Bethel, ready to make an offering. Suddenly one of God's prophets arrived from Judah and shouted:
The Lord sent me with a message about this altar. A child named Josiah will be born into David's family. He will sacrifice on this altar the priests who make offerings here, and human bones will be burned on it.
3You will know that the Lord has said these things when the altar splits in half, and the ashes on it fall to the ground.
4Jeroboam pointed at the prophet and shouted, “Grab him!” But at once, Jeroboam's hand became stiff, and he could not move it. 5The altar split in half, and the ashes fell to the ground, just as the prophet had warned.
6“Please pray to the Lord your God and ask him to heal my hand,” Jeroboam begged.
The prophet prayed, and Jeroboam's hand was healed.
7“Come home with me and eat something,” Jeroboam said. “I want to give you a gift for what you have done.”
8“No, I wouldn't go with you, even if you offered me half of your kingdom. I won't eat or drink here either. 9The Lord said I can't eat or drink anything and that I can't go home the same way I came.” 10Then he started home down a different road.
An Old Prophet from Bethel
11At that time an old prophet lived in Bethel, and one of his sons told him what the prophet from Judah had said and done.
12“Show me which way he went,” the old prophet said, and his sons pointed out the road. 13“Put a saddle on my donkey,” he told them. After they did, he got on the donkey 14and rode off to look for the prophet from Judah.
