2The chief officer there with the king replied, “I don't believe it! Even if the Lord sent a rainstorm, it couldn't produce that much grain by tomorrow.”
“You will see it happen, but you won't eat any of the food,” Elisha warned him.
The Syrian Army Stops Its Attack
3About the same time, four men with leprosy were just outside the gate of Samaria. They said to each other, “Why should we sit here, waiting to die? 4There's nothing to eat in the city, so we would starve if we went inside. But if we stay out here, we will die for sure. Let's sneak over to the Syrian army camp and surrender. They might kill us, but they might not.” 5-8That evening the four men got up and left for the Syrian camp.
As they walked toward the camp, the Lord caused the Syrian troops to hear what sounded like the roar of a huge cavalry. The soldiers said to each other, “Listen! The king of Israel must have hired Hittite and Egyptian troops to attack us. Let's get out of here!” So they ran out of their camp that night, leaving their tents and horses and donkeys.
When the four men with leprosy reached the edge of the Syrian camp, no one was there. They walked into one of the tents, where they ate and drank, before carrying off clothes, as well as silver and gold. They hid all this, then walked into another tent; they took what they wanted and hid it too.
9They said to each other, “This isn't right. Today is a day to celebrate, and we haven't told anyone else what has happened. If we wait until morning, we will be punished. Let's go to the king's palace at once and tell the good news.”
10They went back to Samaria and shouted up to the guards at the gate, “We've just come from the Syrian army camp, and all the soldiers are gone! The tents are empty, and the horses and donkeys are still tied up. We didn't see or hear anybody.”
11The guards reported the news to the king's palace. 12The king got out of bed and said to his officers, “I know what those Syrians are doing. They know we're starving, so they're hiding in the fields, hoping we will go out to look for food. When we do, they can capture us and take over our city.”
13One of his officers replied, “We have a few horses left—why don't we let some men take five of them and go to the Syrian camp and see what's happening? We're going to die anyway like those who have already died.” 14They found two chariots, and the king commanded the men to find out what had happened to the Syrian troops.
15The men rode as far as the Jordan River. All along the way they saw clothes and equipment that the Syrians had thrown away as they escaped. Then they went back to the king and told him what they had seen.
16At once the people went to the Syrian camp and carried off what was left. They took so much that a large sack of flour and two large sacks of barley sold for almost nothing, just as the Lord had promised.
17The king of Israel had put his chief officer in charge of the gate, but he died when the people trampled him as they rushed out of the city. 18Earlier, when the king was at Elisha's house, Elisha had told him that flour or barley would sell for almost nothing. 19But the officer refused to believe that even the Lord could do that. So Elisha warned him that he would see it happen, but would not eat any of the food. 20And that's exactly what happened—the officer was trampled to death.
translation_text:
1Eeliisee kíí yii: «Ní pīlifìmaan ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi. Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ yii: <Fool naŋkɔnampuee, bi làá fu dā ŋyim kiiloobi saalaa nì bili àá ɔɔji yim kiiloobi mmuŋku nì binaa animbil kúti jitɔn ubɔ ní Samaarii nyɔŋkin.>»
2Niinee ní ubɔti kpambal un nìn cēentí-u laakin kamaa ní u yaa nìn cée bí yii: «Báà ti-Dindaan yaa cúú kutagbɔŋu tɔkɔlab ki pīitì, tin a sòon̄ nee ŋūǹ kí bàń mimmaaa?» Ní Eeliisee bí yii: «Too! A-nimbil làá ká tin m sòon̄ nee, ama a kpá kí dáká tijin gbanti.»
Siirii yab sáǹ ki fá bi-janjanaapaal
3 Binyaŋgbantiibi binaa biba nìn bí kitiŋ kpaanceetiŋu kaa dátiǹ kipunyɔkɔ. Ní bi bí tɔb yii: «Ba pu ní tí nīn kā doo ki cí ŋkúm? 4Ti yaa bí yii ti làá kɔ́ kitiŋin, ti làá kpú kun puee tijin kaa ti bí niin. Ti yaa tí kā dooyaaa, ti làá kpú. Mimmee taa pùtì cá Siirii yab janjanaapaal puɔɔɔ? Bi yaa kaa kūū-ti ki yāntì ti bí dimaŋfalinaaa, ti-yimɔɔl dee. Bi yaa ti kūū-taaa, tí kpú.»
5Kujoou jóotèe ní bi yíkì ki nín cá Siirii yab janjanaapaal pu. Bi bàn̄ Siirii yab janjanaapaal puee, báà ubɔ kpá niin.
6Tin jítì Siirii yab janjanaapaal puee di sá yii ti-Dindaan nìn yāntì bi gbìl̄ janjatɔrɔkub nì itaamu nì dijanjakitikpaandi wooku pu. Niinee ní Siirii yab lī tɔb cee yii: «Isirayeel bɔtiu tīī Eeti yab nì Eejipiti yab bɔtiibi animbil ní bi cáań bi-janjaliibi kí tɔ̄ ti-pu.» 7Kunyeeu gbantee ní bi yíkìi sáǹ ki fá bi-tantib nì bi-taamui nì bi-mammu nì bi-naapaal nín pée bí puee kɔkɔ, di sá yii bi nìn sáń kí fīī bi-ba ní.
8Binyaŋgbantiibee yìin̄ dinaapaal pu míǹ ki dóòyee ní bi jítìi kɔ́ tanti ubɔ poon ní ki jíń ki nyùn̄. Bi ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki kóoǹ animbil nì sindaariya nì tiwampeeŋkaal tin bí niinee ki cáa cūnnì ki bál̀ laaba. Bi gítìńee ní ki kɔ́ tanti ubɔ mun poon ki tí kóoǹ tin kɔkɔ bí u-poonee ki cáa cūnnì ki bál̀.
Bijanjaliibi bin māntìi tú kitiŋee yíkì ŋkùm mun kúntì
9Niinee ní bi kíĺ ki bíi lì tɔb cee yii: «Kun ti bíi ŋáańee kaa kítì. Díǹ wiiŋŋu sá tibɔmɔntiil wiiŋŋu ní. Ti yaa kaa lī tiba ní ki cíitì kutaa wúntèe, taa làá lóó ditafadaaldi. Tí nīn cámaan. Tí kɔ́maan kitiŋin kí dū tibɔti nee kí māafì ubɔti cindin yab.» 10Bi lī mimmee ní ki nín gítiń kitiŋin ní ki yíiń bin cí kitiŋ punyɔkɔkee ki dū tibɔtee ki máafì-bi. Bi bí-bi yii: «Ti cūtì Siirii yab janjanaapaal pu kaa ká báà uniseen, kaa gbìl̄ báà unil neen pu. Kun ti pée kée di sá itaamu nì mmamu gbìn̄ ní tantib sí fám.» 11Niinee bipunyɔɔciitiliibee yíiń ubɔ ú dū tibɔtee kí māafì ubɔti cindin yab.
12Ubɔti yíkì kunyeeuee ní ki bí u-kàliŋkpilib yii: «M làá tùkù-ni kun ní Siirii yab bíi bɔ́ntí ti-puee. Bi nyí ŋkùm nín cáá-tee, an pu ní bi yíkì bi-janjanaapaal pu ki cūtìi bál̀ tisatin ki lī tɔb cee yii: <Bin bí kitiŋinee làá nyānní ní tí cúú-bi binifoobi ní kí kɔ́ bi-tiŋkin.>» 13Ubɔti kàliŋkpilibee kansikin ubɔ fōō dinyɔɔbundi ki lī yii: «Tí yòon̄ itaamu in kíǹ kitiŋinee poon iŋmoo, di sá yii báà i yaa pée báaa, i làá pée kpú kii kitiŋ nee nib kɔkɔee ní. Ti yaa lēē-i mimmee ní tí dū binikaaŋkaabi kí tɔ̄ bí cùú kpèè tin di bíi jītí niinee.» 14Niinee ní bi yōoǹ tɔrɔkub bili ki dūu kpàl̄ bi-taamui ní ubɔti lēē bijanjaliibi ki dū-bi ki tú bí cùú nyàab̀ Siirii yab janjaliibi nín bí laakiŋyee kí kpáàa kpèè tin di bíi jītée. 15Bi páaǹ bi-boon ki tin bàn̄ Jɔɔdan buŋŋu. Bi nín cée bi ká tiwampeeŋkaal nì tiwan tin Siirii yab dūu fá fá kí ŋmā kí sāǹ malaa malaayee. Ituunee gítìńee ní ki dū tin bi kée ki dūu máafì ubɔti.
16Niinee Samaarii yab nyáń ki cūtìi fúkúl̀ Siirii yab janjanaapaal. Kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn lī puee, bi nìn dá ŋyim kiiloobi saalaa nì bili àá ɔɔji yim kiiloobi mmuŋku nì binaa animbil jitɔn ubɔ ní. 17Ubɔti nìn dū kitiŋ punyɔkɔki ki ŋá u-janjakpiliu un nìn cēentí-u laakin kamaa u yaa nìn cée ŋaan yii ú nīn kpèé. Ama binib nìn tàn̄ tàn̄-u ki nákáǹ kipunyɔkɔ ní u kpíì kii Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Eeliisee nín nìn lī puee. Ubɔti nín nìn dɔ́miń u-ceeyee, tin ní u nìn lēe dee.
18Tiŋman, Eeliisee nìn sòon̄ nì ubɔti ki bí-u yii: «Fool naŋkɔnampu, bi làá fu dā ŋyim kiiloobi saalaa nì bili àá ɔɔji yim kiiloobi mmuŋku nì binaa animbil kúti jitɔn ubɔ ní Samaarii nyɔŋkin.» 19Ubɔti janjakpiliuee nìn kíí Eeliisee yii: «Báà ti-Dindaan yaa cúú kutagbɔŋu tɔkɔlab ki pīitì, tin a sòon̄ nee ŋūǹ kí bàń mimmaaa?» Ní Eeliisee nìn kíí yii: «Too! A-nimbil làá ká tin m sòon̄ nee, ama a kpá kí dáká tijin gbanti.» 20Eeliisee nín nìn lī puee, míǹ deedee di jítì: binib nìn tàn̄ tàn̄ ubɔti janjakpiliuee ki nákáǹ kipunyɔkɔpu ní u kpíì.

english_text:
The Woman from Shunem Is Given Back Her Land
1 Elisha told the woman whose son he had brought back to life, “The Lord has warned that there will be no food here for seven years. Take your family and go live somewhere else for a while.” 2The woman did exactly what Elisha had said and went to live in Philistine territory.
She and her family lived there seven years. 3Then she returned to Israel and immediately begged the king to give back her house and property.
4Meanwhile, the king was asking Gehazi the servant of Elisha about the amazing things Elisha had been doing. 5While Gehazi was telling him that Elisha had brought a dead boy back to life, the woman and her son arrived.
“Here's the boy, Your Majesty,” Gehazi said. “And this is his mother.”
6The king asked the woman to tell her story, and she told him everything that had happened. He then said to one of his officials, “I want you to make sure that this woman gets back everything that belonged to her, including the money her crops have made since the day she left Israel.”
Hazael Kills Benhadad
7Some time later Elisha went to the capital city of Damascus to visit King Benhadad of Syria, who was sick. And when Benhadad was told he was there, 8he said to Hazael, “Go meet with Elisha the man of God and get him to ask the Lord if I will get well. And take along a gift for him.”
9Hazael left with forty camel loads of the best things made in Damascus as a gift for Elisha. He found the prophet and said, “Your servant, King Benhadad, wants to know if he will get well.”
10“Tell him he will,” Elisha said to Hazael. “But the Lord has already told me that Benhadad will definitely die.” 11Elisha stared at him until Hazael was embarrassed, then Elisha began crying.
12“Sir, why are you crying?” Hazael asked.
Elisha answered, “Because I know the terrible things you will do to the people of Israel. You will burn down their walled cities and slaughter their young men. You will even crush the heads of their babies and rip open their pregnant women.”
13 “How could I ever do anything like that?” Hazael replied. “I'm only a servant and don't have that kind of power.”
“Hazael, the Lord has told me that you will be the next king of Syria.”
14Hazael went back to Benhadad and told him, “Elisha said that you will get well.” 15But the very next day, Hazael got a thick blanket; he soaked it in water and held it over Benhadad's face until he died. Hazael then became king.
King Jehoram of Judah
(2 Chronicles 21.2-20)
16Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat became king of Judah in Joram's fifth year as king of Israel, while Jehoshaphat was still king of Judah. 17Jehoram was 32 years old when he became king, and he ruled 8 years from Jerusalem.
18Jehoram disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong. He married Ahab's daughter and was as sinful as Ahab's family and the kings of Israel. 19 But the Lord refused to destroy Judah, because he had promised his servant David that someone from his family would always rule in Judah.
20 While Jehoram was king, the people of Edom rebelled and chose their own king. 21So Jehoram and his cavalry marched to Zair, where the Edomite army surrounded him and his commanders. During the night he attacked the Edomites, but he was defeated, and his troops escaped to their homes. 22Judah was never able to regain control of Edom. Even the town of Libnah rebelled at that time.
23Everything else Jehoram did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah. 24Jehoram died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem. His son Ahaziah then became king.
King Ahaziah of Judah
(2 Chronicles 22.1-6)
25Ahaziah son of Jehoram became king of Judah in the twelfth year of Joram's rule in Israel. 26Ahaziah was 22 years old when he became king, and he ruled from Jerusalem for only one year. His mother was Athaliah, a granddaughter of King Omri of Israel. 27Since Ahaziah was related to Ahab's family, he acted just like them and disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong.
28Ahaziah went with King Joram of Israel to attack King Hazael and the Syrian troops at Ramoth in Gilead. Joram was wounded in that battle, 29so he went to the town of Jezreel to recover. Ahaziah went there to visit him.
translation_text:
Usuneennimpuee bɔti nín kúntì puee
1Dalbee ní Eeliisee sòon̄ nì unimpu un biki u nìn fīkitèe ki bí-u yii: «Yīkì doo, sii nì a-dicaŋku kí nīn cá laakin ni yaa ŋūǹee kí kàl̄. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan bɔ́ntì kí cáań ŋkùm Isirayeel tiŋki pu. Án kaa ti làá yúntí ŋkùmee làá kíĺ ní kí ŋá abin aluli.» 2Ní Unimpuee yíkì ki ŋá kii Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu nín bí-u yii ú ŋá puee. U nì u-dicaŋku kɔkɔ nìn yíkì ní ki cūtìi kāl̀ Fiiliistii yab tiŋkin ki ŋá abin aluli. 3Abin aluli boonee ní unimpuee nyánní Fiiliistii yab tiŋkin ki fātìi gítìń. U bāańee ní ki cūtìi ká ubɔti ní ki mēē-u yii ú fōō u-diiku nì u-kpaatanti kí tīī-u.
4Ŋyunti gbantee, ubɔti nì Eeliisee tɔntɔnliu Geeyaasii di nìn bíi sòoǹ. Ubɔti nìn bí-u yii: «Māafì-mi atuŋkpaan ŋin kɔkɔ ní Eeliisee ŋáaǹee!» 5Geeyaasii nìn bíi máafí ubɔti Eeliisee nín fīkitì utaŋkpiil ubɔ puee, kpalaayee unimpu un biki Eeliisee nìn fīkitèe dūu kɔ́ní ubɔti cee kí gbàam̀-u ú fōō u-diiku nì u-kpaatanti kí tīī-u. Niinee Geeyaasii téeń yii: «Ti-baa ubɔti, kpèè unimpu un jipɔɔn Eeliisee nìn fīkitèe nì u-jipɔɔnee sɔ̀!» 6Ubɔti nìn bālifì unimpuee ní úǹ dū tibɔtee ki máafì-u. Niinee ní ubɔti dū unimpuee bɔti ki ŋá u-janjakpiliu ubɔ ŋaan ki lī yii: «M là yii bí fàtīí gíiǹ u-wanti kɔkɔ kí tīī-u, ní kí pà-u bi nín túń ditundi u-kpaatanti pu ki ká ipaati iŋyee kɔkɔ kí yòon̄ daliŋkin u yíkèe kí dāá sāā díǹ nee.»
Eeliisee nì Asayeel bɔti
7Dalbee Eeliisee yíkì ki nín cá Damaasi tiŋkin. Ŋyunti gbantee Siirii bɔtiu Been-Adaadi būǹ. Ní bi tùkū-u yii: «Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu dɔ́miń doo.» 8Ní ubɔti bí Asayeel yii: «Nyàab̀ tiwampɔkaal kí cáá pɔ̄ Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Eeliisee kí kpáàa gbàam̀-u ú bàlifì ti-Dindaan kí kpèè yii m làá ká dicáaǹdaaa, maa làá ká.»
9Ní Asayeel yíkì ki nín cá ki cūtìi ká Eeliisee. U nìn yōoǹ tiwammɔntiil tin bí Damaasi tiŋkinee ki túǹ igutaamu imuŋku ili kí cáá pɔ̄ Eeliisee. U bàn̄ ki síl̀ Eeliisee nimbiinee ní ki bí-u yii: «A-tɔntɔnliu Siirii bɔtiu Been-Adaadi di túnní-mi a-cee ḿ bàlifì-si yii u làá pɔ̄ɔkàaa, waa làá pɔ̄ɔkì.» 10Ní Eeliisee kíí-u yii: «Cùú tùkù-u yii u làá pɔ̄ɔkì. Ama tiŋman puee ti-Dindaan lēē ki dàkā-mi yii u bàà làá kpú ní.»
11Kpalaayee Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Eeliisee kíĺ ki bíi kpèé Asayeel címmm áli icoo dāa kpáàa cúú-u, ní Eeliisee kíĺ ki bíi sūǹ. 12Ní Asayeel bālifì-u yii: «M-kpiliu, ba pu ní a bíi sūǹ ní?» Ní Eeliisee kíí yii: «M sūǹ kun puee m nyí inikpiti in a làá dāá ŋá Isirayeel yabee. A làá dāá tūū bi-timmu mun bi máń agun ki túee ŋŋmi, kí dāá làntī bi-naacimpɔmbiyaamu, ní kí dāá tāā tāā kí mátí bi-biyaamu ní kí dāá pùtī bi-nimpoobi bin sá bipɔdambee.» 13Ní Asayeel bí yii: «Mana ní man a-tɔntɔnliu un bí kii kibɔgbaŋfii nee làá dāá ŋmā kí ŋá míǹ?» Ní Eeliisee kíí-u yii: «Ti-Dindaan lēē ki dàkā-mi yii a làá dāá kpántí Siirii bɔtiu.»
14Asayeel yíkì Eeliisee ceeyee ní ki nín gítí u-kpiliu cee. U bàn̄ee ní u-kpiliu bālifì-u yii: «Eeliisee tùkūń-si yii ba?» Ní u kíí yii: «U bí-mi yii a làá ŋmátí.» 15Ama kutaa wúntèe ní Asayeel yōoǹ ŋŋaabu ki dūu ŋá nnyimin ní ki dūu bīiǹ ubɔti nimbiin waa ti ŋūǹ kí fòotī. Ubɔti kpíìyee ní Asayeel fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.
Juuda bɔtiu Jooram bɔti
(2 Kroo 21.2-20)
16Akaab jipɔɔn Jooram nín kāl̀ Isirayeel beelin tibɔtiil dibiŋŋmooŋmootiil poonee, ní Joosafaati jipɔɔn Jooram kpántì Juuda beelin ubɔti. 17U nìn cáá abin mmuŋku nì saalaa nì ali ní ki kpántì ubɔti, ní ki kāl̀ dibeel pu Jeerusaleem abin anii. 18U nìn pée nóó Isirayeel bɔtiibi tabɔbiliŋ ní, a lì kii Akaab dicaŋkun yab nín nìn bí puee, di sá yii u nìn cáá Akaab bisal ubɔ ní. U nìn ŋá tin kaa nìn kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee. 19Ama ti-Dindaan tɔntɔnliu Daafiidi puee, waa nìn là kí nàan̄ Juuda tiŋki, kun puee u nìn pōoǹ Daafiidi yii u-jipɔmbi làá nīn pée kā dibeel pu Jeerusaleem ní kí nīn cá jaanjaan.
20Jooram beel yuntiŋu ní Eedoom yab yíkì kaa kíí bi-ba pu kí nīn gbíntìi bí Juuda yab taapu ní ki kāaǹ bi-ba nì bi-bɔtiu. 21Jooram nìn yíkì ki nín cá Sayiir tiŋkin ki kpáaǹ u-janjatɔrɔkub kɔkɔ. Kunyeeuee ní u nì u-janjatɔrɔkub kpootiliibi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Eedoom yab bin nìn māntìi tú-bee. Ama Juuda janjaliibi nìn sáǹ ki nín kóò bi-tantibin. 22Kí yòon̄ yaadal wiiŋŋu ní Eedoom yab fōō bi-ba kaa ti bí Juuda yab taapu.
Ŋyunti gbanti mbaanti ní Liibiba yab mun kaa kíí bi-ba pu.
23Jooram tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee nì tin kɔkɔ u ŋée ŋmàn̄ ki kā Juuda bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun. 24Jooram kpíì ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ u-baabi ní bi síb́-u Daafiidi Tiŋkin. U-jipɔɔn Akasiyasi di fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.
Juuda bɔtiu Akasiyasi bɔti
(Kpèè 2 Kroo 22.1-6)
25Akaab jipɔɔn Jooram nín kāl̀ Isirayeel tibɔtiil abin saalaa nì ali poonee ní Juuda bɔtiu Jooram jipɔɔn Akasiyasi kpántì Juuda beelin ubɔti. 26Akasiyasi nìn cáá abin mmuŋku nì ali ní ki kpántì ubɔti. U nìn kāl̀ Jeerusaleem dibindi diba ní ki jíń dibeel. U-na di nìn sá Isirayeel bɔtiu Oomirii bisal ní bi yíì-u yii Atalii. 27U nìn nóó Akaab dicaŋkun yab tabɔbiliŋ ní ki nìn ŋá tin kaa kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee kii Akaab dicaŋkun yabee, di sá yii u nìn sá Akaab dicaŋkun yab coo ní.
28U nì Akaab jipɔɔn Jooram nìn cūtì ki jáń nì Siirii bɔtiu Asayeel Ramooti tiŋki kin bí Galaadi tiŋkpaaŋkinee ni. Ama kujaaunee ní Siirii yab tīī Jooram tiweendi. 29Ní Jooram nín gítí Jisirayeel kí cáaǹ tiweendi tin u fōō Siirii yab cee Raama tiŋkin ŋyunti ŋun u nìn bíi jáà nì Siirii bɔtiu Asayeelee. U bí Jisirayeel niinee ní Juuda bɔti Akasiyasi, Jooram jipɔɔn cūtì kí màntì u-pu.

english_text:
Jehu Becomes King of Israel
1One day, Elisha called for one of the other prophets and said:
Take this bottle of olive oil and get ready to go to the town of Ramoth in Gilead. 2When you get there, find Jehu son of Jehoshaphat and grandson of Nimshi. Take him to a place where the two of you can be alone, 3then pour olive oil on his head to show that he is the new king. Say to him, “The Lord has chosen you to be king of Israel.” Then leave quickly—don't wait around for anything!
4The young prophet left for Ramoth. 5When he arrived, the army officers were meeting together. “Sir, I have a message for you,” he said.
“For which one of us?” Jehu asked.
“You, sir,” the prophet answered. 6 So Jehu got up and went inside. The prophet poured olive oil on Jehu's head and told him:
The Lord God of Israel has this message for you: “I am the Lord, and I have chosen you to be king of my people Israel. 7I want you to wipe out the family of Ahab, so Jezebel will be punished for killing the prophets and my other servants. 8Every man and boy in Ahab's family must die, whether slave or free. 9His whole family must be destroyed, just like the families of Jeroboam son of Nebat and Baasha son of Ahijah. 10 As for Jezebel, her body will be eaten by dogs in the town of Jezreel. There won't be enough left of her to bury.”
Then the young prophet opened the door and ran out.
11Jehu went back to his officers, and one of them asked, “What did that crazy prophet want? Is everything all right?”
“You know him and how he talks,” Jehu answered.
12“No, we don't. What did he say?” they asked.
“He had a message from the Lord,” Jehu replied. “He said that the Lord has chosen me to be the next king of Israel.”
13They quickly grabbed their coats and spread them out on the steps where Jehu was standing. Someone blew a trumpet, and everyone shouted, “Jehu is king!”
Jehu Kills Joram and Ahaziah
14-16King Joram of Israel had been badly wounded in the battle at Ramoth, trying to defend it against King Hazael and the Syrian army. Joram was now recovering in Jezreel, and King Ahaziah of Judah was there, visiting him.
Meanwhile, Jehu was in Ramoth, making plans to kill Joram. He said to his officers, “If you want me to be king, then don't let anyone leave this town. They might go to Jezreel and tell Joram.” Then Jehu got in his chariot and rode to Jezreel.
17When the guard in the watchtower at Jezreel saw Jehu and his men riding up, he shouted to the king, “I see a large group of men coming this way.”
Joram ordered, “Send someone out to ask them if this is a friendly visit.”
18One of the soldiers rode out and said to Jehu, “King Joram wants to know if this is a friendly visit.”
“What's it to you?” Jehu asked. “Just stay behind me with the rest of my troops!”
About the same time the guard in the watchtower said, “Your Majesty, the rider got there, but he isn't coming back.”
19So Joram sent out another rider, who rode up to Jehu and said, “The king wants to know if this is a friendly visit.”
“What's it to you?” Jehu asked. “Just get behind me with the rest of my troops!”
20The guard in the watchtower said, “Your Majesty, the rider got there, but he isn't coming back either. Wait a minute! That one man is a reckless chariot driver—it must be Jehu!”
21Joram commanded, “Get my chariot ready.” Then he and Ahaziah got in their chariots and rode out to meet Jehu. They all met on the land that had belonged to Naboth. 22Joram asked, “Jehu, is this a peaceful visit?”
“How can there be peace?” Jehu asked. “Your mother Jezebel has caused everyone to worship idols and practice witchcraft.”
23“Ahaziah, let's get out of here!” Joram yelled. “It's a trap!” As Joram tried to escape, 24Jehu shot an arrow. It hit Joram between his shoulders, then it went through his heart and came out his chest. He fell over dead in his chariot.
25-26 Jehu commanded his assistant Bidkar, “Get Joram's body and throw it in the field that Naboth once owned. Do you remember when you and I used to ride side by side behind Joram's father Ahab? It was then that the Lord swore to Ahab that he would be punished in the same field where he had killed Naboth and his sons. So throw Joram's body there, just as the Lord said.”
27Ahaziah saw all of this happen and tried to escape to the town of Beth-Haggan, but Jehu caught up with him and shouted, “Kill him too!” So his troops shot Ahaziah with an arrow while he was on the road to Gur near Ibleam. He went as far as Megiddo, where he died. 28Ahaziah's officers put his body in a chariot and took it back to Jerusalem, where they buried him beside his ancestors.
29Ahaziah had become king of Judah in the eleventh year of the rule of Ahab's son Joram.
Jehu Kills Jezebel
30Jehu headed toward Jezreel, and when Jezebel heard he was coming, she put on eye shadow and brushed her hair. Then she stood at the window, waiting for him to arrive. 31As he walked through the city gate, she shouted down to him, “Why did you come here, you murderer? To kill the king? You're no better than Zimri!”
32He looked up toward the window and asked, “Is anyone up there on my side?” A few palace workers stuck their heads out of a window, 33and Jehu shouted, “Throw her out the window!” They threw her down, and her blood splattered on the walls and on the horses that trampled her body.
34Jehu left to get something to eat and drink. Then he told some workers, “Even though she was evil, she was a king's daughter, so make sure she has a proper burial.”
35But when they went out to bury her body, they found only her skull, her hands, and her feet. 36 They reported this to Jehu, and he said, “The Lord told Elijah the prophet that Jezebel's body would be eaten by dogs right here in Jezreel. 37And he warned that her bones would be spread all over the ground like manure, so that no one could tell who it was.”
translation_text:
Jeewuu kpántì Isirayeel bɔtiu
1Dalbee ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Eeliisee yíiń bibɔnaatiliibi kitil kansikin unaacimpɔɔn ubɔ ní ki bí-u yii: «Bɔ́ntí a-ba kí yòon̄ circir kpam kpalba kí nīn cá Ramooti tiŋkin Galaadi tiŋkpaaŋkin. 2A yaa bàn̄ niinee, á pɔ́ɔǹ a-ba kí ká Joosafaati jipɔɔn Jeewuu, Nimisii naantiu. Á yíiń-u ní kàkatī ni-ba kí wàatī u-nabiyaamu kí kɔ́ kudii kubɔn. 3Kudiin niinee ní á yòon̄ ŋkpam kpalbee kí bàtī kí sìtī u-yil pu kí tùkù-u yii: <Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Nì ŋkpam min m bātì ki sītì a-yil pu nee, m kāaǹ-si Isirayeel beelin ubɔti dee!> A yaa ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee, ní á pìitī kudii kí sāǹní kí taa ti tàan̄.»
4Eeliisee lī míǹ ki dóòyee ní kinaacimpɔmbikee nín cá Ramooti tiŋkin Galaadi tiŋkpaaŋkin. 5Ŋyunti ŋun u bàn̄ee, Isirayeel janjakpilib bíi ŋáań dikpafil. Ní unaacimpɔɔnee bí yii: «Ukpil, m cáá tiba ki làá tùkù-si!» Ní Jeewuu bí yii: «Ti-kansikin ŋma ní a là kí sòoǹ nì ní?» Ní kinaacimpɔmbikee kíí yii: «Ukpil, sii ní an sá!»
6Niinee Jeewuu yíkì ki nín kóò dicindin, ní kinaacimpɔmbikee bātì ŋkpam ki sītì u-yil pu ki lī yii: «Ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Nì ŋkpam min m bātì ki sītì a-yil pu nee, m dū-si ki kāaǹ man ni-Dindaan nibul Isirayeel pu ubɔti. 7Sii di làá kpɔ̀ a-kpiliu Akaab naantiibi. A yaa ŋá mimmee, a tɔ̀n̄ m-tɔntɔnliibi bibɔnaatiliibi nì bin kɔkɔ Jeesabeel kūūyee pɔntooŋyi dee. 8Akaab dicaŋkun yab kɔkɔ máaǹ kí kpú ní. M làá nàan̄ u-dicaŋkun bin kɔkɔ bí ki sá bininjabee Isirayeel tiŋkin. Maa làá kíń uyumbuɔɔɔ, kaa làá kíń un tɔ́ u-bee mun. 9M làá ŋá u-dicaŋku kii m nín ŋá Neebaati jipɔɔn Jeerooboowaam dicaŋku nì Ayiiya jipɔɔn Bayeesa puee ní. 10An yaa kíǹ Jeesabeel úŋ̀wuee, baa làá síb́-u, di sá yii iboo di làá ŋmɔ́-u tisatin.>» U lī mimmee ní ki pīitì kudii ki sáǹ ki kátì.
11Jeewuu nyánnée ní ki nín gítí ubɔti janjakpilib bin kíǹee cee ní bíǹ bālifì-u yii: «An mɔ̄ deeee? Uwaati gbanti nyàab̀ ba ní a-cee ní?» Ní u kíí-bi yii: «Nimbi ni-ba, ni pée nyí bibɔnaatiliibi nee nì tin bi sòoǹee.» 12Ní bin kíǹee bí-u yii: «A mɔ́ntí, māafì-ti tin jítèe!» Ní u kíí-bi yii: «Too, u bí-mi yii: <Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Nì ŋkpam min m bātì ki sītì a-yil pu nee, m kāaǹ-si ubɔti Isirayeel beelin dee.>»
13Bijanjakpilibee gbìl̄ mimmee ní báà ŋma ŋá malaa ki kpátì u-wanti tin u pēēyee ki bíl̀ dikɔl pu ki dū Jeewuu ki kāaǹ. Bi nìn búń ŋyin ní bi-kɔkɔ kíĺ ki kíǹ ki tátí yii: «Ubɔti Jeewuu ń ká mmaŋfafɔkɔn!»
Jeewuu bɔ́ntì kí kpɔ̀ Isirayeel bɔtiu Jooram
14Joosafaati jipɔɔn Jeewuu, Nimisii naantiu bɔ́ntì kí kpɔ̀ Jooram. Ŋyunti gbantee úǹ nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ bí Ramooti tiŋki kin bí Galaadi tiŋkpaaŋkinee ki jáà nì Siirii bɔtiu Asayeel ú taa fōō-kì. 15Ama bi nín bíi jáàyee ubɔti Jooram nìn fōō tiweendi. An pu ní u nìn fātìi gítìń Jisirayeel kí cáaǹ u-ba. Jeewuu nìn tùkū bijanjakpilibee yii: «Nimbi di sá bin bí m-jandi púee, an puee ubɔ ń taa nyā kitiŋ nee poon kí cù Jisirayeel kí dū tin jítì dooyee kí māafì.»
16Niinee Jeewuu jɔ́m̀ u-janjatɔrɔkuu pu ki nín cá Jisirayeel. Jooram nìn dɔ̄ u-dooŋu pu ní Juuda bɔtiu Akasiyasi cūtì kí màntì u-pu. 17Un nìn sí sintil Jisirayeel tiŋkinee nín ká Jeewuu nì dijanjakitil din nìn táá-uee dòońee ní u bí ubɔti yii: «M wāĺ dijanjakitil diba dòoń.» Ní ubɔti Jooram bí yii: «Nyàab̀ utanjakal ubɔ kí tɔ̄ ú cùú tūŋkì-bi kí bàlifì-bi yii bi dòoń nì ŋgbansɔŋfaaa?» 18Ní utanjakalee nín cá kí tūŋkì-bi. U bàn̄-bee ní ki bí yii: «Ubɔti bí yii ḿ bàlifì-ni yii an mɔ̄ deeee?» Ní Jeewuu kíí yii: «Ŋgbansɔŋfi bɔti ká-si la? Páań m-boon!» Ní un sí sintilee bí yii: «Ntuunee bàn̄ bi-cee, ama ŋuaa ti gítìń.»
19Ní ubɔti gíti lēē utanjakal uliliiti ki tú ní u mun bàn̄ bi-cee ki bí yii: «Ubɔti bí yii ḿ bàlifì-ni yii an mɔ̄ deeee?» Ní Jeewuu kíí yii: «Ŋgbansɔŋfi bɔti ká-si la? Páań m-boon!» 20Ní un sí sintilee bí yii: «Ntuun nliliitee bàn̄ bi-cee, ama ŋuaa ti gítìń. Bi nín jàkāń puee m béè un ní an sée. An sá Nimisii naantiu Jeewuu, di sá yii u jàkāń kii uwaatee ní.»
21Ní ubɔti Jooram yāntì bi kpàl̄ u-taamuu ní u jɔ́m̀ ki kāl̀, ní Juuda bɔtiu Akasiyasi mun jɔ́m̀ ki kāl̀ u-taamuu pu ní bi-liitil nín túŋkí Jeewuu, ní ki tin dūu tú-u ujiseeraayeelja Nabooti kpaatantin.
Isirayeel bɔtiu Jooram kúm
22Ŋyunti ŋun ní Jooram nyáń Jeewuu puee ní u bālifì-u yii: «An mɔ̄ deeee, Jeewuu?» Ní Jeewuu kíí-u yii: «Mana ní a ŋūǹ kí bàlifì-mi míǹ? Sii a-ba nyí yii a-na Jeesabeel gbíntìi tòotī awaa ki ŋáań kukpaŋkpantiiu tuuŋŋi.» 23Niinee Jooram fātìi lábitì u-ba ki bíi sáń, ní ki bí Akasiyasi yii: «Á nīn nyí nì a-ba Akasiyasi, bi nyáń ti-boon ní!»
24Niinee Jeewuu lēē mpiin ki páaǹ u-tɔbu pu ki dáaĺ ní an cūtìi cúú Jooram gbigbipati kansikin ki kɔ́ ki pūutì diŋuul ní ki tin nyáń ki lítì. Úǹ u-ba nìn nyáń u-tɔrɔkuu poon ki lítì. 25Ní Jeewuu bí un bí u-cee ki tútúǹ-u bi yíì-u yii Bidikaaree yii: «Nyāntí-u tɔrɔkun kí dū-u kí tɔ̄ ujiseeraayeelja Nabooti kpaatantin. A yaa téetí ŋyunti ŋun ní man nì sii nìn kā tɔrɔkun dicilpu ki cēentí u-baa Akaabee, ti-Dindaan nìn sòon̄ tibɔti tiba ki tɔ́ u-pu. 26Ti-Dindaan nìn bí-u yii: <Fool a nín fu kūū Nabooti nì u-jipɔmbee, man a-Dindaan, m fu ká kɔkɔ. Bukpaa bun poon a fu kūū-bee, bukpaa gbanti bubaantiiu poon ní m làá dáaĺ a-tafal, man ni-Dindaan di sòon̄ míǹ!> An puee nyāntí Jooram kí dū-u kí tɔ̄ bukpaayee poon, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn sòon̄ puee.»
Juuda bɔtiu Akasiyasi kúm
(Kpèè 2 Kroo 22.7-9)
27Juuda bɔtiu Akasiyasi nín ká mimmee, ní u cúú Beeti-Gan saŋŋu ki sáń ki cá, ama ní Jeewuu kùl̄ ki páaǹ u-boon. Jeewuu nìn tīī u-naacimbi mara yii bí kpɔ̀ u mun! Ŋyunti ŋun u kā u-tɔrɔkuun ki bíi dàb̀ Guur gbantaŋki kin kaa dátì nì Ibileeyamee ní bi yá u mun mpiin. Ama u nìn pɔ́ɔǹ ki sáǹ ki bàn̄ Meegiidoo tiŋkin ní ki kpíì niin. 28U-tɔntɔnliibi nìn dū-u ki ŋá u-tɔrɔkuun ní ki cáá-u ki cūnnì Jeerusaleem, ní ki tin síb́-u u-baabi kaakulin, Daafiidi Tiŋkin. 29Akaab jipɔɔn Jooram nín jíń dibeel abin saalaa nì diba poonee ní Akasiyasi kpántì ubɔti Juuda tiŋkin.
Jeesabeel kúm
30Jeewuu nìn kíǹ fiii kí kɔ́ Jisirayeel tiŋkin ní Jeesabeel gbìl̄ tin jítèe kɔkɔ. Ní u nyàab̄ culoo ki bɔ̄ntì ní ki nyáantì u-ba ní ki cūtìi kíǹ ki ŋōō tɔkɔla pu. 31Ŋyunti ŋun Jeewuu lákatì kitiŋ punyɔkɔki kí kɔ́ee ní Jeesabeel téeń yii: «Simrii, sii un kūū a-kpiliuee, an mɔ̄ deeee?» 32Jeewuu wáaǹ ki kpēē tɔkɔla watil púee ní ki bí yii: «Ŋma bí m-jandi púee?» Niinee ubɔti cindin bifaabi bili kii bita ŋɔ̄ntìń tɔkɔlabin. 33Ní u bí-bi yii: «Téeḿmaan-u kí lúkuń kitiŋ!» Ní bíǹ téeń-u ki lúkú kitiŋ. U lítèe ní u-fatikuu yāaǹ kitiŋ gundi nì itaamu pu, ní Jeewuu dū u-tɔrɔkuu ki tāā-u ki jítì.
34Míǹ boonee ní Jeewuu nín cá dibeecindin ki jíń ki nyùn̄, ní ki bí u-naacimbi yii: «Ní bɔ́ntímaan unimpusoopu nee kí síb́-u, di sá yii u sá ubɔti bisal ní.» 35Niinee bi nyáń kí síb́-u, ama kun bi pée kée di sá kuyikpabiku nì ataa nì iŋal. 36Ní bi fātìi gítìń ki tùkū Jeewuu ní úǹ bí yii: «Ti-Dindaan nín nìn dī u-bɔnaatiliu Eelii, utiiseebeeja pu ki sòon̄ tiŋyee dee yii: <Iboo làá dāá ŋmɔ́ Jeesabeel wunti Jisirayeel satin, 37ní u-wunti ń yàl̄ tisatin kii tinaabin tin bi bīil̀ kitiŋ tì yàntī tiwan lòoǹee, áli gba baa dāa gíti ŋūǹ kí lì yii: Jeesabeel sèé!>»

english_text:
Jehu Kills All of Ahab's Descendants
1Ahab still had 70 descendants living in Samaria. So Jehu wrote a letter to each of the important leaders and officials of the town, and to those who supported Ahab. In the letters he wrote:
2Your town is strong, and you're protected by chariots and an armed cavalry. And I know that King Ahab's descendants live there with you. So as soon as you read this letter, 3choose the best person for the job and make him the next king. Then be prepared to defend Ahab's family.
4The officials and leaders read the letters and were very frightened. They said to each other, “Jehu has already killed King Joram and King Ahaziah! We have to do what he says.” 5The prime minister, the mayor of the city, as well as the other leaders and Ahab's supporters, sent this answer to Jehu, “We are your servants, Your Majesty, and we will do whatever you tell us. But it's not our place to choose someone to be king. You do what you think is best.”
6Jehu then wrote another letter which said, “If you are on my side and will obey me, then prove it. Bring me the heads of the descendants of Ahab! And be here in Jezreel by this time tomorrow.”
The 70 descendants of King Ahab were living with some of the most important people of the city. 7And when these people read Jehu's second letter, they called together all 70 of Ahab's descendants. They killed them, put their heads in baskets, and sent them to Jezreel.
8When Jehu was told what had happened, he said, “Put the heads in two piles at the city gate, and leave them there until morning.”
9The next morning, Jehu went out and stood where everyone could hear him, and he said, “You people are not guilty of anything. I'm the one who plotted against Joram and had him killed. But who killed all these men? 10Listen to me. Everything the Lord's servant Elijah promised about Ahab's family will come true.”
11 Then Jehu killed the rest of Ahab's relatives living in Jezreel, as well as his highest officials, his priests, and his closest friends. No one in Ahab's family was left alive in Jezreel.
12-13Jehu left for Samaria, and along the way, he met some relatives of King Ahaziah of Judah at a place where shepherds meet. He asked, “Who are you?”
“We are relatives of Ahaziah,” they answered. “We're going to visit his family.”
14“Take them alive!” Jehu said to his officers. So they grabbed them and led them to the well near the shepherds' meeting place, where they killed all 42 of them.
15As Jehu went on, he saw Jehonadab son of Rechab coming to meet him. Jehu greeted him, then said, “Jehonadab, I'm on your side. Are you on mine?”
“Yes, I am.”
“Then give me your hand,” Jehu answered. He helped Jehonadab into his chariot 16and said, “Come with me and see how faithful I am to the Lord.”
They rode together in Jehu's chariot 17to Samaria. Jehu killed everyone there who belonged to Ahab's family, as well as all his officials. Everyone in his family was now dead, just as the Lord had promised Elijah.
Jehu Kills All the Worshipers of Baal
18Jehu called together the people in Samaria and said:
King Ahab sometimes worshiped Baal, but I will be completely faithful to Baal. 19I'm going to offer a huge sacrifice to him. So invite his prophets and priests, and be sure everyone who worships him is there. Anyone who doesn't come will be killed.
But this was a trick—Jehu was really planning to kill the worshipers of Baal. 20He said, “Announce a day of worship for Baal!” After the day had been announced, 21Jehu sent an invitation to everyone in Israel. All the worshipers of Baal came, and the temple was filled from one end to the other. 22Jehu told the official in charge of the sacred robes to make sure that everyone had a robe to wear.
23Jehu and Jehonadab went into the temple, and Jehu said to the crowd, “Look around and make sure that only the worshipers of Baal are here. No one who worships the Lord is allowed in.” 24Then they began to offer sacrifices to Baal.
Earlier, Jehu had ordered 80 soldiers to wait outside the temple. He had warned them, “I will get all these worshipers here, and if any of you let even one of them escape, you will be killed instead!”
25As soon as Jehu finished offering the sacrifice, he told the guards and soldiers, “Come in and kill them! Don't let anyone escape.” They slaughtered everyone in the crowd and threw the bodies outside. Then they went back into the temple 26and carried out the image of Baal. They burned it 27and broke it into pieces, then they completely destroyed Baal's temple. And since that time, it's been nothing but a public toilet.
28That's how Jehu stopped the worship of Baal in Israel. 29 But he did not stop the worship of the gold statues of calves at Dan and Bethel that Jeroboam had made for the people to worship.
30Later the Lord said, “Jehu, you have done right by destroying Ahab's entire family, just as I had planned. So I will make sure that the next four kings of Israel will come from your own family.”
31But Jehu did not completely obey the commands of the Lord God of Israel. Instead, he kept doing the sinful things that Jeroboam had caused the Israelites to do.
Jehu Dies
32In those days the Lord began to reduce the size of Israel's territory. King Hazael of Syria defeated the Israelites and took control 33of the regions of Gilead and Bashan east of the Jordan River and north of the town of Aroer near the Arnon River. This was the land where the tribes of Gad, Reuben, and Manasseh had once lived.
34Everything else Jehu did while he was king, including his brave deeds, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. 35Jehu died and was buried in Samaria, and his son Jehoahaz became king. 36Jehu had ruled Israel 28 years from Samaria.
translation_text:
Jeewuu kūū Akaab dicaŋkun yab kɔkɔ
1Akaab nìn cáá naantiibi imuŋku ita nì saalaa kóò Samaarii tiŋkin. Jeewuu nìn ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu ki tú bí cáá tīī Samaarii tindaŋkpilib nì Jisirayeel janjakpilib nì bin nìn kpèé Akaab naantiibee kí tùkù-bi yii: 2«Nimbi di kpèé ubɔti biyaamu, ki cáá tɔrɔkub nì itaamu nì tijanjawan, ní ki kóò kitiŋ kin poon bi máń digundi ki māntìi túee. Ŋyunti ŋun ni yaa fōō kugbɔŋu neeyee, 3ní kpèè ubɔti jipɔmbi kansikin kí lēē un kítì ki máaǹ kí nīn sá ubɔtee kí dū-u kí kàan̄ tibɔtiil ú fōō u-baa yil. Ni yaa ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee, ní bɔ́ntí ni-ba kí já kí mɔ̄tì ni-kpiliu dicaŋku pu.»
4Bi gbìl̄ mimmee ní ki fāŋkì tikpil ki kíǹ ki lì tɔb cee yii: «Bibɔtiibi bili kaa ŋúń ki síl̀ u-nimbiin, kin mana ní timbi nee làá ŋmā kí já nì u?» 5Niinee ukpil un kpèé ubɔti cindee nì ujanjakpil un kpèé kitiŋ gbantee nì bitindaŋkpilib nì bin kpèé mbiyaamuee tú bí cùú tùkù Jeewuu yii: «Timbi sá a-tɔntɔnliibi ní. Kun a yaa pée bí yii tí ŋée, ti làá ŋá. Taa làá lēē báà ubɔ kí kàan̄ tibɔtiil. Míǹ puee ŋá min di ŋān̄ a-ceeyee.»
6Ní Jeewuu fātìi ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu kuliliitiiu ki tùkū-bi yii: «Ni yaa bí m-jandi pú ní ki yaa làá pīlifì m-nyɔkɔee, ní lēēmaan ni-kpiliu Akaab jipɔmbi nì u-naantiibi kɔkɔ yiliŋ kí fu cáań-mi fool naŋkɔnampu Jisirayeel tiŋkin.» Ubɔti jipɔmbi nì u-naantiibi imuŋku ita nì saalaa gbantee nìn kā Samaarii nikpaambi cee ní bi kpèé-bi.
7Bikpilibee nín fōō kugbɔŋuee ní bi cúú ubɔti jipɔmbi nì u-naantiibi imuŋku ita nì saalaayee kɔkɔ ki lāntì, ní ki dū bi-yiliŋ ki ŋá tikabitin ki tú bi cáa tīī Jeewuu Jisirayeel tiŋkin. 8Ubɔ nìn dɔ́miń ki tùkū Jeewuu yii: «Bi cáań ubɔti jipɔmbi nì u-naantiibi yiliŋ.» Ní Jeewuu bí yii: «Dūmaan-ŋi kí bíĺ akpuku ali kitiŋ punyɔkɔki caŋin áli fool kutaafaau!» 9Kutaa wúntèe ní Jeewuu nyáń ki síl̀ samaa nimbiin ki lī yii: «Nimbee, ni sá deedeedambi! Man di bɔ́ntì kí kpɔ̀ m-kpiliu ubɔti ní ki lafun kūū-u mun. Ama ŋma di kūū bin bí nee kɔkɔ? 10Ní béémaan yii tin kɔkɔ ní ti-Dindaan nìn sòon̄ ki tɔ́ Akaab dicaŋku puee, báà dinyɔɔbundi kpá kí gbíntí fám! Ti-Dindaan nín dī u-bɔnaatiliu Eelii pu ki sòon̄ tin kɔkɔee, u ŋá míǹ.» 11Niinee Jeewuu kūū bin kɔkɔ nìn kíǹ Akaab dicaŋkun ki bí dimaŋfalin ki kóò Jisirayeelee kɔkɔ. U nìn kūū ki kpáaǹ bikpilib bin kɔkɔ nìn pá u-boonee nì u-bɔɔbi nì u-tandambi. Waa nìn yāntì bi-kansikin ubɔ ŋmátì.
Jeewuu kūū Juuda bɔtibiliŋ
(Kpèè 2 Kroo 22.8)
12Boonee Jeewuu kíĺ nsan ki nín cá Samaarii. U bàn̄ laakin bi yíì yii Beeti-Eekeedi-Bipikpaabee, 13ní ki tú Juuda bɔtiu Akasiyasi nabiyaamu. Ní u bālifì-bi yii: «Ni sá bilab ní?» Ní bi kíí yii: «Ti sá Akasiyasi nabiyaamu ní. Ti dɔ́miń kí jāam̀ ubɔti nimpuu Jeesabeel biyaamu nì bin kíǹ ki bí ubɔti dicaŋkunee ní.» 14Ní Jeewuu téeń yii: «Ní cúúmaan-bi nì bi-nimbiliŋ!» Ní u-naacimbi cúú-bi nì bi-nimbiliŋ ki lāntì ní ki dū-bi ki tɔ́ Beeti-Eekeedi lɔkɔun. Binib gbanti nìn sá binib imuŋku ili nì bili ní. Bi-kansikin báà ubɔ kaa nìn ŋmátì.
Jeewuu tú Yoonadaab nsanni
15U nyáń niin kí nīn cée ní ki dūu tú Reekaab jipɔɔn Yoonadaab, u mun nìn còom̄ ki túŋkí-u. Jeewuu jáam̀-uee ní ki bí-u yii: «A sí m-boon kii ma mun nín sí a-boon pueeee?» Ní Yoonadaab kíí yii: «Iiin!» Ní Jeewuu gíti bí-u yii: «An yaa sée, tīī-mi kuboou!» Ní Yoonadaab tīī-u kuboou. Niinee ní Jeewuu cúú u-ŋal ki cáá-u ki kɔ́ǹ u-cee tɔrɔkun, 16ní ki bí-u yii: «Dāan̄ tí cù á kpèè man nín cáá ti-Dindaan pu difaŋgiil puee!» U lī mimmee ní ki yōoǹ-u u-tɔrɔkuu pu ki cáá-u ki búntì. 17Bi bàn̄ Samaarii tiŋkinee ní Jeewuu kūū Akaab dicaŋkun yab bin kɔkɔ nìn kíǹ ki bí kitiŋin niinee. U nìn nāaǹ bi-kɔkɔ ki nóó nì ti-Dindaan nín nìn dī ubɔnaatil Eelii pu ki sòon̄ puee.
Jeewuu nāaǹ diwaal Baal tɔntɔnliibi kɔkɔ
18Míǹ boonee ní Jeewuu kóoǹ samaa kɔkɔ ki kpáfì ní ki bí-bi yii: «Ubɔti Akaab tōotì diwaal Baal, man làá gíti tòotī-dì kí jītíǹ-u. 19An puee ní yíiń Baal bɔnaatiliibi kɔkɔ nì bin kɔkɔ tòotī-dèe nì di-tandambi kɔkɔ bí kpāfì m-cee. Ubɔ ń taa kíń, di sá yii m làá ŋá saraakpaŋkpaan ní kí tīī diwaal Baal. Un yaa kaa dɔ́mińee, bi làá kpɔ̀-u ní.»
Jeewuu nìn bíi ŋmàtíǹ-bi kí ŋmā kí kpɔ̀ kí céetí bin nìn tòotī diwaal Baalee ní. 20An pu ní u nìn bí yii bí kóoǹ kí kpāfì kí jāam̀ diwaal Baal. Bi nìn ŋmàn̄ tigbɔn 21ki yākatì ki tīī Isirayeel beel kɔkɔn. Bin kɔkɔ nìn pée tòotī diwaal Baalee nìn dɔ́miń ní. Ubɔ kaa nìn kíǹ kaa dɔ́miń. Bi nìn kɔ́ diwaal Baal diikun ní an gbí. 22Ní Jeewuu bí un kpèé diwaal wampeeŋkaatee yii: «Nyāntí tiwampeeŋkaal kí yàkatīí tīī bin kɔkɔ pée tòotī Baalee!» Ní úǹ nyántì tiwampeeŋkaal ki tīī-bi. 23Jeewuu nì Reekaab jipɔɔn Yoonadaab nìn kɔ́ diwaal Baal diikun ní ki bí bin tòotī Baalee yii: «Ní kpèèmaan ni-kansikin tiŋan kí kpèè yii bin jáaḿ ti-Dindaanee yaa bí doo, di sá yii ti pée là bin tòotī Baalee ŋmaniŋma ní.»
24Jeewuu nì Yoonadaab nìn nín kóò kí ŋá mpèé saraabi nì bisaraawɔkaabi. Kaa nyí kii Jeewuu ŋá mimmee ki nyàab̄ bijanjaliibi imuŋku inaa ki síiǹ mmɔŋki ki bí-bi yii: «M dū binib nee kɔkɔ ki ŋá ni-ŋaan, ama ubɔ yaa yāntì bi-kansikin ubɔ ŋmátèe, udaan làá dū úǹ u-ba maŋfal ní kí téeǹ un ŋmátèe yal pu.» 25Ŋyunti ŋun Jeewuu ŋá saraabi ki dóòyee ní u bí bijanjaliibi nì bi-kpilib yii: «Ní kɔ́ kí kpɔ̀ binib nee! Ní taa yàntī ubɔbɔ ń ŋmátí.» Ní bi kɔ́ ki dū ntàataajimu ki kūū bi-kɔkɔ. Bi kūū-bi ki dóòyee ní ki nyántì-bi ki tɔ́ ki fá kitiŋ kpaanceetiŋu. Bi ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki nín gítiń diwaal Baal diikun, 26ní ki nyántìń ditaŋkpal din nìn cɔ́ diwaal Baal diikun bi tòotēe ki tūū ŋŋmi. 27Bi nín wùn̄ Baal taŋkpal míǹ ki dóòyee ní bi gbáń ki wīī di-diiku ki dūu ŋá kupɔɔndii. Ku bí ki dāa sāā díǹ.
Jeewuu kpántì Isirayeel bɔtiu
28Jeewuu nín ŋá pu ní ki kúntì diwaal Baal Isirayeel beelinee dee. 29Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, waa nìn kākatì u-ba ki wāatì ikpiti in ní Neebaati jipɔɔn Jeerooboowaam nìn yāntì Isirayeel yab ŋá ki cūtìi bíi jáaḿ sindaariya nabiliŋ ŋin bi nìn mɔ́ɔ́ an bí Beeteel nì Daanee.
30Niinee ti-Dindaan bí Jeewuu yii: «A ŋá an ŋān̄, a ŋá tin fáatiǹ-mee. A ŋá Akaab dicaŋkun yab kii m nín là puee. An puee a-naantiibi làá kàl̄ Isirayeel tiŋki pu tibɔtiil kí cáá sāā anaantitɔntɔkɔ anaa pu.» 31Ama nì míǹ kɔkɔee, Jeewuu kaa nìn ŋúb́ ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu marab nì u-pɔbil kɔkɔ, waa nìn kākatì u-ba ki wāatì ikpiti in Jeerooboowaam nìn yāntì Isirayeel yab ŋée.
32Ŋyunti gbantee, ti-Dindaan nìn kíĺ ki bíi bàtī Isirayeel tiŋki pu. U nìn yāntì Siirii bɔtiu Asayeel jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Isirayeel yab bi-tiŋki kɔkɔ poon. 33Siirii yab nìn jáń ki fōō kitiŋ kin bí Jɔɔdan ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee nì Arooweer tiŋki kin bí Arinɔn buŋŋu ŋgan púee, an dàkà yii Galaadi nì Baasan timmu. Ntimu gbanti poon ní Rubeen nì Gaadi nì Manasee naakɔti yab nìn kóò.
34Jeewuu tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee nì tin kɔkɔ u ŋée nì u-pɔ́ɔǹtam kɔkɔ ŋmàn̄ ki kā Isirayeel bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun. 35Jeewuu kpíì ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ u-baabi ní bi síb́-u Samaarii tiŋkin. U-jipɔɔn Joowakaasi di fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti. 36Jeewuu nìn jíń dibeel Isirayeel tiŋki pu abin mmuŋku nì anii ní. Samaarii tiŋkin ní u nìn kóò.

english_text:
Queen Athaliah of Judah
(2 Chronicles 22.10-12)
1As soon as Athaliah heard that her son King Ahaziah was dead, she decided to kill any relative who could possibly become king. She would have done that, 2but Jehosheba rescued Joash son of Ahaziah just as he was about to be murdered. Jehosheba, who was Jehoram's daughter and Ahaziah's half sister, hid her nephew Joash and his personal servant in a bedroom in the Lord's temple where he was safe from Athaliah. 3Joash hid in the temple with Jehosheba for six years while Athaliah ruled as queen of Judah.
Jehoiada Makes Joash King of Judah
(2 Chronicles 23.1-21)
4Joash son of Ahaziah had hidden in the Lord's temple six years. Then in the seventh year, Jehoiada the priest sent for the commanders of the king's special bodyguards and the commanders of the palace guards. They met him at the temple, and he asked them to make a promise in the name of the Lord. Then he brought out Joash 5and said to them:
Here's what I want you to do. Three of your guard units will be on duty on the Sabbath. I want one unit to guard the palace. 6Another unit will guard Sur Gate, and the third unit will guard the palace gate and relieve the palace guards.
7The other two guard units are supposed to be off duty on the Sabbath. But I want both of them to stay here at the temple and protect King Joash. 8Make sure they follow him wherever he goes, and tell them to keep their swords ready to kill anyone who tries to get near him.
9The commanders followed Jehoiada's orders. Each one called together his guards—those coming on duty and those going off duty. 10Jehoiada brought out the swords and shields that had belonged to King David and gave them to the commanders. 11Then they gave the weapons to their guards, who took their positions around the temple and the altar to protect Joash on every side.
12Jehoiada brought Joash outside, where he placed the crown on his head and gave him a copy of instructions for ruling the nation. Olive oil was poured on his head to show that he was now king, while the crowd clapped and shouted, “Long live the king!”
13Queen Athaliah heard the crowd and went to the temple. 14 There she saw Joash standing by one of the columns, which was the usual place for the king. The singers and the trumpet players were standing next to him, and the people were celebrating and blowing trumpets. Athaliah tore her clothes in anger and shouted, “You betrayed me, you traitors!”
15At once, Jehoiada said to the army commanders, “Kill her! But don't do it anywhere near the Lord's temple. Take her out in front of the troops and kill anyone who is with her!” 16So the commanders dragged her to the gate where horses are led into the palace, and they killed her there.
17Jehoiada the priest asked King Joash and the people to promise that they would be faithful to each other and to the Lord. 18Then the crowd went to the temple built to honor Baal and tore it down. They smashed the altars and idols and killed Mattan the priest of Baal right in front of the altars.
After Jehoiada had placed guards around the Lord's temple, 19he called together all the commanders, the king's special bodyguards, the palace guards, and the people. They led Joash from the temple, through the Guards' Gate, and into the palace. He took his place on the throne and became king of Judah. 20Everyone celebrated because Athaliah had been killed and Jerusalem was peaceful again. 21Joash was only seven years old when this happened.
translation_text:
Atalii fōō dibeel Jeerusaleem
(Kpèè 2 Kroo 22.10-12)
1Akasiyasi na Atalii nín ká yii u-jipɔɔn kpíìyee ní u lēē yii u làá kpɔ̀ kí céetí ubɔti naantiibi kɔkɔ. 2Ama ubɔti Jooram bisal Yooseeba, Akasiyasi niisal nìn ŋúń ki yōoǹ Akasiyasi jipɔɔn Joowaasi u-mambi kansikin baa ŋúń ki kūū-u ní ki cáá kibikee nì ki-bilooliu ki bál̀ kunimbɔtidii didooŋkaaku kubɔn. Atalii kaa nìn béè, an puee baa nìn kūū kibiki gbanti. 3Kibikee nì ki-bilooliu nìn bál̀ ti-Dindaan diikun niin áli abin aluu. Ŋyunti gbanti kɔkɔee, Atalii di nìn kā dibeel pu.
Bi kpántì ubɔti
(Kpèè 2 Kroo 23.1-21)
4Dibinluluútiil poonee, ní Yooyadaa tú bi cūtìi yíiń Karii yab janjakpilib nì bijanjaliibi bin cīití dibeecindi nì ti-Dindaan diikuee. Bi bāańee ní u cáá-bi ki cūnnì ti-Dindaan Diikun ní u nì bi ŋá kinyɔkɔbaantii. U nìn yāntì bi pūtì ní u dū ubɔti jipɔɔnee ki dàkā-bi. 5Boonee ní u tīī-bi mara nee yii: «Ni nín làá ŋá puee sɔ̀. Ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa nee, ni-kitil diba làá tɔ̄ ditundi. Dikitipeekaal làá cīití dibeecindi kii di nín kpàà ŋáań puee, 6ní dikitililiitiil ń nīn cí Suur punyɔkɔki ní ditataatiil ń nīn cí kipunyɔkɔ kin bí biciitiliibi boonee. Akiti ata gbanti làá nīn cīití dibeecindi ní ki fòol̄ tɔb. 7Akiti ali ŋin kaa làá nīn bí ditundin ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dalee ń dāá dāan̄ ti-Dindaan Diikun kí nīn cí ubɔti. 8Ní dāá màntīí tū ubɔti báà ŋma ń nīn ŋúb́ u-janjawanti u-ŋaan. Un yaa là kí ŋá mpɔn kí kɔ́née, ní kpɔ̀-u. Laakin kamaa ubɔti yaa cée, ní nīn bí u-cee.»
9Bijanjakpilibee nìn ŋá kii usaraaŋakpil Yooyadaa nín bí yii bí ŋá puee. Báà ŋma nìn yōoǹ u-janjaliibi, bin tundi nìn kífí ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dalee nì bin tundi nìn kúntí ŋwiin gbanti dalee, ní bi nín cá usaraaŋakpil Yooyadaa cee. 10Usaraaŋakpil nìn dū ubɔti Daafiidi kpaŋki nì u-gbampɔɔŋi ŋin nìn bí ti-Dindaan Diikunee ki tīī bijanjakpilib. 11Bijanjaliibee nìn māntìi tú ubɔti ti-Dindaan Diiku nì nsaraafan nimbiin kí yòon̄ ŋgiil pú ki cáa sāā ŋgan pú. Bi nìn ŋúb́ tijanjawan ní ki lūtìi gíb́ ubɔti. 12Niinee Yooyadaa nyántì Joowaasi, ki dū kibeefuulii ki cíkiǹ-u ní ki dū dipoondi taŋkpapilinti ki ŋúbiǹ-u. Boonee ní u bātì ŋkpam ki sītì u-yil pu ki kāaǹ-u tibɔtiil ní samaa kɔkɔ kpáafì abaal ki kíǹ ki tátí yii: «Ubɔti ń nīn cáá mmaŋfafɔkɔn!»
13Atalii nín gbìl̄ samaa nì bijanjaliibi wooku puee ní u nín cá ti-Dindaan Diiku watil pú diniwulee cee. 14U kpēēyee, ubɔtipɔɔn di tɔ́kɔ́ ti-Dindaan Diiku kɔl pu kii bi nín kpààa ŋáań puee, bijanjakpilib nì bikantámbunliibi sí ki kɔ́ĺ-u. Samaa kɔkɔ nìn bí mmɔnni ní bikantámbunliibi búǹ akantán. Niinee Atalii cúú tiwan tin u pēēyee ki dáaĺ ki cátì ní ki téeń yii: «Bi nyáń m-boon ní! Bi nyáń m-boon ní!»
15Ní usaraaŋakpil Yooyadaa tīī bijanjakpilib bin nìn kpèé bijanjaliibi bin bí ti-Dindaan diikunee mara yii: «Nyāntímaan-u doo! Un di yaa páaǹ u-boonee, bí kpɔ̀-u!» Di sá yii usaraaŋakpil nìn lī yii: «Bí taa kpɔ̀-u ti-Dindaan Diikun doo.» 16Bi nìn dáaĺ-u ki cūnnì kubɔtinaakoou watil pú, ní ŋyunti ŋun bi bàn̄ Itaamu punyɔkɔkee ní bi kūū-u niin.
17Yooyadaa nìn ŋá mpèé ti-Dindaan nì ubɔti nì samaa kansikin bí nīn kíǹ ki sá ti-Dindaan nibul. U nìn yāntì ubɔti nì samaa mun ŋá mpèé. 18Niinee ní samaa kɔkɔ nín cá diwaal Baal diikun ki gbáń ki wīī-ku. Bi nìn gbáń ki wīī Baal saraafaŋyi nì ataŋkpee ŋin nìn bí niin bi tòotēe. Bi nìn kūū Baal tandaaŋwu Matan ki bíl̀ isaraafan caŋin. Boonee ní usaraaŋakpil Yooyadaa lēē binib bí nīn cí ti-Dindaan Diiku.
19Yooyadaa nìn kóoǹ bijanjakpilib nì Karii yab nì bijanjaliibi bin nìn sá biciitiliibee nì samaa kɔkɔ ní bi yōoǹ ubɔti ti-Dindaan Diikun, ki dūu dī biciitiliibi saŋŋu ki céeǹ-u ki cáa cūnnì ubɔti dumpu. Joowaasi nìn kāl̀ dibeejal pu, 20ní samaa kɔkɔ kíĺ ki bíi fàal̀.
Bi nín kūū Atalii dibeecindin boonee ní kitiŋ kɔ́ ŋgbansɔŋfin. Atalii úŋ̀wuee, bi nìn dū kitàataajiki ní ki kūū-u dibeecindin.

english_text:
King Joash of Judah
(2 Chronicles 24.1-16)
1Joash became king of Judah in Jehu's seventh year as king of Israel, and he ruled 40 years from Jerusalem. His mother Zibiah was from the town of Beersheba.
2Jehoiada the priest taught Joash what was right, and so for the rest of his life Joash obeyed the Lord. 3But even Joash did not destroy the local shrines, and they were still used as places for offering sacrifices.
4 One day, Joash said to the priests, “Collect all the money that has been given to the Lord's temple, whether from taxes or gifts, 5and use it to repair the temple whenever you see the need.”
6But the priests never started repairing the temple. So in the twenty-third year of his rule, 7Joash called for Jehoiada and the other priests and said, “Why aren't you using the money to repair the temple? Don't take any more money for yourselves. It is only to be used to pay for the repairs.” 8The priests agreed that they would not collect any more money or be in charge of the temple repairs.
9Jehoiada found a wooden box; he cut a hole in the top of it and set it on the right side of the altar where people went into the temple. Whenever someone gave money to the temple, the priests guarding the entrance would put it into this box. 10When the box was full of money, the king's secretary and the chief priest would count the money and put it in bags. 11Then they would give it to the men supervising the repairs to the temple. Some of the money was used to pay the builders, the woodworkers, 12the stonecutters, and the men who built the walls. And some was used to buy wood and stone and to pay any other costs for repairing the temple.
13While the repairs were being made, the money that was given to the temple was not used to make silver bowls, lamp snuffers, small sprinkling bowls, trumpets, or anything gold or silver for the temple. 14It went only to pay for repairs. 15 The men in charge were honest, so no one had to keep track of the money.
16 The fines that had to be paid along with the sacrifices to make things right and the sacrifices for sin did not go to the temple. This money belonged only to the priests.
17About the same time, King Hazael of Syria attacked the town of Gath and captured it. Next, he decided to attack Jerusalem. 18So Joash collected everything he and his ancestors Jehoshaphat, Jehoram, and Ahaziah had dedicated to the Lord, as well as the gold in the storage rooms in the temple and palace. He sent it all to Hazael as a gift, and when Hazael received it, he ordered his troops to leave Jerusalem.
19Everything else Joash did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah. 20-21At the end of his rule, some of his officers rebelled against him. Jozabad son of Shimeath and Jehozabad son of Shomer murdered him in a building where the land was filled in on the east side of Jerusalem, near the road to Silla. Joash was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Amaziah became king.
translation_text:
Juuda bɔtiu Joowaasi bɔti
(Kpèè 2 Kroo 24.1-3)
1Joowaasi nìn cáá abin aluli ní ki kpántì ubɔti. 2Isirayeel bɔtiu Jeewuu nín jíń dibeel dibinluluútiil poonee ní Joowaasi kpántì ubɔti. Jeerusaleem ní u nìn kóò ní ki jíń dibeel abin imuŋku ili. U-na nìn sá Beerseeba ní bi yíì-u yii Sibiya. 3Joowaasi maŋfal wiiŋyi kɔkɔ poonee, u nìn ŋá tin kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee ní, kun puee usaraaŋakpil Yooyadaa nìn dàkā-u tiŋan. 4Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, isaraafan in nìn bí ŋgbantamu puee nìn gbíntìi bí. Samaa nìn gbíntìi ŋáań saraabi ki tùutī talaalub ŋgbantamu gbanti pu.
Joowaasi fātìi ŋáŋkì ti-Dindaan Diiku
(Kpèè 2 Kroo 24.4-14)
5Dalbee ní Joowaasi bí bisaraaŋaliibi yii: «Animbil ŋin bi cāabìń ti-Dindaan Diikun bí dūú tɔ̄ ku-tundee nì ŋin bi cáa pà patantibee nì ŋin binib pée cāabìń nì dipɔbil dibee, 6nimbi ni-ba ń fōō an nimbiliŋee bin ni nyée cee kí dūú ŋāŋkì ti-Dindaan Diiku laakin bíil̀ee.»
7Ama Joowaasi nín jíń dibeel abin mmuŋku nì ata poonee, bisaraaŋaliibi kaa nìn dáá ŋáŋkì ti-Dindaan Diiku. 8Ní ubɔti Joowaasi yíiń usaraaŋakpil Yooyadaa nì bisaraaŋaliibi bin kíǹee ki bālifì-bi yii: «Ba pu ní naa ŋáŋkì ti-Dindaan Diiku laakin bíil̀ bíil̀ee? Kí yòon̄ díǹ kí nīn cée, naa ti làá fōō animbil binib bin ni nyée cee, di sá yii ni máaǹ kí dūú tīī bí dūú ŋāŋkì ti-Dindaan Diiku ní.» 9Niinee bisaraaŋaliibi kíí yii baa ti làá fōō samaa cee animbil, kí taa ti kpèè ti-Dindaan Diiku ŋāŋkitam bɔti.
10Usaraaŋakpil Yooyadaa nìn nyàab̄ dakaa ubɔ ní ki sāā ki cíl̀ yilpu ki dūu síiǹ nsaraafan caŋin, a yaa kóò ti-Dindaan Diikunee, ŋŋaŋgiil pú. Bisaraaŋaliibi bin nìn cīití kipunyɔkɔee nìn cáá animbil ŋin kɔkɔ ní binib nìn cāabìń ti-Dindaan Diikunee ki ŋáań poon ní. 11Bi yaa nìn ká yii animbil bí dakaayee poon ki náaǹee, ní ubɔti gbaŋŋmaliu nì usaraaŋakpil ń dāan̄ kí yòon̄ animbil gbanti kí kàaǹ. 12Bi yaa nìn kàan̄ animbil gbanti ki dóòyee ní bí dūú tīī bin nìn tūǹ atuunee nì bin nìn kpèé ti-Dindaan Diiku tuuŋŋee. Bíǹ yaa fōōyee ní bí lēē kí pà bitɔntɔnliibi bin nìn bí ki ŋáŋkée nì kapintab bin nìn bí ti-Dindaan Diikun ki tūǹ ditundee, 13nì bidimaliibi nì bin nìn kpítí ataŋkpeeyee. Bi nìn tí lèekī animbilee poon kí dā idɔ nì ataŋkpee ŋin bi kpítèe kí ŋmā kí dūú ŋāŋkì ti-Dindaan Diiku. Ti-Dindaan Diiku ŋāŋkitam nín nìn pée bàlifī kuŋyee, animbilee poon ní bi nìn lèekī kí ŋá tíǹ kɔkɔ.
14Ama baa nìn lēē animbil ŋin bi nìn cāabìń ti-Dindaan Diikunee kí ŋá tikúti sambiliŋ, àá nsamu mun bi cáa gbíntí fitilabee, àá asambil ŋin poon bi nìn ŋáań fatiku ki cáa yàantí nsaraafan puee, àá akantán, àá sindaariya àá animbil wanti tiba ki síiǹ ti-Dindaan Diiku poon. 15Bi nìn dū animbil gbanti kɔkɔ ki tīī atuun kpilib ní bíǹ dūu ŋáŋkì ti-Dindaan Diiku. 16Binib bin bi nìn cáá animbil gbanti ki tìì bí nīn cáa pà bitɔntɔnliibee, baa nìn bàlifī-bi yii bí gbá akɔntaa bí kpèè bi nín jíń animbil gbanti puee, di sá yii bi nìn sá bibulcinnib ní.
17Baa nìn cáá dibɔkpil saraabi nì ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraabi nimbiliŋ ki ŋáŋkí ti-Dindaan Diiku. Bisaraaŋaliibi di nìn yì an nimbiliŋ.
Joowaasi kúm
(2 Kroo 24.23-27)
18Ŋyunti gbantee Siirii bɔtiu Asayeel dɔ́miń ki jáń nì Gaati tiŋki. U jáń ki fōō-kèe ní u lēē yii u làá já nì Jeerusaleem mun. 19Niinee Juuda bɔtiu Joowaasi yōoǹ tiwan tin kɔkɔ ní Juuda bɔtiibi, u-naanjab Joosafaati nì Jooram nì Akasiyasi nì tin úǹ u-ba nìn dūu sú ti-Dindaanee. Bi nìn kpáaǹ sindaariya un nìn bí ti-Dindaan Diikun laakin bi kpáafí animbilee ki cáa cūnnì ki pú ubɔti Asayeel ní úǹ gbēeǹ kaa ti dɔ́miń ki jáń nì Jeerusaleem tiŋki yab.
20Joowaasi tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee nì tin kɔkɔ u ŋée ŋmàn̄ ki kā Juuda bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun. 21U-janjakpilib nìn bɔ́ntì kí kpɔ̀-u. Dalba Joowaasi sìntī Siila tiŋki watil púee ní bi kíntì-u ki kūū-u.
22U-janjakpilib bin nìn kūū-u gbantee di nìn sá Simeeyaati jipɔɔn Yoosabaadi nì Soomeer jipɔɔn Yeewoosabaadi. Bi nìn síb́-u ki ŋàl̄ u-naanjab Daafiidi Tiŋkin, ní u-jipɔɔn Amasiya fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.

english_text:
King Jehoahaz of Israel
1Jehoahaz son of Jehu became king of Israel in the twenty-third year of Joash's rule in Judah. Jehoahaz ruled 17 years from Samaria 2and disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong. He never stopped following the example of Jeroboam, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
3The Lord was angry with the Israelites, so he let King Hazael of Syria and his son Benhadad rule over them for a long time. 4Jehoahaz prayed to the Lord for help, and the Lord saw how terribly Hazael was treating the Israelites. He answered Jehoahaz 5by sending Israel a leader who rescued them from the Syrians, and the Israelites lived in peace as they had before. 6-7But Hazael had defeated Israel's army so badly that Jehoahaz had only 10 chariots, 50 cavalry troops, and 10,000 regular soldiers left in his army.
The Israelites kept sinning and following the example of Jeroboam's family. They did not tear down the sacred poles that had been set up in Samaria for the worship of the goddess Asherah.
8Everything else Jehoahaz did while he was king, including his brave deeds, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. 9Jehoahaz died and was buried in Samaria, and his son Jehoash became king.
King Jehoash of Israel
10Jehoash became king of Israel in the thirty-seventh year of Joash's rule in Judah, and he ruled 16 years from Samaria. 11He disobeyed the Lord by doing just like Jeroboam, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
12Everything else Jehoash did while he was king, including his war against King Amaziah of Judah, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. 13Jehoash died and was buried in Samaria beside the other Israelite kings. His son Jeroboam then became king.
Elisha the Prophet Dies
14 Some time before the death of King Jehoash, Elisha the prophet was very sick and about to die. Jehoash went in and stood beside him, crying. He said, “Master, what will Israel's chariots and cavalry be able to do without you?”
15-16“Grab a bow and some arrows,” Elisha told him, “and hold them in your hand.” Jehoash grabbed the bow and arrows and held them. Elisha placed his hand on the king's hand 17and said, “Open the window facing east.” When it was open, Elisha shouted, “Now shoot!” Jehoash shot an arrow and Elisha said, “That arrow is a sign that the Lord will help you completely defeat the Syrian army at Aphek.”
18Elisha said, “Pick up the arrows and hit the ground with them.” Jehoash grabbed the arrows and hit the ground three times, then stopped. 19Elisha became angry with the king and exclaimed, “If you had struck it five or six times, you would completely wipe out the Syrians. Now you will defeat them only three times.”
20Elisha died and was buried.
Every year in the spring, Moab's leaders sent raiding parties into Israel. 21Once, while some Israelites were burying a man's body, they saw a group of Moabites. The Israelites quickly threw the body into Elisha's tomb and ran away. As soon as the man's body touched the bones of Elisha, the man came back to life and stood up.
Israel Defeats Syria
22Israel was under the power of King Hazael of Syria during the entire rule of Jehoahaz. 23But the Lord was kind to the Israelites and showed them mercy because of his solemn agreement with their ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. In fact, he has never turned his back on them or let them be completely destroyed.
24Hazael died, and his son Benhadad then became king of Syria. 25King Jehoash of Israel attacked and defeated the Syrian army three times. He took back from Benhadad all the towns Hazael had captured in battle from his father Jehoahaz.
translation_text:
Joowakaasi, Isirayeel bɔtiu
1Akasiyasi jipɔɔn Joowaasi nín kpántì Juuda bɔtiu abin mmuŋku nì ata poonee ní Jeewuu jipɔɔn Joowakaasi kpántì Isirayeel bɔtiu. U nìn kóò Samaarii tiŋkin ní ki jíń dibeel abin saalku nì ali. 2U nìn ŋá tin kaa kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee. U nìn dū u-ba ki yá ki nákáǹ ikpiti in Neebaati jipɔɔn Jeerooboowaam nìn ŋá ki yāntì Isirayeel yab kɔ́ ikpitinee. Waa nìn fātì u-boon ki tīī-i. 3Ti-Dindaan nìn gíí Isirayeel pu diŋuul ní ki nìn dū-bi ki ŋá Siirii bɔtiu Asayeel nì u-jipɔɔn Been-Adaadi ŋaan. U nìn gíí bi-pu diŋuul míǹ an yúntì.
4Ama Joowakaasi nìn gbāam̀ ti-Dindaan ú sɔ̀ŋkì u-ŋuul Isirayeel yab pu ní u pílifiǹ-bi, di sá yii u nìn ká Siirii yab nín nìn wɔ́b́ Isirayeel yab puee. 5Ti-Dindaan nìn tīī Isirayeel yab ufiil ubɔ ní úǹ dɔ́miń ki fīī-bi ki nyántì Siirii yab ŋaan. Kí yòon̄ ŋyunti gbantee ní Isirayeel yab fātìi ká ŋgbansɔŋfi. 6Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, baa nìn kākatì bi-ba ki wāatì Jeerooboowaam nì u-dicaŋku yab kpitii in bi nìn ŋá ki yāntì Isirayeel yab kɔ́ ikpitinee. Áli gba diwaal Aseera waadɔŋu nìn gbíntìi cɔ́ Samaarii tiŋkin.
7Joowakaasi janjakitil poonee, an nìn pée kíǹ bitanjakaliibi binib imuŋku ili nì saalaa nì janjatɔrɔkub saalaa nì bijanjaliibi kutukub saalaa ja ní. Di sá yii Siirii bɔtiu nìn kūū bin kɔkɔ kíǹee. U nìn ŋá-bi kii ŋkpɔŋkpɔm min unil tèe ní.
8Joowakaasi tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee nì tin kɔkɔ u ŋée nì u-pɔ́ɔǹtam kɔkɔ ŋmàn̄ ki kā Isirayeel bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun. 9U kpíì ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ u-baabi ní bi síb́-u Samaarii tiŋkin. U-jipɔɔn Joowaasi di nìn fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.
Joowaasi, Isirayeel bɔtiu
10Juuda bɔtiu Joowaasi nín kpántì ubɔti abin ata kpá imuŋku ili poonee ní Joowakaasi jipɔɔn Joowaasi kpántì Isirayeel bɔtiu. U nìn kóò Samaarii tiŋkin ní ki jíń dibeel abin saalku nì diba. 11U nìn ŋá tin kaa kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee. U nìn dū u-ba ki yá ki nákáǹ ikpiti in Neebaati jipɔɔn Jeerooboowaam nìn ŋá ki yāntì Isirayeel yab kɔ́ ikpitinee. Waa nìn fātì u-boon ki tīī-i.
12Joowaasi tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee nì tin kɔkɔ u ŋée nì u-pɔ́ɔǹtam nì u nín jáń kujaau nì Juuda bɔtiu Amasiya puee ŋmàn̄ ki kā Isirayeel bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun. 13Joowaasi kpíì ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ u-baabi ní bi síb́-u Isirayeel bɔtiibi kaakulin Samaarii tiŋkin. Jeerooboowaam nín nìn fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.
Eeliisee nāatì yii Isirayeel yab làá já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ Siirii yab
14Eeliisee nìn búŋkì ki làá kpú ní Isirayeel bɔtiu cūtì kí màntì u-pu. U bàn̄ee ní ki tīntì u-pu ki bíi sūǹ ki lì yii: «M-baa! M-baa! A jítiǹ Isirayeel janjatɔrɔkub nì u-tanjakaliibi!» 15Ní Eeliisee bí-u yii: «Yòon̄ butɔbu nì ipiin!» Ní Joowaasi yōoǹ butɔbu nì ipiin. 16Ní Eeliisee bí-u yii: «Dáaĺ butɔbu!», ní u dáaĺ.
Ní Eeliisee dū u-ŋal ki ŋá ubɔti ŋalin 17ní ki bí yii: «Pìitī tɔkɔla un bí ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee!» Ní Joowaasi pīitì. Ní Eeliisee bí-u yii: «Dáaĺ butɔbu kí tɔ̄ mpiin!», ní u tɔ́. Ní Eeliisee bí yii: «Ti-Dindaan jajil piiŋŋu dee, dijajil din a làá jī Siirii yab puee dee. A làá já kí pɔ́ɔkiǹ Siirii yab Afeeki tiŋkin kí nàan̄-bi.» 18Ní Eeliisee bí Joowaasi yii: «Yòon̄ a-piiŋyi!» Ní ubɔti yōoǹ. Ní Eeliisee bí-u yii: «Dáaĺ kí yā kitiŋ!» Ní ubɔti dáaĺ ki yá kitiŋ ŋfunyɔm mita ní ki síl̀. 19Ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Eeliisee gíí u-pu diŋuul ki bí yii: «A yaa bàà dáaĺ ki yá kitiŋ ŋfunyɔm miŋmoo àá miluu puee, a bàà làá já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ Siirii yab kí nàan̄-bi kɔkɔ múb. Too, kɔŋkɔnnee, mita ja ní a làá já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ Siirii yab.»
20Eeliisee kpíìyee ní bi síb́-u.
Dibindi kamaayee, Moowaab yab nìn dòoń Isirayeel tiŋkin ki fúkuĺ-bi. 21Dalbee Isirayeel yab biba cūtì kí síb́ unil ní ki ká akiti gbanti tí dòoń. Bi nìn dū utaŋkpiilee ki bíl̀ Eeliisee kaakulin malaa ki sáǹ ki nín kùnní. Utaŋkpiilee gbēē Eeliisee kpabiŋee ní ki fīkitì ki yáatìi yúl̀.
Isirayeel yab jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Siirii yab
22Siirii bɔtiu Asayeel nìn sāaǹ Isirayeel yab iwiin in kɔkɔ Joowakaasi dūu kāl̀ tibɔtiil Isirayeel beelinee. 23Ama ti-Dindaan nìn súń Isirayeel yab saai ki dàkā-bi u-laŋŋaŋfitiiku ki dū bi-kpitii ki pú-bi. Dipoondi din u nìn pōoǹ Abraam nì Isaaki nì Jaakɔbee pu ní u nìn ŋá míǹ ki tīī-bi. An puee waa nìn nāaǹ-bi. Waa nìn dá láá dū-bi ki fá.
24Siirii bɔtiu Asayeel kpíìyee ní u-jipɔɔn Been-Adaadi fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti. 25Joowakaasi jipɔɔn Joowaasi nìn fātìi fōō ntimu mun Asayeel nìn jáń ki fōō u-baa Joowakaasi ceeyee u-jipɔɔn Been-Adaadi ŋaan. Joowaasi nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Been-Adaadi ŋfunyɔm mita pu ní ki fātìi fōō Isirayeel timmu gbanti kɔkɔ.

english_text:
King Amaziah of Judah
(2 Chronicles 25.1-24)
1Amaziah son of Joash became king of Judah in the second year of Jehoash's rule in Israel. 2Amaziah was 25 years old when he became king, and he ruled 29 years from Jerusalem, which was also the hometown of his mother Jehoaddin.
3Amaziah followed the example of his father Joash by obeying the Lord and doing right. But he was not as faithful as his ancestor David. 4Amaziah did not destroy the local shrines, and they were still used as places for offering sacrifices.
5As soon as Amaziah had control of Judah, he arrested and killed the officers who had murdered his father. 6 But the children of those officers were not killed. The Lord had commanded in the Law of Moses that only the people who sinned were to be punished, not their parents or children.
7While Amaziah was king, he killed 10,000 Edomite soldiers in Salt Valley. He captured the town of Sela and renamed it Joktheel, which is still its name.
8One day, Amaziah sent a message to King Jehoash of Israel: “Come out and face me in battle!”
9Jehoash sent back this reply:
Once upon a time, a small thornbush in Lebanon announced that his son was going to marry the daughter of a large cedar tree. But a wild animal came along and trampled the small bush.
10Amaziah, you think you're so powerful because you defeated Edom. Go ahead and celebrate—but stay at home. If you cause any trouble, both you and your kingdom of Judah will be destroyed.
11But Amaziah refused to listen. So Jehoash and his troops marched to the town of Beth-Shemesh in Judah to attack Amaziah and his troops. 12During the battle, Judah's army was crushed. Every soldier from Judah ran back home, 13and Jehoash captured Amaziah.
Jehoash then marched to Jerusalem and broke down the city wall from Ephraim Gate to Corner Gate, a section nearly 200 meters long. 14He took the gold and silver, as well as everything of value from the Lord's temple and the king's treasury. He took hostages, then returned to Samaria.
15Everything else Jehoash did while he was king, including his brave deeds and how he defeated King Amaziah of Judah, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. 16Jehoash died and was buried in Samaria beside the other Israelite kings. His son Jeroboam then became king.
17Fifteen years after Jehoash died, 18-20some people in Jerusalem plotted against Amaziah. He was able to escape to the town of Lachish, but another group of people caught him and killed him there. His body was taken back to Jerusalem on horseback and buried beside his ancestors.
Everything else Amaziah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah. 21After his death the people of Judah made his son Azariah king, even though he was only 16 at the time. 22Azariah was the one who later recaptured and rebuilt the town of Elath.
King Jeroboam the Second of Israel
23Jeroboam son of Jehoash became king of Israel in the fifteenth year of Amaziah's rule in Judah. Jeroboam ruled 41 years from Samaria. 24He disobeyed the Lord by following the evil example of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
25 Jeroboam extended the boundaries of Israel from Lebo-Hamath in the north to the Dead Sea in the south, just as the Lord had promised his servant Jonah son of Amittai, who was a prophet from Gath-Hepher. 26The Lord helped Jeroboam do this because he had seen how terribly the Israelites were suffering, whether slave or free, and no one was left to help them. 27And since the Lord had promised that he would not let Israel be completely destroyed, he helped Jeroboam rescue them.
28Everything else Jeroboam did while he was king, including his brave deeds and how he recaptured the towns of Damascus and Hamath, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. 29Jeroboam died and was buried, and his son Zechariah became king.
translation_text:
Amasiyaawuu, Juuda bɔtiu
(2 Kroo 25.1-4,11-12,17-28, 26.1-2)
1Joowakaasi jipɔɔn Joowaasi nín kāl̀ Isirayeel beelin pu tibɔtiil abin alee, ní Joowaasi jipɔɔn Amasiyaawuu kpántì Juuda tiŋki bɔtiu. 2U nìn cáá abin mmuŋku nì aŋmoo ní ki kpántì ubɔti ní ki jíń dibeel abin mmuŋku nì awa Jeerusaleem tiŋkin. U-na nìn sá Jeerusaleem ní bi yíì-u yii Yoowadan. 3Amasiyaawuu nìn ŋá tin fáatiǹ ti-Dindaanee, ama waa nìn nín bàn̄ u-naanja Daafiidi ní. U nìn pée ŋá kii u-baa Joowaasee ní. 4Nì míǹ kɔkɔee waa nìn kúntì isaraafan in nìn bí ŋgbantamu puee. Samaa nìn gbíntìi cáà niin ki ŋáań saraabi ki tùutī talaalub.
5Ŋyunti ŋun Amasiyaawuu beel kāl̀ tiŋan ki báaǹ inyaanee ní u kūū u-janjakpilib bin nìn kūū u-baa ubɔti Joosiyaasee. 6Ama waa nìn kūū binikpɔliibi gbanti biyaamu, ki nóó nì án nín ŋmàn̄ Mooyiisi Marau gbɔŋkun puee. Ti-Dindaan nìn sòon̄ mara gbɔŋku gbanti poon yii: «Baa máaǹ kí kpɔ̀ bibaatiibi, bi-biyaamu kpitii pu, kaa tí máaǹ kí kpɔ̀ mbiyaamu, mu-baabi kpitii pu. Un ŋá ikpitee, úǹ ní bí kpɔ̀». 7Úǹ di jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Eedoom yab janjaliibi binib kutukub saalaa Ŋyaam tantakalin. Kujaau gbanti poon ní u jáń ki fōō Seera tiŋki ki pú-kì diyindi yii Yookiteel. Bi gbíntìi yíì kitiŋ gbanti míǹ ki dāa sāā díǹ.
8Niinee ní Amasiyaawuu lēē ituun ki tú Isirayeel bɔtiu Joowaasi, Joowakaasi jipɔɔn nì Jeewuu naantiiu cee bí tùkù-u yii: «Dāan̄, man nì si tí já!» 9Ní Isirayeel bɔtiu Joowaasi tú bí cùú tùkù Juuda bɔtiu Amasiyaawuu yii: «Bukuŋkumbu subiki kiba di nìn bí Leebanɔn jool pu. Dalbee ní kì cūtìi ká Seedir subu ní ki bí-bu yii: <Dū a-bisal kí tīī m-jipɔɔn ú cáá!> Ama upeel ubɔ nyánní Leebanɔn joolee pu ní ki tāā ki mátì bukuŋkumbuee. 10Tiŋman a jáń ki pɔ̄ɔkiǹ Eedoom yabee ní an yòontí-si. Nín̄ kā a-dumpu soooo kí nīn fàal̀ a-jajil gbanti pu. Ba pu ní a là kí kíĺ kujaau kun poon ní bi làá já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ sii nì Juuda janjaliibee?»
11Ama Amasiyaawuu kaa nìn pílifiǹ-u. Niinee Isirayeel bɔtiu Joowaasi yíkìń kujaau pu ki bāań ki dūu sìkī nì Juuda bɔtiu Amasiyaawuu Beeti-Seemeesi tiŋkin, Juuda tiŋkpaaŋki kiban. 12Isirayeel yab nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Juuda yab ní bíǹ sáǹ ki nín kùǹ. 13Isirayeel bɔtiu nìn cúú Juuda bɔtiu Amasiyaawuu, Joosiyaasi jipɔɔn, Akasiyasi naantiiu kuyuŋu Beeti-Seemeesi tiŋkin, ní ki dɔ́miń Jeerusaleem ki gbáń ki wīī digundi an wāā kii meetab alaataa ali kí yòon̄ Eefiraayiim punyɔkɔki kí cáá sāā Ŋfaŋfakam punyɔkɔki. 14U nìn yōoǹ sindaariya nì animbil nì tiwan tin kɔkɔ nìn bí ti-Dindaan Diikun nì tigaajawan tin kɔkɔ nìn bí dibeecindinee. U nìn cúú binib biba mun ki kpáàa búntì Samaarii tiŋkin.
15Joowaasi tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee nì tin kɔkɔ u ŋée nì u-pɔ́ɔǹtam nì u nì Juuda bɔtiu nín jáń kujaau kuŋyee kɔkɔ ŋmàn̄ ki kā Isirayeel bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun. 16Joowaasi kpíì ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ u-baabi ní bi síb́-u Samaarii tiŋkin Isirayeel bɔtiibi kaakulin. U-jipɔɔn Jeerooboowaam di nìn fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.
17Isirayeel bɔtiu Joowaasi, Joowakaasi jipɔɔn nín kpíì boonee, Juuda bɔtiu Amasiyaawuu, Joowaasi jipɔɔn gíti ŋá abin saalku ní ki nín kpíì. 18Amasiyaawuu tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee ŋmàn̄ ki kā Juuda bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun.
19Bi nìn bɔ́ntì kí kpɔ̀-u Jeerusaleem ní u sáǹ ki búntì Lakiisi. Ní bi tú binib jìn̄ u-boon ki tin kūuń-u niin. 20Boonee ní bi dū-u ki ŋá tɔrɔku un itaamu kupaau dátée poon ki gíiǹní Jeerusaleem, ní bi dū-u ki síb́ u-baabi kaakulin Daafiidi Tiŋkin. 21U-jipɔɔn Asariyasi nìn cáá abin saalku nì diba ní Juuda yab kɔkɔ dū-u ki kāaǹ dibeel u-baa yil pu. 22U-baa Amasiyaawuu kpíì ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ u-naanjab boonee, ní u fātìi fōō Eelaati tiŋki ki tīī Juuda yab ní ki fātìi máń-kì.
Jeerooboowaam liliiti, Isirayeel bɔtiu
23Juuda bɔtiu Amasiyaawuu, Joowaasi jipɔɔn nín jíń dibeel abin saalku poonee, ní Isirayeel bɔtiu Joowaasi jipɔɔn Jeerooboowaam kpántì Isirayeel bɔtiu. U nìn kóò Samaarii ní ki jíń dibeel abin imuŋku ili nì diba. 24U nìn ŋá tin kaa kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee. U nìn dū u-ba ki yá ki nákáǹ ikpiti in Neebaati jipɔɔn Jeerooboowaam nìn ŋá ki yāntì Isirayeel yab kɔ́ ikpitinee. 25Úǹ di jáń ki fātìi fōō Isirayeel timmu kí yòon̄ Leeboo-Amaati kí cáá sāā Arabaa tiŋkuu, ki nóó nì ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín nìn dī u-bɔnaatiliu Yoona, Amiitaayi jipɔɔn, ugaati-Eebeerja pu ki sòon̄ tiŋyee. 26Di sá yii ti-Dindaan nìn lafun ká inimɔɔn in poon ní Isirayeel yab nìn bée. Bi nìn bíi jīǹ falaa tikpil. Uyumbuɔɔɔ, un tɔ́ u-beeyaaa, báà ubɔ nì ubɔ kaa nìn bí kí ŋmā kí jòoń-bi. 27Ama ti-Dindaan kaa nìn lēē yii u làá pítí Isirayeel nibul kitiŋ pu. An pu ní u nìn dī Joowaasi jipɔɔn Jeerooboowaam pu ki fīī-bi.
28Jeerooboowaam tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee nì tin kɔkɔ u ŋée nì u-pɔ́ɔǹtam nì u nín jáń tijáti puee nì u nín fātìi fōō Juuda timmu Damaasi nì Amaati ki tīī Isirayeel puee kɔkɔ ŋmàn̄ ki kā Isirayeel bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun. 29Jeerooboowaam kpíì ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ u-naanjab ní bi síb́-u Samaarii tiŋkin, Isirayeel bɔtiibi kaakulin. U-jipɔɔn Sakari di nìn fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.

english_text:
King Azariah of Judah
(2 Chronicles 26.1-23)
1Azariah son of Amaziah became king of Judah in Jeroboam's twenty-seventh year as king of Israel. 2He was only 16 years old when he became king, and he ruled 52 years from Jerusalem, which was also the hometown of his mother Jecoliah.
3Azariah obeyed the Lord by doing right, as his father Amaziah had done. 4But Azariah did not destroy the local shrines, and they were still used as places for offering sacrifices.
5The Lord punished Azariah with leprosy for the rest of his life. He wasn't allowed to live in the royal palace, so his son Jotham lived there and ruled in his place.
6Everything else Azariah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah. 7 Azariah died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem. His son Jotham then became king.
King Zechariah of Israel
8Zechariah son of Jeroboam became king of Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Azariah's rule in Judah, but he ruled only six months from Samaria. 9Like his ancestors, Zechariah disobeyed the Lord by following the evil ways of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
10Shallum son of Jabesh plotted against Zechariah and killed him in public. Shallum then became king. 11-12 So the Lord had kept his promise to Jehu that the next four kings of Israel would come from his family.
Everything else Zechariah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
King Shallum of Israel
13Shallum became king of Israel in the thirty-ninth year of Azariah's rule in Judah. But only one month after Shallum became king, 14-16Menahem son of Gadi came to Samaria from Tirzah and killed him. Menahem then became king. The town of Tiphsah would not surrender to him, so he destroyed it and all the surrounding towns as far as Tirzah. He killed everyone living in Tiphsah, and with his sword he even ripped open pregnant women.
Everything else Shallum did while he was king, including his plot against Zechariah, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
King Menahem of Israel
17Menahem became king of Israel in Azariah's thirty-ninth year as king of Judah, and he ruled Israel ten years from Samaria. 18He constantly disobeyed the Lord by following the example of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
19During Menahem's rule, King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria invaded Israel. He agreed to help Menahem keep control of his kingdom, if Menahem would pay him over 34 tons of silver. 20So Menahem ordered every rich person in Israel to give him at least 50 pieces of silver, and he gave it all to Tiglath Pileser, who stopped his attack and left Israel.
21Everything else Menahem did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. 22Menahem died, and his son Pekahiah became king.
King Pekahiah of Israel
23Pekahiah became king of Israel in the fiftieth year of Azariah's rule in Judah, and he ruled two years from Samaria. 24He disobeyed the Lord and caused the Israelites to sin, just as Jeroboam son of Nebat had done.
25Pekah son of Remaliah was Pekahiah's chief officer, but he made plans to kill the king. So he and 50 men from Gilead broke into the strongest part of the palace in Samaria and murdered Pekahiah, together with Argob and Arieh. Pekah then became king.
26Everything else Pekahiah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
King Pekah of Israel
27Pekah son of Remaliah became king of Israel in Azariah's fifty-second year as king of Judah, and he ruled 20 years from Samaria. 28He disobeyed the Lord and followed the evil example of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
29During Pekah's rule, King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria marched into Israel. He captured the territories of Gilead and Galilee, including the towns of Ijon, Abel-Bethmaacah, Janoah, Kedesh, and Hazor, as well as the entire territory of Naphtali. Then he took Israelites from those regions to Assyria as prisoners.
30In the twentieth year of Jotham's rule in Judah, Hoshea son of Elah plotted against Pekah and murdered him. Hoshea then became king of Israel.
31Everything else Pekah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
King Jotham of Judah
(2 Chronicles 27.1-9)
32Jotham son of Azariah became king of Judah in the second year of Pekah's rule in Israel. 33Jotham was 25 years old when he became king, and he ruled 16 years from Jerusalem. His mother Jerusha was the daughter of Zadok.
34Jotham followed the example of his father by obeying the Lord and doing right. 35It was Jotham who rebuilt the Upper Gate that led into the court around the Lord's temple. But the local shrines were not destroyed, and they were still used as places for offering sacrifices.
36Everything else Jotham did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah. 37During his rule, the Lord let King Rezin of Syria and King Pekah of Israel start attacking Judah. 38Jotham died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Ahaz became king.
translation_text:
Asariyasi, Juuda bɔtiu
(2 Kroo 26.3-4,21-23)
1 Isirayeel bɔtiu Jeerooboowaam nín jíń dibeel abin mmuŋku nì aluli poonee ní Amasiyaawuu jipɔɔn Asariyasi kpántì Juuda bɔtiu. 2U nìn cáá abin saalku nì diba ní ki kpántì ubɔti. U nìn kóò Jeerusaleem ní ki jíń dibeel abin imuŋku ili nì saalaa nì ali. U-na nìn sá Jeerusaleem ní bi yíì-u yii Yeekooliya. 3U nìn ŋá tin fáatiǹ ti-Dindaanee, kii u-baa Amasiyaawuu nín nìn ŋá puee ní deedee. 4Ama waa nìn kúntì isaraafan in nìn bí ŋgbantamu puee. Samaa nìn gbíntìi cáà niin ki ŋáań saraabi ki tùutī talaalub.
5Ti-Dindaan nìn yāntì ubɔti búŋkì. U nìn kpántì unyaŋgbanti áli u-kúm dal. An puee u nìn kóò kudii kubɔn laaba ní u-jipɔɔn Yootam un nìn sá bin kpèé dibeecindi kpiliuee kpòotī kitiŋ.
6Jooram tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee nì tin kɔkɔ u ŋée ŋmàn̄ ki kā Juuda bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun. 7Asariyasi kpíì ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ u-baabi ní bi síb́-u Daafiidi Tiŋkin. U-jipɔɔn Yootam di fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.
Sakari, Isirayeel bɔtiu
8Juuda bɔtiu Asariyasi nín jíń dibeel abin ali kpá imuŋku ili poonee ní Jeerooboowaam jipɔɔn Sakari kpántì Isirayeel bɔtiu. U nìn kóò Samaarii ní ki jíń dibeel iŋmal iluu. 9U nìn ŋá tin kaa kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee kii u-naanjab nín nìn ŋá puee. Waa nìn kākatì u-ba ki wāatì ikpiti in Neebaati jipɔɔn Jeerooboowaam nìn ŋá ki yāntì Isirayeel yab kɔ́ ikpitinee. 10Yabeesi jipɔɔn Saluum nìn bɔ́ntì u-pu ní ki kūū-u samaa nimbiin. U kpíìyee ní úǹ fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.
11Sakari tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee ŋmàn̄ ki kā Isirayeel bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun.
