12Ti-Dindaan nín nìn tùkū Jeewuu puee dee yii: «A-jipɔmbi kí cáá sāā anaantitɔntɔkɔ anaa pu di làá kàl̄ Isirayeel beel pu.» Míǹ ní an lafun jítì.
Saluum, Isirayeel bɔtiu
13Juuda bɔtiu Oosiyasi nín jíń dibeel abin dibindi kpá imuŋku ili poonee ní Yabeesi jipɔɔn Saluum kpántì Isirayeel bɔtiu. U nìn kóò Samaarii ní ki jíń dibeel uŋmal ubɔ ja. 14Gaadi jipɔɔn Meenayeem nìn nyánní Tiirsa ki dɔ́miń Samaarii ní ki kūū Saluum ní ki fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.
15Saluum tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee nì u nín bɔ́ntì pu ki kūū Sakaree ŋmàn̄ ki kā Isirayeel bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun.
16Niinee ní Meenayeem cūtìi jáń nì Tapuuwa tiŋki ki kūū ki céetì ki-nib kɔkɔ, ní ki bīlim̀ kí yòon̄ kitiŋ kin dɔ̄ Tiirsee ki tin sāā Tapuuwa. Kun pu u nìn kūū-bee di sá yii baa nìn pīitì-u kitiŋee punyɔkɔki ú kɔ́. U nìn pūtì bipɔdambi kɔkɔ.
Meenayeem, Isirayeel bɔtiu
17Juuda bɔtiu Asariyasi nín jíń dibeel dibindi diba kpá imuŋku ili poonee ní Gaadi jipɔɔn Meenayeem kpántì Isirayeel bɔtiu. U nìn kóò Samaarii ní ki jíń dibeel abin saalaa. 18U nìn ŋá tin kaa kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee. U-maŋfal wiiŋyi kɔkɔ poonee, waa nìn kākatì ki wāatì Neebaati jipɔɔn Jeerooboowaam kpitii in u nìn ŋá ki yāntì Isirayeel yab kɔ́ ikpitinee.
19Asuur bɔtiu Puul nìn kɔ́ Isirayeel tiŋkin kí já nì Meenayeem, ama ní u ŋá malaa ki nyàab̄ animbil tɔɔnib mmuŋku nì saalaa ki tīī-u ú tūtuǹ-u ú ká mpɔn kí mɔ̀tīí kàan̄ u-beel. 20Kí ŋmā kí pà an nimbiliŋee, Meenayeem nìn síiǹ yii Isirayeel tiŋki poon gaajab kɔkɔ ń pà lampoo. Unil kamaa nìn máaǹ kí tīī animbil jitɔmbi imuŋku ili nì saalaa ní. Asuur bɔtiu fōō an nimbiliŋee ní ki fātìi nín gítí u-tiŋkin.
21Meenayeem tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee nì tin kɔkɔ u ŋée ŋmàn̄ ki kā Isirayeel bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun. 22Meenayeem kpíì ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ u-baabi ní u-jipɔɔn Peekaya fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.
Peekaya, Isirayeel bɔtiu
23Juuda bɔtiu Asariyasi nín jíń dibeel abin imuŋku ili nì saalaa poonee ní Meenayeem jipɔɔn Peekaya kpántì Isirayeel bɔtiu. U nìn kóò Samaarii ní ki jíń dibeel abin ali. 24U nìn ŋá tin kaa kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee. Waa nìn kākatì u-ba ki wāatì Neebaati jipɔɔn Jeerooboowaam kpitii in u nìn ŋá ki yāntì Isirayeel yab kɔ́ ikpitinee. 25Reemaliyawuu jipɔɔn Peekaa un sá un nìn ŋúb̀ ubɔti janjawanti kujaau poonee nìn bɔ́ntì ki kūū ubɔti Peekaya nì Argoob nì Ariyee Samaarii tiŋkin, ubɔti diiku kubɔn. Galaadi yab janjaliibi imuŋku ili nì saalaa nìn bí u-cee. U kūū Peekaya ki dóò mimmee ní ki fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.
26Peekaya tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee nì tin kɔkɔ u ŋée ŋmàn̄ ki kā Isirayeel bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun.
Peekaa, Isirayeel bɔtiu
27Juuda bɔtiu Asariyasi nín jíń dibeel abin imuŋku ili nì saalaa nì ali poonee ní Reemaliyawuu jipɔɔn Peekaa kpántì Isirayeel bɔtiu. U nìn kóò Samaarii ní ki jíń dibeel abin mmuŋku. 28U nìn ŋá tin kaa kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee. Waa nìn kākatì u-ba ki wāatì Neebaati jipɔɔn Jeerooboowaam kpitii in u nìn ŋá ki yāntì Isirayeel yab kɔ́ ikpitinee.
29Isirayeel bɔtiu Peekaa beel yuntiŋuee ní Asuur bɔtiu Tiigilaati-Piilneeseer dɔ́miń ki jáń ki fōō Yoon nì Abeel-Beeti-Maaka nì Yanoowa nì Keedeesi nì Asɔɔr nì Galaadi nì Galiilee timmu ki kpáaǹ Neefitalii yab timmu kɔkɔ. U nìn kóoǹ ntimu gbanti nib kɔkɔ ki cáa cūnnì Asuur tiŋkin. 30Eela jipɔɔn Oosee nìn bɔ́ntì Reemaliyawuu jipɔɔn Peekaa pu ní ki kūū-u ní ki fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti. Oosiyasi jipɔɔn Yootam nín jíń dibeel Juuda tiŋkin abin mmuŋku poonee ní tíǹ jítì.
31Peekaa tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee nì tin kɔkɔ u ŋée ŋmàn̄ ki kā Isirayeel bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun.
Yootam, Juuda bɔtiu
(2 Kroo 27.1-3,7-9)
32Reemaliyawuu jipɔɔn Peekaa nín jíń dibeel Isirayeel tiŋkin abin ali poonee ní Oosiyasi jipɔɔn Yootam kpántì Juuda bɔtiu. 33U nìn cáá abin mmuŋku nì aŋmoo ní ki kpántì ubɔti ní ki nìn kóò Jeerusaleem ki jíń dibeel abin saalku nì diba. Bi nìn yíì u-na yii Yeerusaa, Sadooki bisal. 34U nìn ŋá tin fáatiǹ ti-Dindaanee. U nìn pée ŋá kii u-baa Oosiyasi nín nìn ŋá puee ní deedee. 35Ama waa nìn kúntì isaraafan in nìn bí ŋgbantamu puee. Samaa nìn gbíntìi cáà niin ki ŋáań saraabi ki tùutī talaalub.
Úǹ di nìn máń ti-Dindaan Diiku punyɔkɔki kin bí Yilpu púee.
36Yootam tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee nì tin kɔkɔ u ŋée ŋmàn̄ ki kā Juuda bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun. 37Yootam beel yuntiŋuee, ti-Dindaan nìn yāntì Siirii bɔtiu Reesiin nì Reemaliyawuu jipɔɔn Peekaa dòoń ki jáà nì Juuda yab. 38Yootam kpíì ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ u-baabi ní bi síb́-u u-baabi kaakulin, u-naanja Daafiidi Tiŋkin. U-jipɔɔn Akaasi di nìn fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.

english_text:
King Ahaz of Judah
(2 Chronicles 28.1-27)
1Ahaz son of Jotham became king of Judah in the seventeenth year of Pekah's rule in Israel. 2He was 20 years old at the time, and he ruled from Jerusalem for 16 years.
Ahaz wasn't like his ancestor David. Instead, he disobeyed the Lord 3 and was even more sinful than the kings of Israel. He sacrificed his own son, which was a disgusting custom of the nations that the Lord had forced out of Israel. 4Ahaz offered sacrifices at the local shrines, as well as on every hill and in the shade of large trees.
5-6 While Ahaz was ruling Judah, the king of Edom recaptured the town of Elath from Judah and forced out the people of Judah. Edomites then moved into Elath, and they still live there.
About the same time, King Rezin of Syria and King Pekah of Israel marched to Jerusalem and attacked, but they could not capture it.
7Ahaz sent a message to King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria that said, “Your Majesty, King Rezin and King Pekah are attacking me, your loyal servant. Please come and rescue me.” 8Along with the message, Ahaz sent silver and gold from the Lord's temple and from the palace treasury as a gift for the Assyrian king.
9As soon as Tiglath Pileser received the message, he and his troops marched to Syria. He captured the capital city of Damascus, then he took the people living there to the town of Kir as prisoners and killed King Rezin.
10Later, Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath Pileser. And while Ahaz was there, he saw an altar and sent a model of it back to Uriah the priest, along with the plans for building one. 11Uriah followed the plans and built an altar exactly like the one in Damascus, finishing it just before Ahaz came back.
12When Ahaz returned, he went to see the altar and to offer sacrifices on it. He walked up to the altar 13and poured wine over it. Then he offered sacrifices to please the Lord, to give him thanks, and to ask for his blessings. 14 After that, he had the bronze altar moved aside, so his new altar would be right in front of the Lord's temple. 15He told Uriah the priest:
From now on, the morning and evening sacrifices as well as all gifts of grain and wine are to be offered on this altar. The sacrifices for the people and for the king must also be offered here. Sprinkle the blood from all the sacrifices on it, but leave the bronze altar for me to use for prayer and finding out what God wants me to do.
16Uriah did everything Ahaz told him.
17 Ahaz also had the side panels and the small bowls taken off the movable stands in the Lord's temple. He had the large bronze bowl, called the Sea, removed from the bronze bulls on which it rested and had it placed on a stand made of stone. 18He took down the special tent that was used for worship on the Sabbath and closed up the private entrance that the kings of Judah used for going into the temple. He did all these things to please Tiglath Pileser.
19Everything else Ahaz did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah. 20 Ahaz died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Hezekiah became king.
translation_text:
Akaasi, Juuda bɔtiu
(2 Kroo 28.1-27)
1Reemaliyawuu jipɔɔn Peekaa nín jíń dibeel Isirayeel tiŋkin abin saalku nì ali poonee ní Yootam jipɔɔn Akaasi kpántì Juuda bɔtiu. 2Akaasi nìn cáá abin mmuŋku ní ki kpántì ubɔti. U nìn kóò Jeerusaleem ní ki jíń dibeel abin saalku nì diba. Waa nìn ŋá tin fáatì ti-Dindaan u-Nimbɔtiuee kii u-naanja Daafiidi nín nìn ŋá puee. 3Ama u nìn dī Isirayeel yab bɔtiibi saŋŋu ní, áli gba u nìn dū u-jipɔɔn ubɔ ki tōotì. Ntimbiil tuuŋŋi gbanti ní atimbun ŋin nib ti-Dindaan nìn jìn̄ ki fōō bi-tiŋki ki dūu tīī Isirayeel yabee nìn ŋáań. 4U nìn ŋá saraabi ki tūutì talaalub awaa saraafaŋyi nì ŋgbantamu pu nì isufi in cáá tifaalee taapu.
5Niinee Siirii bɔtiu Reesiin nì Reemaliyawuu jipɔɔn Peekaa, Isirayeel bɔtiu dɔ́miń kí já nì Akaasi ní ki māntìi tú Jeerusaleem tiŋki, ama baa nìn ŋúń ki jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-u. 6Ŋyunti gbanti ní Siirii bɔtiu Reesiin fōō Eelaati tiŋki Juuda yab ŋaan ki gíiǹ ki tīī Eedoom yab ní bíǹ fātìi gítìń ki kíǹ ki kóò niin áli ki dāa sāā díǹ.
7Akaasi nìn tú binib bí cù Asuur bɔtiu Tiigilaati-Piilneeseer cee kí tùkù-u yii: «M sá a-tɔntɔnliu nì a-jipɔɔn ní. Siirii nì Isirayeel bɔtiibi dɔ́miń kí já nì mi, dāan̄ kí fīī-mi kí nyāntí bi-ŋaan!» 8Ní Akaasi yōoǹ animbil nì sindaariya un nìn bí ti-Dindaan Diikunee nì tigaajawan tin bí dibeecindinee ki tú bí cáá pɔ̄ Asuur bɔtiu. 9Asuur bɔtiu nìn pílifiǹ-u ní ki cūtì u-ba ki jáń nì Damaasi yab ní ki fōō bi-tiŋki. U nìn kóoǹ binib bin kɔkɔ nìn bí kitiŋee poonee ki cáa cūnnì Kiiri tiŋkin ní ki kūū ubɔti Reesiin.
10Ubɔti Akaasi nìn yíkìi cūtì Damaasi tiŋkin kí ká Asuur bɔtiu Tiigilaati-Piilneeseer. U bàn̄ee ní ki ká nsaraafan ŋubɔ niin, ní u lēē nsaraafanee nín bí puee kɔkɔ ki tú bi cáa cūnnì ki tīī usaraaŋal Uriya ú mā míǹ deedeedee. 11Uriya nìn máń nsaraafanee ki nóó nì ubɔti Akaasi nín bí yii ú mā-ŋu puee. U nìn máń-ŋu ki dóò ki wāatì ní ubɔti nín nyánní Damaasi ki fātìi gítìń. 12Ŋyunti ŋun ubɔti nyánní Damaasi ki fātìi gítìń ki ká nsaraafanee ní u sútìi pìl̄-ŋu, 13ní úǹ u-ba ŋá nsaraafanee pu saraawɔkaa nì tijin saraau, ní ki fá ŋu-pu ndaam. U nìn gíti ŋá mpèé saraau nsaraafanee pu ní ki dū saraayee fatikuu ki yāaǹ ŋu-pu. 14U nìn yāntì bi nìkī tasa kúti saraafaŋŋu ŋun bi nìn máń ki dūu sú ti-Dindaanee. Nsaraafan gbanti ŋúǹ nìn bí ti-Dindaan Diiku punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu, an dàkà yii nsaraafan mpɔɔn ŋun ubɔti yāntì bi máńee nì ti-Dindaan Diiku kansikin, ama ní u nìkī-ŋu ki cáa cūnnì ubɔti saraafaŋŋuee boon, ŋgiil pú. 15Boonee ní ubɔti Akaasi tīī usaraaŋakpil Uriya mara nee yii: «Kí yòon̄ díǹ kí nīn cée, nsaraafan ŋkpaan nee pu ní a làá nīn kíǹ ki ŋáań saraawɔkaa un a ŋáań kutaafaau kamaayee nì tijimpin saraau un a ŋáań kujoou kamaayee, nì ubɔti saraawɔkaabi nì tijimpin saraabi, nì samaa kɔkɔ nín ŋáań tijimpin saraabi biŋyee nì ndaam min bi féeńee. Saraabi gbanti kɔkɔ fatikubee, á kpáatí kí pɔ̀l̄ nsaraafanee pu. An yaa kíǹ tasa kúti saraafaŋŋu ŋúǹ bɔtee, m làá dàkafì kí kpèè m nín làá ŋá-ŋu puee.»
16Usaraaŋakpil Uriya nìn ŋá ubɔti nín tīī-u mara ú ŋá puee kɔkɔ. 17Ubɔti nìn gíí ki lēē adɔpampan ŋin bi nìn dūu kpáá tasa kúti tɔrɔkub bin nìn sí ti-Dindaan Diikunee, ní ki cúú kusɔŋkpaaŋŋu kun nìn tɔ́kɔ́ tɔrɔkubee puee nì kusɔŋkpaaŋŋu dikuŋkundi kun nìn tɔ́kɔ́ inajaa saalaa nì ili puee ki tɔ́kɔtì tɔ́kɔtì ki dūu síiǹ kitiŋ ataŋkpee pu. 18Kí fáatiǹ Asuur bɔtiuee, ubɔti nìn kpītì ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dikpaaŋku kun bi nìn máń ti-Dindaan Diikunee, nì nsan ŋun ubɔti nìn dìŋfī kí kɔ́ kunimbɔtidiinee.
19Akaasi tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee nì tin kɔkɔ u ŋée ŋmàn̄ ki kā Juuda bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun. 20Akaasi kpíì ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ u-baabi ní bi síb́-u Daafiidi Tiŋkin. U-jipɔɔn Eeseekiyaasi di fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.

english_text:
King Hoshea of Israel
1Hoshea son of Elah became king of Israel in the twelfth year of Ahaz's rule in Judah, and he ruled nine years from Samaria. 2Hoshea disobeyed the Lord and sinned, but not as much as the earlier Israelite kings had done.
3During Hoshea's rule, King Shalmaneser of Assyria invaded Israel; he took control of the country and made Hoshea pay taxes. 4But later, Hoshea refused to pay the taxes and asked King So of Egypt to help him rebel. When Shalmaneser found out, he arrested Hoshea and put him in prison.
Samaria Is Destroyed and the Israelites Are Taken to Assyria
5Shalmaneser invaded Israel and attacked the city of Samaria for three years, 6before capturing it in the ninth year of Hoshea's rule. The Assyrian king took the Israelites away to Assyria as prisoners. He forced some of them to live in the town of Halah, others to live near the Habor River in the territory of Gozan, and still others to live in towns where the Median people lived.
7All of this happened because the people of Israel had sinned against the Lord their God, who had rescued them from Egypt, where they had been slaves. They worshiped foreign gods, 8followed the customs of the nations that the Lord had forced out of Israel, and were just as sinful as the Israelite kings. 9Even worse, the Israelites tried to hide their sins from the Lord their God. They built their own local shrines everywhere in Israel—from small towns to large, walled cities. 10 They also built stone images of foreign gods and set up sacred poles for the worship of Asherah on every hill and under every shady tree. 11They offered sacrifices at the shrines, just as the foreign nations had done before the Lord forced them out of Israel. They did sinful things that made the Lord very angry.
12Even though the Lord had commanded the Israelites not to worship idols, they did it anyway. 13So the Lord made sure that every prophet warned Israel and Judah with these words: “I, the Lord, command you to stop doing sinful things and start obeying my laws and teachings! I gave them to your ancestors, and I told my servants the prophets to repeat them to you.”
14But the Israelites would not listen; they were as stubborn as their ancestors who had refused to worship the Lord their God. 15They ignored the Lord's warnings and commands, and they rejected the solemn agreement he had made with their ancestors. They worshiped worthless idols and became worthless themselves. The Lord had told the Israelites not to do the things that the foreign nations around them were doing, but Israel became just like them.
16 The people of Israel disobeyed all the commands of the Lord their God. They made two gold statues of calves and set up a sacred pole for Asherah; they also worshiped the stars and the god Baal. 17 They used magic and witchcraft and even sacrificed their own children. The Israelites were determined to do whatever the Lord hated. 18The Lord became so furious with the people of Israel that he allowed them to be carried away as prisoners.
Only the people living in Judah were left, 19but they also disobeyed the Lord's commands and acted like the Israelites. 20So the Lord turned his back on everyone in Israel and let them be punished and defeated until no one was left.
21Earlier, when the Lord took the northern tribes away from David's family, the people living in northern Israel chose Jeroboam son of Nebat as their king. Jeroboam caused the Israelites to sin and to stop worshiping the Lord. 22The people kept on sinning like Jeroboam, 23until the Lord got rid of them, just as he had warned his servants the prophets.
That's why the people of Israel were taken away as prisoners to Assyria, and that's where they remained.
Foreigners Are Resettled in Israel
24The king of Assyria took people who were living in the cities of Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath, and Sepharvaim, and forced them to move to Israel. They took over the towns where the Israelites had lived, including the capital city of Samaria.
25At first these people did not worship the Lord, so he sent lions to attack them, and the lions killed some of them. 26A messenger told the king of Assyria, “The people you moved to Israel don't know how to worship the god of that country. So he sent lions that have attacked and killed some of them.”
27The king replied, “Get one of the Israelite priests we brought here and send him back to Israel. He can live there and teach them about the god of that country.” 28One of the Israelite priests was chosen to go back to Israel. He lived in Bethel and taught the people how to worship the Lord.
29But in towns all over Israel, the different groups of people made statues of their own gods, then they placed these idols in local Israelite shrines. 30The people from Babylonia made the god Succoth-Benoth; those from Cuthah made the god Nergal; those from Hamath made Ashima; 31those from Avva made Nibhaz and Tartak; and the people from Sepharvaim sacrificed their children to their own gods Adrammelech and Anammelech. 32-33They worshiped their own gods, just as they had before they were taken away to Israel. They also worshiped the Lord, but they chose their own people to be priests at the shrines. 34 Everyone followed their old customs. None of them worshiped only the Lord, and they refused to obey the laws and commands that the Lord had given to the descendants of Jacob, the man he named Israel. 35 At the time when the Lord had made his solemn agreement with the people of Israel, he told them:
Do not worship any other gods! Do not bow down to them or offer them a sacrifice. 36 Worship only me! I am the one who rescued you from Egypt with my mighty power. Bow down to me and offer sacrifices. 37Never worship any other god, always obey my laws and teachings, 38and remember the solemn agreement between us.
I will say it again: Do not worship any god 39except me. I am the Lord your God, and I will rescue you from all your enemies.
40But the people living in Israel ignored that command and kept on following their old customs. 41They did worship the Lord, but they also worshiped their own idols. Their descendants did the same thing.
translation_text:
Oosee, Isirayeel bɔtiluŋkikaau
1Juuda bɔtiu Akaasi nín jíń dibeel abin saalaa nì ali poonee ní Eela jipɔɔn Oosee kpántì Isirayeel bɔtiu. U nìn kóò Samaarii tiŋkin ní ki jíń dibeel abin awa. 2U nìn ŋá tin kaa kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee, ama waa nín bàn̄ Isirayeel bɔtiibi bin nìn līntiǹ-uee ní. 3Asuur bɔtiu Salmanasaar nìn dɔ́miń ki jáń nì Oosee, ní úǹ kíí ki sīntì u-ba ki tīī-u kí nīn bí u-taapu kí nīn pà lampoo ki tìì-u. 4Ama an dāa kúntèe, ní Oosee yíkì kaa kíí u-ba pu. U nìn tú binib Eejipiti bɔtiu Soo cee ní ki yíì yii waa ti làá pà lampoo kí tīī Asuur bɔtiu. Ubɔti Salmanasaar dāa béè mimmee ní ki cúú Oosee ki pīiǹ kudii. 5U ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki cáań u-janjaliibi Samaarii tiŋkin ki māntìi tú-kì. Ki yōoǹ abin ata, 6an dàkà yii Oosee nín jíń dibeel abin awa poonee, ní Asuur bɔtiu jáń ki fōō Samaarii tiŋki ní ki cúú Isirayeel yab kí cáa cūnnì kuyuŋu Asuur tiŋkin. U nìn dū-bi ki kāaǹ Alaa tiŋkpaaŋkin nì Abɔɔr tiŋkpaaŋki kin poon ní Goosan buŋŋu pùub̀ee, nì Meedii timmun.
Kun pu ní Isirayeel tiŋki kpántì adigbuŋkati ŋmee
7Kun pu ní agìń nee nìn bāań Isirayeel yabee di sá yii bi nìn yīntiǹ ti-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu un nìn fīī-bi ki nyántì Eejipiti bɔtiu Faaroo ŋaan ki nyántìń-bi Eejipiti tiŋkinee. Di sá yii bi nìn kíǹ ki tòotī awaa, 8ní ki nìn nóó atimbun ŋin nib ti-Dindaan nìn jìn̄ ki fōō bi-tiŋki ki dūu tīī Isirayeel yabee koobiliŋ, nì akoobil ŋin ní Isirayeel bɔtiibi nìn cáań ki kɔ́ǹ kitiŋinee. 9Isirayeel yab nìn ŋáań ti-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu tin ní baa máaǹ kí ŋée. Bi nìn máń awaa saraafaŋyi bi-timmu kɔkɔn nì sintil difɔkɔŋin nì bi-timmu mun bi máń agun ki túee poon. 10Bi nìn cóoǹ awaa taŋkpeeŋi nì iwaadɔ ŋgbantamu kɔkɔ pu nì busubu bun kamaa pée cáá tifaapɔnee taapu. 11Bi nìn ŋá saraabi awaa saraafaŋyi gbanti kɔkɔ pu kii atimbun ŋin nib ti-Dindaan nìn jìn̄ ní ki cáań bíǹ ki kāaǹee nín nìn ŋáań puee. Bi nìn ŋá atuŋkpiti ŋin gíti lákatèe ki gbítì ti-Dindaan ŋuul. 12Bi nìn tōotì awaa, min kamaa ti-Dindaan nìn bí-bi yii bí taa ŋá mimmee.
13Ti-Dindaan nìn dī u-bɔnaatiliibi kɔkɔ pu nì bin wāĺee kɔkɔ pu ki kpáafì Isirayeel yab nì Juuda yab. U nìn bí-bi yii: «Fámaan ni-saŋkpitii kí nīn ŋúb́maan m-marab nì m-bɔkpaaŋi ŋin kā marab gbɔŋkun m nìn dūu tīī ni-naanjabee. M nìn dūu dī m-tɔntɔnliibi bibɔnaatiliibi pu ki yāntì ni béè marab gbanti.» 14Ama Isirayeel yab kaa nìn pílifì tin bi nìn sòon̄ nì bee. Bi nìn pɔ́ɔkì bi-pɔbiliŋ kii bi-naanjab nín nìn ŋá pu kaa fōō ti-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu ki kíí puee ní. 15Unimbɔti nìn tīī-bi marab, ki nìn pōoǹ bi-naanjab dipoondi ní ki nìn tīī-bi isaŋki, ama bi nìn dū tíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ ki fá. Bi nìn dū bi-ba ki yá ki nákáǹ awaa ŋin kaa bí tibanee, ní bíǹ bi-ba mun kpántì binib bin kaa ti bí tibanee, ní ki fōō atimbun ŋin māntìi tú-bee bimbim, min kamaa ti-Dindaan nìn kpáafì-bi yii bí taa ŋá mimmee. 16Bi nìn dū ti-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu marab kɔkɔ ki fá. Bi nìn dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ anabil ali kí nīn jáaḿ. Bi nìn nyàab̄ ŋwindɔ ki cóoǹ ki tīī diwaal Aseera. Bi nìn gbāaǹ ki jáam̀ iŋmalbi in bí kutaa puee ki tōotì diwaal Baal. 17Bi nìn dū bi-jipɔmbi nì bi-bisalib ki tōotì awaa ki wùn̄ ŋŋmi, ki nìn búń tibɔɔl ní ki bālifì tin bí ki dòoń fool boonee pu. Bi nìn dū bi-ba ki líiǹ atuŋkpiti, ki ŋá tin kaa kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee ki gbítì u-ŋuul. 18An pu ní ti-Dindaan nìn gíí Isirayeel yab pu diŋuul ŋkpitim pu ní kaa nìn gíti là u-nimbil ń wāl̀-bi. Juuda naakooku yab baba di nìn pée kíǹ ki bí.
19Ama Juuda yab mun kaa nìn ŋúb́ ti-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu marab. Bi nìn fōō Isirayeel yab bimbim ní. 20An pu ní ti-Dindaan nìn dū Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ ki fá ní ki sīntiǹ-bi taapu. U nìn dū-bi ki ŋá anibul ŋin fúkuĺ binib wantee ŋaan. Kí kúntée, u dāa yāntì bi cúú-bi ki cūnnì kuyuŋu ní.
21Ti-Dindaan nín nìn cúú Isirayeel tiŋki ki nyántì Daafiidi beelinee, Isirayeel yab nìn dū Neebaati jipɔɔn Jeerooboowaam ní ki kāaǹ ubɔti. Jeerooboowaam nìn yāntì Isirayeel yab fātì bi-boon ki tīī ti-Dindaan ní ki nìn cáá-bi ki kɔ́ǹ ikpitikpaan poon. 22Kí yòon̄ ŋyunti gbanti kí nīn cée, Isirayeel yab nìn gbíntìi nìkì ki ŋáań ikpiti in kɔkɔ ní Jeerooboowaam nìn ŋée ní, baa nìn dū-i ki fá. 23An di yāntì ti-Dindaan kaa nìn gíti là kí wāl̀-bi ní ki cáá-bi ki cūnnì kuyuŋu Asuur tiŋkin. Niin ní bi gbíntìi bí ki dāa sāā díǹ. Ti-Dindaan nín dī pu ki ŋá kii u nín nìn dī u-tɔntɔnliibi bibɔnaatiliibi pu ki sòon̄ ki síiǹee dee.
Samaarii yab nyeeŋu
24Asuur bɔtiu nìn cáań Babiloon yab nì Kuuta yab nì Afa yab nì Amaati yab nì Seefarfayiim yab ki kāaǹ Samaarii timmun bi fōō Isirayeel yab paaŋŋu. Bíǹ nìn fōō Samaarii tiŋkpaaŋki ní ki kíǹ kóò ki-timmun. 25Bi nín bāań Samaarii tiŋkin ŋkilkaaminee, baa nìn jáaḿ ti-Dindaan. An puee ti-Dindaan nìn dū gbikintib ki tɔ́ bi-pu ní bíǹ kūū bi-kansikin binib tikpil. 26Niinee ní bi cūtìi ká Asuur bɔtiu ní ki bí-u yii: «Binib bin ní a cáań ki kāaǹ Samaarii timmunee kaa nyí bi nín máaǹ kí ŋá pu ní kí jāam̀ kitiŋ gbanti nimbɔtiuee. An puee unimbɔti gbanti dū gbikintib ki tɔ́ bi-pu ní bíǹ bíi kù-bi, di sá yii baa nyí bi nín máaǹ kí ŋá pu ní kí jāam̀ kitiŋ gbanti nimbɔtiuee.» 27Niinee Asuur bɔtiu tīī mara nee yii: «Ní gíiǹní bisaraaŋaliibi bin ni cúú ki cūnnì kuyuŋuee kansikin ubɔ Samaarii tiŋkin. Ú cù kí nīn kíǹ ki kóò niin kí ŋmā kí dàkà-bi bi nín máaǹ kí ŋá pu ní kí nīn jáaḿ kitiŋ gbanti nimbɔtiuee.» 28Míǹ ní an ŋá ní bisaraaŋaliibi bin bi nìn cúú Samaarii tiŋkin ki cūnnì kuyuŋuee kansikin ubɔ gítìń ki kíǹ ki kóò Beeteel. U nìn dàkà-bi bi nín máaǹ kí nīn ŋáań pu kí nīn jáaḿ ti-Dindaanee.
29Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, binicambi bin bi nìn cáań ki kāaǹee kɔkɔ nìn kpítì bi-waaŋi ŋin bi jáaḿee ní. Bi nìn dū bi-waaŋi gbanti ki síiǹ ŋwaadibiyaamu mun Isirayeel yab bin nìn kóò Samaariiyee nìn máń ŋgbantamu puee ní. Kitiŋ kin kamaa poon ní binibee nìn kóòyee, bi nìn pée ŋá míǹ ní. 30Bin nìn nyánní Babiloonee nìn kpítì diwaal Suukooti-Beenooti, ní bin nyánní Kuutee kpítì diwaal Neergaal, ní bin nyánní Amaatee kpítì diwaal Asima, 31ní Afa yab kpítì awaa Niibaasi nì Taartaki. Seefarfayiim yab bíǹ nìn gbíntìi nìkì ki cáá bi-biyaamu ki tòotī bi-waaŋi Adirameeleeki nì Anameeleeki. 32Bi nìn ŋáań mimmee ní ki jáaḿ ti-Dindaan mun. Bi nìn lēē bi-kansikin binib biba bí nīn sá bisaraaŋaliibi bi-waadibiyaamu poon kí nīn ŋáań saraabi ki tìì-bi. 33Bi nìn jáaḿ ti-Dindaan, ní ki nìn tòotī bíǹ bi-ba waaŋi mun, ki nóó nì ntimu mun poon bi nyánnée nín ŋáań puee.
34Áli nì díǹ, bi gbíntìi ŋúb́ bi-koobiliŋ gbanti ní. Baa fàŋkí ti-Dindaan. Baa ŋúb́ bíǹ bi-ba marab nì bi-koobiliŋaaa, kaa ti ŋúb́ ti-Dindaan marab bin u nìn tīī Jaakɔb naantiibee mun. Jaakɔb gbanti ní ti-Dindaan nìn gíti páaǹ diyindi yii Isirayeel. 35Ti-Dindaan nìn pōoǹ Jaakɔb naantiibi dipoondi ní ki nìn tīī-bi mara nee yii: «Ní taa jāam̀ awaa, kí taa gbàan̄ ŋi-nimbiin, kí taa tòotī-ŋi ní kaa nín ŋá saraabi ki tīī-ŋi. 36Man ni-Dindaan un di dū mpɔŋkpaan ki nyántìń-ni Eejipiti tiŋkinee baba ní ni máaǹ kí jāam̀. Man baba nimbiin ní ni máaǹ kí gbàan̄, ní man baba nì m-baba ní ni máaǹ kí ŋá saraabi kí tīī. 37Ní nīn ŋúb́ marab nì akoobil nì abɔkpaa ŋin m yāntì bi ŋmàn̄ ki síiǹ-nee, ní kí pɔ́ɔǹ kí nīn ŋáań kii ŋi nín bí yii ní ŋá puee baabadal. Ní taa pée jāam̀ báà diwaal. 38Ní taa súntí dipoondi din m pōoǹ-nee, ní m gíti bíi bùsī ki tùkù-ni yii ní taa jāam̀ báà diwaal. 39Man ni-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu baba ní ni máaǹ kí jāam̀, di sá yii man baba di ŋūǹ kí fīī-ni kí nyāntí ni-nannanliibi kɔkɔ ŋaan.»
40Ama binib gbanti kaa nìn pílifì. Bi nìn gbíntìi ŋúb́ bi-yaajakoobiliŋ ní. 41Míǹ puee bi nìn jáaḿ ti-Dindaan ní ki nìn gbíntìi tòotī bi-waaŋi. Bíǹ boonee bi-biyaamu nì bi-naantiibi nìkī ki ŋá míǹ mbaantiim ki dāa sāā díǹ.

english_text:
King Hezekiah of Judah
(2 Chronicles 29.1,2; 31.1)
1Hezekiah son of Ahaz became king of Judah in the third year of Hoshea's rule in Israel. 2Hezekiah was 25 years old when he became king, and he ruled 29 years from Jerusalem. His mother Abi was the daughter of Zechariah.
3Hezekiah obeyed the Lord, just as his ancestor David had done. 4 He destroyed the local shrines, then tore down the images of foreign gods and cut down the sacred pole for worshiping the goddess Asherah. He also smashed the bronze snake Moses had made. The people had named it Nehushtan and had been offering sacrifices to it.
5Hezekiah trusted the Lord God of Israel. No other king of Judah was like Hezekiah, either before or after him. 6He was completely faithful to the Lord and obeyed the laws the Lord had given to Moses for the people. 7The Lord helped Hezekiah, so he was successful in everything he did. He even rebelled against the king of Assyria, refusing to be his servant. 8Hezekiah defeated the Philistine towns as far away as Gaza—from the smallest towns to the large, walled cities.
9During the fourth year of Hezekiah's rule, which was the seventh year of Hoshea's rule in Israel, King Shalmaneser of Assyria led his troops to Samaria, the capital city of Israel. They attacked 10and captured it three years later, in the sixth year of Hezekiah's rule and the ninth year of Hoshea's rule. 11The king of Assyria took the Israelites away as prisoners; he forced some of them to live in the town of Halah, others to live near the Habor River in the territory of Gozan, and still others to live in towns where the Median people lived. 12All of that happened because the people of Israel had not obeyed the Lord their God. They rejected the solemn agreement he had made with them, and they ignored everything that the Lord's servant Moses had told them.
King Sennacherib of Assyria Invades Judah
(2 Chronicles 32.1-19; Isaiah 36.1-22)
13 In the fourteenth year of Hezekiah's rule in Judah, King Sennacherib of Assyria invaded the country and captured every walled city, except Jerusalem. 14Hezekiah sent this message to Sennacherib, who was in the town of Lachish: “I know I am guilty of rebellion. But I will pay you whatever you want, if you stop your attack.”
Sennacherib told Hezekiah to pay ten tons of silver and one ton of gold. 15So Hezekiah collected all the silver from the Lord's temple and the royal treasury. 16He even stripped the gold that he had used to cover the doors and doorposts in the temple. He gave it all to Sennacherib.
17The king of Assyria ordered his three highest military officers to leave Lachish and take a large army to Jerusalem. When they arrived, the officers stood on the road near the cloth makers' shops along the canal from the upper pool. 18They called out to Hezekiah, and three of his highest officials came out to meet them. One of them was Hilkiah's son Eliakim, who was the prime minister. The other two were Shebna, assistant to the prime minister, and Joah son of Asaph, keeper of the government records.
19One of the Assyrian commanders told them:
I have a message for Hezekiah from the great king of Assyria. Ask Hezekiah why he feels so sure of himself. 20Does he think he can plan and win a war with nothing but words? Who is going to help him, now that he has turned against the king of Assyria? 21Is he depending on Egypt and its king? That's the same as leaning on a broken stick, and it will go right through his hand.
22Is Hezekiah now depending on the Lord your God? Didn't Hezekiah tear down all except one of the Lord's altars and places of worship? Didn't he tell the people of Jerusalem and Judah to worship at that one place?
23The king of Assyria wants to make a bet with you people. He will give you 2,000 horses, if you have enough troops to ride them. 24How could you even defeat our lowest ranking officer, when you have to depend on Egypt for chariots and cavalry? 25Don't forget that it was the Lord who sent me here with orders to destroy your nation!
26Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said, “Sir, we don't want the people listening from the city wall to understand what you are saying. So please speak to us in Aramaic instead of Hebrew.”
27The Assyrian army commander answered, “My king sent me to speak to everyone, not just to you leaders. These people will soon have to eat their own body waste and drink their own urine! And so will the three of you.”
28Then, in a voice loud enough for everyone to hear, he shouted in Hebrew:
Listen to what the great king of Assyria says! 29Don't be fooled by Hezekiah. He can't save you. 30Don't trust him when he tells you that the Lord will protect you from the king of Assyria. 31Stop listening to Hezekiah! Pay attention to my king. Surrender to him. He will let you keep your own vineyards, fig trees, and cisterns 32for a while. Then he will come and take you away to a country just like yours, where you can plant vineyards, raise your own grain, and have plenty of olive oil and honey. Believe me, you won't starve there.
Hezekiah claims the Lord will save you. But don't be fooled by him. 33Were any other gods able to defend their land against the king of Assyria? 34What happened to the gods of Hamath and Arpad? What about the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah? Were the gods of Samaria able to protect their land against the Assyrian forces? 35None of these gods kept their people safe from the king of Assyria. Do you think the Lord your God can do any better?
36-37Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah had been warned by King Hezekiah not to answer the Assyrian commander. So they tore their clothes in sorrow and reported to Hezekiah everything the commander had said.
translation_text:
Eeseekiyaasi, Juuda bɔtiu
(2 Kroo 29.1-2)
1Eela jipɔɔn Oosee nín jíń dibeel Isirayeel tiŋkin dibintataatiil poonee ní Akaasi jipɔɔn Eeseekiyaasi kpántì Juuda bɔtiu. 2U nìn cáá abin mmuŋku nì aŋmoo ní ki kpántì ubɔti ní ki kāl̀ Jeerusaleem ki jíń dibeel abin mmuŋku nì awa. Bi nìn yíì u-na Abii, Seekariya bisal. 3U nìn ŋá tin fáatì ti-Dindaanee kii u-naanja Daafiidi nín nìn ŋá puee ní deedee. 4U nìn kúntì ŋgbantamu pu saraabi, ki gbáń ki wīī ataŋkpee ŋin bi kpítì ki dūu ŋá awaayee, ki gāatì ŋwindɔ ŋun bi nìn dūu cóoǹ ki tīī diwaal Aseerayee. U nìn tí gbáń ki wīī kukoonaŋu kun Mooyiisi nìn dū tasa kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́yee, di sá yii kí cáá sāā ŋyunti gbantee, Isirayeel yab nìn tùutī talaalub ki tìì kukoonaŋu gbanti ní. Bi nìn yíì-ku yii Neeyuusitan. 5Eeseekiyaasi nìn dū u-mákal ki páaǹ ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu pu. Juuda bɔtiibi bin nìn līntiǹ-uee nì bin dāa páaǹní u-boonee, bi-kansikin báà ubɔ kaa bàn̄-u. 6U nìn dū u-ba ki yá ki nákáǹ ti-Dindaan, kaa fātì u-boon ki tīī-u. U nìn ŋúb́ marab bin kɔkɔ ní ti-Dindaan nìn tīī Mooyiisee. 7An puee ti-Dindaan nìn bí u-cee, ní tin kɔkɔ u nìn ŋáańee bútí-u. Waa nìn kíí u-ba pu Asuur bɔtiu cee ní kaa nìn gíti bí u-taapu. 8U nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Fiiliistii yab ki jìn̄-bi ki cáa sāā Gaasaa tiŋki. U nìn jáń ki fōō ntimu mun bi máń agun ki túee nì ntimu mun pée cáá sintil difɔŋfɔkɔŋi ŋmaniŋmee.
Bi fātìi sòon̄ bi nín fōō Samaarii tiŋki puee
9Eeseekiyaasi nín jíń dibeel dibinnanaatiil poonee nì Eela jipɔɔn Oosee nín jíń Isirayeel tiŋki pu dibeel abin aluli poonee, ní Asuur bɔtiu Salmanasaar dɔ́miń kí já nì Samaarii tiŋki ní ki māntìi tú-kì. 10Abin ata boon, an dàkà yii Eeseekiyaasi beel binluluutiil poon nì Oosee beel biŋwawatiil poon ní Asuur yab jáń ki fōō Samaarii tiŋki. 11Asuur bɔtiu nìn cúú Isirayeel yab kí cáa cūnnì kuyuŋu Asuur tiŋkin. U nìn dū-bi ki kāaǹ Alaa tiŋkpaaŋkin nì Abɔɔr tiŋkpaaŋki kin poon ní Goosan buŋŋu pùub̀ ki jītée, nì Meedii timmun. 12Kun pu ní tíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ bāań-bee di sá yii baa nìn pílifì ti-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu nyɔkɔ, ní kaa nìn síl̀ nì u-poondi deedee. Marab bin ní ti-Dindaan tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi nìn dūu tīī-bee, baa nìn tɔ́-bi ní kaa nín ŋá bi nín bí yii bí ŋá puee.
Seenakeeriibi dɔ́miń kí já nì Juuda yab
(Kpèè Yees 36.1, kpèè 2 Kroo 32.1 mun)
13Eeseekiyaasi nín jíń dibeel dibindi diba kpá saalku poonee ní Asuur bɔtiu Seenakeeriibi dɔ́miń ki jáń nì Juuda yab timmu mun bi máń agun ki túee ki fōō mu-kɔkɔ. 14Niinee ní Juuda bɔtiu tú bí cùú tùkù Asuur bɔtiu Lakiisi tiŋkin yii: «M yīntì! Taa ti já nì mi. A yaa gíí-mi dipɔndi diŋyee, m kíí kí pà.»
Asuur bɔtiu nìn gíí Juuda bɔtiu Eeseekiyaasi dipɔndi animbil kúti kiiloobi kutukub biwa nì sindaariya kiiloobi alaataa awa. 15Ní Eeseekiyaasi yōoǹ animbil ŋin kɔkɔ bí ti-Dindaan Diikunee nì ŋin kɔkɔ bí ubɔti nimbikpaafidiikunee ki tīī Asuur bɔtiu. 16U nìn lēē gba sindaariya un u nìn dūu nyūntì ti-Dindaan Diiku punyɔmmu dɔi ilalikaa nì icooŋkaayee kɔkɔ ki dūu tīī Asuur bɔtiu.
Asuur yab māntìi tú Jeerusaleem kí já nì kì
(Kpèè Yees 36.2-22, 2 Kroo 32.9-16)
17Asuur bɔtiu nìn bí Lakiisi tiŋkin ní ki dū u-janjakpiliu nì un sá bijanjaliibi kɔkɔ yidaaŋwuee nì un bi yaa cūtì kujaau u ŋúb̀ ubɔti janjawantee ki tú ubɔti Eeseekiyaasi cee, bi nì dijanjakitikpaandi diba nóó. Bi bàn̄ Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee ní ki jɔ́m̀ ki síl̀ kunyiŋfuŋu kun bi cátì nnyim dì ki kóò dinyimbɔbil din bí yilpu púee. Dinyimbɔbil gbanti nìn dɔ̄ didandi din cá biwaŋfintiliibi kpaabunee watil pú ní. 18Bi síl̀ niinee ní ki téeń yii bi là kí sòoǹ nì ubɔti. Bin kpèé ubɔti cindee kpiliu Eeliyaakiim, Yiilkiyaawuu nì ubɔti gbaŋŋmaliu Seebina nì Asafi jipɔɔn Yoowa un kpáafí ubɔti gbɔntee di nìn nyáń ki túŋkì-bi nsanni. 19Ní un nìn ŋúb̀ Asuur bɔtiu janjawanti kujaaunee bí-bi yii: «Ní tùkù Eeseekiyaasi yii: Ubɔtikpaan, Asuur bɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Ba pu ní a máká ní? 20A dàkafī yii anyɔɔbun fám ŋūǹ kí fōō kujaau bɔ́ntitam nì dibaatandi paaŋŋu kí já kujaauaaa? Ŋma pu ní a baasii máká ní ki yíkì kaa kíí a-ba pu m-cee na? 21Eejipiti pu ní a mákáaa? Saa nyí yii Eejipiti sá kii kukaluu kun gíìyee ní un yaa dū u-ŋal ki nyīī ku-puee, an gíí-uaaa? Too, míǹ ní Eejipiti bɔtiu Faaroo sá ki tīī un kamaa yaa dū u-mákal ki páaǹ u-puee! 22An yaa yíì a làá lì yii: <Ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu pu ní timbi máká!> Kin an kaa sá sii Eeseekiyaasi ubaantee di kúntì ŋgbantamu pu saraabi nì mu-saraafaŋyi ní ki bí Juuda nì Jeerusaleem yab yii nsaraafan ŋun bí Jeerusaleemee baba nimbiin ní bí nīn gbàantí ki jáaḿ ti-Dindaanaaa? 23A yaa là sii nì m-kpiliu Asuur bɔtiu ń kpáká kí kpèè. A yaa ŋúń ki ká bitanjakaliibi, m làá tīī-si itaamu kutukub bili mun! 24Á kpáàa ŋūǹ kí já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ m-kpiliu tɔntɔnliibi kansikin kiwaai gba! Kin ba pu ní a nín máká Eejipiti pu ú tīī-si janjatɔrɔkub nì itaamu na! 25A dàkafī yii ti-Dindaan kaa là ní m dɔ́miń kí jáǹ kitiŋ nee kí nàan̄-kàaa? Ti-Dindaan u-ba di bí-mi yii: <Cùú já nì kitiŋ nee kí nàan̄-kì!>»
26Niinee Yiilkiyaawuu jipɔɔn Eeliyaakiim nì Seebina nì Yoowa bí Asuur janjakpiliuee yii: «Ti gbāam̀-si ní, sòoǹ nì timbi a-tɔntɔnliibi Aram yab sooŋyi poon, di sá yii ti gbìl̀-i. Taa ti sòoǹ nì ti eebru sooŋyi poon, di sá yii binib tɔ́kɔ́ digundi pu ki pílifí.» 27Ama ní Asuur janjakpiliuee kíí-bi yii: «A dàkafī yii sii nì a-bɔtiu baba cee ní m-kpiliu túnní-mi ḿ cáań tibɔti nee kí sòoǹaaa? Tibɔti gbanti sá ki tīī binib bin kɔkɔ bí digundi pu nee mun ní. An kaa làá ti yúntí, bi làá ŋmɔ́ bi-binti ní kí nyɔ̀ bi-nyeem kii ni muee.»
28Míǹ boonee ní Asuur yab janjakpiliuee yíkìi síl̀, ní ki téeń mpɔn eebru sooŋyi poon yii: «Ní pīlifìmaan tibɔti tin ubɔtikpaan, Asuur bɔtiu cáá kí sòoǹee! 29Ubɔti nín lī puee sèé: <Ní taa yàntī Eeseekiyaasi ń kīil̀-ni, di sá yii waa làá ŋmā kí fīī-ni! 30Ní taa yàntī Eeseekiyaasi ń kīil̀-ni ní dū ni-mákal kí páań ti-Dindaan pu, u bí ki lì yii báà an ŋá pu, ti-Dindaan làá fīī-ni. Kitiŋ nee kpá kí kɔ́ Asuur bɔtiu ŋaan!> 31Ní taa pīlifì Eeseekiyaasi, ama ní pīlifì tin Asuur bɔtiu bí ki sòoǹee, yii: <Píímaan-mi kubɔɔtiiu, ní sāǹ kí kɔ́maan-mi! Ni yaa ŋá míǹ, báà ŋma làá ŋmɔ́ u-fiinyi subu nì u-fiigi subu biliŋ ní ki nyɔ̀ u-lɔkɔu poon nyim, 32kí nīn cí ŋyunti ŋun ní m làá dāan̄ kí yòon̄-ni kí cùnnì kitiŋ kin bí kii ni-yaka nee poonee. Kitiŋ gbanti poonee, bilee nì ndamam nì tikpaajin nì fiinyi biliŋ nì ɔliifi biliŋ nì ŋkpam nì tisiil bí ní. Mimmee ni làá nīn bí dimaŋfalin kaa làá kpú.> Míǹ puee ní taa pīlifìmaan Eeseekiyaasi, di sá yii nnyimɔn ní u bí ki mɔ́ntí-ni ki lì yii: <Ti-Dindaan làá fīī-ti!> 33Atimbun ŋin kíǹee waaŋi ŋúń ki fīī ŋi-timmu ki nyántì Asuur bɔtiu ŋaanaaa? 34Amaati nì Aripaadi yab waaŋi bí la? Seefarfayiim nì Eena nì Afa yab waaŋi bí la? Awaa gbanti ŋúń ki fīī Samaarii tiŋkaaa? 35Ntimu gbanti kɔkɔ waaŋi dilal di ŋúń ki fīī di-tiŋki ki nyántì m-ŋaan? Kin án làá dī mana ní ti-Dindaan ń pìin̄-mi nsan ḿ taa fōō Jeerusaleem?»
36Bin kɔkɔ nìn bí niinee, báà ubɔ kaa nìn wāaǹ kinyɔkɔ ní kaa nín gātì-u, di sá yii ubɔti nìn kpáafì-bi yii: «Ní taa pée kíí-u tiba!» 37Míǹ boonee ní Yiilkiyaawuu jipɔɔn Eeliyaakiim nì ugbaŋŋmal Seebina nì Asafi jipɔɔn Yoowa un kpáafí ubɔti gbɔntee nín gítí ubɔti Eeseekiyaasi cee. Bi nìn dáaĺ ki cátì tiwan tin bi pēēyee, ní ki dū tibɔti tin ujanjakpilee sòon̄ee ki máafì-u.

english_text:
Hezekiah Asks Isaiah the Prophet for Advice
(Isaiah 37.1-13)
1As soon as Hezekiah heard the news, he tore off his clothes in sorrow and put on sackcloth. Then he went into the temple of the Lord. 2He told Prime Minister Eliakim, Assistant Prime Minister Shebna, and the senior priests to dress in sackcloth and tell the prophet Isaiah:
3These are difficult and disgraceful times. Our nation is like a woman too weak to give birth, when it's time for her baby to be born. 4Please pray for those of us who are left alive. The king of Assyria sent his army commander to insult the living God. Perhaps the Lord heard what he said and will do something, if you will pray.
5When these leaders went to Isaiah, 6he told them that the Lord had this message for Hezekiah:
I am the Lord. Don't worry about the insulting things that have been said about me by these messengers from the king of Assyria. 7I will upset him with rumors about what's happening in his own country. He will go back, and there I will make him die a violent death.
8Meanwhile, the commander of the Assyrian forces heard that his king had left the town of Lachish and was now attacking Libnah. So he went there.
9About this same time the king of Assyria learned that King Tirhakah of Ethiopia was on his way to attack him. Then the king of Assyria sent some messengers with this note for Hezekiah:
10Don't trust your God or be fooled by his promise to defend Jerusalem against me. 11You have heard how we Assyrian kings have completely wiped out other nations. What makes you feel so safe? 12The Assyrian kings before me destroyed the towns of Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and everyone from Eden who lived in Telassar. What good did their gods do them? 13The kings of Hamath, Arpad, Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah have all disappeared.
Hezekiah Prays
(Isaiah 37.14-20)
14After Hezekiah had read the note from the king of Assyria, he took it to the temple and spread it out for the Lord to see. 15 He prayed:
Lord God of Israel, your throne is above the winged creatures. You created the heavens and the earth, and you alone rule the kingdoms of this world. 16But just look how Sennacherib has insulted you, the living God.
17It is true, our Lord, that Assyrian kings have turned nations into deserts. 18They destroyed the idols of wood and stone that the people of those nations had made and worshiped. 19But you are our Lord and our God! We ask you to keep us safe from the Assyrian king. Then everyone in every kingdom on earth will know that you are the only God.
The Lord's Answer to Hezekiah
(Isaiah 37.21-35)
20Isaiah went to Hezekiah and told him that the Lord God of Israel had said:
Hezekiah, I heard your prayer about King Sennacherib of Assyria. 21Now this is what I say to that king:
The people of Jerusalem
hate and make fun of you;
they laugh
behind your back.
22Sennacherib, you cursed,
shouted, and sneered at me,
the holy God of Israel.
23You let your officials
insult me, the Lord.
And this is how you
bragged about yourself:
“I led my chariots
to the highest heights
of Lebanon's mountains.
I went deep into its forest,
cutting down the best cedar
and cypress trees.
24I dried up every stream
in the land of Egypt,
and I drank water
from wells I had dug.”
25Sennacherib, now listen
to me, the Lord.
I planned all this long ago.
And you don't even realize
that I alone am the one
who decided that you
would do these things.
I let you make ruins
of fortified cities.
26Their people became weak,
terribly confused.
They were like wild flowers
or tender young grass
growing on a flat roof,
scorched before it matures.
27I know all about you,
even how fiercely angry
you are with me.
28I have seen your pride
and the tremendous hatred
you have for me.
Now I will put a hook
in your nose,
a bit in your mouth,
then I will send you back
to where you came from.
29Hezekiah, I will tell you what's going to happen. This year you will eat crops that grow on their own, and the next year you will eat whatever springs up where those crops grew. But the third year you will plant grain and vineyards, and you will eat what you harvest. 30Those who survive in Judah will be like a vine that puts down deep roots and bears fruit. 31I, the Lord All-Powerful, will see to it that some who live in Jerusalem will survive.
32I promise that the king of Assyria won't get into Jerusalem, or shoot an arrow into the city, or even surround it and prepare to attack. 33As surely as I am the Lord, he will return by the way he came and will never enter Jerusalem. 34I will protect it for myself and for my servant David.
The Death of King Sennacherib
(Isaiah 37.36-38)
35 That same night the Lord sent an angel to the camp of the Assyrians, and he killed 185,000 of them. And so the next morning, the camp was full of dead bodies. 36After this King Sennacherib went back to Assyria and lived in the city of Nineveh. 37One day he was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch, when his sons, Adrammelech and Sharezer, killed him with their swords. They escaped to the land of Ararat, and his son Esarhaddon became king.
translation_text:
Eeseekiyaasi cūtì dibalifil Yeesaya cee
(Kpèè Yees 37.1-7)
1Ubɔti Eeseekiyaasi nín gbìl̄ tin bi máafì-uee ní u cúú tiwan tin u pēēyee ki dáaĺ ki cátì, ní ki dū kutuku ki pēeǹ ní ki nín cá ti-Dindaan Diikun. 2U nìn dū bin kpèé ubɔti cindee kpiliu Eeliyaakiim nì ugbaŋŋmal Seebina nì bisaraaŋaliibi bin yúntèe ki tú Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeesaya, Amɔtisi jipɔɔn cee. Bi-kɔkɔ nìn pēē kutukub ní ki cūtì. 3U nìn bí-bi bí tùkù-u yii: «Eeseekiyaasi nín bí tí tùkù-si puee sɔ̀. Díǹ wiiŋŋu nee sá-ti kunimbaau nì ditafadaaldi nì icoo wiiŋŋu ní! A lì kii kibiki di bīń ki-na poon ki ŋmāntì bí bàà màal̀-kì, ama ní unaati kaa ti cáá ŋfam kí núuĺ kibiki ń nyānnée! 4An yaa yíì ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu tin máaǹ ki gbìl̄ tibɔti tin Asuur bɔtiu janjakpiliu sòon̄ee kí dáaĺ u-tafal. U-kpiliu túnní-u u dɔ́miń ki sīī Unimbɔti un bí dimaŋfalinee. An puee, sii Yeesaya, mèè ti-Dindaan kí tīī a-nibul yab bin kíǹee.»
5Niinee ní ubɔti Eeseekiyaasi tɔntɔnliibi bin u túee nín cá Yeesaya cee. 6Bi bàn̄ee ní Yeesaya tùkū-bi yii: «Ní gítí kí tùkù ni-kpiliu yii ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé: <Taa fàŋkì anyɔɔbun ŋin a gbìl̄ Asuur bɔtiu janjakpiliu sòon̄ee, u nín sòon̄ ki bíil̀-mi puee. 7Bi làá cáań tibɔti tiba kí tùkù ubɔti ní ḿ yàntī ú nīn gítí u-tiŋkin. U-tiŋkin niin ní m làá yàntī bí dū kitàataajiki kí kpɔ̀-u.»
Asuur bɔtiu Seenakeeriibi tí bíikì Jeerusaleem pu
(Yees 37.8-13, 2 Kroo 32.17)
8Ujanjakpilee nín gbìl̄ yii u-kpiliu Asuur bɔtiu yíkì Lakiisi tiŋki ki cūtìi bíi jáà nì Liibina tiŋkee, ní u mun nín cá niin ki cūtìi ká-u. 9Asuur bɔtiu nìn gbìl̄ yii Eejipiti bɔtiu Tiiraka un sá Kuusi tiŋkinee dòoń kí já nì u. Niinee ní u tí tú binib Eeseekiyaasi cee ki bí yii: 10«Ní cùú tùkù Juuda bɔtiu Eeseekiyaasi yii: <A-Nimbɔtiu un pu ní a dū a-mákal ki páaǹee ń taa kīil̀-si kí lì yii Jeerusaleem tiŋki kaa làá kɔ́ Asuur bɔtiu ŋaan. 11Sisi a-ba gbìl̄ Asuur bɔtiibi nín ŋáaǹ ntimu mun kíǹee kɔkɔ pu ki nāaǹ-muee, ní sii dàkafī yii a làá ŋmátáa! 12Goosan nì Karan nì Reeseefi timbuŋŋi nì Eedeen yab bin nìn kóò Teelasaar tiŋkin ní m-naanjab nìn nāaǹ bi-kɔkɔee, bi-waaŋi nìn ŋúń ki fīī-baaa? 13Amaati bɔtiu nì Aripaadi bɔtiu nì Layiir nì Seefariim nì Eena nì Iwa bɔtiibi bí la díǹ pu na?»
Ubɔti Eeseekiyaasi wimmeem
14Eeseekiyaasi nìn fōō kugbɔŋu kun Asuur bɔtiu túnní bí cáań kí tīī-uee ki kàan̄. U kàan̄ ki dóòyee ní ki nín jɔ́ḿ ti-Dindaan Diikun, ní ki kpátì kugbɔŋuee ki bíl̀ ti-Dindaan nimbiin. 15U ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki mēē ŋwimmeem nee yii: «Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu un beejal tɔ́kɔ́ keerubimbi puee. Sii baba di sá kitiŋ kɔkɔ pu beeŋi Nimbɔtiu. Sii di náań kutagbɔŋu nì kitiŋ. 16Ti-Dindaan, kpòon̄ a-tafal kí pīlifì! Ti-Dindaan, ŋúbití a-nimbiliŋ kí kpèè! Pīlifì asiibil ŋin kɔkɔ ní Seenakeeriibi tuuŋyi sīī sii Unimbɔti un bí dimaŋfalinee! 17Ti-Dindaan, an lafun sá tiŋman ní yii Asuur bɔtiibi kūū ki céetì atimbun ŋin kíǹee nib ki nāaǹ bi-timmu. 18Bi nìn dū atimbun gbanti waaŋi ki tɔ́ ŋŋmin ki kúntì-ŋi, di sá yii bi-waaŋi gbanti kaa nìn sá Unimbɔti, idɔ nì ataŋkpee ní binib nìn dūu mɔ́ɔ́-ŋi. 19Ama sii ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu, fīī-ti kí nyāntí Seenakeeriibi ŋaan ní kitiŋ pu beeŋi kɔkɔ ń béé yii sii, ti-Dindaan baba di sá Unimbɔti.»
Yeesaya dū ti-Dindaan nín kíí ubɔti puee ki nāatì-u
(Kpèè Yees 37.21-35)
20Niinee ní Amɔtisi jipɔɔn Yeesaya tú bi cūtìi tùkū Eeseekiyaasi yii: «A nín mēē Seenakeeriibi pu puee, ti-Dindaan nín kíiń a-wimmeem puee sɔ̀. 21Tibɔti tin ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ Seenakeeriibi puee sɔ̀.
Siiyɔn tiŋki bíi kpèé-si fám,
kì bíi bèel̄-si.
Jeerusaleem tiŋki kinyannyaaŋŋi
bí ki lāā-si ki gbákafí diyil.
22Ŋma ní a sīī ní?
Ŋma ní a sòon̄ ki bíil̀ ní?
Ŋma pu ní a téeń ní?
Ŋma ní a yáatì ki kpēē nì dilambil ní?
An sá man Isirayeel Circir Nimbɔtiu.
23A dī a-tuuŋyi pu ki sīī man ni-Dindaan.
A lī yii: <Man Seenakeeriibi,
m cáá janjatɔrɔkub náaǹ,
an pu ní m ŋúń ki jɔ́m̀ ki tin bàn̄ ajoon yilpu,
m jɔ́m̀ ki tin bàn̄ Leebanɔn jool yilpu.
M gāatì ki-seedir sufii in pée fɔ̀kɔ̀ee,
ki gāatì ki-siipreesi sufii in pée ŋān̄ee.
M jɔ́m̀ ki bàn̄ ki-jooŋŋi ŋin fɔ̀kɔ̀ee yilpu,
ki kɔ́ ki-bambaŋku kun múkúee poon.
24M gbìn̄ lɔkɔb ntincamun
ki nyùn̄ bi-nyim niin.
M dū m-taaŋi ki tāā Eejipiti tiŋki,
ní ki-buŋyi kɔkɔ fóotì.>
25«Mimmee Seenakeeriibi,
saa nyí yii an sá man di bɔ́ntì
tin bíi jītí nee kɔkɔ ki yóoǹ doooodooooyeeee?
Saa nyí yii an yúntì tikpil m nín bɔ́ntì-tèeee?
Kɔŋkɔnnee ní m yāntì tin m bɔ́ntèe bíi jītí.
Man di lēē-si á nà ntimu mun bi máń
agun ki māntìi túee kɔkɔ dúsi dusi.
26Binib bin kóò ntimu gbantinee ŋalii jòon̄ fám ní,
dinyoondi kɔ́-bi ní icoo cúú-bi.
Bi bí kii timool tin bí tisatinee,
kii kumɔsɔŋu kun dáá pɔ̀fèe,
kii timool tin nyēē kudii yilpuee,
àá tin nyēē tisatin kaa láá bīńee.
27«A yaa kāaa, a yaa yúɔɔɔ,
a yaa nyēēyaaa, a yaa kóòyaaa,
a yaa tí gíí m-pu diŋuulaaa,
m nyí.
28Tiŋman, a lafun gíí m-pu diŋuul,
ní tibɔfan tin a sòon̄-mee kɔ́ m-tafalin.
An pu ní m làá dū dibɔmbil kí túuń a-maŋfal,
kí dū tikúti kí kpàl̄ a-nyɔkɔ kí ŋmā kí kpòotī-si.
Nsan ŋun a dī ki dɔ́miń dooyee,
nsan gbanti ní a làá fàtīí dī kí kpì.
29«Eeseekiyaasi, kudaaŋŋu kun m tīī-see sɔ̀. Dun bindi nee, ni làá jī dibindi din jítèe jinti tin sá aleenee, ní jiilee ní dāá tí jī míǹ. Ama dibintataatiil poonee, ni làá dāá kpɔ̀ kí bɔ̄l̀ kí cā ni-kpaajinti, ní kí dāá kpɔ̀ afiinyikpaan kí dāá kìtī abil kí ŋmɔ́. 30Juuda beel nib bin làá dāá ŋmátée làá dāá nìn bí kii disupɔmbilee ní. Bi làá dāá tɔ̄ inyaampɔɔn kitiŋ poon ní kí dāá lòoǹ abil yilpu. 31Di sá yii binib biba làá dāá kíń Jeerusaleem tiŋkin, bin ŋmátì kaa kpíìyee làá dāá yīkì kí yūĺ Siiyɔn jool pu.»
Ní Yeesaya kútì ki lī yii: «Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan neeŋkpaandi puee, u làá dāá ŋá míǹ. 32Ti-Dindaan nín lī Asuur bɔtiu pu puee sèé: <Waa làá kɔ́ kitiŋ nee poon. Waa làá tɔ̄ mpimbambaanti doo. Waa làá dū digbampɔɔl kí lìkin̄ u-ba kí jáǹ-kì, kaa làá tí bíĺ ataŋkpuku ki-guŋŋi pu kí jáǹ-kì. 33Nsan ŋun u dī ki dɔ́mińee, nsan gbanti ní u làá fàtīí dī kí gítí. U-taal kpá kí tāā kitiŋ nee poon. Man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ. 34M làá wúń Jeerusaleem tiŋki pu kí fīī-kì. Mama m-ba nì m-tɔntɔnliu Daafiidi pu ní m làá ŋá míǹ.>»
Asuur yab nín kùǹ, ní bi kūū Seenakeeriibi
(Kpèè Yees 37.36-38, 2 Kroo 32.21-22)
35Kunyeeu gbantee ní ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋu dɔ́miń Asuur yab janjanaapaal pu ki kūū binib kutukub dilaataal nì imuŋku inaa nì kutukub biŋmoo. Kutaa wúntì bin kaa kpíìyee fīntèe, ki ká anikpil dɔ̄ an kɔkɔ fìlfilfil. 36Niinee ní Asuur bɔtiu Seenakeeriibi yíkì dinaapaalee pu ki nín gítí Niiniifi tiŋkin ki cūtìi gbíntì niin. 37Dalba u gbāā u-waal Niisrooki diikun ki jáaḿ-dèe, ní u-jipɔmbi Adirameeleeki nì Sareeseer dū kitàataajiki ki gāā ki kūū-u ní ki sáǹ ki nín cá Ararati tiŋkin. U-jipɔɔn Asaradɔn di fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.

english_text:
Hezekiah Gets Sick and Almost Dies
(2 Chronicles 32.24-26; Isaiah 38.1-8,21,22)
1About this time, Hezekiah got sick and was almost dead. Isaiah the prophet went in and told him, “The Lord says you won't ever get well. You are going to die, so you had better start doing what needs to be done.”
2Hezekiah turned toward the wall and prayed, 3“Don't forget that I have been faithful to you, Lord. I have obeyed you with all my heart, and I do whatever you say is right.” After this, he cried bitterly.
4Before Isaiah got to the middle court of the palace, 5the Lord sent him back to Hezekiah with this message:
Hezekiah, you are the ruler of my people, and I am the Lord God, who was worshiped by your ancestor David. I heard you pray, and I saw you cry. I will heal you, so that three days from now you will be able to worship in my temple. 6I will let you live 15 years more, while I protect you and your city from the king of Assyria. I will defend this city as an honor to me and to my servant David.
7Then Isaiah said to the king's servants, “Bring some mashed figs and place them on the king's open sore. He will then get well.”
8Hezekiah asked Isaiah, “Can you prove that the Lord will heal me, so that I can worship in his temple in three days?”
9Isaiah replied, “The Lord will prove to you that he will keep his promise. Will the shadow made by the setting sun on the stairway go forward ten steps or back ten steps?”
10“It's normal for the sun to go forward,” Hezekiah answered. “But how can it go back?”
11Isaiah prayed, and the Lord made the shadow go back ten steps on the stairway built for King Ahaz.
The Lord Is Still with Hezekiah
(Isaiah 39.1-8)
12Merodach Baladan, the son of Baladan, was now king of Babylonia. And when he learned that Hezekiah had been sick, he sent messengers with letters and a gift for him. 13Hezekiah welcomed the messengers and showed them all the silver, the gold, the spices, and the fine oils that were in his storehouse. He even showed them where he kept his weapons. Nothing in his palace or in his entire kingdom was kept hidden from them.
14Isaiah asked Hezekiah, “Where did these men come from? What did they want?”
“They came all the way from Babylonia,” Hezekiah answered.
15“What did you show them?” Isaiah asked.
Hezekiah answered, “I showed them everything in my kingdom.”
16Then Isaiah told Hezekiah:
I have a message for you from the Lord. 17 One day everything you and your ancestors have stored up will be taken to Babylonia. The Lord has promised that nothing will be left. 18 Some of your own sons will be taken to Babylonia, where they will be disgraced and made to serve in the king's palace.
19Hezekiah thought, “At least our nation will be at peace for a while.” So he told Isaiah, “The message you brought me from the Lord is good.”
Hezekiah Dies
(2 Chronicles 32.32,33)
20Everything else Hezekiah did while he was king, including his brave deeds and how he made the upper pool and tunnel bring water into Jerusalem, is written in The History of the Kings of Judah. 21Hezekiah died, and his son Manasseh became king.
translation_text:
Eeseekiyaasi búŋkì ki ká dicáaǹdi
(Kpèè Yees 38.1-8, kpèè 2 Kroo 32.24 mun)
1Ŋyunti gbantee Eeseekiyaasi nìn búŋkì ki làá kpú. Ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeesaya, Amɔtisi jipɔɔn cūtìi māntì u-pu ní ki bí-u yii: «Ti-Dindaan bí yii á bɔ́ntí a-dicaŋku, di sá yii a làá kpú ní, saa làá ŋmátí.» 2Niinee ní Eeseekiyaasi fātì u-nimbiin ki túĺ digundi ní ki mēē ti-Dindaan yii: 3«M-Dindaan, m gbāam̀-si ní. Téetí yii m nóó-si nì ibaamɔn nì dipɔbil diba ní ki ŋá tin fáatiǹ-see.» U mēē mimmee ní ki súń tikpil.
4Yeesaya kaa nìn dá láá nyáń diciŋkpaandin ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì u ki bí-u yii: 5«Gítí kí tùkù m-nibooliŋu kpootiliu Eeseekiyaasi yii: <Ti-Dindaan, a-naanja Daafiidi Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M gbìl̄ a-wimmeem ki ká a-nyinnyim. Béé yii m làá cáaǹ-si. Nì iwiin ita dal, a làá ŋmā kí fàtīí kíĺ kí nīn cáà ti-Dindaan Diikun. 6Áli gba m làá fɔ̀kɔn̄ a-maŋfal wiiŋyi abin saalku kí kūtì. M làá fīī sii nì kitiŋ nee kí nyāntí Asuur bɔtiu ŋaan. M-yindi pu nì m-tɔntɔnliu Daafiidi puee, m làá wúń kitiŋ nee pu.>»
7Ní Yeesaya tīī mara nee yii: «Nàmaan fiigi biliŋ kí cáań!» Ní bi nàn̄ ki cáań ki nákáǹ ubɔti wunti laakin wùee pu ní u pɔ́ɔkì. 8Niinee Eeseekiyaasi bí Yeesaya yii: «Ba daaŋku ní m làá dūú béé yii m làá ká dicáaǹdi ní iwiin ita dalee, m làá ŋmā kí fàtīí kíĺ kí nīn cáà ti-Dindaan Diikun?» 9Ní Yeesaya kíí-u yii: «Ti-Dindaan làá tīī-si kudaaŋŋu kí dàkà-si yii u nín pōoǹ puee u làá ŋá míǹ. Ti-Dindaan làá yàntī mboon ŋun lítì Akaasi kɔliŋ puee ń fàtīí sútí kí jɔ̄m̀ akɔl saalaa pu. A là mboon ń cù nyɔkɔpu puɔɔɔ, boon pú ní?» 10Ní Eeseekiyaasi kíí yii: «An sá sɔkɔmii ki tīī mboon ŋú cù nyɔkɔpu ki jítiǹ ŋú sútí boon.» 11Niinee Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeesaya mēē ti-Dindaan ní úǹ yāntì mboon sútì ki jɔ́m̀ Akaasi kɔliŋ pu, akɔl saalaa ŋin pu ŋu bàà lítèe pu.
Babiloon bɔtiu Meeroodaki-Baladan tú binib Eeseekiyaasi cee
(Kpèè Yees 39)
12Ŋyunti gbantee, Babiloon bɔtiu Baladan jipɔɔn Meeroodaki-Baladan nìn gbìl̄ yii Eeseekiyaasi búŋkì. Niinee ní u ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu ki nyàab̄ tiwampɔkaal ki tú bí cáá cùnnì kí tīī-u. 13Bin bi túee nín bàn̄ee, ní an mɔ́ɔkiǹ Eeseekiyaasi ní u yōoǹ-bi ki kɔ́ǹ kudii kun poon ní u nìn kpáafí u-gaajawanti nì animbil nì sindaariya nì talaalub nì ikpafi in sɔ́fèe ki dàkā-bi. U nìn dàkā-bi laakin u nìn kpáafí u-janjawanti mun nì tijanjawan kɔkɔee. Tiba kaa nìn kíǹ Eeseekiyaasi cindin nì u-beelin waa dūu dàkā-bi.
14Tíǹ boonee ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeesaya dɔ́miń ki ká ubɔti Eeseekiyaasi ní ki bālifì-u yii: «Binib nee tùkū-si yii ba, ní la ní bi nyánní?» Ní Eeseekiyaasi kíí yii: «Bi nyánní ndan ní. Doooo Babiloon tiŋkin ní bi nyánní.» 15Ní Yeesaya gíti nìkī ki bālifì-u yii: «Ba ní bi ká a-beecindin?» Ní Eeseekiyaasi kíí yii: «Bi pée ká tin kɔkɔ pée bí m-beecindinee ní. Tiba kaa kíǹ m-nimbikpaafidiikun maa dūu dàkā-bi.» 16Niinee ní Yeesaya bí Eeseekiyaasi yii: «Pīlifì tibɔti tin ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan sòon̄ee: 17<Ŋwiin ŋubɔ bí ki dòoń, tin kɔkɔ bí a-dumpu nee nì tin kɔkɔ a-baabi kpáafì ki síiǹee, bi làá dāá kóoǹ kɔkɔ kí cùnnì Babiloon tiŋkin. Tiba kaa làá dāá kíń doo, ti-Dindaan di sòon̄ míǹ. 18Bi làá dāá cúú a-jipɔmbi tikpil bin sisi a-ba màl̄ee, kí cùnnì Babiloon bɔtiu cee kí dū-bi kí ŋá bifaabi bí nīn tūǹ atuun ki tìì-u.>» 19Ní Eeseekiyaasi kíí Yeesaya yii: «Tibɔmɔntiil ní ti-Dindaan tùkū-si a cáań ki nāatì-mi nee.» Di sá yii u nìn lī u-neen yii: «Ti làá nīn bí ŋgbansɔŋfi nì dibatɔlin m-maŋfal wiiŋyi kɔkɔ poon.»
20Eeseekiyaasi tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee nì u-pɔ́ɔǹtam kɔkɔ nì tin kɔkɔ u ŋée nì u nín gbìn̄ dinyimbɔbil nì u nín cátì nnyinsan pu ki dáaĺ nnyim ki kɔ́ǹ kitiŋin puee ŋmàn̄ ki kā Juuda bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun. 21Eeseekiyaasi kpíì ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ u-naanjab ní u-jipɔɔn Manasee fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.

english_text:
King Manasseh of Judah
(2 Chronicles 33.1-20)
1Manasseh was 12 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled 55 years from Jerusalem. His mother was Hephzibah. 2 Manasseh disobeyed the Lord by following the disgusting customs of the nations that the Lord had forced out of Israel. 3He rebuilt the local shrines that his father Hezekiah had torn down. He built altars for the god Baal and set up a sacred pole for worshiping the goddess Asherah, just as King Ahab of Israel had done. And he faithfully worshiped the stars in heaven.
4 In the temple, where only the Lord was supposed to be worshiped, Manasseh built altars for the worship of pagan gods 5and the stars. He placed these altars in both courts of the temple, 6-7 and even set up the pole for Asherah there. Manasseh practiced magic and witchcraft; he asked fortunetellers for advice and sacrificed his own son. He did many sinful things and made the Lord very angry.
Years ago the Lord had told David and his son Solomon:
Jerusalem is the place I prefer above all others in Israel. It belongs to me, and there I will be worshiped forever. 8If my people will faithfully obey all the commands in the Law of my servant Moses, I will never make them leave the land I gave to their ancestors.
9But the people of Judah disobeyed the Lord. They listened to Manasseh and did even more sinful things than the nations the Lord had wiped out.
10One day the Lord said to some of his prophets:
11King Manasseh has done more disgusting things than the Amorites, and he has led my people to sin by forcing them to worship his idols. 12Now I, the Lord God of Israel, will destroy both Jerusalem and Judah! People will hear about it but won't believe it. 13Jerusalem is as sinful as Ahab and the people of Samaria were. So I will wipe out Jerusalem and be done with it, just as someone wipes water off a plate and turns it over to dry.
14I will even get rid of my people who survive. They will be defeated and robbed by their enemies. 15My people have done what I hate and have not stopped making me angry since their ancestors left Egypt.
16Manasseh was guilty of causing the people of Judah to sin and disobey the Lord. He also refused to protect innocent people—he even let so many of them be killed that their blood filled the streets of Jerusalem.
17Everything else Manasseh did while he was king, including his terrible sins, is written in The History of the Kings of Judah. 18He died and was buried in Uzza Garden near his palace, and his son Amon became king.
King Amon of Judah
(2 Chronicles 33.21-25)
19Amon was 22 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled from Jerusalem for 2 years. His mother Meshullemeth was the daughter of Haruz from Jotbah. 20Amon disobeyed the Lord, just as his father Manasseh had done. 21Amon worshiped the idols Manasseh had made and 22refused to be faithful to the Lord, the God his ancestors had worshiped.
23Some of Amon's officials plotted against him and killed him in his palace. 24-26He was buried in Uzza Garden. Soon after that, the people of Judah killed the murderers of Amon, then they made his son Josiah king.
Everything else Amon did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_text:
Manasee, Juuda bɔtiu
(Kpèè 2 Kroo 33.1-10,18-20)
1Manasee nìn cáá abin saalaa nì ali ní ki kpántì ubɔti. U nìn kóò Jeerusaleem ní ki jíń dibeel abin aŋmoo kpá imuŋku ita. Bi nìn yíì u-na yii Eefisiba. 2U nìn ŋá tin kaa kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee. U nìn dū u-ba ki líiǹ ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin atimbun ŋin nib ti-Dindaan nìn jìn̄ ki cáań Isirayeel yab ki kāaǹee. 3U nìn fātìi máń isaraafan in nìn bí ŋgbantamu pu u-baa Eeseekiyaasi nìn kúntèe. U nìn máń diwaal Baal nsaraafan, ní ki nyàab̄ ŋwindɔ ki cóoǹ kii Isirayeel bɔtiu Akaab nín nìn ŋá puee, ní ki nìn gbàantí ki jáaḿ iŋmalbi. 4U nìn máń isaraafan iba mun ti-Dindaan Diikun, min kɔkɔ ti-Dindaan nìn lī yii: «Jeerusaleem niin ní m làá nīn lèekī m-ba ki dàkèe.» 5U nìn gíti máń isaraafan ti-Dindaan Diiku ciŋŋi liitilin ki tīī iŋmalbi in bí kutaa puee. 6U nìn dū u-jipɔɔn ki wùn̄ ŋŋmi ki ŋá saraa. U nìn būū tibɔɔl ki ŋáań kukpaŋkpantiiu tuuŋŋi ní ki bàlifī bitaŋkpiibi kí béé tin bí ki dòońee. U nìn ŋá tin kaa pée kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee ki gbítì u-ŋuul. 7U nìn máń Aseera waal ki síiǹ ti-Dindaan Diikun. Ama ti-Dindaan nìn tùkū Daafiidi nì u-jipɔɔn Saloomɔn yii: «Kudii nee poon nì Jeerusaleem tiŋki kin m lēē Isirayeel naakɔti kɔkɔ kansikinee poon ní m làá nīn pée lèekī m-ba ki dàkà. 8M-nibooliŋu yaa tɔ́ m-bɔkpaaŋi kɔkɔ nì m-marab bin kɔkɔ m-tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi tīī-bee, m kpá kí yàntī bí nīn tú ki yìiǹ kí wàatī kitiŋ kin ní m tīī bi-naanjabee.» 9Ama Juuda yab kaa nìn pílifì ti-Dindaan nyɔkɔ. Ubɔti Manasee nìn yāntì bi gáatì ki ŋá tin kaa kítèe ki jítiǹ atimbun ŋin nib ti-Dindaan nìn kūū ki céetì ki cáań Isirayeel yab ki kāaǹee.
10Niinee ti-Dindaan dī u-tɔntɔnliibi bibɔnaatiliibi pu ki lī yii: 11«Juuda bɔtiu Manasee ŋá ntimbiil tuuŋŋi nee kɔkɔ. U ŋá tin kaa kítèe ki jítiǹ Amɔɔr yab nín nìn ŋá puee. U dī u-waaŋi pu ki yāntì Juuda yab ŋá ikpiti. 12An puee man ni-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <M làá cáań nnaabukpaan ŋubɔ kí tɔ̄ Juuda yab nì Jeerusaleem pu. Án làá dāá ŋá un yaa láa gbìl̄ nnaabu gbanti puee bitii. 13M làá nàan̄ Jeerusaleem kii m nín nāaǹ Samaarii tiŋki nì Akaab dicaŋku puee ní. M làá ŋàtī bin kóò Jeerusaleemee kí fá kii bi nín cákaĺ disambil pu kí lábití-dì kí cíkińee ní. 14M làá dāá fàtī m-boon kí tīī m-nibooliŋu nib bin làá dāá kíń kí nīn bí dimaŋfalinee. M làá dāá dū-bi kí ŋá bi-nannanliibi ŋaan ní bíǹ ń fūkul̀-bi kí yòon̄ tin kɔkɔ bi cááyee. 15Kun pu m làá ŋá mimmee di sá yii m-nibooliŋu pée ŋáań tin kaa kítèe ní m-nimbiin. Kí yòon̄ ŋwiin ŋun ní m nyántìń bi-naanjab Eejipiti tiŋkin ki dāa sāā díǹ neeyee, bi pée bí ní ki gbítí m-ŋuul.>»
16Manasee nìn kūū maanyiibab tikpil ki yāntì Jeerusaleem tiŋki kɔkɔ gbí fatiku, kí dūú kūtì ikpiti in u ŋá ki yāntì Juuda yab ŋá tin kaa kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee.
17Manasee tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee nì tin kɔkɔ u ŋée nì ikpiti in ní u ŋée kɔkɔ ŋmàn̄ ki kā Juuda bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun. 18Manasee kpíì ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ u-baabi ní bi síb́-u bukpaa bun bí u-cindinee. Bi nìn gíti yíì bukpaayee Usa kpaabu ní. U-jipɔɔn Amɔn di fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.
Amɔn, Juuda bɔtiu
(2 Kroo 33.21-25)
19Amɔn nìn cáá abin mmuŋku nì ali ní ki kpántì ubɔti. U nìn kóò Jeerusaleem ní ki jíń dibeel abin ali. Bi nìn yíì u-na Meesuleemeeti. U-na nìn sá Yootiba tiŋkin ní ki sá Aruusi bisal. 20U nìn ŋá tin kaa nìn kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee kii u-baa Manasee nín nìn ŋá puee. 21U nìn pée dī u-baa tabɔbiliŋ ní deedee. U nìn jáaḿ awaa ŋin u-baa nìn jáaḿee ki gbàantí ŋi-nimbiin. 22U nìn dū ti-Dindaan, u-naanjab Nimbɔtiu ki fá, kaa nìn pée dī u-saŋŋu báà fiii.
23U-janjakpilib nìn bɔ́ntì u-pu ní ki kūū-u u-diikun. 24Ama Juuda yab nìn kūū bin kɔkɔ nìn bɔ́ntì ubɔti Amɔn puee ní ki dū u-jipɔɔn Joosiyaasi ki kāaǹ dibeel u-yil pu.
25Amɔn tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee nì tin kɔkɔ u ŋée ŋmàn̄ ki kā Juuda bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun. 26Bi nìn síb́-u u-kaakulin, Usa kpaabun. U-jipɔɔn Joosiyaasi di nìn fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.

english_text:
King Josiah of Judah
(2 Chronicles 34.1,2)
1 Josiah was 8 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled 31 years from Jerusalem. His mother Jedidah was the daughter of Adaiah from Bozkath. 2Josiah always obeyed the Lord, just as his ancestor David had done.
Hilkiah Finds The Book of God's Law
(2 Chronicles 34.8-28)
3After Josiah had been king for 18 years, he told Shaphan, one of his highest officials:
Go to the Lord's temple 4and ask Hilkiah the high priest to collect from the guards all the money that the people have donated. 5Tell Hilkiah to give it to the men supervising the repairs to the temple. They can use some of the money to pay 6the workers, and with the rest of it they can buy wood and stone for the repair work. 7 They are honest, so we won't ask them to keep track of the money.
8While Shaphan was at the temple, Hilkiah handed him a book and said, “Look what I found here in the temple—The Book of God's Law.”
Shaphan read it, 9then went back to Josiah and reported, “Your officials collected the money in the temple and gave it to the men supervising the repairs. 10But there's something else, Your Majesty. The priest Hilkiah gave me this book.” Then Shaphan read it out loud.
11When Josiah heard what was in The Book of God's Law, he tore his clothes in sorrow. 12At once he called together Hilkiah, Shaphan, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Achbor son of Micaiah, and his own servant Asaiah. He said, 13“The Lord must be furious with me and everyone else in Judah, because our ancestors did not obey the laws written in this book. Go find out what the Lord wants us to do.”
14The five men left at once and went to talk with Huldah the prophet. Her husband was Shallum, who was in charge of the king's clothes. Huldah lived in the northern part of Jerusalem, and when they met in her home, 15she said:
You were sent here by King Josiah, and this is what the Lord God of Israel says to him: 16“Josiah, I am the Lord! And I will see to it that this country and everyone living in it will be destroyed. It will happen just as this book says. 17The people of Judah have rejected me. They have offered sacrifices to foreign gods and have worshiped their own idols. I cannot stand it any longer. I am furious.
18“Josiah, listen to what I am going to do. 19I noticed how sad you were when you read that this country and its people would be completely wiped out. You even tore your clothes in sorrow, and I heard you cry. 20So I will let you die in peace, before I destroy this place.”
The men left and took Huldah's answer back to Josiah.
translation_text:
Joosiyaasi, Juuda bɔtiu
(2 Kroo 34.1-2)
1Joosiyaasi nìn cáá abin anii ní ki kpántì ubɔti. U nìn kóò Jeerusaleem ní ki jíń dibeel abin mmuŋku nì saalaa nì diba. Bi nìn yíì u-na yii Yeediida. U-na nìn sá Bootikaati tiŋkin ní ki sá Adaaya bisal. 2U nìn ŋá tin fáatiǹ ti-Dindaanee. U nìn nóó u-naanja Daafiidi tabɔbiliŋ ní deedeedee, waa nìn kpēetì ki cūtì ŋgan púɔɔɔ, ŋgiil pú.
Usaraaŋakpil ká Marab Gbɔŋku
(2 Kroo 34.8-18)
3Ubɔti Joosiyaasi nín jíń dibeel abin saalku nì ata poonee ní u tú u-gbaŋŋmaliu Safan, Asaliya jipɔɔn, Meesulam naantiiu ti-Dindaan Diikun ní ki bí-u yii: 4«Cùú ká usaraaŋakpil Ilikiya kí tùkù yii ú kàaǹ animbil ŋin kɔkɔ ní bi cáań ti-Dindaan Diikunee nì ŋin ní bipunyɔɔciitiliibi fōōyee. 5Bí dū animbilee kí tīī bin kpèé ti-Dindaan Diiku ŋāŋkitam tuuŋŋee kpilib, ní bíǹ ń lēē kí pà bitɔntɔnliibi bin bí ki tūǹ ti-Dindaan Diiku ŋāŋkitam tuuŋŋee. 6Bí lēē kí pà kapintab nì bidimaliibi nì bitɔntɔnliibi bin kíǹee, ní kí lēē kí dā idɔ nì ataŋkpee ŋin bi kpítèe kí dūú ŋāŋkì ti-Dindaan Diiku. 7Bí taa bàlifì-bi yii bí gbá animbil ŋin bi dūu tīī-bee kɔntaau, di sá yii bi sá bibulcinnib ní.»
8Ubɔti gbaŋŋmaliu Safan cáań ubɔti nyɔɔbundee ki bíl̀ usaraaŋakpil Ilikiyawuu nimbiin ní úǹ bí-u yii: «M ká Marab gbɔŋku ti-Dindaan Diikun!» Ilikiyawuu dū ti-Dindaan gbɔŋkuee ki tīī Safanee ní úǹ kàan̄. 9U kàan̄ mimmee ní ki cūtìi ká ubɔti ki bí-u yii: «A-tɔntɔnliibi bisaraaŋaliibi yōoǹ animbil ŋin kā dakaa poon ki sí ti-Dindaan Diikunee ki dūu tīī bin kpèé ti-Dindaan Diiku ŋāŋkitam tuuŋŋee kpilib.» 10Ní ubɔti gbaŋŋmaliu Safan gíti kútì ki lī yii: «Usaraaŋakpil Ilikiyawuu dū kugbɔŋu nee ki tīī-mi.»
Ní Safan kàan̄ kugbɔŋuee ki tīī ubɔti.
Joosiyaasi yāntì bi bālifì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Uulida
(Kpèè 2 Kroo 34.19-28)
11Bi nín kàan̄ tin kā Marab gbɔŋkun ubɔti gbìl̄ee ní u-pɔbil bíil̀ ní u cúú tiwan tin u pēēyee ki dáaĺ ki cátì. 12Míǹ boonee ní u yíiń usaraaŋakpil Ilikiyawuu nì Safan jipɔɔn Ayiikaam nì Mikaya jipɔɔn Akibɔɔr nì ugbaŋŋmal Safan nì u-kàliŋkpiliu Asaya ní ki tīī-bi mara yii: 13«Ní cùú bàlifì ti-Dindaan man nì Juuda yab kɔkɔ yil pu. Ní bàlifì-u tin di ŋmàn̄ ki kā kugbɔŋu nee poonee pu. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan gíí ti-pu diŋuul ŋkpitim pu. U gíí ti-pu diŋuul kun puee ti-naanjab kaa tɔ́ tin ŋmàn̄ ki kā kugbɔŋu nee pooneeyaaa, kaa ŋá kii tibɔtee nín bí yii bí ŋá puee.»
14Niinee usaraaŋakpil Ilikiyawuu nì Ayiikaam nì Akibɔɔr nì Safan nì Asaya nín cá Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Uulida cee. U-cal di nìn sá Saluum, Tiikifa jipɔɔn, Araasi naantiiu. U nìn kóò Jeerusaleem tincaliiki kipɔŋ poon ní. Úǹ di nìn kpèé bisaraaŋaliibi wampeeŋkaati ti-Dindaan Diikun. Usaraaŋakpil nì u-naacimbi dū tin bée ki máafì-uee, 15ní u bí-bi yii: «Ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Ní cùú tùkù un túnní-ni m-ceeyee yii: 16<M làá cáań nnaabu kí tɔ̄ Jeerusaleem tiŋki nì bin kɔkɔ kóò ki-nee pu, kii an nín ŋmàn̄ ki kā kugbɔŋu kun Juuda bɔtiu kàan̄ee poon puee, ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ. 17Jeerusaleem yab dū-mi ki fá ní ki tūutì talaalub ki tīī awaa ŋin sá bíǹ bi-ba ŋalii pu tuuŋŋee ki gbítì m-ŋuul. An pu ní m gíí kitiŋ nee pu diŋuul ŋkpitim pu, ní m-ŋuulee kpá kí sɔ̀ŋkì!> 18Ama ní tùkù Juuda bɔtiu un di túnní-ni ní dāan̄ kí bàlifì ti-Dindaanee yii: <Ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. A gbìl̄ tibɔti tin kā kugbɔŋu nee poonee, ní 19tibɔtee gbēē-si. A nín gbìl̄ tin m sòon̄ yii án làá bàń Jeerusaleem nì ki-nib puee, a sīntiǹ a-ba taapu. Tilafuŋman, kitiŋ nee làá kpántí kii kuteeuee, ní kí kpántí kii kitiŋ kin bi tɔ́ mbusuee. A nín gbìl̄ mimmee ní a dáaĺ ki cátì tiwan tin a pēēyee ní ki súń m-nimbiin. An puee ma mun gbìl̄ a-wimmeem. Man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ. 20Míǹ puee m làá yàntī á kpú kí cùú ŋàl̄ a-baabi nì ŋgbansɔŋfi ní bí síb́-si a-kaakulin. Sii kaa làá ká nnaabu ŋun m làá cáań kí tɔ̄ Jeerusaleem tiŋki puee.>»
Joosiyaasi fātìi pōoǹ ti-Dindaan dipoondi
(Kpèè 2 Kroo 34.29-32)
Ubɔti tuuŋyee gítì ki dū Unimbɔti nín kíí puee ki tùkū-u.

english_text:
Josiah Reads The Book of God's Law
(2 Chronicles 34.29-33)
1King Josiah called together the older leaders of Judah and Jerusalem. 2Then he went to the Lord's temple, together with the people of Judah and Jerusalem, the priests, and the prophets. Finally, when everybody was there, he read aloud The Book of God's Law that had been found in the temple.
3After Josiah had finished reading, he stood by one of the columns. He asked the people to promise in the Lord's name to faithfully obey the Lord and to follow his commands. The people agreed to do everything written in the book.
Josiah Follows the Teachings of God's Law
(2 Chronicles 34.3-7)
4 Josiah told Hilkiah the priest, the assistant priests, and the guards at the temple door to go into the temple and bring out the things used to worship Baal, Asherah, and the stars. Josiah had these things burned in Kidron Valley just outside Jerusalem, and he had the ashes carried away to the town of Bethel.
5Josiah also got rid of the pagan priests at the local shrines in Judah and around Jerusalem. These were the men that the kings of Judah had appointed to offer sacrifices to Baal and to the sun, moon, and stars. 6Josiah had the sacred pole for Asherah brought out of the temple and taken to Kidron Valley, where it was burned. He then had its ashes ground into dust and scattered over the public cemetery there. 7He had the buildings torn down where the male prostitutes lived next to the temple, and where the women wove sacred robes for the idol of Asherah.
8In almost every town in Judah, priests had been offering sacrifices to the Lord at local shrines. Josiah brought these priests to Jerusalem and had their shrines made unfit for worship—every shrine from Geba just north of Jerusalem to Beersheba in the south. He even tore down the shrine at Beersheba that was just to the left of Joshua Gate, which was named after the highest official of the city. 9Those local priests could not serve at the Lord's altar in Jerusalem, but they were allowed to eat sacred bread, just like the priests from Jerusalem.
10 Josiah sent some men to Hinnom Valley just outside Jerusalem with orders to make the altar there unfit for worship. That way, people could no longer use it for sacrificing their children to the god Molech. 11He also got rid of the horses that the kings of Judah used in their ceremonies to worship the sun, and he destroyed the chariots along with them. The horses had been kept near the entrance to the Lord's temple, in a courtyard close to where an official named Nathan-Melech lived.
12 Some of the kings of Judah, especially Manasseh, had built altars in the two courts of the temple and in the room that Ahaz had built on the palace roof. Josiah had these altars torn down and smashed to pieces, and he had the pieces thrown into Kidron Valley, just outside Jerusalem. 13 After that, he closed down the shrines that Solomon had built east of Jerusalem and south of Spoil Hill to honor Astarte the disgusting goddess of Sidon, Chemosh the disgusting god of Moab, and Milcom the disgusting god of Ammon. 14He tore down the stone images of foreign gods and cut down the sacred pole used in the worship of Asherah. Then he had the whole area covered with human bones.
15 But Josiah was not finished yet. At Bethel he destroyed the shrine and the altar that Jeroboam son of Nebat had built and that had caused the Israelites to sin. Josiah had the shrine and the Asherah pole burned and ground into dust. 16 As he looked around, he saw graves on the hillside. He had the bones in them dug up and burned on the altar, so that it could no longer be used. This happened just as God's prophet had said when Jeroboam was standing at the altar, celebrating a festival.
Then Josiah saw the grave of the prophet who had said this would happen 17 and he asked, “Whose grave is that?”
Some people who lived nearby answered, “It belongs to the prophet from Judah who told what would happen to this altar.”
18Josiah replied, “Then leave it alone. Don't dig up his bones.” So they did not disturb his bones or the bones of the old prophet from Israel who had also been buried there.
19Some of the Israelite kings had made the Lord angry by building pagan shrines all over Israel. So Josiah sent troops to destroy these shrines just as he had done to the one in Bethel. 20He killed the priests who served at them and burned their bones on the altars.
After all that, Josiah went back to Jerusalem.
Josiah and the People of Judah Celebrate Passover
(2 Chronicles 35.1-19)
21Josiah told the people of Judah, “Celebrate Passover in honor of the Lord your God, just as it says in The Book of God's Law.”
22This festival had not been celebrated in this way since the time that tribal leaders ruled Israel or the kings ruled Israel and Judah. 23But in Josiah's eighteenth year as king of Judah, everyone came to Jerusalem to celebrate Passover.
The Lord Is Still Angry with the People of Judah
24Josiah got rid of every disgusting person and thing in Judah and Jerusalem—including magicians, fortunetellers, and idols. He did his best to obey every law written in the book that the priest Hilkiah found in the Lord's temple. 25No other king before or after Josiah tried as hard as he did to obey the Law of Moses.
26But the Lord was still furious with the people of Judah because Manasseh had done so many things to make him angry. 27The Lord said, “I will desert the people of Judah, just as I deserted the people of Israel. I will reject Jerusalem, even though I chose it to be mine. And I will abandon this temple built to honor me.”
Josiah Dies in Battle
(2 Chronicles 35.20—36.1)
28Everything else Josiah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah. 29During Josiah's rule, King Neco of Egypt led his army north to the Euphrates River to help the king of Assyria. Josiah led his troops north to fight Neco, but when they met in battle at Megiddo, Josiah was killed. 30A few of Josiah's servants put his body in a chariot and took it back to Jerusalem, where they buried it in his own tomb. Then the people of Judah found his son Jehoahaz and poured olive oil on his head to show that he was their new king.
King Jehoahaz of Judah
(2 Chronicles 36.2-4)
31Jehoahaz was 23 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled from Jerusalem only 3 months. His mother Hamutal was the daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah. 32Jehoahaz disobeyed the Lord, just as some of his ancestors had done.
33King Neco of Egypt had Jehoahaz arrested and put in prison at Riblah near Hamath. Then he forced the people of Judah to pay him 3.4 tons of silver and 34 kilograms of gold as taxes. 34 Neco appointed Josiah's son Eliakim king of Judah, and changed his name to Jehoiakim. He took Jehoahaz as a prisoner to Egypt, where he died.
35Jehoiakim forced the people of Judah to pay higher taxes, so he could give Neco the silver and gold he demanded.
King Jehoiakim of Judah
(2 Chronicles 36.5-8)
36 Jehoiakim was 25 years old when he was appointed king, and he ruled 11 years from Jerusalem. His mother Zebidah was the daughter of Pedaiah from Rumah. 37Jehoiakim disobeyed the Lord by following the example of his ancestors.
translation_text:
1Ubɔti nìn tú bi yíiń Juuda nì Jeerusaleem tindaŋkpilib ní bi kóoǹ ki kpáfì u-cee. 2Boonee ní u nín jɔ́ḿ ti-Dindaan Diikun ki kpáaǹ Juuda yab kɔkɔ nì Jeerusaleem yab kɔkɔ, an dàkà yii bisaraaŋaliibi nì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi nì samaa kɔkɔ kí yòon̄ ŋwaamu kí tin cáá sāā bikpaambi, ubɔ kaa nìn kíǹ. Niinee ní ubɔti kàan̄-bi tin kɔkɔ bi ŋmàn̄ an kā dipoondi gbɔŋku kun bi ká ti-Dindaan Diikunee. 3Ubɔti nìn yú ti-Dindaan Diiku kasarkau nyɔkɔpu ní ki pōoǹ kí nīn sí nì ti-Dindaan deedee, kí nīn ŋúb́ u-marab nì u-dàkatam nì u-bɔkpaaŋi nì u-pɔbil kɔkɔ nì u-naŋki kɔkɔ. U nìn gíti pōoǹ kí nīn tɔ́ tin kɔkɔ ŋmàn̄ ki kā dipoondi taŋkpapilintinee. Samaa kɔkɔ mun nìn kíí kí ŋá kii ubɔti nín nìn pōoǹ puee.
Joosiyaasi fātìi bɔ́ntì dinimbɔtinool
(2 Kroo 34.3-5)
4Míǹ boonee ní ubɔti tīī usaraaŋakpil Ilikiyawuu nì bisaraaŋaliibi bin bí ki tútúǹ-uee nì bin cí ti-Dindaan Diiku punyɔkɔkee mara yii bí nyāntí tiwan tin kɔkɔ bi nìn máń ki cáa jáaḿ diwaal Baal nì diwaal Aseera nì iŋmalbi in bí kutaa puee mmɔŋki. Ní bi nyántì tiwanee Jeerusaleem tiŋki kpaanceetiŋu, Seedrɔn tantakalin ki wùn̄ ŋŋmi, ní ki yōoǹ ŋfantam ki cūnnì Beeteel. 5Joosiyaasi nìn jìn̄ awaa saraaŋaliibi bin Juuda bɔtiibi nìn kāaǹ bí nīn ŋáań saraabi ŋgbantamu pu nì Juuda timmun nì Jeerusaleem kpaanceetiiyee. U nìn jìn̄ bin mun nìn tùutī talaalub ki tìì diwaal Baal nì ŋwìiń nì uŋmal nì iŋmalbi nì tin kɔkɔ pée ŋmíntí kutaa puee. 6U nìn cóotì diwaal Aseera windɔŋu ŋun nìn bí ti-Dindaan Diikunee ki cáa cūnnì Seedrɔn tantakalin, Jeerusaleem tiŋki kpaanceetiŋu. Bi nìn wùn̄-ŋu ŋŋmi niin ní ki dū ŋu-fantam ki yāaǹ samaa ceekun. 7U nìn gbáń ki wīī binib bin nìn bí ti-Dindaan Diikun ki ŋáań alaakpaatuunee diiŋŋi. Adiin gbantin ní binimpoobi nìn kàal̀ ki lù tiwampeeŋkaal tin bi pèentí ki jáaḿ diwaal Aseerayee.
8Míǹ boonee ní u yāntì bisaraaŋaliibi bin kɔkɔ bí Juuda tiŋkinee dɔ́miń. U nìn bíil̀ ipaan in bí ŋgbantamu pu bisaraaŋaliibi nìn tùutī talaalub ki tìì awaayee ki yōoǹ Geeba tiŋki ki cáa sāā Beerseeba. U nìn yāntì bi gbáń ki wīī isaraafan in bi nìn máń ki síiǹ Jeerusaleem tiŋki punyɔmmu caŋinee, cilinjee nsaraafan ŋun nìn bí Joosuwa un nìn sá gɔminee punyɔkɔpuee. Nsaraafanee nìn bí a yaa dī kipunyɔkɔee ki kóò kitiŋinee ŋgan pú ní. 9Baa nìn pú ŋgbantamu pu saraaŋaliibi gbanti nsan bí ŋá saraabi ti-Dindaan saraafaŋŋu ŋun bí Jeerusaleemee pu. Ama bi nìn ŋūǹ kí ŋmɔ́ kpɔnɔb bin baa ŋá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee kii bisaraaŋaliibi bin kíǹee nín ŋmóò puee.
10Ubɔti nìn bíil̀ Toofeeti naapaal din nìn bí Inoom tantakalinee, án nín làá ŋá pu ubɔ ń taa ti dū u-jipɔɔn àá u-bisal kí wà ŋŋmi kí ŋá saraa kí tīī diwaal Mooleeki mpaan gbanti puee. 11U nìn kúntì itaamu in ní Juuda bɔtiibi nìn dūu sú bi cáa jáaḿ ŋwìińee. Itaamu gbanti nìn bí ti-Dindaan Diiku punyɔkɔki caŋin ní, kaa dátiǹ ufaal Neetan-Meeleeki diiku, ní ki bí adiin ŋin bi máń ki kútì ti-Dindaan Diiku puee. Bi nìn wùn̄ ŋwìiń tɔrɔkub mun. 12U nìn tí gbáń ki wīī isaraafan in Juuda bɔtiibi nìn máń ki síiǹ Akaasi diiŋŋi yilpuee. U nìn wīī isaraafan in Manasee nìn máń ki síiǹ ti-Dindaan Diiku ciŋŋi aliitil poonee. U nín gbáń ki wīī-i míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki yōoǹ ki cáa fá Seedrɔn tantakalin. 13U nìn bíil̀ ŋgbantamu pu saraafaŋyi in ubɔti Saloomɔn nìn máń Ɔliifi jool ŋgiil pú, Jeerusaleem caŋinee.
