An pu ní man a-tɔntɔnliu ká dipɔbil ki gbāā a-nimbiin ki mèé-si nee. 26Kɔŋkɔnnee ti-Dindaan, sii un di sá Unimbɔtee, sii di pōoǹ yii a làá ŋá-mi tiŋaŋkpaandi gbanti! 27A lēē kí bìin̄ m-dicaŋku pu án nín làá ŋá pu m-naantiibi ń nīn pée sá bibɔtiibi a-nimbiin kí nīn cá jaanjaanee. An nín sá yii sii ti-Dindaan di bīiǹ bi-puee, bi làá pée ká dibiindi ní kí nīn cá jaanjaan!»

english_text:
A List of David's Victories in War
(2 Samuel 8.1-14)
1Later, David attacked and defeated the Philistines. He captured their town of Gath and the nearby villages.
2David also defeated the Moabites, and so they had to accept him as their ruler and pay taxes to him.
3While King Hadadezer of Zobah was trying to gain control of the territory near the Euphrates River, David met him in battle at Hamath and defeated him. 4David captured 1,000 chariots, 7,000 chariot drivers, and 20,000 soldiers. And he crippled all but 100 of the horses.
5When troops from the Syrian kingdom of Damascus came to help Hadadezer, David killed 22,000 of them. 6Then David stationed some of his troops in Damascus, and the people there had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him.
Everywhere David went, the Lord helped him win battles.
7Hadadezer's officers had carried gold shields, but David took these shields and brought them back to Jerusalem. 8 He also took a lot of bronze from the cities of Tibhath and Cun, which had belonged to Hadadezer. Later, Solomon used this bronze to make the large bowl called the Sea, and to make the pillars and other furnishings for the temple.
9-10King Tou of Hamath and King Hadadezer had been enemies. So when Tou heard that David had defeated Hadadezer's whole army, he sent his son Hadoram to congratulate David on his victory. Hadoram also brought him gifts made of gold, silver, and bronze. 11David gave these gifts to the Lord, just as he had done with the silver and gold he had captured from Edom, Moab, Ammon, Philistia, and Amalek.
12 Abishai the son of Zeruiah defeated the Edomite army in Salt Valley and killed 18,000 of their troops. 13Then he stationed troops in Edom, and the people there had to accept David as their ruler.
Everywhere David went, the Lord gave him victory in war.
A List of David's Officials
(2 Samuel 8.15-18)
14David ruled all Israel with fairness and justice.
15Joab the son of Zeruiah was the commander in chief of the army.
Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept the government records.
16Zadok the son of Ahitub and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar were the priests.
Shavsha was the secretary.
17Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was the commander of David's bodyguard.
David's sons were his highest-ranking officials.
translation_text:
Daafiidi nín jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ atimbun ŋiŋyee
(Kpèè 2 Sami 8.1-14)
1Míǹ boonee Daafiidi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Fiiliistii yab ki dū-bi ki ŋá u-taapu. U nìn fōō Gaati tiŋki nì ntimbilimu mun bí ki-taapuee. 2U nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Moowaab yab mun ní bi kpántì u-yumbui ki kíǹ ki pà lampoo ki tìì-u. 3U nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Adadeeseer. Siirii tiŋki Sooba kin bí Amaati watil púee bɔtiu dee. Ŋyunti gbantee, Adadeeseer nìn bíi mɔ̀ kí wàan̄ u-beel kí tin cáá sāā Eefiraati mɔɔl ní. 4Daafiidi nìn fōō u-cee janjatɔrɔkub kutuku ní ki cúú u-janjaliibi bitanjakaliibi binib kutukub biluli nì u-janjaliibi bin còom̄ kitiŋee binib kutukub mmuŋku. Daafiidi nìn lēē itaamu dilaataal ki síiǹ úǹ u-ba ní ki gāā ki kpātì in kíǹee tabilɔnti. 5Aram yab bin sá Damaasi tiŋkinee nìn dɔ́miń kí tūtuǹ Adadeeseer, Sooba bɔtiu. Daafiidi nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ bi mun, ki kūū Aram yab gbanti kansikin binib kutukub mmuŋku nì bili. 6Daafiidi nìn kāaǹ gɔminab Damaasi tiŋki pu. Aram yab nìn kíǹ ki bí Daafiidi taapu ní ki pà lampoo ki tìì-u. Laakin kamaa Daafiidi yaa nìn cūtèe, ti-Dindaan nìn tìì-u dijajil ní. 7Daafiidi nìn kóoǹ Adadeeseer janjaliibi gbampɔɔŋi ŋin sá sindaariyee ki cáa cūnnì Jeerusaleem tiŋkin. 8U nìn yōoǹ tasa kúti mun tikpil tikpil Tiibaati nì Kuuni timmu mun nìn bí Adadeeseer beelinee. An kúti ní Saloomɔn dāa dūu mɔ́ɔ́ kusɔŋkpaaŋŋu dikuŋkundi ki síiǹ kunimbɔtidiin nì ki-jaantalkub, ní ki mɔ́ɔ́ ku-sambiliŋ ŋin kɔkɔ bi nìn dū tasa kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́yee.
9Amaati bɔtiu Toowu gbìl̄ yii Daafiidi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Sooba bɔtiu Adadeeseer janjaliibi kɔkɔ. 10U nìn dū u-jipɔɔn Adooram ki tú yii ú cùú jāam̀ ubɔti Daafiidi. Adooram nìn jáam̀ ubɔti ki pàkā-u, kun puee u nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Adadeeseer. Di sá yii Toowu nì Adadeeseer nìn jáà ní. Adooram nìn kpáàa tú sindaariya nì animbil kúti nì tasa kúti wanti ki cáań ki pú Daafiidi. 11Ubɔti Daafiidi nìn dū an wanti gbanti kɔkɔ ki sú ti-Dindaan, kii u nín nìn dū animbil nì sindaariya un u nìn fōoń Eedoom yab nì Moowaab yab nì Amɔn yab nì Fiiliistii yab nì Amaleeki yab cee ki sú puee. 12Seeruya jipɔɔn Abiisayi nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Eedoom yab Ŋyaam tantakalin. U nìn kūū bi-kansikin binib kutukub saalku nì bita. 13Daafiidi nìn kāaǹ gɔminab Eedoom tiŋki pu ní ki dū ki-nib ki ŋá u-taapu. Laakin kamaa Daafiidi yaa nìn cūtèe, ti-Dindaan nìn tìì-u dijajil ní.
Daafiidi kàlimbi yiŋŋi
(Kpèè 2 Sami 8.15-18)
14Daafiidi nìn jíń dibeel Isirayeel tiŋki kɔkɔ pu ní. U nìn cáá ibaamɔn ní ki sòoǹ u-nibul kɔkɔ bɔti kaa pɔ̀ gandi. 15Seeruya jipɔɔn Joowaab di nìn sá bijanjaliibi kpiliu ukpaan. Ayiiluudi jipɔɔn Yoosafaati di nìn sá ubɔti taapu yɔu. 16Ayiituub jipɔɔn Sadooki nì Abiyataar jipɔɔn Abimeeleeki di nìn sá bisaraaŋaliibi. Safeesa di nìn sá ugbaŋŋmal. 17Yooyadaa jipɔɔn Beenayawuu di nìn kpèé Keereeti yab nì Peeleeti yab bin cí ubɔtee. Ubɔti Daafiidi u-ba jipɔmbi di sá u-kàliŋkpilib bin nìn pée bí ki kɔ́ĺ-uee.

english_text:
Israel Fights Ammon and Syria
(2 Samuel 10.1-19)
1Some time later, King Nahash of Ammon died, and his son Hanun became king. 2David said, “Nahash was kind to me, so I will be kind to his son.” He sent some officials to Ammon to tell Hanun how sorry he was that his father had died.
But when David's officials arrived at Ammon, 3the Ammonite leaders said to Hanun, “Do you really believe King David is honoring your father by sending these men to comfort you? He probably sent them to spy on our country, so he can come and destroy it.”
4Hanun arrested David's officials and had their beards shaved off and their robes cut off just below the waist, and then he sent them away. 5They were terribly ashamed.
When David found out what had happened to his officials, he sent a message that told them, “Stay in Jericho until your beards grow back. Then you can come home.”
6The Ammonites realized they had made David furious. So they paid 34 tons of silver to hire chariot troops from Mesopotamia and from the Syrian kingdoms of Maacah and Zobah. 7Thirty-two thousand troops, as well as the king of Maacah and his army, came and camped near Medeba. The Ammonite troops also left their towns and came to prepare for battle.
8David heard what was happening, and he sent out Joab with his army. 9The Ammonite troops marched to the entrance of the city and prepared for battle, while the Syrian troops took their positions in the open fields.
10Joab saw that the enemy troops were lined up on both sides of him. So he picked some of the best Israelite soldiers to fight the Syrians. 11Then he put his brother Abishai in command of the rest of the army and told them to fight against the Ammonites. 12Joab told his brother, “If the Syrians are too much for me to handle, come and help me. And if the Ammonites are too strong for you, I'll come and help you. 13Be brave and fight hard to protect our people and the towns of our Lord God. I pray he will do whatever pleases him.”
14Joab and his soldiers attacked the Syrians, and the Syrians ran from them. 15When the Ammonite troops saw that the Syrians had run away, they ran from Abishai's soldiers and went back into their own city. Joab then returned to Jerusalem.
16As soon as the Syrians realized they had been defeated, they sent for their troops that were stationed on the other side of the Euphrates River. Shophach, the commander of Hadadezer's army, led these troops to Ammon.
17David found out what the Syrians were doing, and he brought Israel's entire army together. They crossed the Jordan River, and he commanded them to take their positions facing the Syrian troops.
Soon after the fighting began, 18the Syrians ran from Israel. David killed 7,000 chariot troops and 40,000 regular soldiers. He also killed Shophach, their commander.
19When the kings who had been under Hadadezer's rule saw that Israel had defeated them, they made peace with David and accepted him as their new ruler. The Syrians never helped the Ammonites again.
translation_text:
Bi kpēē Daafiidi kàliŋkpilib fám
(Kpèè 2 Sami 10.1-5)
1Ŋyunti ŋubɔ boonee ní Amɔn yab bɔtiu Naasi kpíì ní u-jipɔɔn fōō u-yil ki kāl̀ dibeel. 2Niinee Daafiidi bí yii: «M làá ŋá Naasi jipɔɔn Anuun tiŋan kii u-baa nín nìn ŋá man tiŋan puee.» Daafiidi nìn lēē binib ki tú bí cù kí sɔ̀ŋkì Anuun pɔbil u-baa nín kpíìyee pu. Ní Daafiidi tɔntɔnliibi bin u lēē ki túee dūu bàn̄ Amɔn yab tiŋkin. 3Ama ní Amɔn yab yidambi bí Anuun yii: «A dàkafī yii Daafiidi nín là kí tīī a-baa tinyool kí sɔ̀ŋkì a-pɔbil puee ní u túnní binib a-ceeee? Waa túnní u-nib bí dāan̄ kí yìiǹ kí cɔ̄ŋkì kí béé kitiŋ filiŋfeetii níii?» 4Niinee ní Anuun yāntì bi cúú Daafiidi kàliŋkpilib ki kōol̀ bi-nyimpuliŋ, ki cátì bi-bɔkutiŋ ki ŋmāntiǹ bi-kpiliŋ ní ki jìn̄-bi. 5Ní bi cūtìi máafì Daafiidi binibee bɔti. U nìn lēē binib ki tú bi cūtìi túŋkì-bi nsanni kun puee bi nìn kɔ́ǹ-bi icoo tikpil. Ubɔti nìn tú bi tùkū-bi yii: «Ní gbíntí Jeeriikoo tiŋkin ni-nyimpuliŋ ń fàtīí nyā. Míǹ boonee ní nín gítiń doo nee.»
Daafiidi jáń nì Amɔn yab nì Siirii yab
(Kpèè 2 Sami 6–19)
6Anuun nì Amɔn yab ká yii Daafiidi kaa làá dū tin bí ŋée kí pɔ̄-bi. Niinee ní bi nyàab̄ animbil kúti tɔɔnib mmuŋku nì saalaa ki tú bi cūnnì ki tīī Aram yab bin kóò amɔɔ ali kansikinee nì bin kóò Maaka nì Sooba timmunee janjaliibi, bí dāá já kujaau kí tīī-bi kí kpáaǹ bi-janjatɔrɔkub nì bi-tanjakaliibi. 7Bi nìn ŋúń ki ká janjatɔrɔkub kutukub mmuŋku nì saalaa nì bili, ní ki tīī Maaka bɔtiu nì u-janjaliibi animbil. Bíǹ nìn dɔ́miń ki ŋātì bi-janjanaapaal Meedeeba tiŋki caŋin. Amɔn yab mun nìn nyánní bi-timmun ki dɔ́miń ki kpáfì kí já kujaau.
8Daafiidi nín gbìl̄ mimmee, ní u dū ujanjakpil Joowaab nì bijanjaliibi bin sá bibaatandambee ki tú. 9Amɔn yab nìn cūtì ki yúl̀ mpɔn pu bi-tiŋyil punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu kí já kujaau. Ama bibɔtiibi bin nìn dɔ́miń kí tūtuǹ-bee bíǹ nìn yúl̀ tisatin laaba. 10Joowaab ká yii kujaau làá nīn bí u-nyɔkɔpu nì u-boon pú. Di sá ní u lēē Isirayeel janjaliibi bimɔntiibi ki yāntì bi yúl̀ mpɔn pu ki bíitiǹ Aram yab. 11U nìn dū u-janjaliibi bin kíǹee ki ŋúbíǹ u-naal Abisayi ní ki yāntì bi yúl̀ mpɔn pu ki bíitiǹ Amɔn yab. 12Joowaab tùkū u-nabiki yii: «Siirii yab yaa bíi pɔ́ɔkíǹ-mee, á dāá tíkiń-mi. M yaa tí ká yii Amɔn yab bíi pɔ́ɔkíǹ-see, ma mun làá dāan̄ kí tíkiń-si. 13Dàkà dibaatandi, tí dàkà dibaatandi kí fīī ti-nibul nì ti-Nimbɔtiu timmu. Ti-Dindaan ń ŋá min u lèe.» 14Niinee Joowaab nì u-janjaliibi nín cá kí já nì Siirii yab, ní bíǹ sáǹ-bi. 15Amɔn yab nín ká yii Siirii yab sáǹee, ní bi mun sáǹ Abisayi, ki kɔ́ kitiŋin. Niinee ní Joowaab nín gítí Jeerusaleem tiŋkin.
16Siirii yab nín ká yii Isirayeel yab pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bee, ní bi tú binib bí cùú yíiń Siirii yab janjaliibi bin kóò Eefiraati mɔɔl lapu púee. Adadeeseer janjakpiliu Soobaaki di nìn līī bi-nyɔkɔpu. 17Ní bi tùkū Daafiidi an bɔti, ní u kóoǹ Isirayeel yab janjaliibi kɔkɔ ki kpáfì, ní bi nín cá ki dūtì Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ki cūtìi yúl̀ ŋkɔnjaloon pu. Siirii yab nìn yúl̀ mpɔ̀n pu ki tātìi gbāaǹ dikɔ̀ndi pu kí já nì Daafiidi. 18Ama Isirayeel yab nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi, ní bi sáǹ. Daafiidi yab nìn kūū itaamu in dátí janjatɔrɔkubee kutukub biluli, ní ki kūū bijanjaliibi bin còom̄ ataa puee binib kutukub imuŋku ili. Bi nìn kūū Siirii yab janjakpiliu Soobaaki. 19Bibɔtiibi bin kɔkɔ nìn bí Adadeeseer taapuee nìn ká yii Isirayeel yab jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi. Niinee ní bi nì Daafiidi sòon̄ ki gbìlīǹ tɔb ŋgbansɔŋfi ń nīn bí bi-kansikin. Bi nìn kíǹ ki bí u-taapu ní. Kí yòon̄ ŋyunti gbantee, Siirii yab kíǹ ki fàŋkí kí jòò Amɔn yab.

english_text:
The End of the War with Ammon
(2 Samuel 11.1; 12.26-31)
1 The next spring, the time when kings go to war, Joab marched out in command of the Israelite army and destroyed towns all over the country of Ammon. He attacked the capital city of Rabbah and left it in ruins. But David stayed in Jerusalem.
2Later, David himself went to Rabbah, where he took the crown from the statue of their god Milcom. The crown was made of about 34 kilograms of gold, and there was a valuable jewel on it. David put the jewel on his crown, then carried off everything else of value. 3He forced the people of Rabbah to work with saws, iron picks, and axes. He also did the same thing with the people in all the other Ammonite towns.
David then led Israel's army back to Jerusalem.
The Descendants of the Rephaim
(2 Samuel 21.15-22)
4Some time later, Israel fought a battle against the Philistines at Gezer. During this battle, Sibbecai from Hushah killed Sippai, a descendant of the Rephaim, and the Philistines were defeated.
5 In another battle against the Philistines, Elhanan the son of Jair killed Lahmi the brother of Goliath from Gath, whose spear shaft was like a weaver's beam.
6Another one of the Philistine soldiers who was a descendant of the Rephaim was as big as a giant and had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot. During a battle at Gath, 7he made fun of Israel, so David's nephew Jonathan killed him.
8David and his soldiers killed these three men from Gath who were descendants of the Rephaim.
translation_text:
Joowaab jáń ki fōō Raaba tiŋki
(Kpèè 2 Sami 11.1, 12.26-31)
1Dibindi tú an bàn̄ ŋyunti ŋun bibɔtiibi nyēē ki cáà kujaauee, ní Joowaab līntì Isirayeel janjaliibi nyɔkɔpu ki cūtìi nāaǹ Amɔn yab tiŋki kɔkɔ. U nìn bíi bɔ́ntí kí já nì bi-tiŋyil Raaba kí fōō-kì. Ama Daafiidi úǹ nìn gbíntì Jeerusaleem tiŋkin.
Joowaab nìn jáń ki fōō Raaba tiŋki ki nāaǹ-kì. 2Míǹ boonee ní Daafiidi cíkitì sindaariya beefuuliiki kin nìn cíkí Amɔn yab waal Miilkɔm yil puee. U nìn dáań ki ká yii ki-nyiŋfiŋu nìn jítiǹ kiiloobi mmuŋku nì saalaa pu. Ditaŋkpamɔntiil diba nìn náká ki-pu, ní bi cúú ki nákatì ki dūu nákáǹ Daafiidi beefuuliiki pu. Daafiidi nìn gíti yōoǹ tigaajawan tikpil kitiŋ gbantin. 3Daafiidi nìn cúú kitiŋee nib ki cūnnì ki tɔ́ atuun ŋin pɔ̄ɔ̄yee poon: bi nìn sèekì idɔ, ki kpítí ataŋkpee ní ki gàatī isufi. Míǹ ní Daafiidi ŋá Amɔn yab timmu mun kíǹee kɔkɔ poon. Boonee ní u fātìi nín gítí Jeerusaleem tiŋkin, u nì u-janjaliibi kɔkɔ.
Isirayeel yab nì Fiiliistii yab jaaku
(Kpèè 2 Sami 10.6-19)
4Míǹ boonee kujaau kubɔ nyáń Isirayeel yab nì Fiiliistii yab kansikin Geeseer tiŋkin. An jaaku poon ní Siibkayi un sá Usa tiŋkinee kūū Siipayi un sá Reefa naantiiu ubɔee. Bi nìn dū Fiiliistii yab ki ŋá bi-taapu. 5Kujaau kubɔ mun nìn gíti nyáń Isirayeel yab nì Fiiliistii yab kansikin ní Yayiir jipɔɔn kūū Gooliyaati un sá Gaati tiŋkinee naal Laamii. Laamii kpaŋki kin u nìn ŋúb́ee dɔŋu nìn gbìfì kii nsataludɔee ní. 6Kujaau kubɔ mun dāa gíti nyáń Gaati tiŋkin. Ku-poonee unaaciin ubɔ nìn bí ki cáá ŋŋambiyaamu muluu kuŋaŋfaau kamaa pu nì ntaŋambiyaamu muluu kutafaau kamaa mun pu. U-ŋambiyaamu nì u-taŋambiyaamu kɔkɔ nìn nyáń mmuŋku nì munaa dee. U mun nìn sá Arafa maaliŋun ní. 7U nìn sīī Isirayeel yab. Niinee Sama jipɔɔn Joonatan, Daafiidi wee kūū-u.
8Daafiidi nì u-janjaliibi di nìn kūū Fiiliistii yab janjaliibi gbanti. Bi nìn sá Gaati tiŋkin Arafa dicaŋkun ní.

english_text:
David Counts the People
(2 Samuel 24.1-9)
1Satan decided to cause trouble for Israel by making David think it was a good idea to find out how many people there were in Israel and Judah. 2David told Joab and the army commanders, “Count everyone in Israel, from the town of Beersheba in the south all the way north to Dan. Then I will know how many people can serve in my army.”
3Joab answered, “Your Majesty, even if the Lord made your kingdom a hundred times larger, you would still rule everyone in it. Why do you need to know how many soldiers there are? Don't you think that would make the whole nation angry?”
4But David would not change his mind. And so Joab went everywhere in Israel and Judah and counted the people. He returned to Jerusalem 5and told David that the total number of men who could serve in the army was 1,100,000 in Israel and 470,000 in Judah. 6Joab refused to include anyone from the tribes of Levi and Benjamin, because he still disagreed with David's orders.
God Punishes Israel
(2 Samuel 24.10-17)
7David's order to count the people made God angry, and he punished Israel. 8David prayed, “I am your servant. But what I did was stupid and terribly wrong. Please forgive me.”
9The Lord said to Gad, one of David's prophets, 10“Tell David that I will punish him in one of three ways. But he will have to choose which one it will be.”
11Gad went to David and told him:
You must choose how the Lord will punish you: 12Will there be three years when the land won't grow enough food for its people? Or will your enemies constantly defeat you for three months? Or will the Lord send a horrible disease to strike your land for three days? Think about it and decide, because I have to give your answer to God who sent me.
13David was miserable and said, “It's a terrible choice to make! But the Lord is kind, and I'd rather be punished by him than by anyone else.”
14So the Lord sent a horrible disease on Israel, and 70,000 Israelites died. 15Then he sent an angel to destroy the city of Jerusalem. But just as the angel was about to do that, the Lord felt sorry for all the suffering he had caused the people, and he told the angel, “Stop! They have suffered enough.” This happened at the threshing place that belonged to Araunah the Jebusite.
16David saw the Lord's angel in the air, holding a sword over Jerusalem. He and the leaders of Israel, who were all wearing sackcloth, bowed with their faces to the ground, 17and David prayed, “It's my fault! I sinned by ordering the people to be counted. They have done nothing wrong—they are innocent sheep. Lord God, please punish me and my family. Don't let the disease wipe out your people.”
David Buys Araunah's Threshing Place
(2 Samuel 24.18-25)
18The Lord's angel told the prophet Gad to tell David that he must go to Araunah's threshing place and build an altar in honor of the Lord. 19David followed the Lord's instructions.
20Araunah and his four sons were threshing wheat at the time, and when they saw the angel, the four sons ran to hide. 21Just then, David arrived, and when Araunah saw him, he stopped his work and bowed down.
22David said, “Would you sell me your threshing place, so I can build an altar on it to the Lord? Then this disease will stop killing the people. I'm willing to pay whatever you say it's worth.”
23Araunah answered, “Take it, Your Majesty, and do whatever you want with it. I'll even give you the oxen for the sacrifice and the wheat for the grain sacrifice. And you can use the threshing-boards for the fire. It's all yours!”
24But David replied, “No! I want to pay you what they're worth. I can't just take something from you and then offer the Lord a sacrifice that cost me nothing.”
25So David paid Araunah 600 gold coins for his threshing place. 26David built an altar and offered sacrifices to please the Lord and sacrifices to ask his blessing. David prayed, and the Lord answered him by sending fire down on the altar. 27Then the Lord commanded the angel to put the sword away.
28When David saw that the Lord had answered his prayer, he offered more sacrifices there at the threshing place, 29-30because he was afraid of the angel's sword and did not want to go all the way to Gibeon. That's where the sacred tent that Moses had made in the desert was kept, as well as the altar where sacrifices were offered to the Lord.
translation_text:
Daafiidi yāntì bi kàan̄ Isirayeel yab
(Kpèè 2 Sami 24.1-9)
1Ŋwiin ŋubɔee, Sitaan yíkì kí já nì Isirayeel yab ní ki lūkutì Daafiidi ú kàaǹ Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ. 2Daafiidi nìn bí Joowaab nì u-janjakpilib bin kíǹee yii: «Ní cùú kàam̀maan Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ, kí yòon̄ Beerseeba tiŋki ŋgiil pú kí cáá sāā Daani tiŋki ŋgan pú. Ni yaa kàan̄ ki dóòyee, ní gítiń kí dāá tùkù-mi ḿ béé bi-wíiŋŋu nyɔkɔm.» 3Ní Joowaab kíí-u yii: «Ti-baa ubɔti, m mèé yii ti-Dindaan ń yàntī u-nibul Isirayeel yab ń bùtī ŋfunyɔm dilaataal pu. Bi-kɔkɔ bí díǹ pu nee sii ti-baa ubɔti taapu ní. Kin ba pu ní a baasii nyàab̀ kí kàaǹ Isirayeel yab kí yàntī bí yìntī míǹ?» 4Nì míǹ kɔkɔee ubɔti marau nìn pɔ̄ɔ̄ ki jítiǹ Joowaab nín nìn dàkafī puee, ní úǹ dāa gīī ki ŋá míǹ. Joowaab nìn cúú nsan ki yìin̄ Isirayeel tiŋki kɔkɔn ní ki fātìi gítìń Jeerusaleem tiŋkin. 5Joowaab bāańee ní ki tùkū Daafiidi u nín kàan̄ binib bi-nyɔkɔm nyáń puee. U bí yii Isirayeel naakookun yab bin bàn̄ kí cù kujaauee sá binib miiliyɔn ubɔ nì binib kutukub dilaataal, ní Juuda naakookun yab bin bàn̄ kí cù kujaauee sá binib kutukub alaataa anaa nì imuŋku ita nì saalaa.
6Joowaab kaa nìn kàan̄ Leefii naakookun yab nì Beenjameen naakookun yab ki kútì bin kíǹee pu. Di sá yii ubɔti marauee kaa nìn kāliǹ-u báà fiii.
Unimbɔti dáaĺ Daafiidi tafal
(Kpèè 2 Sami 24.10-17)
7Tibɔti gbanti kaa nìn mɔ́ɔkiǹ Unimbɔti, ní u dáaĺ Isirayeel yab tafal. 8Ní Daafiidi bí Unimbɔti yii: «Ikpitikpaan ní m ŋá nee. Ama kɔŋkɔnnee m mèé-si yii á dū m-yìntitam gbanti kí pɔ̄-mi, kun puee m lafun ŋá kii m sá uwaatee ní.»
9Niinee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì ubɔnaatil Gaadi un di kpòotī Daafiidee ní ki bí-u yii: 10«Cùú tùkù Daafiidi yii man ni-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé: <Man ni-Dindaan, m dū tiwan tita ní ki bíl̀ u-nimbiin ú lēē tin u là ḿ dūú dáaĺ u-tafalee.>» 11Ní Gaadi cūtì Daafiidi cee ki bí-u yii: «Ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé. Ba ní a là ḿ dūú dáaĺ a-tafal ní? 12Ŋkùm ń nyā a-tiŋki pu abin ataaa, binannanliibi ń já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ-si iŋmal itaaa, bìlbil kúm ń jēetí kitiŋ nee pu ní ntuun ń dū ti-Dindaan tàataajiki kí pɔ̀fì binib Isirayeel tiŋki kɔkɔn iwiin ita? Kɔŋkɔnnee, dàkafì tiŋan kí tùkù-mi tin m làá tin kíí un túnní-mee.» 13Ní Daafiidi bí Gaadi yii: «M bí kunimbaakpaaŋŋu poon ní. Ama an sɔ́ ḿ kɔ́ ti-Dindaan ŋaan ki jítiǹ ḿ kɔ́ unil ŋaan, di sá yii ti-Dindaan úǹ poon mɔ̄ ní.»
14Di sá ní ti-Dindaan dū bìlbil kúm ki tɔ́ Isirayeel yab pu ní an kūū binib kutukub imuŋku ita nì saalaa. 15Unimbɔti nìn tú ntuun ŋú cùú nàan̄ Jeerusaleem tiŋki. Ama ti-Dindaan nín ká ntuunee bí ki nà binib puee, ní an gíti kɔ́-u falaa nnaabu gbanti pu. Di sá ní u bí ntuunee yii: «An ŋmāntèe, gbèen̄ee!»
Ŋyunti gbantee ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋu nìn yú ujeebusja Araafina bileegbanaapaal caŋin. 16Daafiidi wáaǹ ki kpēēyee ní ki ká ntuunee yú yilpu nì taapu kansikin ki fɔ́fì kitàataajiki ki túĺ Jeerusaleem tiŋki. Niinee ní Daafiidi nì bitindaŋkpilib tātìi gbāaǹ bi-yigbeeŋi tūū kitiŋ ki pēē kutukub. 17Ní Daafiidi bí Unimbɔti yii: «Man di kaa bí yii bí kàaǹ binibaaa? Man di ŋá ikpiti, man di yīntì, m-nibul mun ŋá ba? An sá man nì m-dicaŋku tafal ní á dáaĺ? Ti-Dindaan m-Nimbɔtiu, an sá man nì m-dicaŋku yab tafal ní á dáaĺ. Taa dū iween nee kí tɔ̄ a-nibul pu.»
Daafiidi máń ti-Dindaan nsaraafan
(Kpèè 2 Sami 24.18-25)
18Ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋu bí Gaadi ń tùkù Daafiidi yii: «Jɔ̄m̀ ujeebusja Araafina bileegbanaapaal pu kí mā ti-Dindaan nsaraafan.» 19Ní Daafiidi nín jɔ́ḿ kii ti-Dindaan nín dī Gaadi pu ki tīī mara puee. 20Ŋyunti gbantee Ɔrinan nìn bí u-naapaal pu ki gbáà bilee. U fātèe ní ki ká ntuun, ní u-jipɔmbi binaa bin nìn bí u-cee niinee sáǹ ki bál̀. 21Ní Daafiidi cōom̀ ki nín cá Ɔrinan cee. Ɔrinan kpēēyee Daafiidi dee ní u nyáń ki túŋkì-u ní ki tātìi gbāaǹ u-yigbeel tūū kitiŋ ubɔti nimbiin. 22Ní Daafiidi bí Ɔrinan yii: «Dū a-naapaal nee kí tīī-mi. M là kí mā ti-Dindaan nsaraafan ŋu-pu. Mimmee nnaabu ŋun jéetì dinibul pu nee làá gbèen̄. Dū-ŋu kí tīī-mi ḿ pà-si ŋu-daaku nín sá puee.» 23Ní Ɔrinan kíí Daafiidi yii: «Ti-baa ubɔti, yòon̄ tin kɔkɔ fáatì-see kí dūú ŋá saraabi. Kpèè inaa sèé á dūú ŋá saraawɔkaa. Tɔrɔku dɔkpalkaai mun sèé á dūú kpāā ŋŋmi kí wà saraabi, bilee mun sèé á dūú ŋá tijimpin saraau. M dū kɔkɔ ki tīī-si.» 24Ama ní ubɔti Daafiidi bí Ɔrinan yii: «Aayee, m làá dā a-bileegbanaapaal ní kí pà-si kunimbiŋmiiu nín sá puee. Maa là kí dū tin sá a-wantee nì faalaa wanti kí ŋá saraawɔkaa kí tīī m-Dindaan m-Nimbɔtiu.»
25Di sá ní Daafiidi pàn̄-u animbil jitɔmbi alaataa aluu dibileegbanaapaal pu. 26Daafiidi máń ti-Dindaan nsaraafan niin ní ki ŋá bisaraawɔkaabi nì mpèé saraabi. U nìn mēē ti-Dindaan ní úǹ kíí-u ki yāntì ŋŋmi nyánní yilpu ki wùn̄ bisaraawɔkaabi bin pá ŋfan puee. 27Niinee ní ti-Dindaan tùkū ntuunee yii ŋú gíiǹ kitàataajiki kí fúuń kujitooun.
28Daafiidi nìn ká yii ti-Dindaan kíí ki fōō u-wimmeem Ɔrinan un sá Jeebusi tiŋkinee bileegbanaapaal pu. Kí yòon̄ ŋyunti gbantee ní u kíǹ ki cáà niin múlmul ki ŋáań saraabi. 29Ŋyunti gbantee, circir kɔŋkooŋŋu ŋun Mooyiisi nìn ŋá kuteeunee nì bisaraawɔkaabi faŋŋu nìn bíń nsaraaŋapaan laŋki Gabawɔn tiŋkin ní. 30Ama Daafiidi kaa nìn gíti ŋūǹ kí cù niin kí bàlifì Unimbɔti, kun puee u nìn fāŋkì ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋu jikee tikpil.

english_text:
1David said, “The temple of the Lord God must be built right here at this threshing place. And the altar for offering sacrifices will also be here.”
David Prepares To Build the Temple
2David ordered the foreigners living in Israel to come to Jerusalem. Then he assigned some to cut blocks of stone for building the temple. 3He got a large supply of iron to make into nails and hinges for the doors, and he provided so much bronze that it could not be weighed. 4He also brought an endless supply of cedar logs from the cities of Sidon and Tyre.
5He said, “The temple for the Lord must be great, so that everyone in the world will know about it. But since my son Solomon is young and has no experience, I will make sure that everything is ready for the temple to be built.”
That's why David did all these things before he died.
David Instructs Solomon To Build the Temple
6David sent for his son Solomon and told him to build a temple for the Lord God of Israel. 7 He said:
My son, I wanted to build a temple where the Lord my God would be worshiped. 8But some time ago, he told me, “David, you have killed too many people and have fought too many battles. That's why you are not the one to build my temple. 9But when your son becomes king, I will give him peace throughout his kingdom. His name will be Solomon, because during his rule I will keep Israel safe and peaceful. 10Solomon will build my temple. He will be like a son to me, and I will be like a father to him. In fact, one of his descendants will always rule in Israel.”
11Solomon, my son, I now pray that the Lord your God will be with you and keep his promise to help you build a temple for him. 12May he give you wisdom and knowledge, so that you can rule Israel according to his Law. 13 If you obey the laws and teachings that the Lord gave Moses, you will be successful. Be strong and brave and don't get discouraged or be afraid of anything.
14I have all the supplies you'll need to build the temple: You have more than 3,000 tons of gold and over 34,000 tons of silver. There's also plenty of wood, stone, and more bronze and iron than I could weigh. Ask for anything else you need. 15I have also assigned men who will cut and lay the stone. And there are carpenters and people who are experts in working with 16gold, silver, bronze, and iron. You have plenty of workers to do the job. Now get started, and I pray that the Lord will be with you in your work.
17David then gave orders for the leaders of Israel to help Solomon. 18David said:
The Lord our God has helped me defeat all the people who lived here before us, and he has given you peace from all your enemies. Now this land belongs to the Lord and his people. 19Obey the Lord your God with your heart and soul. Begin work on the temple to honor him, so that the sacred chest and the things used for worship can be kept there.
translation_text:
1An di yì-tì ní Daafiidi nìn lī yii: «Doo di sá ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti diiku, ní doo di làá nīn kíǹ ki sá Isirayeel yab saraawɔkaabi faŋŋu.»
Daafiidi bɔ́ntì kunimbɔtidii mātam
2Daafiidi nìn yāntì bi kóoǹ binicambi bin kóò Isirayeel tiŋkinee ki kpáfì ní u lēē bi-kansikin bin làá kpítí ataŋkpee bí dūú mā Unimbɔti diikuee. 3U nìn bɔ́ntì tikúti tikpil ki yóoǹ bí dūú mɔ́ɔ́ ipiŋkpaakaa kí kpáá punuubi, nì ipiin in pu punuubi làá nīn sàkēe. U nìn bɔ́ntì tasa kúti tin wīikí unil kaa ŋūǹ kí ŋmàntēe ki síiǹ. 4U nìn bɔ́ntì seedir dɔi an kaa cáá ŋkaan ki kpúkuǹ, di sá yii Tiir nì Siidɔn yab nìn cáań-u seedir dɔi tikpil tikpil. 5Daafiidi nìn lī u-ban yii: «M-jipɔɔn Saloomɔn dáá pɔ̀ɔǹ, kaa láá nyí tiba. Ama kudii kun u làá mā ti-Dindaanee máaǹ kí nīn sá kukpaaŋŋu kí nīn cáá kunyaaŋŋu binib ń gbìl̄ ku-pu ntimu kɔkɔ poon. An puee m làá bɔ́ntí ku-mātam kí yóoń-u.» Di sá ní Daafiidi lafun bɔ́ntì tiwan tikpil ki síiǹ ki wāatì ní ki nín kpíì.
Daafiidi tīī Saloomɔn mara yii ú mā kunimbɔtidii
6Daafiidi yíiń u-jipɔɔn Saloomɔn ní ki tīī-u mara yii ú mā ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu kudii. 7Daafiidi tùkū Saloomɔn yii: «M-jipɔɔn, mama m-ba nìn lēē m-pɔbilin yii m làá mā ti-Dindaan m-Nimbɔtiu kudii. 8Ama ní ti-Dindaan tùkū-mi yii: <A jáń tijakpaandi tikpil ki kūū binib tikpil. Fatiku un kɔkɔ nyáń ki fá kitiŋ man nimbiinee puee, an kaa sá sii di làá mā kudii kun poon binib làá nīn dòoń ki jáaḿ-mee. 9Kpèè, a làá màal̀ kibininjabiki kiba, kì làá nīn sá ŋgbansɔŋfi niliu ní. M làá yàntī ŋgbansɔŋfi ń nīn bí u nì binannanliibi bin māntìi tú-uee kansikin. U-yindi di làá nīn sá Saloomɔn, taapu di sá yii <Ŋgbansɔŋfi daan>. U-beel yuntiŋuee, m làá dāá yàntī ŋgbansɔŋfi nì dibatɔl ń nīn bí Isirayeel tiŋki pu. 10Úǹ di làá dāá mā-mi kunimbɔtidii. U làá dāá nīn sá-mi ujipɔnti ní ḿ dāá nīn sá-u ubaati. M làá yàntī u-beel ń báań inyaan Isirayeel tiŋki pu kí nīn cá jaanjaan.>» 11«Míǹ puee kɔŋkɔnnee, m-jipɔɔn, ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu ń nīn bí a-cee á ŋmā kí mā-u kudii, kii u nín nìn pōoǹ a-pu puee. 12U yaa láa dū Isirayeel tiŋki pɔŋŋu ki ŋúbiǹ-see, ú dāá tīī-si iciin nì dinyil á ŋmā kí nīn tɔ́ úǹ ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu marau. 13A yaa tɔ́ abɔkpaa nì marab bin u dī Mooyiisi pu ki tīī Isirayeel yabee, ki cáá-bi ki tūǹ ditundee, án làá bútí-si tikɔkɔ poon. Pɔ́ɔǹ a-ba, kí ká dipɔbil, a-wunti ń taa yɔ̀tī, ní kí taa fàŋkì báà tiba. 14Kpèè, báà nì m-sool poonee, m pɔ́ɔǹ m-ba ki bɔ́ntì sindaariya un nyiŋfiŋu jítì tɔɔnib kutukub bita puee, nì animbil kúti tin nyiŋfiŋu jítì tɔɔnib kutukub mmuŋku nì saalaa puee. M bɔ́ntì tasa kúti nì tikúmɔntiil tin baa ŋūǹ kí ŋmàntēe mun ki yóoǹ, ki bɔ́ntì idɔ nì ataŋkpee mun. A dāa ŋūǹ kí nyàab̀ kí kūtì. 15Bitɔntɔnliibi tikpil bí ki làá tɔ̄-si atuun. Bitaŋkpakpitiliibi bí, bidɔkpitiliibi bí, kapintab bí, ní atuun ŋin kíǹee kɔkɔ tɔntɔnliibi bí ki nyí bi-tuuŋŋi tiŋan pu. 16Sindaariya nì animbil kúti nì tasa kúti nì tikúmɔntiil bí tikpil tikpil, baa ŋūǹ kí ŋmàntī kí béé ti-nyɔkɔm gba. An puee yīkì kí kíĺ ditundi ní ti-Dindaan ń nīn bí a-cee!»
17Míǹ boonee ní Daafiidi tīī Isirayeel bɔtibiliŋ kɔkɔ mara yii bí tūtuǹ u-jipɔɔn Saloomɔn. 18U bí-bi yii: «Kéè ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu bí ni-ceeyaa! U tīī-ni diŋuŋfil ajan kɔkɔ pu. U dū binib bin nìn kóò kitiŋ nee puee ki ŋá m-ŋaan. Díǹ pu nee bi kíǹ ki bí ti-Dindaan nì u-nibul taapu ní. 19An puee ní nyàab̀maan ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nì ni-pɔbil kɔkɔ nì ni-naŋki kɔkɔ. Ní yīkì kí kíĺ ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti circir kɔŋkooŋŋu mātam. Niinee, ni dāa ŋūǹ kí yòon̄ ti-Dindaan Poondi dakaau nì tiwan tin bi dūu sú Unimbɔtee kí yóoń kudii kun ni làá mā ti-Dindaan yindi puee poon.»

english_text:
David Assigns the Levites Their Duties
1 David was old when he chose his son Solomon to be king of Israel. 2Some time later, David called together all of Israel's leaders, priests, and Levites. 3He then counted the Levite men who were at least 30 years old, and the total was 38,000. 4He said, “Twenty-four thousand of the Levites will be in charge of the temple, 6,000 will be temple officials and judges, 54,000 will be guards at the temple, and 4,000 will praise the Lord by playing the musical instruments I have given them.”
6David then divided the Levites into three groups according to the clans of Levi's sons, Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
7Gershon had two sons: Ladan and Shimei. 8Ladan was the father of Jehiel, Zetham, and Joel. 9They were all family leaders among their father's descendants. Shimei was the father of Shelomoth, Haziel, and Haran. 10-11Later, Shimei had four more sons, in the following order: Jahath, Ziza, Jeush, and Beriah. But Jeush and Beriah didn't have many children, so their descendants were counted as one family.
12Kohath had four sons: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel. 13 Amram was the father of Aaron and Moses. Aaron and his descendants were chosen to be in charge of all the sacred things. They served the Lord by offering sacrifices to him and by blessing the people in his name. 14-15Moses, the man of God, was the father of Gershom and Eliezer, and their descendants were considered Levites. 16Gershom's oldest son was Shebuel. 17Rehabiah, who was Eliezer's only son, had many children. 18The second son born to Kohath was Izhar, and his oldest son was Shelomith. 19Hebron, the third son of Kohath, was the father of Jeriah, Amariah, Jahaziel, and Jekameam. 20Kohath's youngest son, Uzziel, was the father of Micah and Isshiah.
21Merari had two sons: Mahli and Mushi. Mahli was the father of Eleazar and Kish. 22Eleazar had no sons, only daughters, and they married their uncle's sons. 23Mushi the second son of Merari, was the father of Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth.
24These were the clans and families of the tribe of Levi. Those who were 20 years and older were assigned to work at the Lord's temple.
25David said:
The Lord God of Israel has given his people peace, and he will live in Jerusalem forever. 26 And so, the Levites won't need to move the sacred tent and the things used for worship from place to place. 27From now on, all Levites at least 20 years old 28 will serve the Lord by helping Aaron's descendants do their work at the temple, by keeping the courtyards and rooms of the temple clean, and by making sure that everything used in worship stays pure. 29They will also be in charge of the sacred loaves of bread, the flour for the grain sacrifices, the thin wafers, any offerings to be baked, and the flour mixed with olive oil. These Levites will weigh and measure these offerings.
30Every morning and evening, the Levites are to give thanks to the Lord and sing praises to him. 31They must also give thanks and sing praises when sacrifices are offered on each Sabbath, as well as during New Moon Festivals and other religious feasts. There must always be enough Levites on duty at the temple to do everything that needs to be done. 32They were once in charge of taking care of the sacred tent; now they are responsible for the temple and for helping Aaron's descendants.
translation_text:
Daafiidi yākatì Leefii yab akiti akiti
1Daafiidi nìn púĺ tikpil tikpil. U nìn dū u-jipɔɔn Saloomɔn ki kāaǹ dibeel Isirayeel tiŋki pu. 2Míǹ boonee ní u tú bi yíiń Isirayeel bɔtibiliŋ kɔkɔ ki kpáfì u-cee, ki kpáaǹ bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab.
3Niin ní u yāntì bi kàan̄ Leefii yab binicikitikaabi bin cáá kí yòon̄ abin mmuŋku nì saalaa kí nīn jɔ́ḿee. Bi nìn nyáń binib kutukub bili kpá imuŋku ili. 4Daafiidi nìn lēē bi-kansikin binib kutukub mmuŋku nì binaa bí nīn kpèé ti-Dindaan Diiku mātam tuuŋŋi, binib kutukub biluu bí nīn sá bigbaŋŋmaliibi nì bibɔsoonliibi, 5binib kutukub binaa bí nīn sá bipunyɔɔciitiliibi. U nìn lēē binib kutukub binaa bí nīn gà ilan ki nyɔ́ŋkí ti-Dindaan, kí nīn bɔ̀ɔ́ tibɔɔkaal tin úǹ Daafiidi u-ba mɔ́ɔ́ bí nīn cáa nyɔ́ŋkí ti-Dindaanee. 6U nìn yākatì Leefii yab akiti akiti ki nóó nì bi nín pēē pēē mmaal pu Leefii jipɔmbi Geersɔn nì Keeyaati nì Meerarii dicaŋŋinee.
7Geersɔn jipɔmbi Laadan nì Simeeyii dicaŋŋi di nìn náań Geersɔn kitil. 8Laadan nìn màl̄ mbininjabiyaamu muta ní, ujipɔŋkpil di sá Yeeyiyeel ní bin kíǹee sá Seetam nì Jooweel. 9Simeeyii mun nìn màl̄ mbininjabiyaamu muta ní. Múǹ di sá Seeloomiiti nì Asiyeel nì Aran ní ki sá Laadan yab dicaŋŋi kpilib. 10Simeeyii nìn gíti màl̄ mbininjabiyaamu munaa mubɔ mun. Múǹ di sá Yakaati nì Siisa nì Yeewusi nì Beeriya. 11Yakaati di sá ujipɔŋkpil ní Siisa pá. Yeewusi nì Beeriya bíǹ kaa màl̄ mbininjabiyaamu tikpil. Di sá ní bi dū bi-nib ki kpáfì ki tīī-bi kudicambaantiiu tundi.
12Keeyaati nìn màl̄ mbininjabiyaamu munaa. Múǹ di sá Amiiraam nì Isaar nì Eebrɔn nì Usiyeel. 13Amiiraam jipɔmbi di sá Aarɔn nì Mooyiisi. Bi nìn gāntì Aarɔn ki yóoǹ ú dū u-ba kí sú kí nīn tūǹ circir páaa laŋki tuuŋŋi kí nīn cá jaanjaan. U nì u-naantiibi tundi di sá bí nīn ŋáań talaalutuukaa saraabi ki tìì ti-Dindaan, kí nīn tūǹ Unimbɔti tundi ní kí nīn tìì binib dibiindi ti-Dindaan yindi pu. 14Mooyiisi úǹ nìn sá Unimbɔti niliu ní. Bi nìn kàan̄ u-jipɔmbi ki kútì Leefii naakookun yab poon ní. 15Mooyiisi jipɔmbi di sá Geersɔm nì Eeliyeeseer. 16Geersɔm jipɔŋkpiliu di sá Seebuyeel. 17Eeliyeeseer màl̄ kibininjabiki kibaba ja ní. Waa nìn gíti màl̄ ki kútì u-pu. Ama Reekabiya úǹ nìn màl̄ binib tikpil tikpil. 18Isaar jipɔŋkpiliu di sá Seeloomiiti. 19Eebrɔn jipɔŋkpiliu di sá Yeeriya, uliliiti di sá Amaariya, utataati di sá Yasiyeel ní unanaati sá Yeekamam. 20Usiyeel jipɔŋkpiliu di sá Miika ní uliliiti sá Isiya.
21Meerarii jipɔmbi di sá Maalii nì Musii. Maalii jipɔmbi di sá Eelasaar nì Kiisi. 22Eelasaar kaa màl̄ kibininjabiki ní ki kpíì. U màl̄ mbinimpubiyaamu ŋma ní, ní bi-niijab Kiisi jipɔmbi fātìi cáá-bi bi kpántì bi-nimpoobi. 23Musii nìn màl̄ mbininjabiyaamu muta ní. Múǹ di sá Maalii nì Eedeer nì Yeereemooti.
24Binib nee kɔkɔ nìn sá Leefii naakookun ní. Báà ŋma nìn sá u-dicaŋkun ukpil ní. Bi nìn kàan̄-bi ubɔ ubɔ ní ki ŋmàn̄ bi-yiŋŋi ki ŋá tigbɔn poon. Un yaa nìn bàn̄ abin mmuŋkuee, u nìn tūǹ ditundi ti-Dindaan diikun ní. 25Di sá yii Daafiidi nìn bí yii: «Ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu tīī u-nibul diŋuŋfil. Úǹ u-ba kíǹ ki kóò Jeerusaleem tiŋkin ní kí nīn cá jaanjaan. 26Mimmee an kaa ti cáá yii Leefii yab làá gíti túń circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nì tiwan tin kɔkɔ bi cáa tūǹ ŋu-poon ditundee.» 27An pu ní ki nóó nì Daafiidi bɔjoolkaatee, Leefii yɔu un yaa nìn bàn̄ abin mmuŋkuee, bi nìn ŋmà udaan yindi ní kí ŋá kugbɔŋun. 28Bi máaǹ kí nīn tɔ́ Aarɔn naantiibi marab ní ki nīn tūǹ ditundi ti-Dindaan diikun. Bíǹ di kpèé kunimbɔtidii ciŋŋi nì ku-dibiyaamu, ní ki ŋáań tiwan tin bi dūu sú Unimbɔtee circir, ní ki bí kunimbɔtidiin ki tūǹ ditundi. 29Bíǹ di làá nīn pūul̀ kpɔnɔb bin bi pāantí teebil pu Unimbɔti nimbiinee, kí nīn bɔ́ntí ŋyim min bi cáa ŋáań tijimpin saraabee, kí nīn pūul̀ ŋkpɔnɔbiyaamu mun poon baa ŋáań ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee nì kalaabi bin bi pūul̀ ataŋkpee puee, nì kalaabi bin kíǹee. Bíǹ di tí kpèé tiwan tin bi cáa ŋmàntī tiwan nyifiŋŋu nì ti-púuŋŋuee. 30Leefii yab máaǹ kí nīn bí kunimbɔtidiin taafaau nì joou ki gà ilan ki pàkà ti-Dindaan ki nyɔ́ŋkí-u. 31Bi máaǹ kí nīn bí ŋyunti ŋun kamaa binib yaa dɔ́miń kí ŋá bisaraawɔkaabee, nì ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa kamaa, nì uŋmal kamaa wimpeepeekaaŋu dal, nì jiŋaalib wiiŋyi kɔkɔ. Bi máaǹ kí tɔ̄ ditundi gbanti ti-Dindaan nimbiin kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaan, kí nīn wīikí kii mara nín bālifì puee. 32Míǹ ní bi làá nīn tūǹ Unimbɔti Tantiu nì dikpafindi tantiu tuuŋŋi. Bi làá nīn tútúǹ bi-nabiyaamu Aarɔn naantiibi bi tūǹ ditundi kunimbɔtidii poon.

english_text:
David Assigns the Priests Their Duties
1Aaron's descendants were then divided into work groups. Aaron had four sons: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar. 2 But Nadab and Abihu died long before their father, without having any sons. That's why Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests.
3David divided Aaron's descendants into groups, according to their assigned work. Zadok, one of Eleazar's descendants, and Ahimelech, one of Ithamar's descendants, helped David.
4Eleazar's descendants were divided into 16 groups, and Ithamar's were divided into eight groups, because Eleazar's family included more family leaders. 5However, both families included temple officials and priests, and so to make sure the work was divided fairly, David asked God what to do.
6As each group was assigned their duties, Shemaiah the son of Nethanel the Levite wrote down the name of the family leader in charge of that group. The witnesses were David and his officials, as well as Zadok the priest, Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, and the family leaders from the clans of the priests and the Levites.
7-18Each group of priests went by the name of its family leader, and they were assigned their duties in the following order: Jehoiarib, Jedaiah, Harim, Seorim, Malchijah, Mijamin, Hakkoz, Abijah, Jeshua, Shecaniah, Eliashib, Jakim, Huppah, Jeshebeab, Bilgah, Immer, Hezir, Happizzez, Pethahiah, Jehezkel, Jachin, Gamul, Delaiah, Maaziah. 19These men were assigned their duties at the temple, just as the Lord God of Israel had commanded their ancestor Aaron.
The Rest of the Levites Are Assigned Their Duties
20Here is a list of the other descendants of Levi:
Amram was the ancestor of Shubael and Jehdeiah.
21Rehabiah was the ancestor of Isshiah, the oldest son in his family.
22Izhar was the father of Shelomoth and the grandfather of Jahath.
23Hebron had four sons, in the following order: Jeriah, Amariah, Jahaziel, and Jekameam.
24Uzziel was the father of Micah and the grandfather of Shamir.
25Isshiah, Micah's brother, was the father of Zechariah.
26Merari was the father of Mahli, Mushi, and Jaaziah.
27Jaaziah had three sons: Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri. 28-29Mahli was the father of Eleazar and Kish. Eleazar had no sons, but Kish was the father of Jerahmeel. 30Mushi had three sons: Mahli, Eder, and Jerimoth.
These were the descendants of Levi, according to their clans. 31Each one was assigned his duties in the same way that their relatives the priests had been assigned their duties. David, Zadok, Ahimelech, and the family leaders of the priests and Levites were the witnesses.
translation_text:
Bisaraaŋaliibi kitiŋi
1Bi nìn yākatì Aarɔn naantiibi akiti akiti. Aarɔn jipɔmbi di sá Nadaab nì Abiyuu nì Eeleeyasaar nì Itamaar. 2Nadaab nì Abiyuu nìn péeǹ bi-baa ki kpíì kaa nìn màl̄ mbininjabiyaamu. Eeleeyasaar nì Itamaar baba di nìn kpántì bisaraaŋaliibi. 3Eeleeyasaar naantiiu Sadooki nì Itamaar naantiiu Ayiimeeleeki nìn tútúǹ Daafiidi u yākatì bisaraaŋaliibi kɔkɔ akiti akiti, ki nóó nì ditundi din bi tūǹee. 4Bi nìn dáań ki ká yii Eeleeyasaar naantiibi bininjab nìn wīikí ki jítiǹ Itamaar naantiibi yab. An pu ní bi cúú Eeleeyasaar yab ki yākatì akiti saalku nì diba, ní ki yākatì Itamaar yab akiti anii. Dikitil kamaa nìn cáá kudicaŋu kpiliu ubɔ. 5Bi nìn tɔ́ kasi ní ki yākatì yākatì akiti gbanti. Di sá yii an yaa sá Eeleeyasaar naantiibi poonaaa, Itamaar naantiibi poonaaa, «circir kɔŋkooŋŋu tɔntɔnliibi» nì «Unimbɔti tɔntɔnliibi» nìn bí ní.
6Neetaneeyeel jipɔɔn Seemaya, un sá ugbaŋŋmal Leefii naakookunee ŋmàn̄ bi-yiŋŋi ubɔti nì abɔtibil nì usaraaŋakpil Sadooki nì Abiyataar jipɔɔn Ayiimeeleeki, nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab dicaŋŋi kpilib kɔkɔ nimbiin. Bi yaa nìn tɔ́ kasi mili pu ki lēē Eeleeyasaar maaliŋun bikpilib bilee, ní bí tɔ̄ kasi diba pu kí lēē Itamaar maaliŋun kudicaŋu kpiliu ubɔ. 7Bi nín nìn tɔ́ kasee, unipeekaa un an nìn tāāyee di sá Yooyariib, ní uliliiti sá Yeedaya, 8ní utataati sá Ariim, ní unanaati sá Seewooriim, 9ní uŋmooŋmooti sá Maalkiya, ní ululuuti sá Miiniyaamiini, 10ní ululuúti sá Akoosi, ní uniniiti sá Abiiya, 11ní uwawati sá Yeesuwa, ní usaalaati sá Seekaniyawuu, 12ní saalaa nì upeekaa sá Eeliyasiib, ní saalaa nì uliliiti sá Yakiim, 13ní saalaa nì utataati sá Kuupa, ní saalaa nì unanaati sá Yeeseebaab, 14ní saalaa nì uŋmooŋmooti sá Biiliga, ní saalaa nì ululuuti sá Imeer, 15saalaa nì ululuúti sá Eesiir, ní saalaa nì uniniiti sá Apiiseesi, 16ní saalaa nì uwawati sá Peetaya, ní un pá saalaa nì uwawati sá Yeesikeel, 17ní mmuŋku nì upeekaa sá Yaakiin, ní mmuŋku nì uliliiti sá Gamuul, 18ní mmuŋku nì utataati sá Deelaya ní mmuŋku nì unanaati sá Maasiya.
19Akiti gbanti nìn nóó bi nín pá pá tɔb pu puee ní ki tūǹ ditundi ti-Dindaan Diikun. Bi nìn tūǹ ditundi niin ki nóó nì bi-naanja Aarɔn nín nìn tīī marab biŋyee ní. Úǹ nìn fōō marab gbanti ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu cee ní.
Leefii yab bin kíǹee yiŋŋi
20Leefii kpilib bin kíǹee yiŋŋi sèé.
Un nìn sá Amiiraam naantiibi poon ukpilee di sá Suubayeel, ní un sá Suubayeel naantiibi poon ukpilee di sá Yeediya. 21Un nìn sá Reekabiya naantiibi poon ukpilee di sá Isiya un sá u-dicaŋkun ujipɔŋkpilee. 22Isaar naantiibi poonee, Seeloomiiti di nìn sá ukpil, ní Seeloomiiti naantiibi poonee, Yakaati sá ukpil. 23Eebrɔn jipɔmbi sèé. Upeekaa di sá Yeeriya ní uliliiti sá Amaariya, ní utataati sá Yasiyeel ní unanaati sá Yeekamam. 24Usiyeel jipɔɔn di sá Miika. Miika naantiibi poonee, Samiir di nìn sá ukpil. 25Miika naal Isiya naantiibi poonee, Seekariyawuu di nìn sá ukpil. 26Meerarii jipɔmbi di sá Maalii nì Musii nì Yaasiyawuu. 27Meerarii naantiibi bin u-jipɔɔn Yaasiyawuu màl̄ee di sá Sooyam nì Sakuur nì Ibirii. 28Maalii jipɔmbi ubɔ di sá Eeleeyasaar. Úǹ kaa nìn màl̄ kibininjabiki. 29Uliliiti di sá Kiisi. Úǹ nìn màl̄ kibininjabiki bi yíì-kì Yeerameel. 30Musii jipɔmbi di sá Maalii nì Eedeer nì Yeereemooti.
Bininjab gbanti kɔkɔ nìn sá Leefii naakookun ní. Báà ŋma nìn sá u-dicaŋkun ukpil ní. 31Kii bi-nabiyaamu Aarɔn naantiibi nín ŋá puee, bi nìn tɔ́ kasi ní ki lēē bi nín làá nīn tūǹ ditundi ki pá pá tɔb pu puee. Ubɔti Daafiidi nì Sadooki nì Ayiimeeleeki, nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab dicaŋŋi kpilib nimbiin ní bi nìn ŋá míǹ gbanti kɔkɔ. Mimmee bi ŋá ujipɔŋkpil dicaŋku mbaantiim kii bi nín ŋá kiwaai mun dicaŋku puee dee.

english_text:
David Assigns the Temple Musicians Their Duties
1David and the temple officials chose the descendants of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun to be in charge of music. They were to praise the Lord by playing cymbals, harps and other stringed instruments. Here is a list of the musicians and their duties:
2Asaph's four sons, Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asarelah, were under the direction of their father and played music whenever the king told them to.
3Jeduthun's six sons, Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Shimei, Hashabiah, and Mattithiah, were under the direction of their father and played harps and sang praises to the Lord.
4Heman had 14 sons: Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, Romamtiezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, Mahazioth. 5Heman was one of the king's prophets, and God honored Heman by giving him 14 sons and 3 daughters. 6His sons were under his direction and played cymbals, harps, and other stringed instruments during times of worship at the temple.
Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman took their orders directly from the king.
7There were 288 of these men, and all of them were skilled musicians. 8David assigned them their duties by asking the Lord what he wanted. Everyone was responsible for something, whether young or old, teacher or student.
9-31The musicians were divided into 24 groups of twelve, and each group went by the name of their family leader. They were assigned their duties in the following order: Joseph, Gedaliah, Zaccur, Zeri, Nethaniah, Bukkiah, Asarelah, Jeshaiah, Mattaniah, Shimei, Uzziel, Hashabiah, Shebuel, Mattithiah, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Joshbekashah, Hanani, Mallothi, Eliathah, Hothir, Giddalti, Mahazioth, and Romamtiezer.
translation_text:
Bilaŋgaaliibi kitiŋi
1Akiti ŋin tūǹ ditundi ti-Dindaan Diikunee kpilib nìn tútúǹ Daafiidi bi gāntì Asaafi nì Eeman nì Yeedutun naantiibi bí nīn kpèé dilaŋgaal tundi. Bi nìn bɔ̀ɔ́ tibati nì saŋgub, ki cákafí cancakantib ní ki gà ilan ki nàatī binib Unimbɔti bɔti. Binib bin tūǹ ditundi gbantee yiŋŋi sèé. 2Asaafi jipɔmbi di sá Sakuur nì Jooseefi nì Neetaniya nì Asaareela. Bi-baa un nìn gà ilan ki nàatī Unimbɔti bɔtee di nìn kpòotī-bi kii ubɔti nín tīī mara puee. 3Yeedutun jipɔmbi di sá Geedaliyawuu nì Seerii nì Yeesaya nì Simeeyii nì Aseebiyawuu nì Mataatiyawuu. Bi-baa un nìn cáá kubeeu ki gà ilan ki nyɔ́ŋkí ki pàkà ti-Dindaanee di nìn kpòotī bi-luutil.
4Eeman jipɔmbi di sá Buukiyawuu nì Mataatiyawuu nì Usiyeel nì Seebuyeel nì Yeereemooti nì Ananiya nì Ananii nì Eeliyata nì Giidalitii nì Roomamitii-Eeseer nì Yoosbeekasaa nì Malootii nì Ootiir nì Maasiyooti. 5Bin bí nee kɔkɔ sá Eeman un wāĺ ki nàatī ubɔti Unimbɔti bɔtee jipɔmbi ní. U nìn nāatì Daafiidi tin Unimbɔti sòon̄ kí mɔ̀tīí kūtì-u mpɔnee. Unimbɔti nìn pú Eeman mbininjabiyaamu kiba kpá saalku nì nnimpubiyaamu muta ní.
6Binib gbanti kɔkɔ nìn bí bi-baa taapu ní ki tūǹ ditundi ti-Dindaan diikun. Bi nìn cákafí cancakantib, ní ki bɔ̀ɔ́ saŋgub nì tibati. Bi nìn bí ubɔti tundin ní Asaafi nì Yeedutun nì Eeman kpòotī-bi. 7Bilaŋgaaliibi gbanti nì bi-kitiŋi yab bin bi nìn bífì bí nīn gà ilan ki nyɔ́ŋkí ti-Dindaanee nìn nyáń binib alaataa ali nì imuŋku inaa nì binib binii ní. Bi nìn bífì dilaŋgaal tundi tiŋan.
8Bi nìn tɔ́ kasi ní ki lēē bi nín làá nīn tūǹ ditundi ki fòol̄ tɔb puee. Digàntil kaa nìn bí kiwaayaaa, ukpil kansikin, àá un bífì ki nyí dilaŋgaal tiŋanee nì un dáá bíi bífée kansikin.
9Bi nín tɔ́ kasee, ukpipeepeekaa un an tāāyee di sá Asafi jipɔɔn Jooseefi.
Unililiiti di sá Geedaliyawuu, u nì u-jipɔmbi nì u-nabiyaamu binib saalaa nì bili.
10Utataati di sá Sakuur, u nì u-jipɔmbi nì u-nabiyaamu binib saalaa nì bili.
11Unanaati di sá Yiseerii, u nì u-jipɔmbi nì u-nabiyaamu binib saalaa nì bili.
12Uŋmooŋmooti di sá Neetaniyawuu, u nì u-jipɔmbi nì u-nabiyaamu binib saalaa nì bili.
13Ululuuti di sá Bukiyawuu, u nì u-jipɔmbi nì u-nabiyaamu binib saalaa nì bili.
14Ululuúti di sá Yeesareela, u nì u-jipɔmbi nì u-nabiyaamu binib saalaa nì bili.
15Uniniiti di sá Yeesaya, u nì u-jipɔmbi nì u-nabiyaamu binib saalaa nì bili.
16Uwawati di sá Mataniyawuu, u nì u-jipɔmbi nì u-nabiyaamu binib saalaa nì bili.
17Usaalaati di sá Simeeyii, u nì u-jipɔmbi nì u-nabiyaamu binib saalaa nì bili.
18Saalaa nì upeekaa di sá Asareeyeel, u nì u-jipɔmbi nì u-nabiyaamu binib saalaa nì bili.
19Saalaa nì uliliiti di sá Asafiya, u nì u-jipɔmbi nì u-nabiyaamu binib saalaa nì bili.
20Saalaa nì utataati di sá Subayeel, u nì u-jipɔmbi nì u-nabiyaamu binib saalaa nì bili.
21Saalaa nì unanaati di sá Maatitiyawuu, u nì u-jipɔmbi nì u-nabiyaamu binib saalaa nì bili.
22Saalaa nì uŋmooŋmooti di sá Yeereemooti, u nì u-jipɔmbi nì u-nabiyaamu binib saalaa nì bili.
23Saalaa nì ululuuti di sá Ananiyawuu, u nì u-jipɔmbi nì u-nabiyaamu binib saalaa nì bili.
24Saalaa nì ululuúti di sá Yoosbeekasaa, u nì u-jipɔmbi nì u-nabiyaamu binib saalaa nì bili.
25Saalaa uniniiti di sá Ananii, u nì u-jipɔmbi nì u-nabiyaamu binib saalaa nì bili.
26Saalaa nì uwawati di sá Malootii, u nì u-jipɔmbi nì u-nabiyaamu binib saalaa nì bili.
27Un pá saalaa nì uwawati puee di sá Eeliyata, u nì u-jipɔmbi nì u-nabiyaamu binib saalaa nì bili.
28Mmuŋku nì upeekaa di sá Ootiir, u nì u-jipɔmbi nì u-nabiyaamu binib saalaa nì bili.
29Mmuŋku nì uliliiti di sá Giidalitii, u nì u-jipɔmbi nì u-nabiyaamu binib saalaa nì bili.
30Mmuŋku nì utataati di sá Maasiyooti, u nì u-jipɔmbi nì u-nabiyaamu binib saalaa nì bili.
31Mmuŋku nì unanaati di sá Roomamitii-Eeseer, u nì u-jipɔmbi nì u-nabiyaamu binib saalaa nì bili.

english_text:
The Temple Guards Are Assigned Their Duties
1The temple guards were also divided into groups according to clans.
Meshelemiah son of Kore was from the Korah clan and was a descendant of Asaph. 2He had seven sons, who were born in the following order: Zechariah, Jediael, Zebadiah, Jathniel, 3Elam, Jehohanan, and Eliehoenai.
4-5 Obed-Edom had been blessed with eight sons: Shemaiah, Jehozabad, Joah, Sachar, Nethanel, Ammiel, Issachar, and Peullethai.
6-7Shemaiah was the father of Othni, Rephael, Obed, Elzabad, Elihu, and Semachiah. They were all respected leaders in their clan. 8There were 62 descendants of Obed-Edom who were strong enough to be guards at the temple.
9Eighteen descendants of Meshelemiah were chosen for this work.
10-11Hosah, from the Merari clan, was the father of Shimri, Hilkiah, Tebaliah, and Zechariah. Hosah had made Shimri the family leader, even though he was not the oldest son. Thirteen men from Hosah's family were chosen to be temple guards.
12The guards were divided into groups, according to their family leaders, and they were assigned duties at the temple, just like the other Levites. 13Each group, no matter how large or small, was assigned a gate to guard, and they let the Lord show them what he wanted done.
14Shelemiah was chosen to guard the East Gate. Zechariah his son was a wise man and was chosen to guard the North Gate. 15Obed-Edom was then chosen to guard the South Gate, and his sons were chosen to guard the storerooms. 16Shuppim and Hosah were chosen to guard the West Gate and the Shallecheth Gate on the upper road.
The guards were assigned the following work schedule: 17Each day six guards were on duty on the east side of the temple, four were on duty on the north side, and four were on duty on the south side. Two guards were stationed at each of the two storerooms, 18four were stationed along the road leading to the west courtyard, and two guards stayed in the court itself.
19These were the guard duties assigned to the men from the clans of Korah and Merari.
Guards Are Assigned to the Treasury
20The Levites who were relatives of the Korahites and the Merarites were in charge of guarding the temple treasury and the gifts that had been dedicated to God.
21Ladan was from the Gershon clan and was the father of Jehieli. Many of his other descendants were family leaders in the clan. 22Jehieli was the father of Zetham and Joel, and they were responsible for guarding the treasury.
23Other guards at the treasury were from the Kohathite clans of Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
24Shebuel was a descendant of Gershom the son of Moses. He was the chief official in charge of the temple treasury. 25The descendants of Gershom's brother Eliezer included Rehabiah, Jeshaiah, Joram, Zichri, and Shelomoth.
26Shelomoth and his relatives were in charge of all the gifts that were dedicated to the Lord. These included the gifts that King David had dedicated, as well as those dedicated by the family leaders, army officers, and army commanders. 27And whenever valuable things were captured in battle, these men brought back some of them to make repairs to the temple. 28Shelomoth and his relatives were responsible for any gifts that had been given to the temple, including those from Samuel the prophet, King Saul the son of Kish, Abner the son of Ner, and Joab the son of Zeruiah.
Other Officers Are Assigned Their Duties
29Chenaniah from the Izhar clan and his sons were government officials and judges. They did not work at the temple.
30Hashabiah from the Hebron clan and 1,700 of his skilled relatives were the officials in charge of all religious and government business in the Israelite territories west of the Jordan River.
31-32Jerijah was the leader of the Hebron clan. David assigned him and 2,700 of his relatives, who were all respected family leaders, to be the officials in charge of all religious and government business in the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh. David found out about these men during the fortieth year of his rule, when he had a list made of all the families in the Hebron clan. They were from the town of Jazer in the territory of Gilead.
translation_text:
Bipunyɔɔciitiliibi kitiŋi
1Bi nìn yākatì bipunyɔɔciitiliibi mun akiti akiti ní. Kooree jipɔɔn Meeseeleemiyawuu, Asaafi naantiiu un sá Kooree maaliŋunee 2nìn màl̄ mbininjabiyaamu. U nín màl̄-mu mu pá pá tɔb pu puee yiŋŋi sèé: Seekariyawuu nì Yeediyeel nì Seebadiyawuu nì Yatiniyeel, 3Eelam nì Yeewoowanan Eeliyooweenayi.
4Oobeedi-Eedoom nìn màl̄ mbininjabiyaamu munii ní. Mu nín pá pá tɔb pu puee sèé: Seemaya nì Yoosabaadi nì Yoowa nì Sakaar nì Neetaneeyeel, 5nì Amiyeel nì Isakaar nì Peewuleetaayi. Tiŋman, ti-Dindaan nìn lafun bīiǹ Oobeedi-Eedoom boon.
6U-jipɔŋkpiliu Seemaya nìn màl̄ mbininjabiyaamu. Bi nìn cáá mpɔn bi-baa dicaŋkun, di sá yii bi-kɔkɔ nìn sá bibaatandambi ní. 7Seemaya jipɔmbi di sá Ɔtinii nì Reefayeel nì Oobeedi nì Eelsabaadi, ní kí kūtì bi-nabiyaamu Eeliiwuu nì Seemakiya. Bíǹ liitil nìn sá bibaatandambi ní. 8Oobeedi-Eedoom jipɔmbi nee nì bíǹ bi-ba jipɔmbi nì bi-nabiyaamu kɔkɔ nìn sá bibaatandambi, ní ki cáá difaŋgiil bi-tundi poon. Bi-kɔkɔ nìn nyáń binib imuŋku ita nì binib bili ní.
9Meeseeleemiyawuu nìn cáá jipɔmbi nì nnabiyaamu, bi nìn nyáń bibaatandambi saalku nì bita ní.
10Koosa un sá Meerarii maaliŋunee nìn cáá jipɔmbi binaa ní. Simrii di nìn jíń tikpiti kudicaŋu poon. Waa nìn sá ujipɔŋkpil, ama ní u-baa dū tikpiti ki tīī-u. 11Koosa jipɔnliliitiu di sá Ilikiyawuu, ní utataati sá Teebaaliyawuu ní unanaati sá Seekariyawuu. Koosa jipɔmbi nì u-nabiyaamu kɔkɔ nìn nyáń binib saalaa nì bita ní.
12Bipunyɔɔciitiliibi kitiŋi nee kpilib nì bi-yab nìn tūǹ bi-tundi dicilpu ti-Dindaan Diikun ní. 13Binipɔmbaaa, binicikitikaabaaa, bi nìn tɔ́ kasi ní ki yākatì mpunyɔmu mun bi làá nīn cīitée ki nóó nì bi-dicaŋŋi.
14Bi nín tɔ́ kasee, an nyáń yii Seeleemiyawuu di làá nīn cīití kipunyɔkɔ kin bí ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee. Bi gíti tɔ́ee ní an nyáń yii u-jipɔɔn Seekariyawuu un sá usaŋkimɔntee di làá nīn cīití kipunyɔkɔ kin bí ŋgan púee. 15Oobeedi-Eedoom di làá nīn cīití kipunyɔkɔ kin bí ŋgiil púee, ní u-jipɔmbi ń nīn cīití adiin ŋin poon bi yōontí tijikaalee. 16Supiim nì Koosa di làá nīn cīití kipunyɔkɔ kin bí ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki púee nì Saleekeeti punyɔkɔki kin bí yilpu dandi púee. Bi nín làá nīn cīití ki fòol̄ tɔb puee sèé. 17Ŋwiinee, Leefii yab binib biluu di làá nīn cīití ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú punyɔkɔki, ní binib binaa ń nīn cīití ŋgan pú yaka, ní binib binaa ń nīn cīití ŋgiil pú punyɔkɔki, ní akiti ali ń nīn cīití adiin ŋin poon bi yōontí tijikaalee, dikitil kamaa cáá binib bili bili. 18Kudii kun bí ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki púee, binib binaa làá nīn yú didandi pu ki cí ní bili ń nīn bí kudiin.
19Bipunyɔɔciitiliibi kitiŋi ŋin bi nìn lēē Kooree nì Meerarii maalii poonee dee.
Bi dū atuun aba ki ŋúbiǹ Leefii yab biba
20Leefii yab biba mun nìn sá bin kpèé kunimbɔtidii gaajawanti nì tiwan tin bi cáań ki ŋá Unimbɔti saraayee. 21Laadan naantiibi bin sá Geersɔn maaliŋunee nì bi-dicaŋŋi kpilib di sá Yeeyeelii, 22nì Yeeyeelii jipɔmbi nì Seetam nì u-naal Jooweel. Bíǹ di nìn kpèé ti-Dindaan Diiku gaajawanti. 23Amiiraam nì Isaar nì Eebrɔn nì Usiyeel maaliŋunee, 24Mooyiisi jipɔɔn, Geersɔm naantiiu Seebuyeel di sá ukpikpaan un kpèé tigaajawan kɔkɔee. 25U-nabiyaamu kansikinee, Geersɔm maan Eeliyeeseer naantiibi nìn bí. Bíǹ di sá Eeliyeeseer jipɔɔn Reekabiya nì Yeesaya nì Yooram nì Sikirii nì Seeloomiiti. 26Seeloomiiti gbanti nì u-nabiyaamu di nìn kpèé tigaajawan tin kɔkɔ ubɔti Daafiidi nì adican kpilib nì bijanjakpilib bin kpòotī bijanjaliibi kutuku kutukuee nì bin kpòotī bijanjaliibi dilaataal dilaataalee nì bijanjakpilib bin kíǹee nìn dūu sú Unimbɔtee. 27Binib gbanti nìn lēē tiwan tin bi jáń kujaau ki fōōyee tiba ki dūu sú Unimbɔti bí nīn cáa ŋáŋkí ti-Dindaan Diiku. 28Seeloomiiti nì u-nabiyaamu ní bi nìn dū tiwan tin kɔkɔ Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Samiyeel, nì Kiisi jipɔɔn Saayuul, nì Neer jipɔɔn Abineer, nì Joowaab un na bi yíì Seeruyee nìn dūu sú Unimbɔtee ki ŋúbíǹ bí nīn kpèé.
29Keenaniyawuu nì u-jipɔmbi bin sá Isaar maaliŋunee di nìn kpèé Isirayeel tiŋki kɔkɔn tin kaa sá tinimbɔtibɔtee bɔti. Bíǹ di nìn kpèé akàlintuun bɔti, ní ki sá bibɔsoonliibi mun. 30Eebrɔn maaliŋunee, Asabiya nì u-nabiyaamu bibaatandambi binib kutuku ubɔ nì alaataa aluli di nìn kpèé Isirayeel tiŋki dijandi din bí Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki púee. Bíǹ di nìn kpèé dinimbɔtinool nì akàlintuun bɔti. 31Yeeriya di nìn sá Eebrɔn maaliŋun yab kpiliu. Daafiidi nín kāl̀ dibeel abin imuŋku ili poonee, ní u yāntì bi nyàab̄ mmaal gbanti nib nì bi-dicaŋŋi nyeeŋu, ní ki ká yii bi-kansikin biba bí Yeeseer, Galaadi tiŋkin, ki sá bibaatandambi. 32Ubɔti Daafiidi nìn gíti lēē bibaatandambi bin sá mmaal gbantin ki sá adican kpilibee binib kutukub bili nì alaataa aluli ki kútì Yeeriya pu. Bíǹ di làá nīn kpèé dinimbɔtinool nì akàlintuun bɔti ntimu mun poon ní Rubeen nì Gaadi naakɔti, nì Manasee naakooku dijandi diba yab kóòyee.

Bijanjaliibi kitiŋi
1Isirayeel yab bin bí ubɔti tundinee sɔ̀. Adican kpilib nì bijanjakpilib bin kpòotī binib kutuku kutukuee nì bin kpòotī binib dilaataal dilaataalee nì bikàliŋkpilib. Bíǹ di nìn kpèé ajanjakiti ŋin nìn bí ditundinee, di sá yii dijanjakitil kamaa nìn cáá dibindi poonee uŋmal ubɔ ní kí tɔ̄ ditundi. Dijanjakitil kamaa poonee, binib kutukub mmuŋku nì binaa di nìn bí. 2Dijanjakitipeekaal din nìn yì ditundi uŋmapeepeekaa poonee kpiliu di sá Sabidiyeel jipɔɔn Yasoobaam. U-janjakitil poonee, binib kutukub mmuŋku nì binaa di nìn bí. 3U nìn sá Peereesi maaliŋun ní ki nìn kpèé ajanjakiti kpilib bin cáá kí tɔ̄ ditundi uŋmapeepeekaa poonee. 4Dikitil din nìn yì kí tɔ̄ ditundi uŋmaliliiti poonee kpiliu di sá uakooliija Doodayii. Miikilooti di nìn kpòotī dijanjakitil gbanti ní di nìn cáá binib kutuku mmuŋku nì binaa. 5Dijanjakitil ditataatiil din nìn yì kí tɔ̄ ditundi uŋmatataati poonee kpiliu di nìn sá usaraaŋakpil Yooyadaa jipɔɔn Beenayawuu. U-janjakitil nìn cáá binib kutukub mmuŋku nì binaa ní. 6Beenayawuu gbanti nìn kútì Bibaatandambi Mmuŋku nì Saalaa kitil pu ní ki nìn sá di-kpiliu. U-janjakitil poonee u-jipɔɔn Amiisafaadi nìn bí. 7Dijanjakitil dinanaatiil din nìn yì kí tɔ̄ ditundi uŋmananaati poonee kpilib di nìn sá Joowaab naal Asayeel nì u-jipɔɔn Seefadiya. Bi-janjakitil nìn cáá binib kutukub mmuŋku nì binaa ní. 8Dijanjakitil diŋmooŋmootiil din nìn yì kí tɔ̄ ditundi uŋmaŋmooŋmooti poonee kpiliu di nìn sá uiseerayiitija Sameekuuti. U-janjakitil nìn cáá binib kutukub mmuŋku nì binaa ní. 9Dijanjakitil diluluutiil din nìn yì kí tɔ̄ ditundi uŋmaluluuti poonee kpiliu di sá uteekooyiija Yiira, Ikeesi jipɔɔn. U-janjakitil nìn cáá binib kutukub mmuŋku nì binaa ní. 10Dijanjakitil diluluútiil din nìn yì kí tɔ̄ ditundi uŋmaluluúti poonee kpiliu di sá upeelooniija Eeleesi, Eefiraayiim naantiibi kansikin ubɔ. U-janjakitil nìn cáá binib kutukub mmuŋku nì binaa ní. 11Dijanjakitil dininiitiil din nìn yì kí tɔ̄ ditundi uŋmaniniiti poonee kpiliu di sá ukusatiija Sibeekayii, Saarkii maaliŋun ubɔ. U-janjakitil nìn cáá binib kutukub mmuŋku nì binaa ní. 12Dijanjakitil diwawaatiil din nìn yì kí tɔ̄ ditundi uŋmawawati poonee kpiliu di nìn sá uanatootija Afiyeeseer, Beenjameen naakookun yɔu ubɔ. U-janjakitil nìn cáá binib kutukub mmuŋku nì binaa ní. 13Dijanjakitil disaalaatiil din nìn yì kí tɔ̄ ditundi uŋmasaalaati poonee kpiliu di sá uneetoofatiija Maarayii, Saarkii maaliŋun ubɔ. U-janjakitil nìn cáá binib kutukub mmuŋku nì binaa ní. 14Dijanjakitil saalaa nì dipeepeekaal din nìn yì kí tɔ̄ ditundi uŋmal saalaa nì upeepeekaa poonee kpiliu di sá upiiratooniija Beenaya, Eefiraayiim naakookun yɔu ubɔ. U-janjakitil nìn cáá binib kutukub mmuŋku nì binaa ní. 15Dijanjakitil saalaa nì dililiitiil din nìn yì kí tɔ̄ ditundi uŋmal saalaa nì uliliiti poonee kpiliu di nìn sá uneetoofatiija Eeldayii, Ootiniyeel maaliŋun ubɔ. U-janjakitil nìn cáá binib kutukub mmuŋku nì binaa ní.
Isirayeel yab naakɔti kpilib yiŋŋi
16Isirayeel yab naakɔti kpilib yiŋŋi sɔ̀.
Rubeen naakookunee, Sikirii jipɔɔn Eeliyeeseer di sá ukpil.
Simeeyɔn naakookunee, Maaka jipɔɔn Seefatiyawuu di sá ukpil.
17Leefii naakookunee, Keemuyeel jipɔɔn Asabiya di sá ukpil.
Aarɔn dicaŋkunee, Sadooki di sá ukpil.
18Juuda naakookunee, Eeliiwuu un sá Daafiidi maanee di sá ukpil.
Isakaar naakookunee, Miikayeel jipɔɔn Oomirii di sá ukpil.
19Sabulɔn naakookunee, Oobadiya jipɔɔn Isimaya di sá ukpil.
Neefitalii naakookunee, Asiriyeel jipɔɔn Yeereemooti di sá ukpil.
20Eefiraayiim naakookunee, Asasiyawuu jipɔɔn Ooseeya di sá ukpil.
Manasee naakooku dijandi din bí Jɔɔdan buŋŋu ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki púee, Peedaya jipɔɔn Jooweel di sá ukpil.
21Manasee naakooku dijandi din kóòń Galaadi tiŋkinee, Seekariyawuu jipɔɔn Idoo di sá ukpil.
Beenjameen naakookunee, Abineer jipɔɔn Yasiyeel di sá ukpil.
22Daani naakookunee, Yeeroowaam jipɔɔn Asareeyeel di sá ukpil.
Isirayeel naakɔti kpilib dee.
23Daafiidi kaa nìn yāntì bi kàan̄ binipɔmbi bin cáá abin mmuŋku kí nīn cáa sìntēe. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan nìn lī yii u làá yàntī Isirayeel yab ń bùtī kii iŋmalbijaa in bí kutaa puee ní. 24Seeruya jipɔɔn Joowaab nìn kíĺ ki bíi kàaǹ Isirayeel yab, ama waa nìn púntì. Unimbɔti nìn gíí Isirayeel yab pu diŋuul dikàandi gbanti pu. An pu ní Isirayeel nibul kɔkɔ nyɔkɔm kaa ŋmàn̄ ki kā Daafiidi Tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun.
Binib bin kpèé ubɔti gaajawantee
25Adiyeel jipɔɔn Asimafeeti di nìn sá un kpèé ubɔti gaajawantee.
Oosiyasi jipɔɔn Yoowanan di nìn kpèé tikpaajin tin bi kpáafì ntiŋkpaamun nì ntimbilimun nì laakin sintil difɔkɔŋi bée.
26Keeluub jipɔɔn Eesirii di nìn sá bikpaabi kpiliu Isirayeel tiŋki kɔkɔn.
27Simeeyii un sá Raama tiŋkinee di nìn kpèé fiinyi sufii kpaaŋŋi kɔkɔ.
Sabidii un sá Seefam tiŋkinee di nìn kpèé ndamam min nyánní akpaan gbantin bi cāabìń ki kpáafée.
28Baal-Anan un sá Beeti-Geedeer tiŋkinee di nìn kpèé ɔliifi sufii nì siikoomɔɔr sufii kpaaŋŋi ŋin bí Seefeelaayee.
Yoowasi di nìn kpèé ŋkpam min bi cāabìń ki kpáafée.
29Siitirayi un sá Saarɔn tiŋkinee di nìn kpèé tinacaŋkpun tin bi kpàá Saarɔn naakpaapɔɔkunee.
Adilayi jipɔɔn Safaati di nìn kpèé tinacaŋkpun tin bi kpàá ditantakalinee.
30Ɔbiil un sá Isimaayeel maaliŋunee di nìn kpèé igutaamu.
Yeediya un sá Meerɔnɔti tiŋkinee di nìn kpèé mmansalimu.
31Yasiisi un sá Agaar maaliŋunee di nìn kpèé ipii nì iŋoobu.
Binib bin nìn kpèé ubɔti Daafiidi gaajawantee dee.
Binib bin pìlīǹ ubɔti Daafiidee
32Daafiidi wee Joonatan nìn sá unyil ki ŋá sukul. Úǹ di nìn sá ubɔti saŋkiliu. Yeeyeel un baa nìn sá Akimoonii tiŋkee di nìn kpèé ubɔti jipɔmbi. 33Ubɔti saŋkiliu ubɔ mun di sá Ayiitoofeel. Usayii un sá Arkii maaliŋunee di nìn sá ubɔti bɔɔ un u cáá u-poon bɔti ki tùkùee. 34Ayiitoofeel kúm boonee, Beenayawuu jipɔɔn Yooyadaa nì Abiyataar di nìn fōō u-yil. Joowaab di nìn sá ubɔti janjakitil kpiliu.

english_text:
David Gives Solomon the Plans for the Temple
1David called a meeting in Jerusalem for all of Israel's leaders, including the tribal leaders, the government officials, the army commanders, the officials in charge of the royal property and livestock, the palace officials, and the brave warriors.
2 After everyone was there, David stood up and said:
Listen to me, my people. I wanted to build a place where the sacred chest would be kept, so we could go there and worship the Lord our God. I have prepared all the supplies for building a temple, 3but the Lord has refused to let me build it, because he said I have killed too many people in battle.
4The Lord God chose Judah to be the leading tribe in Israel. Then from Judah, he chose my father's family, and from that family, he chose me to be the king of Israel, and he promised that my descendants will also rule as kings. 5The Lord has blessed me with many sons, but he chose my son Solomon to be the next king of Israel. 6The Lord said to me, “Your son Solomon will build my temple, and it will honor me. Solomon will be like a son to me, and I will be like a father to him. 7If he continues to obey my laws and commands, his kingdom will never end.”
8My friends, you are the Lord's people. And now, with God as your witness, I want you to promise that you will do your best to obey everything the Lord God has commanded us. Then this land will always belong to you and your descendants.
9Solomon, my son, worship God and obey him with all your heart and mind, just as I have done. He knows all your thoughts and your reasons for doing things, and so if you turn to him, he will hear your prayers. But if you ignore him, he will reject you forever. 10The Lord has chosen you to build a temple for worshiping him. Be confident and do the work you have been assigned.
11After David finished speaking, he gave Solomon the plans for building the main rooms of the temple, including the porch, the storerooms, the rooms upstairs and downstairs, as well as the most holy place. 12He gave Solomon his plans for the courtyards and the open areas around the temple, and for the rooms to store the temple treasures and gifts that had been dedicated to God.
13David also gave Solomon his plans for dividing the priests and the Levites into groups, as well as for the work that needed to be done at the temple and for taking care of the objects used for worship. 14He told Solomon how much gold and silver was to be used in making the sacred objects, 15including the lampstands and lamps, 16the gold table which held the sacred loaves of bread, the tables made of silver, 17the meat forks, the bowls and cups, 18the gold incense altar, and the gold statue of a chariot for the winged creatures which were on the lid of the sacred chest.
19David then said to Solomon:
The Lord showed me how his temple is to be built. 20But you must see that everything is done according to these plans. Be confident, and never be afraid of anything or get discouraged. The Lord my God will help you do everything needed to finish the temple, so it can be used for worshiping him. 21The priests and Levites have been assigned their duties, and all the skilled workers are prepared to do their work. The people and their leaders will do anything you tell them.
translation_text:
Daafiidi lēē Saloomɔn ú fōō u-yil kí mā kunimbɔtidii
1Daafiidi nìn yíiń Isirayeel yab kpilib kɔkɔ ki kpáfì Jeerusaleem tiŋkin. U nìn yíiń tinaakɔti kpilib nì ajanjakiti kpilib bin bí u-tundinee, nì bijanjakpilib bin sá bijanjaliibi kutuku kutuku nì dilaataal dilaataal kpilibee. U nìn gíti kpáfì bikàlimbi bin kpèé ubɔti nì u-jipɔmbi gaajawanti nì bi-waŋkutee, nì bifaabi nì bibaatandambi nì binikpaambi kɔkɔ. 2Ubɔti Daafiidi nìn yíkì ní ki bí-bi yii: «M-nibul yab, m-nabiyaamu, pīlifìmaan-mi! M nìn ká nlandɔkɔ yii m làá mā kudii kun poon ní ti-Dindaan poondi dakaau làá nīn yúee, laakin ti-Nimbɔtiu taaŋi làá nīn yūlifée. An puee m bɔ́ntì kí mā kudii gbanti. 3Ama ní Unimbɔti bí-mi yii: <Sii di kaa làá mā-mi kudii kun poon binib làá nīn dòoń ki jáaḿ-mee. Di sá yii a jáń tijáti tikpil ki yāntì binib tikpil fatikuu nyáń.> 4Nì míǹ kɔkɔee man ní ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu lēē m-baa dicaŋku kɔkɔ poon. U lēē man nì m-jipɔmbi nì m-naantiibi tí jī dibeel Isirayeel tiŋki pu kí nīn cá jaanjaan. Dooooyee m-naanja Juuda ní u nìn lēē ú nīn sá uyidaan. Míǹ boonee, Juuda naakookunee ní u lēē m-baa dicaŋku. An dāa kúntèe, man ní u lēē m-baa jipɔmbi kansikin ḿ nīn sá Isirayeel tiŋki kɔkɔ pu ubɔti. 5Mbininjabiyaamu kupaau mun ti-Dindaan tīī-mee kansikinee, Saloomɔn ní u lēē yii ú kàl̄ úǹ ti-Dindaan beel Isirayeel pu tibɔtiil. 6Ti-Dindaan tùkū-mi yii: <A-jipɔɔn Saloomɔn di làá mā m-Diiku nì ku-ciŋŋi. Tiŋman úǹ ní m lēē. U làá nīn sá-mi ujipɔnti ní man ń nīn sá-u ubaati. 7U yaa gbíntìi nìkì ki tɔ́ m-marab nì m-bɔkpaaŋi kii díǹ neeyee, m làá yàntī u-beel ń báań inyaan kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaan.> 8Kɔŋkɔnnee m-nabiyaamu, ti-Dindaan nibul Isirayeel kɔkɔ nimbiinee, nì ti-Nimbɔtiu un gbìl̀ tin ti bíi sòoǹee nimbiinee, ní lēē kí bīfì ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu marab kɔkɔ kí nīn tɔ́-bi. Ni yaa ŋá mimmee, ni làá nīn pée gbíntìi yì kitimmɔntii kin pu ni kā nee, ní kí dāá dū-kì kí tīī ni-naantiibi án nīn sá bi-tindaŋwanti kí nīn cá jaanjaan. 9Sii m-jipɔɔn Saloomɔn, nyàab̀ kí béé man a-baa Nimbɔtiu un m jáaḿee tiŋan, kí nīn jáaḿ-u nì dipɔbil diba nì a-naŋki kɔkɔ. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan kpèé ki wāĺ tin bí binib pɔbiliŋ poon poon kábuee ní ki nyí bi nín dàkafī puee kɔkɔ. A yaa nyàab̀-u, u làá yàntī á ká-u. Ama a yaa dū-u ki fá, u mun làá dū-si kí fá ní kí nīn cá jaanjaan. 10Kɔŋkɔnnee sii a-ba wāĺ, sii ní ti-Dindaan lēē yii á mā-u kudii kun làá nīn sá u-circir kɔŋkooŋŋuee. An puee, ká dipɔbil kí kíĺ ditundi gbanti!»
Daafiidi tùkū Saloomɔn kunimbɔtidii nín làá nīn bí puee
11Daafiidi nìn tīī u-jipɔɔn Saloomɔn kugbɔŋu kun poon bi lēē kunimbɔtidii dikpaaŋku nì ku-dibiyaamu, nì adiin ŋin poon bi kpáafí tiwanee nì aditɔntɔkɔ nì poon pú diiŋŋi nì circir dakaau diiku. 12Daafiidi gíti tīī Saloomɔn kugbɔŋu kun poon ní bi lēē tin kɔkɔ u dākafì kí mā kí kūtèe, an dàkà yii kunimbɔtidii ciŋŋi nì adiin ŋin māntìi tú-ŋee, nì adiin ŋin poon bi làá nīn kpáafí kunimbɔtidii gaajawanti nì tiwan tin bi dūu sú Unimbɔtee. 13U nìn dū bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab kitiŋi yiŋŋi gbɔŋku ki tīī-u, ki kpáaǹ bi nín máaǹ kí nīn tūǹ atuun ŋin ti-Dindaan Diikunee. U nìn gíti dū kugbɔŋu kun poon bi ŋmàn̄ tiwan tin kɔkɔ bi làá nīn cáa tūǹ kunimbɔtidiin tuuŋŋee ki ŋée ki tīī-u. 14U nìn dàkā-u sindaariya nyiŋfiŋu ŋun bi làá dūú mɔ́ɔ́ sindaariya wanti kamaayee, ní ki dàkā-u animbil kúti nyiŋfiŋu ŋun bi làá dūú mɔ́ɔ́ animbil kúti wanti kamaayee, ki nóó nì atuun ŋin bi làá nīn cáá tiwan gbanti ki tūǹee. 15U nìn dàkā-u sindaariya fitilab nì bi-tɔkɔŋkaati nyiŋfiŋu, ki dàkā-u animbil kúti fitilab nì bi-tɔkɔŋkaati nyiŋfiŋu ki nóó nì atuun ŋin bi làá nīn cáá fitilab tɔ́kɔŋkaati kamaa ki tūǹee. 16U nìn dàkā-u sindaariya teebilib bin pu bi làá nīn pāantí kpɔnɔb bin bi dūu ŋá Unimbɔti saraayee nyiŋfiŋu, ki dàkā-u animbil kúti teebilib nyiŋfiŋu, 17nì njiimu mun bi cáa sàatī ki bàantí tinanee nyiŋfiŋu. U nìn dàkā-u fatiku sambiyaamu nì sindaariyamɔnti sambiyaamu nyiŋfiŋu, nì sindaariya sambiyaamu nì animbil kúti sambiyaamu nyiŋfiŋu. 18U nìn dàkā-u sindaariyamɔnti saraafaŋŋu ŋun pu bi làá nīn tùutī talaalubee nyiŋfiŋu. Míǹ boonee ní Daafiidi dàkā-u min bi máaǹ kí mɔ́ɔ́ circir janjatɔrɔkuuee, nì keerubimbi bin bi dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ bi kpátì bi-feeŋyi ki bīiǹ ti-Dindaan Poondi Dakaau puee nyiŋfiŋu.
19Niinee ní Daafiidi bí yii: «Tin bí nee kɔkɔ ŋmàn̄ ki kā kugbɔŋu kun ti-Dindaan tīī-mee poon. Kugbɔŋu gbanti poon ní bi nín máaǹ kí tɔ̄ kunimbɔtidii tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ puee ŋmàn̄ ki kā.» 20U lī mimmee ní ki kútì yii: «M-jipɔɔn, pɔ́ɔǹ a-ba kí ká dipɔbil. Kíĺ atuun gbanti kí taa fàŋkì báà tiba, ní a-wunti ń taa yɔ̀tī mun! Tiŋman, ti-Dindaan m-Nimbɔtiu làá nīn bí a-cee. Waa làá dū-si kí fá, ní ki kpá kí fàtī u-boon kí tīī-si kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋun a làá tɔ̄ úǹ Unimbɔti diiku mātam tuuŋŋi kí dóóyee. 21Kpèè, bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab yākatì akiti akiti ki cí kí tɔ̄ kunimbɔtidiin tuuŋŋi. Kí kūtèe, binib bin cáá nlammɔntiimee nì bin cáá kí tɔ̄ atuun kɔkɔ nì ŋi-bulifee, nì Isirayeel kpilib nì samaa kɔkɔ bí a-cee kí ŋá a nín là puee.»

english_text:
Gifts for Building the Temple
1 David told the crowd:
God chose my son Solomon to build the temple, but Solomon is young and has no experience. This is not just any building—this is the temple for the Lord God! 2That's why I have done my best to get everything Solomon will need to build it—gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, onyx, turquoise, colored gems, all kinds of precious stones, and marble.
3Besides doing all that, I have promised to give part of my own gold and silver as a way of showing my love for God's temple. 4More than 100 tons of my finest gold and almost 240 tons of my silver will be used to decorate its walls 5and to make the gold and silver objects. Now, who else will show their dedication to the Lord by giving gifts for building his temple?
6After David finished speaking, the family leaders, the tribal leaders, the army commanders, and the government officials voluntarily gave gifts 7for the temple. These gifts included more than 170 tons of gold, over 340 tons of silver, 620 tons of bronze, and more than 3,400 tons of iron. 8Everyone who owned precious stones also donated them to the temple treasury, where Jehiel from the Levite clan of Gershon guarded them.
9David and the people were very happy that so much had been given to the Lord, and they all celebrated.
David Praises the Lord
10Then, in front of everyone, David sang praises to the Lord:
I praise you forever, Lord! You are the God our ancestor Jacob worshiped. 11 Your power is great, and your glory is seen everywhere in heaven and on earth. You are king of the entire world, 12and you rule with strength and power. You make people rich and powerful and famous. 13We thank you, our God, and praise you.
14But why should we be happy that we have given you these gifts? They belong to you, and we have only given back what is already yours. 15We are only foreigners living here on earth for a while, just as our ancestors were. And we will soon be gone, like a shadow that suddenly disappears.
16Our Lord God, we have brought all these things for building a temple to honor you. They belong to you, and you gave them to us. 17But we are happy, because everyone has voluntarily given you these things. You know what is in everyone's heart, and you are pleased when people are honest. 18Always make us eager to give, and help us be faithful to you, just as our ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob faithfully worshiped you. 19And give Solomon the desire to completely obey your laws and teachings, and the desire to build the temple for which I have provided these gifts.
20David then said to the people, “Now it's your turn to praise the Lord, the God your ancestors worshiped!” So everyone praised the Lord, and they bowed down to honor him and David their king.
Solomon Is Crowned King
21The next day, the Israelites slaughtered 1,000 bulls, 1,000 rams, and 1,000 lambs, and they offered them as sacrifices to please the Lord, along with offerings of wine. 22The people were very happy, and they ate and drank there at the Lord's altar.
That same day, Solomon was again crowned king. The people celebrated and poured olive oil on Solomon's head to show that he would be their next king. They also poured oil on Zadok's head to show that he was their priest.
23 So Solomon became king after David his father. Solomon was successful, and everyone in Israel obeyed him. 24Every official and every soldier, as well as all of David's other sons, were loyal to him. 25The Lord made Solomon a great king, and the whole nation was amazed at how famous he was. In fact, no other king of Israel was as great as Solomon.
David Dies
26David the son of Jesse was king of Israel 27 for 40 years. He ruled from Hebron for 7 years and from Jerusalem for 33 years. 28David was rich and respected and lived to be an old man. Then he died, and his son Solomon became king.
29Everything David did while he was king is included in the history written by the prophets Samuel, Nathan, and Gad. 30They wrote about his powerful rule and about the things that happened not only to him, but also to Israel and the other nations.
translation_text:
Binib tīī tiwan bí dūú mā kunimbɔtidii
1Ubɔti Daafiidi bí samaa un kpáfì u-ceeyee kɔkɔ yii: «M-jipɔɔn Saloomɔn un ní ti-Dindaan lēēyee dáá sá kibiki kaa cáá dinyil báà tiba poon. Ama ditundi din dɔ̄ ki cí-uee kaa sá gbaŋgbam yal. Di sá yii an kaa sá dibeecindi ní u làá mā kí tīī unifoo, ama an sá ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti diiku ní u làá mā. 2M dū m-pɔŋŋu kɔkɔ ki bɔ́ntì tiwan tin ní bi làá dūú mā m-Nimbɔtiu Diikuee ki síiǹ. M nyàab̄ sindaariya nì animbil kúti nì tasa kúti nì tikúmɔntiil nì idɔ bí dūú mɔ́ɔ́ tiwan tin kɔkɔ an máaǹee. M bɔ́ntì ataŋkpee ŋin bi yíì kɔɔrnaliinee nì ataŋkpee aba mun bí dūú nyɔ̀kɔntì kunimbɔtidii, ataŋkpabɔn bí ní ŋin nyim nyáń mi-ba mi-bee mun bí, an dàkà yii ataŋkpamɔnti kɔkɔ nì ŋi-bulifi nì ataŋkpee ŋin bi kpítí ki cáa māā adiinee. 3Kí kūtèe, m nín néeń m-Nimbɔtiu Diikuee pu ní m dū mama m-ba sindaariyau nì m-nimbiliŋ ki tīī. M dūu kútì tin kɔkɔ m bɔ́ntì ki síiǹ bí dūú mā Circir Diiku gbantee pu. 4M tīī sindaariyamɔnti un nyánní Oofiiri tiŋkinee tɔɔnib dilaataal, nì animbil kúti tɔɔnib alaataa ali nì imuŋku ili bí dūú dùntī kí nákań kunimbɔtidii guŋŋi pu. 5Kɔŋkɔnnee ni-kansikin ŋma di kíí nì dipɔbil diba kí tīī ti-Dindaan sindaariya nì animbil kúti? Mimmee bitɔntɔnliibi làá dāá dūú mɔ́ɔ́ tiwan tin kɔkɔ máaǹ bí dū sindaariya nì animbil kúti kí mɔ́ɔ́yee.»
6Niinee ní adican kpilib, nì Isirayeel naakɔti kpilib, nì bijanjakpilib bin kpòotī bijanjaliibi kutuku kutukuee, nì bin kpòotī bijanjaliibi dilaataal dilaataalee nì anikiti ŋin tūǹ ubɔti tuuŋŋee kpilib kɔkɔ kíí ki tīī tiwan nì dipɔbil diba. 7Tin bi nìn tīī bí dūú mā ti-Dindaan Diikuee di sá sindaariya tɔɔnib dilaataal nì imuŋku ita nì saalaa, nì sindaariya jitɔmbi kutukub saalaa, nì animbil kúti tɔɔnib alaataa ata, nì tasa kúti an jítì kii tɔɔnib alaataa aluu pu nì tikúmɔntiil an jítì tɔɔnib kutukub bita pu. 8Binib bin kɔkɔ nìn cáá ataŋkpamɔntee nìn dū-ŋi ki tīī Yeeyeel un sá Geersɔn maaliŋunee ú dūú ŋá Unimbɔti diiku gaajawanti poon. 9Binib gbanti nìn dū bi-gaajawanti ki tīī ti-Dindaan nì dipɔbil diba ní ki nìn bí mmɔnni. An nìn mɔ́ɔkiǹ ubɔti Daafiidi mun tikpil.
Daafiidi wimmeem
10Niinee ní Daafiidi jáam̀ ti-Dindaan samaa kɔkɔ nimbiin ki lī yii: «Bí nyɔ̄ŋkì sii ti-Dindaan, ti-naanja Jaakɔb Nimbɔtiu kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaan. 11Sii ti-Dindaan di sá ukpaan ki yì mpɔn nì tinyool nì jilma nì dibeel!
