Tiŋman, sii ti-Dindaan di yì tin kɔkɔ bí yilpu nì taapuee. Sii di sá ubɔti, sii un tɔ́kɔ́ tin kɔkɔ cáá kufoouee puee. 12Sii cee ní tigaajati nì tinyool nyēeń. Sii di cáá mpɔn tiwan kɔkɔ pu. Sii di cáá dikpabil nì mpɔn. Sii di cáá mpɔn kí yòon̄ unil yilpu ú báań inyaan. 13An pu ní ti jáaḿ sii ti-Nimbɔtiu, ní ki nyɔ́ŋkí a-yinnyaandi. 14Maa sá tibaaa, m-nibul yab mun kaa sá tiba. An kaa sá timbi ti-ba di cáá mpɔn kí tīī-si tiwan tin ti bíi tìì-si nee. Sii di tīī-ti an wanti kɔkɔ. Tin a tīī-tee ní timbi fàtīi gīintí ki tìì-si nee. 15Timbi sá binicambi nì binikɔkaabi ní a-nimbiin, kii ti-naanjab kɔkɔ nín nìn bí puee. Ti-maŋfal wiiŋyi kitiŋ nee pu sá kii mboon nín jītí puee ní, dimákal kpá. 16Ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu, ti kóoǹ tiwan tikpil ki kpúkuǹ kí dūú mā kudii kí tīī a-circir yindi tinyool. Too, tikɔkɔ nyánní a-cee ní ki sá a-wanti. 17M-Nimbɔtiu, m nyí yii a kóò unil pɔbilin kí nyɔ̀kɔfì kí kpèè, ní ki néeń tin bí deedeeyee. Mamee nì dipɔbil diba ní m dū m-gaajawanti ki ŋá-si nlammɔntiim saraau. Ní m gíti ká díǹ mun nì dipɔɔpindi yii a-nibul din kóoǹ ki kpáfì doo nee mun ŋá míǹ mbaantiim. 18Ti-Dindaan, ti-naanjab Abraam nì Isaaki nì Jaakɔb Nimbɔtiu, yàntī a-nibul ń nīn cáá dipɔɔmɔntiil gbanti, ní bi-landɔkɔŋu kɔkɔ ń nīn pée bí sii baba pu kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaan. 19Tīī m-jipɔɔn Saloomɔn tibulcin pɔbil ú nīn nóó a-marab nì a-dàkatam nì a-bɔkpaaŋi, kí nīn tɔ́-ŋi. Ú mā a-Circir Diiku kun pu m bɔ́ntì tikɔkɔ ki yóoǹee.»
20Boonee ní Daafiidi bí samaa yii: «Ní jāam̀maan ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu!» Ní samaa kɔkɔ jáam̀ ti-Dindaan, bi-naanjab Nimbɔtiu. Bi nìn tātìi gbāaǹ bi-yigbeeŋi tūū kitiŋ Unimbɔti nì ubɔti nimbiin.
Bi nín kāaǹ Saloomɔn dibeel puee nì Daafiidi kúm bɔti
21Ku wúntèe ní Isirayeel yab ŋá ti-Dindaan mpèé saraabi nì bisaraawɔkaabi. Bi nìn kūū inajaa kutuku, ipijaa kutuku nì apibil kutuku, ní ki kútì ndamam min nyɔkɔm an sá bí kūtèe ki dūu ŋá saraabi. Mpèé saraabi bin bi nìn ŋée nìn wīikí kí kpíiǹ Isirayeel yab bin kɔkɔ nìn bí niinee. 22Ŋwiin gbantee, Isirayeel yab nìn jíń ki nyùn̄ ti-Dindaan nimbiin nì dipɔɔpindi nì ifaal. Ŋwiin gbanti ní bi kāaǹ Daafiidi jipɔɔn Saloomɔn ubɔti nliliitiim. Bi nìn bātì ŋkpam ki sītì u-yil pu ki kāaǹ-u tibɔtiil ú nīn bí ti-Dindaan tundin. Bi nìn bātì ŋkpam ki sītì Saadooki mun yil pu ú kpántí usaraaŋakpil. 23Saloomɔn nìn kāl̀ ti-Dindaan beejal pu ki fōō u-baa Daafiidi yil ki kpántì ubɔti. An nìn bútì-u tikpil ní Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nìn tɔ́-u tiŋan pu. 24Bijanjakpilib kɔkɔ nì bibaatandambi kɔkɔ, ki kpáaǹ Daafiidi jipɔmbi bin kíǹee kɔkɔ nìn sīntì bi-ba taapu ki tīī Saloomɔn ki tɔ́-u. 25Ti-Dindaan nìn yāntì Saloomɔn yindi yíkì yilpu tikpil Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nimbiin. U nìn yāntì Saloomɔn ká jilma tiŋan tiŋan pu, ní u-nyooti nìn jítiǹ Isirayeel bibɔtiibi bin kɔkɔ līntiǹ-uee.
26Isayi jipɔɔn Daafiidi nìn jíń dibeel Isirayeel kɔkɔ pu ní. 27U nìn jíń dibeel Isirayeel tiŋki kɔkɔ pu abin imuŋku ili ní. U nìn kāl̀ dibeel Eebrɔn tiŋkin abin aluli ní ki kāl̀ dibeel Jeerusaleem tiŋkin abin mmuŋku nì saalaa nì ata. 28U nìn púĺ tiŋan ní ki nín kpíì. U nìn cáá tigaajati tikpil, ki nìn nyáń diyindi mun. U nín kpíìyee, u-jipɔɔn Saloomɔn di fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.
29Ubɔti Daafiidi tuuŋŋi, kí yòon̄ ŋi nín kíĺ puee kí tin sāā ŋi nín kúntì puee ŋmàn̄ ki kā Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Samiyeel tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun, nì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Naatan tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun nì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Gaadi tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun. 30Tigbɔn gbantin ní bi ŋmàn̄ tin jítì Daafiidi pu ŋyunti ŋun u sá ubɔtee nì u nín dàkā dibaatandi puee nì agìń ŋin u kée nì tin jítì Isirayeel tiŋki puee nì tin jítì abee ŋin kíǹee puee.

english_text:
The Lord Makes Solomon Wise
(1 Kings 3.1-15)
1King Solomon, the son of David, was now in complete control of his kingdom, because the Lord God had blessed him and made him a powerful king.
2-5 At that time, the sacred tent that Moses the servant of the Lord had made in the desert was still kept at Gibeon, and in front of the tent was the bronze altar that Bezalel had made.
One day, Solomon told the people of Israel, the army commanders, the officials, and the family leaders, to go with him to the place of worship at Gibeon, even though his father King David had already moved the sacred chest from Kiriath-Jearim to the tent that he had set up for it in Jerusalem. Solomon and the others went to Gibeon to worship the Lord, 6and there at the bronze altar, Solomon offered a thousand animals as sacrifices to please the Lord.
7God appeared to Solomon that night in a dream and said, “Solomon, ask for anything you want, and I will give it to you.”
8Solomon answered:
Lord God, you were always loyal to my father David, and now you have made me king of Israel. 9 I am supposed to rule these people, but there are as many of them as there are specks of dust on the ground. So keep the promise you made to my father 10and make me wise. Give me the knowledge I'll need to be the king of this great nation of yours.
11God replied:
Solomon, you could have asked me to make you rich or famous or to let you live a long time. Or you could have asked for your enemies to be destroyed. Instead, you asked for wisdom and knowledge to rule my people. 12So I will make you wise and intelligent. But I will also make you richer and more famous than any king before or after you.
13Solomon then left Gibeon and returned to Jerusalem, the capital city of Israel.
Solomon's Wealth
(1 Kings 10.26-29)
14 Solomon had a force of 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horses that he kept in Jerusalem and other towns.
15While Solomon was king of Israel, there was silver and gold everywhere in Jerusalem, and cedar was as common as ordinary sycamore trees in the foothills.
16-17 Solomon's merchants bought his horses and chariots in the regions of Musri and Kue. They paid 600 pieces of silver for a chariot and 150 pieces of silver for a horse. They also sold horses and chariots to the Hittite and Syrian kings.
translation_text:
ISIRAYEEL BƆTIU SALOOMƆN BƆTI
(1–9)
1Daafiidi jipɔɔn Saloomɔn nìn cúú u-beel pɔŋŋu ki báaǹ inyaan. Ti-Dindaan u-Nimbɔtiu nìn bí u-cee ní ki nìn yāntì u kpántì ubɔtikpaŋkpaan.
Saloomɔn mēē Unimbɔti yii ú tīī-u iciin ú dūú kàl̄ dibeel
(Kpèè 1 Bib 3.4-15)
2Saloomɔn nìn sòon̄ nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ, cilinjee bijanjakpilib bin nìn sá bijanjaliibi kutuku kutuku kpilibee nì bin nìn sá dilaataal dilaataal kpilibee, nì bibɔsoonliibi nì Isirayeel tindaŋkpilib kɔkɔ, an dàkà yii adican kpilib. 3Saloomɔn nì binib bin nìn kóoǹ ki kpáfì u-cee gbantee nìn táá ki cūtì Circir paaŋŋu ŋun bí Gabawɔn tiŋkinee. Di sá yii niin ní Unimbɔti kpafindi tantiu un ti-Dindaan tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi nìn ŋá kuteeunee nìn bí.
4Daafiidi nìn yōoǹ Unimbɔti Dakaau Kiiriyati-Yeeyariim tiŋkin ki cáa cūnnì Jeerusaleem tiŋkin. U nìn dū-u ki síiǹ mpaan ŋun u nìn bɔ́ntèe pu, tanti poon. 5Ama ti-Dindaan circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nyɔkɔpu, Gabawɔn tiŋkin niin ní tasa saraafaŋŋu ŋun Uurii jipɔɔn, Uur naantiiu Beesaleel nìn máńee bí.
Niin ní Saloomɔn nì samaa nìn cūtì ki bālifì ti-Dindaan. 6Saloomɔn nìn jɔ́m̀ tasa saraafaŋŋu ŋun nìn bí ti-Dindaan nimbiin, dikpafindi tantiu nyɔkɔpuee ki ŋá bisaraawɔkaabi. U nìn kūū tiwaŋkuti kutuku ní ki dū ti-kɔkɔ ki wùn̄ ŋŋmi. 7Kunyeeu gbantee ní Unimbɔti lēē u-ba ki dàkā Saloomɔn ní ki bí-u yii: «Bàlifì kun ní a là ḿ tīī-see!» 8Ní Saloomɔn kíí Unimbɔti yii: «Ti-Dindaan, a dàkā m-baa Daafiidi kulaŋŋaŋfitiiu tikpil, ki yāntì kɔŋkɔnnee m kpántì ubɔti ki fōō u-yil. 9Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti, a nín nìn pōoǹ m-baa Daafiidi puee, yàntī án ŋá míǹ. Di sá yii sii di dū-mi ki kāaǹ binib bin wīikí kii kitiŋ pu tam nee pu ubɔti. 10Tīī-mi iciin nì dinyil ḿ dūú kpòotī a-nibul. An yaa sá fám, ŋma di ŋūǹ kí kpòotī a-nibul dikpaandi nee?»
11Ní Unimbɔti kíí Saloomɔn yii: «Aa bālifì tigaajati àá tigaajawan àá tinyool àá a-nannanliibi kúm, ní kaa bālifì mun yii ḿ tīī-si mmaŋfafɔkɔn. Ama a bālifì kí nīn cáá iciin nì dinyil kí ŋmā kí dūú kpòotī m-nibul din pu m kāaǹ-si dibeelee. A nín bālifì mimmee puee, 12m làá tīī-si iciin nì dinyil. M làá tīī-si tigaajati nì tigaajawan nì tinyool kí kūtì. A làá nīn cáá tíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ kí jītíǹ bibɔtiibi bin līntiǹ-see nì bin làá dāá páanní a-boonee.» 13Niinee Saloomɔn yíkì Circir Paaŋŋu ŋun bí Gabawɔn tiŋkin, laakin ti-Dindaan kpafindi tantiu nìn bée. U nìn fātìi gítì Jeerusaleem tiŋkin ní ki kāl̀ Isirayeel tiŋki pu dibeel.
Saloomɔn gaajati
(Kpèè 1 Bib 10.26-28, 2 Kroo 9.25-28)
14Saloomɔn nìn kóoǹ janjatɔrɔkub nì itaamu ki kpáfì. U nìn cáá janjatɔrɔkub kutuku ubɔ nì alaataa anaa, nì itaamu kutukub saalaa nì bili. Tijanjawan gbanti tiba nìn bí ntimu mun poon ní ajanjanaapaa bée, ní tin kíǹee bí u-cee Jeerusaleem. 15Ubɔti nìn yāntì animbil nì sindaariya gbí Jeerusaleem tiŋkin kii ataŋkpeeyee, ní seedir dɔi wīikí kii Seefeelaa tiŋki sufii in bi yíì siikoomɔɔree. 16Saloomɔn taamui nìn nyēeń Eejipiti nì Siisilii timmun ní. Niin ní ubɔti nyampoobi nìn dāań-i. 17Bi yaa nìn cáań kujaau tɔrɔkuu Eejipiti tiŋkinee, u-nyampooku nìn sá animbil kúti jitɔmbi alaataa aluu ní, ní utaamu nyampooku sá animbil kúti jitɔmbi dilaataal nì imuŋku ili nì saalaa. Binyampoobi gbanti nìn cāabìń janjatɔrɔkub nì itaamu gbanti ki nyáfíǹ Eeti yab nì Siirii yab bɔtiibi mun.
Saloomɔn bɔ́ntì kí mā ti-Dindaan Diiku
(Kpèè 1 Bib 5.15-32, 7.13-14)
18Saloomɔn nìn lēē yii u làá mā Kudii kí dūú sú ti-Dindaan, ní kí mā úǹ u-ba kubɔtinaakoou.

english_text:
Solomon Asks Hiram To Help Build the Temple
(1 Kings 5.1-12)
1Solomon decided to build a temple where the Lord would be worshiped, and also to build a palace for himself. 2He assigned 70,000 men to carry building supplies and 80,000 to cut stone from the hills. And he chose 3,600 men to supervise these workers.
3Solomon sent the following message to King Hiram of Tyre:
Years ago, when my father David was building his palace, you supplied him with cedar logs. Now will you send me supplies? 4I am building a temple where the Lord my God will be worshiped. Sweet-smelling incense will be burned there, and sacred bread will be offered to him. Worshipers will offer sacrifices to the Lord every morning and evening, every Sabbath, and on the first day of each month, as well as during all our religious festivals. These things will be done for all time, just as the Lord has commanded.
5This will be a great temple, because our God is greater than all other gods. 6 No one can ever build a temple large enough for God—even the heavens are too small a place for him to live in! All I can do is build a place where we can offer sacrifices to him.
7Send me a worker who can not only carve, but who can work with gold, silver, bronze, and iron, as well as make brightly colored cloth. The person you send will work here in Judah and Jerusalem with the skilled workers that my father has already hired.
8I know that you have workers who are experts at cutting lumber in Lebanon. So would you please send me some cedar, pine, and juniper logs? My workers will be there to help them, 9because I'll need a lot of lumber to build such a large and glorious temple. 10I will pay your woodcutters 2,000 tons of wheat, the same amount of barley, 400,000 liters of wine, and that same amount of olive oil.
11Hiram sent his answer back to Solomon:
I know that the Lord must love his people, because he has chosen you to be their king. 12Praise the Lord God of Israel who made heaven and earth! He has given David a son who isn't only wise and smart, but who has the knowledge to build a temple for the Lord and a palace for himself.
13I am sending Huram Abi to you. He is wise and very skillful. 14His mother was from the Israelite tribe of Dan, and his father was from Tyre. Not only is Huram an expert at working with gold, silver, bronze, iron, stone, and wood, but he can also make colored cloth and fine linen. And he can carve anything if you give him a pattern to follow. He can help your workers and those hired by your father King David.
15Go ahead and send the wheat, barley, olive oil, and wine you promised to pay my workers. 16I will tell them to start cutting down trees in Lebanon. They will cut as many as you need, then tie them together into rafts, and float them down along the coast to Joppa. Your workers can take them to Jerusalem from there.
Solomon's Work Force
17Solomon counted all the foreigners who were living in Israel, just as his father David had done when he was king, and the total was 153,600. 18He assigned 70,000 of them to carry building supplies and 80,000 of them to cut stone from the hills. He chose 3,600 others to supervise the workers and to make sure the work was completed.
translation_text:
1U nìn fōō binib kutukub imuŋku ita nì saalaa bí nīn tūntí tiwan nì binib kutukub imuŋku inaa bí nīn bí dijool pu ki kpítí ataŋkpee, ní ki fōō binib kutukub bita nì alaataa aluu bí nīn kpèé bitɔntɔnliibi.
2Saloomɔn nìn tú binib Tiir yab bɔtiu Yiiram cee bí tùkù-u yii: «A nìn tútúǹ m-baa Daafiidi ki tīiń-u seedir dɔi u dūu máń kudii kun poon u làá nīn kóòyee. M bàà là yii á ŋá míǹ mbaantiim kí tīī-mi. 3Kpèè, m làá mā kudii kí tīī ti-Dindaan m-Nimbɔtiu tinyool. Isirayeel yab làá dū kudiiyee kí sú-u. Bi làá nīn tùutī talaalub ki tìì-u, ní kí nīn pāantí kpɔnɔb bin bi dūu sú-uee baabadal. Bi làá nīn ŋáań bisaraawɔkaabi kutaafaau nì kujoou, ki kpáaǹ iwiŋŋuŋfikaa dal nì uŋmal kamaa wimpeekaaŋu nì jiŋaalib wiiŋyi in ti jīǹ ki jáaḿ ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiuee saraabi. Unimbɔti nín nìn síiǹ Isirayeel yab yii bí nīn ŋáań míǹ ki cá jaanjaan. 4Kudii kun m làá mēe máaǹ kí nīn sá kudikpaaŋŋu, di sá yii ti-Nimbɔtiu di sá ukpaan ki jítiǹ inimbɔti kɔkɔ. 5Ama ŋma di ŋūǹ kí mā-u kudii? Di sá yii yilpu nì yilpu fɔ́ŋŋŋ kaa wāā ú ŋmā kí kɔ́. Ní ŋma ní m sá kí ŋmā kí mā-u kudii? Kun m pée là kí ŋée di sá ḿ mā mpaan ŋun pu bi làá nīn ŋáań-u saraabee. 6Míǹ puee, á tīiń-mi unil un ŋūǹ kí tɔ̄ sindaariya nì animbil nì tasa nì tikúti tundi tiŋanee. Udaan máaǹ kí nīn nyí bi nín bɔ́ntí satab bí nīn cáá nnyim min máǹee nì nnyim min máǹ cínciŋee nì nnyim min máǹ gùŋgumee, ní kí nīn gíti nyí tikpiŋkpiil bɔti. Udaan làá kūtì man m-ba tɔntɔnliibi bin m-baa Daafiidi nìn lēē bi bí Jeerusaleem tiŋkin nì Juuda timmunee pu kí tɔ̄ ditundi. 7Á tīiń-mi seedir nì siipreesi nì santaal dɔi in bí Leebanɔn jooŋŋi puee, di sá yii m nyí a-tɔntɔnliibi di ŋūǹ ki gà Leebanɔn sufii tiŋanee. M-tɔntɔnliibi làá dāá kūtì bi-pu. 8Bi làá bɔ́ntí-mi idɔ an nīn náaǹ, di sá yii Unimbɔti diiku kun m làá mēe làá nīn sá kukpaaŋŋu ní kí nīn ŋān̄. 9M làá tīī a-tɔntɔnliibi bin làá gāā isufee bilee yim tɔɔnib kutukub biluu nì ɔɔji yim tɔɔnib kutukub biluu nì ndamam liitirib kutukub alaataa anii nì ŋkpam liitirib kutukub alaataa anii.»
10Tiir bɔtiu Yiiram ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu ki kíí Saloomɔn yii: «Ti-Dindaan néeń u-nibul. An pu ní u dū-si ki kāaǹ di-pu ubɔti.» 11Ní Yiiram gíti kútì ki lī yii: «Tí jāam̀ ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu un di náań kutagbɔŋu nì kitiŋee. Tiŋman u tīī ubɔti Daafiidi kibininjabiki kin cáá iciin nì dinyil nì nlandɔkɔee. U làá mā kudii kí tīī ti-Dindaan ní kí mā úǹ u-ba diiku. 12Too, m làá dū Uram-Abii kí tīiń-si. U sá utɔntɔnli un nyí ditundi tiŋan ki yáb̀ee. 13U-na sá Daani naakookun ní u-baa sá utiirja. U nyí sindaariya nì animbil nì tasa nì tikúti nì ataŋkpee nì idɔ tundi tiŋan. U gíti ŋūǹ kí bɔ́ntí satab bí nīn cáá nnyim min máǹee nì nnyim min máǹ cínciŋee nì nnyim min máǹ gùŋgumee nì satab bin bí fálfalee. U gíti tí ŋūǹ kí kpítí tikpiŋkpiil kí lēē kunaŋu ataŋkpee pu. Ditundi din a yaa pée dūu ŋúbiǹ-uee, u làá bɔ́ntí kí tīī-si ní. U nì sii a-ba tɔntɔnliibi nì a-baa ubɔti Daafiidi tɔntɔnliibi di làá kpāfì kí tɔ̄ ditundi. 14Bilee nì ɔɔji nì ŋkpam nì ndamam min bɔti a nìn sòon̄ee, dūú tīiń man a-tɔntɔnliu kɔŋkɔnnee. 15Ti làá cùú gāań isufi Leebanɔn kii a nín pée là puee, ní kí bóob́ kí dūú tɔ̄ń tiŋkun kí cáań-si Jafaa tiŋkin. Niinee ní á dāá yòon̄-i kí cùnnì Jeerusaleem.»
16Saloomɔn nìn kàan̄ binicambi bin kɔkɔ nìn bí Isirayeel tiŋki puee, kii u-baa Daafiidi nín nìn kàan̄-bi pu ŋyunti ŋun u nìn sá ubɔtee. Bi nìn nyáń binib kutukub dilaataal nì imuŋku ili nì saalaa nì bita nì binib alaataa aluu. 17U nìn lēē bi-kansikin binib kutukub imuŋku ita nì saalaa bí nīn tūntí tiwan, ní ki lēē binib kutukub imuŋku inaa bí nīn kpítí ataŋkpee dijool pu, ní ki lēē binib kutukub bita nì alaataa aluu bí nīn kpèé bitɔntɔnliibi gbanti ditundi ń còom̀.

english_text:
The Temple Is Built
(1 Kings 6.1-38)
1-2 Solomon's workers began building the temple in Jerusalem on the second day of the second month, four years after Solomon had become king of Israel. It was built on Mount Moriah where the Lord had appeared to David at the threshing place that had belonged to Araunah from Jebus.
3The inside of the temple was 27 meters long and 9 meters wide, according to the older standards. 4Across the front of the temple was a porch 9 meters wide and 9 meters high. The inside walls of the porch were covered with pure gold.
5Solomon had the inside walls of the temple's main room paneled first with pine and then with a layer of gold, and he had them decorated with carvings of palm trees and designs that looked like chains. 6He used precious stones to decorate the temple, and he used gold imported from Parvaim 7to decorate the ceiling beams, the doors, the door frames, and the walls. Solomon also told the workers to carve designs of winged creatures into the walls.
8 The most holy place was nine meters square, and its walls were covered with over 20 tons of fine gold. 9Five hundred and seventy grams of gold was used to cover the heads of the nails. The walls of the small storage rooms were also covered with gold.
10 Solomon had two statues of winged creatures made to put in the most holy place, and he covered them with gold. 11-13Each creature had two wings and was four and a half meters from the tip of one wing to the tip of the other wing. Solomon set them next to each other in the most holy place, facing the doorway. Their wings were spread out and reached all the way across the nine-meter room.
14 A curtain was made of fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool, and embroidered with designs of winged creatures.
The Two Columns
(1 Kings 7.15-22)
15Two columns were made for the entrance to the temple. Each one was 16 meters tall and had a cap on top that was over 2 meters high. 16The top of each column was decorated with designs that looked like chains and with 100 carvings of pomegranates. 17Solomon had one of the columns placed on the south side of the temple's entrance; it was called Jachin. The other one was placed on the north side of the entrance; it was called Boaz.
translation_text:
Kunimbɔtidii mātam
(Kpèè 1 Bib 6.1-38)
1Saloomɔn nìn kíĺ ki bíi māā ti-Dindaan Diiku Jeerusaleem tiŋkin, Mooriya jool pu. Niin ní ti-Dindaan nìn lēē u-ba ki dàkā u-baa Daafiidi. Daafiidi nín nìn bɔ́ntì mpaan gbanti ujeebusja Ɔrinan naapaal pu. 2U nín jíń dibeel dibinnanaatiil ŋmaliliitiu poonee ní u kíĺ ki bíi māā-ku.
3Ti-Dindaan Diiku kun Saloomɔn nìn máńee nyeel nìn fɔ̀kɔ̀ mpúun pu meetab mmuŋku nì saalaa ní ku-waaŋŋu sá meetab saalaa. 4Kunimbɔtidii nyɔkɔpuee, kudii kubɔ nìn bí bi tà kí kɔ́, ku-waaŋŋu nìn sá meetab saalaa kii kunimbɔtidii ku-ba waaŋŋuee, ní ku-púuŋŋu sá meetab biŋmoo. U nìn dū sindaariyamɔnti ní ki nákáǹ ku-poon. 5U nìn dū siipreesi dɔi in bi látì apampan ki dū sindaariya ki nyūntèe ki nákáǹ kudikpaaŋŋuee poon. Bi nìn lēē ibafi nì ikusaka ki nákáǹ adɔpampanee pu. 6Bi nìn gíti dū ataŋkpamɔnti ní ki nyɔ̄kɔntì kudii gbanti. Sindaariya un bi nìn dūu túń ku-pu ditundee nìn nyánní Paarwayiim tiŋkin ní. 7Bi nìn dū sindaariya ki nyūntì kudiiyee dɔi in bi dūu kpáá ki bɔ̀b̄ yilpuee nì ku-punyɔmmu nì ku-guŋŋi nì ku-punuubi, ní ki kpítì keerubimbi ki nákáǹ agun pu.
8U nìn máń kudii kun bi yíì circir páaa laŋkee, ku-waaŋŋu nì kunimbɔtidii waaŋŋu nìn sá mbaantiim ní: meetab saalaa, ní ku-fɔkɔŋŋu sá meetab saalaa. Bi nìn dū sindaariyamɔnti tɔɔnib mmuŋku ní ki nyūntì ki bīiǹ ku-poon. 9Bi nìn dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ ipiin ní i-nyiŋfiŋu nìn sá graambi alaataa aŋmoo. Ki kpáaǹ adiin ŋin nìn tɔ́kɔ́ yilpuee, bi nìn dū sindaariya ní ki nyūntì ki bīiǹ ŋi-guŋŋi pu.
10Bi nìn dūntì tikúti ki dūu mɔ́ɔ́ keerubimbi bili. Bi nìn dū sindaariya ki nyūntì-bi, ní ki dū-bi ki síiǹ circir páaa diikun. 11Keerubimbee feeŋyi fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá meetab saalaa. Keerubim peekaa feeŋŋu ŋubɔ fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá meetab bili nì dijandi ní ki nìn tūū digundi, ní ŋfeen ŋun kíǹee sá meetab bili nì dijandi, ní ki nìn tūū Keerubim un kíǹee feeŋŋu ŋubɔ. 12Keerubim liliitee feeŋŋu ŋubɔ fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá meetab bili nì dijandi ní ki nìn tūū kunimbɔtidii gundi ní ŋun kíǹee mun nìn sá meetab bili nì dijandi ní ki nìn tūū keerubim upeekaayee feeŋŋu ŋubɔ. 13Keerubimbee feeŋyi nìn kpátì ní ki nìn wāā ki bàn̄ meetab saalaa. Bi nìn yú ní bi-nimbiiŋyi túĺ poon pú. 14Bi nìn dū ŋŋaabu ŋun dàfèe nì ŋŋaaman gùŋgum nì ŋŋaaman cínciŋ nì ŋŋaaman wèeee ki lùn̄ ŋŋaasakaŋkaa. Bi nìn lùn̄ keerubimbi ki nákáǹ ŋu-pu.
Tasa kúti jaantalkub nì nsaraafan bɔti
(Kpèè 1 Bib 7.15-22)
15Bitɔntɔnliibi nìn dū tasa kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́ jaantalkub bili ki síiǹ kunimbɔtidii nyɔkɔpu, bi-fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá meetab saalku nì bili. Bi nìn mɔ́ɔ́ akɔl ali yam ki páaǹ jaantalkubee pu. Akɔlee fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá meetab bili nì dijandi ní. 16Bi nìn gíti ŋá tinyɔkɔntikaal ikusaka yam ki dūu sākaǹ jaantalkubee yilpu. Bi nìn gíti mɔ́ɔ́ greenaadi biliŋ ki sākaǹ ikusakee pu. 17Bi nìn dū jaantalkubee ki cóoǹ kunimbɔtidii nyɔkɔpu, ubɔ bí ŋgan pú ní un kíǹee bí ŋgiil pú. Bi nìn yíì un bí ŋgiil púee yii Yakiin, taapu sá yii: <Unimbɔti di tìì mpɔn>, ní ki yíì un bí ŋgan púee yii Boowaasi, taapu sá yii: <Unimbɔtin ní mpɔn bí>.

english_text:
The Furnishings for the Temple
(1 Kings 7.23-51)
1 Solomon had a bronze altar made that was nine meters square and four and a half meters high. 2He also gave orders to make a large metal bowl called the Sea. It was 4.5 meters across, just over two meters deep, and 13.5 meters around. 3Its outer edge was decorated with two rows of carvings of bulls, ten bulls to about every 45 centimeters, all made from the same piece of metal as the bowl. 4The bowl itself sat on top of twelve bronze bulls, with three bulls facing outward in each of four directions. 5The sides of the bowl were 75 millimeters thick, and its rim was in the shape of a cup that curved outward like flower petals. The bowl held about 60,000 liters.
6 He also made ten small bowls and put five on each side of the large bowl. The small bowls were used to wash the animals that were burned on the altar as sacrifices, and the priests used the water in the large bowl to wash their hands.
7 Ten gold lampstands were also made according to the plans. Solomon placed these lampstands inside the temple, five on each side of the main room. 8 He also made ten tables and placed them in the main room, five on each side. And he made 100 small gold sprinkling bowls.
9Solomon gave orders to build two courtyards: a smaller one that only priests could use and a larger one. The doors to these courtyards were covered with bronze. 10The large bowl called the Sea was placed near the southeast corner of the temple.
11Huram made shovels, sprinkling bowls, and pans for hot ashes. Here is a list of the other furnishings he made for God's temple: 12two columns, two bowl-shaped caps for the tops of these columns, two chain designs on the caps, 13400 pomegranates in two rows for the chain designs, 14the stands and the small bowls, 15the large bowl and the twelve bulls that held it up, 16pans for hot ashes, as well as shovels and meat forks.
Huram made all these things out of polished bronze 17by pouring melted bronze into the clay molds he had set up near the Jordan River, between Succoth and Zeredah.
18There were so many bronze furnishings that no one ever knew how much bronze it took to make them.
19Solomon also gave orders to make the following temple furnishings out of gold: the altar, the tables that held the sacred loaves of bread, 20the lampstands and the lamps that burned in front of the most holy place, 21flower designs, lamps and tongs, 22lamp snuffers, small sprinkling bowls, ladles, fire pans, and the doors to the most holy place and the main room of the temple.
translation_text:
1Bi nìn dū tasa ki mɔ́ɔ́ nsaraafan ŋubɔ, ŋu-púuŋŋu sá meetab saalaa, ŋu-waaŋŋu sá meetab saalaa ní ŋu-fɔkɔŋŋu sá meetab biŋmoo.
Bi dū tasa ki mɔ́ɔ́ kusɔŋkpaaŋŋu nì asambil
(Kpèè 1 Bib 7.23-26)
2Bi nìn dū tasa ki mɔ́ɔ́ kusɔŋkpaaŋŋu dikuŋkundi. Kí yòon̄ dinyɔɔgbandi diba kí cáá sāā din kíǹee, mpúun nìn sá meetab biŋmoo, ku-fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá meetab bili nì dijandi, ní kí màntīí tū-kùee sá meetab saalku. 3Bi nìn lēē inajaa yam ki māntìi tú kusɔŋuee nyɔɔgbaŋŋi, dimeetajandi kamaa puee, inajaa saalaa di nìn bí ikuul ili pu. Ŋyunti ŋun bi nìn dūntì tasa ki mɔ́ɔ́ kusɔŋuee ní bi dūntì ki mɔ́ɔ́ inajaa gbanti mun. 4Bi nìn dūntì tasa ní ki dūu mɔ́ɔ́ inajaa saalaa nì ili: ita nìn kpèé ŋgan pú ní ita kpèé ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú ní ita kpèé ŋgiil pú ní ita mun kpèé ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú, ní bi dū kusɔŋuee ki tɔ́kɔǹ i-pu. 5Kusɔŋuee gbifiŋŋu nìn sá kii santimeetab binii waaŋŋuee ní, ní bi nìn ŋáŋkì ku-nyɔɔgbaŋŋi kii kɔŋkɔnnyɔkaa nyɔɔgbaŋŋee, ní an gíti bí kii lii supumpukumee. Nnyim liitirib kutukub dilaataal nì mmuŋku di nìn kàal̀ poon.
6Bi nìn gíti mɔ́ɔ́ nsampeemu saalaa ní ki dū muŋmoo ki síiǹ kusɔŋuee gaŋŋu pú ní ki dū muŋmoo mun kíǹee ki síiǹ ŋgiil pú. Nnyim min nìn kā nsampeemu gbanti poonee ní bi nìn cáa fíntí ki ŋáań tiwan circir. Nsampeemu gbantin ní bi nìn fíntí saraawɔkaa nanti, ama kusɔŋkpaaŋŋu poon nyim ní bisaraaŋaliibi nìn cáa fíntí bi-ba.
Tiwan tin bi nìn dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́yee
(Kpèè 1 Bib 7.40-51)
7Uram nìn dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ fitilab tɔ́kɔŋkaati saalaa ki nóó nì bi nín síiǹ mara bí mɔ́ɔ́-bi puee. U nìn dū-bi ki síiǹ kunimbɔtidiin, biŋmoo bí ŋŋaŋgiil pú ní biŋmoo bí ŋŋaŋgan pú.
8U nìn kpáá teebilib saalaa ki dūu síiǹ kunimbɔtidiin, biŋmoo ŋŋaŋgiil pú ní biŋmoo mun ŋŋaŋgan pú.
U nìn dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ nsambiyaamu dilaataal ki ŋáań mu-poon fatiku kí nīn cáa yàantí.
9U nìn ŋá kiciŋwaai ki tīī bisaraaŋaliibi ní ki ŋá diciŋkpaandi. Diciŋkpaandi gbanti nìn cáá mpunyɔmu ní u dū tasa ki nyūntì-mu.
10U nìn dū kusɔŋkpaaŋŋu dikuŋkundee ki síiǹ kunimbɔtidii ŋŋaŋgiil pú, ki nákáǹ ŋgan pú nì ŋwìiń nyalaŋki faŋfakam.
11Uram nìn ŋá asambil nì peelab nì nsambiyaamu mun poon bi ŋáań tiwan ki cáa yàantée. U nìn túń ditundi din ubɔti Saloomɔn nìn tīī-u ú tɔ̄ kunimbɔtidiinee ki dóò, an dàkà yii: 12jaantalkub bili,
nì akɔl akuŋkun ŋin bi làá dūú páań jaantalkubee yilpuee,
nì tilaandi tili tin bi làá dūú bìin̄ akɔl ŋin pá jaantalkubee puee,
13nì greenaadi subiliŋ alaataa anaa ŋin bi làá dūú lúntí tilaandee puee, an dàkà yii kulaaŋŋu kamaa puee, bi nìn lúntì greenaadi subiliŋ gbanti ikuul ili pu ní ki bīiǹ jaantalkub kɔliŋee pu,
14nì tɔrɔkub nì tisɔn tin tɔ́kɔ́ tɔrɔkub gbanti puee,
15nì kusɔŋkpaaŋŋu dikuŋkundee,
nì inajaa saalaa nì ili in tú kusɔŋu gbantee,
16nì asambil nì peelab nì njiimu mun cáá anyin bi cáa sàatī tinanee nì tiwan tin pée kíǹ bi cáa tūǹ ditundee.
Tasa kúmɔntiiti ní Uram nìn dūu mɔ́ɔ́ tiwan gbanti kɔkɔ ki tīī ubɔti Saloomɔn ú dūú síiń ti-Dindaan Diikun. 17Jɔɔdan tantakalin, Sukooti nì Saartan timbilimmu kansikin ní ubɔti nìn yāntì bi dūntì tasa, kuyɔkɔu paamun ki mɔ́ɔ́ tiwan gbanti kɔkɔ. 18Tiwan tin Saloomɔn nìn ŋée nìn wīikí tikpil, an puee baa nìn gíti nyàab̀ kí béé tasa kúti tin bi dūu ŋá an tuuŋŋi gbanti kɔkɔee nyiŋfiŋu.
19Saloomɔn nìn gíti yāntì bi dū sindaariya ki ŋá ti-Dindaan Diiku wanti tin an bàlifēe.
Bi nìn dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ nsaraafan ŋun pu bi tùutī talaalubee,
ki dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ teebil un pu bi pāantí kpɔnɔb kí dūú sú Unimbɔtee,
20ní ki dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ fitilab tɔ́kɔŋkaati nì bi-fitilab ki síiǹ Circir páaa laŋki nyɔkɔpuee bí nīn tùutī-bi ki nóó nì bi nín síiǹ puee,
21ní ki dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ nsupumpukum nì fitilab nì tibabiti,
22ní ki dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ bɔlfitantab nì asambil ŋin poon bi ŋáań fatiku ki yàantée nì kɔŋkɔnnyɔkaabi nì nfantansamu.
Bi nìn dū sindaariya ní ki mɔ́ɔ́ kunimbɔtidii punyɔmmu nì mpunyɔmu mun bi dì kí kɔ́ Circir páaa laŋkee nì kunimbɔtidii dikpaaŋku.

english_text:
1 After the Lord's temple was finished, Solomon put in its storage rooms everything that his father David had dedicated to the Lord, including the gold and silver, and the objects used in worship.
Solomon Brings the Sacred Chest to the Temple
(1 Kings 8.1-13)
2-3 The sacred chest had been kept on Mount Zion, also known as the city of David. But Solomon decided to have the chest moved to the temple while everyone was in Jerusalem to celebrate the Festival of Shelters during the seventh month.
Solomon called together all the important leaders of Israel. 4-5Then the priests and the Levites picked up the sacred chest, the sacred tent, and the objects used for worship, and they carried them to the temple. 6Solomon and a crowd of people stood in front of the chest and sacrificed more sheep and cattle than could be counted.
7The priests carried the chest into the most holy place and put it under the winged creatures, 8whose wings covered both the chest and the poles used for carrying it. 9The poles were so long that they could be seen from just outside the most holy place, but not from anywhere else. And they stayed there from then on.
10 The only things kept in the chest were the two flat stones Moses had put there when the Lord made his agreement with the people of Israel at Mount Sinai, after bringing them out of Egypt.
11-13 The priests of every group had gone through the ceremony to make themselves clean and acceptable to the Lord. The Levite musicians, including Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun, and their sons and relatives, were wearing robes of fine linen. They were standing on the east side of the altar, playing cymbals, small harps, and other stringed instruments. One hundred and twenty priests were with these musicians, and they were blowing trumpets.
They were praising the Lord by playing music and singing:
“The Lord is good,
and his love never ends.”
Suddenly a cloud filled the temple as the priests were leaving the holy place. 14The Lord's glory was in that cloud, and the light from it was so bright that the priests could not stay inside to do their work.
translation_text:
1Míǹ ní ubɔti Saloomɔn nìn túń kunimbɔtidii tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ ki dóò. Míǹ boonee ní u yāntì bi cáań tiwan tin kɔkɔ u-baa Daafiidi nìn dūu sú ti-Dindaanee, an dàkà yii animbil nì sindaariya nì tiwan tikpil, ní bi dūu síiǹ ti-Dindaan Diiku nimbikpaafidiikun.
Bi dū Dipoondi Dakaau ki síiǹ kunimbɔtidiin
(Kpèè 1 Bib 8.1-13)
2Míǹ boonee ní ubɔti Saloomɔn yíiń Isirayeel tindaŋkpilib nì tinaakɔti kpilib kɔkɔ nì Isirayeel dicaŋŋi kpilib u-cee bí yòon̄ ti-Dindaan Poondi Dakaau Daafiidi Tiŋkin, an dàkà yii Siiyɔn jool pu, kí cáá cùnnì kunimbɔtidiin. 3Niinee ní Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ kóoǹ ki kpáfì ubɔti Saloomɔn cee kí jī uŋmaluluúti jiŋaaliu. 4Ŋyunti ŋun ní Isirayeel kpilib kɔkɔ bāańee ní Leefii yab yōoǹ Dipoondi Dakaau ki túǹ. 5Bisaraaŋaliibi Leefii yabee nìn yōoǹ ti-Dindaan Poondi Dakaau nì circir kɔŋkooŋŋu nì tiwan tin kɔkɔ bí ku-poonee ki túǹ. 6Ubɔti Saloomɔn nì Isirayeel samaau kɔkɔ kóoǹ ki kpáfì u-cee ti-Dindaan Poondi Dakaau nimbiin ní bi kūū ipii nì inaa ki ŋá saraabi an kaa cáá ŋkaan.
7Míǹ boonee ní bisaraaŋaliibi nín dū Dipoondi Dakaau ki kɔ́ǹ Circir Páaa laŋki diikun ki síiǹ u-paaŋŋu, keerubimbi feeŋyi taapu. 8Di sá yii keerubimbi nìn kpátì bi-feeŋyi mpaan ŋun bi nìn bɔ́ntì kí síiń Dipoondi Dakaauee yilpu, ní ki bīiǹ Dipoondi Dakaau nì idɔ in bi cáa tūntí-uee pu. 9Dakaa dɔi gbanti nìn fɔ̀kɔ̀ tiŋan, an puee a yaa nìn bí Circir laŋkee, a nìn wāĺ i-nyɔkɔ ní, ama a yaa nìn bí mmɔŋkee, an kaa nìn wāĺ. Idɔee dáá gbíntìi bí ki dāa sāā díǹ. 10Tiba kaa nìn bí Dipoondi Dakaau poon an yaa kaa sá ataŋkpee pilinti tili tin Mooyiisi nìn dūu ŋée. Ti-Dindaan nín nìn nyántì Isirayeel yab Eejipiti tiŋkin u nì bi ŋá mpèéyee ní Mooyiisi dū ataŋkpee pilinti gbanti ki ŋá poon Ooreeb jool pu.
11Bisaraaŋaliibi nìn nyáń Circir laŋki. Bisaraaŋaliibi bin kɔkɔ nìn bí niinee nìn ŋá bi-ba circir, kaa nóó nì bi-kitiŋi. 12Leefii yab bin nìn sá biwambɔɔliibi ki bí Asafi nì Eeman nì Yeedutun kitiŋinee nì bi-jipɔmbi nì bi-nabiyaamu nìn pēē iŋaabu in bí fálfalee bɔkutiŋ. Bi nìn yú nsaraafan ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú ki ŋúb́ cancakantib nì saŋgub nì tibati. Bisaraaŋaliibi binib dilaataal nì mmuŋku nìn yú ki kɔ́ĺ-bi ki búǹ akantán. 13Bikantámbunliibee nì biwambɔɔliibee nìn bíi bɔ̀ɔ́ dicilpu ki nyɔ́ŋkí ki pàkà ti-Dindaan. Ŋyunti ŋun bi bíi búǹ akantán ki bɔ̀ɔ́ cancakantib nì tiwambɔɔkaal tin kíǹee ki gà ilan ki nyɔ́ŋkí ti-Dindaan yii: «Di sá yii u ŋān̄, ní u-neendi bí kí nīn cá talkuee», ní ditagbandi diba dɔ́miń ki gbí ti-Dindaan Diikun. 14Ditagbandee puee, bisaraaŋaliibi kaa nìn gíti ŋūǹ kí sīĺ poon kí tɔ̄ bi-tundi, di sá yii ti-Dindaan nyooti nìn gbí u-diiku poon.

english_text:
1Solomon prayed:
“Our Lord, you said that you
would live in a dark cloud.
2Now I've built a glorious temple
where you can live forever.”
Solomon Speaks to the People
(1 Kings 8.14-21)
3Solomon turned toward the people standing there. Then he blessed them 4-6 and said:
Praise the Lord God of Israel! He brought his people out of Egypt long ago and later kept his promise to make my father David the king of Israel. The Lord also promised him that Jerusalem would be the city where his temple will be built, and now that promise has come true.
7When my father wanted to build a temple for the Lord God of Israel, 8the Lord said, “It's good that you want to build a temple where I can be worshiped. 9But you're not the one to do it. Your son will build the temple to honor me.”
10The Lord has done what he promised. I am now the king of Israel, and I've built a temple for the Lord our God. 11I've also put the sacred chest in the temple. And in that chest are the two flat stones on which is written the solemn agreement the Lord made with our ancestors when he rescued them from Egypt.
Solomon Prays at the Temple
(1 Kings 8.22-53)
12-13Earlier, Solomon had a bronze platform made that was about two meters square and over a meter high, and he put it in the center of the outer courtyard near the altar. Solomon stood on the platform facing the altar with everyone standing behind him. Then he lifted his arms toward heaven; he knelt down 14and prayed:
Lord God of Israel, no other god in heaven or on earth is like you!
You never forget the agreement you made with your people, and you are loyal to anyone who faithfully obeys your teachings. 15My father David was your servant, and today you have kept every promise you made to him.
16 You promised that someone from his family would always be king of Israel, if they do their best to obey you, just as he did. 17Please keep this promise you made to your servant David. 18 There's not enough room in all of heaven for you, Lord God. How could you possibly live on earth in this temple I have built? 19But I ask you to answer my prayer. 20 This is the temple where you have chosen to be worshiped. Please watch over it day and night and listen when I turn toward it and pray. 21I am your servant, and the people of Israel belong to you, and so whenever any of us look toward this temple and pray, answer from your home in heaven and forgive our sins.
22Suppose someone accuses a person of a crime, and the accused has to stand in front of the altar in your temple and say, “I swear I am innocent!” 23Listen from heaven and decide who is right. Then punish the guilty person and let the innocent one go free.
24Suppose your people Israel sin against you, and then an enemy defeats them. If they come to this temple and beg for forgiveness, 25listen from your home in heaven. Forgive them and bring them back to the land you gave their ancestors.
26Suppose your people sin against you, and you punish them by holding back the rain. If they stop sinning and turn toward this temple to pray in your name, 27listen from your home in heaven and forgive them. The people of Israel are your servants, so teach them to live right. And send rain on the land you promised them forever.
28Sometimes the crops may dry up or rot or be eaten by locusts or grasshoppers, and your people will be starving. Sometimes enemies may surround their towns, or your people will become sick with deadly diseases. 29Please listen when anyone in Israel truly feels sorry and sincerely prays with arms lifted toward your temple. 30You know what is in everyone's heart. So from your home in heaven answer their prayers, according to what they do and what is in their hearts. 31Then your people will worship you and obey you for as long as they live in the land you gave their ancestors.
32Foreigners will hear about you and your mighty power, and some of them will come to live among your people Israel. If any of them pray toward this temple, 33listen from your home in heaven and answer their prayers. Then everyone on earth will worship you, just as your own people Israel do, and they will know that I have built this temple in your honor.
34Sometimes you will order your people to attack their enemies. Then your people will turn toward this temple I have built for you in your chosen city, and they will pray to you. 35Answer their prayers from heaven and give them victory.
36Everyone sins. But when your people sin against you, suppose you get angry enough to let their enemies drag them away to foreign countries. 37-39Later, they may feel sorry for what they did and ask your forgiveness. Answer them when they pray toward this temple I have built for you in your chosen city, here in this land you gave their ancestors. From your home in heaven, listen to their sincere prayers and forgive your people who have sinned against you.
40 Lord God, hear us when we pray in this temple. 41 Come to your new home, where we have already placed the sacred chest, which is the symbol of your strength. I pray that when the priests announce your power to save people, those who are faithful to you will celebrate what you've done for them. 42Always remember the love you had for your servant David, so that you will not reject your chosen kings.
translation_text:
1Niinee ní Saloomɔn téeń yii:
«Ti-Dindaan, a nìn lēē yii a làá nīn kóò ditagbambɔndin.
2Ama man máń-si kudinyaaŋŋu nee,
kudii kun poon ní a làá nīn kóò talkuee!»
Saloomɔn sòon̄ ki dū kunimbɔtidii ki sú Unimbɔti
(Kpèè 1 Bib 8.14-21)
3Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nìn sí ní ubɔti fātì u-nimbiin ki túĺ-bi ní ki mēē ki bīiǹ bi-pu. 4U nìn bí yii: «Tí jāam̀maan ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu! Úǹ u-ba ŋá kii u nín nìn pōoǹ m-baa Daafiidi puee. U nìn bí-u yii: 5<Man di nyántì m-nibul Isirayeel Eejipiti tiŋkin. Kí yòon̄ ŋwiin gbantee, maa lēē Isirayeel timmu kɔkɔ kansikin kitiŋ kiba kin poon ní bi làá mā-mi kudii ḿ nīn lèekī m-ba ki dàkèe. Maa tí lēē unil ubɔ un nyáń u-bee ú nīn sá m-nibul Isirayeel kpootiliu. 6Ama m lēē Jeerusaleem kí nīn lèekī m-ba ki dàkà. M lēē sii Daafiidi mun á nīn sá m-nibul Isirayeel bɔtiu.> 7M-baa Daafiidi nìn cáá nlandɔkɔ kí mā kudii kí dū-ku kí sú ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu. 8Ama ti-Dindaan nìn bí-u yii: <A nín ká nlandɔkɔ yii a làá mā-mi kudiiyee, an ŋān̄ tikpil. 9Tin bée di sá yii an kaa sá sii di làá mā kudii gbanti, ama sii a-ba jipɔɔn un a màl̄ee di làá mā-mi kudii gbanti.> 10Kɔŋkɔnnee, ti-Dindaan nín nìn pōoǹ puee u ŋá míǹ. Di sá yii m fōō m-baa Daafiidi yil ki jíń Isirayeel tiŋki pu dibeel, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn lī puee. M máń kudii nee ki dū-ku ki sú ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu. 11M kpáàa bɔ́ntì Dipoondi Dakaau un poon ti-Dindaan poondi nyɔɔbuŋŋi kēe mpaan. Dipoondi gbantee, u nín nìn nyántì ti-naanjab Eejipiti tiŋkinee ní u nìn pōoǹ.»
Saloomɔn wimmeem
(Kpèè 1 Bib 8.22-53)
12Míǹ boonee ní Saloomɔn yíkìi síl̀ ti-Dindaan saraafaŋŋu nì Isirayeel yab bin kɔkɔ nìn kóoǹ ki kpáfèe nimbiin. U nìn yōoǹ u-ŋalii ki túĺ kutaa kí mèè. 13Di sá yii Saloomɔn nìn yāntì bi dū tasa kúti ki máń dikɔl ki síiǹ dicindi kansikin. Dikɔl gbanti waaŋŋu nìn sá meetab bili nì dijandi ní di-púuŋŋu sá meetab bili nì dijandi ní di-fɔkɔŋŋu sá meeta ubɔ nì dijandi. Saloomɔn nìn jɔ́m̀ ki tɔ́kɔǹ dikɔl pu ní ki tātìi gbāaǹ Isirayeel samaau kɔkɔ nimbiin. U nìn yōoǹ iŋal ki túĺ kutaa 14ki bí yii: «Ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu, unimbɔti ubɔ kaa bí yilpu àá kitiŋ pu ki bí kii siiyee. A ŋúb̀ a-poondi ki dàkà a-tɔntɔnliibi bin sí nì si nì dipɔbil dibee kulaŋŋaŋfitiiu. 15A nín nìn pōoǹ a-tɔntɔnliu m-baa Daafiidi yii a làá ŋá pu kí tīī-uee, a ŋá míǹ. Mbaamɔn tin a nìn pōoǹ-uee, sii a-ba ŋá míǹ ki tīī-u díǹ. 16Kɔŋkɔnnee, ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu, ŋá a nín nìn pōoǹ a-tɔntɔnliu m-baa Daafiidi yii a làá ŋá pu kí tīī-uee. A nìn bí-u yii: <A-naantiibi yaa nóó-mi ibaamɔn poon kii sii a-ba nín nóó-mi puee, ibaamɔn ní m tùkù-si, a-kpátam boonee, a-naantiibi kansikin ubɔ làá nīn pée sá ubɔti ní Isirayeel tiŋkin.» 17Míǹ puee ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu, m gbàam̄-si ní, ŋá kɔŋkɔnnee a nín nìn pōoǹ a-tɔntɔnliu m-baa Daafiidi yii a làá ŋá pu gbantee kí tīī-u!
18«Mimmee Unimbɔti ŋūǹ kí kɔ́ kitiŋ pu u nì binibaaa? Áli gba kutagbɔŋu nín wāā pu nee kaa bàn̄-si á kɔ́, ki dāa nín kàaǹ kudii kun m máń nee. 19Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, m-Dindaan m-Nimbɔtiu, pīlifì man a-tɔntɔnliu wimmeem nì m-gbaamii! Pīlifì m-kuŋkuuntii nì m-wimmeem min man a-tɔntɔnliu bíi mèé-si díǹ neeyee! 20A-nimbikpeeŋu ń nīn pée cɔ́ kudii nee pu ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu. Ŋú nīn pée cɔ́ mpaan ŋun pu a nìn sòon̄ yii: <M-yindi làá nīn bí niin> nee pu. Pīlifì ŋwimmeem min m bí doo ki mèé-si nee. 21Pīlifì man a-tɔntɔnliu nì Isirayeel, a-nibul wimmeem min ti bí doo ki mèé-si nee. Pīlifiǹ-ti doooo yilpu laakin a kóòyee. Pīlifiǹ-ti kí dū ti-kpitii kí pɔ̄-ti.
22«Ubɔ yaa yīntiǹ u-juti, bi ŋūǹ kí lì yii ú pùtī yii u yaa ká mbusu ń lítí u-pu. Udaan yaa lafun dɔ́miń kudii nee poon, a-saraafaŋŋu nyɔkɔpu ki pūtèe, 23á pīlifì doooo yilpu kí kpèè tibɔti gbanti kí sòoǹ a-tɔntɔnliibi bɔti. Á kpɔ̀ dibɔkpil daan bɔti kí dáaĺ u-tafal, ní kí pɔ̀ un bɔti ŋān̄ee báà ŋma ń béé yii u sá maanyiiba.
24«Isirayeel yab a-nibul yaa yīntiǹ-si ní bi-nannanliibi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi, ní bi fātìi gítìń a-cee, ki nyɔ́ŋkì-si, ki mēē-si ní ki gbāam̀-si kudii nee poonee, 25sii ti-Dindaan, á pīlifì a-nibul Isirayeel yab doooo yilpu, kí dū bi-kpitii kí pɔ̄-bi, ní kí fàtīí gíiǹní-bi kitiŋ kin a nìn dūu tīī bi-naanjabee poon.
26«A-nibul yaa yīntiǹ-si ní a dū kutaa ki pīiǹ utaa kaa ti bíi nì, ní bi fātì bi-ba ki túĺ mpaan nee pú, ki mēē ki nyɔ́ŋkì a-yindi, ní ki fātì bi-boon ki tīī bi-kpitii a nín dáaĺ bi-tafal pueeyee, 27sii ti-Dindaan, á pīlifiǹ a-tɔntɔnliibi Isirayeel yab doooo yilpu. Á dū bi-kpitii kí pɔ̄-bi, kí dàkà-bi nsammɔnti ŋun bi máaǹ kí nóóyee, ní kí yàntī utaa ń nì a-tiŋki nee pu, kitiŋ kin ní a dūu tīī a-nibul án nīn sá bi-fakalee.
28«Ŋkùm àá bìlbil kúm yaa jéetì kitiŋ nee pu, àá tikpaajin kaa láá bīń ní ki kūń àá ki sūū, àá inaakitoon nì inaaki di ŋmɔ́ ki bíil̀ tikpaajin, àá bi-nannanliibi di māntìi tú bi-timmu kí já nì bi, àá an yaa pée sá tibumbun àá igbaŋween iŋyee, 29Isirayeel yab kansikin ubɔ àá a-nibul Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ di yaa béè tin bāań-bee, ki yōoǹ bi-ŋalii ki túĺ Kudii nee watil pú ki mēē-si àá ki gbāam̀-see, 30sii ti-Dindaan, á pīlifiǹ-bi doooo yilpu laakin a kóoǹnée kí dū bi-kpitii kí pɔ̄-bi, ní kí ŋá kí tīī báà ŋma kii an nín máaǹ puee, di sá yii a nyí báà ŋma pɔbil poon bɔti. 31Ŋá míǹ án nín làá ŋá pu ní Isirayeel yab ń fàŋkì-si iwiin in kɔkɔ bi cáá kí kàl̄ kitiŋ kin a tīī bi-naanjabee puee.
32«Unicaan un kaa sá a-nibul Isirayeel yab kansikin ubɔee yaa nyánní kitindandatiin ki dɔ́miń a-yindi pu, di sá yii u gbìl̄ bi sòon̄ a-yiŋkpaandi nì a-pɔŋkpaaŋŋu pu, ní ki dɔ́miń míǹ ki mēē-si kudii nee poonee, 33sii ti-Dindaan, á pīlifiǹ-u doooo yilpu laakin a kóoǹnée. Á ŋá u nín bālifì-si puee kí tīī-u. A yaa ŋá míǹ, kitiŋ pu nib kɔkɔ làá béé a-yindi, kí fàŋkì-si kii Isirayeel yab nín fàŋkí-si puee, ní bí béé yii a lafun bí kudii kun m máń nee ni.
34«A yaa tīī a-nibul Isirayeel yab mara yii bí cù kí já nì bi-nannanliibi, ní bi fātì bi-ba ki túĺ kitiŋ kin a lēē nee nì kudii kun m máń-si nee watil pú ki mēēyee, 35á pīlifiǹ bi-wimmeem nì bi-gbaamii doooo yilpu, ní kí tīī-bi dijajil.
36«An ŋūǹ kí ŋá yii Isirayeel yab yīntiǹ-si, di sá yii unil ubɔ kpá kaa yìntī. Bi yaa ŋá míǹ ní a gíí bi-pu diŋuul ki yāntì bi-nannanliibi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi ki cúú-bi ki cūnnì bi-tiŋki kin dátèe àá kin kaa dátèe ni kuyuŋu, 37ní bi yaa kíĺ ki bíi dàkafī, ki kpántì bi-bimbim, ki gbāam̀-si kitiŋ gbanti poon ki lī yii: <Ti ŋá ikpiti, ti yīntì, ti jíń dibɔkpil>, 38ní bi-nannanliibi tiŋki gbanti poonee, bi fātìi gítìń a-cee nì bi-pɔbil kɔkɔ nì bi-naŋki kɔkɔ, ní ki fātì bi-ba ki túĺ kitiŋ kin a tīī bi-naanjab nì kitiŋ kin ní a lēē nee nì kudii kun ní m máń ki tīī-si nee ki mēē-see, 39sii ti-Dindaan, á pīlifiǹ-bi doooo yilpu laakin a kóoǹnée. Pīlifì bi-wimmeem nì bi-gbaamii kí jòò-bi, kí dū bi nín yīntiǹ-si puee kí pɔ̄-bi.
40«Ŋúbití a-nimbiliŋ, m-Nimbɔtiu. Pīlifì m-wimmeem min m bíi mèé-si mpaan nee puee.
41Kɔŋkɔnnee, ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti, yīkìm̄,
dāan̄ kí nīn bí a-ŋuŋfil paaŋŋu pu,
sii nì a-dakaau un poon a-pɔŋŋu bée.
Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti, yàntī a-saraaŋaliibi ń dū difiil kí pèen̄ kii tiwampeeŋkaalee!
Yàntī bin yú nì si deedeeyee ń nīn fàal̀ a-ŋanti pu.
42Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti, taa dū ubɔti un sii a-ba lēēyee kí fá.
Téetí tiŋan tin kɔkɔ a ŋá ki tīī a-tɔntɔnliu Daafiidee pu!»

english_text:
Solomon Dedicates the Temple
(1 Kings 8.62-66)
1 As soon as Solomon finished praying, fire came down from heaven and burned up the offerings. The Lord's dazzling glory then filled the temple, 2and the priests could not go in.
3 When the crowd of people saw the fire and the Lord's glory, they knelt down and worshiped the Lord. They prayed:
“The Lord is good,
and his love never ends.”
4-5Solomon and the people dedicated the temple to the Lord by sacrificing 22,000 cattle and 120,000 sheep. 6Everybody stood up during the ceremony. The priests were in their assigned places, blowing their trumpets. And the Levites faced them, playing the musical instruments that David had made for them to use when they praised the Lord for his never-ending love.
7On that same day, Solomon dedicated the courtyard in front of the temple and got it ready to be used for worship. The bronze altar he had made was too small, so he used the courtyard to offer sacrifices to please the Lord and grain sacrifices, and also to send up in smoke the fat from the other offerings.
8For 7 days, Solomon and the crowd celebrated the Festival of Shelters, and people came from as far away as the Egyptian Gorge in the south and Lebo-Hamath in the north. 9Then on the next day, everyone came together for worship. They had celebrated a total of 14 days, 7 days for the dedication of the altar and 7 more days for the festival. 10Then on the twenty-third day of the seventh month, Solomon sent everyone home. They left very happy because of all the good things the Lord had done for David and Solomon, and for his people Israel.
The Lord Appears to Solomon Again
(1 Kings 9.1-9)
11The Lord's temple and Solomon's palace were now finished. In fact, everything Solomon had planned to do was completed.
12Some time later, the Lord appeared to Solomon in a dream and said:
I heard your prayer, and I have chosen this temple as the place where sacrifices will be offered to me.
13Suppose I hold back the rain or send locusts to eat the crops or make my people suffer with deadly diseases. 14If my own people will humbly pray and turn back to me and stop sinning, then I will answer them from heaven. I will forgive them and make their land fertile once again. 15I will hear the prayers made in this temple, 16because it belongs to me, and this is where I will be worshiped forever. I will never stop watching over it.
17Your father David obeyed me, and now, Solomon, you must do the same. Obey my laws and teachings, 18 and I will keep my solemn promise to him that someone from your family will always be king of Israel.
19But if you or any of the people of Israel disobey my laws or start worshiping foreign gods, 20I will pull you out of this land I gave you. I will desert this temple where I said I would be worshiped, so that people everywhere will think it is only a joke and will make fun of it. 21This temple is now magnificent. But when these things happen, everyone who walks by it will be shocked and will ask, “Why did the Lord do such a terrible thing to his people and to this temple?” 22Then they will answer, “It was because the people of Israel rejected the Lord their God, who rescued their ancestors from Egypt, and they started worshiping other gods.”
translation_text:
Saraabi bin bi ŋá ki tīī ti-Dindaanee
(Kpèè 1 Bib 8.62-66)
1Saloomɔn mēē míǹ ki dóòyee ní ŋŋmi nyánní yilpu ki dɔ́miń ki wùn̄ bisaraawɔkaabi nì mpèé saraabee. Ti-Dindaan nyooti nìn gbí kunimbɔtidii. 2Bisaraaŋaliibi kaa nìn gíti ŋūǹ kí kɔ́ kunimbɔtidiin, di sá yii ti-Dindaan nyooti nìn gbí-kù. 3Isirayeel yab bin kɔkɔ nìn bí niinee nìn ká ŋŋmi nyánní yilpu ki kpákatìń ní ti-Dindaan nyooti jìliŋkī kunimbɔtidiin. Niinee ní bi tātìi gbāaǹ bi-nimbiiŋyi tūū kitiŋ ki jáaḿ-u ki nyɔ́ŋkí-u ki lì yii: «U ŋān̄ ní u-neendi bí kí nīn cá jaanjaan.»
4Ubɔti saloomɔn nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ kpáfì ki ŋá ti-Dindaan saraabi. 5Saloomɔn nìn kūū inaa kutukub mmuŋku nì bili, ní ki kūū ipii nì iŋoobu kutukub dilaataal nì mmuŋku ki ŋá mpèé saraau. Bi nín ŋá pu ki dū kunimbɔtidii ki sú ti-Dindaanee dee. 6Bisaraaŋaliibi nìn yú bi-tundi laŋki. Leefii yab nìn ŋúb́ tiwambɔɔkaal tin ubɔti Daafiidi nìn yāntì bi kpítì ki tīī-bee ki nyɔ́ŋkí ti-Dindaan ki lì yii: «Di sá yii u-neendi bí ní ki cá jaanjaan.» Daafiidi di nìn ŋmàn̄ nlan gbanti ki tīī-bi. Bisaraaŋaliibi nìn yú ki túĺ-bi ki búǹ akantán ní Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ yíkìi yúl̀. 7Niinee Saloomɔn dū dicindi din bí kunimbɔtidii nyɔkɔpuee ki sú ti-Dindaan. Di sá yii niin ní u nìn ŋá saraawɔkaa nì tijimpin saraabi nì mpèé saraabi kpam, kun puee tasa saraafaŋŋu ŋun nìn bí kunimbɔtidii punyɔkɔki caŋinee kaa nìn náaǹ bí ŋmā kí wà an pu saraawɔkaa nì tijimpin saraabi nì mpèé saraabi kpam.
8Ŋyunti gbanti ní Saloomɔn nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ kpáfìi jíń tibìń jiŋaaliu. An nìn sá dinikitikpaandi ní. Binib nìn nyánní doooo Leeboo-Amaati, kitiŋ ŋgan pú ki cáa sāā Eejipiti buŋŋu kitiŋ ŋgiil pú. Bi nìn jíń jiŋaal gbanti iwiin iluli ní. 9Iwiin inii dalee ní bi kóoǹ ki kpáfì ki jáam̀ ti-Dindaan. Mimmee bi nìn dū iwiin iluli ní ki jíń kunimbɔtidii jiŋaaliu ní ki dū iwiin iluli ki jíń tibìń jiŋaaliu. 10Míǹ boonee, uŋmaluluúti iwiin mmuŋku nì ita dalee ní Saloomɔn yāntì Isirayeel yab nín kùǹ bi-dumpu. Bi nìn nín kùǹ nì mmɔn nì dipɔɔpindi, kun puee ti-Dindaan nìn dàkā u-tɔntɔnliu Daafiidi nì Saloomɔn nì u-nibul Isirayeel yab kulaŋŋaŋfitiiu.
Ti-Dindaan fātìi lēē u-ba ki dàkā Saloomɔn nliliitiim
(Kpèè 1 Bib 9.1-9, 2 Kroo 1.7-12)
11Saloomɔn nìn máń ti-Dindaan Diiku nì úǹ u-ba naakooku nì tin u nìn pée là kí mēe ki dóò. 12Míǹ boonee ní ti-Dindaan nyántì u-ba ki dàkā-u kunyeeu ní ki bí-u yii: «M gbìl̄ a-wimmeem ní ki lēē kudii nee kú nīn sá mpaan ŋun pu bi làá nīn ŋáań saraabi ki tìì-mee. 13An ŋūǹ kí bàń yii m dū kutagbɔŋu ki pīiǹ ní utaa kaa ti bíi nì. An tí ŋūǹ kí bàń mun yii m tīī inaakitoon mara í dāan̄ kí ŋmɔ́ kitiŋ nee kpaajinti, àá m cáań bìlbil kúm ki tɔ́ m-nibul pu. 14M-nibul din pu bi yíì m-yindee nib yaa sīntì bi-ba taapu, ki mēē, ki nyàab̄-mi ní ki dū bi-saŋkpitii ki fée, man làá pīlifiǹ-bi doooo yilpu, kí dū bi-kpitii kí pɔ̄-bi, ní kí fàtīí tīī bi-tiŋki ki-gaajati. 15M-nimbiliŋ làá nīn kpítì ní m-tafaliŋ ń nīn píĺ ki cí kí pīlifì ŋwimmeem min kamaa bi làá pée mèè kudii nee poonee. 16Too, m lēē kudii nee ki dū-ku ki sú m-ba kí nīn lèekī m-ba ki dàkà ku-poon kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaan. M-nimbikpeeŋu làá nīn cɔ́ ku-pu, ní m-pɔbil ń nīn kā ku-pu baabadal. 17Ama siiyee, nín̄ nóó-mi kii a-baa Daafiidee. Nín̄ ŋáań tin kɔkɔ m kpáafì-see, ní kí nīn ŋúb́ m-bɔkpaaŋi nì m-koobiliŋ. 18A yaa ŋá míǹ, m làá tīī a-beel mpɔn kii m nín nìn pōoǹ a-baa Daafiidi puee. M nìn bí-u yii: <A-kpátam boonee, a-naantiibi kansikin ubɔ làá nīn pée sá ubɔti ní Isirayeel tiŋkin.> 19Ama sii nì a-nibul yaa fātì ni-boon ki tīī-mi, ní kaa ŋúb́ m-marab nì m-koobiliŋ ŋin m tīī-nee, ní ki cūtìi nóó awaa ki gbàantí ŋi-taapuee, 20m làá jà-ni kitiŋ kin pu m tīī-nee. M làá fàtī m-boon kí tīī kudii kun m dūu sú m-ba nee. Anibul kɔkɔ làá dāá nīn ŋúb́ Isirayeel ki lāā ki bèel̄. 21Kudii nee sá díǹ pu nee kukpaaŋŋu. Ama binib bin làá dāá jītí kudii nee caŋinee làá dāá bàkatī ní kí bàlifì yii: <Ba yì-tì ní ti-Dindaan nín ŋá kitiŋ nee nì kudii nee míǹ?> 22Ní bí dāá kíí-bi yii: <Kun yì-tèe di sá yii Isirayeel yab dū ti-Dindaan bi-baabi Nimbɔtiu un di nyántìń-bi Eejipiti tiŋkinee ki fá. Bi dū bi-ba ki yá ki nákáǹ awaa ki gbāaǹ ŋi-taapu ki jáam̀-ŋi. An pu ní ti-Dindaan yāntì nnaabu nee jéetì bi-pu.>»

english_text:
Other Things Solomon Did
(1 Kings 9.10-28)
1It took 20 years for the Lord's temple and Solomon's palace to be built. 2After that, Solomon had his workers rebuild the towns that Hiram had given him. Then Solomon sent Israelites to live in those towns.
3Solomon attacked and captured the town of Hamath-Zobah. 4He ordered his workers to build the town of Tadmor in the desert and some towns in Hamath where he could keep his supplies. 5He strengthened Upper Beth-Horon and Lower Beth-Horon by adding walls and gates that could be locked. 6He did the same thing to the town of Baalath and to the cities where he kept supplies, chariots, and horses. Solomon ordered his workers to build whatever he wanted in Jerusalem, Lebanon, and anywhere else in his kingdom.
7-9Solomon did not force the Israelites to do his work. Instead, they were his soldiers, officers, army commanders, and cavalry troops. But he did make slaves of the Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites who were living in Israel. These were the descendants of those foreigners the Israelites did not destroy, and they remained Israel's slaves.
10Solomon appointed 250 officers to be in charge of his workers.
11Solomon's wife, the daughter of the king of Egypt, moved from the part of Jerusalem called David's City to her new palace that Solomon had built. The sacred chest had been kept in David's City, which made his palace sacred, and so Solomon's wife could no longer live there.
12Solomon offered sacrifices to the Lord on the altar he had built in front of the temple porch. 13 He followed the requirements that Moses had given for sacrifices offered on the Sabbath, on the first day of each month, the Festival of Thin Bread, the Harvest Festival, and the Festival of Shelters.
14Solomon then assigned the priests and the Levites their duties at the temple, and he followed the instructions that his father, the man of God, had given him. Some of the Levites were to lead music and help the priests in their duties, and others were to guard the temple gates 15and the storage rooms. The priests and Levites followed these instructions exactly.
16Everything Solomon had planned to do was now finished—from the laying of the temple's foundation to its completion.
17Solomon went to Ezion-Geber and Eloth, two Edomite towns on the Red Sea. 18Hiram sent him ships and some of his experienced sailors. They went with Solomon's own sailors to the country of Ophir and brought back more than 15 tons of gold for Solomon.
translation_text:
Atuun ŋin Saloomɔn gíti túńee aba
(Kpèè 1 Bib 9.10-28)
1Abin mmuŋku ní Saloomɔn nìn dūu máń ti-Dindaan Diiku nì úǹ u-ba diiku. 2U nìn fātìi máń ntimu mun Tiir bɔtiu Yiiram nìn tīī-uee. U nìn cáań Isirayeel yab ki kāaǹ ntimuee ni. 3Míǹ boonee ní Saloomɔn cūtìi jáń ki fōō Amati-Sooba tiŋki. 4U nìn fātìi máń Tadimɔɔr tiŋki kuteeun nì ntimu mun nìn bí Amati tiŋkpaaŋkin bi kpáafí u-jintee. 5U nìn fātìi máń Beeti-Oorɔn tiŋki kin bí yilpu púee nì Beeti-Oorɔn tiŋki kin bí taapu púee. U nìn máń agun ki tú ntimu gbanti ní mu cáá punuubi nì tikpàlkaal. 6U nìn gíti ŋá Balaati tiŋki nì ntimu mun poon u nìn kpáafí u-jinti nì u-janjatɔrɔkub nì u-taamuuyee míǹ ní. Saloomɔn nìn pée máń tin ní u nìn lèe ní Jeerusaleem tiŋkin nì Leebanɔn jool pu nì ntimu mun kɔkɔ nìn bí u-taapuee.
7Eeti yab nì Amɔɔr yab nì Peeriisi yab nì Eefi yab nì Jeebusi yab biba nìn kíǹ Isirayeel tiŋkin, bíǹ gbanti kaa nìn sá Isirayeel tindambiyaamu. 8Bi nìn gbíntìi bí kun puee Isirayeel yab kaa nìn ŋúń ki kūū ki céetì-bi. Saloomɔn nìn dū bi-naantiibi ki ŋá diwɔ́bil tundin ki dāa sāā díǹ. 9Ama Saloomɔn kaa nìn dū Isirayeel yab ki ŋá diwɔ́bil tundi gbantin. Bíǹ di nìn sá u-janjaliibi nì bijanjakpilib nì bin ŋàal̀ janjatɔrɔkubee nì bitanjakaliibi. 10Kɔmandambi nìn lēē bikàliŋkpilib alaataa ali nì imuŋku ili nì saalaa bí nīn kpèé bin bí ki tūǹ Saloomɔn tuuŋŋee.
11Saloomɔn nìn yāntì u-nimpuu Faaroo bisal nyáń Daafiidi Tiŋkin ki cūtìi kɔ́ kudii kun u nìn máń ki tīī-uee ni. Di sá u nìn lī yii: «M-nimpuu kaa máaǹ kí nīn kóò Isirayeel bɔtiu Daafiidi cindin. Di sá yii adiin ŋin poon bi dū ti-Dindaan Dakaau ki yóoǹee sá circir diiŋŋi ní.»
12Saloomɔn nìn ŋáań ti-Dindaan bisaraawɔkaabi nsaraafan ŋun u nìn máń ki tīī-u ŋu bí kunimbɔtidii nyɔkɔpuee ní. 13Kii Mooyiisi nín nìn síiǹ mara bí nīn ŋáań ŋwiin kamaa puee, u nìn ŋáań ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa saraabi, ki ŋáań uŋmal kamaa wimpeekaaŋu saraabi nì bijiŋaakpaambi bita bin bi nìn jīǹee saraabi. Jiŋaalib gbanti di sá jiŋaal un bi jīǹ ki ŋmóò kpɔnɔb bin kaa cáá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee nì Pantikooti jiŋaaliu nì Tibìń jiŋaaliu. 14Kii u-baa Daafiidi nín nìn lēē pu ki síiǹee, Saloomɔn nìn tīī bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab bi-tuuŋŋi nín sá pu kunimbɔtidiinee, ki nóó nì bi-kitiŋi. Leefii yab biba tundi di nìn sá bí nīn nyɔ́ŋkí ti-Dindaan baabadal, àá kí tūtuǹ bisaraaŋaliibi bi-tuuŋŋi poon. U nìn yāntì bipunyɔɔciitiliibi kitiŋi ŋin nìn cí kunimbɔtidii punyɔmmuee mun kíĺ bi-tundi. Unimbɔti niliu Daafiidi nín nìn síiǹ mara bí ŋá puee dee. 15Daafiidi nín nìn síiǹ mara un bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab tuuŋŋi pu, nì kunimbɔtidii nimbiliŋ pu puee, míǹ deedee ní bi nìn ŋá.
16Míǹ ní Saloomɔn nìn túń u-tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ ki dóò, kí yòon̄ ŋwiin ŋun u bíl̀ kunimbɔtidii nyeelee ki cáa sāā bi nín máń-ku ki dóòyee. Saloomɔn nìn máń kunimbɔtidii ki dóò.
17Niinee Saloomɔn nín cá Eesiiyɔn-Geebeer nì Eelaati timmun. Eelaati tiŋki gbanti nìn bí Tikati Mɔɔl gbandi, Eedoom tiŋkin ní. 18Yiiram nìn dū u-tɔntɔnliibi bimeelaŋaaliliibi bin nyí tiŋku bɔti tiŋanee ki tú bí tūtuǹ Saloomɔn tɔntɔnliibi. Bimeelaŋaaliliibi gbanti nì Saloomɔn yab nìn cūtì Oofiiri tiŋkin ki nyàab̄ sindaariya tɔnnib saalaa nì bili ki cáa cūnnì ki tīī ubɔti Saloomɔn.

english_text:
The Queen of Sheba Visits Solomon
(1 Kings 10.1-13)
1 The Queen of Sheba heard how famous Solomon was, so she went to Jerusalem to test him with difficult questions. She took along several of her officials, and she loaded her camels with gifts of spices, jewels, and gold. When she arrived, she and Solomon talked about everything she could think of. 2He answered every question, no matter how difficult it was.
3-4The Queen was amazed at Solomon's wisdom. She was breathless when she saw his palace, the food on his table, his officials, all his servants in their uniforms, and the sacrifices he offered at the Lord's temple. 5She said:
Solomon, in my own country I had heard about your wisdom and all you've done. 6But I didn't believe it until I saw it with my own eyes! And there's so much I didn't hear about. You are greater than I was told. 7Your people and officials are lucky to be here where they can listen to the wise things you say.
8I praise the Lord your God. He is pleased with you and has made you king of Israel. God loves the people of this country and will never desert them, so he has given them a king who will rule fairly and honestly.
9The Queen of Sheba gave Solomon more than four tons of gold, a large amount of jewels, and the best spices anyone had ever seen.
10-12In return, Solomon gave her everything she wanted—even more than she had given him. Then she and her officials went back to their own country.
Solomon's Wealth
(1 Kings 10.14-29)
Hiram's and Solomon's sailors brought gold, juniper wood, and jewels from the country of Ophir. Solomon used the wood to make steps for the temple and palace, and harps and other stringed instruments for the musicians. Nothing like these had ever been made in Judah.
13Solomon received almost 23 tons of gold each year, 14not counting what the merchants and traders brought him. The kings of Arabia and the leaders of Israel also gave him gold and silver.
15Solomon made 200 gold shields that weighed over three kilograms each. 16He also made 300 smaller gold shields that weighed almost two kilograms, and he put these shields in his palace in Forest Hall.
17His throne was made of ivory and covered with pure gold. 18It had a gold footstool attached to it and armrests on each side. There was a statue of a lion on each side of the throne, 19and there were two lion statues on each of the six steps leading up to the throne. No other throne in the world was like Solomon's.
20Solomon's cups and dishes in Forest Hall were made of pure gold, because silver was almost worthless in those days.
21Solomon had a lot of seagoing ships. Every three years he sent them out with Hiram's ships to bring back gold, silver, and ivory, as well as monkeys and peacocks.
22Solomon was the richest and wisest king in the world. 23-24Year after year, other kings came to hear the wisdom God had given him. And they brought gifts of silver and gold, as well as clothes, weapons, spices, horses, and mules.
25 Solomon had 4,000 stalls for his horses and chariots, and he owned 12,000 horses that he kept in Jerusalem and other towns.
26 He ruled all the nations from the Euphrates River in the north to the land of Philistia in the south, as far as the border of Egypt.
27While Solomon was king, there was silver everywhere in Jerusalem, and cedar was as common as the sycamore trees in the western foothills. 28 Solomon's horses were brought in from other countries, including Musri.
Solomon Dies
(1 Kings 11.41-43)
29Everything else Solomon did while he was king is written in the records of Nathan the prophet, Ahijah the prophet from Shiloh, and Iddo the prophet who wrote about Jeroboam son of Nebat. 30After Solomon had ruled 40 years from Jerusalem, 31he died and was buried in the city of his father David. His son Rehoboam then became king.
translation_text:
Sabaa nimpubɔtiu māntì Saloomɔn pu
(1 Bib 10.1-13)
1Sabaa nimpubɔtiu nìn gbìl̄ Saloomɔn nín nyáń diyindi puee. U nìn dɔ́miń Jeerusaleem kí pɔ́ɔǹ-u ipɔɔn kí màkan̄-u kí kpèè. U nì dinikitikpaandi di nìn dɔ́miń ki kpáaǹ igutaamu in tú talaalub nì sindaariya tikpil nì ataŋkpamɔntee. U bāań Saloomɔn ceeyee ní ki bālifì-u tibɔti tin kɔkɔ nìn pée kā u-pɔbilinee. 2Saloomɔn nìn pée kíí-u tin kɔkɔ u nìn bālifì-uee ní. Tiba kaa nìn bí ki pɔ̄ɔ̄ ki tīī-u waa ŋúń ki kíí. 3Sabaa tiŋki nimpubɔtiu nín ká Saloomɔn ciiŋyi nì kudii kun u máńee 4nì tijin tin tɔ́kɔ́ u-teebiliu puee nì u-tɔntɔnliibi kɔŋkooŋyi nì u-tɔntɔnliibi bin tìì-u tijin u jīǹ nì nnyim u nyùee wampeeŋkaati nì saraabi bin u nìn ŋáań kunimbɔtidiinee ní an ŋá-u bitii waa ti nyí tin poon u bée. 5Niinee ní u bí ubɔti yii: «Tin m gbìl̄ m-tiŋkin a-tuuŋŋi pu nì a-ciiŋyi puee lafun sá mbaamɔn ní. 6Ama maa nìn fōō ki kíí, see m nín dɔ́miń m-ba ki ká nì m-nimbilee. Tin bi máafì-mee kaa bàn̄ tin m ká nee dijandi gba. A-ciiŋyi jítiǹ tin m gbìl̄ee pu kpataaa. 7A-nib nì a-tɔntɔnliibi bin bí a-nimbiin baabadal ki pílifí a-ciiŋyi nyɔɔbuŋŋee bí mmɔnneeee! 8Tí nyɔ̄ŋkì ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu un di lēē-si á kàl̄ Isirayeel tiŋki pu dibeelee! Kun puee u néeń Isirayeel kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaan ní, an pu ní u dū-si ki kāaǹ dibeel á yàntī tin bí deedeeyee nì ibaamɔn ń nīn bí.»
9Míǹ boonee ní Sabaa tiŋki nimpubɔtiu tīī ubɔti Saloomɔn sindaariya tɔnnib bita nì dijandi nì talaalub tikpil nì ataŋkpamɔnti. Sabaa nimpubɔtiu nín nìn tīī ubɔti Saloomɔn talaalub puee, baa ti pée ká an talaalub bulifi kɔ́ Isirayeel tiŋkin ki ká.
10Kí kūtì muee, Yiiram tɔntɔnliibi nì Saloomɔn yab nìn cáań sindaariya Oofiiri tiŋkin nì santaal dɔi tikpil tikpil nì ataŋkpamɔnti. 11Ubɔti nìn dū idɔ gbanti ki ŋá jaantalkub ki tíkiǹ ti-Dindaan Diiku nì kubɔtinaakoou, ní ki nìn lēē ki kpítì tibati ki tīī u-laŋgaaliibi. Baa nìn pée ká míǹ Juuda tiŋkin dalba dalba.
12Ubɔti Saloomɔn mun nìn tīī Sabaa nimpubɔtiu tin kɔkɔ u nìn là ki bālifèe. Tin u nìn tīī-uee nìn jítiǹ tin unimpubɔti nìn cáańee pu kpataaa. Míǹ boonee ní u nì u-tɔntɔnliibi nín gítí bi-tiŋkin.
Ubɔti Saloomɔn gaajati
13Dibimbaantiil poonee, sindaariya un bi nìn cáań ki tīī ubɔti Saloomɔŋyee nìn nyáń tɔnnib mmuŋku ní, 14ní kí nín kūtì bibantiliibi nì binyampoobi nín nìn cāabìń sindaariya un ki pà patantibee. Arabii bɔtiibi kɔkɔ nì Isirayeel tiŋkpaammu gɔminab nìn cāabìń sindaariya nì animbil ki tìì Saloomɔn.
15Ubɔti Saloomɔn nìn yāntì bi dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ agbampɔɔ akpaan alaataa ali. Bi nìn dū sindaariya kiiloobi biluu ní ki mɔ́ɔ́ digbampɔɔl kamaa. 16U nìn gíti dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ agbampɔɔ ŋwaamu alaataa ata. Bi nìn dū sindaariya kiiloo ubɔ nì dijandi ní ki mɔ́ɔ́ digbampɔɔl kamaa. Ubɔti nìn dū agbampɔɔyee ki síiǹ kudii kun bi yíì yii <Leebanɔn Pɔɔkuee> poon ní.
17Ubɔti nìn gíti kpítì dibeejal dikpaandi diba ní ki dū sindaariyamɔnti ki nyūntì ní ki dū kunti nyiŋŋi ki nákáǹ nákáǹ. 18Dibeejalee nìn cáá akɔl ŋin pu bi tà ki jɔ́ḿ-dèe aluu, ní ki cáá laakin ataa tɔ̄kɔntée an sá sindaariya. Bi nìn kpítì gbikintib bili ki síiǹ laakin bi pāantí iŋalee. 19Gbikintib nìn bí saalaa nì bili ní ki bí akɔl aluuyee nín kúntí puee. Baa nìn pée kpítì dibeejal diba míǹ dibeel diba poon ki ká.
20Ubɔti Saloomɔn kɔŋkɔnnyɔkaabi kɔkɔ nìn sá sindaariya ŋma ní, ní asambil ŋin bí <Leebanɔn Pɔɔku> diikunee nìn sá sindaariyamɔnti ŋma. Baa nìn dù animbil kúti kí ŋá tiba, di sá yii Saloomɔn yuntiŋuee, animbil kúti kaa nìn cáá kunyampoou. 21Di sá yii ubɔti nìn cáá meelab Taarsiisi tiŋkin. Yiiram meelaŋaaliliibi di nìn ŋàal̀-bi. Abin ata poon diba puee, meelab gbanti nìn cāabìń sindaariya nì animbil kúti nì kunti nyiŋŋi nì ilantan nì ikooŋaan.
22Ubɔti Saloomɔn nìn jítiǹ kitiŋ pu bɔtiibi kɔkɔ tigaajati poon nì iciin poon. 23Kitiŋ pu bɔtiibi kɔkɔ nìn nyàab̀ kí ká Saloomɔn kí ŋmā kí pīlifì iciin in Unimbɔti nìn tīī-uee. 24Bi yaa nìn dòońee, báà ŋma nìn cāabìń animbil kúti wanti nì sindaariya wanti nì tiwampeeŋkaal nì tijanjawan nì talaalub nì itaamu nì imamboon ki pūǹ-u. Dibindi kamaayee, binib nìn pée ŋáań míǹ ní.
25Saloomɔn nìn cáá itaamu nì janjatɔrɔkub naabakati kutukub binaa, ní ki cáá itaamu kutukub saalaa nì bili. Tijanjawan gbanti tiba nìn bí ntimu mun poon ní ajanjanaapaa bée, ní tiba mun bí u-cee Jeerusaleem. 26Bibɔtiibi bin nìn bí kí yòon̄ Eefiraati mɔɔl kí cáá sāā Fiiliistii yab tiŋki nì Eejipiti tiŋki kpaanyɔkɔee kɔkɔ nìn bí Saloomɔn taapu ní. 27Ubɔti nìn yāntì animbil gbí Jeerusaleem kii ataŋkpeeyee ní, ní seedir dɔi wīikí kii Seefeelaa tiŋki sufii in bi yíì siikoomɔɔree. 28Saloomɔn taamui nìn nyēeń Eejipiti nì ntimu mun kɔkɔ kíǹee poon ní.
Saloomɔn kúm
(1 Bib 11.41-43)
29Saloomɔn tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee, kí yòon̄ tin u péé ki ŋée nì tin u ŋá ki lúŋkèe, ŋmàn̄ ki kā Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Naatan gbɔŋkun nì Ayiiya, ubɔnaatil un nyánní Siiloo tiŋkinee gbɔŋkun nì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Idoo leedakal gbɔŋkun. Kugbɔŋu gbanti sòoǹ Neebaati jipɔɔn Jeerooboowaam mun pu. 30Saloomɔn nìn kāl̀ Jeerusaleem ki jíń Isirayeel tiŋki kɔkɔ pu dibeel abin imuŋku ili ní. 31Saloomɔn kpíì ki cūtì ki ŋàl̄ u-naanjab ní bi síb́-u u-baa Daafiidi Tiŋkin. U-jipɔɔn Rooboowaam di fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.

english_text:
Some of the People Rebel against Rehoboam
(1 Kings 12.1-20)
1Rehoboam went to Shechem where everyone was waiting to crown him king.
2Jeroboam son of Nebat heard what was happening, and he returned from Egypt, where he had gone to hide from Solomon. 3The people from the northern tribes of Israel sent for him. Then together they went to Rehoboam and said, 4“Your father Solomon forced us to work very hard. But if you make our work easier, we will serve you and do whatever you ask.”
5Rehoboam replied, “Come back in three days for my answer.” So the people left.
6Rehoboam went to some leaders who had been his father's senior officials, and he asked them, “What should I tell these people?”
7They answered, “If you want them to serve and obey you, then you should be kind and promise to make their work easier.”
8But Rehoboam refused their advice and went to the younger men who had grown up with him and were now his officials. 9He asked, “What do you think I should say to these people who asked me to make their work easier?”
10His younger advisors said:
Here's what we think you should say to them: “Compared to me, my father was weak. 11He made you work hard, but I'll make you work even harder. He punished you with whips, but I'll use whips with pieces of sharp metal!”
12Three days later, Jeroboam and the others came back. 13Rehoboam ignored the advice of the older advisors. He spoke bluntly 14and told them exactly what his own advisors had suggested. He said: “My father made you work hard, but I'll make you work even harder. He punished you with whips, but I'll use whips with pieces of sharp metal!”
15-19 When the people realized that Rehoboam would not listen to them, they shouted: “We don't have to be loyal to David's family. We can do what we want. Come on, people of Israel, let's go home! Rehoboam can rule his own people.”
Adoniram was in charge of the work force, and Rehoboam sent him to talk to the people. But they stoned him to death. Then Rehoboam ran to his chariot and hurried back to Jerusalem.
Everyone from Israel's northern tribes went home, leaving Rehoboam to rule only the people from Judah. And since that day, the people of Israel have been opposed to David's descendants in Judah. All of this happened just as Ahijah the Lord's prophet from Shiloh had told Jeroboam.
translation_text:
JUUDA YAB BƆTIIBI MAAM
(10–36)
Siikeem kpafil
(Kpèè 1 Bib 12.1-15)
1Rooboowaam nìn cūtì Siikeem, di sá yii niin ní Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nìn kóoǹ ki kpáfì kí kàan̄-u dibeel. 2Neebaati jipɔɔn Jeerooboowaam nìn dáá gbíntìi bíń Eejipiti tiŋkin, laakin u nìn sáǹ ubɔti Saloomɔn ki cūtìi kāl̀ee. U nín gbìl̄ Siikeem kooŋyi gbanti puee ní u yíkì Eejipiti tiŋkin ki dɔ́miń. 3Bi nìn tú binib bi cūtìi yíiń-u. U bāańee ní u nì Isirayeel beel samaau kɔkɔ cūtì Rooboowaam cee ki bí-u yii: 4«A-baa nìn túǹ-ti ditúndi din nyìm̀ee. Siiyee, ti là yii á bàtī-ti ditumpɔɔl din a-baa nìn yāntì ti túńee nì diwaŋgul din u nìn dūu nyīkiǹ ti-puee. A yaa ŋá míǹ ti kíí kí nīn sá a-tɔntɔnliibi.» 5Ní u kíí-bi yii: «Nín̄ cámaan, iwiin ita dalee ní fàtīí gítiń.»
U lī mimmee ní samaa nín cá. 6Niinee ní ubɔti Rooboowaam bālifì bitindaŋkpilib bin nìn bí u-baa Saloomɔn tundin ŋyunti ŋun u nìn dáá bí dimaŋfalinee yii: «Ni sáŋkí-mi ḿ kíí binib nee yii ba?» 7Ní bikpilibee bí-u yii: «A yaa dàkā binib nee kulaŋŋaŋfitiiu ki ŋá bi nín là puee ní ki yaa kíí-bi kinyɔɔmɔɔyee, bi làá nīn sá a-tɔntɔnliibi kí nīn cá jaanjaan.»
8Ama ní Rooboowaam kaa dū bikpilibee saŋkii ki túń ditundi, ní ki yíiń binipɔmbi u nì bin jíń tinaacimpɔn dicilpu bi bí u-tundinee. 9U nìn bí bíǹ yii: «Nimbi fáà, ni sáŋkí-mi yii ba? Ḿ kíí binib bin bíi bàlifī-mi ḿ bàtī diwaŋgul din m-baa nìn dūu túǹ-bee nyiŋfiŋu pu yii ba?» 10Ní binipɔmbi u nì bin kpáfìi jíń tinaacimpɔnee kíí-u yii: «Kpèè a nín làá kíí binib bin dɔ́miń ki bí-si yii: <A-baa nìn túǹ-ti diwaŋgul din nyìm̀ee, siiyee bàtī di-nyiŋfiŋu pu kí tīī-ti> puee sɔ̀: <M-ŋambikpakpalii gbìfiǹ m-baa ŋal. 11M-baa yaa nìn túǹ-ni diwaŋgul din nyìm̀ee, man làá gíti kūtì diwaŋgul gbanti nyiŋfiŋu pu. M-baa nìn dū anaalab ní ki dáaĺ ni-tafal, mamee, m làá dū anaalab ŋin cáá agatee ní kí dáaĺ ni-tafal.>»
12Ŋwintataati dalee ní Jeerooboowaam nì samaa kɔkɔ dɔ́miń ki ká Rooboowaam kii úǹ u-ba nín nìn lī puee yii: «Fàtīí gítiḿmaan ŋwintataati dal kí ká-mi.» 13Bikpilib nín nìn sáŋkì u-bɔti puee, waa dūu túń ditundi, ní ki sòon̄ nì samaa an pɔ̄ɔ̄. 14Binipɔmbee nín sáŋkì-u puee, míǹ ní u dūu sòon̄ nì binibee. U nìn bí-bi yii: «M-baa yaa nìn túǹ-ni diwaŋgul din nyìm̀ee, man làá gíti kūtì diwaŋgul gbanti nyiŋfiŋu pu. M-baa nìn dū anaalab ní ki dáaĺ ni-tafal, mamee, m làá dū anaalab ŋin cáá agatee ní kí dáaĺ ni-tafal.» 15Ubɔti kaa nìn pílifiǹ binibee, kun puee ti-Dindaan nín nìn bɔ́ntì míǹ kí ŋmā kí ŋá kii u nín nìn dī u-bɔnaatiliu usiilooja Ayiiya pu ki pōoǹ Neebaati jipɔɔn Jeerooboowaam puee ní.
Isirayeel beel cúu yākatì
(Kpèè 1 Bib 12.16-25)
16Isirayeel beelin yab nín ká yii ubɔti kaa bíi pílifíǹ-bee ní bi bí-u yii:
«Ti nì Daafiidi cáá tilati?
Ti nì Jeesee jipɔɔn kaa cáá mpèé ŋubɔɔ!
Isirayeel yab, tí nīn gítímaan ti-tantibin!
Kɔŋkɔnnee sii Daafiidi, nín̄ jīǹ a-dicaŋku pu dibeel!»
Bi lī mimmee ní báà ŋma nín gítí u-tantiun. 17Ama Isirayeel yab bin nìn kóò Juuda tiŋkinee baba pu ní Rooboowaam nìn nìkī ki jíń dibeel. 18Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, ubɔti Rooboowaam nìn dū Adooram un kpèé diwɔ́bil tuuŋŋee ki tú Isirayeel yab cee, ama ní bíǹ yáŋkì-u ataŋkpee ki kūū. Niinee ní ubɔti Rooboowaam ŋá malaa ki jɔ́m̀ u-tɔrɔkuu poon ki sáǹ ki nín cá Jeerusaleem. 19Kí yòon̄ ŋwiin gbanti ní Isirayeel yab bin kóò ŋgan pú beelinee kíĺ ki jáà nì Daafiidi dicaŋku bɔtiibi. Kujaau gbanti bí ki dāa sāā díǹ.

english_text:
Shemaiah the Prophet Warns Rehoboam
(1 Kings 12.21-24)
1After Rehoboam returned to Jerusalem, he decided to attack Israel and regain control of the whole country. So he called together 180,000 soldiers from the tribes of Judah and Benjamin.
2Meanwhile, the Lord had told Shemaiah the prophet 3to tell Rehoboam and everyone from Judah and Benjamin, 4“The Lord warns you not to go to war against the people from the northern tribes—they are your relatives. Go home! The Lord is the one who made these things happen.”
Rehoboam and his army obeyed the Lord's message and did not attack Jeroboam and his troops.
Rehoboam Fortifies Cities in Judah
5Rehoboam ruled from Jerusalem, and he had several cities in Judah turned into fortresses so he could use them to defend his country. These cities included 6Bethlehem, Etam, Tekoa, 7Beth-Zur, Soco, Adullam, 8Gath, Mareshah, Ziph, 9Adoraim, Lachish, Azekah, 10Zorah, Aijalon, and Hebron. After he had fortified these cities in the territories of Judah and Benjamin, 11he assigned an army commander to each of them and stocked them with supplies of food, olive oil, and wine, 12as well as with shields and spears. He used these fortified cities to keep control of Judah and Benjamin.
The Priests and the Levites Support Rehoboam
13The priests and Levites from the northern tribes of Israel gave their support to King Rehoboam. 14And since Jeroboam and the kings of Israel that followed him would not allow any Levites to serve as priests, most Levites left their towns and pasturelands in Israel and moved to Jerusalem and other towns in Judah. 15 Jeroboam chose his own priests to serve at the local shrines in Israel and at the places of worship where he had set up statues of goat-demons and of calves.
16But some of the people from Israel wanted to worship the Lord God, just as their ancestors had done. So they followed the priests and Levites to Jerusalem, where they could offer sacrifices to the Lord. 17For the next three years, they lived in Judah and were loyal to Rehoboam and his kingdom, just as they had been loyal to David and Solomon.
Rehoboam's Family
18Rehoboam married Mahalath, whose father was Jerimoth son of David, and whose mother was Abihail the daughter of Eliab and granddaughter of Jesse. 19Rehoboam and Mahalath had three sons: Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham. 20Then Rehoboam married Maacah the daughter of Absalom. Their sons were Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith.
21Rehoboam had 18 wives, but he also married 60 other women, and he was the father of 28 sons and 60 daughters. Rehoboam loved his wife Maacah the most, 22so he chose their oldest son Abijah to be the next king. 23Rehoboam was wise enough to put one of his sons in charge of each fortified city in his kingdom. He gave them all the supplies they needed and found wives for every one of them.
translation_text:
1Ŋyunti ŋun Rooboowaam bàn̄ Jeerusaleemee ní u kóoǹ Juuda nì Beenjameen naakɔtin janjaliibi bibaamɔmbi kutukub dilaataal nì imuŋku inaa ki kpáfì kí cùú já nì Isirayeel yab, án nín làá ŋá pu úǹ Rooboowaam ń fàtīí fōō dibeelee. 2Ama ní ti-Dindaan bí u-bɔnaatiliu Seemaya yii: 3«Tùkù Juuda bɔtiu Rooboowaam, Saloomɔn jipɔɔn nì Juuda nì Beenjameen naakɔti yab nì samaa un kɔkɔ pée kíǹee yii: 4Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Naa máaǹ kí cùú já nì ni-nabiyaamu Isirayeel yab. Báà ŋma ń nīn gítí u-dumpu, di sá yii man di yāntì tin bíi jītí nee bāań.>» Niinee ní bi gbìl̄ ki tīī nì ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi ní ki yāntì kaa ti cūtìi jáń nì Jeerooboowaam.
Rooboowaam máń agun ki tú ntimu kupaau
5Rooboowaam nìn kóò Jeerusaleem tiŋkin ní ki máń agun ki tú Juuda timmu. Ntimu gbanti di sá: 6Beetileem nì Eetaam nì Teekoowa 7nì Beeti-Suur nì Sookoo nì Adulaam 8nì Gaati nì Mareeka nì Siifi 9nì Adoorayiim nì Lakiisi nì Aseeka 10nì Soora nì Ayalɔn nì Eebrɔn. Ntimu mun bi nìn máń agun ki tú gbantee nìn bí Juuda yab nì Beenjameen yab timmu poon ní. 11An nìn sá agun ŋin pɔ̄ɔ̄ tiŋanee ní Rooboowaam nìn máń ki tú-mu. U nìn nyàab̄ gɔminab ki kāaǹ mu-pu, ní bi nìn kpáafí tijin nì ɔliifi kpam nì ndamam niin. 12Agbampɔɔ nì ŋkpamu nìn bí ntimu gbanti kɔkɔ poon. Míǹ ní u nìn ŋá ní ki ŋúń ki jíń Juuda nì Beenjameen timmu pu dibeel.
Bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab páaǹ Rooboowaam boon
13Bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab nìn nyáń Isirayeel timmu kɔkɔn ki dɔ́miń ki páaǹ Rooboowaam boon. 14Leefii yab nìn yíkìi fá bi-timmu nì bi-kpaatanti ki nín cá Juuda beelin nì Jeerusaleem. Di sá yii Jeerooboowaam nì u-jipɔmbi kaa nìn pú-bi nsan bí nīn gbíntìi sá ti-Dindaan saraaŋaliibi. 15Jeerooboowaam nìn lēē úǹ u-ba saraaŋaliibi, ní bíǹ bí ŋgbantamu pu ki ŋáań saraabi ki tìì iŋɔjaa nì anabil ŋin u nìn máń ki síiǹee. 16Isirayeel beel naakɔti kɔkɔnee, binib bin nìn nyàab̀ ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nì bi-pɔbil kɔkɔee nìn táá Leefii yab ki dɔ́miń Jeerusaleem tiŋkin. Bi nìn là kí nīn ŋáań saraabi ki tìì ti-Dindaan, bi-naanjab Nimbɔtiu. 17Bíǹ nìn gíti kútì Juuda beel mpɔn ní ki nìn tútúǹ Saloomɔn jipɔɔn Rooboowaam abin ata. Di sá yii abin ata gbanti poonee, u nìn nóó Daafiidi nì Saloomɔn tabɔbiliŋ.
Rooboowaam dicaŋku
18Rooboowaam nìn cáá Maalaati. U-baa di nìn sá Daafiidi jipɔɔn Yeereemooti ní u-na sá Eeliyaab bisal Abiyayiil, Jeesee naantiiu. 19U nìn màl̄-u mbininjabiyaamu muta: Yeewusi nì Seemariya nì Sayam. 20Boonee ní Rooboowaam cáá Abisaloom bisal Maaka. U nìn màl̄-u mbininjabiyaamu munaa: Abiiya nì Atayii nì Siisa nì Seeloomiiti. 21Rooboowaam nìn néeń Abisaloom bisal Maaka ki jítiǹ u-nimpoobi nì u-bɔntiibi bin kɔkɔ kíǹee. Di sá yii u nìn cáá binimpoobi saalku nì bita ní ki cáá bibɔntiibi imuŋku ita, ní ki màl̄ mbininjabiyaamu mmuŋku nì munii nì nnimpubiyaamu imuŋku ita. 22Rooboowaam nìn dū Maaka jipɔɔn Abiiya ní ki kāaǹ u-mambi nì u-naalib kɔkɔ pu ukpil, di sá u nìn là yii úǹ ń dāá kpántí ubɔti ní. 23U nìn ŋá iciin ní ki yāntì u-jipɔmbi bin kíǹee kɔkɔ yàl̄ ki tin bíń Juuda nì Beenjameen timmu mun bi nìn máń agun ki túee poon. U nìn tīī-bi tijin tikpil ní ki nyàab̄ binimpoobi kupaau ki tīī-bi.

english_text:
King Shishak of Egypt Invades Judah
(1 Kings 14.25-28)
1Soon after Rehoboam had control of his kingdom, he and everyone in Judah stopped obeying the Lord. 2So in the fifth year of Rehoboam's rule, the Lord punished them for their unfaithfulness and allowed King Shishak of Egypt to invade Judah. 3Shishak attacked with his army of 1,200 chariots and 60,000 cavalry troops, as well as countless Egyptian soldiers from Libya, Sukkoth, and Ethiopia. 4He captured every one of the fortified cities in Judah and then marched to Jerusalem.
5Rehoboam and the leaders of Judah had gone to Jerusalem to escape Shishak's invasion. And while they were there, Shemaiah the prophet told them, “The Lord says that because you have disobeyed him, he has now abandoned you. The Lord will not help you against Shishak!”
6Rehoboam and the leaders were sorry for what they had done and admitted, “The Lord is right. We have deserted him.”
7When the Lord heard this, he told Shemaiah:
The people of Judah are truly sorry for their sins, and so I won't let Shishak completely destroy them. But because I am still angry, 8he will conquer and rule them.
Then my people will know what it's like to serve a foreign king instead of serving me.
9 Shishak attacked Jerusalem and took all the valuable things from the temple and from the palace, including Solomon's gold shields.
