10Rehoboam had bronze shields made to replace the gold ones, and he ordered the guards at the city gates to keep them safe. 11Whenever Rehoboam went to the Lord's temple, the guards carried the shields. But they always took them back to the guardroom as soon as he had finished worshiping.
12Rehoboam turned back to the Lord, and so the Lord did not let Judah be completely destroyed, and Judah was prosperous again.
Rehoboam's Rule in Judah
(1 Kings 14.21,29-31)
13Rehoboam was 41 years old when he became king, and he ruled 17 years from Jerusalem, the city where the Lord had chosen to be worshiped. His mother Naamah was from Ammon. Rehoboam was a powerful king, 14but he still did wrong and refused to obey the Lord.
15Everything else Rehoboam did while he was king, including a history of his family, is written in the records of the two prophets, Shemaiah and Iddo. During Rehoboam's rule, he and King Jeroboam of Israel were constantly at war. 16When Rehoboam died, he was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Abijah became king.
translation_text:
Eejipiti bɔtiu Siisaaki dɔ́miń ki jáń nì Juuda yab
(Kpèè 1 Bib 14.25-28)
1Ŋyunti ŋun Rooboowaam cúú u-beel pɔŋŋu ki báaǹ inyaanee ní u fātì u-boon ki tīī ti-Dindaan marau, ní u-samaau kɔkɔ mun ŋá míǹ mbaantiim. 2Rooboowaam nín kāl̀ dibeel dibiŋŋmooŋmootiil poonee ní Eejipiti bɔtiu Siisaaki dɔ́miń ki jáń nì Jeerusaleem, di sá yii baa nìn gíti yú nì ti-Dindaan deedee. 3Siisaaki nìn cáá janjatɔrɔkub kutuku ubɔ nì alaataa ali nì bitanjakaliibi kutukub imuŋku ita. Bijanjaliibi bin nìn nyánní Eejipiti tiŋkin ki táá-u ki dɔ́mińee kaa nìn cáá ŋkaan: Liibii yab nìn bí, ní Sukii yab bí ní Eetiiyoopii yab bí. 4U nìn jáń ki fōō Juuda timmu mun bi máń agun ki túee, ní ki nìkī ki dāa bāań áli Jeerusaleem. 5Siisaaki nìn tóobiń ní Rooboowaam nì Juuda kpilib kóoǹ ki kpáfì Jeerusaleem. Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Seemaya nìn cūtìi ká-bi ní ki bí-bi yii: «Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀: <Ni dū man ni-Dindaan ki fá! Too, ma mun dū-ni ki ŋá Siisaaki ŋaan.>»
6Isirayeel kpilibee nì ubɔti nìn lafun béè yii bi yīntì ní ki bí yii: «Ti-Dindaan cáá mbaamɔn.» 7Ti-Dindaan nín ká bi sīntì bi-ba taapuee, ní u tùkū Seemaya yii: «Bi nín béè bi-yìntitamee puee, maa làá kpɔ̀ kí céetí-bi. Ama an kaa ti làá yúntí, m làá fīī-bi, di sá yii maa làá dī Siisaaki pu ní kí yàntī m-ŋuul ń jēetí Jeerusaleem pu. 8Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, m làá yàntī bí kpántí u-tɔntɔnliibi. Niinee bi làá béé yii bi yaa sá man tɔntɔnliibi di sɔ́ɔɔ, bi yaa sá ntimu mubɔ bɔtiibi tɔntɔnliibi di sɔ́.»
9Eejipiti bɔtiu Siisaaki nìn jáń nì Jeerusaleem yab. U nìn yōoǹ tigaajawan tin bí ti-Dindaan Diikun nì kubɔtinaakoounee. U nìn pée yōoǹ kɔkɔ ní, ki kpáaǹ agbampɔɔ ŋin Saloomɔn nìn dū sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́yee kɔkɔ. 10Niinee ní ubɔti Rooboowaam dū tasa kúti ki mɔ́ɔ́ agbampɔɔ ki téeǹ ŋin bi yōoǹee yil pu, ní ki dū-ŋi ki ŋá bijanjaliibi bin cí ubɔti naakooku punyɔmmuee kpiliu ŋaan ú nīn kpèé. 11Ubɔti yaa nìn pée yíkì ki kóò kunimbɔtidiinee, bijanjaliibi nìn yòontí agbampɔɔ gbanti ní ki līī, ní kí fàtīí gíiǹní-ŋi biciitiliibi diikun.
12Rooboowaam nín nìn sīntì u-ba taapu puee, ti-Dindaan nìn páatì u-ŋuul u-pu kaa nāaǹ-u kɔkɔ. Kí kūtì muee, tiwammɔntiil nìn dáá bí Juuda tiŋkin.
Rooboowaam maŋfal wiiŋyi kúntitam
(1 Bib 14.21-24,29-31)
13Ubɔti Rooboowaam nìn kāl̀ Jeerusaleem ki ká mpɔn ki jíń dibeel. U nìn cáá abin imuŋku ili nì dibindi diba ní ki kpántì ubɔti. U nìn jíń Jeerusaleem, kitiŋ kin ti-Dindaan nìn lēē Isirayeel naakɔti kɔkɔ kansikin bí nīn jáaḿ-uee pu dibeel abin saalku nì ali. U-na nìn sá uamɔnnimpu ní bi yíì-u yii Naama. 14U nìn ŋá tin kaa kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee, di sá yii waa nìn dū u-pɔbil kɔkɔ ki nyàab̄ ti-Dindaan.
15Rooboowaam tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee, kí yòon̄ tin u péé ki ŋée nì tin u ŋá ki lúŋkèe, ŋmàn̄ ki kā Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Seemaya gbɔŋkun nì Idoo un wāĺee gbɔŋkun. Kujaau nìn pée bí Rooboowaam nì Jeerooboowaam kansikin ní kaa gbèentí. 16Rooboowaam kpíì ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ u-baabi ní bi síb́-u Daafiidi Tiŋkin. U-jipɔɔn Abiiya di nìn fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.

english_text:
King Abijah of Judah
(1 Kings 15.1-8)
1Abijah became king of Judah in Jeroboam's eighteenth year as king of Israel, 2and he ruled from Jerusalem for three years. His mother was Micaiah the daughter of Uriel from Gibeah.
Some time later, Abijah and King Jeroboam of Israel went to war against each other. 3Abijah's army had 400,000 troops, and Jeroboam met him in battle with 800,000 troops.
4Abijah went to the top of Mount Zemaraim in the hills of Ephraim and shouted:
Listen, Jeroboam and all you Israelites! 5The Lord God of Israel has made a solemn promise that every king of Israel will be from David's family. 6But Jeroboam, you were King Solomon's official, and you rebelled. 7Then right after Rehoboam became king, you and your bunch of worthless followers challenged Rehoboam, who was too young to know how to stop you.
8Now you and your powerful army think you can stand up to the kingdom that the Lord has given to David's descendants. The only gods you have are those gold statues of calves that Jeroboam made for you. 9You don't even have descendants of Aaron on your side, because you forced out the Lord's priests and Levites. In their place, you appoint ordinary people to be priests, just as the foreign nations do. In fact, anyone who brings a bull and seven rams to the altar can become a priest of your so-called gods.
10But we have not turned our backs on the Lord God! Aaron's own descendants serve as our priests, and the Levites are their assistants. 11Two times every day they offer sacrifices and burn incense to the Lord. They set out the sacred loaves of bread on a table that has been purified, and they light the lamps in the gold lampstand every day at sunset. We follow the commands of the Lord our God—you have rejected him! 12That's why God is on our side and will lead us into battle when the priests sound the signal on the trumpets. It's no use, Israelites. You might as well give up. There's no way you can defeat the Lord, the God your ancestors worshiped.
13But while Abijah was talking, Jeroboam had sent some of his troops to attack Judah's army from behind, while the rest attacked from the front. 14Judah's army realized they were trapped, and so they prayed to the Lord. The priests blew the signal on the trumpet, 15and the troops let out a battle cry. Then with Abijah leading them into battle, God defeated Jeroboam and Israel's army. 16The Israelites ran away, and God helped Judah's soldiers slaughter 17500,000 enemy troops. 18Judah's army won because they had trusted the Lord God of their ancestors.
19Abijah kept up his attack on Jeroboam's army and captured the Israelite towns of Bethel, Jeshanah, and Ephron, as well as the villages around them.
20Jeroboam never regained his power during the rest of Abijah's rule. The Lord punished Jeroboam, and he died, but Abijah became more powerful.
21Abijah had a total of 14 wives, 22 sons, and 16 daughters. 22Everything Abijah said and did while he was king is written in the records of Iddo the prophet.
translation_text:
Juuda bɔtiu Abiiya bɔti
(Kpèè 1 Bib 15.1-8)
1Jeerooboowaam nín kāl̀ Isirayeel beel pu dibeel abin saalku nì ata poonee ní Abiiya kpántì Juuda tiŋki bɔtiu. 2U nìn jíń dibeel Jeerusaleem abin ata ní. U-na nìn sá ugiibeeyaja Uriyeel bisal ní bi yíì-u yii Miikaya.
Abiiya nì Jeerooboowaam nìn pée jáà ní kaa gbèentí. 3Abiiya nìn cūtì kí já nì Jeerooboowaam. U nìn yōoǹ bijanjaliibi bibaatandambi kutukub alaataa anaa, ní Jeerooboowaam mun yōoǹ bijanjaliibi bibaatandambi kutukub alaataa anii. 4Abiiya nìn jɔ́m̀ Seemarayiim jool din bí Eefiraayiim jooŋŋi puee ní ki bí yii: «Jeerooboowaam nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ, ní pīlifìmaan. 5Naa nyí yii ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu dū Isirayeel beel ki tīī Daafiidi nì u-naantiibi ní ki nīn cáa cá jaanjaanaaa? An sá dipoondi din bí kaa kpìtēe ní. 6Ama Neebaati jipɔɔn Jeerooboowaam un nìn sá Daafiidi jipɔɔn Saloomɔn tɔntɔnliuee yíkì ki jáń nì u-kpiliu. 7Naayeekub nì binib bin kaa bí tibanee yíkìi páaǹ u-boon ki jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Saloomɔn jipɔɔn Rooboowaam. Rooboowaam mun nìn dáá sá kinaacimpɔmbiki, kaa nìn dáá nyí tiba ní kaa nìn ŋúń ki síl̀ bi-nimbiin. 8Too kɔŋkɔnnee, ni bíi lì yii ni làá já nì dibeel din ti-Dindaan dūu ŋá Daafiidi naantiibi ŋaanee. Tiŋman ni wīikí ní ki cáá sindaariya nabil din Jeerooboowaam mɔ́ɔ́ ki tīī-ni dí nīn sá ni-nimbɔtiuee. 9Ni jìn̄ ti-Dindaan saraaŋaliibi, Aarɔn naantiibi nì Leefii yab ni-kansikin. Ni lēē nimbi ni-ba bisaraaŋaliibi kii anibul ŋin kíǹee yab nín ŋáań puee. Ubɔ yaa cáań unaja nì iŋɔjaa ilulee, udaan kpáàa kpántì inimbɔti in kaa kpáàa sá Unimbɔtee saraaŋaliu dee. 10Ama timbee, ti-Dindaan di sá timbi Nimbɔtiu, ní taa dū-u ki fá. Bisaraaŋaliibi bin tūǹ ti-Dindaan tundee sá Aarɔn naantiibi ní, ní Leefii yab mun bí ki tūǹ bi-tundi. 11Kutaafaau nì kujoou kamaayee, bi ŋáań bisaraawɔkaabi ní ki tùutī talaalub ki tìì ti-Dindaan. Bi pāantí kpɔnɔb bin bi dūu ŋá Unimbɔti saraayee circir teebiliu pu, ní ki tùutī fitilab bin tɔ́kɔ́ sindaariya tɔ́kɔŋkaati puee kujoou kamaa. Di sá yii timbee, ti ŋúb́ ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu nín bí yii tí ŋá puee ní. Ama nimbee, ni dū-u ki fá. 12Kɔŋkɔnnee, Unimbɔti u-ba di līī timbi nyɔkɔpu. U-saraaŋaliibi mun bí ki bɔ́ntì kí búń bi-yiŋyi ti kíĺ nì ni kujaau. Míǹ puee Isirayeel yab, ní taa já nì ti-Dindaan, ni-naanjab Nimbɔtiu! Naa làá ŋmā kí já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ-u.»
13Ŋyunti gbantee, Jeerooboowaam nìn lēē u-janjaliibi biba bi cūtìi bál̀ Juuda yab janjaliibi boon pú kí túuǹ-bi. An ŋá mimmee ní Isirayeel janjaliibi biba bí Juuda yab nyɔkɔpu ní bin bál̀ee mun bí bi-boon pú. 14Juuda yab fātèe ní ki ká yii bi cáá kí jáǹ bijanjaliibi bin bí bi-nyɔkɔpuee nì bin bí bi-boon púee. Niinee ní bi kúuǹ ki yíiń ti-Dindaan, ní bisaraaŋaliibi búń iyin. 15Juuda yab nìn fáá ijanjakuŋkuunti. Ŋyunti ŋun bi bíi kūuntí mimmee ní Unimbɔti yāntì Abiiya nì Juuda yab jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Jeerooboowaam nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ. 16Isirayeel yab nìn sáǹ Juuda yab nimbiin ní Unimbɔti dū-bi ki ŋá Juuda yab ŋaan. 17Abiiya nì u-janjaliibi nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Isirayeel janjaliibi sɔ́kɔ sɔkɔ. Bi nìn kūū bi-janjaliibi bibaatandambi kutukub alaataa aŋmoo. 18Ŋwiin gbantee, bi nìn nàn̄ Isirayeel yab dúsi dusi, ama Juuda yab bíǹ nìn ká dijajil, di sá yii bi nìn dū bi-mákal ki páaǹ ti-Dindaan, bi-naanjab Nimbɔtiu pu. 19Abiiya nìn kùl̄ ki páaǹ Jeerooboowaam boon. U nìn jáń ki fōō u-cee Beeteel nì Yeesana Eefrɔn timmu nì ntimbilimu mun pìl̄-muee.
20Ŋyunti ŋun Abiiya sá ubɔtee, Jeerooboowaam kaa nìn gíti ká mpɔn. An dāa kúntèe ní ti-Dindaan fáá-u ní u kpíì. 21Ama Abiiya úǹ nìn mɔ̄tìi ká mpɔn. U nìn cáá binimpoobi ubɔ kpá saalku ní ki cáá jipɔmbi mmuŋku nì bili nì bisalib saalku nì ubɔ.
22Abiiya tuuŋŋi ŋin u túńee, tin kɔkɔ u ŋée nì tin u lēe ŋmàn̄ ki kā Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Idoo gbɔŋkun. 23Abiiya kpíì ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ u-baabee ní bi síb́-u Daafiidi Tiŋkin. U-jipɔɔn Asaa di fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.
Asaa beel bɔti
(Kpèè 1 Bib 15.9-11)
Asaa nín kāl̀ dibeel puee, ŋgbansɔŋfi nìn dɔ́miń Juuda tiŋki pu ki cáa sāā abin saalaa.

english_text:
King Asa of Judah
1Abijah died and was buried in Jerusalem. Then his son Asa became king, and Judah had ten years of peace.
2Asa obeyed the Lord his God and did right. 3He destroyed the local shrines and the altars to foreign gods. He smashed the stone images of gods and cut down the sacred poles used in worshiping the goddess Asherah. 4Then he told everyone in Judah to worship the Lord God, just as their ancestors had done, and to obey his laws and teachings. 5He destroyed every local shrine and incense altar in Judah.
6The Lord blessed Judah with peace while Asa was king, and so during that time, Asa fortified many of the towns. 7He said to the people, “Let's build walls and defense towers for these towns, and put in gates that can be locked with bars. This land still belongs to us, because we have obeyed the Lord our God. He has given us peace from all our enemies.” The people did everything Asa had suggested.
8Asa had a large army of brave soldiers: 300,000 of them were from the tribe of Judah and were armed with shields and spears; 280,000 were from Benjamin and were armed with shields and bows.
Judah Defeats Ethiopia's Army
9Zerah from Ethiopia led an army of 1,000,000 soldiers and 300 chariots to the town of Mareshah in Judah. 10Asa met him there, and the two armies prepared for battle in Zephathah Valley.
11Asa prayed:
Lord God, only you can help a powerless army defeat a stronger one. So we depend on you to help us. We will fight against this powerful army to honor your name, and we know that you won't be defeated. You are the Lord our God.
12The Lord helped Asa and his army defeat the Ethiopians. The enemy soldiers ran away, 13but Asa and his troops chased them as far as Gerar. It was a total defeat—the Ethiopians could not even fight back!
The soldiers from Judah took everything that had belonged to the Ethiopians. 14The people who lived in the villages around Gerar learned what had happened and were afraid of the Lord. So Judah's army easily defeated them and carried off everything of value that they wanted from these towns. 15They also attacked the camps where the shepherds lived and took a lot of sheep, goats, and camels. Then they went back to Jerusalem.
translation_text:
1Asaa nìn ŋá tin fáatiǹ ti-Dindaan u-Nimbɔtiuee. 2U nìn kúntì awaa saraafaŋyi iwaatootipaan pu. U nìn wīil̀ ataŋkpawaa ŋin bi nìn cóoǹ ki tòotēe ki gāatì iwindɔ ki fá. 3U nìn kpáafì Juuda yab yii bí nyàab̀ ti-Dindaan, bi-baabi Nimbɔtiu, kí nīn tɔ́ u-bɔkpaaŋi nì u-marab. 4U nìn kúntì iwaatootipaan nì isaraafan in pu bi nìn tùutī talaalubee Juuda timmu kɔkɔn. An puee, u-beel yuntiŋuee, Juuda beel nìn bí ŋgbansɔŋfin ní.
5U nìn máń agun ki tú Juuda timmu, di sá yii ŋgbansɔŋfi nìn bí. Abin gbanti poonee, ubɔ kaa nìn dɔ́miń ki jáń nì u, di sá yii ti-Dindaan di nìn tīī-u diŋuŋfil. 6U nìn bí Juuda yab yii: «Yàntīmaan tí mā agun kí tū ntimu nee. Tí mā sintil difɔkɔŋi, kí kpáá punuubi bí nīn cáá tikpàlkaal, ŋyunti ŋun ní kitiŋ nee dáá sá ti-yakee. Di sá yii ti yúl̀ ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu deedee, ní ti-deedeeu puee, u tīī-ti diŋuŋfil ijaan kɔkɔ pu.» Bi nìn ŋúń ki máń agun ki tú ntimu gbanti.
7Juuda naakookunee, Asaa nìn cáá bijanjaliibi kutukub alaataa ata, bi ŋúb̀ agbampɔɔ akpaan nì ŋkpamu. U nìn cáá Beenjameen naakookun bijanjaliibi kutukub alaataa ali nì imuŋku inaa, bi ŋúb̀ agbampɔɔ ŋwaamu ki ŋūǹ ki tòó itɔfi. Bíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ nìn sá bibaatandambi ní. 8Ueetiiyoopiija Seera nìn cáań bijanjaliibi miiliyɔn ubɔ nì janjatɔrɔkub alaataa ata kí já nì bi. U nìn ŋúń ki bāań áli Mareesa tiŋkin. 9Asaa nìn nyáń kí jáǹ-u. U nì u-janjaliibi kɔkɔ nìn tātìi gbāaǹ kí kíĺ dikɔ̀ndi Seefata tantakalin, Mareesa caŋin. 10Asaa nìn kúuǹ ki yíiń ti-Dindaan u-Nimbɔtiu. U nìn lī yii: «Ti-Dindaan, sii baba di ŋūǹ kí tūtuǹ uwɔfi ki tí ŋūǹ kí tūtuǹ upɔɔl mun. Dāá tūtuǹ-ti, ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu. Di sá yii sii pu ní ti máká. A-yindi pu ní ti dòoń kí já nì dijanjakitikpaandi nee. Ti-Dindaan, sii di sá ti-Nimbɔtiu. Taa yàntī unil ń já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ-si.»
11Ti-Dindaan nìn yāntì Asaa nì Juuda yab jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Eetiiyoopii yab. Bi nìn sáǹ 12ní Asaa nì u-janjaliibi jìn̄-bi áli Geeraar tiŋki. Bi nìn kūū Eetiiyoopii yab tikpil áli ki dāa kūū ki céetì-bi múb, ubɔ kaa kíǹ. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan nì u-janjaliibi di nìn nàn̄-bi. Juuda yab nìn kóoǹ bi-gaajawanti tikpil. 13Bi nìn jáń ki fōō ntimu mun kɔkɔ nìn bí ki pìlīǹ Geeraar tiŋkee. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan nìn yāntì dinyoondi kɔ́-bi. Juuda yab nìn fúkúl̀ ntimu gbanti kɔkɔ yab wanti, kun puee tigaajawan tikpil nìn bí niin bí fūkul̀. 14Bi nìn gāatì bipikpaaliibi naabakati ní ki nìn kóoǹ bi-piii nì bi-gutaamui tikpil. Bi ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki nín gítí Jeerusaleem.

english_text:
Asa Destroys the Idols in Judah
1Some time later, God spoke to Azariah son of Oded. 2At once, Azariah went to Asa and said:
Listen to me, King Asa and you people of Judah and Benjamin. The Lord will be with you and help you, as long as you obey and worship him. But if you disobey him, he will desert you.
3For a long time, the people of Israel did not worship the true God or listen to priests who could teach them about God. They refused to obey God's Law. 4But whenever trouble came, Israel turned back to the Lord their God and worshiped him.
5There was so much confusion in those days that it wasn't safe to go anywhere in Israel. 6Nations were destroying each other, and cities were wiping out other cities, because God was causing trouble and unrest everywhere.
7So you must be brave. Don't give up! God will honor you for obeying him.
8As soon as Asa heard what Azariah the prophet said, he gave orders for all the idols in Judah and Benjamin to be destroyed, including those in the towns he had captured in the territory of Ephraim. He also repaired the Lord's altar that was in front of the temple porch.
9Asa called together the people from Judah and Benjamin, as well as the people from the territories of Ephraim, West Manasseh, and Simeon who were living in Judah. Many of these people were now loyal to Asa, because they had seen that the Lord was with him.
10In the third month of the fifteenth year of Asa's rule, they all met in Jerusalem. 11That same day, they took 700 bulls and 7,000 sheep and goats from what they had brought back from Gerar and sacrificed them as offerings to the Lord. 12They made a solemn promise to faithfully worship the Lord God their ancestors had worshiped, 13and to put to death anyone who refused to obey him. 14The crowd solemnly agreed to keep their promise to the Lord, then they celebrated by shouting and blowing trumpets and horns. 15Everyone was happy because they had made this solemn promise, and in return, the Lord blessed them with peace from all their enemies.
16Asa's grandmother Maacah had made a disgusting idol of the goddess Asherah, so he cut it down, crushed it, and burned it in Kidron Valley. Then he removed Maacah from her position as queen mother. 17As long as Asa lived, he was faithful to the Lord, even though he did not destroy the local shrines in Israel. 18He placed in the temple all the silver and gold objects that he and his father had dedicated to God.
19There was peace in Judah until the thirty-fifth year of Asa's rule.
translation_text:
Asaa fātìi ŋáŋkì dinimbɔtinool
(Kpèè 1 Bib 15.12-15)
1Unimbɔti Fam nìn kpákatì Oodeedi jipɔɔn Asariyawuu pu. 2U nìn cūtìi túŋkì Asaa ní ki bí-u yii: «Asaa nì Juuda nì Beenjameen yab kɔkɔ, ní pīlifìmaan-mi! Ni yaa bí ti-Dindaan ceeyee, u mun bí ni-cee ní. Ni yaa nyàab̄-uee, u làá yàntī ní ká-u, ama ni yaa dū-u ki fée, see u mun ń dū-ni kí fá. 3Isirayeel yab nìn dū iyunti tikpil ki kāl̀ ibaamɔn Nimbɔtiu kpá bi-ceeyaaa, usaraaŋal ubɔ kpá kí dàkà-baaa, ní mara ubɔ mun nìn kpá. 4Ama bi-nimbinaamandi poonee, bi fātìi gítìń ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu cee, ki nyàab̄-u, ní úǹ yāntì bi ká-u. 5Ŋyunti gbantee, unil kaa nìn ŋūǹ kí nyā kí fàtīí kɔ́nní nì ŋgbansɔŋfi, di sá yii kitiŋ kamaa pu nib nìn bí dinyoondin ní. 6Ditimbundi diba nìn jáà nì di-juti, ní kitiŋ kiba jáà nì ki-juti, di sá yii Unimbɔti di nìn cáań animbinaaman gbanti kɔkɔ nì ŋi-bulifi ki tɔ́ bi-pu. 7Ama nimbee, ní nīn ŋúb́ an píkí, ni-wunti ń taa yɔ̀tī. Di sá yii ni-tundi dāa cáá tipaal.»
8Ŋyunti ŋun Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Asariyawuu, Oodeedi jipɔɔn dū tibɔti gbanti ki nāatì Asaayee, ní u ká kunyannyaau. U nìn kúntì awaa ŋin kɔkɔ nìn bí Juuda nì Beenjameen timmunee. U nìn kúntì ŋin mun nìn bí ntimu mun u nìn jáń ki fōō Eefiraayiim jooŋŋi puee. U nìn ŋáŋkì ti-Dindaan saraafaŋŋu ŋun nìn bí kunimbɔtidii nyɔkɔpuee. 9U nìn kóoǹ Juuda yab nì Beenjameen yab kɔkɔ nì Isirayeel yab bin nìn nyánní Eefiraayiim nì Manasee nì Simeeyɔn naakɔtin ki dɔ́mińee ki kpáfì. Di sá yii Isirayeel yab tikpil nìn dɔ́miń ki páaǹ u-boon ŋyunti ŋun ní bi ká yii ti-Dindaan u-Nimbɔtiu bí u-ceeyee. 10Asaa nín jíń dibeel abin saalku ŋmatataatiu poonee, ní bi kóoǹ ki kpáfì Jeerusaleem. 11Yaadal wiiŋŋuee, bi nìn lēē tiwaŋkuti tin bi nìn fúkúl̀ bi-nannanliibi ceeyee poon inaa alaataa aluli nì ipii kutukub biluli ki ŋá ti-Dindaan saraa. 12Bi nìn pōoǹ kí nyàab̀ ti-Dindaan, bi-naanjab Nimbɔtiu nì bi-pɔbiliŋ kɔkɔ nì bi-nammu kɔkɔ. 13Bi nìn pōoǹ yii kibikeeee, unikpaaneeee, uninjeeee, unimpueeee, un kamaa yaa kaa nyàab̄ ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiuee, bí kpɔ̀-u. 14Ní bi téeń mpɔn ki fáá iwiliili, ní ki búń akantán nì iyin ki pūtì ki pōoǹ ti-Dindaan. 15Juuda yab kɔkɔ nìn bí mmɔnni, kun puee bi nìn pūtì ki pōoǹ nì bi-pɔbiliŋ kɔkɔ ní. Bi nìn lēē bi-ban kí nyàab̀ ti-Dindaan, ní ti-Dindaan mun nìn yāntì bi ká-u. Ti-Dindaan nìn tīī-bi ŋgbansɔŋfi ijaan kɔkɔ pu.
16Ubɔti Asaa nìn lēē u-naan Maaka tinimpubɔtiilin, kun puee u nìn kpítì diwaal ki nántiǹ ntimbiil waal Aseera. Asaa nìn gāā diwaalee ki lúkú, ní ki càkā càkā-dì ki dūu tɔ́ ŋŋmin Seedrɔn tantakalin. 17Ama ŋgbantamu pu waatootipaaŋyi kaa nìn kúntì Isirayeel tiŋkin. Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, Asaa pɔbil nìn bí diba nì ti-Dindaan ní u-maŋfal wiiŋyi kɔkɔ poon. 18U nìn cáań animbil nì sindaariya nì tiwan tin kɔkɔ u-baa nì úǹ u-ba nìn dūu sú Unimbɔtee ki síiǹ kunimbɔtidiin.
19Asaa nín jíń dibeel ki cáá sāā abin aŋmoo kpá imuŋku ili poonee, baa ti gbìl̄ kujaau pu.

english_text:
King Baasha of Israel Invades Judah
(1 Kings 15.16-22)
1In the thirty-sixth year of Asa's rule, King Baasha of Israel invaded Judah and captured the town of Ramah. He started making the town stronger, and he put troops there to stop people from going in and out of Judah.
2When Asa heard about this, he took the silver and gold from his palace and from the Lord's temple. Then he sent it to Damascus with this message for King Benhadad of Syria: 3“I think we should sign a peace treaty, just as our fathers did. This silver and gold is a present for you. Would you please break your treaty with King Baasha of Israel and force him to leave my country?”
4Benhadad did what Asa asked and sent the Syrian army into Israel. They captured the towns of Ijon, Dan, Abel-Maim, and all the towns in Naphtali where supplies were kept. 5When Baasha heard about it, he stopped his work on the town of Ramah.
6Asa ordered everyone in Judah to carry away the stones and wood Baasha had used to fortify Ramah. Then he fortified the towns of Geba and Mizpah with these same stones and wood.
Hanani the Prophet Condemns Asa
7Soon after that happened, Hanani the prophet went to Asa and said:
You depended on the king of Syria instead of depending on the Lord your God. And so, you will never defeat the Syrian army. 8Remember how powerful the Ethiopian and Libyan army was, with all their chariots and cavalry troops! You trusted the Lord to help you then, and you defeated them. 9The Lord is constantly watching everyone, and he gives strength to those who faithfully obey him. But you have done a foolish thing, and your kingdom will never be at peace again.
10When Asa heard this, he was so angry that he put Hanani in prison. Asa was also cruel to some of his people.
Asa Dies
(1 Kings 15.23,24)
11Everything Asa did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah and Israel. 12In the thirty-ninth year of his rule, he got a very bad foot disease, but he relied on doctors and refused to ask the Lord for help. 13He died two years later.
14Earlier, Asa had his own tomb cut out of a rock hill in Jerusalem. So he was buried there, and the tomb was filled with spices and sweet-smelling oils. Then the people built a bonfire in his honor.
translation_text:
Asaa nì Isirayeel yab bí kujaaun
1Asaa nín jíń dibeel abin anaa kpá imuŋku ili poonee ní Isirayeel bɔtiu Bayeesa dɔ́miń kí já nì Juuda tiŋki. U bāańee ní ki máń digundi ki tú Raama timbiliiki kí pìin̄ Juuda bɔtiu Asaa nsan. 2Niinee ní Asaa lēē animbil nì sindaariya un nìn bí kunimbɔtidii nimbikpaafidiikun nì ubɔti nimbikpaafidiikunee ki tīī u-tɔntɔnliibi bí cáá cùnnì Damaasi kí tīī Siirii bɔtiu Been-Adaadi, kí tùkù-u yii: 3«Yàntī mpèé ń nīn bí man nì sii kansikin kii an nín nìn bí man baa nì sii baa kansikin puee. Kpèè animbil nì sindaariya ní m tú bí cáań kí tīī-si nee. Míǹ puee cùú kpìtī mpèé ŋun bí si nì Isirayeel bɔtiu Bayeesa kansikinee ú taa ti dāan̄ kí já nì mi.» 4Been-Adaadi nìn gbìl̄ ki tīī nì ubɔti Asaa ní ki dū u-janjakpilib ki tú bi cūtìi jáń nì Isirayeel timmu. Bi nìn jáń ki fōō Iyɔn nì Daani nì Abeel-Mayiim-Maaka timmu nì Neefitalii naakookun timmu mun kɔkɔ poon bi nìn sīintí tijinee. 5Bayeesa nín gbìl̄ tibɔti gbantee ní u gbēeǹ kaa ti bíi māā Raama timbiliiki gundi. 6Niinee ní ubɔti Asaa yōoǹ Juuda yab kɔkɔ ní bi cūtìi kóoǹ ataŋkpee nì idɔ in Bayeesa nìn cáa bíi māā Raama gundee ki cáań. Ubɔti Asaa nìn dūu máń digundi ki tú Geeba nì Miisipa timmu.
Asaa pīiǹ Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Ananii kudii
7Ŋyunti gbantee ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Ananii dɔ́miń ki ká Juuda bɔtiu Asaa ní ki bí-u yii: «An nín bàà sá á nyàab̀ dijòońdi ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu ceeyee, a cūtìi nyàab̄ dijòońdi Siirii bɔtiu cee. A nín ŋá mimmee puee, Siirii bɔtiu janjaliibi ŋmátìi nyáń a-ŋaan. 8Eetiiyoopii yab nì Liibii yab janjaliibi nì bi-tɔrɔkub nì bi-tanjakaliibi nìn wīikí ní tikpil tikpil. Ama nì míǹ kɔkɔee, a nín nìn dū a-mákal ki páaǹ ti-Dindaan puee, u nìn dū-bi ki ŋá a-ŋaan. 9Di sá yii ti-Dindaan nimbiliŋ làaǹ kitiŋ kɔkɔ pu kí tíkiń bin néeń-u nì bi-pɔbiliŋ kɔkɔee ní. Min bí neeyee, a ŋá kii ugbaanee, ní kí yòon̄ kɔŋkɔnnee kí nīn cée, kujaau poon ní a làá nīn kíǹ ki bí.» 10Asaa nìn gíí Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu pu diŋuul ní ki cúú-u ki pīiǹ kudii. Di sá yii tin Ananii nìn sòon̄ee nìn yāntì u gíí diŋuul ŋkpitim pu. Ŋyunti gbanti ní Asaa kíĺ ki kíǹ ki wɔ́b́ samaa kansikin binib biba.
Asaa beel nín kúntì puee
(Kpèè 1 Bib 15.23-24)
11Atuun ŋin kɔkɔ Asaa túńee kí yòon̄ apeekaa kí cáá sāā aluŋkikaayee ŋmàn̄ ki kā Juuda bɔtiibi nì Isirayeel bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔntin. 12Asaa nín jíń dibeel dibindi diba kpá imuŋku ili poonee ní u búŋkì ní u-taaŋi dūu fàl̄. Ama u-weeŋyi gbanti poonee, waa nìn nyàab̄ ti-Dindaan jòońdi, see binyɔɔdambi. 13U nín jíń dibeel abin imuŋku ili nì awee, ní u kpíì ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ u-baabi. 14Bi nìn síb́-u dikaakul din úǹ u-ba yāntì bi gbìn̄ Daafiidi Tiŋkinee poon ní. Bi nìn bɔ́ntì talaalub ki páaǹ kilambaŋ kin pu bi dū-u ki bíl̀ee, ní ki nyàab̄ ikpafi in sɔ́fèe ki ŋmītì u-wunti an taa sūū. Bi nìn tūū talaalub tikpil ki tīī-u tinyool.

english_text:
King Jehoshaphat of Judah
1Jehoshaphat son of Asa became king and strengthened his defenses against Israel. 2He assigned troops to the fortified cities in Judah, as well as to other towns in Judah and to those towns in Ephraim that his father Asa had captured.
3-4When Jehoshaphat's father had first become king of Judah, he was faithful to the Lord and refused to worship the god Baal as the kings of Israel did. Jehoshaphat followed his father's example and obeyed and worshiped the Lord. And so the Lord blessed Jehoshaphat 5and helped him keep firm control of his kingdom. The people of Judah brought gifts to Jehoshaphat, but even after he became very rich and respected, 6he remained completely faithful to the Lord. He destroyed all the local shrines in Judah, including the places where the goddess Asherah was worshiped.
7In the third year of Jehoshaphat's rule, he chose five officials and gave them orders to teach the Lord's Law in every city and town in Judah. They were Benhail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethanel, and Micaiah. 8Their assistants were the following nine Levites: Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah, and Tob-Adonijah. Two priests, Elishama and Jehoram, also went along. 9They carried with them a copy of the Lord's Law wherever they went and taught the people from it.
10The nations around Judah were afraid of the Lord's power, so none of them attacked Jehoshaphat. 11Philistines brought him silver and other gifts to keep peace. Some of the Arab people brought him 7,700 rams and the same number of goats.
12As Jehoshaphat became more powerful, he built fortresses and cities 13where he stored supplies. He also kept in Jerusalem some experienced soldiers 14from the Judah and Benjamin tribes. These soldiers were grouped according to their clans.
Adnah was the commander of the troops from Judah, and he had 300,000 soldiers under his command. 15Jehohanan was second in command, with 280,000 soldiers under him. 16Amasiah son of Zichri, who had volunteered to serve the Lord, was third in command, with 200,000 soldiers under him.
17Eliada was a brave warrior who commanded the troops from Benjamin. He had 200,000 soldiers under his command, all of them armed with bows and shields. 18Jehozabad was second in command, with 180,000 soldiers under him. 19These were the troops who protected the king in Jerusalem, not counting those he had assigned to the fortified cities throughout the country.
translation_text:
Joosafaati kpántì ubɔti
1Asaa jipɔɔn Joosafaati fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti. U nìn bɔ́ntì u-janjaliibi kí ŋmā kí jáǹ Isirayeel beel. 2U nìn dū bijanjaliibi ki síiǹ Juuda timmu mun bi nìn máń agun ki túee kɔkɔ poon, ní ki nìn kāaǹ gɔmina Juuda nì Eefiraayiim timmu mun u-baa nìn jáń ki fōōyee. 3Ti-Dindaan nìn bí Joosafaati cee. Di sá yii u-naanja Daafiidi nín nìn dī nsan ŋun mpeepeekaamee ní u nìn nóó. Waa nìn jáam̀ diwaal Baal. 4Ama u nìn nyàab̄ ti-Dindaan, u-baa Nimbɔtiu, ní ki nìn tɔ́ u-marab. U nìn fātì u-boon ki tīī Isirayeel beel yab ŋáaǹtam. 5Ti-Dindaan nìn tīī Joosafaati beel mpɔn ní Juuda yab kɔkɔ nìn cāabìń tiwan ki pūǹ-u. U nìn dūu kpántì ugaajakpaan ki ká tinyool tikpil. 6U nìn dū u-pɔbil kɔkɔ ki tīī ki nóó ti-Dindaan, ní ki nìn kúntì iwaatootipaan in pu bi nìn tòotī awaayee nì diwaal Aseera ŋgbantamu puee nì iwindɔ Juuda tiŋkin.
7U nín jíń dibeel dibintataatiil poonee ní u lēē u-kàliŋkpaambi biba ki tú Juuda timmun bí cùú dàkà niin yab. Bin u nìn lēē ki túee di sá Been-Ayiil nì Oobadiya nì Seekariyawuu nì Neetaneeyeel nì Miikayawuu. 8U nìn yāntì Leefii yab biba céeǹ-bi. Bíǹ di sá Seemayawuu nì Neetaniyawuu nì Seebadiyawuu nì Asayeel nì Seemiiramooti nì Yoonatan nì Adooniyasi nì Toobiyawuu nì Toob-Adooniya. Bisaraaŋaliibi bili biba mun nìn kútì bi-pu, bíǹ di sá Eeliisama nì Yooram. 9Bi nìn yōoǹ ti-Dindaan Marau gbɔŋku ní ki yìin̄ Juuda timmu kɔkɔn ki dàkā mu-nib ti-Dindaan marau.
Joosafaati pɔŋŋu
10Abee ŋin nìn bí ki māntìi tú Juuda tiŋkee nìn fāŋkì ti-Dindaan, ní báà ubɔ kaa nìn kíikí kí jáǹ Joosafaati. 11Fiiliistii yab gba nìn cāabìń tiwampɔkaal nì animbil nì patantib ki tìì Joosafaati. Bilaalibub mun nìn cāabìń tiwaŋkuti ki pūǹ-u. Bi nìn cáań ipijaa kutukub biluli nì alaataa aluli nì iŋɔjaa kutukub biluli.
12Joosafaati nìn mɔ̀tīi kāntí mpɔn ní ki cá. U nìn máń agun ki māntìi tú ntimu mubɔ, ní ki nìn máń mubɔ mun poon adiin bí nīn kpáafí tijin. 13U nìn kpáafì tijin tikpil tikpil Juuda timmun. U nìn dū bijanjaliibi bin sá bibaatandambee ki kāaǹ Jeerusaleem tiŋkin ní. 14U nìn yākatì bijanjaliibi gbanti akiti akiti ki nóó nì bi-dicaŋŋi. Juuda naakookunee, bin nìn kpòotī bijanjaliibi kutukub kutukubee sɔ̀. Ujanjakpil Adina nìn kpòotī bijanjaliibi bin sá bibaatandambee kutukub alaataa ata, 15ní un dī-uee di sá ujanjakpil Yoowanan. Úǹ nìn kpòotī bijanjaliibi kutukub alaataa ali nì imuŋku inaa. 16Utataati di sá Sikirii jipɔɔn Amaseeyaawuu. Úǹ nìn dū u-ba ki tīī kí tɔ̄ ti-Dindaan tundi. U nìn kpòotī bijanjaliibi kutukub alaataa ali ní. 17Beenjameen naakookunee, ubaatandaan ubɔ nìn bí bi yíì-u Eeliyadaa. Úǹ di nìn kpòotī bijanjaliibi bin jáà nì abaatan nì agbampɔɔyee binib kutukub alaataa ali. 18Un nìn dī-uee di sá Yoosabaadi. Úǹ nìn kpòotī bijanjaliibi bin bɔ́ntì kí cù dikɔ̀ndee binib kutukub dilaataal nì imuŋku ili ní. 19Bijanjaliibi bin nìn bí ubɔti tundin Jeerusaleemee dee. Bijanjaliibi bin ubɔti nìn dūu kāaǹ Juuda timmu mun bi máń agun ki túee poon kaa kútì.

english_text:
Micaiah Warns King Ahab of Israel
(1 Kings 22.1-28)
1Jehoshaphat was now very rich and famous. He signed a treaty with King Ahab of Israel by arranging the marriage of his son and Ahab's daughter.
2One day, Jehoshaphat went to visit Ahab in his capital city of Samaria. Ahab slaughtered sheep and cattle and prepared a big feast to honor Jehoshaphat and the officials with him. Ahab talked about attacking the city of Ramoth in Gilead, 3and finally asked, “Jehoshaphat, would you go with me to attack Ramoth?”
“Yes,” Jehoshaphat answered. “My army is at your command. 4But first let's ask the Lord what to do.”
5Ahab sent for 400 prophets and asked, “Should I attack the city of Ramoth?”
“Yes!” the prophets answered. “God will help you capture the city.”
6But Jehoshaphat said, “Just to make sure, is there another of the Lord's prophets we can ask?”
7“We could ask Micaiah son of Imlah,” Ahab said. “But I hate Micaiah. He always has bad news for me.”
“Don't say that!” Jehoshaphat replied. 8Then Ahab sent someone to bring Micaiah as soon as possible.
9All this time, Ahab and Jehoshaphat were dressed in their royal robes and were seated on their thrones at the threshing place near the gate of Samaria, listening to the prophets tell them what the Lord had said.
10Zedekiah son of Chenaanah was one of the prophets. He had made some horns out of iron and shouted, “Ahab, the Lord says you will attack the Syrians like a bull with iron horns and wipe them out!”
11All the prophets agreed that Ahab should attack the Syrians at Ramoth and promised that the Lord would help him defeat them.
12Meanwhile, the messenger who went to get Micaiah whispered, “Micaiah, all the prophets have good news for Ahab. Now go and say the same thing.”
13“I'll say whatever the living Lord my God tells me to say,” Micaiah replied.
14Then Micaiah went up to Ahab, who asked, “Micaiah, should we attack Ramoth?”
“Yes!” Micaiah answered. “The Lord will help you capture the city.”
15Ahab shouted, “Micaiah, I've told you over and over to tell me the truth! What does the Lord really say?”
16 Micaiah answered, “In a vision I saw Israelite soldiers wandering around, lost in the hills like sheep without a shepherd. The Lord said, ‘These troops have no leader. They should go home and not fight.’ ”
17Ahab turned to Jehoshaphat and said, “I told you he would bring me bad news!”
18Micaiah replied:
I then saw the Lord seated on his throne with every creature in heaven gathered around him. 19The Lord asked, “Who can trick Ahab and make him go to Ramoth where he will be killed?”
They talked about it for a while, 20then finally a spirit came forward and said to the Lord, “I can trick Ahab.”
“How?” the Lord asked.
21“I'll make Ahab's prophets lie to him.”
“Good!” the Lord replied. “Now go and do it. You will be successful.”
22Ahab, this is exactly what has happened. The Lord made all your prophets lie to you, and he knows you will soon be destroyed.
23Zedekiah walked over and slapped Micaiah on the face. Then he asked, “Do you really think the Lord would speak to you and not to me?”
24Micaiah answered, “You'll find out on the day you have to hide in the back room of some house.”
25Ahab shouted, “Arrest Micaiah! Take him to Prince Joash and Governor Amon of Samaria. 26Tell them to put him in prison and to give him nothing but bread and water until I come back safely.”
27Micaiah said, “If you do come back, I was wrong about what the Lord wanted me to say.” Then he told the crowd, “Don't forget what I said!”
Ahab Dies at Ramoth
(1 Kings 22.29-35)
28Ahab and Jehoshaphat led their armies to Ramoth in Gilead. 29Before they went into battle, Ahab said, “Jehoshaphat, I'll disguise myself, but you wear your royal robe.” Ahab disguised himself and went into battle.
30The king of Syria had ordered his chariot commanders to attack only Ahab. 31So when they saw Jehoshaphat in his robe, they thought he was Ahab and started to attack him. But Jehoshaphat prayed, and the Lord made the Syrian soldiers stop. 32And when they realized he wasn't Ahab, they left him alone.
33However, during the fighting a soldier shot an arrow without even aiming, and it hit Ahab between two pieces of his armor. He shouted to his chariot driver, “I've been hit! Get me out of here!”
34The fighting lasted all day, with Ahab propped up in his chariot so he could see the Syrian troops. He stayed there until evening, and by sundown he was dead.
translation_text:
Joosafaati nì Isirayeel bɔtiu Akaab ŋá mpèé
(Kpèè 1 Bib 22.1-4)
1Joosafaati nìn ká tigaajati nì tinyool tikpil. U nìn yāntì u-dicaŋkun niliu ubɔ cáá Isirayeel bɔtiu Akaab dicaŋkun biki kiba. 2Abin aba boonee ní Joosafaati cūtìi māntì Akaab pu Samaarii tiŋkin. Akaab nìn kūū ipii nì inaa kupaau ki fōō u nì bin céeǹní-uee kucaŋu. U nìn páb́-u yii ú kūtì u-pu bí cùú já nì Ramooti tiŋki kin bí Galaadee. 3Isirayeel bɔtiu Akaab nìn bí Juuda bɔtiu Joosafaati yii: «A làá céeǹ-mi ḿ cùú já kí fōō Ramooti tiŋki kin bí Galaadi tiŋkpaaŋkineeee?» Ní Joosafaati kíí Isirayeel bɔtiu yii: «Man nì si sá unibaanti ní. A-nibul sá m-nibul ní. Ti làá kūtì a-pu tí cù kujaau.»
Tipɔjikaal bɔnaatiliibi nāatì dijajil
(Kpèè 1 Bib 22.5-12)
4Ama ní Joosafaati gíti kútì ki lī yii: «Tí bàlifì ti-Dindaan kí wàatī.» 5Niinee ní Isirayeel bɔtiu kóoǹ u-bɔnaatiliibi ki kpáfì. Bi nìn bí binib alaataa anaa nyɔkɔm ní ubɔti bālifì-bi yii: «Tí cùú já kí fōō Ramooti tiŋki kin bí Galaadi tiŋkpaaŋkeeyaaa, tí taa cù?» Ní bíǹ kíí-u yii: «Nín̄ cá! Ti-Dindaan dū-kì ki ŋá a-ŋaan.» 6Ama ní Joosafaati gíti bālifì yii: «Mimmee báà ti-Dindaan bɔnaatiliu ubɔ gíti kpá doo tí ŋmā kí cù u-cee kí bàlifì kí béé ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ pueeee?» 7Ní Isirayeel bɔtiu kíí Joosafaati yii: «Ubɔ gíti bí un pu ti ŋūǹ kí bàlifì kí béé ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee, ama maa là u-bɔti, di sá yii tin kaa ŋān̄ee ŋma ní u nàatī-mi, waa nàatī-mi tin ŋān̄ee dalba dalba. Úǹ di sá Yiimila jipɔɔn Miisee.» Ní Joosafaati bí yii: «Taa sòoǹ míǹ!» 8Niinee ní Isirayeel bɔtiu yíiń u-kàlinjau ubɔ ní ki bí-u yii: «Cùú cáań Yiimila jipɔɔn Miika doo malaa!»
9Isirayeel bɔtiu nì Juuda bɔtiu Joosafaati nìn kā báà ŋma u-beejal pu Samaarii tiŋki punyɔkɔki caŋin ki pēē bi-beebɔkutiŋ. Bibɔnaatiliibi kɔkɔ nìn bí ki nàatī tibɔti bi-nimbiin. 10Keenaana jipɔɔn Siideekiyawuu nìn dū tikúti ki mɔ́ɔ́ ŋyin. U nìn bí yii: «Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Nì ŋyin nee ní a làá dūú jáǹ Siirii yab kí céetí-bi múb.>» 11Bibɔnaatiliibi bin kɔkɔ nìn kíǹee nìn pée sòoǹ tibɔbaantiil ní ki lì yii: «A ŋūǹ kí cùú já kí fōō Ramooti tiŋki kin bí Galaadi tiŋkpaaŋkinee. A làá já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ-kì, ti-Dindaan làá dū-kì kí ŋá a-ŋaan.»
Miika nāatì yii Akaab kaa làá já kí jī
(Kpèè 1 Bib 22.13-28)
12Un bi tú ú cùú yíiń Miikayee bàn̄ee ní ki bí-u yii: «Kpèè, Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi kɔkɔ ŋá kinyɔɔbaantii ki sòoǹ ki nàatī ubɔti tiŋan ŋma ní. Si mun yaa bàn̄ee, á sòoǹ kí nàatī ubɔti tin ŋān̄ee ŋma kii bin béeyee.» 13Ama ní Miika kíí-u yii: «Nì ti-Dindaan un bí dimaŋfalin nee puee, tin ti-Dindaan yaa tīī-mi ḿ nàatēe, tíǹ ní m làá nàatī.»
14U bāań ubɔti ceeyee ní ubɔti bālifì-u yii: «Miika, tí cùú já kí fōō Ramooti tiŋki kin bí Galaadi tiŋkpaaŋkineeyaaa, tí taa cù?» Ní Miika kíí-u yii: «Nín̄ cá! A làá já kí fōō-kì! Ti-Dindaan dū kitiŋ gbanti ki ŋá a-ŋaan.» 15Ama ní ubɔti gíti bí-u yii: «Ŋfunyɔm miŋa ní m máaǹ kí yàntī á pùtī kí tùkù-mi ibaamɔn ti-Dindaan yindi pu ní á nín tùkù-mi ní?» 16Niinee ní Miika bí yii:
«M ká Isirayeel nibul
yàl̄ ki gbí ajoon pu
kii ipii in kaa cáá ukpaalee
Ní ti-Dindaan bí yii:
<Baa ti cáá ukpil.
Báà ŋma ń nīn gítí u-dumpu nì ŋgbansɔŋfi.>»
17Ní Isirayeel bɔtiu bí Joosafaati yii: «M bàà tùkū-si yii bee! Waa pée nàatī tin ŋān̄ee kí tīī-mi, see tikpitil!» 18Ama ní Miika gíti bí-u yii: «Too! Pīlifì tin ti-Dindaan sòon̄ee. M ká ti-Dindaan kā u-beejal pu ní yilpu janjaliibi yú ki kɔ́ĺ-u, biba yú u-ŋaŋgiil pú ní bin kíǹee yú u-ŋaŋgan pú. 19Ní ti-Dindaan bí yii: <Ŋma ní m làá nín ká ú cùú ŋmàtiǹ Akaab kí yàntī ú cùú já nì Ramooti tiŋki kin bí Galaadi tiŋkpaaŋkinee bí kpɔ̀-u ní?> Niinee ní ubɔ ń bí yii tina, ní un kíǹee ń bí yii tina. 20An ŋá mimmee ní ŋfam miba dɔ́miń ki síl̀ ti-Dindaan nimbiin ní ki bí yii: <Man di làá cù kí ŋmàtiǹ-u.> Ní ti-Dindaan bālifì-mì yii: <A làá ŋá mana ní?> 21Ní mì kíí yii: <M làá cù kí kɔ́ bibɔnaatiliibi kɔkɔn ní kí yàntī bí sòoǹ tinyimɔmbɔti kí tùkù ubɔti.> Ní ti-Dindaan bí-mì yii: <A làá cùú ŋmàtiǹ-u ní m nyí yii a làá ŋmā. Nín̄ cá kí ŋá míǹ.> 22Ti-Dindaan yaa lafun dū nnyimɔn fam ki ŋá a-bɔnaatiliibi kɔkɔ nyɔmmunee, á béé yii u là dinimbinaamandi ń jēetí a-pu ní.»
23Niinee ní Keenaana jipɔɔn Siideekiyawuu sútì ki pìl̄ Miika ní ki fáá-u ntampa ki lī yii: «La pú ní ti-Dindaan Fam nyáń m-ni ki cūtìi bíi sòoǹ nì si?» 24Ní Miika kíí yii: «Tiŋman, ŋwiin ŋun ní a yaa láa sáń ki póotí adiin ki bāal̀ee, a làá dāá gbìl̄ taapu.» 25Niinee ní Isirayeel bɔtiu tīī mara yii: «Ní cúúmaan Miika kí cùnnì kí tīī Amɔn tiŋki kɔmandaŋwu nì ubɔti jipɔɔn Yoowasi, 26ní kí tùkù-bi yii: <Man ubɔti di bí yii, ní dū kijapaai nee kí tɔ̄ sarka. Ní tīī-u tijin ŋwaam pu nì nnyim kí nīn cí ŋyunti ŋun m làá fàtīí gítiń nì ŋgbansɔŋfee.>» 27Ní Miika bí-u yii: «A yaa fātìi gítìń nì laafiyee, mimmee ti-Dindaan kaa dī m-pu ki sòon̄ dee.» Ní u gíti kútì yii: «Nimbi samaa kɔkɔ, pīlifìmaan!»
Bi kūū ubɔti Akaab dikɔ̀ndin
(Kpèè 1 Bib 22.29-40)
28 Isirayeel bɔtiu Akaab nì Juuda bɔtiu Joosafaati nín cá kí já nì Ramooti tiŋki kin bí Galaadi tiŋkpaaŋkinee. 29Ní Isirayeel bɔtiu bí Joosafaati yii: «M làá kpántí m-wampeeŋkaati bí taa béé-mi ní kí cùú já kujaau. Ama siiyee, dū a-beebɔkutil kí pèen̄.» Ní Isirayeel bɔtiu lafun kpántì u-wampeeŋkaati bí taa béé-u ní ki cūtìi bíi jáà. 30Siirii mun bɔtiu nìn tīī u-janjaliibi mmuŋku nì saalaa nì bili bin sá bin kpèé janjatɔrɔkub kpilibee mara yii: «Ní taa já nì bijanjaliibi ŋwaamuɔɔɔ, kí taa já nì bijanjakpilib, ama ní pée já nì Isirayeel bɔtiu baba.» 31An pu ní bin kpèé janjatɔrɔkub kpilibee nín ká Joosafaatee, bi bí yii: «Báà an ŋá pu, Isirayeel bɔtiu dee», ní bi fātì bi-ba ki túĺ-u ki bíi jáà nì u, ní Joosafaati kíĺ ki bíi kūuntí. 32Niinee ní bijanjakpilibee nín béè yii an kaa sá Isirayeel bɔtiu ní bi yāntì-u kaa tí bíi jì-u.
33Ama Siirii yab janjaliu ubɔ pée tɔ́ mpiin yìkíl̄ yikil ní an cūtìi yá Isirayeel bɔtiu laakin u-gbampɔɔl janliitiliŋ tūū tɔbee. Ní ubɔti bí un ŋàal̀ u-tɔrɔkuuee yii: «Fàtīí gítí a-boon tí nyā dikɔmbool pu, di sá m ká tiweendi.» 34Ama ŋwiin gbantee, kujaau nín nìn pɔ́ɔkì puee, bi nìn yāntì ubɔti yú u-tɔrɔkuu poon ki túĺ Siirii yab áli kujoou, ní u kpíì.

english_text:
1Jehoshaphat returned safely to his palace in Jerusalem. 2But the prophet Jehu son of Hanani met him and said:
By helping that wicked Ahab, you have made friends with someone who hates the Lord. Now the Lord God is angry with you! 3But not everything about you is bad. You destroyed the sacred poles used in worshiping the goddess Asherah—that shows you have tried to obey the Lord.
Jehoshaphat Appoints Judges To Settle Cases
4Jehoshaphat lived in Jerusalem, but he often traveled through his kingdom, from Beersheba in the south to the edge of the hill country of Ephraim in the north. He talked with the people and convinced them to turn back to the Lord God and worship him, just as their ancestors had done.
5He assigned judges to each of the fortified cities in Judah 6and told them:
Be careful when you make your decisions in court, because you are judging by the Lord's standards and not by human standards, and he will know what you decide. 7So do your work in honor of him and know that he won't allow you to be unfair to anyone or to take bribes.
8Jehoshaphat also chose some Levites, some priests, and some of the family leaders, and he appointed them to serve as judges in Jerusalem. 9He told them:
Faithfully serve the Lord! 10The people of Judah will bring you legal cases that involve every type of crime, including murder. You must settle these cases and warn the people to stop sinning against the Lord, so that he won't get angry and punish Judah. Remember, if you follow these instructions, you won't be held responsible for anything that happens.
11Amariah the high priest will have the final say in any religious case. And Zebadiah, the leader of the Judah tribe, will have the final say in all other cases. The rest of the Levites will serve as your assistants. Be brave, and I pray that the Lord will help you do right.
translation_text:
Joosafaati kāaǹ bibɔsoonliibi Juuda tiŋkin
1Juuda bɔtiu Joosafaati nìn fātìi gítì Jeerusaleem nì ŋgbampɔn. 2Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeewuu, Ananii jipɔɔn nìn túŋkì-u nsanni ní ki bí-u yii: «Ba pu ní a cūtìi tútúǹ unikpiti? Mimmee sii néeń bin ná ti-Dindaaneeee? Kun ní a ŋée puee, ti-Dindaan gíí a-pu diŋuul. 3Nì míǹ kɔkɔee a túń atummɔnti. A wùn̄ diwaal Aseera windɔi Juuda tiŋki kɔkɔn ní ki nyàab̄ ti-Dindaan nì dipɔbil diba.»
4Joosafaati nìn kóò Jeerusaleem ní. Ama u nìn yìiǹ Juuda tiŋki kɔkɔ pu kí yòon̄ Beerseeba kí tin cáá sāā Eefiraayiim jooŋŋi pu. U nìn sòoǹ nì binib bí fàtīí gítiń ti-Dindaan, bi-baabi Nimbɔtiu cee. 5Juuda timmu mun bi nìn máń agun ki túee kɔkɔ poonee, u nìn kāaǹ bibɔsoonliibi. 6U nìn bí-bi yii: «Ní tɔ̄maan ni-tundi tiŋan. Di sá yii an kaa sá nniyaamin ní ni làá dūú sòoǹ tibɔti, ama nì ti-Dindaan yindi pu ní ni làá dūú sòoǹ. Ni yaa láa bíi sòoǹ tibɔtee, úǹ u-ba làá dāá nīn bí ni-cee. 7Míǹ puee, ní yàntī ti-Dindaan faaŋku ń nīn bí ni-ni. Ní nīn ŋúb́ tin m tùkū-ni nee kí ŋámaan míǹ. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu kaa gèetíǹ bin kaa sòoǹ tibɔti nì ibaamɔnee, àá bin pɔ̀ gandee, àá bin fòol̄ dinyɔɔŋeebil jim kí sòoǹ kí pɔ̀ ubɔee.»
8Ki kpáaǹ Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee, Joosafaati nìn lēē Leefii yab nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì Isirayeel dicaŋŋi kpilib biba ki kāaǹ bí nīn sòoǹ tibɔti ti-Dindaan yindi pu, ní kí nīn ŋáŋkí Jeerusaleem yab bɔti. 9U nìn tīī-bi mara nee yii: «Ni máaǹ kí tɔ̄ ni-tundi nì ti-Dindaan faaŋku poon nì deedee poon nì dipɔbil diba. 10Tí dūú ŋmàntī yii ni-nabiyaamu nyánní ntimu mun poon ní bi kóòyee ki cáań-ni tibɔti ní sòoǹ. An ŋūǹ kí nīn sá nnikpaakoon bɔti, àá mara bɔti, àá abɔkpaa bɔti, àá akoobil bɔti tiba. Too an yaa pée sá tiŋyee, ní dàkà-bi tin bi máaǹ kí ŋée. Mimmee baa làá yìntīǹ ti-Dindaan ní waa nín gíí ni-pu àá ni-nabiyaamu pu diŋuul. Ni yaa ŋá míǹ, naa làá fōō dibɔkpil. 11Usaraaŋakpil Amariyawuu di làá nīn kpèé dinimbɔtinool bɔti ki tìì-ni. Juuda beel kàlinjakpiliu Seebadiyawuu, Isimaayeel jipɔɔn di làá nīn kpèé dibeel pu bɔti. Leefii yab làá nīn bí ni-cee ki tútúǹ-ni ni kpèé kitiŋ pu bɔti. Ní kámaan dipɔbil kí tɔ̄ ni-tundi! Ti-Dindaan ń nīn bí bin ŋáań tiŋanee cee.»

english_text:
Moab and Ammon Are Defeated
1Some time later, the armies of Moab and Ammon, together with the Meunites, went to war against Jehoshaphat. 2Messengers told Jehoshaphat, “A large army from Edom east of the Dead Sea has invaded our country. They have already reached En-Gedi.”
3Jehoshaphat was afraid, so he asked the Lord what to do. He then told the people of Judah to go without eating to show their sorrow. 4They immediately left for Jerusalem to ask for the Lord's help.
5After everyone from Judah and Jerusalem had come together at the Lord's temple, Jehoshaphat stood in front of the new courtyard 6and prayed:
You, Lord, are the God our ancestors worshiped, and from heaven you rule every nation in the world. You are so powerful that no one can defeat you. 7 Our God, you forced out the nations who lived in this land before your people Israel came here, and you gave it to the descendants of your friend Abraham forever. 8Our ancestors lived in this land and built a temple to honor you. 9They believed that whenever this land is struck by war or disease or famine, your people can pray to you at the temple, and you will hear their prayer and save them.
10 You can see that the armies of Ammon, Moab, and Edom are attacking us! Those are the nations you would not let our ancestors invade on their way from Egypt, so these nations were not destroyed. 11Now they are coming to take back the land you gave us. 12Aren't you going to punish them? We won't stand a chance when this army attacks. We don't know what to do—we are begging for your help.
13While every man, woman, and child of Judah was standing there at the temple, 14the Lord's Spirit suddenly spoke to Jahaziel, a Levite from the Asaph clan. 15 Then Jahaziel said:
Your Majesty and everyone from Judah and Jerusalem, the Lord says that you don't need to be afraid or let this powerful army discourage you. God will fight on your side! 16So here's what you must do. Tomorrow the enemy armies will march through the desert around the town of Jeruel. March down and meet them at the town of Ziz as they come up the valley. 17 You won't even have to fight. Just take your positions and watch the Lord rescue you from your enemy. Don't be afraid. Just do as you're told. And as you march out tomorrow, the Lord will be there with you.
18Jehoshaphat bowed low to the ground and everyone worshiped the Lord. 19Then some Levites from the Kohath and Korah clans stood up and shouted praises to the Lord God of Israel.
20Early the next morning, as everyone got ready to leave for the desert near Tekoa, Jehoshaphat stood up and said, “Listen my friends, if we trust the Lord God and believe what these prophets have told us, the Lord will help us, and we will be successful.” 21Then he explained his plan and appointed men to march in front of the army and praise the Lord for his holy power by singing:
“Praise the Lord!
His love never ends.”
22As soon as they began singing, the Lord confused the enemy camp, 23so that the Ammonite and Moabite troops attacked and completely destroyed those from Edom. Then they turned against each other and fought until the entire camp was wiped out!
24When Judah's army reached the tower that overlooked the desert, they saw that every soldier in the enemy's army was lying dead on the ground. 25So Jehoshaphat and his troops went into the camp to carry away everything of value. They found a large herd of livestock, a lot of equipment, clothes, and other valuable things. It took them three days to carry it all away, and there was still some left over.
26Then on the fourth day, everyone came together in Beracah Valley and sang praises to the Lord. That's why that place was called Praise Valley.
27-28Jehoshaphat led the crowd back to Jerusalem. And as they marched, they played harps and blew trumpets. They were very happy because the Lord had given them victory over their enemies, so when they reached the city, they went straight to the temple.
29When the other nations heard how the Lord had fought against Judah's enemies, they were too afraid 30to invade Judah. The Lord let Jehoshaphat's kingdom be at peace.
Jehoshaphat Dies
(1 Kings 22.41-50)
31Jehoshaphat was 35 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled from Jerusalem for 25 years. His mother was Azubah daughter of Shilhi. 32Jehoshaphat obeyed the Lord, just as his father Asa had done, 33but he did not destroy the local shrines. So the people still worshiped foreign gods, instead of faithfully serving the God their ancestors had worshiped.
34Everything else Jehoshaphat did while he was king is written in the records of Jehu son of Hanani that are included in The History of the Kings of Israel.
35While Jehoshaphat was king, he signed a peace treaty with Ahaziah the wicked king of Israel. 36They agreed to build several seagoing ships at Ezion-Geber. 37But the prophet Eliezer warned Jehoshaphat, “The Lord will destroy these ships because you have supported Ahaziah.” The ships were wrecked and never sailed.
translation_text:
Amɔn yab dɔ́miń kí já nì Juuda yab
1Míǹ boonee ní Moowaab yab nì Amɔn yab, kí dūú kūtì Meewun yab dɔ́miń kí já nì Joosafaati. 2Ní bi dɔ́miń ki tùkū Joosafaati yii: «Dijanjakitikpaandi diba dòoń kí jáǹ-si. Dì nyánní Ŋyaam Mɔɔgbandi lapu yal pú, an dàkà yii Eedoom tiŋkin. Dì bāań Asasɔn-Tamaar, an dàkà yii Eeni-Geedii.» 3Joosafaati nìn fāŋkì, ní ki nìn lēē yii u làá mēē ti-Dindaan. U nìn tīī mara yii Juuda beel kɔkɔn bí bóob́ kinyɔkɔ. 4Juuda yab nìn nyánní Juuda timmu kɔkɔn ki kóoǹ ki kpáfì Jeerusaleem kí mèè ti-Dindaan. 5Joosafaati nìn yíkìi yúl̀ Juuda yab nì Jeerusaleem yab kansikin, ti-Dindaan Diikun ki túĺ Dicimpɔndi. 6U nìn bí yii: «Ti-Dindaan, ti-baabi Nimbɔtiu, sii di bí yilpu ní ki jīǹ atimbun kɔkɔ pu dibeel. Sii di cáá mpɔn nì dikpabil ní ubɔ kaa ŋūǹ kí sīĺ a-nimbiin kí jáǹ-si. 7Sii ti-Nimbɔtiu di nìn jìn̄ kitiŋ nee pu nib ŋyunti ŋun Isirayeel yab, a-nibul nìn dòońee. A dū kitiŋ nee ki tīī a-bɔɔ Abraam naantiibi kí nīn cá jaanjaan. 8Bi nìn kāl̀ kitiŋee poon ní ki máń-si ŋkɔŋkoon ki lī yii: 9<Nnaabu ŋubɔ yaa jéetì ti-pu, an ŋūǹ kí nīn sá yii kujaau, àá ditafadaaldi diba àá bìlbil kúm àá ŋkùm, ti làá dāan̄ kí yūĺ ŋkɔŋkoon nee nyɔkɔpu, an dàkà yii a-nimbiin, di sá yii niin ní a lèekī a-ba ki dàkà. Ti làá kúuǹ kí yíiń-si ti-nimbinaamandi poon. Niinee, a làá pīlifiǹ-ti ní kí fīī-ti.> 10Too, kɔŋkɔnnee, Amɔn yab nì Moowaab yab nì Eedoom yab dɔ́miń kí já nì ti. Ti-naanjab nín nìn nyánní Eejipiti tiŋkin ki dòońee, aa nìn pú-bi nsan bí dī bi-tiŋki pu. An puee ti-baabi nìn dūu dī nsan ŋubɔ fám ní ki yāntì-bi kaa kūū ki céetì-bi. 11Ama kpèè binib gbanti nín bíi pà-ti tipaal tiŋyee! Bi dɔ́miń kí jà-ti kitiŋ kin a dūu tīī-tee pu. 12Ti-Nimbɔtiu, mimmee aa làá dáaĺ bi-tafalaaa? Di sá yii binib bin dòoń kí já nì ti nee wīikí tikpil ní taa cáá mpɔn kí ŋmā kí sīĺ bi-nimbiin. Taa nyí ti nín làá ŋá puee, ama ti-nimbikpeeŋu cɔ́ a-pu ní.» 13Juuda yab kɔkɔ, ki kpáaǹ bi-nimpoobi nì bi-biyaamu nìn yú ti-Dindaan nimbiin.
Ti-Dindaan tīī Juuda yab dijajil
14Ti-Dindaan Fam nìn kpákatìń uleefiija ubɔ pu samaa kansikin. Bi nìn yíì-u Yasiyeel ní u nìn sá Asafi maaliŋun. U-baa di nìn sá Seekariyawuu ní u-naanja sá Beenaya ní u-naanja Beenaya baa sá Yeeyiyeel, Mataniya jipɔɔn. 15Yasiyeel nìn bí yii: «Nimbi Juuda yab, Jeerusaleem yab nì sii ubɔti Joosafaati, ní pīlifìmaan! Ti-Dindaan nín bíi sòoǹ nì ni puee sèé: <Ni-pɔbiliŋ ń taa bīil̀, kí taa fàŋkì dijanjakitikpaandi nee, di sá yii kujaau nee kaa sá ni-jaaku, ama an sá man ni-Nimbɔtiu jaaku ní. 16Foolee, ní fu cùú já nì bi. Bi bíi dàb̀ Nsupumpukum gbantaŋki. Ni làá fu ká-bi ditantakal nín kúntí puee, Yeeruweel teeku nyɔkɔpu. 17An kaa fu bàlifī ní já nì bi. Nimbi dee, ní fu nyā kí yūĺ kí kpèè dijajil din ti-Dindaan làá fu tīī-nee. Juuda nì Jeerusaleem yab, ni-pɔbiliŋ ń taa bīil̀, ní taa fàŋkì! Foolee, ní fu nyā kí tūŋkì-bi, man ni-Dindaan làá fu nín̄ bí ni-cee.>»
18Niinee Joosafaati tātìi gbāaǹ u-yigbeel tūū kitiŋ. Juuda yab nì Jeerusaleem yab kɔkɔ mun nìn tātìi gbāaǹ kitiŋ ti-Dindaan nimbiin ki bíi jáaḿ-u. 19Míǹ boonee ní Leefii yab bin sá Keeyaati nì Kooree maaliŋunee yíkìi yúl̀. Bi nìn gāā ilan mpɔn ki nyɔ́ŋkì ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu.
20Kutaa wúntì kutaafaau pɔ̀lpɔlee ní bi-kɔkɔ kíĺ nsan ki nín cá Teekoowa teekun. Kí wàatī bí yīkèe ní Joosafaati bí-bi yii: «Juuda nì Jeerusaleem yab, ní pīlifìmaan. Ní nīn máká ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu pu, ní ubɔ kaa làá já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ-ni! Ní nīn máká u-bɔnaatiliibi pu ní kí ká dijajil!» 21Míǹ boonee ní u nì samaa sòon̄ ki bɔ́ntì ní ki lēē bilaŋgaaliibi ki dū circir bɔkutiŋ ki pēeǹ-bi ní bíǹ līī dijanjakitil nyɔkɔpu ki gà ilan ki nyɔ́ŋkí ti-Dindaan u nín sá circir ki sá ukpaan puee ki lì yii: «Nyɔ̄ŋkìmaan ti-Dindaan, di sá yii u-neendi bí ní ki cá jaanjaan.» 22Ŋyunti ŋun bi kíĺ ki bíi gà inyɔŋki laŋyee ní ti-Dindaan yāntì fikil fikil dɔ́miń ki kɔ́ Amɔn yab nì Moowaab yab nì Seeyiir jool yab bin nìn dɔ́miń kí já nì Juuda yabee kansikin. Bi nìn kíĺ ki bíi jáà nì tɔb. 23Amɔn yab nì Moowaab yab nìn bíi jáà nì Seeyiir jool yab ní ki kūū ki céetì-bi múb. Míǹ boonee ní bi nyáń tɔb pu ki kūū ki céetì tɔb. 24Ŋyunti ŋun Juuda yab jɔ́m̀ laakin bi ŋūǹ kí tɔ́kɔń kí wāl̀ kuteeu puee ki kpēē dijanjakitikpaandi watil púee, anikpil ŋmaniŋma di dɔ̄ kitiŋ fìlfilee. Uniseen kaa nìn kíǹ. 25Niinee Joosafaati nì u-samaau cūtì ki fúkúl̀ anikpilee wanti ní ki ká tiwaŋkuti tikpil nì tigaajawan tikpil nì tiwampeeŋkaal nì tiwan tin cáá kunyampoouee tikpil. Tiwan nìn wīikí tikpil áli gba baa nìn gíti ŋūǹ kí túń. Bi nìn dū iwiin ita ní ki kóoǹ tiwaŋfukulkaal gbanti, di sá yii tì nìn wīikí tikpilku. 26Ŋwinnanaati dalee ní bi kóoǹ ki kpáfì Beeraka tantakalin kí jāam̀ ti-Dindaan. An pu ní bi pú ditantakal gbanti diyindi yii Beeraka, taapu sá yii «si nì ditundi». 27Niinee ní Joosafaati līntì Juuda yab nì Jeerusaleem yab nyɔkɔpu ní bi nín gítí Jeerusaleem nì mmɔn poon, di sá yii ti-Dindaan nìn fīī-bi ki nyántì bi-nannanliibi ŋaan ki tīī-bi dipɔɔpindi. 28Bi nìn bɔ̀ɔ́ tibati, ki búǹ awul nì akantán ní ki dūu kɔ́ Jeerusaleem tiŋkin ki tin nyáń ti-Dindaan Diiku pu. 29Atimbun ŋin kɔkɔ kíǹee beeŋi nìn gbìl̄ ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín jáń nì Isirayeel nannanliibi puee, bi nìn fāŋkì tikpil. 30Joosafaati beel nìn bí ŋgbansɔŋfin, di sá yii u-Nimbɔtiu nìn tīī-u diŋuŋfil ijaan kɔkɔ pu.
Joosafaati beel nín kúntì puee
(Kpèè 1 Bib 22.41-51)
31Joosafaati nìn cáá abin aŋmoo kpá imuŋku ili ní ki kpántì Juuda bɔtiu, ní ki kāl̀ Jeerusaleem abin mmuŋku nì aŋmoo ki jíń dibeel. Bi nìn yíì u-na Asuuba, Siilii bisal. 32U nìn nóó u-baa Asaa tabɔbiliŋ ní deedee, ní ki nìn ŋá tin fáatiǹ ti-Dindaanee. 33Ama waa nìn gbáń ki kpītì isaraafan in nìn bí ŋgbantamu puee, ní samaa kaa nìn nóó bi-baabi Nimbɔtiu nì dipɔbil diba. 34Joosafaati tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee kí yòon̄ ŋi nín kíĺ puee kí cáá sāā ŋi nín kúntì puee ŋmàn̄ ki kā Ananii jipɔɔn Yeewuu gbɔntin. Bi nìn dū tigbɔn gbanti ki sákaǹ Isirayeel bɔtiibi gbɔŋkun.
35Kí kūtèe, Juuda bɔtiu Joosafaati nìn ŋá mpèé nì Isirayeel bɔtiu Akasiyasi. Ubɔti gbanti bimbim kaa nìn ŋān̄. 36U nì u nìn kpáfì ki kpáá meelab bin làá nīn cáà Taarsiisee. Eesiiyɔn-Geebeer tiŋkin ní bi nìn kpáá meelab gbanti. 37Ama Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Eeliyeeseer, Doodafa jipɔɔn un sá Mareesa tiŋkinee nìn fōō tibɔti ki nāatì Joosafaati yii: «A nín ŋá pu ní a nì Akasiyasi ŋá mpèéyee, ti-Dindaan bíil̀ ditundi din ní a túńee.» Tiŋman míǹ ní an lafun jítì, meelabee nìn bíil̀ kaa ŋúń ki cūtì Taarsiisi.

english_text:
1Jehoshaphat died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Jehoram became king.
King Jehoram of Judah
(2 Kings 8.16-24)
2King Jehoshaphat had seven sons: Jehoram, Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariah, Michael, and Shephatiah. 3Jehoshaphat gave each of them silver and gold, as well as other valuable gifts. He also put them in charge of the fortified cities in Judah, but he had chosen his oldest son Jehoram to succeed him as king.
4After Jehoram had taken control of Judah, he had his brothers killed, as well as some of the nation's leaders. 5He was 32 years old when he became king, and he ruled eight years from Jerusalem.
6Jehoram married Ahab's daughter and followed the sinful example of Ahab's family and the other kings of Israel. He disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong, 7 but because the Lord had made a solemn promise to King David that someone from his family would always rule in Judah, he refused to wipe out David's descendants.
8 While Jehoram was king, the people of Edom rebelled and chose their own king. 9Jehoram, his officers, and his cavalry marched to Edom, where the Edomite army surrounded them. He escaped during the night, 10but Judah was never able to regain control of Edom. Even the town of Libnah rebelled at that time.
Those things happened because Jehoram had turned away from the Lord, the God his ancestors had worshiped. 11Jehoram even built local shrines in the hills of Judah and let the people sin against the Lord by worshiping foreign gods.
12One day, Jehoram received a letter from Elijah the prophet that said:
I have a message for you from the Lord God your ancestor David worshiped. He knows that you have not followed the example of Jehoshaphat your father or Asa your grandfather. 13Instead you have acted like those sinful kings of Israel and have encouraged the people of Judah to stop worshiping the Lord, just as Ahab and his descendants did. You even murdered your own brothers, who were better men than you.
14Because you have done these terrible things, the Lord will severely punish the people in your kingdom, including your own family, and he will destroy everything you own. 15You will be struck with a painful stomach disease and suffer until you die.
16The Lord later caused the Philistines and the Arabs who lived near the Ethiopians to become angry with Jehoram. 17They invaded Judah and stole the royal property from the palace, and they led Jehoram's wives and sons away as prisoners. The only one left behind was Ahaziah, his youngest son.
18After this happened, the Lord struck Jehoram with an incurable stomach disease. 19About two years later, Jehoram died in terrible pain. No bonfire was built to honor him, even though the people had done this for his ancestors.
20Jehoram was 32 years old when he became king, and he ruled 8 years from Jerusalem. He died, and no one even felt sad. He was buried in Jerusalem, but not in the royal tombs.
translation_text:
1Joosafaati kpíì ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ u-baabee ní bi síb́-u ki kɔ́ĺ-bi, Daafiidi Tiŋkin. U-jipɔɔn Jooram di fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.
Jooram beel
(Kpèè 2 Bib 8.16-24)
2Joosafaati jipɔɔn Jooram nìn cáá naalib pēē baa. Bíǹ di sá Asariya nì Yeeyiyeel nì Seekariyawuu nì Asariyawuu nì Miikayeel nì Seefatiyawuu. 3Bi-baa Joosafaati nìn púb́-bi animbil nì sindaariya nì tiwan tin cáá kunyampoouee tikpil. U nìn gíti tīī-bi Juuda timmu mun bi máń agun ki túee bí nīn kpòotī. Ama Jooram ní u nìn lēē ú fōō u-yil kí kpántí ubɔti, di sá yii úǹ di nìn sá ujipɔŋkpil.
4Jooram nìn fōō u-baa beel ki kpántì ubɔti ní ki báaǹ inyaan. Míǹ boonee ní u cúú u-naalib kɔkɔ ki lāntì, ki kpáaǹ Isirayeel bɔtibiliŋ aba. 5Jooram nìn cáá abin mmuŋku nì saalaa nì ali ní ki kpántì ubɔti, ní ki kāl̀ dibeel pu Jeerusaleem abin anii. 6U nìn pée nóó Isirayeel bɔtiibi tabɔbiliŋ ní, a lì kii Akaab dicaŋkun yab nín nìn bí puee, di sá u nìn cáá Akaab bisal ubɔ ní. U nìn ŋá tin kaa nìn kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee. 7Ama ti-Dindaan tɔntɔnliu Daafiidi puee, waa nìn là kí nàan̄ Juuda tiŋki, kun puee u nìn pōoǹ Daafiidi yii u-jipɔmbi làá nīn pée kā dibeel pu Jeerusaleem ní kí nīn cá jaanjaan.
8Jooram beel yuntiŋu ní Eedoom yab yíkì kaa kíí bi-ba pu kí nīn gbíntìi bí Juuda yab taapu ní ki kāaǹ bi-ba nì bi-bɔtiu. 9Jooram nìn yíkì ki nín cá Seeyiir tiŋkin ki kpáaǹ u-janjatɔrɔkub kɔkɔ. Ama kunyeeuee ní u nì u-janjatɔrɔkub kpootiliibi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Eedoom yab bin nìn māntìi tú-bee. 10Kí yòon̄ yaadal wiiŋŋu gbanti ní Eedoom yab fōō bi-ba kaa ti bí Juuda yab taapu.
Ŋyunti gbanti mbaanti ní Liibina yab mun kaa kíí bi-ba pu. 11Jooram u-ba nìn máń iwaatootipaan Juuda jooŋŋi pu, ní ki yāntì Jeerusaleem yab nì Juuda yab kɔ́ tijɔkɔndin ki dū Unimbɔti ki fá.
12Dalbee ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu ŋmàn̄-u kugbɔŋu ki bí-u yii: «Ti-Dindaan, a-naanja Daafiidi Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Aa dī a-baa Joosafaati tabɔbiliŋ kaa ti dī a-naanja Asaa, Juuda bɔtiu tabɔbiliŋ. 13Ama a dī Isirayeel yab bɔtiibi saŋŋu ki yāntì Jeerusaleem yab nì Juuda yab bíi tòotī awaa kii Akaab dicaŋkun yab nín ŋáań puee. Áli gba a kūū a-naalib bin nìn sɔ́ǹ-see. 14An pu ní ti-Dindaan làá cáań atulim ki tɔ̄ a-nibul nì a-jipɔmbi nì a-nimpoobi nì a-gaajawanti kɔkɔ pu. 15Sii a-bee, tiweeŋkpiil di làá cúú-si, iween in làá ŋmɔ́ kí bà a-nai ní kí nīn púntí-si baabadal áli a-nai ń dāá nyā mpaampiin puee.»
16Niinee ti-Dindaan yāntì Fiiliistii yab nì Bilaalibub bin kóò ki pìlīǹ Kuusi yabee dɔ́miń kí já nì Jooram. 17Bi nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Juuda yab ní ki kɔ́ kitiŋin ki kóoǹ tigaajawan tin kɔkɔ nìn bí ubɔti dicaŋkunee. Bi nìn kpáaǹ u-jipɔmbi nì u-nimpoobi. U-jipɔŋwaaliu Akasiya baba ní bi nìn kíǹ-u. 18Míǹ boonee ní ti-Dindaan yāntì ina weeŋyi in baa ŋūǹ kí cáaǹee dɔ́miń ki cúú-u. 19An pée bí míǹ ki cá abin ali boonee, iweenee píĺ-u ní u-nai nyáń, ní u dāa kpíì nsansaaŋkúm. U-naacimbi kaa nìn kpāā ŋŋmi ki súń u-kpool kii bi nín nìn ŋá pu ki tīī u-naanjab tinyoolee.
20Jooram nìn cáá abin mmuŋku nì saalaa nì ali ní ki kpántì ubɔti ní ki kāl̀ Jeerusaleem tiŋkin ki jíń dibeel abin anii. U nín kpíìyee, ubɔ nì ubɔ kaa yáliŋkì u-pu. Bi nìn síb́-u Daafiidi Tiŋkin, ama baa nìn síb́-u bibɔtiibi kaakuliŋin.

english_text:
King Ahaziah of Judah
(2 Kings 8.25-29; 9.21,27,28)
1Earlier, when the Arabs led a raid against Judah, they killed all of Jehoram's sons, except Ahaziah, the youngest one. So the people of Jerusalem crowned him their king. 2He was 22 years old at the time, and he ruled only one year from Jerusalem.
Ahaziah's mother was Athaliah, a granddaughter of King Omri of Israel, 3and she encouraged her son to sin against the Lord. He followed the evil example of King Ahab and his descendants. 4In fact, after his father's death, Ahaziah sinned against the Lord by appointing some of Ahab's relatives to be his advisors.
Their advice led to his downfall. 5He listened to them and went with King Joram of Israel to attack King Hazael and the Syrian troops at Ramoth in Gilead. Joram was wounded in that battle, 6and he went to the town of Jezreel to recover. And Ahaziah later went there to visit him. 7It was during that visit that God had Ahaziah put to death.
When Ahaziah arrived at Jezreel, he and Joram went to meet with Jehu grandson of Nimshi. The Lord had already told Jehu to kill every male in Ahab's family, 8and while Jehu was doing that, he saw some of Judah's leaders and Ahaziah's nephews who had come with Ahaziah. Jehu killed them on the spot, 9then gave orders to find Ahaziah. Jehu's officers found him hiding in Samaria. They brought Ahaziah to Jehu, who immediately put him to death. They buried Ahaziah only because they respected Jehoshaphat his grandfather, who had done his best to obey the Lord.
There was no one from Ahaziah's family left to become king of Judah.
Queen Athaliah of Judah
(2 Kings 11.1-3)
10As soon as Athaliah heard that her son King Ahaziah was dead, she decided to kill any relative who could possibly become king. She would have done just that, 11but Jehosheba rescued Joash son of Ahaziah just as the others were about to be murdered. Jehosheba, who was Jehoram's daughter and Ahaziah's half sister, was married to Jehoiada the priest. So she was able to hide her nephew Joash and his personal servant in a bedroom in the Lord's temple where he was safe from Athaliah. 12Joash hid in the temple with them for six years while Athaliah ruled as queen of Judah.
translation_text:
Juuda bɔtiu Akasiyasi bɔti
(Kpèè 2 Bib 8.25-29, 9.27-29)
1Jeerusaleem yab nìn yāntì ubɔti Jooram jipɔɔn Akasiyasi un sá uwaalee di fōō u-baa yil ki kpántì ubɔti. Di sá yii Bilaalibub bin nìn dɔ́miń ki jáń nì Juuda yabee nìn kūū u-mambi kɔkɔ. Míǹ ní Jooram jipɔɔn Akasiyasi dūu kpántì Juuda bɔtiu. 2Akasiyasi nìn cáá abin imuŋku ili nì ali ní ki kpántì ubɔti, ní ki kāl̀ Jeerusaleem ki jíń dibeel dibindi diba. Bi nìn yíì u-na yii Atalii, Oomirii bisal. 3Úǹ mun nìn nóó Akaab dicaŋkun yab tabɔbiliŋ ní, di sá yii u-na di nìn sáŋkí-u ú nīn ŋáań tin kaa ŋān̄ee. 4U nìn ŋá tin kaa fáatiǹ ti-Dindaanee kii Akaab dicaŋkun yabee, di sá yii u-baa kúm boonee, bíǹ di kpántì u-saŋkiliibi ní bi-sansaŋkii gbanti nāaǹ-u. 5Bíǹ di sáŋkì-u ní u nì Isirayeel bɔtiu Jooram, Akaab jipɔɔn cūtìi jáń nì Aram bɔtiu Asayeel, Ramooti tiŋki kin bí Galaadi tiŋkpaaŋkinee. Ama bi bíi jáàyee ní Aram yab tīī Jooram tiweendi. 6Ní Jooram nín gítí Jisirayeel kí cáaǹ tiweendi tin u fōō Siirii yab cee Raama tiŋkin ŋyunti ŋun u nìn bíi jáà nì Siirii bɔtiu Asayeelee. U bí Jisirayeel niinee ní Juuda bɔti Akasiyasi, Jooram jipɔɔn cūtì kí màntì u-pu.
7Akasiyasi nín nìn cūtìi māntì Jooram pu puee ní ti-Dindaan dī an pu ki nāaǹ-u. Di sá u bàn̄ee ní u nì Jooram nyáń kí já nì Nimisii jipɔɔn Jeewuu. Tin waa nyée di sá yii ti-Dindaan di nìn yāntì Jeewuu kpántì ubɔti kí nàan̄ Akaab dicaŋku. 8Ŋyunti ŋun ní Jeewuu bíi dátí Akaab dicaŋku yab tafalee ní ki ká Juuda bɔtibiliŋ nì Akasiyasi nabiyaamu mun bí ubɔti tundinee ní u kūū ki céetì-bi. 9Míǹ boonee ní u yāntì bi nyàab̄ Akasiyasi. Bi nìn ká-u u cūtìi bál̀ Samaarii tiŋkin, ní bi cúú-u ki cáań Jeewuu cee ní úǹ kūū-u. Bi nìn síb́-u, di sá yii bi nìn lī yii: «Joosafaati un nìn nyàab̄ ti-Dindaan nì u-pɔbil kɔkɔee jipɔɔn dee.»
Ubɔ kaa nìn gíti kíǹ Akasiyasi dicaŋkun kí ŋmā kí kpántí ubɔti.
Atalii fōō dibeel mpɔn
(Kpèè 2 Bib 11.1-3)
10Akasiyasi na Atalii nín ká yii u-jipɔɔn kpíìyee ní u lēē yii u làá kpɔ̀ kí céetí ubɔti naantiibi kɔkɔ. 11Ama ubɔti Jooram bisal Yooseeba nìn ŋúń ki yōoǹ Akasiyasi jipɔɔn Joowaasi u-mambi kansikin baa ŋúń ki kūū-u. U nìn cáá kibikee nì ki-bilooliu ki bál̀ kunimbɔtidii didooŋkaaku kubɔn. Míǹ ní ubɔti Jooram bisal Yooseeba un nìn sá usaraaŋakpil Yooyadaa nimpuu, ki gíti sá Akasiyasi niisalee nìn ŋúń ki fīī kibikee Atalii ŋaan waa kūū-kì. 12Joowaasi nìn bál̀ ti-Dindaan Diikun niin áli abin aluu, ŋyunti gbanti kɔkɔee, Atalii di nìn kā dibeel pu.

english_text:
Jehoiada Makes Joash King of Judah
(2 Kings 11.4-21)
1After Ahaziah's son Joash had hidden in the temple for six years, Jehoiada the priest knew that something had to be done. So he made sure he had the support of several army officers. They were Azariah son of Jeroham, Ishmael son of Jehohanan, Azariah son of Obed, Maaseiah son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat son of Zichri. 2These five men went to the towns in Judah and called together the Levites and the clan leaders. They all came to Jerusalem 3 and gathered at the temple, where they agreed to help Joash.
Jehoiada said to them:
Joash will be our next king, because long ago the Lord promised that one of David's descendants would always be king. 4Here is what we will do. Three groups of priests and Levites will be on guard duty on the Sabbath—one group will guard the gates of the temple, 5one will guard the palace, and the other will guard Foundation Gate. The rest of you will stand guard in the temple courtyards. 6Only the priests and Levites who are on duty will be able to enter the temple, because they will be the only ones who have gone through the ceremony to make themselves clean and acceptable. The others must stay outside in the courtyards, just as the Lord has commanded. 7You Levites must protect King Joash. Don't let him out of your sight! And keep your swords ready to kill anyone who comes into the temple.
8The Levites and the people of Judah followed Jehoiada's orders. The guards going off duty were not allowed to go home, and so each commander had all his guards available—those going off duty as well as those coming on duty. 9Jehoiada went into the temple and brought out the swords and shields that had belonged to King David, and he gave them to the commanders. 10They gave the weapons to the guards, and Jehoiada then made sure that the guards took their positions around the temple and the altar to protect the king on every side.
11Jehoiada and his sons brought Joash outside, where they placed the crown on his head and gave him a copy of the instructions for ruling the nation. Olive oil was poured on his head to show that he was now king, and the crowd cheered and shouted, “Long live the king!”
12As soon as Queen Athaliah heard the crowd cheering for Joash, she went to the temple. 13There she saw Joash standing by one of the columns near the entrance, which was the usual place for the king. The commanders and the trumpet players were standing next to him, and the musicians were playing instruments and leading the people as they celebrated and blew trumpets. Athaliah tore her clothes in anger and shouted, “You betrayed me, you traitors!”
14At once, Jehoiada said to the army commanders, “Don't kill her near the Lord's temple. Take her out in front of the troops, and be sure to kill all of her followers!” 15She tried to escape, but the commanders caught and killed her near the gate where horses are led into the palace.
16Jehoiada asked King Joash and the people to join with him in being faithful to the Lord. They agreed, 17then rushed to the temple of the god Baal and tore it down. They smashed the altars and the idols and killed Mattan the priest of Baal in front of the altars.
18Jehoiada assigned the priests and Levites their duties at the temple, just as David had done. They were in charge of offering sacrifices to the Lord according to the Law of Moses, and they were responsible for leading the celebrations with singing. 19Jehoiada ordered the guards at the temple gates to keep out anyone who was unclean.
20Finally, Jehoiada called together the army commanders, the most important citizens of Judah, and the government officials. The crowd of people followed them as they led Joash from the temple, through the Upper Gate, and into the palace, where he took his place as king of Judah. 21Everyone celebrated because Athaliah had been killed and Jerusalem was peaceful again.
translation_text:
Joowaasi kpántì ubɔti
(Kpèè 2 Bib 11.4-20)
1Dibinluluútiil poonee, ní Yooyadaa dàkā tininjati. U nì bijanjakpilib bin kpòotī bijanjaliibi dilaataal dilaataalee nìn ŋá kunyɔɔbaantii. Bíǹ di sá Yeeroowaam jipɔɔn Asariyawuu nì Yoowanan jipɔɔn Isimaayeel nì Oobeedi jipɔɔn Asariyawuu nì Adaaya jipɔɔn Maaseeyawuu nì Sikirii jipɔɔn Eeliisafaati. 2Bi nìn yìin̄ Juuda timmu kɔkɔn ki kóoǹ Leefii yab nì Isirayeel dicaŋŋi kpilib ki kpáfì. Míǹ boonee ní bi nì bi táań ki gítì Jeerusaleem. 3Samaa kɔkɔ nìn kóoǹ ki kpáfì ti-Dindaan Diikun ní bi nì ubɔti ŋá mpèé. Yooyadaa nìn bí-bi yii: «Ubɔti jipɔɔn sèé. U máaǹ kí jī dibeel kí nóó nì ti-Dindaan nín nìn pōoǹ Daafiidi naantiibi puee. 4Ni nín làá ŋá puee sɔ̀. Bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab yaa dɔ́miń kí tɔ̄ ditundi ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaayee, bí ŋá akiti ata ní diba ń nīn cí kunimbɔtidii punyɔkɔki. 5Dikitililiitiil làá nīn cí dibeecindi ní ditataatiil ń nīn cí Dinyeel punyɔkɔki. Samaa un kɔkɔ kíǹee làá nīn bí ti-Dindaan Diiku cindin. 6Ubɔ kaa cáá nsan kí kɔ́ ti-Dindaan Diikun, see bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab baba. Bíǹ ŋūǹ kí kɔ́, di sá yii bi dū-bi ki sú ti-Dindaan ní. Samaa un kɔkɔ kíǹee máaǹ kí nīn ŋúb́ ti-Dindaan nín síiǹ puee kí nīn yú mmɔŋki. 7Leefii yab làá màntīí tū ubɔti báà ŋma ń nīn ŋúb́ u-janjawanti u-ŋaan. Un yaa là kí ŋá mpɔn kí kɔ́née, bí kpɔ̀-u. Laakin kamaa ubɔti yaa cée, bí nīn bí u-cee.»
8Leefii yab nì Juuda yab nìn ŋá kii usaraaŋakpil Yooyadaa nín nìn tīī-bi mara puee. Ukpil kamaa nìn yōoǹ u-nib, bin tundi nìn kífí ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dalee nì bin tundi nìn kúntí ŋwiin gbanti dalee, di sá yii Yooyadaa kaa nìn tīī báà dikitil diŋuŋfil. 9U nìn tīī bijanjakpilib bin kpèé bijanjaliibi dilaataal dilaataalee ŋkpamu nì ubɔti Daafiidi gbampɔɔŋi ŋin bí a-ba a-ba ki nìn bí kunimbɔtidiinee. 10U nìn yāntì bijanjaliibee kɔkɔ māntìi tú ubɔti ki ŋúb́ bi-janjawanti, ki kíĺ ti-Dindaan Diiku ŋgiil pú ki cáa sāā ŋgan pú, nsaraafan nì kunimbɔtidii caŋin. 11Niinee Yooyadaa nì u-jipɔmbi nyántì Joowaasi. Bi nìn dū kibeefuulii ki cíkiǹ-u ní ki dū dipoondi taŋkpapilinti ki ŋúbiǹ-u. Boonee ní bi bātì ŋkpam ki sītì u-yil pu ki kāaǹ-u tibɔtiil ní ki téeń mpɔn yii: «Ubɔti ń nīn cáá mmaŋfafɔkɔn!»
12Atalii nín gbìl̄ samaa wooku puee ní u nín cá ti-Dindaan Diiku watil pú, diniwul cee. 13U kpēēyee, ubɔti di tɔ́kɔ́ ti-Dindaan Diiku nyɔkɔpu kɔl puee. Bijanjakpilib nì bikantámbunliibi nìn yú ki kɔ́ĺ-u. Samaa kɔkɔ nìn bí mmɔnni ní bikantámbunliibi búǹ akantán, ní bi bɔ̀ɔ́ tiwan ní bilaŋgaaliibi gà ilan. Niinee Atalii cúú tiwan tin u pēēyee ki dáaĺ ki cátì ní ki téeń yii: «Bi nyáń m-boon ní! Bi nyáń m-boon ní!» 14Yooyadaa nìn nyántì bijanjakpilib bin kpèé bijanjaliibi dilaataal dilaataalee ki bí-bi yii: «Nyāntímaan-u doo! Un di yaa páaǹ u-boonee, bí kpɔ̀-u!» Di sá yii usaraaŋakpil nìn lī yii bí taa kpɔ̀-u ti-Dindaan Diikun doo. 15Bi nìn cúú Atalii ní ki dáaĺ-u ki cūnnì kubɔtinaakoou watil pú, ní ŋyunti ŋun bi bàn̄ Itaamu punyɔkɔkee ní bi kūū-u niin.
16Yooyadaa nì samaa nì ubɔti nìn ŋá mpèé ki pōoǹ kí nīn kíǹ ki sá ti-Dindaan nibul. 17Niinee ní samaa kɔkɔ nín cá diwaal Baal diikun ki gbáń ki wīī-ku. Bi nìn gbáń ki wīī Baal saraafaŋyi nì ataŋkpee ŋin nìn bí niin bi tòotēe. Bi nìn kūū Baal tandaaŋwu Matan ki bíl̀ isaraafan nyɔkɔpu. 18Yooyadaa nìn dū ti-Dindaan Diiku ki ŋúbiǹ bisaraaŋaliibi bin sá Leefii yabee bí nīn cí. Daafiidi nìn kpáfì-bi akiti akiti bí nīn ŋáań bisaraawɔkaabi ti-Dindaan Diikun, kii an nín ŋmàn̄ ki kā Mooyiisi marau poon puee. U nìn gíti kpáafì-bi yii bí nīn tūǹ ditundi gbanti ki gà ilan nì mmɔn. 19Yooyadaa nìn dū bipunyɔɔciitiliibi ki síiǹ bí nīn cí ti-Dindaan Diiku, án nín làá ŋá pu unil un yaa bí tijɔkɔndinee ń taa kɔ́ ku-nee.
20Yooyadaa nìn kóoǹ bijanjakpilib nì akpambal nì bikàliŋkpilib nì samaa kɔkɔ ní bi yōoǹ ubɔti ti-Dindaan Diikun, ki dū-u ki dī mpunyɔɔjaati ki cáá-u ki kɔ́ǹ dibeecindi. Bi nìn dū-u ki kāaǹ dibeejal pu, 21ní samaa kɔkɔ kíĺ ki bíi fàal̀.
Bi nín kūū Atalii míǹ boonee ní kitiŋ kɔ́ ŋgbansɔŋfin.

english_text:
King Joash of Judah
(2 Kings 12.1-16)
1Joash was only 7 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled 40 years from Jerusalem. His mother Zibiah was from the town of Beersheba.
2While Jehoiada the priest was alive, Joash obeyed the Lord by doing right. 3Jehoiada even chose two women for Joash to marry so he could have a family.
4Some time later, Joash decided it was time to repair the temple. 5He called together the priests and Levites and said, “Go everywhere in Judah and collect the annual tax from the people. I want this done at once—we need that money to repair the temple.”
But the Levites were in no hurry to follow the king's orders. 6 So he sent for Jehoiada the high priest and asked, “Why didn't you send the Levites to collect the taxes? The Lord's servant Moses and the people agreed long ago that this tax would be collected and used to pay for the upkeep of the sacred tent. 7And now we need it to repair the temple because the sons of that evil woman Athaliah came in and wrecked it. They even used some of the sacred objects to worship the god Baal.”
8Joash gave orders for a wooden box to be made and had it placed outside, near the gate of the temple. 9He then sent letters everywhere in Judah and Jerusalem, asking everyone to bring their taxes to the temple, just as Moses had required their ancestors to do.
10The people and their leaders agreed, and they brought their money to Jerusalem and placed it in the box. 11Each day, after the Levites took the box into the temple, the king's secretary and the high priest's assistant would dump out the money and count it. Then the empty box would be taken back outside.
This happened day after day, and soon a large amount of money was collected. 12Joash and Jehoiada turned the money over to the men who were supervising the repairs to the temple. They used the money to hire stonecutters, carpenters, and experts in working with iron and bronze.
13These workers went right to work repairing the temple, and when they were finished, it looked as good as new. 14They did not use all the tax money for the repairs, so the rest of it was handed over to Joash and Jehoiada, who then used it to make dishes and other gold and silver objects for the temple.
Sacrifices to please the Lord were offered regularly in the temple for as long as Jehoiada lived. 15He died at the ripe old age of 130 years, 16and he was buried in the royal tombs in Jerusalem, because he had done so much good for the people of Israel, for God, and for the temple.
Joash Turns Away from the Lord
17After the death of Jehoiada the priest, the leaders of Judah went to Joash and talked him into doing what they wanted. 18The people of Judah soon stopped worshiping in the temple of the Lord God and started worshiping idols and the symbols of the goddess Asherah. These sinful things made the Lord God angry with the people of Judah and Jerusalem, 19but he still sent prophets who warned them to turn back to him. The people refused to listen.
20 God's Spirit spoke to Zechariah son of Jehoiada the priest, and Zechariah told everyone that God was saying: “Why are you disobeying me and my laws? This will only bring punishment! You have deserted me, so now I will desert you.”
21-22King Joash forgot that Zechariah's father had always been a loyal friend. So when the people of Judah plotted to kill Zechariah, Joash joined them and gave orders for them to stone him to death in the courtyard of the temple. As Zechariah was dying, he said, “I pray that the Lord will see this and punish all of you.”
Joash Is Killed
23In the spring of the following year, the Syrian army invaded Judah and Jerusalem, killing all of the nation's leaders. They collected everything of value that belonged to the people and took it back to their king in Damascus. 24The Syrian army was very small, but the Lord let them defeat Judah's large army, because he was punishing Joash and the people of Judah for turning away from him.
25-26Joash was severely wounded during the battle, and as soon as the Syrians left Judah, two of his officials, Zabad and Jehozabad, decided to revenge the death of Zechariah.
