1Manasee nìn cáá abin saalaa nì ali ní ki kpántì ubɔti ní ki kāl̀ Jeerusaleem ki jíń dibeel abin aŋmoo kpá imuŋku ita. 2U nìn ŋá tin kaa kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee. U nìn ŋá ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin ní atimbun ŋin ti-Dindaan nìn jìn̄ ki fōō bi-tiŋki ki tīī Isirayeel yabee nìn ŋáańee ní. 3U nìn fātìi ŋáŋkì iwaatootipaan in u-baa nìn gbáń ki bíil̀ee, ní ki máń isaraafan bí nīn ŋáań i-pu saraabi ki tìì diwaal Baal. U nìn cóoǹ iwindɔ ní ki gbāaǹ ki jáam̀ iŋmalbi in kɔkɔ bí kutaa puee. 4U nìn máń isaraafan iba mun ti-Dindaan Diikun, min kɔkɔ ti-Dindaan nìn lī yii: «Jeerusaleem niin ní m làá nīn lèekī m-ba ki dàkèe.» 5U nìn gíti máń isaraafan ti-Dindaan Diiku ciŋŋi aliitilin bí nīn ŋáań saraabi ki tìì iŋmalbi in bí kutaa puee. 6U nìn dū u-jipɔmbi ki wùn̄ ŋŋmi ki ŋá saraabi Been Inoom tantakalin. U nìn būū tibɔɔl ki ŋáań kukpaŋkpantiiu tuuŋŋi ní ki bàlifī bitaŋkpiibi kí béé tin bí ki dòońee. U nìn ŋá tin kaa pée kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee ki gbítì u-ŋuul. 7U nìn máń diwaal ki síiǹ ti-Dindaan Diikun. Ama ti-Dindaan nìn tùkū Daafiidi nì u-jipɔɔn Saloomɔn yii: «Kudii nee poon nì Jeerusaleem tiŋki kin m lēē Isirayeel naakɔti kɔkɔ kansikinee poon ní m làá nīn pée lèekī m-ba ki dàkà. 8M-nibooliŋu yaa tɔ́ m-bɔkpaaŋi kɔkɔ nì m-marab bin kɔkɔ m-tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi tīī-bee, m kpá kí yàntī bí nīn tú ki yìiǹ kí wàatī kitiŋ kin ní m tīī bi-naanjabee». 9Ama Manasee nìn yāntì Juuda yab nì Jeerusaleem yab gáatì, áli gba bi gíti ŋá ikpiti ki jítiǹ atimbun ŋin ti-Dindaan nìn kúntì ki fōō bi-tiŋki ki tīī Isirayeel yabee.
10Ti-Dindaan nìn sòon̄ nì Manasee nì u-nibul, ama baa nìn fātìi tɔ́. 11Niinee ní ti-Dindaan cáań Asuur bɔtiu janjakpilib ki tɔ́ bi-pu. Bi nìn cúú Manasee ní ki dū abɔmbil ki kpàl̄ u-nyɔɔkpaweeŋyi, ní ki dū tasa kusakai ki bóob́-u mili pu ní ki cáá-u ki cūnnì Babiloon tiŋkin. 12U nìn nyàab̄ ti-Dindaan u-Nimbɔtiu u-nimbinaamandi poon ní ki sīntiǹ u-ba u-baabi Nimbɔtiu nimbiin. 13U nìn mēē-u ní an gbēē Unimbɔti ní u pílifì u-wimmeem ní ki yāntì u fātìi gítì Jeerusaleem u-beelin. Niinee ní Manasee nín béè yii ti-Dindaan di sá Unimbɔti.
14Míǹ boonee, ní u máń Daafiidi Tiŋki boonee diguŋfɔkɔl diba. Digundi gbanti nìn dī Giiyɔn nyimbuliŋu ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú ní ki kpākaǹ Seedrɔn tantakal ki cáa sāā Ijɔm punyɔkɔki, ní ki fātìi pɔ́ĺ ki māntì Oofeel gbantaŋki ki tú. U nìn kāaǹ bijanjakpilib Juuda timmu mun kɔkɔ bi nìn máń agun ki túee poon. 15U nìn nyántì awaa ŋin u nìn cáań ki síiǹ kunimbɔtidiinee nì kunaŋu kun u nìn máń ki síiǹ niinee. U nìn gbáń ki wīī isaraafan in u nìn máń ti-Dindaan gbantaŋki pu nì Jeerusaleemee kɔkɔ, ní ki nyántìi fá kitiŋ kpaanceetiŋu. 16U nìn fātìi máń ti-Dindaan saraafaŋŋu ní ki ŋá mpèé saraabi nì ijaam saraabi ŋu-pu. U nìn tīī Juuda yab mara yii bí nīn jáaḿ ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu. 17Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, binib nìn gbíntìi ŋáań saraabi iwaatootipaan pu, ama bi nìn ŋáań ki tìì ti-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu ní.
18Manasee tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee, u nín mēē u-Nimbɔtiu nì anyɔɔbun ŋin ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi fōō ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu cee ki dūu nāatì-uee kɔkɔ ŋmàn̄ ki kā Isirayeel bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun. 19U nín nìn mēē Unimbɔti pu nì úǹ nín kíí-u puee, u-kpitii nì u nín kaa yúl̀ Unimbɔti deedee puee, ipaan in pu u nìn máń iwaatootipaanee nì u nín nìn cóoǹ iwindɔ puee nì u nín nìn sīntiǹ u-ba taapu puee kɔkɔ ŋmàn̄ ki kā Oosayii maam gbɔŋkun. 20Manasee kpíì ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ u-baabee ní bi síb́-u u-cindin. U-jipɔɔn Amɔn nín nìn fōō u-yil ki kpántì ubɔti.
Amɔn, Juuda bɔtiu
(Kpèè 2 Bib 21.19-26)
21Amɔn nìn cáá abin mmuŋku nì ali ní ki kpántì ubɔti. U nìn kāl̀ Jeerusaleem ní ki jíń dibeel abin ali. 22U nìn ŋá tin kaa kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee kii u-baa Manasee nín nìn ŋá puee. U nìn ŋá saraabi ki tīī awaa ŋin ní u-baa nìn máńee ki jáam̀-ŋi. 23Ama úǹ kaa nìn sīntiǹ u-ba taapu ti-Dindaan nimbiin kii u-baa Manasee nín nìn sīntiǹ u-ba taapu puee. Úǹ nìn gíti ŋá ikpiti ki jítiǹ u-baa gba.
24U-tɔntɔnliibi nìn bɔ́ntì u-pu ní ki kūū-u u-naakookun. 25Ama Juuda yab nìn kūū bin kɔkɔ nìn kūū Amɔŋyee ní ki dū u-jipɔɔn Joosiyaasi ki kāaǹ ubɔti u-yil pu.

english_text:
King Josiah of Judah
(2 Kings 22.1,2)
1 Josiah was 8 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled 31 years from Jerusalem. 2He followed the example of his ancestor David and always obeyed the Lord.
Josiah Stops the Worship of Foreign Gods
(2 Kings 23.4-20)
3When Josiah was only 16 years old he began worshiping God, just as his ancestor David had done. Then, 4 years later, he decided to destroy the local shrines in Judah and Jerusalem, as well as the sacred poles for worshiping the goddess Asherah and the idols of foreign gods. 4 He watched as the altars for the worship of the god Baal were torn down, and as the nearby incense altars were smashed. The Asherah poles, the idols, and the stone images were also smashed, and the pieces were scattered over the graves of their worshipers. 5 Josiah then had the bones of the pagan priests burned on the altars.
And so Josiah got rid of the worship of foreign gods in Judah and Jerusalem. 6He did the same things in the towns and ruined villages in the territories of West Manasseh, Ephraim, and Simeon, as far as the border of Naphtali. 7Everywhere in the northern kingdom of Israel, Josiah tore down pagan altars and Asherah poles; he crushed idols to dust and smashed incense altars.
Then Josiah went back to Jerusalem.
Hilkiah Finds The Book of God's Law
(2 Kings 22.3-20)
8In the eighteenth year of Josiah's rule in Judah, after he had removed all the sinful things from the land and from the Lord's temple, he sent three of his officials to repair the temple. They were Shaphan son of Azaliah, Governor Maaseiah of Jerusalem, and Joah son of Joahaz, who kept the government records.
9These three men went to Hilkiah the high priest. They gave him the money that the Levite guards had collected from the people of West Manasseh, Ephraim, and the rest of Israel, as well as those living in Judah, Benjamin, and Jerusalem. 10Then the money was turned over to the men who supervised the repairs to the temple. They used some of it to pay the workers, 11and they gave the rest of it to the carpenters and builders, who used it to buy the stone and wood they needed to repair the other buildings that Judah's kings had not taken care of.
12The workers were honest, and their supervisors were Jahath and Obadiah from the Levite clan of Merari, and Zechariah and Meshullam from the Levite clan of Kohath. Other Levites, who were all skilled musicians, 13were in charge of carrying supplies and supervising the workers. Other Levites were appointed to stand guard around the temple.
14While the money was being given to these supervisors, Hilkiah found the book that contained the laws that the Lord had given to Moses. 15Hilkiah handed the book to Shaphan the official and said, “Look what I found here in the temple—The Book of God's Law.”
16Shaphan took the book to Josiah and reported, “Your officials are doing everything you wanted. 17They have collected the money from the temple and have given it to the men supervising the repairs. 18But there's something else, Your Majesty. The priest Hilkiah gave me this book.” Then Shaphan read it aloud.
19When Josiah heard what was in The Book of God's Law, he tore his clothes in sorrow. 20At once he called together Hilkiah, Shaphan, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Abdon son of Micah, and his own servant Asaiah. He said, 21“The Lord must be furious with me and everyone else in Israel and Judah, because our ancestors did not obey the laws written in this book. Go find out what the Lord wants us to do.”
22Hilkiah and the four other men left at once and went to talk with Huldah the prophet. Her husband was Shallum, who was in charge of the king's clothes. Huldah lived in the northern part of Jerusalem, and when they met in her home, 23she said:
You were sent here by King Josiah, and this is what the Lord God of Israel says to him: 24“Josiah, I am the Lord! And I intend to punish this country and everyone in it, just as this book says. 25The people of Judah and Israel have rejected me. They have offered sacrifices to foreign gods and have worshiped their own idols. I can't stand it any longer. I am furious.
26-27“Josiah, listen to what I am going to do. I noticed how sad you were when you heard that this country and its people would be completely wiped out. You even tore your clothes in sorrow, and I heard you cry. 28So before I destroy this place, I will let you die in peace.”
The men left and reported to Josiah what Huldah had said.
Josiah Reads The Book of God's Law
(2 Kings 23.1-3)
29King Josiah called together the leaders of Judah and Jerusalem. 30Then he went to the Lord's temple, together with all the people of Judah and Jerusalem, the priests, and the Levites.
Finally, when everybody was there, he read aloud The Book of God's Law that had been found in the temple.
31After Josiah had finished reading, he stood in the place reserved for the king. He promised in the Lord's name to faithfully obey the Lord and to follow his laws and teachings that were written in the book. 32Then he asked the people of Jerusalem and Benjamin to make that same promise and to obey the God their ancestors had worshiped.
33Josiah destroyed all the idols in the territories of Israel, and he commanded everyone in Israel to worship only the Lord God. The people did not turn away from the Lord God of their ancestors for the rest of Josiah's rule as king.
translation_text:
Joosiyaasi, Juuda bɔtiu
(Kpèè 2 Bib 22.1-2, 23.4-20)
1Joosiyaasi nìn cáá abin anii ní ki kpántì ubɔti. U nìn kóò Jeerusaleem ní ki jíń dibeel abin mmuŋku nì saalaa nì diba. 2U nìn ŋá tin kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee. U nìn nóó u-naanja Daafiidi tabɔbiliŋ ní deedee, waa kpēetì ki cūtì ŋgan púɔɔɔ, ŋgiil pú.
3U nín jíń dibeel abin anii poon ki dáá sá unaacimpɔɔnee, ní u kíĺ ki bíi nyàab̀ u-naanja Daafiidi Nimbɔtiu. U nín jíń dibeel abin saalaa nì ali poonee, ní u kíĺ ki bíi kúntí iwaatootipaan nì iwindɔ nì awaa ŋin bi kpítèe nì ŋin bi dūntì tikúti ki mɔ́ɔ́yee Juuda tiŋkin nì Jeerusaleem. 4U-nimbiin ní bi gbáń ki wīī diwaal Baal saraafaŋyi nì talaalutuukaa saraafaŋyi in nìn tɔ́kɔ́ i-puee. Bi nìn gāatì iwindɔ ki fá ní ki nàn̄ awaa ŋin bi kpítèe nì ŋin bi dūntèe dúsi dusi ki dūu yāaǹ bin nìn ŋá saraabi ki tīī-bee kaakuliŋ pu. 5U nìn dū awaa gbanti saraaŋaliibi kpabiŋ ki tūū bi-saraafaŋyi pu ŋŋmi. Míǹ ní u nìn ŋá ki fíntì Juuda nì Jeerusaleem ki nyántì tijɔkɔndin.
6U nìn ŋá míǹ mbaantiim Manasee nì Eefiraayiim nì Simeeyɔn ki kpáaǹ Neefitalii timmun nì ntimu mun māntìi tú-muee. 7U nìn gbáń ki wīī isaraafan, ki gāatì iwindɔ ki fá ní ki nàn̄ awaa dúsi dusi ní ki kpéelikì talaalutuukaa saraafaŋyi Isirayeel beel kɔkɔn. U ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki nín gítí Jeerusaleem tiŋkin.
Usaraaŋakpil ká Marab gbɔŋku
(Kpèè 2 Bib 22.3-10)
8Joosiyaasi nín jíń dibeel abin saalku nì ata poon ki fíntì Isirayeel tiŋki nì kunimbɔtidii ki nyántì tijɔkɔndin ki dóòyee, ní u tú Asaliya jipɔɔn Safan nì Jeerusaleem Gɔminau Maaseeyawuu nì Joowakaasi jipɔɔn Yoowa, ubɔti gbaŋŋmaliu bí cùú ŋāŋkì ti-Dindaan, u-Nimbɔtiu Diiku. 9Binibee nìn nín cá usaraaŋakpil Yilkiya cee. Bi nìn dū animbil ŋin bi cáań kunimbɔtidiinee ki tīī-u. Leefii yab bin nìn cí kipunyɔkɔee di nìn fōō animbil gbanti Manasee yab nì Eefiraayiim yab nì Isirayeel yab bin kɔkɔ kíǹee nì Juuda yab nì Beenjameen yab bin nìn kóò Jeerusaleemee cee. 10Bi nìn dū animbilee ki ŋúbiǹ bin bi nìn lēē bí nīn kpèé ditundi ti-Dindaan Diikunee, ní bíǹ cáa pà bin bí niin ki ŋáŋkí ti-Dindaan Diikuee. 11Bi nìn tīī kapintab nì bidimaliibi animbil bí dūú dā ataŋkpee ŋin bi kpítèe nì idɔ in bi làá dūú kpáá kudiiyee, kí fàtīí mā adiin ŋin Juuda bɔtiibi nìn yāntì an bíil̀ee. 12Binibee nìn túń ditundee deedee. Leefii yab Yayati nì Oobadiya bin sá Meerarii maaliŋunee nì Seekariya nì Meesulam bin sá Keeyaati maaliŋunee di nìn kpèé-bi. Leefii yab bin nìn ŋūǹ tibɔɔkaal tiŋanee biba 13nìn kpèé bin tūntí tiwanee nì bitɔntɔnliibi kɔkɔ, báà udaan tundi yaa nìn sá diŋyee. Leefii yab kansikinee, biba mun nìn sá bigbaŋŋmaliibi ní biba sá bikàliŋkpilib ní bin kíǹ sá bipunyɔɔciitiliibi.
14Ŋyunti ŋun bi nìn bíi nyāntí animbil ŋin bi nìn cáań ti-Dindaan Diikunee ní usaraaŋakpil Yiilkiyaawuu ká ti-Dindaan marau un u nìn dūu tīī Mooyiisee gbɔŋku. 15Yiilkiyaawuu nìn bí ugbaŋŋmal Safan yii: «M ká Marab gbɔŋku ti-Dindaan Diikun.» U lī mimmee ní ki dū kugbɔŋuee ki tīī-u. 16Safan nìn cáań kugbɔŋuee ki tīī ubɔti ní ki kpáàa tùkū-u ditundi nín bíi còom̄ puee. U nìn bí-u yii: «Tin kɔkɔ a bí timbi a-tɔntɔnliibi ń ŋée, ti bíi ŋáań. 17Bisaraaŋaliibi yōoǹ animbil ŋin bí ti-Dindaan Diikunee ki dūu tīī bin bíi kpèé ditundee nì bitɔntɔnliibi.» 18Niinee ní ubɔti gbaŋŋmaliu Safan kútì ki tùkū ubɔti yii: «Usaraaŋakpil Yiilkiyaawuu dū kugbɔŋu kubɔ ki tīī-mi.» Safan nìn kàan̄ kugbɔŋuee ubɔti nimbiin.
Joosiyaasi yāntì bi cūtì Ulda cee dibalifil
(Kpèè 2 Bib 22.11-20a)
19Ubɔti nín gbìl̄ tin kā Marab gbɔŋkuee poonee ní u cúú tiwan tin u pēēyee ki dáaĺ ki cátì. 20Ní u tīī Yiilkiyaawuu nì Safan jipɔɔn Ayiikaam nì Miika jipɔɔn Abidɔn nì ugbaŋŋmal Safan nì u-kàliŋkpiliu Asaya mara nee yii: 21«Ní cùú bàlifì ti-Dindaan kí tīī man nì Isirayeel yab bin kíǹee nì Juuda yab. Ní bàlifì-u tin ŋmàn̄ ki kā kugbɔŋu nee poonee pu. Di sá yii ti-naanjab kaa pílifì u-nyɔkɔ. Baa ŋá tin ŋmàn̄ ki kā kugbɔŋu nee poonee. An pu ní ti-Dindaan gíí ti-pu diŋuul ŋkpitim pu.»
22Niinee Yiilkiyaawuu nì bin ubɔti lēēyee nín cá Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Ulda cee. U-cal di nìn sá Saluum, Tiikifa jipɔɔn, Araasi naantiiu. U nìn kóò Jeerusaleem Tincaliiki Kipɔŋ poon ní. Úǹ di nìn cí bisaraaŋaliibi wampeeŋkaati ti-Dindaan Diikun. Bi nìn dū tin bée ki máafì-u 23ní u bí-bi yii: «Ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Ní cùú tùkù un di túnní-ni m-ceeyee yii: 24<M làá cáań nnaabu kí tɔ̄ Jeerusaleem tiŋki nì bin kɔkɔ kóò ki-nee pu, kí nóó nì mbusub bin ŋmàn̄ ki kā kugbɔŋu kun ni kàan̄ Juuda bɔtiu nimbiinee. 25Jeerusaleem yab dū-mi ki fá ní ki tūutì talaalub ki tīī awaa ŋin bíǹ bi-ba dū bi-ŋalii ki ŋée ki gbítì m-ŋuul. An pu ní m gíí kitiŋ nee pu diŋuul ŋkpitim pu, ní m-ŋuulee kpá kí sɔ̀ŋkì!> 26Ama ní tùkù Juuda bɔtiu un di túnní-ni ní dāan̄ kí bàlifì ti-Dindaanee yii ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <A gbìl̄ tibɔti tin kā kugbɔŋu nee poonee, 27ní tibɔtee gbēē-si. A nín gbìl̄ tin m sòon̄ yii an làá bàń Jeerusaleem nì ki-nib puee, a sīntiǹ a-ba m-nimbiin, ní ki dáaĺ ki cátì tiwan tin a pēēyee ní ki súń m-nimbiin. An puee ma mun gbìl̄ a-wimmeem. Man ni-Dindaan di sòon̄ míǹ. 28Míǹ puee m làá yàntī á kpú kí cùú ŋàl̄ a-baabi nì ŋgbansɔŋfi ní bí síb́-si a-kaakulin. Sii kaa làá ká nnaabu ŋun m làá cáań kí tɔ̄ Jeerusaleem nì ki-nib puee.>»
Joosiyaasi fātìi pōoǹ ti-Dindaan dipoondi
(Kpèè 2 Bib 22.20b–23.3)
Ubɔti tuuŋyee nìn gítì ki dū Unimbɔti nín kíí puee ki tùkū-u. 29Niinee ní ubɔti tú bi yíiń Juuda nì Jeerusaleem tindaŋkpilib ní bi kóoǹ ki kpáfì u-cee. 30Míǹ boonee ní u nì Juuda yab nì bin kóò Jeerusaleemee nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab nì samaa kɔkɔ, kí yòon̄ bikpaambi kí cáá sāā mbiyaamu nín jɔ́ḿ kunimbɔtidiin. Niinee ní ubɔti kàan̄-bi tin kɔkɔ bi ŋmàn̄ an kā dipoondi gbɔŋku kun bi ká ti-Dindaan Diikunee. 31Ubɔti nìn yú u-paaŋŋu ní ki pōoǹ kí nīn yú nì ti-Dindaan deedee, kí nīn ŋúb́ u-marab nì u-dàkatam nì u-bɔkpaaŋi nì u-pɔbil kɔkɔ nì u-naŋki kɔkɔ. U nìn gíti pōoǹ kí nīn tɔ́ tin kɔkɔ ŋmàn̄ ki kā dipoondi taŋkpapilintinee. 32Ubɔti nìn yāntì bin kɔkɔ nìn bí Jeerusaleem nì Beenjameen timmunee pōoǹ míǹ mbaantiim. Kí yòon̄ ŋyunti gbantee, bin nìn kóò Jeerusaleemee nìn ŋá ki nóó nì dipoondi din bi nìn pōoǹ bi-baabi Nimbɔtiuee. 33Joosiyaasi nìn kúntì ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin kɔkɔ ní bi nìn ŋáań Isirayeel tiŋkinee, ní ki páb́ bin kɔkɔ nìn bí Isirayeelee bí nīn jáaḿ ti-Dindaan, bi-Nimbɔtiu. An puee, u-maŋfal wiiŋyi kɔkɔ poonee, Isirayeel yab kaa nìn fātì bi-boon ki tīī ti-Dindaan, bi-baabi Nimbɔtiu.

english_text:
Passover Is Celebrated
(2 Kings 23.21-23)
1Josiah commanded that Passover be celebrated in Jerusalem to honor the Lord. So, on the fourteenth day of the first month, the lambs were killed for the Passover celebration.
2On that day, Josiah made sure the priests knew what duties they were to do in the temple. 3He called together the Levites who served the Lord and who taught the people his laws, and he said:
No longer will you have to carry the sacred chest from place to place. It will stay in the temple built by King Solomon son of David, where you will serve the Lord and his people Israel. 4 Get ready to do the work that David and Solomon assigned to you, according to your clans. 5Divide yourselves into groups, then arrange yourselves throughout the temple so that each family of worshipers will be able to get help from one of you. 6When the people bring you their Passover lamb, you must kill it and prepare it to be sacrificed to the Lord. Make sure the people celebrate according to the instructions that the Lord gave Moses, and don't do anything to make yourselves unclean and unacceptable.
7Josiah donated 30,000 sheep and goats, and 3,000 bulls from his own flocks and herds for the people to offer as sacrifices. 8Josiah's officials also voluntarily gave some of their animals to the people, the priests, and the Levites as sacrifices. Hilkiah, Zechariah, and Jehiel, who were the officials in charge of the temple, gave the priests 2,600 sheep and lambs and 300 bulls to sacrifice during the Passover celebration. 9Conaniah, his two brothers Shemaiah and Nethanel, as well as Hashabiah, Jeiel, and Jozabad were leaders of the Levites, and they gave the other Levites 5,000 sheep and goats, and 500 bulls to offer as sacrifices.
10When everything was ready to celebrate Passover, the priests and the Levites stood where Josiah had told them. 11Then the Levites killed and skinned the Passover lambs, and they handed some of the blood to the priests, who splattered it on the altar. 12The Levites set aside the parts of the animal that the worshipers needed for their sacrifices to please the Lord, just as the Law of Moses required. They also did the same thing with the bulls. 13 They sacrificed the Passover animals on the altar and boiled the meat for the other offerings in pots, kettles, and pans. Then they quickly handed the meat to the people so they could eat it.
14All day long, the priests were busy offering sacrifices and burning the animals' fat on the altar. And when everyone had finished, the Levites prepared Passover animals for themselves and for the priests.
15 During the celebration some of the Levites prepared Passover animals for the musicians and the guards, so that the Levite musicians would not have to leave their places, which had been assigned to them according to the instructions of David, Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun the king's prophet. Even the guards at the temple gates did not have to leave their posts.
16So on that day, Passover was celebrated to honor the Lord, and sacrifices were offered on the altar to him, just as Josiah had commanded. 17 The worshipers then celebrated the Festival of Thin Bread for the next seven days.
18People from Jerusalem and from towns all over Judah and Israel were there. Passover had not been observed like this since the days of Samuel the prophet. In fact, this was the greatest Passover celebration in Israel's history! 19All these things happened in the eighteenth year of Josiah's rule in Judah.
Josiah Dies in Battle
(2 Kings 23.28-30)
20Some time later, King Neco of Egypt led his army to the city of Carchemish on the Euphrates River. And Josiah led his troops north to meet the Egyptians in battle.
21Neco sent the following message to Josiah:
I'm not attacking you, king of Judah! We're not even at war. But God has told me to quickly attack my enemy. God is on my side, so if you try to stop me, he will punish you.
22But Josiah ignored Neco's warning, even though it came from God! Instead, he disguised himself and marched into battle against Neco in the valley near Megiddo.
23During the battle an Egyptian soldier shot Josiah with an arrow. Josiah told his servants, “Get me out of here! I've been hit.” 24They carried Josiah out of his chariot, then put him in the other chariot he had there and took him back to Jerusalem, where he soon died. He was buried beside his ancestors, and everyone in Judah and Jerusalem mourned his death.
25Jeremiah the prophet wrote a funeral song in honor of Josiah. And since then, anyone in Judah who mourns the death of Josiah sings that song. It is included in the collection of funeral songs.
26Everything else Josiah did while he was king, including how he faithfully obeyed the Lord, 27is written in The History of the Kings of Israel and Judah.
translation_text:
Joosiyaasi yāntì bi jíń Dilákatil jiŋaaliu
(Kpèè 2 Bib 23.21-23)
1Joosiyaasi nìn jíń Dilákatil jiŋaaliu Jeerusaleem ki tīī ti-Dindaan tinyool. Uŋmapeekaa, ŋwiin ŋubɔ kpá saalku dalee, ní bi kūū Dilákatil jiŋaaliu waŋkuti. 2U nìn dū bisaraaŋaliibi tundi nín sá puee ki ŋúbiǹ-bi ní ki tīī-bi kunyannyaau bí tɔ̄ ti-Dindaan Diikun tundi. 3U nìn bí Leefii yab bin nìn dū biba ki sú ti-Dindaan ki dàkà Isirayeel yab kɔkɔee yii: «Ní dū ti-Dindaan Dakaau kí síiń kunimbɔtidii kun ní Isirayeel bɔtiu Saloomɔn, Daafiidi jipɔɔn máńee poon. An kaa ti bàlifī ní nīn gbíntìi yòontí ki bùkuntí. Kɔŋkɔnnee, ní tɔ̄ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nì u-nibul Isirayeel tundi. 4Ní bɔ́ntímaan ni-ba kí nóó nì ni-maalii nì ni-tuuŋŋi nín sá puee, kii an nín ŋmàn̄ pu ki kā Isirayeel bɔtiu Daafiidi nì u-jipɔɔn Saloomɔn gbɔntin puee. 5Nín̄ bímaan circir paaŋŋu pu kí nóó nì ni-dicaŋŋi nín sá puee, ní kí tɔ̄ ditundi kí tīī ni-nabiyaamu Isirayeel yab kí nóó nì bi-maalii nín sá puee. 6Kpɔ̀maan Dilákatil jiŋaaliu waŋkuti, ŋámaan ni-ba circir ní kí tūtuǹ ni-nabiyaamu Isirayeel yab bí ŋá ti-Dindaan nín dī Mooyiisi pu ki sòon̄ pu ki síiǹee.»
7Ubɔti Joosiyaasi nìn lēē úǹ u-ba waŋkuti poon apibil nì aŋɔbil kutukub mmuŋku nì saalaa nì inajaa kutukub bita ki tīī binib bin kɔkɔ nìn bí niinee bí dūú ŋá Dilákatil jiŋaaliu saraabi. 8U-kàliŋkpilib mun nìn tīī samaa nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab tiwaŋkuti nì nlammɔntiim. Ilikiya nì Seekariyawuu nì Yeeyiyeel nín nìn kpèé kunimbɔtidii. Bíǹ nìn tīī bisaraaŋaliibi apibil kutukub bili nì alaataa aluu nì inajaa alaataa ata bí dūú ŋá Dilákatil jiŋaaliu saraabi. 9Leefii yab kpilib Koonaniyawuu nì u-naalib Seemayawuu nì Neetaneeyeel nì Asabiya nì Yeeyiyeel nì Yoosabaadi nìn tīī Leefii yab apibil kutukub biŋmoo nì inajaa alaataa aŋmoo bí dūú ŋá Dilákatil jiŋaaliu saraabi. 10Bi nín nìn bɔ́ntì jiŋaal gbanti puee sɔ̀. Bisaraaŋaliibi nìn yú bi-paaŋŋu ní Leefii yab mun yúl̀ akiti akiti ki nóó nì ubɔti nín nìn síiǹ-bi puee. 11Bi nìn làntī Dilákatil jiŋaaliu waŋkuti ní bisaraaŋaliibi tīkintí fatiku ki cáa yàantí nsaraafan pu ní Leefii yab lèekī igban. 12Bi nìn gāntì tiwaŋkuti tin bi làá dūú ŋá ti-Dindaan saraawɔkaayee, cilinjee inajaayee. Bi nìn yākatì ki tīī samaa ki nóó nì bi-maalii kii an nín ŋmàn̄ pu ki kā Mooyiisi gbɔŋkun puee. 13Bi nìn púĺ Dilákatil jiŋaaliu pibiliŋ kii dikoobil nín sá puee, ní ki dū saraabi bin kíǹee nanti ki tɔ́kɔǹ daanseebin nì ŋkumbɔbiyaamun nì sirbabin. Bi nìn ŋáań malaa ki cáa yàkatī ki tìì samaa kɔkɔ. 14Leefii yab nìn ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki bɔ́ntì bíǹ bi-ba nì bisaraaŋaliibi yati, di sá yii bisaraaŋaliibi, Aarɔn naantiibee kaa nìn cáá mpaan. Bi nìn bí ki ŋáań bisaraawɔkaabi ki cáá ŋkpam ki wù ŋŋmi áli kunyeeu dāa mɔ́. An pu ní Leefii yab nìn bɔ́ntì bíǹ bi-ba nì bisaraaŋaliibi jinti. 15Asafi naantiibi bilaŋgaaliibi nìn yú bi-paaŋŋu ki nóó nì Daafiidi nì Asafi nì Eeman nì Yeedutun, ubɔti saŋkiliu nín nìn síiǹ puee. Bipunyɔɔciitiliibi mun nìn yú ki cí kipunyɔkɔ kamaa. Báà ŋma nìn pée bí u-tundin ní, di sá yii bi-nabiyaamu Leefii yab nìn bɔ́ntì bi mun jinti ki tīī-bi. 16Kii ubɔti Joosiyaasi nín nìn tīī mara puee, bi nìn bɔ́ntì atuun kɔkɔ ŋwiin gbanti kí jāam̀ ti-Dindaan, kí jī Dilákatil jiŋaaliu ní kí ŋmā kí ŋá bisaraawɔkaabi ti-Dindaan saraafaŋŋu pu.
17Míǹ ní Isirayeel yab bin nìn bí niinee nìn jíń Dilákatil jiŋaaliu ŋyunti gbanti, ní ki dū iwiin iluli ki jíń jiŋaal un bi ŋmóò kpɔnɔ un kaa cáá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee. 18Baa nìn gíti jíń Dilákatil jiŋaaliu ubɔ míǹ Isirayeel tiŋkin kí yòon̄ doooo Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Samiyeel yuntiŋu. Isirayeel bɔtiu ubɔ mun kaa nìn jíń Dilákatil jiŋaaliu ubɔ kii un ní Joosiyaasi nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab nì Juuda yab nì Isirayeel yab bin kɔkɔ nìn bí niinee nì Jeerusaleem yab jíńee. 19Joosiyaasi nín jíń dibeel abin ali kpá mmuŋku poonee ní bi jíń Dilákatil jiŋaaliu gbanti.
Joosiyaasi maŋfal wiiŋyi nín kúntì puee
(Kpèè 2 Bib 23.28-30)
20Tin bí nee kɔkɔ boonee, ŋyunti ŋun ní Joosiyaasi ŋáŋkì kunimbɔtidii ki dóòyee ní Eejipiti bɔtiu Neekoo nín cá Kaarkeemiisi, Eefiraati mɔɔl caŋin kí já kujaau. Joosiyaasi nìn túŋkì-u kí bàà pìin̄-u nsan. 21Ama ní Neekoo tú binib bí tùkù-u yii: «Juuda bɔtiu, tilati di bí man nì sii kansikin? An kaa sá sii ní m dòoń kí já kujaau díǹ, ama m-nannanliu ubɔ mun ní m dòoń kí jáǹ. Unimbɔti bí-mi yii ḿ yáb́. Unimbɔti bí m-cee. An puee á taa jáǹ Unimbɔti, yaa sá fám, u làá kpɔ̀-si.» 22Ama Joosiyaasi kaa nìn kpántì u-landɔkɔŋu. Di sá yii waa nìn pílifiǹ Neekoo bɔti tin nìn nyánní Unimbɔti u-ba ceeyee. U nìn cúú u-beebɔkutil ki pēetì bí taa béé-u ní ki cūtìi bíi jáà kujaau Meegiidoo tantakalin. 23Bi bíi jáà mimmee ní bin tòó ipiinee tɔ́ ipiin ki yá-u ní u bí u-tɔntɔnliibi yii: «Yòom̄maan-mi kí cùnnì, di sá yii m fōō tiweendi.» 24Ní u-tɔntɔnliibi kpákatì-u janjatɔrɔku poon ní ki yōoǹ-u ki ŋá u-tɔrɔkuliliitiu poon ki cáá-u ki cūnnì Jeerusaleem. Niin ní u kpíì ní bi síb́-u u-baabi kaakuliŋin. Bin kɔkɔ nìn kóò Jeerusaleemee nì Juuda yab nìn súń u-kpool.
25Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii nìn gāā Joosiyaasi ŋkpiisilan. Kí yòon̄ ŋyunti gbanti kí cáá sāā díǹ, bilaŋgaaliibi bininjab nì binimpoobi gà ikpiisilan ki téetí Joosiyaasi kúm pu. An nìn dūu kpántì dikoobil ní Isirayeel tiŋkin. Bi ŋmàn̄ ilan gbanti nyɔɔbuŋŋi ki ŋá Iyaliŋki gbɔŋkun.
26Joosiyaasi tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee, u-deedee tuuŋŋi ŋin u túń ki nóó nì tin ŋmàn̄ ki kā ti-Dindaan marab gbɔŋkunee, 27nì ubɔti nín kíĺ pu ki dāa kúntì puee kɔkɔ ŋmàn̄ ki kā Isirayeel nì Juuda bɔtiibi gbɔŋkun.

english_text:
King Jehoahaz of Judah
(2 Kings 23.30-35)
1After the death of Josiah, the people of Judah crowned his son Jehoahaz their new king. 2He was 23 years old at the time, and he ruled only 3 months from Jerusalem. 3King Neco of Egypt captured Jehoahaz and forced Judah to pay 3.4 tons of silver and 34 kilograms of gold as taxes. 4 Then Neco appointed Jehoahaz's brother Eliakim king of Judah and changed his name to Jehoiakim. He led Jehoahaz away to Egypt as his prisoner.
King Jehoiakim of Judah
(2 Kings 23.36—24.7)
5 Jehoiakim was 25 years old when he was appointed king, and he ruled 11 years from Jerusalem. Jehoiakim disobeyed the Lord his God by doing evil.
6 During Jehoiakim's rule, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia invaded Judah. He arrested Jehoiakim and put him in chains, and he sent him to the capital city of Babylon. 7Nebuchadnezzar also carried off many of the valuable things in the Lord's temple, and he put them in his palace in Babylon.
8Everything else Jehoiakim did while he was king, including all the disgusting and evil things, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel and Judah. His son Jehoiachin then became king.
King Jehoiachin of Judah
(2 Kings 24.8-17)
9Jehoiachin was 18 years old when he became king of Judah, and he ruled only 3 months and 10 days from Jerusalem. Jehoiachin also disobeyed the Lord by doing evil. 10 In the spring of the year, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia had Jehoiachin arrested and taken to Babylon, along with more of the valuable items in the temple. Then Nebuchadnezzar appointed Zedekiah king of Judah.
King Zedekiah of Judah
(2 Kings 24.18-20; Jeremiah 52.1-3)
11 Zedekiah was 21 years old when he was appointed king of Judah, and he ruled from Jerusalem for 11 years. 12He disobeyed the Lord his God and refused to change his ways, even after a warning from Jeremiah, the Lord's prophet.
13 King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia had forced Zedekiah to promise in God's name that he would be loyal. Zedekiah was stubborn and refused to turn back to the Lord God of Israel, so he rebelled against Nebuchadnezzar. 14The people of Judah and even the priests who were their leaders became more unfaithful. They followed the disgusting example of the nations around them and made the Lord's holy temple unfit for worship. 15But the Lord God felt sorry for his people, and instead of destroying the temple, he sent prophets who warned the people over and over about their sins. 16But the people only laughed and insulted these prophets. They ignored what the Lord God was trying to tell them, until he finally became so angry that nothing could stop him from punishing Judah and Jerusalem.
Jerusalem Is Destroyed
(2 Kings 25.1-21; Jeremiah 52.3-30)
17 The Lord sent King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia to attack Jerusalem. Nebuchadnezzar killed the young men who were in the temple, and he showed no mercy to anyone, whether man or woman, young or old. God let him kill everyone in the city. 18Nebuchadnezzar carried off everything that was left in the temple; he robbed the treasury and the personal storerooms of the king and his officials. He took everything back to Babylon.
19 Nebuchadnezzar's troops burned down the temple and destroyed every important building in the city. Then they broke down the city wall. 20The survivors were taken to Babylonia as prisoners, where they were slaves of the king and his sons, until Persia became a powerful nation.
21 Judah was an empty desert, and it stayed that way for 70 years, to make up for all the years it was not allowed to rest. These things happened just as Jeremiah the Lord's prophet had said.
Cyrus Lets the Jews Return Home
(Ezra 1.1-4)
22In the first year that Cyrus was king of Persia, the Lord had Cyrus send a message to all parts of his kingdom. This happened just as Jeremiah the Lord's prophet had promised. 23 The message said:
I am King Cyrus of Persia.
The Lord God of heaven has made me the ruler of every nation on earth. He has also chosen me to build a temple for him in Jerusalem, which is in Judah. The Lord God will watch over any of his people who want to go back to Judah.
translation_text:
Joowakaasi nì Yooyakiim nì Yooyakiin, Juuda bɔtiibi
(Kpèè 2 Bib 23.30–24.17)
1Juuda yab nìn yōoǹ Joosiyaasi jipɔɔn Joowakaasi ki kāaǹ ubɔti Jeerusaleem, u-baa yil pu. 2Joowakaasi nìn cáá abin mmuŋku nì ata ní ki kpántì ubɔti ní ki kāl̀ Jeerusaleem ki jíń dibeel iŋmal ita. 3Eejipiti bɔtiu nìn kpákatì-u dibeel Jeerusaleem, ní ki gíí Juuda yab lampoo animbil kúti kiiloobi kutukub bita nì sindaariya kiiloobi mmuŋku nì saalaa. 4Míǹ boonee ní Eejipiti bɔtiu yōoǹ u-naal Eeliyaakiim ki kāaǹ Juuda nì Jeerusaleem pu ubɔti, ní ki kpántì-u diyindi yii Yooyakiim. U nìn yōoǹ Yooyakiim maan Joowakaasi ki cūnnì Eejipiti.
5Yooyakiim nìn cáá abin mmuŋku nì aŋmoo ní ki kpántì ubɔti, ní ki kāl̀ Jeerusaleem ki jíń dibeel abin saalaa nì diba. U nìn ŋá tin kaa kítì ti-Dindaan, u-Nimbɔtiu nimbiinee. 6Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar nìn dɔ́miń ki jáń nì u. U nìn dū tasa kusakai ki bóob́-u tiŋan ki cáa cūnnì Babiloon. 7Neebukadineesaar nìn gíti yōoǹ kunimbɔtidii poon tiwan tikpil ki cáa cūnnì ki síiǹ úǹ u-ba beecindin Babiloon.
8Yooyakiim tuuŋŋi ŋin kíǹee nì ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin u ŋée nì tin bāań-uee kɔkɔ ŋmàn̄ ki kā Isirayeel nì Juuda yab bɔtiibi tuuŋŋi gbɔŋkun.
9Yooyakiin nìn cáá abin anii ní ki kpántì ubɔti ní ki kāl̀ Jeerusaleem ki jíń dibeel iŋmal ita nì iwiin saalaa. U nìn ŋá tin kaa kítì ti-Dindaan nimbiinee. 10Dibindi cá kí kúntée ní Neebukadineesaar tú u-janjaliibi bí cùú cúuń Yooyakiin, kí kpáaǹ tiwammɔntiil tin bí kunimbɔtidiinee Babiloon tiŋkin. U nìn dū u-nabiki Seedeesiyasi ki kāaǹ ubɔti Juuda nì Jeerusaleem.
Seedeesiyasi, Juuda bɔtiu
(Kpèè 2 Bib 24.18–25.21, Yeer 39.1-10, 52.1-27)
11Seedeesiyasi nìn cáá abin mmuŋku nì diba ní ki kpántì ubɔti ní ki kāl̀ Jeerusaleem ki jíń dibeel abin saalaa nì diba. 12U nìn ŋá tin kaa kítì ti-Dindaan, u-Nimbɔtiu nimbiinee. Waa nìn sīntiǹ u-ba Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii un nìn bíi nàatī-u ti-Dindaan bɔtee nimbiin. 13Ubɔti Neebukadineesaar nìn yāntì u pūtì ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti yindi pu, ama nì míǹ kɔkɔee, waa nìn kíí u-ba pu ní ki yíkìi bíi jáà nì u. U nìn ŋá ntafapɔn ní ki pɔ́ɔkì u-pɔbil, ní ki yíì kaa kpántì u-ba ki fātìi gítìń ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu cee. 14Abɔtibil nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì samaa kɔkɔ kaa nìn yúl̀ nì Unimbɔti deedee. Bi nìn ŋá ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin ní atimbun ŋin māntìi tú-bee ŋáańee ki kɔ́ǹ kunimbɔtidii kun bí Jeerusaleem ti-Dindaan dūu sú u-bee tijɔkɔndi. 15Ti-Dindaan, bi-baabi Nimbɔtiu nìn túnní binib ŋfunyɔm kupaau bí kpāafì-bi, di sá yii u-nibooliŋu nì u-saraafaŋŋu nìn gbí-u inimɔɔn. 16Ama Isirayeel yab nìn bēel̀ Unimbɔti tuuŋyi gbanti, ki kpēē u-nyɔɔbundi fám ní ki láń u-bɔnaatiliibi. Niinee ní ti-Dindaan ŋuul jéetì u-nibul pu nnyɔkɔ gíti kpá. 17Ti-Dindaan nìn cáań Babiloon yab bɔtiu ki tɔ́ bi-pu. Úǹ nìn dū kitàataajiki ki kūū bi-naacimpɔmbi áli gba circir kɔŋkooŋŋun. Waa nìn súń unaacimpɔɔnaaa, usapɔɔnaaa, utikpilaaa, unicikitikaa saai. Unimbɔti nìn dū tikɔkɔ ki ŋá u-ŋaan. 18U nìn yōoǹ tiwan tin sá tikpaandi nì ŋwaamu ki nìn bí kunimbɔtidiinee kɔkɔ ki cáa cūnnì Babiloon tiŋkin. U nìn yōoǹ ki kpáaǹ tigaajawan tin bí kunimbɔtidiinee nì tin bí dibeecindinee nì u-kàliŋkpilib yati. 19Bi nìn gāā ŋŋmi ki tūū kunimbɔtidii ní ki gbáń ki wīī digundi din bi nìn máń ki tú Jeerusaleem tiŋkee. Bi nìn gāā ŋŋmi ki tūū adimɔnti kɔkɔ ní ki gbáń ki bíil̀ tiwan tin cáá kunyampoouee kɔkɔ. 20Babiloon bɔtiu nìn yōoǹ bin nìn kíǹ kaa kpíìyee ki cūnnì Babiloon ní bi kpántì úǹ nì u-jipɔmbi yumbui ki cáa sāā ŋyunti ŋun ní Peeriisi yab fōō dibeelee. 21Ti-Dindaan nín nìn dī u-bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii pu ki sòon̄ tiŋyee ŋá míǹ dee yii: «Kitiŋ làá dòon̄ kí ŋùŋfì. Ŋyunti ŋun ní binib kaa ti kóò ki-puee, kì làá ŋùŋfì kí cáá sāā abin imuŋku ita nì saalaa.»
Siirusi pú kinyɔkɔ bí fàtīí mā kunimbɔtidii
22Peeriisi bɔtiu Siirusi nín jíń dibeel dibimpeepeekaal poonee, ní ti-Dindaan lēē kí ŋá kii u nín nìn dī u-bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii pu ki sòon̄ pu ki síiǹee. Ti-Dindaan nìn gbēē Siirusi pɔbil ní ki yāntì u báakì u-beel kɔkɔ poon, ki ŋmàn̄ mun ki síiǹ yii: 23«Peeriisi bɔtiu Siirusi nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Ti-Dindaan, yilpu Nimbɔtiu dū abee ŋin kɔkɔ bí kitiŋ puee ki ŋá m-ŋaan ní ki lēē-mi yii ḿ mā-u kudii Jeerusaleem, Juuda tiŋkin. Ni-kansikin un sá u-nibul yɔuee, ti-Dindaan u-Nimbɔtiu ń nīn bí udaan cee ú jɔ̄m̀ Jeerusaleem!»

english_text:
Cyrus Lets the Jews Return Home
1 Years ago the Lord sent Jeremiah with a message about a promise for the people of Israel. Then in the first year that Cyrus was king of Persia, the Lord kept his promise by telling Cyrus to send this official message to all parts of his kingdom:
2-3 I am King Cyrus of Persia.
The Lord God of heaven, who is also the God of Israel, has made me the ruler of all nations on earth. And he has chosen me to build a temple for him in Jerusalem, which is in Judah. The Lord God will watch over and encourage any of his people who want to go back to Jerusalem and help build the temple.
4Everyone else must provide what is needed. They must give money, supplies, and animals, as well as gifts for rebuilding God's temple.
5Many people felt that the Lord God wanted them to help rebuild his temple, and they made plans to go to Jerusalem. Among them were priests, Levites, and leaders of the tribes of Judah and Benjamin. 6The others helped by giving silver articles, gold, personal possessions, cattle, and other valuable gifts, as well as offerings for the temple.
7King Cyrus gave back the things that Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the Lord's temple in Jerusalem and had put in the temple of his own gods. 8Cyrus placed Mithredath, his chief treasurer, in charge of these things. Mithredath counted them and gave a list to Sheshbazzar, the governor of Judah. 9-10Included among them were: 30 large gold dishes; 1,000 large silver dishes; 29 other dishes; 30 gold bowls; 410 silver bowls; and 1,000 other articles.
11Altogether, there were 5,400 gold and silver dishes, bowls, and other articles. Sheshbazzar took them with him when he and the others returned to Jerusalem from Babylonia.
translation_text:
Siirusi pú kinyɔkɔ bí fàtīí mā kunimbɔtidii
1Peeriisi yab bɔtiu Siirusi beel bimpeepeekaal poonee, ti-Dindaan nìn là kí ŋá min u nìn dī u-bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii pu ki sòon̄ee. U nìn tīī ubɔti Siirusi nlandɔkɔ ú bāakì u-beel kɔkɔ poon, kí ŋmà kugbɔŋu mun ki síiń yii: 2«Man Peeriisi bɔtiu nín sòon̄ tiŋyee sèé: <Ti-Dindaan yilpu Nimbɔtiu dū kitiŋ pu kɔkɔ beeŋi ki ŋá m-ŋaan, ní ki bí-mi yii ḿ mā-u kunimbɔtidii Jeerusaleem, Juuda tiŋkin. 3Ni-kansikin un kamaa sá u-nibul yɔuee, ti-Dindaan u-Nimbɔtiu ń nīn bí udaan cee ú jɔ̄m̀ Jeerusaleem, Juuda tiŋkin kí fàtīí mā ti-Dindaan Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu kunimbɔtidii. Úǹ di sá Unimbɔti un bí Jeerusaleemee. 4Laakin kamaa ní u-nibul din kíǹee yaa bée, niin yab ń tīī-bi animbil kúti nì sindaariya nì tigaajawan nì tiwaŋkuti nì nlammɔntiim saraabi bí dūú tɔ̄ kunimbɔtidii kun bí Jeerusaleemee tundi.»
5Niinee ní Juuda yab nì Beenjameen yab dicaŋŋi kpilib nì bisaraaŋaliibi Leefii yab, an dàkà yii bin kɔkɔ Unimbɔti nìn tīī nlandɔkɔee yíkì ki nín jɔ́ḿ Jeerusaleem kí fàtīí mā kunimbɔtidii kun bí niinee. 6Bi-kɔŋkɔnnaatɔb nìn cáań animbil kúti nì sindaariya wanti nì tigaajawan nì tiwaŋkuti nì tiwan tin pɔ̄ɔ̄ kudaauee kí tūtuǹ-bi, ní kí nín kūtì tiwan tin bi nìn tīī-bi nì dipɔbil dibee.
7Ubɔti Siirusi nìn kóoǹ tiwan tin kɔkɔ ubɔti Neebukadineesaar nìn yōoǹ kunimbɔtidiin Jeerusaleem ki cáań ki yóoǹ u-waadiiŋŋinee ki kpáfì. 8Peeriisi yab bɔtiu Siirusi nìn yāntì Miitireedati un kpèé animbil bɔtee dū an wantee ki ŋúbiǹ Seesbasaar, Juuda yab kpiliu. 9Bi nín kàan̄ tiwan gbantee, ti-nyɔkɔm sɔ̀. Sindaariya sambiliŋ nìn sá mmuŋku nì saalaa, animbil kúti sambiliŋ nìn sá kutuku ubɔ, njimu nìn sá kiba kpá mmuŋku nì saalaa, 10sindaariya sampeemu nìn sá mmuŋku nì saalaa, animbil kúti sampeemu nìn sá alaataa anaa nì saalaa, ní tiwan tin kíǹee kɔkɔ nìn sá kutuku ubɔ. 11Sindaariya nì animbil kúti wantee kɔkɔ nìn nyáń kutukub biŋmoo nì alaataa anaa ní. Ŋyunti ŋun bi nìn nyáń kuyuŋu Babiloon ki fàtīi gítí Jeerusaleemee ní Seesbasaar kpáaǹ an wanti gbanti kɔkɔ.

english_text:
A List of People Who Returned from Exile
(Nehemiah 7.4-73)
1King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia had captured many of the people of Judah and had taken them as prisoners to Babylonia. Now they were on their way back to Jerusalem and to their own towns everywhere in Judah.
2-20Zerubbabel, Joshua, Nehemiah, Seraiah, Reelaiah, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispar, Bigvai, Rehum, and Baanah were in charge of the ones who were coming back. And here is a list of how many returned from each family group: 2,172 from Parosh; 372 from Shephatiah; 775 from Arah; 2,812 descendants of Jeshua and Joab from Pahath Moab; 1,254 from Elam; 945 from Zattu; 760 from Zaccai; 642 from Bani; 623 from Bebai; 1,222 from Azgad; 666 from Adonikam; 2,056 from Bigvai; 454 from Adin; 98 from Ater, also known as Hezekiah; 323 from Bezai; 112 from Jorah; 223 from Hashum; and 95 from Gibbar.
21-35Here is how many people returned whose ancestors had come from the following towns: 123 from Bethlehem; 56 from Netophah; 128 from Anathoth; 42 from Azmaveth; 743 from Kiriatharim, Chephirah, and Beeroth; 621 from Ramah and Geba; 122 from Michmas; 223 from Bethel and Ai; 52 from Nebo; 156 from Magbish; 1,254 from the other Elam; 320 from Harim; 725 from Lod, Hadid, and Ono; 345 from Jericho; and 3,630 from Senaah.
36-39Here is a list of how many returned from each family of priests: 973 descendants of Jeshua from the family of Jedaiah; 1,052 from the family of Immer; 1,247 from the family of Pashhur; and 1,017 from the family of Harim.
40-42And here is a list of how many returned from the families of Levites: 74 descendants of Hodaviah from the families of Jeshua and Kadmiel; 128 descendants of Asaph from the temple musicians; and 139 descendants of Shallum, Ater, Talmon, Akkub, Hatita, and Shobai from the temple guards.
43-54Here is a list of the families of temple workers whose descendants returned: Ziha, Hasupha, Tabbaoth, Keros, Siaha, Padon, Lebanah, Hagabah, Akkub, Hagab, Shamlai, Hanan, Giddel, Gahar, Reaiah, Rezin, Nekoda, Gazzam, Uzza, Paseah, Besai, Asnah, Meunim, Nephisim, Bakbuk, Hakupha, Harhur, Bazluth, Mehida, Harsha, Barkos, Sisera, Temah, Neziah, and Hatipha.
55-57Here is a list of Solomon's servants whose descendants returned: Sotai, Hassophereth, Peruda, Jaalah, Darkon, Giddel, Shephatiah, Hattil, Pochereth Hazzebaim, and Ami.
58A total of 392 descendants of temple workers and of Solomon's servants returned.
59-60There were 652 who returned from the families of Delaiah, Tobiah, and Nekoda, though they could not prove that they were Israelites. They had lived in the Babylonian towns of Tel-Melah, Tel-Harsha, Cherub, Addan, and Immer.
61-62The families of Habaiah, Hakkoz, and Barzillai could not prove that they were priests. The ancestor of the family of Barzillai had married the daughter of Barzillai from Gilead and had taken his wife's family name. But the records of these three families could not be found, and none of them were allowed to serve as priests. 63 In fact, the governor told them, “You cannot eat the food offered to God until we find out if you really are priests.”
64-67There were 42,360 who returned, in addition to 7,337 servants and 200 musicians, both women and men. They brought with them 736 horses, 245 mules, 435 camels, and 6,720 donkeys.
68When the people came to where the Lord's temple had been in Jerusalem, some of the family leaders gave gifts so it could be rebuilt in the same place. 69They gave all they could, and it came to a total of 500 kilograms of gold, 500 kilograms of silver, and 100 robes for the priests.
70 Everyone returned to the towns from which their families had come, including the priests, the Levites, the musicians, the temple guards, and the workers.
translation_text:
Bin nyánní kuyuŋu ki fātìi gítìńee nyɔkɔm
1Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar nìn cúú Juuda yab ki cūnnì Babiloon tiŋkin kuyuŋu. Bin nìn gítìń Jeerusaleem nì Juuda timmu mun kíǹee poonee nìn wīikí. Báà ŋma nìn fātìi kāl̀ u-tiŋkin. 2Bin di nìn līiń bi-nyɔkɔpuee di sá Sooroobabeel nì Joosuwa nì Neeyeemiya nì Seeraya nì Reelaya nì Mɔɔrdookayi nì Biilisan nì Miisipaar nì Biigifayi nì Reewum nì Baana.
Isirayeel yab bininjab nyɔkɔm sɔ̀. 3Pareeyoosi maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib kutukub bili nì dilaataal nì binib binii kpá imuŋku inaa. 4Seefatiya maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib alaataa ata nì binib binii kpá imuŋku inaa. 5Araa maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib alaataa aluli nì binib biŋmoo kpá imuŋku inaa. 6Paati-Moowaab maaliŋun yab, an dàkà yii Joosuwa nì Joowaab yab nìn sá binib kutukub bili nì alaataa anii nì binib saalaa nì bili. 7Eelaam maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib kutuku ubɔ nì alaataa ali nì binib biluu kpá imuŋku ita. 8Saatuu maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib alaataa awa nì imuŋku ili nì binib biŋmoo. 9Sakayi maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib alaataa aluli nì imuŋku ita. 10Banii maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib alaataa aluu nì imuŋku ili nì binib bili. 11Beebaayi maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib alaataa aluu nì binib mmuŋku nì bita. 12Asigaadi maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib kutuku ubɔ nì alaataa ali nì binib mmuŋku nì bili. 13Adooniikam maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib alaataa aluu nì imuŋku ita nì binib biluu. 14Biigifayi maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib kutukub bili nì binib binaa kpá imuŋku ita. 15Adiini maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib alaataa anaa nì imuŋku ili nì unil ubɔ kpá saalku. 16Ateer maaliŋun yab, an dàkà yii Eeskiya yab nìn sá binib bili kpá dilaataal. 17Beesayi maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib alaataa ata nì binib mmuŋku nì bita. 18Yoora maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib dilaataal nì saalaa nì bili. 19Asuum maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib alaataa ali nì binib mmuŋku nì bita. 20Giibaar maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib biŋmoo kpá dilaataal. 21Beetileem tiŋkin yab nìn sá binib dilaataal nì binib mmuŋku nì bita. 22Neetoofa tiŋkin yab nìn sá binib binaa kpá imuŋku ita. 23Anatooti tiŋkin yab nìn sá binib dilaataal nì binib mmuŋku nì binii. 24Asimafeeti tiŋkin yab nìn sá binib imuŋku ili nì bili. 25Kiiriyati-Yeeyariim nì Keefiira nì Beerooti timmun yab nìn sá binib alaataa aluli nì binib imuŋku ili nì bita. 26Raama nì Geeba timmun yab nìn sá binib alaataa aluu nì binib mmuŋku nì unil. 27Miikimaasi tiŋkin yab nìn sá binib dilaataal nì binib mmuŋku nì bili. 28Beeteel nì Aayi timmun yab nìn sá binib alaataa ali nì binib mmuŋku nì bita. 29Neeboo tiŋkin yab nìn sá binib imuŋku ili nì saalaa nì bili. 30Magibiisi tiŋkin yab nìn sá binib dilaataal nì binib binaa kpá imuŋku ita. 31Eelaam ubɔ mun maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib kutuku ubɔ nì alaataa ali nì binib biluu kpá imuŋku ita. 32Ariim maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib alaataa ata nì binib mmuŋku. 33Loodi nì Adiidi nì Oona timmun yab nìn sá binib alaataa aluli nì binib mmuŋku nì biŋmoo. 34Jeeriikoo tiŋkin yab nìn sá binib alaataa ata nì binib imuŋku ili nì biŋmoo. 35Seenaa tiŋkin yab nìn sá binib kutukub bita nì alaataa aluu nì binib mmuŋku nì saalaa.
36Bisaraaŋaliibi kitilinee, Yeedaya maaliŋun yab, an dàkà yii Joosuwa maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib alaataa awa nì binib biluli kpá imuŋku inaa. 37Imeer maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib kutuku ubɔ nì binib binii kpá imuŋku ita. 38Pasuur maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib kutuku ubɔ nì alaataa ali nì binib imuŋku ili nì biluli. 39Ariim maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib kutuku ubɔ nì binib saalku nì bili.
40 Leefii yab kitilinee, Joosuwa nì Kadimiyeel, an dàkà yii Oodafiya maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib imuŋku ita nì unil ubɔ kpá saalku.
41Bilaŋgaaliibi kitilinee, Asaafi maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib dilaataal nì binib mmuŋku nì binii.
42Bipunyɔɔciitiliibi kitilinee, Saaluum nì Ateer nì Talmɔn nì Akuub nì Atiita nì Soobayi maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib dilaataal nì unil ubɔ kpá imuŋku ili.
43 Kunimbɔtidii poon tɔntɔnliibi nín nìn pēē pēē mmaal puee di sá Siiya nì Asufa nì Tabayooti nì 44Keeroosi nì Siyaaka nì Padɔn, 45nì Leebana nì Agaaba nì Akuub, 46nì Agaab nì Samlayi nì Aani, 47nì Giideel nì Gayaar nì Reeyaya, 48nì Reesiin nì Neekooda nì Gaasaam, 49nì Usa nì Paseeya nì Beesayi, 50nì Asina nì Meewuniim nì Neefusiim, 51Bakibuuki nì Nasufa nì Aruuri, 52nì Basluuti nì Meeyida nì Arisa, 53nì Barkoosi nì Siseela nì Taama, 54nì Neesiya nì Atiifa yab. 55Saloomɔn tɔntɔnliibi nín nìn pēē pēē mmaal puee di sá Sootayi nì Soofeereeti nì Peeruda, 56nì Yala nì Darkɔn nì Giideel, 57nì Seefatiya nì Atiil nì Pookeereeti-Aseebayiim nì Amii maaliŋun yab.
58Kunimbɔtidii poon tɔntɔnliibi nì Saloomɔn tɔntɔnliibi maaliŋun yab nìn kpáfì binib binii kpá alaataa anaa.
59Binib bin nìn nyánní Teel-Meela nì Teel-Arisa nì Keerub-Adaani nì Imeer timmunee kaa nìn ŋúń ki béè yii bi-naanjab maaliŋun yab nì bi-nyeeŋŋu nìn baasii sá Isirayeel. 60Bíǹ di nìn sá Deelaya nì Toobiya nì Neekooda maaliŋun yab. Bi nìn sá binib alaataa aluu nì binii kpá imuŋku ita ní.
61Bisaraaŋaliibi kansikinee, Yoobaya nì Akoosi nì Barsilayii maaliŋun yab mun nìn bí. Barsilayii gbanti di nìn cáá ugalaadija Barsilayii bisal ubɔ. An pu ní bi nìn dū diyindi gbanti ki pú-u. 62Binibee nìn nyàab̄ bi-naanjab yiŋŋi gbɔnti kaa ká. An puee bi nìn dū-bi ki yíiń bijɔkɔnnib ní ki nyántì-bi disaraaŋal tundin. 63Ní bi-gɔminau bí-bi yii bí taa ti jī tijin tin bi dūu ŋá saraa tì bí circir páaayee kí nīn cí usaraaŋakpil ubɔ ń dāá dū Uriim nì Tumiim kí bàlifì dibalifil.
64Isirayeel yab bin kɔkɔ nìn nyánní kuyuŋu ki bāańee nìn sá binib kutukub imuŋku ili nì bili nì binib alaataa ata nì imuŋku ita ní. 65Bi-tɔntɔnliibi bininjab nì binimpoobi kaa nìn kútì. Bíǹ nìn sá binib kutukub biluli nì alaataa ata nì binib bita kpá imuŋku ili. Biwambɔɔliibi nì bilaŋgaaliibi bininjab nì binimpoobi nìn sá binib alaataa ali. 66Bi nìn cáá itaamu alaataa aluli nì itaamu inaa kpá imuŋku ili, ki cáá imamboon alaataa ali nì imuŋku ili nì iŋmoo. 67Bi nìn cáá igutaamu alaataa anaa nì iŋmoo kpá imuŋku ili, ní ki cáá mmamu kutukub biluu nì alaataa aluli nì mmuŋku.
68Bi nín fātìi bāań Jeerusaleem laakin ti-Dindaan diiku nìn bée, ní adican kpilib biba ŋá nlammɔntiim saraabi, bí fàtīí mā kunimbɔtidii laakin ku nìn pée yú ŋkpikimee. 69Kí nóó nì bi-pɔŋŋu nyɔkɔmee, bi nìn tīī asindaariyakún kutukub imuŋku ita nì diba, nì animbil kúti kiiloobi kutukub bili nì dijandi nì bisaraaŋaliibi bɔkutiŋ dilaataal.
70Niinee bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab nì samaa kansikin biba, nì bilaŋgaaliibi nì bipunyɔɔciitiliibi nì kunimbɔtidiin tɔntɔnliibi cūtìi kāl̀ bi-timmun. Isirayeel yab bin kíǹee mun nìn cūtìi kāl̀ bi-naanjab timmun.

english_text:
The First Offering on the New Altar
1During the seventh month of the year, the Israelites who had settled in their towns went to Jerusalem. 2 The priest Joshua son of Jozadak, together with the other priests, and Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and his relatives rebuilt the altar of Israel's God. Then they were able to offer sacrifices there by following the instructions God had given to Moses, the man of God. 3 And they built the altar where it had stood before, even though they were afraid of the people who were already living around there. Then every morning and evening they burned sacrifices and offerings to the Lord.
4 The people followed the rules for celebrating the Festival of Shelters and offered the proper sacrifices each day. 5 They offered sacrifices to please the Lord, sacrifices at each New Moon Festival, and sacrifices at the rest of the Lord's festivals. Every offering the people had brought voluntarily was also presented to the Lord.
6Although work on the temple itself had not yet begun, the people started offering sacrifices on the Lord's altar on the first day of the seventh month of that year.
The Rebuilding of the Temple Begins
7King Cyrus of Persia had said the Israelites could have cedar trees brought from Lebanon to Joppa by sea. So they sent grain, wine, and olive oil to the cities of Tyre and Sidon as payment for these trees, and they gave money to the stoneworkers and carpenters.
8During the second month of the second year after the people had returned from Babylonia, they started rebuilding the Lord's temple. Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, Joshua son of Jozadak, the priests, the Levites, and everyone else who had returned started working. Every Levite over 20 years of age was put in charge of some part of the work. 9The Levites in charge of the whole project were Joshua and his sons and relatives and Kadmiel and his sons from the family of Hodaviah. The family of Henadad worked along with them.
10 When the builders had finished laying the foundation of the temple, the priests put on their robes and blew trumpets in honor of the Lord, while the Levites from the family of Asaph praised God with cymbals. All of them followed the instructions given years before by King David. 11 They praised the Lord and gave thanks as they took turns singing:
“The Lord is good!
His faithful love for Israel
will last forever.”
Everyone started shouting and praising the Lord because work on the foundation of the temple had begun. 12 Many of the older priests and Levites and the heads of families wept bitterly because they remembered seeing the first temple years before. But others were so happy that they celebrated with joyful shouts. 13Their shouting and crying were so noisy that it all sounded alike and could be heard a long way off.
translation_text:
Joosuwa nì Sooroobabeel fātìi bɔ́ntì dinimbɔtinool
1Dibindi poon ŋmaluluútiu bāańee, Isirayeel yab bin kɔkɔ nìn gítìń ki kāl̀ bi-timmunee nìn kóoǹ ki cūtìi kpáfì kii unibaantee Jeerusaleem tiŋkin. 2Niinee ní usaraaŋakpil Joosuwa, Yoosadaaki jipɔɔn nì u-nabiyaamu bisaraaŋaliibi nì Saltiyeel jipɔɔn Sooroobabeel nì u-dicaŋkun yab yíkìi kíĺ ki bíi māā Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu saraafaŋŋu kí ŋá bisaraawɔkaabi kii Unimbɔti niliu Mooyiisi nín yóoǹ mara yii bí nín ŋáań puee. 3Nì min kɔkɔ bi nìn fàŋkí binib bin nìn bí niinee, bi nìn fātìi máń nsaraafan ŋu-paaŋkpikiŋu pu, ní ki kíǹ ki ŋáań kutaafaau nì kujoou saraabi ki tìì ti-Dindaan. 4Míǹ boonee ní bi jíń tantib jiŋaaliu kii bi nín síiǹ mara bí nīn jīǹ-u puee, ní ki ŋáań kutaa kamaa saraabi bin nyɔkɔm bi máaǹ kí ŋée. 5Boonee ní bi kíĺ ki bíi ŋáań baabadal saraabi nì saraabi bin bi ŋáań uŋmapɔɔn kamaayee, nì bin bi ŋáań ti-Dindaan jiŋaalib yuntiŋuee nì saraabi bin kɔkɔ binib nìn cāabìń ki tìì ti-Dindaanee. 6Uŋmaluluúti wimpeekaaŋu dalee ní bi kíĺ ki bíi ŋáań bisaraawɔkaabi ki tìì ti-Dindaan, nì min kɔkɔ baa nìn dáá bíl̀ ti-Dindaan diiku kun bi làá mēe nyeelee.
7Míǹ boonee ní bi tīī bin kpítí ataŋkpeeyee nì kapintab animbil, ní ki tīī Siidɔn yab nì Tiir yab tijin nì ndaam nì ŋkpam bí bóob́ seedir dɔi kí dūú tɔ̄ń tiŋkun doooo Leebanɔn tiŋkin án dāá nyā Jafaa tiŋkin. Peeriisi yab bɔtiu Siirusi di pú-bi kinyɔkɔ ní bi ŋúń ki ŋá míǹ. 8Bi nín fātìi bāań Jeerusaleem laakin kunimbɔtidii nìn bée, dibinliliitiil ŋmaliliitiu poon ní Samiyeel jipɔɔn Sooroobabeel, nì Yoosadaaki jipɔɔn Joosuwa, nì bi-nabiyaamu mun kíǹee, an dàkà yii bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab nì bin kɔkɔ nìn nyánní kuyuŋu ki kūnnée, kíĺ ki bíi bɔ́ntí Leefii yab bin nìn cáá abin mmuŋku kí nīn cáa cée bí kpòotī kunimbɔtidii mātam tuuŋŋi. 9Joosuwa nì u-jipɔmbi nì u-nabiyaamu, nì Kadimiyeel nì u-jipɔmbi nì u-nabiyaamu Juuda naakookun yab di nìn kpáfì dicilpu kí kpòotī bin kɔkɔ làá nīn bí kunimbɔtidii mātam tuuŋŋi poonee. Eeniyadaadi maaliŋun yab nì bi-jipɔmbi nì bi-nabiyaamu Leefii yab nìn kútì bi-pu.
10Ŋyunti ŋun bidimaliibi nìn kíĺ ki bíi bīil̀ kunimbɔtidii nyeelee, bisaraaŋaliibi nìn yú ki pēē bi-saraaŋabɔkutiŋ ki ŋúb́ akantán, ní Leefii yab bin sá Asaafi maaliŋunee ŋúb́ cancakantib, ki nyɔ́ŋkí ti-Dindaan kii Isirayeel yab bɔtiu Daafiidi nín nìn yóoǹ mara pu bi ŋmàn̄ ki síiǹee. 11Bi nìn gà ilan ki tìì tɔb ki nyɔ́ŋkí ti-Dindaan yii: «Tiŋman, u ŋān̄ ní u-neendi bí Isirayeel yab pu kí nīn cá jaanjaan.» Ní samaa kɔkɔ kūuntí mpɔn ki nyɔ́ŋkí ti-Dindaan, kun puee bi nìn kíĺ kunimbɔtidii nyeel ki bíi māā.
12Bisaraaŋaliibi tikpil nì Leefii yab nì adican kpilib kansikin bin nìn púĺ ki ká dooooyee Nimbɔtidiiku nín nìn bí puee, nìn bíi sūǹ mpɔn bi nín ká bi bíi bīil̀ kupɔŋu nyeelee. Ama ní tikpil mun nìn bíi kūuntí mpɔn nì dipɔɔpindi. 13An ŋá mimmee binib kaa nìn gíti ŋūǹ kí gàntī bin nìn bí ki kūuntí nì dipɔɔpindee nì bin nìn bí ki sūǹ mpɔnee, kun puee bi nìn kūuntí mpɔn mpɔn ní an gbìl̀ ndan.

english_text:
Foreigners
Want To Help Rebuild the Temple
1The enemies of the tribes of Judah and Benjamin heard that the people had come back to rebuild the temple of the Lord God of Israel. 2 So they went to Zerubbabel and to the family leaders and said, “Let us help! Ever since King Esarhaddon of Assyria brought us here, we have worshiped your God and offered sacrifices to him.”
3But Zerubbabel, Joshua, and the family leaders answered, “You cannot take part in building a temple for the Lord our God! We will build it ourselves, just as King Cyrus of Persia commanded us.”
4Then the neighboring people began to do everything possible to frighten the Jews and to make them stop building. 5During the time that Cyrus was king and even until Darius became king, they kept bribing government officials to slow down the work.
Trouble Rebuilding Jerusalem
6 In the first year that Xerxes was king, the neighboring people brought written charges against the people of Judah and Jerusalem.
7Later, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and their advisors got together and wrote a letter to Artaxerxes when he was king of Persia. It was written in Aramaic and had to be translated.
8-10 A letter was also written to Artaxerxes about Jerusalem by Governor Rehum, Secretary Shimshai, and their advisors, including the judges, the governors, the officials, and the local leaders. They were joined in writing this letter by people from Erech and Babylonia, the Elamites from Susa, and people from other foreign nations that the great and famous Ashurbanipal had forced to settle in Samaria and other parts of Western Province.
11This letter said:
Your Majesty King Artaxerxes, we are your servants from everywhere in Western Province, and we send you our greetings.
12You should know that the Jews who left your country have moved back to Jerusalem and are now rebuilding that rebellious city. In fact, they have almost finished rebuilding the walls and repairing the foundations. 13You should also know that if the walls are completed and the city is rebuilt, the Jews won't pay any kind of taxes, and there will be less money in your treasury.
14We are telling you this, because you have done so much for us, and we want everyone to respect you. 15If you look up the official records of your ancestors, you will find that Jerusalem has constantly rebelled and has led others to rebel against kings and provinces. That's why the city was destroyed in the first place. 16If Jerusalem is rebuilt and its walls completed, you will no longer have control over Western Province.
17King Artaxerxes answered:
Greetings to Governor Rehum, Secretary Shimshai, and to your advisors in Samaria and other parts of Western Province.
18After your letter was translated and read to me, 19I had the old records checked. It is true that for years Jerusalem has rebelled and caused trouble for other kings and nations. 20And powerful kings have ruled Western Province from Jerusalem and have collected all kinds of taxes.
21I want you to command the people to stop rebuilding the city until I give further notice. 22Do this at once, so that no harm will come to the kingdom.
23As soon as this letter was read, Governor Rehum, Secretary Shimshai, and their advisors went to Jerusalem and forced everyone to stop rebuilding the city.
Work on the Temple Starts Again
24 The Jews were forced to stop work on the temple and were not able to do any more building until the year after Darius became king of Persia.
translation_text:
Juuda yab nannanliibi kaa kíí bí mā kunimbɔtidii
1Juuda nì Beenjameen yab nannanliibi nìn gbìl̄ yii bin nyánní kuyuŋu ki gítìńee bíi māā bi-Dindaan Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu diiku. 2Niinee ní bi sútì ki pìl̄ Sooroobabeel nì adican kpilib ki bí-bi yii: «Ti làá kūtì ni-pu ní mā kunimbɔtidii nee, di sá yii ti mun pée nóó Unimbɔtibaantee ní. Kí yòon̄ daliŋkin Asuur bɔtiu Asaradɔn yōoǹní-ti ki cáań dooyee, ti pée ŋáań saraabi ní ki tìì Unimbɔti.»
3Ama ní Sooroobabeel nì Joosuwa nì Isirayeel dicaŋŋi kpilib bin kíǹee kíí-bi yii: «An kaa kítì yii ní kūtì ti-pu tí mā ti-Nimbɔtiu kudii. An sá timbi baba ní ń mā ti-Dindaan Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu kudii, kii Peeriisi yab bɔtiu Siirusi nín tīī-ti mara yii tí ŋá puee.»
4Niinee ní binib bin kóò kitiŋ gbantinee yɔ̄tì Juuda yab wunti ki kɔ́ǹ-bi tifaandi bí gbèen̄ kí taa ti mā kunimbɔtidii. 5Kí yòon̄ ŋyunti ŋun Peeriisi yab bɔtiu Siirusi kā dibeel ki tin cáa sāā ŋyunti ŋun Daariyusi dāa kāl̀ dibeelee, bi nìn pée tìì kitiŋ gbanti kàliŋkpilib animbil yii bíǹ ń pìin̄ Juuda yab nsan atuun ń gbèen̄ ní.
Bi ŋmàn̄ tigban ki mɔ́ntì Juuda yab nyɔkɔpu
6Ubɔti Asuweerusi nín kāl̀ dibeel pu kpalaayee, ní Juuda yab nannanliibi ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu ki túǹ Juuda nì Jeerusaleem yab pu dibɔgaandi.
7Peeriisi yab bɔtiu Aritaseerseesi yuntiŋuee ní Biseelam nì Miitireedati nì Taabeel nì u-jutiibi mun ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu ki tīī ubɔti. Bi nìn ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu gbanti poon Aram yab ŋmaŋmabiti nì bi-sooŋyin ní.
8Kitiŋ gbanti gɔminau Reewum nì u-gbaŋŋmaliu Simsayi mun nìn ŋmàn̄ ubɔti kugbɔŋu ki sòon̄ Jeerusaleem pu yii:
9«An sá gɔmina Reewum nì ugbaŋŋmal Simsayi nì bi-tɔntɔnjutiibi bin bí Diini nì Afarsataki nì Tarpeel nì Afarasi nì Eereeki nì Babiloon nì Suusi nì Deeya nì Eelaam timmun, 10ki kpáaǹ anibul ŋin Asinapaar un nyáń diyindee nìn cáań ki kāaǹ Samaarii tiŋkinee, nì ntimu mun kíǹ ki bí Eefiraati mɔɔl ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki púee di ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu nee.»
11Tibɔti tin bi nìn ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu gbanti poonee sèé:
«Ubɔti Daariyusi, an sá timbi a-tɔntɔnliibi bin kóò ntimu mun bí Eefiraati mɔɔl ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki púee di ŋmàn̄-si kugbɔŋu nee.
12«Ti-baa ubɔti, ti là á béé yii Juuda yab bin nyánní a-cee ki fātìi bāań timbi cee Jeerusaleem dooyee kíĺ ki fātìi bíi māā kitiŋ kin kaa ŋān̄ ní ki-nib sá pɔɔgaatibee. Bi ŋáŋkì digundi din māntìi tú-kèe nyeel ki bíi māā ki tɔ̄kɔntí. 13Míǹ puee ti-baa ubɔti, ti là á béé yii bi yaa fātìi máń kitiŋ nee ki yōoǹ ki-gundee, baa làá gíti pà lampoobi nì patantib nì animbil ŋin bisaŋkinliibi pèe, an di làá dāá cáań sii ubɔti agìń. 14An puee timbi bin ká diyimɔɔl a-cee ki sá a-tɔntɔnliibee kaa ŋūǹ kí nīn kā ki kpèé bí nīn kpèé sii ubɔti fám míǹ. An pu ní ti bíi tùkù-si tibɔti nee 15á yàntī bí nyàab̀ bibɔtikpikib gbɔnti poon. Sii a-ba làá ká yii kitiŋ gbanti nib pée sá pɔɔgaatib ní, ki kɔ̄ntí bibɔtiibi nì ntimu yidambi agìń. Laakin kamaa ní bi yaa bée, bi pée cāabìń agìń ŋma ní. An pu gba ní bi dāa nāaǹ kitiŋ gbanti. 16Míǹ pu ní ti là sii ti-baa ubɔti ń béé yii bi yaa fātìi máń kitiŋ nee nì ki-gundee, sii di kaa ti làá nīn yì Eefiraati mɔɔl ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki timmu gbanti.»
Ubɔti Aritaseerseesi kíí kugbɔŋu kun bi ŋmàn̄-uee
17Ubɔti nìn ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu ki kíí-bi yii:
«Gɔmina Reewum nì ugbaŋŋmal Simsayi nì bi-tɔntɔnjutiibi bin bí Samaarii nì ntimu mun kíǹ ki bí Eefiraati mɔɔl ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki púee,
«m jáam̀-ni.
18«M fōō kugbɔŋu kun ni ŋmàn̄ní-mee, bi kàan̄-ku m-nimbiin ní ki nāatì. 19M yāntì bi nyàab̄ tibɔkpikil gbɔnti poon ní ki lafun ká yii doooo cannaakuee, Jeerusaleem yab nìn pée jáà nì bibɔtiibi ní, kaa nìn kíikí bi-ba pu, ní ki nìn gáatí binib. 20Njaminee, Jeerusaleem tiŋki nìn cáá bibɔtikpaambi bin nìn cáá mpɔnee. Bíǹ di nìn kpèé Eefiraati mɔɔl ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú timmu kɔkɔ, ní ki nìn fòol̄ ntimu gbanti nib lampoobi nì patantib nì animbil ŋin bisaŋkinliibi nìn pèe. 21An puee ní yóoń mara yii binib gbanti ń gbèen̄ bi-tuuŋŋi, kí tùkù-bi yii bí taa fàtīí mā tiba kí nīn cí ŋyunti ŋun ní man làá dāá pɔ̄ kinyɔkɔee. 22Ní kpèèmaan tiŋan kí taa ŋá bugbambu tibɔti nee poon, án nín làá ŋá pu án taa láa kpántí tibɔkpaandi kí dāá cáań bibɔtiibi agìńee.»
23Ŋyunti ŋun ní bi fōō ubɔti Aritaseerseesi gbɔŋkuee ki kàan̄-ku Reewum nì ugbaŋŋmal Simsayi nì bi-tɔntɔnjutiibi bin kíǹee nimbiinee, dicilpu niin ní bi nín cá Jeerusaleem, ki tin dàkā Juuda yab mpɔn bí gbèen̄ atuun.
Bi fātìi kíĺ kunimbɔtidii mātam
24Niin ní bi gbēeǹ Unimbɔti diiku mātam tuuŋŋi Jeerusaleem tiŋkin, ki tin cáa sāā Peeriisi yab bɔtiu Daariyusi nín kāl̀ dibeelee binliliitiil poon.

english_text:
1 Then the Lord God of Israel told the prophets Haggai and Zechariah to speak in his name to the people of Judah and Jerusalem. And they did. 2 So Zerubbabel the governor and Joshua the priest urged the people to start working on the temple again, and God's prophets encouraged them.
3Governor Tattenai of Western Province and his assistant Shethar Bozenai got together with some of their officials. Then they went to Jerusalem and said to the people, “Who told you to rebuild this temple? 4Give us the names of the workers!”
5But God was looking after the Jewish leaders. So the governor and his group decided not to make the people stop working on the temple until they could report to Darius and get his advice.
6Governor Tattenai, Shethar Bozenai, and their advisors sent a report to Darius, 7which said:
King Darius, we wish you the best! 8We went to Judah, where the temple of the great God is being built with huge stones and wooden beams set in the walls. Everyone is working hard, and the building is going up quickly.
9We asked those in charge to tell us who gave them permission to rebuild the temple. 10We also asked for the names of their leaders, so that we could write them down for you.
11They claimed to be servants of the God who rules heaven and earth. And they said they were rebuilding the temple that was built many years ago by one of Israel's greatest kings.
12 We were told that their people had made God angry, and he let them be captured by Nebuchadnezzar, the Babylonian king who took them away as captives to Babylonia. Nebuchadnezzar tore down their temple, 13-15 took its gold and silver articles, and put them in the temple of his own god in Babylon.
They also said that during the first year Cyrus was king of Babylonia, he gave orders for God's temple to be rebuilt in Jerusalem where it had stood before. So Cyrus appointed Sheshbazzar governor of Judah and sent these gold and silver articles for him to put in the temple. 16Sheshbazzar then went to Jerusalem and laid the foundation for the temple, and the work is still going on.
17Your Majesty, please order someone to look up the old records in Babylonia and find out if King Cyrus really did give orders to rebuild God's temple in Jerusalem. We will do whatever you think we should.
translation_text:
1Ŋyunti gbantee ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi Agaayi nì Idoo jipɔɔn Sakari sòon̄ nì Juuda yab bin bí Jeerusaleemee nì bin bí Juuda tiŋki kɔkɔnee, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu un nìn bí bi-nee yindi pu. 2Niinee Sooroobabeel jipɔɔn Saltiyeel nì Joosuwa jipɔɔn Yoosadaaki yíkì ki kíĺ ki bíi māā Unimbɔti diiku Jeerusaleem. Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi nìn kútì bi-pu ki tútúǹ-bi.
3Ŋyunti gbantee ní Tateenaayi un nìn sá gɔmina Eefiraati mɔɔl ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki timmunee nì Seetaar-Boosinayi nì bi-tɔntɔnjutiibi dɔ́miń bi-cee ki bālifì-bi yii: «Ŋma di pú-ni kinyɔkɔ yii ní fàtīí mā kunimbɔtidii nee nì ku-guŋŋi ní? 4Ní tīī-ti binib bin bíi māā kunimbɔtidii neeyee yiŋŋi.»
5Ama Unimbɔti nìn wúń Juuda yab kpilib pu. Baa nìn ŋúń ki pīiǹ-bi nsan bí taa ti mā, kí nīn cí tibɔti gbanti ń bà ubɔti Daariyusi, ní úǹ ń kíiń ní bí nín béé bi nín làá ŋá puee.
Bi kúŋfì Juuda yab boon ubɔti cee
6Gɔmina Tateenaayi nì Seetaar-Boosinayi nì u-tɔntɔnjutiibi nì bikàliŋkpilib bin sá Eefiraati ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú timmu kpilibee nìn ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu ki tīī ubɔti Daariyusi. 7Bi nìn ŋmàn̄ yii:
«Ubɔti Daariyusi, Unimbɔti ń yàntī á nīn bí ŋgbansɔŋfin.
8«Ti là ti-baa ubɔti ń béé yii ti cūtì Juuda tiŋkin áli ki bàn̄ Unimbɔtikpaan diiku laŋki. Bi fātìi kíĺ ki bíi māā kunimbɔtidii. Ataŋkpakpaan ní bi kpítì ní ki cáá idɔjaa ki kútí ki māā agun. Bi baasii bíi tūǹ ditundi mmɔntiimin, ní an bíi cá malaa malaa mun. 9Ní ti bālifì bi-kpilib yii: <Ŋma di pú-ni kinyɔkɔ yii ní fàtīí mā kunimbɔtidii nee nì ku-guŋŋi ní?> 10Boonee ní ti fōō bi-yiŋŋi ki ŋmàn̄ kí dūú tīiń-si á béé bikpilib bin di bíi kpòotī atuunee. 11Kpèè binib gbanti nín kíí-ti tibɔti tiŋyee sèé:
«<Timbi sá Unimbɔti un náań yilpu nì taapuee tɔntɔnliibi ní ki fātìi bíi māā kunimbɔtidii kun Isirayeel bɔtikpaaŋwu ubɔ nìn máń ki dóò dooooyee. 12Ama ti-naanjab nìn kɔ́ǹ Unimbɔti un náań yilpuee diŋuul ní u dū-bi ki líiǹ Babiloon tiŋki bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar, ní úǹ dɔ́miń ki gbáń ki wīī kunimbɔtidii ní ki cúú-bi ki cūnnì kuyuŋu Babiloon tiŋkin. 13Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, Siirusi nín kāl̀ dibeel Babiloon tiŋkinee, u-bimpeepeekaal poon ní u pú-ti kinyɔkɔ yii tí fàtīí mā kunimbɔtidii. 14Ubɔti Neebukadineesaar nìn yōoǹ sindaariya nì animbil kúti sambiliŋ ŋin nìn yú kunimbɔtidiin Jeerusaleemee ki cáa cūnnì ki yóoǹ Babiloon yab waadiikun. Ama ní ubɔti Siirusi nìn yōoǹ tiwan gbanti Babiloon yab waadiikun ki dūu tīī Seesbasaar un u nìn kāaǹ ú nīn sá gɔmina Juuda tiŋkinee. 15U nìn bí-u yii ú yòon̄ tiwan gbanti kí cáá cùnnì kunimbɔtidiin Jeerusaleem. Bí fàtīí mā kunimbɔtidii ku-paaŋŋu ŋkpiki pu ní kí dū tiwan gbanti kí yóoń poon.> 16Di sá ní Seesbasaar gbanti dɔ́miń Jeerusaleem doo ki bíl̀ Unimbɔti diiku nyeel. Kí yòon̄ ŋyunti gbanti kí dāá sāā díǹ ti pée bí ku-pu dimal ní an kaa láá dóò. 17Kɔŋkɔnnee ti-baa ubɔti, a yaa là, a ŋūǹ kí yàntī bí nyàab̀ Babiloon niin, bibɔtiibi gbɔnti poon kí kpèè yii ubɔti Siirusi yaa nìn lafun pú kinyɔkɔ bí fàtīí mā kunimbɔtidii Jeerusaleem. Boonee sii ti-baa ubɔti ń yàntī tí gbìl̄ a nín síiǹ-ti puee.»

english_text:
King Cyrus' Order Is Rediscovered
1King Darius ordered someone to go through the old records kept in Babylonia. 2Finally, a scroll was found in Ecbatana, the capital of Media Province, and it said:
This official record will show 3that in the first year Cyrus was king, he gave orders to rebuild God's temple in Jerusalem, so that sacrifices and offerings could be presented there. It is to be built 27 meters high and 27 meters wide, 4with one row of wooden beams for each three rows of large stones. The royal treasury will pay for everything. 5Then the gold and silver things that Nebuchadnezzar took from the temple and brought to Babylonia are to be returned to their proper places.
King Darius Orders the Work To Continue
6King Darius sent this message:
Governor Tattenai of Western Province and Shethar Bozenai, you and your advisors must stay away from the temple. 7Let the Jewish governor and leaders rebuild it where it stood before. And stop slowing them down!
8Starting at once, I am ordering you to help the leaders by paying their expenses from the tax money collected in Western Province. 9And don't fail to let the priests in Jerusalem have whatever they need each day so they can offer sacrifices to the God of heaven. Give them young bulls, rams, sheep, as well as wheat, salt, wine, and olive oil. 10I want them to be able to offer pleasing sacrifices to God and to pray for me and my family.
11If any of you don't obey this order, a wooden beam will be taken from your house and sharpened on one end. Then it will be driven through your body, and your house will be torn down and turned into a garbage dump. 12I ask the God who is worshiped in Jerusalem to destroy any king or nation who tries either to change what I have said or to tear down his temple. I, Darius, give these orders, and I expect them to be followed carefully.
The Temple Is Dedicated
13Governor Tattenai, Shethar Bozenai, and their advisors carefully obeyed King Darius. 14 With great success the Jewish leaders continued working on the temple, while Haggai and Zechariah encouraged them by their preaching. And so, the temple was completed at the command of the God of Israel and by the orders of kings Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes of Persia. 15On the third day of the month of Adar in the sixth year of the rule of Darius, the temple was finished.
16The people of Israel, the priests, the Levites, and everyone else who had returned from exile were happy and celebrated as they dedicated God's temple. 17One hundred bulls, two hundred rams, and four hundred lambs were offered as sacrifices at the dedication. Also twelve goats were sacrificed as sin offerings for the twelve tribes of Israel. 18Then the priests and Levites were assigned their duties in God's temple in Jerusalem, according to the instructions Moses had written.
The Passover
19 Everyone who had returned from exile celebrated Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month. 20The priests and Levites had gone through a ceremony to make themselves acceptable to lead in worship. Then some of them killed Passover lambs for those who had returned, including the other priests and themselves.
21The sacrifices were eaten by the Israelites who had returned and by the neighboring people who had given up the sinful customs of other nations in order to worship the Lord God of Israel. 22For seven days they celebrated the Festival of Thin Bread. Everyone was happy because the Lord God of Israel had made sure that the king of Assyria would be kind to them and help them build the temple.
translation_text:
Ubɔti Daariyusi nín kíí puee
1Niinee ní ubɔti Daariyusi tīī mara yii bí nyàab̀ Babiloon yab gbɔnti tin bí adiin ŋin poon bi kpáafí bi-gaajawantee poon kí kpèè. 2Ama Eekibataani, kitiŋ kin bi máń digundi ki māntìi tú kì bí Meedi tiŋkpaaŋki poonee ní bi tin ká kugbɔŋu kubɔ. Bi nìn ŋmàn̄ ku-poon yii:
«Tibɔti tin bi ŋmàn̄ ki yóoǹ fool boon puee.
3«Ubɔti Siirusi nín nìn kāl̀ dibeel dibimpeepeekaalee, u nìn pú kinyɔkɔ yii bí fàtīí mā kunimbɔtidii Jeerusaleem, án nīn sá laakin bi làá nīn ŋáań saraabee. Bí fàtīí gíiǹ-ku kí mā kí tɔ́kɔń kukpikuu nyeel pu. Ku-fɔkɔŋŋu ń nīn sá meetab mmuŋku nì saalaa, ku-waaŋŋu mun ń nīn sá meetab mmuŋku nì saalaa. 4Bí kpítí ataŋkpakpaan kí dūú mā ikuul ita ní kí dū idɔ kí páań ŋkuul ŋubɔ. Dibeel nimbiliŋ poon ní bi làá lēē kí dūú tɔ̄ atuun gbanti kɔkɔ. 5Kí kūtèe, bí gíiǹ sindaariya wanti nì animbil kúti wanti tin Neebukadineesaar nìn yōoǹ kunimbɔtidiin Jeerusaleem ki cáa cūnnì Babiloonee. Bí cáá-tì kí yóoń kunimbɔtidiin Jeerusaleem, tikɔkɔ ń nīn yú ti-laŋki.»
6Míǹ puee, sii Tateenaayi, Eefiraati ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú timmu gɔminau nì Seetaar-Boosinayi nì ni-tɔntɔnjutiibi nì bikàliŋkpilib bin bí Eefiraati ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú timmunee:
«Ní taa ti bɔ̄ ni-nyɔkɔ kunimbɔtidii gbanti mātam bɔti poon. 7Yàntīmaan Juuda yab ń tɔ̄ bi-ba kí mā kunimbɔtidii. Juuda yab gɔminau nì bi-kpilib ń fàtīí gíiǹ kunimbɔtidii gbanti kí mā kí tɔ́kɔń ku-nyeel ŋkpiki pu. 8M tīī-ni mara ní tūtuǹ Juuda yab kpilib bí fàtīí mā kunimbɔtidii. Ní dū lampoo nimbiliŋ ŋin binib bin bí Eefiraati mɔɔl ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki púee pà ki tìì ubɔtee kí dūú tīī-bi bí nīn cáa pà bitɔntɔnliibi, ditundi ń taa gbèen̄. 9Ní tīī-bi tin kɔkɔ pée máaǹee, an dàkà yii anajapɔmbil nì ipijaa nì apibil bí nīn cáa ŋáań bisaraawɔkaabi ki tìì Unimbɔti un náań yilpu nì taapuee, ní kí tīī bilee nì ŋyaam nì ndamam nì ŋkpam kí nóó nì bisaraaŋaliibi bin bí Jeerusaleemee nín síiǹ puee bí nīn cáa ŋáań baabadal saraau an taa lóó ŋwindal. 10Mimmee bi làá ŋmā kí nīn ŋáań saraabi bin sɔnsɔfiŋu sɔ̀ŋkī Unimbɔti un náań yilpuee pɔbil, ní kí mèè kí tīī ubɔti nì u-jipɔmbi ń nīn bí dimaŋfalin. 11Un kamaa di yaa yīntì mara gbantee, bí lēē u-diiku dɔjaatiŋu kí cóoń kí dū-u kí lúntí ŋu-pu, ní u-cindi ń kpántí ditampundi. 12Bibɔtiibi nì atimbun ŋin kɔkɔ yaa yīntì mara un m yóoǹ nee, ki tāntì bi-ŋal kí wīī kunimbɔtidii kun bi bíi māā Jeerusaleem nee, Unimbɔti un bí niin bi yíì u-yindee ń lábití bi-beeŋi kí cìb̄. Man ubɔti Daariyusi di yóoǹ mara nee, bí ŋá m nín lī puee deedee.»
13Niinee Tateenaayi, Eefiraati ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú timmu gɔminau nì Seetaar-Boosinayi nì bi-tɔntɔnjutiibi ŋá kii ubɔti nín tīiń mara yii bí ŋá puee deedee.
Bi jíń kunimbɔtidii kun bi fātìi máńee jiŋaaliu
14Juuda yab kpilib nìn nìkī kunimbɔtidii mātam an cōom̀ tiŋan, kii Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi Agaayi nì Idoo jipɔɔn Sakari nín nìn sòon̄ puee. Bi nìn máń kunimbɔtidii ki dóò kii Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nì Peeriisi yab bɔtiibi Siirusi nì Daariyusi nì Aritaseerseesi nín nìn yóoǹ mara yii bí ŋá puee. 15Ubɔti Daariyusi beel dibinluluutiil, uŋmal un bi yíì Adaaree wiiŋyi ita dal ní bi máń kunimbɔtidii ki dóò. 16Isirayeel yab nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab nì bin kɔkɔ nìn nyánní kuyuŋuee nìn jíń kunimbɔtidii gbanti jiŋaaliu ki dū-ku ki sú Unimbɔti nì dipɔɔpindi. 17Bi nìn dū inajaa dilaataal nì ipijaa alaataa ali nì apibil alaataa anaa ní ki ŋá saraa kunimbɔtidii jiŋaaliu gbanti poon. Bi nìn dū iŋɔjaa saalaa nì ili ki ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ pu ki nóó nì Isirayeel naakɔti saalaa nì tilee nyɔkɔm. 18Bi nìn kāaǹ bisaraaŋaliibi ki nóó nì bi-tuuŋŋi nín sá puee, ní ki yākatì Leefii yab akiti akiti ki nóó nì bi-tuuŋŋi nín sá puee bí nīn tūǹ Unimbɔti tundi Jeerusaleem, kii an nín ŋmàn̄ pu Mooyiisi marab gbɔŋkunee.
Juuda yab jíń Dilákatil jiŋaaliu
19Bin nìn nyánní kuyuŋu ki bāańee nìn jíń Dilákatil jiŋaaliu uŋmapeepeekaa poon ŋwiin ŋubɔ kpá saalku dal ní. 20Bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab nín nìn kpáfì dicilpu ki ŋá akoobil ŋin bi ŋáań kí nyā tijɔkɔndinee, bi-kɔkɔ nìn bí circir dee. An pu ní bi nìn lāntì Dilákatil jiŋaaliu pibiliŋ ki tīī bin kɔkɔ nìn nyánní kuyuŋuee, nì bi-nabiyaamu bisaraaŋaliibi nì bíǹ bi-ba mun. 21Isirayeel yab bin nìn nyánní kuyuŋuee nì bin kɔkɔ nìn bí kitiŋin niin ní ki dū bin kaa nyí Unimbɔtee jɔkɔntuuŋŋi ki fée nìn kpáfì ki jíń Dilákatil jiŋaaliu. Binib gbantee nìn bí ki nyàab̀ ti-Dindaan Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu. 22Míǹ boonee ní bi jíń jiŋaal un bi ŋmóò kpɔnɔb bin kaa cáá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee iwiin iluli nì dipɔɔpindi. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan nìn yāntì dipɔɔpindi gbí-bi u nín kpántì Asuur yab bɔtiu pɔbil ki yāntì bi ká diyimɔɔl u-ceeyee pu. An nìn tīī-bi kunyannyaau bi ŋúń ki túń Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu diiku mātam tuuŋŋi.

english_text:
Ezra Comes to Jerusalem
1-6Much later, when Artaxerxes was king of Persia, Ezra came to Jerusalem from Babylonia. Ezra was the son of Seraiah and the grandson of Azariah. His other ancestors were Hilkiah, Shallum, Zadok, Ahitub, Amariah, Azariah, Meraioth, Zerahiah, Uzzi, Bukki, Abishua, Phinehas, Eleazar, and Aaron, the high priest.
Ezra was an expert in the Law that the Lord God of Israel had given to Moses, and the Lord made sure that the king gave Ezra everything he asked for.
7Other Jews, including priests, Levites, musicians, the temple guards, and servants, came to Jerusalem with Ezra. This happened during the seventh year that Artaxerxes was king.
8-9God helped Ezra, and he arrived in Jerusalem on the first day of the fifth month of that seventh year, after leaving Babylonia on the first day of the first month. 10Ezra had spent his entire life studying and obeying the Law of the Lord and teaching it to others.
Artaxerxes Gives a Letter to Ezra
11Ezra was a priest and an expert in the laws and commands that the Lord had given to Israel. One day King Artaxerxes gave Ezra a letter which said:
12 Greetings from the great King Artaxerxes to Ezra the priest and expert in the teachings of the God of heaven.
13-14Any of the people of Israel or their priests or Levites in my kingdom may go with you to Jerusalem if they want to. My seven advisors and I agree that you may go to Jerusalem and Judah to find out if the laws of your God are being obeyed.
15When you go, take the silver and gold that I and my advisors are freely giving to the God of Israel, whose temple is in Jerusalem. 16Take the silver and gold that you collect from everywhere in Babylonia. Also take the gifts that your own people and priests have so willingly contributed for the temple of your God in Jerusalem.
17Use the money carefully to buy the best bulls, rams, lambs, grain, and wine. Then sacrifice them on the altar at God's temple in Jerusalem. 18If any silver or gold is left, you and your people may use it for whatever pleases your God. 19Give your God the other articles that have been contributed for use in his temple. 20If you need to get anything else for the temple, you may have the money you need from the royal treasury.
21Ezra, you are a priest and an expert in the laws of the God of heaven, and I order all treasurers in Western Province to do their very best to help you. 22They will be allowed to give as much as 3.4 tons of silver, 10 tons of wheat, 2,000 liters of wine, 2,000 liters of olive oil, and all the salt you need.
23They must provide whatever the God of heaven demands for his temple, so that he won't be angry with me and with the kings who rule after me. 24We want you to know that no priests, Levites, musicians, guards, temple servants, or any other temple workers will have to pay any kind of taxes.
25Ezra, use the wisdom God has given you and choose officials and leaders to govern the people of Western Province. These leaders should know God's laws and have them taught to anyone who doesn't know them. 26Everyone who fails to obey God's Law or the king's law will be punished without pity. They will either be executed or put in prison or forced to leave their country, or have all they own taken away.
Ezra Praises God
27Because King Artaxerxes was so kind, Ezra said:
Praise the Lord God of our ancestors! He made sure that the king honored the Lord's temple in Jerusalem. 28God has told the king, his advisors, and his powerful officials to treat me with kindness. The Lord God has helped me, and I have been able to bring many Jewish leaders back to Jerusalem.
translation_text:
Usaraaŋakpil Eesiraasi bɔti
1Míǹ jítì boon, Peeriisi yab bɔtiu Aritaseerseesi beel yuntiŋuee, uninja ubɔ nìn bí bi yíì-u Eesiraasi. U-baa di nìn sá Seeraya ní u-naanjab nìn sá Asariya nì Ilikiya nì 2Saaluum nì Sadooki nì Ayiituub nì 3Amariya nì Asariya nì Meerayooti nì 4Seeraya nì Usii nì Bukii nì 5Abiisuwa nì Piinaasi nì usaraaŋakpil Aarɔn jipɔɔn Eeleeyasaar. 6Eesiraasi gbanti nìn nyánní Babiloon ní. U nìn sá unil un nyí Mooyiisi marab bin ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nìn tīī u-nibul Isirayeel yabee tiŋan.
