Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nìn yú u-boon, an puee tin u yaa nìn bālifì ubɔtee, u nìn tìì-u ní. 7Ubɔti Aritaseerseesi beel dibinluluútiil poon ní Isirayeel yab kansikin bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab nì biwambɔɔliibi nì bipunyɔɔciitiliibi nì bin bí kunimbɔtidiin ki tútúǹ atuunee biba nìn yíkì ki nín gítí Jeerusaleem. 8Bi nì Eesiraasi di nìn nóó ki dɔ́miń Jeerusaleem ubɔti beel dibinluluútiil uŋmaŋmooŋmooti poon. 9U nìn bɔ́ntì ki yíkìń Babiloon uŋmapeepeekaa wimpeekaaŋu dal, ní ki dāa dūu bāań Jeerusaleem uŋmaŋmooŋmooti wimpeekaaŋu dal, kun puee u-Nimbɔtiu nìn yú u-boon. 10Di sá yii Eesiraasi nìn dū u-pɔbil kɔkɔ ki tīī ti-Dindaan marau bīfitam. U nìn ŋáań marabee nín lī yii bí ŋá puee, ní ki nìn cáá mara gbanti bɔkpaaŋi nì u-koobiliŋ ki dàkà Isirayeel yab.
Atuun ŋin ubɔti Aritaseerseesi tīī Eesiraasee
11Kugbɔŋu kun ubɔti Aritaseerseesi nìn ŋmàn̄ ki tīī Eesiraasi un sá usaraaŋal ki sá un nyí ti-Dindaan marab nì u-koobiliŋ tiŋan pu ki cáa dàkà Isirayeel yabee sèé:
12«Man Aritaseerseesi, bibɔtiibi kɔkɔ bɔtiu di ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu nee ki tīī sii usaraaŋal Eesiraasi un nyí Unimbɔti un bí yilpuee marabee.
13«M yóoǹ mara yii m-beel jaaŋŋi kɔkɔnee, bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab nì Isirayeel yab bin kíǹee kɔkɔ kansikin bin yaa là kí cù Jeerusaleemee ń nóó-si kí cù. 14Man ubɔti nì m-saŋkiliibi bilulee di tú-si á cù Jeerusaleem nì Juuda timmu mun kíǹee poon kí cɔ̄ŋkì kí kpèè yii binib nóó a-Nimbɔtiu marab bin kā a-ŋaanee mana. 15Sii ní man nì m-saŋkiliibi tú á cáá animbil nì sindaariya un ti ŋá saraa kí tīī Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiuee kí cùnnì Jeerusaleem laakin Unimbɔti kɔŋkooŋŋu bée. 16Á kpáaǹ animbil nì sindaariya nì tin kɔkɔ Babiloon timmu kɔkɔ yab tɔ́ ki tīī-see, nì Unimbɔti nibul nì bisaraaŋaliibi nín ŋá nlammɔntiim saraabi bin kí tūtuǹ bi-Nimbɔtiu diiku kun bí Jeerusaleemee tuuŋŋee. 17Á tin dū animbil ŋin bi tɔ́ ki tīī-see kí dā inajaa nì ipijaa nì apibil nì tin kɔkɔ bi cáa ŋáań saraayee nì ndaam min bi làá fée, kí dūú ŋá saraabi ni-Nimbɔtiu diiku saraafaŋŋu pu Jeerusaleem. 18Sii nì a-nabiyaamu ń kpèè kí dū animbil nì Sindaariya un kíǹee kí ŋá min ŋān̄ ni-ceeyee kí nóó ni-Nimbɔtiu nín là puee. 19Tiwan tin bi tīī-si bí nīn cáa tūǹ kunimbɔtidii poon tuuŋŋee, á cáá-tì kí yóoń Jeerusaleem Nimbɔtiu nimbiin. 20Á dāá lēē lampoo nimbiliŋ ŋin ntimu pà ki tìì ubɔtee kí pà atuun ŋin kíǹ ki sá á púntí kí tɔ̄ a-Nimbɔtiu Diikunee.
21«Man ubɔti Aritaseerseesi, m yóoǹ mara ntimu mun bí Eefiraati ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki púee nimbiŋubiliibi yii usaraaŋal Eesiraasi un dàkà Unimbɔti un bí yilpuee marabee yaa bālifì tiŋyee, bí ŋá míǹ kí tīī-u deedee. 22Bí tīī-u animbil kúti kii kiiloobi kutukub bita nì bilee kiiloobi kutukub mmuŋku nì saalaa nì ndamam liitirib kutukub binaa, nì ŋkpam liitirib kutukub binaa nì ŋyaam u yaa là puee. 23Tin kɔkɔ Unimbɔti un náań yilpuee bālifèe, ŋámaan míǹ deedee, án nín làá ŋá pu ú taa fōō diŋuul m-beel nì m-jipɔmbi puee. 24Ti gíti là ní béé yii mara kaa pú yii bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab nì bilaŋgaaliibi nì bipunyɔɔciitiliibi nì bitɔntɔnliibi nì bin tūǹ kunimbɔtidii poon atuunee ń pà lampoo nì patantib nì animbil ŋin bisaŋkinliibi pèe.
25«An yaa kíǹ sii Eesiraasee, á dū iciin in Unimbɔti marau un kā a-ŋaanee dàkèe kí kàan̄ bibɔsoonliibi bí dū ibaamɔn kí sòoǹ ntimu mun bí Eefiraati ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki púee nib bin kɔkɔ nyí a-Nimbɔtiu marabee bɔti, ní kí dàkà bin kaa nyí marabee bí béé-bi. 26Un sá kamaa kaa tɔ́ a-Nimbɔtiu marau kaa tɔ́ ubɔti marauee, bí dáaĺ udaan tafal. An yaa sá bí kpɔ̀-uee, bí kpɔ̀-u. An yaa sá bí jà-u kí nyāntí kitiŋ puee, bí jà-u. An yaa sá bí gíí-u dipɔndee, bí gíí-u, an yaa tí sá bí pìin̄-u sarkee, bí pìin̄-u.»
Eesiraasi jáam̀ Unimbɔti
27«Ti jáam̀ ti-Dindaan ti-naanjab Nimbɔtiu un gbēē ubɔti pɔbil ki yāntì u tīī ti-Dindaan Diiku kun bí Jeerusaleemee tinyoolee. 28Ubɔti nì u-saŋkinliibi nì u-kàliŋkpilib nimbiin ní ti-Dindaan dàkā-mi u-ŋanti yii u bí m-cee. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan m-Nimbɔtiu ŋal nìn pá m-pu ní m ŋúń ki kpáfì Isirayeel yab kpilib biba ní man nì bi yíkìń Babiloon.»

Binib bin nì Eesiraasi nìn nyánní kuyuŋuee
1Ubɔti Aritaseerseesi beel yuntiŋu bin nìn nóoń-mi ti yíkìń Babiloonee dicaŋŋi kpilib nì bi nín pēē pēē mmaal puee sèé.
2Geersɔm sá Fineeyaasi maaliŋun yab kpiliu
ní Daniyeel sá Itamaar maaliŋun yab kpiliu,
ní Atuusi sá Daafiidi maaliŋun yab kpiliu,
3ní Seekaniya jipɔmbi kansikin ubɔ,
ní Seekariya sá Pareeyoosi maaliŋun yab kpiliu. U-nib nìn nyáń bininjab dilaataal nì imuŋku ili nì saalaa,
4ní Seeraya jipɔɔn Eeliyooweenayi sá Pati-Moowaab maaliŋun kpiliu. U-nib nìn nyáń bininjab alaataa ali,
5ní Yasiyeel jipɔɔn Seekaniya sá Saatuu maaliŋun yab kpiliu. U-nib nìn nyáń bininjab alaataa ata,
6ní Joonatan jipɔɔn Eebeedi sá Adiini maaliŋun yab kpiliu. U-nib nìn nyáń bininjab imuŋku ili nì saalaa,
7ní Ataliya jipɔɔn Yeesaya sá Eelaam maaliŋun yab kpiliu. U-nib nìn nyáń bininjab imuŋku ita nì saalaa,
8ní Miikayeel jipɔɔn Seebadiya sá Seefatiya maaliŋun yab kpiliu. U-nib nìn nyáń bininjab imuŋku inaa,
9ní Yeeyiyeel jipɔɔn Oobadiya sá Joowaab maaliŋun yab kpiliu. U-nib nìn nyáń bininjab alaataa ali nì binib bili kpá mmuŋku,
10ní Yoosfiya jipɔɔn Seeloomiiti sá Banii maaliŋun yab kpiliu. U-nib nìn nyáń bininjab dilaataal nì imuŋku ita,
11ní Beebaayi jipɔɔn Seekariya sá Beebaayi maaliŋun yab kpiliu. U-nib nìn nyáń bininjab mmuŋku nì binii.
12Akatan jipɔɔn Yoowanan sá Asigaadi maaliŋun yab kpiliu. U-nib nìn nyáń bininjab dilaataal nì saalaa.
13Eeliifeeleeti nì Yeeyiyeel nì Seemaya sá Adooniikam maaliŋun yab ŋwaamu. Bi-nib nìn nyáń bininjab imuŋku ita,
14ní Utayii nì Sakuur sá Biigifayi maaliŋun yab kpilib. Bi-nib nìn nyáń bininjab imuŋku ita nì saalaa.
Eesiraasi yíkìi ki nín cá Jeerusaleem
15Niinee ní m yíiń binib gbanti ki kpáfì mbun ŋun pùub̀ ki cá Aafa watil púee. Ti nìn kāl̀ niin iwiin ita. M nìn dáań ki ká yii bisaraaŋaliibi dikitil gbanti poon, Leefii yab báà ubɔ nìn kpá. 16Niinee ní m yíiń adican kpilib Eeliyeeseer nì Ariyeel nì Seemaya nì Eelnatan nì Yariib nì Eelnatan nì Naatan nì Seekariya nì Meesulam nì Yooyariib nì Eelnatan bimaradakaliibi bilee. 17M nìn tú-bi Kasfiya timbiliiki bɔtiu Idoo cee, ní ki tùkū-bi bi nín làá tin sòoǹ tin Idoo nì u-nabiyaamu bin bí Kasfiya tiŋkin ki sá kunimbɔtidii poon tɔntɔnliibee pu bí tīiń-ti bitɔntɔnliibi bí nīn bí ti-Nimbɔtiu diiku poon ki tūǹ atuunee. 18Kii ti-Nimbɔtiu ŋal nín nìn wúń ti-pu puee, bi nìn cáań-ti uninja ubɔ bi yíì-u Seereebiya. U nìn cáá dinyil ní ki nìn sá Malii maaliŋun, Jaakɔb jipɔɔn Leefii naakookun, u nì u-nabiyaamu nì u-jipɔmbi saalku nì bita. 19Bi nìn gíti cáań Meerarii maaliŋun yab Asabiya nì u-nabiki Yeesaya nì bi-jipɔmbi. Bi nìn kpáfì binib mmuŋku. 20Bitɔntɔnliibi bin Daafiidi nì u-kàliŋkpilib nìn lēē bí nīn tútúǹ Leefii yab atuun kunimbɔtidiinee kansikinee, bi nìn cáań binib alaataa ali nì mmuŋku. Bi nìn yíiń bi-kɔkɔ yiŋŋi ní ki lēē-bi.
21Aafa buŋŋu caŋin niin ní m lēē yii tí bóob́ kinyɔkɔ kí sìntī ti-ba taapu ti-Nimbɔtiu nimbiin kí mèè-u ú pɔ̄-ti diyimɔɔl tí còom̀ disaŋkimmɔntiil ti nì ti-biyaamu nì tin kɔkɔ ti cááyee. 22An nìn cáá-mi icoo ḿ bàlifì ubɔti yii ú tīī-ti bijanjaliibi nì bitanjakaliibi bí céeǹ-ti ti-nannanliibi ń taa tin páb́-ti nsanni. Di sá yii ti nìn tùkū-u yii: «Ti-Nimbɔtiu ŋal wúń bin kɔkɔ yú nì u deedeeyee pu, ama ní u fòol̄ diŋuul tikpil bin dū-u ki fée pu.» 23An pu ní ti bóob́ kinyɔkɔ ki mēē ti-Nimbɔtiu ú yūĺ ti-boon, ní u fōō ti-wimmeem.
24Míǹ boonee ní m lēē bisaraaŋaliibi saalaa nì bili, ní ki dū Seereebiya nì Asabiya nì bi-nabiyaamu saalaa mun ki kútì bi-pu. 25M nìn ŋmāntì animbil kúti nì sindaariya nì tigaajawan tin ubɔti nì u-saŋkiliibi nì u-kàliŋkpilib nì Isirayeel yab bin kɔkɔ bí Babiloon niinee nìn tɔ́ bí cáań kí tɔ̄ Unimbɔti diiku tuuŋŋee ki tīī-bi. 26M nìn ŋmāntì animbil kúti tɔɔnib mmuŋku, animbil kúti wanti tɔɔnib bita, nì sindaariya tɔɔnib bita, 27nì sindaariya sampati mmuŋku, ti-nyampooku sá sindaariya jitɔmbi kutuku, nì tasa sampeemu mun jìl̀ ki ŋān̄ ki pɔ̄ɔ̄ kudaau kii sindaariyee muli ki tīī-bi. 28M nìn bí-bi yii: «Ni sá binib bin dū bi-ba ki sú ti-Dindaanee ní. Tiwan nee mun sá tin bi dūu súee ní. Animbil nì sindaariya nee sá nlammɔntiim saraau ní bi ŋá ki tīī ni-baabi Nimbɔtiu. 29Ní kpèè tiwan gbanti mmɔntiim, kí ŋúb́-tì tiŋan kí cáá-tì kí bànnì Jeerusaleem bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab nì Isirayeel dicaŋŋi kpilib nimbiin kunimbɔtidii dibiyaamun.»
30Niinee ní bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yabee yōoǹ sindaariya nì animbil kúti nì tigaajawan tin bi ŋmāntì ki tīī-bee ki cáa cūnnì Jeerusaleem ki yóoǹ ti-Nimbɔtiu diikun.
Eesiraasi nì u-yab bàn̄ Jeerusaleem
31Ti nìn yíkì uŋmapeepeekaa poon iwiin saalaa nì ili dal Aafa buŋŋu caŋin ki nín cá Jeerusaleem. Ti-Nimbɔtiu nìn bīiǹ ti-saŋkindi gbanti pu, binannanliibi kaa táká-taaa, biyipɔɔdambi mun kaa kíntì-ti nsanni ki fúkúl̀-ti. 32Ti nìn bàn̄ Jeerusaleemee ní ki dū iwiin ita ki kāl̀ ki ŋūŋfì. 33Ŋwinnanaatee ní ti ŋmāntì animbil kúti nì sindaariya nì tigaajawanee ti-Nimbɔtiu diikun ki dūu tīī usaraaŋal Uriya jipɔɔn Meereemooti. U nì Piinaasi jipɔɔn Eeleeyasaar nì Leefii yab Joosuwa jipɔɔn Yoosabaadi nì Binuyii jipɔɔn Noowadiya di nìn bí. 34Bi nìn kàan̄ tiwan gbanti kɔkɔ ní ki ŋmāntì-tì ní ki ŋmàn̄ ti-nyiŋfiŋu nín nyáń puee ki ŋá kugbɔŋun niin niin.
35Bin nìn nyánní kuyuŋu ki fātìi gítìńee nìn ŋá bisaraawɔkaabi samaa kɔkɔ yil pu ki tīī Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu. Bi nìn dū inajaa saalaa nì ili nì ipijaa inaa kpá dilaataal nì apibil ata kpá imuŋku inaa ní ki ŋá saraawɔkaa gbanti, ní ki dū iŋɔjaa saalaa nì ili ki ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau. Bi nìn dū tiwaŋkuti gbanti kɔkɔ ki wùn̄ ŋŋmi ki tīī ti-Dindaan. 36Míǹ boonee ní bi dū kugbɔŋu kun ubɔtikpaan ŋmàn̄née ki tīī ubɔti kàliŋkpilib nì gɔminab bin bí Eefiraati mɔɔl ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú timmunee, ní bi-kɔkɔ tútúǹ Isirayeel yab bi máń Unimbɔti diiku.

english_text:
Ezra Condemns Mixed Marriages
1Later the Jewish leaders came to me and said:
Many Israelites, including priests and Levites, are living just like the people around them. They are even guilty of some of the horrible sins of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, the Ammonites, the Moabites, the Egyptians, and the Amorites.
2Some Israelite men have married foreign women and have let their sons do the same thing. Our own officials and leaders were the first to commit this disgusting sin, and now God's holy people are mixed with foreigners.
3This news made me so angry that I ripped my clothes and tore hair from my head and beard. Then I just sat in shock 4until the time for the evening sacrifice. Many of our people were greatly concerned and gathered around me, because the God of Israel had warned us to stay away from foreigners.
Ezra's Prayer
5At the time of the evening sacrifice, I was still sitting there in sorrow with my clothes all torn. So I got down on my knees, then lifted my arms, 6and prayed:
I am much too ashamed to face you, Lord God. Our sins and our guilt have swept over us like a flood that reaches up to the heavens. 7Since the time of our ancestors, all of us have sinned. That's why we, our kings, and our priests have often been defeated by other kings. They have killed some of us and made slaves of others; they have taken our possessions and made us ashamed, just as we are today.
8But for now, Lord God, you have shown great kindness to us. You made us truly happy by letting some of us settle in this sacred place and by helping us in our time of slavery. 9We are slaves, but you have never turned your back on us. You love us, and because of you, the kings of Persia have helped us. It's as though you have given us new life! You let us rebuild your temple and live safely in Judah and Jerusalem.
10Our God, what can we say now? Even after all this, we have disobeyed the commands 11that were given to us by your servants the prophets. They said the land you are giving us is full of sinful and wicked people, who never stop doing disgusting things. 12 And we were warned not to let our daughters and sons marry their sons and daughters.
Your prophets also told us never to help those foreigners or even let them live in peace. You wanted us to become strong and to enjoy the good things in the land, then someday to leave it to our children forever.
13You punished us because of our terrible sins. But you did not punish us nearly as much as we deserve, and you have brought some of us back home. 14Why should we disobey your commands again by letting our sons and daughters marry these foreigners who do such disgusting things? That would make you angry enough to destroy us all! 15Lord God of Israel, you have been more than fair by letting a few of us survive. But once again, our sins have made us ashamed to face you.
translation_text:
Juuda yab cáá binicannimpoobi
1Tíǹ jítì boonee ní Isirayeel kpilib biba dɔ́miń ki tùkū-mi yii: «Isirayeel nibul nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab kaa gāntì bi-ba nì kitiŋ nee pu nibuliŋ ŋin kíǹee. Bi mun bí ki ŋáań ntimbiil tuuŋŋi kii Kanaan yab nì Eeti yab nì Peeriisi yab nì Jeebusi yab nì Amɔn yab nì Moowaab yab nì Eejipiti yab nì Amɔɔr yab nín ŋáań puee ní. 2Bíǹ bi-ba cáá niin tiŋkin binimpoobi, ní ki cáá ki tīī bi-jipɔmbi mun ní dinibul din bí circiree dūu ŋmālim̀ niin tiŋki nibin. Adican kpilib nì abɔtibil di péé péé ki kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi gbantin.»
3M nín gbìl̄ an bɔtee ní m dáaĺ ki cátì tiwan tin m pēēyee, ní ki dáaĺ ki fùkū m-yikpiti nì m-nyimpul, ní ki kíǹ ki kā nì kunimbaau. 4Bin kɔkɔ nìn tɔ́ Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu bɔtee nín gbìl̄ atuŋkpiti ŋin bin nyánní kuyuŋuee ŋée, ní bi kóoǹní ki dɔ́miń ki kpáfì m-cee. Ama mamee, m nìn pée kā nì kunimbaau míǹ ní áli kujoou saraau yuntiŋu.
Eesiraasi mēē ki tīī Juuda yab bin yīntèe
5Kujoou saraau yuntiŋu ní m nyáń m-nimbaaku poon. M nìn gbíntìi pēē m-wanti tin m nìn dáaĺ ki cátèe, ní ki gbāaǹ m-tabiŋyiliŋ pu, ní ki yōoǹ m-ŋalii ki túĺ ti-Dindaan m-Nimbɔtiu watil pú. 6M nìn mēē-u yii: «M-Nimbɔtiu, icoo cúú-mi ní m bākatì, maa ŋūǹ kí wáaǹ kí kpèè sii m-Nimbɔtiu watil pú gba. Di sá ti-kpitii wíiǹ ki lákatì ti-yil pu ní ti-yìntitam kpúkú ki tin sāā kutagbɔŋu. 7Kí yòon̄ ti-naanjab yuntiŋu kí dāá sāā díǹ nee, ti yīntiǹ-si ŋkpitim pu. Ti-kpitii puee a dū timbi nì ti-bɔtiibi nì ti-saraaŋaliibi ki líiǹ kitiŋ pu bɔtiibi nì kujaau, ki yāntì bi cúú-ti kuyuŋu ki fúkúl̀-ti ki kɔ́ǹ-ti icoo, kii an nín bí-ti díǹ pu nan ní. 8Ama kɔŋkɔnnee, ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu, a dàkā-ti kulaŋŋaŋfitiiu ki yāntì ti-kansikin biba dáá gbíntìi bí dimaŋfalin ki gítìń ki kāl̀ a-circir tiŋkin. Ti-Nimbɔtiu, a ŋá míǹ ki yāntì ti-nimbiliŋ ŋāatì ní ti ká dimaŋfapɔndi ti-yuŋku poon. 9Di sá yii ti nìn sá iyumbu ní, ama ti-yuŋku gbanti poonee, sii ti-Nimbɔtiu kaa nìn dū-ti ki fá. A yāntì Peeriisi yab bɔtiibi dàkā-ti kulaŋŋaŋfitiiu. A tīī-ti dimaŋfal ti ŋúń ki fātìi máń sii ti-Nimbɔtiu diiku, ní ki ŋáŋkì ku-digbuŋŋi ní ki ŋúń ki máń agun ki tú Jeerusaleem nì Juuda timmu mun kíǹee.
10«Kɔŋkɔnnee ti-Nimbɔtiu, tilati ní ti cáá kí lì tin bāań nee pu? Di sá yii ti fātì ti-boon ki tīī a-marab 11bin ní a nìn dī a-tɔntɔnliibi bibɔnaatiliibi pu ki tīī-tee. A nìn kpáafì-ti ki lī yii: <Kitiŋ kin ni làá cùú fōō kí nīn kóò nee kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi binib bin kóò ki-nee jɔkɔntuuŋŋi pu. Di sá yii kí yòon̄ laakin kitiŋ nee kífée kí cáá kúntí ki-gbeennyɔkɔee, an sá ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin bi tūǹee ŋma ní bi dūu gbéeǹ-kì. 12An puee ní taa dū ni-bisalib kí tīī bi-jipɔmbi ticati, kí taa cáá bi-bisalib kí tīī ni-jipɔmbi. Ni yaa là kí nīn cáá mpɔn kí jī kitiŋ gbanti naam, ni-biyaamu mun ń dāá yīkì kí tɔ́kɔń kí nīn pée jīǹ ki cá jaanjaanee, ní taa dī isaŋkpiti in pu bíǹ bí an bútì-bee pu, kí taa nyàab̀ bi-gbansɔŋfiŋu juti ŋwindal.> 13Tin kɔkɔ pée bāań-ti nee nyánní ti-tuŋkpitiŋ nì ikpitikpaan in ti ŋée pu ní. Óò ti-Nimbɔtiu, nì míǹ kɔkɔee, aa dáaĺ ti-tafal ki bàn̄ ti-kpitii nín sá puee nyɔkɔm, ní ki yāntì ti-nibul poon biba kíǹ kaa kpíì. 14Tinee boonee, ti bàà gíti cáá nsan kí tí kíĺ kí nīn yìntīǹ a-marab ti nì anibul ŋin ŋáań ntimbiil tuuŋŋee ń ŋá ubaanti, ti cāab̀ tɔbaaa? Aa fòol̄ ti-pu diŋuul áli kí kúntí-ti ubɔ ń taa kíń, àá ubɔ ń taa ŋmátáaa? 15Ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu, a sá deedeedaan ní. Díǹ pu nee a yāntì ti-kansikin biba kíǹ kaa kpíì. Kpèè timbi di yú a-nimbiin ti nì ti-kpitii nee, ama ubɔ kpá ki bí tin poon timbi bí nee kí ŋmā kí yūĺ a-nimbiin.»

english_text:
The Plan for Ending Mixed Marriages
1While Ezra was down on his knees in front of God's temple, praying with tears in his eyes and confessing the sins of the people of Israel, a large number of men, women, and children gathered around him and cried bitterly.
2Shecaniah son of Jehiel from the family of Elam said:
Ezra, we have disobeyed God by marrying these foreign women. But there is still hope for the people of Israel, 3if we follow your advice and the advice of others who truly respect the laws of God. We must promise God that we will divorce our foreign wives and send them away, together with their children.
4Ezra, it's up to you to do something! We will support whatever you do. So be brave!
5Ezra stood up and made the chief priests, the Levites, and everyone else in Israel swear that they would follow the advice of Shecaniah. 6Then Ezra left God's temple and went to spend the night in the living quarters of Jehohanan son of Eliashib. He felt sorry because of what the people had done, and he did not eat or drink a thing.
7-8The officials and leaders sent a message to all who had returned from Babylonia and were now living in Jerusalem and Judah. This message told them to meet in Jerusalem within three days, or else they would lose everything they owned and would no longer be considered part of the people that had returned from Babylonia.
9Three days later, on the twentieth day of the ninth month, everyone from Judah and Benjamin came to Jerusalem and sat in the temple courtyard. It was a serious meeting, and they sat there, trembling in the rain.
10Ezra the priest stood up and said:
You have broken God's Law by marrying foreign women, and you have made the whole nation guilty! 11Now you must confess your sins to the Lord God of your ancestors and obey him. Divorce your foreign wives and don't have anything to do with the rest of the foreigners who live around here.
12Everyone in the crowd shouted:
You're right! We will do what you say. 13But there are so many of us, and we can't just stay out here in this downpour. A lot of us have sinned by marrying foreign women, and the matter can't be settled in only a day or two.
14Why can't our officials stay on in Jerusalem and take care of this for us? Let everyone who has sinned in this way meet here at a certain time with leaders and judges from their own towns. If we take care of this problem, God will surely stop being so terribly angry with us.
15Jonathan son of Asahel and Jahzeiah son of Tikvah were the only ones who objected, except for the two Levites, Meshullam and Shabbethai.
16Everyone else who had returned from exile agreed with the plan. So Ezra the priest chose men who were heads of the families, and he listed their names. They started looking into the matter on the first day of the tenth month, 17and they did not finish until the first day of the first month of the next year.
The Men Who Had Foreign Wives
18-19Here is a list of the priests who had agreed to divorce their foreign wives and to sacrifice a ram as a sin offering:
Maaseiah, Eliezer, Jarib, and Gedaliah from the family of Joshua son of Jozadak and his brothers; 20Hanani and Zebadiah from the family of Immer; 21Maaseiah, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel, and Uzziah from the family of Harim; 22Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabad, and Elasah from the family of Pashhur.
23Those Levites who had foreign wives were: Jozabad, Shimei, Kelaiah (also known as Kelita), Pethahiah, Judah, and Eliezer.
24Eliashib, the musician, had a foreign wife.
These temple guards had foreign wives:
Shallum, Telem, and Uri.
25Here is a list of the others from Israel who had foreign wives:
Ramiah, Izziah, Malchijah, Mijamin, Eleazar, Hashabiah, and Benaiah from the family of Parosh;
26Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Abdi, Jeremoth, and Elijah from the family of Elam;
27Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, Zabad, and Aziza from the family of Zattu;
28Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, and Athlai from the family of Bebai;
29Meshullam, Malluch, Adaiah, Jashub, Sheal, and Jeremoth from the family of Bani;
30Adna, Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel, Binnui, and Manasseh from the family of Pahath Moab;
31-32Eliezer, Isshijah, Malchijah, Shemaiah, Shimeon, Benjamin, Malluch, and Shemariah from the family of Harim;
33Mattenai, Mattattah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, and Shimei from the family of Hashum;
34-37Maadai, Amram, Uel, Benaiah, Bedeiah, Cheluhi, Vaniah, Meremoth, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Mattenai, and Jaasu from the family of Bani;
38-42Shimei, Shelemiah, Nathan, Adaiah, Machnadebai, Shashai, Sharai, Azarel, Shelemiah, Shemariah, Shallum, Amariah, and Joseph from the family of Binnui;
43Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Jaddai, Joel, and Benaiah from the family of Nebo.
44These men divorced their foreign wives, then sent them and their children away.
translation_text:
Juuda yab jìn̄ binicannimpoobi bin bi cááyee
1Ŋyunti ŋun Eesiraasi gbāā ki sūǹ kunimbɔtidii nyɔkɔpu ki mèé Unimbɔti bi-kpitii pɔ̄tam puee, Isirayeel yab dinikitikpaandi, bininjab nì binimpoobi nì mbiyaamu dɔ́miń ki māntì tú-u ní ki bíi sūǹ tikpil. 2Niinee ní Yeeyiyeel jipɔɔn Seekaniya un sá Eelaam maaliŋunee bí Eesiraasi yii: «Taa yúliǹ ti-Nimbɔtiu deedee ki cáá binicannimpoobi bin sá kitiŋ nee poon nimpubiyaamuee. Ama nì míǹ kɔkɔee, dimákal diba gbíntìi dáá bí ki tīī Isirayeel yab. 3Tí lēēmaan ti-pɔbiliŋ poon kɔŋkɔnnee kí ŋá mpèé nì ti-Nimbɔtiu yii ti làá jà binicannimpoobi gbanti kɔkɔ ki kpáaǹ bi-biyaamu, kii sii ti-kpiliu nì bin kɔkɔ fàŋkí ti-Nimbɔtiu marabee nín sáŋkì-ti puee. Ti làá ŋá kí nóó nì mara. 4Yīkìm̄, kun puee sii di làá ŋāŋkì tibɔti nee. Timbi yú a-boon, ká kunyannyaau kí ŋá min máaǹee kí taa gùgufì.»
5Niinee Eesiraasi yíkì ní ki yāntì bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab nì Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ pūtì yii bi làá ŋá kii Seekaniya nín sòon̄ puee, ní bi-kɔkɔ pūtì. 6Ní Eesiraasi nyáń kunimbɔtidii cindin ki cūtìi kɔ́ Eeliyasiib jipɔɔn Yoowanan diikun ki dōoǹ, ama waa nìn jíń báà tiba kaa nìn nyùn̄ mun. Di sá yii bin nìn nyánní kuyuŋuee nín nìn ŋá ikpitikpaan iŋyee nìn sá-u kii dikpoolee ní u kā.
7Bi nìn báakì Jeerusaleem nì Juuda timmu mun kíǹee poon yii bin kɔkɔ nìn nyánní kuyuŋuee ń kpāfì Jeerusaleem. 8Adican kpilib nì abɔtibil nìn sòon̄ ki yóoǹ yii nì iwiin ita poonee, un yaa kaa dɔ́mińee, bí fōō u-wanti tin kɔkɔ u cááyee, ní kí jà úǹ u-ba kí nyāntí bin nyánní kuyuŋuee kansikin.
9Niinee ní Juuda yab nì Beenjameen yab bininjab kɔkɔ kóoǹ ki kpáfì Jeerusaleem tiŋkin iwiin ita gbanti poon. An nìn sá uŋmawawati poon iwiin mmuŋku dal ní. Binib kɔkɔ nìn kpáfì kunimbɔtidii mɔŋkiŋu tiwun jìkì tin poon bi bée pu. Kí kūtèe utaa nín bíi nì. 10Usaraaŋal Eesiraasi nìn yáatìi yúl̀ ní ki bí-bi yii: «Ni nín cáá binicannimpoobee, naa yúliǹ Unimbɔti deedee, ní ki yāntì Isirayeel yab bɔkpil gíti nyāŋkì. 11Kɔŋkɔnnee, ní tīīmaan ti-Dindaan ni-baabi Nimbɔtiu tinyool, kí ŋámaan min u lèe. Ni nì kitiŋ nee pu yab ń yàkatī tɔbin ní ní jà binicannimpoobi bin ni cááyee.»
12Bin kɔkɔ nìn kpáfì niinee nìn kíí mpɔn yii: «A cáá mbaamɔn! Án pée sá tí ŋá kii a nín lī pu nee ní. 13Ama ti wīikí ní an sá kuseeun mun. Taa ŋūǹ kí nīn yú mpaampiin pu míǹ. Kí wàatī muee taa ŋūǹ kí dū ŋwiin ŋubɔ àá ili gba kí ŋāŋkì tibɔti nee, kun puee ti-kansikin tikpil bí ki ŋá ikpiti tibɔti nee poon. 14Míǹ puee ti-kpilib ń gbíntí doo samaa kɔkɔ yil pu. Bí yóoń bin kɔkɔ cáá binicannimpoobee iyunti ní báà ŋma ń nīn dòoń ŋyunti ŋun bi yóoǹ-uee, u nì u-tiŋki kpilib nì ki-bɔsoonliibi, ní bí kpèè tibɔti gbanti kí tin sāā ŋyunti ŋun ní Unimbɔti ŋuul làá sɔ̀ŋkì timbi puee.»
15Asayeel jipɔɔn Joonatan nì Tiisfa jipɔɔn Yasiya baba di kaa nìn kíí ki tɔ́kɔǹ nlandɔkɔ ŋun bi cáańee pu. Meesulam nì uleefiija Sabeetayi mun nìn yú bi-boon. 16Ama Isirayeel yab bin nìn nyánní kuyuŋuee nìn fōō an bɔtee ki làá ŋá míǹ. Usaraaŋal Eesiraasi nìn sāā kudicaŋu kamaa poonee bininjab kansikin ubɔ diŋambil, ki lēē-u ú nīn sá kudicaŋu kpiliu. An nibee nìn kpáfì uŋmaliliiti wimpeekaaŋu dal ki kíĺ kí kpèè tibɔti gbanti. 17Bi dāa ŋáŋkì bininjab bin kɔkɔ cáá binicannimpoobee bɔti ki dóò dibindi poon uŋmapeepeekaa wimpeepeekaaŋu dal ní.
Bininjab bin nìn ŋá ikpitee yiŋŋi
18Bisaraaŋaliibi kansikin bin nìn cáá binicannimpoobee yiŋŋi sɔ̀.
Yoosadaaki jipɔɔn Joosuwa maaliŋun yab nì bi-nabiyaamu kansikinee, Maseeyawuu nì Eeliyeeseer nì Yaariiba nì Geedaliya. 19Bi nìn pūtì yii bi làá jà bi-nimpoobi ní kí dū upìja ki ŋá dibɔkpil saraau.
20Imeer maaliŋun yab kansikinee, Ananii nì Seebadiya.
21Ariim maaliŋun yab kansikinee, Maseeyawuu nì Eeliya nì Seemaya nì Yeeyiyeel nì Usiyasi.
22Pasuur maaliŋun yab kansikinee, Eeliyooweenayi nì Maseeyawuu nì Isimaayeel nì Neetaneeyeel nì Yoosabaadi nì Eeleeyasa.
23Bi-kansikinee bin sá Leefii naakookun yabee di sá Yoosabaadi nì Simeeyii nì Keedaya, (bi gíti yíì-u yii Keeliita) nì Peetayia nì Yeewuda nì Eeliyeeseer.
24Biwambɔɔliibi kansikinee, Eeliyasiib. Bipunyɔɔciitiliibi kansikinee, Saaluum nì Teeleem nì Uurii.
25Isirayeel yab bin kíǹee kansikinee,
Pareeyoosi maaliŋun yab di sá Ramiya nì Yiisiya nì Maalkiya nì Miiniyaamiini nì Eeleeyasaar nì Maalkiya nì Beenaya.
26Eelaam maaliŋun yab di sá Mataniya nì Seekariya nì Yeeyiyeel nì Abidii nì Yeereemooti nì Eeliya.
27Satu maaliŋun yab di sá Eeliyooweenayi nì Eeliyasiib nì Mataniya nì Yeereemooti nì Sabaadi nì Asiisa.
28Beebaayi maaliŋun yab di sá Yoowanan nì Ananiya nì Sabaayi nì Atilayi.
29Banii maaliŋun yab di sá Meesulam nì Maluuki nì Adaaya nì Akuub nì Seeyal nì Yeereemooti.
30Paati-Moowaab maaliŋun yab di sá Adina nì Keelaal nì Beenaya nì Maseeyawuu nì Mataniya nì Beesaleel nì Binuyii nì Manasee.
31Ariim maaliŋun yab di sá Eeliyeeseer nì Yisiya nì Maalkiya nì Seemaya nì Simeeyɔn,
32nì Beenjameen nì Maluuki nì Seemariya.
33Asuum maaliŋun yab di sá Mateenayi nì Mataata nì Sabaadi nì Eeliifeeleeti nì Yeereemayi nì Manasee nì Simeeyii.
34Banii maaliŋun yab di sá Maadayi nì Amiiraam nì Uyeel 35nì Beenaya nì Beediya nì Keeluyii 36nì Faniya nì Meereemooti nì Eeliyasiib 37nì Mataniya nì Mateenayi nì Yaasayi 38nì Banii nì Binuyii nì Simeeyii 39nì Seeleemiya nì Naatan nì Adaaya 40nì Makinaadibayi nì Saasayi nì Saarayi 41nì Asareeyeel nì Seeleemiyawuu nì Seemariya 42nì Saaluum nì Amariya nì Jooseefi.
43Neeboo maaliŋun yab di sá Yiyeel nì Matitiya nì Sabaadi nì Seebina nì Yadidayi nì Jooweel nì Beenaya.
44Bininjab gbanti kɔkɔ di nìn cáá binicannimpoobi, ní bi-kansikin tikpil nìn màl̄ mbiyaamu.

english_text:
Nehemiah's Prayer
1I am Nehemiah son of Hacaliah, and in this book I tell what I have done.
During the month of Chislev in the twentieth year that Artaxerxes ruled Persia, I was in his fortress city of Susa, 2when my brother Hanani came with some men from Judah. So I asked them about the Jews who had escaped from being captives in Babylonia. I also asked them about the city of Jerusalem.
3They told me, “Those captives who have come back are having all kinds of troubles. They are terribly disgraced, Jerusalem's walls are broken down, and its gates have been burned.”
4When I heard this, I sat down on the ground and cried. Then for several days, I mourned; I went without eating to show my sorrow, and I prayed:
5 Lord God of heaven, you are great and fearsome. And you faithfully keep your promises to everyone who loves you and obeys your commands. 6I am your servant, so please have mercy on me and answer the prayer that I make day and night for these people of Israel who serve you. I, my family, and the rest of your people have sinned 7by choosing to disobey you and the laws and teachings you gave to your servant Moses.
8 Please remember the promise you made to Moses. You told him that if we were unfaithful, you would scatter us among foreign nations. 9 But you also said that no matter how far away we were, we could turn to you and start obeying your laws. Then you would bring us back to the place where you have chosen to be worshiped.
10Our Lord, I am praying for your servants—those you rescued by your great strength and mighty power. 11Please answer my prayer and the prayer of your other servants who gladly honor your name. When I serve the king his wine today, make him pleased with me and let him do what I ask.
translation_text:
1Tibɔti tin Akaliya jipɔɔn Neeyeemiya máafèe.
Bi máafì Neeyeemiya tin bíi jītí Jeerusaleemee
Ubɔti Aritaseerseesi nín kāl̀ dibeel abin mmuŋku, Kiisileewu ŋmaliu poonee, m nìn bí Suusi ditiŋyil, 2ní Ananii m-nabiyaamu kansikin ubɔ, u nì Juuda yab dikitil diba dɔ́miń m-cee. M nìn bālifì-bi Juuda yab bin nyáń kuyuŋu ki kùn̄ee nì Jeerusaleem pu. 3Ní bi kíí-mi yii: «Bin ŋmátì kaa kpíì kuyuŋun ní ki kóò Juuda timmunee bí falaakpaan nì icoo poon ní. Jeerusaleem gundi bátì bátì ki lítì, abun dōoǹ dōoǹ ní punuubi wùn̄ ŋŋmi.»
Neeyeemiya mēē ki tīī Juuda yab
4M nín nìn gbìl̄ an bɔtee, m nìn kāl̀ ní ki bíi sūǹ. M nìn kāl̀ kunimbaaun iwiin kupaau, ki bóob́ kinyɔkɔ, ki gbāaǹ yilpu Nimbɔtiu nimbiin ki mēē. 5M nìn mēē yii: «Too, m-Dindaan yilpu Nimbɔtiu, Unimbɔti un sá ukpaan ki sá kuwambiiuee, sii di kaa súntí jaanjaan a nín pōoǹ bin néeń-si ki ŋúb́ a-marabee pu ní ki ŋáań-bi tiŋan. 6Kpòon̄ a-tafal kí pīlifì, kí ŋúbití a-nimbiliŋ kí wāl̀ man a-tɔntɔnliu nín bí ki mèé-si iyunti nee poon ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu a-tɔntɔnliibi Isirayeel yab pu puee. M bí ki bìitī ikpiti in ní timbi Isirayeel yab ŋá-see. Ti yīntiǹ-si, tiŋman man nì m-naanjab yīntiǹ-si. 7Tiŋman ti baasii yīntiǹ-si ní, kun puee taa ŋúb́ marab nì abɔkpaa nì akoobil ŋin a nìn tīī a-tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi u dūu tīī-tee. 8Téetí anyɔɔbun ŋin a nìn dī a-tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi pu ki sòon̄ee. A nìn bí yii: <Ni yaa kaa yúliǹ-mi deedee, m làá dāá jà-ni ní yàl̄ kí kɔ́ atimbun aban. 9Ama ni yaa láa fātìi gítìń m-cee, ki ŋúb́ m-marab, ki ŋáań bi nín bí ní ŋá puee, báà ni yaa láa bíń kitiŋ gbeennyɔkɔ, m làá dāá kóoǹní-ni kí kpāfì kí yàntī ní dāan̄ laakin m làá lēē bí nīn jáaḿ-mee.> 10Ti-Dindaan, bi sá a-tɔntɔnliibi ní ki sá a-nibul din a dū a-pɔŋkpaaŋŋu nì a-kpabil ki dée. 11M-Dindaan, m gbàam̄-si, kpòon̄ a-tafal kí pīlifì man a-tɔntɔnliu nì a-tɔntɔnliibi bin an mɔ̄ǹ bí nīn fàŋkí-see wimmeem. Yàntī án kàlīǹ man a-tɔntɔnliu tiŋan díǹ ubɔti ń fōō-mi nì tiniti.» Ŋyunti gbantee, m nìn sá un tìì ubɔti ndaamee ní.

english_text:
Nehemiah Goes to Jerusalem
1During the month of Nisan in the twentieth year that Artaxerxes was king, I served him his wine, as I had done before. But this was the first time I had ever looked depressed. 2So the king said, “Why do you look so sad? You're not sick. Something must be bothering you.”
Even though I was frightened, 3 I answered, “Your Majesty, I hope you live forever! I feel sad because the city where my ancestors are buried is in ruins, and its gates have been burned down.”
4The king asked, “What do you want me to do?”
I prayed to the God who rules from heaven. 5Then I told the king, “Sir, if it's all right with you, please send me back to Judah, so that I can rebuild the city where my ancestors are buried.”
6The queen was sitting beside the king when he asked me, “How long will it take, and when will you be back?” The king agreed to let me go, and I told him when I would return.
7Then I asked, “Your Majesty, would you be willing to give me letters to the governors of the provinces west of the Euphrates River, so that I can travel safely to Judah? 8I will need timber to rebuild the gates of the fortress near the temple and more timber to construct the city wall and to build a place for me to live. And so, I would appreciate a letter to Asaph, who is in charge of the royal forest.” God was good to me, and the king did everything I asked.
9The king sent some army officers and cavalry troops along with me, and as I traveled through the Western Provinces, I gave the letters to the governors. 10But when Sanballat from Horon and Tobiah the Ammonite official heard about what had happened, they became very angry, because they didn't want anyone to help the people of Israel.
Nehemiah Inspects the Wall of Jerusalem
11Three days after arriving in Jerusalem, 12I got up during the night and left my house. I took some men with me, without telling anyone what I thought God wanted me to do for the city. The only animal I took was the donkey I rode on. 13I went through Valley Gate on the west, then south past Dragon Spring, before coming to Garbage Gate. As I rode along, I took a good look at the crumbled walls of the city and the gates that had been torn down and burned. 14On the east side of the city, I headed north to Fountain Gate and King's Pool, but then the trail became too narrow for my donkey. 15So I went down to Kidron Valley and looked at the wall from there. Then before daylight I returned to the city through Valley Gate.
16None of the city officials knew what I had in mind. And I had not even told any of the Jews—not the priests, the leaders, the officials, or any other Jews who would be helping in the work. 17But when I got back, I said to them, “Jerusalem is truly in a mess! The gates have been torn down and burned, and everything is in ruins. We must rebuild the city wall so that we can again take pride in our city.”
18Then I told them how kind God had been and what the king had said.
Immediately, they replied, “Let's start building now!” So they got everything ready.
19When Sanballat, Tobiah, and Geshem the Arab heard about our plans, they started insulting us and saying, “Just look at you! Do you plan to rebuild the walls of the city and rebel against the king?”
20I answered, “We are servants of the God who rules from heaven, and he will make our work succeed. So we will start rebuilding Jerusalem, but you have no right to any of its property, because you have had no part in its history.”
translation_text:
Ubɔti pú Neeyeemiya nsan ú cù Jeerusaleem
1Dalba Niisan ŋmaliu poon, ubɔti Aritaseerseesi nín kāl̀ dibeel abin mmuŋku poonee, ndaam nìn yú u-nimbiin ní m yōoǹ ki tīī-u. Doooo nee, maa láá pée yúl̀ u-nimbiin nì kunimbaau míǹ ki ká. 2Ubɔti nìn bālifì-mi yii: «Ba pu ní a-nimbiin bóob́ míǹ? A būǹ níii? Kunimbaau di cáá-saaa?»
Niinee ní tifaandi tiba cúú-mi tikpil. 3Ní m bí ubɔti yii: «Ubɔti ń nīn cáá mmaŋfafɔkɔn baabadal! Mana ní m-nimbiin kaa làá nīn bóob́, ŋyunti ŋun ní kitiŋ kin poon bi síb́ m-naanjabee kpántì adigbun ní ŋŋmi wùn̄ ki-punuubee?» 4Ní ubɔti bālifì-mi yii: «Ba ní a là ḿ ŋá kí tīī-si?»
Ní m mēē yilpu Nimbɔtiu, 5ní ki bí ubɔti yii: «Ti-baa ubɔti, an yaa ŋān̄ a-cee ní man a-tɔntɔnliu bɔti yaa fáatiǹ-si, á tɔ̄-mi Juuda tiŋkin laakin bi síb́ m-naanjabee, ḿ cùú fàtīí mā-kì.» 6Unimpubɔti nìn kā ki kɔ́ĺ ubɔti ní u bālifì-mi yii: «A-saŋŋu gbanti làá fōō iwiin iŋa? Ní ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu ní a làá fàtīí gítiń?»
An nìn kítì ubɔti cee ú yàntī ḿ cù, ní m yóoǹ-u ŋyunti ŋun m làá gítińee. 7Ní m gíti bí ubɔti yii: «A yaa bàà kíikí kí tīī-mi kugbɔŋu ḿ cáá tīī ntimu mun bí Eefiraati ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki púee gɔminab, bí pɔ̄-mi nsan ḿ jītí bi-timmun kí cù Juuda tiŋkin. 8Á bàà gíti tīī-mi kugbɔŋu kubɔ mun ḿ cáá tīī sii ubɔti saakpeeliu Asaafi ú tīī-mi idɔ ḿ cáá kpáá sintil difɔkɔku kun yú ki pìl̄ kunimbɔtidiiyee punyɔmmu nì kitiŋ gundi nì kudii kun m làá nīn kóòyee.»
Ubɔti nìn tīī-mi kugbɔŋu gbanti, kun puee Unimbɔti nìn yú m-boon. 9M nìn cūtì ntimu mun bí Eefiraati mɔɔl ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki púee gɔminab cee, ní ki dū tigbɔn tin ubɔti nìn tīī-mee ki tīī-bi. Ubɔti nìn yāntì bijanjakpilib nì bitanjakaliibi céeǹ-mi. 10Sambalati un sá Oorɔn tiŋkinee nì uamɔnja Toobiya, u-taapu yɔu nín gbìl̄ yii m bāańee, an kaa mɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi yii ubɔ dɔ́miń ki nyàab̀ Isirayeel yab ŋanti.
Neeyeemiya yìin̄ ki kpēē Jeerusaleem guŋŋi
11M bàn̄ Jeerusaleemee, m kāl̀ iwiin ita ní. 12Kunyeeuee, man nì bininjab biba nìn yíkì, ama maa nìn pée tùkū báà ubɔ tin Unimbɔti nìn dūu ŋá m-pɔbilin ḿ ŋá kí tīī Jeerusaleemee. Maa nìn cáá kuwaŋkuluu kubɔ ki kútì kimaŋ kin m nìn kēe pu. 13M nìn dūu dī Ditantakal punyɔkɔki ki nyáń ki cūtì Draagɔn nyimbuliŋu nì titampuntan punyɔkɔki. M nìn kpēē Jeerusaleem gundi ki tin kátì ní ki ká yii ajan bátì bátì ki lítì, ní punuubi wùn̄ ŋŋmi. 14Ní m nìkī ki nín cá Nnyimbul punyɔkɔki watil, ki jítì ubɔti bɔɔku caŋin, ní nsan nìn gíti kpá kimaŋ kin m kēe ń dī. 15Kunyeeu gbanti ní m fātìi tí dī ki nín jɔ́ḿ Seedrɔn bùmbiki watil pú ki pée bí ki kpèé Jeerusaleem tiŋki gundi, ní ki fātìi gítì m-boon ki dī Ditantakal punyɔkɔki ki kɔ́.
16Kitiŋ pu bɔsoonliibi kaa nìn nyí laakin m cūtèe, kaa nyí tin mun m ŋée. Kí cáá sāā ŋyunti gbantee, maa nìn tùkū Juuda yab nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì akpambal nì bibɔsoonliibi nì bin kɔkɔ nìn bí ki kpèé atuunee kun pu ní m dɔ́mińee. 17Niinee ní m bí-bi yii: «Nimbi ni-ba ká nnaabu ŋun poon ti kɔ́ee. Jeerusaleem tiŋki kpántì adigbun ní ki-punuubi wùn̄ ŋŋmi. Yīkìmaan tí fàtīí mā Jeerusaleem tiŋki guŋŋi kí nyā icoo ni.» 18Ní m máafì-bi m-Nimbɔtiu nín bīī m-pu puee, nì ubɔti nín sòon̄ nì mi puee. Niinee ní bi téeń yii: «Tí yīkì kí māmaan.» Ní bi yíkì nì kunyannyaau ki kíĺ ditummɔntiil gbanti.
19Sambalati un sá Oorɔn tiŋkinee nì u-taapu yɔu Toobiya uamɔnja, nì ulaalibuja Geeseem nín gbìl̄ an bɔtee, ní bi kíĺ ki bíi bèel̄-ti, ní ki kpèé-ti fám ki lì yii: «Ba ní ni bíi ŋáań nan ní? Ni là kí já nì ubɔti deeyaaa?» 20Ní m kíí-bi yii: «Yilpu Nimbɔtiu u-ba di làá tīī-ti ŋŋmam. Timbi u-tɔntɔnliibi làá yīkì kí fàtīí mā ti-tiŋki. Ama nimbee, naa cáá nsan kí fōō Jeerusaleem tiŋki wanti tiba. Naa tí cáá ki-pu mpɔn ŋubɔ, ní ubɔ kpá kí dāá téetí ni-pu dalba!»

english_text:
Rebuilding the Wall of Jerusalem
1These are the people who helped rebuild the wall and gates of Jerusalem:
The high priest Eliashib and the other priests rebuilt Sheep Gate and hung its doors. Then they dedicated Sheep Gate and the section of the wall as far as Hundred Tower and Hananel Tower.
2The people of Jericho rebuilt the next section of the wall, and Zaccur son of Imri rebuilt the section after that.
3The family of Hassenaah built Fish Gate. They put the beams in place and hung the doors, then they added metal bolts and wooden beams as locks.
4Meremoth, son of Uriah and grandson of Hakkoz, completed the next section of the wall.
Meshullam, son of Berechiah and grandson of Meshezabel, rebuilt the next section, and Zadok son of Baana rebuilt the section beside that.
5The next section was to be repaired by the men of Tekoa, but their town leaders refused to do the hard work they were assigned.
6Joiada son of Paseah and Meshullam son of Besodeiah restored Ancient Gate. They put the beams in place, hung the doors, and added metal bolts and wooden beams as locks. 7Melatiah from Gibeon, Jadon from Meronoth, and the men from Gibeon and Mizpah rebuilt the next section of the wall. This section reached as far as the house of the governor of West Euphrates Province.
8Uzziel son of Harhaiah the goldsmith rebuilt the next section.
Hananiah the perfume maker rebuilt the section next after that, and it went as far as Broad Wall.
9Rephaiah son of Hur ruled half of the Jerusalem District, and he rebuilt the next section of the wall.
10The section after that was close to the home of Jedaiah son of Harumaph, and he rebuilt it.
Hattush son of Hashabneiah constructed the next section of the wall.
11Malchijah son of Harim and Hasshub son of Pahath Moab rebuilt the section after that, and they also built Oven Tower.
12Shallum son of Hallohesh ruled the other half of the Jerusalem District, and he rebuilt the next section of the wall. Shallum's daughters also worked with him.
13Hanun and the people who lived in the town of Zanoah rebuilt Valley Gate. They hung the doors and added metal bolts and wooden beams as locks. They also rebuilt the wall for 440 meters, all the way to Garbage Gate.
14Malchijah son of Rechab ruled the district of Beth-Haccherem, and he rebuilt Garbage Gate. He hung the doors and added metal bolts and wooden beams as locks.
15Shallum son of Colhozeh ruled the district of Mizpah, and he rebuilt Fountain Gate. He put a cover over the gateway, then hung the doors and added metal bolts and wooden beams as locks. He also rebuilt the wall at Shelah Pool. This section was next to the king's garden and went as far as the stairs leading down from David's City.
16Nehemiah son of Azbuk ruled half of the district of Beth-Zur, and he rebuilt the next section of the wall. It went as far as the royal cemetery, the artificial pool, and the army barracks.
Levites Who Worked on the Wall
17The Levites who worked on the next sections of the wall were Rehum son of Bani; Hashabiah, who ruled half of the district of Keilah and did this work for his district; 18Binnui son of Henadad, who ruled the other half of the district of Keilah; 19Ezer son of Jeshua, who ruled Mizpah, rebuilt the section of the wall that was in front of the armory and reached to the corner of the wall; 20Baruch son of Zabbai eagerly rebuilt the section of the wall that went all the way to the door of the house of Eliashib the high priest; 21Meremoth, son of Uriah and grandson of Hakkoz, built up to the far end of Eliashib's house.
Priests Who Worked on the Wall
22Here is a list of the priests who worked on the wall:
Priests from the region around Jerusalem rebuilt the next section of the wall.
23Benjamin and Hasshub rebuilt the wall in front of their own houses.
Azariah, who was the son of Maaseiah and the grandson of Ananiah, rebuilt the section in front of his house.
24Binnui son of Henadad rebuilt the section of the wall from Azariah's house to the corner of the wall.
25Palal son of Uzai rebuilt the next section, which began at the corner of the wall and the tower of the upper palace near the court of the guard.
Pedaiah son of Parosh rebuilt the next section of the wall. 26He stopped at a place near the Water Gate on the east and the tower guarding the temple. This was close to a section in the city called Ophel, where the temple workers lived.
Other Builders Who Worked on the Wall
27The men from Tekoa rebuilt the next section of the wall, and it was their second section. It started at a place across from the large tower that guarded the Temple, and it went all the way to the wall near Ophel.
28Some priests rebuilt the next section of the wall. They began working north of Horse Gate, and each one worked on a section in front of his own house.
29Zadok son of Immer rebuilt the wall in front of his house.
Shemaiah son of Shecaniah, who looked after the East Gate, rebuilt the section after that.
30Hananiah and Hanun rebuilt the next section, which was the second section for them.
Meshullam son of Berechiah rebuilt the next section, which happened to be in front of his house.
31Malchijah, a goldsmith, rebuilt the next section, as far as the house used by the temple workers and merchants. This area was across from Gathering Gate, near the room on top of the wall at the northeast corner.
32The goldsmiths and merchants rebuilt the last section of the wall, which went from the corner room all the way to Sheep Gate.
translation_text:
Juuda yab fātìi bíi māā Jeerusaleem tiŋki gundi
1Usaraaŋakpil Eeliyaasiib nì u-nabiyaamu bisaraaŋaliibi nìn yíkì ki kíĺ ditundi. Bíǹ di nìn máń Apibil punyɔkɔki. Bi nìn dū-kì ki sú Unimbɔti ní ki cóoǹ ki-punuubi. Bi nìn dū digundi ki sú Unimbɔti ní ki ŋáŋkì-dì ki cáa sāā bijanjaliibi Dilaataal difɔkɔku, ní ki yōoǹ niin ki cáa sāā Ananeeyeel difɔkɔku. 2Jeeriikoo yab nìn bí bi-cee ki tūǹ ditundi, nì Imirii jipɔɔn Sakuur. 3Aseena yab di nìn máń Ijɔm punyɔkɔki. Bíǹ di nìn kpáá punuubi dɔcooŋkaai ní ki sākaǹ punuubi ní ki nákáǹ ipiin nì tikpàlkaal. 4Bin nìn bí bi-caŋin ki tūǹ ditundee di sá Uriya jipɔɔn Meereemooti, Akoosi naantiiu nì Beereekiya jipɔɔn Meekulaam, Meeseesaabeel naantiiu nì Tiisaadooki jipɔɔn Baana. 5Bin nìn dī bi muee di sá Teekoowa yab. Ama bi-kpilib nìn yíì yii baa là kí nīn bí bi-tɔntɔŋkpilib taapu kí tɔ̄ ditundi.
6Paseeya jipɔɔn Yooyadaa nì Beesoodiya jipɔɔn Meekulaam di nìn ŋáŋkì Yeesana punyɔkɔki. Bíǹ di nìn kpáá punuubi dɔcooŋkaai ní ki sākaǹ punuubi ní ki nákáǹ ipiin nì tikpàlkaal. 7Bin nìn bí bi-caŋin ki tūǹ ditundee di sá ugabaawɔnja Meelatiya nì umeeroonootija Yaadɔn nì Gabawɔn yab nì Miisipa yab bin nìn bí Eefiraati ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú timmu gɔminau cee ki sòoǹ tibɔtee. 8Bin nìn bí bi mun caŋin ki tūǹ ditundee di sá Araya jipɔɔn Usiyeel un sá goosimiitee, ní úǹ caŋinee, utalaaluŋal Ananiya nìn bí. Bi nìn túń ditundi Jeerusaleem ki cáa sāā laakin ní digundi wāāyee ní ki gbēeǹ. 9Bíǹ caŋinee, Uur jipɔɔn Reefaya, Jeerusaleem jandi diba bɔtiu di nìn bí ki tūǹ ditundi. 10U mun caŋinee, Arumaafi jipɔɔn Yeedaya di nìn bí ki tūǹ ditundi dijandi din túĺ u-mɔŋkiŋu watilee. U mun caŋinee, Asabineeya jipɔɔn Atuusi di nìn bí ki tūǹ ditundi. 11Ariim jipɔɔn Maalkiya nì Paati-Moowaab jipɔɔn Akuub di nìn ŋáŋkì digundi janliliitiil, nì Mpaamu difɔkɔku. 12Bíǹ caŋinee, Alooweesi jipɔɔn Saaluum un sá Jeerusaleem tiŋki jandi din kíǹee bɔtiu di nìn bí ki tūǹ ditundi, u nì u-bisalib. 13Anuun nì Saamoowa yab di nìn ŋáŋkì Ditantakal punyɔkɔki. Bíǹ di nìn kpáá punuubi dɔcooŋkaai ní ki sākaǹ punuubi ní ki nákáǹ ipiin nì tikpàlkaal. Bíǹ di tí máń digundi mpúun cáá meetab alaataa aŋmoo ki tin cáa sāā Titampuntan punyɔkɔki. 14Reekaab jipɔɔn Maalkiya, Beeti-Akeereem tiŋki bɔtiu di nìn ŋáŋkì Titampuntan punyɔkɔki. U nìn fātìi máń-kì ki kpáá punuubi dɔcooŋkaai ní ki sākaǹ punuubi ní ki nákáǹ ipiin nì tikpàlkaal.
15Kool-Ooseeya jipɔɔn Saaluum, Miisipa tiŋki bɔtiu di nìn ŋáŋkì Nnyimbul punyɔkɔki. U nìn fātìi máń-kì ki píń ní ki sākaǹ punuubi ní ki nákáǹ ipiin nì tikpàlkaal. Úǹ di nìn tí fātìi máń Siiloowee nyimbɔbil gundi, kí yòon̄ ubɔti kpaabu kí cáá sāā nsan ŋun jɔ́ḿ Daafiidi Tiŋkinee. 16Úǹ boonee, Asibuki jipɔɔn Neeyeemiya, Beeti-Suur tiŋki bɔtiu di nìn bí ki tūǹ ditundi kí yòon̄ dijandi din dɔ̄ ki cáa gūū Daafiidi ceekuee, ki nìkī ki tin sāā nnyimbilkaam nì ubɔti janjaliibi dumpu. 17Úǹ boonee, Leefii yab di nìn pá ki tūǹ ditundi. Banii jipɔɔn Reewum nìn bí, ní Keeyiila tiŋki dijandi bɔtiu Asabiya nìn bí u-caŋin ki tūǹ ditundi u-tinjandi pu. 18Úǹ boonee, bi-nabiyaamu Eenadaadi jipɔɔn Bafayi, Keeyiila tiŋki jandi din kíǹee bɔtiu, 19nì Yeesuwa jipɔɔn Eeseer, Miisipa bɔtiu di nìn pá. Eeseer di nìn ŋáŋkì dijanliliitiil din nìn túĺ laakin bi yōontí tijanjawan digundi lɔ́kɔ́ee. 20Sabaayi jipɔɔn Baruuki di nìn bí u-caŋin ki tūǹ ditundi nì difaŋgiil ki yōoǹ dijandi din bí digunlɔkɔl laŋki kí cáá sāā usaraaŋakpil Eeliyasiib diiku nyɔkɔpuee. 21Úǹ boonee, Uurii jipɔɔn Meereemooti, Akoosi naantiiu di nìn yōoǹ dijandi din bí usaraaŋakpil Eeliyasiib diiku nyɔkɔpuee ki ŋáŋkì ki cáa tin kátì.
22Ní úǹ boonee, bisaraaŋaliibi bin māntìi tú Jeerusaleemee di nìn bí ki tūǹ ditundi. 23Bíǹ boonee, Beenjameen nì Asuub di nìn bí ki ŋáŋkí dijandi din túĺ bi-diiŋŋee. Bíǹ boonee, Maseeyawuu jipɔɔn Asariya, Ananiya naantiiu di nìn bí ki ŋáŋkí laakin pìlīǹ u-diikuee. 24Úǹ boonee, Eenadaadi jipɔɔn Binuyii di nìn bí ki ŋáŋkí dijandi din bí kí yòon̄ Asariya dumpu kí cáá sāā digunlɔkɔlee. 25Paalali jipɔɔn Usaayii di ŋáŋkì diguŋkpindi nyɔkɔpu nì kudifɔkɔu kun lībitì ubɔti diiŋŋi puee ki tin sāā bisarkadambi mɔŋkiŋu. Úǹ boonee, Paaneeyoosi jipɔɔn, 26nì bin bí ki tútúǹ kunimbɔtidii poon tuuŋŋi ki kóò Oofeel tiŋgbaŋkinee túń ditundi ki tin sāā kudifɔkɔu kun bí Nnyim punyɔkɔki kin bí ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee. 27Bíǹ boonee ní Teekoowa yab yōoǹ digundi din túĺ kudifɔkɔuee ki túń ditundi ki cáa sāā Oofeel gundi.
28Bisaraaŋaliibi di nìn yōoǹ kí kíĺ Itaamu punyɔkɔki yilpu pú, ní báà ŋma túń ditundi ki cáá sāā u-diiku nyɔkɔpu. 29Boonee, Saadooki jipɔɔn Imeer di nìn bí ki ŋáŋkí digundi laakin túĺ u-diikuee. Úǹ boonee, Seekaniya jipɔɔn Seemaya un nìn cí ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú punyɔkɔkee di nìn bí ki tūǹ ditundi. 30Úǹ boonee Seeleemiya jipɔɔn Ananiya, nì Salafi jipɔnluluutiu Anuun di nìn bí ki ŋáŋkí dijanliliitiil. Úǹ boonee, Beereekiya jipɔɔn Meesulam di nìn bí ki ŋáŋkí dijandi din túĺ u-diikuee. 31Úǹ boonee, goosimiiti Maalkiya di nìn bí ki tūǹ ditundi kí cáá sāā kunimbɔtidiin tɔntɔnliibi nì bibantiliibi diiŋŋi ŋin túĺ Miifkaadi watilee, ní ki yōoǹ niin ki tin cáa sāā sintil diiku kun tɔ́kɔ́ digunlɔkɔl puee. 32Goosimiitib nì bibantiliibi di nìn bí ki ŋáŋkí sintil diiku kun tɔ́kɔ́ digunlɔkɔl puee nì Apibil punyɔkɔki kansikin.
Binannanliibi kaa kíí bí mā digundi
33Sambalati nín gbìl̄ yii timbi Juuda yab fātìi bíi māā digundee ní u fōō mbum ki gíí diŋuul tikpil. U nìn bíi bèel̄-ti 34ní ki lì u-yab nì Samaarii yab nimbiin yii: «Ba ní Juuda yab bin kaa bí tiban nee bíi ŋáań ní? Bi làá ŋmā kí tɔ̄ ditundi din bi kíĺ nee kí cáa kátí kí ŋá saraabi kí tīī Unimbɔtaaa? Bi làá ŋmā kí dū ataŋkpee ŋin wùn̄ ki dɔ̄ dikpúkul ki kpántì ntam nee kí dūú mā digundi kí dóó ŋwimbaantaaa?» 35Uamɔnja Toobiya nìn bí ki kɔ́ĺ-u ní ki lī yii: «Bí māa! Kiŋɔkɔ yaa pée dàb̄ bi-gundi din bi cáá ataŋkpee ki māā nee, dì làá lítí ní!»
36«Áù ti-Nimbɔtiu, pīlifì bi nín bí ki kpèé ki sìŋkīǹ-ti puee. Yàntī bi-siibiliŋ ŋin bi bí ki sìí-ti nee ń fàtīí lítí bi-pu. Yàntī bi-nannanliibi ń dāá fūkul̀-bi, kí cúú-bi kí cùnnì kitiŋ kiba poon kuyuŋu! 37Á taa dū bi-kpitii kí pɔ̄-bi, kí taa pítí bi-yìntitam a-nimbiin, kun puee bi sīī timbi bin bin fātìi bíi māā digundee.»
38Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, ti fātìi máń digundi ki yākatìi ŋmāntì di-púuŋŋu kansikin nì kansikin, di sá yii samaa nìn dū bi-pɔbil kɔkɔ ki tīī.

english_text:
Nehemiah's Enemies
1When Sanballat, the governor of Samaria, heard that we were rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem, he became angry and started insulting our people. 2In front of his friends and the Samaritan army he said, “What is this feeble bunch of Jews trying to do? Are they going to rebuild the wall and offer sacrifices all in one day? Do they think they can make something out of this pile of scorched stones?”
3Tobiah from Ammon was standing beside Sanballat and said, “Look at the wall they are building! Why, even a fox could knock over this pile of stones.”
4But I prayed, “Our God, these people hate us and have wished horrible things for us. Please answer our prayers and make their insults fall on them! Let them be the ones to be dragged away as prisoners of war. 5Don't forgive the mean and evil way they have insulted the builders.”
6The people worked hard, and we built the walls of Jerusalem halfway up again. 7But Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabs, the Ammonites, and the people from the city of Ashdod saw the walls going up and the holes being repaired. So they became angry 8and decided to stir up trouble, and to fight against the people of Jerusalem. 9But we kept on praying to our God, and we also stationed guards day and night.
10Meanwhile, the people of Judah were singing a sorrowful song:
“So much rubble for us to haul!
Worn out and weary,
will we ever finish this wall?”
11Our enemies were saying, “Before those Jews know what has happened, we will sneak up and kill them and put an end to their work.”
12On at least ten different occasions, the Jews living near our enemies warned us against attacks from every side, 13and so I sent people to guard the wall at its lowest places and where there were still holes in it. I placed them according to families, and they stood guard with swords and spears and with bows and arrows. 14Then I looked things over and told the leaders, the officials, and the rest of the people, “Don't be afraid of your enemies! The Lord is great and fearsome. So think of him and fight for your relatives and children, your wives and homes!”
15Our enemies found out that we knew about their plot against us, but God kept them from doing what they had planned. So we went back to work on the wall.
16From then on, I let half of the young men work while the other half stood guard. They wore armor and had spears and shields, as well as bows and arrows. The leaders helped the workers 17who were rebuilding the wall. Everyone who hauled building materials kept one hand free to carry a weapon. 18Even the workers who were rebuilding the wall strapped on a sword. The worker who was to blow the signal trumpet stayed with me.
19I told the people and their officials and leaders, “Our work is so spread out, that we are a long way from one another. 20If you hear the sound of the trumpet, come quickly and gather around me. Our God will help us fight.”
21Every day from dawn to dark, half of the workers rebuilt the walls, while the rest stood guard with their spears.
22I asked the men in charge and their workers to stay inside Jerusalem and stand guard at night. So they guarded the city at night and worked during the day. 23I even slept in my work clothes at night; my relatives, the workers, and the guards slept in theirs as well. And we always kept our weapons close by.
translation_text:
1Ŋyunti ŋun Sambalati nì Toobiya nì bilaalibub nì Amɔn yab nì Asidoodi yab gbìl̄ yii Jeerusaleem gundi mātam bíi cá nyɔkɔpu, ní bi fātìi bíi māā ki ŋēeb̀ digundi jaŋŋi ŋin lítèe, ní bi fōō mbum tiŋan pu. 2Bi nìn kpáfì ki bóob́ kí dāá já nì Jeerusaleem yab kí cáań fìkil fikil. 3Niinee ní ti mēē ti-Nimbɔtiu, ní bi-puee, ti lēē binib ki yóoǹ sintil bí nīn cí-ti ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu. 4Ama ní Juuda yab bíi gbùkum̄ yii:
«Ndigbuntam kpúkú tikpil,
ní bin bíi fèe gīī an dáá gbíntìi dɔ̄.
Taa làá ŋmā kí fàtīí mā digundi nee.»
5Ní ti-nannanliibi bí ki lì yii: «Bi làá nīn pée kā kaa nyí, kaa wāĺ ní tí dāá túuǹ-bi kí nà-bi ní kí yàntī digundi mātam ń gbèen̄.»
Neeyeemiya tīī bitɔntɔnliibi tijanjawan
6Juuda yab bin nìn kóò bi-kansikinee dɔ́miń ki tùkū-ti ŋfunyɔm saalaa pu yii: «Laakin kamaa ní ni yaa pée fātèe, bi kā ti-pu ní.» 7Niinee ní m dū binib ki yóoǹ digundi boon laakin tàkēe. M nìn yóoǹ-bi ki nóó nì bi nín pēē pēē mmaal puee ní bi ŋúb́ ntàataajimu nì ŋkpamu nì itɔfi. 8M yóoǹ-bi míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki bí abɔtibil nì bibɔsoonliibi nì samaa un kíǹee yii: «Taa fàŋkìmaan ni-nannanliibi! Téetímaan ni-Dindaan un sá ukpaan ki sá kuwambiiuee pu, kí já ni-nabiyaamu nì ni-jipɔmbi nì ni-bisalib nì ni-nimpoobi nì ni-diiŋŋi pu.»
9Ti-nannanliibi nín gbìl̄ yii ti béè tin bi bɔ́ntèe nì Unimbɔti nín bíil̀ tin bi bàà bóob́ kí ŋée puee, ní ti-kɔkɔ fātìi gítì digundi cee, ní báà ŋma nìkī ditundi din u bàà bíi tūǹee. 10Ama kí yòon̄ ŋwiin gbantee, m-tɔntɔnliibi bininjab dijandi di nìn bí ki tūǹ ditundi ní dijandi din kíǹee ŋúb́ ŋkpamu nì agbampɔɔ nì itɔfi ní ki pēē ajanjabɔkuti. Bikpilib nìn yú Juuda yab kɔkɔ boon. 11Bin nìn bíi māā digundee nì bin nìn tūntí awaŋgulee nìn cáá ŋŋal ŋubɔ ní ki tūǹ ditundi, ní ŋun kíǹee ŋúb́ tijanjawan. 12Bimaliibi nìn gbìn̄ bi-tàataajimmu bi-cammu ní ki māā, ní uninja un búǹ ŋyinee yú m-tikindi. 13Ní m bí abɔtibil nì bibɔsoonliibi nì samaa un kíǹee kɔkɔ yii: «Digundi tundi din kíǹee dáá náaǹ ki wīikí, ní ajancuku ŋin pu ti bí ki tūǹ ditundee dátiǹ tɔb. 14Míǹ puee laakin kamaa ni yaa bí ní ki gbìl̄ bi búń ŋyinee, ní dāá kpāfì m-cee. Ti-Nimbɔtiu làá já kí tīī-ti!»
15Ti nìn tūǹ ditundi kí kíĺ kutaafaau kí dāá sāā kunyeeu iŋmalbijaa nyātam, ní ti-kansikin dijandi ŋúb́ ŋkpamu. 16Ŋyunti gbanti mbaanti ní m tùkū samaa yii: «Kunyeeuee, utɔntɔŋkpil kamaa nì u-tɔntɔnliibi ń cù Jeerusaleem kí cīití sintil, kutaa yaa wúntèe, bí dāá tɔ̄ ditundi. 17Man m-ba nì m-nabiyaamu nì m-tɔntɔnliibi nì m-janjaliibi bin cí-mee, ti-kansikin báà ubɔ kaa nìn pèetī u-wanti, see ti yaa làá fàl̀ baba.»

english_text:
Nehemiah's Concern for the Poor
1Some of the men and their wives complained about the Jews in power 2and said, “We have large families, and it takes a lot of grain merely to keep us alive.”
3Others said, “During the famine we even had to mortgage our fields, vineyards, and homes to them in order to buy grain.”
4Then others said, “We had to borrow money from those in power to pay the government tax on our fields and vineyards. 5We are Jews just as they are, and our children are as good as theirs. But we still have to sell our children as slaves, and some of our daughters have already been raped. We are completely helpless; our fields and vineyards have even been taken from us.”
6When I heard their complaints and their charges, I became very angry. 7 So I thought it over and said to the leaders and officials, “How can you charge your own people interest?”
Then I called a public meeting and accused the leaders 8by saying, “We have tried to buy back all of our people who were sold into exile. But here you are, selling more of them for us to buy back!” The officials and leaders did not say a word, because they knew this was true.
9I continued, “What you have done is wrong! We must honor our God by the way we live, so the Gentiles can't find fault with us. 10My relatives, my friends, and I are also lending money and grain, but we must no longer demand payment in return. 11Now give back the fields, vineyards, olive orchards, and houses you have taken and also the interest you have been paid.”
12The leaders answered, “We will do whatever you say and return their property, without asking to be repaid.”
So I made the leaders promise in front of the priests to give back the property. 13Then I emptied my pockets and said, “If you don't keep your promise, that's what God will do to you. He will empty out everything you own, even taking away your houses.”
The people answered, “We will keep our promise.” Then they praised the Lord and did as they had promised.
Nehemiah Is Generous
14I was governor of Judah from the twentieth year that Artaxerxes was king until the thirty-second year. And during these entire twelve years, my relatives and I refused to accept the food that I was allowed. 15Each governor before me had been a burden to the people by making them pay for his food and wine and by demanding forty silver coins a day. Even their officials had been a burden to the people. But I respected God, and I didn't think it was right to be so hard on them. 16I spent all my time getting the wall rebuilt and did not buy any property. Everyone working for me did the same thing. 17I usually fed 150 of our own Jewish people and their leaders, as well as foreign visitors from surrounding lands. 18Each day one ox, six of the best sheep, and lots of chickens were prepared. Then every ten days, a large supply of wine was brought in. I knew what a heavy burden this would have been for the people, and so I did not ask for my food allowance as governor.
19I pray that God will bless me for everything I have done for my people.
translation_text:
Neeyeemiya kúntì inaamuul Isirayeel yab kansikin
1Ŋyunti ŋubɔ poonee ní samaa poon bininjab biba nì bi-nimpoobi dɔ́miń ki bíi yáliŋkí tikpil bi-nabiyaamu Juuda yab bimbim pu. 2Biba nìn bí ki lì yii: «Timbi nì ti-jipɔmbi nì ti-bisalib wīikí tikpil. Ti là tijin kí jī kí ŋmátí.» 3Bin kíǹee nìn lì yii: «Timbi dù ti-sati nì ti-fiinyi sufii nì ti-diiŋŋi ní kí yóoń toolima ŋkùm yuntiŋu ní kí nín ká kí jī.» 4Ní biba mun nìn lì yii: «Kí ŋmā kí pà lampoo kí tīī gɔminee, see tí pìnnì animbil kí dū ti-sati nì ti-fiinyi sufii kí yóoń toolima. 5Ti nì bi bàà sá binibaantiibi, ní bi-jipɔmbi nì ti-jipɔmbi sá bibaantiibi. Ama nì míǹ kɔkɔee, see timbi ń dū ti-jipɔmbi nì ti-bisalib kí tīī bí kpántí iyumbu. Ti-bisalib biba gba pée kpántì iyumbu ki dóò. Taa ŋūǹ kí ŋá mbamin. Ti-sati nì ti-fiinyi sufii kpántì bin ti jíń apɔɔnee wanti ní.»
6Ŋyunti ŋun m gbìl̄ bi nín bíi yáliŋkí puee nì tin bi sòoǹee ní an kɔ́ǹ-mi diŋuul tikpil. 7Niinee ní m ká yii an máaǹ ḿ wòoǹ abɔtibil nì bibɔsoonliibi. M nìn bí-bi yii: «Ni bíi wɔ́b̀ ni-nabiyaamu dee yaa!» Niinee ní m yíiń dikpafikpaandi kí kpèè tibɔti gbanti. 8M nìn bí-bi yii: «Timbi ti-ba nì ti-ŋmam ní ti fātìi dūu dá ti-nabiyaamu Juuda yab bin bi nìn dūu nyáfiǹ binicambee. Ama ní nimbi fàtīi cáá ni-nabiyaamu ki nyáfí, ní timbi ti-ba di fàtīi bíi dāā-bi!»
Ní bi ŋmí fɔ́ŋfɔŋ, kaa pée ká dinyɔɔbundi ki gātì. 9M nìn nìkī ki lī yii: «Ni nín ŋá puee kaa ŋān̄! Ni máaǹ kí fàŋkì ti-Nimbɔtiu ní ti-nannanliibi ń taa ká nsan kí sìì-ti. 10Man nì m-nabiyaamu nì m-tɔntɔnliibi, ti mun pīnnì binib animbil nì tijin. An puee ti-kɔkɔ ń dū ti-pɔnliibi pɔɔŋŋi kí pɔ̄-bi. 11Ní gíiǹ bi-sati nì bi-fiinyi sufii nì bi-ɔliifi sufii nì bi-diiŋŋi kí tīī-bi díǹ. Ní dū tin kɔkɔ ni nìn pīnnì-bi bí dāá pà kí páańee, an yaa sá animbilaaa, tijinaaa, ŋkpamaaa, ní dūú yàntī kí taa ti fōō ipaati.» 12Ní bi bí yii: «Ti làá gíiǹ tin kɔkɔ ti fōōyee kí tīī, kaa làá bàlifì tiba pu, kii a nín lī puee.»
Ní m yíiń bisaraaŋaliibi ní ki yāntì bin kɔkɔ bi cáá apɔɔnee pūtì kí ŋá bi nín lī yii bi làá ŋá puee. 13Ní m gbáfì m-bɔkutil lɔbiki ki bí-bi yii: «Míǹ ní Unimbɔti làá gbāfì un di kaa ŋá min tibɔti nee bí yii bí ŋée kí fá ndandati kí wàatī u-dicaŋku nì u-gaajati, ú taa nín̄ gíti cáá báà tiba.» Ní samaa kɔkɔ kíí yii: «Ameeni, án ŋá míǹ.»
Samaa kɔkɔ nìn nyɔ́ŋkì ti-Dindaan, ní ki ŋá min bi lī yii bi làá ŋée.
14Kí yòon̄ ŋyunti ŋun bi lēē-mi ḿ nīn sá Juuda tiŋkin gɔmina, ubɔti Aritaseerseesi beel yuntiŋu abin mmuŋku kí cáá sāā abin mmuŋku nì saalaa nì alee, an dàkà yii abin saalaa nì alee, man nì m-yab kaa lēē gɔmina lampoou nimbiliŋ, kii án nín bàà sá tí lēē puee. 15Gɔminab bin nìn kāl̀ ní man nín bāańee nìn sàantí samaa tikpil. Bi nìn fòol̄-bi tijin nì ndaam ní kí kūtì animbil jitɔmbi imuŋku ili. Bi-tɔntɔnliibi mun nìn wɔ́b́ samaa. Ama man nín fàŋkí Unimbɔtee puee, maa ŋá míǹ. 16Kí kūtèe, man m-ba túń digundi nee mātam tundi. Maa dá kusaau kubɔ, ní man tɔntɔnliibi kɔkɔ nìn kpáfì niin ki bíi tūǹ ditundi. 17Juuda yab nì abɔtibil ŋin nìn jīǹ m-dumpuee nìn sá binib dilaataal nì imuŋku ili nì saalaa ní. Maa kpáaǹ binicambi bin nyēeń atimbun ŋin māntìi tú-ti ki dòoń ki kóò m-puee. 18Ŋwiin kamaayee, m nìn kù unaa ubɔ nì ipii in yáàyee iluu nì ikɔl ní. Man m-ba nimbiliŋ ní m nìn cáa dāā, ní iwiin saalaa kamaayee, m nìn yàntī bi cāabìń-mi ndaam tikpil tikpil. Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, maa nìn bālifì yii bí tīī tin sá bí tīī-mi yii m nín sá gɔminee pu, di sá yii atuun ŋin samaa nìn bíi tūǹee nìn sá kii diwaŋgulee ní ki nyìm̀ bi-pu.
19«M-Nimbɔtiu, téetí tin kɔkɔ m ŋá ki tīī samaa neeyee pu, kí ŋá-mi tiniti.»

english_text:
Plots against Nehemiah
1Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem, and our other enemies learned that I had completely rebuilt the wall. All I lacked was hanging the doors in the gates. 2Then Sanballat and Geshem sent a message, asking me to meet with them in one of the villages in Ono Valley. I knew they were planning to harm me in some way. 3So I sent messengers to tell them, “My work is too important to stop now and go there. I can't afford to slow down the work just to visit with you.” 4They invited me four times, but each time I refused to go.
5Finally, Sanballat sent an official to me with an unsealed letter, 6which said:
A rumor is going around among the nations that you and the other Jews are rebuilding the wall and planning to rebel, because you want to be their king. And Geshem says it's true! 7You even have prophets in Jerusalem, claiming you are now the king of Judah. You know the Persian king will hear about this, so let's get together and talk it over.
8I sent a message back to Sanballat, saying, “None of this is true! You are making it all up.”
9Our enemies were trying to frighten us and to keep us from our work. But I asked God to give me strength.
10One day I went to visit Shemaiah. He wasn't supposed to leave his house, but he said, “Let's hurry to the holy place of the temple and hide there. We will lock the temple doors, because your enemies are planning to kill you tonight.”
11I answered, “Why should someone like me have to run and hide in the temple to save my life? I won't go!”
12Suddenly I realized that God had not given Shemaiah this message. But Tobiah and Sanballat had paid him to trick me 13and to frighten me into doing something wrong, because they wanted to ruin my good name.
14Then I asked God to punish Tobiah and Sanballat for what they had done. I prayed that God would punish the prophet Noadiah and the other prophets who, together with her, had tried to frighten me.
The Work Is Finished
15On the twenty-fifth day of the month Elul, the wall was completely rebuilt. It had taken 52 days. 16When our enemies in the surrounding nations learned that the work was finished, they felt helpless, because they knew that our God had helped us rebuild the wall.
17All this time the Jewish leaders and Tobiah had been writing letters back and forth. 18Many people in Judah were loyal to Tobiah for two reasons: Shecaniah son of Arah was his father-in-law, and Tobiah's son Jehohanan had married the daughter of Meshullam son of Berechiah. 19The people would always tell me about the good things Tobiah had done, and then they would tell Tobiah everything I had said. So Tobiah kept sending letters, trying to frighten me.
translation_text:
Neeyeemiya nannanliibi nyàab̀ kí ŋá-u tikpitil
1Sambalati nì Toobiya nì Geeseem ulaalibuja nì ti-nannanliibi bin kíǹee nìn gbìl̄ yii m fātìi máń digundi dibùndi diba kaa ti bí. Ŋyunti gbantee, punuubi di nìn kíǹ maa láá dūu cóoǹ. 2Sambalati nì Geeseem nìn túnní binib bí tùkù-mi yii ḿ dāan̄ tí kpāfì Keefiriim tiŋkin Oonoo tantakalin. Bi nìn cáá nlandɔkɔ kí ŋá-mi tikpitil. 3M nìn tú binib bí cùú tùkù-bi yii: «Atuun ŋin m bíi tūǹ dooyee wīikí tikpil, an pɔ̄ɔ̄ ḿ ŋmā kí dāan̄ ni-cee. M yaa yíkì ki nín dòoń ni-cee, ditundi làá gbèen̄.»
4Bi túnní bi yíí-mi míǹ ŋfunyɔm minaa pu, ní m kíí-bi tibɔbaantiil. 5Sambalati nìn gíti túnní u-tɔntɔnliu ubɔ ŋŋmooŋmootiim, u ŋúbiń kugbɔŋu ncal an kaa fúuń tiba poon. 6Bi nìn ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu gbanti poon yii: «Atimbun kɔkɔ poonee, bi sòoǹ ní Geeseem mun lī yii sii nì a-nabiyaamu Juuda yab cáá nlandɔkɔ kí nyā ni-ba. An pu ní a fātìi bíi māā digundi. Bi lī gba yii a là kí kpántí bi-bɔtiu ní. 7Bi bí yii a lēē Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi Jeerusaleem bí bāakì yii a kpántì Juuda tiŋkin ubɔti. Tibɔti gbanti làá bà Peeriisi yab bɔtiu cee, an puee dāan̄ man cee tí kpāfì kí sòoǹ.» 8Ní m tú bí tùkù-u yii: «Tin kɔkɔ a sòon̄ nee, mbaamɔn ŋubɔ kpá poon, sii a-ba di náań-tì.» 9Binib gbanti kɔkɔ nìn nyàab̀ kí fàaǹ-ti ní. Bi nìn dàkafī yii ti-wunti làá yɔ̀tī tí gbèen̄ ditundi ní.
«Kɔŋkɔnnee m-Dindaan, tīī-mi mpɔn!»
10Dalbee man nìn cūtì ki ká Deelaya jipɔɔn Seemaya, Meetabeel naantiiu, kun puee waa nìn ŋūǹ kí nyā. Ní u bí-mi yii: «Tí kɔ́ kunimbɔtidiin, poon poon diikun kí kpāfì. Tí pìin̄ mpunyɔmu kí kpàl̄, di sá bi là kí kpɔ̀-si. Kunyeeu ní a-nannanliibi làá dāan̄ kí kpɔ̀-si.» 11Ní m kíí-u yii: «Kii man nee di sáńaaa? Àá unil ulɔu di bí kii man nee ní kí kɔ́ kunimbɔtidiin kí taa kpú? Maa làá cù.»
12M nìn béè yii an kaa sá Unimbɔti di nìn tīī-u dinyɔɔbundi ú dūú nàatī-mi, ama an sá Sambalati nì Toobiya di nìn tīī-u animbil ú sòoǹ nì mi míǹ. 13Ba pu ní bi nìn tīī-u animbil? An nìn sá ú sòoǹ míǹ ḿ fàŋkì kí nóó u-saŋkii kí ŋá ikpiti. Niinee bi bàà ká nsan kí bīil̀ m-yindi kí kɔ́ǹ-mi icoo dee.
14«M-Nimbɔtiu, taa súntí tin Toobiya nì Sambalati nì Noowadiya, unimpu un nàatī a-bɔtee, nì a-bɔnaatiliibi bin kíǹee nín ŋá tin ki nyàab̀ kí fàan̄-mee pu.»
15Bi nìn dū iwiin imuŋku ili nì saalaa nì ili ní ki máń ki dóò digundi, uŋmal un bi yíì Eeluulee wiiŋyi mmuŋku nì iŋmoo dal. 16Ti-nannanliibi kɔkɔ nín gbìl̄ mimmee, tifaandi nìn kɔ́ atimbun ŋin nìn māntìi tú-tee kɔkɔ ní bíǹ bi-ba nìn ká yii bi sīntì taapu. Niinee bi béè yii an sá ti-Nimbɔtiu di tútúǹ-ti ní ti túń ditundi gbanti ki dóò.
17Ŋyunti gbanti kɔkɔ mun poonee, Juuda yab bɔtibiliŋ nìn ŋmà Toobiya tigban ní úǹ kíikí-bi. 18Di sá u nì Juuda yab tikpil nìn pūtì ki pōoǹ tɔb, kun puee u nìn sá Araa jipɔɔn Seekaniya coo, ní úǹ u-ba jipɔɔn Yeewoowanan nìn cáá Beereekiya jipɔɔn Meesulam bisal. 19Bi nìn sòoǹ ki pàkà-u m-nimbiin, ní ki cáǹ ma mun bɔti ki máafí-u. Toobiya nìn ŋmà-mi tigban kí fàaǹ-mi.

english_text:
1After the wall had been rebuilt and the gates hung, then the temple guards, the singers, and the other Levites were assigned their work. 2I put my brother Hanani in charge of Jerusalem, along with Hananiah, the commander of the fortress, because Hananiah could be trusted, and he respected God more than most people did. 3I said to them, “Don't let the gates to the city be opened until the sun has been up for a while. And make sure that they are closed and barred before the guards go off duty at sunset. Choose people from Jerusalem to stand guard at different places around the wall and others to stand guard near their own houses.”
A List of Exiles Who Returned
(Ezra 2.1-70)
4Although Jerusalem covered a large area, not many people lived there, and no new houses had been built. 5-6So God gave me the idea to bring together the people, their leaders, and officials and to check the family records of those who had returned from captivity in Babylonia, after having been taken there by King Nebuchadnezzar. About this same time, I found records of those who had been the first to return to Jerusalem from Babylon Province. By reading these records, I learned that they settled in their own hometowns, 7and that they had come with Zerubbabel, Joshua, Nehemiah, Azariah, Raamiah, Nahamani, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispereth, Bigvai, Nehum, and Baanah.
8-25This is a list of how many returned from each family group: 2,172 from Parosh; 372 from Shephatiah; 652 from Arah; 2,818 from Pahath Moab, who were all descendants of Jeshua and Joab; 1,254 from Elam; 845 from Zattu; 760 from Zaccai; 648 from Binnui; 628 from Bebai; 2,322 from Azgad; 667 from Adonikam; 2,067 from Bigvai; 655 from Adin; 98 from Ater, also known as Hezekiah; 328 from Hashum; 324 from Bezai; 112 from Hariph; and 95 from Gibeon.
26-38This is a list of how many returned whose ancestors had come from the following towns: 188 from Bethlehem and Netophah; 128 from Anathoth; 42 from Beth-Azmaveth; 743 from Kiriath-Jearim, Chephirah, and Beeroth; 621 from Ramah and Geba; 122 from Michmas; 123 from Bethel and Ai; 52 from Nebo; 1,254 from Elam; 320 from Harim; 345 from Jericho; 721 from Lod, Hadid, and Ono; and 3,930 from Senaah.
39-42This is a list of how many returned from each family of priests: 973 descendants of Jeshua from Jedaiah; 1,052 from Immer; 1,247 from Pashhur; and 1,017 from Harim.
43-45This is a list of how many returned from the families of Levites: 74 descendants of Hodevah from the families of Jeshua and Kadmiel; 148 descendants of Asaph from the temple musicians; and 138 descendants of Shallum, Ater, Talmon, Akkub, Hatita, and Shobai from the temple guards.
46-56These are the names of the families of temple workers whose descendants returned: Ziha, Hasupha, Tabbaoth, Keros, Sia, Padon, Lebana, Hagaba, Shalmai, Hanan, Giddel, Gahar, Reaiah, Rezin, Nekoda, Gazzam, Uzza, Paseah, Besai, Meunim, Nephushesim, Bakbuk, Hakupha, Harhur, Bazlith, Mehida, Harsha, Barkos, Sisera, Temah, Neziah, and Hatipha.
57-59Here are the names of Solomon's servants whose descendants returned: Sotai, Sophereth, Perida, Jaala, Darkon, Giddel, Shephatiah, Hattil, Pochereth Hazzebaim, and Amon.
60A total of 392 descendants of temple workers and of Solomon's servants returned.
61-62There were 642 who returned from the families of Delaiah, Tobiah, and Nekoda, though they could not prove they were Israelites. They had lived in the Babylonian towns of Tel-Melah, Tel-Harsha, Cherub, Addon, and Immer.
63-64The families of Hobaiah, Hakkoz, and Barzillai could not prove they were priests. The ancestor of the family of Barzillai had married the daughter of Barzillai from Gilead and had taken his wife's family name. But the records of these three families could not be found, and none of them were allowed to serve as priests. 65 In fact, the governor told them, “You cannot eat the food offered to God until he lets us know if you really are priests.”
66-69There were 42,360 who returned, in addition to 7,337 servants and 245 musicians, counting both men and women. Altogether, they brought with them 736 horses, 245 mules, 435 camels, and 6,720 donkeys.
70-72Many people gave gifts to help pay for the materials to rebuild the temple. The governor himself gave 8 kilograms of gold, 50 bowls to be used in the temple, and 530 robes for the priests. Family leaders gave 153 kilograms of gold and 1,458 kilograms of silver. The rest of the people gave 153 kilograms of gold, 1,325 kilograms of silver, and 67 robes for the priests.
73 And so, by the seventh month, priests, Levites, temple guards, musicians, workers, and many of the ordinary people had settled in the towns of Judah.
translation_text:
Bi nín làá nīn cí Jeerusaleem tiŋki puee
1Bi nín fātìi máń digundi ki dóòyee, ní m cóoǹ punuubi ní ki kāaǹ bipunyɔɔciitiliibi nì bi-laŋgaaliibi nì Leefii yab bi-tundin. 2M nìn kāaǹ m-nabiki Ananii ukàliŋkpil un làá nīn kpèé Jeerusaleem tiŋkee, ní ki nìn kāaǹ Ananiya un làá nīn kpèé sintil difɔkɔkuee. U nìn sá unil un pu bi cáá dimákalee, ki nìn fàŋkí Unimbɔti ki jítiǹ binib tikpil. 3M nìn yóoǹ-bi mara yii: «Kutaa yaa kaa wúntì ŋwìiń nyánnée, ní taa pìitī digundi punyɔmmu. Kujoouee, ní pìin̄ kí kpàl̄ mpunyɔmu kí wàatī ní bipunyɔɔciitiliibi ń nín búntí. Bin kóò Jeerusaleemee làá nīn yūlifí sintil, biba ń nīn yú ipaan in pu bi yóoǹ-bee, ní bin kíǹee ń nīn cí bi-diiŋŋi nyɔkɔpu.»
Juuda yab bin fātìi gítìńee
4Jeerusaleem nìn sá kitiŋkpaaŋŋi ki dɔ̄ ki cá ajan liitil pú, ní ki-nib kaa nìn náaǹ. Baa nìn dá láá fātìi máń adiin aba. 5Unimbɔti nìn dū nlandɔkɔ nee ki ŋá m-pɔbilin ḿ kpāfì abɔtibil nì bibɔsoonliibi nì samaa un kíǹee kí kàaǹ-bi. M nìn ká kugbɔŋu kun poon bi nìn ŋmàn̄ bin nìn nyánní kuyuŋu ki gítìń mpeepeekaaminee yiŋŋee, ní ki nìn ká an ŋmàn̄ ku-poon yii:
6«Juuda yab bin Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar nìn cúú kuyuŋu ki cūnnì Babiloonee, bin nìn gítìń Jeerusaleem nì Juuda timmu mun kíǹee poon báà ŋma fātìi kāl̀ u-tiŋkinee sèé. 7Bin di nìn līiń bi-nyɔkɔpuee di sá Sooroobabeel nì Yeesuwa nì Neeyeemiya nì Asariya nì Ramiya nì Naaman nì Mɔɔrdookayi nì Biilisan nì Miisipeereeti nì Biigifayi nì Neewum nì Baana.»
Isirayeel yab bininjab nyɔkɔm sɔ̀.
8Pareeyoosi maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib kutukub bili nì dilaataal nì binib binii kpá imuŋku inaa.
9Seefatiya maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib alaataa ata nì binib binii kpá imuŋku inaa.
10Araa maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib alaataa aluu nì binib binii kpá imuŋku ita.
11Paati-Moowaab maaliŋun yab, an dàkà yii Joosuwa nì Joowaab nib nìn sá binib kutukub bili nì alaataa anii nì binib saalku nì bita.
12Eelaam maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib kutuku ubɔ nì alaataa ali nì binib biluu kpá imuŋku ita.
13Saatuu maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib alaataa anii nì imuŋku ili nì binib biŋmoo.
14Sakayi maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib alaataa aluli nì binib imuŋku ita.
15Banii maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib alaataa aluu nì binib imuŋku ili nì binii.
16Beebaayi maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib alaataa aluu nì binib mmuŋku nì binii.
17Asigaadi maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib kutukub bili nì alaataa ata nì binib mmuŋku nì bili.
18Adooniikam maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib alaataa aluu nì binib imuŋku ita nì biluli.
19Biigifayi maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib kutukub bili nì binib imuŋku ita nì biluli.
20Adiini maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib alaataa aluu nì binib biŋmoo kpá imuŋku ita.
21Ateer maaliŋun yab, an dàkà yii Eeskiya yab nìn sá binib bili kpá dilaataal.
22Asuum maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib alaataa ata nì binib mmuŋku nì binii.
23Beesayi maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib alaataa ata nì binib mmuŋku nì binaa.
24Ariifi maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib dilaataal nì binib saalaa nì bili.
25Gabawɔn tiŋkin yab nìn sá binib biŋmoo kpá dilaataal.
26Beetileem nì Neetoofa timmun yab nìn sá binib dilaataal nì imuŋku inaa nì binib binii.
27Anatooti tiŋkin yab nìn sá binib dilaataal nì binib mmuŋku nì binii.
28Beeti-Asmafeeti tiŋkin yab nìn sá binib imuŋku ili nì binib bili.
29Kiiriyati-Yeeyariim nì Keefiira nì Beerooti timmun yab nìn sá binib alaataa aluli nì imuŋku ili nì binib bita.
30Raama nì Geeba timmun yab nìn sá binib alaataa aluu nì binib mmuŋku nì ubɔ.
31Miikimaasi tiŋkin yab nìn sá binib dilaataal nì binib mmuŋku nì bili.
32Beeteel nì Aayi timmun yab nìn sá binib dilaataal nì binib mmuŋku nì bita.
33Neeboo tiŋkin yab nìn sá binib binii kpá imuŋku ita.
34Eelaam ubɔ mun maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib kutuku ubɔ nì alaataa ali nì binaa kpá imuŋku ita.
35Ariim maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib alaataa ata nì binib mmuŋku.
36Jeeriikoo tiŋkin yab nìn sá binib alaataa ata nì imuŋku ili nì binib biŋmoo.
37Loodi nì Adiidi nì Oonoo timmun yab nìn sá binib alaataa aluli nì binib mmuŋku nì ubɔ.
38Seenaa tiŋkin yab nìn sá binib kutukub bita nì alaataa awa nì binib mmuŋku nì saalaa.
39Bisaraaŋaliibi kitilinee, Yeedaya maaliŋun yab, an dàkà yii Yeesuwa maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib alaataa awa nì binib biluli kpá imuŋku inaa.
40Imeer maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib kutuku ubɔ nì binib binii kpá imuŋku ita.
41Pasuur maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib kutuku ubɔ nì alaataa ali nì imuŋku ili nì binib biluli.
42Ariim maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib kutuku ubɔ nì binib saalku nì bili.
43Leefii yab kitilinee, Yeesuwa maaliŋun yab, an dàkà yii Oodeewa jipɔɔn Kadimiyeel yab nìn sá binib imuŋku ita nì unil ubɔ kpá saalku.
44Bilaŋgaaliibi kitilinee, Asaafi maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib dilaataal nì imuŋku ili nì binib binii.
45Bipunyɔɔciitiliibi kitilinee, Saaluum nì Ateer nì Talmɔn nì Akuub nì Atiita nì Soobayi maaliŋun yab nìn sá binib dilaataal nì binib bili kpá imuŋku ili.
46 kunimbɔtidii poon tɔntɔnliibi nín nìn pēē pēē mmaal puee di sá Siya nì Asufa nì Tabayooti nì 47Keeroosi nì Siiya nì Padɔn, 48nì Leebana nì Agaaba nì Salmayii, 49nì Anaani nì Giideel nì Gayaar 50nì Reeyaya nì Reesiin nì Neekooda 51nì Gaasaam nì Usa nì Paseeya 52nì Beesayi nì Meewuniim nì Neefiiseesiim 53nì Bakibuuki nì Akufa nì Aruuri, 54nì Basliiti nì Meeyida nì Arisa, 55nì Barkoosi nì Siseela nì Taama, 56nì Neesiya nì Atiifa yab.
57Saloomɔn tɔntɔnliibi nín nìn pēē pēē mmaal puee di sá Sootayi nì Soofeereeti nì Peeriida, 58nì Yaala nì Darkɔn nì Giideel, 59nì Seefatiya nì Atiil nì Pookeereeti-Aseebayiim nì Amɔn maaliŋun yab.
60Kunimbɔtidii poon tɔntɔnliibi nì Saloomɔn tɔntɔnliibi maaliŋun yab nìn kpáfì binib binii kpá alaataa anaa.
61Binib bin bí nee di nìn nyánní Teel-Meela nì Teel-Arisa nì Keerub-Adɔn nì Imeer timmun kaa nìn ŋúń ki béè yii bi-naanjab maaliŋun yab nì bi-nyeeŋŋu nìn baasii sá Isirayeel. 62Bíǹ di nìn sá Deelaya nì Toobiya nì Neekooda maaliŋun yab. Bi nìn sá binib alaataa aluu nì imuŋku ili nì binib bili.
63Bisaraaŋaliibi kansikinee, Yoobaya nì Akoosi nì Barsilayii maaliŋun yab mun nìn bí. Barsilayii gbanti di nìn cáá ugalaadija Barsilayii bisal ubɔ. An pu ní bi nìn dū diyindi gbanti ki pú-u. 64Binibee nìn nyàab̄ bi-naanjab yiŋŋi gbɔntin kaa ká. An puee bi nìn dū-bi ki yíiń bijɔkɔnnib ní ki nyántì-bi disaraaŋal tundin. 65Ní bi-gɔminau bí-bi yii bí taa ti jī tijin tin bi dūu ŋá saraa tì bí circir páaayee kí nīn cí usaraaŋakpil ubɔ ń dāá dū Uriim nì Tumiim kí bàlifì dibalifilee.
66Isirayeel yab bin kɔkɔ nìn nyánní kuyuŋu ki bāańee nìn sá binib kutukub imuŋku ili nì bili nì binib alaataa ata nì imuŋku ita ní. 67Bi-tɔntɔnliibi bininjab nì binimpoobi kaa nìn kútì. Bíǹ nìn sá binib kutukub biluli nì alaataa ata nì binib bita kpá imuŋku ili. Biwambɔɔliibi nì bilaŋgaaliibi bininjab nì binimpoobi nìn sá binib alaataa ali nì imuŋku ili nì binib biŋmoo. 68Bi nìn cáá igutaamu alaataa anaa nì iŋmoo kpá imuŋku ili nì mmamu kutukub biluu nì alaataa aluli nì mmuŋku. 69Adican kpilib nìn tīī tiwampɔkaal bí dūú tɔ̄ kunimbɔtidii tuuŋŋi. Gɔmina nìn tīī asindaariyakún kutuku ubɔ nì asambil ŋin poon bi ŋáań fatiku ki yàantée imuŋku ili nì saalaa, nì bisaraaŋaliibi bɔkutiŋ alaataa aŋmoo nì mmuŋku nì saalaa. 70Adican kpilib nín tīī tiwampɔkaal tin bí dūú tɔ̄ kunimbɔtidii tuuŋŋee kɔkɔ nyáń asindaariyakún kutukub mmuŋku nì animbil kúti kiiloobi kutuku ubɔ nì dilaataal. 71Isirayeel yab bin kíǹee mun tīī asindaariyakún kutukub mmuŋku nì animbil kúti kiiloobi kutuku ubɔ nì bisaraaŋaliibi bɔkutiŋ imuŋku ita nì aluli.
72«Míǹ boonee ní bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab nì bipunyɔɔciitiliibi nì bilaŋgaaliibi nì kunimbɔtidii poon tɔntɔnliibi nì Isirayeel yab bin kíǹee kɔkɔ fātìi kāl̀ bi-timmun.»
Eesiraasi kàan̄ Unimbɔti Marab samaa nimbiin
Dibindi poon ŋmaluluútiu bāańee, Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nìn kāl̀ bi-timmun.

english_text:
Ezra Reads God's Law to the People
1-2On the first day of the seventh month, the people came together in the open area in front of the Water Gate. Then they asked Ezra, who was a teacher of the Law of Moses, to read to them from this Law that the Lord had given his people. Ezra the priest came with the Law and stood before the crowd of men, women, and the children who were old enough to understand. 3From early morning till noon, he read the Law of Moses to them, and they listened carefully. 4Ezra stood on a high wooden platform that had been built for this occasion. Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah were standing to his right, while Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hash Baddanah, Zechariah, and Meshullam were standing to his left.
