5Ezra was up on the high platform, where he could be seen by everyone, and when he opened the book, all the people stood up. 6Ezra praised the great Lord God, and they lifted their hands, shouting “Amen! Amen!” Then they bowed with their faces to the ground and worshiped the Lord.
7-8After this, the Levites Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, and Pelaiah went among the people, explaining the meaning of what Ezra had read.
9The people started crying when God's Law was read to them. Then Nehemiah the governor, Ezra the priest and teacher, and the Levites who had been teaching the people all said, “This is a special day for the Lord your God. So don't be sad and don't cry!”
10Nehemiah told the people, “Enjoy your good food and wine and share some with those who didn't have anything to bring. Don't be sad! This is a special day for the Lord, and he will make you happy and strong.”
11The Levites encouraged the people by saying, “This is a sacred day, so don't worry or mourn!” 12When the people returned to their homes, they celebrated by eating and drinking and by sharing their food with those in need, because they had understood what had been read to them.
Celebrating the Festival of Shelters
13On the second day of the seventh month, the leaders of all the family groups came together with the priests and the Levites, so Ezra could teach them the Law 14 that the Lord had given to Moses. They learned from the Law that the people of Israel were to live in shelters when they celebrated the festival in the seventh month of the year. 15They also learned that they were to go into the woods and gather branches of leafy trees such as olives, myrtles, and palms for making these shelters.
16So the people gathered branches and made shelters on the flat roofs of their houses, in their yards, in the courtyard of the temple, and in the open areas around the Water Gate and Ephraim Gate. 17Everyone who had returned from Babylonia built shelters. They lived in them and joyfully celebrated the Festival of Shelters for the first time since the days of Joshua son of Nun. 18On each of the first seven days of the festival, Ezra read to the people from God's Law. Then on the eighth day, everyone gathered for worship, just as the Law had said they must.
translation_text:
1Samaa kɔkɔ nìn kóoǹ ki kpáfì ki ŋá kii unibaantee Jeerusaleem, Inyiŋfi punyɔkɔki nnimbiin pú. Bi nìn bí Eesiraasi un nyí Unimbɔti marab tiŋanee yii ú cáań kugbɔŋu kun Mooyiisi Marab bin ti-Dindaan nìn tīī Isirayeel yabee kēe. 2Usaraaŋal Eesiraasi nìn cáań kugbɔŋuee samaa kɔkɔ nimbiin. Bininjab nì binimpoobi nì mbiyaamu mun nìn ŋūǹ kí gbìl̄ tibɔti taapuee nìn kpáfì ki bí niin. An nìn sá uŋmaluluúti wimpeepeekaaŋu dal ní. 3Eesiraasi nìn yúl̀ Inyiŋfi punyɔkɔki nimbiin pú ki kàan̄ kugbɔŋu doooo kutaafaau ki cáa sāā kuwiŋkuluu bininjab nì binimpoobi nì bin kɔkɔ nìn pée ŋūǹ kí gbìl̄ tibɔti taapuee nimbiin. Báà ŋma nìn pée yú soooo ní ki pílifí bi nín bíi kàaǹ Marab gbɔŋku puee.
4Bi nìn dū idɔ ní ki ŋá dikɔl dikpafil gbanti pu, ní Eesiraasi un nyí Unimbɔti marab tiŋanee tɔ́kɔ́ di-pu. Bin nìn yú ki kɔ́ĺ-u ŋŋaŋgiil púee di sá Matatiya nì Seema nì Anaaya nì Uriya nì Ilikiya nì Maseeyawuu. Bin nìn yú u-ŋaŋgan púee di sá Peedaya nì Miikayeel nì Maalkiya nì Asuum nì Aseebadana nì Seekariya nì Meesulam. 5Eesiraasi nìn kpátì kugbɔŋu samaa kɔkɔ nimbilin, kun puee úǹ nìn tɔ́kɔ́ yilpu. Ŋyunti ŋun ní u kpátì kugbɔŋuee, samaa kɔkɔ nìn yíkìi yúl̀. 6Ní Eesiraasi jáam̀ ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti un sá ukpaanee, ní samaa kɔkɔ kíí yii: «Ameeni! Ameeni!» ki yōoǹ bi-ŋalii yilpu. Bi nìn gbāaǹ ti-Dindaan nimbiin ki jáam̀-u. 7Niinee ní Leefii yab Yeesuwa nì Banii nì Seereebiya nì Yaamiini nì Akuub nì Sabeetayi nì Oodiya nì Maseeyawuu nì Keeliita nì Asariya nì Yoosabaadi nì Anan nì Peelaya kíĺ ki bíi bɔ́bití marab taapu ki dàkà, ní samaa gbíntìi yú bi-paaŋyi pu. 8Bi nìn kàaǹ Unimbɔti marau gbɔŋku ki lèekī ajan kɔkɔ taapu ki cántí, án nín làá ŋá pu báà ŋma ń gbìl̄ tin bi kàan̄ee taapuee.
9Bi nín kàan̄ Unimbɔti marau gbɔŋku samaa gbìl̄ee, ní bi bíi sūǹ. Niinee, Neeyeemiya un sá gɔminee nì Eesiraasi un nyí Unimbɔti marab tiŋanee nì Leefii yab bin nìn bí ki lèekī taapu ki dàkèe bí yii: «Díǹ wiiŋŋu nee sá ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu wiiŋŋu ní. Ní taa nín̄ sūǹ kí nīn bí kunimbaaun.» 10Eesiraasi nìn gíti bí-bi yii: «Nín̄ kùm̀maan kí cùú ŋá tijimmɔntiil kí jī, kí nyɔ̀maan ndamɔntiim. Ní pɔ̄maan bin kaa ŋúń ki ŋá tijinee bí jī, kun puee díǹ wiiŋŋu nee sá ti-Dindaan wiiŋŋu ní. Ní taa nín̄ bí kunimbaaun, kun puee dipɔɔpindi din ti-Dindaan tììyee di sá ti-pɔŋŋu!» 11Ní Leefii yab bí ki ŋmēentí samaa ki lì yii: «Ní ŋmīĺmaan! Díǹ wiiŋŋu sá ti-Dindaan wiiŋŋu ní. Ní taa nín̄ bímaan kunimbaaun!»
12Niinee ní samaa kɔkɔ nìn nín kùǹ ki cūtìi jíń ki nyùn̄. Bi nìn tīī biwɔfib mun jíń ní ki ŋá jiŋaakpaan, kun puee bi nìn gbìl̄ tibɔti tin bi sòon̄ nì bee taapu.
Tibìń jiŋaaliu
13Kutaa wúntèe, Isirayeel dicaŋŋi kpilib nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab kóoǹ ki kpáfì Eesiraasi un nyí Unimbɔti marab tiŋanee cee kí mɔ̀tīí bīfì marabee taapu mmɔntiim. 14Bi nìn ká marab bin Unimbɔti yāntì Mooyiisi nìn ŋmàn̄ ki tīī-bee poon yii, tibìń jiŋaaliu un bi jīǹ uŋmaluluúti poonee, Isirayeel yab máaǹ kí nīn kóò tibìń poon ní, jiŋaal gbanti wiiŋyi kɔkɔ poon. 15An puee bi nìn báakì Jeerusaleem timmu kɔkɔ poon yii: «Nyāmaan kí jɔ̄m̀ ajoon pu kí bátímaan ɔliifi un bi kùn̄ee nì un nyáń kumoounee faati nì miirti faati nì tikpakpati nì isufi in cáá tifaapɔnee kí cáań tí gāā tibìń kii an nín ŋmàn̄ puee.»
16Niinee ní samaa nyáń ki cūtìi cáań nsupamu nì tifaal ki gāā tibìń bi-diiŋŋi nyɔkɔpu nì bi-mɔŋkii, nì kunimbɔtidii mɔŋkiŋu nì Inyiŋfi punyɔkɔki paaŋŋu pu, nì Eefiraayiim punyɔkɔki paaŋŋu pu. 17Bin kɔkɔ nìn kóoǹ ki kpáfì niinee, an dàkà yii bin kɔkɔ nìn nyánní kuyuŋu ki fātìńee nìn gāā tibìń ki kɔ́ ki bí niin. Doooo Nuuni jipɔɔn Joosuwa yuntiŋu ní Isirayeel yab kaa nìn gíti jíń jiŋaal gbanti. An puee bi nìn jíń jiŋaal gbanti ŋkpaamin nì ifaal ní. 18Kí yòon̄ jiŋaal wimpeekaaŋu kí cáá sāā ŋwinjoolkaa dalee, Eesiraasi nìn pée kàaǹ marab gbɔŋku ní baabadal. Bi jíń jiŋaal gbanti iwiin iluli, ní winnii dalee bi ŋá dikpafikpaandi, kii an nín ŋmàn̄ mara poon puee.

english_text:
The People Confess Their Sins
1On the twenty-fourth day of the seventh month, the people of Israel went without eating, and they dressed in sackcloth and threw dirt on their heads to show their sorrow. 2They refused to let foreigners join them, as they met to confess their sins and the sins of their ancestors. 3For three hours they stood and listened to the Law of the Lord their God, and then for the next three hours they confessed their sins and worshiped the Lord.
4Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Chenani stood on the special platform for the Levites and prayed aloud to the Lord their God. 5Then the Levites Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah said:
“Stand and shout praises
to your Lord,
the eternal God!
Praise his wonderful name,
though he is greater
than words can express.”
The People Pray
6You alone are the Lord,
Creator of the heavens
and all the stars,
Creator of the earth
and those who live on it,
Creator of the ocean
and all its creatures.
You are the source of life,
praised by the stars
that fill the heavens.
7 You are the Lord our God,
the one who chose Abram—
you brought him from Ur
in Babylonia
and named him Abraham.
8 Because he was faithful,
you made an agreement
to give his descendants
the land of the Canaanites
and Hittites,
of the Amorites and Perizzites,
and of the Jebusites
and Girgashites.
Now you have kept your promise,
just as you always do.
9 When our ancestors
were in Egypt,
you saw their suffering;
when they were at the Red Sea,
you heard their cry for help.
10 You knew that the King of Egypt
and his officials and his nation
had mistreated your people.
So you worked fearsome miracles
against the Egyptians
and earned a reputation
that still remains.
11 You divided the deep sea,
and your people walked through
on dry land.
But you tossed their enemies in,
and they sank down
like a heavy stone.
12 Each day you led your people
with a thick cloud,
and at night you showed the way
with a flaming fire.
13 At Sinai you came down
from heaven,
and you gave your people
good laws and teachings
that are fair and honest.
14You commanded them to respect
your holy Sabbath,
and you instructed
your servant Moses
to teach them your laws.
15 When they were hungry,
you sent bread from heaven,
and when they were thirsty,
you let water flow
from a rock.
Then you commanded them
to capture the land
that you had solemnly promised.
* 16 Our stubborn ancestors
refused to obey—
they forgot about the miracles
you had worked for them,
and they were determined
to return to Egypt
and become slaves again.
17 But, our God, you are merciful
and quick to forgive;
you are loving, kind,
and very patient.
So you never turned away
from them—
18 not even when they made
an idol shaped like a calf
and insulted you by claiming,
“This is the god who rescued us
from Egypt.”
19 Because of your great mercy,
you never abandoned them
in the desert.
And you always guided them
with a cloud by day
and a fire at night.
20Your gentle Spirit
instructed them,
and you gave them manna to eat
and water to drink.
21You took good care of them,
and for forty years
they never lacked a thing.
Their clothes didn't wear out,
and their feet were never swollen.
22 You let them conquer kings
and take their land,
including King Sihon of Heshbon
and King Og of Bashan.
23 You brought them into the land
that you had promised
their ancestors,
and you blessed their nation
with people that outnumbered
the stars in the sky.
24 Then their descendants
conquered the land.
You helped them defeat
the kings and nations
and treat their enemies
however they wished.
25 They captured strong cities
and rich farmland;
they took furnished houses,
as well as cisterns,
vineyards, olive orchards,
and numerous fruit trees.
They ate till they were satisfied,
and they celebrated
your abundant blessings.
26 In spite of this, they rebelled
and disobeyed your laws.
They killed your prophets,
who warned them
to turn back to you,
and they cursed your name.
27So you handed them over
to their enemies,
who treated them terribly.
But in their sufferings,
they begged you to help.
From heaven you listened
to their prayers
and because of your great mercy,
you sent leaders to rescue them.
28 But when they were at peace,
they would turn against you,
and you would hand them over
to their enemies.
Then they would beg for help,
and because you are merciful,
you rescued them
over and over again.
29 You warned them to turn back
and discover true life
by obeying your laws.
But they stubbornly refused
and continued to sin.
30 For years, you were patient,
and your Spirit warned them
with messages spoken
by your prophets.
Still they refused to listen,
and you handed them over
to their enemies.
31But you are merciful and kind,
and so you never forgot them
or let them be destroyed.
32 Our God, you are powerful,
fearsome, and faithful,
always true to your word.
So please keep in mind
the terrible sufferings
of our people, kings, leaders,
priests, and prophets,
from the time Assyria ruled
until this very day.
33You have always been fair
when you punished us
for our sins.
34Our kings and leaders,
our priests and ancestors
have never obeyed your commands
or heeded your warnings.
35You blessed them with a kingdom
and with an abundance
of rich, fertile land,
but they refused to worship you
or turn from their evil.
36Now we are slaves
in this fruitful land
you gave to our ancestors.
37Its plentiful harvest is taken
by kings you placed over us
because of our sins.
Our suffering is unbearable,
because they do as they wish
to us and our livestock.
The People Make an Agreement
38And so, a firm agreement was made that had the official approval of the leaders, the Levites, and priests.
translation_text:
Isirayeel yab mēē bi-kpitii pɔ̄tam pu
1Uŋmabaanti gbanti poon iwiin mmuŋku nì inaa dal ní Isirayeel yab dū kutukub ki pēeǹ, ki dū ntam ki pùkū bi-yiliŋ ní ki kpáfì ki bóob́ kinyɔkɔ. 2Bin nìn sá Isirayeel yabee nìn gāntì bi-ba nì bin kaa sée ní ki yúl̀ ki bīitì bi-kpitii nì bi-naanjab yìntitam pu. 3Bi nìn yíkìi yúl̀. Báà ŋma yú u-paaŋŋu pu mimmee, ní bi kàan̄ ti-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu marau gbɔŋku áli tikúti tita. Bi nìn dū tikúti tita mun ki gbāaǹ ti-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu nimbiin ki bīitì bi-kpitii pu.
4Leefii yab kɔl puee, Yeesuwa nì Banii nì Kaadimiyeel nì Seebaniya nì Bunii nì Seereebiya nì Banii nì Keenanii nìn yíkì ki mēē ti-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu mpɔn. 5Leefii yab Yeesuwa nì Kaadimiyeel nì Banii nì Asabineeya nì Seereebiya nì Oodiya nì Seebaniya nì Peetaya nìn téeń mpɔn yii: «Yīkìmaan! Nyɔ̄ŋkìmaan ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu, nyɔ̄ŋkìmaan-u ŋyunti kamaa!»
Neeyeemiya mēē samaa nimbiin
«Ti-Dindaan, báà ŋma ń nyɔ̄ŋkì
a-yindi din cáá tinyoolee!
A sá ukpaan ki jítiǹ ijaam nì inyɔŋki
in ŋūǹ kí nyā unil nyɔkɔnee.
6Sii baba di sá ti-Dindaan!
Sii di náań yilpu, yilpu fɔ́ŋŋŋ nì iŋmalbijaa kɔkɔ.
Sii di náań tiŋkub nì tin kɔkɔ bí bi-poonee.
Sii di tīī tin kɔkɔ pée bée kufoou,
ní iŋmalbijaa gbàantí a-nimbiin.
7Sii ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti di lēē Abram.
Sii di nyántìń-u Uur, Kaaldee yab tiŋkin
ní ki pú-u diyindi yii Abraam.
8A ká yii u yú nì si deedee nì dipɔbil diba,
ní a pūtì ki pōoǹ-u yii a làá dū Kanaan yab
nì Eeti yab nì Amɔɔr yab nì Peeriisi yab nì
Jeebusi yab nì Giirgaasi yab timmu kí tīī u-naantiibi.
A lafun ŋá míǹ, kun puee a sá deedeedaan.
9«A nìn ká falaa un poon ní
ti-naanjab nìn bí Eejipiti tiŋkinee,
ki nìn gbìl̄ bi nín nìn yúl̀ Tikati mɔɔl gbandi
ki kúuǹ ki yíiń-si á dāá jòoń-bee.
10A nìn ŋá maamaaci daanti nì atuŋkpaan
ki dàkā Faaroo nì u-kàliŋkpilib
nì u-tiŋki kɔkɔ nib,
kun puee a nìn nyí bi nín nìn sāaǹ
ti-naanjab dilambil poon puee.
Míǹ pu ní a nìn nyáń diyiŋkpaandi,
di bí ki dāa sāā díǹ.
11A nìn búkutì tiŋku nyim mili ti-naanjab nimbiin
ní bi dūtì ŋkulimmi.
A nìn téé bin nìn jìń-bee ki tɔ́ nnyimin,
ní bi múĺ taapu taapu kii ditaŋkpalee.
12A nìn yāntì ditagbancancaal kpòotī a-nibul ŋwiimpu,
ní kunyeeuee ditagbancancaalee kpántí ŋŋmi
ki ŋmíntí nsan ŋun pu bi nìn còom̄ee.
13A nìn kpákatìń Siinaayi jool pu
ki sòon̄ní-bi doooo yilpu.
A nìn tīī-bi abɔkpaa ŋin tèen̄ee,
a-dàkatam min sá ibaamɔnee
nì akoobil nì marab bin sá bimɔntiibee.
14A nìn dī a-tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisi pu
ki yāntì bi béè ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa ŋun bi dūu sú-see.
A nìn dàkā-bi marab nì akoobil nì a-dàkatam.
15A nìn yāntì tijin nyánní yilpu bi jíń ki díkí,
ki nìn yāntì nnyim nyáń ditaŋkpakpaandin
bi nyùn̄ nnyinnyoo kpíì.
A nìn bí-bi yii bí nīn cá kí fōō kitiŋ
kin a pūtì ki pōoǹ yii a làá tīī-bee.
16«Ama bíǹ ti-naanjab nìn yōoǹ bi-ba yilpu.
Bi nìn pɔ́ɔkì bi-pɔbiliŋ
ní kaa nìn tɔ́ a-marab.
17Bi nìn yíì kaa pílifiǹ-si.
Bi nìn súntì maamaaci tuŋkpaaŋŋi
ŋin a nìn ŋá ki tīī-bee pu.
Bi nìn pɔ́ɔkì bi-pɔbiliŋ
ní ki nìn ká nlandɔkɔ
kí fàtīí gítí Eejipiti tiŋkin,
laakin bi nìn bí kuyuŋunee.
Ama sii sá Unimbɔti un pūǹ ikpitee ní.
A-poon mɔ̄ ní a sá ulaŋŋaŋfiti.
Aa fòol̄ diŋuul malaa,
ní a-ŋanti wīikí tikpilku.
Aa nìn dū-bi ki fá,
18ki kpáaǹ gba ŋyunti ŋun bi nìn dūntì tikúti
ki dūu mɔ́ɔ́ dinabil ki bí yii:
<Kpèè a-Nimbɔtiu un nyántìń-si Eejipiti tiŋkinee sèéyee,>
bi nìn ŋá-si ikpitikpaan.
19Ama sii poon nín mɔ̄ee puee,
aa nìn dū-bi ki fá kuteeun.
Ditagbancancaal din nìn dàkà-bi nsan ŋwiimpuee
kaa nìn kākatì ki wāatì-bi,
ní ditagbancancaal din nìn kpántí ŋŋmi kunyeeu
ki ŋmíntí nsan ŋun bi nìn còom̄ee mun
nìn gbíntìi bí ki ŋmíntí-bi.
20A nìn tīī-bi a-fammɔntiim bí nīn nyí ki gàntī.
Aa nìn ŋmīntì-bi maana bí dūú kpíiǹ bi-ba,
kaa nìn tí ŋmīntì-bi nnyim bí dūú kpɔ̀ nnyinnyoo.
21Abin imuŋku ili ŋin bi nìn ŋá kuteeunee,
baa tiba kaa nìn lóò-bi.
Bi-wampeeŋkaati kaa nìn cátàaa,
bi-taaŋi mun kaa nìn díkí.
22«A nìn dū abee nì anibul ki ŋá bi-ŋaan.
A nìn yāntì bi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ
ntimu mun nì bi nìn cáá ŋkpaanyɔmuee,
an dàkà yii Eesbɔn bɔtiu Siiwɔn tiŋki
nì Baasan bɔtiu Ɔɔgi tiŋki.
23A nìn yāntì bi-naantiibi būtì kii
iŋmalbijaa in bí kutaa puee
ní ki cáá-bi ki kɔ́ǹ kitiŋ kin poon a nìn bí bi-naanjab yii
bí cùú fōō án kpántí bi-tiŋkee.
24Bi-naantiibi gbanti nìn cūtì ki fōō-kì kì kpántì bi-tiŋki.
A nìn yāntì Kanaan yab nìn sīntì bi-ba taapu ki tīī-bi
ní ki nìn dū-bi ki ŋá bi-ŋaan,
bi nì bi-bɔtiibi nì bi-samaau.
Ti-naanjab nìn ŋá-bi bi nín là puee.
25Bi nìn fōō ntimu mun bi nìn máń agun ki māntìi túee
nì tikpaatan tin cáá ntiŋkpamee.
Bi nìn fōō adiin ŋin poon tigaajati gbée,
nì lɔkɔb bin baa gbìn̄ee,
nì fiinyi nì ɔliifi sufii nì isufi in lòoǹ asubiŋmɔkaayee tikpil.
A-ŋanti puee, bi nìn jíń ki bál̀ bi nín là puee,
bi nìn jíń ki díkí, ki nɔ́ĺ
ní ki nìn kíǹ ki bí nnaam poon.
26«Ama nì míǹ kɔkɔee, bi nìn yíkì kaa kíí bi-ba pu,
ki nìn jáń nì si
ní ki fātì bi-boon ki tīī a-marab.
Bi nìn kūū a-bɔnaatiliibi
bin nìn bí ki sáŋkí-bi yii bí gítiń a-ceeyee.
Bi nìn ŋá-si ikpitikpaan.
27An puee a nìn dū-bi ki líiǹ bi-nannanliibi
bi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi.
Bi-nimbinaamandi poonee, bi nìn fáá mbiil yii á jòoń-bi,
ní a kāl̀ doooo yilpu ki gbìl̄.
A-neeŋkpaandi puee, a nìn tīiń-bi
binib bin nìn nyāntí-bi bi-nannanliibi ŋaanee.
28Ama bi yaa nìn fīī-bi míǹ bi-wunti sɔ̄ŋkèe,
ní bí fàtīí kíĺ ki bíi ŋáań-si ikpiti,
ní á fàtīí tí dū-bi ki líiǹ bi-nannanliibi.
Niinee ní bí tí fáá mbiil yii á jòoń-bi
ní á kàl̄ yilpu kí gbìl̄.
A-neeŋkpaandi puee,
a nìn fīī-bi míǹ ki líí ŋfunyɔm tikpil.
29A nìn kpáafì-bi bí gítiń kí nóó a-marab,
ama bi nìn ŋá dilambil kaa tɔ́ a-marab.
Bi nìn yīntiǹ abɔkpaa ŋin unil máaǹ kí nóó kí ŋmátée.
Bi nìn pɔ́ɔkì bi-pɔbiliŋ ki kpáá bi-tafaliŋ
kaa nìn pée là kí gbìl̄ tiba.
30«A nìn dū abin kupaau ki jíń kimɔtii bi-pu.
A nìn tīī a-bɔnaatiliibi a-Fam bi kpáafì-bi,
ama baa nìn pílifì.
An puee a nìn dū-bi ki líiǹ ntincamu nib.
31Nì míǹ kɔkɔ, a-neeŋkpaandi puee,
aa nìn yāntì bi nāaǹ-bi kɔkɔ,
kaa nìn dū-bi ki fá,
kun puee a sá Unimbɔti un poon mɔ̄
ki cáá kulaŋŋaŋfitiiuee ní.
32«Kɔŋkɔnnee ti-Nimbɔtiu,
Unimbɔti un sá ukpaan, ki cáá mpɔn,
ki sá kuwambiiuee,
sii un di ŋúb́ ipoon in a pūtì ki pōoǹ-tee nì deedeeyee,
taa lì yii kí yòon̄ Asuur yab bɔtiibi yuntiŋu ki cáa sāā ti-yuntiŋu nee,
falaa un ti nì ti-bɔtiibi nì ti-kpootiliibi nì ti-saraaŋaliibi
nì ti-bɔnaatiliibi nì ti-naanjab nì a-nibul kɔkɔ jíńee kaa ká-si.
33Tin kɔkɔ bāań-ti nee,
a ŋá-tì deedee nì mbaamɔn ní,
ama ní timbi ŋá tin kaa kítèe.
34Ti-bɔtiibi nì ti-kpootiliibi nì ti-saraaŋaliibi nì ti-naanjab
kaa nìn dū a-dàkatam ki túń ditundi,
kaa nìn fātìi tɔ́ a-marab
nì a-bɔti tin a nìn dūu kpáafì-bee.
35Bíǹ bin nìn kā bi-beelin,
ki cáá tiwammɔntiil tin kɔkɔ a nìn tīī-bee,
nì kitiŋ kin wāā ki cáá ntiŋkpam
a nìn cáá-bi ki kɔ́ǹ poonee,
baa nìn nóó-si,
kaa nìn fātì bi-boon ki tīī bi-tuŋkpitiŋ.
36Díǹ pu nee, ti kpántì iyumbu!
Ti kpántì iyumbu kitiŋ kin a nìn dūu tīī ti-naanjab
bí jī tiwammɔntiil tin kɔkɔ kì lòoǹee poon.
37Ti-kpitii puee, bin a kāaǹ bí nīn sá ti-bɔtiibee
di yì tijimmɔntiil tin kitiŋ gbanti lòoǹ tikpilee.
Bíǹ di yì timbi ti-ba nì ti-waŋkuti ki ŋáań min bi lèe.
Ti bí kunimbaakpaaŋŋu poon ní!»

english_text:
1As governor, I signed the agreement together with Zedekiah and the following priests: 2-8Seraiah, Azariah, Jeremiah, Pashhur, Amariah, Malchijah, Hattush, Shebaniah, Malluch, Harim, Meremoth, Obadiah, Daniel, Ginnethon, Baruch, Meshullam, Abijah, Mijamin, Maaziah, Bilgai, and Shemaiah.
9The Levites who signed were: Jeshua son of Azaniah, Binnui from the clan of Henadad, Kadmiel, 10Shebaniah, Hodiah, Kelita, Pelaiah, Hanan, 11Mica, Rehob, Hashabiah, 12Zaccur, Sherebiah, Shebaniah, 13Hodiah, Bani, and Beninu.
14The leaders who signed were: Parosh, Pahath Moab, Elam, Zattu, Bani, 15Bunni, Azgad, Bebai, 16Adonijah, Bigvai, Adin, 17Ater, Hezekiah, Azzur, 18Hodiah, Hashum, Bezai, 19Hariph, Anathoth, Nebai, 20Magpiash, Meshullam, Hezir, 21Meshezabel, Zadok, Jaddua, 22Pelatiah, Hanan, Anaiah, 23Hoshea, Hananiah, Hasshub, 24Hallohesh, Pilha, Shobek, 25Rehum, Hashabnah, Maaseiah, 26Ahiah, Hanan, Anan, 27Malluch, Harim, and Baanah.
The Agreement
28-29All of us, including priests, Levites, temple guards, singers, temple workers and leaders, together with our wives and children, have separated ourselves from the foreigners in this land and now enter into an agreement with a complete understanding of what we are doing. And so, we now place ourselves under the curse of the Lord our God, if we fail to obey his laws and teachings that were given to us by his servant Moses.
30 We won't let our sons and daughters marry foreigners.
31 We won't buy goods or grain on the Sabbath or on any other sacred day, not even from foreigners.
Every seven years we will let our fields rest, and we will cancel all debts.
32 Once a year we will each donate a small amount of silver to the temple of our God. 33This is to pay for the sacred bread, as well as for the daily sacrifices and special sacrifices such as those offered on the Sabbath and during the New Moon Festival and the other festivals. It will also pay for the sacrifices to forgive our sins and for all expenses connected with the worship of God in the temple.
34We have decided that the families of priests, Levites, and ordinary people will supply firewood for the temple each year, so that sacrifices can be offered on the altar, just as the Lord our God has commanded.
35 Each year we will bring to the temple the first part of our harvest of grain and fruit.
36 We will bring our first-born sons and the first-born males of our herds and flocks and offer them to the priests who serve in the temple, because this is what is written in God's Law.
37 To the priests in the temple of our God, we will bring the bread dough from the first harvest, together with our best fruit, and an offering of new wine and olive oil.
We will bring ten percent of our grain harvest to those Levites who are responsible for collecting it in our towns. 38 A priest from the family of Aaron must be there when we give this to the Levites. Then the Levites will put one tenth of this part in the temple storeroom, 39which is also the place for the sacred objects used by the priests, the temple guards, and the singers.
Levites and everyone else must bring their gifts of grain, wine, and olive oil to this room.
We will not neglect the temple of our God.
translation_text:
Samaa lēē kí nóó marab nì dipɔbil diba
1Tin bāań-ti nee puee, ti lēē nì dipɔbil diba kí nóó marab. Ti làá ŋmà kí ŋá kugbɔŋu poon ní ti-kpootiliibi nì Leefii yab nì ti-saraaŋaliibi ń nyīī ŋŋal. 2Binib bin nìn nyīī ŋŋalee yiŋŋi sèé.
- Akaliya jipɔɔn Neeyeemiya un sá gɔminee nì Sideekiya, 3nì Seeraya nì Asariya nì Yiirmeeya, 4nì Pasuur nì Amariya nì Maalkiya, 5nì Atuusi nì Seebaniya nì Maluuki 6nì Ariim nì Meereemooti nì Oobadiya, 7nì Daniyeel nì Giineetɔn nì Baruuki, 8nì Meesulam nì Abiiya nì Miiniyaamiini, 9nì Maasiya nì Biiligayi nì Seemaya. Bíǹ kɔkɔ nìn sá bisaraaŋaliibi ní.
- 10Leefii yab yiŋŋi sèé. Asaniya jipɔɔn Yeesuwa nì Biinuyii un sá Eenadaadi maaliŋunee nì Kadimiyeel 11nì bi-nabiyaamu Seebaniya nì Oodiya nì Keeliita nì Peelaya nì Anan, 12nì Miika nì Reewoob nì Asabiya, 13nì Sakuur nì Seereebiya nì Seebaniya, 14nì Oodiya nì Banii nì Beeniinuu.
15Adican kpilib bin nìn nyīī ŋŋalee sèé. Pareeyoosi nì Paati-Moowaab nì Eelaam nì Saatuu nì Banii, 16nì Buunii nì Asigaadi nì Beebaayi, 17nì Adooniya nì Biigifayi nì Adiini, 18nì Ateer nì Isikiya nì Asuur, 19nì Oodiya nì Asuum nì Beesayi, 20nì Ariifi nì Anatooti nì Neebaayi, 21nì Magipiyaasi nì Meesulam nì Eesiir, 22nì Meeseesaabeel nì Saadooki nì Yaduwa, 23nì Peelatiya nì Anan nì Anaaya, 24nì Ooseeya nì Ananiya nì Asuub, 25nì Alooweesi nì Piileeya nì Soobeeki, 26nì Reewum nì Asaabina nì Maseeyawuu 27nì Ayiiya nì Anan nì Aanan 28nì Maluuki nì Ariim nì Baana.
29Isirayeel yab bin nìn kíǹee nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab nì bipunyɔɔciitiliibi nì bilaŋgaaliibi nì kunimbɔtidii poon tɔntɔnliibi, nì bin kɔkɔ nìn gāntì bi-ba nì ntimu mun kíǹee nib ki nóó Unimbɔti marabee, ki kpáaǹ bi-nimpoobi nì bi-jipɔmbi nì bi-bisalib nì bin kɔkɔ nìn ŋūǹ kí gbìl̄ tibɔti taapuee nìn kútì bi-pu. 30Bi-kɔkɔ nìn kíí ki tɔ́kɔǹ bi-nabiyaamu mun pu bi máká tikpilee nín sòon̄ tiŋyee pu. Bi nìn lēē nì dipɔbil diba, ki pūtì ki pōoǹ yii bi làá nīn nóó marab bin Unimbɔti nìn tīī u-tɔntɔnliu Mooyiisee, án nín làá ŋá pu tí ŋmā kí ŋá kii ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu marab kɔkɔ nì u-bɔkpaaŋi nì u-koobiliŋ nín bí yii tí ŋá puee.
31An puee taa ti làá dū ti-bisalib kí tīī kitiŋ nee nib ticati, míǹ ní kaa làá tí yòon̄ bi-bisalib kí tīī ti-jipɔmbi ticati. 32Kitiŋ nee nib yaa cáań bi-nyampuwanti àá tijin tin an yaa pée sée ki nyáfí ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dal nì ti-jiŋaalib wiiŋyi dalee, taa làá dā. Abin aluli kamaayee, ti làá yàntī ti-kpaatanti ń dòon̄ kí ŋùŋfì, ní kí dū apɔɔn ŋin binib cáá-tee kí pɔ̄-bi. 33Ti gíí ti-ba dipɔndi kí nīn tìì dibindi kamaa animbil graambi binaa bí nīn cáa tūǹ ti-Nimbɔtiu diiku poon tuuŋŋi. 34Animbilee ní bi làá nīn cáa dāā kpɔnɔb bin bi pāantí ti-Dindaan nimbiinee, nì tijimpin saraabi bin bi ŋáań kutaa kamaayee, nì saraawɔkaa un bi ŋáań kutaa kamaayee, nì saraabi bin bi ŋáań ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dal nì uŋmapɔɔn nì jiŋaalib bin kíǹee wiiŋyee, nì tin kɔkɔ bi dūu sú ti-Dindaanee, nì Isirayeel yab kpitii pɔ̄tam saraabi, nì tin kɔkɔ pée sá bí nīn cáa kpèé ti-Nimbɔtiu diiku ŋāŋkitamee. 35Timbi bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab nì samaa un kíǹee, ti tɔ́ kasi kí kpèè ŋyunti ŋun ní kudicaŋu kamaa máaǹ kí cáań idɔ ti-Nimbɔtiu diikunee. Di sá yii dibindi kamaa, ŋyunti ŋun bi síiǹee yaa bàn̄ee, ti làá cáań idɔ in an bàlifēe bí nīn cáa kpà ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu saraafaŋŋu pu ŋŋmi, kii an nín ŋmàn̄ marab gbɔŋkun poon puee. 36Míǹ ní ti làá nīn tí cāabìń ti-tiŋki jincɔ̀fikaati nì busubu kamaa nín lòoǹ abil ŋiŋyee apeekaa dibintil kamaa ti-Dindaan diikun. 37Ti làá gíti cáań ti-biseebiyaamu nninjabiyaamu nì ti-waŋkuti biseemaliŋ, kii an nín ŋmàn̄ marab gbɔŋkun poon puee. Ti làá cáá ti-naai nì ti-piii nì ti-ŋoobui biseemaliŋ kí cùnnì ti-Nimbɔtiu diikun kí tīī bisaraaŋaliibi bin bí niin ki tūǹ ti-Dindaan tundee. 38Kí kūtèe, ti làá cáań bukpɔnɔsaa bun ti péé péé ki nùkūee nì dijandi din ti lèekī ti-saraabi poon ki tìì Unimbɔtee nì ti-sufii kɔkɔ subiliŋ apeepeekaa nì ti-dapɔm nì ti-kpam ti-Nimbɔtiu Diiku dibiyaamu mun poon bi sīintí tijinee kí tīī bisaraaŋaliibi. Ti lēē ti-kpaajinti poon tisaalaatiil kí tīī Leefii yab. Bíǹ bi-ba làá dāan̄ ntimu mun kɔkɔ poon ti bí ki tūǹ ditundee kí fōō tisaalaatiil gbanti. 39Leefii yab yaa cá kí fōoń tisaalaatiilee, usaraaŋal un sá Aarɔn maaliŋu poonee ń céeǹ-bi. Leefii yab làá lēē tisaalaatiil gbanti saalaatiiti kí tīī ti-Nimbɔtiu diiku bí cáań kí síiń kunimbɔtidii dibiyaamu mun poon bi yōontí tijinee. 40Di sá yii ndibiyaamu gbanti poon ní Isirayeel yab nì Leefii yab làá nīn cāabìń bilee nì ndapɔm nì ŋkpam saraabi ki yōontí. Niin ní circir kɔŋkooŋŋu wanti nì bisaraaŋaliibi bin bí ditundinee nì bipunyɔɔciitiliibi nì bilaŋgaaliibi bí.
Ti yaa ŋá mimmee, taa féeń ti-Nimbɔtiu diiku.

english_text:
People Who Settled in Jerusalem
1The nation's leaders and their families settled in Jerusalem. But there was room for only one out of every ten of the remaining families, and so they asked God to show them who would live there. 2Then everyone else asked God to bless those who were willing to live in Jerusalem.
3 Some of the people of Israel, the priests, the Levites, the temple workers, and the descendants of Solomon's servants lived on their own property in the towns of Judah. But the leaders of the province lived in Jerusalem with their families.
The Judah Tribe
4-6From the Judah tribe, two leaders settled in Jerusalem with their relatives. One of them was Athaiah son of Uzziah. His ancestors were Zechariah, Amariah, Shephatiah, Mahalalel, and Perez, the son of Judah. From the descendants of Perez, 468 of the best men lived in Jerusalem.
The other leader from Judah was Maaseiah the son of Baruch. His ancestors were Colhozeh, Hazaiah, Adaiah, Joiarib, Zechariah, and Shelah, the son of Judah.
The Benjamin Tribe
7-8From the Benjamin tribe, three leaders settled in Jerusalem. The first was Sallu son of Meshullam, and the others were Gabbai and Sallai. Sallu's ancestors were Joed, Pedaiah, Kolaiah, Maaseiah, Ithiel, and Jeshaiah. Altogether, there were 928 men of the Benjamin tribe living in Jerusalem. 9Joel son of Zichri was their leader, and Judah son of Hassenuah was second in command.
Priests
10Four priests settled in Jerusalem. The first was Jedaiah; he was the son of Joiarib and the uncle of Jachin.
11The second priest to settle there was Seraiah son of Hilkiah. His ancestors were Meshullam, Zadok, Meraioth, and Ahitub, who had been a high priest. 12Altogether, there were 822 from his clan who served in the temple.
The third priest to settle there was Adaiah son of Jeroham. His ancestors were Pelaliah, Amzi, Zechariah, Pashhur, and Malchijah. 13Altogether, there were 242 clan leaders among his relatives.
The fourth priest to settle there was Amashsai son of Azarel. His ancestors were Ahzai, Meshillemoth, and Immer. 14Altogether, there were 128 brave warriors from their clans, and their leader was Zabdiel son of Haggedolim.
Levites
15Several Levites settled in Jerusalem. First, there was Shemaiah son of Hasshub. His ancestors were Azrikam, Hashabiah, and Bunni.
16Next, there were Shabbethai and Jozabad, the Levite leaders in charge of the work outside the temple.
17Then there was Mattaniah son of Mica. His ancestors were Zabdi and Asaph. Mattaniah led the temple choir in the prayer of praise. Bakbukiah, who also settled in Jerusalem, was his assistant.
Finally, there was Abda son of Shammua; his grandfather was Galal, and his great-grandfather was Jeduthun.
18Altogether, 284 Levites settled in the holy city.
Temple Guards and Others
19One hundred seventy-two temple guards settled in Jerusalem; their leaders were Akkub and Talmon.
20The rest of the Israelites, including priests and Levites, lived on their own property in the other towns of Judah. 21But the temple workers lived in the section of Jerusalem known as Ophel, and the two men in charge of them were Ziha and Gishpa.
22Uzzi son of Bani was the leader of the Levites in Jerusalem. His grandfather was Hashabiah, his great-grandfather was Mattaniah, and his great-great-grandfather was Mica. He belonged to the Asaph clan that was in charge of the music for the temple services, 23though the daily choice of music and musicians was decided by royal decree of the Persian king.
24The people of Israel were represented at the Persian court by Pethahiah son of Meshezabel from the Zerah clan of the Judah tribe.
The People in the Other Towns and Villages
25Some of the people of Judah lived in the following towns near their farms: Kiriath-Arba, Dibon, Jekabzeel, 26Jeshua, Moladah, Beth-Pelet, 27Hazar-Shual, Beersheba, 28Ziklag, Meconah, 29Enrimmon, Zorah, Jarmuth, 30Zanoah, Adullam, Lachish, and Azekah. In fact, they settled the towns from Beersheba in the south to Hinnom Valley in the north.
31The people of Benjamin lived in the towns of Geba, Michmash, Aija, Bethel with its nearby villages, 32Anathoth, Nob, Ananiah, 33Hazor, Ramah, Gittaim, 34Hadid, Zeboim, Neballat, 35Lod, and Ono, as well as in Craft Valley. 36Several groups of Levites from the territory of Judah were sent to live among the people of Benjamin.
translation_text:
Juuda yab bin fātìi gítìń ki kāl̀ Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee
1Samaa kpilib nìn kóò Jeerusaleem ní. Bi nìn tɔ́ kasi samaa un kíǹee pu kí lēē binib saalaa kamaa poonee, unil ubɔ ú cùú nīn kóò Jeerusaleem, circir tiŋkin, ní binib biwa bin kíǹee ń gbíntí kí nīn kóò ntimu mun kíǹee poon. 2Samaa nìn mēē ki bīiǹ bin kɔkɔ nìn lēē bi-pɔbilin yii bi làá cù kí nīn kóò Jeerusaleemee pu.
3Isirayeel yab nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab nì kunimbɔtidiin tɔntɔnliibi nì Saloomɔn tɔntɔnliibi naantiibi di nìn kóò Juuda tiŋkin. Báà ŋma nìn kóò u-tiŋkin laakin u nìn yèe ní. Juuda timmu mun kíǹee kpilib bin nìn dɔ́miń ki kóò Jeerusaleemee yiŋŋi sɔ̀. 4Juuda yab nì Beenjameen yab biba mun nìn dɔ́miń ki kóò Jeerusaleem.
Juuda yab kansikinee, Peereesi maaliŋun yab di sá Usiyaa jipɔɔn Ataaya, u-naanjab sá Seekariya nì Amariya nì Seefatiya nì Maalaleeyeel. 5Maseeyawuu mun nìn bí, u-naanjab sá Kool-Ooseeya nì Asaaya nì Adaaya nì Yooyariib nì Seekariya nì Asiloonii. 6Peereesi maaliŋun yab bisaraaŋaliibi bin nìn dɔ́miń ki kóò Jeerusaleemee nìn nyáń binib alaataa anaa nì imuŋku ita nì binib binii.
7Beenjameen yab kansikin ubɔ di sá Meesulam jipɔɔn Saluu. U-naanjab di sá Yooweedi nì Peedaya nì Koolaya nì Maseeyawuu nì Itiyeel nì Yeesaya. 8Bin kíǹee di sá Gabayi nì Salayi. Bi-kɔkɔ nìn nyáń binib alaataa awa nì binib mmuŋku nì binii. 9Sikirii jipɔɔn Jooweel di nìn sá bi-kpiliu, ní Aseenuwa jipɔɔn Juuda sá kitiŋee kpiliu taapu yɔu.
10Bisaraaŋaliibi kansikinee, bin nìn bée di sá Yooyariib jipɔɔn Peedaya, nì Yakiin 11nì Ilikiya jipɔɔn Seeraya. Seeraya gbanti naanjab di sá Meesulam nì Sadooki nì Meerayooti nì bin kpèé kunimbɔtidiiyee kpiliu Ayiituub, 12nì bi-nabiyaamu binib alaataa anii nì mmuŋku nì bili bin di bí kunimbɔtidiin ki tūǹ atuunee. Yeeroowaam jipɔɔn Adaaya mun nìn bí. U-naanjab di sá Peelaliya nì Amisii nì Seekariya nì Pasuur nì Maalkiya, 13nì u-nabiyaamu bin sá adican kpilibee binib alaataa ali nì imuŋku ili nì binib bili. Asaareeyeel jipɔɔn Amasaayi mun nìn bí. U-naanjab di sá Asayi nì Meesileemooti nì Imeer, 14nì bi-nabiyaamu bibaatandambi binib dilaataal nì binib mmuŋku nì binii. Ageedooliim jipɔɔn Sabidiyeel di nìn sá bi-kpiliu.
15Leefii yab kansikinee, bin nìn bée ubɔ di sá Asuub jipɔɔn Seemaya. U-naanjab di sá Asiirikam nì Asabiya nì Bunii 16nì Sabeetayi nì Yoosabaadi bin nìn sá Leefii yab kpilib kansikin biba ní ki nìn kpèé kunimbɔtidii boon tuuŋŋee mun nìn bí. 17Miika jipɔɔn Mataniya mun nìn bí. U-naanjab di sá Sabidii nì Asaafi un di nìn tōontí inyɔŋki laŋyi ŋwimmeem yuntiŋuee, nì u-nabiki Bakibukiya un nìn sá u-taapu yɔuee nì Samuwa jipɔɔn Abidaa. Úǹ naanjab di sá Galaal nì Yeedutun. 18Leefii yab bin nìn kóò Circir tiŋkinee nìn sá binib alaataa ali nì imuŋku inaa nì binib binaa.
19Bipunyɔɔciitiliibi kansikinee, bi nìn bée di sá Akuub nì Talmɔn nì bi-dicaŋŋin yab. Bi nìn sá binib dilaataal nì binib binii kpá imuŋku inaa.
20Isirayeel yab bin kíǹee nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab nìn cūtìi kāl̀ bi-tinjaŋŋin Juuda timmu mun kíǹee poon. 21Kunimbɔtidii poon tɔntɔnliibi nìn kóò Oofeel, Jeerusaleem tiŋgbaŋkin ní. Siiya nì Giiseepa di nìn sá bi-kpilib.
22Un nìn sá Leefii yab kpiliu Jeerusaleemee di sá Banii jipɔɔn Uusi. U-naanjab di sá Asabiya nì Mataniya nì Miika. U nìn sá kunimbɔtidiin laŋgaaliibi ubɔ ní Asaafi maaliŋun. 23Ubɔti nìn yóoǹ bilaŋgaaliibi gbanti mara ní ki nìn bɔ́ntì bi nín làá nīn tūǹ dilaŋgaal tundi pu ŋwiin kamaa puee ki tīī-bi.
24Meeseesaabeel jipɔɔn Peetaya un sá Juuda jipɔɔn, Seera maaliŋunee di nìn bí Peeriisi yab bɔtiu cee ki kpèé Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ bɔti.
Juuda yab bin kaa nìn kóò Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee
25Ntimbilimu mun bí tisatinee jaaŋŋu púee, Juuda yab biba nìn kóò Kiiriyati-Ariba nì ki-timbilimmun nì Diibɔn nì ki-timbilimmun nì Yeekabiseel nì ki-timbilimmun, 26nì Yeesuwa nì Moolada nì Beeti-Peeleeti, 27nì Asaar-Suwaal nì Beerseeba nì ki-timbilimmun, 28nì Siikilaagi nì Meekoona nì ki-timbilimmun, 29nì Eeni-Riimɔn nì Soora nì Yaarmuti, 30nì Sanoowa nì Adulaam nì ki-timbilimmu nì Lakiisi nì ki-timbilimmun nì Aseeka nì ki-timbilimmun. Bi nìn kāl̀ kí yòon̄ Beerseeba kí cáá sāā Inoom tantakalin.
31Beenjameen naakookun yab nìn kāl̀ kí yòon̄ Geeba kí nīn cá doooo Miikimaasi nì Aya nì Beeteel nì ki-timbilimmun, 32nì Anatooti nì Noob nì Ananiya 33nì Asɔɔr nì Raama nì Giitayiim, 34nì Adiidi nì Seebooyiim nì Neebalati, 35nì Loodi nì Oonoo nì Iŋal pu tɔntɔnliibi tantakal.
36 Leefii yab kansikinee, biba nìn yíkì Juuda yab timmun ki cūtìi kóò Beenjameen yab cee.

english_text:
A List of Priests and Levites
1Many priests and Levites had returned from Babylonia with Zerubbabel and Joshua as their leaders. Those priests were Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra, 2Amariah, Malluch, Hattush, 3Shecaniah, Rehum, Meremoth, 4Iddo, Ginnethoi, Abijah, 5Mijamin, Maadiah, Bilgah, 6Shemaiah, Joiarib, Jedaiah, 7Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, and another Jedaiah. These were the leading priests and their assistants during the time of Joshua.
8The Levites who returned were Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah. They and their assistants were responsible for the songs of praise, 9while Bakbukiah and Unno, together with their assistants, were responsible for the choral responses.
Descendants of Joshua the High Priest
10Joshua was the father of Joiakim, the grandfather of Eliashib, and the great-grandfather of Joiada. 11Joiada was the father of Jonathan and the grandfather of Jaddua.
Leaders of the Priestly Clans
12When Joiakim was high priest, the following priests were leaders of their clans: Meraiah of the Seraiah clan, Hananiah of Jeremiah, 13Meshullam of Ezra, Jehohanan of Amariah, 14Jonathan of Malluchi, Joseph of Shebaniah, 15Adna of Harim, Helkai of Meraioth, 16Zechariah of Iddo, Meshullam of Ginnethon, 17Zichri of Abijah, Piltai of Moadiah, 18Shammua of Bilgah, Jehonathan of Shemaiah, 19Mattenai of Joiarib, Uzzi of Jedaiah, 20Kallai of Sallai, Eber of Amok, 21Hashabiah of Hilkiah, and Nethanel of Jedaiah.
The Priestly and Levite Families
22During the time of the high priests Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua, and including the time that Darius was king of Persia, a record was kept of the heads of the Levite and priestly families. 23However, no official record was kept of the heads of the Levite clans after the death of Johanan, the grandson of Eliashib.
24Hashabiah, Sherebiah, Jeshua son of Kadmiel, and their assistants organized two choirs of Levites to offer praises to God, just as King David, the man of God, had commanded.
25Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were responsible for guarding the storerooms near the temple gates.
26All of these men lived during the time of Joiakim and during the time that I was governor and Ezra, a teacher of the Law of Moses, was priest.
Nehemiah Dedicates the City Wall
27When the city wall was dedicated, Levites from everywhere in Judah were invited to join in the celebration with songs of praise and with the music of cymbals, small harps, and other stringed instruments. 28-29The Levite singers lived in villages around Jerusalem, and so they came from there, as well as from the villages around Netophah, Beth-Gilgal, Geba, and Azmaveth. 30The priests and Levites held special ceremonies to make themselves holy, and then they did the same for the rest of the people and for the gates and walls of the city.
31I brought the leaders of Judah to the top of the city wall and put them in charge of the two groups that were to march around on top of the wall, singing praises to God. One group marched to the right in the direction of Garbage Gate. 32Hoshaiah and half of the leaders followed them. 33Then came the priests Azariah, Ezra, Meshullam, 34Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, and Jeremiah, 35all of them blowing trumpets. Next, there was Zechariah of the Asaph clan 36and his relatives, Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani. They played musical instruments like those that had been played by David, the man of God. And they marched behind Ezra, the teacher of the Law. 37When they reached Fountain Gate, they climbed the steps to David's City and went past his palace, before stopping at the Water Gate near the eastern wall of the city.
38The second group of singers marched along the wall in the opposite direction, and I followed them, together with the other half of the leaders of Judah. We went past Oven Tower, Broad Wall, 39Ephraim Gate, Old Gate, Fish Gate, Hananel Tower, Hundred Tower, and on to Sheep Gate. Finally, we stopped at Gate of the Guard, 40where we stood in front of the temple with the other group, praising God. In the group with me were half of the leaders, 41as well as the priests Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah, who were blowing trumpets. 42Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer also stood there, as Jezrahiah led the singers. 43God had made the people very happy, and so on that day they celebrated and offered many sacrifices. The women and children joined in the festivities, and joyful shouts could be heard far from the city of Jerusalem.
Preparation for Worship
44On that same day, some leaders were appointed to be responsible for the safekeeping of gifts for the temple and to be in charge of receiving the first part of the harvest and the ten percent of the crops and livestock that was offered to God. These same leaders also collected the part of crops that the Law of Moses taught was to be given to the Levites.
Everyone was pleased with the work of the priests and Levites, 45 when they performed the ceremonies to make people acceptable to worship God. And the singers and the temple guards did their jobs according to the instructions given by David and his son Solomon. 46In fact, ever since the days of David and Asaph, there had been song leaders and songs of praise and worship. 47During the time that Zerubbabel and I were in charge, everyone in Israel gave what they were supposed to give for the daily needs of the singers and temple guards from the Levi tribe. Then the Levites would give the priests their share from what they had received.
translation_text:
Bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab yiŋŋi
1Bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab bin nìn nóoń Saltiyeel jipɔɔn Sooroobabeel nì Yeesuwa ki nyánní kuyuŋu ki fātìńee di sá Seeraya nì Yiirmeeya nì Eesiraasi, 2nì Amariya nì Maluuki nì Atuusi, 3nì Seekaniya nì Reewum nì Meereemooti, 4nì Idoo nì Giineetɔyi nì Abiiya, 5nì Miiniyaamiini nì Maadiya nì Biiliga, 6nì Seemaya nì Yooyariib nì Yeedaya, 7nì Saluu nì Amooki nì Ilikiya nì Yeedaya. Yeesuwa yuntiŋuee, bíǹ nì bi-nabiyaamu di nìn sá bisaraaŋaliibi kpilib. 8Leefii yab kansikinee, bin nìn bée di sá Yeesuwa nì Binuyii nì Kadimiyeel nì Seereebiya nì Yeewuda nì Mataniya. Mataniya nì u-nabiyaamu di nìn kpòotī inyɔŋki laŋyi. 9Bakibukiya nì Unii, bi-nabiyaamu di nìn yú ki túĺ-bi ki kíikí ilan.
10Yeesuwa di màl̄ Yooyakiim, ní Yooyakiim màl̄ Eeliyasiib, ní Eeliyasiib màl̄ Yooyadaa, 11ní Yooyadaa màl̄ Joonatan, ní Joonatan màl̄ Yaduwa.
12Ŋyunti ŋun Yooyakiim sá usaraaŋakpilee, bin nìn sá bisaraaŋaliibi dicaŋkpilibee sɔ̀. Seeraya dicaŋkunee, Meeraya di nìn sá ukpil. Yiirmeeya dicaŋkunee, Ananiya di nìn sá ukpil. 13Eesiraasi dicaŋkunee, Meesulam di nìn sá ukpil. Amariya dicaŋkunee, Yoowanan di nìn sá ukpil. 14Meeliiku dicaŋkunee, Joonatan di nìn sá ukpil. Seebaniya dicaŋkunee, Jooseefi di nìn sá ukpil. 15Ariim dicaŋkunee, Adina di nìn sá ukpil. Meerayooti dicaŋkunee, Eelkayi di nìn sá ukpil. 16Idoo dicaŋkunee, Sakari di nìn sá ukpil. Giineetɔn dicaŋkunee, Meesulam di nìn sá ukpil. 17Abiiya dicaŋkunee, Sikirii di nìn sá ukpil. Miiniyaamiini dicaŋkunee. Moowadiya dicaŋkunee, Piiltayi di nìn sá ukpil. 18Biiliga dicaŋkunee, Samuwa. Seemaya dicaŋkunee, Joonatan di nìn sá ukpil. 19Yooyariib dicaŋkunee, Mateenayi di nìn sá ukpil. Yeedaya dicaŋkunee, Uusi di nìn sá ukpil. 20Salayi dicaŋkunee, Kalayi di nìn sá ukpil. Amooki dicaŋkunee, Eebeer di nìn sá ukpil. 21Ilikiya dicaŋkunee, Asabiya di nìn sá ukpil. Ní Yeedaya dicaŋkunee, Neetaneeyeel di nìn sá ukpil.
22Eeliyasiib nì Yooyadaa nì Yoowanan nì Yaduwa yuntiŋu ní bi nìn ŋmàn̄ Leefii yab dicaŋŋi kpilib nì bisaraaŋaliibi yiŋŋi ki tin cáa sāā Peeriisi yab bɔtiu Daariyusi yuntiŋu.
23Bi nìn ŋmàn̄ Leefii yab dicaŋŋi kpilib yiŋŋi ki ŋá kugbɔŋu kun poon bi ŋmà tin jītí ŋwiin kamaayee ki tin sāā Eeliyasiib naantiiu Yoowanan yuntiŋu.
24Leefii yab kpilib di nìn sá Asabiya nì Seereebiya nì Kadimiyeel jipɔɔn Yeesuwa. Bi-nabiyaamu nìn yú ki túĺ-bi, ní ki gà ilan ki fòol̄ tɔb ki nyɔ́ŋkí ti-Dindaan ki pàkà-u, kii Unimbɔti niliu Daafiidi nín nìn síiǹ mara bí nīn ŋáań puee.
25Bipunyɔɔciitiliibi Mataniya nì Bakibukiya nì Oobadiya nì Meesulam nì Talmɔn nì Akuub di nìn cí adiin ŋin nìn yú ki nákáǹ kunimbɔtidii punyɔkɔki bi yōontí tijin poonee. 26Bíǹ di nìn tūǹ kunimbɔtidii poon ditundi Yeesuwa jipɔɔn Yooyakiim un nìn sá Yoosadaaki naantiiu nì Gɔmina Neeyeemiya nì Eesiraasi un sá usaraaŋal nì umaradakalee yuntiŋu.
Bi jíń Jeerusaleem gundi jiŋaaliu
27Jeerusaleem gundi jiŋaaliu puee, bi nìn yíiń Leefii yab bin nìn kóò ijaan kɔkɔ puee bí dāan̄ Jeerusaleem bí jī digundi jiŋaaliu nì dipɔɔpindi. Bi nìn gà inyɔŋki laŋyi, ki cákafí cancakantib ní ki bɔ̀ɔ́ saŋgub nì tibati. 28Bilaŋgaaliibi nìn nyánní ntimbilimu mun nìn māntìi tú Jeerusaleemee nì Neetoofa timbilimmu ki dɔ́miń ki kpáfì 29nì Beeti-Giilgaal, nì Geeba nì Asimafeeti timbilimmun yab. Di sá yii bilaŋgaaliibi nìn náań ntimbilimu ki māntìi tú Jeerusaleem tiŋki ní ki kóò. 30Bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab nìn ŋá akoobil nín sá puee ki ŋá bíǹ bi-ba nì samaa kɔkɔ nì mpunyɔmu nì digundi circir.
31M nìn yāntì Juuda yab kpilib jɔ́m̀ digundi pu. M nìn náań alaŋgakitikpaan ali. Dikitipeekaalee nìn búntì ŋŋaŋgiil pú ki tɔ́kɔ́ digundi pu ki còom̄ ki cá Titampuntan punyɔkɔki watil pú. 32Bin nìn pá bilaŋgaaliibi gbanti boonee di sá Oosaya nì Juuda yab kpilib dijandi, 33an dàkà yii Asariya nì Eesiraasi nì Meesulam, 34nì Yeewuda nì Beenjameen nì Seemaya nì Yiirmeeya. 35Bíǹ boon ní bisaraaŋaliibi bin ŋúb́ akantánee pá. Bíǹ di sá Joonatan jipɔɔn Seekariya. U-naanjab di sá Seemaya nì Mataniya nì Miikaya nì Sakuur nì Asaafi. 36U-nabiyaamu Seemaya nì Asareeyeel nì Miilalayi nì Giilalayi nì Maayi nì Neetaneeyeel nì Yeewuda nì Ananii nìn pá bi-boon ki ŋúb́ tiwambɔɔkaal tin Unimbɔti niliu Daafiidi nìn kpítèe. Umaradakal Eesiraasi di nìn līī bi-nyɔkɔpu. 37Bi bàn̄ Nnyimbul punyɔkɔkee, laakin dàb̀ ki jɔ́ḿ Daafiidi Tiŋkee bí bi-nimbiin. Bi nìn dàb̄ akɔl ki jɔ́m̀ ki tɔ́kɔǹ digundi pu, ní Daafiidi diiŋŋi bí taapu. Bi nìn cōom̀ ki tin bàn̄ Inyiŋfi punyɔkɔki ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú.
38Dilaŋgakitil dililiitiil nìn dī ŋŋaŋgan pú. Man nì samaa kpilib bin kíǹee nìn pá bi-boon ki tɔ́kɔǹ digundi pu. Ti nìn cōom̀ ki jítì Mpaamu difɔkɔku pu, ní ki tin bàn̄ laakin pú digundi wāāyee. 39Ti nìn nìkī ki nín cá Eefiraayiim punyɔkɔki yilpu pu nì Yeesana punyɔkɔki nì Ijɔm punyɔkɔki, nì Ananeeyeel difɔkɔku nì Dilaataal difɔkɔku ki tin cáa sāā Apibil punyɔkɔki ní ki tin gbēeǹ Sintil punyɔkɔki. 40Alaŋgakiti alee nìn kɔ́ ki yúl̀ kunimbɔtidiin. Man nì samaa kpilib dijandi din nìn nóó-mee mun nìn kɔ́ ki yúl̀. 41Bisaraaŋaliibi Eeliyaakiim nì Maseeyawuu nì Miiniyaamiini nì Miika nì Eeliyooweenayi nì Seekariya nì Ananiya nìn bí ki búǹ akantán. 42Bin mun nìn bée di sá Maseeyawuu nì Seemaya nì Eeleeyasaar nì Uusi nì Yoowanan nì Maalkiya nì Eelaam nì Eeseer. Isiraya di nìn kpòotī bilaŋgaaliibi ní bi gà ilan.
43Yaadalee, bi nìn ŋá saraabi tikpil ní ki nìn bí dipɔɔpindi poon, kun puee Unimbɔti nìn tīī-bi dipɔɔpiŋkpaandi. Binimpoobi nì mbiyaamu mun nìn bíi fàal̀, ní binib nìn bíń ndan ki gbìl̄ dipɔɔpindi faalii pu Jeerusaleem tiŋkin.
Tin sá bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab yatee
44Ŋyunti gbanti ní bi nìn lēē binib biba bí nīn cí adiin ŋin poon bi yōontí saraabi nì tisaalaatiil nì tijincɔ̀fikaalee. An nibee di làá nīn fòolìń ntimu mun bí ikpaanceetee yab cee mara nín yóoǹ yii bí nīn tìì bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab dijandi diŋyee. Ditundi din bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab nìn bí ki tūǹee nìn mɔ́ɔkiǹ Juuda yab. 45Bi nìn bí ki tūǹ bi-Nimbɔtiu tundi ní ki nìn ŋáań circir tin kɔkɔ sá bí ŋá circiree. Bilaŋgaaliibi nì bipunyɔɔciitiliibi mun nìn bí ki tūǹ bi-tuuŋŋi deedee, kii Daafiidi nì u-jipɔɔn Saloomɔn nín nìn yóoǹ mara yii bí nīn ŋáań puee. 46Di sá yii doooo ubɔti Daafiidi nì Asaafi yuntiŋuee, bilaŋgaaliibi kpilib nìn kpòotī bilaŋgaaliibi ní bi gà inyɔŋki nì ipampaka laŋyi ki tìì Unimbɔti tinyool. 47Sooroobabeel nì Neeyeemiya yuntiŋuee, Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ nìn tìì bilaŋgaaliibi nì bipunyɔɔciitiliibi dijandi din nìn pée sá bí nīn tìì-bi baabadalee ní. Bi nìn dùŋfī dijandi din sá circiree ní kí tīī Leefii yab, ní Leefii yab mun ń dū tin bi dūu sú ti-Dindaanee kí tīī Aarɔn maaliŋun yab.

english_text:
Foreigners Are Sent Away
1 On that day when the Law of Moses was read aloud to everyone, it was discovered that Ammonites and Moabites were forbidden to belong to the people of God. 2 This was because they had refused to give food and water to Israel and had hired Balaam to call down a curse on them. However, our God turned the curse into a blessing. 3Following the reading of the Law of Moses, the people of Israel started sending away anyone who had any foreign ancestors.
Nehemiah Makes Other Changes
4The priest Eliashib was a relative of Tobiah and had earlier been put in charge of the temple storerooms. 5So he let Tobiah live in one of these rooms, where all kinds of things had been stored—the grain offerings, incense, utensils for the temple, as well as the tenth of the grain, wine, and olive oil that had been given for the use of the Levites, singers, and temple guards, and the gifts for the priests.
6This happened in the thirty-second year that Artaxerxes ruled Babylonia. I was away from Jerusalem at the time, because I was visiting him. Later I received permission from the king 7to return to Jerusalem. Only then did I find out that Eliashib had done this terrible thing of letting Tobiah have a room in the temple. 8It upset me so much that I threw out every bit of Tobiah's furniture. 9Then I ordered the room to be cleaned and the temple utensils, the grain offerings, and the incense to be brought back into the room.
10 I also found out that the temple singers and several other Levites had returned to work on their farms, because they had not been given their share of the harvest. 11I called the leaders together and angrily asked them, “Why is the temple neglected?” Then I told them to start doing their jobs. 12 After this, everyone in Judah brought a tenth of their grain, wine, and olive oil to the temple storeroom. 13Finally, I appointed three men with good reputations to be in charge of what was brought there and to distribute it to the others. They were Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the teacher of the Law, and Pedaiah the Levite. Their assistant was Hanan, the son of Zaccur and the grandson of Mattaniah.
14I pray that my God will remember these good things that I have done for his temple and for those who worship there.
The Sabbath
15 I also noticed what the people of Judah were doing on the Sabbath. Not only were they trampling grapes to make wine, but they were harvesting their grain, grapes, figs, and other crops, and then loading these on donkeys to sell in Jerusalem. So I warned them not to sell food on the Sabbath. 16People who had moved to Jerusalem from the city of Tyre were bringing in fish and other things to sell there on the Sabbath. 17I got angry and said to the leaders of Judah, “This evil you are doing is an insult to the Sabbath! 18Didn't God punish us and this city because our ancestors did these very same things? And here you are, about to make God furious again by disgracing the Sabbath!”
19I ordered the gates of Jerusalem to be closed on the eve of the Sabbath and not to be opened until after the Sabbath had ended. Then I put some of my own men in charge of the gates to make certain that nothing was brought in on the Sabbath. 20Once or twice some merchants spent the night outside Jerusalem with their goods. 21But I warned them, “If you do this again, I'll have you arrested.” From then on, they did not come on the Sabbath. 22I ordered the Levites to make themselves holy and to guard the gates on the Sabbath, so that it would be kept holy.
God is truly merciful, and I pray that he will treat me with kindness and bless me for doing this.
Mixed Marriages
23 I discovered that some Jewish men had married women from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab. 24About half of their children could not speak Hebrew—they spoke only the language of Ashdod or some other foreign language. 25So in my anger, I called down curses on those men. I had them beaten and even pulled out the hair of some of them. Then I made them promise:
In the name of God we solemnly promise not to let our sons and daughters marry foreigners. 26 God dearly loved King Solomon of Israel and made him the greatest king on earth, but Solomon's foreign wives led him into sin. 27So we will obey you and not rebel against our God by marrying foreign women.
28 Jehoiada, the son of the high priest Eliashib, had a son who had married a daughter of Sanballat from Horon, and I forced his son to leave.
29I pray that God will punish them for breaking their priestly vows and disgracing the Levi tribe.
30Then I made sure that the people were free from every foreign influence, and I assigned duties for the priests and Levites. 31I also arranged for the people to bring firewood to the altar each day and for them to bring the first part of their harvest to the temple.
I pray that God will bless me for the good I have done.
translation_text:
Neeyeemiya fātìi bɔ́ntì tikɔkɔ
1Ŋyunti gbantee, bi nìn bí ki kàaǹ Mooyiisi gbɔŋkun Isirayeel yab nimbiin, ní ki ká an ŋmàn̄ yii Amɔn yab nì Moowaab yab kaa máaǹ kí cèeǹ Unimbɔti nibul poon. 2Di sá yii baa nìn túŋkì Isirayeel yab ki tīī-bi tijin nì nnyim. Kí kūtèe, Moowaab yab nìn tīī Balaam animbil ú tɔ̄ Isirayeel yab mbusu, ama ní ti-Nimbɔtiu nìn dū mbusuee ki kpántì dibiindi. 3Isirayeel yab nín gbìl̄ bi kàan̄ mara gbantee, ní bi nyántì binicambi kɔkɔ Isirayeel nibul kansikin.
4Kí wàatī bí nìn lēē nlandɔkɔ neeyee, usaraaŋal Eeliyasiib ní bi nìn lēē ú nīn kpèé ndibiyaamu mun nákáǹ ti-Nimbɔtiu diiku bi yōontí saraabi wantee. U nì Toobiya nín nìn pēē kunabitiiuee puee, 5u nìn tīī-u kudii kun poon wāā tiŋan bi nìn cāabìń saraabi nì talaalutuukaa nì asambil nì bilee nì ndapɔm nì ŋkpam saalaatiiti ki yōontée. An dàkà yii tin kɔkɔ mara nìn lī yii bí nīn cāabìń ki tìì Leefii yab nì bilaŋgaaliibi nì bipunyɔɔciitiliibee, ki kpáaǹ tin bi nìn lèekī ki tìì bisaraaŋaliibee.
6Ŋyunti ŋun tibɔti nee jítèe, maa nìn bí Jeerusaleem, di sá m nìn fātìi gítì Babiloon bɔtiu Aritaseerseesi cee u nín jíń dibeel abin mmuŋku nì saalaa nì ali poonee. Boonee ní m mēē ubɔti nsan, 7ní ki gítìń Jeerusaleem. Niin ní m ká ikpiti in Eeliyasiib ŋá ki dū kudii kun bí kunimbɔtidii cindinee ki tīī Toobiya kóòyee. 8M nìn fōō diŋuul tikpil ní ki kɔ́ kudiin ki kóoǹ Toobiya wanti kɔkɔ ki tɔ́ ki fá kudii boon. 9M nìn yāntì bi fíntì kudii gbanti ki ŋá-ku circir, ní m fātìi dū kunimbɔtidiin sambiliŋ nì saraabi nì talaalutuukaa ki síiǹ ti-laŋki.
10M nìn gbìl̄ mun yii baa nìn tìì dijandi din sá bí nīn tìì Leefii yabee, an puee Leefii yab nì bilaŋgaaliibi bin nìn bí kunimbɔtidiin ki tūǹ atuunee nìn dū bi-tuuŋŋi ki fá ki gítì ki bíi kù tikpaal. 11M nìn wòon̄ bibɔsoonliibi ki bí-bi yii: «Ba pu ní ni dū Unimbɔti diiku ki fá míǹ?» Niinee ní m fātìi kpáfì Leefii yab nì bilaŋgaaliibi ní ki dū bi-tuuŋŋi ki gíiǹ ki ŋúbiǹ-bi. 12Míǹ boonee Juuda yab kɔkɔ nìn cáań bilee nì ndapɔm nì ŋkpam saalaatiiti ki dūu yóoǹ kudii kun poon bi nìn yōontí saraabi jintee. 13M nìn lēē usaraaŋal Seeleemiya nì umaradakal Saadooki nì uleefiija Peedaya, ní ki dū Saakuur jipɔɔn, Mataniya naantiiu Anan ki ŋàl̄-bi bí nīn kpèé tijin tin bi cāabìń ki yōontée bɔti. Di sá yii báà ŋma nìn máká binib gbanti pu ní. Bíǹ ní bi nìn lēē bí nīn yàkatī bi-nabiyaamu tijin.
14«Óò m-Nimbɔtiu, taa súntí tin kɔkɔ m ŋée pu! Taa súntí m nín túń kunimbɔtidii tuuŋŋi nì deedee ki bɔ́ntì dinimbɔtinool puee pu.»
15Ŋyunti gbanti mbaanti ní m nìn ká Juuda yab tiŋkinee, binib nìn bí ki tà ki fɔ́bití asubil ndaam còol̀ ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dal. Biba mun nìn bíi tūntí bi-mammu bilee nì ndamam nì fiinyi subiliŋ nì fiigi subiliŋ nì awaŋgul aba mun ki cáa cáǹ Jeerusaleem ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dal. M nìn wòon̄-bi ŋwiin ŋun bi nìn bíi nyáfí bi-wantee. 16Tiir yab bin nìn kóò Jeerusaleemee nìn cāabìń ijɔm nì tinyampuwan ki nyáfíǹ Juuda yab Jeerusaleem tiŋkin ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dal. 17M nìn wòon̄ Juuda yab bɔtibiliŋ ki bí-bi yii: «Ba kpitii bulifi ní ni ŋá míǹ, ki kpēē ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa ŋun bí circiree fám mimmee? 18Míǹ ní ti-naanjab nìn ŋá. An pu ní Unimbɔti nìn yāntì mbusub nín bí puee nì bi-nyɔkɔm dɔ́miń ki jéetì ti nì ti-tiŋki pu. Ni nín bí ki kpèé ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa ŋun fám nee, ni bíi kùtī Unimbɔti ŋuul Isirayeel yab pu dee!»
19M nìn pú kinyɔkɔ yii bí pìin̄ Jeerusaleem punyɔmmu kujoou kun ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa kífée, kí taa pìitī kí nīn cí ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa ń jītí. Ní m lēē m-tɔntɔnliibi biba bí cīití mpunyɔmu báà ubɔ ń taa túnní tinyampuwan kí kɔ́ǹní ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dal. 20An puee binyampoobi nì biwannyafiliibi bin nyáfí tiwan nín bí ti-ba ti-ba puee nìn gbíntì Jeerusaleem guŋŋi boon ki dōoǹ diba kii mili pu. 21Ní m kpáafì-bi ki bí-bi yii: «Ba pu ní ni dɔ̀ digundi nyɔkɔpu kunyeeu ní? Ni yaa gbíntìi dɔ̀ míǹ, m làá yàntī bí cúú-ni.» Kí yòon̄ ŋyunti gbantee ní bi gbēeǹ kaa ti dòoń ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dal. 22Ní m bí Leefii yab yii bí ŋá bi-ba circir kí cùú cīití mpunyɔmu bí ŋmā kí nīn tɔ́ ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa.
«Kii míǹ mun puee, taa súntí m-pu m-Nimbɔtiu. A-laŋŋaŋfitiiku nín wīikí miŋyee puee, sɔ̄ m-saai!»
23Ŋyunti gbanti mbaanti ní m dáań ki ká yii Juuda yab nìn cáá Asidoodi nì Amɔn nì Moowaab yab bisalib. 24Bi-biyaamu dijandi nìn sòoǹ Asidoodi yab sooŋyi ní biba mun sòoǹ ntimu mubɔ yab sooŋyi. Bi-kansikin báà ubɔ kaa nìn gbìl̀ Juuda yab sooŋyi. 25M nìn wòon̄-bi, ki mēē mbusu ki tɔ́-bi. M nìn gbáń bi-kansikin biba ki dátì ki fùkū bi-yikpiti, ní ki yāntì bi pūtì Unimbɔti yindi pu. M nìn bí-bi yii: «Ní taa ti dū ni-bisalib kí tīī-bi ticati, ní ni nì ni-jipɔmbi ń taa cáá bi-bisalib. 26An kaa sá tibɔti gbanti juti di nìn dáaĺ Isirayeel yab bɔtiu Saloomɔn ki kɔ́ǹ ikpitinaaa? Waa nìn cáá juti atimbuŋkpaan bɔtiibi kansikin. Unimbɔti nìn néeń-u, ki nìn dū-u ki kāaǹ dibeel Isirayeel kɔkɔ pu. Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, úǹ ní binicannimpoobi nìn dáaĺ ki tɔ́ ikpitin. 27Bí dāá gíti gbìl̄ ni mun cee yii ni ŋá ikpitikpaan gbanti kaa yúliǹ Unimbɔti deedee, ki cáá binicannimpoobaaa?»
28Yooyadaa jipɔɔn ubɔ, usaraaŋakpil Eeliyasiib naantiu coo di nìn sá Sambalati un sá Oorɔn tiŋkinee. An pu ní m nìn jìn̄-u ki nyántì Jeerusaleem.
29«Óò m-Nimbɔtiu, taa súntí binib bin di bíil̀ disaraaŋal tundee nì mpèé ŋun a ŋá si nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yabee pu.»
30M nìn yāntì bi ŋá Isirayeel nibul kɔkɔ circir bi nì binicambi nín kpáfèe pu, ki nìn fātìi síiǹ marab bin ní bisaraaŋaliibi nì Leefii yab làá nīn nóó báà ŋma ń nīn tūǹ u-tundi tiŋanee. 31M nìn fātìi síiǹ idɔkpaakaa saraabi bin sá bí nīn cāabìń ŋwiin ŋun bi yóoǹ bí cáańee nì tijincɔ̀fikaal tin bi péetí kí lēē kitiŋ puee saraabi.
«Óò m-Nimbɔtiu, nì a-laŋŋaŋfitiiku puee, taa súntí m-pu.»

english_text:
Queen Vashti Disobeys King Xerxes
1-2 King Xerxes of Persia lived in his capital city of Susa and ruled 127 provinces from India to Ethiopia. 3During the third year of his rule, Xerxes gave a big dinner for all his officials and officers. The governors and leaders of the provinces were also invited, and even the commanders of the Persian and Median armies came. 4For 180 days he showed off his wealth and spent a lot of money to impress his guests with the greatness of his kingdom.
5At the end of this time, King Xerxes gave another dinner and invited everyone in the city of Susa, no matter who they were. The eating and drinking lasted seven days in the beautiful palace gardens. 6The area was decorated with blue and white cotton curtains tied back with purple linen cords that ran through silver rings fastened to marble columns. Couches of gold and silver rested on pavement that had all kinds of designs made from costly bright-colored stones and marble and mother-of-pearl.
7The guests drank from gold cups, and each cup had a different design. The king was generous 8and said to them, “Drink all you want!” Then he told his servants, “Keep their cups full.”
9While the men were enjoying themselves, Queen Vashti gave the women a big dinner inside the royal palace.
10By the seventh day, King Xerxes was feeling happy because of so much wine. And he asked his seven personal servants, Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carkas, 11to bring Queen Vashti to him. The king wanted her to wear her crown and let his people and his officials see how beautiful she was. 12The king's servants told Queen Vashti what he had said, but she refused to go to him, and this made him terribly angry.
13-14The king called in the seven highest officials of Persia and Media. They were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan. These men were very wise and understood all the laws and customs of the country, and the king always asked them what they thought about such matters.
15The king said to them, “Queen Vashti refused to come to me when I sent my servants for her. What does the law say I should do about that?”
16Then Memucan told the king and the officials:
Your Majesty, Queen Vashti has not only embarrassed you, but she has insulted your officials and everyone else in all the provinces.
17The women in the kingdom will hear about this, and they will refuse to respect their husbands. They will say, “If Queen Vashti doesn't obey her husband, why should we?” 18Before this day is over, the wives of the officials of Persia and Media will find out what Queen Vashti has done, and they will refuse to obey their husbands. They won't respect their husbands, and their husbands will be angry with them.
19Your Majesty, if you agree, you should write for the Medes and Persians a law that can never be changed. This law would keep Queen Vashti from ever seeing you again. Then you could let someone who respects you be queen in her place.
20When the women in your great kingdom hear about this new law, they will respect their husbands, no matter if they are rich or poor.
21King Xerxes and his officials liked what Memucan had said, 22and he sent letters to all of his provinces. Each letter was written in the language of the province to which it was sent, and it said that husbands should be in charge of their wives and children.
translation_text:
Ubɔti Asuweerusi ŋá tican
1Ŋyunti ŋun Asuweerusi nìn sá ubɔtee ní tibɔti nee jítì. Asuweerusi gbanti nìn jíń dibeel ntimu dilaataal nì mmuŋku nì mululi pu ní, kí yòon̄ Indiya tiŋki kí tin cáá sāā Kusa tiŋki. 2Ŋyunti gbanti ní ubɔti Asuweerusi kāl̀ u-beejal pu Suusi ditiŋyil. 3U-beel bintataatiil poonee ní u ŋá tican ki yíiń u-kàliŋkpilib nì u-tɔntɔnliibi nì Peeriisi nì Meedi yab janjakpilib nì ntimu yidambi nì mu-kàliŋkpilib. 4Ní u nyántì u-gaajawanti nì tiwannyaandi tin dàkà u-beel nyootee ki dàkā-bi ŋwiin ŋubɔ ŋubɔ dilaataal nì imuŋku inaa. 5Iwiin gbanti boonee ní ubɔti ŋá binib bin kɔkɔ bí Suusi ditiŋyilinee tican ubɔti mɔŋkiŋu, kí yòon̄ binikpaambi kí tin cáá sāā ŋwaamu bi jíń áli iwiin iluli. 6Bi nìn dū gulfa ki lùn̄ bisatapimbi nì bimambi gàaa, ní ki dū gulfaman ki lùn̄ iŋmii ki dūu bɔ́ tikúti bɔmbiyaamun, ki dū satabee ki sākaǹ jaantalkub bin bi dū kaaluubi ki nákáǹee pu. Ní ki dū kaaluubi nì tin jìl̀ee nì bikaaluubɔmbi ki ŋàl̄ kitiŋ, ní ki dū sindaariya lambammu nì tikúti lambammu ki yóoǹ an pu. 7Sindaariya kɔŋkɔnnyɔkaabi poon ní bi nìn tìì binib ndaam, ní kɔŋkɔnnyɔkaabee nìn bí tɔbin. Mbɔtidaamee nìn pùub̀ ní. Nì tiniti ní bi nìn bàtī ndaamee ki tìì binib. 8Ubɔti nìn pú nsan yii báà ŋma ń nyɔ̀ ndaam u nín là puee, di sá yii u nìn síiǹ u-tɔntɔnliibi mara yii bí ŋá min un sá kamaa lèe kí tīī udaan. 9Unimpubɔti Fastii mun nìn bɔ́ntì tican dibɔticindi poon ki yíiń binimpoobi.
Ubɔti jìn̄ unimpubɔti Fastii
10Bi bí jiŋaal poon míǹ iwiin iluli dalee, ndaam nyāatì ubɔti. Niinee ní u yíiń Meewuman nì Biisita nì Arboona nì Biigita nì Abagita nì Seetaar nì Karkasi, u-tɔntɔnliibi biluli bin sá bifaabi ki bí u-cindinee. 11Ní u bí-bi yii bí cùú yíiń unimpubɔti Fastii ú dāan̄ kí nīn cíkiń u-beefuuliiki. U nìn là kí dū u-nyaaŋku kí dàkà abɔtibil nì bikàliŋkpilib bin u nìn yíiń ticanee, di sá unimpubɔtee nìn ŋān̄ kunyaaŋŋu tikpil. 12Bifaabi cūtìi tùkū unimpubɔti Fastii ubɔti nín lī puee, ama ní u yíì kaa cūtì. Niinee ubɔti fōō diŋuul ŋkpitim pu. 13Ní u bālifì u-kpootiliibi tibɔti gbanti pu, kun puee tin yaa nìn pée sá dibeel pu bɔtee, biciŋfitiibi bin nyí marab nì min máaǹ bí ŋée di kpèé-tì. 14Bikpootiliibi biluli bin nìn bí ki nákáǹ ubɔtee di nìn sá Kaarseena nì Keetaar nì Adimata nì Taarsiisi nì Meereesi nì Maarseena nì Meemukan. Binib biluli gbanti di nìn sá Peeriisi nì Meedi kàliŋkpilib bin pu ubɔti nìn mákée, bíǹ di nìn kā ipaaŋkpaan ubɔti gɔminau poon. 15Ní ubɔti bí-bi yii: «Man ubɔtikpaan, m tú m-faabi unimpubɔti Fastii cee ki tīī-bi dinyɔɔbundi yii bí yíiń-u, ní u yíì kaa dɔ́miń. Mara poonee ditafadaaldi dilal ní u máaǹ ní?»
16Ní Meemukan fōō dinyɔɔbundi ubɔti kàliŋkpilib nimbiin ki bí yii: «An kaa sá ubɔti baba ní unimpubɔti Fastii kpēē fám, ama an sá ki kpáaǹ bikàliŋkpilib nì anibul ŋin kɔkɔ bí ubɔti Asuweerusi tiŋki jaaŋŋi kɔkɔnee ní. 17Di sá yii binimpoobi làá gbìl̄ tibɔti tin unimpubɔti ŋá nee, ní ki mun dāa kíǹ ki kpèé bi-calib fám, ní kí dūú kpáĺ yii: <Ubɔtikpaan nìn tú bí yíiń unimpubɔti Fastiiyee, u nìn yíì ní kaa cūtì.> 18Díǹ gba Peeriisi nì Meedi kàliŋkpilib nimpoobi làá gbìl̄ unimpubɔti nín ŋá tiŋyee. Míǹ mbaantiim ní bi mun làá kpèè timbi a-kàliŋkpilib bin sá bi-calibee fám, kun làá dāá yàntī bininjab ń fōō aŋuuyee dee. 19A yaa bàà kíikée, ti-baa ubɔti, á bàà síiń mara yii Fastii ń taa ti gbóonní a-cee, ní kí fàtīí lēē unimpubɔti un jítiǹ-uee. Mara gbantee, bí ŋmà-u Peeriisi nì Meedi yab marabin ubɔ ń taa ŋmā kí kpìtī-u. 20Ŋyunti ŋun mara un sii ubɔti yóoǹee yaa bàn̄ a-beekpaandi jaaŋŋi kɔkɔnee, binimpoobi kɔkɔ, bikpaambi nì ŋwaamu dāa kíǹ ki tɔ́ bi-calib ní.»
21Nlandɔkɔee nìn mɔ́ɔkiǹ ubɔti nì u-kàliŋkpilib, ní ubɔti ŋá kii Meemukan nín kpōotì-u puee. 22U nìn ŋmàn̄ tigbɔn ki tīī u-beel tinjaŋŋi kɔkɔ, kitiŋ kamaa nì ki-ŋmaŋmabiti nì ki-sooŋyi poon. Bi nìn ŋmàn̄ yii uninja kamaa ń nīn sá uyidaan u-dicaŋkun, kí páb́ bí nīn sòoǹ u-nibul sooŋyi.

english_text:
Esther Becomes Queen
1After a while, King Xerxes got over being angry. But he kept thinking about what Vashti had done and the law that he had written because of her. 2Then the king's personal servants said:
Your Majesty, a search must be made to find you some beautiful young women. 3You can select officers in every province to bring them to the place where you keep your wives in the capital city of Susa. Put your servant Hegai in charge of them since that is his job. He can see to it that they are given the proper beauty treatments. 4Then let the young woman who pleases you most take Vashti's place as queen.
King Xerxes liked these suggestions, and he followed them.
5At this time a Jew named Mordecai was living in Susa. His father was Jair, and his grandfather Shimei was the son of Kish from the tribe of Benjamin. 6 Kish was one of the people that Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem, when he took King Jeconiah of Judah to Babylonia.
7Mordecai had a very beautiful cousin named Esther, whose Hebrew name was Hadassah. He had raised her as his own daughter, after her father and mother died. 8When the king ordered the search for beautiful women, many were taken to the king's palace in Susa, and Esther was one of them.
Hegai was put in charge of all the women, 9and from the first day, Esther was his favorite. He began her beauty treatments at once. He also gave her plenty of food and seven special maids from the king's palace, and they had the best rooms.
10Mordecai had warned Esther not to tell anyone that she was a Jew, and she obeyed him. 11He was anxious to see how Esther was getting along and to learn what had happened to her. So each day he would walk back and forth in front of the court where the women lived.
12The young women were given beauty treatments for one whole year. The first six months their skin was rubbed with olive oil and myrrh, and the last six months it was treated with perfumes and cosmetics. Then each of them spent the night alone with King Xerxes. 13When a young woman went to the king, she could wear whatever clothes or jewelry she chose from the women's living quarters. 14In the evening she would go to the king, and the following morning she would go to the place where his wives stayed after being with him. There a man named Shaashgaz was in charge of the king's wives. Only the ones the king wanted and asked for by name could go back to the king.
15-16Xerxes had been king for seven years when Esther's turn came to go to him during Tebeth, the tenth month of the year. Everyone liked Esther. The king's personal servant Hegai was in charge of the women, and Esther trusted Hegai and asked him what she ought to take with her.
17Xerxes liked Esther more than he did any of the other young women. None of them pleased him as much as she did, and he immediately fell in love with her and crowned her queen in place of Vashti. 18In honor of Esther he gave a big dinner for his leaders and officials. Then he declared a holiday everywhere in his kingdom and gave expensive gifts.
Mordecai Saves the King's Life
19When the young women were brought together again, Esther's cousin Mordecai had become a palace official. 20He had told Esther never to tell anyone that she was a Jew, and she obeyed him, just as she had always done.
21Bigthana and Teresh were the two men who guarded King Xerxes' rooms, but they got angry with the king and decided to kill him. 22Mordecai found out about their plans and asked Queen Esther to tell the king what he had found out. 23King Xerxes learned that Mordecai's report was true, and he had the two men hanged. Then the king had all of this written down in his record book as he watched.
translation_text:
Eesiteer kpántì unimpubɔti
1Míǹ jítì boon, ubɔti Asuweerusi ŋuul sɔ̄ŋkèe, ní u téetì Fastii nín nìn ŋá-u miŋyee, nì u mun nín nìn síiǹ-u laakiŋyee. 2Niinee ní bin sá ubɔti kpambaliŋee bí-u yii: «An máaǹ tí nyàab̀ bisapɔmbi bin ŋān̄ kunyaaŋŋu tikpil kaa nyí uninjee kí tīī ubɔti. 3An puee ubɔti ń lēē u-tiŋki jaaŋŋi kɔkɔn bikàlimbi bí nyàab̀ bisapɔmbi bin ŋān̄ kunyaaŋŋu tikpil kaa nyí uninjee. Bí cáań-bi Suusi ditiŋyil, kí kɔ́ǹ-bi binimpoobi diiŋŋin. Bí dū-bi kí ŋúbiǹ Eegee, ubɔti faaliu un cí u-nimpoobee, ní úǹ ń tīī-bi ikpafi in ŋáŋkí tiwunee bí nīn ŋmìtī. 4Ní usapɔɔn un yaa fáatì ubɔtee ń kpántí unimpubɔti kí fōō Fastii yil.» Tibɔti gbantee nìn mɔ́ɔkiǹ ubɔti ní u yāntì bi ŋá míǹ.
5Ujuudaja ubɔ nìn bí Suusi tiŋki kin sá ditiŋyilee poon, bí yíì-u Maardoosee. U sá Beenjameen naakookun. U-naanjab di sá Yaayiir nì Simeeyii nì Kiisi. 6Kijapaayee nìn kútì binib bin Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar nìn cúuń kuyuŋu Jeerusaleem tiŋkin ki kpáaǹ Juuda yab bɔtiu Yookooniyayee poon. 7Maardoosee nìn fōō u-baawaai bisal u kā u-cee, bi yíì-u Adaasa àá Eesiteer. U-na nì u-baa nìn kpíì, ní Maardoosee fōō-u ki ŋúb́ kii u-bisalee. Usapɔɔnee nìn ŋān̄ tikpil.
8Bi nín dū ubɔti nín lī puee nì u-marau ki báakì ntimu poon yii ubɔti nyàab̀ bisapɔmbee, ní bi kóoǹní bisapɔmbi tikpil ki cáań ki kpáfì Suusi tiŋki kin sá ditiŋyilee poon, ní Eegee kpèé-bi. Bi cáań Eesiteer mun ubɔti cindi, ki dū-u ki ŋúbiǹ Eegee un cí ubɔti nimpoobee. 9Eesiteer nìn kɔ́ kijapaayee, ki ká diyimɔɔl u-cee, ní u nyàab̄ ikpafi in u làá nīn ŋmìtī u-wunti ń nīn ŋān̄ee nì tin u làá nīn jīǹee malaa ki tīī-u. U nìn lēē bisapɔmbi bin bí ubɔti cindinee biluli ki tīī-u bí nīn bí u-cee ki tútúǹ-u, ní ki kpēē ubɔti diiŋŋi kudimɔntiiu ki cáá-bi ki kɔ́ǹ niin. 10Eesiteer kaa nìn nyántì u-ba ki dàkā yii u sá dinibul dinee àá u-nyeeŋŋu sá doo, kun puee Maardoosee nìn kpáafì-u yii ú taa pée tùkù ubɔ u-nyeeŋŋu. 11Baabadalee, Maardoosee pée cá binimpoobi diiŋŋi mɔŋkiŋu ní ki kpèé yii Eesiteer bí mana àá bi ŋúb́-u mana.
12Ŋyunti ŋun ní usapɔɔn yaa dū ikpafi ki ŋmītì u-wunti iŋmal saalaa nì ili ki dóò kii an nín bàlifī unimpu ń dū ŋyunti ŋun kí bɔ́ntí u-bee, ní ú nín cù ubɔti Asuweerusi cee. Di sá bi nìn dù ŋkpam min bi yíì miiree ní kí nùkù bi-wunti iŋmal iluu, ní kí dū iŋmal iluu mun kí ŋmìtī binimpoobi kpafii in ŋáŋkí tiwunee. 13Usapɔɔn un yuntiŋu yaa bāań ú cù ubɔti ceeyee, bi tìì-u tin kɔkɔ u yaa là kí ŋúb́ kí cù ubɔti cindinee ní. 14U nìn cá kujoou ní kutaa yaa wúntì kutaafaauee ní ú fàtīí gítiń kí kɔ́ binimpoobi bililiitiibi diikun, ní ufaal Saakigaasi un cí ubɔti bɔmbee cí-bi. Baa ti gítí ubɔti cee, see un di yaa kɔ́-u ní u yíiń u-yindi yii ú dāan̄ee baba di gítí.
15Abisayiil bisal Eesiteer, Maardoosee baawaai bisal un u nìn fōō ki dūu kpántì u-bisalee, mun yuntiŋu bāań ú cù ubɔti cee. Waa nìn bālifì yii u là kí nīn ŋúb́ tiba, see tin Eegee ufaal un cí ubɔti nimpoobee sáŋkì-u yii ú yòon̄ee. Eesiteer nìn kāntí diyimɔɔl un kamaa yaa nìn pée ká-uee cee. 16Ubɔti Asuweerusi nín jíń dibeel dibinluluútiil uŋmasaalaati poon, uŋmal un bi yíì Teebeetee, ní bi cáá Eesiteer ki cūnnì ubɔti dumpu. 17Ubɔti naŋki nìn kɔ́ Eesiteer tikpil ki jítiǹ binimpoobi bin kíǹee kɔkɔ. U nìn ká ubɔti cee diyimɔɔl nì kulaŋŋaŋfitiiu ki jítiǹ bisapɔmbi bin kíǹee kɔkɔ. Ubɔti nìn dū kibeefuulii ki cíkiǹ-u, ní ki dū-u ki kpántì unimpubɔti Fastii paaŋŋu. 18Ní ubɔti ŋá tican Eesiteer pu, ní ki yíiń u-tɔntɔŋkpilib nì u-kàliŋkpilib, ní ki pú u-tiŋki jaaŋŋi kɔkɔ lampoo, ní ki ŋá binib tiniti mbɔtiyaamin.
19Bi nìn gíti nyàab̄ bisapɔmbi nliliitiim ki kpáfì ubɔti dumpu. Ŋyunti gbantee, Maardoosee bí ubɔti cindi ki sá ukàlinja. 20Eesiteer kaa nìn yāntì bi béè u-nyeeŋŋu nì dinibul din u sée, kii Maardoosee nín nìn kpáafì-u puee. Eesiteer pée gbíntìi ŋúb́ tin Maardoosee nìn dàkā-uee kii u nín nìn pée bí u-cee ki ŋúb́-tì puee ní.
Maardoosee cúú binib bin là kí kpɔ̀ ubɔtee
21Ŋyunti ŋun Maardoosee bí ubɔti cindin ki tūǹ u-kàlintundee, ní bifaabi bili Bigitan nì Teereesi bin nìn cí ubɔti punyɔkɔkee fōō ubɔti pu diŋuul ki nyàab̀ kí kpɔ̀-u. 22Ama ní Maardoosee gbìl̄ an bɔti, ní ki dūu tùkū unimpubɔti Eesiteer, ní úǹ dū an bɔtee ki nāatì ubɔti. 23Bi cɔ́ŋkì ki kpēēyee, tibɔtee lafun sá mbaamɔn, ní bi cúú bi-liitil ki lúntì idɔ pu bi kpíì. Ní bi dū an bɔtee ki ŋmàn̄ ki ŋá kugbɔŋu kun poon bi ŋmà tibɔti ki cáa kpáafée ubɔti nimbiin.

english_text:
Haman Plans To Destroy the Jews
1Later, King Xerxes promoted Haman the son of Hammedatha to the highest position in his kingdom. Haman was a descendant of Agag, 2and the king had given orders for his officials at the royal gate to honor Haman by kneeling down to him. All of them obeyed except Mordecai. 3When the other officials asked Mordecai why he disobeyed the king's command, 4he said, “Because I am a Jew.” They spoke to him for several days about kneeling down, but he still refused to obey. Finally, they reported this to Haman, to find out if he would let Mordecai get away with it.
5Haman was furious to learn that Mordecai refused to kneel down and honor him. 6And when he found out that Mordecai was a Jew, he knew that killing only Mordecai was not enough. Every Jew in the whole kingdom had to be killed.
7It was now the twelfth year of the rule of King Xerxes. During Nisan, the first month of the year, Haman said, “Find out the best time for me to do this.” The time chosen was Adar, the twelfth month.
8 Then Haman went to the king and said:
Your Majesty, there are some people who live all over your kingdom and won't have a thing to do with anyone else. They have customs that are different from everyone else's, and they refuse to obey your laws. We would be better off to get rid of them! 9Why not give orders for all of them to be killed? I can promise that you will get tons of silver for your treasury.
10The king handed his official ring to Haman, who hated the Jews, and the king told him, 11“Do what you want with those people! You can keep their money.”
12On the thirteenth day of Nisan, Haman called in the king's secretaries and ordered them to write letters in every language used in the kingdom. The letters were written in the name of the king and sealed by using the king's own ring. At once they were sent to the king's highest officials, the governors of each province, and the leaders of the different nations in the kingdom of Xerxes.
13The letters were taken by messengers to every part of the kingdom, and this is what was said in the letters:
On the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month, all Jewish men, women, and children are to be killed. And their property is to be taken.
14-15King Xerxes gave orders for these letters to be posted where they could be seen by everyone all over the kingdom. The king's command was obeyed, and one of the letters was read aloud to the people in the walled city of Susa. Then the king and Haman sat down to drink together, but no one in the city could figure out what was going on.
translation_text:
Amaani nì Maardoosee jaaku bɔti
1Míǹ boonee ní ubɔti Asuweerusi kāaǹ Ameedata jipɔɔn Amaani u-tɔntɔŋkpilib kɔkɔ pu tikpiti. Amaani gbanti nìn sá Agaagi naakookun ní. 2Ubɔti nìn yóoǹ bikàlimbi bin bí u-cindin ki tūǹ atuunee mara yii Amaani yaa jītée, báà ŋma ń gbàan̄ u-nimbiin kí tīī-u jilma. Ama Maardoosee nìn yíì kaa gbàantí, kaa tàtīi dòontí dicincibil Amaani nimbiin. 3Ní bikàlimbi bin kɔ kíǹ ubɔti cindinee bālifì Maardoosee yii: «Ba pu ní sii kaa tɔ́ ubɔti marau un u yóoǹee ní?» 4Bi pée dāantí tibɔbaantiil gbanti ní ki tùkù Maardoosee ní waa fātìi tɔ́. Ní u bí-bi yii úǹ sá ujuudaja ní. An pu ní bi dūu tùkū Amaani kí kpèè u yaa làá nīn gbíntì ki ŋáań míǹ. 5Amaani nín lafun dáań ki ká yii Maardoosee kaa gbàantí u-nimbiin kaa tí tàtīi dòontí dicincibil ki tìì-u jilmee, ní u fōō diŋuul u-pu. 6U nín béè yii Maardoosee sá ujuudajee, ní u ká nlandɔkɔ yii Maardoosee baba maŋfal ní waa làá lēē, ama u làá kúntí Maardoosee nì u-yab Juuda yab bin kɔkɔ bí ubɔti Asuweerusi tiŋki kɔkɔnee ní. 7Ubɔti Asuweerusi nín jíń dibeel abin saalaa nì ali, uŋmapeepeekaa un bi yíì Niisaŋyee poon ní bi tɔ́ Puur, an dàkà yii bi tɔ́ kasi Amaani nimbiin ŋwiin kamaa pu nì uŋmal kamaa pu kí kpèè ŋwiin àá uŋmal un di máaǹ ú kpɔ̀ kí céetí Juuda yabee. Ní an dūu lítì uŋmal saalaa nì uliliiti pu, uŋmal gbanti ní bi yíì Adaar.
Amaani bíi bɔ́ntí kí kpɔ̀ kí céetí Juuda yab
8Ní Amaani bí ubɔti yii: «Dinibul diba bí ki yàl̄ ki kɔ́ a-tinjaŋŋi kɔkɔn, ki nyáń di-ba nì anibul ŋin kíǹee. Di-marab nyáń bi-ba nì anibul kɔkɔ marab, ní bíǹ kaa tɔ́ ubɔti marab. Aa cáá ipaati iba bi-pu kí yàntī bí nīn bí ŋgbansɔŋfin. 9Ti-baa ubɔti, an yaa bàà ŋān̄ a-ceeyee, á bàà ŋmà kugbɔŋu kí pɔ̄ kinyɔkɔ bí kpɔ̀ kí céetí-bi. Man làá ŋmàntī animbil kúti kutukub saalaa kí tīī a-kàlimbi bin bí a-cindin ki tūǹ atuunee bí dūú ŋá ubɔti nimbiliŋ dakaau poon.» 10Niinee ní ubɔti fúutì u-bɔmbiki kin cáá u-daaŋkuee u-ŋaan ki dūu tīī Juuda yab pulincɔnti Amaani un sá Ameedata jipɔɔn ki sá Agaagi naakookunee. 11Ní ubɔti kíí-u yii: «M gíiǹ a-nimbiliŋ ki kpáaǹ dinibulee ki tīī-si á ŋá-bi min a lèe.»
12Ní bi yíiń ubɔti gbaŋŋmaliibi uŋmapeepeekaa iwiin saalaa nì ita dal. Ní Amaani yāntì bi ŋmàn̄ tigbɔn ki tīī atinjan kɔkɔ bɔtibiliŋ nì ŋi-gɔminab nì dinibul kamaa bɔtiu. Bi nìn ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu ki tīī dinibul kamaa di-sooŋyin nì di-ŋmaŋmabiti ní. Ubɔti Asuweerusi yindi pu ní bi ŋmàn̄, ki dū u-bɔmbiki kin cáá u-daaŋkuee ki nyīī tigbɔnee pu. 13Ní ubɔti tuuŋyi yōoǹ tigbɔnee ki yākatì ubɔti tinjaŋŋi kɔkɔn. Bi nìn ŋmàn̄ tigbɔnee poon yii: «Bi pú kinyɔkɔ yii uŋmal saalaa nì uliliiti poon, Adaar ŋmaliu iwiin saalaa nì ita dalee, bí kpɔ̀ kí céetí Juuda yab kɔkɔ, binipɔmbi nì bitikpilib nì binimpoobi nì mbiyaamu. An sá ŋwimbaanti ní bí kpɔ̀ kí céetí-bi kí yòon̄ bi-wanti. 14Kugbɔŋu kun bi ŋmàn̄ ki tīī kitiŋ jaaŋŋi kɔkɔee sá mara ní bi yóoǹ, ní ki tùkù anibul kɔkɔ ń bɔ́ntí ŋi-ba kí cīití ŋwiin gbanti.» 15Ní ubɔti bí yii u-tuuŋyi ń yòon̄ tigbɔnee kí cáá yàkatī malaa malaa, ní bi cáa yākatì, ní maree dūu gbītì Suusi ditiŋyil poon. Ŋyunti gbantee Amaani nì ubɔti cūtìi kāl̀ ki bíi nyù ndaam, ní Suusi tiŋki kɔkɔ kɔ́ dinimbinaamandin.

english_text:
Mordecai Asks for Esther's Help
1When Mordecai heard about the letter, he tore his clothes in sorrow and put on sackcloth. Then he covered his head with ashes and went through the city, crying and weeping. 2But he could go only as far as the palace gate, because no one wearing sackcloth was allowed inside the palace. 3 In every province where the king's orders were read, the Jews cried and mourned, and they went without eating. Many of them even put on sackcloth and sat in ashes.
4When Esther's servant girls and her other servants told her what Mordecai was doing, she became very upset and sent Mordecai some clothes to wear in place of the sackcloth. But he refused to take them.
5Esther had a servant named Hathach, who had been given to her by the king. So she called him in and said, “Find out what's wrong with Mordecai and why he's acting this way.”
