6Hathach went to Mordecai in the city square in front of the palace gate, 7and Mordecai told him everything that had happened. He also told him how much money Haman had promised to add to the king's treasury, if all the Jews were killed.
8Mordecai gave Hathach a copy of the orders for the murder of the Jews and told him that these had been read in Susa. He said, “Show this to Esther and explain what it means. Ask her to go to the king and beg him to have pity on her people, the Jews!”
9Hathach went back to Esther and told her what Mordecai had said. 10She answered, “Tell Mordecai 11there is a law about going in to see the king, and all his officials and his people know about this law. Anyone who goes in to see the king without being invited by him will be put to death. The only way that anyone can be saved is for the king to hold out the gold scepter to that person. And it's been thirty days since he has asked for me.”
12When Mordecai was told what Esther had said, 13he sent back this reply, “Don't think that you will escape being killed with the rest of the Jews, just because you live in the king's palace. 14If you don't speak up now, we will somehow get help, but you and your family will be killed. It could be that you were made queen for a time like this!”
15Esther sent a message to Mordecai, saying, 16“Bring together all the Jews in Susa and tell them to go without eating for my sake! Don't eat or drink for three days and nights. My servant girls and I will do the same. Then I will go in to see the king, even if it means I must die.”
17Mordecai did everything Esther told him to do.
translation_text:
Maardoosee bālifì Eesiteer ú jòoń-bi
1Maardoosee nín gbìl̄ tin kɔkɔ jítèe, ní u dáaĺ ki cátì tiwan tin u pēēyee, ki dū kutukub ki pēeǹ, ki dū ŋfantam ki pùkū u-ba, ní ki nyáń kitiŋin ki gbáà ibiil mpɔn ki yáliŋkí. 2U bàn̄ ubɔti mɔŋkiŋuee ní ki yúl̀, kun puee ubɔ kaa cáá nsan kí nīn pēē kutuku kí kɔ́ ubɔti cindi. 3Míǹ ní kitiŋ jaaŋŋi laakin kamaa ní mara un ubɔti yóoǹee yaa bàn̄ee, an sá dikpool ní Juuda yab cee. Bi nìn bōob̀ nnyɔmu, ní binib tikpil sūǹ ki yáliŋkí, ní ki pēē kutukub ki dɔ̄ ŋfantamin ki bíntí.
4Eesiteer tɔntɔnliibi bisapɔmbi nì u-faabi cūtìi tùkū-u tin bi kée, ní u-pɔbil bíil̀ tikpil. Ní u nyàab̄ abɔkuti ki tīī-bi bí cáá tīī-u, ú pèetī kutukub bin u pēēyee kí dū abɔkuti ŋin u tīī-uee kí pèen̄, ama ní Maardoosee yíì. 5Niinee Eesiteer yíiń Ataaki, ufaal un ubɔti nìn tīī-u ú nīn bí ki tútúǹ-uee ki tú ú cùú bàlifì Maardoosee kí béé kun di yì-tì ní u bíi ŋáań mimmee. 6Ní Ataaki nín cá ki bàn̄ ki ká-u u yú mmɔŋkijaa, ubɔti naakooku nyɔkɔpu. 7Ní Maardoosee máafì-u tin kɔkɔ jítèe, nì animbil ŋin nyɔkɔm Amaani pōoǹ ubɔti yii bi yaa kūū ki céetì Juuda yab u làá cáá ŋá ubɔti nimbiliŋ dakaaunee. 8Ní u dū kugbɔŋu kun bi ŋmàn̄ Suusi an gbītì an kɔkɔ yii bí kpɔ̀ kí céetí Juuda yabee ki tīī-u ú cáá dàkà Eesiteer, ú béé tin poon bi bée, kí ká ubɔti kí gbàam̀-u ú sɔ̄ u-nibul Juuda yab saai. 9Ní Ataaki cáá tibɔti tin Maardoosee sòon̄ee ki tùkū Eesiteer. 10Ní Eesiteer bí Ataaki yii ú cùú tùkù Maardoosee yii: 11«Ubɔti tɔntɔnliibi kɔkɔ nì anibul ŋin kɔkɔ bí ubɔti tinjaŋŋi poonee nyí yii ubɔti yaa kaa yíiń sii ubɔ ní a jítìi kɔ́ u-cindinee, see bí kpɔ̀-si, an sá mara ní. Ama sii un ní ubɔti yaa tāntì u-bɔtikpandɔŋu ŋun sá sindaariyee ki túĺee, sii di ŋmátí. Man ŋá iwiin mmuŋku nì saalaa dee ubɔti kaa yíiń-mi m cūtì u-cee.» 12Ní Ataaki cáá Eesiteer nín lī puee ki tùkū Maardoosee. 13Ní Maardoosee kíí Eesiteer yii: «Á taa dàkafì yii a nín bí dibeecindinee puee, sii baba di làá ŋmátí Juuda yab kɔkɔ kansikin. 14A yaa kaa ŋá tiba agìń yuntii in poon ti bí nee, Unimbɔti làá jòò Juuda yab kí fīī-bi, ama ní sii nì a-baa dicaŋkun yab kɔkɔ ń kpú. Ŋma tin ká an yaa kaa sá tin bí nee pu ní a kpántì unimpubɔti?» 15Ní Eesiteer kíí Maardoosee yii: 16«Á cù kí kpāfì Juuda yab bin kɔkɔ bí Suusi tiŋkinee, bí bóob́ kinyɔkɔ kí mèè Unimbɔti kí tīī-mi. Ní taa jī kí taa nyɔ̀ iwiin ita ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu. Ma mun nì m-tɔntɔnliibi binimpoobi làá bóob́ kinyɔkɔ míǹ mbaantiim. Boonee ní ḿ cùú ká ubɔti nì min kɔkɔ mara yú yii ubɔ kaa cée, ní an yaa sá ŋkúmaaa, ḿ kpú.» 17Ní Maardoosee cūtìi ká u-yab ní ki ŋá kii Eesiteer nín bālifì yii bí ŋá puee.

english_text:
Esther Invites the King and Haman to a Dinner
1Three days later, Esther dressed in her royal robes and went to the inner court of the palace in front of the throne. The king was sitting there, facing the open doorway. 2He was happy to see Esther, and he held out the gold scepter to her.
When Esther came up and touched the tip of the scepter, 3the king said, “Esther, what brings you here? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom.”
4Esther answered, “Your Majesty, please come with Haman to a dinner I will prepare for you later today.”
5The king said to his servants, “Hurry and get Haman, so we can accept Esther's invitation.”
The king and Haman went to Esther's dinner, 6and while they were drinking wine, the king asked her, “What can I do for you? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom.”
7-8Esther replied, “Your Majesty, if you really care for me and are willing to do what I want, please come again tomorrow with Haman to the dinner I will prepare for you. At that time I will answer Your Majesty's question.”
Haman Plans To Kill Mordecai
9Haman was feeling great as he left. But when he saw Mordecai at the palace gate, he noticed that Mordecai did not stand up or show him any respect. This made Haman really angry, 10but he did not say a thing.
When Haman got home, he called together his friends and his wife Zeresh 11and started bragging about his great wealth and all his sons. He told them the many ways that the king had honored him and how all the other officials and leaders had to respect him. 12Haman added, “That's not all! Besides the king himself, I'm the only person Queen Esther invited for dinner. She has also invited the king and me to dinner tomorrow. 13But none of this makes me happy, as long as I see that Jew Mordecai serving the king.”
14Haman's wife and friends said to him, “Have a gallows built about 22 meters high, and tomorrow morning ask the king to hang Mordecai there. Then later, you can have dinner with the king and enjoy yourself.”
This seemed like a good idea to Haman, and he had the gallows built.
translation_text:
Eesiteer cūtì ubɔti cee
1Bi bóob́ kinyɔkɔ míǹ winta dalee, ní Eesiteer dū unimpubɔti bɔkutiŋ ki pēeǹ ki nín cá ubɔti cee. U bàn̄ee ní ki kɔ́ ki yú ubɔti beecindin ki bíitiǹ kunaakoou. Ubɔti kā u-naakookun u-beejal pu ní u-nimbiin túĺ mmɔŋki punyɔkɔki. 2U nín ká unimpubɔti Eesiteer yú dibeecindinee, ní u pú-u diyimɔɔl ki tāntì u-bɔtikpandɔŋu ŋun sá sindaariyee, ní Eesiteer sútìń ki gbēē nyɔkɔpu.
3Ní ubɔti bālifì-u yii: «Unimpubɔti Eesiteer, ba ŋá? Ba ní a là ní? Báà an yaa sá m-beel dijandi ní a là, m làá tīī-si.» 4Ní Eesiteer kíí-u yii: «An yaa bàà fáatì ti-baa ubɔti u nì Amaani ń bàà dāan̄ m-cee díǹ kí jī tican tin m bɔ́ntì kí ŋá kí tīī-uee.» 5Ní ubɔti tú unil dicilpu niin ú tùkù Amaani yii ú bɔ́ntí malaa malaa kí dāan̄ bí cùú jī tican tin Eesiteer bɔ́ntì ki yíiń-bee. Ní Amaani dɔ́miń ki céeǹ ubɔti bí cùú jī tican tin Eesiteer bɔ́ntì ki yíiń-bee. 6Bi jíń tijin ki dóòyee ní ubɔti bālifì Eesiteer yii: «Ba ní a là ní? Báà an yaa sá m-beel dijandi ní a yaa là, m làá tīī-si.» 7Ní Eesiteer kíí-u yii: «Tin páb́-mi m là kí mèè-see sèé. 8Ti-baa ubɔti, m yaa ká diyimɔɔl a-cee, ní an yaa fáatì-si yii á ŋá tin páb́-mi m là kí mèè-si á tīī-mee, sii nì Amaani ń fu gítiń fool kí dāá jī tican tin m làá fu tí bɔ́ntí kí tīī-nee. Niin ní m làá fu tùkù ti-baa ubɔti tin m là ú ŋá kí tīī-mee.»
Amaani bɔ́ntì ndɔ kí lúntí Maardoosee
9Yaadalee Amaani nìn nyáń unimpubɔti dumpu an mɔ́ɔkiǹ-u u-pɔbil píil̀. Niinee ní u ká Maardoosee ubɔti naakooku nyɔkɔpu, ama ní úǹ kaa cīŋkì u-ba báà fiii ní kaa nín tīī-u disíndi. Niinee Amaani fōō Maardoosee pu diŋuul ŋkpitim pu. 10Ní u cúú u-ba kaa lī tiba ní ki nín kùǹ. U bàn̄ee ní ki yíiń u-bɔɔbi nì u-nimpuu Seereesi. 11Niinee ní Amaani bíi dàkà u-ba ki sòoǹ nì bi u nín cáá tigaajati tikpil nì jipɔmbi kupaau puee nì jilma un ubɔti tīī-u ki dū-u ki kāaǹ mpaan ŋun pu u jítiǹ u-kàliŋkpilib kɔkɔee. 12Amaani nìn gíti bí yii: «Unimpubɔti Eesiteer nín ŋá tican ki yíiń ubɔtee, man baba ní u yíiń ḿ céeǹ ubɔti, ní ti cūtì díǹ ki jíń. U gíti tí yíiń-ti fool man nì ubɔti tí fu cù u-cee kí jī. 13Ama tin bí nee kaa pée tìì-mi mmɔn ŋubɔ, ŋyunti ŋun ní Maardoosee ujuudaja gbíntìi kā u-paaŋŋu dibeecindi nyɔkɔpu m wāĺ-uee.» 14Niinee ní u-nimpuu Seereesi nì u-bɔɔbi kɔkɔ bí-u yii: «Nyàab̀ ndɔ ŋun fɔ̀kɔ̀ kii meetab mmuŋku nì biŋmooyee. Fool kutaafaauee, á fu mèè ubɔti yii bí dū ŋŋmii kí kúĺ Maardoosee neen kí cáá-u kí lúntí ndɔ pu ní sii nì ubɔti ń nīn cá jiŋaal nì dipɔɔsɔŋkil.» An nyɔɔbundee mɔ́ɔkiǹ Amaani, ní u yāntì bi bɔ́ntì ndɔ ki yóoǹ.

english_text:
The King Honors Mordecai
1That night the king could not sleep, and he had a servant read him the records of what had happened since he had been king. 2 When the servant read how Mordecai had kept Bigthana and Teresh from killing the king, 3the king asked, “What has been done to reward Mordecai for this?”
“Nothing, Your Majesty!” the king's servants replied.
4About this time, Haman came in to ask the king to have Mordecai hanged on the gallows he had built. The king saw him and asked, “Who is that man waiting in front of the throne room?”
5The king's servants answered, “Your Majesty, it is Haman.”
“Tell him to come in,” the king commanded.
6When Haman entered the room, the king asked him, “What should I do for a man I want to honor?”
Haman was sure that he was the one the king wanted to honor. 7So he replied, “Your Majesty, if you wish to honor a man, 8get someone to bring him one of your own robes and one of your own horses with a fancy headdress. 9Tell one of your highest officials to place your robe on this man and lead him through the streets on your horse, while someone shouts, ‘This is how the king honors a man!’ ”
10The king replied, “Hurry and do just what you have said! Don't forget a thing. Get the robe and the horse for Mordecai the Jew, who serves as one of the king's officials!”
11Haman got the king's robe and put it on Mordecai. He led him through the city on the horse and shouted as he went, “This is how the king honors a man!”
12Afterwards, Mordecai returned to his duties in the king's palace, and Haman hurried home, hiding his face in shame. 13Haman told his wife and friends what had happened. Then his wife and his advisors said, “If Mordecai is a Jew, this is just the beginning of your troubles! You will end up a ruined man.” 14They were still talking, when the king's servants came and quickly took Haman to the dinner that Esther had prepared.
translation_text:
Ubɔti tīī Maardoosee tinyool
1Kunyeeu gbantee, ŋgeem nìn sáǹ ubɔti nimbiliŋ pu, ní u yāntì bi cáań kugbɔŋu kun poon bi ŋmàn̄ tibɔti tin nìn jítì bibɔtiibi pu dooooyee ki kàan̄ u-nimbiin. 2Bi kàan̄ee ki ká laakin ubɔti Asuweerusi faabi bili, Bagitan nì Teereesi bin nìn cí ubɔti punyɔkɔkee nìn nyàab̀ kí kpɔ̀ ubɔtee, nì Maardoosee nín nìn bīitì bi-pu puee. 3Ní ubɔti bí yii: «Maardoosee nín nìn ŋá mimmee, ba nyooti nì ba paati ní bi nìn tīī-u?» Ní ubɔti kpambaliŋ bí yii: «Baa nìn tīī-u tiba.» 4Ni ubɔti bí yii: «Ŋma di bí dicindi?» Ŋyunti gbantee Amaani kóoń ubɔti cindi kí bàà tùkù-u yii u bɔ́ntì ndɔ ki cáań kí dūú lúntí Maardoosee dee. 5Ní ubɔti kpambaliŋ kíí-u yii: «Amaani di bí dicindi.» Ní ubɔti bí yii: «Tùkùmaan-u yii ú kóoń.» 6Ní Amaani kɔ́, ní ubɔti bālifì-u yii: «Ubɔti yaa là kí tīī unil ubɔ jilmee, u ŋáań-u mana ní?» Amaani nìn dākafì yii: «Ŋma di gíti bí ubɔti là kí tīī-u jilma an yaa kaa sá man?» 7Ní Amaani kíí ubɔti yii: «Ti-baa ubɔti, a yaa là kí tīī unil ubɔ jilmee, 8an sá bí cáań dibeebɔkutil din ubɔti pēeǹee, nì ubɔti taamuu un pu u kāl̀ee, ní kí dū ubɔti beefuuliiki kí cíkiń-u. 9Ní bí lēē bikàliŋkpilib kansikin ubɔ, kí dū dibeebɔkutilee nì utaamu kí dūú ŋúbiǹ udaan ń dūú pèen̄ unil un ubɔti là kí tīī jilmee ní kí dū-u kí kàan̄ utaamuee pu. Ní ú cáá-u kí nīn yìiǹ kitiŋin, ní binib ń nīn līī u-nyɔkɔpu ki tátí yii: <Kpèèmaan, bi nín ŋáań unil un ubɔti là kí tīī jilmee puee sèé!>»
10Ní ubɔti bí Amaani yii: «Too, malaa cùú yòon̄ dibeebɔkutil nì utaamu kí ŋá kii a nín pée sòon̄ pu nee kí tīī Maardoosee ujuudaja un kā dibeecindi punyɔkɔpuee. A nín pée lī puee, á ŋá míǹ deedee kí taa bàtī tiba.» 11Ní Amaani cūtìi nyàab̄ dibeebɔkutil nì utaamu, ní ki dū dibeebɔkutilee ki pēeǹ Maardoosee, ní ki dū-u ki kāaǹ utaamu pu, ní ki cáá-u ki yìin̄ kitiŋin, ní ki līī u-nyɔkɔpu ki tátí yii: «Kpèèmaan, bi nín ŋáań unil un ubɔti là kí tīī jilmee puee sèé!»
12Bi ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee, ní Maardoosee fātì dibeecindi punyɔkɔpu, ní Amaani nín kùǹ malaa u-dumpu nì icoo, u-yil tīī. 13Amaani bàn̄ee ní ki máafì u-nimpuu Seereesi nì u-bɔɔbi tin jítèe kɔkɔ. Niinee ní u-bɔɔbi bin kpòotī-uee nì u-nimpuu Seereesi bí-u yii: «Maardoosee un nimbiin a kíĺ ki bíi gbàantí nee sá ujuudaja ní. An puee a pée gíti kpá kí ŋmā-u, sii làá mɔ̀tīí nīn sìntī taapu ní ki cá.» 14Bi bí ki sòoǹee ní ubɔti faabi dɔ́miń ki yōoǹ Amaani malaa, bi búntì tican tin Eesiteer bɔ́ntì ki yíiń-bee laŋki.

english_text:
Haman Is Punished
1The king and Haman were dining with Esther 2and drinking wine during the second dinner, when the king again said, “Esther, what can I do for you? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom!”
3Esther answered, “Your Majesty, if you really care for me and are willing to help, you can save me and my people. That's what I really want, 4because a reward has been promised to anyone who kills my people. Your Majesty, if we were merely going to be sold as slaves, I would not have bothered you.”
5“Who would dare to do such a thing?” the king asked.
6Esther replied, “That evil Haman is the one out to get us!”
Haman was terrified, as he looked at the king and the queen.
7The king was so angry that he got up, left his wine, and went out into the palace garden.
Haman realized that the king had already decided what to do with him, and he stayed and begged Esther to save his life.
8Just as the king came back into the room, Haman got down on his knees beside Esther, who was lying on the couch. The king shouted, “Now you're even trying to rape my queen here in my own palace!”
As soon as the king said this, his servants covered Haman's head. 9Then Harbona, one of the king's personal servants, said, “Your Majesty, Haman built a gallows 22 meters high beside his house, so he could hang Mordecai on it. And Mordecai is the very one who spoke up and saved your life.”
“Hang Haman from his own gallows!” the king commanded. 10At once, Haman was hanged on the gallows he had built to hang Mordecai, and the king calmed down.
translation_text:
Amaani kúm
1Ubɔti nì Amaani búntì unimpubɔti Eesiteer cee kí jī tican. 2Ŋwinliliiti dal bi jíń ki nyùn̄ ki dóòyee ní ubɔti bālifì unimpubɔti Eesiteer yii: «Ba ní a là ní? Báà an yaa sá m-beel dijandi ní a yaa bālifì-mi, m làá tīī-si.» 3Ní unimpubɔti bí yii: «Too ti-baa ubɔti, m yaa ká diyimɔɔl a-cee ní an yaa fáatì-see, á dā man nì m-nibul maŋfal kí líí. Tin páb́-mi m là kí mèè-see dee, ti-baa ubɔti. 4Di sá yii bi dū man nì m-nibul ki nyáfì bí kpɔ̀ kí céetí-ti. An yaa bàà sá yii bi dū-ti ki nyáfì tí bàà kpántí iyumbu, maa bàà lì tiba a-cee, kun puee tíǹ kaa bàn̄ tibɔti ḿ cáań kí páb́ ubɔti.» 5Niinee ní ubɔti bālifì unimpubɔti Eesiteer yii: «Ŋma di sá-u ní ki cáá nlandɔkɔ gbanti? Udaan bí la?» 6Ní Eesiteer kíí-u yii: «Un páb́-ti ki sá ti-nannanliuee di sá Amaani unikpiti nee!» Niinee ní dinyoondi kɔ́ Amaani ubɔti nì unimpubɔti nimbiin. 7Ní ubɔti fōō diŋuul ní ki yíkì ki yāntì tijin ki nyáń ki yú mmɔŋki. Ní Amaani gbíntì Eesiteer cee ki bíi gbàam̄-u kí fīī u-maŋfal, kun puee u nìn ká yii ubɔti nín yíkì miŋyee, an sá ŋkúm di dɔ̄ ki cí-u. 8Ní u lítì kilambaŋ kin pu Eesiteer nìn kēe taapu ki bíi gbàam̄-u. Ubɔti nyánní mmɔŋki ki fātìi kóońee ki ká Amaani kudii kun poon bi bàà bíi jīǹ ticanee, u dɔ̄ dicincibil laakin Eesiteer kēe, ní ubɔti téeń mpɔn yii: «Kijapaai nee là kí dòon̄ nì Eesiteer mpɔn man nimbiin m-diikunaaa?» Ubɔti tin pée lì míǹ kaa láá ŋmíl̀ee bi dɔ́miń ki cúú Amaani ki dū tiwan ki bīiǹ u-nimbiin. 9Ní Arboona, ubɔti faabi kansikin ubɔ lī ubɔti cee yii: «Ti-baa bɔti, Amaani u-ba bɔ́ntì ndɔ ŋubɔ kí dū Maardoosee un mɔ́tì ubɔti puee kí lúntí, ndɔ gbanti dìin̄ u-mɔŋkiŋu. Ŋu-fɔkɔŋŋu sá meetab mmuŋku nì biŋmoo.» Ní ubɔti bí yii: «Bí dū Amaani kí lúntí ndɔ gbanti pu.» 10Ní bi dū Amaani ki lúntì ndɔ ŋun u nìn bɔ́ntì ki yóoǹ bí dū Maardoosee kí lúntée. Niinee ní ubɔti ŋuul sɔ̄ŋkì.

english_text:
A Happy Ending for the Jews
1Before the end of the day, King Xerxes gave Esther everything that had belonged to Haman, the enemy of the Jews. Esther told the king that Mordecai was her cousin. So the king made Mordecai one of his highest officials 2and gave him the royal ring that Haman had worn. Then Esther put Mordecai in charge of Haman's property.
3Once again Esther went to speak to the king. This time she fell down at his feet, crying and begging, “Please stop Haman's evil plan to have the Jews killed!” 4King Xerxes held out the golden scepter to Esther, 5and she got up and said, “Your Majesty, I know that you will do the right thing and that you really love me. Please stop what Haman has planned. He has already sent letters demanding that the Jews in all your provinces be killed, 6and I can't bear to see my people and my own relatives destroyed.”
7King Xerxes then said to Esther and Mordecai, “I have already ordered Haman to be hanged and his house given to Esther, because of his evil plans to kill the Jews. 8 I now give you permission to make a law that will save the lives of your people. You may use my ring to seal the law, so that it can never be changed.”
9On the twenty-third day of Sivan, the third month, the king's secretaries wrote the law. They obeyed Mordecai and wrote to the Jews, the rulers, the governors, and the officials of all 127 provinces from India to Ethiopia. The letters were written in every language used in the kingdom, including the Jewish language. 10They were written in the name of King Xerxes and sealed with his ring. Then they were taken by messengers who rode the king's finest and fastest horses.
11-13In these letters the king said:
On the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month, the Jews in every city and province will be allowed to get together and defend themselves. They may destroy any army that attacks them, and they may kill all of their enemies, including women and children. They may also take everything that belongs to their enemies.
A copy of this law is to be posted in every province and read by everyone.
14-15Then the king ordered his messengers to take their fastest horses and deliver the law as quickly as possible to every province. When Mordecai left, he was wearing clothes fit for a king. He wore blue and white robes, a large gold crown, and a cape made of fine linen and purple cloth.
After the law was announced in Susa, everyone shouted and cheered, 16and the Jews were no longer afraid. In fact, they were very happy and felt that they had won a victory.
17In every province and city where the law was sent, the Jews had parties and celebrated. Many of the people in the provinces accepted the Jewish religion, because they were now afraid of the Jews.
translation_text:
1Ŋwiin gbanti dal ní ubɔti Asuweerusi dū Juuda yab nannanliu Amaani gaajawanti kɔkɔ ki tīī unimpubɔti Eesiteer. Míǹ boonee ní Eesiteer cáá Maardoosee ki dàkā ubɔti ki tùkū-u yii úǹ di sá u-baa. 2Ní ubɔti fúutì u-bɔmbiki kin cáá u-daaŋku u nìn fōō Amaani ceeyee ki dūu tīī Maardoosee. Ní unimpubɔti Eesiteer dū Maardoosee ki kāaǹ tigaajawan tin kɔkɔ Amaani nìn cááyee pu.
Ubɔti nyántì mara kí mɔ̄tì Juuda yab pu
3Ní Eesiteer lítì ubɔti nimbiin nì nnyinnyim ki fātìi sòon̄ nì u ki gbāam̀-u yii ú kpìtī mbusu un Amaani un sá Agaagi naakookunee nìn nyàab̄ kí kɔ́ǹ-bee, nì u nín lēē nsàmbiyaamu mun kí céetí Juuda yabee. 4Ní ubɔti tāntì u-kpandɔŋu ŋun sá sindaariyee ki túĺ Eesiteer. Niinee ní Eesiteer yíkì kitiŋ ki yúl̀ ubɔti nimbiin 5ní ki bí-u yii: «Ti-baa ubɔti, m yaa ká diyimɔɔl a-cee, ní an yaa ŋān̄ a-cee m-bɔti fáatì-see, á ŋmà kí kpìtī mara un Ameedata jipɔɔn Amaani un sá Agaagi naakookunee ŋmàn̄ yii bí kpɔ̀ kí céetí Juuda yab bin kɔkɔ kóò a-tinjaŋŋi kɔkɔnee. 6Mana ní m ŋūǹ kí nīn kā ki kpèé inimɔɔn in bíi jīǹ m-nibulee? Mana ní m ŋūǹ kí nīn kā ki wāĺ bi bíi kù ki céetí m-nabiyaamu?»
7Ní ubɔti kíí unimpubɔti nì Maardoosee, ujuudaja yii: «Kpèè, m dū Amaani gaajati kɔkɔ ki tīī Eesiteer ní ki yāntì bi lúntì-u ndɔ pu, kun puee u bàà là bí kpɔ̀ Juuda yab. 8Di sá kugbɔŋu kun bi ŋmàn̄ ubɔti yindi pu, ki dū ubɔti jaliiki ki nyīīyee, nsan kpá ubɔ ń kpìtī tibɔti tin bi ŋmàn̄ee. Míǹ puee, ni mun ŋmàmaan min làá tūtuǹ Juuda yab bí mɔ̄tì bi-ba puee ubɔti yindi pu, kí dū ubɔti jaliiki kí nyīī.» 9Dicilpu niin ní bi yíiń ubɔti gbaŋŋmaliibi. Uŋmatataati un bi yíì yii Sifanee iwiin mmuŋku nì ita dal ní bi nìn yíiń-bi. Ní Maardoosee tùkū-bi bi nín làá ŋmà tibɔti tiŋyee. Bi nìn ŋmàn̄ tigbɔn ki tīī Juuda yab nì abɔtibil nì gɔminab nì bikàliŋkpilib bin bí ubɔti tinjaŋŋi dilaataal nì mmuŋku nì aluli poonee, kí yòon̄ Indiya tiŋki kí tin cáá sāā Kusa tiŋki. Bi nìn ŋmàn̄ ki tīī kitiŋ kamaa nì ki-ŋmaŋmabiti nì ki-sooŋyi poon ní ki ŋmàn̄ ki tīī Juuda yab mun nì bi-ŋmaŋmabiti nì bi-sooŋyi poon. 10Bi ŋmàn̄ tigbɔnee ubɔti Asuweerusi yindi pu, ní ki dū u-bɔmbiki kin cáá u-daaŋkuee ki nyīī ní ki dūu tīī bitanjakaliibi, bí yòon̄ ubɔti taamui in sá itammɔntee kí cáá tigbɔnee kí yàkatī. 11Tin bi ŋmàn̄ tigbɔn gbanti poonee sèé: «Ubɔti pú kinyɔkɔ yii Juuda yab bin bí u-tinjaŋŋi kɔkɔnee ń kpāfì kitiŋ kin poon bi bée kí mɔ̄tì bi-ba pu. Bí kpɔ̀ kí céetí dinibul din kamaa làá bóob́ dikɔ̀ndi kí jáǹ-bee, kí kpɔ̀ kí kpáaǹ bi-nimpoobi nì bi-biyaamu, kí kóoǹ bi-gaajawanti kɔkɔ.» 12Mara gbantee sá ŋwimbaanti ní an tɔ̄ ditundi ubɔti Asuweerusi tinjaŋŋi kɔkɔn. An dāa sá uŋmal saalaa nì uliliiti poon, Adaar ŋmaliu iwiin saalaa nì ita dal. 13Tin bi ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋuee poonee kpántì mara ní bi dūu tīī atinjan kɔkɔ nibuliŋ, án nín làá ŋá pu ní Juuda yab ń bɔ́ntí ŋwiin gbanti yaa láa bāańee, bí tɔ̀ bi-nannanliibi ipɔntoonee. 14Ubɔti nín pú kinyɔkɔ yii bí cáá tigbɔnee kí yàkatēe ní bitanjakaliibi yōoǹ ubɔti taamui in sá itammɔntee ki búntì malaa malaa ki cáa yākatì. Ní maree gbītì Suusi ditiŋyil kɔkɔn.
15Niinee Maardoosee nyánní ubɔti dumpu ki pēē dibeebɔkutil din ŋmàl̄ mmam gàaa nì mpimee, ki dū iŋaaman in bí fálfalee bɔkutifɔkɔl ki páaǹ ní ki cíkí sindaariya beefuuliiki kikpaaŋŋi. Suusi yab nìn kūuntí nì dipɔɔpindi ki fàal̀. 16An nìn sá dipɔɔpindi nì ifaal nì dinyandi ní Juuda yab cee. 17Atinjan nì ntimu mun kɔkɔ poon ní ubɔti marauee nìn bàn̄ee, an nìn sá dipɔɔpindi nì ifaal nì jiŋaal ní Juuda yab cee. Ní dinyoondi kɔ́ anibul ŋin kɔ kíǹee, ní an yāntì binib tikpil kpántì Juuda yab.

english_text:
The Jews Destroy Their Enemies
1The first law that the king had made was to be followed on the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month. This was the very day that the enemies of the Jews had hoped to do away with them. But the Jews turned things around, 2and in the cities of every province they came together to attack their enemies. Everyone was afraid of the Jews, and no one could do anything to oppose them.
3The leaders of the provinces, the rulers, the governors, and the court officials were afraid of Mordecai and took sides with the Jews. 4Everyone in the provinces knew that the king had promoted him and had given him a lot of power.
5The Jews took their swords and did away with their enemies, without showing any mercy. 6-10They killed 500 people in Susa, but they did not take anything that belonged to the ones they killed. Haman had been one of the worst enemies of the Jews, and ten of his sons were among those who were killed. Their names were Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha, Poratha, Adalia, Aridatha, Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai, and Vaizatha.
11Later that day, someone told the king how many people had been killed in Susa. 12Then he told Esther, “Five hundred people, including Haman's ten sons, have been killed in Susa alone. If that many were killed here, what must have happened in the provinces? Is there anything else you want done? Just tell me, and it will be done.”
13Esther answered, “Your Majesty, please let the Jews in Susa fight to defend themselves tomorrow, just as they did today. And order the bodies of Haman's ten sons to be hanged in public.”
14King Xerxes did what Esther had requested, and the bodies of Haman's sons were hung in Susa. 15Then on the fourteenth day of Adar the Jews of the city got together and killed 300 more people. But they still did not take anything that belonged to their enemies.
16-17On the thirteenth day of Adar, the Jews in the provinces had come together to defend themselves. They killed 75,000 of their enemies, but the Jews did not take anything that belonged to the ones they killed. Then on the fourteenth day of the month the Jews celebrated with a feast.
18 On the fifteenth day of the month the Jews in Susa held a holiday and celebrated, after killing their enemies on the thirteenth and the fourteenth. 19This is why the Jews in the villages now celebrate on the fourteenth day of the month. It is a joyful holiday that they celebrate by feasting and sending gifts of food to each other.
The Festival of Purim
20Mordecai wrote down everything that had happened. Then he sent letters to the Jews everywhere in the provinces 21and told them:
Each year you must celebrate on both the fourteenth and the fifteenth of Adar, 22the days when we Jews defeated our enemies. Remember this month as a time when our sorrow was turned to joy, and celebration took the place of crying. Celebrate by having parties and by giving to the poor and by sharing gifts of food with each other.
23They followed Mordecai's instructions and set aside these two days every year as a time of celebration.
The Reason for the Festival of Purim
24 Haman was the son of Hammedatha and a descendant of Agag. He hated the Jews so much that he planned to destroy them, but he wanted to find out the best time to do it. So he cast lots.
25Esther went to King Xerxes and asked him to save her people. Then the king gave written orders for Haman and his sons to be punished in the same terrible way that Haman had in mind for the Jews. So they were hanged. 26Mordecai's letter had said that the Jews must celebrate for two days because of what had happened to them. This time of celebration is called Purim, which is the Hebrew word for the lots that were cast. 27Now every year the Jews set aside these two days for having parties and celebrating, just as they were told to do. 28From now on, all Jewish families must remember to celebrate Purim on these two days each year.
29Queen Esther, daughter of Abihail, wanted to give full authority to Mordecai's letter about the Festival of Purim, and with his help she wrote a letter about the feast. 30Copies of this letter were sent to Jews in the 127 provinces of King Xerxes. In the letter they said:
We pray that all of you will live in peace and safety.
31You and your descendants must always remember to celebrate Purim at the time and in the way that we have said. You must also follow the instructions that we have given you about mourning and going without eating.
32These laws about Purim are written by the authority of Queen Esther.
translation_text:
Juuda yab tɔ̀n̄ bi-nannanliibi ipɔntoon
1Uŋmal saalaa nì uliliiti poon, Adaar ŋmaliu iwiin saalaa nì ita dal, ŋwiin ŋun bi nìn yóoǹ yii bí kpɔ̀ kí céetí Juuda yabee dūu bāań. Juuda yab nannanliibi dākafì yii bíǹ di làá pɔ̄ɔkiǹ-bi ŋwiin gbanti, ama ní an cúu lábitì ní Juuda yab pɔ́ɔkiǹ bin kpēē ki sīŋkiǹ-bee. 2Juuda yab nìn kpáfì ntimu mun poon bi bée ubɔti Asuweerusi tinjaŋŋi kɔkɔn ki cíitì bin kɔkɔ làá táká-bee. Ama báà ubɔ kaa nìn ŋúń ki yúl̀ bi-nimbiin, kun puee dinyoondi nìn cúú bi-nannanliibi kɔkɔ. 3Atinjan kɔkɔ kàliŋkpilib nì abɔtibil nì gɔminab nì ubɔti tɔntɔŋkpilib kɔkɔee nìn yú Juuda yab boon ní, kun puee bi nìn fàŋkí Maardoosee ní yɔ́kɔ́ yɔkɔ. 4Di sá Maardoosee nìn kā ŋkakaakpaan pu ní ubɔti beecindin, ní ki nìn nyáń diyindi kitiŋ jaaŋŋi kɔkɔn. Maardoosee yindi nìn mɔ̀tīi yíkí yilpu ní ki cá.
5Juuda yab nìn dū ntàataajimu ki kūū ki nāaǹ bi-nannanliibi kɔkɔ. Bíǹ bin nìn kpèé ki sìŋkīǹ Juuda yabee, Juuda yab ŋá-bi bi nín là puee. 6Juuda yab nìn kūū Suusi ditiŋyil poon bininjab alaataa aŋmoo. 7Bi nìn kūū ki kpáaǹ Parsandata nì Daalifɔn nì Asipata 8nì Poorata nì Adaliya nì Ardata 9nì Parmasta nì Arisayi nì Ardayi nì Wayisata. 10Ameedata jipɔɔn Amaani, Juuda yab pulincɔnti jipɔmbi saalaa gbantee, bi nìn kūū bi-kɔkɔ, ama baa nìn gbēē bin bi kūūyee wanti báà kubɔ.
11Ŋwimbaanti gbanti ní bi tùkū ubɔti bininjab bin nyɔkɔm bi kūū Suusi ditiŋyilinee. 12Ní ubɔti bí unimpubɔti Eesiteer yii: «Suusi ditiŋyil ní Juuda yab kūū bininjab alaataa aŋmoo ki kpáaǹ Amaani jipɔmbi saalaayee, mimmee m-tinjaŋŋi ŋin kíǹee poonee, bi ŋá mana? A yaa gíti là tiba ḿ ŋá kí tīī-si, bàlifì-mi m làá tīī-si kudɔŋu. Ba ní a là ní?» 13Ní Eesiteer kíí yii: «Ti-baa ubɔti, a yaa bàà kíikée, á pɔ̄ kinyɔkɔ fool marauee ń nìkī díǹ Juuda yab bin bí Susee ń nìkī kujaau, ní kí dū Amaani jipɔmbi saalaayee kí lúntí ndɔ pu.» 14Ní ubɔti pú kinyɔkɔ yii bí ŋá míǹ, ní bi báakì maree Suusi tiŋkin. Ní bi dū Amaani jipɔmbi saalaa bin bi kūūyee ki lúntì ndɔ pu. 15Ní Juuda yab bin bí Suusee kpáfì Adaar ŋmaliu ŋwiin ŋubɔ kpá saalku dal Suusi tiŋkin, ní ki kūū bininjab alaataa ata. Ama baa nìn gbēē bin bi kūūyee wanti báà kubɔ.
16Juuda yab bin nìn bí ubɔti tinjaŋŋi ŋin kíǹee poonee mun nìn kpáfì ki mɔ́tì bi-ba pu ní ki kūū bi-nannanliibi kutukub biŋmoo kpá imuŋku inaa, ki ŋūŋfì bi-pu, ama baa nìn gbēē bin bi kūūyee wanti báà kubɔ. 17Uŋmal gbanti ŋwiin ŋubɔ kpá saalku dal ní bi gbēeǹ kaa ti bíi kù binib, ní bi dū ŋwiin gbanti ki kpántì jiŋaal nì dipɔɔpindi wiiŋŋu. 18Ama Juuda yab bin nìn bí Suusi ki nìn kpáfì iwiin saalaa nì ita, nì ŋubɔ kpá saalku dal ki tɔ̀n̄ bi-nannanliibi pu ipɔntoonee nìn kāl̀ iwiin saalku dal ní ki ŋūŋfì. Bíǹ nìn dū ŋwiin gbanti ní ki kpántì jiŋaal nì dipɔɔpindi wiiŋŋu. 19An pu ní Juuda yab bin nìn kóò ntiŋgbamu poonee nìn dū Adaar ŋmaliu ŋwiin ŋubɔ kpá saalku dal ki kpántì jiŋaal nì dipɔɔpindi wiiŋŋu, ki ŋáań tijin ki pūǹ tɔb.
Bi yóoǹ kí nīn kíǹ ki jīǹ Puuriim jiŋaaliu
20Maardoosee nìn ŋmàn̄ tin kɔkɔ jítèe ki bíl̀. U nìn ŋmàn̄ tigbɔn ki tīī Juuda yab bin kɔkɔ bí ubɔti Asuweerusi tinjaŋŋi ŋin pìl̄ee nì ŋin dátèe kɔkɔn. 21U nìn tùkū-bi yii dibintil kamaa, Adaar ŋmaliu ŋwiin ŋubɔ kpá saalku nì iwiin saalku dalee, bí nīn jīǹ jiŋaal gbanti. 22Di sá yii iwiin gbanti poon ní Juuda yab fōō bi-ba ki ŋūŋfì bi-nannanliibi pu. Adaar ŋmaliu poon ní mpɔn nìn cúu lábitì ní kunimbaau kpántì dipɔɔpindi ní dikpool kpántì jiŋaal. Iwiin gbantin ní Juuda yab ŋáań tijin ki tìì tɔb ní ki pūǹ biwɔfib tiwan. 23Ní Juuda yab fōō Maardoosee nyɔkɔ, ní ki dū jiŋaal un bi jíńee ki kpántì diyaajakoobil kí nīn kíǹ ki ŋáań míǹ.
24Di sá Ameedata un sá Agaagi naakookunee jipɔɔn Amaani, Juuda yab nannanliu nìn bóob́ yii bí kúntí Juuda yab. U nìn tɔ́ Puur, an dàkà yii u tɔ́ kasi kí béé ŋwiin ŋun máaǹ bí kpɔ̀ kí kúntí-bee. 25Ama Eesiteer nìn cūtì ki ká ubɔti tibɔti gbanti pu, ní ubɔti yāntì bi ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu yii ntoom tafadaaldi din Amaani bɔ́ntì Juuda yab puee ń fàtīí lítí u-pu, ní bi dū u nì u-jipɔmbi ki lúntì idɔ pu. 26An pu ní bi nìn pú jiŋaal gbanti wiiŋyi yii Puuriim, kí dàkà yii bi nìn tɔ́ Puur ní ki lēē iwiin gbanti.
Maardoosee nín nìn ŋmàn̄ tibɔti tin kugbɔŋu poonee nì Juuda yab bi-ba nín nìn ká tiŋyee nì tin nìn jítì bi-puee, 27ní bi dūu kpántì bi-yaajakoobil. Bíǹ nì bi-naantitɔntɔkɔŋ nì bin kɔkɔ làá dāá páanní bi-boonee làá nīn jīǹ jiŋaal gbanti dibintil kamaa iwiin ili gbanti poon, kii bi nín ŋmàn̄ ki yóoǹ yii bí nīn jīǹ-u puee. 28Míǹ ní kudicaŋu kamaa nì atinjan kɔkɔ nì kitiŋ kamaa nib làá nīn téetí iwiin gbanti pu ki jīǹ jiŋaal kí nīn cáa cá. An puee Juuda yab ń taa gbèen̄ Puuriim jiŋaaliu nee jītam, kí taa súntí u-pu kí nīn pée cáa cá jaanjaan.
29Unimpubɔti Eesiteer, Abiikayiil bisal nì ujuudaja Maardoosee ŋmàn̄ kugbɔnliliitiiu kí tīī kugbɔŋu kun bi nìn ŋmàn̄ Puuriim puee mpɔn. 30Bi nìn ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋuee ní ki dūu yākatì ubɔti Asuweerusi tinjaŋŋi dilaataal nì mmuŋku nì alulee poon. Bi nìn mēē ŋgbansɔŋfi nì dipɔɔpindi ki tīī Juuda yab kugbɔŋuee poon, 31ní ki kpáafì-bi bí nīn jīǹ Puuriim jiŋaaliu iwiin gbanti. Án nīn sá-bi dinyɔɔboobil nì itiminsi wiiŋyi, kii Maardoosee ujuudaja nì unimpubɔti Eesiteer nín yóoǹ yii bíǹ bi-ba nì bi-naantitɔntɔkɔŋ ń nīn ŋáań puee. 32Ní bi dū Eesiteer nín yóoǹ mara un Puuriim puee bɔti ki ŋmàn̄ ki ŋá kugbɔŋun.

english_text:
The Greatness of Xerxes and Mordecai
1King Xerxes made everyone in his kingdom pay taxes, even those in lands across the sea. 2All the great and famous things that King Xerxes did are written in the record books of the kings of Media and Persia. These records also tell about the honors that the king gave to Mordecai. 3Next to the king himself, Mordecai was the highest official in the kingdom. He was a popular leader of the Jews, because he helped them in many ways and would even speak to the king on their behalf.
translation_text:
Maardoosee nyandi diluŋkikaal
1Ubɔti Asuweerusi nìn wɔ́b́ u-tinjaŋŋi kɔkɔ nib, ki kpáaǹ bin kóò ntimu mun tiŋku māntìi túee bi pà lampoo. 2Dibaatandi din u cááyee nì atuŋkpaan ŋin u ŋáaǹee nì u nín yōoǹ Maardoosee yilpu u-beelin puee, bi ŋmàn̄ an bɔti kɔkɔ Meedi nì Peeriisi yab bɔtiibi gbɔŋkun. 3Tiŋman, Maardoosee ujuudaja nìn sá unikpaan ní. Ubɔtikpaan Asuweerusi yaa nìn līntèe, Maardoosee di nìn pá. U-yab Juuda yab nìn néeń-u ní ki nìn tɔ́-u. U nìn pée mɔ̀ ki nyàab̀ bi-ŋanti ŋma ní, ní ki nìn mɔ́tí u-nibul kɔkɔ pu.

english_text:
Job and His Family
1Many years ago, a man named Job lived in the land of Uz. He was a truly good person, who respected God and refused to do evil.
2Job had 7 sons and 3 daughters. 3He owned 7,000 sheep, 3,000 camels, 500 pair of oxen, 500 donkeys, and a large number of servants. He was the richest person in the East.
4Job's sons took turns having feasts in their homes, and they always invited their three sisters to join in the eating and drinking. 5After each feast, Job would send for his children and perform a ceremony, as a way of asking God to forgive them of any wrongs they may have done. He would get up early the next morning and offer a sacrifice for each of them, just in case they had sinned or silently cursed God.
Angels, the Lord, and Satan
6 One day, when the angels had gathered around the Lord, and Satan was there with them, 7the Lord asked, “Satan, where have you been?”
Satan replied, “I have been going all over the earth.”
8Then the Lord asked, “What do you think of my servant Job? No one on earth is like him—he is a truly good person, who respects me and refuses to do evil.”
9 “Why shouldn't he respect you?” Satan remarked. 10“You are like a wall protecting not only him, but his entire family and all his property. You make him successful in whatever he does, and his flocks and herds are everywhere. 11Try taking away everything he owns, and he will curse you to your face.”
12The Lord replied, “All right, Satan, do what you want with anything that belongs to him, but don't harm Job.”
Then Satan left.
Job Loses Everything
13Job's sons and daughters were having a feast in the home of his oldest son, 14when someone rushed up to Job and said, “While your servants were plowing with your oxen, and your donkeys were nearby eating grass, 15a gang of Sabeans attacked and stole the oxen and donkeys! Your other servants were killed, and I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
16That servant was still speaking, when a second one came running and said, “God sent down a fire that killed your sheep and your servants. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
17Before that servant finished speaking, a third one raced up and said, “Three gangs of Chaldeans attacked and stole your camels! All of your other servants were killed, and I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
18That servant was still speaking, when a fourth one dashed up and said, “Your children were having a feast and drinking wine at the home of your oldest son, 19when suddenly a windstorm from the desert blew the house down, crushing all of your children. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
20When Job heard this, he tore his clothes and shaved his head because of his great sorrow. He knelt on the ground, then worshiped God 21 and said:
“We bring nothing at birth;
we take nothing
with us at death.
The Lord alone gives and takes.
Praise the name of the Lord!”
22In spite of everything, Job did not sin or accuse God of doing wrong.
translation_text:
Unimbɔti yāntì Sitaan cɔ́ŋkì Yoob
1Uninja ubɔ nìn bí Uusi tiŋkin bi yíì-u Yoob. Baa nìn kāntí u-pu tikpitil tiba ní u-pɔbil nìn bí diba nì Unimbɔti. U nìn fàŋkí Unimbɔti ní ki nìn fàtī u-boon ki tìì ikpiti. 2U nìn cáá mbininjabiyaamu mululi nì nnimpubiyaamu muta. 3U nìn cáá ipii kutukub biluli, igutaamu kutukub bita, inajaa kutuku nì mmansalimu alaataa aŋmoo nì bitɔntɔnliibi tikpil. Ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee, ubɔ kaa nìn cáá tigaajati ki bàn̄ Yoob.
4Yoob jipɔmbi kansikin ubɔ nìn ŋáań tijin u-dumpu ní u nì bin kɔkɔ kíǹee ń kpāfì kí jī. Bi nìn ŋáań míǹ ní ki kpántí ní ki nìn yíì bi-niisalib bitee, ní bí kpāfì kí jī kí nyɔ̀. 5Bi yaa nìn jíń jíń míǹ ki dóòyee ní Yoob ń yíiń-bi ní kí ŋá-bi circir. U nìn yíkí kutaafaau pɔ̀lpɔl ní kí ŋá saraawɔkaa u-biyaamu kɔkɔ yil pu, di sá yii u nìn lì yii: «An yaa yíì m-jipɔmbi ŋá ikpiti ki tɔ́ Unimbɔti mbusu bi-pɔbiliŋin.» Míǹ ní Yoob nìn pée ŋáań ŋyunti kamaa.
6Dalba, Unimbɔti tuuŋyi dɔ́miń ti-Dindaan kpafil. Sitaan, ukuŋfil mun nìn bí bi-kansikin. 7Ti-Dindaan nìn bālifì Sitaan yii: «La ní a nyánní ní?» Ní Sitaan kíí ti-Dindaan yii: «M cūtìi yìin̄ yìin̄ ki māntì kitiŋ pu ní.» 8Niinee ní ti-Dindaan bí Sitaan yii: «A ká m-tɔntɔnliu Yoobaa! Waa cáá juti kitiŋ pu. Baa kāntí u-pu tikpitil tiba ní u-pɔbil bí diba nì mi. U fàŋkí man Unimbɔti ní ki fàtī u-boon ki tìì ikpiti.» 9Ama ní ukuŋfil kíí-u yii: «A nyí yii an sá fám ní Yoob fàŋkí-saaa? 10Sii di kaa dū a-wundi ki bàkā u nì u-dicaŋku nì u-gaajati kɔkɔ pu kii digundeeee? A bīiǹ u-tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ pu ní ki yāntì u-waŋkuti būtì ki gbí kitiŋ kɔkɔ. 11Ama a yaa là, á tàntī a-ŋal kí fōō tin kɔkɔ u cááyee kí kpèè u yaa kaa sòon̄ ki bíil̀-si!» 12Niinee ní ti-Dindaan bí ukuŋfil yii: «Too, tin kɔkɔ u cááyee bí a-ŋaan. Ama á nīn nyíǹ a-ba kí taa gbēē úǹ u-ba.»
Niinee ní ukuŋfil nyáń ti-Dindaan nimbiin ki nín cá.
13Dalba Yoob bisalib nì u-jipɔmbi kpáfì bi-maan ukpil cee ki bíi jīǹ ki nyù, 14ní ntuun dūu bāań Yoob cee ki bí-u yii: «Inaa bàà bíi kù tikpaal ní mmansalimu bí ki kɔ́ĺ-i ki ŋmóò timool, 15ní Seeba yab péetì-i ní ki kūū a-tɔntɔnliibi. Man baba di pée ŋmátì ní ki dɔ́miń kí tùkù-si.»
16Yoob tɔntɔnliuee nìn dáá bíi sòoǹ u-nyɔkɔ kaa láá ŋmíl̀ ní ubɔ mun dūu bāań ki bí-u yii: «Unimbɔti ŋmiŋu ŋubɔ nyánní yilpu ki wùn̄ ipii nì a-tɔntɔnliibi kɔkɔ. Man baba di pée ŋmátì ní ki dɔ́miń kí tùkù-si.»
17U nìn dáá bíi sòoǹ kaa láá ŋmíl̀ ní ubɔ mun tí bāań ki bí yii: «Kaaldee yab ŋá akiti ata ki dɔ́miń ki jéetì a-gutaamui pu ki péetì-i ní ki dū ntàataajimu ki kūū a-tɔntɔnliibi kɔkɔ. Man baba di pée ŋmátì ní m dɔ́miń kí tùkù-si.»
18U nìn dáá bíi sòoǹ kaa láá ŋmíl̀ ní ubɔ mun tí bāań ki bí yii: «A-bisalib nì a-jipɔmbi bàà bí bi-maan ukpil cee ki bíi jīǹ ki nyù 19ní kubuŋkpaaŋŋu kubɔ nyánní kuteeu pú ki yá kudii jannaatiliŋ. Kudiiyee lítì ki tàb̄ binipɔmbee ki kūū-bi. Man baba di pée ŋmátì ní m dɔ́miń kí tùkù-si.»
20Niinee Yoob nyīī yíkì ki cúú u-bɔkutikpaandi ki dáaĺ ki cátì ní ki kōol̀ u-yil diyibaakpandi ní ki tātìi gbāaǹ u-yigbeel tūū kitiŋ 21ki lī yii:
«M nyáń m-na poon dicancaŋgbeel ní,
dicancaŋgbeel ní m làá tí fàtīí gítí.
Ti-Dindaan di tīī,
ti-Dindaan di cúú ki fōō.
Ti-Dindaan yindi ń ká tinyool!»
22Agìń gbanti kɔkɔ poonee, Yoob kaa nìn ŋá ikpiti. Waa nìn sòon̄ ki bíil̀ Unimbɔti.

english_text:
Job Loses His Health
1When the angels gathered around the Lord again, Satan was there with them, 2and the Lord asked, “Satan, where have you been?”
Satan replied, “I have been going all over the earth.”
3Then the Lord asked, “What do you think of my servant Job? No one on earth is like him—he is a truly good person, who respects me and refuses to do evil. And he hasn't changed, even though you persuaded me to destroy him for no reason.”
4Satan answered, “There's no pain like your own. People will do anything to stay alive. 5Try striking Job's own body with pain, and he will curse you to your face.”
6“All right!” the Lord replied. “Make Job suffer as much as you want, but just don't kill him.” 7Satan left and caused painful sores to break out all over Job's body—from head to toe.
8Then Job sat on the ash-heap to show his sorrow. And while he was scraping his sores with a broken piece of pottery, 9his wife asked, “Why do you still trust God? Why don't you curse him and die?”
10Job replied, “Don't talk like a fool! If we accept blessings from God, we must accept trouble as well.” In all that happened, Job never once said anything against God.
Job's Three Friends
11Eliphaz from Teman, Bildad from Shuah, and Zophar from Naamah were three of Job's friends, and they heard about his troubles. So they agreed to visit Job and comfort him. 12When they came near enough to see Job, they could hardly recognize him. And in their great sorrow, they tore their clothes, then sprinkled dust on their heads and cried bitterly. 13For seven days and nights, they sat silently on the ground beside him, because they realized what terrible pain he was in.
translation_text:
Sitaan gíti cɔ́ŋkì Yoob nliliitiim
1Dalba muee, Unimbɔti tuuŋyi tí dɔ́miń ti-Dindaan kpafil. Sitaan, ukuŋfil mun nìn tí bí bi-kansikin kí dū u-ba kí dàkà. 2Ti-Dindaan nìn bālifì-u yii: «La ní a nyánní ní?» Ní Sitaan kíí ti-Dindaan yii: «M cūtìi yìin̄ yìin̄ ki māntì kitiŋ pu ní.» 3Niinee ní ti-Dindaan bí Sitaan yii: «A ká m-tɔntɔnliu Yoobaa! Waa cáá juti kitiŋ pu. Baa kāntí u-pu tikpitil tiba ní u-pɔbil bí diba nì mi. U fàŋkí man Unimbɔti ní ki fàtī u-boon ki tìì ikpiti. U gbíntìi yú nì mi nì dipɔbil diba, min kamaa a yāntì m nāaǹ-u fámee.» 4Ama ní Sitaan kíí ti-Dindaan yii: «Iween iba kaa wù ki bàn̄ an yaa kā sii a-ba puee! Unil kíikí kí dū tin kɔkɔ u cááyee kí tīī kí ŋmā kí fīī u-ba. 5Míǹ puee dū igbaŋween kí tɔ̄ u-pu kí kpèè u yaa kaa sòon̄ ki bíil̀-si!» 6Niinee ní ti-Dindaan bí ukuŋfilee yii: «Too, u bí a-ŋaan, ama á taa nín gbēē u-maŋfal ní.»
7Sitaan nyáń ti-Dindaan nimbiinee ní ki nín cá, ní ki cūtìi dū ibunsoon ki tɔ́ Yoob pu kí kíĺ u-taaŋi taapu kí cáá sāā u-yil kansikin. 8Niinee ní Yoob tātìi kāl̀ ŋfantamin ní ki nyàab̄ abɔkati ki kɔ́tí u-ba.
9Ní u-nimpuu bí-u yii: «A gbíntìi dáá máká Unimbɔti puɔɔɔ? Pùtì sòoǹ kí bīil̀ Unimbɔti kí kpú!» 10Ama ní Yoob kíí-u yii: «A sòoǹ kii unimpu un yil kaa bí kudiinee. Ti fòol̄ nnaam min Unimbɔti tìì-tee, kin ba pu ní tí yíí kí taa fōō nnaabu ŋun u tīī-ti nee?»
Tin bí nee kɔkɔ poonee, Yoob kaa nìn wāaǹ u-nyɔkɔ ki sòon̄ ki yīntiǹ Unimbɔti.
Yoob bɔɔbi bita dɔ́miń ki māntì u-pu
11Yoob bɔɔbi bita gbìl̄ agìń ŋin jéetì u-puee ní báà ŋma yíkìń u-tiŋkin ki ŋá kinyɔɔbaantii kí cùú sɔ̄ kí tūtuǹ Yoob kí ŋméeǹ-u. Bíǹ di sá uteemanja Eeliifaasi nì usuwaja Biilidaadi nì unaamaja Soofaar. 12Bi nín wálìń-u ndanee, baa ti béè-u. Niinee ní bi kíĺ ki bíi sūǹ mpɔn. Bi nìn cúú tiwan tin bi pēēyee ki cátì ní ki nìn dū ŋfantam ki pùkū bi-yiliŋ kí dàkà bi-nimbaaku. 13Bi ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki dɔ́miń ki kāl̀ kitiŋ ki kɔ́ĺ Yoob ki ŋá iwiin iluli ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu. Báà ubɔ kaa nìn wāaǹ kinyɔkɔ ki sòon̄ nì u, di sá yii bi nìn ká yii u bíi jīǹ falaa tikpil.

english_text:
Job's First Speech
Blot Out the Day of My Birth
1 Finally, Job cursed the day
of his birth
2by saying to God:
3Blot out the day of my birth
and the night when my parents
created a son.
4Forget about that day,
cover it with darkness,
5and send thick, gloomy shadows
to fill it with dread.
6Erase that night from the calendar
and conceal it with darkness.
7Don't let children be created
or joyful shouts be heard
ever again in that night.
8Let those with magic powers
place a curse on that day.
9Darken its morning stars
and remove all hope of light,
10because it let me be born
into a world of trouble.
Why Didn't I Die at Birth?
11Why didn't I die at birth?
12Why was I accepted
and allowed to nurse
at my mother's breast?
13Now I would be at peace
in the silent world below
14with kings and their advisors
whose palaces lie in ruins,
15and with rulers once rich
with silver and gold.
16I wish I had been born dead
and then buried, never to see
the light of day.
17In the world of the dead,
the wicked and the weary rest
without a worry.
* 18Everyone is there—
19where captives and slaves
are free at last.
Why Does God Let Me Live?
20Why does God let me live
when life is miserable
and so bitter?
21 I keep longing for death
more than I would seek
a valuable treasure.
22Nothing could make me happier
than to be in the grave.
23Why do I go on living
when God has me surrounded,
and I can't see the road?
24Moaning and groaning
are my food and drink,
25and my worst fears
have all come true.
26I have no peace or rest—
only troubles and worries.
translation_text:
YOOB NÌ U-BƆƆBI BITEE NÍN SÒON̄ NÌ TƆB PUEE
(3–31)
Yoob bíi yáliŋkí nì u-ba
1Míǹ boonee ní Yoob dāa wāaǹ kinyɔkɔ ki tɔ́ ŋwiin ŋun bi màl̄-uee mbusu. 2U nín nìn sòon̄ puee sɔ̀.
3M bàà là yii Unimbɔti ń kúntí ŋwiin ŋun ní bi màl̄-mee,
kí kúntí kunyeeu kun ní m-na cáá m-poolee.
4Ŋwiin gbanti ń kpántí dibɔmbɔndi wiiŋŋu!
Ŋu-bɔti ń taa ti nín̄ ká Yilpu Fɔ́ŋŋŋ Nimbɔtiu!
Ŋwalifi ŋubɔ ń taa ti ŋmíntí-ŋu!
5Dibɔmbɔndi nì ŋkúm booŋŋu ń nīn bàlifī ŋu-pu,
atagban ń nīn pée bīī ŋu-pu,
uŋmal ń cúú ŋwìiń ŋwiin gbanti.
6Kunyeeu kun ní m-na díkí m-poolee ń nīn bɔ̀ǹ kí jītíǹ tinyati kɔkɔ,
bí taa ti kàaǹ-ŋu kí kūtì dibindi poon wiiŋyi pu,
ní bí taa ti kàaǹ-ŋu kí kūtì iŋmal wiiŋyi pu!
7Unimpu ubɔ ń taa ti cáá dipool kunyeeu kun ní m-na nìn cáá m-poolee,
bí taa ti gbìl̄ ifaal kuŋkuuntii pu kunyeeu gbanti!
8Bin tòó iwiin mbusu,
ki nyí bi nín fìntī kupeebiliŋŋu Draagɔn puee
ń tɔ̄ kunyeeu gbanti mbusu.
9Ku-taafaaŋmalbijaai ń kpántí dibɔmbɔndi!
Kú cīití kutaa wúntitam kí gīī
kí taa wāl̀ ntaafaawìiń!
10Di sá yii kuaa ŋá tiba ki pīiǹ m-na maaliŋu ki yāntì u màl̄-mi
m dāa kɔ́ nnaabu ŋun poon m kɔ́ nee.
*
11Ba pu ní maa kpíì m-na poon ní?
Ba pu ní bi nín màl̄-mi kpalaayee, maa kpíì ní?
12Ba pu ní m ká ataa ali ŋin làl̄-mee ní?
Ba pu ní m ká abii ali ki ŋáam̀ ní?
13Kɔnampu nee m bàà bí ŋgbansɔŋfin dikaakulin.
M bàà dɔ̄ ki gèeǹ ki ŋùŋfī
14nì bibɔtiibi nì kitiŋ pu yidambi
bin nìn fātìi máń tibɔtinaakɔti tin nìn lítèe,
15nì abɔtibil ŋin cáá sindaariya
ní animbil gbí bi-diiŋŋinee.
16Àá ba pu ní baa dū-mi ki bál̀ kitiŋin kii kibiki kin bi lēē ki fée,
a lì kii kibiki kin bi màl̄ kaa yōoǹee.
17Dikaakulinee, binikpitib kàal̀ soooo,
ní binib bin túń ditundi ki gīīyee kāntí diŋuŋfil.
18Bisarkadambi kāntí dibatɔl,
baa ti gbìl̀ bijanjaliibi bin cí-bee nyɔkɔ pu.
19Ŋwaamu nì bikpaambi kɔkɔ bí niin ní,
uyumbu kpiliu kaa ti cáá u-pu mpɔn.
*
20Ba pu ní Unimbɔti yàntī bin jīǹ falaayee gbíntì bí dimaŋfalin ní?
Ba pu ní bin poon kaam cɔ́tèe gbíntìi fòotī ní?
21Bi kā ki cí ŋkúm, ama ŋkúm kaa dòoń,
bi fíkití an kɔkɔ pu ki nyàab̀-mì kii tigaajawammɔntiilee.
22Bi yaa bàà ká dikaakul diba poon kí dòon̄,
bi bàà làá nīn bí dipɔɔpindin ki fàal̀ ní!
23Ba pu ní Unimbɔti tìì unil un kaa nyí laakin u cée dimaŋfal ní?
An niliu ní Unimbɔti dù kunaabakau kí bàkā u-pu!
24Diniindi di kpántì m-jinti,
ní m dùǹ kii nnyim nín pùub̀ puee.
25Kun fàantí-mee di bàń-mi,
kun m fàŋkée ní m kāntí.
26Maa cáá ŋgbansɔŋfi, kaa cáá dibatɔl,
kaa cáá diŋuŋfil, ama iyaliŋki di māntìi tú-mi.

english_text:
Eliphaz's First Speech
Please Be Patient and Listen
1Eliphaz from Teman said:
2Please be patient and listen
to what I have to say.
* 3Remember how your words
4have guided and encouraged
many in need.
5But now you feel discouraged
when struck by trouble.
6You respect God and live right,
so don't lose hope!
7No truly innocent person
has ever died young.
8In my experience, only those
who plant seeds of evil
harvest trouble,
9and then they are swept away
by the angry breath of God.
10They may roar and growl
like powerful lions.
But when God breaks their teeth,
11they starve, and their children
are scattered.
A Secret Was Told to Me
12A secret was told to me
in a faint whisper—
13 I was overcome by sleep,
but disturbed by dreams;
14I trembled with fear,
15and my hair stood on end,
as a wind blew past my face.
16It stopped and stood still.
Then a form appeared—
a shapeless form.
And from the silence,
I heard a voice say,
17“No humans are innocent
in the eyes of God
their Creator.
18He finds fault with his servants
and even with his angels.
19Humans are formed from clay
and are fragile as moths,
so what chance do you have?
20Born after daybreak,
you die before nightfall
and disappear forever.
21Your tent pegs are pulled up,
and you leave this life,
having gained no wisdom.”
translation_text:
Eeliifaasi nín sòon̄ puee: Unil un Unimbɔti dátí u-tafalee bí mmɔnneeee!
1Niinee ní uteemanja Eeliifaasi fōō dinyɔɔbundi ní ki bí yii:
2An nín píĺ-si puee, taa bàà là kí sòoǹ.
Ama taa ŋūǹ kí nīn ŋmí míǹ ki cá.
3A nìn dàkā binib tikpil
ki nìn tútuǹ biwɔfib bi ká mpɔn.
4A-nyɔɔbuŋŋi nìn tīkintí bin cá kí lítée.
A nìn tìì bin gīīyee mpɔn.
5Kɔŋkɔnnee, sii ní agìń bāań a-wunti yɔ̄tèe.
An bāań-si dee, ní tifaandi cúú-si!
6A nín fàŋkí Unimbɔti puee kaa sá a-mákalaaa?
Bi nín kaa kāntí tikpitil tiba a-puee kaa tìì-si dimákalaaa?
7Téetí tin bí nee, Unimbɔti pée nāaǹ maanyiiba dalba a káaa,
àá u nāaǹ ubulcinnil ní a ká ní?
8M dáań ki ká tin bí nee yii:
Unil yaa kùn̄ tikpitil ki búĺ agìńee,
u dāa cēē tikpitil nì agìń mun ní.
9Unimbɔti yaa fōotèe, bi kúù ní,
u-ŋuul fooku di wù-bi kii ŋŋmee.
10U yàntī gbikinti kaa ti mùuǹ ní upeecuncuti kaa ti sūǹ
ní agbikintipɔmbil nyiŋŋi kɔ́fí.
11Ugbikintija kúù, kun puee waa ká tiba kí cúú kí ŋmɔ́,
ugbikintinaati biyaamu sáǹ ki yàl̄.
*
12M fōō tibɔti tiba dibalin,
bi lɔ́kɔfì tibɔti tiba m-tafalin,
13ŋyunti ŋun binib dámintí kunyeeu
bi-landɔkɔi kóò fikil fikil poonee,
ŋyunti ŋun binib dɔ̄ ki gèeǹ fɔ̀rtititee.
14M nìn fāŋkì ní tiwool kɔ́-mi
ní m-wunti bíi jìkì.
15Kubuŋu kubɔ nìn bíi fátí m-nimbiin
ní m-wunti sáǹ yàrrr.
16Ubɔ nìn yú niin maa béè-u tiŋan,
kujiliŋu kubɔ nìn bí m-nimbiin.
An nìn dáá ŋmí, ní boonee m dāa gbìl̄ m-neen ŋubɔ pu yii:
17«Nisaal ŋūǹ kí nīn bí deedee Unimbɔti nimbiinaaa?
Unil ŋūǹ kí nīn bí circir un náań-uee nimbiinaaa?
18Unimbɔti kaa máká u-tuuŋyi pu,
u kāntí úǹ u-ba tɔntɔnliibi pu tikpitil ki sòoǹ.
19Kin ataa aŋa pu ní u làá nīn máká nisaalib pu?
Di sá yii kuyɔkɔu ní bi dūu máń-bi
ní bi-wunti sá ntam.
Baa pée pɔ̄ɔ̄ dimatil kii kugbuluŋgbuŋŋuee ní!
20Unil ŋūǹ kí nīn bí dimaŋfalin kutaafaau,
ama ku dāa jóotée, u kpántì un kaa ti bée kí nīn cá jaanjaan,
ní ubɔ kaa kpáàa dūu yíiń tiba.
21Ŋŋmii ŋun ŋúb́ bi-maŋfalee cúu tīl̀,
ní bí kpú kaa kpáàa ká iciin.»

english_text:
Eliphaz Continues
Call Out for Help
1Job, call out for help
and see if an angel comes!
2Envy and jealousy
will kill a stupid fool.
3I have seen fools take root.
But God sends a curse,
suddenly uprooting them
4and leaving their children
helpless in court.
5Then hungry and greedy people
gobble up their crops
and grab their wealth.
6Our suffering isn't caused
by the failure of crops;
7it's all part of life,
like sparks shooting skyward.
8Job, if I were you,
I would ask God for help.
9 His miracles are marvelous,
more than we can count.
10God sends showers on earth
and waters the fields.
11He protects the sorrowful
and lifts up those
who have been disgraced.
* 12God swiftly traps the wicked
13 in their own evil schemes,
and their wisdom fails.
14Darkness is their only companion,
hiding their path at noon.
15God rescues the needy
from the words of the wicked
and the fist of the mighty.
16The poor are filled with hope,
and injustice is silenced.
Consider Yourself Fortunate
17 Consider yourself fortunate
if God All-Powerful
chooses to correct you.
18 He may cause injury and pain,
but he will bandage and heal
your cuts and bruises.
19God will protect you from harm,
no matter how often
trouble may strike.
20In times of war and famine,
God will keep you safe.
21You will be sheltered,
without fear of hurtful words
or any other weapon.
22You will laugh at the threat
of destruction and famine.
And you won't be afraid
of wild animals—
23they will no longer be fierce,
and your rocky fields
will become friendly.
24Your home will be secure,
and your sheep will be safe.
25You will have more descendants
than there are blades of grass
on the face of the earth.
26You will live a very long life,
and your body will be strong
until the day you die.
27Our experience has proven
these things to be true,
so listen and learn.
translation_text:
1Fáá mbiil kí kpèè ubɔ yaa kíí-si.
U-tuuŋyi ŋulɔŋu ní a ŋūǹ kí sòoǹ nì ní?
2Ugbaan ŋuul di kù-u,
kinaatuui poompooŋyi di yàntī u kúù.
3Tiŋman, m lafun ká an bútì ugbaan,
ama maa tāaǹ ní ki tɔ́ u-kɔŋkooŋŋu mbusu yii:
4«U-biyaamu ń taa ká dijòońdi!
Bí sòoǹ kí kpɔ̀ mu-bɔti kubɔsoondiin, ubɔ ń nīn kpá kí mɔ̄tì mu-pu!
5Kun udaan cáńee, bin ŋkùm cááyee ń dūú jī!
Bí yòon̄ kí kpáàa búntí, min kamaa bi dū ikuŋkum ki bàkēe!
Bin nnyinnyoo cááyee ń gbáb́ kí bìin̄ u-gaajati pu.»
6Di sá yii nnaabu kaa nyēeń kitiŋ,
míǹ ní falaa mun kaa ti cɔ́tiń kitiŋ.
7Ama bi màl̄ unil digìńdi pu ní,
a lì kii iŋmiyatiyaal nín yíkí ki ŋàaǹ puee.
*
8Man di yaa bàà sá siiyee, m bàà làá nyàab̀ Unimbɔti ní,
úǹ ŋaan ní m bàà làá dū m-bɔti kí ŋá.
9U tūǹ atuŋkpaan ŋin nyóò unil kaa ŋūǹ kí gbìl̄ ŋi-taapuee ní.
U-maamaaci tuuŋŋi kaa cáá ŋkaan.
10Úǹ di yàntī utaa nì kitiŋ pu,
ki yàntī nnyim nyēeń yilpu ki sɔ̀ŋkī tisati.
11Úǹ di yòontí bin dɔ̄ kitiŋ ki fìlim̀ee yilpu,
ní ki yàntī bin kā dikpoolee kāntí mmɔn.
12Úǹ di bíiĺ milimilidambi nín bɔ́ntì kí ŋá tiŋyee.
Waa yàntī an bútí-bi.
13Úǹ di gīintí biciŋfitiibi ciiŋyi ki fàtīi cáa cútí-bi,
ní ki bíiĺ milimilidambi nín bɔ́ntì puee.
14Bi gbéetí dibɔmbɔndi ŋwiimpu,
ní ki táfí kuwiŋkaŋu pu kii kunyeeuee.
15Ama Unimbɔti fìil̄ unandaan ki nyāntí bi-nyɔmmun,
u fìil̄ ufalaadaan ki nyāntí ubaatandaan ŋaan.
16Uwɔfi kíǹ ki cáá dimákal,
ama Unimbɔti pīiǹ binikpitib nyɔmmu.
17Kpèè, unil un tafal Unimbɔti dátée bí mmɔnneeee!
Míǹ puee Yoob, taa kpèè
Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan tafadaaldi fám.
*
18Unimbɔti di tìì unil tiweendi,
úǹ di tí nyìitī u-buuŋŋu,
úǹ di kù unil ní kí tí cáaǹ-u mun.
19U làá nyāntí-si agìń poon ŋfunyɔm miluu pu,
ní nluluútiimee, tikpitil tiba kaa làá ŋá-si.
20Ŋkùm yuntiŋuee, u làá fīī-si kí nyāntí ŋkúm ŋaan,
ní kí fīī-si kí nyāntí kitàataajiki ŋaan kujaau yuntiŋu.
21Unimbɔti làá wúń a-pu bikuŋfiliibi ń taa ŋá-si tiba,
nnaabu yuntiŋuee, aa làá fàŋkì tiba.
22Nnaabu nì ŋkùm yuntiŋuee, a làá nīn bí ní ki lāā,
ní kaa làá fàŋkì ipeel mun.
23Ataŋkpee kaa làá páb́-si a-saakun,
ní ipeel ń kpántí a-bɔɔbi.
24Ŋgbansɔŋfi làá nīn bí a-dicaŋkun.
A làá dāá kpèè a-waŋkuti ní kí ká yii kubɔ kaa wáŋkì.
25A làá dāá ká yii a-maaliŋu būtì.
A-naantiibi làá dāá nīn bí kii timool nín nyēē kitiŋ pu puee ní.
26A làá dāá púĺ kí bà a-wiiŋyi ní kí nín kpú,
kii kudiceeu yuntiŋu bi nín cēē idi kí páań kukaatuŋu pu puee.
27Kpèè, ti nín nyàab̄ ki dāa ká kuŋyee dee,
ní an lafun sá ibaamɔn.
Pīlifì tiŋan kí dūú kpāafì kí tīī a-ba.

english_text:
Job's Reply to Eliphaz
It's Impossible
1Job said:
2It's impossible to weigh
my misery and grief!
3They outweigh the sand
along the beach,
and that's why I have spoken
without thinking first.
4The fearsome arrows
of God All-Powerful
have filled my soul
with their poison.
5Do oxen and wild donkeys
cry out in distress
unless they are hungry?
6What is food without salt?
What is more tasteless
than the white of an egg?
7That's how my food tastes,
and my appetite is gone.
* 8How I wish that God
would answer my prayer
9and do away with me.
10Then I would be comforted,
knowing that in all of my pain
I have never disobeyed God.
11Why should I patiently hope
when my strength is gone?
12I am not strong as stone
or bronze,
13and I have finally reached
the end of my rope.
My Friends, I Am Desperate
14My friends, I am desperate,
and you should help me,
even if I no longer respect
God All-Powerful.
* 15But you are treacherous
16like streams that swell
with melting snow,
17then suddenly disappear
in the summer heat.
18I am like a caravan,
lost in the desert
while searching for water.
19Caravans from Tema and Sheba
20thought they would find water.
But they were disappointed,
21just as I am with you.
Only one look at my suffering,
and you run away scared.
What Have I Done Wrong?
22Have I ever asked any of you
to give me a gift
23or to purchase my freedom
from brutal enemies?
24What have I done wrong?
Show me,
and I will keep quiet.
25The truth is always painful,
but your arguments
prove nothing.
26Here I am desperate,
and you consider my words
as worthless as wind.
27Why, you would sell an orphan
or your own neighbor!
28Look me straight in the eye;
I won't lie to you.
29Stop accusing me falsely;
my reputation is at stake.
30I know right from wrong,
and I am not telling lies.
translation_text:
Yoob nín kíí puee: U bíi yáliŋkí u-bɔɔbi pu
1Niinee ní Yoob fōō dinyɔɔbundi ki kíí yii:
2M̀mm, unil yaa bàà ŋūǹ kí ŋmàntī m-gìńdi,
unil yaa bàà ŋūǹ kí dū m-nimbinaamandi
kí ŋá saniya pu kí ŋmàntī!
3Ama m-nimbinaamandi nyìm̀ ki jítiǹ tiŋku bul.
An pu ní m bíi sòoǹ fám fám.
4Tiŋman, Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan dū u-piiŋyi ki yá-mi,
ní m kíǹ ki bíi nyù i-looti.
Unimbɔti nyoondi bíi jáà nì mi.
5Kumooun maŋki sūǹ ŋyunti ŋun ní
timɔsɔn dɔ̄ ki-nimbiin kí ŋmɔ́ee?
Àá unaa gíti sūǹ ŋyunti ŋun ní bi tīī-u timool ú ŋmɔ́ee?
6A ŋūǹ kí jī tijin kaa ŋá ŋyaam an nīn mɔ̄ɔɔ?
Àá mmɔn ŋulɔŋu ní dijindi laakin pīiǹee cáá?
7M yíì kí gbēē tijin tin bí mimmee.
M-falaau sá tijin tin di núutì-mee ní.
*
8M bàà là yii ubɔ ń ŋá tin m mēēyee kí tīī-mi,
Unimbɔti ń tīī-mi kun m lèe.
9Unimbɔti yaa bàà kíikí kí nà-mi dúsi dusi,
u yaa bàà kíikí kí tàntī u-ŋal kí púntí-mi.
10M bàà làá yùkū nì dipɔɔpindi
digìńdi din poon m bí an kaa kúntí nee,
ní kí bàà ká diŋmeendi.
Maa bàà làá nyā Unimbɔti circirdaan nyɔɔbuŋŋi boon.
11Ama maa ti cáá mpɔn kí nīn gbíntìi kā ki cɔ́tí.
M làá nīn bí dimaŋfalin kí tɔ̄ dilal?
Maa cáá foolboon ubɔ dee.
12M-pɔŋŋu kaa sá ditaŋkpal pɔŋŋu,
ní m-wunti mun kaa tí pɔ̄ɔ̄ kii tasa kútee.
13Maa tí cáá mpɔn ŋubɔ m-ni kí ŋmā kí fīī m-ba,
ní ubɔ mun kaa ti bí laaba kí tíkiń-mi.
*
14Unil un wunti yɔ̄tèe cáá nsan u-juti ń sɔ̄ u-saai,
yaa sá fám, u dù Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan faaŋku kí fá ní.
15M-nabiyaamu fātì bi-boon ki tīī-mi kii mbun ŋun fóotèe,
a lì kii mbùmbiyaamu mun poon kūńee.
16Anyintaŋkpee nì ntaayim yaa dūntèe
ní dinyiŋgbagbal ń gbí ibun gbanti.
17Ama ní dipeel puee, ní í fóotí,
kutuntuŋu yuntiŋuee ní í kpā dicilpu dicilpu.
18Kpaŋgulib kaa ti pàatī ibun gbanti cee,
bi dūú bɔ̄ kuteeun ní kí tin wāŋkì.
19Kpaŋgulib bin nyánní Teema tiŋkinee nimbiliŋ nìn cɔ́ i-pu ní,
bisaŋkinliibi bin nyánní Seeba tiŋkinee nìn máká i-pu ní.
20Ama an wùn̄-bi bi nín dū bi-mákal ki páaǹ kibùmbikee puee:
bi bàn̄ee, kun pu bi nìn mákée ŋá fám.
21Ni sá kii ibun gbantee ní ki tīī man ni-bɔɔ!
Ni nín ká m-naabuŋuee ní an cúú-ni tifaandi.
22M bālifì-ni yii ní tīī-mi tibaaa,
àá ní lēē ni-gaajawanti poon tiba kí pɔ̄-maaa?
23M bālifì-ni yii ní fīī-mi kí nyāntí m-nannanliu,
àá upɔɔl ubɔ ŋaanaaa?
24Dàkàmaan-mi, m làá ŋmīĺ,
dàkàmaan-mi tin poon m yīntèe.
25Tibulcin nyɔɔbuŋŋi kaa tìì unil tiweendi.
Ama ní tùkù-mi kun pu ni wòoǹ-mee.
26Ni là kí wòoǹ m-nyɔɔbuŋŋi fám níii?
Ama an sá anyɔɔbun fám ní,
unil un kaa ti cáá dimákalee nín sòon̄ ki tɔ́ kutaa puee.
27Ni yaa ká kí tɔ̄ ditaŋkpiibil pu kasi,
kí dū nimbi ni-ba bɔɔ kí nyāfì, ni là!
28Too, m gbàam̄-ni, kpèèmaan-mi,
kí tùkù-mi m yaa bíi mɔ́ntí-ni.
29Ní fàtīí gítímaan ni-boon, nín̄ sámaan deedeedambi.
Fàtīí gítímaan! Ní béémaan yii maa ŋá tikpitil tiba.
30Mili mili bɔti nyēē m-nyɔkɔnaaa?
Ni dàkafī yii m-limbil kaa gbìl̀ falaa níii?

english_text:
Job Continues
Why Is Life So Hard?
1Why is life so hard?
Why do we suffer?
2We are slaves in search of shade;
we are laborers longing
for our wages.
3God has made my days drag on
and my nights miserable.
4I pray for night to end,
but it stretches out
while I toss and turn.
5My parched skin is covered
with worms, dirt, and sores,
6and my days are running out
quicker than the thread
of a fast-moving needle.
Don't Forget!
7I beg you, God, don't forget!
My life is just a breath,
and trouble lies ahead.
8I will vanish from sight,
and no one, including you,
will ever see me again.
9 I will disappear in the grave
or vanish from sight
like a passing cloud.
10Never will I return home;
soon I will be forgotten.
11And so, I cry out to you
in agony and distress.
12Am I the sea or a sea monster?
Is that why you imprison me?
13I go to bed, hoping for rest,
14but you torture me
with terrible dreams.
* 15I'd rather choke to death
than live in this body.
16Leave me alone and let me die;
my life has no meaning.
17 What makes you so concerned
about us humans?
18Why do you test us
from sunrise to sunset?
19Won't you look away
just long enough
for me to swallow?
20Why do you watch us so closely?
What's it to you, if I sin?
Why am I your target
and such a heavy burden?
21Why do you refuse to forgive?
Soon you won't find me,
because I'll be dead.
translation_text:
Yoob bíi yáliŋkí Unimbɔti pu
1Unil bítam kitiŋ nee pu bí kii sooja tundee ní,
a lì kii upaadaan maŋfal wiiŋyee.
2Kii uyumbu nín fèefī ki nyàab̀ mboon puee,
kii upaadaan nín cí kí fōō u-paati puee,
3míǹ ní an bí-mi.
Iŋmal iŋmal sɔ̀ m-maŋfal kaa ti bí tiban.
M-paatii di sá iyaliŋki nyati.
4M tin pée lì yii m dòontée, m kíĺ ki bíi bàlifī m-ba yii:
«Ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu ní kutaa làá wúntí dee?»
Kunyeeu nee fɔ̀kɔ̀,
ní m dɔ̄ ki lábití m-ba áli kutaa ń dāá wúntí.
5Ijiliŋkpaam nì ipɔkɔ gbí m-wunti kɔkɔ pu,
m-wuŋgbaŋŋu lɔ̄tì lɔ̄tì ki kíǹ ki nyēē nnyim.
6M-maŋfal wiiŋyi bíi sáń malaa malaa ki jítiǹ
usatalul gulfajantiliikee.
M-maŋfal wiiŋyi bíi kúntí dee,
dimákal kaa ti bí.
*
7Unimbɔti, téetí yii m-maŋfal sá kufoou ní,
m-nimbibul pée gíti kpá kí ká nnaam.
8Sii un di nìn kpèé-mee, aa ti làá wāl̀-mi.
A làá dāá nyàab̀-mi, ama m dāa gíti kpá.
9Kii ditagbandi nín búntí pu kí wāŋkèe,
míǹ ní unil un nín sìntī ditaŋkpiilinee kaa ti gítiń.
10Udaan yaa búntèe, waa ti gítiń u-dumpu,
ní laakin u nìn kóòyee, bi kpáàa pée súntì u-pu kpalaa.
11An pu ní maa ti làá ŋmā kí nīn ŋmí.
M làá sòoǹ m-nimbinaamandi nee poon,
m làá yāliŋkì, kun puee m-nyɔkɔ túŋkì.
12M sá tiŋku àá kupeebiliŋŋu kun bí nnyimineeee?
Kin ba pu ní a cí-mi míǹ?
13M yaa lī yii m làá dòon̄ m-lambaŋki pu kí ŋùŋfì,
aayee, m làá dòon̄ m-dooŋu pu m-pɔbil ń sɔ̀ŋkèe,
14ní a cáá tidamintiil ki fàantí-mi.
Kun kun a lèekī ki dàkà-mee kɔ̄ntí-mi dinyoondi.
15A yaa bàà nyīī m-sil ki kūū-mi gba, m bàà là!
M yaan kpíì gba, an sɔ́ǹ m nín bí ki sá akpab ŋma nee.
16M gīiǹ m-ba, maa làá nīn bí ki cá jaanjaan.
Maa ti bí tiban, yàntī-mi soooo.
*
17Ba ní unil sá ní a dàkafī u-pu ní?
Ba pu ní aa pée mɔ̄ u-pu míǹ?
18A-nimbikpeeŋu pée cɔ́ u-pu ní kutaafaau kamaa,
ní ki cɔ́ŋkí-u ŋyunti kamaa.
19Ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu ní a làá gbèen̄ kí taa ti kpèè-mi ní?
A làá pée yàntī kubuŋu ń fáá m-pu dalbaaa?
20Báà m yaa yīntì, ba ní an ŋáań-si ní,
sii un cɔ́ŋkí inifunaanee?
Ba pu ní a màkantí-mi kii ukpan nín màkà upeel puee ní?
M kalin kpántì diwaŋgul ki tīī-si níii?
21Ba pu ní aa là kí dū m-yìntitam kí pɔ̄-mi,
kí fàtī a-boon kí tīī m-kpitii ní?
Man di cá kí dòon̄ ntaminee,
a làá dāá nyàab̀-mi, ama m dāa gíti kpá.

english_text:
Bildad's First Speech
How Long Will You Talk?
1Bildad from Shuah said:
2How long will you talk
and keep saying nothing?
3Does God All-Powerful
stand in the way of justice?
4He made your children pay
for their sins.
5So why don't you turn to him
6and start living right?
Then he will decide
to rescue and restore you
to your place of honor.
7Your future will be brighter
by far than your past.
Our Ancestors Were Wise
8 Our ancestors were wise,
so learn from them.
9Our own time has been short,
like a fading shadow,
and we know very little.
10But they will instruct you
with great understanding.
11Papyrus reeds grow healthy
only in a swamp,
12and if the water dries up,
they die sooner than grass.
13Such is the hopeless future
of all who turn from God
14and trust in something as frail
as a spider's web—
15they take hold and fall
because it's so flimsy.
16Sinful people are like plants
with spreading roots and plenty
of sun and water.
17They wrap their roots tightly
around rocks.
18But once they are pulled up,
they have no more place;
19their life slips away,
and other plants grow there.
20We know God doesn't reject
an innocent person
or help a sinner.
21And so, he will make you happy
and give you something
to smile about.
22But your evil enemies
will be put to shame
and disappear forever.
translation_text:
Biilidaadi nín sòon̄ tiŋyee
1Niinee ní usuwaja Biilidaadi fōō dinyɔɔbundi ki bí yii:
2A làá nīn pée sòoǹ yéè kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu ní?
Anyɔɔbun ŋin nyēē a-nyɔkɔnee bí kii kubuŋkpaaŋŋuee ní.
3Unimbɔti pɔ̀ gandaaa?
Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan kaa sòoǹ tibɔti ti-púɔɔ?
4A-jipɔmbi máaǹ ki tin ŋá ikpiti,
an pu ní u dáaĺ bi-tafal bi-kpitii pu.
5Ama sii, a yaa nyàab̄ Unimbɔti,
ki yaa gbāam̀ Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan,
6a yaa kaa ŋá tiba ní a-pɔbil bí dibee,
u làá wúń a-pu ní kí fàtīí tīī-si mpaan ŋun máaǹ-see.
7A nín nìn bí min njaminee
kaa làá nīn téé a nín làá dāá nīn sá kun foolee.
*
8Bàlifì bin līntiǹ-tee,
ní kí dàkafì bi-naanjab nín nìn kántì kántì tiŋyee pu.
9Bi màl̄-ti nee, taa yúntì ní kaa nyí tiba mun.
Ti-maŋfal wiiŋyi kitiŋ nee pu jītí malaa kii mboonee ní.
10Ama bíǹ làá dàkà-si ní kí sòoǹ nì si.
Bi làá lēē tin bi kāl̀ ki kée poon iciin nyɔɔbundi nee kí tùkù-si yii:
11«Dikal ŋūǹ kí nyā laaba an yaa kaa sá kupuunaaa?
Kukaluu ŋūǹ kí nyā laakin nnyim kpéeee?
12Nnyim yaa kpée, ku péetíǹ timool tin kíǹee kí kpā,
ŋyunti ŋun ku dáá púkuḿ baa láá gāā-kuee!»
*
13Bin súntí Unimbɔti puee nín kúntíǹ puee dee.
Binikpitib mákal nín kúntí puee dee.
14Kun pu bi mákée cúu tīl̀,
di sá yii bi-mákal gbanti bí kii tinaŋgbantalindee ní.
15Bi yaa bàà dīntì bi-diiku puee, ku cìŋkī ní màkà maka,
báà bí nyā kí báań ku-pu, see kú lítí.
16Bi bí kii busubu bun cáá ŋkpiim tikpil ki wīintí ŋwìiń puee ní,
bu tòó bu-paŋŋi bukpaa bun poon bu cɔ́ee.
17Bu tòó bu-nyaaŋyi ataŋkpee kansikin,
ní ki nyàab̀ nsan ki kóò ataŋkpee poon.
18Ama bi yaa kpīkitì-bu mpaan ŋun pu bu nìn yúee,
mpaan gbanti làá lì yii màa pée ká-bu jaanjaan.
19Bin súntí Unimbɔti puee naam nín kúntí laakiŋyee dee!
Biba di làá nyā kí fōō bu-paaŋŋu.
20Unil un baa kāntí u-pu tibee, Unimbɔti kaa féeń-u,
ní kaa tútúǹ un ŋáań ikpitee.
21U làá yàntī á fàtīí ká tilaal,
ní kí yàntī á nīn bí dipɔɔpindin ki fàal̀.
22Icoo làá cúú a-nannanliibi,
binikpitib làá wāŋkì.

english_text:
Job's Reply to Bildad
What You Say Is True
1Job said:
2 What you say is true.
No human is innocent
in the sight of God.
3Not once in a thousand times
could we win our case
if we took him to court.
4God is wise and powerful—
who could possibly
oppose him and win?
5When God becomes angry,
he can move mountains
before they even know it.
6God can shake the earth loose
from its foundations
7 or command the sun and stars
to hold back their light.
8God alone stretched out the sky,
stepped on the sea,
9 and set the stars in place—
the Big Dipper and Orion,
the Pleiades and the stars
in the southern sky.
10Of all the miracles God works,
we cannot understand a one.
11God walks right past me,
without making a sound.
12And if he grabs something,
who can stop him
or raise a question?
13When God showed his anger,
the servants of the sea monster
fell at his feet.
14How, then, could I possibly
argue my case with God?
Though I Am Innocent
15Even though I am innocent,
I can only beg for mercy.
16And if God came into court
when I called him,
he would not hear my case.
17He would strike me with a storm
and increase my injuries
for no reason at all.
18Before I could get my breath,
my miseries would multiply.
19God is much stronger than I am,
and who would call me into court
to give me justice?
20Even if I were innocent,
God would prove me wrong.
21I am not guilty,
but I no longer care
what happens to me.
22What difference does it make?
God destroys the innocent
along with the guilty.
23When a good person dies
a sudden death,
God sits back and laughs.
24And who else but God
blindfolds the judges,
then lets the wicked
take over the earth?
My Life Is Speeding By
25My life is speeding by,
without a hope of happiness.
26Each day passes swifter
than a sailing ship
or an eagle swooping down.
27Sometimes I try to be cheerful
and to stop complaining,
28but my sufferings frighten me,
because I know that God
still considers me guilty.
29So what's the use of trying
to prove my innocence?
30Even if I washed myself
with the strongest soap,
31God would throw me into a pit
of stinking slime, leaving me
disgusting to my clothes.
32God isn't a mere human like me.
I can't put him on trial.
33Who could possibly judge
between the two of us?
34Can someone snatch away
the stick God carries
to frighten me?
35Then I could speak up
without fear of him,
but for now, I cannot speak.
translation_text:
Yoob kíí yii Unimbɔti nyí tikɔkɔ
1Niinee ní Yoob kíí yii:
2Tiŋman, m nyí yii an lafun sá míǹ.
Di sá yii mana ní unil ŋūǹ kí nīn bí deedee Unimbɔti nimbiin?
3Unil nì Unimbɔti yaa làá kpáká,
Unimbɔti kaa làá kíí anyɔɔbun kutuku poonee dibaba gba.
4U-ciiŋyi nyóò ní u-pɔŋŋu sá ŋkpaan,
ŋma di ŋūǹ kí yūĺ u-nimbiin kaa ká ditafadaaldi?
5Úǹ di kpìkitī ajoon dicilpu dicilpu
ní ki lábití-ŋi ki cìb̀ u-ŋuul poon.
6U yàntī kitiŋ nyeel cìŋkī,
u yàntī ki-jaantalkub kpìntī.
7Úǹ di tìì ŋwìiń mara ní ŋú taa nyā,
ní kí dū iŋmalbijaa kí pìin̄ kudii í taa ŋmíntí.
8Úǹ baba di kpátì kutagbɔŋu,
ní ki dū u-taaŋi ki tɔ́kɔǹ tiŋkub nyiŋgbanti pu ki cōom̀.
9Úǹ di náań iŋmalbi kitiŋi nín bí pu aba abee:
dikitil din bí ŋgan púee nì din bí ti-yil kansikinee nì din bí ŋgiil púee.
10U tūǹ atuŋkpaan ŋin ubɔ kaa ŋūǹ kí gbìl̄ ŋi-taapuee,
ní ki ŋáań maamaaci tuuŋŋi ŋin kaa cáá ŋkaanee.
11Kpèè u ŋūǹ kí jītí m-caŋin ḿ taa wāl̀-u,
ní u yaa tí búntì ndanaaa, maa làá kpáàa béé.
12U yaa fìkī tiba, ŋma di ŋūǹ kí yàntī ú fàtīí gíiǹní-tì?
Ŋma di ŋūǹ kí bàlifì-u yii: «Ba ní a ŋáańee?»
13Unimbɔti yaa gíí diŋuulee, waa gítí u-boon.
Tipeebilindi tin bí tiŋkunee dòoń ki gbàantí u-taaŋi taapu,
an dàkà yii Raab nì u-naacimbi.
*
14Kin mana ní man un bí nee, m làá ŋmā kí kíí-u?
La ní m làá ká anyɔɔbun kí dūú kíí-u?
15Báà m yaa cáá ibaamɔn, maa làá ŋmā kí kíí-u.
Kun m pée ŋūǹ kí ŋée di sá ḿ mèè m-bɔsoonliu ú sɔ̄ m-saai!
16Báà m yaa yíiń-u ní u kíí-mi,
maa máká yii u làá pīlifiǹ m-nyɔkɔ.
17U yāntì u-buŋkpaaŋku fáá-mi ki lúkú,
u bíi tìì-mi tiweendi fám.
18Waa yàntī ḿ fòotī báà fiii,
ama ní ki yāntì m-nyɔkɔ túŋkì.
19Mimmee man nì Unimbɔti ń mɔ̀ɔɔ?
Báà an yaa sá dimool, u pɔ̄ɔǹ-mi sɔ́kɔ sɔkɔ!
Ḿ cùnnì-u ibɔsoonaaa?
Báà an yaa sá ibɔsoonaaa, ŋma di làá yíiń-u tibuul ní?
20Báà m-bɔti yaa ŋān̄aaa, tin m làá sòoǹee làá fàtīí kpɔ̀ m-bɔti.
Báà m yaa kaa ŋá tibaaa, m-nyɔɔbuŋŋi làá tīī-mi dibɔkpil.
21Maa kalin ŋá tibaaa?
Maa ti kpáàa nyí gba.
M gīiǹ nì m-ba ní.
22Man ceeyee, a ŋá tibaaa,
aa ŋá tibaaa, an sá ubaanti ní.
An pu ní m lì yii: Unimbɔti yàntī
maanyiiba nì dibɔkpil daan kúù.
23Nnaabukpaan ŋubɔ yaa jéetì kitiŋ pu ki kūū binibee,
Unimbɔti bí ní ki lāā maanyiibab bi-nimbinaamandi poon!
24Unimbɔti yaa dū duulinya ki líiǹ binikpitibee,
ní ú bìin̄ bibɔsoonliibi nimbiin!
An yaa kaa sá úǹ di ŋáań míǹ, ŋma di gíti ŋūǹ kí ŋá míǹ?
*
25M-maŋfal wiiŋyi sáń malaa malaa ki jítiǹ utaatanli,
i sáǹ kaa kpáàa ká nnaam ki dáká.
26M-maŋfal wiiŋyi sáń malaa malaa kii meelabee,
a lì kii ukaabu nín tòó pu yilpu kí cúú u-jintee.
27M yaa bàà bí yii m làá súntí m-yaliŋkii pu,
kí bútí m-nimbiin kí lēe,
28ní falaa un poon m bée fàantí-mi.
Di sá yii m nyí sii Unimbɔti nín kaa làá sòoǹ kí pɔ̀-mee.
29Kii a nín sòon̄ ki kūū m-bɔtee,
ba pu ní ḿ gíti tīī m-ba digìńdi fám?
30Báà m yaa dū fɔfɔ ki fùl̄
ki dū njeem ki fíntì m-ŋalii,
31a làá fàtīí gíiǹ-mi kí tɔ̄ tikpatin,
ní m-wampeeŋkaati gba kaa dāa gíti là-mi.
32Di sá yii Unimbɔti kaa sá unil kii mamee ḿ ŋmā kí kíí-u,
àá ḿ ŋmā man nì u ń cù ibɔsoon.
33Upàtil ubɔ mun kpá
kí ŋmā kí dū u-ŋal kí páań ti-liitil pu kí pàtī-ti.
34Udaan bàà fòol̄ mbambaan ŋun Unimbɔti cáa gbáà-mi nee,
ní kí yàntī ú taa ti fàaǹ-mi.
35M bàà làá ŋmā kí sòoǹ nì u kí taa fàŋkì.
Ama míǹ ní an kaa sá, maa ti yì m-ba.

english_text:
Job Complains to God
I Am Sick of Life!
1I am sick of life!
And from my deep despair,
I complain to you, my God.
2Don't just condemn me!
Point out my sin.
3Why do you take such delight
in destroying those you created
and in smiling on sinners?
4Do you look at things
the way we humans do?
5Is your life as short as ours?
6Is that why you are so quick
to find fault with me?
7 You know I am innocent,
but who can defend me
against you?
8Will you now destroy
someone you created?
9Remember that you molded me
like a piece of clay.
So don't turn me back
into dust once again.
10 As cheese is made from milk,
you created my body
from a tiny drop.
11Then you tied my bones together
with muscles and covered them
with flesh and skin.
12You, the source of my life,
showered me with kindness
and watched over me.
You Have Not Explained
13You have not explained
all of your mysteries,
14but you catch and punish me
each time I sin.
15Guilty or innocent,
I am condemned and ashamed
because of my troubles.
16No matter how hard I try,
you keep hunting me down
like a powerful lion.
17You never stop accusing me;
you become furious and attack
over and over again.
18Why did you let me be born?
I would rather have died
before birth
19and been carried to the grave
without ever breathing.
20I have only a few days left.
Why don't you leave me alone?
Let me find some relief,
* 21before I travel to the land
22of darkness and despair,
the place of no return.
translation_text:
Unimbɔti náań-mi kí nàan̄-mi ní
1M gīī nì m-ba,
an puee maa làá ŋmā kí cúú m-ba kí taa yāliŋkì.
M-poon kaam cɔ́tì ní m làá sòoǹ kí tùkù-u.
2M làá tùkù Unimbɔti yii: taa kpɔ̀ m-bɔti,
tùkù-mi kun ní m ŋá ní a wòoǹ-mee.
3An mɔ̄ǹ-si á nīn sàantí-mi,
kí fàtī a-boon kí tīī a-wannaaŋkaati,
ama ní kí yàntī án bútí binikpitibaaa?
4Nisaal nimbiliŋ ní a cáaa?
Unil nín kpèé ki wāĺ tiwan puee,
míǹ ní si mun kpèé ki wāĺ-tàaa?
5A-maŋfal wiiŋyi kaa náaǹ kii unilee níii?
A-biŋŋi jītí malaa malaa kii unil yaŋee níii?
6Ba pu ní a nyàab̀ kí béé m-yìntitam ní?
Ba pu ní a fíkití ki nyàab̀ kí ká m-kpitii ní?
7Sii a-ba pée nyí yii maa ŋá tiba
ní kaa tí ŋūǹ kí ŋmátí kí nyā a-ŋaan.
8Sii a-ba ŋalii ní a dūu máń-mi ki náań-mi.
Íǹ di māntìi tú-mi, ní a là kí nàan̄-mi!
9Téetí yii sii di máń-mi kii bi nín māā ditansambil puee,
ama ní a là kí nà-mi dúsi dusi ḿ kpántí ntam.
10Sii di náań-mi ki tākaǹ m-na poon
kii bi nín bàtī nnaabiim kí ŋá disambilin mí kìl̄ puee.
11A dū anancal nì ŋwuŋgban ki bīiǹ-mi,
ní ki ŋá-mi akpab nì igiin ki túkuǹ tɔb pu.
12Míǹ boonee ní a ŋá-mi tiŋan ki tīī-mi dimaŋfal,
ní ki wúń m-pu tiŋan.
*
13A dū abɔɔn bɔti tiba ki bál̀ a-pɔbilin.
M nyí kun ní a dàkafēe:
14A là kí ká-mi m bíi ŋáań ikpiti ní,
ní kaa là kí dū m-yìntitam kí pɔ̄-mi.
15M yaa lafun ŋá ikpitee, mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí-mi!
Báà m yaa kaa ŋá tibaaa, maa máaǹ kí yáatí m-yil.
Icoo nì falaa yāntì m gbí kii m nyùn̄ ndaamee.
16M yaa gántì m-yilee, a jì-mi kii gbikintee ní,
a ŋáań maamaacib kí gbéeǹ m-weeŋyi pu.
17A jáà nì mi kaa gbèentí,
diŋuul din a gíí m-puee mɔ̀tīí gbēentí,
ní a-janjaliibi dòoń akiti akiti kí jáǹ-mi.
18Ba pu ní a nyántìń-mi m-na poon ní?
Bi yaa bàà màl̄-mi kaa yōoǹee, ubɔ kaa bàà kāntí-mi.
19M bàà pée nyēē m-na poonee,
m bàà cá dikaakulin ní dicilpu,
m bàà bí kii unil un kaa pée kāl̀ kitiŋ pu ki kée ní.
20M-wiiŋyi kaa ti kíǹ ki náaǹ.
Gbèen̄ kí taa ti jáǹ-mi, kí yàntī-mi soooo
ḿ pée ká dipɔɔpindi fiii iwiin in kíǹ-mi ḿ dūú kàl̄ nee poon,
21kí wàatī ḿ búntí dibɔmbɔndi nì ŋkúm booku tiŋki
kin poon bi cá kaa gítińee.
22Niinee, dibɔmbɔŋkpaandi nì fikil fikil di bí,
ní ŋwalifi bí niin kii dibɔmbɔndee.

english_text:
Zophar's First Speech
So Much Foolish Talk
1Zophar from Naamah said:
2So much foolish talk
cannot go unanswered.
3Your words have silenced others
and made them ashamed;
now it is only right for you
to be put to shame.
4You claim to be innocent
and argue that your beliefs
are acceptable to God.
5But I wish God would speak
6and let you know that wisdom
has many different sides.
You would then discover
that God has punished you
less than you deserve.
7Can you understand the mysteries
surrounding God All-Powerful?
8They are higher than the heavens
and deeper than the grave.
So what can you do
when you know so little,
9and these mysteries outreach
the earth and the ocean?
10If God puts you in prison
or drags you to court,
what can you do?
11God has the wisdom to know
when someone is worthless
and sinful,
12but it's easier to tame
a wild donkey
than to make a fool wise.
Surrender Your Heart to God
13Surrender your heart to God,
turn to him in prayer,
14and give up your sins—
even those you do in secret.
15Then you won't be ashamed;
you will be confident
and fearless.
16Your troubles will go away
like water beneath a bridge,
17and your darkest night
will be brighter than noon.
18You will rest safe and secure,
filled with hope
and emptied of worry.
19You will sleep without fear
and be greatly respected.
20But those who are evil
will go blind and lose their way.
Their only escape is death!
translation_text:
Soofaar nín sòon̄ puee: Fàtīí gítiń Unimbɔti cee
1Niinee ní unaamaja Soofaar fōō dinyɔɔbundi ní ki bí Yoob yii:
2Unil un sòoǹ tikpil kii a nín sòoǹ pu nee kaa kāntí ubɔ ń kíí-uaaa?
A yaa nyí isoonee di dàkà yii a cáá ibaamɔnaaa?
3A nín cáá kinyɔkɔee di làá yàntī binib ń kpántí bimuumbaaa?
A làá bèel̀ binib ubɔ ń taa wòoǹ-saaa?
4A lī gba yii: «Tin m sòoǹee sá ibaamɔn,
Unimbɔti kaa làá ká m-pu tiba kí sòoǹ.»
5M bàà pée là yii Unimbɔti ń wàan̄ kinyɔkɔ
kí sòoǹ kí kíí-si u-ba!
6U bàà làá lēē dinyil bɔɔŋŋi kí dàkà-si.
Abɔɔn gbanti jítiǹ unil ciiŋyi ń ŋmā kí gbìl̄ taapu.
A bàà làá gbìl̄ niin yii
Unimbɔti súntì a-kpitii dijandi pu.
*
7Ŋma ŋūǹ kí béé kí cíĺ Unimbɔti?
Ŋma di ŋūǹ kí béé Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan
nín sá ukpaan puee gbeennyɔkɔ?
8Unimbɔti ciiŋyi nyóò kii yilpu nín dátiǹ kitiŋ puee ní,
ba ní a ŋūǹ kí ŋá?
I nyóò ki jítiǹ ditaŋkpiilin.
Tilati ní a ŋūǹ kí béé?
9I wāā ki jítiǹ kitiŋ,
ki wāā ki jítiǹ tiŋku.
10Unimbɔti yaa cúú dibɔkpil daan ki pīiǹ kudii,
ní ki yaa yíiń udaan ibeeyiinee,
ŋma di ŋūǹ kí pìin̄ nsan?
11Di sá yii Unimbɔti nyí binib bin kaa bí tibanee.
An kaa bàlifī ú kpèè címmm ní kí nín ká laakin ikpiti bée.
12Ama ugbaan kaa ŋūǹ kí kpántí uciŋfiti dalba dalba,
a lì kii kumooun maŋki di kaa ŋūǹ kí kpántí kimɔŋkimaŋ puee ní.
*
13Yoob, dū a-pɔbil kí tīī Unimbɔti,
ní kí yòon̄ a-ŋalii kí túĺ-u kí mèè-u.
14Ikpiti yaa táká a-ŋaliiyee, á pítí-i kí fá,
kí taa yàntī tin kaa bí deedeeyee ń ká mpaan a-dumpu.
15Niinee a làá gántí a-yil kí nyā icoon,
tiba kpá kí cìŋkì-si, ní aa làá fàŋkì tiba mun.
16Di sá yii a làá súntí a-nimbinaamandi pu,
a làá dāá súntí kii nnyim min pùub̄ ki búntèe ní.
17A-maŋfal wiiŋyi làá wāl̀ bɔ́iii kí jītíǹ kuwiŋkaŋu pu,
ní dibɔmbɔndi ń kpántí kii kutaafaauee.
18A làá dāá nīn cáá dimákal ní kaa làá fàŋkì tiba.
Báà icoo boonee, a làá dāá gèeǹ nì ŋgbansɔŋfi.
19A yaa láa bíi ŋùŋfēe, ubɔ kaa làá dāá pìkil̀-si.
Binib tikpil gba làá dāá nyàab̀ kí pàkà-si.
20Ama binikpitib làá dāá nyàab̀ dijòońdi áli bi-nimbiliŋ ń lóoĺ.
Baa làá dāá ká kibalilaŋ.
Bi-mákal kɔkɔ di dāa sá ŋkúm.

english_text:
Job's Reply to Zophar
You Think You Are So Great
* 1Job said to his friends:
2You think you are so great,
with all the answers.
3But I know as much as you do,
and so does everyone else.
4I have always lived right,
and God answered my prayers;
now friends make fun of me.
5It's easy to condemn
those who are suffering,
when you have no troubles.
6Robbers and other godless people
live safely at home and say,
“God is in our hands!”
If You Want To Learn
7If you want to learn,
then go and ask
the wild animals and the birds,
8the flowers and the fish.
9Any of them can tell you
what the Lord has done.
10Every living creature
is in the hands of God.
11We hear with our ears,
taste with our tongues,
12and gain some wisdom from those
who have lived a long time.
13But God is the real source
of wisdom and strength.
14No one can rebuild
what he destroys, or release
those he has imprisoned.
15God can hold back the rain
or send a flood,
