We are like sheep on their way
to be slaughtered.
23Wake up! Do something, Lord!
Why are you sleeping?
Don't desert us forever.
24Why do you keep looking away?
Don't forget our sufferings
and all our troubles.
25We are flat on the ground,
holding on to the dust.
26Do something! Help us!
Show how kind you are
and come to our rescue.
translation_text:
Ti-Dindaan, taa dū-ti kí fá talku
1Koora dicaŋkun yab di ŋmàn̄ nlan nee ki tīī bilaŋgaaliibi kpiliu.
2Unimbɔti, ti-tafal gbìl̄ ní ti-baabi mun máafì-ti
atuŋkpaan ŋin ní a nìn ŋá bi-yuntiŋu,
iyunti in jítèe poonee.
3A nìn dū a-pɔŋkpaaŋŋu ki jìn̄ atimbun
ní ki dū ti-baabi ki kāaǹ.
A nìn dáaĺ anibul tafal
ní ki yāntì an bútì ti-baabi.
4An kaa sá bi-janjawanti ní bi nìn dūu jáń ki fōō kitiŋ,
kaa tí sá bi-pɔŋŋu pu ní bi nìn ká dijajil.
Ama an nìn sá a-pɔŋŋu nì a-kpabil pu,
nì a-bítam bi-cee, di sá yii bi-bɔti nìn mɔ̄ǹ-si.
5Sii di sá m-Bɔtiu nì m-Nimbɔtiu,
tīī mara ní a-nibul ń ká dijajil.
6Sii pu ní ti jáà ki pɔ́ɔkíǹ ti-nannanliibi,
a-yindi pu ní ti tà ki mátí bin dòoń ki jáà nì tee.
7Maa máká m-tɔbu pu,
an kaa tí sá m-tàataajiki di tìì-mi dijajil.
8Sii di fìil̄-ti ti-nannanliibi ŋaan,
ní ki kɔ̄ntí bin ná-tee icoo.
9Ti làá nīn gà ilan ki nyɔ́ŋkí sii Unimbɔti baabadal,
ní kí nīn jáaḿ-si kí taa gbèen̄.
10Kɔŋkɔnnee, a dū-ti ki fá ki kɔ́ǹ-ti icoo.
Aa ti lìntī ti-janjakitiŋ nyɔkɔpu.
11A yāntì taa ŋúń ki síl̀ ti-nannanliibi nimbiin,
ní bi dɔ́miń ki fúkúl̀-ti pílpil.
12A dū-ti ki tīī kii ipii in bi cáǹ kí kpɔ̀ee,
a yāntì ti yàl̄ ki tin kóòń nnicantimun.
13A dū a-nib ki nyáfì tilèel,
kaa kpáàa nyàab̄ kí ká ipaati poon.
14A yāntì ti-kɔŋkɔnaatɔb sìí-ti,
ní bin māntìi tú-tee bèel̄-ti ki lāā.
15A yāntì atimbun ŋin kíǹee cáá ti-bɔti ki gà ilan,
ní bi bèel̄-ti ki gbákafí bi-yiliŋ.
16Baabadalee, m-naabuŋu di dɔ̄ m-nimbiin m wāĺ,
ní maa ti ŋūǹ kí yáatí m-yil icoo pu.
17M gbìl̀ bi bèel̄-ti ki sìí-ti.
M wāĺ unannanli nín bí ki tɔ̀ ipɔntoon puee.
18Tin bí nee kɔkɔ bāań-ti, ama taa súntì a-pu,
kaa tí fātì ti-boon ki tīī a-poondi.
19Taa fātì ti-kpaŋkpamboon ki tīī-saaa,
kaa yīntiǹ a-marab mun.
20Ama a jìn̄-ti ki tɔ́ laakin jiiŋkpaaibi kóòyee,
ki dū dibɔmbɔŋkpaandi ki bīiǹ ti-pu.
21Ti yaa nìn súntì ti-Nimbɔtiu pu
ní ki mēē awaa abee,
22sii Unimbɔti kaa bàà béetí-tàaa,
sii un di nyí ti-pɔbiliŋ bɔɔŋŋee?
23Sii ti-Dindaan pu ní ti tūŋkí ŋkúm baabadal,
ní bi ŋáań-ti kii ipii in bi cáǹ kí kpɔ̀ee.
24Ti-Dindaan, fìntī! Ba pu ní a dɔ̄ ki gèeǹ ní?
Yīkìm̄, taa dū-ti kí fá kí nīn cá jaanjaan!
25Ba pu ní a dū a-nimbiin ki bál̀-ti
ki súntì ti-falaau nì bi nín wɔ́b́-ti puee míǹ?
26Di sá yii ti dɔ̄ ntamin ki fìlim̀,
ki cìb̄ kitiŋ.
27Yīkìm̄, dāá jòoń-ti!
A-neeŋkpaandi puee, dāá fīī-ti kí líí.

english_text:
(A special psalm by the clan of Korah and for the music leader. To the tune “Lilies.” A love song.)
For a Royal Wedding
1My thoughts are filled
with beautiful words
for the king,
and I will use my voice
as a writer would use
pen and ink.
2No one is as handsome as you!
Your words are always kind.
That is why God
will always bless you.
3Mighty king, glorious ruler,
strap on your sword
4and ride out in splendor!
Win victories for truth
and mercy and justice.
Do fearsome things
with your powerful arm.
5Send your sharp arrows
through enemy hearts
and make all nations fall
at your feet.
6 You are God, and you will rule
forever as king.
Your royal power
brings about justice.
7You love justice and hate evil.
And so, your God chose you
and made you happier
than any of your friends.
8The sweet aroma of the spices
myrrh, aloes, and cassia
covers your royal robes.
You enjoy the music of harps
in palaces decorated
with ivory.
9Daughters of kings are here,
and your bride stands
at your right side,
wearing a wedding gown
trimmed with pure gold.
10Bride of the king,
listen carefully to me.
Forget your own people
and your father's family. 11The king adores you.
He is your master,
so do what he desires.
12All of the richest people
from the city of Tyre
will try to influence you
13with precious treasures.
Your bride, my king,
has inward beauty,
and her wedding gown is woven
with threads of gold.
14Wearing the finest garments,
she is brought to you,
followed by her young friends,
the bridesmaids.
15Everyone is excited,
as they follow you
to the royal palace.
16Your sons and your grandsons
will also be kings
as your ancestors were.
You will make them rulers
everywhere on earth.
17I will make your name famous
from now on,
and you will be praised
forever and ever.
translation_text:
Ubɔti nimpucanti laŋŋu
1Koora dicaŋkun yab di ŋmàn̄ nlan nee ki tīī bilaŋgaaliibi kpiliu. Bi bɔ̀ɔ́ kubeeu ní ki gà-ŋu. Dineendi laŋŋu.
2Anyɔɔbunnyaan di gbí m-pɔbilin.
M làá gāā nlammɔnti kí tīī ubɔti tinyool.
M-nyɔkɔ ń nīn yáb̀ kí gāā nlan
kii ugbaŋŋmal un yáb̀ee ŋmamɔɔŋŋuee.
3Sii di ŋān̄ ki jítiǹ binib kɔkɔ, a nyí isoon.
An pu ní Unimbɔti bīiǹ a-boon kí nīn cá jaanjaan.
4Ubaatandaan, yòon̄ a-gbajau kí gbìn̄.
An di sá a-nyooti nì a-kpaanti daaŋku.
5Jàkà nì kunyaaŋŋu kí mɔ̄tì
ibaamɔn nì dibasintil nì deedee pu.
A-ŋaŋgiil ń dàkà a-tuuŋŋi ŋin sá maamaaci tuuŋŋee.
6A-piiŋyi cɔ́m̀ tiŋan,
- i sàatī ki kóò sii ubɔti nannanliibi pɔbiliŋ poon.
Atimbun nib làá lítí a-taaŋi taapu.
7Unimbɔti, a-beel bí ní ki cá jaanjaan.
A jīǹ a-beel nì deedee ní.
8A néeń tin bí deedeeyee ní ki ná tin kaa ŋān̄ee,
an pu ní Unimbɔti, a-Nimbɔtiu lēē-si,
ki sītì a-pu dipɔɔpindi kpam a jítiǹ a-jutiibi kɔkɔ.
9A-wampeeŋkaati kɔkɔ sɔ́fì miiri
nì disaaweendi nì kasiya talaalub ní,
ní a-bɔtinaakooku kun bi dū
kunti nyiŋŋi ki nákáǹ nákáǹee poonee,
bi bɔ̀ɔ́ tibati ki gà ilan in tìì-si dipɔɔpindee.
10Ubɔti sapɔmbi bí ki ŋúb́ a-wanleeŋkaati,
ní ubɔti nimpuu yú a-ŋaŋgiil pú
ki lá sindaariyamɔnti wanléeŋkaati.
11Pīlifì m-bisal, kpèè kí kpòon̄ a-tafal kí pīlifì.
Súntí a-nibooliŋu nì a-baa dicaŋku yab pu.
12Yàntī a-nyaaŋku ń fáatíǹ ubɔti!
Úǹ di kíǹ ki sá a-dindaan,
gbàan̄ u-nimbiin.
13Tiir yab bin sá bigaajakpaambee
làá dāá pɔ̄-si tiwan á nīn kíǹ ki là-bi.
14Ubɔti bɔɔn di kóòń nì tinyookpaandee,
sindaariya ní bi dūu nyūntì u-bɔkutil.
15Dibɔkutil din u pēēyee cáá inyiŋfi kutuku pu,
ní bi cáǹ-u ubɔti cee.
Bisapɔmbi bin pá u-boon ki tútúǹ-uee
mun kɔ́nní a-cee.
16Nì mmɔn nì ifaal ní bi kɔ̄ntí-bi
ubɔti naakooku poon.
17Ubɔti, a-jipɔmbi làá dāá fōō a-naanjab yil kí kàl̄ dibeel,
a làá dāá yàntī bí kpántí kitiŋ kɔkɔ pu abɔtibil.
18M làá yàntī bí nīn téetí a-yindi pu abin abin.
Niinee báà ŋma làá nīn nyɔ́ŋkí-si kí taa gbèen̄.

english_text:
(A special song by the clan of Korah and for the music leader.)
God Is Our Mighty Fortress
1God is our mighty fortress,
always ready to help
in times of trouble.
2And so, we won't be afraid!
Let the earth tremble
and the mountains tumble
into the deepest sea.
3Let the ocean roar and foam,
and its raging waves
shake the mountains.
4A river and its streams
bring joy to the city,
which is the sacred home
of God Most High.
5God is in that city,
and it won't be shaken.
He will help it at dawn.
6Nations rage! Kingdoms fall!
But at the voice of God
the earth itself melts.
7The Lord All-Powerful
is with us.
The God of Jacob
is our fortress.
8Come! See the fearsome things
the Lord has done on earth.
9God brings wars to an end
all over the world.
He breaks the arrows,
shatters the spears,
and burns the shields.
10Our God says, “Calm down,
and learn that I am God!
All nations on earth
will honor me.”
11The Lord All-Powerful
is with us.
The God of Jacob
is our fortress.
translation_text:
Ti-Dindaan bí ti-cee
1Koora dicaŋkun yab laŋgaakpiliu laŋŋu, bi gà-ŋu nì kineejaka ní.
2Unimbɔti di sá timbi balilaŋki nì ti-pɔŋŋu,
dinimbinaamandi yuntiŋuee, u pée bí ní kí jòoń-ti.
3An pu ní taa fàŋkí tiba,
báà kitiŋ yaa bíi cìŋkāaa,
ajoon yaa bíi kpìkitī ki lítí tiŋkunaaa,
4tiŋku nyiŋgbanti yaa yāŋkí tɔb ki ŋáań kuwoou
ajoon cìŋkī.
5Mbun ŋubɔ bí ki cāabìń dipɔɔpindi Unimbɔti tiŋkin,
laakin sá Yilpu Fɔ́ŋŋŋ Nimbɔtiu circir kɔŋkooŋŋu páaayee.
6Unimbɔti bí kitiŋ gbantin, tiba kpá kí ŋá-kì,
kutaa tin pée lì yii ku wúntée,
Unimbɔti bí kí jòoń-kì.
7Atimbun kɔ́ fìkil fikil poon, abee cīŋkì,
Unimbɔti téeń ní kitiŋ dūntì.
8Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan bí ti-cee,
Jaakɔb Nimbɔtiu di sá timbi balilaŋki.
9Dāá kpèèmaan tin ti-Dindaan ŋée,
maamaaci tuuŋŋi ŋin ní u ŋá kitiŋ puee.
10U yàntī tijáti gbèentí duulinya kɔkɔn,
u kɔ́fí itɔfi, ki nyìitī ki gífí ŋkpamu,
ní ki tùutī agbampɔɔ ŋŋmi.
11Ti-Dindaan téeń yii: «Gbèem̄maan kujaauee!
Béémaan yii man di sá Unimbɔti!
Man di jīǹ atimbun pu dibeel,
man di jīǹ kitiŋ kɔkɔ pu dibeel.»
12Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan bí ti-cee,
Jaakɔb Nimbɔtiu di sá timbi balilaŋki.

english_text:
(A psalm by the clan of Korah and for the music leader.)
God Rules the Nations
1All of you nations,
clap your hands and shout
joyful praises to God.
2The Lord Most High is fearsome,
the ruler of all the earth.
3God has put every nation
under our power,
4and he chose for us the land
that was the pride of Jacob,
his favorite.
5God goes up to his throne,
as people shout
and trumpets blast.
6Sing praises to God our King,
7the ruler of all the earth!
Praise God with songs.
8God rules the nations
from his sacred throne.
9Their leaders come together
and are now the people
of Abraham's God.
All rulers on earth
surrender their weapons,
and God is greatly praised!
translation_text:
Kpāafìmaan abaal kí tīī ti-Dindaan Ubɔtikpaan
1Koora dicaŋkun yab di gāā nlan nee.
2Anibul kɔkɔ nib, kpāafìmaan abaal,
fáámaan ŋwiliili kí nyɔ̄ŋkì Unimbɔti nì ifaal.
3Di sá yii ti-Dindaan, Yilpu Fɔ́ŋŋŋ Nimbɔtiu sá kuwambiiu ní.
U sá ubɔtikpaan ní kitiŋ kɔkɔ pu.
4U sīntì anibul ki ŋá ti-taapu,
u dū atimbun ki ŋá ti-taaŋi taapu.
5U lēē ti-fakal ki tīī-ti,
kun tìì Jaakɔb un u néeńee mmɔnee.
6Bi nìn bí ki fátí iwiliili ní Unimbɔti nín jɔ́ḿ Siiyɔn jool pu,
bi bí ki búǹ iyin ní ti-Dindaan nín jɔ́ḿ.
7Gāāmaan ilan kí nyɔ̄ŋkì Unimbɔti, nyɔ̄ŋkìmaan-u!
Gāāmaan ilan kí nyɔ̄ŋkì ti-bɔtiu, nyɔ̄ŋkìmaan-u!
8Di sá yii Unimbɔti di sá kitiŋ kɔkɔ bɔtiu.
Gāāmaan ilan in mɔ̄ee kí nyɔ̄ŋkì-u.
9Unimbɔti di jīǹ atimbun pu dibeel,
Unimbɔti kā u-circir beejal pu.
10Anibul bɔtibiliŋ kpáfì nì
Abraam Nimbɔtiu nibul.
Di sá yii Unimbɔti di cáá bibɔtiibi
bin wúń kitiŋ puee pu mpɔn.
Úǹ di tɔ́kɔ́ tikɔkɔ pu.

english_text:
(A song and a psalm by the clan of Korah.)
The City of God
1The Lord God is wonderful!
He deserves all praise
in the city where he lives.
His holy mountain,
2 beautiful and majestic,
brings joy to all on earth.
Mount Zion, truly sacred,
is home for the Great King.
3God is there to defend it
and has proved to be
its protector.
4Kings joined forces
to attack the city,
5but when they saw it,
they were terrified
and ran away.
6They trembled all over
like women giving birth
7or like seagoing ships
wrecked by eastern winds.
8We had heard about it,
and now we have seen it
in the city of our God,
the Lord All-Powerful.
This is the city that God
will let stand forever.
9Our God, here in your temple
we think about your love.
10You are famous and praised
everywhere on earth,
as you win victories
with your powerful arm.
11Mount Zion will celebrate,
and all Judah will be glad,
because you bring justice.
12Let's walk around Zion
and count its towers.
13We will see its strong walls
and visit each fortress.
Then you can say
to future generations,
14“Our God is like this forever
and will always guide us.”
translation_text:
Ubɔtikpaan tiŋki
1Nlan. Koora dicaŋkun yab laŋŋu.
2Ti-Dindaan sá ukpaan
ní ki máaǹ bí nyɔ̄ŋkì-u
úǹ ti-Nimbɔtiu tiŋkin,
u-circir jool pu.
3Dì ŋān̄ ki fɔ̀kɔ̀ ní ki tìì kitiŋ kɔkɔ mmɔn.
Ŋgan pú kúnti kuntee, Siiyɔn jool dee, ubɔtikpaan tiŋki.
4Siiyɔn guŋŋi poonee,
bi nyí Unimbɔti nín sá bi-balilaŋkee.
5Kpèè, bibɔtiibi nìn kóoǹ ki kpáfì,
bi còom̄ dicilpu ki cá kí já nì Siiyɔn tiŋki.
6Ama ŋyunti ŋun bi ká ti-Dindaanee,
ní an ŋá-bi bitii.
Bi fāŋkì ní ki sáǹ ki kátì.
7Dibɔbil pu niin ní bi-wunti kpíì,
a lì kii unimpu un kā imatiŋween puee.
8A lì kii ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú buŋku
nín wìil̄ Taarsiisi meelab puee.
9Tin ti gbìl̄ bi sòon̄ee
lafun sá tin ti ká
ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan tiŋkinee,
an dàkà yii ti-Nimbɔtiu tiŋkin.
Unimbɔti di ŋúb́-kì kí nīn cá jaanjaan.
10Unimbɔti, ti téetí
a-neeŋkpaandi pu a-diiku poon.
11Unimbɔti, kii a-yindi nín gbītì
ki tin sāā kitiŋ gbeennyɔkɔ puee,
míǹ ní a-nyɔŋkii mun gbītì.
Deedee gbí a-ŋaŋgiilin.
12Siiyɔn jool bíi fàal̀,
Juuda timmu bí mmɔnni
a-bɔsooŋyi pu.
13Còom̀maan kí màntīí tū Siiyɔn jool,
kàam̀maan u-gunlɔkɔŋi.
14Kpèèmaan digundi din bi máń ki tú-dèe,
kàam̀maan di-bɔtinaakɔti
kí dāá dūú māafì bin baa láá màl̄ee
15yii Unimbɔti gbanti di sá ti-Nimbɔtiu kí nīn cá jaanjaan.
Úǹ di làá nīn kpòotī-ti ŋyunti kamaa.

english_text:
(A psalm by the clan of Korah and for the music leader.)
Don't Depend on Wealth
1Everyone on this earth,
now listen to what I say!
2Listen, no matter who you are,
rich or poor.
3I speak words of wisdom,
and my thoughts make sense.
4I have in mind a mystery
that I will explain
while playing my harp.
5Why should I be afraid
in times of trouble,
when I am surrounded
by vicious enemies?
6They trust in their riches
and brag about
all their wealth.
7You cannot buy back your life
or pay off God!
8It costs far too much
to buy back your life.
You can never pay God enough
9to stay alive forever
and safe from death.
10 We see that wise people die,
and so do stupid fools.
Then their money is left
for someone else.
11The grave will be their home
forever and ever,
although they once had land
of their own.
12Our human glory disappears,
and, like animals, we die.
13Here is what happens to fools
and to those who trust
the words of fools:
14They are like sheep
with death as their shepherd,
leading them to the grave.
In the morning God's people
will walk all over them,
as their bodies lie rotting
in their home, the grave.
15But God will rescue me
from the power of death.
16Don't let it bother you
when others get rich
and live in luxury.
17Soon they will die
and all their wealth
will be left behind.
18We humans are praised
when we do well,
and all of us are glad
to be alive.
19But we each will go down
to our ancestors,
never again to see
the light of day.
20Our human glory disappears,
and, like animals, we die.
translation_text:
Unil yaa kpíì, waa kpāantí tiba
1Koora dicaŋkun yab di gāā nlan nee ki tīī bilaŋgaaliibi kpiliu.
2Anibul kɔkɔ ń pīlifì tin bí nee,
duulinya kɔkɔ nib ń kpòon̄ bi-tafaliŋ kí pīlifì,
3binifantantiibi nì binikpaambi,
bigaajab nì bisoodambi kɔkɔ:
4m làá sòoǹ iciin nyɔɔbuŋŋi,
tin kā m-pɔbilin m dàkafēe cáá taapu.
5M kpōoǹ m-tafal ki pílifì dilaŋkpandi,
m làá bɔ̀ɔ̀ m-beeku kí lēē m-pɔɔŋŋu taapu kí dàkà.
6Ba pu ní ḿ nīn fàŋkí iwiŋkpiti dal,
ŋyunti ŋun m-nannanliibi māntìi tú-mee?
7Bi máká bi-gaajati pu,
ní ki yòontí bi-ba yilpu bi-gaajati nín wīikí puee pu.
8Ama báà unil mun kaa ŋūǹ
kí dā Unimbɔti cee u-juti maŋfal,
àá kí pà úǹ u-ba maŋfal pu.
9Báà unil yaa tīī pu kí dā u-maŋfalee,
dì làá dāá pée kúntí ní kí nīn cá jaanjaan.
10Unil ŋūǹ kí nīn bí jaanjaan
kí taa kpú dalba dalbaaa?
11Ti ká ki gíti káa! Biciŋfitiibi kúù,
ní bigbaambi nì biwaatiibi mun kúù,
ní kí búntí kí yàntī bi-gaajati ní biba ń dāá yòon̄.
12Min kamaa bi dū bi-yiŋŋi ki pú bi-tampaaŋyee,
dikaakul di làá nīn sá bi-dumpui kí nīn cá jaanjaan,
ní bí nīn kóò niin kí nīn cá abin abin.
13Unil nyooti kaa làá ŋmā kí yàntī ú taa kpú,
u làá pée kpú kii kuwaŋkuluuee ní.
14Kpèè bin máká bi-ba puee kúntitam dee,
nì bin pá bi-boon ki néeń bi nín sòoǹ puee.
15Bi téekí-bi ki cáǹ ditaŋkpiilin kii ipiiyee,
ŋkúm di làá nīn kpàá-bi.
- Kutaafaauee, deedeedambi làá nīn tà-bi, -
ní bi-nyaaŋku ń wāŋkì ditaŋkpiilin,
ní bí nīn kíǹ ki dátiǹ bi-dumpui.
16Ama Unimbɔti làá dā m-naŋki kí nyāntí ditaŋkpiilin,
tiŋman, u làá fīī-mi.
17Ubɔ yaa kpántì ugaajee, án taa kɔ́-si nnimbitaataam,
báà u-gaajati gbanti yaa mɔ̀tīi wīintí ki cá.
18Di sá yii u yaa kpíì, waa làá kpáaǹ báà tiba
ní u-nyooti kaa làá táá-u kí kɔ́ dikaakulin.
19Ŋyunti ŋun u nìn dáá bí dimaŋfalinee, u nìn pàkà u-ba ki lì yii:
«Bi nyɔ́ŋkí-si, di sá yii an bútì-si tikɔkɔ poon!»
20U làá cùú ŋàl̄ u-naanjab ditaŋkpiilin,
bíǹ bin gíti kpá kí ká ŋwalifi dalba dalbee.
21Unil nì u-nyooti kɔkɔee, u yaa kaa gbìl̀ taapuee,
u làá kpú kii kuwaŋkuluuee ní.

english_text:
(A psalm by Asaph.)
What Pleases God
1From east to west,
the powerful Lord God
has been calling together
everyone on earth.
2God shines brightly from Zion,
the most beautiful city.
3Our God approaches,
but not silently;
a flaming fire comes first,
and a storm surrounds him.
4God comes to judge his people.
He shouts to the heavens
and to the earth,
5“Call my followers together!
They offered me a sacrifice,
and we made an agreement.”
6The heavens announce,
“God is the judge,
and he is always honest.”
7My people, I am God!
Israel, I am your God.
Listen to my charges
against you.
8Although you offer sacrifices
and always bring gifts,
9I won't accept your offerings
of bulls and goats.
10Every animal in the forest
belongs to me,
and so do the cattle
on a thousand hills.
11I know all the birds
in the mountains,
and every wild creature
is in my care.
12If I were hungry,
I wouldn't tell you,
because I own the world
and everything in it.
13I don't eat the meat of bulls
or drink the blood of goats.
14I am God Most High!
The only sacrifice I want
is for you to be thankful
and to keep your word.
15Pray to me in time of trouble.
I will rescue you,
and you will honor me.
16But to the wicked I say:
“You don't have the right
to mention my laws or claim
to keep our agreement!
17You refused correction
and rejected my commands.
18You made friends
with every crook you met,
and you liked people who break
their wedding vows.
19You talked only about violence
and told nothing but lies;
20you sat around gossiping,
ruining the reputation
of your own relatives.”
21When you did all this,
I didn't say a word,
and you thought,
“God is just like us!”
But now I will accuse you.
22You have ignored me!
So pay close attention
or I will tear you apart,
and no one can help you.
23The sacrifice that honors me
is a thankful heart.
Obey me, and I, your God,
will show my power to save.
translation_text:
Unimbɔti páaǹní kí sòoǹ kitiŋ kɔkɔ bɔti
1Asaafi di ŋmàn̄ nlan nee.
Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan, ti-Dindaan sòon̄,
u yíiń kitiŋ kɔkɔ tibuul,
kí yòon̄ ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú kí cáá sāā ŋu-jeetilaŋki.
2Doooo Siiyɔn, kitinnyaaŋŋi poon
ní Unimbɔti páaǹní ŋwalifi māntìi tú-u.
3Ti-Nimbɔtiu ń dāan̄
kí taa nín̄ ŋmí!
Ŋŋmi ŋun fòol̄ bìlbilee līī u-nyɔkɔpu,
ní kubuŋkpaaŋŋu māntìi tú-u.
4Unimbɔti yíiń kutagbɔŋu kun dàn̄ yilpu nee,
nì kitiŋ bí dāá kpèè u nín làá sòoǹ u-niboolii bɔti puee.
5U bí yii: «Kóom̀maan bin yú nì mi deedeeyee kí kpāfì,
bin ŋá saraa ki pūtì ki pōoǹ dipoondi nì mee!»
6Kutagbɔŋu sòoǹ Unimbɔti deedeeu pu,
di sá yii Unimbɔti u-ba di sòoǹ binib bɔti!
7M-nibul pīlifì, m làá sòoǹ,
Isirayeel, m làá sòoǹ kí kpɔ̀ a-bɔti,
man di sá Unimbɔti, a-Nimbɔtiu.
8M làá wòoǹ-si,
ama an kaa nín sá a-saraabi pu,
di sá yii a pée ŋáań-mi bisaraawɔkaabi ní baabadal.
9Maa làá lēē unaja a-dumpuɔɔɔ,
kaa làá tí lēē iŋɔjaa a-naabakakun.
10Di sá yii man di yì kupɔɔun peelii
nì ajoon kutukub kutukub pu peelii.
11M nyí inoon in kɔkɔ bí ajoon puee,
man di tí yì kumooun peelii kɔkɔ.
12Ŋkùm yaa bàà cáá-mee, an kaa sá sii ní m làá tùkù,
di sá yii duulinya nì tin kɔkɔ bí u-poonee, man di yì.
13M ŋmóò inajaa nantaaa,
iŋɔjaa fatikuu ní m nyù ní?
14Ijaam ń nīn sá saraa un a làá ŋá kí tīī man Unimbɔtee,
ní kí ŋá a nín pōoǹ yii a làá ŋá puee
kí tīī man Yilpu Fɔ́ŋŋŋ Nimbɔtiu.
15Niinee a yaa kɔ́ dinimbinaamandin ní ki yíiń-mee,
m làá fīī-si ní á nyɔ̄ŋkì-mi.
16Ama Unimbɔti bíi tùkù unikpiti yii:
«Ba pu ní a sòoǹ ki bùsī m-marab?
Ba pu ní a sòoǹ m-poondi pu?
17Sii ná m-dàkatam
ní ki féeń m-marab.
18A yaa ká unaayuuyee ní u-bɔti mɔ̄ǹ-si,
sii nì bilaakpaadambi di kpáfí ki kàal̀.
19A yāntì a-nyɔkɔ sòoǹ tibɔkpitil,
ní a-limbil sòoǹ tinyimɔmbɔti.
20A yaa kāl̀ee, a-juti bɔti ŋma ní a sòoǹ,
ní ki cāab̀ a-nabiki kiŋkiŋ disambiil.
21Kpèè kun ní a ŋáań ki là ḿ nīn ŋmée.
A dàkafī yii m bí kii siiyee níii?
M làá wòoǹ-si ní kí bìitī a-tuŋkpitiŋ kɔkɔ pu kí bíĺ a-nimbiin.»
22Nimbi bin súntí man Unimbɔti puee,
ní gbìl̄maan tibɔti gbanti taapu!
An yaa kaa sá míǹ, m làá tɔ̀ntī-ni,
ní ubɔ dāa kpá kí fīī-ni.
23Un cáá ijaam ki ŋáań-mi saraayee, úǹ di tìì-mi tinyool.
Udaan dī nsan ŋun poon m làá yàntī
ú ká man Unimbɔti fiilee dee.

english_text:
(For the music leader. A psalm by David when the prophet Nathan came to him after David had been with Bathsheba.)
A Prayer for Forgiveness
1 You are kind, God!
Please have pity on me.
You are always merciful!
Please wipe away my sins.
2Wash me clean from all
of my sin and guilt.
3I know about my sins,
and I cannot forget
the burden of my guilt.
4 You are really the one
I have sinned against;
I have disobeyed you
and have done wrong.
So it is right and fair for you
to correct and punish me.
5I have sinned and done wrong
since the day I was born.
6But you want complete honesty,
so teach me true wisdom.
7Wash me with hyssop
until I am clean
and whiter than snow.
8Let me be happy and joyful!
You crushed my bones,
now let them celebrate.
9Turn your eyes from my sin
and cover my guilt.
10Create pure thoughts in me
and make me faithful again.
11Don't chase me away from you
or take your Holy Spirit
away from me.
12Make me as happy as you did
when you saved me;
make me want to obey!
13I will teach sinners your Law,
and they will return to you.
14Keep me from any deadly sin.
Only you can save me!
Then I will shout and sing
about your power to save.
15Help me to speak,
and I will praise you, Lord.
16Offerings and sacrifices
are not what you want.
17The way to please you
is to be truly sorry
deep in our hearts.
This is the kind of sacrifice
you won't refuse.
18Please be willing, Lord,
to help the city of Zion
and to rebuild its walls.
19Then you will be pleased
with the proper sacrifices,
and we will offer bulls
on your altar once again.
translation_text:
M-Nimbɔtiu, dū m-kpitii kí pɔ̄-mi
1Daafiidi di ŋmàn̄ nlan nee ki tīī bilaŋgaaliibi kpiliu. 2Daafiidi dōoǹ nì Urii nimpuu Batiseeba ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Naatan cūtì u-cee ki sòon̄ nì u. Ŋyunti gbanti ní u gāā nlan nee.
3Unimbɔti, a-neeŋkpaandi puee, á sɔ̄ m-saai.
Sii un poon mɔ̄ tikpilee, pítí m-yìntitam.
4Fíntí-mi kí nyāntí m-kpitiin ḿ nyā dándan,
ní kí pítí m-yìntitam kí ŋá-mi circir.
5Di sá yii m nyí m nín yīntiǹ-see,
m-kpitii dɔ̄ m-nimbiin ní baabadal.
6Sii baba nì a-baba ní m yīntiǹ,
di sá yii m ŋá tin kaa ŋān̄ a-ceeyee.
Míǹ puee báà a yaa sòon̄ m-bɔtaaa, a cáá nsan,
a yaa sòon̄ ki kūū m-bɔtaaa, a cáá mbaamɔn.
7Tiŋman, ikpitin ní bi màl̄-mi,
m-na nín cáá m-poolee, m sá unikpiti ní.
8Tiŋman, min kamaa a dū ibaamɔn ki bál̀ dibɔmbɔndinee,
tibɔbalkaal gbanti poon ní a dàkà-mi iciin.
9Dū kifaapibiki kin bi yíì isɔpee kí yàaǹ
m-kpitii pu ḿ nīn bí circir,
fàl̀-mi, ní ḿ nīn kíǹ ki pīiǹ káŋkaŋ.
10Yàntī ḿ gbìl̄ mmɔn nì dipɔɔpindi m-ni,
ní akpab ŋin a nàn̄ dúsi dusee ń yīkì kí nīn ŋōō.
11Fàtī a-boon kí tīī m-kpitii,
pítí m-yìntitam kɔkɔ.
12Unimbɔti, náań dipɔbil din bí circiree kí tīī-mi,
dū ŋfam min pɔ̀ɔǹee kí ŋá m-ni.
13Taa dū-mi kí fá,
kí taa fàtīí fōō a-circir Fam m-cee.
14Fàtīí tīī-mi mmɔn ŋun bí a-fiil poonee,
ní nlammɔntiim fam ń nīn tíkí-mi.
15M làá dàkà bikpitiŋaliibi a-saŋŋu,
ní ikpitidambi ń fàtīí gítiń a-cee.
16M-Nimbɔtiu, Unimbɔti m-fiiliu, fīī-mi nnikpaakoon bɔkpilin
ní ḿ gāā ilan mpɔn kí sòoǹ a-deedeeu pu.
17Ti-Dindaan, tábití m-nyunculiŋ
ní ḿ dū m-nyɔkɔ kí gāā ilan kí nyɔ̄ŋkì-si.
18Di sá yii a yaa là saraabi, m bàà ŋáań kí tīī-si.
Bisaraawɔkaabi gba kaa fáatiǹ-si.
19 Saraa un di fáatiǹ Unimbɔtee
di sá dipɔbil din sīntiǹ di-ba taapuee.
Unimbɔti, aa fàtī a-boon kí tīī dipɔbil din sīntiǹ di-ba kɔkɔee.
20Án nīn mɔ̄ǹ-si á ŋá Siiyɔn tiŋki tiŋan,
fàtīí mā digundi kí tū Jeerusaleem.
21Niinee a làá fōō deedee saraabi,
nì bisaraawɔkaabi kɔkɔ.
Ŋyunti gbantee ti làá dū inajaa kí ŋá saraa nsaraafan pu.

english_text:
(A special psalm by David for the music leader. He wrote this when Doeg from Edom went to Saul and said, “David has gone to Ahimelech's house.”)
God Is in Control
1 You people may be strong
and brag about your sins,
but God can be trusted
day after day.
2You plan brutal crimes,
and your lying words cut
like a sharp razor.
3You would rather do evil
than good, and tell lies
than speak the truth.
4You love to say cruel things,
and your words are a trap.
5God will destroy you forever!
He will grab you and drag you
from your homes.
You will be uprooted
and left to die.
6When good people see
this fearsome sight,
they will laugh and say,
7“Just look at them now!
Instead of trusting God,
they trusted their wealth
and their cruelty.”
8But I am like an olive tree
growing in God's house,
and I can count on his love
forever and ever.
9I will always thank God
for what he has done;
I will praise his good name
when his people meet.
translation_text:
Taa nín̄ máká a-gaajati pu
1Daafiidi di ŋmàn̄ nlan nee ki tīī bilaŋgaaliibi kpiliu. 2Ueedoomja Dooweegi nìn cūtìi tùkū Sayuul yii: «Daafiidi cūtì Ayiimeeleeki cee.»
3Ubaatandaan, ba pu ní a yòontí a-ba a-kpitii pu míǹ?
Unimbɔti ŋanti bí ní baabadal.
4A-limbil sòoǹ ki bɔ́ntí min a làá ŋá ikpitee,
dì jītí kii bɔlfi un bi lōoǹee,
ní ki yáb̀ ki sòoǹ tinyimɔmbɔti.
5A néeń tikpitil ki jítiǹ tiŋan,
ní ki néeń nnyimɔn ki jítiǹ mbaamɔn.
6A néeń kí sòoǹ kí bīil̀ unil,
a-limbil ŋmàtíǹ binib ŋma ní.
7Unimbɔti u-ba di làá nàan̄-si múb,
u làá dáaĺ-si kí nyāntí a-diikun,
ní kí lēē-si binifoobi tiŋki pu.
8Deedeedambi làá dāá ká ní kí fàŋkì,
ní kí dāá nīn lāā ki lì yii:
9«Kpèè ubaatandaan
un kaa nìn sáǹ ki kɔ́ Unimbɔti,
ama ní ki nìn máká u-gaajati pu,
ki dàkafī yii u pɔ̄ɔ̄yee sèé!»
10Ama mamee, m bí kii ɔliifi subu
bun túkúee ní Unimbɔti diikun.
Unimbɔti neeŋkpaandi pu ní
m máká kí nīn cá jaanjaan.
11M làá nīn pée nyɔ́ŋkí-si ní kí taa gbèen̄
kun ní a ŋée pu.
M làá nīn máká a-yindi pu bin yú nì si deedeeyee nimbiin,
di sá yii an ŋān̄ míǹ.
M làá nyɔ̄ŋkì-si deedeedambi nimbiin.

english_text:
(A special psalm by David for the music leader. To the tune “Mahalath.”
)
No One Can Ignore God
1 Only a fool would say,
“There is no God!”
People like that are worthless!
They are heartless and cruel
and never do right.
2From heaven God
looks down to see
if anyone is wise enough
to search for him.
3But all of them
are crooked and corrupt.
Not one of them does right.
4Won't you lawbreakers learn?
You refuse to pray,
and you gobble up
the people of God.
5But you will be terrified
worse than ever before.
God will scatter the bones
of his enemies,
and you will be ashamed
when God rejects you.
6I long for someone from Zion
to come and save Israel!
Our God, when you bless
your people again,
Jacob's family will be glad,
and Israel will celebrate.
translation_text:
Ubɔ bí ki nyàab̀ Unimbɔtaaa?
(Kpèè Ilan 14)
1Daafiidi di ŋmàn̄ nlan nee ki tīī bilaŋgaaliibi kpiliu.
2Bigbaambi lì bi-ban yii:
«Unimbɔti kpá!»
Bi gáatì ní ki ŋáań ntimbiil tuuŋŋi,
bi-kansikin ubɔ kaa pée ŋáań tin kítèe.
3Doooo yilpu ní Unimbɔti gbóoń ki kpēē binib,
kí kpèè ubɔ yaa bí ki cáá iciin ki nyàab̀ Unimbɔti.
4Bi-kɔkɔ wáŋkì, ugàntil kpá ki ŋáań tin kítèe,
báà ubɔ kaa bí ki ŋáań tin ŋān̄ee,
báà uniseen, an kpá ní.
5«Bikpitiŋaliibi nee kalin sá bigbaambi níii?
Bi mùul̄ m-nibul ki jīǹ,
ní kaa pée jáaḿ-mi dalba dalba.»
6Niinee ní bi fāŋkì bi-wunti bíi jìkì,
bíǹ bin kaa nìn fāŋkì ki kée,
di sá yii Unimbɔti làá yàaǹ u-nibul nannanliibi kpabiŋ.
Bi làá kɔ́ icoon,
di sá yii Unimbɔti dū-bi ki fá.
7Ŋma làá nyānní doooo Siiyɔn kí fīī Isirayeel ní?
Unimbɔti yaa láa fātìi gíiǹní u-nib
bin bi nìn cúú kuyuŋuee,
Jaakɔb naantiibi làá dāá nīn fàal̀,
Isirayeel yab làá dāá nīn bí mmɔnni.

english_text:
(For the music leader. Use with stringed instruments. A special psalm that David wrote when the people of Ziph went to Saul and said, “David is hiding here with us.”)
Trusting God in Times of Trouble
1 Save me, God, by your power
and prove that I am right.
2Listen to my prayer
and hear what I say.
3Cruel strangers have attacked
and want me dead.
Not one of them cares
about you.
4You will help me, Lord God,
and keep me from falling;
5you will punish my enemies
for their evil deeds.
Be my faithful friend
and destroy them.
6I will bring a gift
and offer a sacrifice
to you, Lord.
I will praise your name
because you are good.
7You have rescued me
from all my troubles,
and my own eyes have seen
my enemies fall.
translation_text:
Unimbɔti, fīī-mi kí nyāntí m-nannanliibi ŋaan
1Daafiidi di ŋmàn̄ nlan nee ki tīī bilaŋgaaliibi kpiliu. Bi bɔ̀ɔ́ tibati ní ki gà-ŋu. 2Siifi yab nìn cūtìi tùkū Sayuul yii Daafiidi cūtìi bál̀ bi-cee.»
3Unimbɔti, a-yindi puee, fīī-mi.
Dū a-pɔŋŋu kí sòoǹ m-bɔti kí pɔ̀-mi.
4Unimbɔti, pīlifì m-wimmeem,
kpòon̄ a-tafal kí pīlifì tibɔti tin nyēeń m-nyɔkɔnee.
5Binicambi bíi jáà nì mi
ní bin néeń tipɔmbɔtee bíi nyàab̀ kí kpɔ̀-mi.
An nibee kaa dū Unimbɔti ki yíiń tiba.
6Kpèè, Unimbɔti di sá m-jòońliu,
ti-Dindaan di sá un tíkí-mee.
7Yàntī bin cɔ́ŋkí-mee kpitii ń gítí bi-pu!
A-baamɔŋyi puee, nàan̄-bi.
8Ti-Dindaan, m làá ŋá saraabi kí tīī-si nì dipɔbil diba.
M làá nyɔ̄ŋkì a-yindi, di sá yii a ŋān̄.
9A fīī-mi ki nyántì dinimbinaamandi kamaa poon,
ní m-nimbil ká m-nannanliibi lítitam.

english_text:
(A special psalm by David for the music leader. Use with stringed instruments.)
Betrayed by a Friend
1Listen, God, to my prayer!
Don't reject my request.
2Please listen and help me.
My thoughts are troubled,
and I keep groaning
3because my enemies attack
with loud shouts.
They treat me terribly
and hold angry grudges.
4My heart is racing fast,
and I am afraid of dying.
5I am trembling with fear,
completely terrified.
6I wish I had wings
like a dove,
so I could fly far away
and be at peace.
7I would go and live
in some distant desert.
8I would quickly find shelter
from howling winds
and raging storms.
9Confuse my enemies, Lord!
Upset their plans.
Cruelty and violence
are all I see in the city,
10and they are like guards
on patrol day and night.
The city is full of trouble,
evil, 11and corruption.
Troublemakers and liars
freely roam the streets.
12My enemies are not the ones
who sneer and make fun.
I could put up with that
or even hide from them.
13But it was my closest friend,
the one I trusted most.
14We enjoyed being together,
when we went with others
to your house, our God.
15All who hate me are controlled
by the power of evil.
Sentence them to death
and send them down alive
to the world of the dead.
16I ask for your help, Lord God,
and you will keep me safe.
17Morning, noon, and night
you hear my concerns
and my complaints.
18I am attacked from all sides,
but you will rescue me
unharmed by the battle.
19You have always ruled,
and you will hear me.
You will defeat my enemies
because they won't turn
and worship you.
20My friend turned against me
and broke his promise.
21His words were smoother
than butter, and softer
than olive oil.
But hatred filled his heart,
and he was ready to attack
with a sword.
22Our Lord, we belong to you.
We tell you what worries us,
and you won't let us fall.
23But what about those people
who are cruel and brutal?
You will throw them down
into the deepest pit
long before their time.
I trust you, Lord!
translation_text:
Unil un u-bɔɔ nyáń u-boonee wimmeem
1Daafiidi di ŋmàn̄ nlan nee ki tīī bilaŋgaaliibi kpiliu. Bi bɔ̀ɔ́ tibati ní ki gà-ŋu.
2Unimbɔti, pīlifì m-wimmeem,
m yaa bíi gbàam̄-see, á taa fàtī a-boon kí tīī-mi.
3Pīlifì-mi kí kíí-mi.
Maa ti nyí tin poon m bée ní m bí ki yáliŋkí
4m-nannanliibi nín sòoǹ puee,
nì bitɔŋfitiibi nín wɔ́b̀-mi puee.
Di sá yii bi cáá agìń ki tòó m-pu,
ní ki jáà nì mi nì diŋuul.
5M-pɔbil máfí
ní ŋkúm nyoondi cúú-mi.
6Kufaaŋŋu cúú-mi m bíi jìkì,
ní m-wunti dūu kpíì.
7Niinee ní m lī m-ban yii:
«M kāntí la dibeenanjil feeŋyi!
M bàà làá ŋàaǹ kí cùú nīn bíń laaba.
8Tiŋman, m bàà làá cù ndandati,
kí tin nín̄ kóò kuteeun.
9M bàà làá ŋá malaa kí ká kibalilaŋ,
kí nīn dátiǹ kubuŋkpaaŋŋu nee.»
10Ti-Dindaan, kɔ́ǹ-bi fìkil fikil poon,
kí yàntī bi-limbiliŋ ń nyìŋfì.
Di sá yii m ká tipɔmbɔti nì
kunikpɔŋkpɔkɔu kitiŋ nee poon.
11Bi tɔ́kɔ́ digundi yilpu ki còom̄
ki màntī ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu.
Kitiŋ ki-ba poonee, an sá digaŋgam nì dinimbinaamandi ní,
12nnikpaakoon bí ki-poon.
Ki-sampaambi kaa lóotí tipɔmbɔti nì dikiildi.
13An yaa bàà sá m-nannanliu di bíi sìí-mi,
m bàà ŋūǹ kí ŋmèè.
An yaa sá m-pulincɔnti di kpèé ki sìŋkīǹ-mi,
m bàà búntí kí wàatī-u.
14Ama an sá sii, m-nabiki,
m-bɔɔmɔnti, unil un man nì u tāatée!
15Ti nìn sòoǹ ní an mɔ̄
ní ki nìn còom̄ dicilpu míǹ kunimbɔtidiin.
16Yàntī m-nannanliibi ń kpú ŋkúntuntukum!
Bí nīn wāĺ nì bi-nimbiliŋ ní kí sìntī ditaŋkpiilin,
di sá yii ntoom bí bi-dumpui ki bí bi-pɔbiliŋin.
17Mamee, Unimbɔti ní m yíì,
ní úǹ ti-Dindaan di làá fīī-mi.
18Kutaafaau nì ŋwiimpu nì kujoou,
m yáliŋkí ki fátí diniindi.
Ama u gbìl̄ m-neen pu,
19ki fīī-mi ki wúń m-pu
ŋyunti ŋun bi nìn bíi jáà nì mee,
di sá yii m-nannanliibi nìn wīikí m-pu.
20Unimbɔti ń pīlifiǹ-mi kí sìntīǹ-bi taapu,
úǹ un sá ubɔti kí nīn cá jaanjaanee!
Baa làá kpántí bi-ba,
baa fàŋkí Unimbɔti.
21M-bɔɔmɔnti gbanti jáà nì u-bɔɔbi ní,
waa tɔ́ dipoondi din u pōoǹee.
22U-nyɔkɔ mɔ̄ kii tisiilee ní,
ama ní u-poon tū kátí kati.
U-nyɔɔbuŋŋi mèeǹ kii dikpajundee ní,
ama ki jītí kii kitàataajikee.
23Túutí a-waŋgul kí dūú túń ti-Dindaan,
u làá tíkiń-si,
u kpá kí yàntī tiba ń cìŋkì deedeedaan.
24Ama sii Unimbɔti, a làá yàntī
binib gbanti ń sìntī ditaŋkpiilin.
Nnikpaakoon dambi nì binyimɔndambi nee
kaa làá bà bi-wiiŋyi dijandi gba.
Ama mamee, sii pu ní m máká.

english_text:
(For the music leader. To the tune “A Silent Dove in the Distance.”
A special psalm by David when the Philistines captured him in Gath.)
A Prayer of Trust in God
1 Have pity, God Most High!
My enemies chase me all day.
2Many of them are pursuing
and attacking me,
3but even when I am afraid,
I keep on trusting you.
4I praise your promises!
I trust you and am not afraid.
No one can harm me.
5Enemies spend the whole day
finding fault with me;
all they think about
is how to do me harm.
6They attack from ambush,
watching my every step
and hoping to kill me.
7They won't get away
with these crimes, God,
because when you get angry,
you destroy people.
8You have kept record
of my days of wandering.
You have stored my tears
in your bottle
and counted each of them.
9When I pray, Lord God,
my enemies will retreat,
because I know for certain
that you are with me.
10I praise your promises!
11I trust you and am not afraid.
No one can harm me.
12I will keep my promises
to you, my God,
and bring you gifts.
13You protected me from death
and kept me from stumbling,
so that I would please you
and follow the light
that leads to life.
translation_text:
M máká Unimbɔti pu ní kaa fàŋkí tiba
1Fiiliistii yab nín cúú Daafiidi Gaati tiŋkinee, boon ní u ŋmàn̄ nlan nee ki tīī bilaŋgaaliibi kpiliu. Bi gà-ŋu kii dibeenanjil nín sūǹní ndan puee ní.
2Unimbɔti, sɔ̄ m-saai, di sá yii bi kā m-pu,
ŋwiin kamaa, bi jáà nì mi ki wɔ́b̀-mi.
3M-nannanliibi kā m-pu baabadal.
Bin bí ki jáà nì mee wīikí tikpil.
4Ama ŋyunti ŋun kufaaŋŋu yaa cúú-mee,
m dù m-mákal kí páań sii pu ní.
5M nyɔ́ŋkí Unimbɔti u-nyɔɔbundi pu,
m máká u-pu ní kaa fàŋkí tiba.
Ba ní nisaaleen ŋūǹ kí ŋá-mi?
6Ŋwiin kamaayee, bi cútí m-nyɔɔbuŋŋi ki kpántí,
bi pée dàkafī m-pu tikpitil ŋma ní.
7Bi bāal̀ ki cɔ́ŋkí-mi
ní ki kpèé tin kɔkɔ m ŋáańee
ki pée nyàab̀ kí lēē m-maŋfal.
8Atuŋkpiti nee puee, bi làá ŋmátáaa?
Unimbɔti, a-ŋuul ń fáá binib nee kí lúkú!
9A kàan̄ ŋfunyɔm min m sáǹee.
Tíkiń m-nyinnyim kí ŋá a-lookun.
Aa kàan̄-mì ki ŋá a-gbɔŋkunaaa?
10Ŋwiin ŋun m làá dāá yíiń-see,
m-nannanliibi làá dāá fàtīí gítí bi-boon.
Tin m nyée di sá yii Unimbɔti bí m-jandi pú.
11M nyɔ́ŋkí Unimbɔti tin u sòon̄ee pu,
m nyɔ́ŋkí ti-Dindaan u-nyɔɔbundi pu.
12M máká Unimbɔti pu ní kaa fàŋkí tiba.
Ba ní unil ŋūǹ kí ŋá-mi?
13Unimbɔti, m nín pōoǹ-si puee, m làá ŋá míǹ.
M làá ŋá ijaam saraau kí tīī-si.
14Di sá yii a fīī-mi ki nyántì ŋkúmin,
kaa yāntì m lítì.
Míǹ puee, m làá nīn còom̄ Unimbɔti nimbiin
ŋwalifi ŋun ŋmíntí binifoobee poon.

english_text:
(For the music leader. To the tune “Don't Destroy.”
A special psalm by David when he was in the cave while running from Saul.)
Praise and Trust in Times of Trouble
1 God Most High, have pity on me!
Have mercy. I run to you
for safety.
In the shadow of your wings,
I seek protection
till danger dies down.
2I pray to you, my protector.
3You will send help from heaven
and save me,
but you will bring trouble
on my attackers.
You are faithful,
and you can be trusted.
4My enemies are fierce,
much worse than lions!
They have spears and arrows
instead of teeth,
and they have sharp swords
instead of tongues.
5May you, my God, be honored
above the heavens;
may your glory be seen
everywhere on earth.
6 Enemies set traps for my feet
and struck me down.
They dug a pit in my path,
but fell in it themselves.
7I am faithful to you,
and you can trust me.
I will sing and play music
for you, my God.
8I feel wide awake!
I will wake up my harp
and wake up the sun.
9I will praise you, Lord,
for everyone to hear,
and I will sing hymns to you
in every nation.
10Your love reaches higher
than the heavens;
your loyalty extends
beyond the clouds.
11May you, my God, be honored
above the heavens;
may your glory be seen
everywhere on earth.
translation_text:
Yilpu fɔ́ŋŋŋ Nimbɔtiu ní m yíì
(B. 8-12. kpèè 108.2-6)
1Daafiidi nín sáǹ ki kɔ́ ntaŋkpalɔkɔn ki ŋmátì Sayuul ŋaanee ní u gāā nlan nee ki tīī bilaŋgaaliibi kpiliu.
2Sɔ̄ m-saai, Unimbɔti sɔ̄ m-saai,
di sá yii sii ní m sáǹ ki kɔ́.
A-feeŋyi booŋŋu taapu ní m sáǹ ki kɔ́
kí nīn cí dinimbinaamandi nee ń jītí.
3Yilpu fɔ́ŋŋŋ Nimbɔtiu ní m yíì,
Unimbɔti un làá ŋá tikɔkɔ kí tīī-mee.
4U làá tīiń-mi difiil doooo yilpu,
u làá yàntī icoo ń cúú un kā m-puee.
Unimbɔti làá dàkà-mi u-neeŋkpaandi nì u-deedeeu.
5M dɔ̄ binib bin bí kii
gbikintib bin ŋmóò binibee kansikin ní.
Bi-nyiŋŋi cɔ́m̀ kii ŋkpamu nì ipiinee ní,
ní bi-limbiliŋ jītí kii bɔlfee.
6Unimbɔti, a sá ukpaan ki jítiǹ kutagbɔŋu,
yàntī a-nyooti ń gbí kitiŋ kɔkɔ!
7Bi dū kulaaŋŋu ki píĺ m-saŋŋu pu,
maa ti cáá dimákal.
Bi gbìn̄ mbòó ki píĺ-mi,
ama bíǹ bi-ba di jéetì ŋu-poon.
8M cáá dimákal, Unimbɔti,
m lafun baasii cáá dimákal ní,
m làá gāā nlan kí nyɔ̄ŋkì-si.
9M-naŋki, fìntī,
iŋmii saalaa beeku saŋguu, fìntīmaanee,
m làá péeǹ kutaa kí fìntī.
10Ti-Dindaan, m làá nyɔ̄ŋkì-si anibul kansikin,
m làá gāā ilan kí pàkà-si atimbun kansikin.
11Di sá yii a-neeŋkpaandi tùutī kutagbɔŋu,
ní a-deedeeu sàatī atagban.
12Unimbɔti, a sá ukpaan ki jítiǹ kutagbɔŋu,
yàntī a-nyooti ń gbí kitiŋ kɔkɔ!

english_text:
(A special psalm by David for the music leader. To the tune “Don't Destroy.”
)
A Prayer When All Goes Wrong
1Do you mighty people talk
only to oppose justice?
Don't you ever judge fairly?
2You are always planning evil,
and you are brutal.
3You have done wrong and lied
from the day you were born.
4Your words spread poison
like the bite of a cobra
5that refuses to listen
to the snake charmer.
6My enemies are fierce
as lions, Lord God!
Shatter their teeth.
Snatch out their fangs.
7Make them disappear
like leaking water,
and make their arrows miss.
8Let them dry up like snails
or be like a child that dies
before seeing the sun.
9Wipe them out quicker
than a pot can be heated
by setting thorns on fire.
10Good people will be glad
when they see the wicked
getting what they deserve,
and they will wash their feet
in their enemies' blood.
11Everyone will say, “It's true!
Good people are rewarded.
God does indeed rule the earth
with justice.”
translation_text:
Unimbɔti di sá un sòoǹ binib bɔtee
1Daafiidi di ŋmàn̄ nlan nee ki tīī bilaŋgaaliibi kpiliu. Bi gà-ŋu nì nneen ŋun sá «Taa yàntī bí bīil̀ee...» ní.
2Tiŋman, ni yaa sòoǹee, ibaamɔn ŋmí ní.
Nnibiyaamu, ni sòoǹ binib bɔti deedeeee?
3Aayee! Ni pée nyí ní ki ŋáań ikpiti,
nimbi ni-ba di ŋáań tipɔmbɔti kitiŋ pu.
4Binikpitib pée sá bikpitib doooo bi-na poon ní,
bi tin pée lì yii bi màal̀-bee, bi kíĺ bi bíi mɔ́ntí.
5Bi cáá tilool kii ukoobuee ní.
Bi bí kii ukoowaati un kpáá u-tafaliŋ,
6kaa pílifí ikoobu laŋgaaliu laŋŋu,
àá ukpaŋkpanti un bīń tiŋanee.
7Unimbɔti, gbá kí wūkul̀ bi-nyiŋŋi bi-nyɔmmun,
ti-Dindaan, gbá kí fúkutí agbikintipɔmbil gbanti nyiŋŋi.
8Yàntī bí wāŋkì kii nnyim min dɔ̄ ki pùub̀ee!
Yàntī bi-piiŋyi in bi tòóyee ń kpántí ipincal.
9Bí nīn bí kii yaaweel un còom̄ ki kōō ki cée!
Bí taa wāl̀ ŋwìiń kii kibiki kin bi màl̄ kaa yōoǹee!
10Kí wàatī bi-bɔjanaakuŋŋi ń wíiǹ kí ŋá akpaanee,
kunaakpaabuŋŋu kubɔ ń dāá yòon̄-ŋi,
báà ŋi yaa dá láá sɔ̀m̀aaa, ŋi yaa kūńaaa, an kaa páb́.
11Deedeedaan yaa láa ká Unimbɔti bíi dátí binikpitib tafalee,
án làá dāá mɔ̄ɔkiǹ-u ní ú dāá fíntí u-taaŋi bi-fatikuu poon.
12Binib làá dāá lì yii: «Deedeedaan lafun cáá tipaal.
Tiŋman, Unimbɔti ubɔ lafun bí kitiŋ nee pu ki sòoǹ binib bɔti.»

english_text:
(For the music leader. To the tune “Don't Destroy.”
A special psalm by David when Saul had David's house watched so that he could kill him.)
A Prayer for Protection
1 Save me, God! Protect me
from enemy attacks!
2Keep me safe from brutal people
who want to kill me.
3Merciless enemies, Lord,
are hiding and plotting,
hoping to kill me.
I have not hurt them
in any way at all.
4But they are ready to attack.
Do something! Help me!
Look at what's happening.
5 Lord God All-Powerful,
you are the God of Israel.
Punish the other nations
and don't pity those terrible
and rebellious people.
6My enemies return at evening,
growling like dogs
roaming the city.
7They curse, and their words
cut like swords,
as they say to themselves,
“No one can hear us!”
8You, Lord, laugh at them
and sneer at the nations.
9You are my mighty fortress,
and I depend on you.
10You love me and will let me
see my enemies defeated.
11Don't kill them,
or everyone may forget!
Just use your mighty power
to make them tremble
and fall.
You are a shield
for your people.
12My enemies are liars!
So let them be trapped
by their boastful lies.
13Get angry and destroy them.
Leave them in ruin.
Then all the nations will know
that you rule in Israel.
14Those liars return at evening,
growling like dogs
roaming the city.
15They search for scraps of food,
and they snarl
until they are stuffed.
16But I will sing about
your strength, my God,
and I will celebrate
because of your love.
You are my fortress,
my place of protection
in times of trouble.
17I will sing your praises!
You are my mighty fortress,
and you love me.
translation_text:
M-Nimbɔtiu, fīī-mi kí nyāntí m-nannanliibi ŋaan
1Daafiidi di ŋmàn̄ nlan nee ki tīī bilaŋgaaliibi kpiliu. Bi gà-ŋu nì nneen ŋun sá «Taa yàntī bí bīil̀ee...» ní. Saayuul nìn tú binib bí cù Daafiidi dumpu kí kpèè yii u yaa bée, bí kpɔ̀-u.
2Unimbɔti, fīī-mi kí nyāntí m-nannanliibi ŋaan,
wúń m-pu bin jáà nì mee ń taa ŋmā kí ŋá-mi tiba.
3Fīī-mi kí nyāntí binikpitib nee ŋaan,
fīī-mi binikpɔliibi nee ŋaan.
4Kpèè! Bi cí kí lēē m-maŋfal,
bin pɔ̄ɔ̄yee bíi jáà nì mi.
Ma mun kaa ŋá ikpiti ibaaa,
kaa tí yīntì mun, ti-Dindaan!
5Maa ŋá tikpitil tiba, ama bi sáń kí cùú bɔ́ntí kí cīití-mi.
Fìntī! Dāan̄ m-cee kí kpèè.
6Sii ti-Dindaan, Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiuee,
fìntī kí dáaĺ atimbun nee kɔkɔ tafal.
Taa sɔ̄ bin nyēē bi-bɔɔbi booŋyi nee saai.
7Bi fàtīi gítiń kujoou kamaa
ki mùuǹ kii ibooyee,
ní ki còom̄ ki màntī kitiŋ.
8Ntoonam di gbí bi-nyɔmmun,
ní bi-nyɔɔbuŋŋi bí kii kitàataajikee.
Bi dàkafī bi-ni yii: «Ŋma di làá gbìl̄?»
9Ama sii ti-Dindaan, a bí ní ki lāā-bi,
a bèel̄ atimbun nee kɔkɔ nib.
10Sii ní m kpèé, man pɔŋŋu.
Unimbɔti di sá man taŋkpanaakooku.
11Man Nimbɔtiu néeń-mi ní ki làá dāá fīī-mi.
Man Nimbɔtiu làá yàntī ń jī m-nannanliibi pu dinyandi.
12Taa nàan̄-bi kɔŋkɔnnee,
an yaa kaa sá míǹ, m-nibul làá súntí a-jajil pu.
Dū a-pɔŋŋu kí gbāfì-bi kí fá
ní kí sìntī-bi taapu,
ti-Dindaan, ti-gbampɔɔl.
13Bi yaa pée kíĺ isoonee,
ikpiti ŋma di nyēē bi-nyɔmmun,
yàntī bi-lambil ń kpántí kii kutaliŋŋuee kí sàl̀-bi,
kun puee bi tòó mbusu ki mɔ́ntí inyimɔn!
14Nàan̄-bi a-ŋuul poon,
kpɔ̀ kí céetí-bi múb ubɔ ń taa ti kíń.
Yàntī bí béé yii Unimbɔti di sá Jaakɔb bɔtiu
kí cáá sāā kitiŋ kúntilaŋki.
15Bi fàtīi gítiń kujoou kamaa
ki mùuǹ kii ibooyee,
ní ki còom̄ ki màntī kitiŋ.
16Bi còom̄ ki nyàab̀ kun ní bi làá jēe,
ní bi yaa kaa jíń ki díkée,
ní bí kíĺ ki bíi gbóoĺ.
17Ama mamee, m làá nīn gà ilan ki pàkà a-pɔŋŋu,
m làá nīn gà ilan kutaafaau ki lì yii: «A ŋān̄,»
di sá yii sii di sá m-taŋkpanaakooku,
dinimbinaamandi yuntiŋuee, sii Unimbɔti ní m sáń ki kóò.
18Sii un sá m-pɔŋŋuee, m làá nīn nyɔ́ŋkí-si.
Man taŋkpanaakooku di sá Unimbɔti,
Unimbɔti gbanti di néeń-mi.

english_text:
(For the music leader. To the tune “Lily of the Promise.” A special psalm by David for teaching. He wrote it during his wars with the Arameans of northern Syria,
when Joab came back and killed twelve thousand Edomites
in Salt Valley.)
You Can Depend on God
1 You, God, are angry with us!
We are rejected and crushed.
Make us strong again!
2You made the earth shake
and split wide open;
now heal its wounds
and stop its trembling.
3You brought hard times
on your people,
and you gave us wine
that made us stagger.
4You gave a signal to those
who worship you,
so they could escape
from enemy arrows.
5Answer our prayers, God!
Use your powerful arm
and give us victory.
Then the people you love
will be safe.
6Our God, you solemnly promised,
“I would gladly divide up
the city of Shechem
and give away Succoth Valley
piece by piece.
7The lands of Gilead
and Manasseh are mine.
Ephraim is my war helmet,
and Judah is the symbol
of my royal power.
8Moab is merely my washbasin.
Edom belongs to me,
and I shout in triumph
over the Philistines.”
9Our God, who will bring me
to the fortress,
or lead me to Edom?
10Have you rejected us
and deserted our armies?
11Help us defeat our enemies!
No one else can rescue us.
12You will give us victory
and crush our enemies.
translation_text:
Unimbɔti, pīlifì a-nibul kuŋkuuntii
(B. 7-14. kpèè 108.7-14)
1Daafiidi di ŋmàn̄ nlan nee ki tīī bilaŋgaaliibi kpiliu bí nīn cáa dàkà. Bi bɔ̀ɔ́ kubeeu ní ki gà-ŋu. 2Daafiidi cūtìi jáń nì Aram yab bin kóò Meesoopootamii nì Sooba timmunee. Bi nín kūnnée, Joowaab fātìi gítì ki kūū Eedoom yab binib kutukub saalaa nì bili Ŋyaam tantakalin. Niinee ní Daafiidi lī yii:
3Unimbɔti, a dū-ti ki fá, ki yāntì ti yàl̄.
Min kamaa a gíí ti-pu diŋuulee, fàtīí tīī-ti mpɔn.
4A yāntì kitiŋ cīŋkì ki fáá iwèeń,
fàtīí ŋéeb́ ki-wèeŋ́yi, di sá yii kàa ti yú ki pɔ̄ɔ̄.
5A yāntì a-nibul jíń falaa tikpil,
a yāntì ti nyùn̄ ndaam min pɔ̄ɔ̄yee.
6A tīī bin fàŋkí-see kudaaŋŋu bí sāǹ
ipiin ń taa cúú-bi.
7Dū a-pɔŋkpaaŋŋu kí fīī-ti kí fōō ti-wimmeem,
án nín làá ŋá pu a-nib bin a néeńee ń ká difiilee.
8Unimbɔti sòon̄ u-circir diiku poon.
M jáń ki jíń! M làá yàkatī Siikeem tiŋki,
ní kí ŋmàntī Sukooti tantakal.
9Man di yì Galaadi, man di tí yì Manasee mun.
Eefiraayiim di sá man janjafuuliiki,
ní Juuda sá m-beel pɔŋŋu.
10Moowaab sá kusampeeu kun poon m fùul̀ee ní.
M tákatì m-naatakal ki lúkú Eedoom tiŋki pu,
m fátí dijajil kuŋkuuntii Fiiliistii tiŋki pu.
11Ŋma di làá cùnnì-mi kitiŋ kin bi máń digundi ki túee poon ní?
Ŋma di làá cùnnì-mi Eedoom tiŋkin,
12an kaa sá sii Unimbɔti un di dū-ti ki fá,
kaa ti cēentí ti-janjakitiŋeeee?
13Dāá tūtuǹ-ti tí já nì unannanli,
di sá yii unil tūtuntam sá fám ní.
14Unimbɔti yaa bí ti-ceeyee, ti làá já kí jī,
úǹ di làá tāā kí mátí ti-nannanliibi.

english_text:
(A psalm by David for the music leader. Use with stringed instruments.)
Under the Protection of God
1Please listen, God,
and answer my prayer!
2I feel hopeless,
and I cry out to you
from a faraway land.
Lead me to the mighty rock
high above me.
3You are a strong tower,
where I am safe
from my enemies.
4Let me live with you forever
and find protection
under your wings, my God.
5You heard my promises,
and you have blessed me,
just as you bless everyone
who worships you.
6Let the king have a long
and healthy life.
7May he always rule
with you, God, at his side;
may your love and loyalty
watch over him.
8I will sing your praises
forever, God, and will always
keep my promises.
translation_text:
M bàà là kí nīn kóò ti-Dindaan diikun baabadal
1Daafiidi di ŋmàn̄ nlan nee ki tīī bilaŋgaaliibi kpiliu. Bi bɔ̀ɔ́ kubeeu ní ki gà-ŋu.
2Unimbɔti, pīlifì m-biilii,
kpòon̄ a-tafal kí pīlifì m-wimmeem.
3Doooo kitiŋ gbeennyɔkɔ,
ŋyunti ŋun m-pɔbil bíil̀ee,
m kúuǹ ki yíiń-si á jòoń-mi.
Cáá-mi kí cùnnì ditaŋkpal din fɔ̀kɔ̀ maa ŋūǹ kí bà nee cee.
4Di sá yii sii ní m sáń ki kóò,
a sá digunlɔkɔl din pɔ̄ɔ̄yee ní m-nannanliibi nimbiin.
5M bàà là kí nīn kóò a-circir kɔŋkooŋŋun baabadal,
ní kí ká kibalilaŋ a-feeŋyi taapu.
6Unimbɔti, sii di gbìl̄ m-pooŋyi,
ní ki tīī bin fàŋkí a-yindee kun bi lèe.
7Kūtì ubɔti mmaŋfafɔkɔn,
yàntī ú kàl̄ kitiŋ pu doo kí yúntí tikpil tikpil!
8Ú nīn pée kā dibeel pu ki cá jaanjaan a-nimbiin.
Yàntī a-neeŋkpaandi nì a-baamɔŋyi ń nīn wúń u-pu.
9Niinee m làá nīn gà ilan baabadal ki nyɔ́ŋkí-si,
ní kí nīn ŋúb́ m-pooŋyi baabadal.

english_text:
(A psalm by David for Jeduthun, the music leader.)
God Is Powerful and Kind
1Only God can save me,
and I calmly wait for him.
2God alone is the mighty rock
that keeps me safe
and the fortress
where I am secure.
3I feel like a shaky fence
or a sagging wall.
How long will all of you
attack and assault me?
4You want to bring me down
from my place of honor.
You love to tell lies,
and when your words are kind,
hatred hides in your heart.
5Only God gives inward peace,
and I depend on him.
6God alone is the mighty rock
that keeps me safe,
and he is the fortress
where I feel secure.
7God saves me and honors me.
He is that mighty rock
where I find safety.
8Trust God, my friends,
and always tell him
each of your concerns.
God is our place of safety.
9We humans are only a breath;
none of us are truly great.
All of us together weigh less
than a puff of air.
10Don't trust in violence
or depend on dishonesty
or rely on great wealth.
11I heard God say two things:
“I am powerful,
12 and I am very kind.”
The Lord rewards each of us
according to what we do.
translation_text:
M yaa pìlīǹ Unimbɔtee, m-pɔbil sɔ̀m̀ ní
1Daafiidi di ŋmàn̄ nlan nee ki tīī bilaŋgaaliibi kpiliu.
2Unimbɔti cee ní m kāntí dipɔɔsɔŋkil.
U-cee ní m-fiil nyēeń.
3Úǹ di sá m-taŋkpanaakooku nì m-fiil.
U sá m-balilaŋki, tiba kpá kí cìŋkì-mi.
4Kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu ní ni làá kpāfì
kí lùkù unibaanti kí líí-u
kii digundi din wāntèe,
àá kunaabakau kun bíi lítée ní?
5Tinyool paaŋŋu ŋun pu u bée pu
ní ni bí ki mɔ̀ kí kpákatí-u.
Kun pée mɔ̄ǹ-nee di sá inyimɔn.
Ni mèé kinyɔkɔn fám ní ki bìintí,
ama ni-pɔbiliŋ poonee, ni tòó mbusu.
6Unimbɔti cee ní m kāntí dipɔɔsɔŋkil,
u-cee ní m-mákal nyēeń.
7Úǹ di sá m-taŋkpanaakooku nì m-fiil.
U sá m-balilaŋki, tiba kpá kí cìŋkì-mi.
8Unimbɔti di fìil̄-mi ki tìì-mi tinyool.
Úǹ di sá m-taŋkpanaakooku nì laakin m sáń ki kóòyee.
9Nimbi m-nibul, nín̄ mákámaan u-pu ŋyunti kamaa!
Dūmaan tin páb́-nee kí bíĺ u-nimbiin.
Unimbɔti ní ti sáń ki kóò.
10Unil sá kii kubuŋuee ní,
bikpaambeeee, ŋwaamueeee, ubɔ kaa bí tiban.
Dū bi-kɔkɔ kí páań saniya pu kí ŋmàntī,
bi-nyiŋfiŋu kaa làá bà kufoou nyiŋfiŋu gba.
11Taa nín̄ mákámaan tipɔmbɔti pu,
kí taa nín̄ máká tiwan tin ni fìkēe pu.
Báà ni-gaajati yaa bíi wīintáaa,
ní taa nín̄ máká ti-pu.
12Unimbɔti sòon̄ tibɔti tiba,
u sòon̄ tibɔliliitiil tiba mun m gbìl̄,
yii: «Unimbɔti di yì mpɔn.»
13Sii ti-Dindaan di cáá dineeŋkpaandi,
ní ki pà báà ŋma u-tuuŋŋi paati.

english_text:
(A psalm by David when he was in the desert of Judah.)
God's Love Means More than Life
1 You are my God. I worship you.
In my heart, I long for you,
as I would long for a stream
in a scorching desert.
2I have seen your power
and your glory
in the place of worship.
3Your love means more
than life to me,
and I praise you.
4As long as I live,
I will pray to you.
5I will sing joyful praises
and be filled with excitement
like a guest at a banquet.
6I think about you, God,
before I go to sleep,
and my thoughts turn to you
during the night.
7You have helped me,
and I sing happy songs
in the shadow of your wings.
8I stay close to you,
and your powerful arm
supports me.
9All who want to kill me
will end up in the ground.
10Swords will run them through,
and wild dogs will eat them.
11Because of you, our God,
the king will celebrate
with your faithful followers,
but liars will be silent.
translation_text:
A-ŋanti jítiǹ dimaŋfal
1Ŋyunti ŋun Daafiidi nìn bí Juuda teekunee ní u ŋmàn̄ nlan nee.
2Unimbɔti, sii di sá m-Nimbɔtiu! M baasii nyàab̀-si ní.
Kii nnyinnyoo nín cútí unil u nyàab̀ nnyim puee,
míǹ ní m nyàab̀-si.
M fèefī ki nyàab̀-si,
kii kitiŋ kin kūń búkú buku, nnyim kpá ki-puee ní.
3M nyàab̄-si a-kɔŋkooŋŋun,
ki pée nyàab̀ kí wāl̀ a-pɔŋŋu nì a-nyooti.
4Di sá yii a-ŋanti jítiǹ dimaŋfal,
an puee m làá nyɔ̄ŋkì-si.
5M làá nīn jáaḿ-si m-maŋfal wiiŋyi kɔkɔ poon,
ní kí nīn yòontí m-ŋalii yilpu ki mèé-si.
6M làá jī tijimmɔntiil kí díkí,
ní kí gāā ilan nì dipɔɔpindi kí nyɔ̄ŋkì-si.
7M yaa dɔ̄ m-dooŋu puee, m téetí a-pu,
ní ki mèé-si kunyamɔŋu kɔkɔ.
8Di sá yii sii di jòoń-mi,
ní m gāā ilan nì dipɔɔpindi a-feeŋyi booŋŋu taapu.
9M dū m-ba kɔkɔ ki nákáǹ-si,
ní a-ŋaŋgiil tíkí-mi.
10Án nàan̄ bin nyàab̀ kí lēē m-maŋfalee!
Bí sìntī taapu ditaŋkpiilin!
11Yàntī bí kpɔ̀-bi kujaau poon,
bí kpántí sinsiŋkub jinti!
12Ubɔti ń nīn fàal̀ Unimbɔti pu!
Bin yíì Unimbɔti yindi ki pùtēe ń nyɔ̄ŋkì-u,
di sá yii u làá pìin̄ binyimɔndambi nyɔmmu.

english_text:
(A psalm by David for the music leader.)
Celebrate because of the Lord
1Listen to my concerns, God,
and protect me
from my enemies' threats.
2Keep me safe from secret plots
of corrupt and evil gangs.
3Their words cut like swords,
and their cruel remarks
sting like sharp arrows.
4They fearlessly ambush
and shoot innocent people.
5They are determined to do evil,
and they tell themselves,
“Let's set traps!
No one can see us.”
6They make evil plans and say,
“We'll commit a perfect crime.
No one knows our thoughts.”
7But God will shoot his arrows
and quickly wound them.
8They will be destroyed
by their own words,
and everyone who sees them
will tremble with fear.
9They will be afraid and say,
“Look at what God has done
and keep it all in mind.”
10May the Lord bless his people
with peace and happiness
and let them celebrate.
translation_text:
Unimbɔti làá dáaĺ bin sòoǹ ki bíiĺ binibee tafal
1Daafiidi di ŋmàn̄ nlan nee ki tīī bilaŋgaaliibi kpiliu.
2Unimbɔti, pīlifì m-yaliŋkii.
Fīī-mi kí nyāntí unannanli un m fàŋkée ŋaan.
3Fīī-mi kí nyāntí binikpitib nín bíi bɔ́ntí m-pu puee,
nì bikpitiŋaliibi nín bíi kpáfí m-pu miŋyee poon.
4Bi-limbiliŋ jītí kii bɔlfee,
ní bi-nyɔɔbuŋŋi cáá tilool kii ilɔpiinee.
5Bi bāal̀ kí tɔ̄ deedeedaan mpiin.
Bi tòó-u dicilpu niin, kaa fàŋkí tiba.
6Bi tìì tɔb kunyannyaau bi-tuŋkpitiŋ poon,
ki sòoǹ titalindi tin bi làá píĺ dibalinee pu
yii: «Ŋma di làá wāl̀?»
7Bi bɔ́ntí atuŋkpiti ŋin bi làá ŋée.
Bi lì yii: «Ti bɔ́ntì ti-tundi nee tiŋan:
ubɔ kaa ŋūǹ kí béé kun kā unil pɔbilinee!»
8Ama Unimbɔti làá tɔ̄-bi u-piiŋyi.
Dicilpu niinee, bi fōō tiweendi.
9Bíǹ bi-ba nyɔɔbuŋŋi di fātìi gítì bi-pu.
Bin kɔkɔ làá dāá ká-bee dāa gàatī bi-yiliŋ ní.
10Báà ŋma làá dāá fàŋkì.
Binib làá dāá māafì tin Unimbɔti ŋée,
ní kí dāá gbìl̄ tin u ŋée taapu.
11Deedeedambi ń nīn fàal̀ ti-Dindaan pu,
bí sāǹ kí kɔ́-u,
ní bin kɔkɔ pɔbil bí diba nì Unimbɔtee ń nyɔ̄ŋkì-u.

english_text:
(A psalm by David and a song for the music leader.)
God Answers Prayer
1Our God, you deserve praise
in Zion, where we keep
our promises to you.
2Everyone will come to you
because you answer prayer.
3When our sins get us down,
you forgive us.
4You bless your chosen ones,
and you invite them
to live near you
in your temple.
We will enjoy your house,
the sacred temple.
5Our God, you save us,
and your fearsome deeds answer
our prayers for justice!
You give hope to people
everywhere on earth,
even those across the sea.
6You are strong,
and your mighty power
put the mountains in place.
7You silence the roaring waves
and the noisy shouts
of the nations.
8People far away marvel
at your fearsome deeds,
and all who live under the sun
celebrate and sing
because of you.
9You take care of the earth
and send rain to help the soil
grow all kinds of crops.
Your rivers never run dry,
and you prepare the earth
to produce abundant grain.
10You water all its fields
and level the lumpy ground.
You send showers of rain
to soften the soil
and help the plants sprout.
11Wherever your footsteps
touch the earth,
a rich harvest is gathered.
12Desert pastures blossom,
and mountains celebrate.
13Meadows are filled
with sheep and goats;
valleys overflow with grain
and echo with joyful songs.
translation_text:
Unimbɔti, a máaǹ inyɔŋki
1Daafiidi di ŋmàn̄ nlan nee ki tīī bilaŋgaaliibi kpiliu. Nlan.
2Unimbɔti un bí Siiyɔn tiŋkinee,
an máaǹ tí nyɔ̄ŋkì-si,
ní kí ŋá min ti pōoǹ-see.
3Di sá yii a fòol̄ binib wimmeem.
Unil kamaa dòoń a-cee.
4M-kpitii nyìmiǹ-mi,
ama a cáá ti-kpitii kɔkɔ ki pūǹ-ti.
5Unil un a lēē ki yíiń ú dāan̄ a-ceeyee bí mmɔnneeee!
Udaan làá nīn kóò a-kɔŋkooŋŋun.
Ti làá dāá fōō tiwammɔntiil tin bí a-diikunee,
circir wanti tin bí a-kɔŋkooŋŋunee.
6Unimbɔti ti-fiiliu, a sá deedeedaan,
a cáá maamaaci tuuŋŋi ki fòol̄ ti-wimmeem.
Kitiŋ kɔkɔ pu nib
nì tiŋkub bin bíń ndandatee máká sii pu ní.
7Nì a-pɔŋŋu ní a dūu báaǹ ajoon ní ŋi bá ki pɔ̄ɔ̄,
kun puee a dū mpɔn ki gbìn̄ a-caŋ kii gbajee.
8A pèefī tiŋkub wooku,
ki pèefī bi-nyiŋgbanti fuuku,
nì inibool kuŋkuuntii.
9A-maamaaci tuŋkpaaŋŋi ŋin a ŋée puee,
duulinya nib kɔkɔ fāŋkì.
A yàntī ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú nì ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú
timmu kūuntí nì dipɔɔpindi.
10A kpèé kitiŋ, ki sɔ̀ŋkī-kì ntaanyim,
ki gbéeǹ-kì tigaajati.
Unimbɔti, nnyim gbí a-buŋŋu,
a yàntī kitiŋ lòoǹ tikpaajin tiŋan,
min ní a bɔ́ntí-kèe dee.
11A yàantí ki-pɔŋyi,
ki kpátí ki-tannaapikiŋ,
ki yàntī utaa nì ki sɔ̀ŋkī-kì,
ní ki tìì iwambool mpɔn í nyā.
12A yàntī dibindi kúntí tiŋan
laakin kamaa a yaa jítèe, digbíl pùub̀ ní.
13Kuteeu pu naakpaapɔɔku mun cáá tigaajati tibaantiil ní,
ní mmɔn māntìi tú ŋgbantamu.
14Tiwaŋkuti kpátìi gbí kunaakpaapɔɔun,
ní tikpaajin bīī atantaka pu,
tikɔkɔ kūuntí nì mmɔn ki gà ilan.

english_text:
(A song and a psalm for the music leader.)
Shout Praises to God
1Tell everyone on this earth
to shout praises to God!
2Sing about his glorious name.
Honor him with praises.
3Say to God, “Everything you do
is fearsome,
and your mighty power makes
your enemies come crawling.
4You are worshiped by everyone!
We all sing praises to you.”
5Come and see the fearsome things
our God has done!
6 When God made the sea dry up,
our people walked across,
and because of him,
we celebrated there.
7His mighty power rules forever,
and nothing the nations do
can be hidden from him.
So don't turn against God.
8All of you people,
come praise our God!
Let his praises be heard.
9God protects us from death
and keeps us steady.
10Our God, you tested us,
just as silver is tested.
11You trapped us in a net
and gave us heavy burdens.
12You sent war chariots
to crush our skulls.
We traveled through fire
and through floods,
but you brought us
to a land of plenty.
13I will bring sacrifices
into your house, my God,
and I will do what I promised
14when I was in trouble.
15I will sacrifice my best sheep
and offer bulls and goats
on your altar.
16All who worship God,
come here and listen;
I will tell you everything
God has done for me.
17I prayed to the Lord,
and I praised him.
18If my thoughts had been sinful,
he would have refused
to hear me.
19But God did listen
and answered my prayer.
20Let's praise God!
He listened when I prayed,
and he is always kind.
translation_text:
Tí nyɔ̄ŋkì Unimbɔti ufiil
1 Bilaŋgaaliibi kpiliu laŋŋu. Nlan.
Kitiŋ pu kɔkɔ nib, fáámaan ŋwiliili kí nyɔ̄ŋkì Unimbɔti.
2Gāāmaan ilan kí nyɔ̄ŋkì u-yindi,
dūmaan inyɔŋki laŋyi kí tīī-u tinyool.
3Ní lì Unimbɔti yii: «A-tuuŋŋi sá maamaaceeee!»
A-pɔŋŋu nín sá ŋkpaan puee, a-nannanliibi pàkà-si.
4Kitiŋ pu nib kɔkɔ gbàantí a-nimbiin ki jáaḿ-si.
Bi gà ilan ki nyɔ́ŋkí-si,
bi gà ilan ki nyɔ́ŋkí a-yindi.
5Dāá kpèèmaan tin Unimbɔti ŋée,
u-tuuŋŋi kɔ̄ntí binib dinyoondi.
6U yāntì tiŋku fóotì ki kpántì kitiŋkuliŋŋi,
binib dūtì dimɔɔl ŋkulimmi.
An puee tí fàal̀ tin u ŋá nee pu.
7Nì dibaatandi ní u jīǹ dibeel ki cá talku.
U kpèé ki wāĺ atimbun kɔkɔ.
Bin jáà nì uee ń taa nín̄ yòontí bi-ba yilpu!
8Anibul kɔkɔ, jāam̀maan ti-Nimbɔtiu,
nyɔ̄ŋkìmaan-u mpɔn mpɔn.
9Úǹ di yāntì ti bí dimaŋfalin
ní kaa yāntì ti-taaŋi ŋātì.
10Unimbɔti, a cɔ́ŋkì-ti ki kpēē.
A cɔ́ŋkì-ti ki kpēē kii bi nín ŋáań sindaariya ŋŋmin
kí cɔ̄ŋkì-u kí kpèè puee ní,
míǹ ní a cɔ́ŋkì-ti.
11A cáá-ti ki kɔ́ǹ kulaaŋŋun,
a dū awaŋgul ŋin nyìm̀ee ki túǹ-ti.
12A yāntì bitanjakaliibi dū itaamu ki tāā ti-yiliŋ pu ki jítì.
Ti kɔ́ ŋŋmi nì nnyimin,
ama a nyántì-ti ki kɔ́ǹ digbíl poon.
13M làá cáań bisaraawɔkaabi a-diikun,
m làá ŋá tin m pōoǹ yii m làá ŋá kí tīī-see.
14M làá cáań tin nìn nyáń m-nyɔkɔn
ŋyunti ŋun m nìn bí dinimbinaamandinee kí tīī-si.
15M làá dū tiwaŋkuti tin cáá ŋkpamee
kí ŋá saraawɔkaa kí tīī-si.
M làá dū ipijaa kí ŋá saraa kí wà ŋŋmi,
m làá dū inajaa nì iŋɔjaa kí ŋá saraa.
16Nimbi bin kɔkɔ fàŋkí Unimbɔtee, dāá pīlifìmaan,
m làá māafì-ni tin ní u ŋá ki tīī-mee.
17M fáá mbiil ki yíiń-u,
ní ki kíĺ ki bíi nyɔ́ŋkí-u.
18M yaa bàà cáá ilandɔkɔkpiti m-nee,
ti-Dindaan kaa bàà pílifíǹ-mi.
19Ama Unimbɔti pílifiǹ-mi,
u kpōoǹ u-tafal ki pílifì m-wimmeem.
20Tí jāam̀ Unimbɔti,
kun puee waa fātì u-boon ki tīī m-wimmeem,
ní kaa ŋmīntì-mi u-ŋaŋkpaanti.

english_text:
(A psalm and a song for the music leader. Use with stringed instruments.)
Tell the Nations To Praise God
1Our God, be kind and bless us!
Be pleased and smile.
2Then everyone on earth
will learn to follow you,
and all nations will see
your power to save us.
3Make everyone praise you
and shout your praises.
4Let the nations celebrate
with joyful songs,
because you judge fairly
and guide all nations.
5Make everyone praise you, God,
and shout your praises.
6Our God has blessed the earth
with a wonderful harvest!
7Pray for his blessings
to continue
and for everyone on earth
to worship our God.
translation_text:
Anibul kɔkɔ ń nyɔ̄ŋkì-si
1Bilaŋgaaliibi kpiliu laŋŋu. Bi bɔ̀ɔ́ tibati ní ki gà-ŋu. Nlan.
2Unimbɔti, sɔ̄ ti-saai kí bìin̄ ti-pu.
Bútí ti-pu nnimbiin,
3án nín làá ŋá pu binib ń béé kitiŋ pu min a lèe,
ní atimbun kɔkɔ ń béé yii a sá ufiil.
4Unimbɔti, anibul ń nyɔ̄ŋkì-si,
anibul kɔkɔ ń kpāfì kí nyɔ̄ŋkì-si!
5Atimbun kɔkɔ ń gāā ilan nì dipɔɔpindi,
di sá yii a sòoǹ binib bɔti nì mbaamɔn ní,
ní ki kpòotī atimbun ŋin kɔkɔ bí kitiŋ puee.
6Unimbɔti, anibul ń nyɔ̄ŋkì-si,
anibul kɔkɔ ń kpāfì kí nyɔ̄ŋkì-si!
7Kitiŋ lòon̄ tikpaajin,
Unimbɔti, ti-Nimbɔtiu ń bìin̄ ti-pu!
8Unimbɔti ń bìin̄ ti-pu,
ní kitiŋ kɔkɔ pu nib ń fàŋkì-u!

english_text:
(A psalm and a song by David for the music leader.)
God Will Win the Battle
1Do something, God!
Scatter your hateful enemies.
Make them turn and run.
2Scatter them like smoke!
When you come near,
make them melt
like wax in a fire.
3But let your people be happy
and celebrate because of you.
4Our God, you are the one
who rides on the clouds,
and we praise you.
Your name is the Lord,
and we celebrate
as we worship you.
5Our God, from your sacred home
you take care of orphans
and protect widows.
6You find families
for those who are lonely.
You set prisoners free
and let them prosper,
but all who rebel will live
in a scorching desert.
7You set your people free,
and you led them
through the desert.
8 God of Israel,
the earth trembled,
and rain poured down.
You alone are the God
who rules from Mount Sinai.
9When your land was thirsty,
you sent showers
to refresh it.
10Your people settled there,
and you were generous
to everyone in need.
11You gave the command, Lord,
and a chorus of women told
what had happened:
12“Kings and their armies
retreated and ran,
and everything they left
is now being divided.
13And for those who stayed back
to guard the sheep,
there are metal doves
with silver-coated wings
and shiny gold feathers.”
14God All-Powerful, you scattered
the kings like snow falling
on Mount Zalmon.
15Our Lord and our God,
Bashan is a mighty mountain
covered with peaks.
16Why is it jealous of Zion,
the mountain you chose
as your home forever?
17When you, Lord God, appeared
to your people at Sinai,
you came with thousands
of mighty chariots.
18 When you climbed
the high mountain,
you took prisoners with you
and were given gifts.
Your enemies didn't want you
to live there,
but they gave you gifts.
19We praise you, Lord God!
You treat us with kindness
day after day,
and you rescue us.
20You always protect us
and save us from death.
21Our Lord and our God,
your terrible enemies
are ready for war,
but you will crush
their skulls.
22You promised to bring them
from Bashan
and from the deepest sea.
23Then we could wash our feet
in their blood,
and our dogs could chew
on their bones.
24We have seen crowds marching
to your place of worship,
our God and King.
25Singers come first,
and then the musicians,
surrounded by young women
playing tambourines.
26They come shouting,
“People of Israel,
praise the Lord God!”
27The small tribe of Benjamin
leads the way,
followed by the leaders
from Judah.
Then come the leaders
from Zebulun and Naphtali.
28Our God, show your strength!
Show us once again.
29Then kings will bring gifts
to your temple
in Jerusalem.
30Punish that animal
that lives in the swamp!
Punish that nation
whose leaders and people
are like wild bulls.
Make them come crawling
with gifts of silver.
Scatter those nations
that enjoy making war.
31Force the Egyptians to bring
gifts of bronze;
make the Ethiopians hurry
to offer presents.
32Now sing praises to God!
Every kingdom on earth,
sing to the Lord!
33Praise the one who rides
across the ancient skies;
listen as he speaks
with a mighty voice.
34Tell about God's power!
He is honored in Israel,
and he rules the skies.
35The God of Israel is fearsome
in his temple,
and he makes us strong.
Let's praise our God!
translation_text:
Unimbɔti ujajil laŋŋu
1Daafiidi di ŋmàn̄ nlan nee ki tīī bilaŋgaaliibi kpiliu. Nlan.
2Unimbɔti ń yīkì u-nannanliibi ń yàl̄,
bin ná-uee ń sāǹ u-nimbiin.
3Kii ŋŋminyiim nín wáŋkí puee, yàntī bí wāŋkì míǹ,
kii kisikampiŋ nín dùntī ŋŋmin puee,
míǹ ní an nàantí binikpitib Unimbɔti nimbiin.
4Ama ní deedeedambi bí mmɔnni,
bi fàal̀ Unimbɔti nimbiin, ní ki bí dipɔɔpindin!
5Gāāmaan ilan kí tīī Unimbɔti,
gāāmaan ilan kí nyɔ̄ŋkì u-yindi,
cátímaan nsan kí tīī un kā u-janjatɔrɔkuu
pu ki páaǹní atagbannee.
U-yindi di sá ti-Dindaan, nín̄ fàal̀maan u-nimbiin!
6Unimbɔti un di kóò u-circir kɔŋkooŋŋunee
sá ataŋkpiibil baa nì un mɔ́tí bikpiipoobi puee ní.
7Unimbɔti di tìì un kaa cáá ubɔee kudicaŋu,
ní ki tìì bisarkadambi mmɔn nì dibatɔl.
Ama bin jáà nì Unimbɔtee kóò kitiŋkuliŋŋi pu ní.
8Unimbɔti, ŋyunti ŋun a nìn nyáń ki līntì a-nibul nyɔkɔpuee,
ŋyunti ŋun a nìn dū a-ba ki bíl̀ kuteeu puee,
9kitiŋ nìn cīŋkì ní kutagbɔŋu cōotì
Unimbɔti un sá Siinaayi jool Nimbɔtiuee nimbiin,
Unimbɔti un sá Isirayeel Nimbɔtiuee nimbiin.
10Unimbɔti, a nìn yāntì utaa nìn̄ tiŋan pu,
a-nibul nìn gīī ní a fātìi tīī-dì mpɔn.
11A-tiŋki pu ní a-nib kāl̀,
a-ŋanti poonee, Unimbɔti,
a bɔ́ntì mpaan gbanti ki tīī bifalaadambi.
12Ti-Dindaan tīī mara,
ní binimpoobi bin sòoǹ tibɔmɔntiilee dūu ŋá dikitikpaandi.
13Bibɔtiibi nì bi-janjakitiŋi sáǹ sáǹ,
ní binimpoobi bin kíǹ mmɔŋkee yākatì tin bi sáǹ ki fée.
14Ni dáá gbíntìi dɔ̄ kunaabakaunaaa?
Animbil kúti náká náká dibeenanjil feeŋyi pu,
ní sindaariyasoon náká náká di-kuti pu.
15Ŋyunti ŋun Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan nìn bíi jì ki yàantí bibɔtiibee,
ntaayim nìn bíi lítí Saalmɔn jool pu.
16 Baasan jool sá Unimbɔti jool ní,
Baasan jool sá dijool din cáá yilpu kúnti kunti wīikée.
17Kin ba pu ní sii, dijool din cáá yilpu kúnti kunti wīikée
ŋáań dijool din Unimbɔti lēē kí nīn kóò di-puee ipoompoon?
Tiŋman, Unimbɔti làá nīn kóò niin ní talku.
18Unimbɔti cáá janjatɔrɔkub kutukub kutukub cutimaanyi.
Ti-Dindaan bí bi-kansikin,
Siinaayi jool din bí circir laŋkee pu.
19Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti, a jɔ́m̀ yilpu niin kí nīn kóò.
A cúú binib bi kíǹ ki sá bisarkadambi.
Binib cáań-si tiwampɔkaal, ki kpáaǹ bin kaa tɔ́-see.
20Tí jāam̀ ti-Dindaan ŋwiin kamaa!
U sá Unimbɔti ti-fiiliu un tūntí ti-gìŋ́ŋi ki tìì-tee ní.
21Ti-Nimbɔtiu sá Unimbɔti un fìil̄ee ní.
Úǹ ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti di cáá mpɔn
kí fīī-ti kí nyāntí ŋkúmin.
22Ama Unimbɔti làá wìil̀ u-nannanliibi yiliŋ,
nì bin tú tiyikpifɔkɔl ki sá binikpɔliibee yaŋ.
23Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «M làá yòon̄ní-bi Baasan jool pu kí gíiǹní,
m làá nyāntí-bi dimɔɔl taapu kí gíiǹní,
24án nín làá ŋá pu á còom̀ fatiku poon,
ní a-booi ń ŋmɔ́ a-nannanliibi nantee.»
25Unimbɔti, ti ká binib nín còom̄ ki pàkà-si puee.
M-Nimbɔtiu, m-bɔtiu bi còom̄ ki kóò a-kɔŋkooŋŋun.
26Bilaŋgaaliibi līī, ní biwambɔɔliibi lúŋkì,
ní bisapɔmbi bí kansikin ki cákafí cancakantib.
27Ní jāam̀maan Unimbɔti ni-kooŋyi poon,
nimbi bin nyeeŋu sá Isirayeelee,
ní jāam̀ ti-Dindaan.
28Upeepeekaa di sá Beenjameen, ujipɔnjoolkaa naakooku,
ní Juuda bɔtibiliŋ ŋin pēē abɔkuti ŋin bi gbáńee ń páań,
ní Sabulɔn nì Neefitalii bɔtibiliŋ ń lūŋkì.
29Unimbɔti, dàkà a-pɔŋŋu,
Unimbɔti, dàkà a-baatandi, sii un di túń atuŋkpaan ki tīī-tee.
30A-diiku kun bí Jeerusaleemee puee,
bibɔtiibi làá dāá cáań-si bi-wampɔkaati.
31Kpàtī tikatin waŋkuluku pu,
inajaa nacaŋkpuŋku pu,
kí kpáaǹ anibul ŋin bí kii anabil nee pu.
Bi gbàantí ki tìì-si animbil kúti.
Gbá kí yàaǹ anibul ŋin néeń kujaau nee.
32Bikàliŋkpaambi nyánní Eejipiti ki dɔ́miń,
Eetiiyoopii yab tāntì bi-ŋalii ki túĺ Unimbɔti watil pú.
33Kitiŋ pu beeŋi, gāāmaan ilan kí nyɔ̄ŋkì Unimbɔti,
nyɔ̄ŋkìmaan ti-Dindaan
34un jàkāń doooo cannaaku tagbɔŋku yilpuee.
Pīlifìmaan, u tátiń mpɔmpɔn.
35Sòom̀maan Unimbɔti pɔŋŋu pu.
U jīǹ Isirayeel pu dibeel,
ní u-pɔŋŋu bí atagbanni.
36Unimbɔti, a cáá tifaandi a-circir kɔŋkooŋŋun.
An sá Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu
di tìì u-nibul dikpabil nì mpɔn.
Tí nyɔ̄ŋkì Unimbɔti!

english_text:
(By David for the music leader. To the tune “Lilies.”)
God Can Be Trusted
1Save me, God!
I am about to drown.
2I am sinking deep in the mud,
and my feet are slipping.
I am about to be swept under
by a mighty flood.
3I am worn out from crying,
and my throat is dry.
I have waited for you
till my eyes are blurred.
4 There are more people
who hate me for no reason
than there are hairs
on my head.
Many terrible enemies
want to destroy me, God.
Am I supposed to give back
something I didn't steal?
5You know my foolish sins.
Not one is hidden from you.
6 Lord God All-Powerful,
ruler of Israel,
don't let me embarrass anyone
who trusts and worships you.
7It is for your sake alone
that I am insulted
and blush with shame.
8I am like a stranger
to my relatives
and like a foreigner
to my own family.
9 My love for your house
burns in me like a fire,
and when others insult you,
they insulted me as well.
10I cried and went without food,
but they still insulted me.
11They sneered at me
for wearing sackcloth
to show my sorrow.
12Rulers and judges gossip
about me,
and drunkards make up songs
to mock me.
13But I pray to you, Lord.
So when the time is right,
answer me and help me
with your wonderful love.
14Don't let me sink in the mud,
but save me from my enemies
and from the deep water.
15Don't let me be
swept away by a flood
or drowned in the ocean
or swallowed by death.
16Answer me, Lord!
You are kind and good.
Pay attention to me!
You are truly merciful.
17Don't turn away from me.
I am your servant,
and I am in trouble.
Please hurry and help!
18Come and save me
from my enemies.
19You know how I am insulted,
mocked, and disgraced;
you know every one
of my enemies.
20I am crushed by insults,
and I feel sick.
I had hoped for mercy and pity,
but there was none.
21 Enemies poisoned my food,
and when I was thirsty,
they gave me vinegar.
22 Make their table a trap
for them and their friends.
23Blind them with darkness
and make them tremble.
24Show them how angry you are!
Be furious and catch them.
25 Destroy their camp
and don't let anyone live
in their tents.
26They cause trouble for people
you have already punished;
their gossip hurts those
you have wounded.
27Make them guiltier than ever
and don't forgive them.
28 Wipe their names from the book
of the living;
remove them from the list
of the innocent.
29I am mistreated and in pain.
Protect me, God,
and keep me safe!
30I will praise the Lord God
with a song
and a thankful heart.
31This will please the Lord
better than offering an ox
or a full-grown bull.
32When those in need see this,
they will be happy,
and the Lord's worshipers
will be encouraged.
33The Lord will listen
when the homeless cry out,
and he will never forget
his people in prison.
34Heaven and earth
will praise our God,
and so will the oceans
and everything in them.
35God will rescue Jerusalem,
and he will rebuild
the towns of Judah.
His people will live there
on their own land,
36and when the time comes,
their children will inherit
the land.
Then everyone who loves God
will also settle there.
translation_text:
Unimbɔti, m néeń a-diiku
1Daafiidi di ŋmàn̄ nlan nee ki tīī bilaŋgaaliibi kpiliu. Bi bɔ̀ɔ́ tibati ní ki gà-ŋu.
2Unimbɔti, fīī-mi,
nnyim jɔ́m̀ ki sāā m-neen.
3M nín sìntī tikpatin taapu taapu,
ní m-taaŋi kaa gbèetī kitiŋ.
M bí nnyim min nyóòyee poon,
ní nnyinjil bíi yòontí-mi.
4M gbáń ibiil ki tin gīī,
m-neen séeb́.
M nín kā ki kpèé a-saŋŋu pú puee
yāntì m-nimbiliŋ gīī.
5Bin pée ná-mi fámee
wīikí ki jítiǹ m-yil pu yikpiti.
M-nannanliibi tūntí-mi abɔgabil,
ní bi lafun cáá mpɔn kí nàan̄-mi.
Tin maa yùn̄ee ní bí bí yii ḿ nyàab̀ kí téeǹ.
6Unimbɔti, a nyí m-gbaandi pu,
ní m-yìntitam kaa lìkī a-cee.
7Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan,
taa yàntī man puee, icoo ń cúú bin máká a-puee.
Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu, taa yàntī man puee,
bí sìì bin nyàab̀-see.
8Di sá yii sii pu ní bi sìí-mi,
ní m-yil tīī kaa yáatí.
9M kpántì m-nabiyaamu cee unicaan,
ní man nì bin pēē dinabiilee kaa ti nyí-mi.
10Dineendi din m cáá a-diiku puee
fòol̄ m-pɔbilin lìblib kii ŋŋmee.
Asiibil ŋin bi sìí-see fàtīi gítiń man pu ní.
11M súń ki bóob́ kinyɔkɔ,
ama ní binib sìí-mi.
12M dū kutuku ki pēeǹ kí dàkà m-nimbaaku,
ní m-bɔti kpántì nlan bi gà.
13Kpacantib puɔɔɔ, man bɔti ní bi sòoǹ,
áli gba bidanyɔgbiliibi gà-mi ilan.
14Ama mamee, sii ti-Dindaan ní m bíi mèé,
ŋyunti nee ní a máaǹ kí pīlifiǹ-mi.
Unimbɔti, a-ŋanti wīikí tikpil,
kíí-mi, di sá yii sii di sá difiil tiŋman pu.
15Nyāntí-mi tikpati nee poon ḿ taa múĺ.
Nyāntí-mi bin ná-mee ŋaan,
nì mbúun nee poon.
16Taa yàntī nnyinjil nee ń yòon̄-maaa,
mbúun nee ń dū-mi kí náĺaaa,
dikaakul nee mun ń dūú bìin̄ m-pu.
17Ti-Dindaan kíí-mi, di sá yii a-neeŋkpaandi ŋān̄.
A-poommɔŋŋu puee, fàtī a-ba kí túĺ-mi.
18Taa fàtī a-boon kí tīī man a-tɔntɔnliu.
M bí dinimbinaamandin, kíí-mi malaa.
19Sútí kí pìl̄-mi kí fīī-mi.
M-nannanliibi puee, fīī-mi.
20A nyí bi nín sìí-mee,
a nyí m-cooi nì bi nín sòoǹ ki bíiĺ-mi puee,
a nyí m-nannanliibi kɔkɔ.
21Asiibil bíil̀ m-pɔbil
ní m dūu kpántì ubunli.
M bàà cí ubɔ ń sɔ̄ m-saai, ama báà ubɔ kaa dɔ́miń.
M bàà nyàab̀ ubɔ ń ŋméeǹ-mi kaa ká.
22Bi dū ndabiim ki ŋá m-jinti poon,
ní nnyinnyoo yaa cáá-mee, bi tìì-mi ndaam min gàm̀ee.
23Bi-jiŋaalib jinti ń kpántí-bi kutaliŋŋu,
ní kí kpántí bin bi yíińee kpaalaa!
24Bi-nimbiliŋ ń jɔ̀b̄ kí taa ti nín̄ wāĺ.
Bí nīn pée bōō baabadal.
25Kpáatí a-bum kí sìtī bi-pu,
kí yàntī a-ŋuul ń jà kí cúú-bi.
26Bi-kɔŋkooŋyi ń kpántí adigbun
ubɔ ń taa ti kɔ́ bi-diiŋŋin,
27kun puee bi sāaǹ un tafal a dáaĺee,
ní ki sòoǹ bin a tīī tiweendee falaau pu.
28Gíiǹ bi-kpitii kɔkɔ kí túń-bi,
taa pée dūú pɔ̄-bi.
29Pítí bi-yiŋŋi binifoobi gbɔŋkun,
taa kàaǹ-bi kí kūtì deedeedambi pu.
30Ama mamee m sá unandaan ki bíi jīǹ falaa,
a-jòońdi làá wúń m-pu, Unimbɔti.
31M làá gāā nlan kí nyɔ̄ŋkì-si,
ní kí jāam̀-si kí lì yii a sá ukpaan.
32Tíǹ fáatiǹ sii, ti-Dindaan ki jítiǹ unaa,
ki jítiǹ unaja nì iyin nì titafuŋfukul.
33Bin sīntiǹ bi-ba taapuee làá ká míǹ ní kí nīn fàal̀.
«Nimbi bin nyàab̀ Unimbɔtee,
nimbi di yì mmaŋfafɔkɔn!
34Di sá yii ti-Dindaan pílifíǹ bifalaadambi,
waa féeń u-yab, ŋyunti ŋun bi yaa bí sarkanee.
35Kutagbɔŋu nì kitiŋ, nyɔ̄ŋkìmaan-u,
ki kpáaǹ tiŋkub nì tin kɔkɔ bí bi-poonee.
36Di sá Unimbɔti làá fīī Siiyɔn jool,
ní kí fàtīí mā Juuda timmu.
U-nib làá dāá fōō-mu kí nīn kíǹ ki kóò.
37U-tɔntɔnliibi biyaamu làá dāá fōō-mu difakal,
ní bin kɔkɔ néeń ti-Dindaanee ń dāá nīn kóò niin.»

english_text:
(By David for the music leader. To be used when an offering is made.)
God Is Wonderful
1Save me, Lord God!
Hurry and help.
2Disappoint and confuse
all who want to kill me.
Turn away and disgrace
all who want to hurt me.
3Embarrass and shame those
who say, “We told you so!”
4Let your worshipers celebrate
and be glad because of you.
They love your saving power,
so let them always say,
“God is wonderful!”
5I am poor and needy,
but you, the Lord God,
care about me.
You are the one who saves me.
Please hurry and help!
translation_text:
Dāá jòoń-mi malaa, ti-Dindaan
(Kpèè Ilan 40.14-18)
1Daafiidi di ŋmàn̄ nlan nee ki tīī bilaŋgaaliibi kpiliu kí téetí Unimbɔti pu.
2Unimbɔti, fīī-mi,
dāá jòoń-mi malaa!
3Bin nyàab̀ kí lēē m-maŋfalee, kɔ́ǹ-bi icoo!
Bin nyàab̀-mi tikpitilee,
bí gítí bi-boon kí fá bi-nyooti!
4Bin bin bèel̄-mi ki lāāyee,
yàntī bí gítí bi-boon nì icoo!
5Ama yàntī bin kɔkɔ nyàab̀-see
ń nīn bí mmɔnni ki fàal̀.
Yàntī bin néeń sii ufiilee ń nīn pée lì yii:
«Unimbɔti sá ukpaaneeee!»
6Mamee, m sá ufalaadaan nì unandaan ní.
Dāan̄ m-cee malaa, Unimbɔti!
Sii di sá m-jòońliu nì m-fiiliu.
M-Dindaan, taa tàan̄!

english_text:
A Prayer for God's Protection
1I run to you, Lord,
for protection.
Don't disappoint me.
2You do what is right,
so come to my rescue.
Listen to my prayer
and keep me safe.
3Be my mighty rock, the place
where I can always run
for protection.
Save me by your command!
You are my mighty rock
and my fortress.
4Come and save me, Lord God,
from vicious and cruel
and brutal enemies!
5I depend on you,
and I have trusted you
since I was young.
6I have relied on you
from the day I was born.
You brought me safely
through birth,
and I always praise you.
7Many people think of me
as something evil.
But you are my mighty protector,
8and I praise and honor you
all day long.
9Don't throw me aside
when I am old;
don't desert me
when my strength is gone.
10My enemies are plotting
because they want me dead.
11They say, “Now we'll catch you!
God has deserted you,
and no one can save you.”
12Come closer, God!
Please hurry and help.
13Embarrass and destroy
all who want me dead;
disgrace and confuse
all who want to hurt me.
14I will never give up hope
or stop praising you.
15All day long I will tell
the wonderful things you do
to save your people.
But you have done much more
than I could possibly know.
16I will praise you, Lord God,
for your mighty deeds
and your power to save.
17You have taught me
since I was a child,
and I never stop telling about
your marvelous deeds.
18Don't leave me when I am old
and my hair turns gray.
Let me tell future generations
about your mighty power.
19Your deeds of kindness
are known in the heavens.
No one is like you!
20You made me suffer a lot,
but you will bring me
back from this deep pit
and give me new life.
21You will make me truly great
and take my sorrow away.
22I will praise you, God,
the Holy One of Israel.
You are faithful.
I will play the harp
and sing your praises.
23You have rescued me!
I will celebrate and shout,
singing praises to you
with all my heart.
24All day long I will announce
your power to save.
I will tell how you disgraced
and disappointed those
who wanted to hurt me.
translation_text:
Ti-Dindaan, taa fá-mi
1Ti-Dindaan, sii ní m sáǹ ki kɔ́,
taa yàntī icoo ń cúú-mi dalba dalba.
2Fīī-mi kí wúń m-pu a-deedeeu poon.
Kpòon̄ a-tafal m-watil pú, ní kí fīī-mi.
3Nín̄ sá kutaŋkpanaakoou
kun m làá nīn sáń ki kóò ŋyunti kamaayee.
A lēē yii a làá fīī-mi.
Tiŋman, a sá m-taŋkpanaakooku nì m-balilaŋki!
4M-Nimbɔtiu, fīī-mi binikpitib ŋaan,
nyāntí-mi binikpɔliibi nì bin dàkà tipɔmbɔtee ŋaan.
5Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti, sii pu ní m máká,
doooo m-naacimpɔntin ní m máká a-pu.
6Daliŋkin bi màl̄-mee, sii pu ní m báká,
sii di nyántìń-mi m-na poon.
Sii ní m làá nīn pée nyɔ́ŋkí.
7M nìn sá ŋabika ki tīī binib tikpil,
ama sii ní m sáǹ ki kɔ́.
8A-nyɔŋkii di pée gbí m-nyɔkɔn,
ní m sòoǹ a-nyooti pu iwiin kɔkɔ.
9M-puti poon nee, taa fá-mi,
m-pɔŋŋu nín bātì nee, taa fàtī a-boon kí tīī-mi.
10M-nannanliibi sòoǹ m-pu,
bin cɔ́ŋkí-mee kpáfì kinyɔkɔ m-pu.
11Bi lì yii: «Unimbɔti dū-u ki fá,
jàmaan kí cúú-u,
ubɔ kpá ki làá fīī-u!»
12Unimbɔti, taa nín̄ dátiǹ-mi,
m-Nimbɔtiu, dāá jòoń-mi malaa.
13Bin kɔ́kɔĺ-mee,
yàntī icoo ń cúú-bi án nàan̄-bi!
Bin nyàab̀-mi tikpitilee,
yàntī icoo ń cúú-bi bí fá bi-nyooti!
14Mamee, m làá nīn pée máká a-pu ní,
m làá nīn pée gà ilan ní ki nyɔ́ŋkí-si.
15M-nyɔkɔ làá nīn sòoǹ
a-deedeeu nì a-fiil pu baabadal,
di sá yii maa ŋūǹ kí kàaǹ a-ŋanti gbanti.
16Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti, m làá sòoǹ a-tuŋkpaaŋŋi pu,
m làá téetí yii sii baba di sá deedeedaan.
17Unimbɔti, doooo m-naacimpɔntin ní a dàkā-mi,
ní m sòon̄ a-maamaaci tuuŋŋi pu ki dāa sāā díǹ.
18Kɔŋkɔnnee m nín púĺ m-yikpiti píil̀ nee,
Unimbɔti, taa fá-mi.
Niinee m làá ŋmā kí sòoǹ
a-tuŋkpaaŋŋi pu kí tùkù binipɔmbi,
