when the Lord corrects you.
12 The Lord corrects
everyone he loves,
just as parents correct
a child they dearly love.
The Value of Wisdom
13God blesses everyone
who has wisdom
and common sense.
14Wisdom is worth more
than silver;
it makes you much richer
than gold.
15Wisdom is more valuable
than precious jewels;
nothing you want
compares with her.
16In her right hand
Wisdom holds a long life,
and in her left hand
are wealth and honor.
17Wisdom makes life pleasant
and leads us safely along.
18Wisdom is a life-giving tree,
the source of happiness
for all who hold on to her.
19By his wisdom and knowledge
the Lord created
heaven and earth.
20By his understanding
he let the ocean break loose
and clouds release the rain.
21My child, use common sense
and sound judgment!
Always keep them in mind.
22They will help you to live
a long and beautiful life.
23You will walk safely
and never stumble;
24you will rest without a worry
and sleep soundly.
25So don't be afraid
of sudden disasters
or storms that strike
those who are evil.
26You can be sure that the Lord
will protect you from harm.
27 Do all you can for everyone
who deserves your help.
28Don't tell your neighbor
to come back tomorrow,
if you can help today.
29Don't try to be mean
to neighbors who trust you.
30Don't argue just to be arguing,
when you haven't been hurt.
31Don't be jealous
of cruel people
or follow their example.
32The Lord doesn't like
anyone who is dishonest,
but he lets good people
be his friends.
33He places a curse on the home
of everyone who is evil,
but he blesses the home
of every good person.
34 The Lord sneers at those
who sneer at him,
but he is kind to everyone
who is humble.
35You will be praised
if you are wise,
but you will be disgraced
if you are a stubborn fool.
translation_text:
Kí nīn cáá iciin ki tɔ́ Unimbɔti
1M-biki, taa súntí tin m dàkā-see, kpāafì m-marab a-pɔbilin. 2M-saŋkii puee, a làá ká mmaŋfafɔkɔn ní kí jī nnaam a-maŋfal wiiŋyi poon. 3Nín̄ pée ŋáań tiŋan, kí nīn nóó ibaamɔn saŋŋu. Dū tiwan gbanti kí léeń a-neen, dū-tì kí ŋmà a-pɔbilin. 4Niinee Unimbɔti nì binib làá nīn néeń-si, ní kí nīn pàkà-si. 5Nín̄ máká ti-Dindaan pu nì a-pɔbil kɔkɔ, kí taa nín̄ máká a-nyil pu. 6Dū tin kɔkɔ a làá ŋée kí ŋá u-ŋaan, ní ú kpòotī-si a-sàmbiyaamu kɔkɔ poon. 7Taa dàkafì yii a sá uciŋfiti, ama á nīn fàŋkí ti-Dindaan ní kí fàtī a-boon kí tīī ikpiti. 8Án làá cáaǹ a-gbaŋweeŋyi ní kí tīī-si mpɔn. 9Dū a-gaajawanti nì a-kpaajinti ticɔfikaal kí tīī ti-Dindaan tinyool. 10Niinee tikpaajin làá gbí a-cakalaabi ní ndaam ń gbí a-lɔnti kí pùtifì. 11M-biki, ti-Dindaan yaa bíi dátí a-tafalee, á taa dūú kpèè fám, u yaa bíi wòoǹ-see, an taa wà-si. 12Di sá yii ti-Dindaan wòoǹ un u néeńee kii ubaati nín wòoǹ u-jipɔɔn un u lèe puee ní. 13Unil un ká iciinee, unil un cáá dinyilee bí mmɔnneeee! 14Di sá yii á nīn cáá iciinee jítiǹ á nīn cáá animbil. Ipaati in i tììyee jítiǹ sindaariya pu. 15Iciin pɔ̄ɔ̄ kudaau ki jítiǹ abeedimbil, tin unil bìǹ ki nyàab̀ee tiba kaa bàn̄ iciin. 16I tìì unil mmaŋfafɔkɔn, ki tìì tigaajati nì tinyool. 17I-saŋyi mɔ̄, ní i-sàmbiyaamu poon cáá ŋgbansɔŋfi. 18Iciin sá kii busubu bun tìì dimaŋfalee ní ki tīī unil un ŋúb́-iee, un cáá-iee bí mmɔnneeee. 19Ti-Dindaan dū iciin ní ki náań kitiŋ, ní ki dū dinyil ki náań yilpu. 20Nì u-nyil pu ní nnyim min bí kitiŋ taapuee tɔ́nní ki yāaǹ, ní atagban yàntī utaa nì.
Ti-Dindaan wúǹ uciŋfiti pu
21M-biki, dū a-ba kí nákáǹ dinyil nì nlandɔkɔmɔnti, taa pée fàtī a-boon kí tīī tiwan tili gbanti jaanjaan. 22Tì làá yàntī á ká dimaŋfamɔntiil nì tiŋan. 23A làá còom̀ a-saŋŋu poon nì ŋgbansɔŋfi, ní a-taal kaa làá gbéetí tiba. 24A yaa làá dòon̄ee, aa làá fàŋkì tiba, a làá gèeǹ ŋgeemmɔntiim a-dooŋu pu. 25Aa làá fàŋkì atulim abaaa, binikpitib kaa làá dāan̄ kí táká-si. 26Di sá yii ti-Dindaan di làá nīn wúń a-pu tiba ń taa ŋá-si, ní kí nīn bīī a-boon kutaliŋŋu kubɔ ń taa sàl̄-si.
Á nīn néeń a-juti
27A yaa cáá ŋŋmamee, á taa yíí yii saa làá tūtuǹ unil un nyàab̀ ditutundee. 28A yaa ŋūǹ kí tīī a-juti kun u mēē-see, á taa tùkù-u yii: «Nín̄ cá kí fu gítiń fool ḿ fu tīī-si.» 29Sii nì a-bɔɔ yaa kóò ní u máká a-puee, á taa nyàab̀ nsàmbiyaamu kí ŋá-u tikpitil. 30Á taa táká unil tibɔti fám ní já, udaan kaa ŋá-si tiba. 31Taa nín̄ cáá bin ŋáań tipɔmbɔtee pu nnimbitaataam, kí taa nóó bi-tabɔbiliŋ. 32Di sá yii ti-Dindaan ná ikpitidambi, ama ní ki néeń bin bí deedeeyee. 33Ti-Dindaan tòó binikpitib dumpui mbusu, ama ní ki bìintí deedeedambi kɔŋkooŋyi pu. 34U bèel̄ bin bèel̄-uee, ama ní ki ŋáań bin sìntīǹ bi-ba taapuee tiŋan. 35Kun dɔ̄ ki cí biciŋfitiibee di sá tinyool, ama bigbaambee, icoo di dɔ̄ ki cí-bi.

english_text:
Advice to Young People
1My child, listen closely
to my teachings
and learn common sense.
2My advice is useful,
so don't turn away.
3When I was still very young
and my mother's favorite child,
my father 4said to me:
“If you follow my teachings
and keep them in mind,
you will live.
5Be wise and learn good sense;
remember my teachings
and do what I say.
6“If you love Wisdom
and don't reject her,
she will watch over you.
7The best thing about Wisdom
is Wisdom herself;
good sense is more important
than anything else.
8If you value Wisdom
and hold tightly to her,
great honors will be yours.
9It will be like wearing
a glorious crown
of beautiful flowers.”
The Right Way and the Wrong Way
10My child, if you listen
and obey my teachings,
you will live a long time.
11I have shown you the way
that makes sense;
I have guided you
along the right path.
12Your road won't be blocked,
and you won't stumble
when you run.
13Hold firmly to my teaching
and never let go.
It will mean life for you.
14Don't follow the bad example
of cruel and evil people.
15Turn aside and keep going.
Stay away from them.
16They can't sleep or rest
until they do wrong or harm
some innocent victim.
17Their food and drink
are cruelty and wickedness.
18The lifestyle of good people
is like sunlight at dawn
that keeps getting brighter
until broad daylight.
19The lifestyle of the wicked
is like total darkness,
and they will never know
what makes them stumble.
20My child, listen carefully
to everything I say.
21Don't forget a single word,
but think about it all.
22Knowing these teachings
will mean true life
and good health for you.
23Carefully guard your thoughts
because they are the source
of true life.
24Never tell lies or be deceitful
in what you say.
25Keep looking straight ahead,
without turning aside.
26 Know where you are headed,
and you will stay
on solid ground.
27Don't make a mistake by turning
to the right or the left.
translation_text:
A yaa ká iciinee, á nīn ŋúb́-i
1M-biyaamu, pīlifìmaan ubaati dàkatam. Ní pīlifì tiŋan ní kí kpántí binyiliibi. 2Di sá yii dinyil din sá dimɔntiilee ní m bíi tìì-ni, ní taa dū tin m bíi dàkà-ni nee kí fá. 3Ma mun nìn sá m-baa jipɔmmɔntiu ní, ní m-na nìn néeń-mi tikpil kii dijipɔmbaabilee. 4M-baa nìn dàkà-mi ki lì yii: «Cúú m-nyɔɔbuŋŋi kí ŋá a-pɔbilin, kí nīn nóó m-bɔkpaaŋi tiŋan, mimmee a làá kàl̄ kitiŋ pu kí yúntí. 5Ká iciin nì dinyil, kí taa súntí m-nyɔɔbuŋŋi puɔɔɔ, kí taa fàtī a-boon kí tīī-ŋi mun. 6Taa dū iciin kí fá, i làá nīn cí-si, nín̄ néeń-i, i làá nīn wúń a-pu. 7Iciin kílilaŋki di sá á pɔ́ɔǹ kí bīfì kí béé-i, dū tin kɔkɔ a cááyee kí sú kí ŋmā kí ká dinyil. 8Dū iciin kí nákáǹ a-ba kpátí kpati, i làá yòon̄ a-yindi yilpu. Bìb̄ iciin, i làá tīī-si tinyool. 9I làá nīn sá kii ŋŋaamɔntee ki yíĺ a-yil, ní kí nīn sá kii kibeefuulii kimɔmmɔntiiyee ki cíkí a-yil pu.»
Taa nín̄ cáá binikpitib bimbim
10M-biki, pīlifiǹ-mi, fōō m-nyɔɔbuŋŋi ní kí kàl̄ kitiŋ pu kí yúntí. 11M bíi dàkà-si iciin saŋŋu, m kpòotī-si á nīn còom̄ deedee sàmbiyaamu pu ní. 12Mimmee a yaa bíi còom̄ee, tiba kaa làá lìkin̄-si, a yaa tí bíi sáńaaa, aa làá gbéetí. 13Nín̄ ŋúb́ tin bi dàkā-see, taa dū-tì kí fá. Nín̄ ŋúb́-tì, kun puee tíǹ di sá a-maŋfal. 14Taa fōō binikpitib bimbim, kí taa nóó bikpitiŋaliibi saŋŋu. 15Yàntī-ŋu, taa nóó-ŋu. Gɔ́ntí-ŋu ní kí cùú dī laaba. 16Di sá yii an nibee yaa kaa ŋá tin kaa ŋān̄ee, baa ŋūǹ kí gèeǹ, bi yaa kaa yāntì ubɔ lítì, ŋgeem kaa cútí-bi. 17Di sá yii bi ŋáań ikpiti ní ki kāntí ki jīǹ, tipɔmbɔti ní bi ŋáań ki kāntí ki nyù. 18Nsan ŋun deedeedambi nóóyee sá kii ntaafaabɔmbɔm walifiŋuee ní, ŋu pée nyàatī ní ki pɔ́ɔkí ki cá áli kutaa ń dāá wúntí kɔkɔ. 19Ama binikpitib bíǹ saŋŋu sá dibɔmbɔndi ní. Baa wāĺ tin dɔ̄ nsanni bi làá cùú gbéetée.
Nín̄ cáá mbimbimɔntiim
20M-biki, pīlifì m-nyɔɔbuŋŋi tiŋan, kpòon̄ a-tafal kí pīlifì m-saŋkii. 21A-nimbiliŋ ń nīn pée cɔ́ i-pu, dū-i kí ŋá a-pɔbil poon poon. 22I sá dimaŋfal ní ki tīī bin ká-iee, ní ki sá ŋgbampɔn ki tīī bi-wunti kɔkɔ. 23Kpèè a-pɔbil tiŋan, di sá yii díǹ di sá a-maŋfal nyeeŋu. 24Cúú a-nyɔkɔ kí taa pée sòoǹ tinyimɔmbɔti, kí taa pée sòoǹ kí bīil̀ a-juti. 25Á nīn pée kpèé a-nimbiin, yàntī a-nimbikpeeŋu ń nīn pée bá nyɔkɔpu. 26Á kpèè nsan ŋun a làá dēe tiŋan, a-sàmbiyaamu ń nīn sá mun tèen̄ee. 27Taa kpèetī kí cù ŋgiil puɔɔɔ, kí taa kpèetī kí cù ŋgan pú. Sāǹ kí wàatī tin kaa ŋān̄ee.

english_text:
Be Faithful to Your Wife
1My son, if you listen closely
to my wisdom and good sense,
2you will have sound judgment,
and you will always know
the right thing to say.
3The words of an immoral woman
may be as sweet as honey
and as smooth as olive oil.
4But all that you really get
from being with her
is bitter poison and pain.
5If you follow her,
she will lead you down
to the world of the dead.
6She has missed the path
that leads to life
and doesn't even know it.
7My son, listen to me
and do everything I say.
8Stay away from a bad woman!
Don't even go near the door
of her house.
9You will lose your self-respect
and end up in debt
to some cruel person
for the rest of your life.
10Strangers will get your money
and everything else
you have worked for.
11When it's all over,
your body will waste away,
as you groan 12and shout,
“I hated advice and correction!
13I paid no attention
to my teachers,
14and now I am disgraced
in front of everyone.”
15You should be faithful
to your wife,
just as you take water
from your own well.
16And don't be like a stream
from which just any woman
may take a drink.
17Save yourself for your wife
and don't have sex
with other women.
18Be happy with the wife
you married
when you were young.
19She is beautiful and graceful,
just like a deer;
you should be attracted to her
and stay deeply in love.
20Don't go crazy over a woman
who is unfaithful
to her own husband!
21The Lord sees everything,
and he watches us closely.
22Sinners are trapped and caught
by their own evil deeds.
23They get lost and die
because of their foolishness
and lack of self-control.
translation_text:
Nín̄ nyí nì a-ba nì unimpu un nyēē u-cal boonee
1M-biki, pīlifì iciin in m dàkà-see tiŋan, kpòon̄ a-tafal kí pīlifì isaŋki in m-nyil tììyee. 2Mimmee a làá kpāafì nlandɔkɔmɔnti ní kí nīn sòoǹ nì dinyil. 3Di sá yii ubɔ nimpuu nyɔkɔ mɔ̄ kii tisiilee ní ki mèeǹ kii ŋkpamee. 4Ama án dāa kúntée u-nyɔkɔ túŋkí ní kátí kati kii kisutuntuŋee, ní ki jītí pámpam kii kitàataajiki kin jītí ajan liitil púee. 5An nimpuuee bimbim cáǹ ŋkúmin ní, ditaŋkpiilin ní u còom̄ ki cá. 6Waa nóó nsan ŋun cáǹ-u dimaŋfalinee, u yīntì nsan ní kaa kpáàa nyí. 7An puee pīlifiǹ-mi, m-biki. Taa dū m-saŋkii kí fá. 8Taa cù an nimpuuee cee, kí taa pée sútí kí pìl̄ u-diiku punyɔkɔpu gba. 9Án yaa kaa sá míǹ, u làá bīil̀ a-jilmau, ní kí yàntī uninja un kaa sūǹ isaayee ń nàan̄-si. 10Ní binicambi ń dāá jī a-gaajawanti, ní a-tundi paati ń dāá kɔ́ binifantantiibi ŋaan. 11Ŋyunti ŋun a tóob́ ŋkúm a-wunti dóò ki pēefèe, ní a kíǹ ki yáliŋkí. 12Niinee ní a dāa lì yii: «An ŋá mana ní maa pílifì tibɔti tin bi kpáafì-mee? An ŋá mana ní maa kíí bí wòoǹ-mi ní? 13Ba pu ní maa pílifì m-dàkaliibi nyɔkɔ, kaa fātìi tɔ́ bin nìn bíi dàkà-mee bɔti? 14An bàà pée kíǹ fiii dee ḿ bàà kɔ́ dinimbinaamandi din kaa cáá jutee poon samaa kɔkɔ kansikin!»
Nín̄ néeń a-taafaanimpuu
15A-nimpuu sá kii a-nyimbɔbil nyim nì min nyēeń a-lɔkɔunee ní. Nín̄ nyù nnyim gbanti! 16Taa yàntī a-nyimbuliŋu ń pùub̀ kí nyā mmɔŋki àá a-bùmbiyaamu ń pùub̀ kí nyā didandi pu. 17A-nimpuu ń nīn sá sii baba wanti, á taa yàntī sii nì binicambi ń kpāfì kí nīn yì-u. 18Yàntī a-nyimbuliŋu, a-taafaanimpuu pɔbil ń nīn sɔ̀m̀, yàntī u-bɔti ń nīn mɔ̄ǹ-si. 19A-nimpuu cáá dineendi kii upeemanee, ki ŋān̄ kii ucaŋkpalimee. U-biiŋi ń nīn pée tìì-si mmɔn. Ŋyunti kamaayee u-neendi ń nīn pée gbéè-si kii ndaamee. 20M-biki, ba pu ní a-nimbil máǹ ubɔ nimpuu pu ní ki ŋúb́ unimpu un aa nyée biiŋi ki ŋmáliŋkí ní? 21Di sá yii ti-Dindaan nyí unil kamaa bimbim, ní ki wāĺ tin kɔkɔ u ŋáańee. 22Ikpiti kɔ̄ntí ukpitiŋal sarka, u-kpitii sàtī-u kii kutaliŋŋuee ní. 23U làá kpú u nín kaa ŋūǹ kí ŋúb́ u-ba puee. U-gbaandi nín wīikí puee di làá yàntī ú wāŋkì.

english_text:
Don't Be Foolish
1 My child, suppose you agree
to pay the debt of someone,
who cannot repay a loan.
2Then you are trapped
by your own words,
3and you are now in the power
of someone else.
Here is what you should do:
Go and beg for permission
to call off the agreement.
4Do this before you fall asleep
or even get sleepy.
5Save yourself, just as a deer
or a bird tries to escape
from a hunter.
6You lazy people can learn
by watching an anthill.
7Ants don't have leaders,
8but they store up food
during harvest season.
9How long will you lie there
doing nothing at all?
When are you going to get up
and stop sleeping?
10 Sleep a little. Doze a little.
Fold your hands
and twiddle your thumbs.
11Suddenly, everything is gone,
as though it had been taken
by an armed robber.
12Worthless liars go around
13 winking and giving signals
to deceive others.
14They are always thinking up
something cruel and evil,
and they stir up trouble.
15But they will be struck
by sudden disaster
and left without a hope.
16There are six or seven
kinds of people
the Lord doesn't like:
17Those who are too proud
or tell lies or murder,
18those who make evil plans
or are quick to do wrong,
19those who tell lies in court
or stir up trouble
in a family.
20Obey the teaching
of your parents—
21always keep it in mind
and never forget it.
22Their teaching will guide you
when you walk,
protect you when you sleep,
and talk to you
when you are awake.
23The Law of the Lord is a lamp,
and its teachings
shine brightly.
Correction and self-control
will lead you through life.
24They will protect you
from the flattering words
of someone else's wife.
25Don't let yourself be attracted
by the charm and lovely eyes
of someone like that.
26A woman who sells her love
can be bought for as little
as the price of a meal.
But making love
to another man's wife
will cost you everything.
27If you carry burning coals,
you burn your clothes;
28if you step on hot coals,
you burn your feet.
29And if you go to bed
with another man's wife,
you pay the price.
30We don't put up with thieves,
not even with one who steals
for something to eat.
31And thieves who get caught
must pay back
seven times what was stolen
and lose everything.
32But if you go to bed
with another man's wife,
you will destroy yourself
by your own stupidity.
33You will be beaten
and forever disgraced,
34because a jealous husband
can be furious and merciless
when he takes revenge.
35He won't let you pay him off,
no matter what you offer.
translation_text:
Á taa yūĺ ubɔ boon ú jī dipɔndi
1M-biki, tí lì yii a fáá ubɔ ŋaan ki pōoǹ kí pà a-juti pɔndi, 2ní tin nyáń a-nyɔkɔnee dūu bóob́-si ki sàl̄-si kii kutaliŋŋuee. 3M-biki, kii a nín kɔ́ a-juti ŋaanee, ŋá tin bí nee kí nyā u-bɔtin. Cù u-cee kí lítí u-nimbiin kí gbàam̀-u. 4A yaa kaa ŋúń ki ŋá míǹ, á taa pée púkuń ní kaa nín gèen̄. 5Fōō a-ba kí líí kii ucaŋkpalim nín ŋmátí ukpan ŋaan puee, àá kii unoon nín ŋmátí kí nyā kutaliŋŋun puee.
Taa nín̄ sá uwutijoodaan
6Uwutijoodaan, cùú kpèè unaanyanti. Cùú kpèè u-bimbim kí kpántí uciŋfiti. 7Unaanyanti kaa cáá un kpèé-u ní u tūǹ ditundee, kaa cáá un ŋmà ditundi din u túń ŋwiinee, kaa cáá ukpil un fōō-u ditundee. 8Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, dipeel puee u kōontí tijin ní kí yóoń, u kpáafí tijikaal ŋyunti ŋun bi cēē tikpaajinee ní. 9Uwutijoodaan, kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu ní a làá nīn pée dɔ̄ ki gèeǹ ní? Ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu ní a làá fìntī ŋgeem pu ní? 10A là kí gèeǹ fiii, a là kí dáb́ fiii, a là kí dòon̄ fiii kí kpàl̄ iŋal. 11A dɔ̄ mimmee ní disool ń cíliń a-pu kii unaayuuyee, ní falaa ń cúú-si kii bin fúkuĺ binibee.
Kun dɔ̄ ki cí unyimɔndaanee
12Unikpiti sá un kaa bí tibanee, u yìiǹ ní ki mɔ́ntí inyimɔn. 13U wàb̀ u-nimbil ki cáá u-taaŋi nì u-ŋambiyaamu ki dàkà tidaandi kí ŋmā kí mɔ̄ntì u-nyimɔŋyi. 14Ikpiti diŋál di kā u-pɔbilin. U pée dàkafī tin kaa ŋān̄ee ŋma pu ní, ki jāantí binib. 15An pu ní nnaabu làá jēetí u-pu dicilpu dicilpu. Dibɔbilin niin ní án làá nàan̄-u nnyɔkɔ kpá!
Tin ti-Dindaan kaa lèe
16Tiwan tiluu ní ti-Dindaan pée ná, ní kululuútiiu ní u-nimbil kaa là kí ká: 17Unil un dàkà u-bee,
unil un mɔ́ntí inyimɔnee,
unil un kù maanyiibabee,
18unil un bɔ́ntí kí ŋá atuŋkpitee,
unil un yáb̀ kí ŋá tin kaa ŋān̄ee,
19Unil un lèekī nnyimɔn seerauee.
Kuwanluluútiiu di sá unil un jāantí nnabiyaamuee.
Á nīn nyíǹ a-ba nì tilaakpaal
20M-biki, nín̄ ŋúb́ tin a-baa kpáafì-see, taa fàtī a-boon kí tīī tin a-na dàkā-see. 21Tí nīn pée kā a-pɔbilin, yàntī tí nīn sá tiléeŋkaal á dūú léeń a-neen. 22Tì làá nīn kpòotī-si a-saŋkindi poon, ki làá nīn cí-si a-geem poon ní a yaa fīntèe í sāŋkì-si. 23Di sá yii tibɔkpaafikaal sá kii fitilee ní, ní didàkal sá kii ŋwalifee, ní iwoon sá kii dimaŋfal saŋŋuee. 24An wantee làá wúń a-pu kí nyāntí-si unimpu un saŋkindi kaa ŋān̄ee, nì ubɔ nimpuu nyɔɔmálmaluu ŋaan. 25Taa nín̄ là an nimpuuee u-nyaaŋku pu, taa yàntī u-nimbikpeeŋu ń dáaĺ-si kí kɔ́ǹ u-taliŋkun. 26Di sá yii a yaa mɔ̄nnì kinimpulaakpaayee, kalaa nimbiliŋ ní a làá dūú pà, ama a yaa mɔ̄nnì ubɔ nimpuuee, a-maŋfal kɔkɔ ní a dūú pà. 27Ŋma dù ŋŋmi kí ŋá u-bɔkutilookun an kaa fōō? 28Ŋma còom̄ amɔsiŋkoon pu u-taal kaa wùn̄? 29Míǹ ní an sá ki tīī un di yaa mɔ̄nnì u-juti nimpuuee. Un di yaa gbēē-uee, see ú fōō ditafadaaldi. 30Baa wòoǹ unaayuu un yùn̄ kí jī kí kpɔ̀ ŋkùm u-poonee. 31Ama ní bi yaa cúú-uee, see ú téeǹ tin u yùn̄ee miluli pu, see ú kóoǹ tin kɔkɔ u cáá u-dumpuee kí dūú pà dipɔndi. 32Uninja un di yaa ŋá tilaakpaal nì ubɔ nimpuuee kaa cáá diyil. Un di ŋáań mimmee bíiĺ u-ba ní. 33U làá fōō tiweendi, bí kpèè-u fám ní u-cooi kpá kí kúntí jaanjaan. 34Di sá yii ipoompoon làá yàntī unimpuee cal ń fōō mbum ní ŋwiin ŋun u làá dāá tɔ̀ ipɔntoonee, disaasɔl dāa kpá. 35Tiba kaa bí bí tīī-u án sɔ̀ŋkì u-pɔbil. Báà a yaa tīī-u tiwampɔkaal tikpil, waa làá fōō.

english_text:
The Foolishness of Unfaithfulness
1My son, pay close attention
and don't forget
what I tell you to do.
2Obey me, and you will live!
Let my instructions be
your greatest treasure.
3Keep them at your fingertips
and write them
in your mind.
4Let wisdom be your sister
and make common sense
your closest friend.
5They will protect you
from the flattering words
of someone else's wife.
6From the window of my house,
I once happened to see
7some foolish young men.
8It was late in the evening,
sometime after dark.
9One of these young men
turned the corner
and was walking by the house
of an unfaithful wife.
10She was dressed fancy
like a woman of the street
with only one thing in mind.
11She was one of those women
who are loud and restless
and never stay at home,
12who walk street after street,
waiting to trap a man.
13She grabbed him and kissed him,
and with no sense of shame,
she said:
14“I had to offer a sacrifice,
and there is enough meat
left over for a feast.
15So I came looking for you,
and here you are!
16The sheets on my bed
are bright-colored cloth
from Egypt.
17And I have covered it
with perfume made of myrrh,
aloes, and cinnamon.
18“Let's go there
and make love all night.
19My husband is traveling,
and he's far away.
20He took a lot of money along,
and he won't be back home
before the middle
of the month.”
21And so, she tricked him
with all of her sweet talk
and her flattery.
22At once he followed her
like an ox on the way
to be slaughtered,
or like a fool on the way
to be punished
23and killed with arrows.
He was no more than a bird
rushing into a trap,
without knowing
it would cost him his life.
24My son, pay close attention
to what I have said.
25Don't even think about
that kind of woman
or let yourself be misled
by someone like her.
26Such a woman has caused
the downfall and destruction
of a lot of men.
27Her house is a one-way street
leading straight down
to the world of the dead.
translation_text:
Kinimpulaakpaai kíil̀ unaacimpɔɔn
1M-biki, taa súntí m-nyɔɔbuŋŋi pu, kpāafì m-marab tiŋan. 2A yaa là kí nīn bí dimaŋfalinee, á nīn ŋúb́ m-marab nì tin m dàkā-see kii a nín ŋúb́ a-nimbibul puee. 3Taa yàntī an wantee ń ŋmátí a-ŋaan, dū-tì kí ŋá a-pɔbilin. 4Yàntī iciin ń nīn sá a-niisal, kí yàntī dinyil ń nīn sá a-bɔɔmɔnti. 5Tì làá fīī-si ubɔ nimpuu ŋaan, uninjamɔnnil un cáá nyɔɔmálmalee ŋaan.
6Dalba m nìn yú m-tɔkɔlau caŋin ní ki kpèé mmɔŋki. 7M nìn ká binaacimpɔmbi bin kaa nyí tibee, ní bi-kansikinee m dáań ki ká ubɔ, úǹ kaa pée cáá nlandɔkɔ báà fiii. 8U nìn bíi còom̄ didandi pu laakin uninjamɔnnil ubɔ kóòyee, ní u pāatì unimpuee dumpu saŋŋu. 9An nìn sá kujoou ní, ŋyunti ŋun ní kunyeeu bíi móotí an bíi bɔ̀ntēe. 10Niinee ní unimpuee nyánní ki túŋkì-u nsan, ki pēē kii kinimpulaakpaayee ki cáá biibii pɔbil. 11U gbí kufuu kaa cáá icoo, ní u-mul kaa cōontí u-dumpu. 12An yaa sá adan pueeee, an yaa sá laakin binib kpáfí ki wīikéeyeeee, u pée nyàab̀ un làá mɔ̀nnì-uee ní. 13U tú unaacimpɔɔnee nsanee ní ki kpàl̄-u ní ki sòon̄ nì dilambil yii: 14«M nìn pōoǹ Unimbɔti yii m làá ŋá ijaam saraau kí tīī-u, ní m ŋá saraa gbanti díǹ nee. 15An pu ní m bàà nyáń kí nyàab̀-si ní ki dūu ká-si nee. 16M dū satakpaambi nì Eejipiti tiŋkin satamɔntiibi ki páaǹ m-dooŋu pu. 17M yāaǹ-ŋu nì miiri nì disaaweendi nì siinamoom talaalub. 18Dāan̄ tí cùú dòon̄ kí jī mmɔn áli kutaa nì ku-wuntil. 19Di sá yii m-cal kaa bí mmɔŋki, u búntì nsandandati ŋubɔ. 20U gbéeǹ u-nimbifɔŋki animbil ní ki yōoǹ ki nín cá, waa làá fàtīí gítiń malaa.» 21U kíil̀ unaacimpɔɔnee míǹ ní úǹ dāa kíí, u yōoǹ nyɔɔmálmal ní ki ŋúń-u. 22Ní u kùl̄ ki páaǹ u-boon dicilpu niin kii unaa ní bi dàtī ki cáǹ kí kpɔ̀ee, a lì kii uwaati ní bi bóob́ ki cáǹ kí tɔ̄ ditafadaaldinee, 23áli mpiin ń dāá sāā kí kɔ́ u-pɔɔl. Kii kinɔmbiki nín ŋàaǹ malaa malaa pu kí cáá ki-ba kí tɔ̄ kulaaŋŋun puee, waa nyí yii u-maŋfal ní u làá dūú pà tin u bíi ŋáańee pu.
24Kɔŋkɔnnee, m-biyaamu, pīlifìmaan-mi ní kí kpòon̄ ni-tafal tiŋan kí pīlifì anyɔɔbun ŋin nyēē m-nyɔkɔnee. 25Ní taa yàntī an nimpuu juti ń ŋmàtiǹ-ni. Ní taa nóó u-sàmbiyaamu kí wāŋkì. 26U tīī binib tikpil tiweendi ní ki kūū-bi, u kūū ki kpáaǹ bipɔɔbi gba. 27U-dumpu di sá nsan ŋun cá bitaŋkpiibi kɔŋkooŋŋunee, ŋu sìntī ditaŋkpiilin ní cáaa.

english_text:
In Praise of Wisdom
1 With great understanding,
Wisdom is calling out
2as she stands at the crossroads
and on every hill.
3She stands by the city gate
where everyone enters the city,
and she shouts:
4“I am calling out
to each one of you!
5Good sense and sound judgment
can be yours.
6Listen, because what I say
is worthwhile and right.
7I always speak the truth
and refuse to tell a lie.
8Every word I speak is honest,
not one is misleading
or deceptive.
9“If you have understanding,
you will see that my words
are just what you need.
10Let instruction and knowledge
mean more to you than silver
or the finest gold.
11 Wisdom is worth much more
than precious jewels
or anything else you desire.”
Wisdom Speaks
12I am Wisdom—Common Sense
is my closest friend;
I possess knowledge
and sound judgment.
13If you respect the Lord,
you will hate evil.
I hate pride and conceit
and deceitful lies.
14I am strong, and I offer
sensible advice
and sound judgment.
15By my power kings govern,
and rulers make laws
that are fair.
16Every honest leader rules
with help from me.
17I love everyone who loves me,
and I will be found by all
who honestly search.
18I can make you rich and famous,
important and successful.
19What you receive from me
is more valuable
than even the finest gold
or the purest silver.
20I always do what is right,
21and I give great riches
to everyone who loves me.
22 From the beginning,
I was with the Lord.
I was there before he began
23to create the earth.
At the very first,
the Lord gave life to me.
24When I was born,
there were no oceans
or springs of water.
25My birth was before
mountains were formed
or hills were put in place.
26It happened long before God
had made the earth
or any of its fields
or even the dust.
27 I was there when the Lord
put the heavens in place
and stretched the sky
over the surface of the sea.
28I was with him when he placed
the clouds in the sky
and created the springs
that fill the ocean.
29I was there when he set
boundaries for the sea
to make it obey him,
and when he laid foundations
to support the earth.
30I was right beside the Lord,
helping him plan and build.
I made him happy each day,
and I was happy at his side.
31I was pleased with his world
and pleased with its people.
32 Pay attention, my children!
Follow my advice,
and you will be happy.
33Listen carefully
to my instructions,
and you will be wise.
34Come to my home each day
and listen to me.
You will find happiness.
35By finding me, you find life,
and the Lord will be pleased
with you.
36But if you don't find me,
you hurt only yourself,
and if you hate me,
you are in love with death.
translation_text:
Iciin fātìi tí bíi yíì binib
1Iciin bí ki tátí ki yíì,
dinyil bí ki kūuntí ki yíì.
Naa gbìl̀aaa?
2Ŋgbantamu mun bí didandi caŋinee,
isampuyakati ní iciin yú.
3Kitiŋ punyɔkɔ caŋin,
laakin binib dìŋfī ki kóòyee,
iciin yú ki tátí mpɔn yii:
4«Nimbi binib ní m yíì.
Nimbi binifoobi ní m lì.
5Nimbi bin kaa nyí tibee,
ní bīfì kí nīn cáá nlandɔkɔmɔnti.
Nimbi bin sá bigbaambee,
bīfìmaan kí nīn cáá dinyil.
6Ní pīlifìmaan, tibɔti tin páb́ee ní m làá sòoǹ,
deedee bɔti di làá nyānní m-nyɔkɔn.
7Kun puee m-nyɔkɔ sòoǹ ibaamɔn ní,
m-nyɔkɔ ń sòoǹ tibɔkpitilee, m kòó.
8Deedee bɔti ŋma ní man pée sòoǹ,
maa sòoǹ tinyimɔmbɔti àá biibii bɔti.
9Tì sá ibaamɔn bɔti uciŋfiti cee,
ní ki sá deedee bɔti unyil cee.
10Ní fōō tin man dàkèe kí yàntī animbil kúti,
kí fōō dinyil kí yàntī sindaariyamɔnti.
11Man Iciin pɔ̄ɔ̄ kudaau ki jítiǹ abeedimbil kpataaa.
Tin ni bìǹ ki nyàab̀ee, tiba kaa bàn̄-mi.»
Iciin lēē i-ba ki dàkā
12«Man di sá Iciin, m baasii wálifì ní.
M ŋáań tikɔkɔ nì nlandɔkɔ ní.
13Kí fàŋkì ti-Dindaanee, a ná ikpiti dee.
Man ná dibadakal nì dilambil nì atuŋkpiti nì inyimɔn.
14Man tundi di sá ḿ nīn sáŋkí binib kí nīn kpáafí-bi.
Man di baasii sá dinyil.
Man di yì mpɔn.
15Man pu ní bibɔtiibi jīǹ dibeel,
ní biyidambi yōontí bimarabaamɔmbi.
16Man pu ní bibɔtiibi ŋúb́ bi-timmu,
bi nì abɔtibil nì bibɔsoonliibi kɔkɔ.
17Man néeń bin néeń-mee ní.
Bin yaa nyàab̀-mee kāntí-mi ní.
18Man di tìì tigaajati nì tinyool,
nì tigaajawan tin yúntée nì dibútil.
19Tiwan tin m pūǹee ŋān̄ ki jítiǹ sindaariyamɔmmɔnti,
tin m tììyee jítiǹ animbil kúti timɔntiil.
20M còom̄ deedee saŋŋu pu ní,
ibaamɔn sàmbiyaamu pu ní m còom̄.
21M tìì bin néeń-mee tigaajati,
ki gbēentí bi-dumpui tigaajawammɔntiil.
22Ti-Dindaan péé péé ki náań-mi
ki wāatì ní ki nín náań tin kɔkɔ kíǹee.
23M nìn pée bí doooo jaanjaan,
ki wāatì ní duulinya nín kíĺ kí nīn bí.
24Bi nín màl̄-mee, tiŋkub kaa nìn bí,
inyimbul in jàkà nnyimee kaa nìn bí.
25Kí wàatī ajoon ń nyā kí nīn bée,
kí wàatī ŋgbantamu ń nīn bée, man nìn pée bí ní.
26Ti-Dindaan kaa nìn dá láá náań kitiŋ nì ipaan.
Waa nìn dá láá náań duulinya tampeepeekaam.
27M nìn bí ŋyunti ŋun u nìn dū kutagbɔŋu ki báaǹee,
ŋyunti ŋun u nìn lūtì nloon ki māntìi tú tiŋkuee.
28M nìn bí ŋyunti ŋun u nìn kpátì atagban ki bīiǹ kutaa puee,
nì ŋyunti ŋun tiŋku nyimbulii nìn tòoń nì mpɔnee.
29U nìn yóoǹ tiŋku kikpaanyɔkɔ
kin nnyim kaa máaǹ kí gbí kí lákatée.
U nìn bíl̀ dinyeel din pu kitiŋ làá nīn tɔ́kɔ́ee.
30Ŋyunti gbantee, m nìn bí u-cee kii utammakpilee.
Kutaa kamaayee m-bɔti nìn mɔ̄ǹ-u,
ní ŋyunti kamaa m nìn fàal̀ u-nimbiin.
31M nìn fàal̀ kitiŋ kin u náańee pu,
ní an nìn mɔ̄ǹ-mi ḿ nīn bí binib kansikin.»
Unil un pílifí Iciin bɔtee bí mmɔnneeee!
32«Kɔŋkɔnnee, m-biyaamu, pīlifìmaan-mi,
bin fōō m-saŋkiiyee bí mmɔnneeee!
33Ní pīlifìmaan tibɔti tin m dàkà-nee kí kpántí biciŋfitiibi,
ní taa dū-tì kí fá.
34Unil un pílifí m-bɔti,
ki pée bí m-punyɔkɔpu baabadal,
ki cí m-diiku punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpuee bí mmɔnneeee!
35Di sá yii un yaa ká-mee ká dimaŋfal,
ní ti-Dindaan dàkà udaan u-ŋanti.
36Ama unil un yaa kaa ká-mee tìì u-ba ní tiweendi.
Bin kɔkɔ ná-mee néeń ŋkúm ní.»

english_text:
Wisdom Gives a Feast
1Wisdom has built her house
with its seven columns.
2She has prepared the meat
and set out the wine.
Her feast is ready.
3She has sent her servant women
to announce her invitation
from the highest hills:
4“Everyone who is ignorant
or foolish is invited!
5All of you are welcome
to my meat and wine.
6If you want to live,
give up your foolishness
and let understanding
guide your steps.”
True Wisdom
7Correct a worthless bragger,
and all you will get
are insults and injuries.
8Any bragger you correct
will only hate you.
But if you correct someone
who has common sense,
you will be loved.
9If you have good sense,
instruction will help you
to have even better sense.
And if you live right,
education will help you
to know even more.
10 Respect and obey the Lord!
This is the beginning
of wisdom.
To have understanding,
you must know the Holy God.
11I am Wisdom. If you follow me,
you will live a long time.
12Good sense is good for you,
but if you brag,
you hurt yourself.
A Foolish Invitation
13Stupidity is reckless,
senseless, and foolish.
14She sits in front of her house
and on the highest hills
in the town.
15She shouts to everyone
who passes by,
16“If you are stupid,
come on inside!”
And to every fool she says,
17“Stolen water tastes best,
and the food you eat in secret
tastes best of all.”
18None who listen to Stupidity
understand that her guests
are as good as dead.
translation_text:
Iciin bíi yíì bin kaa nyí tibee
1Iciin máń i-diiku nì ku-jaantalkub biluli bin pu ku tɔ́kɔ́ee. 2I kūū i-waŋkuti, ki ŋāaǹ i-daam ní ki bɔ́ntì tijin ki yóoǹ. 3I tú i-tɔntɔnliibi binimpoobi kitiŋin bí jɔ̄m̀ kí tɔ́kɔń laakin bí yilpuee kí bāakì kí tùkù binib yii: 4«Nimbi bin kaa nyí tibee, dāam̄maan doo!» Ní i yāntì bi tùkū bigbaambi yii: 5«Ní dāam̄maan kí jī m-jinti, ní kí nyɔ̀ m-daam min m ŋāaǹee. 6Fámaan digbaandi ní kí nīn bí dimaŋfalin, ní kí nóó dinyil saŋŋu.»
Uciŋfiti nì ulambidaan
7A yaa sáŋkì ulambidaanee, u bèel̄-si ní, a yaa kpōotì unikpitee, asiibil ní a dāa kāntí. 8Á taa kpòotī ulambidaan, di sá yii u làá nīn ná-si, ama a yaa kpōotì uciŋfitee, u làá nīn néeń-si ní. 9A yaa sáŋkì uciŋfitee, u mɔ̀tīi cíkití iciin ní, a yaa dàkā deedeedaanee, u-nyil mɔ̀tīi gbēentí ní. 10Á fàŋkì ti-Dindaan di sá iciin kílilaŋki, á béé un di sá circiree di dàkà yii a sá unyil. 11Tiŋman, man Iciin làá gbéeǹ a-wiiŋyi pu, m làá yàntī á kàl̄ kitiŋ pu kí yúntí. 12A yaa sá uciŋfitee, sii di làá páatí a-ciiŋyi pu, a yaa sá ulambidaanee, sii baba di làá túń a-lambil gìńdi. 13Digbaandi sá kii unimpu un di cáá kufuu fám, kaa nyí tiba ní tiba pée kpá u-yilinee ní. 14U nyēē ní ki kā u-diiku punyɔkɔpu, dijal pu, kitiŋ poon laakin tɔ́kɔ́ yilpu yilpuee 15ní ki yíì bisanjitiliibi bin túĺ bi-saŋŋu cáaa ki cée yii: 16«Nimbi bin kaa nyí tibee, dāam̄maan doo!» Ní u tùkù bigbaambi yii: 17«Nnaayudaam mɔ̄ dinyɔl, ní tijin tin bi jīǹ dibalinee mɔ̄ dijil!» 18Ama bin cá u-ceeyee kaa nyí yii bi cá kí ŋàl̄ bin kaa ti bée pu, baa nyí yii ditaŋkpiilin ní bin u yíìyee cá.

english_text:
Solomon's Wise Sayings
1Here are some proverbs
of Solomon:
Children with good sense
make their parents happy,
but foolish children
make them sad.
2What you gain by doing evil
won't help you at all.
Obeying God is the only way
to be saved from death.
3If you obey the Lord,
you won't go hungry;
if you are wicked,
God won't let you have
what you want.
4Laziness leads to poverty;
hard work makes you rich.
5At harvest season
it's smart to work hard,
but stupid to sleep.
6Everyone praises good people,
but evil hides behind
the words of the wicked.
7Good people are remembered
long after they are gone,
but the wicked
are soon forgotten.
8If you have good sense,
you will listen and obey;
if all you do is talk foolishly,
you will destroy yourself.
9You will be safe,
if you always do right,
but you will get caught,
if you are dishonest.
10Deceit causes trouble,
and foolish talk
will bring you to ruin.
11The words of good people
are a source of life,
but evil hides behind
the words of the wicked.
12 Hatred stirs up trouble;
love overlooks the wrongs
that others do.
13If you have good sense,
it will show when you speak.
But if you are stupid,
you will be beaten
with a stick.
14If you have good sense,
you will learn all you can,
but foolish talk
will soon destroy you.
15Great wealth can be a fortress,
but poverty
is no protection at all.
16If you live right,
the reward is a good life;
if you are evil,
all you have is sin.
17Accept correction,
and you will find life;
reject correction,
and you will miss the road.
18You can hide your hatred
by telling lies,
but you are a fool
to spread lies.
19You will say the wrong thing
if you talk too much—
so be sensible and watch
what you say.
20The words of a good person
are like pure silver,
but the thoughts
of an evil person
are almost worthless.
21Many are helped
by useful instruction,
but fools are killed
by their own stupidity.
22When the Lord blesses you
with riches,
you have nothing to regret.
23Fools enjoy doing wrong,
but anyone with good sense
enjoys acting wisely.
24What evil people dread most
will happen to them,
but good people will get
what they want most.
25Those crooks will disappear
when a storm strikes,
but God will keep safe
all who obey him.
26Having a lazy person on the job
is like a mouth full of vinegar
or smoke in your eyes.
27If you respect the Lord,
you will live longer;
if you keep doing wrong,
your life will be cut short.
28If you obey the Lord,
you will be happy,
but there is no future
for the wicked.
29The Lord protects everyone
who lives right,
but he destroys anyone
who does wrong.
30Good people will stand firm,
but the wicked will disappear
from the land.
31Honest people speak sensibly,
but deceitful liars
will be silenced.
32If you obey the Lord,
you will always know
the right thing to say.
But no one will trust you
if you tell lies.
translation_text:
Alaŋkpan ŋin sòoǹ unil nín máaǹ kí nīn bí miŋyee
1Saloomɔn laŋkpaŋŋi.
Kibiki kin cáá iciinee yàntī ki-baa bí mmɔnni ní, kin kaa cáá iciinee sá kunimbaau ní ki tīī ki-na.
2Tigaajati tin bi dī isaŋkpiti pu ki kée kaa kèetī, ama deedee saŋŋu nyāntí unil ŋkúmin.
3Ti-Dindaan kaa yàntī deedeedaan ń kpú ŋkùm, ama waa yàntī binikpitib ń ká tin bi lèe.
4Iŋal in jòon̄ee cāabìń disool ní, iŋal in tūǹ ditundee tìì tigaajati.
5Unil un cēē tikpaajin dipeel puee sá ulandɔkɔdaan ní, ama un dɔ̄ ki gèeǹ ŋyunti ŋun bi cēē tikpaajinee cāabìń icoo ní.
6Unimbɔti bìintí deedeedaan pu, ama tipɔmbɔti nyɔɔbuŋŋi di gbí binikpitib sooŋyi poon.
7Bi téetí deedeedaan pu nì kupampakau, ama ní kí súntí binikpitib pu kí kpáaǹ bi-yiŋŋi.
8Uciŋfiti kíikí kí nóó marab kí nīn tɔ́-bi, ama unil un sòoǹ kaa dàkafēe làá nàan̄ u-ba ní.
9Un cáá tibulcinee còom̄ nì ŋgbansɔŋfi, ama un dī isan in gɔ́ĺee, Unimbɔti làá nyāntí udaan kí páań mpaampiin pu.
10Unil un cáá ibaamɔn ki bāal̀ u-jutiibee sàantí-bi ní, ní un sòoǹ kaa dàkafēe nàantí u-ba.
11Deedeedaan nyɔɔbuŋŋi sá kii nnyimbul ŋun tìì dimaŋfalee ní, ama tipɔmbɔti nyɔɔbuŋŋi di gbí binikpitib sooŋyi poon.
12Kináŋ cāabìń kujaau binib kansikin ní, ama dineendi díǹ bìintí ikpiti kɔkɔ pu ní.
13Iciin bí unil un cáá dinyilee nyɔɔbuŋŋin, ama mbambaan dɔ̄ ki cí ugbaan boon ní.
14Biciŋfitiibi kpáafí dinyil kii tigaajatee ní, ama bigbaambi nyɔɔbuŋŋi làá nàan̄-bi dicilpu dicilpu ní.
15Ugaaja wanti wúń u-pu kii digundee ní, ama bisoodambi sool di nàantí-bi.
16Deedeedaan paati di sá dimaŋfal, ama unikpiti paati di sá ikpiti.
17Unil un kíikí bí kpāafì-uee tàkā dimaŋfal saŋŋun, ama un kaa là bí wòoǹ-uee wáŋkí ní.
18Un ná u-juti dibalinee sá mpɔnnyoondaan, ama un kúŋfí u-juti boonee sá ugbaan ní.
19Unil un sòoǹ tikpilee, see ú yìntī, ama un kaa sòoǹ tikpilee sá uciŋfiti ní.
20Deedeedaan nyɔɔbuŋŋi sá kii animbil kúti timɔntiilee ní, ama binikpitib pɔbiliŋ kaa bí tiban.
21Deedeedaan nyɔɔbuŋŋi kèetī kunipaau ní, ama bigbaambi bíǹ kúù, kun puee baa nyí tiba.
22Ti-Dindaan biindi baba di yì unil gaajati, u-pɔ́ɔǹtam kaa pée kútí tiba.
23Kí ŋá ikpitee sá agbiil ní ugbaan cee, míǹ ní iciin mɔ̄ unyil cee.
24Kun unikpiti fàŋkée di bàń-u, ama tin kā deedeedambi naŋki puee ní bi kāntí.
25Utaafiiŋkaa tin lì yii u nì kí báatée, unikpiti kaa ti bí, ama deedeedaan úǹ yú kaa cìŋkī.
26Kii ayeen nín nyàŋfī unil nyiŋŋi pu ní nnyiim kóò unil nimbiliŋin puee, míǹ ní uwutijoodaan sá ki tīī un yaa tú-uee.
27Unil un fàŋkí ti-Dindaanee maŋfal làá fɔ̀kɔn̄, ama binikpitib kaa bà bi-wiiŋŋu ní kí kpú.
28Deedeedambi mákal cāabìń-bi dipɔɔpindi ní, ama binikpitib bíǹ mákal dāa pée kúntí nì fám ní.
29Ti-Dindaan saŋŋu sá kutaŋkpanaakoou ní ki tīī deedeedaan, ama ní ki sá dinàandi ki tīī binib bin di ŋáań ikpitee.
30Tiba kpá ki cìŋkì deedeedaan dalba dalba, ama binikpitib bíǹ kaa làá kàl̄ kitiŋ pu.
31Iciin nyɔɔbuŋŋi di nyēē deedeedaan nyɔkɔn, bi làá dāá gíí kí tìl̄ bin sòoǹ tibɔkpitilee limbil.
32Deedeedaan nyɔɔbuŋŋi mɔ̄ dipilifil, ama binikpitib bíǹ nyɔmmu nyēē tibɔkpitil ŋma ní.

english_text:
Watch What You Say and Do
1The Lord hates anyone
who cheats,
but he likes everyone
who is honest.
2Too much pride
can put you to shame.
It's wiser to be humble.
3If you do the right thing,
honesty will be your guide.
But if you are crooked,
you will be trapped
by your own dishonesty.
4When God is angry,
money won't help you.
Obeying God is the only way
to be saved from death.
5If you are truly good,
you will do right;
if you are wicked,
you will be destroyed
by your own sin.
6Honesty can keep you safe,
but if you can't be trusted,
you trap yourself.
7When the wicked die,
their hopes die with them.
8Trouble goes right past
the Lord's people
and strikes the wicked.
9Dishonest people use gossip
to destroy their neighbors;
good people are protected
by their own good sense.
10When honest people prosper
and the wicked disappear,
the whole city celebrates.
11Good people bring prosperity
to their city,
but deceitful liars
can destroy a city.
12It's stupid to say bad things
about your neighbors.
If you are sensible,
you will keep quiet.
13A gossip tells everything,
but a true friend
will keep a secret.
14 A city without wise leaders
will end up in ruin;
a city with many wise leaders
will be kept safe.
15It's a dangerous thing
to guarantee payment
for someone's debts.
Don't do it!
16A gracious woman
will be respected,
but a ruthless man
will only get rich.
17Kindness is rewarded—
but if you are cruel,
you hurt yourself.
18Meanness gets you nowhere,
but goodness is rewarded.
19Always do the right thing,
and you will live;
keep on doing wrong,
and you will die.
20The Lord hates sneaky people,
but he likes everyone
who lives right.
21You can be sure of this:
All crooks will be punished,
but God's people won't.
22A beautiful woman
who acts foolishly
is like a gold ring
on the snout of a pig.
23Good people want what is best,
but troublemakers
hope to stir up trouble.
24Sometimes you can become rich
by being generous
or poor by being greedy.
25Generosity will be rewarded:
Give a cup of water,
and you will receive
a cup of water in return.
26Charge too much for grain,
and you will be cursed;
sell it at a fair price,
and you will be praised.
27Try hard to do right,
and you will win friends;
go looking for trouble,
and you will find it.
28Trust in your wealth,
and you will be a failure,
but God's people will prosper
like healthy plants.
29Fools who cause trouble
in the family
won't inherit a thing.
They will end up as slaves
of someone with good sense.
30Live right, and you will eat
from the life-giving tree.
And if you act wisely,
others will follow.
31 If good people are rewarded
here on this earth,
all who are cruel and mean
will surely be punished.
translation_text:
1Ti-Dindaan ná saniyab bin kaa ŋmàntī tiwan deedeeyee, ama tiwaŋŋmantikaal tin bí deedeeyee di fáatì ti-Dindaan pɔbil.
2Dilambil di cāabìń icoo, ama binib bin sīntiǹ bi-ba taapuee di cáá iciin.
3Deedeedambi bulcinti di kpòotī-bi, ama biibiidambi saŋkiŋkpitiŋ di nàantí-bi.
4Ti-Dindaan ŋuul dalee, tigaajati kaa dāa kèetī, ama deedee saŋŋu di dāa nyāntí unil ŋkúmin.
5Bibulcinnib deedeeu di tàntī bi-saŋŋu, ama ní binikpitib bíǹ lítí bi-tuŋkpitiŋ pu.
6Deedeedambi deedeeu di fìil̄-bi, ama biibiidambi nimbitaataam di fàtīi sàtī-bi kii kutaliŋŋuee.
7Unikpiti yaa kpíìyee, u-mákal mun kúntì dee, ní dimákal din u cáá u-gaajati puee mun ń ŋá fám.
8Deedeedaan làá nyā dinimbinaamandin, ní unikpiti ń fōō u-yil kí kɔ́ di-ni.
9Unyimɔndaan nyɔkɔ ní u cáa kù u-juti, ama deedeedambi nyil pu ní bi kāntí difiil.
10An yaa bútì deedeedambee, ifaal bí kitiŋin ní, ama binikpitib yaa kpíìyee, bi kūuntí ní ki fàal̀.
11Deedeedambi biindi di yì-tì ní an bútí bi-tiŋki, ama binikpitib nyɔɔbuŋŋi di nàantí-kì.
12Unil un kpèé u-juti fámee kaa nyí tiba, ama unil un cáá dinyilee ŋmí ní.
13Unil un cāab̀ u-juti disambiilee kaa bāal̀ tibɔti, ama unil un pu bi mákée kaa sòoǹ.
14Dinibul din baa kpòotī tiŋanee lítí ní, din cáá bisaŋkiliibi kupaauee di ŋmátí.
15A yaa fáá ubɔ ŋaan ki pōoǹ kí pà a-juti pɔndee, án píl̀-si ní, ama a yaa yíì kaa dū a-ba ki kɔ́ǹ an bɔtinee, a làá ŋùŋfì.
16Unimpu un cáá kunyaaŋŋuee, bi pàkà-u ní, ama uninja un cáá difaŋgiilee kāntí tigaajati.
17Unil un ŋáań binib tinitee ŋáań ki tìì u-ba ní, ama unil un cáá ntoomee kɔ̄ntí u-ba ní digìńdi.
18Unikpiti tundi kaa cáá tipaal, ama tipaal dɔ̄ ki cí un tūǹ deedee tundee.
19Deedee saŋŋu cáǹ unil dimaŋfalin, ama unil un yaa nóó ikpiti saŋŋuee cá ŋkúmin ní.
20Ti-Dindaan ná milimilidambi, ama bibulcinnib bɔti fáatiǹ-u ní.
21Kí sɔ̄ kí lā, unikpiti kaa làá lóó ditafadaaldi, ama tiba kaa làá gbēē deedeedambi maaliŋun yab.
22Unimpunyaan un kaa nyí tibee sá kii ugbeeti un túuń sindaariya bɔmbil u-maŋfalee ní.
23Tin deedeedambi nyàab̀ee di sá tiŋan, ama tin binikpitib pée ŋūǹ kí nīn kā ki cée di sá ti-Dindaan ŋuul.
24Unil un ŋal tàntēe mɔ̀tīi kpántí ugaaja ní, ama un kpáafí tigaajati tikpilee kpántí usoodaan ní.
25Án làá dāá bútí unil un di cáá tinitee, ní bí dāá pɔ̄ un pūǹ bin kíǹee bi nyùee ú nyɔ̀.
26Binib tòó bin kpáafí bi-kpaajinti kí dāá nyāfì boonee mbusu, ama ní ki mèé ki bìintí bin nyáfí-tì malaa malaayee pu.
27Binib pàkà unil un nyàab̀ kí nīn ŋáań tin ŋān̄ee ní, ama un nyàab̀ kí ŋá tikpitilee, tikpitil ní udaan làá ká.
28Unil un máká u-gaajati puee làá lítí, ama án làá bútí deedeedambi kii busubu bun túkú tifaapɔnee ní.
29Unil un cāabìń fikil fikil u-dicaŋkunee dāa yáatí nì iŋaŋkulim ní. Ugbaan làá dāá kpántí uciŋfiti yumbuu.
30Atuun ŋin deedeedaan tūǹee sá kii busubu bun tìì dimaŋfalee ní. Uciŋfiti fìil̄ binib.
31Deedeedaan fòol̄ u-paati kitiŋ pu doo ní, míǹ mbaantiim ní unikpiti nì ukpitiŋal mun fòol̄ bi-paati kitiŋ pu doo.

english_text:
You Can't Hide behind Evil
1 To accept correction is wise,
to reject it is stupid.
2The Lord likes everyone
who lives right,
but he punishes everyone
who makes evil plans.
3Sin cannot offer security!
But if you live right,
you will be as secure
as a tree with deep roots.
4A helpful wife is a jewel
for her husband,
but a shameless wife
will make his bones rot.
5Good people have kind thoughts,
but you should never trust
the advice of someone evil.
6Bad advice is a deadly trap,
but good advice
is like a shield.
7Once the wicked are defeated,
they are gone forever,
but no one who obeys God
will ever be thrown down.
8Good sense is worthy of praise,
but stupidity is a curse.
9It's better to be ordinary
and have only one servant
than to think you are somebody
and starve to death.
10Good people are kind
to their animals,
but a mean person is cruel.
11Hard working farmers have more
than enough food;
daydreamers are nothing more
than stupid fools.
12An evil person tries to hide
behind evil;
good people are like trees
with deep roots.
13We trap ourselves
by telling lies,
but we stay out of trouble
by living right.
14We are rewarded or punished
for what we say and do.
15Fools think they know
what is best,
but a sensible person
listens to advice.
16Losing your temper is foolish;
ignoring an insult is smart.
17An honest person
tells the truth in court,
but a dishonest person
tells nothing but lies.
18Sharp words cut like a sword,
but words of wisdom heal.
19Truth will last forever;
lies are soon found out.
20An evil mind is deceitful,
but gentle thoughts
bring happiness.
21Good people never have trouble,
but troublemakers
have more than enough.
22The Lord hates every liar,
but he is the friend of all
who can be trusted.
23Be sensible and don't tell
everything you know—
only fools spread
foolishness everywhere.
24Work hard, and you
will be a leader;
be lazy, and you
will end up a slave.
25Worry is a heavy burden,
but a kind word
always brings cheer.
26You are better off to do right,
than to lose your way
by doing wrong.
27Anyone too lazy to cook
will starve,
but a hard worker
is a valuable treasure.
28Living right is a pathway
that leads to life
and away from death.
translation_text:
1Unil un néeń ikpootee néeń dinyil ní. Ama unil un kaa là bí wòoǹ-uee sá ugbaan ní.
2Unimɔnti bɔti fáatiǹ ti-Dindaan ní, ama u kù ilandɔkɔkpiti daan bɔti.
3Unikpiti kaa bá ki pɔ̄ɔ̄, ama deedeedaan úǹ yú atajal ali ní.
4Unimpu tiŋman pu yɔu tìì u-cal tinyool ní, ama unimpu un kɔ̄ntí u-cal icooyee sá-u iween in ŋmóò ki bùkù akpabee ní.
5Deedeedambi pée dàkafī kí ŋá tin bí deedeeyee, ama ní binikpitib dàkafī kí mùul̀.
6Binikpitib nyɔɔbuŋŋi sá titalindi tin kùee ní, ama deedeedambi nyɔɔbuŋŋi cāabìń difiil.
7Binikpitib yaa lítèe, bi-yindi kúntì dee, ama deedeedambi dicaŋku kpá kí kúntí jaanjaan.
8Unil un cáá dinyilee, bi pàkà-u ní, ama bi kpèé un kaa nyí tibee fám.
9An sɔ́ á nīn cáá utɔntɔnli ubɔ ja bí kpèè-si fám ki jítiǹ á nīn néeń a-ba timɔn kaa cáá kí jī.
10Deedeedaan nyí kun lóò u-waŋkutee, ama unikpiti úǹ poon tū ní.
11Unil un kù u-saakuee jīǹ ki díkì ní, ama unil un jòó ki pá tin kaa bí tibanee boonee sá ugbaan ní.
12Unikpiti cáá bikpitiŋaliibi wanti pu nnimbitaataam, see deedeedambi pɔ́ɔǹdi baba di kèetī.
13Unikpiti bɔkpitii sá-u kutaliŋŋu ní, ama deedeedaan úǹ nyēē tibɔtin ní.
14Unil nyɔɔbuŋŋi ŋūǹ kí yàntī ú ká tiwammɔntiil kii unil tundi nín yàntī ú fōō tipaal puee ní.
15Ugbaan dàkafī yii tin u ŋáańee di pée ŋān̄, ama un fòol̄ isaŋkee di sá uciŋfiti.
16Ugbaan di yàntī bí béé dicilpu yii u gíí diŋuul, ama unil un nyí nì u-bee, báà bi yaa sīī-u waa gífí diŋuul.
17Unil un sòoǹ ibaamɔnee nyāntí deedee mpaampiin pu, ama un lèekī inyimɔn seerabee nyāntí diyìntil ní mpaampiin pu.
18Unil un sòoǹ kaa dàkafēe tìì tiweendi kii kitàataajikee ní, ama biciŋfitiibi bíǹ nyɔɔbuŋŋi cāabìń dicáaǹdi ní.
19Ibaamɔn bɔti bí kí nīn cá jaanjaan, ama tinyimɔmbɔti kaa pée súŋkí ní kí wāŋkì.
20Inyimɔn bí bin dàkafī kí ŋá ikpitee pɔbiliŋin, ama ní dipɔɔpindi bí bin nyàab̀ ŋgbansɔŋfee yaŋin.
21Digìńdi báà diba kaa bàń deedeedaan, ama ní binikpitib bíǹ pée kāntí agìŋ́kpaan.
22Ti-Dindaan ná binyimɔndambi, ama ní ki néeń ibaamɔndambi.
23Unil un cáá iciinee bāal̀ tin u nyée ní, ama ugbaan úǹ bāakì u-gbaandi ki tùkù báà ŋma ní.
24Unil un cáá difaŋgiilee làá dāá nīn cáá mpɔn bin kíǹee pu, ama unil un yaa cáá diwutijoolee làá dāá kpántí uyumbu.
25Digìńdi yaa bàn̄ unilee, an nyìitī-u kí múĺ ní, ama dinyɔɔbummɔɔl di ŋūǹ kí sɔ̀ŋkì u-pɔbil.
26Deedeedaan dàkà u-juti nsammɔnti ní, ama binikpitib saŋŋu cáǹ bíǹ bi-ba diyìntilin ní.
27Ukpan un sá uwutijoodaanee kaa kāntí upeel kí púĺ, ama unil un cáá difaŋgiilee cáá tigaajati.
28Deedee saŋŋun ní dimaŋfal bí, nsan gbanti ŋúǹ kaa cáǹ unil ŋkúmin.

english_text:
Wise Friends Make You Wise
1Children with good sense
accept correction
from their parents,
but stubborn children
ignore it completely.
2You will be well rewarded
for saying something kind,
but all some people think about
is how to be cruel and mean.
3 Keep what you know to yourself,
and you will be safe;
talk too much,
and you are done for.
4No matter how much you want,
laziness won't help a bit,
but hard work will reward you
with more than enough.
5A good person hates deceit,
but those who are evil
cause shame and disgrace.
6Live right, and you are safe!
But sin will destroy you.
7Some who have nothing
may pretend to be rich,
and some who have everything
may pretend to be poor.
8The rich may have
to pay a ransom,
but the poor don't have
that problem.
9The lamp of a good person
keeps on shining;
the lamp of an evil person
soon goes out.
10Too much pride causes trouble.
Be sensible and take advice.
11Money wrongly gained
will disappear bit by bit;
money earned little by little
will grow and grow.
12Not getting what you want
can break your heart,
but a wish that comes true
is a life-giving tree.
13If you reject God's teaching,
you will pay the price;
if you obey his commands,
you will be rewarded.
14Sensible instruction
is a life-giving fountain
that helps you escape
all deadly traps.
15Sound judgment is praised,
but people without good sense
are on the way to disaster.
16If you have good sense,
you will act sensibly,
but fools act like fools.
17Whoever delivers your message
can make things better
or worse for you.
18All who refuse correction
will be poor and disgraced;
all who accept correction
will be praised.
19It's a good feeling
to get what you want,
but only a stupid fool
hates to turn from evil.
20 Wise friends make you wise,
but you hurt yourself
by going around with fools.
21You are in for trouble
if you sin,
but you will be rewarded
if you live right.
22If you obey God,
you will have something
to leave your grandchildren.
If you don't obey God,
those who live right
will get what you leave.
23Even when the land of the poor
produces good crops,
they get cheated
out of what they grow.
24If you love your children,
you will correct them;
if you don't love them,
you won't correct them.
25If you live right,
you will have plenty to eat;
if you don't live right,
you will go away empty.
translation_text:
1Kibiki kin cáá iciinee fòol̄ ki-baa dàkal, ama kin bèel̄ binibee kaa kíikí bí lìǹ-kì.
2Tin nyēē unil nyɔkɔnee pu ní u kāntí njimmɔntiim, ama tipɔmbɔti ní biibiidambi jīǹ ki bí.
3Unil un ŋūǹ ki ŋúb̀ u-nyɔkɔee wúń u-maŋfal pu ní, ama unil un sòoǹ pùsi pusi kaa dàkafēe nàantí u-ba ní.
4Uwutijoodaan kpèé ní làm kaa kāntí, ama ufaŋgiidaan úǹ kāntí tin kamaa u yaa lèe ní.
5Deedeedaan ná inyimɔn, unikpiti kɔ̄ntí binib icoo ní ki bíiĺ-bi.
6Tibulcin wúǹ ubulcindaan pu, ama ikpiti nàantí unikpiti.
7Binib biba yíì bi-ba bigaajab ní kaa cáá báà tiba, ní biba yíì bi-ba bisoodambi ama ní ki cáá tigaajakpaandi.
8Ugaaja gaajati di fìil̄-u, ama ubɔ kaa wɔ́b̀ usoodaan.
9Deedeedambi sá kii ŋwalifi ŋun wāĺ bɔ́iiyee ní, ama binikpitib bíǹ bí kii fitila un bíi kúùyee ní.
10Dilambil di yàntī unil tákà tibɔti, ama unil un fòol̄ isaŋkee di sá uciŋfiti.
11Tigaajati tin unil ká malaayee kaa yúntí, ama tigaajati tin unil ŋá soooo soooo ki kée kaa kúntí.
12Unil yaa máká tiba pu ní kaa ká-tì malaayee, u-wunti yɔ̀tī ní, ama unil yaa ká tin fáatì u-pɔbilee, an bí kii busubu bun tìì dimaŋfalee ní.
13Unil un kpèé ki sìŋkīǹ isaŋkee làá kɔ́ agìń poon, ama un tɔ́ marabee làá ká ipaati.
14Uciŋfiti dàkatam sá dimaŋfal nyimbuliŋu ní. Ŋúǹ di yàntī unil ń gɔ́ntí ŋkúm talinti.
15Un cáá dinyil tikpilee bɔti fáatiǹ binib ní. Ama biibiidambi saŋŋu cáǹ dinàandin ní.
16Un nyí nì u-bee dàkafī ní kí nín ŋá tiba, ama ugbaan úǹ cáá u-gbaandi ki dàkà báà ŋma ní.
17Ntuun ŋun kaa ŋān̄ee cāabìń mbusu ní, ama ntuun ŋun sá mmɔntee cāabìń diŋaŋkil ní.
18Disool nì icoo dɔ̄ ki cí un kaa là bí dàkà-uee, ama un kíikí bí wòoǹ-uee làá fōō kupampakau.
19An sá mmɔn ní unil ń ká kun fáatiǹ-uee, an pu ní ugbaan kaa là kí fá atuŋkpiti.
20Unil un nōotí biciŋfitiibee kpántí uciŋfiti ní, ama un nōotí bigbaambee kɔ̄ntí u-ba agìńni.
21Nnaabu kā bikpitiŋaliibi pu kàti kati, ama nnaam di sá deedeedambi bíǹ paati.
22Unimɔnti naantiibi jīǹ u-gaajawanti difakal ní, ama unikpiti úǹ gaajatee, deedeedaan di jīǹ-tì.
23Bisoodambi kpaaŋŋi lòoǹ tikpil, ama bin kaa bí deedeeyee kpaaŋŋi yɔ́l̀ ní.
24Unil un kaa gbáà u-bikee ná-kì dee. Unil un néeń u-bikee dátí ki-tafal ní.
25Deedeedaan cáá kí jī kí díkí, ama ní binikpitib pooŋi náká.

english_text:
Wisdom Makes Good Sense
1A woman's family
is held together
by her wisdom,
but it can be destroyed
by her foolishness.
2By living right, you show
that you respect the Lord;
by being deceitful, you show
that you despise him.
3Proud fools are punished
for their stupid talk,
but sensible talk
can save your life.
4Without the help of an ox
there can be no crop,
but with a strong ox
a big crop is possible.
5An honest witness
tells the truth;
a dishonest witness
tells nothing but lies.
6Make fun of wisdom,
and you will never find it.
But if you have understanding,
knowledge comes easily.
7Stay away from fools,
or you won't learn a thing.
8Wise people have enough sense
to find their way,
but stupid fools get lost.
9Fools don't care
if they are wrong,
but God is pleased
when people do right.
10No one else can really know
how sad or happy you are.
11The tent of a good person
stands longer than the house
of someone evil.
12 You may think you are
on the right road
and still end up dead.
13Sorrow may hide
behind laughter,
and happiness may end
in sorrow.
14You harvest what you plant,
whether good or bad.
15Don't be stupid
and believe all you hear;
be smart and know
where you are headed.
16Only a stupid fool
is never cautious—
so be extra careful
and stay out of trouble.
17Fools have quick tempers,
and no one likes you
if you can't be trusted.
18Stupidity leads to foolishness;
be smart and learn.
19The wicked will come crawling
to those who obey God.
20You have no friends
if you are poor,
but you have lots of friends
if you are rich.
21It's wrong to hate others,
but God blesses everyone
who is kind to the poor.
22It's a mistake
to make evil plans,
but you will have loyal friends
if you want to do right.
23Hard work is worthwhile,
but empty talk
will make you poor.
24Wisdom can make you rich,
but foolishness leads
to more foolishness.
25An honest witness
can save your life,
but liars can't be trusted.
26If you respect the Lord,
you and your children
have a strong fortress
27and a life-giving fountain
that keeps you safe
from deadly traps.
28Rulers of powerful nations
are held in honor;
rulers of weak nations
are nothing at all.
29It's smart to be patient,
but it's stupid
to lose your temper.
30It's healthy to be content,
but envy can eat you up.
31If you mistreat the poor,
you insult your Creator;
if you are kind to them,
you show him respect.
32In times of trouble
the wicked are destroyed,
but even at death
the innocent have faith.
33Wisdom is found in the minds
of people with good sense,
but fools don't know it.
34Doing right brings honor
to a nation,
but sin brings disgrace.
35Kings reward servants
who act wisely,
but they punish those
who act foolishly.
translation_text:
1Unimpuciŋfiti máń u-diiku, ama unimpugbaan dù úǹ u-ba ŋalii ní kí gbá kí wīī-ku.
2Unil un còom̄ deedee saŋkindee fàŋkí ti-Dindaan ní. Ama un dī isan in gɔ́ĺee kpèé-u fám dee.
3Ugbaan nyɔɔbuŋŋi poon ní a kāntí u-badakal, ama biciŋfitiibi nyɔɔbuŋŋi di wúǹ bi-pu.
4Unil un kaa cáá inaa í kpɔ̀-u tikpaalee, u-cakalaau yú ukulim ní, ama un cáá inaa pɔ̄ɔ̄yee cáá tijin tikpil ní.
5Deedee seeradaaŋwu kaa mɔ́ntí, ama inyimɔn seeradaaŋwu mɔ́ntí ŋma ní.
6Unil un dàkà u-bee nyàab̀ iciin ní kaa kāntí-i, ama an kaa pɔ̄ɔ̄ ulandɔkɔdaan úǹ ń ká dinyil.
7Kàkatī a-ba kí wàatī ugbaan, di sá yii aa làá pée ká dinyil diba u-nyɔɔbuŋŋi poon.
8Un nyí nì u-bee ciiŋyi di sá ú kpèè u-saŋkindi tiŋan, ama bigbaambi gbaandi di sá bí mɔ̄ntì bin kíǹee.
9Bigbaambi kaa fātìi tɔ́ yii bí ŋāŋkì bi-yìntitam. Ama deedeedambi kansikin ní a kāntí Unimbɔti saasɔl.
10Unil un bí kunimbaaunee baba di nyí u-nimbaaku. U yaa tí bí mmɔnee, u nì ubɔ kaa tí ŋūǹ kí yàkatī u-mɔŋŋu.
11Binikpitib diiku làá dāá lítí kí nàan̄, ama ní deedeedambi tantiu ń nīn yú ki pɔ̄ɔ̄.
12Unil ŋūǹ kí dàkafì yii nsan ŋun u nóóyee ŋān̄, ama án dāá kúntée, ŋu cáǹ-u ŋkúmin ní.
13Unil ŋūǹ kí nīn lāā ama ní u-pɔbil poonee, u bí kunimbaaun, ní dipɔɔpindi ń dāá kúntí nì kunimbaau.
14Unil un pɔbil gáatèe làá dāá fōō digáatil paati, ní deedeedaan mun ń dāá fōō u-deedeeu paati.
15Kinaatuui di fòol̄ tin kɔkɔ bi tùkù-uee, ama unil un nyí nì u-bee kpèé u-saŋkindi tiŋan ní.
16Uciŋfiti fàŋkí tikpitil ní ki gɔ́ntí-tì, ama ugbaan úǹ ŋáań tikɔkɔ malaa malaa, kun puee u máká u-ba pu.
17Unil un gífí diŋuul malaayee ŋáań tigbaambɔti, ní biibiidaan dátí kináŋ ki tòó u-ba pu.
18Nnaatuumu fakal di sá digbaandi, ama binib bin nyí nì bi-bee nyooti di sá dinyil.
19Binikpitib làá gbàan̄ binimɔntiibi nimbiin, ní bikpitiŋaliibi ń dāá yūĺ deedeedambi punyɔkɔpu ki nyàab̀ dijòońdi.
20Usoodaan kɔŋkɔnnaatɔb gba ná-u ní, ama bin néeń ugaajee wīikí tikpil ní.
21Unil un kpèé u-juti fámee ŋá ikpiti, ama un sūǹ binandambi saayee bí mmɔnni.
22Binib bin dàkafī ilandɔkɔkpitee wáŋkì dee, ama bin dàkafī nlandɔkɔmɔntee làá ká tiŋan nì ibaamɔn bi-saŋŋu pu.
23Unil ń tɔ̄ ditundi nì difaŋgiilee cáá tipaal ní, ama kubɔcaau cāabìń disool ní.
24Biciŋfitiibi paatii di sá tigaajati, ama ní bigbaambi bíǹ gbíntíǹ bi-gbaandi.
25Useeradaan un sòoǹ ibaamɔnee fìil̄ binib ní, ama un mɔ́ntí inyimɔnee nàantí binib ní.
26Unil un fàŋkí ti-Dindaanee cáá dimákakpaandi, kun puee u sá kibalilaŋ ki tīī u-biyaamu.
27Unil ń fàŋkì ti-Dindaanee di sá dimaŋfal nyimbuliŋu. An di yàntī ú gɔ́ntí ŋkúm talinti.
28Dinibul din wīikée bɔtiu cáá tinyool ní, ama kitiŋ kin nib yaa bíi bàtēe bɔtiu beel bíi kúntí dee.
29Unil un kaa gífí diŋuul malaayee cáá dinyil tikpil, ama un kaa pɔ̄ɔ̄ diŋuul digiilee dàkà u-gbaandi ní.
30Dipɔɔsɔŋkil di yì ŋgbampɔn, ama ní ipoompoon sá iween in ŋmóò ki bùkù akpabee.
31Unil un wɔ́b̀ binandambee sìí bi-náanliu ní, ama un sūǹ usoodaan saayee tìì Unimbɔti ní tinyool.
32Unikpiti tuŋkpitiŋ di yàntī ú lítí, ama deedeedaan cáá dimákal ki kpáaǹ u-kúmin.
33Iciin bí unil un cáá dinyilee pɔbilin ní, ama ŋma di ŋūǹ kí ká iciin bigbaambi kansikin?
34Ditimbundi din nóó deedee saŋŋuee yíkí yilpu ní, ama ní ikpiti íǹ kɔ̄ntí-dì icoo.
35Ubɔti pàkà u-tɔntɔnliu un cáá dinyilee ní, ama u gífí diŋuul un kɔ̄ntí-u icooyee pu.

english_text:
The Lord Sees Everything
1A kind answer
soothes angry feelings,
but harsh words
stir them up.
2Words of wisdom
come from the wise,
but fools speak foolishness.
3The Lord sees everything,
whether good or bad.
4Kind words are good medicine,
but deceitful words
can really hurt.
5Don't be a fool
and disobey your parents.
Be smart! Accept correction.
6Good people become wealthy,
but those who are evil
will lose what they have.
7Words of wisdom
make good sense;
the thoughts of a fool
make no sense at all.
8The Lord is disgusted
by gifts from the wicked,
but it makes him happy
when his people pray.
9The Lord is disgusted
with all who do wrong,
but he loves everyone
who does right.
10If you turn from the right way,
you will be punished;
if you refuse correction,
you will die.
11If the Lord can see everything
in the world of the dead,
he can see in our hearts.
12Those who sneer at others
don't like to be corrected,
and they won't ask help
from someone with sense.
13Happiness makes you smile;
sorrow can crush you.
14Anyone with good sense
is eager to learn more,
but fools are hungry
for foolishness.
15The poor have a hard life,
but being content is as good
as an endless feast.
16It's better to obey the Lord
and have only a little,
than to be very rich
and terribly anxious.
17A simple meal with love
is better than a feast
where there is hatred.
18Losing your temper
causes a lot of trouble,
but staying calm
settles arguments.
19A lazy person refuses
to clear a thorny path,
but everyone who does right
walks on a smooth road.
20Children with good sense
make their parents happy,
but foolish children
despise them.
21Stupidity brings happiness
to senseless fools,
but everyone with good sense
follows the straight path.
22Without good advice
everything goes wrong—
it takes careful planning
for things to go right.
23Giving the right answer
at the right time
makes everyone happy.
24All who are wise follow a road
that leads upward to life
and away from death.
25The Lord destroys the homes
of those who are proud,
but he protects the property
of widows.
26The Lord hates evil thoughts,
but kind words please him.
27Being greedy causes trouble
for your family,
but you protect yourself
by refusing bribes.
28Good people think
before they answer,
but the wicked speak evil
without ever thinking.
29The Lord never even hears
the prayers of the wicked,
but he answers the prayers
of all who obey him.
30A friendly smile
makes you happy,
and good news
makes you feel strong.
31Healthy correction is good,
and if you accept it,
you will be wise.
32You hurt only yourself
by rejecting instruction,
but it makes good sense
to accept it.
33Showing respect to the Lord
will make you wise,
and being humble
will bring honor to you.
translation_text:
1Unil yaa kíí u-juti dinyɔɔbummɔɔndee, án sɔ̀ŋkī u-ŋuul ní, ama u yaa kíí mpɔn nì mpɔnee, án gbítí u-ŋuul ní.
2Biciŋfitiibi yaa bíi sòon̄ee, an nyàatī unil ń bīfì ní, ama bigbaambi bíǹ yaa wāaǹ bi-nyɔkɔee, tigbaambɔti ŋma di nyēē.
3Ti-Dindaan nimbiliŋ làaǹ an kɔkɔ, ki kpèé binikpitib nì binimɔntiibi kɔkɔ.
4Dinyɔɔbundi din sɔ̀ŋkī dipɔbilee sá kii busubu bun tìì dimaŋfalee ní, dinyɔɔbuŋkpil yaa ŋmàl̄ tibɔtinee, an yòontí unil pɔbil ní.
5Ugbaan kaa fātìi tɔ́ u-baa dàkatam, ama un là bí kpòotī-uee sá uciŋfiti ní.
6Tigaajati tikpaandi di bí deedeedaan dumpu, ama ní unikpiti gaajawanti cāabìń-u nnaabu.
7Biciŋfitiibi nyɔɔbuŋŋi tìì binib dinyil, ama an kaa sá míǹ bigbaambi cee.
8Ti-Dindaan ná binikpitib saraabi, ama deedeedambi bíǹ wimmeem tìì-u mmɔn.
9Ti-Dindaan ná binikpitib bimbim, ama ní ki néeń unil un nóó deedee saŋŋuee.
10Un yaa fá nsammɔntee làá ká ditafadaaldi, unil un kaa là bí wòoǹ-uee làá kpú.
11Ti-Dindaan nyí tin bí ki jītí ditaŋkpiil poon poon kábuee, ŋma nín yíiń tin ní unil dàkafī u-pɔbilinee.
12Ulambidaan kaa là bí kpòotī-u, an pu ní waa cá biciŋfitiibi cee.
13Dipɔɔpindi bútí nnimbiin ní, ama dipɔɔbiildi cāabìń diwuŋyɔtil ní.
14Unil un cáá iciinee nyàab̀ dinyil ní, ama bigbaambi nyɔmmunee, tigbaambɔti di gbí.
15Unandaan ceeyee, iwiin kɔkɔ pée pɔ̄ɔ̄ ki tīī-u ní, ama un pɔbil sɔ̀m̀ee ceeyee, ŋwiin kamaa sá-u jiŋaal ní.
16An sɔ́ unil ń nīn cáá tigaajawan fiii kí nīn fàŋkí ti-Dindaan, ki jítiǹ ú nīn cáá tigaajati tikpil ki bí iyaliŋki poon.
17An sɔ́ unil ń ŋmɔ́ tikaŋkaŋfaal tin bi tɔ́kɔǹ nì dineendee ki jítiǹ unaa un bí màlmalee nanti tin bi dū kináŋ ki ŋāāyee.
18Unil un kaa pɔ̄ɔ̄ diŋuul digiilee sàal̄ kujaau ní, ama un kaa gífí diŋuul malaayee pèefī kujaau ní.
19Uwutijoodaan saŋŋu sá kii ikuŋkumee ní, ama deedeedaan saŋŋu ŋúǹ pée tèen̄ ní.
20Kibiki kin cáá iciinee yàntī ki-baa pɔbil pīiǹ ní, ama ugbaanee, úǹ kpèé u-na fám ní.
21Unil un kaa cáá iciinee fàal̀ u-gbaandi pu ní, ama unil un cáá dinyilee nóó deedee saŋŋu ní.
22Unil yaa kaa bàlifī isaŋkee, tin u bɔ́ntée kaa còom̄, ama bisaŋkiliibi yaa wīikée an còom̄ ní.
23Unil yaa kíí tibɔti tì nín sá puee, an tìì mmɔn ní, dinyɔɔbundi yaa nyáń ŋyunti ŋun di máaǹ kí nyēe, di cáá mpɔn ní.
24Unil un nyée nóó nsan ŋun jɔ́ḿ ki cá dimaŋfal laŋkee ní. Waa nōotí ŋun sìntī ditaŋkpiilin taapuee.
25Ti-Dindaan nàantí bilambidambi diiŋŋi, ama u mɔ́tí ukpiipu tampaaŋŋu pu.
26Ti-Dindaan ná ilandɔkɔkpiti, ama u fáatì anyɔɔbummɔnti.
27Unil un néeń animbil tikpilee kɔ̄ntí u-dicaŋku agìńni ní. Ama un ná dinyɔɔŋeebil jimee cáá mmaŋfafɔkɔn ní.
28Deedeedaan dàkafī kí wàatī ní kí nín kíí tibɔti, ama binikpitib bíǹ wùliŋkī tibɔfan ní.
29Ti-Dindaan dátiǹ binikpitib, ama u pílifí deedeedambi wimmeem.
30Nnimbiin ŋun bútèe tìì mmɔn, ní tibɔmɔntiil tìì mpɔn.
31Unil un pílifí isaŋki in tìì dimaŋfalee cáá u-kɔŋkooŋŋu biciŋfitiibi kansikin.
32Unil un kaa là bí kpòotī-uee ná u-ba ní, ama un fòol̄ iwoonee béetí iciin.
33Á fàŋkì ti-Dindaanee, an bífí iciin ní. Kí wàatī á ká tinyoolee, see á sìntīǹ a-ba.

english_text:
The Lord Has the Final Word
1We humans make plans,
but the Lord
has the final word.
2We may think we know
what is right,
but the Lord is the judge
of our motives.
3Share your plans with the Lord,
and you will succeed.
4The Lord has a reason
for everything he does,
and he lets evil people live
only to be punished.
5The Lord doesn't like
anyone who is conceited—
you can be sure
they will be punished.
6 If we truly love God,
our sins will be forgiven;
if we show him respect,
we will keep away from sin.
7When we please the Lord,
even our enemies
make friends with us.
8 It's better to be honest
and poor
than to be dishonest
and rich.
9We make our own plans,
but the Lord decides
where we will go.
10Rulers speak with authority
and are never wrong.
11The Lord watches to see
if we are fair
or if we cheat others.
12Justice makes rulers powerful.
They should hate evil
13and like honesty and truth.
14An angry ruler
can put you to death.
So be wise!
Don't make one angry.
15When a ruler is happy
and pleased with you,
it's like refreshing rain,
and you will live.
16It's much better to be wise
and sensible
than to be rich.
17God's people avoid evil ways,
and they protect themselves
by watching where they go.
18Too much pride
will destroy you.
19You are better off
to be humble and poor
than to get rich
from what you take by force.
20If you know what you're doing,
you will prosper.
God blesses everyone
who trusts him.
21Good judgment proves
that you are wise,
and if you speak kindly,
you can teach others.
22Good sense is a fountain
that gives life,
but fools are punished
by their foolishness.
23You can persuade others
if you are wise
and speak sensibly.
24Kind words are like honey—
they cheer you up
and make you feel strong.
25 Sometimes what seems right
is really a road to death.
26The hungrier you are,
the harder you work.
27Worthless people plan trouble.
Even their words burn
like a flaming fire.
28 Gossip is no good!
It causes hard feelings
and comes between friends.
29Don't trust violent people.
They will mislead you
to do the wrong thing.
30When someone winks
or grins behind your back,
trouble is on the way.
31Gray hair is a glorious crown
worn by those
who have lived right.
32Controlling your temper
is better than being a hero
who captures a city.
33We make our own decisions,
but the Lord alone
determines what happens.
translation_text:
Ti-Dindaan ń nīn bí unil maŋfal wiiŋyi kɔkɔn
1Unil màkà, ama ti-Dindaan di lèekī min u làá ŋée.
2Unil dàkafī yii tin u pée ŋáańee kɔkɔ ŋān̄ ní, ama ti-Dindaan di kpèé ki wāĺ unil pɔbilin.
3Tin kɔkɔ a là kí ŋée, dūú ŋá ti-Dindaan ŋaan, ní kí ŋmā kí ŋá tin a bɔ́ntèe.
4Ti-Dindaan nyí kun pu ní u náań tiwan kɔkɔee. U náań unikpiti mun ki cíitì ŋwiin ŋun u làá dáaĺ u-tafalee ní.
5Ti-Dindaan ná bilambidambi, báà án ŋá pu, u làá dáaĺ bi-tafal.
6Dineeŋkpaandi nì ibaamɔn pu ní unil kāntí ikpiti pɔ̄tam. Unil un fàŋkí ti-Dindaanee sáń ikpiti ní.
7Unil bimbim yaa fáatiǹ ti-Dindaanee, u yàntī u nì u-nannanliibi gba ń mɔ̄ɔkì ní.
8Unil ń dī tibulcin pu kí ká tigaajawan fiiiyee sɔ́ǹ ú dī isaŋkpiti pu kí ká tigaajati tikpil.
9Unil pɔbil poon ní u bɔ́ntí nsan ŋun u làá còom̀ee, ama ti-Dindaan di lèekī ŋun u làá nóóyee.
Alaŋkpan ŋin sòoǹ bibɔtiibi puee
10Unimbɔti bɔti di kā ubɔti nyɔkɔn ní u sòoǹ, an kaa cáá yii u sòon̄ ki yīntì ibɔsoon poon.
11Ti-Dindaan cee ní saniyab bin bí deedeeyee nyēē, ataŋkpaŋmantikaa ŋin kā tilɔtinee kɔkɔ nyiŋfiŋu sá u-tundi ní.
12Bibɔtiibi ná binib bin ŋáań ikpitee, di sá yii deedee di tìì dibeel mpɔn.
13Bin sòoǹ ibaamɔnee bɔti di fáatì bibɔtiibi, bi néeń binib bin sòoǹ tibɔti deedeeyee ní.
14Ubɔti ŋuul sá ŋkpituun ní, ama uciŋfiti ŋūǹ kí sɔ̀ŋkì-dì
15Ubɔti nimbiin yaa ŋān̄ee, an sá dimaŋfal ní, u-ŋanti bí kii ukpaasiitaayee ní.
Unil nín máaǹ kí nīn bí min samaa kansikinee laŋkpaŋŋi
16Unil ń nīn cáá iciin sɔ́ǹ ú nīn cáá sindaariya. Unil ń nīn cáá dinyil sɔ́ǹ ú nīn cáá animbil kúti.
17Deedeedambi còom̄ nsan ŋun tèen̄ee poon ní ki gɔ́ntí tikpitil. Unil un nyí u nín còom̄ puee fìil̄ u-maŋfal ní.
18Dilambil cáǹ unil dinàandin, ní dibadakal cáǹ unil dilitilin.
19Unil ń sìntīǹ u-ba taapu kí nīn bí biwɔfib kansikinee sɔ́ǹ u nì bilambidambi ń nīn yàkatī tigaajawan.
20Unil un yaa pílifí ti-Dindaan bɔtee, án làá bútí-u, un yaa máká ti-Dindaan puee bí mmɔnni.
21Unil un sòoǹ tibɔti nì iciinee ní bi yíì unyil. Dinyɔɔbummɔɔndi din u sòoǹee di kútí dinyil.
22Iciin sá kii nnyimbul ŋun tìì dimaŋfalee ní ki tīī un cáá-iee. Bigbaambi bi-ba gbaandi di dátí bi-tafal.
23Unil un cáá iciinee dàkafī ní kí nín sòoǹ, ní u-nyil mɔ̀tīi kútí tin u sòoǹee pu mpɔn.
24Dinyɔɔbummɔɔndi sá kii tisiilee ní, tì mɔ̄ kinyɔkɔn ní ki tìì ŋgbampɔn.
25Unil ŋūǹ kí dàkafì yii nsan ŋun u nóóyee ŋān̄, ama án dāá kúntée, ŋu cáǹ-u ŋkúmin ní.
26Ŋkùm di yàntī utɔntɔnli ń tɔ̄ ditundi, di sá yii u-pool di páb̀-u ú tɔ̄ ditundi.
27Unil un kaa bí tibanee dàkafī kí ŋá tikpitil ní, tibɔti tin nyēē u-nyɔkɔnee sèetī kii ŋŋmee ní.
28Biibiidaan jāantí binib, ní ubɔmbɔtukul yàkatī bibɔɔtiibi.
29Unil un ŋáań tipɔmbɔtee ŋmàtíǹ u-juti ní ki cáǹ-u nsaŋkpitin.
30Unil yaa dū u-nimbiliŋ ki ŋúb́ ki dākafì kí tɔ̄ atuŋkpiti, ní ki ŋmáaḿ u-nyunculiŋee, u pée ŋá tikpitil ki dóò dee.
31Tiyikpipin sá tinyool beefuuliiki ní, bin nóó deedee saŋŋuee di kāntí-kì.
32Unil un kaa gífí diŋuul malaayee jítiǹ ubaatandaan. Unil un ŋúb́ u-bee jítiǹ un di ŋūǹ kí já kí fōō kitimmɔŋee.
33Bi ŋūǹ kí tɔ̄ kasi tiba pu, ama ti-Dindaan di lèekī tin u là án ŋée.

english_text:
Our Thoughts Are Tested by the Lord
1A dry crust of bread eaten
in peace and quiet
is better than a feast eaten
where everyone argues.
2A wise slave
will be placed in charge
of a no-good child,
and that slave will be given
the same inheritance
that each child receives.
3Silver and gold are tested
by flames of fire;
our thoughts are tested
by the Lord.
4Troublemakers listen
to troublemakers,
and liars listen to liars.
5By insulting the poor,
you insult your Creator.
You will be punished
if you make fun
of someone in trouble.
6Grandparents are proud
of their grandchildren,
and children should be proud
of their parents.
7It sounds strange for a fool
to talk sensibly,
but it's even worse
for a ruler to tell lies.
8A bribe works miracles
like a magic charm
that brings good luck.
9You will keep your friends
if you forgive them,
but you will lose your friends
if you keep talking about
what they did wrong.
10A sensible person
accepts correction,
but you can't beat sense
into a fool.
11Cruel people want to rebel,
and so vicious attackers
will be sent against them.
12A bear robbed of her cubs
is far less dangerous
than a stubborn fool.
13You will always have trouble
if you are mean to those
who are good to you.
14The start of an argument
is like a water leak—
so stop it before
real trouble breaks out.
15The Lord doesn't like those
who defend the guilty
or condemn the innocent.
16Why should fools have money
for an education
when they refuse to learn?
17 A friend is there to help,
in any situation,
and relatives are born
to share our troubles.
18It's stupid to guarantee
someone else's loan.
19The wicked and the proud
love trouble and keep begging
to be hurt.
20Dishonesty does you no good,
and telling lies
will get you in trouble.
21It's never pleasant
to be the parent of a fool
and have nothing but pain.
22If you are cheerful,
you feel good;
if you are sad,
you hurt all over.
23Crooks accept secret bribes
to keep justice
from being done.
24Anyone with wisdom knows
what makes good sense,
but fools can never
make up their minds.
25Foolish children bring sorrow
and pain to their parents.
26It isn't fair
to punish the innocent
and those who do right.
27It makes a lot of sense
to be a person of few words
and to stay calm.
28 Even fools seem smart
when they are quiet.
translation_text:
1Laakin ní a làá ká kinɔkatii kikuliŋŋi kí pɔ̀kɔ̄ ní ŋgbansɔŋfi bée sɔ́ǹ dicindi din poon busamɔntiibu bun pu tinan pée gbí, ama ní kujaau bée.
2Uyumbu un wálifèe làá dāá fōō u-dindaan jipɔɔn un kɔ̄ntí-u icooyee paaŋŋu, ní u nì u-dindaan jipɔmbi ń dāá yàkatī difakal din u yóoǹ-bee.
3Ŋŋmi ní bi cáa cɔ́ŋkí kí béé animbil kúti timɔntiil nì sindaariyamɔnti, ama ti-Dindaan di cɔ́ŋkí unil pɔbil kí béé di nín sá diŋyee.
4Unikpiti pílifíǹ binib bin sòoǹ anyɔɔbuŋkpitee, ní unyimɔndaan pílifíǹ bin sòoǹ ki bíiĺ bi-jutiibee.
5Unil un bèel̄ usoodaanee sìí u-náanliu ní. Un juti yaa bí dinimbinaamandin an mɔ̄ǹ-uee kaa làá lóó ditafadaaldi.
6Bitikpilib naantiibi di yì bi-nyooti, ama ní bibaatiibi yì bi-jipɔmbi yati.
7Tibɔmɔntiil kaa máaǹ ugbaan, míǹ ní inyimɔn kaa máaǹ unil un bi tìì disíndee.
8Bin cáá tiwan kí pɔ̄ee ceeyee, tiwampɔkaal sá kii diyimɔɔl sabilee ní. Laakin pú ní u yaa fātèe, an bútí-u ní.
9Unil un súntí u-juti nín yìntīǹ-u puee kāntí bibɔɔtiibi, ama un pée téetí ki sòoǹ múlmulee yàkatī bibɔɔtiibi ní.
10Á wòoǹ unyil dibaba ja làá tɔ̄ u-ni ditundi ki jítiǹ á gbá ugbaan anaalab dilaataal.
11Unikpiti pée nyàab̀ kí nīn ŋáań tikpitil ŋma ní, ní un kaa ŋān̄ee bí ní ki gbì bin kíǹee taapu, ama bi làá dāá dū ntuun ŋun cáá ntoomee kí tɔ̄ u-pu.
12Á tū digbiŋgbil din biyaamu bi cúúyee nsanni sɔ́ǹ ugbaan un bí ki tūǹ agbaantuunee.
13Unil yaa dū tikpitil ki pàn̄ tiŋan tin bi ŋá-uee, u-dicaŋkun tikpitil làá nīn pée bí ní ki cá talku.
14Á kíĺ kunikpɔŋkpɔkɔu sá kii á pìitī nnyimbilkaam kí pɔ̄-mì nsan mí pùub̀ee ní. Dūú gbèen̄ kí taa yàntī án kpántí kujaau.
15Unil un pɔ̀ dibɔkpil daanee nì unil un kù ibaamɔndaan bɔtee, ti-Dindaan ná binib gbanti liitil.
16Animbil yaa bí ugbaan ŋaanee, u làá dūú ŋá nì ba? Ú cáá dā iciinaaa? Míǹ kaa bí u-yilin.
17Ubɔɔti dàkà u-neendi ŋyunti kamaa ní, ama kinabiki kíǹ bí kí tíkiń dinimbinaamandin ní.
18Unil un kaa cáá iciinee di fátí ubɔ ŋaan kí pòon̄ kí pà u-juti pɔndi.
19Un néeń kujaauee néeń ikpiti ní, un yòontí u-ba yilpuee dāa lítí.
20An kaa bútí milimilidaan, ní nnaabu làá jēetí un kaa sòoǹ ibaamɔnee pu.
21Un màl̄ ugbaanee pée bí kunimbaaun ŋma ní. Un kaa nyí tibee baa kaa ŋūǹ kí nīn bí mmɔnni.
22Dipɔɔpindi cāantí iween ní, ama kunimbaau bàtī unil pɔŋŋu ní.
23Unikpiti fòol̄ tiwampɔkaal dibalin, kí taa sòoǹ tibɔti ti-pú.
24Unyil nimbikpeeŋu pée cɔ́ iciin pu ní, ama ugbaan úǹ nimbikpeeŋu cɔ́ ndandati ní kaa wāĺ tiba.
25Ugbaan tìì u-baa kunimbaau, ní ki tìì u-na un màl̄-uee nnyɔɔtun.
26An kaa ŋān̄ bí dáaĺ maanyiiba tafal báà fiii pu, an kaa tí ŋān̄ yii bí gbá jilmadaan u-baamɔŋyi pu.
27Unil un kaa sòoǹ tikpilee di cáá iciin, ní un dàkafī kí nín sòoǹee di cáá dinyil.
28Ugbaan gba yaa kā ki ŋmí, a làá dū-u kí yíiń uciŋfiti ní. U yaa kā ki táb́ u-nyɔkɔ, a làá lì yii unyil ní.

english_text:
It's Wrong To Favor the Guilty
1It's selfish and stupid
to think only of yourself
and to sneer at people
who have sense.
2Fools have no desire to learn,
instead they would rather
give their own opinion.
3Wrongdoing leads to shame
and disgrace.
4Words of wisdom
are a stream that flows
from a deep fountain.
5It's wrong to favor the guilty
and keep the innocent
from getting justice.
6Foolish talk will get you
into a lot of trouble.
7Saying foolish things
is like setting a trap
to destroy yourself.
8There's nothing so delicious
as the taste of gossip!
It melts in your mouth.
9Being lazy is no different
from being a troublemaker.
10The Lord is a mighty tower
where his people can run
for safety—
11the rich think their money
is a wall of protection.
12Pride leads to destruction;
humility leads to honor.
13 It's stupid and embarrassing
to give an answer
before you listen.
14Being cheerful helps
when you are sick,
but nothing helps
when you give up.
15Everyone with good sense
wants to learn.
16A gift will get you in
to see anyone.
17You may think you have won
your case in court,
until your opponent speaks.
18Drawing straws is one way
to settle a difficult case.
19Making up with a friend
you have offended
is harder than breaking
through a city wall.
20Make your words good—
you will be glad you did.
21Words can bring death or life!
Talk too much, and you will eat
everything you say.
22 A man's greatest treasure
is his wife—
she is a gift from the Lord.
23The poor must beg for help,
but the rich can give
a harsh reply.
24Some friends don't help,
but a true friend is closer
than your own family.
translation_text:
1Unil un dàkafī u-baba puee kaa kàal̀ bin kíǹee cee, bi yaa là kí tūtuǹ-uee, ní ú gíí diŋuul.
2Tin mɔ̄ǹ ugbaanee kaa sá yii ú gbìl̄ tibɔti taapu, ama ú lēē u-landɔkɔi kí bíĺ mpaampiin pu.
3Atuŋkpiti di cāabìń kpeefam, ní icoo yàntī unil ń fá u-nyooti.
4Unil nyɔɔbuŋŋi sá kii nnyim min nyóòyee, mbun ŋun gbée nì nnyimbul ŋun nyim sá kii iciin ki pùub̀ee ní.
5An kaa ŋān̄ bí dī dibɔkpil daan boon kí sòoǹ kí kpɔ̀ deedeedaan un cáá ibaamɔnee bɔti.
6Ugbaan nyɔɔbuŋŋi cāabìń kunikpɔŋkpɔkɔu, ní tibɔti tin nyēē u-nyɔkɔnee dāa kúntí nì kujaau.
7Ugbaan nyɔkɔ di nàantí-u, u-nyɔɔbuŋŋi sàtī-u kii kutaliŋŋuee ní.
8Ubɔmbɔtukul nyɔɔbuŋŋi sá tijin tin mɔ̄ee ní, tì kóò unil poon ní fíŋfiŋ.
9Unil un ŋáań diwutijool u-tundinee nì unil un bíiĺ ditundee sá kuyuu nì ku-bukul ní.
10Ti-Dindaan yindi di wúń m-pu, deedeedaan yaa sáǹ kí kɔ́-uee, u bí ŋgbansɔŋfin ní.
11Ugaaja gaajati sá-u kii kitiŋ kin bi máń digundi ki túee ní. U-landɔkɔŋu poonee, tì sá digundi din fɔ̀kɔ̀ yilpu yilpu baa ŋūǹ kí dàb̄ee ní.
12Kí wàatī án nàan̄ unilee, u yòontí u-ba yilpu ní. Ama kí wàatī unil ń ká tinyoolee, see ú sìntī u-ba taapu.
13Unil un kíikí tibɔti kí wàatī kí nín gbìl̄-tèe dàkà u-gbaandi ní ki kɔ̄ntí u-ba icoo.
14Unil mákal di tīkintí-u u-weeŋyi poon, ama u yaa kaa ti cáá dimákalee, ŋma di gíti ŋūǹ kí tūtuǹ-u?
15Unil un cáá dinyilee kāntí dinyil ní, ní un cáá iciinee nyàab̀ iciin ki kútí.
16Tiwampɔkaal pìitī unil nsan ú ŋmā kí cù binikpaambi cee.
17Unil un péé ki sòon̄ tibɔtee yati di bí kii tì ŋān̄ee. Ama u nì un cáá tɔbee yaa sòon̄ u-yatee ní bí ká yii an nyáń ti-ba.
18Bi tòó kasi ní kí kúntí kujaau, ní kí pàtī bipɔɔbi.
19An pɔ̄ɔ̄ unil ń sòoǹ nì kinabiki kin u yīntèe ki jítiǹ ú já kí fōō kitiŋ kin bi máń digundi ki túee. Kujaau táb̀ unil nyɔkɔ kii kudii kun pɔ̄ɔ̄yee punuubee ní.
20Unil nyɔɔbuŋŋi di yì-tì ní ú ká kí jī. Tibɔti tin u sòoǹee di yàntī ní ú díkí.
21Ibɔsoon ŋūǹ kí cáań dimaŋfal àá ŋkúm, unil un néeń ki sòoǹee máaǹ kí kíí kí fōō isoon paati.
22Unil un ká unimpu ki cááyee ká tiwammɔntiil dee. An sá tiŋaŋkpaandi ní ti-Dindaan ŋá ki tīī-u.
23Unandaan sòoǹ ki gbàam̄, ama ní ugaaja kíikí nì mpɔn.
24Unil yaa cáá bibɔɔtiibi tikpilee, án ŋūǹ kí bīil̀-u, ama ubɔɔti ubɔ bí ki ŋūǹ kí nīn nákáǹ-si ki jītíǹ kinabiki.

english_text:
It's Wise To Be Patient
1It's better to be poor
and live right
than to be a stupid liar.
2Willingness and stupidity
don't go well together.
If you are too eager,
you will miss the road.
3We are ruined
by our own stupidity,
though we blame the Lord.
4The rich have many friends;
the poor have none.
5Dishonest witnesses and liars
won't escape punishment.
6Everyone tries to be friends
of those who can help them.
7If you are poor,
your own relatives reject you,
and your friends are worse.
When you really need them,
they are not there.
8Do yourself a favor
by having good sense—
you will be glad you did.
9Dishonest witnesses and liars
will be destroyed.
10It isn't right for a fool
to live in luxury
or for a slave to rule
in place of a king.
11It's wise to be patient
and show what you are like
by forgiving others.
12An angry king roars
like a lion,
but when a king is pleased,
it's like dew on the crops.
13Foolish children bring disgrace
to their fathers.
A nagging wife goes on and on
like the drip, drip, drip
of the rain.
14You may inherit all you own
from your parents,
but a sensible wife
is a gift from the Lord.
15If you are lazy
and sleep your time away,
you will starve.
16Obey the Lord's teachings
and you will live—
disobey and you will die.
17Caring for the poor
is lending to the Lord,
and you will be well repaid.
18Correct your children
before it's too late;
if you don't punish them,
trouble will come their way.
19People with bad tempers
are always in trouble,
and they need help
over and over again.
20Pay attention to advice
and accept correction,
so you can live sensibly.
21We may make a lot of plans,
but the Lord will do
what he has decided.
22What matters most is loyalty.
It's better to be poor
than to be a liar.
23Showing respect to the Lord
brings true life—
if you do it, you can relax
without fear of danger.
24Some people are too lazy
to lift a hand
to feed themselves.
25Stupid fools learn good sense
by seeing others punished;
a sensible person learns
by being corrected.
26Disgraceful children
rob their father
and chase their mother away.
