27If you stop learning,
you will forget
what you already know.
28A lying witness makes fun
of the court system,
and criminals think crime
is really delicious.
29A stupid fool should expect
to be punished.
translation_text:
1Unil un sá usoodaan ki còom̄ deedee saŋŋunee sɔ́ǹ unil un di sá unyimɔndaan ki sá ugbaanee.
2An kaa ŋān̄ unil ń nīn bí kaa cáá nlandɔkɔ. Unil un di jìkì tikpilee làá lítí ikpitin.
3Unil u-ba gbaandi yaa nāaǹ-uee, ní ú dūú nyìntī ti-Dindaan pu.
4Tigaajati yàntī unil bɔɔbi mɔ̀tīi wīintí ní, ama ní unandaan úǹ nì u-bɔɔ ń yàkatīǹ tɔbin.
5Unil un lèekī nnyimɔn seerauee kaa làá lóó ditafadaaldi, ní unil un mɔ́ntée kaa làá nyā ditafadaaldin.
6Binib tikpil cáá nyɔɔmálmal ki ŋmàtíǹ binikpaambi, ní báà ŋma bɔɔ sá unil un pūǹee.
7Usoodaan nabiyaamu kɔkɔ kaa là u-bɔti, míǹ ní u-bɔɔbi mun sáń ki wàatī-u. U yaa bàà là kí sòoǹ nì bee, baa bí.
8Unil un yaa cáá iciinee néeń u-ba. Un di yaa pɔ́ɔǹ kí gbìl̄ tibɔti taapuee làá gbìl̄ mmɔn.
9Unil un lèekī nnyimɔn seerauee kaa làá lóó ditafadaaldi, ní án làá nàan̄ unil un mɔ́ntée.
10An kaa kítì yii ugbaan ń nīn bí mmɔnni, míǹ ní uyumbu kaa máaǹ kí nīn cáá bikpootiliibi pu mpɔn.
11Unil un cáá dinyilee kaa gífí diŋuul malaa, tin yì u-nyootee di sá u súntí tin bi yīntiǹ-uee pu.
12Ubɔti yaa gíí diŋuulee, an bí kii gbikinti nín sūǹ puee ní. Ama u-ŋanti sá kii dimalindi nín tòó kumoou pu puee ní.
13Ugbaan sá dinimbinaamandi ní ki tīī u-baa. Unimpubɔmbɔdaan sá kii nnyim min còol̀ kaa gúǹee ní.
14Unil ŋūǹ kí jī u-baabi diiku nì animbil difakal, ama ti-Dindaan di tìì uninja unimpu un cáá iciinee.
15Diwutijool cāabìń ŋgeem, ní ŋkùm cútí un kā ki kpàl̄ iŋalee.
16Unil un tɔ́ marabee wúń u-maŋfal pu ní. Un kaa kpèé u-bimbim tiŋanee làá kpú ní.
17Unil un yaa pú unandaan tiwanee pīnnì ti-Dindaan ní, di sá yii ti-Dindaan làá dāá téeǹ-u.
18Dáaĺ a-biki tafal ŋyunti ŋun dimákal dáá béé, ama á taa nín gíí diŋuul kí tin nyàab̀ kí kpɔ̀-kì ní.
19Unil un yaa gíí diŋuul ŋkpitim puee máaǹ kí pà dipɔndi. Di sá yii a yaa yāntì-uee, a bíi tìì-u kunyannyaau ú fàtīí kíĺ dee.
20Pīlifì isaŋki, kí kíí bí dàkà-si ní kí kpántí uciŋfiti.
21Unil pɔbil poonee, u bɔ́ntí tiwan tikpil tin u làá ŋée, ama ti-Dindaan nín là puee di làá dāá pée ŋá.
22Tin bi cí kí ká unil ceeyee di sá u-niti. An ŋān̄ unil ń nīn sá usoodaan ki jítiǹ ú nīn sá unyimɔndaan.
23Unil ń fàŋkì ti-Dindaanee tìì dimaŋfal. Udaan làá nīn bí digbilin ní kaa làá gbìl̄ tibɔkpitil tiba pu.
24Uwutijoodaan dùŋfī u-ŋal kí bɔ̄ disambilin, ama ní kaa ŋūǹ kí gíiǹní-ŋu u-nyɔkɔn.
25A yaa gbáń ulambidaanee, un kaa nyí tibee kíǹ ki nyí nì u-ba ní. A yaa wòon̄ uciŋfitee, u làá bīfì iciin kí kūtì ní.
26Kibiki kin sāaǹ ki-baa ki jìn̄ ki-nee sá kibiki kin bíil̀-bi ki kɔ́ǹ-bi icooyee ní.
27M-biki, a yaa gbēeǹ kaa ti bíi pílifí isaŋkee, a fātì a-boon ki tīī dinyil dee.
28A yaa yíiń maabiiban ń dāá lēē seerayee, waa dù deedee bɔti ki yíiń tiba. Tikpitil ní binikpitib jīǹ ki bí.
29Bi bɔ́ntì ditafadaaldi ki cíitì bilambidambi, ní ki bɔ́ntì bigbaambi boon ki cíitì tigbati.

english_text:
Words of Wisdom Are Better than Gold
1It isn't smart to get drunk!
Drinking makes a fool of you
and leads to fights.
2An angry ruler
is like a roaring lion—
make either one angry,
and you are dead.
3It makes you look good
when you avoid a fight—
only fools love to quarrel.
4If you are too lazy to plow,
don't expect a harvest.
5Someone's thoughts may be
as deep as the ocean,
but if you are smart,
you will discover them.
6There are many who say,
“You can trust me!”
But can they be trusted?
7Good people live right,
and God blesses the children
who follow their example.
8When rulers decide cases,
they weigh the evidence.
9Can any of us really say,
“My thoughts are pure,
and my sins are gone”?
10Two things the Lord hates
are dishonest scales
and dishonest measures.
11The good or bad
that children do
shows what they are like.
12Hearing and seeing
are gifts from the Lord.
13If you sleep all the time,
you will starve;
if you get up and work,
you will have enough food.
14Everyone likes to brag
about getting a bargain.
15Sensible words are better
than gold or jewels.
16You deserve to lose your coat
if you loan it to someone
to guarantee payment
for the debt of a stranger.
17The food you get by cheating
may taste delicious,
but it turns to gravel.
18Be sure you have sound advice
before making plans
or starting a war.
19Stay away from gossips—
they tell everything.
20Children who curse their parents
will go to the land of darkness
long before their time.
21Getting rich quick
may turn out to be a curse.
22Don't try to get even.
Trust the Lord,
and he will help you.
23The Lord hates dishonest scales
and dishonest weights.
So don't cheat!
24How can we know
what will happen to us
when the Lord alone decides?
25Don't fall into the trap
of making promises to God
before you think!
26A wise ruler severely punishes
every criminal.
27Our inner thoughts are a lamp
from the Lord,
and they search our hearts.
28Rulers are protected
by God's mercy and loyalty,
but they must be merciful
for their kingdoms to last.
29Young people take pride
in their strength,
but the gray hairs of wisdom
are even more beautiful.
30A severe beating can knock all
of the evil out of you!
translation_text:
1Ndaam yàntī unil ń kpántí ulambidaan, ní ndaam min pɔ̄ɔ̄yee yàntī ú kpántí kufuudaan. Unil un nyù-mì tikpilee kaa cáá iciin.
2Ubɔti yaa gíí diŋuulee, an bí kii gbikinti nín sūǹ puee ní. Unil un yaa gbítì ubɔti ŋuulee nyàab̄ tibɔti ki tɔ́ u-ba pu ní.
3An sá jilma ní ki tīī unil un yíití kunikpɔŋkpɔkɔuee. Ama ugbaan úǹ néeń kujaau ní.
4Ukpaayoon yaa kaa kùn̄ tikpaal ti-yuntiŋu, waa dāa kāntí tiba kí cā kudiceeu.
5Unil landɔkɔi sá kii lɔkɔ un nyóòyee nyim ní. Unil un cáá dinyilee di ŋūǹ kí dáaĺ-i kí nyāntí.
6Binib tikpil lì yii bíǹ di sá bimɔntiibi. Ama ŋma di baasii ŋūǹ kí ká unil un bí deedeeyee?
7Deedeedaan còom̄ deedee saŋŋu ní, u-kpátam boonee u-biyaamu làá nīn bí mmɔnni!
8Ubɔti yaa kāl̀ kubɔsoondiin kí sòoǹ tibɔtee, dicilpu malaayee, u kpáàa pée wál̀ tin kaa ŋān̄ee.
9Ŋma ŋūǹ kí lì yii: <M fíntì m-pɔbil píil̀ káŋkaŋ, m fíntì m-ba ki nyáń m-kpitiin?>
10Unil ń nīn cáá ataŋkpee ŋin bi cáa ŋmàntī tiwan nyiŋfiŋuee nì tiwaŋŋmantikaal mili mili pu kí nīn cáa mùul̄ee, an sá tiwan tin ti-Dindaan née ní.
11Kibiki tuuŋŋi pu ní unil béetí yii kun kì ŋée ŋān̄ ki bí deedee.
12Ti-Dindaan di náań atafal bí nīn cáa pílifí nì animbil bí nīn cáa kpèé.
13Taa nín̄ néeń ŋgeem, a làá dāá kpántí usoodaan. Nín̄ wāĺ ní kí ká kí jī kí díkí.
14Uwandal lì yii: <Tiwan pɔ̄ɔ̄ kudaau>, ama u yaa līkiǹee ní u kíǹ ki pàkà u-ba yii an mɔ̄ kudaau.
15Sindaariya gbōō, ní abeedimbil dɔ̄ tilèel, ama iciin nyɔɔbuŋŋi di sá tin pée cáá kunyampoouee.
16Unil yaa yúl̀ unil un waa nyée boon kí pìnnì tibee, á fōō u-bɔkutil kí yóoń. U nín yúl̀ unicaan boonee puee, á fōō u-cee toolima kí yóoń.
17Tinaayujin dá láá mɔ̄ unil nyɔkɔn ní. Ama boon kinyɔkɔ yaa gbée, an kpántí itaŋkpabiiti ní.
18Isaŋki di yàntī unil ń ŋmā kí ŋá tin u bɔ́ntèe. A yaa làá cù kujaauee, a bɔ́ntí tiŋan ní.
19Unil un cāab̀ u-juti disambiilee kaa bāal̀ tibɔti. Á taa nín̄ nōotí unil un di néeń kubɔcaauee.
20Unil un di yaa kpēē ki sīŋkiǹ u-baa nì u-nee, u làá kpú kii fitila nín kúù dibɔmbɔndin puee ní.
21Unil yaa jíń difakal malaayee, kí dāá kúntée, dàa cáá dibiindi.
22Taa lì yii a làá téeǹ ikpiti in bi ŋá-see. Nín̄ pée máká ti-Dindaan pu, u làá dāá fīī-si.
23Ti-Dindaan ná tiwaŋŋmantikaal tin kaa bí deedeeyee. Saniya un kaa ŋmàntī tiwan deedeeyee mun kaa ŋān̄ u-cee.
24Ti-Dindaan di kpòotī unil u-saŋkindi poon. Nisaaleen làá ŋá mana kí béé laakin u cée.
25An sá kutaliŋŋu ní unil ń lì u-nyɔkɔn fám yii: <M dū tiwan nee ki sú Unimbɔti,> àá kí pòon̄ Unimbɔti ipoon kí wàatī kí nín dàkafì.
26Ubɔti un cáá iciinee béetí kí gàntì binikpitib malaa, ní kí yàntī bí dáaĺ bi-tafal ŋkpitim pu.
27Unil fam sá fitila ní ti-Dindaan dūu tīī-u, ú nīn cáa ŋmíntí ki wāĺ u-poon fɔ́ŋfɔŋ.
28Ubɔti ŋanti nì u-baamɔŋyi di wúń u-pu, tiŋan tin u ŋáańee di tíkí u-beejal.
29Mpɔn di sá binipɔmbi nyooti, ní tiyikpipin sá bitikpilib nyaaŋku.
30Tigbati buuŋyi sá tikpitil nyɔkɔŋu ní, míǹ mbaantiim ní i kóò kí bà unil poon fɔ́ŋfɔŋ.

english_text:
The Lord Is In Charge
1 The Lord controls rulers,
just as he determines
the course of rivers.
2We may think we are doing
the right thing,
but the Lord always knows
what is in our hearts.
3Doing what is right and fair
pleases the Lord
more than an offering.
4Evil people are proud
and arrogant,
but sin is the only crop
they produce.
5If you plan and work hard,
you will have plenty;
if you hurry to get rich,
you will end up poor.
6Cheating to get rich
is a foolish dream
and no less than suicide.
7You destroy yourself
by being cruel and violent
and refusing to live right.
8All crooks are liars,
but anyone who is innocent
will do right.
9 It's better to stay outside
on the roof of your house
than to live inside
with a nagging wife.
10Evil people want to do wrong,
even to their friends.
11An ignorant fool learns
by seeing others punished;
a sensible person learns
by being instructed.
12God is always fair!
He knows what the wicked do
and will punish them.
13If you won't help the poor,
don't expect to be heard
when you cry out for help.
14A secret bribe will save you
from someone's fierce anger.
15When justice is done,
good citizens are glad
and crooks are terrified.
16If you stop using good sense,
you will find yourself
in the grave.
17Heavy drinkers and others
who live only for pleasure
will lose all they have.
18God's people will escape,
but all who are wicked
will pay the price.
19It's better out in the desert
than at home with a nagging,
complaining wife.
20Be sensible and store up
precious treasures—
don't waste them
like a fool.
21If you try to be kind and good,
you will be blessed with life
and goodness and honor.
22One wise person can defeat
a city full of soldiers
and capture their fortress.
23Watching what you say
can save you
a lot of trouble.
24If you are proud and conceited,
everyone will say,
“You're a snob!”
25If you want too much
and are too lazy to work,
it could be fatal.
26But people who obey God
are always generous.
27 The Lord despises the offerings
of wicked people
with evil motives.
28If you tell lies in court,
you are done for;
only a reliable witness
can do the job.
29Wicked people bluff their way,
but God's people think
before they take a step.
30No matter how much you know
or what plans you make,
you can't defeat the Lord.
31Even if your army has horses
ready for battle,
the Lord will always win.
translation_text:
1Ubɔti pɔbil sá kii mbunee ní ti-Dindaan ŋaan, ní laakin pú ní u yaa lèe, ú kpòotī-dì kí túĺ.
2Unil dàkafī yii tin kɔkɔ u ŋáańee ŋān̄ ní, ama un nyí tin kā unil pɔbilinee di sá ti-Dindaan.
3Mbimbim min ŋān̄ ki bí deedeeyee ŋān̄ ti-Dindaan cee ki jítiǹ saraabi.
4Dibadakal nì dilambil di sá tin lèekī binikpitib kpitii ki dàkēe.
5Ufaŋgiifiti landɔkɔi kɔ̄ntí-u digbilin ní, ama kujinjikilaapaau daan kóò disoolin ní.
6Binib bin mɔ́ntì inyimɔn ki ká tigaajatee sá bin sáń ki kóò ŋkúm ŋaanee ní. Bi kāntí tiwan tin kaa bí tiban kaa yúntée ní.
7Tipɔmbɔti tin binikpitib ŋáańee di kù-bi, kun puee bi yíì kí tɔ̄ deedee tuuŋŋi.
8Unikpiti nóó nsan ŋun gɔ́ĺee ní, ama maanyiiba úǹ nóó nsan ŋun tèen̄ee ní.
9An sɔ́ á nīn kóò digunlɔkɔlin ki jítiǹ si nì unimpu un néeń kujaauee ń nīn kóò.
10Unikpiti úǹ pée nyàab̀ kí ŋá ikpiti ŋma ní, waa sūǹ u-bɔɔ gba saai.
11Bi yaa dáaĺ ulambidaan tafalee, un kaa nyí tibee cíikí ní. Bi yaa dàkā uciŋfitee, u-nyil mɔ̀tīi kútí ní.
12Deedeedaan nyí tin jītí unikpiti dicaŋkunee. U làá téé-bi kí tɔ̄ nnaabun.
13Unil un yaa kpáá u-tafal kaa pílifì unandaan kuŋkuuntiiyee, u mun yaa láa bíi kūuntí ki nyàab̀ dijòońdee, baa làá dāá pīlifiǹ-u.
14Tiwan tin bi yaa pú unil un gíí diŋuulee dibalinee sɔ̀ŋkī dipɔbil ní. Tiwampɔkaal tin a dūu nēeǹ udaan lookunee sɔ̀ŋkī diŋuul ní.
15Kí ŋá tin tèen̄ee sá mmɔn ní ki tīī deedeedaan, ama ní ki sá tifaandi ki tīī bikpitiŋaliibi.
16Unil un yaa kākatì u-ba ki wāatì dinyil saŋŋuee làá cùú ŋàl̄ bitaŋkpiibi ní.
17Unil un néeń ki jīǹ mmɔnee làá kpántí usoodaan. Un néeń ki nyù ndaam ki jīǹ tijin tin mèeǹee kpá kí kpántí ugaaja.
18Unikpiti làá fōō deedeedaan paaŋŋu kí kɔ́ nnaabun, ní biibiidaan ń fōō ibaamɔndaan paaŋŋu.
19An sɔ́ unil ń nīn kóò u-baba kuteeun ki jítiǹ u nì unimpu un néeń kujaau u-nyɔkɔ pɔ̄ɔ̄yee ń nīn kóò.
20Uciin dumpuee, tigaajamɔntiil nì ŋkpam bí ní, ama ugbaan úǹ yati kaa dɔ̀.
21Unil un nyàab̀ kí nīn nóó deedee saŋŋu ki ŋáań tiŋanee làá dāá ká mmaŋfafɔkɔn nì deedee nì tinyool.
22Uciŋfiti ŋūǹ ki kɔ́ bibaatandambi tiŋkin, kí gbá kí wīī digundi din bi máń ki tú-kì bi máká di-puee.
23Unil un ŋúb́ u-nyɔkɔ nì u-limbilee nyāntí u-ba tibɔtin ní.
24Kpeefam daan di cáá dilambil ní ki dàkà u-ba, tin kamaa ní u yaa ŋáańee, dibadakal di līī.
25Tin uwutijoodaan bàà là ní kaa ŋūǹ kí kée di yì u-kúm, di sá yii waa kíikí kí dū u-ŋalii kí tɔ̄ ditundi.
26Ŋyunti kamaayee u-nimbiliŋ pée máń tiwan pu ní, ama deedeedaan úǹ pūǹ kaa kpáàa dàkafī u-ba pu.
27Binikpitib saraau sá ntimbiil ní, ŋma nín yíiń bí ŋá an saraabi nì ilandɔkɔkpiti.
28Unil un lèekī nnyimɔn seerauee làá kpú, ama unil un gbìl̄ tibɔtee yaa làá sòoǹee, bi yàntī ú sòoǹ ní.
29Unikpiti ŋáań kii u máká u-ba puee, ama ní deedeedaan úǹ máká u-saŋkindi pu.
30Unil ciiŋyi àá u-nyil àá u-landɔkɔŋu kaa bí tiban ti-Dindaan nimbiin.
31Bi bɔ́ntí utaamu kí yóoń dikɔ̀ndi wiiŋŋu pu ní, ama dijajil díǹ nyēeń ti-Dindaan baba cee ní.

english_text:
The Value of a Good Reputation
1A good reputation and respect
are worth much more
than silver and gold.
2The rich and the poor
are all created
by the Lord.
3When you see trouble coming,
don't be stupid
and walk right into it—
be smart and hide.
4Respect and serve the Lord!
Your reward will be wealth,
a long life, and honor.
5Crooks walk down a road
full of thorny traps.
Stay away from there!
6 Teach your children
right from wrong,
and when they are grown
they will still do right.
7The poor are ruled by the rich,
and those who borrow
are slaves of moneylenders.
8Troublemakers get in trouble,
and their terrible anger
will get them nowhere.
9The Lord blesses everyone
who freely gives food
to the poor.
10Arguments and fights
will come to an end,
if you chase away those
who insult others.
11The king is the friend of all
who are sincere
and speak with kindness.
12The Lord watches over everyone
who shows good sense,
but he frustrates the plans
of deceitful liars.
13Don't be so lazy that you say,
“If I go to work,
a lion will eat me!”
14The words of a bad woman
are like a deep pit;
if you make the Lord angry,
you will fall right in.
15All children are foolish,
but firm correction
will make them change.
16Cheat the poor to make profit
or give gifts to the rich—
either way you lose.
Thirty Wise Sayings
17Here are some sayings
of people with wisdom,
so listen carefully
as I teach.
18You will be glad
that you know these sayings
and can recite them.
19I am teaching them today,
so that you
may trust the Lord.
20I have written thirty sayings
filled with sound advice.
21You can trust them completely
to give you the right words
for those in charge of you.
–1–
22Don't take advantage
of the poor
or cheat them in court.
23The Lord is their defender,
and what you do to them,
he will do to you.
–2–
24Don't make friends with anyone
who has a bad temper.
25You might turn out like them
and get caught in a trap.
–3–
26Don't guarantee to pay
someone else's debt.
27If you don't have the money,
you might lose your bed.
–4–
28Don't move a boundary marker
set up by your ancestors.
–5–
29If you do your job well,
you will work for a ruler
and never be a slave.
translation_text:
1Diyimmɔntiil jítiǹ tigaajakpaandi, disíndi jítiǹ sindaariya nì animbil kúti.
2Ugaaja nì usoodaan sá ubaanti ní, ti-Dindaan di pée náań bi-liitil kɔkɔ.
3Un nyíǹ u-bee yaa ká nnaabu dòońee, u sáń kí báĺ ní. Ama bin kaa nyí tibee cáǹ bi-ba kí tɔ̄ poon ní án píĺ-bi.
4Unil un sīntì u-ba taapuee fàŋkí ti-Dindaan ní. U-paatii di sá tigaajati nì tinyool nì mmaŋfafɔkɔn.
5Ikuŋkum nì titalindi bí milimilidaan saŋŋu pu ní, un là kí fīī u-maŋfalee gɔ́ntí an wanti ní.
6Dàkà kibiki nsan ŋun kì máaǹ kí nóóyee, báà kì yaa láa púĺ, kì kpá kí fá-ŋu.
7Ugaaja cáá mpɔn bisoodambi pu, ní un jíń dipɔndee sá un u jíń dipɔndee yumbuu.
8Unil un yaa búĺ tin kaa bí deedeeyee, agìŋ́kpaan ní u làá cā, di sá yii mpɔn ŋun u cáa ŋáań tipɔmbɔtee làá kúntí.
9Unil un cáá tinitee làá ká Unimbɔti biindi, di sá yii u kpīintí unandaan.
10Jà ulambidaan ní kunikpɔŋkpɔkɔu ń gbèen̄, mimmee kujaau nì asiibil mun kúntì dee.
11Un néeń unil un pɔbil bí diba nì Unimbɔti ní ki sòoǹ nì dineendee bɔɔ di sá ubɔti.
12Ti-Dindaan nimbiliŋ pée bá dinyil pu ní, ama waa fòol̄ biibiidambi bíǹ nyɔɔbuŋŋi.
13Uwutijoodaan di lì yii: «Gbikinti bí mmɔŋki! M yaa nyáń u làá tin cúú-mi nsanni!»
14Ubɔ nimpuu nyɔkɔ sá kpaalaa ní, unil un ti-Dindaan dūu fée di jēetí u-poon.
15Digbaandi jíń kibiki pɔbilin. Mbambaan ŋun bi cáa dátí ki-tafalee di nyāntí-kì digbaandin.
16Bi yaa bíi wɔ́b̀ unandaanee, bi bíi tìì-u tigaajati ní, bi yaa tí pú ugaaja tiwanee, bi bíi kɔ̄ntí-u disool ní.
Tibɔkpaafikaal tiba mun
17Kpòon̄ a-tafal kí pīlifì biciŋfitiibi bɔti, pìitī a-pɔbil kí fōō tin m nyí kí dàkà-see. 18A yaa dū-tì ki kpáafì a-pɔbilin ní ki yaa nyí-tì ki yóoǹ, án làá mɔ̄ɔkiǹ-si. 19M là á dū a-mákal kí ŋá ti-Dindaan ni ní. An pu ní m làá dū tibɔti gbanti kí dàkà si mun díǹ. 20M ŋmàn̄-si alaŋkpan mmuŋku nì saalaa ŋin sá isaŋki nì dinyilee. 21Ŋi làá dàkà-si tin ŋān̄ ki sá ibaamɔnee, án nín làá ŋá pu bi yaa tú-see, á sòoǹ tibɔti ti-púee.
22Taa fūkul̀ uwɔfi wanti yii u nín sá uwɔfee pu, kí taa wɔ́b́ unandaan ibɔsoon laŋki, u nín kaa cáá ubɔee pu. 23Di sá yii ti-Dindaan di làá dāá mɔ̄tì bi-pu, ní kí dāá lēē binib bin fìkī-bee maŋfal.
24Taa bɔ́ɔtí unil un cáá diŋuulee. Taa nīn tāatí unil un fòol̄ mbum malaayee. 25Yaa sá fám a làá fōō bi-bimbikpitim, ní án sàl̄-si kii kutaliŋŋuee.
26Taa fáá ubɔ ŋaan kí pòon̄ kí pà a-juti pɔndi. 27A yaa kaa ká kí téeǹee, a dāa dɔ̄ a-lambaŋki pu ní bí dāá cúú kí tíkití.
28Taa cóotí ditaŋkpal din a-baabi nìn cóoǹ kikpaanyɔkɔee kí nìkī.
29Kpèè unil un di nyí u-tundi tiŋanee. U ŋūǹ kí cù bibɔtiibi cee kí tɔ̄ ditundi. Waa làá nīn sá utɔntɔnli un pu baa nyée.

english_text:
–6–
1When you are invited
to eat with a king,
use your best manners.
2Don't go and stuff yourself!
That would be just the same
as cutting your throat.
3Don't be greedy for all
of that fancy food!
It may not be so tasty.
–7–
4Give up trying so hard
to get rich.
5Your money flies away
before you know it,
just like an eagle
suddenly taking off.
–8–
6Don't accept an invitation
to eat a selfish person's food,
no matter how good it is.
7People like that take note
of how much you eat.
They say, “Take all you want!”
But they don't mean it.
8Each bite will come back up,
and all your kind words
will be wasted.
–9–
9Don't talk to fools—
they will make fun of you.
–10–
10Don't move a boundary marker
or take the land
that belongs to orphans.
11God All-Powerful is there
to defend them against you.
–11–
12Listen to instruction
and do your best to learn.
–12–
13Don't fail to correct
your children.
You won't kill them
by being firm,
14and it may even
save their lives.
–13–
15My children,
if you show good sense,
I will be happy,
16and if you are truthful,
I will really be glad.
–14–
17Don't be jealous of sinners,
but always honor the Lord.
18Then you will truly have hope
for the future.
–15–
19Listen to me, my children!
Be wise and have enough sense
to follow the right path.
20Don't be a heavy drinker
or stuff yourself with food.
21It will make you feel drowsy,
and you will end up poor
with only rags to wear.
–16–
22Pay attention to your father,
and don't neglect your mother
when she grows old.
23Invest in truth and wisdom,
discipline and good sense,
and don't part with them.
24Make your father truly happy
by living right and showing
sound judgment.
25Make your parents proud,
especially your mother.
–17–
26My son, pay close attention,
and gladly follow
my example.
27Bad women and unfaithful wives
are like a deep pit—
28they are waiting to attack you
like a gang of robbers
with victim after victim.
–18–
29Who is always in trouble?
Who argues and fights?
Who has cuts and bruises?
Whose eyes are red?
30Everyone who stays up late,
having just one more drink.
31Don't even look
at that colorful stuff
bubbling up in the glass!
It goes down so easily,
32but later it bites
like a poisonous snake.
33You will see weird things,
and your mind
will play tricks on you.
34You will feel tossed about
like someone trying to sleep
on a ship in a storm.
35You will be bruised all over,
without even remembering
how it all happened.
And you will lie awake asking,
“When will morning come,
so I can drink some more?”
translation_text:
1Sii nì unikpaan yaa kāl̀ kí jī tijinee, á nīn nyíǹ a-ba nì un kā a-nimbiinee. 2A yaa kpàà jīǹ tikpilee, á bàtī a-pool pu. 3Taa yàntī u-jinti gbanti ń cúú-si nnimbitaataam. Tì ŋūǹ kí nīn sá-si kutaliŋŋu.
4Taa bìǹ kí nyàab̀ tigaajati, pée lēē a-landɔkɔŋu an pu. 5A tin lì yii a-nimbil pāantí tigaajati puee, tì wáŋkì. Di sá yii tì túkù ifeen kii ukaalunee ní kí kɔ́ kutaa.
6Á taa jī ukummunti jinti, ní kí taa yàntī u-jimmɔntiiti ń cúú-si nnimbitaataam. 7Di sá yii waa sá un ní ni dàkafī yii u sée. U làá pée tùkù-si yii: <Jī kí nyɔ̀>, ama waa sòoǹ nì míǹ nì dipɔbil diba. 8A làá wùliŋkì tijin tin a jíńee kɔkɔ kí fá, ní anyɔɔbummɔnti ŋin a sòon̄-uee ń kúntíǹ fám.
9Taa sàaǹ a-ba yii a bíi kútí ugbaan tibɔti, kun puee u làá kpèè iciin nyɔɔbuŋŋi ŋin a sòoǹee fám ní.
10Taa cóotí ditaŋkpal din bi cóoǹ kikpaanyɔkɔee kí nìkī, kí kɔ́ kí fōō ataŋkpiibil kpaatanti. 11Di sá yii Unimbɔti un mɔ́tí bi-puee sá mpɔndaan ní. Úǹ di làá yūĺ bi-boon kí sòoǹ kí pɔ̀-bi ní kí kpɔ̀ a-bɔti.
12Pìitī a-pɔbil kí fōō tin ní bi dàkà-see, ní kí ŋátí a-tafaliŋ kí pīlifì tin bi bíi bífí-see.
13Taa gùkufì kí dáaĺ kibiki tafal. A yaa dū mbambaan ki gbáń-kì, kàa làá kpú. 14A yaa gbáń-kì nì mbambaanee gba ní a làá fīī-kì kí nyāntí ditaŋkpiilin.
Isaŋki in ubaati tìì u-jipɔɔnee
15M-biki, a-pɔbilin a yaa cáá iciinee, ma mun pɔbil làá nīn pīiǹ ní. 16Án làá nīn baasii mɔ̄ǹ-mi tikpil, a yaa bíi sòoǹ deedee bɔtee.
17Taa nín cáá bikpitiŋaliibi pu nnimbitaataam a-pɔbilin, ama kutaa kamaayee, á nīn fàŋkí ti-Dindaan. 18Niinee a-foolbooŋwu làá nīn ŋān̄, ní dimákal din a cááyee kaa làá gbíntí fám.
19M-biki, pīlifiǹ-mi kí kpántí uciŋfiti, ní kí nīn nóó deedee saŋŋu. 20Taa nín̄ tāatí binib bin nyù ndaam tikpilee, àá binib bin néeń ki sàfī tinanee. 21Di sá yii disool cútí udanyɔgbil nì unaŋŋmɔl, ní unil un néeń ŋgeemee dāa pèentí ikpalcati.
22Pīlifiǹ a-baa un di màl̄-see, kí taa kpèè a-na fám yii u nín púĺee pu. 23Nyàab̀ kí ká ibaamɔn nì iciin nì nlandɔkɔmɔnti nì dinyil. A yaa ká tiwan gbantee, á ŋúb́-tì tiŋan. 24An mɔ̄ǹ deedeedaan baa ki tin lákatì, ní unil un màl̄ uciŋfitee fàal̀. 25Yàntī a-baa nì a-na ń nīn fàal̀, ní kí yàntī a-na un màl̄-see ń nīn bí dipɔɔpindin.
26M-biki, dū a-pɔbil kí tīī-mi, ní kí yàntī m-bimbim ń nīn sá-si ŋabika. 27Á nīn nyí yii kinimpulaakpaai sá kpaalaa, ní ubɔ nimpuu sá lɔkɔ un nyɔkɔ kaa wāāyee. 28Bi mun nākantí ki cí kii digaŋgandambee. Aa ŋūǹ kí kàaǹ bininjab bin an nimpoobee yāntì bi nyáń bi-nimpoobi boonee.
Udanyɔgbil bítam
29Ŋma bí falaa poon? Ŋma bí iyaliŋki poon? Ŋma néeń kujaau? Ŋma bí ki gbáà diniindi an kaa kúntí? Ŋma fòol̄ tiweendi fám? Ŋma nimbiliŋ máǹ cínciŋee? 30An sá bin kàal̀ ndaam taapu ki yúntée, an sá bin ŋmàlintí idafi in pɔ̄ɔ̄yee ki nyùee. 31Á taa kpèè ndaam nyaaŋku nì mì nín tòó cábcab pu kuyuunee. A yaa nyù-mèe, mì sìntī ní soooo a-neen. 32Án dāa kúntée, mì dāa júntí-si kii ukoobuee ní, a lì kii ukoowaati nín júntí puee. 33A-nimbiliŋ dāa kíǹ ki kpèé ki wāĺ maamaaci wanti, ní a kíǹ ki sòoǹ fám fám. 34Án dāa bí-si kii unil un dɔ̄ tiŋku kansikinee, àá unil un lúń ndɔ ŋun pu bi sàkantí meela satau yilpu kúnti kuntee ní. 35A làá lì yii: «Bi gbáń-mi, ama an kaa píĺ-mi! Bi tāfì-mi tiŋan, ama maa gbìl̄ tiba! Ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu ní m làá fìntī ní kí gíti bàlifì bí cáań-mi ní?»

english_text:
–19–
1Don't be jealous of crooks
or want to be their friends.
2All they think about
and talk about
is violence and cruelty.
–20–
3Use wisdom and understanding
to establish your home;
4let good sense fill the rooms
with priceless treasures.
–21–
5Wisdom brings strength,
and knowledge gives power.
6Battles are won
by listening to advice
and making a lot of plans.
–22–
7Wisdom is too much for fools!
Their advice is no good.
–23–
8No one but troublemakers
think up trouble.
9Everyone hates senseless fools
who think up ways to sin.
–24–
10Don't give up and be helpless
in times of trouble.
–25–
11Don't fail to rescue those
who are doomed to die.
12Don't say, “I didn't know it!”
God can read your mind.
He watches each of us
and knows our thoughts.
And God will pay us back
for what we do.
–26–
13Honey is good for you,
my children,
and it tastes sweet.
14Wisdom is like honey
for your life—
if you find it,
your future is bright.
–27–
15Don't be a cruel person
who attacks good people
and hurts their families.
16Even if good people
fall seven times,
they will get back up.
But when trouble strikes
the wicked,
that's the end of them.
–28–
17Don't be happy
to see your enemies trip
and fall down.
18The Lord will find out
and be unhappy.
Then he will stop
being angry with them.
–29–
19Don't let evil people
worry you
or make you jealous.
20They will soon be gone
like the flame of a lamp
that burns out.
–30–
21My children, you must respect
the Lord and the king,
and you must not make friends
with anyone who rebels
against either of them.
22Who knows what sudden disaster
the Lord or a ruler
might bring?
More Sayings That Make Good Sense
23Here are some more sayings
that make good sense:
When you judge,
you must be fair.
24If you let the guilty
go free,
people of all nations
will hate and curse you.
25But if you punish the guilty,
things will go well for you,
and you will prosper.
26Giving an honest answer
is a sign
of true friendship.
27Get your fields ready
and plant your crops
before starting a home.
28Don't accuse anyone
who isn't guilty.
Don't ever tell a lie
29or say to someone,
“I'll get even with you!”
30I once walked by the field
and the vineyard
of a lazy fool.
31Thorns and weeds
were everywhere,
and the stone wall
had fallen down.
32When I saw this,
it taught me a lesson:
33 Sleep a little. Doze a little.
Fold your hands
and twiddle your thumbs.
34Suddenly poverty hits you
and everything is gone!
translation_text:
Uciŋfiti nì unikpiti bɔti
1Taa nín̄ cáá bikpitiŋaliibi pu nnimbitaataam, taa nyàab̀ si nì bi ń nīn bɔ́ɔtí. 2Di sá yii bi pée dàkafī kí ŋá tipɔmbɔti ŋma ní, ní ki sòoǹ tikpitil tin bi làá ŋée ŋma pu.
3Nì iciin ní bi māā kudii, nì dinyil ní bi dùú tīī-ku mpɔn. 4Nì nlandɔkɔ ní bi gbēentí kudii tigaajawammɔntiil nì tin cáá kunyampoouee.
5Uciŋfiti cáá mpɔn ní. Unil un cáá dinyilee cáá mpɔn mili pu ní. 6A yaa làá cù kujaauee, a bɔ́ntí tiŋan ní, di sá yii bisaŋkiliibi wíiŋŋu di yì dijajil.
7Iciin bɔti pɔ̄ɔ̄ ki tīī ugbaan ń ŋmā kí gbìl̄ taapu. Bi yaa kpáfì kí sòoǹ kitiŋ pu bɔtee, u kā ki ŋmí ní.
8Unil un pée dàkafī kí ŋá tikpitilee, bi yíì-u uŋmatinli ní. 9Ugbaan pée dàkafī kí ŋá tin kaa ŋān̄ee, ní binib ná un bèel̄ binibee.
10A-wunti yaa yɔ̄tì dinimbinaamandi dalee, á nīn nyí yii a-pɔŋŋu kaa náaǹ dee.
11Fīī bin bi dàtī ki cáǹ ŋkúminee, bin bi dàtī ki cáǹ kí kpɔ̀ee, ŋá tiba kí fīī-bi. 12Án yaa yíì a làá lì yii: «Taa nìn béè míǹ!» Un di nyí tin kā unil pɔbilinee gbìl̀ taapu. Un kpèé-see pée nyí-tì, ní ki làá pà báà ŋma u-tuuŋŋi nín sá puee paati.
13Ŋmɔ́ tisiil, m-biki, kun puee an ŋān̄ ní. Kisikampiŋ mɔ̄ kinyɔkɔn ní. 14Ama á nīn nyí yii míǹ ní iciin ŋān̄ ki tīī-si. A yaa cáá-iee, a-foolbooŋwu làá nīn ŋān̄ ní dimákal din a cááyee kaa làá gbíntí fám.
15Unikpiti, taa nákań deedeedaan diiku boon kí fūkul̀ u-wanti kɔkɔ u-dumpu. 16Di sá yii deedeedaan yaa lítì miluli pu, u làá fàtīí yīkì, ama digìńdi di làá jēetí binikpitib pu.
17A-nannanliu yaa lítèe, án taa nín̄ mɔ̄ǹ-si, u yaa gbéetèe, á taa nín̄ fàal̀. 18An yaa kaa sá míǹ, ti-Dindaan làá ká ní án kaa làá mɔ̄ɔkiǹ-u, ní ú páatí u-ŋuul u-pu.
19Taa gíí binikpitib pu diŋuul, taa nín̄ cáá bikpitiŋaliibi pu nnimbitaataam. 20Di sá yii binikpitib foolbooŋwu kaa làá nīn ŋān̄, ní bikpitiŋaliibi bí kii fitila un bíi kúùyee.
21M-biki, fàŋkì ti-Dindaan nì ubɔti. Á taa nín nōotí binib bin là tikɔkɔ ń kpántée. 22Di sá yii nnaabu làá jēetí bi-pu dicilpu dicilpu, ní ŋma nyí ditafadaaldi din bi-liitil bɔ́ntì bi-puee?
Biciŋfitiibi saŋkii iba mun
23Biciŋfitiibi saŋkii iba mun gíti sɔ̀.
An kaa ŋān̄ unil ń sòoǹ kí pɔ̀ digàndi. 24Ubɔsoonli yaa tùkū unikpiti yii: «A-bɔti ŋān̄ee», diniwul tòó-u mbusu, ní samaa kɔkɔ kíǹ ki ná-u. 25Ama bin yaa kūū unikpiti bɔtee bí mmɔnni. Binib làá nīn mèé tiŋan ki bìintí bi-pu.
26Unil yaa kíí tibɔti nì ibaamɔnee, u dàkā kubɔɔtiiu kumɔntiiu dee.
27Tɔ̄ mmɔŋki tuuŋŋi kí dóó, kí bɔ́ntí asaatuun kí wàatī ní kí nín mā kudii.
28Taa túń a-juti pu dibɔgabil fám. A là kí sòoǹ kí mɔ̄ntàaa? 29Taa lì yii: «U nín ŋá-mi puee, míǹ ní m làá ŋá-u. M làá téeǹ-u tin u ŋée pu.»
Uwutijoodaan bimbim
30M cōom̀ ki kpākaǹ uwutijoodaan ubɔ saaku, m kpākaǹ unil un kaa cáá dinyilee fiinyi sufii kpaabu. 31M kpēēyee ikuŋkum di pée múkú an kɔkɔee, kumoou di nyáń ki jíń mpaan bukpaa kɔkɔnee, ataŋkpee gundi din māntìi tú-buee di dɔ̄ kitiŋee. 32M nín ká mimmee ní m dākafì an pu, m kpēēyee ní an dàkā-mi tibɔti nee. 33A là kí gèeǹ fiii, a là kí dáb́ fiii, a là kí dòon̄ fiii kí kpàl̄ iŋal. 34A dɔ̄ mimmee ní disool ń cíliń a-pu kii unaayuuyee, ní falaa ń cúú-si kii bin fúkuĺ binibee.

english_text:
More of Solomon's Wise Sayings
1Here are some more
of Solomon's proverbs.
They were copied by the officials
of King Hezekiah of Judah.
2God is praised
for being mysterious;
rulers are praised
for explaining mysteries.
3Who can fully understand
the thoughts of a ruler?
They reach beyond the sky
and go deep in the earth.
4Silver must be purified
before it can be used
to make something of value.
5Evil people must be removed
before anyone can rule
with justice.
6 Don't try to seem important
in the court of a ruler.
7It's better for the ruler
to give you a high position
than for you to be embarrassed
in front of royal officials.
Be sure you are right
8before you sue someone,
or you might lose your case
and be embarrassed.
9When you and someone else
can't get along,
don't gossip about it.
10Others will find out,
and your reputation
will then be ruined.
11The right word
at the right time
is like precious gold
set in silver.
12Listening to good advice
is worth much more
than jewelry made of gold.
13A messenger you can trust
is just as refreshing
as cool water in summer.
14Broken promises
are worse than rain clouds
that don't bring rain.
15Patience and gentle talk
can convince a ruler
and overcome any problem.
16Eating too much honey
can make you sick.
17Don't visit friends too often,
or they will get tired of it
and start hating you.
18Telling lies about friends
is like attacking them
with clubs and swords
and sharp arrows.
19A friend you can't trust
in times of trouble
is like having a toothache
or a sore foot.
20Singing to someone
in deep sorrow
is like pouring vinegar
in an open cut.
21 If your enemies are hungry,
give them something to eat.
And if they are thirsty,
give them something
to drink.
22This will be the same
as piling burning coals
on their heads.
And the Lord
will reward you.
23As surely as rain blows in
from the north,
anger is caused
by cruel words.
24It's better to stay outside
on the roof of your house
than to live inside
with a nagging wife.
25Good news from far away
refreshes like cold water
when you are thirsty.
26When a good person gives in
to the wicked,
it's like dumping garbage
in a stream of clear water.
27Don't eat too much honey
or always want praise.
28Losing self-control
leaves you as helpless
as a city without a wall.
translation_text:
1Ubɔti Saloomɔn laŋkpaŋŋi aba gíti sèé. Juuda bɔtiu Eeseekiyaasi nib di ŋmàn̄-ŋi.
Alaŋkpan aba mun
2Unimbɔti nyooti di sá bí taa nín̄ gbìl̀ tin u ŋáańee taapu, bibɔtiibi nyooti di sá bí ŋmā kí lēē tin kɔkɔ binib ŋáańee taapu.
3Taa nyí kutaa nín dátìń-ti puee, kaa nyí kitiŋ nín nyóò puee. Míǹ mbaantiim ní taa ŋūǹ kí béé tin kā bibɔtiibi pɔbiliŋinee.
4A yaa lēē tijɔkɔndi tin bí animbil kúti puee, bi làá ŋmā kí dūú mɔ́ɔ́ tiwan tin cáá kunyaaŋŋuee.
5Jà binikpitib kí nyāntí ubɔti cee, ní deedee ń tīī u-beel mpɔn.
6Taa nín̄ yòontí a-ba ubɔti nimbiin, kí taa nín̄ fòol̄ binikpaambi paaŋŋu. 7Di sá yii an sɔ́ ubɔti ń tùkù-si yii: «Jɔ̄mìń kí kāl̀ m-cee doo!» ki jítiǹ bí sìntīǹ-si taapu unikpaan ubɔ nimbiin.
8Tin a-nimbil kée, taa jìkì kí lì-tì ni yaa bí ibɔsoonni. A-juti yaa kpákáǹ-si yii aa cáá ibaamɔn, a làá ŋá mana.
9Sii nì a-juti yaa cáá tɔbee, ní kpèè kí ŋāŋkì, ama á taa dū tin ubɔ tùkū-si dibalinee kí māafì. 10An yaa kaa sá míǹ, ubɔ ŋūǹ kí gbìl̄ ní kí kɔ́ǹ-si icoo, ní tin a sòon̄ee, aa ti ŋūǹ kí gítí boon.
11Dinyɔɔbundi din nyáń ŋyunti ŋun máaǹee ŋān̄ kii sindaariya wanti tin bi dū animbil kúti ki nyɔ̄kɔntèe ní.
12Unil un pílifíǹ uciŋfiti wooŋyee bí kii sindaariya bɔmbil nì sindaariyamɔnti léeŋkaatee ní.
13Kii utaa nín nì kí sɔ̀ŋkì tikɔkɔ kutuntuŋu yuntiŋu puee, míǹ ní deedee tuuŋŋu sɔ̀ŋkī ŋu-kpiliu ŋun túń-ŋuee pɔbil.
14Unil un pōoǹ kí pɔ̄ tiba ní kaa púee náań nì atagban nín lúntí, kubuŋu ń jītí utaa kaa nì puee ní.
15Unil un cáá kimɔtii tikpilee ŋūǹ kí kpántí ubɔsoonli landɔkɔŋu, míǹ ní dilimbil din pɔ̀fèe ŋūǹ kí wīī dikpabil.
16A yaa ká tisiilee, á taa ŋmɔ́ kí lákatí a-ba pu, an yaa kaa sá míǹ, án làá núutíǹ-si ní á wùliŋkì. 17Taa nín̄ cá a-bɔɔ dumpu múlmul, an yaa kaa sá míǹ u-naŋki dāa nyēē-si, ní u kíǹ ki ná-si.
18Unil un lēē u-juti pu nnyimɔn seerauee bí kii ditambɔndi àá kitàataajiki àá mpiin ŋun cɔ́m̀ líkí likee ní.
19Dinimbinaamandi yuntiŋu un yaa dū u-mákal ki páaǹ un nyēē binib boonee puee bí kii unil un dù u-nyindi din cìŋkēe kí jú tiwan, àá un còom̄ u-taal din wùee puee ní.
20Á gāā un bí kunimbaaunee dipɔɔpindi laŋyee bí kii a cúú u-bɔkutil ki pēetì tiwool yuntiŋu àá a dū ndaam min nyàm̀ee ki sītì mbuun puee ní.
21Ŋkùm yaa cáá a-nannanliu, á tīī-u tijin ú jī, nnyinnyoo yaa tí cáá-u, á tīī-u nnyim ú nyɔ̀. 22A yaa ŋá mimmee, an bí kii amɔsiŋkoon ní a cáa pāantí u-yil puee, ní ti-Dindaan ń dāá pà-si.
23Kubuŋu kun nyēeń ŋgan púee cāabìń utaa, ní tinyimɔmbɔti kɔ̄ntí binib diŋuul.
24An sɔ́ á nīn kóò digunlɔkɔlin ki jítiǹ si nì unimpu un néeń kujaauee ń nīn kóò.
25Dinyɔɔbummɔɔndi din nyánní ndandatee bí kii nnyinsɔm min sɔ̀ŋkī nneenee ní.
26Nnyimbul ŋun gbātèe àá dinyimbɔbil din nyim bíil̀ee sá kii deedeedaan un mátifí unikpiti nimbiinee ní.
27An kaa ŋān̄ unil ń ŋmɔ́ tisiil tikpil, míǹ ní an kaa tí ŋān̄ unil ń nyàab̀ tinyool tikpil.
28Kitiŋ kin dɔ̄ ki wāā fám kaa cáá digundi din māntì ki tú-kèe bí kii unil un gíí diŋuul kaa ŋūǹ kí cúú u-bee ní.

english_text:
Don't Be a Fool
1Expecting snow in summer
and rain in the dry season
makes more sense
than honoring a fool.
2A curse you don't deserve
will take wings and fly away
like a sparrow or a swallow.
3Horses and donkeys
must be beaten and bridled—
and so must fools.
4Don't make a fool of yourself
by answering a fool.
5But if you answer any fools,
show how foolish they are,
so they won't feel smart.
6Sending a message by a fool
is like chopping off your foot
just to spite yourself.
7A fool with words of wisdom
is like an athlete
with legs that can't move.
8Are you going to honor a fool?
Why not shoot a slingshot
with the rock tied tight?
9A thornbush waved around
in the hand of a drunkard
is no worse than a proverb
in the mouth of a fool.
10It's no smarter to shoot arrows
at every passerby
than it is to hire a bunch
of worthless nobodies.
11 Dogs return to eat their vomit,
just as fools repeat
their foolishness.
12There is more hope for a fool
than for someone who says,
“I'm really smart!”
13Don't be lazy and keep saying,
“There's a lion outside!”
14A door turns on its hinges,
but a lazy person
just turns over in bed.
15Some of us are so lazy
that we won't lift a hand
to feed ourselves.
16A lazy person says,
“I am smarter
than everyone else.”
17It's better to take hold
of a mad dog by the ears
than to take part
in someone else's argument.
18It's no crazier to shoot
sharp and flaming arrows
19than to cheat someone and say,
“I was only fooling!”
20Where there is no fuel
a fire goes out;
where there is no gossip
arguments come to an end.
21Troublemakers start trouble,
just as sparks and fuel
start a fire.
22There is nothing so delicious
as the taste of gossip!
It melts in your mouth.
23Hiding hateful thoughts
behind smooth talk
is like coating a clay pot
with a cheap glaze.
24The pleasant talk
of an enemy
hides more evil plans
25than can be counted—
so don't believe a word!
26Everyone will see through
those evil plans.
27 If you dig a pit,
you will fall in;
if you start a stone rolling,
it will roll back on you.
28Watch out for anyone
who tells lies and flatters—
they are out to get you.
translation_text:
Bigbaambi bɔti
1Kii an nín kaa máaǹ ntaayim ń lítí dipeel pu, utaa ń nì ŋyunti ŋun bi cēē tikpaajinee, míǹ ní tinyool kaa máaǹ ugbaan.
2Kii udiyaal àá kikoosiyaakpaai nín yíkí ki ŋàaǹ puee, míǹ ní mbusu kaa lítí maanyiiba pu.
3Utaamu máaǹ dinaalabil, ní kimaŋ máaǹ dikpàldi, ní ugbaan máaǹ ndɔ.
4Ugbaan yaa bālifì tibɔti ŋgbaaŋyaamin, á taa kíí-u kii si mun sá ugbaanee. An yaa kaa sá míǹ, a làá kpántí ugbaan kii úŋ̀wuee ní. 5Ugbaan yaa bālifì tibɔti ŋgbaaŋyaaminee, á kíí-u ŋgbaaŋyaamin, án nín làá ŋá pu ú taa dū u-ba ki yíiń uciinee.
6Un yaa dū tibɔti ki ŋúbiǹ ugbaanee ŋá kii unil un gāā ki gūutì a-taaŋi àá un dáaĺ agìń ki tɔ́ u-ba puee ní.
7Kii ufaliŋfaan taaŋi nín fáká puee, míǹ ní dilaŋkpandi fáká ki kā ugbaan nyɔkɔn.
8Á tīī ugbaan jilmee bí kii á dū ditaŋkpal kí fúuń kujaataafuŋun kí bóob́ kí nákańee ní.
9Kii udanyɔgbil nín ŋúb́ ikuŋkum u-ŋaan puee, míǹ ní dilaŋkpandi fáká ugbaan nyɔkɔn.
10Ukpil un di fòol̄ ugbaan àá udanyɔgbil un jītée ditundee sá un ŋáań báà ŋma tiweendee ní.
11Kii kibɔkɔ nín wùliŋkī kí fàtīí gíiǹ kí ŋmɔ́ puee, míǹ ní ugbaan fàtīi gítí u-gbaandi pu.
12A yaa tin ká unil yíì u-ba uciinee, a yaa pūtì máká ugbaan pu gba, an sɔ́.
Uwutijoodaan bɔti
13Uwutijoodaan lì yii: «Upeecuncuti bí didandi pu! Gbikinti bí nsanni!»
14Kii punuu nín màntī tikúti tin pu u sàkēe puee, min ní uwutijoodaan dɔ̄ u-dooŋu pu ki lábití.
15Uwutijoodaan dùŋfī u-ŋal kí bɔ̄ disambilin, ama ní u-wutijool puee, an pɔ̄ɔ̄ ú fàtīí gíiǹní-ŋu u-nyɔkɔn.
16Uwutijoodaan yíì u-ba uciin ki jítiǹ binib biluli bin kíikí tibɔti nì dinyilee.
Alaŋkpan aba mun sɔ̀
17Unil un dù u-ba kí kɔ́ǹ kujaau kun kaa sá u-yɔkɔee poonee bí kii unil un là kí cúú kibɔkɔ ki dūu cúú ki-tafalee ní.
18Kii unil un wáatèe nín tòó aŋmisaatee nì mpiin nì tiwan tin kùee puee, 19míǹ ní unil un kíiĺ u-juti, ní boonee kí lì yii: «M ŋáań-si tinaacinee» bí.
20Idɔ yaa wùn̄ ki kúntèe, ŋŋmi kpíì dee, míǹ ní usambiidaan yaa kaa ti bée, kujaau mun kúntì.
21Akoon di tìì amɔsiŋkoon ní idɔ tìì aŋmilimbil, míǹ ní ubɔmbɔdaan nyàatī kujaau.
22Ubɔmbɔtukul nyɔɔbuŋŋi sá tijin tin mɔ̄ee ní, tì kóò unil poon ní fíŋfiŋ.
23Anyɔɔbummɔɔn ŋin nyēē dipɔɔkpitilinee bí kii animbil kúti tin cáá tijɔkɔndi bi dūu nákáǹ kuyɔkɔu sambil puee ní.
24Unil un cáá kináŋee kaa sòoǹ kí dóó u-poon bɔti kɔkɔ, ama u-pɔbilinee, u bɔ́ntí tinyimɔmbɔti ní. 25U yaa bíi sòoǹ nì si kinyɔɔmɔɔyee, taa fōō kí kíí, di sá yii u-pɔbilinee, tilandɔkɔkpiil di gbí. 26U cáá nciin kí ŋmā kí bìin̄ u-náŋki pu, ama ŋwiinee u-tuŋkpitiŋ làá dāá nyā mpaampiin pu báà ŋma ń ká.
27Unil un yaa gbìn̄ mbòóyee làá dāá lítí ŋu-poon, un yaa bíntí ditaŋkpalee, dì làá gítiń kí tàb̄-u ní.
28Unil un mɔ́ntí u-jutiibee ná-bi ní ki ŋáań-bi tiweendi, ní un cáá nyɔɔmálmalee nàantí-bi.

english_text:
Don't Brag about Tomorrow
1 Don't brag about tomorrow!
Each day brings
its own surprises.
2Don't brag about yourself—
let others praise you.
3Stones and sand are heavy,
but trouble caused by a fool
is a much heavier load.
4An angry person is dangerous,
but a jealous person
is even worse.
5A truly good friend
will openly correct you.
6You can trust a friend
who corrects you,
but kisses from an enemy
are nothing but lies.
7If you have had enough to eat,
honey doesn't taste good,
but if you are really hungry,
you will eat anything.
8When you are far from home,
you feel like a bird
without a nest.
9The sweet smell of incense
can make you feel good,
but true friendship
is better still.
10Don't desert an old friend
of your family
or visit your relatives
when you are in trouble.
A friend nearby is better
than relatives far away.
11My child, show good sense!
Then I will be happy
and able to answer anyone
who criticizes me.
12Be cautious and hide
when you see danger—
don't be stupid and walk
right into trouble.
13You deserve to lose your coat
if you loan it to someone
to guarantee payment
for the debt of a stranger.
14A loud greeting
early in the morning
is the same as a curse.
15The steady dripping of rain
and the nagging of a wife
are one and the same.
16It's easier to catch the wind
or hold olive oil in your hand
than to stop a nagging wife.
17Just as iron sharpens iron,
friends sharpen the minds
of each other.
18Take care of a tree,
and you will eat its fruit;
look after your master,
and you will be praised.
19You see your face in a mirror
and your thoughts
in the minds of others.
20Death and the grave
are never satisfied,
and neither are humans.
21Gold and silver are tested
in a red-hot furnace,
but we are tested by praise.
22No matter how hard
you beat a fool,
you can't pound out
the foolishness.
23You should take good care
of your sheep and goats,
24because wealth and honor
don't last forever.
25After the hay is cut
and the new growth appears
and the harvest is over,
26you can sell lambs and goats
to buy clothes and land.
27From the milk of the goats,
you can make enough cheese
to feed your family
and all your servants.
translation_text:
1Taa nín̄ pàkà a-ba fool wiiŋŋu pu, di sá yii saa nyí tin làá jītí díǹ wiiŋŋuee.
2Yàntī ubɔ ń pàkà-si, taa pàkà a-ba, yà unicaan ń pàkà-si, án taa nín̄ sá sisi a-ba!
3Ditaŋkpal nì dibul nyìm̀ tikpil, ama ugbaan ŋuul nyìm̀ nì tiwan liitil gbanti.
4Mbum ŋáań tipɔmbɔti ní diŋuul bí kii mbun ŋun gbée, ama ŋma ŋūǹ kí yūĺ ipoompoon íǹ nimbiin?
5Á wòoǹ unil mpaampiin pu sɔ́ nì á nīn néeń-u dibalin ubɔ kaa wāĺ.
6A-bɔɔ yaa tīī-si tiweendee, án cáá dimákal, ama a-nannanliu yaa kpàl̄-see, á nīn nyíǹ a-ba.
7Unil un jíń ki díkée yaa ká tisiilee, u yákafí ditaal ní, ama un ŋkùm cááyee ceeyee, tin tūee mɔ̄ ní.
8Kii kinɔmbiki nín yìiǹ kí cù ndan kí fá ki-diiku puee, míǹ ní unil un yìiǹ kí cù ndan kí fá u-dicaŋkuee bí.
9Ikpafi nì talaalub tìì unil pɔbil mmɔn, ama ní kubɔɔtiiu kun mɔ̄ee jítiǹ talaalumɔmmɔnti.
10Taa fá a-bɔɔ, kí taa fá a-baa mun bɔɔ. Digìńdi yaa kɔ́-see, á taa cù a-nabiki cee. A-kɔŋkɔnnaatɔ un pìlīǹ-see sɔ́ǹ kinabiki kin bíń ndandatee.
11M-biki, nín̄ cáá iciin kí tīī-mi dipɔɔpindi. Niinee ubɔ yaa bíi kpākantí-mee, ḿ ŋmā kí kíí-u.
12Un nyíǹ u-bee yaa ká nnaabu dòońee, u sáń kí báĺ ní. Ama bin kaa nyí tibee cáǹ bi-ba kí tɔ̄ poon ní án píĺ-bi.
13Ubɔ yaa yúl̀ unil un waa nyée boon kí pìnnì tibee, á fōō udaan bɔkutil kí yóoń, u nín yúl̀ unicaan boonee puee, á fōō u-cee toolima kí yóoń.
14Unil yaa téeń ki jáam̀ u-juti mpɔn kutaafaau pɔ̀lpɔlee, udaan jaamii gbanti kpántí mbusu ní.
15Utaa yaa bíi nì nnyim nín còol̀ kaa gúǹ puee, míǹ ní unimpu un néeń kujaauee bí. 16Unil ń ŋmā kí cúú-uee bí kii u bíi cútí kubuŋuee ní, àá kii ŋkpam ní u bíi nyàab̀ kí dū u-ŋal kí cúúyee.
17Tikúti ní bi cáa lòontí tikúti, unil nākantí u-juti ní kí cíkití.
18Unil un kpèé u-fiigi subu tiŋanee làá dāá ŋmɔ́ bu-bil. Bi làá tīī utɔntɔnli un ŋúb́ u-kpiliu tiŋanee jilma.
19Kii unil nín kpèé nnyimin kí wāl̀ u-ba puee, míǹ ní a kpèé unil nimbiin ní kí wāl̀ u-landɔkɔi nín sá puee.
20Taapu taŋkpiil nì Mbookpaan kaa gbéè, míǹ ní unil nimbil kaa kpèé kí díkí.
21Ŋŋmi ní bi cáa cɔ́ŋkí kí béé animbil kúti timɔntiil nì sindaariyamɔnti, ama bi nín pàkà unil puee di dàkà dinicil din ní u sée.
22Báà a yaa dū ŋkuntudɔ ki sáń ugbaan kukuntuu poon kii bi nín cùkutī tijimpin puee, u-gbaandi kaa làá nyā u-ni.
23Nín̄ nyí a-waŋkuti tiŋan, kí nīn kpèé a-picaŋkpunti tiŋan. 24Di sá yii tigaajati kaa bí kí nīn cá jaanjaan kaa kúntí, míǹ ní dibeel kaa bí kí nīn cá abin abin. 25Á gāā timool tisatin, ní timɔpɔn yaa bíi nyēēyee, á cù dijool pu kí kùliń timɔkulindi. 26Kpàà ipii kí cā i-kuti kí dūú ŋáĺ tiwampeeŋkaal, ní kí kpàà iŋɔjaa kí nyāfì kí dā kitiŋ kí kpɔ̀ tikpaal. 27Kpàà iŋɔsal tikpil kí ká ŋŋɔbiim kí kpíiǹ a-ba, kí kpáaǹ a-dicaŋkun yab nì a-tɔntɔnliibi binimpoobi.

english_text:
The Law of God Makes Sense
1Wicked people run away
when no one chases them,
but those who live right
are as brave as lions.
2In time of civil war
there are many leaders,
but a sensible leader
restores law and order.
3When someone poor takes over
and mistreats the poor,
it's like a heavy rain
destroying the crops.
4Lawbreakers praise criminals,
but law-abiding citizens
always oppose them.
5Criminals don't know
what justice means,
but all who respect the Lord
understand it completely.
6It's better to be poor
and live right,
than to be rich
and dishonest.
7It makes good sense
to obey the Law of God,
but you disgrace your parents
if you make friends
with worthless nobodies.
8If you make money by charging
high interest rates,
you will lose it all to someone
who cares for the poor.
9God cannot stand the prayers
of anyone who disobeys
his Law.
10By leading good people to sin,
you dig a pit for yourself,
but all who live right
will have a bright future.
11The rich think highly
of themselves,
but anyone poor and sensible
sees right through them.
12When an honest person wins,
it's time to celebrate;
when crooks are in control,
it's best to hide.
13If you don't confess your sins,
you will be a failure.
But God will be merciful
if you confess your sins
and give them up.
14The Lord blesses everyone
who is afraid to do evil,
but if you are cruel,
you will end up in trouble.
15A ruler who mistreats the poor
is like a roaring lion
or a bear hunting for food.
16A heartless leader is a fool,
but anyone who refuses
to get rich by cheating others
will live a long time.
17Don't give help to murderers!
Make them stay on the run
for as long as they live.
18Honesty will keep you safe,
but everyone who is crooked
will suddenly fall.
19Work hard, and you will have
a lot of food;
waste time, and you will have
a lot of trouble.
20God blesses his loyal people,
but punishes all who want
to get rich quick.
21It isn't right to be unfair,
but some people can be bribed
with only a piece of bread.
22Don't be selfish
and eager to get rich—
you will end up worse off
than you can imagine.
23Honest correction
is appreciated
more than flattery.
24If you cheat your parents
and don't think it's wrong,
you are a common thief.
25Selfish people cause trouble,
but you will live a full life
if you trust the Lord.
26Only fools would trust
what they alone think,
but if you live by wisdom,
you will do all right.
27Giving to the poor
will keep you from poverty,
but if you close your eyes
to their needs,
everyone will curse you.
28When crooks are in control,
everyone tries to hide,
but when they lose power,
good people are everywhere.
translation_text:
1Báà ubɔ yaa kaa bíi jì unikpiti, u sáń ní. Ama deedeedaan úǹ cáá dipɔbil kii digbikintipɔmbilee ní.
2Binib yaa yíkì kaa kíí bi-ba pu kitiŋ kin poonee, bikpilib wīintí ní. Ama unil un cáá iciin nì dinyilee yaa bée, kitiŋ sɔ̀m̀ ní.
3Upɔɔl un di cáá ntoom ní ki wɔ́b̀ binandambee bí kii utaa un nì ki bíiĺ tikpaajinee ní.
4Binib bin féeń Unimbɔti marauee pàkà binikpitib ní, ama ní binib bin ŋúb́ Unimbɔti marauee jáà nì bi.
5Binikpitib kaa gbìl̀ tin bí deedeeyee taapu, ama bin nyàab̀ ti-Dindaanee gbìl̀ tikɔkɔ taapu ní.
6Unil un sá usoodaan ki còom̄ deedee saŋŋunee sɔ́ǹ unil un di sá ugaaja ki nóó isaŋkpitee.
7Kibiki kin ŋúb́ Unimbɔti marauee sá unyil ní, ama un nōotí biyipɔɔdambee kɔ̄ntí u-baa ní icoo.
8Unil un pìntí binib animbil kí dāá fōō kí páań kí kpántí ugaajee kōontí u-gaajati gbanti ki yōontí un sūǹ biwɔfib saayee ní.
9Unil un yaa lēē u-tafal Unimbɔti maraunee, ti-Dindaan ná udaan wimmeem gba ní.
10Un yaa kíil̀ deedeedambi ki tɔ́ nsaŋkpitinee làá dāá jēetí mbòó ŋun úǹ u-ba gbìn̄ee poon. Ama bibulcinnib làá dāá jī nnaam.
11Ugaaja kā ki dàkafī yii úǹ di cáá iciin, ama usoodaan un cáá dinyilee nyí kun ní u sée.
12Deedeedambi di yaa fōō mpɔnee,
an sá ifaal ní. Ama binikpitib yaa fōō mpɔnee, báà ŋma bāal̀ ní.
13Unil un yaa cáá u-kpitii ki bāal̀ee, an kaa bútí-u. Ama unil un bìitī u-kpitii pu kí dū-i kí fée kāntí u-kpitii pɔ̄tam.
14Unil un fàŋkí kí taa pée ŋá ikpitee bí mmɔnni, ama un yaa cáá mpɔɔgbifinee làá ká nnaabu.
15Kii gbikinti nín sūǹ pu àá digbiŋgbil nín wúlìń puee, míǹ ní unikpiti un wɔ́b̀ dinibul din sá binandambee bí.
16Uyidaan un kaa cáá dinyilee fìkì binib wanti ní. Ama un kaa néeń ki mùul̄ ki jīǹee kāntí mmaŋfafɔkɔn ní.
17Unil un kūū u-jutee sáń ki cá dikaakulin ní, ubɔ ń taa cúú-u.
18Unil un cáá tibulcinee làá ká difiil, ama un nóó mili mili saŋŋuee làá lítí ŋubɔ poon.
19Unil un kù u-saakuee jīǹ ki díkì ní, ama unil un jòó ki pá tin kaa bí tibanee boonee làá nīn pée sá usoodaan ní.
20Unil un bí deedeeyee làá ká dibiindi, ama un jìkì kí ká tigaajatee kaa làá lóó ditafadaaldi.
21An kaa ŋān̄ unil ń pɔ̀ digàndi, ama fiii un bi làá nyíĺ kí ŋá-u ú jēe puee, unil ŋáań ikpiti gbanti.
22Unil un cáá nnimbitaataamee jòó ki pá tigaajati boon ní. Waa nyí yii disool làá kɔ́-u.
23Unil yaa wòon̄ u-jutee, kí dāá kúntée, úǹ ní u làá dāá jāam̀ ki jítiǹ un nìn pàkā-uee.
24Un yaa yù u-baa nì u-na ki lì yii: «An kaa sá ikpitee!» udaan nì digaŋgandambi sá ubaanti ní.
25Un cáá binib wanti pu nnimbitaataamee jāantí binib ní, ama un máká ti-Dindaan puee, an bútí-u ní.
26Unil un máká úǹ u-ba puee sá ugbaan ní, ama un còom̄ nì iciinee làá ká difiil.
27Un yaa pūǹ biwɔfibee, tiba kpá kí lóó udaan. Ama un yíì kaa fātìi tɔ́-bee làá kɔ́ mbusukpaanni.
28Binikpitib yaa fōō mpɔnee, báà ŋma bāal̀ ní. Ama bi yaa kúntèe, deedeedambi bùtī tikpil ní.

english_text:
Use Good Sense
1If you keep being stubborn
after many warnings,
you will suddenly discover
you have gone too far.
2When justice rules a nation,
everyone is glad;
when injustice rules,
everyone groans.
3If you love wisdom
your parents will be glad,
but chasing after bad women
will cost you everything.
4An honest ruler
makes the nation strong;
a ruler who takes bribes
will bring it to ruin.
5Flattery is nothing less
than setting a trap.
6Your sins will catch you,
but everyone who lives right
will sing and celebrate.
7The wicked don't care
about the rights of the poor,
but good people do.
8Sneering at others is a spark
that sets a city on fire;
using good sense can put out
the flames of anger.
9Be wise and don't sue a fool.
You won't get satisfaction,
because all the fool will do
is sneer and shout.
10A murderer hates everyone
who is honest
and lives right.
11Don't be a fool
and quickly lose your temper—
be sensible and patient.
12A ruler who listens to lies
will have corrupt officials.
13The poor and all who abuse them
must each depend on God
for light.
14Kings who are fair to the poor
will rule a long time.
15Correct your children,
and they will be wise;
children out of control
disgrace their mothers.
16Crime increases
when crooks are in power,
but law-abiding citizens
will see them fall.
17If you correct your children,
they will bring you peace
and happiness.
18Without guidance from God
law and order disappear,
but God blesses everyone
who obeys his Law.
19 Even when servants are smart,
it takes more than words
to make them obey.
20There is more hope for a fool
than for someone who speaks
without thinking.
21Slaves that you treat kindly
from their childhood
will cause you sorrow.
22A person with a quick temper
stirs up arguments
and commits a lot of sins.
23Too much pride brings disgrace;
humility leads to honor.
24If you take part in a crime
you are your worst enemy,
because even under oath
you can't tell the truth.
25Don't fall into the trap
of being a coward—
trust the Lord,
and you will be safe.
26Many try to make friends
with a ruler,
but justice comes
from the Lord.
27Good people and criminals
can't stand each other.
translation_text:
1Bi yaa bíi wòoǹ unil ní u pɔ́ɔkí u-pɔbilee, án làá nàan̄-u dibɔbilin niin ní nnyɔkɔ kpá.
2Deedeedambi yaa ŋúb́ kitiŋee, samaa kɔkɔ fàal̀ ní. Ama unikpiti yaa ŋúb́ kitiŋee, samaa kɔkɔ yáliŋkí ní.
3Unil un néeń iciinee tìì u-baa dipɔɔsɔŋkil. Ama un gbōō ki cá nnimpulaakpaamu ceeyee bíiĺ u-gaajati ní.
4Ubɔti yaa nóó deedee saŋŋuee, u-tiŋki cá nyɔkɔpu ní. Ama un fòol̄ lampoo tikpilee gīintí u-tiŋki boon ní.
5Unil un bíi pàkà u-jutee bíi pīil̀-u kutaliŋŋu dee.
6Ikpiti in unikpiti ŋáańee sá kutaliŋŋu ní, ama deedeedaan úǹ fàal̀ ní an mɔ̄ǹ-u.
7Deedeedaan nyí biwɔfib bɔti, ama unikpiti úǹ kaa cáá dinyil kí ŋmā kí béé-tì.
8Binib bin kaa bí tibanee cāabìń fikil fikil kitiŋin, ama biciŋfitiibi bíǹ sɔ̀ŋkī binib pɔbil.
9Uciŋfiti nì ugbaan yaa cáá tɔb ki bàn̄ ibɔsoon laŋkee, báà u yaa gíí diŋuulaaa, u yaa lāāyaaa, u kpá kí ŋùŋfì.
10Binikpɔliibi ná bibulcinnib, ama deedeedambi nyàab̀ bíǹ ní.
11Ugbaan nyāntí u-ŋuul kɔkɔ ní mpaampiin pu, ama uciŋfiti cútí u-ba ní ki sɔ̀ŋkī u-ŋuul.
12Uyidaan yaa pílifí tinyimɔmbɔtee, u-kpambaliŋ kɔkɔ kpántí binikpitib ní.
13Unandaan nì un wɔ́b́-uee sá ubaanti ní, ti-Dindaan di tīī bi-liitil animbil ní bi cáa kpèé.
14Ubɔti yaa sòoǹ biwɔfib bɔti nì ibaamɔnee, u-beel làá nīn bá ki pɔ̄ɔ̄ ní ki cá jaanjaan.
15Mbambaan nì isaŋki dàkà kibiki iciin ní, kibiki kin ŋáań min kì lèe kɔ̄ntí ki-na icoo ní.
16Binikpitib yaa ŋúb́ kitiŋee, ikpiti gbóotí ní. Ama deedeedambi làá dāá ká binikpitib gbanti lítitam.
17Dáaĺ a-biki tafal ní kí dāá ká diŋuŋfil. Kì làá dāá tīī-si dipɔɔpindi.
18Dileedakal yaa kaa ti bée, dinibul ŋáań di nín là puee ní. Ama un yaa ŋúb́ Unimbɔti Marauee bí mmɔnni!
19Baa dátí utɔntɔnli tafal nì anyɔɔbun fám. Báà u yaa gbìl̄ taapu, waa làá ŋá míǹ.
20A yaa tin ká unil sòoǹ kaa dàkafēe, a yaa pūtì máká ugbaan pu gba an sɔ́.
21Unil yaa sɔ̄kɔl̀ u-tɔntɔnliu doooo tibiyatinee, u làá dāá kpántí uwutijoodaan ní.
22Unil un kaa pɔ̄ɔ̄ diŋuul digiilee sàal̄ kujaau ní, unil un fōō mbumee ŋáań ikpiti tikpil ní.
23Unil nín yòontí u-ba yilpu puee làá sìntīǹ-u taapu. Ama un sīntiǹ u-ba taapuee làá ká tinyool.
24Un nì unaayuu yaa pēē kinyɔkɔee ná u-ba ní. U nyí mbusu un dɔ̄ ki cí-uee, ama waa làá bìitī unaayuu pu.
25Á nīn fàŋkí binibee sá kii kutaliŋŋuee ní. Ama unil un máká ti-Dindaan puee kaa fàŋkí tiba.
26Binib tikpil nyàab̀ bi-kpilib pampakaku ní, ama ti-Dindaan baba di sòoǹ unil kamaa bɔti.
27Deedeedambi ná binikpitib, ní binikpitib ná deedeedambi.

english_text:
The Sayings of Agur
1These are the sayings
and the message
of Agur son of Jakeh.
Someone cries out to God,
“I am completely worn out!
How can I last?
2I am far too stupid
to be considered human.
3I never was wise,
and I don't understand
what God is like.”
4 Has anyone gone up to heaven
and come back down?
Has anyone grabbed hold
of the wind?
Has anyone wrapped up the sea
or marked out boundaries
for the earth?
If you know of any
who have done such things,
then tell me their names
and their children's names.
5Everything God says is true—
and it's a shield for all
who come to him for safety.
6Don't change what God has said!
He will correct you and show
that you are a liar.
7There are two things, Lord,
I want you to do for me
before I die:
8Make me absolutely honest
and don't let me be too poor
or too rich.
Give me just what I need.
9If I have too much to eat,
I might forget about you;
if I don't have enough,
I might steal
and disgrace your name.
10Don't tell a slave owner
something bad about one
of the slaves.
That slave will curse you,
and you will be in trouble.
11Some people curse their father
and even their mother;
12others think they are perfect,
but they are stained by sin.
13Some people are stuck-up
and act like snobs;
14others are so greedy
that they gobble up
the poor and homeless.
15Greed has twins,
each named “Give me!”
There are three or four things
that are never satisfied:
16The world of the dead
and a childless wife,
the thirsty earth
and a flaming fire.
17Don't make fun of your father
or disobey your mother—
crows will peck out your eyes,
and buzzards will eat
the rest of you.
18There are three or four things
I cannot understand:
19 How eagles fly so high
or snakes crawl on rocks,
how ships sail the ocean
or people fall in love.
20An unfaithful wife says,
“Sleeping with another man
is as natural as eating.”
21There are three or four things
that make the earth tremble
and are unbearable:
22A slave who becomes king,
a fool who eats too much,
23a hateful woman
who finds a husband,
and a slave who takes the place
of the woman who owns her.
24On this earth four things
are small but very wise:
25Ants, who seem to be feeble,
but store up food
all summer long;
26badgers, who seem to be weak,
but live among the rocks;
27locusts, who have no king,
but march like an army;
28lizards, which can be caught
in your hand,
but sneak into palaces.
29Three or four creatures
really strut around:
30Those fearless lions
who rule the jungle,
31those proud roosters,
those mountain goats,
and those rulers
who have no enemies.
32If you are foolishly bragging
or planning something evil,
then stop it now!
33If you churn milk
you get butter;
if you pound on your nose,
you get blood—
and if you stay angry,
you get in trouble.
translation_text:
Aguur nyɔɔbuŋŋi
1Yaakee jipɔɔn Aguur nyɔɔbuŋŋi sèé. Uninja gbanti nín sòon̄ pu ki tùkū Itiyeel nì Itiyeel nì Ukaalee sèé:
2«Binib kansikinee, man di pée sá ugbaan,
maa cáá dinyil din unil máaǹ kí nīn cááyee.
3Maa bífì iciin
in bàà làá yàntī ḿ béé Circirdaanee.
4Ŋma di jɔ́m̀ yilpu ki fātìi sīntìń?
Ŋma di cúú kubuŋu ki ŋá u-ŋaan ki ká?
Ŋma di dū u-bɔkutil ki póob́ nnyim?
Ŋma di yóoǹ kitiŋ kpaanyɔmmu kɔkɔ?
Bi yíì udaan yii ba? Bi yíì u-jipɔɔn yii ba?
A yaa nyí á tùkù-maa!
5«Unil ŋūǹ kí nīn máká Unimbɔti nyɔɔbuŋŋi kɔkɔ pu. U sá digbampɔɔl ní ki tīī bin di sáń ki kóò-uee. 6Á taa kūtì tiba u-nyɔɔbuŋŋi pu. An yaa sá fám, u làá wòoǹ-si ní kí yíiń-si unyimɔndaan.
7«M-Nimbɔtiu, tiwan tili ja pu ní m mèé-si, taa ŋmìntī-mi an wanti kí wàatī ḿ nín kpú. 8Kàkatī mili mili bimbim nì inyimɔn kí wàatī-mi. Taa tīī-mi disool, kí taa tīī-mi tigaajati mun. Tīī-mi tin làá pée ŋmàntī ḿ jī kí nīn bée. 9Di sá yii m yaa sá ugaajee, m fàtī m-boon kí tīī-si ní kí lì yii: «Ŋma di sá ti-Dindaan ní?» M yaa tí sá usoodaanee, m ŋūǹ kí cùú yɔ̀ ní kí bīil̀ sii m-Nimbɔtiu yindi.
10«Taa sòoǹ kí bīil̀ uyumbu u-dindaan cee. An yaa kaa sá míǹ, u làá tɔ̄-si mbusu ní ikpiti in a ŋée ń gítí a-pu.
11«Binib biba tòó bi-baabi mbusu, ní kaa mèé ki bìintí bi-nab pu.
12«Binib biba yíì bi-ba circirdambi, ama ní kaa fíntì tijɔkɔndi tin bí bi-puee.
13«Binib biba cáá dilambil bi-yiliŋ gáań, ní bi kpèé bin kíǹee fám.
14«Binib biba nyiŋŋi sá kii ntàataajimu, ní bi nyɔɔkpaweeŋyi sá kii njimu. Bi tɔ̀ntī binandambi kitiŋ pu, ní ki kúntí biwɔfib binib kansikin.»
Alaŋkpan ŋin nóó ikaanee
15Dikoosibil din nyù fatikuee cáá bisapɔmbi bili. Bi lì yii: «Tīī-mi! Tīī-mi!» Tiwan tita di bí kaa pée díkì, ní kunanaatiiu kun kaa lì yii: «An ŋmāntèe!»
16Tíǹ di sá ditaŋkpiilin,
nì unimpuŋmaŋŋmanti,
nì kitiŋ kin pu utaa nì an kaa dɔ̄ee,
nì ŋŋmi ŋun wù an kaa cáá ŋu bál̀ee.
17Unil un yaa bèel̄ u-baa, ní kaa fātìi tɔ́ u-nee, tilaagaal tin bí mbunnee làá lúkutí udaan nimbiliŋ, ní kaajiikub ń dāá jī-u.
18Tiwan tita di bí ní ki jítì m-nyil pu, ní kunanaatiiu bí maa gbìl̀ ku-taapu.
19Tíǹ di sá ukaabu un ŋàaǹ kutaa puee saŋŋu,
nì ukoobu un còom̄ ataŋkpee puee saŋŋu,
nì meela un dēē tiŋku nyim puee saŋŋu,
nì nsan ŋun uninja dì ki cá unimpu ceeyee.
20Unimpu un nyáń u-cal boonee nín ŋáań puee sèé: U jīǹ ní kí pítí u-nyɔkɔ ní kí lì yii: «Maa ŋá ikpiti iba!»
21Tiwan tita di bí ki cìŋkī kitiŋ, ní kunanaatiiu bí kàa là ki-nimbil ń ká.
22Tíǹ di sá uyumbu ń kpántí ubɔti,
nì unil un kaa bí tibanee ń ká tijin kí jī kí díkí,
23nì unimpu un kaa cáá mbimbimɔntiimee ń ká uninja kí mɔ̄ǹ,
nì unimpuyumbu ń fōō u-kpiliu paaŋŋu.
24Tiwan tinaa di bí kitiŋ pu ki sá ŋwaŋwaamu, ama ní ki cáá iciin tikpil.
25Icati kaa cáá mpɔn, ama i kōontí tijin dipeel pu ki kpáafí.
26Kumooun jaŋgbeenapulii kaa cáá mpɔn, ama i ŋáań i-kɔŋkooŋyi ataŋkpee kansikin.
27 Inaakitoon kaa cáá ubɔti, ama ní ki nóó tɔb dikitil.
28Dijikpal din unil ŋūǹ kí cúú nì u-ŋalee, ama di kóò dibeecindin.
29Tiwan tita di bí ti-saŋkiŋŋi cáá kunyaaŋŋu, kunanaatiiu mun bí ki ŋān̄ an kaa cáá bí lì.
30Tíǹ di sá gbikinti un sá ipeel kɔkɔ kansikin upɔɔl,
kaa fàŋkí tibee,
31nì ukooja un di còom̄ u-taŋambiyaamu puee, nì uŋɔja
nì ubɔti un di līī u-janjaliibi nyɔkɔpuee.
32A yaa nìn ŋá digbaandi ní ki yōoǹ a-ba yilpu, ní boon a dākafèe, á pìin̄ a-nyɔkɔ pu. 33Di sá yii a yaa ŋmáaḿ nnaabiimee, naanum di nyēē, a yaa fáá unil maŋfalee, fatiku di nyēē ní a yaa gíí diŋuulee, kujaau ní an cāabìń.

english_text:
What King Lemuel's Mother Taught Him
1These are the sayings
that King Lemuel of Massa
was taught by his mother.
2My son Lemuel, you were born
in answer to my prayers,
so listen carefully.
3Don't waste your life
chasing after women!
This has ruined many kings.
4Kings and leaders
should not get drunk
or even want to drink.
5Drinking makes you forget
your responsibilities,
and you mistreat the poor.
6Beer and wine are only
for the dying or for those
who have lost all hope.
7Let them drink and forget
how poor and miserable
they feel.
8But you must defend
those who are helpless
and have no hope.
9Be fair and give justice
to the poor and homeless.
In Praise of a Good Wife
10A truly good wife
is the most precious treasure
a man can find!
11Her husband depends on her,
and she never
lets him down.
12She is good to him
every day of her life,
13and with her own hands
she gladly makes clothes.
14She is like a sailing ship
that brings food
from across the sea.
15She gets up before daylight
to prepare food for her family
and for her servants.
16She knows how to buy land
and how to plant a vineyard,
17and she always works hard.
18She knows when to buy or sell,
and she stays busy
until late at night.
19She spins her own cloth,
20and she helps the poor
and the needy.
21Her family has warm clothing,
and so she doesn't worry
when it snows.
22She does her own sewing,
and everything she wears
is beautiful.
23Her husband is a well-known
and respected leader
in the city.
24She makes clothes to sell
to the shop owners.
25She is strong and graceful,
as well as cheerful
about the future.
26Her words are sensible,
and her advice
is thoughtful.
27She takes good care
of her family
and is never lazy.
28Her children praise her,
and with great pride
her husband says,
29“There are many good women,
but you are the best!”
30Charm can be deceiving,
and beauty fades away,
but a woman
who honors the Lord
deserves to be praised.
31Show her respect—
praise her in public
for what she has done.
translation_text:
Ubinaati bíi sáŋkí u-jipɔɔn ubɔti
1Isaŋki in Maasa bɔtiu Leemuyeel fōō u-na ceeyee sèé:
2«Áù, m-jipɔɔn! Áù, m-poon biki! Áù, kibiki kin m mēē ki kée! 3Taa dū a-pɔŋŋu kí fìtīǹ binimpoobi, taa nóó bin di yàntī bibɔtiibi wáŋkée. 4Leemuyeel, bibɔtiibi kaa máaǹ kí nyɔ̀ ndaam, abɔtibil mun kaa máaǹ kí nyɔ̀ ndaam min pɔ̄ɔ̄yee. 5Bi yaa nyùn̄ee, bi súntí marab pu, ní kaa ti mɔ́tí binandambi pu. 6Dūmaan ndaam min pɔ̄ɔ̄yee kí tīī bin làá kpúee, kí dū ndamam kí tīī binib bin di bí kunimbaaunee. 7Udaan yaa nyùn̄ee u làá súntí u-falaau pu, ní kaa ti làá téetí u-nimbaaku pu. 8Siiyee, sii máaǹ kí sòoǹ kí tīī binib bin yaa sòoǹ baa pílifíǹ-bee, binib bin bi dūu fée. 9Á nīn sòoǹ tibɔti nì ibaamɔn, kí mɔ̄tì biwɔfib nì binandambi pu.»
Unimpu tiŋman pu yɔu
10Ŋma ŋūǹ kí ká unimpu tiŋman pu yɔu? U pɔ̄ɔ̄ kudaau ki jítiǹ abeedimbil.
11U-cal cáá u-pu dimákal. Waa ŋáań u-cal gaajati fám fám.
12U-maŋfal wiiŋyi kɔkɔ poonee, u ŋáań u-cal tiŋan ŋma ní, waa ŋáań-u tikpitil.
13U nyàab̀ ipii kuti nì gulfa un bí fálfalee, ní ki tūǹ ditundi nì difaŋgiil.
14U sá kii meela un tūntí tinyampuwanee ní, u cāabìń u-jikaati ndandati ní.
15U fìntī ntaafaabɔmbɔm ní. U ŋáań tijin kí tīī u-dicaŋku, ní ki tìì u-tɔntɔnliibi bi-tundi.
16U kàal̀ ní kí dàkafì ní kí dā u-ba nì u-nimbiliŋ kusaau ní kí cóoń fiinyi sufii ku-pu.
17U tūǹ ditundi nì difaŋgiil, waa ŋūǹ kí nīn kā iŋal jòon̄ fám.
18U ká yii u-tundi còom̄-u tiŋan. U-fitilau pée wāĺ ní kunyeeu kɔkɔ ní u tūǹ ditundi.
19U pée ŋúb́ kigulfajantilii u-ŋaan, ní ki ŋál̀ tiwan.
20U pūǹ bisoodambi tiwan, ní ki tútúǹ binandambi.
21Tiwool yuntiŋuee, waa fàŋkí u-dicaŋku pu, kun puee u-dicaŋkun yab kɔkɔ cáá tiwool bɔkutiŋ.
22U lù u-ba ndoo pu satab, ní ki pèentí iŋaamɔnti in bí fálfal ki máǹ cínciŋee wanti.
23Akpambal yaa kpáfèe, bi tìì u-cal tinyool. U-cal kútí bitindaŋkpilib pu bi kpáfí ki kpèé kitiŋ pu bɔti.
24Unimpuee ŋál̀ tiwampeeŋkaal ki nyáfí, ki lù dambalab ki nyáfíǹ binyampoobi.
25U cáá mpɔn ní binib tìì-u jilma, u cáá dimákal foolboon pu.
26U sòoǹ nì iciin ní ki tìì isaŋkimɔnti nì tiniti.
27U-nimbil cɔ́ tin kɔkɔ pée jītí u-dicaŋkunee pu, ní waa jīǹ tijin tin pu waa nyántì kutuntuŋuee.
28U-biyaamu pàkà-u binib nimbiin, ní u-cal mun tìì-u tinyool.
29U lì yii: «Binimpoobi tikpil bí ki sá tiŋman pu nimpoobi, ama sii jítiǹ bíǹ kɔkɔ!»
30Unimpu un bí gbàlgbalgbalee ŋūǹ kí ŋmàtiǹ unil, ní kunyaaŋŋu mun kaa yúntí, ama unimpu un fàŋkí ti-Dindaanee di máaǹ tinyool.
31Bi máaǹ kí tīī-u u-faŋgiil paati. Binib kɔkɔ máaǹ kí pàkà-u u-tundi pu.

english_text:
Nothing Makes Sense
1When the son of David was king in Jerusalem, he was known to be very wise, and he said:
2Nothing makes sense!
Everything is nonsense.
I have seen it all—
nothing makes sense!
3What is there to show
for all of our hard work
here on this earth?
4 People come, and people go,
but still the world
never changes.
5The sun comes up,
the sun goes down;
it hurries right back
to where it started from.
6The wind blows south,
the wind blows north;
round and round it blows
over and over again.
7All rivers empty into the sea,
but it never spills over;
one by one the rivers return
to their source.
8All of life is far more boring
than words could ever say.
Our eyes and our ears
are never satisfied
with what we see and hear.
9Everything that happens
has happened before;
nothing is new,
nothing under the sun.
10Someone might say,
“Here is something new!”
But it happened before,
long before we were born.
11No one who lived in the past
is remembered anymore,
and everyone yet to be born
will be forgotten too.
It Is Senseless To Be Wise
12I said these things when I lived in Jerusalem as king of Israel. 13With all my wisdom I tried to understand everything that happens here on earth. And God has made this so hard for us humans to do. 14I have seen it all, and everything is just as senseless as chasing the wind.
15If something is crooked,
it can't be made straight;
if something isn't there,
it can't be counted.
16 I said to myself, “You are by far the wisest person who has ever lived in Jerusalem. You are eager to learn, and you have learned a lot.” 17Then I decided to find out all I could about wisdom and foolishness. Soon I realized that this too was as senseless as chasing the wind.
18The more you know,
the more you hurt;
the more you understand,
the more you suffer.
translation_text:
Tikɔkɔ sá fám ní
1Daafiidi jipɔɔn Uciŋfiti un sá ubɔti Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee nyɔɔbuŋŋi sèé.
2Uciŋfiti di lī yii:
Kubuŋu fám, kubuŋu fám,
tikɔkɔ pée sá kii kubuŋuee ní.
3Nisaal bìǹ kitiŋ pu doo,
ama ipaati ilai ní u cáá?
4Biba kúù
ní bi màal̀ biba,
ama ní kitiŋ kíǹ pée bí ki-laŋki.
5Ŋwìiń nyēē, ŋwìiń jēetí,
ní kí ŋá malaa kí fàtīí gítí ŋu-nyalaŋki.
6Kubuŋu jītí kí cù ŋgan pú,
ní kí màntī ki gítí ŋgiil pú.
Ku màntī ní kí màntī ní kí fàtīí màntī,
ní kí fàtīí gítí laakin ku kílińee.
7Ibun kɔkɔ pùub̀ ki kóò tiŋku poon,
ama tiŋku kaa pée gbéè dalba dalba.
Laakin ní ibun pùub̀ ki kóòyee,
niin ní i gbíntìi pùub̀ ki kóò kaa gbèentí.
8Anyɔɔbun kɔkɔ sátì an kaa cáá bí lì.
An kaa cáá yii ditafal pílifì tibɔti ki bál̀,
ní dinimbil mun kaa kpèé kí núutí.
9Tin nìn pée bée di làá nīn pée bí.
Tin bi nìn pée ŋée ní bi làá fàtīí ŋá.
Tiba kaa bí ki sá tipɔn kitiŋ pu doo.
10Ti kāntí tiwan tibee ní kí lì yii:
«Kpèè, tiwan nee sá tiwampɔn ní!»
Ama an wantee nìn pée bí dooooyee
ki wāatì ní timbi nín nyáń.
11Timbee, ti súntí tin nìn jítì doooodooooyee pu.
Bin mun làá dāá páannée
làá dāá súntí tin làá dāá jītí timbi boonee pu.
Uciŋfiti bífì ki béè duulinya poon bɔti
12Man Uciŋfiti jíń Isirayeel nibul pu dibeel Jeerusaleem tiŋkin. 13M dū m-ciiŋyi kɔkɔ kí béé tin kɔkɔ bíi jītí kitiŋ puee kí gbìl̄ ti-taapu. An sá digìŋ́kpaandi ní Unimbɔti dūu túǹ nisaalib. 14M ká tin kɔkɔ ní binib ŋáań kitiŋ pu dooyee. Ama tíǹ kɔkɔ sá fám ní, an bí kii unil nín jì kubuŋu puee ní.
15Tiwan tin pɔ́ĺee, baa ŋūǹ kí tàntī-tì.
Tin kaa bée, baa ŋūǹ kí kàaǹ-tì.
16M lī m-ban yii: «M béè iciin ki yāntì i cūtì nyɔkɔpu ki jítiǹ bibɔtiibi bin kɔkɔ péeǹ-mi ki kāl̀ dibeel Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee.» M béè iciin tikpilku, ki ká dinyil tiŋan pu. 17M bífì ki béè tin di sá iciinee nì tin kaa sée, tin sá dinyil nì tin sá digbaandee. M dáań ki ká yii tíǹ kɔkɔ sá kii unil nín jì kubuŋu puee ní.
18Iciin tikpil cāabìń agìń tikpil mun ní,
míǹ ní dinyil tikpil mun cāabìń diwumpildi.

english_text:
It Is Senseless To Be Selfish
1I said to myself, “Have fun and enjoy yourself!” But this didn't make sense. 2Laughing and having fun is crazy. What good does it do? 3I wanted to find out what was best for us during the short time we have on this earth. So I decided to make myself happy with wine and find out what it means to be foolish, without really being foolish myself.
4 I did some great things. I built houses and planted vineyards. 5I had flower gardens and orchards full of fruit trees. 6And I had pools where I could get water for the trees. 7 I owned slaves, and their sons and daughters became my slaves. I had more sheep and goats than anyone who had ever lived in Jerusalem. 8 Foreign rulers brought me silver, gold, and precious treasures. Men and women sang for me, and I had many wives who gave me great pleasure.
9 I was the most famous person who had ever lived in Jerusalem, and I was very wise. 10I got whatever I wanted and did whatever made me happy. But most of all, I enjoyed my work. 11Then I thought about everything I had done, including the hard work, and it was simply chasing the wind. Nothing on earth is worth the trouble.
Wisdom Comes from God
12I asked myself, “What can the next king do that I haven't done?” Then I decided to compare wisdom with foolishness and stupidity. 13And I discovered that wisdom is better than foolishness, just as light is better than darkness. 14Wisdom is like having two good eyes; foolishness leaves you in the dark. But wise or foolish, we all end up the same.
15Finally, I said to myself, “Being wise got me nowhere! The same thing will happen to me that happens to fools. Nothing makes sense. 16Wise or foolish, we all die and are soon forgotten.” 17This made me hate life. Everything we do is painful; it's just as senseless as chasing the wind.
18Suddenly I realized that others would someday get everything I had worked for so hard, then I started hating it all. 19Who knows if those people will be sensible or stupid? Either way, they will own everything I have earned by hard work and wisdom. It doesn't make sense.
20I thought about all my hard work, and I felt depressed. 21When we use our wisdom, knowledge, and skill to get what we own, why do we have to leave it to someone who didn't work for it? This is senseless and wrong. 22What do we really gain from all of our hard work? 23 Our bodies ache during the day, and work is torture. Then at night our thoughts are troubled. It just doesn't make sense.
24 The best thing we can do is to enjoy eating, drinking, and working. I believe these are God's gifts to us, 25and no one enjoys eating and living more than I do. 26 If we please God, he will make us wise, understanding, and happy. But if we sin, God will make us struggle for a living, then he will give all we own to someone who pleases him. This makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
translation_text:
1M lī m-ban yii: «Toooo! M làá jī mmɔn kí jī nnaam.» Ama m ká yii niin mun sá fám ní. 2Mmɔn sá digbaandi, ní ifaal mun kaa bí tiban.
3M lēē m-pɔbil poon yii m làá nīn kíǹ ki nyù ndaam kí nīn ŋáań kii bigbaambi nín ŋáań puee, kí nīn gbíntìi yì m-ba. M nìn là kí ká kun unil ŋūǹ kí ŋá án nīn sá tiŋan u-maŋfal wiiŋyi poon duulinya nee poonee ní. 4M túń atuŋkpaan tikpil, ki máń m-ba adiin, ki kùn̄ fiinyi sufii kpaaŋŋi. 5M kùn̄ poojab nì isufi kpaaŋŋi ki cóoǹ isufi in lòoǹ abilee kɔkɔ nì i-bulifi. 6M gbìn̄ anyimbɔbil bí nīn lúù nnyim ki yàantí isufi in ní m cóoǹ cóoǹee. 7M dá iyumbu bininjab nì binimpoobi, ki cáá bitɔntɔnliibi tikpil. M cáá inaa nì ipii nì iŋoobu ki jítiǹ bibɔtiibi bin nìn péeǹ-mi ki kāl̀ dibeel Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee kɔkɔ. 8M nìn kóoǹ ntimu mun kɔkɔ bí m-taapuee nì mu-bɔtiibi gaajati nì bi-nimbiliŋ kúti nì bi-sindaariyab ki kpúkuǹ m-cee. Bilaŋgaaliibi bininjab nì binimpoobi nìn dòoń ki gà ilan ki kɔ̀ntī m-nimbiliŋ. M nìn cáá kun unifoo kamaa pée lèe, an dàkà yii kunimpupaau. 9M kpántì unikpaan ki jítiǹ bibɔtiibi binib bin kɔkɔ kāl̀ Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee. Ama nì míǹ kɔkɔee, m-ciiŋyi dáá gbíntìi bí m-cee. 10Kun kamaa ní m-nimbil yaa wál̀ ní ku fáatiǹ-mee, maa nìn yíití kudɔŋu. Maa ŋmīntì m-pɔbil mmɔn báà ŋubɔ. Tiŋman, m jíń m-tuuŋŋi paati ní ki páatì m nín gīī ki túń ditundi diŋyee kɔkɔ pu. 11M kāl̀ ki kpēē atuun ŋin m túńee kɔkɔ nì digìńdi din m gīī ní ki túń an tuuŋŋee. M dáań ki ká yii tíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ mun sá kii kubuŋuee ní.
12M nyàab̄ kí gbìl̄ iciin nì kuwaatiiu nì digbaandi taapu. M bālifì m-ba yii unil un làá dāá kàl̄ dibeel m-boonee làá dāá ŋá kii bin līntiǹ-ueeee? 13Mama m-ba dáań ki ká yii iciin sɔ́ǹ digbaandi, kii ŋwalifi nín sɔ́ǹ dibɔmbɔndi puee ní. 14Di sá yii uciŋfiti wāĺ laakin u còom̄ ki cée, ama ní ugbaan úǹ pée bí ki tìliŋkī dibɔmbɔndin ní ki cá, kaa wāĺ. Ama m nyí mun yii bi-liitil làá dāá pée kúntí mbaantiim ní. 15Niinee ní m lī m-pɔbil poon yii: «Tin dɔ̄ ki cí ugbaanee di dɔ̄ ki cí ma mun. Mimmee m nín sá uciŋfiti ki jítiǹ-u nee, m páatì ba? M lī m-ban yii tíǹ kɔkɔ mun sá kubuŋu ní.» 16Baa téetí uciŋfiti àá ugbaan pu kí nīn cá jaanjaan. Ugbaan kúù ní uciŋfiti mun kúù, ama iwiŋkaaŋkaa boonee binib súntì uciŋfiti puɔɔɔ, ki súntì ugbaan mun pu. Ba pu ní an bí míǹ ní? 17Niin ní m-naŋki nyáń nì dimaŋfal din poon ti bí nee, kun puee m ká yii tin binib ŋáań kitiŋ pu dooyee kaa fáatiǹ-mi. Di sá yii tíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ kaa bí tiban, an bí kii unil nín jì kubuŋu puee ní.
18M ná ditundi din m gīī digìńdi ki túń kitiŋ pu dooyee kɔkɔ. Di sá yii un làá dāá fōō m-yil m-kpátam boonee di làá dāá jī tin kɔkɔ ní m ŋá ki yóoǹee. 19Udaan yaa làá dāá nīn sá uciŋfiti àá ugbaanaaa, ubɔ kaa nyí. Ama úǹ di làá dāá jī tiwan tin kɔkɔ ní m gīī digìńdi ki dàkā iciin ki ká kitiŋ pu dooyee. Niin mun sá kii unil nín jì kubuŋu puee ní. 20M nín ká digìńdi din m gīī kitiŋ pu dooyee, ní m-wunti yɔ̄tì. 21Á kpèè yii unil ń dū iciin nì dinyil kí tɔ̄ ditundi ní án bútí-u tiŋan, kí dāá dū tin kɔkɔ u gīī digìńdi ki ká gbantee kí tīī ubɔ un kaa pée ŋá tibee. Niin gbanti mun sá kii kubuŋuee ní, ki wù tikpil. 22Di sá yii unil nín tūǹ ditundi kí gbá kí gīī kitiŋ nee puee, ba ní u páatí ní? 23Tiŋman, unil maŋfal wiiŋyi kɔkɔ poonee, u pɔ̄ɔntí kí jī falaa kí tɔ̄ ditundi. Kunyeeu gbee, waa ŋūǹ kí ŋùŋfì. Niin mun sá kubuŋu fám ní.
24Kun pée sá binifoobi naamee di sá bí jī kí nyɔ̀ ní kí fàal̀ digìńdi din bi gīīyee pu. M dáań ki ká yii Unimbɔti di tīī nnaam gbanti. 25Di sá yii ŋma di ŋūǹ kí jī kí nīn bí mmɔnni an yaa kaa nyánní Unimbɔti cee. 26Unil un bɔti fáatì Unimbɔtee, udaan ní u tìì iciin nì dinyil nì dipɔɔpindi. Ama unil un ŋáań ikpitee, u yàntī u kōontí tigaajawan ki kpáafí un fáatiǹ-uee ní. An mun kaa cáá taapu ní ki bí kii unil nín jì kubuŋu puee.

english_text:
Everything Has Its Time
1Everything on earth
has its own time
and its own season.
2There is a time
for birth and death,
planting and reaping,
3for killing and healing,
destroying and building,
4for crying and laughing,
weeping and dancing,
5for throwing stones
and gathering stones,
embracing and parting.
6There is a time
for finding and losing,
keeping and giving,
7for tearing and sewing,
listening and speaking.
8There is also a time
for love and hate,
for war and peace.
What God Has Given Us To Do
9What do we gain by all our hard work? 10I have seen what difficult things God demands of us. 11God makes everything happen at the right time. Yet none of us can ever fully understand all he has done, and he puts questions in our minds about the past and the future. 12I know the best thing we can do is to always enjoy life, 13because God's gift to us is the happiness we get from our food and drink and from the work we do. 14Everything God has done will last forever; nothing he does can ever be changed. God has done all this, so that we will worship him.
15Everything that happens
has happened before,
and all that will be
has already been—
God does everything
over and over again.
The Future Is Known Only to God
16Everywhere on earth I saw violence and injustice instead of fairness and justice. 17So I told myself that God has set a time and a place for everything. He will judge everyone, both the wicked and the good. 18I know God is testing us to show us that we are merely animals. 19Like animals we breathe and die, and we are no better off than they are. It just doesn't make sense. 20All living creatures go to the same place. We are made from earth, and we return to earth. 21Who really knows if our spirits go up and the spirits of animals go down into the earth? 22We were meant to enjoy our work, and that's the best thing we can do. We can never know the future.
translation_text:
Tiwan kamaa nì ti-yuntiŋu ní
1Kitiŋ nee puee, tiwan kamaa cáá ti-yuntiŋu, ní ŋyunti kamaa cáá ti-wanti.
2Ŋyunti bí bí màal̀ unil
ní ŋyunti bí ú kpú,
ŋyunti bí bí cóoń busubu,
ní ŋyunti bí bí fùkù-bu.
3Ŋyunti bí bí kpɔ̀
ní ŋyunti bí bí cáaǹ,
ŋyunti bí bí nàan̄
ní ŋyunti bí bí mā.
4Ŋyunti bí bí sɔ̄
ní ŋyunti bí bí lā,
ŋyunti bí bí yāliŋkì
ní ŋyunti bí bí ŋɔ̄.
5Ŋyunti bí bí tɔ̄ ataŋkpee
ní ŋyunti bí bí tòò-ŋi,
ŋyunti bí bí kpàl̄ tɔb,
ní ŋyunti bí bí kpàtī.
6Ŋyunti bí bí nyàab̀
ní ŋyunti bí bí fá.
7Ŋyunti bí bí cátí
ní ŋyunti bí bí ŋáĺ,
ŋyunti bí bí nīn ŋmí
ní ŋyunti bí bí nīn sòoǹ.
8Ŋyunti bí bí nīn néeń
ní ŋyunti bí bí nīn ná.
Kujaau yuntiŋu bí
ní ŋgbansɔŋfi yuntiŋu bí.
9Ba paatii ní un tūǹ ditundee kāntí u-tundi gìńdi poon? 10M kpēē atuun ŋin ní Unimbɔti dūu túǹ unil puee. 11Unimbɔti yàntī tikɔkɔ bàń ti-yuntiŋu ní. U gíti tí tīī binifoobi nlandɔkɔ bí béé tin jítèe nì tin bí ki dòońee. Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, baa ŋūǹ kí béé tin kɔkɔ Unimbɔti ŋée. 12M nyí mun yii nnaam min pée bí ki tīī-bee di sá bí jī mmɔn bi-maŋfal wiiŋyi poon kí fàal̀. 13Unil yaa ká kí jī, kí nyɔ̀ ní ki bíi jīǹ u-tundi puee, an sá Unimbɔti pɔl ní. 14M nyí mun yii tin kɔkɔ ní Unimbɔti ŋáańee làá nīn pée bí kí nīn cá jaanjaan, tiba kaa kútí tin u ŋée puɔɔɔ, tiba kaa bàtī mun. Unimbɔti ŋáań míǹ yii unil ń nīn fàŋkí-u ní. 15Tibɔti tin bíi jītí kɔŋkɔnnee nìn pée jítì dooooyee. Tin bí ki làá jītí fool boonee mun nìn pée jítì dooooyee ní. Unimbɔti yàntī tin kɔkɔ pée jītée fàtīi kífí mpɔm ní.
Tikɔkɔ kúntíǹ ŋkúm ní
16Kpèè tin m gíti dáań ki ká kitiŋ pu dooyee: laakin marab bàà máaǹ kí tɔ̄ ditundee, tin kaa bí deedeeyee di bí, laakin ibaamɔn bàà máaǹ kí nīn bée, tin kaa bí deedeeyee di bí niin. 17Niinee ní m lī m-ban yii Unimbɔti làá sòoǹ deedeedaan nì unikpiti bɔti. Di sá yii tiwan kɔkɔ cáá ti-yuntiŋu, ní u làá sòoǹ ti-tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ bɔti. 18M lī m-pɔbilin binifoobi pu yii: Unimbɔti là kí ká bi nín cáá kudapɔɔu kuŋyee ní kí dàkà-bi yii bi bí kii tiwaŋkutee ní. 19Di sá yii unil nín kúntíǹ puee, míǹ mbaantiim ní kuwaŋkuluu mun kúntíǹ. Unil kúù ní kuwaŋkuluu mun kúù. Bi-kɔkɔ pée cáá kufoobaantiiuee ní. Unil kaa jítiǹ kuwaŋkuluu, kun puee tikɔkɔ pée sá kii kubuŋuee ní. 20Tin kɔkɔ pée cáá kufoouee nín kúntíǹ puee dee. Kufoou kamaa nyánní ntamin ní ki làá fàtīí gítí ntamin. 21Ubɔ kaa ŋūǹ kí lì yii unil fooku kúǹ jɔ́ḿ yilpu yilpu, ama ní kuwaŋkuluu kúǹ yɔkɔ sìntī kitiŋ taapu taapu. 22An pu ní man ká yii tin pée ŋān̄ ki tīī unilee di sá ú jī u-tuuŋŋi ŋin u túńee pu, kun puee u paatii dee. Di sá yii ubɔ kaa ti làá gíiǹní-u ú ká u-kpátam nín làá dāá nīn bí puee.

english_text:
1I looked again and saw people being mistreated everywhere on earth.
