They were crying, but no one was there to offer comfort, and those who mistreated them were powerful. 2I said to myself, “The dead are better off than the living. 3But those who have never been born are better off than anyone else, because they have never seen the terrible things that happen on this earth.”
4Then I realized that we work and do wonderful things just because we are jealous of others. This makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
5Fools will fold their hands
and starve to death.
6Yet a very little food
eaten in peace
is better than twice as much
earned from overwork
and chasing the wind.
7Once again I saw that nothing on earth makes sense. 8For example, some people don't have friends or family. But they are never satisfied with what they own, and they never stop working to get more. They should ask themselves, “Why am I always working to have more? Who will get what I leave behind?” What a senseless and miserable life!
It Is Better To Have a Friend
9You are better having a friend than to be all alone, because then you will get more enjoyment out of what you earn. 10If you fall, your friend can help you up. But if you fall without having a friend nearby, you are really in trouble. 11If you sleep alone, you won't have anyone to keep you warm on a cold night. 12Someone might be able to beat up one of you, but not both of you. As the saying goes, “A rope made from three strands of cord is hard to break.”
13You may be poor and young, but if you are wise, you are better off than a foolish old king who won't listen to advice. 14Even if you were not born into the royal family and have been a prisoner and poor, you can still be king. 15I once saw everyone in the world follow a young leader who came to power after the king was gone. 16His followers could not even be counted. But years from now, no one will praise him—this makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
translation_text:
Ŋkúm sɔ́ǹ dimaŋfal
1M gíti dáań ki ká mun yii diwɔ́bil bí kitiŋ pu doo tikpil. Bin bi wɔ́b̀ee bí ki gbòoǹ pɔ̀ɔɔɔ, ama ní báà ubɔ kaa bí kí ŋméeǹ-bi. Mpɔn kā bin sàantí-bee ŋaan, ní ubɔ kaa bí kí ŋméeǹ-bi. 2Niinee m ká yii bin kpíìyee bí mmɔnni ki jítiǹ binifoobi. 3Ama un baa láá màl̄ee úǹ gíti bí mmɔnni ki jítiǹ bitaŋkpiibi nì binifoobi. Di sá yii úǹ kaa ká atuŋkpiti ŋin bi tūǹ kitiŋ nee puee.
4M ká mun yii unil gì ki là án bútí-u u-tuuŋŋi poon, kun puee u là kí jītíǹ u-juti ní. An mun kaa cáá taapu, an bí kii unil nín jì kubuŋu puee ní. 5Ugbaan di kā ki kpàl̄ iŋal ní ŋkùm ń kpɔ̀-u. 6Ama unil ń ká diŋuŋfil fiii sɔ́ ki jítiǹ á tɔ̄ ditundi din di sá kii bi nín jì kubuŋu puee kí gīī kí tin kpáàa lákatí a-ba puee.
7M gíti dáań ki ká yii tibɔti tiba bí kitiŋ pu doo ki sá kii unil nín jì kubuŋu puee: 8Unil di bí u-baba nì u-baba, kaa cáá ubɔɔtaaa, kaa cáá kibikaaa, kaa cáá kinabiki mun. An niliuee tūǹ ditundi kaa gbèentí kí mɔ̀tīí ká tigaajati. Ama ní u bàlifī u-ba yii: «Ŋma ní m tūǹ ditundi ki tìì ní? Ŋma pu ní m ŋmìntī m-ba mmɔn ní?» An mun bí kii unil nín jì kubuŋu puee ní. An sá dituŋfandi ní. 9An sɔ́ binib ń nīn bí bili ki jítiǹ unil ń nīn bí u-baba, kun puee binib bili tundi nyēē nnyim ki jítiǹ unibaanti. 10Di sá yii bi-kansikin ubɔ yaa lítèe, un kíǹee làá yòon̄-u. Ama unil un bí u-babee bɔti gbí isaa, kun puee úǹ yaa lítèe, ubɔ kaa bí kí yòon̄-u. 11Míǹ mbaantiim, binib bili yaa kpáfì ki dɔ̄ee, an tùm̀ bi-pu ní, ama unil yaa dɔ̄ u-babee, u làá ŋá mana ní án nīn tùm̀ u-pu? 12Bi ŋūǹ kí já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ unibaanti sɔkɔmii, ama an yaa sá binib bilee, an pɔ̄ɔ̄. Dipal din bi dū iŋmii ita ki pàal̄ee kaa tìfī sɔkɔmii.
13Campɔnti un sá usoodaan ki cáá iciinee sɔ́ǹ ubɔtigbaan un púĺ kaa ti kíikí bí sāŋkì-uee. 14Báà campɔnti gbanti yaa nyánní sarkan ki kpántì ubɔti àá u yaa mèé u-beelin ki kāntí ki jīǹ, 15m ká yii kitiŋ nee puee, binib kɔkɔ làá nīn bí campɔnti gbanti jaaŋŋu pú ní ú dāá fōō ubɔtikpikee yil kí kàl̄ dibeel. 16U làá kpántí dinibukpaandi bɔtiu ní. Ama bin làá dāá páań u-boonee kaa dāa gíti bí dipɔɔpindin u-pu. Di sá yii tíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ sá fám ní ki bí kii bi nín jì kubuŋu puee.
Taa nín sòoǹ ki bùsī anyɔɔbun Unimbɔti nimbiin
17A yaa cá Unimbɔti diikunee, á nīn nyí nì a-ba. Á nīn cáá nlandɔkɔ yii a cá niin kí pīlifì ní. Míǹ sɔ́ǹ á cù niin kí ŋá bigbaambi saraau. Di sá yii bíǹ kaa nyí yii bi bíi ŋáań tin kaa ŋān̄ee.

english_text:
Be Careful How You Worship
1Be careful what you do when you enter the house of God. Fools go there to offer sacrifices, because all they do is sin. But it's best just to listen when you go to worship. 2Don't talk before you think or make promises to God without thinking them through. God is in heaven, and you are on earth, so don't talk too much. 3If you keep thinking about something, you will dream about it. If you talk too much, you will say the wrong thing.
4 God doesn't like fools. So don't be slow to keep your promises to God. 5It's better not to make a promise at all than to make one and not keep it. 6Don't let your mouth get you in trouble! And don't say to the worship leader, “I didn't mean what I said.” God can destroy everything you have worked for, so don't say something that makes God angry.
7Respect and obey God! Daydreaming leads to a lot of senseless talk.
8Don't be surprised if the poor of your country are abused, and injustice takes the place of justice. After all, the lower officials must do what the higher ones order them to do. 9And since the king is the highest official, he benefits most from the taxes paid on the land.
10If you love money and wealth, you will never be satisfied with what you have. This doesn't make a bit of sense. 11The more you have, the more everyone expects from you. Your money won't do you any good—others will just spend it for you. 12If you have to work hard for a living, you can rest well at night, even if you don't have much to eat. But if you are rich, you can't even sleep.
13I have seen something terribly unfair. People get rich, but it does them no good. 14Suddenly they lose everything in a bad business deal, then have nothing to leave for their children. 15 They came into this world naked, and when they die, they will be just as naked. They can't take anything with them, and they won't have anything to show for all their work. 16That's terribly unfair. They leave the world just as they came. They gained nothing from running after the wind. 17Besides all this, they are always gloomy at mealtime, and they are troubled, sick, and bitter.
18What is the best thing to do in the short life God has given us? I think we should enjoy eating, drinking, and working hard. This is what God intends for us to do. 19Suppose you are very rich and able to enjoy everything you own. Then go ahead and enjoy working hard—this is God's gift to you. 20God will keep you so happy that you won't have time to worry about each day.
translation_text:
1Á dàkafì tiŋan kí wàatī kí nín sòoǹ, kí taa jìkì kí pòon̄ Unimbɔti ipoon. Di sá yii Unimbɔti bí yilpu ní sii bí kitiŋ pu. An puee á taa nín̄ sòoǹ tikpil. 2Unil yaa dàkafī tikpilee, u dámintí tidamintiil ní, ní un sòoǹ tikpilee sòoǹ tibɔfan. 3A yaa pōoǹ Unimbɔti ipoonee, taa tàan̄ kí ŋá tin a pōoǹ-uee. Di sá yii Unimbɔti kaa gèetíǹ bin ŋáań tibɔti kaa dàkafēe. An puee a yaa pōoǹ-u puee, á ŋá míǹ. 4An sɔ́ á taa pōoǹ Unimbɔti ipoon ki jítiǹ á pòon̄-u ní kí taa ŋmā kí ŋá tin a pōoǹee. 5Taa yàntī a-nyɔkɔ ń ŋmátí-si á ŋá ikpiti ki dāa gíti cá ki tùkù usaraaŋal yii: «M sòon̄ ki yīntì ní.» An yaa sá fám, Unimbɔti làá gíí a-pu diŋuul tin a sòon̄ee pu, ní kí nàan̄ a-tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ. 6Unil yaa dámintí tikpilee, u sòoǹ tikpil ní an kaa cáá taapu. Míǹ puee fàŋkì Unimbɔti.
Biyidambi cáá bi-pɔŋŋu ki tūǹ atummɔnti
7A yaa ká kitiŋ kiban bi bí ki wɔ́b̀ unandaan, kaa nóó marab nì ibaamɔn saŋŋuee, án taa ŋá-si bitii. Di sá yii ukàlinjakpaan ubɔ yaa bí yilpuee, ukpil ubɔ di bí ki wúń u-pu, ní bi-liitil cáá bikpikpaambi bin mun wúń bi mun puee. 8Ama kitiŋ kíǹ kèetī báà ŋma ní. Tikpaal kèetī ki kpáaǹ ubɔti.
Tigaajati kaa sá tiba
9Unil un néeń animbilee kaa díkì animbil, míǹ ní un néeń tigaajatee, tin u cááyee kaa fáatiǹ-u. Tinee mun sá kii bi nín jì kubuŋu puee ní. 10Unil yaa cáá tigaajati tikpilee, binib bin jīǹ-tèe mun wīikí ní. Mimmee ipaati ilai ní udaan cáá, an yaa kaa sá ú nīn cáa kɔ̀ntī u-nimbiliŋ? 11Utɔntɔnli yaa cáá tikpil kí jāaa, u yaa cáá fiii kí jāaa, u gèeǹ mmɔntiim ní. Ama ugaaja úǹ kaa ŋūǹ kí gèeǹ, kun puee u cáá tigaajawan tikpil. 12M dáań ki ká dinimbinaamandi bɔti tiba kitiŋ pu doo. Kijapaai kiba di kpáafì tigaajati ki yóoǹ, ní tigaajatee dāa cáań-u nnaabu. 13U dū tigaajatee ki túń ditundi diba ní ki lítì. U dāa màl̄ kibininjabikee, waa ti cáá báà tiba nì tiba. 14Kii u nín nyánní u-na poon dicancaŋgbeel puee, míǹ ní u làá fàtīí gítí. Waa pée páatì u-tundi pu, kaa làá ŋmā kí kpáaǹ báà tiba. 15An sá nnaabukpaan ní ki tīī-u. U làá yīkì kitiŋ nee pu kii u nín dɔ́miń puee. U túń ditundi ki tīī kubuŋu dee. 16Kí kūtèe, u-maŋfal wiiŋyi poonee, u ká agìń tikpil nì kunimbaau nì diŋuul nì diwuŋyɔtil. 17An puee man nín dàkafī puee di sá yii tin ŋān̄ ki tīī unilee di sá ú jī, kí nyɔ̀ ní kí jī u-tundi pu u-maŋfal wiiŋyi in Unimbɔti tīī-uee. Unil gìńdi paatii dee. 18Unimbɔti yaa pú unil diyimɔɔl ú nīn cáá animbil nì tigaajawanee, ú jī tin Unimbɔti tīī-uee pu, an dàkà yii u-tundi paati. Unimbɔti di pú-u. 19Niinee ní ú súntí yii u-maŋfal wiiŋyi kaa náaǹ, kun puee Unimbɔti tīī-u dipɔɔpindi.

english_text:
Don't Depend on Wealth
1There is something else terribly unfair, and it troubles everyone on earth. 2God may give you everything you want—money, property, and wealth. Then God doesn't let you enjoy it, and someone you don't even know gets it all. That's senseless and terribly unfair!
3You may live a long time and have a hundred children. But a child born dead is better off than you, unless you enjoy life and have a decent burial. 4-5That child will never live to see the sun or to have a name, and it will go straight to the world of darkness. But it will still find more rest than you, 6even if you live two thousand years and don't enjoy life. As you know, we all end up in the same place.
7We struggle just to have enough to eat, but we are never satisfied. 8We may be sensible, yet we are no better off than a fool. And if we are poor, it still doesn't do us any good to try to live right. 9It's better to enjoy what we have than to always want something else, because that makes no more sense than chasing the wind.
10Everything that happens was decided long ago. We humans know what we are like, and we can't argue with God, because he is too strong for us. 11The more we talk, the less sense we make, so what good does it do to talk? 12Life is short and meaningless, and it fades away like a shadow. Who knows what is best for us? Who knows what will happen after we are gone?
translation_text:
1M gíti tí dáań ki ká nnaabu ŋubɔ mun kitiŋ pu doo, an sá nnaabukpaan ní ki tīī unil. 2Unil di bí ní Unimbɔti tīī-u tigaajati nì tigaajawan nì tinyool. Tin kɔkɔ pée kā unil gbanti naŋki puee, u cáá-tì. Ama ní Unimbɔti kaa pú-u ú jī an wantee pu, ní unifantanti ubɔ ń dāá jī-tì. Tíǹ gbanti mun sá kii unil nín jì kubuŋu puee ní, ki sá falaakpaan. 3Unil ŋūǹ kí màal̀ mbiyaamu dilaataal, kí kàl̄ kitiŋ pu kí yúntí. U nín kāl̀ ki yúntì mimmee, u yaa kaa jíń nnaam ní baa kpáàa síb́-u mmɔntiimee, u páatì ba? Man ká yii kibiki kin bi màl̄ kaa yōoǹee sɔ́ǹ udaan. 4Di sá yii kíǹ dɔ́miń fám ní, ki fātìi gítì dibɔmbɔndin ní dibɔmbɔndi bīiǹ ki-yindi pu. 5Kí kūtèe, kàa pée ká ŋwìiń gba ní kaa nín béè-ŋu. An puee kíǹ cáá diŋuŋfil ki jítiǹ un kāl̀ ki yúntì kitiŋ pu doo fámee. 6Báà udaan yaa kāl̀ kitiŋ pu doo abin kutukub bili, ama ní kaa jíń mmɔnee, u páatì ba? Di sá yii kufoou kamaa làá kúntíǹ ŋkúm ní.
7Unil tūǹ ditundi u-pool pu ní, ama ní kaa díkì dalba dalba. 8Kin ba ní uciŋfiti cáá ki jítiǹ ugbaan? Unandaan un còom̄ disaŋkimmɔntiil binifoobi kansikinee úǹ páatì ba? 9Tiwan tin a cáá a-nimbil wāĺee sɔ́ǹ tin a là kí nīn cááyee. Niin mun pée sá fám ní, a lì kii unil nín jì kubuŋu puee.
Uciŋfiti saŋkii
10Tin kɔkɔ pée bée, bi nìn pée nyí-tì dooooyee ní, ní ti nyí kun unil sée. Waa ŋūǹ kí yíiń un pɔ̄ɔǹ-uee ibeeyiin. 11A yaa sòoǹ tikpilee, a sòoǹ tibɔti tin kaa cáá taapuee mun tikpil ní. Ipaati ilai di bí poon. 12Unil maŋfal jītí malaa kii mboonee ní. Ŋma di nyí tin ŋān̄ ki tīī unil u-maŋfal wiiŋyi in kaa kpáàa náaǹ nee poon? Ubɔ kaa làá ŋmā kí tùkù-u tin làá bàń kitiŋ nee pu u-kpátam boonee.

english_text:
The Best in Life
1 A good reputation
at the time of death
is better than loving care
at the time of birth.
2It's better to go to a funeral
than to attend a feast;
funerals remind us
that we all must die.
3Choose sorrow over laughter
because a sad face
may hide a happy heart.
4A sensible person mourns,
but fools always laugh.
5Correction from someone wise
is better by far
than praise from fools.
6Foolish laughter is stupid.
It sounds like thorns
crackling in a fire.
7Corruption makes fools
of sensible people,
and bribes can ruin you.
8Something completed is better
than something just begun;
patience is better
than too much pride.
9 Only fools get angry quickly
and hold a grudge.
10It isn't wise to ask,
“Why is everything worse
than it used to be?”
11Having wisdom is better
than an inheritance.
12Wisdom will protect you
just like money;
knowledge with good sense
will lead you to life.
13Think of what God has done!
If God makes something crooked,
can you make it straight?
14When times are good,
you should be cheerful;
when times are bad,
think about what it means.
God makes them both
to keep us from knowing
what will happen next.
Some of Life's Questions
15I have seen everything during this senseless life of mine. I have seen good citizens die for doing the right thing, while criminals live and prosper. 16So don't destroy yourself by being too good or acting too smart! 17Don't die before your time by being too evil or acting like a fool. 18Keep to the middle of the road. You can do this if you truly respect God.
19Wisdom will make you stronger than the ten most powerful leaders in your city.
20No one in this world always does right.
21Don't listen to everything that everyone says, or you might hear your servant cursing you. 22Haven't you cursed many others?
23I told myself that I would be smart and try to understand all this, but it was too much for me. 24The truth is beyond us. It's far too deep. 25So I decided to learn everything I could and become wise enough to discover what life is all about. At the same time, I wanted to understand why it's stupid and senseless to be an evil fool.
26Here is what I discovered: A bad woman is worse than death. She is a trap, reaching out with body and soul to catch you. But if you obey God, you can escape. If you don't obey, you are done for. 27With all my wisdom I have tried to find out how everything fits together, 28but so far I have not been able to. I do know there is one good man in a thousand, but never have I found a good woman. 29I did learn one thing: We were completely honest when God created us, but now we have twisted minds.
translation_text:
1Diyimmɔntiil sɔ́ǹ talaalumɔnti, ní unil kúm dal sɔ́ǹ ŋwiin ŋun bi màl̄-uee.
2Á kɔ́ dikpɔcindin sɔ́ǹ á kɔ́ dicindi din poon binib bí ki jīǹ jiŋaalee. Di sá yii unil sá kamaa kúntilaŋki di sá ŋkúm, ní an ŋān̄ yii unifoo kamaa ń nīn téetí an pu.
3Kunimbaau sɔ́ǹ tilaal, di sá yii binib ŋūǹ kí nīn wāĺ yii a bí kunimbaaun, ama ní a-pɔbil bí mmɔnni.
4Dikpɔcindin ní a kāntí uciŋfiti,
ama ugbaan úǹ néeń dijiŋaacindin ní.
5Á kíí uciŋfiti ń wòoǹ-si sɔ́ǹ á nīn bí ki pílifí ugbaan gà ilan ki nyɔ́ŋkí-si. 6Di sá yii ugbaan laati sá kii idɔ in bí dikumbool taapu ki pòol̄ee ní. An mun sá kii bi nín jì kubuŋu puee ní.
7Uciŋfiti un cáá mpɔn ki wɔ́b̀ binibee ŋūǹ kí kpántí ugbaan, ní dinyɔɔŋeebil jim ŋūǹ kí yàntī u-pɔbil ń gáatí.
8Tiwan kúntitam sɔ́ǹ ti-kíltam. An sɔ́ á nīn cáá kimɔtii ki jítiǹ á nīn cáá dibayoondi.
9Taa nín̄ gífí diŋuul malaa malaa, di sá yii ugbaan di kaa pɔ̄ɔ̄ diŋuul digiil.
10Taa lì yii: «Ba ŋá ní dooooyee nìn ŋān̄ ki jítiǹ kɔŋkɔnnee?» Un bàlifī mimmee kaa sá uciŋfiti. 11Iciin cáá kudapɔɔu kii difakalee ní, i kèetī báà ŋma ní. 12Iciin wúǹ unil pu kii animbilee ní. Bin cáá-iee kàal̀ kitiŋ pu kí yúntí ní. An pu ní an páb́ yii unil ń béé-i.
13Kpèè ditundi din Unimbɔti túńee kɔkɔ. Ŋma di ŋūǹ kí tàntī tiwan tin u nyīī ki pɔ́ĺee?
14Tikɔkɔ yaa còom̄ nì si tiŋanee, nín̄ bí dipɔɔpindin. An yaa kaa ti ŋān̄ee, á dàkafì. Unimbɔti di yàntī nnaam nì nnaabu dòoń, mimmee taa làá béé tin làá dāan̄ee.
15M-maŋfal din kaa bí tiban nee poonee, m ká tikɔkɔ. M dáań ki ká yii deedeedaan kúù u-deedeeu pu, ní ukpitiŋal bí dimaŋfalin u-kpitii pu. 16Taa nín̄ dàkafī yii a sá deedeedaan tikpil, kí taa nín̄ yíì a-ba uciŋfiti. Ba pu ní a là kí bīil̀ a-ba? 17Taa dū a-ba kí líiǹ ikpiti diŋál, kí taa nín̄ sá ugbaan. Ba pu ní a là kí kpú kaa bàn̄ a-wiiŋŋu? 18An ŋān̄ á nīn ŋúb́ isaŋki gbanti liitil, di sá yii unil un fàŋkí Unimbɔtee di ŋūǹ kí ŋá tibɔti gbanti liitil.
19Iciin yàntī uciŋfiti cáá mpɔn ki jítiǹ gɔminab saalaa bin kpáfì ki kpòotī kitimbaantiiyee.
20Deedeedaan ubɔ pée kpá kitiŋ pu doo kí lì yii úǹ ŋūǹ kí ŋá tiŋan kí taa yìntī.
21Taa nín̄ pílifí tin kɔkɔ binib sòoǹee. Mimmee aa dāa gbìl̀ a-tɔntɔnliu sòoǹ ki bíiĺ-si. 22Sii a-ba mun pée nyí yii iyunti iba poonee, a sòon̄ ki bíil̀ biba.
23Tin bí nee kɔkɔee, m dū iciin ki mākaǹ ki kpēē. M lī yii: «M làá nīn cáá iciin», ama ní i dáá gbíntìi dátiǹ-mi. 24Ŋma di ŋūǹ kí gbìl̄ tin nyáń ki bée taapu? An dátiǹ-ti ní ki nyóò lúkú luku. 25Niinee m dū m-ba ki tīī kí nyàab̀ kí béé kun di sá iciinee. M nyàab̄ kí gbìl̄ kun pu ní tiwan dòoń ki jītée. M bífì ki béè mun yii ntoom nì digbaandi kɔkɔ sá kuwaatiiu ní. 26M dáań ki ká tin bí nee: unimpu un sàtī bininjabee cāabìń ntuntun kii ŋkúmee ní. U-neendi sá kii kutaliŋŋuee ní, ní u-ŋalii sá kii ikusakee. Unil un bɔti fáatiǹ Unimbɔtee ŋmátí kí nyā u-ŋaan, ama un yaa sá unikpitee, asee ú ŋmā udaan. 27Uciŋfiti lī yii: M cɔ́ŋkì ki kpēē tiwan kɔkɔ kubɔ kubɔ kí béé ti-taapu. 28M nyàab̄ ki tin gīī kaa ŋúń ki béè. Bininjab kutuku poonee, m ká yii ubɔbɔ di pée sá uŋman. Ama binimpoobi kɔkɔ poonee, maa ká báà ubɔ. 29Tin man dáań ki kée di sá yii Unimbɔti náań unil u bí deedee, ama ní unil nyàab̄ agìń tikpil ki tɔ́ u-ba pu.

english_text:
1Who is smart enough
to explain everything?
Wisdom makes you cheerful
and gives you a smile.
Obey the King
2If you promised God that you would be loyal to the king, I advise you to keep that promise. 3Don't quickly oppose the king or argue when he has already made up his mind. 4The king's word is law. No one can ask him, “Why are you doing this?” 5If you obey the king, you will stay out of trouble. So be wise and learn what to do and when to do it. 6Life is hard, but there is a time and a place for everything, 7though no one can tell the future. 8We cannot control the wind or determine the day of our death. There is no escape in time of war, and no one can hide behind evil. 9I noticed all this and thought seriously about what goes on in the world. Why does one person have the power to hurt another?
Who Can Understand the Ways of God?
10I saw the wicked buried with honor, but God's people had to leave the holy city and were forgotten. None of this makes sense. 11When we see criminals commit crime after crime without being punished, it makes us want to start a life of crime. 12They commit hundreds of crimes and live a long time, in spite of the saying:
Everyone who lives right
and respects God
will prosper,
13but no one who sins
and rejects God
will prosper or live very long.
14There is something else that doesn't make sense to me. Good citizens are treated as criminals, while criminals are honored as though they were good citizens. 15So I think we should get as much out of life as we possibly can. There is nothing better than to enjoy our food and drink and have a good time. Then we can make it through this troublesome life that God has given us here on earth.
16Day and night I went without sleep, trying to understand what goes on in this world. 17I saw everything God does, and I realized no one can really understand what happens. We may be very wise, but no matter how much we try or how much we claim to know, we cannot understand it all.
translation_text:
1Ubɔ kaa sá uciŋfiti, ubɔ kaa nyí kí lēē tin dòońee taapu kí lì. Ama unil ciiŋyi yàntī u-nimbiin ń bútí ní u-nimbiin nín bàà kūń puee ń cúú kpántí.
Un tɔ́ ubɔtee sá uciŋfiti
2Ubɔti yaa lī puee, á ŋá míǹ kii ti nín pūtì ki pōoǹ Unimbɔti nimbiin puee. 3Á taa kàkatī a-ba kí wàatī-u malaa. Taa nín̄ nìkì ki ŋáań tin kaa fáatiǹ-uee, di sá yii u ŋáań u nín là puee ní. 4Ubɔti nyɔɔbundi cáá mpɔn, ní ubɔ kaa ŋūǹ kí bàlifì-u yii: «Ba ní a ŋáań nee?». 5Un yaa tɔ́ ubɔtee kpá kí kɔ́ tibɔtin. Ama uciŋfiti úǹ nyí tiŋan yii ibɔsoon yuntiŋu bí ki dòoń. 6Tiŋman, ŋwindal bí, Unimbɔti làá dāá sòoǹ unil bɔti kí nóó nì atuun ŋin u túńee, ama nnaabukpaan dɔ̄ ki cí unil. 7Unil kaa nyí tin bí ki dòońee, kaa nyí ŋyunti ŋun tì làá dāan̄ee. 8Unil kaa yì u-maŋfal kí cúú-dì kí taa kpú. Ubɔ kaa tí cáá mpɔn kí sútí u-kúm wiiŋŋu. Kujaau yaa nyáńee, kuaa gàntī ubɔ, ní inikpiti kaa fìil̄ ukpitiŋal.
Nisaal falaau
9M ká tíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ: m kpēē tin kɔkɔ pée bí ki jītí kitiŋ pu dooyee tiŋan. An sá laakin ní binib tɔ́kɔ́ bi-jutiibi pu ki ŋáań-bi tikpitilee. 10M ká binikpitib kpíì bi bíi ŋáań bi-kpool. Binib gbanti nìn cáà kunimbɔtidiin múlmul. Bi nìn súntì Jeerusaleem tiŋkin atuŋkpiti ŋin kɔkɔ bi ŋée. Tíǹ mun pée tí sá kii bi nín jì kubuŋu puee ní. 11Unil yaa ŋá ikpitee, waa fòol̄ ditafadaaldi dicilpu niin. An pu ní binib néeń ki tūǹ atuŋkpiti tikpil. 12Unikpiti ŋūǹ kí ŋá ikpiti ŋfunyɔm dilaataal pu, ama ní kí kàl̄ kitiŋ pu kí yúntí. Ama m gíti nyí mun yii bin fàŋkí Unimbɔtee bí mmɔnni, kun puee bi cáá Unimbɔti faaŋku. 13Unikpiti kaa làá nīn bí nnaamin. U làá jītí malaa kii mboonee, u-maŋfal wiiŋyi kaa làá nīn náaǹ, kun puee waa cáá Unimbɔti faaŋku. 14Tiba gíti bí kitiŋ pu doo kaa cáá taapu. Binib bí ki sá deedeedambi, ki fòol̄ binikpitib paati. Ní binikpitib bí ki fòol̄ deedeedambi nín máaǹ tipaal tiŋyee. M lī ki gíti bíi bùsī ki lì yii tíǹ sá kii bi nín jì kubuŋu puee ní.
15An puee m tìì kunyannyaau kí jī mmɔn. Di sá yii kun pée ŋūǹ kí nīn sá nnaam ki tīī unil kitiŋ nee puee di sá ú jī, kí nyɔ̀ kí gbìl̄ mmɔn. Tíǹ di ŋūǹ kí céeǹ unil u-tundi poon iwiin in Unimbɔti tīī-u ú dūú kàl̄ kitiŋ pu dooyee. 16M lēē m-pɔbil poon yii m làá nyàab̀ kí béé iciin, ní kí kpèè atuun ŋin kɔkɔ binib tūǹ kitiŋ pu doo kaa gèeǹ ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeuee soooo. 17Niinee ní m ká Unimbɔti tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ. Unil kaa ŋūǹ kí nyàab̀ kí ká atuun ŋin bi tūǹ kitiŋ pu dooyee kɔkɔ. Min kamaa unil gì ki nyàab̀ee, u pée kpá kí ká. Baa gba uciŋfiti yaa bí yii u nyí, waa làá ŋmā kí ká.

english_text:
One Day at a Time
1I thought about these things. Then I understood that God has power over everyone, even those who are wise and live right. Anything can happen to any one of us, and so we never know if life will be good or bad. 2But exactly the same thing will finally happen to all of us, whether we live right and respect God or sin and don't respect God. Yes, the same thing will happen if we offer sacrifices to God or if we don't, if we keep our promises or are afraid to make them.
3It's terribly unfair for the same thing to happen to each of us. We are mean and foolish while we live, and then we die. 4As long as we are alive, we still have hope, just as a live dog is better off than a dead lion. 5We know we will die, but the dead don't know a thing. Nothing good will happen to them—they are gone and forgotten. 6Their loves, their hates, and their jealous feelings have all disappeared with them. They will never again take part in anything that happens on this earth.
7So be happy and enjoy eating and drinking! God decided long ago that this is what you should do. 8Dress up, comb your hair, and look your best. 9Life is short, and you love your wife, so enjoy being with her. This is what you are supposed to do as you struggle through life on this earth. 10Work hard at whatever you do. You will soon go to the world of the dead, where no one works or thinks or reasons or even knows anything.
11Here is something else I have learned:
The fastest runners
and the greatest heroes
don't always win races
and battles.
Wisdom, intelligence, and skill
don't always make you healthy,
rich, or popular.
We each have our own share
of misfortune.
12None of us know when we might fall victim to a sudden disaster and find ourselves like fish in a net or birds in a trap.
Better To Be Wise than Foolish
13Once I saw what people really think of wisdom, and it made an impression on me. 14It happened when a powerful ruler surrounded and attacked a small city where only a few people lived. The enemy army was getting ready to break through the city walls. 15But the city was saved by the wisdom of a poor person who was soon forgotten. 16So I decided that wisdom is better than strength. Yet if you are poor, no one pays any attention to you, no matter how smart you are.
17Words of wisdom spoken softly
make much more sense
than the shouts of a ruler
to a crowd of fools.
18Wisdom is more powerful
than weapons,
yet one mistake can destroy
all the good you have done.
translation_text:
1M dākafì tin bí nee kɔkɔ pu ní tin m kée sèé: deedeedambi nì biciŋfitiibi nì bi-tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ kā Unimbɔti ŋaan ní. Binib kaa kpáàa nyí bi yaa làá ká dineendi àá kináŋ. Baa nyí kun dɔ̄ ki cí-bee. 2Tibɔbaantiilee di dɔ̄ ki cí báà ŋma. Tin làá bàń deedeedaanee, tíǹ di làá bàń ukpitiŋal. Tin làá bàń unimɔntee, tíǹ di làá bàń unikpiti. Tin làá bàń circirdaanee, tíǹ di làá bàń un kaa bí circiree. Tin làá bàń un ŋáań saraabee, tíǹ di làá bàń un kaa ŋáańee. Digàntil diba kaa bí unimɔnti nì unikpiti kansikin, un pòontí Unimbɔti ipoonee nì un fàŋkí kí pòon̄ee. 3Tibɔbaantiil di bàń báà ŋma, ní tin an cāabìńee kaa ŋān̄ kitiŋ pu doo. An di yì-tì ní ikpiti gbí binib pɔbiliŋin ní bi tūǹ agbaantuun, ní boonee bí kpú. 4Ama unil un bí dimaŋfalinee ŋūǹ kí nīn cáá dimákal, kun puee kibɔkɔ kin bí dimaŋfalinee sɔ́ǹ gbikinti un kpíìyee. 5Binifoobi di nyí yii bi bí ki làá kpú ŋwindal, ama bitaŋkpiibi bíǹ kaa ti nyí báà tiba pu. Baa ti cí kí fōō tipaal tiba, kun puee bi súntì bi-pu. 6Tin bi nìn néeńee nì tin bi nìn née nì bi-poompooŋyi kɔkɔ wáŋkì. Baa ti pée bí kí kūtì tin bí ki jītí kitiŋ pu dooyee poon.
7An puee jī a-jinti nì mmɔn, kí nyɔ̀ a-daam nì dipɔɔpindi, di sá yii a-tuuŋŋi fáatiǹ Unimbɔti dooooyee. 8Á nīn pée pèentí ajiŋaabɔkuti, kí taa súntí kí yàaǹ a-yil pu talaalu. 9Sii nì unimpu un a néeńee ń jī mmɔn a-maŋfal wiiŋyi in kaa náaǹ Unimbɔti tīī-si á dūú kàl̄ kitiŋ nee puee. Tiŋman, a-maŋfal wiiŋyi kaa náaǹ ní ditundi din a túń kitiŋ nee puee paati dee. 10Ditundi din kamaa a pée ŋūǹ kí tɔ̄ee, tɔ̄-dì nì a-pɔŋŋu kɔkɔ. Di sá yii ditaŋkpiilin laakin a cée, aa ŋūǹ kí tɔ̄ dibaaa, kaa ŋūǹ kí dàkafàaa, dinyil kpáaa, iciin mun kpá.
Kaa sá tikɔkɔ poon ní iciin tūǹ ditundi
11M gíti dáań ki ká kitiŋ pu doo nee tiba. An kaa sá ŋyunti kamaa ní bin yáb̀ee sáń kí jī ditaatandi kpaŋkpakantikuu. Bibaatandambi kaa tí jáà ki jīǹ ŋyunti kamaa. Biciŋfitiibi kaa tí kāntí ki jīǹ sɔkɔmii. Binyiliibi kaa tí sá bin cáá tigaajati ki jítiǹ bin kíǹee. Bin yiliŋ poon tūǹ ditundi tikpilee kaa tí sá bin ní bi tìì jilmee. Di sá yii bi-kɔkɔ kāntí nnaam nì nnaabu. 12Tiŋman, unil kaa nyí tin làá bàń-uee. Kii kulaaŋŋu nín sàtī ijɔm pu, àá kii bi nín pīil̀ kí sàl̄ unoon puee, míǹ ní unil kā ní nnaabu ń dāá túuǹ-u.
13M gíti dáań ki ká tiba kitiŋ nee pu ní an yāntì m gíti dākafì iciin pu. 14Kitimbilii kiba di bí ní ki-nib kaa náaǹ báà fiii. Ní ubɔtikpaan ubɔ dɔ́miń kí já nì kì. U nìn píĺ píĺ kujaau talinti ki māntìi tú-kì. 15Unandaan ubɔ nìn kóò kitimbiliiyee poon ki sá uciŋfiti. U bàà nìn ŋūǹ kí dū u-ciiŋyi kí fīī kitimbiliiyee, ama ní báà ubɔ kaa nìn téetì u-pu. 16An pu ní man lī yii iciin sɔ́ǹ mpɔn, ama uciŋfiti yaa sá unandaanee, binib ŋèeǹ nì u ní, kaa pílifí tin u sòoǹee. 17Bi pílifí uciŋfiti un sòoǹ sooooyee nyɔɔbuŋŋi ki jítiǹ ubɔti un tìì bigbaambi marab ki tátée. 18Iciin sɔ́ǹ tijanjawan, ama ní ukpitiŋal ubaanti bíiĺ tiwammɔntiil tikpil.

english_text:
1A few dead flies in perfume
make all of it stink,
and a little foolishness
outweighs a lot of wisdom.
2Sensible thoughts lead you
to do right;
foolish thoughts lead you
to do wrong.
3Fools show their stupidity
by the way they live;
it's easy to see
they have no sense.
4Don't give up your job
when your boss gets angry.
If you stay calm,
you'll be forgiven.
5Rulers do some things that are terribly unfair: 6They honor fools, but dishonor the rich; 7they let slaves ride on horses, but force slave owners to walk.
8 If you dig a pit,
you might fall in;
if you break down a wall,
a snake might bite you.
9You could even get hurt
by chiseling a stone
or chopping a log.
10If you don't sharpen your ax,
it will be harder to use;
if you are wise,
you'll know what to do.
11The power to charm a snake
does you no good
if it bites you anyway.
12If you talk sensibly,
you will have friends;
if you talk foolishly,
you will destroy yourself.
13Fools begin with nonsense,
and their stupid chatter
ends with disaster.
14They never tire of talking,
but none of us really know
what the future will bring.
15Fools wear themselves out—
they don't know enough
to find their way home.
16A country is in for trouble
when its ruler is childish,
and its leaders
party all day long.
17But a nation will prosper
when its ruler is mature,
and its leaders
don't party too much.
18Some people are too lazy
to fix a leaky roof—
then the house collapses.
19Eating and drinking
make you feel happy,
and money can buy
everything you need.
20Don't let yourself think about
cursing the king;
don't curse the rich,
not even in secret.
A little bird might hear
and tell everything.
translation_text:
1Isii yaa jéetì talaalu kpam poonee, i yàntī mí nūukì ní kí bīil̀. Míǹ ní digbaandi fiii bíiĺ iciin nì tinyool. 2Uciŋfiti dàkafī tiŋan ní, ama ugbaan úǹ kaa gbìl̀ tibɔti taapu.
3Ugbaan yaa bíi còom̄ didandi puee, kii nlandɔkɔmɔnti nín kaa bí u-yilin puee, un kamaa yaa ká-uee béetí yii u sá ugbaan ní.
4A-kpiliu yaa gíí a-pu diŋuulee, taa dū a-tundi kí fá. A yaa cúú a-ba, an yàntī á taa kɔ́ diyintikpaandi poon.
5Ubɔti mun ŋūǹ kí yìntī. Míǹ ní m dáań ki ká dimuuldi kitiŋ nee pu. 6Ŋyunti ŋubɔee, bi dù ugbaan ní kí kàan̄ mpaaŋkpaan pu, ní kí dū ntuŋwaamu kí ŋúbíǹ biniŋmambi. 7M ká iyumbu kā itaamu pu ama ní binikpaambi còom̄ ataa pu fám kii iyumbuee.
8Unil yaa bíi gbì mbòóyee, u ŋūǹ kí dāá jēetí ŋu-poon, ukoobu ŋūǹ kí jú un bíi wìil̄ digundee. 9Unil yaa bíi kpìkitī ataŋkpeeyee, ŋi ŋūǹ kí tīī-u tiweendi, míǹ ní un bíi látí idɔee, an ŋūǹ ki cáań-u in bí iwa.
10Kicɔkɔ yaa gbītì ní baa lōoǹ-kì, ní a cáa bíi tūǹ ditundee, asee á mɔ̀tīí dàkà dikpabil ní kí ŋmā kí dūú gāā tiba. Di sá yii iciin di yàntī tin unil bíi ŋáańee ń nyā nnyim.
11Un cáá nnyɔkɔ ki cútí ikoobuee yaa yāntì ukoobu péé-u dijulee, u páatì u-nyɔkɔŋuee pu ba?
Taa nín̄ sòoǹ tikpil
12Uciŋfiti yaa sòoǹee, an mɔ̄ dipilifil ní. Ama ugbaan nyɔɔbuŋŋi yàntī u wáŋkí ní. 13U kífí kí sòoǹ tigbaambɔti ní kí dāá kúntíǹ tinifambɔti tin kaa cáá taapuee. 14Ugbaan di sòoǹ ki sòoǹ kaa ŋmīlifí. Ama unil úǹ kaa nyí tin bí ki dòońee. Ŋma ŋūǹ kí tùkù u-juti tin bí ki dòoń udaan kpátam boonee? 15Ugbaan di gì digìńdi fám. Waa kpáàa nyí gba u nín làá túĺ pu kí cù kitiŋinee.
16Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí kitiŋ kin bɔtiu sá campɔnti ní ki-kàliŋkpilib nyēē ki jīǹ jiŋaalib baabadalee! 17Án nīn mɔ̄ǹ kitiŋ kin bɔtiu nyánní dibeecindin àá akpambal dicaŋkunee, ki-kàliŋkpilib jīǹ bi-jinti ŋyunti ŋun ní an máaǹ bí jēe ní. Bi jīǹ kí ká mpɔn ní, kaa sá kí nyɔ̀ kí gbí.
18Uwutijoodaan diiku bɔ̀b̀ ní. Unil un kpàl̄ iŋal kaa tūǹ dibee, utaa nì u-diikun ní.
19Bigaajab jīǹ jiŋaal kí kɔ̀ntī bi-nimbiliŋ ní. Ndaam tìì-bi mmɔn, ní animbil yàntī bí ká tin kɔkɔ bí lèe. 20Á taa tɔ̄ ubɔti mbusu, báà a-pɔbilin. Á taa kpákáǹ binikpaambi, báà a-didooŋkaakun. Unoon ŋūǹ kí yòon̄ tin a sòon̄ee, kí dū tin a lēe kí māafì.

english_text:
It Pays To Work Hard
1Be generous, and someday
you will be rewarded.
2Share what you have
with seven or eight others,
because you never know
when disaster may strike.
3Rain clouds always bring rain;
trees always stay
wherever they fall.
4If you worry about the weather
and don't plant seeds,
you won't harvest a crop.
5No one can explain how a baby breathes before it is born. So how can anyone explain what God does? After all, God created everything.
6Plant your seeds early in the morning and keep working in the field until dark. Who knows? Your work might pay off, and your seeds might produce.
Youth and Old Age
7Nothing on earth is more beautiful than the morning sun. 8Even if you have a very long life, you should try to enjoy each day, because darkness will come and will last a long time. Nothing makes sense.
9Be cheerful and enjoy life while you are young! Do what you want and find pleasure in what you see. But don't forget that God will judge you for everything you do.
10Rid yourself of all worry and pain, because the wonderful moments of youth quickly disappear.
translation_text:
Tí màkan̄ kí kpèè
1Dū a-kpɔnɔu kí tɔ̄ nnyimin, di sá yii a làá dāá fàtīí ká-u iwiin iba boon. 2Dū a-gaajati kí yóoń binib biluli kii binii cee, di sá yii aa nyí mbusu un di ŋūǹ kí dāá bàń kitiŋ puee.
3Atagban yaa nyùn̄ nnyim ki díkée ní utaa ń kíĺ kí nīn bíi nì. Busubu ŋūǹ kí lítí ŋgiil pú àá ŋgan pú. Báà laakin ní bu yaa lítèe, niin ní bu làá nīn dɔ̄.
4Ukpaal un fàŋkí kubuŋuee kaa kù kí bɔ̄l̀. Un fàŋkí utaayee kaa dāa kāntí kí cā.
5Aa ŋūǹ kí béé an nín ŋáań pu ní kibiki ń náań ki-na poonee, kaa tí nyí laakin kufoou nyēeńee. Míǹ mbaantiim ní aa làá ŋmā kí gbìl̄ Unimbɔti nín tūǹ u-tundi puee taapu, úǹ un náań tikɔkɔee. 6An puee á kíĺ kutaafaau kí kpɔ̀ kí bɔ̄l̀ a-wamboolii kí tɔ̄ ditundi kí jóotí-ku. Di sá yii aa nyí a-tuuŋŋi kansikin din làá bútí-see. An yaa yíì a ŋūǹ kí páatí a-tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ pu.
7Ŋwalifi mɔ̄ dikpeel, ní an ŋān̄ unil ń nīn bí dimaŋfalin. 8Unil yaa kāl̀ kitiŋ pu ki yúntèe, u máaǹ kí jī abin gbanti kɔkɔ pu. Tí téetí tin bí nee pu: dinimbinaamandi wiiŋyi di làá nīn wīikí, ní tin kɔkɔ dòońee sá kii kubuŋuee.
Tí jīmaan nnaam án taa nà-ti
9Unaacimpɔɔn, jī a-naacimpɔnti kí nīn bí mmɔnni ŋyunti gbanti poon. Pée ŋá tin a lèe nì tin fáatiǹ-see. Ama á nīn nyí ŋwindal Unimbɔti làá dāá sòoǹ a-bɔti ki nóó nì tin kɔkɔ a ŋée. 10Gɔ́ntí tin kamaa ŋūǹ kí yàntī á kɔ́ kunimbaaunee, kí kàkatī tin kɔkɔ pée ŋūǹ kí cáań-si igbaŋweenee. Di sá yii tinaacimpɔn nì tiyikpibɔn yuntiŋu jītí malaa ní.

english_text:
1Keep your Creator in mind while you are young! In years to come, you will be burdened down with troubles and say, “I don't enjoy life anymore.”
2Someday the light of the sun
and the moon and the stars
will all seem dim to you.
Rain clouds will remain
over your head.
3Your body will grow feeble,
your teeth will decay,
and your eyesight fail.
4The noisy grinding of grain
and the voices of singers
will be shut out
by your deaf ears,
but even the song of a bird
will keep you awake.
5You will be afraid
to climb up a hill
or walk down a road.
Your hair will turn as white
as almond blossoms.
You will feel lifeless
and drag along
like an old grasshopper.
We each go to our eternal home,
and the streets here are filled
with those who mourn.
6The silver cord snaps,
the golden bowl breaks;
the water pitcher is smashed,
and the pulley at the well
is shattered.
7So our bodies return
to the earth,
and the life-giving breath
returns to God.
8Nothing makes sense.
I have seen it all—
nothing makes sense.
Respect and Obey God
9I was a wise teacher with much understanding, and I collected a number of proverbs that I had carefully studied. 10Then I tried to explain these things in the best and most accurate way.
11Words of wisdom are like the stick a farmer uses to make animals move. These sayings come from a shepherd, and they are like nails that fasten things together. 12My child, I warn you to stay away from any teachings except these.
There is no end to books,
and too much study
will wear you out.
13Everything you were taught can be put into a few words:
Respect and obey God!
This is what life
is all about.
14God will judge
everything we do,
even what is done in secret,
whether good or bad.
translation_text:
1Taa súntí a-náanliu pu ŋyunti ŋun ní a dáá pɔ̀ɔǹee. Téetí u-pu kí wàatī ní iwiŋkpiti ń bàń, ŋyunti ŋun ní a làá dāá lì yii: «An kaa ti mɔ̄ǹ-mi ḿ nín bí dimaŋfalin.»
2Ŋyunti gbantee,
ŋwìiń nì ŋwalifi làá dāá dūú kpántí dibɔmbɔndi,
ní uŋmal nì iŋmalbijaa kaa dāa gíti wāĺ,
ní utaa tin lì yii u nì ki báatée atagban fātìi lúntì.
3Niinee udiciitil kíǹ ki jìkì tɔ́sí tɔsi,
ní bibaatandambi ń dūú pɔ́ĺ ki kíǹ ki bōō,
ní binimpoobi ń gbèen̄ dinanal bi nín kaa ti náaǹee pu,
ní bin gbōontí tɔkɔlabinee kaa ti cáá kunyaaŋŋu.
4Niinee kudii kun punyɔkɔki túĺ didandi púee dūu pīiǹ,
ní baa ti gbìl̀ tinàti pu.
Kinɔmbiki gbēeǹ kaa ti bíi sūǹ,
ní baa ti gbìl̀ ilan pu.
5Binib kíǹ ki fàŋkí kí dàb̄ kigbantaŋ pu,
ní dinyoondi bí nsan pu.
Tiyikpiti píil̀ kii nsupumpukumee,
ní tiwun dūu nyīŋfì kii unaakitoon di nyáń ki lítèe,
ní unil maŋfal ń lítí kii disubil di kītì ki lítèe.
Tiŋman ŋwiin bí ki dòoń báà ŋma làá kɔ́ dikaakulin
laakin sá u-kɔŋkooŋŋu njoolkaayee.
Ŋyunti gbantee, binib lālim̀ ki gbí didandi pu
kí sɔ̄ u-kpool.
6Niinee ní animbil kúti ŋmibiki ń cúú tìl̄,
ní sindaariya sambil ń cúú yàaǹ,
ní dibool din poon nnyim gbée ń lítí kí wīī,
ní guuka ŋmiiŋu ń kútí ní ú jēetí lɔkɔn.
7Niinee ní ntam ń fàtīí gítí kitiŋin laakin mì nyánnée,
ní kufoou ń fàtīí gítí Unimbɔti un tīī-kuee cee.
8Uciŋfiti di lī yii: <Kubuŋu fám, kubuŋu fám, tikɔkɔ pée sá kii kubuŋuee ní.
Tibɔkuntikaal
9Tin ti làá dūú kūtì tin bí nee puee di sá yii Uciŋfiti kaa dàkā yii u sá uciŋfiti ŋmaniŋma, ama u dàkā binib kun u nyée. U bɔ́ntì alaŋkpan tikpil, ki dākafì tiŋan ki nyàab̄ ŋi-taapu ki dɔ́ntì-ŋi. 10Uciŋfiti pɔ́ɔǹ u-ba ki nyàab̄ anyɔɔbummɔɔn ní ki dūu ŋmàn̄ tibɔŋman. 11Biciŋfitiibi nyɔɔbuŋŋi sá kii inyanyee ní, a lì kii akpakpaa ŋin bin ŋmàn̄ tigbɔnee dūu cóoǹee. Unimbɔti un sá upikpaabaantee di tìì tikɔkɔ. 12M-jipɔɔn, á taa pée kūtì tiba. Á ŋmà tigbɔnee sá ditundi din kaa kúntée ní, ní kí bīfì tikpil muee gì tiwun.
13Kí kúntí tin kɔkɔ bi sòon̄ neeyee, tin ti làá lèe sèé: Nín̄ fàŋkí Unimbɔti kí nīn tɔ́ u-marab. Tin unifoo kamaa máaǹ kí ŋée dee. 14Di sá yii Unimbɔti làá dāá sòoǹ tin kɔkɔ ti ŋée bɔti, ki kpáaǹ atummɔnti nì atuŋkpiti ŋin ti ŋá dibalinee.

english_text:
Love Is Better than Wine
1 This is Solomon's
most beautiful song.
She Speaks:
2Kiss me tenderly!
Your love is better than wine,
3and you smell so sweet.
All the young women adore you;
the very mention of your name
is like spreading perfume.
* 4Hurry, my king! Let's hurry.
Take me to your home.
The Young Women Speak:
We are happy for you!
And we praise your love
even more than wine.
She Speaks:
Young women of Jerusalem,
it is only right
that you should adore him.
5My skin is dark and beautiful,
like a tent in the desert
or like Solomon's curtains.
6Don't stare at me
just because the sun
has darkened my skin.
My brothers were angry with me;
they made me work in the vineyard,
and so I neglected
my complexion.
7My darling, I love you!
Where do you feed your sheep
and let them rest at noon?
Don't let the other shepherds
think badly of me.
I'm not one of those women
who shamelessly follow
after shepherds.
He Speaks:
8My dearest, if you don't know,
just follow the path
of the sheep.
Then feed your young goats
near the shepherds' tents.
9You move as gracefully
as the pony that leads
the chariot of the king.
10Earrings add to your beauty,
and you wear a necklace
of precious stones.
11Let's make you some jewelry
of gold, woven with silver.
She Speaks:
12My king, while you
were on your couch,
my aroma was a magic charm.
13My darling, you are perfume
between my breasts;
14you are flower blossoms
from the gardens of En-Gedi.
He Speaks:
15My darling, you are lovely,
so very lovely—
your eyes are those of a dove.
She Speaks:
16My love, you are handsome,
truly handsome—
the fresh green grass
will be our wedding bed
17in the shade of cedar
and cypress trees.
translation_text:
1Ilan kɔkɔ poonee, ŋunee di mɔ̄. Saloomɔn di ŋmàn̄-ŋu.
Bibɔntiibi bili
Usapɔɔn
2Kpàl̄-mi kí nákań a-ba,
móotí-mi!
A-neendi yàntī m gbéè
kii m nyùn̄ ndaamee,
3ki mɔ̄ ki jítiǹ
a-talaalub sɔnsɔfiŋu.
A bí kii talaalumɔntee ní.
An pu ní bisapɔmbi
kɔkɔ là-si!
4Kpáaǹ-mi kí cùnnì,
tí sāǹ dicilpu!
M-bɔtiu, cáá-mi
ki kɔ́ǹ a-diikun.
Niinee, sii puee,
ti làá nīn bí mmɔŋkpaanni.
Ti làá nyɔ̄ŋkì a-neendi din
nyàatī kii ndaamee.
Bisapɔmbi lafun cáá mbaamɔn
kí nīn néeń-si!
5M sá unibɔn,
ama m cáá kunyaaŋŋu.
M-wunti bɔ̀ǹ jíbjib
kii Keedaar yab tantibee,
ki ŋān̄ kii iŋaamɔnti in sàkā
kubɔtinaakoou punyɔkɔpuee.
Jeerusaleem sapɔmbi,
6ní taa kpèè m-wunti
nín bɔ̄ntì puee,
an sá ŋwìiń di gbáń-mi.
M-niijab di fōō m-pu diŋuul,
ní ki ŋá-mi mpɔn ḿ cīití bi-fiinyib.
Ama man m-ba fiinyibee,
maa cíitì!
7Sii un m néeńee, tùkù-mi
la ní a kpàá a-picaŋkpuŋku ní?
Tùkù-mi ŋwìiń yaa píĺee laakin a cáǹ-i
i dɔ̀ ki ŋùŋfēe?
Mimmee maa làá nīn gíti tú ki yìiǹ
a-bɔɔbi picaŋkpunti cee.
Bipikpaaliibi
8Unimpunyannyaan, a yaa kaa nyée,
nín̄ nóó ipii taaŋi,
kí kpàà a-ŋɔbiliŋ
bipikpaaliibi bimmu caŋin.
Unaacimpɔɔn
9M-bɔɔn, m dū-si ki ŋmāntiǹ
utannyaan un dátí Faaroo tɔrɔkuee ní.
10Falfatib bin a túuńee
tìì a-taŋkpunti kunyaaŋŋu.
A-leeŋkaati máaǹ a-neen.
Bipikpaaliibi
11Ti làá dū sindaariya ní kí mɔ́ɔ́-si falfatib,
ní kí dū animbil kúti kí nyùntī.
Usapɔɔn
12Ŋyunti ŋun m-bɔtiu kā ki jīǹee,
ní m-talaaluu sɔnsɔfiŋu ń gbìtī.
13M-bɔɔn un m gbàl̄ee sá-mi
kii talaalu un bi yíì miiri
m dūu yāaǹ m-biiŋi kansikinee ní.
14Un m néeńee bí kii
nsupumpukum min sɔ́fì
ki bí Eeni-Geedii fiinyi sufii kansikinee ní.
Unaacimpɔɔn
15M-bɔɔn, a ŋān̄,
a baasii ŋān̄ ní!
A-nimbiliŋ bí kùlkul
kii dibeenanjilee!
Usapɔɔn
16Sii un m néeńee,
a ŋān̄ kunyaaŋŋu.
Man nì sii dooŋu sɔ̀m̀
kii kumɔsɔŋuee ní.
17Seedir dɔi ní bi dūu kpáá ki píń ti-diiku
ní ki cátì siipreesi dɔi apampan
ki kpáá ki bīiǹ agun pu.

english_text:
Love Makes Everything Beautiful
She Speaks:
1I am merely a rose
from the land of Sharon,
a lily from the valley.
He Speaks:
2My darling, when compared
with other young women,
you are a lily among thorns.
She Speaks:
3And you, my love,
are an apple tree
among trees of the forest.
Your shade brought me pleasure;
your fruit was sweet.
4You led me to your banquet room
and showered me with love.
5Refresh and strengthen me
with raisins and apples.
I am hungry for love!
6Put your left hand under my head
and embrace me
with your right arm.
7Young women of Jerusalem,
promise me by the power
of deer and gazelles
never to awaken love
before it is ready.
Winter Is Past
She Speaks:
8I hear the voice
of the one I love,
as he comes leaping
over mountains and hills
9like a deer or a gazelle.
Now he stands outside our wall,
looking through the window
10and speaking to me.
He Speaks:
My darling, I love you!
Let's go away together.
11Winter is past,
the rain has stopped;
12flowers cover the earth,
it's time to sing.
The cooing of doves
is heard in our land.
13Fig trees are bearing fruit,
while blossoms on grapevines
fill the air with perfume.
My darling, I love you!
Let's go away together.
14You are my dove
hiding among the rocks
on the side of a cliff.
Let me see how lovely you are!
Let me hear the sound
of your melodious voice.
15Our vineyards are in blossom;
we must catch the little foxes
that destroy the vineyards.
She Speaks:
16My darling, I am yours,
and you are mine,
as you feed your sheep
among the lilies.
17Pretend to be a young deer
dancing on mountain slopes
until daylight comes
and shadows fade away.
translation_text:
1Man sá Sarɔn timpiliŋki supumpukum ní,
nsupumpukum min yú atantakanee.
Unaacimpɔɔn
2Kii nsupumpukum min ŋān̄
ki yú ikuŋkum kansikinee,
míǹ ní m-bɔɔn bí
bisapɔmbi kansikin.
Usapɔɔn
3Kii pɔɔmi subu nín yú
kubambaŋŋu sufii kansikin puee,
míǹ ní m-bɔɔn bí
binaacimpɔmbi kansikin.
M yaa kā u-booŋŋu taapuee
an mɔ̄ǹ-mi,
u-biliŋ mɔ̄ m-nyɔkɔn.
4U cáá-mi ki kɔ́ǹ jiŋaal diikun.
Bi ŋmàn̄ m nín kā puee yilpu yii <Dineendi>.
5«Cáaḿmaan-mi fiinyi subiliŋ kalaau malaa
ḿ ŋmɔ́ kí ká mpɔn,
kí tīī-mi pɔɔmi subiliŋ ḿ ŋmɔ́
m-pɔbil ń sɔ̀ŋkì.
Di sá yii m būǹ dineendi weeŋŋu ní.»
6U-ŋaŋgan tíkí m-yil,
ní u-ŋaŋgiil pá m-caŋ pu.
Unaacimpɔɔn
7Jeerusaleem sapɔmbi,
m dū ipeeman nì ikɔnii ki gbāam̀-ni,
ní taa fìntī m-neendi kí taa páb́-dì
kí nīn cí ŋyunti ŋun dì yaa lèe.
Úǹ di dòońee
Usapɔɔn
8M gbìl̄ un m néeńee pu.
Kpèè úǹ di dòońee.
Úǹ di yùkufī ajoon
nì ŋgbantamu yilpuee.
9Un m néeńee bí kii upeeman
àá dikɔniipɔmbilee ní.
Kpèè u bāań ki yúl̀ ti-diiku boon.
U lɔ́kɔtí ki kpèé tɔkɔla watil pú,
u gbōontí tɔkɔla laaŋkin ki kpèé.
10U bí-mi yii:
«Yīkìm̄, m-bɔɔn
unyaan kí dāan̄.
11Kuseeu jítì, utaa yúl̀
kutaa kɔ́ ndan.
12Ti ká ti-satin mpumpukum bíi màtī.
Ilan yuntiŋu bāań.
Ti gbìl̄ nnanjimamu siim pu ti-satin.
13Fiigi subipeepeekaaŋi bíi mántí.
Fiinyi pumpukum gbītì mi-sɔnsɔfiŋu.
Yīkìń, m-bɔɔn unyaan kí dāan̄.
14Man beenanjil din páaǹ
di-diiku ntaŋkpalɔkɔnee,
ki bál̀ ntaŋkpafaŋfakaminee,
yàntī ḿ wāl̀ a-nimbiin,
yàntī ḿ gbìl̄ a-neen pu
di sá yii a-neen sɔ̀m̀ ki mɔ̄,
ní a-nimbiin ŋān̄.»
Ubinaati
15Ní cúúmaan-ti iŋɔkɔ nee,
ŋŋɔkɔbiyaamu mun bí
ki ŋmóò ki bíiĺ fiinyibee.
Di sá yii ti-fiinyib bàà púkuḿ dee!
Usapɔɔn
16Un m néeńee bí ki tīī-mi,
ní ma mun bí ki tīī-u.
U kpàá u-picaŋkpuŋku
mpumpukum kansikin ní.
17Kí wàatī kutaa ń ŋàatī,
ní ibóon ń wāŋkèe,
fàtīí gítiń, sii un man néeńee.
Sāǹní kii upeemanee,
kii ukɔnii biki di sánní
ajoon ŋin yākatèe pu puee.

english_text:
Beautiful Dreams
She Speaks:
1While in bed at night,
I reached for the one I love
with heart and soul.
I looked for him,
but he wasn't there.
2So I searched through the town
for the one I love.
I looked on every street,
but he wasn't there.
3I even asked the guards
patrolling the town,
“Have you seen the one
I love so much?”
4Right after that, I found him.
I held him and would not let go
until I had taken him
to the home of my mother.
5Young women of Jerusalem,
promise me by the power
of deer and gazelles,
never to awaken love
before it is ready.
The Groom and the Wedding Party
Their Friends Speak:
6What do we see approaching
from the desert
like a cloud of smoke?
With it comes the sweet smell
of spices, including myrrh
and frankincense.
7It is King Solomon
carried on a throne,
surrounded by sixty
of Israel's best soldiers.
8Each of them wears a sword.
They are experts at fighting,
even in the dark.
9The throne is made of trees
from Lebanon.
10Its posts are silver,
the back is gold,
and the seat is covered
with purple cloth.
You women of Jerusalem
have taken great care
to furnish the inside.
11Now come and see the crown
given to Solomon by his mother
on his happy wedding day.
translation_text:
M nyàab̀ un m néeńee ní
Usapɔɔn
1Kunyeeu m-dooŋu puee
m nyàab̀ un m néeńee,
m nyàab̄-u, ama kaa ká-u.
2M làá yīkì kí yìiǹ kitiŋin
nì adan pu nì sampaambi pu.
M nyàab̀ un m néeńee.
M nyàab̄-u, ama kaa ká-u.
3M tūŋkí bijanjaliibi bin màntī
ki kpèé kitiŋee ki bàlifī-bi yii:
«Ni ká un m néeńeeee?»
4M pūtì pée jítì bi-pu kpalaayee
ní ki dūu tú un m néeńee.
M cúú u-ŋal kaa ti líì-ŋu,
see m nín cáá-u ki kɔ́ǹ m-na diikun
laakin u cáá m-poolee.
5«Jeerusaleem sapɔmbi,
m dū ipeeman nì ikɔnii ki gbāam̀-ni.
Ní taa fìntī m-neendi
kí taa páb́-dì kí nīn cí
ŋyunti ŋun dì yaa láa lèe.»
Usapɔɔn
6Ŋma di nyánní kuteeun ki dòoń
kii ŋŋmi tagbanlooŋŋuee?
U sɔ́fìń miiri talaaluu nì bitalaalutuukaabi
nì talaalub bin kɔkɔ nyánní
laaba nì bi-bulifee.
7An sá ubɔti Saloomɔn di pá
u-lambaŋki pu.
Bijanjaliibi bin cáá dipɔbilee
imuŋku ita māntìi tú-u.
Isirayeel baatandambi dee.
8Bi-kɔkɔ ŋúb́ kitàataajiki
ki bɔ́ntì dikɔ̀ndi.
Báà ŋma gbìn̄ u-gbajau,
kí mɔ̄tì u-ba pu kunyeeu jaaku pu.
9Saloomɔn yāntì bi dū Leebanɔn dɔi
ki kpáá-u dijakpatikaal.
10Idɔ in tɔ́kɔ́ di-puee sá animbil kúti
ní laakin u dìntēe sá sindaariya,
ní ki dū bisatamambi binyannyaambi
ki ŋáĺ ki tākaǹ dijalee poon.
Jeerusaleem sapɔmbi
dū nì dineendi ní ki lùn̄ iŋaabu
ki nyáantì di-poon.
11«Jeerusaleem sapɔmbi,
nyānnímaan kí dāá kpèè ubɔti Saloomɔn.
U cíkí kibeefuulii kin u-na nìn tīī-u
u-nimpucaal dalee!
Ŋwiin gbantee, u nìn bí dipɔɔpindin ní.»

english_text:
What a Beautiful Bride
He Speaks:
1My darling, you are lovely,
so very lovely—
as you look through your veil,
your eyes are those of a dove.
Your hair tosses about
as gracefully as goats
coming down from Gilead.
2Your teeth are whiter
than sheep freshly washed;
they match perfectly,
not one is missing.
3Your lips are crimson cords,
your mouth is shapely;
behind your veil are hidden
beautiful rosy cheeks.
4Your neck is more graceful
than the tower of David,
decorated with thousands
of warriors' shields.
5Your breasts are perfect;
they are twin deer
feeding among lilies.
6I will hasten to those hills
sprinkled with sweet perfume
and stay there till sunrise.
7My darling, you are lovely
in every way.
8My bride, together
we will leave Lebanon!
We will say goodbye
to the peaks of Mount Amana,
Senir, and Hermon,
where lions and leopards
live in the caves.
9My bride, my very own,
you have stolen my heart!
With one glance from your eyes
and the glow of your necklace,
you have stolen my heart.
10Your love is sweeter than wine;
the smell of your perfume
is more fragrant than spices.
11Your lips are a honeycomb;
milk and honey
flow from your tongue.
Your dress has the aroma
of cedar trees from Lebanon.
12My bride, my very own,
you are a garden, a fountain
closed off to all others.
13Your arms are vines,
covered with delicious fruits
and all sorts of spices—
henna, nard, 14saffron,
calamus, cinnamon,
frankincense, myrrh, and aloes
—all the finest spices.
15You are a spring in the garden,
a fountain of pure water,
and a refreshing stream
from Mount Lebanon.
She Speaks:
16Let the north wind blow,
the south wind too!
Let them spread the aroma
of my garden,
so the one I love
may enter and taste
its delicious fruits.
translation_text:
Unaacimpɔɔn
1A ŋān̄ kunyaaŋŋu, m-bɔɔn,
a ŋān̄ kunyaaŋŋu!
A yaa dū a-ŋaabiiŋkaaŋu ki bīiǹee,
a-nimbiliŋ ŋān̄ kii dibeenanjilee ní.
A-yikpiti nín dɔ̄ puee bí kii
kuŋɔcaŋkpuŋu di kpákatiń
Galaadi jool puee.
2A-nyiŋŋi pīiǹ káŋkaŋ kii ipii in
bi dáá cáń i-kuti ki fùl̄-iee.
Dinyindi kamaa cáá di-ŋaliŋu ní,
báà dibaba kaa fúkutì.
3A-nyunculiŋ ŋān̄ kii kiŋaamaŋee,
ní a-nyɔkɔ cáá kunyaaŋŋu.
A yaa dū a-ŋaabiiŋkaaŋu ki bīiǹee,
a-taŋkpunti bí kii kpakpaapu
un bi búkutì milee poon nín bí puee ní.
4A-sil bí kii Daafiidi difɔkɔku
kun bi máń ku yú ki pɔ̄ɔ̄ jìbuee ní.
Niin ní agbampɔɔ kutuku sàkā.
Bibaatandambi kɔkɔ janjawanti dee.
5A-biiŋi bí kii aŋɔbil alee,
a lì kii ipeeman in bi màl̄ ŋwimbaanti,
i yú nsupumpukum kansikin ki jīǹee.
6Kí wàatī kutaa ń ŋàatī,
ní mboon ń lítí kitiŋ puee,
m làá cù miiri jool pu,
ní kí cù talaalu tūukaa gbantaŋki pu.
7M-bɔɔn, a baasii ŋān̄ kunyaaŋŋu ní,
a-laaba kaa pée wɔ̀b̄.
8M-bɔɔn, nyānní Leebanɔn jooŋŋi pu kí dāan̄ m-cee,
dāan̄ m-cee.
Kpákatiń Arimina nì Seeniir
nì Eermɔn jooŋŋi pu.
Nyā gbikintib kɔŋkooŋyin
nì igbii jooŋŋi pu.
9A yāntì maa ti yì m-ba
m-niisal, m-bɔɔn,
a yaa pée fātìi kpēē-mi yéè
ní m yaa ká a-leeŋkaati dimbil diba jee,
maa ti yì m-ba.
10A-neendi tìì-mi mmɔn,
m-niisal, m-bɔɔn!
Dì mɔ̄ m-cee ki jítiǹ ndaam pu gba!
A-talaalub sɔ́fì ki jítiǹ
talaalumɔntiibi kɔkɔ.
11M-bɔɔn, m yaa móotí a-nyunculiŋee,
an mɔ̄ kii tisiilee ní.
Tisiil nì nnaabiim bál̀
ki kā a-limbil pu.
A-wampeeŋkaati sɔ́fì kii
Leebanɔn bambaŋku sɔnsɔfiŋuee ní.
12M-niisal, m-bɔɔn,
a sá bukpaa bun man baba yèe ní,
man baba nyimbulnimbil,
nnyimbul ŋun m pīiǹ ki kpàl̄ kpálkpalee.
13A sɔ̀m̀ fílfil kii yilpu beel sufii
in biliŋ mɔ̄ cɔ́ncɔŋee.
Niin ní isufi in sɔ́fèe nyēē.
Íǹ di sá eenee nì naar,
14nì safran nì looriyee nì kanneel
nì isufi in kɔkɔ bi cáa ŋáań talaalu tūukaayee,
nì miiri nì disaaweendi
nì talaalub bin sɔ́fì tiŋan tiŋanee.
15A sá nnyimbul ŋun dɔ̄
bukpaa kansikinee ní,
dinyimbunimbil din nyim wāĺ kílkil
ki pùubìń Leebanɔn jooŋŋi puee.
Usapɔɔn
16Fìntim̄, ŋgan pú buŋku!
Dāan̄ malaa ŋgiil pú buŋku!
Dāá jītí m-kpaabu pu
bú gbìtī bu-sɔnsɔfiŋu!
Sii un m néeńee,
kɔ́ a-kpaabun
kí ŋmɔ́ bu-subimɔntiŋ!

english_text:
He Speaks:
1My bride, my very own,
I come to my garden
and enjoy its spices.
I eat my honeycomb and honey;
I drink my wine and milk.
Their Friends Speak:
Eat and drink until
you are drunk with love.
Another Dream
She Speaks:
2I was asleep, but dreaming:
The one I love was at the door,
knocking and saying,
“My darling, my very own,
my flawless dove,
open the door for me!
My head is drenched
with evening dew.”
3But I had already undressed
and bathed my feet.
Should I dress again
and get my feet dirty?
4Then my darling's hand
reached to open the latch,
and my heart stood still.
5When I rose to open the door,
my hands and my fingers
dripped with perfume.
6And I yearned for him
while he spoke to me,
but when I opened the door,
my darling had disappeared.
I searched and shouted,
but I could not find him—
there was no answer.
7Then I was found by the guards
patrolling the town
and guarding the wall.
They beat me up
and stripped off my robe.
8Young women of Jerusalem,
if you find the one I love,
please say to him,
“She is weak with desire.”
Their Friends Speak:
9Most beautiful of women,
why is the one you love
more special than others?
Why do you ask us
to tell him how you feel?
She Speaks:
10He is handsome and healthy,
the most outstanding
among ten thousand.
11His head is purest gold;
his hair is wavy,
black as a raven.
12His eyes are a pair of doves
bathing in a stream
flowing with milk.
13His face is a garden
of sweet-smelling spices;
his lips are lilies
dripping with perfume.
14His arms are branches of gold
covered with jewels;
his body is ivory
decorated with sapphires.
15His legs are columns of marble
on feet of gold.
He stands there majestic
like Mount Lebanon
and its choice cedar trees.
16His kisses are sweet.
I desire him so much!
Young women of Jerusalem,
he is my lover and friend.
translation_text:
Unaacimpɔɔn
1M kɔ́ m-kpaabun
m-niisal, m-bɔɔn.
M kītì m-subu bun bi yíì miiree
nì talaalu sufii iba mun.
M ŋmɔ́ m-sigbandi nì m-siiti,
ki nyùn̄ m-daam nì m-naabiim.
Bibɔɔtiibi
«M-bɔɔbi, jī kí nyɔ̀maan
kí gbímaan dineendi.
Waa pīitì-u kipunyɔkɔ malaa
Usapɔɔn
2M dɔ̄ ki gèeǹ,
ama m-pɔbil kaa gèeǹ.
M gbìl̄ kuwoou kubɔ pu,
an sá un m néeńee di bíi fátí kipunyɔkɔ.
Unaacimpɔɔn
Pìitī-mi, m-niisal,
m-bɔɔn, m-beenanjil, unyaan.
Dimalindi tɔ́ ki sɔ̄ŋkì m-yil gbàtii,
ní kunyeeu sɔnsɔm sɔ̄ŋkì m-yikpiti.
Usapɔɔn
3M pēetì m-bɔkutil,
maa là kí gíiǹ-dì kí pèen̄!
M fíntì m-taaŋi,
maa là kí kɔ́ǹ-ŋi tijɔkɔndi.»
4Un m néeńee dū u-ŋal ki bɔ́
dikampiil buŋŋun
ní m-pɔbil máĺ.
5M yíkì kí pìitī-u.
Talaalu kpam min bi yíì miiree
nìn gbí m-ŋaan
ní ŋkpamee mèetī m-ŋambiyaamu pu
ki tōontí dikampiil kpàlkaati pu.
6M pīitì un m néeńee,
ama ní u fātì u-boon ki tīī-mi,
ki búntì.
M nyáń kí nyàab̀-u.
M nyàab̄-u ama kaa ká-u,
ki yíiń-u ama waa kíí-mi.
7Ama m tú bijanjaliibi bin cí kitiŋ
ki màntī ki kpèé-kèe
kitiŋ gundi pu.
Bi cúú-mi ki gbáń ki ŋá-mi tiweendi,
bi cúú ŋŋaabu ŋun pá m-gbigbil puee ki fōō.
8Jeerusaleem sapɔmbi
m gbāam̀-ni:
ni yaa ká un m néeńee,
ni làá tùkù-u yii ba dee?
Ní tùkù-u yii
m būǹ dineendi weeŋŋu.
Bisapɔmbi
9Sii unimpunyaan,
ba pu ní a bàlifī-ti tin bí nee?
Un a néeńee, ba ní u cáá
ki jítiǹ bin kíǹee ní?
Ba ní u baasii cáá ki jítiǹ-bi ní?
Usapɔɔn
10Un m néeńee yaa sáká bininjab
kutukub saalaa kansikin,
bi béetí-u ní.
Di sá yii u-wunti máǹ ní ki jìl̀.
11U-yikpiti bí kii sindaariyee ní,
ní ki gɔ́liḿ gɔ́liḿ kii tikpakpatee,
ní ki bɔ̀ǹ kii kunaambɔŋŋuee.
12U-nimbiliŋ jìl̀ kii dibeenanjil
di bí mbun caŋinee.
Di tɔ́kɔ́ kusampeeu nyɔɔgbandi
ki fùul̀ nnaabiim poon.
13U-taŋkpuŋŋi bí kii
talaalu sufii kpaabuee ní.
U-nyunculiŋ bí kii nsupumpukum
min pu miiri kpam còol̀ee ní.
14U-ŋalii bí kii sindaariya bɔmbiliŋ
ŋin bi dū ataŋkpanyaan ki nyáantèe.

tell us where he has gone.

2My darling has gone down
to his garden of spices,
where he will feed his sheep
and gather lilies.
3I am his, and he is mine,
as he feeds his sheep
among the lilies.
He Speaks:
4My dearest, the cities of Tirzah
and Jerusalem
are not as lovely as you.
Your charms are more powerful
than all of the stars
in the heavens.
5Turn away your eyes—
they make me melt.
Your hair tosses about
as gracefully as goats
coming down from Gilead.
6Your teeth are whiter
than sheep freshly washed;
they match perfectly,
not one is missing.
7Behind your veil are hidden
beautiful rosy cheeks.
8What if I could have
sixty queens, eighty wives,
and thousands of others!
9You would be my only choice,
my flawless dove,
the favorite child
of your mother.
The young women, the queens,
and all the others
tell how excited you are
as they sing your praises:
10“You are as majestic
as the morning sky—
glorious as the moon—
blinding as the sun!
Your charms are more powerful
than all the stars above.”
She Speaks:
11I went down to see if blossoms
were on the walnut trees,
grapevines, and fruit trees.
12But in my imagination
I was suddenly riding
on a glorious chariot.
Their Friends Speak:
13Dance! Dance!
Beautiful woman from Shulam,
let us see you dance!
She Speaks:
Why do you want to see
this woman from Shulam
dancing with the others?

Bisapɔmbi
1Unimpunyannyaan,
un a néeńee bí la ní?
La ní u túĺ ní?.
Ti làá tūtuǹ-si á nyàab̀-u.
Usapɔɔn
2Un m néeńeee sīntì u-kpaabun,
mpumpukum min sɔ́fèe watil.
Niin ní u kāntí u-jinti,
ki kìtī mpumpukum.
3M sá ki tīī un m néeńee,
ní u mun sá ki tīī-mi.
Laakin mpumpukum bée,
niin ní u kpàá u-waŋkuti.
Un bi néeńee nín bí puee
Unaacimpɔɔn
4M-bɔɔn, a ŋān̄ kunyaaŋŋu,
kii Tiirsa tiŋkee.
A ŋān̄ ki mɔ̄ nnimbikpee
kii Jeerusaleem tiŋkee,
ama a kɔ̄ntí binib tifaandi
kii dijanjakitil di bí dikɔmbool puee.
5Fàtī a-nimbiin kí taa ti kpèè-mi,
di sá yii a-nimbiliŋ sàtī-mi.
A-yikpiti fɔ̀kɔ̀ ki bí kii
kuŋɔcaŋkpuŋu di kpákatiń
Galaadi jool puee.
6A-nyiŋŋi pīiǹ káŋkaŋ kii ipii in
bi dáá cáń i-kuti ki fùl̄-iee ní.
Dinyindi kamaa cáá di-ŋaliŋu ní,
báà dibaba kaa fúkutì.
7A yaa dū a-ŋaabiiŋkaaŋu ki bīiǹee,
a-taŋkpunti bí kii kpakpaapu
un bi búkutì milee poon nín bí puee ní.
8Ubɔti ŋūǹ kí nīn cáá
binimpoobi imuŋku ita,
bibɔntiibi imuŋku inaa,
nì bisapɔmbi kupaau.
9Man ceeyee,
unimpubambaanti di bí.
Úǹ di sá man beenanjil, unyaan.
U sá u-na bibaabil ní,
kibiki kin u nìn néeń tikpilkuee.
Bisapɔmbi yaa wál̀-uee, bi pàkà-u ní,
ní ubɔti nimpoobi nì
u-bɔmbi nyɔ́ŋkí-u ki lì yii:
10«Batii nimpuu di bí kii
kutaawuntuŋu walifiŋu na!
U ŋān̄ kii uŋmalee,
ki jìl̀ kii ŋwìińee,
ki kɔ̄ntí binib tifaandi kii
dijanjakitil di bí dikɔmbool puee.»
11M sīntì m-sufii kpaabun.
M là kí kpèè asupɔmbil ŋin bí ditantakalinee.
Fiinyi sufii púkuḿaaa?
Greenaadi mun púkuḿaaa?
12Maa tí gbìl̀ taapu,
ubɔtiisal, a yāntì maa ti nyí
tin poon m bée.

1Most beautiful of women,

Let us help you find him.
She Speaks:
2My darling has gone down

where he will feed his sheep

4My dearest, the cities of Tirzah

Your charms are more powerful

5Turn away your eyes—

Your hair tosses about

6Your teeth are whiter
than sheep freshly washed;
they match perfectly,
not one is missing.
7Behind your veil are hidden
beautiful rosy cheeks.
8What if I could have
sixty queens, eighty wives,
and thousands of others!
9You would be my only choice,
my flawless dove,
the favorite child

The young women, the queens,
and all the others
tell how excited you are

10“You are as majestic
as the morning sky—
glorious as the moon—
blinding as the sun!
Your charms are more powerful
than all the stars above.”
She Speaks:
11I went down to see if blossoms
were on the walnut trees,
grapevines, and fruit trees.
12But in my imagination
I was suddenly riding
on a glorious chariot.
Their Friends Speak:
13Dance! Dance!
Beautiful woman from Shulam,
let us see you dance!
She Speaks:

english_text:
The Wedding Dance
He Speaks:
1You are a princess,
and your feet are graceful
in their sandals.
Your thighs are works of art,
each one a jewel;
2your navel is a wine glass
filled to overflowing.
Your body is full and slender
like a bundle of wheat
bound together by lilies.
3Your breasts are like twins
of a deer.
4Your neck is like ivory,
and your eyes sparkle
like the pools of Heshbon
by the gate of Bath-Rabbim.
Your nose is beautiful
like Mount Lebanon
above the city of Damascus.
5Your head is held high
like Mount Carmel;
your hair is so lovely
it holds a king prisoner.
6You are very beautiful,
so desirable!
7You are tall and slender
like a palm tree,
and your breasts are full.
8I will climb that tree
and cling to its branches.
I will discover that your breasts
are clusters of grapes,
and that your breath
is the aroma of apples.
9Kissing you is more delicious
than drinking the finest wine.
How wonderful and tasty!
She Speaks:
10My darling, I am yours,
and you desire me.
11Let's stroll through the fields
and sleep in the villages.
12At dawn let's slip out and see
if grapevines and fruit trees
are covered with blossoms.
When we are there,
I will give you my love.
13Perfume from the magic flower
fills the air, my darling.
Right at our doorstep
I have stored up for you
all kinds of tasty fruits.
translation_text:
Binimpoobi nì bisapɔmbi
1Gítiń, gítiń usulamiitinimpu,
gítiń tí ŋmā kí kpèè-si.
Ba pu ní ni kpèé usulamiitinimpu
un bí akiti ali kansikin ki ŋōōyee?
Unaacimpɔɔn
2Bɔtiisal, anaataka ŋin a tákée ŋān̄
ki máaǹ-si!
A-caŋ gíí ki ŋān̄ kii
tiwanléeŋkaal tin bi mɔ́ɔ́yee.
3A-puluul sá kii kɔɔpu un poon
ndaam min sɔ́fèe kaa lóotée ní.
A-pool sá kii dibileekpukul,
ní mpumpukum yú ki māntìi túee.
4A-biiŋi liitil bí kii ŋŋɔjamu mulee,
a lì kii upeeman jaasibee.
5A-sil bí kii dikuntinyindi difɔkɔkuee.
A-nimbiliŋ bí kii a yaa nyēē Eesbɔn tiŋkpaaŋkin
anyimbɔbil ŋin bí niinee.
A-maŋfal tɔ́kɔ́ kii Leebanɔn sintil difɔkɔku
kun bí ki túĺ Damaasee.
6A-yil tɔ́kɔ́ a-wunti pu jìb̀
kii Kaarmeel joolee,
ní a-yikpiti fɔ̀kɔ̀ ki máǹ wúŋwuŋ,
ní tì nín gɔ́liḿ gɔ́liḿ puee sàl̄ ubɔti ubɔ.
7A ŋān̄ ki bí gbàlgbal.
M-neeŋkaau, sii di sá man pɔɔpindi.
8A fɔ̀kɔ̀ càb̀ kii bubabuee
ní a-biiŋi sá bu-sakaŋ.
9M lī yii:
«M làá jɔ̄m̀ bubabu nee
kí gāā bu-sakaŋ!»
A-biiŋi ń nīn sá ki tīī-mi
kii fiinyi sakaŋee.
A-fooku sɔnsɔfiŋu
ń nīn náań nì asubil sɔnsɔfiŋu!
10A-nyɔkɔ ń nīn mɔ̄
kii ndamɔntiimee!
Usapɔɔn
Tiŋman, ndamɔntiim min m kpáafì
ki yóoǹ un m néeńee,
còol̀ ti-nyunculiŋ pu ti-geem yuntiŋu.
11M bí ki tīī un m néeńee,
man ní u baasii là.
Un bi néeńee bí mmɔnni
Usapɔɔn
12Sii un m néeńee, dāan̄ tí nyā!
Tí cù kitimbiliiyin kí dòon̄.
13Kù yaa wúntì kutaafaau pɔ̀lpɔlee,
ti làá cù fiinyi kpaaŋŋin
kí kpèè yii an púkuḿaaa,
an mātì.
Ti làá kpèè yii greenaadi mun yaa púkuḿ.
Niin ní m làá ŋmāliŋkì-si.
14Dineendi subiliŋ gbītì ŋi-sɔnsɔfiŋu.
Ti cáá asubil ŋin mɔ̄ee kɔkɔ nì ŋi-bulifi ti-punyɔkɔpu,
akpiki nì apɔɔn kɔkɔ.
Sii un m néeńee, sii ní m kpáafì ki yóoǹ.

english_text:
If Only You and I …
She Speaks:
1If you were my brother,
I could kiss you
whenever we happen to meet,
and no one would say
I did wrong.
2I could take you to the home
of my mother,
who taught me all I know.
I would give you delicious wine
and fruit juice as well.
3Put your left hand under my head
and embrace me
with your right arm.
4Young women of Jerusalem,
promise me never to awaken love
before it is ready.
Their Friends Speak:
5Who is this young woman
coming in from the desert
and leaning on the shoulder
of the one she loves?
She Speaks:
I stirred up your passions
under the apple tree
where you were born.
6Always keep me in your heart
and wear this bracelet
to remember me by.
The passion of love
bursting into flame
is more powerful than death,
stronger than the grave.
7Love cannot be drowned
by oceans or floods.
It cannot be bought—
any offer would be scorned
no matter how great.
Their Friends Speak:
8We have a little sister
whose breasts
are not yet formed.
If someone asks to marry her,
what should we do?
9She isn't a wall
that we can defend
behind a silver shield.
Neither is she a room
that we can protect
behind a wooden door.
She Speaks:
10I am a wall around a city,
my breasts are towers,
and just looking at me
brings him great pleasure.
11Solomon has a vineyard
at Baal-Hamon,
which he rents to others
for a thousand pieces
of silver each.
12My vineyard is mine alone!
Solomon can keep his silver
and the others can keep
their share of the profits.
He Speaks:
13You are in the garden
with friends all around.
Let me hear your voice!
She Speaks:
14Hurry to me, my darling!
Run faster than a deer
to mountains of spices.
translation_text:
1A yaa bàà sá m-niija,
man nì un ŋáam̀ dibiibaantiilee!
M yaa tú-si mmɔŋki laabee,
m bàà kpàl̀-si,
ní ubɔ kaa làá cɔ́kɔ́-mi.
2M bàà cáǹ-si m-na cee
ní á bīfì-mi dineendi.
M bàà tìì-si ndaam min sɔ́fèe á nyɔ̀,
asubiman ŋin m ŋmáaḿee nyim.
3U-ŋaŋgan tíkí m-yil,
ní u-ŋaŋgiil pá m-caŋ pu.
4Jeerusaleem sapɔmbi,
m gbàam̄-ni,
ní taa fìntī m-neendi,
kí taa páb́-dì
kí nīn cí ŋyunti ŋun
ní di yaa láa lèe.
Bisapɔmbi
5Unimpu ulɔu di nyánní kuteeun
u-ŋal nyīī un u néeńee pu na?
Dineendi pɔŋŋu
Usapɔɔn
Dineendi subu taapu ní m fīntì-si
laakin a-na cáá a-pool,
laakin u màl̄-see.
6Dū-mi kí nákań a-pɔbil pu
kii kijalii kin a cáa nyìitī a-wanti puee.
Yàntī ḿ nīn pée bí ki lɔ́kɔ́-si
kii ditaŋkpal din pu bi kpítì a-yindi
a dūu fúuń a-ŋalee.
Tiŋman, dineendi pɔ̄ɔ̄ kii ŋkúmee ní,
ní kpɔkɔsi pɔ̄ɔ̄ kpaŋkpam kii ditaŋkpiilinee,
tiba kaa ŋūǹ kí pèefì-dì.
Di fòol̄ kii ŋŋmee
ní ki tòó kii utaayee.
7Nnyiŋkpaam kɔkɔ kaa ŋūǹ
kí gbíntí dineendi ŋmiŋu.
Amɔɔ kɔkɔ nyim kaa ŋūǹ
kí bìin̄ di-pu.
Ubɔ yaa dū u-diikun gaajati kɔkɔ
yii u làá dūú dā dineendee,
u làá kúntíǹ ibeel ní.
8Ti cáá naal ubɔ,
ama waa láá nyáń abii.
Ti-naal gbanti yaa bàn̄ dicamɔndee,
ba ní ti làá dāá ŋá kí tīī-u?
9U yaa bàà sá kii digundee,
ti bàà dù animbil kúti ní kí mā
sintil difɔkɔŋi kí wúń u-pu.
U yaa bàà sá kipunyɔkɔee,
ti bàà làá dū seedir dɔi
ní kí kpáá punuu kí pìin̄-u.
Usapɔɔn
10Man sá digundi ní,
ní m-biiŋi sá adifɔkɔ.
An puee, u-ceeyee, m sá
un tìì-u dipɔɔpindee ní.
Unaacimpɔɔn
11Saloomɔn cáá bufiinyikpaa
Baal-Amɔn tiŋkin.
U dū-bu ki kpāaǹ bipaadambi ní.
Kí kìtī fiinyi gbanti biliŋee,
báà ŋma máaǹ kí pà animbil kúti jitɔmbi kutuku ní.
12Saloomɔn, animbil jitɔmbi
kutukuee, sii di yì,
ní kí dū jitɔmbi kulaafaau
kí tīī bipaadambi bin cí kusaauee.
An yaa kíǹ man fiinyi kpaabuee,
m làá nīn cí-bu m-ba ní.
13Sii un kóò bukpaa kansikinee,
a-bɔɔbi kpōoǹ bi-tafal
kí pīlifì tin a làá sòoǹee.
Ama man ní a máaǹ kí lì yii:
14«Sii un m néeńee,
sāǹ kí kátí malaa!
sāǹ kii upeemanee,
àá kii kikɔniibikee
ajoon ŋin sɔ́fèe pu.»

english_text:
1 I am Isaiah, the son of Amoz.
And this is the message that I was given about Judah and Jerusalem when Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were the kings of Judah:
A Guilty Nation
2The Lord has said,
“Listen, heaven and earth!
The children I raised
have turned against me.
3Oxen and donkeys know
who owns and feeds them,
but my people won't ever learn.”
4Israel, you are a sinful nation
loaded down with guilt.
You are wicked and corrupt
and have turned from the Lord,
the holy God of Israel.
5Why be punished more?
Why not give up your sin?
Your head is badly bruised,
and you are weak all over.
6From your head to your toes
there isn't a healthy spot.
Bruises, cuts, and open sores
go without care
or oil to ease the pain.
A Country in Ruins
7Your country lies in ruins;
your towns are in ashes.
Foreigners and strangers
take and destroy your land
while you watch.
8Enemies surround Jerusalem,
alone like a hut
in a vineyard
or in a cucumber field.
9 Zion would have disappeared
like Sodom and Gomorrah,
if the Lord All-Powerful
had not let a few
of its people survive.
Justice, Not Sacrifices
10You are no better
than the leaders and people
of Sodom and Gomorrah!
So listen to the Lord God:
11 “Your sacrifices
mean nothing to me.
I am sick of your offerings
of rams and choice cattle;
I don't like the blood
of bulls or lambs or goats.
12“Who asked you to bring all this
when you come to worship me?
Stay out of my temple!
13Your sacrifices are worthless,
and your incense disgusting.
I can't stand the evil you do
on your New Moon Festivals
or on your Sabbaths
and other times of worship.
14I hate your New Moon Festivals
and all others as well.
They are a heavy burden
I am tired of carrying.
15“No matter how much you pray,
I won't listen.
You are too violent.
16Wash yourselves clean!
I hate your filthy deeds.
Stop doing wrong
17and learn to live right.
See that justice is done.
Defend widows and orphans
and help the oppressed.”
An Invitation from the Lord
18I, the Lord, invite you
to come and talk it over.
Your sins are scarlet red,
but they will be whiter
than snow or wool.
19If you willingly obey me,
the best crops in the land
will be yours.
20But if you turn against me,
your enemies will kill you.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Lord Condemns Jerusalem
21Jerusalem, you are like
an unfaithful wife.
Once your judges were honest
and your people lived right;
now you are a city
full of murderers.
22Your silver is fake,
and your wine
is watered down.
23Your leaders have rejected me
to become friends of crooks;
your rulers are looking
for gifts and bribes.
Widows and orphans
never get a fair trial.
24I am the Lord All-Powerful,
the mighty ruler of Israel,
and I make you a promise:
You are now my enemy,
and I will show my anger
by taking revenge on you.
25I will punish you terribly
and burn away everything
that makes you unfit
to worship me.
26Jerusalem, I will choose
judges and advisors
like those you had before.
Your new name will be
“Justice and Faithfulness.”
The Lord Will Save Jerusalem
27Jerusalem, you will be saved
by showing justice;
Zion's people who turn to me
will be saved
by doing right.
28But those rebellious sinners
who turn against me, the Lord,
will all disappear.
29You will be made ashamed
of those groves of trees
where you worshiped idols.
30You will be like a grove of trees
dying in a drought.
31Your strongest leaders
will be like dry wood
set on fire by their idols.
No one will be able to help,
as they all go up in flames.
translation_text:
DIJAMPEEPEEKAAL
(1–39)
1Yeesaya, Amɔtisi jipɔɔn nín nìn ká tibɔti tin Juuda beel nì Jeerusaleem tiŋki puee sèé. Ŋyunti gbantee, Oosiyasi nì Yootam nì Akaasi nì Eeseekiyaasi nìn kāl̀ kāl̀ Juuda beel pu tibɔtiil ki fōol̀ tɔb.
Ti-Dindaan nibul kaa nyí di-Nimbɔtiu
2Kutagbɔŋu, pīlifì!
Kitiŋ, kpòon̄ a-tafal kí pīlifì!
Ti-Dindaan di bíi sòoǹ nee.
«M lōō mbiyaamu,
ki kpēē-mu mu cíkitì,
ní mu kíǹ ki bíi jáà nì mi.
3Unaa nyí u-dindaan,
ní kimaŋ nyí laakin ki-dindaan ŋáań-kì tijin kì jīǹee.
Ama Isirayeel yab kaa nyí báà tiba,
m-nibul kaa gbìl̀ tibɔti taapu.»
Juuda tiŋki kíǹ ki náań nì Soodoom ní
4Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí-ni, nimbi ditimbundi din ŋáań ikpitee,
dinibul din yīntèe,
nnibool ŋun ŋáań tin kaa ŋān̄ee,
mbiyaamu mun yiliŋ gáatèe.
Ni dū ti-Dindaan ki fá,
ki kpēē Isirayeel Circir Nimbɔtiu fám,
ki fātì ni-boon ki tīī-u.
5Ni nín gbíntìi jáà nì u nee,
ni-la ní u làá gíti fáá ní?
Diyil kɔkɔ fōō tiweendi,
dipɔbil kɔkɔ gīī ki yúl̀.
6Kí yòon̄ titafati kí cáá sāā diyilee,
laaba kaa ti bí mmɔm.
Tiwun kɔkɔ fōō tiweendi,
ki lākatì lākatì, ki kpántì ibuun.
Ubɔ kaa fíntì-i, kaa póob́-i,
kaa ŋá-i ŋkpam kí bàtī iween pu.
7Ni-tiŋki kpántì kuteeu,
ni-timmu wùn̄ ŋŋmi kɔkɔ múb.
Ni-nimbilaaliyin ní binicambi
bí ki ŋàfī ni-kpaajinti.
An kpéelikì ni-sati nyíki nyiki
kii binannanliibi di jítèe.
8Siiyɔn tiŋki baba di pée kíǹ,
kii kibiŋ di yú fiinyi kpaabunee,
kii uciitil bìŋ́ki di yú aputaajul kpaabunee,
kii kitiŋ ní bijanjaliibi māntìi túee.
9Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan yaa kaa bàà yāntì
ti-kansikin binikaaŋkaabi ŋmátèe,
ti bàà làá nīn bí kii Soodoom yabee ní,
kí nīn náań nì Goomoora yab.
Ti-Dindaan ná binikpitib saraabi
10Pīlifìmaan ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi, Soodoom kpilib.
Ní ŋátí ni-tafal kí pīlifì ti-Nimbɔtiu dàkatam, Goomoora nibul.
11Ti-Dindaan bí yii:
«Ba ní m làá ŋá nì saraabi bin ni ŋáań tikpil nee?
M núutiǹ ipijaa saraawɔkaabi nì anabil kpam.
M gīī nì inajaa nì apibil nì iŋoobu fatikuu.
12Ni nín dòoń ki yūlifí m-nimbiinee,
man di bí yii ni-taal ń tāā m-cindinaaa?
13Ní taa ti cáań-mi saraabi,
an kaa kèetī tiba.
M ná talaalub bin ni tùutēe nyiim!
Ni jīǹ uŋmapɔɔn nì ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa jiŋaalib
ki kpáfí ki jīǹ jiŋaalib
ki ŋáań ikpiti.
Maa ti là kí ká míǹ.
14M ná uŋmapɔɔn jiŋaalib bin ni jīǹee,
ni-kpafiŋ kpántì diwaŋgul ní ki tīī-mi,
ní m túǹ ki gīī m-naŋki nyáń.
15Ni yaa tāntì ni-ŋalii kí mèèyee,
m fàtī m-kpaŋkpamboon ní kí tīī-ni.
Báà ní mèè kí gíti mèè, maa làá pīlifì-ni,
kun puee ni-ŋalii táká fatiku.
16Ní fàl̀maan, kí ŋámaan ni-ba circir.
Ní nyāntí ni-tuŋkpitiŋ m-nimbiin,
kí gbèen̄ kí taa ti ŋá ikpiti.
17Ní bīfì kí nīn ŋáań tin ŋān̄ee.
Ní nyàab̀ kí nīn nóó deedee saŋŋu.
Ní nīn kpòotī bin wɔ́b̀ bi-jutiibee.
Ní sòoǹ kí pɔ̀ ditaŋkpiibil,
kí sòoǹ kí mɔ̄tì ukpiipu pu.»
Ní taa ti já nì ti-Dindaan
18Ti-Dindaan bí yii:
«Ní dāam̄maan tí sòoǹ kí gbìlīǹ tɔb.
Báà ni-kpitii yaa yāntìi máǹ cíncinciŋ kii fatikuee,
i làá pīil̀ káŋkaŋkaŋ kii ntaayimee.
Báà i yaa máǹ kii ŋwɔmee,
i làá pīil̀ kii upipiin kutee ní.
19Ni yaa kíí ki pílifì m-nyɔkɔ,
ni làá jī tijin tin kitiŋ nee lòon̄ee.
20Ama ni yaa yíì kaa pílifì,
ní ki gbíntìi jáà nì mee,
kitàataajiki ní bi làá dūú kúntí-ni.»
Ti-Dindaan di sòon̄ míǹ.
Ti-Dindaan làá ŋá Jeerusaleem tiŋki circir
21An ŋá mana ní kitiŋ kin kaa nìn cáá tijɔkɔndee
dūu kpántì kii kinimpulaakpaayee ní?
Dooooyee, ki-nib nìn nóó ibaamɔn saŋŋu,
ní ki nìn bí deedee.
Ama kɔŋkɔnnee, binikpɔliibi
di kíǹ ki gbí ki-ni.
22A-nimbiliŋ kúti kaa ti nyìm̀,
ní bi cēeǹ a-damɔmmɔntiimin nnyim!
23A-bɔtiibi sá pɔɔgaatib ní,
bi nì binaayub di pēē kinyɔkɔ.
Bi-kɔkɔ néeń tiwampɔkaal,
ki jòó ki pá dinyɔɔŋeebil jim boon.
Baa pɔ̀ ditaŋkpiibil,
kaa mɔ́tí ukpiipu pu.
24An pu ní ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan
un di sá Isirayeel Nimbɔtikpaaŋwuee lī yii:
«Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí-ni! M làá téeǹ nimbi bin ná-mee!
M làá tɔ̀ nimbi m-nannanliibi ipɔntoon!
25Jeerusaleem, m làá tāā kí bīikì a-pu.
M làá dū kaŋwa kí fàl̀-si á nyā,
m làá nyāntí-si a-jɔkɔnti kɔkɔn.
26M làá yàntī a-bɔsoonliibi ń kpántí kii njamin yabee,
kí yàntī a-saŋkiliibi ń nīn bí kii cannaaku yabee.
Ní bí dāá nīn kíǹ ki yíì-si yii <Ibaamɔn Tiŋki,
Kitiŋ kin yú nì Unimbɔti deedeeyee>».
27Ibaamɔn làá fīī Siiyɔn tiŋki,
ní deedee ń yàntī ki-nib bin kpántì bi-bee ń ŋmátí.
28Ama pɔɔgaatib nì bikpitiŋaliibi làá nàan̄,
ní bin dū ti-Dindaan ki fée ń kúntí.
29Icoo làá cúú-ni iwaasufi in ni néeń tikpilee pu.
Ni-wunti làá yɔ̀tī ni-kpaaŋŋi ŋin ni lēē
kí nīn tòotī awaayee poon.
30Kun puee ni làá dāá nīn sá kii
buwaasubu bun faati yɔ́ĺee ní,
kii bukpaa bun poon ní nnyim fóotèe.
31Upɔɔl làá dāá nīn sá usá,
ní u-tuuŋŋi dāa sá kii ŋŋmiyatiyaalee.
Bi-liitil làá dāá fōō ŋŋmi,
ní ubɔ kaa dāa bí kí gbíntí.

english_text:
Peace That Lasts Forever
1This is the message I was given about Judah and Jerusalem:
2In the future, the mountain
with the Lord's temple
will be the highest of all.
It will reach above the hills;
every nation will rush to it.
3Many people will come and say,
“Let's go to the mountain
of the Lord God of Jacob
and worship in his temple.”
The Lord will teach us his Law
from Jerusalem,
and we will obey him.
4 He will settle arguments
between nations.
They will pound their swords
and their spears
into rakes and shovels;
they will never make war
or attack one another.
5People of Israel, let's live
by the light of the Lord.
Following Sinful Customs
6Our Lord, you have deserted
your people, Israel,
because they follow customs
of nations from the east.
They worship Philistine gods
and are close friends
of foreigners.
7They have endless treasures
of silver and gold;
they have countless horses
and war chariots.
8Everywhere in the country
they worship the idols
they have made.
9And so, all of them
will be ashamed and disgraced.
Don't forgive them!
A Day of Judgment
10 Every one of you,
go hide among the rocks
and in the ground,
because the Lord is fearsome,
marvelous, and glorious.
11When the Lord comes,
everyone who is proud
will be made humble,
and the Lord alone
will be honored.
12The Lord All-Powerful
has chosen a day
when those who are proud
and conceited
will be put down.
13The tall and towering
cedars of Lebanon
will be destroyed.
So will the oak trees of Bashan,
14all high mountains and hills,
15every strong fortress,
16all the seagoing ships,
and every beautiful boat.
17When that day comes,
everyone who is proud
will be put down.
Only the Lord will be honored.
18Idols will be gone for good.
19You had better hide
in caves and holes—
the Lord will be fearsome,
marvelous, and glorious
when he comes to terrify
people on earth.
20On that day everyone will throw
to the moles and bats
their idols of silver and gold
they made to worship.
21The Lord will be fearsome,
marvelous, and glorious
when he comes to terrify
people on earth—
they will hide in caves
and in the hills.
22Stop trusting the power
of humans.
They are all going to die,
so how can they help?
translation_text:
1Tibɔti tin an lēē ki dàkā Amɔtisi jipɔɔn Yeesaya Juuda beel nì Jeerusaleem tiŋki puee sèé.
Anibul kɔkɔ làá dāá kpāfì Jeerusaleem tiŋkin
(B. 2-4: kpèè Miika 4.1-3)
2Ŋwiin bí ki dòoń, dijool din pu ti-Dindaan diiku tɔ́kɔ́ee
làá dāá lìbitī ajoon kɔkɔ pu.
Di làá dāá nīn fɔ̀kɔǹ ŋgbantamu kɔkɔ.
Anibul kɔkɔ làá dāá nīn bìtifī ki dòoń di-cee.
3Anibul tikpil làá dāá tàkan̄ nsan
ki cá ki lì yii: «Dāam̄maan!
Tí jɔ̄m̀maan ti-Dindaan jool pu,
tí jɔ̄m̀maan Jaakɔb Nimbɔtiu diikun.
U làá tin dàkà-ti tin ní u là tí ŋée,
ní tí nóó u-sàmbiyaamu pu.»
Tiŋman, Siiyɔn ní Mara làá nyānní,
u-nyɔɔbundi làá nyānní Jeerusaleem ní.
4U làá dāá sòoǹ kí ŋāŋkì atimbun kansikin bɔti,
kí dāá pàtī anibul tikpil bí taa ti já.
Bi làá dāá dū bi-tàataajimmu kí mɔ́ɔ́ akoo,
ní kí dāá dū bi-kpammu kí mɔ́ɔ́ igɔti.
Ditimbundi diba kaa dāa gíti jáà nì di-juti,
ní binib kaa dāa gíti bífí bi nín jáà kujaau puee.
5Jaakɔb naantiibi, dāam̄maan
tí còom̀ ti-Dindaan walifiŋun.
Ti-Dindaan bɔsooŋyi wiiŋŋu
6Ti-Dindaan, a dū a-nibul
Jaakɔb naantiibi ki fá.
Kun puee ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú
bɔɔbi di kíǹ ki gbí bi-tiŋkin.
Bin kpèé iŋmalbijaa ki cáa būū tibɔɔlee
gbóotì kii Fiiliistii yab ceeyee.
A-nibul nì binicambi di kíǹ ki sòoǹ ki ŋàatī tɔb pu.
7Animbil kúti nì sindaariya gbí bi-tiŋkin,
ní ki-gaajawanti wīikí tikpil an kaa cáá bí lì.
Itaamu gbí bi-tiŋkin,
ní bi-janjatɔrɔkub wīikí tikpil.
8Awaa gbí bi-tiŋkin,
bi gbàantí ki jáaḿ awaa,
tiwan tin bi dū bi-ŋalii ki mɔ́ɔ́yee.
9An pu ní binib kɔkɔ làá nīn dɔ̄ kitiŋ ki fìlim̀,
ama ti-Dindaan, á taa yòon̄-bi kí síiń.
10Kɔ́maan kí báĺ itaŋkpalɔkɔ poon,
ní kɔ́ kitiŋ taapu kí báĺ
kí sāǹ ti-Dindaan ŋuukpaandi,
kí sāǹ u-kpaanti nín ŋmóò pu nyàlibuee nimbiin.
11Unil un yòontí u-ba yilpuee làá dāá tìntī u-yil,
bilambidambi làá dāá sìntī bi-ba taapu.
Ŋwiin gbantee, ti-Dindaan baba ní bi làá dāá tīī tinyool.
12Di sá yii ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan
lēē ŋwiin ŋun ní u làá dāá sòoǹ
bilambidambi nì bin dàkà bi-bee
nì binib bin yòontí bi-ba yilpuee bɔti,
ní kí dāá sìntī-bi taapu.
13U làá dāá sòoǹ Leebanɔn tiŋki sufii
in bi yíì seedir i fɔ̀kɔ̀ tikpilee bɔti,
kí dāá sòoǹ Baasan tiŋki waasufii in bi yíì seenee bɔti,
14kí dāá sòoǹ ajoon ŋin fɔ̀kɔ̀ee kɔkɔ bɔti,
kí dāá sòoǹ ŋgbantamu mun dúkutèe kɔkɔ bɔti,
15kí dāá sòoǹ adiin ŋin fɔ̀kɔ̀ líkí likee kɔkɔ bɔti,
nì agun ŋin baa ŋūǹ kí dàb̄ee kɔkɔ bɔti,
16kí dāá sòoǹ Taarsiisi tiŋkin meelab kɔkɔ bɔti,
ní kí dāá sòoǹ meelanyaambi kɔkɔ bɔti.
17Unil un yòontí u-ba yilpuee làá dāá tìntī u-yil,
bilambidambi làá dāá sìntī bi-ba taapu.
Ŋwiin gbantee, ti-Dindaan baba ní bi làá dāá tīī tinyool.
18Awaa kɔkɔ làá dāá wāŋkì.
19Kɔ́maan kí báĺ itaŋkpalɔkɔ poon,
ní kɔ́maan kí báĺ afaginni
kí sāǹ ti-Dindaan ŋuukpaandi,
kí sāǹ u-kpaanti nín ŋmóò pu nyàlibuee nimbiin,
u yaa láa yíkì ki bíi kɔ̄ntí kitiŋ kɔkɔ dinyoondee.
20Yaadalee, binib làá dāá dū awaa ŋin bi dū animbil kúti nì sindaariya ki mɔ́ɔ́ ki gbàantí ŋi-nimbiin ki jáaḿee kí lúkú isiiboo nì tinanjin. 21Binib làá kɔ́ kí báĺ itaŋkpalɔkɔ poon, kí kɔ́ kí báĺ ntaŋkpafaŋfakamin kí sāǹ ti-Dindaan ŋuukpaandi, kí sāǹ u-kpaanti nín ŋmóò pu nyàlibuee nimbiin, u yaa láa yíkì ki bíi kɔ̄ntí kitiŋ kɔkɔ dinyoondee.
22Ní taa nín̄ máká nisaaleen pu,
kufoou kun u cááyee pu ní u bí.
An yaa sá fám, unil sá ba?

english_text:
Judgment on Jerusalem and Judah
1The mighty Lord All-Powerful
is going to take away
from Jerusalem and Judah
everything you need—
your bread and water,
* 2soldiers and heroes,
judges and prophets,
leaders and army officers,
3officials and advisors,
fortunetellers and others
who tell the future.
4He will let children and babies
become your rulers.
5You will each be cruel
to friends and neighbors.
Young people will insult
their elders;
no one will show respect
to those who deserve it.
6Some of you will grab hold
of a relative and say,
“You still have a coat.
Be our leader and rule
this pile of ruins.”
7But the answer will be,
