Dibindi kamaayee,
u síiǹ-ti nnyɔmu mun ti làá nīn cēē tikpaajinee.>
25An sá ni-kpitii di pìkil̄ tin Unimbɔti bɔ́ntì ki síiǹee,
ni-yìntitam di pìintí tiŋan gbanti nsan.
26Di sá yii m-nibul kansikinee,
binikpitib bí.
Kii un kpáŋkí inoonee nín bí puee,
míǹ ní bi bāal̀ ki cí.
Bi píĺ titalindi ki sātì binib.
27Kii inoon nín gbí anɔndiinni puee,
míǹ ní tiwan tin bi fìkēe gbí bi-diiŋŋin.
Bi nín dī pu ki kpántì binikpaambi nì bigaajab,
28ki gbīfiǹ ki ŋá ŋkpamee dee.
Bi ŋá ikpiti an lákatì.
Baa sòoǹ tibɔti ti-pú,
kaa mɔ́tí ditaŋkpiibil pu,
ama ní an bútí-bi.
Baa pɔ̀ uwɔfi.
29Maa cáá nsan kí ŋá binib nee tibaaa?
Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.
Maa máaǹ kí tɔ̀ ditimbundi
din bí kii di neeyee ipɔntoonaaa?
30«Ntimbiil nì atulim bɔti
bíi jītí kitiŋ nee pu.
31Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi nàatī tinyimɔmbɔti,
ní bisaraaŋaliibi kāntí ipaati,
ní m-nibul ká yii míǹ ŋān̄!
Mimmee tin bí nee kɔkɔ yaa láa kúntèe,
ni làá dāá ŋá mana dee?»

english_text:
A Warning for the People of Jerusalem
The Lord said:
1Run for your lives,
people of Benjamin.
Get out of Jerusalem.
Sound a trumpet in Tekoa
and light a signal fire
in Beth-Haccherem.
Soon you will be struck
by disaster from the north.
2Jerusalem is a lovely pasture,
3but shepherds will surround it
and divided up,
then let their flocks
eat all the grass.
4Kings will tell their troops,
“If we reach Jerusalem
in the morning,
we'll attack at noon.
But if we arrive later,
5we'll attack after dark
and destroy its fortresses.”
6I am the Lord All-Powerful,
and I will command these armies
to chop down trees
and build a ramp up to the walls
of Jerusalem.
People of Jerusalem,
I must punish you
for your injustice.
7Evil pours from your city
like water from a spring.
Sounds of injustice and violence
echo within your walls;
victims are everywhere,
wounded and dying.
8Listen to me,
you people of Jerusalem
and Judah.
I will abandon you,
and your land will become
an empty desert.
9I will tell your enemies
to leave your nation bare
like a vine stripped of grapes.
I, the Lord All-Powerful,
have spoken.
Jeremiah's Anger
10I have told the people
that you, Lord,
will punish them,
but they just laugh
and refuse to listen.
11Your anger against Judah
flames up inside me,
and I can't hold it in
much longer.
The Lord's Anger Will Sweep Everyone Away
The Lord answered:
Don't hold back my anger!
Let it sweep away everyone—
the children at play
and all adults,
young and old alike.
12 I'll punish the people of Judah
and give to others
their houses and fields,
as well as their wives.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
13Everyone is greedy and dishonest,
whether poor or rich.
Even the prophets and priests
cannot be trusted.
14 All they ever offer
to my deeply wounded people
are empty hopes for peace.
15They should be ashamed
of their disgusting sins,
but they don't even blush.
And so, when I punish Judah,
they will end up on the ground,
dead like everyone else.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
The People of Judah Rejected God's Way of Life
16The Lord said:
My people, when you stood
at the crossroads,
I told you, “Follow the road
your ancestors took,
and you will find peace.”
But you refused.
17I also sent prophets
to warn you of danger,
but when they sounded the alarm,
you paid no attention.
18So I tell all nations on earth,
“Watch what I will do!
19My people ignored me
and rejected my laws.
They planned to do evil,
and now the evil they planned
will happen to them.”
20People of Judah,
you bring me incense from Sheba
and spices from distant lands.
You offer sacrifices of all kinds.
But why bother?
I hate these gifts of yours!
21So I will put stumbling blocks
in your path,
and everyone will die,
including parents and children,
neighbors and friends.
An Army from the North
22The Lord said,
“Look toward the north,
where a powerful nation
has prepared for war.
23Its well-armed troops are cruel
and never show mercy.
Their galloping horses sound
like ocean waves
pounding on the shore.
This army will attack you,
lovely Jerusalem.”
24Then the people said,
“Just hearing about them
makes us tremble with fear,
and we twist and turn in pain
like a woman giving birth.”
25The Lord said,
“Don't work in your fields
or walk along the roads.
It's too dangerous.
The enemy is well armed
26and attacks without warning.
So mourn, my people, as though
your only child had died.
Wear clothes made of sackcloth
and roll in the ash pile.”
The Lord's People Must Be Tested
The Lord said:
27Jeremiah, test my people
as though they were metal.
28And you'll find they are hard
like bronze and iron.
They are stubborn rebels,
always spreading lies.
* 29-30Silver can be purified
in a fiery furnace,
but my people are too wicked
to be made pure,
and so I have rejected them.
translation_text:
Binannanliibi māntìi tú Jeerusaleem tiŋki
1Beenjameen yab, sām̀maan
kí nyā Jeerusaleem tiŋkin.
Ní cùú báĺmaan laaba.
Búḿmaan ŋyin Teekoowa tiŋkin,
kí cóoḿmaan kudaaŋŋu ŋaabiki Beeti-Keereem tiŋkin,
di sá yii mbusu ubɔ, nnaabukpaan ŋubɔ
làá nyānní ŋgan pú kí dāan̄.
2 Siiyɔn tiŋki kin ŋān̄ dándanee,
bi nāaǹ-kì ní nee.
3Binib làá dāan̄ kí bìin̄ ki-pu,
kii bipikpaaliibi nì bi-picaŋkpuntee.
Bi làá gāā bi-bìńti kí màntīí tū-kì.
Báà ŋma làá nīn cáá u-jandi.
4Bi téeń yii: «Yīkìmaan!
Tí bɔ́ntímaan kujaau.
Tí cùú já nì Jeerusaleem tiŋki diwiŋkaŋkambil pu.
Timbi bɔlii na! Ŋwìiń bíi jēetí,
njooboon bíi lítí.
5Yīkìmaan tí cùú jáǹ-bi kunyeeu nee,
tí wīīmaan bi-dinyaaŋŋi!»
6Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín lī puee sèé:
«Gàatìmaan isufi kí kpúkuń kí nákáǹ Jeerusaleem gundi.»
M làá dáaĺ kitiŋ gbanti tafal,
kun puee tipɔmbɔti ŋma di gbí ki-poon.
7Kii nnyimbul nín tòoń di-nyim puee,
míǹ ní kì tòó ki-toom ki yàantí.
Ki-ceeyee, bi pée sòoǹ tipɔmbɔti nì dinàandi pu ní.
Falaabi nì tiweendi di pée dɔ̄ m-nimbiin baabadal.
8«Jeerusaleem, kpèè tiŋan,
an yaa kaa sá míǹ, m làá cúú m-ba kí nákatí kí wàatī-si,
kí nàan̄-si á kpántí kuteeu,
kitiŋ kin báà ubɔ kaa ti kóòyee.»
Isirayeel yab yíì kaa pílifiǹ ti-Dindaan
9Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín lī puee sèé.
«Kóom̀maan bin kɔkɔ kíǹ ki bí Isirayeel tiŋkinee
kii bi nín kōontí fiinyi subiliŋ sakaŋ bukpaan puee.
Fàtīí dūmaan ni-ŋalii kí máań máań
afiinyipan pu ŋfunyɔm kupaau,
kii bufiinyikpaa dindaan nín ŋáań puee.»
Yeereemii
10Tibɔti nee, ŋma cee ní m làá sòoǹ-tì?
Ŋma ní m làá kpāafì ní ú gbìl̄ ní?
Bi-tafaliŋ kpáá baa ŋūǹ kí gbìl̄.
Ti-Dindaan bɔti kpántì bi-cee ibeel ní,
baa pée là kí gbìl̄-tì.
11Ti-Dindaan ŋuul fòol̄ m-ni lìblib,
maa ti ŋūǹ kí ŋmèè.
ti-Dindaan
«Kpáatí diŋuul gbanti kí sìtī
mbiyaamu mun còom̄ adan puee
nì binipɔmbi kɔkɔ pu.
Bi-kɔkɔ làá kpántí bisarkadambi,
bininjab nì binimpoobi,
bijaŋkpilib nì bin púĺ sɔ́kɔ sɔkɔee.
12Biba di làá dāá jī bi-diiŋŋi
nì bi-sati nì bi-nimpoobi.
M làá tàntī m-ŋal kí gbēē kitiŋ nee nib,
ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ!
13Di sá yii kí yòon̄ bikpaambi kí tin sāā ŋwaamuee,
bi-kɔkɔ bìǹ ki nyàab̀ njim ní.
Kí yòon̄ Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi kí cáá sāā bisaraaŋaliibee,
bi-kɔkɔ cáá inaamuul ní.
14Bi cáá m-nibul naabuŋu
ki ŋáań bugbambu
ní ki lì yii: <Ŋgbansɔŋfi bí! Ŋgbansɔŋfi bí!>
Ama ní ŋgbansɔŋfi kpá.
15Ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin bi tūǹee,
an kɔ́ǹ-bi icoooo?
Aayee, kpataaa!
Baa kpáàa nyí gba yii bi ŋá tiba.
Ti-Dindaan bí yii:
An pu ní bi làá kūtì bin bíi lítée pu bí lítí.
M yaa láa tāā ki bíikì bi-puee,
bi làá dāá ká yii bi dɔ̄ kitiŋ ní.
16Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé:
Gbèem̄maan nsan ŋun ni dēe pu kí dàkafì.
Bàlifìmaan bí tùkù-ni njamin saŋyi bɔti.
Nyàab̀maan nsammɔnti kí nóó-ŋu.
Niin ní ni ŋūǹ kí ká dipɔɔsɔŋkil kí ŋùŋfì.
Ama ní bi kíí yii: <Taa làá nóó-ŋu.>
17M yóoǹ binib sintil bí kpāafì-bi yii:
<Ni yaa gbìl̄ bi búń ŋyinee, ní nīn nyí nì ni-ba!>
Ama ní bi kíí yii:
<Taa làá nīn nyí nì ti-ba.>
18An puee nimbi atimbun, pīlifìmaan!
Báà ŋma ń béé tin làá bàń bi-puee.
19Anibul ŋin kɔkɔ bí duulinyanee, pīlifìmaan.
M làá cáań nnaabu kí tɔ̄ binib nee pu.
Án làá nīn sá bi-tuŋkpitiŋ paati.
Baa dū m-bɔti ki yíiń tiba,
ní ki kpèé m-marab fám.
20Ba ní ni làá ŋá nì talaalutuukaa un
ni cāabìń Seeba tiŋkin,
nì kukaluu kun sɔ́fì
ni cáań kitiŋ kin dátèe poonee?
Maa là bisaraawɔkaabi bin ni ŋáań ki tìì-mee.
Ni-saraabi kaa fáatì-mi.
21An pu ní ti-Dindaan bí yii:
M làá dū tiwaŋgbeetikaal kí bíĺ
dinibul nee nyɔkɔpu dí gbéetí kí lítí.
Bibaatiibi nì bi-jipɔmbi,
bi-kɔŋkɔnnaatɔb nì bi-bɔɔbi
kɔkɔ làá kpú dicilpu.»
Binannanliibi làá nyānní ŋgan pú kí dāan̄
22Ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé.
«Dinibul diba làá nyānní ŋgan pú kí dāan̄.
Ditimbuŋkpaandi diba kālìń nsan pu
ki nyánní kitiŋ gbeennyɔkɔ ki dòoń.
23Bi-bijanjaliibi ŋúb́ itɔfi nì ŋkpamu.
Bi cáá ntoom kaa cáá disaasɔl.
Bi-bìntindi bí kii tiŋku wookuee ní.
Bi kā itaamu pu,
ki lūtì mpɔn pu
kí já nì sii Siiyɔn tiŋki.»
Isirayeel nibul
24«Ti nín gbìl̄ an bɔtee, ti-wunti yɔ̄tì.
Dinimbinaamandi kɔ́-ti fíŋfiŋ
ní ti bíi jīǹ falaa kii
unimpu un kā imatiŋween puee.
25Ní taa nyā kí cù tisatin,
kí taa nyā kí còom̀ adan pu,
di sá yii unannanli bí ki kù binib.
Dinyoondi bí an kɔkɔ pu.»
ti-Dindaan
26«Sii man nibul, dū kpɔsata kí pèen̄
kí nīn dɔ̄ ŋfantam poon ki bíntí.
Kíĺ kí nīn bíi ŋáań dikpool koobiliŋ
kii bi nín ŋáań dijipɔmbaabil kpool puee.
Nín̄ gà ikpiisilan ki yáliŋkí.
Di sá yii unannanli un làá nàan̄-see
làá páatí kí jēetí a-pu dicilpu dicilpu.»
Tikúti tin baa ŋūǹ kí lēē tijɔkɔndee
27Yeereemii, m kāaǹ-si á nīn sá kii un cɔ́ŋkí tikútee
kí ŋmā kí cɔ̄ŋkì m-nibul.
A máaǹ kí cɔ̄ŋkì kí béé bi-bimbim.
28Bi-kɔkɔ gáatì, baa ti ŋūǹ kí gíiǹní-bi,
bi kúŋfí bi-jutiibi boon.
Bi pɔ̄ɔ̄ kii tasa kúti àá kii tikúbɔnee ní.
Bi-kɔkɔ sá binàanliibi ní.
29Ŋfukum bíi fùkum̄
tikúti ń mántí tijɔkɔndi ń nyā.
Ucaa bíi pɔ̄ɔntí kí gbá kí lēē
tijɔkɔndi tin bí animbil puee, ama waa ŋúń.
Tijɔkɔndi kaa là kí nyā.
30Bi yíì binib gbanti yii,
<Animbil ŋin kaa ti bí tibanee.>
Tiŋman, ti-Dindaan dū-bi ki fá.

english_text:
Jeremiah Speaks in the Temple
(Jeremiah 26.1-6)
1-3The Lord told me to stand by the gate of the temple and tell the people who were going in that the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, had said:
Pay attention, people of Judah! Change your ways and start living right, then I will let you keep on living in your own country. 4Don't fool yourselves! My temple is here in Jerusalem, but that doesn't mean I will protect you. 5I will keep you safe only if you change your ways and are fair and honest with each other. 6Stop taking advantage of foreigners, orphans, and widows. Don't kill innocent people. And stop worshiping other gods. 7Then I will let you enjoy a long life in this land I gave your ancestors.
8But just look at what is happening! You put your trust in worthless lies. 9You steal and murder; you lie in court and are unfaithful in marriage. You worship idols and offer incense to Baal, when these gods have never done anything for you. 10And then you come into my temple and worship me! Do you think I will protect you so that you can go on sinning? 11 You are thieves, and you have made my temple your hideout. But I've seen everything you have done.
12 Go to Shiloh, where my sacred tent once stood. Take a look at what I did there. My people Israel sinned, and so I destroyed Shiloh!
13While you have been sinning, I have been trying to talk to you, but you refuse to listen. 14Don't think this temple will protect you. Long ago I told your ancestors to build it and worship me here, but now I have decided to tear it down, just as I destroyed Shiloh. 15And as for you, people of Judah, I'm going to send you away from my land, just as I sent away the people of Ephraim and the other northern tribes.
Punishment for Worshiping Other Gods
16Jeremiah, don't pray for these people! I, the Lord, would refuse to listen. 17Do you see what the people of Judah are doing in their towns and in the streets of Jerusalem? 18 Children gather firewood, their fathers build fires, and their mothers mix dough to bake bread for the goddess they call the Queen of Heaven. They even offer wine sacrifices to other gods, just to insult me. 19But they are not only insulting me; they are also harming themselves by doing these shameful things.
20And now, I, the Lord All-Powerful, will flood Judah with my fiery anger until nothing is left—no people or animals, no trees or crops.
It Is Useless To Offer Sacrifices
21The Lord told me to say to the people of Judah:
I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, but I won't accept sacrifices from you. So don't even bother bringing them to me. You might as well just cook the meat for yourselves.
22At the time I brought your ancestors out of Egypt, I didn't command them to offer sacrifices to me. 23Instead, I told them, “If you listen to me and do what I tell you, I will be your God, you will be my people, and all will go well for you.” 24But your ancestors refused to listen. They were stubborn, and whenever I wanted them to go one way, they always went the other. 25Ever since your ancestors left Egypt, I have been sending my servants the prophets to speak for me. 26But you have ignored me and become even more stubborn and sinful than your ancestors ever were!
Slaughter Valley
The Lord said:
27Jeremiah, no matter what you do, the people won't listen. 28So you must say to them:
People of Judah, I am the Lord your God, but you have refused to obey me, and you didn't change when I punished you. And now, you no longer even pretend to be faithful to me.
29Shave your head bald
and throw away the hair.
Sing a funeral song
on top of a barren hill.
You people have made me angry,
and I have abandoned you.
30You have disobeyed me by putting your disgusting idols in my temple, and now the temple itself is disgusting to me. 31 At Topheth in Hinnom Valley you have built altars where you kill your children and burn them as sacrifices to other gods. I would never think of telling you to do this. 32So watch out! Someday that place will no longer be called Topheth or Hinnom Valley. It will be called Slaughter Valley, because you will bury your dead there until you run out of room, 33and then bodies will lie scattered on the ground. Birds and wild animals will come and eat, and no one will be around to scare them off. 34 When I am finished with your land, there will be deathly silence in the empty ruins of Jerusalem and the towns of Judah—no happy voices, no sounds of parties or wedding celebrations.
translation_text:
Dimákakulindi
(Kpèè Yeer 26.1-19)
1Tibɔti tin Unimbɔti nìn sòon̄ ki tùkū Yeereemiiyee sèé: 2Cùú yūĺ kunimbɔtidii punyɔkɔpu kí bāakì tibɔti nee: «Ní pīlifìmaan ti-Dindaan bɔti nee, nimbi Juuda yab bin dì kipunyɔkɔ nee ki kóò ki jáaḿ ti-Dindaanee. 3Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Kpántímaan ni-bimbim nì ni-ŋáaǹtam, án nín làá ŋá pu ḿ nīn kóò ni-cee kitiŋ nee poonee. 4Ní taa nín̄ kùbitī ki lì yii: <Doo di sá ti-Dindaan Diiku, doo di sá ti-Dindaan Diiku, doo di sá ti-Dindaan Diiku.> Ní taa dū ni-mákal kí páań anyɔɔbuŋkiilkaa gbanti pu. 5Ní kpántí ni-bimbim nì ni-ŋáaǹtam. Ni nì ni-jutiibi kansikinee, ubɔ ń taa mùul̀ u-juti. 6Ní taa mùul̀ unicaan nì ditaŋkpiibil nì ukpiipu. Ní taa kpɔ̀ maanyiiba kitiŋ nee pu. Ní taa nín̄ jòó ki pá awaa ŋin làá cáá-ni kí kɔ́ǹ mbusunee boon. 7Niinee ní ḿ yàntī ní kàl̄ kitiŋ kin m nìn tīī ni-naanjab kí nīn cá abin abinee pu.
8«Ama ní ni dū ni-mákal ki ŋá tinyimɔmbɔti tin kaa bí tiba nee ni. 9Baaa! Ni yù, ki kù binib, ki ŋáań tilaakpaal, ki pùtī fám, ki tùutī talaalu ki tìì diwaal Baal, ki sáń ki pá awaa ŋin ni nì ŋi kaa cáá mpèé ŋubɔee boon. 10Míǹ boonee ní ní dāan̄ kí gbàan̄ m-nimbiin, kudii kun bi dūu sú-mee poon ki lì yii: <Ti ká difiil!> ní boonee ki gbíntìi nìkì ki tūǹ ntimbiil tuuŋŋi. 11Kunimbɔtidii kun bi dūu sú-mee ní ni dūu kpántì kunaayudii naaa? Too man nín wāĺ-ku puee dee.» Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.
12«Cùmaan Siiloo circir paaŋŋu pu kí kpèè. Dooooyee, niin ní m nìn kóò. Ní kpèè, Isirayeel m-nibul toom puee, m nín ŋá mpaan gbanti puee. 13Too, man ni-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Ni mun yīntì kii bimbee. M yōoǹ ŋyunti ki kpáafì-ni, ama ní naa pílifì, m yíiń-ni ní naa kíí-mi. 14Kpèè ni dū ni-mákal ki páaǹ kunimbɔtidii nee pu. Bi dū-ku ki sú-mi, ní man dū-ku ki tīī ni nì ni-naanjab. Too, m làá ŋá-ku kii m nín nìn ŋá Siiloo circir paaŋŋu puee ní. 15M làá dū-ni kí fá ndan kii m nín fá ni-nabiyaamu Eefiraayiim naantiibi puee ní.»
Ŋwimmeem min Unimbɔti kaa pílifée
16«An puee sii Yeereemii, á taa gbàam̀-mi dinibul nee pu. Á taa ti mèè-mi bi-pu, kí taa ti tīminsì bi-pu. Á taa nīn kā m-pu, maa làá pīlifiǹ-si. 17Saa wāĺ tin kɔkɔ bi bí ki ŋáań Juuda timmun nì Jeerusaleem daŋŋi pueeee? 18Mbiyaamu là idɔ ní bibaatiibi kpà ŋŋmi, ní binaatiibi nùkù ŋyim kí ŋá kalaabi kí tīī yilpu Nimpubɔtiu. Ni féeń awaa nnyim ki gbítí m-ŋuul. 19Ti-Dindaan bālifì yii: <Mimmee man ní bi dàkafī yii bi ŋáań ikpitaaa? Bi ŋáań bi-ba ní, ní an sá bi-cooi!>»
20«Too, m làá kpáatí m-ŋuukpaandi kí sìtī mpaan nee nì binib nì ipeel nì tisatin sufii nì tikpaajin pu. Di làá nīn bí kii ŋŋmi ŋun kaa kúùyee ní.»
Ditimbundi din kaa pílifí di-Nimbɔtiuee
21Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín lī puee sèé: «Dūmaan ni-saraawɔkaabi nanti kí kūtì saraafantantiibi nanti pu kí ŋmɔ́maan ni-ba. 22M nín nìn nyántì ni-naanjab kuyuŋun Eejipiti tiŋkinee, maa nìn tùkū-bi yii bí ŋá tiba. Maa nìn bí-bi yii bí ŋá bisaraawɔkaabi àá saraabi biba kí tīī-mi. 23Ama m nìn kpáafì-bi yii: <Ní pīlifìmaan m-nyɔkɔ. Ni yaa ŋá míǹ, m làá nīn sá ni-Nimbɔtiu, ní nimbi ń nīn sá man nibul. Nóómaan nsan ŋun m cátì ki bíl̀-nee ní án nīn ŋān̄ ki tīī-ni. 24Ama baa nìn pílifiǹ-mi, kaa kpōoǹ bi-tafal ki pílifì. Bi lēē kí nóó bi-landɔkɔkpitii. An nìn bàà sá bí fàtī bi-nimbiin kí túĺ-mee, ní bi fātì bi-boon ki tīī-mi. 25Kí yòon̄ ŋwiin ŋun m nyántì ni-naanjab Eejipiti tiŋkin kí dāá sāā díǹee, m pée tūǹ baabadal m-tɔntɔnliibi bibɔnaatiliibi ni-cee ní kaa gbèentí. 26Ama ní naa pílifiǹ-mi. Naa kpōoǹ ni-tafal kí pīlifì. Ni ŋá ŋyipɔn, ki ŋá tin jítiǹ ni-naanjabee.>
27«Sii Yeereemii, a làá tùkù-bi tibɔti gbanti, ama baa làá pīlifiǹ-si. A làá dāá téeń kí yíiń-bi, ama baa làá kíí-si. 28Tùkù-bi yii: <Kpèèmaan, ni sá ditimbundi din kaa pílifí di-Dindaan di-Nimbɔtiu nyɔkɔ, ní kaa fòol̄ u-saŋkiiyee ní. Tin bí deedeeyee kpíì ni-cee, ní ubɔ kaa ti sòoǹ ti-pu.>»
Laakin bi pɔ̄fì binibee tantakal
29Ti-Dindaan bí yii:
«Juuda nibul,
Cā a-yikpiti tin dàkà yii a dū a-ba ki sú-mee kí fá,
kí tóoń ŋkpiisilan ajoon ŋin yilpu kaa cáá timoolee pu.
Di sá yii a sá dinibul din kɔ́ǹ man ni-Dindaan diŋuulee ní.
An pu ní maa ti là kí wāl̀-si
ki dū-si ki fá.»
30Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Juuda yab ŋá tin kaa ŋān̄ee m-nimbiin. Bi cáá bi-waaŋi ŋin sá ntimbiilee ki kɔ́ǹ Kudii kun bi dūu sú-mee poon ki kɔ́ǹ-ku tijɔkɔndi. 31Been-Inɔɔm tantakalinee, bi bɔ́ntì ŋwaapaan ŋun bi yíì Toofeetee. Niin ní bi cáá bi-jipɔmbi nì bi-bisalib ki tòotī ki wù ŋŋmi ki ŋáań saraabi. Maa pée tīī-bi mara yii bí ŋá míǹ dalba dalba, kaa kpáàa dākafì an pu ŋwindal.»
32Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Iwiin bí ki dòoń, baa dāa gíti yíì mpaan gbanti yii: <Toofeeti> àá <Been-Inɔɔm tantakal>, ama <dipɔ̀fil tantakal>. Niin ní bi làá dāá síb́ anikpil, di sá yii mpaan kaa dāa gíti bí laaba bí síb́-ŋi. 33Inoon nì ipeel làá dāá gbáb́ kí bìin̄ anikpil gbanti pu ki jīǹ, ní ubɔ dāa kpá kí jà-i. 34M làá dāá yàntī Juuda timmun nì Jeerusaleem daŋŋi pu ifaal nì dipɔɔpindi laŋyi ń ŋmīĺ. Ubɔ kaa dāa gíti gbìl̀ animpucaŋgbiil pu. Di sá yii kitiŋ làá dāá kpántí adigbuŋkati ŋma ní.

english_text:
1Then the bones of the dead kings of Judah and their officials will be dug up, along with the bones of the priests, the prophets, and everyone else in Jerusalem 2who loved and worshiped the sun, moon, and stars. These bones will be scattered and left lying on the ground like trash, where the sun and moon and stars can shine on them.
3Some of you people of Judah will be left alive, but I will force you to go to foreign countries, and you will wish you were dead. I, the Lord God All-Powerful, have spoken.
The People Took the Wrong Road
4The Lord said:
People of Jerusalem,
when you stumble and fall,
you get back up,
and if you take a wrong road,
you turn around and go back.
5So why do you refuse
to come back to me?
Why do you hold so tightly
to your false gods?
6I listen carefully,
but none of you admit
that you've done wrong.
Without a second thought,
you run down the wrong road
like horses running blindly
into battle.
7Storks, doves, swallows,
and thrushes
all know when it's time
to fly away for the winter
and when to come back.
But you, my people,
don't know what I demand.
8You say, “We are wise
because we have the teachings
and laws of the Lord.”
But I say that your teachers
have turned my words
into lies!
9Your wise men
have rejected what I say,
and so they have no wisdom.
Now they will be trapped
and put to shame;
they won't know what to do.
10 I'll give their wives and fields
to strangers.
Everyone is greedy and dishonest,
whether poor or rich.
Even the prophets and priests
cannot be trusted.
11 All they ever offer
to my deeply wounded people
are empty hopes for peace.
12They should be ashamed
of the way they live,
but they don't even blush.
And so, when I punish Judah,
they will end up on the ground,
dead like everyone else.
13I will wipe them out.
They are vines without grapes;
fig trees without figs or leaves.
They have not done a thing
that I told them!
I, the Lord, have spoken.
The People and Their Punishment
14The people of Judah
say to each other,
“What are we waiting for?
Let's run to a town with walls
and die there.
We rebelled against the Lord,
and we were sentenced to die
by drinking poison.
15We had hoped for peace
and a time of healing,
but all we got was terror.
16Our enemies have reached
the town of Dan in the north,
and the snorting of their horses
makes us tremble with fear.
The enemy will destroy Jerusalem
and our entire nation.
No one will survive.”
17“Watch out!” the Lord says.
“I'm sending poisonous snakes
to attack you,
and no one can stop them.”
Jeremiah Mourns for His People
18I'm burdened with sorrow
and feel like giving up.
19In a foreign land
my people are crying.
Listen! You'll hear them say,
“Has the Lord deserted Zion?
Is he no longer its king?”
I hear the Lord reply,
“Why did you make me angry
by worshiping useless idols?”
20The people complain,
“Spring and summer
have come and gone,
but still the Lord
hasn't rescued us.”
21My people are crushed,
and so is my heart.
I am horrified and mourn.
22If medicine and doctors
may be found in Gilead,
why aren't my people healed?
translation_text:
1«Ti-Dindaan bí yii: <Ŋyunti gbantee, bi làá dāá nyāntiń Juuda yab bɔtiibi nì bi-kàliŋkpilib nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi nì bin kóò Jeerusaleemee kpabiŋ akaakul poon. 2Bi làá dāá dū akpab gbanti kí yàl̄ an kɔkɔ pu ŋwìiń nì uŋmal nì iŋmalbijaa in bitaŋkpiibi gbanti nìn néeń, ki jáaḿ, ki nóó ní ki bàlifēe nimbiin. An pu ní ubɔ kaa dāa gíti kōontí akpab gbanti kí gíiǹ-ŋi kí ŋá akaakulin. Ama ŋi làá dāá dòon̄ kitiŋ kí kpántí ntiŋkpam. 3Binikpitib nee kansikin bin yaa láa kíǹ ki bí dimaŋfalinee dāa lì yii ŋkúm sɔ́ǹ dimaŋfal.> Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di lī míǹ.»
Ti-Dindaan nibul kaa ti là kí gítiń u-cee
4«Á tùkù-bi yii, ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sɔ̀.
Unil yaa lítèe, waa ti yíkáaa?
Unil yaa yīntì nsanee,
waa gítiń u-boonaaa?
5Ama ba pu ní Jeerusaleem yab yīntì nsan,
ní ki gbíntìi nìkì ki fàtī bi-boon ki tìì man ní?
Binib gbanti dū bi-ba ki yá ki nákáǹ awaa
ní ki yíì kaa là kí fàtīí gítiń m-cee.
6M pílifì tin bi sòoǹee tiŋan,
ní tin bi sòoǹee kaa cáá taapu.
Ubɔ kaa pée lēē kí fá u-tuŋkpitiŋ.
Bi-kansikin ubɔ kaa bàlifī u-ba yii:
<Ba ní m ŋá nee?>
Bi-kɔkɔ fātìi kíĺ bi-taatandi,
a lì kii utaŋwaati di bí kujaaunee.
7Áli gba naakpaapiimbi bin ŋàaǹ kutaa puee
nyí ŋyunti ŋun sá bí yīkì kí búntée.
Ananjil nì jikpaasib nì ŋkoosiyaakpaamu
nyí bi-yuntii kí gítiń.
Ama m-nibul kaa nyí kí nóó
man bi-Dindaan marab bin m síiǹ-bee.»
8Mana ní ni ŋūǹ kí lì yii:
«Ti sá biciŋfitiibi, ti-Dindaan marab bí ti-cee?»
Di sá yii bimaradakaliibi bin fàtīi ŋmà marabee
sá binyimɔndambi ní ki kpántí marab gbanti.
9Biciŋfitiibi gbanti dū ti-Dindaan marab ki fá.
Mimmee bi-ciiŋŋu gbanti gíti bí tilatin?
Icoo cúú-bi gbòooo.
Dinyoondi kɔ́-bi ní an sàl̄-bi kii kutaliŋŋuee.
Binib bí ki sòoǹ yii tikɔkɔ còom̄ tiŋan
(Kpèè Yeer 6.12-15)
10An pu ní ti-Dindaan bí yii:
«M làá dū bi-nimpoobi kí tīī biba,
kí dū bi-sati kí tīī bin làá dāá fōō-tèe.
Di sá yii kí yòon̄ bikpaambi kí tin sāā ŋwaamuee,
bi-kɔkɔ bìǹ ki nyàab̀ njim ní.
Kí yòon̄ Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi kí cáá sāā bisaraaŋaliibee,
bi-kɔkɔ cáá inaamuul ní.
11Bi cáá m-nibul naabuŋu
ki ŋáań bugbambu
ní ki lì yii: <Ŋgbansɔŋfi bí! Ŋgbansɔŋfi bí!>
Ama ní ŋgbansɔŋfi kpá.
12Ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin bi tūǹee,
an kɔ́ǹ-bi icoooo?
Aayee, kpataaa!
Baa kpáàa nyí gba yii bi ŋá tiba.»
Ti-Dindaan bí yii:
«An pu ní bi làá kūtì bin bíi lítée pu bí lítí.
M yaa láa tāā ki bíikì bi-puee,
bi làá dāá ká yii bi dɔ̄ kitiŋ ní.»
Dimákal kaa ti bí
ti-Dindaan
13Ti-Dindaan bí yii:
«An yaa ŋmāntì ḿ kìtī asubil bi-ceeyee,
maa kāntí fiinyi pu abilaaa,
kaa kāntí fiigi pu abil.
Tifaal gba kūń,
m làá dū-bi kí fìtīǹ bisanjitiliibi.»
Isirayeel nibul
14«Ba pu ní tí nīn kā kaa cìŋkī?
Tí kóoǹ kí kpāfì,
kí cùú kɔ́ ntimu mun bi máń digundi ki túee poon,
kí nīn kíǹ ki kā ki cí ŋkúm.
Di sá yii ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu

15Ti bàà kā ki cí ŋgbansɔŋfi,

Ti bàà kā ki cí kí ká dicáaǹdi,

16Binannanliibi bāań Daani tiŋkin ki dóò.
Ti gbìl̄ itanjaa nín fèefī
doooo kitiŋ gbantinee.
Kuwoou kun bi ŋáańee

Bi dòoń kí nàan̄ kitiŋ nì ki-nib,
kitiŋee nì bin kóò ki-puee.»
ti-Dindaan
17«M làá dū ikoobu in cáá tilool

Yeereemii
18Tiba kaa bí ki ŋūǹ kí cáaǹ m-nimbaaku,

19Pīlifìmaan, m-nibul di kūuntí

23M yaa bàà ŋūǹ kí dū m-yil
