english_text:
1I wish that my eyes
were fountains of tears,
so I could cry day and night
for my people
who were killed.
2I wish I could go into the desert
and find a hiding place
from all who are treacherous
and unfaithful to God.
The Lord Answers Jeremiah
3The Lord replied:
Lies come from the mouths
of my people,
like arrows from a bow.
With each dishonest deed
their power increases,
and not one of them will admit
that I am God.
4Jeremiah, all your friends
and relatives
tell lies about you,
so don't trust them.
5They wear themselves out,
always looking for a new way
to cheat their friends.
6Everyone takes advantage
of everyone else,
and no one will admit
that I am God.
7And so I will purify
the hearts of my people
just as gold is purified
in a furnace.
I have no other choice.
8They say they want peace,
but this lie is deadly,
like an arrow that strikes
when you least expect it.
9Give me one good reason
not to punish them
as they deserve.
I, the Lord All-Powerful,
have spoken.
Jeremiah Weeps for His People
10I weep for the pastureland
in the hill country.
It's so barren and scorched
that no one travels there.
No cattle can be found there,
and birds and wild animals
have all disappeared.
11I heard the Lord reply,
“When I am finished,
Jerusalem and the towns of Judah
will be piles of ruins
where only jackals live.”
Why the Land Was Destroyed
12I said to the Lord, “None of us can understand why the land has become like an uncrossable desert. Won't you explain why?”
13The Lord said:
I destroyed the land because the people disobeyed me and rejected my laws and teachings. 14They were stubborn and worshiped Baal, just as their ancestors did. 15So I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, promise them poison to eat and drink. 16I'll scatter them in foreign countries that they and their ancestors have never even heard of. Finally, I will send enemy soldiers to kill every last one of them.
The Women Who Are Paid To Weep
17The Lord All-Powerful said,
“Make arrangements now
for the women who are paid
to weep at funerals,
especially the women
who can cry the loudest.”
18The people answered,
“Let them come quickly
and cry for us,
until our own eyes
are flooded with tears.
19Now those of us on Zion cry,
‘We are ruined!
We can't stand the shame.
Our homes have been destroyed,
and we must leave our land.’
20“We ask you women
to pay attention
to what the Lord says.
We will teach you a funeral song
that you can teach
your daughters and friends:
21‘We were in our fortress,
but death sneaked in
through our windows.
It even struck down
children at play
and our strongest young men.’
22“The Lord has told us
the ground will be covered
with dead bodies,
like ungathered stalks of grain
or manure in a field.”
What the Lord Likes Best
23The Lord says:
Don't brag about your wisdom
or strength or wealth.
24 If you feel you must brag,
then have enough sense
to brag about worshiping me,
the Lord.
What I like best
is showing kindness,
justice, and mercy
to everyone on earth.
25-26Someday I will punish the nations of Egypt, Edom, Ammon, and Moab, and the tribes of the desert. The men of these nations are circumcised, but they don't worship me. And it's the same with you people of Judah. Your bodies are circumcised, but your hearts are unchanged.
translation_text:
Ibaamɔn dóò
1M bàà là kí nīn bí kuteeun
laakin bisaŋkinliibi túutée!
M bàà làá dū m-nibul nee kí fá
kí cùú nīn bí niin ki dátiǹ-bi.
Di sá bi-kɔkɔ sá bilaakpaadambi,
ki nyēē binib boon.
2Ti-Dindaan bí yii:
«Bi-limbiliŋ bí kii butɔbu bun bi dáaĺee ní.
Bi dū nnyimɔn ní ki jíń dibeel kitiŋ pu,
kaa sá mbaamɔn.
Bi ŋáań ikpiti ní kaa gbèentí,
ama baa nyí-mi.
3Báà ŋma ń nīn nyí nì u-ba nì u-bɔɔ.
Ubɔ ń taa nín̄ máká u-nabiki pu,
di sá yii kì ŋūǹ kí kīil̀-u
ní ubɔɔti mun ŋūǹ kí kūŋfì u-boon.
4Báà ŋma kíiĺ u-juti,
ubɔ kaa sòoǹ ibaamɔn.
Bi mántì kí nīn mɔ́ntí.
Bi-tuŋkpitiŋ puee
baa ti ŋūǹ kí gítiń m-cee.»
5Ti-Dindaan bí yii:
Bi ŋáań tipɔmbɔti kaa gbèentí,
ki mɔ́ntí inyimɔn ki bùsī.
Bi yíití kaa là kí béé-mi.
6An pu ní ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan bí yii:
«M làá dū-bi kí ŋá ŋŋmin kí ŋá-bi circir,
ní kí cɔ̄ŋkì-bi kí kpèè.
Ba ní m gíti ŋūǹ kí ŋá nì
m-nibul nee kpitii?»
7Bi-limbiliŋ bí kii nlɔpiinee ní,
tinyimɔmbɔti ŋma di nyēē bi-nyɔmmun.
Bi-nyunculiŋ pu ní bi sòoǹ nì bi-juti yii
ŋgbansɔŋfi ń nīn bí u-cee,
ama ní bi-pɔbiliŋ poonee,
bi pīil̀ udaan kutaliŋŋu.
8Ti-Dindaan bí yii:
«Kii tin bí nee kɔkɔ puee,
m taa dáaĺ bi-tafalaaa?
M taa tɔ̀ ditimbundi
din bí kii di neeyee ipɔntoonaaa?»
Nsiim nì iyaliŋki yuntiŋu
9M bí ajoon pu ki sūǹ ki yáliŋkí,
m bí ki gà kunaakpaapɔɔu ikpiisilan.
Baa ti gbìl̀ tiwaŋkuti siim pu.
Inoon nì tiwaŋkuti kɔkɔ sáǹ. Báà tiba kaa ti bí.
10M làá yàntī Jeerusaleem ń kpántí ataŋkpakpuku,
laakin sinsiŋkub làá nīn kóòyee,
ní kí yàntī Juuda timmu
ń kpántí kuteeu,
laakin binib kaa làá nīn gíti kóòyee.
11Unil ubɔ bí ki cáá iciin
ki ŋūǹ kí gbìl̄ tibɔti nee taapuɔɔɔ?
Ti-Dindaan yaa sòon̄ nì udaanee,
ú tùkū-ti kun pu ní bi nāaǹ kitiŋ nee,
ki wùn̄-kì ŋŋmi kì kpántì kii kuteeu
ubɔ kaa ti jītí niinee.
12Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Kun pu tin bí nee bāań-bee di sá yii bi dū marab bin m tīī-bee ki fá. Baa pílifiǹ-mi kaa nóó-mi.» 13Ama bi nóó bíǹ bi-ba landɔkɔi ní. Bi-baabi nìn dàkā-bi awaa ŋin bi yíì Baalee, ní awaa gbanti ní bi nóó. 14Too, ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu bí yii: M làá tīī kisubiki kin tū ki cáá tiloolee bí ŋmɔ́, ní kí tīī-bi nnyim min cáá ndabiimee bí nyɔ̀. 15M làá jà-bi bí yàl̄ kí kɔ́ atimbun ŋin bíǹ bi-ba kaa nyáaa, bi-naanjab mun kaa nìn nyée poon. M làá dū ajanjakiti kí páań bi-boon, ŋí kpɔ̀ kí céetí-bi. 16Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan bí yii:
Isirayeel nibul
«Bɔ́ntímaan kí yíiń binimpoobi bin sūǹee
bí dāan̄ kí sɔ̄.
Ní nyàab̀ bimɔmmɔntiibi!
17Bí yáb́ malaa.
Bí gāā-ti ikpiisilan!
Nnyinnyim ń gbí ti-nimbiliŋin.
Ti-niŋgbunti ń díkí nnyinnyim ń nīn pùub̀!»
Yeereemii
18Ti gbìl̄ Siiyɔn pú ikpiisilan pu.
Bi nāaǹ-ti!
«Ba cooi bulifi poon ní ti bí na!
Ti làá yīkì kí fá ti-tiŋki,
di sá yii bi kpéelikì ti-diiŋŋi.»
19Nimbi binimpoobee, pīlifìmaan
ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi nee.
Ní ŋátí ni-tafal kí pīlifì u-nyɔɔbundi!
Ní dàkà ni-bisalib ŋkpiisilan nee,
báà ŋma ń dàkà u-kɔŋkɔnnaatɔ
iyaliŋki laŋŋu nee:
20«Di sá yii ŋkúm dàb̄ ti-tɔkɔlab ki kɔ́ ti-pu,
mì kɔ́ ti-dinyaaŋŋin.
Mì yōoǹ ti-biyaamu adan pu,
ki yōoǹ binipɔmbi sampaambi pu.»
ti-Dindaan
21«Sii Yeereemii, gíti sòoǹ tin ti-Dindaan lēe yii:
<Anikpil dɔ̄ kitiŋ fìlfil
kii tinaabin ní bi bíl̀ kusaaunee.
Ŋi náań nì idifin in bicaliibi cáń ki bíl̀
ubɔ kaa pá bi-boon ki kōontée.>»
Iciin in sá tiŋman pu yayee
22Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé:
«Uciŋfiti ń taa nín̄ yòontí u-ba u-ciiŋyi pu.
Upɔndaan ń taa nín̄ yòontí u-ba u-pɔŋŋu pu.
Ugaaja ń taa nín̄ yòontí u-ba u-gaajati pu.
23Ama ubɔ yaa làá yòon̄ u-ba yilpuee,
án nīn sá u nín ká dinyil ki béè-mee pu.
Di sá yii man ni-Dindaanee,
m cáá disaasɔl
ní ki ŋáań tin dɔ̄ nsan ki bí deedeeyee kitiŋ pu.
Tíǹ di fáatì-mi.»
Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.
Bin kaa gíí dikpancandi tiŋman pu yalee
24Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Ŋwiin ŋubɔ dòoń m làá tāā kí bīikì bin gíí dikpancandi ŋwuŋgban pu gíitamee pu, 25an dàkà yii Eejipiti yab nì Juuda yab nì Eedoom yab nì Amɔn yab nì Moowaab yab nì bin kɔkɔ kòol̄ bi-gatikii ki kóò kuteeunee. Di sá yii anibul gbanti kɔkɔ kaa gíí tiŋman pu gíitam, ní Isirayeel yab bi-ba kaa gíí bi-pɔbiliŋ.»

english_text:
The Lord Talks about Idols
1-2The Lord said:
Listen to me,
you people of Israel.
Don't follow the customs
of those nations
who become frightened
when they see something strange
happen in the sky.
3Their religion is worthless!
They chop down a tree,
carve the wood into an idol,
4cover it with silver and gold,
and then nail it down
so it won't fall over.
5An idol is no better
than a scarecrow.
It can't speak,
and it has to be carried,
because it can't walk.
Why worship an idol
that can't help or harm you?
Jeremiah Praises the Lord
6Our Lord, great and powerful,
you alone are God.
7 You are King of the nations.
Everyone should worship you.
No human anywhere on earth
is wiser than you.
8Idols are worthless,
and anyone who worships them
is a fool!
9Idols are made by humans.
A carver shapes the wood.
A metalworker hammers out
a covering of gold from Uphaz
or of silver from Tarshish.
Then the idol is dressed
in blue and purple clothes.
10You, Lord, are the only true
and living God.
You will rule for all time.
When you are angry
the earth shakes,
and nations are destroyed.
11You told me to say
that idols did not create
the heavens and the earth,
and that you, the Lord,
will destroy every idol.
12With your wisdom and power
you created the earth
and spread out the heavens.
13The waters in the heavens roar
at your command.
You make clouds appear—
you send the winds
from your storehouse
and make lightning flash
in the rain.
14People who make idols
are so stupid!
They will be disappointed,
because their false gods
are not alive.
15Idols are merely a joke,
and when the time is right,
they will be destroyed.
16But you, Israel's God,
created all things,
and you chose Israel
to be your very own.
Your name is the Lord
All-Powerful.
Judah Will Be Thrown from Its Land
17I said to the people of Judah,
“Gather your things;
you are surrounded.
18The Lord said these troubles
will lead to your capture,
and he will throw you
from this land
like a rock from a sling.”
19The people answered,
“We are wounded
and doomed to die.
Why did we say
we could stand the pain?
20Our homes are destroyed;
our children are dead.
No one is left
to help us find shelter.”
21But I told them,
“Our leaders were stupid failures,
because they refused
to listen to the Lord.
And so we've been scattered
like sheep.
22“Sounds of destruction
rumble from the north
like distant thunder.
Soon our towns will be ruins
where only jackals live.”
Jeremiah Prays
23I know, Lord, that we humans
are not in control
of our own lives.
24Correct me, as I deserve,
but not in your anger,
or I will be dead.
25Our enemies refuse
to admit that you are God
or to worship you.
They have wiped out our people
and left our nation
lying in ruins.
So get angry
and sweep them away!
translation_text:
Unimbɔti un bí dimaŋfalinee làá kúntí awaa
1Isirayeel yab, pīlifìmaan tibɔti tin ti-Dindaan sòon̄ ni-puee! 2U bí yii:
«Ní taa nín̄ túŋkíǹ atimbun ŋin kíǹee!
Ní taa fàŋkì tidaandi tin nyēē
ki pāantí kutagbɔŋu puee.
Atimbun ŋin kíǹee di fàŋkí an wanti.
3Di sá yii anibul ŋin kíǹee koobiliŋ kaa bí tiban!
Bi gà ndɔ kubambaŋŋun,
ní ukpiŋkpiiti ń dū kicɔkɔ kí kpítí diwaal.
4U dù animbil kúti nì sindaariya kí nyɔ̀kɔntì-dì,
ní kí dū dikújal nì mpiin kí kpáá-dì kí nákań,
dí nīn pɔ̄ɔ̄ kí taa nín̄ cìŋkī.
5Awaa gbanti náań nì tiwan tin bi sākaǹ
diputaajul kpaabun ki fàantí inoonee ní.
Awaa gbanti kaa sòoǹ.
Bi tūntí-ŋi ní,
di sá yii ŋaa ŋūǹ kí còom̀.
Taa fàŋkìmaan-ŋi,
di sá yii ŋaa ŋūǹ kí ŋá tikpitilaaa, kaa ŋūǹ kí ŋá tiŋan mun.»
6Sii, ti-Dindaan, ubɔ kaa bí kii siiyee!
A sá ukpaan,
ní a-yindi sá dikpaandi ki cáá mpɔn.
7Ŋma di kaa fàŋkí sii atimbun bɔtiu?
Kun puee sii ní bi máaǹ kí fàŋkì.
Di sá yii duulinya ciŋfitiibi kansikin,
nì abee kɔkɔ poonee, ubɔ kaa bí kii siiyee.
8Bi-kɔkɔ nín bí pu nee, ugàntil kpá,
bi sá bigbaambi kaa nyí tiba.
Bi-waaŋi kaa ŋūǹ kí dàkà-bi tiba,
di sá yii ŋì sá idɔ ní.
9Ukpiŋkpiiti di kpítì-ŋi,
ní ukúduntil dūu tikúti ki dūntì ki nyūntì-ŋi
ní ki dū animbil kúti tin nyánní Taarsiisi tiŋkinee,
nì sindaariya un nyánní Ufasi tiŋkinee ki nyɔ̄kɔntì-ŋi.
Míǹ boonee ní bi dū iŋaaman cínciŋ nì in máǹ wèeeeyee
ki ŋáĺ dibɔkutil ki pēeǹ-ŋi.
Bin nyí iŋal pu tundi tiŋanee di mɔ́ɔ̀ an wanti.
10Ama ti-Dindaan di sá Unimbɔti tiŋman pu yɔu.
U sá Unimbɔti un bí dimaŋfalinee,
ki sá ubɔti kí nīn cá jaanjaan.
U yaa fōō diŋuulee, kitiŋ cìŋkī ní,
ní atimbun kaa ŋūǹ kí yūĺ u-bum nimbiin.
11Kpèè ni nín làá sòoǹ nì bi puee sèé:
Bi máaǹ kí kúntí awaa ŋin kaa náań yilpu nì taapuee,
ŋi máaǹ kí wāŋkì kutagbɔŋu taapu.
12Ti-Dindaan di dū u-pɔŋŋu ki ŋá kitiŋ,
ki dū u-ciiŋŋu ki náań duulinya,
ki dū u-nyil ki kpátì kutagbɔŋu ki dāntì.
13U yaa téeńee,
inyiŋfi kōontí ní kí kpāfì kutagbɔŋu pu.
U yàntī atagbaŋkpaan ń nyānní kitiŋ gbeennyɔkɔ kí jɔ̄m̀.
U yàntī utaa ń ŋmɔ́ kí cáań utaa,
ní ki nyāntiń kubuŋu ku-walimbookun.
14Binib kɔkɔ bākatì sèee,
kaa ti nyí tin poon bi bée.
Awaa ŋin bikúduntiliibi mɔ́ɔ́yee cáá-bi icoo.
Awaa gbanti sá tinyimɔmbɔti ní.
Ŋaa cáá kufoou.
15Ŋì sá tiwan tin kaa bí tibanee,
ki mɔ̄ tilaal.
Ŋwiin ŋun ti-Dindaan làá yīkì ŋi-puee,
ŋì làá wāŋkì ní.
16Ama Unimbɔti un sá Jaakɔb gaajawantee,
kaa bí kii ŋíǹ nín bí puee.
Jaakɔb Nimbɔtiu di náań duulinya kɔkɔ,
ní Isirayeel naakooku sá u-fakal.
U-yindi di sá ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan.
Nnaabu tóobiń
17Jeerusaleem, sii un bi māntìi túee,
kóoǹ a-waŋguliŋ ŋin dɔ̄ kitiŋee!
18Ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé:
«Min bí nee, m làá dū kitiŋ nee nib
kí tɔ̄ ndan kii kujaataafuŋ taŋkpalee.
M làá cáań dinimbinaamandi kí tɔ̄ bi-pu
áli ubɔ ń taa ŋmátí.»
19Ba busuu dee! Nnaabu ŋulɔŋu ŋúǹ dee!,
Tiweendi tin m fōōyee kaa cáá dicáaǹdi!
M lī m-ban yii:
«An kaa páb́,
m làá ŋmā kí túń m-gìńdi.
20Bi nāaǹ m-tantiu, u-ŋmiii kɔkɔ tīfì.
M-biyaamu yíkì-mi, muaa ti bí.
Ubɔ kaa ti bí kí cóoń m-tantiu,
kí ŋāŋkì m-kɔŋkooŋŋu.»
21Tin yì-tèe di sá yii bikpootiliibi ŋá digbaandi.
Baa nyàab̄ ti-Dindaan.
An pu ní an kaa bútì-bi,
ní bin bi nìn kpòotēe yàl̄ an kɔkɔ pu.
22Ti gbìl̄ kuwoou kubɔ pu, ku tóobiń.
Kukunsaŋu kubɔ nyánní ŋgan pú tiŋkin.
Ku làá yàntī Juuda tiŋki ń kpántí kuteeu,
laakin sinsiŋkub làá nīn kóòyee.
Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu wimmeem
23M-Dindaan, m nyí yii,
unil kaa yì u-ba.
Unil un còom̄ee kaa ŋūǹ
kí kpòotī u-ba.
24Dáaĺ m-tafal,
ama á taa lákatí marab pu.
Taa fōō diŋuul, an yaa sá fám, a làá nàan̄-mi.
25Kpáatí a-ŋuul kí sìtī
atimbun ŋin kaa nyí-see pu,
kí sìtī anibul ŋin kaa jáaḿ-see pu.
Kun puee bi tɔ̄ntì a-nibul Jaakɔb naantiibi,
bi fúkúl̀-bi ki púntì-bi,
ní ki nāaǹ bi-tiŋki.

english_text:
Judah Has Broken the Lord's Agreement
1-3The Lord God told me to say to the people of Judah and Jerusalem:
I, the Lord, am warning you that I will put a curse on anyone who doesn't keep the agreement I made with Israel. So pay attention to what it says. 4My commands haven't changed since I brought your ancestors out of Egypt, a nation that seemed like a blazing furnace where iron ore is melted. I told your ancestors that if they obeyed my commands, I would be their God, and they would be my people. 5Then I did what I had promised and gave them this wonderful land, where you now live.
“Yes, Lord,” I replied, “that's true.”
6Then the Lord told me to say to everyone on the streets of Jerusalem and in the towns of Judah:
Pay attention to the commands in my agreement with you. 7Ever since I brought your ancestors out of Egypt, I have been telling your people to obey me. But you and your ancestors 8have always been stubborn. You have refused to listen, and instead you have done whatever your sinful hearts have desired.
You have not kept the agreement we made, so I will make you suffer every curse that goes with it.
9The Lord said to me:
Jeremiah, the people of Judah and Jerusalem are plotting against me. 10They have sinned in the same way their ancestors did, by turning from me and worshiping other gods. The northern kingdom of Israel broke the agreement I made with your ancestors, and now the southern kingdom of Judah has done the same.
11Here is what I've decided to do. I will bring suffering on the people of Judah and Jerusalem, and no one will escape. They will beg me to help, but I won't listen to their prayers. 12-13Then they will offer sacrifices to their other gods and ask them for help. After all, the people of Judah have more gods than towns, and more shameful altars for Baal than there are streets in Jerusalem. But those gods won't be able to rescue the people of Judah from disaster.
14Jeremiah, don't pray for these people or beg me to rescue them. If you do, I won't listen, and I certainly won't listen if they pray!
15Then the Lord told me to say to the people of Judah:
You are my chosen people,
but you have no right
to be here in my temple,
doing such evil things.
The sacrifices you offer me
won't protect you from disaster,
so stop celebrating.
16Once you were like an olive tree
covered with fruit.
But soon I will send a noisy mob
to break off your branches
and set you on fire.
17I am the Lord All-Powerful. You people of Judah were like a tree that I had planted, but you have made me angry by offering sacrifices to Baal, just as the northern kingdom did. And now I'm going to pull you up by the roots.
The Plot To Kill Jeremiah
* 18Some people plotted to kill me.
And like a lamb
being led to the butcher,
I knew nothing
about their plans.
19But then the Lord told me
that they had planned
to chop me down like a tree—
fruit and all—
so that no one would ever
remember me again.
20 I prayed, “Lord All-Powerful,
you always do what is right,
and you know every thought.
So I trust you to help me
and to take revenge.”
21Then the Lord said:
Jeremiah, some men from Anathoth say they will kill you, if you keep on speaking for me. 22But I will punish them. Their young men will die in battle, and their children will starve to death. 23And when I am finished, no one from their families will be left alive.
translation_text:
Unimbɔti nibul nyáń u-pèéŋu boon
1Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Yeereemii yii: 2«Ní nīn tɔ́ mpèé ŋun bí man nì ni kansikinee.» Ní u kútì ki lī yii: «Á sòoǹ nì Juuda nì Jeerusaleem yab. 3Á tùkù-bi yii: Ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí unil un kaa tɔ́ mpèé nee nyɔɔbuŋŋee! 4M nìn nyántì ni-naanjab Eejipiti tiŋkin, kipaai ŋmiŋun. Ŋyunti gbanti ní man nì bi nìn ŋá mpèé nee. M nìn bí-bi yii: <Ní pīlifì m-nyɔkɔ kí ŋá tin kɔkɔ m bí yii ní ŋée. Niinee, ni làá nīn sá m-nibul, ní ma mun ń nīn sá ni-Nimbɔtiu.> 5Niinee, m làá ŋá m nín nìn pōoǹ ni-naanjab puee kí tīī-bi. M nìn pōoǹ-bi yii m làá dū kitiŋ kin poon nnaabiim nì tisiil còol̀ee kí tīī-bi. Kitiŋ gbanti poon ní ni bí díǹ nee.»
Ní m kíí yii: «An sá míǹ ní ti-Dindaan.»
6Ní ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii:
«Dū an bɔti gbanti kɔkɔ kí bāakì Juuda timmu nì Jeerusaleem daŋŋi pu yii: <Ní pīlifìmaan mpèé nee bɔti, kí ŋá tì nín bí yii ní ŋá puee. 7M nín nìn nyántì ni-naanjab Eejipiti tiŋkin ki dāa sāā díǹ nee, m nìn pée kpáafí-bi ní kaa gbèentí, kii m nín bíi kpáafí ni mun díǹ pu nee ní. M lì ki bùsī yii bí pīlifì m-nyɔkɔ. 8Ama baa pílifàaa, kaa fātìi tɔ́. Bi-landɔkɔkpitii ní bi nóó. Niinee ní m yāntì agìń ŋin m nìn tùkū-bi yii bi yaa kaa ŋúb́ mpèé nee bɔti bi làá kée, bāań-bi.>»
9Boonee ní ti-Dindaan gíti bí-mi yii: «Juuda nì Jeerusaleem yab ŋá kinyɔkɔ kí já nì mi. 10Bi fātìi gítì ikpiti in bi-naanjab bin nìn yíì kaa pílifì m-bɔtee nìn ŋée pu. Bi nóó awaa ki tòotī-ŋi. Isirayeel nì Juuda yab bíil̀ mpèé ŋun nìn bí man nì bi-naanjab kansikinee.
11«Too, an pu ní ti-Dindaan bí yii: <M làá cáań nnaabu ŋubɔ kí tɔ̄ bi-pu, ní baa làá ŋmā kí ŋmátí. Bi làá dāá kúuǹ kí yíiń-mi ḿ jòò-bi, ama maa làá dāá pīlifiǹ-bi. 12Juuda yab nì Jeerusaleem yab làá dāá cù kí mèè bi-waaŋi ŋin bi cá ki tùutī talaalub ki tììyee, ama ŋaa làá dāá ŋmā kí fīī-bi nnaabu yuntiŋu gbantin. 13Juuda yab timmu nín wīikí puee, míǹ ní bi-waaŋi mun wīikí. Jeerusaleem daŋŋi nín wīikí puee, míǹ ní ki-saraafaŋyi mun wīikí. Bi tùutī i-pu saraabi ki tìì diwaal Baal din sá-bi icooyee.> 14Sii Yeereemii, á taa pée mèè dinibul nee pu. Á taa sɔ̄ di-pu, kí taa gbàam̀ di-pu. Di sá yii dinimbinaamandi yuntiŋu poonee, bi làá dāá mèè-mi, ama maa làá dāá pīlifiǹ-bi.»
Ti-Dindaan làá gāā ɔliifi subu kí lúkú
15«Ba ní dinibul din m néeńee nib
dòoń kí ŋá m-Diikun ní?
Bi ŋá bi-landɔkɔkpitii nín sá puee.
Bi dàkafī yii ipoon nì tiwaŋkuti tin bi cáa ŋáań-mi saraayee
ŋūǹ kí kpàà bi-naabuŋu kí cùnnì ndan kí wàatī-bi ní.
Mimmee míǹ ní bi làá ŋá kí ŋmátáaa?
16M nìn pú-bi diyindi yii:
<Ɔliifi subu bun faati pée sɔ̀m̀ bu-biliŋ ŋān̄ee ní.>
Ama dibintiŋkpaandi poonee,
m gāā ŋŋmi ki tūū bu-faati
ní bu-paŋŋi wáŋkì.»
17An sá ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di cóoǹ-si. Ama kɔŋkɔnnee, u bíi tùkù-si yii u làá cáań nnaabu kí tɔ̄ a-pu Isirayeel nì Juuda yab kpitii pu. Di sá yii bi tūutì talaalub ki tīī diwaal Baal ki gbítì ti-Dindaan ŋuul.
Yeereemii dicaŋkun yab nyáń u-pu
18Ti-Dindaan lēē ki dàkā-mi, ní m béè tin m-nannanliibi bíi búkù m-puee. 19Mamee, m nìn bí kii dipibil din pɔ̀fì bi cáǹ-dì kí kpɔ̀ee ní. Maa nìn nyí tin bi nìn bíi bɔ́ntí m-puee. Bi nìn lì yii: «Tí gāā busubu bun dáá sɔ̀m̀ee kí lúkú. Tí lēē-u binifoobi tiŋkin bí taa ti téetí u-yindi pu.»
20Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan,
a sòoǹ tibɔti nì deedee ní.
Sii di nyí unil pɔbilin nì u-landɔkɔi.
M dū m-ba ki líiǹ-si á sòoǹ m-bɔti kí tīī-mi.
Niinee ní ḿ ká a nín làá pɔ̀-mi puee.
21Too, ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ nì Anatooti yab bin là kí kpɔ̀-see puee sèé. Bi lì yii: «Taa ti nàatī Unimbɔti bɔti ti-Dindaan yindi pu, an yaa kaa sá míǹ, ti làá kpɔ̀-si.» 22Too, ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «M làá tāā kí bīikì bi-pu. Bi làá kpɔ̀ bi-nipɔmbi kujaaun, ní bi-jipɔmbi nì bi-bisalib ń kpú ŋkùm. 23Dibindi din m làá tāā kí bīikì Anatooti yab pu kí cáań nnaabu kí tɔ̄ bi-puee, báà uniseen kaa làá ŋmátí.»

english_text:
Jeremiah Complains to the Lord
1Whenever I complain
to you, Lord,
you are always fair.
But now I have questions
about your justice.
Why is life easy for sinners?
Why are they successful?
2You plant them like trees;
you let them prosper
and produce fruit.
Yet even when they praise you,
they don't mean it.
3But you know, Lord,
how faithful I've always been,
even in my thoughts.
So drag my enemies away
and butcher them like sheep!
4How long will the ground be dry
and the pasturelands parched?
The birds and animals
are dead and gone.
And all of this happened because
the people are so sinful.
They even brag, “God can't see
the sins we commit.”
The Lord Answers Jeremiah
5Jeremiah, if you get tired
in a race against people,
how can you possibly run
against horses?
If you fall in open fields,
what will happen in the forest
along the Jordan River?
6Even your own family
has turned against you.
They act friendly,
but don't trust them.
They're out to get you,
and so is everyone else.
The Lord Is Furious with His People
7I loved my people and chose them
as my very own.
But now I will reject them
and hand them over
to their enemies.
8My people have turned against me
and roar at me like lions.
That's why I hate them.
9My people are like a hawk
surrounded and attacked
by other hawks.
Tell the wild animals
to come and eat their fill.
10My beautiful land is ruined
like a field or a vineyard
trampled by shepherds
and stripped bare
by their flocks.
11Every field I see lies barren,
and no one cares.
12A destroying army
marches along desert roads
and attacks everywhere.
They are my deadly sword;
no one is safe from them.
13My people, you planted wheat,
but because I was furious,
I let only weeds grow.
You wore yourselves out
and gained only shame!
The Lord Will Have Pity on Other Nations
14The Lord said:
I gave this land to my people Israel, but enemies around it have attacked and robbed it. So I will uproot them from their own countries just as I will uproot Judah from its land. 15But later, I will have pity on these nations and bring them back to their own lands. 16They once taught my people to worship Baal. But if they admit I am the only true God, and if they let my people teach them how to worship me, these nations will also become my people. 17However, if they don't listen to me, I will uproot them from their lands and completely destroy them. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
1M-Dindaan, a baasii sá deedeedaan ní,
maa ŋūǹ kí kpákáǹ-si.
Ama m là kí sòoǹ nì si tin bí deedeeyee pu.
Ba pu ní an bútí binikpitib ní?
Ba pu ní bin kaa bí deedeeyee bí ŋgbansɔŋfin ní?
2A cóoǹ-bi bi báaǹ inyaan
áli ki lòon̄ abil.
A-yindi pée kā bi-nyɔkɔn,
ama ní bi-pɔbiliŋ dátiǹ-si.
3Ama mamee, m-Dindaan, a nyí-mi,
a wāĺ-mi ki nyí m-landɔkɔi,
i dɔ̄ a-nimbiin.
Gàntī binikpitib kí síiń
kii bi nín lèekī ipii in bi làá kpɔ̀ee kí síiń puee.
Kpāafì-bi kí síiń ŋwiin ŋun a làá kpɔ̀-bee.
4Kí tin sāā ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu ní kitiŋ nee làá nīn bí kunimbaaun ní? Kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu ní akpaan làá nīn dɔ̄ ki kūń ní? Kitiŋ nee peelii nì ki-nooŋyi bíi kúù bin kóò ki-puee kpitii pu. Bi lì yii: «Yeereemii kaa ti làá nīn bí kí ká tin làá bàń-tee.»
5«Sii nì binib yaa bíi sáń ní a gīīyee,
kin mana ní si nì itaamu ŋūǹ kí sāǹ kí kpáká?
An yaa sá kitiŋ kin cáá ŋgbansɔŋfee poon
ŋmaniŋma ní a ŋūǹ kí nīn bí a-pɔbil sɔ̀m̀ee,
kin mana ní a làá ŋá
a yaa láa kɔ́ Jɔɔdan mɔgbaakin?
6«Di sá yii, a-nabiyaamu, a-dicaŋkun yab nyēē a-boon. Bi kóoǹ binib ki kpáfì bí já nì si ní saa nyí. Bi yaa bíi sòoǹ nì si nì anyɔɔbummɔntee, á taa nín̄ máká bi-pu.»
Ti-Dindaan dū u-diiku nì u-nibul ki fá
7«M dū m-Diiku ki fá,
m fātì m-boon ki tīī tin sá m-yatee.
M dū dinibul din m néeńee
ki líiǹ di-nannanliibi.
8Bin nìn sá man yabee kpántì
kii gbikinti di bí kupɔɔunee.
Bi gbùkum̄ ki tátí m-pu,
an puee ní maa ti là bi-bɔti.
9Bin nìn sá man yabee
kpántì kii kinɔmbiki kin ŋān̄,
ní ikaabu gbáb́ ki bīiǹ ki-puee.
Ní cùmaan kí kóoǹ ipeel kí kpāfì,
í dāan̄ kí jī jiŋaal.
10 Bipikpaaliibi tikpil dɔ́miń ki bíil̀ m-fiinyi kpaabu,
bi tāā m-tiŋki kì ŋá púb,
ki dū m-tinjandi din ŋān̄ee
ki kpántì kunimbaau teeku.
11Bi yāntì kì kpántì inimɔɔn tiŋki,
ki bí kunimbaaun,
kì kpántì kitiŋkuliŋŋi.
Bi nāaǹ kitiŋee kɔkɔ
ní báà ubɔ kaa fātìi tɔ́.»
12Binàanliibi páaǹní kuteeu jooŋŋi pu ki dòoń.
Ti-Dindaan tàataajiki bíi pɔ̀fī tikɔkɔ,
kí yòon̄ kitiŋ kílilaŋki ki tin sāā ki-kúntilaŋki.
Báà uniseen kaa ti bí ŋgbansɔŋfin.
13Bi nìn búĺ bilee ní ki dāa cáń ikuŋkum,
bi bìn̄ ki gīī púb, ama kaa ká ipaati.
Ti-Dindaan ŋuukpaandi din u fōō ni-puee
di yì-tì ní tin ni cáńee cáá-ni icoo.
Ti-Dindaan nì Isirayeel yab kɔŋkɔnnaatɔb bɔti
14Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M-kɔŋkɔnaatɔb bin kɔkɔ sá binikpitib ki gbēē kitiŋ kin m dūu tīī m-nibul Isirayeelee, m làá jà-bi bi-tiŋki pu. Ama m làá cúú Juuda nibul kí nyāntí bi-kansikin. 15Míǹ boonee, m làá sɔ̄ bi-saai, ní kí gíiǹní-bi bi-tiŋkin, báà ŋma nì u-kpaatanti pu. 16Bi nìn bífì m-nibul bí nīn pùtī Baal yindi pu. Ama bíǹ bi-ba yaa kíǹ ki cáá m-nibul bimbim, ki kíǹ ki cáá m-yindi ki pùtī ki lì yii: <M pūtì ti-Dindaan un bí dimaŋfalinee>, m làá dāá fōō-bi m-nibul kansikin. 17Ama atimbun gbanti diba yaa yíì kaa pílifiǹ-mee, m làá kpìkitī-dì kii bi nín kpìkitī busubu puee ní kí dū-dì kí líiǹ ŋkúm, ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_text:
Jeremiah's Linen Shorts
1The Lord told me, “Go and buy a pair of linen shorts. Wear them for a while, but don't wash them.” 2So I bought a pair of shorts and put them on.
3Then the Lord said, 4“Take off the shorts. Go to Parah and hide the shorts in a crack between some large rocks.” 5And that's what I did.
6Some time later the Lord said, “Go back and get the shorts.” 7I went back and dug the shorts out of their hiding place, but the cloth had rotted, and the shorts were ruined.
8Then the Lord said:
9Jeremiah, I will use Babylonia to destroy the pride of the people of Judah and Jerusalem. 10The people of Judah are evil and stubborn. So instead of listening to me, they do whatever they want and even worship other gods. When I am finished with these people, they will be good for nothing, just like this pair of shorts. 11These shorts were tight around your waist, and that's how tightly I held onto the kingdoms of Israel and Judah. I wanted them to be my people. I wanted to make them famous, so that other nations would praise and honor me, but they refused to obey me.
Wine Jars
The Lord said:
12Jeremiah, tell the people of Judah, “The Lord God of Israel orders you to fill your wine jars with wine.”
They will answer, “Of course we fill our wine jars with wine! Why are you telling us something we already know?”
13Then say to them:
I am the Lord, and what I'm going to do will make everyone in Judah and Jerusalem appear to be full of wine. And the worst ones will be the kings of David's family and the priests and the prophets. 14Then I will smash them against each other like jars. I will have no pity on the young or the old, and they will all be destroyed. I, the Lord, have spoken.
The People of Judah Will Be Taken Away
15People of Judah,
don't be too proud to listen
to what the Lord has said.
16You hope for light,
but God is sending darkness.
Evening shadows already deepen
in the hills.
So return to God
and confess your sins to him
before you trip and fall.
17If you are too proud to listen,
I will weep alone.
Tears will stream from my eyes
when the Lord's people
are taken away as prisoners.
18The Lord told me to tell you
that your king and his mother
must surrender their thrones
and remove their crowns.
19The cities in the Southern Desert
are surrounded;
no one can get in or out.
Everyone in Judah
will be taken away.
20Jerusalem, you were so proud
of ruling the people of Judah.
But where are they now?
Look north, and you will see
your enemies approaching.
21You once trusted them to help,
but now I'll let them rule you.
What do you say about that?
You will be in pain
like a woman giving birth.
22Do you know why
your clothes were torn off
and you were abused?
It was because
of your terrible sins.
23Can you ever change
and do what's right?
Can people change the color
of their skin,
or can a leopard
remove its spots?
If so, then maybe you can change
and learn to do right.
24I will scatter you,
just as the desert wind
blows husks from grain
tossed in the air.
25I won't change my mind.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
You rejected me
and worshiped false gods.
* 26You were married to me,
but you were unfaithful.
You even became a prostitute
by worshiping disgusting gods
on hilltops and in fields.
27So I'll rip off your clothes
and leave you naked and ashamed
for everyone to see.
You are doomed!
Will you ever be worthy
to worship me again?
translation_text:
Yeereemii dambalau bɔti
1Ti-Dindaan nín tùkū-mi puee sèé: «Cùú dā ŋŋaabu ŋun bí fálfalee dambalau kí gbìn̄ a-caŋ, ama á taa dū-u kí tɔ̄ nnyimin.» 2Ní m cūtìi dá dambala kii ti-Dindaan nín bí yii ḿ ŋá puee, ki dūu gbìn̄ m-caŋ. 3Ti-Dindaan nìn gíti sòon̄ nì mi nliliitiim yii: 4«Yòon̄ dambala un ní a dá ki gbìn̄ a-caŋee kí nīn cá Eefiraati mɔɔl caŋin kí dū-u kí báĺ ntaŋkpaween ŋubɔn.» 5Ní m cáá dambalee ki bál̀ Eefiraati mɔɔl caŋin, kii ti-Dindaan nín nìn tīī-mi mara puee. 6Iwiin iba boonee ní ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: «Yīkì kí gítí dimɔɔlee caŋin kí yòon̄ní dambala un m nìn tīī-si mara yii á cáá báĺ niinee.» 7Niinee ní m nín cá Eefiraati mɔɔl caŋin. M bàn̄ee ní ki nyàab̄ dambalee ki lēeń-u laakin m nìn dū-u ki bál̀ee. Ama m nìn ká yii dambalee nìn bíil̀ kaa ti pée bí tiban.
8Niinee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii: 9«Man ni-Dindaan nín lī puee sɔ̀. Míǹ ní m làá bīil̀ Juuda yab lambil nì Jeerusaleem yab lambikpaandi. 10Di sá yii an sá dinibul din nib kaa ŋān̄ee ní. Bi yíì kaa pílifì m-nyɔkɔ, ki nóó bíǹ bi-ba nín là puee saŋŋu. Bi jòó ki pá awaa boon ki tòotī-ŋi. Too, dinibul nee ń kpántí kii dambala un bíil̀ kaa ti bí tiban nee.» 11Ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé: «Kii unil nín dù dambala kí gbìn̄ u-caŋ puee, míǹ ní m nìn dū Isirayeel yab nì Juuda yab ki bóob́ ki nákáǹ m-ba. M nín nìn là puee di sá bí nīn sá man nibul, kí nyā diyindi, kí nīn sá m-jilmau nì m-nyooti. Ama ní baa gbìl̄ ki tīiǹ-mi.»
Ndamam nì ti-Dindaan ŋuul
12«Á tùkù-bi yii: <Ti-Dindaan Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu nín lī puee sɔ̀. Tilɔn bí bí nīn fūuntí ndaam ní>. Bi yaa kíí-si yii: <Mimmee timbi kaa nyí tilɔn nín bí bí nīn fūuntí ndaameeee?> 13Niinee ní á tùkù-bi yii: <Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M làá yàntī kitiŋ nee pu nib nì bibɔtiibi bin kā Daafiidi beejal puee, nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì m-bɔnaatiliibi nì Jeerusaleem yab kɔkɔ ń gbí. 14Man ni-Dindaan di bí yii m làá dū-bi kí yāŋkì tɔb kí kɔ̄fì, bibaatiibi nì mbiyaamu dicilpu. Maa làá tàan̄ báà ubɔ. Maa làá dàkà kulaŋŋaŋfitiiuaaa, kaa làá sɔ̄ isaa mun. Tiba nì tiba kaa làá cúú-mi ḿ taa nàan̄-bi.>»
Ti-Dindaan bíi kpáafí u-nibul
15Pīlifìmaan, kpòom̄maan ni-tafal,
taa nín̄ sámaan bilambidambi.
Ti-Dindaan di bíi sòoǹ.
16Tīīmaan ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu tinyool
kí wàatī ní dibɔmbɔndi wiiŋŋu ń nín bàń,
án nín làá ŋá pu ní taa láa gbéetí
ajoon ŋin pu kunyeeu mɔ́ee.
Ni bàà kā ki cí ŋwalifi dee,
ama ní u dūu kpántì ŋkúm bɔmbɔndi,
ki dūu kpántì ditagbambɔndi.
17Ni yaa kaa pílifì tibɔkpaafikaal nee,
m làá nīn sūǹ dibalin ni-lambil pu.
Nnyinnyim làá gbí m-nimbiliŋ kí nīn bàtifī,
kun puee bi cúú ti-Dindaan picaŋkpuŋku
ki cūnnì kuyuŋu.
18Tùkù ubɔti nì u-na yii:
«Kàl̄maan kitiŋ,
di sá ni-beefuunyaaŋki nyáń ni-yil pu
ki lítì kitiŋ.
19Bi pīiǹ Neegeeb timmu punyɔmmu,
ubɔ kaa ti pìitī-mu.
Bi cúú Juuda yab ki cūnnì kuyuŋu,
bi-kɔkɔ búntì ubɔ kaa kíǹ.
Jeerusaleem tiŋki fá ki-nyooti
20Wáaǹ kí kpèè bin nyánní ŋgan pú ki dòońee.
Kupicaŋkpuŋu kun m nìn kpāaǹ-see bí la?
Apibil ŋin nìn tìì-si tinyoolee bí la?
21A yāntì biba kpántì a-bɔɔbi.
An nib gbanti yaa láa yíkì ki bíi jáà nì si
kí jī a-pu dinyandee,
a làá dāá lì yii ba dee?
A làá dāá jī falaa
kii unimpu di kāl̀ imatiŋween puee.
22Niinee, a làá dāá bàlifì yii:
<Ba di yì-tì ní nnaabu nee bāań-mi míǹ?>
Too, bi yaa láa kóoǹ a-wɔndoou,
ki bíi ŋáań-si tipɔmbɔtee,
an sá a-kpitii nín wīikée pu.
23«Unibɔn ŋūǹ kí kpántí u-wuŋgbaŋŋuɔɔɔ?
Ugbii ŋūǹ kí pítí u-tàmaaa?
Míǹ mbaantiim ní nimbi bin mántiǹ ikpiti diŋálee,
naa ŋūǹ kí ŋá tiŋan.
24M làá jà-ni kí yàl̄ an kɔkɔ pu
kii kuteeun buŋku nín yòontí timool puee ní.»
25Ti-Dindaan bí yii:
«Jeerusaleem, tin dɔ̄ ki cí-see dee.
Dijandi din m kpáafì ki yóoǹ-see dee.
Di sá yii a súntì man pu,
ní ki dū a-mákal ki páaǹ awaa pu.
26An puee ma mun làá kóoǹ a-wɔndoou
kí cáá sāā a-nimbiin pu,
ní bí wāl̀ a-cooi.
27Yéēee! A-laakpaati nì a-mɔŋŋu biilii
nì a-laakpaatuuŋŋi ŋin kɔ̄ntí-si icoo na!
M ká a-gbantammu pu nì a-satin
a-waaŋi ŋin sá ntimbiil wantee.
Ba naabuŋu ŋúǹ bulifi dee, Jeerusaleem,
aa là kí ŋá a-ba circir.
Án làá nīn bí míǹ kí tin sāā ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu ní?»

english_text:
The Land Dries Up
1When there had been no rain for a long time, the Lord told me to say to the people:
2Judah and Jerusalem weep
as the land dries up.
3Rulers send their servants
to the storage pits for water.
But there's none to be found;
they return in despair
with their jars still empty.
4There has been no rain,
and farmers feel sick
as they watch cracks appear
in the dry ground.
5A deer gives birth in a field,
then abandons her newborn fawn
and leaves in search of grass.
6Wild donkeys go blind
from starvation.
So they stand on barren hilltops
and sniff the air,
hoping to smell green grass.
The Lord's People Pray
7We rejected you and did evil,
so we deserve to be punished.
But if you rescue us, Lord,
everyone will see
how great you are.
8You're our only hope;
you alone can save us now.
You help us one day,
but you're gone the next.
9Did this disaster
take you by surprise?
Are you a warrior
with your hands tied?
You have chosen us,
and your temple is here.
Don't abandon us!
The Lord's Answer
10My people,
you love to wander away;
you don't even try
to stay close to me.
So now I will reject you
and punish you for your sins.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
Lying Prophets
11The Lord said, “Jeremiah, don't ask me to help these people. 12They may even go without eating and offer sacrifices to please me and to give thanks. But when they cry out for my help, I won't listen, and I won't accept their sacrifices. Instead, I'll send war, starvation, and disease to wipe them out.”
13I replied, “The other prophets keep telling everyone that you won't send starvation or war, and that you're going to give us peace.”
14The Lord answered:
They claim to speak for me, but they're lying! I didn't even speak to them, much less choose them to be my prophets. Their messages come from worthless dreams, useless fortunetelling, and their own imaginations.
15Those lying prophets say there will be peace and plenty of food. But I say that those same prophets will die from war and hunger. 16And everyone who listens to them will be killed, just as they deserve. Their dead bodies will be thrown out into the streets of Jerusalem, because their families will also be dead, and no one will be left to bury them.
17Jeremiah, go and tell the people how you feel about all this.
So I told them:
“Tears will flood my eyes
both day and night,
because my nation suffers
from a deadly wound.
18In the fields I see the bodies
of those killed in battle.
And in the towns I see crowds
dying of hunger.
But the prophets and priests
go about their business,
without understanding
what has happened.”
Jeremiah Prays to the Lord
19Have you rejected Judah, Lord?
Do you hate Jerusalem?
Why did you strike down Judah
with a fatal wound?
We had hoped for peace
and a time of healing,
but all we got was terror.
20We and our ancestors are guilty
of rebelling against you.
21If you save us, it will show
how great you are.
Don't let our enemies
disgrace your temple,
your beautiful throne.
Don't forget that you promised
to rescue us.
22Idols can't send rain,
and showers don't fall
by themselves.
Only you control the rain,
so we put our trust in you,
the Lord our God.
translation_text:
Ŋweel yuntiŋu
1Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Yeereemii ŋweel bɔti pu.
2«Juuda yab kā dikpool,
bi-timmu pɔŋŋu dóò.
Binib bí kunimbaaun ki kā kitiŋ.
Jeerusaleem yab kuŋkuuntii nín jɔ́ḿ yilpu.
3Akpambal tú bi-tɔntɔnliibi
bí cùú nyàabìń nnyim.
Bi bàn̄ dinyimbɔbilinee, nnyim fóotì.
Bi fātìi gítìń nì abɔkulim.
Bi-wunti yɔ̄tì kunimbaau kɔ́-bi
ní bi kíǹ ki tīī bi-yil.
4Utaa nín yúl̀ee puee, kitiŋ fáá iwèeń.
Niinee bikpaabi wunti yɔ̄tì,
bi-yil kíǹ ki tīī.
5Kipeewuŋ gba màl̄ tisatin
ki dū ki-biki ki fá,
kun puee timool kaa ti bí.
6Kumooun mammu tɔ́kɔ́ ajoon pu
ki tíkì kubuŋu kii sinsiŋkubee.
Mu nyàab̄ timool mu-nimbiliŋ tin kpáàa lóoĺ,
ama ní muaa ká báà tiba.»
Isirayeel nibul
7«Báà ti-kpitii yaa bíi kɔ́kɔĺ-ti,
ti-Dindaan, a-yindi puee, ŋá tiba kí tīī-ti.
Tiŋman ti nyáń a-boon, ti yīntiǹ-si.
8Ti-Dindaan,
sii un pu Isirayeel yab mákée,
a nìn fīī-bi dinimbinaamandi yuntiŋu poon.
Too, kɔŋkɔnnee,
a sá kii unicaanee ní kitiŋ nee poon,
a lì kii usaŋkinli nín dɔ́miń kí dòon̄
kunyabambaantiiu kutaa ń wúntí ú nìkēe ní.
9Ba pu ní a bí kii unil un wunti kpíìyee,
a lì kii ubaatandaan un kaa ti ŋūǹ kí fīī bin kíǹee?
Ama ní a bí ti-kansikin ti-Dindaan,
bi dū-ti ki sú-si ní,
taa dū-ti kí fá.»
*
10Kpèèmaan ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ dinibul nee pu tiŋyee: «Tiŋman, bi néeń ki sáń ki póotí an kɔkɔ kii bi nín là puee.» Ama tíǹ kaa fáatiǹ ti-Dindaan. Kɔŋkɔnnee u làá téetí bi-yìntitam nì bi-kpitii pu ní kí dáaĺ bi-tafal.
11Ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: «Á taa gbàam̀ dinibul nee yab pu, á taa mèè kí nyàab̀ bi-ŋanti. 12Báà bi yaa bóob́ kinyɔkɔ ki mēē-mi, maa làá pīlifiǹ-bi. Báà bi yaa cáań-mi bisaraawɔkaabi nì saraabi bin kíǹee, maa làá fōō. Ama m làá kpɔ̀-bi kujaaun ní kí yàntī ŋkùm nì bìlbil kúm ń kpɔ̀ kí céetí-bi.»
13Ní m kíí yii: «Too, ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti, bibɔnaatiliibi bí-bi yii: <Naa làá ká kujaauaaa, ŋkùm mun kaa làá jēetí ni-pu, ama Unimbɔti làá tīī-ni mbaamɔn gbansɔŋfiŋu mpaan nee pu.>»
14Niinee ní ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: «Tin bibɔnaatiliibi gbanti sòoǹ m-yindi puee sá nnyimɔn ní. Maa tú-bi, kaa tīī-bi mara ubɔ, kaa tí sòon̄ nì bi tiba. Bi-leedakaŋ sá tinyimɔmbɔti, ní tin bi sòoǹee kaa bí tiban. Bíǹ bi-ba di pée kāl̀ ki náań tinyimɔmbɔti gbanti kɔkɔ. 15An puee man ni-Dindaan nín cáá tin kí sòoǹ bibɔnaatiliibi gbanti pu puee sèé: <Maa tú-bi, ama ní bi sòoǹ m-yindi pu yii kujaau àá ŋkùm kaa làá jēetí kitiŋ nee pu. Too, kujaau nì ŋkùm di làá kpɔ̀ kí céetí bi-kɔkɔ. 16Ní kujaau nì ŋkùm ń kpɔ̀ binib bin bi nāatì tinyimɔmbɔti ki tīīyee kí bíĺ Jeerusaleem daŋŋi pu an kɔkɔ fìlfil. Ubɔ dāa kpá kí síb́ bi nì bi-nimpoobi nì bi-jipɔmbi nì bi-bisalib. M làá yàntī ikpiti in bi ŋée ń gítí bi-pu.
17«Á tùkù-bi tibɔti nee yii:
«Nnyinnyim ń nyā m-nimbiliŋ kí nīn bàtifī
kí taa gbèen̄ ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu!
Di sá yii asaluukpaan kɔ́ m-nibul.
Tiweendi tin di fōōyee kaa cáá dicáaǹdi.
18M yaa nyáń ki cá kusaauee,
m kāntí binib bin bi kūū kujaaunee dɔ̄ dɔ̄.
M yaa tí nín kóò kitiŋinaaa,
m tí kāntí bin ŋkùm kūū kūūyee.
Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi nì bisaraaŋaliibi
tú ki yìiǹ kitiŋee ni,
baa bíi gbìl̀ tin bíi jītée taapu.»
Isirayeel nibul
19«Ti-Dindaan, a lafun dū Juuda yab ki fá níii?
A núutiǹ Siiyɔn yab níii?
Ba pu ní a ŋáań-ti tiweendi tin
ubɔ kaa ŋūǹ kí cáaǹee ní?
Ti bàà kā ki cí ŋgbansɔŋfi,
ama ní tiwammɔntiil tiba kaa bíi dòoń.
Ti bàà kā ki cí kí ká dicáaǹdi,
ama ní dinyoondi bāań.
20Ti-Dindaan, ti nyí ti nín ŋá tin kaa ŋān̄ee.
Ti béè mun yii ti-naanjab yīntiǹ-si.
Tiŋman, ti baasii yīntiǹ-si ní.
21A-yindi puee,
taa kpèè kí sìŋkīǹ a-beejal din cáá tinyoolee,
taa fàtī a-boon kí tīī-dì.
Taa súntí mpèé ŋun a nìn ŋá nì tee pu,
taa kpìtī-ŋu.
22Atimbun ŋin kíǹee waaŋi kansikinee,
diba ŋūǹ kí yàntī utaa ń nàaa?
Kutagbɔŋu ku-ba di yàntī utaa nàaa?
An kaa sá sii ti-Dindaanaaa?
Ti-Dindaan, sii pu ní timbi máká,
di sá yii sii di ŋáań tíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ.»

english_text:
The People of Judah Will Die
1 The Lord said to me:
Even if Moses and Samuel were here, praying with you, I wouldn't change my mind. So send the people of Judah away. 2 And when they ask where they are going, tell them that I, the Lord, have said:
Some of you are going to die
of horrible diseases.
Others are going to die in war
or from starvation.
The rest will be led away
to a foreign country.
3I will punish you
in four different ways:
You will be killed in war
and your bodies dragged off
by dogs,
your flesh will be eaten by birds,
and your bones will be chewed on
by wild animals.
4 This punishment will happen
because of the horrible things
your King Manasseh did.
And you will be disgusting
to all nations on earth.
5People of Jerusalem,
who will feel sorry for you?
Will anyone bother
to ask if you are well?
6My people, you abandoned me
and walked away.
I am tired of showing mercy;
that's why I'll destroy you
7by scattering you like straw
blown by the wind.
I will punish you with sorrow
and death,
because you refuse
to change your ways.
8There will be more widows
in Judah
than grains of sand on a beach.
A surprise attack at noon!
And the mothers in Jerusalem
mourn for their children.
9A mother is in deep despair
and struggles for breath.
Her daylight has turned
to darkness—
she has suffered the loss
of her seven sons.
I will kill anyone who survives.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
Jeremiah Complains
10I wish I had never been born!
I'm always in trouble
with everyone in Judah.
I never lend or borrow money,
but everyone curses me
just the same.
11Then the Lord replied,
“I promise to protect you,
and when disaster comes,
even your enemies
will beg you for help.”
The Enemy Cannot Be Defeated
The Lord told me to say:
12People of Judah,
just as you can't break iron
mixed with bronze,
you can't defeat the enemies
that will attack
from the north.
13I will give them
everything you own,
because you have sinned
everywhere in your country.
14My anger is a fire
that cannot be put out,
so I will make you slaves
of your enemies
in a foreign land.
Jeremiah Complains Again
15You can see how I suffer
insult after insult,
all because of you, Lord.
Don't be so patient
with my enemies;
take revenge on them
before they kill me.
16When you spoke to me,
I was glad to obey,
because I belong to you,
the Lord All-Powerful.
17I don't go to parties
and have a good time.
Instead, I keep to myself,
because you have filled me
with your anger.
18I am badly injured
and in constant pain.
Are you going to disappoint me,
like a stream that goes dry
in the heat of summer?
The Lord Replies
19Then the Lord told me:
Stop talking like a fool!
If you turn back to me
and speak my message,
I will let you be my prophet
once again.
I hope the people of Judah
will accept what you say.
But you can ignore their threats,
* 20because I am making you strong,
like a bronze wall.
They are evil and violent,
but when they attack,
21I will be there to rescue you.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
1Ní ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: «Báà gba Mooyiisi nì Samiyeel yaa gbāam̀-mi dinibul nee yab pu, maa làá pée sɔ̄ bi-saai. Jà-bi kí nyāntí bí búntí kí wàatī-mi. 2Ní bi yaa bālifì-si yii: <La ní ti làá cù ní?> Á kíí-bi yii: <Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀.
«Bìlbil kúm ń kpɔ̀ un sá bìlbil kúm yɔuee!
Un máaǹ kí kpú kujaaunee ń kpú kujaaun!
Ŋkùm ń kpɔ̀ un sá ŋkùm yɔuee!
Ní un sá kuyuŋun yɔuee ń búntí kuyuŋu!»
3Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «M làá jáǹ-bi minaa pu ní: kitàataajiki làá kpɔ̀-bi, ní iboo ń fù-bi kí cùnnì ndan, ní kaajiikub ń jī-bi ní sinsiŋkub ń ŋmɔ́ kí tɔ̀ntī-bi. 4Mimmee, kitiŋ pu beeŋi kɔkɔ yaa ká-bee, bi làá kɔ́ dinyoondin. Kun pu m làá ŋá mimmee di sá Eeseekiyaasi jipɔɔn Manasee, Juuda yab bɔtiu nín ŋáaǹ atuŋkpiti ŋin kɔkɔ Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee.»
Ti-Dindaan gīī kí sɔ̄ isaa
5Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Jeerusaleem, ŋma di làá gíti sɔ̄ a-saai?
Ŋma di làá sɔ̄ a-pu?
Ŋma di làá dūú páb́ u-ba kí bàlifì kí kpèè tin poon a bée?»
6Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Sii di dū-mi ki fá,
ní ki fātì a-boon ki tīī-mi.
An pu ní ma mun jáń nì si
ki nāaǹ-si.
Di sá yii m gīī kí nīn sūǹ a-saai.
7Kitiŋee timmu kɔkɔ poonee,
m yōoǹ ndɔ ŋun m cáa gbáà tijimpinee
ki gbáń ki yāaǹ-bi.
M nāaǹ-bi ki yāntì baa ti cáá mbiyaamu,
ama ní baa kpántì bi-bimbim.
8M yāntì bikpiipoobi wíiǹ
ki jítiǹ tiŋku gbandi bul.
M cáań nnaabu ki tɔ́ unipɔɔn
un sá ujanjalee na pu kuwiŋkaŋu pu.
Dibɔbil pu niinee ní m yāntì
dinyooŋkpaandi jéetì u-pu.
9Unimpu un nìn cáá jipɔmbi bilulee kaa ti bí tiban.
U fìkī ki dɔ̄.
Úǹ wìiŋ́ŋu jéetì kuwiŋkaŋu pu.
Icoo cúú-u,
u fá u-jilmau.
Bin kíǹ ki bí dimaŋfalinee,
m làá yàntī bí kpú kujaaun
bi-nannanliibi nimbiin.»
Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.
Yeereemii bíi yáliŋkí, Unimbɔti dàkā-u u-tundi
Yeereemii
10M-na, mbusu kɔ́-mi a nín màl̄-mee pu!
Kitiŋ nee kɔkɔ poonee,
binib jáà nì mi
ní kaa là kí wāl̀-mi.
Ma mun kaa pīnnì ubɔ animbil,
kaa tí cūtì ubɔ mun cee ki pīnnì animbil.
Ama ní báà ŋma tòó-mi mbusu.
11Ama ti-Dindaan nìn bí-mi yii:
«M pūtì yii m làá fīī-si kí kɔ́ǹ-si nnaamin.
Nnaabu nì dinimbinaamandi yuntiŋuee,
m làá yàntī a-nannanliibi ń dāá gbàan̄ a-nimbiin.
12Ubɔ ŋūǹ kí kóoĺ tikútaaa,
tikúti tin nyánní ŋgan púee nì tasa kútaaa?»
ti-Dindaan
13«Juuda yab, m làá yàntī bí fūkul̀
ni-gaajawanti nì ni-gaajati,
ní an kaa cáá yii ubɔ làá téeǹ-ni.
Ikpiti in kɔkɔ ni ŋá ni-tiŋki kɔkɔnee paati dee.
14M làá yàntī ní kpántí ni-nannanliibi yumbui
kitiŋ kin a nyée poon.
Di sá yii m-ŋuul sēē ŋŋmi
ŋun di làá wà-see.»
Yeereemii
15Sii ti-Dindaan nyí tikɔkɔ!
Dàkafì m-pu kí téetí m-pu.
Tɔ̀ bin kā m-puee ipɔntoon.
Kimɔtii kin a cáá bi-puee puee,
á taa yàntī ḿ jī falaa.
Béé yii sii pu ní man bíi jīǹ takaasi.
16M yaa nìn ká a-nyɔɔbundee,
m dù-dì kí ŋmɔ́ ní kí náĺ.
Di nìn tìì-mi mmɔn nì dipɔɔpindi ní.
Di sá yii bi dū-mi ki sú sii
m-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan ní.
17Maa kāl̀ bibeeliliibi kansikin
ki kɔ̄ntì m-nimbiliŋ.
Ama a ŋá-mi mpɔn m kākatì m-baba,
di sá yii a yāntì m díkí a-ŋuul ki gbí.
18Ba pu ní m-falaau kaa cáá dikúntil ní?
Ba pu ní m-buuŋŋu kaa kúù
ki kpántì taagbunjaanjaan ní?
Ibaamɔn, a kpántì m-cee kii
mbun ŋun kíiĺ binib,
baa ŋūǹ kí nīn máká ŋu-pu yii
ŋu cáá nnyimaaa, ŋuaa cááyee ní.
19Too, ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀.
«A yaa fātìi gítìń m-cee,
m làá fàtīí fōō-si á nīn bí m-tundin
ní á dāá yūĺ m-nimbiin.
A yaa ŋūǹ kí lì tibɔti tin cáá kudapɔɔuee
kí yàntī tibɔfanee,
m làá fàtīí dū-si kí kpántí kii m-nyɔkɔee.
An sá Juuda yab nín fàtīí gítiń a-cee,
an kaa sá sii di làá fàtīí gítí bi-cee.
20Binib nee nimbiinee, m làá dū-si kí kpántí
kii tasa kúti gundi din yú ki pɔ̄ɔ̄ kaa cìŋkēe ní.
Bi làá jáǹ-si, ama baa làá ŋmā kí ŋá-si tiba,
di sá yii m làá nīn bí a-cee kí fīī-si,
ní kí gbìntī-si kí líí.
Man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ.
21M làá fīī-si kí nyāntí bitɔŋfitiibi ŋaan,
m làá fōō-si bin dàkà tipɔmbɔtee ŋaan kí líí.»

english_text:
Jeremiah Must Live His Message
1The Lord said to me:
2Jeremiah, don't get married and have children—Judah is no place to raise a family. 3I'll tell you what's going to happen to children and their parents here. 4They will die of horrible diseases and of war and starvation. No one will give them a funeral or bury them, and their bodies will be food for the birds and wild animals. And what's left will lie on the ground like manure.
5When someone dies, don't visit the family or show any sorrow. I will no longer love or bless or have any pity on the people of Judah. 6Rich and poor alike will die and be left unburied. No one will mourn and show their sorrow by cutting themselves or shaving their heads. 7No one will bring food and wine to help comfort those who are mourning the death of their father or mother.
8Don't even set foot in a house where there is eating and drinking and celebrating. 9 Warn the people of Judah that I, the Lord All-Powerful, will put an end to all their parties and wedding celebrations. 10They will ask, “Why has the Lord our God threatened us with so many disasters? Have we done something wrong or sinned against him?”
11Then tell them I have said:
People of Judah, your ancestors turned away from me; they rejected my laws and teachings and started worshiping other gods. 12And you have done even worse! You are stubborn, and instead of obeying me, you do whatever evil comes to your mind. 13So I will throw you into a land that you and your ancestors know nothing about, a place where you will have to worship other gods both day and night. And I won't feel the least bit sorry for you.
14A time will come when you will again worship me. But you will no longer call me the Living Lord who rescued Israel from Egypt. 15Instead, you will call me the Living Lord who rescued you from that country in the north and from the other countries where I had forced you to go.
Someday I will bring you back to this land that I gave your ancestors. 16But for now, I am sending enemies who will catch you like fish and hunt you down like wild animals in the hills and the caves.
17I can see everything you are doing, even if you try to hide your sins from me. 18I will punish you double for your sins, because you have polluted my own land. You have filled it with lifeless idols that remind me of dead bodies.
The Lord Gives Strength
I prayed to the Lord:
19Our Lord, you are the one
who gives me strength
and protects me like a fortress
when I am in trouble.
People will come to you
from distant nations and say,
“Our ancestors worshiped
false and useless gods,
20worthless idols
made by human hands.”
21Then the Lord replied,
“That's why I will teach them
about my power,
and they will know that I
truly am the Lord.”
translation_text:
Yeereemii bí u-baba
1Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi tibɔti nee yii: 2«Á taa cáá unimpu, kí taa màal̀ mbininjabiyaamu nì nnimpubiyaamu kitiŋ nee poon. 3Di sá yii man ni-Dindaan nín sòon̄ mbininjabiyaamu nì nnimpubiyaamu mun bi làá màal̀ kitiŋ nee poonee, nì bibinaatiibi nì bibaatiibi bin làá màal̀-muee puee sɔ̀. 4Tigbaŋweeŋkpiil di làá kpɔ̀-bi. Ubɔ kaa làá sɔ̄ bi-kpool, ní ubɔ mun kaa dāa bí kí síb́-bi. Bi làá dāá dòon̄ kitiŋ kí sūū ní kí dāá kpántí ntiŋkpam. Kujaaun ní bi làá kpú àá ŋkùm di làá kpɔ̀-bi. Kaajiikub nì sinsiŋkub di làá ŋmɔ́ bi-nanti.»
5Ti-Dindaan gíti bí-mi yii: «Á taa kɔ́ dicindi din poon ní binib kpáfì ki kā dikpoolee, kí taa cù dikpool. Á taa ŋá ubɔ fɔ̀ɔ́, di sá yii m cúú m-saasɔl nì m-ŋanti nì m-poommɔŋŋu ki fōō dinibul nee cee. Man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ. 6Kitiŋ nee poonee, binikpaambi nì ŋwaamu làá kpú. Ubɔ kaa làá síb́-bi. Ubɔ kaa làá cāfì u-wunti kí dàkà kunimbaau ní kaa nín kōol̀ diyibaakpandi. 7Ubɔ kaa làá mɔ̄ǹ bukpɔsaa kí cùnnì dikpool kí ŋméeǹ-bi. Ubɔ mun kaa làá dā un baa kpíì àá u-na kpíìyee ndaam.
8«Taa kɔ́ kudicaŋu kun poon bi bíi jīǹ jiŋaalee. Taa kàl̄ si nì bi ń jī kí nyɔ̀. 9Di sá yii man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Ni-maŋfal wiiŋyi poon nì ni-nimbilaaliyin ní m làá kúntí kitiŋ nee pu ni-jiŋaalib gbiiliŋ nì ni-pɔɔpindi faalii nì animpucaŋgbiil.>
10«A yaa láa dū tibɔti nee ki tùkū dinibul nee yab ní bi yaa láa bālifì-si yii: <Ba pu ní ti-Dindaan cáań nnaabu nee ki tɔ́ ti-pu? Ba ní ti ŋá ki yīntì ní? Ba kpitii ní ti baasii ŋá ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu ní?> 11Á dāá kíí-bi yii: <Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Kun pu m ŋá mimmee di sá yii ni-naanjab nìn dū-mi ki fá ki cūtìi nóó awaa ki tōotì-ŋi ní ki gbāaǹ ŋi-taapu. Mamee, bi dū-mi ki fá ní kaa ŋúb́ m-marab. 12Nimbee, ni-kpitii gíti nyāŋkì nì ni-naanjab yai. Báà ŋma nóó u-landɔkɔkpitii kaa pílifiǹ-mi. 13M làá jà-ni kí nyāntí kitiŋ nee poon kí cùnnì kitiŋ kin poon ni nì ni-naanjab kaa nyí ki kée. Niinee, ni làá ŋmā kí nīn tòotī awaa ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu. Di sá yii maa ti làá dàkà-ni m-laŋŋaŋfitiiku.>»
Ti-Dindaan fātìi gíiǹní bin u nìn jìn̄ee bi-tiŋki pu
14An pu ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ yii: «Ŋwiin bí ki dòoń baa làá dāá gíti lì yii: <M pūtì ti-Dindaan un bí dimaŋfalin ki nyántìń Isirayeel yab kuyuŋun Eejipiti tiŋkinee!>, 15ama bi làá dāá lì yii: <nì ti-Dindaan un bí dimaŋfalin, ki nyántìń Isirayeel yab kitiŋ kin bí ŋgan púee nì ntimu mun kɔkɔ poon u nìn jìn̄-bi ki kɔ́ǹee.> Tiŋman m làá fàtīí gíiǹní-bi kitiŋ kin m nìn dūu tīī bi-naanjabee poon.»
Unimbɔti làá fàtīí fōō bin jíń dibɔkpilee
16Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «M làá tɔ̄ bijɔncuuliibi tikpil bí cùú cúuń-bi. Míǹ boonee ní ḿ tɔ̄ bikpambi kupaau bí cù ajoon kɔkɔ pu nì ŋgbantamu kɔkɔ pu nì itakpalɔkɔn kí kpāŋkì-bi. 17Di sá yii m wāĺ tin kɔkɔ bi ŋáańee. Bi-tuuŋŋi báà dibaba kaa bál̀-mi, ní tiba kaa lìkī bi-kpitii m-nimbiin. 18M làá yàntī bí pà bi-kpitii paati mili pu nì bi-yìntitam. Di sá yii bi dū bi-waaŋi ŋin sá ntimbiil wanti kaa cáá dimaŋfalee ki kɔ́ǹ m-tiŋki tijɔkɔndi. Bi dū bi-waaŋi ŋin m-nimbil kaa là kí wāl̀ee ki gbéeǹ m-tiŋki kin sá m-gaajawantee.»
Báà ŋma béè Unimbɔti un sá tiŋman pu yɔuee
19M-Dindaan, sii di sá man pɔŋŋu nì m-balilaŋki,
dinimbinaamandi yuntiŋuee,
sii ní m sáń ki kóò.
Atimbun làá nyānní kitiŋ gbeennyɔkɔ kí dāan̄.
Bi làá dāá lì yii:
«Difakal din ti-naanjab fōōyee di sá tinyimɔmbɔti,
tiwan tin kaa bí tiban kaa kèetēe.
20Unil ŋūǹ kí mɔ́ɔ́ inimbɔtaaa?
Tin bi māāyee kaa sá inimbɔti.»
21«Too, min bí nee m làá dàkà-bi
m-kpabil nì m-pɔŋŋu.
Niinee bi làá béé yii man di sá bi-Dindaan.»

english_text:
The Lord Will Punish Judah
The Lord said:
1People of Judah,
your sins cannot be erased.
They are written on your hearts
like words chiseled in stone
or carved on the corners
of your altars.
* 2One generation after another
has set up pagan altars
and worshiped the goddess Asherah
everywhere in your country—
on hills and mountains,
and under large trees.
3So I'll take everything you own,
including your altars,
and give it all
to your enemies.
4You will lose the land
that I gave you,
and I will make you slaves
in a foreign country,
because you have made my anger
blaze up like a fire
that won't stop burning.
Trust the Lord
5I, the Lord, have put a curse
on those who turn from me
and trust in human strength.
6They will dry up like a bush
in salty desert soil,
where nothing can grow.
7But I will bless those
who trust me, the Lord.
8 They will be like trees
growing beside a stream—
trees with roots that reach
down to the water,
and with leaves
that are always green.
They bear fruit every year
and are never worried
by a lack of rain.
9You people of Judah
are so deceitful
that you even fool yourselves,
and you can't change.
10 But I know your deeds
and your thoughts,
and I will make sure
you get what you deserve.
11You cheated others,
but everything you gained
will fly away, like birds
hatched from stolen eggs.
Then you will discover
what fools you are.
Jeremiah Prays to the Lord
12Our Lord, your temple
is a glorious throne
that has stood on a mountain
from the beginning.
13You are a spring of water
giving Israel life and hope.
But if the people reject
what you have told me,
they will be swept away
like words written in dust.
14You, Lord, are the one I praise.
So heal me and rescue me!
Then I will be completely well
and perfectly safe.
15The people of Judah say to me,
“Jeremiah, you claimed to tell us
what the Lord has said.
So why hasn't it come true?”
16Our Lord, you chose me
to care for your people,
and that's what I have done.
You know everything I have said,
and I have never once
asked you to punish them.
17I trust you for protection
in times of trouble,
so don't frighten me.
18Keep me from failure
and disgrace,
but make my enemies fail
and be disgraced.
Send destruction to make
their worst fears come true.
Resting on the Sabbath
19-20The Lord said:
Jeremiah, stand at each city gate in Jerusalem, including the one the king uses, and speak to him and everyone else. Tell them I have said:
I am the Lord, so pay attention. 21-24 If you value your lives, don't do any work on the Sabbath. Don't carry anything through the city gates or through the door of your house, or anywhere else. Keep the Sabbath day sacred!
I gave this command to your ancestors, but they were stubborn and refused to obey or to be corrected. But if you obey, 25then Judah and Jerusalem will always be ruled by kings from David's family. The king and his officials will ride through these gates on horses or in chariots, and the people of Judah and Jerusalem will be with them. There will always be people living in Jerusalem, 26and others will come here from the nearby villages, from the towns of Judah and Benjamin, from the hill country and the foothills to the west, and from the Southern Desert. They will bring sacrifices to please me and to give me thanks, as well as offerings of grain and incense.
27But if you keep on carrying things through the city gates on the Sabbath and keep treating it as any other day, I will set fire to these gates and burn down the whole city, including the fortresses.
translation_text:
Ti-Dindaan bīitì Juuda yab kpitii pu
1«Juuda yab kpitiiyee,
bi dū kigaai ní ki cáká ki ŋmàn̄,
àá ataŋkpanyaan ní bi dūu ŋmàn̄-i.
Bi ŋmàn̄-i ki ŋá bi-pɔbiliŋin,
ní ki ŋmàn̄-i ki nákáǹ nsaraafan kpiŋŋi pu.
2Kii bi nín dàkafī bi-jipɔmbi pu puee,
míǹ ní bi dàkafī bi-saraafaŋyi nì bi-windɔi
nì isufi in cáá tifaasɔn ki bí ŋgbantamu puee pu.
3Nimbi Juuda yab,
nimbi bin tòotī awaa
ajoon pu nì tisatinee,
m làá dū ni-gaajati nì ni-gaajawanti
nì ni-waatootipaaŋyi kí tīī bí fūkul̀.
Ikpiti in ni ŋá ni-tiŋki kɔkɔ poonee pu
ní m làá ŋá míǹ.
4Ni làá yīkì kí dū kitiŋ kin m nìn tīī-ni
ní nīn kíǹ ki yèe kí fá.
M làá yàntī ní kpántí ni-nannanliibi yumbui
kitiŋ kin naa nyée poon.
Di sá yii ni tūū m-ŋuul ŋmiŋu,
ní ŋu làá nīn pée wù míǹ ní ki cá jaanjaan.
Ibaamɔn wundi nì inyimɔn wundi
5Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé:
«An sá mbusu ní ki tīī unil un máká nisaal pu,
ki nyàab̀ dijòońdi nisaaleen cee,
ní ki fàtī u-boon ki tìì ti-Dindaanee.»
6U bí kii kisubiki kin cɔ́ kitiŋkuliŋŋi puee ní,
kì pée kpá kí ká mmɔn.
Kì làá nīn cɔ́ kuteeu taŋkpeeŋi kansikin,
kitiŋ kin cáá ŋyaam ubɔ kaa kóò ki-puee ní.
7Ama unil un di máká man pu
ki fōō-mi ki kíí nì u-pɔbil kɔkɔee,
man u-Dindaan làá bìin̄ u-pu.
8Udaan bí kii busubu bun yú mbun caŋin,
bu-nyaaŋyi lālim̀ ki kɔ́ mbunee ní.
Kutuntuŋu yuntiŋuee,
buaa fàŋkí tiba,
ní bu-faati pée sɔ̀m̀ ŋma.
Báà ŋweel yaa yúl̀ dibimmɔndi,
bu pée lòoǹ abil ní kaa gbèentí.
9Unil pɔbil ŋmàtíǹ ki jítiǹ tikɔkɔ!
Ubɔ kaa ŋūǹ kí cáaǹ-dì.
Ubɔ mun kaa ŋūǹ kí béé-dì.
10«Man ni-Dindaanee,
m wāĺ tin kā unil pɔbil poon poon kábuee,
ní ki nyí u-landɔkɔi kɔkɔ nín sá puee.
An pu ní m ŋūǹ kí pà báà ŋma bimbim
nì u-tuuŋŋi paati.
11Kii ujikpal nín nākantí ajin ŋin waa tɔ́ee puee,
míǹ ní unil un dī isaŋkpiti pu ki ká tigaajatee bí.
U-maŋfal wiiŋyi kansikin nì kansikinee
ní u-gaajati ń wāŋkì,
ní ú dūú kpántí kii kinaatuuyee.»
Ti-Dindaan baba di sá dimaŋfal nyeel
12Tinyool beejal din tɔ́kɔ́ yilpu doooo ŋkilkaaminee,
míǹ ní ti-circir kɔŋkooŋŋu bí.
13Ti-Dindaan, sii un pu Isirayeel mákée,
icoo ń cúú bin kɔkɔ dū-si ki fée!
Bin kɔkɔ fātì bi-boon ki tīī-see,
bí nīn bí kii ayin ŋin bi ŋmàn̄ ntaminee.
Di sá yii bi dū sii ti-Dindaan
un sá dimaŋfal nyimbuliŋuee ki fá.
Yeereemii bíi mèé ti-Dindaan
14M-Dindaan, cáaǹ-mi ní ḿ ká dicáaǹdi,
fīī-mi ní ḿ ká difiil.
Di sá yii sii di sá m-nyɔŋkii.
15Bi lì-mi yii:
«Ti-Dindaan bɔti tin u sòon̄ee bí la?
Tibɔti gbanti ń ŋá míǹ tí kpèèyaa!»
16Ti-Dindaan, man di kaa páb́-si á cáań nnaabu.
Maa tí mēē kí ká nnaabu wiiŋŋu,
sii a-ba nyí míǹ.
Tin m sòon̄ee, a-nimbiin ní m sòon̄-tì.
17Taa kpántí dinyoondi kí tīī-mi,
sii ní m sáń ki kóò dinimbinaamandi yuntiŋu.
18Icoo ń cúú bin sàantí-mee
kí taa cúú man.
Tifaandi ń cúú-bi, ama kí taa cúú man.
Cáań nnaabu kí tɔ̄ bi-pu,
kí nàan̄-bi dúsi dusi.
Ti-Dindaan wiŋŋuŋfikaaŋu bɔti
19Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ nì mi puee sèé: «Cùú yūĺ kipunyɔɔkpaaŋŋi caŋin. Niin ní Juuda yab bɔtiibi dì ki kóò ki dì ki nyēē Jeerusaleem tiŋkin. Míǹ boonee, á cùú yūĺ kitiŋee punyɔmmu kɔkɔ caŋin. 20Á tùkù Juuda yab bɔtiibi nì Juuda yab kɔkɔ nì Jeerusaleem yab bin kɔkɔ dì mpunyɔmu gbantee yii: <Pīlifìmaan ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi. 21U nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Ní nīn nyíǹ ni-ba tiŋan kí taa túń diwaŋgul ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dal kí dī Jeerusaleem punyɔmmu nee kí kɔ́ àá kí nyā. 22Ní taa nyāntiń ni-diiŋŋin diwaŋgul ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dal, kí taa tɔ̄ ditundi báà diba yaadal. Ama ní dū ŋwiin gbanti kí sú-mi kii m nín nìn yóoǹ ni-naanjab mara puee. 23Baa nìn kpōoǹ bi-tafal ní kaa nín pílifì. Bi nìn ŋá ŋyipɔn kí taa pīlifì ní kaa nín fōō isaŋki.
24«<Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Nimbee, ní pīlifiǹ-mi. Ní taa túń diwaŋgul ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dal kí dī kitiŋ nee punyɔmmu kí kɔ́. Ní dū ŋwiin gbanti kí sú-mi kí taa tɔ̄ ditundi diba ŋwiin gbanti. 25Niinee, bibɔtiibi nì abɔtibil bin kā Daafiidi beejal puee làá nīn kàal̀ itaamu nì tɔrɔkub pu kí nīn pée dì kitiŋ nee punyɔmmu pu ki kóò ki nyēē. Bi-kàliŋkpilib nì Juuda yab nì Jeerusaleem yab làá nīn dì niin, ní binib ń nīn pée kóò kitiŋ nee ni kí nīn cá jaanjaan. 26Binib làá nyānní Juuda timmun nì Jeerusaleem kpaanceetii nì Beenjameen tiŋkin nì Seefeelaa tiŋkin nì ajoon pu timmun nì Neegeeb. Bi làá dāá ŋá bisaraawɔkaabi nì saraabi biba mun nì tijimpin saraabi nì talaalutuukaa nì ijaam saraabi ti-Dindaan diikun. 27Ama ni yaa kaa pílifiǹ-mi kaa dū ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa ki sú-mi, ki túǹ diwaŋgul ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dal ki dī Jeerusaleem punyɔmmu pu ki kɔ́ee, m làá tūū ki-punyɔmmu ŋŋmi. Ŋu làá wà Jeerusaleem beeciŋŋi, ní kaa làá kpú.>»

english_text:
Jeremiah Goes to the Pottery Shop
1The Lord told me, 2“Jeremiah, go to the pottery shop, and when you get there, I will tell you what to say to the people.”
3I went there and saw the potter making clay pots on his pottery wheel. 4And whenever the clay would not take the shape he wanted, he would change his mind and form it into some other shape.
5Then the Lord told me to say:
6People of Israel, I, the Lord, have power over you, just as a potter has power over clay. 7If I threaten to uproot and shatter an evil nation, 8and that nation turns from its evil, I will change my mind.
9If I promise to make a nation strong, 10but its people start disobeying me and doing evil, then I will change my mind and not help them at all.
11So listen to me, people of Judah and Jerusalem! I have decided to strike you with disaster, and I won't change my mind unless you stop sinning and start living right.
12But I know you won't listen. You might as well answer, “We don't care what you say. We have made plans to sin, and we are going to be stubborn and do as we please!”
13So I, the Lord, command you to ask the nations, and find out if they have ever heard of such a horrible sin as what you have done.
14The snow
on Lebanon's mountains
never melts away,
and the streams there
never run dry.
15But you, my people,
have turned from me
to burn incense
to worthless idols.
You have left the ancient road
to follow an unknown path
where you stumble over idols.
16Your land will be ruined,
and every passerby
will look at it with horror
and make insulting remarks.
17When your enemies attack,
I will scatter you like dust
blown by an eastern wind.
Then, on that day of disaster,
I will turn my back on you.
The Plot against Jeremiah
18Some of the people said, “Let's get rid of Jeremiah! We will always have priests to teach us God's laws, as well as wise people to give us advice, and prophets to speak the Lord's messages. So, instead of listening to Jeremiah any longer, let's accuse him of a crime.”
Jeremiah Prays about His Enemies
19Please, Lord, answer my prayer.
Make my enemies stop
accusing me of evil.
20I tried to help them,
but they are paying me back
by digging a pit to trap me.
I even begged you
not to punish them.
21But now I am asking you
to let their children starve
or be killed in war.
Let women lose
their husbands and sons
to disease and violence.
22These people have dug pits
and set traps for me, Lord.
Make them scream in fear
when you send enemy troops
to attack their homes.
23You know they plan to kill me.
So get angry and punish them!
Don't ever forgive
their terrible crimes.
translation_text:
Kuyɔkɔu nì uyɔɔmaati bɔti
1Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Yeereemii tibɔti nee yii: 2«Yīkìí sìntī uyɔɔmaati cee. Niin ní m làá sòoǹ nì si tin m cááyee.»
3Niinee ní m nín sìntī uyɔɔmaati cee. M bàn̄ee u bíi māā dibool kupiliŋu kun pu bi māā abookuŋkunee. 4Ama dibool din u nìn bíi māāyee kaa nìn kāl̀ kii iyunti iba án nín pée bàń uyɔɔmaati puee. Niinee ní u fātìi máń dibool diba din fáatiǹ-uee. 5Niinee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi tibɔti nee yii: 6«Mimmee Isirayeel yab, maa ŋūǹ kí ŋá-ni kii uyɔɔmaati nee nín ŋá pueeee? Man ni-Dindaan di sòon̄ míǹ. Kii kuyɔkɔu nín kā uyɔɔmaati ŋaan puee, míǹ ní nimbi Isirayeel yab mun kā m-ŋaan. 7Iyunti ibee m sòoǹ yii m làá cóotí ditimbundi àá dibeel diba kí lábití-dì kí cìb̄ ní kí nàan̄-dì. 8Ama ditimbundi gbanti yaa fá di-tuŋkpitiŋee, ma mun kpántí m-landɔkɔŋu ní kí taa ti ŋá-dì tin m bàà bɔ́ntì kí ŋá-dèe. 9Iyunti ibee m tí sòoǹ ditimbundi àá dibeel diba pu yii bí fàtīí náań-dì kí mā-dì. 10Ama ditimbundi gbanti yab yaa kaa pílifì m-nyɔkɔ ní ki bíi ŋáań min maa lèe, m kpántí m-landɔkɔŋu ní kí taa ti ŋá-bi tiŋan tin m bàà bɔ́ntì kí ŋá-bee.
11«Kɔŋkɔnnee, Yeereemii, á tùkù Juuda nì Jeerusaleem yab yii: <Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M bíi bɔ́ntí nnaabu kí tɔ̄ ni-pu, m bíi dàkafī min m làá ŋá-nee. An puee báà ŋma ń fá u-saŋkiŋkpitil. Ní ŋāŋkì ni-bítam nì ni-ŋáaǹtam.>»
12Ama bi làá lì-si yii: «Tin a sòoǹ nee sá fám ní! Ti nín pée lēē kí ŋá puee, míǹ ní ti làá ŋá, ti làá nóó ti-landɔkɔkpitii ní.»
Isirayeel yab súntì bi-Dindaan pu
13An pu ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ yii:
«Ní bàlifìmaan atimbun ŋin kíǹee yab.
Ni pée gbìl̄ tibɔti nee juti ki káaa?>
Isirayeel un bí kii usapɔɔn un kaa nyí uninjee
túń ntimbiil tuuŋŋi tikpil.
14Ntaayim kaa bìintí Leebanɔn jooŋŋi taŋkpeeŋi puɔɔɔ?
Ibun in nyim sìntī ajoon pu ki sɔ̀m̀ee
ŋūǹ kí gbèen̄ kí taa ti pùub̀aaa? Aayee!
15Ama man nibul súntì m-pu!
Bi tòotī awaa ŋin kaa bí tibanee.
Awaa gbanti di líikí-bi bi-saŋŋu poon.
Ŋi yàntī bi féeń dooooyee saŋyi
kí cùú nóó nsan ŋun baa cátèe.
16M-nibul yāntì di-tiŋki kpántì ataŋkpakpuku,
ki yàntī binib gbáà inimɔɔn biilii kaa gbèentí.
An ŋáań bisanjitiliibi bitii,
ní bi gbēentí bi-yiliŋ.
17Binannanliibi yaa láa bāańee,
m làá gbá kí yàaǹ m-nibul
kii ŋwìiń nyalaŋki buŋku nín kpàá ntam ki féeń puee ní.
Bi-nimbinaamandi dalee,
án nín bàà sá ḿ fàtī m-nimbiin kí tīī-bee,
m-boon ní m làá fàtī kí tīī-bi.»
Binib bíi bɔ́ntí kí kpɔ̀ Yeereemii
18Binib biba bí yii: «Tí cùmaan kí bɔ́ntí kí jáǹ Yeereemii! An kaa sá ti lóò bisaraaŋaliibi bin làá dàkà-ti marabee àá biciŋfitiibi bin làá tīī-ti isaŋkee. Taa tí lóò bibɔnaatiliibi bin làá nàatī-ti Unimbɔti bɔtee. Tí cùmaan kí jáǹ-u kí sòoǹ kí bīil̀-u. Ti taa pīlifì tin u sòoǹee.»
19Ama sii m-Dindaan, gíiǹní a-landɔkɔŋu m-cee,
pīlifì tibɔti tin bin bíi kɔ́kɔĺ-mee sòoǹee.
20Bi dù tikpitil kí pà tiŋan puɔɔɔ?
Bi gbìn̄ mbòó ḿ jēetí poon.
Ti-Dindaan, téetí yii m yúl̀ a-nimbiin
ki gbāam̀-si binib nee pu
yii á páatí a-ŋuul bi-pu.
21Míǹ puee yàntī ŋkùm ń kpɔ̀ bi-biyaamu,
bí dū ntàataajimu kí kpɔ̀-mu!
Bi-nimpoobi ń kpántí biŋmaŋŋmantiibi nì bikpiipoobi!
Bìlbil kúm ń kpɔ̀ bi-calib!
Bi-naacimpɔmbi ń kpúń kujaaun.
22A yaa láa dū binannanliibi ki tɔ́ bi-puee,
bí dāá gbìl̄ ibiil pu bi-dumpui!
Di sá yii bi gbìn̄ mbòó ḿ jēetí poon,
ki píĺ-mi titalindi kí sàl̄-mi.
23Ama sii ti-Dindaanee,
a nyí tin kɔkɔ bi bíi búkù m-pu
ki là kí kpɔ̀-mee.
Á taa dū bi-kpitii kí pɔ̄-bi!
Taa kpìtī bi-yìntitam a-nimbiin!
Bí lítí a-nimbiin.
A-ŋuul wiiŋŋu dalee,
á dāá jáǹ-bi.

english_text:
Jeremiah and the Clay Jar
1The Lord said:
Jeremiah, go to the pottery shop and buy a clay jar. Then take along some of the city officials and leading priests 2 and go to Hinnom Valley, just outside Potsherd Gate. Tell the people that I have said:
3I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, and you kings of Judah and you people of Jerusalem had better pay attention. I am going to bring so much trouble on this valley that everyone who hears about it will be shocked. 4-5 The people of Judah stopped worshiping me and made this valley into a place of worship for Baal and other gods that have never helped them or their ancestors or their kings. And they have committed murder here, burning their young, innocent children as sacrifices to Baal. I have never even thought of telling you to do that. 6So watch out! Someday this place will no longer be called Topheth or Hinnom Valley. It will be called Slaughter Valley!
7You people of Judah and Jerusalem may have big plans, but here in this valley I'll ruin those plans. I'll let your enemies kill you, and I'll tell the birds and wild animals to eat your dead bodies. 8I will turn Jerusalem into a pile of rubble, and every passerby will be shocked and horrified and will make insulting remarks. 9And while your enemies are trying to break through your city walls to kill you, the food supply will run out. You will become so hungry that you will eat the flesh of your friends and even of your own children.
10Jeremiah, as soon as you have said this, smash the jar while the people are watching. 11Then tell them that I have also said:
I am the Lord All-Powerful, and I warn you that I will shatter Judah and Jerusalem just like this jar that is broken beyond repair. You will bury your dead here in Topheth, but so many of you will die that there won't be enough room.
12-13I will make Jerusalem as unclean as Topheth, by filling the city with your dead bodies. I will do this because you and your kings have gone up to the roofs of your houses and burned incense to the stars in the sky, as though they were gods. And you have given sacrifices of wine to foreign gods.
Jeremiah Speaks in the Temple Courtyard
14I went to Topheth, where I told the people what the Lord had said. Then I went to the temple courtyard and shouted to the people, 15“Listen, everyone! Some time ago, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, warned you that he would bring disaster on Jerusalem and all nearby villages. But you were stubborn and refused to listen. Now the Lord is going to bring the disaster he promised.”
translation_text:
Kulɔŋŋu kun bi wīīyee
1Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «Cù uyɔɔmaati cee kí dā kulɔŋŋu. A yaa cée, á kpáaǹ bitindaŋkpilib biba nì bisaraaŋaliibi kpilib. 2Á dī abɔkati punyɔkɔki kí cù Inɔɔm tantakalin. Niin ní á bāakì tibɔti tin m làá sòon̄ nì si nee. 3Á dāá lì yii: <Juuda yab bɔtiibi nì Jeerusaleem yab, pīlifìmaan ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee. Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M làá cáań nnaabukpaan ŋubɔ kí tɔ̄ mpaan nee pu. Bin yaa láa gbìl̄-tèe làá fàŋkì. 4Di sá yii Juuda yab dū-mi ki fá. Bi-puee, baa ti béetí mpaan nee. Bi tūutì niin talaalutuukaabi ki tīī awaa. Bíǹ bi-baaa, bi-naanjabaaa, Juuda yab bɔtiibi kaa nìn nyí-ŋi. Bi yāntì maanyiibab fatikuu gbí mpaan nee pu. 5Bi ŋātì iwaatootipaan kí nīn tòotī diwaal Baal. Niin ní bi cáǹ bi-jipɔmbi ki tòotī diwaal Baal ki wù ŋŋmi. Maa tīī-bi mara yii bí nīn ŋáań míǹ, maa sòon̄ an pu, kaa dākafì míǹ pu gba.>
6«An pu ní ti-Dindaan bí yii: Ŋwiin ŋubɔ bí ki dòoń, baa làá dāá ti yíiń mpaan nee yii <Toofeeti> àá <Been-Inɔɔm tantakal>, ama bi làá dāá nīn yíì-ŋu yii <Dipɔ̀fil tantakal>. 7Mpaan nee puee, m làá dāá nàan̄ Juuda yab nì Jeerusaleem yab nín bɔ́ntì kí ŋá tiŋyee. M làá yàntī bi-nannanliibi ń kpɔ̀-bi kujaaun. M làá dūú dī bin nyàab̀-bi ŋkúmee pu ní kí ŋá míǹ. M làá dū bi-nikpiliŋ kí tīī inoon ń jī ní ipeel ń ŋmɔ́. 8M làá yàntī kitiŋ nee ń kpántí adigbun ŋma kí yàntī báà ŋma ń nīn gbáà ki-pu ibiil. Bin kɔkɔ làá dāá jītí niinee làá dāá fàŋkì ní kí nīn búǹ ifoon tin bāań-kèe pu. 9Binannanliibi bin là kí kúntí-bee làá dāá màntīí tū bi-tiŋki kí jáǹ-bi. Bi làá dāá nīn bí falaakpaan poon áli kí dāá ŋmɔ́ bi-jipɔmbi nì bi-bisalib nanti ní kí dāá ŋmɔ́ tɔb.
10«Míǹ boonee ní á gbá kí wīī kulɔŋŋuee bin nóó-see nimbiin, 11ní kí tùkù-bi yii: Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M làá wīī dinibul nee nì kitiŋ nee kii bi nín wìil̄ uyɔɔmaati lɔŋku puee ní. An kaa dāa gíti cáá diŋaŋkil.
«Bi làá dāá síb́ anikpil Toofeeti tantakalin gba, kun puee mpaan kaa dāa gíti bí laaba bí síb́-ŋi.» 12Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M làá yàntī kitiŋ nee nì ki-nib ń kpántí kii Toofeeti tantakalee ní. 13Jeerusaleem diiŋŋi nì Juuda bɔtiibi diiŋŋi làá kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi kii Toofeetee ní. Di sá yii bi tūutì talaalub adiin kɔkɔ yilpu bi nín bɔ̀b̄ puee ki tīī iŋmalbijaa in bí kutaa puee, ki fá awaa ndaam.
14Míǹ boonee ní Yeereemii nyánní Toofeeti tantakalin, laakin ti-Dindaan nìn tú-u ú cù kí sòoǹ u-bɔtee. U nìn cūtì ki kɔ́ kunimbɔtidii cindin, ní ki bí samaa kɔkɔ yii: 15«Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <M làá cáań nnaabu ŋun m nìn sòon̄ ki tɔ́ kitiŋ nee nì ki-timbilimmu kɔkɔ puee. Di sá yii kitiŋ nee nib yiliŋ pɔ̄ɔ̄, ní bi yíì kaa pílifì m-nyɔkɔ.>»

english_text:
Pashhur Arrests Jeremiah
1Pashhur son of Immer was a priest and the chief of temple security. He heard what I had said, 2and so he hit me. Then he had me arrested and put in chains at the Benjamin Gate in the Lord's temple. 3The next day, when Pashhur let me go free, I told him that the Lord had said:
No longer will I call you Pashhur. Instead, I will call you Afraid-of-Everything. 4You will be afraid, and you will bring fear to your friends as well. You will see enemies kill them in battle. Then I will let the king of Babylonia take everyone in Judah prisoner, killing some and dragging the rest away to Babylonia. 5He will clean out the royal treasury and take everything else of value from Jerusalem.
6Pashhur, you are guilty of telling lies and claiming they were messages from me. That's why I will let the Babylonians take you, your family, and your friends as prisoners to Babylonia, where you will all die and be buried.
Jeremiah Complains to the Lord
7You tricked me, Lord,
and I was really fooled.
You are stronger than I am,
and you have defeated me.
People never stop sneering
and insulting me.
8You have let me announce
only injustice and death.
Your message has brought me
nothing but insults
and trouble.
9Sometimes I tell myself
not to think about you, Lord,
or even mention your name.
But your message burns
in my heart and bones,
and I cannot keep silent.
10I heard the crowds whisper,
“Everyone is afraid.
Now's our chance
to accuse Jeremiah!”
All of my so-called friends
are just waiting
for me to make a mistake.
They say, “Maybe Jeremiah
can be tricked.
Then we can overpower him
and get even at last.”
11But you, Lord,
are a mighty soldier,
standing at my side.
Those troublemakers
will fall down and fail—
terribly embarrassed,
forever ashamed.
12 Lord All-Powerful,
you test those who do right,
and you know every heart
and mind.
I have told you my complaints,
so let me watch you
take revenge on my enemies.
13I sing praises to you, Lord.
You rescue the oppressed
from the wicked.
14 Put a curse on the day I was born!
Don't bless that day.
15Put a curse on the man
who told my father, “Good news!
You have a son.”
16May that man be like the towns
you destroyed without pity.
Let him hear shouts of alarm
in the morning
and battle cries at noon.
17He deserves to die
for not killing me
before I was born.
Then my mother's body
would have been my grave.
18Why did I have to be born?
Was it just to suffer
and die in shame?
translation_text:
Bi bóob́ Yeereemii ki nákáǹ ndɔ
1Usaraaŋakpil Pasuur, Imeer jipɔɔn, di nìn sá ti-Dindaan Diiku pilisikpiliu. U nìn gbìl̄ Yeereemii nín nāatì ti-Dindaan bɔti puee. 2Niinee ní u fáá Yeereemii ntampa ní ki yāntì bi bóob́-u ki nákáǹ ndɔ Beenjameen punyɔkɔki yilpu pú yaka kin bi dì ki kóò ti-Dindaan Diikunee. 3Kutaa wúntì Pasuur yāntì bi bútì Yeereemiiyee, ní Yeereemii bí-u yii: «Ti-Dindaan kaa ti làá yíiń-si Pasuur, ama u làá nīn kíǹ ki yíì-si yii: <Tifaandi bí an kɔkɔ pu.> 4Di sá yii ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <M làá kɔ́ǹ sii a-ba nì a-bɔɔbi tifaandi ní fàŋkì yɔ́kɔ́ yɔkɔ. A-nimbilaaliyin ní bi-nannanliibi làá kpɔ̀-bi. M làá dū Juuda yab kɔkɔ kí líiǹ Babiloon yab bɔtiu. U làá cúú-bi kí cùnnì u-tiŋkin kuyuŋu ní kí kpɔ̀ bin kíǹee. 5Jeerusaleem tiŋki gaajati kɔkɔ, kì nín túń ditundi ki ká tiŋyee kɔkɔ nì ki-gaajawammɔntiiti nì Juuda yab bɔtiibi gaajati kɔkɔee, m làá dūú ŋá bi-nannanliibi ŋaan. Bi làá fūkul̀ tíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ pílpil kí yòon̄ kí cáá cùnnì Babiloon tiŋkin. 6Sii Pasuur nì a-dicaŋkun yab kɔkɔee, bi làá cúú-ni kí cùnnì kuyuŋu. A yaa láa bàn̄ Babiloon tiŋkinee, a làá kpú. Bi làá síb́-si niin, ki kpáaǹ a-bɔɔbi bin a nì bi nāatì tinyimɔmbɔtee kɔkɔ.>»
Yeereemii timinsii
7M-Dindaan, a kíil̀-mi
ní ma mun lafun fōō ki kíí míǹ.
A cúú-mi mpɔn, ní ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-mi.
Binib lāā-mi baabadal,
báà ŋma bèel̄-mi ní.
8Ŋyunti kamaa m yaa làá sòoǹee,
see ḿ téeń kí bāakì yii:
Tipɔmbɔti nì dinàandi!
Tiŋman baabadalee,
sii ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi puee,
binib sìí-mi ki bèel̄-mi.
9M yaa bí yii:
«Maa làá ti dàkafì ti-Dindaan pu,
maa làá ti nàatī u-nyɔɔbundi.»
Ama ní m-pɔbil poonee,
an wù kii ŋŋmee.
M bíi pɔ̄ɔntí fám kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ-u,
ama ní kaa ŋūǹ.
10M gbìl̄ binib tikpil sòoǹ ki bíiĺ-mi.
Bi yíì-mi yii: «Tifaandi bí an kɔkɔ pu».
Biba lì yii: «Tí bìitī u-pu!»
ní bin kíǹee kíikí yii: «Tiŋman,
tí lafun bìitī u-pu.»
M-bɔɔbi gba kā ki cí yii ḿ lítí ní.
Bi lì yii:
«An yaa yíì u làá yàntī án túuǹ-u.
Niinee ti làá pɔ̄ɔkiǹ-u
ní kí tɔ̀-u ipɔntoon.»
11Ama ti-Dindaan un sá ubaatandaan
ki cáá mpɔnee bí m-cee.
Bin bíi sàantí-mee làá lítí,
baa làá ŋmā kí ŋá-mi tiba.
Icoo làá cúú-bi,
kun puee baa làá ŋmā kí já kí pɔ̄ɔkiǹ-mi.

M làá dū-bi kí ŋá bi-nannanliibi bin nyàab̀ kí kpɔ̀-bee ŋaan. Neebukadineesaar làá yàntī bí pɔ̀fì-bi. Waa làá sɔ̄ bi-saai, kaa làá kíń ubɔ, kaa làá dàkà ubɔ mun kulaŋŋaŋfitiiu.>»

11Tibɔti nee sá ki tīī Juuda bɔtiu dicaŋkun yab ní.
Ní pīlifìmaan ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi,
12Daafiidi dicaŋkun yab!
Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀.

Ní fōōmaan bin bi mùul̄ee bimuuliliibi ŋaan.

Di làá wà tikɔkɔ
ní ubɔ kaa làá ŋmā kí gbíntí-dì.

english_text:
The Lord Will Fight against Jerusalem
1King Zedekiah of Judah sent for Pashhur son of Malchiah and for a priest named Zephaniah son of Maaseiah. Then he told them, “Talk with Jeremiah for me.”
So they came to me and said, 2 “King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia has attacked Judah. Please ask the Lord to work miracles for our people, as he has done in the past, so that Nebuchadnezzar will leave us alone.”
3-7I told them that the Lord God of Israel had told me to say to King Zedekiah:
The Babylonians have surrounded Jerusalem and want to kill you and your people. You are asking me to save you, but you have made me furious. So I will stretch out my mighty arm and fight against you myself. Your army is using spears and swords to fight the Babylonians, but I will make your own weapons turn and attack you. I will send a horrible disease to kill many of the people and animals in Jerusalem, and there will be nothing left to eat. Finally, I will let King Nebuchadnezzar and his army fight their way to the center of Jerusalem and capture everyone who is left alive, including you and your officials. But Nebuchadnezzar won't be kind or show any mercy—he will have you killed! I, the Lord, have spoken.
8 Then I told them that the Lord had said:
People of Jerusalem, I, the Lord, give you the choice of life or death. 9The Babylonian army has surrounded Jerusalem, so if you want to live, you must go out and surrender to them. But if you want to die because of hunger, disease, or war, then stay here in the city. 10I have decided not to rescue Jerusalem. Instead, I am going to let the king of Babylonia burn it to the ground. I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Lord Warns the King of Judah
* 11Pay attention, you that belong
to the royal family.
12Each new day, make sure
that justice is done,
and rescue those
who are being robbed.
Or else my anger will flame up
like a fire that never goes out.
13Jerusalem,
from your mountaintop
you look out over the valleys
and think you are safe.
But I, the Lord, am angry,
14and I will punish you
as you deserve.
I'll set your palace on fire,
and everything around you
will go up in smoke.
