1King Zedekiah of Judah sent for Pashhur son of Malchiah and for a priest named Zephaniah son of Maaseiah. Then he told them, “Talk with Jeremiah for me.”
So they came to me and said, 2 “King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia has attacked Judah. Please ask the Lord to work miracles for our people, as he has done in the past, so that Nebuchadnezzar will leave us alone.”
3-7I told them that the Lord God of Israel had told me to say to King Zedekiah:
The Babylonians have surrounded Jerusalem and want to kill you and your people. You are asking me to save you, but you have made me furious. So I will stretch out my mighty arm and fight against you myself. Your army is using spears and swords to fight the Babylonians, but I will make your own weapons turn and attack you. I will send a horrible disease to kill many of the people and animals in Jerusalem, and there will be nothing left to eat. Finally, I will let King Nebuchadnezzar and his army fight their way to the center of Jerusalem and capture everyone who is left alive, including you and your officials. But Nebuchadnezzar won't be kind or show any mercy—he will have you killed! I, the Lord, have spoken.
8 Then I told them that the Lord had said:
People of Jerusalem, I, the Lord, give you the choice of life or death. 9The Babylonian army has surrounded Jerusalem, so if you want to live, you must go out and surrender to them. But if you want to die because of hunger, disease, or war, then stay here in the city. 10I have decided not to rescue Jerusalem. Instead, I am going to let the king of Babylonia burn it to the ground. I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Lord Warns the King of Judah
* 11Pay attention, you that belong
to the royal family.
12Each new day, make sure
that justice is done,
and rescue those
who are being robbed.
Or else my anger will flame up
like a fire that never goes out.
13Jerusalem,
from your mountaintop
you look out over the valleys
and think you are safe.
But I, the Lord, am angry,
14and I will punish you
as you deserve.
I'll set your palace on fire,
and everything around you
will go up in smoke.
translation_text:
Yeereemii kíí ubɔti Seedeesiyasi
1Tibɔti tin ti-Dindaan nìn sòon̄ nì Yeereemii ú dūú nàatī ubɔti Seedeesiyasee sɔ̀. Ubɔti nìn tú Maalkiya jipɔɔn Paasuur nì usaraaŋal Seefaniya, Maaseeyawuu jipɔɔn bí tùkù-u yii: 2«Bàlifì ti-Dindaan kí kpèè ti-yil pu bɔti, di sá yii Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar bíi jáà nì ti. An yaa yíì ti-Dindaan làá tí ŋá u-maamaacikpaambee ubɔ kí yàntī ú búntí kí wàatī-ti.» 3Ní Yeereemii bí-bi yii: «Ní tin tùkù ubɔti Seedeesiyasi yii: 4Ti-Dindaan Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Ni bí ki jáà nì Babiloon bɔtiu nì u-janjaliibi bin bíi jáà nì nee. M làá ŋá bijanjaliibi bin bin nyáń agun boon ki jáà nì bee mpɔn bí fàtīí gítí kitiŋ poon. 5Man m-ba di làá dū m-pɔŋŋu nì m-kpabil kí já nì ni nì m-ŋuul nì m-bum nì m-biim poon. 6M làá yàntī bìlbil kúm ń kpɔ̀ kitiŋ nee pu nib nì ki-waŋkuti. 7Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Míǹ boonee, m làá dū Juuda bɔtiu Seedeesiyasi nì u-kàliŋkpilib kí ŋá Babiloon bɔtiu ŋaan. M làá dū kitiŋ nee nib bin kaa kpíì bìlbil kúmin àá kujaaun àá ŋkùm yuntiŋuee mun kí ŋá u-ŋaan. M làá dū-bi kí ŋá bi-nannanliibi bin nyàab̀ kí kpɔ̀-bee ŋaan. Neebukadineesaar làá yàntī bí pɔ̀fì-bi. Waa làá sɔ̄ bi-saai, kaa làá kíń ubɔ, kaa làá dàkà ubɔ mun kulaŋŋaŋfitiiu.>»
8Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ nì Yeereemii tibɔti tin ú dūú nàatī samaayee sèé: «Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M dū dimaŋfal saŋŋu nì ŋkúm saŋŋu ki bíl̀ ni-nimbiin. 9Bin kɔkɔ làá gbíntí Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee, kujaau nì ŋkùm nì bìlbil kúm di làá kpɔ̀-bi. Ama bin làá nyā kí cáá bi-ba kí tīī Babiloon yab bin bíi jáà nì nee làá ŋmátí. Tin an nibee páatèe di sá bi nín kaa kpíìyee. 10Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M làá fàtī kí já nì Jeerusaleem tiŋki kí ŋá-kì tikpitil, kaa sá tiŋan. M làá dū kitiŋ nee kí ŋá Babiloon bɔtiu ŋaan ní úǹ ń tūū-kì ŋŋmi.»
Tin làá bàń Juuda yab bɔtiu dicaŋku puee
11Tibɔti nee sá ki tīī Juuda bɔtiu dicaŋkun yab ní.
Ní pīlifìmaan ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi,
12Daafiidi dicaŋkun yab!
Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀.
Ní kíĺ kutaafaau kí sòoǹ tibɔti ibaamɔn.
Ní fōōmaan bin bi mùul̄ee bimuuliliibi ŋaan.
An yaa kaa sá míǹ, m-ŋuul làá pōō kí yàaǹ ni-pu kii ŋŋmee.
Di làá wà tikɔkɔ
ní ubɔ kaa làá ŋmā kí gbíntí-dì.
13Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀.
Nimbi bin kóò ditantakalin
ki bí kii ditaŋkpal din cɔ́ kitimpiliŋ puee,
man nì ni di cáá tibɔti.
Di sá yii ni lì yii:
«Ubɔ kaa ŋūǹ kí sìntīń doo kí já nì ti,
àá kí kɔ́ ti-balilaŋkin.»
14Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «M làá dáaĺ ni-tafal
kí nóó nì ni-tuŋkpitiŋ nín sá puee.
M làá tūū Jeerusaleem bambaŋku ŋŋmi
ní an wà tin kɔkɔ māntìi tú-kuee.»

M làá fàtī kí já nì Jeerusaleem tiŋki kí ŋá-kì tikpitil, kaa sá tiŋan. M làá dū kitiŋ nee kí ŋá Babiloon bɔtiu ŋaan ní úǹ ń tūū-kì ŋŋmi.»
Tin làá bàń Juuda yab bɔtiu dicaŋku puee
11Tibɔti nee sá ki tīī Juuda bɔtiu dicaŋkun yab ní.
Ní pīlifìmaan ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi,
12Daafiidi dicaŋkun yab!
Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀.
Ní kíĺ kutaafaau kí sòoǹ tibɔti ibaamɔn.
Ní fōōmaan bin bi mùul̄ee bimuuliliibi ŋaan.
An yaa kaa sá míǹ, m-ŋuul làá pōō kí yàaǹ ni-pu kii ŋŋmee.
Di làá wà tikɔkɔ
ní ubɔ kaa làá ŋmā kí gbíntí-dì.
13Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀.
Nimbi bin kóò ditantakalin
ki bí kii ditaŋkpal din cɔ́ kitimpiliŋ puee,
man nì ni di cáá tibɔti.
Di sá yii ni lì yii:
«Ubɔ kaa ŋūǹ kí sìntīń doo kí já nì ti,
àá kí kɔ́ ti-balilaŋkin.»
14Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «M làá dáaĺ ni-tafal
kí nóó nì ni-tuŋkpitiŋ nín sá puee.
M làá tūū Jeerusaleem bambaŋku ŋŋmi
ní an wà tin kɔkɔ māntìi tú-kuee.»

english_text:
The Lord Will Punish the King of Judah
1-3The Lord sent me to the palace of the king of Judah to speak to the king, his officials, and everyone else who was there. The Lord told me to say:
I am the Lord, so pay attention! You have been allowing people to cheat, rob, and take advantage of widows, orphans, and foreigners who live here. Innocent people have become victims of injustice, and some of them have even been killed. But now I command you to do what is right and see that justice is done. Rescue everyone who has suffered from injustice.
4If you obey me, the kings from David's family will continue to rule Judah from this palace. They and their officials will ride in and out on their horses or in their chariots. 5 But if you ignore me, I promise in my own name that this palace will lie in ruins. 6Listen to what I think about it:
The palace of Judah's king
is as glorious as Gilead
or Lebanon's highest peaks.
But it will be as empty
as a ghost-town
when I'm through with it.
7I'll send troops to tear it apart,
and its beautiful cedar beams
will be used for firewood.
8People from different nations will pass by and ask, “Why did the Lord do this to such a great city as Jerusalem?” 9Others will answer, “It's because the people worshiped foreign gods and broke the agreement that the Lord their God had made with them.”
King Jehoahaz
The Lord said:
10King Josiah is dead,
so don't mourn for him.
Instead, mourn for his son
King Jehoahaz,
dragged off to another country,
never to return.
11-12 Jehoahaz became king of Judah after his father King Josiah died. But Jehoahaz was taken as a prisoner to a foreign country. Now I, the Lord, promise that he will die there without ever seeing his own land again.
King Jehoiakim
The Lord told me to say:
* 13King Jehoiakim, you are doomed!
You built a palace
with large rooms upstairs.
14You put in big windows
and used cedar paneling
and red paint.
But you were unfair
and forced the builders to work
without pay.
* 15More cedar in your palace
doesn't make you a better king
than your father Josiah.
He always did right—
he gave justice to the poor
and was honest.
16That's what it means
to truly know me.
So he lived a comfortable life
and always had enough
to eat and drink.
17But all you think about
is how to cheat
or abuse or murder
some innocent victim.
18 Jehoiakim, no one will mourn
at your funeral.
They won't turn to each other
and ask,
“Why did our great king
have to die?”
19You will be given a burial
fit for a donkey;
your body will be dragged
outside the city gates
and tossed in the dirt.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
King Jehoiachin and the People of Jerusalem
The Lord told me to say:
20People of Jerusalem,
the nations you trusted
have been crushed.
Go to Lebanon and weep;
cry in the land of Bashan
and in Moab.
21When times were good,
I warned you.
But you ignored me,
just as you have done
since Israel was young.
22Now you will be disgraced
because of your sins.
Your leaders will be swept away
by the wind,
and the nations you trusted
will be captured and dragged
to a foreign country.
23Those who live in the palace
paneled with cedar
will groan with pain
like women giving birth.
24 King Jehoiachin, son of Jehoiakim, even if you were the ring I wear as the sign of my royal power, I would still pull you from my finger. 25I would hand you over to the enemy you fear, to King Nebuchadnezzar and his army, who want to kill you. 26You and your mother were born in Judah, but I will throw both of you into a foreign country, where you will die, 27longing to return home.
28Jehoiachin, you are unwanted
like a broken clay pot.
So you and your children
will be thrown into a country
you know nothing about.
29Land of Judah, I am the Lord.
Now listen to what I say!
30Erase the names
of Jehoiachin's children
from the royal records.
He is a complete failure,
and so none of them
will ever be king.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
1Ti-Dindaan bí Yeereemii yii: «Sìntī Juuda bɔtiu beecindin. A yaa bàn̄ee, á sòoǹ tibɔti nee. 2Á sòoǹ yii: <Sii Juuda bɔtiu un kā Daafiidi beejal puee, pīlifì ti-Dindaan bɔti nee. Tì sá ki tīī a-kàliŋkpilib nì a-nibul yab bin jītí kipunyɔkɔ nee puee ní.> 3Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Ní dàkà ibaamɔn kí sòoǹ tibɔti ti-pú. Ní fōō bin bi mùul̄ee bimuuliliibi ŋaan. Ní taa sàaǹ unicaan nì ditaŋkpiibil nì ukpiipu, kí taa dàkà-bi tipɔmbɔti. Ní taa ti kpɔ̀ maanyiiba mpaan nee pu. 4Ni yaa lafun ŋá míǹ, ni làá nīn pée cáá bibɔtiibi bin làá nīn kàal̀ Daafiidi beejal puee ní. Bi làá nīn gbíntìi kàal̀ itaamu àá janjatɔrɔkub pu ki jītí kipunyɔkɔ nee pu ki kóò dibeecindin, bi nì bi-kàliŋkpilib nì dinibul nee. 5Ama ni yaa kaa pílifì tin m sòoǹee, man ni-Dindaan, m pūtì yii m làá yàntī dibeecindi nee ń kpántí adigbun.
6«Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ tibɔti tin Juuda bɔtiu cindi puee sɔ̀.
«Min kamaa a ŋān̄ kii Galaadi bambaŋku,
àá kii Leebanɔn jooŋŋi yilpu kúntí kuntee,
m làá yàntī á kpántí kuteeu,
kitiŋ kin báà ubɔ kaa ti kóòyee.
7M làá bɔ́ntí binib bí nàan̄-si,
báà ŋma làá nīn ŋúb́ u-tɔntɔŋwanti.
Bi làá gàatì a-jaantalkunyaambi
bin sá seedir dɔyee kí tɔ̄ ŋŋmin.
8«Atimbun kupaau nib làá dāá jītí Jeerusaleem tiŋki caŋin. Bi làá dāá bàlifì tɔb yii: <Ba pu ní ti-Dindaan ŋá kitiŋkpaaŋŋi nee míǹ ní?> 9Ní bí dāá kíí-bi yii: <Kun yì-tèe di sá yii bi fá mpèé ŋun nìn bí bi nì ti-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu kansikinee, ki cūtìi gbāaǹ awaa nimbiin ki jáam̀-ŋi.>»
Bí sɔ̄ ubɔti Saaluum pu
10Ní taa sɔ̄ un kpíìyee pu,
kí taa yāliŋkì u-pu.
Ama ní sɔ̄maan un bi cúú ki cáa cée pu,
kun puee waa ti làá fàtīí gítiń,
ní kaa nín fātìi ká u-tiŋki kin poon bi màl̄-uee.
11Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ Joosiyaasi jipɔɔn Saluum, Juuda bɔtiu un fōō u-baa Joosiyaasi yil ki kāl̀ dibeel, ki dáá nyáń kitiŋ nee poonee puee sèé. «U kpá kí gíti gítiń. 12Bi nín cúú-u ki cūnnì kitiŋ kin poon kuyuŋuee, niin ní u làá tin kpú, waa làá ti ká u-tiŋki.»
Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ ubɔti Yoowakiim pu miŋyee
13An sá mbusu ní ki tīī unil
un máń u-diiku an kaa tɔ́kɔ́ mbaamɔn pu,
ki māā adiin ki tɔ̄kɔntí tɔb pu kaa dī maree.
U yàntī bin kíǹee tūǹ u-tundi fám
ní waa pà-bi bi-paati.
14U lì u-ban yii:
<M làá mā kudikpaaŋŋu
kí mā adiin kí tɔ́kɔń ku-yilpu.
M làá lèekì tɔkɔlab,
ní kí dū seedir dɔi kí nákań agun pu
ní kí dū peentaman kí ŋmìtī-ku.
15A dàkafī yii a nín néeń seedir dɔyee pu
ní a sá ubɔtaaa?
A-baa nìn jīǹ ki nyù kii báà ŋmee ní.
U nìn nóó mara saŋŋu
ki nìn dàkà mbaamɔn
ní tikɔkɔ nìn còom̄-u tiŋan.
16Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀.
A-baa nìn mɔ́tí binandambi nì bisoodambi pu
ní tikɔkɔ nìn còom̄-u tiŋan.
Unil un ŋáań mimmee dàkà yii u lafun nyí-mi ní.
17Ama tin sii nyàab̀ee di sá a-baba paatii
kaa dàkafī bin kíǹee pu.
A pée nyàab̀ kí nīn kù maanyiibab ŋma ní
ki dàkà binib tipɔmbɔti ki mùul̄-bi.
18An pu ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ Joosiyaasi jipɔɔn Yoowakiim, Juuda bɔtiu pu yii:
«U yaa láa kpíìyee, bí taa sɔ̄ u-pu.
Ubɔ ń taa láa lì yii:
<Ba naabuŋu dee, m-nabiki!>
<Ba naabuŋu dee, m-niisal!>
Ubɔ ń taa láa sɔ̄ u-pu kí lì yii:
<Ba naabuŋu dee, m-dindaan!>
<Ba naabuŋu dee, ti-baa!>
19Bi làá dāá síb́-u kii kimaŋee ní.
Bi làá dāá fù-u kí nyāntí kí fá
ú nīn dátiǹ Jeerusaleem punyɔmmu.»
Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ Jeerusaleem yab pu
20«Jeerusaleem, jɔ̄m̀ Leebanɔn jooŋŋi pu
kí nīn tátí.
Cù Baasan tantakalin kí nīn kūuntí.
Tɔ́kɔń Abariim jooŋŋi yilpu kí nīn tátí,
kun puee an dóò a-bɔmbi kɔkɔ pu.
21Ŋyunti ŋun a nìn bí nsɔŋfinee,
m nìn sòon̄ nì si,
ama ní a kíí-mi yii:
<Maa làá pīlifiǹ-si!>
Tin a ŋá doooo a-sapɔntinee dee,
aa pée pílifíǹ-mi dalba dalba.
22Kubuŋu làá yòon̄ a-kpootiliibi kɔkɔ.
An yōoǹ a-bɔmbi ki cūnnì kuyuŋu.
Ikpiti in kɔkɔ a ŋée puee,
a làá fá a-jilmau ní icoo ń cúú-si gbòooo.
23Kɔŋkɔnnee, a kóò Leebanɔn bambaŋkun,
ki máń a-diiku kii kunɔndii di pá seedir sufii puee.
Ama iween yaa láa túuǹ-see,
a làá dāá yāliŋkì,
ní kí dāá jī falaa kii unimpu di kā imatiŋween puee.»
Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Yoowakiim jipɔɔn Yeekooniya pu
24Á sòoǹ nì Yoowakiim jipɔɔn Yeekooniya Juuda bɔtiu yii: «Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <M bí dimaŋfalin, m pūtì yii báà a yaa bàà sá kii kibɔmbiki ki fúuń m-ŋambiki m cáa nyìitī m-daaŋkuee, m làá fúutí-si kí fá. 25M làá dū-si kí ŋá bin nyàab̀ kí kpɔ̀-si a fàŋkí yɔ́kɔ́ yɔkɔee ŋaan, an dàkà yii Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar nì u-janjaliibi ŋaan. 26M làá dū si nì a-na un màl̄-see kí tɔ̄ ndandati, kitincaŋ kin poon baa màl̄-nee. Niin ní ni làá tin kpú. 27Ni làá dāá nyàab̀ nì ni-pɔŋŋu kɔkɔ kí gítiń, ama naa làá dāá ŋmā.>»
28Binib bàlifī yii: «Kooniya gbanti kpántì kii disambil din wīī kaa ti bí tibanee, àá tiwan tin kaa ti kèetēe níii? Ba pu ní bi jìn̄-u ki cáań kitiŋ kin poon ní u nì u-biyaamu kaa nyée poon ní?»
29M-tiŋki, m-tiŋki, pīlifì ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi! 30Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «Bí ŋmà Kooniya nee pu kii unil un kaa màl̄ ki kée. U bíil̀ u-maŋfal. U-dicaŋkun ubɔ kaa làá ŋmā kí kàl̄ Daafiidi beejal pu kí kpòotī Juuda tiŋki.»

english_text:
A Message of Hope
The Lord said:
1 You leaders of my people are like shepherds that kill and scatter the sheep. 2You were supposed to take care of my people, but instead you chased them away. So now I'll punish you severely and make you pay for your crimes!
3I will bring the rest of my people home from the lands where I have scattered them, and they will grow into a mighty nation. 4I promise to choose leaders who will care for them like real shepherds. All of my people will be there, and they will never again be frightened.
5 Someday I will appoint
an honest king
from the family of David,
a king who will be wise
and rule with justice.
6As long as he is king,
Israel will have peace,
and Judah will be safe.
The name of this king will be
“The Lord Gives Justice.”
7A time will come when you will again worship me. But you will no longer call me the Living God who rescued Israel from Egypt. 8Instead, you will call me the Living God who rescued you from the land in the north and from all the other countries where I had forced you to go. And you will once again live in your own land.
Jeremiah Thinks about Unfaithful Prophets
9When I think of the prophets,
I am shocked, and I tremble
like someone drunk,
because of the Lord
and his sacred words.
10Those unfaithful prophets
misuse their power
all over the country.
So God turned the pasturelands
into scorching deserts.
The Lord Will Punish Unfaithful Prophets
11The Lord told me to say:
You prophets and priests
think so little of me, the Lord,
that you even sin
in my own temple!
12Now I will punish you
with disaster,
and you will slip and fall
in the darkness.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
13The prophets in Samaria
were repulsive to me,
because they preached
in the name of Baal
and led my people astray.
14 And you prophets in Jerusalem
are even worse.
You're unfaithful in marriage
and never tell the truth.
You even lead others to sin
instead of helping them
turn back to me.
You and the people of Jerusalem
are evil like Sodom
and Gomorrah.
15You prophets in Jerusalem
have spread evil everywhere.
That's why I, the Lord, promise
to give you bitter poison
to eat and drink.
The Lord Gives a Warning
The Lord said:
16Don't listen to the lies
of these false prophets,
you people of Judah!
The message they preach
is something they imagined;
it did not come from me,
the Lord All-Powerful.
17These prophets go to people
who refuse to respect me
and who are stubborn
and do whatever they please.
The prophets tell them,
“The Lord has promised
everything will be fine.”
18But I, the Lord, tell you
that these prophets
have never attended a meeting
of my council in heaven
or heard me speak.
19They are evil! So in my anger
I will strike them
like a violent storm.
20I won't calm down,
until I have finished
what I have decided to do.
Someday you will understand
exactly what I mean.
21I did not send these prophets
or speak to them,
but they ran to find you
and to preach their message.
22If they had been in a meeting
of my council in heaven,
they would have told
you people of Judah
to give up your sins
and come back to me.
23I am everywhere—
both near and far,
24 in heaven and on earth.
There are no secret places
where you can hide from me.
25These unfaithful prophets claim that I have given them a dream or a vision, and then they tell lies in my name. 26But everything they say comes from their own twisted minds. How long can this go on? 27They tell each other their dreams and try to get my people to reject me, just as their ancestors left me and worshiped Baal. 28Their dreams and my truth are as different as straw and wheat. But when prophets speak for me, they must say only what I have told them. 29My words are a powerful fire; they are a hammer that shatters rocks.
30-32These unfaithful prophets claim I give them their dreams, but it isn't true. I didn't choose them to be my prophets, and yet they babble on and on, speaking in my name, while stealing words from each other. And when my people hear these liars, they are led astray instead of being helped. So I warn you that I am now the enemy of these prophets. I, the Lord, have spoken.
News and Nuisance
The Lord said to me:
33Jeremiah, when a prophet or a priest or anyone else comes to you and asks, “Does the Lord have news for us?” tell them, “You people are a nuisance to the Lord, and he will get rid of you.”
34If any of you say, “Here is news from the Lord,” I will punish you and your families, even if you are a prophet or a priest. 35Instead, you must ask your friends and relatives, “What answer did the Lord give?” or “What has the Lord said?” 36It seems that you each have your own news! So if you say, “Here is news from the Lord,” you are twisting my words into a lie. Remember that I am your God, the Lord All-Powerful.
37If you go to a prophet, it's all right to ask, “What answer did the Lord give to my question?” or “What has the Lord said?” 38But if you disobey me and say, “Here is news from the Lord,” 39I will pick you up and throw you far away. And I will abandon this city of Jerusalem that I gave to your ancestors. 40You will never be free from your shame and disgrace.
translation_text:
Bikpootiliibi bikpitib nì ubɔti ufiil
1Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí m-nibul kpootiliibi bin bí kii bipikpaaliibi bikpitibee. Bi féeń m-piii ní ki gbáà ki yàantí-i.» 2An pu ní ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu bíi sòon̄ bipikpaaliibi gbanti pu yii: «Ni yāntì m-piii wáŋkì ki yàl̄. Naa kpēē-i tiŋan. Too, mama m-ba làá kpèè ni-bɔti nì ni-tuŋkpitiŋ bɔti, man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ.
3«Míǹ boonee, mama m-ba làá kóoǹ m-piii in kíǹ ki yàl̄ ki bí ntimu mun kɔkɔ poon m jìn̄-bi ki kɔ́ǹee kí kpāfì. M làá fàtīí gíiǹní-i i-pikpaapɔɔkun. Niinee, i làá bùtī kí wíiǹ. 4M làá tīī-i bipikpaamɔntiibi bin làá kpàà-iee. Niinee, iaa ti làá fàŋkì, kaa ti làá nyɔ̀ ŋkpatim, ní báà ubɔ kaa ti làá wāŋkì, ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.»
5Ti-Dindaan bí yii:
«Iwiin bí ki dòoń
m làá yàntī bí màal̀ Daafiidi jipɔɔn tiŋman pu yɔu.
U làá dū dinyil ní kí jī dibeel.
U làá yàntī bí nīn tɔ́ mbaamɔn saŋŋu
nì tin bí deedeeyee kitiŋ nee pu.
6U-yuntiŋuee, Juuda beel làá ká difiil
ní Isirayeel yab ń nīn bí ŋgbansɔŋfin.
Bi làá dāá nīn yíì-u yii:
<Ti-Dindaan di sá ti-baamɔŋŋu.>
7«An pu ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ yii, ŋwiin bí ki dòoń baa làá dāá gíti lì yii: <M pūtì ti-Dindaan un bí dimaŋfalin ki nyántìń Isirayeel yab kuyuŋun Eejipiti tiŋkinee!>, 8ama bi làá dāá lì: <Nì ti-Dindaan un bí dimaŋfalin, ki nyántìń Isirayeel yab kitiŋ kin bí ŋgan púee nì ntimu mun kɔkɔ poon u nìn jìn̄-bi ki kɔ́ǹ bi fātìi gítìń ki kíǹ ki kóò bi-tiŋkinee pu.>»
Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi bin kaa bàà máaǹ kí nīn sée
9Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ u-bɔnaatiliibi pu puee sèé:
M-pɔbil bíil̀
m-wunti kɔkɔ jìkì.
M bí kii udanyɔgbilee,
a lì kii unil un nyùn̄ ndaam ki bál̀ee.
An sá ti-Dindaan circir Nimbɔtiu
nì tin u sòon̄ nì mee pu.
10U bí yii: «Kitiŋ nee poonee, binib kɔkɔ sá bilaakpaadambi ní.
Bi-kɔkɔ sáń ki cá tikpitil laŋki ní,
bi cáá tininjati kí ŋá tin kaa ŋān̄ee.
Mbusu ubɔ puee, kitiŋ nee kā dikpool.
Kitiŋ nee naakpaapɔɔku kɔkɔ kūń nyíki nyiki.»
11Ti-Dindaan bí yii:
«M-bɔnaatiliibi nì bisaraaŋaliibi mun sá bikpitib ní.
Áli gba m kāntí bi-tuŋkpitiŋ m-Diikun.
12Míǹ puee bi-saŋŋu ń kpántí dijɔnjɔndi.
Bí wāŋkì dibɔmbɔndin kí lítí.
M làá cáań nnaabu kí tɔ̄ bi-pu
dibindi din bi làá dāá sòoǹ bi-nyɔkɔpu yayee.»
Samaarii bɔnaatiliibi sɔ́ǹ Jeerusaleem yab
13Samaarii bɔnaatiliibi ceeyee,
m ká tiwan tin cáá titantanee.
Diwaal Baal bɔti ní bi nìn nàatī,
ní ki gáatí m-nibul Isirayeel yab.
14Ama tin m ká Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi
bin bí Jeerusaleemee ceeyee
di sá ntimbiil bɔti.
Bi ŋáań tilaakpaal,
ki mɔ́ntí inyimɔn,
ki tìì bikpitiŋaliibi kunyannyaau,
an yāntì báà ubɔ kaa ti ŋūǹ kí fá u-kpitii.
Bi-kɔkɔ bí m-cee kii Soodoom yabee ní.
Jeerusaleem yab náań nì Goomoora yab ní.
15An pu ní ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan
sòon̄ u-bɔnaatiliibi pu yii:
«M làá tīī-bi kisubiki kin tūee bí ŋmɔ́,
kí tīī-bi nnyim min cáá ndabiimee bí nyɔ̀.
Di sá yii Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi bin bí Jeerusaleemee
cee ní ikpiti nyánní ki tīntì kitiŋ nee kɔkɔ.»
16Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan bí yii:
«Ní taa pīlifì tibɔti tin
Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi sòoǹee,
bi mɔ́ntí-ni ní.
Bíǹ bi-ba di nāantí tin bi sòoǹee,
taa nyánní man ni-Dindaan nyɔkɔn.»
17Bi lì bin kpèé-mi fámee cee yii:
<Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ yii ni làá ká ŋgbansɔŋfi.>
Bi tùkù bipɔɔgbifindambi yii:
«Nnaabu ŋubɔ kaa làá bàń-ni.»
18Di sá yii ŋma di cūtì
laakin man ni-Dindaan kàal̀
ki lèekī ilandɔkɔee?
Ŋma di ká m-bɔti ki gbìl̄-tì?
Ŋma di fōotì ki yīkiǹ m-nyɔɔbundi ki gbìl̄ di-taapu.
Yeereemii
19Ti-Dindaan buŋkpaaŋku dòoń,
u-ŋuul làá pōō.
Kunaakpaabuŋkpaaŋŋu kubɔ bíi jītí,
ku bí binikpitib yiliŋ pu ki màntī.
20Ti-Dindaan yaa kaa ŋá u nín lēē kí ŋá puee,
u-ŋuul kpá kí sɔ̀ŋkì.
Boon kpataaayee, ni làá dāá gbìl̄ taapu.
ti-Dindaan
21Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi gbantee,
maa tú-bi, ama ní bi sáń ki cá.
Maa sòon̄ nì bi, ama ní bi bí ki nàatī m-bɔti.
22Bi yaa bàà nìn bí laakin
m kāl̀ ki lēē ilandɔkɔee,
bi bàà sòoǹ nì m-nibul bí béé m-bɔti.
Bi bàà nyāntí binib bi-bimbikpitim poon,
nì ikpiti in bi ŋáańee poon.
Ti-Dindaan bí duulinya kɔkɔn
23Ti-Dindaan bí yii:
«M sá bin bí kɔŋkɔmee baba Nimbɔtiu níii?
Maa sá bin bí ndanee mun Nimbɔtiuaaa?
24Unil ŋūǹ kí báĺ laaba ḿ taa wāl̀-uaaa?
Man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ.
Naa nyí yii m gbí kutagbɔŋu nì kitiŋ kɔkɔɔɔ?»
Man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ.
Idi nì tifin kaa sá ubaanti
25Man ni-Dindaan, m gbìl̄ tin m-bɔnaatiliibi sòoǹee. Bi lì yii bi sòoǹ m-yindi pu ní, ama an kaa sá míǹ. Bi lì yii: <M dámintì kudamintiiu kubɔ, m dámintì kudamintiiu kubɔ.> 26Kí tin cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu dee? Ba di kalin kā bibɔnaatiliibi gbanti yiliŋin ní bi nàatī tinyimɔmbɔti ní? An sá bibɔnaatiliibi bin di nāantí tibɔti bi-ba ki nàatēe ní. 27Nì bi-damintiiti tin bi cáa sòoǹ tɔb ceeyee, bi dàkafī yii m-nibul làá súntí m-pu, kii bi-naanjab nín nìn dī diwaal Baal pu ki súntì m-pu puee ní. 28Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu kansikin un yaa dámintèe ń sòoǹ tin u kée. Ama un fōō m-nyɔɔbundee ń nàatī-dì deedee!
Idi nì tifin kaa sá ubaanti.
Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.
29Ti-Dindaan bí yii:
M-bɔti sá kii ŋŋmee ní,
a lì kii dikújal din bi cáa wìil̄ ditaŋkpakpaandee ní.
30«Ti-Dindaan bí yii: <M làá jáǹ bibɔnaatiliibi bin di yòontí tɔb bɔti ki cáa nàatī yii an sá m-bɔtee. 31M làá jáǹ bibɔnaatiliibi bin di cáá bíǹ bi-ba bɔti ki nàatī yii an sá m-yatee, ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.> 32Ti-Dindaan bí yii: <M làá jáǹ-bi. Bi-damintiiti sá tinyimɔmbɔti ní. Bi yaa sòoǹ bi-damintiiti gbanti puee, bi cáá tinyimɔmbɔti nì nyɔɔmálmal ki kíiĺ m-nibul. Man kaa tú-bi, kaa dū dinyɔɔbundi diba ki ŋúbíǹ-bi. Baa pée ŋūǹ kí kèetī m-nibul tiba poon, ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.>»
Unimbɔti nyɔɔbundi sá diwaŋgulaaa?
33Ti-Dindaan bí Yeereemii yii: «Dinibul nee niliu ubɔ, àá Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu ubɔ àá usaraaŋal ubɔ yaa bālifì-si yii: <Ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi sá dilal? Diwaŋgul dilal ní u làá tí túń-ti ní?> Á kíí-bi yii: <Ti-Dindaan bí yii nimbi di sá diwaŋgul, ní m làá túutí-ni kí fá kí wàatī m-ba, ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.> 34M-nibul niliu ubɔ àá m-bɔnaatiliu ubɔ àá usaraaŋal ubɔ di yaa lī yii: <Ti-Dindaan di túǹ-mi diwaŋgulee,> m làá dáaĺ udaan nì u-dicaŋku tafal. 35Ni máaǹ ki bàlifì tɔb yii: <Ti-Dindaan kíí-ti yii ba ní? Ti-Dindaan bí yii ba ní.> 36Ama ní taa ti sòoǹ yii ti-Dindaan túǹ-ti diwaŋgul dilal ní? Mimmee ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi sá diwaŋgulaaa? Ni yaa bíi lì mimmee ni bíi kpántí ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan un bí dimaŋfalinee bɔti taapu dee. 37Kpèè tin a máaǹ kí bàlifì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliuee sèé: <Ti-Dindaan kíí-si yii bá ní? Ti-Dindaan tùkū-si yii ba ní?> 38Ama ni yaa gbíntìi lì yii ti-Dindaan túǹ-ti diwaŋgulee, min kamaa ti-Dindaan bí yii ní taa ti lì mimmee, man ni-Dindaan nín lī puee sɔ̀. 39M làá yòon̄-ni kí túń kí cáá ni nì ni-tiŋki kin m nìn tīī ni-naanjabee kí tɔ̄ kí fá ndandati. 40M làá yàntī icoo ń cúú-ni kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaan, ní ní fá ni-jilmau kí nīn cá abin abin. Unil dāa pée kpá kí súntí.»

english_text:
Jeremiah Has a Vision of Two Baskets of Figs
1 The Lord spoke to me in a vision after King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia had come to Judah and taken King Jehoiachin, his officials, and all the skilled workers back to Babylonia. In this vision I saw two baskets of figs in front of the Lord's temple. 2One basket was full of very good figs that ripened early, and the other was full of rotten figs that were not fit to eat.
3“Jeremiah,” the Lord asked, “what do you see?”
“Figs,” I said. “Some are very good, but the others are too rotten to eat.”
4Then the Lord told me to say:
5People of Judah, the good figs stand for those of you I sent away as exiles to Babylonia, 6where I am watching over them. Then someday I will bring them back to this land. I will plant them, instead of uprooting them, and I will build them up, rather than tearing them down. 7I will give them a desire to know me and to be my people. They will want me to be their God, and they will turn back to me with all their heart.
8The rotten figs stand for King Zedekiah of Judah, his officials, and all the others who were not taken away to Babylonia, whether they stayed here in Judah or went to live in Egypt. 9I will punish them with a terrible disaster, and everyone on earth will tremble when they hear about it. I will force the people of Judah to go to foreign countries, where they will be cursed and insulted. 10War and hunger and disease will strike them, until they finally disappear from the land that I gave them and their ancestors.
translation_text:
Tikabiti tili tin poon fiigi subiliŋ kēe
1Ti-Dindaan nìn yāntì m ká tikabiti tili tin poon fiigi subiliŋ kēe yú ti-Dindaan kɔŋkooŋŋu nyɔkɔpu. An nìn sá ŋyunti ŋun Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar nìn cúú Yooyakiim jipɔɔn Yeekooniya, Juuda bɔtiu nì Juuda yab kàliŋkpilib nì bicaabi nì bin tūǹ ŋŋal pu tundee Jeerusaleem ki cūnnì Babiloon tiŋkin kuyuŋuee ní. 2Fiigi biliŋ ŋin ŋān̄ kii asubipeekaayee nìn kā kukabiku kubɔ poon ní fiigi biliŋ ŋin bíil̀ unil kaa ŋūǹ kí ŋmɔ́ee kā kukabiku kun kíǹee poon.
3Ní ti-Dindaan bālifì-mi yii: «Yeereemii, ba ní a wāĺ?» Ní m kíí-u yii: «M wāĺ fiigi subiliŋ ní. Amɔntee ŋān̄ tikpilku, ama ní akpilee ŋíǹ baasii bíil̀. Ŋi nín bíil̀ puee, unil kaa ŋūǹ kí ŋmɔ́-ŋi.»
4Niinee ní ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: 5«Ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Kii unil nín kpèé fiigi subimɔntiŋ nee án fáatíǹ-u puee, míǹ ní ma mun làá kpèè Juuda yab bin bínní kuyuŋun nee bí fáatíǹ-mi, bíǹ bin m jìn̄ kitiŋ nee pu ki cūnnì kuyuŋuee. 6M làá kpèè-bi nì kulaŋŋaŋfitiiu ní kí gíiǹní-bi kitiŋ nee poon. Maa ti làá gbá kí kpìtī-bi, ama m làá fàtīí mā-bi ní, maa ti làá cóotí-bi, ama m làá fàtīí cóoń-bi ní. 7M làá dāá tīī-bi dipɔbil din làá yàntī bí béé yii man di sá bi-Dindaanee. Bi làá nīn sá m-nibul, ní man ń nīn sá bi-Nimbɔtiu, di sá yii bi làá fàtīí gítiń m-cee nì bi-pɔbil kɔkɔ.
8«Ama kii bi nín ŋáań asubil ŋin bíil̀ kaa bí diŋmɔlee puee, míǹ ní m làá ŋá Juuda bɔtiu Seedeesiyasi nì u-kàliŋkpilib nì binib bin kíǹ Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee nì bin kóò kɔŋkɔnnee Eejipiti tiŋkinee. Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ. 9Duulinya beeŋi kɔkɔ yaa láa ká mimmee, ŋi làá dāá kɔ́ dinyoondin. Bi yaa láa là kí kɔ́ǹ ubɔ icoo àá kí bèel̀ ubɔ àá kí sìì ubɔ àá kí tɔ̄ ubɔ mbusu ntimu mun kɔkɔ poon m làá dāá jà-bi kí kɔ́ǹee, bíǹ ní bi làá dāá yòon̄ ŋabika. 10M làá dāá dū kujaau nì ŋkùm nì bìlbil kúm kí tɔ̄ bi-pu áli bí dāá wāŋkì kitiŋ kin m tīī bi nì bi-naanjabee poon.»

english_text:
Seventy Years of Exile
1-2 In the fourth year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, which was the first year that Nebuchadnezzar was king of Babylonia, the Lord told me to speak to the people of Judah and Jerusalem. So I told them:
3For 23 years now, ever since the thirteenth year that Josiah was king, I have been telling you what the Lord has told me. But you have not listened.
4The Lord has sent prophets to you time after time, but you refused to listen. 5They told you that the Lord had said:
Change your ways! If you stop doing evil, I will let you stay forever in this land that I gave your ancestors. 6I don't want to harm you. So don't make me angry by worshiping idols and other gods.
7But you refused to listen to my prophets. So I, the Lord, say that you have made me angry by worshiping idols, and you are the ones who were hurt by what you did. 8You refused to listen to me, 9and now I will let you be attacked by nations from the north, and especially by my servant, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia. You and other nearby nations will be destroyed and left in ruins forever. Everyone who sees what has happened will be shocked, but they will still make fun of you. 10 I will put an end to your parties and wedding celebrations; no one will grind grain or be here to light the lamps at night. 11 This country will be as empty as a desert, because I will make all of you the slaves of the king of Babylonia for 70 years.
12When that time is up, I will punish the king of Babylonia and his people for everything they have done wrong, and I will turn that country into a wasteland forever. 13My servant Jeremiah has told you what I said I will do to Babylonia and to the other nations, and he wrote it all down in this book. I will do everything I threatened. 14I will pay back the Babylonians for every wrong they have done. Great kings from many other nations will conquer the Babylonians and force them to be slaves.
The Cup Full of God's Anger
15The Lord God of Israel showed me a vision in which he said, “Jeremiah, here is a cup filled with the wine of my anger. Take it and make every nation drink some. 16They will vomit and act crazy, because of the war this cup of anger will bring to them.”
17I took the cup from the Lord's hand, and I went to the kings of the nations and made each of them drink some. 18I started with Jerusalem and the towns of Judah, and the king and his officials were removed from power in disgrace. Everyone still makes insulting jokes about them and uses their names as curse words. 19The second place I went was Egypt, where everyone had to drink from the cup, including the king and his officials, the other government workers, the rest of the Egyptians, 20and all the foreigners who lived in the country.
Next I went to the king of Uz, and then to the four kings of Philistia, who ruled from Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron, and what was left of Ashdod. 21Then I went to the kings of Edom, Moab, Ammon, 22and to the kings of Tyre, Sidon, and their colonies across the sea. 23-24After this, I went to the kings of Dedan, Tema, Buz, the tribes of the Arabian Desert, 25Zimri, Elam, Media, 26and the countries in the north, both near and far.
I went to all the countries on earth, one after another, and finally to Babylonia.
27The Lord had said to tell each king, “The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, commands you to drink from this cup that is full of the wine of his anger. It will make you so drunk that you will vomit. And when the Lord sends war against the nations, you will be completely defeated.”
28The Lord told me that if any of them refused to drink from the cup, I must tell them that he had said, “I, the Lord All-Powerful, command you to drink. 29Starting with my own city of Jerusalem, everyone on earth will suffer from war. So there is no way I will let you escape unharmed.”
30The Lord told me to say:
From my sacred temple
I will roar like thunder,
while I trample my people
and everyone else
as though they were grapes.
31My voice will be heard
everywhere on earth,
accusing nations of their crimes
and sentencing the guilty
to death.
Disaster Is Coming
32The Lord All-Powerful says:
You can see disaster spreading
from far across the earth,
from nation to nation
like a horrible storm.
33When it strikes, I will kill so many people that their bodies will cover the ground like manure. No one will be left to bury them or to mourn.
The Leaders of Judah Will Be Punished
34The Lord's people are his flock,
and you leaders
were the shepherds.
But now it's your turn
to be butchered like sheep.
You'll shatter like fine pottery
dropped on the floor.
So roll on the ground,
crying and mourning.
35You have nowhere to run,
nowhere to hide.
* 36-37Listen to the cries
of the shepherds,
as the Lord's burning anger
turns peaceful meadows
into barren deserts.
38Like a lion leaving its den,
the Lord has abandoned
his people
to the destruction of war.
translation_text:
Yeereemii dū abin mmuŋku nì ata ki sòon̄ Unimbɔti bɔti
1Joosiyaasi jipɔɔn Yoowakiim nín kāl̀ Juuda tiŋki pu dibeel dibinnanaatiil poonee, ti-Dindaan nìn sòon̄ nì Yeereemii Juuda nibul kɔkɔ pu. An nìn sá Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar beel bimpeepeekaal poon ní. 2Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii nìn sòon̄ nì Juuda yab kɔkɔ nì bin kɔkɔ kóò Jeerusaleemee yii: 3«Amɔn jipɔɔn Joosiyaasi, Juuda bɔtiu nín kāl̀ dibeel abin saalaa nì ata poon kí dāá sāā díǹee, an ŋá abin mmuŋku nì ata dee. M bí ki sòoǹ nì ni ti-Dindaan bɔti kaa gbèentí, ama naa pílifí. 4Ti-Dindaan túnní u-tɔntɔnliibi u-bɔnaatiliibi ni-cee kaa gbēeǹ, ama naa kpōoǹ ni-tafal ki pílifì-bi. 5Bi nìn tùkū-ni yii: <Báà ŋma ń fá u-bimbikpitim nì u-tuŋkpitiŋ. Niinee ni làá ŋmā kí kàl̄ kitiŋ kin man ni-Dindaan tīī ni nì ni-naanjabee poon kí nīn cá jaanjaan. 6Ní taa nín̄ jòó ki pá awaa boon kí nīn jáaḿ-ŋi, kí taa gbàan̄ ŋi-nimbiin kí tòotī-ŋi. Ní taa mā àá kí kpítí awaa kí gbítí m-ŋuul. Mimmee maa làá ŋá-ni tikpitil tiba. 7Ama ní naa pílifiǹ-mi, ní ki kpítì àá ki mɔ́ɔ́ awaa ŋin sá ni-naabuŋuee ki gbítì m-ŋuul. Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.>
8«An pu ní ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan bí yii: <Ni nín kaa pílifì m-bɔtee puee, 9m làá tɔ̄ bí cáań ŋgan pú nibuliŋ. M làá yíiń m-tɔntɔnliu Neebukadineesaar, Babiloon bɔtiu. M làá cáań bíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ kí tɔ̄ kitiŋ nee nì ki-nib nì ntimu mun māntìi tú-kèe pu. M làá nàan̄ ni nì bi kɔkɔ. M làá yàntī kitiŋ nee ń kpántí ntimbiil paaŋŋu, adigbun kí nīn cá jaanjaan. Binib làá dāá nīn gbáà inimɔɔn biilii, man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ. 10M làá kúntí ifaal nì dipɔɔpindi kuŋkuuntii nì inimpucanlan bi-cee. M làá kúntí tinàti tin nà idee wooku ní kí kpɔ̀ fitila ŋmiŋu. 11Kitiŋ kɔkɔ làá kpántí adigbun, mpaan ŋun kaa làá nīn bí ŋkpèéyee. Anibul nee kɔkɔ làá nīn bí Babiloon bɔtiu taapu abin imuŋku ita nì saalaa ní>.»
12Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Abin imuŋku ita nì saalaayee yaa láa jítèe, m làá dāá dáaĺ Babiloon bɔtiu nì u-yab tafal ikpiti in bi ŋée pu. M làá kúntí Babiloon tiŋki ní kí yàntī kí kpántí kuteeu kí nīn cá jaanjaan. 13M làá cáań inaabu in kɔkɔ m nìn sòon̄ bi ŋmàn̄ ki ŋá tigbɔn poonee kitiŋ nee pu. Tíǹ ní m nìn yāntì Yeereemii sòon̄ ki nāatì atimbun kɔkɔ pu. 14Di sá yii ntimu mun cáá mpɔnee nì bibɔtikpaambi mun làá dāá nyīī Babiloon yab kí gùl̄ bi-taapu. Niinee ní ḿ pà-bi bi-tuŋkpitiŋ nì bi-ŋáaǹtam paati.»
Unimbɔti làá dáaĺ atimbun tafal
15Ti-Dindaan Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu bí-mi yii: «Fōō ndamam kɔŋkɔnnyɔkaau un poon m-ŋuul kā nee, kí cáá nyùntī atimbun ŋin kɔkɔ cee m làá tɔ̄-si nee yab. 16Bi yaa láa ká m tú binib bi dū kitàataajiki ki pɔ̄fì binib bi-kansikinee, bi làá dāá nyɔ̀ kí gbí ní ki kíǹ ki kpìntī, ní bi-yiliŋ ń lábití.»
17Ní m fōō ndamam kɔŋkɔnnyɔkaauee ti-Dindaan ŋaan ki cáa nyūntì atimbun ŋin kɔkɔ cee u tú-mee nib. 18M nyūntì Jeerusaleem yab nì Juuda timmun yab nì bibɔtiibi nì bikàliŋkpilib, ní ntimu gbanti kpántì adigbun, ki kíǹ ki fàantí. An yāntì binib gbáà mu-pu ibiil ní ki yāntì mu kpántì ŋabika bi cáa tòó mbusu.
19Míǹ boonee ní m tīī Eejipiti yab bɔtiu Faaroo nì u-kàliŋkpilib nì u-bɔtibiliŋ nì u-nibul kɔkɔ bi nyùn̄, 20nì nyaaŋmaliŋku nibuliŋ ŋin kóò Eejipiti tiŋkinee,
nì Uusi tiŋki bɔtiibi
nì Fiiliistii yab bɔtiibi an dàkà yii Asikeelɔn yab bɔtiibi nì Gaasaa yab bɔtiibi nì Eekrɔn yab bɔtiibi nì Asidoodi yab bin kíǹee.
21M nìn tīī Eedoom yab nì Moowaab yab nì Amɔn yab,
22nì Tiir yab bɔtiibi nì Siidɔn yab bɔtiibi nì ntimu mun bí tiŋku gbandee,
23nì Deedan yab nì Teema yab nì Buusi yab nì bin kòol̄ bi-gatikiiyee,
24nì Bilaalibub tiŋki bɔtiibi kɔkɔ nì nyaaŋmaliŋku nibuliŋ ŋin kóò kuteeunee kɔkɔ.
25M nìn tí tīī Simrii yab bɔtiibi kɔkɔ nì Eelaam yab bɔtiibi nì Meedi yab bɔtiibi,
26nì bibɔtiibi bin kɔkɔ bí ŋgan púee, bin pìl̄ee nì bin bí ndandatee kɔkɔ.
Abee ŋin kɔkɔ bí duulinyanee máaǹ kí nyɔ̀ kɔŋkɔn gbanti kí kíǹ kí tīī tɔb. Bíǹ kɔkɔ yaa láa nyùn̄ ki dóòyee ní Seesaki bɔtiu ń nín nyɔ̀.
27Á tùkù-bi yii ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín lī puee sèé: «Nyɔ̀maan! Gbímaan kí wùliŋkì! Lítímaan kí taa yīkì kí kpèè kitàataajiki kin m làá dūú pɔ̀fì binib ni-kansikinee. 28Biba yaa yíì kaa làá fōō a-ŋaan ndamam kɔŋkɔnnyɔkaauee kí nyɔ̀ee, á tùkù-bi yii: <Ni làaa, naa làaa, ni làá fōō-u kí nyɔ̀, ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di lī míǹ. 29Di sá yii m dū nnaabu ki tɔ́ mama m-ba tiŋki pu, ní nimbi dàkafī yii m làá yàntī-naaa? Aayee, maa làá yàntī-ni fám. M làá dū kujaau kí tɔ̄ kitiŋ nee nib kɔkɔ pu, man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di lī míǹ.>»
30Ní ti-Dindaan gíti bí-mi yii: «Dū tibɔti nee kí nàatī kí tùkù-bi yii:
«Ti-Dindaan kāl̀ yilpu ki téenní.
U kāl̀ u-circir kɔŋkooŋŋun ki yāntì bi gbìl̄ u-neen pu.
U tátí u-tiŋki pu,
u bíi kūuntí kí jáǹ kitiŋ nib kɔkɔ,
kii bin bí ki tà fiinyi biliŋ
kí nyāntí ndaamee.
31Kuwoou kun u ŋáańee bàn̄ kitiŋgbeennyɔkɔ.
Ti-Dindaan di bíi sòoǹ anibul bɔti,
u yíiń inifunaan kɔkɔ u-bɔsoondiikun.
U làá yàntī bí pɔ̀fì bikpitiŋaliibi.»
Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.
32Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé:
«Nnaabu ŋubɔ jéetì ditimbundi diba pu
ki tin póotì din kíǹ pu,
kubuŋkpaaŋŋu nyánní kitiŋgbeennyɔkɔ ki bíi jītí.»
33Ŋwiin gbantee, bin ti-Dindaan làá dāá kpɔ̀ee làá dāá nīn bí kitiŋ gbeennyɔkɔ kiba kí tin sāā kin kíǹee. Tíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ yaa láa bāańee, ubɔ kaa dāa sūǹ bi-pu, kaa dāa kōontí bi-nikpiliŋ ki dāa nín nyàab̀ kí síb́-ŋi. Ŋi làá dāá dòon̄ kitiŋ ní kí kpántí ntiŋkpam.
34Bikpootiliibi, gāāmaan ikpiisilan,
nín̄ gbáàmaan ibiil
kí dòon̄ kitiŋ kí nīn bíliŋkí.
Di sá yii ŋyunti bāań bí kpɔ̀ ni mun dee.
Ni làá lítí ní kí wīī
kii disambil din pɔ̄ɔ̄ kudaauee.
35Bikpootiliibi kaa làá ká kibalilaŋ,
ní bipikpaaliibi kaa làá ŋmā kí sāǹ kí ŋmátí.
36Bi gbìl̄ bikpootiliibi biilii pu
nì bipikpaaliibi yaliŋkii pu.
Di sá yii ti-Dindaan nāaǹ bi-pikpaapɔɔku.
37Ti-Dindaan ŋuukpaandi puee,
kunaakpaapɔɔu ŋmíl̀ díkí diki fɔ́ŋfɔŋ.
38Gbikinti nyáń u-mɔgbaakin.
Kujaau kun poon baa sūǹ ubɔ saayee
nì ti-Dindaan ŋuukpaandi puee,
bi-tiŋki kpántì kuteeu.

english_text:
Jeremiah's Message in the Temple
(Jeremiah 7.1-15)
1 Soon after Jehoiakim became king of Judah, the Lord said:
2Jeremiah, I have a message for everyone who comes from the towns of Judah to worship in my temple. Go to the temple courtyard and speak every word that I tell you. 3Maybe the people will listen this time. And if they stop doing wrong, I will change my mind and not punish them for their sins. 4Tell them that I have said:
You have refused to listen to me and to obey my laws and teachings. 5Again and again I have sent my servants the prophets to preach to you, but you ignored them as well. Now I am warning you that if you don't start obeying me at once, 6 I will destroy this temple, just as I destroyed the town of Shiloh. Then everyone on earth will use the name “Jerusalem” as a curse word.
Jeremiah on Trial
7The priests, the prophets, and everyone else in the temple heard what I said, 8-9and as soon as I finished, they all crowded around me and started shouting, “Why did you preach that the Lord will destroy this temple, just as he destroyed Shiloh? Why did you say that Jerusalem will be empty and lie in ruins? You ought to be put to death for saying such things in the Lord's name!” Then they had me arrested.
10The royal officers heard what had happened, and they came from the palace to the new gate of the temple to be the judges at my trial. 11While they listened, the priests and the prophets said to the crowd, “All of you have heard Jeremiah prophesy that Jerusalem will be destroyed. He deserves the death penalty.”
12-13Then I told the judges and everyone else:
The Lord himself sent me to tell you about the terrible things he will do to you, to Jerusalem, and to the temple. But if you change your ways and start obeying the Lord, he will change his mind.
14You must decide what to do with me. Just do whatever you think is right. 15But if you put me to death, you and everyone else in Jerusalem will be guilty of murdering an innocent man, because everything I preached came from the Lord.
16The judges and the other people told the priests and prophets, “Since Jeremiah only told us what the Lord our God had said, we don't think he deserves to die.”
17Then some of the leaders from other towns stepped forward. They told the crowd that 18 years ago when Hezekiah was king of Judah, a prophet named Micah from the town of Moresheth had said:
“I, the Lord All-Powerful, say
Jerusalem will be plowed under
and left in ruins.
Thorns will cover the mountain
where the temple
now stands.”
19Then the leaders continued:
No one put Micah to death for saying that. Instead, King Hezekiah prayed to the Lord with fear and trembling and asked him to have mercy. Then the Lord decided not to destroy Jerusalem, even though he had already said he would.
People of Judah, if Jeremiah is killed, we will bring a terrible disaster on ourselves.
20-24After these leaders finished speaking, an important man named Ahikam son of Shaphan spoke up for me as well. And so, I wasn't handed over to the crowd to be killed.
Uriah the Prophet
While Jehoiakim was still king of Judah, a man named Uriah son of Shemaiah left his hometown of Kiriath-Jearim and came to Jerusalem. Uriah was one of the Lord's prophets, and he was saying the same things about Judah and Jerusalem that I had been saying. And when Jehoiakim and his officials and military officers heard what Uriah said, they tried to arrest him, but he escaped to Egypt. So Jehoiakim sent Elnathan son of Achbor and some other men after Uriah, and they brought him back. Then Jehoiakim had Uriah killed and his body dumped in a common burial pit.
translation_text:
Bi sòon̄ Yeereemii bɔti kí kpɔ̀-u
1Joosiyaasi jipɔɔn Yoowakiim, Juuda bɔtiu beel nín kíĺ puee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Yeereemii tibɔti nee yii: 2«Man ni-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Cùú yūĺ kunimbɔtidii cindin. Á sòoǹ nì bin kɔkɔ nyēeń Juuda yab timmun ki dòoń ki jáaḿ-mee. Tibɔti tin kɔkɔ m tīī-si mara á tùkù-bee, dūú tùkù-bi, á taa báĺ-bi báà tiba. 3An yaa yíì bi làá pīlifiǹ-si ní báà ŋma ń fá u-bimbikpitim. Bi-tuŋkpitiŋ puee, m bàà lēē kí dū nnaabu kí tɔ̄ bi-pu. Ama bi yaa pílifì, m làá kpántí m-landɔkɔŋu. 4Á dāá tùkù-bi yii, ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Nín̄ nóómaan marab bin m tīī-nee. 5Ní pīlifìmaan m-tɔntɔnliibi m-bɔnaatiliibi. M pée tūǹ-bi ni-cee ní kaa gbèentí ama ní naa pílifíǹ-bi. 6Ni yaa kaa pílifèe, m làá wīī kunimbɔtidii nee kii m nín nìn wīī Siiloo yɔkɔ puee. Niinee atimbun ŋin kɔkɔ bí duulinyanee poonee, m làá dū Jeerusaleem ní kí ŋá ŋabika bí nīn cáa tòó tɔb mbusu.>»
7Bisaraaŋaliibi nì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi nì samaa kɔkɔ gbìl̄ tibɔti tin Yeereemii sòon̄ kunimbɔtidii cindinee. 8Yeereemii nín sòon̄ tin kɔkɔ ti-Dindaan tīī-u mara ú sòoǹee ní bisaraaŋaliibi nì bibɔnaatiliibi nì samaa kɔkɔ cúú-u ní ki bí yii: «A máaǹ ŋkúm! 9A cáá dipɔbil ki nāatì ti-Dindaan bɔti yii: <Bi làá wīī kunimbɔtidii nee kii Siiloo yɔkɔee! Bi làá kpēelikì Jeerusaleem tiŋki ní ubɔ ń taa nín̄ gíti kóò ki-ni!»
Ní bin kɔkɔ nìn bí kunimbɔtidiinee kóoǹ ki múkuǹ Yeereemii pu. 10Juuda yab kàliŋkpilib nín gbìl̄ an bɔtee, ní bi yíkì dibeecindi ki nín cá kunimbɔtidii laŋki. Míǹ boonee ní bi kóoǹ ki kpáfì kunimbɔtidii punyɔkɔki Kipɔŋ nyɔkɔpu. 11Niinee ní bisaraaŋaliibi nì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi bí bikàliŋkpilib nì samaa kɔkɔ yii: «Kijapaai nee máaǹ ŋkúm, di sá yii u sòon̄ ki tɔ́ Jeerusaleem pu, nimbi ni-ba tafal gbìl̄ míǹ.»
12Ama ní Yeereemii bí bikàliŋkpilibee nì samaa kɔkɔ yii: «An sá ti-Dindaan di túnní-mi ḿ dāá sòoǹ tin ni gbìl̄ nee kí tɔ̄ kunimbɔtidii nee nì Jeerusaleem tiŋki pu. 13Kɔŋkɔnnee, ní kpántí ni-bimbim kí nīn ŋáań min kítèe, kí pīlifì ni-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nyɔkɔ. Niinee u làá kpántí u-landɔkɔŋu. Waa làá ti dū nnaabu kí tɔ̄ ni-pu kii u nín sòon̄ puee. 14Mamee, m bí ni-ŋaan. Ŋámaan-mi min ni ká yii an máaǹee. 15Ama ni máaǹ kí béé yii nimbi nì Jeerusaleem tiŋki nì ki-nib yaa kūū-mee, maanyiiba fatikuu kpuulool làá lítí ni-pu. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan di lafun túnní-mi ni-cee ḿ sòoǹ nì ni tibɔti nee kɔkɔ ní gbìl̄.»
16Niinee ní bikàliŋkpilib nì samaayee bí bisaraaŋaliibi nì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi yii: «Kijapaai nee kaa máaǹ ŋkúm, di sá yii tin ti-Dindaan tùkū-uee ní u dūu nāatì-ti.»
17Míǹ boonee ní bitindaŋkpilib kansikin biba yíkì ki bí samaa kɔkɔ yii: 18«Ŋyunti ŋun Eeseekiyaasi nìn sá Juuda bɔtiuee, Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu ubɔ nìn bí bi yíì-u Miisee, u sá Mooreeseeti tiŋkin. U nín tùkū Juuda nibul kɔkɔ puee sɔ̀. Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé:
<Siiyɔn tiŋki làá dāá kpántí kii bukpaa bun bi kùn̄ee ní,
Jeerusaleem làá dāá kpántí adigbun ŋma,
ní kunimbɔtidii gbantaŋki ń kpántí kimɔgbaai.>
19Mimmee Juuda bɔtiu Eeseekiyaasi nì Juuda yab nìn kūū Miiseeee? Aayee, ama bi nìn fāŋkì ti-Dindaan ní ki nìn pɔ́ɔǹ kí ŋá min fáatiǹ-uee. Niinee ní ti-Dindaan nìn yāntì kaa ti cáań nnaabu ŋun u nìn sòon̄ kí cáań kí tɔ̄ bi-puee. Too timbi yaa kūū uninja nee, timbi ti-ba ní ti làá ŋá tikpitil.»
Yooyakiim yāntì bi kūū Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Uriya
20Ŋyunti gbantee, uninja ubɔ mun nìn bí ki sá Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu ki nàatī ti-Dindaan bɔti. Úǹ di nìn sá Seemayawuu jipɔɔn Uriya. U nìn sá Kiiriyati-Yeeyariim tiŋkin ní. U mun nìn sòoǹ ki tòó Jeerusaleem tiŋki nì Juuda nibul pu kii Yeereemii nín nìn ŋáań puee ní deedee. 21Ubɔti Yooyakiim nì u-janjakpilib kɔkɔ nì u-kàliŋkpilib nìn gbìl̄ tin Uriya sòon̄ee. Niinee ní ubɔti nyàab̄ kí kpɔ̀-u. Uriya nín gbìl̄ mimmee ní ki fāŋkì ki sáǹ ki cūtìi bál̀ Eejipiti tiŋkin. 22Ama ní ubɔti Yooyakiim dū Akibɔɔr jipɔɔn Eelnatan nì bininjab biba mun ki tú Eejipiti. 23Bi nìn cūtì Eejipiti tiŋkin ki cúuń Uriya ki cáań ubɔti cee. Yooyakiim nìn yāntì bi kūū-u, ní ki yāntì bi dū u-wunti ki tɔ́ mbòó ŋun poon bi síb̀ báà ŋmee.
24Ama Safan jipɔɔn Ayiikaam nìn wúń Yeereemii pu. Úǹ puee, baa nìn dū Yeereemii ki ŋá samaa un nìn nyàab̀ kí kpɔ̀-uee ŋaan.

english_text:
Slaves of Nebuchadnezzar
1-2 Not long after Zedekiah became king of Judah, the Lord told me:
Jeremiah, make a wooden yoke with leather straps, and place it on your neck. 3Then send a message to the kings of Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyre, and Sidon. Some officials from these countries are in Jerusalem, meeting with Zedekiah. 4So have them tell their kings that I have said:
I am the All-Powerful Lord God of Israel, 5and with my power I created the earth, its people, and all animals. I decide who will rule the earth, 6-7 and I have chosen my servant King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia to rule all nations, including yours. I will even let him rule the wild animals. All nations will be slaves of Nebuchadnezzar, his son, and his grandson. Then many nations will join together, and their kings will make slaves of the Babylonians.
8This yoke stands for the power of King Nebuchadnezzar, and I will destroy any nation that refuses to obey him. Nebuchadnezzar will attack, and many will die in battle or from hunger and disease. 9You might have people in your kingdom who claim they can tell the future by magic or by talking with the dead or by dreams or messages from a god. But don't pay attention if any of them tell you not to obey Nebuchadnezzar. 10If you listen to such lies, I will have you dragged far from your country and killed. 11But if you and your nation are willing to obey Nebuchadnezzar, I will let you stay in your country, and your people will continue to live and work on their farms.
12After I had spoken to the officials from the nearby kingdoms, I went to King Zedekiah and told him the same thing. Then I said:
Zedekiah, if you and the people of Judah want to stay alive, you must obey Nebuchadnezzar and the Babylonians. 13But if you refuse, then you and your people will die from war, hunger, and disease, just as the Lord has warned. 14Your prophets have told you that you don't need to obey Nebuchadnezzar, but don't listen to their lies. 15Those prophets claim to be speaking for the Lord, but he didn't send them. They are lying! If you do what they say, he will have both you and them dragged off to another country and killed. The Lord has spoken.
16When I finished talking to the king, I told the priests and everyone else that the Lord had said:
Don't listen to the prophets when they say that very soon the Babylonians will return the things they took from my temple. Those prophets are lying! 17If you choose to obey the king of Babylonia, you will live. But if you listen to those prophets, this whole city will be nothing but a pile of rubble.
18If I really had spoken to those prophets, they would know what I am going to do. Then they would be begging me not to let everything else be taken from the temple and the king's palace and the rest of Jerusalem. 19-21After all, when Nebuchadnezzar took King Jehoiachin to Babylonia as a prisoner, he didn't take everything of value from Jerusalem. He left the bronze pillars, the huge bronze bowl called the Sea, and the movable bronze stands in the temple, and he left a lot of other valuable things in the palace and in the rest of Jerusalem.
But now I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, say that all these things 22will be taken to Babylonia, where they will remain until I decide to bring them back to Jerusalem. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
Yeereemii dū diwaŋgul ki páaǹ u-gbigbipati pu
1Joosiyaasi jipɔɔn Seedeesiyasi, Juuda bɔtiu beel kíltam ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì man Yeereemii tibɔti nee. 2Ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: «Nyàab̀ iŋmii nì idɔ kí bóob́ kii bi nín bōob̀ pu kí dūú kpàl̄ inaa in kù tikpaalee. Míǹ boonee, á dūú páań a-gbigbipati pu. 3A yaa ŋá míǹ ki dóòyee, á dūú tīī ituun in Eedoom yab bɔtiu nì Moowaab yab bɔtiu nì Amɔn yab bɔtiu nì Tiir yab bɔtiu nì Siidɔn yab bɔtiu túnní Jeerusaleem bi dɔ́miń Juuda bɔtiu Seedeesiyasi ceeyee. 4Á tīī-bi mara bí cùú tùkù bi-kpilib yii ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sèé:
5«Man di náań kitiŋ nì binib nì tiwaŋkuti tin bí kitiŋ puee. M dū m-pɔŋkpaaŋŋu nì m-kpabil ní ki náań tíǹ kɔkɔ ní ki tìì un ní m yaa lèe. 6Kɔŋkɔnnee, m lēē kí dū ntimu kɔkɔ kí ŋá m-tɔntɔnliu Neebukadineesaar, Babiloon yab bɔtiu ŋaan. Áli gba m dū ipeel ki ŋá u-ŋaan í nīn bí u-tundin. 7Atimbun kɔkɔ làá dāá nīn bí u nì u-jipɔɔn nì u-naantiiu taapu, kí tin sāā ŋyunti ŋun ní úǹ u-ba tiŋki làá dāá sìntī kí nīn bí atimbun ŋin pɔ̄ɔǹ-kèe nì bibɔtikpaambi taapuee.
8«Ditimbundi diba àá dibeel diba yaa yíì kaa sīntì di-ba ki tīī Neebukadineesaar, Babiloon bɔtiu, kaa dū u-kpancikiliu ki léeǹee, m làá dū kujaau nì ŋkùm nì bìlbil kúm ní kí tɔ̄ di-pu. M làá dī Babiloon bɔtiu pu ní kí nàan̄ ditimbundi gbanti, man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ.
9«Míǹ puee, nimbi ń taa pīlifì ni-bɔnaatiliibi nì ni-bɔɔbi nì bin lèekī tidamintiil taapuee nì bin kpèé kutagbɔŋu ki būū tibɔɔlee nì bikpaŋkpantiibi. Bi tùkù-ni yii ni kpá kí kɔ́ Babiloon bɔtiu taapu. 10Ama tin bi nàatī-nee sá tinyimɔmbɔti ní. Ni yaa pílifiǹ-bee, bi làá jà-ni ní búntí kí wàatī ni-tiŋki. Tiŋman ní, m làá jà-ni ní yàl̄ kí túĺ an kɔkɔ pu, ní kí kpú.
11«Ama ditimbundi diba yab yaa kíí ki sīntì biba taapu ki tīī Babiloon bɔtiu ki fōō u-kpancikiliu ki léeǹee, m làá yàntī bí nīn bí bi-tiŋkin, kí kpɔ̀ ki-pu tikpaal ní kí nīn kóò ki-pu, ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.»
12«Mama Yeereemii, m sòon̄ nì Juuda bɔtiu Seedeesiyasi tibɔbaantiil gbanti. M tùkū-u yii: <Sii nì a-nibul, ní kíí kí sìntī ni-ba taapu kí nīn bí Babiloon bɔtiu taapu ní kí fōō u-kpancikiliu kí léeń. Ní sìntī ni-ba taapu kí nīn bí u nì u-nibul taapu, niinee ni làá nīn bí dimaŋfalin. 13Ba pu ní sii nì a-nibul là kujaau nì ŋkùm nì bìlbil kúm ń kpɔ̀-ni ní? Di sá yii ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ yii tin làá bàń atimbun ŋin nib kaa làá sìntī bi-ba taapu kí tīī Babiloon bɔtiuee dee. 14Ní taa pīlifiǹ bibɔnaatiliibi bin lì-ni yii ni kpá kí kɔ́ Babiloon bɔtiu ŋaanee. Tin bi sòoǹ nì nee sá tinyimɔmbɔti ní.> 15Ti-Dindaan bí yii: <Man kaa túnní-bi. Bi lì yii bi nàatī m-bɔti, ama an sá inyimɔn ní. Ni yaa pílifiǹ-bee, m làá jà-ni doo, ní ni nì bibɔnaatiliibi bin nàatī an bɔtee ń kpú.>»
16Yeereemii nìn gíti sòon̄ nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì bin kɔkɔ nìn bí niinee. U nìn bí-bi yii: «Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Ní taa pīlifì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi bin bí ki nàatī-ni yii an kaa ti làá yúntí bi làá gíiǹní tiwan tin bi nìn yōoǹ kunimbɔtidiin ki cáa cūnnì Babiloon tiŋkinee. Tin bi sòoǹee sá inyimɔn ní. 17Ní taa pīlifiǹ-bi, sìntīmaan ni-ba taapu kí tīī Babiloon bɔtiu ní kí nīn bí dimaŋfalin. Ba pu ní ni làá yàntī kitiŋ nee ń kpántí adigbun ŋma ní?>»
18«Binib gbanti yaa lafun sá Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi, bi yaa lafun nàatī ti-Dindaan bɔti, bí gbàam̀ ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan ú taa yàntī bí yòon̄ kí púntí tiwan tin kíǹ kunimbɔtidiinee nì tin bí Juuda bɔtiu beecindinee nì tin bí Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee kí cùnnì! 19Di sá yii ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan sòon̄ jaantalkub nì kusampeekpaaŋŋu nì tin pu ku tɔ́kɔ́ee nì tiwammɔntiil tin kíǹ ki bí Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee pu. 20Di sá yii Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar kaa nìn yōoǹ tiwan kɔkɔ Jeerusaleem ki cūnnì Babiloon tiŋkin ŋyunti ŋun u nìn cúú Yooyakiim jipɔɔn Yeekooniya nì Juuda bɔtiu nì Juuda timmu nì Jeerusaleem tiŋki bɔtibiliŋee. 21Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ tiwammɔntiil tin kíǹ kunimbɔtidiin nì Juuda bɔtiu beecindin nì Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee puee sèé: 22<Bi làá yòon̄ tiwan gbanti kɔkɔ kí cùnnì Babiloon tiŋkin. Tì làá nīn bí niin kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋun ní m làá dāá tɔ̄ m-tundi kí gíiǹní-tèe.>» Ti-Dindaan di sòon̄ míǹ.

english_text:
Jeremiah Accuses Hananiah of Being a False Prophet
1 Later that same year, in the fifth month of the fourth year that Zedekiah was king, the prophet Hananiah son of Azzur from Gibeon came up to me in the temple. And while the priests and others in the temple were listening, 2he told me that the Lord had said:
I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, and I will smash the yoke that Nebuchadnezzar put on the necks of the nations to make them his slaves. 3And within two years, I will bring back to Jerusalem everything that he took from my temple and carried off to Babylonia. 4King Jehoiachin and the other people who were taken from Judah to Babylonia will be allowed to come back here as well. All this will happen because I will smash the power of the king of Babylonia!
5The priests and the others were still standing there, so I said:
6Hananiah, I hope the Lord will do exactly what you said. I hope he does bring back everything the Babylonians took from the temple, and that our people who were taken to Babylonia will be allowed to return home. 7But let me remind you and everyone else 8that long before we were born, prophets were saying powerful kingdoms would be struck by war, disaster, and disease. 9Now you are saying we will have peace. We will just have to wait and see if that is really what the Lord has said.
10Hananiah grabbed the wooden yoke from my neck and smashed it. 11Then he said, “The Lord says this is the way he will smash the power Nebuchadnezzar has over the nations, and it will happen in less than two years.”
I left the temple, 12and a little while later, the Lord told me 13-14to go back and say to Hananiah:
I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. You smashed a wooden yoke, but I will replace it with one made of iron. I will put iron yokes on all the nations, and they will have to do what King Nebuchadnezzar commands. I will even let him rule the wild animals.
15-16Hananiah, I have never sent you to speak for me. And yet you have talked my people into believing your lies and rebelling against me. So now I will send you—I'll send you right off the face of the earth! You will die before this year is over.
17Two months later, Hananiah died.
translation_text:
Yeereemii nì Ananiya bɔti
1Dibimbaantiil gbanti poon, an dàkà yii Juuda bɔtiu Seedeesiyasi nín kāl̀ dibeel dibinnanaatiil poon uŋmaŋmooŋmooti poonee ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Ananiya, Asuur jipɔɔn un sá Gabawɔn tiŋkinee nìn bí kunimbɔtidiin. U nìn kíĺ ki bíi sòoǹ nì Yeereemii nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì samaa kɔkɔ nimbiin. U nìn bí yii: 2«Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <M làá léetí-ni kpancikil un Babiloon bɔtiu léeǹ-nee. 3Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar nìn yōoǹ kunimbɔtidii poon wanti ki cūnnì Babiloon tiŋkin. Too an kíǹ abin ali deedee m làá fàtīí gíiǹní tiwan gbanti doo. 4M làá fàtīí gíiǹní Juuda bɔtiu Yeekooniya, Yooyakiim jipɔɔn doo, ki kpáaǹ bin kɔkɔ bi cúú ki cūnnì Babiloon tiŋkin kuyuŋuee, man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ. Tiŋman, m làá léetí kpancikil un Babiloon bɔtiu dūu léeǹ-nee.>»
5Niinee ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii kíí Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Ananiya nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì bin kɔkɔ nìn bí kunimbɔtidiinee nimbiin yii: 6«Ameeni! Ti-Dindaan ń ŋá kii a nín dá láá nāatì tin nee kí gíiǹní kunimbɔtidiin wanti tin kɔkɔ bi yōoǹee nì bin kɔkɔ bi cúú ki cūnnì Babiloon tiŋkin kuyuŋuee doo. 7Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, sii nì samaa kɔkɔ ń pīlifì tibɔti tin m làá sòoǹ nee tiŋan. 8Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi nìn bí an yúntì ki wāatì ní man nì sii dāa nín dɔ́miń. Bi nìn nāatì Unimbɔti bɔti ki tùkū ntimu tikpil nì abeekpaan nib. Bi nìn sòon̄ nì bi kujaau nì nnaabu nì bìlbil kúm pu. 9Ama Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu ubɔ yaa nāatì yii ŋgbansɔŋfi làá nīn bée, mana ní bi ŋūǹ kí béé yii ti-Dindaan di lafun túnní-u? See tin u sòon̄ee yaa láa ŋá mimmee ní bí béé.»
10Niinee ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Ananiya cúú kpancikil un Yeereemii nìn lée ki léetì ki gbáń ki wīī. 11Míǹ boonee ní u bí samaa kɔkɔ yii ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «Abin ali deedeeyee, m làá cúú kpancikil un Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar dūu léeǹ atimbun kɔkɔee kí léetí.>»
Niinee ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii búntì u-laŋki.
12Ananiya nín léetì Yeereemii neen kpancikil ki gbáń ki wīīyee boon ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Yeereemii yii: 13«Cùú tùkù Ananiya yii: <Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. A gbáń ki wīī idɔ kpancikiliu. Too tikúti kpancikiliu ní a làá dūú téeǹ u-yil.>» 14Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «M làá dū tikúti kpancikiliu ní kí léeń atimbun nee kɔkɔ. Niinee bi làá nīn bí Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar taapu kí nīn sá u-tɔntɔnliibi. M làá dū ipeel gba kí ŋá u-ŋaan.»
15Míǹ boonee ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii bí Ananiya yii: «Ananiya, á pīlifì tiŋan! Ti-Dindaan kaa túnní-si ní a bí ki kíiĺ samaa nee bí fōō tinyimɔmbɔti kí kíí. 16An pu ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ yii: <M làá jà-si kitiŋ nee pu. A làá kpú dun bindi, di sá yii a téé samaa bí já nì ti-Dindaan.>»
17Ní Ananiya lafun kpíì dibindi gbanti ŋmaluluútiu poon.

english_text:
Jeremiah's Letter to the People of Judah in Babylonia
1-2 I had been left in Jerusalem when King Nebuchadnezzar took many of the people of Jerusalem and Judah to Babylonia as prisoners, including King Jehoiachin, his mother, his officials, and the metal workers and others in Jerusalem who were skilled in making things. So I wrote a letter to the priests, the prophets, the leaders, and the rest of our people in Babylonia. 3I gave the letter to Elasah and Gemariah, two men that King Zedekiah of Judah was sending to Babylon to talk with Nebuchadnezzar. In the letter, I wrote 4that the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, had said:
I had you taken from Jerusalem to Babylonia. Now I tell you 5to settle there and build houses. Plant gardens and eat what you grow in them. 6Get married and have children, then help your sons find wives and help your daughters find husbands, so they can have children as well. I want your numbers to grow, not to get smaller.
7Pray for peace in Babylonia and work hard to make it prosperous. The more successful that nation is, the better off you will be.
8-9Some of your people there in Babylonia are fortunetellers, and you have asked them to tell you what will happen in the future. But they will only lead you astray with their dreams. And don't let the prophets fool you, either. They speak in my name, but they are liars. I have not spoken to them.
10 After Babylonia has been the strongest nation for 70 years, I will be kind and bring you back to Jerusalem, just as I have promised. 11I will bless you with a future filled with hope—a future of success, not of suffering. 12You will turn back to me and ask for help, and I will answer your prayers. 13 You will worship me with all your heart, and I will be with you 14and accept your worship. Then I will gather you from all the nations where I scattered you, and you will return to Jerusalem.
15You feel secure, because you think I have sent prophets to speak for me in Babylonia.
16-19But I have been sending prophets to the people of Judah for a long time, and the king from David's family and the people who are left in Jerusalem and Judah still don't obey me. So I, the Lord All-Powerful, will keep attacking them with war and hunger and disease, until they are as useless as rotten figs. I will force them to leave the land, and all nations will be disgusted and shocked at what happens to them. The nations will sneer and make fun of them and use the names “Judah” and “Jerusalem” as curse words.
And you have not obeyed me, even though 20I had you taken from Jerusalem to Babylonia. But you had better listen to me now. 21-23You think Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah are prophets because they claim to speak for me. But they are lying! I haven't told them anything. They are also committing other horrible sins in your community, such as sleeping with the wives of their friends. So I will hand them over to King Nebuchadnezzar, who will put them to death while the rest of you watch. And in the future, when you want to put a curse on someone, you will say, “I pray that the Lord will kill you in the same way the king of Babylonia burned Zedekiah and Ahab to death!”
A Message for Shemaiah
24-25The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, told me what would happen to Shemaiah, who was one of our people in Babylonia. After my letter reached Babylonia, Shemaiah wrote letters to the people of Jerusalem, including the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah, and the other priests. The letter to Zephaniah said:
26After the death of Jehoiada the priest, the Lord chose you to be the priest in charge of the temple security force. You know that anyone who acts crazy and pretends to be a prophet should be arrested and put in chains and iron collars. 27Jeremiah from the town of Anathoth is pretending to be a prophet there in Jerusalem, so why haven't you punished him? 28He even wrote a letter to the people here in Babylonia, saying we would be here a long time. He told us to build homes and to plant gardens and grow our own food.
29When Zephaniah received Shemaiah's letter, he read it to me. 30Then the Lord told me what to write in a second letter 31to the people of Judah who had been taken to Babylonia. In this letter, I wrote that the Lord had said:
I, the Lord, have not chosen Shemaiah to be one of my prophets, and he has misled you by telling lies in my name. 32He has even talked you into disobeying me. So I will punish Shemaiah. He and his descendants won't live to see the good things I will do for my people. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
Yeereemii ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu ki tīī bin bí kuyuŋunee
1Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii kāl̀ Jeerusaleem ki ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu ki tīī bitindaŋkpilib nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi nì binib bin kɔkɔ Neebukadineesaar nìn cúú Jeerusaleem ki cūnnì kuyuŋu Babiloon tiŋkinee. 2Bíǹ di sá ubɔti Yeekooniya nì ubɔti na nì ubɔti kàliŋkpaambi nì Juuda nì Jeerusaleem kpilib nì bicaabi nì ŋŋal pu tɔntɔnliibi. 3Yeereemii nìn dū kugbɔŋuee ki ŋúbiǹ Safan jipɔɔn Eeleeyasa nì Ilikiya jipɔɔn Geemariya. Di sá yii Juuda bɔtiu Seedeesiyasi nìn tú-bi Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar cee. Tin bi nìn ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu gbanti poonee sèé: 4«Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu di bíi sòoǹ nì bin kɔkɔ u yāntì bi cúú Jeerusaleem ki cūnnì Babiloon tiŋkin kuyuŋuee. 5Māmaan adiin kí nīn kóò. Kpɔ̀maan akpaan kí lēē tijikaal kí jī. 6Ní cáá binimpoobi kí màal̀ mbininjabiyaamu nì nnimpubiyaamu. Ní cáá binimpoobi kí tīī ni-jipɔmbi, kí dū ni-bisalib kí pɔ̄ ticati bí màal̀ mbiyaamu. Ní màal̀ kí bùtī niin, ni-wíiŋŋu ń taa bàtī. 7Ní nyàab̀maan kitiŋ kin poon ti-Dindaan jìn̄-ni ki kɔ́ǹee nyɔkɔpu cùtam, di sá yii kitiŋ gbanti yaa bí ŋgbansɔŋfinee, ni mun làá nīn bí ŋgbansɔŋfin.
8«Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu gíti bí yii: <Ní taa yàntī Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi bin bí ni-kansikinee ń kīil̀-ni, kí taa pīlifiǹ ni-bɔɔbi nì bin lèekī ni-damintiiti taapu ki tùkù-nee. 9Bi lì yii bi nàatī m-bɔti ní, ama an sá nnyimɔn ní. Maa tú-bi.> Ti-Dindaan di sòon̄ míǹ.
10«Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Babiloon beel yaa láa ŋá abin imuŋku ita nì saalaayee, m làá dāá sɔ̄ ni-saai. M nín nìn pōoǹ-ni dipoommɔntiil diŋyee, m làá dāá ŋá míǹ. M làá dāá fàtīí gíiǹní-ni Jeerusaleem doo. 11Man ni-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M nyí tin m bɔ́ntì kí ŋá kí tīī-nee. Maa bɔ́ntì nnaabu kí tīī-ni, ama an sá nnaam ní m bɔ́ntì kí tīī-ni. M bɔ́ntì ni-foolbooŋwu ń nīn ŋān̄ nì dimákal poon. 12Niinee, ni làá dāá dāan̄ kí yíiń-mi kí mèè-mi, ní ḿ dāá pīlifiǹ-ni. 13Ni làá dāá nyàab̄-mi ní kí dāá ká-mi, di sá yii ni làá dāá nyàab̀-mi nì ni-pɔbil kɔkɔ ní. 14M làá dāá yàntī ní ká-mi, ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ. M làá dāá gíiǹní bin bi cúú ki cūnnì kuyuŋuee ní kí dāá kóoǹ-ni kí kpāfì atimbun nì ipaan in kɔkɔ pu m jìn̄-ni ki kɔ́ǹee, ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ. M làá fàtīí gíiǹní-ni mpaan ŋun pu m nìn jìn̄-ni ki cūnnì kuyuŋu nee.>
15«Ti-Dindaan bíi sòoǹ nì ni míǹ, di sá yii ni lì yii: <Ti-Dindaan tīī-ti Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi Babiloon tiŋkin doo.>
16«Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ tin ubɔti un kā Daafiidi beejal pu puee sɔ̀. U nìn sòon̄ tibɔbaantiil gbanti bin kɔkɔ dáá gbíntìi kóò Jeerusaleem, ni-nabiyaamu mun baa cúú ki cūnnì kuyuŋu kii nimbee pu. 17Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <M làá cáań kujaau nì ŋkùm nì bìlbil kúm kí tɔ̄ bi-pu. M làá yàntī bí kpántí kii fiigi biliŋ ŋin sūū ki bíil̀ unil kaa ti ŋūǹ kí ŋmɔ́ee ní. 18M làá dāá dū kujaau nì ŋkùm nì bìlbil kúm ní kí jà-bi. Kitiŋ pu beeŋi nib yaa láa ká-bee, bi làá dāá kɔ́ dinyoondin ní. Ntimu mun kɔkɔ poon m làá dāá jà-bi kí kɔ́ǹee, bi yaa làá dāá tɔ̄ ubɔ mbusu àá kí sòoǹ kubɔbiiu kubɔ pu àá tibɔti tin cáá tifaandee pu àá kí kɔ́ǹ ubɔ icooyee, bíǹ ní bi làá dāá yòon̄ ŋabika. 19Kun pu tíǹ làá bàń-bee di sá yii baa pílifì m-bɔti, man bi-Dindaan di lī míǹ. Nì min kɔkɔ m tú m-tɔntɔnliibi m-bɔnaatiliibi kaa gbēeǹee, baa pílifiǹ-bi, man bi-Dindaan di sòon̄ míǹ.>
20«Nimbi bin m jìn̄ Jeerusaleem ki tɔ́ Babiloon tiŋkin kuyuŋuee, ní pīlifì man ni-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi.
21«Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ tin Koolaya jipɔɔn Akaab nì Maaseeyawuu jipɔɔn Seedeesiyasi pu puee sɔ̀. Bi-liitil lì yii bi nàatī ti-Dindaan bɔti ní, ama an kaa sá míǹ. Míǹ puee, m làá dū-bi kí ŋá Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar ŋaan ú yàntī bí kpɔ̀-bi ni-nimbilaaliyin. 22Juuda yab bin kɔkɔ bi cúú ki cūnnì Babiloon tiŋkin kuyuŋuee yaa làá dāá tɔ̄ ubɔ mbusuee, binib bili gbanti yiŋŋi ní bi làá nīn cáa tòó mbusu. Bi làá dāá nīn lì yii: <Ti-Dindaan ń ŋá-si kii u nín nìn ŋá Seedeesiyasi nì Akaab pu ki yāntì bi wùn̄-bi ŋŋmee!> 23Tíǹ bāań-bi kun puee bi ŋá ntimbiil tuuŋŋi Isirayeel tiŋkin ki dōoǹ nì bi-jutiibi nimpoobi. Bi nìn lì yii bi nàatī m-bɔti ama ní an kaa sá míǹ, di sá yii maa nìn tīī-bi mara bí ŋá míǹ. M nyí tíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ ní ki sá useeradaan», man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ.
Kugbɔŋu kun Seemayawuu ŋmàn̄ee
24Á sòoǹ nì Seemayawuu un sá Neelam tiŋkinee mun yii 25ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. A gāā a-bindi ki ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu ki tīī Jeerusaleem yab kɔkɔ nì usaraaŋakpil Seefaniya, Maaseeyawuu jipɔɔn nì bisaraaŋaliibi bin kɔkɔ kíǹee yii: 26«Ti-Dindaan di lēē-si á nīn sá usaraaŋakpil kí fōō Yooyadaa yil. Á nīn kpèé kunimbɔtidii poon biwaatiibi bin yíì bi-ba Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibee. Á bóob́-bi ikusaka ní kí bā-bi abaa. 27Ba pu ní aa wòon̄ Yeereemii uanatootija un bí ni-kansikin ki nàatī-ni Unimbɔti bɔtee? 28U ŋmàn̄-ti kugbɔŋu ki tīiń-ti Babiloon doo yii: Ni làá kàl̄ niin kí yúntí. An puee, māmaan adiin kí nīn kóò, kí kpɔ̀maan akpaan kí lēē tijikaal kí jī.»
29Ama usaraaŋakpil Seefaniya kàan̄ kugbɔŋu gbanti ki tùkū Yeereemii. 30Niinee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Yeereemii yii: 31«Á tɔ̄ bí cùú tùkù bin kɔkɔ bi cúú ki cūnnì kuyuŋuee yii: <Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ Seemayawuu uneelamja puee sɔ̀. Seemayawuu nāatì-ni m-bɔti, ama maa túnní-u ni-cee. U dū tinyimɔmbɔti ní ki sɔ̄ŋkì ni-pɔbil. 32Too man ni-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M làá dáaĺ Seemayawuu uneelamja nì u-biyaamu nì u-naantiibi tafal. U-dicaŋkun yab ubɔ kpá kí ká tiŋan tin m làá ŋá m-nibulee. Di sá Seemayawuu lūkutì m-nibul yab bí já nì mi. Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee dee.>»

english_text:
The Lord Will Rescue Israel and Judah
1-2The Lord God of Israel said, “Jeremiah, get a scroll and write down everything I have told you. 3Someday I will let my people from both Israel and Judah return to the land I gave their ancestors.”
4-5Then the Lord told me to say to Israel and Judah:
Screams of terror are heard,
with no word of peace.
6Can men give birth?
Then why do I see them
looking so pale
and clutching their stomachs
like women in labor?
7My people, soon you will suffer
worse than ever before,
but I will save you.
8Now you are slaves
of other nations,
but I will break the chains
and smash the yokes
that keep you in slavery.
9Then you will be my servants,
and I will choose a king for you
from the family of David.
* 10 Israel, you belong to me,
so don't be afraid.
You deserved to be punished;
that's why I scattered you
in distant nations.
But I am with you,
and someday I will destroy
those nations.
11Then I will bring you
and your descendants
back to your land,
where I will protect you
and give you peace.
Then your fears will be gone.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Lord Will Heal Israel and Judah
12The Lord said:
My people, you are wounded
and near death.
13You are accused of a crime
with no one to defend you,
and you are covered with sores
that no medicine can cure.
* 14Your friends have forgotten you;
they don't care anymore.
Even I have acted like an enemy.
And because your sins
are horrible and countless,
I will be cruel
as I punish you.
15So don't bother to cry out
for relief from your pain.
16But if your enemies try to rob
or destroy you,
I will rob and destroy them,
and they will be led as captives
to foreign lands.
17No one wants you as a friend
or cares what happens to you.
But I will heal your injuries,
and you will get well.
The Lord Will Rescue Israel and Judah
18The Lord said:
Israel, I will be kind to you
and let you come home.
Jerusalem now lies in ruins,
but you will rebuild it,
complete with a new palace.
19Other nations will respect
and honor you.
Your homes will be filled
with children,
and you will celebrate,
singing praises to me.
20It will be just like old times.
Your nation will worship me,
and I will punish anyone
who abuses you.
21One of your own people
will become your ruler.
And when I invite him
to come near me
at the place of worship,
he will do so.
No one would dare to come near
without being invited.
22You will be my people,
and I will be your God.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
23I am furious!
And like a violent storm
I will strike those
who do wrong.
24I won't calm down
until I have finished
what I have decided to do.
Someday, you will understand
what I mean.
translation_text:
Unimbɔti pōoǹ Isirayeel nì Juuda yab ipoon
1Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Yeereemii yii: 2«Man ni-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Ŋmà tibɔti tin kɔkɔ m tùkū-see kí ŋá kugbɔŋun. 3Man ni-Dindaan di sòon̄ yii iwiin bí ki dòoń, m làá fàtīí gíiǹní m-nibul Isirayeel nì Juuda yab bin bi cúú ki cūnnì kuyuŋuee, man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ. M làá gíiǹní-bi kitiŋ kin m nìn dūu tīī bi-naanjabee poon bí fōō kí nīn kíǹ ki kóò.»
4Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ Isirayeel nì Juuda yab pu tiŋyee sɔ̀. 5Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ yii:
«Bi gbìl̀ dipɔɔbiildi biilii pu,
an sá dinyoondi ní, kaa sá ŋgbansɔŋfi.
6Ní bàlifì binib kí kpèèmaan,
uninja màal̀ kibikaaa?
Ama m wāĺ bininjab kɔkɔ
yú ki nyīī bi-cammu kii
unimpu di kā imatiŋween puee.
Ba pu ní binib kpèé fáaa míǹ?
7Mbusu! Díǹ wiiŋŋu nee sá ŋwiŋkpaan ní,
ŋwiin nee ŋúǹ kaa cáá juti.
An sá dinimbinaamandi wiiŋŋu
ní ki tīī Jaakɔb naantiibi,
ama bi làá dāá ŋmátí.»
*
8«Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Ŋyunti yaa láa bàn̄ee, m làá dāá léetí bi-neen kpancikiliu. Niinee baa dāa gíti sá binicambi yumbui. 9Ama bi làá dāá nīn sá man bi-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu nì Daafiidi un m làá dāá dūú kàan̄ bi-pu ubɔtee tɔntɔnliibi.»
*
10Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé:
«M-tɔntɔnliu Isirayeel, taa fàŋkì.
Sii un naanja sá Jaakɔbee, taa kɔ́ dinyoondin!
Di sá yii m làá nyāntí-si ntindandatimu nee ni kí fīī-si,
ní kí gíiǹní a-biyaamu mun bíń kuyuŋuee.
Isirayeel, a làá fàtīí gítiń
ní kí nīn bí dipɔɔsɔŋkilin.
Ubɔ kaa dāa gíti bí kí páb́-si.
11M bí a-cee kí fīī-si,
ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.
M làá kúntí anibul ŋin cee
m nìn jìn̄-si ki kɔ́ǹee kɔkɔ.
Ama siiyee, maa làá kúntí-si.
An sá mbaamɔn yii m dáaĺ a-tafal,
ama nì deedee poon ní m ŋá míǹ.
Di sá yii maa bàà ŋūǹ kí yàntī-si
kii a sá maanyiibee.»
*
12Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé:
«Tiweendi tin a fōōyee kaa cáá dicáaǹdi,
baa ŋūǹ kí cáaǹ a-buuŋŋu.
13Ubɔ kaa bí ki mɔ́tí a-pu.
Unil yaa fōō tiweendee, bi cāantí-u ní,
ama sii ceeyee, an kaa cáá nnyɔkɔ.
14A-bɔmbi kɔkɔ súntì a-pu,
ubɔ kaa ti dàkafī a-pu.
Jeerusaleem, m fáá-si kii a sá m-nannanliuee.
M dáaĺ a-tafal ŋkpitim pu,
kun puee a-kpitii wīikí
ní a-yìntitam náaǹ.
15Ba pu ní a gbáà ibiil tiweendi tin a fōōyee pu.
A-buuŋŋu kaa cáá dicáaǹdi.
An sá a-kpitii in wīikí
nì a-yìntitam min náaǹee pu
ní m ŋá-si míǹ.
16Bin kɔkɔ cátikì-see,
bi làá cātikì bi mun.
Bi làá cúú a-nannanliibi kɔkɔ pái
kí cùnnì kuyuŋu.
Bin yùn̄-see, bi làá dāá yɔ̀ bi mun,
bin fúkúl̀-see, bi làá dāá fūkul̀-bi.
17Bi yíì-si yii <un bi jìn̄ee>,
<Siiyɔn un bɔti kaa ti ká ubɔee>.
Ama mama ni-Dindaan, m bí yii:
M làá cáaǹ tiweendi tin a fōōyee,
m làá yàntī a-buuŋyi ń kpú.
*
18Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé:
<M làá fàtīí mā Jaakɔb diiŋŋi,
m làá sɔ̄ bi-kɔŋkooŋyi saai.
Bi làá fàtīí mā ntimu mun bi nìn nāaǹee
kí tɔ́kɔń mu-digbuŋŋi pu,
ní adinyaan ń fàtīí ká ipaan in pu ŋi nìn yúee.
19Bi làá dāá gbìl̄ ilan
nì ifaal kuŋkuuntii pu bi-kansikin.
M làá dāá yàntī bí bùtī,
bi-wíiŋŋu kaa làá dāá bàtī.
Baa làá dāá gíti kpèè-bi fám,
di sá yii m làá dāá tīī-bi tinyool.
20Jaakɔb naantiibi làá dāá nīn bí kii
bi nín nìn bí pu njaminee ní.
Bi làá dāá fàtīí tí kóoǹ kí kpāfì m-nimbiin,
ní ḿ dāá jáǹ bi-wɔ́biliibi kɔkɔ.
21Ni-kansikin ubɔ di làá dāá nīn sá ni-kpiliu,
tiŋman ni-kansikin ubɔ di làá dāá kpòotī-ni.
M làá dāá pɔ̄ udaan diyimɔɔl ú sútí kí pìl̄-mi.
Di sá yii ŋma di sá-u kí sútí kí pìl̄-mi?
Ti-Dindaan di sòon̄ míǹ.
22Niinee ní ní dāá nīn sá m-nibul,
ní man ń nīn sá ni-Nimbɔtiu.>»
*
23Ti-Dindaan buŋkpaaŋku dòoń,
u-ŋuul di pōō.
Kunaakpaabuŋkpaaŋŋu bíi jītí ki fīintí
kí dāá lítí binikpitib pu,
ku bí binikpitib yiliŋ pu ki màntī.
24Ti-Dindaan yaa kaa ŋá u nín lēē kí ŋá puee,
u-ŋuul kpá kí sɔ̀ŋkì.
Boon kpataaayee, ni làá dāá gbìl̄ taapu.

english_text:
Israel Will Return to God
1The Lord said:
Israel, I promise
that someday all your tribes
will again be my people,
and I will be your God.
2In the desert I was kind
to those who escaped death.
I gave them peace,
and when the time is right,
I'll do the same for you.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Lord Will Rebuild Israel
3Some time ago, the Lord appeared to me and told me to say:
Israel, I will always love you;
that's why I've been so patient
and kind.
4You are precious to me,
and so I will rebuild
your nation.
Once again you will dance for joy
and play your tambourines.
5You will plant vineyards
on the hills of Samaria
and enjoy the grapes.
6Someday those who guard
the hill country of Ephraim
will shout, “Let's go to Zion
and worship the Lord our God.”
Israel Will Return to Its Own Land
7The Lord says:
Celebrate and sing for Israel,
the greatest of nations.
Offer praises and shout,
“Come and rescue
your people, Lord!
Save what's left of Israel.”
8I, the Lord, will bring
my people back from Babylonia
and everywhere else on earth.
The blind and the lame
will be there.
Expectant mothers
and women about to give birth
will come and be part
of that great crowd.
9They will weep and pray
as I bring them home.
I will lead them
to streams of water.
They will walk on a level road
and not stumble.
I am a father to Israel,
my favorite children.
10Listen to me, you nations
nearby or across the sea.
I scattered the people of Israel,
but I will gather them again.
I will protect them like a shepherd
guarding a flock;
11I will rescue them from enemies
who could overpower them.
12My people will come
to Mount Zion
and celebrate;
their faces will glow
because of my blessings.
I'll give them grain, grapes,
and olive oil,
as well as sheep and cattle.
Israel will be prosperous
and grow like a garden
with plenty of water.
13Young women and young men,
together with the elderly,
will celebrate and dance,
because I will comfort them
and turn their sorrow
into happiness.
14I will bless my people
with more food
than they need,
and the priests will enjoy
the choice cuts of meat.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Lord Offers Hope
15 In Ramah a voice is heard,
crying and weeping loudly.
Rachel mourns for her children
and refuses to be comforted,
because they are dead.
* 16But I, the Lord, say
to dry your tears.
Someday your children
will come home
from the enemy's land.
Then all you have done for them
will be greatly rewarded.
17So don't lose hope.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
18The people of Israel moan
and say to me,
“We were like wild bulls,
but you, Lord, broke us,
and we learned to obey.
You are our God—
please let us come home.
19When we were young,
we strayed and sinned,
but then we realized
what we had done.
We are ashamed and disgraced
and want to return to you.”
20People of Israel,
you are my own dear children.
Don't I love you best of all?
Though I often make threats,
I want you to be near me,
so I will have mercy on you.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
21With rock piles and signposts,
mark the road well,
my dear people.
The road by which you left
by will now lead you home.
22Will you ever decide
to be faithful?
I will make sure that someday
things will be different,
as different as a woman
protecting a man.
The Lord Will Bring Judah Home
