23The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, said:
I promise to set the people of Judah free and to lead them back to their hometowns. And when I do, they will once again say,
“We pray that the Lord
will bless his home,
the sacred hill in Jerusalem
where his temple stands.”
24The people will live in Jerusalem and in the towns of Judah. Some will be farmers, and others will be shepherds. 25Those who feel tired and worn out will find new life and energy, 26and when they sleep, they will wake up refreshed.
27Someday, Israel and Judah will be my field where my people and their livestock will grow. 28In the past, I took care to uproot them, to tear them down, and to destroy them. But when that day comes, I will take care to plant them and help them grow. 29 No longer will anyone go around saying,
“Sour grapes eaten by parents
leave a sour taste in the mouths
of their children.”
30When that day comes, only those who eat sour grapes will get the sour taste, and only those who sin will be put to death.
The New Agreement with Israel and Judah
31 The Lord said:
The time will surely come when I will make a new agreement with the people of Israel and Judah. 32It will be different from the agreement I made with their ancestors when I led them out of Egypt. Although I was their God, they broke that agreement.
33 Here is the new agreement that I, the Lord, will make with the people of Israel:
“I will write my laws
on their hearts and minds.
I will be their God,
and they will be my people.
34 “No longer will they have to teach one another to obey me. I, the Lord, promise that all of them will obey me, ordinary people and rulers alike. I will forgive their sins and forget the evil things they have done.”
35I am the Lord All-Powerful.
I command the sun
to give light each day,
the moon and stars
to shine at night,
and ocean waves to roar.
36I will never forget
to give those commands,
and I will never let Israel
stop being a nation.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
37Can you measure the heavens?
Can you explore
the depths of the earth?
That's how hard it would be
for me to reject Israel forever,
even though they have sinned.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
Jerusalem Will Be Rebuilt
38The Lord said:
Someday, Jerusalem will truly belong to me. It will be rebuilt with a boundary line running from Hananel Tower to Corner Gate. 39From there, the boundary will go in a straight line to Gareb Hill, then turn toward Goah. 40Even that disgusting Hinnom Valley will be sacred to me, and so will the eastern slopes that go down from Horse Gate into Kidron Valley. Jerusalem will never again be destroyed.
translation_text:
*
1Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Ŋyunti gbantee, man di làá dāá nīn sá Isirayeel dicaŋŋi kɔkɔ Nimbɔtiu, ní ŋí dāá nīn sá m-nibul.»
Isirayeel yab bin kíǹee gítintam
2Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé:
«Kuteeunee, m dàkā dinibul din
ŋmátì ki nyáń ŋkúm ŋaanee m-laŋŋaŋfitiiku.
M làá tīī Isirayeel diŋuŋfil dee.
3Dinibulee nìn lì yii:
<Doooo ndandati ní ti-Dindaan lēē u-ba ki dàkā-mi.>
Ní m kíí-u yii: <Dooooyee ní m néeń-si
ní ki làá nīn pée néeń-si.
An pu ní m dū m-ba ki nákáǹ-si kiŋkiŋ.
4Sii Isirayeel un m néeńee,
m làá fàtīí yòon̄-si kí yóoń,
ní bí fàtīí mā-si.
A làá fàtīí yòon̄ a-gaŋgammu nnyaammuee
kí cùú kūtì bin bí ki jīǹ jiŋaalee pu ní ŋɔ̄.
5A làá dāá fàtīí cóoń fiinyi sufii
Samaarii jooŋŋi pu.
Bin cóoǹ-iee di làá dāá kìtī abil.
6Di sá yii ŋwiin ŋubɔ bí ki dòoń
biciitiliibi làá dāá tɔ́kɔń
Eefiraayiim jooŋŋi pu kí téeń yii:
Yīkìmaan tí jɔ̄m̀ Siiyɔn <jool,
ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu cee.>»
7Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀.
Nín̄ tátímaan nì dipɔɔpindi kí tīī Isirayeel,
nín̄ fàal̀maan ditimbundi din tɔ́kɔ́ atimbun kɔkɔ puee.
Nín̄ gàmaan ilan mpɔn ki lì yii:
«Ti-Dindaan, fīī a-nibul,
fīī bin kíǹ Isirayeel tiŋkin ki bí dimaŋfalinee.»
8Di sá yii m làá nyāntiń-bi ŋgan pú timmun kí gíiǹní,
ní kí kóoǹní-bi ntindandatimun kí kpāfì.
Bi-kansikinee, bijɔfub nì bideembi,
bipɔdambi nì bimatimpɔmbi làá nīn bí.
An dāa sá dinikitikpaandi di làá fàtīí gítiń.
9Bi fàtīi gítiń ki sūǹ,
ní m cēentí-bi ki ŋmēentí-bi.
M làá dāá cáá-bi kí cùnnì ibun in pùub̀ee ni.
M làá dāá dū-bi kí dī nsan ŋun tèen̄ baa làá gbéetée pu.
Di sá yii m sá kii ubaatee ní ki tīī Isirayeel,
ní Eefiraayiim sá m-jipɔŋkpiliu.
*
10Nimbi atimbun, pīlifìmaan ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi.
Ní cáá-dì kí nàatī ntimu mun dátì
nnyim māntìi tú-muee ni.
Ní lì yii:
«Ti-Dindaan nìn jìn̄ Isirayeel yab bi yàl̄ ki gbí an kɔkɔ.
Kɔŋkɔnnee u kóoǹ-bi ki kpáfì,
ki wúń bi-pu kii upikpaal nín wúǹ u-piii pu puee.»
11Di sá yii ti-Dindaan fīī Isirayeel yab,
u nyántì-bi unannanli un pɔ̄ɔǹ-bee ŋaan.
12Bi làá dāá bàń Siiyɔn gbantaŋki pu
ki kūuntí dipɔɔpindi kuŋkuuntii.
Bi fāā mɔ̀ɔɔ ki cá ti-Dindaan wammɔntiiti cee,
an dàkà yii bilee nì ndapɔm nì ŋkpam
nì ipii nì iŋoobu nì inaa.
Bi làá dāá nīn bí kii bukpaa
bun bi yāaǹ nnyim tiŋanee ní.
Bi-pɔŋŋu pée gíti kpá kí bàtī.
13Niinee bisapɔmbi dāa ŋōō nì dipɔɔpindi
ní binaacimpɔmbi nì bijaŋkpilib fàal̀ dicilpu.
M làá dāá yàntī bi-nimbaaku ń kpántí-bi jiŋaal,
m làá ŋméeǹ-bi bi-nimbinaamandi poon,
ní kí yàntī bi-pɔbil ń sɔ̀ŋkì.
14M làá dāá tīī bisaraaŋaliibi
tinan tin cáá ŋkpamee tikpil.
M làá dāá gbéeǹ m-nibul tiwammɔntiil,
ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.
*
15Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé:
«Bi gbìl̀ Raama tiŋkin dituweel nì nsiim pu.
An sá Raaseel di bíi sūǹ u-biyaamu pu.
Waa kíí ubɔ ń ŋméeǹ-u,
di sá yii muaa ti bí.»
16Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀.
Taa ti sɔ̄ kí yīkintì,
pítí a-nyinnyim!
Man ni-Dindaan di sòon̄ míǹ,
m làá pà a-gìńdi paati.
A-biyaamu làá nyānní
binannanliibi tiŋkin kí gítiń.
17Ti-Dindaan bí yii:
«Dimákal bí ki tīī a-naantiibi,
a-biyaamu làá fàtīí gítiń bi-tiŋkin.»
18M gbìl̄ Eefiraayiim yab yáliŋkí ki lì yii:
«Ti-Dindaan, a dáaĺ ti-tafal ŋkpitim pu
kii bi nín tìŋkī dinajapɔmbil din bɔti pɔ̄ɔ̄yee puee.
Ama á fàtīí gíiǹní-ti a-cee
tí bàà fàtīí gítiń a-cee tiŋman pu.
Di sá yii sii ti-Dindaan di sá ti-Nimbɔtiu.
19Ti nìn fātì ti-boon ki tīī-si,
ama kɔŋkɔnnee, ti kpántì ti-ba.
Ti béè ti-yìntitam,
ní ki fátí ti-biŋŋi ki yáliŋkí.
Ti fá ti-jilmau ní icoo cúú-ti gbòooo.
Tiŋman ti ŋá tin kaa kítèe ti-naacimpɔntin,
ní ki bíi fòol̄ an paati.
20Eefiraayiim di sá m-bineeŋkaaki,
m néeń-u ki jítiǹ bin kɔkɔ kíǹee.
An pu ní ŋyunti ŋun kamaa
m yaa bíi sòoǹ ki kù u-bɔtee,
m gbíntìi dàkafī u-pu.
M-pɔ̀ti kaa fù u-pu.
Maa pée ŋūǹ kí gbèen̄ kí taa sɔ̄ u-saai.»
Ti-Dindaan di sòon̄ míǹ.
*
21Cóoń kikpaanyɔkɔ taŋkpeeŋi kí nóó nì a-daanti,
cóoń tidaandi nsan pu.
Nín̄ nyí nì a-ba nì didandi din a dēe,
nì nsan ŋun a cōom̀ee.
Isirayeel un bí kii usapɔɔnee, fàtīí gítiń,
fàtīí gítiń ntimu mun sá a-yaka nee poon!
Fàtīí gítiń a-timmun.
22Usapɔɔn un gáatèe,
a làá nīn sáń ki lábití yéè kí tin sāā ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu ní?
Di sá yii ti-Dindaan náań tiwampɔn tiba kitiŋ pu:
Unimpu di làá nīn kíǹ ki mɔ̀nnì uninja.
*
Bi làá fàtīi mā Juuda nì Jeerusaleem timmu
23Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «M yaa láa fātìi gíiǹní bin bínní kuyuŋuee, bi làá dāá tí lì Juuda tiŋki nì ki-timmu pu yii:
«<Ti-Dindaan ń bìin̄ a-boon,
sii Siiyɔn gbantaŋki kin bí circiree,
laakin difiil bée.>
24«Niinee Juuda yab bin kóò tisatinee nì bin kóò ntimunee, bikpaabi nì biwaŋkpaaliibi kɔkɔ làá dāá nīn kóò kitiŋ nee pu dicilpu. 25M làá dāá tīī bin gīīyee nnyim bí nyɔ̀ ní kí tīī bin kaa ti cáá mpɔnee kunyannyaau. 26Míǹ boonee ní m fīntì ní ki ká yii ŋgeem min m gèen̄ee mɔ̄.
27«Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Iwiin iba bí ki dòoń, m làá dāá yàntī binib nì tiwaŋkuti ń kpátí kí gbí Isirayeel nì Juuda beeŋin kii iwamboolee. 28Kii m nín tāā ki bíikì bi-pu, ki fùkū, ki gāatì ki lúkú, ki kpéelikì, ki nāaǹ ní ki ŋá tikpitil puee, míǹ mbaantiim ní m làá ŋá kí tīī-bi bí fàtīí mā kí cóoń, man bi-Dindaan di lī míǹ. 29Ŋyunti gbantee, ubɔ kaa dāa gíti lì yii:
<Bibaatiibi ŋmɔ́ asubigaan,
ama mbiyaamu nyiŋŋi di nyāŋfì.>
30Un di yaa ŋmɔ́ asubigaanee, udaan nyiŋŋi di làá nyàŋfì. Un di yaa ŋá ikpitee, udaan di kúù.»
31«Ti-Dindaan di lī yii iwiin iba bí ki dòoń, m làá fàtīí pòon̄ Isirayeel nì Juuda yab dipoompɔndi. 32Díǹ kaa dāa sá kii din m nìn pōoǹ bi-naanjab ŋwiin ŋun m nìn cúú bi-ŋal ki nyántì Eejipiti tiŋkin kuyuŋunee. Nì min kɔkɔ man di nìn sá bi-Dindaanee, bi nìn kpītì dipoondi gbanti, ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.» 33Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Dipoompɔndi din m làá dāá líí Isirayeel yab ŋwiin gbantee sɔ̀. M làá dāá dū m-marab kí ŋmà kí ŋá bi-landɔkɔyin, kí ŋmà-bi kí ŋá bi-pɔbilin. Man làá dāá nīn sá bi-Nimbɔtiu ní bíǹ ń nīn sá m-nibul. 34Ubɔ kaa dāa gíti dàkà u-juti àá u-nabiki ú nīn nyí ti-Dindaan. Di sá yii kí yòon̄ bi-kansikin mbiyaawaamu kí tin cáá sāā bikpaambee, báà ŋma làá dāá béé-mi, man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ. Di sá yii m làá dāá dū bi-kpitii kí pɔ̄-bi ní kaa làá ti téetí bi-yìntitam pu.
35Ŋma di dū ŋwìiń ki kāaǹ ŋú nīn ŋmíntí ŋwiimpu ní?
Ŋma di tīī uŋmal nì iŋmalbijaa mara í nīn ŋmíntí kunyeeu ní?
Ŋma di kùtī tiŋku ní ki yàntī
u-nyiŋgbanti yíkí ki gà kuwoou ní?
An sá ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan.
U-yindi dee.»
36Ti-Dindaan bí yii:
«Daliŋkin ní m yaa kíí yii
marab bin kpòotī duulinya nee kaa ti bée,
mimmee m kíí yii
Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ mun
kaa ti kpáfì ki ŋá ditimbundi dee!»
37Ti-Dindaan bí yii:
«Unil yaa ŋūǹ kí ŋmàntī kutagbɔŋu kun dàn̄ee,
ki yaa tí ŋūǹ kí béé kitiŋ nyóoŋŋuee,
mimmee ma mun làá dū Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ kí fá,
ikpiti in kɔkɔ bi ŋée pu,
ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.»
*
38Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Iwiin bí ki dòoń m làá fàtīí mā Jeerusaleem kí tīī m-ba, kí yòon̄ Ananeeyeel difɔkɔku Dikpindi punyɔkɔki. 39Bi làá dāá dū ŋŋmiiŋmantikaa kí tɔ̄ kí ŋmàntī kitiŋ kpaanyɔkɔ kí nīn cá Gareeb gbantaŋki, ní kí yòon̄ niin kí pɔ́ĺ kí nīn cá Goowa tiŋki watil pú. 40Bi làá dāá dū anikpil nì ŋfantam tantakal nì mpaan ŋun kɔkɔ dɔ̄ kí tin sāā Seedrɔn buŋŋuee nì Dikpindi punyɔkɔki kin sá Itaamu punyɔkɔki ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee kí sú-mi. Ubɔ kaa dāa gíti fùkù tiba ki dāa nín bíiĺ tiba mpaan gbanti pu.»

english_text:
Jeremiah Buys a Field
1 The Lord spoke to me in the tenth year that Zedekiah was king of Judah, which was the eighteenth year that Nebuchadnezzar was king of Babylonia. 2At that time, the Babylonian army had surrounded Jerusalem, and I was in the prison at the courtyard of the palace guards. 3Zedekiah had ordered me to be held there because I told everyone that the Lord had said:
I am the Lord, and I am about to let the king of Babylonia conquer Jerusalem. 4King Zedekiah will be captured and taken to King Nebuchadnezzar, who will speak with him face to face. 5Then Zedekiah will be led away to Babylonia, where he will stay until I am finished with him. So, if you people of Judah fight against the Babylonians, you will lose. I, the Lord, have spoken.
6Later, when I was in prison, the Lord said:
7Jeremiah, your cousin Hanamel, the son of your uncle Shallum, will visit you. He must sell his field near the town of Anathoth, and because you are his nearest relative, you have the right and the responsibility to buy it and keep it in the family.
8Hanamel came, just as the Lord had promised. And he said, “Please buy my field near Anathoth in the territory of the Benjamin tribe. You have the right to buy it, and if you do, it will stay in our family.”
The Lord had told me to buy it 9from Hanamel, and so I did. The price was 17 pieces of silver, and I weighed out the full amount on a scale. 10-11I had two copies of the bill of sale written out: an official copy containing the details of our agreement and another copy, without the details. Some witnesses and I signed the official copy, which was folded and tied, before being sealed shut with hot wax. Then I gave Hanamel the silver. 12And while he, the witnesses, and all the other Jews sitting in the courtyard were still watching, I gave both copies to Baruch son of Neriah.
13-14I told Baruch that the Lord had said:
Take both copies of this bill of sale, one sealed shut and the other open, and put them in a clay jar so they will last a long time. 15I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, and I promise you that people will once again buy and sell houses, farms, and vineyards in this country.
Jeremiah Questions the Lord
16Then I prayed:
17 Lord God, you stretched out your mighty arm and made the sky and the earth. You can do anything. 18You show kindness for a thousand generations, but you also punish people for the sins of their parents. You are the Lord All-Powerful. 19With great wisdom you make plans, and with your great power you do all the mighty things you planned. Nothing we do is hidden from your eyes, and you reward or punish us as we deserve.
20You are famous because you worked miracles in Egypt, and you are still working them in Israel and in the rest of the world as well. 21You terrified the Egyptians with your miracles, and you reached out your mighty arm and rescued your people Israel from Egypt. 22Then you gave Israel this land rich with milk and honey, just as you had promised our ancestors.
23But when our ancestors took over the land, they did not obey you. And now you have punished Israel with disaster. 24Jerusalem is under attack, and we suffer from hunger and disease. The Babylonians have already built dirt ramps up to the walls of our city, and you can see that Jerusalem will be captured just as you said.
25So why did you tell me to get some witnesses and buy a field with my silver, when Jerusalem is about to be captured by the Babylonians?
The Lord Explains about the Field
26The Lord explained:
27Jeremiah, I am the Lord God. I rule the world, and I can do anything!
28 It is true that I am going to let King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia capture Jerusalem. 29The Babylonian army is already attacking, and they will capture the city and set it on fire. The people of Jerusalem have made me angry by going up to the flat roofs of their houses and burning incense to Baal and offering wine sacrifices to other gods. Now these houses will be burned to the ground!
30-33The kings and the officials, the priests and the prophets, and everyone else in Israel and Judah have turned from me and made me angry by worshiping idols. Again and again I have tried to teach my people to obey me, but they refuse to be corrected.
I am going to get rid of Jerusalem, because its people have done nothing but evil. 34 They have set up repulsive idols in my temple, and now it isn't a fit place to worship me. 35 And they led Judah into sin by building places to worship Baal in Hinnom Valley, where they also sacrificed their sons and daughters to the god Molech. I have never even imagined they would commit such disgusting sins.
36Jeremiah, what you said is true. The people of Jerusalem are suffering from hunger and disease, and so the king of Babylonia will be able to capture Jerusalem.
37I am angry with the people of Jerusalem, and I will scatter them in foreign countries. But someday I will bring them back here and let them live in safety. 38They will be my people, and I will be their God. 39-41I will make their thoughts and desires pure. Then they will realize that, for their own good and the good of their children, they must worship only me. They will even be afraid to turn away from me. I will make an agreement with them that will never end, and I won't ever stop doing good things for them. With all my heart I promise that they will be planted in this land once again. 42Even though I have brought disaster on the people, I will someday do all these good things for them.
43Jeremiah, when you bought the field, you showed that fields will someday be bought and sold again. You say that this land has been conquered by the Babylonians and has become a desert, emptied of people and animals. 44But someday, people will again spend their silver to buy fields everywhere—in the territory of Benjamin, the region around Jerusalem and the towns of Judah, and in the hill country, the foothills to the west, and the Southern Desert. Buyers and sellers and witnesses will sign and seal the bills of sale for the fields. It will happen, because I will give this land back to my people. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
Yeereemii dá bukpaa
1Juuda bɔtiu Seedeesiyasi nín kāl̀ dibeel abin disaalaatiil poonee, Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar úǹ nìn ŋá abin saalku nì ata dee dibeel pu. Ŋyunti gbanti ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Yeereemii. 2Ŋyunti gbantee Babiloon janjaliibi nìn māntìi tú Jeerusaleem tiŋki kí já nì kì. Bi nìn cúú Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii ki pīiǹ kudii bijanjaliibi dumpu, Juuda bɔtiu beecindin. 3Juuda bɔtiu Seedeesiyasi di nìn yāntì bi pīiǹ-u niin. Di sá yii u nìn wòon̄ Yeereemii u nín nāatì ti-Dindaan bɔti yii: «M làá dū Jeerusaleem tiŋki kí ŋá Babiloon bɔtiu ŋaan ú fōō-kèe. 4Juuda bɔtiu Seedeesiyasi kaa làá ŋmátí kí nyā Babiloon yab ŋaan, di sá yii m lēē kí dū-u kí ŋá Babiloon bɔtiu ŋaan. U làá cùú yūĺ Neebukadineesaar nimbiin ní bí nīn sòoǹ ki kpèé tɔb. 5Bi làá cúú Seedeesiyasi kí cùnnì Babiloon tiŋkin, ní ú nīn bí niin kí tin sāā ŋyunti ŋun ní m làá dāá kpèè u-bɔtee, ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ. Ni yaa gbíntìi bíi jáà nì Babiloon yab, naa làá ŋmā-bi.»
6Yeereemii bí yii: «Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ nì mi puee sèé: 7<A-wee Anameeyeel, Saaluum jipɔɔn làá dāan̄ a-cee kí bí-si yii á dā u-kpaabu bun bí Anatootee. Di sá yii sii nì u di pēē. An puee, sii di cáá nsan kí dā bukpaa gbanti.>»
8Kii ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ nì mi puee, m-wee Anameeyeel nìn lafun dɔ́miń m-cee bijanjaliibi mɔŋkiŋu ki bí-mi yii: «Dā m-kpaabu bun bí Anatooti, Beenjameen tiŋkinee. Di sá yii man nì sii di pēē. Míǹ puee, mara poonee, sii di cáá nsan kí dā-bu.» Niin ní m béè yii ti-Dindaan di sòon̄ nì mi.
9Niinee ní m dá m-wee Anameeyeel kpaabu bun bí Anatooti tiŋkinee, ki pàn̄-u bukpaayee daaku nín sá puee, animbil jitɔmbi saalku nì bili. 10Ní m ŋá kugbɔŋu kun dàkà yii u nyáfiǹ-mi u-kpaabuee mili pu. M-seeradambi nimbiinee, ní m kpáb́ kugbɔŋu kun pu m nyīī m-jaliikee, ní ki ŋmāntì animbil saniya pu. 11Boonee ní m fōō kugbɔŋu kun dàkà yii m dá bukpaayee ki kpáb́ kii mara nín bí yii ḿ ŋá puee nì kun baa kpáb́ee. 12M nìn dū tigbɔnliitilee ki tīī Neeriya jipɔɔn Baruuki, Maaseeyawuu naantiiu. M-wee Anameeyeel nì biseeradambi bin nìn nyīī ŋŋal kugbɔŋuee puee, nì Juuda yab bin kɔkɔ nìn bí bijanjaliibi mɔŋkiŋuee nìn bí. 13Ní m tùkū Baruuki tibɔti nee samaa kɔkɔ nimbiin yii: 14«Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín lī puee sèé: <Yòon̄ tigbɔnliitil tin dàkà yii m dá bukpaayee, kun pu m nyīī ŋŋal ki kpáb́ee nì kun maa kpáb́ee. Á dū-tì kí ŋá diboolin kí kpāafì an nīn bí kí yúntí.>»
15«Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín lī puee sèé: <Ŋwiin bí ki dòoń, bi làá dāá fàtīí dā kitiŋ nee poon adiin nì akpaan nì fiinyi kpaaŋŋi.>»
Yeereemii wimmeem
16M nín dū tigbɔn gbanti ki tīī Neeriya jipɔɔn Baruuki ki dóòyee ní m mēē ti-Dindaan yii: 17«Too, ti-Dindaan, sii di dū a-pɔŋkpaaŋŋu nì a-kpabil ki náań kutagbɔŋu nì kitiŋ. Tiba kaa pɔ̄ɔ̄ a-cee. 18Sii di dàkà binib kulaŋŋaŋfitiiu kí tin sāā anaantitɔntɔkɔ kutuku pu. Ama bibaatiibi yaa yīntèe, bi-biyaamu tafal ní a dátí kí tɔ̀ ipɔntoon. A sá Unimbɔtikpaan, ní ki cáá mpɔn. Sii yindi di sá ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan. 19A nín lēē kí ŋá puee sá ŋkpaami ní a cáá mpɔn kí ŋá míǹ. A kpèé ki wāĺ tin kɔkɔ nnibiyaamu bí ki ŋáańee. A pà báà ŋma paati ki nóó nì u-bimbim nì u-tuuŋŋi nín sá puee ní.
20«Sii di nìn túń atuŋkpaan nì maamaacib Eejipiti tiŋkin. Áli nì díǹ, a dàkà un ní a sée Isirayeel nibul nì inifunaan kɔkɔ kansikin, kii an nín bí pu díǹ nee ní. 21A nìn túń atuŋkpaan nì maamaacib ki dàkā mpɔŋkpaan nì dikpabil ki nyántì a-nibul Isirayeel Eejipiti tiŋkin. 22A nìn pūtì ki pōoǹ ti-naanjab yii a làá dū kitiŋ kin poon nnaabiim nì tisiil pùub̀ee kí tīī-bi ní a lafun ŋá míǹ. 23Bi nìn lafun kɔ́ ki fōō kitiŋ gbanti ki kāl̀. Ama baa pílifiǹ-si, kaa nóó a-dàkatam, kaa tɔ́ a-marab. Niinee ní a yāntì inaabu in kɔkɔ bíi bàń-ti díǹ nee jéetì bi-pu.
24«Kɔŋkɔnnee, Babiloon yab dɔ́miń ki gūū kitiŋee ki bíl̀ ataŋkpuku kí fōō-kì. Bi bíi jáà nì kì ní kì làá pée kɔ́ bi-ŋaan ní kujaau nì ŋkùm nì bìlbil kúm pu. Tin a nìn sòon̄ ki síiǹee bāań ní sii a-ba wāĺ míǹ. 25Too, Jeerusaleem làá kɔ́ bi-ŋaan dee! Kin ba pu ní a tīī-mi mara yii ḿ dā bukpaa Anatooti kí pà biseeradambi nimbiin?»
Ti-Dindaan kíí Yeereemii tibɔti
26Ní ti-Dindaan kíí Yeereemii yii: 27«Man di sá tin kɔkɔ cáá kufoouee Nimbɔtiu. Tiba bí ki pɔ̄ɔ̄ ki jítiǹ-maaa? 28An pu ní man ni-Dindaan bí yii m làá dū kitiŋ nee kí ŋá Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar nì u-janjaliibi ŋaan. U làá fōō-kì. 29Babiloon yab bin bíi jáà nì kitiŋ nee làá kɔ́ ki-ni, kí nàan̄-kì ní kí tūū-kì ŋŋmi. Adiin aba yilpu bi nín bɔ̀b̄ puee, binib tūutì talaalub ki tīī diwaal Baal ní ki fá awaa aba mun ndaam. Bi ŋá míǹ ki gbítì m-ŋuul. Too, Babiloon yab làá tūū adiin gbanti ŋŋmi.
30«Di sá doooo kutaafaau ní Isirayeel yab nì Juuda yab bí ki ŋáań tin kaa ŋān̄ee m-nimbiin. Tiŋman, tin kɔkɔ Isirayeel yab ŋáańee gbítí m-ŋuul ní, ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ. 31Di sá yii doooo bi nín máń kitiŋ nee ki dāa sāā díǹ nee, ki-nib pée gbítí m-ŋuul ní ki yàntī m fòol̄ mbum. An pu ní maa ti là kí wāl̀-bi m-nimbiin. 32Isirayeel yab nì Juuda yab ŋá ikpiti tikpil ki gbítì m-ŋuul, bíǹ nì bi-bɔtiibi nì bi-kpilib nì bi-saraaŋaliibi nì bi-bɔnaatiliibi nì bin kóò Jeerusaleem tiŋkin nì Juuda timmu mun kíǹee poonee. 33An bàà sá bí fàtī bi-nimbiin kí túĺ-mee, bi fātì bi-boon ki tīī-mi. Nì min kamaa m yōoǹ ŋyunti ki dàkā-bee, baa pílifì kaa dū m-saŋkii ki túń ditundi. 34Bi cáá bi-waaŋi ŋin sá ntimbiil tuuŋŋee ki kɔ́ǹ Kudii kun bi dūu sú-mee poon ki kɔ́ǹ-ku tijɔkɔndi. 35Inɔɔm tantakalinee, bi ŋātì mpaan kí nīn tòotī diwaal Baal. Niin ní bi dū bi-jipɔmbi nì bi-bisalib ki tūū ŋŋmi ki tīī diwaal Mooleeki. Maa pée tīī-bi dalba dalba mara bí ŋá míǹ, kaa kpáàa dākafì míǹ ŋwindal. Bi nín ŋá ntimbiil tuuŋŋi gbantee, bi téé Juuda yab ki yāntì bi ŋá ikpiti.
36«Ni sòoǹ Jeerusaleem tiŋki pu yii: <Kujaau nì ŋkùm nì bìlbil kúm di dū-kì ki ŋá Babiloon bɔtiu ŋaan.> Kɔŋkɔnnee, man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ kitiŋ nee pu puee sɔ̀. 37M nìn gíí bi-pu diŋuul ki fōō bi-pu mbum ŋkpitim pu. M nìn jìn̄-bi bi yàl̄ ki kɔ́ ntimu kɔkɔn. Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, m làá kóoǹ-bi kí kpāfì doo bí nīn bí ŋgbansɔŋfin. 38Niinee bi làá fàtīí nīn sá man nibul, ní man ń nīn sá bi-Nimbɔtiu. 39M làá dāá tīī-bi dipɔbibaantiil nì nlandɔkɔbaanti bí ŋmā kí nīn tɔ́-mi ki cá jaanjaan. Niinee bi làá nīn bí mmɔnni, bi nì bi-biyaamu. 40M làá ŋá mpèé nì bi kí nīn cá jaanjaan. M làá nīn pée nóó-bi kí ŋá-bi tiŋan kí taa gbèen̄. Mimmee, bi làá nīn tɔ́-mi ní kaa ti làá fàtī bi-boon kí tīī-mi. 41Án làá dāá nīn mɔ̄ǹ-mi ḿ ŋá-bi tiŋan. M làá dāá kàan̄-bi kitiŋ nee poon katanjoolii nì m-pɔbil kɔkɔ nì m-naŋki kɔkɔ.»
42Ti-Dindaan gíti sòon̄ yii: «Man di cáań nnaabukpaan nee ki tɔ́ Juuda nibul pu. Man ubaantee di làá tí cáań nnaam min m pōoǹ-bee kí tīī-bi. 43Binib lì yii: <Bi dū kitiŋ nee ki ŋá Babiloon yab ŋaan. Kɔŋkɔnnee kì kpántì kuteeu ní binib nì tiwaŋkuti kaa ti bí ki-pu. Ama kitiŋ nee poonee, binib làá dāá fàtīí dā akpaan. 44Tiŋman bi làá dāá fàtīí dā akpaan Beenjameen tiŋkin nì Jeerusaleem tiŋki kpaanceetii nì Juuda timmun nì ntimu mun bí ajoon puee nì mun bí Seefeelaayee nì mun bí Neegeebee. Binib làá dāá ŋmà tigbɔn tin dàkà yii bi nyáfì bi-kpaatantee ní kí dāá dū kijalii kí nyīī ti-pu ŋŋal ní kí kpáb́ biseeradambi nimbiin. Di sá yii m làá fàtīí gíiǹní bi-yab bin bi cúú ki cūnnì kuyuŋuee», ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_text:
The Lord Promises To Give the Land Back to His People
1-2I was still being held prisoner in the courtyard of the palace guards when the Lord told me:
I am the Lord, and I created the whole world. 3Ask me, and I will tell you things that you don't know and can't find out.
4-5Many of the houses in Jerusalem and some of the buildings at the royal palace have been torn down to be used in repairing the walls to keep out the Babylonian attackers. Now there are empty spaces where the buildings once stood. But I am furious, and these spaces will be filled with the bodies of the people I kill. The people of Jerusalem will cry out to me for help, but they are evil, and I will ignore their prayers.
6Then someday, I will heal this place and my people as well, and let them enjoy unending peace. 7I will give this land to Israel and Judah once again, and I will make them as strong as they were before. 8They sinned and rebelled against me, but I will forgive them and take away their guilt. 9When that happens, all nations on earth will see the good things I have done for Jerusalem, and how I have given it complete peace. The nations will celebrate and praise and honor me, but they will also tremble with fear because of the powerful things I have done.
10Jeremiah, you say that this land is a desert without people or animals, and for now, you are right. The towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem are deserted, and people and animals are nowhere to be seen. But someday you will hear 11 happy voices and the sounds of parties and wedding celebrations. And when people come to my temple to offer sacrifices to thank me, you will hear them say:
“We praise you,
Lord All-Powerful!
You are good to us,
and your love never fails.”
The land will once again be productive. 12-13Now it is empty, without people or animals. But when that time comes, shepherds will take care of their flocks in pastures near every town in the hill country, in the foothills to the west, in the Southern Desert, in the land of the Benjamin tribe, and around Jerusalem and the towns of Judah.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Lord's Wonderful Promise
14 The Lord said:
I made a wonderful promise to Israel and Judah, and the days are coming when I will keep it.
15I promise that the time will come
when I will appoint a king
from the family of David,
a king who will be honest
and rule with justice.
16In those days,
Judah will be safe;
Jerusalem will have peace
and will be named,
“The Lord Gives Justice.”
17 The king of Israel will be one of David's descendants, 18 and there will always be priests from the Levi tribe serving at my altar and offering sacrifices to please me and to give thanks.
19Then the Lord told me:
20I, the Lord, have an agreement with day and night, so they always come at the right time. You can't break the agreement I made with them, 21and you can't break the agreements I have made with David's family and with the priests from the Levi tribe who serve at my altar. A descendant of David will always rule as king of Israel, 22and there will be more descendants of David and of the priests from the Levi tribe than stars in the sky or grains of sand on the beach.
23The Lord also said:
24You've heard foreigners insult my people by saying, “The Lord chose Israel and Judah, but now he has rejected them, and they are no longer a nation.”
25Jeremiah, I will never break my agreement with the day and the night or let the sky and the earth stop obeying my commands. 26In the same way, I will never reject the descendants of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob or break my promise that they will always have a descendant of David as their king. I will be kind to my people Israel, and they will be successful again.
translation_text:
Ti-Dindaan fātìi pōoǹ Jeerusaleem ipoon
1Yeereemii nìn gbíntìi dáá pīī kudii bijanjaliibi bin cí ubɔtee dumpu. Ti-Dindaan nìn gíti sòon̄ nì u yii: 2«Ti-Dindaan un di ŋá tin bí nee kɔkɔee, ti-Dindaan un di bɔ́ntì-tì ki yāntì tì bée nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Úǹ ní bi yíì ti-Dindaan. 3Kúuǹ ki yíiń-mi, m làá kíí-si. M làá lēē tiwaŋkpaandi tin bí dibalin aa nyée kí dàkà-si. 4Ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ tin kitiŋ nee diiŋŋi nì Juuda bɔtiibi beeciŋŋi nì ataŋkpakpuku ŋin bi bíl̀ kitiŋ gundi boon nì kitàataajiki pu puee sɔ̀. 5Bi yaa bíi jáà nì Babiloon yabee, bi bíi gbēentí adiin anikpil ŋin m làá kpɔ̀ m-ŋuul nì m-bum poonee dee. Di sá yii Jeerusaleem yab túń atuŋkpiti tikpil, an pu ní m fātì m-boon ki tīī kitiŋ nee.
6«Ama nì míǹ kɔkɔ, m làá dāá cáaǹ-kì kí pɔ̄ɔkì. M làá cáaǹ-kì ní ki-nib ń ká dipɔɔsɔŋkil kí nīn bí ŋgbansɔŋfin. 7M làá fàtīí gíiǹní Juuda nì Isirayeel yab bin bi nìn cúú ki cūnnì kuyuŋuee, m làá fàtīí gíiǹ-bi mpaan ŋun pu bi nìn bí dooooyee. 8M làá dāá ŋá-bi circir kí nyāntí ikpiti in kɔkɔ bi ŋée. Bi nín jáń nì mi puee, m làá dūú pɔ̄-bi. 9An làá dāá nīn mɔ̄ǹ-mi ḿ yíiń Jeerusaleem yindi. Kitiŋ gbanti làá dāá tīī-mi jilma ní ḿ dāá nīn fàal̀ ki-pu kitiŋ pu nibuliŋ kɔkɔ nimbiin. Anibul gbanti kɔkɔ làá dāá béé tiŋan tin kɔkɔ m làá dāá ŋá-kèe. Bi yaa láa ká nnaam nì ŋgbansɔŋfi ŋun kɔkɔ m làá tīī-kèe, bi làá dāá nīn jìkì nì kufaaŋŋu ní kí kɔ́ dinyoondin.»
*
10Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «Nimbi Juuda yab, ni lì yii: <Kitiŋ nee kpántì adigbun binib nì tiwaŋkuti kaa ti kóò ki-pu.> Tiŋman, Juuda timmu nì Jeerusaleem daŋŋi kíǹ ki dɔ̄ fám binib nì tiwaŋkuti kaa ti kóò ntimu gbantin. Too, kitiŋ nee poonee, bi làá fàtīí gbìl̄ 11jiŋaal wooku nì dipɔɔpindi laŋyi nì animpucaŋgbiil pu. Bi làá dāá fàtīí tí gbìl̄ bin cāabìń inyɔŋki saraabi kunimbɔtidiinee laŋyi pu ki lì yii:
<Tí nyɔ̄ŋkìmaan ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan,
di sá yii u ŋān̄ ní u-neendi bí ki cá jaanjaan.>
Di sá yii m làá fàtīí ŋāŋkì kitiŋ nee ní kí fàtīí gítí kii kì nín nìn bí pu dooooyee, ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.»
*
12Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín gíti sòon̄ puee sèé: «Kitiŋ kin kpántì adigbun binib nì tiwaŋkuti kaa ti kóò ki-pu nì ki-timmu kɔkɔ poonee, bi làá dāá gíti ká kunaakpaapɔɔu laakin bipikpaaliibi làá yàntī bi-piii nì bi-ŋoobui ń nīn dɔ̀ ki ŋùŋfēe. 13Dijool pu timmun nì Seefeelaa nì Neegeeb nì Beenjameen timmu nì Jeerusaleem kpaanceetii nì Juuda timmunee, ipii nì iŋoobu làá dāá tí jītí un kàaǹ-iee nimbiin», ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.
Tin Unimbɔti pōoǹee, u làá ŋá míǹ
14«Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Iwiin iba bí ki dòoń, m nín pōoǹ Isirayeel nì Juuda yab nibul kí ŋá-bi tiŋan tiŋyee, m làá ŋá míǹ. 15Ŋyunti gbanti yaa láa sāāyee, m làá yàntī bí màal̀ Daafiidi naantiiu tiŋman pu yɔu. Úǹ di làá dāá yàntī binib ń ŋá tin dɔ̄ nsanee nì tin bí deedeeyee kitiŋ nee pu. 16Iwiin gbantinee Juuda beel làá dāá ká difiil ní Jeerusaleem beel ń dāá nīn bí dipɔɔsɔŋkilin. Bi làá nīn yíì Jeerusaleem yii: <Ti-Dindaan ti-baamɔŋŋu.>»
17Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «Daafiidi maaliŋu poon kpá kí lóó un làá kàl̄ Isirayeel tiŋki pu dibeelee. 18Míǹ mbaantiim Leefii yab bin sá bisaraaŋaliibee kpá kí lóó binib bin làá nīn yú m-nimbiin ki ŋáań bisaraawɔkaabi, ki tùutī saraabi ki ŋáań baabadal saraabee.»
*
19Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Yeereemii yii: 20«Man ni-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Ni ŋūǹ kí kpìtī mpèé ŋun di bí man nì ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu kansikineeee? Ni ŋūǹ kí pìin̄ nsan ŋwiimpu ń taa páań kunyeeu boon, àá kunyeeu ń taa páań ŋwiimpu boonaaa? 21Míǹ mbaantiim ní mpèé ŋun bí man nì m-tɔntɔnliu Daafiidi kansikinee kaa làá kpìtī. An pu ní u-naantiibi kansikin ubɔ làá nīn pée sá ubɔti Jeerusaleem tiŋkin. Míǹ mbaantiim ní bisaraaŋaliibi làá nīn pée bí Leefii dicaŋkun ki tūǹ m-tundi. Ubɔ kaa làá pée ŋmā kí pìin̄ nsan míǹ ń taa ŋá. 22Unil kaa ŋūǹ kí kàaǹ iŋmalbijaa in bí kutaa puee, kaa ŋūǹ kí kàaǹ tiŋku gbandi bul. Míǹ mbaantiim ní m làá bùtī Daafiidi maaliŋun yab nì Leefii maaliŋun bin sá m-tɔntɔnliibee.»
*
23Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Yeereemii yii: 24«Aa gbìl̀ binib nín sòoǹ pueeee? Bi lì yii m dū Isirayeel nì Juuda, adican ali ŋin m lēēyee ki fá. Bi sòoǹ mimmee ní ki kpèé m-nibul fám. Bíǹ ceeyee, ŋaa ti kpáàa sá ditimbundi gba. 25Tin man ni-Dindaan lēe sɔ̀. M ŋá mpèé nì ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu. M síiǹ marab bin kpòotī kutagbɔŋu nì kitiŋee. 26Mimmee m ŋūǹ kí dū Jaakɔb dicaŋkun yab nì m-tɔntɔnliu Daafiidi maaliŋun yab kí fáaa? M ŋūǹ kí yíí kí taa lēē bin làá nīn kpòotī Abraam nì Isaaki nì Jaakɔb nibuleeee?
«Aayee, kpataaa! M làá sɔ̄ bi-saai ní kí fàtīí yàntī án bútí-bi.»

english_text:
Jeremiah Warns Zedekiah
1 King Nebuchadnezzar had a large army made up of people from every kingdom in his empire. He and his army were attacking Jerusalem and all the nearby towns, when the Lord told me 2to say to King Zedekiah:
I am the Lord, and I am going to let Nebuchadnezzar capture this city and burn it down. 3You will be taken prisoner and brought to Nebuchadnezzar, and he will speak with you face to face. Then you will be led away to Babylonia.
4Zedekiah, I promise that you won't die in battle. 5You will die a peaceful death. People will mourn when you die, and they will light bonfires in your honor, just as they did for your ancestors, the kings who ruled before you.
6I went to Zedekiah and told him what the Lord had said. 7Meanwhile, the king of Babylonia was trying to break through the walls of Lachish, Azekah, and Jerusalem, the only three towns of Judah that had not been captured.
The People Break a Promise
8-10King Zedekiah, his officials, and everyone else in Jerusalem made an agreement to free all Hebrew men and women who were slaves. No Jew would keep another as a slave. And so, all the Jewish slaves were given their freedom.
11But those slave owners changed their minds and forced their former slaves back into slavery.
12That's when the Lord told me to say to the people:
13I am the Lord God of Israel, and I made an agreement with your ancestors when I brought them out of Egypt, where they had been slaves. 14 As part of this agreement, you must let a Hebrew slave go free after six years of service.
Your ancestors did not obey me, 15-16but you decided to obey me and do the right thing by setting your Hebrew slaves completely free. You even went to my temple, and in my name you made an agreement to set them free. But you have abused my name, because you broke that agreement and forced your former slaves back into slavery.
17You have disobeyed me by not giving your slaves their freedom. So I will give you freedom—the freedom to die in battle or from disease or hunger. I will make you disgusting to all other nations on earth.
18You asked me to be a witness when you made the agreement to set your slaves free. And as part of the ceremony you cut a calf into two parts, then walked between the parts. But you people of Jerusalem have broken that agreement as well as my agreement with Israel. So I will do to you what you did to that calf. 19-20I will let your enemies take all of you prisoner, including the leaders of Judah and Jerusalem, the royal officials, the priests, and everyone else who walked between the two parts of the calf. These enemies will kill you and leave your bodies lying on the ground as food for birds and wild animals.
21-22These enemies are King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia and his army. They have stopped attacking Jerusalem, but they want to kill King Zedekiah and his high officials. So I will command them to return and attack again. This time they will conquer the city and burn it down, and they will capture Zedekiah and his officials. I will also let them destroy the towns of Judah, so that no one can live there any longer.
translation_text:
Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ ubɔti Seedeesiyasi pu
1Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar nìn bíi jáà nì Jeerusaleem tiŋki nì Juuda timmu mun kíǹee. U-janjakitil kɔkɔ nì kitiŋ pu beeŋi janjaliibi kɔkɔ nì anibul ŋin kɔkɔ bí u-taapuee janjaliibi nìn kútì u-pu. Ŋyunti gbanti ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Yeereemii yii: 2«Man ni-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Cùú ká Juuda bɔtiu Seedeesiyasi kí tùkù-u yii man ni-Dindaan bí yii m làá dū kitiŋ nee kí ŋá Babiloon bɔtiu ŋaan ú wà-kì ŋŋmi. 3Sisee, aa làá ŋmátí kí nyā u-ŋaan. Bi làá cúú-si kí dū-si kí ŋá u-ŋaan. A làá cùú yūĺ u-nimbiin ní ní nīn sòoǹ ki kpèé tɔb. Míǹ boonee ní ú cáá-si kí cùnnì Babiloon tiŋkin.
4«Ama sii Juuda bɔtiu Seedeesiyasi, a yaa pílifì m-bɔtee, aa làá kpú kujaaun. Man a-Dindaan di sòon̄ nì si míǹ. 5A làá kpú ŋgbansɔŋfin ní. Bi làá ŋá a-kpool kii bi nín ŋá a-naanjab bin nìn sá bibɔtiibi ki wāatì ní sii nín kpántì ubɔtee puee ní. Bi làá dāá tūū talaalub kí tīī-si jilma ní kí gāā-si icaalan yii: <Áù, ti-baa ubɔti kpíì!> Man a-Dindaan di sòon̄ míǹ.»
6Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii nìn dū an bɔtee ki nāatì Juuda bɔtiu Seedeesiyasi Jeerusaleem tiŋkin. 7Ŋyunti gbantee Babiloon bɔtiu nì u-janjakitil nìn bíi jáà nì Jeerusaleem nì u-timmu nì Juuda timmu mun bi nìn máń agun ki túee, múǹ di sá Lakiisi nì Aseeka timmu, ntimu muli gbanti di nìn pɔ̄ɔ̄.
Juuda yab tīī iyumbu dibatɔl ki fātìi cúú-i
8Tíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ boonee, ti-Dindaan gíti sòon̄ nì Yeereemii. Ubɔti Seedeesiyasi nìn ŋá mpèé nì Jeerusaleem yab kɔkɔ yii bí tīī iyumbu dibatɔl. 9An nìn sá yii un sá kamaa ń tīī u-yumbuu, uninja àá unimpu un sá eebru niliuee dibatɔl. Ubɔ kaa ti cáá nsan kí dū u-nabiki ujudanil kí kpántí uyumbu. 10Niinee ní biyidambi kɔkɔ nì samaa kɔkɔ ŋá mpèé yii bi làá tīī bi-yumbui bininjab nì binimpoobi dibatɔl, kí taa ti yàntī bí tɔ̄ ditundi kii iyumbuee. 11Ama míǹ boonee ní bi kpántì nlandɔkɔ ki fātìi fōō iyumbu bininjab nì binimpoobi bin bi nìn tīī dibatɔlee, ki fātìi yāntì bi kpántì iyumbu.
12Niinee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Yeereemii yii: 13«Man ni-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M nìn ŋá mpèé ŋubɔ nì ni-naanjab ŋyunti ŋun m nìn nyántìń-bi Eejipiti tiŋkin laakin bi nìn bí ki sá iyumbuee. 14M nìn tùkū-bi yii: <Abin aluli yaa sāāyee, báà ŋma ń gíiǹ u-nabiki eebru yɔu un cáań u-ba ki nyáfiǹ-uee kí líí ú tɔ̄ u-ba. U làá nīn sá u-yumbuu kí tɔ̄ u-tuuŋŋi abin aluu, dibinluluútiilee ú gíiǹ-u kí líí ú tɔ̄ u-ba. Ama ni-naanjab kaa nìn pílifì tibɔti gbanti kaa nìn tí dūu túń nì ditundi. 15Ama nimbee, ni bàà kpántì mbimbim ki ŋá tin kítì m-ceeyee. Di sá yii báà ŋma bàà lī u-juti cee yii u tɔ́ u-ba. Áli gba ni ŋá mpèé nì man kudii kun bi dūu sú-mee poon. 16Ama míǹ boonee ní ni kpántì nlandɔkɔ ki kpēē-mi fám. Báà ŋma fātìi cūtìi gíiǹní u-yumbuu uninja àá unimpu un u tīī dibatɔlee. Ni ŋá-bi mpɔn bí fàtīí kpántí ni-yumbui.»
17Ní Yeereemii gíti kútì ki lī yii: «Too, ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. An bàà sá yii báà ŋma ń tīī u-yumbuu eebru niliu un sá u-nabiki nì u-jutee dibatɔl ní. Ama naa ŋá kii m nín bí yii ní ŋá puee. An pu ní man ni-Dindaan sòon̄ yii m làá cáań kujaau nì bìlbil kúm nì ŋkùm kí tɔ̄ ni-pu. Niinee kitiŋ pu beeŋi nib yaa láa ká mimmee, bi làá dāá kɔ́ dinyoondin.
18«Binib gbanti nyáń mpèé ŋun bi ŋée boon. Baa ŋá kii bi nín yúl̀ m-nimbiin ki pōoǹ puee. M làá ŋá-bi kii dinabil din bi gíí ki nābitì mili ki cōom̀ ki jítì ajan alee kansikinee ní. 19Juuda yidambi nì Jeerusaleem yab nì bikàliŋkpilib bigaakaabi nì bisaraaŋaliibi nì bitindaŋkpilib kɔkɔ, an dàkà yii bin kɔkɔ pée cōom̀ ki jítì dinabil din bi gíí ki nābitì milee kansikinee, 20m làá dū-bi kí ŋá bi-nannanliibi nì bin nyàab̀ kí kpɔ̀-bee ŋaan. Bi-nikpiliŋ làá kpántí inoon nì ipeel jikaati. 21Míǹ mbaantiim ní m làá dū Juuda bɔtiu nì u-kàliŋkpilib kí ŋá bi-nannanliibi nì bin nyàab̀ kí kpɔ̀-bee ŋaan. M làá dū-bi kí ŋá Babiloon bɔtiu janjaliibi ŋaan. Bijanjaliibi gbanti dá láá búntì ki wāatì-ni. 22Ama m làá tīī-bi mara bí gítiń kí jáǹ Jeerusaleem tiŋki. Bi làá fōō kitiŋ nee ní kí wà-kì ŋŋmi. M làá yàntī Juuda timmu ń kpántí kii kuteeuee ubɔ ń taa ti nín̄ kóò mu-ni.» Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_text:
Learn a Lesson from the Rechabites
1 When Jehoiakim was king of Judah, the Lord told me, 2“Go to the Rechabite clan and invite them to meet you in one of the side rooms of the temple. When they arrive, offer them a drink of wine.”
3So I went to Jaazaniah, the leader of the clan, and I invited him and all the men of his clan. 4I brought them into the temple courtyard and took them upstairs to a room belonging to the prophets who were followers of Hanan son of Igdaliah. It was next to a room belonging to some of the officials, and that room was over the one belonging to Maaseiah, a priest who was one of the high officials in the temple.
5I set out some large bowls full of wine together with some cups, and then I said to the Rechabites, “Have some wine!”
6But they answered:
No! The ancestor of our clan, Jonadab son of Rechab, made a rule that we must obey. He said, “Don't ever drink wine 7or build houses or plant crops and vineyards. Instead, you must always live in tents and move from place to place. If you obey this command, you will live a long time.”
8-10Our clan has always obeyed Jonadab's command. To this very day, we and our wives and sons and daughters don't drink wine or build houses or plant vineyards or crops. And we have lived in tents, 11except now we have to live inside Jerusalem because Nebuchadnezzar has taken over the countryside with his army from Babylonia and Syria.
12-13Then the Lord told me to say to the people of Judah and Jerusalem:
I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, want you to learn a lesson 14from the Rechabite clan. Their ancestor Jonadab told his descendants never to drink wine, and to this very day they have obeyed him. But I have spoken to you over and over, and you haven't obeyed me! 15You refused to listen to my prophets, who kept telling you, “Stop doing evil and worshiping other gods! Start obeying the Lord, and he will let you live in this land he gave your ancestors.”
16The Rechabites have obeyed the command of their ancestor Jonadab, but you have not obeyed me, 17your God. I am the Lord All-Powerful, and I warned you about the terrible things that would happen to you if you did not listen to me. But you have ignored me, so now disaster will strike you. I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Lord Makes a Promise to the Rechabites
18Then the Lord told me to say to the Rechabite clan:
“I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. You have obeyed your ancestor Jonadab, 19so I promise that your clan will be my servants and will never die out.”
translation_text:
Reekaab yab bɔŋmantikaati
1Ŋyunti ŋun Joosiyaasi jipɔɔn Yooyakiim sá Juuda bɔtiuee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Yeereemii yii: 2«Cùú ká Reekaab maaliŋun yab, kí sòoǹ nì bi, kí cáań-bi kunimbɔtidii dibiyaamu kiba poon. Niinee á tīī-bi ndaam bí nyɔ̀.»
3Niinee ní m cūtìi nyàab̄ Yaasaniya, Irimeeya jipɔɔn Abasiniya naantiu nì u-nabiyaamu kɔkɔ nì u-jipɔmbi, an dàkà yii Reekaab maaliŋun yab kɔkɔ. 4M nìn cáá-bi ki kɔ́ǹ kunimbɔtidiin, Igidaliya jipɔɔn Anan, Unimbɔti niliu dibikin. Kidibiki gbanti nìn bí ki kɔ́ĺ abɔtibil dibiki, Saluum jipɔɔn Maaseeyawuu un sá usaraaŋal ki kpèé kunimbɔtidii punyɔkɔkee yaka yilpu pú ní. 5M nìn dū aboon ŋin poon ndaam gbée nì tidayuti ki yóoǹ Reekaab maaliŋun yab nimbiin ní ki bí-bi yii: «Bàtīmaan ndaam kí nyɔ̀.»
6Ama ní bi kíí yii: «Taa nyù ndaam. Ti-naanja Yoonadaab, Reekaab jipɔɔn yóoǹ-ti mara yii:
<Nimbi nì ni-naantiibi, ní taa pée nyɔ̀ ndaam dalba dalba.
7Ní taa mā adiin,
kí taa kpɔ̀ tikpaal,
kí taa cóoń fiinyi sufii,
ní kí taa nín̄ cáá an wanti báà tiba.
Ama ní nīn kóò tantibin
ni-maŋfal wiiŋyi kɔkɔ poon,
ní kí ŋmā kí kàl̄ kitiŋ kin ni kóò
kii binicambi nee pu kí yúntí.>»
8«Ti ŋúb́ Reekaab jipɔɔn Yoonadaab, ti-naanja marau un u yóoǹ-tee tiŋan, an puee ti nì ti-nimpoobi nì ti-jipɔmbi nì ti-bisalib kaa nyù ndaam jaanjaan. 9Taa māā adiin ki kóò, kaa cáá fiinyi kpaaŋŋi, kaa tí cáá tisati ki kù. 10Ti kóò tantibin ní. Ti-naanja Yoonadaab nín tīī-ti mara puee, míǹ ní ti ŋúb́. 11Ama ŋyunti ŋun Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar bíi jáà nì kitiŋ neeyee ní ti dākafì yii: <An sɔ́ tí sāǹ kí kɔ́ Jeerusaleem tiŋkin Babiloon janjakitil nì Siirii janjakitil ń taa cúú-ti. Ŋyunti gbantee ní ti dɔ́miń ki kíǹ ki kóò kitiŋin doo.>»
12Niinee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Yeereemii yii: 13«Man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Cùú tùkù Juuda yab nì Jeerusaleem yab yii: <Naa bàà máaǹ kí fōō m-bɔkpaafikaati kí pīlifì tin m sòoǹeeee?> Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ. 14Reekaab jipɔɔn Yoonadaab tīī u-naantiibi mara yii bí taa pée nyɔ̀ ndaam, ní baa lafun nyùn̄ ndaam ki dāa sāā díǹ, kun puee bi tɔ́ bi-naanja marau. Ama man sòon̄ nì ni ki gíti sòon̄ nì ni ní naa pílifiǹ-mi. 15M túnní m-tɔntɔnliibi bibɔnaatiliibi ni-cee ŋfunyɔm kupaau kaa gbēeǹ bí tùkù-ni yii: <Báà ŋma ń dū u-saŋkiŋkpitil kí fá, kí ŋá min kítèe. Taa nín̄ jòó ki pámaan awaa boon ki tòotī-ŋi. Niinee ni làá ŋmā kí kàl̄ kitiŋ kin m tīī ni nì ni-naanjabee poon.> Ama naa kpōoǹ ni-tafal ní kaa nín pílifì. 16Reekaab jipɔɔn Yoonadaab naantiibi ŋúb́ marab bin bi-naanja nìn yóoǹ-bee, ama ní man nibul kaa pílifiǹ man.
17«An puee ti-Dindaan, Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <M làá cáań inaabu in bɔti m nìn sòon̄ee kí tɔ̄ Juuda yab nì Jeerusaleem yab pu. Di sá yii m sòon̄ nì bi, ama ní baa pílifiǹ-mi. M yíiń-bi, ama ní baa kíí-mi.>»
18Míǹ boonee ní Yeereemii bí Reekaab maaliŋun yab yii: «Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Ni tɔ́ ni-naanja Yoonadaab marau, ki ŋúb́ tin kɔkɔ u tīī-ni mara ní ŋée. 19An puee Reekaab jipɔɔn Yoonadaab maaliŋun yab pée kpá kí lóó unil un làá nīn yú m-nimbiin ki tūǹ m-tundee.>
«Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee dee.»

english_text:
King Jehoiakim Burns Jeremiah's First Scroll
1 During the fourth year that Jehoiakim son of Josiah was king of Judah, the Lord said to me, “Jeremiah, 2since the time Josiah was king, I have been speaking to you about Israel, Judah, and the other nations. Now, get a scroll and write down everything I have told you, 3then read it to the people of Judah. Maybe they will stop sinning when they hear what terrible things I plan for them. And if they turn back to me, I will forgive them.”
4I sent for Baruch son of Neriah and asked him to help me. I repeated everything the Lord had told me, and Baruch wrote it all down on a scroll. 5Then I said,
Baruch, the officials refuse to let me go into the Lord's temple, 6so you must go instead. Wait for the next holy day when the people of Judah come to the temple to pray and to go without eating. Then take this scroll to the temple and read it aloud. 7The Lord is furious, and if the people hear how he is going to punish them, maybe they will ask to be forgiven.
8-10In the ninth month of the fifth year that Jehoiakim was king, the leaders set a day when everyone who lived in Jerusalem or who was visiting there had to pray and go without eating. So Baruch took the scroll to the upper courtyard of the temple. He went over to the side of the courtyard and stood in a covered area near New Gate, where he read the scroll aloud.
This covered area belonged to Gemariah, one of the king's highest officials. 11Gemariah's son Micaiah was there and heard Baruch read what the Lord had said. 12When Baruch finished reading, Micaiah went down to the palace. His father Gemariah was in the officials' room, meeting with the rest of the king's officials, including Elishama, Delaiah, Elnathan, and Zedekiah. 13Micaiah told them what he had heard Baruch read to the people. 14Then the officials sent Jehudi and Shelemiah to tell Baruch, “Bring us that scroll.”
When Baruch arrived with the scroll, 15the officials said, “Please sit down and read it to us,” which he did. 16After they heard what was written on the scroll, they were worried and said to each other, “The king needs to hear this!” Turning to Baruch, they asked, 17“Did someone tell you what to write on this scroll?”
18“Yes, Jeremiah did,” Baruch replied. “I wrote down just what he told me.”
19The officials said, “You and Jeremiah must go into hiding, and don't tell anyone where you are going.”
20-22The officials put the scroll in Elishama's room and went to see the king, who was in one of the rooms where he lived and worked during the winter. It was the ninth month of the year, so there was a fire burning in the fireplace, and the king was sitting nearby. After the officials told the king about the scroll, he sent Jehudi to get it. Then Jehudi started reading the scroll to the king and his officials. 23-25But every time Jehudi finished reading three or four columns, the king would tell him to cut them off with his penknife and throw them in the fire. Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah begged the king not to burn the scroll, but he ignored them, and soon there was nothing left of it.
The king and his servants listened to what was written on the scroll, but they were not the least bit afraid, and they did not tear their clothes in sorrow.
26The king told his son Jerahmeel to take Seraiah and Shelemiah and to go arrest Baruch and me. But the Lord kept them from finding us.
Jeremiah's Second Scroll
27I had told Baruch what to write on that first scroll, but King Jehoiakim had burned it. So the Lord told me 28to get another scroll and write down everything that had been on the first one. 29Then he told me to say to King Jehoiakim:
Not only did you burn Jeremiah's scroll, you had the nerve to ask why he had written that the king of Babylonia would attack and ruin the land, killing all the people and even the animals. 30So I, the Lord, promise that you will be killed and your body thrown out on the ground. The sun will beat down on it during the day, and the frost will settle on it at night. And none of your descendants will ever be king of Judah. 31You, your children, and your servants are evil, and I will punish everyone of you. I warned you and the people of Judah and Jerusalem that I would bring disaster, but none of you have listened. So now you are doomed!
32After the Lord finished speaking to me, I got another scroll and gave it to Baruch. Then I told him what to write, so this second scroll would contain even more than was on the scroll Jehoiakim had burned.
translation_text:
Yooyakiim wùn̄ kugbɔŋu kun Baruuki ŋmàn̄ee ŋŋmi
1Yooyakiim jipɔɔn Joosiyaasi nín kpántì Juuda bɔtiu dibinnanaatiil poonee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Yeereemii yii: 2«Yòon̄ kugbɔŋu kun bi ŋūǹ kí kpáb́ee. Á ŋmà ku-pu tibɔti tin kɔkɔ m yāntì a sòon̄ Isirayeel yab nì Juuda yab nì atimbun kɔkɔ puee, kí yòon̄ ubɔti Joosiyaasi yuntiŋu tin m sòon̄ nì see kí dāá sāā díǹ nee. 3An yaa yíì Juuda yab yaa gbìl̄ inaabu in m bíi bɔ́ntí kí cáań kí tɔ̄ bi-puee, báà ŋma làá fá u-bimbikpitim. Niinee ní ḿ dū bi-yìntitam nì bi-kpitii kí pɔ̄-bi.»
4Niinee ní Yeereemii yíiń Neeriya jipɔɔn Baruuki, ní ki kàan̄-u tibɔti tin kɔkɔ ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì uee, ní Baruuki dūu ŋmàn̄ ki ŋá kugbɔŋun.
5Ní Yeereemii tùkū Baruuki yii: «Tiba cúú-mi, an puee man m-ba kaa làá ŋmā kí cù kunimbɔtidiin. 6Ama, sii làá cù dinyɔɔboobil wiiŋŋu dal, ní kí kàaǹ mpɔn ti-Dindaan bɔti tin m kàan̄-si a ŋmàn̄ ki ŋá kugbɔŋunee. Á kàaǹ bin kɔkɔ bí kunimbɔtidiinee ń gbìl̄, ki kpáaǹ bin kɔkɔ nyánní Juuda timmun ki dɔ́mińee. 7An yaa yíì bi làá kíĺ kí nīn bíi gbàam̄ ti-Dindaan, ní báà ŋma ń fá u-bimbikpitim. Di sá yii ti-Dindaan bí yii u-ŋuukpaandi di dàn̄ dinibul nee pu.»
8Niinee ní Neeriya jipɔɔn Baruuki ŋá tin kɔkɔ Yeereemii bí-u yii ú ŋée. U nìn cūtì ki kɔ́ kunimbɔtidiin ki kàan̄ ti-Dindaan bɔti tin ŋmàn̄ ki kā kugbɔŋu poonee. 9Joosiyaasi jipɔɔn Yooyakiim nín kpántì Juuda beel bɔtiu abin aŋmoo uŋmawawati poonee, ní bi yóoǹ yii bí bóob́ kinyɔkɔ ti-Dindaan nimbiin. Jeerusaleem yab kɔkɔ nì Juuda timmun yab kɔkɔ nìn dɔ́miń. 10Kunimbɔtidiin niinee ní Baruuki kàan̄ mpɔn Yeereemii nyɔɔbuŋŋi ŋin ŋmàn̄ ki kā kugbɔŋu poonee. U nìn yú Safan jipɔɔn Geemariya, ubɔti gbaŋŋmaliu dibikin ní. Kidibiki gbanti nìn bí kunimbɔtidii ciŋkpaandin yilpu pu ki nákáǹ kipunyɔkɔ Kipɔŋ ní.
11Geemariya jipɔɔn Miikayeewu, Safan naantiiu gbìl̄ ti-Dindaan bɔti tin kā kugbɔŋu poon Baruuki kàan̄ee. 12Míǹ boonee ní u nín sìntī ubɔti beecindin ki bàn̄ ki kɔ́ ugbaŋŋmal tɔntɔndiikun. Bikàliŋkpilib kɔkɔ nìn kpáfì ki bí niin. Bin nìn bí niinee di sá ubɔti gbaŋŋmaliu Eelsama nì Seemayawuu jipɔɔn Deelaya nì Akibɔɔr jipɔɔn Eelnatan nì Safan jipɔɔn Geemariyawuu nì Ananiyawuu jipɔɔn Seedeesiyasi nì bikàliŋkpilib bin kɔkɔ kíǹee. 13Ní Miikayeewu dū tibɔti tin kɔkɔ Baruuki kàan̄ kugbɔŋu poon samaa kɔkɔ nimbiinee ki máafì-bi.
14Niinee ní bikàliŋkpilibee dū Neetaniyawuu jipɔɔn Yeewuudi, Seeleemiyawuu naantiiu nì Kuusii naantitɔntɔkɔl ki tú Baruuki cee ú tùkù-u yii: «Dāan̄ kí kpáaǹ kugbɔŋu kun a kàan̄ samaa nimbiinee.» Niinee ní Neeriya jipɔɔn Baruuki yōoǹ kugbɔŋuee ki cūnnì bi-cee. 15U bàn̄ee ní bi bí-u yii: «Kàl̄ kí kàaǹ-ti tin kā kugbɔŋu nee poonee.»
Ní Baruuki kàan̄ ki tīī-bi. 16Bi nín gbìl̄ tibɔti gbanti kɔkɔee, ní tifaandi kɔ́-bi. Bi nìn kíǹ ki kā ki fàtī ki kpèé tɔb, ní ki bí Baruuki yii: «See tí cáá tibɔti nee kɔkɔ kí māafì ubɔti.»
17Boonee ní bi bālifì Baruuki yii: «Māafì-ti a nín ŋá pu ki ŋúń ki ŋmàn̄ tibɔti nee kɔkɔee?» 18Ní Baruuki kíí-bi yii: «Yeereemii u-ba nyɔkɔn ní u kàan̄ tibɔti nee kɔkɔ, ní man dū ŋŋmamɔɔn ki ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu nee pu.»
19Niinee ní bikàliŋkpilib bí Baruuki yii: «Si nì Yeereemii ń sāǹ kí báĺ. Ubɔ kaa máaǹ kí béé laakin ni bée!»
20Bi nìn dū kugbɔŋuee ki yóoǹ ubɔti gbaŋŋmaliu Eelsana tɔntɔndiikun. Míǹ boonee ní bi nín cá dibeecindin ubɔti cee ki máafì-u tin kɔkɔ jítèe.
21Niinee ní ubɔti dū Jeewuudi ki tú ú cùú cáań kugbɔŋuee. Úǹ nìn cūtì Eelsama tɔntɔndiikun ki yōoǹní kugbɔŋuee, ní ki kíĺ ki bíi kàaǹ-ku mpɔn ubɔti nì bikàliŋkpilib bin kɔkɔ nìn yú ki māntìi tú-uee nimbiin. 22Ubɔti nìn kā tiwool yuŋtiŋu diikun. An nìn sá dibindi poon uŋmawawati, tiwool yuntiŋu ní. Bi nìn kpāā ŋŋmi niin ní ubɔti yú ki wùl̀. 23Jeewuudi yaa nìn pée kàan̄ ikuul ita àá inaayee ní ubɔti ń dū bɔlfi kí gíí dijandi gbanti kí tɔ̄ ŋŋmin. U nìn pée ŋá míǹ ní ki dāa wùn̄ kugbɔŋuee kɔkɔ ŋŋmi. 24Ubɔti nì u-kàliŋkpilib nìn pílifì an bɔtee kɔkɔ. Ama an kaa nìn kɔ́ǹ-bi tifaandi, ní baa nìn tí dáaĺ tiwan tin bi nìn pēēyee ki cátì kí dàkà bi-nimbaaku. 25Áli gba Eelnatan nì Deelaya nì Geemariya nìn gbāam̀ ubɔti ú taa wà kugbɔŋuee ŋŋmi, ama waa nìn pílifiǹ-bi. 26Ubɔti nìn tīī u-jipɔɔn Yeerameeyeel nì Asiriyeel jipɔɔn Seeraya nì Abideeyeel jipɔɔn Seeleemiyawuu mara yii bí cúú ugbaŋŋmal Baruuki nì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii. Ama ní Unimbɔti dū-bi ki bál̀.
27Ubɔti nìn dū kugbɔŋu kun poon Baruuki nìn ŋmàn̄ tibɔti tin Yeereemii nìn kàan̄-uee ki wùn̄ ŋŋmi. Míǹ boonee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Yeereemii yii: 28«Cùú nyàab̀ kugbɔŋu kubɔ kí fàtīí ŋmà tibɔti tin kɔkɔ nìn ŋmàn̄ ki kā kugbɔmpeepeekaau poon, Juuda yab bɔtiu Yooyakiim dūu wùn̄ ŋŋmee. 29Míǹ boonee á sòoǹ Juuda bɔtiu Yooyakiim pu yii:
«Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: Yeereemii nìn ŋmàn̄ yii Babiloon bɔtiu làá dāan̄ kí nàan̄ kitiŋ nee kí kpɔ̀ binib nì tiwaŋkuti. Ama ní Yooyakiim wòon̄-u ní ki wùn̄ kugbɔŋuee ŋŋmi. 30Too, ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Yooyakiim kpátam boonee, u-maaliŋu poon báà ubɔ kaa làá kàl̄ Daafiidi beejal pu. U yaa láa kpíìyee, bi làá dū-u kí fá mmɔŋki ní ŋwìiń ń gbá-u ŋwiimpu, ní nsɔnsɔm ń tɔ̄-u kunyeeu. 31M làá dáaĺ u nì u-maaliŋun yab nì u-kàliŋkpilib tafal ikpiti in bi ŋée pu. M làá cáań inaabu in bɔti m nìn sòon̄ baa pílifiǹ-mee kí tɔ̄ Jeerusaleem yab nì Juuda yab pu.>»
32Niinee ní Yeereemii nyàab̄ kugbɔmpɔŋ ki tīī ugbaŋŋmal Baruuki, Neeriya jipɔɔn, ní Yeereemii fātìi kàan̄-u tibɔti tin nìn kā kugbɔŋu kun Juuda bɔtiu Yooyakiim dūu wùn̄ ŋŋmee poonee. U nìn gíti kútì tibɔti tin náań nì tíǹ gbantee.

english_text:
King Zedekiah Asks Jeremiah To Pray
1 King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia had removed Jehoiachin son of Jehoiakim from being the king of Judah and had made Josiah's son Zedekiah king instead. 2But Zedekiah, his officials, and everyone else in Judah ignored everything the Lord had told me.
3-5Later, the Babylonian army attacked Jerusalem, but they left after learning that the Egyptian army was headed in this direction.
One day, Zedekiah sent Jehucal and the priest Zephaniah to talk with me. At that time, I was free to go wherever I wanted, because I had not yet been put in prison. Jehucal and Zephaniah said, “Jeremiah, please pray to the Lord our God for us.”
6-7Then the Lord told me to send them back to Zedekiah with this message:
Zedekiah, you wanted Jeremiah to ask me, the Lord God of Israel, what is going to happen. So I will tell you. The king of Egypt and his army came to your rescue, but soon they will go back to Egypt. 8Then the Babylonians will return and attack Jerusalem, and this time they will capture the city and set it on fire. 9Don't fool yourselves into thinking that the Babylonians will leave as they did before. 10Even if you could defeat their entire army, their wounded survivors would still be able to leave their tents and set Jerusalem on fire.
Jeremiah Is Put in Prison
11The Babylonian army had left because the Egyptian army was on its way to help us. 12So I decided to leave Jerusalem and go to the territory of the Benjamin tribe to claim my share of my family's land. 13I was leaving Jerusalem through Benjamin Gate, when I was stopped by Irijah, the officer in charge of the soldiers at the gate. He said, “Jeremiah, you're under arrest for trying to join the Babylonians.”
14“I'm not trying to join them!” I answered. But Irijah wouldn't listen, and he took me to the king's officials. 15-16They were angry and ordered the soldiers to beat me. Then I was taken to the house that belonged to Jonathan, one of the king's officials. It had been turned into a prison, and I was kept in a basement room.
After I had spent a long time there, 17King Zedekiah secretly had me brought to his palace, where he asked, “Is there any message for us from the Lord?”
“Yes, there is, Your Majesty,” I replied. “The Lord is going to let the king of Babylonia capture you.”
18Then I continued, “Your Majesty, why have you put me in prison? Have I committed a crime against you or your officials or the nation? 19Have you locked up the prophets who lied to you and said that the king of Babylonia would never attack Jerusalem? 20Please, don't send me back to that prison at Jonathan's house. If you do, I will die there.”
21King Zedekiah had me taken to the prison cells in the courtyard of the palace guards. He told the soldiers to give me a loaf of bread from one of the bakeries every day until the city ran out of grain.
translation_text:
Ubɔti Seedeesiyasi tú binib Yeereemii cee
1Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar nìn dū Joosiyaasi jipɔɔn Seedeesiyasi ki kāaǹ Juuda beel pu ubɔti. Seedeesiyasi di nìn fōō Yooyakiim jipɔɔn Kooniya yil. 2Ama bi-kansikin báà ubɔ kaa nìn pílifì tibɔti tin ti-Dindaan nìn dī Yeereemii pu ki kpáafì-bee. Ubɔti u-baaa, u-kàliŋkpilibaaa, Juuda yabaaa, ubɔ kaa nìn fōotì ki yīkiǹ.
3Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, ubɔti Seedeesiyasi nìn tú Seeleemiya jipɔɔn Yukaal nì usaraaŋakpil Seefaniya, Maaseeyawuu jipɔɔn Yeereemii cee. Bi nìn bí-u yii: «Mèè ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu ti-pu.»
4Ŋyunti gbantee baa nìn dáá cúú Yeereemii ki pīiǹ kudii, an puee u nìn tɔ́ u-ba kí cù samaa cee kí gítiń. 5Faaroo janjaliibi nìn nyáń Eejipiti tiŋkin. Babiloon yab bin nìn māntìi tú Jeerusaleem tiŋki kí já nì kèe nín gbìl̄ mimmee ní bi sútì ki wāatì-kì. 6Niinee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì u-bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii yii: 7«Ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Ní cùú tùkù Juuda bɔtiu un túnní-ni ní dāan̄ kí bàlifèe yii: Faaroo janjaliibi bin nìn nyáń ki tútúǹ-nee fātìi nín gítí bi-tiŋkin Eejipiti. 8Babiloon yab làá fàtīí gítiń kí dāá já nì kitiŋ nee. Bi làá fōō-kì kí wà-kì ŋŋmi. 9Man ni-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Ní taa mɔ̄ntì ni-ba kí lì yii Babiloon yab yíkì ti-cee ki búntì. Baa búntì. 10Tí lì yii ni ŋúń ki jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Babiloon yab janjaliibi bin bí ki jáà nì nee kɔkɔ ní an kíǹ bin fōō tiweendee. Bíǹ gbanti làá nyānní bi-tantibin kí tūū kitiŋ nee ŋŋmi.>»
Bi cúú Yeereemii ki pīiǹ kudii
11Ubɔti Faaroo janjaliibi pu ní Babiloon janjaliibi sútì ki wāatì Jeerusaleem tiŋki. 12Yeereemii nìn là kí nyā Jeerusaleem tiŋkin kí cù Beenjameen tiŋkin kí fōō bi nín yākatì yākatì atinjan u-dicaŋkunee u-jandi. 13Ama u nín bàn̄ Beenjameen tiŋki punyɔkɔpuee ní u ká bijanjaliibi bin cīití kipunyɔkɔee kpiliu ubɔ. Bi nìn yíì-u Yiiriya, u sá Seeleemiya jipɔɔn nì Ananiya naantiiu. Úǹ nìn cúú Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii ní ki bí-u yii: «A cáǹ a-ba kí tīī Babiloon yabaa!» 14Ní Yeereemii kíí-u yii: «Aayee, maa cáǹ m-ba kí tīī Babiloon yab.»
Ama Yiiriya kaa nìn pīlifiǹ-u. U nìn cúú-u ki cáa cūnnì u-kpilib cee. 15Bíǹ nìn gíí Yeereemii pu diŋuul ŋkpitim pu ní ki gbáń-u ní ki dū-u ki pīiǹ kudii ugbaŋŋmal Joonatan diiku kun bi nìn dūu kpántì kusarkadiiyee poon. 16Bi nìn dū Yeereemii ki tɔ́ dinyimbɔbil din poon an bɔ̀ǹ kpìmmee.
U nìn kāl̀ niin ki yúntì. 17Dalbee ní ubɔti Seedeesiyasi tú unil ú cùú cáań-u. U nìn là kí bàlifì-u tiba dibalin u-beecindin. Ubɔti nìn bālifì-u yii: «Mimmee ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì si tiba m-pu á tùkù-maaa?» Ní Yeereemii kíí yii: «Iiin! Bi làá dū-si kí ŋá Babiloon bɔtiu ŋaan.» 18Ní Yeereemii gíti bí ubɔti Seedeesiyasi yii: «Ba ní m yīntiǹ sii nì a-kàliŋkpilib nì dinibul nee ní ni cúú-mi ki pīiǹ sarka ní? 19Ni-bɔnaatiliibi nìn tùkū-ni yii Babiloon bɔtiu kaa làá dāan̄ kí já ni nì ni-tiŋki kujaau. Bibɔnaatiliibi gbanti bí la díǹ?»
20Ní Yeereemii kútì ki lī yii: «Kɔŋkɔnnee, ti-baa ubɔti, pīlifiǹ-mi. Yàntī m-gbaamii ń kɔ́-si fíŋfiŋ. Taa ti gíiǹ-mi a-gbaŋŋmaliu Yoonatan dumpu, yaa sá fám m làá kpú.»
21Niinee ní ubɔti Seedeesiyasi tīī mara yii bí dū Yeereemii kí pìin̄ bijanjaliibi bin cí ubɔtee dumpu kudii. Bí nīn tìì-u ŋwiin kamaa kikpɔnɔkatii. Bí nīn cāabìń kpɔnɔ gbanti kpɔnɔb bin bi kāntí bikpɔnɔpuliliibi daŋŋi puee kí tin sāā ŋyunti ŋun ní kpɔnɔ làá dóó kitiŋee nee. Míǹ ní Yeereemii nìn gbíntì bijanjaliibi bin cí ubɔtee dumpu.

english_text:
Jeremiah Is Held Prisoner in a Dry Well
1One day, Shephatiah, Gedaliah, Jehucal, and Pashhur heard me tell the people of Judah 2-3that the Lord had said, “If you stay here in Jerusalem, you will die in battle or from disease or hunger, and the Babylonian army will capture the city anyway. But if you surrender to the Babylonians, they will let you live.”
4So the four of them went to the king and said, “You should put Jeremiah to death, because he is making the soldiers and everyone else lose hope. He isn't trying to help our people; he's trying to harm them.”
5Zedekiah replied, “Do what you want with him. I can't stop you.”
6Then they took me back to the courtyard of the palace guards and let me down with ropes into the well that belonged to Malchiah, the king's son. There was no water in the well, but I sank down in the mud.
7-8Ebedmelech from Ethiopia was an official at the palace, and he heard what they had done to me. So he went to speak with King Zedekiah, who was holding court at Benjamin Gate. 9Ebedmelech said, “Your Majesty, Jeremiah is a prophet, and those men were wrong to throw him into a well. And when Jerusalem runs out of food, Jeremiah will starve to death down there.”
10Zedekiah answered, “Take 30 of my soldiers and pull Jeremiah out before he dies.”
11Ebedmelech and the soldiers went to the palace and got some rags from the room under the treasury. He used ropes to lower them into the well. 12Then he said, “Put these rags under your arms so the ropes won't hurt you.” After I did, 13the men pulled me out. And from then on, I was kept in the courtyard of the palace guards.
King Zedekiah Questions Jeremiah
14King Zedekiah had me brought to his private entrance to the temple, and he said, “I'm going to ask you something, and I want to know the truth.”
15“Why?” I replied. “You won't listen, and you might even have me killed!”
16He said, “I swear in the name of the living Lord our Creator that I won't have you killed. No one else can hear what we say, and I won't let anyone kill you.”
17Then I told him that the Lord had said: “Zedekiah, I am the Lord God All-Powerful, the God of Israel. I promise that if you surrender to King Nebuchadnezzar's officers, you and your family won't be killed, and Jerusalem won't be burned down. 18But if you don't surrender, I will let the Babylonian army capture Jerusalem and burn it down, and you will be taken prisoner.”
19Zedekiah answered, “I can't surrender to the Babylonians. I'm too afraid of the people of Judah who have already joined them. The Babylonians might hand me over to them, and they would torture me.”
20I said, “If you will just obey the Lord, the Babylonians won't hand you over to those Jews. You will be allowed to live, and all will go well for you. 21But the Lord has shown me that if you refuse to obey, 22then the women of your palace will be taken prisoner by Nebuchadnezzar's officials. And those women will say to you:
Friends you trusted led you astray.
Now you're trapped in mud,
and those friends you trusted
have all turned away.
23The Babylonian army will take your wives and children captive, you will be taken as a prisoner to the King of Babylonia, and Jerusalem will be burned down.”
24Zedekiah said, “Jeremiah, if you tell anyone what we have talked about, you might lose your life. 25And I'm sure that if my officials hear about our meeting, they will ask you what we said to each other. They might even threaten to kill you if you don't tell them. 26So if they question you, tell them you were begging me not to send you back to the prison at Jonathan's house, because going back there would kill you.”
27The officials did come and question me about my meeting with the king, and I told them exactly what he had ordered me to say. They never spoke to me about the meeting again, since no one had heard us talking.
28 I was held in the courtyard of the palace guards until the day Jerusalem was captured.
translation_text:
Bi dū Yeereemii ki tɔ́ dinyimbɔbilin
1Matan jipɔɔn Seefatiyawuu nì Geedaliyawuu jipɔɔn Paseewuur nì Seeleemiyawuu jipɔɔn Yukaal nì Maalkiya jipɔɔn Paseewuur nìn gbìl̄ tibɔti tin Yeereemii sòon̄ ki tùkū samaa kɔkɔ yii: 2«Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Un làá gbíntí kitiŋ nee poonee, kujaau nì ŋkùm nì bìlbil kúm di làá kpɔ̀-u. Ama un yaa nyáń kí cáá u-ba ki tīī Babiloon yabee làá ŋmátí. Tin an niliuee páatèe di sá u nín kaa kpíìyee.>»
3Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «M làá dū kitiŋ nee kí ŋá Babiloon janjaliibi ŋaan ní bí fōō-kì.»
4Niinee ní bikàliŋkpilib bí ubɔti yii: «Bí kpɔ̀ kijapaai nee, di sá yii tin u sòon̄ee yɔ̀tī bijanjaliibi nì bin kíǹ ki bí kitiŋ nee poonee wunti. Waa nyàab̀ samaa ŋanti, ama u-naabuŋu ní u nyàab̀.»
5Ní ubɔti Seedeesiyasi kíí yii: «U bí ni-ŋaan, m sá ubɔti, ama maa cáá mpɔn kí pìin̄-ni nsan ni ŋá ni nín là puee.»
6Bikàliŋkpilibee nìn cúú Yeereemii ki cáá-u ki tɔ́ ubɔti jipɔɔn Maalkiya nyimbɔbilin. Bi nìn dū iŋmii ní ki cúú Yeereemii ki cáa sīntì dinyimbɔbilin. Dinyimbɔbil gbanti nìn bí bijanjaliibi bin cí ubɔtee dumpu ní, ama nnyim nìn kpá di-poon, asee tikpati. An puee bi nín nìn dū Yeereemii ki tɔ́ee, u nìn nín sìntī tikpatin ní.
7Too, ueetiiyoopiija ubɔ nìn bí bi yíì-u Eebeedi-Meeleeki. U nìn sá ukàliŋkpil ní ki nìn bí ubɔti cindin. U nìn gbìl̄ yii bi dū Yeereemii ki tɔ́ dinyimbɔbilin. Ubɔti mun nìn kā Beenjameen punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpu. 8Niinee ní Eebeedi-Meeleeki nyáń dibeecindin ki cūtìi ká ubɔti ki bí-u yii: 9«Ti-baa ubɔti, binib nee nín ŋá Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii puee kaa ŋān̄. Bi dū-u ki tɔ́ dinyimbɔbilin. U làá kpú ŋkùm dinyimbɔbil gbantin, di sá yii tijin kaa ti bí kitiŋin.»
10Niinee ní ubɔti tīī ueetiiyoopiija Eebeedi-Meeleeki mara yii: «Si nì bininjab mmuŋku nì saalaa ń cù kí nyāntiń Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii dinyimbɔbilin ú taa kpú.»
11Eebeedi-Meeleeki nìn yōoǹ bininjab mmuŋku nì saalaa. U nìn kɔ́ dibeecindin kudii kun bí kunimbikpaafidii taapuee. Niinee ní u yōoǹ ticaliŋkpun. U nìn dūu kúĺ iŋmii pu ki cáa lāaǹ Yeereemii dinyimbɔbilin. 12Ní ueetiiyoopiija Eebeedi-Meeleeki bí Yeereemii yii: «Á dū ticaliŋkpunee kí fìn̄ a-ŋmɔŋŋmɔnti ní kí dū iŋmii kí cúú.»
Ní Yeereemii ŋá míǹ. 13Ní bi dáaĺ iŋmiiyee ki nyántìń-u dinyimbɔbilin. Míǹ boonee ní Yeereemii gbíntì bijanjaliibi bin cí ubɔtee cee.
Ubɔti bíi sòoǹ nì Yeereemii dibalin
14Ubɔti Seedeesiyasi nìn tú bi yíiń Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii, ní u cáá-u ki cūnnì kunimbɔtidii punyɔkɔki kitataatii poon. U nìn bí-u yii: «M làá bàlifì-si tibɔti, á taa báĺ-mi báà tiba.»
15Ní Yeereemii kíí Seedeesiyasi yii: «M yaa tùkū-si ibaamɔn, a làá yàntī bí kpɔ̀-mi. M yaa tí tīī-si isaŋkaaa, aa làá dū-i kí tɔ̄ ditundi.»
16Niinee ní ubɔti Seedeesiyasi pūtì ki pōoǹ Yeereemii dibalin yii: «Nì ti-Dindaan un bí dimaŋfalin nee, m pūtì yii maa làá kpɔ̀-si, kaa làá tí dū-si kí tīī bin nyàab̀ kí kpɔ̀-see.»
17Ní Yeereemii bí Seedeesiyasi yii: «Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <A yaa nyáń ki dū a-ba ki tīī Babiloon bɔtiu janjakpilibee, si nì a-dicaŋkun yab làá ŋmátí, ní baa làá wà Jeerusaleem tiŋki ŋŋmi. 18Ama a yaa kaa nyáń ki dū a-ba ki tīī Babiloon bɔtiu janjakpilibee, Jeerusaleem tiŋki làá kɔ́ Babiloon yab ŋaan. Bi làá sēē-kì ŋŋmi, ní siiyee, aa làá ŋmátí bi-ŋaan.>» 19Ubɔti Seedeesiyasi bí Yeereemii yii: «M fàŋkí Juuda yab bin kɔ́ Babiloon yab ŋaanee. Babiloon yab ŋūǹ kí dū-mi kí ŋá bi-ŋaan bíǹ ń sàaǹ-mi.»
20Ama ní Yeereemii kíí-u yii: «Baa làá dū-si kí ŋá bi-ŋaan. Pīlifì tin ti-Dindaan dī m-pu ki sòon̄ nì see. A yaa ŋá míǹ, án làá nīn ŋān̄ ki tīī-si ní á ŋmátí. 21Ama a yaa yíì kaa cáá a-ba ki tīīyee, ti-Dindaan nín lēē tin làá bàń a-pu ki dàkā-mee sɔ̀. 22Binimpoobi bin kɔkɔ kíǹ ki bí a-beecindinee, bi làá cúú-bi kí cùnnì kí tīī Babiloon bɔtiu janjakpilib. Bi làá dāá gāā-si nlan yii:
«<A-bɔɔmɔmmɔntiibi
baasii kíil̀-si ní!
A cáá a-taaŋi ki múĺ tikpatin,
ní bíǹ sáǹ ki fá-si!>
23Bi làá dāá cúú a-nimpoobi nì a-jipɔmbi kí cùnnì kí tīī Babiloon yab. Sii a-ba kaa làá dāá ŋmátí kí nyā bi-ŋaan. Di sá yii Babiloon bɔtiu làá dāá cúú-si ní kí sēē a-tiŋki ŋŋmi.»
24Ní ubɔti Seedeesiyasi bí Yeereemii yii: «Ubɔ yaa pée gbìl̄ tibɔti nee, see m kūū-si. 25Bikàlinjakpilib yaa gbìl̄ yii m sòon̄ nì si, ní ki dɔ́miń a-cee kí bí-si yii: <Tùkù-ti tin a sòon̄ nì ubɔtee! Á taa báĺ-ti báà tiba, an yaa sá fám ti làá kpɔ̀-si. Ubɔti bí-si yii ba ní?> 26Á kíí-bi yii: <M gbāam̀ ubɔti yii ú taa gíiǹ-mi Joonatan dumpu ḿ tin kpú niin.>»
27Míǹ ní bikàliŋkpilib kɔkɔ lafun dɔ́miń Yeereemii cee ki bālifì-u tibɔti. Ama Yeereemii kíí-bi kii ubɔti nín tīī-u mara yii ú kíí puee ní. Niinee ní bi yāntì-u soooo kaa ŋá-u tiba, kun puee báà ubɔ kaa gbìl̄ tin u nì ubɔti sòon̄ee. 28Niinee Yeereemii gbíntì bijanjaliibi bin cí ubɔtee dumpu ki tin sāā ŋyunti ŋun bi jáń ki fōō Jeerusaleem tiŋkee.
Babiloon yab jáń ki fōō Jeerusaleem tiŋki
(Kpèè 52.4-16, 2 Bib 25.1-12)
Bi nín jáń ki fōō Jeerusaleem tiŋkee, tin jítèe sèé:

english_text:
Jerusalem Is Captured by the Babylonians
(Jeremiah 52.4-16; 2 Kings 25.1-12)
1-3In the tenth month of the ninth year that Zedekiah was king of Judah, King Nebuchadnezzar and the Babylonian army began their attack on Jerusalem. They kept the city surrounded for a year and a half. Then, on the ninth day of the fourth month of the eleventh year that Zedekiah was king, they broke through the city walls.
After Jerusalem was captured, Nebuchadnezzar's highest officials, including Nebo Sarsechim and Nergal Sharezer from Simmagir, took their places at Middle Gate to show they were in control of the city.
4When King Zedekiah and his troops saw that Jerusalem had been captured, they tried to escape from the city that same night. They went to the king's garden, where they slipped through the gate between the two city walls and headed toward the Jordan River valley. 5But the Babylonian troops caught up with them near Jericho. They arrested Zedekiah and took him to the town of Riblah in the land of Hamath, where Nebuchadnezzar put him on trial, then found him guilty, 6and gave orders for him to be punished. Zedekiah's sons were killed there in front of him, and so were the leaders of Judah's ruling families. 7Then his eyes were poked out, and he was put in chains, so he could be dragged off to Babylonia.
8Meanwhile, the Babylonian army had burned the houses in Jerusalem, including the royal palace, and they had broken down the city walls. 9Nebuzaradan, the Babylonian officer in charge of the guards, led away everyone from the city as prisoners, even those who had deserted to Nebuchadnezzar. 10Only the poorest people who owned no land were left behind in Judah, and Nebuzaradan gave them fields and vineyards.
11Nebuchadnezzar had given the following orders to Nebuzaradan: 12“Find Jeremiah and keep him safe. Take good care of him and do whatever he asks.”
13Nebuzaradan, Nebushazban, Nergal Sharezer, and the other officers of King Nebuchadnezzar 14sent some of their troops to bring me from the courtyard of the royal palace guards. They put me in the care of Gedaliah son of Ahikam and told him to take me to my home. And so I was allowed to stay with the people who remained in Judah.
The Lord Promises To Protect Ebedmelech
15While I was a prisoner in the courtyard of the palace guard, the Lord told me to say 16to Ebedmelech from Ethiopia:
I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. I warned everyone that I would bring disaster, not prosperity, to this city. Now very soon I will do what I said, and you will see it happen. 17-18But because you trusted me, I will protect you from the officials of Judah, and when Judah is struck by disaster, I will rescue you and keep you alive. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
1Ubɔti Seedeesiyasi nín kpántì Juuda bɔtiu abin awa ŋmasaalaatiu poon ní Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar nì u-janjaliibi kɔkɔ dɔ́miń ki māntìi tú Jeerusaleem tiŋki kí já nì kì. 2Abin ali boon uŋmananaati poon iwiin iwa dal ní Babiloon yab sāā ki cíl̀ digundi din bi máń ki tú Jeerusaleem tiŋkee. 3Niinee ní Babiloon bɔtiu janjakpilib kɔkɔ kɔ́ Jeerusaleem tiŋkin ní ki cūtìi kāl̀ Kansikin punyɔkɔki poon. Ujanjakpil Neergaal-Sareeseer nì ubɔti tɔntɔŋkpilib Samgaar-Neeboo nì Sarseekiim nì Babiloon bɔtiu janjakpilib bin kíǹee kɔkɔ nìn bí poon.
4Ŋyunti ŋun Juuda bɔtiu Seedeesiyasi nì u-janjaliibi ká-bee ní bi dū itaaci. Kunyeeu ní bi nìn sáǹ ki nyáń Jeerusaleem tiŋkin. Bi nìn dūu dī ubɔti kpaabun ki tin nyáń kipunyɔkɔ kin bí agun ali kansikinee ní ki fōō nsan ŋun cá Jɔɔdan tantakalinee. 5Ama Babiloon janjaliibi nìn kùl̄ ki bīiǹ bi-boon, ní ki tin cúú Seedeesiyasi Jeeriikoo tantakalin. Bi nìn cáá-u ki cūnnì Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar cee, Riibila, Amati tiŋkin. Niin ní Neebukadineesaar sòon̄ Seedeesiyasi bɔti. 6Riibila niin ní Babiloon bɔtiu kūū Seedeesiyasi jipɔmbi bi-baa nimbilaaliyin ki kpáaǹ Juuda yab bɔtibiliŋ kɔkɔ. 7Míǹ boonee ní bi sāā ki cɔ́tì Seedeesiyasi nimbiliŋ, ní ki dū tasa kúti kusakai ki bóob́-u ki cáá-u ki cūnnì Babiloon tiŋkin.
8Ní Babiloon yab tūū dibeecindi nì binib diiŋŋi ŋŋmi. Bi nìn gbáń ki wīī Jeerusaleem gundi. 9Bijanjaliibi bin cí ubɔtee kpiliu Neebusaradan nìn cúú binib bin nìn kíǹ ki kā Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee ki cūnnì Babiloon tiŋkin kuyuŋu. U nìn cáá bin nìn dū bi-ba ki tīī Babiloon bɔtiuee nì ŋŋal pu tɔntɔnliibi bin kíǹee ki cūnnì. 10Ama u nìn yāntì bisoodambi nì bin kaa pée cáá tibee Juuda tiŋkin, ní ki nìn dū fiinyi kpaaŋŋi nì tisati ki yākatì-bi.
Bi nyántì Yeereemii sarkan
11Ubɔti Neebukadineesaar nìn tīī bijanjaliibi bin cí ubɔtee kpiliu Neebusaradan mara Yeereemii pu yii: 12«Á cùú nyàab̀-u kí wúń u-pu ubɔ ń taa ŋá-u tikpitil tiba. U yaa bālifì-si tiŋyee, á ŋá míǹ kí tīī-u.» 13Niinee ní bijanjaliibi bin cí ubɔtee kpiliu Neebusaradan nì ubɔti tɔntɔnliibi kpiliu Neebusasban nì ujanjakpil Neergaal-Sareeseer nì Babiloon bɔtiu janjakpilib bin kíǹee kɔkɔ sòon̄ ki gbìlīǹ tɔb. 14Bi nìn tú binib bí cùú nyàabìń Yeereemii bijanjaliibi bin cí ubɔtee dumpu. Bi nìn dū-u ki ŋúbiǹ Ayiikaam jipɔɔn Geedaliyasi, Safan naantiiu. Geedaliyasi nìn pú-u nsan ú kpì u-dumpu. Míǹ ní Yeereemii nìn gbíntì samaa kansikin ki kóò.
Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ tin Eebeedi-Meeleeki puee
15Ŋyunti ŋun Yeereemii nìn dáá pīī bijanjaliibi bin cí ubɔti dumpuee, ti-Dindaan nìn sòon̄ nì u yii: 16«Cùú tùkù ueetiiyoopiija Eebeedi-Meeleeki yii: <Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín lī puee sèé: M nìn sòon̄ yii an kaa sá nnaam ní m làá cáań kí tɔ̄ Jeerusaleem yab pu ama nnaabu. Too, m nín nìn sòon̄ puee, m làá ŋá míǹ. An kaa làá sūŋkì, sii a-ba nimbil làá ká. 17Ama ŋwiin gbantee, m làá fīī-si, man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ. Maa làá dū-si kí ŋá bin a fàŋkée ŋaan. 18Tiŋman, m làá fīī a-maŋfal. Aa làá kpú kujaaun. Kun a làá páatée dee, kun puee a dū a-mákal ki páaǹ m-pu. Ti-Dindaan di sòon̄ míǹ.>»

english_text:
Jeremiah Is Set Free
1I was led away in chains along with the people of Judah and Jerusalem who were being taken to Babylonia. Nebuzaradan was the officer in charge of the guard, and while we were stopped at Ramah, the Lord caused him to set me free. 2Nebuzaradan said:
Jeremiah, the Lord your God warned your people that he would bring disaster on this land. 3But they continued to rebel against him, and now he has punished them just as he threatened.
4Today I am taking the chains off your wrists and setting you free! If you want to, you can come with me to Babylonia, and I will see that you are taken care of. Or if you decide to stay here, you can go wherever you wish. 5King Nebuchadnezzar has chosen Gedaliah to rule Judah. You can live near Gedaliah, and he will provide for you, or you can live anywhere else you choose.
Nebuzaradan gave me a supply of food, then let me leave. 6I decided to stay with the people of Judah, and I went to live near Gedaliah in Mizpah.
The Harvest Is Brought In
7-8 Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, together with Johanan and Jonathan, the two sons of Kareah, had been officers in Judah's army. And so had Seraiah the son of Tanhumeth, the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Jezaniah from Maacah. They and their troops had been stationed outside Jerusalem and had not been captured. They heard that Gedaliah had been chosen to rule Judah, and that the poorest men, women, and children had not been taken away to Babylonia. So they went to Mizpah and met with their new ruler.
9Gedaliah told them, “There's no need to be afraid of the Babylonians. Everything will be fine, if we live peacefully and obey King Nebuchadnezzar. 10I will stay here at Mizpah and meet with the Babylonian officials on each of their visits. But you must go back to your towns and bring in the harvest, then store the wine, olive oil, and dried fruit.”
11-12Earlier, when the Babylonians had invaded Judah, many of the Jews escaped to Moab, Ammon, Edom, and several other countries. But these Jews heard that the king of Babylonia had appointed Gedaliah as ruler of Judah, and that only a few people were left there. So the Jews in these other countries came back to Judah and helped with the grape and fruit harvest, which was especially large that year.
Gedaliah Is Murdered
13One day, Johanan got together with some of the other men who had been army officers, and they came to Mizpah and met with Gedaliah. 14They said, “Gedaliah, we came to warn you that King Baalis of Ammon hired Ishmael to murder you!”
Gedaliah refused to believe them, 15so Johanan went to Gedaliah privately and said, “Let me kill Ishmael. No one will find out who did it. There are only a few people left in Judah, but they are depending on you. And if you are murdered, they will be scattered or killed.”
16Gedaliah answered, “Don't kill Ishmael! What you've said about him can't be true.”
translation_text:
Yeereemii cūtìi kāl̀ Miisipa
1Yeereemii nìn bí binib bin bi nìn cúú Jeerusaleem nì Juuda timmun kí cùnnì Babiloon tiŋkin kuyuŋuee poon. Bi nìn bóob́ u mun ikusaka. Ama bijanjaliibi bin cí ubɔtee kpiliu Neebusaradan nìn nyántì-u bisarkadambee kansikin ní ki yāntì u búntì Raama tiŋkin. 2Ujanjakpilee nìn yíiń Yeereemii ní ki bí-u yii: «Ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu nìn sòon̄ ki síiǹ yii nnaabu nee làá bàń Jeerusaleem tiŋki pu. 3U lafun cáań nnaabuee ki tɔ́ ki-pu. U nín nìn sòon̄ kí ŋá puee, míǹ ní u ŋá nee. Di sá yii ni yīntiǹ ti-Dindaan kaa pílifì u-nyɔkɔ, an pu ní tin bí nee kɔkɔ bāań-ni. 4Too, m làá bútí-si ikusaka in kā a-ŋaan nee díǹ. A yaa tí là kí nóó-mi tí cù Babiloon tiŋkinaaa, a ŋūǹ kí dāan̄, m làá wúń a-pu. Ama a yaa kaa tí là kí dāan̄aaa, á taa dāan̄. Kpèè, kitiŋ kɔkɔ di dɔ̄ a-nimbiinee, a ŋūǹ kí cù laakin a yaa lèe.»
5Kii Yeereemii nín kaa nìn kíí tiba puee ní Neebusaradan kútì ki lī yii: «A ŋūǹ kí gítí Ayiikaam jipɔɔn Geedaliyasi, Safan naantiiu cee. Babiloon bɔtiu dū úǹ ní ki kāaǹ gɔmina ú nīn kpèé Juuda timmu. Nín̄ cá kí kàl̄ u-cee samaa kansikin àá á nīn cá laakin a yaa lèe.»
Míǹ boonee ní bijanjaliibi bin cí ubɔtee kpiliu tīī Yeereemii tijin tin u làá nīn jīǹ nsanee ní ki pú-u tiwan tiba mun, ní ki yāntì u búntì. 6Niinee Yeereemii nín cá Ayiikaam jipɔɔn Geedaliyasi cee Miisipa tiŋkin. U nìn kɔ́ binib bin nìn kíǹ ki kóò kitiŋee poonee kansikin.
Juuda yab kóoǹ ki kpáfì Geedaliyasi cee
(Kpèè 2 Bib 25.23-24)
7Tisatinee, ajanjakiti nì ŋi-janjakpilib nìn dáá bí. Bi nìn gbìl̄ yii Babiloon bɔtiu nìn dū Ayiikaam jipɔɔn Geedaliyasi ki kāaǹ gɔmina ú nīn kpèé Juuda tiŋki. U nìn dū bisoodambi nì bininjab nì binimpoobi nì mbiyaamu, an dàkà yii bin kɔkɔ baa nìn cúú ki cūnnì Babiloon kuyuŋuee ki ŋúbiǹ-u. 8Niinee ní akitee dɔ́miń Miisipa ki kútì Geedaliyasi pu. Ŋi-janjakpilib di nìn sá Neetaniyawuu jipɔɔn Isimaayeel nì Kareeya jipɔmbi liitil Yoowanan nì Joonatan, nì Taneewumeeti jipɔɔn Seeraya nì Maaka jipɔmbi Eefayii un sá Neetoofa tiŋkinee nì Yasaniyawuu un sá Meeka tiŋkinee. 9Ní Ayiikaam jipɔɔn Geedaliyasi, Safan naantiiu bí bijanjakpilib nì bi-bijanjaliibi yii: «Taa fàŋkìmaan kí nīn bí Babiloon yab taapu.
