Kàl̄maan kitiŋ nee ni kí nīn tūǹ ditundi ki tìì Babiloon yab. Ni yaa ŋá míǹ, an làá nīn sɔ̀m̀ nì ni, man di tùkū-ni míǹ. 10Man kā Miisipa tiŋkin doo nimbi yil pu Babiloon yab bin dòoń ti-ceeyee cee. Ama nimbee, ní kìtīmaan fiinyi biliŋ nì isufi in kíǹee biliŋ nì ŋkpam subiliŋ. Ní kpāafì ni-kpaajinti kí nīn kā ntimu mun poon ni kóòyee.»
11Míǹ mbaantiim ní Juuda yab bin nìn bíń Moowaab yab nì Amɔn yab nì Eedoom yab timmun nì ntimu mun kíǹee poonee nìn gbìl̄ yii Babiloon bɔtiu nìn yāntì binib biba kíǹ Juuda timmun, ní ki lēē Ayiikaam jipɔɔn Geedaliyasi, Safan naantiiu ú nīn kpèé-bi. 12Niinee ní Juuda yab kɔkɔ nyánní laakin bi nìn sáǹ ki cūtìi kɔ́ee ki gítìń. Bi nìn dūu bāań Juuda tiŋkin Miisipa, Geedaliyasi cee. Bi nìn kītì niin fiinyi biliŋ nì asubil aba mun tikpil.
Bi kūū Geedaliyasi
(Kpèè 2 Bib 25.25-26)
13Dalbee ní Kareeya jipɔɔn Yoowanan nì ajanjakiti kpilib bin nìn bí tisatinee dɔ́miń ki ká Geedaliyasi Miisipa tiŋkin. 14U nìn bí-u yii: «Mimmee aa nyí yii Amɔn yab bɔtiu Baliisi lēē Neetaniya jipɔɔn Isimaayeel ú kpɔ̀-saaa?»
Ama Ayiikaam jipɔɔn Geedaliyasi kaa nìn fōō ki kíí. 15Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, Kareeya jipɔɔn Yoowanan nìn dɔ́miń Miisipa ki ká-u dibalin ní ki nìn bí-u yii: «Yàntī ḿ cù kí kpɔ̀ Neetaniya jipɔɔn Isimaayeel dibalin. Ubɔ kaa làá béé. Àá a là yii úǹ nín kpɔ̀-si ní? U yaa kūū-see, Juuda yab bin kɔkɔ bàà kóoǹ ki kpáfì a-ceeyee làá fàtīí tí yàl̄, ní tin bàà kíǹ Juuda beelinee ń wāŋkì.»
16Ama ní Ayiikaam jipɔɔn Geedaliyasi kíí Kareeya jipɔɔn Yoowanan yii: «Taa ŋá míǹ, kun puee tin a sòoǹ Isimaayeel pu nee kaa sá ibaamɔn.»

english_text:
1 But in the seventh month, Ishmael came to Mizpah with ten of his soldiers. He had been one of the king's officials and was a member of the royal family. Ishmael and his men were invited to eat with Gedaliah. 2During the meal, Ishmael and his soldiers killed Gedaliah, the man chosen as ruler of Judah by the king of Babylonia. 3Then they killed the Jews who were with Gedaliah, and they also killed the Babylonian soldiers who were there.
4The next day, the murders had still not been discovered, 5when 80 men came down the road toward Mizpah from the towns of Shechem, Shiloh, and Samaria. They were on their way to the temple to offer gifts of grain and incense to the Lord. They had shaved off their beards, torn their clothes, and cut themselves, because they were mourning.
6Ishmael went out the town gate to meet them. He pretended to be weeping, and he asked them to come into Mizpah to meet with Gedaliah, the ruler of Judah. 7But after they were inside the town, Ishmael ordered his soldiers to kill them and throw their bodies into a well. 8He let ten of the men live, because they offered to give him supplies of wheat, barley, olive oil, and honey they had hidden in a field. 9The well that he filled with bodies had been dug by King Asa of Judah to store rainwater, because he was afraid that King Baasha of Israel might surround Mizpah and keep the people from getting to their water supply.
10Nebuzaradan, King Nebuchadnezzar's officer in charge of the guard, had left King Zedekiah's daughters and many other people at Mizpah, and he had put Gedaliah in charge of them. But now Ishmael took them all prisoner and led them toward Ammon, on the other side of the Jordan River.
11Johanan and the other army officers heard what Ishmael had done. 12So they and their troops chased Ishmael and caught up with him at the large pit at Gibeon. 13When Ishmael's prisoners saw Johanan and the officers, they were happy 14and turned around and ran toward Johanan. 15But Ishmael and eight of his men escaped and went to Ammon.
Johanan Decides To Take the People to Egypt
16Johanan and the officers had rescued the women, children, and royal officials that Ishmael had taken prisoner after killing Gedaliah. Johanan led the people from Gibeon 17-18toward Egypt. They wanted to go there, because they were afraid of what the Babylonians would do when they found out that Ishmael had killed Gedaliah, the ruler appointed by King Nebuchadnezzar.
The People Ask Jeremiah To Pray for Them
On the way to Egypt, we stopped at the town of Geruth Chimham near Bethlehem.
translation_text:
1Ama dibindi poon ŋmaluluútiuee ní Neetaniya jipɔɔn Isimaayeel, Eeliisama naantiiu dɔ́miń Miisipa Geedaliyasi cee. Isimaayeel nìn sá ubɔti dicaŋkun niliu ní ki nìn sá ubɔti kàliŋkpilib ubɔ. U nì bininjab saalaa di nìn táá ki dɔ́miń. Ŋyunti ŋun bi kā u-cee ki jīǹee, 2ní Neetaniya jipɔɔn Isimaayeel nì bininjab saalaa bin nóoń-uee yíkì dicilpu, ní ki dū bi-tàataajimmu ki gāatì ki kūū Ayiikaam jipɔɔn Geedaliyasi, Safan naantiiu. Unil un Babiloon bɔtiu nìn kāaǹ Juuda tiŋki pu gɔminee, bi nín kūū-u puee dee. 3Míǹ boonee ní Isimaayeel kūū Juuda yab bin kɔkɔ nìn bí Geedaliyasi cee Miisipa tiŋkinee. U nìn kūū ki kpáaǹ Babiloon janjaliibi bin nìn bí niinee.
Isimaayeel kūū bisaŋkinliibi imuŋku inaa
4Bi kūū Geedaliyasi iwiin ili jítì báà ubɔ kaa gbìl̄ u-kúm pu. 5Bininjab imuŋku inaa nìn nyánní Siikeem nì Siiloo nì Samaarii timmun ki bāań. Bi nìn kōol̀ bi-nyimpuliŋ, ki pēē ikpalcati ki cáfì cáfì bi-wunti. Bi nìn tú tijimpin saraabi nì bitalaalutuukaabi kí cùú ŋá ti-Dindaan saraabi kunimbɔtidiin. 6Neetaniya jipɔɔn Isimaayeel nìn nyáń Miisipa tiŋkin ki túŋkì-bi nsanni ki sūǹ. U bàn̄ bi-ceeyee, ní ki bí-bi yii: «Dāam̄maan Ayiikaam jipɔɔn Geedaliyasi cee.»
7Ama ŋyunti ŋun bi kɔ́ kitiŋinee ní Isimaayeel nì u-yab kūū-bi ní ki dū-bi ki tɔ́ dinyimbɔbil diban. 8Bi-kansikinee binib saalaa nìn bí Isimaayeel yii: «Taa kpɔ̀-ti, di sá yii ti cáá bilee nì ɔɔji nì ŋkpam nì tisiil ki bál̀ tisatin.»
Niinee ní Isimaayeel yāntì-bi kaa kūū-bi kii u nín kūū bi-jutiibi puee. 9Dinyimbɔbil din poon Isimaayeel nìn dū binib bin u kūūyee nìn sá dinyimbɔbil din ubɔti Asaa nìn yāntì bi gbìn̄ ŋyunti ŋun u nì Isirayeel bɔtiu Basaa nìn bí kujaaunee ní. Dinyimbɔbilee nìn sá dikpaandi. Dinyimbɔbil gbantin ní Neetaniya jipɔɔn nìn dū binib bin u kūūyee ki gbéeǹ.
10Míǹ boonee ní Isimaayeel cúú bin kɔkɔ nìn bí Miisipa tiŋkinee nì ubɔti sapɔmbi ki pīiǹ kudii. U nìn cúú bin kɔkɔ bijanjaliibi bin cí ubɔtee kpiliu Neebusaradan nìn dūu ŋúbiǹ Geedaliyasee. Míǹ boonee ní u kpáaǹ bisarkadambee ki búntì Amɔn yab cee.
Bi fīī bin Isimaayeel cúú kuyuŋuee
11Kareeya jipɔɔn Yoowanan nì ajanjakiti kpilib bin nìn bí u-ceeyee gbìl̄ nnikpaakoon ŋun Neetaya jipɔɔn Isimaayeel ŋée. 12Niinee ní bi kóoǹ bijanjaliibi kɔkɔ ki kpáfì kí cùú jáǹ-u. Bi nìn jìn̄ ki tin cúú-u Gabawɔn puuku caŋin. 13Binib bin Isimaayeel nìn cúúyee nín ká Yoowanan nì bijanjakpilib bin nìn nóó-uee, ní an mɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi. 14Niinee ní bin kɔkɔ Isimaayeel nìn cúú Miisipa tiŋkinee fātì ki nín cá Kareeya jipɔɔn Yoowanan cee. 15Ama Neetaniya jipɔɔn Isimaayeel nín ká Yoowanan tóobiń-bee ní u sáǹ ki nín cá Amɔn yab cee.
16Isimaayeel nín kūū Geedaliyasee, u nìn cúú binib biba Miisipa tiŋkin. Bi-kansikin bin nìn dáá bí dimaŋfalinee, Kareeya jipɔɔn Yoowanan nì bijanjakpilib bin nìn céeǹ-uee nìn kóoǹ-bi ki kpáfì. Bíǹ di sá bininjab - an dàkà yii bijanjaliibi -, nì binimpoobi nì mbiyaamu nì bifaabi, an dàkà yii bin kɔkɔ Yoowanan nì bijanjakpilib nìn yōoǹní Gabawɔn tiŋkin ki gíiǹnée. 17Bi nìn yíkìi kāl̀ nsan pu ki nín cá, ki bàn̄ ki yúl̀ anicandiin ŋin bí Kimeeyam, Beetileem tiŋki caŋinee. Bi nìn là kí nìkī kí nīn cá Eejipiti tiŋkin. 18Di sá yii Isimaayeel nín kūū Geedaliyasi un Babiloon bɔtiu nìn kāaǹ gɔmina ú nīn kpèé Juuda tiŋkee, bi nìn kíǹ ki fàŋkí Babiloon yab ní.

english_text:
1Johanan, Jezaniah, the other army officers, and everyone else in the group, came to me 2and said, “Please, Jeremiah, pray to the Lord your God for us. Judah used to have many people, but as you can see, only a few of us are left. 3Ask the Lord to tell us where he wants us to go and what he wants us to do.”
4“All right,” I answered, “I will pray to the Lord your God, and I will tell you everything he says.”
5They answered, “The Lord himself will be our witness that we promise to do whatever he says, 6even if it isn't what we want to do. We will obey the Lord so that all will go well for us.”
7Ten days later, the Lord gave me an answer for 8Johanan, the officers, and the other people. So I called them together 9and told them that the Lord God of Israel had said:
You asked Jeremiah to pray and find out what you should do. 10I am sorry that I had to punish you, and so I now tell you to stay here in Judah, where I will plant you and build you up, instead of tearing you down and uprooting you. 11Don't be afraid of the King of Babylonia. I will protect you from him, 12and I will even force him to have mercy on you and give back your farms.
13But you might keep on saying, “We won't stay here in Judah, and we won't obey the Lord our God. 14We are going to Egypt, where there is plenty of food and no danger of war.”
15People of Judah, you survived when the Babylonian army attacked. Now you are planning to move to Egypt, and if you do go, this is what will happen. 16-17You are afraid of war, starvation, and disease here in Judah, but they will follow you to Egypt and kill you there. None of you will survive the disasters I will send.
18I, the Lord, was angry with the people of Jerusalem and punished them. And if you go to Egypt, I will be angry and punish you the same way. You will never again see your homeland. People will be horrified at what I do to you, and they will use the name of your city as a curse word.
Jeremiah Gives a Warning
19I told the people:
You escaped the disaster that struck Judah, but now the Lord warns you to stay away from Egypt. 20You asked me to pray and find out what the Lord our God wants you to do, and you promised to obey him. But that was a terrible mistake, 21because now that I have given you the Lord's answer, you refuse to obey him. 22And so, you will die in Egypt from war, hunger, and disease.
translation_text:
Yeereemii sáŋkì bijanjakpilib bí taa cù Eejipiti tiŋkin
1Niinee bijanjakpilib kɔkɔ, cilinjee Kareeya jipɔɔn Yoowanan nì Oosaya jipɔɔn Asariya nì samaa kɔkɔ, bikpaambi nì ŋwaamu kɔkɔ cūtìi ká 2Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii. Bi nìn bí-u yii:
«Ti gbàam̄-si, fōō tin ti là kí mèè-si nee: Gbàam̀ ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu timbi bin ŋmátì ki kíǹ nee pu. Di sá yii taa ti náaǹ kii sii a-ba nín wāĺ pu nee. 3Míǹ puee bàlifì ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu ú dàkà-ti nsan ŋun sá tí dēe, nì kun ti máaǹ kí ŋée.»
4Ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii kíí-bi yii: «M gbìl̄, m làá mèè ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu kii ni nín bālifì-mi puee. Míǹ boonee, m làá tùkù-ni ti-Dindaan nín kíí puee, maa làá báĺ-ni báà tiba.»
5Ní bi kíí Yeereemii yii: «Ti pōoǹ kí ŋá tin ti-Dindaan làá tùkù-si á dūú nàatī-tee deedeedee. Ti-Dindaan ń nīn sá ibaamɔn seeradaaŋwu ki tīī-ti. 6Timbi di tú-si á bàlifì ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu. Tin u yaa lēe yaa ŋān̄aaa, an yaa kaa ŋān̄aaa, ti làá ŋá míǹ. Niinee, án làá nīn ŋān̄ ki tīī-ti, di sá yii ti làá pīlifì ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu nyɔkɔ.»
7Iwiin saalaa boonee, ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Yeereemii. 8Niinee ní u yíiń Kareeya jipɔɔn Yoowanan nì bijanjakpilib bin nìn bí u-ceeyee, nì samaa kɔkɔ, bikpaambi nì ŋwaamu. 9U nìn bí-bi yii: «Ni lēē-mi yii ḿ mèè ti-Dindaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu ni-pu. U nín lī puee sèé:
10«<Ni yaa kíí kí nīn kā kitiŋ nee poonee,
maa ti làá nàan̄-kì,
ama m làá mā m-nibul.
M làá cóoń-ni kii bi nín cōontí busubu puee,
maa ti làá cóotí-ni dalba dalba.
M làá ŋāŋkì tikpitil tin kɔkɔ m ŋá-nee.
11Kɔŋkɔnnee, ní taa ti fàŋkì Babiloon bɔtiu un ni fàŋkí yɔ́kɔ́ yɔkɔ nee.
Man ni-Dindaan di bí-ni yii
ní taa ti fàŋkì-u.
Di sá yii m bí ni-cee,
kí fīī-ni kí nyāntí u-ŋaan kí líí.
12M làá yàntī ní ká diyimɔɔl u-cee,
ní ú sɔ̄ ni-saai,
kí yàntī ní gítiń ni-tiŋki pu.>»
13Ama ni yaa bí yii: «Taa làá kàl̄ kitiŋ nee poon! ní ki yíì kaa pílifì ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu nyɔkɔ», 14ní ki yaa lī yii: «Aayee! Ti làá cù Eejipiti tiŋkin ní. Niinee, taa làá ti ká kujaau, kaa làá ti gbìl̄ iyin in bi búǹ kí cù kujaauee pu, ní ŋkùm kaa làá ti nyā ti-pu. Niin ní ti là kí tin nín̄ bí.» 15Míǹ puee nimbi Juuda yab bin kíǹee, ní pīlifì ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee. Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀.
Ni yaa gbíntìi cɔ́ yii ni làá cù Eejipiti,
ni yaa lafun sáǹ ki cūtìi kɔ́ niinee,
16kujaau kun ni fàŋkée
làá bàń-ni Eejipiti tiŋkin niin,
ní ŋkùm min bɔti páb́-ni nee
ń páań ni-boon niin,
ní ní kpúń niin.
17Bin kɔkɔ làá lēē
kí cùú nīn kóò Eejipiti tiŋkinee,
kujaau nì ŋkùm nì bìlbil kúm di làá kpɔ̀-bi.
Báà ubɔ kaa làá dāá ŋmátí
kí nyā nnaabu ŋun m làá dāá dūú tɔ̄ bi-puee ni.
18Ní Yeereemii gíti bí yii: «Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <M kpáatì m-ŋuul nì mbum ki pɔ̀l̄ Jeerusaleem yab pu. Míǹ mbaantiim ní m làá dāá kpáatí m-ŋuul nì mbum kí pɔ̀l̄ nimbi bin làá cùú kɔ́ Eejipiti tiŋkinee pu. Niinee bi yaa làá dāá tɔ̄ ubɔ mbusu àá kí sòoǹ kubɔbiiu kubɔ pu àá tibɔti tin cáá tifaandee pu àá kí kɔ́ǹ ubɔ icooyee, bíǹ ní bi làá dāá yòon̄ ŋabika. Ni pée gíti kpá kí ká kitiŋ nee.>»
19Ní Yeereemii kútì ki lī yii: «Nimbi Juuda nibul din kíǹee, m bíi kpáafí-ni díǹ. Ti-Dindaan di bíi tìì-ni mara yii ní taa cù Eejipiti, ní béé míǹ. 20Ni tīī-mi ditundi yii ḿ bàlifì ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu dibalifil. Ni bí-mi yii: <Mèè ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu kí tīī-ti. Tùkù-ti tin kɔkɔ u làá tùkù-see, ti làá ŋá míǹ.> Ŋwiin gbantee, an nìn sá nì bugbambu ní ni sòon̄ míǹ. 21Di sá yii díǹ nee, m bíi tùkù-ni tin ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu kíí-nee. Ama naa bíi pílifí tin ti-Dindaan dī m-pu ki sòon̄ee. 22Too, ní béé tiŋan yii kujaau nì ŋkùm nì bìlbil kúm di làá kpɔ̀-ni kitiŋ kin poon ni là kí sāǹ kí tin kɔ́ nee!»

english_text:
The People Go to Egypt
1I told the people everything the Lord had told me. 2But Azariah, Johanan and some other arrogant men said to me, “You're lying! The Lord didn't tell you to say that we shouldn't go to Egypt. 3Baruch son of Neriah must have told you to say that. He wants the Babylonians to capture us, so they can take us away to Babylonia or even kill us.”
4Johanan, the other army officers, and everyone else refused to stay in Judah in spite of the Lord's command. 5 So Johanan and the officers led us away toward Egypt. The group that left Judah included those who had been scattered in other countries and who had then come back to live in Judah. 6Baruch and I and others in the group had been staying with Gedaliah, because Nebuzaradan, the Babylonian officer in charge of the guard, had ordered him to take care of the king's daughters and quite a few men, women, and children.
7The people disobeyed the Lord and went to Egypt. The group had settled in Tahpanhes, 8when the Lord told me:
9Jeremiah, carry some large stones to the entrance of the government building in Tahpanhes. Bury the stones underneath the brick pavement and be sure the Jews are watching.
10Then tell them that I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, have sent for my servant, Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia. I will bring him here and have him set up his throne and his royal tent over these stones that I told you to bury. 11He will attack Egypt and kill many of its people; others will die of disease or be dragged away as prisoners. 12-13I will let him set Egypt's temples on fire, and he will either burn or carry off their idols. He will destroy the sacred monuments at the temple of the sun-god. Then Nebuchadnezzar will pick the land clean, just like a shepherd picking the lice off his clothes. And he will return safely home.
translation_text:
Bi cáá Yeereemii ki cūnnì Eejipiti mpɔn
1Yeereemii nìn dū tibɔti nee kɔkɔ ki nāatì binib bin kɔkɔ nìn bí niinee. An nìn sá tibɔti tin ti-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu nìn dī u-pu ki sòon̄ee ní. 2Niinee ní Oosaya jipɔɔn Asariya nì Kareeya jipɔɔn Yoowanan nì bilambidambi gbanti kɔkɔ bí Yeereemii yii: «A mɔ́ntí ní! Ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu kaa pée tùkū-si á nàatī-ti yii: <Ní taa cù Eejipiti tiŋkin kí kàl̄.> 3An sá Neeriya jipɔɔn Baruuki di bíi sàal̄-si á sòoǹ ti-pu míǹ. Di sá yii u là kí dū-ti kí ŋá Babiloon yab ŋaan bíǹ ń kpɔ̀-ti, àá kí cúú-ti kí cùnnì Babiloon tiŋkin kuyuŋu ní.»
4An puee Kareeya jipɔɔn Yoowanan nì bijanjakpilib nì samaa un nìn dī-bee nìn yíì kaa pílifì ti-Dindaan kí kàl̄ Juuda tiŋkin. 5Niinee Kareeya jipɔɔn Yoowanan nì bijanjakpilib yōoǹ Juuda yab bin kɔkɔ kíǹee. Bíǹ di nìn sá bin nìn yàl̄ ki bíń ntimu kɔkɔn ki fātìi gítìń Juuda tiŋkinee. 6Bininjab nì binimpoobi nì mbiyaamu nì ubɔti bisalib nì binib bin kɔkɔ bijanjaliibi bin cí ubɔtee kpiliu Neebusaradan nìn dūu kāaǹ Juuda tiŋkin Ayiikaam jipɔɔn Geedaliyasi, Safan naantiiu ń nīn kpèéyee. Bi nìn kpáaǹ Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii nì Neeriya jipɔɔn Baruuki. 7Bi nìn yíì kaa tɔ́ ti-Dindaan nín lī puee. Bi nìn yíkì ki búntì Eejipiti tiŋkin, ki dūu bàn̄ Tapaneesi.
Yeereemii nāatì yii Neebukadineesaar làá fōō Eejipiti
8Tapaneesi tiŋkin niinee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Yeereemii yii: 9«Yòon̄ ataŋkpakpaan kí gbà kí síb́ kasarka un bí Eejipiti bɔtiu beecindi nyɔkɔpu Tapaneesee. Á ŋá míǹ Juuda yab nimbilaaliyin.» 10Míǹ boonee ní u bí-bi yii: <Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M làá tɔ̄ bí cùú nyàabìń m-tɔntɔnliu Neebukadineesaar, Babiloon bɔtiu. M làá dū u-beejal kí tɔ́kɔń ataŋkpee ŋin a síb́ nee pu ní. Niin ní u làá cóoń u-beecindi tantiu. 11U yaa láa bāańee, u làá dāá nà Eejipiti tiŋki ní dúsi dusi. U làá dāá kpɔ̀ bin máaǹ ŋkúmee, ní kí cúú bin máaǹ kí cù kuyuŋuee kí cùnnì kuyuŋu, ní kí dū kitàataajiki kí kpɔ̀ bin máaǹ bí dū kitàataajiki kí kpɔ̀ee. 12U làá tūū Eejipiti yab waadiiŋŋi ŋŋmi. U làá wà awaa ŋŋmi, àá u làá cáá-ŋi kí cùnnì Babiloon tiŋkin. U làá gbākal̀ Eejipiti gaajawanti kii upikpaal nín fíkití u-wampeeŋkaati kí lēē ikpɔkpɔb puee ní. Míǹ boonee ní ú yīkì kitiŋee nì ŋgbansɔŋfi. 13Eeliyoopooliisi tiŋkinee, u làá gbá kí wīī ataŋkpee kumpooŋi ní kí tūū Eejipiti yab waadiiŋŋi ŋŋmi.>

english_text:
The Lord Will Destroy the People of Judah
1The Lord told me to speak with the Jews who were living in the towns of Migdol, Tahpanhes, and Memphis in northern Egypt, and also to those living in southern Egypt. He told me to tell them:
2I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. You saw how I destroyed Jerusalem and the towns of Judah. They lie empty and in ruins today, 3because the people of Judah made me angry by worshiping gods that had never helped them or their ancestors.
4Time after time I sent my servants the prophets to tell the people of Judah how much I hated their disgusting sins. The prophets warned them to stop sinning, 5but they refused to listen and would not stop worshiping other gods. 6Finally, my anger struck like a raging flood, and today Jerusalem and the towns of Judah are nothing but empty ruins.
7Why do you now insist on heading for another disaster? A disaster that will destroy not only you, but also your children and babies. 8You have made me angry by worshiping idols and burning incense to other gods after you came here to Egypt. You will die such a disgusting death, that other nations will use the name of Judah as a curse word. 9When you were living in Jerusalem and Judah, you followed the example of your ancestors in doing evil things, just like your kings and queens. 10Even now, your pride keeps you from respecting me and obeying the laws and teachings I gave you and your ancestors.
11I, the Lord All-Powerful, have decided to wipe you out with disasters. 12There were only a few of you left in Judah, and you decided to go to Egypt. But you will die such horrible deaths in war or from starvation, that people of other countries will use the name of Judah as a curse word. 13I punished Jerusalem with war, hunger, and disease, and that's how I will punish you. 14None of you will survive. You may hope to return to Judah someday, but only a very few of you will escape death and be able to go back.
The People Refuse To Worship the Lord
15A large number of Jews from both northern and southern Egypt listened to me as I told them what the Lord had said. Most of the men in the crowd knew that their wives often burned incense to other gods. So they and their wives shouted:
16Jeremiah, what do we care if you speak in the Lord's name? We refuse to listen! 17We have promised to worship the goddess Astarte, the Queen of Heaven, and that is exactly what we are going to do. We will burn incense and offer sacrifices of wine to her, just as we, our ancestors, our kings, and our leaders did when we lived in Jerusalem and the other towns of Judah. We had plenty of food back then. We were well off, and nothing bad ever happened to us. 18But since the time we stopped burning incense and offering wine sacrifices to her, we have been dying from war and hunger.
19Then the women said, “When we lived in Judah, we worshiped the Queen of Heaven and offered sacrifices of wine and special loaves of bread shaped like her. Our husbands knew what we were doing, and they approved of it.”
20Then I told the crowd:
21Don't you think the Lord knew that you and your ancestors, your leaders and kings, and the rest of the people were burning incense to other gods in Jerusalem and everywhere else in Judah? 22And when he could no longer put up with your disgusting sins, he placed a curse on your land and turned it into a desert, as it is today. 23This disaster happened because you worshiped other gods and rebelled against the Lord by refusing to obey him or follow his laws and teachings.
24-25Then I told the men and their wives, that the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, had said:
Here in Egypt you still keep your promises to burn incense and offer sacrifices of wine to the so-called Queen of Heaven. 26Keep these promises! But let me tell you what will happen. As surely as I am the Lord God, I swear that I will never again accept any promises you make in my name. 27Instead of watching over you, I will watch for chances to harm you. Some of you will die in war, and others will starve to death. 28Only a few will escape and return to Judah. Then everyone who went to live in Egypt will know that when I say something will happen, it will—no matter what you say.
29And here is how you will know that I will keep my threats to punish you in Egypt. 30 I will hand over King Hophra of Egypt to those who want to kill him, just as I handed Zedekiah over to Nebuchadnezzar, who wanted to kill him.
translation_text:
Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Juuda yab bin cūtìi kɔ́ Eejipitee
1Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Yeereemii tibɔti ú dūú nàatī Juuda yab bin kɔkɔ nìn cūtìi kɔ́ Eejipiti tiŋkin, ki bí Miigidool nì Tapaneesi nì Meemifiisi nì bin kóò Patroosi tinjaaŋŋinee. 2Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «Ni ká inaabu in kɔkɔ m cáań ki tɔ́ Jeerusaleem nì Juuda timmu mun kíǹee puee. Díǹ pu nee, ntimu gbanti kpántì adigbun, ní báà uniseen kaa ti kóò mu-poon. 3Tin bí nee kɔkɔ yaa bāań-bee, an sá ikpiti in ntimu gbanti yab ŋá ki kɔ́ǹ-mi diŋuulee pu. Di sá yii bi cūtìi ŋá saraabi ki tīī awaa, ki jáaḿ-ŋi. Ama ní baa nyí awaa gbanti. Nimbi ni-ba nì ni-naanjab mun kaa nyí-ŋi. 4M túnní m-tɔntɔnliibi bibɔnaatiliibi kɔkɔ ni-cee kaa gbēeǹ. Bi nìn bí-ni yii: <Ní taa tɔ̄ ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin m ná nee.> 5Ama naa nìn pílifì ní kaa nìn fātìi tɔ́. Naa nìn fātì ni-boon ki tīī ikpiti in ni nìn ŋáańee, ní ki gbíntìi nìkì ki ŋáań saraabi ki tìì awaa. 6Niinee ní m kpáatì m-bum nì m-ŋuul ki sītì ni-pu, ní an wùn̄ Juuda timmu nì Jeerusaleem daŋŋi kii ŋŋmee. Ntimu gbanti kpántì adigbun ŋma nì kuteeu kii ni nín wāĺ an bí pu díǹ nee ní.>»
7Ní Yeereemii nìkī ki lī yii: «Kɔŋkɔnnee ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Ba pu ní ni bíi kɔ̄ntí ni-ba agìŋ́kpaan poon míǹ? Ni là kí kúntí Juuda nibulin, bininjab nì binimpoobi nì binipɔmbi nì mbipɔmu níii? Naa pée là ni-kansikin biba ń kíń níii? 8Di sá yii ni-tuuŋŋi gbítí m-ŋuul. Ni tùutī talaalub ki ŋáań saraabi ki tìì Eejipiti tiŋki kin ni cūtìi kɔ́ee waaŋi. Ni baasii là kí kúntí ni-ba, kí kpántí mbusu nì icoo ŋabikau kí tīī duulinya timbuŋŋi kɔkɔ níii? 9Ni súntì ikpiti in bi ŋá Juuda tiŋkin nì Jeerusaleem daŋŋi pueeee? Ni-naanjab nì Juuda bɔtiibi nì bi-nimpoobi nì nimbi ni-ba nì ni-nimpoobi di ŋá ikpiti gbanti. 10Áli nì díǹ, an kaa ŋá ubɔ nyàaa yii u ŋá tiba. Naa fāŋkì-mi, kaa tɔ́ m-marab nì m-bɔkpaaŋi ŋin m tīī ni nì ni-naanjabee.>»
11Ní Yeereemii gíti kútì ki lī yii: «An pu ní ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu bí yii: <M làá fàtī kí já nì bi, kí cáań nnaabu kí tɔ̄ bi-pu, ní kí kúntí Juuda nibul kɔkɔ. 12M làá kpèè Juuda yab bin kíǹ ki cūtìi kóò Eejipiti tiŋkinee bɔti. Bi-kɔkɔ làá kpú ní. Kitiŋ gbantin ní kujaau àá ŋkùm làá kpɔ̀ bi-kɔkɔ, ŋwaamu nì bikpaambi. Míǹ ní bi làá kpú ní bi yaa làá dāá tɔ̄ ubɔ mbusu àá kí sòoǹ kubɔbiiu kubɔ pu àá tibɔti tin cáá tifaandee pu àá kí kɔ́ǹ ubɔ icooyee, bíǹ ní bi làá dāá yòon̄ ŋabika. 13M làá jáǹ bin cūtìi kóò Eejipiti tiŋkinee, kii m nín jáń nì Jeerusaleem yab puee. M làá dū kujaau nì ŋkùm nì bìlbil kúm kí tɔ̄ bi-pu. 14Juuda yab bin kíǹ ki bí dimaŋfalin, ní ki dɔ́miń ki kɔ́ Eejipiti tiŋkinee, ubɔ kaa làá dāá ŋmā kí sāǹ kí ŋmátí kí nyā ŋkúm ŋaan. Ubɔ kaa làá dāá ŋmā kí gítiń Juuda tiŋki kin bi bàà cáá nlandɔkɔ kí gítiń kí kàl̄ee poon. Baa làá dāá ŋmā kí gítiń, asee bikaaŋkaabi bin làá dāá ŋmátí kí nyā ŋkúm ŋaanee.>»
Juuda yab ŋá saraabi ki tīī yilpu Nimpubɔtiu
15Bininjab bin kɔkɔ nìn nyí yii bi-nimpoobi ŋáań saraabi ki tìì awaayee nì binimpoobi bin kɔkɔ nìn kóoǹ ki kpáfì ki dūu ŋá dikitikpaandee, an dàkà yii bin kɔkɔ nìn cūtìi kɔ́ Eejipiti tiŋkin Patroosee nìn kíí Yeereemii yii: 16«Nì min kɔkɔ an sá ti-Dindaan yindi pu ní a sòoǹ nì tee, taa làá pīlifiǹ-si. 17Ti làá nīn nìkì ki ŋáań ti nín lēē yii ti làá ŋá puee. Ti làá nīn tùutī talaalutuukaabi ki tìì diwaal Asitaartee, yilpu Nimpubɔtiu ní kí fá-u ndaam. Timbi nìn pée ŋáań míǹ ní, ki kpáaǹ ti-naanjab nì ti-bɔtiibi nì ti-kàliŋkpilib Juuda timmun nì Jeerusaleem daŋŋi pu. Ti nín nìn ŋáań mimmee, ti nìn kāntí ki jīǹ ní, ní an nìn bútì-ti ní taa nìn nyí kun bi yíì nnaabuee. 18Ama kí yòon̄ ŋwiin ŋun ti gbēeǹ kaa ti tùutī talaalub ki tìì diwaal yilpu Nimpubɔtiu, kaa ti féeń-dì ndaamee, ti lóò tikɔkɔ, ní kujaau nì ŋkùm bíi kù-ti»
19Ní binimpoobi gíti lī yii: «Ti nín nìn tùutī talaalub ki tìì diwaal yilpu Nimpubɔtiu ki féeń-dì nnyimee, ti-calib kaa nìn nyáaa? Ti yaa nìn ŋáań kalaabi bin náań nì dèe ki féeń-dì ndaamee, bi nìn nyáaa!»
20Ama ní Yeereemii bí bi-kɔkɔ, bininjab nì binimpoobi bin nìn kíí-u mimmee yii: 21«An sá tiŋman, ni nì ni-baabi nì ni-bɔtiibi nì ni-kàliŋkpilib nì Juuda yab bin kɔkɔ kíǹee nìn tùutī talaalub Juuda timmun nì Jeerusaleem daŋŋi pu. Ti-Dindaan dáá gbíntìi téetí an pu, waa súntì. 22Ama ní ti-Dindaan gīī nì ni-tuŋkpitiŋ nì ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin ni ŋáańee. An pu ní ni-tiŋki kpántì adigbun, mpaan ŋun kíǹ ki fàantée, ní binib kaa ti kóò niin. Ni-tiŋki gbanti di kpántì ŋabika bi cáa tòó mbusu, kii an nín bí pu díǹ nee ní. 23Kun pu nnaabu gbanti jéetì ni-puee di sá yii ni tūutì talaalub ki tīī awaa ki yīntiǹ ti-Dindaan. Naa pílifiǹ-u ní kaa nóó u-dàkatam nì u-marab nì u-saŋkii, kii an nín bí pu díǹ nan ní.»
24Boonee ní Yeereemii bí samaa kɔkɔ, bininjab nì binimpoobi yii: «Nimbi Juuda yab bin kɔkɔ bí Eejipiti tiŋkinee, pīlifìmaan ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi. 25Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Ni nì ni-nimpoobi, ni lī yii: <Ti pōoǹ yii ti làá nīn tùutī talaalub ki tìì diwaal yilpu Nimpubɔtiu ki féeń-dì ndaam. Ti nín pōoǹ puee, míǹ ní ti làá ŋá!> Too, nín̄ ŋúb́ ni-pooŋyi, ŋámaan ni nín pōoǹ puee. 26Nimbi Juuda yab bin kɔkɔ cūtìi kɔ́ Eejipiti tiŋkinee, ní pīlifì tin man ni-Dindaan bíi sòoǹ nì ni nee tiŋan: Man ni-Dindaan, m pūtì m-yiŋkpaandi yii ujuudanil ubɔ pée gíti kpá kí pùtī kí yíiń m-yindi Eejipiti tiŋki kɔkɔn. Ubɔ gíti kpá kí lì yii: <Nì ti-Dindaan un bí dimaŋfalin nee.> 27Kun m làá nyàab̀ kí cáań kí tɔ̄ ni-puee, an kaa làá nīn sá nnaam, ama nnaabu ní. Kujaau nì ŋkùm di làá kpɔ̀ Juuda yab bin cūtìi kɔ́ Eejipiti tiŋkinee. Báà uniseen kaa làá kíń. 28Bi-kansikin binikaaŋkaabi di làá dāá ŋmátí kí nyā kujaaun. Bi làá dāá nyānní Eejipiti kí gítiń Juuda tiŋkin. Niinee Juuda yab bin kíǹ ki sáǹ ki cūtìi kɔ́ Eejipiti tiŋkinee làá béé man nì bíǹ un di cáá mbaamɔnee. 29Man ni-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M làá já nì ni Eejipiti tiŋkin doo. M làá tīī-ni kudaaŋŋu kubɔ. Niinee ni làá dāá ká yii tin m sòon̄ee, m bíi ŋáań míǹ kí cáań nnaabu kí tɔ̄ ni-pu. Kudaaŋŋu gbanti sɔ̀. 30M dū Juuda bɔtiu Seedeesiyasi ki ŋá Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar un nìn nyàab̀ kí kpɔ̀-uee ŋaan. Too, míǹ mbaantiim ní m làá dū Eejipiti bɔtiu Faaroo Oofiraa kí ŋá u-nannanliibi bin nyàab̀ kí kpɔ̀-uee ŋáań. Man ni-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee dee.>»

english_text:
The Lord Will Not Let Baruch Be Killed
1 In the fourth year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, Baruch wrote down everything I had told him. 2Then later, the Lord God of Israel told me to say to Baruch:
3You are moaning and blaming me, the Lord, for your troubles and sorrow, and for being so tired that you can't even rest. 4But all over the earth I am tearing down what I built and pulling up what I planted. 5I am bringing disaster everywhere, so don't even think about making any big plans for yourself. However, I promise that wherever you go, I will at least protect you from death. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
Tibɔti tin ti-Dindaan sòon̄ Baruuki puee
1Joosiyaasi jipɔɔn Yoowakiim nín kāl̀ Juuda beel pu tibɔtiil dibinnanaatiilee ní Neeriya jipɔɔn Baruuki ŋmàn̄ tibɔti tin Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu kàan̄-uee ki ŋá kugbɔŋun. Dibindi gbantee, Yeereemii nín nìn tùkū Baruuki tibɔti tiŋyee sèé: 2«Ti-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ tin sii Baruuki puee sɔ̀. 3A lì yii: <Man bɔlii na! M nìn pée bí falaa poon ní ti-Dindaan gíti dū kunimbaau ki kútì-mi. M yáliŋkì ki tin gīī, kaa kpáà ká diŋuŋfil.> 4Too, ti-Dindaan nín tùkū-mi tin ḿ dūú nàatī-see sèé:
<M làá gbá kí kpìtī tin m nìn máńee,
m làá fùkù tin m nìn cóoǹee.
M làá ŋá míǹ ntimu kɔkɔn.
5Ní siiyee, a nyàab̀ kí tɔ̄ atuŋkpaan.
Taa ti pée bàlifì tiba!
Di sá yii man ni-Dindaan,
m nín sòon̄ puee sèé:
M làá cáań nnaabu kí tɔ̄ tin kɔkɔ cáá kufoouee pu.
Ama siiyee, dimaŋfal ní m làá tīī-si
án nīn sá a-paati,
laakin kamaa a làá cùee.>»

english_text:
The Lord Speaks to Jeremiah about the Nations
1The Lord often told me what to say about the different nations of the world.
What the Lord Says about Egypt
2 In the fourth year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia defeated King Neco of Egypt in a battle at the city of Carchemish near the Euphrates River. And here is what the Lord told me to say about the Egyptian army:
3It's time to go into battle!
So grab your shields,
4saddle your horses,
and polish your spears.
Put on your helmets and armor,
then take your positions.
5I can see the battle now—
you are defeated
and running away,
never once looking back.
Terror is all around.
6You are strong and run fast,
but you can't escape.
You fall in battle
near the Euphrates River.
7What nation is this,
that rises like the Nile River
overflowing its banks?
8It is Egypt, rising with a roar
like a raging river
and saying,
“I'll flood the earth,
destroying cities, and killing
everyone in them.”
9Go ahead, Egypt.
Tell your chariots and cavalry
to attack and fight hard.
Order your troops to march out,
with Ethiopians and Libyans
carrying shields,
and the Lydians armed with bows
and arrows.
10But the Lord All-Powerful
will win this battle
and take revenge
on his enemies.
His sword will eat them
and drink their blood
until it is full.
They will be killed in the north
near the Euphrates River,
as a sacrifice to the Lord.
11Egypt, no medicine can heal you,
not even the soothing lotion
from Gilead.
12All nations have heard you weep;
you are disgraced,
and they know it.
Your troops fall to the ground,
stumbling over each other.
A Warning for Egypt
13-14 When King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia was on his way to attack Egypt, the Lord sent me with a warning for every Egyptian town, but especially for Migdol, Memphis, and Tahpanhes. He said to tell them:
Prepare to defend yourselves!
Everywhere in your nation,
people are dying in war.
15I have struck down
your mighty god Apis
and chased him away.
16Your soldiers stumble
over each other
and say, “Get up!
The enemy will kill us,
unless we can escape
to our own land.”
17Give the king of Egypt
this new name,
“Talks-Big-Does-Nothing.”
18Egypt, I am the true king,
the Lord All-Powerful,
and as surely as I live,
those enemies who attack
will tower over you
like Mount Tabor among the hills
or Mount Carmel by the sea.
19You will be led away captive,
so pack a few things
to bring with you.
Your capital, Memphis,
will lie empty and in ruins.
20An enemy from the north
will attack you, beautiful Egypt,
like a fly biting a cow.
21The foreign soldiers you hired
will turn and run.
But they are doomed,
like well-fed calves
being led to the butcher.
* 22The enemy army will go forward
like a swarm of locusts.
Your troops will feel helpless,
like a snake in a forest
23when men with axes
start chopping down trees.
It can only hiss
and try to escape.
24Your people will be disgraced
and captured by the enemy
from the north.
25I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. Soon I will punish the god Amon of Thebes and the other Egyptian gods, the Egyptian kings, the people of Egypt, and everyone who trusts in the Egyptian power. 26I will hand them over to King Nebuchadnezzar and his army. But I also promise that Egypt will someday have people living here again, just as it had before. I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Lord Will Bring Israel Home
The Lord said:
27 Israel, don't be afraid.
Someday I will bring you home
from foreign lands.
You and your descendants
will live in peace and safety,
with nothing to fear.
28So don't be afraid,
even though now
you deserve to be punished
and have been scattered
among other nations.
But when I destroy them,
I will protect you.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
1Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ nì Yeereemii atimbun pu puee sɔ̀.
Bi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Eejipiti yab Kaarkeemiisi
2U sòon̄ Eejipiti tiŋki nì Eejipiti bɔtiu Faaroo Neekoo janjakitil pu. Joosiyaasi jipɔɔn Yooyakiim nín kpántì Juuda bɔtiu dibinnanaatiilee, Eejipiti bɔtiu nìn bí Kaarkeemiisi, Eefiraati mɔɔgbandi. Ŋyunti gbantee, Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-u.
3Bijanjakpilib nìn kūuntí yii:
«Bɔ́ntímaan agbampɔɔ
akpaan nì ŋwaamu.
Ní cùú jámaan kujaau.
4Ní kpàl̄maan itaamu!
Bitanjakaliibi, máĺmaan ni-taamui!
Dūmaan ni-janjafuulimmu kí cíkiń!
Ní páaḿmaan ipɔ̀n pu!
Bɔ́ntímaan ni-kpammu!
Dūmaan ni-gbampɔɔŋi kí pèen̄!»
5Ti-Dindaan bí yii:
«Ama ba bíi jītí ní? Ba ní m wāĺ nan ní?
Tifaandi kɔ́-bi, bi bíi nɔ̀tī ki gítí boon!
Bi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ bijanjaliibi bimɔntiibi sɔ́kɔ sɔkɔ.
Dinyoondi kɔ́-bi bi sáń kaa fàtī,
tifaandi bí an kɔkɔ pu.
6Un ŋūǹ ki yáb̀ee kaa ŋúń ki sáǹ ki ŋmátì,
ubaatandaan kaa ŋūǹ kí fīī u-ba.
Ŋgan pú Eefiraati mɔɔgbaŋŋee,
bi gbéetì ki lítì.
7«Ŋma náań nì Niil mɔɔl din gbée,
a lì kii dimɔɔl din nyim gbí ki páaǹee?
8An sá Eejipiti di jɔ́ḿ kii Niil mɔɔlee.
Kì nìn lì yii:
<Kii Niil mɔɔl nín gbí puee,
a lì kii di-nyim nín gbí ki páaǹ puee,
míǹ ní m làá gbí kí léeń kitiŋ pu
ní kí nàan̄ kitiŋ
kí kpáaǹ mu-timmu.
9Itaamu, kpàtīí líímaan!
Janjatɔrɔkub, dūmaan ni-yil kí bɔ̄!
Bijanjaliibi ń dū bi-ba kí bíĺ,
an dàkà yii Eetiiyoopii yab nì Puuti yab,
bin tūntí agbampɔɔyee
nì Luudi yab bin bàl̀ abaatanee!
10Ama ti-Dindaan un sá Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan ceeyee,
an sá ipɔntoon wiiŋŋu ní.
U làá tɔ̀ u-nannanliibi ipɔntoon.
Kitàataajiki làá ŋmɔ́ bi-nanti kí díkí,
ní kí nyɔ̀ bi-fatikuu kí gbí.
Di sá yii an dāa sá saraa ní ki tīī ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan
ŋgan pú tiŋkin, Eefiraati mɔɔgbaŋŋi.
11Eejipiti tiŋki kinyannyaaŋŋi,
jɔ̄m̀ Galaadi tiŋkin kí nyàab̀ a-buuŋyi kpam.
Ama a bíi kpántí inyɔkɔfi fám ní,
tiweendi tin a fōōyee kaa làá kpú.
12Atimbun gbìl̄ a-cooi pu,
bi gbìl̀ a-yaliŋkii pu an kɔkɔ pu.
Di sá yii ubaatandaan kpéetì ubaatandaan,
ní bi-liitil gbéetì ki lítì dicilpu.>»
Neebukadineesaar lúuń Eejipiti tiŋki
13Ŋyunti ŋun Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar dɔ́miń kí já nì Eejipiti tiŋkee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì u-bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii yii:
14«Ní bāakì tibɔtee Eejipiti tiŋkin,
ní yàntī bí gbìl̄-tì Miigidool tiŋkin,
bí gbìl̄-tì Meemifiisi nì Tapaneesi timmun.
Lìmaan yii:
Yīkìí yūĺmaan kí bɔ́ntí ni-ba,
di sá yii kujaau bíi nà ni-kɔŋkɔnnaatɔb.
15Ba pu ní a-waal din sá unajee
lítì kaa ŋúń ki yúl̀ ní?
Ti-Dindaan nín kpìb̄-dèe,
16dì kpīntì ní ŋkpitim pu.
Bijanjaliibi lítì ki dɔ̄ tɔb pu.
Bi lì tɔb cee yii:
<Tí yīkì kí kpì ti-tiŋkin
kí sāǹ kí wàatī kujaau kun nàantí nee.
17Diyindi din bi làá pɔ̄ Eejipiti bɔtiu Faarooyee sɔ̀.
Kufuu, kufuu, ama kufuu fám!
18«Ubɔti un bi yíì ti-Dindaan
Mpɔŋkɔdaanee nín sòon̄ puee sèé:
<M pūtì m-ba maŋfal yii unannanli làá dāan̄.>
Kii Tabɔɔr nín sá dijool
ní Kaarmeel jool bí tiŋku caŋinee,
míǹ ní u làá dāan̄.
19«Eejipiti yab,
bɔ́ntímaan ni-wanti kí nīn cá kuyuŋu.
Meemifiisi tiŋki làá kpántí kuteeu.
Bi làá nàan̄-kì
ní báà uniseen kaa ti làá nīn kóò ki-ni.
20«Eejipiti nìn sá unasal un ŋān̄ee ní!
Ama dinaagandi diba nyánní ŋgan pú
ki dɔ́miń ki báaǹ u-pu.
21Bijanjaliibi bin kì nìn dée
nìn bí ní màlmal kii dinajapɔmbilee.
Ama bi mun fātì bi-boon ki tīī-kì,
bi-kɔkɔ sáǹ dicilpu,
baa ŋúń ki yúl̀.
Di sá yii nnaabu wiiŋŋu dòoń bi-pu,
ŋwiin ŋun m làá dáaĺ bi-tafalee.
22Binannanliibi fāā mɔ̀ɔɔ ki dòoń
kí léeń Eejipiti tiŋki pu
kii bidɔgaaliibi di ŋúb́ ncɔkɔmu
kí dāá gāā isufee.
Niinee Eejipiti yab janjaliibi sáń kii
ukoobu nín sáń pu kaa ŋáań kuwoouee ní.
23Ti-Dindaan bí yii:
<Bi bíi gà ki-bambaŋku,
kubambaŋŋu kun poon ubɔ kaa nìn ŋūǹ kí kɔ́ee.
Di sá yii bi nìn wīikí ki jítiǹ inaakitoon,
ubɔ kaa ŋūǹ kí kàaǹ-bi.
24Icoo kɔ́ Eejipiti kitinnyanyaaŋŋi,
bi dū-kì ki ŋá ŋgan pú nibuliŋ ŋaan.>»
25Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel yab Nimbɔtiu bí yii: «M làá dáaĺ Tabeesi yab waal Amɔn nì Eejipiti yab nì bi-waaŋi nì bi-bɔtiibi ní Faaroo nì bin kɔkɔ máká u-puee tafal. 26M làá dū-bi kí ŋá bin nyàab̀ kí kpɔ̀-bee ŋaan, an dàkà yii Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar nì u-janjaliibi ŋaan.
«Ama boonee, binib làá dāá fàtīí kɔ́ Eejipiti tiŋki kii dooooyee.» Ti-Dindaan di sòon̄ míǹ.
Ti-Dindaan làá fīī Isirayeel yab
(Kpèè Yeer 30.10-11)
27«Sii m-tɔntɔnliu Jaakɔb, taa fàŋkì,
Isirayeel, taa yàntī a-pɔbil ń bīil̀.
M làá fīī-si kí nyāntí ntindandatimun,
ní kí gíiǹní a-biyaamu mun bí kuyuŋunee.
Jaakɔb, a làá fàtīí gítiń nì dimákal
kí nīn bí ŋgbansɔŋfin.
Ubɔ kaa dāa gíti páb̀-si.
28Sii Jaakɔb m-tɔntɔnliu, taa fàŋkì.
Man a-Dindaan di lī yii m bí a-cee.
M làá kúntí atimbun ŋin poon
m nìn jìn̄-si a yàl̄ ki kɔ́ee.
Ama siiyee, maa làá kúntí-si.
An sá tiŋman yii m dáaĺ a-tafal,
ama an sá kí sāŋkì-si ní.
Di sá yii maa ŋūǹ kí yàntī-si
kii a sá maanyiibee.»

english_text:
What the Lord Says about the Philistines
1 Before the king of Egypt attacked the town of Gaza, the Lord told me to say to the Philistines:
2I, the Lord, tell you
that your land will be flooded
with an army from the north.
It will destroy your towns
and sweep you away,
moaning and screaming.
3When you hear the thunder
of horses and chariots,
your courage will vanish,
and parents will even abandon
their own children.
4You refugees from Crete,
your time has now come,
and I will destroy you.
None of you will be left
to help the cities
of Tyre and Sidon.
5The Anakim who survive
in Gaza and Ashkelon
will mourn for you
by shaving their heads
and sitting in silence.
6You ask how long will I continue
to attack you with my sword,
then you tell me to put it away
and leave you alone.
7But how can my sword rest,
when I have commanded it
to attack Ashkelon
and the seacoast?
translation_text:
Tin ti-Dindaan sòon̄ Fiiliistii yab puee
1Ti-Dindaan nìn sòon̄ nì u-bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii Fiiliistii yab pu. An nìn sá kí wàatī Faaroo ń já nì Gaasaa yabee ní.
2Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé:
«Tinyiŋgbaŋkpaandi nyánní ŋgan pú.
Tì kpántì mbuŋkpaan ki gbí ki páaǹ.
Tì gbí ki léeǹ kitiŋee nì tin kɔkɔ bí ki-poonee,
ntimu nì mu-nib pu.
Binib gbáà ibiil ki nyàab̀ dijòońdi,
kitiŋee nib bíi gà ikpiisilan.
3Bi gbìl̀ itaamu tagbíŋŋi pu.
Janjatɔrɔkub wàkalìń,
bi-taaŋi ŋáań kuwookpaaŋŋu.
Bibaatiibi kaa ti wāĺ bi-biyaamu,
bi-ŋalii kpíì.
4Di sá yii ŋwiin di bāań bí nàan̄ Fiiliistii yab.
Ubɔ kaa ti bí kí tūtuǹ
Tiir nì Siidɔn timmu.
Án taa kíń báà uniseen.
Ti-Dindaan bíi nàantí Fiiliistii yab kɔkɔ,
bin kíǹ ki bí dimaŋfalin
Kafitoor tiŋki kin nnyim māntìi túee poonee.
5Gaasaa yab kōol̀ abaakpan!
Asikeelɔn yab ŋmíl̀ fɔ́ŋfɔŋ díkí diki.
Nimbi tijawɔkɔl tin kíǹ kaa kpíìyee,
ni làá nīn cáá njimu ki gífí ni-wunti pu yéè
kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu ní?
6Ni lì yii: <Abàa, ti-Dindaan tàataajiki,
kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu ní a làá ŋùŋfì ní?
Kɔ́ a-jitookun!
Kàl̄ niin soooo!>
7Mana ní kì ŋūǹ kí ŋùŋfì?
Ti-Dindaan tīī-kì mara yii
kí cù áli Asikeelɔn nì tiŋku gbandi.
U nín síiǹ-kì kí ŋá puee dee.»

english_text:
What the Lord Says about Moab
1 The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, told me to say to the nation of Moab:
The town of Nebo is doomed;
Kiriathaim will be captured
and disgraced,
and even its fortress
will be left in ruins.
2No one honors you, Moab.
In Heshbon, enemies make plans
to end your life.
My sword will leave only silence
in your town named “Quiet.”
3The people of Horonaim
will cry for help,
as their town is attacked
and destroyed.
4Moab will be shattered!
Your children will sob
5and cry on their way up
to the town of Luhith;
on the road to Horonaim
they will tell of disasters.
6Run for your lives!
Head into the desert
like a wild donkey.
7You thought you could be saved
by your power and wealth,
but you will be captured
along with your god Chemosh,
his priests, and officials.
8Not one of your towns
will escape destruction.
I have told your enemies,
“Wipe out the valley
and the flatlands of Moab.
9Spread salt on the ground
to kill the crops.
Leave its towns in ruins,
with no one living there.
10I want you to kill the Moabites,
and if you let them escape,
I will put a curse on you.”
11Moab, you are like wine
left to settle undisturbed,
never poured from jar to jar.
And so, your nation continues
to prosper and improve.
12But now, I will send enemies
to pour out the wine
and smash the jars!
13Then you will be ashamed,
because your god Chemosh
cannot save you,
just as Bethel could not help
the Israelites.
14You claim that your soldiers
are strong and brave.
15But I am the Lord,
the all-powerful King,
and I promise that enemies
will overpower your towns.
Even your best warriors
will die in the battle.
16It won't be long now—
disaster will hit Moab!
17I will order the nearby nations
to mourn for you and say,
“Isn't it sad? Moab ruled others,
but now its glorious power
has been shattered.”
18People in the town of Dibon,
you will be honored no more,
so have a seat in the dust.
Your walls will be torn down
when the enemies attack.
19You people of Aroer,
go wait beside the road,
and when refugees run by,
ask them, “What happened?”
20They will answer,
“Moab has been defeated!
Weep with us in shame.
Tell everyone at the Arnon River
that Moab is destroyed.”
21I will punish every town
that belongs to Moab,
but especially Holon,
Jahzah, Mephaath,
22Dibon, Nebo,
Beth-Diblathaim, 23Kiriathaim,
Beth-Gamul, Beth-Meon,
24Kerioth, and Bozrah.
25My decision is final—
your army will be crushed,
and your power broken.
26People of Moab, you claim
to be stronger than I am.
Now I will tell other nations
to make you drunk
and to laugh while you collapse
in your own vomit.
27You made fun of my people
and treated them like criminals
caught in the act.
28Now you must leave your towns
and live like doves
in the shelter of cliffs
and canyons.
29I know about your pride,
and how you strut and boast.
30But I also know bragging
will never save you.
31So I will cry and mourn
for Moab
and its town of Kir-Heres.
32People of Sibmah,
you were like a vineyard
heavy with grapes,
and with branches reaching
north to the town of Jazer
and west to the Dead Sea.
But you have been destroyed,
and so I will weep for you,
as the people of Jazer weep
for the vineyards.
33Harvest celebrations are gone
from the orchards and farms
of Moab.
I have silenced the shouts
of people making wine.
34Weeping from Heshbon
can be heard as far
as Elealeh and Jahaz;
cries from Zoar are heard
in Horonaim
and Eglath-Shelishiyah.
And Nimrim Creek has run dry.
35I will get rid of anyone
who burns incense
to the gods of Moab
or offers sacrifices
at their shrines.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
36In my heart I moan for Moab,
like a funeral song
played on a flute.
I mourn for the people
of the town of Kir-Heres,
because their wealth is gone.
* 37-38The people of Moab
mourn on the rooftops
and in the streets.
Men cut off their beards,
people shave their heads;
they make cuts on their hands
and wear sackcloth.
And it's all because I, the Lord,
have shattered Moab like a jar
that no one wants.
39Moab lies broken!
Listen to its people cry
as they turn away in shame.
Other nations are horrified
at what happened,
but still they mock her.
40Moab, an enemy swoops down
like an eagle spreading its wings
over your land.
41Your cities and fortresses
will be captured,
and your warriors as fearful
as women giving birth.
42You are finished as a nation,
because you dared oppose me,
the Lord.
43Terror, pits, and traps
are waiting for you.
44If you are terrified and run,
you will fall into a pit;
and if you crawl out of the pit,
you'll get caught in a trap.
The time has come
for you to be punished.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
45Near the city of Heshbon,
where Sihon once ruled,
tired refugees stand in shadows
cast by the flames
of their burning city.
Soon, the towns on other hilltops,
where those warlike people live,
will also go up in smoke.
46People of Moab, you worshiped
Chemosh, your god,
but now you are done for,
and your children are prisoners
in a foreign country.
47Yet someday, I will bring
your people back home.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
Tin ti-Dindaan sòon̄ Moowaab yab puee
1Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nín sòon̄ Moowaab pu puee sèé:
«Ba naabuŋu di jéetì Neeboo tiŋki pu míǹ?
Bi nāaǹ-kì múb!
Icoo cúú Kiiriyatayiim tiŋki,
bi jáń ki fōō-kì!
Kitiŋ kin bi máń digundi ki túee,
ba cooi íǹ bulifi dee,
kì lítì.
2Kun nìn sá Moowaab nyootee kúntì.
Binib bɔ́ntì kí cáań nnaabu kí tɔ̄ Eesbɔn tiŋki pu ki lì yii:
<Tí cùmaan kí kúntí kitiŋ nee
atimbun kansikin!>
Si mun Madimeeni, bi làá pée nàan̄-si ní,
kujaau jìn̄ ki cúú-si dee.
3Bi gbìl̀ ibiil pu doooo Ooroonayiim tiŋkin yii:
<Bi nāaǹ tikɔkɔ.
Ba naabukpaaŋŋu ŋúǹ dee!>
4Bi wīī Moowaab tiŋki.
Bi gbìl̀ ki-biyaamu biilii pu.
5Binib dàb̀ Luwiiti gbantaŋki ki sūǹ.
A yaa sìntī Ooroonayiimee,
a gbìl̀ kunimbaau biilii pu.
6Sām̀maan kí fīī ni-ba!
Ní gbíntí kuteeun
kii kumooun maŋkee.
7Moowaab, a nìn máká a-tuuŋŋi nì a-gaajati pu ní.
Ama bi làá já kí fōō si mun.
Bi làá cúú a-waal Keemoosi nì a-tandambi
nì a-kpilib kí cùnnì kuyuŋu dicilpu.
8Un nàantí tikɔkɔee làá yìiǹ ntimu kɔkɔn,
waa làá súntí báà kibaba pu.
Bi làá nàan̄ ditantakal,
ní kí bīil̀ laakin tɔ́kɔ́ee,»
kii ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ pu ki síiǹee.
9Tīīmaan Moowaab tiŋki ifeen,
kí ŋmā kí yīkì kí ŋàaǹ!
Ki-timmu làá kpántí kuteeu
ubɔ kaa ti làá nīn kóò mu-ni.
10An sá mbusu ní ki tīī un tūǹ
ti-Dindaan tundi nì bugbambuee.
Mbusu sá ki tīī un kaa là
fatiku ń táká u-tàataajikee.
*
11Doooo Moowaab biyatin ní u bí ŋgbansɔŋfin.
Baa cúú-u ki cūnnì kuyuŋu ki ká.
U nìn pée dɔ̄ soooo
kii ndaam min baa tóoń ki lēē tidacaal,
kaa kpáatì-mì ki ŋá dibool diban ki kpáal̀ee ní.
An puee ní u-mɔŋŋu nì u-sɔnsɔfiŋu kaa kpántì.
12An pu ní ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Ŋyunti bí ki dòoń, m làá tɔ̄ń binib bí dāá kpáatí-mì kí ŋá aboon aban. Bi làá kpáatí ndaam min kā tidabuti poonee kí fá ní kí wīī-tì. 13Bi làá dāá nīn cáá diwaal Keemoosi pu icoo. Kii Isirayeel yab nín nìn cáá diwaal Beeteel din pu bi nìn mákée pu puee.
14«Moowaab yab,
mana ní ni ŋūǹ kí lì yii:
<Ti sá bibaatandambi,
bijanjaliibi bimɔmmɔntiibi.>
15Bi nāaǹ Moowaab tiŋki,
bi dàb̄ kí jáǹ ki-timmu.
Bi cúú ki-nipɔmbi bin cáá laafiyee
ki cáǹ kí kpɔ̀.»
Ubɔti un bi yíì ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaanee di sòon̄ míǹ.
16An kaa làá sūŋkì, bi làá nàan̄ Moowaab tiŋki,
nnaabu làá jēetí ki-pu kpalaa.
17Nimbi ki-kɔŋkɔnnaatɔb bin nyí-kì tiŋanee,
ní cùú ŋámaan-kì fɔ̀ɔ́.
Baa! Mpɔn ŋun kaa cáá juti nee,
mbɔtikpandɔ ŋun cáá tinyool nee
cúu kɔ́fàa!
*
18Diibɔn nibul,
kpákatí a-nyooti beejal pu,
kí dāá kàl̄ titampummool pu.
Un nāaǹ Moowaab tiŋkee
dòoń kí já nì si,
u bíi wìil̄ digundi din māntìi tú-see.
19Arooweer nibul,
cùú yūĺ didandi pu
kí nīn cɔ́ŋkí ki kpèé.
Ní bàlifì bin sáń kí ŋmátée yii:
«Ba di ŋá ní?»
20Bi làá kíí yii:
Bi nàn̄ Moowaab tiŋki dúsi dusi!
An puee icoo kɔ́-kì.
Ní fáámaan ibiil bí jòò-ni.
Ní bāakìmaan Arinɔn buŋgbandi pu yii
bi nāaǹ Moowaab tiŋki.
21Ditafadaaldi lítì ditantakal timmu pu nì Oolɔn nì Yaasa nì Meefaati 22nì Diibɔn nì Neeboo nì Beeti-Dibilatayiim timmu pu, 23nì Kiiriyatayiim nì Beeti-Gamuul nì Beeti-Meeyɔn timmu pu 24nì Keeriyooti nì Boosiraa nì Moowaab timmu mun pìl̄ee nì mun bí ndandatee pu.
25«Moowaab pɔŋŋu wáŋkì,
u-kpabil kɔ́fì»,
ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.
26Moowaab dākafì yii u sá ukpaan ki jítiǹ ti-Dindaan ní! Bí nyùntī-u ndaam ú gbí áli kí wùliŋkì. Ŋyunti bāań bí bèel̀ u mun dee! 27Moowaab, kéè a nìn bèel̄ Isirayeel naa! Isirayeel mun kaa nìn sá unaayuuyaa! Kin ba pu ní a nìn gbákafí diyil ki bèel̄-u ŋyunti ŋun kamaa a yaa nìn sòoǹ u-puee ní.
28Moowaab yab, yīkìí fámaan ni-timmu.
Ní cùú nīn kóòmaan itaŋkpalɔkɔn!
Nín̄ bímaan kii dibeenanjilee.
Di pāantí di-diiku nsitim watil pú
laakin unil kaa ŋūǹ kí bèe ní.
*
29Ti gbìl̄ bi sòoǹ Moowaab yab lambil pu.
Bi yòontí bi-ba yilpu an kaa cáá bí lì!
Ba lambil díǹ dee!
Ba badàkatam dee!
Ba bayoondi dee!
Ba mɔnti dee!
30«M nyí u-lambil pu, ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ míǹ.
U càfī tibɔti ní an kaa cáá taapu,
ní tin u ŋáańee kaa túĺ nsan.»
31An pu ní m bíi yáliŋkí Moowaab pu.
M gbáà ibiil bí jòò Moowaab tiŋki kɔkɔ.
M bíi tíminsí Kiiri-Eereesi yab pu.
32M sūǹ sii Sibima nibul pu
ki jítiǹ Yaseer yab nín sūǹ a-pu puee.
A nìn sá kii fiinyi subuee ní.
A nìn tɔ́ apan an lákatì Ŋyaam mɔɔl pu,
ŋi nìn lālim̀ ki tin bàn̄ Yaseer tiŋki.
Ama unàanli páatìi jéetì
a-fiinyi biliŋ nì a-kpaajinti pu.
33Ifaal nì dipɔɔpindi kúntì
asubiŋmɔkaa kpaaŋŋi nì Moowaab tiŋkin.
Ndaam dóò tilɔn poon,
bininjab bin tà ki fɔ́bití fiinyi biliŋ
ki nyāntí ndaamee kaa ti bí.
Dipɔɔpindi kuŋkuuntii kúntì.
34Eesbɔn yab bíi gbáà ibiil bí jòò-bi. Bi gbìl̀ bi-pu Eeleeyalee nì Yaasa, ní kí yòon̄ Soowaar kí tin sāā Ooroonayiim nì Eegilati-Seelisiya. Áli gba Niimriim buŋŋu fóotì.
35Ti-Dindaan bí yii: «M làá kúntí Moowaab tiŋkin bin di cá ŋgbantamu pu ki ŋáań bisaraawɔkaabi ki tùutī talaalub ki tìì awaayee.»
36M bí ki sūǹ Moowaab yab nì Kiiri-Eeseesi yab pu. M-yaliŋkii bí kii kiwulii nín sūǹ puee ní, kun puee tigaajawan tin kɔkɔ bi nìn kóoǹ ki kpúkuǹee wáŋkì. 37Bininjab kɔkɔ kōol̀ abaakpan, ki cáń bi-nyimpuliŋ. Bi gífì gífì bi-ŋalii njimu ki dū kutukub ki gbìn̄ bi-cammu. 38Moowaab diiŋŋi yilpu bi nín bɔ̀b̄ puee nì kpacantib kɔkɔ puee, bi gbìl̀ ikpiisilan pu ní. «M wīī Moowaab kii bi nín wìil̄ dibool din kaa ti bí tibanee puee ní.» Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ. 39Baa! Bi nùkū Moowaab tiŋki púb! Nín̄ yáliŋkímaan! Moowaab sáǹ ki kátì, ba cooi dee! Ki-kɔŋkɔnnaatɔb kɔkɔ bèel̄-kì ní kì kɔ́ dinyoondin.
*
40Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «Binannanliibi kpántì kii kaajiikuee ki ŋàaǹ ki kpátí u-feeŋyi Moowaab tiŋki pu.»
41Bi jáń ki fōō ntimu,
ki gbáń ki wīī sintil difɔkɔŋi.
Yaadalee, Moowaab baatandambi fāŋkì kii unimpu un kā imatiŋween puee ní.
42Bi nāaǹ Moowaab tiŋki,
an kaa ti sá dinibul.
U nìn dākafì yii u sá ukpaan
ki jítiǹ ti-Dindaan ní.
43Dinyoondi nì mbòó nì kulaaŋŋu
dɔ̄ ki cí nimbi Moowaab yab.
Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.
44Un yaa láa bíi sáń dinyoondee
làá dāá jēetí mboon.
Un yaa láa nyáń mboonee
làá cùú kɔ́ kulaaŋŋun.
Tiŋman, dibindi din m làá dāá dáaĺ bi-tafalee,
m làá dāá yàntī tíǹ gbanti ń jēetí Moowaab yab pu.
Man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ.
45Bin bíi sáńee kaa ti cáá mpɔn.
Bi sáǹ ki kɔ́ Eesbɔn tiŋkin.
Ama ŋŋmi ŋubɔ nyánní Eesbɔn tiŋkin,
Siiwɔn bɔtiu beecindin.
Ŋu dɔ́miń ki wùn̄ dinibul din cáá kufuu nee tiŋki
kí yòon̄ ki-kpaanyɔkɔ
kí cáá sāā ki-kansikin.
46Moowaab, an sá nnaabu ní ki tīī-si!
Keemoosi nibul, an dóò a-pu dee!
Bi cúú a-jipɔmbi nì a-bisalib
ki cūnnì kuyuŋu.
47Ama iwiin bí ki dòoń,
m làá gíiǹní Moowaab yab bin bi cúú ki cūnnì kuyuŋuee.
Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.
Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ Moowaab bɔti pu puee nín gbèentí laakiŋyee dee.

english_text:
What the Lord Says about Ammon
1 The Lord has this to say about the nation of Ammon:
The people of Israel
have plenty of children
to inherit their lands.
So why have you worshipers
of the god Milcom
taken over towns and land
belonging to the tribe of Gad?
2Someday I will send an army
to attack you in Rabbah,
your capital city.
It will be left in ruins,
and the surrounding villages
will lie in ashes.
You took some of Israel's land,
but on that day
Israel will take yours!
3Cry, people of Heshbon;
your town will become
a pile of rubble.
You will turn here and there,
but your path will be blocked.
Put on sackcloth and mourn,
you citizens of Rabbah,
because the idol you worship
will be taken
to a foreign country,
along with its priests
and temple officials.
4You rebellious Ammonites
trust your wealth and ask,
“Who could attack us?”
But I warn you not to boast
when your strength is fading.
5I, the Lord All-Powerful,
will send neighboring nations
to strike you with terror.
You will be scattered,
with no one to care
for your refugees.
6Yet someday, I will bring
your people back home.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
What the Lord Says about Edom
7 The Lord All-Powerful says about Edom:
Wisdom and common sense
have vanished from Teman.
8I will send disaster to punish
you descendants of Esau,
so anyone from Dedan
had better turn around
and run back home.
9People who harvest grapes
leave some for the poor.
Thieves who break in at night
take only what they want.
10But I will take everything
that belongs to you,
people of Edom,
and I will uncover every place
where you try to hide.
Then you will die,
and so will your children,
relatives, and neighbors.
11But I can be trusted
to care for your orphans
and widows.
12Even those nations that don't deserve to be punished will have to drink from the cup of my anger. So how can you possibly hope to escape? 13I, the Lord, swear in my own name that your city of Bozrah and all your towns will suffer a horrible fate. They will lie in ruins forever, and people will use the name “Bozrah” as a curse word.
14I have sent a messenger
to command the nations
to prepare for war
against you people of Edom.
15Your nation will be small,
yet hated by other nations.
16Pride tricks you into thinking
that other nations
look at you with fear.
You live along the cliffs
and high in the mountains
like the eagles,
but I am the Lord,
and I will bring you down.
17People passing by your country
will be shocked and horrified
to see a disaster
18 as bad as the destruction
of Sodom and Gomorrah
and towns nearby.
The towns of Edom will be empty.
19 I, the Lord, will attack you
like a lion from the forest,
attacking sheep in a meadow
along the Jordan.
In a moment the flock runs,
and the land is empty.
Who will I choose to attack you?
I will do it myself!
No one can force me to fight
or chase me away.
20Listen to my plans for you,
people of Edom.
Your children will be dragged off
and your country destroyed.
21The sounds of your destruction
will reach the Red Sea
and cause the earth to shake.
22An enemy will swoop down
to attack you,
like an eagle spreading its wings
and circling over Bozrah.
Your warriors will be as fearful
as women giving birth.
What the Lord Says about Damascus
23 The Lord says about Damascus:
The towns of Hamath and Arpad
have heard your bad news.
They have lost hope,
and worries roll over them
like ocean waves.
24You people of Damascus
have lost your courage,
and in panic you turn to run,
gripped by fear and pain.
25Once I was pleased
with your famous city.
But now I warn you, “Escape
while you still can!”
26Soon, even your best soldiers
will lie dead in your streets.
I, the Lord All-Powerful,
have spoken.
27I will set fire to your city walls
and burn down the fortresses
King Benhadad built.
Nebuchadnezzar and the People of the Desert
28Here is what the Lord says about the Kedar tribe and the desert villages that were conquered by King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia:
Listen, you people of Kedar
and the other tribes
of the eastern desert.
I have told Nebuchadnezzar
to attack and destroy you.
29His fearsome army
will surround you,
taking your tents and possessions,
your sheep and camels.
30Run and hide,
you people of the desert
who live in villages!
Nebuchadnezzar has big plans
for you.
31You have no city walls
and no neighbors to help,
yet you think you're safe—
so I told him to attack.
32Then your camels
and large herds
will be yours no longer.
People of the Arabian Desert,
disaster will strike you
from every side,
and you will be scattered
everywhere on earth.
33Only jackals will live
where your villages once stood.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
What the Lord Says about Elam
34-35Not long after Zedekiah became king of Judah, the Lord told me to say:
People of Elam,
I, the Lord All-Powerful,
will kill the archers
who make your army strong.
36Enemies will attack
from all directions,
and you will be led captive
to every nation on earth.
37Their armies will crush
and kill you,
and you will face the disaster
that my anger brings.
38Your king and his officials
will die, and I will rule
in their place.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
39But I promise that someday
I will bring your people
back to their land.
translation_text:
Tin ti-dindaan sòon̄ Amɔn yab puee
1Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ Amɔn yab pu. Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé:
«Ba pu ní diwaal Mooleeki
jíń Gaadi tiŋki mpaan míǹ?
Ba pu ní Amɔn yab
fōō Isirayeel timmu míǹ?
Isirayeel kaa cáá jipɔɔn
un làá fōō ntimu gbanti difakaleeee?»
2An puee ti-Dindaan bí yii:
«Iwiin iba bí ki dòoń m làá yàntī bí gbìl̄
Amɔn yab tiŋyil Raaba poon ijanjakuŋkuunti.
Kitiŋ gbanti làá dāá kpántí adigbun,
bi làá wà ntimbilimu mun māntìi tú-kèe ŋŋmi.
Ŋyunti gbantee Isirayeel yab
làá fàtīí fōō bin nìn jìn̄-bee cee bi-wanti.»
3Eesbɔn yab, nín yáliŋkímaan!
Di sá yii bi nāaǹ Ayi tiŋki.
Ntimbilimu mun māntìi tú Raaba tiŋkee,
gbámaan ibiil bí jòò-ni.
Dūmaan kpɔsatab kí pèen̄,
gāāmaan ikpiisilan!
Yìim̀maan tinaabakalin.
Bi cúú diwaal Mooleeki ki cáǹ kuyuŋu,
ki kpáaǹ di-tandambi nì di-kpilib dicilpu.
4Raaba tiŋki, kisapɔmbiki kin gáatèe,
ba pu ní a nìn dàkà a-ba a-tantakal
nì a-kpaaŋŋi ŋin lòoǹ tiŋanee pu míǹ?
A nìn máká a-gaajati pu.
A nìn bàlifī a-ba yii:
«Ŋma di sá-u ní kí já nì mi?»
5«M làá cáań dinyoondi kí tɔ̄
ni-kɔŋkɔnnaatɔb kɔkɔ pu,
ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.
M làá jà ni-kɔkɔ ní sāǹ
báà ŋma ń nīn pée túĺ u-nimbiin cáaa,
ní báà ubɔ dāa kpá kí kóoǹ
bin bíi sáńee kí kpāfì.
6«Míǹ boonee, m làá fàtīí gíiǹní Amɔn yab
bin bi cúú ki cūnnì kuyuŋuee.»
Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee dee.
Tin ti-Dindaan sòon̄ Eedoom yab puee
7Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ Eedoom yab pu. Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé:
«Biciŋfitiibi kaa ti bí Teeman tiŋkin níii?
Binyiliibi kaa ti nyí níii?
Bi-ciiŋyi wáŋkì níii?
8Deedan yab, sām̀maan!
Fàtīmaan ni-boon kí tīī.
Sām̀maan kí báĺ itaŋkpalɔkɔn!
M làá cáań dinàandi kí tɔ̄ Eesayuu naantiibi pu,
di sá yii ŋyunti bāań bí dáaĺ bi-tafal.
9Bin kìtī fiinyi subiliŋee yaa láa bāań ni-ceeyee,
baa làá dāá kíǹ disubil dibaba.
Binaayub yaa láa dɔ́miń ni-cee kunyeeuee,
bi làá dāá nàan̄ tin kɔkɔ bi dāa ŋūǹee.
10Di sá yii man di làá fūkul̀ Eesayuu naantiibi.
M làá nyāntí ni-balilammu kí páań mpaampiin pu.
Naa dāa gíti ŋūǹ kí cù kí báĺ niin.
Ni-naantiibi nì ni-nabiyaamu nì
ni-kɔŋkɔnnaatɔb làá nàan̄.
Ubɔ dāa kpá kí tùkù-ni yii:
11<Yàntīmaan ni-taŋkpiibiliŋ,
ti làá kpèè-ŋi kí tīī-ni,
ní ni-kpiipoobi ŋūǹ kí nīn máká m-pu.>»
12Di sá yii ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé:
«Pīlifì, bin maa nìn páb́ yii bí nyɔ̀ m-ŋuul kɔŋkɔnnyɔkaaunee nyùn̄ kaa là. Ní sii Eedoom, a dàkafī yii baa làá dáaĺ a-tafalaaa? A làá nyɔ̀ m-ŋuul kɔŋkɔnnyɔkaaun kaa bál̀. 13Man ni-Dindaan di pūtì yii m sá Unimbɔti ní ki làá yàntī a-tiŋyil Boosiraa ń kpántí adigbun ŋma, ntimbiil paaŋŋu. Bi yaa làá dāá tɔ̄ ubɔ mbusu àá kí kɔ́ǹ ubɔ icooyee, kíǹ ní bi làá dāá yòon̄ ŋabika. Ki-timmu kɔkɔ làá dāá kpántí adigbun ŋma kí nīn cá jaanjaan.» Ti-Dindaan di sòon̄ míǹ.
14Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi tibɔti tiba,
ní ntuun ŋubɔ cáań-tì ki nāatì atimbun kɔkɔ:
«Kóom̀maan kí kpāfì! Cùú jámaan Eedoom tiŋki.
Yīkìmaan! Jámaan-kì!»
15«Tiŋman, m làá yàntī sii Eedoom
ń kpántí uluŋkikaa anibul kansikin,
kitiŋ kin ní báà ŋma làá nīn kpèé ki sìŋkīǹee.
16A nìn fàantí báà ŋma,
a nìn dàkafī yii a tɔ́kɔ́ bin kíǹee kɔkɔ pu,
ama a nìn bíi kíiĺ a-ba ní.
A kóò itaŋkpalɔkɔn
ki lúń yilpu yilpu.
Ama báà a yaa máń a-diiku ki tɔ́kɔǹ yilpu
kii ukaabɔnee,
m làá dū-si kí tɔ̄ń taapu.»
Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.
17«Eedoom tiŋki làá kpántí adigbun ŋma ní. Bisanjitiliibi kɔkɔ yaa láa ká bi nín nāaǹ-si puee, án làá dāá ŋá-bi bitii ní bí nīn búǹ ifoon. 18An dāa bí kii Soodoom nì Goomoora timmu nì ntimu mun nìn māntìi tú-muee nín nìn nāaǹ puee ní, ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ. Ubɔ kaa làá dāá gíti kɔ́ niin, uniseen kaa dāa gíti kíikí kí kàl̄ niin.»
19Ti-Dindaan bí yii:
«M làá dāá nīn bí kii gbikinti
nín nyēē kimɔgbaayin Jɔɔdan buŋgbandi
ki cá laakin timɔsɔn bée puee ní.
Kii dinimbil nín kábití puee,
m làá yàntī báà ŋma ń búntí.
Míǹ boonee ní ḿ lēē un m lèe
kí kàan̄ Eedoom tiŋki pu ubɔti.
Di sá yii ŋma di bí kii mamee?
Ŋma di ŋūǹ kí yíiń-mi tibuul?
Uyidaan ulɔu di ŋūǹ kí yūĺ m-nimbiin?»
20Ní pīlifì tin ti-Dindaan bɔ́ntì
kí ŋá Eedoom tiŋkee,
nì tin u lēē kí ŋá Teeman yabee.
Bi làá dāá cúú-bi mpɔn ki dàtī kii tiwaŋkutee,
áli uluŋkikaa, án kpá kí gbíntí.
Bi-puee, bi làá nàan̄ bi-naakpaapɔɔku,
án kaa cáá yii án kpántí.
21Bi nín lítì puee wooku
yāntì kitiŋ cīŋkì.
Bi gbìl̀ bi-biilii pu áli Tikati mɔɔl.
22Unannanli bí kii ukaabɔn nín jɔ́ḿ kutaa pu, ki ŋàaǹ ki kpátí u-feeŋyi Boosiraa tiŋki puee ní. Yaadalee, Eedoom yab baatandambi pɔbiliŋ làá dāá bīil̀ kii imatiŋween nín cútí upɔdaan puee ní.
Tin ti-Dindaan sòon̄ Damaasi yab puee
23Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ tibɔti tin Damaasi yab puee sèé.
«Amaati nì Aripaadi timmu
nín gbìl̄ kubɔbiiu gbanti puee,
ní icoo cúú-mu.
Bi-pɔbil yíkì kii tiŋku un pu
kubuŋkpaaŋŋu jītí waa ŋūǹ kí dòon̄ sooooyee ní.
24Damaasi yab wunti yɔ̄tì
ní bi bíi bɔ́ntí kí sāǹ.
Tifaandi cúú-bi.
Dinyoondi kɔ́-bi ní bi bíi yáliŋkí
kii imatiŋween di cúú upɔdaanee.
25An ŋá mana ní bi dū kitiŋ
kin nyáń diyindee ki fá míǹ,
kitiŋ kin nìn tīī-mi dipɔɔpindee.
26Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. An pu ní ŋwiin gbantee, bi-nipɔmbi làá lítí mpaan nee pu ní bijanjaliibi kɔkɔ ń kpú. 27M làá tūū digundi din māntìi tú Damaasi tiŋkee ŋŋmi ní ŋú wà ubɔti Been-Adaadi beecindi.
Tin ti-Dindaan sòon̄ Bilaalibub nibul puee
28Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ tibɔti tin bilaalibub nì Asɔɔr beeŋi ŋin Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar nìn jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹee sèé:
«Yīkìmaan kí cùú jáǹ Keedaar yab!
Ní nàan̄ bin kóò kuteeunee wanti kɔkɔ.
29Ní fōōmaan bi-tantib nì bi-waŋkuti,
nì bi-kɔŋkooŋyi nì tin kɔkɔ bi cááyee.
Ní kpáaǹ bi-gutaamui,
ní kí nīn kūuntí mpɔn bi-pu yii:
Dinyoondi bí an kɔkɔ pu.»
30Ti-Dindaan bí yii:
«Asɔɔr yab, sām̀maan, yīkìmaan malaa kí fīī ni-ba
Ní sāǹ kí báĺ itaŋkpalɔkɔn.
Di sá yii Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar
bɔ́ntì ni-pu min u làá ŋá-nee.»
31Ti-Dindaan bí yii:
«Yīkìmaan kí cùú jáǹ ditimbundi
din kā ŋgbansɔŋfin
kaa dàkafī yii tiba ŋūǹ kí ŋá-dèe.
Bi-punyɔmmu kaa cáá punuubi,
kaa cáá tikpàlkaal,
ní ki kóò bi-baba ŋkpaanceeti.
32Binannanliibi làá yɔ̀ bi-gutaamui,
ní kí fūkul̀ bi-picaŋkpunti tin náaǹ nee.
Ti-Dindaan bí yii:
M làá jà binib bin kōol̀ jamba nee.
M làá cáań nnaabu kí tɔ̄ bi-pu
laakin kamaa bi yaa pée bée.
33Asɔɔr tiŋki làá kpántí
iŋɔkɔ kɔŋkooŋŋu,
kunimbaau teeku kí nīn cá jaanjaan.
Ubɔ kaa làá nīn gíti kóò ki-ni,
báà uniseen.»
Tin ti-Dindaan sòon̄ Eelam tiŋki puee
34Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì u-bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii Eelam yab pu. Ŋyunti gbantee Seedeesiyasi kpántì Juuda bɔtiu an kaa yúntì. 35Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé:
«M làá kóoĺ Eelam yab tɔbu
bun pu bi pɔ̄ɔ̄yee.
36M làá yàntī kubuŋu ń nyānní
ŋgan pú nì ŋgiil pú,
ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú nì ŋu-jeetilaŋki pú,
an dàkà yii kitiŋ jannaatiliŋ pú
kí túĺ Eelam tiŋki watil.
«M làá jà Eelam yab, bí yàl̄ kí kɔ́ an kɔkɔ pu. Bi làá dāá ká Eelam yab ntimu kɔkɔn.
37«M làá yàntī Eelam yab wunti
ń nīn gbáà kpàkpa bi-nannanliibi
nì bin nyàab̀ kí kpɔ̀-bee nimbiin.
Ti-Dindaan bí yii:
<M làá cáań nnaabu kí tɔ̄ bi-pu
m-ŋuukpaandi poon.
M làá dū kujaau kí tɔ̄ bi-pu
kí tin kúntí-bi.
38M làá kúntí Eelam tiŋkin ubɔti nì u-kàliŋkpilib,
ní kí cáań m-beejal kí yóoń kitiŋ gbantin.>»
Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.
39Ama míǹ boonee,
m làá fàtīí gíiǹní Eelam yab
bin bi nìn cūnnì kuyuŋuee bi-tiŋkin.
Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_text:
Babylon Will Be Captured
1 The Lord told me to say:
Announce what will happen
and don't leave anything out.
2Raise the signal flags;
shout so all nations can hear—
Babylon will be captured!
Marduk, Babylon's god,
will be ashamed and terrified,
and his idols broken.
3The attack on the Babylonians
will come from the north;
they and their animals will run,
leaving the land empty.
Israel and Judah Will Return to Their Land
4The Lord said:
People of Israel and Judah,
when these things happen
you will weep, and together
you will return to your land
and worship me,
the Lord your God.
5You will ask the way to Zion
and then come and join with me
in making an agreement
you won't break or forget.
6My people, you are lost sheep
abandoned in the mountains
by their shepherds.
You don't even remember
your resting place.
7I am your true pastureland,
the one who gave hope
to your ancestors.
But you abandoned me,
so when your enemies found you,
they felt no guilt
as they gobbled you up.
8 Escape from Babylonia,
my people.
Get out of that country!
Don't wait for anyone else.
9In the north I am bringing
great nations together.
They will attack Babylon
and capture it.
The arrows they shoot
are like the best soldiers,
always finding their target.
10Babylonia will be conquered,
and its enemies will carry off
everything they want.
Babylon Will Be Disgraced
The Lord said:
11People of Babylonia,
you were glad
to rob my people.
You had a good time,
making more noise
than horses
and jumping around
like calves threshing grain.
12The city of Babylon
was like a mother to you.
But it will be disgraced
and become nothing
but a barren desert.
13My anger will destroy Babylon,
and no one will live there.
Everyone who passes by
will be shocked to see
what has happened.
14Babylon has rebelled against me.
Archers, take your places.
Shoot all your arrows at Babylon.
15Attack from every side!
Babylon surrenders!
The enemy tears down
its walls and towers.
I am taking my revenge
by doing to Babylon what it did
to other cities.
16There is no one in Babylonia
to plant or harvest crops.
Even foreigners who lived there
have left for their homelands,
afraid of the enemy armies.
17Israel is a flock of sheep
scattered by hungry lions.
The king of Assyria
first gobbled Israel up.
Then Nebuchadnezzar,
king of Babylonia,
crunched on Israel's bones.
18I, the Lord All-Powerful,
the God of Israel,
punished the king of Assyria,
and I will also punish
the king of Babylonia.
19But I will bring Israel
back to its own land.
The people will be like sheep
eating their fill
on Mount Carmel
and in Bashan,
in the hill country of Ephraim
and in Gilead.
20I will rescue a few people
from Israel and Judah.
I will forgive them so completely
that their sin and guilt
will disappear,
never to be found.
The Lord's Commands to the Enemies of Babylonia
21The Lord said:
I have told
the enemies of Babylonia,
“Attack the people of Merathaim
and Pekod.
Kill them all!
Destroy their possessions!”
22Sounds of war
and the noise of destruction
can be heard.
23Babylonia was a hammer
pounding every country,
but now it lies broken.
What a shock to the nations
of the world!
24Babylonia challenged me,
the Lord God All-Powerful,
but that nation doesn't know
it is caught in a trap
that I set.
25I've brought out my weapons,
and with them I will put a curse
on Babylonia.
26Come from far away,
you enemies of Babylon!
Pile up the grain
from its storehouses,
and destroy it completely,
along with everything else.
27Kill the soldiers of Babylonia,
because the time has come
for them to be punished.
28The Babylonian army
destroyed my temple,
but soon I will take revenge.
Then refugees from Babylon
will tell about it in Zion.
29 Attack Babylon, enemy archers;
set up camp around the city,
and don't let anyone escape.
It challenged me, the holy God,
so do to it
what it did to other cities.
Proud Babylon Will Fall
30People of Babylon,
I, the Lord, promise
that even your best soldiers
will lie dead in the streets.
31Babylon, you should be named,
“The Proud One.”
But the time has come when I,
the Lord All-Powerful,
will punish you.
32You are proud,
but you will stumble and fall,
and no one will help you up.
I will set your villages on fire,
and everything around you
will go up in flames.
33You Babylonians were cruel
to Israel and Judah.
You took them captive, and now
you refuse to let them go.
34But I, the Lord All-Powerful,
will rescue and protect them.
I will bring peace to their land
and trouble to yours.
35I have declared war on you,
your officials, and advisors.
36This war will prove
that your prophets
are liars and fools.
And it will frighten
your warriors.
37Then your chariot horses
and the foreigners in your army
will refuse to go into battle,
and the enemy will carry away
everything you treasure.
38Your rivers and canals
will dry up.
All of this will happen,
because your land
is full of idols,
and they have made fools
of you.
39 Never again will people live
in your land—
only desert animals, jackals,
and unclean birds.
40 I destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah
and the nearby towns,
and I will destroy Babylon
just as completely.
No one will live there again.
Babylonia Is Invaded
The Lord said:
41Far to the north,
a nation and its allies
have been awakened.
They are powerful
and ready for war.
42Bows and arrows and swords
are in their hands.
The soldiers are cruel
and show no pity.
The hoofbeats of their horses echo
like ocean waves
crashing against the shore.
The army has lined up for battle
and is coming to attack you,
people of Babylonia!
43Ever since your king heard
about this army,
he has been weak with fear;
he twists and turns in pain
like a woman giving birth.
44Babylonia, I will attack you
like a lion from the forest,
attacking sheep in a meadow
along the Jordan.
In a moment the flock runs,
and the land is empty.
Who will I choose to attack you?
I will do it myself!
No one can force me to fight
or chase me away.
45Listen to my plans for you,
people of Babylonia.
Your children will be dragged off,
and your country destroyed.
46The sounds of your destruction
will be heard among the nations,
and the earth will shake.
translation_text:
Bi làá nàan̄ Babiloon tiŋki ní kí fīī Isirayeel
1Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ nì u-bɔnaatiliu Yeereemii Babiloon tiŋki, an dàkà yii Kaldee yab tiŋki pu puee sèé:
2«Bāakìmaan tibɔti nee kí tùkù atimbun kɔkɔ,
ní cóoḿmaan tidaandi kí yàntī bí béé-tì.
Yàntīmaan bí béé-tì, ní taa báĺ tiba.
Lìmaan yii:
<Bi jáń ki fōō Babiloon tiŋki,
icoo cúú diwaal Beeli,
diwaal Maarduuki lítì.
Icoo cúú u-waaŋi gbanti,
bi kúntì u-jɔkɔŋwanti gbanti.
3Di sá yii ditimbundi diba nyánní ŋgan pú
ki dòoń kí já nì kì
kí yàntī kí kpántí kunimbaau teeku.
Ubɔ kaa ti làá kɔ́ ki-pu.
Binibaaa, tiwaŋkutaaa,
bi-kɔkɔ làá sāǹ kí wāŋkì.>»
4Ti-Dindaan bí yii:
«Ŋyunti gbantee,
Isirayeel yab nì Juuda yab
làá dāá nóoń dicilpu kí dāan̄.
Bi làá dāá nīn còom̄ ki sūǹ
ki nyàab̀ man bi-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu.
5Bi làá dāá bàlifì kí béé nsan
ŋun bi dì ki cá Siiyɔn tiŋkinee.
Bi làá dāá fàtī bi-nimbiin kí túĺ kitiŋee pú.
Bi làá dāá dāan̄ ní bi nì man
ń ŋá mpèé ŋun làá nīn bí ki cá jaanjaanee.
Bi dāa pée kpá kí súntí ŋu-pu.
6M-nibul yab nìn bí kii ipii in wáŋkèe ní.
Bi-kpàaliibi nìn yāntì bi wáŋkì
ní ki yāntì bi tú ki yìiǹ ajoon pu.
Bi nìn yìiǹ ajoon pu
ki póotí ŋgbantamu pu,
ní ki súntì bi-naabakati pu.
7Bin kɔkɔ yaa nìn ká-bee
nìn cútí-bi ní kí tɔ̀ntī
ní bi-nannanliibi lì yii:
<Taa bíi ŋáań tikpitil tibaa!
Tiŋman puee, binib gbanti
yīntiǹ ti-Dindaan
un di sá difiil kɔŋkooŋŋu,
ní bi-naanjab nìn máká u-puee.>»
8Sām̀maan kí nyā Babiloon tiŋki,
yīkìmaan Kaldee yab tiŋki!
Lìntīmaan kupicaŋkpuŋu nyɔkɔpu kii iŋɔjaayee.
9Di sá yii m làá lùkutī atimbuŋkpaan dikitil
ní kí tɔ̄-ŋi ŋí já nì Babiloon tiŋki.
Atimbun gbanti làá nyānní ŋgan pú ní
kí tàtīí gbàan̄ dikɔ̀ndi pu
kí já kí fōō kitiŋ gbanti.
Bi-piiŋyi bí kii ubaatandaan
un kaa fàtīi gítí mmɔŋki iŋaŋkulimee ní.
10Bi làá fūkul̀ Kaldee yab tiŋki,
ní bin kɔkɔ làá fūkul̀-bee làá kóoǹ tigaajawan kí báĺ,
ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.
11Nín̄ fàal̀maan kí nīn bí dipɔɔpindin,
nimbi bin dɔ́miń ki fúkúl̀ man gaajawantee.
Nín̄ yùkufīmaan kii dinabil di yú kumɔsɔŋunee.
Nín̄ sūm̀maan kii itaamuee!
12Icoo cúú ni-tiŋki kin sá kii ni-nee,
un di màl̄-nee fá u-jilmau.
Kɔŋkɔnnee, ni-tiŋki di sá
kin lúŋkèe ntimu kɔkɔ kansikin.
Kì kpántì kuteeu, kitiŋkuliŋŋi.
13Diŋuul din ti-Dindaan fōōyee puee,
binib kaa ti kóò ni-tiŋkin,
kì kpántì kuteekpaaŋŋu ní.
An ŋáań bin kɔkɔ jītí Babiloon tiŋkinee bitii.
Bi yaa ká nnaabu ŋun jéetì kitiŋee puee,
bi fátí dipɔɔbiildi biilii ní.
14Nimbi bipintɔliibi kɔkɔ,
màntīí tūmaan Babiloon tiŋki kí já nì kì.
Ní tɔ̄maan ni-piiŋyi, ní taa mɔ̄tì i-pu,
di sá yii kì yīntiǹ ti-Dindaan.
15Ijaan kɔkɔ puee,
nín̄ kūuntímaan ki-pu ijanjakuŋkuunti!
Bi yōoǹ bi-ŋalii yilpu ki sáǹ ki kɔ́ bi-nannanliibi.
Digundi din bi máń ki tú kitiŋee lítì.
Ti-Dindaan di bíi tɔ̀ ipɔntoon!
Tɔ̀maan Babiloon tiŋki ipɔntoon,
ŋámaan-kì kii kì nín ŋá bin kíǹee puee.
16Ní kúntímaan Babiloon tiŋkin,
bin būul̀ee nì bin cēēyee.
Báà ŋma ń sāǹ kujaau kun nàantí nee
kí gítí u-nibul cee,
báà ŋma ń sāǹ kí gítí u-tiŋkin.
17Isirayeel yab nìn bí kii dipibil din wáŋkì
ní gbikintib sáń ki jèe ní.
Gbikintipeepeekaa un cúú-bi ki ŋmɔ́ee di sá Asuur bɔtiu. Míǹ boonee ní Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar mun dɔ́miń ki kɔ́fì bi-kpabiŋ. 18An pu ní ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu bí yii: «M làá jáǹ Babiloon bɔtiu nì u-tiŋki, kii m nín jáń nì Asuur bɔtiu puee ní.
19«M làá fàtīí gíiǹní Isirayeel yab
bi-pikpaapɔɔkun.
Bi làá ká kí jī Kaarmeel jool pu
nì Baasan timpiliŋki pu,
nì Eefiraayiim jooŋŋi pu
nì Galaadi tiŋkin kí díkí.
20Man ni-Dindaan di bíi sòoǹ yii
ŋyunti gbantee,
bi làá dāá nyàab̀ Isirayeel yìntitam
ama baa làá dāá ká.
Bi làá dāá nyàab̀ Juuda kpitii
kaa làá dāá ká.
Di sá yii m làá dāá dū bin kíǹ
kaa kpíìyee kpitii kí pɔ̄-bi.
21«Bóob́maan dikɔ̀ndi kí cùú jáǹ
Maratiim tiŋki.
Ní cùú já kì nì Peekoodi yab!
Ní pɔ̀fì-bi kí kpɔ̀ kí céetí bi-kɔkɔ múb.
Man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ.
Á ŋá m nín tīī-si mara á ŋá puee deedee.
22Ti gbìl̄ dikɔ̀ndi wooku
nì dibintiŋkpaandi pu kitiŋee ni!
23Babiloon tiŋki nìn bí kii
dikújal din gbáà ki mátí kitiŋ kɔkɔee ní.
Kin an dī mana ní bi gbáń ki wīil̀-kì
kì kíǹ ki dɔ̄ akati akati míǹ?
Babiloon tiŋki kpántì dinyoondi paaŋŋu
atimbun kansikin.
24Babiloon, m píĺ-si kutaliŋŋu
ní a sàl̄ kaa kpáàa béè.
Bi bīitì a-pu ki cúú-si,
kun puee a jáń nì man ni-Dindaan»
25Ti-Dindaan pīitì u-janjawanti diiku
ní ki lēeń u-ŋuul janjawanti.
Di sá yii ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan
cáá ditundi kí tɔ̄ Kaaldee yab tiŋkin.
26Nyānnímaan ajan kɔkɔ pu kí dāan̄ kitiŋ nee ni!
Ní pìitī ki-cakalaabi
kí kóoǹ ki-gaajawanti kí kpúkuń
ní kí nàan̄-kì.
Tiba nì tiba kaa máaǹ kí kíń.
27Kpɔ̀maan ki-janjaliibi bimɔntiibi kɔkɔ,
cùnnìmaan-bi nnaŋkpɔpaan pu!
Dinimbinaamandi kɔ́-bi,
di sá yii ŋyunti bāań
ti-Dindaan ń dáaĺ bi-tafal.
28Pīlifìmaan, bin bíi sáń Babiloon tiŋkee,
bin dáá gbíntìi bí dimaŋfalinee
di dɔ́miń ki máafí Siiyɔn tibɔmɔntiil yii:
«Ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu tɔ̀n̄-ti,
u tɔ̀n̄ u-diiku pɔntooŋyi.
29Kóom̀maan bipintɔliibi,
bin kɔkɔ pīil̀ itɔfee kí kpāfì bí jáǹ Babiloon tiŋki.
Lùkù kí gíb́maan-kì ijaan kɔkɔ pu,
ní taa yàntī báà ubɔ ń sāǹ kí ŋmátí.
Ní pàmaan-kì kí nóó ki-tuŋkpitiŋ.
Ŋámaan-kì kii kì nín ŋá bin kíǹee puee.
Di sá yii kì yōoǹ ki-ba yilpu
ti-Dindaan Isirayeel circir Nimbɔtiu nimbiin.
30«An pu ní bi-nipɔmbi làá lítí mpaan nee pu ŋwiin gbanti, ki-janjaliibi kɔkɔ làá kpú.» Ti-Dindaan di sòon̄ míǹ.
31«Babiloon ulambidaan, man nì sii dee,
man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan di lī míǹ.
A-wiiŋŋu bāań díǹ dee,
ŋyunti ŋun m làá dáaĺ a-tafalee dee.
32Kilambidaŋ gbéetì ki lítì,
ubɔ kaa bí kí yòon̄-kì kí yóoń.
M tūū ki-timmu ŋŋmi,
an làá wà tin kɔkɔ māntìi tú-kèe.»
33Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé:
«Bi ŋúb́ Isirayeel yab
nì Juuda yab ki sàantí.
Bin cúú-bi kuyuŋuee ŋúb́-bi
kaa là kí gíiǹ-bi kí líí.
34Ama man un mɔ́tí bi-puee cáá mpɔn,
man ní bi yíì ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan.
M làá mɔ̄tì bi-pu nì tininjati.
Míǹ ní m làá ŋá kí yàntī Babiloon yab ń nyɔ̀ ŋkpatim
ní kí cáań ŋgbansɔŋfi kitiŋ kɔkɔ pu.»
Tin ti-Dindaan bɔ́ntì Babiloon puee
35Ti-Dindaan bí yii:
«Bí já nì Kaaldee yab,
bí já nì Babiloon yab,
bí já nì Babiloon bɔtibiliŋ nì ki-ciŋfitiibi!
36Bí já nì bibɔɔbi,
bi-yiliŋ ń lábití!
Bí já nì bibaatandambi,
bi-wunti ń yɔ̀tī.
37Bí já nì ki-taamui nì ki-janjatɔrɔkub,
nì nyaaŋmaliŋku nib bin kóò bi-kansikinee,
bí kpántí kii binimpoobee!
Bí já nì laakin ki kpáafí ki-gaajatee.
38Bí já nì ki-buŋyi í kpā!
Di sá yii kì sá awaa tiŋki ní.
Ntimbiil wanti gbanti yāntì bi-yiliŋ lábitì.
39An pu ní alambuntilaŋkpan
làá dāá nīn kóò Babiloon tiŋkin nì isaakpan,
ní taataabi ń dāá kàl̄ niin.
Ubɔ kaa ti làá kɔ́ niin dalba dalba,
kitiŋ nee làá dāá dòon̄ fám abin abin.»
40Ti-Dindaan bí yii:
«Kii m nín nìn nāaǹ
Soodoom nì Goomoora timmu
nì ntimu mun māntìi tú-muee puee,
míǹ ní ubɔ kaa ti làá kɔ́ Babiloon tiŋkin,
uniseen kaa làá ti kàl̄ niin.
41Dinibul diba nyánní ŋgan pú,
an sá ditimbuŋkpaandi ní.
Atimbun kupaau nyánní
doooo kitiŋgbeennyɔkɔ ki dòoń.
42Bi-janjaliibi ŋúb́ itɔfi nì ŋkpamu.
Bi cáá nnimbinaakulim kaa sūǹ isaa.
Dibintindi din bi gèe
náań nì tiŋku nín ŋáań kuwoou puee ní.
Bi jɔ́m̀ ki kā itaamu pu.
Bi páaǹ ipɔ̀n pu tiŋan
kí já nì sii Babiloon tiŋki.
43Babiloon bɔtiu gbìl̄ bi-pu.
U-wunti yɔ̄tì ní dinyoondi cúú-u,
ní u bíi gbìl̀ tiweendi pu
kii imatiŋween di cúú upɔdaanee.
44Ti-Dindaan bí yii:
M làá nīn bí kii gbikinti
un di nyánní kimɔgbaayin
ki kpàkaǹ Jɔɔdan buŋŋu
ki cá kumɔsɔŋu laŋkee ní.
Kii dinimbil nín kábití puee,
míǹ ní m làá yàntī ki-nib ń yīkì.
Míǹ boonee ní ḿ kàan̄ Babiloon tiŋkin
ubɔti un m lēēyee.
Di sá yii ŋma di bí kii mamee?
Ŋma di ŋūǹ kí yíiń-mi tibuul?
Uyidaan ulɔu di ŋūǹ kí já nì mi?»
45Ní pīlifìmaan tin ti-Dindaan
bɔ́ntì kí ŋá Babiloon tiŋkee,
tin u lēē kí ŋá Kaaldee yabee.
Tiŋman, bi làá dāá dàtī-bi mpɔn
ki kpáaǹ bi-biyaamu kii tiwaŋkutee.
Bi-puee, bi làá nàan̄ bi-naabakati,
an kaa cáá digbíntil.
46Bi nín gbìl̄ yii:
«Bi jáń ki fōō Babiloon tiŋkee», kitiŋ cīŋkì ní,
ní ibiil fōō ki píĺ dàii atimbun kɔkɔn.

english_text:
Babylon Will Be Destroyed
1I, the Lord, am sending
a wind to destroy
the people of Babylonia
and Babylon, its capital.
2Foreign soldiers will come
from every direction,
and when the disaster is over,
Babylonia will be empty
and worthless.
3I will tell these soldiers,
“Attack quickly,
before the Babylonians
can string their bows
or put on their armor.
Kill their best soldiers
and destroy their army!”
4Their troops will fall wounded
in the streets of Babylon.
5Everyone in Israel and Judah
is guilty.
But I, the Lord All-Powerful,
their holy God,
have not abandoned them.
6Get out of Babylon!
Run for your lives!
If you stay, you will be killed
when I take revenge on the city
and punish it for its sins.
7 Babylon was my golden cup,
filled with the wine
of my anger.
The nations of the world
got drunk on this wine
and went insane.
8But suddenly, Babylon will fall
and be destroyed.
I, the Lord, told the foreigners
who lived there,
“Weep for the city!
Get medicine for its wounds;
maybe they will heal.”
9The foreigners answered,
“We have already tried
to treat Babylon's wounds,
but they would not heal.
Come on, let's all go home
to our own countries.
Nothing is left in Babylonia;
everything is destroyed.”
10The people of Israel said,
“Tell everyone in Zion!
The Lord has taken revenge
for what Babylon did to us.”
The Lord Wants Babylon Destroyed
11I, the Lord,
want Babylon destroyed,
because its army
destroyed my temple.
So, you kings of Media,
sharpen your arrows
and pick up your shields.
12Raise the signal flag
and attack the city walls.
Post more guards.
Have soldiers watch the city
and set up ambushes.
I have made plans
to destroy Babylon,
and nothing will stop me.
13 People of Babylon, you live
along the Euphrates River
and are surrounded by canals.
You are rich,
but now the time has come
for you to die.
14I, the Lord All-Powerful,
swear by my own life
that enemy soldiers
will fill your streets
like a swarm of locusts.
They will shout
and celebrate their victory.
A Hymn of Praise
(Jeremiah 10.12-16)
