Míǹ puee a làá dū iwiin saalaa kpá alaataa anaa ní kí túń Isirayeel nibul kpitii nyiŋfiŋu. 6Ŋyunti gbanti yaa jítèe, á fàtī kí dòon̄ ŋgiil pú ní kí túń Juuda beel kpitii nyiŋfiŋu iwiin imuŋku ili. M síiǹ-si ŋwiin ŋubɔee dibindi diba. 7Míǹ boonee, á fàtīí kpèè Jeerusaleem tiŋki kin bi māntìi tú kí jáǹ-kèe. Á tàntī a-ŋaliŋu ncal ní kí sòoǹ m-nyɔɔbundi kí tɔ̄ ki-pu. 8Mamee, m làá dū iŋmii kí bóob́-si án nín làá ŋá pu á taa ŋmā kí fàtī dijandi diba pu kí gítí din kíǹee kí nīn cí iwiin in bi nín māntìi tú kitiŋ kí jáǹ-kèe làá kúntée.
9«Yòon̄ bilee nì ɔɔji nì atuun nì ikpintumpu nì iyoo nì bilee un pɔ̄ɔ̄yee. Dū kɔkɔ kí ŋá disambibaantiilin kí ŋmàlim̀ kí dūú ŋá kpɔnɔ. Iwiin saalaa kpá alaataa anaa in a làá dūú dòon̄ a-takakal puee, tijin tin a làá nīn jīǹee dee. 10Ŋwiinee, tijin tin a làá nīn jīǹee làá nyā graambi alaataa ali ní. A làá nīn jīǹ míǹ ní ŋwiin kamaa. 11Nnyim min a làá nīn nyùee muee, bi làá ŋmàntī-mì ní kí tīī-si. Ŋwiinee, a làá nīn nyù liitiri ubɔ ní. 12Bi nín cáá ɔɔji ki ŋáań kalaabi bi bí puee, míǹ ní a-jinti làá nīn bí. Á dū binib binti kí kpāā ŋŋmi kí púĺ kpɔnɔb gbanti báà ŋma nimbiin.» 13Ní ti-Dindaan kútì ki lī yii: «Míǹ ní Isirayeel yab làá jī tijin tin kɔ́ tijɔkɔndee nnicantimu mun poon m làá jà-bi kí cùnnèe.» 14Niinee ní m téeń yii: «Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti, maa kɔ́ǹ m-ba tijɔkɔndi ki ká! Doooo m-biyatin, maa láa pée ŋmɔ́ kuwaŋkuluu kun kpíìyee àá kuwaŋkuluu kun ní upeecuncuti cúúyee. Báà kunaŋu kun kòóyee kaa láa pée kɔ́ m-nyɔkɔn.» 15Ní ti-Dindaan kíí-mi yii: «An yaa sée, m pú-si nsan á dū tinaabin kí kpāā ŋŋmi kí púĺ a-kpɔnɔu kí yàntī tinibin.» 16Ní u gíti kútì ki lī yii: «Nisaaleen, m làá kúntí kpɔnɔb bin bi dūu kpáafì Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee. Binib làá dāá ŋmàntī bi-jinti ní kí ŋmɔ́ kunimbaaun, ní kí dāá ŋmàntī nnyim kí nyɔ̀ kufaaŋŋun. 17Di sá kpɔnɔ nì nnyim làá dāá lóó-bi, ní báà ŋma dāa kíǹ ki bí dinyoondin. Bi làá dāá dúntí ní kí kpú bi-kpitii pu.»

english_text:
Jerusalem's Coming Destruction
The Lord said:
1Ezekiel, son of man, get a sharp sword and use it to cut off your hair and beard. Weigh the hair and divide it into three equal piles. 2After you attack the brick that stands for Jerusalem, burn one pile of your hair on the brick. Chop up the second pile and let the small pieces of hair fall around the brick. Throw the third pile into the wind, and I will strike it with my own sword.
3Keep a few of the hairs and wrap them in the hem of your clothes. 4Then pull out a few of those hairs and throw them in the fire, so they will also burn. This fire will spread, destroying everyone in Israel.
5I am the Lord God, and I have made Jerusalem the most important place in the world, and all other nations admire it. 6But the people of Jerusalem rebelled and refuse to obey me. They ignored my laws and have become even more sinful than the nations around them.
7So tell the people of Jerusalem:
I am the Lord God! You have refused to obey my laws and teachings, and instead you have obeyed the laws of the surrounding nations. You have become more rebellious than any of them! 8Now all those nations will watch as I turn against you and punish you 9for your sins. Your punishment will be more horrible than anything I've ever done or will ever do again. 10 Parents will be so desperate for food that they will eat their own children, and children will eat their parents. Those who survive this horror will be scattered in every direction.
11Your sins have disgusted me and made my temple unfit as a place to worship me. So I swear by my own life that I will cut you down and show you no pity. 12A third of you will die here in Jerusalem from disease or starvation. Another third will be killed in war. And I will scatter the last third of you in every direction, then track you down and kill you.
13You will feel my fierce anger until I have finished taking revenge. Then you will know that I, the Lord, was furious because of your disobedience. 14Every passerby will laugh at your destruction. Foreign nations 15will insult you and make fun of you, but they will also be shocked and terrified at what I did in my anger. 16I will destroy your crops until you starve to death, and disasters will strike you like arrows. 17 Starvation and wild animals will kill your children. I'll punish you with horrible diseases, and your enemies will strike you down with their swords. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
Unimbɔti làá jáǹ Jeerusaleem yab
1«Sii nisaaleen, yòon̄ bɔlfi kí dūú ŋá kijikoolkaai. Á dū-kì kí kòol̀ a-yil nì a-nyimpul. Míǹ boonee, á ŋmàntī tiyikpiti tin a kōol̀ee saniya pu ní kí cúú yàkatī mita pu. 2Bi nín māntìi tú kitiŋ kí jáǹ-kì puee yaa láa kúntèe, á dāá dū dijandi diba kí wà ŋŋmi kitiŋ kansikin. Á dāá yòon̄ dijanliliitiil kí dū a-tàataajiki kí fáá kí màntīí tū kitiŋ. Á dāá dū dijantataatiil din kíǹee kí yàaǹ kubuŋu ń yòon̄ ní man ń dāá dū m-tàataajiki kí páań di-boon. 3Ama á dāá kíń tikutee fiii kí dūú fúuń a-wampeeŋkaati lookun. 4Á dāá lēē pooki kí tɔ̄ ŋŋmin án wà. Ŋŋmi gbanti làá dāá nyàtī kí bà Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ cee.
5«Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di bíi sòoǹ yii: Kpèèmaan Jeerusaleem tiŋki! M dū-kì ki ŋá atimbun kansikin, ní ntimu māntìi tú-kì. 6Ama Jeerusaleem yab dū marab bin m tīī-bee ki fá. Bi yíì kaa nóó m-bɔkpaaŋi. Bi gíti ŋá ikpiti ki jítiǹ atimbun nì ntimu mun māntìi tú-bee nib. Di sá yii bi dū m-bɔkpaaŋi nì m-marab ki fá kaa tɔ́-ŋi. 7An pu ní man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti sòon̄ yii: Ni jáń nì mi ki jítiǹ atimbun ŋin māntìi tú-nee, ní kaa tɔ́ m-marabaaa, kaa tí ŋúb́ m-bɔkpaaŋi mun, ní kaa kpáàa dī atimbun ŋin māntìi tú-nee marab gba. 8An pu ní man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti sòon̄ yii: m làá jáǹ nimbi Jeerusaleem yab. M làá dáaĺ ni-tafal atimbun ŋin kíǹee nimbiin ŋi-nib ń wāl̀. 9Ni-timbiilituuŋŋi puee, m làá jáǹ-ni kii m nín kaa láá pée jáń nì ni dalba dalba puee ní. Maa làá ti pée jáǹ-ni míǹ mun jaanjaan. 10Míǹ puee, bibaatiibi làá dāá ŋmɔ́ bi-biyaamu nanti ní mbiyaamu ń dāá ŋmɔ́ bi-baabi nanti. M làá dāá dáaĺ ni-tafal ní kí jà bin kíǹ kaa kpíìyee kí yàl̄ an kɔkɔ pu.
11«An puee man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti un bí dimaŋfalinee nín lī yii, ni nín ŋá pu ki dū ni-waaŋi nì ni-timbiilituuŋŋi ki kɔ́ǹ m-Diiku tijɔkɔndee, ma mun làá fàtī m-boon kí tīī-ni. M làá dàkà-ni nnimbinaakulim kaa làá sɔ̄ ni-saai. 12Bi yaa cúú-ni ki yākatì mita puee, bìlbil kúm àá ŋkùm làá kpɔ̀ dijandi diba kitiŋin, ní bí dū kitàataajiki kí kpɔ̀ dijandi diba kitiŋ gundi boon. Dijandi din kíǹee, m làá jà-bi kí yàl̄ ijaan kɔkɔ pu ní kí dū m-tàataajiki kí kùl̄ kí páań bi-boon. 13M làá yàntī m-ŋuul ń tɔ̄ di-tundi. M làá yàntī m-bum ń tɔ̄ mi-tundi kí cáá kátí ní ḿ tɔ̀ m-pɔntooŋyi. Niinee, ni làá béé yii man ni-Dindaan di sòon̄, di sá yii ni nín kaa yú nì mi deedeeyee kaa mɔ̄ǹ-mi. 14M làá yàntī Jeerusaleem tiŋki ń kpántí adigbuŋkati ŋma, ní kí yàntī atimbun ŋin māntìi tú-kèe nì bisanjitiliibi ń nīn cáa bèel̄ ki lāā. 15M làá dū m-ŋuul kí sòoǹ Jeerusaleem yab bɔti ní kí wòoǹ-bi tikpil. Atimbun ŋin māntìi tú-kèe làá nīn bèel̄-kì ki sìí-kì, ama kì làá nīn sá mun kii ŋabikee ní ki tīī-bi ní bí fàŋkì. Man ni-Dindaan di bíi sòoǹ nì ni.
16«M làá dū ŋkùm kí tɔ̄ ni-pu mí kpɔ̀-ni. Mi làá tīī-ni tiweendi kii ipiinee ní. M làá bīil̀ ni-jiŋkpaafikaati ní kí yàntī ní kpú ŋkùm. 17M làá dū ŋkùm nì ipeecuncuti kí tɔ̄ ni-pu ní í kpɔ̀ ni-biyaamu. Bìlbil kúm nì tipɔmbɔti nì kujaau làá kpɔ̀ kí céetí-ni. Man ni-Dindaan di sòon̄ nì ni.»

english_text:
Israel Is Doomed
1The Lord God said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, face the hills of Israel and tell them:
3Listen, you mountains and hills, and every valley and gorge! I, the Lord, am about to turn against you and crush all the places where foreign gods are worshiped. 4Every altar will be smashed, and in front of the idols I will put to death the people who worship them. 5Dead bodies and bones will be lying around the idols and the altars. 6Every town in Israel will be destroyed to make sure that each shrine, idol, and altar is smashed—everything the Israelites made will be a pile of ruins. 7All over the country, your people will die. And those who survive will know that I, the Lord, did these things. 8I will let some of the people live through this punishment, but I will scatter them among the nations, 9where they will be prisoners. And when they think of me, they will realize that they disgraced me by rebelling and by worshiping idols. They will hate themselves for the evil things they did, 10and they will know that I am the Lord and that my warnings must be taken seriously.
11The Lord God then said:
Ezekiel, beat your fists together and stomp your feet in despair! Moan in sorrow, because the people of Israel have done disgusting things and now will be killed by enemy troops, or they will die from starvation and disease. 12Those who live far away will be struck with deadly diseases. Those who live nearby will be killed in war. And the ones who are left will starve to death. I will let loose my anger on them! 13These people used to offer incense to idols at altars built on hills and mountaintops and in the shade of large oak trees. But when they see dead bodies lying around those altars, they will know that I am the Lord. 14I will make their country a barren wasteland, from the Southern Desert to the town of Diblah in the north. Then they will know that I, the Lord, have done these things.
translation_text:
Bin tòotī awaayee
1Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii: 2«Nisaaleen, fàtī a-nimbikpeeŋu kí túĺ Isirayeel jooŋŋi kí sòoǹ m-nyɔɔbundi kí tɔ̄ ŋi-pu. 3Lì yii: Isirayeel jooŋŋi, pīlifì anyɔɔbun ŋin ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti cáá kí tùkù bin kóò ni-puee nì bin kóò ŋgbantamu pu nì igalin nì atantaka poonee. U bí yii: <Kpèè, m làá cáań kujaau kí tɔ̄ ni-pu ní kí nàan̄ ni-waatootipaaŋyi. 4Bi làá gbá kí wìil̀ ni-saraafaŋyi nì ni-sambiyaamu mun poon ni tùutī talaalubee. M làá kpɔ̀ ni-kansikin biba kí bíĺ ni-waaŋi gbanti nimbiin. 5M làá dū Isirayeel yab bin kpíìyee wunti kí bíĺ bi-waaŋi nimbiin ní kí kàfì bi-kpabiŋ kí yàaǹ bi-saraafaŋyi pu kí màntīí tū. 6Laakin kamaa ni yaa kóòyee, ni-timmu làá kpántí adigbuŋkati ŋma ní ní sāǹ kí fá ni-waatootipaaŋyi. Bi làá gbá kí wìil̀ ni-saraafaŋyi ní iaa ti làá nīn bí tiban. Bi làá nàan̄ ni-waaŋi kí kúntí-ŋi, ní kí gbá kí bɔ̀b̄ ni-sambiyaamu mun poon ni tùutī talaalubee. Bi làá nàan̄ tin kɔkɔ ni pée dū ni-ŋalii ki máń àá ki kpítèe. 7Ni-kansikin tikpil làá lítí kí kpú. Niinee ní ní béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan. 8Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, m làá yàntī ni-kansikin biba ń ŋmátí kí taa kpú kujaaun. Bíǹ gbanti di làá dāá yàl̄ kí cù nnicantimun. 9Bin ŋmátì gbantee làá dāá téetí m-pu bin cúú-bi kuyuŋuee kansikin. Bi làá dāá téetí m nín nāaǹ-bi miŋyee pu. Di sá yii bi nyáń m-boon: bi fātì bi-boon ki tīī-mi ní ki dū bi-nimbikpeeŋu ki báaǹ awaa pu. Niinee bi-naŋki làá dāá nyā nì bi-ba ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin bi ŋée pu. 10Bi làá béé yii man di sá bi-Dindaan, ní m nín nìn sòon̄ yii nnaabu làá jēetí bi-puee, maa nìn sòon̄ fám!>»
11Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «Kpāafì a-ŋalii, fáá a-taaŋi ní kí lì yii: <An bàn̄ an laŋki!>, ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin Isirayeel yab ŋée bàn̄ an laŋki. An kíǹ kujaau nì ŋkùm nì bìlbil kúm ń kpɔ̀ kí céetí-bi dee. 12Bìlbil kúm làá kpɔ̀ bin bínní ndandatee, kujaau làá kpɔ̀ bin bí ki pìl̄ee ní bin kíǹ ki bí dimaŋfalinee ń kpú ŋkùm. M làá yàntī m-ŋuul ń tɔ̄ di-tundi ní kí cáá kátí. 13Bi-nikpiliŋ làá dāá nīn dɔ̄ an kɔkɔ pu fìlfil bi-waaŋi kansikin ki māntìi tú bi-saraafaŋyi nì ajoon nì ŋgbantamu yilpu, nì isuboon nì iwaasufi taapu laakin bi nìn ŋáań saraabi ki tìì bi-waaŋee. Niinee, bi làá dāá béé yii man di sá bi-Dindaan. 14M làá dàkà-bi m-pɔŋŋu ní kí nàan̄ bi-tiŋki. M làá jà bin kóò ki-puee kí yòon̄ kuteeu ŋgiil pú kí cáá sāā Riibila tiŋki ŋgan pú. Bi làá dāá béé niin yii man di sá bi-Dindaan.»

english_text:
Disaster Is Near
1The Lord God said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Israel that I am saying:
Israel will soon come to an end! Your whole country is about to be destroyed 3as punishment for your disgusting sins. I, the Lord, am so angry 4that I will show no pity. I will punish you for the evil you've done, and you will know that I am the Lord.
5There's never been anything like the coming disaster. 6And when it comes, your life will be over. 7You people of Israel are doomed! Soon there will be panic on the mountaintops instead of celebration. 8I will let loose my anger and punish you for the evil things you've done. You'll get what you deserve. 9Your sins are so terrible, that you'll get no mercy from me. Then you will know that I, the Lord, have punished you.
10Disaster is near! Injustice and arrogance are everywhere, 11and violent criminals run free. None of you will survive the disaster, and everything you own and value will be shattered. 12The time is coming when everyone will be ruined. Buying and selling will stop, 13and people who sell property will never get it back, because all of you must be punished for your sins. And I won't change my mind!
14A signal has been blown on the trumpet, and weapons are prepared for battle. But no one goes to war, because in my anger I will strike down everyone in Israel.
Israel Is Surrounded
The Lord said to the people of Israel:
15War, disease, and starvation are everywhere! People who live in the countryside will be killed in battle, and those who live in towns will die from starvation or deadly diseases. 16Anyone who survives will escape into the hills, like doves who leave the valleys to find safety.
All of you will moan because of your sins. 17Your hands will tremble, and your knees go limp. 18You will put on sackcloth to show your sorrow, but terror will overpower you. Shame will be written all over your faces, and you will shave your heads in despair. 19Your silver and gold will be thrown into the streets like garbage, because those are the two things that led you into sin, and now they cannot save you from my anger. They are not even worth enough to buy food. 20You took great pride in using your beautiful jewelry to make disgusting idols of foreign gods. So I will make your jewelry worthless.
21Wicked foreigners will rob and disgrace you. 22They will break into my temple and leave it unfit as a place to worship me, but I will look away and let it happen.
23Your whole country is in confusion! Murder and violence are everywhere in Israel, 24so I will tell the most wicked nations to come and take over your homes. They will put an end to the pride you have in your strong army, and they will make your places of worship unfit to use. 25You will be terrified and will desperately look for peace—but there will be no peace. 26One tragedy will follow another, and you'll hear only bad news. People will beg prophets to give them a message from me. Priests will stop teaching my Law, and wise leaders won't be able to give advice. 27Even your king and his officials will lose hope and cry in despair. Your hands will tremble with fear.
I will punish you for your sins and treat you the same way you have treated others. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_text:
Nnaabu tóobiń
1Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii: 2«Nisaaleen, pīlifì tin man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti bíi sòoǹ nì Isirayeel yabee: An dóò! Nnaabu kpátì ki bàn̄ kitiŋ jannaatiliŋ. 3Kɔŋkɔnnee an dóò ni-pu: m làá yàntī m-ŋuul ń jēetí ni-pu. Ni-bimbim ní m làá dūú sòoǹ ni-bɔti ní kí pà-ni ni-timbiilituuŋŋi paati. 4M làá dàkà-ni nnimbinaakulim kaa làá sɔ̄ ni-saai báà fiii. M làá pà-ni ni-bimbim paati ní kí nyāntí ni-timbiilituuŋŋi kí páań mpaampiin pu. Niinee ni làá béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan.
5«Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀: Nnaabu dòoń, nnaabu ŋun baa láá pée kée dòoń! 6An dóò, an dóò ní, nnaabu bíi bɔ́ntí kí jēetí ni-pu, ŋu dòoń! 7Nimbi bin kóò kitiŋ nee puee, dinàandi dòoń ni-pu! Ŋyunti dòoń, ibɔsoon wiiŋŋu tóobiń. Dipɔɔbiildi làá fōō dipɔɔpindi paaŋŋu ajoon pu. 8An kaa ti làá tàan̄, kɔŋkɔnnee m làá kpáatí m-ŋuul kí sìtī ni-pu ní kí yàntī m-bum ń tɔ̄ mi-tundi kí cáá kátí. Ni-bimbim ní m làá dūú sòoǹ ni-bɔti ní kí pà-ni ni-timbiilituuŋŋi paati. 9M làá dàkà-ni nnimbinaakulim kaa làá sɔ̄ ni-saai. M làá pà ni-bimbim paati ní kí nyāntí ni-timbiilituuŋŋi kí páań mpaampiin pu. Ni làá dāá béé niinee yii man ni-Dindaan di bíi dátí ni-tafal.
10«Ibɔsoon wiiŋŋu sèé! Ŋu bāań ki dóò. Ipɔŋkpiti bí an kɔkɔ pu, dilambil yíkì tiŋan pu. 11Tipɔmbɔti bí kii ndɔ ní bi dūu cóoǹ kí ŋá ikpitee. Ni-wanti tiba kaa ti làá kíń ni-cee, ni-gaajati kaa làá kíńaaa, ni-wíiŋŋu kaa làá kíńaaa, ni-nyooti mun kaa làá tí kíń. 12Ŋyunti bāań ní nee, ibɔsoon wiiŋŋu tóobiń. Biwandaliibi ń taa nín̄ bíi fàal̀, biwannyafiliibi mun ń taa nín̄ bí kunimbaaun. Di sá yii m gíí samaa kɔkɔ pu diŋuul ní. 13Báà uwannyafil yaa ŋmátì kaa kpíìyaaa, waa ti làá ŋmā kí gítí kí yòon̄ u-wanti tin u nyáfée. Di sá yii dileedakal din sòoǹ án nín làá nàan̄ samaa kɔkɔ puee kaa làá gbíntí fám. Báà ŋma bí ikpitin, an pu ní báà ubɔ kaa làá ti ká mpɔn. 14Bi dāa ŋūǹ kí búń ŋyin kí bɔ́ntí kí cù kujaau, ama báà unibambaanti kaa làá cù. Di sá yii m gíí samaa kɔkɔ pu diŋuul ní.»
Ditafadaaldi dɔ̄ ki cí báà ŋma
15An làá nīn sá kujaau ní mmɔŋki, ní bìlbil kúm nì ŋkùm bí adiinni ki nà. Bin bí tisatinee làá kpú kujaaun, ní bin bí kitiŋinee, ŋkùm nì iween ń kpɔ̀-bi. 16Bin làá dāá kíń ki bí dimaŋfalinee làá dāá sāǹ kí cù ajoonni. Kii abeenanjil nín yáliŋkí puee, míǹ ní bi làá dāá yāliŋkì bi-kpitii pu.
17Bi-ŋalii kaa dāa gíti cáá mpɔn,
ní bi-tabiŋyiliŋ ń dāá yɔ̀tī.
18Bi làá dāá nīn lōō kpɔsatab,
ní bi-wunti ń dāá sāǹ yàrrr.
Icoo làá dāá cúú-bi ní gbòooo,
ní bí dāá kòol̀ ayibaakpan.
19Bi làá dāá dū bi-nimbiliŋ kí fá adan pu,
bi-sindaariyau làá dāá kpántí kii
titampummoolee ní kí tīī-bi.
Di sá yii ŋwiin ŋun ti-Dindaan làá dāá gíí diŋuulee,
bi-nimbiliŋ àá bi-sindaariyau kaa dāa ŋūǹ kí fīī-bi.
Baa làá dāá ká tijin kí jī,
ní bi-pooŋyi ń dāá dūú fáká.
Di sá yii animbil nì sindaariya di sá bi-yìntitam nyeel.
20Bi-gaajati nyaaŋku di nìn yòontí-bi
ní bi dūu mɔ́ɔ́ awaa ŋin sá
ntimbiil wanti nì titantaŋwanee.
An pu ní ti-Dindaan bí yii:
«M làá dū bi-gaajati gbanti
kí kpántí titampummool.
21M làá yàntī binicambi ń fūkul̀-tì,
ní bin kaa bí tibanee ń yòon̄-tì
kí cáá búntí kii kujaau poon ní bi kée.
Bi làá dāá kɔ́ǹ-tì tijɔkɔndi.
22Bi yaa láa bíi kɔ̄ntí m-Diiku kun sá
m-gaajawantee tijɔkɔndee,
maa làá pée ŋá tiba.
Digaŋgandambi làá dāá dāan̄ kí kɔ́ǹ-ku tijɔkɔndi.
23Mɔ́ɔ́ ikusaka,
di sá yii binikpɔliibi gbí kitiŋin,
ní tipɔmbɔti gbí Jeerusaleem tiŋkin.
24M làá cáań anibul ŋin cáá nnimbinaakulimee
ŋí dāan̄ kí fōō bi-diiŋŋi.
M làá kúntí bi-pɔndambi lambil,
ní kí bīil̀ bi-waatootipaaŋyi.
25Dinyoondi bí ki dòoń.
Bi làá dāá nyàab̀ ŋgbansɔŋfi
kaa làá dāá ká-ŋu.
26Inaabu làá dāá nīn dī tɔb,
ní atulim bɔti ń dāá nīn dòoń kaa gbèentí.
Binib làá dāá gbàam̀ Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu yii ú ká dileedakal.
Usaraaŋakpil kaa dāa gíti cáá tiba kí dàkà,
ní bitindaŋkpilib kaa dāa gíti cáá isaŋki kí tīī.
27Ubɔti làá dāá nīn kā dikpool,
dibɔtibil kaa dāa gíti cáá dimákal,
ní kitiŋee nib báà ŋma wunti dāa gbáà kpàkpakpa.
M làá dāá dū bi-bimbim ní kí sòoǹ bi-bɔti,
ní kí sòoǹ bi-bɔti kii an nín máaǹ puee.
Niinee bi làá dāá béé yii man di sá bi-Dindaan.»

english_text:
Ezekiel Sees the Terrible Sins of Jerusalem
1Six years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the leaders of Judah were meeting with me in my house. On the fifth day of the sixth month, the Lord God suddenly took control of me, 2 and I saw something in the shape of a human. This figure was like fire from the waist down, and it was bright as polished metal from the waist up. 3It reached out what seemed to be a hand and grabbed my hair. Then in my vision the Lord's Spirit lifted me into the sky and carried me to Jerusalem.
The Spirit took me to the north gate of the temple's inner courtyard, where there was an idol that disgusted the Lord and made him furious. 4 Then I saw the brightness of the glory of the God of Israel, just as I had seen it near the Chebar River.
5God said to me, “Ezekiel, son of man, look north.” And when I did, I saw that repulsive idol by the altar near the gate.
6God then said, “Do you see the terrible sins of the people of Israel? Their sins are making my holy temple unfit as a place to worship me. Yet you will see even worse things than this.”
7Next, I was taken to the entrance of the courtyard, where I saw a hole in the wall.
8God said, “Make this hole bigger.” And when I did, I realized it was a doorway. 9“Go in,” God said, “and see what horrible and evil things the people are doing.”
10Inside, I saw that the walls were covered with pictures of reptiles and disgusting, unclean animals, as well as with idols that the Israelites were worshiping. 11Seventy Israelite leaders were standing there, including Jaazaniah son of Shaphan. Each of these leaders was holding an incense burner, and the smell of incense filled the room.
12God said, “Ezekiel, do you see what horrible things Israel's leaders are doing in secret? They have filled their rooms with idols. And they say I can't see them, because they think I have already deserted Israel. 13But I will show you something even worse than this.”
14He took me to the north gate of the temple, where I saw women mourning for the god Tammuz. 15God asked me, “Can you believe what these women are doing? But now I want to show you something even worse.”
16I was then led into the temple's inner courtyard, where I saw about 25 men standing near the entrance, between the porch and the altar. Their backs were to the Lord's temple, and they were bowing down to the rising sun.
17God said, “Ezekiel, it's bad enough that the people of Judah are doing these disgusting things. But they have also spread violence and injustice everywhere in Israel and have made me very angry. They have disgraced and insulted me in the worst possible way. 18So in my fierce anger, I will punish them without mercy and refuse to help them when they cry out to me.”
translation_text:
Iwaatooti in bí kunimbɔtidiinee
1Bi nín cúú Isirayeel yab kuyuŋu ki cùnnì Babiloon abin aluu poon, iŋmal iluu wiŋŋmooŋmootiŋuee, m nìn kā m-dumpu ní Juuda yab tindaŋkpilib kā m-nimbiin. Dicilpu niinee ní ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti pɔŋŋu kpákatìń m-pu. 2M bí yii ḿ kpèèyee, tiwan tiba nìn bí ki náań nì unil. Kí yòon̄ tin bí ki náań nì u-caŋ yamee taapuee, an sá ŋŋmi ní. Kí yòon̄ u-caŋ gbanti kí nīn jɔ́ḿee, an bí kii ŋwalifee ní ki jìl̀ kii sindaariya un bi dūu ŋá ŋŋmin an mántèe. 3U nìn tāntì tiba bí kii ŋŋalee ní ki cúú m-yikpiti. Niinee, dileedakal din nìn nyánní Unimbɔti cee gbanti poonee, Ŋfam nìn yōoǹ-mi m kíǹ ki bí yilpu nì taapu kansikin ní ki cáá-mi ki cūnnì Jeerusaleem tiŋkin. M ká yii m bí kitiŋ punyɔkɔki kin bí ŋgan púee poon pú, laakin bi nìn dū diwaal din bí ki kùtī Unimbɔti poonee ki síiǹee. 4Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nìn tí nyántì u-nyooti ki dàkā-mi niin, kii m nín nìn ká dileedakal poon pu ditantakalinee. 5Unimbɔti bí-mi yii: «Nisaaleen, kpèè ŋgan pú.» Ní m wáaǹ ki kpēē. Kipunyɔkɔ kin bí ŋgan púee, nsaraafan ŋubɔ nìn bí niin. Diwaal din nìn bí ki kùtī Unimbɔti poonee nìn bí nsan ŋun cá nsaraafan gbanti ceeyee. 6Ní Unimbɔti bí-mi yii: «Nisaaleen, a wāĺ tin bi bíi ŋáańeeee? Isirayeel yab baasii dū bi-ba ki líiǹ ntimbiil tuuŋŋi kí jà-mi kí wàatī m-circir Kɔŋkooŋŋu ní. Ama a làá gíti ká ntimbiil tuuŋŋi aba mun.»
7Ŋfamee nìn yōoǹ-mi ki cūnnì dicindi punyɔkɔpu. M bí yii ḿ kpèèyee, dibundi diba bí digundin. 8Unimbɔti bí-mi yii: «Nisaaleen, lùkù kí cíĺ digundi.» Niinee ní m lùkū ki cíl̀ ní dibundi dōoǹ. 9Ní u bí-mi yii: «Kɔ́ kí kpèè ntimbiil nì titantan tuuŋŋi ŋin binib bí doo ki tūǹeee.» 10M nín kɔ́ee, kun m kée sɔ̀: m nín kpēē ki māntìi túee, m ká bi lēē ikoobu nì tiwaŋkuti tin cáá titantanee digundi kɔkɔ pu. Bi nìn lēē awaa ŋin kɔkɔ Isirayeel yab tòotēe di-pu. 11Isirayeel yab tindaŋkpilib imuŋku ita nì saalaa nìn yú awaayee nimbiin. Bi-kansikinee, Safan jipɔɔn Yasaniya nìn bí. Bi-kɔkɔ nìn ŋúb́ kisambiki kin poon bi tùutī talaalubee ní talaalu un bi tūūyee nyiim nìn jɔ́ḿ kutaa. 12Unimbɔti bālifì-mi yii: «Nisaaleen, a wāĺ kun dinibul nee tindaŋkpilib bíi ŋáań dibalineeee? Báà ŋma yú mpaan ŋun pu u-waal bée ní. Bi bí ki pɔ̀ bi-ba ki lì yii: <Ti-Dindaan kaa wāĺ-ti, u dū u-tiŋki ki fá.>» 13Ní Unimbɔti gíti bí-mi yii: «A làá gíti ká bi bíi ŋáań ntimbiil tuuŋŋi aba mun.»
14Niinee ní u yōoǹ-mi u-diiku punyɔkɔki kin bí ŋgan púee. Binimpoobi biba nìn kā niin ki sūǹ diwaal Tamuusi kpool. 15U bālifì-mi yii: «Nisaaleen, kéè a káa! A làá gíti ká ntimbiil tuuŋŋi aba mun.»
16Niinee ní u yōoǹ-mi ki cáa cūnnì kunimbɔtidii cindi poon yal. Kí kɔ́ kudiin, kasarka nì nsaraafan kansikinee, bininjab mmuŋku nì biŋmoo nìn bí. Bi nìn fātì bi-boon ki tīī kunimbɔtidii ní bi-nimbiiŋyi túĺ ŋwìiń nyalaŋki. Bi nìn bí ki gbàantí ki jáaḿ ŋwìiń. 17Niinee ní Unimbɔti bālifì-mi yii: «Nisaaleen, kéè a káa! An kaa sá ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin Juuda yab bí doo ki ŋáań nee ŋmaniŋma ní bi ŋáań, ama bi gíti bí ní ki ŋáań tipɔmbɔti ki gbítí m-ŋuul. Kɔŋkɔnnee, bíǹ di bátì kisupaŋŋi ki cáa cáǹ bi-maŋfal watil púee. 18An puee, ma mun làá tɔ̄ m-tundi nì m-ŋuul poon. M làá dàkà-bi nnimbinaakulim kaa làá fīī-bi. Bi làá dāá kúuǹ mpɔn kí yíiń-mi, ama maa làá pīlifiǹ-bi.»

english_text:
The Lord Gives the Command To Punish Jerusalem
1After that, I heard the Lord shout, “Come to Jerusalem, you men chosen to destroy the city. And bring your weapons!”
2I saw six men come through the north gate of the temple, each one holding a deadly weapon. A seventh man dressed in a linen robe was with them, and he was carrying things to write with. The men went into the temple and stood by the bronze altar.
3The brightness of God's glory then left its place above the statues of the winged creatures inside the temple and moved to the entrance. The Lord said to the man in the linen robe, 4 “Walk through the city of Jerusalem and mark the forehead of anyone who is truly upset and sad about the terrible things that are being done here.”
5-6He turned to the other six men and said, “Follow him and put to death everyone who doesn't have a mark on their forehead. Show no mercy or pity! Kill men and women, parents and children. Begin here at my temple, but be sure not to harm those who are marked.”
The men immediately killed the leaders who were standing there.
7Then the Lord said, “Pollute the temple by piling the dead bodies in the courtyards. Now get busy!” They left and started killing the people of Jerusalem.
8I was then alone, so I bowed down and cried out to the Lord, “Why are you doing this? Are you so angry with the people of Jerusalem that everyone must die?”
9The Lord answered, “The people of Israel and Judah have done horrible things. Their country is filled with murderers, and Jerusalem itself is filled with violence. They think that I have deserted them, and that I can't see what they are doing. 10And so I will not have pity on them or forgive them. They will be punished for what they have done.”
11Just then, the man in the linen robe returned and said, “I have done what you commanded.”
translation_text:
Unimbɔti làá jáǹ Jeerusaleem
1Míǹ boonee, m gbìl̄ ti-Dindaan yíiń mpɔn yii: «Nimbi bin di làá jáǹ Jeerusaleem tiŋkee, ní dāam̄maan! Báà ŋma ń nīn ŋúb́ u-janjawanti u-ŋaan kí dāá nàan̄-kì.» 2Niinee m ká bininjab biluu nyánní kunimbɔtidii punyɔkɔki yilpu pú yaka ki ŋúb́ bi-janjawanti. Uninja ubɔ nìn yú bi-kansikin ki pēē ŋŋaapiin bɔkutil ki gbìn̄ kun pu u làá ŋmèe u-caŋ. Bi táá dicilpu ki dɔ́miń ní ki yúl̀ ki kɔ́ĺ tasa kúti saraafaŋŋu. 3Ní Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nyooti yíkìi dāntì keerubimbi bin pu tì nìn bée ki nín cá kunimbɔtidii punyɔkɔpu. Ní ti-Dindaan yíiń uninja un pēē ŋŋaapiin bɔkutil, ki gbìn̄ tipilindi tin pu u làá ŋmèe u-caŋ, 4ní ki bí-u yii: «Yìiǹ Jeerusaleem tiŋki kɔkɔn. Un kamaa bíi yáliŋkí an páb́-u bi nín bíi tūǹ ntimbiil tuuŋŋee puee, á dáań udaan yigbeel.» 5Míǹ boonee, m gbìl̄ u tùkū bin kíǹee yii: «Ní páań uninja nee boon kí kpɔ̀ bin kóò kitiŋ nee puee. Ní ŋá nnimbinaakulim, kí taa kíń báà ubɔ. 6Ní kpɔ̀ kí céetí bitikpilib kí kpáaǹ nnaacimpɔmbiyaamu nì nsapɔmbiyaamu nì mbiyaamu nì binimpoobi. Ama ní taa gbēē bin cáá kudaaŋŋu bi-yigbeel puee. Ní kíĺ m-Diikun doo.» Niinee ní bi kíĺ ki bíi kù bitindaŋkpilib bin nìn bí kunimbɔtidii nyɔkɔpuee. 7Ti-Dindaan nìn bí-bi yii: «Dūmaan anikpil kí gbéeǹ kunimbɔtidii cindi kí kɔ́ǹ-ku tijɔkɔndi. Nín̄ cámaan!» Ní bi nyáń kunimbɔtidiin ki cūtìi pɔ̄fì binib kitiŋin.
8Bi nín bíi kù binib mimmee, m kíǹ m-baba niin ní m tātìi gbāaǹ kitiŋ m-yigbeel tūū kitiŋ ki téeń yii: «Abàa, ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti, a nín kpáatì a-ŋuul ki sītì Jeerusaleem pu minee, a làá kpɔ̀ kí céetí Isirayeel yab bin kíǹee níii?» 9Ní u kíí-mi yii: «Isirayeel yab nì Juuda yab nín ŋá ikpiti iŋyee wīikí tikpil. Bi yāntì nnikpaakoon gbí kitiŋ kɔkɔ pu ní Jeerusaleem tiŋki gbí ikpiti. Binib bí ki lì yii: <Ti-Dindaan dū kitiŋ nee ki fá ní kaa wāĺ-ti.> 10An puee m làá dàkà-bi nnimbinaakulim kaa làá sɔ̄ bi-saai. M làá yàntī kun bi ŋée ń fàtīí lítí bi-yil pu.» 11Ŋyunti gbantee, uninja un bàà pēē ŋŋaapiin bɔkutil ki gbìn̄ tipilindi tin pu bi ŋmèe dɔ́miń ki sòon̄ u nín túń ditundi an cōom̀ puee, yii: «A nín bí yii ḿ ŋá puee, m ŋá míǹ.»

english_text:
The Lord's Glory Leaves the Temple
1 I saw the dome that was above the four winged creatures, and on it was the sapphire throne. 2 The Lord said to the man in the linen robe, “Walk among the four wheels beside the creatures and pick up as many hot coals as you can carry. Then scatter them over the city of Jerusalem.” I watched him as he followed the Lord's instructions.
3The winged creatures were standing south of the temple when the man walked among them. A cloud filled the inner courtyard, 4and the brightness of the Lord's glory moved from above the creatures and stopped at the entrance of the temple. The entire temple was filled with his glory, and the courtyard was dazzling bright. 5The sound of the creatures' wings was as loud as the voice of God All-Powerful and could even be heard in the outer courtyard.
6The man in the robe was now standing beside a wheel. 7One of the four creatures reached its hand into the fire among them and gave him some of the hot coals. The man took the coals and left.
8I noticed again that each of the four winged creatures had what looked like human hands under their wings, 9 and I saw the four wheels near the creatures. These wheels were shining like chrysolite. 10Each wheel was exactly the same and had a second wheel that cut through the middle of it, 11so that they could move in any direction without turning. The wheels moved together whenever the creatures moved. 12 I also noticed that the wheels and the creatures' bodies, including their backs, their hands, and their wings, were covered with eyes. 13And I heard a voice calling these “the wheels that spin.”
14 Each of the winged creatures had four faces: the face of a bull, the face of a human, the face of a lion, and the face of an eagle. 15-17These were the same creatures I had seen near the Chebar River. They controlled when and where the wheels moved—the wheels went wherever the creatures went and stopped whenever they stopped. Even when the creatures flew in the air, the wheels stayed beside them.
18Then I watched the brightness of the Lord's glory move from the entrance of the temple and stop above the winged creatures. 19They spread their wings and flew into the air with the wheels at their side. They stopped at the east gate of the temple, and the Lord's glory was above them.
20I knew for sure that these were the same creatures I had seen beneath the Lord's glory near the Chebar River. 21-22They had four wings with hands beneath them, and they had the same four faces as those near the River. Each creature moved straight ahead without turning.
translation_text:
Unimbɔti tí lēē u-ba ki dàkā Eeseekiyeel
(Kpèè 1.1-28)
1M bí yii ḿ kpèèyee, kugbɔŋu kubɔ bí keerubimbi yilpu. Kugbɔŋuee puee, Safiir taŋkpal bí ki náań nì dibeejal. 2Unimbɔti bí unil un pēē dibɔkutipindee yii: «Kɔ́ ataa ŋin bí keerubimbi taapuee. Yáfí amɔsiŋkoon ŋin bí keerubimbi kansikinee kí gbéeǹ a-ŋaan kí cáá cùnnì kí yàaǹ kitiŋee pu.» M-nimbilaaliyin ní uninjee nín cá. 3Ŋyunti ŋun u nín cée, keerubimbee nìn bí kunimbɔtidii ŋŋaŋgiil pú ní ditagbandi diba gbí dicindi poon pú yalin. 4Niinee ti-Dindaan nyooti yíkì ki dāntì keerubimbee yilpu ki nín cá kunimbɔtidii punyɔkɔpu. Ditagbandee nìn gbí kunimbɔtidii ní ti-Dindaan nyooti nìn ŋmíntí dicindi kɔkɔ. 5A yaa nìn bí dicindi boon púee, a nìn gbìl̀ keerubimbi feeŋyi nín nìn ŋáań kuwoou kuŋyee pu. An nìn bí kii Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan yaa bíi sòoǹ u-neel nín bí puee ní. 6Uninja un nìn pēē ŋŋaapiin bɔkutilee nìn yú ki kɔ́ĺ ditaal diba. Ŋyunti ŋun Unimbɔti nìn tīī-u mara yii ú lēē ŋŋmi ŋun bí ataayee kansikin keerubimbee kansikinee ní u cūtìi yúl̀ ki kɔ́ĺ ditaal gbanti. 7Keerubimbee kansikinee, unil ubɔ nìn tāntì u-ŋal ki túĺ ŋŋmi ŋun bí bi-kansikinee. U lēē amɔsiŋkoon ki gbéeǹ uninjee ŋaaŋyi ní úǹ cáa búntì.
8Niinee tiba nyáń keerubimbee feeŋyi taapu ki náań nì nniŋal. 9M gíti bí yii ḿ kpèèyee, ataa anaa dee, ditaal diba bí ki kɔ́ĺ keerubimbee ubɔ. Ataayee nìn jìl̀ kii ditaŋkpamɔntiil din bi yíì Kriistooliitee ní. 10Ataayee nìn náań ní ki bí kii ŋi kɔ́ tɔbinee. 11Ŋi nìn ŋūǹ kí cù ajannaatil pú kaa māntì. Keerubimbee yaa fātì bi-nimbiiŋyi ki túĺ laakiŋyee, niin ní ŋi cá kaa fàtī ŋi-ba. 12Keerubimbee wunti kɔkɔ nì bi-boon nì bi-ŋalii nì bi-feeŋyi nìn sá animbil ŋma ní ki jìl̀, míǹ mbaantiim ní ataayee mun nìn bí. 13M nìn gbìl̄ bi yíiń ataayee yii «kunaakpaabuŋŋu.» 14Keerubim kamaa nìn cáá inimbiin inaa: Mpeekaa nìn sá Keerubim nimbiin, ní nliliiti sá unil nimbiin, ní ntataati sá gbikinti nimbiin ní nnanaati sá ukaalun nimbiin. 15Keerubimbee nìn ŋūǹ kí yīkì kí dàntī kutaa. Bi náań nì tiwan tin cáá kufoou m nìn ká Keebaar mɔɔgbandee ní. 16Bi yaa nìn còom̄ ki cée, ataayee nìn táá-bi ní ki còom̄ ki cá. Bi yaa nìn kpátì bi-feeŋyi kí yīkì kí ŋàaǹee, ataayee nìn táá-bi ní. 17Bi yaa nìn yúl̀ee, ataayee mun nìn yūlifí ní. Bi yaa nìn yíkì ki dāntèe, ŋi mun nìn yíkí kí dàntī ní, di sá yii tiwan tin cáá kufoouee di nìn kpāantí-ŋi ki còom̄.
Ti-Dindaan yíkì kunimbɔtidiin
18Ti-Dindaan nyooti nìn yíkì kunimbɔtidii punyɔkɔpu ní ki cūtì ki kíǹ ki bí keerubimbi pu. 19Niinee keerubimbi kpátì bi-feeŋyi ní m ká bi yíkì kitiŋ, bi nì ataayee dicilpu ki nín cá. Bi cūtìi yúl̀ ki kɔ́ĺ kunimbɔtidii punyɔkɔki kin bí ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee. Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nyooti nìn bí bi-pu ki jìl̀. 20Keebaar mɔɔgbaŋŋi puee, m nìn ká tiwannáaŋkaal tibaantiil gbanti yú Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu taapu. Niinee ní m béè yii an sá keerubimbi. 21Bi-kɔkɔ nìn cáá inimbiin inaa ní ki cáá ifeen inaa ní ki cáá iŋal, iba náań nì unil ŋalii ki bí bi-feeŋyi taapu. 22Bi-nimbiiŋyi nìn náań nì bin m bàà ká Keebaar mɔɔl caŋinee. Keerubimbee nìn còom̄ ní ki túĺ bi-nimbiin cáaa.

english_text:
Ezekiel Condemns Jerusalem's Wicked Leaders
1The Lord's Spirit lifted me up and took me to the east gate of the temple, where I saw 25 men, including the two leaders, Jaazaniah son of Azzur and Pelatiah son of Benaiah. 2The Lord said, “Ezekiel, son of man, these men are making evil plans and giving dangerous advice to the people of Jerusalem. 3They say things like, ‘Let's build more houses. This city is like a cooking pot over a fire, and we are the meat, but at least the pot keeps us from being burned in the fire.’ 4So, Ezekiel, condemn them!”
5The Lord's Spirit took control of me and told me to tell these leaders:
I, the Lord God, know what you leaders are saying. 6You have murdered so many people that the city is filled with dead bodies! 7This city is indeed a cooking pot, but the bodies of those you killed are the meat. And so I will force you to leave Jerusalem, 8and I'll send armies to attack you, just as you fear. 9Then you will be captured and punished by foreign enemies. 10You will be killed in your own country, but not before you realize that I, the Lord, have done these things.
11You leaders claim to be meat in a cooking pot, but you won't be protected by this city. No, you will die at the border of Israel. 12You will realize that while you were following the laws of nearby nations, you were disobeying my laws and teachings. And I am the Lord!
13Before I finished speaking, Pelatiah dropped dead. I bowed down and cried out, “Please, Lord God, don't kill everyone left in Israel.”
A Promise of Hope
14The Lord replied:
15Ezekiel, son of man, the people living in Jerusalem claim that you and the other Israelites who were taken to Babylonia are too far away to worship me. They also claim that the land of Israel now belongs only to them. 16But here is what I want you to tell the Israelites in Babylonia:
It's true that I, the Lord God, have forced you out of your own country and made you live among foreign nations. But for now, I will be with you wherever you are, so that you can worship me. 17And someday, I will gather you from the nations where you are scattered and let you live in Israel again. 18When that happens, I want you to clear the land of all those idols I hate so much. 19 Then I will take away your stubbornness and make you eager to be completely faithful to me. You will want to obey me 20and all my laws and teachings. You will be my people, and I will be your God. 21But those who worship idols will be punished and get what they deserve. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
The Lord's Glory Leaves Jerusalem
22 After the Lord had finished speaking, the winged creatures spread their wings and flew into the air, and the wheels were beside them. The brightness of the Lord's glory above them 23left Jerusalem and stopped at a hill east of the city.
24Then in my vision, the Lord's Spirit lifted me up and carried me back to the other exiles in Babylonia. The vision faded away, 25and I told them everything the Lord had shown me.
translation_text:
Bi làá sòoǹ Jeerusaleem bɔti ki-kpitii pu
1Ti-Dindaan Fam yōoǹ-mi kitiŋ ní ki cáá-mi ki cūnnì kunimbɔtidii punyɔkɔki kin bí ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee. Kipunyɔkɔ gbanti caŋinee, m nìn ká bininjab mmuŋku nì biŋmoo ní ki béè bi-kansikin bitindaŋkpilib bili, Asuur jipɔɔn Yasaniya nì Beenaya jipɔɔn Peelatiya. 2Ŋfamee nìn tùkū-mi yii: «Nisaaleen, kpèè binib bin di bɔ́ntí atuŋkpiti ki tìì isaŋkikpiti kitiŋ nee poonee sɔ̀. 3Bi bí ki lì yii: <Kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋubɔ poonee, baa ti làá mā adiin doo! Kitiŋ nee sá kii daanseeyee ní, ní timbi sá kii tinan tin bi làá dūú tɔ́kɔń u-poonee.> 4An puee nisaaleen, nàatī Unimbɔti bɔti kí tɔ̄ bi-pu, sòoǹ kí tɔ̄ bi-pu!»
5Niinee ní ti-Dindaan Fam kpákatìń m-pu ní ki kpáafì-mi ḿ sòoǹ yii: «Lì yii ti-Dindaan nín bí puee sɔ̀. Ni nín sòoǹ puee dee, Isirayeel yab! M nyí ni-landɔkɔi kɔkɔ. 6Ni kūū binib tikpil kitiŋ nee poon. Ni yāntì anikpil dɔ̄ ki-saŋkakpiliŋ fìlfil. 7An pu ní ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti sòon̄ yii: Kitiŋ nee sá kii daanseeyee ní, ama bin ni kūū kitiŋ nee poonee di sá tinan. Ama nimbee, m làá jà-ni kí nyāntí kitiŋ nee poon. 8Ni fàŋkí kujaauaa! Too m làá cáań kujaau kí tɔ̄ ni-pu, man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ. 9M làá jà-ni kí nyāntí kitiŋ nee poon, m làá dū-ni kí ŋá binicambi ŋaan. Bíǹ pu ní m làá dī kí sòoǹ ni-bɔti. 10M làá yàntī ní kpú kujaaun ní kí sòoǹ ni-bɔti Isirayeel tiŋkin táb. Niinee ní ni làá béé yii m sá ni-Dindaan. 11Kitiŋ nee kaa ti làá nīn sá kii daanseeyee ní nimbi mun kaa ti làá nīn sá tinan kin kā u-poon. Isirayeel tiŋki poon ní m làá sòoǹ ni-bɔti. 12Niinee ni làá béé yii m sá ni-Dindaan. Naa nóó m-marab kaa tí ŋúb́ m-koobiliŋ mun. Ama ni nóó atimbun ŋin māntìi tú-nee koobiliŋ ní.»
13Ŋyunti ŋun m bíi nàatī Unimbɔti bɔtee ní Peelatiya jipɔɔn Beenaya kpíì. Niinee ní m tātìi gbāaǹ m-yigbeel tūū kitiŋ ní ki téeń mpɔn yii: «Áù, ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti, a làá kpɔ̀ kí céetí Isirayeel yab bin kíǹee níii?»
Unimbɔti làá kóoǹ u-nibul din yàl̄ee kí kpāfì
14Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi tibɔti nee yii: 15«Nisaaleen, a-nabiyaamu dee, a-nabiyaamu mun a nì bi pēē mmaalee, Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ, bin ní bin kóò Jeerusaleemee lì yii: <Ní taa sútí kí pìl̄ ti-Dindaan, di sá yii timbi ní u dū kitiŋ nee ki tīī tí nīn yì.> 16An puee á tùkù-bi ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee yii: <M dū-ni ki tɔ́ atimbun ŋin dátèe poon, ní ki yāntì ni yàl̄ ki bí nnicantimun, ama niin muee, m bí ni-kansikin kii m nín bí circir kɔŋkooŋŋun puee>. 17An puee, á tùkù-bi yii tin man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti bíi sòoǹ nì bee sèé: <M làá nyāntí-ni anibul kansikin kí kóoǹ-ni kí kpāfì. M làá cáań-ni ntimu mun poon ni yàl̄ee kí kpāfì ní kí dū Isirayeel tiŋki kí tīī-ni. 18Niin ní ni làá nyānní ní kí kúntí ntimbiil tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ nì ajɔkɔntuun kɔkɔ. 19M làá tīī ni-kɔkɔ dipɔbil diba ní kí tīī-ni ŋfampɔm. M làá lēē ni-wuntin dipɔbil din pɔ̄ɔ̄ kii ditaŋkpalee ní kí tīī-ni dipɔbil din pɔ̀fèe. 20Án nín làá ŋá pu ní nóó m-bɔkpaaŋi kí nīn ŋúb́ m-koobiliŋ kí ŋá kii ŋi nín bí yii ní ŋá puee. Ni làá nīn sá m-nibul ní man ń nīn sá ni-Nimbɔtiu. 21Ama bin pɔbiliŋ fáatiǹ bi-timbiilituuŋŋi nì bi-jɔkɔntuuŋŋee, m làá yàntī bi-tuuŋŋi ń gítí bíǹ bi-ba pu.> Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di lī míǹ.»
Unimbɔti nyooti yíkì Jeerusaleem
22Niinee keerubimbee kpátì bi-feeŋyi ki kpáaǹ ataayee ní Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nyooti nìn bí bi-pu ki ŋmíntí. 23Ti-Dindaan nyooti nìn yíkì kitiŋ kansikin ní ki cūtìi yúl̀ dijool din bí kitiŋ ŋgan púee. 24Ŋfam nìn yōoǹ-mi ki cáa cūnnì Babiloon, bin bi cúú kuyuŋuee cee. Unimbɔti Fam di nìn lēē ki dàkā-mi. Dileedakal din m nìn ká gbantee nìn wáŋkì. 25M nìn tùkū bin bi cúú kuyuŋuee tin ti-Dindaan lēē ki dàkā-mee.

english_text:
Ezekiel Acts Out Israel's Captivity
1The Lord said:
2 Ezekiel, son of man, you are living among rebellious people. They have eyes, but refuse to see; they have ears, but refuse to listen. 3So before it gets dark, here is what I want you to do. Pack a few things as though you were going to be taken away as a prisoner. Then go outside where everyone can see you and walk around from place to place. Maybe as they watch, they will realize what rebels they are. 4After you have done this, return to your house.
Later that evening leave your house as if you were going into exile. 5Dig through the wall of your house and crawl out, carrying the bag with you. Make sure everyone is watching. 6Lift the bag to your shoulders, and with your face covered, take it into the darkness, so that you cannot see the land you are leaving. All this will be a warning for the people of Israel.
7I did everything the Lord had said. I packed a few things. Then as the sun was going down, and while everyone was watching, I dug a hole through one of the walls of my house. I pulled out my bag, then lifted it to my shoulders and left in the darkness.
8The next morning, the Lord 9reminded me that those rebellious people didn't even ask what I was doing. 10So he sent me back to tell them:
The Lord God has a message for the leader of Jerusalem and everyone living there!
11I have done these things to show them what will happen when they are taken away as prisoners.
12The leader of Jerusalem will lift his own bag to his shoulders at sunset and leave through a hole that the others have dug in the wall of his house. He will cover his face, so he can't see the land he is leaving. 13 The Lord will spread out a net and trap him as he leaves Jerusalem. He will then be led away to the city of Babylon, but will never see that place, even though he will die there. 14His own officials and troops will scatter in every direction, and the Lord will track them down and put them to death.
15The Lord will force the rest of the people in Jerusalem to live in foreign nations, where they will realize that he has done all these things. 16Some of them will survive the war, the starvation, and the deadly diseases. That way, they will be able to tell foreigners how disgusting their sins were, and that it was the Lord who punished them in this way.
A Sign of Fear
17The Lord said:
18Ezekiel, son of man, shake with fear when you eat, and tremble when you drink. 19Tell the people of Israel that I, the Lord, say that someday everyone in Jerusalem will shake when they eat and tremble when they drink. Their country will be destroyed and left empty, because they have been cruel and violent. 20Every town will lie in ruins, and the land will be a barren desert. Then they will know that I am the Lord.
The Words of the Lord Will Come True
21The Lord said:
22Ezekiel, son of man, you've heard people in Israel use the saying, “Time passes, and prophets are proved wrong.” 23Now tell the people that I, the Lord, am going to prove that saying wrong. No one will ever be able to use it again in Israel, because very soon everything I have said will come true! 24The people will hear no more useless warnings and false messages. 25I will give them my message, and what I say will certainly happen. Warn those rebels that the time has come for them to be punished. I, the Lord, make this promise.
26-27Ezekiel, the people of Israel are also saying that your visions and messages are only about things in the future. 28So tell them that my words will soon come true, just as I have warned. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
Eeseekiyeel tīī bin bi làá cúú kuyuŋuee kudaaŋŋu
1Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii: 2«Nisaaleen, a kóò pɔɔgaatib kansikin ní. Bi cáá animbil ní kaa wāĺ, ní ki cáá atafal kaa gbìl̀. Di sá yii bi sá pɔɔgaatib ní. 3Sii, nisaaleen, bɔ́ntí a-tɔkɔl kii a cá kuyuŋuee ní kí búntí kuyuŋu ŋwiimpu bi-nimbilaaliyin! Yīkì laakin a bée kí nīn cá laaba kuyuŋu bi-nimbilin. An yaa yíì bi làá gbìl̄ taapu yii bi sá pɔɔgaatib. 4Nyāntí a-tɔkɔl din a bɔ́ntì ki cáa cá kuyuŋuee mmɔŋki ŋwiimpu báà ŋma ń wāl̀. Kujoou yaa jóotèe, á nyā kii bin bi cúú kuyuŋuee nín nyēē puee bi-nimbilaaliyin. 5Á lùkù kí cíĺ digundi din bi máń ki tú kitiŋee bi-nimbilaaliyin ní kí dī niin kí nyā. 6Á yòon̄ ditɔkɔl kí páań a-gbigbipeeu pu bí nīn wāĺ-si ní á nyāntí-dì dibɔmbɔndin. Á dū tiwan kí bìin̄ a-nimbiin kí taa kpèè kitiŋ nee. Di sá yii a làá nīn sá kii kudaaŋŋuee ní ki tīī Isirayeel yab.» 7Niinee ní m ŋá kii ti-Dindaan nín kpáafì-mi puee. M nyántì ditɔkɔl din m bɔ́ntì kii uyumbu tɔkɔlee ŋwiimpu. Kujoouee ní m dū m-ŋal ki lùkū ki cíl̀ digundi din bi máń ki tú kitiŋee ní ki nyántì ditɔkɔl dibɔmbɔndi poon ní ki yōoǹ ki páaǹ m-gbigbipeeu pu bi-nimbilaaliyin niin.
8Kutaa wúntì kutaafaauee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii: 9«Nisaaleen, mimmee Isirayeel yab pɔɔgaatib nee kaa bālifì-si yii ba ní a ŋáańaaa? 10Tùkù-bi yii: <Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Tibɔti nee sá ki tīī dibɔtibil din bí Jeerusaleemee nì Isirayeel yab bin kɔkɔ bí ki kóò kitiŋ nee poonee ní.> 11Tùkù-bi yii a ŋá míǹ kí tīī kudaaŋŋu ní. Kun a ŋá nee, kun làá bàń bi-puee dee, di sá yii bi làá cúú-bi kí cùnnì kuyuŋu. 12Dibɔtibil din bí bi-kansikinee làá dāá yòon̄ u-wanti kí páań u-gbigbipeeu pu ní kí nyā dibɔmbɔndin. Bi làá dāá sāā kí cíĺ digundi ní ú dī niin kí nyā. U làá dāá dū tiwan kí bìin̄ u-nimbiin án nín làá ŋá pu ú taa ti ká kitiŋ nee nì u-nimbiliŋee. 13M làá dāá dū m-laaŋku kí tɔ̄ u-pu ní m-taliŋku ń sàl̄-u. M làá cùnnì-u Babiloon, Kaldee yab tiŋkin. Ama waa làá ká kitiŋ gbanti ní kí kpú. 14M làá yàaǹ bin kɔkɔ māntìi tú-uee nì u-tɔntɔnliibi nì u-janjaliibi ijaan kɔkɔ pu. Míǹ boonee ní ḿ dū kitàataajiki kí jà-bi. 15Bi làá dāá béé yii m sá bi-Dindaan, ŋyunti ŋun m yaa láa jìn̄-bi ki yàl̄ atimbun kɔkɔn nì ntimu kupaau poonee. 16Ama m làá dāá kíń bi-kansikin binikaaŋkaabi bin làá dāá ŋmátí kí nyā kujaaun nì ŋkùmin nì bìlbil kúminee. Bíǹ làá dāá māafì ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin kɔkɔ bi ŋée. Ŋyunti gbantee, bin kóò niinee làá dāá béé yii man di sá bi-Dindaan.»
17Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii: 18«Nisaaleen, a làá dāá jī a-jinti ní a-wunti jìkì, ní kí nyɔ̀ a-nyim nì dipɔɔbiildi nì inimɔɔn poon. 19Á dāá tùkù kitiŋ nee nib yii: Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ nì bin kóò Jeerusaleem ki bí Isirayeel tiŋkinee pu puee sɔ̀. Bi làá dāá jī bi-jinti inimɔɔn poon ní kí nyɔ̀ bi-nyim dipɔɔbiildi poon. Di sá yii bi làá dāá nàan̄ bi-tiŋki. Tiba nì tiba kaa làá dāá gíti kíń doo, di sá yii bin kóò kitiŋ nee dū tipɔmbɔti ki gbéeǹ-kì. 20Ntimu mun poon binib nìn kóòyee làá kpántí adigbuŋkati ŋma, ní kitiŋ nee ń kpántí kuteeu. Niinee ni làá dāá béé yii m sá ni-Dindaan.»
Ti-Dindaan nín lī puee, án làá ŋá míǹ
21Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii: 22«Nisaaleen, ba pu ní ni gà Isirayeel tiŋki dilaŋkpandi nee yii: <Iwiin fɔ̀kɔntí ki cá, ama ní an kaa ŋáań kii an nín lēē ki dàkā puee ní>? 23Too tùkù-bi yii ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M làá kúntí dilaŋkpandi gbanti. Baa làá ti gāā dilaŋkpandi gbanti Isirayeel tiŋkin. Ama á tùkù-bi yii: <Iwiin tóobiń, míǹ ní an nín lēē ki dàkā puee kɔkɔ làá ŋá.> 24Di sá yii nnyimɔn leedakaŋ kaa ti làá nīn bí, ní ubɔ mun kaa làá ti sòoǹ kí mɔ̄ntì yii tiba làá ŋá Isirayeel yab kansikin. 25Di sá yii m sá ni-Dindaan ní. M sòoǹ tin m cáá kí sòoǹee, ní án lafun làá ŋá míǹ kaa làá tàan̄. Tiŋman pɔɔgaatib, ni-yuntii nee poon ní m làá sòoǹ ní kí ŋá m nín sòon̄ puee. Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ.»
26Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii: 27«Nisaaleen, Isirayeel yab nín bí ki sòoǹ tiŋyee sèé: <Kijapaai nee leedakaŋ sá iwiin iba poon bɔti ní. U bíi sòoǹ ki nàatī iwiin in dátèe poon bɔti ní.> 28An pu ní an sá á tùkù-bi yii ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Tin m sòon̄ee, m làá yàntī án ŋá míǹ kaa làá tàan̄.> Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄.»

english_text:
Lying Prophets
1The Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the prophets of Israel who say they speak in my name, but who preach messages that come from their own imagination. Tell them it's time to hear my message.
3I, the Lord God, say those lying prophets are doomed! They don't see visions—they make up their own messages! 4Israel's prophets are no better than jackals that hunt for food among the ruins of a city. 5They don't warn the people about coming trouble or tell them how dangerous it is to sin against me. 6Those prophets lie by claiming they speak for me, but I have not even chosen them to be my prophets. And they still think their words will come true. 7They say they're preaching my messages, but they are full of lies—I did not speak to them!
8So I am going to punish those lying prophets for deceiving the people of Israel with false messages. 9I will turn against them and no longer let them belong to my people. They will not be allowed to call themselves Israelites or even to set foot in Israel. Then they will realize that I am the Lord God.
10 Those prophets refuse to be honest. They tell my people there will be peace, even though there's no peace to be found. They are like workers who think they can fix a shaky wall by covering it with paint. 11But when I send rainstorms, hailstones, and strong winds, the wall will surely collapse. 12People will then ask the workers why the paint didn't hold it up.
13That wall is the city of Jerusalem. And I, the Lord God, am so angry that I will send strong winds, rainstorms, and hailstones to destroy it. 14The lying prophets have tried to cover up the evil in Jerusalem, but I will tear down the city, all the way to its foundations. And when it collapses, those prophets will be killed, and everyone will know that I have done these things.
15The city of Jerusalem and its lying prophets will feel my fierce anger. Then I will announce that the city has fallen and that the lying prophets are dead, 16because they promised my people peace, when there was no peace. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
Women Who Wear Magic Charms
The Lord said:
17Ezekiel, son of man, now condemn the women of Israel who preach messages that come from their own imagination. 18Tell them they're doomed! They wear magic charms on their wrists and scarves on their heads, then trick others into believing they can predict the future. They won't get away with telling those lies. 19They charge my people a few handfuls of barley and a couple pieces of bread, and then give messages that are insulting to me. They use lies to sentence the innocent to death and to help the guilty go free. And my people believe them!
20I hate the magic charms they use to trick people into believing their lies. I will rip those charms from their wrists and set free the people they have trapped like birds. 21I will tear the scarves from their heads and rescue my people from their power once and for all. Then they will know that I am the Lord God.
22They do things I would never do. They lie to good people and encourage them to do wrong, and they convince the wicked to ruin their own lives by not turning from sin. 23I will no longer let these women give false messages and use magic, and I will free my people from their control. Then they will know that I, the Lord, have done these things.
translation_text:
Inyimɔn bɔnaatiliibi
1Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii: 2«Sii nisaaleen, fōō m-bɔti kí nàatī bin yíì bi-ba yii bi sá Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi Isirayeel tiŋkin ní ki nàatī tin bíǹ bi-ba lèe. Tùkù-bi yii bí pīlifì m-nyɔɔbundi. 3Mama ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti bíi lì yii nnaabu làá jēetí bibɔnaatiliibi bin kaa nyí tiba gbantee pu! Bi nóó tin bíǹ bi-ba bɔ́ntì kí sòoǹee ní ki nāantí bíǹ bi-ba leedakaŋ. 4Isirayeel yab, ni-bɔnaatiliibi bí kii ŋŋɔkɔmu mun tú ki yìiǹ adigbunnee ní. 5Baa jɔ́m̀ ki ŋéeb́ abun ŋin bí digundi puee, kaa tí máń digundi din làá wúń ni-pu ní ŋmā kí já kujaau ti-Dindaan wiiŋŋu dalee. 6Bi cáá inyimɔn leedakaŋ ní tin bi sòoǹ yii án làá dāan̄ee kaa sá ibaamɔn. Bi lì yii: <Ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé>, ama ní man ni-Dindaan kaa tú-bi. Ní bi kā ki cí yii ḿ ŋá tin bi sòon̄ee kí tīī-bi! 7Ama ní m bí-bi yii: <Aleedaka ŋin ni kée kaa sá inyimɔn leedakaŋaaa? Tin ni sòon̄ yii an làá dāan̄ee kaa sá inyimɔnaaa? Ni gà ni-biŋŋi ki lì yii ni nàatī tin ti-Dindaan tīī-ni ní nàatēe, ama ní maa kpáàa sòon̄ nì ni gba! 8Too, man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti bíi sòoǹ yii: ni nín ŋá pu ki yāntì inyimɔn nyɔɔbuŋŋi nì inyimɔn leedakaŋee gbītì an kɔkɔ puee, m làá jáǹ-ni.> Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee dee!
9«M làá dàkà bibɔnaatiliibi bin kántì inyimɔn leedakaŋ ki sòon̄ tinyimɔmbɔtee m-pɔŋŋu. Baa ti làá nīn cáá mpaan m-samaau kansikin. Baa làá ŋmà bi-yiŋŋi Isirayeel nibul gbɔŋkun ní baa ti làá gítí bi-tiŋkin mun. Niinee bi làá béé yii m sá ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti.
10«Bibɔnaatiliibi bí ki kíiĺ m-nibul ki lì yii ŋgbansɔŋfi bí, ama ní ŋgbansɔŋfi kaa bí. M-samaau bíi māā digundi ní bíǹ bí ki pōontí-dì. 11Too, tùkù bin bíi pōontí gbanti yii: Digundi làá lítí! Utaakpaan ubɔ làá nì ní ataanyiŋkumbil ń lítí ní kubuŋkpaaŋŋu ń jītí. 12Digundee yaa láa lítèe, bi làá dāá bàlifì-ni yii: <Ni nín póoń digundi puee bí la?> 13An ní man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nìn bíi tùkù-nee yii: M-ŋuul poonee, m làá cáań kubuŋkpaaŋŋu, ní m-bum ń cáań utaakpaan ní ataanyiŋkumbil ń lítí kí nàan̄ tikɔkɔ. 14M làá kpēelikì digundi din ni póońee. M làá téé-dì kí lúkú kitiŋ ní di-nyeel ń nyā kí páań mpaampiin pu. Di làá lítí ní kí nà-ni dúsi dusi ní ní béé yii m sá ni-Dindaan. 15M làá yàntī m-ŋuul ń tɔ̄ di-tundi digundi nee nì bin póoń-dèe pu kí cáá kátí. Bi làá dāá tùkù-ni yii: <Digundee kaa ti bí! Ubɔ kaa ti bí kí póoń-dì! 16Isirayeel bɔnaatiliibi bin nìn sòoǹ ki nàatī Jeerusaleem puee kaa ti bí. Bi nìn kāntí aleedaka ki lì yii ŋgbansɔŋfi bí, ama ní ŋgbansɔŋfi kaa bí! Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄.»
Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí bikpaŋkpantiibi
17«Nisaaleen, pīlifì, sòoǹ nì Isirayeel nimpoobi bin bɔ́ntí tin bi lèe ki cáa nàatēe, fōō Unimbɔti nyɔɔbundi kí dūú nàatī-bi. 18Tùkù-bi tin man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti sòon̄ee yii: Nnaabu làá jēetí ni-pu! Ni cáá igban ki lù abɔmbil ki fūuntí, ní ki lù iŋaabu nì i-bulifi ki tìì binib kɔkɔ kí ŋmā kí nīn cáá mpɔn bi-pu. Ni là kí fōō m-nibul maŋfal kí gāā ni-bindi ní ki kpáafí nimbi ni-ba yal. 19Ni bíiĺ-mi m-nibul nimbiin kí ŋmā kí ká ɔɔji aŋaŋkul akaaŋkaa nì kpɔnɔb bikaaŋkaabi. Ni nín bíi mɔ́ntí m-samaau un di néeń ki pílifí tinyimɔmbɔtee, ni bíi kù bin kaa bàà máaǹ ŋkúmee ní ki yàntī bin kaa bàà máaǹ kí nīn bí dimaŋfalinee bí dimaŋfalin dee. 20An pu ní man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti bíi lì yii m làá jáǹ ni-bɔmbiliŋ ŋin ni cáa sàl̀ bin kíǹee. M làá dáaĺ-ŋi kí tìfì kí fúutí ni-ŋaliyin ní kí fīī bin ni cúúyee kí líí. 21M làá dáaĺ ni-ŋaabui kí cátí ní kí fīī m-samaau kí nyāntí ni-ŋaan. Naa ti làá ŋmā kí dū-bi kí kpántí ni-wanti tin ni cúúyee ní ní béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan. 22Ni dū ni-nyimɔŋyi ki yɔ̄tì deedeedambi wunti ŋyunti ŋun ní maa bàà là bi-wunti ń yɔ̀tēe. Ni tīī binikpitib kunyannyaau, ki pīiǹ-bi nsan bí fá bi-bimbikpitim kí ŋmátí. 23Míǹ puee, naa ti làá ká inyimɔn leedakaŋ kaa ti làá sòoǹ tinyimɔmbɔti. M làá fīī m-nibul kí nyāntí ni-ŋaan. Mimmee ni làá béé yii m sá ni-Dindaan.»

english_text:
Ezekiel Encourages the People To Turn Back to the Lord
1One day, some of Israel's leaders came to me and asked for a message from the Lord. 2While they were there, the Lord said:
3Ezekiel, son of man, these men have started worshiping idols, though they know it will cause them to sin even more. So I refuse to give them a message!
4Tell the people of Israel that if they sin by worshiping idols and then go to a prophet to find out what I say, I will give them the answer their sins deserve. 5When they hear my message, maybe they will see that they need to turn back to me and stop worshiping those idols.
6Now, Ezekiel, tell everyone in Israel:
I am the Lord God. Stop worshiping those idols I hate so much and come back to me.
7Suppose one of you Israelites or a foreigner living in Israel rejects me and starts worshiping idols. If you then go to a prophet to find out what I say, I will answer 8by turning against you. I will make you a warning to anyone who might think of doing the same thing, and you will no longer belong to my people. Then you will know that I am the Lord and that you have sinned against me.
9If a prophet gives a false message, I am the one who caused that prophet to lie. But I will still reject him and cut him off from my people, 10and anyone who goes to that prophet for a message will be punished in the same way. 11I will do this, so that you will come back to me and stop destroying yourselves with these disgusting sins. So turn back to me! Then I will be your God, and you will be my people. I, the Lord God, make this promise.
Judgment on a Sinful Nation
12The Lord God said:
13Ezekiel, son of man, suppose an entire nation sins against me, and I punish it by destroying the crops and letting its people and livestock starve to death. 14 Even if Noah, Daniel, and Job were living in that nation, their faithfulness would not save anyone but themselves.
15Or suppose I punish a nation by sending wild animals to eat people and scare away every passerby, so that the land becomes a barren desert. 16As surely as I live, I promise that even if these three men lived in that nation, their own children would not be spared. The three men would live, but the land would be an empty desert.
17Or suppose I send an enemy to attack a sinful nation and kill its people and livestock. 18If these three men were in that nation when I punished it, not even their children would be spared. Only the three men would live.
19And suppose I am so angry that I send a deadly disease to wipe out the people and livestock of a sinful nation. 20Again, even if Noah, Daniel, and Job were living there, I, the Lord, promise that the children of these faithful men would also die. Only the three of them would be spared.
21 I am the Lord God, and I promise to punish Jerusalem severely. I will send war, starvation, wild animals, and deadly disease to slaughter its people and livestock. 22And those who survive will be taken from their country and led here to Babylonia. Ezekiel, when you see how sinful they are, you will know why I did all these things to Jerusalem. 23You will be convinced that I, the Lord God, was right in doing what I did.
translation_text:
Isirayeel yab máaǹ kí dū awaa kí fá
1Dalbee Isirayeel tindaŋkpilib biba dɔ́miń ki kāl̀ m-nimbiin. 2Niinee ní ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: 3«Nisaaleen, binib nee tú bi-waaŋi bi-pɔbiliŋin ní. Bi-nimbikpeeŋu pée cɔ́ kun di yàntī bi ŋáań ikpitee pu ní. A dàkafī yii m làá yàntī bí bàlifì-mi tiba ḿ kíí-baaa? 4An puee sòoǹ nì bi kí tùkù-bi tin man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti lēe yii: Tí dūú ŋmàntī kii Isirayeel yab kansikin ubɔ tú u-waaŋi u-pɔbilin ní u-nimbikpeeŋu pée cɔ́ tin di yàntī u ŋáań ikpitee pu, ní boonee ki dɔ́miń kí bàlifì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu, man ni-Dindaan di làá kíí-u m-ba. M làá kíí-u kí nóó nì awaa ŋin nyɔkɔm u cááyee ní. 5M làá ŋá míǹ ní kí gbēē Isirayeel yab bin dū-mi ki fá ki kíǹ ki nóó awaayee pɔbil. 6An pu ní á tùkù Isirayeel yab yii: <Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti bí-ni yii ní kpántí ni-bimbim. Fàtīmaan ni-boon kí tīī ni-waaŋi ní kí dū ni-timbiilituuŋŋi kɔkɔ kí fá.>
7«Isirayeel niliu ubɔ àá unicaan un kóò Isirayeel tiŋkinee yaa dū-mi ki fá ní ki yāntì tiwaabɔti jíń u-pɔbil ní kaa fātì u-boon ki tīī tin di yàntī u ŋáań ikpitee, udaan yaa dɔ́miń m-bɔnaatiliu cee kí bàlifì kí béé m-lammee, man ni-Dindaan di làá kíí-u m-ba. 8M làá jáǹ unil gbanti. M làá yàntī ú kpántí ŋabika bí nīn kíǹ ki cáa gà ilan. M làá nyāntí-u m-samaau kansikin ní ní béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan.
9«Ama ubɔnaatil yaa yāntì an ŋmātiǹ-u ní u gāā u-bindi ki kíí udaan tibee, mimmee an dàkà yii man ni-Dindaan di ŋmātiǹ ubɔnaatil gbanti. M làá dàkà udaan m-pɔŋŋu ní kí nyāntí-u m-nibul Isirayeel yab kansikin. 10Ubɔnaatil gbanti nì un dɔ́miń ki bālifèe kɔkɔ ŋá ikpitibaanti ní bi làá túń bi-kpitii kpuulool. 11An yaa ŋá mimmee, Isirayeel yab kaa ti làá gáatí kí wàatī-mi. Baa ti làá ŋá ikpiti kí kɔ́ǹ bi-ba tijɔkɔndi. Ama bi làá nīn sá m-nibul ní man ḿ nīn sá bi-Nimbɔtiu. Man bi-Dindaan Unimbɔti di lī míǹ.»
Tiba kaa ŋūǹ kí pìin̄ Unimbɔti bɔsooŋyi nsan
12Ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: 13«Nisaaleen, kitiŋ kiba pu nib yaa kaa yúl̀-mi deedee ki ŋá ikpitee, m làá dàkà-bi m-pɔŋŋu. M làá bīil̀ bi-kpaajinti tin bi kpáafèe ní kí yàntī ŋkùm ń nyā, ní kí kpɔ̀ kí céetí kitiŋee nib nì ki-waŋkuti. 14Báà binib bita nee, Noowa nì Daniyeel nì Yoob yaa bí kitiŋ gbanti nib kansikin, bi-deedeeu làá fīī bíǹ ŋmaniŋma ní. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di lī míǹ.
15«Àá tí lì yii m dū ipeecuncuti ki tɔ́ kitiŋ gbanti nib pu. Kitiŋee làá kpántí kii kuteeuee ní, di sá ipeel làá kpɔ̀ kí céetí ki-nib ní ipeel puee, ubɔ mun kaa ti làá kíí kí dī niin. 16Báà binib bita gbanti yaa bí kitiŋee poon, bíǹ baba di làá ŋmátí. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti un bí dimaŋfalinee di bíi lì yii, baa làá ŋmā kí fīī bíǹ bi-ba biyaamu gba, ní kitiŋee làá kpántí kuteeu.
17«Àá m yaa cáań kujaau ki tɔ́ kitiŋee nib pu ní ki pú bijanjaliibi nsan bí kpɔ̀ kí céetí kitiŋee pu nib nì ki-waŋkuti, 18ní binib bita gbanti yaa kóò kitiŋee poonee, bíǹ baba di làá ŋmátí. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti un bí dimaŋfalinee di bíi lì yii, baa làá ŋmā kí fīī bíǹ bi-ba biyaamu gba.
19«M yaa tí cáań bìlbil kúm ki tɔ́ kitiŋee nib pu ki kpáatì m-ŋuul ki sītì bi-pu kí kpɔ̀ kí céetí ki-nib nì ki-waŋkuti, 20ní Noowa nì Daniyeel nì Yoob bí kitiŋee poon, bi-deedeeu làá fīī bíǹ ŋmaniŋma ní. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti un bí dimaŋfalinee di bíi lì yii, baa làá ŋmā kí fīī bíǹ bi-ba biyaamu gba.»
21Míǹ boonee ní ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti bí-mi yii: «M dū inaabukpaan inaa ki tɔ́ Jeerusaleem pu kí kpɔ̀ kí céetí binib nì tiwaŋkuti. Inaabu gbanti di sá kujaau nì ŋkùm nì ipeecuncuti nì bìlbil kúm. 22Ama biba làá ŋmátí. Bi làá nyāntí bininjab nì binimpoobi kitiŋin. Bi làá dāan̄ kí kūtì ni-pu. Ni làá dāá ká bi-bimbim nì bi-tuuŋŋi ní kí tīī-mi mmɔ́ɔn m nín dū nnaabukpaan ŋun ki tɔ́ Jeerusaleem puee. 23Ni làá kpántí ni-landɔkɔŋu, di sá yii ni làá ká-bi ní kí béé yii m cáá nsan kí ŋá kitiŋ nee kii m nín ŋá-kì pu nee. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ.»

english_text:
Jerusalem Is a Useless Vine
1Some time later, the Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, what happens to the wood of a grapevine after the grapes have been picked? It isn't like other trees in the forest, 3because the wood of a grapevine can't be used to make anything, not even a small peg to hang things on. 4It can only be used as firewood. But after its ends are burnt and its middle is charred, it can't be used for anything. 5The wood is useless before it is burned, and afterwards, it is completely worthless.
6I, the Lord God, promise that just as the wood of a grapevine is burned as firewood, 7I will punish the people of Jerusalem with fire. Some of them have escaped one destruction, but soon they will be completely burned. And when that happens, you, Ezekiel, will know that I am the Lord. 8I will make their country an empty wasteland, because they have not been loyal to me. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_text:
Bufiinyisubu bun ŋŋmi wùn̄ee
1Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi ki bí yii: 2«Nisaaleen, bufiinyisubu cáá kunyampoou ki jítiǹ isufi in kɔkɔ kíǹeeee? Mimmee bu-paŋŋi cáá kunyampoou ki jítiǹ kubambaŋŋun sufii paŋŋaaa? 3Unil ŋūǹ kí dū fiinyi subu kí kpítí tibaaa? Bi ŋūǹ kí dūú ŋá dikpakpaal kí sàkan̄ tiwanaaa? 4Bu pée ŋān̄ bí dū-bu kí tɔ̄ ŋŋmin an wà ní. Ní ŋŋmi yaa wùn̄ anyɔɔgbanliitilee, ndɔee kansikin mun wù ní. An yaa wùn̄ mimmee, bi gíti ŋūǹ kí dū-bu kí ŋá ba? 5Bu nín nìn sá bumɔmbuee, baa nìn ŋūǹ kí dū-bu kí ŋá tiba. Kin bu nín wùn̄ ŋŋmee ní bi gíti ŋūǹ kí dū-bu kí ŋá tibaaa? Aayee, kpataaa!
6«Too, man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòoǹ puee sèé: <Kii bi nín dù bufiinyisubu dɔŋu kí tɔ̄ ŋŋmin kí yàntī isufi in kíǹee dɔyee, míǹ ní m làá wà Jeerusaleem yab. 7M làá jáǹ-bi. Bi dàkafī yii bi sáǹ ki nyáń ŋŋmin ní, ama ŋŋmi làá wà-bi. M yaa láa bíi jáà nì bee, ni làá dāá béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan. 8M làá yàntī bi-tiŋki ń kpántí kuteeu, kun puee baa yúl̀-mi nì deedee.> Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee dee.»

english_text:
Jerusalem Is Unfaithful
1The Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, remind the people of Jerusalem of their disgusting sins 3and tell them that I, the Lord God, am saying:
Jerusalem, you were born in the country where Canaanites lived. Your father was an Amorite, and your mother was a Hittite. 4When you were born, no one cut you loose from your mother or washed your body. No one rubbed your skin with salt and olive oil, and wrapped you in warm blankets. 5Not one person loved you enough to do any of these things, and no one even felt sorry for you. You were despised, thrown into a field, and forgotten.
6I saw you lying there, rolling around in your own blood, and I couldn't let you die. 7I took care of you, like someone caring for a tender, young plant. You grew up to be a beautiful young woman with mature breasts and hair, but you were still naked.
8When I saw you again, you were old enough to have sex. So I covered your naked body with my own robe. Then I solemnly promised that you would belong to me and that I, the Lord God, would take care of you.
9I washed the blood off you and rubbed your skin with olive oil. 10I gave you the finest clothes and the most expensive robes, as well as sandals made from the best leather. 11I gave you bracelets, a necklace, 12a ring for your nose, some earrings, and a beautiful crown. 13Your jewelry was gold and silver, and your clothes were made of only the finest material and embroidered linen. Your bread was baked from fine flour, and you ate honey and olive oil. You were as beautiful as a queen, 14and everyone on earth knew it. I, the Lord God, had helped you become a lovely young woman.
15You learned that you were attractive enough to have any man you wanted, so you offered yourself to every passerby. 16You made shrines for yourself and decorated them with some of your clothes. That's where you took your visitors to have sex with them. These things should never have happened! 17You made idols out of the gold and silver jewelry I gave you, then you sinned by worshiping those idols. 18You dressed them in the clothes you got from me, and you offered them the olive oil and incense I gave you. 19I supplied you with fine flour, olive oil, and honey, but you sacrificed it all as offerings to please those idols. I, the Lord God, watched this happen.
20But you did something even worse than that—you sacrificed your own children to those idols! 21You slaughtered my children, so you could offer them as sacrifices. 22You were so busy sinning and being a prostitute that you refused to think about the days when you were young and were rolling around naked in your own blood.
23Now I, the Lord God, say you are doomed! Not only did you do these evil things, 24but you also built places on every street corner 25where you disgraced yourself by having sex with anyone who walked by. And you did that more and more every day! 26To make me angry, you even offered yourself to Egyptians, who were always ready to sleep with you.
27So I punished you by letting those greedy Philistine enemies take over some of your territory. But even they were offended by your repulsive behavior.
28You couldn't get enough sex, so you chased after Assyrians and slept with them. You still weren't satisfied, 29so you went after Babylonians. But those merchants could not satisfy you either.
30I, the Lord God, say that you were so disgusting that you would have done anything to get what you wanted. 31You had sex on every street corner, and when you finished, you refused to accept money. That's worse than being a prostitute! 32You are nothing but an unfaithful wife who would rather have sex with strangers than with your own husband. 33Prostitutes accept money for having sex, but you bribe men from everywhere to have sex with you. 34You're not like other prostitutes. Men don't ask you for sex—you offer to pay them!
Jerusalem Must Be Punished
The Lord said:
35Jerusalem, you prostitute, listen to me. 36You chased after lovers, then took off your clothes and had sex. You even worshiped disgusting idols and sacrificed your own children as offerings to them. 37So I, the Lord God, will gather every one of your lovers, those you liked and those you hated. They will stand around you, and I will rip off your clothes and let all of those lovers stare at your nakedness. 38I will find you guilty of being an unfaithful wife and a murderer, and in my fierce anger I will sentence you to a violent death! 39Then I will hand you over to your lovers, who will tear down the places where you had sex. They will take your clothes and jewelry, leaving you naked and empty-handed.
40Your lovers and an angry mob will stone you to death; they will cut your dead body into pieces 41and burn down your houses. Other women will watch these terrible things happen to you. I promise to stop you from being a prostitute and paying your lovers for sex.
42Only then will I calm down and stop being angry and jealous. 43You made me furious by doing all these disgusting things and by forgetting how I took care of you when you were young. Then you made things worse by acting like a prostitute. You must be punished! I, the Lord God, have spoken.
Jerusalem's Two Sisters
The Lord said:
44People will use this saying about you, Jerusalem: “If the mother is bad, so is her daughter.” 45You are just like your mother, who hated her husband and her own children. You are also like your sisters, who hated their husbands and children. Your father was an Amorite, and your mother was a Hittite. 46Your older sister was Samaria, that city to your north with her nearby villages. Your younger sister was Sodom, that city to your south with her nearby villages. 47You followed their way of life and their wicked customs, and soon you were more repulsive than they were.
48As surely as I am the living Lord God, the people of Sodom and its nearby villages were never as sinful as you. 49They were arrogant and spoiled; they had everything they needed and still refused to help the poor and needy. 50They thought they were better than everyone else, and they did things I hate. And so I destroyed them.
51You people of Jerusalem have sinned twice as much as the people of Samaria. In fact, your evil ways have made both Sodom and Samaria look innocent. 52So their punishment will seem light compared to yours. You will be disgraced and put to shame because of your disgusting sins.
Jerusalem Will Be Ashamed
The Lord said to Jerusalem:
53Someday I will bless Sodom and Samaria and their nearby villages. I will also bless you, Jerusalem. 54Then you will be ashamed of how you've acted, and Sodom and Samaria will be relieved that they weren't as sinful as you. 55When that day comes, you and Sodom and Samaria will once again be well-off, and all nearby villages will be restored.
56Jerusalem, you were so arrogant that you sneered at Sodom. 57But now everyone has learned how wicked you really are. The countries of Syria and Philistia, as well as your other neighbors, hate you and make insulting remarks. 58You must pay for all the vulgar and disgusting things you have done. I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Lord Makes a Promise to Jerusalem
The Lord said:
59Jerusalem, you deserve to be punished, because you broke your promises and ignored our agreement. 60But I remember the agreement I made with you when you were young, and so I will make you a promise that will last forever. 61When you think about how you acted, you will be ashamed, especially when I return your sisters to you as daughters, even though this was not part of our agreement. 62I will keep this solemn promise, and you will know that I am the Lord. 63I will forgive you, but you will think about your sins and be too ashamed to say a word. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_text:
Jeerusaleem nìn bí kii kibiki kin bi dūu fée ní
1Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii: 2«Nisaaleen, dàkà Jeerusaleem tiŋki ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin kì ŋée. 3Á tùkù-kì yii: <Ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín bíi sòoǹ nì Jeerusaleem puee sɔ̀. Kanaan sá a-naanjab tiŋki ní. Niin ní bi màl̄-si. A-baa sá uamɔɔrja ní a-na sá ueetinimpu. 4Daliŋkin bi màl̄-see, ubɔ kaa nìn gíí a-puluuŋmiiŋu. Baa nìn fùl̄-si nnyim kí ŋá-si circir. Baa nìn dū ŋyaam ki ŋmītì-si, ní kaa nìn tí dū sata ki bīiǹ-si. 5Ubɔ kaa nìn súń a-saai àá ki dàkā-si kulaŋŋaŋfitiiu kí ŋá-si tíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ. Ama bi nín màl̄-see, bi dū-si ki bíl̀ kitiŋ ní, di sá yii baa nìn là bi-nimbil ń wāl̀-si. 6M nín jítì a-ceeyee, m ká yii a dɔ̄ a-fatikuun. A nín dɔ̄ a-fatikuun mimmee ní m bí-si yii á nīn bí dimaŋfalin, ní ki būsì ki lī yii á nīn bí dimaŋfalin. 7M yāntì a wíiǹ kii kusaaun subuee ní. A wíiǹ ki cíkitì ní ki kpántì usapɔnnyaan. A nìn nyáń abii ki túkú tikuti. Ama a nìn pée bí dicancaŋgbeel ní. 8Míǹ boonee ní m gíti tí jítì a-cee ní ki ká yii a cíkitì ki bàn̄ dicamɔndi. Niinee ní m dū m-bɔkutikpaandi ki bīiǹ a-cancaŋgbeel pu. M nìn pūtì yii m làá nīn yú nì si deedee ní man nì si ŋá mpèé. Niinee ní a kpántì m-yɔu>. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di lī míǹ.
9«Niinee ní m yōoǹ nnyim ki fíntì fatiku un bí a-puee ní ki dū ŋkpam min sɔ́fèe ki ŋmītì-si. 10M nìn dū tiwampeeŋkaal tin bi gbáńee nì igban imɔnti naatakaŋ nì dambalamɔnti nì ŋŋaamɔnti bɔkutikpaandi ki tīī-si. 11M nìn dū tinyɔkɔntikaal ki nyɔ̄kɔntì-si, ki nìn dū dibɔmbil ki fúuń a-ŋal ní ki dū tiléeŋkaal ki léeǹ-si. 12M nìn dū kibɔmbiki ki túuń a-maŋfal ní ki dū falfatib ki túuń a-tafaliŋ ní ki dū kibeefuulii kinyannyaaŋŋi ki cíkiǹ-si. 13A-wannyɔkɔntikaati nìn sá sindaariya nì animbil ní, ní a-wampeeŋkaati sá ŋŋaapiin ní bi dū gulfamɔnti ki gbáń. Ŋyimmɔntiim nì tisiil nì ɔliifi kpam ní a nìn jīǹ. Niinee ní a dūu kpántì usapɔnnyaan ki bàn̄ kí nīn sá ubeenimpu. 14A-nyaaŋku puee, a-yindi nìn gbītì ki bàn̄ atimbun kɔkɔn, di sá yii m nín nyɔ̄kɔntì-si puee, a lafun kpántì unyannyaan. Man a-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ.»
Jeerusaleem kpántì kii kinimpulaakpaayee
15«Ama a dū a-mákal ki páaǹ a-nyaaŋku pu. A-yindi nín gbītì an kɔkɔ puee, a dūu kpántì kilaakpaai. A dōoǹ nì bisanjitiliibi kɔkɔ ní ki dūu kpántì bi-wanti. 16A lēē a-wampeeŋkaati tin cáá inyiŋfi tikpilee ki dūu nyɔ̄kɔntì a-waatootipaaŋyi ki ŋá niin a-laakpaatuuŋŋi. Ubɔ kaa nìn pée ŋá míǹ ki ká, ní kaa ti làá ŋá míǹ mun jaanjaan. 17A dū sindaariya nì animbil wannyɔkɔntikaati tin m tīī-see ki dūu mɔ́ɔ́ iwaajaa, ní ki dōoǹ nì i ki ŋá tilaakpaal. 18A dū a-wampeeŋkaati tin bi gbáńee ki bīiǹ bi-pu, ní ki dū ŋkpam nì talaalub bin m tīī-see ki ŋá saraa ki tīī-bi. 19Kí fáatíǹ-bee, a dū tijin tin kɔkɔ m nìn tīī-see ki ŋá-bi saraa, ŋyimmɔntiim nì ŋkpam nì tisiil. Kpèè tin ní a ŋée dee, man a-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ. 20Jeerusaleem, a dū a-jipɔmbi nì a-bisalib bin a màl̄-mee ki ŋá saraa ki tīī awaa gbanti an kpántì ŋi-jinti. A-laakpaatuuŋŋi ŋin a ŋáańee kaa bàn̄-see, 21see a nín lāntì m-jipɔmbi ki dūu ŋá saraa ki tīī a-waaŋee! 22Ŋyunti ŋun a nìn bíi ŋáań ntimbiil nì alaakpaatuun gbantee, aa dākafì ki téetì a-sapɔnti yuntiŋu, ŋyunti ŋun ní a nìn bí dicancaŋgbeel ki dēē a-fatikuunee.
23«A nín ŋá atuŋkpiti gbanti kɔkɔ ki dóòyee, nnaabu di dɔ̄ ki cí-si, man a-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ. 24Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, a gbíntìi nìkì ki māā akumpoo nì isaraafan ipaan kɔkɔ pu. 25A máń dikumpool disaŋkaŋkpil kamaa pu ní ki dū a-nyaaŋku ki ŋá ntimbiil tuuŋŋi. A dū a-ba ki tīī usanjitil kamaa ní ki mɔ̄tìi būtì a-laakpaati. 26A kpáfì nì Eejipiti yab, a-kɔŋkɔnnaatɔb bin cáá ŋgbannyaanee ki ŋá tilaakpaal, ní ki gíti ŋá tin jítì mimmee ki gbítì m-ŋuul. 27Niinee ní m dàkā-si m-pɔŋŋu. M fōō tin a cááyee dijandi diba ní ki dū-si ki líiǹ a-nannanliibi, Fiiliistii yab timmu mun a-laakpaabimbim nìn kɔ̄ntí icooyee. 28Ama an kaa bàn̄-see ní a cūtìi bíi ŋáań tilaakpaal nì Asuur yab. Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, an kaa yá ki kɔ́-si. 29A gíti ŋá alaakpaatuun tikpil nì Babiloon yab, binyampoobi tiŋkin, ama an kaa túń-si ditundi. 30Ama a-mul kaa bōotí mmɔ́ɔneeee! Man a-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ. A nín nìn ŋáań tíǹ gbanti kɔkɔee, a náań nì kinimpulaakpaai páaa ní. 31A máń akumpoo disaŋkaŋkpil kamaa pu. A máń iwaatootipaan an kɔkɔ pu. Ama aa fōō animbil kii bilaakpaadambi bin kíǹee nín ŋáań puee! 32A bí kii unimpu un néeń binicambi ki jítiǹ u-calee ní. 33Nnimpulaakpaamu kɔkɔ fòol̄ a-nimbil ní, ama siiyee, a pūǹ a-bɔmbi tiwan ní ki pà-bi bí nīn nyēeń an kɔkɔ pu ki dòoń ki dɔ̀ nì si. 34A-laakpaatuuŋŋi poonee, sii kaa ŋáań kii nlaakpaadamu mun kíǹee nín ŋáań puee. Baa nyàab̀-si, kaa pà-si, ama sii di pà-bi. Sii kaa ŋáań kii bin kíǹee nín ŋáań puee.
35«Too, Jeerusaleem kilaakpaai, pīlifì ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi. 36Pīlifì tin man a-Dindaan Unimbɔti bíi sòoǹee. A dū a-cancaŋgbeel ki páaǹ mpaampiin pu ki yāntì a-wunti ncal ŋyunti ŋun ní a bíi ŋáań tilaakpaal nì a-bɔmbi, a-timbiiliŋu waaŋee. A dū a-jipɔmbi ki ŋá saraa ki tīī a-waaŋi ki kpáatì bi-fatikuu ki fá. 37An pu ní m làá kóoǹ a-bɔmbi bin nìn tìì-si mmɔnee kɔkɔ kí kpāfì, bin a nìn néeńee nì bin bɔti kaa nìn mɔ̄ǹ-see. M làá kóoǹ-bi an kɔkɔ pú kí kpāfì a-cee ní kí pèetī-si ní bí wāl̀ a-cancaŋgbeel. 38Binimpoobi bin ŋáań tilaakpaal nì bin kù binibee tafadaaldi ní m làá dūú dáaĺ a-tafal. M-ŋuul nì m-poompooŋyi poonee, m làá dū ŋkúm ní kí dáaĺ a-tafal. 39M làá dū-si kí líiǹ a-bɔmbi. Bi làá gbá kí wìil̀ a-kumpooŋi ní kí bīil̀ a-waatootipaaŋyi. Bi làá cúú a-wampeeŋkaati kí pèetī ní kí gbākal̀-si a-wannyɔkɔntikaati tinyaandee kɔkɔ ní kí yàntī-si dicancaŋgbeel. 40Míǹ boonee ní bí lùkutī diniwul kí tɔ̄ a-pu. Bi làá yāŋkì-si ataŋkpee kí kpɔ̀ ní kí dū ntàataajimu kí tɔ̀ntī-si, 41ní kí wà a-diiŋŋi ŋŋmi. Bi làá dáaĺ a-tafal min máaǹee kunimpupaau nimbiin. M làá kúntí a-laakpaatuuŋŋi ní aa ti làá ŋmā kí pà a-bɔmbi. 42M làá yàntī m-ŋuul ń tɔ̄ a-pu di-tundi kí cáá kátí. Míǹ boonee ní m-ŋuul ń páatí a-pu ní m-pɔbil ń sɔ̀ŋkì, ní maa ti làá gíí diŋuul. 43Aa ti téetí tin ní m ŋá ki tīī-si doooo a-sapɔnti yuntiŋuee ní ki dū a-tuuŋŋi ki gbítì a-ŋuul. Too, ma muee, m làá pà a-bimbim paati. Man a-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ. Di sá yii a ŋá icoo tuuŋŋi ki kútì ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin kɔkɔ a ŋá nì awaayee pu.
Ntimu mun kíǹee sɔ́ǹ Jeerusaleem
44«Jeerusaleem, bilaŋgaaliibi làá gāā-si nlan yii: <Unaati nín bí puee, míǹ ní u-bisal mun bí>. 45Ibaamɔn poonee, a lafun sá a-na bisal, unimpu un di nìn ná u-cal nì u-biyaamuee. A pée bí kii a-naalib bin di nìn ná bi-calib nì bi-biyaamuee ní. Ni-na nìn sá ueetinimpu ní, ní ni-baa sá uamɔɔrja. 46A-maan di sá Samaarii ŋgan pú tiŋki ki kpáaǹ ntimbilimu mun māntìi tú-kèe. A-naal di sá Soodoom ŋgiil pú tiŋki nì ntimbilimu mun māntìi tú-kèe. 47An kaa sá bi-bimbim nì bi-timbiilituuŋŋi ŋmaniŋma ní a fōō, ama a gíti ŋá tin jítiǹ mimmee! 48Man a-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín bí dimaŋfalin nee, a-naal Soodoom nì ntimbilimu mun māntìi tú-kèe kaa pée ŋá ikpiti kii sii nì ntimbilimu mun māntìi tú-see nín ŋá puee. 49Soodoom nì ntimu mun māntìi tú-kèe yìntitam sɔ̀. Mu nìn cáá dilambil, ki nìn jīǹ ki lákatí mu-ba pu ní ki nìn bí ŋgbansɔŋfin kaa dàkafī tiba pu. Muaa nìn jōō bisoodambi nì binandambi. 50Mu nìn yòontí mu-ba yilpu ní ki nìn ŋá ntimbiil tuuŋŋi. Niinee ní m kúntì-mu kitiŋ pu kii a nín nyí puee. 51Samaarii tiŋki kíǹ kaa ŋá ikpiti in a ŋá nee dijandi gba! A ŋá ntimbiil tuuŋŋi tikpil ki jítiǹ-kì. Bi yaa dū a-maan Samaarii nì a-naal Soodoom ki ŋmāntiǹ siiyee, bíǹ sá deedeedambi ní! 52Too, kɔŋkɔnnee, an kíǹ á túń a nín fá a-jilmau puee cooi dee.
