A tīī a-naal nì a-maan ibaamɔn, di sá yii ikpiti in a ŋée nyāŋkì ki jítì bi-yai, ní ki yāntì bi kpántì deedeedambi ki jítiǹ-si. Icoo ń nīn cáá-si ní á jī falaa a nín fá a-jilmauee pu. 53M làá yàntī ntimu gbanti ń fàtīí gítí kii mu nín nìn bí puee. M làá yàntī an fàtīí bútí Soodoom nì ntimbilimu mun māntìi tú-kèe nì Samaarii nì ntimbilimu mun māntìi tú-kèe. Míǹ boonee ní ḿ dāá yàntī án bútí si mun. 54An yaa ŋá mimmee, icoo làá cúú-si ní á fá a-jilmau tin kɔkɔ a ŋée pu. An di làá ŋméeǹ-mu. 55Án làá fàtīí bútí Soodoom nì Samaarii nì ntimbilimu mun māntìi tú-muee. Án làá fàtīí bútí si mun nì ntimbilimu mun māntìi tú-see. 56Ŋyunti ŋun a nìn cáá dilambilee, a nìn kpèé a-naal Soodoom fám ní. 57An sá ŋyunti ŋun ní a-kpitii nìn dáá bí dibalinee ní. Sii mun yuntiŋu bāań Eedoom timmu nì ntimu mun māntìi tú-muee ń bèel̀-si dee. Fiiliistii yab timmu làá kpèè-si fám ijaan kɔkɔ pu. 58Icoo nì ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin a ŋée paati dee. Man a-Dindaan di sòon̄ míǹ.
59«Man a-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. A kpēē dipùtil din a pūtèe fám ki kpītì mpèé ŋun bí man nì si kansikinee. Míǹ puee, a nín ŋá-mi puee, míǹ ní m làá ŋá-si. 60Ama mamee, maa làá súntí dipoondi din ní m pōoǹ-si a-sapɔnti yuntiŋuee. M làá yàntī dipoondi gbanti ń kpántí talku poondi. 61A làá dāá téetí a-bimbim pu ní icoo ń cúú-si ŋyunti ŋun ní a yaa láa fōō a-mambi nì a-naalib a-ceeyee. M làá dāá dū-bi kí ŋá a-taapu bí kpántí kii a-bisalibee, min kamaa an kaa bí dipoondi din m pōoǹ-see poonee. 62M làá fàtīí pɔ̀ntī dipoondi din ní m pōoǹ-see, niinee a làá béé yii m sá a-Dindaan. 63A làá téetí tin jítèe pu ní icoo ń cúú-si ní a-nyɔkɔ ń kpú, kun puee a fá a-jilmau. Ama mamee, m làá dū tin kɔkɔ a ŋée kí pɔ̄-si.» Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ.

english_text:
A Story about Two Eagles and a Vine
1The Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Israel the following story, 3so they will understand what I am saying to them:
A large eagle with strong wings and beautiful feathers once flew to Lebanon. It broke the top branch off a cedar tree, 4then carried it to a nation of merchants and left it in one of their cities. 5The eagle also took a seed from Israel and planted it in a fertile field with plenty of water, like a willow tree beside a stream. 6The seed sprouted and grew into a grapevine that spread over the ground. It had lots of leaves and strong, deep roots, and its branches grew upward toward the eagle.
7There was another eagle with strong wings and thick feathers. The roots and branches of the grapevine soon turned toward this eagle, hoping it would bring water for the soil. 8But the vine was already growing in fertile soil, where there was plenty of water to produce healthy leaves and large grapes.
9Now tell me, Ezekiel, do you think this grapevine will live? Or will the first eagle pull it up by its roots and pluck off the grapes and let its new leaves die? The eagle could easily kill it without the help of a large and powerful army. 10The grapevine is strong and healthy, but as soon as the scorching desert wind blows, it will quickly wither.
The Lord Explains the Story
11The Lord said:
12 Ezekiel, ask the rebellious people of Israel if they know what this story means.
Tell them that the king of Babylonia came to Jerusalem, then he captured the king of Judah and his officials, and took them back to Babylon as prisoners. 13He chose someone from the family of Judah's king and signed a treaty with him, then made him swear to be loyal. He also led away other important citizens, 14so that the rest of the people of Judah would obey only him and never gain control of their own country again.
15But this new king of Judah later rebelled against Babylonia and sent officials to Egypt to get horses and troops. Will this king be successful in breaking the treaty with Babylonia? Or will he be punished for what he's done?
16As surely as I am the living Lord God, I swear that the king of Judah will die in Babylon, because he broke the treaty with the king of Babylonia, who appointed him king. 17Even the king of Egypt and his powerful army will be useless to Judah when the Babylonians attack and build towers and dirt ramps to destroy the cities of Judah and its people. 18The king of Judah broke his own promises and ignored the treaty with Babylonia. And so he will be punished!
19He made a promise in my name and swore to honor the treaty. And now that he has broken that promise, my name is disgraced. He must pay for what he's done. 20I will spread out a net to trap him. Then I will drag him to Babylon and see that he is punished for his unfaithfulness to me. 21His best troops will be killed in battle, and the survivors will be scattered in every direction. I, the Lord, have spoken.
22Someday, I, the Lord,
will cut a tender twig
from the top of a cedar tree,
then plant it on the peak
of Israel's tallest mountain,
23where it will grow
strong branches
and produce large fruit.
All kinds of birds will find
shelter under the tree,
and they will rest in the shade
of its branches.
24Every tree in the forest
will know that I, the Lord,
can bring down tall trees
and help short ones grow.
I dry up green trees
and make dry ones green.
I, the Lord, have spoken,
and I will keep my word.
translation_text:
Ikaalun ili nì fiinyi subu bubɔ bɔti
1Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii: 2«Nisaaleen, pɔ́ɔǹ Isirayeel yab ipɔɔn nee kí dū tibɔti nee kí ŋmàntī-bi. 3Tùkù-bi yii man a-Dindaan Unimbɔti di bíi sòoǹ yii: <Ukaaluŋkpaan ubɔ di nìn bí ki cáá ifeeŋkpaan ní u-kuti fɔ̀kɔ̀ ki náaǹ ki cáá inyiŋfi kupaau. U nìn ŋàan̄ ki bāań Leebanɔn jooŋŋi. U nìn yá ki kɔ́fì seedir subu bubɔ yilpu. 4U nìn bátì bu-pandi din fɔ̀kɔǹ ŋi-kɔkɔ kíǹee ní ki yōoǹ-dì ki cáa cūnnì binyampoobi tiŋkin ki dū-dì ki bíl̀ bibantiliibi tiŋkin. 5Míǹ boonee ní u yōoǹ Isirayeel tiŋkin subu bubɔ ki cáa cóoǹ kitiŋ kin bi yɔ̄kɔtèe ni. U nìn cóoǹ-bu mbun ŋun cáá nnyim tikpilee gbandi, a lì kii busubu bun néeń nnyimee. 6Busubuee cɔ́tì ní ki pɔ̄kɔtì ki kpántì bufiinyisubu ki lālim̀. Bu nìn tòó bu-paŋŋi ki cá ukaalunee watil pú ní bu-nyaaŋyi wīintí u-feeŋyi taapu. Busubuee nìn dūu kpántì bufiinyisubu ki cɔ́tì cɔ́tì ní ki tɔ́ tɔ́ mpamu. 7Ama ní ukaaluŋkpaan uliliiti ubɔ mun dūu bāań. U-feeŋyi nìn sá ikpaan ní ki cáá tikuti tikpil. Niinee ní bufiinyisubuee tɔ́ bu-nyaaŋyi ki túĺ ukaalunee cee ní ki fātì bu-paŋŋi u-watil pú. Bu nìn dàkafī kí ká u-cee nnyim kí jītíǹ laakin bu cɔ́ee. 8Ama bi nìn cóoǹ-bu kitiŋ kin ŋān̄ee poon ní, mbun ŋun cáá nnyim tikpilee gbandi, bú ŋmā kí tɔ̄ apan, kí lòoǹ abil kí kpántí bufiinyisubu bunyaambu.>
9«Dū tin man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti sòon̄ee kí nàatī yii: <Bufiinyisubu gbanti ŋūǹ kí wíiǹaaa? Ukaalumpeekaayee kaa làá cúú bu-nyaaŋyi kí fùkù, kí bīil̀ bu-biliŋ ní kí yàntī bu nín cɔ́tì cɔ́tì pu mpɔminee ń kpāaa? Kí fùkù-buee, an kaa làá bàlifì ú ŋá mpɔn àá ú nyàab̀ binib tikpil. 10Bi baasii cóoǹ bufiinyisubuee ní, ama bu làá ŋmā kí pɔ̀kɔtāaa? Kubuŋu yaa nyánní ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú ki jítì bu-puee, buaa làá kpā dicilpu dicilpu niinaaa? Laakin bi cóoǹ-bu bú bàà wíiǹee, niin ní bu làá kpā!>»
Tibɔŋmantikaalee taapu
11Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii: 12«Bàlifì pɔɔgaatib nee yii bi gbìl̄ tibɔŋmantikaal nee taapuɔɔɔ? Tùkù-bi yii Babiloon bɔtiu dɔ́miń Jeerusaleem ki cúú ubɔti nì bitindaŋkpilib ki cūnnì u-tiŋkin. 13U nìn yōoǹ ubɔti dicaŋkun niliu ubɔ, ní u nì u ŋá mpèé ní ki yāntì u pūtì yii waa làá nyā mpèéyee boon. U nìn yōoǹ kitiŋee pu bɔtibiliŋ 14án nín làá ŋá pu kitiŋee ń sìntī ki-ba taapu kí taa ti ŋmā kí yīkì, ní kí nīn tɔ́ mpèéyee deedeeyee. 15Ama ní ubɔtipɔɔnee yíkìi bíi jáà nì Babiloon bɔtiu. U tú ituun Eejipiti án nín làá ŋá pu Eejipiti ń tīī-u itaamu nì bijanjaliibi tikpilee. Án làá ŋmā kí bútí-uaaa? U nín bíi ŋáań mimmee, u làá ŋmā kí fīī u-baaa? Waa làá ŋmā kí fīī u-ba, di sá yii u nyáń mpèé boon!
16«Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín bí dimaŋfalin nee, ubɔti gbanti làá kpú Babiloon bɔtiu un di kāaǹ-u dibeelee tiŋkin ní. Di sá yii u kpēē dipùtil din u pūtèe fám ki nyáń mpèéyee boon. Míǹ puee Babiloon tiŋkin ní u làá kpú. 17Báà Eejipiti bɔtiu Faaroo yaa cáań bijanjaliibi bin pɔ̄ɔ̄yee tikpil gba, waa làá ŋmā kí mɔ̄tì u-pu, kun puee Babiloon yab làá mā ŋgumu mun boon bi làá nīn bāal̀ee, ní kí gbà ibòó kí pɔ̀fì binib tikpil. 18U nín kpēē dipùtil din u pūtèe fámee, u nyáń mpèéyee boon dee. U nín ŋá pu ki kíí ki nyīī ŋŋal ní ki ŋá tin bí nee kɔkɔee, waa làá ŋmátí!
19«Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti un bí dimaŋfalin nee nín bíi sòoǹ puee sɔ̀. Isirayeel bɔtiu nín ŋá pu ki nyáń mpèé ŋun ní u nìn pūtì m-nimbiin ki nyīī ŋŋalee boonee, m làá dáaĺ u-tafal. 20M làá píĺ-u kutaliŋŋu ní kí cúú-u. M làá cùnnì-u Babiloon tiŋkin ní kí sòoǹ u-bɔti niin, di sá yii waa yúl̀ nì mi deedee. 21Bi làá kpɔ̀ u-janjamɔntiibi kujaaun ní bin kíǹ kaa kpíìyee ń sāǹ kí yàl̄ ijaan kɔkɔ pu. Niinee ni làá béé yii man ni-Dindaan di sòon̄.»
Ti-Dindaan pooŋyi
22«Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Man m-ba làá lēē seedir subu yilpu dipampɔmbil din túkú bu-paŋkpaaŋŋi nyɔkɔpuee ní kí cáá cóoń dijoofɔŋfɔkɔl diba yilpu. 23M làá dū-dì kí cóoń Isirayeel jool din fɔ̀kɔ̀ee yilpu. Di làá wíiǹ kí tɔ̄ apan, kí lòoǹ abil ní kí kpántí buseedirisubu bunyannyaambu. Inoon kɔkɔ nì i-bulifi làá páań i-diiŋi bu-paŋŋi pu, ní kí nīn ŋùŋfī bu-booŋŋu taapu. 24Niinee tisatin sufii kɔkɔ làá béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan. M gùutī isufi in fɔ̀kɔ̀ee pu ní kí yàntī in kaa fɔ̀kɔ̀ee ń wíiǹ. M làá yàntī isufi in sɔ̀m̀ee ń kpā ní kí tīī in kūńee ŋkpiim. Man ni-Dindaan di sòon̄, ní tin m yaa lēe, m ŋáań míǹ ní.»

english_text:
Those Who Sin Will Die
1The Lord said:
2 Ezekiel, I hear the people of Israel using the old saying,
“Sour grapes eaten by parents
leave a sour taste in the mouths
of their children.”
3Now tell them that I am the Lord God, and as surely as I live, that saying will no longer be used in Israel. 4The lives of all people belong to me—parents as well as children. However, only those who sin will be put to death.
5Suppose there is a truly good man who always does what is fair and right. 6He refuses to eat meat sacrificed to foreign gods at local shrines or to worship Israel's idols. He doesn't have sex with someone else's wife or with a woman having her monthly period. 7He never cheats or robs anyone and always returns anything taken as security for a loan; he gives food and clothes to the poor 8and doesn't charge interest when lending money. He refuses to do anything evil; he is fair to everyone 9 and faithfully obeys my laws and teachings. This man is good, and I promise he will live.
10But suppose this good man has an evil son who is violent and commits sins 11his father never did. He eats meat at local shrines, has sex with someone else's wife, 12cheats the poor, and robs people. He keeps what is given to him as security for a loan. He worships idols, does disgusting things, 13and charges high interest when lending money. An evil man like that will certainly not live. He is the one who has done these horrible sins, so it's his own fault that he will be put to death.
14But suppose this evil man has a son who sees his father do these things and refuses to act like him. 15He doesn't eat meat at local shrines or worship Israel's idols, and he doesn't have sex with someone else's wife. 16He never cheats or robs anyone and doesn't even demand security for a loan. He gives food and clothes to the poor 17and refuses to do anything evil or to charge interest. And he obeys all my laws and teachings. Such a man will live. His own father sinned, but this good man will not be put to death for the sins of his father. 18It is his father who will die for cheating and robbing and doing evil.
19You may wonder why a son isn't punished for the sins of his father. It is because the son does what is right and obeys my laws. 20 Only those who sin will be put to death. Children won't suffer for the sins of their parents, and parents won't suffer for the sins of their children. Good people will be rewarded for what they do, and evil people will be punished for what they do.
21Suppose wicked people stop sinning and start obeying my laws and doing right. They won't be put to death. 22All their sins will be forgiven, and they will live because they did right. 23I, the Lord God, don't like to see wicked people die. I had much rather see them turn back from their sins and live.
24But when good people start sinning and doing disgusting things, will they live? No! All their good deeds will be forgotten, and they will be put to death because of their sins.
25You people of Israel accuse me of being unfair! But listen—I'm not unfair; you are! 26If good people start doing evil, they must be put to death, because they have sinned. 27And if wicked people start doing right, they will save themselves from punishment. 28They will think about what they've done and stop sinning, and so they won't be put to death. 29But you still say that I am unfair. You are the ones who have done wrong and are unfair!
30I will judge each of you for what you've done. So stop sinning, or else you will certainly be punished. 31Give up your evil ways and start thinking pure thoughts. And be faithful to me! Do you really want to be put to death for your sins? 32 I, the Lord God, don't want to see that happen to anyone. So stop sinning and live!
translation_text:
Unimbɔti sòoǹ binib bɔti ki nóó nì bi-bimbim ní
1Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii: 2«Isirayeel tiŋkinee, ba pu ní bi gà nlan nee yii:
<Bibaatiibi ŋmɔ́ ayeeŋgaan,
ama ní mbiyaamu nyiŋŋi nyāŋfì ní?>
3Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti un bí dimaŋfalin nee di bíi sòoǹ yii, naa ti làá gāā nlan gbanti Isirayeel tiŋkin. 4Tiŋman, unil kamaa maŋfal kā man ŋaan ní. Bibaatiibi nì mbiyaamu kɔkɔ maŋfal kā man ŋaan ní. Un yaa ŋá ikpitee, udaan di kúù.
5«Tí dūú ŋmàntī kii deedeedaan di bí ní ki ŋáań tin kítèe nì tin bí deedeeyee. 6Waa jīǹ tiwaajin awaajoon pu, kaa tòotī Isirayeel yab waaŋi. Waa mɔ̀nnì u-juti nimpuu, ní kaa dɔ̀ nì unimpu un bíi fùul̀ ŋkpinee. 7Waa mùul̄ u-juti kaa yù u-juti wanti mun. U gīintí u-pɔ̀nliu nín dū tin ki síiǹ u-cee toolimee ki tìì-u. U tìì un ŋkùm cááyee tijin, ki tìì un kaa cáá tiba kí pèen̄ee tiwampeeŋkaal. 8Waa pìntí u-nimbiliŋ bí dāá téeǹ-u kí páań àá ki nyàab̀ ipaati. U fàtī u-boon ki tìì tin kaa bí deedeeyee ní ki sòoǹ binib bɔti nì ibaamɔn. 9U tɔ́ m-bɔkpaaŋi nì m-marab ní ki nóó ibaamɔn saŋŋu. Too, man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di bíi sòoǹ yii an niliuee sá deedeedaan ní ki làá nīn bí dimaŋfalin.
10«Tí tí dūú ŋmàntī kii an niliuee cáá jipɔɔn ní u-jipɔɔnee fìkì binib wanti ki kù binib ní ki ŋáań atuŋkpiti kɔkɔ nì ŋi-bulifi. 11U-baa kaa pée ŋá míǹ ki ká. U jīǹ tiwaajin awaajoon pu, ki mɔ̀nnì u-juti nimpuu. 12U mùul̄ usoodaan nì unandaan, ki yù u-juti wanti, kaa gīintí u-pɔnliibi nín dù tin ki sīintí u-cee toolimee ki tìì-bi. U tòotī awaa ní ki ŋáań ntimbiil tuuŋŋi. 13U pìntí u-nimbiliŋ bí dāá téeǹ-u kí páań àá ki nyàab̀ ipaati. An niliu gbanti làá nīn bí dimaŋfalinaaa? Aayee, kpataaa! U ŋá ntimbiil tuuŋŋi nee kɔkɔ, see ú kpú, ní u-kúm kpuulool làá gítí úǹ u-ba pu ní.
14«Tí tí dūú ŋmàntī kii u cáá jipɔɔn. U-jipɔɔn gbanti ká u-baa tuŋkpitiŋ, ama ní kaa nóó u-tabɔbiliŋ. 15Waa jīǹ tiwaajin awaajoon pu, kaa tòotī Isirayeel yab waaŋi. Waa mɔ̀nnì u-juti nimpuu kí kɔ́ǹ u-ba tijɔkɔndi. 16Waa mùul̄ u-juti kaa yù u-juti wanti. U gīintí u-pɔ̀nliu nín dū tin ki síiǹ u-cee toolimee ki tìì-u. U tìì un ŋkùm cááyee tijin nì un kaa cáá tiba kí pèen̄ee tiwampeeŋkaal. 17U fàtī u-boon ki tìì tin kaa bí deedeeyee ní kaa pìntí u-nimbiliŋ bí dāá téeǹ-u kí páań àá ki nyàab̀ ipaati. U tɔ́ m-bɔkpaaŋi nì m-marab ní ki nóó ibaamɔn saŋŋu. An niliuee kaa làá kpú u-baa kpitii pu. U làá nīn pée bí dimaŋfalin ní. 18U-baa nín mūul̀ binib, ki yùn̄ u-nabiki wanti ki sāaǹ bin māntìi tú-uee, úǹ di máaǹ kí kpú u-kpitii pu.
19«Ama ní ni bàlifī yii ba pu ní ujipɔnti kaa máaǹ kí fōō u-baa yìntitam tafadaaldi? Too, kun di yì-tèe di sá yii ujipɔntee ŋá tin bí deedee ki kítèe ní ki tɔ́ m-bɔkpaaŋi kɔkɔ. An puee u làá nīn bí dimaŋfalin. 20Un ŋá ikpitee di kúù. Mbiyaamu kaa cáá kí pà mu-baabi kpitii pɔndi, ní bibaatiibi mun kaa cáá kí pà bi-biyaamu kpitii pɔndi. Bi làá pà deedeedaan u-deedeetuuŋŋi paati ní, ní kí pà unikpiti u-kpitii tuuŋŋi paati.
Nín̄ ŋáaḿmaan tiŋan
21«Unikpiti yaa gbēeǹ kaa tí bíi ŋáań u-tuŋkpitiŋ ní ki kíǹ ki tɔ́ m-bɔkpaaŋi ki ŋáań tin bí deedee ki kítèe, waa làá kpú, u làá pée ŋmátí ní. 22Bi làá súntí u-yìntitam kɔkɔ pu, ní ú nīn kíǹ ki bí dimaŋfalin u-deedee tuuŋŋi ŋin u kíǹ ki bíi ŋáańee pu. 23Ni dàkafī yii an mɔ̄ǹ-mi ḿ ká unikpiti ń kpú níii? Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di bíi tùkù-ni yii kun m lèe di sá unikpiti ń kpántí u-bimbim kí nīn kíǹ ki bí dimaŋfalin. 24Ama deedeedaan yaa gbēeǹ kaa tí bíi ŋáań deedee tuuŋŋi, ní ki kíĺ ki kíǹ ki bíi ŋáań ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin binikpitib ŋáańee, ni dàkafī yii an niliuee làá nīn bí dimaŋfalinaaa? Aayee, kpataaa! Bi làá súntí u-deedee tuuŋŋee kɔkɔ pu. U làá kpú, di sá yii waa yúl̀ deedee ní ki bíi ŋáań ikpiti. 25Ni lì yii: <Ti-Dindaan nín ŋáań puee kaa kítì!> Isirayeel yab, pīlifìmaan-mi tiŋan. Man di ŋáań tin kaa kítèeee? An kaa sá nimbaaa? 26Deedeedaan yaa gbēeǹ kaa tí bíi ŋáań deedee tuuŋŋi ní ki bíi ŋáań ikpitee, see ú kpú. Ikpiti in u bíi ŋáańee pu ní u làá kpú. 27Ama unikpiti yaa fātì u-boon ki tīī u-tuŋkpitiŋ ní ki kíĺ ki bíi ŋáań deedee tuuŋŋi nì tin kítèe, u làá fīī u-maŋfal. 28U yaa dáań ki ká yii u bíi ŋáań atuŋkpiti ní ki fātì u-boon ki tīī-ŋee, u làá nīn bí dimaŋfalin, waa làá kpú. 29Ama ní nimbi Isirayeel yab bí ki lì yii: <Tin ti-Dindaan ŋáańee kaa kítì!> Mimmee man nín ŋáań puee di kaa kítàaa? Nimbi nín ŋáań puee di kaa kítàa! 30An pu ní m làá sòoǹ nimbi Isirayeel niliu kamaa bɔti ubɔ ubɔ kí nóó nì u-tundi, man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ. Kpántímaan mbimbim, kí fàtīmaan ni-boon kí tīī ikpiti in kɔkɔ ni bí ki ŋáańee. Ní taa yàntī ikpiti iba ń kpántí ditaŋkpagbéetikaal kí tīī-ni. 31Fámaan atuŋkpiti ŋin ni ŋáańee, kpántímaan ni-pɔbiliŋ nì ni-landɔkɔi. Isirayeel yab, ba pu ní ni là kí kpú ní? 32Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti, m bíi lì yii maa là ubɔ kúm. Fàtīmaan ni-boon kí tīī ikpiti ní kí nīn bí dimaŋfalin!»

english_text:
A Funeral Song for Israel's Leaders
The Lord said:
1Ezekiel, sing a funeral song for two of Israel's leaders:
2Your mother was a brave lioness
who raised her cubs
among lions.
3She taught one of them to hunt,
and he learned to eat people.
4When the nations heard of him,
they trapped him in a pit,
then they used hooks
to drag him to Egypt.
5His mother waited
for him to return.
But soon she lost all hope
and raised another cub,
who also became fierce.
6He hunted with other lions
and learned to eat people.
7He destroyed fortresses
and ruined towns;
his mighty roar
terrified everyone.
8Nations plotted to kill him,
and people came from all over
to spread out a net
and catch him in a trap.
9They put him in a cage
and took him to Babylonia.
The lion was locked away,
so that his mighty roar
would never again be heard
on Israel's hills.
10Your mother was a vine like you,
growing near a stream.
There was plenty of water,
so she was filled with branches
and with lots of fruit.
11Her strong branches
became symbols of authority,
and she was taller
than all other trees—
everyone could see how strong
and healthy she was.
12But in anger, I pulled her up
by the roots
and threw her to the ground,
where the scorching desert wind
dried out her fruit.
Her strong branches wilted
and burned up.
13Then she was planted
in a hot, dry desert,
14where her stem caught fire,
and flames burned
her branches and fruit.
Not one strong branch is left;
she is stripped bare.
This funeral song must be sung with sorrow.
translation_text:
Gbikintib yaliŋkii
1Ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii ḿ gāā iyaliŋki laŋŋu nee kí tīī Isirayeel bɔtibiliŋ:
2«Ni-na nìn sá ugbikintinaati
ní ki bí gbikintib kansikin.
U nìn dɔ̀ agbikintipɔmbil kansikin
ní ki kpīintí u-biyaamu.
3U nìn péé u-biki kiba.
Kíǹ kpántì digbikintipɔmbilee,
ní ki bífì ki kíǹ ki ŋūǹ kí tɔ̀ntī kuwaŋkuluu,
ní ki cútì binib ki ŋmɔ́.
4Binicambi nìn gbìl̄ u-pu.
Bi nìn gbìn̄ mbòó ki sàl̄-u
ní ki dū dibɔmbil ki túuń u-maŋfal
ki cáá-u ki cūnnì Eejipiti tiŋkin.
5Ugbikintinaati kāl̀ ki cíitì ki gīī.
Ŋyunti ŋun u ká yii dimákal kaa ti bée,
ní u lēē u-biyaamu kansikin kiba.
U nìn dū-kì ki kpántì digbikintipɔmbil din cáá mpɔnee.
6U nìn kóò gbikintib kansikin
ní ki dūu kpántì digbikintipɔmbil.
U bífì ki ŋūǹ kí tɔ̀ntī kuwaŋkuluu
ní ki cútì binib ki ŋmɔ́.
7U nìn gbáń ki wīil̀ bi-gunlɔkɔŋ
ní ki nāaǹ bi-timmu.
Kitiŋee pu nib yaa nìn gbìl̄ u sūǹee,
dinyoondi nìn cútí-bi ní.
8Niinee atimbun nib kpáfì kí jáǹ-u,
anibul nìn nyánní an kɔkɔ pu.
Bi nìn dū kulaaŋŋu ki cúú-u
ní ki dū-u ki tɔ́ mbòó poon.
9Bi dū dibɔmbil ki lɔ̀kɔ̄-u
ní ki dū-u ki tɔ́ dikantandin
ki cáá-u ki cūnnì Babiloon bɔtiu cee.
Bi nìn dū-u ki tɔ́ sarkan kí taa ti gbìl̄ u-pu
yii u gbùkum̄ Isirayeel jooŋŋi pu.»
Bufiinyisubu yaliŋkii
10«Ni-na nìn náań nì bufiinyisubu
bun bi cóoǹ mbun caŋinee ní.
Bu nìn lòoǹ tiŋan ní ki cáá tifaal tikpil,
kun puee bu nìn kāntí nnyim tiŋan pu.
11Bu-paŋŋi nìn pɔ̄ɔ̄ tiŋan,
ní ki kpántì bibɔtiibi kpandɔŋu.
Bu nìn wíiǹ ki fɔ̄kɔǹ ki páaǹ isufi pu.
Bu-fɔkɔŋŋu nì bu-paŋŋi puee,
báà ŋma nìn wāĺ-bu ní.
12Ama ní bi fùkū-bu nì diŋuul poon
ki lúkú kitiŋ.
Ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú buŋku yāntì bu-biliŋ kūń ki lítì.
Bu-paŋŋi ŋin nìn pɔ̄ɔ̄yee kūń
ní ki wùn̄ ŋŋmi.
13Kɔŋkɔnnee, bi dū bufiinyisubu ki cóoǹ kuteeun,
kitiŋ kin kūń nnyim kpée.
14Ŋŋmi ŋubɔ nyáń bu-dɔŋu poon,
ŋu wùn̄ bu-paŋŋi nì bu-biliŋ.
Buaa ti cáá dipandi din pɔ̄ɔ̄
ki ŋūǹ kí kpántí ubɔti kpandɔŋuee.»
Bí nīn gà nlan nee kii bi nín gà ŋkpiisilan puee.

english_text:
Israel Keeps On Rebelling
1Seven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, some of Israel's leaders came to me on the tenth day of the fifth month. They sat down and asked for a message from the Lord. 2Just then, the Lord God said:
3Ezekiel, son of man, these leaders have come to find out what I want them to do. As surely as I live, I will not give them an answer of any kind.
4Are you willing to warn them, Ezekiel? Then remind them of the disgusting sins of their ancestors.
5 Tell them that long ago I, the Lord God, chose Israel to be my own. I appeared to their ancestors in Egypt and made a solemn promise that I would be their God and the God of their descendants. 6I swore that I would rescue them from Egypt and lead them to a land I had already chosen. This land was rich with milk and honey and was the most splendid land of all. 7I told them to get rid of their disgusting idols and not to sin by worshiping the gods of Egypt. I reminded them that I was the Lord their God, 8but they still rebelled against me. They refused to listen and kept on worshiping their idols and foreign gods.
In my anger, I decided to punish the Israelites in Egypt. 9But that would have made me look like a liar, because I had already promised in front of everyone that I would lead them out of Egypt. 10So I brought them out and led them into the desert. 11 I gave them my laws and teachings, so they would know how to live right. 12 And I commanded them to respect the Sabbath as a way of showing that they were holy and belonged to me. 13But the Israelites rebelled against me in the desert. They refused to obey my laws and teachings, and they treated the Sabbath like any other day.
Then in my anger, I decided to destroy the Israelites in the desert once and for all. 14But that would have disgraced me, because many other nations had seen me bring the Israelites out of Egypt. 15 Instead, I told them in the desert that I would not lead them into the beautiful, fertile land I had promised. 16I said this because they had not only ignored my laws and teachings, but had disgraced my Sabbath and worshiped idols.
17Yet, I felt sorry for them and could not let them die in the desert. 18So I warned the children not to act like their parents or follow their evil ways or worship their idols. 19I reminded them that I was the Lord their God and that they should obey my laws and teachings. 20I told them to respect my Sabbath to show that they were my people and that I was the Lord their God. 21But the children also rebelled against me. They refused to obey my laws and teachings, and they treated the Sabbath as any other day.
I became angry and decided to punish them in the desert. 22But I did not. That would have disgraced me in front of the nations that had seen me bring the Israelites out of Egypt. 23 So I solemnly swore that I would scatter the people of Israel across the nations, 24because they had disobeyed my laws and ignored my teachings; they had disgraced my Sabbath and worshiped the idols their ancestors had made. 25I gave them laws that bring punishment instead of life, 26and I let them offer me unacceptable sacrifices, including their first-born sons. I did this to horrify them and to let them know that I, the Lord, was punishing them.
27Ezekiel, tell the people of Israel that their ancestors also rejected and insulted me 28by offering sacrifices, incense, and wine to gods on every hill and under every large tree. I was very angry, because they did these things in the land I had given them! 29I asked them where they went to worship those gods, and they answered, “At the local shrines.” And those places of worship are still called shrines.
30Then ask the Israelites why they are following the example of their wicked ancestors 31by worshiping idols and by sacrificing their own children as offerings. They commit these sins and still think they can ask me for a message. As surely as I am the living Lord God, I will give them no answer. 32They may think they can be like other nations and get away with worshiping idols made of wood and stone. But that will never happen!
The Lord Promises To Restore Israel
The Lord said to the people of Israel:
33As surely as I am the living Lord God, I will rule over you with my powerful arm. You will feel my fierce anger 34and my power, when I gather you from the places where you are scattered 35and lead you into a desert surrounded by nations. I will meet you there face to face. Then I will pass judgment on you 36and punish you, just as I punished your ancestors in the desert near Egypt. 37I will force each of you to obey the regulations of our solemn agreement. 38I will separate the sinful rebels from the rest of you, and even though I will bring them from the nations where they live in exile, they won't be allowed to return to Israel. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
39Go ahead and worship your idols for now, you Israelites, because soon I will no longer let you dishonor me by offering gifts to them. You will have no choice but to obey me! 40When that day comes, everyone in Israel will worship me on Mount Zion, my holy mountain in Jerusalem. I will once again call you my own, and I will accept your sacred offerings and sacrifices. 41When I bring you home from the places where you are now scattered, I will be pleased with you, just as I am pleased with the smell of the smoke from your sacrifices. Every nation on earth will see that I am holy, 42and you will know that I, the Lord, am the one who brought you back to Israel, the land I promised your ancestors. 43Then you will remember your wicked sins, and you will hate yourselves for doing such horrible things. They have made you unacceptable to me, 44so you deserve to be punished. But I will treat you in a way that will bring honor to my name, and you will know that I am the Lord God.
Fire from the South
45The Lord said, 46“Ezekiel, son of man, turn toward the south and warn the forests 47that I, the Lord God, will start a fire that will burn up every tree, whether green or dry. Nothing will be able to put out the blaze of that fire as it spreads to the north and burns everything in its path. 48Everyone will know that I started it, and that it cannot be stopped.”
49But I complained, “Lord God, I don't want to do that! People already say I confuse them with my messages.”
translation_text:
Isirayeel kaa yúl̀ nì Unimbɔti deedee
1Bi nín cúú Isirayeel yab ki cūnnì kuyuŋu abin aluli boon, uŋmaŋmooŋmooti iwiin saalaa dalee, ní Isirayeel tindaŋkpilib biba dɔ́miń ki kāl̀ m-nimbiin kí bàlifì kí béé Unimbɔti lammi. 2Niinee ní ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: 3«Nisaaleen, tùkù Isirayeel tindaŋkpilib yii man bi-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Kéè ni dɔ́miń kí bàlifì kí béé m-lammi naa! Too, m nín bí dimaŋfalin nee, maa làá yàntī ní bàlifì-mi tiba, man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ.
4«Sii un sá nisaaleenee, a bɔ́ntì kí sòoǹ bi-bɔtaaa? Māafì-bi bi-baabi nín túń ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋiŋyee. 5Á tùkù-bi yii man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M nín lēē Isirayeelee, m nìn yōoǹ m-ŋal yilpu ki pūtì ki pōoǹ Jaakɔb naantiibi. M nìn yāntì bi béè-mi Eejipiti tiŋkin. M nìn yōoǹ m-ŋal yilpu ki pūtì ki lī yii: <Man di sá ni-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu.> 6Ŋwiin gbantee, m nìn yōoǹ m-ŋal yilpu ki pūtì kí nyāntí-bi Eejipiti tiŋkin kí cáá-bi kí kɔ́ǹ kitiŋ kin poon m nyàab̄ kí tīī-bee. Kitiŋ kin di ŋān̄ ki jítiǹ ntimu kɔkɔ nnaabiim nì tisiil còol̀ee. 7M nìn tīī-bi mara nee yii: <Ni-kɔkɔ ń dū ntimbiil waaŋi ŋin dátí-ni nee kí fá. Ní taa ti tòotī Eejipiti yab waaŋi nee kí kɔ́ǹ ni-ba tijɔkɔndi. Man di sá ni-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu>
8«Ama ní bi yíkìi jáń nì mi, ní kaa kíí kí pīlifiǹ-mi. Báà ubɔ kaa dū ntimbiil waaŋi ŋin nìn dátí-bee ki fá. Baa nìn dū Eejipiti waaŋee ki fá. M nìn ká nlandɔkɔ yii m làá kpáatí m-ŋuul kí sìtī bi-pu, kí ŋá kii m nín bí yii m làá ŋá puee kí cáá kátí Eejipiti tiŋkin niin. 9Ama man m-ba yindi puee ní maa nìn ŋá míǹ. Maa nìn là yii atimbun ŋin kansikin bi nìn kóòyee nib ń kpèè-mi fám. Di sá yii m nìn lēē m-ba ki dàkā-bi atimbun gbanti nimbiin ní ki pōoǹ yii m làá nyāntí-bi Eejipiti tiŋkin. 10Niinee ní m nyántìń-bi Eejipiti tiŋkin ki cáá-bi ki cūnnì kuteeun. 11M nìn dàkā-bi m-bɔkpaaŋi nì m-marab bin ní un yaa dūu túń ditundee kāntí dimaŋfalee. 12M nìn tīī-bi ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa án nīn sá kudaaŋŋu kí nīn bí man nì bi kansikin, án nín làá ŋá pu bí béé yii man di sá bi-Dindaan un di ŋáań-bi circiree. 13Ama Isirayeel yab nìn yíkìi jáń nì mi kuteeun. Baa nìn ŋúb́ m-bɔkpaaŋi ní ki dū m-marab bin tìì un ŋúb́-bee dimaŋfalee ki fá. Baa nìn tɔ́ ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dal. M nìn tí ká nlandɔkɔ yii m làá kpáatí m-ŋuul kí sìtī bi-pu kuteeun niin kí céetí-bi. 14Ama ní m tí kpēē m-yindi pu, án nín làá ŋá pu atimbun ŋin nib nìn ká m nín nyántìń-bi Eejipiti tiŋkinee ń taa kpèè m-yindi fámee. 15Ama, kuteeun niinee ní m pūtì yii maa làá cáá-bi kí kɔ́ǹ kitiŋ kin poon m bàà bí yii m làá tīī-bee, kitiŋ kin poon ní nnaabiim nì tisiil còol̀ee. 16M nìn pūtì kun puee bi nìn dū m-marab nì m-bɔkpaaŋi ki fá ní kaa nìn tɔ́ ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dal. Di sá yii bi nìn baasii dū bi-ba ki yá ki nákáǹ bi-waaŋee ní. 17Ama m nìn súń bi-saai ní kaa kūū ki céetì-bi kuteeun.
Isirayeel gbíntìi nìkì ki yìntīǹ Unimbɔti
18«M nìn tīī bi-biyaamu abɔkpaa nee kuteeun yii: <Ní taa nín̄ nóó abɔkpaa nì marab bin ni-baabi bi-ba mɔ́ɔ́yee. Ní taa tòotī awaa kí kɔ́ǹ ni-ba tijɔkɔndi. 19Man di sá ni-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu! Ní nīn nóó m-bɔkpaaŋi kí nīn tɔ́ m-marab kí dū-bi kí tɔ̄ ditundi. 20Ní dūmaan ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa dal kí sú-mi kí dàkà mpèé ŋun di bí man nì ni kansikinee, ní kí téetí yii man di sá ni-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu.> 21Ama bíǹ mun yíkì ki jáń nì mi. Baa nìn nóó m-bɔkpaaŋi ní kaa ŋúb́ m-marab bin ní unil máaǹ kí nīn ŋúb́ kí ŋmátée. Baa nìn tɔ́ ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa. Niinee ní m ká nlandɔkɔ yii m làá kpáatí m-bum kí sìtī bi-pu kuteeun, kí yàntī m-ŋuul ń tɔ̄ di-tundi kí tin cáá kátí. 22Ama m nìn tí cúú m-ba m-yindi pu, án nín làá ŋá pu atimbun ŋin nib ká-mi m nín nyántìń-bi Eejipiti tiŋkinee ń taa kpèè-mi fámee. 23Kuteeun niinee ní m yōoǹ m-ŋal ki pūtì yii m làá jà-bi kí yàl̄ atimbun aban nì ntincamun. 24Di sá yii baa nìn ŋúb́ m-bɔkpaaŋi nì m-marab, ní kaa tɔ́ ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa, ama ní ki nìn yāntì bi-baabi waaŋi dáaĺ-bi. 25Áli gba m nìn tīī-bi abɔkpaa ŋin kaa nìn ŋān̄ee nì marab bin kaa nìn ŋūǹ kí yàntī bí nīn bí dimaŋfalinee. 26M nìn yāntì bi kɔ́ǹ bi-ba tijɔkɔndi. Di sá yii bi nìn cáá bi-jipɔŋkpilib ki wù ŋŋmi ki ŋáań saraabi. M nìn là kí kɔ́ǹ-bi agìń poon bí béé yii man di sá bi-Dindaan ní.
Unimbɔti làá kúntí Isirayeel yab waatootii
27«An puee, nisaaleen, sòoǹ nì Isirayeel yab kí tùkù-bi tin man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti sòon̄ee. Ni-baabi nìn sīī-mi kaa nìn yúl̀ nì mi deedee. 28M nìn cáań-bi kitiŋ kin ní m nìn pōoǹ kí tīī-bee poon. Bi bāań ki kpēē ŋgbantamu puee ki ká isufi cáá tifaasɔn ní bi kíĺ ki bíi ŋáań saraabi niin. Bi nìn ŋá saraabi ki tūutì talaalub ní ki fá idafi ki gbítì m-ŋuul. 29Niinee ní m bālifì-bi yii: <Ba di sá iwaatootipaan in pu ni cá nee ní?> Kí yòon̄ ŋyunti gbanti ní bi kíǹ ki yíì ipaan gbanti yii iwaatootipaan. 30An puee á tùkù Isirayeel yab yii man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ yii: <Ní taa kɔ́ǹ ni-ba tijɔkɔndi kii ni-baabi nín nìn ŋá puee, kí taa nyā m-boon kí cùú nīn tòotī bi-timbiiliwaaŋi. 31Too kɔŋkɔnnee, ni yaa bíi ŋáań ni-saraabi ki yaa bíi wù ni-biyaamu ŋŋmi ki ŋáań saraabi ki tìì awaayee, ni bíi kɔ̄ntí ni-ba tijɔkɔndi dee. Ní ni dàkafī yii m làá kíí ní bàlifì-maaa, Isirayeel yab? Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín bí dimaŋfalin nee, maa làá kíí ní bàlifì-mi. 32Ni lì yii: <Ti là kí nīn bí kii atimbun ŋin kíǹee nín bí puee, a lì kii ntimu mun kíǹee nib nín bí puee. Ti là kí nīn tòotī isufi nì ataŋkpee. Ama an kaa làá ŋá kii ni nín dàkafī puee. 33Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín bí dimaŋfalin nee, m nín lī puee sɔ̀. M làá dàkà-ni m-pɔŋŋu nì m-kpabil ní kí kpáatí m-ŋuul kí sìtī ni-pu ní kí nín ŋmā kí jī ni-pu dibeel. 34M làá dàkà-ni m-pɔŋŋu nì m-kpabil nì m-ŋuul ní kí ŋmā kí nyāntí-ni atimbun nì ntimu mun poon ni yàl̄ee, ní kí kóoǹ-ni kí kpāfì. 35M làá cùnnì-ni kuteeun kí kàkatī-ni kí wàatī atimbun ŋin kíǹee, ní kí sòoǹ ni-bɔti niin. 36Kii m nín nìn sòon̄ ni-bɔti Eejipiti teekun puee, míǹ ní m làá sòoǹ ni-bɔti. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ. 37M làá dū m-kpandɔŋu ní kí kpàà-ni, ní kí yàntī ní nīn tɔ́ m-poondi. 38M làá nyāntí bin jáń nì mi kaa tɔ́-mee ni-kansikin. M làá nyāntiń-bi ntimu mun poon bi kóòyee, ama bi-taal kaa làá tāā Isirayeel tiŋkin. Niinee ni làá béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan.> 39Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Isirayeel yab, báà ŋma ŋūǹ kí tòotī u-waaŋi, ama míǹ boonee, ni là kaa là, ní làá dāá nīn tɔ́-mi ní. Ní taa kpèè m-circir yindi fám kí nīn ŋáań saraabi ki tìì ni-waaŋi. 40Di sá yii Isirayeel yab, ni-kɔkɔ làá dāá jāam̀-mi m-circir jool pu, Isirayeel joofɔkɔl pu. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ. Niin ní m làá dāá fōō-ni nì iŋal ili ní kí dāá fōō tin ni dūu sú-mee, ni-wampɔkaati nì ni-saraamɔntiibi. 41M yaa láa nyántìń-ni atimbun kansikin nì ntimu mun poon ni yàl̄ee ki kóoǹ-ni ki kpáfì ki dóòyee ní ḿ dāá fōō ni-saraabi bí nīn sɔ́fì ki sɔ̀ŋkī m-pɔbil. M yaa ŋá-ni mimmee, m dàkā atimbun ŋin kíǹee yii m sá circir Nimbɔtiu dee. 42M làá dāá gíiǹní-ni Isirayeel tiŋkin, kitiŋ kin ní m yōoǹ m-ŋal yilpu ki pūtì kí tīī ni-baabee. Ŋyunti gbantee, ni làá béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan. 43Niinee, ni làá dāá téetí ni-bimbim nì atuun ŋin kɔkɔ ni ŋá ki kɔ́ǹ ni-ba tijɔkɔndee pu. Atuŋkpiti ŋin kɔkɔ ni ŋée puee, ni-naŋki làá dāá nyā nì ni-ba. 44Isirayeel yab, an kaa sá ni-bimbikpitim nì ni-jɔkɔntuuŋŋi ní m làá kpèè, ama m-yindi pu ní m làá ŋá míǹ kí tīī-ni. Niinee ni làá béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan, man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ.>»

english_text:
The Lord Will Punish Jerusalem
1The Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the places in Jerusalem where people worship. Warn everyone in Israel 3that I am about to punish them. I will pull out my sword and have it ready to kill everyone, whether good or evil. 4From south to north, people will die, 5knowing that my sword will never be put away.
6Ezekiel, groan in sorrow and despair so that everyone can hear you. 7When they ask why you are groaning, tell them you have terrifying news that will make them faint and tremble in fear and lose all courage. These things will happen soon. I, the Lord God, make this promise!
A Sword Is Ready To Attack Israel
8The Lord said:
9-10Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Jerusalem:
I have sharpened my sword
to slaughter you;
it is shiny and will flash
like lightning!
Don't celebrate—
punishment is coming,
because everyone has ignored
my warnings.
11My sword has been polished;
it's sharp and ready to kill.
12Groan in sorrow, Ezekiel;
the sword is drawn against
my people and their leaders.
They will die!
So give up all hope.
13I am testing my people,
and they can do nothing
to stop me.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
14Ezekiel, warn my people,
then celebrate my victory
by clapping your hands.
My vicious sword will attack
again and again,
killing my people
with every stroke.
15They will lose all courage
and stumble with fear.
My slaughtering sword
is waiting at every gate,
flashing and ready to kill.
16It will slash right and left,
wherever the blade is pointed.
17Then I will stop being angry,
and I will clap my hands
in victory.
I, the Lord, have spoken.
The King of Babylonia and His Sword
18The Lord said:
19Ezekiel, son of man, mark two roads for the king of Babylonia to follow when he comes with his sword. The roads will begin at the same place, but be sure to put up a signpost where the two roads separate and go in different directions. 20Clearly mark where the two roads lead. One goes to Rabbah, the capital of Ammon, and the other goes to Jerusalem, the fortified capital of Judah. 21When the Babylonian king stands at that signpost, he will decide which way to go by shaking his arrows, by asking his idols, and by carefully looking at the liver of a sacrificed animal. 22His right hand will pull out the arrow marked “Jerusalem.” Then he will immediately give the signal to shout the battle cry, to build dirt ramps up to the top of the city walls, to break down its walls and gates with large wooden poles, and to kill the people. 23Everyone in Jerusalem had promised to be loyal to Babylonia, and so none of them will believe that this could happen to them. But Babylonia's king will remind them of their sinful ways and warn them of their coming captivity.
24Ezekiel, tell the people of Jerusalem and their ruler that I, the Lord God, am saying:
Everything you do is wicked and shows how sinful you are. You are guilty and will be taken away as prisoners.
25And now, you evil and wicked ruler of Israel, your day of final punishment is almost here. 26I, the Lord God, command you to take off your royal turban and your crown, because everything will be different. Those who had no power will be put in charge, and those who now rule will become nobodies. 27I will leave Jerusalem in complete ruins like no one has ever seen until my chosen one comes to punish this city.
Judgment against Ammon
28 The Lord God said:
Ezekiel, son of man, the Ammonites have insulted Israel, so condemn them and tell them I am saying:
A sword is drawn,
ready to slaughter;
it is polished and prepared
to kill as fast as lightning.
29You wicked Ammonites see false visions and believe untrue messages. But your day of punishment is coming soon, and my sword will slaughter you!
30Your days to punish others are over, so put your swords away. You will be punished in the land of your birth. 31My furious anger will scorch you like fire, and I will hand you over to cruel men who are experts in killing. 32You will be burned and will die in your own land. Then you will be forgotten forever. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
Atulim bɔti tin sá ki tīī Isirayeel yabee
1Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii: 2«Nisaaleen, fàtī a-nimbiin kí túĺ ŋgiil pú. Sòoǹ kí tɔ̄ dijandi gbanti pu, ní kí dū m-bɔti kí nàatī binib bin kóò Neegeeb bambaŋkunee. 3Á tùkù-bi yii bí pīlifì tin man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti cáá kí sòoǹ kí tɔ̄ ŋgiil pú bambaŋku puee. M làá tūū ŋŋmi ni-kansikin ní ŋú wà kí céetí isufi in sɔ̀m̀ee nì in kūńee kɔkɔ. Aŋmilimbil kaa làá kpú, ní án làá wà báà ŋma, kí yòon̄ ŋgiil pú kí cáá sāā ŋgan pú. 4Báà ŋma làá dāá wāl̀ yii man ni-Dindaan di tūū ŋŋmi gbanti ní ubɔ kaa dāa ŋūǹ kí gbíntí-ŋu.» 5Ní m kíí yii: «Áù ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti, bi bí ki yáliŋkí m-pu ki lì yii: <Alaŋkpan ŋma ní u pée nyí ki gà.>»
6Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii: 7«Nisaaleen, fàtī a-nimbiin kí túĺ Jeerusaleem tiŋki, kí sòoǹ kí tɔ̄ circir kɔŋkooŋŋu pu. Fōō m-bɔti kí nàatī Isirayeel yab. 8Tùkù Isirayeel yab yii ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <M làá jáǹ-ni, m làá dáaĺ m-tàataajiki kí fúutí kujitooun ní kí kpɔ̀ deedeedaan nì unikpiti kɔkɔ. 9M nín làá kpɔ̀ deedeedaan nì unikpiti puee pu ní m làá fúutí m-tàataajiki kujitooun kí tàntī-kì ni-kɔkɔ pu, kí yòon̄ ŋgiil pú kí cáá sāā ŋgan pú. 10Báà ŋma làá béé yii man, ni-Dindaan di fúutì m-tàataajiki kujitooun. Maa làá fàtīí gíiǹ-kì kí fúuń.> 11An puee, sii nisaaleen, nín̄ yáliŋkí. Nín̄ yáliŋkí nì dipɔɔbiildi poon nì ntuntun bi-kɔkɔ nimbiin. 12Bi yaa láa bālifì-si yii ba pu ní a yáliŋkée, á kíí-bi yii: <M gbìl̄ atulim bɔti tin dòońee pu. Báà ŋma pɔbil làá bīil̀, iŋal kɔkɔ làá kpú, binib landɔkɔi làá gátí ní bi-tabiŋyiliŋ làá nīn jìkì. Ŋyunti bāań! Án làá pée ŋá míǹ ní kɔŋkɔnnee, ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ.>»
Ti-Dindaan tàataajiki
13Ti-Dindaan gíti tí sòon̄ nì mi yii: 14«Nisaaleen, fōō m-bɔti kí nàatī. Tùkù binib tin man ni-Dindaan bíi sòoǹ nì bee.
Kitàataajiki kiba sɔ̀,
kitàataajiki kin jītí ki jìl̀ pàlpalee.
15Bi lōoǹ-kì kí pɔ̀fì binib ní,
bi pítì-kì kí nīn jìl̀ ní.
16M dū-kì ki tīī bí pítí-kì
kí ŋmā kí dū-kì kí tɔ̄ ditundi.
Bi lōoǹ-kì kì jìl̀ pàlpal
kí dū-kì kí ŋúbíǹ un làá kpɔ̀ binibee ní.
17Nisaaleen, fáá dinimbinaamandi biilii!
Bi tāntì kitàataajiki gbanti m-nibul
nì abɔtibil ŋin kɔkɔ kpòotī Isirayeel tiŋkee pu ní.
Bi làá kpɔ̀-bi kí kpáaǹ m-nibul.
Fáá a-bindi kí dàkà a-nimbaaku.
18An sá icɔŋki in pɔ̄ɔ̄yee ní.
Ba di làá jītí ŋyunti ŋun ní
mbɔtikpandɔ ŋun kaa bí tibanee gíti kpée?
Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee dee.
19Sii nisaaleenee, fōō m-bɔti kí nàatī.
Kpāafì abaal,
diba, mili, mita pu,
di sá yii ŋkúm tàataajiki dee,
kitàataajiki kin di làá pɔ̀fì binib
ki māntìi tú-bi an kɔkɔ puee.
20Kì làá bīil̀ bi-pɔbil kí yàntī bí lítí tikpil.
M dū ŋkúm tàataajiki ki bíl̀ mpunyɔmu kɔkɔ pu.
Bi bɔ́ntì-kì kí nīn jìl̀ ní,
bi lōoǹ-kì kí ŋmā kí pɔ̀fì binib ní.
21Kitàataajiki kin jītí pámpamee,
pɔ̀fì binib ŋgan pú nì ŋgiil pú.
Fàtī a-nyɔkɔ kin cɔ́m̀ee an kɔkɔ pú.
22Ma mun làá kpāafì abaal ní kí yàntī m-ŋuul ń tɔ̄ di-tundi. Man ni-Dindaan di sòon̄.»
Bi bíi jáà nì Jeerusaleem tiŋki
23Ti-Dindaan bí yii: 24«Nisaaleen, cátí adan ali ŋin pu ní Babiloon bɔtiu tàataajiki làá ŋmā kí dī kí dāan̄ee. Adan alee làá nyānní kitimbaantiin ní. Didandi kamaa kílilaŋkee, ní ŋmà kupiliŋu pu kitiŋ kin poon ní di cée yindi. 25Cátí didandi din pu ní Babiloon janjaliibi làá dī kí cù Amɔn yab tiŋki Raabee, ní didandi din kíǹee ń nīn cá Jeerusaleem tiŋki kin bi máń digundi ki tú kì bí Juuda tiŋkinee. 26Babiloon bɔtiu síl̀ isampuyakati, laakin adan alee kífée kí bɔ̄ tibɔɔl. U cīkifì ipiin, ki bālifì awaa ki kpēē tiwaŋkuti pɔɔŋi címmm. 27Mpiin ŋun dàkà Jeerusaleemee lítì u-ŋaŋgiilin. U làá pɔ̄ kinyɔkɔ bí cùú kpɔ̀ binib bin bí niinee ní kí fáá iwinliili bí kíĺ kujaau. U làá dū kujaau masiimbi kí gbàan̄ kitiŋ punyɔmmu pu, kí mā agun ŋin boon bi làá nīn bāal̀ ki jáà kujaauee, ní kí gbà abɔbil ŋin poon bi làá nīn kàal̀ ki jáàyee. 28Jeerusaleem yab dākafì yii bi nín bālifì an cúú Jeerusaleemee kaa sá tiba, di sá yii bi pūtì yii bi làá wúń bi-pu. Ama ní Babiloon bɔtiu bíi téetí-bi bi nín kaa yúl̀ nì ti-Dindaan deedeeyee pu. An puee u làá cúú-bi kí cùnnì kuyuŋu. 29An puee man bi-Dindaan Unimbɔti bíi sòoǹ nì bi tin bí nee yii: <Ni pée téetí-mi ni-yìntitam nì ni-kpitii pu ní kaa gbèentí. Ni-tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ poonee, ni-kpitii pée nyáń ní ki pá mpaampiin pu. Too, ni nín kaa yàntī bí súntí ni-puee puee, ni làá kɔ́ unannanli ŋaan.
30«Sii dibɔtibil din di kā Isirayeel tiŋki pu dibeel kaa yú deedee ki sá unikpitee, ŋwiin ŋun ní a-kpitii làá gbèen̄ee dòoń. 31Man a-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Bi làá fōō ŋŋaabu ŋun dàkà yii a sá ubɔtee ní kí cíkití a-beefuuliiki. Tiwan làá kpántí ti-paaŋyi! Bi làá yòon̄ un nìn sīntì u-ba taapuee yilpu, ní kí sìntī un nìn yōoǹ u-ba yilpuee taapu. 32Adigbuŋkati, adigbuŋkati ŋma! M làá yàntī Jeerusaleem ń kpántí adigbuŋkati ŋma. M tīī ubɔ mpɔn ú jáǹ-kì. Bi làá yàaǹ Jeerusaleem tiŋki kɔkɔ, ama see un m tīī mpɔn gbantee ń bàń kí wàatī.»
Bi làá jáǹ Amɔn yab
33«Nisaaleen, sòoǹ m-bɔti kí nàatī Amɔn yab. Sòoǹ nì bi yii ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ Amɔn yab nì bi nín sīī Isirayeel yab pu puee sèé, yii: <Kitàataajiki! kitàataajiki! bi fúutì-kì kujitooun. Bi lōoǹ-kì kí dūú kpɔ̀ binib, kí tɔ̀ntī binib ní kí nīn bí ki ŋmóò làka laka. 34Ŋyunti ŋun ni kā ki máká inyimɔn leedakaŋ nì bi nín sòon̄ ki nāatì-ni tinyimɔmbɔti puee, kitàataajikee kíǹ bɔ́ntì kí tùkutī binikpitib nì bikpitiŋaliibi yiliŋ dee. Di sá yii ŋyunti ŋun ní bi-tuŋkpitiŋ làá gbèen̄ee dee.> 35Kɔŋkɔnnee, gíim̀maan ni-tàataajimmu kí fúuń mu-jitootin. M làá sòoǹ ni-bɔti laakin bi náań-nee, kitiŋ kin poon bi màl̄-nee ní. 36M làá kpáatí m-ŋuul kí sìtī ni-pu. M làá dū m-ŋuul ŋmiŋu kí tɔ̄ ni-pu, ní kí dū-ni kí ŋá kìrikiri nib ŋaan, binib bin tundi pée sá yii bí nīn kù ki céetée ŋaan. 37Ŋŋmi di làá wà-ni ní ni-fatikuu ń nīn pùub̀ kitiŋ nee kɔkɔn. Míǹ boonee ubɔ kaa ti làá téetí ni-pu. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄.»

english_text:
Jerusalem Is Condemned
1Some time later, the Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, are you ready to condemn Jerusalem? That city is filled with murderers, so remind the people of their sins 3and tell them I am saying:
Jerusalem, you have murdered many of your own people and have worshiped idols. You will soon be punished! 4Those crimes have made you guilty, and the idols have made you unacceptable to me. So your final punishment is near. Other nations will laugh at you and make insulting remarks, 5and people far and near will make fun of your misery.
6Your own leaders use their power to murder. 7 None of you honor your parents, and you cheat foreigners, orphans, and widows. 8 You show no respect for my sacred places and treat the Sabbath just like any other day. 9Some of your own people tell lies, so that others will be put to death. Some of you eat meat sacrificed to idols at local shrines, and others never stop doing vulgar things. 10 Men have sex with their father's wife or with women who are having their monthly period 11or with someone else's wife. Some men even sleep with their own daughter-in-law or half sister. 12 Others of you accept money to murder someone. Your own people charge high interest when making a loan to other Israelites, and they get rich by cheating. Worst of all, you have forgotten me, the Lord God.
13I will shake my fist in anger at your violent crimes. 14When I'm finished with you, your courage will disappear, and you will be so weak that you won't be able to lift your hands. I, the Lord, have spoken and will not change my mind. 15I will scatter you throughout every nation on earth and put a stop to your sinful ways. 16You will be humiliated in the eyes of other nations. Then you will know that I, the Lord God, have done these things.
Jerusalem Must Be Purified
17The Lord said:
18Ezekiel, son of man, I consider the people of Israel as worthless as the leftover metal in a furnace after silver has been purified. 19So I am going to bring them together in Jerusalem. 20-21I will be like a metalworker who collects that metal from the furnace and melts it down. I will collect the Israelites and blow on them with my fiery anger. They will melt inside the city of Jerusalem 22like silver in a furnace. Then they will know that I, the Lord, have punished them in my anger.
Everyone in Jerusalem Is Guilty
23The Lord said:
24Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Israel that their country is full of sin, and that I, the Lord, am furious! 25Their leaders are like roaring lions, tearing apart their victims. They put people to death, then steal everything of value. Husbands are killed, and many women are left as widows.
26 The priests of Israel ignore my Law! Not only do they refuse to respect any of my sacred things, but they don't even teach the difference between what is sacred and what is ordinary or between what is clean and what is unclean. They treat my Sabbath like any other day, and so my own people no longer honor me.
27Israel's officials are like ferocious wolves, ripping their victims apart. They make a dishonest living by injuring and killing people.
28And then the prophets in Israel cover up these sins by giving false visions. I have never spoken to them, but they lie and say they have a message from me. 29The people themselves cheat and rob; they abuse the poor and take advantage of foreigners.
30I looked for someone to defend the city and to protect it from my anger, as well as to stop me from destroying it. But I found no one. 31So in my fierce anger, I will punish the Israelites for what they have done, and they will know that I am furious. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
Jeerusaleem yab timbiilituuŋŋi
1Ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: 2«Nisaaleen, bɔ́ntí a-ba kí sòoǹ Jeerusaleem, nnikpaakoon tiŋki nee bɔti, á taa gùgufì! Yàntī kí béé ki-tuŋkpitiŋ. 3Dū tin man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti tùkū-see kí nàatī-kì yii: <A sá kitiŋ kin nib kù binibee. Bi nín bíi ŋáań mimmee, bi bíi bɔ́ntí a-nàantam yuntiŋu dee. Bi bí ki māā awaa ki kɔ̄ntí-si tijɔkɔndi. 4Binib bin bi kūūyee puee, a jíń dibɔkpil. Binib bin kóò a-nee nín máń awaa ŋiŋyee puee, a kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi. Bi nín ŋá mimmee puee, a sútìń a-bɔsooŋyi wiiŋŋu dee, bi làá nàan̄-si án kaa ti làá yúntí! An pu ní m làá kɔ́ǹ-si icoo anibul ŋin kíǹee nimbiin, ntimu kɔkɔ nib làá bèel̀-si. 5A sá tijɔkɔndi nì fikil fikil tiŋki ní. An puee bin pìlīǹ-see nì bin dátiǹ-see làá bèel̀-si.>
6«Sii cee ní Isirayeel bɔtibiliŋ cáá mpɔn ŋun bi cááyee ki kù binib. 7Sii cee ní unil kpèé u-baa nì u-na fám, ki mùul̄ unicaan ní ki wɔ́b̀ ataŋkpiibil nì bikpiipoobi. 8Baa dū tin bi dūu sú-mee ki yíiń tiba, ní kaa tɔ́ ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa. 9Sii cee ní binib tūntí bi-jutiibi abɔgabil kí ŋmā kí kpɔ̀-bi. A-nib jīǹ tiwaajin ajoon pu ní ki ŋáań ajɔkɔntuun. 10Biba dɔ̀ nì bi-baa nimpoobi, ní biba mun dɔ̀ nì binimpoobi ŋyunti ŋun bi bíi fùul̀ ŋkpinee. 11Biba ŋáań ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ki dɔ̀ nì bi-jutiibi nimpoobi, biba mun ŋáań mpɔn ki dɔ̀ nì bi-jipɔmbi nimpoobi, àá bi-niisalib pēē baa. 12Sii cee ní unil kíikí bí tīī-u animbil ú kpɔ̀ u-juti. Unil yaa pīnnì u-juti animbilee, u nyàab̀ udaan ń dāá téeǹ-u kí páań ní. Binib bí ki fìkì bi-jutiibi wanti kí ŋmā kí kpántí bigaajab ní kí súntí man pu kpataaa. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ.
13«Ma mun làá kpāafì abaal kí jáǹ-ni ni-paatii in kaa sá tibulcin paatiiyee, nì nnikpaakoon tuuŋŋi ŋin ni ŋáaǹee pu. 14Ŋwiin ŋun m làá dāá jáǹ-nee, ni làá dāá ká mpɔn nì dipɔbil kí yūĺ m-nimbiinaaa? Man ni-Dindaan di sòon̄, ní m yaa sòon̄ puee, míǹ ní m ŋáań. 15M làá jà-ni kí yàl̄ atimbun ŋin kíǹee poon ntincamun, ní kí kúntí ni-jɔkɔntuuŋŋi kɔkɔ. 16Ni làá fá ni-jilmau atimbun ŋin kíǹee cee, ama ni làá béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan.»
17Ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: 18«Nisaaleen, pīlifì. Isirayeel kpántì m-cee kii agɔŋgɔŋkpilee ní. Bi bí kii animbil nì tasa kúti nì tikúnyuntikaal nì tikúti nì tikúbɔn tin nyìm̀ ki kā ucaa ŋmiŋunee ní. 19An pu ní man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti sòon̄ yii: <Ni kpántì kii agɔŋgɔŋkpil ŋin kaa bí tibanee ní. An puee m làá kóoǹ-ni kí kpúkuń Jeerusaleem tiŋki kansikin. 20Bi kōontí animbil kúti nì tasa kúti nì tikúti nì tikúbɔn nì tikúman kí ŋá ucaa ŋmiŋun ní kí fùkum̀ ŋŋmi ní an kɔkɔ ń dùntī. Too, m-ŋuukpaandi poonee, m làá kóoǹ ni-mun kí kpúkuń ní kí yàntī ŋŋmi ń dùntī-ni. 21M làá kóoǹ-ni kí kpāfì Jeerusaleem tiŋkin táb ní kí yàntī m-ŋuul ŋmiŋu ń wà-ni ní dùntī kii tikútee. 22Ni làá nīn bí kii animbil kúti tin bi dūntì kipaai poonee ní. Niinee ni làá dāá béé yii man ni-Dindaan di kpáatì m-ŋuul ki sītì ni-pu.>»
23Ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: 24«Nisaaleen, tùkù Jeerusaleem tiŋki yii kì sá kitiŋ kin kaa ŋá ki-ba circiree ní, kitiŋ kin pu utaa kaa nìn̄ m-ŋuul dalee. 25A-bɔnaatiliibi bí kii gbikinti un nimbiliŋ máǹ ú cúú kuwaŋkuluu kí tɔ̀ntēe ní. Míǹ ní bi tɔ̀ntī binib, ki fòol̄ bi-gaajati nì bi-wammɔntiiti, ní ki yāntì bi-kpiipoobi wíiǹ kitiŋ nee poon. 26Bi-saraaŋaliibi nyēē m-marab boon ní kaa tɔ́ m-circir paaŋyi. Baa gàntī tin bí circiree nì tin kaa bí circiree. Baa dàkà binib bí ŋmā kí gàntī tin sá tijɔkɔndee nì tin kaa sá tijɔkɔndee. Baa pée fātìi tɔ́ iwiŋŋuŋfikaa. Bi-puee baa tìì-mi tinyool. 27Bitindaŋkpilib bí kii agbiŋgbil ŋin di cúú kuwaŋkuluu kí tɔ̀ntēe ní. Bi kù binib kí kpántí bigaajab. 28Bi-bɔnaatiliibi bìintí tíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ pu kii bi nín pōontí digundi puee ní. Bi kāntí aleedaka ŋin kaa sá ibaamɔn leedakaŋee ní ki sòoǹ ki nàatī tinyimɔmbɔti. Bi lì yii bi fòol̄ man cee tibɔti ní ki cáa nàatī, ama ní man ni-Dindaan kaa sòon̄ nì bi. 29Kitiŋ nee kɔkɔ poonee, binib dàkà dikpabil ní ki yù. Bi mùul̄ usoodaan nì unandaan ní ki wɔ́b̀ unicaan, kaa nóó ibaamɔn saŋŋu. 30M nyàab̄ bi-kansikin ubɔ ń bàà mā digundi, kí yūĺ laakin digundi bátìi lítì dibundi dōoǹee kí mɔ̄tì kitiŋ nee pu m-ŋuul ń taa bīil̀-kèe, ama maa ká báà ubɔ. 31Niinee ní m kpáatì m-ŋuul ki sītì bi-pu. M nāaǹ-bi m-ŋuul ŋmiŋu poon ní ki pàn̄-bi bi-tuŋkpitiŋ paati. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄.»

english_text:
Two Sinful Sisters
1The Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, listen to this story about two sisters. 3While they were young and living in Egypt, they became prostitutes. 4The older one was named Oholah, which stands for Samaria; the younger one was Oholibah, which stands for Jerusalem. They became my wives and gave birth to my children.
5Even though Oholah was my wife, she continued to be a prostitute and chased after Assyrian lovers. 6She offered herself to soldiers in purple uniforms: handsome, high-ranking officers and cavalry troops. 7She had sex with all the important Assyrian officials and even worshiped their disgusting idols. 8Once she started doing these things in Egypt, she never stopped. Men slept with her, and she was always ready for sex.
9So I gave Oholah to the Assyrian lovers she wanted so badly. 10They ripped off her clothes, then captured her children and killed her. Women everywhere talked about what had happened to Oholah.
11Oholibah saw all this, but she was more sinful and wanted sex more than her sister Oholah ever did. 12Oholibah also chased after good-looking Assyrian officers, uniformed soldiers, and cavalry troops. 13Just like her sister, she did vulgar things.
14But Oholibah behaved worse than her sister. Oholibah saw images of Babylonian men carved into walls and painted red. 15They had belts around their waists and large turbans on their heads, and they reminded her of Babylonian cavalry officers. 16As soon as she looked at them, she wanted to have sex with them. And so, she sent messengers to bring them to her. 17Men from Babylonia came and had sex with her so many times that she got disgusted with them. 18She let everyone see her naked body and didn't care if they knew she was a prostitute. That's why I turned my back on her, just as I had done with her older sister.
19Oholibah didn't stop there, but became even more immoral and acted as she had back in Egypt. 20She eagerly wanted to go to bed with Egyptian men, who were famous for their sexual powers. 21And she longed for the days when she was a young prostitute, when men enjoyed caressing her body.
The Lord Will Punish Oholibah
22The Lord God said:
Oholibah, though you no longer want to be around your lovers, they will surround you like enemies, when I turn them against you. 23I will gather all the handsome young officials and the high-ranking cavalry officers from Babylonia and Assyria, as well as from the Chaldean tribes of Pekod, Shoa, and Koa. 24Their large armies will come from the north with chariots and wagons carrying weapons. They will wear shields and helmets and will surround you, and I will let them judge and sentence you according to their own laws. 25I am angry with you, so I will let them be very cruel. They will cut off your nose and ears; they will kill your children and burn alive anyone in your family who survives. 26Your clothes and jewelry will be torn off. 27I will stop your wickedness and the prostitution you started back in Egypt. You will never want to think about those days again.
28I, the Lord God, am ready to hand you over to those hateful enemies that you find so disgusting. 29They will cruelly take away everything you have worked for and strip you naked. Then everyone will see you for the prostitute you really are. Your own vulgar sins 30have led to this. You were the one determined to have sex with men from other nations and to worship their idols. 31You have turned out no better than your older sister, and now you must drink from the cup filled with my anger.
32I, the Lord God, gave your sister a large, deep cup filled with my anger. And when you drink from that cup, you will be mocked and insulted. 33You will end up drunk and devastated, because that cup is filled with horror and ruin. 34But you must drink every drop! Then smash the cup and chew on its broken pieces. Use them to cut your breasts in sorrow. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
35You have completely rejected me, and so I promise that you will be punished for the disgusting things you did as a prostitute.
The Two Sisters Are Condemned
36The Lord said:
Ezekiel, son of man, it's time for you to tell Oholah and Oholibah that they are guilty. Remind them of their evil ways! 37They have been unfaithful by worshiping idols, and they have committed murder by sacrificing my own children as offerings to idols. 38-39They came into my temple that same day, and that made it unfit as a place to worship me. They have even stopped respecting the Sabbath.
40They sent messengers to attract men from far away. When those men arrived, the two sisters bathed themselves and put on eye shadow and jewelry. 41They sat on a fancy couch, and in front of them was a table for the olive oil and incense that had belonged to me. 42Their room was always filled with a noisy crowd of drunkards brought in from the desert. These men gave the women bracelets and beautiful crowns, 43and I noticed that the men were eager to have sex with these women, though they were exhausted from being prostitutes. 44In fact, the men had sex over and over with Oholah and Oholibah, the two sinful sisters. 45But honest judges will someday accuse those two of murder and of being unfaithful, because they are certainly guilty.
46So I, the Lord God, now say to these sisters:
I will call together an angry mob that will abuse and rob you. 47They will stone you to death and cut you to pieces; they will kill your children and burn down your houses. 48I will get rid of sinful prostitution in this country, so that women everywhere will be warned not to act as you have. 49You will be punished for becoming prostitutes and for worshiping idols. Then you will know that I am the Lord God.
translation_text:
Samaarii ŋá tilaakpaal
1Ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: 2«Nisaaleen, binimpoobi bili di bí ki pēē na. 3Bi nín nìn sá bisapɔmbee, bi nìn kpántì nlaakpaamu Eejipiti tiŋki kin poon bi nìn kóòyee. Niin ní bininjab ŋmáaḿ ŋmáaḿ bi-biiŋi ní ki ŋmáliŋkì bi-bindi din sá disapɔmbindee. 4Bi nìn yíì ukpil yii Ooyoola ní ki yíì uwaal yii Ooyooliiba. Ukpilee, Samaarii dee, ní uwaal sá Jeerusaleem. Man di nìn cáab́-bi ní bi màl̄-mi mbininjabiyaamu nì nnimpubiyaamu. 5Min kamaa man di yì Ooyoolayee, u nìn kpántì kinimpulaakpaai. U nìn cáá kukpeeu ki néeń u-bɔmbi, Asuur yab bijanjaliibi 6bin pēē abɔkutiman cínciŋee nì gɔminab nì kɔmandambi nì binaacimpɔmbi bin ŋān̄ee nì bitanjakaliibi. 7Ooyoola nìn néeń Asuur yab kàliŋkpaambi gbanti ní ki nìn kɔ̄ntí u-ba tijɔkɔndi ki tòotī bin kɔkɔ u nìn pée néeńee waaŋi. 8U nín nìn bí Eejipiti tiŋkin ki kíĺ alaakpaatuun ŋiŋyee, ŋíǹ ní u gbíntìi nìkì. U nín nìn bí niin ki sá usapɔɔnee, bininjab nìn dɔ̀ nì u ní ki ŋúb́ u-sapɔmbiiŋi ki ŋmáliŋkí ní ki kɔ́ǹ-u ajɔkɔntuun poon. 9Niinee ní m dū-u ki ŋá u-bɔmbi, Asuur yab bin u nìn lèe ŋaan. 10Bíǹ cúú-u ki pēetì ní ki yōoǹ u-jipɔmbi nì u-sapɔmbi ní ki dū kitàataajiki ki kūū-u. Míǹ ní bi nìn dáaĺ u-tafal ní u kpántì ŋabika ki tīī binimpoobi bin kíǹee.»
Jeerusaleem ŋá tilaakpaal
11«U-naal Ooyooliiba ká tíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ. Ama u-kpeeku poonee, úǹ gíti kɔ́ tijɔkɔndin ki jítiǹ Ooyoola. Úǹ gíti ŋá alaakpaatuun ki jítiǹ u-maan gba. 12U mun nìn néeń Asuur yab ní, gɔminab nì kɔmandambi nì bijanjaliibi bin pēē tiwannyaandee nì bitanjakaliibi nì binaacimpɔmbi bin ŋān̄ee. 13U mun nìn dū u-ba ki múĺ tijɔkɔndin. M nìn ká yii bi-liitil dī nsambaanti ní. 14Ama Ooyooliiba úǹ nìn gíti ŋá tilaakpaal kí jítiǹ u-maan. Dalbee ní u ká bi lēē bininjab ki nákáǹ digundi pu ki dū peentaman ki kɔ̀l̄-bi. Bininjab gbanti nìn sá Babiloon yab ní. 15Bi nìn dū dambalab ki gbìn̄ bi-cammu ní ki dū ŋŋaabu ki fìn̄ bi-yiliŋ. Bin nìn náań nì bibaatandambi binyaambi. Babiloon yab nín pée bí pu bi-dumpuee ní bi nìn lēē ki nákáǹ. 16Ooyooliiba nín pée wál̀-bi yéèyee ní bi kɔ́-u ní u tú binib bi-cee bi-tiŋkin. 17Niinee ní Babiloon yab dɔ́miń ki dōoǹ nì u. Bi nìn kɔ́ǹ-u tijɔkɔndi. Ŋyunti ŋun bi bíil̀-u kpataaayee, ní u kíǹ ki ná-bi. 18U ŋá alaakpaatuun báà ŋma nimbiin ki yāntì báà ŋma wál̀ u-cancaŋgbeel. Niinee ní m fātì m-boon ki tīī-u kii m nín fātì m-boon ki tīī u-maan puee. 19Ama ní u mɔ̀tīi múl̀ alaakpaatuunni ní ki ŋáań ajɔkɔntuun kii ŋyunti ŋun u sá usapɔɔn ki bí Eejipiti tiŋkinee. 20U nìn néeń bilaakpaadambi bin di bí kii ipeelee. Mmamu nì itaamu sɔ́ǹ-bi.»
Jeerusaleem tafadaaldi
21«Ooyooliiba, a kíĺ ki bíi ŋáań ajɔkɔntuun kii a-sapɔntin ŋyunti ŋun a nìn yàntī Eejipiti yab ŋmáliŋkí a-bindi ki ŋúb́ a-biiŋi ki ŋmāam̀ee. 22An pu ní, Ooyooliiba, man a-Dindaan Unimbɔti bíi sòoǹ nì si yii: <M làá yàntī a-bɔmbee kɔkɔ ń jáǹ-si. Kɔŋkɔnnee, a-naŋki nín nyáń nì bi nee, m làá yàntī bí nyānní an kɔkɔ pu kí jáǹ-si. 23M làá lùkutī Babiloon yab, Kaldee yab kɔkɔ, bin kóò Peekoodi nì Soowa nì Koowa ní Asuur yab ń kūtì bi-pu. M làá kóoǹ binaacimpɔnnyaambi gbanti nì gɔminab nì kɔmandambi nì bibaatandambi nì bikàliŋkpilib nì bitanjakaliibi gbanti kɔkɔ kí kpāfì a-cee. 24Bi làá nyānní ŋgan pú ki kāń janjatɔrɔkub nì loolib kɔkɔ nì bi-bulifi nì dijanjakitikpaandi. Bi làá dāá nīn ŋúb́ agbampɔɔ ki cíkí kujaau fuulimmu kí dāá màntīí tū-si. M làá dāá dū a-bɔti kí bíĺ bi-nimbiin ní bíǹ ń sòoǹ a-bɔti kí nóó nì bi-marab. 25M nín gíí a-pu diŋuul diŋyee puee, bi làá jáǹ-si nì diŋuul poon. Bi làá gíí kí gùutī a-maŋfal nì a-tafaliŋ ní kí dū ntàataajimu kí púntí-si. Bi làá yòon̄ a-bininjabiyaamu nì a-nimpubiyaamu ní ŋŋmi ń wà kí céetí bin kíǹ ki bí dimaŋfalinee. 26Bi làá dāá gbākal̀-si a-wampeeŋkaati nì a-wannyɔkɔntikaati. 27M làá dāá kúntí a-jɔkɔntuuŋŋi nì a-laakpaatuuŋŋi ŋin a kíĺ Eejipiti tiŋkinee. Aa dāa gíti là báà ubɔ ní kaa dāa gíti dàkafī Eejipiti yab pu gba.
28«Man a-Dindaan Unimbɔti di bíi sòoǹ yii m làá dū-si kí ŋá bin a née ŋaan, bin pu a-naŋki nyánnée. 29Bi làá dū kináŋ ní kí jáǹ-si. Bi làá dāá yòon̄ a nín túń ditundi ki ká tiŋyee kɔkɔ. Bi làá yàntī-si dicancaŋgbeel, ní kí dū-si kí síiń mpaampiin pu kii kinimpulaakpaayee báà ŋma ń nīn kpèé. A-laakpaatuuŋŋi nì a-jɔkɔntuuŋŋi 30di làá cáań tíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ a-pu. Si nì ntincamun ninjab ŋá tilaakpaal ní ki kɔ́ǹ a-ba tijɔkɔndi ki tōotì bi-waaŋi. 31A dī a-maan tabɔbiliŋ, an pu ní m làá yàntī á nyɔ̀ m-ŋuul yuku poon.> 32Man a-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sèé:
<A làá nyɔ̀ a-maan yuku poon ní,
kuyuu kun wāā ki nyóòyee.
Bi làá lā-si kí bèel̀-si,
di sá yii kuyuuee gbí tiŋan.
33Kuyuuee làá yàntī iween ń gbí-si.
Tifaandi nì falaa yuku gbantee,
a-maan Samaarii úǹ nyùn̄-ku ki dóò.
34A làá nyɔ̀ kun kā ku-poonee ní kɔkɔ,
a làá dū a-nyiŋŋi kí wīī-ku,
a làá dū ku-jaŋŋi kí gíí a-biiŋi.
Man a-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄,
m nín sòon̄ puee dee.
35An puee man a-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. A nín súntì m-pu ki fātì a-boon ki tīī-mee puee, a làá fōō a-jɔkɔntuuŋŋi nì a-laakpaatuuŋŋi paati.>»
Unimbɔti sòon̄ Samaarii nì Jeerusaleem bɔti
36Ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: «Nisaaleen, aa làá sòoǹ Ooyoola nì Ooyooliiba bɔtaaa? Dū ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin bi ŋée kí bíĺ bi-nimbiin. 37Bi sá binimpoobi bin ŋá tilaakpaal ki kūū binibee ní. Bi tōotì awaa ki ŋá tilaakpaal, ní ki dū mbininjabiyaamu mun bi màl̄-mee ki kūū ki ŋá saraa. 38An kaa sá tíǹ gbanti baba ní bi ŋá. Ŋwimbaantee, bi kɔ́ǹ m-circir paaŋyi tijɔkɔndi ní kaa tɔ́ ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa ŋun bi dūu sú-mee. 39Di sá yii ŋwiin ŋun bi kūū bi-jipɔmbi ki ŋá saraa ki tīī awaayee, ŋwiin gbanti ní bi kɔ́ m-circir kɔŋkooŋŋun ki kɔ́ǹ-ŋu tijɔkɔndi. Tin ní bi ŋá man m-ba diikunee dee. 40Kí kūtèe, bi tú binib bí yíiń bininjab bin nyánní ndandati timmunee. Bíǹ tin pée lì yii bi fòol̄ bi-nyɔɔbundee, bi kpáàa bāań bi-cee. Bi nìn fùl̄ ki bɔ̄ntì culoo ki nyɔ̄kɔntì bi-ba ki kíǹ ki kā ki cí-bi. 41Míǹ boonee ní bi tātìi dōoǹ nlambanyaamu pu. Nlambamuee nyɔkɔpuee, teebil un pu talaalutuukaa nì ŋkpam min sɔ́fì m nìn tīī-uee tɔ́kɔ́. 42Binib tikpil nìn bí niin, ní bi gbìl̀ kunipaau kun tiba kaa pée páb́ee wooku pu. Bininjab biba mun nìn nyánní ijaan tikpil kuteeun. Bi nìn dū tifuuŋkaal ki fúuń unil nì u-naalee ŋal ní ki dū kibeefuulii kinyannyaaŋŋi ki cíkiǹ-bi. 43Niinee ní m bí yii: <Ki kpáaǹ un ní alaakpaatuun nùkū waa ti bí tibanee gbíntìi ŋáań tilaakpaal! 44Bininjab dòoń u-cee kii bi nín cá kinimpulaakpaai cee puee! Kii bininjab nín cá kinimpulaakpaai cee puee, míǹ ní bi dɔ́miń Ooyoola nì Ooyooliiba, nnimpulaakpaamu nee cee. 45Ama deedeedambi làá sòoǹ kí kpɔ̀ binimpoobi gbanti bɔti yii bi nín ŋá tilaakpaal ki kūū binibee pu, di sá yii bi ŋá tilaakpaal ki kūū binib!
46«Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Lùkutī diniwul kí tɔ̄ bi-pu bí fàaǹ-bi kí gbākal̀ bi-gaajawanti. 47Yāŋkìmaan-bi ataŋkpee, dūmaan ntàataajimu kí kpɔ̀-bi. Kpɔ̀maan bi-jipɔmbi nì bi-bisalib ní kí tūū bi-diiŋŋi ŋŋmi. 48M làá kúntí alaakpaatuun kitiŋ nee poon. Án làá nīn sá ŋabika ki tīī binimpoobi kɔkɔ bí taa nóó nnabiyaamu muli nee laakpaatuuŋŋi tabɔbiliŋ. 49Binimpoobi bili nee làá fōō bi-laakpaatuuŋŋi paati ní bi-waatootii gìŋ́ŋi làá fàtīí gítí bi-pu. Niinee ni làá béé yii m sá ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti.»

english_text:
A Cooking Pot
1Nine years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the tenth day of the tenth month. He said:
2 Ezekiel, son of man, write down today's date, because the king of Babylonia has just begun attacking the city of Jerusalem. 3Then tell my rebellious people:
“Pour water in a cooking pot
and set it over a fire.
* 4Throw in the legs and shoulders
of your finest sheep
and put in the juicy bones.
5Pile wood underneath the pot,
and let the meat and bones
boil until they are done.”
6These words mean that Jerusalem is doomed! The city is filled with murderers and is like an old, rusty pot. The meat is taken out piece by piece, and no one cares what happens to it. 7The people of Jerusalem murdered innocent people in the city and didn't even try to cover up the blood that flowed out on the hard ground. 8But I have seen that blood, and it cries out for me to take revenge.
9I, the Lord God, will punish that city of violence! I will make a huge pile of firewood, 10so bring more wood and light it. Cook the meat and boil away the broth to let the bones scorch. 11Then set the empty pot over the hot coals until it is red-hot. That will clean the pot and burn off the rust. 12I've tried everything else. Now the rust must be burned away.
13Jerusalem is so full of sin and evil that I can't get it clean, even though I have tried. It will stay filthy until I let loose my fierce anger against it. 14That time will certainly come! And when it does, I won't show the people of Jerusalem any pity or change my mind. They must be punished for the evil they have done. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
Ezekiel's Wife Dies
15The Lord said, 16“Ezekiel, son of man, I will suddenly take the life of the person you love most. But I don't want you to complain or cry. 17Mourn in silence and don't show that you are grieving. Don't remove your turban or take off your sandals; don't cover your face to show your sorrow, or eat the food that mourners eat.”
18One morning, I was talking with the people as usual, and by sunset my wife was dead. The next day I did what the Lord had told me, 19and when people saw me, they asked, “Why aren't you mourning for your wife?”
20I answered:
The Lord God says 21he is ready to destroy the temple in which you take such pride and which makes you feel so safe. Your children who now live in Jerusalem will be killed. 22Then you will do the same things I have done. You will leave your face uncovered and refuse to eat the food that mourners usually eat. 23You won't take off your turbans and your sandals. You won't cry or mourn, but all day long you will go around groaning because of your sins.
24I am a warning sign—everything I have done, you will also do. And then you will know the Lord God has made these things happen.
25The Lord said, “Ezekiel, I will soon destroy the temple that makes everyone feel proud and safe, and I will take away their children as well. 26On that same day, someone will escape from the city and come to tell you what has happened. 27Then you will be able to speak again, and the two of you will talk. You will be a warning sign to the people, and they will know that I am the Lord.”
translation_text:
Jeerusaleem bí kii daansee un dámintèe ní
1Bi nín cúú Isirayeel yab ki cūnnì kuyuŋu abin awa boon, iŋmal saalaa poon iwiin saalaa dalee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii: 2«Nisaaleen, ŋmà díǹ wiiŋŋu nín sá ŋwiin ŋuŋyee kí bíĺ. Di sá yii díǹ ní Babiloon bɔtiu làá jáǹ Jeerusaleem tiŋki. 3Dū tibɔŋmantikaal nee kí ŋmàntī m-nibul yab yii man bi-Dindaan Unimbɔti di bíi sòoǹ nì bi yii:
<Bɔ́ntí daansee.
Jōō nnyim kí gbéeǹ.
4Dū anaŋkún kí ŋá poon,
anaŋkún ŋin ŋān̄ee, ditaal nì kugbigbipeeu.
Dū akpamɔnti kí gbéeǹ kí púntí.
5Yòon̄ upii nammɔntiiti,
kí dū akpab kí ŋá daansee taapu.
Yàntī an kɔkɔ ń nùuǹ dicilpu,
di sá yii bi máaǹ kí tɔ́kɔń akpab mun.
6Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀.
Nnikpaakoon tiŋki, nnaabu dɔ̄ ki cí-kèeee!
Kì náań nì daansee un dámintì
baa ŋūǹ kí fíntí-uee ní.
Kpáatí anaŋkúnee daansee poon kí bíĺ diba diba
kí taa tɔ̄ kasi.
7Fatiku un Jeerusaleem kpáatìi fée
dáá gbíntìi bí kitiŋ nee poon.
U kpáatì-u ki fá ditaŋkpal pu ní,
waa kpáatì-u ki fá kitiŋ,
kaa ti dū ntam ki bīiǹ u-pu.
8M yāntì fatikuee bí ditaŋkpal pu,
laakin ní baa ŋūǹ kí dū-u kí báĺee,
án nín làá ŋá pu ú gbítí m-ŋuul
ḿ ŋmā kí tɔ̀ ipɔntoonee.
9Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ yii:
Nnikpaakoon tiŋki, nnaabu dɔ̄ ki cí-si,
di sá yii m làá kpāā ŋŋmikpaan kí bíĺ!
10Nyàab̀ idɔ kí ŋá poon kí pàà ŋŋmi.
Púntí kí tɔ́kɔń tinanee,
nyàab̀ tikpàntikaal kí ŋá
ní kí yàntī akpab ń wà kɔkɔ múb.
11Dū daanseekulimee kí tɔ́kɔń amɔsiŋkoon pu
ú píĺ kí mántí cínciŋ.
An yaa ŋá mimmee, tijɔkɔndi
tin bí u-poonee làá wāŋkì
ní an wà an nín dámintì puee.>
12Ama dipɔ́ɔǹdi kɔkɔ sá fám ní. Ŋŋmi kaa làá wà an nín dámintì pu nee kɔkɔ. 13Jeerusaleem, a ŋá alaakpaatuun nee kɔkɔ ki kɔ́ǹ a-ba tijɔkɔndi. M bàà nyàab̄ kí ŋá-si circir ama ní a yíì kaa kpántì circirdaan. Too, aa làá ŋmā kí kpántí circirdaan kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋun ní m-ŋuul làá tɔ̄ a-pu di-tundi kí cáá kátée. 14Man ni-Dindaan nín sòon̄ ní án làá bàń míǹ. Maa làá gítí m-boon kaa làá sɔ̄ isaa mun. Án kaa làá nīn páb́-mi gba. M làá sòoǹ a-bimbim nì a-tuuŋŋi bɔti. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ.»
Eeseekiyeel kāl̀ dikpool
15Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii: 16«M làá yòon̄ un tìì-si dipɔɔpindee. Aa làá ŋá u-kpool, kaa làá sɔ̄ u-pu ní a-nyinnyim kaa làá nyā. 17Nín̄ nìiǹ diŋmiŋŋmilin kí taa kàl̄ dikpool. Dū a-ŋaabuŋu kí yíĺ kí dū a-naatakaŋ kí táká. Taa dū tiba kí bìin̄ a-nimbiin kí taa jī bukpɔsaa.»
18M sòon̄ nì samaa kutaafaauee, ní m-nimpuu kpíì kujoou. Kutaa wúntì ní m ŋá kii ti-Dindaan nín kpáafì-mi yii ḿ ŋá puee. 19Ní binib bālifì-mi ḿ tùkù-bi kun ní m ŋée taapu. 20Ní m kíí-bi yii: «Ti-Dindaan tīī-mi dinyɔɔbundi nee 21ḿ dūú nàatī nimbi Isirayeel yab yii: <Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ yii m làá kɔ́ǹ m-circir kɔŋkooŋŋu ŋun pu ni fàal̀, an mɔ̄ǹ-ni ni kpèé an tìì-ni dimákalee tijɔkɔndi. Bi làá dū ntàataajimu kí kpɔ̀ ni-jipɔmbi nì ni-bisalib bin kíǹ Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee. 22Ni làá ŋá kii Eeseekiyeelee. Naa làá dū tiba kí bìin̄ ni-nimbiin kaa làá jī bukpɔsaa. 23Ní dū iŋaabu kí fìn̄ ni-yiliŋ kí nīn táká anaataka. Ní taa yāliŋkì kí taa sɔ̄. Ama, ni-kpitii puee, ni làá dúntí ní báà ŋma làá nīn yáliŋkí u-juti pu. 24Eeseekiyeel làá nīn sá kudaaŋŋu ní ki tīī-ni. Tin bi sòon̄ ki síiǹ yii án làá bàńee yaa láa bāańee, ní dāá ŋámaan kii úǹ nín ŋá puee deedee. Niinee, ni làá béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti.>»
25«Sii nisaaleen, pīlifì, m làá yòon̄ bi-kansikin circir kɔŋkooŋŋu ŋun di sá bi-balilaŋki, ki sá bi-pɔɔpindi bi kpèé, ŋkɔŋkoon ŋun pu bi fàal̀ ní ki dū bi-mákal ki páaǹee. M làá dāá yòon̄ bi-jipɔmbi nì bi-bisalib. 26Ŋwiin gbantee, un ŋmátì ki nyáń nnaabu gbantinee làá dāá māafì-ni tin jítèe. 27Ŋwiin gbantee, a làá dāá ŋmā kí sòoǹ. A làá dāá ká kinyɔkɔ kí sòoǹ nì un ŋmátì ki nyáń nnaabun ki dɔ́mińee. A làá dāá nīn sá kudaaŋŋu ní ki tīī m-nibul ní bí dāá béé yii man di sá bi-Dindaan.»

english_text:
Judgment on Ammon
1 The Lord God said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the people of Ammon 3and tell them:
You celebrated when my temple was destroyed, when Israel was defeated, and when my people were taken away as prisoners. 4Now I am going to let you be conquered by tribes from the eastern desert. They will set up their camps in your land and eat your fruit and drink your milk. 5Your capital city of Rabbah will be nothing but pastureland for camels, and the rest of the country will be pastures for sheep. Then you will know that I am the Lord God.
6You hated Israel so much that you clapped and shouted and celebrated. 7And so I will hand you over to enemies who will rob you. I will completely destroy you. There won't be enough of your people left to be a nation ever again, and you will know that I, the Lord, have done these things.
Judgment on Moab
8 The Lord God said, “The people of Moab thought Judah was no different from any other nation. 9So I will let Moab's fortress towns along its border be attacked, including Beth-Jeshimoth, Baal-Meon, and Kiriathaim. 10The same eastern desert tribes that invade Ammon will invade Moab, and just as Ammon will be forgotten forever, 11Moab will be punished. Then the people there will know that I am the Lord.”
Judgment on Edom
12 The Lord God then said, “The people of Edom are guilty of taking revenge on Judah. 13So I will punish Edom by killing all its people and livestock. It will be an empty wasteland all the way from Teman to Dedan. 14I will send my own people to take revenge on the Edomites by making them feel my fierce anger. And when I punish them, they will know that I am the Lord God.”
Judgment on Philistia
15 The Lord God said, “The cruel Philistines have taken revenge on their enemies over and over and have tried to destroy them. 16Now it's my turn to treat the Philistines as my enemies and to kill everyone living in their towns along the seacoast. 17In my fierce anger, I will take revenge on them. And when I punish them, they will know that I am the Lord.”
translation_text:
Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ ki bíikì Amɔn yab pu
1Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii: 2Nisaaleen, fàtī a-ba kí túĺ Amɔn yab cee kí sòoǹ kí tɔ̄ bi-pu. 3Tùkù-bi yii bí pīlifì tibɔti tin man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti cáá kí sòoǹ nì bee. Ŋyunti ŋun ní bi kɔ́ǹ m-circir kɔŋkooŋŋu tijɔkɔndi, ki nāaǹ Isirayeel tiŋki ní ki cúú Juuda yab ki cūnnì kuyuŋuee, ni nìn láń. 4An puee, m làá yàntī ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú yab ń fōō ni-tiŋki. Bi làá gāā bi-janjanaapaaŋi ni-tiŋki pu ní kí cóoń bi-tantib niin. Bíǹ di làá ŋmɔ́ ni-sufii biliŋ ní kí nyɔ̀ ni-waŋkuti naabiim. 5M làá yàntī ni-tiŋyil Raaba ń kpántí kunaakpaapɔɔu kí tīī igutaamu, ní kí yàntī Amɔn tiŋki ń kpántí ipii naabakati. Niinee ni làá béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan.
6«Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Ni nín gbìl̄ nnaabu ŋun jéetì Isirayeel puee, an mɔ́ɔkiǹ-ni tikpil ní ni kpáafì abaal. Ni ŋá míǹ ki dàkā ni nín kpèé m-nibul fám puee ní. 7An puee m làá dàkà-ni m-pɔŋŋu ní kí dū-ni kí líiǹ atimbun ŋin kíǹee nib bí fūkul̀-ni pílpil. M làá kúntí-ni anibul kansikin, naa ti làá nīn cáá kitiŋ ní kí kúntí-ni múb. Niinee ni làá béé yii m sá ni-Dindaan.»
Ti-Dindaan làá jáǹ Moowaab yab
8«Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Moowaab yab lī yii Juuda yab kpántì kii atimbun ŋin kíǹee nib nín bí puee ní. 9An puee m làá yàntī bí jáǹ ntimu mun wúń Moowaab tiŋkpaanyɔmmuee. Binannanliibi làá nàan̄-mu kiba kiba ki kpáaǹ ntinnyaammu kii Beeti-Yeesimooti nì Baal-Meeyɔn nì Kiiriyatayiimee. 10M làá yàntī ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú yab ń já kí fōō Moowaab tiŋki kii bi nín jáń ki fōō Amɔn tiŋki puee. An yaa ŋá mimmee, baa ti làá téetí Amɔn yab pu atimbun kansikin. 11M làá dáaĺ Moowaab yab tafal ní bí béé yii man di sá bi-Dindaan.»
Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ ki bíikì Eedoom yab pu
12«Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Eedoom yab tɔ̀n̄ Juuda yab ipɔntoon, an pu ní bi fōō dibɔkpil. 13An puee man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M làá dàkà Eedoom yab m-pɔŋŋu. M làá kúntí kitiŋ gbanti nib nì ki-waŋkuti. M làá yàntī kí kpántí kuteeu kí yòon̄ Teeman tiŋki kí cáá sāā Deedan tiŋki. Bi làá kpɔ̀ bin kóò Eedoom tiŋkinee kujaaun ní. 14M làá yàntī m-nibul Isirayeel yab nín tɔ̀ m-pɔntooŋyi Eedoom yab pu. M-ŋuukpaandi nín bàlifī puee, míǹ ní Isirayeel yab làá ŋá-bi. Mimmee, Eedoom yab làá béé kun di sá m-pɔntooŋyee. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ.»
Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ ki bíikì Fiiliistii yab pu
15«Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Fiiliistii yab tɔ̀n̄ ipɔntoon. Bi dū nnimbidiki ki tɔ̀n̄ bi-nannanliibi bin sá talku nannanliibee ipɔntoon ní ki céetì-bi. 16An puee, man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M làá dàkà-bi m-pɔŋŋu. M làá kúntí-bi, bíǹ bin kɔkɔ nyánní Kafitoor ki dɔ́miń ki kāl̀ ditiŋkugbandee. 17M làá tɔ̀-bi ipɔntoon in sá ikpaanee ní kí dáaĺ bi-tafal ŋkpitim pu. Niinee bi làá béé yii man di sá bi-Dindaan.»

english_text:
Judgment on the City of Tyre
1 Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the month. He said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, the people of the city of Tyre have celebrated Jerusalem's defeat by singing,
“Jerusalem has fallen!
It used to be powerful,
a center of trade.
Now the city is shattered,
and we will take its place.”
3Because the people of Tyre have sung that song, I have the following warning for them: I am the Lord God, and I am now your enemy! I will send nations to attack you, like waves crashing against the shore. 4They will tear down your city walls and defense towers. I will sweep away the ruins until all that's left of you is a bare rock, 5where fishermen can dry their nets along the coast. I promise that you will be robbed 6and that the people who live in your towns along the coast will be killed. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
7King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia is the world's most powerful king, and I will send him to attack you. He will march from the north with a powerful army, including horses and chariots and cavalry troops. 8First, he will attack your towns along the coast and kill the people who live there. Then he will build dirt ramps up to the top of your city walls and set up rows of shields around you. 9He will command some of his troops to use large wooden poles to beat down your walls, while others use iron rods to knock down your watchtowers. 10He will have so many horses that the dust they stir up will seem like a thick fog. And as his chariots and cavalry approach, even the walls will shake, especially when he proudly enters your ruined city. 11His troops will ride through your streets, killing people left and right, and your strong columns will crumble to the ground. 12The troops will steal your valuable possessions; they will break down your walls, and crush your expensive houses. Then the stones and wood and all the remains will be dumped into the sea. 13 You will have no reason to sing or play music on harps, 14because I will turn you into a bare rock where fishermen can dry their nets. And you will never rebuild your city. I, the Lord God, make this promise.
15The people of the nations up and down the coast will shudder when they hear your screams and moans of death. 16 The kings will step down from their thrones, then take off their royal robes and fancy clothes, and sit on the ground, trembling. They will be so shocked at the news of your defeat that they will shake in fear 17and sing this funeral song:
“The great city beside the sea
is destroyed!
Its people once ruled the coast
and terrified everyone there.
18But now Tyre is in ruins,
and the people on the coast
stare at it in horror
