and tremble in fear.”
19I, the Lord God, will turn you into a ghost-town. The ocean depths will rise over you 20and carry you down to the world of the dead, where you will join people of ancient times and towns ruined long ago. You will stay there and never again be a city filled with people. 21 You will die a horrible death! People will come looking for your city, but it will never be found. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ kí bíikì Tiir yab pu
1Bi nín cúú Isirayeel yab ki cūnnì kuyuŋu abin saalaa nì diba boon, uŋmal wimpeekaaŋuee, ti-Dindaan nìn bí-mi yii: 2«Nisaaleen, pīlifì, Tiir yab bíi bèel̄ Jeerusaleem yab ki lì yii: <An nāaǹ Jeerusaleem, kitiŋ kin pu báà ŋma nìn jītée. An māaǹ-kì! Ti mun yuntiŋu bāań tí kpántí bigaajab deeyaa! Di sá yii kì kpántì adigbuŋkati ŋma ní!> 3An puee man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ yii m làá jáǹ sii Tiir tiŋki. M làá cáań atimbun kupaau kí léeń a-pu kii tiŋku nín yòontí u-nyiŋgbanti yilpu puee. 4Bi làá kpēelikì agun ŋin a máń ki tú a-tiŋkee ní kí wìil̀ a-sintil difɔkɔŋi. M làá kɔ́tí kitiŋ tam ní kí pée kíń ditaŋkpal dí nīn dɔ̄ fám. 5Tiir làá kpántí tiŋku kansikin mpaan ŋun pu bijɔncuuliibi làá nīn díntí bi-laantee ní. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ ní ki làá ŋá míǹ. Atimbun aba làá dāan̄ kí fūkul̀ Tiir tiŋki. 6Bi làá kpēelikì ki-timbilimmu mun bí ditiŋkugbandee. Niinee báà ŋma làá béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan.
7«Di sá yii man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ yii: <M làá cáań ŋgan pú bɔtiu un pɔ̄ɔ̄yee, an dàkà yii Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar ú jáǹ-si. U làá cáań itaamu nì janjatɔrɔkub nì bitanjakaliibi nì dijanjakitikpaandi kí jáǹ-si. 8U làá kpēelikì a-timbilimu mun bí ditiŋkugbandee. Míǹ boonee, bijanjaliibi bin dɔ́miń kí jáǹ-see làá gbà gɔtab bin poon bi làá nīn kàal̀ ki jáà nì see ní kí mā ŋgumu mun boon bi làá nīn bí ki jáà nì see, ní kí mā digundi din làá nīn sá kii digbampɔɔlee kí jáǹ-si. 9Bi làá dū bi-janjamasiimbi kí gbá kí wìil̀ a-guŋŋi ŋin māntìi tú-see ní kí dū jikab kí kpēelikì a-sintil difɔkɔŋi. 10Bi-taamui nín làá nīn wīikí puee kpɔŋkpɔŋku di làá bìin̄ a-pu, ní bi-tanjakaliibi wooku nì bi-tɔrɔkub taaŋi nín màntī puee làá yàntī a-guŋŋi ń cìŋkì. Di sá yii bi làá dī a-punyɔmmu kí kɔ́ kii bi nín wìil̄ digundi pu kí dī kí kɔ́ puee ní. 11Bi-taamui taaŋi làá tāā tāā a-daŋŋi kɔkɔ pu ní bí dū ntàataajimu kí kpɔ̀ a-nib ní kí téé a-jantalkukpaambee kí lúkú. 12Bi làá yòon̄ a-gaajati ní kí fūkul̀ a-wanti. Bi làá wìil̀ a-guŋŋi ní kí kpēelikì a-dinyaaŋŋi. Bi làá yòon̄ ŋi-taŋkpeeŋi nì ŋi-dɔi nì ŋi-tam kí cáá tɔ̄ tiŋkun. 13M làá kúntí ilan in a gèe, baa ti làá gbìl̄ a-bati pu. 14M làá yàntī á kpántí kii ditaŋkpal din pu tiba kaa bīīyee ní bijɔncuuliibi ń nīn díntí bi-laanti di-pu. Baa ti làá fàtīí náań kitiŋ gbanti dalba dalba. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ ní tin m sòon̄ee, tíǹ ní m làá ŋá.>
15«Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ Tiir pu tiŋyee sɔ̀. Bi yaa láa nāaǹ sii Tiir tiŋki ki kūū a-nib ní ki gbìl̄ bin fōō tiweendee yaliŋkii puee, bin kóò ntimu mun poon nnyim māntìi túee wunti làá dāá fōō dijinjikil. 16Atimbun ŋin kóò atiŋkugbánee bɔtiibi làá kpákatí bi-beejaliŋ pu kí pèetī bi-bɔkutikpaaŋŋi nì bi-bɔkutiŋ ŋin bi gbáńee. Bi làá nyɔ̀ ŋkpatim ní kí kàl̄ kitiŋ. Bi-wunti làá nīn gbíntìi jìkì, ní bí kɔ́ dinyoondin a-pu. 17Bi làá dāá gāā-si ŋkpiisilan nee yii:
<Bi nāaǹ kitiŋ kin nyáń diyindee,
bi kúntì-si tiŋkub kansikin!
Ki-nib nìn cáá tiŋkub pu mpɔn,
ní báà ŋma nìn fàŋkí-bi.
18Ama kɔŋkɔnnee, bi nín nāaǹ-kì nee
atimbun ŋin bí tiŋkub kansikinee wunti bíi jìkì,
bin kóò atiŋkugbánee nyùn̄ ŋkpatim,
kun puee aa ti bí.>
19«Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ yii m làá yàntī á kpántí kii ntimu mun kpántì adigbuŋkati ubɔ nì ubɔ kaa ti kóò mu-poonee. M làá yàntī tiŋku taapu nyim ń yīkì kí bìin̄ a-pu. 20M làá yàntī á cùú ŋàl̄ taapu taŋkpiibi pu, bin bí niin cannaakuee. M làá yàntī á cùú nīn kóò kitiŋ taapu taapu, kí nīn bí kii jaanjaan digbuŋkatiŋ ŋin bí niinee. Sii nì bitaŋkpiibi bin līntiǹ-see di làá nīn bí. Aa ti làá ŋmā kí jɔ̄mìń kaa ti làá nīn cáá mpaan binifoobi tiŋki pu. 21Tin làá bàń a-puee làá kɔ́ǹ báà ŋma dinyoondi, di sá yii aa ti làá nīn bí. Bi làá dāá nyàab̀-si, ama ubɔ kaa ti làá ká-si jaanjaan. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ.»

english_text:
A Funeral Song for Tyre
1The Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, sing a funeral song for Tyre, 3the city that is built along the sea and that trades with nations along the coast. Tell the people of Tyre that the following message is from me:
Tyre, you brag about
your perfect beauty,
4and your control of the sea.
You are a ship
built to perfection.
5Builders used cypress trees
from Mount Hermon
to make your planks
and a cedar tree from Lebanon
for your tall mast.
6Oak trees from Bashan
were shaped into oars;
pine trees from Cyprus
were cut for your deck,
which was then decorated
with strips of ivory.
7The builders used fancy linen
from Egypt for your sails,
so everyone could see you.
Blue and purple cloth
from Cyprus was used
to shade your deck.
8Men from Sidon and Arvad
did the rowing,
and your own skilled workers
were the captains.
9Experienced men from Byblos
repaired any damages.
Sailors from all over
shopped at the stores
in your port.
10Brave soldiers from Persia,
Lydia, and Libya
served in your navy,
protecting you with shields
and helmets,
and making you famous.
11Your guards came from
Arvad and Cilicia,
and men from Gamad
stood watch in your towers.
With their weapons
hung on your walls,
your beauty was complete.
12Merchants from southern Spain traded silver, iron, tin, and lead for your products. 13The people of Greece, Tubal, and Meshech traded slaves and things made of bronze, 14and those from Beth-Togarmah traded work horses, war horses, and mules. 15You also did business with people from Rhodes, and people from nations along the coast gave you ivory and ebony in exchange for your goods. 16Edom traded emeralds, purple cloth, embroidery, fine linen, coral, and rubies. 17Judah and Israel gave you their finest wheat, fancy figs, honey, olive oil, and spices in exchange for your merchandise. 18The people of Damascus saw what you had to offer and brought you wine from Helbon and wool from Zahar. 19Vedan and Javan near Uzal traded you iron and spices. 20The people of Dedan supplied you with saddle blankets, 21while people from Arabia and the rulers of Kedar traded lambs, sheep, and goats. 22Merchants from Sheba and Raamah gave you excellent spices, precious stones, and gold in exchange for your products. 23You also did business with merchants from the cities of Haran, Canneh, Eden, Sheba, Asshur, and Chilmad, 24and they gave you expensive clothing, purple and embroidered cloth, brightly colored rugs, and strong rope. 25 Large, seagoing ships carried your goods wherever they needed to go.
You were like a ship
loaded with heavy cargo
26and sailing across the sea,
but you were wrecked
by strong eastern winds.
27Everything on board was lost—
your valuable cargo,
your sailors and carpenters,
merchants and soldiers.
28The shouts of your drowning crew
were heard on the shore.
29Every ship is deserted;
rowers and sailors and captains
all stand on shore,
30mourning for you.
They show their sorrow
by putting dust on their heads
and rolling in ashes;
31they shave their heads
and dress in sackcloth
as they cry in despair.
32In their grief they sing
a funeral song for you:
“Tyre, you were greater
than all other cities.
But now you lie in silence
at the bottom of the sea.
33“Nations that received
your merchandise
were always pleased;
kings everywhere got rich
from your costly goods.
34But now you are wrecked
in the deep sea,
with your cargo and crew
scattered everywhere.
35People living along the coast
are shocked at the news.
Their rulers are horrified,
and terror is written
across their faces.
36The merchants of the world
can't believe what happened.
Your death was gruesome,
and you are gone forever.”
translation_text:
Tiir tiŋki kpiisilaŋyi
1Ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: 2«Nisaaleen, gāā Tiir tiŋki ŋkpiisilan. 3Kitiŋ gbanti bí ditiŋkugbandi ní ki bàntī nì atimbun ŋin timmu tiŋku nyim māntìi túee. Nàatī-kì tin man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti sòon̄ee yii:
Sii, Tiir tiŋki, a lì yii:
<M ŋān̄ kunyaaŋŋu!>
4A-tiŋki wāā ki tin bàn̄ tiŋku kansikin.
Bi máń-si a ŋān̄ tikpilku.
5Bi máń-si kii meelee.
Bi dū Seeniir tiŋkin subu bun bi yíì siipreesee
ki dūu kpáá a-wunti boon.
Bi dū Leebanɔn tiŋkin subu bun bi yíì seediree
ní ki cóoǹ ki sàkantí a-ŋaabiki.
6Bi dū Baasan tiŋkin subu bun bi yíì seenee
ki kpítì a-laalii in a cáa kùtī nnyiminee.
Bi dū Siipiri tiŋkin subu bun bi yíì seedir
bi dū akuntinyin ki nyūntèe
ki máń a-kadulkau.
7Bi dū fálfal ŋaabui in nyánní Eejipiti bi gbáńee
ki lùn̄ a-ŋaabui in bi cáa sàkantí iŋaliŋfi puee.
Iŋaabu gbanti di yàntī a yaa páaǹní ndanee bí béé-si.
Satab bin máǹ wèeee ki máń cínciŋ
ki nyánní Siipiri tiŋkinee
ní a nìn cáa bìintí a-wannyafikaati pu.
8Bin nìn ŋàal̀ a-meelauee
nìn nyánní Siidɔn nì Arfaadi timmun ní,
Tiir yab bin yáb̀ee
di nìn ŋàal̀ meela gbanti.
9Biibiloosi tɔntɔnliibi
bin nìn nyí ditundi ki yáb̀ee
di nìn ŋáŋkí meelee.
Meelab bin kɔkɔ nìn bí tiŋku puee
nìn yūlifí a-cee ní,
ní bin nìn kā u-poonee dāā a-wanti tin a nyáfée.
10Peersi nì Luudi nì Puuti yab janjaliibi
di nìn bí a-janjakitilin.
Bi nìn cáá bi-gbampɔɔŋi nì bi-janjafuulimmu
ki sīintí a-cee ní.
Bíǹ di nìn tìì-si tinyool.
11Arfaadi yab nìn kútí a-janjaliibi pu ní bí jɔ̄m̀ a-guŋŋi pu ki cí kitiŋ, ní Gamaadi yab nìn yūlifí a-sintil difɔkɔŋi pu sintil. Bi nìn dù bi-gbampɔɔŋi ní kí lúntí agun ŋin māntìi tú-see pu. Bíǹ di nìn gíti kútí-si kunyaaŋŋu.»
12«Taarsiisi yab nìn cáá tigaajati kɔkɔ nì ti-bulifi ki kpántí a-wanti. Bi nìn cáá animbil nì tikúti nì tikúnyuntikaal nì tikúbɔn tin nyìm̀ee ki dāā a-wanti. 13Greeki yab nì Tuubaal yab nì Meeseeki yab nìn bàntī a-cee ní. Bi nìn cáá iyumbu nì tasa kúti ki kpántí a-wanti. 14Beeti Toogarma yab nìn nyáfíǹ-si itaamu in tūǹ ditundee nì itaamu in pu bi kàal̀ ki jáà kujaauee nì imamboon. 15Deedan yab mun nìn bàntī a-cee. Ntimu tikpil nib nìn dòoń ki dāā a-wanti. Bi nìn cáá kunti nyiŋŋi nì busubu bun bi yíì eebeenee dɔi ní ki pà-si. 16Eedoom yab nìn dāā a-cee tiwan tikpil ní ki nìn cáá ataŋkpamɔnti nì satab bin bi dū nnyim min bí gùŋgumee ki nyūntèe nì satab bin bi gbáńee nì iŋaabu in bí fálfalee nì ataŋkpamɔnti ŋin bi yíì kooraai nì rubiisee ki kpántí-si tiwan. 17Juuda yab nì Isirayeel yab nìn dāā a-cee tiwan ní ki nyáfíǹ-si Miiniiti tiŋki bileeu nì idi nì tisiil nì ŋkpam nì talaalu un bi dū digbumbitiki ki ŋée. 18Damaasi yab nìn dāā a-cee tiwan tin a ŋáańee tikpil nì tigaajawan yíri yiri. Bi nìn cáá Eelbɔn tiŋki damam nì ipii kuti tin nyánní Sawaar tiŋkinee ki pà-si. 19Daani nì Yafan naakɔti nìn cáá tikúti tin bi mɔ́ɔ̀yee nì talaalub ki pà tin bi dāā a-ceeyee Uusal tiŋkin. 20Deedan yab nìn nyáfíǹ-si igban in bi cáa pāantí itaamu puee. 21Bilaalibub nì Keedaar tiŋki yab cáá apibil nì ipii nì iŋɔsal ki pà tiwan tin bi dāā a-ceeyee pu. 22Saba nì Ragima nyampoobi nìn bàntī a-cee. Bi nìn cáá talaalumɔntiibi nì ataŋkpamɔnti kɔkɔ nì ŋi-bulifi nì sindaariya ki kpántí nì tiwan tin a nyáfée. 23Karan nì Kanee nì Eedeen timmun yab nìn bàntī a-cee. Míǹ mbaantiim ní Saba nì Asuur nì Kilmad timmun yab nìn bàntī. 24Bi nìn nyáfíǹ-si tiwampeeŋkaal tin pɔ̄ɔ̄ kudaau ki máń wèeeeyee nì tiwampeeŋkaal tin bi gbáńee nì satab bin cáá inyiŋfi kupaauee nì iŋmii in bi lùn̄ i dàfì tiŋanee. 25Taarsiisi tiŋkin meelab di nìn tūntí a-wanti.»
Tiir kpiisilaŋŋuee di gbíntìi nìkì
«Bi dū tiwannyafikaal ki gbéeǹ-si
an nyìm̀ a bí tiŋku kansikin.
26Bin ŋàal̀-see cáá-si ki cūnnì laakin nnyim nyóòyee.
A bàn̄ tiŋku kansikinee ní ŋwìiń nyalaŋki buŋku yāntì a wīī.
27A-gaajati nì a-wanti tin a nyáfée nì a-gaajawanti kɔkɔ,
nì bin kɔkɔ bí meela poon ki tūǹ ditundee,
nì bin nìn ŋáŋkí a-meelabee,
nì binyampoobi bin bàntī a-ceeyee,
nì bijanjaliibi bin bí a-tundinee,
nì samaa un bí a-ceeyee kɔkɔ
tɔ́ nnyimin ŋwiin ŋun a wīī ki gbíntì nnyiminee.
28Bin bí meela poon ki tūǹ ditundee nín fáá mbiilee,
atiŋkugbán cīŋkì ní.
29Niinee bin kɔkɔ ŋúb́ buŋalimbu laaliiyee
yíkì ki yāntì bi-meelab.
Bin bí meelabinee kpákatì kitiŋ.
30Bi kíĺ ki bíi sūǹ a-pu,
ki bíi yáliŋkí ŋkpitim pu.
Bi kāfì ntam ki sītì bi-yiliŋ pu
ki dɔ̄ ki bíntí ŋfantamin.
31A-puee, bi kōol̀ diyibaakpandi
ki dū kpɔsata ki lōoǹ.
Bi bíi sūǹ a-pu nì kunimbaau
ki yáliŋkí ŋkpitim pu.
32An nín wù-bi puee, bi bíi gà-si iyaliŋki laŋŋu,
bi bíi gà-si ŋkpiisilan nee yii:
<Ŋma di nìn bí kii Tiir tiŋkee,
ama kɔŋkɔnnee, kì nāaǹ múb tiŋku kansikin.>
33Bi yaa nìn nyāntí a-bantil wanti a-meelabinee,
anibul tikpil nìn jīǹ ní kí díkí.
A-gaajawanti nín nìn wīikí puee nì tiwan tin a nyáfée
nìn yàntī kitiŋ pu bɔtiibi kpántí bigaajab.
34Kɔŋkɔnnee, tinyiŋgban yá ki wīī-si,
a múĺ tiŋku taapu.
Tiwan tin a túee nì bin bí a-poon ki tūǹ ditundee
kútì a-pu ki múĺ tiŋkun.
35Bin kɔkɔ kóò atiŋkugbánee
bí kunimbaakpaaŋŋun sii pu.
Bi-bɔtiibi kɔ́ dinyoondin,
a yaa kpēē-bee, a béetí yii bi-bɔbiliŋ bíil̀.
36Anibul ŋin kíǹee nyampoobi
fátí dipɔɔbiildi biilii a-pu,
di sá yii a kpántì tiwan tin fàantée,
a wáŋkì kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaan!»

english_text:
Judgment on the King of Tyre
1The Lord God said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, tell the king of Tyre that I am saying:
You are so arrogant that you think you're a god and that the city of Tyre is your throne. You may claim to be a god, though you're nothing but a mere human. 3You think you're wiser than Daniel and know everything.
4Your wisdom has certainly made you rich, because you have storehouses filled with gold and silver. 5You're a clever businessman and are extremely wealthy, but your wealth has led to arrogance!
6You compared yourself to a god, so now I, the Lord God, 7will make you the victim of cruel enemies. They will destroy all the possessions you've worked so hard to get. 8Your enemies will brutally kill you, and the sea will be your only grave.
9When you face your enemies, will you still claim to be a god? They will attack, and you will suffer like any other human. 10Foreigners will kill you, and you will die the death of those who don't worship me. I, the Lord, have spoken.
A Funeral Song for the King of Tyre
11The Lord said:
12Ezekiel, son of man, sing a funeral song for the king of Tyre and tell him I am saying:
At one time, you were perfect, intelligent, and good-looking. 13You lived in the garden of Eden and wore jewelry made of brightly colored gems and precious stones. They were all set in gold and were ready for you on the day you were born. 14I appointed a winged creature to guard your home on my holy mountain, where you walked among gems that dazzled like fire.
15You were truly good from the time of your birth, but later you started doing wicked things. 16You traded with other nations and became more and more cruel and evil. So I forced you to leave my mountain, and the creature that had been your protector now chased you away from the jewels.
17It was your good looks that made you arrogant, and you were so famous that you started acting like a fool. That's why I threw you to the ground and let other kings sneer at you. 18You have cheated so many other merchants that your places of worship are corrupt. So I set your city on fire and burned it down. Now everyone sees only ashes where your city once stood, 19and the people of other nations are shocked. Your punishment was horrible, and you are gone forever.
Judgment on Sidon and Peace for Israel
20 The Lord said:
21Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the city of Sidon 22and tell its people:
I, the Lord God, am your enemy! People will praise me when I punish you, and they will see that I am holy. 23I will send deadly diseases to wipe you out, and I will send enemies to invade and surround you. Your people will be killed, and you will know that I am the Lord.
24When that happens, the people of Israel will no longer have cruel neighbors that abuse them and make them feel as though they are in a field of thorns and briers. And the Israelites will know that I, the Lord God, have done these things.
A Blessing for Israel
25The Lord God said:
Someday I will gather the people of Israel from the nations where they are now scattered, and every nation will see that I am holy. The Israelites will once again live in the land I gave to my servant Jacob. 26They will be safe and will build houses and plant vineyards. They will no longer be in danger, because I will punish their hateful neighbors. Israel will know that I am the Lord their God.
translation_text:
Unimbɔti sòon̄ ki bíikì Tiir bɔtiu pu
1Ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: 2«Nisaaleen, tùkù Tiir bɔtikpaaŋwu tin man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti sòon̄ee: Dilambil kɔ́-see ní a kíǹ ki lì yii: <M sá unimbɔti. M kā inimbɔti jal pu tiŋku kansikin.> A dàkafī yii si nì unimbɔti ŋmà ní, ama a sá unil ní, aa sá unimbɔti! 3A dàkafī yii a sá uciŋfiti ki jítiǹ Daniyeel ní ki ŋūǹ kí gbìl̄ tibɔti tin sá abɔɔnee taapu. 4A dū dinyil nì nciin ki ká tigaajati tikpil. A kóoǹ sindaariya nì animbil ki kpáafì a-cee. 5A nín nyí dibàntil tundi tikpil puee, a kútì a-gaajati pu ní an yōoǹ-si.
6«An pu ní man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti bíi sòoǹ yii, a dū a-ba ki síiǹ unimbɔti paaŋŋu. 7A nín ŋá mimmee puee, m làá cáań atimbuncaan ŋin nib néeń tipɔmbɔtee kí tɔ̄ a-pu. Bi làá bīil̀ tiwammɔntiil tin a dū a-nyil ki nyàab̄ ki kée ní kí kpèè kí sìŋkīǹ a-nyooti. 8Bi làá yàntī á sìntī ditaŋkpiilin ní kí kpú dulim kúm tiŋku kansikin. 9Bi yaa láa dɔ́miń kí kpɔ̀-see, a làá dāá gíti lì yii a sá unimbɔtaaa? Ama a làá dāá nīn sá unil ní bin làá kpɔ̀-see ŋaan, kaa sá unimbɔti. 10A làá kpú bin kaa gíí dikpancandee kúm ní binicambi ŋaan. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ ní tin m sòon̄ee dee.»
11Ti-Dindaan gíti sòon̄ nì mi yii: 12«Nisaaleen, gāā Tiir bɔtiu iyaliŋki laŋŋu. Á tùkù-u yii man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Sii boonee, an nìn gíti kpá. A nìn cáá dinyil tikpil ní ki nìn ŋān̄ kunyaaŋŋu. 13A nìn kóò Unimbɔti kpaabun, Eedeen tiŋkin ní bi nìn dū ataŋkpamɔnti ki máń digundi ki māntìi tú-si. Ataŋkpamɔnti ŋin bi yíì rubiisi nì diyaaman nì Kriistooliiti nì Koornaliini nì jaaspi nì greenaati nì eemeeroodee ní bi nìn dūu máń-dì. Sindaariya un bi nyūntì a-gaŋgaŋŋi nì a-wulimmuee, bi bɔ́ntì-u ŋwiin ŋun bi náań-see ní. 14M nìn dū keerubim un yáàyee ki yóoǹ a-cee ú nīn cí-si. A nìn kóò m-circir jool pu, ní ki nìn còom̄ ataŋkpee ŋin jìl̀ee kansikin. 15Kí yòon̄ ŋwiin ŋun bi náań-see, a cōom̀ disaŋkimmɔntiil ki cáá sāā daliŋkin bi ká ikpiti a-ceeyee. 16A-nyampuyil nín cōom̀ tiŋan puee yāntì a ŋá tipɔmbɔti. A yīntì. An puee ní m làá yàntī á kpántí kii binifantantiibee ní kí jà-si m-jool pu. Keerubim un cí-see làá jà-si kí nyāntí ataŋkpee ŋin jìl̀ee kansikin. 17A-nyaaŋku yāntì a kɔ́ dilambilin ní an nín bútì-si puee yāntì a-yil lábitì. An pu ní m làá lúkú-si kitiŋ ní á kpántí tinimbikɔntiwan kí tīī bibɔtiibi bin kíǹee. 18A ŋá ikpiti tikpil ní ki mūul̀ binib a-nyampuyil poon ki kɔ́ǹ circir paaŋyi tijɔkɔndi. An pu ní m kpāā ŋŋmi ŋun làá nàan̄-see a-tiŋki kansikin. A làá dāá kpántí ŋfantam ní bin bíi kpèé-see nimbiin. 19Kun làá bàń a-puee làá kɔ́ǹ anibul ŋin nyí-see kunimbaau, di sá yii a làá kpántí tiwan tin fàantée ní. A làá wāŋkì ní kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaan.>»
Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ ki bíikì Siidɔn tiŋki pu
20Ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: 21«Nisaaleen, fàtī a-nimbiin kí túĺ Siidɔn tiŋki kí sòoǹ m-bɔti kí tɔ̄ ki-nib pu. 22Dū tin man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti sòon̄ee kí nàatī-bi yii: <M làá jáǹ sii Siidɔn tiŋki! M làá dàkà m-nyooti tin m làá ŋá-see poon. M yaa láa dáaĺ a-tafal ki dàkā m nín bí circir puee, báà ŋma làá dāá béé yii m sá ni-Dindaan. 23M làá cáań bìlbil kúm weeŋyi kí tɔ̄ a-pu, ní fatiku ń nīn dɔ̄ ki pùub̀ a-daŋŋi pu. Bi làá dāá jáǹ-si ijaan kɔkɔ pu ní kí kpɔ̀ bin kóò a-tiŋki poonee tikpil. Niinee báà ŋma làá dāá béé yii m sá ni-Dindaan.»
Isirayeel làá nīn bí ŋgbansɔŋfin
24«Atimbun ŋin māntìi tú Isirayeel yabee diba kaa ti làá kpèè-bi fám. Ŋaa ti làá páb́-bi kii ikuŋkum nín sàatī unil pu, àá abɔjanaakun nín pàtī unil puee. Niinee báà ŋma làá béé yii m sá ni-Dindaan.
25«Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ yii m làá nyāntí Isirayeel yab kɔkɔ anibul ŋin poon m jìn̄-bi ki cūnnèe kansikin kí kóoǹ-bi kí kpāfì. M làá ŋá míǹ ní kí dàkà anibul ŋin kíǹee yii m sá circir Nimbɔtiu. Isirayeel yab làá fàtīí gítí kí kɔ́ bi-tiŋkin, kitiŋ kin ní m tīī m-tɔntɔnliu Jaakɔbee. 26Bi làá dāá nīn kóò niin nì ŋgbansɔŋfi, kí mā adiin ní kí cóoń fiinyib. Bi làá dāá nīn bí ŋgbansɔŋfin, di sá yii m làá dáaĺ bin kɔkɔ kóò ki māntìi tú-bi ki kpēē-bi fámee tafal. Niinee bi làá dāá béé yii man di sá bi-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu.>»

english_text:
Judgment on the King of Egypt
1 Ten years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the twelfth day of the tenth month. He said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the king of Egypt. Tell him and his people 3that I am saying:
King of Egypt, you were like a giant crocodile lying in a river. You acted as though you owned the Nile and made it for yourself. But now I, the Lord God, am your enemy! 4I will put a hook in your jaw and pull you out of the water, and all the fish in your river will stick to your scaly body. 5I'll throw you and the fish into the desert, and your body will fall on the hard ground. You will be left unburied, and wild animals and birds will eat your flesh. 6 Then everyone in Egypt will know that I am the Lord.
You and your nation refused to help the people of Israel and were nothing more than a broken stick. 7When they reached out to you for support, you broke in half, cutting their arms and making them fall.
8So I, the Lord God, will send troops to attack you, king of Egypt. They will kill your people and livestock, 9until your land is a barren desert. Then you will know that I have done these things.
You claimed that you made the Nile River and control it. 10Now I am turning against you and your river. Your nation will be nothing but an empty wasteland all the way from the town of Migdol in the north to Aswan in the south, and as far as the border of Ethiopia. 11No human or animal will even dare travel through Egypt, because no sign of life will be found there for 40 years. 12It will be the most barren place on earth. Every city in Egypt will lie in ruins during those 40 years, and I will scatter your people throughout the nations of the world.
13Then after those 40 years have passed, I will bring your people back from the places where I scattered them. 14They will once again live in their homeland in southern Egypt. But they will be a weak kingdom 15and won't ever be strong enough to rule nations, as they did in the past. 16My own people Israel will never again depend on your nation. In fact, when the Israelites remember what happened to you Egyptians, they will realize how wrong they were to turn to you for help. Then the Israelites will know that I, the Lord God, did these things.
King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia Will Conquer Egypt
17Twenty-seven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the first month. He said:
18King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia has attacked the city of Tyre. He forced his soldiers to carry so many heavy loads that their heads were rubbed bald, and their shoulders were red and sore. Nebuchadnezzar and his army still could not capture the city. 19So now I will hand over the nation of Egypt to him. He will take Egypt's valuable treasures and give them to his own troops. 20Egypt will be his reward, because he and his army have been following my orders. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
21Ezekiel, when Egypt is defeated, I will make the people of Israel strong, and I will give you the power to speak to them. Then they will know that I, the Lord, have done these things.
translation_text:
Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ ki bíikì Eejipiti tiŋki pu
1Bi nín cúú Isirayeel yab kuyuŋu abin saalaa boon, uŋmal usaalaati wiiŋyi saalaa nì ili dalee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii: 2«Nisaaleen, fàtī a-nimbiin kí túĺ Eejipiti bɔtiu Faaroo watil pú kí sòoǹ kí tɔ̄ u nì Eejipiti tiŋki kɔkɔ pu. 3Nàatī-u tibɔti tin ní man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti bíi sòoǹ nì uee yii: <M làá jáǹ sii Faaroo, Eejipiti bɔtiu. A bí kii kunyiibiliŋŋuee ní ki dɔ̄ Niil mɔɔlin. A lì yii sii di yì Niil mɔɔl, sii di náań-dì ki tīī a-ba. 4Too, m làá dū tikúti kí kpàl̄ a-nyɔɔkpaweeŋyi ní kí dū a-mɔɔl poon jɔmii kí nákań a-pɔkɔi pu. M làá nyāntí-si Niil mɔɔlin kí kpáaǹ ijɔm in kɔkɔ náká a-jɔmpɔkɔi puee. 5M làá dū-ni kí lúkú kuteeun, sii nì ijɔm gbanti kɔkɔ. A làá lítí kitiŋ ní kí kpú ní ubɔ mun kpá kí yòon̄-si àá kí síb́-si. M làá yàntī á kpántí inoon nì ipeel jinti. 6Niinee Eejipiti yab kɔkɔ làá béé yii man di sá bi-Dindaan.
«A nín tútúǹ Isirayeel yab puee kaa bàn̄ kukaluu nín ŋūǹ kí tūtuǹ-bi puee. 7Bi nín dīntì a-puee, a kɔ́fì ki gbíntì bi-ŋalin ní ki gíí bi-gbigbipeeu ní ki yɔ̄tì bi-wunti. 8Too, man a-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M làá dū ajanjakiti kí tɔ̄ń a-pu ní kí kpɔ̀ kí céetí a-tiŋkin nib nì ki-waŋkuti. 9Bi làá nàan̄ Eejipiti tiŋki ní kitiŋee ń kpántí kii kuteeuee. Niinee binib làá béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan.
«A lī yii sii di yì Niil mɔɔl, sii di náań-dì. 10An puee m làá jáǹ sii nì a-mɔɔl. M làá yàntī Eejipiti ń kpántí adigbuŋkati ŋma. M làá yàntī kí kpántí kuteeu kí yòon̄ Miigidool tiŋki ŋgan pú kí cáá sāā Asuwan tiŋki nì Eetiiyoopii tiŋkpaanyɔkɔ ŋgiil pú. 11Báà unil àá kuwaŋkuluu kaa ti làá kíí kí cù niin. Baa làá ti ká tin cáá kufoouee abin imuŋku ili Eejipiti tiŋkin. 12M làá yàntī Eejipiti tiŋki ń kpántí kuteeu kun pée kūń ki jítiǹ kuteeu kamaayee. Bi làá nàan̄ Eejipiti timmu min ní baa láa pée ká kitiŋ pu dooyee. Abin imuŋku ilee, m làá yàntī Eejipiti yab ń yàl̄ kí tin nín̄ bí atimbuncaan poon, kí nīn bí ntincamun.
13«Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ yii: Abin imuŋku ili boonee, m làá kóoǹní Eejipiti yab kí nyāntí atimbun ŋin poon bi yàl̄ ki bíńee kí kpāfì. 14M làá fàtīí gíiǹní iyumbu, m làá fàtīí gíiǹní-bi Eejipiti tiŋkin, ŋgiil pú, kitiŋ kin poon bi màl̄-bee. Bi làá fàtīí náań kibeewaai, 15dibeel din di làá nīn sá abee kɔkɔ poon kiwaayee, ní baa làá ti yīkì kí tɔ́kɔń atimbun ŋin kíǹee pu. M làá bàtī bi-wíiŋŋu pu án nín làá ŋá pu bí taa ti jī abee ŋin kíǹee pu dinyandee. 16Isirayeel yab kaa làá ti nín̄ báká bi-pu bí jòoń-bi. Isirayeel yab kaa làá ti yíiń Eejipiti yab ń dāá jòoń-bi kí gíti ŋá ikpiti. Niinee báà ŋma làá béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan.>»
Ubɔti Neebukadineesaar làá já kí fōō Eejipiti tiŋki
17Bi nín cúú Isirayeel yab ki cūnnì kuyuŋu abin mmuŋku nì aluli boon, uŋmapeekaa wimpeekaaŋuee, ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii: 18«Nisaaleen, Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar yāntì u-janjakitil ŋá ditumpɔɔl ki jáń nì Tiir yab. Bijanjaliibi gbanti kɔkɔ yiliŋ nìn ŋātì ní bi-gbigbipati fōō tiweendi, ama nì míǹ kɔkɔee, ubɔtaaa, u-janjaliibaaa, ubɔ kaa páatì ditundi din bi túń ki jáń nì Tiir tiŋkee pu. 19Too, man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M làá dū Eejipiti tiŋki kí ŋá Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar ŋaan. U làá fūkul̀-kì, kí yòon̄ ki-gaajawanti ní kí nàan̄-kì. Eejipiti gaajawanti di làá nīn sá u-janjaliibi paati. 20M làá dū Eejipiti ní ki tīī-u kí pà u-tundi paati, di sá yii man ní u-janjakitil túń ditundi ki tīī. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ.
21«Ŋwiin gbantee, m làá dāá kūtì Isirayeel yab mpɔn. Sii Eeseekiyeelee, m làá tīī-si ŋŋmam á sòoǹ nì bi. Niinee bi làá béé yii man di sá bi-Dindaan.»

english_text:
Egypt Will Be a Barren Desert
1The Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Egypt that I am saying:
Cry out in despair,
3because you will soon
be punished!
That will be a time
of darkness and doom
for all nations.
4Your own nation of Egypt
will be attacked,
and Ethiopia will suffer.
You will be killed in battle,
and your land will be robbed
and left in ruins.
5Soldiers hired from Ethiopia, Libya, Lydia, Arabia, Kub, as well as from Israel, will die in that battle. 6All of your allies will be killed, and your proud strength will crumble. People will die from Migdol in the north to Aswan in the south. I, the Lord, have spoken.
7Your nation of Egypt will be the most deserted place on earth, and its cities will lie in complete ruin. 8I will set fire to your land, and anyone who defended your nation will die. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
9On the same day I destroy Egypt, I will send messengers to the Ethiopians to announce their coming destruction. They think they are safe, but they will be terrified.
10Your Egyptian army is very strong, but I will send King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia to completely defeat that army. 11He and his cruel troops will invade and destroy your land and leave your dead bodies piled everywhere.
12I will dry up the Nile River, then sell the land to evil buyers. I will send foreigners to turn your entire nation into a barren desert. I, the Lord, have spoken.
Egypt's Proud Cities Will Lie in Ruins
The Lord said to the people of Egypt:
13All the idols and images you Egyptians worship in the city of Memphis will be smashed. No one will be left to rule your nation, and terror will fill the land. 14The city of Pathros will be left in ruins, and Zoan will be burned to the ground. Thebes, your capital city, will also be destroyed! 15The fortress city of Pelusium will feel my fierce anger, and all the troops stationed at Thebes will be slaughtered.
16I will set fire to your nation of Egypt! The city of Pelusium will be in anguish. Thebes will fall, and the people of Memphis will live in constant fear. 17The young soldiers in the cities of Heliopolis and Bubastis will die in battle, and the rest of the people will be taken prisoner. 18You were so proud of your nation's power, but when I crush that power and kill that pride, darkness will fall over the city of Tahpanhes. A dark, gloomy cloud will cover the land as you are being led away into captivity. 19When I'm through punishing Egypt, you will know that I am the Lord.
Egypt's King Is Powerless
20Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the seventh day of the first month. He said:
21Ezekiel, son of man, I, the Lord, have defeated the king of Egypt! I broke his arm, and no one has wrapped it or put it in a sling, so that it could heal and get strong enough to hold a sword. 22So tell him that I am now his worst enemy. I will break both his arms—the good one and the broken one! His sword will drop from his hand forever, 23and I will scatter the Egyptians all over the world.
24-25I will strengthen the power of Babylonia's king and give him my sword to use against Egypt. I will also make the wounded king of Egypt powerless, and he will moan in pain and die in front of the Babylonian king. Then everyone on earth will know that I am the Lord. 26I will force the Egyptians to live as prisoners in foreign nations, and they will know that I, the Lord, have punished them.
translation_text:
Ti-Dindaan làá yàntī u-ŋuul ń jēetí Eejipiti pu
1Ti-Dindaan gíti sòon̄ nì mi yii: 2«Nisaaleen, fōō m-bɔti kí nàatī kí lì yii: Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nyɔɔbundi sèé: <Nín̄ yáliŋkímaan iyunti in bí ki dòońee pu! 3Di sá yii ti-Dindaan wiiŋŋu dòoń, ŋu tóobiń. Án làá dāá nīn sá atagbambɔn wiiŋŋu ní, ŋwiin ŋun ní bi làá sòoǹ atimbun ŋin kíǹee bɔtee. 4Kujaau làá dāá nīn bí Eejipiti tiŋkin ní Eetiiyoopii ń kɔ́ dinyoondin. Bi làá dāá pɔ̀fì Eejipiti yab, kí fūkul̀ bi-gaajati ní kí nàan̄ bi-tiŋki. 5Bi làá dāá kpɔ̀ Eetiiyoopii yab nì Puuti yab nì Luudi yab nì Arabii yab nì Liibii yab kí kpáaǹ Isirayeel yab kujaaun. 6Man ni-Dindaan di sòon̄ yii, kí yòon̄ Miigidool ŋgan pú kí cáá sāā Asuwan ŋgiil púee, bi làá kpɔ̀ bin mɔ́tí Eejipiti puee dikɔ̀ndin, ní kí nàan̄ Eejipiti pɔŋŋu ŋun yòontí-kèe. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ. 7Eejipiti làá dāá kpántí kuteeu kun baasii kūń kitiŋ puee ní. Ki-timmu làá dāá kpántí adigbuŋkati ŋma ní. 8M yaa láa tūū Eejipiti tiŋki ŋŋmi ki kūū ki céetì bin mɔ́tí ki-puee kɔkɔee, ni làá dāá béé yii m sá ni-Dindaan. 9Ŋwiin gbantee, ituun làá dāá kɔ́ meela kí cùú yàntī Eetiiyoopii yab bin dàkafī yii bi bí ŋgbansɔŋfinee ń nyɔ̀ ŋkpatim. Ŋwiin ŋun m làá dāá nàan̄ Eejipitee, bin kóò Eetiiyoopiiyee làá dāá kɔ́ dinyoondin ní bi-wunti ń nīn jìkì. Ŋwiin gbanti tóobiń!>
10«Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <M làá dī Babiloon bɔtiu Neebukadineesaar pu ní kí kpɔ̀ kí céetí Eejipiti nipaaku nee. 11Úǹ nì u-nibul din néeń tipɔmbɔti ki jítiǹ binib kɔkɔee làá dāan̄ kí nàan̄ kitiŋ gbanti. Bi làá jáǹ Eejipiti yab ní kí yàntī anikpil ń gbí Eejipiti tiŋki. 12M làá yàntī Eejipiti buntaaŋi ń kpā ní kí dū Eejipiti yab kí ŋá binikpitib ŋaan. M làá yàntī binicambi ń nàan̄ kitiŋ gbanti ní kí fūkul̀ ki-gaajawanti kɔkɔ. Man ni-Dindaan di sòon̄.>
13«Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín gíti sòon̄ puee sèé: <M làá kúntí awaakpitikaa nì amakaa ŋin bí Meemifiisi tiŋkinee. Ubɔti dāa gíti kpá Eejipiti tiŋkin. M làá yàntī dinyoondi ń gbí kitiŋee kɔkɔ. 14M làá nàan̄ Eejipiti tiŋki ŋgiil pú, kí tūū Soowan tiŋki ŋŋmi ní kí sòoǹ Teebi tiŋki bɔti kí dáaĺ ki-tafal. 15M làá kpáatí m-bum kí sìtī Siini tiŋki kin di wúń Eejipiti tiŋki puee. M làá kúntí Teebi nipaaku nee. 16M làá tūū Eejipiti tiŋki ŋŋmi. Siini yab làá kɔ́ dinyoondin. Bi làá sāā kí cíĺ digundi din māntìi tú Teebi tiŋkee ní nnyim ń gbí kí léeń ki-pu. 17Bi làá dāá kpɔ̀ Ooni nì Pii-Beeseeti naacimpɔmbi kujaaun ní kí cúú binib bin kíǹee kí cùnnì kuyuŋu. 18M yaa láa nāaǹ Eejipiti pɔŋŋu ki kúntì ki-lambil din kì cáá mpɔn gbanti puee, kutaa kaa làá dāá wúntí Tapaneesi tiŋki pu. Ditagbambɔndi làá dāá bìin̄ kitiŋee pu ní ki-nib ń búntí kuyuŋu. 19M làá dāá sòoǹ Eejipiti bɔti kí dáaĺ ki-tafal ní báà ŋma ń béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan.>»
Babiloon bɔtiu, Unimbɔti tɔntɔŋwanti
20Bi nín cúú Isirayeel yab kuyuŋu abin saalaa nì diba boon, uŋmapeekaa winluluútiŋuee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii: 21«Nisaaleen, m nyīī ki kɔ́fì Eejipiti bɔtiu Faaroo ŋal. Ubɔ kaa bí ki dáaĺ-u àá ki ŋá-u nnyɔkɔ. Ubɔ mun kaa tí nyàab̄ kiŋaabiki ki fìn̄-u ú bàà fàtīí ká mpɔn kí ŋúb́ kitàataajiki. 22Too, man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ yii m làá jáǹ Faaroo, Eejipiti bɔtiu. M làá nyīī kí kɔ̄fì u-ŋalii, ŋun pée kɔ́fèe nì ŋun dáá pɔ̄ɔ̄yee. U-tàataajiki làá ŋmátíí nyā u-ŋaan kí lítí. 23Niinee ní ḿ jà Eejipiti yab kí kɔ́ǹ atimbun aban, m làá yàaǹ-bi kí kɔ́ǹ ntincamun. 24M làá kūtì Babiloon bɔtiu mpɔn ní kí dū man m-ba tàataajiki kí ŋúbiǹ-u. M làá nyīī kí kɔ̄fì Faaroo ŋalii, ní ú nīn dɔ̄ ki yáliŋkí u-nannanliu nimbiin kii unil un bi tīī tiweendi waa ti làá ŋmátée. 25M làá kūtì Babiloon bɔtiu ŋalii mpɔn, ama ní Faaroo yai ń nīn jòon̄ fám. M làá dū man m-ba tàataajiki kí ŋúbiǹ-u ní ú dū-kì kí jáǹ Eejipiti yab. Niinee báà ŋma làá béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan. 26M làá yàntī Eejipiti yab ń yàl̄ kí kɔ́ atimbun aban, m làá yàaǹ-bi kí kɔ́ǹ ntincamun. Niinee bi làá béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan.»

english_text:
Egypt's King Will Be Chopped Down like a Cedar Tree
1Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the third month. He said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, tell the king of Egypt and his people that I am saying:
You are more powerful
than anyone on earth.
Now listen to this.
3There was once a cedar tree
in Lebanon
with large, strong branches
reaching to the sky.
4This tree had plenty of water
to help it grow tall,
and nearby streams watered
the other trees
in the forest.
5But this tree towered over
those other trees,
and its branches
grew long and thick.
6Birds built nests
in its branches,
and animals were born
beneath it.
People from all nations
lived in the shade
of this strong tree.
7It had beautiful,
long branches,
and its roots found water
deep in the soil.
8 None of the cedar trees
in my garden of Eden
were as beautiful
as this tree;
no tree of any kind
had such long branches.
9I, the Lord, gave this tree
its beauty,
and I helped the branches
grow strong.
All other trees in Eden
wanted to be just like it.
10King of Egypt, now listen to what I, the Lord God, am saying about that tree:
The tree grew so tall that it reached the sky and became very proud and arrogant. 11So I, the Lord God, will reject the tree and hand it over to a foreign ruler, who will punish it for its wickedness. 12Cruel foreigners will chop it down and leave it wherever it falls. Branches and broken limbs will be scattered over the mountains and in the valleys. The people living in the shade of those branches will go somewhere else. 13Birds will then nest on the stump of the fallen tree, and wild animals will trample its branches.
14Never again will any tree dare to grow as tall as this tree, no matter how much water it has. Every tree must die, just as humans die and go down to the world of the dead.
15On the day this tree dies and goes to the world below, I, the Lord God, will command rivers and streams to mourn its death. Every underground spring of water and every river will stop flowing. The mountains in Lebanon will be covered with darkness as a sign of their sorrow, and all the trees in the forest will wither. 16This tree will crash to the ground, and I will send it to the world below. Then the nations of the earth will tremble.
The trees from Eden and the choice trees from Lebanon are now in the world of the dead, and they will be comforted when this tree falls. 17Those people who found protection in its shade will also be sent to the world below, where they will join the dead.
18King of Egypt, all these things will happen to you and your people! You were like this tree at one time—taller and stronger than anyone on earth. But now you will be chopped down, just as every tree in the garden of Eden must die. You will be sent down to the world of the dead, where you will join the godless and the other victims of violent death. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_text:
Bi dū Eejipiti bɔtiu ki ŋmāntiǹ seedir subu
1Bi nín cúú Isirayeel yab ki cūnnì kuyuŋu abin saalaa nì diba boon, uŋmatataati wimpeekaaŋuee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii: 2«Nisaaleen, tùkù Eejipiti bɔtiu Faaroo nì kunipaau kun pu u kā dibeelee yii:
<Sii un cáá mpɔŋkpaan nee,
m làá dū-si kí ŋmàntīǹ ba dee?
3A náań nì Leebanɔn subu bun bi yíì seedir
bu cáá apan ŋin ŋān̄
ki tìì mboon ŋun taapu sɔ̀m̀ fílfilee ní.
Busubuee fɔ̀kɔ̀ tiŋan
ní bu-yilpu tùutī atagban.
4Ntaanyim yāntì bu wíiǹ.
Kitiŋ taapu buŋŋu ŋubɔ yāntì bu yíkì ki jɔ́m̀.
Nnyim nìn kōontí kí màntīí tū bu-nyaaŋyi,
ní kí pùub̀ kí cù tisatin sufii kɔkɔ cee.
5Nnyim min u nìn kāntí tikpilee puee,
bu nìn wíiǹ ki jítiǹ isufi in kíǹee kɔkɔ.
U nìn cáá apan náaǹ ki lālim̀ ki cūtì ndan.
6Inoon kɔkɔ nì i-bulifi nìn pāantí i-diti bu-paŋŋi pu.
Ipeel kɔkɔ nìn dɔ̀ ŋi-taapu ki màal̀
ní atimbun tikpil nìn kóò ŋi-booŋyi taapu.
7Busubuee nìn ŋān̄ ní ki fɔ̀kɔ̀
ní bu-paŋŋi béetì tiŋan pu,
di sá yii bu-nyaaŋyi nìn kóò kitiŋ taapu taapu
laakin nnyim wīikée.
8Unimbɔti kpaabunee,
seedir subu bubɔ kaa bí bí dū-bu kí ŋmàntīǹ,
siipreesi subu bubɔ kaa cáá apan ŋān̄ kii bu-yaŋee,
plataani subu bubɔ faati kaa bàn̄ bu-faati
ní busubu bubɔ kaa bí bukpaayee poon ki ŋān̄ nì bu.
9M nìn tīī-u apan ŋin ŋān̄ee
áli gba Unimbɔti kpaabu Eedeen
sufii kɔkɔ nìn cáá bu-pu ipoompoon ní.>»
Eejipiti bɔtiu làá kɔ̄fì kii seedir subuee
10«Too, man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Buseedirisubu wíiǹ. Bu yíkì ki tūū atagban ní ki kpántì ulambidaan. 11An pu ní m dū-bu ki fá ní ki dū-bu ki ŋá kitiŋ pu bɔtiu un pɔ̄ɔ̄yee ŋaan. Busubuee nín ŋá ikpiti puee, míǹ ní ubɔtee làá ŋá-bu kí téeǹ. 12Binicambi bin néeń tipɔmbɔti tikpilee gāā-bu ki lúkú ní ki fātì bi-boon ki tīī-bu. Bu-paŋŋi kɔkɔ lítì ki dɔ̄ kitiŋee jooŋŋi pu nì ki-tantakaŋin. Binib bin kɔkɔ nìn kóò bu-booŋŋu taapuee yíkì ki dū kitiŋee ki fá. 13Inoon kɔkɔ nì i-bulifi dòoń ki tɔ̄kɔntí bu-dɔŋu pu ní ipeel kɔkɔ yùkufī ki póotí bu-paŋŋi pu. 14Tin bí nee kɔkɔ ŋá míǹ án nín làá ŋá pu isufi in yú ibun caŋinee bubɔ ń taa tí kɔ́ dilambilin kí wíiǹ kí tūū atagban, ní isufi in kāntí ntaanyimee bubɔ ń taa yòon̄ bu-ba yilpu kí fɔ̀kɔn̄ kí jītíǹ in kíǹee. Di sá yii isufi nì binib kɔkɔ bí kí kpú ŋwindal. Bi-kɔkɔ làá kɔ́ kitiŋ taapu kí cùú ŋàl̄ bin kpíì ki dɔ̄ niinee.>
15«Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Daliŋkin seedir subu nín cá ditaŋkpiilinee, m nìn yāntì tin kɔkɔ bí duulinyanee kāl̀ dikpool ní. Bu-puee, m yāntì mmɔɔnyim min bí kitiŋ taapuee bīiǹ bu-pu. M yāntì mi-buŋyi yúl̀, m cúú mi-nyim mí taa ti pùub̀. Bu-puee, m yāntì Leebanɔn bambaŋku kɔ́ dibɔmbɔndin ní ki yāntì tisatin sufii kɔkɔ kūń. 16M nín yāntì busubuee lítì kí cùú ŋàl̄ bin bí ditaŋkpiilinee, atimbun nib gbìl̄ ní ki kɔ́ dinyoondin. Ditaŋkpiilin niinee ní an mɔ́ɔkiǹ Eedeen kpaabun sufii nì Leebanɔn sufii in ŋān̄ ki kāntí ntaanyim tiŋanee. 17Bi mun kútì seediree pu ki sīntì ditaŋkpiilin ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ bin di kpíì kujaaunee. Bíǹ di nìn tíkí-u ní ki nìn kóò bu-booŋŋu taapu atimbun kansikin.>
18«Eedeen kpaabunee, busubu bubɔ kaa ŋān̄ àá ki wíiǹ ki bàn̄-si. Ama m làá yàntī sii nì bíǹ kɔkɔ ń sìntī kitiŋ taapu. Niinee sii nì bin kaa gíí dikpancandee nì bin kpíì kujaaunee di làá kpāfi kí dòon̄. Kun di làá bàń Eejipiti bɔtiu Faaroo nì u-samaau puee dee. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄.»

english_text:
A Funeral Song for the King of Egypt
1Twelve years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the twelfth month. He said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the king of Egypt and tell him I am saying:
You act like a lion
roaming the earth;
but you are nothing more than
a crocodile in a river,
churning up muddy water
with your feet.
3King of Egypt, listen to me. I, the Lord God, will catch you in my net and let a crowd of foreigners drag you to shore. 4I will throw you into an open field, where birds and animals will come to feed on your flesh. 5I will spread your rotting flesh over the mountains and in the valleys, 6and your blood will flow throughout the land and fill up the streams. 7 I will cover the whole sky and every star with thick clouds, so that the sun and moon will stop shining. 8The heavens will become black, leaving your country in total darkness. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
9Foreign nations you have never heard of will be shocked when I tell them how I destroyed you. 10They will be horrified, and when I flash my sword in victory on the day of your death, their kings will tremble in the fear of what could happen to them.
11The king of Babylonia is coming to attack you, king of Egypt! 12Your soldiers will be killed by the cruelest army in the world, and everything you take pride in will be crushed. 13I will slaughter your cattle that graze by the river, and no people or livestock will be left to muddy its water. 14The water will be clear, and streams will be calm. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
15Egypt will become a barren wasteland, and no living thing will ever survive there. Then you and your people will know that I am the Lord.
16This is your warning, and it will be used as a funeral song by foreign women to mourn the death of your people. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
A Sad Ending for Egypt
17On the fifteenth day of that same month, the Lord said:
18Ezekiel, son of man, mourn for the Egyptians and condemn them to the world of the dead, where they will be buried alongside the people of other powerful nations. 19Say to them:
You may be more beautiful
than the people
of other nations,
but you will also die
and join the godless
in the world below.
20You cannot escape! The enemy's sword is ready to slaughter every one of you. 21Brave military leaders killed in battle will gladly welcome you and your allies into the world of the dead.
22-23The graves of soldiers from Assyria are there. They once terrified people, but they were killed in battle and now lie deep in the world of the dead.
24-25The graves of soldiers from Elam are there. The very sight of those godless soldiers once terrified their enemies and made them panic. But now they are disgraced and ashamed as they lie in the world of the dead, alongside others who were killed in battle.
26The graves of soldiers from Meshech and Tubal are there. These godless soldiers who terrified people were all killed in battle. 27They were not given a proper burial like the heroes of long ago, who were buried with their swords under their heads and with their shields over their bodies. These were the heroes who made their enemies panic.
28You Egyptians will be cruelly defeated, and you will be buried alongside these other godless soldiers who died in battle.
29The graves of kings and leaders from Edom are there. They were powerful at one time. Now they are buried in the world of the dead with other godless soldiers killed in battle.
30The graves of the rulers of the north are there, as well as those of the Sidonians. Their powerful armies once terrified enemies. Now they lie buried in the world of the dead, where they are disgraced like other soldiers killed in battle.
31The Lord God says:
When your king of Egypt sees all of these graves, he and his soldiers will be glad they are not the only ones suffering. 32I sent him to terrify people all over the earth. But he and his army will be killed and buried alongside other godless soldiers in the world of the dead. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_text:
Eejipiti nì ki-bɔtiu kpiisilaŋŋu
1Bi nín cúú Isirayeel yab ki cūnnì kuyuŋu abin saalaa nì ali boon, uŋmal saalaa nì uliliiti wimpeekaaŋu dalee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii: 2«Nisaaleen, gāā Eejipiti bɔtiu Faaroo ŋkpiisilan nee yii:
<A bí atimbun kansikin kii digbikintipɔmbilee ní.
Ama a nìn bí kii upɔɔnyaanee ní ki bí tiŋkun.
A nìn yíkí ki dèentí nnyim pu.
A nìn cáá a-taaŋi ki gbàtī nnyim.
A nìn kùtī ibun nyim ki gbàtī-mì.
3Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti sòon̄ yii binib tikpil yaa láa kpáfèe, m làá dāá tɔ̄ m-laaŋku a-pu ní an cúú-si ní bí dáaĺ kí nyāntí dimɔɔgbandi. 4M làá dāá dū-si kí lúkú kitiŋ ní kí dū-si kí tɔ̄ tisatin inoon kɔkɔ ń gbáb́ kí bìin̄ a-pu ní ipeel ń dāan̄ kí ŋmɔ́ a-wunti. 5M làá dāá dū a-wunti laakin kíǹee kí yàaǹ ajoon pu ní kí yàntī án gbí atantaka. 6M làá dāá dū a-fatikuu kí yàaǹ kitiŋ pu. An làá dāá bìin̄ ajoon pu kí gbí mbùmbiyaamu. 7A yaa kaa láa gíti bí dimaŋfalinee, m làá dāá dū tiba kí bìin̄ kutagbɔŋu pu ní iŋmalbijaa ń kpántí dibɔmbɔndi. M làá dū atagban kí bìin̄ ŋwìiń pu ní uŋmal kaa ti làá nīn ŋmíntí. 8A-puee, m làá yàntī iwalfi in kɔkɔ bí yilpuee ń kpántí dibɔmbɔndi ní kí yàntī kunyeeu ń mɔ́ a-tiŋki pu. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ. 9Anibul tikpil ki kpáaǹ ntimu mun ní a nyée nib yaa láa gbìl̄ m nín yāntì nnaabu ŋun jítì a-pueeyee, bi-pɔbiliŋ làá dāá bīil̀. 10Sii puee, anibul tikpil làá dāá kɔ́ kunimbaaun. M yaa láa tāntì m-tàataajiki bi-bɔtiibi nimbiinee, bi làá dāá kɔ́ dinyoondin. Ŋwiin ŋun a làá dāá lítée, bi-wunti làá dāá nīn jìkì di sá yii báà ŋma dāa kíǹ ki sūǹ u-ba pu ní.
11«<Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Babiloon bɔtiu janjaliibi làá cíliń a-pu. 12M làá tɔ̄ń bijanjaliibi bin néeń tipɔmbɔti ki jítiǹ báà ŋmee bí kpɔ̀ a-nib cutimaanyi nee. Bi làá nàan̄ Eejipiti ulambidaan ní kí kpɔ̀ kí céetí ki-nib kɔkɔ múb. 13M làá yàntī tiwaŋkuti tin a cáá Niil mɔɔgbandee kɔkɔ ń kpú. Binib àá tiwaŋkuti taaŋi kaa làá ti tāā kí gbàtī nnyim. 14M làá yàntī mí ŋùŋfì. Mì làá nīn dɔ̄ ki ŋùŋfī soooo kii ŋkpamee ní. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ. 15M làá yàntī Eejipiti tiŋki ń kpántí kii kuteeuee ní. M làá nyāntí tin kɔkɔ bí ki-poonee ní kí kpɔ̀ kí céetí ki-nib. Niinee bi làá béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan.>
16«Atimbun kɔkɔ nimpoobi nín làá dāá gāā Eejipiti tiŋki nì ki-nib kuwaawiiu pu ŋkpiisilan ŋuŋyee dee. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄.»
Anibul ŋin bi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹee yaliŋkii
17Bi nín cúú Isirayeel yab ki cūnnì kuyuŋu abin saalaa nì ali boon, uŋmal saalaa nì uliliiti iwiin saalku dalee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii: 18«Nisaaleen, yāliŋkì Eejipiti yab kɔkɔ pu. A-yaliŋkii ń kpáaǹ bi nì atimbuŋkpaan ŋin kíǹee kí sìntī ditaŋkpiilin, laakin bin kpíìyee sìntēe. 19Tùkù-bi yii: A dàkafī yii a sɔ́ǹ bin kíǹee níii? Nín̄ sìntī ditaŋkpiilin kí cùú dòon̄ kí ŋàl̄ bin kaa gíí dikpancandee pu. 20Di sá yii bi làá kpɔ̀ Eejipiti yab dikɔ̀ndin ní. Ntàataajimu bɔ́ntì kí kpɔ̀ binib. Mú kpɔ̀ Eejipiti yab nì bi-janjakitil kɔkɔ. 21Ditaŋkpiilinee, bibaatandambi nì bin nìn kútì Eejipiti yab pu bi jáńee làá dāá téeń yii: <Bin ní bi kūū kujaaunee, bi nín sìntī kí cùú dòon̄ kí ŋàl̄ bin kaa gíí dikpancandee pu.>
22«Asuur bɔtiu nì u-janjakitil bí niin. U-janjaliibi kaakuliŋ māntìi tú-u. Bi kūū bi-kɔkɔ kujaaun ní. 23Bi-kaakuliŋ bí ditaŋkpiilin taapu taapu ki māntìi tú ubɔti kaakul. Bíǹ bin di nìn yàntī binifoobi kóò dinyoondinee, bi kūū bi-kɔkɔ kujaaun.
24«Eelam bɔtiu nì u-janjakitil bí niin. U-janjaliibi kaakuliŋ māntìi tú-u. Bi kūū bi-kɔkɔ kujaaun ní. Bíǹ bin kaa gíí dikpancandi ki nìn fàantí binifoobee sīntìń kitiŋ taapu. Kɔŋkɔnnee, bi kútì bin kɔkɔ sīntì ditaŋkpiilinee pu ki tú icoo gbòooo. 25Eelam bɔtiu nì u-janjakitil dɔ̄ bin bi kūū kujaaunee kansikin. U-janjaliibi kaakuliŋ māntìi tú-u. Bin baa gíí dikpancandi nee kɔkɔee, kujaaun ní bi kūū-bi. Bíǹ puee, binib wunti nìn gbáà ní kpàkpakpa binifoobi tiŋkin. Kɔŋkɔnnee, bi kútì bin kɔkɔ bi kūū kujaaunee pu ki tú icoo gbòooo.
26«Meeseeki nì Tuubaal bɔtiibi mun bí niin, bi nì bi-janjakitil. Bi-janjaliibi kaakuliŋ māntìi tú-bi. Bin baa gíí dikpancandi nee kɔkɔee, kujaaun ní bi kūū-bi. Bíǹ puee, binib wunti nìn gbáà ní kpàkpakpa binifoobi tiŋkin. 27Baa síb́-bi cannaaku baatandambi bin nìn fàantí binib binifoobi tiŋkinee cee. Bi nín sìntī ditaŋkpiilin ki ŋúb́ bi-janjawanti. Bi dū bi-tàataajimmu ki kūĺ bi-yiliŋ ní ki dū bi-gbampɔɔŋi ki páaǹ bi-pu. 28Eejipiti yab, ni mun yuntiŋu bāań dee, ni làá kpú ní bí síb́-ni bin kaa gíí dikpancandi ki kpíì kujaaunee kansikin.
29«Eedoom yab nì bi-bɔtiibi nì bi-bɔtibiliŋ mun bí niin. Nì min kamaa bi cáá dipɔbilee, bi dū-bi ki kútì bin bi kūū kujaaunee pu. Bi síb́-bi ki kútì bin kaa gíí dikpancandi ki sīntì ditaŋkpiilinee pu.
30«Ŋgan pú nibuliŋ kpootiliibi mun bí niin, ki kpáaǹ Siidɔn yab bin sīntì ditaŋkpiilinee. Bi nìn sá bibaatandambi ní binib nìn fàŋkí-bi yɔ́kɔ́ yɔkɔ. Ama kɔŋkɔnnee, binib bin baa gíí dikpancandi gbantee kpíì ki cūtìi ŋàl̄ bin bi kūū kujaaunee pu. Bi tú icoo ní gbòooo, bi nì bin kɔkɔ bí ditaŋkpiilinee.
31«Faaroo yaa láa ká bijanjaliibi gbanti kɔkɔ niinee, án làá dāá ŋméeǹ-u tin bāań u-janjaliibee pu. Di sá yii bi làá kpɔ̀ u nì u-janjaliibi kujaaun. Man ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄. 32M yāntì Faaroo kɔ́ǹ binib dinyoondi binifoobi tiŋkin. Ama kɔŋkɔnnee, bi làá síb́ úǹ u-ba nì u-janjaliibi binib bin kaa gíí dikpancandi ki kpíì kujaaunee kansikin. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄.»

english_text:
The Lord Appoints Ezekiel To Stand Watch
(Ezekiel 3.16-21)
1The Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, warn your people by saying:
Someday, I, the Lord, may send an enemy to invade a country. And suppose its people choose someone to stand watch 3and to sound a warning signal when the enemy is seen coming. 4-5If any of these people hear the signal and ignore it, they will be killed in battle. But it will be their own fault, because they could have escaped if they had paid attention.
6But suppose the person watching fails to sound the warning signal. The enemy will attack and kill some of the sinful people in that country, and I, the Lord, will hold that person responsible for their death.
7Ezekiel, I have appointed you to stand watch for the people of Israel. So listen to what I say, then warn them for me. 8When I tell wicked people they will die because of their sins, you must warn them to turn from their sinful ways. But if you refuse to warn them, you are responsible for their death. 9If you do warn them, and they keep sinning, they will die because of their sins, and you will be innocent.
The Lord Is Always Fair
(Ezekiel 18.21-30)
10The Lord said:
Ezekiel, son of man, the people of Israel are complaining that the punishment for their sins is more than they can stand. They have lost all hope for survival, and they blame me. 11Tell them that as surely as I am the living Lord God, I don't like to see wicked people die. I enjoy seeing them turn from their sins and live. So if the Israelites want to live, they must stop sinning and turn back to me.
12Tell them that when good people start sinning, all the good they did in the past cannot save them from being punished. And remind them that when wicked people stop sinning, their past sins will be completely forgiven, and they won't be punished.
13Suppose I promise good people that they will live, then later they start sinning and believe they will be saved by the good they did in the past. These people will certainly be put to death because of their sins. Their good deeds will be forgotten.
14Suppose I warn wicked people that they will die because of their sins, and they stop sinning and start doing right. 15For example, they need to return anything they have taken as security for a loan and anything they have stolen. Then if they stop doing evil and start obeying my Law, they will live. 16Their past sins will be forgiven, and they will live because they have done right.
17Ezekiel, your people accuse me of being unfair. But they are the ones who are unfair. 18If good people start doing evil, they will be put to death, because they have sinned. 19And if wicked people stop sinning and start doing right, they will save themselves from punishment. 20But the Israelites still think I am unfair. So warn them that they will be punished for what they have done.
The News of Jerusalem's Fall
21 Twelve years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, a refugee who had escaped from Jerusalem came to me on the fifth day of the tenth month. He told me that the city had fallen.
22The evening before this man arrived at my house, the Lord had taken control of me. So when the man came to me the next morning, I could once again speak.
What Will Happen to Those Left in Israel?
23Then the Lord said:
24Ezekiel, son of man, the people living in the ruined cities of Israel are saying, “Abraham was just one man, and the Lord gave him this whole land of Israel. There are many of us, and so this land must be ours.”
25So, Ezekiel, tell them I am saying:
How can you think the land is still yours? You eat meat with blood in it and worship idols. You commit murder 26and spread violence throughout the land. Everything you do is wicked; you are even unfaithful in marriage. And you claim the land is yours!
27As surely as I am the living Lord God, you people in the ruined cities will be killed in battle. Those of you living in the countryside will be eaten by wild animals, and those hiding in caves and on rocky cliffs will die from deadly diseases. 28I will make the whole country an empty wasteland and crush the power in which you take such pride. Even the mountains will be bare, and no one will try to cross them. 29I will punish you because of your sins, and I will turn your nation into a barren desert. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
The People Listen, but Don't Change
The Lord said:
30Ezekiel, son of man, the people with you in Babylonia talk about you when they meet by the city walls or in the doorways of their houses. They say, “Let's ask Ezekiel what the Lord has said today.” 31So they all come and listen to you, but they refuse to do what you tell them. They claim to be faithful, but they are forever trying to cheat others out of their money. 32They treat you as though you were merely singing love songs or playing music. They listen, but don't do anything you say.
33Soon they will be punished, just as you warned, and they will know that a prophet has been among them.
translation_text:
Unimbɔti dū Eeseekiyeel ki kāaǹ uciitil
(Kpèè 3.16-21)
1Ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: 2«Nisaaleen, sòoǹ nì Isirayeel yab kí tùkù-bi yii: M yaa dū kujaau ki tɔ́ kitiŋ kiba puee, kitiŋ gbanti yab lèekī bi-kansikin ubɔ ní ú nīn sá bi-ciitiliu. 3Uciitilee yaa wál̀ bijanjaliibi dòoń kí jáǹ-bee, u búǹ ŋyin ní kí kpāafì samaa. 4Ubɔ yaa gbìl̄ ŋyin pu ní kaa fātìi tɔ́ ní bi yaa dɔ́miń ki kūū-uee, udaan kúm kpuulool làá lítí úǹ u-ba pu ní. 5U gbìl̄ bi nín búń ŋyinee ní kaa fātìi tɔ́. U-kúm kpuulool làá fàtīí gítí úǹ u-ba pu ní. U yaa bàà dūu túń ditundee, u bàà fìil̄ u-ba ní. 6Ama uciitilee yaa wál̀ bijanjaliibi dòoń kí jáǹ-bi ní waa búń ŋyinee, samaa kaa làá béé yii tiba bí ki dòoń. Unannanli yaa dūu túuǹ ubɔ ki kūū-uee, uciitilee bɔti dee. M làá dāá bàlifì uciitil un bi kūūyee fatikuu pu.
7«Nisaaleen, sii ní m dūu síiǹ á nīn sá Isirayeel nibul pu uciitil. Á pīlifì m-nyɔɔbuŋŋi kí dūú nàatī Isirayeel yab kí kpāafì-bi. 8M yaa tùkū unikpiti yii: <Unikpiti, a làá pée kpú ní>, ama ní sii kaa kpáafì-u ú kpántí u-bimbimee, unikpiti gbanti làá kpú u-kpitii pu, ama sii ní m làá dāá bàlifì u-fatikuu pu. 9Ama a yaa kpáafì unikpiti ú bàà kpántí u-bimbim ní waa kpántèe, u làá kpú u-kpitii pu ní sii ń fīī a-ba.»
Unikpiti un gítìń Unimbɔti ceeyee kāntí dimaŋfal
10«Sii nisaaleen, tùkù Isirayeel yab bi nín bí ki lì yii: <Ti-yìntitam nì ti-kpitii nyìm̀ ti-pu. I-puee, taa ti cáá mpɔn báà fiii. Ti làá ŋá mana ní kí ŋmátí nan?> 11Tùkù-bi yii m bí dimaŋfalin! Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ yii, unikpiti kúm bɔti kaa mɔ̄ǹ-mi. Kun m pée nyàab̀ee di sá ú kpántí u-bimbim kí nīn bí dimaŋfalin. Isirayeel yab, m gbàam̄-ni ní, fámaan ni-bimbikpitim. Ba pu ní ni là kí kpú ní?
12«Sii nisaaleen, tùkù a-nibul yab yii: <Deedeedaan yaa kíĺ ki bíi ŋáań tin kaa ŋān̄ee, deedee tuuŋŋi ŋin u ŋá an jítèe kaa làá fīī-u. Ama unikpiti yaa fá u-bimbikpitim, ikpiti in u ŋá an jítèe kaa làá yàntī ú wāŋkì. An puee deedeedaan yaa kíĺ ki bíi ŋáań ikpitee, deedee tuuŋŋi ŋin u nìn ŋá dooooyee kaa làá ŋmā kí fīī-u. 13M yaa pōoǹ kí tīī deedeedaan dimaŋfal ní u dākafì yii deedee tuuŋŋi ŋin u ŋá an jítèe wíiǹ ní u kíĺ ki bíi ŋáań ikpitee, bi làá súntí u-deedee tuuŋŋee kɔkɔ pu ní ú kpú ikpiti in ní u ŋée pu. 14Ama m yaa kpáafì unikpiti yii u máaǹ ŋkúm ní u fá u-bimbikpitim ki kíĺ ki kíǹ ki bíi ŋáań tin kítèe nì tin bí deedeeyee, waa làá kpú. 15U yaa gíiǹ toolima un ubɔ cáań ki yóoǹ u-ceeyee ki tīī-u, àá u gíiǹ tin u yùn̄ee ki tīī uwandaan ki kíĺ ki kíǹ ki tɔ́ marab bin tìì dimaŋfalee, ní kaa ti bíi ŋáań ikpitee, udaan làá pée ŋmátí ní, waa làá kpú. 16Bi làá súntí u-tuŋkpitiŋ ŋin ní u ŋée kɔkɔ pu ní ú ŋmátí, di sá yii u kíĺ ki bíi ŋáań tin kítèe nì tin bí deedeeyee.
17«A-tiŋkin nib lì yii man ni-Dindaan nín ŋáań puee kaa kítì. Ama an sá bíǹ nín ŋáań puee di kaa kítì! 18Deedeedaan yaa gbēeǹ kaa ti bíi ŋáań deedee tuuŋŋi ní ki bíi ŋáań tikpitilee, see ú kpú. 19Ama unikpiti yaa fá u-bimbikpitim ní ki kíĺ ki bíi ŋáań deedee tuuŋŋi nì tin kítèe, u làá ŋmátí an pu.
20«Ama ní nimbi Isirayeel yab lì yii man nín ŋáań puee kaa kítì! Too, ní béé yii m làá sòoǹ báà ŋma bɔti kí nóó nì tin u ŋée ní!>»
Isirayeel tiŋki kpántì adigbuŋkati ŋma
21Bi nín cúú Isirayeel yab ki cūnnì kuyuŋu abin saalaa nì ali boon, uŋmal usaalaati wiŋŋmooŋmootiŋu dalee, uninja ubɔ nìn sáǹ ki nyáń bin jáń ki fōō Jeerusaleem tiŋkee ŋaan ní u bí-mi yii: «Bi jáń ki fōō Jeerusaleem tiŋki!» 22Kí wàatī ú bàń m-cee kujoouee ní ti-Dindaan yāntì m gbìl̄ u-pɔŋŋu m-ni ní m kíǹ ki ŋūǹ kí sòoǹ. Kutaa wúntì ŋyunti ŋun un sáǹ ki ŋmátèe bāań m-ceeyee, maa nìn gíti sá umuun, m nìn kíǹ ki ŋūǹ kí sòoǹ. 23Ní ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: 24«Nisaaleen, binib bin kíǹ ki kóò Isirayeel timmu mun kpántì adigbuŋkatee lì yii: <Abraam nìn bí u-baba ní, ama ní ki nìn yì kitiŋ nee kɔkɔ. Kin ataa aŋa pu ní baa làá dū kitiŋ nee kí tīī timbi bin wīikí nee tí nīn yì.> 25Too, tùkù-bi tin man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti cáá kí sòoǹ nì bee yii: <Ni ŋmóò tinan tin poon ní fatiku kēe, ki tòotī awaa, ki kù binib, kin mana ní ni ŋūǹ kí lì yii nimbi di yì kitiŋ nee>. 26Ni-janjawanti ŋmaniŋma pu ní ni máká. Ni ŋáań ntimbiil tuuŋŋi, ki fòol̄ ni-jutiibi nimpoobi, kin mana ní ni ŋūǹ kí lì yii nimbi di yì kitiŋ nee?
27«Tùkù-bi yii man bi-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <M bí dimaŋfalin! M bíi tùkù-ni yii bin kíǹ ki bí ntimu mun kpántì adigbuŋkatee poonee, bi làá dū ntàataajimu kí kpɔ̀-bi, ní ipeecuncuti ń tɔ̀ntī bin bí tisatinee ní bìlbil kúm ń kpɔ̀ bin sáǹ ki bál̀ ajoon pu nì itaŋkpalɔkɔnee. 28M làá nàan̄ kitiŋ nee ní kí yàntī kí kpántí kuteeu. Mpɔn ŋun di nìn yàntī bin kóò kinee cáá dilambilee làá kúntí. Isirayeel jooŋŋi làá kpántí kii kuteeuee ní, ubɔ kaa làá ti dī niin kí cù laaba.> 29M làá yàntī kitiŋ nee ń kpántí kii kuteeuee ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin Isirayeel yab ŋáaǹee pu. Ŋyunti gbantee, bi làá béé yii man di sá bi-Dindaan.
30«Nisaaleen, pīlifì, a-tiŋkin nib kpáfí digundi din bi máń ki tú kitiŋee caŋin àá bi-diiŋŋi nyɔkɔpu ki sòoǹ a-bɔti. Bi sòoǹ nì tɔb yii: <Tí cùú pīlifì tin ti-Dindaan cáá kí tùkù-tee>. 31Niinee ní a-tiŋkin yab ń kóoǹ kí kpāfì ki kā a-nimbiin kí pīlifì tin a cáá kí sòoǹee, ama baa tɔ́ tin a sòoǹee. Bi nín là puee ní bi ŋáań ní ki nyàab̀ bíǹ bi-ba paatii. 32Tiŋmanee, a bí kii ulaŋgaanyaan un neen mɔ̄ bi bɔ̀ɔ́ tibɔɔkaal ki kìntēe ní. Bi pílifí a-bɔti, ama ní kaa cáa tūǹ nì ditundi. 33Tin a sòon̄ nee kɔkɔ yaa láa bāań, ní an lafun dòoń mun, bi làá dāá béé yii ubɔnaatil ubɔ nìn kāl̀ bi-kansikin.»

english_text:
Israel's Leaders Are Worthless Shepherds
1 The Lord God said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, Israel's leaders are like shepherds taking care of my sheep, the people of Israel. But I want you to condemn these leaders and tell them:
I, the Lord God, say you shepherds of Israel are doomed! You take care of yourselves while ignoring my sheep. 3You drink their milk and use their wool to make your clothes. Then you butcher the best ones for food. But you don't take care of the flock! 4You have never protected the weak ones or healed the sick ones or bandaged those that get hurt. You let them wander off and never look for those that get lost. You are cruel and mean to my sheep. 5 They strayed in every direction, and because there was no shepherd to watch them, they were attacked and eaten by wild animals. 6So my sheep were scattered across the earth. They roamed on hills and mountains, without anyone even bothering to look for them.
7-8Now listen to what I, the living Lord God, am saying to you shepherds. My sheep have been attacked and eaten by wild animals, because you refused to watch them. You never went looking for the lost ones, and you fed yourselves without feeding my sheep. 9-10So I, the Lord, will punish you! I will rescue my sheep from you and never let you be their shepherd again or butcher them for food. I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Lord Is the Good Shepherd
11The Lord God then said:
I will look for my sheep and take care of them myself, 12just as a shepherd looks for lost sheep. My sheep have been lost since that dark and miserable day when they were scattered throughout the nations. But I will rescue them 13and bring them back from the foreign nations where they now live. I will be their shepherd and will let them graze on Israel's mountains and in the valleys and fertile fields. 14They will be safe as they feed on grassy meadows and green hills. 15I promise to take care of them and keep them safe, 16to look for those that are lost and bring back the ones that wander off, to bandage those that are hurt and protect the ones that are weak. I will also slaughter those that are fat and strong, because I always do right.
Judgment on the Strong Sheep
17The Lord God said to his sheep, the people of Israel:
I will carefully watch each one of you to decide which ones are the strong sheep and which ones are weak. 18Some of you eat the greenest grass, then trample down what's left when you finish. Others drink clean water, then step in the water to make the rest of it muddy. 19That means my other sheep have nothing fit to eat or drink.
20So I, the Lord God, will separate you strong sheep from the weak. 21You strong ones have used your powerful horns to chase off those that are weak, 22but I will rescue them and no longer let them be mistreated. I will separate the good from the bad.
23 After that, I will give you a shepherd from the family of my servant King David. All of you, both strong and weak, will have the same shepherd, and he will take good care of you. 24 He will be your leader, and I will be your God. I, the Lord, have spoken.
A Bright Future for the Lord's Sheep
The Lord God said:
25The people of Israel are my sheep, and I solemnly promise that they will live in peace. I will chase away every wild animal from the desert and the forest, so my sheep will not be afraid. 26They will live around my holy mountain, and I will bless them by sending more than enough rain 27to make their trees produce fruit and their crops to grow. I will set them free from slavery and let them live safely in their own land. Then they will know that I am the Lord. 28Foreign nations will never again rob them, and wild animals will no longer kill and eat them. They will have nothing to fear. 29I will make their fields produce large amounts of crops, so they will never again go hungry or be laughed at by foreigners. 30Then everyone will know that I protect my people Israel. I, the Lord, make this promise. 31They are my sheep; I am their God, and I take care of them.
translation_text:
Ti-Dindaan làá jáǹ Isirayeel kpootiliibi
1Ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: 2«Nisaaleen, dū m-bɔti tin jáà nì Isirayeel kpootiliibi nee kí nàatī-bi. Dū m-bɔti kí nàatī-bi kí tùkù-bi yii: <Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Nimbi bin kpàá Isirayeel yabee, mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí-ni, di sá yii nimbi ni-ba ní ni kpàá! An kaa sá ipii ní upikpaal máaǹ kí kpààa? 3Ama nimbee, ipii biim ní ni nyù, ní ki cēē i-kuti ki lù tiwampeeŋkaal ki pèentí ní ki kù tiwaŋkuti tin cáá ŋkpamee ki ŋmóò, ama ní ipii bɔti kaa ká-ni. 4Naa tīī ipii in pɔ̀fèe mpɔn, kaa cáaǹ in būǹee. Naa nyàab̄ ŋŋaabu ki bóob́ un taal gíìyee, kaa gíiǹní un kākatì u-ba ki wāatì kupicaŋkpuŋuee, ní kaa tí nyàab̄ un nìn wáŋkèe. Ama ni dū mpɔn nì nnimbinaakulim ní ki kpōotì-bi. 5Niinee ipii túĺ laakin i yaa kée, di sá yii iaa nìn gíti cáá ukpaal, ní ki kpántì tijin ki tīī ipeel. 6M-piii kpátìi gbí ajoon kɔkɔ nì ŋgbantamu kɔkɔ pu. I yàl̄ kitiŋ nee kɔkɔ pu ní ubɔ kpá kí nyàab̀-i, ní an kaa ká báà ubɔ mun. 7An puee, Isirayeel pikpaaliibi, ní pīlifì tin m cáá kí tùkù-nee: 8M bí dimaŋfalin! Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M-piii kɔ́ binaayub ŋaan. I nín kaa cáá bikpàaliibee puee, ipeecuncuti cúú-i ki tɔ̄ntì. Di sá yii m-pikpàaliibi kaa cūtìi nyàab̄ m-piii. Ama bipikpaaliibi gbanti kpàá bi-ba ní kaa fātìi tɔ́ m-piii. 9Too, Isirayeel pikpaaliibi, pīlifìmaan tin man ni-Dindaan bíi sòon̄ee: 10Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti bíi tùkù-ni yii m làá jáǹ-ni ní kí fōō m-piii ni-ŋaan. Maa làá ti yàntī ní kpàà m-piii. An yaa ŋá mimmee, naa làá ti jī i-pu. M làá dáaĺ m-piii kí nyāntí ni-nyɔmmun, ní iaa làá ti kpántí tijin kí tīī-ni.
11«Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Kí yòon̄ kɔŋkɔnnee kí nīn cée, man m-ba di làá cù kí nyàab̀ m-piii ní kí kpàà-i m-ba. 12Kii upikpaal piii nín yaa yàl̄, u péetí-i kí kpāfì puee, míǹ ní m làá kpàà m-piii. M làá cù kí nyàabìń m-piii laakin kɔkɔ ní i yàl̄ ki cūtì dipɔ̀ńdi nì dibɔmbɔndi dalee. 13M làá nyāntí-i anibul kansikin ní kí kóoǹní-i nnicantimun kí kpāfì ní kí fàtīí gíiǹní-i i-tiŋkin. M làá cáá-i kí cùnnì Isirayeel jooŋŋi pu nì atantakan nì kitiŋ nee jaŋŋi laakin kɔkɔ ní binib kóòyee kí kpàà-i. 14M làá cáá-i kí cùnnì kunaakpaapɔɔu kumɔntiiun. I làá ká timool Isirayeel jooŋŋi pu kí ŋmɔ́. Niin ní i làá ká timɔmɔntiil taapu kí dòon̄ kí ŋùŋfì, ní kí ká Isirayeel jooŋŋi pu laakin kitiŋ ŋān̄ee timool kí ŋmɔ́. 15Man m-ba di làá kpàà m-piii ní kí yàntī í ŋùŋfì. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ. 16Upii un wáŋkèe, man m-ba di làá nyàab̀-u. Un búntì ndanee, man di làá fàtīí gíiǹní-u. Un fōō tiweendee, man di làá nyàab̀ ŋŋaabu kí fìn̄-u ní kí tīī un būǹee mpɔn. Ama upii un di bí màlmal ki pɔ̄ɔ̄yee, m làá lēē-u. M làá dū deedee marab ní kí kpòotī m-piii.»
Unimbɔti jòó u-nibul
17«Nimbi m-piii, man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín bíi sòoǹ nì ni puee sèé: <Man di làá sòoǹ kí ŋāŋkì m-waŋkuti kansikin, kí sòoǹ ipijaa nì iŋɔjaa bɔti. 18An kaa fáatiǹ ni-kansikin bi-ba bí ŋmɔ́ kunaakpaapɔɔu moomɔntiiti. Ba di yì míǹ? Ba pu ní ni tà timool tin kíǹee ní? An kaa bàn̄-ni ní nyɔ̀ nnyim min wāĺ kílkil neeee? Ba pu ní ni cáá ni-taaŋi ki tà ki gbàtī nnyim min kíǹee ní? 19See m-piii in kíǹee ń ŋmɔ́ timool tin ni tàn̄ tàn̄ee ní kí nyɔ̀ nnyim min ni gbātèe. 20An pu ní man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti sòon̄ yii man m-ba di làá nīn sá m-piii in gbìfèe nì in bí ŋkaŋkalimuee kansikin ubɔsoonli. 21Di sá yii ni dū ni-gbigbipati nì ni-takakalii ki yáŋkì ipii in būǹee, ní ki dū ni-yiŋyi ki sāatì-i ki nyántì kupicaŋkpuŋu kansikin. 22An puee m làá dāan̄ kí jòoń-bi, án nín làá ŋá pu bí taa dāan̄ kí yɔ̀-iee. Man di làá nīn sá nimbi nì bíǹ kansikin ubɔsoonli. 23M làá yàntī upikpaabaanti nín kpàà m-piii. Úǹ di sá m-tɔntɔnliu Daafiidi. U làá kpàà m-piii ní kí nīn sá i-pikpaaliu. 24Man ni-Dindaan, man di làá nīn sá bi-Nimbɔtiu ní man tɔntɔnliu Daafiidi ń nīn sá bi-bɔtibil. Man ni-Dindaan di sòon̄.
25«Man nì m-piii làá ŋá ŋgbansɔŋfi pèéŋu ní kí kúntí ipeel kitiŋ nee pu. Niinee m-piii làá ŋmā kí nīn bí ŋgbansɔŋfin kuteeun ní kí dòon̄ kubambaŋŋun kí gèeǹ. 26M làá yàntī bí nīn kóò m-circir jool caŋin. M làá yàntī utaa ń nīn nì ŋyunti ŋun ní an máaǹee, utaa gbanti làá nīn sá dibiindi taau ní. 27Isufi làá lòoǹ abil ní kitiŋ ń lòoǹ tikpaajin ní báà ŋma ń nīn bí ŋgbansɔŋfin kitiŋ nee poon. M làá gbá kí tìl̄ ikusaka in di ŋúb́-bee ní kí nyāntí-bi kuyuŋu kun poon bi bée. Ŋyunti gbantee bi làá béé yii man di sá bi-Dindaan. 28Binicambi kaa ti làá yɔ̀-i ní ipeecuncuti kaa ti làá cúú-i kí ŋmɔ́. Bi làá nīn bí ŋgbansɔŋfin ní ubɔ kaa làá fàaǹ-bi. 29M làá tīī-bi tikpaatan tin di lòoǹ tiŋanee. Ŋkùm kaa làá ti cúú-bi kitiŋ nee poon. Atimbun ŋin kíǹee kaa làá ti kpèè-bi fám. 30Báà ŋma làá dāá béé yii man bi-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu bí bi-cee, ní Isirayeel yab lafun sá man nibul. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ.
31«Nimbi m-piii, m-piii in ní m kpàáyee, nimbi binib, man di sá ni-Nimbɔtiu. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄.»

english_text:
Edom Will Be a Wasteland
1 The Lord said:
2Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the people of Edom 3and say to them:
I, the Lord God,
am now your enemy!
And I will turn your nation
into an empty wasteland,
4leaving your towns in ruins.
Your land will be a desert,
and then you will know
that I am the Lord.
5People of Edom, not only have you been Israel's longtime enemy, you simply watched when disaster wiped out its people as punishment for their sins. 6And so, as surely as I am the living Lord God, you are guilty of murder and must be put to death. 7I will destroy your nation and kill anyone who travels through it. 8Dead bodies will cover your mountains and fill up your valleys, 9and your land will lie in ruins forever. No one will live in your towns ever again. You will know that I am the Lord.
10You thought the nations of Judah and Israel belonged to you, and that you could take over their territory. But I am their God, 11and as surely as I live, I will punish you for treating my people with anger and hatred. Then they will know that I, the Lord, am punishing you! 12And you will finally realize that I heard you laugh at their destruction and say their land was yours to take. 13You even insulted me, but I heard it all.
14Everyone on earth will celebrate when I destroy you, 15just as you celebrated when Israel was destroyed. Your nation of Edom will be nothing but a wasteland. Then everyone will know that I am the Lord.
translation_text:
Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ ki bíikì Eedoom yab pu
1Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii: 2«Nisaaleen, fàtī a-ba kí túĺ Eedoom jooŋŋi watil pú kí sòoǹ m-bɔti kí tɔ̄ ki-pu. 3Dū tin man a-Dindaan Unimbɔti sòon̄ee kí nàatī-bi yii: <M làá jáǹ-ni! M làá dàkà sii Eedoom tiŋki m-pɔŋŋu ní kí nàan̄-si ní kí yàntī á kpántí kuteeu. 4M làá yàntī a-timmu ń kpántí adigbuŋkati ŋma. M làá yàntī á kpántí kii kuteeuee. Niinee a làá béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan. 5Sii pée ná Isirayeel yab ní. Bi nín kɔ́ dinimbinaamandinee, ŋyunti ŋun ní bi kúntì bi-kpitiiyee, a nìn jáń nì bi kujaau. 6Too, man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti un bí dimaŋfalin nee nín sòon̄ puee di sá yii m làá yàntī a-fatikuu ń nyā, di sá yii fatiku un a yāntì an nyáńee bíi bàlifī bí tɔ̀-u ipɔntoon. A nín kaa gūgufì ki yāntì fatiku nyáńee, si mun fatikuu làá nyā. 7Eedoom, m làá nàan̄ a-tiŋki. M làá yàntī kí kpántí kii kuteeuee ní kí kpɔ̀ un kamaa làá dī niinee. 8M làá dū anikpil kí gbéeǹ a-jooŋŋi pu. Bin bi làá kpɔ̀ kujaaunee làá lítí a-gbantammu pu nì a-tantakaŋin nì a-buŋyin. 9M làá yàntī a-tiŋki ń kpántí kuteeu kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaan. Báà unil kaa làá ti kɔ́ a-timmun. Niinee a làá béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan>.
10«A lī yii: <Man di làá nīn yì atimbun ali nee, Isirayeel nì Juuda beeŋi. Min kamaa ti-Dindaan kóò niinee, man làá fōō-mu kí nīn kíǹ ki yì.> 11Too, man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín bí dimaŋfalin nee, a nín ŋá tipɔmbɔti nì ipoompoon nì kináŋ ki dàkā Isirayeel yab puee, míǹ ní m làá dàkà-si. M làá dàkà Isirayeel yab un ní m sée ŋyunti ŋun ní m yaa láa bíi sòoǹ a-bɔtee. 12Niinee a làá dāá béé yii man ni-Dindaan, m gbìl̄ a-siibiliŋ pu ŋyunti ŋun ní a lī yii: <Timbi di yì Isirayeel jooŋŋi! Ŋi kpántì kii kuteeuee. Ti ŋūǹ kí cùú fōō-ŋi!> 13A sòon̄ nì mi dilambil poon ki sòon̄-mi tikpan. Man gbìl̄ tin kɔkɔ ní a sòon̄ee.
14«Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Kitiŋ nee kɔkɔ yaa láa bíi fàal̀ee ní ḿ nàan̄-si á kpántí kii kuteeuee. 15Bi nín nāaǹ Isirayeel m-nibul, bi-tiŋki kpántì kii kuteeuee, a nìn fàal̄. Too, m làá yàntī míǹ mbaantiim nín bàń-si. A-jooŋŋi, a-tiŋki kɔkɔ làá kpántí kii kuteeuee ní. Niinee báà ŋma làá béé yii m sá ni-Dindaan.>»

english_text:
A Message for Israel's Mountains
1The Lord said:
Ezekiel, son of man, tell the mountains of Israel 2that I, the Lord God, am saying:
Your enemies sneered and said that you mountains belonged to them. 3They ruined and crushed you from every side, and foreign nations captured and made fun of you. 4So all you mountains and hills, streams and valleys, listen to what I will do. Your towns may now lie in ruins, and nations may laugh and insult you. 5But in my fierce anger, I will turn against those nations, and especially the Edomites, because they laughed at you the loudest and took over your pasturelands. 6You have suffered long enough, and, I, the Lord God, am very angry! Nations have insulted you, 7so I will now insult and disgrace them. That is my solemn promise.
8Trees will grow on you mountains of Israel and produce fruit for my people, because they will soon come home. 9I will take care of you by plowing your soil and planting crops on your fertile slopes. 10The people of Israel will return and rebuild your ruined towns and live in them. 11Children will be born, and animals will give birth to their young. You will no longer be deserted as you are now, but you will be covered with people and treated better than ever. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
12I will bring my people Israel home, and they will live on you mountains, because you belong to them, and your fertile slopes will never again let them starve. 13It's true that you have been accused of not producing enough food and of letting your people starve. 14-15But I, the Lord, promise that you won't hear other nations laugh and sneer at you ever again. From now on, you will always produce plenty of food for your people. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
The Lord Will Be Honored
16The Lord said:
17Ezekiel, son of man, when the people of Israel were living in their own country, they made the land unclean by the way they behaved, just as a woman's monthly period makes her unclean. 18They committed murders and worshiped idols, which made the land even worse. So in my anger, I punished my people 19and scattered them throughout the nations, just as they deserved. 20Wherever they went, my name was disgraced, because foreigners insulted my people by saying I had forced them out of their own land.
21I care what those foreigners think of me, 22so tell the Israelites that I am saying:
You have disgraced my holy name among the nations where you now live. So you don't deserve what I'm going to do for you. I will lead you home to bring honor to my name 23and to show foreign nations that I am holy. Then they will know that I am the Lord God. I have spoken.
24I will gather you from the foreign nations and bring you home. 25I will sprinkle you with clean water, and you will be clean and acceptable to me. I will wash away everything that makes you unclean, and I will remove your disgusting idols. 26 I will take away your stubborn heart and give you a new heart and a desire to be faithful. You will have only pure thoughts, 27because I will put my Spirit in you and make you eager to obey my laws and teachings. 28You will once again live in the land I gave your ancestors; you will be my people, and I will be your God.
29I will protect you from anything that makes you unclean. Your fields will overflow with grain, and no one will starve. 30Your trees will be filled with fruit, and crops will grow in your fields, so that you will never again feel ashamed for not having enough food. 31You will remember your evil ways and hate yourselves for what you've done. 32People of Israel, I'm not doing these things for your sake. You sinned against me, and you must suffer shame and disgrace for what you have done. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
33After I have made you clean, I will let you rebuild your ruined towns and let you live in them. 34Your land will be plowed again, and nobody will be able to see that it was once barren. 35Instead, they will say that it looks as beautiful as the garden of Eden. They won't see towns lying in ruins, but they will see your strong cities filled with people. 36Then the nearby nations that survive will know that I am the one who rebuilt the ruined places and replanted the barren fields. I, the Lord, make this promise.
37I will once again answer your prayers, and I will let your nation grow until you are like a large flock of sheep. 38The towns that now lie in ruins will be filled with people, just as Jerusalem was once filled with sheep to be offered as sacrifices during a festival. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_text:
Isirayeel yab làá fàtīí fōō bi-tiŋki
1«Nisaaleen, fōō m-cee Isirayeel jooŋŋi bɔti kí dūú nàatī. Tùkù-ŋi ŋí pīlifì man ni-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi. 2Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Ni-nannanliibi nín bēel̀-mi ki lī yii: <Àa! Àa! Kɔŋkɔnnee Isirayeel cannaaku jooŋŋi nee kpántì ti-yaŋ dee!> 3Too, dū m-bɔti kí nàatī kí tùkù-bi yii man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sèé: <Ijaan kɔkɔ puee, bi nāaǹ-ni ki kā ni-pu ki bàà là yii ní kpántí atimbun ŋin kíǹee wanti. Bi bēel̀-ni ki sīī-ni.> 4An puee Isirayeel jooŋŋi, pīlifìmaan m-nyɔɔbuŋŋi! Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti, m bíi sòoǹ nì ajoon nì ŋgbantamu nì mbùmbiyaamu nì atantaka nì adigbuŋkati nì ntimu mun ni yíkì ki dūu fá anibul ŋin māntìi tú-nee fúkúl̀ ki sīīyee. 5Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti sòon̄ m-ŋuul poon kí jáǹ atimbun ŋin kɔkɔ kíǹee nì Eedoom tiŋki kɔkɔ. Di sá yii nì dipɔɔpiŋkpaandi nì kpeefam ní bi fōō m-tiŋki nì ki-naakpaapɔɔku ki gāā bi-bindi. 6An puee á fōō m-bɔti tin sòoǹ Isirayeel tiŋki puee kí nàatī. Nàatī ajoon nì ŋgbantamu nì mbùmbiyaamu nì atantaka tin man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti sòon̄ee yii: M làá yàntī m-ŋuul ń tɔ̄ di-tundi. Atimbun ŋin kíǹee sīī-ni ki kpēē ki sīŋkiǹ-ni. 7Too, man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ yii bi làá kpèè kí sìŋkīǹ atimbun ŋin māntìi tú-ni nee. 8Ŋyunti gbantee, isufi in bí Isirayeel jooŋŋi puee làá tɔ̄ apan kí lòoǹ abil kí tīī nimbi m-nibul Isirayeel yab. Di sá yii ni làá fàtīí gítí ni-tiŋkin án kaa làá yúntí. 9M bí ni-cee, m làá fàtī m-ba kí túĺ-ni, ni làá kpɔ̀ ni-sati kí bɔ̄l̀. 10Isirayeel tiŋki kɔkɔnee, m làá yàntī ní bùtī. Binib làá fàtīí kɔ́ ni-timmun, di sá yii bi làá fàtīí mā adiin ŋin nìn lítèe. 11Binib nì tiwaŋkuti làá bùtī. Ni làá nīn wīikí ní kí màal̀ mbiyaamu tikpil. Kitiŋ nee làá fàtīí ká ki-nib kii an nín nìn bí pu dooooyee, ní kí yàntī án bútí-ni kí jītíǹ dooooyee. Niinee ni làá béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan. 12Isirayeel yab, m-nibul, m làá yàntī ní còom̀ kitiŋ nee kɔkɔ poon. Ni làá fōō-kì ní kí nīn kíǹ ki sá ni-yaka. Kàa ti làá kpɔ̀ ni-biyaamu. 13Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Binib lì yii Isirayeel tiŋki tɔ̀ntī ki-nib ní ki kù bi-biyaamu. 14Too, kitiŋ nee kaa làá ti tɔ̀ntī ki-nib kaa làá ti kpɔ̀ bi-biyaamu. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ. 15Naa làá ti gbìl̄ atimbun ŋin kíǹee beelii àá ŋi-siibiliŋ pu. Di sá yii ni-tiŋki kaa ti làá nīn kù ki-biyaamu. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ.»
Ti-Dindaan làá fàtīí kóoǹ Isirayeel yab kí kpāfì
