16Ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: 17«Nisaaleen, pīlifì! Isirayeel yab nín nìn dáá kóò bi-tiŋkinee, bi nìn dū bi-bimbikpitim nì bi-tuŋkpitiŋ ki kɔ́ǹ bi-tiŋki tijɔkɔndi. Bi-bimbim nìn bí m-cee kii unimpu nín yaa ká u-ba u bí tijɔkɔndin puee ní. 18Bi dū nnikpaakoon nì iwaatooti ki kɔ́ǹ kitiŋ tijɔkɔndi. An pu ní m kpáatì m-ŋuul ki sītì bi-pu. 19M jìn̄-bi ki kɔ́ǹ atimbun aban nì nnicantimun. Bi-bimbim nì bi-tuuŋŋi nín cáań-bi m-tafadaaldi diŋyee dee. 20Atimbun ŋin kɔkɔn bi cūtèe, binib kpēē m-circir yindi fám bi-pu. Di sá yii bi nìn lì yii: <Ti-Dindaan nibul nìn yá, bi yíkì u-tiŋki pu.> 21An nìn páb́-mi ḿ ká yii atimbun aba bí ki kpèé m-circir yindi fám Isirayeel yab bin nìn dòoń bi-ceeyee kpitii pu. 22An puee, á nàatī-bi tin man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti sòon̄ee yii: <Isirayeel yab, kun m làá ŋée, an kaa sá ni-pu ní m làá ŋá, ama an sá m-circir yindi din ní ni bíil̀ atimbun ŋin poon ni cūtèe pu ní m làá ŋá míǹ. 23Ni-puee, atimbun ŋin kíǹee nib kpēē m-yindi fám. An puee, m làá dàkà-bi yii man di sá Unimbɔtikpaan nì circirdaan. Ni-pu ní m làá dī kí dàkà-bi tíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ. Niinee bi làá béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan, man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ.>
24«M làá nyāntí-ni atimbun kansikin, m làá kóoǹní-ni ntimu mun kɔkɔ poon ní ni bée ní kí fàtīí gíiǹní-ni ni-tiŋkin. 25M làá kpáatí nnyim min bí circiree kí sìtī ni-pu, ní kí ŋá-ni circir. M làá fíntí-ni kí nyāntí ni-jɔkɔntuuŋŋi kɔkɔ poon nì ni-waatootii poon. 26M làá tīī-ni dipɔɔpɔndi ní kí dū ŋfampɔm kí ŋá ni-ni. M làá lēē ni-pɔbil din pɔ̄ɔ̄ kii ditaŋkpalee ni-ni, ní kí tīī-ni dipɔbil din pɔ̀fì ki gbìl̀ tibɔti taapuee. 27M làá dū m-Fam kí ŋá ni-ni. M làá yàntī ní ŋmā kí nīn tɔ́ m-marab ní kí ŋúb́ m-bɔkpaaŋi kí ŋá ŋi nín bí yii ní ŋá puee. 28Niinee ni làá ŋmā kí kɔ́ kitiŋ kin ní m tīī ni-naanjabee poon. Ni làá nīn sá m-nibul ní man ń nīn sá ni-Nimbɔtiu. 29M làá nyāntí-ni ni-jɔkɔnti kɔkɔn. Maa làá ti dū ŋkùm kí tɔ̄ ni-pu, ama m làá yàntī ni-bileeu ń nyā ní kí lòoǹ tikpil. 30M làá yàntī ni-sufii ń lòoǹ abil tikpil tikpil ní ni-kpaajinti mun ń lòoǹ tiŋan tiŋan. An yaa ŋá mimmee, ŋkùm kaa làá ti cúú-ni ní kɔ́ icoon atimbun ŋin kíǹee kansikin. 31Niinee ni làá téetí ni-bimbikpitim nì ni-tuŋkpitiŋ pu. Ni-naŋki làá nyā nì ni-ba ni-kpitii nì ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin ni ŋée pu. 32Ní béé yii an kaa sá ni-pu ní m làá ŋá míǹ, man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ. Isirayeel yab, ní yàntī ni-bimbim ń kɔ́ǹ-ni icoo ní yāliŋkì i-pu!
33«Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M yaa láa fíntì-ni ki nyántì ni-kpitii kɔkɔ poon ni nyáń dándanee, m làá yàntī binib ń fàtīí kɔ́ ni-timmun ní bí fàtīí mā adiin ŋin nìn lítèe. 34Ni làá fàtīí kpɔ̀ tikpaatan tin ni nìn dūu fée, bisanjitiliibi kaa làá ti ká yii bi dū tikpaatan ki fá. 35Bi làá lì yii: <Kitiŋ kin bi nìn dūu fée fātìi kpántì kii Eedeen kpaabuee. Ntimu mun poon bi nìn gbáń ki wīil̀ adiin an kpántì adigbuŋkati ŋmee, bi fātìi máń adiin binib kíǹ ki kóò mu-ni. 36Niinee atimbun ŋin dáá gbíntìi bí ki māntìi tú-nee làá béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan, un di fàtīi māā ntimu mun poon bi gbáń ki wīil̀ adiinee, ní ki fàtīi cōontí tin bi fùkū ki fée. Man ni-Dindaan di sòon̄ ní tin m yaa sòon̄ee, tíǹ ní m ŋáań.
37«Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M làá yàntī Isirayeel yab ń mèè-mi ní ḿ kíí-bi ní kí yàntī bí bùtī kii ipiiyee. 38Dooooyee, binib yaa nìn kpáfì kí jī jiŋaalibee, ipii in bi nìn cáa ŋáań saraabee nìn gbéè Jeerusaleem tiŋkin ní. Bi nìn cāabìń-i tipicaŋkpun tipicaŋkpun ní. Míǹ ní binib bin làá dāan̄ kí kɔ́ ni-timmu mun kpántì adigbuŋkati nee làá nīn wīikí. Niinee, báà ŋma làá béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan.»

english_text:
Dry Bones Live Again
1Some time later, I felt the Lord's power take control of me, and his Spirit carried me to a valley full of bones. 2The Lord showed me all around, and everywhere I looked I saw bones that were dried out. 3He said, “Ezekiel, son of man, can these bones come back to life?”
I replied, “Lord God, only you can answer that.”
4He then told me to say:
Dry bones, listen to what the Lord is saying to you, 5“I, the Lord God, will put breath in you, and once again you will live. 6I will wrap you with muscles and skin and breathe life into you. Then you will know that I am the Lord.”
7I did what the Lord said, but before I finished speaking, I heard a rattling noise. The bones were coming together! 8I saw muscles and skin cover the bones, but they had no life in them.
9The Lord said:
Ezekiel, now say to the wind, “The Lord God commands you to blow from every direction and to breathe life into these dead bodies, so they can live again.”
10 As soon as I said this, the wind blew among the bodies, and they came back to life! They all stood up, and there were enough to make a large army.
11The Lord said:
Ezekiel, the people of Israel are like dead bones. They complain that they are dried up and that they have no hope for the future. 12So tell them, “I, the Lord God, promise to open your graves and set you free. I will bring you back to Israel, 13and when that happens, you will realize that I am the Lord. 14My Spirit will give you breath, and you will live again. I will bring you home, and you will know that I have kept my promise. I, the Lord, have spoken.”
Judah and Israel Together Again
15The Lord said:
16Ezekiel, son of man, get a stick and write on it, “The kingdom of Judah.” Then get another stick and write on it, “The kingdom of Israel.” 17Hold these two sticks end to end, so they look like one stick. 18And when your people ask you what this means, 19tell them that I, the Lord, will join together the stick of Israel and the stick of Judah. I will hold them in my hand, and they will become one.
20Hold these two sticks where they can be seen by everyone 21and then say:
I, the Lord God, will gather the people of Israel and bring them home from the foreign nations where they now live. 22I will make them into one nation and let them once again live in the land of Israel. Only one king will rule them, and they will never again be divided into two nations. 23They will no longer worship idols and do things that make them unacceptable to me. I will wash away their sin and make them clean, and I will protect them from everything that makes them unclean. They will be my people, and I will be their God.
24-25 Their king will always come from the family of my servant King David and will care for them like a shepherd. The people of Israel will faithfully obey my laws. They and their descendants will live in the land I gave my servant Jacob, just as their ancestors did. 26I solemnly promise to bless the people of Israel with unending peace. I will protect them and let them become a powerful nation. My temple will stand in Israel for all time, 27 and I will live among my people and be their God. 28Every nation on earth will know that my temple is in Israel and that I have chosen the Israelites to be my people.
translation_text:
Ti-Dindaan lēē akpakulim ki dàkā Eeseekiyeel
1M nìn gbìl̄ ti-Dindaan pɔŋŋu m-ni ní u-Fam yōoǹ-mi ki cáa yóoǹ ditantakal diba kansikin. Akpab di nìn gbí ditantakalee poon. 2Ti-Dindaan nìn yāntì m māntìi tú akpabee ditantakalee poon. Akpabee nìn wīikí tikpilku ní ki nìn kūń. 3Niinee ní ti-Dindaan bālifì-mi yii: «Nisaaleen, mimmee akpab nee ŋūǹ kí fàtīí ká dimaŋfalaaa?» Ní m kíí yii: «M-Dindaan Unimbɔti, sii baba di nyí.» 4Ní u bí-mi yii: «Fōō m-bɔti kí nàatī akpab nee. Tùkù-ŋi yii: <Akpakulim, pīlifìmaan ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi! 5Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín bíi sòoǹ nì ni puee sɔ̀. M làá cáań dimaŋfal fooku kí ŋá ni-ni, ní ní fàtīí ká dimaŋfal. 6M làá dū igiin kí páań ni-pu ní kí yàntī tiwunnan ń nyā ni-pu ní kí dū ŋwuŋgban kí bìin̄. M làá dū dimaŋfal fooku kí ŋá ni-ni, ní ní fàtīí ká dimaŋfal. Niinee ni làá béé yii m sá ni-Dindaan.>» 7Ní m dū tibɔtee ki sòon̄ nì akpabee kii ti-Dindaan nín kpáafì-mi puee. Ŋyunti ŋun m bíi sòoǹee ní m gbìl̄ kuwoou kubɔ pu ní akpabee kíĺ ki bíi sútí ki pìl̀ tɔb. 8M bíi kpèéyee ní ki ká yii igiin páaǹ ŋi-pu, ní tiwunnan nyáń ki páaǹ ní ŋwuŋgban dūu bīiǹ. Ama dimaŋfal fooku kaa nìn dáá bí ŋi-ni. 9Niinee ní ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: «Nisaaleen, fōō m-nyɔɔbundi kí dūú sòoǹ nì dimaŋfal fooku yii: <Dimaŋfal fooku, ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Nyānní kitiŋ jannaatiliŋ pú kí dāan̄ kí fáá anikpil nee pu ŋí ká dimaŋfal.>» 10Ní m dū ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi ki nāatì kii u nín kpáafì-mi ḿ ŋá puee. Dimaŋfal fookuee dɔ́miń ki kɔ́ anikpilee ni ní ŋi fātìi ká dimaŋfal ní ki nìn yíkìi yúl̀. Bi nìn dūu ŋá dijanjakitikpaŋkpaandi ní.
11Míǹ boonee ní ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: «Nisaaleen, akpab nee sá Isirayeel nibul ní. Bi bí ki lì yii: <Ti bí kii akpakulimee, ti-mákal dóò, an dóò ti-pu dee.> 12An puee dū m-nyɔɔbundi kí nàatī-bi kí tùkù-bi tin man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti bíi sòoǹ nì bee yii: <M làá cúú ni-kaakuliŋ kí pìitī ní kí cúú nimbi, man nibul kí nyāntiń. M làá fàtīí gíiǹ-ni ni-tiŋki pu. 13M yaa láa pīitì ni-kaakuliŋ ki nyántìń-nee, ni làá dāá béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan. 14M làá dū m-Fam kí ŋá ni-ni, ní ní nīn bí dimaŋfalin. M làá dū-ni kí kàan̄ ni-tiŋkin. Niinee ni làá béé yii man ni-Dindaan di sòon̄, ní tin m yaa lēe, tíǹ ní m ŋáań. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄.»
Ti-Dindaan làá dū Isirayeel tiŋki kɔkɔ kí kpāfì
15Ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: 16«Sii nisaaleen, yòon̄ didɔgindi kí ŋmà di-pu yii: <Juuda nì Isirayeel yab bin bí dibeel nee poonee>. Míǹ boonee, á gíti yòon̄ didɔgindi diba mun kí ŋmà di-pu yii: <Jooseefi àá Eefiraayiim nì Isirayeel yab bin bí dibeel nee poonee.> 17Dū adɔgin ali gbanti nyɔmmu kí bíĺ kí tūū tɔb án kpántí kii didɔgimbaantiilee a-ŋaan. 18A-nibul yab làá bàlifì-si á cántí taapu kí tùkù-bi. 19Á tùkù-bi yii man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ nì bi puee sɔ̀. M làá yòon̄ didɔgindi din di sá Jooseefi nì Isirayeel yabee kí dūú túkuń Juuda dɔgindi pu. Adɔgin alee làá kpántí didɔgimbaantiil ní m-ŋaan.
20«Á nīn ŋúb́ adɔgin ŋin pu ní a ŋmàn̄ee a-ŋaan báà ŋma ń wāl̀. 21Míǹ boonee, á dū tin man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti sòon̄ee kí nàatī-bi yii: <Isirayeel yab, m làá nyāntiń-ni atimbun ŋin cee ni cūtèe ŋaan. M làá kóoǹ-ni kí kpāfì ní kí fàtīí gíiǹní-ni ni-tiŋkin. 22M làá yàntī ní kpántí ditimbumbaantiil Isirayeel jooŋŋi pu. Ni-kɔkɔ làá nīn cáá ubɔtibaanti ní. Naa ti làá nīn sá atimbun ali ní baa làá ti yàkatī-ni abee ali pu. 23Naa ti làá tòotī awaa, kaa ti làá ŋá ntimbiil tuuŋŋi àá kí yìntīǹ-mi kí kɔ́ǹ ni-ba tijɔkɔndi. M làá nyāntí-ni laakin kɔkɔ ni cūtì ki yīntiǹ-mee ní kí fíntí-ni kí nyāntí ni-jɔkɔnti kɔkɔn. Ni làá nīn sá m-nibul ní man ń nīn sá ni-Nimbɔtiu. 24M-tɔntɔnliu Daafiidi làá nīn sá ni-bɔtiu. U làá nīn sá upikpaabaanti ní kí tīī ni-kɔkɔ. Ni làá nīn tɔ́ m-marab ní kí nīn tɔ́ m-bɔkpaaŋi ní kí ŋá ŋi nín bí yii ní ŋá puee. 25Ni làá nīn kóò kitiŋ kin ní m tīī m-tɔntɔnliu Jaakɔb ní ni-naanjab kāl̀ ki-poonee. Ni làá nīn kíǹ ki kóò niin ní jaanjaan, ni nì ni-biyaamu nì ni-naantiibi. Man tɔntɔnliu Daafiidi di làá nīn sá ni-bɔtibil kí nīn cá talku. 26M làá pòon̄-ni ŋgbansɔŋfi poondi din làá nīn bí ki cá jaanjaanee. M làá dū-ni kí kàan̄ kitiŋ nee poon ní kí bùtī ni-maaliŋu. M làá dū m-circir kɔŋkooŋŋu kí síiń ni-kansikin ŋú nīn bí ki cá jaanjaan. 27M làá nīn kóò ni-kansikin. M làá nīn sá ni-Nimbɔtiu ní nimbi ń nīn sá m-nibul. 28M yaa láa dū m-kɔŋkooŋŋu ki síiǹ ni-kansikin kí nīn cá jaanjaanee ní atimbun ŋin kíǹee làá béé yii m sá ni-Dindaan ní ki dū Isirayeel ki sú ú nīn bí m-tundin kí nīn cá jaanjaan.»

english_text:
Gog Invades Israel
1The Lord said:
2 Ezekiel, son of man, condemn Gog, that wicked ruler of the kingdoms of Meshech and Tubal in the land of Magog. Tell him:
3I, the Lord God, am your enemy, 4and I will make you powerless! I will put a hook in your jaw and drag away both you and your large army. You command cavalry troops that wear heavy armor and carry shields and swords. 5Your army includes soldiers from Persia, Ethiopia, and Libya, 6as well as from Gomer and Beth-Togarmah in the north. Your army is enormous!
7So keep your troops prepared to fight, 8because in a few years, I will command you to invade Israel, a country that was ruined by war. It was deserted for a long time, but its people have returned from the foreign nations where they once lived. The Israelites now live in peace in the mountains of their own land. 9But you and your army will attack them like a fierce thunderstorm and surround them like a cloud.
10When that day comes, I know that you will have an evil plan 11to take advantage of Israel, that weak and peaceful country where people live safely inside towns that have no walls or gates or locks. 12You will rob the people in towns that were once a pile of rubble. These people lived as prisoners in foreign nations, but they have returned to Israel, the most important place in the world, and they own livestock and property. 13The people of Sheba and Dedan, along with merchants from villages in southern Spain, will be your allies. They will want some of the silver and gold, as well as the livestock and property that your army takes from Israel.
14I, the Lord God, know that when you see my people Israel living in peace, 15you will lead your powerful cavalry from your kingdom in the north. 16You will attack my people like a storm-cloud that covers their land. I will let you invade my country Israel, so that every nation on earth will know that I, the Lord, am holy.
Judgment on Gog
17The Lord said to Gog:
Long ago, I ordered my prophets to warn the people of Israel that someday I would send an enemy to attack them. You, Gog, are that enemy, and that day is coming. 18When you invade Israel, I will become furious, 19and in my anger I will send a terrible earthquake to shake Israel. 20Every living thing on earth will tremble in fear of me—every fish and bird, every wild animal and reptile, and every human. Mountains will crumble, cliffs will fall, and cities will collapse. 21I, the Lord, will make the mountains of Israel turn against you. Your troops will be so terrified that they will attack each other. 22I will strike you with diseases and punish you with death. You and your army will be pounded with rainstorms, hailstones, and burning sulfur. 23I will do these things to show the world that I, the Lord, am holy.
translation_text:
Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ ki bíikì Gɔɔgi pu
1Ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii: 2«Nisaaleen, fàtī a-nimbiin kí túĺ Gɔɔgi un bí Maagoogi tiŋkin, ki sá Meeseeki nì Tubaal bɔtibilee. Dū m-bɔti kí nàatī-u. 3Dū tin man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti sòon̄ee kí nàatī-u yii: M làá jáǹ sii Gɔɔgi, Meeseeki nì Tubaal bɔtibil ukpil. 4M làá dū tikúti kí kpàl̄ a-nyɔɔkpaween ní kí dáaĺ-si mpɔn kí nyāntí. M làá nyāntí-si mpɔn a-tiŋkin, sii nì a-janjaliibi kɔkɔ nì a-taamui nì a-tanjakaliibi bin pēē tiwannyaandee nì a-janjakitikpaandi din ŋúb́ agbampɔɔ nì ntàataajimuee. 5Peersi nì Eetiiyoopii nì Puuti janjaliibi làá nīn tú agbampɔɔ ki cíkí kujaau fuulimmu ní kí táá-si kí búntí. 6Goomeer tiŋki janjakitiŋ kɔkɔ nì Beeti-Toogarima tiŋki kin bí ŋgan púee janjakitiŋ kɔkɔ nì atimbun tikpil mun làá táá-si kí búntí. 7Bɔ́ntí a-ba an nín máaǹ puee, sii nì samaa un kɔkɔ kóoǹ ki kpáfì a-ceeyee, sii di làá nīn kpòotī-bi. 8Abin kupaau boon kpataaayee, m làá dāá tɔ̄-si á cùú jáǹ Isirayeel tiŋki. Ŋyunti gbantee, ki-nib ŋmátì ki nyáń kujaaun, ki nyáń ntimu mun poon bi nìn kóòyee ki kóoǹ ki kpáfì Isirayeel jooŋŋi ŋin kpántì adigbuŋkati an yúntèe pu dee. Bi nín nyáń atimbun ŋin kíǹee kansikinee, bi kíǹ ki bí ŋgbansɔŋfin ní. 9Sii nì a-janjakitil nì atimbun kupaau ŋin kútì a-puee làá jáǹ-bi. Ni làá jēetí bi-pu kii kubuŋkpaaŋŋuee, ní ní kpátí kí bìin̄ bi-tiŋki pu kii ditagbandee.
10«Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ yii, ŋyunti gbanti yaa láa bāańee, ilandɔkɔ tikpil làá dāan̄ a-ni ní á bɔ́ntí kí tɔ̄ dituŋkpitil diba. 11A làá lì yii a làá cùú jáǹ kitiŋ kin di kaa cáá ubɔ ń mɔ̄tì ki-puee. A làá jáǹ binib bin di bí ŋgbansɔŋfin tiba kaa páb́-bee. Binib gbanti kóò ntimu mun baa máń agun ki tú, muaa cáá mpunyɔmuɔɔ kaa cáá tikpàlkaalee. 12A làá dāan̄ kí fūkul̀-bi kí kóoǹ bi-gaajawanti. Binib bin fātìi kɔ́ kitiŋ kin nìn kpántì adigbuŋkati ŋmee, a làá jáǹ-bi. Bi nyánní ntincamun ki kóoǹ ki kpáfì. Bi cáá tipicaŋkpun nì tigaajati ní ki kóò duulinya kansikin nì kansikin. 13Binib bin kóò Sabaa nì Deedaŋyee nì Taarsiisi nyampoobi nì ntimbilimu mun māntìi tú-nee làá bàlifì-si yii: <Mimmee kí fūkul̀ binib wanti pu ní a dɔ́mińaaa? Kí kóoǹ tigaajawan kí kpúkuńee pu ní a kóoǹ a-janjakitil ki kpáfàaa? A dɔ́miń kí fōō animbil nì sindaariya nì tipicaŋkpun nì tigaajawan kí kpúkuń níii?>
14«An puee nisaaleen, fōō m-bɔti kí dūú nàatī. Lēē tin man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti sòon̄ee kí dàkà Gɔɔgi yii: <Ŋwiin ŋun m-nibul Isirayeel yaa láa bí ŋgbansɔŋfinee, a làá dāá kíĺ nsan. 15A làá nyānní a-tiŋki kin bí ŋgan púee kí dāan̄, sii nì ntimu tikpil janjaliibi. Ni-kɔkɔ làá dāá nīn kāń itaamu pu ki náaǹ, ní kí ŋá dijanjakitikpaandi. 16A làá dāan̄ kí jáǹ m-nibul Isirayeel yab ní kí gbá kí bìin̄ bi-tiŋki pu kii ditagbandi nín bìintí kitiŋ pu puee. Iyuntijoolkaa poon ní tíǹ làá jītí. M làá tɔ̄ sii Gɔɔgi á cù kí fōō m-tiŋki kí ŋmā kí dàkà anibul ŋin kíǹee yii man di sá Unimbɔti Circirdaan. Kun ní m làá dī a-pu kí dàkà-bee dee.
17«Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Dooooyee, m nìn dūu dī m-tɔntɔnliibi Isirayeel bɔnaatiliibi pu ki sòon̄ a-pu. Bi dū abin kupaau ki sòon̄ yii m làá tɔ̄-si á jáǹ m-nibul. 18Ama ŋwiin ŋun ní a làá já kí fōō Isirayeel tiŋkee, Gɔɔgi, yaadal ní m làá gíí diŋuul, man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ. 19M pūtì yii m-ŋuukpaandi gbanti poonee, kitiŋ làá cìŋkì Isirayeel tiŋkin. 20Ijɔm in bí tiŋkunee nì inoon in ŋàaǹ kutaa puee nì ipeel nì ikoobu in fù kitiŋee nì binib bin bí kitiŋ puee kɔkɔ làá nyɔ̀ ŋkpatim m-nimbiin. Ajoon làá wùtī ní ataŋkpee ń lítí kitiŋ ní agun ŋin bi máń ki tú ntimuee ń lítí. 21Gɔɔgi, m làá jáǹ-si m-jooŋŋi kɔkɔ pu, man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di lī míǹ. A-janjaliibi làá kpɔ̀ tɔb. 22M làá dū bìlbil kúm weeŋŋu kí tɔ̄ a-pu ní kí yàntī á kpú kí dáaĺ a-tafal. M làá yàntī utaakpaan nì ataanyiŋkumbil nì farwata un fòol̄ lìblibee ń nì sii nì a-janjaliibi nì bin kɔkɔ kútì a-pu ni cūtì kujaauee pu. 23M làá dàkā atimbun kɔkɔ yii m sá ukpaan ki bí circir. M làá lēē m-ba kí dàkà atimbun kupaau ń béé-mi, ní ŋi làá béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan.»

english_text:
Gog Is Defeated
The Lord said:
1Ezekiel, son of man, condemn Gog and tell him:
You are the ruler of Meshech and Tubal, but I, the Lord, am your enemy! 2I will turn you around and drag you from the north until you reach the mountains of Israel. 3I will knock the bow out of your left hand and the arrows out of your right hand, 4 and you and your army will die on those mountains. Then birds and wild animals will eat the flesh 5of your dead bodies left lying in open fields. I, the Lord, have spoken.
6I will set fire to the land of Magog and to those nations along the seacoast that think they are so secure, and they will know that I am the Lord.
7My people Israel will know me, and they will no longer disgrace my holy name. Everyone on earth will know that I am the holy Lord God of Israel. 8The day is coming when these things will happen, just as I have promised.
9When that day comes, the people in the towns of Israel will collect the weapons of their dead enemies. They will use these shields, bows and arrows, spears, and clubs as firewood, and there will be enough to last for seven years. 10They will burn these weapons instead of gathering sticks or chopping down trees. That's how the Israelites will take revenge on those who robbed and abused them. I, the Lord, have spoken.
The Burial of Gog
The Lord said:
11After Gog has been destroyed, I will bury him and his army in Israel, in Travelers' Valley, east of the Dead Sea. That graveyard will be so large that it will block the way of anyone who tries to walk through the valley, which will then be known as “The Valley of Gog's Army.” 12The Israelites will spend seven months burying dead bodies and cleaning up their land. 13Everyone will help with the burial, and they will be honored for this on the day the brightness of my glory is seen. 14After those seven months, the people will appoint a group of men to look for any dead bodies left unburied. This must be done for seven months to make sure that the land is no longer unclean. 15Whenever they find a human bone, they will set up a marker next to it. Then the gravediggers will bury it in “The Valley of Gog's Army” 16near the town of “Gog's Army.” After that, the land will be pure again.
17 Ezekiel, son of man, I am going to hold a feast on Israel's mountains and offer sacrifices there. So invite all the birds and wild animals to come from every direction and eat the meat of sacrifices and drink the blood. The birds and animals 18will feast on the bodies of warriors and foreign rulers that I will sacrifice like sheep, goats, and bulls. 19I want the birds and animals to eat until they are full and drink until they are drunk. 20They will come to my table and stuff themselves with the flesh of horses and warriors of every kind. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
Israel Will Be Restored
The Lord said:
21When I punish the nations of the earth, they will see the brightness of my glory. 22The people of Israel will know from then on that I am the Lord their God. 23Foreign nations will realize that the Israelites were forced to leave their own land because they sinned against me. I turned my back on my people and let enemies attack and kill them. 24Their lives were wicked and corrupt, and they deserved to be punished.
25Now I will show mercy to the people of Israel and bring them back from the nations where they are living. They are Jacob's descendants, so I will bless them and show that I am holy. 26They will live safely in their own land, but will be ashamed when they remember their evil ways and how they disgraced me. 27Foreign nations will watch as I take the Israelites from enemy lands and bring them back home, and those nations will see that I am holy.
28My people will realize that I, the Lord their God, sent them away as prisoners and now will bring them back to their own land. 29Never again will I turn my back on the people of Israel, and my Spirit will live in them. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_text:
Ti-Dindaan gíti sòon̄ ki bíikì Gɔɔgi pu
1«Sii nisaaleen, dū m-nyɔɔbundi kí nàatī Gɔɔgi kí tùkù-u man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee yii: <Sii Gɔɔgi, Meeseeki nì Tuubaal bɔtibikpiliu, m làá jáǹ-si. 2M làá nyāntí-si a-tiŋkin. M làá ŋá-si mpɔn á nyā a-tiŋki kin bí ŋgan púee kí jáǹ Isirayeel jooŋŋi. 3Míǹ boonee ní ḿ fáá-si ní butɔbu ń ŋmátí kí nyā a-ŋaŋgan poon kí lítí, ní ipiin ń ŋmátí kí nyā a-ŋaŋgiil poon kí lítí. 4Niinee, sii nì a-janjakitil nì a-bɔɔbi bin kútì a-puee ń kpú Isirayeel jooŋŋi pu. M làá yàntī kaajiikub nì ipeel ń ŋmɔ́ ni-nanti. 5A làá lítí kitiŋ kí kpú, di sá yii man di sòon̄, man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di lī míǹ. 6M làá sēē Maagoogi tiŋki ŋŋmi nì bin kóòń ntimu mun nnyim māntìi tú bi bí ŋgbansɔŋfinee. Niinee báà ŋma làá béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan. 7M làá yàntī m-nibul Isirayeel ń béé m nín bí circir puee. Maa làá ti yàntī bí kpèè m-circir yindi fám ní atimbun ŋin kíǹee ń béé yii man di sá ni-Dindaan, Isirayeel circir Nimbɔtiu. 8Tiŋman, tíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ làá ŋá míǹ, ní an kíĺ ki bíi ŋáań míǹ gba. Ibɔsoon wiiŋŋu ŋun bɔti m nìn sòon̄ ki síiǹee dee. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di lī míǹ. 9Isirayeel yab làá dāá nyā bi-timmun. Bi làá dāá kpāā ŋŋmi ní kí dū bi-nannanliibi janjawanti kí ŋá poon án wà. Agbampɔɔ, akpaan nì ŋwaamu nì itɔfi nì ipiin nì ŋkpamu nì ntàataajimu làá nīn bí ŋŋmee poon ki wù áli abin aluli. 10Binib kaa dāa gíti cá kusaau idɔpu àá kí cù kupɔɔun kí gāā isufi, di sá yii tijanjawan gbanti ní bi làá nīn cáa kpà ŋŋmi. Bin nìn fúkúl̀-bee, bi làá dāá fūkul̀-bi kí téeǹ. Bin nìn kóoǹ ni-wantee, ni làá dāá kóoǹ bi-wanti kí téeǹ. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di lī míǹ.
11«Ŋwiin gbantee, m làá dāá tīī Gɔɔgi ntaŋkpiifal ŋun poon bi làá síb́-uee Isirayeel tiŋkin. Bisanjitiliibi tantakalin, Ŋyaam mɔɔl ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú ní án làá nīn sá, ní ntaŋkpiifal gbanti làá pìin̄ bisanjitiliibi nsan. Niin ní bi làá síb́ Gɔɔgi nì u-janjakitil kɔkɔ. Bi làá nīn yíì mpaan gbanti yii <Gɔɔgi Nipaaku Tantakal>. 12Isirayeel yab làá dāá dū iŋmal iluli ní kí síb́-bi, ní kí fíntí kitiŋ kí nyāntí tijɔkɔndin. 13Kitiŋ nee nib kɔkɔ làá dāá síb́-bi, ní kí dāá nīn bí dipɔɔpindin daliŋkin m làá lēē m-nyooti kí dàkèe. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ. 14Iŋmal iluli gbanti boonee, bi làá dāá lēē bininjab biba. Bíǹ tundi di làá nīn sá bí nīn yìiǹ kitiŋ kɔkɔ pu, kí nyàab̀ anikpil ŋin dáá gbíntìi dɔ̄ kitiŋee kí síb́, kí ŋá kitiŋ circir. 15Bi làá dāá yìiǹ kitiŋ nee kɔkɔ pu. Bi-kansikin ubɔ yaa ká anikpabee ní ú tòò ataŋkpee kí kpúkuń ŋi-caŋin. An di làá nīn sá kudaaŋŋu. Niinee ní bin gbì itaŋkpiifalee ń dāan̄ kí yòon̄ akpabee kí cáá síb́ Gɔɔgi Nipaaku Tantakalin. 16Kitiŋ kiba gba làá dāá nīn bí niin bí nīn yíì-kì yii Amoona, taapu di sá yii: <Kunipaau>. Án nín làá ŋá pu kitiŋ nee ń nyā tijɔkɔndinee dee.»
17Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti gíti bí-mi yii: «Nisaaleen, tùkù inoon kɔkɔ nì i-buluku nì ipeel kɔkɔ yii í nyānní an kɔkɔ pu kí dāá kpāfì kí jī saraa un m làá ŋá kí tīī-bee jinti. Án làá nīn sá saraakpaan ní m làá ŋá Isirayeel jooŋŋi pu. Ni ŋūǹ kí ŋmɔ́ tinan kí nyɔ̀ fatiku. 18Ni làá ŋmɔ́ bibaatandambi nanti kí nyɔ̀ abɔtibil fatikuu, bibaatandambi nì abɔtibil ŋin bi dūu ŋá saraa ipijaa nì apibil nì iŋɔjaa nì Baasan nabiliŋ ŋin cáá ŋkpamee yil puee. 19Saraa gbanti pu ní m yíì-ni, ni làá ŋmɔ́ ŋkpam kí díkí ní kí nyɔ̀ fatiku kí gbí. 20Jiŋaakpaan gbanti poonee, ni làá ŋmɔ́ itaamu nì bitanjakaliibi nì bijanjaliibi nì bijanjaliibi bin kíǹee kɔkɔ nì bi-bulifi kii ni nín là puee. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ.
21«M làá dàkà atimbun ŋin kíǹee nib m-nyooti. Bi-kɔkɔ làá ká m nín cáá m-pɔŋŋu ki tūǹ ditundi ki sòoǹ binib bɔti puee. 22Kí yòon̄ ŋwiin gbantee, Isirayeel yab làá béé yii man di sá bi-Dindaan, bi-Nimbɔtiu.»
Bi nín kúlifì Eeseekiyeel bɔti puee
23«Atimbun ŋin kíǹee nib làá béé yii bi cúú Isirayeel yab ki cūnnì kuyuŋu bi-yìntitam pu ní, di sá yii baa yúl̀ man bi-Dindaan deedee. An pu ní m fātì m-boon ki tīī-bi. M dū-bi ki ŋá bi-nannanliibi ŋaan ní ki yāntì bi kūū-bi kujaaun. 24M nín fātì m-boon ki tīī-bee, m dàkā-bi bi-jɔkɔntuuŋŋi nì bi-yìntitam nín máaǹ kuŋyee ní.
25«Ama man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Kɔŋkɔnnee, m làá sɔ̄ Isirayeel yab, Jaakɔb naantiibi saai. M làá nyāntí-bi kuyuŋun kí fàtīí gíiǹní-bi ní kí yàntī bi-kɔkɔ ń nīn kíǹ ki tɔ́ m-circir yindi kii an nín máaǹ puee. 26Niinee bi làá súntí bi-cooi nì bi nín yīntiǹ-mi puee. Bi làá kàl̄ bi-tiŋkin ŋgbansɔŋfi ní ubɔ kaa làá ti fàaǹ-bi. 27M làá nyāntí-bi bi-nannanliibi tiŋkin ní kí kóoǹ-bi kí kpāfì ní kí gíiǹní-bi bi-dumpu. M làá dī bi-pu ní kí dàkà atimbun tikpil yii man di sá Unimbɔti circirdaan. 28M yaa láa kóoǹ Isirayeel yab ki kpáfì bi-tiŋkin kaa yāntì ubɔbɔ gbíntì kinicantiŋin kuyuŋunee, bi làá béé yii man di sá bi-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu. 29Maa làá ti fàtī m-boon kí tīī Isirayeel yab, kun puee m làá tīī-bi m-Fam. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ.»

english_text:
Ezekiel Sees the Future Temple in Jerusalem
1-2 Twenty-five years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, and 14 years after the Babylonians had captured Jerusalem, the Lord's power took control of me on the tenth day of the first month. The Lord showed me some visions in which I was carried to the top of a high mountain in Jerusalem. I looked to the south and saw what looked like a city full of buildings. 3 In my vision the Lord took me closer, and I saw a man who was sparkling like polished bronze. He was standing near one of the gates and was holding a tape measure in one hand and a measuring stick in the other. 4The man said, “Ezekiel, son of man, pay close attention to everything I'm going to show you—that's why you've been brought here. Listen carefully, because you must tell the people of Israel what you see.”
The East Gate
5 The first thing I saw was an outer wall that completely surrounded the temple area. The man took his measuring stick, which was three meters long, and measured the wall; it was three meters high and three meters thick. 6-7Then he went to the east gate, where he walked up steps that led to a long passageway. On each side of this passageway were three guardrooms, which were three meters square, and they were separated by walls two and a half meters thick. The man measured the distance between the opening of the gate and the first guardroom, and it was three meters, the thickness of the outer wall.
At the far end of this passageway, I saw an entrance room that faced the courtyard of the temple itself. There was also a distance of three meters between the last guardroom and the entrance room 8-9at the end of the passageway. The man measured this room: It was four meters from the doorway to the opposite wall, and the distance from the doorway to the wall on either side was one meter. 10The three guardrooms on each side of the passageway were the same size, and the walls that separated them were the same thickness.
11Next, the man measured the width of the passageway, and it was six and a half meters, but the two doors of the gate were only five meters wide. 12In front of the guardrooms, which were three meters square, was a railing about 50 centimeters high and 50 centimeters thick. 13The man measured the distance from the back wall of one of these rooms to the same spot in the room directly across the passageway, and it was twelve and a half meters. 14He measured the entrance room at the far end of the passageway, and it was ten meters wide. 15Finally, he measured the total length of the passageway, from the outer wall to the entrance room, and it was 25 meters. 16The three walls in the guardrooms had small windows in them, just like the ones in the entrance room. The walls along the passageway were decorated with carvings of palm trees.
The Outer Courtyard
17The man then led me through the passageway and into the outer courtyard of the temple, where I saw 30 rooms built around the outside of the courtyard. These side rooms were built against the outer wall, and in front of them was a sidewalk that circled the courtyard. 18This was known as the lower sidewalk, and it was 25 meters wide.
19I saw the gates that led to the inner courtyard of the temple and noticed that they were higher than those leading to the outer courtyard. The man measured the distance between the outer and inner gates, and it was 50 meters.
The North Gate
20Next, the man measured the north gate that led to the outer courtyard. 21This gate also had three guardrooms on each side of a passageway. The measurements of these rooms, the walls between them, and the entrance room at the far end of the passageway were exactly the same as those of the east gate. The north gate was also 25 meters long and 12.5 meters wide, 22and the windows, the entrance room, and the carvings of palm trees were just like those in the east gate. The entrance room also faced the courtyard of the temple and had seven steps leading up to it. 23Directly across the outer courtyard was a gate that led to the inner courtyard, just as there was for the east gate. The man measured the distance between the outer and inner gate, and it was 50 meters.
The South Gate
24The man then took me to the south gate. He measured the walls and the entrance room of this gate, and the measurements were exactly the same as those of the other two gates. 25There were windows in the guardrooms of this gate and in the entrance room, just like the others, and this gate was also 25 meters long and 12.5 meters wide. 26Seven steps led up to the gate; the entrance room was at the far end of the passageway and faced the courtyard of the temple. Carvings of palm trees decorated the walls along the passageway. 27And directly across the outer courtyard was a gate on the south side of the inner courtyard. The man measured the distance between the outer and inner gate, and it was also 50 meters.
The Gates Leading to the Inner Courtyard
28We then went into the inner courtyard, through the gate on the south side of the temple. The man measured the gate, and it was the same size as the gates in the outer wall. 29-30In fact, everything along the passageway was also the same size, including the guardrooms, the walls separating them, the entrance room at the far end, and the windows. This gate, like the others, was 25 meters long and 12.5 meters wide. 31The entrance room of this gate faced the outer courtyard, and carvings of palm trees decorated the walls of the passageway. Eight steps led up to this gate.
32Next, we went through the east gate to the inner courtyard. The man measured this gate, and it was the same size as the others. 33The guardrooms, the walls separating them, and its entrance room had the same measurements as the other gates. The guardrooms and the entrance room had windows, and the gate was 25 meters long and 12.5 meters wide. 34The entrance room faced the outer courtyard, and the walls in the passageway were decorated with carvings of palm trees. Eight steps also led up to this gate.
35Then the man took me to the north gate. He measured it, and it was the same size as the others, 36including the guardrooms, the walls separating them, and the entrance room. There were also windows in this gate. It was 25 meters long and 12.5 meters wide, 37and like the other inner gates, its entrance room faced the outer courtyard, and its walls were decorated with carvings of palm trees. Eight steps also led up to this gate.
The Rooms for Sacrificing Animals
38-39Inside the entrance room of the north gate, I saw four tables, two on each side of the room, where the animals to be sacrificed were killed. Just outside this room was a small building used for washing the animals before they were offered as sacrifices to please the Lord or sacrifices for sin or sacrifices to make things right. 40Four more tables were in the outer courtyard, two on each side of the steps leading into the entrance room. 41So there was a total of eight tables, four inside and four outside, where the animals were killed, 42-43and where the meat was placed until it was sacrificed on the altar.
Next to the tables in the entrance room were four stone tables 50 centimeters high and 75 centimeters square; the equipment used for killing the animals was kept on top of these tables. All around the walls of this room was a 75-millimeter shelf.
The Rooms Belonging to the Priests
44The man then took me to the inner courtyard, where I saw two buildings, one beside the inner gate on the north and the other beside the inner gate on the south. 45He said, “The building beside the north gate belongs to the priests who serve in the temple, 46and the building beside the south gate belongs to those who serve at the altar. All of them are descendants of Zadok and are the only Levites allowed to serve as the Lord's priests.”
The Inner Courtyard and the Temple
47Now the man measured the inner courtyard; it was 50 meters square. I also saw an altar in front of the temple.
48We walked to the porch of the temple, and the man measured the doorway of the porch: It was seven meters long, two and a half meters wide, and the distance from the doorway to the wall on either side was one and a half meters. 49The porch itself was ten meters by six meters, with steps leading up to it. There was a column on each side of these steps.
translation_text:
UNIMBƆTI LĒĒ KUNIMBƆTIDII KUPƆŊU KI DÀKĀ EESEEKIYEEL
Tibɔkilkaal
1Bi nín cúú-ti ki cūnnì kuyuŋu abin mmuŋku nì aŋmoo poon, dibindi nín kíĺ puee iwiin saalaa dal, an dàkà yii bi nín jáń ki fōō Jeerusaleem tiŋki dibindi diba kpá saalku deedeeyee ní ti-Dindaan pɔŋŋu kpákatìń m-pu ní ki cáá-mi ki cūnnì niin. 2Dileedakal diba poonee ní Unimbɔti yōoǹ-mi ki cáa cūnnì Isirayeel tiŋkin. U nìn dū-mi ki tɔ́kɔ́ǹ dijoofɔŋfɔkɔl diba yilpu kúntí kunti. Dijoolee jandi ŋgiil púee, adiin aba bí ki náań nì kitiŋ kiba. 3U cáá-mi ki cūnnì niinee ní m ká uninja ubɔ. Uninjee nìn náań nì tasa kúti ní ki yú ki kɔ́ĺ kipunyɔkɔ kiba. U nìn ŋúb́ u-ŋaan ŋŋaabu ŋun bí fálfalee ŋmiiŋu nì kukaluu kun bi cáa ŋmàntēe. 4U bí-mi yii: «Nisaaleen, kpítí a-nimbiliŋ kí ŋátí a-tafaliŋ. Á kpèè tin kɔkɔ m làá dàkà-si nee tiŋan, di sá yii an sá á kpèè-tèe pu ní bi cáań-si doo. Míǹ boonee, a làá dū tin kɔkɔ a ká dooyee kí māafì Isirayeel yab ní.»
Mmɔŋki cindi nì di-punyɔmmu
5Kun m kée sɔ̀. Digundi diba nìn bí ki māntìi tú kunimbɔtidii. Kukaluu kun uninjee nìn ŋúb́ee fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá santimeetab imuŋku ili nì saalaa ní. U nìn dū kukaluuee ki ŋmāntì digundee gbifiŋŋu nì di-fɔkɔŋŋu ní ki ká kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu diba pu ajanliitil pu. 6U nín cá kipunyɔkɔ kin bí kunimbɔtidii ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee ní ki dàb̄ akɔl. U nìn ŋmāntì kipunyɔkɔee nyɔkɔpu ní ki ká kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu diba pu. 7Biciitiliibi diiŋŋi kamaa púuŋŋu pú nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu diba pu ní ku-waaŋŋu sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu diba pu. Agun ŋin nìn pītì adiinee kansikinee gbifiŋŋu nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu miŋmoo pu. Kipunyɔkɔee nì kudii kun bi tà kí kɔ́ kunimbɔtidiin ku bíitiǹ-kuee kansikin nìn nyáń kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu diba pu. 8Bi nìn ŋmāntì kudii gbanti. 9Ku-nyooŋŋu nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu minii pu, ní ku-jaantalkub nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu mili pu. Kudii kun bi tà kí kɔ́ gbantee nìn bí poon pú ní. 10Bipunyɔɔciitiliibi diiŋŋi ŋin nìn bí kunimbɔtidii ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee nìn ŋmà ní. Adiin ata nìn bí nsanjaati ŋgan pú, ní ata mun bí ŋgiil pú. Agun ŋin nìn pītì ŋi-kansikinee kɔkɔ gbifiŋŋu nìn ŋmà ní. 11Uninjee nìn ŋmāntì kipunyɔkɔee punuu nín pìitī puee waaŋŋu ní ki ká kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu saalaa pu. Nsanjaatee waaŋŋu nìn nyáń kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu saalaa nì mita pu. 12Bipunyɔɔciitiliibi diiŋŋi ŋin jannaatiliŋ nìn ŋmà ki bí nsanjaati jaŋŋi kɔkɔ puee nyɔkɔpuee, bi nìn máń kiguŋŋi ní ki-fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu diba pu. 13Uninjee nìn ŋmāntì kí yòon̄ kudii kubɔ poon gundi kí cáá sāā kun bíitiǹ-kuee poon gundi ní ki ká kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu mmuŋku nì miŋmoo pu. 14U nìn ŋmāntì kudii kun ní bi tà kí kɔ́ kunimbɔtidiinee ní ki ká kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu mmuŋku pu. Kunimbɔtidii cindi nìn māntìi tú-ku an kɔkɔ pu. 15Kipunyɔkɔ kin bi dì kí kɔ́ kì bí boon pú gundi pu nì poon pú cindi punyɔkɔki kansikinee nìn nyáń kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu imuŋku ili nì saalaa. 16Bi nìn kpáá tilaandi ki nákáǹ tɔkɔlab ki māntìi tú bipunyɔɔciitiliibi diiŋŋi nì ŋi-jaantalkub nì kipunyɔkɔ poon pú nì agun ŋin pītì adiinee. Tɔkɔlab bin bi kpáá tilaandi ki nákáǹee mun nìn bí kudii kun bi tà kí kɔ́ee guŋŋi pu. Bi nìn lēē ibafi ki nyɔ̄kɔntì agun gbanti pu.
17Uninjee cáá-mi ki cūnnì kunimbɔtidii boon cindi. Bi nìn bɔ̀b̄ dicindi gbanti yilpu ní ki máń adiin mmuŋku nì saalaa ki māntìi tú. 18Bi nìn ŋàl̄ ki māntìi tú mpunyɔmu kɔkɔ. Adiinee nìn gíti bí taapu ki jítiǹ poon pú cindi. 19Uninjee nìn ŋmāntì digundi din bi máń ki tú kunimbɔtidii boon cindi kipunyɔkɔ bí bi dì ki kóò kunimbɔtidiinee nì digundi din bi máń ki tú kunimbɔtidii poon cindee ní ki ká kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu dilaataal pu. Ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú dee. Ŋgan púee, 20u ŋmāntì kipunyɔkɔ kin bí ŋgan pú bi dì ki kóò kunimbɔtidii boon cindinee. 21A yaa dī kipunyɔkɔ ki kóò kunimbɔtidiinee, bipunyɔɔciitiliibi diiŋŋi ata bí ŋgan pú ní ata bí ŋgiil pú. Agun nì kudii kun bi tà kí kɔ́ee púuŋŋu pú nì ku-waaŋŋu ŋwiin nyalaŋki pú punyɔkɔkee púuŋŋu pú nì ki-waaŋŋu ŋmà ní. Ŋgan pú punyɔkɔki púuŋŋu pú nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu imuŋku ili nì saalaa pu ní ki-waaŋŋu sá mmuŋku nì miŋmoo pu. 22Kudii kun bi tà kí kɔ́ee nì tɔkɔlab nì ibafi in bi nìn dūu nyɔ̄kɔntèe nì kipunyɔkɔ kin béeyee nìn ŋmà mpúun pú nì ŋwaan pu ní. Bi nìn dàb̀ akɔl aluli pu ní kí nín bà ŋgan pú punyɔkɔki, ní nyɔkɔpuee, kudii kun bi tà kí kɔ́ kunimbɔtidii poonee bí. 23Ŋgan pú punyɔkɔki nyɔkɔpuee, kipunyɔkɔ kiba gíti bí. Kíǹ ní bi dì kí kɔ́ kunimbɔtidii poon cindi. An pée bí kii ŋgan pú nín bí puee ní. Uninjee ŋmāntì mpunyɔmu mulee kansikin ní ki ká kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu dilaataal pu. 24Míǹ boonee ní u cáá-mi ki cūnnì ŋgiil pú ní m ká kipunyɔkɔ kiba mun niin. U nìn ŋmāntì bipunyɔɔciitiliibi diiŋŋi nì agun nì kudii kun bi tà kí kɔ́ee ní ki ká yii an nì mpunyɔmu mun kíǹee ŋmà mpúun pú nì ŋwaan pu. 25Niin muee, tɔkɔlab bí ki māntìi tú kipunyɔkɔ nì kudii kun bi tà ki kóòyee. Tɔkɔlab gbanti pée bí kii ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú nì ŋgan pú yab nín bí puee ní. Ŋgiil pú punyɔkɔki gbantee púuŋŋu kɔkɔ nìn kpáfì kukaluuee imuŋku ili nì saalaa pu ní ŋwaan nyáń kukaluuee mmuŋku nì miŋmoo pu. 26Bi nìn dàb̀ akɔl aluli pu ní kí nín bà ŋgiil pú punyɔkɔki, ní nyɔkɔpuee, kudii kun bi tà kí kɔ́ kunimbɔtidii poonee bí. Bi nìn dū ibafi ki nyɔ̄kɔntì poon pú guŋŋi gbanti ŋgan nì ŋgiil kɔkɔ pú. 27Kipunyɔkɔ gbanti nyɔkɔpuee, kiba mun nìn gíti bí. Kíǹ ní bi nìn dì kí kɔ́ kunimbɔtidii poon cindi. Uninjee nìn ŋmāntì mpunyɔmu gbanti kansikin ní ki ká kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu dilaataal pu.
Kunimbɔtidii poon cindi nì ki-punyɔmmu
28Uninjee nìn dū-mi ki dī ŋgan pú punyɔkɔki ní ti kɔ́ kunimbɔtidii poon cindi. U nìn ŋmāntì kipunyɔkɔ gbanti ní ki ká yii kì nì mpunyɔmu mun bí boon pú gundi puee ŋmà. 29Bipunyɔɔciitiliibi diiŋŋi nì agun ŋin bi dūu pītèe nì kudii kun bi tà kí kɔ́ee nì mpunyɔmu mun kíǹee púuŋŋu nì ku-waaŋŋu nìn ŋmà. Kudii kun bi tà kí kɔ́ee nìn cáá tɔkɔlab ní ki māntìi tú. Kipunyɔkɔee púuŋŋu kɔkɔ nyáń kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu imuŋku ili nì saalaa pu ní ki-waaŋŋu nyáń kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu mmuŋku nì miŋmoo pu. 30Adiin nìn māntìi tú kipunyɔkɔ gbanti. Kudii kubɔ púuŋŋu nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu mmuŋku nì miŋmoo pu, ní ki-waaŋŋu sá kukaluuee miŋmoo pu. 31Kipunyɔkɔ gbanti diiku kun bi tà kí kɔ́ee nìn bíitiǹ kunimbɔtidii boon cindi ní. Bi nìn lēē ibafi ki nyɔ̄kɔntì ki-jaantalkub. Bi nìn tà akɔl anii pu ní kí kɔ́ ku-ni. 32Uninjee nìn dū-mi ki dī ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú punyɔkɔki ki kɔ́ kunimbɔtidii poon cindi. U nìn ŋmāntì kipunyɔkɔ gbanti ní ki ká yii ki nì mun kíǹee ŋmà. 33Bipunyɔɔciitiliibi diiŋŋi nì agun ŋin pītèe nì kudii kun bi tà kí kɔ́ kunimbɔtidiinee nì mpunyɔmu mun kíǹee púuŋŋu nì ŋwaan nìn pée ŋmà ní. Tɔkɔlab nìn bí ki māntìi tú kipunyɔkɔee nì kudii kun bi tà kí kɔ́ee. Kipunyɔkɔ gbanti kɔkɔ fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu imuŋku ili nì saalaa pu, ní ki-waaŋŋu sá kukaluee mmuŋku nì miŋmoo pu. 34Kipunyɔkɔ gbanti diiku kun bi tà kí kɔ́ee nìn bíitiǹ kunimbɔtidii boon cindi ní. Bi nìn lēē ibafi ki nyɔ̄kɔntì ki-jaantalkub. Bi nìn dàb̀ akɔl anii pu ní kí kɔ́. 35Uninjee nìn dū-mi ki dī ŋgan pú punyɔkɔki ní ki ŋmāntì-kì. Kipunyɔkɔ gbanti nì mun kíǹee ŋmà ní. 36Ki mun cáá bipunyɔɔciitiliibi diiŋŋi nì agun ŋin pītèe nì kudii kun bi tà kí kɔ́ kunimbɔtidiinee ní tɔkɔlab māntìi tú-kì. Kipunyɔkɔ gbanti kɔkɔ fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu imuŋku ili nì saalaa pu, ní ki-waaŋŋu sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu mmuŋku nì miŋmoo pu. 37Kipunyɔkɔ gbanti diiku kun bi tà kí kɔ́ee nìn bíitiǹ kunimbɔtidii boon cindi ní. Bi nìn lēē ibafi ki nyɔ̄kɔntì ki-jaantalkub. Bi nìn dàb̀ akɔl anii pu ní kí kɔ́.
38Ŋgan pú punyɔkɔki jaantalkub kansikinee, kudii kubɔ nìn bí niin. Niin ní bi nìn fíntí tiwaŋkuti tin bi kù ki ŋáań bisaraawɔkaabee. 39Kipunyɔkɔ gbanti diiku kun bi tà kí kɔ́ee poonee, teebilib bili nìn sí dijandi diba pú ní bili mun sí dijandi din kíǹee. Teebilib gbanti pu ní bi nìn làntī bisaraawɔkaabi nì ikpiti pɔ̄tam nì dibɔkpil saraabi waŋkuti. 40Kudii gbanti boonee, teebilib binaa nìn bí. A yaa jɔ́ḿ ŋgan pú punyɔkɔki watil púee, bili bí ŋgan pú ní bili bí ŋgiil pú. 41Teebilib nìn kpáfì binii ní bi làntī saraabi waŋkuti bi-pu, binaa bí kipunyɔkɔee dijandi diba pú ní binaa mun bí dijandi din kíǹee pú. 42Bi nìn kpítì ataŋkpee ní ki dūu ŋá teebilib binaa bin pu bi kù saraawɔkaa waŋkutee. Teebilibee jannaatiliŋ nìn ŋmà ní. Dijandi diba nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu diba pu nì dijandi ní ŋfɔkɔn sá diba pu. Teebilib gbanti pu ní bi nìn pāantí tiwan tin bi cáa bɔ́ntí saraabee. 43Bi nìn cátì inyinsan ki māntìi tú teebilibee, ní inyinsanee waaŋŋu nìn sá kii kuŋaŋfaau waaŋŋuee. Teebilib gbanti pu ní bi nìn cáá saraabi nanti ki pāantí. 44Uninjee nìn cáá-mi ki kɔ́ǹ kunimbɔtidii poon cindi. Niin ní bilaŋgaaliibi diiŋŋi nìn bí. Kubɔ nìn bí ŋgan pú punyɔkɔki caŋin ní bi pìitī-ku ŋgiil watil pú, ní kun kíǹee bí ŋgiil watil pú punyɔkɔki caŋin ní bi pìitī-ku ŋgan pú. 45Uninjee nìn bí-mi yii: «Kudii kun nimbiin túĺ ŋgiil pú nee, bisaraaŋaliibi bin tūǹ ditundi kunimbɔtidiinee diiku dee. 46Kudii kun nimbiin túĺ ŋgan pú nee, bisaraaŋaliibi bin tūǹ ditundi nsaraafan puee diiku dee. Leefii naakookun yab kansikinee, Sadooki naantiibi baba di ŋūǹ kí sútí kí pìl̄ ti-Dindaan kí tɔ̄ ditundi kí tīī-u.»
Kunimbɔtidii nín bí puee
47Uninjee nìn ŋmāntì kunimbɔtidii poon pú cindi: di-jannaatiliŋ nìn ŋmà ní. Dijandi diba nìn nyáń kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu dilaataal pu. Nsaraafan nìn bí kunimbɔtidii nyɔkɔpu ní. 48U nìn cáá-mi kí kɔ́ǹ kudii kun bi tà kí kɔ́ kunimbɔtidiinee. U nìn ŋmāntì ki-jaantalkub ní ki ká kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu miŋmoo pu dijandi kamaa pú, ní kipunyɔkɔ ki-ba waaŋŋu sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu diba kpá saalku pu. Agun ŋin bi nìn máń ki pūntèe gbifiŋŋu nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu mita pu. 49Kudii kun bi tà kí kɔ́ee fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu mmuŋku pu, ní ku-waaŋŋu sá saalaa nì mili pu. Bi nìn dàb̀ akɔl saalaa pu ní kí kɔ́ ku-poon. Kipunyɔkɔee janliitiliŋ puee, jaantalkub nìn bí ní.

english_text:
1Next we went into the main room of the temple. The man measured the doorway of this room: It was 3 meters wide, 2five meters long, and the distance from the doorway to the wall on either side was two and a half meters. The main room itself was 20 meters by 10 meters.
3-4Then the man walked to the far end of the temple's main room and said, “Beyond this doorway is the most holy place.” He first measured the doorway: It was one meter wide, 3 meters long, and the distance from the doorway to the wall on either side was 3.5 meters. Then he measured the most holy place, and it was 10 meters square.
The Storage Rooms of the Temple
5The man measured the wall of the temple, and it was three meters thick. Storage rooms two meters wide were built against the outside of the wall. 6There were three levels of rooms, with 30 rooms on each level, and they rested on ledges that were attached to the temple walls, so that nothing was built into the walls. 7The walls of the temple were thicker at the bottom than at the top, which meant that the storage rooms on the top level were wider than those on the bottom level. Steps led from the bottom level, through the middle level, and into the top level.
8The temple rested on a stone base three meters high, which also served as the foundation for the storage rooms. 9The outside walls of the storage rooms were two and a half meters thick; there was nothing between these walls 10and the nearest buildings ten meters away. 11One door led into the storage rooms on the north side of the temple, and another door led to those on the south side. The stone base extended two and a half meters beyond the outside wall of the storage rooms.
The West Building and the Measurements of the Temple
12I noticed another building: It faced the west end of the temple and was 35 meters wide, 45 meters long, and had walls over 2.5 meters thick.
13The man measured the length of the temple, and it was 50 meters. He then measured from the back wall of the temple, across the open space behind the temple, to the back wall of the west building; it was 50 meters. 14The distance across the front of the temple, including the open space on either side, was also 50 meters.
15Finally, the man measured the length of the west building, including the side rooms on each end, and it was also 50 meters.
The Inside of the Temple
The inside walls of the temple's porch and main room 16were paneled with wood all the way from the floor to the windows, while the doorways, the small windows, and the three side rooms were trimmed in wood. 17The paneling stopped just above the doorway. These walls were decorated 18-20with carvings of winged creatures and had a carving of a palm tree between the creatures. Each winged creature had two faces: A human face looking at the palm tree on one side, and a lion's face looking at the palm tree on the other side. These designs were carved into the paneling all the way around the two rooms.
21The doorframe to the temple's main room was in the shape of a rectangle.
The Wooden Altar
In front of the doorway to the most holy place was something that looked like 22a wooden altar. It was one and a half meters high and one meter square, and its corners, its base, and its sides were made of wood. The man said, “This is a reminder that the Lord is constantly watching over his temple.”
The Doors in the Temple
23Both the doorway to the main room of the temple and the doorway to the most holy place had two doors, 24and each door had two sections that could fold open. 25The doors to the main room were decorated with carvings of winged creatures and palm trees just like those on the walls, and there was a wooden covering over the porch just outside these doors. 26The walls on each side of this porch had small windows and were also decorated with carvings of palm trees.
translation_text:
1Uninjee nìn cáá-mi ki kɔ́ǹ kunimbɔtidii dikpaaŋkun ní ki ŋmāntì-ku. Bi nìn máń agun ali ní agunee kansikinee, nsan ŋun bi dì ki kóò kudikpaaŋŋu gbantinee nìn bí. Digundi kamaa gbifiŋŋu nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu miluu pu. 2Kipunyɔkɔ waaŋŋu nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu saalaa pu, ní agun ŋin bí ajanliitil puee gbifiŋŋu sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu miŋmoo pu. Kudii ku-ba púuŋŋu nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu imuŋku ili pu, ní ŋwaan sá mmuŋku pu. 3Míǹ boonee ní u jítìi kɔ́ poon poon diiku ki ŋmāntì kipunyɔkɔ jaantalkub ní ki ká kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu mili pu, ní kipunyɔkɔ ki-ba waaŋŋu sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu miluu pu. Ki-guŋŋi gbifiŋŋu nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu miluli pu. 4U nìn ŋmāntì kudii ku-ba ní ki ká mpúun pú kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu mmuŋku pu, ní ki ká ŋwaan pú mmuŋku pu. Niinee ní u tùkū-mi yii niin di sá <Circir páaa laŋki>.
Ndibiyaamu mun kútì kunimbɔtidii puee
5Míǹ boonee ní u ŋmāntì kunimbɔtidii poon gundi ní ki ká ŋgbifin kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu miluu pu. Bi nìn máń ndibiyaamu ki māntìi tú digundi gbanti ní ndibiyaamu gbanti waaŋŋu nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu mili pu. 6Ndibiyaamu gbanti nìn tɔ́kɔ́ tɔb pu mita pu, ní dicindi kamaa cáá adiin mmuŋku nì saalaa. Bi nìn máń kidibiki kamaa ki tɔ́kɔǹ boon pú gundin, ama an kaa nìn kɔ́ kunimbɔtidii ku-ba gundin. 7Dicindi kamaa puee, bi nìn bàtī digundi gbifiŋŋu pu, ní ndibiyaamu wàantí ki cá, míǹ ní an nìn bí ki māntì kunimbɔtidii ki tú. An puee, yilpu dibiyaamu nìn wāā ki jítiǹ taapu yamu. A yaa nìn kíĺ taapuee, a nìn jɔ́ḿ adiin ŋin tɔ́kɔ́ taapu yaŋ puee ní kí nín bà ŋin mun gíti tɔ́kɔ́ kansikin yaŋ puee. 8M nìn gíti ká yii ndibiyaamu mun bi nìn máń ki tú kunimbɔtidiiyee nìn lībitì adiin ŋin kíǹee kɔkɔ. Mu nìn lībitì-ŋi kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu miluu pu ní. 9Ndibiyaamu gundi din bí boonee gbifiŋŋu sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu miŋmoo pu. Adiin ŋin bi nìn máń ki nákáǹ kunimbɔtidii boon gundi 10nì adiin ŋin kíǹee kansikin nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu mmuŋku pu ki māntìi tú. 11Ndibiyaamuee punyɔmmu muli nìn túĺ mpaan ŋun bí fám gbanti watil pú. Kipunyɔkɔ kiba nìn bí ŋgan pú ní kiba mun bí ŋgiil pú. Digundi din bi nìn máń ki tú mpaan gbantee gbifiŋŋu nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu miluu pu. 12Kunimbɔtidii ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki púee, kudii kubɔ nìn bí mpaan ŋun dɔ̄ fám gbanti nyɔkɔpu. Kudiiyee púuŋŋu nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu imuŋku inaa nì saalaa pu, ní ku-waaŋŋu sá imuŋku ita nì saalaa pu. Ku-guŋŋi gbifiŋŋu nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu miŋmoo pu. 13Uninjee nìn ŋmāntì kunimbɔtidii ní ki ká yii ku-púuŋŋu nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu dilaataal pu. Mpaan ŋun nìn dɔ̄ fámee nì kudii kun bí ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki púee nì ku-guŋŋi púuŋŋu kɔkɔ nìn kpáfì kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu dilaataal pu. 14Kunimbɔtidii jandi din bí ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee nì mpaan ŋun dɔ̄ fámee waaŋŋu nìn nyáń kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu dilaataal pu. 15Uninjee nìn tí ŋmāntì kudii kun bí kunimbɔtidii boonee. Kudiiyee nì isan in bí ku-jaŋŋi liitil puee fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu dilaataal pu.
Kunimbɔtidii poon
Kudii kun bi tà kí kɔ́ kunimbɔtidii poonee nì kudikpaaŋŋuee nì kudii kun bí poonee 16nì kipunyɔkɔ nì tɔkɔlab bin bi dū tilaandi ki kpáá ki nákáǹee nì isan in bí ki māntìi tú aditɔntɔkɔee, bi nìn dū ndɔpampamu ní ki bīiǹ ki māntìi tú kí yòon̄ kitiŋ kí cáá sāā tɔkɔlab. Bi nìn dū ndɔpampamu ní ki bīiǹ tɔkɔlab bi-ba. 17Kunimbɔtidii boon nì ku-poon, kí yòon̄ kipunyɔkɔ kí cáá sāā poon poon diikuee, bi nìn bɔ́ntì mpaan ŋubɔ 18kí lēē keerubimbi nì ibafi. Bi nìn lēē bubabu bubɔ ki sákaǹ keerubimbi bili kansikin. Keerubim kamaa nìn cáá inimbiin ili ní: 19unil nimbiin nìn túĺ bubabu kpakpalku kubɔ, ní gbikinti nimbiin túĺ bubabu kpakpalku kun kíǹee watil pú. Bi nìn pée kpítì míǹ ní ki nákáǹ nákáǹ ki māntìi tú kunimbɔtidii. 20Bi nìn kpítì keerubimbi nì ibafi agun pu kí yòon̄ kitiŋ kí cáá sāā punuubi yilpu. 21Idɔ in pu kudikpaaŋŋu punuu nìn sàkēe jannaatiliŋ nìn ŋmà ní.
<Circir páaa laŋki> nyɔkɔpuee, tiba nìn bí niin ki náań nì 22ndɔ saraafaŋŋu. Ŋu-fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu mita pu ní ŋu-waaŋŋu sá mili pu.
23Kunimbɔtidii nì circir laŋki nìn cáá mpunyɔmu muli ní. Bi dì kiba pu ní kí kɔ́ kudikpaaŋŋun ní kí dī kin kíǹee pu kí kɔ́ circir páaa laŋki. 24Mpunyɔmu gbanti nìn cáá punuubi bili bili ní. 25Bi nìn kpítì keerubimbi nì ibafi ki nákáǹ kudikpaaŋŋu punuubi pu, kii bi nín ŋá agun pu puee ní. 26Kipunyɔkɔ pu guŋŋi puee, tɔkɔlab bin pu bi kpáá tilaandi ki nákáǹee nìn bí, ní bi kpítì ibafi ki nákáǹ nákáǹ.

english_text:
The Sacred Rooms for the Priests
1-2After the man and I left the temple and walked back to the outer courtyard, he showed me a set of rooms on the north side of the west building. This set of rooms was 50 meters long and 25 meters wide. 3On one side of them was the 10 meters of open space that ran alongside the temple, and on the other side was the sidewalk that circled the outer courtyard. The rooms were arranged in three levels 4with doors that opened toward the north, and in front of them was a walkway five meters wide and 50 meters long. 5The rooms on the top level were narrower than those on the middle level, and the rooms on the middle level were narrower than those on the bottom level. 6The rooms on the bottom level supported those on the two upper levels, and so these rooms did not have columns like other buildings in the courtyard. 7-8To the north was a privacy wall 25 meters long, 9-10and at the east end of this wall was the door leading from the courtyard to these rooms.
There was also a set of rooms on the south side of the west building. 11These rooms were exactly like those on the north side, and they also had a walkway in front of them. 12The door to these rooms was at the east end of the wall that stood in front of them.
13The man then said to me:
These rooms on the north and south sides of the temple are the sacred rooms where the Lord's priests will eat the most holy offerings. These offerings include the grain sacrifices, the sacrifices for sin, and the sacrifices to make things right. 14When the priests are ready to leave the temple, they must go through these rooms before they return to the outer courtyard. They must leave their sacred clothes in these rooms and put on regular clothes before going anywhere near other people.
The Size of the Temple Area
15After the man had finished measuring the buildings inside the temple area, he took me back through the east gate and measured the wall around this area. 16He used his measuring stick to measure the east side of this wall; it was 250 meters long. 17-19Then he measured the north side, the south side, and the west side of the wall, and they were each 250 meters long, 20and so the temple area was a perfect square. The wall around this area separated what was sacred from what was ordinary.
translation_text:
Adiin ŋin bi nìn máń ki kɔ́ĺ kunimbɔtidiiyee
1Uninjee nìn nyántì-mi kunimbɔtidii boon cindin ŋgan pú ní ki yāntì m kɔ́ adiin ŋin bí ki túĺ mpaan ŋun dɔ̄ famee nì kudii kun bí kunimbɔtidii boonee. 2Adiin ŋin nìn bí niin gbantee kɔkɔ púuŋŋu nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu dilaataal pu ní ŋi-waaŋŋu sá imuŋku ili nì saalaa pu. 3Dijandi diba púee, adiinee túĺ mpaan ŋun dɔ̄ fám ki māntìi tú kunimbɔtidiiyee ki yōoǹ kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu mmuŋku pu. Dijandi din kíǹee púee, ŋi nìn bíitiǹ bi nín bɔ̀b̄ kunimbɔtidii puee boon pú ní. Bi nìn bɔ́ntì adiin gbanti ní ŋi tɔ́kɔ́ tɔb pu mita pu. 4Adiinee nyɔkɔpu, poon cindi watil púee, nsan ŋubɔ nìn dɔ̄ ŋwaan sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu saalaa pu, ní mpúun sá dilaataal pu. Bi nìn dì ŋgan pú ní kí kɔ́ kudii gbantin. 5Adiin ŋin nìn tɔ́kɔ́ yilpuee kaa nìn wāā ki bàn̄ ŋin bí taapuee, di sá yii isan nìn fōō mpaan yilpu diiŋŋi pu ki jítiǹ kansikin nì taapu yaŋ pu. 6Adiin gbanti nìn tɔ́kɔ́ tɔb pu mita pu ní kaa nìn cáá jaantalkub kii kunimbɔtidii cindin diiŋŋi ŋin kíǹee nín cáá puee. An pu ní adiin ŋin nìn tɔ́kɔ́ yilpuee nìn sá ŋwaamu ki jítiǹ ŋin bí taapuee nì ŋin bí kansikinee. 7Boon pú cindi jandi púee, digundi din nìn bí adiinee púuŋŋu puee nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu imuŋku ili nì saalaa pu. 8Di sá yii adiinee ŋi-ba púuŋŋu nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu imuŋku ili nì saalaa pu ní. Ama adiin ŋin nìn bíitiǹ kunimbɔtidiiyee púuŋŋu nìn sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu dilaataal pu. 9Adiinee taapu púee, kipunyɔkɔ kin bi dì kí kɔ́ kí nyānní boon pú cindinee nìn bí. 10Kipunyɔkɔ gbanti nìn bí laakin dicindi gundi kífée ní.
Ŋgiil púee, adiin aba nìn bí ki túĺ dicindi nì kudii kun bí kunimbɔtidii boonee. 11Adiin gbanti nyɔkɔpuee, nsan ŋubɔ nìn bí. Adiin gbanti púuŋŋu nì ŋi-waaŋŋu nì ŋin bí ŋgan púee yaŋ nìn ŋmà ní. Ŋi-punyɔmmu nì bi nín máń-ŋi puee nì bi-punuubi sá tiwambaantiil ní. 12Adiin ŋin bí ŋgiil gbantee punuubi sá bibaantiibi nì ŋin bí ŋgan púee yab ní. Nsanee nín kífí puee, kipunyɔkɔ kiba nìn bí ki túĺ digundi din bi máń ki tú circir paaŋŋuee. Bi nìn dì ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú ní kí kɔ́ niin. 13Uninjee nìn bí-mi yii: «Adiin ŋin bí ŋgan pú nì ŋgiil pú ki túĺ dicindee, bi dū-ŋi ki sú Unimbɔti ní. Niin ní bisaraaŋaliibi bin nìn ŋūǹ kí kɔ́ circir páaa laŋkee nìn jīǹ saraabi bin bí circir páaayee jinti. Niin ní bi máaǹ kí dū tiwan tin bí circir páaayee nì saraabi nì ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraabi nì dibɔkpil saraabi kí bíĺ, di sá yii mpaan gbanti bí circir ní. 14Bisaraaŋaliibi bin yaa kɔ́ circir kɔŋkooŋŋunee kaa ŋūǹ kí nyānní boon pú cindin dicilpu. Bi máaǹ kí dū bi-circir wampeeŋkaati tin bi pēeǹ ki túń ti-Dindaan tundee kí bíĺ adiin gbantin, ní kí dū abɔkuti aba kí pèen̄ ní kí nín nyā laakin samaa kpáfèe.»
Boon pú gundi ŋmàntitam
15Uninjee nín ŋmāntì adiin ŋin bí kunimbɔtidiinee ki dóòyee ní u dū-mi ki dī ŋwìiń nyalaŋki punyɔkɔ pú ki nyántì. Niinee ní u kíĺ ki bíi ŋmàntī mpaan ŋun māntìi tú kunimbɔtidiiyee. 16U nìn dū kukaluu kun u cáa ŋmàntēe ki ŋmāntì ní ki ká yii ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee, mpúun sá kukaluuee fɔkɔŋŋu alaataa aŋmoo pu. 17U nìn dū kukaluuee ki ŋmāntì ŋgan pú jandi ní ki ká alaataa aŋmoo pu. 18U nìn dū kukaŋmantikaauee ki ŋmāntì ŋgiil pú jandi ní ki ká alaataa aŋmoo pu. 19Ní u fātì u-ba ki túĺ ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú ki dū kukaluuee ki ŋmāntì ŋgan pú jandi ní ki ká alaataa aŋmoo pu. 20Míǹ ní u nìn ŋmāntì digundi din māntìi tú kunimbɔtidiiyee jannaatiliŋ. Digundee jannaatiliŋ nìn ŋmà ní ki nìn pītì mpaan ŋun bí circiree nì ŋfantanti kansikin.

english_text:
The Lord's Glory Returns to the Temple
1The man took me back to the east gate of the temple, 2 where I saw the brightness of the glory of Israel's God coming from the east. The sound I heard was as loud as ocean waves, and everything around was shining with the dazzling brightness of his glory. 3This vision was like the one I had seen when God came to destroy Jerusalem and like the one I had seen near the Chebar River.
I immediately bowed with my face to the ground, 4and the Lord's glory came through the east gate and into the temple. 5The Lord's Spirit lifted me to my feet and carried me to the inner courtyard, where I saw that the Lord's glory had filled the temple.
6The man was standing beside me, and I heard the Lord say from inside the temple:
7Ezekiel, son of man, this temple is my throne on earth. I will live here among the people of Israel forever. They and their kings will never again disgrace me by worshiping idols at local shrines or by setting up memorials to their dead kings. 8Israel's kings built their palaces so close to my holy temple that only a wall separated them from me. Then these kings disgraced me with their evil ways, and in my fierce anger I destroyed them. 9But if the people and their kings stop worshiping other gods and tear down those memorials, I will live among them forever.
10The people of Israel must suffer shame for sinning against me, so tell them about my holy temple. Let them think about it, 11then if they are truly sorry, describe for them the design and shape of the temple, the gates, the measurements, and how the buildings are arranged. Explain the regulations about worshiping there, then write down these things, so they can study and obey them.
12The temple area on my holy mountain must be kept sacred! This is the most important law about the temple.
The Altar
13 According to the official standards, the altar in the temple had the following measurements: Around the bottom of the altar was a gutter 50 centimeters wide and 50 centimeters deep, with a 25-centimeter ledge on the outer rim. 14-17The altar rested on a base and had three sections, each one of them square. The bottom section was 8 meters on each side and one meter high. The middle section was 7 meters on each side and 2 meters high, and it had a 25-centimeter rim around its outer edge. The top section, which was 6 meters on each side and 2 meters high, was the place where sacrifices were burned, and the four corners of the top section looked like the horns of a bull. The steps leading up to the altar were on the east side.
The Dedication of the Altar
18 The Lord God said:
Ezekiel, son of man, after the altar is built, it must be dedicated by offering sacrifices on it and by splattering it with blood. Here is what you must do: 19The priests of the Levi tribe from the family of Zadok the priest are the only ones who may serve in my temple—this is my law. So give them a young bull to slaughter as a sacrifice for sin. 20Take some of the animal's blood and smear it on the four corners of the altar, some on the corners of the middle section, and some more on the rim around its edge. That will purify the altar and make it fit for offering sacrifices to me. 21Then take the body of the bull outside the temple area and burn it at the special place.
22The next day, a goat that has nothing wrong with it must be offered as a sacrifice for sin. Purify the altar with its blood, just as you did with the blood of the bull. 23Then choose a young bull and a young ram that have nothing wrong with them, 24and bring them to my temple. The priests will sprinkle salt on them and offer them as sacrifices to please me.
25Each day for the next seven days, you must offer a goat and a bull and a ram as sacrifices for sin. These animals must have nothing wrong with them. 26The priests will purify the altar during those days, so that it will be acceptable to me and ready to use. 27From then on, the priests will use this altar to offer sacrifices to please me and sacrifices to ask my blessing. Then I will be pleased with the people of Israel. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_text:
Unimbɔti fātìi gítìń kunimbɔtidiin
1Uninjee nìn cáá-mi ki cūnnì ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú. 2Niinee ní m ká Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu nyooti nyánní ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú ki dòoń. Tinyoolee nín nìn ŋáań kuwoou kuŋyee nìn náań nì tiŋku wookuee ní, ní ki nìn cáá tì-walifiŋu ki ŋmíntí kitiŋ. 3Dileedakal nee náań nì din m bàà ká ŋyunti ŋun ní Unimbɔti dɔ́miń kí nàan̄ Jeerusaleem nì ŋyunti ŋun m bí Keebaar buŋgbandee ní. Niinee ní m tātìi gbāaǹ m-yigbeel tūū kitiŋ. 4Ti-Dindaan nyootee nìn dīń ŋwìiń nyalaŋki punyɔkɔki ki kɔ́nní kunimbɔtidiin. 5Unimbɔti Fam yōoǹ-mi ní ki cáá-mi ki kɔ́ǹ poon cindin. M nìn ká yii ti-Dindaan nyooti nìn gbí kunimbɔtidii poon. 6Ní m gbìl̄ ubɔ sòon̄ní-mi doooo kunimbɔtidii poon. Ŋyunti gbantee uninja un céeǹ-mee nìn yú ki kɔ́ĺ-mi. 7Ti-Dindaan nìn bí-mi yii: «Nisaaleen, mpaan nee di sá laakin m-beejal bée, laakin m cáá m-taaŋi ki sīintée. M làá nīn kóò niin, Isirayeel yab kansikin kí nīn cá jaanjaan. Isirayeel yab nì bi-bɔtiibi kaa ti làá kpèè m-circir yindi fám. Baa làá ti ŋá ajɔkɔntuun ní kaa nín kɔ́ǹ bi-bɔtiibi doo kí síb́. 8Bibɔtiibi dū bi-bɔtinaakɔti punyɔmmu nì bi-naakɔti dɔi in pu bi sàkantí punuubee ki cóoǹ ki kɔ́ĺ m-Diiku punyɔmmu nì idɔ in pu m-Diiku punuubi sàkantée. Digundi dibaba di pée pītì man Diiku nì bi-diiŋŋi. Bi bíil̀ m-circir yindi, di sá yii bi ŋá ntimbiil tuuŋŋi. An pu ní m gíí bi-pu diŋuul ki nāaǹ-bi. 9Kɔŋkɔnnee, Isirayeel yab làá gbèen̄ kí taa ti nín̄ bí tijɔkɔndin. Bi làá yòon̄ bi-bɔtiibi bin kpíìyee wunti kí wàatī-mi, ní ḿ nīn kíǹ ki kóò bi-kansikin kí nīn cá jaanjaan.
10«Sii nisaaleen, tùkù Isirayeel yab kunimbɔtidii nee nín bí puee. Icoo ń cúú-bi bi-tuŋkpitiŋ pu, ní bí bīfì kí béé bi nín lēē kudii nee ku bí puee tiŋan. 11Atuun ŋin bi ŋée yaa lafun kɔ́ǹ-bi icooyee, á dū kunimbɔtidii nee footau kí dàkà-bi nì adiin nín bí puee nì mpunyɔmu nì bi nín bɔ́ntì-ku pu ki dāa máń-kuee. Á ŋmà marab nì akoobil ŋin bi máaǹ kí nīn ŋúb́ bi yaa bí mpaan nee puee kí dūú bíĺ bi-nimbiin. A yaa ŋá mimmee, bi làá nīn ŋúb́-bi kí nīn tɔ́-bi. 12Kunimbɔtidii nee bɔkpaal dipeekaal sɔ̀. Mpaan ŋun kɔkɔ māntìi tú-ku dijool yilpuee sá ki tīī Unimbɔti ní.»
Nsaraafan nì saraabi
13Bi nìn ŋmāntì nsaraafan. Ndɔ ŋun bi nìn dūu ŋmāntèe nìn jítì santimeetab imuŋku ili nì saalaa pu fiii. Mbòó ŋubɔ nìn māntìi tú nsaraafan ní ŋu-nyooŋŋu nìn sá ndɔŋmantikaayee diba pu ní ŋu-waaŋŋu mun sá diba pu. Boon púee, mbòóyee nìn jɔ́m̀ kii ndɔŋmantikaayee dijandi. Nsaraafan ŋu-ba fɔkɔŋŋu, 14taapu laakin síb́ kitiŋee kí cáá sāā laakin nyáńee, bi nìn máń dinyeel dipeekaal ki tɔ́kɔǹ. Laakin nìn síb́ gbantee nìn sá ndɔŋmantikaayee mili pu ní. Dinyeel gbanti jaŋŋi kamaayee, ndɔŋmantikaayee ŋubɔ di nìn pátì kí bà laakin síb́ee. Dinyeel dipeekaal gbanti yilpuee, bi nìn gíti máń dinyeel dililiitiil ki tɔ́kɔǹ. Díǹ fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá ndɔŋmantikaayee minaa pu ní. Dinyeel gbanti jaŋŋi kamaayee, ndɔŋmantikaayee ŋubɔ di nìn pátì kí bà dipeekaalee. 15Dinyeel dililiitiil gbanti yilpuee ní bi máń ŋfan yam. Ŋfanee fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá ndɔŋmantikaayee minaa pu ní ki nìn cáá iyin inaa. 16Ŋfanee jannaatiliŋ nìn ŋmà ní, ní dijandi diba nìn sá ndɔŋmantikaayee saalaa nì mili pu. 17Dinyeeliliitiilee mun jannaatiliŋ nìn ŋmà ní, ní dijandi diba fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá ndɔŋmantikaayee ŋubɔ kpá saalku pu. Digbándi boon púee fɔkɔŋŋu nìn sá ndɔŋmantikaayee dijandi. Nnyinsan ŋubɔ nìn māntìi tú nsaraafanee ní ŋu-waaŋŋu nìn sá ndɔŋmantikaayee diba pu. Akɔl nìn bí ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú ní bi dàb̀ kí bà yilpu.
18Uninjee nìn bí-mi yii: «Nisaaleen, ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Bi yaa láa máń nsaraafan kí nīn ŋáań bisaraawɔkaabi, kí nīn yàantí saraabi waŋkuti fatikuuee, akoobil ŋin bi làá dāá ŋée sɔ̀. 19Á dū unaja kí tīī Leefii yab bisaraaŋaliibi bin sá Sadooki maaliŋunee bí sútí kí pìl̄-mi kí tɔ̄ ditundi kí tīī-mi. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ. Bí dāá dū unajee kí ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau. 20Á dāá yòon̄ u-fatikuu kí dūú ŋmìtī nsaraafan yiŋyi naatil nì ŋu-nyeel gbiŋŋi anaatil nì ŋu-nyɔɔgbandi kí màntīí tū. A yaa ŋá mimmee, a ŋá nsaraafanee circir ki dū-ŋu ki sú-mi dee. 21Míǹ boonee, á yòon̄ unaja un bi dūu ŋá saraayee kí cáá wà ŋŋmi mpaan ŋun bi bɔ́ntì kí nīn ŋáań mimmee, circir kɔŋkooŋŋu kpaanceetiŋu. 22Kutaa yaa wúntèe, á yòon̄ uŋɔja un laaba kaa wɔ̀b̄ee kí dūú ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau kí ŋá nsaraafan circir, kii a nín bàà dū unaja ki ŋá puee. 23A yaa dóò saraa gbantee ní á yòon̄ unaja nì upìja in laaba kaa wɔ̀b̄ee 24kí cáań man a-Dindaan nimbiin. Bisaraaŋaliibi làá dū ŋyaam kí yàaǹ i-pu ní kí dū-bi kí ŋá saraawɔkaa kí tīī-mi. 25Iwiin iluli in làá páannée, á dū uŋɔja kí ŋá ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraau ŋwiin kamaa, ní kí dū unaja nì upìja in laaba kaa wɔ̀b̄ee kí ŋá míǹ mbaantiim. 26Iwiin iluli ní ni làá ŋá nsaraafan circir kí dū-ŋu kí sú-mi ní bí nín kíĺ ŋu-pu ditundi. 27Iwiin iluli gbanti yaa kúntèe, ŋwinniniiti dal nì iwiin in làá páannée, bisaraaŋaliibi ń ŋá ni-saraawɔkaabi nì mpèé saraabi bin ni cáańee nsaraafan pu. Niinee, m làá dàkà-ni kulaŋŋaŋfitiiu. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ.»

english_text:
The East Gate Must Remain Closed
1The man took me back to the outer courtyard, near the east gate of the temple area. I saw that the doors to this gate were closed. 2The Lord said:
I, the Lord God of Israel, came through this gate, so it must remain closed forever! No one must ever use it. 3The ruler of Israel may come here to eat a sacrificial meal that has been offered to me, but he must use only the entrance room of this gate.
People Who Are Not Allowed in the Temple
4Then the man took me through the north gate to the front of the temple. I saw that the brightness of the Lord's glory had filled the temple, and I immediately bowed with my face to the ground.
5The Lord said:
Ezekiel, son of man, I am going to give you the laws for my temple. So pay attention and listen carefully to what kind of people are allowed to come in the temple, and what kind are not. 6Tell those rebellious people of Israel:
I, the Lord God, command you to stop your evil ways! 7My temple has been disgraced, because you have let godless, stubborn foreigners come here when sacrifices are being offered to me. You have sinned and have broken our solemn agreement. 8Instead of following the proper ways to worship me, you have put foreigners in charge of worship at my temple.
9And so I, the Lord God, say that no godless foreigner who disobeys me will be allowed in my temple. This includes any foreigner living in Israel.
The Levites Are Punished
The Lord said:
10Some of the Levites turned their backs on me and joined the other people of Israel in worshiping idols. So these Levites must be punished! 11They will still be allowed to serve me as temple workers by guarding the gates and by killing the animals to be sacrificed and by helping the worshipers. 12But because these Levites served the people of Israel when they worshiped idols, I, the Lord God, promise that the Levites will be punished. They did not stop the Israelites from sinning, 13and now I will no longer let the Levites serve as my priests or come near anything sacred to me. They must suffer shame and disgrace for their disgusting sins. 14They will be responsible for all the hard work that must be done in the temple.
Rules for Priests
The Lord said:
15The priests of the Levi tribe who are descendants of Zadok the priest were faithful to me, even when the rest of the Israelites turned away. And so, these priests will continue to serve as my priests and to offer the fat and the blood of sacrifices. 16They will come into my temple, where they will offer sacrifices at my altar and lead others in worship.
17 When they come to the inner courtyard, they must wear their linen priestly clothes. My priests must never wear anything made of wool when they are on duty in this courtyard or in the temple. 18Even their turbans and underwear must be made of linen to keep my priests from sweating when they work. 19 And before they leave to join the other people in the outer courtyard, they must take off their priestly clothes, then place them in the sacred rooms and put on their regular clothes. That way, no one will touch their sacred clothes and be harmed.
20 Priests must never shave their heads when they are mourning. But they must keep their hair properly trimmed and not let it grow too long. 21 They must not drink wine before going to the inner courtyard.
22 A priest must not marry a divorced woman; he can marry only a virgin from Israel or the widow of another priest.
23 Priests must teach my people the difference between what is sacred and what is ordinary, and between what is clean and what is unclean. 24They will make decisions in difficult legal cases, according to my own laws. They must also observe the religious festivals my Law requires and must always respect the Sabbath.
25 Touching a dead body will make a person unclean. So a priest must not go near a dead body, unless it is one of his parents or children, or his brother or unmarried sister. 26If a priest touches a dead body, he is unclean and must go through a ceremony to make himself clean. Then seven days later, 27he must go to the inner courtyard of the temple and offer a sacrifice for sin. After that, he may once again serve as my priest. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
28 I myself will provide for my priests, and so they won't receive any land of their own. 29 Instead, they will receive part of the grain sacrifices, as well as part of the sacrifices for sin and sacrifices to make things right. They will also be given everything in Israel that has been completely dedicated to me. 30The first part of every harvest will belong to the priests. They will also receive part of all special gifts and offerings the Israelites bring to me. And whenever any of my people bake bread, they will give their first loaf as an offering to the priests, and I will bless the homes of the people when they do this.
31 Priests must not eat any bird or animal that dies a natural death or that has been killed by a wild animal.
translation_text:
Bi dū ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú punyɔkɔki ki tīī dibɔtibil
1Uninjee nìn cūnnì-mi kipunyɔkɔ kin bí boon ŋwìiń nyalaŋki púee. Kì nìn pīī. 2Ti-Dindaan nìn bí-mi yii: «Kipunyɔkɔ nee làá nīn pée pīī ní, baa máaǹ kí pìitī-kì. Ubɔ ń taa dī ki-poon kí jītí, di sá yii man ni-Dindaan Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu dī niin ní ki kɔ́nní. Ŋú nīn pée pīī. 3Ama dibɔtibil din kā dibeelee díǹ ŋūǹ kí kàl̄ niin kí jī circir jinti m-nimbiin. Ú dāá dī kipunyɔkɔee kí jītí kuditaakaau kun bí niinee kí kɔ́ ní kí fàtīí dī niin kí nyā.»
Binicambi kaa máaǹ kí kɔ́ kunimbɔtidiin
4Uninjee nìn dū-mi ki dī ŋgan pú punyɔkɔki ki cūtìi nyáń kunimbɔtidii nyɔkɔpu. M nìn ká yii ti-Dindaan nyooti nìn gbí kunimbɔtidii. Niinee ní m tātìi gbāaǹ m-nimbiin tūū kitiŋ. 5Ti-Dindaan nìn bí-mi yii: «Nisaaleen, ŋá ŋká. Kpítí a-nimbiliŋ kí ŋátí a-tafaliŋ. Á pīlifì marab nì akoobil ŋin m cáá kí tīī-si m-Diiku puee. Á cúú marab bin sòoǹ bi nín máaǹ kí kɔ́ circir laŋki pu kí fàtīí nyā puee tiŋan.
6«Á tùkù Isirayeel yab, pɔɔgaatib nee tin man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti bíi sòoǹee. Isirayeel yab, m gīī nì ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin ni ŋáańee. 7Ŋyunti ŋun ni cáá m-jandi, ni-saraabi kpam nì bi-fatikuu ki tìì-mee, ni cáá binicambi bin kaa gíí dikpancandi kaa tɔ́-mee ki kɔ̄ntí circir laŋki. Ni ŋáań míǹ ní ki kɔ̄ntí m-Diiku tijɔkɔndi. Ni ŋá ntimbiil tuuŋŋi gbanti ki kpītì mpèé ŋun bí man nì nimbi kansikinee. 8Nimbi ni-ba kaa túń m-tundi m-circir paaŋŋu pu, ama ní ki yāntì binicambi fōō ni-paaŋŋu ki túń. 9Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ yii báà unicaan yaa kóò Isirayeel yab kansikin, ní kaa gíí dikpancandi kaa tɔ́-mee, ú taa kɔ́ m-circir kɔŋkooŋŋun.»
Marab bin sá ki tīī Leefii yabee
10«Ŋyunti ŋun Isirayeel gáatì ki cūtìi nóó awaayee, Leefii yab nìn fātì bi-boon ki tīī-mi ní ki dū-mi ki fá. An puee, m làá dáaĺ bi-tafal bi-kpitii pu. 11Bi làá nīn gbíntìi bí m-tundin circir kɔŋkooŋŋun kí nīn cīití m-Diiku punyɔmmu ki tūǹ atuun nín pée bí pu a-ba a-ba m-Diikunee. Bi ŋūǹ kí làntì tiwaŋkuti tin bi làá dūú ŋá bisaraawɔkaabee nì saraabi bin kíǹee. Bi làá nīn tūǹ ditundi ki tìì m-nibul. 12Ŋyunti ŋun m-nibul nìn bí ki tòotī awaayee, bi nìn túń ditundi ki tīī-bi ní ki yāntì Isirayeel yab kɔ́ ikpitin. An puee man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. M làá jáǹ-bi ní bi-kpitii tafadaaldi ń gítí bi-pu. 13Baa làá ti ŋmā kí sútí kí pìl̄-mi kí tɔ̄ disaraaŋal tundi, kaa làá ti sútí kí pìl̄ tiwan tin bi dūu sú-mee. Baa máaǹ kí sútí kí pìl̄ circir páaa laŋki. Min ní bi làá túń icoo tuuŋŋi nì ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ŋin bi ŋée tafadaaldee dee. 14M làá dū kunimbɔtidii poon tundi kí ŋá bi-ŋaan ní bí nīn tūǹ atuun ŋin kɔkɔ bí ku-poon bí tɔ̄ee.»
Marab bin sá ki tīī bisaraaŋaliibee
15Ŋyunti ŋun Isirayeel yab nìn fātì bi-boon ki tīī man ni-Dindaanee, Leefii yab bisaraaŋaliibi bin sá Saadooki maaliŋunee nìn túń ditundi m-circir paaŋŋu pu an nín máaǹ puee. Bíǹ baba di ŋūǹ kí yūĺ m-nimbiin kí tɔ̄ m-tundi kí dū tiwaŋkuti tin bi dūu ŋá saraabee kpam nì ti-fatikuu kí ŋá-mi saraa. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ. 16Bíǹ baba di làá kɔ́ m-circir kɔŋkooŋŋun ní kí sútí kí pìl̄ m-teebiliu un pu bi tūǹ m-tundee. Bi làá nīn ŋúb́ m-tundi koobiliŋ. 17Kí wàatī bí kɔ́ kunimbɔtidii poon cindinee, bi máaǹ kí dū bi-wampeeŋkaati tin bi dū iŋaabu in bí fálfal ki jàkēe kí pèen̄. Bí taa dū ipii kuti wampeeŋkaati kí pèen̄ ŋyunti ŋun bi bí kunimbɔtidiin nì ku-cindi poon ki tūǹ ditundee. 18Bí dū ŋŋaabu ŋun bí fálfalee kí yíĺ ní kí dū fálfal ŋaabuŋu kí cúú kicaŋ. Kutuntuŋu puee, bí taa cúú dambala. 19Kí wàatī bí nyā kí kɔ́ boon pú cindin, laakin samaa bée, bí pèetī tiwan tin bi pēeǹ ki túń ditundee. Bí dū tiwampeeŋkaal gbanti kí síiń adiin ŋin bí circir laŋkee, ní kí kpántí tiwan, kí taa nín pēē tiwan tin bí circiree kí gbēē samaa.
20«Bisaraaŋaliibi kaa máaǹ kí kòol̀ diyibaakpandi, kaa tí máaǹ kí yàntī bi-yikpiti ń wíiǹ tikpil, ama bí cā bi-yikpiti tiŋan. 21Usaraaŋal ubɔ kaa máaǹ kí nyɔ̀ ndaam kí kɔ́ poon cindin. 22Usaraaŋal kaa máaǹ kí cáab́ ukpiipu àá unimpu un bi jìn̄ee. Ú cáab́ Isirayeel sapɔmbiki kin kaa nyí uninja ki kée kiba àá usaraaŋal ubɔ kpiipuu.
23«Bisaraaŋaliibi máaǹ kí dàkà m-nibul bí béé kí gàntī tin bí circiree nì tin kaa bí circiree, tin sá tijɔkɔndee nì tin kaa sá tijɔkɔndee. 24Bíǹ di làá nīn sòoǹ binib bɔti ní kí sòoǹ kí nóó nì m-marab. Bí nīn jīǹ jiŋaalib kí nóó nì akoobil nì abɔkpaa ŋin m tīī-bee. Bi máaǹ kí dū m-wiŋŋuŋfikaai kí sú-mi.
25«Usaraaŋal kaa máaǹ kí sútí kí pìl̄ dinikpil kí kɔ́ǹ u-ba tijɔkɔndi. Ama an yaa sá u-baa àá u-na àá u-biyaamu kansikin kiba àá u-naal àá u-maan àá u-niisal un kaa láá mɔ́ǹee, u ŋūǹ kí sútí kí pìl̄. 26Míǹ boonee, ú ŋá u-ba circir ní kí cīití iwiin iluli ní kí nín kíĺ ditundi. 27Ŋwiin ŋun u yaa fātìi gítì kunimbɔtidii poon cindinee, ú ŋá u-kpitii pɔ̄tam saraau. Man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sòon̄ míǹ. 28Bisaraaŋaliibi làá nīn cáá diyimɔɔl kí nīn bí m-tundin. Bí taa tīī-bi tikpaatan Isirayeel tiŋkin. Man di sá bi-fakal. 29Bi làá nīn jīǹ saraabi nì tiwaŋkuti tin bi cáa ŋáań ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraabee. Isirayeel tiŋkin tin kɔkɔ bi dūu sú-mee kpántì bi-wanti ní. 30Bisaraaŋaliibi di tí yì tijincɔ̀fikaal kɔkɔ nì tin kɔkɔ Isirayeel yab lèekī bi-gaajawanti pu ki tìì-mee. Binib yaa púĺ kpɔnɔee, bí lēē un ŋān̄ ki jítiǹ bi-kɔkɔee kí tīī-bi ní ḿ bìin̄ bi-dicaŋŋi pu. 31Ama bisaraaŋaliibi kaa máaǹ kí ŋmɔ́ unoon àá kuwaŋkuluu kun kpíì àá upeel ubɔ cúúyee nanti.»

english_text:
The Lord's Sacred Land
The Lord said:
1When the land of Israel is divided among the twelve tribes, you must set aside an area that will belong to me. This sacred area will be 12.5 kilometers long and 10 kilometers wide. 2The temple will be on a piece of land 255 meters square, and the temple will be completely surrounded by an open space 25 meters wide.
3-4I will give half of my sacred land, a section 12.5 kilometers long and 5 kilometers wide, to the priests who serve in the temple. Their houses will be in this half, as well as my temple, which is the most sacred place of all.
5I will give the other half of my land to the Levites who work in my temple, and the towns where they will live will be there.
6Next to my sacred land will be an area 12.5 kilometers long and 3 kilometers wide. This will belong to the people of Israel and will include the city of Jerusalem.
Land for Israel's Ruler
The Lord said:
7-8The regions west and east of my sacred land and the city of Jerusalem will belong to the ruler of Israel. He will be given the region between the western edge of my land and the Mediterranean Sea, and between the eastern edge of my land and the Jordan River. This will mean that the length of his property will be the same as the sections of land given to the tribes.
This property will belong to every ruler of Israel, so they will always be fair to my people and will let them live peacefully in the land given to their tribes.
Israel's Rulers Must Be Honest
9The Lord God said:
You leaders of Israel have cheated and abused my people long enough! I want you to stop sinning and start doing what is right and fair. You must never again force my people off their own land. I, the Lord, have spoken.
10 So from now on, you must use honest weights and measures. 11The ephah will be the standard dry measure, and the bath will be the standard liquid measure. Their size will be based on the homer, which will equal ten ephahs or ten baths.
12The standard unit of weight will be the shekel. One shekel will equal 20 gerahs, and 60 shekels will equal one mina.
