m làá dāá nīn sá Unimbɔti un fòol̄ ŋwimmeemee.
M làá dāá tīī kutagbɔŋu kun ku nyàab̀ m-ceeyee,
ní kutagbɔŋu mun ń dāá tīī kitiŋ
ntaanyim min kì nyàab̀ ku-ceeyee.
24Ní kitiŋ ń yàntī bilee nì fiinyi nì fiigi
ń lòoǹ tiŋan
Jisirayeel tantakalin.
25Man làá dāá yàaǹ iwambool kitiŋ nee pu.
M làá dāá nīn néeń 'Baa là-mi'
ní kí dāá tùkù 'Naa sá m-nibul' yii:
<A sá m-nibul>,
ní úǹ ń dāá kíí-mi yii: <M-Nimbɔtiu.>»

english_text:
God's Love Offers Hope
1Once again the Lord spoke to me. And this time he said, “Hosea, fall in love with an unfaithful woman who has a lover. Do this to show that I love the people of Israel, even though they worship idols and enjoy the offering cakes made with fruit.”
2So I paid 15 pieces of silver and about 150 kilograms of grain for such a woman. 3Then I said, “Now you are mine! You will have to remain faithful to me, though it will be a long time before we sleep together.”
4It will also be a long time before Israel has a king or before sacrifices are offered at the temple or before there is any way to get guidance from God. 5But later, Israel will turn back to the Lord their God and to David their king. At that time they will come to the Lord with fear and trembling, and he will be good to them.
translation_text:
Dimɔɔkil daaku
1Ní ti-Dindaan tùkū-mi yii: «Nín̄ gbíntìi néeń unimpu un nyáń a-boon ki cáá bɔɔnee. Nín̄ néeń-u kii man ni-Dindaan nín néeń Isirayeel yab puee, nì min kɔkɔ bi dū bi-ba ki tīī awaa ki néeń fiinyi biliŋ kalaabee.» 2Niinee ní m pàn̄ tikúti nimbiliŋ jitɔmbi saalku nì ɔɔji liitirib alaataa aluu ki fātìi fōō m-nimpuu. 3Ní m tùkū-u yii: «Á kàl̄ m-cee doo kí yúntí, kí taa ti ŋá tilaakpaal, ní kaa nín dōoǹ nì uninja ubɔ. Ma mun làá ŋá míǹ mbaantiim kí tīī-si.»
4Di sá yii Isirayeel yab làá dāá kàl̄ kí yúntí, kaa cáá ubɔtaaa, kaa cáá ukpootilaaa, kaa ti ŋáań saraayaaa, kaa ti cáá ditaŋkpacooŋkaal àá tiwambalifikaal tin bi cáa bàlifī kí béé Unimbɔti lammee mun.
5Míǹ boonee, Isirayeel yab làá dāá fàtīí gítiń. Bi làá dāá nyàab̀ ti-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu nì Daafiidi naantiiu un sá bi-bɔtiuee. Bi làá dāá fàtīí gítiń nì kufaaŋŋu ti-Dindaan cee kí nyàab̀ u-ŋanti.

english_text:
Israel Is Unfaithful
1Israel, listen
as the Lord accuses
everyone in the land!
No one is faithful or loyal
or truly cares about God.
2Cursing, dishonesty, murder,
robbery, unfaithfulness—
these happen all the time.
Violence is everywhere.
3And so your land is a desert.
Every living creature is dying—
people and wild animals,
birds and fish.
The Lord Warns the Priests
4Don't accuse just anyone!
Not everyone is at fault.
My case is against you,
the priests.
5You and the prophets
will stumble day and night;
I'll silence your mothers.
6You priests have rejected me,
and my people are destroyed
by refusing to obey.
Now I'll reject you and forget
your children, because you
have forgotten my Law.
7By adding more of you priests,
you multiply the number
of people who sin.
Now I'll change your pride
into shame.
8You encourage others to sin,
so you can stuff yourselves
on their sin offerings.
9That's why I will punish
the people for their deeds,
just as I will punish
you priests.
10Their food won't satisfy,
and having sex at pagan shrines
won't produce children.
My people have rebelled
11and have been unfaithful
to me, their Lord.
God Condemns Israel's Idolatry
My people, you are foolish
because of too much pleasure
and too much wine.
12You expect wooden idols
and other objects of wood
to give you advice.
Lusting for sex at pagan shrines
has made you unfaithful
to me, your God.
13You offer sacrifices
on mountaintops and hills,
under oak trees, and wherever
good shade is found.
Your own daughters
and daughters-in-law
sell themselves for sex.
14But I won't punish them.
You men are to blame,
because you go to prostitutes
and offer sacrifices with them
at pagan shrines.
Your own foolishness
will lead to your ruin.
15Israel, you are unfaithful,
but don't lead Judah to sin.
Stop worshiping at Gilgal
or at sinful Bethel.
And quit making promises
in my name—the name
of the living Lord.
16You are nothing more
than a stubborn cow—
so stubborn that I, the Lord,
cannot feed you like lambs
in an open pasture.
17You people of Israel
are charmed by idols.
Leave those people alone!
18You get drunk, then sleep
with prostitutes;
you would rather be vulgar
than lead a decent life.
19And so you will be swept away
in a whirlwind
for sacrificing to idols.
translation_text:
Unimbɔti làá sòoǹ u-nibul bɔti
1Isirayeel yab, pīlifìmaan ti-Dindaan bɔti,
di sá yii ti-Dindaan bíi sòoǹ bin kóò kitiŋ nee puee bɔti.
Kitiŋ nee puee, mbaamɔn gíti kpáaa, dineendi gíti kpáaa,
bin nyí Unimbɔtee gíti kpá.
2Bi tòó tɔb mbusu,
ki mɔ́ntí inyimɔn, ki kù binib,
ki yù bunaayubu, ki ŋáań tilaakpaal,
ki ŋáań tipɔmbɔti,
ní ki cáá nnikpaakoon.
3An pu ní kitiŋ nee kɔkɔ làá kpā,
ní bin kɔkɔ kóò ki-puee ń yɔ̀l̄,
kí kpáaǹ ipeel nì inoon.
Áli gba tiŋkun jɔmii làá céetí.
Bisaraaŋaliibi kpitii
4Ama ubɔ ń taa kɔ̄kɔl̀ ubɔ,
ubɔ ń taa wòoǹ u-juti.
An sá man nì nimbi bisaraaŋaliibi
di cáá tɔb tibɔti.
5Ni làá dāá gbéetí kuwiŋkaŋu pu,
bibɔnaatiliibi mun làá gbéetí
kunyeeu kii nimbee,
ní ḿ kpɔ̀ ni-na Isirayeel.
6M-nibul kúù
kun puee di lóò dinyil.
Kii ni nín fātì ni-boon ki tīī dinyilee puee,
ma mun làá fàtī m-boon kí tīī-ni
ní naa ti làá nīn sá m-saraaŋaliibi.
Ni súntì mama, ni-Nimbɔtiu marau puɔɔ!
Ma mun làá súntí ni-jipɔmbi pu.
7Kii bisaraaŋaliibi nín būtì tikpil tikpil puee,
míǹ ní bi yīntiǹ-mi mun.
M làá yàntī tin nìn tìì-bi tinyoolee
ń kpántí-bi ticoobɔti
8M-nibul nín ŋáań ikpiti pɔ̄tam
saraabi biŋyee di kpīintí-bi.
An pu ní bi tìì m-nibul kunyannyaau
bí nīn mɔ̀tīi ŋáań ikpiti.
9Tin dɔ̄ ki cí bisaraaŋaliibee
di dɔ̄ ki cí samaa un kíǹee.
M làá dáaĺ bi-tafal bi-bimbikpitim pu,
ní kí pà-bi bi-tuŋkpitiŋ paati.
10Bi làá jī kí gíti jī,
ama ŋkùm làá nīn pée gbíntìi cáá-bi ní.
Bi làá ŋá alaakpaatuun kí gíti ŋá,
ama bi kpá kí ká mbiyaamu.
Di sá yii bi dū man bi-Dindaan ki fá
ki dū bi-ba ki líì nì alaakpaatuun.
11Alaakpaatuun nì ndanyoon
gábitì m-nibul yil.
12M-nibul bàlifī awaa ŋin sá idɔee ní
bi-yil pu bɔti,
ní mbɔɔkpandɔ tùkù-bi tin bi là kí bééyee.
Di sá yii alaakpaatuun fam gáatì-bi.
Bi dū bi-ba ki líì nì awaa,
ki dū man bi-Nimbɔtiu ki fá.
13Ajoon yilpu kúntí kunti
ní bi ŋáań bi-saraabi.
Ŋgbantamu pu ní bi tùutī
talaalub ki ŋáań saraa.
Iwaasufi in bi yíì yii seeni nì peepiliiyee
nì teereebintee taapu ní bi kàal̀,
di sá yii i-booŋyi sɔ̀m̀.
An pu ní ni-bisalib ŋáań alaakpaatuun
ní ni-coopoobi nyēē bi-calib boon.
14Ama maa làá dáaĺ ni-bisalib tafal
bi-laakpaatuuŋŋi pu,
kaa làá dáaĺ ni-coopoobi tafal
bi nín nyáń bi-calib boonee pu.
Nimbi bisaraaŋaliibi tafal ní m làá dáaĺ,
kun puee nimbi di nyāntí nnimpulaakpaamu
ŋkpaanceeti ki dɔ̀ nì mu,
ní ni nì nlaakpaamu mun bí awaadiinnee
kpáfí ki jīǹ saraabi jinti.
Kii dilaŋkpandi diba nín lī puee yii:
<Dinibul din kaa cáá iciinee
sá dinibul din wáŋkèe ní.>
15Báà nimbi Isirayeel beel yab
yaa nyáń m-boonaaa,
Juuda beel yab ń taa ŋá míǹ mbaantiim.
Ní taa cùmaan Giilgaal circir paaŋŋu pu,
kí taa cù Beeti Aween,
kí taa tí pùtī kí lì yii:
«Nì Unimbɔti un bí nee pu!»
16Kii unapɔɔl nín bí puee, míǹ ní Isirayeel beel yab tafaliŋ pɔ̄ɔ̄. Mimmee, kɔŋkɔnnee ní ti-Dindaan làá nín ŋá u-nibul kii apibil ŋin bi cáǹ kupikpaaueeee? 17Eefiraayiim yab nì awaa ŋá mpèé. Yàntī-bi. 18Bi yaa nyùn̄ ki gbée ní bí kɔ́ alaakpaatuun poon. Bi-kpootiliibi néeń tin kɔ̄ntí-bi icooyee ní. 19Kubuŋu làá dāá yòon̄-bi kí páań ku-feeŋyi pu, ní icoo ń dāá cúú-bi saraabi bin bi ŋáańee pu.

english_text:
Israel and Judah Will Be Judged
The Lord said:
1Listen, you priests!
Pay attention, Israel!
Listen, you members
of the royal family.
Justice was your duty.
But at Mizpah and Mount Tabor
you trapped the people.
2At the place of worship
you were a treacherous pit,
and I will punish you.
3Israel, I know all about you,
and because of your unfaithfulness,
I find you unacceptable.
4Your evil deeds are the reason
you won't return to me,
your Lord God.
And your constant craving for sex
keeps you from knowing me.
5Israel, your pride
testifies to your guilt;
it makes you stumble,
and Judah stumbles too.
6You offer sheep and cattle
as sacrifices to me,
but I have turned away
and refuse to be found.
7You have been unfaithful
to me, your Lord;
you have had children
by prostitutes.
So at the New Moon Festival,
you and your crops
will be destroyed.
The Lord Warns Israel and Judah
8Give a warning on the trumpet!
Let it be heard in Gibeah,
Ramah, and sinful Bethel.
Benjamin, watch out!
9I, the Lord, will punish
and wipe out Israel.
This is my solemn promise
to every tribe of Israel.
10Judah's leaders are like crooks
who move boundary markers;
that's why I will flood them
with my anger.
11Israel was brutally crushed.
They got what they deserved
for worshiping useless idols.
12Now I, the Lord,
will fill Israel with maggots
and make Judah rot.
13When Israel and Judah saw
their sickness and wounds,
Israel asked help from Assyria
and its mighty king.
But the king cannot cure them
or heal their wounds.
14So I'll become a fierce lion
attacking Israel and Judah.
I'll snatch and carry off
what I want,
and no one can stop me.
15Then I'll return to my temple
until they confess their guilt
and worship me,
until they are desperate
and beg for my help.
translation_text:
Bikpootiliibi bin ŋáań ikpitee
1«Bisaraaŋaliibi, pīlifìmaan tin bí nee,
Isirayeel beel yab kpootiliibi, ní pīlifìmaan.
Ubɔti dicaŋkun yab,
kpòom̄maan ni-tafal kí pīlifì.
An bàà sá nimbi nín sòoǹ
binib bɔti nì mbaamɔn.
Ama ní ni kpántì kutaliŋŋu
ki tīī m-nibul Miisipa tiŋkin,
ní ki kpántì kulaaŋŋu
kun bi píĺ Tabɔɔr jool puee.
2Bi gbìn̄ kubookpaaŋŋu Siitiim tantakalin.
M bíi bɔ́ntí bi-kɔkɔ tafadaaldi.
3«Mamee, m nyí Eefiraayiim naakookun yab tiŋan,
Isirayeel beel yab mun kaa lìkī m-nimbiin.
Eefiraayiim yab kɔ́ alaakpaatuun poon,
ní ki yāntì Isirayeel beel yab kɔkɔ kɔ́ tijɔkɔndin.»
4Isirayeel beel yab tuŋkpitiŋ kaa pūǹ-bi nsan
bí ŋmā kí fàtīí gítí bi-Nimbɔtiu cee.
Di sá yii alaakpaatuun fam miba bí bi-ni,
ní baa nyí ti-Dindaan.
5Isirayeel beel yab lambil di lèekī bi-pu mmɔ́ɔn.
Isirayeel beel yab nì Eefiraayiim naakookun yab
kpitii pu ní bi gbéetì ki lítì.
Bi nì Juuda beelin yab mun kpáfì ki gbéetì.
6Bi làá dāá cáań bi-piii nì bi-naai
kí ŋá saraa kí nyàab̀ ti-Dindaan,
ama baa làá dāá ká-u.
Di sá yii u dū-bi ki fá.
7Bi nyáń ti-Dindaan boon ki màl̄
mbiyaamu mun kaa sá u-yɔmuee.
Too, an kaa ti làá bà uŋmal,
án làá nàan̄ bi nì bi-tiŋki.
Juuda beel yab nì Isirayeel beel yab jaaku
8Búḿmaan ŋyin Giibeeya jool pu,
búḿmaan dikantándi Raama tiŋkin!
Kpāafìmaan Beeti-Aween yab!
Beenjameen naakookun yab, bi bíi jáà nì ni ni-boon pú.
9Ŋwiin ŋun m làá dāá dáaĺ Eefiraayiim naakooku tafalee,
kì làá dāá kpántí kuteeu ní.
Tin m bíi sòoǹ Isirayeel naakɔti pu nee
sá tibɔŋman ní.
10Juuda beel kpootiliibi náań nì bin cóotí
bi-sati kpaanyɔmmu taŋkpeeŋi ki nìkèe ní.
An pu ní m làá kpáatí m-ŋuul kii
nnyimee kí sìtī bi-pu.
11«Bi sāaǹ Eefiraayiim yab,
ibɔsoon nàn̄-bi,
di sá yii bi sáń ki pá
tin kaa bí tibanee boon.
12Too, m làá dāá kpántí kii dinalee ní
Eefiraayiim yab cee,
ní kí kpántí kii taagbunjaanjaanee
Juuda beel yab cee.
13Ŋyunti ŋun Eefiraayiim yab ká yii bi būǹ
ní Juuda beel yab ká bi-bunsooŋyee,
ní Eefiraayiim yab nín cá Asuur tiŋkin
ní ki tú binib bí cùú ká ubɔtikpaan.
Ama u mun kaa ŋūǹ kí cáaǹ-naaa,
kaa tí cáá ni-bunsooŋyi nyɔkɔŋu.
14Di sá yii m làá nīn sá kii gbikintee ní
Eefiraayiim yab cee,
ní kí nīn sá kii digbikintipɔmbilee
Juuda beel yab cee.
Mama m-ba di làá tɔ̀ntī-ni,
ní kí kpáaǹ-ni kí búntí,
ní ubɔ mun dāa kpá kí fīī-ni m-ŋaan.»
Unimbɔti fātì u-boon ki tīī u-nibul
15«M làá búntí, m làá nīn gítí m-dumpu
kí dāá sāā ŋyunti ŋun bi làá béé
bi-bɔkpil kí nyàab̀-mee.
Bi-nimbinaamandi poonee,
bi làá dāá nyàab̀-mi.»

english_text:
The Lord's People Speak
1Let's return to the Lord.
He has torn us to shreds,
but he will bandage our wounds
and make us well.
2In two or three days
he will heal us
and restore our strength
that we may live with him.
3Let's do our best
to know the Lord.
His coming is as certain
as the morning sun;
he will refresh us like rain
renewing the earth
in the springtime.
The Lord Speaks to Israel and Judah
4People of Israel and Judah,
what can I do with you?
Your love for me disappears
more quickly than mist
or dew at sunrise.
5That's why I slaughtered you
with the words
of my prophets.
That's why my judgments blazed
like the dawning sun.
6 I'd rather for you to be faithful
and to know me
than to offer sacrifices.
7At a place named Adam,
you betrayed me
by breaking our agreement.
8Everyone in Gilead is evil;
your hands are stained
with the blood of victims.
9You priests are like a gang
of robbers in ambush.
On the road to Shechem
you murder and commit
other horrible crimes.
10I have seen a terrible thing
in Israel—
you are unfaithful
and unfit to worship me.
11People of Judah,
your time is coming too.
The Lord Wants To Help Israel
I, the Lord, would like to make
my nation prosper again

english_text:
1and to heal its wounds.
But then I see the crimes
in Israel and Samaria.
Everyone is deceitful;
robbers roam the streets.
2No one realizes
that I have seen their sins
surround them like a flood.
3The king and his officials
take great pleasure
in their sin and deceit.
4Everyone burns with desire—
they are like coals in an oven,
ready to burst into flames.
5On the day their king
was crowned,
his officials got him drunk,
and he joined
in their foolishness.
6Their anger is a fire
that smolders all night,
then flares up at dawn.
7They are flames
destroying their leaders.
And their kings are powerless;
none of them trust me.
8The people of Israel
have mixed with foreigners;
they are a thin piece of bread
scorched on one side.
9They don't seem to realize
how weak and feeble they are;
their hair has turned gray,
while foreigners rule.
10I am the Lord, their God,
but in all of their troubles
their pride keeps them
from returning to me.
No Help from Foreign Nations
The Lord said:
11Israel is a senseless bird,
fluttering back and forth
between Egypt and Assyria.
12But I will catch them in a net
as hunters trap birds;
I threatened to punish them,
and indeed I will.
13Trouble and destruction
will be their reward
for rejecting me.
I would have rescued them,
but they told me lies.
14They don't really pray to me;
they just howl in their beds.
They have rejected me for Baal
and slashed themselves,
in the hope that Baal
will bless their crops.
15I taught them what they know,
and I made them strong.
Now they plot against me
16and refuse to obey.
They are more useless
than a crooked arrow.
Their leaders will die in war
for saying foolish things.
Egyptians will laugh at them.
translation_text:
1m yaa baa là kí cáaǹ Isirayeelee,
ní Eefiraayiim yab kpitii
nì Samaarii yab tuŋkpitiŋ
ń nyā kí páań mpaampiin pu.
Di sá yii bi kíiĺ tɔb,
ní binaayub kóò adiinni ki yù,
ní digaŋgam daan bí adan pu ki bìlim̄.
2Ama an kaa sòoǹ nì bi-pɔbiliŋin yii
m téetí bi-kpitii in bi ŋáańee kɔkɔ pu.
Kɔŋkɔnnee bi-kpitii gbanti di māntìi tú-bee.
I dɔ̄ m-nimbiin ní baabadal.
3Bi cáá bi-tuŋkpitiŋ
ki kɔ̀ntī ubɔti nimbiliŋ,
ní ki cáá bi-nyimɔŋyi
ki kɔ̀ntī bikàliŋkpilib yaŋ.
4Bi-kɔkɔ sá bilaakpaadambi ní.
Bi náań nì dikpɔnɔbubul din píĺ kpaŋkpam
ní ukpɔnɔŋal kaa ti bíi pàá án nyàtī
kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋun ní bukpɔnɔsaa
làá jɔ̄m̀ee ní.
5Ubɔti maaliwiiŋŋu jiŋaaliu dalee,
abɔtibil nyù ndaam áli kí tin būŋkì.
Ubɔti tàntī u-ŋal ki tìì bin bèel̄-uee kuboou.
6Di sá yii bi sútìń ki pìlìń-u
ki tùm̀ kpaŋkpam kii kipaai ŋmiŋuee.
Biibii di gbí bi-pɔbiliŋin.
Kunyeeu kɔkɔee, bi-ŋuul dɔ̄ ki gèeǹ,
ama kutaa yaa wúntèe,
dì fòol̄ bìlbil kii ŋŋmikpaanee ní.
7Bi-kɔkɔ píĺ ní kpaŋkpam kii dikpɔnɔbubulee,
bi kù ki céetí bi-kpootiliibi.
Bi kpákatì bi-bɔtiibi kɔkɔ,
ama bi-kansikin báà ubɔ
mun kaa kúuǹ ki yíiń-mi.
8«Eefiraayiim dū u-ba ki ŋmālim̀
anibul ŋin kíǹee poon.
U náań nì kalaa
un bi tɔ́ kaa lábitèe ní.
9Binicambi fóofì u-pɔŋŋu,
ní waa kpáàa nyí gba.
Tiyikpipin nyáń u-yil pu
ní waa kpáàa béè.
10Isirayeel beel yab badakal
di lèekī bi-pu mmɔ́ɔn.
Isirayeel beel yab kaa fātìi gítìń
man bi-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu cee.
Min kamaa tin bí nee kɔkɔ jítèe,
baa nyàab̄-mi.
11Eefiraayiim sá kii dibeenanjil
din kaa nyí tiba kaa dàkafēe ní.
U yíì Eejipiti tiŋki ń dāá jòoń-u,
ní ki sáń ki cá Asuur tiŋkin.
12Ama ŋyunti ŋun u tú ki lábití mimmee,
ní ḿ dū m-laaŋku kí tɔ̄-u,
ní kí cúuń-u kii bi nín cútí inoon puee.
M làá dáaĺ u-tafal
kii m nín sòon̄ pu bi-kpafil poonee.
13Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí-bi, di sá yii bi sáǹ-mi!
Án làá nàan̄-bi, di sá yii bi yíkìi bíi jáà nì mi!
M bàà nyàab̄ kí fīī-bi dee,
ama ní bi bí ki sòoǹ m-pu tinyimɔmbɔti!
14Baa kūuntí ki yíì-mi mbaamɔm,
ama ní bi dɔ̄ bi-dooŋu pu ki yáliŋkí.
Bi cáá njimu ki gífí bi-ba
kí ŋmā kí ká tijin nì ndaam.
Baa nyí yii bi yaa bíi ŋáań mimmee,
bi bíi jáà nì man dee.
15Man di kpōotì-bi ki tīī-bi mpɔn,
ama nì míǹ kɔkɔee,
bi dàkafī m-pu ilandɔkɔkpiti ŋma ní.
16Bi yaa gítìńaaa, an kaa sá man cee ní bi gítìń.
Bi náań nì butɔbu bun gíì ki gbàkēe ní.
Ama bi-kpilib nín sòoǹ ki bíiĺ-mi puee,
kujaaun ní bi làá kpú,
ní binib ń nīn bèel̄-bi Eejipiti tiŋkin.»

english_text:
Israel Rejects the Lord
The Lord said:
1Sound a warning!
Israel, you broke our agreement
and ignored my teaching.
Now an eagle is swooping down
to attack my land.
2Israel, you say, “We claim you,
the Lord, as our God.”
3But your enemies
will chase you for rejecting
our good agreement.
4You chose kings and leaders
without consulting me;
you made silver and gold idols
that led to your downfall.
5City of Samaria, I'm angry
because of your idol
in the shape of a calf.
When will you ever
be innocent again?
6Someone from Israel built
that idol for you,
but only I am God.
And so it will be smashed
to pieces.
7If you scatter wind
instead of wheat,
you will harvest a whirlwind
and have no wheat.
Even if you harvest grain,
enemies will steal it all.
8Israel, you are ruined,
and now the nations
consider you worthless.
9You are like a wild donkey
that goes its own way.
You've run off to Assyria
and hired them as allies.
10You can bargain with nations,
but I'll catch you anyway.
Soon you will suffer abuse
by kings and rulers.
11Israel, you have built
many altars where you offer
sacrifices for sin.
But these altars have become
places for sin.
12My instructions for sacrifices
were written in detail,
but you ignored them.
13You sacrifice your best animals
and eat the sacrificial meals,
but I, the Lord,
refuse your offerings.
I will remember your sins
and punish you.
Then you will return to Egypt.
14Israel, I created you,
but you forgot me.
You and Judah built palaces
and many strong cities.
Now I will send fire to destroy
your towns and fortresses.
translation_text:
A yaa búĺ kubuŋuee, a dāa cēē kubuŋkpaaŋŋu ní
1Búḿmaan ŋyin kí kpāafì binib!
Kii ukaabu nín tòó puee,
míǹ ní mbusu làá jēetí ti-Dindaan tiŋki pu.
Di sá yii Isirayeel beel yab kaa tɔ́ m-poondi
ní kaa yúl̀ deedee m-marab poon.
2Bi kūuntí fám ki lì yii:
<Ti-Nimbɔtiu, timbi Isirayeel yab, ti nyí-si!>
3Isirayeel beel yab dū tin ŋān̄ee ki fá.
An pu ní unannanli bíi jì-bi.
4Bi kāaǹ bi-bɔtiibi kaa bālifì m-pu.
Bi lēē bi-kpilib kaa tùkū-mi.
Bi dū bi-nimbiliŋ nì bi-sindaariyab
ki mɔ́ɔ́ awaa ŋin làá nàan̄-bee.
5Samaarii yab,
maa là m-nimbil ń ká ni-nabil.
Ni yāntì m gíí ni-pu diŋuul.
Kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu ní
m làá ká yii naa ti bí ikpitin?
6Ni-nabil gbantee nyánní Isirayeel beelin ní.
Unil di máń-dì,
dàa sá Unimbɔti.
Tiŋman, Samaarii nabil gbanti
làá nà ní dúsi dusi.
7Kii ni nín búĺ kubuŋuee,
kubuŋkpaaŋŋu ní ni làá cā.
<Didikakal yaa kaa cáá ŋfinee,
ŋyim mun kpá dee.>
Báà di yaa lòon̄aaa,
binicambi di dāa yì kí jī.
8«Bi dū Isirayeel beel ki náĺ.
Dì kíǹ ki bí atimbun kansikin
kii kuyukpuŋuee ní.
9Di sá yii bi yíkìi cūtì Asuur tiŋkin,
bi bí kii kumooun maŋki kin tú ki yìiǹ ki-babee ní.
Eefiraayiim yab dá bibɔntiibi.
10Báà bi yaa yākatì tiwan ki pú
atimbun ŋin kíǹee,
ŋyunti bāań ḿ kóoǹ-bi kí kpāfì.
Án kaa làá ti sūŋkì bi làá jī falaa
abɔtibil bɔtiu ŋaan.
11Eefiraayiim yab máń isaraafan tikpil
kí nīn ŋáań ikpiti pɔ̄tam saraabi.
- Ama isaraafan gbanti di yàntī
bi mɔ̀tīi ŋáań ikpiti. -
12Báà m yaa ŋmàn̄ m-marab nee
bɔkpaaŋi ŋfunyɔm kutuku pu,
án làá nīn bí-bi kii tibɔcan tibee ní.
13Bi ŋáań saraabi ki tìì-mi,
kun puee tinan ní bi nyàab̀ kí ŋmɔ́.
Ama man bi-Dindaan,
maa làá fōō saraabi gbanti.
Too m làá téetí bi-yìntitam pu,
m làá dáaĺ bi-tafal bi-kpitii pu.
Bi làá fàtīí gítí Eejipiti tiŋkin.
14«Isirayeel beel yab máń adinyaan
ní ki súntì bi-náanliu pu.
Juuda beel yabee, bíǹ máń
agun ní ki tú bi-timmu.
Ama m làá yàntī ŋŋmi
ń wà bi-timmu gbanti,
ní kí wà bi-dinyaaŋŋi mun.»

english_text:
Israel Will Be Punished
1Israel, don't celebrate
or make noisy shouts
like other nations.
You have been unfaithful
to your God.
Wherever grain is threshed,
you behave like prostitutes
because you enjoy
the money you receive.
2But you will run short
of grain and wine,
3and you will have to leave
the land of the Lord.
Some of you will go to Egypt;
others will go to Assyria
and eat unclean food.
4You won't be able to offer
sacrifices of wine
to the Lord.
None of your sacrifices
will please him—
they will be unclean
like food offered to the dead.
Your food will only be used
to satisfy your hunger;
none of it will be brought
to the Lord's temple.
5You will no longer be able
to celebrate the festival
of the Lord.
6Even if you escape alive,
you will end up in Egypt
and be buried in Memphis.
Your silver treasures
will be lost among weeds;
thorns will sprout in your tents.
7 Israel, the time has come.
You will get what you deserve,
and you will know it.
“Prophets are fools,” you say.
“And God's messengers
are crazy.”
Your terrible guilt
has filled you with hatred.
8Israel, the Lord sent me
to look after you.
But you trap his prophets
and flood his temple
with your hatred.
9 You are brutal and corrupt,
as were the men of Gibeah.
But God remembers your sin,
and you will be punished.
Sin's Terrible Results
10 Israel, when I, the Lord,
found you long ago
it was like finding
grapes in a barren desert
or tender young figs.
Then you worshiped Baal Peor,
that disgusting idol,
and you became as disgusting
as the idol you loved.
11And so, Israel, your glory
will fly away like birds—
your women will no longer
be able to give birth.
12Even if you do have children,
I will take them all
and leave you to mourn.
I will turn away,
and you will sink down
in deep trouble.
13Israel, when I first met you,
I thought of you as palm trees
growing in fertile ground.
Now you lead your people out,
only to be slaughtered.
Hosea's Advice
14Our Lord, do just one thing
for your people—
make their women unable
to have children
or to nurse their babies.
The Lord's Judgment on Israel
15Israel, I first began
to hate you because
you did evil at Gilgal.
Now I will chase you
out of my house.
No longer will I love you;
your leaders betrayed me.
16Israel, you are a vine
with dried-up roots
and fruitless branches.
Even if you had more children
and loved them dearly,
I would slaughter them all.
Hosea Warns Israel
17Israel, you disobeyed my God.
Now he will force you to roam
from nation to nation.
translation_text:
Unimbɔti nibul làá fá tikɔkɔ
1Isirayeel, taa nín̄ fàal̀ kí lákatí mara pu
kii atimbun ŋin kíǹee nín ŋáań puee.
Di sá yii alaakpaatuun puee,
a dū a-Nimbɔtiu ki fá,
ki ŋá alaakpaatuun.
A néeń kí fōō a-laakpaatuuŋŋi paati
laakin kamaa ní bilee naapaaŋi bée.
2Bilee un bi gbáà dinaapaal puee
nì ŋkpam min bi ŋmāam̀
kutaŋkpaboounee, aa làá ká.
Ndapɔm min a kā ki cée,
a kpá kí ká-mì kí dáká.
3Eefiraayiim yab kaa làá ŋmā
kí nīn gbíntìi kóò ti-Dindaan tiŋkin.
Bi làá fàtīí gítí Eejipiti tiŋkin,
ní kí jī tijin tin bi kòóyee Asuur tiŋkin.
4Baa dāa gíti féeń ndaam
kí ŋá ti-Dindaan saraa,
bi-saraabi kaa làá dāá nīn fáatiǹ-u.
Bi-jinti làá dāá kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi kii dikpoolin jintee,
un kamaa yaa jíń-tèe kóò tijɔkɔndin ní.
Bi làá dāá ká tijin kí jī kí díkí,
ama baa dāa ŋūǹ kí kɔ́ǹ-tì ti-Dindaan diikun.
5Ni làá dāá ŋá mana
dikpafil wiiŋŋu dal,
ti-Dindaan jiŋaaliu wiiŋŋu dal?
6Ni yaa láa yíkì ni-tiŋki kin bi nāaǹee nee,
Eejipiti tiŋki làá dāá fōō-ni,
ama Meemifiisi tiŋkin ní bi làá dāá síb́-ni.
Abɔjanaakun di làá dāá jī bi-gaajawammɔntiiti fakal,
ní ikuŋkum ń dāá nyā bi-diiŋŋin.
7Ditafadaaldi yuntiŋu bāań dee,
ŋyunti ŋun báà ŋma làá sòoǹ
u-nyɔkɔpu yayee bāań.
Isirayeel beel yab máaǹ kí béé míǹ!
Ni lì yii: «Ubɔnaatil nee wáatì ní,
unil un pu Ŋfam bí nee yil lábitì.»
Tiŋman, m yaa wáatèe,
an sá ni-kpitii nín wīikí puee,
nì ni nín bí ki jáà nì mi mpɔn nì mpɔnee pu.
8Man ubɔnaatil,
man di sá un cí Eefiraayiimee,
man nì m-Nimbɔtiu di bí.
Ama binib pīil̀-mi titalindi
laakin kamaa ní m yaa cée.
Bi jáà nì mi
áli m-Nimbɔtiu diikun.
9Bi pée kɔ́ ikpiti poon poon ní kábu,
a lì kii bi nín nìn ŋá pu Giibeeya tiŋkinee.
Ama Unimbɔti kpá kí súntí bi-kpitii pu,
asee u pée dáaĺ bi-tafal
bi-kpitii gbanti pu.
Tin nìn jítì Baal-Peewɔree
10Ti-Dindaan lī yii: «Dooooyee,
m nìn ká Isirayeel yab
kii ɔliifi biliŋ ŋin bi kītì kuteeunee
nín mɔ̄ puee ní.
M nìn ká ni-naanjab
kii difiigibipeepeekaal din
bi kāntí bufiigisubu puee ní.
Ama ni-naanjab nín nìn bāań Beeti-Peewɔɔree,
bi nìn dū bi-ba ki líiǹ ticoobɔti.
Bi ŋá mimmee ní m kíǹ ki ná-bi
kii m nín ná diwaal din bi néeńee puee.
11Eefiraayiim yab, kun tìì-ni tinyoolee
làá yīkì kí ŋàaǹ kii unoonee ní.
Binimpoobi kaa dāa gíti màal̀ mbiyaamuɔɔɔ,
baa dāa gíti cāab̀ apooyaaa,
mbiyaamu kaa dāa gíti nāantí bi-pooŋŋin.
12Báà bi yaa cáá mbiyaamu mu cíkitàaa,
maa làá yàntī mú nīn bí kí kpántí binib.
Ama m yaa fātì m-boon ki tīī-bi,
dinimbinaamandi làá kɔ́-beeee!
13M wāĺ Eefiraayiim kii Tiir tiŋki
kin nìn bí laakin timool múkú an sɔ̀m̀ fílfilee ní,
nì míǹ kɔkɔee Eefiraayiim làá dāá dū u-biyaamu
kí tīī bí kpɔ̀.»
14Ti-Dindaan, a yaa làá dáaĺ binib nee tafalee,
ba ní a làá dūú dáaĺ ní?
Yàntī bi-nimpoobi ń kpántí biŋmaŋŋmantiibi,
bi-biiŋi ń fáká.
15Ti-Dindaan gíti bí yii:
«Bi-tuŋkpitiŋ kɔkɔ kíĺ Giilgaal ní.
Niin ní m kíĺ ki kíǹ ki ná-bi.
Ikpiti in ní bi ŋée puee,
m làá jà-bi kí nyāntí m-diikun.
Maa ti làá nīn néeń-bi.
Bi-kpootiliibi kɔkɔ sá pɔɔgaatib ní.
16Bi gbáń Eefiraayiim yab an bàn̄-bi.
Bi-nyaaŋyi kūń.
Baa ti làá lòoǹ abil.
Báà binimpoobi yaa dáá gbíntìi cáá mbiyaamuɔɔɔ,
m làá fáá kí kpɔ̀ bi-poon naŋu
biyaamu mun bi néeńee.»
17M-Nimbɔtiu làá dū-bi kí fá
di sá yii baa pílifiǹ-u.
Bi làá nīn kíǹ ki tú ki yìiǹ
atimbun ŋin kíǹee kansikin ní.

english_text:
1You were a healthy vine
covered with grapes.
But the more grapes you grew,
the more altars you built;
the better off you became,
the better shrines you set up
for pagan gods.
2You are deceitful and disloyal.
So you will pay
for your sins,
because the Lord will destroy
your altars and images.
3“We don't have a king,”
you will say.
“We don't fear the Lord.
And what good are kings?”
4Israel, you break treaties
and don't keep promises;
you turn justice
into poisonous weeds
where healthy plants should grow.
5All who live in Samaria tremble
with concern for the idols
at sinful Bethel.
The idol there was the pride
of the priests,
but it has been put to shame;
now everyone will cry.
6It will be taken to Assyria
and given to the great king.
Then Israel will be disgraced
for worshiping that idol.
7Like a twig in a stream,
the king of Samaria
will be swept away.
8 The altars at sinful Bethel
will be destroyed
for causing Israel to sin;
they will be grown over
with thorns and thistles.
Then everyone will beg
the mountains and hills
to cover and protect them.
The Lord Promises To Punish Israel
9 Israel, you have never
stopped sinning
since that time at Gibeah.
That's why you
will be attacked at Gibeah.
10Your sins have doubled,
and you are rebellious.
Now I have decided
to send nations to attack
and put you in chains.
11Once you were obedient
like a calf
that loved to thresh grain.
But I will put a harness
on your beautiful neck;
you and Judah must plow
and cultivate the ground.
12 Plow your fields,
scatter seeds of justice,
and harvest faithfulness.
Worship me, the Lord,
and I will send my saving power
down like rain.
13You have planted evil,
harvested injustice, and eaten
the fruit of your lies.
You trusted your own strength
and your powerful forces.
14So war will break out,
and your fortresses
will be destroyed.
Your enemies will do to you
what Shalman did to the people
of Beth-Arbel—
mothers and their children
will be beaten to death
against rocks.
15Bethel, this will be your fate
because of your evil.
Israel, at dawn your king
will be killed.
translation_text:
Isirayeel yab beel kúntitam
1Isirayeel beel nìn sá bufiinyisubu
bun nìn lòoǹ abil tikpilee ní.
U yaa nìn lòon̄ abil tikpilee,
míǹ ní u nìn māā isaraafan mun tikpil.
An yaa nìn bútì u-tiŋkee,
míǹ ní u nìn nyāantí u-taŋkpacooŋkaaŋi.
2Isirayeel yab sá milimilidambi ní.
Too, ŋyunti bāań bí fōō bi-kpitii paati.
Ti-Dindaan u-ba di làá wìil̀ bi-saraafaŋyi,
ní kí kpēelikì bi-taŋkpacooŋkaaŋi.
3Bi bí ki lì kɔŋkɔnnee yii:
«Taa cáá ubɔti,
di sá yii taa fāŋkì ti-Dindaan.
Báà ti yaa cáá ubɔti,
ba ní u ŋūǹ kí ŋá kí tīī-ti?»
4Bi sòoǹ tikpil,
ki pùtī fám,
bi nì binib ŋáań mpèé,
ama bi-baamɔŋyi
bí kii ujil nín nyēē
adan pu bukpaan puee ní.
5Samaarii yab fàŋkí tin làá bàń
Beeti-Aween nabil puee.
Dinabilee nibul nì di-saraaŋaliibi
bíi ŋáań di-kpool.
Bi nìn fàal̀ di-nyaaŋku pu,
too, bi yōoǹ-dì ki cáa búntì.
6Bi làá yòon̄ dinabilee kí cáá cùnnì Asuur tiŋkin
kí pɔ̄ kitiŋ gbanti bɔtikpaaŋwu.
Icoo làá dāá cúú Eefiraayiim yab,
tiŋman, icoo làá dāá cúú Isirayeel beel yab
tin bi bɔ́ntì kí ŋée pu.
7An dóò Samaarii yab pu dee.
Bi-bɔtiu sá kii didɔjal din dēē
nnyim puee ní.
8Bi làá dāá kpìtī Aween saraaŋapaaŋyi,
íǹ in pu Isirayeel yab nìn ŋáań ikpitee.
Abɔjanaakun nì ikuŋkum làá dāá nyā
kí múkuǹ i-saraafaŋyi pu.
Samaarii yab làá dāá tùkù ajoon yii:
«Bìim̄maan ti-pu!»
ní kí dāá lì ŋgbantamu yii:
«Lítímaan ti-pu!»
9Doooo Giibeeya ní Isirayeel yab yīntiǹ-mi,
ní doooo nee, baa kpántì bi-ba.
An pu ní bi làá já nì bíǹ binikpitib
gbanti Giibeeya jool pu.
10Ti-Dindaan lī yii:
«M làá dáaĺ bi-tafal.
Atimbun làá dāá kpāfì kí já nì bi
kí dáaĺ bi-tafal ikpiti in bi ŋáań kaa gbèentée pu.
11«Eefiraayiim nìn sá kii dinabil din
nìn néeń ki tà ki gbátí adibilee ní.
Ŋyunti ŋun m ká u-sil nyaaŋkuee,
ní m kpàl̄-u ú nīn kù tikpaal.
Juuda làá nīn dátí akoo ŋin cátí adanee
ní Isirayeel ń nīn dátí akoo ŋin kpátée.
12Bɔ̄l̀maan tin bí deedeeyee
kí dāá cā tiniti.
Ní bēel̀maan kusapɔŋu,
di sá yii ŋyunti bāań ní nyàab̀ man ni-Dindaan
kí nīn cí ŋyunti ŋun ní m làá dāan̄
kí dū tin bí deedeeyee kí yàaǹ ni-puee.
13Ama ní ni búĺ tikpitil
ní ki bíi cēē ikpiti.
Ni ŋmɔ́ disubil din ni-nyimɔŋyi lòon̄ee.
«Di sá yii ni nìn máká ni-ba pɔŋŋu
nì ni-janjaliibi wíiŋŋu pu.
14An pu ní kujaau làá pōō
ni-nibul kansikin,
ní bí dāá nàan̄ ni-timmu mun
bi máń agun ki túee kɔkɔ.
Ŋi làá dāá kpántí kii Beeti Arbeel tiŋkee ní.
Ubɔti Calman nín nìn jáń nì kitiŋ gbantee,
u nìn kūū bibinaatiibi ki kpáaǹ bi-biyaamu ní.
15Kun ni ŋá Beeteelee
nín cáań-ni kuŋyee dee,
di sá yii ni-kpitii gíti jítì mara pu.
Kutaa tin lì yii ku wúntée,
an dóò Isirayeel bɔtiu pu dee.»

english_text:
God's Love for His People
1 When Israel was a child,
I loved him, and I called
my son out of Egypt.
2But as the saying goes,
“The more they were called,
the more they rebelled.”
They never stopped offering
incense and sacrifices
to the idols of Baal.
3I took Israel by the arm
and taught them to walk.
But they would not admit
that I was the one
who had healed them.
4I led them with kindness
and with love,
not with ropes.
I held them close to me;
I bent down to feed them.
5But they rejected me,
and so must return to Egypt;
now Assyria will rule them.
6War will visit their cities,
and their plans will fail.
7My people are determined
to reject me for a god
they think is stronger,
but he can't help.
8 Israel, I can't let you go.
I can't give you up.
How could I possibly destroy you
as I did the towns of Admah
and Zeboiim?
I just can't do it.
My feelings for you
are much too strong.
9Israel, I won't lose my temper
and destroy you again.
I am the Holy God—
not merely some human,
and I won't stay angry.
10I, the Lord, will roar like a lion,
and my children will return,
trembling from the west.
11They will come back,
fluttering like birds from Egypt
or like doves from Assyria.
Then I will bring them
back to their homes.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
Israel and Judah Compared
12Israel is deceitful to me,
their loyal and holy God;
they surround me with lies,
and Judah worships
other gods.
translation_text:
Ti-Dindaan neendi din u cáá u-nibul puee
1«Ŋyunti ŋun Isirayeel nìn sá kibikee
ní m nìn kíĺ ki néeń-u,
ní ki yíiń úǹ, m-jipɔɔn
ki nyántìń Eejipiti tiŋkin.»
2Ama míǹ boonee, m yaa gíti yíiń-uee,
u kíǹ ki sáń-mi ní.
Bi ŋáań saraabi ki tìì awaa ŋin bi yíì Baalee,
ní ki tùutī talaalub ki tìì awaakpitikaa.
3Min kamaa man di ŋúb́ Eefiraayiim ŋalii,
ki dātì-u tàatáa u cōom̀ee,
waa béè gba yii man di lōō-u.
4Nì mpoommɔn nì dineendi ní m dūu kpēē-u.
M nìn sá kii ubinaati nín yòontí u-biki
kí nákań u-ba pu,
kí bòon̄ kí tīī-kì dibiil kí ŋāam̀ puee ní.
5«Baa làá fàtīí gítí Eejipiti tiŋkin,
ama Asuur yab di làá dāá nīn cáá bi-pu mpɔn,
di sá yii bi yíì kaa fātìi gítìń m-cee.
6An pu ní kujaau tùm̀ bi-timmun dàii,
ku bíiĺ bi-timmu punyɔmmu,
ki làá kpɔ̀ kí céetí bin kóò mu-nee
bi-saŋkpitii pu.
7M-nibul lafun lēē bi-pɔbilin kí dū-mi kí fá.
Bi yíì-bi doooo yilpu,
ama bi-kansikin báà ubɔ kaa yíkì.
8«Mana ní m ŋūǹ kí fàtī m-boon
kí tīī-si ní, Eefiraayiim?
Mana ní m ŋūǹ kí dū-si
kí fá ní, Isirayeel?
Mana ní m ŋūǹ kí ŋá-si kii
m nín ŋá Adima tiŋki puee,
àá kí ŋá-si kii m nín ŋá
Seebooyiim tiŋki puee?
M yaa ŋá míǹ, an làá páb́-mi tikpil.
An gbí-mi isaa.
9Maa làá dū m-ŋuukpaandi kí tɔ̄ ditundi.
Maa ti làá nàan̄ Eefiraayiim,
di sá yii m sá Unimbɔti ní,
maa sá unil.
M sá circirdaan ní ki bí ni-kansikin,
maa làá dāan̄ nì diŋuul poon.»
10Bi làá dāá páań ti-Dindaan boon.
Ti-Dindaan làá dāá mùuǹ kii gbikintee.
U yaa láa bíi mùuǹee,
u-biyaamu làá dāá nyānní
ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú bi-wunti gbáà kí dāan̄.
11Bi làá dāá nyānní Eejipiti tiŋkin
bi-wunti gbáà kpàkpa kii idiyaalee,
ní kí dāá nyānní Asuur tiŋkin kii abeenanjilee.
M làá dāá yàntī bí gítí bi-diiŋŋi poon.
Ti-Dindaan di sòon̄.

english_text:
1All day long Israel chases
wind from the desert;
deceit and violence
are found everywhere.
Treaties are made with Assyria;
olive oil is taken to Egypt.
Israel and Judah Condemned
2The Lord also brings charges
against the people of Judah,
the descendants of Jacob.
He will punish them
for what they have done.
3 Even before Jacob was born,
he cheated his brother,
and when he grew up,
he fought against God.
4 At Bethel, Jacob wrestled
with an angel and won;
then with tears in his eyes,
he asked for a blessing,
and God spoke to us there.
5God's name is the Lord,
the Lord God All-Powerful.
6So return to your God.
Patiently trust him,
and show love and justice.
7Israel, you enjoy cheating
and taking advantage
of others.
8You say to yourself, “I'm rich!
I earned it all on my own,
without committing a sin.”
The Lord Is Still the God of Israel
9 Israel, I, the Lord,
am still your God,
just as I have been
since the time
you were in Egypt.
Now I will force you
to live in tents once again,
as you did in the desert.
10I spoke to the prophets—
often I spoke in visions.
And so, I will send my prophets
with messages of doom.
11Gilead is terribly sinful
and will end up ruined.
Bulls are sacrificed in Gilgal
on altars made of stones,
but those stones will be scattered
in every field.
12 Jacob escaped to Syria
where he tended sheep
to earn himself a wife.
13 I sent the prophet Moses
to lead Israel from Egypt
and to keep them safe.
14Israel, I will make you pay
for your violent crimes
and for insulting me.
translation_text:
Eefiraayiim kpitii
1Eefiraayiim yab dū inyimɔn ki māntìi tú-mi,
ní Isirayeel beel yab dū diŋmatindi ki fìn̄-mi.
Ama Juuda beel yab bíǹ dá láá gbíntìi còom̄ nì Unimbɔti,
ní ki dáá gbíntìi yú nì circirdaan deedee.
2Eefiraayiim yab jīǹ kubuŋu ní kí díkí,
ní ki jì ki bīī ŋwìiń nyalaŋki boon kaa gbèentí.
Bi yāntì inyimɔn nì tipɔmbɔti gbóotì.
Bi nì Asuur yab ŋá mpèé,
ní ki tìì Eejipiti yab ŋkpam.
3Ti-Dindaan nì Juuda yab cáá ibɔsoon.
U làá dáaĺ Jaakɔb nibooliŋu tafal
bi-bimbikpitim pu,
ní kí pà-bi bi-tuuŋŋi paati.
4Jaakɔb bí u-na poon
ní ki fōō u-maan paaŋŋu.
U cíkitì muee ní u nì Unimbɔti mɔ̀n̄.
5U nì Unimbɔti tuuŋŋu mɔ̀n̄ ní u pɔ́ɔkiǹ-ŋu.
U nìn súń ki gbāam̀-ŋu.
U nìn ká Unimbɔti Beeteel,
niin ní Unimbɔti sòon̄ nì ti.
6Niin ní Ti-Dindaan, Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan,
un bi yíì yii <ti-Dindaanee> lī yii:
7«Míǹ puee, á fàtīí gítiń man a-Nimbɔtiu cee,
nín̄ yú nì mi deedee kí nīn ŋáań tin ŋān̄ee.
Nín̄ pée máká mama a-Nimbɔtiu pu baabadal.»
8«Kii Kanaan yab nín bí puee,
míǹ ní sii Eefiraayiim mun bí,
a ŋúb́ saniya un kaa sá umɔntee.
A néeń ki mùul̄ binib
9ki lì yii:
<M kpántì ugaaja,
m ká tigaajati tikpil.
M-tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ poonee,
maa ŋá tikpitil tiba,
maa pée yīntì báà tiba poon.>
10Ama mamee, doooo Eejipiti tiŋkin
ní m sá a-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu.
M làá yàntī á fàtīí nīn kíǹ ki kóò tibìń ni,
kii ŋwiin ŋun man nì sii nìn kpáfèe.
11M nìn sòon̄ nì bibɔnaatiliibi,
ní ki nìn yāntì bi kántì aleedaka tikpil.
M làá gíti dī bibɔnaatiliibi pu kí gāā alaŋkpan.
12Galaadi yab baasii sá binikpitib ní,
tiba kaa ti kíǹ bi-ni.
Giilgaalee, bi nìn cáá inaa
ki ŋáań saraabi kaa gbèentí.
Ama bi-saraafaŋyi kpántì
ataŋkpakpuku ŋin dɔ̄ ipɔ̀n pu tisatinee ní.»
13Jaakɔb sáǹ ki cūtì Aram tantakalin.
Isirayeel cūtìi túń ditundi unimpu pu.
Unimpu puee, u nìn kpántì un kpàá tiwaŋkutee.
14Ama ti-Dindaan dī ubɔnaatil ubɔ pu
ní ki nyántì Isirayeel yab Eejipiti tiŋkin.
U làá yàntī ubɔnaatil ń kpàà u-nibul.
15Eefiraayiim kɔ́ Unimbɔti poon ki lēē baadakam.
U-Dindaan làá yàntī fatiku un u
kpáatìi fée ń gítí u-pu,
ní kí dáaĺ u-tafal u nín kpēē-u fámee pu.

english_text:
Israel Is Doomed
The Lord said:
1When your leaders spoke,
everyone in Israel trembled
and showed great respect.
But you sinned by worshiping Baal,
and you were destroyed.
2Now you continue to sin
by designing and making
idols of silver
in the shape of calves.
You are told to sacrifice
to these idols—
yes, even to kiss them.
3And so, all of you will vanish
like the mist or the dew
of early morning,
or husks of grain in the wind
or smoke from a chimney.
4I, the Lord, have been your God
since the time
you were in Egypt.
I am the only God you know,
the only one who can save.
5 I took care of you
in a thirsty desert.
6I fed you till you were satisfied,
then you became proud
and forgot about me.
7Now I will attack like a lion,
ambush you like a leopard,
8and rip you apart like a bear
robbed of her cubs.
I will gnaw on your bones,
as though I were a lion
or some other wild animal.
9Israel, you are done for.
Don't expect help from me.
10 You wanted a king and rulers.
Where is your king now?
What cities have rulers?
11 In my anger, I gave you a king;
in my fury, I took him away.
Israel's Terrible Fate
The Lord said:
12Israel, your terrible sins
are written down
and stored away.
13You are like a senseless child
who refuses to be born
at the proper time.
14 Should I, the Lord, rescue you
from death and the grave?
No! I call death and the grave
to strike you like a plague.
I refuse to show mercy.
15No matter if you prosper
more than the other tribes,
I, the Lord, will wipe you out,
just as a scorching desert wind
dries up streams of water.
I will take away
your precious treasures.
16Samaria will be punished
for turning against me.
It will be destroyed in war—
children will be beaten
against rocks,
and pregnant women
will be ripped open.
translation_text:
Ti-Dindaan gíí Isirayeel beel pu diŋuul
1Njaminee, Eefiraayiim yaa nìn sòoǹee,
báà ŋma nìn fàŋkí ní.
Isirayeel naakɔti kansikinee, úǹ di nìn līī.
Ama u nóó diwaal Baal ki fōō dibɔkpil,
ní ki kpíì an pu.
2Díǹ pu nee, bi dáá gbíntìi nìkì ki ŋáań ikpiti.
Bi dūntì bi-nimbiliŋ ki dūu mɔ́ɔ́ awaa,
awaa ŋin ní bíǹ bi-ba dākafì ki mɔ́ɔ́yee.
An sá uwammɔ́ɔl tuuŋŋi aba ní,
awaa gbanti pu ní bi lì yii:
«Tí ŋámaan saraabi kí tīī-ŋi!»
Binib móotí anabil ki ŋáań saraabi.
3An pu ní bi làá nīn bí kii ditaafaapɔ̀ńdee,
a lì kii ditaafaamalindi nín wáŋkí pu malaayee.
Bi làá nīn bí kii tifeel nín yíkí pu
kí cù ndandati kí wàatī dibileenaapaal puee ní,
àá kii ŋŋminyiim nín nyēē mbùń ŋubɔ poon puee ní.
4Doooo Eejipiti tiŋkin
ní man sá a-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu.
Aa ti nyí Unimbɔti ubɔ ki kútì man pu,
ufiil ubɔ mun kaa ti bí laaba, asee man baba.
5Mamee, kuteeun, ŋweel tiŋkin
ní m béè-si.
6A pée bàn̄ kunaakpaapɔɔunee
ní a jíń ki díkí.
Ama ŋyunti ŋun a jíń ki díkée
ní a kɔ́ dilambilin.
An pu ní a súntì man pu.
7Niinee ní m kpántì kii
gbikintee ki tīī-si,
a lì kii ugbii un di
náká nsan caŋin ki cée.
8M làá kpìl̄-si kii digbiŋgbil
din ní bi cúú di-biyaamuee.
M làá yā kí cátí a-bindi.
M làá cúú-si kí tɔ̀ntī kii
ugbikintinaatee dibɔbil pu niin,
ní ipeel ń cúú-si kí tɔ̀ntī tɔ̀ntī.
9Kɔŋkɔnnee Isirayeel, an nāaǹ-si!
Too, man baba di bàà ŋūǹ kí jòoń-si?
10A-bɔtiuee bí la ní kaa làá dāan̄
kí fīī-si a-timmu poon ní?
A-kpootiliibee bí là ní?
Ŋyuntee, a nìn bí-mi yii:
<Tīī-mi ubɔti nì bikpootiliibi.>
11Tiŋman m nìn tīī-si ubɔti m-ŋuul poon,
ní ki fātìi fōō-u m-bum poon.
12M ŋmàn̄ Eefiraayiim yab
yìntitam ki síiǹ.
M dū bi-kpitii ki kpáafì tiŋan.
13Imatiŋween làá jēetí bi-pu.
Ama kibikee sá kibigbaaŋŋi ní.
Ŋyunti bàà bàn̄ dee,
ama kì yíì kaa là kí nyā ki-na poon.
14Mimmee mama bi-Dindaan,
m máaǹ kí dā-bi
kí nyāntí ditaŋkpiil ŋaanaaa?
Ḿ fīī-bi kí nyāntí ŋkúm ŋaanaaa?
Too, ŋkúm, a-pɔŋŋu bí la?
Too, ditaŋkpiil, a-looti bí la?
Disaasɔl nyáń m-nimbiliŋin.
15Min kamaa an bútì Eefiraayiim yab
bi-nabiyaamu kansikinee,
ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú buŋku dòoń,
ti-Dindaan buŋku làá nyānní kuteeu pú.
Ku làá fáá nnyimbul pu ní ŋú fóotí
ní dinyimbɔbil ń kpā,
ní bí fūkul̀ laakin bi dū
bi-gaajawammɔntiiti ki kpáafèe.

english_text:
Turn Back to the Lord
1Israel, return! Come back
to the Lord, your God.
Sin has made you fall.
2Return to the Lord and say,
“Please forgive our sins.
Accept our good sacrifices
of praise instead of bulls.
3Assyria can't save us,
and chariots can't help.
So we will no longer worship
the idols we have made.
Our Lord, you show mercy
to orphans.”
The Lord Promises To Forgive
4Israel, you have rejected me,
but my anger is gone;
I will heal you and love you
without limit.
5I will be like the dew—
then you will blossom like lilies
and have roots like a tree.
6Your branches will spread
with the beauty
of an olive tree
and with the aroma
of Lebanon Forest.
7You will rest in my shade,
and your grain will grow.
You will blossom
like a vineyard
and be famous as the wine
from Lebanon.
8Israel, give up your idols!
I will answer your prayers
and take care of you.
I am that glorious tree,
the source of your fruit.
9If you are wise, you will know
and understand what I mean.
I am the Lord, and I lead you
along the right path.
If you obey me,
we will walk together,
but if you are wicked,
you will stumble.
translation_text:
1Samaarii yab fōō dibɔkpil
ní ki máaǹ ditafadaaldi,
kun puee bi jáń nì man bi-Nimbɔtiu.
Kujaaun ní bi làá tin kpúnní,
ní bí tāā kí mátí bi-bipɔmmu
ní kí pùtī bi-pɔdambi.
Dibakpántil nì dimaŋfapɔndi
2Isirayeel, fàtīí gítiń
ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu cee,
di sá yii a-kpitii di yāntì
a gbéetì ki lítì.
3Gítiḿmaan ti-Dindaan cee
kí kpáaǹ anyɔɔbun nee kí tin tùkù-u yii:
«Dū ti-kpitii kí pɔ̄-ti,
ní kí fōō tin ŋān̄ ti cáa ŋáań-si saraayee.
An nín bàà sá tí dū anabil kí ŋá-si saraayee,
ti làá dū ti-nyɔmmu poon nyɔɔbuŋŋi
ní kí ŋá-si saraa.
4Asuur tiŋki kaa ŋūǹ kí fīī-ti.
Taa làá ti máĺ kí kàl̄
kujaau taamui pu.
Ti-waaŋi sá tiwan tin ti dū ti-ŋalii ki kpítèe ní.
Taa làá ti tùkù-ŋi yii ŋi sá ti-Nimbɔtiu,
di sá yii sii baba di dàkà
ditaŋkpiibil kulaŋŋaŋfitiiu.»
5Ti-Dindaan bí yii:
«M làá cáaǹ Isirayeel
u nín kaa yúl̀ nì mi deedeeyee pu.
M làá nīn néeń-u nì dipɔbil diba,
di sá yii diŋuul din m gíí u-puee sɔ̄ŋkì.
6M làá nīn bí kii dimalindee
ní ki tīī Isirayeel.
U làá púkuḿ kii nsupumpukumee
ní kí báań inyaan kii
Leebanɔn tiŋkin isufi in bi yíì Seediree.
7U làá dāá tɔ̄ apan kí làlim̀
ní kí nīn cáá kunyaaŋŋu kii ɔliifi subuee,
ní kí nīn sɔ́fì
kii Leebanɔn satin sufiiyee.
8Bin nìn kóò u-booŋŋu taapuee
làá dāá fàtīí gítiń.
Bi làá dāá kpɔ̀ bilee kpaaŋŋi.
Bi làá dāá púkuḿ kii fiinyi subuee,
ní kí dāá nyā diyindi kii Leebanɔn daamee.
9Eefiraayiim,
mpèé ŋulɔŋu di bí man nì awaa kansikin ní?
Man di fòol̄ a-wimmeem
ní ki wúǹ a-pu.
M sá kii siipreesi susɔmbuee ní,
man di yì-tì ní a-kpaajinti lòoǹ.»
10Un cáá dinyilee làá gbìl̄
tibɔti nee taapu.
Un cáá iciinee
làá béé-tì?
Tiŋman, ti-Dindaan saŋyi tèen̄ ní.
Deedeedambi di dìŋfī-i,
ama pɔɔgaatib yaa dī-iee,
see bí gbéetí kí lítí.

english_text:
1I am Joel the son of Pethuel.
And this is the message
the Lord gave to me.
Locusts Cover the Land
2Listen, you leaders
and everyone else
in the land.
Has anything like this
ever happened before?
3Tell our children!
Let it be told
to our grandchildren
and their children too.
4Swarm after swarm of locusts
has attacked our crops,
eating everything in sight.
5Sober up, you drunkards!
Cry long and loud;
your wine supply is gone.
6 A powerful nation
with countless troops
has invaded our land.
They have the teeth and jaws
of powerful lions.
7Our grapevines and fig trees
are stripped bare;
only naked branches remain.
8Grieve like a young woman
mourning for the man
she was to marry.
9Offerings of grain and wine
are no longer brought
to the Lord's temple.
His servants, the priests,
are deep in sorrow.
10Barren fields mourn;
grain, grapes, and olives
are scorched and shriveled.
11Mourn for our farms
and our vineyards!
There's no wheat or barley
growing in our fields.
12Grapevines have dried up
and so has every tree—
figs and pomegranates,
date palms and apples.
All happiness has faded away.
Return to God
13Mourn, you priests who serve
at the altar of my God.
Spend your days and nights
wearing sackcloth.
Offerings of grain and wine
are no longer brought
to the Lord's temple.
14Tell the leaders and people
to come together
at the temple.
Order them to go without eating
and to pray sincerely.
15 We are in for trouble!
Soon the Lord All-Powerful
will bring disaster.
16Our food is already gone;
there's no more celebrating
at the temple of our God.
17Seeds dry up in the ground;
no harvest is possible.
Our barns are in bad shape,
with no grain
to store in them.
18Our cattle wander aimlessly,
moaning for lack of pasture,
and sheep are suffering.
19I cry out to you, Lord.
Grasslands and forests are eaten
by the scorching heat.
20Wild animals have no water
because of you;
rivers and streams are dry,
and pastures are parched.
translation_text:
1Ti-Dindaan di sòon̄ nì Peetuweel jipɔɔn Jooweel tibɔti nee.
Inaakitoon nì ŋweel bɔti
2Nimbi bikpilibee, ní pīlifìmaan!
Ní ŋátímaan ni-tafaliŋ kí pīlifì, Juuda yab kɔkɔ!
Tin bí nee juti jítì ni-yuntii nee poon ni káaa,
àá tì jítì ni-naanjab yuntii ni gbìl̄ ní?
3Ní dūú māafìmaan ni-biyaamu.
Ni-biyaamu mun ń dāá dūú māafì bi-biyaamu,
ní bi-biyaamu ń dāá dūú māafì bi-boon yab.
4Tijin tin anaakitɔmbil ŋmɔ́ ki kíǹee,
inaakitoon dūu ŋmɔ́,
tin ní inaakitoon ŋmɔ́ ki kíǹee,
inaakicaan dūu ŋmɔ́,
ní tin ní inaakicaan ŋmɔ́ ki kíǹee,
inaaki dūu ŋmɔ́.
5Bidanyɔgbiliibi, fìntīmaan kí nīn sūǹ.
Nín̄ yáliŋkímaan, nimbi bidanyɔliibi kɔkɔ.
Di sá yii naa ti làá ká ndapɔm kí nyɔ̀.
6Ditimbundi diba nib bíi jáà nì m-tiŋki.
Bi pɔ̄ɔ̄ ní ki wīikí baa ŋūǹ kí kàaǹ-bi.
Bi-nyiŋŋi bí kii gbikinti nyiŋŋee ní,
ní bi-nyɔɔkpaweeŋyi bí kii ugbikintisal yaŋee.
7Bi yāntì m-fiinyi kpaabu kpántì kii kuteeuee,
bi bíil̀ m-fiigi sufii kɔkɔ múb.
Bi ŋmɔ́ ki lēē i-pɔkɔti kɔkɔ,
ki yāntì i-pammu kíǹ ki pīiǹ kpáu.
8Nín̄ yáliŋkímaan kii usapɔɔn un
dáá pée mɔ́ǹ ní u-cal kpíì u kā dikpoolee.
9Baa ti cáǹ tijimpin saraau
nì ndaam saraau ti-Dindaan diikun.
Bisaraaŋaliibi bin sá
ti-Dindaan tɔntɔnliibee kā dikpool.
10Bi bíil̀ tisati,
kitiŋ kɔ́ kunimbaaun.
Tijin gíti kpáaa,
ndapɔm gíti kpáaa,
ŋkpam mun gúń.
11Bikpaabi wunti yɔ̄tì.
Bin kù fiinyee yáliŋkí
ɔɔji nì bilee pu,
di sá yii tikpaajin kpá bí cā.
12Fiinyi kūń,
ní fiigi sufii fáaḿ.
Greenaadi sufii nì ibafi nì pɔɔmi sufii,
an dàkà yii kusaaun sufii kɔkɔ kūń.
Dipɔɔpindi wáŋkì binib kansikin.
Binib ń bóob́ kinyɔkɔ kí gbàam̀ ti-Dindaan
13Bisaraaŋaliibi, dūmaan kpɔsatab kí pèen̄
kí nīn sūm̀maan.
Nimbi bin tūǹ nsaraafan pu tundee,
nín̄ yáliŋkímaan!
Nimbi bin sá m-Nimbɔtiu tɔntɔnliibee,
dūmaan kutuku kí pèen̄ kutaa ń wúntí.
Di sá yii baa ti cāabìń tijimpin
nì ndamam saraau ni-Nimbɔtiu diikun.
14Bɔ́ntímaan ni-ba kí bóob́ kinyɔkɔ,
yíiḿmaan binib bí kóoǹ kí kpāfì.
Ní kóom̀maan bitindaŋkpilib
nì bin kɔkɔ kóò Juuda tiŋkinee
kí kpāfì ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu diikun,
ní kí kúuǹ kí yíiń ti-Dindaan.
Ti-Dindaan wiiŋŋu dal
15Óooo! Ba wiiŋŋu ŋúǹ bulifi dee!
Ti-Dindaan wiiŋŋuee tóobiń.
Ŋu dòoń kí nàan̄ tikɔkɔ,
ŋu làá nyānní Mpɔŋkɔdaan cee ní kí dāan̄.
16An kaa sá ti-nimbilaaliyin ní tijin wáŋkì,
ní mmɔn nì dipɔɔpindi
yíkì ti-Nimbɔtiu diikunaaa?
17Iwambool in bi búĺee dōoǹ kitiŋin ki sūū.
Cakalaabi poon kūń,
adiin ŋin poon bi kpáafí tijinee lítì,
di sá yii bilee kaa ti bí.
18Pīlifìmaan tiwaŋkuti nín bí ki yáliŋkí puee!
Inaa kaa ti nyí laakin pú i làá túĺee,
di sá yii timool kaa ti bí í ŋmɔ́.
Ipii gba bíi jīǹ falaa.
Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu bíi mèé
19M-Dindaan, sii ní m kūuntí ki yíì!
Di sá yii ŋŋmi wùn̄ kuteeu pu mooti,
aŋmilimbil wùn̄ kusaau sufii kɔkɔ.
20Ipeel gba fèefī ki nyàab̀-si,
di sá yii ibun fóotì.
Ŋŋmi wùn̄ kuteeu pu mooti.

english_text:
Locusts and an Enemy Army
1Sound the trumpet on Zion,
the Lord's sacred hill.
Warn everyone to tremble!
The judgment day of the Lord
is coming soon.
2It will be dark and gloomy
with storm clouds overhead.
Troops will cover the mountains
like thunderclouds.
No army this powerful
has ever been gathered before
or will be gathered again.
3Fiery flames surround them;
no one escapes.
Before they invaded,
the land was like Eden;
now only a desert remains.
4 They look like horses
and charge like cavalry.
5They roar over mountains
like noisy chariots,
or a mighty army
ready for battle.
They are a forest fire
that feasts on straw.
6The very sight of them
is frightening.
7They climb over walls
like warriors;
they march in columns
and never turn aside.
8They charge straight ahead,
without pushing each other;
even arrows and spears
cannot make them retreat.
9They swarm over city walls
and enter our homes;
they crawl in through windows,
just like thieves.
10 They make the earth tremble
and the heavens shake;
the sun and moon turn dark,
and stars stop shining.
11 The Lord God leads this army
of countless troops,
and they obey his commands.
The day of his judgment
is so terrible
that no one can stand it.
The Lord's Invitation
12The Lord said:
It isn't too late.
You can still return to me
with all your heart.
Start crying and mourning!
Go without eating.
13Don't rip your clothes
to show your sorrow.
Instead, turn back to me
with broken hearts.
I am merciful, kind, and caring.
I don't easily lose my temper,
and I don't like to punish.
14I am the Lord your God.
Perhaps I will change my mind
and treat you with mercy.
Then you will be blessed
with enough grain and wine
for offering sacrifices to me.
15Sound the trumpet on Zion!
Call the people together.
Show your sorrow
by going without food.
16 Make sure that everyone
is fit to worship me.
Bring adults, children, babies,
and even bring newlyweds
from their festivities.
17 Tell my servants, the priests,
to cry inside the temple
and to offer this prayer
near the altar:
“Save your people, Lord God!
Don't let foreign nations
make jokes about us.
Don't let them laugh and ask,
‘Where is your God?’ ”
The Lord Will Bless the Land
18The Lord was deeply concerned
about his land
and had pity on his people.
19In answer to their prayers
he said,
“I will give you enough grain,
wine, and olive oil
to satisfy your needs.
No longer will I let you
be insulted by the nations.
20An army attacked from the north,
but I will chase it
into a scorching desert.
There it will rot and stink
from the Dead Sea
to the Mediterranean.”
The Lord works wonders
21and does great things.
So tell the soil to celebrate
22and wild animals
to stop being afraid.
Grasslands are green again;
fruit trees and fig trees
are loaded with fruit.
Grapevines are covered
with grapes.
23People of Zion,
celebrate in honor
of the Lord your God!
He is generous and has sent
the autumn and spring rains
in the proper seasons.
24Grain will cover
your threshing places;
jars will overflow
with wine and olive oil.
The Lord Will Rescue His People
25I, the Lord your God,
will make up for the losses
caused by those swarms
and swarms of locusts
I sent to attack you.
26My people, you will eat
until you are satisfied.
Then you will praise me
for the wonderful things
I have done.
Never again will you
be put to shame.
27Israel, you will know
that I stand at your side.
I am the Lord your God—
there are no other gods.
Never again will you
be put to shame.
The Lord Will Work Wonders
The Lord said:
28 Later, I will give my Spirit
to everyone.
Your sons and daughters
will prophesy.
Your old men
will have dreams,
and your young men
will see visions.
29In those days I will even give
my Spirit to my servants,
both men and women.
30I will work wonders
in the sky above
and on the earth below.
There will be blood and fire
and clouds of smoke.
31 The sun will turn dark,
and the moon
will be as red as blood
before that great
and terrible day
when I appear.
32 Then I, the Lord will save everyone who faithfully worships me. I have promised there will be survivors on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, and among them will be my chosen ones.
translation_text:
Ti-Dindaan wiiŋŋu tóobiń
1Ní búḿmaan dikantándi Siiyɔn tiŋkin,
kúum̀maan mpɔn m-circir jool pu.
Kitiŋee pu nib kɔkɔ wunti ń fáá dijinjikil,
di sá yii ti-Dindaan wiiŋŋu dòoń,
ŋu tóobiń gba.
2Dibɔmbɔŋkpaandi wiiŋŋu dee ŋu-baba,
atagbambɔn nì dipɔ̀ńdi wiiŋŋu dee.
Inaaki janjakitil dòoń.
I pɔ̄ɔ̄ ní ki wīikí bɔ̀m,
a lì kii kunyeeu di mɔ́ ki bīiǹ ajoon puee.
Baa láá pée ká míǹ ki ká
ní ki pée gíti kpá kí ká míǹ jaanjaan
kí nīn cáá cá abin abin.
3I-nyɔkɔpuee, ŋŋmi di wù,
ní i-boon púee, aŋmilimbil nàantí.
Kí wàatī í jītée,
kitiŋ nìn sɔ̀m̀ kii Eedeen kpaabuee ní,
ama i nín jítì ki dóòyee,
an kpántì kii kuteeuee.
Tiba nì tiba kaa ŋūǹ kí ŋmátí kí nyā i-ŋaan.
4I yaa páaǹnée, a lì kii itaamuee ní,
ní i sáń kii bitanjakaliibee.
5I gà kuwoou kii janjatɔrɔkub
di dàb̀ ki póotí ajoonee,
a lì kii ŋŋmi di yaa wù timool,
an pòol̄ puee.
I dòoń kii dijanjakitil din pɔ̄ɔ̄
ki tātìi gbāaǹ dikɔ̀ndi puee.
6I yaa páaǹnée, anibul kɔkɔ kóò dinyoondin ní,
ní ŋi-nimbiiŋyi ń cúú kpántí.
7I sáń kii bibaatandambee,
ní ki dàb̀ agun kii bijanjaliibee.
Báà ŋma pée túĺ u-saŋŋu ní cáaa ki cá,
kaa kpèetī kí dī laaba pú.
8Ubɔ kaa pìkil̄ u-juti,
di sá yii báà ŋma tàkā u-saŋŋu ní.
Laakin aganlaka bée, niin ní bi cátí bi-saŋyi,
ní tiba kaa ŋūǹ kí cúú-bi kí síiń.
9I gbáb̀ kí bìin̄ kitiŋ pu,
ki tɔ̄kɔntí digundi din bi máń ki tú kitiŋee pu ki sáń,
ní ki dìŋfī tɔkɔlabin
ki kóò adiinni kii unaayuuyee.
10I yaa bāańee, kitiŋ cìŋkī ní,
ní an bí kii kutagbɔŋu làá kìtī kí lítée.
Uŋmal nì ŋwìiń kpántí dibɔmbɔndi,
ní iŋmalbijaa kaa ti wāĺ.
11Ti-Dindaan līī u-janjakitil nyɔkɔpu ki téeń.
U-janjakitiŋ ŋin tɔ́ u-marabee
wīikí tikpil ní ki pɔ̄ɔ̄.
Di sá yii ti-Dindaan wiiŋŋu dal sá ŋwiŋkpaan ní,
ŋwiinee nyāŋkì ní ŋma di dāa ŋūǹ kí ŋmátí?
Tí fàtīí gítiḿmaan ti-Dindaan cee
12Ti-Dindaan bí yii:
«Ŋyunti bāań ní fàtīí gítiń m-cee
nì ni-pɔbil kɔkɔ.
Bóob́maan kinyɔkɔ, kí sɔ̄maan
ní kí gbàam̀-mi.
13An kaa sá ni-wampeeŋkaati ní ní cátí,
ama an sá ni-pɔbiliŋ ní ní kpántí.»
Fàtīí gítiḿmaan ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu cee.
U sá ulaŋŋaŋfiti ní u-poon mɔ̄,
waa gífí diŋuul malaa, ama ní u-ŋanti wīikí tikpil,
ní ki bɔ́ntì kí yàntī ditafadaaldi din pu u sòon̄ee.
14An yaa yíì, u ŋūǹ kí kpántí u-landɔkɔŋu
ní kí bìin̄ ni-pu.
Niinee, ni dāa ŋūǹ kí cáań tijimpin
nì ndaam saraau kí tīī ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu.
Tí bóob́ kinyɔkɔ kí gbàam̀ Unimbɔti
15Búḿmaan dikantándi Siiyɔn tiŋkin,
bóob́maan kinyɔkɔ.
Yíiḿmaan dikpafikpaandi.
16Yíiḿmaan samaa kɔkɔ
bí kpāfì circir kpafil.
Kpāfìmaan bitikpilib nì binipɔmbi,
kí kpáaǹ mbipɔmu mun ŋáaḿee.
Unimpucaan nì u-cal ń nyānní kunimpucandiin.
17Ti-Dindaan tɔntɔnliibi bisaraaŋaliibi
ń yūĺ kunimbɔtidiin
kipunyɔkɔ nì nsaraafan kansikin kí nīn sūǹ.
Bí nīn lì yii:
«Ti-Dindaan, sɔ̄ timbi a-nibul saai.
Taa yàntī icoo ń cúú a-nibooliŋu.
Taa yàntī anibul ŋin kíǹee
ń nīn bèel̄-ti ki lì yii:
<Bi-Nimbɔtiuee bí là?>»
Ti-Dindaan fōō u-nibul wimmeem
18Ti-Dindaan cáá u-tiŋki pu dineeŋkpaandi,
u súń u-nibul saai.
19U fōō u-nibul wimmeem ki bí-bi yii:
«Too, m làá tīī-ni tijin nì ndamam nì ŋkpam.
Ni làá dāá jī kí díkí.
Kí yòon̄ díǹ kí nīn cée,
maa ti làá dū-ni kí líiǹ
atimbun ŋin kíǹee ŋí nīn bèel̄-ni.
20M làá jà ni-nannanliibi bin nyánní ŋgan pú puee
kí cùnnì kuteeu pu laakin kūńee.
M làá jà bin līī nyɔkɔpuee
kí tɔ̄ Ŋyaam mɔɔl poon,
ní kí jà bin kíǹ ki pá boonee
kí tɔ̄ Meediiteeranee tiŋkuun.
Niin ní bijanjaliibi bin kpíìyee
làá sūū kí nūukì,
di sá yii bi ŋá-ni inikpiti tikpil.
21Sii kitiŋ, taa fàŋkì!
Yàntī án nīn mɔ̄ǹ-si á nīn fàal̀,
di sá yii ti-Dindaan túń atuŋkpaan.
22Ipeel, ní taa fàŋkìmaan.
Kuteeu pu mooti bíi túkù ki sɔ̀m̀ fílfil.
Isufi bíi lòoǹ,
ní fiigi nì fiinyi sufii mun lòon̄ sàka saka.
23Nín̄ bímaan mmɔnni, Siiyɔn yab,
nín̄ fàal̀maan ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu pu,
di sá yii u tīī-ni ukpaasiitaa kí fīī-ni.
U yāntì ukpaasiitaa nì useetaa
nìn̄ tiŋan kii dooooyee.
24Tijimpin gbí dinaapaal pu,
ní ndamam nì ŋkpam gbí tilɔn ki féeń.
25M làá fàtīí téeǹ-ni ni-kpaajinti
tin ní anaakitɔmbil nì inaakitoon
nì inaakicaan nì inaaki dūu ŋmɔ́ee.
Man di nìn dū dijanjakitil gbanti ki tɔ́ ni-pu.
26Ni làá jī kí díkí,
ní kí nyɔ̄ŋkì man ni-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu
un di túń atunnyaan ki tīī-nee.
Icoo pée gíti kpá kí jī m-nibul jaanjaan.
27Niin ní nimbi Isirayeel yab làá béé yii
m bí ni-kansikin.
Man di sá ni-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu,
ní maa cáá juti.
Icoo pée gíti kpá kí jī m-nibul jaanjaan.»

english_text:
The Lord Will Judge the Nations
1At that time I, the Lord, will make Judah and Jerusalem prosperous again. 2Then in Judgment Valley I will bring together the nations that scattered my people Israel everywhere in the world, and I will bring charges against those nations. They divided up my land 3and gambled to see who would get my people; they sold boys and girls to pay for prostitutes and wine.
4 You people of Tyre and Sidon and you Philistines, why are you doing this? Are you trying to get even with me? I'll strike back before you know what's happened. 5You've taken my prized possessions, including my silver and gold, and carried them off to your temples. 6You have dragged the people of Judah and Jerusalem from their land and sold them to the Greeks.
7But I'll make the people of Judah determined to come home, and what happened to them will happen to you. 8I'll hand over your sons and daughters to the people of Judah, and they will sell them to the Sabeans, who live far away. I, the Lord, have spoken!
Judgment in Judgment Valley
9Say to the nations:
“Get ready for war!
Be eager to fight.
Line up for battle
and prepare to attack.
10 Make swords out of plows
and spears out of garden tools.
Strengthen every weakling.”
11Hurry, all you nations!
Come quickly.
Ask the Lord to bring
his warriors along.
12You must come now
to Judgment Valley,
where the Lord will judge
the surrounding nations.
13 They are a field of ripe crops.
Bring in the harvest!
They are grapes piled high.
Start trampling them now!
If our enemy's sins were wine,
every jar would overflow.
14Crowds fill Decision Valley.
The judgment day of the Lord
will soon be here—
15no light from the sun or moon,
and stars no longer shine.
16 From the heart of Jerusalem
the Lord roars like a lion,
shaking the earth and sky.
But the Lord is a fortress,
a place of safety
for his people Israel.
God Will Bless His People
17I am the Lord your God.
And you will know I live on Zion,
my sacred hill,
because Jerusalem will be sacred,
untouched by foreign troops.
18On that day, fruitful vineyards
will cover the mountains.
And your cattle and goats
that graze on the hills
will produce a lot of milk.
Streams in Judah
will never run dry;
a stream from my house
will flow in Acacia Valley.
19Egypt and Edom were cruel
and brutal to Judah,
without a reason.
Now their countries will become
a barren desert,
20but Judah and Jerusalem
will always have people.
21I, the Lord, live on Mount Zion.
I will punish the guilty
and defend the innocent.
translation_text:
Ti-Dindaan Fam làá kpákatiń
1Míǹ boonee,
m làá dāá yàntī m-Fam
ń kpákatiń unil sá kamaa pu.
Ni-jipɔmbi nì ni-bisalib làá dāá kpántí m-bɔnaatiliibi.
M làá dāá sòoǹ nì ni-jaŋkpilib tidamintiil poon,
ní kí dāá lēē m-bɔti kí dàkà ni-nipɔmbi.
2M làá dāá yàntī m-Fam ń kpákatiń
kí kpáaǹ iyumbu bininjab nì binimpoobi pu.
3M làá dāá yàntī maamaacikpaambi ń nyā
kutagbɔŋu nì kitiŋ pu.
Fatiku nì ŋŋmi nì nnyiim tagbaŋŋi
làá dāá nyā.
4Ŋwìiń dāa kpántí dibɔmbɔndi
ní uŋmal ń dāá mántí kii fatikuee,
kí wàatī ní ti-Dindaan wiiŋŋu ń nín bàń.
Dinyoondi nì ŋwiŋkpaan dal dee ŋu-baba.
5Niinee, un kamaa yaa láa kúuǹ ki yíiń
ti-Dindaan yindee dāa kāntí difiil.
Di sá yii Siiyɔn jool pu, Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee,
biba làá dāá ŋmátí kí nyā nnaabu gbantin,
kii ti-Dindaan nín lī puee.
An dāa sá bin ní ti-Dindaan dāa yíińee ní.

english_text:
1 I am Amos. And I raised sheep near the town of Tekoa when Uzziah was king of Judah and Jeroboam son of Jehoash was king of Israel.
Two years before the earthquake, the Lord gave me several messages about Israel, 2 and I said:
When the Lord roars
from Jerusalem,
pasturelands and Mount Carmel
dry up and turn brown.
Judgment on Syria
3 The Lord said:
I will punish Syria
for countless crimes,
and I won't change my mind.
They dragged logs with spikes
over the people of Gilead.
4Now I will burn down the palaces
and fortresses of King Hazael
and of King Benhadad.
5I will break through
the gates of Damascus.
I will destroy the people
of Wicked Valley
and the ruler of Beth-Eden.
Then the Syrians will be dragged
as prisoners to Kir.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
Judgment on Philistia
6 The Lord said:
I will punish Philistia
for countless crimes,
and I won't change my mind.
They dragged off my people
from town after town
to sell them as slaves
to the Edomites.
7That's why I will burn down
the walls and fortresses
of the city of Gaza.
8I will destroy the king of Ashdod
and the ruler of Ashkelon.
I will strike down Ekron,
and that will be the end
of the Philistines.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
Judgment on Phoenicia
9 The Lord said:
I will punish Phoenicia
for countless crimes,
and I won't change my mind.
They broke their treaty
and dragged off my people
from town after town
to sell them as slaves
to the Edomites.
10That's why I will send flames
to burn down the city of Tyre
along with its fortresses.
Judgment on Edom
11 The Lord said:
I will punish Edom
for countless crimes,
and I won't change my mind.
They killed their own relatives
and were so terribly furious
that they showed no mercy.
12Now I will send fire to wipe out
the fortresses of Teman
and Bozrah.
Judgment on Ammon
13 The Lord said:
I will punish Ammon
for countless crimes,
and I won't change my mind.
In Gilead they ripped open
pregnant women,
just to take the land.
14Now I will send fire to destroy
the walls and fortresses
of Rabbah.
Enemies will shout and attack
like a whirlwind.
15Ammon's king and leaders
will be dragged away.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_text:
1Tibɔti tin Amoosi upikpaal un sá Teekoowa tiŋkinee sòon̄ee sɔ̀. Abin ali kí wàatī kitiŋ ń cìŋkèe, ti-Dindaan nìn lēē tin u làá sòoǹ Isirayeel beel puee bɔti ki dàkā-u. Ŋyunti gbantee, Oosiyasi di nìn sá Juuda tiŋki bɔtiu ní Joowaasi jipɔɔn Jeerooboowaam nìn sá Isirayeel tiŋki bɔtiu. 2Amoosi nìn lī yii:
«Ti-Dindaan téeń mpɔn doooo Siiyɔn jool pu,
u yāntì bi gbìl̄ u-nyɔkɔ pu doooo Jeerusaleem.
Niinee kupikpaau mooti fáaḿ,
ní Kaarmeel jool pu mooti kūń.»
Ti-Dindaan wòon̄ Isirayeel yab nì abee ŋin pìlīǹ-bee
Siirii yab
3Ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé:
«Damaasi yab ŋá ikpiti tikpil,
bi gíti ŋá an jítì mara pu.
An puee m nín pée síiǹ kí ŋá puee,
míǹ ní m làá ŋá.
Bi dū apinjal ŋin inaa dátí ki kpátí atannaapikee
ki nàn̄ Galaadi yab.
4An puee m làá sēē Asayeel beecindi ŋŋmi,
Been-Adaadi beecindi làá wà kí lítí.
5M làá wīī Damaasi tiŋki punyɔkɔki kpàlkaati.
M làá kúntí ikpiti tantakal tiŋki bɔtiu,
nì un kā mmɔn tiŋki pu dibeelee,
ní kí yàntī bí cúú Aram yab
kí cùnnì Kiiri tiŋkin kuyuŋu.»
Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.
Fiiliistii yab
6Ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé:
«Gaasaa yab ŋá ikpiti tikpil,
bi gíti ŋá an jítì mara pu.
An puee m nín pée síiǹ kí ŋá puee, míǹ ní m làá ŋá.
Bi cáá ditimbummɔndi nib
ki nyáfiǹ Eedoom tiŋkin yab.
7M làá sēē Gaasaa tiŋki gundi ŋŋmi,
ní ki-beeciŋŋi ń wà kí lítí.
8M làá kúntí Asidoodi tiŋki bɔtiu,
nì un sá Asikeelɔn tiŋki bɔtiuee.
M làá dū m-ba kí bíití Eekrɔn yab,
kí yàntī Fiiliistii yab ń kúntí.»
Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti di lī míǹ.
Tiir yab
9Ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé:
«Tiir yab ŋá ikpiti tikpil,
bi gíti ŋá an jítì mara pu.
An puee m nín pée síiǹ kí ŋá puee,
míǹ ní m làá ŋá.
Bi cáá ditimbummɔndi nib
ki nyáfiǹ Eedoom tiŋki yab,
kun puee baa dū kunabitiiu
poondi ki yíiń tiba.
10M làá sēē Tiir tiŋki ŋŋmi,
ní ki-beeciŋŋi ń wà kí lítí.»
Eedoom yab
11Ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé:
«Eedoom yab ŋá ikpiti tikpil,
bi gíti ŋá an jítì mara pu.
An puee m nín pée síiǹ kí ŋá puee,
míǹ ní m làá ŋá.
Bi kùl̄ ki bīiǹ bi-nabiyaamu
Isirayeel yab boon nì ntàataajimu.
Baa pée súń bi-saai báà fiii.
Bi fōō mbum an kaa kúntí,
bi-ŋuul kaa cáá yii an sɔ̄ŋkì.
12M làá sēē Teeman tiŋki ŋŋmi,
ní Bɔsiraa beeciŋŋi ń wà kí lítí.»
Amɔn yab
13Ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé:
«Amɔn yab ŋá ikpiti tikpil,
bi gíti ŋá an jítì mara pu.
An puee m nín pée síiǹ kí ŋá puee,
míǹ ní m làá ŋá.
Kun puee bi pūtì Galaadi tiŋkin pɔdambi
kí ŋmā kí wàan̄ bi-tiŋki.
14M làá sēē Raaba tiŋki gundi ŋŋmi,
ní ki-beeciŋŋi ń wà kí lítí.
An dāa sá ikuŋkuunti nì kujaau wiiŋŋu dal,
utaa nì kubuŋkpaaŋŋu kun pɔ̄ɔ̄yee wiiŋŋu ní.
15Bi làá dāá cúú bi-bɔtiu,
kí kpáaǹ u-kàliŋkpilib kí cùnnì kuyuŋu.»
Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_text:
Judgment on Moab
1 The Lord said:
I will punish Moab
for countless crimes,
and I won't change my mind.
They made lime from the bones
of the king of Edom.
2Now I will send fire to destroy
the fortresses of Kerioth.
Battle shouts and trumpet blasts
will be heard as I destroy Moab
3with its king and leaders.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
Judgment on Judah
4The Lord said:
I will punish Judah
for countless crimes,
and I won't change my mind.
They have rejected my teachings
and refused to obey me.
They were led astray
by the same false gods
their ancestors worshiped.
5Now I will send fire on Judah
and destroy the fortresses
of Jerusalem.
Judgment on Israel
6The Lord said:
I will punish Israel
for countless crimes,
and I won't change my mind.
They sell honest people for money,
and the needy are sold
for the price of sandals.
7They smear the poor in the dirt
and push aside
those who are helpless.
My holy name is dishonored,
because fathers and sons sleep
with the same young women.
8They lie down beside altars
on clothes taken
as security for loans.
And they drink wine in my temple,
wine bought with the money
they received from fines.
9 Israel, the Amorites were there
when you entered Canaan.
They were tall as cedars
and strong as oaks.
But I wiped them out—
I destroyed their branches
and their roots.
10I had rescued you from Egypt,
and for forty years I had led you
through the desert.
Then I gave you the land
of the Amorites.
11 I chose some of you
to be prophets
and others to be Nazirites.
People of Israel,
you know this is true.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
12But you commanded the prophets
not to speak their message,
and you pressured the Nazirites
into drinking wine.
13And so I will crush you,
just as a wagon full of grain
crushes the ground.
14No matter how fast you run,
you won't escape.
No matter how strong you are,
you will lose your strength
and your life.
15Even if you are an expert
with a bow and arrow,
you will retreat.
And you won't get away alive,
not even if you run fast
or ride a horse.
16You may be brave and strong,
but you will run away,
stripped naked.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_text:
Moowaab yab
1Ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé:
«Moowaab yab ŋá ikpiti tikpil,
bi gíti ŋá an jítì mara pu.
An puee m nín pée síiǹ kí ŋá puee,
míǹ ní m làá ŋá.
Bi wùn̄ Eedoom bɔtiu kpabiŋ
an kpántì ŋfantam.
2M làá sēē Moowaab tiŋki ŋŋmi,
ní Keeriyooti beeciŋŋi ń wà kí lítí.
Moowaab yab làá kpú
kuwookpaaŋŋu nì ijanjakuŋkuunti
nì iyin dibúndi poon.
3M làá kpɔ̀ bi-bɔtiu,
kí kpáaǹ u-kàliŋkpilib dicilpu.»
Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.
Juuda yab
4Ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé:
«Juuda yab ŋá ikpiti tikpil,
bi gíti ŋá an jítì mara pu.
An puee m nín pée síiǹ kí ŋá puee,
míǹ ní m làá ŋá.
Bi fá m-marab,
kaa nóó m-koobiliŋ.
Kii bi-naanjab nín nìn nóó awaa
ŋi kíil̀-bi puee,
míǹ ní bi yāntì awaa gbanti mun kíil̀-bi.
5M làá sēē Juuda tiŋki ŋŋmi,
Jeerusaleem beeciŋŋi làá wà kí lítí.»
Isirayeel yab
6Ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé:
«Isirayeel yab ŋá ikpiti tikpil,
bi gíti ŋá an jítì mara pu.
An puee m nín pée síiǹ kí ŋá puee,
míǹ ní m làá ŋá.
Bi nyáfí deedeedaan kí ká animbil,
ki nyáfí usoodaan kalaa nimbiliŋ
7Bi nyìitī uwɔfi yil ki gùl̀ ntamin,
kaa sòoǹ unandaan bɔti deedee.
Unil nì u-jipɔɔn kpáfí usapɔɔn pu,
ki ŋáań míǹ ki bíiĺ man circir yindi.
8Ipaan in kɔkɔ pu bi jáaḿ Unimbɔtee,
abɔkuti ŋin bi fōol̀ toolima
bisoodambi ceeyee pu ní bi dɔ̀,
ki nyù ndaam min bi fìkēe
bi-Nimbɔtiu diikun.
9Ama bi-puee m nìn kúntì Amɔɔr yab.
Binib gbanti nìn kpílifì ní ki yáà
kii seedir nì seeni sufiiyee.
M kúntì bi-kɔkɔ pílpil.
10Man di nyántìń-ni Eejipiti tiŋkin,
ki kpōotì-ni abin imuŋku ili kuteeun
ní ŋmā kí fōō Amɔɔr yab tiŋki.
11M lēē ni-jipɔmbi biba bí nīn sá m-bɔnaatiliibi,
ki lēē ni-naacimpɔmbi biba bí dū bi-ba kí sú-mi.
An kaa sá mimmaaa, Isirayeel yab?»
Ti-Dindaan di sòon̄ míǹ.
12Ama ni nyūntì bin dū bi-ba ki sú-mee ndaam,
ki pīiǹ m-bɔnaatiliibi nsan yii
bí taa ti nàatī m-bɔti.
13«An puee m làá tāā kí mátí-ni,
kii tɔrɔku un tú tiwan tikpilee
nín tà ki mátí tin kɔkɔ dɔ̄ u-saŋŋu pu puee ní.
14Binib bin yáb̀ee
kaa làá dāá ŋmā kí sāǹ kí ŋmátí,
bipɔɔbi pɔŋŋu kaa làá kèetī-bi,
bijanjamɔntiibi kaa làá dāá ŋmā kí fīī bi-maŋfal.
15Upintɔl kaa làá dāá ŋmā kí yūĺ kí tɔ̄.
Un ŋūǹ ki sáńee kaa làá dāá ŋmā
kí sāǹ kí ŋmátí.
Utanjakal kaa làá dāá ŋmā kí fīī u-maŋfal.
16Ujanjal un cáá dibaatandee
làá dāá dū u-janjawanti kí fá,
kí sāǹ kí kátí ŋwiin gbanti».
Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_text:
1People of Israel,
I rescued you from Egypt.
Now listen to my judgment
against you.
2Of all nations on earth,
you are the only one
I have chosen.
That's why I will punish you
because of your sins.
The Work of a Prophet
3Can two people walk together
without agreeing to meet?
4Does a lion roar in the forest
unless it has caught
a victim?
Does it growl in its den
unless it is eating?
5How can anyone catch a bird
without using a net?
Does a trap spring shut
unless something is caught?
6Isn't the whole city frightened
when the trumpet
signals an attack?
Isn't the Lord the one who brings
disaster on a city?
7Whatever the Lord God
plans to do,
he tells his servants,
the prophets.
8Everyone is terrified
when a lion roars—
and ordinary people
become prophets
when the Lord God speaks.
Samaria Is Doomed
9Here is a message
for the leaders
of Philistia and Egypt—
tell everyone to come together
on the hills of Samaria.
Let them see the injustice
and the lawlessness
in that city.
10The Lord has said
that they don't even know how
to do right.
They have become rich
from violence and robbery.
11And so the Lord God has sworn
that they will be surrounded.
Enemies will break through
their defenses
and steal their treasures.
12The Lord has promised
that only a few from Samaria
will escape with their lives
and with some broken pieces
of their beds and couches.
It will be like when a shepherd
rescues two leg bones
and part of a sheep's ear
from the jaws of a lion.
The Altars at Bethel
13The Lord God All-Powerful
told me to speak this message
against Jacob's descendants:
14 When I, the Lord, punish Israel
for their sins,
I will destroy the altars
at Bethel.
Even the corners of the altar
will be left in the dirt.
15I will tear down winter homes
and summer homes.
Houses decorated with ivory
and all other mansions
will be gone forever.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_text:
Unimbɔti làá dáaĺ u-nibul tafal
1Isirayeel yab, nimbi bin di sá kudicaŋu kun ti-Dindaan nyántìń Eejipiti tiŋkinee, pīlifìmaan tin ti-Dindaan cáá kí sòoǹ ni-puee.
2«Kitiŋ pu dicaŋŋi kɔkɔ poonee,
nimbi baba ní m lēē ki kpèé.
An pu ní m làá dáaĺ ni-tafal
ikpiti in kɔkɔ ni ŋáaǹee pu.»
Unimbɔti yaa sòon̄ee, u-bɔnaatiliu kaa ŋūǹ kí nīn ŋmí
3Binib bili cá nsan
kaa kpáfì ki sòon̄ ki bɔ́ntàaa?
4Gbikinti yaa kaa ká upeel kí cúú,
u làá nīn sūǹ kupɔɔun fámaaa?
Kigbikintibiki yaa kaa cúú tiba,
kì làá nīn bí ki-kɔŋkooŋŋun ki mùuǹaaa?
5Kutaliŋŋu sàtī unoon fám
baa dū tiba kí píĺaaa?
Kutaliŋŋu mun tòó fám
kaa pée sàl̄ báà tibaaa?
6Bi búǹ dibaŋwul kitiŋin
tifaandi kaa cútí binibaaa?
Dinimbinaamandi kóòń kitiŋin
kaa nyánní ti-Dindaan ceeee?
7Míǹ mbaantiim ní ti-Dindaan kaa ŋáań tiba kaa lēē ki dàkā u-tɔntɔnliibi bibɔnaatiliibi.
8Gbikinti yaa téeńee,
ŋma sá-u ní kaa làá fàŋkì?
Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti yaa sòon̄ee,
ŋma làá yíí kaa làá nàatī?
Samaarii bɔsooŋyi
9Asidoodi tiŋki beeciŋŋi yilpu
nì Eejipiti tiŋki beeciŋŋi yilpuee,
ní bāakìmaan kí lì yii:
«Kóoǹ kí kpāfìmaan Samaarii jooŋŋi pu
kí kpèè fìkil fikil un bí kitiŋ gbantinee,
nì tipɔmbɔti tin ŋáań ki-nee!»
10Ti-Dindaan di lī yii:
«Samaarii yab kaa nyí kí tɔ̄ ditummɔntiil.
Tiwaŋfìkikaal nì tinaayuwan
ní bi kùl̄ ki gbéeǹ bi-dimɔntiŋ poon.»
11An pu ní ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti
sòon̄ sii Samaarii tiŋki pu ki lī yii:
«Unannanli làá dāá màntīí tū a-tiŋki,
kí gbākal̀ a-pɔŋŋu
ní kí fūkul̀ a-dimɔntiŋ wanti.»
Difiil nín bí la dee?
12Ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé:
«Gbikinti yaa cúú upiiyee,
upikpaal dátí ayaka ali nì kitafakatii
ní kí fōō u-nyɔkɔn.
Míǹ mbaantiim ní bi làá dāá fīī
Isirayeel yab bin kóò Samaarii tiŋkin,
ki dɔ̄ dijal pu àá ndoo puee.»
Ti-Dindaan kpáafì Isirayeel yab
13Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti,
Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé:
«Ní pīlifìmaan kí dū tibɔkpaafikaal nee
kí nàatī Jaakɔb naantiibi.
14Ŋwiin ŋun m làá dāá dáaĺ
Isirayeel yab tafal bi-kpitii puee,
m làá dāá gbá kí wìil̀ isaraafan
in bí Beeteel tiŋkinee kɔkɔ.
M làá dāá gbá kí kéetí nsaraafan yiŋyi
ní í nīn kíǹ ki dɔ̄ kitiŋ.
15M làá dāá wìil̀ bi-dikpaaŋŋi,
nì bi-diwaammu.
M làá dāá wìil̀ adiin ŋin pu bi nákáǹ akuntinyin
ki nyáantì-ŋee,
adikpaan kɔkɔ làá dāá lítí.»
Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ!

english_text:
The Women of Samaria
The Lord said:
1You women of Samaria
are fat cows!
You mistreat and abuse
the poor and needy,
then you say to your husbands,
“Bring us more drinks!”
2I, the Lord God, have sworn
by my own name
that your time is coming.
Not one of you will be left—
you will be taken away
by sharp hooks.
3You will be dragged through holes
in your city walls,
and you will be thrown
toward Harmon.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
Israel Refuses To Obey
The Lord said:
4Come to Bethel and Gilgal.
Sin all you want!
Offer sacrifices the next morning
and bring a tenth of your crops
on the third day.
5Bring offerings to show me
how thankful you are.
Gladly bring more offerings
than I have demanded.
You really love to do this.
I, the Lord God, have spoken!
How the Lord Warned Israel
6 I, the Lord, took away the food
from every town and village,
but still you rejected me.
7Three months before harvest,
I kept back the rain.
Sometimes I would let it fall
on one town or field
but not on another,
and pastures dried up.
8People from two or three towns
would go to a town
that still had water,
but it wasn't enough.
Even then you rejected me.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
9I dried up your grain fields;
your gardens and vineyards
turned brown.
Locusts ate your fig trees
and olive orchards,
but even then you rejected me.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
10I did terrible things to you,
just as I did to Egypt—
I killed your young men in war;
I let your horses be stolen,
and I made your camp stink
with dead bodies.
Even then you rejected me.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
11 I destroyed many of you,
just as I did the cities
of Sodom and Gomorrah.
You were a burning stick
I rescued from the fire.
But even then you rejected me.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
12Now, Israel, I myself
will deal with you.
Get ready to face your God!
13I created the mountains
and the wind.
I let humans know
what I am thinking.
I bring darkness at dawn
and step over hills.
I am the Lord God All-Powerful!
translation_text:
1Nimbi Samaarii yab nimpoobi,
nimbi bin jíń ki gbīfiǹ kii
Baasan tiŋkin nasaliiyee,
ní pīlifìmaan tibɔti nee.
Ni mùul̄ biwɔfib,
ki sàantí binandambi
ní ki lì ni-calib yii:
«Ní cáań ndaam tí nyɔ̀!»
2Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti un bí circiree,
pūtì ki lī yii:
«Ŋwiin bí ki dòoń,
bi làá dāá dū ipiin kí lɔ̀kɔ̄-ni,
kí dáaĺ-ni kí kpáàá búntí
kii njɔmpiin nín cútí ujɔm puee ní.
3Kitiŋ guŋŋi laakin bátì bátìi lítèe
ní bi làá dī kí cáá-ni kí nyāntí,
báà ŋma ń nīn kpèé u-nimbiin.
Bi làá dāá cáá-ni kí tɔ̄ ŋgan pú.»
Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ!
Inyimɔn nimbɔtinool
4«Ní cùmaan Beeteel tiŋkin
kí já nì mi,
kí cù Giilgaal tiŋkin
kí mɔ̀tīí já nì mi tikpil.
Ni yaa bàn̄ kutaafaauee,
ní cáań kuwaŋkuluu kí ŋá-mi saraa,
ní ŋwintataatee ní cáań ni-saalaatiiti.
5Ní wà kpɔnɔb bin bi ŋá ŋkpɔnɔnyɔkɔee
nsaraafan pu kí ŋá ijaam saraabi.
Ní bāakì kí tùkù báà ŋma
nlammɔntiim saraabi bin ni ŋá ki tīī-mee,
kun puee nimbi Isirayeel yab nín là puee dee!»
Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti di lī míǹ.
Ti-Dindaan kpáafì Isirayeel yab ki gīī
6«Ni-tiŋkpaammu kɔkɔnee,
m yāntì ŋkùm cúú-ni,
ki ŋmīntì-ni tijin ni-timbilimmun,
ama ní naa fātìi gítìń m-cee.»
Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.
7«Maa yāntì utaa jōō ni-satin
ki tin sāā iŋmal ita kudiceeu ń bàń.
M yāntì utaa nìn̄ kitiŋ kiban
kaa yāntì u nìn̄ kin kíǹee poon,
ki yāntì utaa nìn̄ bukpaa bubɔn,
ní bun ni u nìn̄ee kpaajinti kūń.»
8«Ntimu tikpil nib
yíkì ki cūtì kitiŋ kiban ki kpìntī
ki nyàab̀ nnyim kí nyɔ̀,
ama kaa ká ki nyùn̄ ki bál̀,
nì míǹ kɔkɔee, naa fātìi gítìń m-cee.»
Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.
9«M dū iween ki tɔ́ ni-kpaajinti,
di sá tì dáá yú tisatin kaa láá bīń
ní ki bíi kōō àá ki bíi sù.
M yāntì inaakitoon ŋmɔ́ ki bíil̀
ni-kuŋfaati nì fiinyi sufii kpaaŋŋi,
nì ni-fiigi sufii nì ni-ɔliifi sufii,
ama ní naa fātìi gítìń m-cee.»
Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.
10«M dū bìlbil kúm ki tɔ́ ni-waŋkuti pu
kii m nín nìn ŋá pu Eejipiti tiŋkinee.
M yāntì binannanliibi kūū ni-nipɔmbi,
ki cútì ni-taamui ki cáa búntì.
M yāntì ni-nikpiliŋ sūū ki núukì
ki kɔ́-ni fíŋfiŋ ni-naapaal pu,
ama ní naa fātìi gítìń m-cee.»
Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.
11«M nāaǹ ni-kansikin biba,
a lì kii m nín nìn nāaǹ
Soodoom nì Goomoora timmu puee.
Ni-kansikin bin ŋmátèe sá kii
kisanteei kin bi tātèe ní,
ama ní naa fātìi gítìń m-cee.»
Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.
12«An puee Isirayeel,
kpèè m nín làá ŋá-si puee sɔ̀.
Kii tin m làá ŋá-see puee,
á bɔ́ntí a-ba kí cīití man a-Nimbɔtiu.»
13Di sá yii úǹ di náań ajoon,
ki náań kubuŋu,
ki lèekī tin u làá ŋée ki dàkà unil.
U dù ŋwiimpu kí kpántí kunyeeu
ní ki tɔ́kɔ́ kitiŋ kɔkɔ yilpu ki còom̄.
Úǹ ní bi yíì yii: <Ti-Dindaan,
Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan>.

english_text:
Turn Back to the Lord
1Listen, nation of Israel,
to my mournful message:
2You, dearest Israel, have fallen,
never to rise again—
you lie deserted in your own land,
with no one to help you up.
3The Lord God has warned,
“From every ten soldiers
only one will be left;
from a thousand troops,
only a hundred will survive.”
4The Lord keeps saying,
“Israel, turn back to me
and you will live!
5Don't go to Gilgal or Bethel
or even to Beersheba.
Gilgal will be dragged away,
and Bethel will end up
as nothing.”
6Turn back to the Lord,
you descendants of Joseph,
and you will live.
If you don't, the Lord
will attack like fire.
Bethel will burn to the ground,
and no one can save it.
7You people are doomed!
You twist the truth
and trample on justice.
8 But the Lord created the stars
and put them in place.
He turns darkness to dawn
and daylight to darkness;
he scoops up the ocean
and empties it on the earth.
9God destroys mighty soldiers
and strong fortresses.
Choose Good Instead of Evil!
The Lord said:
10You people hate judges
and honest witnesses;
11you abuse the poor and demand
heavy taxes from them.
You have built expensive homes,
but you won't enjoy them;
you have planted vineyards,
but you will get no wine.
12I am the Lord, and I know
your terrible sins.
You cheat honest people
and take bribes;
you rob the poor of justice.
13Times are so evil
that anyone with good sense
will keep quiet.
