14If you really want to live,
you must stop doing wrong
and start doing right.
I, the Lord God All-Powerful,
will then be on your side,
just as you claim I am.
15Choose good instead of evil!
See that justice is done.
Maybe I, the Lord All-Powerful,
will be kind to what's left
of your people.
Judgment Is Coming
16This is what the Lord has sworn:
Noisy crying will be heard
in every town and street.
Even farmers will be told
to mourn for the dead,
together with those
who are paid to mourn.
17Your vineyards will be filled
with crying and weeping,
because I will punish you.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
When the Lord Judges
18You look forward to the day
when the Lord comes to judge.
But you are in for trouble!
It won't be a time of sunshine;
all will be darkness.
19You will run from a lion,
only to meet a bear.
You will escape to your house,
rest your hand on the wall,
and be bitten by a snake.
20The day when the Lord judges
will be dark, very dark,
without a ray of light.
What the Lord Demands
21 I, the Lord, hate and despise
your religious celebrations
and your times of worship.
22I won't accept your offerings
or animal sacrifices—
not even your very best.
23No more of your noisy songs!
I won't listen
when you play your harps.
24But let justice and fairness
flow like a river
that never runs dry.
25 Israel, for forty years
you wandered in the desert,
without bringing offerings
or sacrifices to me.
26Now you will have to carry
the two idols you made—
Sakkuth, the one you call king,
and Kaiwan, the one you built
in the shape of a star.
27I will force you to march
as captives beyond Damascus.
I, the Lord God All-Powerful,
have spoken!
translation_text:
Ti-Dindaan sūǹ Isirayeel yab pu
1Isirayeel yab, pīlifìmaan tibɔti nee, ŋkpiisilan ŋun m làá gāā ni-pu nee.
2Isirayeel bí kii usapɔɔn un kpíì ki dɔ̄ gbàlaayee ní.
U lítì ki dɔ̄ ki gíti kpá kí yīkì.
U pée gbíntì ki dɔ̄ u-tiŋki pu
ní báà ubɔ kaa bí kí yòon̄-u!
3Di sá yii ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti
nín sòon̄ Isirayeel nibul pu puee sèé:
«Kitiŋ kiba yaa tú bijanjaliibi kutuku,
bijanjaliibi dilaataal di làá kínní.
Kitimbilii kiba yaa tú bijanjaliibi dilaataal,
bijanjaliibi saalaa di làá kínní.»
Unil yaa kaa kpántì u-ba, u kpá kí ká difiil
4Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ nì Isirayeel yab puee sèé:
«Ni yaa là kí nīn bi dimaŋfalinee,
nyàab̀maan-mi.
5Ama ní taa nyàab̀-mi Beeteel tiŋkin,
kí taa cù Giilgaal tiŋkin,
ni-taal ń taa tāā Beerseeba tiŋkin.
Giilgaal yab kɔkɔ làá búntí kuyuŋu,
ní Beeteel, Unimbɔti diiku
ń kpántí kuwaadii.»
6Ni yaa là kí nīn bí dimaŋfalinee,
nyàab̀maan ti-Dindaan.
An yaa kaa sá míǹ,
u làá dāá jēetí Jooseefi yab pu kii ŋŋmee.
U làá wà ti-kɔkɔ Beeteel tiŋkin,
ní báà uniseen dāa kpá kí gbíntí-ŋu.
7Ni yāntì ibaamɔn túŋkì kátí kati,
ní kaa dū tin bí deedeeyee ki yíiń tiba!
8Úǹ di náań kuŋmalbicukuu kɔkɔ.
Úǹ di yàntī dibɔmbɔndi
ń kpántí ntaafaawalifi,
ki yàntī ŋwiimpu
kpántí kunyeeu.
Úǹ di yíì tiŋku nyim
ní ki cáá-mì ki yàantí kitiŋ pu.
Úǹ ní bi yíì yii <Ti-Dindaan>.
9Úǹ di yàntī bí nàan̄ upɔɔl,
ní kí nàan̄ kitiŋ kin bi máń digundi ki túee.
10Bi ná un sòoǹ tibɔti ti-puee,
kaa là bi-nimbil ń wāl̀ bin sòoǹ ibaamɔnee.
11Ni mùul̄ binandambi,
ki fòol̄ bi-kpaajinti dijandi.
An puee naa làá kɔ́ adinyaan
ŋin ni máń ki yóoǹee poon,
kaa làá nyɔ̀ ni-fiinyi sufimɔntiŋ
ŋin ni kùn̄ee damam.
12M nyí ni-kpitii nín wīikí tikpil puee,
nì ni-yìntitam nín gíti lákatì mara pu puee.
Ni sá deedeedambi nannanliibi,
ki fòol̄ tiwampɔkaal tin bi cáa ŋēeb̀ ni-nyɔmmuee.
Ni pìintí nsan ibɔsoon laŋki
bí taa sòoǹ biwɔfib bɔti.
13Ŋyunti gbanti sá mbusu yuntiŋu ní,
an pu ní un sá uciŋfitee kíǹ ki ŋmí.
14Ní nyàab̀maan kí nīn ŋáań tin ŋān̄ee,
kí fàtī ni-boon kí tīī ikpiti.
Niinee ni làá nīn bí dimaŋfalin,
ní ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan
ń lafun nín̄ bí ni-cee,
kii nimbi ni-ba nín lì puee.
15Nín̄ námaan tikpitil,
kí nīn néeń tiŋan.
Ní nīn sòoǹ tibɔti ti-pu ibɔsoon laŋki.
An yaa yíì, ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan
làá sɔ̄ nimbi Jooseefi yab
bin kíǹ nee saai.
16An puee ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan,
ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé:
«Bi làá dāá nīn gbìl̀ nsiim pu imɔŋkijaa kɔkɔ pu,
dituweel làá dāá nīn gà adan kɔkɔ pu.
Bi làá dāá bòotīń bikpaabi kusaau
bí dāan̄ dinisibil,
ní kí yíiń bin gà ikpiisilanee bí dāá gāā.
17M yaa láa jítì ni-kansikinee,
binib làá dāá nīn gà ikpiisilan
ni-fiinyi sufii satin.»
Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.
Ti-Dindaan wiiŋŋu dal
18Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí bin kā ki cí
ti-Dindaan wiiŋŋuee!
Ti-Dindaan wiiŋŋu gbanti
làá dāá nīn sá ba ní ki tīī-ni ní?
Ŋu làá dāá nīn sá dibɔmbɔndi wiiŋŋu ní,
kaa sá ŋwalifi wiiŋŋu.
19Ŋu sá kii unil nín sáń gbikinti
kí cùú tū digbiŋgbil nsanni puee ní.
Àá u nín kùǹ u-dumpu
ki dū u-ŋal ki nyīī digundi
ní ukoobu jú-uee ní.
20Ti-Dindaan wiiŋŋu dāa sá ŋwalifi níii?
Aayee, ŋu dāa sá dibɔmbɔndi ní,
ŋu dāa bɔ̀ǹ ní kpìmm,
ŋuaa dāa wāĺ báà fiii.
Unimbɔti kaa là Isirayeel yab jaamii
21M ná ni-jiŋaalib,
maa pée là kí wāl̀-bi.
Ni-kpafiŋ kóò m-poon
ki lèekī baadakam.
22 Bisaraawɔkaabi nì tijimpin saraabi
bin ni ŋáań ki tìì-mee kaa fáatiǹ-mi.
Ni-waŋkuti tin bí màlmal
ni cáa ŋáań-mi saraayee,
maa fàtīi kpèé gba.
23Ní kpáaǹ ni-laŋyi wookuee kí nyā niin.
Maa ti là kí gbìl̄ ni-bati pu.
24Ama ní yàntī ibaamɔn
ń nīn pùub̀ kii nnyimee,
ní tin bí deedeeyee ń nīn bí kii
mbun ŋun kaa fóotée.
25«Isirayeel yab, ni nín nìn ŋá abin imuŋku ili kuteeunee, ni nìn ŋá tiwaŋkuti nì tijimpin saraabi ki tīī-maaa? 26Ama díǹ pu nee, ni tūntí awaa ŋin nimbi ni-ba kpítèe, din ni yíì Siikuuti di sá ni-bɔtiu nì ni-nimbɔtiuee, nì din ni yíì Kiiyuuni di sá ni-ŋmalbijau nì ni-nimbɔtiuee.
27An puee m làá cáá-ni kí cùnnì kuyuŋu
laakin dátì ki jítiǹ Damaasee.»
Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.
U-yindi di sá Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan.

english_text:
Israel Will Be Punished
1Do you rulers in Jerusalem
and in the city of Samaria
feel safe and at ease?
Everyone bows down to you,
and you think you are better
than any other nation.
But you are in for trouble!
2Look what happened
to the cities of Calneh,
powerful Hamath,
and Gath in Philistia.
Are you greater than any
of those kingdoms?
3You are cruel, and you forget
the coming day of judgment.
4You rich people lounge around
on beds with ivory posts,
while dining on the meat
of your lambs and calves.
5You sing foolish songs
to the music of harps,
and you make up new tunes,
just as David used to do.
6You drink all the wine you want
and wear expensive perfume,
but you don't care about
the ruin of your nation.
7So you will be the first
to be dragged off as captives;
your good times will end.
8The Lord God All-Powerful
has sworn by his own name:
“You descendants of Jacob
make me angry by your pride,
and I hate your fortresses.
And so I will surrender your city
and possessions
to your enemies.”
9If only ten of you survive
by hiding in a house
you will still die.
10As you carry out a corpse
to prepare it for burial,
your relative in the house
will ask, “Are there others?”
You will answer, “No!”
Then your relative will reply,
“Be quiet! Don't dare mention
the name of the Lord.”
11At the Lord's command,
houses great and small
will be smashed to pieces.
12Horses can't gallop on rocks;
oceans can't be plowed.
But you have turned justice
and fairness
into bitter poison.
13You celebrate the defeat
of Lo-Debar and Karnaim,
and you boast by saying,
“We did it on our own.”
14But the Lord God All-Powerful
will send a nation to attack
you people of Israel.
They will capture Lebo-Hamath
in the north,
Arabah Creek in the south,
and everything in between.
translation_text:
Bin dàkafī yii tiba kaa ŋūǹ kí bàń-bee
1Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí nimbi bin kóò
Siiyɔn jool pu ni-pɔbiliŋ sɔ̀m̀ee,
nimbi bin kóò Samaarii jool pu
kaa fàŋkí yii tiba ŋūǹ kí ŋá-nee.
Binib lì yii atimbun kɔkɔ kansikinee, nimbi di līī,
ní ni-nabiyaamu Isirayeel yab kpèé ni-pú!
2Ní cùmaan Kalnee tiŋkin kí kpèè!
Niinee ní cù Amaati kitiŋkpaaŋŋin kí kpèè.
Míǹ boonee, ní sìntī Gaati tiŋkin Fiiliistii yab cee.
Ni sɔ́ǹ ntimu gbantaaa?
Ni-tiŋki wāā ki jítiǹ bi-tiŋkaaa?
3Ni nín bíi téekí mbusu wiiŋŋu
ń taa bàń kɔŋkɔnnee,
ni bíi yíì tipɔmbɔti wiiŋŋu
ń bàń malaa dee.
4Ni dɔ̄ idoomɔnti in pɔ̄ɔ̄ kudaauee pu
ki dɔ̄ ni-lambammu pu
ki ŋmóò ni-picaŋkpunti pibiliŋ
nì ni-nacaŋkpunti nabiliŋ nanti.
5Ni bɔ̀ɔ́ kubeeu ki gà ilan.
Ni mɔ́ɔ́ tiwambɔɔkaal tipɔn kii Daafiidee.
6Ni nyù ndamam asambikpaan poon,
ki ŋmìtī ikpafi in sɔ́fèe,
ama naa bí ki sūǹ
mbusu un dòoń Jooseefi yab puee pu.
7An pu ní kɔŋkɔnnee,
nimbi di làá nīn sá bipeepeekaabi
bin bi làá cúú kí cùnnì kuyuŋuee.
Ní nimbi biwutijoodambi kitil nee ń kúntí.
Samaarii tiŋki làá wīī
8Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti,
Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan pūtì ki lī yii:
«Isirayeel yab lambil kóò ki dóotí-mi,
m ná bi-dimɔntiŋ.
An puee m làá dū Samaarii tiŋki
kí ŋá ki-nannanliibi ŋaan.»
9Binib saalaa di yaa kíǹ kudicaŋu poon, bi làá kpú. 10Bi-nabiki làá nyāntí bi-wuntee kí wà ŋŋmi. Ubɔ yaa kíǹ ki bí poon diikunee, kinabikee làá dāá bàlifì udaan yii: «Ubɔ gíti bí ki kútì a-pu niinaaa?» Ní úǹ ń dāá kíí yii: «Aayee, ubɔ gíti kpá.» Ní kinabikee ń dāá lì yii: «Ŋmīĺ fɔ́ŋfɔŋ! Ubɔ ń taa ti pútí ti-Dindaan yindi!»
11Di sá yii ti-Dindaan yaa pée tīī maree,
adikpaan wùtī ní kí lítí,
ní ndiwaamu ń fáá iwèeń.
Dijajil mili pu fám
12Itaamu sáń ataŋkpajal puɔɔɔ?
Inaa kù ataŋkpajal puɔɔɔ?
Kin ba ŋá ní ni dū ibaamɔn ki kpántì tilool,
ki dū tin bí deedeeyee ki kpántì ntuntun?
13Ni bí ki fàal̀ ni nín jáń ki fōō Loo-Deebaar tiŋki, an dàkà yii kitiŋ kin kaa bí tibanee pu. Ni bí ki lì yii: «Timbi ti-ba pɔŋŋu pu ní ti jáń ki fōō Kaarnayiim tiŋki, an dàkà yii Iyin ili tiŋki.» 14Ama man ni-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín lī puee sèé: «Isirayeel yab, m làá yàntī ditimbundi diba ń jáǹ-ni ní kí nà-ni, kí yòon̄ Leeboo-Amaati tiŋki ŋgan pú kí tin cáá bà Arabaa buŋŋu ŋgiil pú.»

english_text:
A Vision of Locusts
1The Lord God showed me that he is going to send locusts to attack your crops. It will happen after the king has already been given his share of the grain and before the rest of the grain has been harvested. 2In my vision the locusts ate every crop in the land, and I said to the Lord, “Please forgive your nation. It's so weak. How can it survive?”
3Then the Lord felt sorry and answered, “I won't let it be destroyed.”
A Vision of Fire
4The Lord showed me that he is going to send a ball of fire to burn up everything on earth, including the ocean. 5Then I said, “Won't you please stop? How can our weak nation survive?”
6Again the Lord felt sorry and answered, “I won't let it be destroyed.”
A Vision of a Measuring Line
7The Lord showed me a vision of himself standing beside a wall and holding a string with a weight tied to the end of it. The string and weight had been used to measure the straightness of the wall. 8Then he asked, “Amos, what do you see?”
“A measuring line,” I answered.
The Lord said, “I'm using this measuring line to show that my people Israel don't measure up, and I won't forgive them any more. 9Their sacred places will be destroyed, and I will send war against the nation of King Jeroboam.”
Amos and Amaziah
10Amaziah the priest at Bethel sent this message to King Jeroboam of Israel, “Amos is plotting against you in the very heart of Israel. Our nation cannot put up with his message for very long. 11Here is what he is saying:
‘Jeroboam will be put to death,
and the people will be taken
to a foreign country.’ ”
12Then Amaziah told me, “Amos, take your visions and get out! Go back to Judah and earn your living there as a prophet. 13Don't do any more preaching at Bethel. The king worships here at our national temple.”
14I answered:
I'm not a prophet! And I wasn't trained to be a prophet. I am a shepherd, and I take care of fig trees. 15But the Lord told me to leave my herds and preach to the people of Israel. 16And here you are, telling me not to preach! 17Now, listen to what the Lord says about you:
Your wife will become
a prostitute in the city,
your sons and daughters
will be killed in war,
and your land will be divided
among others.
You will die in a country
of foreigners,
and the people of Israel
will be dragged
from their homeland.
translation_text:
Dileedakal dipeepeekaal: inaakitoon
1Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nín nìn lēē tin ki dàkā-mee sɔ̀. U nìn bíi nāantí inaakitoon. An nìn sá ŋyunti ŋun bi gāā ubɔti taamui mooti ki dóò ní timool fātìi kíĺ ki bíi túkùee. 2Inaakitoonee nín dāa ŋmɔ́ kitiŋee pu mɔsɔnti kɔkɔee ní m bí yii: «Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti, m gbāam̀-si ní, dū a-nibul kpitii kí pɔ̄-bi. An yaa kaa sá míǹ, mana ní bi làá ŋmátí, bíǹ bin kaa pée náaǹ nee?» 3Ní ti-Dindaan kpántì nlandɔkɔ ní ki bí yii: «Án kaa làá bàń míǹ!»
Dileedakal dililiitiil: ŋŋmi
4Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti gíti lēē tibɔti tiba ki dàkā-mi. U nìn cáá ŋŋmi ki sòoǹ u-nibul bɔti. Ŋŋmifaam nìn yāntì nnyim min dɔ̄ kitiŋ taapuee fóotì ní ki wùn̄ Isirayeel tiŋki búkú buku. 5Niinee ní m bí yii: «Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti, m gbāam̀-si, yàntēe! Yaa sá fám, mana ní a-nibul Isirayeel yab bin kaa náaǹ nee làá ŋmátí?» 6Ní ti-Dindaan kpántì nlandɔkɔ ní ki bí yii: «Tin bí nee mun kaa làá bàń míǹ!»
Dileedakal ditataatiil: ŋŋmiiŋmantikaa
7Tin ti-Dindaan nìn gíti lēē ki dàkā-mee sɔ̀. U nìn yú digundi diba caŋin ki ŋúb́ ŋŋmii ŋun bi cáa ŋmàntī kí kpèè yii digundi tèen̄aaa, dàa tèen̄ee. 8Ti-Dindaan bālifì-mi yii: «Amoosi, ba ní a wāĺ?» Ní m kíí yii: «M wāĺ ŋŋmii ŋun bi cáa ŋmàntī kí kpèè yii digundi tèen̄aaa, dàa tèen̄ee ní.» Ní ti-Dindaan nìkī ki bí yii: «Kpèè, m làá dū ŋŋmii nee kí ŋmàntī kí kpèè yii m-nibul Isirayeel yab tèen̄aaa, baa tèen̄, di sá yii maa làá ti dū bi-kpitii kí pɔ̄-bi.
9M làá kúntí ipaan in pu ní
Isaaki naantiibi ŋáań saraabee,
kí nàan̄ Isirayeel yab circir paaŋyi,
ní kí já nì ubɔti Jeerooboowaam dicaŋkun yab.»
Bi jìn̄ Amoosi Beeteel tiŋkin
10Amasiya un nìn sá Beeteel tiŋkin usaraaŋakpilee nìn tú bí tùkù Isirayeel bɔtiu Jeerooboowaam yii: «Amoosi bí Isirayeel yab kansikin ki bíi gbì a-taapu. Binib gīī nì tibɔti tin u bí ki sòoǹee. 11Tibɔti tin Amoosi sòon̄ee sèé:
<Bi làá kpɔ̀ Jeerooboowaam kujaaun,
ní bí dāá cáá Isirayeel yab kí cùnnì kuyuŋu
bí nīn dátiǹ bi-tiŋki.>»
12Niinee ní Amasiya bí Amoosi yii: «Sii un wāĺee, yīkì doo kí nīn gítí Juuda tiŋkin. Niinee, a ŋūǹ kí nīn nàatī tibɔti kí nīn kāntí ki jīǹ. 13Ama á taa ti nàatī tibɔti Beeteel tiŋkin doo! Di sá yii doo sá ubɔti circir paaŋŋu laŋki, dibeel nimbɔtidiiku ní.» 14Ní Amoosi kíí Amasiya yii: «Maa sá ubɔnaatil, kaa tí nyánní bibɔnaatiliibi kitil diban. M sá upikpaal ní ki kpèé siikoomɔɔr sufii. 15Ama ní ti-Dindaan cúú-mi ki páatì m-piii boon ní ki bí yii: <Cáá m-bɔti kí nàatī m-nibul Isirayeel yab.> 16Ama sii Amasiya bí-mi yii ḿ taa dū Unimbɔti bɔti kí nàatī Isirayeel yab, kí taa sòoǹ kí tɔ̄ Isaaki naantiibi pu. Míǹ puee kɔŋkɔnnee, pīlifì tibɔti tin ti-Dindaan sòon̄ a-puee. 17A-nimpuu làá kpántí kilaakpaai kitiŋin.
Bi làá kpɔ̀ a-jipɔmbi nì a-bisalib.
Bi làá ŋmàntī a-kpaatanti kí dūú yàkatī kí tīī biba.
Sisi a-ba làá kpúnní kitiŋ kin yab kaa nyí Unimbɔtee ni,
ní bí cùnnì Isirayeel yab kuyuŋu
bí nīn dátiǹ bi-tiŋki.»

english_text:
A Basket of Fruit
1The Lord God showed me a basket of ripe fruit 2and asked, “Amos, what do you see?”
“A basket of ripe fruit,” I replied.
Then he said,
“This is the end
for my people Israel.
I won't forgive them again.
3Instead of singing
in the temple,
they will cry and weep.
Dead bodies will be everywhere.
So keep silent!
I, the Lord, have spoken!”
Israel Is Doomed
The Lord said:
4You people crush those in need
and wipe out the poor.
5You say to yourselves,
“How much longer before the end
of the New Moon Festival?
When will the Sabbath be over?
Our wheat is ready,
and we want to sell it now.
We can't wait to cheat
and charge high prices
for the grain we sell.
We will use dishonest scales
6and mix dust in the grain.
Those who are needy and poor
don't have any money.
We will make them our slaves
for the price
of a pair of sandals.”
7I, the Lord, won't forget
any of this,
though you take great pride
in your ancestor Jacob.
8Your country will tremble,
and you will mourn.
It will be like the Nile River
that rises and overflows,
then sinks back down.
9On that day, I, the Lord God,
will make the sun
go down at noon,
and I will turn daylight
into darkness.
10Your festivals and joyful singing
will turn into sorrow.
You will wear sackcloth
and shave your heads,
as you would at the death
of your only son.
It will be a horrible day.
11I, the Lord, also promise you
a terrible shortage,
but not of food and water.
You will hunger and thirst
to hear my message.
12You will search everywhere—
from north to south,
from east to west.
You will go all over the earth,
seeking a message
from me, the Lord.
But you won't find one.
13Your beautiful young women
and your young men
will faint from thirst.
14You made promises
to the goddess Ashimah
at Samaria;
you made vows to other gods
at the shrines
of Dan and Beersheba.
So now you will fall
and never get up.
translation_text:
Dileedakal dinanaatiil: asubil kukabiku
1Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nìn lēē asubil ŋin mántèe kukabiku ki dàkā-mi. 2U nìn bālifì-mi yii: «Amoosi, ba ní a wāĺ?» Ní m kíí-u yii: «Kukabiku nì asubil ŋin mántèe.» Niinee ní ti-Dindaan bí-mi yii:
«M-nibul Isirayeel mántì ki bàn̄ dikúntil.
Maa ti làá dūú pɔ̄-bi.»
3Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti di lī yii:
«Yaadalee ilan in bi gà dibeecindee
làá dāá kpántí ikpiisilan.
Anikpil làá dāá nīn wīikí tikpilku.
Bi làá dāá dū anikpil kí fá an kɔkɔ pu.
Án làá dāá ŋmīĺ an kɔkɔ pu fɔ́ŋfɔŋ!»
Binyampoobi nimbineeliŋu
4Nimbi bin tà biwɔfib pu ki còom̄ee,
nimbi bin là kí kúntí binandambi kitiŋ nee puee,
ní pīlifìmaan tibɔti tin m làá sòoǹ nee.
5Ni kā ki lì yii: «Ba dal ní uŋmapɔɔn jiŋaaliu
làá nín jītí tí ŋmā kí nyāfì ti-kpaajinti dee?
Ba dal ní ŋwiŋŋuŋfikaa làá nín jītí
tí ŋmā kí nyāfiǹ binib bilee dee?»
Ti làá bàtī tiwaŋŋmantikaal wíiŋŋu pu,
kí gbéeǹ animbil ŋmàntikaati nyiŋfiŋu pu,
kí tútí ti-saniyab bí taa tí nín̄ ŋmàntī tiwan deedee.
6Ti làá dū animbil kí dā unandaan
ní kí dū kalaa nimbiliŋ kí dā usoodaan.
Ti làá nyāfì kí kpáaǹ tijaliŋgbiti.
7Ti-Dindaan pūtì ní ki lī yii:
«Kitiŋ kin pu Jaakɔb naantiibi gúntí bi-bee puee,
m kpá kí súntí tin kɔkɔ bi ŋáańee pu.»
8An puee kitiŋ nee làá cìŋkì,
ní ki-nib kɔkɔ ń kàl̄ dikpool.
Kii Eejipiti mɔɔl Niil nín yaa gbí an yíkí puee,
míǹ ní kitiŋ nee làá yīkì yilpu,
ní kí fàtīí lítí bɔ̀b.
9Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti lī yii: «Ŋwiin gbantee,
m làá dāá yàntī ŋwìiń ń jēetí kuwiŋkaŋu pu,
ní kí yàntī kitiŋ kɔkɔ ń kɔ́ dibɔmbɔndin ŋwiimpu.
10M làá yàntī ni-jiŋaalib ń kpántí akpoo
ní kí yàntī ni-laŋyi kɔkɔ ń kpántí ikpiisilan.
Báà ŋma làá dāá nīn pēē kpɔsatab ní.
Báà ŋma làá dāá pée kòol̀ diyibaakpandi
kii unil jipɔmbaabil nín yaa kpíì u kòol̄ puee.
Ŋwiin gbanti làá dāá kúntí nì ntuntun ní.»
11Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti di lī yii:
«Ŋwiin bí ki dòoń, m làá dāá dū ŋkùm kí tɔ̄ kitiŋ nee pu.
Ŋkùm làá dāá cúú binib,
ama kaa dāa sá tijikaal kùm.
Nnyinnyoo làá dāá cúú binib,
ama kaa dāa sá nnyim nyinnyooŋu.
Ama man ni-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi
kùm nì di-nyinnyooŋu di làá dāá cúú-bi.
12Binib làá dāá nīn tú ki yìiǹ an kɔkɔ pu,
kí yīkì tiŋku ubɔ kí cáá sāā un kíǹee,
kí yòon̄ ŋgan pú kí cù ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú,
ki bàà pée nyàab̀ kí gbìl̄ man ni-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi
ama kaa làá dāá ká.
13«Ŋwiin gbantee, bisapɔnnyaambi
nì binaacimpɔmbi làá dāá kpú nnyinnyoo.
14Bin kɔkɔ pùtī Samaarii waal yindi,
bin lì yii: <Nì Daani waal yindi pu!>
àá <nì Beerseeba waasaŋŋu yindi puee>,
bi-kɔkɔ làá dāá lítí kaa làá ti yīkì.»

english_text:
Judgment on Israel
1I saw a vision of the Lord
standing by the temple altar,
and he said,
“Shake the columns
until the tops fall loose,
and the doorposts crumble.
Then make the pieces fall
on the people below.
I will take a sword and kill
anyone who escapes.
2“If they dig deep into the earth
or climb to the sky,
I'll reach out and get them.
3If they escape to the peaks
of Mount Carmel,
I'll search and find them.
And if they hide from me
at the bottom of the ocean,
I'll command a sea monster
to bite them.
4I'll send a sword to kill them,
wherever their enemies
drag them off as captives.
I'm determined to hurt them,
not to help them.”
His Name Is the Lord
5When the Lord God All-Powerful
touches the earth, it melts,
and its people mourn.
God makes the earth rise
and then fall,
just like the Nile River.
6He built his palace in the heavens
and let its foundations
rest on the earth.
He scoops up the ocean
and empties it on the earth.
His name is the Lord.
The Lord Is God
7Israel, I am the Lord God,
and the Ethiopians
are no less important to me
than you are.
I brought you out of Egypt,
but I also brought
the Philistines from Crete
and the Arameans from Kir.
8My eyes have seen
what a sinful nation you are,
and I'll wipe you out.
But I will leave a few
of Jacob's descendants.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
9At my command, all of you
will be sifted like grain.
Israelites who remain faithful
will be scattered
among the nations.
And the others will be trapped
like trash in a sifter.
10Some of you are evil,
and you deny
that you will ever get caught.
But you will be killed.
The Lord's Promise to Israel
11 In the future, I will rebuild
David's fallen kingdom.
I will build it from its ruins
and set it up again,
just as it used to be.
12Then you will capture Edom
and the other nations
that are mine.
I, the Lord, have spoken,
and my words will come true.
13You will have such a harvest
that you won't be able
to bring in all of your wheat
before plowing time.
You will have grapes left over
from season to season;
your fruitful vineyards
will cover the mountains.
14I'll make Israel prosper again.
You will rebuild your towns
and live in them.
You will drink wine
from your own vineyards
and eat the fruit you grow.
15I'll plant your roots deep
in the land I have given you,
and you won't ever
be uprooted again.
I, the Lord God, have spoken!
translation_text:
Dileedakal diŋmooŋmootiil
1M ká ti-Dindaan yú nsaraafan pu ki lì yii: «Gbá kí wìil̀ jaantalkub yilpu ní taapu ń cìŋkì!
Gbá kí wìil̀-bi bí lítí kí tàbitì bi-yiliŋ.
Bi-kansikin bin kíǹ kaa kpíìyee,
m làá dū ntàataajimu kí kpɔ̀-bi.
Báà unil kaa làá dāá ŋmā kí sāǹ,
ní uniseen kaa làá dāá ŋmátí.
2Báà bi yaa pɔ́ɔǹ kí kɔ́ ditaŋkpiilinaaa,
m làá dāá cù niin kí fàtīí gíiǹní-bi.
Bi yaa láa tí jɔ́m̀ yilpuɔɔɔ,
m làá dāá cù niin kí sìntīń-bi.
3Bi yaa láa bál̀ Kaarmeel jool yilpu kúntí kuntaaa,
m làá dāá cù niin kí cúuń-bi.
Bi yaa láa sáǹ ki bál̀ tiŋku taapu ḿ taa ká-baaa,
m làá dāá tɔ̄ tiŋkun koobuu ú jūntì-bi.
4Bi-nannanliibi yaa láa jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-bi
ní ki cúú-bi kuyuŋu ki cūnnì bi-tiŋkinee,
m làá dāá tīī-bi mara bí pɔ̀fì-bi.
M-nimbil làá dāá nīn cɔ́ bi-pu,
kí ŋá-bi tikpitil, kaa sá tiŋan.»
5Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti Mpɔŋkɔdaan
yaa gbēē kitiŋee, kì cìŋkī ní,
ní ki-nib kɔkɔ ń kàl̄ dikpool.
Kii Eejipiti mɔɔl Niil nín yaa gbí an yíkí puee,
míǹ ní kitiŋ nee làá yīkì yilpu,
ní kí fàtīí lítí bɔ̀b.
6U máń u-kɔŋkooŋŋu yilpu fɔ́ŋŋŋ
ki dū kutagbɔŋu ki dāntì kitiŋ pu.
Úǹ di yíì tiŋku nyim
ní ki cáá-mì ki yàantí kitiŋ pu.
Úǹ ní bi yíì yii <Ti-Dindaan>.
Dibɔkpil dambi bɔsooŋyi
7Ti-Dindaan lī yii: «Isirayeel yab,
ni pɔ̄ɔ̄ m-cee kudaau ki jítiǹ Kuusi yabaaa?
M nyántì-ni Eejipiti tiŋkin,
ama ki nyántì Fiiliistii yab Kafitoor tiŋkin,
ní ki nyántì Aram yab Kiiri tiŋkin.»
8Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nimbil cɔ́
Isirayeel beel din fōō dibɔkpil nee pu.
U lī yii: «M làá kúntí-dì kitiŋ pu.
Ama maa làá nàan̄ Jaakɔb naantiibi kɔkɔ.
9Di sá yii m làá tīī mara
ní bí jáká Isirayeel timbundi
atimbun ŋin kíǹee kɔkɔ poon,
kii bi nín dù kidicaai kí jáká tiwan pu,
báà kitaŋkpalii kaa lùntī kí lítée.
10M-nibul kansikin bikpitiŋaliibi
làá kpú kujaaun,
bíǹ bin lì yii:
<Nnaabu ŋubɔ kpá kí làá dāan̄,
u làá sútiń kí pìlīń-ti!>»
Nnaabu yaa láa jítèe bɔti
11«Ŋwiin gbantee m làá dāá yòon̄
Daafiidi bìŋ́ku kun bíi lítée kí yóoń,
ní kí ŋéeb́ ku-digbuŋweeŋyi kɔkɔ,
kí mā ku-guŋŋi ŋin lítì ki dɔ̄ee,
dí fàtīí gítí di nín nìn bí puee.
12Án nín làá ŋá pu Isirayeel yab
ń dāá fàtīí fōō Eedoom yab cee
nì atimbun ŋin kíǹee kɔkɔ yab cee
ntimu mun di nìn sá man yɔmuee.
Man ni-Dindaan di sòon̄,
ní ki làá yàntī án ŋá míǹ!»
13Ti-Dindaan gíti lī yii:
«Ŋwiin dòoń
bi làá dāá cā tikpaajin tikpil
án nīn dɔ̄ kí tin sāā
ŋyunti ŋun bi làá kpɔ̀ tipɔnee.
Míǹ mbaantiim, bi làá dāá kìtī fiinyi biliŋ
án nīn dɔ̄ kí tin sāā
ŋyunti ŋun ní bi làá bɔ̄l̀ bileeyee.
Niinee ndapɔm dāa pùub̀ ajoon pu
ní ki còol̀ ŋgbantamu kɔkɔ pu.
14M làá fàtīí gíiǹní m-nibul Isirayeel yab bi-tiŋkin
bí fàtīí mā bi-timmu mun wīil̀ee kí kàl̄.
Bi làá dāá cóoń fiinyi sufii kí nyɔ̀ i-daam.
Bi làá kpɔ̀ tikuŋfaal kpaaŋŋi kí dāá ká kí jī.
15M làá dāá fàtīí gíiǹ m-nibul
kí kàan̄ bi-tiŋki pu.
Baa làá ti jà-bi kitiŋ kin
m tīī-bee pu jaanjaan.
Man ni-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu di lī míǹ!»

english_text:
Edom's Pride and Punishment
1 The Lord God gave Obadiah
a message about Edom,
and this is what we heard:
“I, the Lord, have sent
a messenger
with orders for the nations
to attack Edom.”
2The Lord said to Edom:
I will make you the weakest
and most despised nation.
3You live in a mountain fortress,
because your pride
makes you feel safe from attack,
but you are mistaken.
4I will still bring you down,
even if you fly higher
than an eagle
or nest among the stars.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
5If thieves break in at night,
they steal
only what they want.
And people who harvest grapes
always leave some unpicked.
But, Edom, you are doomed!
6Everything you treasure most
will be taken from you.
7Your allies can't be trusted.
They will force you out
of your own country.
And your best friends
will trick and trap you,
even before you know it.
8Edom, when this happens,
I, the Lord, will destroy
all your marvelous wisdom.
9Warriors from the city of Teman
will be terrified,
and you descendants of Esau
will be wiped out.
The Lord Condemns Edom's Cruelty
10You were cruel to your relatives,
the descendants of Jacob.
Now you will be destroyed,
disgraced forever.
11You stood there and watched
as foreigners entered Jerusalem
and took what they wanted.
In fact, you were no better
than those foreigners.
12Why did you celebrate
when such a dreadful disaster
struck your relatives?
Why were you so pleased
when everyone in Judah
was suffering?
13They are my people,
and you were cruel to them.
You went through their towns,
sneering and stealing
whatever was left.
14In their time of torment,
you ambushed refugees
and handed them over
to their attackers.
The Lord Will Judge the Nations
15The day is coming
when I, the Lord,
will judge the nations.
And, Edom, you will pay in full
for what you have done.
16I forced the people of Judah
to drink the wine of my anger
on my sacred mountain.
Soon the neighboring nations
must drink their fill—
then vanish without a trace.
Victory for Israel
17The Lord's people who escape
will go to Mount Zion,
and it will be holy.
Then Jacob's descendants
will capture the land of those
who took their land.
18Israel will be a fire,
and Edom will be straw
going up in flames.
The Lord has spoken!
19The people of Israel
who live in the Southern Desert
will take the land of Edom.
Those who live in the hills
will capture Philistia,
Ephraim, and Samaria.
And the tribe of Benjamin
will conquer Gilead.
20Those who return from captivity
will control Phoenicia
as far as Zarephath.
Captives from Jerusalem
who were taken to Sepharad
will capture the towns
of the Southern Desert.
21Those the Lord has saved
will live on Mount Zion
and rule over Edom.
Then the kingdom will belong
to the Lord.
translation_text:
1Tibɔti tin ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti lēē ki dàkā Oobadiyee. U nín sòon̄ Eedoom tiŋki pu puee sɔ̀.
Ti-Dindaan yāntì ti gbìl̄ tibɔti nee,
bi tú ntuun ŋubɔ atimbun kɔkɔn ŋu lì yii:
«Yīkìmaan! Tí cùú já nì Eedoom tiŋki!»
2Ti-Dindaan lī yii:
«Eedoom, atimbun kɔkɔnee,
m làá yàntī á kpántí kiwaŋwaai.
Báà ŋma làá nīn kpèé ki sìŋkīǹ-si.
3A-lambikpaandi di kíiĺ-si!
A kóò itaŋkpalɔkɔn,
ní ki máń a-diiŋŋi ki tɔ́kɔǹ ajoon yilpu,
ní ki lì yii:
<Ŋma di ŋūǹ kí kpákatí-mi taapu?>
4Báà a yaa là kí ŋàaǹ kí kɔ́ kutaa kii ukaalunee,
kí mā a-diiku iŋmalbijaa kansikin,
see m kpákatìń-si taapu!
5Binaayub àá kunyeeu fukuliliibi
yaa kɔ́ a-puee,
bi yòontí tin kɔkɔ bi ŋūǹee ní,
baa kīntí-si báà tiba.
Bitɔntɔnliibi bin kìtī fiinyi subiliŋee
yaa kɔ́ a-saakunee,
tin làá pée kíńee di sá tilulifikaal.
6Bi fúkúl̀ nimbi Eesayuu naantiibi pílpil,
bi bīitì ni-gaajawanti tin bí dibalinee pu!
7Bi jìn̄-si ki nyántì a-tiŋkin,
si nì bin pēē kinyɔkɔee nyáń a-boon.
A-bɔɔmɔntiibi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ-si.
Si nì bin nìn jīǹ disambibaantiilinee
bíi pīil̀-si titalindi taapu taapu.
Bi sòoǹ ni-pu yii: <Waa ti cáá diyil!>
8Tiŋman, man ni-Dindaan nín lī puee sɔ̀.
M-ŋuul wiiŋŋu dalee,
m làá kpɔ̀ kí céetí biciŋfitiibi Eedoom tiŋkin,
maa làá kíń Eesayuu jool pu
unyil ubambaanti.
9Teeman tiŋki, dinyoondi làá dāá kɔ́ a-janjaliibi,
án nín làá ŋá pu bí kpɔ̀ kí kúntí
unil sá kamaa Eesayuu jool puee.
Eedoom yìntitam
10A fúkúl̀ ki kūū a-nabiki,
Jaakɔb naantiibi.
An pu ní icoo làá cúú-si tikpil
ní bí kúntí-si kí nīn pée cá jaanjaan.
11Ŋwiin ŋun a nìn yú ki kpèé
binannanliibi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ u-janjaliibi
ki kɔ́ u-tiŋkin,
ki tɔ́ Jeerusaleem pu kasee,
a mun nìn bí kii bi-kansikin ubɔee dee.
12Eedoom, aa bàà nìn máaǹ
kí nīn fàal̀ ŋyunti ŋun
a-nabiki kɔ́ dinimbinaamandinee.
Aa bàà nìn máaǹ kí nīn fàal̀
ŋyunti ŋun bi bíi nàantí Juuda yabee.
Aa bàà nìn máaǹ kí nīn bíi lāā-bi
ŋyunti ŋun bi kɔ́ dinimbinaamandi poonee.
13Aa bàà nìn máaǹ kí kɔ́ m-nibul tiŋkin,
ŋyunti ŋun bi nìn bíi nàantí-kèe.
Aa bàà nìn máaǹ kí nīn fàal̀
u-nimbinaamandi wiiŋŋu dal.
Aa bàà nìn máaǹ kí yòon̄ u-gaajawanti
ŋwiin ŋun bi nìn bíi fúkuĺ-uee.
14Aa bàà nìn máaǹ kí nīn yú isampuyakati pu
ki kù bin nìn sáń kí ŋmátée,
kaa bàà nìn tí máaǹ kí dū bin baa kūūyee
kí ŋá binannanliibi ŋaan
nnaabu wiiŋŋu gbanti dal.
15Di sá yii ti-Dindaan wiiŋŋu ŋun
u làá sòoǹ atimbun kɔkɔ bɔtee tóobiń.
A nín ŋá bin beeyee puee,
míǹ ní bi làá téeǹ-si.
A-tuŋkpitiŋ làá dāá fàtīí gítí a-pu ní.»
Isirayeel làá tɔ̀ Eedoom ipɔntoon
16«Nimbi Isirayeel yab, kii ni nín nìn nyùn̄
m-ŋuul kii ndaamee
m-circir jool puee,
míǹ mbaantiim ní atimbun kɔkɔ
làá dāá nyɔ̀-dì kí taa gbèen̄.
Ŋi làá dāá nyɔ̀-dì kí gbí,
ní boonee kí wāŋkì.
17Ama bin yaa láa bí kaa kpíìyee
làá dāá sāǹ kí kɔ́ Siiyɔn jool.
Dì làá fàtīí kpántí circir jool.
Jaakɔb naantiibi làá dāá
fàtīí fōō bi-tiŋki
bin nìn fōō-kèe ŋaan.
18Jaakɔb naantiibi làá dāá nīn sá kii ŋŋmee ní,
Jooseefi naantiibi làá dāá nīn sá kii diŋmilimbilee.
Ama Eesayuu naantiibi làá dāá nīn sá kii timoolee ní.
Bi làá dāá wà Eesayuu naantiibi ní kɔkɔ múb.»
19Bin kóò ŋgiil pú tiŋkee di làá dāá nīn yì Eesayuu jool nì Seefeelaa tiŋki kin pu Fiiliistii yab kóòyee. Bi làá dāá nīn yì Eefiraayiim tiŋki nì Samaarii tiŋki mun, ní Beenjameen ń dāá nīn yì Galaadi tiŋki.
20Isirayeel beel ŋgan pú yab bin bi nìn cúú ki cūnnì kuyuŋuee làá dāá kpántí dijanjakitikpaandi. Bi làá dāá já kí fōō Kanaan yab tiŋki kí tin sāā Sareepita tiŋki. Jeerusaleem yab bin bi nìn cúú ki cūnnì kuyuŋu bi bí Seefaradee làá dāá já kí fōō ntimu mun bí ŋgiil púee. 21Bi nín jáń ki jíń mimmee ní bí jɔ̄m̀ Siiyɔn jool pu. Niin ní bi làá dāá nīn bí ní kí jī Eedoom jool pu dibeel.
Ti-Dindaan di dāa sá ubɔti!

english_text:
Jonah Runs from the Lord
1 One day the Lord told Jonah, the son of Amittai, 2to go to the great city of Nineveh and say to the people, “The Lord has seen your terrible sins. You are doomed!”
3Instead, Jonah ran from the Lord. He went to the seaport of Joppa and found a ship that was going to Spain. So he paid his fare, then got on the ship and sailed away to escape.
4But the Lord made a strong wind blow, and such a bad storm came up that the ship was about to be broken to pieces. 5The sailors were frightened, and they all started praying to their gods. They even threw the ship's cargo overboard to make the ship lighter.
All this time, Jonah was down below deck, sound asleep. 6The ship's captain went to him and said, “How can you sleep at a time like this? Get up and pray to your God! Maybe he will have pity on us and keep us from drowning.”
7Finally, the sailors got together and said, “Let's ask our gods to show us who caused all this trouble.” It turned out to be Jonah.
8They started asking him, “Are you the one who brought all this trouble on us? What business are you in? Where do you come from? What is your country? Who are your people?”
9Jonah answered, “I'm a Hebrew, and I worship the Lord God of heaven, who made the sea and the dry land.”
10When the sailors heard this, they were frightened, because Jonah had already told them he was running from the Lord. Then they said, “Do you know what you have done?”
11The storm kept getting worse, until finally the sailors asked him, “What should we do with you to make the sea calm down?”
12Jonah told them, “Throw me into the sea, and it will calm down. I'm the cause of this terrible storm.”
13The sailors tried their best to row to the shore. But they could not do it, and the storm kept getting worse every minute. 14So they prayed to the Lord, “Please don't let us drown for taking this man's life. Don't hold us guilty for killing an innocent man. All of this happened because you wanted it to.” 15Then they threw Jonah overboard, and the sea calmed down. 16The sailors were so terrified that they offered a sacrifice to the Lord and made all kinds of promises.
17 The Lord sent a big fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was inside the fish for three days and three nights.
translation_text:
Yoona mākaǹ kí sāǹ kí báĺ ti-Dindaan
1Dalba ti-Dindaan nìn sòon̄ nì Amiitaayi jipɔɔn Yoona ki bí-u yii: 2«Yīkì kí cù Niiniifi kitiŋkpaaŋŋi poon kí bāakì kí tùkù kitiŋ gbanti nib yii bi-kpitii nyāŋkì, di sá yii m-nimbil ká ikpiti in bi bí ki ŋáańee.»
3Ama ní Yoona yíkì ki dūu túĺ Taarsiisi tiŋki pú, kí sāǹ kí cù ndandati ti-Dindaan ń taa ti ká-u. U yíkèe ní ki nín sìntī Jaafa tiŋkin ki bàn̄ ki ká meela ubɔ bɔ́ntì ki cá Taarsiisi tiŋkin, ní u pàn̄ ki kɔ́ ki kāl̀ meelan bí cáá-u kí nīn cá Taarsiisi tiŋkin ú cùú báĺ ti-Dindaan.
4Ní ti-Dindaan dū kubuŋkpaaŋŋu kubɔ ki tɔ́ tiŋku pu. Kubuŋkpaaŋŋuee bíi fīintí tiŋku mpɔn mpɔn ní ki bàà làá wīī meela. 5Niinee tifaandi kɔ́ meela tɔntɔnliibi, ní báà ŋma kíǹ ki bíi tíminsí ki yíì u-nimbɔtiu. Ní bi yōoǹ tiwan tin bi tākaǹ meelanee kɔkɔ ki tɔ́ tiŋkun kí ŋmā kí bàtī meela nyiŋfiŋu pu. Nì mimmee, Yoona úǹ pée kɔ́ meela poondiikun ki dōoǹ ki bíi gèeǹ fɔ̀rtititi! 6Ní meelan tɔntɔnliibi kpiliu sútì ki pìl̄-u ní ki bí-u yii: «Sii dɔ̄ ki gèeǹ níii? Yīkì kí tīminsì kí yíiń a-nimbɔtiu. An yaa yíì úǹ làá sɔ̄ ti-saai kí jòoń-ti tí taa kpú.» 7Ní meelan tɔntɔnliibi bí tɔb yii: «Ní yàntī tí tɔ̄maan kasi kí béé udaan un pu ní dinimbinaamandi nee dī ki bāań-tee.» Bi tɔ́ kasee ní an dūu tāā Yoona. 8Ní bi bālifì Yoona yii: «Too, sii un pu dinimbinaamandi nee dī ki bāań-ti nee, a-tundi baasii sá dilal ní doo ní? La pu ní a nyánní ní? A sá kitiŋ kilakan ní? A sá dinibul dilal niliu ní?» 9Ní Yoona kíí-bi yii: «Man sá ueebruja ní. Ti-Dindaan yilpu Nimbɔtiu un náań tiŋku nì kitiŋee ní m jáaḿ!» 10Binibee nín ká yii Yoona u-ba nín lī puee dàkà yii ti-Dindaan ní u bíi sáńee ní bi fāŋkì tikpil tikpil, ki bí-u yii: «Batii bɔti ní a ŋá mimmee!» 11Bi lī mimmee ní ki bālifì Yoona yii: «Mana ní ti máaǹ kí ŋá-si ní tiŋku ń ŋmīĺ án ŋá ti-pu fòooo dee?» Di sá yii kubuŋu nìn dáá pée gbíntìi jītí mpɔn ní tiŋku nyim nìn mɔ̀tīi yíkí mpɔn. 12Ní Yoona kíí-bi yii: «Ní yòom̄maan-mi kí tɔ̄ tiŋkun, tiŋku làá ŋmīĺ ní án ŋá ni-pu fòooo! Mama m-ba pée nyí yii man pu ní kubuŋkpaaŋŋu nee bí ki jītí tiŋku pu ki páb́-ni míǹ.» 13Binibee pɔ́ɔǹ bi-ba kí bàà ŋàal̀ meela kí fàtīí bà tiŋku gbandi ama baa ŋúń, kun puee tiŋku nyim nìn mɔ̀tīi jɔ́ḿ ní ki páb́-bi. 14Niinee ní bi tíminsì ki yíiń ti-Dindaan ní ki bí yii: «Áù, ti-Dindaan, ti gbàam̄-si! Taa yàntī tí kpú kijapaai nee pu. Taa dū kijapaai nee kpuulool kí lúntí ti-pu, waa ŋá-ti tiba. Ti-Dindaan, sisi a-ba nín là puee, míǹ ní a ŋá.» 15Bi mēē ti-Dindaan míǹ ki dóòyee ní ki cúú Yoona ki yōoǹ ki dūu tɔ́ tiŋkun. Niin niin ní kubuŋu nín bàà bí ki yòontí tiŋku nyim pu an fīintí-bi mpɔn mpɔnee gbēeǹ ní an ŋmíl̀ fɔ́ŋfɔŋ. 16Binibee nín ká mimmee, bi fāŋkì ti-Dindaan tikpil tikpil ní ki ŋá saraa ki tīī ti-Dindaan ní ki pōoǹ-u ipoon.

english_text:
Jonah's Prayer
1From inside the fish, Jonah prayed to the Lord his God:
2When I was in trouble, Lord,
I prayed to you,
and you listened to me.
From deep in the world
of the dead,
I begged for your help,
and you answered my prayer.
3You threw me down
to the bottom of the sea.
The water was churning
all around;
I was completely covered
by your mighty waves.
4I thought I was swept away
from your sight,
never again to see
your holy temple.
5I was almost drowned
by the swirling waters
that surrounded me.
Seaweed had wrapped
around my head.
6I had sunk down deep
below the mountains
beneath the sea.
I knew that forever,
I would be a prisoner there.
But, you, Lord God,
rescued me from that pit.
7When my life was slipping away,
I remembered you—
and in your holy temple
you heard my prayer.
8All who worship worthless idols
turn from the God
who offers them mercy.
9But with shouts of praise,
I will offer a sacrifice
to you, my Lord.
I will keep my promise,
because you are the one
with power to save.
10 The Lord commanded the fish to vomit up Jonah on the shore. And it did.
translation_text:
Yoona wimmeem
1Bi dū Yoona ki tɔ́ tiŋkunee ní ti-Dindaan lēē ujɔŋkpaan ubɔ ki tú u dū Yoona ki náĺ, ní u kāl̀ ujɔmee poon iwiin ita, ŋwiimpu nì kunyeeu. 2Yoona kā ujɔm poonee ní ki mēē ti-Dindaan u-Nimbɔtiu ŋwimmeem yii:
3«M nìn bí dinimbinaamandin,
ki tíminsì ki yíiń sii ti-Dindaan
ní a kíí-mi.
M nìn sīntì taapu taŋkpiilin
ki kúuǹ ki yíiń-si á dāá jòoń-mi
ní a gbìl̄ m-timinsii.
4A dū-mi ki tɔ́ tiŋku poon
m nín sìntī nnyimbuun taapu taapu
ní nnyim māntìi tú-mi an kɔkɔ pu,
ní a yāntì tinyiŋgban kɔkɔ nì nnyinjil
dòoń ki jītí m-pu.
5Ní m lī m-neen yii:
<Man nì sii yākatì tɔbin ní nee,
m pée gíti kpá kí ká-si!
Nì míǹ kɔkɔee m gbíntìi bíi kpèé
a-circir kɔŋkooŋŋu watil pú>.
6Nnyim jɔ́m̀ ki tin sāā m-neen,
m mɔ̄tìi nín sìntī tiŋku taapu taapu,
ní timool tin bí nnyiminee dūu lùl̄ m-yil.
7M sīntì doooo taapu taapu
ki tin nyáń ajoon nyeel pu,
ditaŋkpiil dū di-punyɔmmu ki pīiǹ m-pu
kí nīn pée cá jaanjaan.
Ama ní sii ti-Dindaan m-Nimbɔtiu
fātìi nyántìń-mi
m dáá gbíntìi bí dimaŋfalin.
8Ŋyunti ŋun m ká yii an dóò m-puee,
m-landɔkɔŋu fātìi gítì sii ti-Dindaan pu,
ní m yāntì m-wimmeem nín jɔ́ḿ a-watil pú
ki tin bàn̄-si a-circir kɔŋkooŋŋu poon.
9Bin dū awaa ŋin kaa bí tibanee ki yíĺ bi-yilee,
bíǹ kaa ti cáá diyimɔɔl kí ká difiil dee!
10An yaa kíǹ kii mamee,
man làá gāā ilan kí nyɔ̄ŋkì-si,
ki làá ŋá saraa kí tīī-si,
ki làá ŋá tin ní m pōoǹ yii
m làá ŋá kí tīī-see.
Sii ti-Dindaan cee ní difiil nyēeń!»
11Míǹ boonee ní ti-Dindaan pú ujɔmee kinyɔkɔ u fātìi wūliŋkì Yoona ki bíl̀ tiŋku gbandi.

english_text:
Jonah Goes to Nineveh
1Once again the Lord told Jonah 2to go to that great city of Nineveh and preach his message of doom.
3Jonah obeyed the Lord and went to Nineveh. The city was so big that it took three days just to walk through it. 4 After walking for a day, Jonah warned the people, “Forty days from now, Nineveh will be destroyed!”
5They believed God's message and set a time when they would go without eating to show their sorrow. Then everyone in the city, no matter who they were, dressed in sackcloth.
6When the king of Nineveh heard what was happening, he also dressed in sackcloth; he left the royal palace and sat in dust. 7-9Then he and his officials sent out an order for everyone in the city to obey. It said:
None of you or your animals may eat or drink a thing. Each of you must wear sackcloth, and you must even put sackcloth on your animals.
You must also pray to the Lord God with all your heart and stop being sinful and cruel. Maybe God will change his mind and have mercy on us, so we won't be destroyed.
10When God saw that the people had stopped doing evil things, he had pity and did not destroy them as he had planned.
translation_text:
Yoona báakì ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi Niiniifi tiŋkin
1An ŋá mimmee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Yoona nliliitiim ki bí-u yii: 2«Yīkì kí cù Niiniifi kitiŋkpaaŋŋi poon kí dū tibɔti tin m dūu ŋúbiǹ-see kí bāakì kí tùkù niin yab.» 3Niinee ní Yoona yíkì ki nín cá Niiniifi tiŋkin, ki nóó nì ti-Dindaan nín bí yii ú ŋá puee. Niiniifi tiŋki gbanti nìn sá kitiŋkpaŋkpaaŋŋi ní, an kaa cáá bí lì. Iwimmɔn ita kɔkɔ ní unil nìn dùŋfī ní kí còom̀ kí pùntī-kì. 4Yoona kɔ́ kitiŋin ki kíĺ ki cōom̀ ŋwiin ŋubɔ ní ki báakì ki lī yii: «An gíti kíǹ iwiin imuŋku ili Niiniifi tiŋki làá kúntí!» 5Niiniifi yab nìn fōō Unimbɔti bɔti tin u sòon̄ee ki kíí, ní bi yóoǹ yii báà ŋma ń bóob́ kinyɔkɔ. Di sá kí yòon̄ bikpilib kí tin cáá sāā ŋwaamuee, báà ŋma nìn dū kutuku ki pēeǹ kí dàkà yii bi fá bi-kpitii ki kpántì bi-ba. 6Tibɔti dūu bàn̄ Niiniifi bɔtiu ceeyee ní u yíkì u-beejal pu, ki cúú dibeebɔkutil din u pēēyee ki pēetì, ki dū kutuku ki pēeǹ ní ki kāl̀ ŋfantamin. 7U ŋée ní ki yāntì bi báakì Niiniifi tiŋki kɔkɔn ki lī yii: «Ubɔti nì u-kpambaliŋ yóoǹ mara yii binib nì tiwaŋkuti, inaa nì ipii nì iŋoobu, báà ubɔ ń taa jī tijinaaa, kí taa nyɔ̀ nnyim mun. 8Binib nì tiwaŋkuti kɔkɔ ń dū kutukub kí pèen̄ kí tīminsì kí yíiń Unimbɔti nì bi-pɔŋŋu kɔkɔ. Báà ŋma ń dū isaŋkpiti in u còom̄ee nì tipɔmbɔti tin u ŋáańee kí fá. 9Án yaa yíì Unimbɔti làá kpántí u-landɔkɔŋu, kí yàntī u-ŋuukpaandi din u gíí ti-puee ń sɔ̀ŋkì ní tí ŋmátí kí taa kpú!»
10Unimbɔti nín ká yii Niiniifi yab pɔ́ɔǹ bi-ba ki dū isaŋkpiti in bi nóóyee ki fée, ní u kpántì u-landɔkɔŋu kaa ti dáaĺ bi-tafal kii u nín bàà là kí ŋá puee.

english_text:
Jonah Gets Angry with the Lord
1Jonah was really upset and angry. 2 So he prayed:
Our Lord, I knew from the very beginning that you wouldn't destroy Nineveh. That's why I left my own country and headed for Spain. You are a kind and merciful God, and you are very patient. You always show love, and you don't like to punish anyone.
3 Now let me die! I'd be better off dead.
4The Lord replied, “What right do you have to be angry?”
5Jonah then left through the east gate of the city and made a shelter to protect himself from the sun. He sat under the shelter, waiting to see what would happen to Nineveh.
6The Lord made a vine grow up to shade Jonah's head and protect him from the sun. Jonah was very happy to have the vine, 7but early the next morning the Lord sent a worm to chew on the vine, and the vine dried up. 8During the day the Lord sent a scorching wind, and the sun beat down on Jonah's head, making him feel faint. Jonah was ready to die, and he shouted, “I wish I were dead!”
9But the Lord asked, “Jonah, do you have the right to be angry about the vine?”
“Yes, I do,” he answered, “and I'm angry enough to die.”
10But the Lord said:
You are concerned about a vine that you did not plant or take care of, a vine that grew up in one night and died the next. 11In that city of Nineveh there are more than 120,000 people who cannot tell right from wrong, and many cattle are also there. Don't you think I should be concerned about that big city?
translation_text:
Yoona béè kun pu ní ti-Dindaan súń Niiniifi tiŋki saayee
1An bɔtee kaa mɔ́ɔkiǹ Yoona báà fiii ní u fōō mbum. 2Ní Yoona mēē ti-Dindaan ki bí yii: «Áù, ti-Dindaan! Tibɔti tin m nìn lī ŋyunti ŋun m nìn bí m-tiŋkinee kaa sɔ̀ɔɔ? Kun pu m nìn yíkì ki bàà nìn sáń ki cá Taarsiisi tiŋkinee deeyaa! M pée nyí yii a sá Unimbɔti un poon mɔ̄, ki cáá disaasɔl nì kimɔtii tikpil ki ŋáań tiŋan ní unil yaa yīntiǹ-si ki bàà máaǹ á dáaĺ u-tafalee, á kpántí a-landɔkɔŋu malaa kí dūú pɔ̄ udaanee. 3An puee, ti-Dindaan, m mèé-si yii kɔŋkɔnnee á fàtīí fōō m-maŋfal. M yaa pūtì kpíì an sɔ́ nì ḿ nīn bí dimaŋfalin!» 4Ní ti-Dindaan bālifì-u yii: «A cáá nsan kí gíí diŋuulaaa?» 5Ní Yoona yíkì ki nyáń Niiniifi tiŋkin ki cūtì ki kāl̀ ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú. U gāā kibiŋ kiba niin ní ki kāl̀ ki-booŋŋu taapu ki cí kí kpèè tin làá jītí Niiniifi tiŋki poonee. 6Ní ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti yāntì digbumbitiki subiki nyáń ki wíiǹ, ki-booŋŋu bīiǹ Yoona yil ŋwìiń, kí sɔ̀ŋkì u-pɔbil. Kisubiki gbanti bɔti mɔ́ɔkiǹ Yoona tikpil. 7Ama kutaa wúntì an dáá bɔ̀ǹ gúuuyee, ní Unimbɔti lēē dikoosibil diba ki tú di ŋmɔ́ digbumbitiki subikee ní kì kūń. 8Ŋyunti ŋun ŋwìiń jɔ́m̀ee ní Unimbɔti túnní kubuŋu, kù tùm̀ kpaŋkpam, ki nyánní ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú ki jítì. Ŋwìiń wùn̄ Yoona yil ŋkpitim pu áli u bàà làá fìkī. Ní u mēē yii ŋkúm ń dāá dū-u ki lī yii: «M yaa pūtì kpíì an sɔ́ nì ḿ nīn bí dimaŋfalin.» 9Niinee ní Unimbɔti bālifì Yoona yii: «A cáá nsan kí gíí diŋuul digbumbitiki subiki nee puɔɔɔ?» Ní u kíí yii: «Iiin, m cáá nsan kí gíí diŋuul tikpil áli kí tin nyàab̀ ŋkúm.» 10Niinee ní ti-Dindaan bí yii: «Kpèè, sii bí ki sūǹ digbumbitiki subiki nee pu dee. Ama sii di kaa cóoǹ-kì, ní kaa tí kpēē-kì ní ki wíiǹ. Kunyeeu kubɔ ní kì nyáń ki wíiǹ, kunyeeu fātìi mɔ́ee ní kì kpíì. 11Ní a bí yii man ń taa sɔ̄ Niiniifi, kitiŋkpaaŋŋi nee nib saayaa! Binib bin kóò kitiŋ gbantin kaa nyí tin ŋān̄ ki tīī-bee jítì binib kutukub dilaataal nì mmuŋku pu, ní kí nín kūtì tiwaŋkuti tikpil tikpil tin kpátìi gbí ki-poonee mun.»

english_text:
1 I am Micah from Moresheth. And this is the message about Samaria and Jerusalem that the Lord gave to me when Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were the kings of Judah.
Judgment on Samaria
2Listen, all of you!
Earth and everything on it,
pay close attention.
The Lord God accuses you
from his holy temple.
3And he will come down
to crush underfoot
every pagan altar.
4Mountains will melt
beneath his feet
like wax beside a fire.
Valleys will vanish like water
rushing down a ravine.
5This will happen because of
the terrible sins of Israel,
the descendants of Jacob.
Samaria has led Israel to sin,
and pagan altars at Jerusalem
have made Judah sin.
6So the Lord will leave Samaria
in ruins—
merely an empty field
where vineyards are planted.
He will scatter its stones
and destroy its foundations.
7Samaria's idols will be smashed,
and the wages
of temple prostitutes
will be destroyed by fire.
Silver and gold from those idols
will then be used by foreigners
as payment for prostitutes.
Judah Is Doomed
8Because of this tragedy,
I go barefoot and naked.
My crying and weeping
sound like howling wolves
or ostriches.
9The nation is fatally wounded.
Judah is doomed.
Jerusalem will fall.
10Don't tell it in Gath!
Don't even cry.
Instead, roll in the dust
at Beth-Leaphrah.
11Depart naked and ashamed,
you people of Shaphir.
The town of Bethezel mourns
because no one from Zaanan
went out to help.
12Everyone in Maroth
hoped for the best,
but the Lord sent disaster
down on Jerusalem.
13Get the war chariots ready,
you people of Lachish.
You led Jerusalem into sin,
just as Israel did.
14Now you will have to give
a going-away gift
to Moresheth.
Israel's kings will discover
that they cannot trust
the town of Achzib.
15People of Mareshah,
the Lord will send someone
to capture your town.
Then Israel's glorious king
will be forced to hide
in Adullam Cave.
16Judah, shave your head
as bald as a vulture
and start mourning.
Your precious children
will be dragged off
to a foreign country.
translation_text:
1Ti-Dindaan nìn sòon̄ nì Miika un sá Mooreeseeti timbiliikin iyunti in ní Yootam nì Akaasi nì Eeseekiyaasi nìn kāl̀ kāl̀ dibeel Juuda tiŋki puee. Tibɔti tin ti-Dindaan nìn lēē ki dàkā-u Samaarii nì Jeerusaleem timmu puee sɔ̀.
Ti-Dindaan bíi wòoǹ u-nibul
2Anibul kɔkɔ nib, ní pīlifìmaan!
Kitiŋ nì bin kɔkɔ kóò ki-puee,
ní kpòom̄maan ni-tafal kí pīlifì.
Ti-Dindaan làá sòoǹ ni-tuŋkpitiŋ pu
doooo u-circir kɔŋkooŋŋun.
3Tiŋman, ti-Dindaan nyánní u-kɔŋkooŋŋun.
U sìntìń ki còom̄
ŋgbantamu yilpu kúntí kunti.
4Ajoon ŋin pu u tɔ́kɔ́ee dùntī
kii tikaliŋkpun di kā ŋŋminee,
ní atantaka fátí iwèeń
kii nnyim nín pùub̀ dijool pu puee.
5Tin bí nee kɔkɔ bāań
kun puee Jaakɔb naantiibi ŋá ikpiti,
Isirayeel yab kaa yúl̀ deedee.
Ŋma yàntī Jaakɔb naantiibi ŋáań ikpiti ní?
An kaa sá Samaarii tiŋkaaa?
Ŋma yàntī Juuda yab kóò iwaatootin ní?
An kaa sá Jeerusaleem tiŋkaaa?
6«Ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sɔ̀.
An puee m làá yàntī
Samaarii tiŋki ń kpántí adigbuŋkati ŋma
kitiŋ kin pu bi dāa ŋūǹ kí kpɔ̀ fiinyi sufiiyee.
M làá yàntī bí bíntí
u-diiŋŋi taŋkpeeŋi kí tɔ̄ nsitimin,
ní kí bìitī bi-tiŋki nyeel pu
án nīn wāĺ.
7M làá gbá kí wīī bi-waaŋi kɔkɔ,
ní kí dū tiwampɔkaal
tin bi pú-ŋee kí tɔ̄ ŋŋmin.
M làá nà awaa gbanti dúsi dusi,
di sá yii nlaakpaamu paati
ní bi dūu ká tiwan gbanti kɔkɔ,
ní tiwan gbanti làá fàtīí kpántí nlaakpaamu paati.»
Nnaabu bāań áli Jeerusaleem
8«Miika nín lī puee sɔ̀.
M làá sɔ̄ kí yāliŋkì.
M làá nīn còom̄ kaa táká anaataka,
kaa pēē tiba.
M làá gāā dituweel
kii jiiŋkpaai nín sūǹ puee,
kí nīn yáliŋkí kii taataayee.
9Di sá yii tiweendi tin Samaarii tiŋki fōōyee
kaa cáá nnyɔkɔ.
Tì nyātì ki bàn̄ Juuda tiŋki,
ki tin gūū Jeerusaleem punyɔmmu,
laakin m-nibul kóòyee.
10Ní taa māafì an bɔti Gaati tiŋkin,
taa sɔ̄maan.
Beeti-Leeyafiira tiŋkin yab,
ní dòom̄maan ntampukumin kí nīn bíntí.
11Nimbi bin kóò Safiir tiŋkinee,
kíĺmaan kuyuŋu saŋŋu
nì icoo nì dicancaŋgbeel.
Bin kóò Saanan tiŋkinee
kaa kíikí kí nyā bi-tiŋkin.
12Bin kóò Marɔti tiŋkinee
kíǹ ki sūǹ bi-ba pu
ki mèé yii mbusu ń cù ndan.
Di sá yii nnaabu ŋun nyánní ti-Dindaan ceeyee
bāań ki gūū Jeerusaleem punyɔmmu.
13Nimbi bin kóò Lakiisi tiŋkinee,
ní dū janjatɔrɔkub kí kúĺ kí lúntí itaamu.
Naa yúl̀ nì Unimbɔti deedee
kii Isirayeel yabee,
ní ki dáaĺ Jeerusaleem yab
ki kɔ́ǹ ni-tuŋkpitiŋin.
14An pu ní ni máaǹ ni nì
Mooreeseeti-Gaati tiŋkin yab
ń yàkatī tɔbin.
Akisiib tiŋkin yab kaa làá dāá ŋmā
kí jòò Isirayeel yab bɔtiibi.
15Nimbi bin kóò Mareesa tiŋkinee,
ti-Dindaan làá dū ujanjapɔɔl ubɔ
kí tɔ̄ ni-pu.
Isirayeel nigaakaabi làá dāá sāǹ
kí cù Adulaam taŋkpalɔkɔŋun kí báĺ.
16Nimbi bin kóò Jeerusaleemee,
ní cāmaan ni-yikpiti,
ní kòol̀maan dibaakpandi
ni-biyaamu mun ni néeń tikpilee pu.
Ní nīn tú dibaakpandi kii kaajiikuee,
kun puee bi làá cùnnì ni-biyaamu kuyuŋu
kitiŋ kin dátiǹ-nee poon.

english_text:
Punishment for Those Who Abuse Their Power
1Doomed! You're doomed!
At night you lie in bed,
making evil plans.
And when morning comes,
you do what you've planned
because you have the power.
2You grab any field or house
that you want;
you cheat families
out of homes and land.
3But here is what the Lord says:
“I am planning trouble for you.
Your necks will be caught
in a noose,
and you will be disgraced
in this time of disaster.”
4When that happens,
this sorrowful song
will be sung about you:
“Ruined! Completely ruined!
The Lord has taken our land
and given it to traitors.”
5And so you will never again
own property
among the Lord's people.
6“Enough of your preaching!”
That's what you tell me.
“We won't be disgraced,
so stop preaching!”
7Descendants of Jacob,
is it right for you to claim
that the Lord did what he did
because he was angry?
Doesn't he always bless
those who do right?
8My people, you have turned against
one another!
You have even stolen
clothes right off the backs
of innocent neighbors
who pass by in peace.
9You take over lovely homes
that belong to the women
of my nation.
Then you cheat their children
out of the inheritance
that comes from the Lord.
10Get out of here, you crooks!
You'll find no rest here.
You're not fit to belong
to the Lord's people,
and you will be destroyed.
11The only prophet you want
is a liar who will say,
“Drink and get drunk!”
A Promise of Hope
12I, the Lord, promise
to bring together
the people of Israel
who have survived.
I will gather them,
just as a shepherd
brings sheep together,
and there will be many.
13I will break down the gate
and lead them out—
then I will be their king.
translation_text:
Ti-Dindaan làá dáaĺ bin fìkì binibee tafal
1«Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí bin dɔ̄ kunyeeu
ki dàkafī kí ŋá tibɔkpitil
ki bɔ́ntí kí tɔ̄ atuŋkpitee!
Kutaa tin pée lì yii ku wúntéee,
bi ŋá bi nín bɔ́ntì puee,
di sá yii bi cáá an pɔŋŋu.
2Biba kpaatanti yaa kɔ́-bi nnimbitaataamee,
bi cútí ní kí fōō.
Bi yaa tí ká adiin fáatiǹ-bee,
ní bí cúú kí fōō.
Bi fìkì kudiidaan nì u-dicaŋku,
unil nì u-fakal.
3An pu ní ti-Dindaan lī yii:
<M bíi bɔ́ntí nnaabu kí tɔ̄
nimbi bin tūǹ an tuuŋŋee pu.
Naa làá dāá ŋmā kí ŋmátí.
Naa làá dāá nīn gíti còom̄ ni-yiliŋ gáań,
di sá yii an dāa sá
dinimbinaamandi yuntiŋu ní.>
4Ŋwiin gbantee, bi làá dāá gāā-ni nlan,
bi làá dāá nīn gà ŋkpiisilan nee yii:
<Bi fúkúl̀-ti pílpil.
Ti-nibul kaa ti cáá kitiŋ.
Bin bíi fúkuĺ-tee
dū ti-sati ki yākatì.»
5Too, ti-Dindaan nibul
yaa làá dāá fàtīí yàkatī tikpaatanee,
ni-kansikin báà ubɔ
kaa dāa cáá kí fōō dijandi.
Bin jáà nì Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi bɔtee
6Biba sòoǹ nì mi yii:
«Taa ti sòoǹ tin a sòoǹ nee.
Aa máaǹ kí nīn lì yii:
Icoo làá jī-ti.
7Bi ŋūǹ kí sòoǹ mimmaaa, Isirayeel yab?
Ti-Dindaan kaa ti cáá kimɔtii níii?
Míǹ ní u tūǹ u-tuuŋŋaaa?»
Mamee, m cáá dinyɔɔbummɔɔndi
kí tīī un bí deedeeyee.
8Nimbi pu ní an lī yii:
«Ni dū m-nibul ki kpántì m-nannanliibi.
Ni fòol̄ bin nyánní kujaau
ki còom̄ ki cá nì ŋgbansɔŋfee bɔkutikpaaŋŋi.
9Ni jì m-nibul nimpoobi
ki nyāntí bi-diiŋŋi ŋin bi néeńee poon.
Ni fòol̄ bi-biyaamu cee
tinyool tin m tīī-bi kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaanee.
10Yīkìmaan! Nín̄ cámaan!
An kaa sá diŋuŋfil yuntiŋu!
Ni-jɔkɔntuuŋŋi puee,
nnaabukpaan dɔ̄ ki cí-ni.»
11Binib yaa bí ki cáá kubɔcaau,
ki nāantí tinyimɔmbɔti
ki lì yii:
«Ni làá ká ndamam
nì ndaam min pɔ̄ɔ̄yee kí nyɔ̀.»
Kubɔcaau gbanti dambi gíti lì yii:
12«M làá kóoǹ ni-kɔkɔ kí kpāfì,
Jaakɔb naantiibi.
M làá kóoǹ Isirayeel yab
bin kíǹ kaa kpíìyee kí kpāfì ubaanti.
M làá kóoǹ-ni kí kpāfì ubaanti
kii ipii nín kpáfí pu kupikpuŋkpuŋunee.
Ni làá dāá bùtī kí ŋá dinikitikpaandi bí gbìl̄ ni-pu.
13Un pìitī nsanee
làá nīn līī ni-nyɔkɔpu.
Ni tɔ́ ni-ba,
dīmaan kipunyɔkɔ kí nyā.
An sá ti-Dindaan ni-bɔtiu
di līī ni-nyɔkɔpu ki kpòotī-ni.»

english_text:
Evil Rulers and Lying Prophets
1Listen to me,
you rulers of Israel!
You know right from wrong,
2but you prefer to do evil
instead of what is right.
You skin my people alive.
You strip off their flesh,
3break their bones,
cook it all in a pot,
and gulp it down.
4Someday you will beg the Lord
to help you,
but he will turn away
because of your sins.
5You lying prophets promise
security for anyone
who gives you food,
but disaster for anyone
who refuses to feed you.
Here is what the Lord says
to you prophets:
6“You will live in the dark,
far from the sight of the sun,
with no message from me.
7You prophets and fortunetellers
will all be disgraced,
with no message from me.”
8But the Lord has filled me
with power and his Spirit.
I have been given the courage
to speak about justice
and to tell you people of Israel
that you have sinned.
9So listen to my message,
you rulers of Israel!
You hate justice
and twist the truth.
10You make cruelty and murder
a way of life in Jerusalem.
11You leaders accept bribes
for dishonest decisions.
You priests and prophets
teach and preach,
but only for money.
Then you say,
“The Lord is on our side.
No harm will come to us.”
12 And so, because of you,
Jerusalem will be plowed under
and left in ruins.
Thorns will cover the mountain
where the temple now stands.
translation_text:
Bi bíi kpáafí bikpootiliibi
1Ama man bí yii:
«Pīlifìmaan, nimbi bin kpòotī Jaakɔb naantiibee,
nimbi Isirayeel nibul bɔsoonliibi.
Nimbi di kaa bàà máaǹ
kí nīn nyí tin bí deedeeyeeee?
2Ama nimbi di ná tin ŋān̄ee
ní ki néeń tin kaa ŋān̄ee.
Ni cátí binib gbaŋŋu ki bìitī
tiwunnan nì akpab pu.»
3Bi ŋmóò m-nibul nanti kii upeecuncutee.
Bi lèekī bi-gbaŋŋu
kii naŋkoosinaa nín lèekī puee,
ki kɔ́fí bi-kpabiŋ,
ki càkà bi-nanti
kii an sá tinan ní
bi làá tɔ́kɔń dikumboolinee.
4An pu ní bi yaa láa kúuǹ ki yíiń ti-Dindaanee,
waa làá dāá kíí-bi.
Ŋyunti gbantee,
u làá dāá fàtī u-kpaŋkpamboon kí tīī-bi,
atuŋkpiti ŋin kɔkɔ bi ŋée pu.
Inyimɔn bɔnaatiliibi bɔkpaaŋi
5Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ bibɔnaatiliibi bin mɔ́ntí m-nibulee pu puee sèé:
«Bin yaa tīī-bi njimee,
bi lì yii Unimbɔti ń tīī-bi ŋgbansɔŋfi.
Ama bin kaa tìì-bi tiba bí jēe,
bi jáà nì bi.
6An puee kunyeeu làá mɔ́ ni-pu,
naa làá ti ká aleedaka.
Dibɔmbɔndi làá jēetí ni-pu,
naa làá ti ká tiba kí sòoǹ.
Ŋwìiń làá jēetí ni-pu,
ní ŋwiimpu ń dūú kpántí dibɔmbɔndi.»
7Icoo làá cúú bin wāĺee
nì bin būūyee.
Bi làá bìin̄ bi-nyɔɔkuti pu,
kun puee Unimbɔti kaa ti kíikí-bi.
8Ama mamee, nì ti-Dindaan Fam puee,
m cáá mpɔn,
ki nyí tin bí deedeeyee,
ki cáá dipɔbil.
M ŋūǹ kí yàntī Jaakɔb naantiibi,
Isirayeel nibul ń béé
bi-yìntitam nì bi-kpitii.
Jeerusaleem tiŋki làá wīī
9Pīlifìmaan tin bí nee,
nimbi Jaakɔb naantiibi kpootiliibi,
nimbi Isirayeel nibul bɔsoonliibi.
Ni ná tin bí deedeeyee,
kaa sòoǹ tibɔti ibaamɔn.
10Ni kù binib ki kāntí animbil
ki cáa nyāantí Siiyɔn tiŋki.
Ni wɔ́b̀ binib ki kāntí animbil
ki cáa nyāantí Jeerusaleem.
11Bibɔsoonliibi fòol̄ tiwampɔkaal
ní ki sòoǹ binib bɔti,
bisaraaŋaliibi dàkà Unimbɔti marab
ní bi pà-bi,
ní Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliibi fòol̄ animbil
ní kí nín nàatī Unimbɔti bɔti.
Ti-Dindaan yindi pu ní bi tɔ́kɔ́
ki ŋáań tíǹ kɔkɔ ki lì yii:
«Ti-Dindaan bí ti-cee.
Nnaabu ŋubɔ kpá ki làá jēetí ti-pu.»
12Too, ni-puee, bi làá kpɔ̀ Siiyɔn tiŋki
kii bi nín kù bukpaa puee,
ní Jeerusaleem tiŋki
ń kpántí adigbun ŋma,
ní ikuŋkum ń nyā kí múkúǹ
dijool din pu bi máń
kunimbɔtidii ki tɔ́kɔ́ǹee.

english_text:
Peace and Prosperity
1In the future, the mountain
with the Lord's temple
will be the highest of all.
It will reach above the hills,
and every nation
will rush to it.
2People of many nations
will come and say,
“Let's go up to the mountain
of the Lord God of Jacob
and worship in his temple.”
The Lord will teach us his Law
from Jerusalem,
and we will obey him.
3 He will settle arguments
between distant
and powerful nations.
They will pound their swords
and their spears
into rakes and shovels;
they will never again make war
or attack one another.
4 Everyone will find rest
beneath their own fig trees
or grape vines,
and they will live in peace.
This is a solemn promise
of the Lord All-Powerful.
5Others may follow their gods,
but we will always follow
the Lord our God.
The Lord Will Lead His People Home
6The Lord said:
At that time
I will gather my people—
the lame and the outcasts,
and all others into whose lives
I have brought sorrow.
7Then the lame and the outcasts
will belong to my people
and become a strong nation.
I, the Lord, will rule them
from Mount Zion forever.
8Mount Zion in Jerusalem,
guardian of my people,
you will rule again.
9Jerusalem, why are you crying?
Don't you have a king?
Have your advisors gone?
Are you suffering
like a woman in childbirth?
10Keep on groaning with pain,
you people of Jerusalem!
If you escape from your city
to the countryside,
you will still be taken
as prisoners to Babylonia.
But later I will rescue you
from your enemies.
11Zion, because of your sins
you are surrounded
by many nations who say,
“We can hardly wait
to see you disgraced.”
12But they don't know
that I, the Lord,
have gathered them here
to grind them like grain.
13Smash them to pieces, Zion!
I'll let you be like a bull
with iron horns
and bronze hoofs.
Crush those nations
and bring their wealth to me,
the Lord of the earth.
translation_text:
Jeerusaleem, ŋgbansɔŋfi tiŋyil
1«Ŋwiin bí ki dòoń,
dijool din pu ti-Dindaan Diiku tɔ́kɔ́ee
làá dāá nīn tɔ́kɔ́ ajoon kɔkɔ pu,
di làá dāá nīn fɔ̀kɔǹ ŋgbantamu kɔkɔ.
Anibul làá dāá nīn bìtifī ki dòoń di-cee.
2Atimbun tikpil làá dāá tàkan̄ nsan
ki cá ki lì yii:
<Dāam̄maan tí jɔ̄m̀ ti-Dindaan jool pu,
tí jɔ̄m̀maan Jaakɔb Nimbɔtiu Diikun!
U làá dàkà-ti kun u là tí ŋée
ní tí nóó u-sàmbiyaamu.>
Tiŋman, Siiyɔn ní Mara làá nyānní,
u-nyɔɔbundi làá nyānní Jeerusaleem ní.
3U làá dāá sòoǹ kí ŋāŋkì
anibul tikpil kansikin bɔti,
kí dāá ŋāŋkì atimbun ŋin cáá mpɔn
ki bínní ndandatee kansikin bɔti.
Binib làá dāá dū bi-tàataajimmu
kí dūú mɔ́ɔ́ akoo,
ní kí dāá dū bi-kpammu
kí mɔ́ɔ́ igɔti.
Ditimbundi diba kaa dāa gíti
jáà nì di-juti,
ní binib kaa dāa bífí kujaau.
4Báà ŋma dāa kíǹ ki kā
u-fiinyi nì u-fiigi sufii taapu,
ní ubɔ kaa dāa bí kí páb́-u.»
Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di sòon̄ míǹ.
5Ditimbundi kamaa ŋáań
tin làá fáatíǹ di-waaŋee ní,
ama timbi làá nīn ŋáań tin làá fáatíǹ
ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiuee ní kí nīn cá jaanjaan.
Ti-Dindaan làá jī dibeel Jeerusaleem tiŋkin
6Ti-Dindaan lī yii:
«Ŋyunti gbantee, m làá kóoǹní
bin fōō tiweendee kí kpāfì,
m làá gíiǹní bin tafal m dáaĺ
ki yāntì bi yàl̄ ki bínní kuyuŋuee.
7Bin fōō tiweendi gbantee,
m làá dū-bi kí náań dinibul din bí dimaŋfalinee.
Bin bínní kuyuŋunee,
m làá dū-bi kí kpántí ditimbundi din pɔ̄ɔ̄yee.
Man bi-Dindaan
di làá dāá nīn sá bi-bɔtiu
Siiyɔn jool pu,
kí yòon̄ ŋyunti gbanti
kí nīn cáa cá jaanjaan!
8Sii Jeerusaleem jool,
a wúǹ dinibul pu
kii upikpaal nín tɔ̄kɔntí kudifɔkɔu pu
ki kpèé u-piii puee ní.
A làá fàtīí ká mpɔn ŋun a nìn cáá njaminee.
A làá fàtīí kpántí dibeel tiŋyil.»
Jeerusaleem làá kɔ́ agìńni ní kí ŋmátí
9Kɔŋkɔnnee Jeerusaleem yab,
ba pu ní ni sūǹ ki tátí míǹ?
Ba pu ní ni bí ki yáliŋkí
kii imatiŋween di bāań-nee?
Naa ti cáá ubɔti níii?
Ni-saŋkiliibi kpíì níii?
10Nín̄ yáliŋkí nì ni-ba,
kí nīn kūuntí kii
upɔdaan di bíi màal̀ee.
Di sá yii kɔŋkɔnnee ni làá nyā kitiŋin
kí tin nín̄ kóò tisatin,
áli kí tin bà Babiloon tiŋkin.
Niin ní bi làá dā-ni kí líí,
niin ní ti-Dindaan làá fīī-ni kí nyāntí
ni-nannanliibi ŋaan.
11Kɔŋkɔnnee Jeerusaleem, atimbun tikpil
kóoǹ ki kpáfì kí já nì si.
Ŋi lì yii: «Tí bīil̀-kì!
Bi yaa nāaǹ Siiyɔn tiŋki,
án làá nīn mɔ̄ǹ-teeee!»
12Atimbun gbanti nín kaa nyí
ti-Dindaan nín bɔ́ntì kí ŋá pu,
kaa nyí u-landɔkɔyee pu ní ŋi ŋáań míǹ.
Úǹ là kí kóoǹ-ŋi kí kpāfì
kii bi nín kōontí idi kí bíĺ
dinaapaal pu kí gbée ní.
13Nimbi bin kóò Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee,
yīkìmaan kí gbá idi.
M làá yàntī ní nīn pɔ̄ɔ̄
kii unaa un yiŋyi sá tikúti
ní u-tafuŋfukuti sá tasa kútee.
Ni làá nàan̄ anibul tikpil.
Tigaajawan tin ni làá fōō bi-ceeyee,
ní dū-tì kí sú man ni-Dindaan,
duulinya kɔkɔ kpiliu.
14Kɔŋkɔnnee, nimbi bin kóò Jeerusaleemee,
kóom̀maan kí kpāfì.
Binannanliibi māntìi tú-ti kí jáǹ-ti.
Bi ŋúb́ ndɔ ki fátí
Isirayeel bɔsoonliu nimbiin.

english_text:
A Promised Ruler
1Jerusalem, enemy troops
have surrounded you;
they have struck Israel's ruler
in the face with a stick.
2 Bethlehem Ephrath,
you are one of the smallest towns
in the nation of Judah.
But the Lord will choose
one of your people
to rule the nation—
someone whose family
goes back to ancient times.
3The Lord will abandon Israel
only until this ruler is born,
and the rest of his family
returns to Israel.
4Like a shepherd
taking care of his sheep,
this ruler will lead
and care for his people
by the power and glorious name
of the Lord his God.
His people will live securely,
and the whole earth will know
his true greatness,
5because he will bring peace.
Assyria Will Be Defeated
Let Assyria attack our country
and our palaces.
We will counterattack,
led by a number of rulers
6 whose strong army will defeat
the nation of Assyria.
Yes, our leaders will rescue us,
if those Assyrians
dare to invade our land.
The Survivors Will Be Safe
7A few of Jacob's descendants
survived and are scattered
among the nations.
But the Lord will let them
cover the earth like dew and rain
that refreshes the soil.
8At present they are scattered,
but later they will attack,
as though they were fierce lions
pouncing on sheep.
Their enemies will be torn
to shreds,
with no one to save them;
9they will be helpless,
completely destroyed.
Idols Will Be Destroyed in Israel
10The Lord said:
At that time I will wipe out
your cavalry and chariots,
11as well as your cities
and your fortresses.
12I will stop you
from telling fortunes
and practicing witchcraft.
13You will no longer worship
the idols or stone images
you have made—
I will destroy them,
14together with the sacred poles
and even your towns.
15I will become furious
and take revenge on the nations
that refuse to obey me.
translation_text:
Ubɔti ufiil làá nyánní Beetileem tiŋkin ní
1Sii Beetileem Eefiraata,
Juuda timmu kansikinee,
sii di sá kitiŋwaŋwaai.
Ama sii poon ní m làá yàntī
ubɔti un làá kpòotī
m-nibul Isirayeelee ń nyānní.
U-nyeeŋŋu kíliń doooo cannaaku ní,
iyunti kpiŋkpiki poon.
2Ti-Dindaan làá dū u-nibul kí fá
ŋyunti ŋubɔ poon,
kí nīn cí ŋyunti ŋun ní
unimpu un làá màal̀-uee
ń dāá màal̀-u.
Ŋyunti gbantee, u-nabiyaamu
mun làá dāá kíń kí nīn bí dimaŋfalinee
làá dāá dāan̄ kí kūtì
Isirayeel yab bin kíǹee pu.
3Ubɔti gbantee làá dāá yīkì
kí dū ti-Dindaan pɔŋŋu,
ti-Dindaan u-Nimbɔtiu yiŋkpaandi kí kpàà-bi.
U-nibul làá dāá nīn bí ŋgbansɔŋfin.
Di sá yii u-kpaanti làá dāá gbìtī
kí bà ilaan kɔkɔ.
4Úǹ di làá dāá cáań ŋgbansɔŋfi!
Asuur yab yaa láa kɔ́nní ti-tiŋkin,
bi-taaŋi yaa láa tāā ti-beeciŋŋinee,
ti làá dāá lēē ti-kpilib kupaau
bí já nì bi.
5Bi làá dāá dū kitàataajiki kí já nì Asuur tiŋki
kí dāá dū kijisaakaai kí já nì Niimroodi tiŋki.
Asuur yab yaa láa dòoń kí já nì ti
ní ki kɔ́nní ti-tiŋkinee,
ti-bɔtiuee làá dāá fīī-ti.
Isirayeel yab bin kíǹee pɔŋŋu
6Jaakɔb naantiibi bin làá dāá kíń
kí nīn bí anibul tikpil kansikinee
làá dāá nīn náań nì dimalindi
din nyánní ti-Dindaan ceeyee ní,
kii utaa nín nì ki sɔ̀ŋkī timool puee.
Baa làá nīn kā ki máká unil pu,
kaa làá nīn kā ki cɔ́tí nisaal pu.
7Jaakɔb naantiibi bin làá dāá kíń
kí nīn bí atimbunni,
anibul kupaau kansikinee,
bi làá dāá nīn bí kii gbikintee ní
kupɔɔun peelii kansikin,
kii digbikintipɔmbil
din bí tipicaŋkpun kansikinee ní.
U yaa pée jítì laakin kamaayee,
u cútí ipeel ní ki tɔ̀ntī,
ní ubɔ kaa ŋūǹ kí fīī-i.
8«Dúkutí a-ŋal a-nannanliu pu
kí nà kí dóó bin ná-see kɔkɔ.»
Ti-Dindaan làá kúntí dimákakulindi
9«Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀.
Tin làá dāá bàń ŋwiin gbantee sèé:
<M làá dāá nàan̄ a-taamui,
ní kí dāá kúntí a-janjatɔrɔkub.
10M làá dāá nàan̄ a-timmu,
ní kí dāá wīī agun ŋin a máń ki tú a-timmuee.
11M làá dāá kúntí kusoou tuuŋŋi ni-kansikin.
Baa dāa gíti kāntí u-kpaŋkpanti ni-kansikin.
12M làá dāá kúntí awaa
nì ataŋkpee ŋin ni cóoǹ ki tòotēe.
Naa ti làá gbàan̄ tiwan tin
ni dū ni-ŋalii ki máńee nimbiin.
13M làá dāá cóotí ni-windɔi,
ní kí kúntí ni-timmu.
14Nì mbum nì diŋuul poon
ní m làá dāá tɔ̀ atimbun ŋin
kaa tɔ́-mee ipɔntoon.»

english_text:
The Lord's Challenge to His People
1The Lord said to his people:
Come and present your case
to the hills and mountains.
2Israel, I am bringing charges
against you—
I call upon the mountains
and the earth's firm foundation
to be my witnesses.
3My people, have I wronged you
in any way at all?
Please tell me.
4 I rescued you from Egypt,
where you were slaves.
I sent Moses, Aaron, and Miriam
to be your leaders.
5 Don't forget the evil plans
of King Balak of Moab
or what Balaam son of Beor
said to him.
Remember how I, the Lord,
saved you many times
on your way from Acacia
to Gilgal.
True Obedience
6What offering should I bring
when I bow down to worship
the Lord God Most High?
Should I try to please him
by sacrificing
calves a year old?
7Will thousands of sheep
or rivers of olive oil
make God satisfied with me?
Should I sacrifice to the Lord
my first-born child as payment
for my terrible sins?
8The Lord God has told us
what is right
and what he demands:
“See that justice is done,
let mercy be your first concern,
and humbly obey your God.”
Cheating and Violence
9I am the Lord,
and you are wise to respect
my power to punish.
So listen to my message
for the city of Jerusalem:
10You store up stolen treasures
and use dishonest scales.
11But I, the Lord, will punish you
for cheating with weights
and with measures.
12You rich people are violent,
and everyone tells lies.
13Because of your sins,
I will wound you and leave you
ruined and defenseless.
14You will eat,
but still be hungry;
you will store up goods,
but lose everything—
I, the Lord, will let it all
be captured in war.
15You won't harvest what you plant
or use the oil
from your olive trees
or drink the wine
from grapes you grow.
16 Jerusalem, this will happen
because you followed
the sinful example
of kings Omri and Ahab.
Now I will destroy you
and your property.
Then the people of every nation
will make fun and insult you.
translation_text:
Ti-Dindaan nì u-nibul cáá ibɔsoon
1Ní pīlifìmaan tibɔti tin ti-Dindaan sòon̄ee.
Yīkì kí sòoǹ kí mɔ̄tì m-pu
ajoon nimbiin,
kí mɔ̄tì m-pu ŋgbantamu nimbiin.
2Nimbi ajoon nì dinyeel din pu
kitiŋ tɔ́kɔ́ kaa cìŋkēe, pīlifìmaan.
Ti-Dindaan yíiń u-nibul ibeeyiin,
u bíi sòoǹ Isirayeel yab bɔti.
3U bí yii: «M-nibul, ba ní m ŋá-si ní?
Digìńdi dilal poon ní m kɔ́ǹ-si ní?
Á kíí-mi!
4M nín nyántìń-si Eejipiti tiŋkineeyaaa,
m nín dá-si ki nyántì kuyuŋuneeyaaa,
m nín tú Mooyiisi nì Aarɔn nì Miiriyam
bí kpòotī-see ní m yīntì ní.
5M-nibul, á téetí tin bí nee!
Moowaab bɔtiu Balaaki
nìn bɔ́ntì kí ŋá-si tikpitil.
Téetí tin Beewɔɔr jipɔɔn
Balaam nìn kíí-uee.
Míǹ boonee, a yíkì Siitiim tantakalin
ki cūtì Giilgaal paaŋŋu pu.
A nìn ŋúń ki ká tiŋaŋkpaandi
tin man a-Dindaan ŋá ki tīī-see.»
Unimbɔti nín là unil ń nīn bí puee
6Ti yaa dɔ́miń kí jāam̀ ti-Dindaanee,
ba ní ti máaǹ kí nīn ŋúb́
kí cáań kí ŋá saraa kí tīī
Yilpu Fɔ́ŋŋŋ Nimbɔtiu dee?
Ti kalin cāabìń dibindi diba nabil
kí ŋá saraa kí tīī-uaaa?
7U là ipijaa kutukub naaa,
ŋkpam ń nīn pùub̀
ibun kutukub kutukub poon ní?
Tí dū ti-jipɔŋkpilib kí ŋá saraa ti-yìntitam puɔɔɔ,
ti nín dù ti-poon naŋu
kí ŋá saraa ti-kpitii pu ní?
8Unil, ti-Dindaan dàkā-si tin ŋān̄ee.
Kun u bàlifī-see di sá
á nīn ŋáań tin bí deedeeyee,
kí nīn néeń ki ŋáań tikɔkɔ nì tiniti
ní kí nīn nóó a-Nimbɔtiu nì dibasintil.
Inaamuul dambi nì bi ŋáań tipɔmbɔtee tafadaaldi
9Ti-Dindaan bíi sòoǹ nì
bin kóò kitiŋ nee poonee!
U làá fīī bin fàŋkí-uee.
«Pīlifìmaan, Juuda naakookun yab,
nimbi bin kɔkɔ kóoǹ ki
kpáfì kitiŋ nee poonee!
10Binikpitib dumpuyee,
bi kāntí tigaajawan
tin bi mūul̀ binib ki kée ní.
Di sá yii ni cáá tiwaŋŋmantikaal
tin kaa bí deedeeyee ki mùul̄ binib.
An sá ntimbiil tuuŋŋi ní.
Maa ŋūǹ kí nīn wāĺ míǹ kí nīn kā ki ŋmí.
11Biba tútì bi-saniyab
baa ti ŋmàntī tiwan deedee,
ki cáá bi-lookun ataŋkpee ŋin
bi cáa ŋmàntī nnyiŋfee mili pu
ki cáa mùul̄ binib.
Ḿ sòoǹ kí pɔ̀ binib gbantaaa?
12Kitiŋ nee gaajab fìkì binib ŋma ní.
Ki-nib sá binyimɔndambi ní.
Bi yaa pée wāaǹ kinyɔkɔ kí sòoǹee,
an sá kí kīil̀ binib ní.
13An pu ní m dū falaa ki gbáń-ni,
ki làá nàan̄-ni ni-kpitii pu.
14Ni làá jī ama kaa làá díkì,
ŋkùm làá nīn pée bí ni-dicaŋŋin ní.
Ni làá dāá kpāafì ni-kpaajinti,
ama tì làá bùkū.
Báà ni yaa láa kpáafì ni-wanti tibaaa,
m làá dāá bīil̀-tì kujaaun.
15Ni làá dāá kpɔ̀ kí bɔ̄l̀,
ama kaa làá dāá ŋmā kí cā.
Ni làá dāá ŋmáaḿ kí lēē ɔliifi subiliŋ kpam,
ama kaa làá dāá ká-mì kí ŋmìtī.
Ni làá dāá ŋàan̄ ndaam,
ama kaa làá dāá nyɔ̀-mì.
16Ni nóó ubɔti Oomirii
nì u-jipɔɔn Akaab
dicaŋkun yab bimbikpitim.
Ni ŋáań kii binib gbanti nín ŋáań puee.
An pu ní m làá nàan̄ ni-tiŋki,
ní kí yàntī bin kíǹee ń nīn bèel̄
nimbi bin kóò ki-nee.
Icoo in jíń m-nibulee
làá jī ni mun.»

english_text:
Israel Is Corrupt
1I feel so empty inside—
like someone starving
for grapes or figs,
after the vines and trees
have all been picked clean.
2No one is loyal to God;
no one does right.
Everyone is brutal
and eager to deceive
everyone else.
3People cooperate to commit crime.
Judges and leaders demand bribes,
and rulers cheat in court.
4The most honest of them
is worse than a thorn patch.
Your doom has come!
Lookouts sound the warning,
and everyone panics.
5Don't trust anyone,
not even your best friend,
and be careful what you say
to the one you love.
6 Sons refuse to respect
their own fathers,
daughters rebel against
their own mothers,
and daughters-in-law despise
their mothers-in-law.
Your family is now your enemy.
7But I trust the Lord God
to save me,
and I will wait for him
to answer my prayer.
The Nation Turns to God
8My enemies, don't be glad
because of my troubles!
I may have fallen,
but I will get up;
I may be sitting in the dark,
but the Lord is my light.
9I have sinned against the Lord.
And so I must endure his anger,
until he comes to my defense.
But I know that I will see him
making things right for me
and leading me to the light.
10You, my enemies, said,
“The Lord God is helpless.”
Now each of you
will be disgraced
and put to shame.
I will see you trampled
like mud in the street.
A Bright Future
11Towns of Judah, the day is coming
when your walls will be rebuilt,
and your boundaries enlarged.
12People will flock to you
from Assyria and Egypt,
from Babylonia
and everywhere else.
13Those nations will suffer disaster
because of what they did.
Micah's Prayer and the Lord's Answer
14Lead your people, Lord!
Come and be our shepherd.
Grasslands surround us,
but we live in a forest.
So lead us to Bashan and Gilead,
and let us find pasture
as we did long ago.
15I, the Lord, will work miracles
just as I did when I led you
out of Egypt.
16Nations will see this
and be ashamed because
of their helpless armies.
They will be in shock,
unable to speak or hear,
17because of their fear of me,
your Lord and God.
Then they will come trembling,
crawling out of their fortresses
like insects or snakes,
lapping up the dust.
No One Is Like God
The people said:
18Our God, no one is like you.
We are all that is left
of your chosen people,
and you freely forgive
our sin and guilt.
You don't stay angry forever;
you're glad to have pity
19and pleased to be merciful.
You will trample on our sins
and throw them in the sea.
20You will keep your word
and be faithful to Jacob
and to Abraham,
as you promised our ancestors
many years ago.
translation_text:
Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu yaliŋkii
1Óo, man falaau na!
M sá kii unil un di nyáń
kí kìtī fiinyi subiliŋ
ŋyunti ŋun ní bi kìtī-ŋee ní,
ki cūtì kí nyàab̀ fiinyi biliŋ
ŋyunti ŋun bi kītì-ŋi ki dóòyee ní.
Báà difiinyisakal diba kaa kíǹ!
Báà difiigipɔmbil din
m néeńee kaa bí!
2Bin yú nì Unimbɔti deedeeyee
kúntì kitiŋ nee pu,
báà ubulcinnil ubɔbɔ kaa ti bí.
Báà unil kaa ti bí ki-ni ki yú deedee nì Unimbɔti.
Bi-kɔkɔ pée dàkafī nnikpaakoon pu ní.
Báà ŋma pīil̀ u-juti kutaliŋŋu.
3Bi yáb̀ kí ŋá ikpiti.
Kí wàatī bí ŋá tiŋanee,
bibɔtiibi sīintí bi nín là puee,
ní bibɔsoonliibi sīintí kunimbiŋmiiu,
ní akpambal lì bi nín là puee.
4Bi-kansikin un pée sá unimɔntee
bí kii abɔjanaakunee ní,
un pée sá deedeedaanee
jítiǹ kukuŋkuncikuu pu.
Ni-tafadaaldi yuntiŋu bāań dee.
Ni-bɔnaatiliibi bin cí-nee
nìn sòon̄ an pu.
Too, kɔŋkɔnnee, naa ti nyí tin poon ni bée.
5Ní taa fōō ni-jutiibi bɔti kí kíí,
kí taa nín̄ máká ni-bɔɔbi pu.
Báà sii a-ba nimpuu nimbiin gba,
á nīn nyí nì a-ba nì tin a sòoǹee.
6Di sá yii kibininjabiki sìí ki-baa,
ní kinimpubiki jáà nì ki-na,
ní unimpu nì u-beel kaa kpí.
Báà ŋma nannanliu sá u-dicaŋkun yɔu ní.
7Ama mamee, ti-Dindaan watil pú ní m kpèé,
Unimbɔti un làá fīī-mee pu ní m máká.
M-Nimbɔtiu làá pīlifiǹ-mi.
Isirayeel yab máká Unimbɔti pu
8Nimbi ti-nannanliibi, ní taa nín̄ fàal̀maan
tin bāań-ti nee pu.
Báà ti yaa lítì,
ti làá fàtīí yīkì.
Báà ti yaa bí dibɔmbɔndin,
ti-Dindaan di sá ti-walifiŋu.
9Diŋuul din ti-Dindaan gíí ti-puee,
ti máaǹ kí fōō-dì,
kun puee ti yīntiǹ-u.
Ama ŋyunti bí ki dòoń,
u làá sòoǹ ti-bɔti kí pɔ̀-ti.
U làá dāá nyāntí-ti kí gíiǹ ŋwalifin,
kí gbéeǹ-ti u-ŋanti.
10Ti-nannanliibi yaa láa ká mimmee,
bi làá dāá kɔ́ icoo ni.
Bíǹ bin nìn bàlifī-ti yii:
«Ni-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiuee bí lee?»
Bi làá dāá tāā-bi kí ŋmàtifì
kii adan pu kpatee.
Ti làá dāá ká míǹ nì ti-nimbibulii.
11Ŋwiin bí ki dòoń,
bi làá dāá fàtīí mā digundi
kí tū ni-tiŋyil.
Ŋwiin gbantee,
ni-tiŋki làá dāá wàan̄ kí kūtì.
12Ŋwiin gbantee, ni-nabiyaamu
làá dāá fàtīí gítiń ni-cee.
Bi làá dāá nyānní
Asuur nì Eejipiti timmun,
Niil nì Eefiraati mɔɔgbaŋŋi,
kí nyānní tiŋku ubɔ kí cáá sāā un kíǹee,
dijool diba kí cáá sāā din kíǹee kí dāan̄.
13Kitiŋ laakin kɔkɔ kíǹee
làá dāá kpántí kuteeu
binib bin kóò ki-puee kpitii pu.
14Ti-Dindaan, dū a-pikpaadɔŋu
kí kpàà a-nibul din sá a-fakalee.
Dì bí kuteeun di-baba
isufi in lòoǹ abilee māntìi tú-dì.
Péetí-dì kí cùnnì Baasan pikpaakun
nì Galaadi tiŋkin kii dooooyee.
15Kii ŋyunti ŋun a nìn
nyántìń-ti Eejipiti tiŋkinee,
gíti ŋá a-maamaaci tuuŋŋi kí dàkà-ti.
16Atimbun ŋin kíǹee nib làá dāá ká míǹ
ní icoo ń dāá cúú-bi,
min kamaa bi cáá mpɔnee.
Bi làá dāá cúú bi-nyɔmmu,
ní bi-tafaliŋ ń kpáá baa ti gbìl̀.
17Bi làá dāá bàlim̀ ntampukumin
kii ikoobu nì ipeel in fù i-biŋŋi puee.
Bi làá dāá nyānní bi-balilaŋki
bi-wunti jìkì kí dāan̄
sii ti-Dindaan ti-Nimbɔtiu cee.
Bi làá dāá fàŋkì-si.
18Ti-Dindaan, Unimbɔti ulɔu
di gíti bí kii sisee?
A lèekī a-nibul din kíǹ
ki bí dimaŋfalinee yìntitam,
ki pūǹ di-kpitii.
Aa fòol̄ diŋuul kí nīn cá jaanjaan,
ama an mɔ̄ǹ-si
á nīn dàkà-ti a-ŋanti.
19A làá fàtīí tí sɔ̄ ti-saai,
a làá tāā ti-yìntitam kí múĺ,
ní kí dū ti-kpitii kí tɔ̄ tiŋku taapu taapu.
20A làá dàkà Jaakɔb naantiibi a-deedeeu,
kí dàkà Abraam naantiibi a-laŋŋaŋfitiiku,
kii a nín nìn pūtì ki pōoǹ
ti-baabi dooooyee puee.

english_text:
1 I am Nahum from Elkosh. And this is the message that I wrote down about Nineveh.
The Fierce Anger of the Lord
2The Lord God demands loyalty.
In his anger, he takes revenge
on his enemies.
3The Lord is powerful,
yet patient;
he makes sure that the guilty
are always punished.
He can be seen in storms
and in whirlwinds;
clouds are the dust from his feet.
4At the Lord's command,
oceans and rivers dry up.
Bashan, Mount Carmel,
and Lebanon wither,
and their flowers fade.
5At the sight of the Lord,
mountains and hills
tremble and melt;
the earth and its people
shudder and shake.
6Who can stand the heat
of his furious anger?
It flashes out like fire
and shatters stones.
The Power of Assyria Will Be Broken
7The Lord is good.
He protects those who trust him
in times of trouble.
8But like a roaring flood,
the Lord chases his enemies
into dark places
and destroys them.
9So don't plot against the Lord!
He wipes out his enemies,
and they never revive.
10They are like drunkards
overcome by wine,
or like twisted thornbushes
burning in a fire.
11Assyria, one of your rulers
has made evil plans
against the Lord.
12But the Lord says, “Assyria,
no matter how strong you are,
you will be cut down!
My people Judah,
I have troubled you before,
but I won't do it again.
13I'll snap your chains
and set you free
from the Assyrians.”
14Assyria, this is what else
the Lord says to you:
“Your name will be forgotten.
I will destroy every idol
in your temple,
and I will send you to the grave,
because you are worthless.”
15 Look toward the mountains,
people of Judah!
Here comes a messenger
with good news of peace.
Celebrate your festivals.
Keep your promises to God.
Your evil enemies are destroyed
and will never again
invade your country.
translation_text:
1Kugbɔŋu nee poonee, tibɔti tin sòoǹ Niiniifi tiŋki puee kā. Tibɔti gbantee, Unimbɔti lēē-tì ki dàkā Nawum un sá ueelikoosjee.
Ti-Dindaan gíí Niiniifi tiŋki pu diŋuul
2Ti-Dindaan sá Unimbɔti un cáá ipoompoonee
ní ki tɔ̀ ipɔntoon.
U dátí bin jáà nì uee tafal.
U-ŋuul pɔ̄ɔ̄ an kaa cáá bí lì.
U tɔ̀ u-nannanliibi ipɔntoon,
ní kaa súntí bi-kpitii in bi ŋáańee pu.
3Ti-Dindaan kaa fòol̄ diŋuul malaa
ní ki cáá mpɔŋkpaan,
ama waa yàntī dibɔkpil daan fám
kaa dáaĺ u-tafal.
Kunaakpaabuŋŋu nì kubuŋkpaaŋŋu
poon ní u còom̄.
Atagban di sá u yaa tà, kukpɔŋkpɔŋu kun yíkée.
4U kpàtī tiŋku pu ní ú kpā,
ní ki yàntī ibun kɔkɔ nyim fóotí.
Baasan pɔɔku nì Kaarmeel jool mooti fáaḿ,
ní Leebanɔn pumpukum yɔ́ĺ.
5U yaa dòońee, ajoon cìŋkī ní,
ní ŋgbantamu kpìkitī.
U yaa páaǹnée kitiŋ cìŋkī,
ní binib bin kɔkɔ bí ki-puee jìkì.
6U yaa fōō diŋuulee, ŋma di ŋūǹ kí ŋmátí?
U yaa fōō mbumee, ŋma di ŋūǹ kí yūĺ?
U-ŋuul fòol̄ bìlbil kii ŋŋmee ní,
ataŋkpee gba wìil̄ u-nimbiin ní.
7Ti-Dindaan ŋān̄!
U sá kibalilaŋ ní dinimbinaamandi yuntiŋu poon.
U wúǹ bin di sáń ki kóò-uee pu,
8báà digìńdi yaa dɔ́miń ki bīiǹ bi-pu kii nnyiŋgbeenee.
Ama u làá nàan̄ bin bí ki jáà nì uee,
ní kí jà u-nannanliibi kí kɔ́ǹ dibɔmbɔndin.
Tin ti-Dindaan sòon̄ Juuda nì Niiniifi puee
9Ba ní ni bíi bɔ́ntí ti-Dindaan pu?
Úǹ di nàantí u-nannanliibi,
ní baa ti làá wɔ́b́-ni nliliitiim.
10Di sá yii bi bí kii abɔjanaakun ŋin sɔ̀kɔ̄ee ní,
bíǹ bin nyù idafi ki gbéèyee.
Ŋŋmi làá wà-bi múb kii timɔkulindee ní.
11Unil un bíi bɔ́ntí kí já nì ti-Dindaanee,
unil un di cáá ilandɔkɔkpitee
nyánní sii Niiniifi tiŋkin ní.
12Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé:
«Báà ni-nannanliibi yaa wīikí ki pɔ̄ɔ̄,
m làá nàan̄-bi ní bí kúntí múb.
M sīntiǹ-ni taapu,
maa ti làá ŋá míǹ.
13Kɔŋkɔnnee, m làá nyìkitī diwaŋgul
din bi dūu nyīkiǹ ni-puee,
ní kí tìl̄ ni-kusakai.»
14Ti-Dindaan nín sòon̄ tin
nimbi Niiniifi yab puee sèé:
«Naa ti làá màal̀ mbiyaamu
mun làá dāá fōō ni-yindee.
M làá kúntí awaakpitikaa nì amɔɔkaa
ŋin bí ni-waadiikunee.
M bíi bɔ́ntí ni-kaakul,
di sá yii naa bí tiban.»

english_text:
Nineveh Will Fall
1Nineveh, someone is coming
to attack and scatter you.
Guard your fortresses!
Watch the road! Be brave!
Prepare for battle!
2Judah and Israel are like trees
with branches broken
by their enemies.
But the Lord is going to restore
their power and glory.
* 3Nineveh, on this day of attack,
your enemies' shields are red;
their uniforms are crimson.
4Their horses prance,
and their armored chariots
dart around like lightning
or flaming torches.
5An officer gives a command.
But his soldiers stumble,
as they hasten to build
a shelter to protect themselves
against rocks thrown down
from the city wall.
6The river gates fly open,
and panic floods the palace.
7Nineveh is disgraced.
The queen is dragged off.
Her servant women mourn;
they moan like doves,
