and they beat their breasts
in sorrow.
8Nineveh is like a pond
with leaking water.
Shouts of “Stop! Don't go!”
can be heard everywhere.
But everyone is leaving.
9Enemy soldiers shout,
“The city is full of treasure
and all kinds of wealth.
Steal her silver! Grab her gold!”
10Nineveh is doomed! Destroyed!
Her people tremble with fear;
their faces turn pale.
11What happened to this city?
They were safer there
than powerful lions in a den,
with no one to disturb them.
12These are the same lions
that ferociously attacked
their victims,
then dragged away the flesh
to feed their young.
13The Lord All-Powerful
is against you, Nineveh.
God will burn your chariots
and send an army to kill
those young lions of yours.
You will never again
make victims of others
or send messengers to threaten
everyone on this earth.
translation_text:
1Juuda yab, ntuun ŋun cāabìń
tibɔmɔntiilee di dòoń ajoon puee,
ŋu sòoǹ ŋgbansɔŋfi bɔti ní!
Jīmaan ni-jiŋaalib,
cáaḿmaan ni-pooŋyi saraabi kí tīī Unimbɔti.
Kun puee, ukpitee kaa ti làá dāan̄ kí fōō ni-tiŋki,
bi pée nāaǹ-u ní múb.
2Niiniifi, bi dòoń kí jáǹ-si dee.
Bijanjaliibi, jɔ̄m̀maan sintil difɔkɔŋi pu kí nīn cí,
nín̄ cɔ́ŋkímaan adan pu ki kpèé,
yòom̄maan ni-gbajab kí gbìn̄,
kámaan kunyannyaau kí pɔ́ɔǹ ni-ba.
3Di sá yii ti-Dindaan fātìi gíiǹ
Jaakɔb nyooti ki tīī-u.
Úǹ u-ba di sá Isirayeel nyooti.
Binannanliibi nìn fúkúl̀-bi,
ki bíil̀ bi-fiinyi paŋŋi.
Bi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹ Niiniifi tiŋki ki fúkúl̀-kì
4Bi-nannanliibi janjaliibi gbampɔɔŋi máǹ,
ní bi pēē tiwamman cínciŋ.
Bi yaa gbāaǹ dikɔ̀ndi puee,
bi-tɔrɔkub kúti ŋmóò ní làka laka kii ŋŋmee,
ní bi fīintí bi-kpammu.
5Janjatɔrɔkub dū bi-ba ki bíl̀ adan pu,
bi kpátìi gbí kitiŋ jaŋŋi kɔkɔ pu
a lì kii iŋminaapoolee.
Bi yáb̀ kii utaa nín ŋmóò puee ní.
6Niiniifi bɔtiu yíiń u-janjaliibi kpilib,
ama ní bi còom̄ ki cá ki gùgufī.
Binannanliibi sáń ki cá kitiŋ gundi caŋin.
Bi bál̀ digbampɔɔl din boon bi làá báĺee.
7Bi gbáń ki pīitì mpunyɔmu
mun bíitiǹ ibunee mpɔn,
bi jáń ki fōō dibeecindi.
8Binannanliibi yōoǹ diwaal ki cáa cūnnì kuyuŋu.
Binimpoobi bin nìn jáaḿ-dèe bíi sūǹ
ki yáliŋkí kii abeenanjilee,
ní ki fátí bi-biŋŋi nì kunimbaau.
9Niiniifi yab sá kii nnyimbilkaam
min nnyim nyáń ki dóòyee ní.
Bi nìn kūuntí ki yíì-bi yii:
«Sīĺmaan! Sīĺmaan,»
ama báà ubɔ kaa fātìi kpēē u-boon gba.
10Fūkul̀maan kitiŋee nimbiliŋ nì ki-sindaariyau!
Ki-gaajawanti kaa cáá dikúntil,
tiwammɔntiil kɔkɔ nì ti-bulifi gbí ki-ni.
11Bi fúkúl̀-kì ki gbákal̀-kì ki nāaǹ-kì.
Un cáá dipɔbilee gíti kpá,
bi-taaŋi yɔ̄tì,
tiwun kɔkɔ gbáà kpàkpakpa
ní inimbiin cúu kpántì.
Niiniifi bí kii gbikinti un bi jáń ki pɔ́ɔkiǹee ní
12Kitiŋ kin poon gbikintib nìn kóòyee bí la?
Niin ní agbikintipɔmbil nìn kāntí ki jīǹ.
Ugbikintija yaa nìn búntì dijinnyaabilee,
ubɔ kaa nìn gbèetī u-biyaamu.
13Ugbikintija nìn cútí tinan ní ki
tìì u-biyaamu.
U nìn kù ipeel ki tìì ugbikintinaati,
u nìn gbēentí laakin u kóòyee
ipeel in u cúú ki tɔ̄ntèe.
14Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan lī yii:
«Sii Niiniifi, m làá já nì si,
m làá yàntī a-janjatɔrɔkub
ń wà kí kpántí ŋfantam.
Kujaaun ní bi làá tin kpɔ̀ń a-gbikintipɔmbiliŋ.
M làá kúntí a nín yìin̄ ki fúkúl̀ ntimu puee,
ní ubɔ kaa làá ti gbìl̄ a-tuuŋyi nyɔmmu pu.»

english_text:
Punishment for Nineveh
The Lord said:
1Doom to the crime capital!
Nineveh, city of murder
and treachery,
2here is your fate—
cracking whips,
churning wheels;
galloping horses,
roaring chariots;
3cavalry attacking,
swords and spears flashing;
soldiers stumbling
over piles of dead bodies.
4You were nothing more
than a prostitute
using your magical charms
and witchcraft
to attract and trap nations.
5But I, the Lord All-Powerful,
am now your enemy.
I will pull up your skirt
and let nations and kingdoms
stare at your nakedness.
6I will cover you with garbage,
treat you like trash,
and rub you in the dirt.
7Everyone who sees you
will turn away and shout,
“Nineveh is done for!
Is anyone willing to mourn
or to give her comfort?”
Nineveh's Fate Is Sealed
8Nineveh, do you feel safer
than the city of Thebes?
The Nile River
was its wall of defense.
9Thebes trusted the mighty power
of Ethiopia and Egypt;
the nations of Put and Libya
were her allies.
10But she was captured and taken
to a foreign country.
Her children were murdered
at every street corner.
The members of her royal family
were auctioned off,
and her high officials
were bound in chains.
11Nineveh, now it's your turn!
You will get drunk and try to hide
from your enemy.
12Your fortresses are fig trees
with ripe figs.
Merely shake the trees,
and fruit will fall
into every open mouth.
13Your army is weak.
Fire has destroyed the crossbars
on your city gates;
now they stand wide open
to your enemy.
14Your city is under attack.
Haul in extra water!
Strengthen your defenses!
Start making bricks!
Stir the mortar!
15You will still go up in flames
and be cut down by swords
that will wipe you out like a field
attacked by grasshoppers.
So, go ahead and increase
like a swarm of locusts!
16More merchants are in your city
than there are stars
in the sky—
but they are like locusts
that eat everything,
then fly away.
17Your guards and your officials
are swarms of locusts.
On a chilly day
they settle on a fence,
but when the sun comes out,
they take off
to who-knows-where.
18King of Assyria,
your officials and leaders
are sound asleep,
while your people are scattered
in the mountains.
Yes, your people are sheep
without a shepherd.
19You're fatally wounded.
There's no hope for you.
But everyone claps
when they hear this news,
because your constant cruelty
has caused them pain.
translation_text:
Bi pɔ̄fì nnikpaakoon tiŋki Niiniifi yab
1Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí Niiniifi tiŋki
kin poon nnikpaakoon bée!
Dimuuldi nì tipɔmbɔti di gbí ki-poon.
Bi pée fúkuĺ binib ní kaa gbèentí.
2Pīlifìmaan! Anaalab di nìiǹnée!
Tɔrɔkub taaŋi di wàkalìńee!
Itaamu di tòó càlib calibee!
Kujaau tɔrɔkub di jàkànée!
3Bitanjakaliibi dū bi-ba ki bílìń!
Ntàataajimu di ŋmóò làka lakee!
Ŋkpamu di jìl̀ pàlpalee!
Bitaŋkpiibi dɔ̄ an kɔkɔ fìlfilfil!
Anikpil dɔ̄ akpuku akpuku!
Baa ti ŋūǹ kí kàaǹ-ŋi gba!
Binib kíǹ ki gbéetí-ŋi ní.
Icoo cúú Niiniifi tiŋki
4Niiniifi tiŋki ŋá alaakpaatuun
ŋfunyɔm kutuku kutuku pu.
Kì nìn ŋān̄ ki bí gbàlgbalgbal,
ní ki nìn sàtī binib.
Kì nìn cáá ki-laakpaati ki cútí
atimbun tikpil kuyuŋu,
ní kì nìn cáá ki-nyɔkɔŋu
ki sàtī anibul.
5Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín lī puee sɔ̀.
M làá já nì si.
M làá kóoǹ a-wɔndoou
kí bìitī a-cancaŋgbeel pu kí dàkà atimbun,
ní kí bìitī a-cooi pu kí dàkà abee ŋin kíǹee.
6M làá dū titampummool kí bìin̄ a-pu
kí kɔ́ǹ-si icoo,
ní kí nyāntí-si kí páań mpaampiin pu.
7Bin kɔkɔ làá dāá ká-see
dāa sáń-si ní ki lì yii:
«Niiniifi tiŋki pée nāaǹ ní múb,
ŋma làá yāliŋkì ki-pu dee?
La ní m làá nín ká binib
bí dāá ŋméeǹ-kì dee?»
Bi làá ŋá Niiniifi kii bi nín ŋá Teebeesi puee ní
8Niiniifi tiŋki, a dàkafī yii
a sɔ́ǹ Teebeesi tiŋki
kin bí Niil buntaaŋi kansikinee níii?
Nnyim di nìn māntìi tú-kì,
ní dimɔɔl cí-kì,
ní nnyim sá ki-guŋŋi.
9Eetiiyoopii nì Eejipiti di nìn sá ki-pɔŋŋu
ŋun kaa cáá dikúntilee.
Puuti yab nì Liibii yab
di nìn sá ki-bɔɔbi.
10Ama nì míǹ kɔkɔee,
bi cúú Teebeesi yab
ki cūnnì kuyuŋu.
Bi nìn nàn̄ bi-bipɔmmu
asaŋkaŋkpil kɔkɔ pu.
Bi nìn tɔ́ kasi ki yākatì bi-kpambaliŋ
ki cáá-bi ki cūnnì kuyuŋu,
ní ki bóob́ ki-kpootiliibi ikusaka.
11Sii Niiniifi tiŋki, digìńdi làá dāá kɔ́ si mun,
a làá dāá nyàab̀ kí báĺ.
Sii mun làá dāá nyàab̀ kibalilaŋ
a-nannanliibi ń taa cúú-si.
Niiniifi tiŋki làá lítí
12A-sintil difɔkɔŋi sá kii fiigi biliŋ
ŋin lúń busubu pu ki mántèe ní.
Bi yaa pée yáká-buee, abil gbátí ní
kí kɔ́ un là kí ŋmɔ́-ŋee nyɔkɔn.
13Kpèè a-janjaliibi bí kii binimpoobee ní,
a-nannanliibi yaa páaǹnée,
a-tiŋki punyɔmmu cútí kí pìitī ní bàaa bí kɔ́,
di sá yii ŋŋmi wùn̄ mu-kpàlkaati.
14Niiniifi yab, lúḿmaan nnyim kí yóoń,
di sá yii binannanliibi làá màntīí tū ni-tiŋki.
Mɔ̀tīí ŋāŋkìmaan ni-sintil difɔkɔŋi,
tāāmaan kuyɔkɔu,
ní kí yòon̄ ni-brikisi gaŋgammu!
15Ama niin ní ŋŋmi làá wà-ni ní kpú,
kujaaun ní ni làá kpú kí céetí.
Bi làá kpɔ̀ kí céetí-ni kii inaakitoon
nín ŋmóò ki céetí tikɔkɔ puee ní.
Báà ubɔ kaa ti kóò Niiniifi tiŋkin
Niiniifi, a-nib nìn wīikí kii inaakitoonee ní!
16Ni-nyampoobi nìn wīikí ki jítiǹ
iŋmalbijaa in bí kutaa puee.
Kɔŋkɔnnee bi wáŋkì kii inaakicaan
nín yíkí kí búntí puee.
17A-ciitiliibi nìn būtì kii inaakicaanee ní,
ní a-kàlimbi mun nìn wīikí kii kunaakicikuee.
An yaa dá láá sɔ̀m̀ee,
inaaki náká an pu.
Ama ŋwìiń yaa nyáńee, i yíkí ní kí búntí
ní ubɔ kaa nyí laakin i túĺee.
I nín bí la dee?
Asaluu un baa ŋūǹ kí ŋāŋkèe
18Asuur bɔtiu,
a-kpootiliibi gèen̄ kaa fīntì!
A-baatandambi kaa ti bíi cìŋkī bi-ba!
A-janjaliibi yàl̄ ki gbí ajoon pu,
ní ubɔ kaa bí kí kóoǹ-bi kí kpāfì.
19Asaluu un gbáń-see kaa ti cáá diŋaŋkil.
Nnyɔkɔ kaa bí kí cáaǹ tiweendi tin a fōōyee.
Bin kɔkɔ gbìl̄ tin bāań-see
kpáafí bi-ŋalii nnaabu ŋun bāań-see pu,
di sá yii a ŋá ntoom ki kíǹ ŋma?
A-toom kaa cáá kikuntilaŋ.

english_text:
1I am Habakkuk the prophet. And this is the message that the Lord gave me.
Habakkuk Complains to the Lord
2Our Lord, how long must I beg
for your help
before you listen?
How long before you save us
from all this violence?
3Why do you make me watch
such terrible injustice?
Why do you allow violence,
lawlessness, crime, and cruelty
to spread everywhere?
4Laws cannot be enforced;
justice is always the loser;
criminals crowd out honest people
and twist the laws around.
The Lord Answers Habakkuk
5 Look and be amazed
at what's happening
among the nations!
Even if you were told,
you would never believe
what's taking place now.
6 I am sending the Babylonians.
They are fierce and cruel—
marching across the land,
conquering cities and towns.
7How fearsome and frightening.
Their only laws and rules
are the ones they make up.
8Their cavalry troops are faster
than leopards,
more ferocious than wolves
hunting at sunset,
and swifter than hungry eagles
suddenly swooping down.
9They are eager to destroy,
and they gather captives
like handfuls of sand.
10They make fun of rulers
and laugh at fortresses,
while building dirt mounds
so they can capture cities.
11Then suddenly they disappear
like a gust of wind—
those sinful people who worship
their own strength.
Habakkuk Complains Again
12Holy Lord God, mighty rock,
you are eternal,
and we are safe from death.
You are using those Babylonians
to judge and punish others.
13But you can't stand sin or wrong.
So don't sit by in silence
while they gobble up people
who are better than they are.
14The people you put on this earth
are like fish or reptiles
without a leader.
15Then an enemy comes along
and takes them captive
with hooks and nets.
It makes him so happy
16that he offers sacrifices
to his fishing nets,
because they make him rich
and provide choice foods.
17Will he keep hauling in his nets
and destroying nations
without showing mercy?
translation_text:
1Unimbɔti bɔti tin ní u lēē ki dàkā u-bɔnaatiliu Abakuukee.
Abakuuki bíi yíì Unimbɔti ú jòoń-u
2M-Dindaan, kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu
ní m làá nīn yíì-si á jòoń-mi
ní á nín pīlifì-mi ní?
M bíi kūuntí yii tipɔmbɔti gbóotì,
ama ní aa bíi fìil̄-ti.
3Ba pu ní a yàntī m kāntí atuŋkpiti ní?
Ba pu ní unil wɔ́b̀ u-juti ní a kpèé ki ŋmí ní?
Diwɔ́bil nì tipɔmbɔti di māntìi tú-mi.
Kunikpɔŋkpɔkɔu nì kujaau di kíǹ ki bí an kɔkɔ.
4Mara wɔ̀b̄ kaa ti cáá mpɔn,
ní an kaa ti sá un bɔti ŋān̄ee ní bi pɔ̀.
Unikpiti nyīī deedeedaan ki múĺ,
an pu ní ibɔsoon poonee, ibaamɔn kaa ti bí.
Ti-Dindaan kíí Abakuuki: Babiloon yab cīiń
5Ti-Dindaan bí yii:
«Kpèèmaan tin bíi jītí
atimbun ŋin kíǹee kansikin tiŋan.
Yàntīmaan án bàkatīǹ-ni sèeee!
Di sá yii m làá ŋá maamaaci tundi diba
ni-yuntii nee poon.
Ubɔ di yaa bàà máafì-ni tibɔti gbanti,
naa bàà làá fōō-tì kí kíí.
6Kpèèmaan, m làá yàntī Babiloon yab ń dāan̄,
dinibul gbanti kaa sūǹ isaa
ní ki néeń tipɔmbɔti.
Bi yìiǹ duulinya kɔkɔn
ki fòol̄ binib timmu ki cáa gà bi-biŋŋi.
7Bi sá tinibilindi ní ki cáá tifaandi.
Bíǹ bi-ba di sīintí bi-marab nì bi-pɔŋŋu.
8Bi-taamui yáb̀ ki jítiǹ iguloobu,
ki cáá ntoom ki jítiǹ digbiŋgbil
din cá kukpɔŋu kujoouee.
Bi-tanjakaliibi nyánní ndan ki dòoń
bi-taamui yùkufìń.
Bi ŋàaǹ kii ukaalun nín tòó pu
kí cúú tiba kí jēe ní.
9Bi-kɔkɔ dòoń kí fūkul̀,
ní bi-nimbikpeeŋu pée cɔ́ bi-nyɔkɔpu.
Bi kóoǹ iyumbu ki kpáfì i wīikí kii dibulee.
10Dinibul gbanti bèel̄ bibɔtiibi ní.
Abɔtibil sá kii tigbiŋgbiiliwanee ní bi-cee.
Baa fàŋkí ntimu mun
bi máń digundi ki túee.
Bi fà ntam ní kí kpúkuń digundi gbanti caŋin,
ní kí tāā kí dàb̄ kí já kí fōō-mu.
11Bi jītí kii kubuŋkpaaŋŋuee
ní ki nìkì bi-saŋŋu.
Kun pée páb́-bee di sá bi-pɔŋŋu,
ŋúǹ di sá bi-nimbɔtiu.»
Ubɔnaatil tí bíi kūuntí ki yíì Unimbɔti
12Doooo ŋkilkaaminee, sii di sá ti-Dindaan,
sii di sá m-Nimbɔtiu, ki sá circirdaan
ní kaa kúù.
M-Dindaan, sii di lēē dinibul nee dí sòoǹ ti-bɔti.
M-taŋkpanaakooku, a tīī-dì mpɔn dí dáaĺ ti-tafal.
13A-nimbiliŋ bí circir tikpil,
ŋaa ŋūǹ kí kpèè ikpiti.
Aa tí ŋūǹ kí kíí kí nīn kpèé
ubɔ ń nīn bíi wɔ́b̀ u-juti.
Kin ba pu ní a kíí ki kpèé binikpitib
bin nyēē bi-jutiibi boon nee kaa lì tiba ní?
Ba pu ní a ŋmí ki kpèé unikpiti ń bīil̀
un sá deedeedaan ki jítiǹ-uee ní?
14Di sá yii a yāntì binib bí kii tiŋkun jɔmiiyee,
a lì kii tin fù ti-pool pu kaa cáá ukpootilee.
15Babiloon yab cútí binib kii
ujɔm un bi tɔ́ njɔmpiin ki cúúyee ní.
Kulaaŋŋu ní bi dù kí cúú-bi,
ní kí dū bi-naanyaaŋŋu kí kóoǹ-bi.
Niinee ní an kíǹ ki mɔ̄ǹ-bi ní bi fàal̀.
16Bi ŋáań saraabi ki tìì bi-laanti,
ní ki tùutī talaalub ki tìì bi-naanyaaŋyi.
Di sá yii bi-laanti nì bi-naanyaaŋyi pu
ní bi-jinti mèeǹ ki mɔ̄.
17Mimmee bi làá nīn gbíntìi fúutí
bi-tàataajimmu kujitooun
ki kù atimbun ŋin kíǹee nib nì inimbinaakulimaaa?

english_text:
The Lord Answers Habakkuk Again
1While standing guard
on the watchtower,
I waited for the Lord's answer,
before explaining the reason
for my complaint.
2Then the Lord told me:
“I will give you my message
in the form of a vision.
Write it clearly enough
to be read at a glance.
3 At the time I have decided,
my words will come true.
You can trust what I say
about the future.
It may take a long time,
but keep on waiting—
it will happen!
4 “I, the Lord, refuse to accept
anyone who is proud.
Only those who live by faith
are acceptable to me.”
Trouble for Evil People
5Wine is treacherous,
and arrogant people
are never satisfied.
They are no less greedy
than death itself—
they open their mouths as wide
as the world of the dead
and swallow everyone.
6But they will be mocked
with these words:
You're doomed!
You stored up stolen goods
and cheated others
of what belonged to them.
7But without warning,
those you owe
will demand payment.
Then you will become
a frightened victim.
8You robbed cities and nations
everywhere on earth
and murdered their people.
Now those who survived
will be as cruel to you.
9You're doomed!
You made your family rich
at the expense of others.
You even said to yourself,
“I'm above the law.”
10But you will bring shame
on your family
and ruin to yourself
for what you did to others.
11The very stones and wood
in your home
will testify against you.
12You're doomed! You built a city
on crime and violence.
13 But the Lord All-Powerful
sends up in flames
what nations and people
work so hard to gain.
14 Just as water fills the sea,
the land will be filled
with people who know
and honor the Lord.
15You're doomed!
You get your friends drunk,
just to see them naked.
16Now you will be disgraced
instead of praised.
The Lord will make you drunk,
and when others see you naked,
you will lose their respect.
17You destroyed trees and animals
on Mount Lebanon;
you were ruthless to towns
and people everywhere.
Now you will be terrorized.
Idolatry Is Foolish
18What is an idol worth?
It's merely a false god.
Why trust a speechless image
made from wood or metal
by human hands?
19What can you learn from idols
covered with silver or gold?
They can't even breathe.
Pity anyone who says to an idol
of wood or stone,
“Get up and do something!”
20Let all the world be silent—
the Lord is present
in his holy temple.
translation_text:
1M làá yūĺ sintil,
m làá jɔ̄m̀ kí tɔ́kɔń digunlɔkɔl pu
kí kpèè tin Unimbɔti làá tùkù-mee,
nì m nín bíi yáliŋkée, u nín làá kíí-mi puee.
Kun dɔ̄ ki cí deedeedaan nì un wɔ́b̀ u-jutiibee
2Niinee ní ti-Dindaan kíí-mi yii:
«Ŋmà tin m bíi lèekī ki dàkà-si nee.
Ŋmà kí nákań tipilindi pu,
binib ń ŋmā kí kàaǹ sɔkɔmii.
3Dileedakal nee cí di-yuntiŋu ní
kí ŋá kii an nín lēē ki dàkā puee.
Di-yuntiŋu tóobiń,
dàa làá gbíntí.
Báà an yaa yúntàaa, cīití-dì.
Tin m lēē ki dàkā-si nee,
án làá pée ŋá míǹ ní.
An pée kpá kí gbíntí.
4Kpèè, unil un kaa bí deedeeyee
yòontí u-ba yilpu,
ama deedeedaan kāntí dimaŋfal
u-deedeeu pu ní.
5Tiŋman ndaam kíiĺ unileeee!
Ulambidaan kaa cáá diŋuŋfil.
U wàatī u-nyɔkɔ bàaa kii ditaŋkpiilee,
waa díkì kii ŋkúmee.
U jáà ki fòol̄ atimbun kɔkɔ,
ní ki cáá anibul kɔkɔ pu mpɔn.
6Ama, binib gbanti kɔkɔ
làá dāá nīn gà alaŋkpan ki bèel̄-u
ní ki lāā-u.»
Mbusub bɔti
Bi dāa lì yii:
«Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí-ni!
Ni bí ki fìkì binib wanti
kí cáá sāā ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu?
Ni mɔ̀tīi kútí ni-pɔɔŋŋi nyiŋfiŋu pu dee!
7Bin pīnnì-ni animbilee
làá dāá cíliń ni-pu ní dicilpu dicilpu.
Bi làá dāá yīkì kí cìŋkì cìŋkì-ni.
Bi làá dāá fūkul̀-ni kí téeǹ.
8Ni fúkúl̀ atimbun tikpil.
Anibul ŋin kíǹee mun
làá dāá fūkul̀-ni míǹ mbaantiim.
Di sá yii ni kūū binib,
ki ŋá Juuda tiŋki nì ki-timmu
nì bin kóò mu-nee tipɔmbɔti!
9«Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí-ni!
Ni nyàab̀ dulim gaajati
kí dūú kpāafì kí síiń ni-dicaŋŋi yab,
ní ki māā ni-diiŋŋi ki tɔ̄kɔntí yilpu,
nnaabu yaa páaǹnée, án taa gbēē-ni.
10Tin ni bɔ́ntì kí ŋée làá cáań icoo
kí tɔ̄ ni-dicaŋŋi yab pu ní.
Ni nín nāaǹ anibul tikpil puee,
nimbi ni-ba maŋfal ní ni nāaǹ.
11Ataŋkpee ŋin bi dūu máń agunee gba
làá nīn kūuntí ki kɔ́kɔĺ-ni,
ní idɔ in bi dūu tɔ́kɔǹ kudiiyee ń kíí-ŋi.
12«Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí-ni!
Ni māā ni-timmu ki tɔ̄kɔntí
nnikpaakoon nì tin kaa bí deedeeyee pu ní.
13An pu ní anibul gìńdi kúntí ŋŋmin,
ní atimbun bí ki bìǹ fám.
Tíǹ gbanti kɔkɔ kaa nyánní
ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan cee níii?
14Tiŋman, báà ŋma làá béé ti-Dindaan nyooti,
tì làá dāá gbí kitiŋ pu kii
nnyim nín gbí tiŋku poon puee ní.
15«Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí-ni!
Ni páb̀ ni-jutiibi bí nyɔ̀ ndaam,
ki tìì-bi ndaam min poon ni ŋmālim̀ nnyɔkɔee
bí nyɔ̀ kí gbí kí fá bi-ba
ní wāl̀ bi-cancaŋgbeel.
16Ama icoo làá cúú-ni gbòooo,
kaa sá tinyool!
Ni mun, nyɔ̀maan kí gbí bí ká ni-cancaŋgbeeŋi.
Ti-Dindaan làá páb́-ni ní nyɔ̀ u-ŋuul
din kā u-yukubilinee.
Ni-jilmau làá kpántí icoo.
17Di sá yii tipɔmbɔti tin ni ŋá Leebanɔn tiŋkinee
làá fàtīí gítiń ni-pu.
Ni pɔ̄fì tiwaŋkuti.
Too tiwaŋkuti gbanti
di làá kɔ́ǹ-ni dinyoondin.
Di sá yii ni kūū binib,
ki ŋá Juuda tiŋki nì ki-timmu
nì bin kóò mu-nee tipɔmbɔti!
18Ba ní bi làá dū diwaal kí ŋá
ní ukpiŋkpiiti kpítí-dì ní?
An sá tikúti ní bi dūntì ki dūu mɔ́ɔ́
ní an dàkà tinyimɔmbɔti.
Ukpiŋkpiiti di kpítì-dì ní dàa ŋūǹ kí sòoǹ.
Kin ba pu ní u gíti máká di-pu nan dee?
19«Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí-ni!
Ni tùkù didɔgindi yii: <Yīkì!>
ki tùkù ditaŋkpal din kaa ŋūǹ
kí sòoǹee yii: <Fìntī.>
Ditaŋkpal kaa ŋūǹ kí dàkà-si tiba.
Báà bi yaa dūntì sindaariya nì animbil ki nákaǹ-dàaa,
dàa cáá kufoou!
20Ama ti-Dindaan úǹ kóò u-circir diikun ní.
Kitiŋ kɔkɔ pu nib ń ŋmīĺ fɔ́ŋfɔŋ u-nimbiin!»

english_text:
Habakkuk's Prayer
1This is my prayer:
2I know your reputation, Lord,
and I am amazed
at what you have done.
Please turn from your anger
and be merciful;
do for us what you did
for our ancestors.
3You are the same Holy God
who came from Teman
and Paran to help us.
The brightness of your glory
covered the heavens,
and your praises were heard
everywhere on earth.
4Your glory shone like the sun,
and light flashed from your hands,
hiding your mighty power.
5Dreadful diseases and plagues
marched in front
and followed behind.
6When you stopped,
the earth shook;
when you stared,
nations trembled;
when you walked
along your ancient paths,
eternal mountains and hills
crumbled and collapsed.
7The tents of desert tribes
in Cushan and Midian
were ripped apart.
8Our Lord, were you angry
with the monsters
of the deep?
You attacked in your chariot
and wiped them out.
9Your arrows were ready
and obeyed your commands.
You split the earth apart
with rivers and streams;
10mountains trembled
at the sight of you;
rain poured from the clouds;
ocean waves roared and rose.
11The sun and moon stood still,
while your arrows and spears
flashed like lightning.
12In your furious anger,
you trampled on nations
13to rescue your people
and save your chosen one.
You crushed a nation's ruler
and stripped his evil kingdom
of its power.
14His troops had come like a storm,
hoping to scatter us
and glad to gobble us up.
To them we were refugees
in hiding—
but you smashed their heads
with their own weapons.
15Then your chariots churned
the waters of the sea.
Habakkuk's Response to God's Message
16When I heard this message,
I felt weak from fear,
and my lips quivered.
My bones seemed to melt,
and I stumbled around.
But I will patiently wait.
Someday those vicious enemies
will be struck by disaster.
Trust in a Time of Trouble
17Fig trees may no longer bloom,
or vineyards produce grapes;
olive trees may be fruitless,
and harvest time a failure;
sheep pens may be empty,
and cattle stalls vacant—
18but I will still celebrate
because the Lord God
is my Savior.
19 The Lord gives me strength.
He makes my feet as sure
as those of a deer,
and he helps me stand
on the mountains.
To the music director:
Use stringed instruments.
translation_text:
Abakuuki wimmeem
1Ŋwimmeem min Unimbɔti bɔnaatiliu Abakuuki nìn mēē nì itiminsi poonee sɔ̀.
2Ti-Dindaan, m gbìl̄ atuŋkpaan ŋin a ŋée pu.
An cúú-mi tifaandi gba.
Ti-Dindaan, fàtīí ŋá a-tuuŋŋi gbanti
ti-wiiŋyi nee poon,
yàntī báà ŋma ń béé-ŋi
ti-yuntii nee poon.
Báà a yaa fōō ti-pu diŋuulaaa,
téetí a-poommɔŋŋu pu.
3Unimbɔti nyánní Teeman tiŋkin ki dòoń,
circir Nimbɔtiu páaǹní Paaran jooŋŋi pu.
U nín sá ukpaan puee bīī kutagbɔŋu pu,
ní u-nyɔŋkii gbí kitiŋ kɔkɔ pu.
4U wāĺ bɔ́iii kii ŋwalifee,
ní itaaŋmɔŋmɔ nyēeń u-ŋaan ki jìl̀ pàlpal.
Niin ní u-pɔŋŋu mun kā.
5Bìlbil kúm līī u-nyɔkɔpu
ní nnaanyeem tēentí u-tabɔbiliŋ.
6U yaa sāā ki yúl̀ee, kitiŋ cìŋkī ní.
U yaa fātìi kpēē atimbun nibee,
bi-wunti gbáà ní kpàkpakpa.
Jaanjaan jooŋŋi fáá iwèeń,
ní cannaaku gbantammu lábitì ki cìb̄,
ŋíǹ mun di nìn sá njaminee u-saŋŋu.
7M ká Kusan yab tantib kaa ti bí tiban.
Madiyan yab kɔŋkooŋyi cīŋkì nì tifaandi.
8Mimmee ti-Dindaan, ibun pu ní a fōō diŋuulaaa?
Ibun pu ní a fōō mbum naaa?
Tiŋku pu ní a-ŋuul gà lìblib yéèee?
A jɔ́m̀ ki kāl̀ atagban pu
kii dijajil tɔrɔkubee.
9A bɔ́ntì a-tɔbu,
ní dinyɔɔbundi din a sòon̄ee sá kii ipiinee.
A dū ibun ki búkutì kitiŋ.
10Ajoon wál̀-si ní ki fāŋkì ki fōō dijinjikil.
Utaakpaan nìn̄ nì mpɔn,
ní tiŋku yāntì bi gbìl̄ u-bintindi pu.
U tòó u-nyiŋgbanti yilpu.
11Ŋwìiń nì uŋmal nín wál̀
a-piiŋyi in a tɔ́ee nín ŋàaǹ ki wāĺ puee,
nì a-kpaŋki nín ŋmóò pu làka lakee,
ní bi sāā ki yúl̀ laakin bi bée.
12A-ŋuul poonee, a yìiǹ kitiŋ kɔkɔ pu,
a-bum poonee, a tà ki mátí atimbun.
13A nyáń kí fīī a-nibul
kí fīī ubɔti un a lēēyee.
A líì un sá uyidaan binikpitib dicaŋkunee,
ki nāaǹ u-yab kɔkɔ múb.
14A dū úǹ u-ba piiŋyi ní
ki sāatìi cífì u-janjaliibi yiliŋ.
Bi bàà sáń ki dòoń kii kubuŋkpaaŋŋuee
kí dāá yàaǹ-ti.
Bi nìn kūuntí nì dipɔɔpindi,
a lì kii bi kpáàa cúú uwɔfi ki bíi tɔ̀ntī dibalinee.
15A cátì nsan tiŋkun laakin tinyiŋgban pɔ̄ɔ̄yee
a-taamui cōom̀ ki jítì.
16M gbìl̄ kuwoou nee kɔkɔ pu
ní m-poon kaam cɔ́tì.
M-nyunculiŋ bíi jìkì
ní m-kpabiŋ bíi bùkù.
M-taaŋi yɔ̄tì maa ti ŋūǹ kí yūĺ.
M ŋmíl̀ fɔ́ŋfɔŋ
ki cí dinimbinaamandi wiiŋŋu
kí cùú já nì anibul ŋin bíi jáà nì tee.
17Fiigi subu kaa ti púkuḿ,
fiinyi subu kaa ti lòoǹ,
ɔliifi subu kaa ti lòoǹ,
ní tisati mun kaa ti lòoǹ tikpaajin.
Ipii kaa ti bí kupikpuŋkpuŋun,
ní inaa mun kaa ti bí kunaabakaun.
18Ama mamee, m làá nīn fàal̀ ti-Dindaan pu,
m làá nīn bí mmɔnni Unimbɔti un di fīī-mee pu.
19Ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti di sá m-pɔŋŋu.
U yàntī m tóotí kii upeemanee,
ní ki yàntī m tɔ́kɔ́ yilpu ki còom̄.
Bilaŋgaaliibi kpiliu di ŋmàn̄ nlan nee.
Bi bɔ̀ɔ́ kubeeu ní ki gà-ŋu.

english_text:
1 I am Zephaniah, the son of Cushi, the grandson of Gedaliah, the great-grandson of Amariah, and the great-great-grandson of Hezekiah.
When Josiah son of Amon was king of Judah, the Lord gave me this message.
Judgment on Judah
2I, the Lord, now promise
to destroy everything
on this earth—
3people and animals,
birds and fish.
Everyone who is evil
will crash to the ground,
and I will wipe out
the entire human race.
4I will reach out to punish
Judah and Jerusalem—
nothing will remain
of the god Baal;
nothing will be remembered
of his pagan priests.
5Not a trace will be found
of those who worship stars
from their rooftops,
or bow down to the god Milcom,
while claiming loyalty
to me, the Lord.
6Nothing will remain of anyone
who has turned away
and rejected me.
7Be silent! I am the Lord God,
and the time is near.
I am preparing
to sacrifice my people
and to invite my guests.
8On that day I will punish
national leaders
and sons of the king,
along with all who follow
foreign customs.
9I will punish worshipers
of pagan gods
and cruel palace officials
who abuse their power.
10I, the Lord, promise
that on that day
noisy crying will be heard
from Fish Gate, New Town,
and Upper Hills.
11Everyone in Lower Hollow
will mourn loudly,
because merchants
and money changers
will be wiped out.
12I'll search Jerusalem with lamps
and punish those people
who sit there unworried
while thinking,
“The Lord won't do anything,
good or bad.”
13Their possessions will be taken,
their homes left in ruins.
They won't get to live
in the houses they build,
or drink wine from the grapes
in their own vineyards.
A Terrible Day
14The great day of the Lord
is coming soon, very soon.
On that terrible day,
fearsome shouts of warriors
will be heard everywhere.
15It will be a time of anger—
of trouble and torment,
of disaster and destruction,
of darkness and despair,
of storm clouds and shadows,
16of trumpet calls
and battle cries
against fortified cities
and mighty fortresses.
17The Lord warns everyone
who has sinned against him,
“I'll strike you blind!
Then your blood and your insides
will gush out like vomit.
18Not even your silver or gold
can save you on that day
when I, the Lord, am angry.
My anger will flare up
like a furious fire
scorching the earth
and everyone on it.”
translation_text:
1Tibɔti tin ti-Dindaan nìn sòon̄ nì Seefaniya ŋyunti ŋun Amɔn jipɔɔn Joosiyaasi nìn sá ubɔti Juuda tiŋkinee sɔ̀. Seefaniya gbanti nìn sá Kuusi naakookun, Geedaliya jipɔɔn, ki sá Amariya naantiiu, ní ki sá Eeseekiyaasi naantitɔntɔkɔl.
Juuda nì Jeerusaleem yab tafadaaldi
2Ti-Dindaan bí yii:
«M làá kúntí tin kɔkɔ
bí kitiŋ puee.
3M làá kúntí binib nì tiwaŋkuti,
nì inoon in bí kutaa puee
nì ijɔm in bí dimɔɔlinee.
M làá kúntí bitɔŋfitiibi
nì tin yàntī bi tūǹ atuŋkpitee.
M làá kúntí binib kɔkɔ kitiŋ pu.
Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.
Unimbɔti làá jáǹ Juuda nì Jeerusaleem tiŋki
4M làá já nì Jeerusaleem
nì Juuda yab kɔkɔ.
M làá kúntí awaatuun ŋin kíǹee mpaan nee pu,
ní kí kúntí awaa tɔntɔnliibi nì ŋi-tandambi.
5M làá kúntí bin tɔ̄kɔntí adibɔ̀bikaa yilpu
ki jáaḿ iŋmalbijaayee.
M làá kúntí bin gbàantí man bi-Dindaan nimbiin,
ní ki gíti pùtī diwaal Mooleeki yindee.
6Man ni-Dindaan, m làá kúntí
bin fàtī bi-boon ki tìì-mi
kaa nyàab̀-mi
ní kaa bàlifī-mi isaŋkee.»
7Ní ŋmīĺmaan díkí diki ti-Dindaan Unimbɔti nimbiin,
di sá yii u-ŋuul wiiŋŋu tóobiń.
Ti-Dindaan bɔ́ntì saraa,
kí ŋá bin u yíińee circir.
8Ti-Dindaan bí yii:
«M-saraau wiiŋŋu gbanti dalee,
m làá dāá já nì bikàliŋkpilib nì abɔtibil,
nì bin di pèentí tiwan kii binicambee.
9Yaadal wiiŋŋuee m làá dāá dáaĺ
bin di yùkufī ki lákatí kunimbɔtidii punyɔkɔkee tafal.
M làá dāá dáaĺ bin kɔkɔ fìkì binib
ki mùul̄-bi ki fòol̄ tiwan
ki gbēentí bi-waadiikuee.
10Ti-Dindaan bí yii,
ŋwiin gbantee, Jeerusaleem tiŋkinee,
bi dāa gbìl̀ ibiil Ijɔm punyɔkɔ watil,
ní ikuŋkuunti tùm̀ kitimpɔŋ watil,
ní kuwookpaaŋŋu gà ŋgbantamu pu.
11Makteesi yab, nín̄ kūuntímaan!
Di sá yii binyampoobi kɔkɔ làá kpú,
bin ŋmàntī animbilee làá kúntí.
12Ŋyunti gbantee, m làá dāá tūū fitila
ní kí kɔ́ Jeerusaleem tiŋkin kí kpùkul̀ an kɔkɔ pu.
M làá dāá dáaĺ binib bin kā kaa ŋáań tibee tafal
kii tidakpati nín dɔ̀ ndaam taapu puee.
Bi dàkafī yii: <Ti-Dindaan kaa ŋūǹ kí ŋá tiŋanaaa,
kaa tí ŋūǹ kí ŋá tikpitil mun!>
13Too, bi làá dāá fūkul̀ bi-gaajawanti
ní kí kpēelikì bi-diiŋŋi.
Bi māā adiin, ama baa làá kɔ́-ŋi.
Bi kù fiinyi sufii kpaaŋŋi,
ama baa làá ká i-daam kí nyɔ̀.»
Ti-Dindaan wiiŋŋu dal
14Ti-Dindaan wiŋkpaaŋŋu tóobiń,
ŋu tóobiń, ŋu dòoń malaa malaa.
Ŋwiin gbantee, binib làá dāá gbá ibiil
nì dinimbinaamandi.
Bibaatandambi gba làá dāá gbá ibiil
ki nyàab̀ dijòońdi.
15An dāa sá diŋuul wiiŋŋu ní,
dinimbinaamandi nì kufaaŋŋu wiiŋŋu,
asaluu nì ŋkúm wiiŋŋu,
kunyeeu nì dibɔmbɔndi wiiŋŋu,
atagbambɔn nì dipɔ̀ńdi wiiŋŋu ní an dāa sá.
16Ŋwiin gbantee, bi làá dāá gbìl̄
bijanjaliibi búǹ dikantándi,
ní kí fáá ijanjakuŋkuunti
kí já nì ntimu mun bi máń digundi ki túee
nì mu-sintil difɔkɔŋi.
17Ti-Dindaan bí yii:
«M làá dāá kɔ́ǹ binib dinimbinaamandin,
ní bí nīn còom̄ kii bijɔfubee,
kun puee bi yīntiǹ man bi-Dindaan.
Bi-fatikuu làá dāá kpáatí kí fá kitiŋ kii dibulee,
ní bí cáá bi-wunti kí fá kii titampummoolee.»
18Bi-nimbiliŋ nì bi-sindaariyab
kaa dāa ŋūǹ kí fīī-bi.
Ti-Dindaan ŋuul dalee,
u-ŋuukpaandi ŋmiŋu dalee,
kitiŋ kɔkɔ làá dāá wà kí céetí.
Tiŋman, u làá dāá kpɔ̀ kí céetí
binib kɔkɔ kitiŋ pu.

english_text:
Turn to the Lord
1You disgraceful nation,
gather around,
2before it's too late.
The Lord has set a time
when his fierce anger
will strike like a storm
and sweep you away.
3If you humbly obey the Lord,
then come and worship him.
If you do right and are humble,
perhaps you will be safe
on that day when the Lord
turns loose his anger.
Judgment on Philistia
4 Gaza and Ashkelon
will be deserted
and left in ruins.
Ashdod will be emptied
in broad daylight,
and Ekron uprooted.
5To you people of Philistia
who live along the coast,
the Lord has this to say:
“I am now your enemy,
and I'll wipe you out!”
6Your seacoast will be changed
into pastureland
and sheep pens.
7The Lord God hasn't forgotten
those survivors in Judah,
and he will help them—
his people will take your land
to use for pasture.
And when evening comes,
they will rest
in houses at Ashkelon.
Judgment on Moab and Ammon
* 8 The Lord All-Powerful,
the God of Israel, said:
I've heard Moab and Ammon
insult my people
and threaten their nation.
9 And so, I swear by my very life
that Moab and Ammon will end up
like Sodom and Gomorrah—
covered with thornbushes
and salt pits forever.
Then my people who survive
will take their land.
10This is how Moab and Ammon
will at last be repaid
for their pride—
and for sneering at the nation
that belongs to me,
the Lord All-Powerful.
11I will fiercely attack.
Then every god on this earth
will shrink to nothing,
and everyone of every nation
will bow down to me,
right where they are.
Judgment on Ethiopia
12 People of Ethiopia,
the sword of the Lord
will slaughter you!
Judgment on Assyria
13 The Lord will reach to the north
to crush Assyria
and overthrow Nineveh.
14Herds of wild animals
will live in its rubble;
all kinds of desert owls
will perch on its stones
and hoot in the windows.
Noisy ravens will be heard
inside its buildings,
stripped bare of cedar.
15This is the glorious city
that felt secure and said,
“I am the only one!”
Now it's merely ruins,
a home for wild animals.
Every passerby simply sneers
and makes vulgar signs.
translation_text:
An bālifì yii binib ń kpántí bi-bimbim
1Nimbi atimbun ŋin kaa cáá icooyee,
kóom̀maan tɔb kí kpāfì kí nīn nyìkī tɔb pu,
2kí wàatī ní ní nín kpántí kii
timool tin kubuŋu yòontí ki féeń ŋwimbaantee.
Ti-Dindaan bum làá dāá jēetí ni-pu.
Ti-Dindaan ŋuukpaandi wiiŋŋu làá dāá jēetí ni-pu.
3Nimbi bin kɔkɔ bí kitiŋ nee pu ki sīntiǹ ni-ba taapu,
ki tɔ́ ti-Dindaan marabee,
nyàab̀maan ti-Dindaan.
Nín̄ ŋáaḿmaan tin bí deedeeyee,
kí sìntīmaan ni-ba taapu Unimbɔti nimbiin.
An yaa yíì u-ŋuul wiiŋŋu dalee,
u làá dāá fīī-ni.
Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ ki bíikì ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú nibuliŋ pu
4Binib làá dāá yīkì kí fá Gaasaa tiŋki,
ní bí nàan̄ Asikeelɔn tiŋki.
Bi làá dāá jà Asidoodi yab kuwiŋkaŋu pu,
ní kí kpìtī Eekrɔn tiŋki.
5Mbusu dɔ̄ ki cí nimbi Kafitoor yab
bin kóò ditiŋkugbandee.
Kaana, Fiiliistii yab tiŋki,
ti-Dindaan bɔsooŋyi dàn̄ a-pu.
M làá kúntí-si,
di sá yii binib kaa ti kóò a-pu.
6Tiŋku kpaanceetii dāa kpántí kunaakpaapɔɔu,
laakin bipikpaaliibi kpàá tiwaŋkutee,
nì laakin bi làá mā ipii naabakatee.
7Juuda yab bin kíǹ ki bí dimaŋfalinee
làá dāá jī ditinjandi gbanti.
Niin ní bi làá dāá nīn kpàá bi-waŋkuti,
ní kujoouee, bí cùú kɔ́ Asikeelɔn yab timmun
kí dòon̄.
Di sá yii ti-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu
làá dāá sɔ̄ bi-saai,
ní kí cúú tin poon bi bée kí kpántí.
Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ ki bíikì ŋwìiń nyalaŋki pú nibuliŋ pu
8«M gbìl̄ Moowaab yab siibiliŋ
nì Amɔn yab beelii pu.
Bi sīī m-nibul
ní ki fōō di-timmu ki kútì bi-yɔmu pu.
9An pu ní man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan,
Isirayeel Nimbɔtiu pūtì ki lī yii:
<Moowaab tiŋki làá dāá kpántí kii Soodoom tiŋkee,
ní Amɔn yab tiŋki mun ń kpántí kii Goomoora tiŋkee.
Bi-tiŋki làá dāá kpántí ikuŋkum
nì diyataŋkpal kí nīn cá jaanjaan.
M-nibul yab bin làá dāá kíńee làá dāá fūkul̀-kì,
m-timbundi yab bin kíǹee làá dāá fōō-kì.>»
10Bi-bayoondi puee, tipaal tin bi làá dāá fōōyee sèé.
Di sá yii bi sīī ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nibul
ní ki fōō di-timmu ki kútì bi-yɔmu pu.
11Ti-Dindaan kaa làá dāá tàan̄-bi,
u làá dāá kúntí awaa kɔkɔ kitiŋ pu.
Atimbun ŋin bíń ndandatee
làá dāá gbàan̄ u-nimbiin laakin ŋi bée.
Ti-Dindaan sòon̄ ki bíikì ŋgan pú nì ŋgiil pú nibuliŋ pu
12«Nimbi Eetiiyoopii yab mun,
m làá dāá yàntī ní kpúń kujaaun ní.»
13Ti-Dindaan làá dāá já nì ŋgan pú tiŋki
ní kí dāá nàan̄ Asuur tiŋki.
Niiniifi tiŋki làá dāá kpántí ataŋkpakpuku,
kitiŋkuliŋŋi kii kuteeuee.
14Kitiŋ kansikin nì kansikin
ní tiwaŋkuti dāa dɔ̀.
Tiwaŋkuti kɔkɔ nì ti-buluku,
atulinjoo nì nlabinsamu dāa dɔ̀
jaantalkub yilpu ní.
Bi dāa gbìl̀ adiin tɔkɔlab pu
nnɔmbiyaamu siim pu.
A tin pée lì yii a kóò kitiŋinee,
tin a làá dāá kée di sá adigbun nì idɔ.
15Kpèèmaan kitiŋ kin nìn bí dipɔɔsɔŋkilin
ki máká ki-ba pu ki lì yii:
«Man di bí, m-boonee ubɔ gíti kpée.»
Too, Niiniifi kpántì ataŋkpakpuku ŋma ní,
tiwaŋkuti kɔŋkooŋŋu.
Bin kɔkɔ jītí ki-caŋinee búǹ ifoon
ki dɔ̀tī-kì dinyuncul.

english_text:
Sinful Jerusalem
1Too bad for that disgusting,
corrupt, and lawless city!
2Forever rebellious
and rejecting correction,
Jerusalem refuses to trust
or obey the Lord God.
3Its officials are roaring lions,
its judges are wolves;
in the evening they attack,
by morning nothing is left.
4Jerusalem's prophets are proud
and not to be trusted.
The priests have disgraced
the place of worship
and abused God's Law.
5All who do evil are shameless,
but the Lord does right
and is always fair.
With the dawn of each day,
God brings about justice.
6The Lord wiped out nations
and left fortresses
crumbling in the dirt.
Their streets and towns
were reduced to ruins
and emptied of people.
7God felt certain that Jerusalem
would learn to respect
and obey him.
Then he would hold back
from punishing the city
and not wipe it out.
But everyone there was eager
to start sinning again.
Nations Will Turn to the Lord
8The Lord said:
Just wait for the day
when I accuse you nations.
I have decided on a day,
when I will bring together
every nation and kingdom
and punish them all
in my fiery anger.
I will become furious
and destroy the earth.
9I will purify each language
and make those languages
acceptable for praising me.
Then, with hearts united,
everyone will serve
only me, the Lord.
10From across the rivers
of Ethiopia,
my scattered people,
my true worshipers,
will bring offerings to me.
11When that time comes,
you won't rebel against me
and be put to shame.
I'll do away with those
who are proud and arrogant.
Never will any of them
strut around
on my holy mountain.
12But I, the Lord, won't destroy
any of your people
who are truly humble
and turn to me for safety.
13 The people of Israel who survive
will live right
and refuse to tell lies.
They will eat and rest
with nothing to fear.
A Song of Celebration
14Everyone in Jerusalem and Judah,
celebrate and shout
with all your heart!
15Zion, your punishment is over.
The Lord has forced your enemies
to turn and retreat.
Your Lord is King of Israel
and stands at your side;
you don't have to worry
about any more troubles.
16Jerusalem, the time is coming,
when it will be said to you:
“Don't be discouraged
or grow weak from fear!
17The Lord your God
wins victory after victory
and is always with you.
He celebrates and sings
because of you,
and he will refresh your life
with his love.”
The Lord's Promise to His People
18The Lord has promised:
Your sorrow has ended,
and you can celebrate.
19I will punish those
who mistreat you.
I will bring together the lame
and the outcasts,
then they will be praised,
instead of despised,
in every country on earth.
20I will lead you home,
and with your own eyes
you will see me bless you
with all you once owned.
Then you will be famous
everywhere on this earth.
I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_text:
Isirayeel yab kaa pílifì isaŋki
1Mbusu kɔ́ pɔɔgaati tiŋki,
kitiŋ kin kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi
ki wɔ́b́ binibee.
2Kàa pílifì ti-Dindaan nyɔkɔ,
kaa fōō u-saŋkii,
kaa dū ki-mákal ki páaǹ ki-Dindaan pu,
kaa sútì ki pìl̄ ki-Nimbɔtiu.
3Ki-yidambi bí kii gbikintib bin sūǹee ní.
Ki-bɔsoonliibi bí kii agbiŋgbil
ŋin cá kukpɔŋu kujoou,
ama ní kutaa nì ku-wuntilee,
ŋaa ti cáá tiba kí ŋmɔ́ee ní.
4Ki-bɔnaatiliibi kaa bí tiban,
bi sá binib bin kíiĺ bi-jutiibee.
Ki-saraaŋaliibi kɔ́ǹ tin bí circiree tijɔkɔndi,
ní kaa fātìi tɔ́ mara.
5Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, ti-Dindaan bí kitiŋin,
waa ŋáań tin kaa bí deedeeyee.
Kutaafaau kamaayee, u sòoǹ tibɔti,
ntaafaabɔmbɔmee, u ŋáań tin ŋān̄ee.
Ama nì míǹ kɔkɔee, binikpitib
pée gbíntìi tūǹ atuŋkpiti kaa cáá icoo.
6Ti-Dindaan bí yii:
«M kúntì atimbun ki wīī ŋi-guŋkpaaŋŋi
ki yāntì ŋi-saŋyi kūń ubɔ kaa ti dì.
M bíil̀ ŋi-tiŋki,
uniseen kaa ti kóò ki-ni.
7M lī m-ban yii:
<Kɔŋkɔnnee kitiŋ nee nib làá nīn tɔ́-mi,
bi làá fōō m-bɔkpaafikaati.
Maa làá ti ŋá kii m nín bí yii m làá ŋá-kì puee,
kaa làá ti kúntí-kì.>
Ama ní ki-nib yáb́
ki túń atuŋkpiti.
8An puee ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sɔ̀.
Ní cīitímaan-mi!
Ní cīití ŋwiin ŋun m làá dāan̄ kí kɔ̄kɔl̀-nee.
Di sá yii m lēē ki síiǹ yii m làá kóoǹ
anibul nì abee kí kpāfì
ní kí kpáatí m-ŋuul kí sìtī ŋi-pu.
M-ŋuul ŋmiŋuee làá wà kí céetí kitiŋ kɔkɔ.»
Unimbɔti kpántì u-nibul bimbim
9«Tiŋman, m làá ŋá m-nibul
nyunculiŋ circir,
ní bí ŋmā kí nīn yíì
man bi-Dindaan yindi,
ní kí kpāfì ubaanti kí nīn tūǹ m-tundi.
10Bin jáaḿ-mi ki yàl̄
ki bíń Eetiiyoopii mɔɔgbandee
làá dāá cáań-mi saraabi.»
Isirayeel yab bin kíǹee
11«Ŋwiin gbantee, m-nibul,
icoo kaa làá ti cúú-si
atuŋkpiti ŋin kɔkɔ a ŋá-mee pu.
Di sá yii ŋyunti gbantee, m làá dāá nyāntí ni-kansikin
timɔn dambi nì bin yòontí bi-ba yilpuee.
Niinee, a làá dāá gbèen̄ kí taa ti yòon̄ a-ba yilpu
m-circir jool pu.
12M làá dāá kíń binib bin sīntiǹ bi-ba taapuee
nì bisoodambi a-ni.
Bi làá dāá nyàab̀ ḿ wúń bi-pu.
13Isirayeel yab bin làá dāá kíńee
kaa ti làá dāá ŋá ikpiti,
kaa ti làá dāá mɔ̄ntì inyimɔn,
kaa ti làá dāá kīil̀ bi-jutiibi.
Bi làá dāá kpàà bi-waŋkuti nì ŋgbansɔŋfi
kí ŋùŋfì ní ubɔ dāa kpá kí fàaǹ-bi.»
Bi làá fàtīí mā Jeerusaleem tiŋki
14 Siiyɔn tiŋki, nín̄ kūuntí nì dipɔɔpindi,
Isirayeel yab, nín̄ fàal̀maan.
Jeerusaleem, nín̄ fàal̀ nì a-pɔbil kɔkɔ!
15Ti-Dindaan kākatì ditafadaaldi
din bàà dàn̄ a-puee ki wāatì-si,
u kākatì a-nannanliibi ki wāatì-si.
Ti-Dindaan Isirayeel bɔtiu bí a-cee.
Aa ti máaǹ kí fàŋkì mbusu ubɔ.
16Ŋwiin gbantee, bi làá dāá tùkù Jeerusaleem yii:
«Siiyɔn tiŋki, taa fàŋkì,
a-wunti ń taa yɔ̀tī.
17Di sá yii ti-Dindaan a-Nimbɔtiu bí a-cee,
úǹ di sá ubaatandaan un tìì-si dijajilee.
A-pu ní u bí dipɔɔpindin,
ní u-neendi tìì-si dimaŋfapɔndi,
u fàal̀ ní ki bí dipɔɔpindin a-pu,
18kii jiŋaal wiiŋŋuee.»
Ti-Dindaan bí yii:
«Jeerusaleem, m làá dāá kàkatī nnaabu kí wàatī-si,
án nín làá ŋá pu icoo ń taa ti cúú-see.
19Ŋyunti gbantee, m làá dāá dáaĺ
bin kɔkɔ sāaǹ-nee tafal.
M làá dāá fīī apibil ŋin dúlifée,
kí kóoǹ ŋin wáŋkèe kí kpāfì.
M làá dāá tīī-ni tinyool
ní ni-yindi ń gbìtī ntimu mun kɔkɔ poon
bi nìn kɔ́ǹ-ni icooyee.
20Ŋyunti gbantee, m làá dāá gíiǹní-ni.
Án dāa sá ŋyunti ŋun ní m làá dāá kóoǹ-ni kí kpāfèe.
M làá dāá tīī-ni tinyool
ní ni-yindi ń dāá gbìtī ilaan kɔkɔ
anibul ŋin kɔkɔ bí kitiŋ puee kansikin.
Di sá yii ni-nimbilaaliyin
ní m làá dāá gíiǹní-ni diŋuŋfilin.»
Man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ.

english_text:
Rebuild the Temple
1 On the first day of the sixth month of the second year that Darius was king of Persia, the Lord told Haggai the prophet to speak his message to the governor of Judah and to the high priest.
So Haggai told Governor Zerubbabel and High Priest Joshua 2-5that the Lord All-Powerful had said to them and to the people:
You say this isn't the right time to build a temple for me. But is it right for you to live in expensive houses, while my temple is a pile of ruins? Just look at what's happening. 6You harvest less than you plant, you never have enough to eat or drink, your clothes don't keep you warm, and your wages are stored in bags full of holes.
7Think about what I have said! 8But first, go to the hills and get wood for my temple, so I can take pride in it and be worshiped there. 9You expected much, but received only a little. And when you brought it home, I made that little disappear. Why have I done this? It's because you hurry off to build your own houses, while my temple is still in ruins. 10That's also why the dew doesn't fall and your harvest fails. 11And so, at my command everything will become barren—your farmland and pastures, your vineyards and olive trees, your animals and you yourselves. All your hard work will be for nothing.
12Zerubbabel and Joshua, together with the others who had returned from exile in Babylonia, obeyed the Lord's message spoken by his prophet Haggai, and they started showing proper respect for the Lord. 13Haggai then told them that the Lord had promised to be with them. 14So the Lord God All-Powerful made everyone eager to work on his temple, especially Zerubbabel and Joshua. 15And the work began on the twenty-fourth day of that same month.
translation_text:
Ŋyunti ŋun sá bí fàtīí mā kunimbɔtidiiyee bāań
1Daariyusi nín kāl̀ dibeel abin ali iŋmal iluu wimpeepeekaaŋu dalee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì u-bɔnaatiliu Agaayi. U nìn bí ú tùkù Seeyaltiyeel jipɔɔn Sooroobabeel un sá Juuda yab gɔminauee, nì Yoosadaaki jipɔɔn Joosuwa un sá usaraaŋakpilee yii: 2Man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé: «Binib nee lì yii: <Ŋyunti ŋun ti máaǹ kí fàtīí mā kunimbɔtidiiyee kaa láá bāań.>» 3Ŋyunti gbanti ní ti-Dindaan dī u-bɔnaatiliu Agaayi pu ki sòon̄ nì bi yii: 4«Mimmee ŋyunti ŋmāntì nimbi ń nīn kóò adinyaan poon ní man diiku ń lítí kí kpántí kudigbuŋuɔɔɔ? 5Kɔŋkɔnnee, man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Dàkafìmaan tin poon ni bí nee pu tiŋan! 6Ni búĺ tikpil ama ní ki cáń fiii, ni jīǹ ama ní kaa díkì, ni nyù ndaam ama ní an kaa nyàatī-ni, ni pèentí abɔkuti ama ní tiwool gbíntìi cáá-ni, ní utɔntɔnli ń fōō tipaal ní án kɔ́ kuloou kun cíl̀ee poon. 7An puee man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Dàkafìmaan tin poon ni bí nee pu tiŋan! 8Jɔ̄m̀maan dijool pu kí cáań idɔ kí fàtīí mā m-Diiku. Án làá mɔ̄ɔkiǹ-mi ní ḿ nyāntí m-nyooti kí dàkà, man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ. 9Ni bàà cɔ́tí kí cā tikpil ní ki dūu cáń fiii. M tɔ́ tin ni yōoǹ ki cáań mmɔŋkee pu kubuŋu. Ba pu ní m ŋá míǹ? Man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di bālifì míǹ. Di sá yii m-diiku lítì ki kpántì kudigbuŋu, ama ní báà ŋma nimbiliŋ máǹ u-diiku pu. 10An pu ní utaa kaa jōō, ní kitiŋ mun kaa lòon̄ báà tiba. 11An pu ní m cáań ŋweel ki tɔ́ kitiŋ nee nì ajoon nì fiinyi nì ɔliifi sufii sati pu, nì tin kɔkɔ kitiŋ pée lòoǹee pu. M cáań ki tɔ́ binib nì ipeel pu, nì tin kɔkɔ ni kùn̄ee pu.»
12Ní Seeyaltiyeel jipɔɔn Sooroobabeel nì Yoosadaaki jipɔɔn Joosuwa un sá usaraaŋakpilee, nì samaa un kɔkɔ kíǹee pílifì tibɔti tin bi-Dindaan bi-Nimbɔtiu dī u-bɔnaatiliu Agaayi pu ki sòon̄ nì bee. Min Agaayi túń ditundi din ti-Dindaan dūu ŋúbíǹ-uee dee, ní tifaandi kɔ́ samaa kɔkɔ ti-Dindaan nimbiin. 13Ní Agaayi, ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋu dū tibɔti tin u fōōyee ki nāatì samaa yii: «M bí ni-cee, man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ.» 14Ní ti-Dindaan fīntì Seeyaltiyeel jipɔɔn Sooroobabeel, Juuda yab gɔminau landɔkɔŋu, nì Yoosadaaki jipɔɔn Joosuwa, usaraaŋakpil landɔkɔŋu nì samaa un kɔkɔ kíǹee landɔkɔi. Bi nìn dɔ́miń ki fātìi kíĺ ki bíi māā ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan un sá bi-Nimbɔtiuee diiku. 15An nìn sá dibindi gbanti dibaantiil poon uŋmaluluuti, iwiin mmuŋku nì inaa dal ní.

english_text:
The Glorious New Temple
1-2On the twenty-first day of the next month, the Lord told Haggai the prophet to speak this message to Governor Zerubbabel, High Priest Joshua, and everyone else:
3 Does anyone remember how glorious this temple used to be? Now it looks like nothing. 4But cheer up! Because I, the Lord All-Powerful, will be here to help you with the work, 5 just as I promised your ancestors when I brought them out of Egypt. Don't worry. My Spirit is right here with you.
6 Soon I will again shake the heavens and the earth, the sea and the dry land. 7I will shake the nations, and their treasures will be brought here. Then the brightness of my glory will fill this temple. 8All silver and gold belong to me, 9and I promise that this new temple will be more glorious than the first one. I will also bless this city with peace.
The Past and the Future
10On the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, the Lord God All-Powerful told the prophet Haggai 11to ask the priests for their opinion on the following matters:
12Suppose meat ready to be sacrificed to God is being carried in the folds of someone's clothing, and the clothing rubs against some bread or stew or wine or olive oil or any other food. Would those foods that were touched then become acceptable for sacrifice?
“Of course not,” the priests answered.
13 Then Haggai said, “Suppose someone has touched a dead body and is considered unacceptable to worship God. If that person touches these foods, would they become unclean?”
“Of course they would,” the priests answered.
14So the Lord told Haggai to say:
That's how it is with this entire nation. Everything you do and every sacrifice you offer is unacceptable to me. 15But from now on, things will get better. Before you started laying the foundation for the temple, 16you recalled what life was like in the past. When you wanted 200 kilograms of wheat, there were only 10, and when you wanted 50 jars of wine, there were only 20. 17I made all of your hard work useless by sending mildew, mold, and hail—but you still did not return to me, your Lord.
18Today you have completed the foundation for my temple, so listen to what your future will be like. 19Although you have not yet harvested any grain, grapes, figs, pomegranates, or olives, I will richly bless you in the days ahead.
God's Promise to Zerubbabel
20That same day the Lord spoke to Haggai again and said:
21Tell Governor Zerubbabel of Judah that I am going to shake the heavens and the earth 22and wipe out kings and their kingdoms. I will overturn war chariots, and then cavalry troops will start slaughtering each other. 23But tell my servant Zerubbabel that I, the Lord All-Powerful, have chosen him, and he will rule in my name.
translation_text:
Kunimbɔtidii kun bi fātìi máńee nyaaŋku
1Daariyusi nín kāl̀ dibeel abin ali uŋmaluluúti iwiin mmuŋku nì ŋubɔ dal ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì u-bɔnaatiliu Agaayi. 2U nìn bí ú tùkù Seeyaltiyeel jipɔɔn Sooroobabeel, Juuda yab gɔminau nì Yoosadaaki jipɔɔn Joosuwa usaraaŋakpil, nì samaa un kɔkɔ kíǹee yii: 3«Ubɔ bí ni-kansikin ki nìn ká kunimbɔtidii kukpikuuee nyaaŋkuɔɔɔ? Ni wāĺ kupɔŋu nee kúǹ mana? Naa ká yii kúǹ kaa bí tibanaaa? 4Kɔŋkɔnnee, Sooroobabeel, ká kunyannyaau! Man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ. Yoosadaaki jipɔɔn Yoosuwa usaraaŋakpil, ká kunyannyaau. Nimbi kitiŋ nee kɔkɔ nib, kámaan kunyannyaau. Kíĺmaan ditundi, man bí ni-cee. Man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di lī míǹ. 5M nín nìn nyántìń-ni Eejipiti tiŋkinee, m nìn lēē kí ŋá míǹ kí tīī-ni. M-Fam làá nīn bí ni-kansikin, ní taa fàŋkì tiba. 6Tiŋman, man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín lī puee sɔ̀. Án kaa làá ti yúntí m làá cìŋkì yilpu nì taapu nì tiŋku nì kitiŋ. 7M làá cìŋkì atimbun kɔkɔ ní ŋi-gaajati ń kpìntīí dāan̄ doo. M làá yàntī tinyool ń gbí kudii nee. Man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di lī míǹ. 8Di sá yii, man di yì sindaariya, man di tí yì animbil. 9Míǹ puee kunimbɔtidii kun ni fātìi máń nee nyooti làá nīn jítiǹ kukpikuu. Man ni-Dindaan di lī yii niinee, m làá tīī-ni ŋgbansɔŋfi. Man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di lī míǹ.»
Dinibul bí tijɔkɔndin
10Daariyusi nín kāl̀ dibeel dibinliliitiil ŋmawawatiu iwiin mmuŋku nì inaa dalee ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì u-bɔnaatiliu Agaayi. 11U bí-u yii ú bàlifì bisaraaŋaliibi tibɔti nee taapu: 12«Tí lì yii ubɔ dū saraa nanti ki ŋá dibɔkutil lookun. Boonee, dibɔkutilee gbēē kpɔnɔ àá tikuŋfaal àá ndamam àá ŋkpam àá tijin tin kamaa an yaa pée sée. Mimmee tijin gbanti làá kpántí circir jintaaa?» Ní bisaraaŋaliibi kíí-u yii: «Aayee». 13Ní Agaayi gíti bālifì yii: «Ubɔ yaa gbēē dinikpil ki kɔ́ tijɔkɔndin ní ki gbēē tiwan gbanti kɔkɔee, tì làá kpántí tijɔkɔŋwanaaa?» Ní bisaraaŋaliibi kíí-u yii: «Iiin, tì làá kpántí tijɔkɔŋwan.» 14Ní Agaayi fātìi bí-bi yii: «Too, ti-Dindaan nín lī puee sèé: <Míǹ ní kitiŋ nee nib nì atuun ŋin bi tūǹee bí. Míǹ ní tin kɔkɔ bi cāabìń ki ŋáań-mi saraayee kɔ́ tijɔkɔndi>».
Ŋyunti nee ní an sá tí dàkafì
15Ti-Dindaan gíti bí yii: «Kɔŋkɔnnee, ní dàkafì kí yòon̄ díǹ kí nīn cée, tin làá jītée. Kí wàatī ní kíĺ kí dū ataŋkpee kí tɔ́kɔń tɔb pu kí mā man ni-Dindaan diikuee, 16ba di nìn jītí ni-pu ní? Ubɔ yaa nìn bíi gbáà ndibɔɔ ki dàkafī yii u làá ká asambil mmuŋkuee, saalaa ní u dāa kāntí. Ubɔ yaa nìn cūtì u-dalɔŋkun kí kpíĺ ndaam liitirib imuŋku ili nì saalaayee ní ú dūú ká liitirib mmuŋku. 17M kɔ́ǹ-ni agìń ni-tuuŋŋi kɔkɔ poon. M yāntì ni-kpaajinti tiba kūń, tiba bùkū ní ataanyiŋkumbil lítì ki bíil̀ tiba, ama naa fātìi gítìń m-cee. Man ni-Dindaan di lī míǹ. 18Kí yòon̄ díǹ kí nīn cée, ní dáań tin làá jītée kí yóoń. Díǹ wiiŋŋu ŋun ni bíl̀ man ni-Dindaan diiku nyeel nee sá uŋmawawati iwiin mmuŋku nì inaa ní. Ní cúú kí yóoń! 19Kéè tijimpin kaa kíǹ cakalaabinaa! Ki kpáaǹ isufi in bi yíì fiinyi nì fiigi nì greenaadi nì ɔliifee kaa lòon̄aa! Ama kí yòon̄ díǹ kí nīn cée, m làá bìin̄ ni-pu.»
Ti-Dindaan pōoǹ Sooroobabeel dipoondi
20Iwiin mmuŋku nì inaa dal gbanti mbaantee, ti-Dindaan gíti sòon̄ nì Agaayi nliliitiim. 21U nìn bí ú tùkù Sooroobabeel, Juuda yab gɔminau yii: «M làá cìŋkì kutagbɔŋu nì kitiŋ. 22M làá lábití bibɔtiibi beejaliŋ kí cìb̄, ní kí kúntí atimbun beeŋi pɔŋyi. M làá lábití janjatɔrɔkub nì bin kā bi-puee kí cìb̄. Bi làá dāá kpɔ̀ itaamu ní bitanjakaliibi ń kpɔ̀ tɔb. 23Ama ŋwiin gbantee, sii Seeyaltiyeel jipɔɔn Sooroobabeel un sá man tɔntɔnliuee, m làá ŋúbíǹ-si ditundi diba, ti-Dindaan nyɔɔbundi dee. M làá dū-si kí ŋá m-jaliiki kin m cáa nyìitī ki dāantí m-wantee, kun puee sii ní man lēē. Man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di lī míǹ.»

english_text:
Turn to the Lord
1 I am the prophet Zechariah, the son of Berechiah and the grandson of Iddo.
In the eighth month of the second year that Darius was king of Persia, the Lord told me to say:
2-3Israel, I, the Lord All-Powerful, was very angry with your ancestors. But if you people will return to me, I will turn and help you. 4Don't be stubborn like your ancestors. They were warned by the earlier prophets to give up their evil and turn back to me, but they paid no attention.
5Where are your ancestors now? Not even prophets live forever. 6But my warnings and my words spoken by the prophets caught up with your ancestors. So they turned back to me and said, “Lord All-Powerful, you have punished us for our sins, just as you had planned.”
First Vision: Horses and Riders
7-8 On the twenty-fourth day of Shebat, which was the eleventh month of that same year, the Lord spoke to me in a vision during the night: In a valley among myrtle trees, I saw someone on a red horse, with riders on red, brown, and white horses behind him. 9An angel was there to explain things to me, and I asked, “Sir, who are these riders?”
“I'll tell you,” the angel answered.
10At once, the man standing among the myrtle trees said, “These are the ones the Lord has sent to find out what's happening on earth.”
11Then the riders spoke to the Lord's angel, who was standing among the myrtle trees, and they said, “We have gone everywhere and have discovered that the whole world is at peace.”
12At this, the angel said, “Lord All-Powerful, for 70 years you have been angry with Jerusalem and the towns of Judah. When are you ever going to have mercy on them?”
13The Lord's answer was kind and comforting. 14So the angel told me to announce:
I, the Lord All-Powerful, am very protective of Jerusalem. 15For a while I was angry at the nations, but now I am furious, because they have made things worse for Jerusalem and are not the least bit concerned. 16And so, I will have pity on Jerusalem. The city will be completely rebuilt, and my temple will stand again. 17I also promise that my towns will prosper—Jerusalem will once again be my chosen city, and I will comfort the people of Zion.
Second Vision: Animal Horns
18Next, I saw four animal horns. 19-21The angel who was sent to explain was there, and so I asked, “What do these mean?”
His answer was, “These horns are the nations that scattered the people of Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem, and took away their freedom.”
Then the Lord showed me four blacksmiths, and I asked, “What are they going to do?”
He replied, “They are going to terrify and crush those horns.”
translation_text:
TIN TI-DINDAAN LĒĒ KI DÀKĀ SAKAREE
Ti-Dindaan yíì Isirayeel yab bí kpántí bi-ba
1Daariyusi nín jíń dibeel dibinliliitiil ŋmaniniitiu poonee, ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì u-bɔnaatiliu Sakari, Baraaki jipɔɔn, Didoo naantiiu.
2U bí-u yii: «Ti-Dindaan fōō ni-baabi pu diŋuul ŋkpitim pu.» 3Á tùkù Isirayeel yab yii ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín lī puee sèé yii: «Fàtīí gítiḿmaan man cee, ní ma mun ń fàtīí gítiń ni-cee. Man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di lī míǹ. 4Ní taa fōōmaan ni-baabi bimbim. Ŋyunti ŋun nìn jítèe, m-bɔnaatiliibi nìn dū m-nyɔɔbundi ki sòon̄ nì bi yii: <Fámaan ni-saŋkpitii nì ni-bimbikpitim>, ama baa nìn pílifiǹ-mi kaa fātìi tɔ́ mun. Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di lī míǹ. 5Ni-baabi gbanti bí la? M-bɔnaatiliibi gbíntìi báaa? 6Nì míǹ kɔkɔee, m-nyɔɔbuŋŋi nì m-bɔkpaaŋi ŋin m nìn dūu tùkū m-tɔntɔnliibi bibɔnaatiliibee nìn gbēē ni-baabi pɔbiliŋ. An di nìn yāntì bi kpántì bi-bimbim ki lī yii: <Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín nìn lī yii ti-saŋkpitii nì ti-tuŋkpitiŋ pu u làá ŋá-ti miŋyee, míǹ ní u ŋá nee.>»
Dileedakal dipeekaal: itaamu
7Daariyusi nín jíń dibeel dibinliliitiil iŋmal saalaa nì ubɔ, uŋmal un bi yíì Seebatee poon iwiin mmuŋku nì inaa dal ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì u-bɔnaatiliu Sakari, Baraaki jipɔɔn, Didoo naantiiu.
Sakari nín sòon̄ tiŋyee sɔ̀. 8An lēē ki dàkā-mi kunyeeu gbanti. M ká utanjakal ubɔ kā utaamu un máǹ wèeeeyee pu. U nìn yú nsutantamu mun bi yíì miirtee taapu ditantakal diban. Itaamu in máń wèeeeyee nì in máǹ gàaayee nì itampiin iba mun yú u-boon. 9Ní m bālifì-u yii: «M-Dindaan, itaamu nee taapu là kí lì yii ba dee?» Ní ntuun ŋun bíi sòoǹ nì mee bí-mi yii: «M làá tùkù-si i-taapu nín sá puee.» 10Ní uninja un yú nsutantamu mun bi yíì miirtee kansikinee kíí yii: «An sá bin ti-Dindaan tú bí yìiǹ kí màntì kitiŋee.» 11Niinee ní binibee bí ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋu ŋun yú nsutantamuee kansikinee yii: «Ti yìin̄ ki māntì kitiŋ ki kpēē, ti ká yii kitiŋ kɔkɔ bí ŋgbansɔŋfin, tiba kaa páb́ ki-nib.» 12Ní ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋu bí yii: «Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, a nín fōō Jeerusaleem tiŋki nì Juuda timmu mun kíǹee pu diŋuulee, abin imuŋku ita nì saalaa sèé. Mimmee kí tin sāā ŋyunti ŋulɔŋu ní a làá sɔ̄ bi-saai?» 13Ní ti-Dindaan kíí ntuun ŋun bíi sòoǹ nì mee kunyannyaau nì dipɔɔsɔŋkil nyɔɔbundi.
Unimbɔti làá sɔ̄ Siiyɔn saai
14Ní ntuun ŋun bíi sòoǹ nì mee bí-mi yii ḿ bāakì ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan bɔti nee yii:
«M cáá dineeŋkpaandi Jeerusaleem tiŋki
nì Siiyɔn gbantaŋki pu tikpil.
15Ama m fōō atimbun
ŋin máká ŋi-ba puee pu mbiim tikpil,
di sá yii ŋyunti ŋun m nìn fōō
m-nibul pu diŋuul fiiiyee,
bíǹ dɔ́miń ki púntì ki nāaǹ-dì.
16An pu ní man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan, m lī yii
m làá fàtīí gítiń Jeerusaleem
kí dàkà m-laŋŋaŋfitiiku.
Bi làá fàtīí mā m-diiku niin
nì Jeerusaleem tiŋki.»
17Míǹ boonee ní ntuunee bí-mi yii ḿ dū ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nyɔɔbundi nee kí nàatī:
«M-timmu làá fàtīí tí kɔ́ digbíl poon.
M làá fàtīí sɔ̀ŋkì Siiyɔn gbantaŋki pɔbil,
ní kí fàtīí tí lēē Jeerusaleem tiŋki.»

english_text:
Third Vision: A Measuring Line
1This time I saw someone holding a measuring line, 2and I asked, “Where are you going?”
“To measure Jerusalem,” was the answer. “To find out how wide and long it is.”
3The angel who had spoken to me came toward me, when another angel came up to him 4and said, “Hurry! Tell that man with the measuring line that Jerusalem won't have any boundaries. It will be too full of people and animals even to have a wall. 5The Lord himself has promised to be a protective wall of fire surrounding Jerusalem, and he will be its shining glory in the heart of the city.”
A Call to Action
6The Lord says to his people, “Run! Escape from the land in the north, where I scattered you to the four winds. 7Leave Babylonia and hurry back to Zion.”
8Then the glorious Lord All-Powerful ordered me to say to the nations that had raided and robbed Zion:
Zion is as precious to the Lord as are his eyes. Whatever you do to Zion, you do to him. 9And so, he will put you in the power of your slaves, and they will raid and rob you. Then you will know that I am a prophet of the Lord All-Powerful.
10City of Zion, sing and celebrate! The Lord has promised to come and live with you. 11When he does, many nations will turn to him and become his people. At that time you will know that I am a prophet of the Lord All-Powerful. 12Then Judah will be his part of the holy land, and Jerusalem will again be his chosen city.
13Everyone, be silent!
The Lord is present
and moving about
in his holy place.
translation_text:
Dileedakal dililiitiil: iyin nì bicaabi bɔti
1M wáaǹ ki kpēē kutaayee ní ki ká iyin inaa. 2Ní m bālifì ntuun ŋun bíi sòoǹ nì mee yii: «Iyin nee taapu là kí lì yii ba ní?» Ní ŋu kíí-mi yii: «Iyin nee sá atimbun ŋin jìn̄ Juuda nì Isirayeel nì Jeerusaleem yab ki yàl̄ee ní.»
3Míǹ boonee, ti-Dindaan lēē bicaabi binaa ki dàkā-mi. 4Ní m bālifì yii: «Bi dɔ́miń kí ŋá ba ní?» Ní ŋu kíí-mi yii: «Bi dɔ́miń kí kɔ́ǹ atimbun ŋin jìn̄ Juuda yab ki yàl̄ee dinyoondi kí nàan̄-ŋi ní. Bi jìn̄ Juuda yab bi yàl̄ an kɔkɔ pu ní ubɔ kaa ŋúń ki yúl̀ bi-nimbiin.»
Dileedakal ditataatiil: ŋŋmii ŋun bi cáa ŋmàntēe
5M wáaǹ kutaayee ní an lēē ki dàkā-mi. M ká uninja ubɔ u ŋúb́ ŋŋmii ŋun bi cáa ŋmàntēe u-ŋaan. 6Ní m bālifì-u yii: «A cá la?» Ní u kíí-mi yii: «M cá kí ŋmàntī Jeerusaleem tiŋki kí béé ki-púuŋŋu nì ki-waaŋŋu nín sá puee.»
7Niinee ní ntuun ŋun bíi sòoǹ nì mee cōom̀ ki nín cá ní ŋubɔ mun cōom̀ ki túŋkiǹ-ŋu. 8Ní ŋu bí ŋun túŋkí-ŋuee yii: «Sāǹ kí cùú tùkù unaacimpɔɔn un ŋúb́ ŋŋmii nee yii: <Jeerusaleem tiŋki kaa làá dāá nīn cáá digundi, binib nì tiwaŋkuti wíiŋŋu pu. 9Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín sòon̄ puee sɔ̀. Man m-ba làá nīn bí bi-cee kí nīn sá kii ŋŋmi gundee kí màntīí tù kitiŋ, ní kí lēē m-nyooti kí dàkà ki-kansikin.>»
Bi yíiń bin bíń kunicaŋuee ń fàtīí gítiń
10Ti-Dindaan lī yii:
Ēeyi! Nimbi bin m nìn jìn̄ ni yàl̄ an kɔkɔ pu,
ki bíń ŋgan nì ŋgiil púee,
ŋwìiń nyalaŋki nì ŋu-jeetilaŋki púee,
sām̀maan kɔŋkɔnnee,
nyānnímaan ŋgan pú tiŋkin.
11Ēeyi! Nimbi Jeerusaleem yab
bin bíń Babiloon tiŋkin kuyuŋuee,
sām̀maan malaa kí ŋmátí.
12Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan un túnní-mi ki tīī-mi mpɔnee nín sòon̄ atimbun ŋin fúkúl̀-nee puee sèé:
«Un kamaa yaa gbēē-nee
gbēē man nimbibul dee.
13Tiŋman, m làá já nì atimbun gbanti yab.
M làá yàntī bin bi nìn cúú kuyuŋuee
ń fūkul̀-bi.
Niinee, ni làá dāá béé yii
ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di túnní-mi.
14Jeerusaleem tiŋki, kúuǹ nì dipɔɔpindi,
nín̄ fàal̀.
Di sá yii m dòoń
kí dāá nīn kóò a-cee.
Ti-Dindaan di lī míǹ.
15Ŋwiin gbantee, atimbun tikpil
làá dāá dū ŋi-ba kí nákáǹ man ni-Dindaan.
Ŋi làá dāá kpántí m-nibul.
M làá dāá nīn kóò ni-kansikin.»
Niinee, ni làá dāá béé yii ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di túnní-mi ni-cee.
16Juuda tiŋki làá dāá fàtīí kpántí
ti-Dindaan gaajawanti circir tiŋki.
U làá dāá fàtīí tí lēē Jeerusaleem
kí nīn sá u-tiŋki.
17Tiwan tin kɔkɔ cáá kufoouee
ń ŋmīĺ fɔ́ŋfɔŋ díkí diki
ti-Dindaan nimbiin.
Di sá yii u làá yīkìí nyānní
u-circir kɔŋkooŋŋun.

english_text:
Fourth Vision: Joshua and Satan
1 I was given another vision. This time Joshua the high priest was standing in front of the Lord's angel. And there was Satan, standing at Joshua's right side, ready to accuse him. 2 But the Lord said, “Satan, you are wrong. Jerusalem is my chosen city, and this man was rescued like a stick from a flaming fire.”
3Joshua's clothes were filthy. 4So the angel told some of the people to remove Joshua's filthy clothes. Then he said to Joshua, “This means you are forgiven. Now I will dress you in priestly clothes.”
5I spoke up and said, “Also put a clean priestly turban on his head.” Then they dressed him in priestly clothes and put the turban on him, while the Lord's angel stood there watching.
6After this, the angel encouraged Joshua by telling him that the Lord All-Powerful had promised:
7If you truly obey me, I will put you in charge of my temple, including the courtyard around it, and you will be allowed to speak at any time with the angels standing beside me. 8 Listen carefully, High Priest Joshua and all of you other priests. You are a sign of things to come, because I am going to bring my servant, the Chosen King.
9Joshua, I have placed in front of you a stone with seven sides. I will engrave something on that stone, and in a single day I will forgive this guilty country. 10 Then each of you will live at peace and entertain your friends in your own vineyard and under your own fig trees.
translation_text:
Dileedakal dinanaatiil: Usaraaŋakpil Joosuwa
1Boonee ní ti-Dindaan yāntì m wál̀ Joosuwa usaraaŋakpil, u yú ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋu nimbiin. Sitaan nìn yú Joosuwa ŋaŋgiil pú ki kúŋfí u-boon. 2Ní ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋu bí Sitaan yii: «Ti-Dindaan di làá kpìin̄-si, Sitaan. Tiŋman ti-Dindaan un di lēē Jeerusaleemee di làá kpìin̄-si. Joosuwa kaa sá kii kisanteei kin bi lēeńeeee?»
3Joosuwa nìn yú ntuun nimbiin ki pēē tiwan tin cáá tijɔkɔndee. 4Ní ntuun bí bin yú ŋu-nimbiinee yii: «Pèetīmaan-u tiwan tin u pēē tì cáá tijɔkɔndee.» Boonee ní ŋu bí Joosuwa yii: «Kpèè, m cúú a-kpitii ki lēē a-pu, m làá dū jiŋaal bɔkutiŋ ní kí pèen̄-si.» 5Ní ŋu bí yii: «Bí dū ŋŋaabu ŋun ŋān̄ dándanee kí fìn̄ u-yil. Ní bi dū ŋŋaabu ŋun ŋān̄ dándanee ki fìn̄ u-yil, ní ki pēeǹ-u abɔkutimɔnti ti-Dindaan tuuŋŋuee nimbiin niin.» 6Boonee ntuunee nín sòon̄ nì Joosuwa puee sɔ̀. 7Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé:
«A yaa nóó m-saŋŋu,
ki ŋúb́ m-marabee,
sii di làá nīn kpòotī m-diiku poon tuuŋŋi,
ní kí nīn cí m-cindi.
M làá dū-si kí kūtì bin bí
m-cee doo m-tundinee pu.»
Unimbɔti làá fàtīí gíiǹ u-tɔntɔnliu
8«Pīlifì Joosuwa,
sii un sá usaraaŋakpilee.
Ni mun pīlifìmaan, nimbi bin sá u-tɔntɔnjutiibee.
Di sá yii ni sá difiil din dòońee daaŋku ní.
M làá yàntī m-tɔntɔnliu
un bi yíì <Nnaantee> ń dāan̄.
9Di sá yii m dū ditaŋkpal diba ki bíl̀ Joosuwa nimbiin,
ditaŋkpabaabil gbanti cáá animbil aluli ní.
Man m-ba làá ŋmà di-pu tiŋmaŋmabiti.
M làá dāá lēē kitiŋ gbanti kpitii ŋwimbaanti ní.
Man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di lī míǹ.
10Ŋwiin gbanti yaa láa bāańee,
ni dāa yíì tɔb fiinyi nì fiigi
subooŋyi taapu ní ki fàal̀ dibatɔl pu.»

english_text:
Fifth Vision: A Lampstand and Olive Trees
1The angel who explained the visions woke me from what seemed like sleep. 2Then he asked, “What do you see?”
“A solid gold lampstand with an oil container above it,” I answered. “On the stand are seven lamps, each with seven flames. 3 One olive tree is on the right side and another on the left of the oil container. 4But, sir, what do these mean?”
5Then he asked, “Don't you know?”
“No sir,” I replied.
6 So the angel explained that it was the following message of the Lord to Zerubbabel:
I am the Lord All-Powerful. So don't depend on your own power or strength, but on my Spirit. 7Zerubbabel, that mountain in front of you will be leveled to the ground. Then you will bring out the temple's most important stone and shout, “God has been very kind.”
8The Lord spoke to me again and said:
9Zerubbabel laid the foundation for the temple, and he will complete it. Then everyone will know that you were sent by me, the Lord All-Powerful. 10 Those who have made fun of this day of small beginnings will celebrate when they see Zerubbabel holding this important stone.
Those seven lamps represent my eyes—the eyes of the Lord—and they see everything on this earth.
11 Then I asked the angel, “What about the olive trees on each side of the lampstand? What do they represent? 12And what is the meaning of the two branches from which golden olive oil flows through the two gold pipes?”
13“Don't you know?” he asked.
“No sir, I don't,” was my answer.
14Then he told me, “These branches are the two chosen leaders who stand beside the Lord of all the earth.”
translation_text:
Dileedakal diŋmooŋmootiil: fitilab tɔ́kɔŋkaati nì ɔliifi sufii bɔti
1 Ntuun ŋun nìn bí ki sòoǹ nì mee fātìi gítìń ki fīntì-mi kii bi nín fìntī unil ŋgeem pu puee. 2Ní ŋu bālifì-mi yii: «Ba ní a wāĺ ní?» Ní m kíí-ŋu yii: «M wāĺ fitilab tɔ́kɔŋkaati tin sá sindaariya ŋmee ní. Kusɔŋu kun poon bi ŋáań fitilab kpamee tɔ́kɔ́ ti-yilpu. Fitilab biluli tɔ́kɔ́ ti-pu ní fitila kamaa cáá iŋmii iluli. 3Ní ɔliifi sufii ili yú ki kɔ́ĺ kusɔŋuee, bubɔ yú ŋŋaŋgiil pú, bun kíǹee yú ŋŋaŋgan pú.» 4Ní m fātìi bālifì ntuun ŋun bíi sòoǹ nì mee yii: «M-dindaan, tin kɔkɔ m wāĺ nee taapu sá yii ba ní?» 5Ní ŋu kíí-mi yii: «Aa nyí ti-taapuɔɔɔ?» Ní m kíí-ŋu yii «Aayee m-dindaan maa nyí.» 6 Ní ŋu bí-mi yii:
7 «Fitilab bilulee sá ti-Dindaan nimbiliŋ ŋin di kpèé tin jītí kitiŋ kɔkɔ puee ní.» 8 Ní m gíti bālifì-ŋu yii: «Kin ɔliifi sufii ili in yú ki kɔ́ĺ fitilab tɔ́kɔŋkaati, bubɔ ŋŋaŋgiil pú, bun kíǹee ŋŋaŋgan púee taapu sá yii ba?» 9 Ní m fātìi bālifì-ŋu nliliitiim yii: «Ɔliifi pammu mun pu sindaariya nai ili túuń ɔliifi kpam dì i-pu ki còol̀ ki kóò fitilabinee taapu sá yii ba?» 10 Ní ŋu bí-mi yii: «Aa nyí taapuɔɔɔ?» Ní m kíí-ŋu yii: «Aayee m-Dindaan maa nyí.» 11 Niinee ní ŋu bí-mi yii: «An sá binib bili bin yil pu bi sītì ŋkpam ki dū-bi ki sú kitiŋ kɔkɔ Dindaan, bi bí u-nimbiin ki tūǹ u-tundee ní.»
Dipoondi din ti-Dindaan pōoǹ Sooroobabeelee
12 Ntuunee tīī dinyɔɔbundi ḿ dūú nàatī Sooroobabeel yii:
«An kaa sá nì mpɔn,
kaa tí sá nì dikpabil,
ama an sá nì man Fam ní.»
Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di lī míǹ.
13 Ní u kútì ki lī yii:
Dijookpaandi, sii di sá ŋma ní?
Sooroobabeel nimbiinee,
a làá kpátí kí tàntī.
Niin ní u làá lēē ditaŋkpal
din làá nīn tíĺ kudiiyee.
Binib làá dāá nīn kūuntí ki lì-dì yii:
«Mbóo! Mbóo!»
14 Ti-Dindaan gíti sòon̄ nì mi tibɔti nee yii: 15 «Sooroobabeel di bíl̀ kunimbɔtidii nee nyeel,
úǹ di làá tí mā-ku kí látí.»
Án yaa láa jítì mimmee, ni làá dāá béé yii ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di túnní-mi ni-cee.
16 Unil ń taa kpèè ditundi
nín kíĺ min falaa falaayee fám.
Ama unil yaa ká Sooroobabeel kíĺ
ki bíi māā kunimbɔtidiiyee,
ú nīn fàal̀.

english_text:
Sixth Vision: A Flying Scroll
1When I looked the next time, I saw a flying scroll, 2and the angel asked, “What do you see?”
“A flying scroll,” I answered. “About nine meters long and four and a half meters wide.”
3Then he told me:
This scroll puts a curse on everyone in the land who steals or tells lies. The writing on one side tells about the destruction of those who steal, while the writing on the other side tells about the destruction of those who lie.
4The Lord All-Powerful has said, “I am sending this scroll into the house of everyone who is a robber or tells lies in my name, and it will remain there until every piece of wood and stone in that house crumbles.”
Seventh Vision: A Woman in a Basket
5Now the angel who was there to explain the visions came over and said, “Look up and tell me what you see coming.”
6“I don't know what it is,” was my reply.
“It's a big basket,” he said. “And it shows what everyone in the land has in mind.”
7The lead cover of the basket was opened, and in the basket was a woman. 8“This woman represents evil,” the angel explained. Then he threw her back into the basket and slammed the heavy cover down tight.
9Right after this I saw two women coming through the sky with wings outstretched like a stork in the wind. Suddenly they lifted the basket into the air, 10and I asked the angel, “Where are they taking the basket?”
11“To Babylonia,” he answered, “where they will build a house for the basket and set it down inside.”
translation_text:
Dileedakal diluluutiil: mbusu gbɔŋku
1M tí wáaǹ kutaayee ní ki ká kugbɔŋu kubɔ ŋàaǹ kutaa pu.
2Ní ntuun bālifì-mi yii: «Ba ní a wāĺ ní?» Ní m kíí yii: «M wāĺ kugbɔŋu kubɔ ŋàaǹ kutaa pu, ku-púuŋŋu sá meetab saalaa, ní ku-waaŋŋu sá meetab biŋmoo.» 3Niinee ní ŋu bí-mi yii: «An sá mbusu bɔti tin bi làá dūú tɔ̄ kitiŋ nee kɔkɔ puee ní. Bi ŋmàn̄ kugbɔŋu gbanti jandi diba pu yii bí jà binaayub kɔkɔ kitiŋ nee pu, ní ki ŋmàn̄ dijandi din kíǹee pu yii bí jà bin kɔkɔ pùtī fám fámee mun.» 4Ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan lī yii: «Mama m-ba di tɔ́ń mbusu gbanti. U làá kɔ́ unaayuu kamaa diikun, unil un kamaa pùtī m-yindi fám fámee diikun. Mbusu gbanti làá gbíntí bi-diiŋŋin ní kí wà tikɔkɔ, kí kpáaǹ ŋi-dɔi nì ŋi-taŋkpeeŋi.»
Dileedakal diluluútiil: unimpu un sá ikpiti daaŋkuee
5 Ntuun ŋun bíi sòoǹ nì mee sútìń ní ki bí-mi yii: «Yáatí kí kpèè kun còom̄ ki dòoń nee.» 6Ní m bālifì-ŋu yii: «Ba ní an sá ní?» Ní ŋu kíí yii: «An sá kukabiku kun poon ní kitiŋ nee kɔkɔ kpitii kēe.»
7Ŋyunti gbantee, dibìil din sá tikúmanee cúu gántì yilpu ní m ká unimpu ubɔ kā kukabikuee poon. 8Ní ntuun bí-mi yii: «Unimpu nee sá tikpitil daaŋku ní.»
Ní u téé-u ki gíiǹ ki tɔ́ kukabikun, ní ki dū ku-bìil kun sá tikúmanee ki púkuǹ. 9Míǹ boon m wáaǹ kutaayee ní ki ká binimpoobi bili páaǹní. Bi nìn cáá ifeen an náań nì naakpaapiin feeŋyi, ní kubuŋu téekí-bi bi ŋàaǹ ki cá. Ní bi yōoǹ kukabikuee ki cáa jɔ́ntì kutaa. 10Ní m bālifì ntuun ŋun bí ki sòoǹ nì mee yii: «Bi cáǹ kukabikuee la?» 11Ní ŋu kíí-mi yii: «Bi cáǹ-kù Sineeyaar tiŋkin kí tin mā-kù kuwaadii ní. Bi làá mā dikɔl ní kí dū-ku kí báań dikɔlee pu.»

english_text:
Eighth Vision: Four Chariots
1Finally, I looked up and saw four chariots coming from between two bronze mountains. 2 The first chariot was pulled by red horses, and the second by black horses; 3 the third chariot was pulled by white horses, and the fourth by spotted gray horses.
4“Sir,” I asked the angel. “What do these stand for?”
5 Then he explained, “These are the four winds of heaven, and now they are going out, after presenting themselves to the Lord of all the earth. 6The chariot with black horses goes toward the north, the chariot with white horses goes toward the west, and the one with spotted horses goes toward the south.”
7The horses came out eager to patrol the earth, and the angel told them, “Start patrolling the earth.”
When they had gone on their way, 8he shouted to me, “Those that have gone to the country in the north will do what the Lord's Spirit wants them to do there.”
The Chosen Leader
9The Lord said to me:
10-11Heldai, Tobijah, and Jedaiah have returned from Babylonia. Collect enough silver and gold from them to make a crown. Then go with them to the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah and put the crown on the head of the high priest Joshua son of Jehozadak. 12-13 Tell him that I, the Lord All-Powerful, say, “Someone will reach out from here like a branch and build a temple for me. I will name him ‘Branch,’ and he will rule with royal honors. A priest will stand beside his throne, and the two of them will be good friends. 14This crown will be kept in my temple as a reminder and will be taken care of by Heldai, Tobijah, Jedaiah, and Josiah.”
15When people from distant lands come and help build the temple of the Lord All-Powerful, you will know that the Lord is the one who sent me. And this will happen, if you truly obey the Lord your God.
translation_text:
Dileedakal dininiitiil: janjatɔrɔkub binaa bɔti
1M fātìi tí wáaǹ kutaa puee, ní ki wál̀ janjatɔrɔkub binaa nyánní tikúman jooŋŋi ali kansikin. 2Itaamu in máǹ gàaayee di nìn dátí tɔrɔkupeepeekaa, ní itambɔn dátí tɔrɔkuliliiti, 3ní itampiin dátí tɔrɔkutataati, ní itaamu in cáá atan atan ki ŋmàl̄ mmam gàaayee dátí tɔrɔkunanaati. 4Ní m bālifì ntuun ŋun bí ki sòoǹ nì mee yii: «Ukpil, itaamu nì tɔrɔkub nee taapu sá yii ba ní?» 5Ní ntuunee kíí-mi yii: «Itaamu nì tɔrɔkub gbanti taapu dàkà kubuŋu kun nyēeń kitiŋ jannaatiliŋee ní. Ku nìn bí kitiŋ kɔkɔ Dindaan cee ní kɔŋkɔnnee ku yíkì u-cee.» 6Ní tɔrɔku un itambɔn dátée búntì ŋgan pú tiŋki watil, ní tɔrɔku un itampiin dátée búntì ŋwìiń jeetilaŋki pú ní tɔrɔku un itaamu in cáá atan atanee dátée búntì ŋgiil pú tiŋki watil. 7Itaamu in máǹ gàaayee nìn nyàab̀ malaa kí cùú yìiǹ kitiŋ pu. Ní ti-Dindaan bí-i yii: «Nín̄ cámaan kí yìiǹ kitiŋ pu.» Ní i búntì ki cūtìi yìin̄ kitiŋ pu. 8Ní ti-Dindaan yíiń-mi ki bí yii: «Kpèè, in búntì ŋgan pú tiŋki watilee làá sɔ̀ŋkì m-ŋuul kitiŋ gbanti pu.»
Kibeefuulii kin sá kudaaŋŋu bi dūu cíkiǹ Joosuwayee
9Ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì mi yii: 10«Cù Eeldayii nì Toobiya nì Yeedaya cee kí fōō animbil ŋin bin bíń kuyuŋuee tɔ́ ki tīińee. Á yīkì díǹ díǹ kí cù Seefaniya jipɔɔn Yoosiya dumpu, binib gbanti nyánní Babiloon ki dáá bàń dee. 11Á fōō animbil nì Sindaariya kí mɔ́ɔ́ kibeefuulii kí cíkiń usaraaŋakpil Yoosadaaki jipɔɔn Joosuwa. 12Ní kí tùkù-u yii: <Kpèè, ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín lī puee sɔ̀.
Unil ubɔ bí doo
u-yindi di sá <nnaanti>.
Laakin u yaa pée bée,
dimaŋfal làá pā kí nyā,
úǹ di làá dāá fàtīí mā ti-Dindaan diiku.
13Tiŋman, úǹ di làá dāá fàtīí mā ti-Dindaan diiku.
U làá dāá nīn pēē abeebɔkuti.
U làá dāá kàl̄ u-beejal pu
kí kpòotī u-nibul.
Usaraaŋal ubɔ làá dāá nīn yú u-ŋaŋgiil pú,
ní bi-liitil ń dāá nīn gbìliǹ tɔb mmɔntiim.
14«<Kibeefuulii gbanti làá dāá nīn bí kunimbɔtidiin bí nīn cáa téetí Eeldayii nì Toobiya nì Yeedaya nì Seefaniya jipɔɔn ŋanti pu.>»
15Binib làá dāá nyānní ndandati kí fàtīí mā ti-Dindaan diiku. Niin ní ni dāa béetí yii ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan di túnní-mi ni-cee. See ni yaa tɔ́ ti-Dindaan ni-Nimbɔtiu mmɔntiimin baba ní án làá ŋá míǹ.

english_text:
A Question about Going without Eating
1On the fourth day of Chislev, the ninth month of the fourth year that Darius was king of Persia, the Lord again spoke to me. 2-3It happened after the people of Bethel had sent Sharezer with Regem-Melech and his men to ask the priests in the Lord's temple and the prophets to pray for them. So they prayed, “Should we mourn and go without eating during the fifth month, as we have done for many years?”
4-5It was then that the Lord All-Powerful told me to say to everyone in the country, including the priests:
For 70 years you have gone without eating during the fifth and seventh months of the year. But did you really do it for me? 6And when you eat and drink, isn't it for your own enjoyment? 7My message today is the same one I commanded the earlier prophets to speak to Jerusalem and its villages when they were prosperous, and when all of Judah, including the Southern Desert and the hill country, was filled with people.
8-9So once again, I, the Lord All-Powerful, tell you, “See that justice is done and be kind and merciful to one another! 10Don't mistreat widows or orphans or foreigners or anyone who is poor, and stop making plans to hurt each other.”
11-12But everyone who heard those prophets, stubbornly refused to obey. Instead, they turned their backs on everything my Spirit had commanded the earlier prophets to preach. So I, the Lord, became angry 13and said, “You people paid no attention when I called out to you, and now I'll pay no attention when you call out to me.”
14That's why I came with a whirlwind and scattered them among foreign nations, leaving their lovely country empty of people and in ruins.
translation_text:
Isirayeel yab baasii bōob̀ kinyɔkɔ Unimbɔti pu níii?
1Daariyusi nín jíń dibeel dibinnanaatiil uŋmawawati, an dàkà yii uŋmal un bi yíì Kiisileefee iwiin inaa dal ní ti-Dindaan sòon̄ nì Sakari tibɔti nee. 2Beeteel yab nìn tú Sareeseer nì Reegeem-Meeleeki ní ki lēē binib ki kútì bi-pu bí cùú gbàam̀ ti-Dindaan ú sɔ̄ bi-saai. 3Binib gbanti nìn máaǹ kí bàlifì ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan saraaŋaliibi bin bí kunimbɔtidiinee nì u-bɔnaatiliibi yii: «Tí nīn gbíntìi sūǹ ki bōob̀ kinyɔkɔ uŋmaŋmooŋmooti poon kii ti nín pée kpààa ŋáań abin ŋin jítèe pueeyaaa, tí taa ti ŋá?» 4Niinee ní ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan sòon̄ nì mi tibɔti nee 5ḿ bàlifì kitiŋ nee pu yab kɔkɔ nì bisaraaŋaliibi yii:
«Ni nín bōob̀ kinyɔkɔ
ki sūǹ ki yáliŋkí uŋmaŋmooŋmooti nì
uŋmaluluúti kamaa áli abin imuŋku ita nì saalaayee,
ni ŋá míǹ án mɔ̄ɔkiǹ-mi níii?
6Ni yaa nìn tí bíi jīǹ ki nyùee,
kaa nìn sá nimbi ni-ba
ní ni jīǹ ki tììii?»
7Ŋyunti ŋun Jeerusaleem yab nì ntimu mun māntìi tú-kèe yab nìn dáá bí nsɔŋfinee, nì ŋyunti ŋun binib nìn dáá kóò Neegeeb teekun nì Seefeelaa paal puee, ti-Dindaan nìn yāntì u-bɔnaatiliibi dooooyee yab báakì ki kpáafì binib tibɔti gbanti.
8Ti-Dindaan nìn sòon̄ nì Sakari yii: 9«Man ni-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan nín sòon̄ puee sèé yii:
<Ní sòoǹ ni-juti bɔti nì mbaamɔn,
ní báà ŋma ń dàkà u-juti dineendi nì disaasɔl.
10Ní taa mùul̀ ukpiipu nì ditaŋkpiibil,
nì unicaan nì bisoodambi.
Ni-kansikin ubɔ ń taa dàkafì
u-juti pu nlandɔkɔkpiti.»
11Ama bi nìn yíì kaa pílifì, ki pɔ́ɔkì bi-pɔbiliŋ. Bi nìn kpáá bi-tafaliŋ kí taa gbìl̄. 12Bi nìn pɔ́ɔkì bi-pɔbiliŋ kii ditaŋkpalee. Baa nìn là kí pīlifì ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan bɔti nì u-dakal din u-Fam nìn dī u-bɔnaatiliibi dooooyee yab pu ki tīī-bee. Niinee ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan gíí bi-pu diŋuul ŋkpitim pu. 13An pu ní ti-Dindaan Mpɔŋkɔdaan lī yii:
«Kii man nín yíiń-bi
baa pílifiǹ-mee,
míǹ mbaantiim ní bi yíiń-mi
ní ma mun kaa pílifiǹ-bi.
14M jìn̄-bi bi yàl̄ ki kɔ́
atimbun ŋin kɔkɔ baa nyée poon.
Kitiŋ kin bi yíkìi yāntèe,
bi nāaǹ-kì,
ní ubɔ kaa ti cá ki-naaa,
ubɔ kaa ti nyēē ki-ni.
Kitiŋ kin nìn sá kimɔntii ki mɔ̄ ŋkaayee
dūu kpántì kuteeu.»

english_text:
The Lord's Promises to Zion
1The Lord All-Powerful said to me:
2I love Zion so much that her enemies make me angry. 3I will return to Jerusalem and live there on Mount Zion. Then Jerusalem will be known as my faithful city, and Zion will be known as my holy mountain.
4Very old people with walking sticks will once again sit around in Jerusalem, 5while boys and girls play in the streets. 6This may seem impossible for my people who are left, but it isn't impossible for me, the Lord All-Powerful. 7I will save those who were taken to lands in the east and the west, 8and I will bring them to live in Jerusalem. They will be my people, and I will be their God, faithful to bring about justice.
9I am the Lord All-Powerful! So don't give up. Think about the message my prophets spoke when the foundation of my temple was laid. 10Before that time, neither people nor animals were rewarded for their work, and no one was safe anywhere, because I had turned them against each other.
11My people, only a few of you are left, and I promise not to punish you as I did before. 12Instead, I will make sure that your crops are planted in peace and your vineyards are fruitful, that your fields are fertile, and the dew falls from the sky. 13People of Judah and Israel, you have been a curse to the nations, but I will save you and make you a blessing to them. So don't be afraid or lose courage.
14When your ancestors made me angry, I decided to punish you with disasters, and I didn't hold back. 15Now you no longer need to be afraid. I have decided to treat Jerusalem and Judah with kindness. 16 But you must be truthful with each other, and in court you must give fair decisions that lead to peace. 17Don't ever plan evil things against others or tell lies under oath. I, the Lord, hate such things.
A Time of Celebration
18The Lord All-Powerful told me to say:
19People of Judah, I, the Lord, demand that whenever you go without food as a way of worshiping me, it should become a time of celebration. No matter if it's the fourth month, the fifth month, the seventh month, or the tenth month, you should have a joyful festival. So love truth and live at peace.
20I tell you that people will come here from cities everywhere. 21Those of one town will go to another and say, “We're going to ask the Lord All-Powerful to treat us with kindness. Come and join us.”
